A solid shaft of diameter 71 mm transmits a torque of 2850 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 71, Tt = 2850 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(2850*1000) / (pi*(71)^3) | Answer: 40.55 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 30 mm and length 1200 mm carries a torque of 1850 N-m. With G = 77 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (30)^4 / 32 = 79522 mm^4 | theta = (1850*1000)(1200) / (77000 * 79522) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 20.77 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 138 mm wide and 280 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 138, h = 280 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 138*(280)^2 / 6 | Answer: 1803200 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (90 mm x 80 mm) carries a bending moment of 26 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (62 mm x 150 mm) has effective length 2400 mm and E = 200 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 330 MPa is designed for a working stress of 90 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 330, sw = 90 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 330 / 90 | Answer: 3.667

question: A steel bar is fully restrained and heated through 35 deg C. With E = 200 GPa and alpha = 11e-6 /deg C, find the thermal stress in MPa.
solution: Given: dT = 35, E = 200, al = 11 | Formula: sigma = E alpha (dT) | Substitute: sigma = 200000 * 11e-6 * 35 | Answer: 77 MPa

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1500 mm and wall thickness 8 mm carries an internal pressure of 0.5 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1500, t = 8, P = 0.5 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 0.5*1500 / (2*8) | Answer: 46.88 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 1020 K and 350 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 1020, Tc = 350 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 350/1020) * 100 | Answer: 65.69 %

question: A refrigerator works between 256 K (cold) and 310 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 256, Th = 310 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 256 / (310 - 256) | Answer: 4.741

question: A heat pump operates between 284 K and 322 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 284, Th = 322 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 322 / (322 - 284) | Answer: 8.474

question: An Otto cycle has a compression ratio of 11. Taking gamma = 1.4, find the air-standard efficiency (%).
solution: Given: r = 11 | Formula: eta = 1 - 1/r^(gamma-1) | Substitute: eta = (1 - 1/11^0.4) * 100 | Answer: 61.68 %

question: 3.2 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 95 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.2, dT = 95 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 3.2 * 0.718 * 95 | Answer: 218.3 kJ

question: 1.1 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 140 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1.1, dT = 140 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 1.1 * 1.005 * 140 | Answer: 154.8 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 1.8 m^3 at 320 K with mass 3.3 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 1.8, Tk = 320, m = 3.3 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 3.3*0.287*320 / 1.8 | Answer: 168.4 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 2.1 kg of air expands isothermally at 450 K from volume V1 to 3*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.1, Tk = 450, ratio = 3 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 2.1*0.287*450*ln(3) | Answer: 298 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 2.4 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.12 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 2.4, D = 0.12 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*2.4*0.12 / 0.001 | Answer: 288000

question: Water flows at 3.4 m/s through a pipe of diameter 300 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 13.9 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 13.9 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*13.9 / 1000 | Answer: 136.4 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 6.9 m. Taking Cv = 0.96, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 6.9, cv = 0.96 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.96*sqrt(2*9.81*6.9) | Answer: 11.17 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 260 mm) water flows at 1.1 m/s. It contracts to diameter 130 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 260, d2 = 130, V1 = 1.1 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 1.1*(260/130)^2 | Answer: 4.4 m/s

question: Water flows at 3.2 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.47 m and length 310 m. With friction factor f = 0.031, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 35 teeth drives a gear of 56 teeth. If the pinion runs at 300 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 35, z2 = 56, N1 = 300 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 300*35 / 56 | Answer: 187.5 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 310 mm rotates at 350 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 310, N = 350 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.31)*350 / 60 | Answer: 5.681 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 14.1 kW at 600 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 14.1, N = 600 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(14.1*1000) / (2*pi*600) | Answer: 224.4 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 5.4 kg rotates at radius 0.43 m at 1000 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 17400 N/m and mass 14.3 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 17400, m = 14.3 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(17400/14.3) | Answer: 5.552 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 8.1 m^2 and thickness 0.29 m has conductivity k = 13.4 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 45 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 8.1, L = 0.29, k = 13.4, dT = 45 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 13.4*8.1*45 / 0.29 | Answer: 16842 W

question: A surface of area 2.6 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 90 W/m^2-K to surroundings 145 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 2.6, h = 90, dT = 145 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 90*2.6*145 | Answer: 33930 W

question: In a counter-flow heat exchanger the terminal temperature differences are 105 deg C and 5 deg C. Find the log mean temperature difference (LMTD) in deg C.
solution: Given: dT1 = 105, dT2 = 5 | Formula: LMTD = (dT1 - dT2) / ln(dT1/dT2) | Substitute: LMTD = (105 - 5) / ln(105/5) | Answer: 32.85 deg C

question: In turning, cutting speed = 220 m/min, feed = 0.31 mm/rev, depth of cut = 1.3 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 220, f = 0.31, d = 1.3 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*220*0.31*1.3 | Answer: 88660 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 260 mm is turned at 450 rpm with a feed of 0.2 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 260, N = 450, f = 0.2 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 260 / (0.2*450) | Answer: 2.889 min

question: A resistor of 153 ohm carries a current of 9.7 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 153, I = 9.7 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 9.7 * 153 | Answer: 1484 V

question: Three resistors 31 ohm, 21 ohm and 47 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 31, R2 = 21, R3 = 47 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 31 + 21 + 47 | Answer: 99 ohm

question: Two resistors 98 ohm and 17 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 98, R2 = 17 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 98*17 / (98+17) | Answer: 14.49 ohm

question: A device draws 2.9 A at 120 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 120, I = 2.9 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 120 * 2.9 | Answer: 348 W

question: A current of 5 A flows through a 38 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 5, R = 38 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (5)^2 * 38 | Answer: 950 W

question: Two capacitors 46.7 uF and 39.6 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 46.7, C2 = 39.6 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 46.7*39.6 / (46.7+39.6) | Answer: 21.43 uF

question: A resistor 57 kohm and capacitor 18.2 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 57, C = 18.2 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (57k)(18.2u) = 1037 ms | Answer: 1037 ms

question: An inductor 304.2 mH is in series with 186 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 304.2, R = 186 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (304.2e-3) / 186 | Answer: 1.635 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 19.7 mH inductor at 920 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 19.7, f = 920 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (920)(19.7e-3) | Answer: 113.9 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 2.3 uF capacitor at 910 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 2.3, f = 910 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (910)(2.3e-6)) | Answer: 76.04 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 94 ohm, XL = 134 ohm and XC = 31 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 94, XL = 134, XC = 31 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(94^2 + (134 - 31)^2) | Answer: 139.4 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 16.8 mH and C = 3.1 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 16.8, C = 3.1 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(16.8e-3 * 3.1e-6)) | Answer: 697.4 Hz

question: A capacitor of 20 uF is charged to 350 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 20, V = 350 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*20e-6*(350)^2 | Answer: 1225 mJ

question: An alternating voltage has a peak value of 162 V. Find its RMS value.
solution: Given: Vp = 162 | Formula: Vrms = Vp / sqrt(2) | Substitute: Vrms = 162 / sqrt(2) | Answer: 114.6 V

question: A transformer has primary voltage 250 V with 580 primary turns and 100 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 250, N1 = 580, N2 = 100 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 250 * 100/580 | Answer: 43.1 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 390 V and draws an armature current of 60 A. If the armature resistance is 1.47 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 390, Ia = 60, Ra = 1.47 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 390 - 60*1.47 | Answer: 301.8 V

question: Find the synchronous speed of a 2-pole machine on a 60 Hz supply, in rpm.
solution: Given: P = 2, f = 60 | Formula: Ns = 120 f / P | Substitute: Ns = 120*60 / 2 | Answer: 3600 rpm

question: A 4-pole induction motor on a 50 Hz supply runs at 810 rpm. Find the slip (%).
formula: s = (Ns - N) / Ns,  Ns = 120 f / P

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 185 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.97. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 185, VL = 400, pf = 0.97 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*400*185*0.97 / 1000 | Answer: 124.3 kW

question: A load has real power 25 kW and apparent power 45 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 25, S = 45 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 25 / 45 | Answer: 0.5556

question: A machine delivers 115 kW output while drawing 202 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 115, Pi = 202 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 115/202 * 100 | Answer: 56.93 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 15 V across R1 = 6 ohm and R2 = 2 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 15, R1 = 6, R2 = 2 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 15*2 / (6+2) | Answer: 3.75 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 30 kohm and Rin = 45 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 30, Rin = 45 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 30 / 45 | Answer: 0.6667

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 100 kohm and Rg = 25 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 100, Rg = 25 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 100/25 | Answer: 5

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 2168. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 2168 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(2168) | Answer: 33.36 dB

question: A first-order system has a time constant of 4.7 s. Find the time (in s) to reach 63.2% of its final value.
solution: For a first-order step response, y = 1 - e^(-t/tau) | y = 0.632 when t = tau | Answer: 4.7 s
formula: At t = tau the response reaches 63.2% (one time constant)

question: A signal is sampled at 126 kHz. According to the Nyquist criterion, what is the maximum signal frequency that can be represented (in kHz)?
solution: Given: fs = 126 | Formula: f_max = fs / 2 | Substitute: f_max = 126 / 2 | Answer: 63 kHz

question: A simply supported beam of span 6 m carries a central point load of 50 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6, W = 50 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 50*6 / 4 | Answer: 75 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.3 m carries a UDL of 15 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6.3, w = 15 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 15*(6.3)^2 / 8 | Answer: 74.42 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 5.7 m carries a point load 15 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.7, W = 15 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 15*5.7 | Answer: 85.5 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 4.4 m carries a UDL of 38 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.4, w = 38 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 38*(4.4)^2 / 2 | Answer: 367.8 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.3 m carries a point load 70 kN at distance 2 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 6.3, a = 2, W = 70 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 70*(6.3 - 2) / 6.3 | Answer: 47.78 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 7.4 m) carries a central point load 10 kN. With E = 200 GPa and I = 210e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=10000 N, L=7400.0 mm, E=200000 MPa, I=210e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 2.01 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 7.1 m carries a UDL of 18 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7.1, w = 18 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 18*(7.1)^2 / 12 | Answer: 75.61 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 300 mm, clear cover 30 mm and main bars of diameter 25 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 300, c = 30, dia = 25 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 300 - 30 - 25/2 | Answer: 257.5 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 33.2 m^2 carrying a factored load of 17.6 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 33.2, w = 17.6 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 17.6 * 33.2 | Answer: 584.3 kN

question: For a bar of diameter 16 mm with design bond stress 1.3 MPa and steel stress 360 MPa, find the development length in mm.
solution: Given: dia = 16, tbd = 1.3, fs = 360 | Formula: Ld = phi fs / (4 tau_bd) | Substitute: Ld = 16*360 / (4*1.3) | Answer: 1108 mm

question: A soil sample has porosity n = 0.54. Find its void ratio e.
solution: Given: n = 0.54 | Formula: e = n / (1 - n) | Substitute: e = 0.54 / (1 - 0.54) | Answer: 1.174

question: A cohesionless soil has an angle of internal friction phi = 32 degrees. Find Rankine's coefficient of active earth pressure Ka.
solution: Given: phi = 32 | Formula: Ka = (1 - sin phi) / (1 + sin phi) | Substitute: Ka = (1 - sin32) / (1 + sin32) | Answer: 0.3073

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 5 m, unit weight 19 kN/m^3, phi = 31 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 4.3 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 20 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 4.3, g = 20 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (20 - 9.81)*4.3 | Answer: 43.82 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 8.8e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.7, area = 5.4e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 8.8, i = 0.7, A = 5.4 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (8.8e-4)*0.7*(5.4e-3) | Answer: 3326 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.1 m, bed slope 0.009 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.019. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 4.5 m under a head of 1.1 m. Taking Cd = 0.61 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 5.1 m wide carries a discharge of 18.4 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 170 m and design speed 80 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 170, V = 80 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (80)^2 / (127*170) | Answer: 0.2964
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: For a design speed of 100 km/h with allowable superelevation 0.08 and lateral friction 0.13, find the minimum curve radius in m.
A tank of volume 1000 m^3 treats a flow of 135 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 1000, Q = 135 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 1000 / 135 | Answer: 7.407 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 370 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.12 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 8 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 370, k = 0.12, t = 8 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 370*(1 - e^(-0.12*8)) | Answer: 228.3 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.38, rainfall intensity 85 mm/h over a catchment of 12.8 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.38, i = 85, A = 12.8 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.38*85*12.8 / 360 | Answer: 1.148 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.07 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 430 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.07, M = 430 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 430*(20+0.07)/20 | Answer: 431.5 m

question: Convert the decimal number 245 to binary.
solution: Divide 245 by 2 repeatedly, recording remainders | Reading remainders in reverse gives 11110101 | Answer: 11110101 (binary)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 2 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the decimal number 876 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 876 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 36C (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the 8-bit binary number 01101101 to decimal.
solution: Binary 01101101 = sum of bit-weights | Answer: 109 (decimal)
formula: Sum each bit times its positional weight (2^i)

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 10010010 and 10110001.
solution: XOR: 00100011 | Count of 1s = 3 | Answer: 3
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: An IPv4 subnet uses a /29 prefix. How many usable host addresses does it provide?
solution: Given: prefix = 29 | Formula: hosts = 2^(32 - prefix) - 2 | Substitute: hosts = 2^(32 - 29) - 2 | Answer: 6

question: A file of 220 megabits is sent over a link of 93 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 220, B = 93 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 220 / 93 | Answer: 2.366 s

question: A link has bandwidth 28 Mbps and round-trip time 100 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 28, R = 100 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 28e6 * 100e-3 bits = 2800 kb | Answer: 2800 kilobits

question: A channel has bandwidth 20 kHz. Using Nyquist's theorem with 16 signal levels, find the maximum data rate in kbps (noiseless).
solution: Given: B = 20, M = 16 | Formula: C = 2 B log2(M) | Substitute: C = 2*20*log2(16) | Answer: 160 kbps

question: A channel of bandwidth 7 kHz has a signal-to-noise ratio of 31 (linear). Using Shannon's theorem, find the channel capacity in kbps.
solution: Given: B = 7, SNR = 31 | Formula: C = B log2(1 + SNR) | Substitute: C = 7*log2(1 + 31) | Answer: 35 kbps

question: A memory has 8192 addressable locations. How many address bits are required?
solution: Given: N = 8192 | Formula: bits = log2(N) | Substitute: bits = log2(8192) | Answer: 13 bits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.83, cache access time 9 ns and main-memory access time 60 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.83, tc = 9, tm = 60 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.83*9 + (1 - 0.83)*60 | Answer: 17.67 ns

question: A disk rotates at 15000 rpm. Find the average rotational latency in milliseconds.
solution: Given: rpm = 15000 | Formula: avg latency = 0.5 * (60 / rpm) * 1000 ms | Substitute: latency = 0.5 * 60000 / 15000 | Answer: 2 ms

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 46858 elements?
solution: Given: n = 46858 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(46858)) + 1 | Answer: 16

question: An O(n^2) algorithm performs c*n^2 basic operations. If c = 1 and n = 120, how many operations are performed?
solution: Given: n = 120 | Formula: operations = n^2 | Substitute: = (120)^2 | Answer: 14400

question: A program is 90% parallelisable and run on 2 processors. Using Amdahl's law, find the maximum speedup.
solution: Parallel fraction f = 0.9 | S = 1 / ((1 - 0.9) + 0.9/2) | Answer: 1.818x speedup

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.004, memory access time 120 ns and page-fault service time 9 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 9 ms = 9000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.004)*120 + 0.004*9000000.0 ns | Answer: 36.12 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: How many distinct Boolean input combinations exist for a logic function of 6 variables?
solution: Given: n = 6 | Formula: combinations = 2^n | Substitute: = 2^6 | Answer: 64

question: A digital-to-analog converter has 8 bits and a full-scale output of 10 V. Find its resolution (voltage per step) in mV.
solution: Given: n = 8, Vfs = 10 | Formula: resolution = Vfs / (2^n - 1) | Substitute: resolution = 10 / (2^8 - 1) | Answer: 39.22 mV

question: A modem transmits at 900 baud using 16-level signalling. Find the bit rate in bps.
solution: Given: baud = 900, M = 16 | Formula: bit rate = baud * log2(M) | Substitute: bit rate = 900 * log2(16) | Answer: 3600 bps

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 1.2 m^3 at 230 kPa and 370 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 1.2, P = 230, Tk = 370 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (230e3)*1.2 / (8.314*370) | Answer: 89.72 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.11 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 3 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.11, t = 3 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.11*3) | Answer: 0.2811

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.31 /min) is to reach 60% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.31, X = 60 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.6) / 0.31 | Answer: 2.956 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.23 /min) reaches 80% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.23, X = 80 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.8 / (0.23*(1 - 0.8)) | Answer: 17.39 min

question: A first-order reaction has a rate constant of 0.28 /min. Find its half-life in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.28 | Formula: t_half = ln(2) / k | Substitute: t_half = 0.6931 / 0.28 | Answer: 2.476 min

question: For a reaction with A = 1e10 /s and activation energy 65 kJ/mol at 320 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 1, Ea = 65, Tk = 320 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 1e10 * exp(-65e3 / (8.314*320)) | Answer: 0.2452 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.98 and bottoms xW = 0.07, with relative volatility alpha = 2.7. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.98, xw = 0.07, al = 2.7 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.98/0.02)(0.93/0.07)] / ln(2.7) | Answer: 6.523 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.76 and x = 0.33. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.76, x = 0.33 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.76/0.24) / (0.33/0.67) | Answer: 6.429

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.11 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 45 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.11, Psat = 45 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.11 * 45 | Answer: 4.95 kPa

question: A stream of 9.2 kg/s with specific heat 1.2 kJ/kg-K is heated through 100 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 9.2, cp = 1.2, dT = 100 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 9.2*1.2*100 | Answer: 1104 kW

question: A reactor of volume 12.3 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 1.1 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 12.3, Q = 1.1 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 12.3 / 1.1 | Answer: 11.18 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 6.5e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 4 mm with a concentration difference of 40 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 6.5, L = 4, dC = 40 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (6.5e-9)*40 / (4e-3) | Answer: 65 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 6.9 min and steady-state gain 1.4. For a step input of magnitude 5, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 6.9, K = 1.4, M = 5 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 1.4 * 5 | Answer: 7 units

question: A reactor operates at a space time of 6.8 min. Find its space velocity in per hour.
solution: Given: tau = 6.8 | Formula: SV = 60 / tau  (per hour) | Substitute: SV = 60 / 6.8 | Answer: 8.824 /h

question: An aircraft wing of area 20 m^2 flies at 120 m/s (air density 1.225 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.4. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 20, V = 120, rho = 1.225, CL = 0.4 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1.225*(120)^2*20*0.4 / 1000 | Answer: 70.56 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 95 m^2 flies at 180 m/s (density 0.4 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.11. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 95, V = 180, rho = 0.4, CD = 0.11 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.4*(180)^2*95*0.11 / 1000 | Answer: 67.72 kN

question: Find the dynamic pressure for air of density 0.7 kg/m^3 moving at 290 m/s, in Pa.
solution: Given: rho = 0.7, V = 290 | Formula: q = 0.5 rho V^2 | Substitute: q = 0.5*0.7*(290)^2 | Answer: 29435 Pa

question: An aircraft flies at 250 m/s where the speed of sound is 295 m/s. Find the Mach number.
solution: Given: V = 250, a = 295 | Formula: M = V / a | Substitute: M = 250 / 295 | Answer: 0.8475

question: Find the circular orbital velocity of a satellite at altitude 2000 km above Earth (Earth radius 6371 km, mu = 3.986e14 m^3/s^2), in km/s.
A specimen under stress 110 MPa shows an elastic strain of 2.8e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 110, eps = 2.8 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 110 / (2.8e-3) MPa = 39.29 GPa | Answer: 39.29 GPa

question: A block of mass 37 kg has a volume of 3.2e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 37, V = 3.2 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 37 / (3.2e-3) | Answer: 11562 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 500 mm is heated through 90 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 17e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 500, dT = 90, al = 17 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 500*17e-6*90 | Answer: 0.765 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 110 ohm, R2 = 190 ohm and R3 = 125 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 110, R2 = 190, R3 = 125 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 190*125 / 110 | Answer: 215.9 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 1000 ohm and gauge factor 2.1 experiences a strain of 1650e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 1000, GF = 2.1, eps = 1650 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 1000*2.1*1650e-6 | Answer: 3465 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 10.74 when the true value is 50. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10.74, true = 50 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10.74 - 50| / 50 * 100 | Answer: 78.52 %

question: Annual demand is 26500 units, ordering cost 30 per order and holding cost 30 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 26500, S = 30, H = 30 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*26500*30 / 30) | Answer: 230.2 units

question: An asset costs 110000 with salvage value 34000 after 13 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 110000, Sv = 34000, n = 13 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (110000 - 34000) / 13 | Answer: 5846 per year

question: A product sells for 190 per unit with variable cost 120 per unit and fixed costs 35000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 190, V = 120, F = 35000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 35000 / (190 - 120) | Answer: 500 units

question: Find the present worth of 55000 received 8 years from now at an interest rate of 7% per year.
solution: Given: F = 55000, n = 8, i = 7 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 55000 / (1 + 0.07)^8 | Answer: 32011 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.91, 0.99 and 0.99 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.91, r2 = 0.99, r3 = 0.99 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.91*0.99*0.99 | Answer: 0.8919

question: Two components each of reliability 0.91 are connected in parallel. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r = 0.91 | Formula: R_parallel = 1 - (1 - r)^2 | Substitute: R = 1 - (1 - 0.91)^2 | Answer: 0.9919

question: A process produces 30 defective items in a batch of 16000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 30, N = 16000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 30/16000 * 1e6 | Answer: 1875 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -2x^3 + 3x^2 - 5x - 7 evaluated at x = -2.
For f(x) = -4x^3 + 2x - 8, find f''(x) at x = -3.

solution: Given: a = 8, b = -9, c = -9, d = -6 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (8)(-6) - (-9)(-9) | Answer: -129

solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: 136

solution: Trace tr = 4, Determinant = -12 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 6

question: Solve for x: -1x + -5y = -11 and -6x + -2y = -6.
solution: Determinant = -1*-2 - -5*-6 = -28 | x = (e d - b f) / det = 0.2857 | Answer: x = 0.2857
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 25, 86, 88, 40, 88.
solution: Sum = 327 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 65.4 | Answer: 65.4

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 16, 41, 29, 1, 35.
solution: Mean = 24.4 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 16.02

question: Find the slope of the line through (4, -5) and (8, -4).
solution: Given: x1 = 4, y1 = -5, x2 = 8, y2 = -4 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (-4 - -5) / (8 - 4) | Answer: 0.25

question: Find the distance between the points (2, 9) and (-9, -2).
solution: Given: x1 = 2, y1 = 9, x2 = -9, y2 = -2 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-11)^2 + (-11)^2) | Answer: 15.56 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (5,-4), (-2,-1), (-1,-7).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 19.5 sq units

question: Evaluate the number of combinations C(18, 8).
solution: Given: n = 18, r = 8 | Formula: C(n, r) = n! / (r! (n - r)!) | Substitute: C(18, 8) = 18! / (8! * 10!) | Answer: 43758

question: Evaluate the number of permutations P(11, 3).
solution: Given: n = 11, r = 3 | Formula: P(n, r) = n! / (n - r)! | Substitute: P(11, 3) = 11! / 8! | Answer: 990

question: Find the 9th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -7 and common difference -7.
solution: Given: a = -7, d = -7, n = 9 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -7 + (9 - 1)*-7 | Answer: -63

question: Find the sum of the first 23 terms of an AP with first term 11 and common difference 4.
solution: Given: a = 11, d = 4, n = 23 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 23/2 [2*11 + (23-1)*4] | Answer: 1265

question: Find the 4th term of a geometric progression with first term 6 and common ratio 2.
solution: Given: a = 6, r = 2, n = 4 | Formula: a_n = a r^(n-1) | Substitute: a_n = 6 * 2^(4-1) | Answer: 48

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 38000 at 6.4% per annum for 8 years.
solution: Given: P = 38000, R = 6.4, Tt = 8 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 38000 * 6.4 * 8 / 100 | Answer: 19456 currency units

question: Find the amount when 30000 is invested at 6.5% per annum compounded annually for 4 years.
solution: Given: P = 30000, R = 6.5, Tt = 4 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 30000 * (1 + 6.5/100)^4 | Answer: 38594 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (7, -7, 2) and (0, -3, 0).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (-3, 6, -1) and (1, -3, 1).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 4.69

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (-5, -4, -1) and (-4, -3, 4).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 47.57 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number -6 + 1i.
solution: Given: a = -6, b = 1 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((-6)^2 + (1)^2) | Answer: 6.083

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number -11 + -3i.
solution: Given: a = -11, b = -3 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(-3, -11) | Answer: -164.7 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -5x^3 + 5x^2 - 5x + 2 at x = -3.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-113 with initial guess x0=6, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.2 and ordinates 9, 13, 16, 13, 6, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 479 and 547.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 479 and 547 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 36 and 66.
solution: Given: a = 36, b = 66 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 36*66 / 6 | Answer: 396
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 54 mm carries an axial tensile load of 96 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 12 mm and length 2300 mm carries an axial load of 15 kN. Take E = 200 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 25 mm transmits a torque of 2850 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 25, Tt = 2850 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(2850*1000) / (pi*(25)^3) | Answer: 929 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 48 mm and length 1000 mm carries a torque of 450 N-m. With G = 77 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (48)^4 / 32 = 521153 mm^4 | theta = (450*1000)(1000) / (77000 * 521153) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 0.6425 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 45 mm wide and 180 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 45, h = 180 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 45*(180)^2 / 6 | Answer: 243000 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (116 mm x 120 mm) carries a bending moment of 2 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (75 mm x 100 mm) has effective length 2000 mm and E = 200 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 820 MPa is designed for a working stress of 200 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 820, sw = 200 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 820 / 200 | Answer: 4.1

question: A steel bar is fully restrained and heated through 105 deg C. With E = 200 GPa and alpha = 11e-6 /deg C, find the thermal stress in MPa.
solution: Given: dT = 105, E = 200, al = 11 | Formula: sigma = E alpha (dT) | Substitute: sigma = 200000 * 11e-6 * 105 | Answer: 231 MPa

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 700 mm and wall thickness 11 mm carries an internal pressure of 0.8 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 700, t = 11, P = 0.8 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 0.8*700 / (2*11) | Answer: 25.45 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 600 K and 280 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 600, Tc = 280 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 280/600) * 100 | Answer: 53.33 %

question: A refrigerator works between 261 K (cold) and 314 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 261, Th = 314 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 261 / (314 - 261) | Answer: 4.925

question: A heat pump operates between 282 K and 326 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 282, Th = 326 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 326 / (326 - 282) | Answer: 7.409

question: An Otto cycle has a compression ratio of 8. Taking gamma = 1.4, find the air-standard efficiency (%).
solution: Given: r = 8 | Formula: eta = 1 - 1/r^(gamma-1) | Substitute: eta = (1 - 1/8^0.4) * 100 | Answer: 56.47 %

question: 3.8 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 180 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.8, dT = 180 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 3.8 * 0.718 * 180 | Answer: 491.1 kJ

question: 6.2 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 35 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 6.2, dT = 35 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 6.2 * 1.005 * 35 | Answer: 218.1 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 2.1 m^3 at 490 K with mass 5.9 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 2.1, Tk = 490, m = 5.9 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 5.9*0.287*490 / 2.1 | Answer: 395.1 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 3.3 kg of air expands isothermally at 440 K from volume V1 to 5*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.3, Tk = 440, ratio = 5 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 3.3*0.287*440*ln(5) | Answer: 670.7 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 1.8 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.3 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 1.8, D = 0.3 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*1.8*0.3 / 0.001 | Answer: 540000

question: Water flows at 1 m/s through a pipe of diameter 240 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 10.2 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 10.2 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*10.2 / 1000 | Answer: 100.1 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 6 m. Taking Cv = 0.96, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 6, cv = 0.96 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.96*sqrt(2*9.81*6) | Answer: 10.42 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 220 mm) water flows at 0.6 m/s. It contracts to diameter 100 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
Water flows at 1.2 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.23 m and length 80 m. With friction factor f = 0.022, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 36 teeth drives a gear of 108 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1150 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 36, z2 = 108, N1 = 1150 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1150*36 / 108 | Answer: 383.3 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 470 mm rotates at 800 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 470, N = 800 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.47)*800 / 60 | Answer: 19.69 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 49.2 kW at 950 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 49.2, N = 950 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(49.2*1000) / (2*pi*950) | Answer: 494.6 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 8.8 kg rotates at radius 0.28 m at 1000 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 2100 N/m and mass 17.9 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 2100, m = 17.9 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(2100/17.9) | Answer: 1.724 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 3.4 m^2 and thickness 0.24 m has conductivity k = 24.6 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 135 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 3.4, L = 0.24, k = 24.6, dT = 135 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 24.6*3.4*135 / 0.24 | Answer: 47048 W

question: A surface of area 2 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 195 W/m^2-K to surroundings 145 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 2, h = 195, dT = 145 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 195*2*145 | Answer: 56550 W

question: In a counter-flow heat exchanger the terminal temperature differences are 85 deg C and 25 deg C. Find the log mean temperature difference (LMTD) in deg C.
solution: Given: dT1 = 85, dT2 = 25 | Formula: LMTD = (dT1 - dT2) / ln(dT1/dT2) | Substitute: LMTD = (85 - 25) / ln(85/25) | Answer: 49.03 deg C

question: In turning, cutting speed = 90 m/min, feed = 0.38 mm/rev, depth of cut = 1.2 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 90, f = 0.38, d = 1.2 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*90*0.38*1.2 | Answer: 41040 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 360 mm is turned at 950 rpm with a feed of 0.17 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 360, N = 950, f = 0.17 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 360 / (0.17*950) | Answer: 2.229 min

question: A resistor of 136 ohm carries a current of 6 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 136, I = 6 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 6 * 136 | Answer: 816 V

question: Three resistors 35 ohm, 10 ohm and 34 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 35, R2 = 10, R3 = 34 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 35 + 10 + 34 | Answer: 79 ohm

question: Two resistors 13 ohm and 99 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 13, R2 = 99 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 13*99 / (13+99) | Answer: 11.49 ohm

question: A device draws 3 A at 100 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 100, I = 3 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 100 * 3 | Answer: 300 W

question: A current of 0.7 A flows through a 138 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 0.7, R = 138 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (0.7)^2 * 138 | Answer: 67.62 W

question: Two capacitors 46.6 uF and 38.4 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 46.6, C2 = 38.4 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 46.6*38.4 / (46.6+38.4) | Answer: 21.05 uF

question: A resistor 34 kohm and capacitor 18.4 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 34, C = 18.4 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (34k)(18.4u) = 625.6 ms | Answer: 625.6 ms

question: An inductor 373.9 mH is in series with 86 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 373.9, R = 86 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (373.9e-3) / 86 | Answer: 4.348 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 7.9 mH inductor at 650 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 7.9, f = 650 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (650)(7.9e-3) | Answer: 32.26 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 25.9 uF capacitor at 60 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 25.9, f = 60 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (60)(25.9e-6)) | Answer: 102.4 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 40 ohm, XL = 129 ohm and XC = 10 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 40, XL = 129, XC = 10 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(40^2 + (129 - 10)^2) | Answer: 125.5 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 53.6 mH and C = 9.9 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 53.6, C = 9.9 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(53.6e-3 * 9.9e-6)) | Answer: 218.5 Hz

question: A capacitor of 44.8 uF is charged to 220 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 44.8, V = 220 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*44.8e-6*(220)^2 | Answer: 1084 mJ

question: An alternating voltage has a peak value of 126 V. Find its RMS value.
solution: Given: Vp = 126 | Formula: Vrms = Vp / sqrt(2) | Substitute: Vrms = 126 / sqrt(2) | Answer: 89.1 V

question: A transformer has primary voltage 360 V with 510 primary turns and 280 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 360, N1 = 510, N2 = 280 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 360 * 280/510 | Answer: 197.6 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 280 V and draws an armature current of 42 A. If the armature resistance is 0.45 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 280, Ia = 42, Ra = 0.45 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 280 - 42*0.45 | Answer: 261.1 V

question: Find the synchronous speed of a 2-pole machine on a 50 Hz supply, in rpm.
solution: Given: P = 2, f = 50 | Formula: Ns = 120 f / P | Substitute: Ns = 120*50 / 2 | Answer: 3000 rpm

question: A 6-pole induction motor on a 60 Hz supply runs at 780 rpm. Find the slip (%).
formula: s = (Ns - N) / Ns,  Ns = 120 f / P

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 40 A at 433 V (line) with a power factor of 0.72. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 40, VL = 433, pf = 0.72 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*433*40*0.72 / 1000 | Answer: 21.6 kW

question: A load has real power 45 kW and apparent power 110 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 45, S = 110 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 45 / 110 | Answer: 0.4091

question: A machine delivers 135 kW output while drawing 217 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 135, Pi = 217 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 135/217 * 100 | Answer: 62.21 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 19 V across R1 = 31 ohm and R2 = 37 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 19, R1 = 31, R2 = 37 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 19*37 / (31+37) | Answer: 10.34 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 170 kohm and Rin = 3 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 170, Rin = 3 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 170 / 3 | Answer: 56.67

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 130 kohm and Rg = 10 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 130, Rg = 10 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 130/10 | Answer: 14

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 1677. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 1677 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(1677) | Answer: 32.25 dB

question: A first-order system has a time constant of 7.8 s. Find the time (in s) to reach 63.2% of its final value.
solution: For a first-order step response, y = 1 - e^(-t/tau) | y = 0.632 when t = tau | Answer: 7.8 s
formula: At t = tau the response reaches 63.2% (one time constant)

question: A signal is sampled at 86 kHz. According to the Nyquist criterion, what is the maximum signal frequency that can be represented (in kHz)?
solution: Given: fs = 86 | Formula: f_max = fs / 2 | Substitute: f_max = 86 / 2 | Answer: 43 kHz

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.5 m carries a central point load of 25 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.5, W = 25 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 25*4.5 / 4 | Answer: 28.12 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.5 m carries a UDL of 30 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 9.5, w = 30 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 30*(9.5)^2 / 8 | Answer: 338.4 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 5.4 m carries a point load 75 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.4, W = 75 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 75*5.4 | Answer: 405 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 4.5 m carries a UDL of 10 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.5, w = 10 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 10*(4.5)^2 / 2 | Answer: 101.2 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 7 m carries a point load 75 kN at distance 1.3 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 7, a = 1.3, W = 75 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 75*(7 - 1.3) / 7 | Answer: 61.07 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 3.6 m) carries a central point load 65 kN. With E = 200 GPa and I = 520e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=65000 N, L=3600.0 mm, E=200000 MPa, I=520e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 0.6075 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 7.8 m carries a UDL of 24 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7.8, w = 24 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 24*(7.8)^2 / 12 | Answer: 121.7 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 450 mm, clear cover 25 mm and main bars of diameter 25 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 450, c = 25, dia = 25 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 450 - 25 - 25/2 | Answer: 412.5 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 16.8 m^2 carrying a factored load of 18.3 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 16.8, w = 18.3 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 18.3 * 16.8 | Answer: 307.4 kN

question: For a bar of diameter 16 mm with design bond stress 2.1 MPa and steel stress 360 MPa, find the development length in mm.
solution: Given: dia = 16, tbd = 2.1, fs = 360 | Formula: Ld = phi fs / (4 tau_bd) | Substitute: Ld = 16*360 / (4*2.1) | Answer: 685.7 mm

question: A soil sample has porosity n = 0.38. Find its void ratio e.
solution: Given: n = 0.38 | Formula: e = n / (1 - n) | Substitute: e = 0.38 / (1 - 0.38) | Answer: 0.6129

question: A cohesionless soil has an angle of internal friction phi = 33 degrees. Find Rankine's coefficient of active earth pressure Ka.
solution: Given: phi = 33 | Formula: Ka = (1 - sin phi) / (1 + sin phi) | Substitute: Ka = (1 - sin33) / (1 + sin33) | Answer: 0.2948

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 3.3 m, unit weight 16 kN/m^3, phi = 34 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 10.5 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 20 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 10.5, g = 20 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (20 - 9.81)*10.5 | Answer: 107 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 3.4e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1, area = 3.1e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 3.4, i = 1, A = 3.1 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (3.4e-4)*1*(3.1e-3) | Answer: 1054 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 0.8 m, bed slope 0.004 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.023. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 2.1 m under a head of 0.4 m. Taking Cd = 0.62 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 5.5 m wide carries a discharge of 14.7 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 410 m and design speed 45 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 410, V = 45 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (45)^2 / (127*410) | Answer: 0.03889
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: For a design speed of 65 km/h with allowable superelevation 0.05 and lateral friction 0.13, find the minimum curve radius in m.
A tank of volume 710 m^3 treats a flow of 150 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 220 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.17 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 3 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 220, k = 0.17, t = 3 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 220*(1 - e^(-0.17*3)) | Answer: 87.89 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.64, rainfall intensity 35 mm/h over a catchment of 44.2 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.01 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 760 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.01, M = 760 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 760*(30+0.01)/30 | Answer: 760.3 m

solution: Divide 1314 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 522 (hex)

solution: Binary 00111010 = sum of bit-weights | Answer: 58 (decimal)

question: An IPv4 subnet uses a /21 prefix. How many usable host addresses does it provide?

question: A file of 920 megabits is sent over a link of 68 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 920, B = 68 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 920 / 68 | Answer: 13.53 s

question: A link has bandwidth 24 Mbps and round-trip time 170 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 24, R = 170 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 24e6 * 170e-3 bits = 4080 kb | Answer: 4080 kilobits

question: A channel has bandwidth 20 kHz. Using Nyquist's theorem with 2 signal levels, find the maximum data rate in kbps (noiseless).
solution: Given: B = 20, M = 2 | Formula: C = 2 B log2(M) | Substitute: C = 2*20*log2(2) | Answer: 40 kbps

question: A channel of bandwidth 17 kHz has a signal-to-noise ratio of 7 (linear). Using Shannon's theorem, find the channel capacity in kbps.
solution: Given: B = 17, SNR = 7 | Formula: C = B log2(1 + SNR) | Substitute: C = 17*log2(1 + 7) | Answer: 51 kbps

question: A memory has 512 addressable locations. How many address bits are required?
solution: Given: N = 512 | Formula: bits = log2(N) | Substitute: bits = log2(512) | Answer: 9 bits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.83, cache access time 8 ns and main-memory access time 160 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.83, tc = 8, tm = 160 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.83*8 + (1 - 0.83)*160 | Answer: 33.84 ns

question: A disk rotates at 10000 rpm. Find the average rotational latency in milliseconds.
solution: Given: rpm = 10000 | Formula: avg latency = 0.5 * (60 / rpm) * 1000 ms | Substitute: latency = 0.5 * 60000 / 10000 | Answer: 3 ms

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 43951 elements?
solution: Given: n = 43951 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(43951)) + 1 | Answer: 16

question: An O(n^2) algorithm performs c*n^2 basic operations. If c = 1 and n = 2540, how many operations are performed?
solution: Given: n = 2540 | Formula: operations = n^2 | Substitute: = (2540)^2 | Answer: 6451600

question: A program is 55% parallelisable and run on 32 processors. Using Amdahl's law, find the maximum speedup.
solution: Parallel fraction f = 0.55 | S = 1 / ((1 - 0.55) + 0.55/32) | Answer: 2.14x speedup

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.006, memory access time 200 ns and page-fault service time 3 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 3 ms = 3000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.006)*200 + 0.006*3000000.0 ns | Answer: 18.2 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: How many distinct Boolean input combinations exist for a logic function of 8 variables?
solution: Given: n = 8 | Formula: combinations = 2^n | Substitute: = 2^8 | Answer: 256

question: A digital-to-analog converter has 11 bits and a full-scale output of 10 V. Find its resolution (voltage per step) in mV.
solution: Given: n = 11, Vfs = 10 | Formula: resolution = Vfs / (2^n - 1) | Substitute: resolution = 10 / (2^11 - 1) | Answer: 4.885 mV

question: A modem transmits at 3900 baud using 4-level signalling. Find the bit rate in bps.
solution: Given: baud = 3900, M = 4 | Formula: bit rate = baud * log2(M) | Substitute: bit rate = 3900 * log2(4) | Answer: 7800 bps

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 1.5 m^3 at 460 kPa and 460 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 1.5, P = 460, Tk = 460 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (460e3)*1.5 / (8.314*460) | Answer: 180.4 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.35 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 20 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.35, t = 20 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.35*20) | Answer: 0.9991

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.43 /min) is to reach 90% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.43, X = 90 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.9) / 0.43 | Answer: 5.355 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.42 /min) reaches 70% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.42, X = 70 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.7 / (0.42*(1 - 0.7)) | Answer: 5.556 min

question: A first-order reaction has a rate constant of 0.19 /min. Find its half-life in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.19 | Formula: t_half = ln(2) / k | Substitute: t_half = 0.6931 / 0.19 | Answer: 3.648 min

question: For a reaction with A = 4e10 /s and activation energy 75 kJ/mol at 300 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 4, Ea = 75, Tk = 300 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 4e10 * exp(-75e3 / (8.314*300)) | Answer: 0.003491 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.99 and bottoms xW = 0.1, with relative volatility alpha = 2.6. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.99, xw = 0.1, al = 2.6 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.99/0.01)(0.9/0.1)] / ln(2.6) | Answer: 7.109 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.65 and x = 0.31. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.34 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 70 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.34, Psat = 70 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.34 * 70 | Answer: 23.8 kPa

question: A stream of 8.7 kg/s with specific heat 3.5 kJ/kg-K is heated through 90 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 8.7, cp = 3.5, dT = 90 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 8.7*3.5*90 | Answer: 274 kW

question: A reactor of volume 16.2 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 1.5 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 16.2, Q = 1.5 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 16.2 / 1.5 | Answer: 10.8 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 7.3e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 4 mm with a concentration difference of 110 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 7.3, L = 4, dC = 110 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (7.3e-9)*110 / (4e-3) | Answer: 200.8 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 9.5 min and steady-state gain 2.6. For a step input of magnitude 2, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 9.5, K = 2.6, M = 2 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 2.6 * 2 | Answer: 5.2 units

question: A reactor operates at a space time of 12.3 min. Find its space velocity in per hour.
solution: Given: tau = 12.3 | Formula: SV = 60 / tau  (per hour) | Substitute: SV = 60 / 12.3 | Answer: 4.878 /h

question: An aircraft wing of area 100 m^2 flies at 200 m/s (air density 0.7 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.8. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 100, V = 200, rho = 0.7, CL = 0.8 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.7*(200)^2*100*0.8 / 1000 | Answer: 1120 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 55 m^2 flies at 120 m/s (density 1 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.09. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 55, V = 120, rho = 1, CD = 0.09 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*1*(120)^2*55*0.09 / 1000 | Answer: 35.64 kN

question: Find the dynamic pressure for air of density 1 kg/m^3 moving at 200 m/s, in Pa.
solution: Given: rho = 1, V = 200 | Formula: q = 0.5 rho V^2 | Substitute: q = 0.5*1*(200)^2 | Answer: 20000 Pa

question: An aircraft flies at 210 m/s where the speed of sound is 295 m/s. Find the Mach number.
solution: Given: V = 210, a = 295 | Formula: M = V / a | Substitute: M = 210 / 295 | Answer: 0.7119

question: Find the circular orbital velocity of a satellite at altitude 1450 km above Earth (Earth radius 6371 km, mu = 3.986e14 m^3/s^2), in km/s.
A specimen under stress 350 MPa shows an elastic strain of 2.4e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.

question: A block of mass 17 kg has a volume of 1.4e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 17, V = 1.4 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 17 / (1.4e-3) | Answer: 12143 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 2500 mm is heated through 90 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 12e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 2500, dT = 90, al = 12 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 2500*12e-6*90 | Answer: 2.7 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 140 ohm, R2 = 105 ohm and R3 = 335 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 140, R2 = 105, R3 = 335 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 105*335 / 140 | Answer: 251.2 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 120 ohm and gauge factor 2.1 experiences a strain of 850e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 120, GF = 2.1, eps = 850 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 120*2.1*850e-6 | Answer: 214.2 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 10.52 when the true value is 10. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10.52, true = 10 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10.52 - 10| / 10 * 100 | Answer: 5.2 %

question: Annual demand is 29500 units, ordering cost 300 per order and holding cost 22 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 29500, S = 300, H = 22 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*29500*300 / 22) | Answer: 897 units

question: An asset costs 490000 with salvage value 22000 after 17 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.

question: A product sells for 300 per unit with variable cost 50 per unit and fixed costs 110000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 300, V = 50, F = 110000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 110000 / (300 - 50) | Answer: 440 units

question: Find the present worth of 35000 received 5 years from now at an interest rate of 9% per year.
solution: Given: F = 35000, n = 5, i = 9 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 35000 / (1 + 0.09)^5 | Answer: 22748 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.94, 0.98 and 0.91 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.94, r2 = 0.98, r3 = 0.91 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.94*0.98*0.91 | Answer: 0.8383

question: Two components each of reliability 0.75 are connected in parallel. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r = 0.75 | Formula: R_parallel = 1 - (1 - r)^2 | Substitute: R = 1 - (1 - 0.75)^2 | Answer: 0.9375

question: A process produces 17 defective items in a batch of 1000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 17, N = 1000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 17/1000 * 1e6 | Answer: 17000 PPM

question: Find the slope of the line through (-6, 0) and (3, 4).
solution: Given: x1 = -6, y1 = 0, x2 = 3, y2 = 4 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (4 - 0) / (3 - -6) | Answer: 0.4444

question: Find the distance between the points (-9, -6) and (-9, -8).
solution: Given: x1 = -9, y1 = -6, x2 = -9, y2 = -8 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((0)^2 + (-2)^2) | Answer: 2 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (6,1), (1,0), (-3,-1).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 0.5 sq units

question: Evaluate the number of combinations C(19, 9).
solution: Given: n = 19, r = 9 | Formula: C(n, r) = n! / (r! (n - r)!) | Substitute: C(19, 9) = 19! / (9! * 10!) | Answer: 92378

question: Evaluate the number of permutations P(8, 1).
solution: Given: n = 8, r = 1 | Formula: P(n, r) = n! / (n - r)! | Substitute: P(8, 1) = 8! / 7! | Answer: 8

question: Find the 17th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 1 and common difference 0.
solution: Given: a = 1, d = 0, n = 17 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = 1 + (17 - 1)*0 | Answer: 1

question: Find the sum of the first 34 terms of an AP with first term 3 and common difference -6.
solution: Given: a = 3, d = -6, n = 34 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 34/2 [2*3 + (34-1)*-6] | Answer: -3264

question: Find the 7th term of a geometric progression with first term 2 and common ratio 4.
solution: Given: a = 2, r = 4, n = 7 | Formula: a_n = a r^(n-1) | Substitute: a_n = 2 * 4^(7-1) | Answer: 8192

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 22000 at 13.7% per annum for 7 years.
solution: Given: P = 22000, R = 13.7, Tt = 7 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 22000 * 13.7 * 7 / 100 | Answer: 21098 currency units

question: Find the amount when 4000 is invested at 7.1% per annum compounded annually for 5 years.
solution: Given: P = 4000, R = 7.1, Tt = 5 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 4000 * (1 + 7.1/100)^5 | Answer: 5636 currency units

question: Find the modulus of the complex number 2 + -7i.
solution: Given: a = 2, b = -7 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((2)^2 + (-7)^2) | Answer: 7.28

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number -3 + -7i.
solution: Given: a = -3, b = -7 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(-7, -3) | Answer: -113.2 degrees

question: A circular rod of diameter 56 mm carries an axial tensile load of 30 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 12 mm and length 2200 mm carries an axial load of 61 kN. Take E = 200 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 76 mm transmits a torque of 300 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 76, Tt = 300 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(300*1000) / (pi*(76)^3) | Answer: 3.481 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 29 mm and length 1900 mm carries a torque of 1100 N-m. With G = 77 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.

question: A rectangular beam section is 43 mm wide and 110 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.

question: A component of ultimate strength 330 MPa is designed for a working stress of 110 MPa. Find the factor of safety.

question: A steel bar is fully restrained and heated through 70 deg C. With E = 200 GPa and alpha = 11e-6 /deg C, find the thermal stress in MPa.
solution: Given: dT = 70, E = 200, al = 11 | Formula: sigma = E alpha (dT) | Substitute: sigma = 200000 * 11e-6 * 70 | Answer: 154 MPa

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1250 mm and wall thickness 7 mm carries an internal pressure of 0.6 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1250, t = 7, P = 0.6 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 0.6*1250 / (2*7) | Answer: 53.57 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 740 K and 300 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 740, Tc = 300 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 300/740) * 100 | Answer: 59.46 %

question: A refrigerator works between 259 K (cold) and 314 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 259, Th = 314 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 259 / (314 - 259) | Answer: 4.709

question: A heat pump operates between 260 K and 312 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 260, Th = 312 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 312 / (312 - 260) | Answer: 6

question: An Otto cycle has a compression ratio of 6. Taking gamma = 1.4, find the air-standard efficiency (%).
solution: Given: r = 6 | Formula: eta = 1 - 1/r^(gamma-1) | Substitute: eta = (1 - 1/6^0.4) * 100 | Answer: 51.16 %

question: 2.5 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 75 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.5, dT = 75 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 2.5 * 0.718 * 75 | Answer: 134.6 kJ

question: 5 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 160 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 5, dT = 160 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 5 * 1.005 * 160 | Answer: 804 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 4 m^3 at 490 K with mass 5.6 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 4, Tk = 490, m = 5.6 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 5.6*0.287*490 / 4 | Answer: 196.9 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 3.3 kg of air expands isothermally at 320 K from volume V1 to 5*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.3, Tk = 320, ratio = 5 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 3.3*0.287*320*ln(5) | Answer: 487.8 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 2.6 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.27 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 2.6, D = 0.27 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*2.6*0.27 / 0.001 | Answer: 702000

question: Water flows at 1.5 m/s through a pipe of diameter 280 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 1.9 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 1.9 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*1.9 / 1000 | Answer: 18.64 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 3.9 m. Taking Cv = 0.98, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 3.9, cv = 0.98 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.98*sqrt(2*9.81*3.9) | Answer: 8.573 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 380 mm) water flows at 2 m/s. It contracts to diameter 80 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 380, d2 = 80, V1 = 2 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 2*(380/80)^2 | Answer: 45.12 m/s

question: Water flows at 3.5 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.44 m and length 340 m. With friction factor f = 0.039, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 30 teeth drives a gear of 68 teeth. If the pinion runs at 550 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 30, z2 = 68, N1 = 550 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 550*30 / 68 | Answer: 242.6 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 220 mm rotates at 650 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 220, N = 650 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.22)*650 / 60 | Answer: 7.487 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 14.2 kW at 750 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 14.2, N = 750 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(14.2*1000) / (2*pi*750) | Answer: 180.8 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 8.2 kg rotates at radius 0.12 m at 700 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 11700 N/m and mass 13.2 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 11700, m = 13.2 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(11700/13.2) | Answer: 4.738 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 8.3 m^2 and thickness 0.11 m has conductivity k = 12.9 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 40 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 8.3, L = 0.11, k = 12.9, dT = 40 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 12.9*8.3*40 / 0.11 | Answer: 38935 W

question: A surface of area 5.8 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 100 W/m^2-K to surroundings 130 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 5.8, h = 100, dT = 130 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 100*5.8*130 | Answer: 75400 W

question: In a counter-flow heat exchanger the terminal temperature differences are 90 deg C and 10 deg C. Find the log mean temperature difference (LMTD) in deg C.
solution: Given: dT1 = 90, dT2 = 10 | Formula: LMTD = (dT1 - dT2) / ln(dT1/dT2) | Substitute: LMTD = (90 - 10) / ln(90/10) | Answer: 36.41 deg C

question: In turning, cutting speed = 70 m/min, feed = 0.29 mm/rev, depth of cut = 1.8 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 70, f = 0.29, d = 1.8 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*70*0.29*1.8 | Answer: 36540 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 330 mm is turned at 1000 rpm with a feed of 0.39 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 330, N = 1000, f = 0.39 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 330 / (0.39*1000) | Answer: 0.8462 min

question: A resistor of 99 ohm carries a current of 4.9 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 99, I = 4.9 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 4.9 * 99 | Answer: 485.1 V

question: Three resistors 16 ohm, 72 ohm and 34 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 16, R2 = 72, R3 = 34 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 16 + 72 + 34 | Answer: 122 ohm

question: Two resistors 48 ohm and 108 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 48, R2 = 108 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 48*108 / (48+108) | Answer: 33.23 ohm

question: A device draws 0.6 A at 70 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 70, I = 0.6 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 70 * 0.6 | Answer: 42 W

question: A current of 9.2 A flows through a 134 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 9.2, R = 134 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (9.2)^2 * 134 | Answer: 11342 W

question: Two capacitors 36.1 uF and 2.8 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 36.1, C2 = 2.8 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 36.1*2.8 / (36.1+2.8) | Answer: 2.598 uF

question: A resistor 65 kohm and capacitor 9.8 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 65, C = 9.8 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (65k)(9.8u) = 637 ms | Answer: 637 ms

question: An inductor 431 mH is in series with 110 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 431, R = 110 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (431e-3) / 110 | Answer: 3.918 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 22.3 mH inductor at 830 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 22.3, f = 830 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (830)(22.3e-3) | Answer: 116.3 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 11.2 uF capacitor at 990 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 11.2, f = 990 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (990)(11.2e-6)) | Answer: 14.35 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 34 ohm, XL = 110 ohm and XC = 44 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 34, XL = 110, XC = 44 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(34^2 + (110 - 44)^2) | Answer: 74.24 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 18.9 mH and C = 1.9 uF (in Hz).
