solution: Given: L = 18.9, C = 1.9 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(18.9e-3 * 1.9e-6)) | Answer: 839.9 Hz

question: A capacitor of 9 uF is charged to 40 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 9, V = 40 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*9e-6*(40)^2 | Answer: 7.2 mJ

question: An alternating voltage has a peak value of 248 V. Find its RMS value.
solution: Given: Vp = 248 | Formula: Vrms = Vp / sqrt(2) | Substitute: Vrms = 248 / sqrt(2) | Answer: 175.4 V

question: A transformer has primary voltage 180 V with 280 primary turns and 190 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 180, N1 = 280, N2 = 190 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 180 * 190/280 | Answer: 122.1 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 130 V and draws an armature current of 8 A. If the armature resistance is 1.2 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 130, Ia = 8, Ra = 1.2 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 130 - 8*1.2 | Answer: 120.4 V

question: Find the synchronous speed of a 4-pole machine on a 50 Hz supply, in rpm.
solution: Given: P = 4, f = 50 | Formula: Ns = 120 f / P | Substitute: Ns = 120*50 / 4 | Answer: 1500 rpm

question: A 8-pole induction motor on a 60 Hz supply runs at 810 rpm. Find the slip (%).
formula: s = (Ns - N) / Ns,  Ns = 120 f / P

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 155 A at 415 V (line) with a power factor of 0.85. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 155, VL = 415, pf = 0.85 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*415*155*0.85 / 1000 | Answer: 94.7 kW

question: A load has real power 110 kW and apparent power 220 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 110, S = 220 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 110 / 220 | Answer: 0.5

question: A machine delivers 65 kW output while drawing 92 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 65, Pi = 92 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 65/92 * 100 | Answer: 70.65 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 17 V across R1 = 12 ohm and R2 = 6 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 17, R1 = 12, R2 = 6 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 17*6 / (12+6) | Answer: 5.667 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 200 kohm and Rin = 37 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 200, Rin = 37 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 200 / 37 | Answer: 5.405

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 150 kohm and Rg = 28 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 150, Rg = 28 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 150/28 | Answer: 6.357

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 3657. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 3657 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(3657) | Answer: 35.63 dB

question: A first-order system has a time constant of 5.2 s. Find the time (in s) to reach 63.2% of its final value.
solution: For a first-order step response, y = 1 - e^(-t/tau) | y = 0.632 when t = tau | Answer: 5.2 s
formula: At t = tau the response reaches 63.2% (one time constant)

question: A signal is sampled at 124 kHz. According to the Nyquist criterion, what is the maximum signal frequency that can be represented (in kHz)?
solution: Given: fs = 124 | Formula: f_max = fs / 2 | Substitute: f_max = 124 / 2 | Answer: 62 kHz

question: A simply supported beam of span 5.9 m carries a central point load of 60 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.9, W = 60 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 60*5.9 / 4 | Answer: 88.5 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 7.9 m carries a UDL of 45 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7.9, w = 45 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 45*(7.9)^2 / 8 | Answer: 351.1 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 5.4 m carries a point load 5 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.4, W = 5 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 5*5.4 | Answer: 27 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 5.9 m carries a UDL of 36 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.9, w = 36 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 36*(5.9)^2 / 2 | Answer: 626.6 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 8.6 m carries a point load 15 kN at distance 3.5 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 8.6, a = 3.5, W = 15 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 15*(8.6 - 3.5) / 8.6 | Answer: 8.895 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 3.7 m) carries a central point load 35 kN. With E = 200 GPa and I = 360e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=35000 N, L=3700.0 mm, E=200000 MPa, I=360e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 0.513 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 7.1 m carries a UDL of 39 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7.1, w = 39 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 39*(7.1)^2 / 12 | Answer: 163.8 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 330 mm, clear cover 50 mm and main bars of diameter 25 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 330, c = 50, dia = 25 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 330 - 50 - 25/2 | Answer: 267.5 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 10.2 m^2 carrying a factored load of 18.9 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 10.2, w = 18.9 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 18.9 * 10.2 | Answer: 192.8 kN

question: For a bar of diameter 16 mm with design bond stress 1.9 MPa and steel stress 435 MPa, find the development length in mm.
solution: Given: dia = 16, tbd = 1.9, fs = 435 | Formula: Ld = phi fs / (4 tau_bd) | Substitute: Ld = 16*435 / (4*1.9) | Answer: 915.8 mm

question: A soil sample has porosity n = 0.33. Find its void ratio e.
solution: Given: n = 0.33 | Formula: e = n / (1 - n) | Substitute: e = 0.33 / (1 - 0.33) | Answer: 0.4925

question: A cohesionless soil has an angle of internal friction phi = 27 degrees. Find Rankine's coefficient of active earth pressure Ka.
solution: Given: phi = 27 | Formula: Ka = (1 - sin phi) / (1 + sin phi) | Substitute: Ka = (1 - sin27) / (1 + sin27) | Answer: 0.3755

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 3.8 m, unit weight 18 kN/m^3, phi = 30 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 2.4 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 21 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 2.4, g = 21 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (21 - 9.81)*2.4 | Answer: 26.86 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 5.8e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.8, area = 2e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 5.8, i = 0.8, A = 2 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (5.8e-4)*0.8*(2e-3) | Answer: 928 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 2.4 m, bed slope 0.01 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.026. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 3.2 m under a head of 1 m. Taking Cd = 0.62 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 5.9 m wide carries a discharge of 24.2 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 330 m and design speed 80 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 330, V = 80 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (80)^2 / (127*330) | Answer: 0.1527
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: For a design speed of 55 km/h with allowable superelevation 0.07 and lateral friction 0.12, find the minimum curve radius in m.
A tank of volume 200 m^3 treats a flow of 75 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 200, Q = 75 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 200 / 75 | Answer: 2.667 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 390 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.13 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 3 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 390, k = 0.13, t = 3 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 390*(1 - e^(-0.13*3)) | Answer: 125.9 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.51, rainfall intensity 115 mm/h over a catchment of 41.4 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.51, i = 115, A = 41.4 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.51*115*41.4 / 360 | Answer: 6.745 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.02 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 260 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.02, M = 260 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 260*(30+0.02)/30 | Answer: 260.2 m

question: Convert the decimal number 178 to binary.
solution: Divide 178 by 2 repeatedly, recording remainders | Reading remainders in reverse gives 10110010 | Answer: 10110010 (binary)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 2 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the decimal number 3975 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 3975 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: F87 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the 8-bit binary number 11110000 to decimal.
solution: Binary 11110000 = sum of bit-weights | Answer: 240 (decimal)
formula: Sum each bit times its positional weight (2^i)

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 01000111 and 00011010.
solution: XOR: 01011101 | Count of 1s = 5 | Answer: 5
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: An IPv4 subnet uses a /28 prefix. How many usable host addresses does it provide?
solution: Given: prefix = 28 | Formula: hosts = 2^(32 - prefix) - 2 | Substitute: hosts = 2^(32 - 28) - 2 | Answer: 14

question: A file of 870 megabits is sent over a link of 12 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 870, B = 12 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 870 / 12 | Answer: 72.5 s

question: A link has bandwidth 22 Mbps and round-trip time 100 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 22, R = 100 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 22e6 * 100e-3 bits = 2200 kb | Answer: 2200 kilobits

question: A channel has bandwidth 5 kHz. Using Nyquist's theorem with 4 signal levels, find the maximum data rate in kbps (noiseless).
solution: Given: B = 5, M = 4 | Formula: C = 2 B log2(M) | Substitute: C = 2*5*log2(4) | Answer: 20 kbps

question: A channel of bandwidth 20 kHz has a signal-to-noise ratio of 7 (linear). Using Shannon's theorem, find the channel capacity in kbps.
solution: Given: B = 20, SNR = 7 | Formula: C = B log2(1 + SNR) | Substitute: C = 20*log2(1 + 7) | Answer: 60 kbps

question: A memory has 256 addressable locations. How many address bits are required?
solution: Given: N = 256 | Formula: bits = log2(N) | Substitute: bits = log2(256) | Answer: 8 bits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.95, cache access time 6 ns and main-memory access time 50 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.95, tc = 6, tm = 50 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.95*6 + (1 - 0.95)*50 | Answer: 8.2 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 495732 elements?
solution: Given: n = 495732 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(495732)) + 1 | Answer: 19

question: An O(n^2) algorithm performs c*n^2 basic operations. If c = 1 and n = 2280, how many operations are performed?
solution: Given: n = 2280 | Formula: operations = n^2 | Substitute: = (2280)^2 | Answer: 5198400

question: A program is 70% parallelisable and run on 2 processors. Using Amdahl's law, find the maximum speedup.
solution: Parallel fraction f = 0.7 | S = 1 / ((1 - 0.7) + 0.7/2) | Answer: 1.538x speedup

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.01, memory access time 180 ns and page-fault service time 6 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 6 ms = 6000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.01)*180 + 0.01*6000000.0 ns | Answer: 60.18 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: How many distinct Boolean input combinations exist for a logic function of 9 variables?
solution: Given: n = 9 | Formula: combinations = 2^n | Substitute: = 2^9 | Answer: 512

question: A digital-to-analog converter has 6 bits and a full-scale output of 5 V. Find its resolution (voltage per step) in mV.
solution: Given: n = 6, Vfs = 5 | Formula: resolution = Vfs / (2^n - 1) | Substitute: resolution = 5 / (2^6 - 1) | Answer: 79.37 mV

question: A modem transmits at 4800 baud using 2-level signalling. Find the bit rate in bps.
solution: Given: baud = 4800, M = 2 | Formula: bit rate = baud * log2(M) | Substitute: bit rate = 4800 * log2(2) | Answer: 4800 bps

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 2.7 m^3 at 130 kPa and 300 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 2.7, P = 130, Tk = 300 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (130e3)*2.7 / (8.314*300) | Answer: 140.7 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.39 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 16 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.39, t = 16 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.39*16) | Answer: 0.9981

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.1 /min) is to reach 65% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.1, X = 65 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.65) / 0.1 | Answer: 10.5 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.29 /min) reaches 80% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.29, X = 80 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.8 / (0.29*(1 - 0.8)) | Answer: 13.79 min

question: A first-order reaction has a rate constant of 0.15 /min. Find its half-life in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.15 | Formula: t_half = ln(2) / k | Substitute: t_half = 0.6931 / 0.15 | Answer: 4.621 min

question: For a reaction with A = 1e10 /s and activation energy 90 kJ/mol at 480 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 1, Ea = 90, Tk = 480 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 1e10 * exp(-90e3 / (8.314*480)) | Answer: 1.606 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.99 and bottoms xW = 0.03, with relative volatility alpha = 3.1. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.99, xw = 0.03, al = 3.1 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.99/0.01)(0.97/0.03)] / ln(3.1) | Answer: 7.134 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.62 and x = 0.28. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.62, x = 0.28 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.62/0.38) / (0.28/0.72) | Answer: 4.195

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.29 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 95 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.29, Psat = 95 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.29 * 95 | Answer: 27.55 kPa

question: A stream of 6 kg/s with specific heat 1.3 kJ/kg-K is heated through 80 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 6, cp = 1.3, dT = 80 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 6*1.3*80 | Answer: 624 kW

question: A reactor of volume 10.5 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 0.8 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 10.5, Q = 0.8 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 10.5 / 0.8 | Answer: 13.12 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 5.6e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 3 mm with a concentration difference of 200 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 5.6, L = 3, dC = 200 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (5.6e-9)*200 / (3e-3) | Answer: 373.3 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 4.5 min and steady-state gain 2.9. For a step input of magnitude 16, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 4.5, K = 2.9, M = 16 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 2.9 * 16 | Answer: 46.4 units

question: A reactor operates at a space time of 18.2 min. Find its space velocity in per hour.
solution: Given: tau = 18.2 | Formula: SV = 60 / tau  (per hour) | Substitute: SV = 60 / 18.2 | Answer: 3.297 /h

question: An aircraft wing of area 25 m^2 flies at 220 m/s (air density 0.4 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.4. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 25, V = 220, rho = 0.4, CL = 0.4 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.4*(220)^2*25*0.4 / 1000 | Answer: 96.8 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 85 m^2 flies at 160 m/s (density 0.4 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.11. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 85, V = 160, rho = 0.4, CD = 0.11 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.4*(160)^2*85*0.11 / 1000 | Answer: 47.87 kN

question: Find the dynamic pressure for air of density 1.225 kg/m^3 moving at 130 m/s, in Pa.
solution: Given: rho = 1.225, V = 130 | Formula: q = 0.5 rho V^2 | Substitute: q = 0.5*1.225*(130)^2 | Answer: 10351 Pa

question: An aircraft flies at 210 m/s where the speed of sound is 310 m/s. Find the Mach number.
solution: Given: V = 210, a = 310 | Formula: M = V / a | Substitute: M = 210 / 310 | Answer: 0.6774

question: Find the circular orbital velocity of a satellite at altitude 1000 km above Earth (Earth radius 6371 km, mu = 3.986e14 m^3/s^2), in km/s.
A specimen under stress 270 MPa shows an elastic strain of 2.6e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 270, eps = 2.6 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 270 / (2.6e-3) MPa = 103.8 GPa | Answer: 103.8 GPa

question: A block of mass 19 kg has a volume of 4e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 19, V = 4 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 19 / (4e-3) | Answer: 4750 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 2800 mm is heated through 20 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 12e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 2800, dT = 20, al = 12 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 2800*12e-6*20 | Answer: 0.672 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 30 ohm, R2 = 125 ohm and R3 = 100 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 30, R2 = 125, R3 = 100 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 125*100 / 30 | Answer: 416.7 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 350 ohm and gauge factor 2.2 experiences a strain of 900e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 350, GF = 2.2, eps = 900 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 350*2.2*900e-6 | Answer: 693 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 10.16 when the true value is 10. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10.16, true = 10 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10.16 - 10| / 10 * 100 | Answer: 1.6 %

question: Annual demand is 42000 units, ordering cost 200 per order and holding cost 20 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 42000, S = 200, H = 20 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*42000*200 / 20) | Answer: 916.5 units

question: An asset costs 70000 with salvage value 24000 after 5 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 70000, Sv = 24000, n = 5 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (70000 - 24000) / 5 | Answer: 9200 per year

question: A product sells for 260 per unit with variable cost 80 per unit and fixed costs 15000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 260, V = 80, F = 15000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 15000 / (260 - 80) | Answer: 83.33 units

question: Find the present worth of 175000 received 9 years from now at an interest rate of 5% per year.
solution: Given: F = 175000, n = 9, i = 5 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 175000 / (1 + 0.05)^9 | Answer: 112807 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.99, 0.97 and 0.99 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.99, r2 = 0.97, r3 = 0.99 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.99*0.97*0.99 | Answer: 0.9507

question: Two components each of reliability 0.94 are connected in parallel. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r = 0.94 | Formula: R_parallel = 1 - (1 - r)^2 | Substitute: R = 1 - (1 - 0.94)^2 | Answer: 0.9964

question: A process produces 37 defective items in a batch of 3500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 37, N = 3500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 37/3500 * 1e6 | Answer: 10571 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -4x^3 - x^2 + 9x evaluated at x = -3.
For f(x) = 2x^3 + 3x^2 - 6x - 5, find f''(x) at x = 2.
Evaluate the definite integral of (x^2 + 5x + 8) dx from x = -3 to x = 3.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = 1x^3/3 + 5x^2/2 + 8x | Evaluate F(3) - F(-3) | Answer: 66
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 3x^2 - 4x - 2 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[-6, 2], [-5, -2]].
solution: Given: a = -6, b = 2, c = -5, d = -2 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (-6)(-2) - (2)(-5) | Answer: 22

question: Find the determinant of [[0, -2, 1], [-2, 4, 5], [-5, -6, 6]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: 58

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[3, 2], [8, 6]].
solution: Trace tr = 9, Determinant = 2 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 8.772

question: Solve for x: -3x + -2y = 1 and -3x + -1y = 5.
solution: Determinant = -3*-1 - -2*-3 = -3 | x = (e d - b f) / det = -3 | Answer: x = -3
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 43, 88, 53, 55, 68.
solution: Sum = 307 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 61.4 | Answer: 61.4

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 13, 8, 49, 23, 41.
solution: Mean = 26.8 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 17.7

question: Find the slope of the line through (6, -6) and (5, -7).
solution: Given: x1 = 6, y1 = -6, x2 = 5, y2 = -7 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (-7 - -6) / (5 - 6) | Answer: 1

question: Find the distance between the points (-4, 2) and (9, 0).
solution: Given: x1 = -4, y1 = 2, x2 = 9, y2 = 0 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((13)^2 + (-2)^2) | Answer: 13.15 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (-4,5), (1,-4), (-7,0).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 26 sq units

question: Evaluate the number of combinations C(14, 13).
solution: Given: n = 14, r = 13 | Formula: C(n, r) = n! / (r! (n - r)!) | Substitute: C(14, 13) = 14! / (13! * 1!) | Answer: 14

question: Evaluate the number of permutations P(11, 2).
solution: Given: n = 11, r = 2 | Formula: P(n, r) = n! / (n - r)! | Substitute: P(11, 2) = 11! / 9! | Answer: 110

question: Find the 5th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -19 and common difference -1.
solution: Given: a = -19, d = -1, n = 5 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -19 + (5 - 1)*-1 | Answer: -23

question: Find the sum of the first 34 terms of an AP with first term -1 and common difference 1.
solution: Given: a = -1, d = 1, n = 34 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 34/2 [2*-1 + (34-1)*1] | Answer: 527

question: Find the 4th term of a geometric progression with first term 7 and common ratio 4.
solution: Given: a = 7, r = 4, n = 4 | Formula: a_n = a r^(n-1) | Substitute: a_n = 7 * 4^(4-1) | Answer: 448

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 7000 at 11.8% per annum for 3 years.
solution: Given: P = 7000, R = 11.8, Tt = 3 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 7000 * 11.8 * 3 / 100 | Answer: 2478 currency units

question: Find the amount when 2000 is invested at 9% per annum compounded annually for 2 years.
solution: Given: P = 2000, R = 9, Tt = 2 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 2000 * (1 + 9/100)^2 | Answer: 2376 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (0, 1, 2) and (-6, 5, -1).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (-5, -3, -5) and (5, 2, -4).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 50.34

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (1, 0, 4) and (-4, -2, 3).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 68.88 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number 3 + 0i.
solution: Given: a = 3, b = 0 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((3)^2 + (0)^2) | Answer: 3

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number -9 + -7i.
solution: Given: a = -9, b = -7 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(-7, -9) | Answer: -142.1 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -x^3 + 7x^2 - 3x - 6 at x = 0.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-54 with initial guess x0=13, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=0.8 and ordinates 17, 3, 9, 3, 15, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 308 and 73.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 308 and 73 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 64 and 42.
solution: Given: a = 64, b = 42 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 64*42 / 2 | Answer: 1344
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 36 mm carries an axial tensile load of 5 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 15 mm and length 2900 mm carries an axial load of 78 kN. Take E = 70 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 46 mm transmits a torque of 150 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 46, Tt = 150 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(150*1000) / (pi*(46)^3) | Answer: 7.849 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 64 mm and length 800 mm carries a torque of 1100 N-m. With G = 45 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (64)^4 / 32 = 1647099 mm^4 | theta = (1100*1000)(800) / (45000 * 1647099) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 0.6803 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 78 mm wide and 190 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 78, h = 190 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 78*(190)^2 / 6 | Answer: 469300 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (60 mm x 110 mm) carries a bending moment of 24 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (77 mm x 90 mm) has effective length 3200 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 690 MPa is designed for a working stress of 160 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 690, sw = 160 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 690 / 160 | Answer: 4.312

question: A steel bar is fully restrained and heated through 45 deg C. With E = 200 GPa and alpha = 12e-6 /deg C, find the thermal stress in MPa.
solution: Given: dT = 45, E = 200, al = 12 | Formula: sigma = E alpha (dT) | Substitute: sigma = 200000 * 12e-6 * 45 | Answer: 108 MPa

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 600 mm and wall thickness 8 mm carries an internal pressure of 2.7 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 600, t = 8, P = 2.7 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 2.7*600 / (2*8) | Answer: 101.2 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 1020 K and 390 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 1020, Tc = 390 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 390/1020) * 100 | Answer: 61.76 %

question: A refrigerator works between 255 K (cold) and 320 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 255, Th = 320 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 255 / (320 - 255) | Answer: 3.923

question: A heat pump operates between 261 K and 306 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 261, Th = 306 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 306 / (306 - 261) | Answer: 6.8

question: 6.1 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 200 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 6.1, dT = 200 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 6.1 * 0.718 * 200 | Answer: 876 kJ

question: 7.1 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 165 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 7.1, dT = 165 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 7.1 * 1.005 * 165 | Answer: 1177 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 1 m^3 at 350 K with mass 3.9 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 1, Tk = 350, m = 3.9 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 3.9*0.287*350 / 1 | Answer: 391.8 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 2.8 kg of air expands isothermally at 340 K from volume V1 to 4*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.8, Tk = 340, ratio = 4 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 2.8*0.287*340*ln(4) | Answer: 378.8 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 2.9 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.23 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 2.9, D = 0.23 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*2.9*0.23 / 0.001 | Answer: 667000

question: Water flows at 1.7 m/s through a pipe of diameter 280 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 18.7 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 18.7 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*18.7 / 1000 | Answer: 183.4 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 9.7 m. Taking Cv = 0.95, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 9.7, cv = 0.95 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.95*sqrt(2*9.81*9.7) | Answer: 13.11 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 180 mm) water flows at 2 m/s. It contracts to diameter 130 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 180, d2 = 130, V1 = 2 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 2*(180/130)^2 | Answer: 3.834 m/s

question: Water flows at 2.2 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.42 m and length 290 m. With friction factor f = 0.033, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 37 teeth drives a gear of 93 teeth. If the pinion runs at 400 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 37, z2 = 93, N1 = 400 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 400*37 / 93 | Answer: 159.1 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 310 mm rotates at 1200 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 310, N = 1200 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.31)*1200 / 60 | Answer: 19.48 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 15.8 kW at 650 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 15.8, N = 650 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(15.8*1000) / (2*pi*650) | Answer: 232.1 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 6.8 kg rotates at radius 0.52 m at 400 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 12100 N/m and mass 15 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 12100, m = 15 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(12100/15) | Answer: 4.52 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 6.4 m^2 and thickness 0.1 m has conductivity k = 40.2 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 40 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 6.4, L = 0.1, k = 40.2, dT = 40 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 40.2*6.4*40 / 0.1 | Answer: 102912 W

question: A surface of area 1.8 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 90 W/m^2-K to surroundings 120 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 1.8, h = 90, dT = 120 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 90*1.8*120 | Answer: 19440 W

question: In a counter-flow heat exchanger the terminal temperature differences are 55 deg C and 30 deg C. Find the log mean temperature difference (LMTD) in deg C.
solution: Given: dT1 = 55, dT2 = 30 | Formula: LMTD = (dT1 - dT2) / ln(dT1/dT2) | Substitute: LMTD = (55 - 30) / ln(55/30) | Answer: 41.24 deg C

question: In turning, cutting speed = 130 m/min, feed = 0.38 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2.8 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 130, f = 0.38, d = 2.8 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*130*0.38*2.8 | Answer: 138320 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 90 mm is turned at 450 rpm with a feed of 0.23 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 90, N = 450, f = 0.23 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 90 / (0.23*450) | Answer: 0.8696 min

question: A resistor of 168 ohm carries a current of 1.1 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 168, I = 1.1 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 1.1 * 168 | Answer: 184.8 V

question: Three resistors 78 ohm, 64 ohm and 27 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 78, R2 = 64, R3 = 27 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 78 + 64 + 27 | Answer: 169 ohm

question: Two resistors 116 ohm and 65 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 116, R2 = 65 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 116*65 / (116+65) | Answer: 41.66 ohm

question: A device draws 13.5 A at 120 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 120, I = 13.5 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 120 * 13.5 | Answer: 1620 W

question: A current of 2.4 A flows through a 12 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 2.4, R = 12 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (2.4)^2 * 12 | Answer: 69.12 W

question: Two capacitors 34.4 uF and 12.1 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 34.4, C2 = 12.1 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 34.4*12.1 / (34.4+12.1) | Answer: 8.951 uF

question: A resistor 90 kohm and capacitor 0.8 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 90, C = 0.8 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (90k)(0.8u) = 72 ms | Answer: 72 ms

question: An inductor 203.1 mH is in series with 167 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 203.1, R = 167 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (203.1e-3) / 167 | Answer: 1.216 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 125.1 mH inductor at 520 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 125.1, f = 520 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (520)(125.1e-3) | Answer: 408.7 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 14.8 uF capacitor at 400 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 14.8, f = 400 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (400)(14.8e-6)) | Answer: 26.88 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 69 ohm, XL = 82 ohm and XC = 24 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 69, XL = 82, XC = 24 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(69^2 + (82 - 24)^2) | Answer: 90.14 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 30.1 mH and C = 3 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 30.1, C = 3 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(30.1e-3 * 3e-6)) | Answer: 529.6 Hz

question: A capacitor of 80.8 uF is charged to 180 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 80.8, V = 180 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*80.8e-6*(180)^2 | Answer: 1309 mJ

question: An alternating voltage has a peak value of 68 V. Find its RMS value.
solution: Given: Vp = 68 | Formula: Vrms = Vp / sqrt(2) | Substitute: Vrms = 68 / sqrt(2) | Answer: 48.08 V

question: A transformer has primary voltage 310 V with 570 primary turns and 360 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 310, N1 = 570, N2 = 360 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 310 * 360/570 | Answer: 195.8 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 230 V and draws an armature current of 21 A. If the armature resistance is 1.04 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 230, Ia = 21, Ra = 1.04 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 230 - 21*1.04 | Answer: 208.2 V

question: Find the synchronous speed of a 12-pole machine on a 50 Hz supply, in rpm.
solution: Given: P = 12, f = 50 | Formula: Ns = 120 f / P | Substitute: Ns = 120*50 / 12 | Answer: 500 rpm

question: A 4-pole induction motor on a 60 Hz supply runs at 790 rpm. Find the slip (%).
formula: s = (Ns - N) / Ns,  Ns = 120 f / P

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 35 A at 433 V (line) with a power factor of 0.74. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 35, VL = 433, pf = 0.74 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*433*35*0.74 / 1000 | Answer: 19.42 kW

question: A load has real power 75 kW and apparent power 120 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 75, S = 120 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 75 / 120 | Answer: 0.625

question: A machine delivers 50 kW output while drawing 127 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 50, Pi = 127 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 50/127 * 100 | Answer: 39.37 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 11 V across R1 = 7 ohm and R2 = 6 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 11, R1 = 7, R2 = 6 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 11*6 / (7+6) | Answer: 5.077 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 170 kohm and Rin = 1 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 170, Rin = 1 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 170 / 1 | Answer: 170

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 70 kohm and Rg = 37 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 70, Rg = 37 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 70/37 | Answer: 2.892

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 6190. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 6190 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(6190) | Answer: 37.92 dB

question: A first-order system has a time constant of 8.8 s. Find the time (in s) to reach 63.2% of its final value.
solution: For a first-order step response, y = 1 - e^(-t/tau) | y = 0.632 when t = tau | Answer: 8.8 s
formula: At t = tau the response reaches 63.2% (one time constant)

question: A signal is sampled at 144 kHz. According to the Nyquist criterion, what is the maximum signal frequency that can be represented (in kHz)?
solution: Given: fs = 144 | Formula: f_max = fs / 2 | Substitute: f_max = 144 / 2 | Answer: 72 kHz

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.2 m carries a central point load of 100 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 9.2, W = 100 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 100*9.2 / 4 | Answer: 230 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 7.7 m carries a UDL of 35 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7.7, w = 35 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 35*(7.7)^2 / 8 | Answer: 259.4 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 4.1 m carries a point load 35 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.1, W = 35 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 35*4.1 | Answer: 143.5 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 1.3 m carries a UDL of 38 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 1.3, w = 38 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 38*(1.3)^2 / 2 | Answer: 32.11 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 4 m carries a point load 20 kN at distance 3 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 4, a = 3, W = 20 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 20*(4 - 3) / 4 | Answer: 5 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 3.9 m) carries a central point load 40 kN. With E = 25 GPa and I = 300e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=40000 N, L=3900.0 mm, E=25000 MPa, I=300e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 6.591 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 7.5 m carries a UDL of 21 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7.5, w = 21 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 21*(7.5)^2 / 12 | Answer: 98.44 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 590 mm, clear cover 35 mm and main bars of diameter 20 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 590, c = 35, dia = 20 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 590 - 35 - 20/2 | Answer: 545 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 12.8 m^2 carrying a factored load of 19.5 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 12.8, w = 19.5 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 19.5 * 12.8 | Answer: 249.6 kN

question: For a bar of diameter 25 mm with design bond stress 1.5 MPa and steel stress 395 MPa, find the development length in mm.
solution: Given: dia = 25, tbd = 1.5, fs = 395 | Formula: Ld = phi fs / (4 tau_bd) | Substitute: Ld = 25*395 / (4*1.5) | Answer: 1646 mm

question: A soil sample has porosity n = 0.51. Find its void ratio e.
solution: Given: n = 0.51 | Formula: e = n / (1 - n) | Substitute: e = 0.51 / (1 - 0.51) | Answer: 1.041

question: A cohesionless soil has an angle of internal friction phi = 37 degrees. Find Rankine's coefficient of active earth pressure Ka.
solution: Given: phi = 37 | Formula: Ka = (1 - sin phi) / (1 + sin phi) | Substitute: Ka = (1 - sin37) / (1 + sin37) | Answer: 0.2486

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 4.9 m, unit weight 20 kN/m^3, phi = 34 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 10.9 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 18 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 10.9, g = 18 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (18 - 9.81)*10.9 | Answer: 89.27 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 7.8e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.7, area = 2.6e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 7.8, i = 0.7, A = 2.6 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (7.8e-4)*0.7*(2.6e-3) | Answer: 142 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 2.5 m, bed slope 0.005 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.027. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 3.9 m under a head of 0.2 m. Taking Cd = 0.61 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 5.6 m wide carries a discharge of 21.3 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 160 m and design speed 100 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 160, V = 100 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (100)^2 / (127*160) | Answer: 0.4921
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: For a design speed of 80 km/h with allowable superelevation 0.06 and lateral friction 0.15, find the minimum curve radius in m.
A tank of volume 490 m^3 treats a flow of 185 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 490, Q = 185 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 490 / 185 | Answer: 2.649 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 260 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.28 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 7 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 260, k = 0.28, t = 7 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 260*(1 - e^(-0.28*7)) | Answer: 223.4 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.45, rainfall intensity 55 mm/h over a catchment of 48.4 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.45, i = 55, A = 48.4 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.45*55*48.4 / 360 | Answer: 3.327 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.07 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 300 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.07, M = 300 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 300*(20+0.07)/20 | Answer: 301.1 m

question: Convert the decimal number 92 to binary.
solution: Divide 92 by 2 repeatedly, recording remainders | Reading remainders in reverse gives 1011100 | Answer: 1011100 (binary)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 2 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the decimal number 3036 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 3036 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: BDC (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the 8-bit binary number 00010000 to decimal.
solution: Binary 00010000 = sum of bit-weights | Answer: 16 (decimal)
formula: Sum each bit times its positional weight (2^i)

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 10111000 and 00101010.
solution: XOR: 10010010 | Count of 1s = 3 | Answer: 3
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: An IPv4 subnet uses a /22 prefix. How many usable host addresses does it provide?
solution: Given: prefix = 22 | Formula: hosts = 2^(32 - prefix) - 2 | Substitute: hosts = 2^(32 - 22) - 2 | Answer: 1022

question: A file of 380 megabits is sent over a link of 81 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 380, B = 81 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 380 / 81 | Answer: 4.691 s

question: A link has bandwidth 78 Mbps and round-trip time 120 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 78, R = 120 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 78e6 * 120e-3 bits = 9360 kb | Answer: 9360 kilobits

question: A channel has bandwidth 11 kHz. Using Nyquist's theorem with 16 signal levels, find the maximum data rate in kbps (noiseless).
solution: Given: B = 11, M = 16 | Formula: C = 2 B log2(M) | Substitute: C = 2*11*log2(16) | Answer: 88 kbps

question: A channel of bandwidth 8 kHz has a signal-to-noise ratio of 255 (linear). Using Shannon's theorem, find the channel capacity in kbps.
solution: Given: B = 8, SNR = 255 | Formula: C = B log2(1 + SNR) | Substitute: C = 8*log2(1 + 255) | Answer: 64 kbps

question: A memory has 4096 addressable locations. How many address bits are required?
solution: Given: N = 4096 | Formula: bits = log2(N) | Substitute: bits = log2(4096) | Answer: 12 bits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.92, cache access time 1 ns and main-memory access time 190 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.92, tc = 1, tm = 190 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.92*1 + (1 - 0.92)*190 | Answer: 16.12 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 170040 elements?
solution: Given: n = 170040 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(170040)) + 1 | Answer: 18

question: An O(n^2) algorithm performs c*n^2 basic operations. If c = 1 and n = 2730, how many operations are performed?
solution: Given: n = 2730 | Formula: operations = n^2 | Substitute: = (2730)^2 | Answer: 7452900

question: A program is 75% parallelisable and run on 16 processors. Using Amdahl's law, find the maximum speedup.
solution: Parallel fraction f = 0.75 | S = 1 / ((1 - 0.75) + 0.75/16) | Answer: 3.368x speedup

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.013, memory access time 80 ns and page-fault service time 3 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 3 ms = 3000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.013)*80 + 0.013*3000000.0 ns | Answer: 39.08 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: How many distinct Boolean input combinations exist for a logic function of 5 variables?
solution: Given: n = 5 | Formula: combinations = 2^n | Substitute: = 2^5 | Answer: 32

question: A digital-to-analog converter has 10 bits and a full-scale output of 5 V. Find its resolution (voltage per step) in mV.
solution: Given: n = 10, Vfs = 5 | Formula: resolution = Vfs / (2^n - 1) | Substitute: resolution = 5 / (2^10 - 1) | Answer: 4.888 mV

question: A modem transmits at 2100 baud using 8-level signalling. Find the bit rate in bps.
solution: Given: baud = 2100, M = 8 | Formula: bit rate = baud * log2(M) | Substitute: bit rate = 2100 * log2(8) | Answer: 6300 bps

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 0.9 m^3 at 490 kPa and 310 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 0.9, P = 490, Tk = 310 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (490e3)*0.9 / (8.314*310) | Answer: 171.1 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.39 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 6 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.39, t = 6 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.39*6) | Answer: 0.9037

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.38 /min) is to reach 85% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.38, X = 85 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.85) / 0.38 | Answer: 4.992 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.17 /min) reaches 90% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.17, X = 90 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.9 / (0.17*(1 - 0.9)) | Answer: 52.94 min

question: A first-order reaction has a rate constant of 0.21 /min. Find its half-life in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.21 | Formula: t_half = ln(2) / k | Substitute: t_half = 0.6931 / 0.21 | Answer: 3.301 min

question: For a reaction with A = 7e10 /s and activation energy 50 kJ/mol at 380 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 7, Ea = 50, Tk = 380 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 7e10 * exp(-50e3 / (8.314*380)) | Answer: 9373 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.93 and bottoms xW = 0.07, with relative volatility alpha = 2.3. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.93, xw = 0.07, al = 2.3 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.93/0.07)(0.93/0.07)] / ln(2.3) | Answer: 6.211 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.61 and x = 0.34. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.61, x = 0.34 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.61/0.39) / (0.34/0.66) | Answer: 3.036

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.15 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 30 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.15, Psat = 30 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.15 * 30 | Answer: 4.5 kPa

question: A stream of 2.3 kg/s with specific heat 1.2 kJ/kg-K is heated through 25 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 2.3, cp = 1.2, dT = 25 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 2.3*1.2*25 | Answer: 69 kW

question: A reactor of volume 16.3 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 0.5 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 16.3, Q = 0.5 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 16.3 / 0.5 | Answer: 32.6 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 3.8e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 5 mm with a concentration difference of 10 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 3.8, L = 5, dC = 10 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (3.8e-9)*10 / (5e-3) | Answer: 7.6 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 6.1 min and steady-state gain 2.7. For a step input of magnitude 20, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 6.1, K = 2.7, M = 20 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 2.7 * 20 | Answer: 54 units

question: A reactor operates at a space time of 11.3 min. Find its space velocity in per hour.
solution: Given: tau = 11.3 | Formula: SV = 60 / tau  (per hour) | Substitute: SV = 60 / 11.3 | Answer: 5.31 /h

question: An aircraft wing of area 50 m^2 flies at 220 m/s (air density 0.7 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.4. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 50, V = 220, rho = 0.7, CL = 0.4 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.7*(220)^2*50*0.4 / 1000 | Answer: 338.8 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 100 m^2 flies at 170 m/s (density 0.4 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.03. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 100, V = 170, rho = 0.4, CD = 0.03 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.4*(170)^2*100*0.03 / 1000 | Answer: 17.34 kN

question: Find the dynamic pressure for air of density 0.7 kg/m^3 moving at 180 m/s, in Pa.
solution: Given: rho = 0.7, V = 180 | Formula: q = 0.5 rho V^2 | Substitute: q = 0.5*0.7*(180)^2 | Answer: 11340 Pa

question: An aircraft flies at 320 m/s where the speed of sound is 310 m/s. Find the Mach number.
solution: Given: V = 320, a = 310 | Formula: M = V / a | Substitute: M = 320 / 310 | Answer: 1.032

question: Find the circular orbital velocity of a satellite at altitude 1200 km above Earth (Earth radius 6371 km, mu = 3.986e14 m^3/s^2), in km/s.
A specimen under stress 220 MPa shows an elastic strain of 1.9e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 220, eps = 1.9 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 220 / (1.9e-3) MPa = 115.8 GPa | Answer: 115.8 GPa

question: A block of mass 24 kg has a volume of 2.7e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 24, V = 2.7 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 24 / (2.7e-3) | Answer: 8889 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 1300 mm is heated through 105 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 17e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 1300, dT = 105, al = 17 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 1300*17e-6*105 | Answer: 2.321 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 10 ohm, R2 = 155 ohm and R3 = 160 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 10, R2 = 155, R3 = 160 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 155*160 / 10 | Answer: 2480 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 120 ohm and gauge factor 2.2 experiences a strain of 750e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 120, GF = 2.2, eps = 750 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 120*2.2*750e-6 | Answer: 198 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 10.15 when the true value is 10. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10.15, true = 10 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10.15 - 10| / 10 * 100 | Answer: 1.5 %

question: Annual demand is 46500 units, ordering cost 290 per order and holding cost 12 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 46500, S = 290, H = 12 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*46500*290 / 12) | Answer: 1499 units

question: An asset costs 470000 with salvage value 26000 after 9 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 470000, Sv = 26000, n = 9 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (470000 - 26000) / 9 | Answer: 49333 per year

question: A product sells for 450 per unit with variable cost 170 per unit and fixed costs 55000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 450, V = 170, F = 55000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 55000 / (450 - 170) | Answer: 196.4 units

question: Find the present worth of 50000 received 4 years from now at an interest rate of 5% per year.
solution: Given: F = 50000, n = 4, i = 5 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 50000 / (1 + 0.05)^4 | Answer: 41135 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.9, 0.98 and 0.93 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.9, r2 = 0.98, r3 = 0.93 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.9*0.98*0.93 | Answer: 0.8203

question: Two components each of reliability 0.85 are connected in parallel. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r = 0.85 | Formula: R_parallel = 1 - (1 - r)^2 | Substitute: R = 1 - (1 - 0.85)^2 | Answer: 0.9775

question: A process produces 22 defective items in a batch of 6500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 22, N = 6500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 22/6500 * 1e6 | Answer: 3385 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = 3x^3 - x^2 + 6x - 9 evaluated at x = -1.
For f(x) = -6x^3 + 4x^2 - 8x + 1, find f''(x) at x = 4.
Evaluate the definite integral of (6x - 5) dx from x = 1 to x = 5.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = 0x^3/3 + 6x^2/2 + -5x | Evaluate F(5) - F(1) | Answer: 52
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of x^2 + 8x - 5 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[7, -5], [-7, -2]].
solution: Given: a = 7, b = -5, c = -7, d = -2 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (7)(-2) - (-5)(-7) | Answer: -49

question: Find the determinant of [[6, 5, -3], [4, -6, -2], [-6, 6, -6]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: 504

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[2, -2], [-4, -2]].
solution: Trace tr = 0, Determinant = -12 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 3.464

question: Solve for x: 0x + -3y = -7 and 1x + 1y = 1.
solution: Determinant = 0*1 - -3*1 = 3 | x = (e d - b f) / det = -1.333 | Answer: x = -1.333
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 62, 44, 94, 33, 12.
solution: Sum = 245 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 49 | Answer: 49

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 9, 14, 10, 18, 29.
solution: Mean = 16 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 8.093

question: Find the slope of the line through (1, -8) and (-1, 8).
solution: Given: x1 = 1, y1 = -8, x2 = -1, y2 = 8 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (8 - -8) / (-1 - 1) | Answer: -8

question: Find the distance between the points (-7, -2) and (-1, 7).
solution: Given: x1 = -7, y1 = -2, x2 = -1, y2 = 7 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((6)^2 + (9)^2) | Answer: 10.82 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (2,3), (-6,8), (4,-3).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 19 sq units

question: Evaluate the number of combinations C(15, 7).
solution: Given: n = 15, r = 7 | Formula: C(n, r) = n! / (r! (n - r)!) | Substitute: C(15, 7) = 15! / (7! * 8!) | Answer: 6435

question: Evaluate the number of permutations P(12, 6).
solution: Given: n = 12, r = 6 | Formula: P(n, r) = n! / (n - r)! | Substitute: P(12, 6) = 12! / 6! | Answer: 665280

question: Find the 39th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 8 and common difference 0.
solution: Given: a = 8, d = 0, n = 39 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = 8 + (39 - 1)*0 | Answer: 8

question: Find the sum of the first 24 terms of an AP with first term -11 and common difference 1.
solution: Given: a = -11, d = 1, n = 24 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 24/2 [2*-11 + (24-1)*1] | Answer: 12

question: Find the 4th term of a geometric progression with first term 2 and common ratio 4.
solution: Given: a = 2, r = 4, n = 4 | Formula: a_n = a r^(n-1) | Substitute: a_n = 2 * 4^(4-1) | Answer: 128

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 13000 at 7.8% per annum for 10 years.
solution: Given: P = 13000, R = 7.8, Tt = 10 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 13000 * 7.8 * 10 / 100 | Answer: 10140 currency units

question: Find the amount when 32500 is invested at 9.8% per annum compounded annually for 2 years.
solution: Given: P = 32500, R = 9.8, Tt = 2 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 32500 * (1 + 9.8/100)^2 | Answer: 39182 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (1, 5, -1) and (3, -1, 5).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (-2, -3, 5) and (6, -6, -3).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 54.74

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (5, -2, 0) and (5, -2, 0).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 0 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number 1 + 0i.
solution: Given: a = 1, b = 0 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((1)^2 + (0)^2) | Answer: 1

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number -5 + -3i.
solution: Given: a = -5, b = -3 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(-3, -5) | Answer: -149 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = 3x^3 + 3x^2 + 3x + 9 at x = 3.
solution: Given: a = 3, b = 3, c = 3, d = 9, x0 = 3 | Formula: f(x0) = a x0^3 + b x0^2 + c x0 + d | Substitute: f(3) = 3(3)^3 + 3(3)^2 + 3(3) + 9 | Answer: 126

question: Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-114 with initial guess x0=15, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.9 and ordinates 8, 6, 2, 8, 20, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 540 and 158.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 540 and 158 | Answer: GCD = 2

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 34 and 65.
solution: Given: a = 34, b = 65 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 34*65 / 1 | Answer: 2210
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 60 mm carries an axial tensile load of 25 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 22 mm and length 2500 mm carries an axial load of 48 kN. Take E = 200 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 79 mm transmits a torque of 2400 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 79, Tt = 2400 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(2400*1000) / (pi*(79)^3) | Answer: 24.79 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 43 mm and length 1200 mm carries a torque of 1400 N-m. With G = 45 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (43)^4 / 32 = 33564 mm^4 | theta = (1400*1000)(1200) / (45000 * 33564) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 6.373 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 64 mm wide and 180 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 64, h = 180 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 64*(180)^2 / 6 | Answer: 345600 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (50 mm x 80 mm) carries a bending moment of 17 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (32 mm x 150 mm) has effective length 3700 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 510 MPa is designed for a working stress of 100 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 510, sw = 100 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 510 / 100 | Answer: 5.1

question: A steel bar is fully restrained and heated through 45 deg C. With E = 210 GPa and alpha = 11e-6 /deg C, find the thermal stress in MPa.
solution: Given: dT = 45, E = 210, al = 11 | Formula: sigma = E alpha (dT) | Substitute: sigma = 210000 * 11e-6 * 45 | Answer: 104 MPa

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1450 mm and wall thickness 18 mm carries an internal pressure of 1.7 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1450, t = 18, P = 1.7 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 1.7*1450 / (2*18) | Answer: 68.47 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 800 K and 320 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 800, Tc = 320 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 320/800) * 100 | Answer: 60 %

question: A refrigerator works between 274 K (cold) and 322 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 274, Th = 322 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 274 / (322 - 274) | Answer: 5.708

question: A heat pump operates between 280 K and 330 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 280, Th = 330 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 330 / (330 - 280) | Answer: 6.6

question: 1.5 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 60 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1.5, dT = 60 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 1.5 * 0.718 * 60 | Answer: 64.62 kJ

question: 1.4 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 180 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1.4, dT = 180 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 1.4 * 1.005 * 180 | Answer: 253.3 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 0.9 m^3 at 510 K with mass 3.3 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 0.9, Tk = 510, m = 3.3 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 3.3*0.287*510 / 0.9 | Answer: 536.7 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 4.9 kg of air expands isothermally at 400 K from volume V1 to 2*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.9, Tk = 400, ratio = 2 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 4.9*0.287*400*ln(2) | Answer: 389.9 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 1.4 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.27 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 1.4, D = 0.27 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*1.4*0.27 / 0.001 | Answer: 378000

question: Water flows at 3.9 m/s through a pipe of diameter 130 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 24.7 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 24.7 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*24.7 / 1000 | Answer: 242.3 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 17.8 m. Taking Cv = 0.97, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 17.8, cv = 0.97 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.97*sqrt(2*9.81*17.8) | Answer: 18.13 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 320 mm) water flows at 1.4 m/s. It contracts to diameter 140 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
Water flows at 2 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.2 m and length 160 m. With friction factor f = 0.033, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 16 teeth drives a gear of 49 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1200 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 16, z2 = 49, N1 = 1200 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1200*16 / 49 | Answer: 391.8 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 250 mm rotates at 900 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 250, N = 900 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.25)*900 / 60 | Answer: 11.78 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 27.7 kW at 850 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 27.7, N = 850 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(27.7*1000) / (2*pi*850) | Answer: 311.2 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 5 kg rotates at radius 0.18 m at 900 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 14600 N/m and mass 11.5 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 14600, m = 11.5 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(14600/11.5) | Answer: 5.671 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 6.3 m^2 and thickness 0.28 m has conductivity k = 25.4 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 190 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 6.3, L = 0.28, k = 25.4, dT = 190 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 25.4*6.3*190 / 0.28 | Answer: 108585 W

question: A surface of area 5.9 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 55 W/m^2-K to surroundings 90 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 5.9, h = 55, dT = 90 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 55*5.9*90 | Answer: 29205 W

question: In a counter-flow heat exchanger the terminal temperature differences are 85 deg C and 10 deg C. Find the log mean temperature difference (LMTD) in deg C.
solution: Given: dT1 = 85, dT2 = 10 | Formula: LMTD = (dT1 - dT2) / ln(dT1/dT2) | Substitute: LMTD = (85 - 10) / ln(85/10) | Answer: 35.05 deg C

question: In turning, cutting speed = 160 m/min, feed = 0.18 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2.2 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 160, f = 0.18, d = 2.2 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*160*0.18*2.2 | Answer: 63360 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 360 mm is turned at 750 rpm with a feed of 0.15 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 360, N = 750, f = 0.15 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 360 / (0.15*750) | Answer: 3.2 min

question: A resistor of 169 ohm carries a current of 1.6 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 169, I = 1.6 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 1.6 * 169 | Answer: 270.4 V

question: Three resistors 39 ohm, 21 ohm and 26 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 39, R2 = 21, R3 = 26 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 39 + 21 + 26 | Answer: 86 ohm

question: Two resistors 26 ohm and 88 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 26, R2 = 88 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 26*88 / (26+88) | Answer: 20.07 ohm

question: A device draws 7.6 A at 180 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 180, I = 7.6 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 180 * 7.6 | Answer: 1368 W

question: A current of 0.4 A flows through a 47 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 0.4, R = 47 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (0.4)^2 * 47 | Answer: 7.52 W

question: Two capacitors 31.3 uF and 6.1 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 31.3, C2 = 6.1 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 31.3*6.1 / (31.3+6.1) | Answer: 5.105 uF

question: A resistor 34 kohm and capacitor 12 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 34, C = 12 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (34k)(12u) = 408 ms | Answer: 408 ms

question: An inductor 282.7 mH is in series with 69 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 282.7, R = 69 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (282.7e-3) / 69 | Answer: 4.097 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 181.1 mH inductor at 880 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 181.1, f = 880 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (880)(181.1e-3) | Answer: 1001 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 20.5 uF capacitor at 220 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 20.5, f = 220 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (220)(20.5e-6)) | Answer: 35.29 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 85 ohm, XL = 141 ohm and XC = 89 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 85, XL = 141, XC = 89 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(85^2 + (141 - 89)^2) | Answer: 99.64 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 47.1 mH and C = 6.1 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 47.1, C = 6.1 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(47.1e-3 * 6.1e-6)) | Answer: 296.9 Hz

question: A capacitor of 47.9 uF is charged to 285 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 47.9, V = 285 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*47.9e-6*(285)^2 | Answer: 1945 mJ

question: An alternating voltage has a peak value of 264 V. Find its RMS value.
solution: Given: Vp = 264 | Formula: Vrms = Vp / sqrt(2) | Substitute: Vrms = 264 / sqrt(2) | Answer: 186.7 V

question: A transformer has primary voltage 130 V with 910 primary turns and 80 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 130, N1 = 910, N2 = 80 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 130 * 80/910 | Answer: 11.43 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 140 V and draws an armature current of 27 A. If the armature resistance is 0.76 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 140, Ia = 27, Ra = 0.76 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 140 - 27*0.76 | Answer: 119.5 V

question: Find the synchronous speed of a 6-pole machine on a 60 Hz supply, in rpm.
solution: Given: P = 6, f = 60 | Formula: Ns = 120 f / P | Substitute: Ns = 120*60 / 6 | Answer: 1200 rpm

question: A 8-pole induction motor on a 60 Hz supply runs at 740 rpm. Find the slip (%).
formula: s = (Ns - N) / Ns,  Ns = 120 f / P

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 45 A at 433 V (line) with a power factor of 0.96. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 45, VL = 433, pf = 0.96 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*433*45*0.96 / 1000 | Answer: 32.4 kW

question: A load has real power 15 kW and apparent power 200 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 15, S = 200 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 15 / 200 | Answer: 0.075

question: A machine delivers 70 kW output while drawing 92 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 70, Pi = 92 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 70/92 * 100 | Answer: 76.09 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 7 V across R1 = 32 ohm and R2 = 22 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 7, R1 = 32, R2 = 22 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 7*22 / (32+22) | Answer: 2.852 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 20 kohm and Rin = 25 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 20, Rin = 25 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 20 / 25 | Answer: 0.8

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 70 kohm and Rg = 6 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 70, Rg = 6 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 70/6 | Answer: 12.67

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 5367. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 5367 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(5367) | Answer: 37.3 dB

question: A first-order system has a time constant of 9.9 s. Find the time (in s) to reach 63.2% of its final value.
solution: For a first-order step response, y = 1 - e^(-t/tau) | y = 0.632 when t = tau | Answer: 9.9 s
formula: At t = tau the response reaches 63.2% (one time constant)

question: A signal is sampled at 134 kHz. According to the Nyquist criterion, what is the maximum signal frequency that can be represented (in kHz)?
solution: Given: fs = 134 | Formula: f_max = fs / 2 | Substitute: f_max = 134 / 2 | Answer: 67 kHz

question: A simply supported beam of span 8.7 m carries a central point load of 40 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 8.7, W = 40 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 40*8.7 / 4 | Answer: 87 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 7.8 m carries a UDL of 10 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7.8, w = 10 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 10*(7.8)^2 / 8 | Answer: 76.05 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 1 m carries a point load 80 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 1, W = 80 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 80*1 | Answer: 80 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 3.6 m carries a UDL of 10 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.6, w = 10 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 10*(3.6)^2 / 2 | Answer: 64.8 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 5.1 m carries a point load 35 kN at distance 2.6 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 5.1, a = 2.6, W = 35 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 35*(5.1 - 2.6) / 5.1 | Answer: 17.16 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 5 m) carries a central point load 80 kN. With E = 200 GPa and I = 140e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=80000 N, L=5000.0 mm, E=200000 MPa, I=140e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 7.44 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 4.4 m carries a UDL of 36 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.4, w = 36 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 36*(4.4)^2 / 12 | Answer: 58.08 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 650 mm, clear cover 50 mm and main bars of diameter 25 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 650, c = 50, dia = 25 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 650 - 50 - 25/2 | Answer: 587.5 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 36.2 m^2 carrying a factored load of 15.4 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 36.2, w = 15.4 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 15.4 * 36.2 | Answer: 557.5 kN
