solution: Given: d = 29, Tt = 2300 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(2300*1000) / (pi*(29)^3) | Answer: 480.3 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 43 mm and length 600 mm carries a torque of 450 N-m. With G = 77 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (43)^4 / 32 = 33564 mm^4 | theta = (450*1000)(600) / (77000 * 33564) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 0.5986 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 102 mm wide and 230 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 102, h = 230 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 102*(230)^2 / 6 | Answer: 899300 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (84 mm x 200 mm) carries a bending moment of 30 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (39 mm x 160 mm) has effective length 3300 mm and E = 200 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 690 MPa is designed for a working stress of 100 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 690, sw = 100 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 690 / 100 | Answer: 6.9

question: A steel bar is fully restrained and heated through 20 deg C. With E = 200 GPa and alpha = 11e-6 /deg C, find the thermal stress in MPa.
solution: Given: dT = 20, E = 200, al = 11 | Formula: sigma = E alpha (dT) | Substitute: sigma = 200000 * 11e-6 * 20 | Answer: 44 MPa

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1350 mm and wall thickness 10 mm carries an internal pressure of 0.5 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1350, t = 10, P = 0.5 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 0.5*1350 / (2*10) | Answer: 33.75 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 740 K and 430 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 740, Tc = 430 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 430/740) * 100 | Answer: 41.89 %

question: A refrigerator works between 252 K (cold) and 318 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 252, Th = 318 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 252 / (318 - 252) | Answer: 3.818

question: A heat pump operates between 262 K and 330 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 262, Th = 330 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 330 / (330 - 262) | Answer: 4.853

question: 7.2 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 55 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 7.2, dT = 55 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 7.2 * 0.718 * 55 | Answer: 284.3 kJ

question: 1 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 175 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1, dT = 175 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 1 * 1.005 * 175 | Answer: 175.9 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 1 m^3 at 340 K with mass 5.9 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 1, Tk = 340, m = 5.9 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 5.9*0.287*340 / 1 | Answer: 575.7 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 4.6 kg of air expands isothermally at 370 K from volume V1 to 4*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.6, Tk = 370, ratio = 4 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 4.6*0.287*370*ln(4) | Answer: 677.2 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 4.9 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.17 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 4.9, D = 0.17 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*4.9*0.17 / 0.001 | Answer: 833000

question: Water flows at 0.9 m/s through a pipe of diameter 270 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 11.7 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 11.7 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*11.7 / 1000 | Answer: 114.8 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 6.7 m. Taking Cv = 0.98, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 6.7, cv = 0.98 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.98*sqrt(2*9.81*6.7) | Answer: 11.24 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 360 mm) water flows at 2.1 m/s. It contracts to diameter 130 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 360, d2 = 130, V1 = 2.1 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 2.1*(360/130)^2 | Answer: 16.1 m/s

question: Water flows at 3 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.35 m and length 360 m. With friction factor f = 0.036, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 23 teeth drives a gear of 58 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1150 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 23, z2 = 58, N1 = 1150 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1150*23 / 58 | Answer: 456 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 130 mm rotates at 500 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 130, N = 500 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.13)*500 / 60 | Answer: 3.403 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 25.7 kW at 1250 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 25.7, N = 1250 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(25.7*1000) / (2*pi*1250) | Answer: 196.3 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 4.6 kg rotates at radius 0.55 m at 850 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 13800 N/m and mass 12.3 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 13800, m = 12.3 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(13800/12.3) | Answer: 5.331 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 9 m^2 and thickness 0.15 m has conductivity k = 29.7 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 60 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 9, L = 0.15, k = 29.7, dT = 60 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 29.7*9*60 / 0.15 | Answer: 106920 W

question: A surface of area 2.7 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 185 W/m^2-K to surroundings 95 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 2.7, h = 185, dT = 95 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 185*2.7*95 | Answer: 47453 W

question: In a counter-flow heat exchanger the terminal temperature differences are 45 deg C and 15 deg C. Find the log mean temperature difference (LMTD) in deg C.
solution: Given: dT1 = 45, dT2 = 15 | Formula: LMTD = (dT1 - dT2) / ln(dT1/dT2) | Substitute: LMTD = (45 - 15) / ln(45/15) | Answer: 27.31 deg C

question: In turning, cutting speed = 180 m/min, feed = 0.35 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2.7 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 180, f = 0.35, d = 2.7 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*180*0.35*2.7 | Answer: 170100 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 470 mm is turned at 1100 rpm with a feed of 0.14 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 470, N = 1100, f = 0.14 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 470 / (0.14*1100) | Answer: 3.052 min

question: A resistor of 54 ohm carries a current of 5.8 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 54, I = 5.8 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 5.8 * 54 | Answer: 313.2 V

question: Three resistors 8 ohm, 88 ohm and 19 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 8, R2 = 88, R3 = 19 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 8 + 88 + 19 | Answer: 115 ohm

question: Two resistors 52 ohm and 80 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 52, R2 = 80 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 52*80 / (52+80) | Answer: 31.52 ohm

question: A device draws 3.6 A at 130 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 130, I = 3.6 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 130 * 3.6 | Answer: 468 W

question: A current of 11.7 A flows through a 61 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 11.7, R = 61 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (11.7)^2 * 61 | Answer: 835 W

question: Two capacitors 28.4 uF and 21.1 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 28.4, C2 = 21.1 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 28.4*21.1 / (28.4+21.1) | Answer: 12.11 uF

question: A resistor 72 kohm and capacitor 11.1 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 72, C = 11.1 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (72k)(11.1u) = 799.2 ms | Answer: 799.2 ms

question: An inductor 160.4 mH is in series with 91 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 160.4, R = 91 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (160.4e-3) / 91 | Answer: 1.763 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 56.2 mH inductor at 410 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 56.2, f = 410 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (410)(56.2e-3) | Answer: 144.8 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 40.2 uF capacitor at 50 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 40.2, f = 50 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (50)(40.2e-6)) | Answer: 79.18 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 22 ohm, XL = 150 ohm and XC = 26 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 22, XL = 150, XC = 26 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(22^2 + (150 - 26)^2) | Answer: 125.9 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 91.5 mH and C = 0.6 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 91.5, C = 0.6 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(91.5e-3 * 0.6e-6)) | Answer: 679.3 Hz

question: A capacitor of 54.4 uF is charged to 90 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 54.4, V = 90 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*54.4e-6*(90)^2 | Answer: 220.3 mJ

question: An alternating voltage has a peak value of 246 V. Find its RMS value.
solution: Given: Vp = 246 | Formula: Vrms = Vp / sqrt(2) | Substitute: Vrms = 246 / sqrt(2) | Answer: 173.9 V

question: A transformer has primary voltage 360 V with 270 primary turns and 60 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 360, N1 = 270, N2 = 60 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 360 * 60/270 | Answer: 80 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 160 V and draws an armature current of 6 A. If the armature resistance is 0.52 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 160, Ia = 6, Ra = 0.52 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 160 - 6*0.52 | Answer: 156.9 V

question: A 4-pole induction motor on a 50 Hz supply runs at 900 rpm. Find the slip (%).
formula: s = (Ns - N) / Ns,  Ns = 120 f / P

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 160 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.86. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 160, VL = 400, pf = 0.86 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*400*160*0.86 / 1000 | Answer: 95.33 kW

question: A load has real power 15 kW and apparent power 110 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 15, S = 110 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 15 / 110 | Answer: 0.1364

question: A machine delivers 70 kW output while drawing 122 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 70, Pi = 122 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 70/122 * 100 | Answer: 57.38 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 30 V across R1 = 45 ohm and R2 = 5 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 30, R1 = 45, R2 = 5 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 30*5 / (45+5) | Answer: 3 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 130 kohm and Rin = 8 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 130, Rin = 8 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 130 / 8 | Answer: 16.25

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 110 kohm and Rg = 10 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 110, Rg = 10 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 110/10 | Answer: 12

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 9021. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 9021 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(9021) | Answer: 39.55 dB

question: A first-order system has a time constant of 1.2 s. Find the time (in s) to reach 63.2% of its final value.
solution: For a first-order step response, y = 1 - e^(-t/tau) | y = 0.632 when t = tau | Answer: 1.2 s
formula: At t = tau the response reaches 63.2% (one time constant)

question: A signal is sampled at 94 kHz. According to the Nyquist criterion, what is the maximum signal frequency that can be represented (in kHz)?
solution: Given: fs = 94 | Formula: f_max = fs / 2 | Substitute: f_max = 94 / 2 | Answer: 47 kHz

question: A simply supported beam of span 5.4 m carries a central point load of 95 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.4, W = 95 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 95*5.4 / 4 | Answer: 128.2 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 3.7 m carries a UDL of 20 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.7, w = 20 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 20*(3.7)^2 / 8 | Answer: 34.23 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 3.1 m carries a point load 50 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.1, W = 50 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 50*3.1 | Answer: 155 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 4.2 m carries a UDL of 22 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.2, w = 22 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 22*(4.2)^2 / 2 | Answer: 194 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 8.2 m carries a point load 35 kN at distance 1.5 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 8.2, a = 1.5, W = 35 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 35*(8.2 - 1.5) / 8.2 | Answer: 28.6 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 5.6 m) carries a central point load 60 kN. With E = 200 GPa and I = 560e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=60000 N, L=5600.0 mm, E=200000 MPa, I=560e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 1.96 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 7.1 m carries a UDL of 36 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7.1, w = 36 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 36*(7.1)^2 / 12 | Answer: 151.2 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 510 mm, clear cover 35 mm and main bars of diameter 25 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 510, c = 35, dia = 25 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 510 - 35 - 25/2 | Answer: 462.5 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 39.6 m^2 carrying a factored load of 11.3 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 39.6, w = 11.3 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 11.3 * 39.6 | Answer: 447.5 kN

question: For a bar of diameter 16 mm with design bond stress 2 MPa and steel stress 435 MPa, find the development length in mm.
solution: Given: dia = 16, tbd = 2, fs = 435 | Formula: Ld = phi fs / (4 tau_bd) | Substitute: Ld = 16*435 / (4*2) | Answer: 870 mm

question: A soil sample has porosity n = 0.3. Find its void ratio e.
solution: Given: n = 0.3 | Formula: e = n / (1 - n) | Substitute: e = 0.3 / (1 - 0.3) | Answer: 0.4286

question: A cohesionless soil has an angle of internal friction phi = 28 degrees. Find Rankine's coefficient of active earth pressure Ka.
solution: Given: phi = 28 | Formula: Ka = (1 - sin phi) / (1 + sin phi) | Substitute: Ka = (1 - sin28) / (1 + sin28) | Answer: 0.361

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 4.4 m, unit weight 20 kN/m^3, phi = 29 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 7.4 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 18 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 7.4, g = 18 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (18 - 9.81)*7.4 | Answer: 60.61 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 7.2e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.4, area = 2.2e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 7.2, i = 0.4, A = 2.2 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (7.2e-4)*0.4*(2.2e-3) | Answer: 633.6 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.9 m, bed slope 0.007 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.028. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 3.9 m under a head of 0.5 m. Taking Cd = 0.62 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 4.4 m wide carries a discharge of 28.9 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 220 m and design speed 75 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 220, V = 75 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (75)^2 / (127*220) | Answer: 0.2013
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: For a design speed of 65 km/h with allowable superelevation 0.07 and lateral friction 0.14, find the minimum curve radius in m.
A tank of volume 620 m^3 treats a flow of 95 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 620, Q = 95 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 620 / 95 | Answer: 6.526 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 210 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.28 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 6 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 210, k = 0.28, t = 6 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 210*(1 - e^(-0.28*6)) | Answer: 170.9 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.62, rainfall intensity 95 mm/h over a catchment of 47.1 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.62, i = 95, A = 47.1 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.62*95*47.1 / 360 | Answer: 7.706 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.06 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 310 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.06, M = 310 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 310*(20+0.06)/20 | Answer: 310.9 m

question: Convert the decimal number 168 to binary.
solution: Divide 168 by 2 repeatedly, recording remainders | Reading remainders in reverse gives 10101000 | Answer: 10101000 (binary)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 2 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the decimal number 1105 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 1105 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 451 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the 8-bit binary number 11101011 to decimal.
solution: Binary 11101011 = sum of bit-weights | Answer: 235 (decimal)
formula: Sum each bit times its positional weight (2^i)

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 10110101 and 10000111.
solution: XOR: 00110010 | Count of 1s = 3 | Answer: 3
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: An IPv4 subnet uses a /24 prefix. How many usable host addresses does it provide?
solution: Given: prefix = 24 | Formula: hosts = 2^(32 - prefix) - 2 | Substitute: hosts = 2^(32 - 24) - 2 | Answer: 254

question: A file of 230 megabits is sent over a link of 87 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 230, B = 87 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 230 / 87 | Answer: 2.644 s

question: A link has bandwidth 49 Mbps and round-trip time 170 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 49, R = 170 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 49e6 * 170e-3 bits = 8330 kb | Answer: 8330 kilobits

question: A channel has bandwidth 19 kHz. Using Nyquist's theorem with 2 signal levels, find the maximum data rate in kbps (noiseless).
solution: Given: B = 19, M = 2 | Formula: C = 2 B log2(M) | Substitute: C = 2*19*log2(2) | Answer: 38 kbps

question: A channel of bandwidth 20 kHz has a signal-to-noise ratio of 255 (linear). Using Shannon's theorem, find the channel capacity in kbps.
solution: Given: B = 20, SNR = 255 | Formula: C = B log2(1 + SNR) | Substitute: C = 20*log2(1 + 255) | Answer: 160 kbps

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.82, cache access time 9 ns and main-memory access time 110 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.82, tc = 9, tm = 110 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.82*9 + (1 - 0.82)*110 | Answer: 27.18 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 945527 elements?
solution: Given: n = 945527 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(945527)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: An O(n^2) algorithm performs c*n^2 basic operations. If c = 1 and n = 2590, how many operations are performed?
solution: Given: n = 2590 | Formula: operations = n^2 | Substitute: = (2590)^2 | Answer: 6708100

question: A program is 95% parallelisable and run on 16 processors. Using Amdahl's law, find the maximum speedup.
solution: Parallel fraction f = 0.95 | S = 1 / ((1 - 0.95) + 0.95/16) | Answer: 9.143x speedup

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.013, memory access time 160 ns and page-fault service time 3 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 3 ms = 3000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.013)*160 + 0.013*3000000.0 ns | Answer: 39.16 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: A digital-to-analog converter has 8 bits and a full-scale output of 5 V. Find its resolution (voltage per step) in mV.
solution: Given: n = 8, Vfs = 5 | Formula: resolution = Vfs / (2^n - 1) | Substitute: resolution = 5 / (2^8 - 1) | Answer: 19.61 mV

question: A modem transmits at 3900 baud using 2-level signalling. Find the bit rate in bps.
solution: Given: baud = 3900, M = 2 | Formula: bit rate = baud * log2(M) | Substitute: bit rate = 3900 * log2(2) | Answer: 3900 bps

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 2.6 m^3 at 240 kPa and 600 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 2.6, P = 240, Tk = 600 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (240e3)*2.6 / (8.314*600) | Answer: 125.1 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.2 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 2 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.2, t = 2 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.2*2) | Answer: 0.3297

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.18 /min) is to reach 85% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.18, X = 85 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.85) / 0.18 | Answer: 10.54 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.27 /min) reaches 65% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.27, X = 65 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.65 / (0.27*(1 - 0.65)) | Answer: 6.878 min

question: A first-order reaction has a rate constant of 0.2 /min. Find its half-life in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.2 | Formula: t_half = ln(2) / k | Substitute: t_half = 0.6931 / 0.2 | Answer: 3.466 min

question: For a reaction with A = 3e10 /s and activation energy 50 kJ/mol at 450 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 3, Ea = 50, Tk = 450 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 3e10 * exp(-50e3 / (8.314*450)) | Answer: 47105 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.98 and bottoms xW = 0.1, with relative volatility alpha = 2.4. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.98, xw = 0.1, al = 2.4 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.98/0.02)(0.9/0.1)] / ln(2.4) | Answer: 6.955 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.83 and x = 0.4. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.83, x = 0.4 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.83/0.17) / (0.4/0.6) | Answer: 7.324

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.2 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 45 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.2, Psat = 45 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.2 * 45 | Answer: 9 kPa

question: A stream of 6.2 kg/s with specific heat 2.1 kJ/kg-K is heated through 65 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 6.2, cp = 2.1, dT = 65 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 6.2*2.1*65 | Answer: 846.3 kW

question: A reactor of volume 5.1 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 5 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 5.1, Q = 5 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 5.1 / 5 | Answer: 1.02 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 3.6e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 3 mm with a concentration difference of 20 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 3.6, L = 3, dC = 20 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (3.6e-9)*20 / (3e-3) | Answer: 24 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 5.9 min and steady-state gain 3.9. For a step input of magnitude 20, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 5.9, K = 3.9, M = 20 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 3.9 * 20 | Answer: 78 units

question: A reactor operates at a space time of 17 min. Find its space velocity in per hour.
solution: Given: tau = 17 | Formula: SV = 60 / tau  (per hour) | Substitute: SV = 60 / 17 | Answer: 3.529 /h

question: An aircraft wing of area 110 m^2 flies at 60 m/s (air density 1 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.7. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 110, V = 60, rho = 1, CL = 0.7 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1*(60)^2*110*0.7 / 1000 | Answer: 138.6 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 15 m^2 flies at 170 m/s (density 0.4 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.08. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 15, V = 170, rho = 0.4, CD = 0.08 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.4*(170)^2*15*0.08 / 1000 | Answer: 6.936 kN

question: Find the dynamic pressure for air of density 1 kg/m^3 moving at 70 m/s, in Pa.
solution: Given: rho = 1, V = 70 | Formula: q = 0.5 rho V^2 | Substitute: q = 0.5*1*(70)^2 | Answer: 2450 Pa

question: An aircraft flies at 540 m/s where the speed of sound is 295 m/s. Find the Mach number.
solution: Given: V = 540, a = 295 | Formula: M = V / a | Substitute: M = 540 / 295 | Answer: 1.831

question: Find the circular orbital velocity of a satellite at altitude 1400 km above Earth (Earth radius 6371 km, mu = 3.986e14 m^3/s^2), in km/s.
A specimen under stress 220 MPa shows an elastic strain of 2.6e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 220, eps = 2.6 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 220 / (2.6e-3) MPa = 84.62 GPa | Answer: 84.62 GPa

question: A block of mass 23 kg has a volume of 1.8e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 23, V = 1.8 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 23 / (1.8e-3) | Answer: 12778 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 1600 mm is heated through 65 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 17e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 1600, dT = 65, al = 17 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 1600*17e-6*65 | Answer: 1.768 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 10 ohm, R2 = 55 ohm and R3 = 490 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 10, R2 = 55, R3 = 490 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 55*490 / 10 | Answer: 2695 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 1000 ohm and gauge factor 2 experiences a strain of 250e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 1000, GF = 2, eps = 250 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 1000*2*250e-6 | Answer: 500 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 9.84 when the true value is 50. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.84, true = 50 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.84 - 50| / 50 * 100 | Answer: 80.32 %

question: Annual demand is 41000 units, ordering cost 170 per order and holding cost 26 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 41000, S = 170, H = 26 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*41000*170 / 26) | Answer: 732.2 units

question: An asset costs 190000 with salvage value 14000 after 8 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 190000, Sv = 14000, n = 8 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (190000 - 14000) / 8 | Answer: 22000 per year

question: A product sells for 230 per unit with variable cost 100 per unit and fixed costs 175000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 230, V = 100, F = 175000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 175000 / (230 - 100) | Answer: 1346 units

question: Find the present worth of 100000 received 8 years from now at an interest rate of 7% per year.
solution: Given: F = 100000, n = 8, i = 7 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 100000 / (1 + 0.07)^8 | Answer: 58201 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.97, 0.9 and 0.94 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.97, r2 = 0.9, r3 = 0.94 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.97*0.9*0.94 | Answer: 0.8206

question: Two components each of reliability 0.83 are connected in parallel. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r = 0.83 | Formula: R_parallel = 1 - (1 - r)^2 | Substitute: R = 1 - (1 - 0.83)^2 | Answer: 0.9711

question: A process produces 11 defective items in a batch of 8500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 11, N = 8500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 11/8500 * 1e6 | Answer: 1294 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -5x^3 + 5x^2 + x + 3 evaluated at x = 1.
For f(x) = 2x^3 - 4x^2 + 1, find f''(x) at x = 0.
Evaluate the definite integral of (-4x^2 + 5x - 5) dx from x = -2 to x = 3.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = -4x^3/3 + 5x^2/2 + -5x | Evaluate F(3) - F(-2) | Answer: -59.17
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 4x^2 + x - 7 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[-4, 8], [-8, -4]].
solution: Given: a = -4, b = 8, c = -8, d = -4 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (-4)(-4) - (8)(-8) | Answer: 80

question: Find the determinant of [[-1, -1, -2], [4, -5, 2], [6, -4, -1]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: -57

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[-8, 0], [3, 3]].
solution: Trace tr = -5, Determinant = -24 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 3

question: Solve for x: -6x + -1y = -3 and -5x + -5y = 0.
solution: Determinant = -6*-5 - -1*-5 = 25 | x = (e d - b f) / det = 0.6 | Answer: x = 0.6
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 43, 13, 2, 83, 62.
solution: Sum = 203 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 40.6 | Answer: 40.6

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 26, 48, 44, 33, 23.
solution: Mean = 34.8 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 10.94

question: Find the slope of the line through (6, 6) and (7, -9).
solution: Given: x1 = 6, y1 = 6, x2 = 7, y2 = -9 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (-9 - 6) / (7 - 6) | Answer: -15

question: Find the distance between the points (4, -8) and (0, -4).
solution: Given: x1 = 4, y1 = -8, x2 = 0, y2 = -4 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-4)^2 + (4)^2) | Answer: 5.657 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (6,6), (-6,3), (2,-7).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 72 sq units

question: Evaluate the number of combinations C(15, 11).
solution: Given: n = 15, r = 11 | Formula: C(n, r) = n! / (r! (n - r)!) | Substitute: C(15, 11) = 15! / (11! * 4!) | Answer: 1365

question: Evaluate the number of permutations P(9, 7).
solution: Given: n = 9, r = 7 | Formula: P(n, r) = n! / (n - r)! | Substitute: P(9, 7) = 9! / 2! | Answer: 181440

question: Find the 7th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -6 and common difference 6.
solution: Given: a = -6, d = 6, n = 7 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -6 + (7 - 1)*6 | Answer: 30

question: Find the sum of the first 38 terms of an AP with first term -11 and common difference -8.
Find the 3th term of a geometric progression with first term 4 and common ratio 2.
solution: Given: a = 4, r = 2, n = 3 | Formula: a_n = a r^(n-1) | Substitute: a_n = 4 * 2^(3-1) | Answer: 16

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 1000 at 12.2% per annum for 4 years.
solution: Given: P = 1000, R = 12.2, Tt = 4 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 1000 * 12.2 * 4 / 100 | Answer: 488 currency units

question: Find the amount when 12000 is invested at 10.4% per annum compounded annually for 6 years.
solution: Given: P = 12000, R = 10.4, Tt = 6 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 12000 * (1 + 10.4/100)^6 | Answer: 21727 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (-5, -3, 4) and (3, 2, -1).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (-5, 2, 2) and (5, 0, -2).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 10.77

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (-4, -3, 3) and (4, -4, 6).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 73.07 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number 2 + -1i.
solution: Given: a = 2, b = -1 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((2)^2 + (-1)^2) | Answer: 2.236

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number 4 + -7i.
solution: Given: a = 4, b = -7 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(-7, 4) | Answer: -60.26 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = 4x^3 + 6x + 1 at x = -5.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-40 with initial guess x0=5, find x1 (one iteration).
solution: Given: N = 40, x0 = 5 | Formula: x1 = x0 - (x0^2 - N)/(2 x0) | Substitute: x1 = 5 - ((5)^2 - 40)/(2*5) | Answer: 6.5

question: Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.9 and ordinates 0, 14, 1, 12, 8, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 197 and 119.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 197 and 119 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 25 and 74.
solution: Given: a = 25, b = 74 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 25*74 / 1 | Answer: 1850
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 27 mm carries an axial tensile load of 109 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 29 mm and length 2400 mm carries an axial load of 22 kN. Take E = 200 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 80 mm transmits a torque of 1650 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 80, Tt = 1650 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(1650*1000) / (pi*(80)^3) | Answer: 16.41 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 54 mm and length 1300 mm carries a torque of 2000 N-m. With G = 80 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (54)^4 / 32 = 834786 mm^4 | theta = (2000*1000)(1300) / (80000 * 834786) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 2.231 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 76 mm wide and 240 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 76, h = 240 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 76*(240)^2 / 6 | Answer: 729600 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (81 mm x 260 mm) carries a bending moment of 22 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (69 mm x 90 mm) has effective length 3200 mm and E = 200 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 430 MPa is designed for a working stress of 180 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 430, sw = 180 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 430 / 180 | Answer: 2.389

question: A steel bar is fully restrained and heated through 40 deg C. With E = 200 GPa and alpha = 11e-6 /deg C, find the thermal stress in MPa.
solution: Given: dT = 40, E = 200, al = 11 | Formula: sigma = E alpha (dT) | Substitute: sigma = 200000 * 11e-6 * 40 | Answer: 88 MPa

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 600 mm and wall thickness 19 mm carries an internal pressure of 1.7 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 600, t = 19, P = 1.7 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 1.7*600 / (2*19) | Answer: 26.84 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 1000 K and 430 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 1000, Tc = 430 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 430/1000) * 100 | Answer: 57 %

question: A refrigerator works between 262 K (cold) and 310 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 262, Th = 310 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 262 / (310 - 262) | Answer: 5.458

question: A heat pump operates between 284 K and 332 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 284, Th = 332 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 332 / (332 - 284) | Answer: 6.917

question: 1.6 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 185 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1.6, dT = 185 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 1.6 * 0.718 * 185 | Answer: 212.5 kJ

question: 3.9 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 55 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.9, dT = 55 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 3.9 * 1.005 * 55 | Answer: 215.6 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 4 m^3 at 390 K with mass 1.1 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 4, Tk = 390, m = 1.1 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 1.1*0.287*390 / 4 | Answer: 30.78 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 2 kg of air expands isothermally at 470 K from volume V1 to 5*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2, Tk = 470, ratio = 5 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 2*0.287*470*ln(5) | Answer: 434.2 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 2.1 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.06 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 2.1, D = 0.06 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*2.1*0.06 / 0.001 | Answer: 126000

question: Water flows at 0.8 m/s through a pipe of diameter 230 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 26.3 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 26.3 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*26.3 / 1000 | Answer: 258 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 4 m. Taking Cv = 0.97, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 4, cv = 0.97 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.97*sqrt(2*9.81*4) | Answer: 8.593 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 230 mm) water flows at 2.1 m/s. It contracts to diameter 100 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
Water flows at 3.1 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.32 m and length 200 m. With friction factor f = 0.036, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 32 teeth drives a gear of 50 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1000 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 32, z2 = 50, N1 = 1000 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1000*32 / 50 | Answer: 640 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 100 mm rotates at 700 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 100, N = 700 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.1)*700 / 60 | Answer: 3.665 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 4 kW at 1050 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 4, N = 1050 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(4*1000) / (2*pi*1050) | Answer: 36.38 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 4 kg rotates at radius 0.54 m at 550 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 19900 N/m and mass 8.1 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 19900, m = 8.1 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(19900/8.1) | Answer: 7.889 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 4.7 m^2 and thickness 0.35 m has conductivity k = 21.5 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 95 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 4.7, L = 0.35, k = 21.5, dT = 95 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 21.5*4.7*95 / 0.35 | Answer: 27428 W

question: A surface of area 0.9 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 75 W/m^2-K to surroundings 85 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 0.9, h = 75, dT = 85 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 75*0.9*85 | Answer: 5738 W

question: In a counter-flow heat exchanger the terminal temperature differences are 40 deg C and 15 deg C. Find the log mean temperature difference (LMTD) in deg C.
solution: Given: dT1 = 40, dT2 = 15 | Formula: LMTD = (dT1 - dT2) / ln(dT1/dT2) | Substitute: LMTD = (40 - 15) / ln(40/15) | Answer: 25.49 deg C

question: In turning, cutting speed = 170 m/min, feed = 0.42 mm/rev, depth of cut = 0.5 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 170, f = 0.42, d = 0.5 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*170*0.42*0.5 | Answer: 35700 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 190 mm is turned at 600 rpm with a feed of 0.16 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 190, N = 600, f = 0.16 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 190 / (0.16*600) | Answer: 1.979 min

question: A resistor of 21 ohm carries a current of 0.7 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 21, I = 0.7 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 0.7 * 21 | Answer: 14.7 V

question: Three resistors 53 ohm, 46 ohm and 94 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 53, R2 = 46, R3 = 94 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 53 + 46 + 94 | Answer: 193 ohm

question: Two resistors 119 ohm and 37 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 119, R2 = 37 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 119*37 / (119+37) | Answer: 28.22 ohm

question: A device draws 3.4 A at 65 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 65, I = 3.4 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 65 * 3.4 | Answer: 221 W

question: A current of 6 A flows through a 36 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 6, R = 36 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (6)^2 * 36 | Answer: 1296 W

question: Two capacitors 15.2 uF and 1.2 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 15.2, C2 = 1.2 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 15.2*1.2 / (15.2+1.2) | Answer: 1.112 uF

question: A resistor 86 kohm and capacitor 1.9 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 86, C = 1.9 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (86k)(1.9u) = 163.4 ms | Answer: 163.4 ms

question: An inductor 167.1 mH is in series with 185 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 167.1, R = 185 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (167.1e-3) / 185 | Answer: 0.9032 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 64.3 mH inductor at 340 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 64.3, f = 340 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (340)(64.3e-3) | Answer: 137.4 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 35.5 uF capacitor at 930 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 35.5, f = 930 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (930)(35.5e-6)) | Answer: 4.821 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 35 ohm, XL = 134 ohm and XC = 57 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 35, XL = 134, XC = 57 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(35^2 + (134 - 57)^2) | Answer: 84.58 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 30.4 mH and C = 7.5 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 30.4, C = 7.5 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(30.4e-3 * 7.5e-6)) | Answer: 333.3 Hz

question: A capacitor of 19.1 uF is charged to 285 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 19.1, V = 285 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*19.1e-6*(285)^2 | Answer: 775.7 mJ

question: An alternating voltage has a peak value of 56 V. Find its RMS value.
solution: Given: Vp = 56 | Formula: Vrms = Vp / sqrt(2) | Substitute: Vrms = 56 / sqrt(2) | Answer: 39.6 V

question: A transformer has primary voltage 180 V with 930 primary turns and 500 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 180, N1 = 930, N2 = 500 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 180 * 500/930 | Answer: 96.77 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 120 V and draws an armature current of 41 A. If the armature resistance is 1.49 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 120, Ia = 41, Ra = 1.49 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 120 - 41*1.49 | Answer: 58.91 V

question: A 4-pole induction motor on a 60 Hz supply runs at 1050 rpm. Find the slip (%).
formula: s = (Ns - N) / Ns,  Ns = 120 f / P

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 30 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.96. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 30, VL = 400, pf = 0.96 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*400*30*0.96 / 1000 | Answer: 19.95 kW

question: A load has real power 75 kW and apparent power 190 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 75, S = 190 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 75 / 190 | Answer: 0.3947

question: A machine delivers 50 kW output while drawing 167 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 50, Pi = 167 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 50/167 * 100 | Answer: 29.94 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 27 V across R1 = 30 ohm and R2 = 16 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 27, R1 = 30, R2 = 16 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 27*16 / (30+16) | Answer: 9.391 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 100 kohm and Rin = 24 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 100, Rin = 24 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 100 / 24 | Answer: 4.167

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 50 kohm and Rg = 10 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 50, Rg = 10 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 50/10 | Answer: 6

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 8609. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 8609 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(8609) | Answer: 39.35 dB

question: A first-order system has a time constant of 4.5 s. Find the time (in s) to reach 63.2% of its final value.
solution: For a first-order step response, y = 1 - e^(-t/tau) | y = 0.632 when t = tau | Answer: 4.5 s
formula: At t = tau the response reaches 63.2% (one time constant)

question: A signal is sampled at 70 kHz. According to the Nyquist criterion, what is the maximum signal frequency that can be represented (in kHz)?
solution: Given: fs = 70 | Formula: f_max = fs / 2 | Substitute: f_max = 70 / 2 | Answer: 35 kHz

question: A simply supported beam of span 7.5 m carries a central point load of 65 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7.5, W = 65 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 65*7.5 / 4 | Answer: 121.9 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 3.9 m carries a UDL of 60 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.9, w = 60 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 60*(3.9)^2 / 8 | Answer: 114.1 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 4.5 m carries a point load 10 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.5, W = 10 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 10*4.5 | Answer: 45 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 3.9 m carries a UDL of 40 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.9, w = 40 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 40*(3.9)^2 / 2 | Answer: 304.2 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.2 m carries a point load 15 kN at distance 1 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 4.2, a = 1, W = 15 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 15*(4.2 - 1) / 4.2 | Answer: 11.43 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 4.3 m) carries a central point load 50 kN. With E = 30 GPa and I = 280e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=50000 N, L=4300.0 mm, E=30000 MPa, I=280e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 9.859 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 7.6 m carries a UDL of 33 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7.6, w = 33 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 33*(7.6)^2 / 12 | Answer: 158.8 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 550 mm, clear cover 45 mm and main bars of diameter 20 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 550, c = 45, dia = 20 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 550 - 45 - 20/2 | Answer: 495 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 39.5 m^2 carrying a factored load of 8.2 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 39.5, w = 8.2 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 8.2 * 39.5 | Answer: 323.9 kN

question: For a bar of diameter 20 mm with design bond stress 1.5 MPa and steel stress 360 MPa, find the development length in mm.
solution: Given: dia = 20, tbd = 1.5, fs = 360 | Formula: Ld = phi fs / (4 tau_bd) | Substitute: Ld = 20*360 / (4*1.5) | Answer: 1200 mm

question: A soil sample has porosity n = 0.35. Find its void ratio e.
solution: Given: n = 0.35 | Formula: e = n / (1 - n) | Substitute: e = 0.35 / (1 - 0.35) | Answer: 0.5385

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 4.8 m, unit weight 19 kN/m^3, phi = 28 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 10.5 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 21 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 10.5, g = 21 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (21 - 9.81)*10.5 | Answer: 117.5 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 4.3e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.3, area = 3.4e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 4.3, i = 0.3, A = 3.4 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (4.3e-4)*0.3*(3.4e-3) | Answer: 438.6 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 2 m, bed slope 0.007 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.019. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 1.1 m under a head of 0.5 m. Taking Cd = 0.62 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 5.7 m wide carries a discharge of 17.5 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 130 m and design speed 40 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 130, V = 40 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (40)^2 / (127*130) | Answer: 0.09691
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: For a design speed of 95 km/h with allowable superelevation 0.08 and lateral friction 0.12, find the minimum curve radius in m.
A tank of volume 920 m^3 treats a flow of 100 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 920, Q = 100 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 920 / 100 | Answer: 9.2 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 150 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.18 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 3 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 150, k = 0.18, t = 3 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 150*(1 - e^(-0.18*3)) | Answer: 62.59 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.65, rainfall intensity 110 mm/h over a catchment of 15.9 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.65, i = 110, A = 15.9 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.65*110*15.9 / 360 | Answer: 3.158 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.07 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 580 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.07, M = 580 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 580*(20+0.07)/20 | Answer: 582 m

question: Convert the decimal number 183 to binary.
solution: Divide 183 by 2 repeatedly, recording remainders | Reading remainders in reverse gives 10110111 | Answer: 10110111 (binary)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 2 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the decimal number 1330 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 1330 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 532 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the 8-bit binary number 00110100 to decimal.
solution: Binary 00110100 = sum of bit-weights | Answer: 52 (decimal)
formula: Sum each bit times its positional weight (2^i)

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 11100101 and 11011101.
solution: XOR: 00111000 | Count of 1s = 3 | Answer: 3
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 210 megabits is sent over a link of 38 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 210, B = 38 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 210 / 38 | Answer: 5.526 s

question: A link has bandwidth 76 Mbps and round-trip time 160 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 76, R = 160 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 76e6 * 160e-3 bits = 12160 kb | Answer: 12160 kilobits

question: A channel has bandwidth 16 kHz. Using Nyquist's theorem with 2 signal levels, find the maximum data rate in kbps (noiseless).
solution: Given: B = 16, M = 2 | Formula: C = 2 B log2(M) | Substitute: C = 2*16*log2(2) | Answer: 32 kbps

question: A channel of bandwidth 14 kHz has a signal-to-noise ratio of 7 (linear). Using Shannon's theorem, find the channel capacity in kbps.
solution: Given: B = 14, SNR = 7 | Formula: C = B log2(1 + SNR) | Substitute: C = 14*log2(1 + 7) | Answer: 42 kbps

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.88, cache access time 10 ns and main-memory access time 190 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.88, tc = 10, tm = 190 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.88*10 + (1 - 0.88)*190 | Answer: 31.6 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 472927 elements?
solution: Given: n = 472927 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(472927)) + 1 | Answer: 19

question: An O(n^2) algorithm performs c*n^2 basic operations. If c = 1 and n = 1660, how many operations are performed?
solution: Given: n = 1660 | Formula: operations = n^2 | Substitute: = (1660)^2 | Answer: 2755600

question: A program is 60% parallelisable and run on 8 processors. Using Amdahl's law, find the maximum speedup.
solution: Parallel fraction f = 0.6 | S = 1 / ((1 - 0.6) + 0.6/8) | Answer: 2.105x speedup

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.013, memory access time 90 ns and page-fault service time 9 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 9 ms = 9000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.013)*90 + 0.013*9000000.0 ns | Answer: 117.1 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: A digital-to-analog converter has 11 bits and a full-scale output of 5 V. Find its resolution (voltage per step) in mV.
solution: Given: n = 11, Vfs = 5 | Formula: resolution = Vfs / (2^n - 1) | Substitute: resolution = 5 / (2^11 - 1) | Answer: 2.443 mV

question: A modem transmits at 2400 baud using 16-level signalling. Find the bit rate in bps.
solution: Given: baud = 2400, M = 16 | Formula: bit rate = baud * log2(M) | Substitute: bit rate = 2400 * log2(16) | Answer: 9600 bps

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 0.7 m^3 at 210 kPa and 560 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 0.7, P = 210, Tk = 560 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (210e3)*0.7 / (8.314*560) | Answer: 31.57 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.27 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 10 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.27, t = 10 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.27*10) | Answer: 0.9328

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.37 /min) is to reach 80% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.37, X = 80 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.8) / 0.37 | Answer: 4.35 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.43 /min) reaches 65% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.43, X = 65 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.65 / (0.43*(1 - 0.65)) | Answer: 4.319 min

question: A first-order reaction has a rate constant of 0.39 /min. Find its half-life in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.39 | Formula: t_half = ln(2) / k | Substitute: t_half = 0.6931 / 0.39 | Answer: 1.777 min

question: For a reaction with A = 3e10 /s and activation energy 50 kJ/mol at 360 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 3, Ea = 50, Tk = 360 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 3e10 * exp(-50e3 / (8.314*360)) | Answer: 1667 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.94 and bottoms xW = 0.04, with relative volatility alpha = 2.2. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.94, xw = 0.04, al = 2.2 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.94/0.06)(0.96/0.04)] / ln(2.2) | Answer: 7.52 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.8 and x = 0.21. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.8, x = 0.21 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.8/0.2) / (0.21/0.79) | Answer: 15.05

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.65 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 80 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.65, Psat = 80 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.65 * 80 | Answer: 52 kPa

question: A stream of 6.4 kg/s with specific heat 3.8 kJ/kg-K is heated through 40 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 6.4, cp = 3.8, dT = 40 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 6.4*3.8*40 | Answer: 972.8 kW

question: A reactor of volume 15.3 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 1 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 15.3, Q = 1 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 15.3 / 1 | Answer: 15.3 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 6.7e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 5 mm with a concentration difference of 80 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 6.7, L = 5, dC = 80 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (6.7e-9)*80 / (5e-3) | Answer: 107.2 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 8.5 min and steady-state gain 1.1. For a step input of magnitude 10, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 8.5, K = 1.1, M = 10 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 1.1 * 10 | Answer: 11 units

question: A reactor operates at a space time of 7.8 min. Find its space velocity in per hour.
solution: Given: tau = 7.8 | Formula: SV = 60 / tau  (per hour) | Substitute: SV = 60 / 7.8 | Answer: 7.692 /h

question: An aircraft wing of area 120 m^2 flies at 80 m/s (air density 1 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 1.1. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 120, V = 80, rho = 1, CL = 1.1 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1*(80)^2*120*1.1 / 1000 | Answer: 422.4 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 115 m^2 flies at 150 m/s (density 0.7 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.03. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 115, V = 150, rho = 0.7, CD = 0.03 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.7*(150)^2*115*0.03 / 1000 | Answer: 27.17 kN

question: Find the dynamic pressure for air of density 1 kg/m^3 moving at 270 m/s, in Pa.
solution: Given: rho = 1, V = 270 | Formula: q = 0.5 rho V^2 | Substitute: q = 0.5*1*(270)^2 | Answer: 36450 Pa

question: An aircraft flies at 290 m/s where the speed of sound is 295 m/s. Find the Mach number.

question: Find the circular orbital velocity of a satellite at altitude 1300 km above Earth (Earth radius 6371 km, mu = 3.986e14 m^3/s^2), in km/s.

question: A block of mass 10 kg has a volume of 5.2e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.

question: A rod of length 2600 mm is heated through 45 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 12e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 135 ohm, R2 = 190 ohm and R3 = 175 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 135, R2 = 190, R3 = 175 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 190*175 / 135 | Answer: 246.3 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 120 ohm and gauge factor 2 experiences a strain of 1150e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 120, GF = 2, eps = 1150 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 120*2*1150e-6 | Answer: 276 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 9.03 when the true value is 20. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.03, true = 20 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.03 - 20| / 20 * 100 | Answer: 54.85 %

question: Annual demand is 23500 units, ordering cost 40 per order and holding cost 28 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 23500, S = 40, H = 28 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*23500*40 / 28) | Answer: 259.1 units

question: An asset costs 320000 with salvage value 20000 after 6 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 320000, Sv = 20000, n = 6 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (320000 - 20000) / 6 | Answer: 50000 per year

question: A product sells for 370 per unit with variable cost 60 per unit and fixed costs 190000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 370, V = 60, F = 190000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 190000 / (370 - 60) | Answer: 612.9 units

question: Find the present worth of 180000 received 6 years from now at an interest rate of 8% per year.

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.93, 0.93 and 0.93 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.93, r2 = 0.93, r3 = 0.93 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.93*0.93*0.93 | Answer: 0.8044

question: Two components each of reliability 0.74 are connected in parallel. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r = 0.74 | Formula: R_parallel = 1 - (1 - r)^2 | Substitute: R = 1 - (1 - 0.74)^2 | Answer: 0.9324

question: A process produces 14 defective items in a batch of 5000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 14, N = 5000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 14/5000 * 1e6 | Answer: 2800 PPM

question: Find the distance between the points (4, -2) and (-9, 4).

question: Evaluate the number of combinations C(20, 14).
solution: Given: n = 20, r = 14 | Formula: C(n, r) = n! / (r! (n - r)!) | Substitute: C(20, 14) = 20! / (14! * 6!) | Answer: 38760

question: Evaluate the number of permutations P(15, 3).
solution: Given: n = 15, r = 3 | Formula: P(n, r) = n! / (n - r)! | Substitute: P(15, 3) = 15! / 12! | Answer: 2730

question: Find the 10th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -4 and common difference 6.
solution: Given: a = -4, d = 6, n = 10 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -4 + (10 - 1)*6 | Answer: 50

question: Find the sum of the first 37 terms of an AP with first term 0 and common difference 4.
solution: Given: a = 0, d = 4, n = 37 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 37/2 [2*0 + (37-1)*4] | Answer: 2664

question: Find the 6th term of a geometric progression with first term 5 and common ratio 2.

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 28500 at 9.3% per annum for 5 years.

question: Find the amount when 10000 is invested at 9.4% per annum compounded annually for 5 years.

question: Find the modulus of the complex number -8 + 3i.

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number 7 + -11i.
solution: Given: a = 7, b = -11 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(-11, 7) | Answer: -57.53 degrees

question: A circular rod of diameter 26 mm carries an axial tensile load of 5 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.

question: A rectangular beam section is 31 mm wide and 210 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.

question: A component of ultimate strength 370 MPa is designed for a working stress of 200 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 370, sw = 200 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 370 / 200 | Answer: 1.85

question: A steel bar is fully restrained and heated through 120 deg C. With E = 200 GPa and alpha = 12e-6 /deg C, find the thermal stress in MPa.

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1100 mm and wall thickness 14 mm carries an internal pressure of 0.9 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.

question: A Carnot engine operates between 1020 K and 280 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 1020, Tc = 280 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 280/1020) * 100 | Answer: 72.55 %

question: A refrigerator works between 252 K (cold) and 300 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.

question: A heat pump operates between 277 K and 328 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 277, Th = 328 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 328 / (328 - 277) | Answer: 6.431

question: 3.2 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 155 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.

question: 5.2 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 105 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 4.4 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.33 m. Find the Reynolds number.

question: Water flows at 4 m/s through a pipe of diameter 180 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 15.2 m. Taking Cv = 0.99, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).

question: In turning, cutting speed = 220 m/min, feed = 0.44 mm/rev, depth of cut = 1.5 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.

question: A workpiece of length 470 mm is turned at 600 rpm with a feed of 0.15 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 470, N = 600, f = 0.15 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 470 / (0.15*600) | Answer: 5.222 min

question: A resistor of 71 ohm carries a current of 4.8 A. Find the voltage across it.

question: A device draws 9.7 A at 185 V. Find the power consumed.

question: Two capacitors 4.9 uF and 10.7 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.

question: A resistor 12 kohm and capacitor 1.1 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.

question: An inductor 349.9 mH is in series with 38 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 349.9, R = 38 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (349.9e-3) / 38 | Answer: 9.208 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 148.9 mH inductor at 260 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 148.9, f = 260 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (260)(148.9e-3) | Answer: 243.2 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 22.1 uF capacitor at 570 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 22.1, f = 570 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (570)(22.1e-6)) | Answer: 12.63 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 11 ohm, XL = 63 ohm and XC = 19 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.

question: A capacitor of 70.9 uF is charged to 185 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.

question: An alternating voltage has a peak value of 82 V. Find its RMS value.

question: A machine delivers 15 kW output while drawing 107 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 90 kohm and Rin = 23 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.9 m carries a central point load of 15 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6.9, W = 15 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 15*6.9 / 4 | Answer: 25.88 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.7 m carries a UDL of 45 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.7, w = 45 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 45*(4.7)^2 / 8 | Answer: 124.3 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 2.3 m carries a point load 40 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 2.3, W = 40 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 40*2.3 | Answer: 92 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 5.6 m carries a UDL of 40 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.6, w = 40 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 40*(5.6)^2 / 2 | Answer: 627.2 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.1 m carries a point load 35 kN at distance 2.7 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 4.1, a = 2.7, W = 35 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 35*(4.1 - 2.7) / 4.1 | Answer: 11.95 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 3.7 m) carries a central point load 80 kN. With E = 25 GPa and I = 530e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=80000 N, L=3700.0 mm, E=25000 MPa, I=530e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 6.371 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 4.6 m carries a UDL of 36 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.6, w = 36 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 36*(4.6)^2 / 12 | Answer: 63.48 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 690 mm, clear cover 35 mm and main bars of diameter 16 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 690, c = 35, dia = 16 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 690 - 35 - 16/2 | Answer: 647 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 12.3 m^2 carrying a factored load of 10.7 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 12.3, w = 10.7 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 10.7 * 12.3 | Answer: 131.6 kN

question: For a bar of diameter 20 mm with design bond stress 1.8 MPa and steel stress 360 MPa, find the development length in mm.
solution: Given: dia = 20, tbd = 1.8, fs = 360 | Formula: Ld = phi fs / (4 tau_bd) | Substitute: Ld = 20*360 / (4*1.8) | Answer: 1000 mm

question: A soil sample has porosity n = 0.45. Find its void ratio e.
solution: Given: n = 0.45 | Formula: e = n / (1 - n) | Substitute: e = 0.45 / (1 - 0.45) | Answer: 0.8182

question: A cohesionless soil has an angle of internal friction phi = 35 degrees. Find Rankine's coefficient of active earth pressure Ka.
solution: Given: phi = 35 | Formula: Ka = (1 - sin phi) / (1 + sin phi) | Substitute: Ka = (1 - sin35) / (1 + sin35) | Answer: 0.271

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 3.9 m, unit weight 20 kN/m^3, phi = 34 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 2.2 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 20 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 2.2, g = 20 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (20 - 9.81)*2.2 | Answer: 22.42 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 4.3e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.4, area = 4.8e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 4.3, i = 0.4, A = 4.8 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (4.3e-4)*0.4*(4.8e-3) | Answer: 825.6 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 0.7 m, bed slope 0.009 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.029. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 4.7 m under a head of 1.1 m. Taking Cd = 0.61 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 4.4 m wide carries a discharge of 23.2 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 370 m and design speed 70 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 370, V = 70 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (70)^2 / (127*370) | Answer: 0.1043
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: For a design speed of 95 km/h with allowable superelevation 0.05 and lateral friction 0.12, find the minimum curve radius in m.
A tank of volume 220 m^3 treats a flow of 25 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 220, Q = 25 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 220 / 25 | Answer: 8.8 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 380 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.33 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 8 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 380, k = 0.33, t = 8 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 380*(1 - e^(-0.33*8)) | Answer: 352.9 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.73, rainfall intensity 110 mm/h over a catchment of 6.9 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.73, i = 110, A = 6.9 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.73*110*6.9 / 360 | Answer: 1.539 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.07 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 130 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.07, M = 130 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 130*(20+0.07)/20 | Answer: 130.5 m

question: Convert the decimal number 14 to binary.
solution: Divide 14 by 2 repeatedly, recording remainders | Reading remainders in reverse gives 1110 | Answer: 1110 (binary)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 2 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the decimal number 210 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 210 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: D2 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the 8-bit binary number 11000000 to decimal.
solution: Binary 11000000 = sum of bit-weights | Answer: 192 (decimal)
formula: Sum each bit times its positional weight (2^i)

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 11011001 and 11101010.
solution: XOR: 00110011 | Count of 1s = 4 | Answer: 4
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 410 megabits is sent over a link of 8 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 410, B = 8 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 410 / 8 | Answer: 51.25 s

question: A link has bandwidth 85 Mbps and round-trip time 90 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 85, R = 90 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 85e6 * 90e-3 bits = 7650 kb | Answer: 7650 kilobits

question: A channel has bandwidth 14 kHz. Using Nyquist's theorem with 4 signal levels, find the maximum data rate in kbps (noiseless).
solution: Given: B = 14, M = 4 | Formula: C = 2 B log2(M) | Substitute: C = 2*14*log2(4) | Answer: 56 kbps

question: A channel of bandwidth 15 kHz has a signal-to-noise ratio of 255 (linear). Using Shannon's theorem, find the channel capacity in kbps.
solution: Given: B = 15, SNR = 255 | Formula: C = B log2(1 + SNR) | Substitute: C = 15*log2(1 + 255) | Answer: 120 kbps

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.95, cache access time 7 ns and main-memory access time 90 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.95, tc = 7, tm = 90 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.95*7 + (1 - 0.95)*90 | Answer: 11.15 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 104834 elements?
solution: Given: n = 104834 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(104834)) + 1 | Answer: 17

question: An O(n^2) algorithm performs c*n^2 basic operations. If c = 1 and n = 720, how many operations are performed?
