question: 2.4 kg of air expands isothermally at 400 K from volume V1 to 2*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.4, Tk = 400, ratio = 2 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 2.4*0.287*400*ln(2) | Answer: 191 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 2.1 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.11 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 2.1, D = 0.11 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*2.1*0.11 / 0.001 | Answer: 231000

question: Water flows at 2.2 m/s through a pipe of diameter 120 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 28.8 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 28.8 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*28.8 / 1000 | Answer: 282.5 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 7.3 m. Taking Cv = 0.97, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 7.3, cv = 0.97 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.97*sqrt(2*9.81*7.3) | Answer: 11.61 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 170 mm) water flows at 2.3 m/s. It contracts to diameter 80 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 170, d2 = 80, V1 = 2.3 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 2.3*(170/80)^2 | Answer: 10.39 m/s

question: Water flows at 2.3 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.36 m and length 180 m. With friction factor f = 0.036, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 29 teeth drives a gear of 47 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1500 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 29, z2 = 47, N1 = 1500 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1500*29 / 47 | Answer: 925.5 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 550 mm rotates at 1200 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 550, N = 1200 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.55)*1200 / 60 | Answer: 34.56 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 38.7 kW at 350 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 38.7, N = 350 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(38.7*1000) / (2*pi*350) | Answer: 1056 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 1.8 kg rotates at radius 0.49 m at 500 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 12600 N/m and mass 12.5 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 12600, m = 12.5 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(12600/12.5) | Answer: 5.053 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 6.7 m^2 and thickness 0.36 m has conductivity k = 41.8 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 160 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 6.7, L = 0.36, k = 41.8, dT = 160 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 41.8*6.7*160 / 0.36 | Answer: 124471 W

question: A surface of area 1.7 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 100 W/m^2-K to surroundings 75 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 1.7, h = 100, dT = 75 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 100*1.7*75 | Answer: 12750 W

question: In a counter-flow heat exchanger the terminal temperature differences are 105 deg C and 10 deg C. Find the log mean temperature difference (LMTD) in deg C.
solution: Given: dT1 = 105, dT2 = 10 | Formula: LMTD = (dT1 - dT2) / ln(dT1/dT2) | Substitute: LMTD = (105 - 10) / ln(105/10) | Answer: 40.4 deg C

question: In turning, cutting speed = 60 m/min, feed = 0.31 mm/rev, depth of cut = 1.4 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 60, f = 0.31, d = 1.4 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*60*0.31*1.4 | Answer: 26040 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 120 mm is turned at 850 rpm with a feed of 0.35 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 120, N = 850, f = 0.35 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 120 / (0.35*850) | Answer: 0.4034 min

question: A resistor of 137 ohm carries a current of 1.1 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 137, I = 1.1 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 1.1 * 137 | Answer: 150.7 V

question: Three resistors 10 ohm, 52 ohm and 81 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 10, R2 = 52, R3 = 81 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 10 + 52 + 81 | Answer: 143 ohm

question: Two resistors 69 ohm and 16 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 69, R2 = 16 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 69*16 / (69+16) | Answer: 12.99 ohm

question: A device draws 5.8 A at 15 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 15, I = 5.8 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 15 * 5.8 | Answer: 87 W

question: A current of 6.9 A flows through a 21 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 6.9, R = 21 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (6.9)^2 * 21 | Answer: 999.8 W

question: Two capacitors 10.6 uF and 11.5 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 10.6, C2 = 11.5 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 10.6*11.5 / (10.6+11.5) | Answer: 5.516 uF

question: A resistor 61 kohm and capacitor 17 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 61, C = 17 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (61k)(17u) = 1037 ms | Answer: 1037 ms

question: An inductor 146 mH is in series with 196 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 146, R = 196 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (146e-3) / 196 | Answer: 0.7449 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 12 mH inductor at 110 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 12, f = 110 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (110)(12e-3) | Answer: 8.294 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 44.2 uF capacitor at 200 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 44.2, f = 200 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (200)(44.2e-6)) | Answer: 18 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 9 ohm, XL = 52 ohm and XC = 67 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 9, XL = 52, XC = 67 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(9^2 + (52 - 67)^2) | Answer: 17.49 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 51.6 mH and C = 0.6 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 51.6, C = 0.6 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(51.6e-3 * 0.6e-6)) | Answer: 904.5 Hz

question: A capacitor of 76.4 uF is charged to 400 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 76.4, V = 400 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*76.4e-6*(400)^2 | Answer: 6112 mJ

question: An alternating voltage has a peak value of 316 V. Find its RMS value.
solution: Given: Vp = 316 | Formula: Vrms = Vp / sqrt(2) | Substitute: Vrms = 316 / sqrt(2) | Answer: 223.4 V

question: A transformer has primary voltage 360 V with 920 primary turns and 220 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 360, N1 = 920, N2 = 220 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 360 * 220/920 | Answer: 86.09 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 290 V and draws an armature current of 19 A. If the armature resistance is 1.45 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 290, Ia = 19, Ra = 1.45 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 290 - 19*1.45 | Answer: 262.4 V

question: A 4-pole induction motor on a 50 Hz supply runs at 750 rpm. Find the slip (%).
formula: s = (Ns - N) / Ns,  Ns = 120 f / P

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 185 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.93. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 185, VL = 400, pf = 0.93 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*400*185*0.93 / 1000 | Answer: 119.2 kW

question: A load has real power 35 kW and apparent power 70 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 35, S = 70 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 35 / 70 | Answer: 0.5

question: A machine delivers 145 kW output while drawing 217 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 145, Pi = 217 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 145/217 * 100 | Answer: 66.82 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 28 V across R1 = 29 ohm and R2 = 7 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 28, R1 = 29, R2 = 7 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 28*7 / (29+7) | Answer: 5.444 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 50 kohm and Rin = 30 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 50, Rin = 30 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 50 / 30 | Answer: 1.667

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 190 kohm and Rg = 4 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 190, Rg = 4 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 190/4 | Answer: 48.5

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 4448. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 4448 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(4448) | Answer: 36.48 dB

question: A first-order system has a time constant of 9.7 s. Find the time (in s) to reach 63.2% of its final value.
solution: For a first-order step response, y = 1 - e^(-t/tau) | y = 0.632 when t = tau | Answer: 9.7 s
formula: At t = tau the response reaches 63.2% (one time constant)

question: A signal is sampled at 166 kHz. According to the Nyquist criterion, what is the maximum signal frequency that can be represented (in kHz)?
solution: Given: fs = 166 | Formula: f_max = fs / 2 | Substitute: f_max = 166 / 2 | Answer: 83 kHz

question: A simply supported beam of span 8.3 m carries a central point load of 110 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 8.3, W = 110 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 110*8.3 / 4 | Answer: 228.3 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.4 m carries a UDL of 25 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 9.4, w = 25 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 25*(9.4)^2 / 8 | Answer: 276.1 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 1.2 m carries a point load 80 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 1.2, W = 80 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 80*1.2 | Answer: 96 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 1.8 m carries a UDL of 10 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 1.8, w = 10 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 10*(1.8)^2 / 2 | Answer: 16.2 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 5.1 m carries a point load 20 kN at distance 3 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 5.1, a = 3, W = 20 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 20*(5.1 - 3) / 5.1 | Answer: 8.235 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 7.4 m) carries a central point load 15 kN. With E = 25 GPa and I = 90e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=15000 N, L=7400.0 mm, E=25000 MPa, I=90e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 56.28 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 7.7 m carries a UDL of 24 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7.7, w = 24 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 24*(7.7)^2 / 12 | Answer: 118.6 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 410 mm, clear cover 40 mm and main bars of diameter 16 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 410, c = 40, dia = 16 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 410 - 40 - 16/2 | Answer: 362 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 11.9 m^2 carrying a factored load of 12.4 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 11.9, w = 12.4 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 12.4 * 11.9 | Answer: 147.6 kN

question: For a bar of diameter 20 mm with design bond stress 1.7 MPa and steel stress 395 MPa, find the development length in mm.
solution: Given: dia = 20, tbd = 1.7, fs = 395 | Formula: Ld = phi fs / (4 tau_bd) | Substitute: Ld = 20*395 / (4*1.7) | Answer: 1162 mm

question: A soil sample has porosity n = 0.34. Find its void ratio e.
solution: Given: n = 0.34 | Formula: e = n / (1 - n) | Substitute: e = 0.34 / (1 - 0.34) | Answer: 0.5152

question: A cohesionless soil has an angle of internal friction phi = 26 degrees. Find Rankine's coefficient of active earth pressure Ka.
solution: Given: phi = 26 | Formula: Ka = (1 - sin phi) / (1 + sin phi) | Substitute: Ka = (1 - sin26) / (1 + sin26) | Answer: 0.3905

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 4.4 m, unit weight 19 kN/m^3, phi = 35 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 11.1 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 18 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 11.1, g = 18 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (18 - 9.81)*11.1 | Answer: 90.91 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 6.6e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.2, area = 1.4e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 6.6, i = 0.2, A = 1.4 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (6.6e-4)*0.2*(1.4e-3) | Answer: 184.8 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 2.4 m, bed slope 0.001 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.029. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 1.8 m under a head of 1.2 m. Taking Cd = 0.61 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 2.6 m wide carries a discharge of 21.9 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 400 m and design speed 100 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 400, V = 100 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (100)^2 / (127*400) | Answer: 0.1969
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: For a design speed of 45 km/h with allowable superelevation 0.05 and lateral friction 0.14, find the minimum curve radius in m.
A tank of volume 180 m^3 treats a flow of 100 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 180, Q = 100 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 180 / 100 | Answer: 1.8 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 190 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.34 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 8 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 190, k = 0.34, t = 8 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 190*(1 - e^(-0.34*8)) | Answer: 177.5 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.89, rainfall intensity 100 mm/h over a catchment of 49.4 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.89, i = 100, A = 49.4 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.89*100*49.4 / 360 | Answer: 12.21 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.06 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 110 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.06, M = 110 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 110*(20+0.06)/20 | Answer: 110.3 m

question: Convert the decimal number 201 to binary.
solution: Divide 201 by 2 repeatedly, recording remainders | Reading remainders in reverse gives 11001001 | Answer: 11001001 (binary)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 2 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the decimal number 2215 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 2215 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 8A7 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the 8-bit binary number 10100110 to decimal.
solution: Binary 10100110 = sum of bit-weights | Answer: 166 (decimal)
formula: Sum each bit times its positional weight (2^i)

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 10111001 and 01000011.
solution: XOR: 11111010 | Count of 1s = 6 | Answer: 6
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 150 megabits is sent over a link of 59 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 150, B = 59 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 150 / 59 | Answer: 2.542 s

question: A link has bandwidth 43 Mbps and round-trip time 60 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 43, R = 60 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 43e6 * 60e-3 bits = 2580 kb | Answer: 2580 kilobits

question: A channel has bandwidth 15 kHz. Using Nyquist's theorem with 2 signal levels, find the maximum data rate in kbps (noiseless).
solution: Given: B = 15, M = 2 | Formula: C = 2 B log2(M) | Substitute: C = 2*15*log2(2) | Answer: 30 kbps

question: A channel of bandwidth 14 kHz has a signal-to-noise ratio of 15 (linear). Using Shannon's theorem, find the channel capacity in kbps.
solution: Given: B = 14, SNR = 15 | Formula: C = B log2(1 + SNR) | Substitute: C = 14*log2(1 + 15) | Answer: 56 kbps

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.93, cache access time 3 ns and main-memory access time 120 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.93, tc = 3, tm = 120 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.93*3 + (1 - 0.93)*120 | Answer: 11.19 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 582347 elements?
solution: Given: n = 582347 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(582347)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: An O(n^2) algorithm performs c*n^2 basic operations. If c = 1 and n = 1830, how many operations are performed?
solution: Given: n = 1830 | Formula: operations = n^2 | Substitute: = (1830)^2 | Answer: 3348900

question: A program is 50% parallelisable and run on 16 processors. Using Amdahl's law, find the maximum speedup.
solution: Parallel fraction f = 0.5 | S = 1 / ((1 - 0.5) + 0.5/16) | Answer: 1.882x speedup

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.004, memory access time 150 ns and page-fault service time 3 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 3 ms = 3000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.004)*150 + 0.004*3000000.0 ns | Answer: 12.15 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: A modem transmits at 1200 baud using 4-level signalling. Find the bit rate in bps.
solution: Given: baud = 1200, M = 4 | Formula: bit rate = baud * log2(M) | Substitute: bit rate = 1200 * log2(4) | Answer: 2400 bps

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 1.8 m^3 at 440 kPa and 510 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 1.8, P = 440, Tk = 510 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (440e3)*1.8 / (8.314*510) | Answer: 186.8 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.15 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 8 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.15, t = 8 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.15*8) | Answer: 0.6988

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.33 /min) is to reach 60% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.33, X = 60 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.6) / 0.33 | Answer: 2.777 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.14 /min) reaches 50% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.14, X = 50 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.5 / (0.14*(1 - 0.5)) | Answer: 7.143 min

question: A first-order reaction has a rate constant of 0.24 /min. Find its half-life in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.24 | Formula: t_half = ln(2) / k | Substitute: t_half = 0.6931 / 0.24 | Answer: 2.888 min

question: For a reaction with A = 6e10 /s and activation energy 80 kJ/mol at 340 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 6, Ea = 80, Tk = 340 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 6e10 * exp(-80e3 / (8.314*340)) | Answer: 0.0307 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.91 and bottoms xW = 0.05, with relative volatility alpha = 2.7. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.91, xw = 0.05, al = 2.7 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.91/0.09)(0.95/0.05)] / ln(2.7) | Answer: 5.294 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.72 and x = 0.38. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.72, x = 0.38 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.72/0.28) / (0.38/0.62) | Answer: 4.195

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.11 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 20 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.11, Psat = 20 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.11 * 20 | Answer: 2.2 kPa

question: A stream of 3.6 kg/s with specific heat 1.3 kJ/kg-K is heated through 90 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 3.6, cp = 1.3, dT = 90 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 3.6*1.3*90 | Answer: 421.2 kW

question: A reactor of volume 6.4 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 0.9 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 6.4, Q = 0.9 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 6.4 / 0.9 | Answer: 7.111 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 8.4e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 2 mm with a concentration difference of 70 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 8.4, L = 2, dC = 70 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (8.4e-9)*70 / (2e-3) | Answer: 294 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 3.9 min and steady-state gain 1.2. For a step input of magnitude 5, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 3.9, K = 1.2, M = 5 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 1.2 * 5 | Answer: 6 units

question: A reactor operates at a space time of 13.1 min. Find its space velocity in per hour.
solution: Given: tau = 13.1 | Formula: SV = 60 / tau  (per hour) | Substitute: SV = 60 / 13.1 | Answer: 4.58 /h

question: An aircraft wing of area 120 m^2 flies at 160 m/s (air density 0.4 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.4. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 120, V = 160, rho = 0.4, CL = 0.4 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.4*(160)^2*120*0.4 / 1000 | Answer: 245.8 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 80 m^2 flies at 120 m/s (density 0.4 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.11. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 80, V = 120, rho = 0.4, CD = 0.11 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.4*(120)^2*80*0.11 / 1000 | Answer: 25.34 kN

question: Find the dynamic pressure for air of density 0.7 kg/m^3 moving at 200 m/s, in Pa.
solution: Given: rho = 0.7, V = 200 | Formula: q = 0.5 rho V^2 | Substitute: q = 0.5*0.7*(200)^2 | Answer: 14000 Pa

question: An aircraft flies at 430 m/s where the speed of sound is 340 m/s. Find the Mach number.
solution: Given: V = 430, a = 340 | Formula: M = V / a | Substitute: M = 430 / 340 | Answer: 1.265

question: Find the circular orbital velocity of a satellite at altitude 1650 km above Earth (Earth radius 6371 km, mu = 3.986e14 m^3/s^2), in km/s.
A specimen under stress 310 MPa shows an elastic strain of 2.7e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 310, eps = 2.7 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 310 / (2.7e-3) MPa = 114.8 GPa | Answer: 114.8 GPa

question: A block of mass 18 kg has a volume of 1.1e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 18, V = 1.1 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 18 / (1.1e-3) | Answer: 16364 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 2500 mm is heated through 45 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 23e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 2500, dT = 45, al = 23 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 2500*23e-6*45 | Answer: 2.587 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 20 ohm, R2 = 40 ohm and R3 = 125 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 20, R2 = 40, R3 = 125 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 40*125 / 20 | Answer: 250 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 120 ohm and gauge factor 2.1 experiences a strain of 1250e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 120, GF = 2.1, eps = 1250 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 120*2.1*1250e-6 | Answer: 315 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 10.4 when the true value is 50. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10.4, true = 50 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10.4 - 50| / 50 * 100 | Answer: 79.2 %

question: Annual demand is 36000 units, ordering cost 250 per order and holding cost 40 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 36000, S = 250, H = 40 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*36000*250 / 40) | Answer: 670.8 units

question: An asset costs 270000 with salvage value 14000 after 19 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 270000, Sv = 14000, n = 19 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (270000 - 14000) / 19 | Answer: 13474 per year

question: A product sells for 260 per unit with variable cost 160 per unit and fixed costs 135000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 260, V = 160, F = 135000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 135000 / (260 - 160) | Answer: 1350 units

question: Find the present worth of 65000 received 8 years from now at an interest rate of 9% per year.
solution: Given: F = 65000, n = 8, i = 9 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 65000 / (1 + 0.09)^8 | Answer: 32621 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.97, 0.99 and 0.98 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.97, r2 = 0.99, r3 = 0.98 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.97*0.99*0.98 | Answer: 0.9411

question: Two components each of reliability 0.78 are connected in parallel. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r = 0.78 | Formula: R_parallel = 1 - (1 - r)^2 | Substitute: R = 1 - (1 - 0.78)^2 | Answer: 0.9516

question: A process produces 34 defective items in a batch of 11500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 34, N = 11500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 34/11500 * 1e6 | Answer: 2957 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -2x^3 - 8x^2 + 7x evaluated at x = -2.
For f(x) = 3x^3 + x^2 - 6, find f''(x) at x = 1.
Evaluate the definite integral of (-4x^2 + 5x + 8) dx from x = -1 to x = 5.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = -4x^3/3 + 5x^2/2 + 8x | Evaluate F(5) - F(-1) | Answer: -60
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 2x^2 + 12x - 9 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[-6, 4], [-9, -4]].
solution: Given: a = -6, b = 4, c = -9, d = -4 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (-6)(-4) - (4)(-9) | Answer: 60

question: Find the determinant of [[6, 5, -2], [-1, -1, 3], [-3, -3, 4]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: 5

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[-8, -2], [4, 7]].
solution: Trace tr = -1, Determinant = -48 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 6.446

question: Solve for x: -2x + 0y = 9 and 4x + -6y = -8.
solution: Determinant = -2*-6 - 0*4 = 12 | x = (e d - b f) / det = -4.5 | Answer: x = -4.5
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 71, 3, 58, 87, 2.
solution: Sum = 221 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 44.2 | Answer: 44.2

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 19, 5, 1, 35, 50.
solution: Mean = 22 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 20.57

question: Find the slope of the line through (0, 1) and (4, -5).
solution: Given: x1 = 0, y1 = 1, x2 = 4, y2 = -5 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (-5 - 1) / (4 - 0) | Answer: -1.5

question: Find the distance between the points (-6, 8) and (-9, -8).
solution: Given: x1 = -6, y1 = 8, x2 = -9, y2 = -8 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-3)^2 + (-16)^2) | Answer: 16.28 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (-2,4), (-8,7), (8,3).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 12 sq units

question: Evaluate the number of combinations C(18, 13).
solution: Given: n = 18, r = 13 | Formula: C(n, r) = n! / (r! (n - r)!) | Substitute: C(18, 13) = 18! / (13! * 5!) | Answer: 8568

question: Evaluate the number of permutations P(9, 6).
solution: Given: n = 9, r = 6 | Formula: P(n, r) = n! / (n - r)! | Substitute: P(9, 6) = 9! / 3! | Answer: 60480

question: Find the 40th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -1 and common difference 8.
solution: Given: a = -1, d = 8, n = 40 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -1 + (40 - 1)*8 | Answer: 311

question: Find the sum of the first 11 terms of an AP with first term -8 and common difference -5.
solution: Given: a = -8, d = -5, n = 11 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 11/2 [2*-8 + (11-1)*-5] | Answer: -363

question: Find the 7th term of a geometric progression with first term 8 and common ratio 2.
solution: Given: a = 8, r = 2, n = 7 | Formula: a_n = a r^(n-1) | Substitute: a_n = 8 * 2^(7-1) | Answer: 512

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 37500 at 6.5% per annum for 10 years.
solution: Given: P = 37500, R = 6.5, Tt = 10 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 37500 * 6.5 * 10 / 100 | Answer: 24375 currency units

question: Find the amount when 23500 is invested at 10.6% per annum compounded annually for 3 years.
solution: Given: P = 23500, R = 10.6, Tt = 3 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 23500 * (1 + 10.6/100)^3 | Answer: 31793 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (8, -2, -8) and (-8, -5, -7).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (2, 3, 6) and (-3, 1, -5).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 25.02

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (-6, -3, -2) and (-1, 0, -4).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 60.98 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number -9 + -11i.
solution: Given: a = -9, b = -11 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((-9)^2 + (-11)^2) | Answer: 14.21

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number 6 + 9i.
solution: Given: a = 6, b = 9 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(9, 6) | Answer: 56.31 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -3x^3 + 6x^2 + 2x - 8 at x = 2.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-35 with initial guess x0=9, find x1 (one iteration).
solution: Given: N = 35, x0 = 9 | Formula: x1 = x0 - (x0^2 - N)/(2 x0) | Substitute: x1 = 9 - ((9)^2 - 35)/(2*9) | Answer: 6.444

question: Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.8 and ordinates 3, 17, 15, 19, 17, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 569 and 314.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 569 and 314 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 34 and 9.
solution: Given: a = 34, b = 9 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 34*9 / 1 | Answer: 306
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 19 mm carries an axial tensile load of 69 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 22 mm and length 1000 mm carries an axial load of 33 kN. Take E = 70 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 60 mm transmits a torque of 2450 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 60, Tt = 2450 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(2450*1000) / (pi*(60)^3) | Answer: 57.77 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 62 mm and length 1400 mm carries a torque of 1250 N-m. With G = 77 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 122 mm wide and 140 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 122, h = 140 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 122*(140)^2 / 6 | Answer: 398533 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (117 mm x 200 mm) carries a bending moment of 31 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (35 mm x 120 mm) has effective length 1700 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 360 MPa is designed for a working stress of 250 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 360, sw = 250 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 360 / 250 | Answer: 1.44

question: A steel bar is fully restrained and heated through 80 deg C. With E = 210 GPa and alpha = 12e-6 /deg C, find the thermal stress in MPa.
solution: Given: dT = 80, E = 210, al = 12 | Formula: sigma = E alpha (dT) | Substitute: sigma = 210000 * 12e-6 * 80 | Answer: 201.6 MPa

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1350 mm and wall thickness 8 mm carries an internal pressure of 1.9 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1350, t = 8, P = 1.9 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 1.9*1350 / (2*8) | Answer: 160.3 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 820 K and 310 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 820, Tc = 310 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 310/820) * 100 | Answer: 62.2 %

question: A refrigerator works between 253 K (cold) and 304 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 253, Th = 304 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 253 / (304 - 253) | Answer: 4.961

question: A heat pump operates between 280 K and 314 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 280, Th = 314 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 314 / (314 - 280) | Answer: 9.235

question: 8 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 125 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 8, dT = 125 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 8 * 0.718 * 125 | Answer: 718 kJ

question: 2.4 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 95 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.4, dT = 95 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 2.4 * 1.005 * 95 | Answer: 229.1 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 2.7 m^3 at 380 K with mass 5.6 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 2.7, Tk = 380, m = 5.6 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 5.6*0.287*380 / 2.7 | Answer: 226.2 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 1.8 kg of air expands isothermally at 460 K from volume V1 to 4*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1.8, Tk = 460, ratio = 4 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 1.8*0.287*460*ln(4) | Answer: 329.4 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 1.1 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.24 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 1.1, D = 0.24 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*1.1*0.24 / 0.001 | Answer: 264000

question: Water flows at 2 m/s through a pipe of diameter 100 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 25.5 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 25.5 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*25.5 / 1000 | Answer: 250.2 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 12.8 m. Taking Cv = 0.96, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 12.8, cv = 0.96 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.96*sqrt(2*9.81*12.8) | Answer: 15.21 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 360 mm) water flows at 2.8 m/s. It contracts to diameter 70 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 360, d2 = 70, V1 = 2.8 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 2.8*(360/70)^2 | Answer: 74.06 m/s

question: Water flows at 1.8 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.45 m and length 230 m. With friction factor f = 0.031, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 26 teeth drives a gear of 102 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1400 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 26, z2 = 102, N1 = 1400 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1400*26 / 102 | Answer: 356.9 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 150 mm rotates at 350 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 150, N = 350 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.15)*350 / 60 | Answer: 2.749 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 8.5 kW at 1000 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 8.5, N = 1000 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(8.5*1000) / (2*pi*1000) | Answer: 81.17 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 4.8 kg rotates at radius 0.32 m at 1200 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 9700 N/m and mass 17.9 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 9700, m = 17.9 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(9700/17.9) | Answer: 3.705 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 9.2 m^2 and thickness 0.21 m has conductivity k = 44.7 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 140 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 9.2, L = 0.21, k = 44.7, dT = 140 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 44.7*9.2*140 / 0.21 | Answer: 274160 W

question: A surface of area 2.4 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 35 W/m^2-K to surroundings 110 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 2.4, h = 35, dT = 110 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 35*2.4*110 | Answer: 9240 W

question: In a counter-flow heat exchanger the terminal temperature differences are 120 deg C and 25 deg C. Find the log mean temperature difference (LMTD) in deg C.
solution: Given: dT1 = 120, dT2 = 25 | Formula: LMTD = (dT1 - dT2) / ln(dT1/dT2) | Substitute: LMTD = (120 - 25) / ln(120/25) | Answer: 60.56 deg C

question: In turning, cutting speed = 160 m/min, feed = 0.36 mm/rev, depth of cut = 1.2 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 160, f = 0.36, d = 1.2 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*160*0.36*1.2 | Answer: 69120 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 210 mm is turned at 250 rpm with a feed of 0.34 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 210, N = 250, f = 0.34 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 210 / (0.34*250) | Answer: 2.471 min

question: A resistor of 141 ohm carries a current of 6.6 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 141, I = 6.6 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 6.6 * 141 | Answer: 930.6 V

question: Three resistors 48 ohm, 41 ohm and 33 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 48, R2 = 41, R3 = 33 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 48 + 41 + 33 | Answer: 122 ohm

question: Two resistors 94 ohm and 39 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 94, R2 = 39 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 94*39 / (94+39) | Answer: 27.56 ohm

question: A device draws 6.7 A at 185 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 185, I = 6.7 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 185 * 6.7 | Answer: 124 W

question: A current of 3.7 A flows through a 111 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 3.7, R = 111 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (3.7)^2 * 111 | Answer: 152 W

question: Two capacitors 35.3 uF and 28.8 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 35.3, C2 = 28.8 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 35.3*28.8 / (35.3+28.8) | Answer: 15.86 uF

question: A resistor 55 kohm and capacitor 6.3 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 55, C = 6.3 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (55k)(6.3u) = 346.5 ms | Answer: 346.5 ms

question: An inductor 279.4 mH is in series with 34 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 279.4, R = 34 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (279.4e-3) / 34 | Answer: 8.218 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 139 mH inductor at 1000 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 139, f = 1000 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (1000)(139e-3) | Answer: 873.4 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 47.5 uF capacitor at 960 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 47.5, f = 960 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (960)(47.5e-6)) | Answer: 3.49 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 9 ohm, XL = 65 ohm and XC = 112 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 9, XL = 65, XC = 112 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(9^2 + (65 - 112)^2) | Answer: 47.85 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 77.3 mH and C = 5 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 77.3, C = 5 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(77.3e-3 * 5e-6)) | Answer: 256 Hz

question: A capacitor of 19.7 uF is charged to 365 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 19.7, V = 365 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*19.7e-6*(365)^2 | Answer: 1312 mJ

question: An alternating voltage has a peak value of 202 V. Find its RMS value.
solution: Given: Vp = 202 | Formula: Vrms = Vp / sqrt(2) | Substitute: Vrms = 202 / sqrt(2) | Answer: 142.8 V

question: A transformer has primary voltage 360 V with 300 primary turns and 100 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 360, N1 = 300, N2 = 100 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 360 * 100/300 | Answer: 120 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 240 V and draws an armature current of 54 A. If the armature resistance is 0.73 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 240, Ia = 54, Ra = 0.73 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 240 - 54*0.73 | Answer: 200.6 V

question: A 8-pole induction motor on a 50 Hz supply runs at 710 rpm. Find the slip (%).
formula: s = (Ns - N) / Ns,  Ns = 120 f / P

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 90 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.75. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 90, VL = 400, pf = 0.75 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*400*90*0.75 / 1000 | Answer: 46.77 kW

question: A load has real power 95 kW and apparent power 210 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 95, S = 210 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 95 / 210 | Answer: 0.4524

question: A machine delivers 105 kW output while drawing 157 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 105, Pi = 157 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 105/157 * 100 | Answer: 66.88 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 20 V across R1 = 16 ohm and R2 = 42 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 20, R1 = 16, R2 = 42 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 20*42 / (16+42) | Answer: 14.48 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 140 kohm and Rin = 31 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 140, Rin = 31 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 140 / 31 | Answer: 4.516

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 80 kohm and Rg = 6 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 80, Rg = 6 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 80/6 | Answer: 14.33

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 9844. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 9844 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(9844) | Answer: 39.93 dB

question: A first-order system has a time constant of 5.9 s. Find the time (in s) to reach 63.2% of its final value.
solution: For a first-order step response, y = 1 - e^(-t/tau) | y = 0.632 when t = tau | Answer: 5.9 s
formula: At t = tau the response reaches 63.2% (one time constant)

question: A signal is sampled at 78 kHz. According to the Nyquist criterion, what is the maximum signal frequency that can be represented (in kHz)?
solution: Given: fs = 78 | Formula: f_max = fs / 2 | Substitute: f_max = 78 / 2 | Answer: 39 kHz

question: A simply supported beam of span 8.2 m carries a central point load of 100 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 8.2, W = 100 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 100*8.2 / 4 | Answer: 205 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.9 m carries a UDL of 15 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6.9, w = 15 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 15*(6.9)^2 / 8 | Answer: 89.27 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 2.2 m carries a point load 35 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 2.2, W = 35 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 35*2.2 | Answer: 77 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 4.9 m carries a UDL of 22 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.9, w = 22 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 22*(4.9)^2 / 2 | Answer: 264.1 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 5.2 m carries a point load 55 kN at distance 1.4 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 5.2, a = 1.4, W = 55 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 55*(5.2 - 1.4) / 5.2 | Answer: 40.19 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 5.1 m) carries a central point load 35 kN. With E = 25 GPa and I = 570e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=35000 N, L=5100.0 mm, E=25000 MPa, I=570e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 6.788 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 4 m carries a UDL of 12 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4, w = 12 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 12*(4)^2 / 12 | Answer: 16 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 570 mm, clear cover 45 mm and main bars of diameter 12 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 570, c = 45, dia = 12 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 570 - 45 - 12/2 | Answer: 519 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 11.2 m^2 carrying a factored load of 17.7 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 11.2, w = 17.7 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 17.7 * 11.2 | Answer: 198.2 kN

question: For a bar of diameter 20 mm with design bond stress 2.1 MPa and steel stress 395 MPa, find the development length in mm.
solution: Given: dia = 20, tbd = 2.1, fs = 395 | Formula: Ld = phi fs / (4 tau_bd) | Substitute: Ld = 20*395 / (4*2.1) | Answer: 940.5 mm

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 3.2 m, unit weight 17 kN/m^3, phi = 33 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 6.2 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 21 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 6.2, g = 21 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (21 - 9.81)*6.2 | Answer: 69.38 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 1.9e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1.2, area = 5.7e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 1.9, i = 1.2, A = 5.7 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (1.9e-4)*1.2*(5.7e-3) | Answer: 13 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 2.4 m, bed slope 0.005 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.016. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 4.3 m under a head of 0.4 m. Taking Cd = 0.61 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 3.2 m wide carries a discharge of 23.1 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 100 m and design speed 60 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 100, V = 60 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (60)^2 / (127*100) | Answer: 0.2835
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: For a design speed of 50 km/h with allowable superelevation 0.07 and lateral friction 0.15, find the minimum curve radius in m.
A tank of volume 420 m^3 treats a flow of 150 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 420, Q = 150 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 420 / 150 | Answer: 2.8 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 160 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.21 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 5 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 160, k = 0.21, t = 5 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 160*(1 - e^(-0.21*5)) | Answer: 104 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.88, rainfall intensity 120 mm/h over a catchment of 19.5 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.88, i = 120, A = 19.5 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.88*120*19.5 / 360 | Answer: 5.72 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.05 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 460 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.05, M = 460 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 460*(20+0.05)/20 | Answer: 461.1 m

question: Convert the decimal number 98 to binary.
solution: Divide 98 by 2 repeatedly, recording remainders | Reading remainders in reverse gives 1100010 | Answer: 1100010 (binary)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 2 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the decimal number 3171 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 3171 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: C63 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the 8-bit binary number 00001111 to decimal.
solution: Binary 00001111 = sum of bit-weights | Answer: 15 (decimal)
formula: Sum each bit times its positional weight (2^i)

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 00011000 and 01111101.
solution: XOR: 01100101 | Count of 1s = 4 | Answer: 4
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 930 megabits is sent over a link of 11 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 930, B = 11 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 930 / 11 | Answer: 84.55 s

question: A link has bandwidth 89 Mbps and round-trip time 200 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 89, R = 200 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 89e6 * 200e-3 bits = 17800 kb | Answer: 17800 kilobits

question: A channel has bandwidth 18 kHz. Using Nyquist's theorem with 4 signal levels, find the maximum data rate in kbps (noiseless).
solution: Given: B = 18, M = 4 | Formula: C = 2 B log2(M) | Substitute: C = 2*18*log2(4) | Answer: 72 kbps

question: A channel of bandwidth 18 kHz has a signal-to-noise ratio of 31 (linear). Using Shannon's theorem, find the channel capacity in kbps.
solution: Given: B = 18, SNR = 31 | Formula: C = B log2(1 + SNR) | Substitute: C = 18*log2(1 + 31) | Answer: 90 kbps

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.94, cache access time 5 ns and main-memory access time 80 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.94, tc = 5, tm = 80 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.94*5 + (1 - 0.94)*80 | Answer: 9.5 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 735087 elements?
solution: Given: n = 735087 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(735087)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: An O(n^2) algorithm performs c*n^2 basic operations. If c = 1 and n = 2840, how many operations are performed?
solution: Given: n = 2840 | Formula: operations = n^2 | Substitute: = (2840)^2 | Answer: 8065600

question: A program is 90% parallelisable and run on 16 processors. Using Amdahl's law, find the maximum speedup.
solution: Parallel fraction f = 0.9 | S = 1 / ((1 - 0.9) + 0.9/16) | Answer: 6.4x speedup

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.005, memory access time 180 ns and page-fault service time 4 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 4 ms = 4000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.005)*180 + 0.005*4000000.0 ns | Answer: 20.18 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: A modem transmits at 2400 baud using 2-level signalling. Find the bit rate in bps.
solution: Given: baud = 2400, M = 2 | Formula: bit rate = baud * log2(M) | Substitute: bit rate = 2400 * log2(2) | Answer: 2400 bps

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 2.2 m^3 at 180 kPa and 450 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 2.2, P = 180, Tk = 450 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (180e3)*2.2 / (8.314*450) | Answer: 105.8 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.09 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 11 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.09, t = 11 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.09*11) | Answer: 0.6284

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.19 /min) is to reach 60% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.19, X = 60 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.6) / 0.19 | Answer: 4.823 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.5 /min) reaches 55% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.5, X = 55 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.55 / (0.5*(1 - 0.55)) | Answer: 2.444 min

question: A first-order reaction has a rate constant of 0.38 /min. Find its half-life in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.38 | Formula: t_half = ln(2) / k | Substitute: t_half = 0.6931 / 0.38 | Answer: 1.824 min

question: For a reaction with A = 6e10 /s and activation energy 65 kJ/mol at 370 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 6, Ea = 65, Tk = 370 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 6e10 * exp(-65e3 / (8.314*370)) | Answer: 39.95 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.94 and bottoms xW = 0.04, with relative volatility alpha = 1.6. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.94, xw = 0.04, al = 1.6 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.94/0.06)(0.96/0.04)] / ln(1.6) | Answer: 12.62 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.81 and x = 0.49. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.81, x = 0.49 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.81/0.19) / (0.49/0.51) | Answer: 4.437

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.14 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 120 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.14, Psat = 120 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.14 * 120 | Answer: 16.8 kPa

question: A stream of 3.8 kg/s with specific heat 2.2 kJ/kg-K is heated through 30 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 3.8, cp = 2.2, dT = 30 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 3.8*2.2*30 | Answer: 250.8 kW

question: A reactor of volume 2.4 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 4.6 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 2.4, Q = 4.6 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 2.4 / 4.6 | Answer: 0.5217 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 3e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 2 mm with a concentration difference of 130 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 3, L = 2, dC = 130 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (3e-9)*130 / (2e-3) | Answer: 195 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 3.4 min and steady-state gain 3.2. For a step input of magnitude 20, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 3.4, K = 3.2, M = 20 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 3.2 * 20 | Answer: 64 units

question: A reactor operates at a space time of 19.9 min. Find its space velocity in per hour.
solution: Given: tau = 19.9 | Formula: SV = 60 / tau  (per hour) | Substitute: SV = 60 / 19.9 | Answer: 3.015 /h

question: An aircraft wing of area 115 m^2 flies at 200 m/s (air density 0.4 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.6. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 115, V = 200, rho = 0.4, CL = 0.6 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.4*(200)^2*115*0.6 / 1000 | Answer: 552 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 50 m^2 flies at 160 m/s (density 0.4 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.03. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 50, V = 160, rho = 0.4, CD = 0.03 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.4*(160)^2*50*0.03 / 1000 | Answer: 7.68 kN

question: Find the dynamic pressure for air of density 0.7 kg/m^3 moving at 70 m/s, in Pa.
solution: Given: rho = 0.7, V = 70 | Formula: q = 0.5 rho V^2 | Substitute: q = 0.5*0.7*(70)^2 | Answer: 1715 Pa

question: An aircraft flies at 410 m/s where the speed of sound is 310 m/s. Find the Mach number.
solution: Given: V = 410, a = 310 | Formula: M = V / a | Substitute: M = 410 / 310 | Answer: 1.323

question: Find the circular orbital velocity of a satellite at altitude 1700 km above Earth (Earth radius 6371 km, mu = 3.986e14 m^3/s^2), in km/s.
A specimen under stress 150 MPa shows an elastic strain of 2.3e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 150, eps = 2.3 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 150 / (2.3e-3) MPa = 65.22 GPa | Answer: 65.22 GPa

question: A block of mass 19 kg has a volume of 5e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 19, V = 5 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 19 / (5e-3) | Answer: 3800 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 2900 mm is heated through 115 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 11e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 2900, dT = 115, al = 11 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 2900*11e-6*115 | Answer: 3.668 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 165 ohm, R2 = 165 ohm and R3 = 40 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 165, R2 = 165, R3 = 40 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 165*40 / 165 | Answer: 40 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 1000 ohm and gauge factor 2.1 experiences a strain of 1050e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 1000, GF = 2.1, eps = 1050 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 1000*2.1*1050e-6 | Answer: 2205 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 10.03 when the true value is 20. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10.03, true = 20 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10.03 - 20| / 20 * 100 | Answer: 49.85 %

question: Annual demand is 31500 units, ordering cost 20 per order and holding cost 16 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 31500, S = 20, H = 16 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*31500*20 / 16) | Answer: 280.6 units

question: An asset costs 170000 with salvage value 24000 after 10 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 170000, Sv = 24000, n = 10 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (170000 - 24000) / 10 | Answer: 14600 per year

question: A product sells for 60 per unit with variable cost 50 per unit and fixed costs 150000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 60, V = 50, F = 150000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 150000 / (60 - 50) | Answer: 15000 units

question: Find the present worth of 125000 received 4 years from now at an interest rate of 11% per year.
solution: Given: F = 125000, n = 4, i = 11 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 125000 / (1 + 0.11)^4 | Answer: 82341 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.92, 0.93 and 0.92 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.92, r2 = 0.93, r3 = 0.92 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.92*0.93*0.92 | Answer: 0.7872

question: Two components each of reliability 0.73 are connected in parallel. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r = 0.73 | Formula: R_parallel = 1 - (1 - r)^2 | Substitute: R = 1 - (1 - 0.73)^2 | Answer: 0.9271

question: A process produces 40 defective items in a batch of 11000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 40, N = 11000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 40/11000 * 1e6 | Answer: 3636 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -2x^3 + x^2 + 9x - 5 evaluated at x = 4.
For f(x) = -6x^3 - 6x^2 + 3x + 1, find f''(x) at x = 2.
Evaluate the definite integral of (5x^2 + 2x + 1) dx from x = 0 to x = 6.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = 5x^3/3 + 2x^2/2 + 1x | Evaluate F(6) - F(0) | Answer: 402
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 3x^2 + 12x + 9 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[1, 4], [-5, 8]].
solution: Given: a = 1, b = 4, c = -5, d = 8 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (1)(8) - (4)(-5) | Answer: 28

question: Find the determinant of [[3, -3, -1], [2, -5, -4], [-4, -4, -5]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: -23

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[4, 1], [7, 5]].
solution: Trace tr = 9, Determinant = 13 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 7.193

question: Solve for x: 3x + 1y = 9 and -4x + 5y = -9.
solution: Determinant = 3*5 - 1*-4 = 19 | x = (e d - b f) / det = 2.842 | Answer: x = 2.842
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 34, 44, 67, 42, 81.
solution: Sum = 268 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 53.6 | Answer: 53.6

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 17, 2, 27, 15, 19.
solution: Mean = 16 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 9.055

question: Find the slope of the line through (6, -8) and (-8, 8).
solution: Given: x1 = 6, y1 = -8, x2 = -8, y2 = 8 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (8 - -8) / (-8 - 6) | Answer: -1.143

question: Find the distance between the points (-1, -9) and (4, -2).
solution: Given: x1 = -1, y1 = -9, x2 = 4, y2 = -2 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((5)^2 + (7)^2) | Answer: 8.602 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (2,4), (1,4), (7,-4).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 4 sq units

question: Evaluate the number of combinations C(11, 5).
solution: Given: n = 11, r = 5 | Formula: C(n, r) = n! / (r! (n - r)!) | Substitute: C(11, 5) = 11! / (5! * 6!) | Answer: 462

question: Evaluate the number of permutations P(12, 10).
solution: Given: n = 12, r = 10 | Formula: P(n, r) = n! / (n - r)! | Substitute: P(12, 10) = 12! / 2! | Answer: 239500800

question: Find the 29th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -4 and common difference 6.
solution: Given: a = -4, d = 6, n = 29 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -4 + (29 - 1)*6 | Answer: 164

question: Find the sum of the first 10 terms of an AP with first term 1 and common difference 5.
solution: Given: a = 1, d = 5, n = 10 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 10/2 [2*1 + (10-1)*5] | Answer: 235

question: Find the 4th term of a geometric progression with first term 8 and common ratio 3.
solution: Given: a = 8, r = 3, n = 4 | Formula: a_n = a r^(n-1) | Substitute: a_n = 8 * 3^(4-1) | Answer: 216

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 5500 at 6.2% per annum for 3 years.
solution: Given: P = 5500, R = 6.2, Tt = 3 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 5500 * 6.2 * 3 / 100 | Answer: 1023 currency units

question: Find the amount when 3500 is invested at 6.7% per annum compounded annually for 3 years.
solution: Given: P = 3500, R = 6.7, Tt = 3 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 3500 * (1 + 6.7/100)^3 | Answer: 4252 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (7, 1, 7) and (4, 2, -6).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (-4, 3, 3) and (5, -5, 3).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 36.47

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (6, 0, -3) and (3, 4, 1).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 63.99 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number 11 + -8i.
solution: Given: a = 11, b = -8 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((11)^2 + (-8)^2) | Answer: 13.6

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number 3 + -1i.
solution: Given: a = 3, b = -1 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(-1, 3) | Answer: -18.43 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -4x^3 - 4x^2 + 9x + 2 at x = -4.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-80 with initial guess x0=4, find x1 (one iteration).
solution: Given: N = 80, x0 = 4 | Formula: x1 = x0 - (x0^2 - N)/(2 x0) | Substitute: x1 = 4 - ((4)^2 - 80)/(2*4) | Answer: 12

question: Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.5 and ordinates 15, 13, 0, 8, 5, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 193 and 255.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 193 and 255 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 16 and 17.
solution: Given: a = 16, b = 17 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 16*17 / 1 | Answer: 272
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 28 mm carries an axial tensile load of 85 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 31 mm and length 2400 mm carries an axial load of 19 kN. Take E = 70 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 43 mm transmits a torque of 2350 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 43, Tt = 2350 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(2350*1000) / (pi*(43)^3) | Answer: 150.5 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 55 mm and length 1900 mm carries a torque of 1000 N-m. With G = 80 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (55)^4 / 32 = 898361 mm^4 | theta = (1000*1000)(1900) / (80000 * 898361) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 1.515 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 75 mm wide and 170 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 75, h = 170 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 75*(170)^2 / 6 | Answer: 361250 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (104 mm x 190 mm) carries a bending moment of 9 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (76 mm x 110 mm) has effective length 2100 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 560 MPa is designed for a working stress of 250 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 560, sw = 250 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 560 / 250 | Answer: 2.24

question: A steel bar is fully restrained and heated through 65 deg C. With E = 210 GPa and alpha = 12e-6 /deg C, find the thermal stress in MPa.
solution: Given: dT = 65, E = 210, al = 12 | Formula: sigma = E alpha (dT) | Substitute: sigma = 210000 * 12e-6 * 65 | Answer: 163.8 MPa

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 850 mm and wall thickness 9 mm carries an internal pressure of 1.1 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 850, t = 9, P = 1.1 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 1.1*850 / (2*9) | Answer: 51.94 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 940 K and 350 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 940, Tc = 350 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 350/940) * 100 | Answer: 62.77 %

question: A refrigerator works between 261 K (cold) and 328 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 261, Th = 328 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 261 / (328 - 261) | Answer: 3.896

question: A heat pump operates between 267 K and 310 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 267, Th = 310 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 310 / (310 - 267) | Answer: 7.209

question: 1.7 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 200 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1.7, dT = 200 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 1.7 * 0.718 * 200 | Answer: 244.1 kJ

question: 7.7 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 200 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 7.7, dT = 200 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 7.7 * 1.005 * 200 | Answer: 1548 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 2.7 m^3 at 480 K with mass 2.5 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 2.7, Tk = 480, m = 2.5 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 2.5*0.287*480 / 2.7 | Answer: 127.6 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 1.9 kg of air expands isothermally at 460 K from volume V1 to 4*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1.9, Tk = 460, ratio = 4 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 1.9*0.287*460*ln(4) | Answer: 347.7 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 3.5 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.28 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 3.5, D = 0.28 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*3.5*0.28 / 0.001 | Answer: 980000

question: Water flows at 1 m/s through a pipe of diameter 70 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 6.6 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 6.6 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*6.6 / 1000 | Answer: 64.75 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 4.5 m. Taking Cv = 0.99, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 4.5, cv = 0.99 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.99*sqrt(2*9.81*4.5) | Answer: 9.302 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 170 mm) water flows at 0.5 m/s. It contracts to diameter 70 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 170, d2 = 70, V1 = 0.5 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 0.5*(170/70)^2 | Answer: 2.949 m/s

question: Water flows at 3.8 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.46 m and length 180 m. With friction factor f = 0.028, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 27 teeth drives a gear of 84 teeth. If the pinion runs at 550 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 27, z2 = 84, N1 = 550 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 550*27 / 84 | Answer: 176.8 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 440 mm rotates at 950 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 440, N = 950 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.44)*950 / 60 | Answer: 21.89 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 34 kW at 650 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 34, N = 650 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(34*1000) / (2*pi*650) | Answer: 499.5 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 6.6 kg rotates at radius 0.59 m at 750 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 8800 N/m and mass 16.2 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 8800, m = 16.2 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(8800/16.2) | Answer: 3.709 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 6.2 m^2 and thickness 0.18 m has conductivity k = 29.6 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 20 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 6.2, L = 0.18, k = 29.6, dT = 20 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 29.6*6.2*20 / 0.18 | Answer: 20391 W

question: A surface of area 1.9 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 100 W/m^2-K to surroundings 30 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 1.9, h = 100, dT = 30 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 100*1.9*30 | Answer: 5700 W

question: In a counter-flow heat exchanger the terminal temperature differences are 50 deg C and 35 deg C. Find the log mean temperature difference (LMTD) in deg C.
solution: Given: dT1 = 50, dT2 = 35 | Formula: LMTD = (dT1 - dT2) / ln(dT1/dT2) | Substitute: LMTD = (50 - 35) / ln(50/35) | Answer: 42.06 deg C

question: In turning, cutting speed = 130 m/min, feed = 0.4 mm/rev, depth of cut = 1.7 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 130, f = 0.4, d = 1.7 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*130*0.4*1.7 | Answer: 88400 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 350 mm is turned at 600 rpm with a feed of 0.31 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 350, N = 600, f = 0.31 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 350 / (0.31*600) | Answer: 1.882 min

question: A resistor of 117 ohm carries a current of 1 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 117, I = 1 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 1 * 117 | Answer: 117 V

question: Three resistors 73 ohm, 95 ohm and 64 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 73, R2 = 95, R3 = 64 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 73 + 95 + 64 | Answer: 232 ohm

question: Two resistors 51 ohm and 101 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 51, R2 = 101 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 51*101 / (51+101) | Answer: 33.89 ohm

question: A device draws 14.7 A at 55 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 55, I = 14.7 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 55 * 14.7 | Answer: 808.5 W

question: A current of 2.5 A flows through a 111 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 2.5, R = 111 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (2.5)^2 * 111 | Answer: 693.8 W

question: Two capacitors 4.2 uF and 28.4 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 4.2, C2 = 28.4 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 4.2*28.4 / (4.2+28.4) | Answer: 3.659 uF

question: A resistor 99 kohm and capacitor 7.2 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 99, C = 7.2 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (99k)(7.2u) = 712.8 ms | Answer: 712.8 ms

question: An inductor 254 mH is in series with 200 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 254, R = 200 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (254e-3) / 200 | Answer: 1.27 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 12.3 mH inductor at 320 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 12.3, f = 320 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (320)(12.3e-3) | Answer: 24.73 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 33.3 uF capacitor at 320 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 33.3, f = 320 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (320)(33.3e-6)) | Answer: 14.94 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 66 ohm, XL = 64 ohm and XC = 67 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 66, XL = 64, XC = 67 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(66^2 + (64 - 67)^2) | Answer: 66.07 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 22.2 mH and C = 2.8 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 22.2, C = 2.8 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(22.2e-3 * 2.8e-6)) | Answer: 638.4 Hz

question: A capacitor of 56.7 uF is charged to 380 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 56.7, V = 380 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*56.7e-6*(380)^2 | Answer: 4094 mJ

question: An alternating voltage has a peak value of 194 V. Find its RMS value.
solution: Given: Vp = 194 | Formula: Vrms = Vp / sqrt(2) | Substitute: Vrms = 194 / sqrt(2) | Answer: 137.2 V

question: A transformer has primary voltage 280 V with 510 primary turns and 260 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 280, N1 = 510, N2 = 260 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 280 * 260/510 | Answer: 142.7 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 140 V and draws an armature current of 22 A. If the armature resistance is 0.61 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 140, Ia = 22, Ra = 0.61 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 140 - 22*0.61 | Answer: 126.6 V

question: A 4-pole induction motor on a 50 Hz supply runs at 830 rpm. Find the slip (%).
formula: s = (Ns - N) / Ns,  Ns = 120 f / P

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 85 A at 433 V (line) with a power factor of 0.9. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 85, VL = 433, pf = 0.9 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*433*85*0.9 / 1000 | Answer: 57.37 kW

question: A load has real power 95 kW and apparent power 180 kVA. Find the power factor.
