solution: Given: P = 95, S = 180 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 95 / 180 | Answer: 0.5278

question: A machine delivers 100 kW output while drawing 172 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 100, Pi = 172 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 100/172 * 100 | Answer: 58.14 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 26 V across R1 = 28 ohm and R2 = 28 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 26, R1 = 28, R2 = 28 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 26*28 / (28+28) | Answer: 13 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 190 kohm and Rin = 18 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 190, Rin = 18 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 190 / 18 | Answer: 10.56

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 120 kohm and Rg = 45 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 120, Rg = 45 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 120/45 | Answer: 3.667

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 2930. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 2930 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(2930) | Answer: 34.67 dB

question: A first-order system has a time constant of 8.7 s. Find the time (in s) to reach 63.2% of its final value.
solution: For a first-order step response, y = 1 - e^(-t/tau) | y = 0.632 when t = tau | Answer: 8.7 s
formula: At t = tau the response reaches 63.2% (one time constant)

question: A signal is sampled at 18 kHz. According to the Nyquist criterion, what is the maximum signal frequency that can be represented (in kHz)?
solution: Given: fs = 18 | Formula: f_max = fs / 2 | Substitute: f_max = 18 / 2 | Answer: 9 kHz

question: A simply supported beam of span 8.7 m carries a central point load of 55 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 8.7, W = 55 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 55*8.7 / 4 | Answer: 119.6 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.3 m carries a UDL of 60 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6.3, w = 60 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 60*(6.3)^2 / 8 | Answer: 297.7 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 3.1 m carries a point load 80 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.1, W = 80 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 80*3.1 | Answer: 248 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 1.4 m carries a UDL of 6 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 1.4, w = 6 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 6*(1.4)^2 / 2 | Answer: 5.88 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 7.1 m carries a point load 30 kN at distance 1.8 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 7.1, a = 1.8, W = 30 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 30*(7.1 - 1.8) / 7.1 | Answer: 22.39 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 4.9 m) carries a central point load 40 kN. With E = 25 GPa and I = 380e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=40000 N, L=4900.0 mm, E=25000 MPa, I=380e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 10.32 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 5.3 m carries a UDL of 42 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.3, w = 42 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 42*(5.3)^2 / 12 | Answer: 98.31 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 680 mm, clear cover 45 mm and main bars of diameter 12 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 680, c = 45, dia = 12 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 680 - 45 - 12/2 | Answer: 629 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 10.1 m^2 carrying a factored load of 9.9 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 10.1, w = 9.9 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 9.9 * 10.1 | Answer: 99.99 kN

question: For a bar of diameter 16 mm with design bond stress 1.9 MPa and steel stress 360 MPa, find the development length in mm.
solution: Given: dia = 16, tbd = 1.9, fs = 360 | Formula: Ld = phi fs / (4 tau_bd) | Substitute: Ld = 16*360 / (4*1.9) | Answer: 757.9 mm

question: A soil sample has porosity n = 0.52. Find its void ratio e.
solution: Given: n = 0.52 | Formula: e = n / (1 - n) | Substitute: e = 0.52 / (1 - 0.52) | Answer: 1.083

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 4.2 m, unit weight 16 kN/m^3, phi = 31 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 8.5 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 19 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 8.5, g = 19 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (19 - 9.81)*8.5 | Answer: 78.11 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 6.2e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.7, area = 1.9e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 6.2, i = 0.7, A = 1.9 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (6.2e-4)*0.7*(1.9e-3) | Answer: 824.6 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 0.7 m, bed slope 0.002 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.03. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 3.7 m under a head of 0.5 m. Taking Cd = 0.64 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 2.3 m wide carries a discharge of 17.9 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 570 m and design speed 55 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 570, V = 55 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (55)^2 / (127*570) | Answer: 0.04179
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: For a design speed of 65 km/h with allowable superelevation 0.08 and lateral friction 0.16, find the minimum curve radius in m.
A tank of volume 160 m^3 treats a flow of 50 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 160, Q = 50 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 160 / 50 | Answer: 3.2 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 370 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.24 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 5 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 370, k = 0.24, t = 5 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 370*(1 - e^(-0.24*5)) | Answer: 258.6 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.57, rainfall intensity 100 mm/h over a catchment of 53.6 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.57, i = 100, A = 53.6 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.57*100*53.6 / 360 | Answer: 8.487 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.03 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 160 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.03, M = 160 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 160*(30+0.03)/30 | Answer: 160.2 m

question: Convert the decimal number 141 to binary.
solution: Divide 141 by 2 repeatedly, recording remainders | Reading remainders in reverse gives 10001101 | Answer: 10001101 (binary)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 2 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the decimal number 3383 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 3383 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: D37 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the 8-bit binary number 10111111 to decimal.
solution: Binary 10111111 = sum of bit-weights | Answer: 191 (decimal)
formula: Sum each bit times its positional weight (2^i)

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 01111011 and 10111000.
solution: XOR: 11000011 | Count of 1s = 4 | Answer: 4
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 900 megabits is sent over a link of 15 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 900, B = 15 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 900 / 15 | Answer: 60 s

question: A link has bandwidth 55 Mbps and round-trip time 190 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 55, R = 190 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 55e6 * 190e-3 bits = 10450 kb | Answer: 10450 kilobits

question: A channel has bandwidth 13 kHz. Using Nyquist's theorem with 8 signal levels, find the maximum data rate in kbps (noiseless).
solution: Given: B = 13, M = 8 | Formula: C = 2 B log2(M) | Substitute: C = 2*13*log2(8) | Answer: 78 kbps

question: A channel of bandwidth 9 kHz has a signal-to-noise ratio of 7 (linear). Using Shannon's theorem, find the channel capacity in kbps.
solution: Given: B = 9, SNR = 7 | Formula: C = B log2(1 + SNR) | Substitute: C = 9*log2(1 + 7) | Answer: 27 kbps

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.88, cache access time 6 ns and main-memory access time 70 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.88, tc = 6, tm = 70 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.88*6 + (1 - 0.88)*70 | Answer: 13.68 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 426839 elements?
solution: Given: n = 426839 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(426839)) + 1 | Answer: 19

question: An O(n^2) algorithm performs c*n^2 basic operations. If c = 1 and n = 760, how many operations are performed?
solution: Given: n = 760 | Formula: operations = n^2 | Substitute: = (760)^2 | Answer: 577600

question: A program is 60% parallelisable and run on 2 processors. Using Amdahl's law, find the maximum speedup.
solution: Parallel fraction f = 0.6 | S = 1 / ((1 - 0.6) + 0.6/2) | Answer: 1.429x speedup

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.013, memory access time 180 ns and page-fault service time 3 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 3 ms = 3000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.013)*180 + 0.013*3000000.0 ns | Answer: 39.18 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: A modem transmits at 4200 baud using 4-level signalling. Find the bit rate in bps.
solution: Given: baud = 4200, M = 4 | Formula: bit rate = baud * log2(M) | Substitute: bit rate = 4200 * log2(4) | Answer: 8400 bps

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 2.1 m^3 at 350 kPa and 380 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 2.1, P = 350, Tk = 380 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (350e3)*2.1 / (8.314*380) | Answer: 232.6 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.09 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 10 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.09, t = 10 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.09*10) | Answer: 0.5934

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.22 /min) is to reach 55% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.22, X = 55 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.55) / 0.22 | Answer: 3.63 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.32 /min) reaches 75% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.32, X = 75 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.75 / (0.32*(1 - 0.75)) | Answer: 9.375 min

question: A first-order reaction has a rate constant of 0.14 /min. Find its half-life in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.14 | Formula: t_half = ln(2) / k | Substitute: t_half = 0.6931 / 0.14 | Answer: 4.951 min

question: For a reaction with A = 8e10 /s and activation energy 65 kJ/mol at 330 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 8, Ea = 65, Tk = 330 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 8e10 * exp(-65e3 / (8.314*330)) | Answer: 4.112 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.94 and bottoms xW = 0.05, with relative volatility alpha = 3. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.94, xw = 0.05, al = 3 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.94/0.06)(0.95/0.05)] / ln(3) | Answer: 5.185 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.81 and x = 0.4. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.81, x = 0.4 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.81/0.19) / (0.4/0.6) | Answer: 6.395

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.36 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 85 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.36, Psat = 85 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.36 * 85 | Answer: 30.6 kPa

question: A stream of 2.3 kg/s with specific heat 2.1 kJ/kg-K is heated through 65 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 2.3, cp = 2.1, dT = 65 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 2.3*2.1*65 | Answer: 313.9 kW

question: A reactor of volume 18.6 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 2 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 18.6, Q = 2 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 18.6 / 2 | Answer: 9.3 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 7.1e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 2 mm with a concentration difference of 90 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 7.1, L = 2, dC = 90 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (7.1e-9)*90 / (2e-3) | Answer: 319.5 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 8.5 min and steady-state gain 3. For a step input of magnitude 15, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 8.5, K = 3, M = 15 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 3 * 15 | Answer: 45 units

question: A reactor operates at a space time of 2.8 min. Find its space velocity in per hour.
solution: Given: tau = 2.8 | Formula: SV = 60 / tau  (per hour) | Substitute: SV = 60 / 2.8 | Answer: 21.43 /h

question: An aircraft wing of area 15 m^2 flies at 80 m/s (air density 1 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.7. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 15, V = 80, rho = 1, CL = 0.7 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1*(80)^2*15*0.7 / 1000 | Answer: 33.6 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 55 m^2 flies at 140 m/s (density 0.7 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.06. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 55, V = 140, rho = 0.7, CD = 0.06 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.7*(140)^2*55*0.06 / 1000 | Answer: 22.64 kN

question: Find the dynamic pressure for air of density 0.7 kg/m^3 moving at 130 m/s, in Pa.
solution: Given: rho = 0.7, V = 130 | Formula: q = 0.5 rho V^2 | Substitute: q = 0.5*0.7*(130)^2 | Answer: 5915 Pa

question: An aircraft flies at 550 m/s where the speed of sound is 295 m/s. Find the Mach number.
solution: Given: V = 550, a = 295 | Formula: M = V / a | Substitute: M = 550 / 295 | Answer: 1.864

question: Find the circular orbital velocity of a satellite at altitude 1750 km above Earth (Earth radius 6371 km, mu = 3.986e14 m^3/s^2), in km/s.
A specimen under stress 140 MPa shows an elastic strain of 2.7e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 140, eps = 2.7 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 140 / (2.7e-3) MPa = 51.85 GPa | Answer: 51.85 GPa

question: A block of mass 2 kg has a volume of 1.1e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 2, V = 1.1 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 2 / (1.1e-3) | Answer: 1818 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 1200 mm is heated through 55 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 23e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 1200, dT = 55, al = 23 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 1200*23e-6*55 | Answer: 1.518 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 20 ohm, R2 = 80 ohm and R3 = 240 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 20, R2 = 80, R3 = 240 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 80*240 / 20 | Answer: 960 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 1000 ohm and gauge factor 2.1 experiences a strain of 1950e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 1000, GF = 2.1, eps = 1950 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 1000*2.1*1950e-6 | Answer: 4095 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 9.62 when the true value is 100. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.62, true = 100 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.62 - 100| / 100 * 100 | Answer: 90.38 %

question: Annual demand is 1500 units, ordering cost 30 per order and holding cost 28 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 1500, S = 30, H = 28 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*1500*30 / 28) | Answer: 56.69 units

question: An asset costs 460000 with salvage value 8000 after 13 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 460000, Sv = 8000, n = 13 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (460000 - 8000) / 13 | Answer: 34769 per year

question: A product sells for 210 per unit with variable cost 90 per unit and fixed costs 125000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 210, V = 90, F = 125000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 125000 / (210 - 90) | Answer: 1042 units

question: Find the present worth of 200000 received 2 years from now at an interest rate of 5% per year.
solution: Given: F = 200000, n = 2, i = 5 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 200000 / (1 + 0.05)^2 | Answer: 181406 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.97, 0.94 and 0.92 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.97, r2 = 0.94, r3 = 0.92 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.97*0.94*0.92 | Answer: 0.8389

question: A process produces 32 defective items in a batch of 18000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 32, N = 18000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 32/18000 * 1e6 | Answer: 1778 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -2x^3 - 3x^2 + 9 evaluated at x = -4.
For f(x) = -4x^3 + 4x^2 + 5x - 6, find f''(x) at x = -1.
Evaluate the definite integral of (3x^2 + 6x + 5) dx from x = 2 to x = 6.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = 3x^3/3 + 6x^2/2 + 5x | Evaluate F(6) - F(2) | Answer: 324
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of x^2 - 9x - 6 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[4, -1], [4, -4]].
solution: Given: a = 4, b = -1, c = 4, d = -4 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (4)(-4) - (-1)(4) | Answer: -12

question: Find the determinant of [[1, 5, -1], [6, 1, -3], [1, -2, -6]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: 166

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[-1, -4], [-8, -3]].
solution: Trace tr = -4, Determinant = -29 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 3.745

question: Solve for x: -2x + 0y = -8 and 4x + -3y = 3.
solution: Determinant = -2*-3 - 0*4 = 6 | x = (e d - b f) / det = 4 | Answer: x = 4
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 27, 95, 85, 80, 59.
solution: Sum = 346 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 69.2 | Answer: 69.2

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 21, 48, 1, 3, 29.
solution: Mean = 20.4 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 19.46

question: Find the slope of the line through (-9, 9) and (-4, 6).
solution: Given: x1 = -9, y1 = 9, x2 = -4, y2 = 6 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (6 - 9) / (-4 - -9) | Answer: -0.6

question: Find the distance between the points (-9, -7) and (-7, 0).
solution: Given: x1 = -9, y1 = -7, x2 = -7, y2 = 0 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((2)^2 + (7)^2) | Answer: 7.28 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (-6,-7), (-1,1), (2,-4).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 24.5 sq units

question: Evaluate the number of combinations C(18, 6).
solution: Given: n = 18, r = 6 | Formula: C(n, r) = n! / (r! (n - r)!) | Substitute: C(18, 6) = 18! / (6! * 12!) | Answer: 18564

question: Evaluate the number of permutations P(6, 3).
solution: Given: n = 6, r = 3 | Formula: P(n, r) = n! / (n - r)! | Substitute: P(6, 3) = 6! / 3! | Answer: 120

question: Find the 12th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 4 and common difference 0.
solution: Given: a = 4, d = 0, n = 12 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = 4 + (12 - 1)*0 | Answer: 4

question: Find the sum of the first 24 terms of an AP with first term -14 and common difference 6.
solution: Given: a = -14, d = 6, n = 24 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 24/2 [2*-14 + (24-1)*6] | Answer: 1320

question: Find the 7th term of a geometric progression with first term 9 and common ratio 2.
solution: Given: a = 9, r = 2, n = 7 | Formula: a_n = a r^(n-1) | Substitute: a_n = 9 * 2^(7-1) | Answer: 576

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 48500 at 9.8% per annum for 8 years.
solution: Given: P = 48500, R = 9.8, Tt = 8 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 48500 * 9.8 * 8 / 100 | Answer: 38024 currency units

question: Find the amount when 7000 is invested at 8.8% per annum compounded annually for 3 years.
solution: Given: P = 7000, R = 8.8, Tt = 3 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 7000 * (1 + 8.8/100)^3 | Answer: 9015 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (4, -5, -7) and (2, -6, -2).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (5, 0, 4) and (-5, 1, 6).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 50.41

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (5, 1, -5) and (2, -1, -4).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 27.61 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number -6 + -2i.
solution: Given: a = -6, b = -2 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((-6)^2 + (-2)^2) | Answer: 6.325

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number -5 + 3i.
solution: Given: a = -5, b = 3 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(3, -5) | Answer: 149 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = 2x^3 + 6x^2 + 6x + 7 at x = 4.
solution: Given: a = 2, b = 6, c = 6, d = 7, x0 = 4 | Formula: f(x0) = a x0^3 + b x0^2 + c x0 + d | Substitute: f(4) = 2(4)^3 + 6(4)^2 + 6(4) + 7 | Answer: 255

question: Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-155 with initial guess x0=5, find x1 (one iteration).
solution: Given: N = 155, x0 = 5 | Formula: x1 = x0 - (x0^2 - N)/(2 x0) | Substitute: x1 = 5 - ((5)^2 - 155)/(2*5) | Answer: 18

question: Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.4 and ordinates 12, 9, 10, 2, 7, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 130 and 91.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 130 and 91 | Answer: GCD = 13

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 12 and 42.
solution: Given: a = 12, b = 42 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 12*42 / 6 | Answer: 84
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 30 mm carries an axial tensile load of 22 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 29 mm and length 1400 mm carries an axial load of 10 kN. Take E = 70 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 52 mm transmits a torque of 1600 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 52, Tt = 1600 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(1600*1000) / (pi*(52)^3) | Answer: 57.95 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 38 mm and length 2000 mm carries a torque of 1550 N-m. With G = 45 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (38)^4 / 32 = 204708 mm^4 | theta = (1550*1000)(2000) / (45000 * 204708) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 19.28 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 92 mm wide and 160 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 92, h = 160 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 92*(160)^2 / 6 | Answer: 392533 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (54 mm x 80 mm) carries a bending moment of 21 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (46 mm x 110 mm) has effective length 2600 mm and E = 200 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 460 MPa is designed for a working stress of 70 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 460, sw = 70 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 460 / 70 | Answer: 6.571

question: A steel bar is fully restrained and heated through 80 deg C. With E = 200 GPa and alpha = 11e-6 /deg C, find the thermal stress in MPa.
solution: Given: dT = 80, E = 200, al = 11 | Formula: sigma = E alpha (dT) | Substitute: sigma = 200000 * 11e-6 * 80 | Answer: 176 MPa

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 300 mm and wall thickness 11 mm carries an internal pressure of 2.6 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 300, t = 11, P = 2.6 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 2.6*300 / (2*11) | Answer: 35.45 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 980 K and 410 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 980, Tc = 410 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 410/980) * 100 | Answer: 58.16 %

question: A refrigerator works between 272 K (cold) and 306 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 272, Th = 306 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 272 / (306 - 272) | Answer: 8

question: A heat pump operates between 274 K and 330 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 274, Th = 330 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 330 / (330 - 274) | Answer: 5.893

question: 5.3 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 95 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 5.3, dT = 95 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 5.3 * 0.718 * 95 | Answer: 361.5 kJ

question: 7.5 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 115 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 7.5, dT = 115 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 7.5 * 1.005 * 115 | Answer: 866.8 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 3.9 m^3 at 380 K with mass 3.5 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 3.9, Tk = 380, m = 3.5 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 3.5*0.287*380 / 3.9 | Answer: 97.87 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 3.9 kg of air expands isothermally at 470 K from volume V1 to 5*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.9, Tk = 470, ratio = 5 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 3.9*0.287*470*ln(5) | Answer: 846.7 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 3.6 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.23 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 3.6, D = 0.23 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*3.6*0.23 / 0.001 | Answer: 828000

question: Water flows at 3.9 m/s through a pipe of diameter 180 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 16.7 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 16.7 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*16.7 / 1000 | Answer: 163.8 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 17.9 m. Taking Cv = 0.96, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 17.9, cv = 0.96 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.96*sqrt(2*9.81*17.9) | Answer: 17.99 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 200 mm) water flows at 1.7 m/s. It contracts to diameter 60 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 200, d2 = 60, V1 = 1.7 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 1.7*(200/60)^2 | Answer: 18.89 m/s

question: Water flows at 2.2 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.34 m and length 180 m. With friction factor f = 0.025, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 27 teeth drives a gear of 91 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1050 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 27, z2 = 91, N1 = 1050 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1050*27 / 91 | Answer: 311.5 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 150 mm rotates at 550 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 150, N = 550 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.15)*550 / 60 | Answer: 4.32 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 14.6 kW at 350 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 14.6, N = 350 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(14.6*1000) / (2*pi*350) | Answer: 398.3 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 8.3 kg rotates at radius 0.4 m at 300 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 18100 N/m and mass 2.7 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 18100, m = 2.7 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(18100/2.7) | Answer: 13.03 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 4.5 m^2 and thickness 0.34 m has conductivity k = 16 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 65 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 4.5, L = 0.34, k = 16, dT = 65 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 16*4.5*65 / 0.34 | Answer: 13765 W

question: A surface of area 2.2 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 175 W/m^2-K to surroundings 30 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 2.2, h = 175, dT = 30 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 175*2.2*30 | Answer: 11550 W

question: In a counter-flow heat exchanger the terminal temperature differences are 120 deg C and 10 deg C. Find the log mean temperature difference (LMTD) in deg C.
solution: Given: dT1 = 120, dT2 = 10 | Formula: LMTD = (dT1 - dT2) / ln(dT1/dT2) | Substitute: LMTD = (120 - 10) / ln(120/10) | Answer: 44.27 deg C

question: In turning, cutting speed = 250 m/min, feed = 0.4 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2.6 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 250, f = 0.4, d = 2.6 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*250*0.4*2.6 | Answer: 260000 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 310 mm is turned at 550 rpm with a feed of 0.34 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 310, N = 550, f = 0.34 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 310 / (0.34*550) | Answer: 1.658 min

question: A resistor of 101 ohm carries a current of 2.1 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 101, I = 2.1 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 2.1 * 101 | Answer: 212.1 V

question: Three resistors 65 ohm, 6 ohm and 30 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 65, R2 = 6, R3 = 30 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 65 + 6 + 30 | Answer: 101 ohm

question: Two resistors 116 ohm and 10 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 116, R2 = 10 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 116*10 / (116+10) | Answer: 9.206 ohm

question: A device draws 8.8 A at 40 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 40, I = 8.8 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 40 * 8.8 | Answer: 352 W

question: A current of 0.7 A flows through a 144 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 0.7, R = 144 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (0.7)^2 * 144 | Answer: 70.56 W

question: Two capacitors 24.4 uF and 34.2 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 24.4, C2 = 34.2 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 24.4*34.2 / (24.4+34.2) | Answer: 14.24 uF

question: A resistor 15 kohm and capacitor 9.2 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 15, C = 9.2 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (15k)(9.2u) = 138 ms | Answer: 138 ms

question: An inductor 48.4 mH is in series with 137 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 48.4, R = 137 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (48.4e-3) / 137 | Answer: 0.3533 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 82.8 mH inductor at 580 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 82.8, f = 580 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (580)(82.8e-3) | Answer: 301.7 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 41.7 uF capacitor at 600 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 41.7, f = 600 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (600)(41.7e-6)) | Answer: 6.361 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 43 ohm, XL = 41 ohm and XC = 101 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 43, XL = 41, XC = 101 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(43^2 + (41 - 101)^2) | Answer: 73.82 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 82.2 mH and C = 3.6 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 82.2, C = 3.6 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(82.2e-3 * 3.6e-6)) | Answer: 292.6 Hz

question: A capacitor of 85.7 uF is charged to 275 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 85.7, V = 275 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*85.7e-6*(275)^2 | Answer: 3241 mJ

question: An alternating voltage has a peak value of 234 V. Find its RMS value.
solution: Given: Vp = 234 | Formula: Vrms = Vp / sqrt(2) | Substitute: Vrms = 234 / sqrt(2) | Answer: 165.5 V

question: A transformer has primary voltage 270 V with 800 primary turns and 470 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 270, N1 = 800, N2 = 470 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 270 * 470/800 | Answer: 158.6 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 220 V and draws an armature current of 6 A. If the armature resistance is 1.09 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 220, Ia = 6, Ra = 1.09 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 220 - 6*1.09 | Answer: 213.5 V

question: A 8-pole induction motor on a 50 Hz supply runs at 720 rpm. Find the slip (%).
formula: s = (Ns - N) / Ns,  Ns = 120 f / P

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 200 A at 433 V (line) with a power factor of 0.97. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 200, VL = 433, pf = 0.97 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*433*200*0.97 / 1000 | Answer: 145.5 kW

question: A load has real power 10 kW and apparent power 20 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 10, S = 20 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 10 / 20 | Answer: 0.5

question: A machine delivers 170 kW output while drawing 182 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 170, Pi = 182 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 170/182 * 100 | Answer: 93.41 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 29 V across R1 = 30 ohm and R2 = 34 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 29, R1 = 30, R2 = 34 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 29*34 / (30+34) | Answer: 15.41 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 120 kohm and Rin = 27 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 120, Rin = 27 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 120 / 27 | Answer: 4.444

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 60 kohm and Rg = 9 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 60, Rg = 9 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 60/9 | Answer: 7.667

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 3844. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 3844 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(3844) | Answer: 35.85 dB

question: A first-order system has a time constant of 1 s. Find the time (in s) to reach 63.2% of its final value.
solution: For a first-order step response, y = 1 - e^(-t/tau) | y = 0.632 when t = tau | Answer: 1 s
formula: At t = tau the response reaches 63.2% (one time constant)

question: A signal is sampled at 12 kHz. According to the Nyquist criterion, what is the maximum signal frequency that can be represented (in kHz)?
solution: Given: fs = 12 | Formula: f_max = fs / 2 | Substitute: f_max = 12 / 2 | Answer: 6 kHz

question: A simply supported beam of span 3.6 m carries a central point load of 60 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.6, W = 60 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 60*3.6 / 4 | Answer: 54 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 3.1 m carries a UDL of 60 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.1, w = 60 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 60*(3.1)^2 / 8 | Answer: 72.08 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 4.5 m carries a point load 80 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.5, W = 80 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 80*4.5 | Answer: 360 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 3.8 m carries a UDL of 24 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.8, w = 24 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 24*(3.8)^2 / 2 | Answer: 173.3 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 5.8 m carries a point load 50 kN at distance 2.6 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 5.8, a = 2.6, W = 50 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 50*(5.8 - 2.6) / 5.8 | Answer: 27.59 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 4.1 m) carries a central point load 80 kN. With E = 30 GPa and I = 530e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=80000 N, L=4100.0 mm, E=30000 MPa, I=530e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 7.224 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 4.1 m carries a UDL of 39 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.1, w = 39 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 39*(4.1)^2 / 12 | Answer: 54.63 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 340 mm, clear cover 25 mm and main bars of diameter 16 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 340, c = 25, dia = 16 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 340 - 25 - 16/2 | Answer: 307 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 13.7 m^2 carrying a factored load of 10.6 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 13.7, w = 10.6 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 10.6 * 13.7 | Answer: 145.2 kN

question: For a bar of diameter 12 mm with design bond stress 1.5 MPa and steel stress 435 MPa, find the development length in mm.
solution: Given: dia = 12, tbd = 1.5, fs = 435 | Formula: Ld = phi fs / (4 tau_bd) | Substitute: Ld = 12*435 / (4*1.5) | Answer: 870 mm

question: A soil sample has porosity n = 0.49. Find its void ratio e.
solution: Given: n = 0.49 | Formula: e = n / (1 - n) | Substitute: e = 0.49 / (1 - 0.49) | Answer: 0.9608

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 3.9 m, unit weight 19 kN/m^3, phi = 30 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 10.9 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 19 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 10.9, g = 19 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (19 - 9.81)*10.9 | Answer: 100.2 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 6.9e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.7, area = 5.5e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 6.9, i = 0.7, A = 5.5 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (6.9e-4)*0.7*(5.5e-3) | Answer: 2656 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 0.8 m, bed slope 0.001 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.023. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 2.1 m under a head of 0.5 m. Taking Cd = 0.62 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 6 m wide carries a discharge of 29.1 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 600 m and design speed 70 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 600, V = 70 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (70)^2 / (127*600) | Answer: 0.0643
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: For a design speed of 80 km/h with allowable superelevation 0.06 and lateral friction 0.13, find the minimum curve radius in m.
A tank of volume 960 m^3 treats a flow of 65 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 960, Q = 65 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 960 / 65 | Answer: 14.77 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 240 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.23 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 6 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 240, k = 0.23, t = 6 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 240*(1 - e^(-0.23*6)) | Answer: 179.6 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.56, rainfall intensity 65 mm/h over a catchment of 8.5 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.56, i = 65, A = 8.5 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.56*65*8.5 / 360 | Answer: 0.8594 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.07 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 750 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.07, M = 750 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 750*(30+0.07)/30 | Answer: 751.8 m

question: Convert the decimal number 11 to binary.
solution: Divide 11 by 2 repeatedly, recording remainders | Reading remainders in reverse gives 1011 | Answer: 1011 (binary)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 2 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the decimal number 283 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 283 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 11B (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the 8-bit binary number 00011110 to decimal.
solution: Binary 00011110 = sum of bit-weights | Answer: 30 (decimal)
formula: Sum each bit times its positional weight (2^i)

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 11100010 and 10011110.
solution: XOR: 01111100 | Count of 1s = 5 | Answer: 5
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 70 megabits is sent over a link of 44 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 70, B = 44 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 70 / 44 | Answer: 1.591 s

question: A link has bandwidth 89 Mbps and round-trip time 100 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 89, R = 100 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 89e6 * 100e-3 bits = 8900 kb | Answer: 8900 kilobits

question: A channel has bandwidth 15 kHz. Using Nyquist's theorem with 8 signal levels, find the maximum data rate in kbps (noiseless).
solution: Given: B = 15, M = 8 | Formula: C = 2 B log2(M) | Substitute: C = 2*15*log2(8) | Answer: 90 kbps

question: A channel of bandwidth 17 kHz has a signal-to-noise ratio of 31 (linear). Using Shannon's theorem, find the channel capacity in kbps.
solution: Given: B = 17, SNR = 31 | Formula: C = B log2(1 + SNR) | Substitute: C = 17*log2(1 + 31) | Answer: 85 kbps

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.98, cache access time 1 ns and main-memory access time 170 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.98, tc = 1, tm = 170 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.98*1 + (1 - 0.98)*170 | Answer: 4.38 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 265618 elements?
solution: Given: n = 265618 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(265618)) + 1 | Answer: 19

question: An O(n^2) algorithm performs c*n^2 basic operations. If c = 1 and n = 1130, how many operations are performed?
solution: Given: n = 1130 | Formula: operations = n^2 | Substitute: = (1130)^2 | Answer: 1276900

question: A program is 80% parallelisable and run on 4 processors. Using Amdahl's law, find the maximum speedup.
solution: Parallel fraction f = 0.8 | S = 1 / ((1 - 0.8) + 0.8/4) | Answer: 2.5x speedup

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.014, memory access time 170 ns and page-fault service time 5 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.

question: A modem transmits at 2700 baud using 4-level signalling. Find the bit rate in bps.
solution: Given: baud = 2700, M = 4 | Formula: bit rate = baud * log2(M) | Substitute: bit rate = 2700 * log2(4) | Answer: 5400 bps

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 1.8 m^3 at 480 kPa and 330 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 1.8, P = 480, Tk = 330 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (480e3)*1.8 / (8.314*330) | Answer: 314.9 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.11 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 19 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.11, t = 19 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.11*19) | Answer: 0.8763

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.36 /min) is to reach 75% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.36, X = 75 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.75) / 0.36 | Answer: 3.851 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.24 /min) reaches 50% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.24, X = 50 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.5 / (0.24*(1 - 0.5)) | Answer: 4.167 min

question: A first-order reaction has a rate constant of 0.09 /min. Find its half-life in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.09 | Formula: t_half = ln(2) / k | Substitute: t_half = 0.6931 / 0.09 | Answer: 7.702 min

question: For a reaction with A = 2e10 /s and activation energy 75 kJ/mol at 310 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 2, Ea = 75, Tk = 310 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 2e10 * exp(-75e3 / (8.314*310)) | Answer: 0.004604 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.98 and bottoms xW = 0.08, with relative volatility alpha = 2.5. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.98, xw = 0.08, al = 2.5 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.98/0.02)(0.92/0.08)] / ln(2.5) | Answer: 6.913 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.59 and x = 0.2. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.59, x = 0.2 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.59/0.41) / (0.2/0.8) | Answer: 5.756

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.56 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 30 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.56, Psat = 30 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.56 * 30 | Answer: 16.8 kPa

question: A stream of 3.2 kg/s with specific heat 1.6 kJ/kg-K is heated through 120 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 3.2, cp = 1.6, dT = 120 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 3.2*1.6*120 | Answer: 614.4 kW

question: A reactor of volume 8.4 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 4.1 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 8.4, Q = 4.1 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 8.4 / 4.1 | Answer: 2.049 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 7.1e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 5 mm with a concentration difference of 150 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 7.1, L = 5, dC = 150 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (7.1e-9)*150 / (5e-3) | Answer: 213 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 8.9 min and steady-state gain 3.5. For a step input of magnitude 5, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 8.9, K = 3.5, M = 5 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 3.5 * 5 | Answer: 17.5 units

question: A reactor operates at a space time of 10.4 min. Find its space velocity in per hour.
solution: Given: tau = 10.4 | Formula: SV = 60 / tau  (per hour) | Substitute: SV = 60 / 10.4 | Answer: 5.769 /h

question: An aircraft wing of area 35 m^2 flies at 150 m/s (air density 0.7 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.6. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 35, V = 150, rho = 0.7, CL = 0.6 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.7*(150)^2*35*0.6 / 1000 | Answer: 165.4 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 70 m^2 flies at 160 m/s (density 1.225 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.09. Find the drag force in kN.
Find the dynamic pressure for air of density 1.225 kg/m^3 moving at 200 m/s, in Pa.
solution: Given: rho = 1.225, V = 200 | Formula: q = 0.5 rho V^2 | Substitute: q = 0.5*1.225*(200)^2 | Answer: 24500 Pa

question: An aircraft flies at 170 m/s where the speed of sound is 295 m/s. Find the Mach number.

question: Find the circular orbital velocity of a satellite at altitude 1950 km above Earth (Earth radius 6371 km, mu = 3.986e14 m^3/s^2), in km/s.

question: A block of mass 21 kg has a volume of 0.6e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 21, V = 0.6 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 21 / (0.6e-3) | Answer: 35000 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 900 mm is heated through 110 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 11e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 900, dT = 110, al = 11 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 900*11e-6*110 | Answer: 1.089 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 195 ohm, R2 = 125 ohm and R3 = 210 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 195, R2 = 125, R3 = 210 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 125*210 / 195 | Answer: 134.6 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 120 ohm and gauge factor 2 experiences a strain of 300e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 120, GF = 2, eps = 300 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 120*2*300e-6 | Answer: 72 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 9.33 when the true value is 10. Find the percentage error.

question: Annual demand is 12000 units, ordering cost 270 per order and holding cost 7 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 12000, S = 270, H = 7 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*12000*270 / 7) | Answer: 962.1 units

question: An asset costs 210000 with salvage value 2000 after 11 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 210000, Sv = 2000, n = 11 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (210000 - 2000) / 11 | Answer: 18909 per year

question: A product sells for 150 per unit with variable cost 40 per unit and fixed costs 50000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 150, V = 40, F = 50000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 50000 / (150 - 40) | Answer: 454.5 units

question: Find the present worth of 120000 received 10 years from now at an interest rate of 11% per year.
solution: Given: F = 120000, n = 10, i = 11 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 120000 / (1 + 0.11)^10 | Answer: 42262 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.9, 0.91 and 0.95 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.9, r2 = 0.91, r3 = 0.95 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.9*0.91*0.95 | Answer: 0.7781

question: A process produces 20 defective items in a batch of 8000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 20, N = 8000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 20/8000 * 1e6 | Answer: 2500 PPM

question: Find the distance between the points (5, 6) and (-8, 6).

question: Evaluate the number of combinations C(14, 9).

question: Find the 6th term of a geometric progression with first term 7 and common ratio 3.

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 36500 at 9.1% per annum for 4 years.

question: Find the amount when 40000 is invested at 10.1% per annum compounded annually for 2 years.

question: A steel bar is fully restrained and heated through 60 deg C. With E = 200 GPa and alpha = 13e-6 /deg C, find the thermal stress in MPa.

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 650 mm and wall thickness 20 mm carries an internal pressure of 1.5 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.

question: A Carnot engine operates between 1120 K and 400 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).

question: A refrigerator works between 257 K (cold) and 308 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.

question: A heat pump operates between 269 K and 306 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.

question: 5.3 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 185 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 5.3, dT = 185 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 5.3 * 0.718 * 185 | Answer: 704 kJ

question: 7.8 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 115 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 7.8, dT = 115 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 7.8 * 1.005 * 115 | Answer: 901.5 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 2.4 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.19 m. Find the Reynolds number.

question: Water flows at 2.9 m/s through a pipe of diameter 110 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 15.1 m. Taking Cv = 0.97, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).

question: In a pipe (diameter 230 mm) water flows at 2.3 m/s. It contracts to diameter 50 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).

question: A pulley of diameter 330 mm rotates at 200 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.

question: A plane wall of area 5.2 m^2 and thickness 0.33 m has conductivity k = 0.7 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 130 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.

question: In a counter-flow heat exchanger the terminal temperature differences are 90 deg C and 30 deg C. Find the log mean temperature difference (LMTD) in deg C.

question: In turning, cutting speed = 140 m/min, feed = 0.49 mm/rev, depth of cut = 1.1 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.

question: A workpiece of length 450 mm is turned at 300 rpm with a feed of 0.15 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 450, N = 300, f = 0.15 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 450 / (0.15*300) | Answer: 10 min

question: Three resistors 63 ohm, 59 ohm and 73 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 63, R2 = 59, R3 = 73 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 63 + 59 + 73 | Answer: 195 ohm

question: Two resistors 116 ohm and 103 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 116, R2 = 103 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 116*103 / (116+103) | Answer: 54.56 ohm

question: A device draws 8.2 A at 95 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 95, I = 8.2 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 95 * 8.2 | Answer: 779 W

question: A current of 2.6 A flows through a 48 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 2.6, R = 48 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (2.6)^2 * 48 | Answer: 324.5 W

question: Two capacitors 8.7 uF and 26.1 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 8.7, C2 = 26.1 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 8.7*26.1 / (8.7+26.1) | Answer: 6.525 uF

question: A resistor 91 kohm and capacitor 8.9 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 91, C = 8.9 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (91k)(8.9u) = 809.9 ms | Answer: 809.9 ms

question: An inductor 281 mH is in series with 94 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 281, R = 94 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (281e-3) / 94 | Answer: 2.989 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 9.4 mH inductor at 200 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 9.4, f = 200 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (200)(9.4e-3) | Answer: 11.81 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 33.3 uF capacitor at 390 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 33.3, f = 390 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (390)(33.3e-6)) | Answer: 12.25 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 15 ohm, XL = 34 ohm and XC = 88 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 15, XL = 34, XC = 88 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(15^2 + (34 - 88)^2) | Answer: 56.04 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 37.8 mH and C = 4.9 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 37.8, C = 4.9 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(37.8e-3 * 4.9e-6)) | Answer: 369.8 Hz

question: A capacitor of 43.8 uF is charged to 150 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 43.8, V = 150 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*43.8e-6*(150)^2 | Answer: 492.7 mJ

question: An alternating voltage has a peak value of 296 V. Find its RMS value.
solution: Given: Vp = 296 | Formula: Vrms = Vp / sqrt(2) | Substitute: Vrms = 296 / sqrt(2) | Answer: 209.3 V

question: A transformer has primary voltage 300 V with 200 primary turns and 150 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 300, N1 = 200, N2 = 150 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 300 * 150/200 | Answer: 225 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 430 V and draws an armature current of 11 A. If the armature resistance is 0.7 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 430, Ia = 11, Ra = 0.7 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 430 - 11*0.7 | Answer: 422.3 V

question: A 4-pole induction motor on a 60 Hz supply runs at 910 rpm. Find the slip (%).
formula: s = (Ns - N) / Ns,  Ns = 120 f / P

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 115 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.9. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 115, VL = 400, pf = 0.9 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*400*115*0.9 / 1000 | Answer: 71.71 kW

question: A load has real power 80 kW and apparent power 115 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 80, S = 115 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 80 / 115 | Answer: 0.6957

question: A machine delivers 70 kW output while drawing 167 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 70, Pi = 167 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 70/167 * 100 | Answer: 41.92 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 20 V across R1 = 3 ohm and R2 = 49 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 20, R1 = 3, R2 = 49 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 20*49 / (3+49) | Answer: 18.85 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 170 kohm and Rin = 14 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 170, Rin = 14 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 170 / 14 | Answer: 12.14

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 150 kohm and Rg = 11 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 150, Rg = 11 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 150/11 | Answer: 14.64

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 1393. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 1393 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(1393) | Answer: 31.44 dB

question: A first-order system has a time constant of 7.9 s. Find the time (in s) to reach 63.2% of its final value.
solution: For a first-order step response, y = 1 - e^(-t/tau) | y = 0.632 when t = tau | Answer: 7.9 s
formula: At t = tau the response reaches 63.2% (one time constant)

question: A signal is sampled at 160 kHz. According to the Nyquist criterion, what is the maximum signal frequency that can be represented (in kHz)?
solution: Given: fs = 160 | Formula: f_max = fs / 2 | Substitute: f_max = 160 / 2 | Answer: 80 kHz

question: A simply supported beam of span 3.1 m carries a central point load of 25 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.1, W = 25 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 25*3.1 / 4 | Answer: 19.38 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.6 m carries a UDL of 45 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 9.6, w = 45 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 45*(9.6)^2 / 8 | Answer: 518.4 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 3.8 m carries a point load 20 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.8, W = 20 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 20*3.8 | Answer: 76 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 4.4 m carries a UDL of 36 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.4, w = 36 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 36*(4.4)^2 / 2 | Answer: 348.5 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 7.2 m carries a point load 55 kN at distance 3.3 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 7.2, a = 3.3, W = 55 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 55*(7.2 - 3.3) / 7.2 | Answer: 29.79 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 5.4 m) carries a central point load 65 kN. With E = 30 GPa and I = 430e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=65000 N, L=5400.0 mm, E=30000 MPa, I=430e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 16.53 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 4.4 m carries a UDL of 21 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.4, w = 21 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 21*(4.4)^2 / 12 | Answer: 33.88 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 390 mm, clear cover 25 mm and main bars of diameter 16 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 390, c = 25, dia = 16 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 390 - 25 - 16/2 | Answer: 357 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 19 m^2 carrying a factored load of 8.8 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 19, w = 8.8 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 8.8 * 19 | Answer: 167.2 kN

question: For a bar of diameter 25 mm with design bond stress 2.1 MPa and steel stress 435 MPa, find the development length in mm.
solution: Given: dia = 25, tbd = 2.1, fs = 435 | Formula: Ld = phi fs / (4 tau_bd) | Substitute: Ld = 25*435 / (4*2.1) | Answer: 1295 mm

question: A soil sample has porosity n = 0.46. Find its void ratio e.
solution: Given: n = 0.46 | Formula: e = n / (1 - n) | Substitute: e = 0.46 / (1 - 0.46) | Answer: 0.8519

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 3.6 m, unit weight 19 kN/m^3, phi = 30 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 5.7 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 19 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 5.7, g = 19 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (19 - 9.81)*5.7 | Answer: 52.38 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 8.8e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1.2, area = 6.6e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 8.8, i = 1.2, A = 6.6 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (8.8e-4)*1.2*(6.6e-3) | Answer: 697 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.4 m, bed slope 0.007 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.024. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 4.3 m under a head of 0.8 m. Taking Cd = 0.61 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.

question: A rectangular channel 4.6 m wide carries a discharge of 8.9 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).

solution: Given: R = 480, V = 90 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (90)^2 / (127*480) | Answer: 0.1329

question: For a design speed of 70 km/h with allowable superelevation 0.06 and lateral friction 0.13, find the minimum curve radius in m.
A tank of volume 370 m^3 treats a flow of 85 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 370, Q = 85 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 370 / 85 | Answer: 4.353 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 230 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.28 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 6 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 230, k = 0.28, t = 6 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 230*(1 - e^(-0.28*6)) | Answer: 187.1 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.37, rainfall intensity 30 mm/h over a catchment of 16.8 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.37, i = 30, A = 16.8 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.37*30*16.8 / 360 | Answer: 0.518 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.07 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 380 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.07, M = 380 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 380*(20+0.07)/20 | Answer: 381.3 m

question: A file of 550 megabits is sent over a link of 60 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.

question: A link has bandwidth 48 Mbps and round-trip time 110 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 48, R = 110 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 48e6 * 110e-3 bits = 5280 kb | Answer: 5280 kilobits

question: A channel has bandwidth 3 kHz. Using Nyquist's theorem with 8 signal levels, find the maximum data rate in kbps (noiseless).
solution: Given: B = 3, M = 8 | Formula: C = 2 B log2(M) | Substitute: C = 2*3*log2(8) | Answer: 18 kbps

question: A channel of bandwidth 13 kHz has a signal-to-noise ratio of 7 (linear). Using Shannon's theorem, find the channel capacity in kbps.
solution: Given: B = 13, SNR = 7 | Formula: C = B log2(1 + SNR) | Substitute: C = 13*log2(1 + 7) | Answer: 39 kbps

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.87, cache access time 1 ns and main-memory access time 90 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.87, tc = 1, tm = 90 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.87*1 + (1 - 0.87)*90 | Answer: 12.57 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 189119 elements?
solution: Given: n = 189119 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(189119)) + 1 | Answer: 18

question: An O(n^2) algorithm performs c*n^2 basic operations. If c = 1 and n = 240, how many operations are performed?
solution: Given: n = 240 | Formula: operations = n^2 | Substitute: = (240)^2 | Answer: 57600

question: A program is 95% parallelisable and run on 8 processors. Using Amdahl's law, find the maximum speedup.
solution: Parallel fraction f = 0.95 | S = 1 / ((1 - 0.95) + 0.95/8) | Answer: 5.926x speedup

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.002, memory access time 200 ns and page-fault service time 10 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 10 ms = 10000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.002)*200 + 0.002*10000000.0 ns | Answer: 20.2 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: A modem transmits at 1200 baud using 16-level signalling. Find the bit rate in bps.
solution: Given: baud = 1200, M = 16 | Formula: bit rate = baud * log2(M) | Substitute: bit rate = 1200 * log2(16) | Answer: 4800 bps

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 1.4 m^3 at 470 kPa and 560 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 1.4, P = 470, Tk = 560 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (470e3)*1.4 / (8.314*560) | Answer: 141.3 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.19 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 18 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.19, t = 18 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.19*18) | Answer: 0.9673

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.24 /min) is to reach 75% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.24, X = 75 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.75) / 0.24 | Answer: 5.776 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.17 /min) reaches 50% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.17, X = 50 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.5 / (0.17*(1 - 0.5)) | Answer: 5.882 min

question: A first-order reaction has a rate constant of 0.3 /min. Find its half-life in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.3 | Formula: t_half = ln(2) / k | Substitute: t_half = 0.6931 / 0.3 | Answer: 2.31 min

question: For a reaction with A = 8e10 /s and activation energy 80 kJ/mol at 450 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 8, Ea = 80, Tk = 450 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 8e10 * exp(-80e3 / (8.314*450)) | Answer: 41.36 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.91 and bottoms xW = 0.08, with relative volatility alpha = 2.5. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.91, xw = 0.08, al = 2.5 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.91/0.09)(0.92/0.08)] / ln(2.5) | Answer: 5.19 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.81 and x = 0.3. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.81, x = 0.3 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.81/0.19) / (0.3/0.7) | Answer: 9.947

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.51 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 100 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.51, Psat = 100 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.51 * 100 | Answer: 51 kPa

question: A stream of 9.3 kg/s with specific heat 3.1 kJ/kg-K is heated through 95 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 9.3, cp = 3.1, dT = 95 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 9.3*3.1*95 | Answer: 2739 kW

question: A reactor of volume 7.6 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 4.6 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 7.6, Q = 4.6 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 7.6 / 4.6 | Answer: 1.652 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 2.5e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 2 mm with a concentration difference of 140 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 2.5, L = 2, dC = 140 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (2.5e-9)*140 / (2e-3) | Answer: 175 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 4.7 min and steady-state gain 1.9. For a step input of magnitude 19, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 4.7, K = 1.9, M = 19 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 1.9 * 19 | Answer: 36.1 units

question: A reactor operates at a space time of 11.2 min. Find its space velocity in per hour.
solution: Given: tau = 11.2 | Formula: SV = 60 / tau  (per hour) | Substitute: SV = 60 / 11.2 | Answer: 5.357 /h

question: An aircraft wing of area 20 m^2 flies at 120 m/s (air density 1 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.5. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 20, V = 120, rho = 1, CL = 0.5 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1*(120)^2*20*0.5 / 1000 | Answer: 72 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 40 m^2 flies at 160 m/s (density 1 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.02. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 40, V = 160, rho = 1, CD = 0.02 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*1*(160)^2*40*0.02 / 1000 | Answer: 10.24 kN

question: Find the dynamic pressure for air of density 1 kg/m^3 moving at 240 m/s, in Pa.
solution: Given: rho = 1, V = 240 | Formula: q = 0.5 rho V^2 | Substitute: q = 0.5*1*(240)^2 | Answer: 28800 Pa

question: An aircraft flies at 400 m/s where the speed of sound is 310 m/s. Find the Mach number.
solution: Given: V = 400, a = 310 | Formula: M = V / a | Substitute: M = 400 / 310 | Answer: 1.29

question: Find the circular orbital velocity of a satellite at altitude 750 km above Earth (Earth radius 6371 km, mu = 3.986e14 m^3/s^2), in km/s.
A specimen under stress 290 MPa shows an elastic strain of 2.8e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 290, eps = 2.8 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 290 / (2.8e-3) MPa = 103.6 GPa | Answer: 103.6 GPa

question: A block of mass 47 kg has a volume of 3.7e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 47, V = 3.7 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 47 / (3.7e-3) | Answer: 12703 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 2900 mm is heated through 60 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 17e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 2900, dT = 60, al = 17 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 2900*17e-6*60 | Answer: 2.958 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 45 ohm, R2 = 115 ohm and R3 = 70 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 45, R2 = 115, R3 = 70 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 115*70 / 45 | Answer: 178.9 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 120 ohm and gauge factor 2 experiences a strain of 350e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 120, GF = 2, eps = 350 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 120*2*350e-6 | Answer: 84 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 10.68 when the true value is 100. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10.68, true = 100 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10.68 - 100| / 100 * 100 | Answer: 89.32 %

question: Annual demand is 8500 units, ordering cost 170 per order and holding cost 20 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 8500, S = 170, H = 20 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*8500*170 / 20) | Answer: 380.1 units

question: An asset costs 460000 with salvage value 10000 after 17 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 460000, Sv = 10000, n = 17 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (460000 - 10000) / 17 | Answer: 26471 per year

question: A product sells for 210 per unit with variable cost 40 per unit and fixed costs 120000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 210, V = 40, F = 120000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 120000 / (210 - 40) | Answer: 705.9 units

question: Find the present worth of 75000 received 8 years from now at an interest rate of 10% per year.
solution: Given: F = 75000, n = 8, i = 10 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 75000 / (1 + 0.1)^8 | Answer: 34988 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.93, 0.9 and 0.98 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.93, r2 = 0.9, r3 = 0.98 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.93*0.9*0.98 | Answer: 0.8203

question: Two components each of reliability 0.93 are connected in parallel. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r = 0.93 | Formula: R_parallel = 1 - (1 - r)^2 | Substitute: R = 1 - (1 - 0.93)^2 | Answer: 0.9951

question: A process produces 43 defective items in a batch of 12500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 43, N = 12500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 43/12500 * 1e6 | Answer: 3440 PPM
