question: Find the larger real root of x^2 + 10x = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[-7, 6], [0, -6]].
solution: Given: a = -7, b = 6, c = 0, d = -6 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (-7)(-6) - (6)(0) | Answer: 42

question: Find the determinant of [[1, 2, 1], [1, 0, 4], [-1, -4, -4]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: 12

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[6, 3], [2, -4]].
solution: Trace tr = 2, Determinant = -30 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 6.568

question: Solve for x: -2x + -5y = 2 and 1x + 5y = -11.
solution: Determinant = -2*5 - -5*1 = -5 | x = (e d - b f) / det = 9 | Answer: x = 9
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 20, 69, 8, 29, 98.
solution: Sum = 224 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 44.8 | Answer: 44.8

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 25, 27, 33, 38, 7.
solution: Mean = 26 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 11.79

question: Find the slope of the line through (-5, -1) and (6, 2).
solution: Given: x1 = -5, y1 = -1, x2 = 6, y2 = 2 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (2 - -1) / (6 - -5) | Answer: 0.2727

question: Find the distance between the points (2, 6) and (-2, 3).
solution: Given: x1 = 2, y1 = 6, x2 = -2, y2 = 3 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-4)^2 + (-3)^2) | Answer: 5 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (-7,8), (-8,-6), (-8,6).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 6 sq units

question: Evaluate the number of combinations C(11, 1).
solution: Given: n = 11, r = 1 | Formula: C(n, r) = n! / (r! (n - r)!) | Substitute: C(11, 1) = 11! / (1! * 10!) | Answer: 11

question: Evaluate the number of permutations P(13, 6).
solution: Given: n = 13, r = 6 | Formula: P(n, r) = n! / (n - r)! | Substitute: P(13, 6) = 13! / 7! | Answer: 1235520

question: Find the 16th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -19 and common difference 3.
solution: Given: a = -19, d = 3, n = 16 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -19 + (16 - 1)*3 | Answer: 26

question: Find the sum of the first 34 terms of an AP with first term -9 and common difference -7.
solution: Given: a = -9, d = -7, n = 34 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 34/2 [2*-9 + (34-1)*-7] | Answer: -4233

question: Find the 5th term of a geometric progression with first term 9 and common ratio 2.
solution: Given: a = 9, r = 2, n = 5 | Formula: a_n = a r^(n-1) | Substitute: a_n = 9 * 2^(5-1) | Answer: 144

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 2500 at 10.8% per annum for 7 years.
solution: Given: P = 2500, R = 10.8, Tt = 7 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 2500 * 10.8 * 7 / 100 | Answer: 1890 currency units

question: Find the amount when 35000 is invested at 11.5% per annum compounded annually for 3 years.
solution: Given: P = 35000, R = 11.5, Tt = 3 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 35000 * (1 + 11.5/100)^3 | Answer: 48517 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (4, -7, -5) and (-2, 5, 0).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (-6, 2, 4) and (-5, -6, -5).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 69.37

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (-4, -1, 6) and (0, 0, -1).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 145.5 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number -9 + -7i.
solution: Given: a = -9, b = -7 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((-9)^2 + (-7)^2) | Answer: 11.4

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number -11 + 9i.
solution: Given: a = -11, b = 9 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(9, -11) | Answer: 140.7 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = 3x^3 - 6x^2 + 8x + 3 at x = 2.
solution: Given: a = 3, b = -6, c = 8, d = 3, x0 = 2 | Formula: f(x0) = a x0^3 + b x0^2 + c x0 + d | Substitute: f(2) = 3(2)^3 + -6(2)^2 + 8(2) + 3 | Answer: 19

question: Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-98 with initial guess x0=2, find x1 (one iteration).
solution: Given: N = 98, x0 = 2 | Formula: x1 = x0 - (x0^2 - N)/(2 x0) | Substitute: x1 = 2 - ((2)^2 - 98)/(2*2) | Answer: 25.5

question: Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=0.6 and ordinates 11, 19, 13, 8, 17, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 247 and 301.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 247 and 301 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 43 and 70.
solution: Given: a = 43, b = 70 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 43*70 / 1 | Answer: 3010
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 26 mm carries an axial tensile load of 107 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 23 mm and length 1800 mm carries an axial load of 47 kN. Take E = 70 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 75 mm transmits a torque of 2700 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 75, Tt = 2700 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(2700*1000) / (pi*(75)^3) | Answer: 32.59 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 65 mm and length 1400 mm carries a torque of 350 N-m. With G = 80 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (65)^4 / 32 = 1752481 mm^4 | theta = (350*1000)(1400) / (80000 * 1752481) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 0.2003 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 142 mm wide and 150 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 142, h = 150 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 142*(150)^2 / 6 | Answer: 532500 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (93 mm x 230 mm) carries a bending moment of 24 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (63 mm x 90 mm) has effective length 1700 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 600 MPa is designed for a working stress of 150 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 600, sw = 150 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 600 / 150 | Answer: 4

question: A steel bar is fully restrained and heated through 30 deg C. With E = 200 GPa and alpha = 13e-6 /deg C, find the thermal stress in MPa.
solution: Given: dT = 30, E = 200, al = 13 | Formula: sigma = E alpha (dT) | Substitute: sigma = 200000 * 13e-6 * 30 | Answer: 78 MPa

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1150 mm and wall thickness 16 mm carries an internal pressure of 1.4 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1150, t = 16, P = 1.4 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 1.4*1150 / (2*16) | Answer: 50.31 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 1140 K and 290 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 1140, Tc = 290 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 290/1140) * 100 | Answer: 74.56 %

question: A refrigerator works between 265 K (cold) and 324 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 265, Th = 324 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 265 / (324 - 265) | Answer: 4.492

question: A heat pump operates between 269 K and 312 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 269, Th = 312 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 312 / (312 - 269) | Answer: 7.256

question: 2.7 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 115 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.7, dT = 115 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 2.7 * 0.718 * 115 | Answer: 222.9 kJ

question: 7.9 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 120 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 7.9, dT = 120 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 7.9 * 1.005 * 120 | Answer: 952.7 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 3.7 m^3 at 460 K with mass 4.7 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 3.7, Tk = 460, m = 4.7 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 4.7*0.287*460 / 3.7 | Answer: 167.7 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 4.7 kg of air expands isothermally at 320 K from volume V1 to 4*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.7, Tk = 320, ratio = 4 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 4.7*0.287*320*ln(4) | Answer: 598.4 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 2.7 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.18 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 2.7, D = 0.18 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*2.7*0.18 / 0.001 | Answer: 486000

question: Water flows at 1.3 m/s through a pipe of diameter 280 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 1.8 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 1.8 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*1.8 / 1000 | Answer: 17.66 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 2.7 m. Taking Cv = 0.95, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 2.7, cv = 0.95 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.95*sqrt(2*9.81*2.7) | Answer: 6.914 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 370 mm) water flows at 1.1 m/s. It contracts to diameter 80 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 370, d2 = 80, V1 = 1.1 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 1.1*(370/80)^2 | Answer: 23.53 m/s

question: Water flows at 2.9 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.16 m and length 300 m. With friction factor f = 0.023, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 35 teeth drives a gear of 120 teeth. If the pinion runs at 500 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 35, z2 = 120, N1 = 500 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 500*35 / 120 | Answer: 145.8 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 250 mm rotates at 450 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 250, N = 450 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.25)*450 / 60 | Answer: 5.89 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 20.2 kW at 950 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 20.2, N = 950 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(20.2*1000) / (2*pi*950) | Answer: 203 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 7.2 kg rotates at radius 0.4 m at 350 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 16100 N/m and mass 13.1 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 16100, m = 13.1 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(16100/13.1) | Answer: 5.58 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 9.2 m^2 and thickness 0.13 m has conductivity k = 48.8 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 60 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 9.2, L = 0.13, k = 48.8, dT = 60 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 48.8*9.2*60 / 0.13 | Answer: 207212 W

question: A surface of area 4.8 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 10 W/m^2-K to surroundings 35 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 4.8, h = 10, dT = 35 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 10*4.8*35 | Answer: 1680 W

question: In a counter-flow heat exchanger the terminal temperature differences are 115 deg C and 10 deg C. Find the log mean temperature difference (LMTD) in deg C.
solution: Given: dT1 = 115, dT2 = 10 | Formula: LMTD = (dT1 - dT2) / ln(dT1/dT2) | Substitute: LMTD = (115 - 10) / ln(115/10) | Answer: 42.99 deg C

question: In turning, cutting speed = 140 m/min, feed = 0.39 mm/rev, depth of cut = 1.1 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 140, f = 0.39, d = 1.1 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*140*0.39*1.1 | Answer: 60060 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 230 mm is turned at 400 rpm with a feed of 0.22 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 230, N = 400, f = 0.22 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 230 / (0.22*400) | Answer: 2.614 min

question: A resistor of 15 ohm carries a current of 6.6 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 15, I = 6.6 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 6.6 * 15 | Answer: 99 V

question: Three resistors 47 ohm, 63 ohm and 72 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 47, R2 = 63, R3 = 72 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 47 + 63 + 72 | Answer: 182 ohm

question: Two resistors 34 ohm and 5 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 34, R2 = 5 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 34*5 / (34+5) | Answer: 4.359 ohm

question: A device draws 8.1 A at 110 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 110, I = 8.1 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 110 * 8.1 | Answer: 891 W

question: A current of 7.1 A flows through a 50 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 7.1, R = 50 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (7.1)^2 * 50 | Answer: 252 W

question: Two capacitors 34.9 uF and 17.9 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 34.9, C2 = 17.9 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 34.9*17.9 / (34.9+17.9) | Answer: 11.83 uF

question: A resistor 16 kohm and capacitor 10.3 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 16, C = 10.3 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (16k)(10.3u) = 164.8 ms | Answer: 164.8 ms

question: An inductor 55.9 mH is in series with 77 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 55.9, R = 77 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (55.9e-3) / 77 | Answer: 0.726 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 42.8 mH inductor at 580 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 42.8, f = 580 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (580)(42.8e-3) | Answer: 156 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 24.9 uF capacitor at 510 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 24.9, f = 510 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (510)(24.9e-6)) | Answer: 12.53 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 77 ohm, XL = 131 ohm and XC = 92 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 77, XL = 131, XC = 92 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(77^2 + (131 - 92)^2) | Answer: 86.31 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 45.6 mH and C = 4.3 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 45.6, C = 4.3 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(45.6e-3 * 4.3e-6)) | Answer: 359.4 Hz

question: A capacitor of 94.9 uF is charged to 40 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 94.9, V = 40 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*94.9e-6*(40)^2 | Answer: 75.92 mJ

question: An alternating voltage has a peak value of 54 V. Find its RMS value.
solution: Given: Vp = 54 | Formula: Vrms = Vp / sqrt(2) | Substitute: Vrms = 54 / sqrt(2) | Answer: 38.18 V

question: A transformer has primary voltage 160 V with 320 primary turns and 270 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 160, N1 = 320, N2 = 270 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 160 * 270/320 | Answer: 135 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 130 V and draws an armature current of 16 A. If the armature resistance is 0.35 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 130, Ia = 16, Ra = 0.35 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 130 - 16*0.35 | Answer: 124.4 V

question: A 6-pole induction motor on a 50 Hz supply runs at 900 rpm. Find the slip (%).
formula: s = (Ns - N) / Ns,  Ns = 120 f / P

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 165 A at 433 V (line) with a power factor of 0.97. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 165, VL = 433, pf = 0.97 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*433*165*0.97 / 1000 | Answer: 120 kW

question: A load has real power 85 kW and apparent power 125 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 85, S = 125 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 85 / 125 | Answer: 0.68

question: A machine delivers 170 kW output while drawing 207 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 170, Pi = 207 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 170/207 * 100 | Answer: 82.13 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 20 V across R1 = 16 ohm and R2 = 25 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 20, R1 = 16, R2 = 25 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 20*25 / (16+25) | Answer: 12.2 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 200 kohm and Rin = 24 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 200, Rin = 24 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 200 / 24 | Answer: 8.333

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 180 kohm and Rg = 45 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 180, Rg = 45 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 180/45 | Answer: 5

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 9531. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 9531 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(9531) | Answer: 39.79 dB

question: A first-order system has a time constant of 3.7 s. Find the time (in s) to reach 63.2% of its final value.
solution: For a first-order step response, y = 1 - e^(-t/tau) | y = 0.632 when t = tau | Answer: 3.7 s
formula: At t = tau the response reaches 63.2% (one time constant)

question: A signal is sampled at 172 kHz. According to the Nyquist criterion, what is the maximum signal frequency that can be represented (in kHz)?
solution: Given: fs = 172 | Formula: f_max = fs / 2 | Substitute: f_max = 172 / 2 | Answer: 86 kHz

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.6 m carries a central point load of 110 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.6, W = 110 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 110*4.6 / 4 | Answer: 126.5 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 8 m carries a UDL of 25 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 8, w = 25 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 25*(8)^2 / 8 | Answer: 200 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 4.9 m carries a point load 80 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.9, W = 80 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 80*4.9 | Answer: 392 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 1.5 m carries a UDL of 30 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 1.5, w = 30 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 30*(1.5)^2 / 2 | Answer: 33.75 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.4 m carries a point load 40 kN at distance 3.7 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 6.4, a = 3.7, W = 40 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 40*(6.4 - 3.7) / 6.4 | Answer: 16.88 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 5.3 m) carries a central point load 75 kN. With E = 25 GPa and I = 510e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=75000 N, L=5300.0 mm, E=25000 MPa, I=510e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 18.24 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 5.5 m carries a UDL of 12 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.5, w = 12 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 12*(5.5)^2 / 12 | Answer: 30.25 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 510 mm, clear cover 45 mm and main bars of diameter 12 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 510, c = 45, dia = 12 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 510 - 45 - 12/2 | Answer: 459 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 15.4 m^2 carrying a factored load of 16.9 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 15.4, w = 16.9 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 16.9 * 15.4 | Answer: 260.3 kN

question: For a bar of diameter 16 mm with design bond stress 1.7 MPa and steel stress 435 MPa, find the development length in mm.
solution: Given: dia = 16, tbd = 1.7, fs = 435 | Formula: Ld = phi fs / (4 tau_bd) | Substitute: Ld = 16*435 / (4*1.7) | Answer: 1024 mm

question: A soil sample has porosity n = 0.44. Find its void ratio e.
solution: Given: n = 0.44 | Formula: e = n / (1 - n) | Substitute: e = 0.44 / (1 - 0.44) | Answer: 0.7857

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 6.9 m, unit weight 16 kN/m^3, phi = 34 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 5.5 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 19 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 5.5, g = 19 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (19 - 9.81)*5.5 | Answer: 50.54 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 3.7e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.6, area = 6.6e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 3.7, i = 0.6, A = 6.6 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (3.7e-4)*0.6*(6.6e-3) | Answer: 1465 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.4 m, bed slope 0.006 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.013. Find the mean velocity in m/s.

question: For a design speed of 60 km/h with allowable superelevation 0.07 and lateral friction 0.15, find the minimum curve radius in m.
A tank of volume 520 m^3 treats a flow of 115 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 380 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.16 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 7 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 380, k = 0.16, t = 7 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 380*(1 - e^(-0.16*7)) | Answer: 256 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.83, rainfall intensity 50 mm/h over a catchment of 33.3 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.83, i = 50, A = 33.3 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.83*50*33.3 / 360 | Answer: 3.839 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.05 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 640 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.05, M = 640 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 640*(30+0.05)/30 | Answer: 641.1 m

solution: Divide 128 by 2 repeatedly, recording remainders | Reading remainders in reverse gives 10000000 | Answer: 10000000 (binary)

solution: Binary 11010100 = sum of bit-weights | Answer: 212 (decimal)

solution: XOR: 11000110 | Count of 1s = 4 | Answer: 4
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 290 megabits is sent over a link of 60 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 290, B = 60 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 290 / 60 | Answer: 4.833 s

question: A link has bandwidth 7 Mbps and round-trip time 110 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 7, R = 110 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 7e6 * 110e-3 bits = 770 kb | Answer: 770 kilobits

question: A channel has bandwidth 7 kHz. Using Nyquist's theorem with 8 signal levels, find the maximum data rate in kbps (noiseless).
solution: Given: B = 7, M = 8 | Formula: C = 2 B log2(M) | Substitute: C = 2*7*log2(8) | Answer: 42 kbps

question: A channel of bandwidth 17 kHz has a signal-to-noise ratio of 63 (linear). Using Shannon's theorem, find the channel capacity in kbps.
solution: Given: B = 17, SNR = 63 | Formula: C = B log2(1 + SNR) | Substitute: C = 17*log2(1 + 63) | Answer: 102 kbps

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.96, cache access time 10 ns and main-memory access time 70 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.96, tc = 10, tm = 70 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.96*10 + (1 - 0.96)*70 | Answer: 12.4 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 745544 elements?
solution: Given: n = 745544 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(745544)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: An O(n^2) algorithm performs c*n^2 basic operations. If c = 1 and n = 2310, how many operations are performed?
solution: Given: n = 2310 | Formula: operations = n^2 | Substitute: = (2310)^2 | Answer: 5336100

question: A program is 65% parallelisable and run on 32 processors. Using Amdahl's law, find the maximum speedup.
solution: Parallel fraction f = 0.65 | S = 1 / ((1 - 0.65) + 0.65/32) | Answer: 2.7x speedup

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.005, memory access time 120 ns and page-fault service time 5 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 5 ms = 5000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.005)*120 + 0.005*5000000.0 ns | Answer: 25.12 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: A modem transmits at 1800 baud using 2-level signalling. Find the bit rate in bps.
solution: Given: baud = 1800, M = 2 | Formula: bit rate = baud * log2(M) | Substitute: bit rate = 1800 * log2(2) | Answer: 1800 bps

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 1.9 m^3 at 460 kPa and 590 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 1.9, P = 460, Tk = 590 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (460e3)*1.9 / (8.314*590) | Answer: 178.2 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.1 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 13 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.1, t = 13 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.1*13) | Answer: 0.7275

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.43 /min) is to reach 80% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.43, X = 80 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.8) / 0.43 | Answer: 3.743 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.13 /min) reaches 50% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.13, X = 50 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.5 / (0.13*(1 - 0.5)) | Answer: 7.692 min

question: A first-order reaction has a rate constant of 0.04 /min. Find its half-life in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.04 | Formula: t_half = ln(2) / k | Substitute: t_half = 0.6931 / 0.04 | Answer: 17.33 min

question: For a reaction with A = 4e10 /s and activation energy 50 kJ/mol at 350 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 4, Ea = 50, Tk = 350 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 4e10 * exp(-50e3 / (8.314*350)) | Answer: 1379 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.96 and bottoms xW = 0.08, with relative volatility alpha = 3. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.96, xw = 0.08, al = 3 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.96/0.04)(0.92/0.08)] / ln(3) | Answer: 5.116 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.74 and x = 0.28. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.74, x = 0.28 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.74/0.26) / (0.28/0.72) | Answer: 7.319

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.56 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 55 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.56, Psat = 55 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.56 * 55 | Answer: 30.8 kPa

question: A stream of 0.7 kg/s with specific heat 3.6 kJ/kg-K is heated through 35 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 0.7, cp = 3.6, dT = 35 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 0.7*3.6*35 | Answer: 88.2 kW

question: A reactor of volume 8.4 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 4.8 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 8.4, Q = 4.8 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 8.4 / 4.8 | Answer: 1.75 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 5.3e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 5 mm with a concentration difference of 140 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 5.3, L = 5, dC = 140 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (5.3e-9)*140 / (5e-3) | Answer: 148.4 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 3.9 min and steady-state gain 3.3. For a step input of magnitude 15, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 3.9, K = 3.3, M = 15 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 3.3 * 15 | Answer: 49.5 units

question: A reactor operates at a space time of 1.8 min. Find its space velocity in per hour.
solution: Given: tau = 1.8 | Formula: SV = 60 / tau  (per hour) | Substitute: SV = 60 / 1.8 | Answer: 33.33 /h

question: An aircraft wing of area 30 m^2 flies at 250 m/s (air density 0.4 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.9. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 30, V = 250, rho = 0.4, CL = 0.9 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.4*(250)^2*30*0.9 / 1000 | Answer: 337.5 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 70 m^2 flies at 150 m/s (density 1 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.05. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 70, V = 150, rho = 1, CD = 0.05 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*1*(150)^2*70*0.05 / 1000 | Answer: 39.38 kN

question: Find the dynamic pressure for air of density 1 kg/m^3 moving at 110 m/s, in Pa.
solution: Given: rho = 1, V = 110 | Formula: q = 0.5 rho V^2 | Substitute: q = 0.5*1*(110)^2 | Answer: 6050 Pa

question: An aircraft flies at 580 m/s where the speed of sound is 295 m/s. Find the Mach number.
solution: Given: V = 580, a = 295 | Formula: M = V / a | Substitute: M = 580 / 295 | Answer: 1.966

question: A specimen under stress 190 MPa shows an elastic strain of 0.8e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 190, eps = 0.8 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 190 / (0.8e-3) MPa = 237.5 GPa | Answer: 237.5 GPa

question: A block of mass 9 kg has a volume of 3.9e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 9, V = 3.9 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 9 / (3.9e-3) | Answer: 2308 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 1100 mm is heated through 140 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 23e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 1100, dT = 140, al = 23 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 1100*23e-6*140 | Answer: 3.542 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 110 ohm, R2 = 125 ohm and R3 = 320 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 110, R2 = 125, R3 = 320 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 125*320 / 110 | Answer: 363.6 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 120 ohm and gauge factor 2.2 experiences a strain of 850e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 120, GF = 2.2, eps = 850 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 120*2.2*850e-6 | Answer: 224.4 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 9.62 when the true value is 10. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.62, true = 10 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.62 - 10| / 10 * 100 | Answer: 3.8 %

question: Annual demand is 10500 units, ordering cost 180 per order and holding cost 20 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 10500, S = 180, H = 20 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*10500*180 / 20) | Answer: 434.7 units

question: An asset costs 230000 with salvage value 16000 after 14 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.

question: A product sells for 330 per unit with variable cost 180 per unit and fixed costs 185000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 330, V = 180, F = 185000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 185000 / (330 - 180) | Answer: 1233 units

question: Find the present worth of 50000 received 9 years from now at an interest rate of 11% per year.
solution: Given: F = 50000, n = 9, i = 11 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 50000 / (1 + 0.11)^9 | Answer: 19546 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.92, 0.98 and 0.96 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.92, r2 = 0.98, r3 = 0.96 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.92*0.98*0.96 | Answer: 0.8655

question: Two components each of reliability 0.88 are connected in parallel. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r = 0.88 | Formula: R_parallel = 1 - (1 - r)^2 | Substitute: R = 1 - (1 - 0.88)^2 | Answer: 0.9856

question: A process produces 24 defective items in a batch of 19500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 24, N = 19500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 24/19500 * 1e6 | Answer: 1231 PPM

question: Find the distance between the points (-2, -2) and (4, 3).

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (-3,7), (-3,5), (-6,7).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 3 sq units

question: Evaluate the number of combinations C(17, 8).
solution: Given: n = 17, r = 8 | Formula: C(n, r) = n! / (r! (n - r)!) | Substitute: C(17, 8) = 17! / (8! * 9!) | Answer: 24310

question: Evaluate the number of permutations P(12, 9).

question: Find the 23th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -11 and common difference -9.

question: Find the sum of the first 20 terms of an AP with first term -10 and common difference -2.

question: Find the 8th term of a geometric progression with first term 7 and common ratio 3.
solution: Given: a = 7, r = 3, n = 8 | Formula: a_n = a r^(n-1) | Substitute: a_n = 7 * 3^(8-1) | Answer: 15309

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 30500 at 4.9% per annum for 2 years.
solution: Given: P = 30500, R = 4.9, Tt = 2 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 30500 * 4.9 * 2 / 100 | Answer: 2989 currency units

question: Find the amount when 21500 is invested at 4.8% per annum compounded annually for 2 years.
solution: Given: P = 21500, R = 4.8, Tt = 2 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 21500 * (1 + 4.8/100)^2 | Answer: 23614 currency units

question: Find the modulus of the complex number 8 + 8i.

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number 12 + 8i.
solution: Given: a = 12, b = 8 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(8, 12) | Answer: 33.69 degrees

question: A circular rod of diameter 16 mm carries an axial tensile load of 28 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 39 mm and length 700 mm carries an axial load of 49 kN. Take E = 70 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 70 mm transmits a torque of 1600 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.

question: A shaft of diameter 25 mm and length 1600 mm carries a torque of 1300 N-m. With G = 80 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.

question: A rectangular beam section is 122 mm wide and 120 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 122, h = 120 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 122*(120)^2 / 6 | Answer: 292800 mm^3

question: A component of ultimate strength 570 MPa is designed for a working stress of 120 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 570, sw = 120 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 570 / 120 | Answer: 4.75

question: A steel bar is fully restrained and heated through 95 deg C. With E = 210 GPa and alpha = 12e-6 /deg C, find the thermal stress in MPa.
solution: Given: dT = 95, E = 210, al = 12 | Formula: sigma = E alpha (dT) | Substitute: sigma = 210000 * 12e-6 * 95 | Answer: 239.4 MPa

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 900 mm and wall thickness 15 mm carries an internal pressure of 1.9 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 900, t = 15, P = 1.9 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 1.9*900 / (2*15) | Answer: 57 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 920 K and 370 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 920, Tc = 370 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 370/920) * 100 | Answer: 59.78 %

question: A refrigerator works between 271 K (cold) and 320 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 271, Th = 320 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 271 / (320 - 271) | Answer: 5.531

question: A heat pump operates between 280 K and 310 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 280, Th = 310 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 310 / (310 - 280) | Answer: 10.33

question: 4.4 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 65 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.4, dT = 65 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 4.4 * 0.718 * 65 | Answer: 205.3 kJ

question: 5.5 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 85 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 5.5, dT = 85 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 5.5 * 1.005 * 85 | Answer: 469.8 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 2.1 m^3 at 350 K with mass 5.6 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 2.1, Tk = 350, m = 5.6 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 5.6*0.287*350 / 2.1 | Answer: 267.9 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 2.6 kg of air expands isothermally at 340 K from volume V1 to 5*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 1.8 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.39 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 1.8, D = 0.39 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*1.8*0.39 / 0.001 | Answer: 702000

question: Water flows at 3 m/s through a pipe of diameter 190 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 11.4 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 11.4 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*11.4 / 1000 | Answer: 111.8 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 13.5 m. Taking Cv = 0.96, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 13.5, cv = 0.96 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.96*sqrt(2*9.81*13.5) | Answer: 15.62 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 310 mm) water flows at 0.7 m/s. It contracts to diameter 100 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
Water flows at 3.8 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.4 m and length 120 m. With friction factor f = 0.03, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 25 teeth drives a gear of 112 teeth. If the pinion runs at 750 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 25, z2 = 112, N1 = 750 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 750*25 / 112 | Answer: 167.4 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 440 mm rotates at 800 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 440, N = 800 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.44)*800 / 60 | Answer: 18.43 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 18.4 kW at 1150 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 18.4, N = 1150 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(18.4*1000) / (2*pi*1150) | Answer: 152.8 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 5 kg rotates at radius 0.55 m at 950 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 2600 N/m and mass 17.9 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 2600, m = 17.9 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(2600/17.9) | Answer: 1.918 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 7.3 m^2 and thickness 0.39 m has conductivity k = 2.3 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 65 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 7.3, L = 0.39, k = 2.3, dT = 65 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 2.3*7.3*65 / 0.39 | Answer: 2798 W

question: A surface of area 5.1 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 155 W/m^2-K to surroundings 20 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 5.1, h = 155, dT = 20 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 155*5.1*20 | Answer: 15810 W

question: In a counter-flow heat exchanger the terminal temperature differences are 95 deg C and 15 deg C. Find the log mean temperature difference (LMTD) in deg C.
solution: Given: dT1 = 95, dT2 = 15 | Formula: LMTD = (dT1 - dT2) / ln(dT1/dT2) | Substitute: LMTD = (95 - 15) / ln(95/15) | Answer: 43.34 deg C

question: In turning, cutting speed = 250 m/min, feed = 0.41 mm/rev, depth of cut = 1.3 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 250, f = 0.41, d = 1.3 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*250*0.41*1.3 | Answer: 133250 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 390 mm is turned at 1100 rpm with a feed of 0.4 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 390, N = 1100, f = 0.4 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 390 / (0.4*1100) | Answer: 0.8864 min

question: A resistor of 56 ohm carries a current of 3.2 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 56, I = 3.2 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 3.2 * 56 | Answer: 179.2 V

question: Three resistors 45 ohm, 39 ohm and 76 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 45, R2 = 39, R3 = 76 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 45 + 39 + 76 | Answer: 160 ohm

question: Two resistors 2 ohm and 66 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 2, R2 = 66 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 2*66 / (2+66) | Answer: 1.941 ohm

question: A device draws 8.9 A at 180 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 180, I = 8.9 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 180 * 8.9 | Answer: 1602 W

question: A current of 2.3 A flows through a 64 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 2.3, R = 64 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (2.3)^2 * 64 | Answer: 338.6 W

question: Two capacitors 37.3 uF and 31.8 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 37.3, C2 = 31.8 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 37.3*31.8 / (37.3+31.8) | Answer: 17.17 uF

question: A resistor 64 kohm and capacitor 2.1 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 64, C = 2.1 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (64k)(2.1u) = 134.4 ms | Answer: 134.4 ms

question: An inductor 421.3 mH is in series with 172 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 421.3, R = 172 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (421.3e-3) / 172 | Answer: 2.449 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 138.7 mH inductor at 240 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 138.7, f = 240 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (240)(138.7e-3) | Answer: 209.2 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 47.4 uF capacitor at 690 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 47.4, f = 690 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (690)(47.4e-6)) | Answer: 4.866 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 74 ohm, XL = 51 ohm and XC = 74 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 74, XL = 51, XC = 74 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(74^2 + (51 - 74)^2) | Answer: 77.49 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 84.6 mH and C = 4.9 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 84.6, C = 4.9 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(84.6e-3 * 4.9e-6)) | Answer: 247.2 Hz

question: A capacitor of 73.5 uF is charged to 165 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 73.5, V = 165 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*73.5e-6*(165)^2 | Answer: 1001 mJ

question: An alternating voltage has a peak value of 306 V. Find its RMS value.
solution: Given: Vp = 306 | Formula: Vrms = Vp / sqrt(2) | Substitute: Vrms = 306 / sqrt(2) | Answer: 216.4 V

question: A transformer has primary voltage 270 V with 680 primary turns and 380 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 270, N1 = 680, N2 = 380 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 270 * 380/680 | Answer: 150.9 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 410 V and draws an armature current of 59 A. If the armature resistance is 1.37 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 410, Ia = 59, Ra = 1.37 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 410 - 59*1.37 | Answer: 329.2 V

question: A 4-pole induction motor on a 60 Hz supply runs at 780 rpm. Find the slip (%).
formula: s = (Ns - N) / Ns,  Ns = 120 f / P

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 40 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.95. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 40, VL = 400, pf = 0.95 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*400*40*0.95 / 1000 | Answer: 26.33 kW

question: A load has real power 15 kW and apparent power 40 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 15, S = 40 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 15 / 40 | Answer: 0.375

question: A machine delivers 35 kW output while drawing 162 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 35, Pi = 162 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 35/162 * 100 | Answer: 21.6 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 25 V across R1 = 20 ohm and R2 = 40 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 25, R1 = 20, R2 = 40 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 25*40 / (20+40) | Answer: 16.67 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 50 kohm and Rin = 45 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 50, Rin = 45 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 50 / 45 | Answer: 1.111

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 30 kohm and Rg = 43 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 30, Rg = 43 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 30/43 | Answer: 1.698

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 4268. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 4268 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(4268) | Answer: 36.3 dB

question: A first-order system has a time constant of 2.3 s. Find the time (in s) to reach 63.2% of its final value.
solution: For a first-order step response, y = 1 - e^(-t/tau) | y = 0.632 when t = tau | Answer: 2.3 s
formula: At t = tau the response reaches 63.2% (one time constant)

question: A signal is sampled at 128 kHz. According to the Nyquist criterion, what is the maximum signal frequency that can be represented (in kHz)?
solution: Given: fs = 128 | Formula: f_max = fs / 2 | Substitute: f_max = 128 / 2 | Answer: 64 kHz

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.9 m carries a central point load of 10 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 9.9, W = 10 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 10*9.9 / 4 | Answer: 24.75 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.8 m carries a UDL of 5 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.8, w = 5 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 5*(4.8)^2 / 8 | Answer: 14.4 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 4 m carries a point load 40 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4, W = 40 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 40*4 | Answer: 160 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 5.8 m carries a UDL of 24 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.8, w = 24 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 24*(5.8)^2 / 2 | Answer: 403.7 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.1 m carries a point load 35 kN at distance 2 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 6.1, a = 2, W = 35 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 35*(6.1 - 2) / 6.1 | Answer: 23.52 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 3.5 m) carries a central point load 10 kN. With E = 200 GPa and I = 200e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=10000 N, L=3500.0 mm, E=200000 MPa, I=200e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 0.2233 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 6.4 m carries a UDL of 24 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6.4, w = 24 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 24*(6.4)^2 / 12 | Answer: 81.92 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 500 mm, clear cover 25 mm and main bars of diameter 16 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 500, c = 25, dia = 16 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 500 - 25 - 16/2 | Answer: 467 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 10.9 m^2 carrying a factored load of 17.3 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 10.9, w = 17.3 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 17.3 * 10.9 | Answer: 188.6 kN

question: For a bar of diameter 16 mm with design bond stress 2.1 MPa and steel stress 395 MPa, find the development length in mm.
solution: Given: dia = 16, tbd = 2.1, fs = 395 | Formula: Ld = phi fs / (4 tau_bd) | Substitute: Ld = 16*395 / (4*2.1) | Answer: 752.4 mm

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 5.8 m, unit weight 17 kN/m^3, phi = 33 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 11.6 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 21 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 11.6, g = 21 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (21 - 9.81)*11.6 | Answer: 129.8 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 2.6e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1.4, area = 2e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 2.6, i = 1.4, A = 2 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (2.6e-4)*1.4*(2e-3) | Answer: 728 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 0.6 m, bed slope 0.003 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.022. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 1.7 m under a head of 0.7 m. Taking Cd = 0.61 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 5.6 m wide carries a discharge of 24.4 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 220 m and design speed 40 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 220, V = 40 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (40)^2 / (127*220) | Answer: 0.05727
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: For a design speed of 50 km/h with allowable superelevation 0.06 and lateral friction 0.14, find the minimum curve radius in m.
A tank of volume 520 m^3 treats a flow of 145 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 520, Q = 145 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 520 / 145 | Answer: 3.586 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 240 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.33 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 5 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 240, k = 0.33, t = 5 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 240*(1 - e^(-0.33*5)) | Answer: 193.9 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.35, rainfall intensity 85 mm/h over a catchment of 45.3 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.35, i = 85, A = 45.3 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.35*85*45.3 / 360 | Answer: 3.744 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.02 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 560 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.02, M = 560 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 560*(30+0.02)/30 | Answer: 560.4 m

question: Convert the decimal number 109 to binary.
solution: Divide 109 by 2 repeatedly, recording remainders | Reading remainders in reverse gives 1101101 | Answer: 1101101 (binary)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 2 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the decimal number 1182 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 1182 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 49E (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the 8-bit binary number 11010101 to decimal.
solution: Binary 11010101 = sum of bit-weights | Answer: 213 (decimal)
formula: Sum each bit times its positional weight (2^i)

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 00110110 and 11100011.
solution: XOR: 11010101 | Count of 1s = 5 | Answer: 5
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 810 megabits is sent over a link of 82 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 810, B = 82 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 810 / 82 | Answer: 9.878 s

question: A link has bandwidth 59 Mbps and round-trip time 190 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 59, R = 190 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 59e6 * 190e-3 bits = 11210 kb | Answer: 11210 kilobits

question: A channel has bandwidth 20 kHz. Using Nyquist's theorem with 8 signal levels, find the maximum data rate in kbps (noiseless).
solution: Given: B = 20, M = 8 | Formula: C = 2 B log2(M) | Substitute: C = 2*20*log2(8) | Answer: 120 kbps

question: A channel of bandwidth 20 kHz has a signal-to-noise ratio of 15 (linear). Using Shannon's theorem, find the channel capacity in kbps.
solution: Given: B = 20, SNR = 15 | Formula: C = B log2(1 + SNR) | Substitute: C = 20*log2(1 + 15) | Answer: 80 kbps

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.86, cache access time 7 ns and main-memory access time 150 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.86, tc = 7, tm = 150 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.86*7 + (1 - 0.86)*150 | Answer: 27.02 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 239169 elements?
solution: Given: n = 239169 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(239169)) + 1 | Answer: 18

question: An O(n^2) algorithm performs c*n^2 basic operations. If c = 1 and n = 2330, how many operations are performed?
solution: Given: n = 2330 | Formula: operations = n^2 | Substitute: = (2330)^2 | Answer: 5428900

question: A program is 55% parallelisable and run on 2 processors. Using Amdahl's law, find the maximum speedup.
solution: Parallel fraction f = 0.55 | S = 1 / ((1 - 0.55) + 0.55/2) | Answer: 1.379x speedup

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.005, memory access time 170 ns and page-fault service time 9 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 9 ms = 9000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.005)*170 + 0.005*9000000.0 ns | Answer: 45.17 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: A modem transmits at 4500 baud using 2-level signalling. Find the bit rate in bps.
solution: Given: baud = 4500, M = 2 | Formula: bit rate = baud * log2(M) | Substitute: bit rate = 4500 * log2(2) | Answer: 4500 bps

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 0.3 m^3 at 170 kPa and 490 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 0.3, P = 170, Tk = 490 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (170e3)*0.3 / (8.314*490) | Answer: 12.52 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.3 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 19 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.3, t = 19 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.3*19) | Answer: 0.9967

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.11 /min) is to reach 80% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.11, X = 80 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.8) / 0.11 | Answer: 14.63 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.26 /min) reaches 55% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.26, X = 55 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.55 / (0.26*(1 - 0.55)) | Answer: 4.701 min

question: A first-order reaction has a rate constant of 0.16 /min. Find its half-life in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.16 | Formula: t_half = ln(2) / k | Substitute: t_half = 0.6931 / 0.16 | Answer: 4.332 min

question: For a reaction with A = 7e10 /s and activation energy 50 kJ/mol at 500 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 7, Ea = 50, Tk = 500 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 7e10 * exp(-50e3 / (8.314*500)) | Answer: 418259 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.95 and bottoms xW = 0.03, with relative volatility alpha = 2.9. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.95, xw = 0.03, al = 2.9 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.95/0.05)(0.97/0.03)] / ln(2.9) | Answer: 6.03 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.65 and x = 0.3. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.65, x = 0.3 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.65/0.35) / (0.3/0.7) | Answer: 4.333

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.68 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 30 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.68, Psat = 30 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.68 * 30 | Answer: 20.4 kPa

question: A stream of 7.3 kg/s with specific heat 3.8 kJ/kg-K is heated through 10 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 7.3, cp = 3.8, dT = 10 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 7.3*3.8*10 | Answer: 277.4 kW

question: A reactor of volume 8.8 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 3.1 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 8.8, Q = 3.1 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 8.8 / 3.1 | Answer: 2.839 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 7.4e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 4 mm with a concentration difference of 20 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 7.4, L = 4, dC = 20 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (7.4e-9)*20 / (4e-3) | Answer: 37 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 3 min and steady-state gain 0.8. For a step input of magnitude 15, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 3, K = 0.8, M = 15 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 0.8 * 15 | Answer: 12 units

question: A reactor operates at a space time of 19.3 min. Find its space velocity in per hour.
solution: Given: tau = 19.3 | Formula: SV = 60 / tau  (per hour) | Substitute: SV = 60 / 19.3 | Answer: 3.109 /h

question: An aircraft wing of area 70 m^2 flies at 220 m/s (air density 0.4 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 1.1. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 70, V = 220, rho = 0.4, CL = 1.1 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.4*(220)^2*70*1.1 / 1000 | Answer: 745.4 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 40 m^2 flies at 240 m/s (density 0.4 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.06. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 40, V = 240, rho = 0.4, CD = 0.06 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.4*(240)^2*40*0.06 / 1000 | Answer: 27.65 kN

question: Find the dynamic pressure for air of density 1 kg/m^3 moving at 190 m/s, in Pa.
solution: Given: rho = 1, V = 190 | Formula: q = 0.5 rho V^2 | Substitute: q = 0.5*1*(190)^2 | Answer: 18050 Pa

question: An aircraft flies at 570 m/s where the speed of sound is 295 m/s. Find the Mach number.
solution: Given: V = 570, a = 295 | Formula: M = V / a | Substitute: M = 570 / 295 | Answer: 1.932

question: Find the circular orbital velocity of a satellite at altitude 1350 km above Earth (Earth radius 6371 km, mu = 3.986e14 m^3/s^2), in km/s.
A specimen under stress 230 MPa shows an elastic strain of 2.9e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 230, eps = 2.9 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 230 / (2.9e-3) MPa = 79.31 GPa | Answer: 79.31 GPa

question: A block of mass 15 kg has a volume of 3.2e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 15, V = 3.2 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 15 / (3.2e-3) | Answer: 4688 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 2900 mm is heated through 120 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 11e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 2900, dT = 120, al = 11 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 2900*11e-6*120 | Answer: 3.828 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 25 ohm, R2 = 125 ohm and R3 = 60 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 25, R2 = 125, R3 = 60 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 125*60 / 25 | Answer: 300 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 1000 ohm and gauge factor 2.2 experiences a strain of 450e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 1000, GF = 2.2, eps = 450 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 1000*2.2*450e-6 | Answer: 990 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 9.43 when the true value is 10. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.43, true = 10 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.43 - 10| / 10 * 100 | Answer: 5.7 %

question: Annual demand is 43000 units, ordering cost 160 per order and holding cost 30 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 43000, S = 160, H = 30 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*43000*160 / 30) | Answer: 677.2 units

question: An asset costs 230000 with salvage value 34000 after 11 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 230000, Sv = 34000, n = 11 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (230000 - 34000) / 11 | Answer: 17818 per year

question: A product sells for 80 per unit with variable cost 70 per unit and fixed costs 45000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 80, V = 70, F = 45000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 45000 / (80 - 70) | Answer: 4500 units

question: Find the present worth of 135000 received 6 years from now at an interest rate of 8% per year.
solution: Given: F = 135000, n = 6, i = 8 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 135000 / (1 + 0.08)^6 | Answer: 85073 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.92, 0.93 and 0.94 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.92, r2 = 0.93, r3 = 0.94 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.92*0.93*0.94 | Answer: 0.8043

question: Two components each of reliability 0.79 are connected in parallel. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r = 0.79 | Formula: R_parallel = 1 - (1 - r)^2 | Substitute: R = 1 - (1 - 0.79)^2 | Answer: 0.9559

question: A process produces 26 defective items in a batch of 3500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 26, N = 3500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 26/3500 * 1e6 | Answer: 7429 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -5x^3 - 4x^2 - 2x + 1 evaluated at x = -2.
For f(x) = 6x^3 + 4x^2 + 4x + 4, find f''(x) at x = 1.
Evaluate the definite integral of (5x^2 + 3x - 5) dx from x = -1 to x = 5.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = 5x^3/3 + 3x^2/2 + -5x | Evaluate F(5) - F(-1) | Answer: 216
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 4x^2 + x - 4 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[-9, 0], [-2, -4]].
solution: Given: a = -9, b = 0, c = -2, d = -4 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (-9)(-4) - (0)(-2) | Answer: 36

question: Find the determinant of [[1, -5, 1], [-6, 4, 2], [-3, 5, -1]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: 28

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[-1, -5], [-8, 1]].
solution: Trace tr = 0, Determinant = -41 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 6.403

question: Solve for x: -6x + 6y = -8 and -1x + 2y = 6.
solution: Determinant = -6*2 - 6*-1 = -6 | x = (e d - b f) / det = 8.667 | Answer: x = 8.667
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 62, 81, 78, 6, 95.
solution: Sum = 322 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 64.4 | Answer: 64.4

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 36, 49, 4, 45, 11.
solution: Mean = 29 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 20.33

question: Find the slope of the line through (9, -3) and (7, -8).
solution: Given: x1 = 9, y1 = -3, x2 = 7, y2 = -8 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (-8 - -3) / (7 - 9) | Answer: 2.5

question: Find the distance between the points (0, 4) and (9, -6).
solution: Given: x1 = 0, y1 = 4, x2 = 9, y2 = -6 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((9)^2 + (-10)^2) | Answer: 13.45 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (-7,6), (-2,-4), (6,-4).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 40 sq units

question: Evaluate the number of combinations C(16, 4).
solution: Given: n = 16, r = 4 | Formula: C(n, r) = n! / (r! (n - r)!) | Substitute: C(16, 4) = 16! / (4! * 12!) | Answer: 1820

question: Evaluate the number of permutations P(11, 7).
solution: Given: n = 11, r = 7 | Formula: P(n, r) = n! / (n - r)! | Substitute: P(11, 7) = 11! / 4! | Answer: 1663200

question: Find the 29th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -4 and common difference 4.
solution: Given: a = -4, d = 4, n = 29 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -4 + (29 - 1)*4 | Answer: 108

question: Find the sum of the first 33 terms of an AP with first term -2 and common difference -3.
solution: Given: a = -2, d = -3, n = 33 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 33/2 [2*-2 + (33-1)*-3] | Answer: -1650

question: Find the 4th term of a geometric progression with first term 1 and common ratio 2.
solution: Given: a = 1, r = 2, n = 4 | Formula: a_n = a r^(n-1) | Substitute: a_n = 1 * 2^(4-1) | Answer: 8

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 2500 at 13.1% per annum for 1 years.
solution: Given: P = 2500, R = 13.1, Tt = 1 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 2500 * 13.1 * 1 / 100 | Answer: 327.5 currency units

question: Find the amount when 20000 is invested at 11.7% per annum compounded annually for 3 years.
solution: Given: P = 20000, R = 11.7, Tt = 3 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 20000 * (1 + 11.7/100)^3 | Answer: 27873 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (1, -1, 8) and (8, -7, 0).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (4, 2, -4) and (2, 3, 6).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 40.79

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (-1, -4, 5) and (2, -2, 5).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 33.62 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number -4 + 2i.
solution: Given: a = -4, b = 2 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((-4)^2 + (2)^2) | Answer: 4.472

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number 9 + 4i.
solution: Given: a = 9, b = 4 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(4, 9) | Answer: 23.96 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -3x^3 + 2x^2 + 8 at x = 5.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-130 with initial guess x0=3, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1 and ordinates 15, 16, 5, 10, 10, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 23 and 577.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 23 and 577 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 61 and 46.
solution: Given: a = 61, b = 46 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 61*46 / 1 | Answer: 2806
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 31 mm carries an axial tensile load of 17 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 27 mm and length 1300 mm carries an axial load of 59 kN. Take E = 210 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 39 mm transmits a torque of 1500 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 39, Tt = 1500 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(1500*1000) / (pi*(39)^3) | Answer: 128.8 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 47 mm and length 900 mm carries a torque of 1350 N-m. With G = 45 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (47)^4 / 32 = 479062 mm^4 | theta = (1350*1000)(900) / (45000 * 479062) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 3.229 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 112 mm wide and 210 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 112, h = 210 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 112*(210)^2 / 6 | Answer: 823200 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (63 mm x 220 mm) carries a bending moment of 19 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (73 mm x 160 mm) has effective length 3600 mm and E = 200 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 330 MPa is designed for a working stress of 180 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 330, sw = 180 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 330 / 180 | Answer: 1.833

question: A steel bar is fully restrained and heated through 110 deg C. With E = 200 GPa and alpha = 13e-6 /deg C, find the thermal stress in MPa.
solution: Given: dT = 110, E = 200, al = 13 | Formula: sigma = E alpha (dT) | Substitute: sigma = 200000 * 13e-6 * 110 | Answer: 286 MPa

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 650 mm and wall thickness 17 mm carries an internal pressure of 0.7 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 650, t = 17, P = 0.7 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 0.7*650 / (2*17) | Answer: 13.38 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 980 K and 430 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 980, Tc = 430 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 430/980) * 100 | Answer: 56.12 %

question: A refrigerator works between 267 K (cold) and 318 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 267, Th = 318 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 267 / (318 - 267) | Answer: 5.235

question: A heat pump operates between 260 K and 330 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 260, Th = 330 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 330 / (330 - 260) | Answer: 4.714

question: 1.8 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 20 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1.8, dT = 20 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 1.8 * 0.718 * 20 | Answer: 25.85 kJ

question: 6.7 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 25 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 6.7, dT = 25 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 6.7 * 1.005 * 25 | Answer: 168.3 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 3.3 m^3 at 590 K with mass 4.9 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 3.3, Tk = 590, m = 4.9 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 4.9*0.287*590 / 3.3 | Answer: 251.4 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 3.2 kg of air expands isothermally at 350 K from volume V1 to 5*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.2, Tk = 350, ratio = 5 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 3.2*0.287*350*ln(5) | Answer: 517.3 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 4.2 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.27 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 4.2, D = 0.27 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*4.2*0.27 / 0.001 | Answer: 1134000

question: Water flows at 2 m/s through a pipe of diameter 140 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 29.3 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 29.3 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*29.3 / 1000 | Answer: 287.4 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 7.5 m. Taking Cv = 0.97, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 7.5, cv = 0.97 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.97*sqrt(2*9.81*7.5) | Answer: 11.77 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 270 mm) water flows at 1.8 m/s. It contracts to diameter 120 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
Water flows at 1.1 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.32 m and length 430 m. With friction factor f = 0.032, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 38 teeth drives a gear of 64 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1450 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 38, z2 = 64, N1 = 1450 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1450*38 / 64 | Answer: 860.9 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 280 mm rotates at 300 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 280, N = 300 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.28)*300 / 60 | Answer: 4.398 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 18.2 kW at 700 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 18.2, N = 700 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(18.2*1000) / (2*pi*700) | Answer: 248.3 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 3.9 kg rotates at radius 0.58 m at 800 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 6800 N/m and mass 13.5 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 6800, m = 13.5 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(6800/13.5) | Answer: 3.572 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 1.2 m^2 and thickness 0.21 m has conductivity k = 30.4 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 65 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 1.2, L = 0.21, k = 30.4, dT = 65 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 30.4*1.2*65 / 0.21 | Answer: 11291 W

question: A surface of area 2.4 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 100 W/m^2-K to surroundings 40 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 2.4, h = 100, dT = 40 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 100*2.4*40 | Answer: 9600 W

question: In a counter-flow heat exchanger the terminal temperature differences are 65 deg C and 25 deg C. Find the log mean temperature difference (LMTD) in deg C.
solution: Given: dT1 = 65, dT2 = 25 | Formula: LMTD = (dT1 - dT2) / ln(dT1/dT2) | Substitute: LMTD = (65 - 25) / ln(65/25) | Answer: 41.86 deg C

question: In turning, cutting speed = 170 m/min, feed = 0.39 mm/rev, depth of cut = 1.2 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 170, f = 0.39, d = 1.2 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*170*0.39*1.2 | Answer: 79560 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 440 mm is turned at 400 rpm with a feed of 0.16 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 440, N = 400, f = 0.16 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 440 / (0.16*400) | Answer: 6.875 min

question: A resistor of 163 ohm carries a current of 7.4 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 163, I = 7.4 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 7.4 * 163 | Answer: 1206 V

question: Three resistors 58 ohm, 7 ohm and 27 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 58, R2 = 7, R3 = 27 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 58 + 7 + 27 | Answer: 92 ohm

question: Two resistors 72 ohm and 8 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 72, R2 = 8 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 72*8 / (72+8) | Answer: 7.2 ohm

question: A device draws 7.5 A at 125 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 125, I = 7.5 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 125 * 7.5 | Answer: 937.5 W

question: A current of 10 A flows through a 94 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 10, R = 94 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (10)^2 * 94 | Answer: 9400 W

question: Two capacitors 44.5 uF and 9.7 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 44.5, C2 = 9.7 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 44.5*9.7 / (44.5+9.7) | Answer: 7.964 uF

question: A resistor 35 kohm and capacitor 5.3 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 35, C = 5.3 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (35k)(5.3u) = 185.5 ms | Answer: 185.5 ms

question: An inductor 323.6 mH is in series with 146 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 323.6, R = 146 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (323.6e-3) / 146 | Answer: 2.216 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 100 mH inductor at 880 Hz.
