solution: Given: L = 100, f = 880 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (880)(100e-3) | Answer: 552.9 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 32.1 uF capacitor at 160 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 32.1, f = 160 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (160)(32.1e-6)) | Answer: 30.99 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 19 ohm, XL = 77 ohm and XC = 129 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 19, XL = 77, XC = 129 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(19^2 + (77 - 129)^2) | Answer: 55.36 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 45.6 mH and C = 9.9 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 45.6, C = 9.9 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(45.6e-3 * 9.9e-6)) | Answer: 236.9 Hz

question: A capacitor of 54.1 uF is charged to 370 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 54.1, V = 370 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*54.1e-6*(370)^2 | Answer: 3703 mJ

question: An alternating voltage has a peak value of 58 V. Find its RMS value.
solution: Given: Vp = 58 | Formula: Vrms = Vp / sqrt(2) | Substitute: Vrms = 58 / sqrt(2) | Answer: 41.01 V

question: A transformer has primary voltage 230 V with 640 primary turns and 100 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 230, N1 = 640, N2 = 100 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 230 * 100/640 | Answer: 35.94 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 110 V and draws an armature current of 50 A. If the armature resistance is 0.22 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 110, Ia = 50, Ra = 0.22 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 110 - 50*0.22 | Answer: 99 V

question: A 4-pole induction motor on a 60 Hz supply runs at 930 rpm. Find the slip (%).
formula: s = (Ns - N) / Ns,  Ns = 120 f / P

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 50 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.75. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 50, VL = 400, pf = 0.75 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*400*50*0.75 / 1000 | Answer: 25.98 kW

question: A load has real power 155 kW and apparent power 165 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 155, S = 165 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 155 / 165 | Answer: 0.9394

question: A machine delivers 70 kW output while drawing 187 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 70, Pi = 187 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 70/187 * 100 | Answer: 37.43 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 26 V across R1 = 11 ohm and R2 = 3 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 26, R1 = 11, R2 = 3 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 26*3 / (11+3) | Answer: 5.571 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 220 kohm and Rin = 27 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 220, Rin = 27 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 220 / 27 | Answer: 8.148

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 40 kohm and Rg = 34 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 40, Rg = 34 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 40/34 | Answer: 2.176

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 6925. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 6925 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(6925) | Answer: 38.4 dB

question: A first-order system has a time constant of 9.2 s. Find the time (in s) to reach 63.2% of its final value.
solution: For a first-order step response, y = 1 - e^(-t/tau) | y = 0.632 when t = tau | Answer: 9.2 s
formula: At t = tau the response reaches 63.2% (one time constant)

question: A signal is sampled at 122 kHz. According to the Nyquist criterion, what is the maximum signal frequency that can be represented (in kHz)?
solution: Given: fs = 122 | Formula: f_max = fs / 2 | Substitute: f_max = 122 / 2 | Answer: 61 kHz

question: A simply supported beam of span 5.8 m carries a central point load of 85 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.8, W = 85 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 85*5.8 / 4 | Answer: 123.2 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.2 m carries a UDL of 30 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.2, w = 30 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 30*(4.2)^2 / 8 | Answer: 66.15 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 1.2 m carries a point load 55 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 1.2, W = 55 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 55*1.2 | Answer: 66 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 5.9 m carries a UDL of 38 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.9, w = 38 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 38*(5.9)^2 / 2 | Answer: 661.4 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.6 m carries a point load 60 kN at distance 3.7 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 6.6, a = 3.7, W = 60 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 60*(6.6 - 3.7) / 6.6 | Answer: 26.36 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 7.4 m) carries a central point load 65 kN. With E = 200 GPa and I = 540e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=65000 N, L=7400.0 mm, E=200000 MPa, I=540e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 5.081 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 5.9 m carries a UDL of 42 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.9, w = 42 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 42*(5.9)^2 / 12 | Answer: 121.8 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 390 mm, clear cover 40 mm and main bars of diameter 20 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 390, c = 40, dia = 20 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 390 - 40 - 20/2 | Answer: 340 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 13.1 m^2 carrying a factored load of 8.1 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 13.1, w = 8.1 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 8.1 * 13.1 | Answer: 106.1 kN

question: For a bar of diameter 20 mm with design bond stress 1.4 MPa and steel stress 395 MPa, find the development length in mm.
solution: Given: dia = 20, tbd = 1.4, fs = 395 | Formula: Ld = phi fs / (4 tau_bd) | Substitute: Ld = 20*395 / (4*1.4) | Answer: 1411 mm

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 4.9 m, unit weight 18 kN/m^3, phi = 37 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 6.3 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 19 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 6.3, g = 19 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (19 - 9.81)*6.3 | Answer: 57.9 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 4e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1.1, area = 6.9e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 4, i = 1.1, A = 6.9 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (4e-4)*1.1*(6.9e-3) | Answer: 3036 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 0.8 m, bed slope 0.005 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.014. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 1.7 m under a head of 0.7 m. Taking Cd = 0.62 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 2.3 m wide carries a discharge of 9.3 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 340 m and design speed 70 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 340, V = 70 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (70)^2 / (127*340) | Answer: 0.1135
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: For a design speed of 65 km/h with allowable superelevation 0.05 and lateral friction 0.15, find the minimum curve radius in m.
A tank of volume 290 m^3 treats a flow of 125 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 290, Q = 125 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 290 / 125 | Answer: 2.32 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 180 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.12 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 3 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 180, k = 0.12, t = 3 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 180*(1 - e^(-0.12*3)) | Answer: 54.42 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.56, rainfall intensity 80 mm/h over a catchment of 52.4 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.56, i = 80, A = 52.4 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.56*80*52.4 / 360 | Answer: 6.521 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.03 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 300 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.03, M = 300 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 300*(30+0.03)/30 | Answer: 300.3 m

question: Convert the decimal number 247 to binary.
solution: Divide 247 by 2 repeatedly, recording remainders | Reading remainders in reverse gives 11110111 | Answer: 11110111 (binary)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 2 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the decimal number 3213 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 3213 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: C8D (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the 8-bit binary number 00100101 to decimal.
solution: Binary 00100101 = sum of bit-weights | Answer: 37 (decimal)
formula: Sum each bit times its positional weight (2^i)

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 10000100 and 10110101.
solution: XOR: 00110001 | Count of 1s = 3 | Answer: 3
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 710 megabits is sent over a link of 89 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 710, B = 89 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 710 / 89 | Answer: 7.978 s

question: A link has bandwidth 46 Mbps and round-trip time 10 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 46, R = 10 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 46e6 * 10e-3 bits = 460 kb | Answer: 460 kilobits

question: A channel has bandwidth 11 kHz. Using Nyquist's theorem with 8 signal levels, find the maximum data rate in kbps (noiseless).
solution: Given: B = 11, M = 8 | Formula: C = 2 B log2(M) | Substitute: C = 2*11*log2(8) | Answer: 66 kbps

question: A channel of bandwidth 17 kHz has a signal-to-noise ratio of 255 (linear). Using Shannon's theorem, find the channel capacity in kbps.
solution: Given: B = 17, SNR = 255 | Formula: C = B log2(1 + SNR) | Substitute: C = 17*log2(1 + 255) | Answer: 136 kbps

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.85, cache access time 4 ns and main-memory access time 170 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.85, tc = 4, tm = 170 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.85*4 + (1 - 0.85)*170 | Answer: 28.9 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 380256 elements?
solution: Given: n = 380256 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(380256)) + 1 | Answer: 19

question: An O(n^2) algorithm performs c*n^2 basic operations. If c = 1 and n = 180, how many operations are performed?
solution: Given: n = 180 | Formula: operations = n^2 | Substitute: = (180)^2 | Answer: 32400

question: A program is 85% parallelisable and run on 4 processors. Using Amdahl's law, find the maximum speedup.
solution: Parallel fraction f = 0.85 | S = 1 / ((1 - 0.85) + 0.85/4) | Answer: 2.759x speedup

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.017, memory access time 110 ns and page-fault service time 9 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 9 ms = 9000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.017)*110 + 0.017*9000000.0 ns | Answer: 153.1 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: A modem transmits at 4800 baud using 4-level signalling. Find the bit rate in bps.
solution: Given: baud = 4800, M = 4 | Formula: bit rate = baud * log2(M) | Substitute: bit rate = 4800 * log2(4) | Answer: 9600 bps

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 1.9 m^3 at 340 kPa and 470 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 1.9, P = 340, Tk = 470 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (340e3)*1.9 / (8.314*470) | Answer: 165.3 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.25 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 16 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.25, t = 16 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.25*16) | Answer: 0.9817

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.25 /min) is to reach 60% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.25, X = 60 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.6) / 0.25 | Answer: 3.665 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.25 /min) reaches 65% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.25, X = 65 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.65 / (0.25*(1 - 0.65)) | Answer: 7.429 min

question: A first-order reaction has a rate constant of 0.34 /min. Find its half-life in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.34 | Formula: t_half = ln(2) / k | Substitute: t_half = 0.6931 / 0.34 | Answer: 2.039 min

question: For a reaction with A = 6e10 /s and activation energy 55 kJ/mol at 480 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 6, Ea = 55, Tk = 480 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 6e10 * exp(-55e3 / (8.314*480)) | Answer: 62046 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.91 and bottoms xW = 0.03, with relative volatility alpha = 3. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.91, xw = 0.03, al = 3 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.91/0.09)(0.97/0.03)] / ln(3) | Answer: 5.27 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.86 and x = 0.49. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.86, x = 0.49 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.86/0.14) / (0.49/0.51) | Answer: 6.394

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.84 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 55 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.84, Psat = 55 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.84 * 55 | Answer: 46.2 kPa

question: A stream of 2.8 kg/s with specific heat 1.6 kJ/kg-K is heated through 25 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 2.8, cp = 1.6, dT = 25 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 2.8*1.6*25 | Answer: 112 kW

question: A reactor of volume 2.3 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 4.5 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 2.3, Q = 4.5 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 2.3 / 4.5 | Answer: 0.5111 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 4.6e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 5 mm with a concentration difference of 30 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 4.6, L = 5, dC = 30 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (4.6e-9)*30 / (5e-3) | Answer: 27.6 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 4 min and steady-state gain 3.2. For a step input of magnitude 7, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 4, K = 3.2, M = 7 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 3.2 * 7 | Answer: 22.4 units

question: A reactor operates at a space time of 3.2 min. Find its space velocity in per hour.
solution: Given: tau = 3.2 | Formula: SV = 60 / tau  (per hour) | Substitute: SV = 60 / 3.2 | Answer: 18.75 /h

question: An aircraft wing of area 105 m^2 flies at 190 m/s (air density 0.7 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 1.1. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 105, V = 190, rho = 0.7, CL = 1.1 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.7*(190)^2*105*1.1 / 1000 | Answer: 1459 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 20 m^2 flies at 230 m/s (density 1 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.03. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 20, V = 230, rho = 1, CD = 0.03 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*1*(230)^2*20*0.03 / 1000 | Answer: 15.87 kN

question: Find the dynamic pressure for air of density 1.225 kg/m^3 moving at 250 m/s, in Pa.
solution: Given: rho = 1.225, V = 250 | Formula: q = 0.5 rho V^2 | Substitute: q = 0.5*1.225*(250)^2 | Answer: 38281 Pa

question: An aircraft flies at 550 m/s where the speed of sound is 340 m/s. Find the Mach number.
solution: Given: V = 550, a = 340 | Formula: M = V / a | Substitute: M = 550 / 340 | Answer: 1.618

question: Find the circular orbital velocity of a satellite at altitude 450 km above Earth (Earth radius 6371 km, mu = 3.986e14 m^3/s^2), in km/s.
A specimen under stress 200 MPa shows an elastic strain of 1.1e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 200, eps = 1.1 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 200 / (1.1e-3) MPa = 181.8 GPa | Answer: 181.8 GPa

question: A block of mass 23 kg has a volume of 2e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 23, V = 2 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 23 / (2e-3) | Answer: 11500 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 1900 mm is heated through 110 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 23e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 1900, dT = 110, al = 23 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 1900*23e-6*110 | Answer: 4.807 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 60 ohm, R2 = 70 ohm and R3 = 200 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 60, R2 = 70, R3 = 200 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 70*200 / 60 | Answer: 233.3 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 1000 ohm and gauge factor 2.1 experiences a strain of 1600e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 1000, GF = 2.1, eps = 1600 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 1000*2.1*1600e-6 | Answer: 3360 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 10.6 when the true value is 100. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10.6, true = 100 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10.6 - 100| / 100 * 100 | Answer: 89.4 %

question: Annual demand is 45500 units, ordering cost 40 per order and holding cost 3 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 45500, S = 40, H = 3 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*45500*40 / 3) | Answer: 1102 units

question: An asset costs 240000 with salvage value 20000 after 6 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 240000, Sv = 20000, n = 6 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (240000 - 20000) / 6 | Answer: 36667 per year

question: A product sells for 250 per unit with variable cost 140 per unit and fixed costs 135000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 250, V = 140, F = 135000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 135000 / (250 - 140) | Answer: 1227 units

question: Find the present worth of 70000 received 5 years from now at an interest rate of 10% per year.
solution: Given: F = 70000, n = 5, i = 10 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 70000 / (1 + 0.1)^5 | Answer: 43464 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.91, 0.92 and 0.97 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.91, r2 = 0.92, r3 = 0.97 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.91*0.92*0.97 | Answer: 0.8121

question: Two components each of reliability 0.76 are connected in parallel. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r = 0.76 | Formula: R_parallel = 1 - (1 - r)^2 | Substitute: R = 1 - (1 - 0.76)^2 | Answer: 0.9424

question: A process produces 13 defective items in a batch of 19500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 13, N = 19500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 13/19500 * 1e6 | Answer: 666.7 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -x^3 + 2x^2 - 8x + 5 evaluated at x = 1.
For f(x) = -5x^3 + 5x^2 + 5x + 6, find f''(x) at x = -2.
Evaluate the definite integral of (-x^2 + 4x + 2) dx from x = 1 to x = 4.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = -1x^3/3 + 4x^2/2 + 2x | Evaluate F(4) - F(1) | Answer: 15
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 6x^2 - 3x - 7 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[2, 9], [6, 1]].
solution: Given: a = 2, b = 9, c = 6, d = 1 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (2)(1) - (9)(6) | Answer: -52

question: Find the determinant of [[0, 3, -4], [4, 6, -1], [1, -2, 2]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: 29

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[2, -4], [-1, -3]].
solution: Trace tr = -1, Determinant = -10 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 2.702

question: Solve for x: -2x + 4y = -10 and -2x + -2y = 7.
solution: Determinant = -2*-2 - 4*-2 = 12 | x = (e d - b f) / det = -0.6667 | Answer: x = -0.6667
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 79, 70, 11, 1, 57.
solution: Sum = 218 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 43.6 | Answer: 43.6

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 21, 6, 9, 36, 30.
solution: Mean = 20.4 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 12.97

question: Find the slope of the line through (6, -4) and (-6, -8).
Find the distance between the points (7, -6) and (-3, -9).
solution: Given: x1 = 7, y1 = -6, x2 = -3, y2 = -9 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-10)^2 + (-3)^2) | Answer: 10.44 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (-8,-1), (3,-1), (1,1).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 11 sq units

question: Evaluate the number of combinations C(16, 1).
solution: Given: n = 16, r = 1 | Formula: C(n, r) = n! / (r! (n - r)!) | Substitute: C(16, 1) = 16! / (1! * 15!) | Answer: 16

question: Evaluate the number of permutations P(14, 8).
solution: Given: n = 14, r = 8 | Formula: P(n, r) = n! / (n - r)! | Substitute: P(14, 8) = 14! / 6! | Answer: 121080960

question: Find the 30th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -17 and common difference 1.
solution: Given: a = -17, d = 1, n = 30 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -17 + (30 - 1)*1 | Answer: 12

question: Find the sum of the first 14 terms of an AP with first term 15 and common difference -4.
solution: Given: a = 15, d = -4, n = 14 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 14/2 [2*15 + (14-1)*-4] | Answer: -154

question: Find the 6th term of a geometric progression with first term 7 and common ratio 2.
solution: Given: a = 7, r = 2, n = 6 | Formula: a_n = a r^(n-1) | Substitute: a_n = 7 * 2^(6-1) | Answer: 224

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 22000 at 9.6% per annum for 9 years.
solution: Given: P = 22000, R = 9.6, Tt = 9 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 22000 * 9.6 * 9 / 100 | Answer: 19008 currency units

question: Find the amount when 38000 is invested at 9.8% per annum compounded annually for 4 years.
solution: Given: P = 38000, R = 9.8, Tt = 4 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 38000 * (1 + 9.8/100)^4 | Answer: 55232 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (-7, -6, 0) and (0, -1, 6).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (4, 6, 1) and (-5, -2, -2).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 24.35

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (1, -1, -5) and (5, 1, 5).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 124.5 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number 11 + 6i.
solution: Given: a = 11, b = 6 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((11)^2 + (6)^2) | Answer: 12.53

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number 9 + -5i.
solution: Given: a = 9, b = -5 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(-5, 9) | Answer: -29.05 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = 5x^3 + 7x^2 + 4x - 8 at x = 2.
solution: Given: a = 5, b = 7, c = 4, d = -8, x0 = 2 | Formula: f(x0) = a x0^3 + b x0^2 + c x0 + d | Substitute: f(2) = 5(2)^3 + 7(2)^2 + 4(2) + -8 | Answer: 68

question: Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-134 with initial guess x0=8, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=0.6 and ordinates 12, 7, 11, 3, 10, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 501 and 418.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 501 and 418 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 43 and 50.
solution: Given: a = 43, b = 50 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 43*50 / 1 | Answer: 2150
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 60 mm carries an axial tensile load of 91 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 34 mm and length 2800 mm carries an axial load of 29 kN. Take E = 110 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 59 mm transmits a torque of 200 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 59, Tt = 200 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(200*1000) / (pi*(59)^3) | Answer: 4.96 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 50 mm and length 500 mm carries a torque of 1550 N-m. With G = 80 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (50)^4 / 32 = 613592 mm^4 | theta = (1550*1000)(500) / (80000 * 613592) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 0.9046 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 139 mm wide and 130 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 139, h = 130 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 139*(130)^2 / 6 | Answer: 391517 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (87 mm x 110 mm) carries a bending moment of 37 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (36 mm x 90 mm) has effective length 3300 mm and E = 200 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 670 MPa is designed for a working stress of 130 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 670, sw = 130 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 670 / 130 | Answer: 5.154

question: A steel bar is fully restrained and heated through 80 deg C. With E = 200 GPa and alpha = 12e-6 /deg C, find the thermal stress in MPa.
solution: Given: dT = 80, E = 200, al = 12 | Formula: sigma = E alpha (dT) | Substitute: sigma = 200000 * 12e-6 * 80 | Answer: 192 MPa

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1100 mm and wall thickness 11 mm carries an internal pressure of 1.8 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1100, t = 11, P = 1.8 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 1.8*1100 / (2*11) | Answer: 90 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 1200 K and 380 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 1200, Tc = 380 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 380/1200) * 100 | Answer: 68.33 %

question: A refrigerator works between 256 K (cold) and 320 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 256, Th = 320 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 256 / (320 - 256) | Answer: 4

question: A heat pump operates between 265 K and 334 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 265, Th = 334 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 334 / (334 - 265) | Answer: 4.841

question: 2.2 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 120 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.2, dT = 120 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 2.2 * 0.718 * 120 | Answer: 189.6 kJ

question: 7.8 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 130 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 7.8, dT = 130 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 7.8 * 1.005 * 130 | Answer: 1019 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 1 m^3 at 550 K with mass 1.8 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 1, Tk = 550, m = 1.8 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 1.8*0.287*550 / 1 | Answer: 284.1 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 3.4 kg of air expands isothermally at 420 K from volume V1 to 4*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.4, Tk = 420, ratio = 4 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 3.4*0.287*420*ln(4) | Answer: 568.2 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 4 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.07 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 4, D = 0.07 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*4*0.07 / 0.001 | Answer: 280000

question: Water flows at 1.3 m/s through a pipe of diameter 160 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 17.7 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 17.7 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*17.7 / 1000 | Answer: 173.6 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 10.3 m. Taking Cv = 0.99, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 10.3, cv = 0.99 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.99*sqrt(2*9.81*10.3) | Answer: 14.07 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 240 mm) water flows at 0.7 m/s. It contracts to diameter 50 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 240, d2 = 50, V1 = 0.7 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 0.7*(240/50)^2 | Answer: 16.13 m/s

question: Water flows at 1.6 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.43 m and length 210 m. With friction factor f = 0.025, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 31 teeth drives a gear of 61 teeth. If the pinion runs at 350 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 31, z2 = 61, N1 = 350 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 350*31 / 61 | Answer: 177.9 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 100 mm rotates at 1400 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 100, N = 1400 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.1)*1400 / 60 | Answer: 7.33 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 6.2 kW at 1300 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 6.2, N = 1300 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(6.2*1000) / (2*pi*1300) | Answer: 45.54 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 7.5 kg rotates at radius 0.3 m at 500 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 19900 N/m and mass 17.5 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 19900, m = 17.5 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(19900/17.5) | Answer: 5.367 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 3.3 m^2 and thickness 0.4 m has conductivity k = 1.9 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 150 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 3.3, L = 0.4, k = 1.9, dT = 150 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 1.9*3.3*150 / 0.4 | Answer: 2351 W

question: A surface of area 5 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 180 W/m^2-K to surroundings 55 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 5, h = 180, dT = 55 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 180*5*55 | Answer: 49500 W

question: In a counter-flow heat exchanger the terminal temperature differences are 50 deg C and 10 deg C. Find the log mean temperature difference (LMTD) in deg C.
solution: Given: dT1 = 50, dT2 = 10 | Formula: LMTD = (dT1 - dT2) / ln(dT1/dT2) | Substitute: LMTD = (50 - 10) / ln(50/10) | Answer: 24.85 deg C

question: In turning, cutting speed = 110 m/min, feed = 0.43 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2.8 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 110, f = 0.43, d = 2.8 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*110*0.43*2.8 | Answer: 132440 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 480 mm is turned at 400 rpm with a feed of 0.28 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 480, N = 400, f = 0.28 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 480 / (0.28*400) | Answer: 4.286 min

question: A resistor of 177 ohm carries a current of 8 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 177, I = 8 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 8 * 177 | Answer: 1416 V

question: Three resistors 79 ohm, 36 ohm and 87 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 79, R2 = 36, R3 = 87 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 79 + 36 + 87 | Answer: 202 ohm

question: Two resistors 62 ohm and 95 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 62, R2 = 95 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 62*95 / (62+95) | Answer: 37.52 ohm

question: A device draws 11.4 A at 160 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 160, I = 11.4 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 160 * 11.4 | Answer: 1824 W

question: A current of 5.2 A flows through a 74 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 5.2, R = 74 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (5.2)^2 * 74 | Answer: 2001 W

question: Two capacitors 46.6 uF and 19.8 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 46.6, C2 = 19.8 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 46.6*19.8 / (46.6+19.8) | Answer: 13.9 uF

question: A resistor 38 kohm and capacitor 18.6 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 38, C = 18.6 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (38k)(18.6u) = 706.8 ms | Answer: 706.8 ms

question: An inductor 357 mH is in series with 65 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 357, R = 65 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (357e-3) / 65 | Answer: 5.492 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 136.5 mH inductor at 420 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 136.5, f = 420 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (420)(136.5e-3) | Answer: 360.2 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 20.8 uF capacitor at 140 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 20.8, f = 140 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (140)(20.8e-6)) | Answer: 54.65 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 100 ohm, XL = 127 ohm and XC = 22 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 100, XL = 127, XC = 22 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(100^2 + (127 - 22)^2) | Answer: 145 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 82.9 mH and C = 1.5 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 82.9, C = 1.5 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(82.9e-3 * 1.5e-6)) | Answer: 451.3 Hz

question: A capacitor of 28.9 uF is charged to 175 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 28.9, V = 175 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*28.9e-6*(175)^2 | Answer: 442.5 mJ

question: An alternating voltage has a peak value of 130 V. Find its RMS value.
solution: Given: Vp = 130 | Formula: Vrms = Vp / sqrt(2) | Substitute: Vrms = 130 / sqrt(2) | Answer: 91.92 V

question: A transformer has primary voltage 190 V with 450 primary turns and 60 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 190, N1 = 450, N2 = 60 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 190 * 60/450 | Answer: 25.33 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 420 V and draws an armature current of 17 A. If the armature resistance is 0.18 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 420, Ia = 17, Ra = 0.18 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 420 - 17*0.18 | Answer: 416.9 V

question: A 6-pole induction motor on a 60 Hz supply runs at 770 rpm. Find the slip (%).
formula: s = (Ns - N) / Ns,  Ns = 120 f / P

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 120 A at 433 V (line) with a power factor of 0.84. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 120, VL = 433, pf = 0.84 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*433*120*0.84 / 1000 | Answer: 75.6 kW

question: A load has real power 95 kW and apparent power 215 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 95, S = 215 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 95 / 215 | Answer: 0.4419

question: A machine delivers 115 kW output while drawing 137 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 115, Pi = 137 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 115/137 * 100 | Answer: 83.94 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 8 V across R1 = 4 ohm and R2 = 38 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 8, R1 = 4, R2 = 38 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 8*38 / (4+38) | Answer: 7.238 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 10 kohm and Rin = 2 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 10, Rin = 2 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 10 / 2 | Answer: 5

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 80 kohm and Rg = 24 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 80, Rg = 24 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 80/24 | Answer: 4.333

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 8019. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 8019 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(8019) | Answer: 39.04 dB

question: A first-order system has a time constant of 6.4 s. Find the time (in s) to reach 63.2% of its final value.
solution: For a first-order step response, y = 1 - e^(-t/tau) | y = 0.632 when t = tau | Answer: 6.4 s
formula: At t = tau the response reaches 63.2% (one time constant)

question: A signal is sampled at 116 kHz. According to the Nyquist criterion, what is the maximum signal frequency that can be represented (in kHz)?
solution: Given: fs = 116 | Formula: f_max = fs / 2 | Substitute: f_max = 116 / 2 | Answer: 58 kHz

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.4 m carries a central point load of 70 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.4, W = 70 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 70*4.4 / 4 | Answer: 77 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.9 m carries a UDL of 15 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 9.9, w = 15 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 15*(9.9)^2 / 8 | Answer: 183.8 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 3.6 m carries a point load 55 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.6, W = 55 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 55*3.6 | Answer: 198 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 1.3 m carries a UDL of 22 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 1.3, w = 22 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 22*(1.3)^2 / 2 | Answer: 18.59 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.9 m carries a point load 80 kN at distance 2.2 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 4.9, a = 2.2, W = 80 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 80*(4.9 - 2.2) / 4.9 | Answer: 44.08 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 6.6 m) carries a central point load 20 kN. With E = 30 GPa and I = 370e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=20000 N, L=6600.0 mm, E=30000 MPa, I=370e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 10.79 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 7 m carries a UDL of 18 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7, w = 18 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 18*(7)^2 / 12 | Answer: 73.5 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 600 mm, clear cover 25 mm and main bars of diameter 12 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 600, c = 25, dia = 12 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 600 - 25 - 12/2 | Answer: 569 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 38.8 m^2 carrying a factored load of 9.7 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 38.8, w = 9.7 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 9.7 * 38.8 | Answer: 376.4 kN

question: For a bar of diameter 20 mm with design bond stress 1.6 MPa and steel stress 360 MPa, find the development length in mm.
solution: Given: dia = 20, tbd = 1.6, fs = 360 | Formula: Ld = phi fs / (4 tau_bd) | Substitute: Ld = 20*360 / (4*1.6) | Answer: 1125 mm

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 3.6 m, unit weight 19 kN/m^3, phi = 36 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 4 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 19 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 4, g = 19 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (19 - 9.81)*4 | Answer: 36.76 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 5.9e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1.5, area = 2.7e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 5.9, i = 1.5, A = 2.7 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (5.9e-4)*1.5*(2.7e-3) | Answer: 239 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 2.2 m, bed slope 0.008 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.023. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 4.9 m under a head of 1.2 m. Taking Cd = 0.63 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 5.3 m wide carries a discharge of 24.5 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 510 m and design speed 70 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 510, V = 70 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (70)^2 / (127*510) | Answer: 0.07565
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: For a design speed of 100 km/h with allowable superelevation 0.06 and lateral friction 0.15, find the minimum curve radius in m.
A tank of volume 370 m^3 treats a flow of 30 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 370, Q = 30 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 370 / 30 | Answer: 12.33 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 350 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.32 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 8 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 350, k = 0.32, t = 8 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 350*(1 - e^(-0.32*8)) | Answer: 322.9 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.68, rainfall intensity 110 mm/h over a catchment of 59.2 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.68, i = 110, A = 59.2 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.68*110*59.2 / 360 | Answer: 12.3 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.03 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 390 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.03, M = 390 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 390*(20+0.03)/20 | Answer: 390.6 m

question: Convert the decimal number 229 to binary.
solution: Divide 229 by 2 repeatedly, recording remainders | Reading remainders in reverse gives 11100101 | Answer: 11100101 (binary)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 2 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the decimal number 2164 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 2164 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 874 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the 8-bit binary number 00101111 to decimal.
solution: Binary 00101111 = sum of bit-weights | Answer: 47 (decimal)
formula: Sum each bit times its positional weight (2^i)

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 01001110 and 11101110.
solution: XOR: 10100000 | Count of 1s = 2 | Answer: 2
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 960 megabits is sent over a link of 4 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 960, B = 4 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 960 / 4 | Answer: 240 s

question: A link has bandwidth 98 Mbps and round-trip time 140 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 98, R = 140 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 98e6 * 140e-3 bits = 13720 kb | Answer: 13720 kilobits

question: A channel has bandwidth 10 kHz. Using Nyquist's theorem with 4 signal levels, find the maximum data rate in kbps (noiseless).
solution: Given: B = 10, M = 4 | Formula: C = 2 B log2(M) | Substitute: C = 2*10*log2(4) | Answer: 40 kbps

question: A channel of bandwidth 7 kHz has a signal-to-noise ratio of 15 (linear). Using Shannon's theorem, find the channel capacity in kbps.
solution: Given: B = 7, SNR = 15 | Formula: C = B log2(1 + SNR) | Substitute: C = 7*log2(1 + 15) | Answer: 28 kbps

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.87, cache access time 7 ns and main-memory access time 120 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.87, tc = 7, tm = 120 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.87*7 + (1 - 0.87)*120 | Answer: 21.69 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 812816 elements?
solution: Given: n = 812816 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(812816)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: An O(n^2) algorithm performs c*n^2 basic operations. If c = 1 and n = 670, how many operations are performed?
solution: Given: n = 670 | Formula: operations = n^2 | Substitute: = (670)^2 | Answer: 448900

question: A program is 90% parallelisable and run on 4 processors. Using Amdahl's law, find the maximum speedup.
solution: Parallel fraction f = 0.9 | S = 1 / ((1 - 0.9) + 0.9/4) | Answer: 3.077x speedup

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.005, memory access time 170 ns and page-fault service time 10 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 10 ms = 10000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.005)*170 + 0.005*10000000.0 ns | Answer: 50.17 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: A modem transmits at 2100 baud using 2-level signalling. Find the bit rate in bps.
solution: Given: baud = 2100, M = 2 | Formula: bit rate = baud * log2(M) | Substitute: bit rate = 2100 * log2(2) | Answer: 2100 bps

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 1.3 m^3 at 360 kPa and 390 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 1.3, P = 360, Tk = 390 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (360e3)*1.3 / (8.314*390) | Answer: 144.3 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.09 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 5 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.09, t = 5 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.09*5) | Answer: 0.3624

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.24 /min) is to reach 50% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.24, X = 50 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.5) / 0.24 | Answer: 2.888 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.19 /min) reaches 80% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.19, X = 80 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.8 / (0.19*(1 - 0.8)) | Answer: 21.05 min

question: A first-order reaction has a rate constant of 0.45 /min. Find its half-life in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.45 | Formula: t_half = ln(2) / k | Substitute: t_half = 0.6931 / 0.45 | Answer: 1.54 min

question: For a reaction with A = 4e10 /s and activation energy 50 kJ/mol at 400 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 4, Ea = 50, Tk = 400 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 4e10 * exp(-50e3 / (8.314*400)) | Answer: 11817 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.97 and bottoms xW = 0.06, with relative volatility alpha = 1.6. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.97, xw = 0.06, al = 1.6 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.97/0.03)(0.94/0.06)] / ln(1.6) | Answer: 13.25 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.57 and x = 0.27. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.57, x = 0.27 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.57/0.43) / (0.27/0.73) | Answer: 3.584

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.15 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 70 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.15, Psat = 70 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.15 * 70 | Answer: 10.5 kPa

question: A stream of 8.7 kg/s with specific heat 3.4 kJ/kg-K is heated through 80 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 8.7, cp = 3.4, dT = 80 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 8.7*3.4*80 | Answer: 2366 kW

question: A reactor of volume 19.1 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 4 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 19.1, Q = 4 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 19.1 / 4 | Answer: 4.775 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 8.8e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 2 mm with a concentration difference of 20 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 8.8, L = 2, dC = 20 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (8.8e-9)*20 / (2e-3) | Answer: 88 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 9.8 min and steady-state gain 0.8. For a step input of magnitude 8, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 9.8, K = 0.8, M = 8 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 0.8 * 8 | Answer: 6.4 units

question: A reactor operates at a space time of 17.3 min. Find its space velocity in per hour.
solution: Given: tau = 17.3 | Formula: SV = 60 / tau  (per hour) | Substitute: SV = 60 / 17.3 | Answer: 3.468 /h

question: An aircraft wing of area 85 m^2 flies at 70 m/s (air density 1 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.4. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 85, V = 70, rho = 1, CL = 0.4 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1*(70)^2*85*0.4 / 1000 | Answer: 83.3 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 90 m^2 flies at 110 m/s (density 0.7 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.11. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 90, V = 110, rho = 0.7, CD = 0.11 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.7*(110)^2*90*0.11 / 1000 | Answer: 41.93 kN

question: Find the dynamic pressure for air of density 1 kg/m^3 moving at 60 m/s, in Pa.
solution: Given: rho = 1, V = 60 | Formula: q = 0.5 rho V^2 | Substitute: q = 0.5*1*(60)^2 | Answer: 1800 Pa

question: An aircraft flies at 350 m/s where the speed of sound is 340 m/s. Find the Mach number.
solution: Given: V = 350, a = 340 | Formula: M = V / a | Substitute: M = 350 / 340 | Answer: 1.029

question: Find the circular orbital velocity of a satellite at altitude 350 km above Earth (Earth radius 6371 km, mu = 3.986e14 m^3/s^2), in km/s.
A specimen under stress 200 MPa shows an elastic strain of 2.9e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 200, eps = 2.9 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 200 / (2.9e-3) MPa = 68.97 GPa | Answer: 68.97 GPa

question: A block of mass 5 kg has a volume of 4.5e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 5, V = 4.5 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 5 / (4.5e-3) | Answer: 1111 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 2400 mm is heated through 20 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 11e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 2400, dT = 20, al = 11 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 2400*11e-6*20 | Answer: 0.528 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 85 ohm, R2 = 35 ohm and R3 = 395 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 85, R2 = 35, R3 = 395 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 35*395 / 85 | Answer: 162.6 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 120 ohm and gauge factor 2.1 experiences a strain of 900e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 120, GF = 2.1, eps = 900 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 120*2.1*900e-6 | Answer: 226.8 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 9.18 when the true value is 10. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.18, true = 10 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.18 - 10| / 10 * 100 | Answer: 8.2 %

question: Annual demand is 6500 units, ordering cost 30 per order and holding cost 23 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 6500, S = 30, H = 23 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*6500*30 / 23) | Answer: 130.2 units

question: An asset costs 90000 with salvage value 26000 after 10 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 90000, Sv = 26000, n = 10 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (90000 - 26000) / 10 | Answer: 6400 per year

question: A product sells for 490 per unit with variable cost 40 per unit and fixed costs 115000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 490, V = 40, F = 115000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 115000 / (490 - 40) | Answer: 255.6 units

question: Find the present worth of 90000 received 3 years from now at an interest rate of 7% per year.
solution: Given: F = 90000, n = 3, i = 7 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 90000 / (1 + 0.07)^3 | Answer: 73467 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.99, 0.96 and 0.92 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.99, r2 = 0.96, r3 = 0.92 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.99*0.96*0.92 | Answer: 0.8744

question: A process produces 23 defective items in a batch of 15500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 23, N = 15500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 23/15500 * 1e6 | Answer: 1484 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = x^3 - 8x^2 - 7x - 2 evaluated at x = -2.
For f(x) = 4x^3 - 6x^2 - 8x - 5, find f''(x) at x = -4.
Evaluate the definite integral of (-3x^2 + 6x + 2) dx from x = -2 to x = 5.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = -3x^3/3 + 6x^2/2 + 2x | Evaluate F(5) - F(-2) | Answer: -56

question: Find the larger real root of 5x^2 - 2x - 7 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[-6, 8], [-8, 0]].
solution: Given: a = -6, b = 8, c = -8, d = 0 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (-6)(0) - (8)(-8) | Answer: 64

question: Find the determinant of [[-2, -1, -4], [4, -5, -1], [-2, 3, -5]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: -86

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[4, 3], [3, -1]].
solution: Trace tr = 3, Determinant = -13 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 5.405

question: Solve for x: 3x + -3y = -10 and 3x + -1y = -10.
solution: Determinant = 3*-1 - -3*3 = 6 | x = (e d - b f) / det = -3.333 | Answer: x = -3.333

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 52, 15, 3, 33, 14.
solution: Sum = 117 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 23.4 | Answer: 23.4

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 49, 32, 36, 46, 35.
solution: Mean = 39.6 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 7.436

question: Find the slope of the line through (5, -3) and (3, 2).
solution: Given: x1 = 5, y1 = -3, x2 = 3, y2 = 2 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (2 - -3) / (3 - 5) | Answer: -2.5

question: Find the distance between the points (8, 4) and (3, 5).
solution: Given: x1 = 8, y1 = 4, x2 = 3, y2 = 5 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-5)^2 + (1)^2) | Answer: 5.099 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (2,0), (2,-3), (-2,-5).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 6 sq units

question: Evaluate the number of combinations C(5, 4).
solution: Given: n = 5, r = 4 | Formula: C(n, r) = n! / (r! (n - r)!) | Substitute: C(5, 4) = 5! / (4! * 1!) | Answer: 5

question: Evaluate the number of permutations P(15, 2).
solution: Given: n = 15, r = 2 | Formula: P(n, r) = n! / (n - r)! | Substitute: P(15, 2) = 15! / 13! | Answer: 210

question: Find the 37th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 18 and common difference 4.
solution: Given: a = 18, d = 4, n = 37 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = 18 + (37 - 1)*4 | Answer: 162

question: Find the sum of the first 34 terms of an AP with first term -8 and common difference 3.
solution: Given: a = -8, d = 3, n = 34 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 34/2 [2*-8 + (34-1)*3] | Answer: 1411

question: Find the 4th term of a geometric progression with first term 1 and common ratio 3.
solution: Given: a = 1, r = 3, n = 4 | Formula: a_n = a r^(n-1) | Substitute: a_n = 1 * 3^(4-1) | Answer: 27

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 3000 at 14% per annum for 1 years.
solution: Given: P = 3000, R = 14, Tt = 1 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 3000 * 14 * 1 / 100 | Answer: 420 currency units

question: Find the amount when 6500 is invested at 8.9% per annum compounded annually for 2 years.
solution: Given: P = 6500, R = 8.9, Tt = 2 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 6500 * (1 + 8.9/100)^2 | Answer: 7708 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (7, 8, 3) and (-8, 8, 1).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (4, 1, 3) and (4, 6, -1).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 31.89

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (2, -2, -1) and (1, 5, -5).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 98.05 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number -8 + -4i.
solution: Given: a = -8, b = -4 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((-8)^2 + (-4)^2) | Answer: 8.944

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number 12 + -12i.
solution: Given: a = 12, b = -12 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(-12, 12) | Answer: -45 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -2x^3 - 5x^2 + x - 6 at x = 3.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-149 with initial guess x0=4, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.8 and ordinates 20, 7, 1, 6, 6, estimate the integral.

solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 80 and 246 | Answer: GCD = 2

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 49 and 34.
solution: Given: a = 49, b = 34 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 49*34 / 1 | Answer: 1666

question: A circular rod of diameter 34 mm carries an axial tensile load of 31 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 14 mm and length 2300 mm carries an axial load of 54 kN. Take E = 200 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 41 mm transmits a torque of 300 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 41, Tt = 300 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(300*1000) / (pi*(41)^3) | Answer: 22.17 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 34 mm and length 1700 mm carries a torque of 1450 N-m. With G = 77 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (34)^4 / 32 = 131194 mm^4 | theta = (1450*1000)(1700) / (77000 * 131194) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 13.98 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 109 mm wide and 290 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 109, h = 290 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 109*(290)^2 / 6 | Answer: 1527817 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (62 mm x 210 mm) carries a bending moment of 6 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (66 mm x 100 mm) has effective length 3600 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 380 MPa is designed for a working stress of 140 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 380, sw = 140 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 380 / 140 | Answer: 2.714

question: A steel bar is fully restrained and heated through 120 deg C. With E = 210 GPa and alpha = 12e-6 /deg C, find the thermal stress in MPa.
solution: Given: dT = 120, E = 210, al = 12 | Formula: sigma = E alpha (dT) | Substitute: sigma = 210000 * 12e-6 * 120 | Answer: 302.4 MPa

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 800 mm and wall thickness 14 mm carries an internal pressure of 2.9 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 800, t = 14, P = 2.9 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 2.9*800 / (2*14) | Answer: 82.86 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 660 K and 440 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 660, Tc = 440 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 440/660) * 100 | Answer: 33.33 %

question: A refrigerator works between 265 K (cold) and 328 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 265, Th = 328 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 265 / (328 - 265) | Answer: 4.206

question: A heat pump operates between 265 K and 306 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 265, Th = 306 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 306 / (306 - 265) | Answer: 7.463

question: 6.3 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 45 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 6.3, dT = 45 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 6.3 * 0.718 * 45 | Answer: 203.6 kJ

question: 5.4 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 25 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 5.4, dT = 25 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 5.4 * 1.005 * 25 | Answer: 135.7 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 2.2 m^3 at 330 K with mass 3.8 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 2.2, Tk = 330, m = 3.8 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 3.8*0.287*330 / 2.2 | Answer: 163.6 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 2.5 kg of air expands isothermally at 300 K from volume V1 to 5*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.5, Tk = 300, ratio = 5 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 2.5*0.287*300*ln(5) | Answer: 346.4 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 3 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.29 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 3, D = 0.29 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*3*0.29 / 0.001 | Answer: 870000

question: Water flows at 3.5 m/s through a pipe of diameter 90 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 20 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 20 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*20 / 1000 | Answer: 196.2 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 15.5 m. Taking Cv = 0.98, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 15.5, cv = 0.98 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.98*sqrt(2*9.81*15.5) | Answer: 17.09 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 320 mm) water flows at 2.5 m/s. It contracts to diameter 110 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
Water flows at 1.6 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.31 m and length 350 m. With friction factor f = 0.022, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 22 teeth drives a gear of 80 teeth. If the pinion runs at 750 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 22, z2 = 80, N1 = 750 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 750*22 / 80 | Answer: 206.2 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 350 mm rotates at 600 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 350, N = 600 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.35)*600 / 60 | Answer: 11 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 13.6 kW at 450 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 13.6, N = 450 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(13.6*1000) / (2*pi*450) | Answer: 288.6 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 4.5 kg rotates at radius 0.19 m at 400 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 17100 N/m and mass 12.8 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 17100, m = 12.8 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(17100/12.8) | Answer: 5.817 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 5.5 m^2 and thickness 0.29 m has conductivity k = 4.6 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 165 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 5.5, L = 0.29, k = 4.6, dT = 165 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 4.6*5.5*165 / 0.29 | Answer: 14395 W

question: A surface of area 3.8 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 10 W/m^2-K to surroundings 125 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 3.8, h = 10, dT = 125 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 10*3.8*125 | Answer: 4750 W

question: In a counter-flow heat exchanger the terminal temperature differences are 60 deg C and 20 deg C. Find the log mean temperature difference (LMTD) in deg C.
solution: Given: dT1 = 60, dT2 = 20 | Formula: LMTD = (dT1 - dT2) / ln(dT1/dT2) | Substitute: LMTD = (60 - 20) / ln(60/20) | Answer: 36.41 deg C

question: In turning, cutting speed = 70 m/min, feed = 0.32 mm/rev, depth of cut = 3 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 70, f = 0.32, d = 3 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*70*0.32*3 | Answer: 67200 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 230 mm is turned at 550 rpm with a feed of 0.11 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 230, N = 550, f = 0.11 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 230 / (0.11*550) | Answer: 3.802 min

question: A resistor of 86 ohm carries a current of 3.3 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 86, I = 3.3 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 3.3 * 86 | Answer: 283.8 V

question: Three resistors 63 ohm, 59 ohm and 22 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 63, R2 = 59, R3 = 22 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 63 + 59 + 22 | Answer: 144 ohm

question: Two resistors 41 ohm and 93 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 41, R2 = 93 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 41*93 / (41+93) | Answer: 28.46 ohm

question: A device draws 1 A at 40 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 40, I = 1 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 40 * 1 | Answer: 40 W

question: A current of 5.6 A flows through a 15 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 5.6, R = 15 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (5.6)^2 * 15 | Answer: 470.4 W

question: Two capacitors 26.7 uF and 11.8 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 26.7, C2 = 11.8 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 26.7*11.8 / (26.7+11.8) | Answer: 8.183 uF

question: A resistor 29 kohm and capacitor 7.1 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 29, C = 7.1 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (29k)(7.1u) = 205.9 ms | Answer: 205.9 ms

question: An inductor 302.3 mH is in series with 59 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 302.3, R = 59 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (302.3e-3) / 59 | Answer: 5.124 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 181.2 mH inductor at 930 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 181.2, f = 930 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (930)(181.2e-3) | Answer: 1059 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 20.9 uF capacitor at 280 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 20.9, f = 280 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (280)(20.9e-6)) | Answer: 27.2 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 19 ohm, XL = 98 ohm and XC = 130 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 19, XL = 98, XC = 130 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(19^2 + (98 - 130)^2) | Answer: 37.22 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 76.9 mH and C = 7.8 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 76.9, C = 7.8 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(76.9e-3 * 7.8e-6)) | Answer: 205.5 Hz

question: A capacitor of 21.1 uF is charged to 325 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 21.1, V = 325 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*21.1e-6*(325)^2 | Answer: 1114 mJ

question: An alternating voltage has a peak value of 198 V. Find its RMS value.
solution: Given: Vp = 198 | Formula: Vrms = Vp / sqrt(2) | Substitute: Vrms = 198 / sqrt(2) | Answer: 140 V

question: A transformer has primary voltage 200 V with 310 primary turns and 260 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 200, N1 = 310, N2 = 260 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 200 * 260/310 | Answer: 167.7 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 120 V and draws an armature current of 22 A. If the armature resistance is 0.52 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 120, Ia = 22, Ra = 0.52 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 120 - 22*0.52 | Answer: 108.6 V

question: A 4-pole induction motor on a 50 Hz supply runs at 920 rpm. Find the slip (%).
formula: s = (Ns - N) / Ns,  Ns = 120 f / P

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 105 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.79. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 105, VL = 400, pf = 0.79 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*400*105*0.79 / 1000 | Answer: 57.47 kW

question: A load has real power 25 kW and apparent power 135 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 25, S = 135 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 25 / 135 | Answer: 0.1852

question: A machine delivers 85 kW output while drawing 87 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 85, Pi = 87 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 85/87 * 100 | Answer: 97.7 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 5 V across R1 = 47 ohm and R2 = 12 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 5, R1 = 47, R2 = 12 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 5*12 / (47+12) | Answer: 1.017 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 180 kohm and Rin = 8 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 180, Rin = 8 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 180 / 8 | Answer: 22.5

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 140 kohm and Rg = 29 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 140, Rg = 29 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 140/29 | Answer: 5.828

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 5033. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 5033 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(5033) | Answer: 37.02 dB

question: A first-order system has a time constant of 2.2 s. Find the time (in s) to reach 63.2% of its final value.
solution: For a first-order step response, y = 1 - e^(-t/tau) | y = 0.632 when t = tau | Answer: 2.2 s
formula: At t = tau the response reaches 63.2% (one time constant)

question: A signal is sampled at 108 kHz. According to the Nyquist criterion, what is the maximum signal frequency that can be represented (in kHz)?
solution: Given: fs = 108 | Formula: f_max = fs / 2 | Substitute: f_max = 108 / 2 | Answer: 54 kHz

question: A simply supported beam of span 3.7 m carries a central point load of 55 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.7, W = 55 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 55*3.7 / 4 | Answer: 50.88 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 5.6 m carries a UDL of 25 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.6, w = 25 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 25*(5.6)^2 / 8 | Answer: 98 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 5.9 m carries a point load 30 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.9, W = 30 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 30*5.9 | Answer: 177 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 1.5 m carries a UDL of 16 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 1.5, w = 16 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 16*(1.5)^2 / 2 | Answer: 18 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 5.7 m carries a point load 100 kN at distance 1.1 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 5.7, a = 1.1, W = 100 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 100*(5.7 - 1.1) / 5.7 | Answer: 80.7 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 4.7 m) carries a central point load 60 kN. With E = 200 GPa and I = 150e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=60000 N, L=4700.0 mm, E=200000 MPa, I=150e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 4.326 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 8.1 m carries a UDL of 27 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 8.1, w = 27 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 27*(8.1)^2 / 12 | Answer: 147.6 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 510 mm, clear cover 25 mm and main bars of diameter 12 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 510, c = 25, dia = 12 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 510 - 25 - 12/2 | Answer: 479 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 12.4 m^2 carrying a factored load of 18.9 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 12.4, w = 18.9 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 18.9 * 12.4 | Answer: 234.4 kN

question: For a bar of diameter 25 mm with design bond stress 2 MPa and steel stress 360 MPa, find the development length in mm.
solution: Given: dia = 25, tbd = 2, fs = 360 | Formula: Ld = phi fs / (4 tau_bd) | Substitute: Ld = 25*360 / (4*2) | Answer: 1125 mm

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 5.2 m, unit weight 19 kN/m^3, phi = 31 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 6.8 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 20 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 6.8, g = 20 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (20 - 9.81)*6.8 | Answer: 69.29 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 1.3e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.3, area = 7.1e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 1.3, i = 0.3, A = 7.1 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (1.3e-4)*0.3*(7.1e-3) | Answer: 276.9 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 2.2 m, bed slope 0.003 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.029. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 2.3 m under a head of 0.4 m. Taking Cd = 0.61 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 4.6 m wide carries a discharge of 17.6 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 580 m and design speed 85 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 580, V = 85 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (85)^2 / (127*580) | Answer: 0.09809
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: For a design speed of 80 km/h with allowable superelevation 0.05 and lateral friction 0.16, find the minimum curve radius in m.
A tank of volume 250 m^3 treats a flow of 100 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 250, Q = 100 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 250 / 100 | Answer: 2.5 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 160 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.14 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 4 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 160, k = 0.14, t = 4 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 160*(1 - e^(-0.14*4)) | Answer: 68.61 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.88, rainfall intensity 90 mm/h over a catchment of 15 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.88, i = 90, A = 15 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.88*90*15 / 360 | Answer: 3.3 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.06 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 390 m with this tape.
