question: A shaft of diameter 61 mm and length 900 mm carries a torque of 1550 N-m. With G = 80 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (61)^4 / 32 = 1359312 mm^4 | theta = (1550*1000)(900) / (80000 * 1359312) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 0.735 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 75 mm wide and 300 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 75, h = 300 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 75*(300)^2 / 6 | Answer: 1125000 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (92 mm x 160 mm) carries a bending moment of 14 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (33 mm x 160 mm) has effective length 2600 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 510 MPa is designed for a working stress of 210 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 510, sw = 210 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 510 / 210 | Answer: 2.429

question: A steel bar is fully restrained and heated through 40 deg C. With E = 200 GPa and alpha = 12e-6 /deg C, find the thermal stress in MPa.
solution: Given: dT = 40, E = 200, al = 12 | Formula: sigma = E alpha (dT) | Substitute: sigma = 200000 * 12e-6 * 40 | Answer: 96 MPa

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 850 mm and wall thickness 7 mm carries an internal pressure of 0.7 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 850, t = 7, P = 0.7 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 0.7*850 / (2*7) | Answer: 42.5 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 1120 K and 430 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 1120, Tc = 430 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 430/1120) * 100 | Answer: 61.61 %

question: A refrigerator works between 265 K (cold) and 320 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 265, Th = 320 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 265 / (320 - 265) | Answer: 4.818

question: A heat pump operates between 266 K and 310 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 266, Th = 310 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 310 / (310 - 266) | Answer: 7.045

question: 7.3 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 90 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 7.3, dT = 90 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 7.3 * 0.718 * 90 | Answer: 471.7 kJ

question: 5.6 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 130 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 5.6, dT = 130 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 5.6 * 1.005 * 130 | Answer: 731.6 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 3.9 m^3 at 550 K with mass 4.3 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 3.9, Tk = 550, m = 4.3 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 4.3*0.287*550 / 3.9 | Answer: 174 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 4.8 kg of air expands isothermally at 440 K from volume V1 to 5*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.8, Tk = 440, ratio = 5 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 4.8*0.287*440*ln(5) | Answer: 975.6 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 2 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.23 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 2, D = 0.23 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*2*0.23 / 0.001 | Answer: 460000

question: Water flows at 1.6 m/s through a pipe of diameter 300 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 29.1 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 29.1 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*29.1 / 1000 | Answer: 285.5 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 6.6 m. Taking Cv = 0.97, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 6.6, cv = 0.97 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.97*sqrt(2*9.81*6.6) | Answer: 11.04 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 350 mm) water flows at 2.4 m/s. It contracts to diameter 110 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 350, d2 = 110, V1 = 2.4 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 2.4*(350/110)^2 | Answer: 24.3 m/s

question: Water flows at 1.3 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.39 m and length 340 m. With friction factor f = 0.035, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 36 teeth drives a gear of 62 teeth. If the pinion runs at 600 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 36, z2 = 62, N1 = 600 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 600*36 / 62 | Answer: 348.4 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 490 mm rotates at 700 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 490, N = 700 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.49)*700 / 60 | Answer: 17.96 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 5.3 kW at 700 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 5.3, N = 700 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(5.3*1000) / (2*pi*700) | Answer: 72.3 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 5.3 kg rotates at radius 0.56 m at 650 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 6400 N/m and mass 10.5 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 6400, m = 10.5 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(6400/10.5) | Answer: 3.929 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 3.6 m^2 and thickness 0.19 m has conductivity k = 10.8 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 125 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 3.6, L = 0.19, k = 10.8, dT = 125 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 10.8*3.6*125 / 0.19 | Answer: 25579 W

question: A surface of area 4.5 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 175 W/m^2-K to surroundings 70 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 4.5, h = 175, dT = 70 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 175*4.5*70 | Answer: 55125 W

question: In a counter-flow heat exchanger the terminal temperature differences are 115 deg C and 30 deg C. Find the log mean temperature difference (LMTD) in deg C.
solution: Given: dT1 = 115, dT2 = 30 | Formula: LMTD = (dT1 - dT2) / ln(dT1/dT2) | Substitute: LMTD = (115 - 30) / ln(115/30) | Answer: 63.26 deg C

question: In turning, cutting speed = 100 m/min, feed = 0.42 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2.1 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 100, f = 0.42, d = 2.1 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*100*0.42*2.1 | Answer: 88200 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 90 mm is turned at 850 rpm with a feed of 0.32 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 90, N = 850, f = 0.32 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 90 / (0.32*850) | Answer: 0.3309 min

question: A resistor of 16 ohm carries a current of 4.9 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 16, I = 4.9 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 4.9 * 16 | Answer: 78.4 V

question: Three resistors 88 ohm, 83 ohm and 15 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 88, R2 = 83, R3 = 15 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 88 + 83 + 15 | Answer: 186 ohm

question: Two resistors 28 ohm and 18 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 28, R2 = 18 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 28*18 / (28+18) | Answer: 10.96 ohm

question: A device draws 2.2 A at 125 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 125, I = 2.2 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 125 * 2.2 | Answer: 275 W

question: A current of 4.6 A flows through a 89 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 4.6, R = 89 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (4.6)^2 * 89 | Answer: 1883 W

question: Two capacitors 43.1 uF and 33.3 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 43.1, C2 = 33.3 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 43.1*33.3 / (43.1+33.3) | Answer: 18.79 uF

question: A resistor 16 kohm and capacitor 9.6 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 16, C = 9.6 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (16k)(9.6u) = 153.6 ms | Answer: 153.6 ms

question: An inductor 435.8 mH is in series with 134 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 435.8, R = 134 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (435.8e-3) / 134 | Answer: 3.252 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 172.1 mH inductor at 270 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 172.1, f = 270 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (270)(172.1e-3) | Answer: 292 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 4.1 uF capacitor at 770 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 4.1, f = 770 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (770)(4.1e-6)) | Answer: 50.41 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 19 ohm, XL = 117 ohm and XC = 92 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 19, XL = 117, XC = 92 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(19^2 + (117 - 92)^2) | Answer: 31.4 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 19.6 mH and C = 5.7 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 19.6, C = 5.7 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(19.6e-3 * 5.7e-6)) | Answer: 476.2 Hz

question: A capacitor of 57.2 uF is charged to 185 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 57.2, V = 185 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*57.2e-6*(185)^2 | Answer: 978.8 mJ

question: An alternating voltage has a peak value of 96 V. Find its RMS value.
solution: Given: Vp = 96 | Formula: Vrms = Vp / sqrt(2) | Substitute: Vrms = 96 / sqrt(2) | Answer: 67.88 V

question: A transformer has primary voltage 180 V with 230 primary turns and 100 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 180, N1 = 230, N2 = 100 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 180 * 100/230 | Answer: 78.26 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 130 V and draws an armature current of 28 A. If the armature resistance is 0.58 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 130, Ia = 28, Ra = 0.58 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 130 - 28*0.58 | Answer: 113.8 V

question: A 6-pole induction motor on a 60 Hz supply runs at 1080 rpm. Find the slip (%).
formula: s = (Ns - N) / Ns,  Ns = 120 f / P

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 105 A at 415 V (line) with a power factor of 0.73. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 105, VL = 415, pf = 0.73 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*415*105*0.73 / 1000 | Answer: 55.1 kW

question: A load has real power 110 kW and apparent power 165 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 110, S = 165 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 110 / 165 | Answer: 0.6667

question: A machine delivers 15 kW output while drawing 67 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 15, Pi = 67 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 15/67 * 100 | Answer: 22.39 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 29 V across R1 = 41 ohm and R2 = 17 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 29, R1 = 41, R2 = 17 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 29*17 / (41+17) | Answer: 8.5 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 150 kohm and Rin = 23 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 150, Rin = 23 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 150 / 23 | Answer: 6.522

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 90 kohm and Rg = 27 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 90, Rg = 27 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 90/27 | Answer: 4.333

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 308. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 308 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(308) | Answer: 24.89 dB

question: A first-order system has a time constant of 8.1 s. Find the time (in s) to reach 63.2% of its final value.
solution: For a first-order step response, y = 1 - e^(-t/tau) | y = 0.632 when t = tau | Answer: 8.1 s
formula: At t = tau the response reaches 63.2% (one time constant)

question: A signal is sampled at 90 kHz. According to the Nyquist criterion, what is the maximum signal frequency that can be represented (in kHz)?
solution: Given: fs = 90 | Formula: f_max = fs / 2 | Substitute: f_max = 90 / 2 | Answer: 45 kHz

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.8 m carries a central point load of 10 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.8, W = 10 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 10*4.8 / 4 | Answer: 12 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 7.7 m carries a UDL of 60 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7.7, w = 60 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 60*(7.7)^2 / 8 | Answer: 444.7 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 4 m carries a point load 60 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4, W = 60 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 60*4 | Answer: 240 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 1.1 m carries a UDL of 20 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 1.1, w = 20 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 20*(1.1)^2 / 2 | Answer: 12.1 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.8 m carries a point load 95 kN at distance 1.3 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 9.8, a = 1.3, W = 95 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 95*(9.8 - 1.3) / 9.8 | Answer: 82.4 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 7.7 m) carries a central point load 25 kN. With E = 30 GPa and I = 310e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=25000 N, L=7700.0 mm, E=30000 MPa, I=310e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 25.57 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 5.1 m carries a UDL of 42 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.1, w = 42 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 42*(5.1)^2 / 12 | Answer: 91.03 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 470 mm, clear cover 50 mm and main bars of diameter 16 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 470, c = 50, dia = 16 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 470 - 50 - 16/2 | Answer: 412 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 38.1 m^2 carrying a factored load of 15.6 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 38.1, w = 15.6 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 15.6 * 38.1 | Answer: 594.4 kN

question: For a bar of diameter 16 mm with design bond stress 1.6 MPa and steel stress 435 MPa, find the development length in mm.
solution: Given: dia = 16, tbd = 1.6, fs = 435 | Formula: Ld = phi fs / (4 tau_bd) | Substitute: Ld = 16*435 / (4*1.6) | Answer: 1088 mm

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 4.2 m, unit weight 19 kN/m^3, phi = 33 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 3.5 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 20 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 3.5, g = 20 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (20 - 9.81)*3.5 | Answer: 35.66 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 2.9e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.8, area = 7e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 2.9, i = 0.8, A = 7 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (2.9e-4)*0.8*(7e-3) | Answer: 1624 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1 m, bed slope 0.006 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.02. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 1.4 m under a head of 1 m. Taking Cd = 0.6 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
solution: Given: L = 1.4, H = 1, cd = 0.6 | Formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2) | Substitute: Q = (2/3)*0.6*sqrt(2*9.81)*1.4*(1)^1.5 | Answer: 2.48 m^3/s
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 2.2 m wide carries a discharge of 26.9 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 320 m and design speed 65 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 320, V = 65 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (65)^2 / (127*320) | Answer: 0.104
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: For a design speed of 50 km/h with allowable superelevation 0.05 and lateral friction 0.14, find the minimum curve radius in m.
A tank of volume 420 m^3 treats a flow of 140 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 420, Q = 140 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 420 / 140 | Answer: 3 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 270 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.23 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 5 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 270, k = 0.23, t = 5 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 270*(1 - e^(-0.23*5)) | Answer: 184.5 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.83, rainfall intensity 75 mm/h over a catchment of 29 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.83, i = 75, A = 29 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.83*75*29 / 360 | Answer: 5.015 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.04 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 290 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.04, M = 290 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 290*(30+0.04)/30 | Answer: 290.4 m

question: Convert the decimal number 49 to binary.
solution: Divide 49 by 2 repeatedly, recording remainders | Reading remainders in reverse gives 110001 | Answer: 110001 (binary)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 2 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the decimal number 2654 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 2654 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: A5E (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the 8-bit binary number 00001110 to decimal.
solution: Binary 00001110 = sum of bit-weights | Answer: 14 (decimal)
formula: Sum each bit times its positional weight (2^i)

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 00100010 and 11011111.
solution: XOR: 11111101 | Count of 1s = 7 | Answer: 7
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 120 megabits is sent over a link of 85 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 120, B = 85 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 120 / 85 | Answer: 1.412 s

question: A link has bandwidth 66 Mbps and round-trip time 110 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 66, R = 110 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 66e6 * 110e-3 bits = 7260 kb | Answer: 7260 kilobits

question: A channel has bandwidth 20 kHz. Using Nyquist's theorem with 4 signal levels, find the maximum data rate in kbps (noiseless).
solution: Given: B = 20, M = 4 | Formula: C = 2 B log2(M) | Substitute: C = 2*20*log2(4) | Answer: 80 kbps

question: A channel of bandwidth 15 kHz has a signal-to-noise ratio of 7 (linear). Using Shannon's theorem, find the channel capacity in kbps.
solution: Given: B = 15, SNR = 7 | Formula: C = B log2(1 + SNR) | Substitute: C = 15*log2(1 + 7) | Answer: 45 kbps

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.89, cache access time 7 ns and main-memory access time 180 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.89, tc = 7, tm = 180 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.89*7 + (1 - 0.89)*180 | Answer: 26.03 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 336379 elements?
solution: Given: n = 336379 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(336379)) + 1 | Answer: 19

question: An O(n^2) algorithm performs c*n^2 basic operations. If c = 1 and n = 1080, how many operations are performed?
solution: Given: n = 1080 | Formula: operations = n^2 | Substitute: = (1080)^2 | Answer: 1166400

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.015, memory access time 140 ns and page-fault service time 9 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 9 ms = 9000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.015)*140 + 0.015*9000000.0 ns | Answer: 135.1 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: A modem transmits at 3300 baud using 16-level signalling. Find the bit rate in bps.
solution: Given: baud = 3300, M = 16 | Formula: bit rate = baud * log2(M) | Substitute: bit rate = 3300 * log2(16) | Answer: 13200 bps

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 1.1 m^3 at 420 kPa and 420 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 1.1, P = 420, Tk = 420 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (420e3)*1.1 / (8.314*420) | Answer: 132.3 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.21 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 15 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.21, t = 15 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.21*15) | Answer: 0.9571

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.11 /min) is to reach 60% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.11, X = 60 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.6) / 0.11 | Answer: 8.33 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.46 /min) reaches 50% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.46, X = 50 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.5 / (0.46*(1 - 0.5)) | Answer: 2.174 min

question: A first-order reaction has a rate constant of 0.33 /min. Find its half-life in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.33 | Formula: t_half = ln(2) / k | Substitute: t_half = 0.6931 / 0.33 | Answer: 2.1 min

question: For a reaction with A = 3e10 /s and activation energy 80 kJ/mol at 460 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 3, Ea = 80, Tk = 460 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 3e10 * exp(-80e3 / (8.314*460)) | Answer: 24.69 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.93 and bottoms xW = 0.06, with relative volatility alpha = 2.8. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.93, xw = 0.06, al = 2.8 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.93/0.07)(0.94/0.06)] / ln(2.8) | Answer: 5.185 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.61 and x = 0.28. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.61, x = 0.28 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.61/0.39) / (0.28/0.72) | Answer: 4.022

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.11 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 25 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.11, Psat = 25 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.11 * 25 | Answer: 2.75 kPa

question: A stream of 5.1 kg/s with specific heat 3 kJ/kg-K is heated through 10 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 5.1, cp = 3, dT = 10 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 5.1*3*10 | Answer: 153 kW

question: A reactor of volume 14.8 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 1.4 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 14.8, Q = 1.4 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 14.8 / 1.4 | Answer: 10.57 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 6.4e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 4 mm with a concentration difference of 50 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 6.4, L = 4, dC = 50 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (6.4e-9)*50 / (4e-3) | Answer: 80 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 4.8 min and steady-state gain 2.5. For a step input of magnitude 9, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 4.8, K = 2.5, M = 9 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 2.5 * 9 | Answer: 22.5 units

question: A reactor operates at a space time of 9.8 min. Find its space velocity in per hour.
solution: Given: tau = 9.8 | Formula: SV = 60 / tau  (per hour) | Substitute: SV = 60 / 9.8 | Answer: 6.122 /h

question: An aircraft wing of area 75 m^2 flies at 260 m/s (air density 1.225 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 1.3. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 75, V = 260, rho = 1.225, CL = 1.3 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1.225*(260)^2*75*1.3 / 1000 | Answer: 4037 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 40 m^2 flies at 140 m/s (density 0.7 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.04. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 40, V = 140, rho = 0.7, CD = 0.04 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.7*(140)^2*40*0.04 / 1000 | Answer: 10.98 kN

question: Find the dynamic pressure for air of density 0.7 kg/m^3 moving at 160 m/s, in Pa.
solution: Given: rho = 0.7, V = 160 | Formula: q = 0.5 rho V^2 | Substitute: q = 0.5*0.7*(160)^2 | Answer: 8960 Pa

question: An aircraft flies at 220 m/s where the speed of sound is 340 m/s. Find the Mach number.
solution: Given: V = 220, a = 340 | Formula: M = V / a | Substitute: M = 220 / 340 | Answer: 0.6471

question: A specimen under stress 250 MPa shows an elastic strain of 2.6e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 250, eps = 2.6 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 250 / (2.6e-3) MPa = 96.15 GPa | Answer: 96.15 GPa

question: A block of mass 11 kg has a volume of 4.3e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 11, V = 4.3 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 11 / (4.3e-3) | Answer: 2558 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 2600 mm is heated through 35 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 17e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 2600, dT = 35, al = 17 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 2600*17e-6*35 | Answer: 1.547 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 120 ohm, R2 = 165 ohm and R3 = 20 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 120, R2 = 165, R3 = 20 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 165*20 / 120 | Answer: 27.5 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 1000 ohm and gauge factor 2.2 experiences a strain of 500e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 1000, GF = 2.2, eps = 500 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 1000*2.2*500e-6 | Answer: 1100 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 9.86 when the true value is 20. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.86, true = 20 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.86 - 20| / 20 * 100 | Answer: 50.7 %

question: Annual demand is 4500 units, ordering cost 190 per order and holding cost 3 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 4500, S = 190, H = 3 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*4500*190 / 3) | Answer: 755 units

question: An asset costs 240000 with salvage value 28000 after 12 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 240000, Sv = 28000, n = 12 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (240000 - 28000) / 12 | Answer: 17667 per year

question: A product sells for 460 per unit with variable cost 140 per unit and fixed costs 75000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 460, V = 140, F = 75000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 75000 / (460 - 140) | Answer: 234.4 units

question: Find the present worth of 25000 received 4 years from now at an interest rate of 10% per year.
solution: Given: F = 25000, n = 4, i = 10 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 25000 / (1 + 0.1)^4 | Answer: 17075 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.97, 0.94 and 0.98 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.97, r2 = 0.94, r3 = 0.98 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.97*0.94*0.98 | Answer: 0.8936

question: A process produces 27 defective items in a batch of 7500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 27, N = 7500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 27/7500 * 1e6 | Answer: 3600 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = 3x^3 + 6x^2 - 7x - 1 evaluated at x = 1.

question: Find the larger real root of 5x^2 + 3x - 12 = 0.

question: Find the determinant of [[-2, -1, -1], [-5, 1, -3], [5, 1, 2]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: 5

question: Find the slope of the line through (9, 7) and (-6, 9).
solution: Given: x1 = 9, y1 = 7, x2 = -6, y2 = 9 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (9 - 7) / (-6 - 9) | Answer: -0.1333

question: Find the distance between the points (-8, -5) and (8, -6).
solution: Given: x1 = -8, y1 = -5, x2 = 8, y2 = -6 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((16)^2 + (-1)^2) | Answer: 16.03 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (-4,4), (5,1), (7,-5).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 24 sq units

question: Evaluate the number of combinations C(17, 14).
solution: Given: n = 17, r = 14 | Formula: C(n, r) = n! / (r! (n - r)!) | Substitute: C(17, 14) = 17! / (14! * 3!) | Answer: 680

question: Evaluate the number of permutations P(10, 1).
solution: Given: n = 10, r = 1 | Formula: P(n, r) = n! / (n - r)! | Substitute: P(10, 1) = 10! / 9! | Answer: 10

question: Find the 10th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 15 and common difference -9.
solution: Given: a = 15, d = -9, n = 10 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = 15 + (10 - 1)*-9 | Answer: -66

question: Find the sum of the first 34 terms of an AP with first term -15 and common difference 3.
solution: Given: a = -15, d = 3, n = 34 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 34/2 [2*-15 + (34-1)*3] | Answer: 1173

question: Find the 5th term of a geometric progression with first term 1 and common ratio 4.
solution: Given: a = 1, r = 4, n = 5 | Formula: a_n = a r^(n-1) | Substitute: a_n = 1 * 4^(5-1) | Answer: 256

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 17500 at 4% per annum for 10 years.
solution: Given: P = 17500, R = 4, Tt = 10 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 17500 * 4 * 10 / 100 | Answer: 7000 currency units

question: Find the amount when 37000 is invested at 10.6% per annum compounded annually for 2 years.
solution: Given: P = 37000, R = 10.6, Tt = 2 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 37000 * (1 + 10.6/100)^2 | Answer: 4526 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (6, -2, 8) and (-2, -5, 5).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 31.03

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (5, 4, 4) and (-4, -3, 5).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 103 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number -7 + 0i.
solution: Given: a = -7, b = 0 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((-7)^2 + (0)^2) | Answer: 7

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number 6 + -5i.
solution: Given: a = 6, b = -5 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(-5, 6) | Answer: -39.81 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -2x^3 + x^2 - 8x + 8 at x = -5.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-174 with initial guess x0=14, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=0.6 and ordinates 11, 14, 2, 15, 5, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 566 and 112.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 566 and 112 | Answer: GCD = 2

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 57 and 56.
solution: Given: a = 57, b = 56 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 57*56 / 1 | Answer: 3192
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 52 mm carries an axial tensile load of 53 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 14 mm and length 800 mm carries an axial load of 23 kN. Take E = 200 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 79 mm transmits a torque of 2600 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 79, Tt = 2600 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(2600*1000) / (pi*(79)^3) | Answer: 26.86 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 26 mm and length 1600 mm carries a torque of 1050 N-m. With G = 80 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (26)^4 / 32 = 44864 mm^4 | theta = (1050*1000)(1600) / (80000 * 44864) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 26.82 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 109 mm wide and 250 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 109, h = 250 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 109*(250)^2 / 6 | Answer: 1135417 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (53 mm x 230 mm) carries a bending moment of 34 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (44 mm x 100 mm) has effective length 3700 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 590 MPa is designed for a working stress of 70 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 590, sw = 70 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 590 / 70 | Answer: 8.429

question: A steel bar is fully restrained and heated through 95 deg C. With E = 200 GPa and alpha = 12e-6 /deg C, find the thermal stress in MPa.
solution: Given: dT = 95, E = 200, al = 12 | Formula: sigma = E alpha (dT) | Substitute: sigma = 200000 * 12e-6 * 95 | Answer: 228 MPa

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 850 mm and wall thickness 12 mm carries an internal pressure of 2.5 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 850, t = 12, P = 2.5 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 2.5*850 / (2*12) | Answer: 88.54 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 1020 K and 320 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 1020, Tc = 320 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 320/1020) * 100 | Answer: 68.63 %

question: A refrigerator works between 269 K (cold) and 316 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 269, Th = 316 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 269 / (316 - 269) | Answer: 5.723

question: A heat pump operates between 275 K and 310 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 275, Th = 310 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 310 / (310 - 275) | Answer: 8.857

question: 7.3 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 70 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 7.3, dT = 70 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 7.3 * 0.718 * 70 | Answer: 366.9 kJ

question: 3 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 20 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3, dT = 20 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 3 * 1.005 * 20 | Answer: 60.3 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 3.9 m^3 at 480 K with mass 2.6 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 3.9, Tk = 480, m = 2.6 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 2.6*0.287*480 / 3.9 | Answer: 91.84 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 4.3 kg of air expands isothermally at 310 K from volume V1 to 4*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.3, Tk = 310, ratio = 4 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 4.3*0.287*310*ln(4) | Answer: 530.4 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 2.4 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.31 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 2.4, D = 0.31 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*2.4*0.31 / 0.001 | Answer: 744000

question: Water flows at 2.4 m/s through a pipe of diameter 190 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 4.9 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 4.9 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*4.9 / 1000 | Answer: 48.07 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 18.5 m. Taking Cv = 0.97, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 18.5, cv = 0.97 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.97*sqrt(2*9.81*18.5) | Answer: 18.48 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 250 mm) water flows at 2.1 m/s. It contracts to diameter 130 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
Water flows at 3.8 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.28 m and length 230 m. With friction factor f = 0.02, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 32 teeth drives a gear of 114 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1400 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 32, z2 = 114, N1 = 1400 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1400*32 / 114 | Answer: 393 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 320 mm rotates at 1200 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 320, N = 1200 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.32)*1200 / 60 | Answer: 20.11 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 45.8 kW at 1250 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 45.8, N = 1250 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(45.8*1000) / (2*pi*1250) | Answer: 349.9 N-m

question: A mass of 1.5 kg rotates at radius 0.13 m at 550 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 1500 N/m and mass 12.5 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 1500, m = 12.5 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(1500/12.5) | Answer: 1.743 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 7.2 m^2 and thickness 0.4 m has conductivity k = 9.3 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 125 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 7.2, L = 0.4, k = 9.3, dT = 125 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 9.3*7.2*125 / 0.4 | Answer: 20925 W

question: A surface of area 2.7 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 65 W/m^2-K to surroundings 135 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 2.7, h = 65, dT = 135 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 65*2.7*135 | Answer: 23692 W

question: In a counter-flow heat exchanger the terminal temperature differences are 100 deg C and 25 deg C. Find the log mean temperature difference (LMTD) in deg C.
solution: Given: dT1 = 100, dT2 = 25 | Formula: LMTD = (dT1 - dT2) / ln(dT1/dT2) | Substitute: LMTD = (100 - 25) / ln(100/25) | Answer: 54.1 deg C

question: In turning, cutting speed = 80 m/min, feed = 0.5 mm/rev, depth of cut = 1 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 80, f = 0.5, d = 1 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*80*0.5*1 | Answer: 40000 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 220 mm is turned at 1000 rpm with a feed of 0.31 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 220, N = 1000, f = 0.31 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 220 / (0.31*1000) | Answer: 0.7097 min

question: A resistor of 53 ohm carries a current of 8.3 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 53, I = 8.3 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 8.3 * 53 | Answer: 439.9 V

question: Three resistors 21 ohm, 25 ohm and 81 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 21, R2 = 25, R3 = 81 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 21 + 25 + 81 | Answer: 127 ohm

question: Two resistors 71 ohm and 25 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 71, R2 = 25 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 71*25 / (71+25) | Answer: 18.49 ohm

question: A device draws 12.9 A at 210 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 210, I = 12.9 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 210 * 12.9 | Answer: 2709 W

question: A current of 6.1 A flows through a 118 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 6.1, R = 118 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (6.1)^2 * 118 | Answer: 4391 W

question: Two capacitors 47.9 uF and 12.8 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 47.9, C2 = 12.8 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 47.9*12.8 / (47.9+12.8) | Answer: 10.1 uF

question: A resistor 30 kohm and capacitor 12.4 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 30, C = 12.4 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (30k)(12.4u) = 372 ms | Answer: 372 ms

question: An inductor 325.6 mH is in series with 172 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 325.6, R = 172 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (325.6e-3) / 172 | Answer: 1.893 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 84.4 mH inductor at 290 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 84.4, f = 290 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (290)(84.4e-3) | Answer: 153.8 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 24.3 uF capacitor at 310 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 24.3, f = 310 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (310)(24.3e-6)) | Answer: 21.13 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 66 ohm, XL = 45 ohm and XC = 93 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 66, XL = 45, XC = 93 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(66^2 + (45 - 93)^2) | Answer: 81.61 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 58.6 mH and C = 3.7 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 58.6, C = 3.7 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(58.6e-3 * 3.7e-6)) | Answer: 341.8 Hz

question: A capacitor of 26.8 uF is charged to 145 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 26.8, V = 145 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*26.8e-6*(145)^2 | Answer: 281.7 mJ

question: An alternating voltage has a peak value of 172 V. Find its RMS value.
solution: Given: Vp = 172 | Formula: Vrms = Vp / sqrt(2) | Substitute: Vrms = 172 / sqrt(2) | Answer: 121.6 V

question: A transformer has primary voltage 320 V with 340 primary turns and 300 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 320, N1 = 340, N2 = 300 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 320 * 300/340 | Answer: 282.4 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 210 V and draws an armature current of 12 A. If the armature resistance is 0.23 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 210, Ia = 12, Ra = 0.23 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 210 - 12*0.23 | Answer: 207.2 V

question: A 6-pole induction motor on a 60 Hz supply runs at 960 rpm. Find the slip (%).
formula: s = (Ns - N) / Ns,  Ns = 120 f / P

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 95 A at 415 V (line) with a power factor of 0.95. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 95, VL = 415, pf = 0.95 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*415*95*0.95 / 1000 | Answer: 64.87 kW

question: A load has real power 30 kW and apparent power 115 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 30, S = 115 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 30 / 115 | Answer: 0.2609

question: A machine delivers 130 kW output while drawing 132 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 130, Pi = 132 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 130/132 * 100 | Answer: 98.48 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 17 V across R1 = 4 ohm and R2 = 33 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 17, R1 = 4, R2 = 33 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 17*33 / (4+33) | Answer: 15.16 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 80 kohm and Rin = 26 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 80, Rin = 26 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 80 / 26 | Answer: 3.077

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 150 kohm and Rg = 17 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 150, Rg = 17 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 150/17 | Answer: 9.824

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 1963. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 1963 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(1963) | Answer: 32.93 dB

question: A first-order system has a time constant of 1.5 s. Find the time (in s) to reach 63.2% of its final value.

formula: At t = tau the response reaches 63.2% (one time constant)

question: A signal is sampled at 74 kHz. According to the Nyquist criterion, what is the maximum signal frequency that can be represented (in kHz)?
solution: Given: fs = 74 | Formula: f_max = fs / 2 | Substitute: f_max = 74 / 2 | Answer: 37 kHz

question: A simply supported beam of span 8.1 m carries a central point load of 45 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 8.1, W = 45 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 45*8.1 / 4 | Answer: 91.12 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 5.8 m carries a UDL of 30 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.8, w = 30 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 30*(5.8)^2 / 8 | Answer: 126.2 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 4.3 m carries a point load 10 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.3, W = 10 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 10*4.3 | Answer: 43 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 3.8 m carries a UDL of 34 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.8, w = 34 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 34*(3.8)^2 / 2 | Answer: 245.5 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 7.9 m carries a point load 95 kN at distance 1.4 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 7.9, a = 1.4, W = 95 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 95*(7.9 - 1.4) / 7.9 | Answer: 78.16 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 4.7 m) carries a central point load 55 kN. With E = 25 GPa and I = 100e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=55000 N, L=4700.0 mm, E=25000 MPa, I=100e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 47.59 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 7.1 m carries a UDL of 12 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7.1, w = 12 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 12*(7.1)^2 / 12 | Answer: 50.41 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 490 mm, clear cover 35 mm and main bars of diameter 12 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 490, c = 35, dia = 12 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 490 - 35 - 12/2 | Answer: 449 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 18.7 m^2 carrying a factored load of 15.9 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 18.7, w = 15.9 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 15.9 * 18.7 | Answer: 297.3 kN

question: For a bar of diameter 12 mm with design bond stress 2.1 MPa and steel stress 360 MPa, find the development length in mm.
solution: Given: dia = 12, tbd = 2.1, fs = 360 | Formula: Ld = phi fs / (4 tau_bd) | Substitute: Ld = 12*360 / (4*2.1) | Answer: 514.3 mm

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 6.1 m, unit weight 19 kN/m^3, phi = 32 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 11.8 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 21 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 11.8, g = 21 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (21 - 9.81)*11.8 | Answer: 132 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 8.6e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1.2, area = 4.4e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 8.6, i = 1.2, A = 4.4 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (8.6e-4)*1.2*(4.4e-3) | Answer: 4541 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.9 m, bed slope 0.007 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.019. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 3.1 m under a head of 1.1 m. Taking Cd = 0.61 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.

question: A rectangular channel 4.1 m wide carries a discharge of 26.6 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).

question: For a design speed of 65 km/h with allowable superelevation 0.06 and lateral friction 0.15, find the minimum curve radius in m.

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 200 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.19 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 4 days.

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.08 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 760 m with this tape.

question: A file of 30 megabits is sent over a link of 12 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.

question: A link has bandwidth 59 Mbps and round-trip time 60 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 59, R = 60 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 59e6 * 60e-3 bits = 3540 kb | Answer: 3540 kilobits

question: A channel has bandwidth 12 kHz. Using Nyquist's theorem with 4 signal levels, find the maximum data rate in kbps (noiseless).
solution: Given: B = 12, M = 4 | Formula: C = 2 B log2(M) | Substitute: C = 2*12*log2(4) | Answer: 48 kbps

question: A channel of bandwidth 7 kHz has a signal-to-noise ratio of 7 (linear). Using Shannon's theorem, find the channel capacity in kbps.
solution: Given: B = 7, SNR = 7 | Formula: C = B log2(1 + SNR) | Substitute: C = 7*log2(1 + 7) | Answer: 21 kbps

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.95, cache access time 8 ns and main-memory access time 70 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.95, tc = 8, tm = 70 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.95*8 + (1 - 0.95)*70 | Answer: 11.1 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 562577 elements?
solution: Given: n = 562577 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(562577)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: An O(n^2) algorithm performs c*n^2 basic operations. If c = 1 and n = 2940, how many operations are performed?
solution: Given: n = 2940 | Formula: operations = n^2 | Substitute: = (2940)^2 | Answer: 8643600

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.004, memory access time 150 ns and page-fault service time 7 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 7 ms = 7000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.004)*150 + 0.004*7000000.0 ns | Answer: 28.15 microseconds

question: A modem transmits at 1800 baud using 8-level signalling. Find the bit rate in bps.
solution: Given: baud = 1800, M = 8 | Formula: bit rate = baud * log2(M) | Substitute: bit rate = 1800 * log2(8) | Answer: 5400 bps

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 1.5 m^3 at 180 kPa and 530 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 1.5, P = 180, Tk = 530 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (180e3)*1.5 / (8.314*530) | Answer: 61.27 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.14 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 12 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.14, t = 12 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.14*12) | Answer: 0.8136

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.16 /min) is to reach 60% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.16, X = 60 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.6) / 0.16 | Answer: 5.727 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.41 /min) reaches 50% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.41, X = 50 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.5 / (0.41*(1 - 0.5)) | Answer: 2.439 min

question: A first-order reaction has a rate constant of 0.41 /min. Find its half-life in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.41 | Formula: t_half = ln(2) / k | Substitute: t_half = 0.6931 / 0.41 | Answer: 1.691 min

question: For a reaction with A = 4e10 /s and activation energy 55 kJ/mol at 480 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 4, Ea = 55, Tk = 480 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 4e10 * exp(-55e3 / (8.314*480)) | Answer: 41364 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.92 and bottoms xW = 0.1, with relative volatility alpha = 2.4. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.92, xw = 0.1, al = 2.4 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.92/0.08)(0.9/0.1)] / ln(2.4) | Answer: 5.3 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.63 and x = 0.45. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.63, x = 0.45 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.63/0.37) / (0.45/0.55) | Answer: 2.081

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.15 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 20 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.15, Psat = 20 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.15 * 20 | Answer: 3 kPa

question: A stream of 8.5 kg/s with specific heat 1.7 kJ/kg-K is heated through 35 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 8.5, cp = 1.7, dT = 35 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 8.5*1.7*35 | Answer: 505.8 kW

question: A reactor of volume 3.4 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 1.6 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 3.4, Q = 1.6 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 3.4 / 1.6 | Answer: 2.125 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 2.5e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 5 mm with a concentration difference of 40 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 2.5, L = 5, dC = 40 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (2.5e-9)*40 / (5e-3) | Answer: 20 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 9.6 min and steady-state gain 3.4. For a step input of magnitude 2, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 9.6, K = 3.4, M = 2 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 3.4 * 2 | Answer: 6.8 units

question: A reactor operates at a space time of 2.5 min. Find its space velocity in per hour.
solution: Given: tau = 2.5 | Formula: SV = 60 / tau  (per hour) | Substitute: SV = 60 / 2.5 | Answer: 24 /h

question: An aircraft wing of area 85 m^2 flies at 190 m/s (air density 1.225 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.7. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 85, V = 190, rho = 1.225, CL = 0.7 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1.225*(190)^2*85*0.7 / 1000 | Answer: 1316 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 55 m^2 flies at 250 m/s (density 0.7 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.12. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 55, V = 250, rho = 0.7, CD = 0.12 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.7*(250)^2*55*0.12 / 1000 | Answer: 144.4 kN

question: Find the dynamic pressure for air of density 1.225 kg/m^3 moving at 150 m/s, in Pa.
solution: Given: rho = 1.225, V = 150 | Formula: q = 0.5 rho V^2 | Substitute: q = 0.5*1.225*(150)^2 | Answer: 13781 Pa

question: An aircraft flies at 280 m/s where the speed of sound is 295 m/s. Find the Mach number.
solution: Given: V = 280, a = 295 | Formula: M = V / a | Substitute: M = 280 / 295 | Answer: 0.9492

question: A specimen under stress 280 MPa shows an elastic strain of 1.1e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 280, eps = 1.1 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 280 / (1.1e-3) MPa = 254.5 GPa | Answer: 254.5 GPa

question: A block of mass 19 kg has a volume of 0.9e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.

question: A rod of length 500 mm is heated through 105 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 23e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 35 ohm, R2 = 145 ohm and R3 = 270 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 35, R2 = 145, R3 = 270 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 145*270 / 35 | Answer: 1119 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 350 ohm and gauge factor 2.2 experiences a strain of 1950e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.

question: A measurement reads 10.63 when the true value is 20. Find the percentage error.

question: Annual demand is 3500 units, ordering cost 50 per order and holding cost 20 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).

question: An asset costs 270000 with salvage value 12000 after 11 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.

question: A product sells for 160 per unit with variable cost 40 per unit and fixed costs 105000. Find the break-even quantity in units.

question: Find the present worth of 200000 received 2 years from now at an interest rate of 7% per year.

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.93, 0.91 and 0.92 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.

question: A process produces 31 defective items in a batch of 16500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).

question: Evaluate the number of combinations C(18, 12).

question: Find the 14th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 7 and common difference -2.

question: A steel bar is fully restrained and heated through 45 deg C. With E = 210 GPa and alpha = 12e-6 /deg C, find the thermal stress in MPa.

question: A Carnot engine operates between 640 K and 400 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).

question: A refrigerator works between 270 K (cold) and 316 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.

question: A heat pump operates between 283 K and 334 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.

question: 6.3 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 130 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.

question: 4 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 180 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4, dT = 180 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 4 * 1.005 * 180 | Answer: 723.6 kJ

question: Water flows at 2.4 m/s through a pipe of diameter 50 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 11.9 m. Taking Cv = 0.95, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
