question: In a pipe (diameter 200 mm) water flows at 2.4 m/s. It contracts to diameter 70 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 200, d2 = 70, V1 = 2.4 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 2.4*(200/70)^2 | Answer: 19.59 m/s

question: Water flows at 3.1 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.35 m and length 400 m. With friction factor f = 0.031, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 35 teeth drives a gear of 49 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1400 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 35, z2 = 49, N1 = 1400 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1400*35 / 49 | Answer: 1000 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 240 mm rotates at 400 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 240, N = 400 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.24)*400 / 60 | Answer: 5.027 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 47.5 kW at 900 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 47.5, N = 900 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(47.5*1000) / (2*pi*900) | Answer: 504 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 2.1 kg rotates at radius 0.54 m at 750 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 16300 N/m and mass 11.4 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 16300, m = 11.4 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(16300/11.4) | Answer: 6.018 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 6.7 m^2 and thickness 0.16 m has conductivity k = 1.7 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 40 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 6.7, L = 0.16, k = 1.7, dT = 40 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 1.7*6.7*40 / 0.16 | Answer: 2848 W

question: A surface of area 0.8 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 20 W/m^2-K to surroundings 105 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 0.8, h = 20, dT = 105 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 20*0.8*105 | Answer: 1680 W

question: In a counter-flow heat exchanger the terminal temperature differences are 65 deg C and 30 deg C. Find the log mean temperature difference (LMTD) in deg C.
solution: Given: dT1 = 65, dT2 = 30 | Formula: LMTD = (dT1 - dT2) / ln(dT1/dT2) | Substitute: LMTD = (65 - 30) / ln(65/30) | Answer: 45.27 deg C

question: In turning, cutting speed = 80 m/min, feed = 0.43 mm/rev, depth of cut = 1.2 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 80, f = 0.43, d = 1.2 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*80*0.43*1.2 | Answer: 41280 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 200 mm is turned at 800 rpm with a feed of 0.2 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 200, N = 800, f = 0.2 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 200 / (0.2*800) | Answer: 1.25 min

question: A resistor of 184 ohm carries a current of 3.6 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 184, I = 3.6 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 3.6 * 184 | Answer: 662.4 V

question: Three resistors 66 ohm, 25 ohm and 57 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 66, R2 = 25, R3 = 57 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 66 + 25 + 57 | Answer: 148 ohm

question: Two resistors 83 ohm and 76 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 83, R2 = 76 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 83*76 / (83+76) | Answer: 39.67 ohm

question: A device draws 12.6 A at 75 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 75, I = 12.6 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 75 * 12.6 | Answer: 945 W

question: A current of 2 A flows through a 6 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 2, R = 6 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (2)^2 * 6 | Answer: 24 W

question: Two capacitors 11.5 uF and 20.7 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 11.5, C2 = 20.7 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 11.5*20.7 / (11.5+20.7) | Answer: 7.393 uF

question: A resistor 23 kohm and capacitor 18.1 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 23, C = 18.1 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (23k)(18.1u) = 416.3 ms | Answer: 416.3 ms

question: An inductor 120.1 mH is in series with 76 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 120.1, R = 76 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (120.1e-3) / 76 | Answer: 1.58 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 173.1 mH inductor at 920 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 173.1, f = 920 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (920)(173.1e-3) | Answer: 1001 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 17.8 uF capacitor at 560 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 17.8, f = 560 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (560)(17.8e-6)) | Answer: 15.97 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 34 ohm, XL = 94 ohm and XC = 32 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 34, XL = 94, XC = 32 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(34^2 + (94 - 32)^2) | Answer: 70.71 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 84.1 mH and C = 8.9 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 84.1, C = 8.9 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(84.1e-3 * 8.9e-6)) | Answer: 184 Hz

question: A capacitor of 26.1 uF is charged to 45 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 26.1, V = 45 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*26.1e-6*(45)^2 | Answer: 26.43 mJ

question: An alternating voltage has a peak value of 50 V. Find its RMS value.
solution: Given: Vp = 50 | Formula: Vrms = Vp / sqrt(2) | Substitute: Vrms = 50 / sqrt(2) | Answer: 35.36 V

question: A transformer has primary voltage 410 V with 670 primary turns and 200 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 410, N1 = 670, N2 = 200 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 410 * 200/670 | Answer: 122.4 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 340 V and draws an armature current of 18 A. If the armature resistance is 1.04 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 340, Ia = 18, Ra = 1.04 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 340 - 18*1.04 | Answer: 321.3 V

question: A 6-pole induction motor on a 60 Hz supply runs at 860 rpm. Find the slip (%).
formula: s = (Ns - N) / Ns,  Ns = 120 f / P

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 60 A at 415 V (line) with a power factor of 0.91. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 60, VL = 415, pf = 0.91 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*415*60*0.91 / 1000 | Answer: 39.25 kW

question: A load has real power 155 kW and apparent power 210 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 155, S = 210 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 155 / 210 | Answer: 0.7381

question: A machine delivers 190 kW output while drawing 197 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 190, Pi = 197 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 190/197 * 100 | Answer: 96.45 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 11 V across R1 = 10 ohm and R2 = 12 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 11, R1 = 10, R2 = 12 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 11*12 / (10+12) | Answer: 6 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 220 kohm and Rin = 3 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 220, Rin = 3 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 220 / 3 | Answer: 73.33

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 180 kohm and Rg = 41 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 180, Rg = 41 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 180/41 | Answer: 5.39

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 9029. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 9029 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(9029) | Answer: 39.56 dB

question: A first-order system has a time constant of 2 s. Find the time (in s) to reach 63.2% of its final value.
solution: For a first-order step response, y = 1 - e^(-t/tau) | y = 0.632 when t = tau | Answer: 2 s
formula: At t = tau the response reaches 63.2% (one time constant)

question: A signal is sampled at 54 kHz. According to the Nyquist criterion, what is the maximum signal frequency that can be represented (in kHz)?
solution: Given: fs = 54 | Formula: f_max = fs / 2 | Substitute: f_max = 54 / 2 | Answer: 27 kHz

question: A simply supported beam of span 8.9 m carries a central point load of 35 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 8.9, W = 35 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 35*8.9 / 4 | Answer: 77.88 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 8.2 m carries a UDL of 35 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 8.2, w = 35 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 35*(8.2)^2 / 8 | Answer: 294.2 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 4.4 m carries a point load 35 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.4, W = 35 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 35*4.4 | Answer: 154 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 1.2 m carries a UDL of 30 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 1.2, w = 30 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 30*(1.2)^2 / 2 | Answer: 21.6 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.8 m carries a point load 30 kN at distance 1.3 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 4.8, a = 1.3, W = 30 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 30*(4.8 - 1.3) / 4.8 | Answer: 21.88 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 6.5 m) carries a central point load 15 kN. With E = 25 GPa and I = 100e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=15000 N, L=6500.0 mm, E=25000 MPa, I=100e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 34.33 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 4.8 m carries a UDL of 21 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.8, w = 21 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 21*(4.8)^2 / 12 | Answer: 40.32 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 680 mm, clear cover 50 mm and main bars of diameter 12 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 680, c = 50, dia = 12 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 680 - 50 - 12/2 | Answer: 624 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 22 m^2 carrying a factored load of 10.9 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 22, w = 10.9 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 10.9 * 22 | Answer: 239.8 kN

question: For a bar of diameter 12 mm with design bond stress 1.8 MPa and steel stress 435 MPa, find the development length in mm.
solution: Given: dia = 12, tbd = 1.8, fs = 435 | Formula: Ld = phi fs / (4 tau_bd) | Substitute: Ld = 12*435 / (4*1.8) | Answer: 725 mm

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 5.5 m, unit weight 16 kN/m^3, phi = 35 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 7.8 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 19 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 7.8, g = 19 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (19 - 9.81)*7.8 | Answer: 71.68 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 1.8e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1.1, area = 2.9e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 1.8, i = 1.1, A = 2.9 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (1.8e-4)*1.1*(2.9e-3) | Answer: 574.2 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 0.8 m, bed slope 0.01 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.027. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 2 m under a head of 0.3 m. Taking Cd = 0.6 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 5.5 m wide carries a discharge of 5.2 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 130 m and design speed 85 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 130, V = 85 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (85)^2 / (127*130) | Answer: 0.4376
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: For a design speed of 60 km/h with allowable superelevation 0.06 and lateral friction 0.12, find the minimum curve radius in m.
A tank of volume 110 m^3 treats a flow of 120 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 110, Q = 120 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 110 / 120 | Answer: 0.9167 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 230 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.33 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 3 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 230, k = 0.33, t = 3 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 230*(1 - e^(-0.33*3)) | Answer: 144.5 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.58, rainfall intensity 60 mm/h over a catchment of 23.3 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.58, i = 60, A = 23.3 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.58*60*23.3 / 360 | Answer: 2.252 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.06 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 410 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.06, M = 410 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 410*(20+0.06)/20 | Answer: 411.2 m

question: Convert the decimal number 76 to binary.
solution: Divide 76 by 2 repeatedly, recording remainders | Reading remainders in reverse gives 1001100 | Answer: 1001100 (binary)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 2 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the decimal number 321 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 321 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 141 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the 8-bit binary number 10001000 to decimal.
solution: Binary 10001000 = sum of bit-weights | Answer: 136 (decimal)
formula: Sum each bit times its positional weight (2^i)

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 10110001 and 11001100.
solution: XOR: 01111101 | Count of 1s = 6 | Answer: 6
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 700 megabits is sent over a link of 65 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 700, B = 65 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 700 / 65 | Answer: 10.77 s

question: A link has bandwidth 40 Mbps and round-trip time 110 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 40, R = 110 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 40e6 * 110e-3 bits = 4400 kb | Answer: 4400 kilobits

question: A channel has bandwidth 13 kHz. Using Nyquist's theorem with 2 signal levels, find the maximum data rate in kbps (noiseless).
solution: Given: B = 13, M = 2 | Formula: C = 2 B log2(M) | Substitute: C = 2*13*log2(2) | Answer: 26 kbps

question: A channel of bandwidth 11 kHz has a signal-to-noise ratio of 7 (linear). Using Shannon's theorem, find the channel capacity in kbps.
solution: Given: B = 11, SNR = 7 | Formula: C = B log2(1 + SNR) | Substitute: C = 11*log2(1 + 7) | Answer: 33 kbps

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.86, cache access time 10 ns and main-memory access time 170 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.86, tc = 10, tm = 170 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.86*10 + (1 - 0.86)*170 | Answer: 32.4 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 193943 elements?
solution: Given: n = 193943 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(193943)) + 1 | Answer: 18

question: An O(n^2) algorithm performs c*n^2 basic operations. If c = 1 and n = 340, how many operations are performed?
solution: Given: n = 340 | Formula: operations = n^2 | Substitute: = (340)^2 | Answer: 115600

question: A program is 75% parallelisable and run on 2 processors. Using Amdahl's law, find the maximum speedup.
solution: Parallel fraction f = 0.75 | S = 1 / ((1 - 0.75) + 0.75/2) | Answer: 1.6x speedup

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.009, memory access time 190 ns and page-fault service time 9 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 9 ms = 9000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.009)*190 + 0.009*9000000.0 ns | Answer: 81.19 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: A modem transmits at 900 baud using 8-level signalling. Find the bit rate in bps.
solution: Given: baud = 900, M = 8 | Formula: bit rate = baud * log2(M) | Substitute: bit rate = 900 * log2(8) | Answer: 2700 bps

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 2.9 m^3 at 370 kPa and 500 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 2.9, P = 370, Tk = 500 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (370e3)*2.9 / (8.314*500) | Answer: 258.1 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.18 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 8 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.18, t = 8 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.18*8) | Answer: 0.7631

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.39 /min) is to reach 60% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.39, X = 60 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.6) / 0.39 | Answer: 2.349 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.4 /min) reaches 55% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.4, X = 55 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.55 / (0.4*(1 - 0.55)) | Answer: 3.056 min

question: For a reaction with A = 9e10 /s and activation energy 80 kJ/mol at 500 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 9, Ea = 80, Tk = 500 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 9e10 * exp(-80e3 / (8.314*500)) | Answer: 394.8 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.96 and bottoms xW = 0.08, with relative volatility alpha = 2.3. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.96, xw = 0.08, al = 2.3 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.96/0.04)(0.92/0.08)] / ln(2.3) | Answer: 6.748 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.86 and x = 0.41. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.86, x = 0.41 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.86/0.14) / (0.41/0.59) | Answer: 8.84

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.2 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 105 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.2, Psat = 105 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.2 * 105 | Answer: 21 kPa

question: A stream of 1.6 kg/s with specific heat 2.7 kJ/kg-K is heated through 85 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 1.6, cp = 2.7, dT = 85 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 1.6*2.7*85 | Answer: 367.2 kW

question: A reactor of volume 16.5 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 1.4 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 16.5, Q = 1.4 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 16.5 / 1.4 | Answer: 11.79 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 3e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 1 mm with a concentration difference of 90 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 3, L = 1, dC = 90 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (3e-9)*90 / (1e-3) | Answer: 270 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 1.5 min and steady-state gain 3.9. For a step input of magnitude 12, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 1.5, K = 3.9, M = 12 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 3.9 * 12 | Answer: 46.8 units

question: A reactor operates at a space time of 12.6 min. Find its space velocity in per hour.
solution: Given: tau = 12.6 | Formula: SV = 60 / tau  (per hour) | Substitute: SV = 60 / 12.6 | Answer: 4.762 /h

question: An aircraft wing of area 115 m^2 flies at 130 m/s (air density 1 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.6. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 115, V = 130, rho = 1, CL = 0.6 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1*(130)^2*115*0.6 / 1000 | Answer: 583 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 110 m^2 flies at 240 m/s (density 0.7 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.11. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 110, V = 240, rho = 0.7, CD = 0.11 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.7*(240)^2*110*0.11 / 1000 | Answer: 243.9 kN

question: Find the dynamic pressure for air of density 1.225 kg/m^3 moving at 120 m/s, in Pa.
solution: Given: rho = 1.225, V = 120 | Formula: q = 0.5 rho V^2 | Substitute: q = 0.5*1.225*(120)^2 | Answer: 8820 Pa

question: An aircraft flies at 300 m/s where the speed of sound is 295 m/s. Find the Mach number.
solution: Given: V = 300, a = 295 | Formula: M = V / a | Substitute: M = 300 / 295 | Answer: 1.017

question: Find the circular orbital velocity of a satellite at altitude 1850 km above Earth (Earth radius 6371 km, mu = 3.986e14 m^3/s^2), in km/s.
A specimen under stress 170 MPa shows an elastic strain of 1.1e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 170, eps = 1.1 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 170 / (1.1e-3) MPa = 154.5 GPa | Answer: 154.5 GPa

question: A block of mass 45 kg has a volume of 2.6e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 45, V = 2.6 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 45 / (2.6e-3) | Answer: 17308 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 1500 mm is heated through 145 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 17e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 1500, dT = 145, al = 17 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 1500*17e-6*145 | Answer: 3.697 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 145 ohm, R2 = 145 ohm and R3 = 485 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 145, R2 = 145, R3 = 485 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 145*485 / 145 | Answer: 485 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 120 ohm and gauge factor 2 experiences a strain of 1400e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 120, GF = 2, eps = 1400 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 120*2*1400e-6 | Answer: 336 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 10.83 when the true value is 10. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10.83, true = 10 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10.83 - 10| / 10 * 100 | Answer: 8.3 %

question: Annual demand is 32500 units, ordering cost 160 per order and holding cost 2 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 32500, S = 160, H = 2 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*32500*160 / 2) | Answer: 228 units

question: An asset costs 80000 with salvage value 4000 after 12 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 80000, Sv = 4000, n = 12 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (80000 - 4000) / 12 | Answer: 6333 per year

question: A product sells for 130 per unit with variable cost 70 per unit and fixed costs 70000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 130, V = 70, F = 70000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 70000 / (130 - 70) | Answer: 1167 units

question: Find the present worth of 65000 received 7 years from now at an interest rate of 10% per year.
solution: Given: F = 65000, n = 7, i = 10 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 65000 / (1 + 0.1)^7 | Answer: 33355 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.97, 0.93 and 0.91 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.97, r2 = 0.93, r3 = 0.91 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.97*0.93*0.91 | Answer: 0.8209

question: A process produces 30 defective items in a batch of 8500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 30, N = 8500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 30/8500 * 1e6 | Answer: 3529 PPM

question: Find the slope of the line through (3, -8) and (9, 0).

question: Find the distance between the points (1, 9) and (-5, 8).
solution: Given: x1 = 1, y1 = 9, x2 = -5, y2 = 8 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-6)^2 + (-1)^2) | Answer: 6.083 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (2,-1), (0,4), (-1,1).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 5.5 sq units

question: Evaluate the number of combinations C(10, 1).
solution: Given: n = 10, r = 1 | Formula: C(n, r) = n! / (r! (n - r)!) | Substitute: C(10, 1) = 10! / (1! * 9!) | Answer: 10

question: Evaluate the number of permutations P(7, 4).
solution: Given: n = 7, r = 4 | Formula: P(n, r) = n! / (n - r)! | Substitute: P(7, 4) = 7! / 3! | Answer: 840

question: Find the 32th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 19 and common difference -7.
solution: Given: a = 19, d = -7, n = 32 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = 19 + (32 - 1)*-7 | Answer: -198

question: Find the sum of the first 8 terms of an AP with first term -7 and common difference 6.
solution: Given: a = -7, d = 6, n = 8 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 8/2 [2*-7 + (8-1)*6] | Answer: 112

question: Find the 5th term of a geometric progression with first term 2 and common ratio 2.
solution: Given: a = 2, r = 2, n = 5 | Formula: a_n = a r^(n-1) | Substitute: a_n = 2 * 2^(5-1) | Answer: 32

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 33000 at 7.6% per annum for 1 years.
solution: Given: P = 33000, R = 7.6, Tt = 1 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 33000 * 7.6 * 1 / 100 | Answer: 2508 currency units

question: Find the amount when 6000 is invested at 10.8% per annum compounded annually for 2 years.
solution: Given: P = 6000, R = 10.8, Tt = 2 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 6000 * (1 + 10.8/100)^2 | Answer: 7366 currency units

question: Find the modulus of the complex number 3 + 6i.
solution: Given: a = 3, b = 6 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((3)^2 + (6)^2) | Answer: 6.708

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number 10 + 9i.
solution: Given: a = 10, b = 9 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(9, 10) | Answer: 41.99 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -2x^3 - x^2 - 7x + 1 at x = 2.

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 11 and 50.

question: A circular rod of diameter 25 mm carries an axial tensile load of 72 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 23 mm and length 2900 mm carries an axial load of 14 kN. Take E = 110 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 63 mm transmits a torque of 600 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.

question: A shaft of diameter 49 mm and length 600 mm carries a torque of 1750 N-m. With G = 80 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.

question: A rectangular beam section is 99 mm wide and 100 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (118 mm x 120 mm) carries a bending moment of 5 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 680 MPa is designed for a working stress of 90 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 680, sw = 90 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 680 / 90 | Answer: 7.556

question: A steel bar is fully restrained and heated through 30 deg C. With E = 200 GPa and alpha = 11e-6 /deg C, find the thermal stress in MPa.
solution: Given: dT = 30, E = 200, al = 11 | Formula: sigma = E alpha (dT) | Substitute: sigma = 200000 * 11e-6 * 30 | Answer: 66 MPa

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1100 mm and wall thickness 13 mm carries an internal pressure of 2 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1100, t = 13, P = 2 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 2*1100 / (2*13) | Answer: 84.62 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 1040 K and 340 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 1040, Tc = 340 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 340/1040) * 100 | Answer: 67.31 %

question: A refrigerator works between 273 K (cold) and 324 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 273, Th = 324 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 273 / (324 - 273) | Answer: 5.353

question: A heat pump operates between 275 K and 330 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 275, Th = 330 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 330 / (330 - 275) | Answer: 6

question: 3.8 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 155 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.8, dT = 155 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 3.8 * 0.718 * 155 | Answer: 422.9 kJ

question: 1.2 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 175 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1.2, dT = 175 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 1.2 * 1.005 * 175 | Answer: 211 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 2.3 m^3 at 480 K with mass 4.5 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 2.3, Tk = 480, m = 4.5 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 4.5*0.287*480 / 2.3 | Answer: 269.5 kPa

question: 1.8 kg of air expands isothermally at 370 K from volume V1 to 5*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 4.9 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.13 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 4.9, D = 0.13 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*4.9*0.13 / 0.001 | Answer: 637000

question: Water flows at 3.3 m/s through a pipe of diameter 150 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 17.7 m. Taking Cv = 0.98, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).

question: Water flows at 4 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.26 m and length 190 m. With friction factor f = 0.025, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).

question: A pinion of 29 teeth drives a gear of 56 teeth. If the pinion runs at 900 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.

question: A pulley of diameter 180 mm rotates at 500 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 180, N = 500 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.18)*500 / 60 | Answer: 4.712 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 39.2 kW at 850 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 39.2, N = 850 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(39.2*1000) / (2*pi*850) | Answer: 440.4 N-m

question: In a counter-flow heat exchanger the terminal temperature differences are 45 deg C and 25 deg C. Find the log mean temperature difference (LMTD) in deg C.

question: In turning, cutting speed = 150 m/min, feed = 0.3 mm/rev, depth of cut = 1.4 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 150, f = 0.3, d = 1.4 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*150*0.3*1.4 | Answer: 63000 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 290 mm is turned at 1150 rpm with a feed of 0.26 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 290, N = 1150, f = 0.26 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 290 / (0.26*1150) | Answer: 0.9699 min

question: A resistor of 113 ohm carries a current of 1.4 A. Find the voltage across it.

question: Three resistors 73 ohm, 42 ohm and 40 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.

question: A device draws 10 A at 85 V. Find the power consumed.

question: A current of 7.6 A flows through a 71 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.

question: Two capacitors 16.7 uF and 28 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 16.7, C2 = 28 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 16.7*28 / (16.7+28) | Answer: 10.46 uF

question: A resistor 75 kohm and capacitor 10.9 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.

question: An inductor 281.5 mH is in series with 150 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 281.5, R = 150 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (281.5e-3) / 150 | Answer: 1.877 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 185.8 mH inductor at 530 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 185.8, f = 530 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (530)(185.8e-3) | Answer: 618.7 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 41.1 uF capacitor at 100 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 41.1, f = 100 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (100)(41.1e-6)) | Answer: 38.72 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 91 ohm, XL = 14 ohm and XC = 23 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 91, XL = 14, XC = 23 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(91^2 + (14 - 23)^2) | Answer: 91.44 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 24.8 mH and C = 2.8 uF (in Hz).

question: A capacitor of 34 uF is charged to 275 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.

question: An alternating voltage has a peak value of 48 V. Find its RMS value.

question: A transformer has primary voltage 330 V with 940 primary turns and 190 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.

question: A DC motor is supplied at 200 V and draws an armature current of 57 A. If the armature resistance is 0.86 ohm, find the back EMF.

question: A machine delivers 85 kW output while drawing 212 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 15 V across R1 = 49 ohm and R2 = 48 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 110 kohm and Rin = 26 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 6185. Express the gain in decibels (power).

question: A first-order system has a time constant of 8.3 s. Find the time (in s) to reach 63.2% of its final value.

question: A simply supported beam of span 10 m carries a central point load of 115 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.

question: A cantilever of length 1.7 m carries a point load 65 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.1 m carries a point load 90 kN at distance 2.6 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.

question: A simply supported beam (span 3.1 m) carries a central point load 30 kN. With E = 30 GPa and I = 500e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=30000 N, L=3100.0 mm, E=30000 MPa, I=500e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 1.241 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 7.2 m carries a UDL of 15 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7.2, w = 15 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 15*(7.2)^2 / 12 | Answer: 64.8 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 390 mm, clear cover 35 mm and main bars of diameter 16 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 390, c = 35, dia = 16 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 390 - 35 - 16/2 | Answer: 347 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 22.8 m^2 carrying a factored load of 13.9 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 22.8, w = 13.9 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 13.9 * 22.8 | Answer: 316.9 kN

question: For a bar of diameter 12 mm with design bond stress 1.8 MPa and steel stress 360 MPa, find the development length in mm.
solution: Given: dia = 12, tbd = 1.8, fs = 360 | Formula: Ld = phi fs / (4 tau_bd) | Substitute: Ld = 12*360 / (4*1.8) | Answer: 600 mm

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 4.1 m, unit weight 20 kN/m^3, phi = 38 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).

question: At a depth of 9.3 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 19 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 9.3, g = 19 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (19 - 9.81)*9.3 | Answer: 85.47 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 2.2e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1, area = 3.7e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1 m, bed slope 0.002 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.02. Find the mean velocity in m/s.

question: A rectangular channel 4.1 m wide carries a discharge of 4.4 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).

solution: Given: R = 580, V = 45 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (45)^2 / (127*580) | Answer: 0.02749

question: For a design speed of 100 km/h with allowable superelevation 0.07 and lateral friction 0.13, find the minimum curve radius in m.
A tank of volume 650 m^3 treats a flow of 180 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 650, Q = 180 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 650 / 180 | Answer: 3.611 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 360 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.26 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 7 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 360, k = 0.26, t = 7 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 360*(1 - e^(-0.26*7)) | Answer: 301.7 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.68, rainfall intensity 65 mm/h over a catchment of 22 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.68, i = 65, A = 22 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.68*65*22 / 360 | Answer: 2.701 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.05 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 160 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.05, M = 160 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 160*(20+0.05)/20 | Answer: 160.4 m

solution: Divide 3507 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: DB3 (hex)

solution: Binary 01011100 = sum of bit-weights | Answer: 92 (decimal)

solution: XOR: 11100101 | Count of 1s = 5 | Answer: 5
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 920 megabits is sent over a link of 55 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 920, B = 55 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 920 / 55 | Answer: 16.73 s

question: A link has bandwidth 90 Mbps and round-trip time 180 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 90, R = 180 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 90e6 * 180e-3 bits = 16200 kb | Answer: 16200 kilobits

question: A channel has bandwidth 17 kHz. Using Nyquist's theorem with 16 signal levels, find the maximum data rate in kbps (noiseless).
solution: Given: B = 17, M = 16 | Formula: C = 2 B log2(M) | Substitute: C = 2*17*log2(16) | Answer: 136 kbps

question: A channel of bandwidth 12 kHz has a signal-to-noise ratio of 255 (linear). Using Shannon's theorem, find the channel capacity in kbps.
solution: Given: B = 12, SNR = 255 | Formula: C = B log2(1 + SNR) | Substitute: C = 12*log2(1 + 255) | Answer: 96 kbps

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.84, cache access time 4 ns and main-memory access time 180 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.84, tc = 4, tm = 180 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.84*4 + (1 - 0.84)*180 | Answer: 32.16 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 965520 elements?
solution: Given: n = 965520 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(965520)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: An O(n^2) algorithm performs c*n^2 basic operations. If c = 1 and n = 1750, how many operations are performed?
solution: Given: n = 1750 | Formula: operations = n^2 | Substitute: = (1750)^2 | Answer: 3062500

question: A program is 50% parallelisable and run on 2 processors. Using Amdahl's law, find the maximum speedup.
solution: Parallel fraction f = 0.5 | S = 1 / ((1 - 0.5) + 0.5/2) | Answer: 1.333x speedup

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.015, memory access time 180 ns and page-fault service time 8 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 8 ms = 8000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.015)*180 + 0.015*8000000.0 ns | Answer: 120.2 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 2.9 m^3 at 180 kPa and 360 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 2.9, P = 180, Tk = 360 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (180e3)*2.9 / (8.314*360) | Answer: 174.4 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.08 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 19 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.08, t = 19 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.08*19) | Answer: 0.7813

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.41 /min) is to reach 75% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.41, X = 75 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.75) / 0.41 | Answer: 3.381 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.43 /min) reaches 85% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.43, X = 85 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.85 / (0.43*(1 - 0.85)) | Answer: 13.18 min

question: A first-order reaction has a rate constant of 0.43 /min. Find its half-life in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.43 | Formula: t_half = ln(2) / k | Substitute: t_half = 0.6931 / 0.43 | Answer: 1.612 min

question: For a reaction with A = 4e10 /s and activation energy 60 kJ/mol at 340 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 4, Ea = 60, Tk = 340 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 4e10 * exp(-60e3 / (8.314*340)) | Answer: 24.2 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.95 and bottoms xW = 0.08, with relative volatility alpha = 3.2. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.95, xw = 0.08, al = 3.2 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.95/0.05)(0.92/0.08)] / ln(3.2) | Answer: 4.631 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.64 and x = 0.41. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.64, x = 0.41 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.64/0.36) / (0.41/0.59) | Answer: 2.558

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.72 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 35 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.72, Psat = 35 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.72 * 35 | Answer: 25.2 kPa

question: A stream of 4.7 kg/s with specific heat 1.4 kJ/kg-K is heated through 110 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 4.7, cp = 1.4, dT = 110 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 4.7*1.4*110 | Answer: 723.8 kW

question: A reactor of volume 8.5 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 2.1 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 8.5, Q = 2.1 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 8.5 / 2.1 | Answer: 4.048 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 7.5e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 1 mm with a concentration difference of 120 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 7.5, L = 1, dC = 120 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (7.5e-9)*120 / (1e-3) | Answer: 900 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 5.4 min and steady-state gain 1.3. For a step input of magnitude 2, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 5.4, K = 1.3, M = 2 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 1.3 * 2 | Answer: 2.6 units

question: A reactor operates at a space time of 5.2 min. Find its space velocity in per hour.
solution: Given: tau = 5.2 | Formula: SV = 60 / tau  (per hour) | Substitute: SV = 60 / 5.2 | Answer: 11.54 /h

question: An aircraft wing of area 20 m^2 flies at 220 m/s (air density 0.7 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.8. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 20, V = 220, rho = 0.7, CL = 0.8 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.7*(220)^2*20*0.8 / 1000 | Answer: 271 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 55 m^2 flies at 100 m/s (density 1.225 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.05. Find the drag force in kN.
Find the dynamic pressure for air of density 0.7 kg/m^3 moving at 140 m/s, in Pa.
solution: Given: rho = 0.7, V = 140 | Formula: q = 0.5 rho V^2 | Substitute: q = 0.5*0.7*(140)^2 | Answer: 6860 Pa

question: An aircraft flies at 520 m/s where the speed of sound is 295 m/s. Find the Mach number.

question: A specimen under stress 310 MPa shows an elastic strain of 1.4e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.

question: A block of mass 31 kg has a volume of 4.7e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.

question: A rod of length 800 mm is heated through 60 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 17e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 60 ohm, R2 = 105 ohm and R3 = 500 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 60, R2 = 105, R3 = 500 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 105*500 / 60 | Answer: 875 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 1000 ohm and gauge factor 2 experiences a strain of 300e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 1000, GF = 2, eps = 300 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 1000*2*300e-6 | Answer: 600 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 10.15 when the true value is 50. Find the percentage error.

question: Annual demand is 25500 units, ordering cost 130 per order and holding cost 5 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 25500, S = 130, H = 5 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*25500*130 / 5) | Answer: 1152 units

question: An asset costs 120000 with salvage value 36000 after 7 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 120000, Sv = 36000, n = 7 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (120000 - 36000) / 7 | Answer: 12000 per year

question: A product sells for 430 per unit with variable cost 160 per unit and fixed costs 15000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 430, V = 160, F = 15000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 15000 / (430 - 160) | Answer: 55.56 units

question: Find the present worth of 85000 received 8 years from now at an interest rate of 11% per year.
solution: Given: F = 85000, n = 8, i = 11 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 85000 / (1 + 0.11)^8 | Answer: 36884 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.94, 0.95 and 0.98 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.94, r2 = 0.95, r3 = 0.98 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.94*0.95*0.98 | Answer: 0.8751

question: A process produces 4 defective items in a batch of 16500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 4, N = 16500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 4/16500 * 1e6 | Answer: 242.4 PPM

question: Find the slope of the line through (-1, 2) and (-2, -9).

question: Find the distance between the points (-4, 5) and (0, 8).
solution: Given: x1 = -4, y1 = 5, x2 = 0, y2 = 8 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((4)^2 + (3)^2) | Answer: 5 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (5,-5), (-7,-4), (1,0).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 28 sq units

question: Evaluate the number of combinations C(16, 8).
solution: Given: n = 16, r = 8 | Formula: C(n, r) = n! / (r! (n - r)!) | Substitute: C(16, 8) = 16! / (8! * 8!) | Answer: 12870

question: Evaluate the number of permutations P(11, 8).
solution: Given: n = 11, r = 8 | Formula: P(n, r) = n! / (n - r)! | Substitute: P(11, 8) = 11! / 3! | Answer: 6652800

question: Find the 40th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -1 and common difference -6.
solution: Given: a = -1, d = -6, n = 40 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -1 + (40 - 1)*-6 | Answer: -235

question: Find the sum of the first 9 terms of an AP with first term 1 and common difference -2.
solution: Given: a = 1, d = -2, n = 9 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 9/2 [2*1 + (9-1)*-2] | Answer: -63

question: Find the 3th term of a geometric progression with first term 4 and common ratio 4.
solution: Given: a = 4, r = 4, n = 3 | Formula: a_n = a r^(n-1) | Substitute: a_n = 4 * 4^(3-1) | Answer: 64

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 16500 at 7.2% per annum for 8 years.
solution: Given: P = 16500, R = 7.2, Tt = 8 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 16500 * 7.2 * 8 / 100 | Answer: 9504 currency units

question: Find the amount when 31000 is invested at 11.9% per annum compounded annually for 6 years.
solution: Given: P = 31000, R = 11.9, Tt = 6 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 31000 * (1 + 11.9/100)^6 | Answer: 60861 currency units

question: Find the modulus of the complex number 1 + -12i.
solution: Given: a = 1, b = -12 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((1)^2 + (-12)^2) | Answer: 12.04

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number 0 + 1i.
solution: Given: a = 0, b = 1 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(1, 0) | Answer: 90 degrees

question: A circular rod of diameter 27 mm carries an axial tensile load of 40 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.

A solid shaft of diameter 59 mm transmits a torque of 450 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.

question: A shaft of diameter 33 mm and length 900 mm carries a torque of 300 N-m. With G = 77 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.

question: A rectangular beam section is 121 mm wide and 90 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 121, h = 90 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 121*(90)^2 / 6 | Answer: 163350 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (114 mm x 170 mm) carries a bending moment of 4 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.

question: A component of ultimate strength 420 MPa is designed for a working stress of 250 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 420, sw = 250 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 420 / 250 | Answer: 1.68

question: A steel bar is fully restrained and heated through 110 deg C. With E = 210 GPa and alpha = 12e-6 /deg C, find the thermal stress in MPa.
solution: Given: dT = 110, E = 210, al = 12 | Formula: sigma = E alpha (dT) | Substitute: sigma = 210000 * 12e-6 * 110 | Answer: 277.2 MPa

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 400 mm and wall thickness 9 mm carries an internal pressure of 1.8 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 400, t = 9, P = 1.8 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 1.8*400 / (2*9) | Answer: 40 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 1000 K and 300 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 1000, Tc = 300 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 300/1000) * 100 | Answer: 70 %

question: A refrigerator works between 250 K (cold) and 304 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 250, Th = 304 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 250 / (304 - 250) | Answer: 4.63

question: A heat pump operates between 271 K and 306 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 271, Th = 306 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 306 / (306 - 271) | Answer: 8.743

question: 7.7 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 55 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 7.7, dT = 55 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 7.7 * 0.718 * 55 | Answer: 304.1 kJ

question: 4.3 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 155 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.3, dT = 155 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 4.3 * 1.005 * 155 | Answer: 669.8 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 1.6 m^3 at 410 K with mass 3.6 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 1.6, Tk = 410, m = 3.6 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 3.6*0.287*410 / 1.6 | Answer: 264.8 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 4.2 kg of air expands isothermally at 390 K from volume V1 to 3*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.2, Tk = 390, ratio = 3 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 4.2*0.287*390*ln(3) | Answer: 516.5 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 1.8 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.07 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 1.8, D = 0.07 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*1.8*0.07 / 0.001 | Answer: 126000

question: Water flows at 1.2 m/s through a pipe of diameter 150 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 4.2 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 4.2 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*4.2 / 1000 | Answer: 41.2 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 2.9 m. Taking Cv = 0.98, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 2.9, cv = 0.98 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.98*sqrt(2*9.81*2.9) | Answer: 7.392 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 340 mm) water flows at 0.5 m/s. It contracts to diameter 130 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 340, d2 = 130, V1 = 0.5 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 0.5*(340/130)^2 | Answer: 3.42 m/s

question: Water flows at 1.8 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.4 m and length 480 m. With friction factor f = 0.023, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 20 teeth drives a gear of 107 teeth. If the pinion runs at 900 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 20, z2 = 107, N1 = 900 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 900*20 / 107 | Answer: 168.2 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 350 mm rotates at 500 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 350, N = 500 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.35)*500 / 60 | Answer: 9.163 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 18.1 kW at 800 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 18.1, N = 800 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(18.1*1000) / (2*pi*800) | Answer: 216.1 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 2.8 kg rotates at radius 0.52 m at 250 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 10500 N/m and mass 15 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 10500, m = 15 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(10500/15) | Answer: 4.211 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 2.9 m^2 and thickness 0.3 m has conductivity k = 32.4 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 25 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 2.9, L = 0.3, k = 32.4, dT = 25 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 32.4*2.9*25 / 0.3 | Answer: 7830 W

question: A surface of area 5.2 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 115 W/m^2-K to surroundings 100 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 5.2, h = 115, dT = 100 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 115*5.2*100 | Answer: 59800 W

question: In a counter-flow heat exchanger the terminal temperature differences are 110 deg C and 35 deg C. Find the log mean temperature difference (LMTD) in deg C.
solution: Given: dT1 = 110, dT2 = 35 | Formula: LMTD = (dT1 - dT2) / ln(dT1/dT2) | Substitute: LMTD = (110 - 35) / ln(110/35) | Answer: 65.49 deg C

question: In turning, cutting speed = 220 m/min, feed = 0.23 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2.9 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 220, f = 0.23, d = 2.9 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*220*0.23*2.9 | Answer: 146740 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 260 mm is turned at 350 rpm with a feed of 0.15 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 260, N = 350, f = 0.15 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 260 / (0.15*350) | Answer: 4.952 min

question: A resistor of 24 ohm carries a current of 0.7 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 24, I = 0.7 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 0.7 * 24 | Answer: 16.8 V

question: Three resistors 27 ohm, 61 ohm and 60 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 27, R2 = 61, R3 = 60 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 27 + 61 + 60 | Answer: 148 ohm

question: Two resistors 41 ohm and 54 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 41, R2 = 54 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 41*54 / (41+54) | Answer: 23.31 ohm

question: A device draws 7.4 A at 10 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 10, I = 7.4 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 10 * 7.4 | Answer: 74 W

question: A current of 3.6 A flows through a 18 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 3.6, R = 18 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (3.6)^2 * 18 | Answer: 233.3 W

question: Two capacitors 6.2 uF and 22.8 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 6.2, C2 = 22.8 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 6.2*22.8 / (6.2+22.8) | Answer: 4.874 uF

question: A resistor 9 kohm and capacitor 4.6 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 9, C = 4.6 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (9k)(4.6u) = 41.4 ms | Answer: 41.4 ms

question: An inductor 368.2 mH is in series with 174 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 368.2, R = 174 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (368.2e-3) / 174 | Answer: 2.116 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 169.1 mH inductor at 730 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 169.1, f = 730 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (730)(169.1e-3) | Answer: 775.6 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 25.4 uF capacitor at 290 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 25.4, f = 290 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (290)(25.4e-6)) | Answer: 21.61 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 95 ohm, XL = 74 ohm and XC = 19 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 95, XL = 74, XC = 19 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(95^2 + (74 - 19)^2) | Answer: 109.8 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 80.7 mH and C = 1.8 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 80.7, C = 1.8 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(80.7e-3 * 1.8e-6)) | Answer: 417.6 Hz

question: A capacitor of 9.4 uF is charged to 255 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 9.4, V = 255 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*9.4e-6*(255)^2 | Answer: 305.6 mJ

question: An alternating voltage has a peak value of 268 V. Find its RMS value.
solution: Given: Vp = 268 | Formula: Vrms = Vp / sqrt(2) | Substitute: Vrms = 268 / sqrt(2) | Answer: 189.5 V

question: A transformer has primary voltage 350 V with 990 primary turns and 250 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 350, N1 = 990, N2 = 250 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 350 * 250/990 | Answer: 88.38 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 280 V and draws an armature current of 41 A. If the armature resistance is 0.52 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 280, Ia = 41, Ra = 0.52 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 280 - 41*0.52 | Answer: 258.7 V

question: A 4-pole induction motor on a 60 Hz supply runs at 840 rpm. Find the slip (%).
formula: s = (Ns - N) / Ns,  Ns = 120 f / P

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 80 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.76. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 80, VL = 400, pf = 0.76 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*400*80*0.76 / 1000 | Answer: 42.12 kW

question: A load has real power 70 kW and apparent power 85 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 70, S = 85 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 70 / 85 | Answer: 0.8235

question: A machine delivers 105 kW output while drawing 142 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 105, Pi = 142 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 105/142 * 100 | Answer: 73.94 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 6 V across R1 = 11 ohm and R2 = 2 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 6, R1 = 11, R2 = 2 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 6*2 / (11+2) | Answer: 0.9231 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 140 kohm and Rin = 6 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 140, Rin = 6 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 140 / 6 | Answer: 23.33

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 10 kohm and Rg = 16 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 10, Rg = 16 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 10/16 | Answer: 1.625

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 684. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 684 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(684) | Answer: 28.35 dB

question: A first-order system has a time constant of 7 s. Find the time (in s) to reach 63.2% of its final value.
solution: For a first-order step response, y = 1 - e^(-t/tau) | y = 0.632 when t = tau | Answer: 7 s
formula: At t = tau the response reaches 63.2% (one time constant)

question: A signal is sampled at 22 kHz. According to the Nyquist criterion, what is the maximum signal frequency that can be represented (in kHz)?
solution: Given: fs = 22 | Formula: f_max = fs / 2 | Substitute: f_max = 22 / 2 | Answer: 11 kHz

question: A simply supported beam of span 8.5 m carries a central point load of 85 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 8.5, W = 85 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 85*8.5 / 4 | Answer: 180.6 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 3.3 m carries a UDL of 30 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.3, w = 30 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 30*(3.3)^2 / 8 | Answer: 40.84 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 4 m carries a point load 10 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4, W = 10 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 10*4 | Answer: 40 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 1.4 m carries a UDL of 14 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 1.4, w = 14 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 14*(1.4)^2 / 2 | Answer: 13.72 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.3 m carries a point load 40 kN at distance 2.4 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 4.3, a = 2.4, W = 40 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 40*(4.3 - 2.4) / 4.3 | Answer: 17.67 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 3.8 m) carries a central point load 15 kN. With E = 25 GPa and I = 400e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=15000 N, L=3800.0 mm, E=25000 MPa, I=400e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 1.715 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 6.4 m carries a UDL of 45 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6.4, w = 45 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 45*(6.4)^2 / 12 | Answer: 153.6 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 370 mm, clear cover 35 mm and main bars of diameter 16 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 370, c = 35, dia = 16 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 370 - 35 - 16/2 | Answer: 327 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 10.5 m^2 carrying a factored load of 19.8 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 10.5, w = 19.8 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 19.8 * 10.5 | Answer: 207.9 kN

question: For a bar of diameter 25 mm with design bond stress 1.4 MPa and steel stress 395 MPa, find the development length in mm.
solution: Given: dia = 25, tbd = 1.4, fs = 395 | Formula: Ld = phi fs / (4 tau_bd) | Substitute: Ld = 25*395 / (4*1.4) | Answer: 1763 mm

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 4.2 m, unit weight 19 kN/m^3, phi = 31 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 5.8 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 19 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 5.8, g = 19 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (19 - 9.81)*5.8 | Answer: 53.3 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 2.8e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1, area = 3.6e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 2.8, i = 1, A = 3.6 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (2.8e-4)*1*(3.6e-3) | Answer: 1008 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 2.4 m, bed slope 0.005 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.03. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 2.4 m under a head of 0.9 m. Taking Cd = 0.61 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 2.1 m wide carries a discharge of 10.5 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 450 m and design speed 85 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 450, V = 85 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (85)^2 / (127*450) | Answer: 0.1264
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: For a design speed of 45 km/h with allowable superelevation 0.06 and lateral friction 0.13, find the minimum curve radius in m.
A tank of volume 170 m^3 treats a flow of 90 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 170, Q = 90 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 170 / 90 | Answer: 1.889 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 370 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.18 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 8 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 370, k = 0.18, t = 8 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 370*(1 - e^(-0.18*8)) | Answer: 282.3 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.69, rainfall intensity 65 mm/h over a catchment of 51.6 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.69, i = 65, A = 51.6 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.69*65*51.6 / 360 | Answer: 6.428 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.07 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 220 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.07, M = 220 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 220*(20+0.07)/20 | Answer: 220.8 m

question: Convert the decimal number 249 to binary.
solution: Divide 249 by 2 repeatedly, recording remainders | Reading remainders in reverse gives 11111001 | Answer: 11111001 (binary)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 2 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the decimal number 138 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 138 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 8A (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the 8-bit binary number 01111110 to decimal.
solution: Binary 01111110 = sum of bit-weights | Answer: 126 (decimal)
formula: Sum each bit times its positional weight (2^i)

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 01101100 and 00001100.
solution: XOR: 01100000 | Count of 1s = 2 | Answer: 2
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 360 megabits is sent over a link of 20 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 360, B = 20 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 360 / 20 | Answer: 18 s

question: A link has bandwidth 77 Mbps and round-trip time 80 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 77, R = 80 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 77e6 * 80e-3 bits = 6160 kb | Answer: 6160 kilobits

question: A channel has bandwidth 16 kHz. Using Nyquist's theorem with 8 signal levels, find the maximum data rate in kbps (noiseless).
solution: Given: B = 16, M = 8 | Formula: C = 2 B log2(M) | Substitute: C = 2*16*log2(8) | Answer: 96 kbps

question: A channel of bandwidth 8 kHz has a signal-to-noise ratio of 31 (linear). Using Shannon's theorem, find the channel capacity in kbps.
solution: Given: B = 8, SNR = 31 | Formula: C = B log2(1 + SNR) | Substitute: C = 8*log2(1 + 31) | Answer: 40 kbps

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.81, cache access time 10 ns and main-memory access time 50 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.81, tc = 10, tm = 50 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.81*10 + (1 - 0.81)*50 | Answer: 17.6 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 799595 elements?
solution: Given: n = 799595 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(799595)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: An O(n^2) algorithm performs c*n^2 basic operations. If c = 1 and n = 1670, how many operations are performed?
solution: Given: n = 1670 | Formula: operations = n^2 | Substitute: = (1670)^2 | Answer: 2788900

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.018, memory access time 190 ns and page-fault service time 5 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 5 ms = 5000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.018)*190 + 0.018*5000000.0 ns | Answer: 90.19 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: A modem transmits at 3300 baud using 4-level signalling. Find the bit rate in bps.
solution: Given: baud = 3300, M = 4 | Formula: bit rate = baud * log2(M) | Substitute: bit rate = 3300 * log2(4) | Answer: 6600 bps

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 2.1 m^3 at 160 kPa and 340 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 2.1, P = 160, Tk = 340 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (160e3)*2.1 / (8.314*340) | Answer: 118.9 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.12 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 14 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.12, t = 14 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.12*14) | Answer: 0.8136

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.25 /min) is to reach 50% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.25, X = 50 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.5) / 0.25 | Answer: 2.773 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.2 /min) reaches 60% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.2, X = 60 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.6 / (0.2*(1 - 0.6)) | Answer: 7.5 min

question: A first-order reaction has a rate constant of 0.02 /min. Find its half-life in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.02 | Formula: t_half = ln(2) / k | Substitute: t_half = 0.6931 / 0.02 | Answer: 34.66 min

question: For a reaction with A = 3e10 /s and activation energy 75 kJ/mol at 440 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 3, Ea = 75, Tk = 440 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 3e10 * exp(-75e3 / (8.314*440)) | Answer: 37.43 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.97 and bottoms xW = 0.06, with relative volatility alpha = 2.9. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.97, xw = 0.06, al = 2.9 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.97/0.03)(0.94/0.06)] / ln(2.9) | Answer: 5.849 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.69 and x = 0.38. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.69, x = 0.38 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.69/0.31) / (0.38/0.62) | Answer: 3.632

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.56 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 65 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.56, Psat = 65 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.56 * 65 | Answer: 36.4 kPa

question: A stream of 8.3 kg/s with specific heat 1.3 kJ/kg-K is heated through 90 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 8.3, cp = 1.3, dT = 90 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 8.3*1.3*90 | Answer: 971.1 kW

question: A reactor of volume 12.5 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 3.5 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 12.5, Q = 3.5 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 12.5 / 3.5 | Answer: 3.571 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 5.2e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 5 mm with a concentration difference of 190 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 5.2, L = 5, dC = 190 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (5.2e-9)*190 / (5e-3) | Answer: 197.6 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 2.2 min and steady-state gain 1.7. For a step input of magnitude 17, find the final (steady-state) change in output.

question: A measurement reads 10.03 when the true value is 50. Find the percentage error.

question: Annual demand is 29500 units, ordering cost 120 per order and holding cost 16 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).

question: Evaluate the number of combinations C(13, 13).

question: Find the 26th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -11 and common difference 8.

question: A first-order system has a time constant of 4.4 s. Find the time (in s) to reach 63.2% of its final value.

question: A signal is sampled at 132 kHz. According to the Nyquist criterion, what is the maximum signal frequency that can be represented (in kHz)?

question: A simply supported beam of span 3.4 m carries a central point load of 35 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.

question: A simply supported beam of span 8.4 m carries a UDL of 50 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.

question: A cantilever of length 3.1 m carries a point load 5 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.

question: A cantilever of length 1.6 m carries a UDL of 16 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 1.6, w = 16 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 16*(1.6)^2 / 2 | Answer: 20.48 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.5 m carries a point load 40 kN at distance 2.6 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 6.5, a = 2.6, W = 40 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 40*(6.5 - 2.6) / 6.5 | Answer: 24 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 4.1 m) carries a central point load 15 kN. With E = 30 GPa and I = 110e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.

question: A fixed beam of span 5.7 m carries a UDL of 21 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.7, w = 21 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 21*(5.7)^2 / 12 | Answer: 56.86 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 340 mm, clear cover 40 mm and main bars of diameter 16 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.

question: A column supports a floor area of 24.2 m^2 carrying a factored load of 16.2 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 24.2, w = 16.2 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 16.2 * 24.2 | Answer: 392 kN

question: For a bar of diameter 25 mm with design bond stress 1.6 MPa and steel stress 360 MPa, find the development length in mm.

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 4.3 m, unit weight 16 kN/m^3, phi = 37 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).

question: At a depth of 6.9 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 20 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 4.2e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.8, area = 7.2e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.

question: For a design speed of 80 km/h with allowable superelevation 0.08 and lateral friction 0.16, find the minimum curve radius in m.

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 270 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.28 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 4 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 270, k = 0.28, t = 4 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 270*(1 - e^(-0.28*4)) | Answer: 181.9 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.34, rainfall intensity 35 mm/h over a catchment of 45.3 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
