question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 5 and 56.
solution: Given: a = 5, b = 56 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 5*56 / 1 | Answer: 280
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 22 mm carries an axial tensile load of 99 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 25 mm and length 2000 mm carries an axial load of 50 kN. Take E = 110 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 27 mm transmits a torque of 2500 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 27, Tt = 2500 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(2500*1000) / (pi*(27)^3) | Answer: 646.9 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 28 mm and length 600 mm carries a torque of 900 N-m. With G = 80 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (28)^4 / 32 = 60344 mm^4 | theta = (900*1000)(600) / (80000 * 60344) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 6.409 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 100 mm wide and 240 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 100, h = 240 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 100*(240)^2 / 6 | Answer: 960000 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (66 mm x 190 mm) carries a bending moment of 17 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (59 mm x 160 mm) has effective length 1500 mm and E = 200 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 640 MPa is designed for a working stress of 160 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 640, sw = 160 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 640 / 160 | Answer: 4

question: A steel bar is fully restrained and heated through 40 deg C. With E = 210 GPa and alpha = 12e-6 /deg C, find the thermal stress in MPa.
solution: Given: dT = 40, E = 210, al = 12 | Formula: sigma = E alpha (dT) | Substitute: sigma = 210000 * 12e-6 * 40 | Answer: 100.8 MPa

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 400 mm and wall thickness 20 mm carries an internal pressure of 1.3 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 400, t = 20, P = 1.3 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 1.3*400 / (2*20) | Answer: 13 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 1040 K and 300 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 1040, Tc = 300 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 300/1040) * 100 | Answer: 71.15 %

question: A refrigerator works between 251 K (cold) and 322 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 251, Th = 322 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 251 / (322 - 251) | Answer: 3.535

question: A heat pump operates between 282 K and 318 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 282, Th = 318 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 318 / (318 - 282) | Answer: 8.833

question: 4.7 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 25 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.7, dT = 25 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 4.7 * 0.718 * 25 | Answer: 84.36 kJ

question: 6.9 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 75 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 6.9, dT = 75 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 6.9 * 1.005 * 75 | Answer: 520.1 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 1.8 m^3 at 480 K with mass 5.6 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 1.8, Tk = 480, m = 5.6 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 5.6*0.287*480 / 1.8 | Answer: 428.6 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 4.4 kg of air expands isothermally at 380 K from volume V1 to 4*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.4, Tk = 380, ratio = 4 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 4.4*0.287*380*ln(4) | Answer: 665.2 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 3.7 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.05 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 3.7, D = 0.05 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*3.7*0.05 / 0.001 | Answer: 185000

question: Water flows at 3.4 m/s through a pipe of diameter 90 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 5.7 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 5.7 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*5.7 / 1000 | Answer: 55.92 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 10.1 m. Taking Cv = 0.96, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 10.1, cv = 0.96 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.96*sqrt(2*9.81*10.1) | Answer: 13.51 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 340 mm) water flows at 0.9 m/s. It contracts to diameter 120 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
Water flows at 3.9 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.2 m and length 450 m. With friction factor f = 0.032, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 19 teeth drives a gear of 119 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1350 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 19, z2 = 119, N1 = 1350 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1350*19 / 119 | Answer: 215.5 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 370 mm rotates at 1400 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 370, N = 1400 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.37)*1400 / 60 | Answer: 27.12 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 44.9 kW at 600 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 44.9, N = 600 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(44.9*1000) / (2*pi*600) | Answer: 714.6 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 4.5 kg rotates at radius 0.45 m at 550 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 3100 N/m and mass 10 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 3100, m = 10 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(3100/10) | Answer: 2.802 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 4.7 m^2 and thickness 0.28 m has conductivity k = 37.2 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 105 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 4.7, L = 0.28, k = 37.2, dT = 105 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 37.2*4.7*105 / 0.28 | Answer: 65565 W

question: A surface of area 5.8 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 20 W/m^2-K to surroundings 140 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 5.8, h = 20, dT = 140 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 20*5.8*140 | Answer: 16240 W

question: In a counter-flow heat exchanger the terminal temperature differences are 70 deg C and 15 deg C. Find the log mean temperature difference (LMTD) in deg C.
solution: Given: dT1 = 70, dT2 = 15 | Formula: LMTD = (dT1 - dT2) / ln(dT1/dT2) | Substitute: LMTD = (70 - 15) / ln(70/15) | Answer: 35.7 deg C

question: In turning, cutting speed = 210 m/min, feed = 0.18 mm/rev, depth of cut = 0.9 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 210, f = 0.18, d = 0.9 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*210*0.18*0.9 | Answer: 34020 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 210 mm is turned at 250 rpm with a feed of 0.17 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 210, N = 250, f = 0.17 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 210 / (0.17*250) | Answer: 4.941 min

question: A resistor of 28 ohm carries a current of 1.5 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 28, I = 1.5 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 1.5 * 28 | Answer: 42 V

question: Three resistors 91 ohm, 12 ohm and 15 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 91, R2 = 12, R3 = 15 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 91 + 12 + 15 | Answer: 118 ohm

question: Two resistors 41 ohm and 111 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 41, R2 = 111 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 41*111 / (41+111) | Answer: 29.94 ohm

question: A device draws 8.1 A at 125 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 125, I = 8.1 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 125 * 8.1 | Answer: 1012 W

question: A current of 5.1 A flows through a 133 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 5.1, R = 133 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (5.1)^2 * 133 | Answer: 3459 W

question: Two capacitors 3.2 uF and 36.8 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 3.2, C2 = 36.8 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 3.2*36.8 / (3.2+36.8) | Answer: 2.944 uF

question: A resistor 99 kohm and capacitor 4.3 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 99, C = 4.3 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (99k)(4.3u) = 425.7 ms | Answer: 425.7 ms

question: An inductor 244 mH is in series with 168 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 244, R = 168 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (244e-3) / 168 | Answer: 1.452 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 24.3 mH inductor at 540 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 24.3, f = 540 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (540)(24.3e-3) | Answer: 82.45 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 33.6 uF capacitor at 710 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 33.6, f = 710 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (710)(33.6e-6)) | Answer: 6.671 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 25 ohm, XL = 116 ohm and XC = 127 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 25, XL = 116, XC = 127 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(25^2 + (116 - 127)^2) | Answer: 27.31 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 33.5 mH and C = 3.8 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 33.5, C = 3.8 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(33.5e-3 * 3.8e-6)) | Answer: 446.1 Hz

question: A capacitor of 89.7 uF is charged to 70 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 89.7, V = 70 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*89.7e-6*(70)^2 | Answer: 219.8 mJ

question: An alternating voltage has a peak value of 64 V. Find its RMS value.
solution: Given: Vp = 64 | Formula: Vrms = Vp / sqrt(2) | Substitute: Vrms = 64 / sqrt(2) | Answer: 45.25 V

question: A transformer has primary voltage 270 V with 680 primary turns and 40 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 270, N1 = 680, N2 = 40 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 270 * 40/680 | Answer: 15.88 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 230 V and draws an armature current of 29 A. If the armature resistance is 1.09 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 230, Ia = 29, Ra = 1.09 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 230 - 29*1.09 | Answer: 198.4 V

question: A 4-pole induction motor on a 50 Hz supply runs at 1120 rpm. Find the slip (%).
formula: s = (Ns - N) / Ns,  Ns = 120 f / P

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 200 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.84. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 200, VL = 400, pf = 0.84 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*400*200*0.84 / 1000 | Answer: 116.4 kW

question: A load has real power 115 kW and apparent power 200 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 115, S = 200 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 115 / 200 | Answer: 0.575

question: A machine delivers 45 kW output while drawing 107 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 45, Pi = 107 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 45/107 * 100 | Answer: 42.06 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 11 V across R1 = 13 ohm and R2 = 22 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 11, R1 = 13, R2 = 22 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 11*22 / (13+22) | Answer: 6.914 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 110 kohm and Rin = 37 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 110, Rin = 37 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 110 / 37 | Answer: 2.973

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 120 kohm and Rg = 35 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 120, Rg = 35 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 120/35 | Answer: 4.429

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 9933. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 9933 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(9933) | Answer: 39.97 dB

question: A first-order system has a time constant of 5.8 s. Find the time (in s) to reach 63.2% of its final value.
solution: For a first-order step response, y = 1 - e^(-t/tau) | y = 0.632 when t = tau | Answer: 5.8 s
formula: At t = tau the response reaches 63.2% (one time constant)

question: A signal is sampled at 40 kHz. According to the Nyquist criterion, what is the maximum signal frequency that can be represented (in kHz)?
solution: Given: fs = 40 | Formula: f_max = fs / 2 | Substitute: f_max = 40 / 2 | Answer: 20 kHz

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.2 m carries a central point load of 75 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.2, W = 75 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 75*4.2 / 4 | Answer: 78.75 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.7 m carries a UDL of 60 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 9.7, w = 60 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 60*(9.7)^2 / 8 | Answer: 705.7 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 1.2 m carries a point load 65 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 1.2, W = 65 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 65*1.2 | Answer: 78 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 3.8 m carries a UDL of 8 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.8, w = 8 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 8*(3.8)^2 / 2 | Answer: 57.76 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.9 m carries a point load 70 kN at distance 2 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 6.9, a = 2, W = 70 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 70*(6.9 - 2) / 6.9 | Answer: 49.71 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 4.8 m) carries a central point load 25 kN. With E = 25 GPa and I = 400e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=25000 N, L=4800.0 mm, E=25000 MPa, I=400e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 5.76 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 5.5 m carries a UDL of 42 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.5, w = 42 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 42*(5.5)^2 / 12 | Answer: 105.9 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 660 mm, clear cover 25 mm and main bars of diameter 20 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 660, c = 25, dia = 20 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 660 - 25 - 20/2 | Answer: 625 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 11.2 m^2 carrying a factored load of 17.3 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 11.2, w = 17.3 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 17.3 * 11.2 | Answer: 193.8 kN

question: For a bar of diameter 25 mm with design bond stress 2.2 MPa and steel stress 360 MPa, find the development length in mm.
solution: Given: dia = 25, tbd = 2.2, fs = 360 | Formula: Ld = phi fs / (4 tau_bd) | Substitute: Ld = 25*360 / (4*2.2) | Answer: 1023 mm

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 5.9 m, unit weight 18 kN/m^3, phi = 30 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 2.8 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 21 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 2.8, g = 21 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (21 - 9.81)*2.8 | Answer: 31.33 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 3.4e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1.3, area = 4.4e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 3.4, i = 1.3, A = 4.4 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (3.4e-4)*1.3*(4.4e-3) | Answer: 1945 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.3 m, bed slope 0.01 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.017. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 1.2 m under a head of 0.6 m. Taking Cd = 0.61 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 5.1 m wide carries a discharge of 26.2 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 530 m and design speed 85 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 530, V = 85 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (85)^2 / (127*530) | Answer: 0.1073
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: For a design speed of 50 km/h with allowable superelevation 0.08 and lateral friction 0.15, find the minimum curve radius in m.
A tank of volume 790 m^3 treats a flow of 105 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 790, Q = 105 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 790 / 105 | Answer: 7.524 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 180 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.27 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 5 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 180, k = 0.27, t = 5 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 180*(1 - e^(-0.27*5)) | Answer: 133.3 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.63, rainfall intensity 60 mm/h over a catchment of 45.2 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.63, i = 60, A = 45.2 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.63*60*45.2 / 360 | Answer: 4.746 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.07 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 120 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.07, M = 120 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 120*(20+0.07)/20 | Answer: 120.4 m

question: Convert the decimal number 160 to binary.
solution: Divide 160 by 2 repeatedly, recording remainders | Reading remainders in reverse gives 10100000 | Answer: 10100000 (binary)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 2 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the decimal number 3898 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 3898 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: F3A (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the 8-bit binary number 00000110 to decimal.
solution: Binary 00000110 = sum of bit-weights | Answer: 6 (decimal)
formula: Sum each bit times its positional weight (2^i)

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 11010111 and 10000000.
solution: XOR: 01010111 | Count of 1s = 5 | Answer: 5
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 990 megabits is sent over a link of 66 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 990, B = 66 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 990 / 66 | Answer: 15 s

question: A link has bandwidth 89 Mbps and round-trip time 90 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 89, R = 90 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 89e6 * 90e-3 bits = 8010 kb | Answer: 8010 kilobits

question: A channel has bandwidth 14 kHz. Using Nyquist's theorem with 8 signal levels, find the maximum data rate in kbps (noiseless).
solution: Given: B = 14, M = 8 | Formula: C = 2 B log2(M) | Substitute: C = 2*14*log2(8) | Answer: 84 kbps

question: A channel of bandwidth 14 kHz has a signal-to-noise ratio of 255 (linear). Using Shannon's theorem, find the channel capacity in kbps.
solution: Given: B = 14, SNR = 255 | Formula: C = B log2(1 + SNR) | Substitute: C = 14*log2(1 + 255) | Answer: 112 kbps

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.86, cache access time 4 ns and main-memory access time 180 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.86, tc = 4, tm = 180 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.86*4 + (1 - 0.86)*180 | Answer: 28.64 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 166944 elements?
solution: Given: n = 166944 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(166944)) + 1 | Answer: 18

question: An O(n^2) algorithm performs c*n^2 basic operations. If c = 1 and n = 920, how many operations are performed?
solution: Given: n = 920 | Formula: operations = n^2 | Substitute: = (920)^2 | Answer: 846400

question: A program is 60% parallelisable and run on 4 processors. Using Amdahl's law, find the maximum speedup.
solution: Parallel fraction f = 0.6 | S = 1 / ((1 - 0.6) + 0.6/4) | Answer: 1.818x speedup

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.015, memory access time 180 ns and page-fault service time 7 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 7 ms = 7000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.015)*180 + 0.015*7000000.0 ns | Answer: 105.2 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: A modem transmits at 1200 baud using 2-level signalling. Find the bit rate in bps.
solution: Given: baud = 1200, M = 2 | Formula: bit rate = baud * log2(M) | Substitute: bit rate = 1200 * log2(2) | Answer: 1200 bps

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 2.7 m^3 at 380 kPa and 370 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 2.7, P = 380, Tk = 370 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (380e3)*2.7 / (8.314*370) | Answer: 333.5 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.23 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 18 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.23, t = 18 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.23*18) | Answer: 0.9841

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.26 /min) is to reach 55% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.26, X = 55 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.55) / 0.26 | Answer: 3.071 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.32 /min) reaches 90% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.32, X = 90 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.9 / (0.32*(1 - 0.9)) | Answer: 28.13 min

question: For a reaction with A = 7e10 /s and activation energy 80 kJ/mol at 470 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 7, Ea = 80, Tk = 470 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 7e10 * exp(-80e3 / (8.314*470)) | Answer: 89.9 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.91 and bottoms xW = 0.03, with relative volatility alpha = 2.1. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.91, xw = 0.03, al = 2.1 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.91/0.09)(0.97/0.03)] / ln(2.1) | Answer: 7.804 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.72 and x = 0.23. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.72, x = 0.23 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.72/0.28) / (0.23/0.77) | Answer: 8.609

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.63 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 105 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.63, Psat = 105 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.63 * 105 | Answer: 66.15 kPa

question: A stream of 6.5 kg/s with specific heat 2.9 kJ/kg-K is heated through 20 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 6.5, cp = 2.9, dT = 20 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 6.5*2.9*20 | Answer: 377 kW

question: A reactor of volume 1.4 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 4.3 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 1.4, Q = 4.3 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 1.4 / 4.3 | Answer: 0.3256 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 2.4e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 1 mm with a concentration difference of 180 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 2.4, L = 1, dC = 180 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (2.4e-9)*180 / (1e-3) | Answer: 432 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 8.2 min and steady-state gain 3.6. For a step input of magnitude 17, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 8.2, K = 3.6, M = 17 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 3.6 * 17 | Answer: 61.2 units

question: A reactor operates at a space time of 6.5 min. Find its space velocity in per hour.
solution: Given: tau = 6.5 | Formula: SV = 60 / tau  (per hour) | Substitute: SV = 60 / 6.5 | Answer: 9.231 /h

question: An aircraft wing of area 100 m^2 flies at 180 m/s (air density 0.7 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 1.3. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 100, V = 180, rho = 0.7, CL = 1.3 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.7*(180)^2*100*1.3 / 1000 | Answer: 1474 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 110 m^2 flies at 70 m/s (density 0.4 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.05. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 110, V = 70, rho = 0.4, CD = 0.05 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.4*(70)^2*110*0.05 / 1000 | Answer: 5.39 kN

question: Find the dynamic pressure for air of density 1.225 kg/m^3 moving at 60 m/s, in Pa.
solution: Given: rho = 1.225, V = 60 | Formula: q = 0.5 rho V^2 | Substitute: q = 0.5*1.225*(60)^2 | Answer: 2205 Pa

question: An aircraft flies at 560 m/s where the speed of sound is 295 m/s. Find the Mach number.
solution: Given: V = 560, a = 295 | Formula: M = V / a | Substitute: M = 560 / 295 | Answer: 1.898

question: Find the circular orbital velocity of a satellite at altitude 800 km above Earth (Earth radius 6371 km, mu = 3.986e14 m^3/s^2), in km/s.
A specimen under stress 320 MPa shows an elastic strain of 2.6e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 320, eps = 2.6 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 320 / (2.6e-3) MPa = 123.1 GPa | Answer: 123.1 GPa

question: A block of mass 43 kg has a volume of 4.9e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 43, V = 4.9 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 43 / (4.9e-3) | Answer: 8776 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 2600 mm is heated through 110 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 23e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 2600, dT = 110, al = 23 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 2600*23e-6*110 | Answer: 6.578 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 200 ohm, R2 = 65 ohm and R3 = 410 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 200, R2 = 65, R3 = 410 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 65*410 / 200 | Answer: 133.2 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 1000 ohm and gauge factor 2.1 experiences a strain of 1750e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 1000, GF = 2.1, eps = 1750 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 1000*2.1*1750e-6 | Answer: 3675 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 9.89 when the true value is 20. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.89, true = 20 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.89 - 20| / 20 * 100 | Answer: 50.55 %

question: Annual demand is 39000 units, ordering cost 240 per order and holding cost 18 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 39000, S = 240, H = 18 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*39000*240 / 18) | Answer: 102 units

question: An asset costs 460000 with salvage value 40000 after 16 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 460000, Sv = 40000, n = 16 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (460000 - 40000) / 16 | Answer: 26250 per year

question: A product sells for 130 per unit with variable cost 120 per unit and fixed costs 90000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 130, V = 120, F = 90000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 90000 / (130 - 120) | Answer: 9000 units

question: Find the present worth of 45000 received 7 years from now at an interest rate of 10% per year.
solution: Given: F = 45000, n = 7, i = 10 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 45000 / (1 + 0.1)^7 | Answer: 23092 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.95, 0.95 and 0.98 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.95, r2 = 0.95, r3 = 0.98 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.95*0.95*0.98 | Answer: 0.8844

question: A process produces 12 defective items in a batch of 17500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 12, N = 17500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 12/17500 * 1e6 | Answer: 685.7 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -5x^3 + 2x^2 - 6x + 5 evaluated at x = 1.
For f(x) = -3x^3 + 2x^2 + 8x, find f''(x) at x = 2.
Evaluate the definite integral of (-3x^2 - 6x + 4) dx from x = -1 to x = 5.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = -3x^3/3 + -6x^2/2 + 4x | Evaluate F(5) - F(-1) | Answer: -174
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 5x^2 + 4x = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[9, -5], [6, 7]].
solution: Given: a = 9, b = -5, c = 6, d = 7 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (9)(7) - (-5)(6) | Answer: 93

question: Find the determinant of [[-5, -6, 3], [-4, 3, -1], [2, 4, 1]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: -113

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[-1, 8], [4, 0]].
solution: Trace tr = -1, Determinant = -32 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 5.179

question: Solve for x: -2x + 5y = -6 and 3x + 6y = 0.
solution: Determinant = -2*6 - 5*3 = -27 | x = (e d - b f) / det = 1.333 | Answer: x = 1.333
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 41, 85, 74, 74, 18.
solution: Sum = 292 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 58.4 | Answer: 58.4

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 19, 20, 42, 35, 19.
solution: Mean = 27 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 10.79

question: Find the slope of the line through (-5, 2) and (-2, -3).
Find the distance between the points (2, -9) and (-7, -4).
solution: Given: x1 = 2, y1 = -9, x2 = -7, y2 = -4 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-9)^2 + (5)^2) | Answer: 10.3 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (-8,-3), (0,4), (-7,0).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 8.5 sq units

question: Evaluate the number of combinations C(7, 6).
solution: Given: n = 7, r = 6 | Formula: C(n, r) = n! / (r! (n - r)!) | Substitute: C(7, 6) = 7! / (6! * 1!) | Answer: 7

question: Evaluate the number of permutations P(14, 3).
solution: Given: n = 14, r = 3 | Formula: P(n, r) = n! / (n - r)! | Substitute: P(14, 3) = 14! / 11! | Answer: 2184

question: Find the 32th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -9 and common difference -8.
solution: Given: a = -9, d = -8, n = 32 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -9 + (32 - 1)*-8 | Answer: -257

question: Find the sum of the first 13 terms of an AP with first term -13 and common difference -7.
solution: Given: a = -13, d = -7, n = 13 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 13/2 [2*-13 + (13-1)*-7] | Answer: -715

question: Find the 8th term of a geometric progression with first term 3 and common ratio 4.
solution: Given: a = 3, r = 4, n = 8 | Formula: a_n = a r^(n-1) | Substitute: a_n = 3 * 4^(8-1) | Answer: 49152

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 46000 at 11.3% per annum for 2 years.
solution: Given: P = 46000, R = 11.3, Tt = 2 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 46000 * 11.3 * 2 / 100 | Answer: 10396 currency units

question: Find the amount when 11000 is invested at 10.5% per annum compounded annually for 6 years.
solution: Given: P = 11000, R = 10.5, Tt = 6 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 11000 * (1 + 10.5/100)^6 | Answer: 20025 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (1, 7, -8) and (-7, 0, 5).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (-6, 2, 3) and (6, 4, -5).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 43.86

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (3, 5, -2) and (2, -5, 5).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 129.8 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number 3 + 8i.
solution: Given: a = 3, b = 8 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((3)^2 + (8)^2) | Answer: 8.544

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number -8 + -8i.
solution: Given: a = -8, b = -8 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(-8, -8) | Answer: -135 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -4x^3 + 5x^2 - 8x + 4 at x = -1.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-12 with initial guess x0=13, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=2 and ordinates 3, 20, 18, 5, 19, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 161 and 67.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 161 and 67 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 51 and 37.
solution: Given: a = 51, b = 37 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 51*37 / 1 | Answer: 1887
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 32 mm carries an axial tensile load of 100 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 38 mm and length 800 mm carries an axial load of 40 kN. Take E = 70 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 45 mm transmits a torque of 1450 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 45, Tt = 1450 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(1450*1000) / (pi*(45)^3) | Answer: 81.04 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 27 mm and length 1700 mm carries a torque of 1450 N-m. With G = 80 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (27)^4 / 32 = 52174 mm^4 | theta = (1450*1000)(1700) / (80000 * 52174) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 33.84 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 34 mm wide and 280 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 34, h = 280 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 34*(280)^2 / 6 | Answer: 444267 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (114 mm x 230 mm) carries a bending moment of 5 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (71 mm x 90 mm) has effective length 3700 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 430 MPa is designed for a working stress of 220 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 430, sw = 220 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 430 / 220 | Answer: 1.955

question: A steel bar is fully restrained and heated through 100 deg C. With E = 210 GPa and alpha = 11e-6 /deg C, find the thermal stress in MPa.
solution: Given: dT = 100, E = 210, al = 11 | Formula: sigma = E alpha (dT) | Substitute: sigma = 210000 * 11e-6 * 100 | Answer: 231 MPa

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 300 mm and wall thickness 6 mm carries an internal pressure of 1.7 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 300, t = 6, P = 1.7 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 1.7*300 / (2*6) | Answer: 42.5 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 780 K and 360 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 780, Tc = 360 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 360/780) * 100 | Answer: 53.85 %

question: A refrigerator works between 262 K (cold) and 302 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 262, Th = 302 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 262 / (302 - 262) | Answer: 6.55

question: A heat pump operates between 285 K and 328 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 285, Th = 328 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 328 / (328 - 285) | Answer: 7.628

question: 2.3 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 35 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.3, dT = 35 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 2.3 * 0.718 * 35 | Answer: 57.8 kJ

question: 7.5 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 135 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 7.5, dT = 135 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 7.5 * 1.005 * 135 | Answer: 1018 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 3 m^3 at 300 K with mass 3.7 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 3, Tk = 300, m = 3.7 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 3.7*0.287*300 / 3 | Answer: 106.2 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 4.9 kg of air expands isothermally at 430 K from volume V1 to 4*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.9, Tk = 430, ratio = 4 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 4.9*0.287*430*ln(4) | Answer: 838.3 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 3.2 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.23 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 3.2, D = 0.23 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*3.2*0.23 / 0.001 | Answer: 736000

question: Water flows at 1.4 m/s through a pipe of diameter 220 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 20.2 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 20.2 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*20.2 / 1000 | Answer: 198.2 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 11.8 m. Taking Cv = 0.96, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 11.8, cv = 0.96 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.96*sqrt(2*9.81*11.8) | Answer: 14.61 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 180 mm) water flows at 0.7 m/s. It contracts to diameter 50 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 180, d2 = 50, V1 = 0.7 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 0.7*(180/50)^2 | Answer: 9.072 m/s

question: Water flows at 2.6 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.31 m and length 260 m. With friction factor f = 0.023, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 18 teeth drives a gear of 92 teeth. If the pinion runs at 800 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 18, z2 = 92, N1 = 800 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 800*18 / 92 | Answer: 156.5 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 200 mm rotates at 1400 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 200, N = 1400 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.2)*1400 / 60 | Answer: 14.66 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 17 kW at 1300 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 17, N = 1300 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(17*1000) / (2*pi*1300) | Answer: 124.9 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 0.9 kg rotates at radius 0.57 m at 450 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 15000 N/m and mass 15.8 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 15000, m = 15.8 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(15000/15.8) | Answer: 4.904 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 8.9 m^2 and thickness 0.17 m has conductivity k = 39.5 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 70 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 8.9, L = 0.17, k = 39.5, dT = 70 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 39.5*8.9*70 / 0.17 | Answer: 144756 W

question: A surface of area 1.3 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 155 W/m^2-K to surroundings 55 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 1.3, h = 155, dT = 55 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 155*1.3*55 | Answer: 11082 W

question: In a counter-flow heat exchanger the terminal temperature differences are 45 deg C and 30 deg C. Find the log mean temperature difference (LMTD) in deg C.
solution: Given: dT1 = 45, dT2 = 30 | Formula: LMTD = (dT1 - dT2) / ln(dT1/dT2) | Substitute: LMTD = (45 - 30) / ln(45/30) | Answer: 36.99 deg C

question: In turning, cutting speed = 90 m/min, feed = 0.17 mm/rev, depth of cut = 1.9 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 90, f = 0.17, d = 1.9 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*90*0.17*1.9 | Answer: 29070 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 430 mm is turned at 1050 rpm with a feed of 0.24 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 430, N = 1050, f = 0.24 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 430 / (0.24*1050) | Answer: 1.706 min

question: A resistor of 9 ohm carries a current of 0.7 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 9, I = 0.7 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 0.7 * 9 | Answer: 6.3 V

question: Three resistors 78 ohm, 96 ohm and 50 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 78, R2 = 96, R3 = 50 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 78 + 96 + 50 | Answer: 224 ohm

question: Two resistors 73 ohm and 18 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 73, R2 = 18 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 73*18 / (73+18) | Answer: 14.44 ohm

question: A device draws 11.6 A at 175 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 175, I = 11.6 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 175 * 11.6 | Answer: 2030 W

question: A current of 5.4 A flows through a 94 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 5.4, R = 94 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (5.4)^2 * 94 | Answer: 2741 W

question: Two capacitors 36.1 uF and 13.7 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 36.1, C2 = 13.7 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 36.1*13.7 / (36.1+13.7) | Answer: 9.931 uF

question: A resistor 70 kohm and capacitor 10.7 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 70, C = 10.7 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (70k)(10.7u) = 749 ms | Answer: 749 ms

question: An inductor 345.3 mH is in series with 60 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 345.3, R = 60 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (345.3e-3) / 60 | Answer: 5.755 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 126.7 mH inductor at 150 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 126.7, f = 150 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (150)(126.7e-3) | Answer: 119.4 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 2.6 uF capacitor at 690 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 2.6, f = 690 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (690)(2.6e-6)) | Answer: 88.72 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 83 ohm, XL = 115 ohm and XC = 125 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 83, XL = 115, XC = 125 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(83^2 + (115 - 125)^2) | Answer: 83.6 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 52.5 mH and C = 6.4 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 52.5, C = 6.4 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(52.5e-3 * 6.4e-6)) | Answer: 274.6 Hz

question: A capacitor of 31.2 uF is charged to 135 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 31.2, V = 135 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*31.2e-6*(135)^2 | Answer: 284.3 mJ

question: An alternating voltage has a peak value of 192 V. Find its RMS value.
solution: Given: Vp = 192 | Formula: Vrms = Vp / sqrt(2) | Substitute: Vrms = 192 / sqrt(2) | Answer: 135.8 V

question: A transformer has primary voltage 210 V with 680 primary turns and 460 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 210, N1 = 680, N2 = 460 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 210 * 460/680 | Answer: 142.1 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 120 V and draws an armature current of 28 A. If the armature resistance is 0.94 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 120, Ia = 28, Ra = 0.94 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 120 - 28*0.94 | Answer: 93.68 V

question: A 4-pole induction motor on a 60 Hz supply runs at 1140 rpm. Find the slip (%).
formula: s = (Ns - N) / Ns,  Ns = 120 f / P

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 105 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.71. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 105, VL = 400, pf = 0.71 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*400*105*0.71 / 1000 | Answer: 51.65 kW

question: A load has real power 50 kW and apparent power 95 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 50, S = 95 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 50 / 95 | Answer: 0.5263

question: A machine delivers 60 kW output while drawing 87 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 60, Pi = 87 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 60/87 * 100 | Answer: 68.97 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 5 V across R1 = 38 ohm and R2 = 15 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 5, R1 = 38, R2 = 15 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 5*15 / (38+15) | Answer: 1.415 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 40 kohm and Rin = 14 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 40, Rin = 14 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 40 / 14 | Answer: 2.857

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 180 kohm and Rg = 46 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 180, Rg = 46 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 180/46 | Answer: 4.913

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 5938. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 5938 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(5938) | Answer: 37.74 dB

question: A first-order system has a time constant of 7.1 s. Find the time (in s) to reach 63.2% of its final value.
solution: For a first-order step response, y = 1 - e^(-t/tau) | y = 0.632 when t = tau | Answer: 7.1 s
formula: At t = tau the response reaches 63.2% (one time constant)

question: A signal is sampled at 150 kHz. According to the Nyquist criterion, what is the maximum signal frequency that can be represented (in kHz)?
solution: Given: fs = 150 | Formula: f_max = fs / 2 | Substitute: f_max = 150 / 2 | Answer: 75 kHz

question: A simply supported beam of span 8.8 m carries a central point load of 100 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 8.8, W = 100 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 100*8.8 / 4 | Answer: 220 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 3.8 m carries a UDL of 55 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.8, w = 55 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 55*(3.8)^2 / 8 | Answer: 99.27 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 5.1 m carries a point load 30 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.1, W = 30 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 30*5.1 | Answer: 153 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 2.9 m carries a UDL of 22 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 2.9, w = 22 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 22*(2.9)^2 / 2 | Answer: 92.51 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 5 m carries a point load 50 kN at distance 1.1 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 5, a = 1.1, W = 50 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 50*(5 - 1.1) / 5 | Answer: 39 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 5.4 m) carries a central point load 45 kN. With E = 30 GPa and I = 250e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=45000 N, L=5400.0 mm, E=30000 MPa, I=250e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 19.68 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 8.3 m carries a UDL of 6 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 8.3, w = 6 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 6*(8.3)^2 / 12 | Answer: 34.45 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 340 mm, clear cover 30 mm and main bars of diameter 25 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 340, c = 30, dia = 25 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 340 - 30 - 25/2 | Answer: 297.5 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 11.6 m^2 carrying a factored load of 19.2 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 11.6, w = 19.2 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 19.2 * 11.6 | Answer: 222.7 kN

question: For a bar of diameter 20 mm with design bond stress 2 MPa and steel stress 395 MPa, find the development length in mm.
solution: Given: dia = 20, tbd = 2, fs = 395 | Formula: Ld = phi fs / (4 tau_bd) | Substitute: Ld = 20*395 / (4*2) | Answer: 987.5 mm

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 4.9 m, unit weight 19 kN/m^3, phi = 38 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 6.1 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 19 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 6.1, g = 19 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (19 - 9.81)*6.1 | Answer: 56.06 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 1.2e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1.4, area = 4.4e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 1.2, i = 1.4, A = 4.4 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (1.2e-4)*1.4*(4.4e-3) | Answer: 739.2 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.8 m, bed slope 0.003 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.018. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 4.4 m under a head of 0.7 m. Taking Cd = 0.62 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 2.7 m wide carries a discharge of 24.4 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 520 m and design speed 80 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 520, V = 80 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (80)^2 / (127*520) | Answer: 0.09691
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: For a design speed of 60 km/h with allowable superelevation 0.06 and lateral friction 0.13, find the minimum curve radius in m.
A tank of volume 240 m^3 treats a flow of 185 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 240, Q = 185 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 240 / 185 | Answer: 1.297 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 360 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.19 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 6 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 360, k = 0.19, t = 6 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 360*(1 - e^(-0.19*6)) | Answer: 244.9 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.49, rainfall intensity 60 mm/h over a catchment of 53.7 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.49, i = 60, A = 53.7 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.49*60*53.7 / 360 | Answer: 4.385 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.05 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 100 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.05, M = 100 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 100*(20+0.05)/20 | Answer: 100.2 m

question: Convert the decimal number 131 to binary.
solution: Divide 131 by 2 repeatedly, recording remainders | Reading remainders in reverse gives 10000011 | Answer: 10000011 (binary)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 2 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the decimal number 2682 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 2682 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: A7A (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the 8-bit binary number 00010110 to decimal.
solution: Binary 00010110 = sum of bit-weights | Answer: 22 (decimal)
formula: Sum each bit times its positional weight (2^i)

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 11100001 and 11111100.
solution: XOR: 00011101 | Count of 1s = 4 | Answer: 4
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 320 megabits is sent over a link of 27 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 320, B = 27 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 320 / 27 | Answer: 11.85 s

question: A link has bandwidth 52 Mbps and round-trip time 170 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 52, R = 170 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 52e6 * 170e-3 bits = 8840 kb | Answer: 8840 kilobits

question: A channel has bandwidth 13 kHz. Using Nyquist's theorem with 16 signal levels, find the maximum data rate in kbps (noiseless).
solution: Given: B = 13, M = 16 | Formula: C = 2 B log2(M) | Substitute: C = 2*13*log2(16) | Answer: 104 kbps

question: A channel of bandwidth 3 kHz has a signal-to-noise ratio of 15 (linear). Using Shannon's theorem, find the channel capacity in kbps.
solution: Given: B = 3, SNR = 15 | Formula: C = B log2(1 + SNR) | Substitute: C = 3*log2(1 + 15) | Answer: 12 kbps

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.86, cache access time 4 ns and main-memory access time 110 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.86, tc = 4, tm = 110 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.86*4 + (1 - 0.86)*110 | Answer: 18.84 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 282958 elements?
solution: Given: n = 282958 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(282958)) + 1 | Answer: 19

question: An O(n^2) algorithm performs c*n^2 basic operations. If c = 1 and n = 900, how many operations are performed?
solution: Given: n = 900 | Formula: operations = n^2 | Substitute: = (900)^2 | Answer: 810000

question: A program is 95% parallelisable and run on 2 processors. Using Amdahl's law, find the maximum speedup.
solution: Parallel fraction f = 0.95 | S = 1 / ((1 - 0.95) + 0.95/2) | Answer: 1.905x speedup

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.004, memory access time 80 ns and page-fault service time 10 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 10 ms = 10000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.004)*80 + 0.004*10000000.0 ns | Answer: 40.08 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 2.5 m^3 at 280 kPa and 460 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 2.5, P = 280, Tk = 460 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (280e3)*2.5 / (8.314*460) | Answer: 183 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.25 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 11 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.25, t = 11 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.25*11) | Answer: 0.9361

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.37 /min) is to reach 65% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.37, X = 65 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.65) / 0.37 | Answer: 2.837 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.33 /min) reaches 50% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.33, X = 50 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.5 / (0.33*(1 - 0.5)) | Answer: 3.03 min

question: For a reaction with A = 6e10 /s and activation energy 50 kJ/mol at 430 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 6, Ea = 50, Tk = 430 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 6e10 * exp(-50e3 / (8.314*430)) | Answer: 50598 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.97 and bottoms xW = 0.08, with relative volatility alpha = 2.7. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.97, xw = 0.08, al = 2.7 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.97/0.03)(0.92/0.08)] / ln(2.7) | Answer: 5.959 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.77 and x = 0.39. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.77, x = 0.39 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.77/0.23) / (0.39/0.61) | Answer: 5.236

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.29 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 75 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.29, Psat = 75 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.29 * 75 | Answer: 21.75 kPa

question: A stream of 6.1 kg/s with specific heat 1.5 kJ/kg-K is heated through 30 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 6.1, cp = 1.5, dT = 30 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 6.1*1.5*30 | Answer: 274.5 kW

question: A reactor of volume 18.7 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 0.6 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 18.7, Q = 0.6 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 18.7 / 0.6 | Answer: 31.17 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 2.3e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 2 mm with a concentration difference of 200 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 2.3, L = 2, dC = 200 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (2.3e-9)*200 / (2e-3) | Answer: 230 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 8.3 min and steady-state gain 0.7. For a step input of magnitude 12, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 8.3, K = 0.7, M = 12 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 0.7 * 12 | Answer: 8.4 units

question: A reactor operates at a space time of 0.6 min. Find its space velocity in per hour.
solution: Given: tau = 0.6 | Formula: SV = 60 / tau  (per hour) | Substitute: SV = 60 / 0.6 | Answer: 100 /h

question: An aircraft wing of area 35 m^2 flies at 120 m/s (air density 1 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.6. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 35, V = 120, rho = 1, CL = 0.6 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1*(120)^2*35*0.6 / 1000 | Answer: 151.2 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 30 m^2 flies at 190 m/s (density 1 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.08. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 30, V = 190, rho = 1, CD = 0.08 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*1*(190)^2*30*0.08 / 1000 | Answer: 43.32 kN

question: Find the dynamic pressure for air of density 1.225 kg/m^3 moving at 290 m/s, in Pa.
solution: Given: rho = 1.225, V = 290 | Formula: q = 0.5 rho V^2 | Substitute: q = 0.5*1.225*(290)^2 | Answer: 51511 Pa

question: An aircraft flies at 510 m/s where the speed of sound is 295 m/s. Find the Mach number.
solution: Given: V = 510, a = 295 | Formula: M = V / a | Substitute: M = 510 / 295 | Answer: 1.729

question: A specimen under stress 240 MPa shows an elastic strain of 2.3e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 240, eps = 2.3 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 240 / (2.3e-3) MPa = 104.3 GPa | Answer: 104.3 GPa

question: A block of mass 36 kg has a volume of 4.7e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 36, V = 4.7 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 36 / (4.7e-3) | Answer: 766 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 3000 mm is heated through 75 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 23e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 3000, dT = 75, al = 23 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 3000*23e-6*75 | Answer: 5.175 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 65 ohm, R2 = 150 ohm and R3 = 435 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 65, R2 = 150, R3 = 435 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 150*435 / 65 | Answer: 1004 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 1000 ohm and gauge factor 2.1 experiences a strain of 1300e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 1000, GF = 2.1, eps = 1300 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 1000*2.1*1300e-6 | Answer: 2730 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 10.45 when the true value is 50. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10.45, true = 50 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10.45 - 50| / 50 * 100 | Answer: 79.1 %

question: Annual demand is 5500 units, ordering cost 170 per order and holding cost 17 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 5500, S = 170, H = 17 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*5500*170 / 17) | Answer: 331.7 units

question: An asset costs 500000 with salvage value 2000 after 6 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 500000, Sv = 2000, n = 6 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (500000 - 2000) / 6 | Answer: 83000 per year

question: A product sells for 120 per unit with variable cost 110 per unit and fixed costs 130000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 120, V = 110, F = 130000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 130000 / (120 - 110) | Answer: 13000 units

question: Find the present worth of 75000 received 5 years from now at an interest rate of 9% per year.
solution: Given: F = 75000, n = 5, i = 9 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 75000 / (1 + 0.09)^5 | Answer: 48745 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.98, 0.94 and 0.92 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.98, r2 = 0.94, r3 = 0.92 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.98*0.94*0.92 | Answer: 0.8475

question: A process produces 36 defective items in a batch of 11000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 36, N = 11000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 36/11000 * 1e6 | Answer: 3273 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -4x^3 - 6x^2 + 4x + 3 evaluated at x = 4.
For f(x) = -3x^3 - 5x^2 - 5x - 8, find f''(x) at x = 1.

question: Find the larger real root of x^2 - 11x - 5 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[3, 4], [-3, 5]].
solution: Given: a = 3, b = 4, c = -3, d = 5 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (3)(5) - (4)(-3) | Answer: 27

question: Find the determinant of [[2, 0, -2], [-2, -4, -6], [5, 3, -3]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: 32

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[5, -1], [0, -1]].
solution: Trace tr = 4, Determinant = -5 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 5

question: Solve for x: 4x + -3y = 2 and 1x + 5y = 1.
solution: Determinant = 4*5 - -3*1 = 23 | x = (e d - b f) / det = 0.5652 | Answer: x = 0.5652

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 63, 77, 48, 22, 54.
solution: Sum = 264 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 52.8 | Answer: 52.8

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 17, 16, 27, 2, 26.
solution: Mean = 17.6 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 10.06

question: Find the slope of the line through (3, 2) and (0, -5).
solution: Given: x1 = 3, y1 = 2, x2 = 0, y2 = -5 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (-5 - 2) / (0 - 3) | Answer: 2.333

question: Find the distance between the points (0, -7) and (-9, 9).
solution: Given: x1 = 0, y1 = -7, x2 = -9, y2 = 9 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-9)^2 + (16)^2) | Answer: 18.36 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (-1,5), (-2,1), (0,6).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 1.5 sq units

question: Evaluate the number of combinations C(11, 4).
solution: Given: n = 11, r = 4 | Formula: C(n, r) = n! / (r! (n - r)!) | Substitute: C(11, 4) = 11! / (4! * 7!) | Answer: 330

question: Evaluate the number of permutations P(12, 7).
solution: Given: n = 12, r = 7 | Formula: P(n, r) = n! / (n - r)! | Substitute: P(12, 7) = 12! / 5! | Answer: 3991680

question: Find the 39th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 12 and common difference 9.
solution: Given: a = 12, d = 9, n = 39 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = 12 + (39 - 1)*9 | Answer: 354

question: Find the sum of the first 29 terms of an AP with first term 10 and common difference -6.
solution: Given: a = 10, d = -6, n = 29 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 29/2 [2*10 + (29-1)*-6] | Answer: -2146

question: Find the 4th term of a geometric progression with first term 5 and common ratio 2.
solution: Given: a = 5, r = 2, n = 4 | Formula: a_n = a r^(n-1) | Substitute: a_n = 5 * 2^(4-1) | Answer: 40

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 27000 at 14.2% per annum for 2 years.
solution: Given: P = 27000, R = 14.2, Tt = 2 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 27000 * 14.2 * 2 / 100 | Answer: 7668 currency units

question: Find the amount when 8500 is invested at 9.7% per annum compounded annually for 3 years.
solution: Given: P = 8500, R = 9.7, Tt = 3 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 8500 * (1 + 9.7/100)^3 | Answer: 11221 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (5, -2, 1) and (5, -5, -8).

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (1, 5, -4) and (3, 5, 5).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 49.13

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (1, 0, 4) and (-2, 6, -2).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 111.4 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number -12 + -2i.
solution: Given: a = -12, b = -2 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((-12)^2 + (-2)^2) | Answer: 12.17

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number -9 + 8i.
solution: Given: a = -9, b = 8 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(8, -9) | Answer: 138.4 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = 3x^3 + 2x^2 - 4x - 1 at x = -2.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-44 with initial guess x0=11, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=0.7 and ordinates 5, 20, 11, 14, 7, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 418 and 390.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 418 and 390 | Answer: GCD = 2

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 36 and 24.
solution: Given: a = 36, b = 24 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 36*24 / 12 | Answer: 72
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 39 mm carries an axial tensile load of 90 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 14 mm and length 900 mm carries an axial load of 56 kN. Take E = 210 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 54 mm transmits a torque of 1400 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 54, Tt = 1400 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(1400*1000) / (pi*(54)^3) | Answer: 45.28 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 55 mm and length 1500 mm carries a torque of 1350 N-m. With G = 77 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (55)^4 / 32 = 898361 mm^4 | theta = (1350*1000)(1500) / (77000 * 898361) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 1.677 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 75 mm wide and 180 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 75, h = 180 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 75*(180)^2 / 6 | Answer: 405000 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (101 mm x 130 mm) carries a bending moment of 30 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (47 mm x 130 mm) has effective length 2700 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 790 MPa is designed for a working stress of 240 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 790, sw = 240 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 790 / 240 | Answer: 3.292

question: A steel bar is fully restrained and heated through 50 deg C. With E = 210 GPa and alpha = 11e-6 /deg C, find the thermal stress in MPa.
solution: Given: dT = 50, E = 210, al = 11 | Formula: sigma = E alpha (dT) | Substitute: sigma = 210000 * 11e-6 * 50 | Answer: 115.5 MPa

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1350 mm and wall thickness 14 mm carries an internal pressure of 1.9 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1350, t = 14, P = 1.9 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 1.9*1350 / (2*14) | Answer: 91.61 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 1080 K and 370 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 1080, Tc = 370 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 370/1080) * 100 | Answer: 65.74 %

question: A refrigerator works between 251 K (cold) and 316 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 251, Th = 316 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 251 / (316 - 251) | Answer: 3.862

question: A heat pump operates between 278 K and 306 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 278, Th = 306 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 306 / (306 - 278) | Answer: 10.93

question: 7.6 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 185 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 7.6, dT = 185 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 7.6 * 0.718 * 185 | Answer: 101 kJ

question: 5.3 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 100 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 5.3, dT = 100 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 5.3 * 1.005 * 100 | Answer: 532.6 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 1.8 m^3 at 340 K with mass 1.9 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 1.8, Tk = 340, m = 1.9 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 1.9*0.287*340 / 1.8 | Answer: 103 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 1 kg of air expands isothermally at 450 K from volume V1 to 2*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1, Tk = 450, ratio = 2 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 1*0.287*450*ln(2) | Answer: 89.52 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 2.6 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.39 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 2.6, D = 0.39 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*2.6*0.39 / 0.001 | Answer: 1014000

question: Water flows at 2.4 m/s through a pipe of diameter 60 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 2.8 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 2.8 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*2.8 / 1000 | Answer: 27.47 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 13 m. Taking Cv = 0.98, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 13, cv = 0.98 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.98*sqrt(2*9.81*13) | Answer: 15.65 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 220 mm) water flows at 2 m/s. It contracts to diameter 80 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 220, d2 = 80, V1 = 2 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 2*(220/80)^2 | Answer: 15.12 m/s

question: Water flows at 3.5 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.18 m and length 460 m. With friction factor f = 0.038, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 35 teeth drives a gear of 59 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1250 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 35, z2 = 59, N1 = 1250 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1250*35 / 59 | Answer: 741.5 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 160 mm rotates at 650 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 160, N = 650 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.16)*650 / 60 | Answer: 5.445 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 49.2 kW at 1450 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 49.2, N = 1450 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(49.2*1000) / (2*pi*1450) | Answer: 324 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 7.2 kg rotates at radius 0.59 m at 950 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 15000 N/m and mass 4.2 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 15000, m = 4.2 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(15000/4.2) | Answer: 9.511 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 9.4 m^2 and thickness 0.27 m has conductivity k = 27.6 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 180 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 9.4, L = 0.27, k = 27.6, dT = 180 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 27.6*9.4*180 / 0.27 | Answer: 172960 W

question: A surface of area 2.1 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 70 W/m^2-K to surroundings 130 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 2.1, h = 70, dT = 130 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 70*2.1*130 | Answer: 19110 W

question: In a counter-flow heat exchanger the terminal temperature differences are 65 deg C and 5 deg C. Find the log mean temperature difference (LMTD) in deg C.
solution: Given: dT1 = 65, dT2 = 5 | Formula: LMTD = (dT1 - dT2) / ln(dT1/dT2) | Substitute: LMTD = (65 - 5) / ln(65/5) | Answer: 23.39 deg C

question: In turning, cutting speed = 160 m/min, feed = 0.46 mm/rev, depth of cut = 1.5 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 160, f = 0.46, d = 1.5 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*160*0.46*1.5 | Answer: 110400 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 490 mm is turned at 350 rpm with a feed of 0.24 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 490, N = 350, f = 0.24 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 490 / (0.24*350) | Answer: 5.833 min

question: A resistor of 164 ohm carries a current of 1.4 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 164, I = 1.4 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 1.4 * 164 | Answer: 229.6 V

question: Three resistors 98 ohm, 59 ohm and 90 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 98, R2 = 59, R3 = 90 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 98 + 59 + 90 | Answer: 247 ohm

question: Two resistors 11 ohm and 53 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 11, R2 = 53 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 11*53 / (11+53) | Answer: 9.109 ohm

question: A device draws 6.9 A at 80 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 80, I = 6.9 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 80 * 6.9 | Answer: 552 W

question: A current of 3.4 A flows through a 142 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 3.4, R = 142 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (3.4)^2 * 142 | Answer: 1642 W

question: Two capacitors 31.5 uF and 19 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 31.5, C2 = 19 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 31.5*19 / (31.5+19) | Answer: 11.85 uF

question: A resistor 89 kohm and capacitor 14.5 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 89, C = 14.5 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (89k)(14.5u) = 129 ms | Answer: 129 ms

question: An inductor 144.6 mH is in series with 68 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 144.6, R = 68 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (144.6e-3) / 68 | Answer: 2.126 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 46.1 mH inductor at 390 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 46.1, f = 390 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (390)(46.1e-3) | Answer: 113 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 39.5 uF capacitor at 500 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 39.5, f = 500 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (500)(39.5e-6)) | Answer: 8.058 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 12 ohm, XL = 92 ohm and XC = 103 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 12, XL = 92, XC = 103 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(12^2 + (92 - 103)^2) | Answer: 16.28 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 97.7 mH and C = 5.4 uF (in Hz).
