solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 284 and 365 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 13 and 63.
solution: Given: a = 13, b = 63 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 13*63 / 1 | Answer: 819
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 51 mm carries an axial tensile load of 110 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 33 mm and length 1200 mm carries an axial load of 16 kN. Take E = 70 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 49 mm transmits a torque of 2300 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 49, Tt = 2300 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(2300*1000) / (pi*(49)^3) | Answer: 99.57 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 56 mm and length 1500 mm carries a torque of 1750 N-m. With G = 77 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (56)^4 / 32 = 965499 mm^4 | theta = (1750*1000)(1500) / (77000 * 965499) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 2.023 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 46 mm wide and 70 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 46, h = 70 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 46*(70)^2 / 6 | Answer: 37567 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (76 mm x 180 mm) carries a bending moment of 7 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (48 mm x 150 mm) has effective length 3100 mm and E = 200 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 390 MPa is designed for a working stress of 100 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 390, sw = 100 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 390 / 100 | Answer: 3.9

question: A steel bar is fully restrained and heated through 80 deg C. With E = 210 GPa and alpha = 13e-6 /deg C, find the thermal stress in MPa.
solution: Given: dT = 80, E = 210, al = 13 | Formula: sigma = E alpha (dT) | Substitute: sigma = 210000 * 13e-6 * 80 | Answer: 218.4 MPa

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 700 mm and wall thickness 17 mm carries an internal pressure of 2.1 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 700, t = 17, P = 2.1 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 2.1*700 / (2*17) | Answer: 43.24 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 1000 K and 290 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 1000, Tc = 290 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 290/1000) * 100 | Answer: 71 %

question: A refrigerator works between 258 K (cold) and 322 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 258, Th = 322 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 258 / (322 - 258) | Answer: 4.031

question: A heat pump operates between 279 K and 324 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 279, Th = 324 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 324 / (324 - 279) | Answer: 7.2

question: 3.2 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 180 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.2, dT = 180 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 3.2 * 0.718 * 180 | Answer: 413.6 kJ

question: 5.7 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 190 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 5.7, dT = 190 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 5.7 * 1.005 * 190 | Answer: 1088 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 1.6 m^3 at 410 K with mass 1 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 1.6, Tk = 410, m = 1 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 1*0.287*410 / 1.6 | Answer: 73.54 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 3.6 kg of air expands isothermally at 410 K from volume V1 to 2*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.6, Tk = 410, ratio = 2 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 3.6*0.287*410*ln(2) | Answer: 293.6 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 3.5 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.11 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 3.5, D = 0.11 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*3.5*0.11 / 0.001 | Answer: 385000

question: Water flows at 3.8 m/s through a pipe of diameter 200 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 23.5 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 23.5 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*23.5 / 1000 | Answer: 230.5 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 7.8 m. Taking Cv = 0.97, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 7.8, cv = 0.97 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.97*sqrt(2*9.81*7.8) | Answer: 12 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 170 mm) water flows at 1.5 m/s. It contracts to diameter 110 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
Water flows at 1.5 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.45 m and length 160 m. With friction factor f = 0.038, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 15 teeth drives a gear of 93 teeth. If the pinion runs at 700 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 15, z2 = 93, N1 = 700 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 700*15 / 93 | Answer: 112.9 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 170 mm rotates at 200 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 170, N = 200 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.17)*200 / 60 | Answer: 1.78 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 49.2 kW at 1400 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 49.2, N = 1400 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(49.2*1000) / (2*pi*1400) | Answer: 335.6 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 6.4 kg rotates at radius 0.55 m at 500 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 19000 N/m and mass 8.3 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 19000, m = 8.3 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(19000/8.3) | Answer: 7.615 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 3 m^2 and thickness 0.3 m has conductivity k = 11.5 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 195 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 3, L = 0.3, k = 11.5, dT = 195 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 11.5*3*195 / 0.3 | Answer: 22425 W

question: A surface of area 3.3 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 15 W/m^2-K to surroundings 45 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 3.3, h = 15, dT = 45 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 15*3.3*45 | Answer: 2228 W

question: In a counter-flow heat exchanger the terminal temperature differences are 50 deg C and 15 deg C. Find the log mean temperature difference (LMTD) in deg C.
solution: Given: dT1 = 50, dT2 = 15 | Formula: LMTD = (dT1 - dT2) / ln(dT1/dT2) | Substitute: LMTD = (50 - 15) / ln(50/15) | Answer: 29.07 deg C

question: In turning, cutting speed = 250 m/min, feed = 0.23 mm/rev, depth of cut = 0.9 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 250, f = 0.23, d = 0.9 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*250*0.23*0.9 | Answer: 51750 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 280 mm is turned at 900 rpm with a feed of 0.26 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 280, N = 900, f = 0.26 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 280 / (0.26*900) | Answer: 1.197 min

question: A resistor of 125 ohm carries a current of 1.3 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 125, I = 1.3 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 1.3 * 125 | Answer: 162.5 V

question: Three resistors 73 ohm, 68 ohm and 41 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 73, R2 = 68, R3 = 41 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 73 + 68 + 41 | Answer: 182 ohm

question: Two resistors 28 ohm and 98 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 28, R2 = 98 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 28*98 / (28+98) | Answer: 21.78 ohm

question: A device draws 1.3 A at 35 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 35, I = 1.3 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 35 * 1.3 | Answer: 45.5 W

question: A current of 6.9 A flows through a 80 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 6.9, R = 80 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (6.9)^2 * 80 | Answer: 3809 W

question: Two capacitors 18.1 uF and 12.4 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 18.1, C2 = 12.4 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 18.1*12.4 / (18.1+12.4) | Answer: 7.359 uF

question: A resistor 71 kohm and capacitor 14.1 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 71, C = 14.1 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (71k)(14.1u) = 1001 ms | Answer: 1001 ms

question: An inductor 99 mH is in series with 78 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 99, R = 78 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (99e-3) / 78 | Answer: 1.269 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 50.9 mH inductor at 830 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 50.9, f = 830 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (830)(50.9e-3) | Answer: 265.4 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 15.3 uF capacitor at 70 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 15.3, f = 70 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (70)(15.3e-6)) | Answer: 148.6 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 34 ohm, XL = 56 ohm and XC = 14 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 34, XL = 56, XC = 14 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(34^2 + (56 - 14)^2) | Answer: 54.04 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 3.3 mH and C = 9.6 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 3.3, C = 9.6 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(3.3e-3 * 9.6e-6)) | Answer: 894.2 Hz

question: A capacitor of 42.8 uF is charged to 300 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 42.8, V = 300 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*42.8e-6*(300)^2 | Answer: 1926 mJ

question: An alternating voltage has a peak value of 326 V. Find its RMS value.
solution: Given: Vp = 326 | Formula: Vrms = Vp / sqrt(2) | Substitute: Vrms = 326 / sqrt(2) | Answer: 230.5 V

question: A transformer has primary voltage 120 V with 960 primary turns and 480 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 120, N1 = 960, N2 = 480 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 120 * 480/960 | Answer: 60 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 120 V and draws an armature current of 42 A. If the armature resistance is 1.37 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 120, Ia = 42, Ra = 1.37 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 120 - 42*1.37 | Answer: 62.46 V

question: A 4-pole induction motor on a 60 Hz supply runs at 800 rpm. Find the slip (%).
formula: s = (Ns - N) / Ns,  Ns = 120 f / P

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 190 A at 415 V (line) with a power factor of 0.98. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 190, VL = 415, pf = 0.98 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*415*190*0.98 / 1000 | Answer: 133.8 kW

question: A load has real power 25 kW and apparent power 215 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 25, S = 215 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 25 / 215 | Answer: 0.1163

question: A machine delivers 125 kW output while drawing 167 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 125, Pi = 167 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 125/167 * 100 | Answer: 74.85 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 17 V across R1 = 38 ohm and R2 = 8 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 17, R1 = 38, R2 = 8 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 17*8 / (38+8) | Answer: 2.957 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 220 kohm and Rin = 5 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 220, Rin = 5 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 220 / 5 | Answer: 44

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 180 kohm and Rg = 18 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 180, Rg = 18 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 180/18 | Answer: 11

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 3581. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 3581 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(3581) | Answer: 35.54 dB

question: A first-order system has a time constant of 3.3 s. Find the time (in s) to reach 63.2% of its final value.
solution: For a first-order step response, y = 1 - e^(-t/tau) | y = 0.632 when t = tau | Answer: 3.3 s
formula: At t = tau the response reaches 63.2% (one time constant)

question: A signal is sampled at 170 kHz. According to the Nyquist criterion, what is the maximum signal frequency that can be represented (in kHz)?
solution: Given: fs = 170 | Formula: f_max = fs / 2 | Substitute: f_max = 170 / 2 | Answer: 85 kHz

question: A simply supported beam of span 5.7 m carries a central point load of 40 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.7, W = 40 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 40*5.7 / 4 | Answer: 57 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.6 m carries a UDL of 10 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6.6, w = 10 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 10*(6.6)^2 / 8 | Answer: 54.45 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 1.3 m carries a point load 25 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 1.3, W = 25 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 25*1.3 | Answer: 32.5 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 1.9 m carries a UDL of 34 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 1.9, w = 34 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 34*(1.9)^2 / 2 | Answer: 61.37 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.4 m carries a point load 20 kN at distance 2.2 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 6.4, a = 2.2, W = 20 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 20*(6.4 - 2.2) / 6.4 | Answer: 13.12 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 3.9 m) carries a central point load 80 kN. With E = 25 GPa and I = 320e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=80000 N, L=3900.0 mm, E=25000 MPa, I=320e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 12.36 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 5.5 m carries a UDL of 18 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.5, w = 18 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 18*(5.5)^2 / 12 | Answer: 45.38 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 510 mm, clear cover 50 mm and main bars of diameter 25 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 510, c = 50, dia = 25 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 510 - 50 - 25/2 | Answer: 447.5 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 32 m^2 carrying a factored load of 9.8 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 32, w = 9.8 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 9.8 * 32 | Answer: 313.6 kN

question: For a bar of diameter 20 mm with design bond stress 1.4 MPa and steel stress 435 MPa, find the development length in mm.
solution: Given: dia = 20, tbd = 1.4, fs = 435 | Formula: Ld = phi fs / (4 tau_bd) | Substitute: Ld = 20*435 / (4*1.4) | Answer: 1554 mm

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 4.1 m, unit weight 19 kN/m^3, phi = 31 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 2.5 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 21 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 2.5, g = 21 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (21 - 9.81)*2.5 | Answer: 27.97 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 4.3e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.7, area = 1.8e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 4.3, i = 0.7, A = 1.8 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (4.3e-4)*0.7*(1.8e-3) | Answer: 541.8 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.4 m, bed slope 0.004 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.03. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 4.4 m under a head of 0.3 m. Taking Cd = 0.62 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 5.5 m wide carries a discharge of 11.3 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 430 m and design speed 50 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 430, V = 50 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (50)^2 / (127*430) | Answer: 0.04578
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: For a design speed of 40 km/h with allowable superelevation 0.05 and lateral friction 0.14, find the minimum curve radius in m.
A tank of volume 230 m^3 treats a flow of 140 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 230, Q = 140 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 230 / 140 | Answer: 1.643 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 270 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.22 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 8 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 270, k = 0.22, t = 8 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 270*(1 - e^(-0.22*8)) | Answer: 223.5 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.87, rainfall intensity 115 mm/h over a catchment of 28.1 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.87, i = 115, A = 28.1 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.87*115*28.1 / 360 | Answer: 7.809 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.05 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 400 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.05, M = 400 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 400*(30+0.05)/30 | Answer: 400.7 m

question: Convert the decimal number 123 to binary.
solution: Divide 123 by 2 repeatedly, recording remainders | Reading remainders in reverse gives 1111011 | Answer: 1111011 (binary)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 2 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the decimal number 2396 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 2396 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 95C (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the 8-bit binary number 01000001 to decimal.
solution: Binary 01000001 = sum of bit-weights | Answer: 65 (decimal)
formula: Sum each bit times its positional weight (2^i)

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 00100101 and 11111011.
solution: XOR: 11011110 | Count of 1s = 6 | Answer: 6
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 240 megabits is sent over a link of 80 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 240, B = 80 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 240 / 80 | Answer: 3 s

question: A link has bandwidth 5 Mbps and round-trip time 110 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 5, R = 110 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 5e6 * 110e-3 bits = 550 kb | Answer: 550 kilobits

question: A channel of bandwidth 3 kHz has a signal-to-noise ratio of 7 (linear). Using Shannon's theorem, find the channel capacity in kbps.
solution: Given: B = 3, SNR = 7 | Formula: C = B log2(1 + SNR) | Substitute: C = 3*log2(1 + 7) | Answer: 9 kbps

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.85, cache access time 8 ns and main-memory access time 170 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.85, tc = 8, tm = 170 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.85*8 + (1 - 0.85)*170 | Answer: 32.3 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 525646 elements?
solution: Given: n = 525646 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(525646)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: An O(n^2) algorithm performs c*n^2 basic operations. If c = 1 and n = 1210, how many operations are performed?
solution: Given: n = 1210 | Formula: operations = n^2 | Substitute: = (1210)^2 | Answer: 1464100

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.002, memory access time 120 ns and page-fault service time 8 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 8 ms = 8000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.002)*120 + 0.002*8000000.0 ns | Answer: 16.12 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 2.3 m^3 at 420 kPa and 560 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 2.3, P = 420, Tk = 560 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (420e3)*2.3 / (8.314*560) | Answer: 207.5 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.36 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 18 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.36, t = 18 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.36*18) | Answer: 0.9985

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.3 /min) is to reach 55% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.3, X = 55 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.55) / 0.3 | Answer: 2.662 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.15 /min) reaches 85% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.15, X = 85 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.85 / (0.15*(1 - 0.85)) | Answer: 37.78 min

question: For a reaction with A = 8e10 /s and activation energy 80 kJ/mol at 440 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 8, Ea = 80, Tk = 440 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 8e10 * exp(-80e3 / (8.314*440)) | Answer: 25.44 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.9 and bottoms xW = 0.04, with relative volatility alpha = 2.8. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.9, xw = 0.04, al = 2.8 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.9/0.1)(0.96/0.04)] / ln(2.8) | Answer: 5.221 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.74 and x = 0.36. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.74, x = 0.36 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.74/0.26) / (0.36/0.64) | Answer: 5.06

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.19 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 75 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.19, Psat = 75 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.19 * 75 | Answer: 14.25 kPa

question: A stream of 7.7 kg/s with specific heat 1.6 kJ/kg-K is heated through 35 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 7.7, cp = 1.6, dT = 35 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 7.7*1.6*35 | Answer: 431.2 kW

question: A reactor of volume 2.3 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 1.3 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 2.3, Q = 1.3 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 2.3 / 1.3 | Answer: 1.769 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 8.1e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 1 mm with a concentration difference of 150 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 8.1, L = 1, dC = 150 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (8.1e-9)*150 / (1e-3) | Answer: 1215 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 3.1 min and steady-state gain 1.9. For a step input of magnitude 6, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 3.1, K = 1.9, M = 6 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 1.9 * 6 | Answer: 11.4 units

question: A reactor operates at a space time of 10 min. Find its space velocity in per hour.
solution: Given: tau = 10 | Formula: SV = 60 / tau  (per hour) | Substitute: SV = 60 / 10 | Answer: 6 /h

question: An aircraft wing of area 85 m^2 flies at 190 m/s (air density 1 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.4. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 85, V = 190, rho = 1, CL = 0.4 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1*(190)^2*85*0.4 / 1000 | Answer: 613.7 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 60 m^2 flies at 250 m/s (density 1 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.12. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 60, V = 250, rho = 1, CD = 0.12 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*1*(250)^2*60*0.12 / 1000 | Answer: 225 kN

question: Find the dynamic pressure for air of density 0.7 kg/m^3 moving at 170 m/s, in Pa.
solution: Given: rho = 0.7, V = 170 | Formula: q = 0.5 rho V^2 | Substitute: q = 0.5*0.7*(170)^2 | Answer: 10115 Pa

question: An aircraft flies at 200 m/s where the speed of sound is 310 m/s. Find the Mach number.
solution: Given: V = 200, a = 310 | Formula: M = V / a | Substitute: M = 200 / 310 | Answer: 0.6452

question: A specimen under stress 370 MPa shows an elastic strain of 2.7e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 370, eps = 2.7 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 370 / (2.7e-3) MPa = 137 GPa | Answer: 137 GPa

question: A block of mass 45 kg has a volume of 2.2e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 45, V = 2.2 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 45 / (2.2e-3) | Answer: 20455 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 2400 mm is heated through 110 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 11e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 2400, dT = 110, al = 11 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 2400*11e-6*110 | Answer: 2.904 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 100 ohm, R2 = 185 ohm and R3 = 440 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 100, R2 = 185, R3 = 440 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 185*440 / 100 | Answer: 814 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 120 ohm and gauge factor 2.1 experiences a strain of 550e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 120, GF = 2.1, eps = 550 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 120*2.1*550e-6 | Answer: 138.6 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 9.07 when the true value is 10. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.07, true = 10 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.07 - 10| / 10 * 100 | Answer: 9.3 %

question: Annual demand is 15500 units, ordering cost 160 per order and holding cost 19 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 15500, S = 160, H = 19 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*15500*160 / 19) | Answer: 510.9 units

question: An asset costs 280000 with salvage value 2000 after 12 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 280000, Sv = 2000, n = 12 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (280000 - 2000) / 12 | Answer: 23167 per year

question: A product sells for 320 per unit with variable cost 10 per unit and fixed costs 45000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 320, V = 10, F = 45000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 45000 / (320 - 10) | Answer: 145.2 units

question: Find the present worth of 195000 received 9 years from now at an interest rate of 7% per year.
solution: Given: F = 195000, n = 9, i = 7 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 195000 / (1 + 0.07)^9 | Answer: 106067 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.97, 0.92 and 0.91 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.97, r2 = 0.92, r3 = 0.91 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.97*0.92*0.91 | Answer: 0.8121

question: A process produces 30 defective items in a batch of 7000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 30, N = 7000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 30/7000 * 1e6 | Answer: 4286 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = 5x^3 + 4x + 4 evaluated at x = 0.
For f(x) = 2x^3 + x + 7, find f''(x) at x = 0.
Evaluate the definite integral of (4x^2 + 6x + 3) dx from x = -2 to x = 6.

question: Find the larger real root of 5x^2 - 8x - 4 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[-2, 0], [-9, 7]].
solution: Given: a = -2, b = 0, c = -9, d = 7 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (-2)(7) - (0)(-9) | Answer: -14

question: Find the determinant of [[-1, 6, 2], [-6, 3, -5], [2, 2, -5]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: -271

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[-1, -6], [-2, -7]].
solution: Trace tr = -8, Determinant = -5 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 0.5826

question: Solve for x: 0x + 2y = 3 and 4x + -2y = -9.
solution: Determinant = 0*-2 - 2*4 = -8 | x = (e d - b f) / det = -1.5 | Answer: x = -1.5

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 14, 71, 63, 80, 81.
solution: Sum = 309 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 61.8 | Answer: 61.8

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 17, 27, 16, 5, 5.
solution: Mean = 14 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 9.274

question: Find the slope of the line through (-1, 3) and (8, 3).
solution: Given: x1 = -1, y1 = 3, x2 = 8, y2 = 3 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (3 - 3) / (8 - -1) | Answer: 0

question: Find the distance between the points (0, 1) and (6, 1).
solution: Given: x1 = 0, y1 = 1, x2 = 6, y2 = 1 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((6)^2 + (0)^2) | Answer: 6 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (2,2), (3,-2), (-8,7).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 17.5 sq units

question: Evaluate the number of combinations C(18, 17).
solution: Given: n = 18, r = 17 | Formula: C(n, r) = n! / (r! (n - r)!) | Substitute: C(18, 17) = 18! / (17! * 1!) | Answer: 18

question: Evaluate the number of permutations P(11, 1).
solution: Given: n = 11, r = 1 | Formula: P(n, r) = n! / (n - r)! | Substitute: P(11, 1) = 11! / 10! | Answer: 11

question: Find the 24th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 3 and common difference 1.
solution: Given: a = 3, d = 1, n = 24 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = 3 + (24 - 1)*1 | Answer: 26

question: Find the sum of the first 26 terms of an AP with first term 11 and common difference -5.
solution: Given: a = 11, d = -5, n = 26 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 26/2 [2*11 + (26-1)*-5] | Answer: -1339

question: Find the 8th term of a geometric progression with first term 5 and common ratio 3.
solution: Given: a = 5, r = 3, n = 8 | Formula: a_n = a r^(n-1) | Substitute: a_n = 5 * 3^(8-1) | Answer: 10935

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 31000 at 13.8% per annum for 9 years.
solution: Given: P = 31000, R = 13.8, Tt = 9 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 31000 * 13.8 * 9 / 100 | Answer: 38502 currency units

question: Find the amount when 39000 is invested at 4.7% per annum compounded annually for 3 years.
solution: Given: P = 39000, R = 4.7, Tt = 3 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 39000 * (1 + 4.7/100)^3 | Answer: 44762 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (6, -5, -1) and (-2, -1, 0).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (-1, 3, -5) and (-5, -3, 2).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 33.67

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (3, 0, -1) and (-5, -3, 0).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 144.4 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number -12 + -8i.
solution: Given: a = -12, b = -8 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((-12)^2 + (-8)^2) | Answer: 14.42

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number -2 + 12i.
solution: Given: a = -2, b = 12 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(12, -2) | Answer: 99.46 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -2x^3 + 3x^2 + 6x + 9 at x = -4.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-173 with initial guess x0=4, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=0.8 and ordinates 2, 0, 9, 7, 7, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 535 and 297.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 535 and 297 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 56 and 31.
solution: Given: a = 56, b = 31 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 56*31 / 1 | Answer: 1736
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 21 mm carries an axial tensile load of 114 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 31 mm and length 1100 mm carries an axial load of 51 kN. Take E = 210 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 55 mm transmits a torque of 1300 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 55, Tt = 1300 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(1300*1000) / (pi*(55)^3) | Answer: 39.79 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 59 mm and length 1300 mm carries a torque of 600 N-m. With G = 77 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (59)^4 / 32 = 1189619 mm^4 | theta = (600*1000)(1300) / (77000 * 1189619) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 0.4879 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 45 mm wide and 70 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 45, h = 70 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 45*(70)^2 / 6 | Answer: 36750 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (80 mm x 140 mm) carries a bending moment of 39 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (65 mm x 120 mm) has effective length 3900 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 370 MPa is designed for a working stress of 230 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 370, sw = 230 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 370 / 230 | Answer: 1.609

question: A steel bar is fully restrained and heated through 90 deg C. With E = 210 GPa and alpha = 11e-6 /deg C, find the thermal stress in MPa.
solution: Given: dT = 90, E = 210, al = 11 | Formula: sigma = E alpha (dT) | Substitute: sigma = 210000 * 11e-6 * 90 | Answer: 207.9 MPa

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 950 mm and wall thickness 9 mm carries an internal pressure of 0.7 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 950, t = 9, P = 0.7 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 0.7*950 / (2*9) | Answer: 36.94 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 960 K and 360 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 960, Tc = 360 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 360/960) * 100 | Answer: 62.5 %

question: A refrigerator works between 262 K (cold) and 312 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 262, Th = 312 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 262 / (312 - 262) | Answer: 5.24

question: A heat pump operates between 265 K and 328 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 265, Th = 328 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 328 / (328 - 265) | Answer: 5.206

question: 2.9 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 190 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.9, dT = 190 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 2.9 * 0.718 * 190 | Answer: 395.6 kJ

question: 2.4 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 160 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.4, dT = 160 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 2.4 * 1.005 * 160 | Answer: 385.9 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 2.1 m^3 at 480 K with mass 5.5 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 2.1, Tk = 480, m = 5.5 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 5.5*0.287*480 / 2.1 | Answer: 360.8 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 4.1 kg of air expands isothermally at 420 K from volume V1 to 3*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.1, Tk = 420, ratio = 3 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 4.1*0.287*420*ln(3) | Answer: 542.9 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 2.4 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.32 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 2.4, D = 0.32 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*2.4*0.32 / 0.001 | Answer: 768000

question: Water flows at 0.9 m/s through a pipe of diameter 190 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 12.9 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 12.9 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*12.9 / 1000 | Answer: 126.5 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 15 m. Taking Cv = 0.97, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 15, cv = 0.97 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.97*sqrt(2*9.81*15) | Answer: 16.64 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 310 mm) water flows at 2.5 m/s. It contracts to diameter 50 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 310, d2 = 50, V1 = 2.5 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 2.5*(310/50)^2 | Answer: 96.1 m/s

question: Water flows at 1.3 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.49 m and length 120 m. With friction factor f = 0.032, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 27 teeth drives a gear of 104 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1200 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 27, z2 = 104, N1 = 1200 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1200*27 / 104 | Answer: 311.5 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 550 mm rotates at 350 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 550, N = 350 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.55)*350 / 60 | Answer: 10.08 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 45.2 kW at 1350 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 45.2, N = 1350 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(45.2*1000) / (2*pi*1350) | Answer: 319.7 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 0.8 kg rotates at radius 0.3 m at 200 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 18800 N/m and mass 12.4 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 18800, m = 12.4 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(18800/12.4) | Answer: 6.197 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 9.3 m^2 and thickness 0.32 m has conductivity k = 36.9 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 35 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 9.3, L = 0.32, k = 36.9, dT = 35 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 36.9*9.3*35 / 0.32 | Answer: 37534 W

question: A surface of area 4.1 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 40 W/m^2-K to surroundings 65 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 4.1, h = 40, dT = 65 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 40*4.1*65 | Answer: 10660 W

question: In a counter-flow heat exchanger the terminal temperature differences are 45 deg C and 10 deg C. Find the log mean temperature difference (LMTD) in deg C.
solution: Given: dT1 = 45, dT2 = 10 | Formula: LMTD = (dT1 - dT2) / ln(dT1/dT2) | Substitute: LMTD = (45 - 10) / ln(45/10) | Answer: 23.27 deg C

question: In turning, cutting speed = 250 m/min, feed = 0.32 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2.7 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 250, f = 0.32, d = 2.7 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*250*0.32*2.7 | Answer: 216000 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 470 mm is turned at 1150 rpm with a feed of 0.33 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 470, N = 1150, f = 0.33 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 470 / (0.33*1150) | Answer: 1.238 min

question: A resistor of 151 ohm carries a current of 6.8 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 151, I = 6.8 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 6.8 * 151 | Answer: 1027 V

question: Three resistors 41 ohm, 33 ohm and 33 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 41, R2 = 33, R3 = 33 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 41 + 33 + 33 | Answer: 107 ohm

question: Two resistors 77 ohm and 71 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 77, R2 = 71 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 77*71 / (77+71) | Answer: 36.94 ohm

question: A device draws 5.1 A at 120 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 120, I = 5.1 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 120 * 5.1 | Answer: 612 W

question: A current of 6.2 A flows through a 139 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 6.2, R = 139 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (6.2)^2 * 139 | Answer: 5343 W

question: Two capacitors 9.7 uF and 12.1 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 9.7, C2 = 12.1 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 9.7*12.1 / (9.7+12.1) | Answer: 5.384 uF

question: A resistor 90 kohm and capacitor 2.2 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 90, C = 2.2 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (90k)(2.2u) = 198 ms | Answer: 198 ms

question: An inductor 403.6 mH is in series with 85 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 403.6, R = 85 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (403.6e-3) / 85 | Answer: 4.748 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 123 mH inductor at 740 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 123, f = 740 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (740)(123e-3) | Answer: 571.9 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 17.6 uF capacitor at 50 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 17.6, f = 50 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (50)(17.6e-6)) | Answer: 180.9 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 11 ohm, XL = 52 ohm and XC = 59 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 11, XL = 52, XC = 59 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(11^2 + (52 - 59)^2) | Answer: 13.04 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 30.3 mH and C = 1.4 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 30.3, C = 1.4 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(30.3e-3 * 1.4e-6)) | Answer: 772.7 Hz

question: A capacitor of 78 uF is charged to 290 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 78, V = 290 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*78e-6*(290)^2 | Answer: 328 mJ

question: An alternating voltage has a peak value of 60 V. Find its RMS value.
solution: Given: Vp = 60 | Formula: Vrms = Vp / sqrt(2) | Substitute: Vrms = 60 / sqrt(2) | Answer: 42.43 V

question: A transformer has primary voltage 260 V with 210 primary turns and 140 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 260, N1 = 210, N2 = 140 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 260 * 140/210 | Answer: 173.3 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 320 V and draws an armature current of 28 A. If the armature resistance is 1.15 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 320, Ia = 28, Ra = 1.15 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 320 - 28*1.15 | Answer: 287.8 V

question: A 6-pole induction motor on a 50 Hz supply runs at 790 rpm. Find the slip (%).
formula: s = (Ns - N) / Ns,  Ns = 120 f / P

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 5 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.89. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 5, VL = 400, pf = 0.89 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*400*5*0.89 / 1000 | Answer: 3.083 kW

question: A load has real power 20 kW and apparent power 25 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 20, S = 25 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 20 / 25 | Answer: 0.8

question: A machine delivers 120 kW output while drawing 127 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 120, Pi = 127 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 120/127 * 100 | Answer: 94.49 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 22 V across R1 = 15 ohm and R2 = 28 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 22, R1 = 15, R2 = 28 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 22*28 / (15+28) | Answer: 14.33 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 110 kohm and Rin = 2 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 110, Rin = 2 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 110 / 2 | Answer: 55

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 190 kohm and Rg = 33 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 190, Rg = 33 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 190/33 | Answer: 6.758

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 7232. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 7232 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(7232) | Answer: 38.59 dB

question: A first-order system has a time constant of 1.1 s. Find the time (in s) to reach 63.2% of its final value.
solution: For a first-order step response, y = 1 - e^(-t/tau) | y = 0.632 when t = tau | Answer: 1.1 s
formula: At t = tau the response reaches 63.2% (one time constant)

question: A signal is sampled at 154 kHz. According to the Nyquist criterion, what is the maximum signal frequency that can be represented (in kHz)?
solution: Given: fs = 154 | Formula: f_max = fs / 2 | Substitute: f_max = 154 / 2 | Answer: 77 kHz

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.8 m carries a central point load of 65 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 9.8, W = 65 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 65*9.8 / 4 | Answer: 159.2 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.9 m carries a UDL of 15 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.9, w = 15 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 15*(4.9)^2 / 8 | Answer: 45.02 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 2.9 m carries a point load 20 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 2.9, W = 20 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 20*2.9 | Answer: 58 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 5.3 m carries a UDL of 12 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.3, w = 12 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 12*(5.3)^2 / 2 | Answer: 168.5 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.6 m carries a point load 30 kN at distance 2.5 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 6.6, a = 2.5, W = 30 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 30*(6.6 - 2.5) / 6.6 | Answer: 18.64 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 4.6 m) carries a central point load 35 kN. With E = 25 GPa and I = 460e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=35000 N, L=4600.0 mm, E=25000 MPa, I=460e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 6.172 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 4.8 m carries a UDL of 6 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.8, w = 6 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 6*(4.8)^2 / 12 | Answer: 11.52 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 520 mm, clear cover 45 mm and main bars of diameter 12 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 520, c = 45, dia = 12 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 520 - 45 - 12/2 | Answer: 469 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 28.6 m^2 carrying a factored load of 10.4 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 28.6, w = 10.4 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 10.4 * 28.6 | Answer: 297.4 kN

question: For a bar of diameter 25 mm with design bond stress 1.9 MPa and steel stress 395 MPa, find the development length in mm.
solution: Given: dia = 25, tbd = 1.9, fs = 395 | Formula: Ld = phi fs / (4 tau_bd) | Substitute: Ld = 25*395 / (4*1.9) | Answer: 1299 mm

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 3.7 m, unit weight 20 kN/m^3, phi = 33 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 6.7 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 19 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 6.7, g = 19 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (19 - 9.81)*6.7 | Answer: 61.57 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 1.3e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1.4, area = 7.6e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 1.3, i = 1.4, A = 7.6 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (1.3e-4)*1.4*(7.6e-3) | Answer: 1383 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.9 m, bed slope 0.009 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.013. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 3.7 m under a head of 0.2 m. Taking Cd = 0.63 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.

question: A rectangular channel 3.8 m wide carries a discharge of 25.4 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).

question: For a design speed of 50 km/h with allowable superelevation 0.08 and lateral friction 0.13, find the minimum curve radius in m.

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.3, rainfall intensity 35 mm/h over a catchment of 29.7 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.07 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 120 m with this tape.

question: A file of 320 megabits is sent over a link of 71 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.

question: A link has bandwidth 19 Mbps and round-trip time 90 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.

question: A channel of bandwidth 18 kHz has a signal-to-noise ratio of 255 (linear). Using Shannon's theorem, find the channel capacity in kbps.
solution: Given: B = 18, SNR = 255 | Formula: C = B log2(1 + SNR) | Substitute: C = 18*log2(1 + 255) | Answer: 144 kbps

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.93, cache access time 10 ns and main-memory access time 70 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.93, tc = 10, tm = 70 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.93*10 + (1 - 0.93)*70 | Answer: 14.2 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 550303 elements?
solution: Given: n = 550303 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(550303)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: An O(n^2) algorithm performs c*n^2 basic operations. If c = 1 and n = 170, how many operations are performed?
solution: Given: n = 170 | Formula: operations = n^2 | Substitute: = (170)^2 | Answer: 28900

question: A program is 75% parallelisable and run on 32 processors. Using Amdahl's law, find the maximum speedup.

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.015, memory access time 180 ns and page-fault service time 10 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 10 ms = 10000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.015)*180 + 0.015*10000000.0 ns | Answer: 150.2 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: A modem transmits at 3300 baud using 8-level signalling. Find the bit rate in bps.
solution: Given: baud = 3300, M = 8 | Formula: bit rate = baud * log2(M) | Substitute: bit rate = 3300 * log2(8) | Answer: 9900 bps

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 2.1 m^3 at 280 kPa and 400 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 2.1, P = 280, Tk = 400 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (280e3)*2.1 / (8.314*400) | Answer: 176.8 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.26 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 15 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.26, t = 15 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.26*15) | Answer: 0.9798

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.35 /min) is to reach 70% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.35, X = 70 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.7) / 0.35 | Answer: 3.44 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.31 /min) reaches 80% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.31, X = 80 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.8 / (0.31*(1 - 0.8)) | Answer: 12.9 min

question: For a reaction with A = 8e10 /s and activation energy 50 kJ/mol at 500 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 8, Ea = 50, Tk = 500 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 8e10 * exp(-50e3 / (8.314*500)) | Answer: 47801 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.93 and bottoms xW = 0.03, with relative volatility alpha = 1.9. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.93, xw = 0.03, al = 1.9 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.93/0.07)(0.97/0.03)] / ln(1.9) | Answer: 9.446 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.85 and x = 0.32. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.85, x = 0.32 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.85/0.15) / (0.32/0.68) | Answer: 12.04

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.29 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 120 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.29, Psat = 120 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.29 * 120 | Answer: 34.8 kPa

question: A stream of 9.8 kg/s with specific heat 4 kJ/kg-K is heated through 75 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 9.8, cp = 4, dT = 75 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 9.8*4*75 | Answer: 2940 kW

question: A reactor of volume 4.7 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 3.8 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 4.7, Q = 3.8 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 4.7 / 3.8 | Answer: 1.237 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 7.6e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 4 mm with a concentration difference of 80 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 7.6, L = 4, dC = 80 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (7.6e-9)*80 / (4e-3) | Answer: 152 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 9 min and steady-state gain 2.6. For a step input of magnitude 6, find the final (steady-state) change in output.

question: A reactor operates at a space time of 10.3 min. Find its space velocity in per hour.

question: An aircraft wing of area 80 m^2 flies at 200 m/s (air density 1 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.8. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 80, V = 200, rho = 1, CL = 0.8 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1*(200)^2*80*0.8 / 1000 | Answer: 1280 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 90 m^2 flies at 60 m/s (density 0.4 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.12. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 90, V = 60, rho = 0.4, CD = 0.12 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.4*(60)^2*90*0.12 / 1000 | Answer: 7.776 kN

question: Find the dynamic pressure for air of density 1.225 kg/m^3 moving at 100 m/s, in Pa.
solution: Given: rho = 1.225, V = 100 | Formula: q = 0.5 rho V^2 | Substitute: q = 0.5*1.225*(100)^2 | Answer: 6125 Pa

question: An aircraft flies at 270 m/s where the speed of sound is 295 m/s. Find the Mach number.
solution: Given: V = 270, a = 295 | Formula: M = V / a | Substitute: M = 270 / 295 | Answer: 0.9153

question: A specimen under stress 250 MPa shows an elastic strain of 1.3e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 250, eps = 1.3 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 250 / (1.3e-3) MPa = 192.3 GPa | Answer: 192.3 GPa

question: A block of mass 17 kg has a volume of 2.1e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.

question: A rod of length 1200 mm is heated through 70 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 23e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 85 ohm, R2 = 85 ohm and R3 = 320 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 85, R2 = 85, R3 = 320 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 85*320 / 85 | Answer: 320 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 350 ohm and gauge factor 2.2 experiences a strain of 1400e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.

question: A measurement reads 10.82 when the true value is 10. Find the percentage error.

question: Annual demand is 48500 units, ordering cost 240 per order and holding cost 25 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).

question: An asset costs 470000 with salvage value 12000 after 10 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.

question: A product sells for 190 per unit with variable cost 100 per unit and fixed costs 115000. Find the break-even quantity in units.

question: Find the present worth of 40000 received 3 years from now at an interest rate of 12% per year.

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.95, 0.93 and 0.92 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.

question: A process produces 9 defective items in a batch of 1000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).

question: Evaluate the number of combinations C(12, 6).

question: A steel bar is fully restrained and heated through 25 deg C. With E = 200 GPa and alpha = 13e-6 /deg C, find the thermal stress in MPa.

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 950 mm and wall thickness 12 mm carries an internal pressure of 2.2 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.

question: A Carnot engine operates between 860 K and 360 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).

question: A refrigerator works between 267 K (cold) and 308 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.

question: A heat pump operates between 269 K and 310 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.

question: 2.2 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 70 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.

question: Water flows at 1.3 m/s through a pipe of diameter 50 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 13.4 m. Taking Cv = 0.99, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).

Water flows at 1.2 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.45 m and length 460 m. With friction factor f = 0.025, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
