question: A pinion of 38 teeth drives a gear of 68 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1150 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 38, z2 = 68, N1 = 1150 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1150*38 / 68 | Answer: 642.6 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 280 mm rotates at 450 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 280, N = 450 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.28)*450 / 60 | Answer: 6.597 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 17.7 kW at 1100 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 17.7, N = 1100 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(17.7*1000) / (2*pi*1100) | Answer: 153.7 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 2.8 kg rotates at radius 0.58 m at 900 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 15000 N/m and mass 12.8 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 15000, m = 12.8 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(15000/12.8) | Answer: 5.448 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 5.4 m^2 and thickness 0.14 m has conductivity k = 41.1 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 20 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 5.4, L = 0.14, k = 41.1, dT = 20 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 41.1*5.4*20 / 0.14 | Answer: 31706 W

question: A surface of area 3 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 140 W/m^2-K to surroundings 145 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 3, h = 140, dT = 145 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 140*3*145 | Answer: 60900 W

question: In a counter-flow heat exchanger the terminal temperature differences are 120 deg C and 35 deg C. Find the log mean temperature difference (LMTD) in deg C.
solution: Given: dT1 = 120, dT2 = 35 | Formula: LMTD = (dT1 - dT2) / ln(dT1/dT2) | Substitute: LMTD = (120 - 35) / ln(120/35) | Answer: 68.99 deg C

question: In turning, cutting speed = 180 m/min, feed = 0.21 mm/rev, depth of cut = 1.7 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 180, f = 0.21, d = 1.7 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*180*0.21*1.7 | Answer: 64260 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 360 mm is turned at 1200 rpm with a feed of 0.4 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 360, N = 1200, f = 0.4 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 360 / (0.4*1200) | Answer: 0.75 min

question: A resistor of 43 ohm carries a current of 6.6 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 43, I = 6.6 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 6.6 * 43 | Answer: 283.8 V

question: Three resistors 64 ohm, 3 ohm and 78 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 64, R2 = 3, R3 = 78 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 64 + 3 + 78 | Answer: 145 ohm

question: Two resistors 92 ohm and 53 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 92, R2 = 53 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 92*53 / (92+53) | Answer: 33.63 ohm

question: A device draws 12.4 A at 150 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 150, I = 12.4 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 150 * 12.4 | Answer: 1860 W

question: A current of 0.4 A flows through a 84 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 0.4, R = 84 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (0.4)^2 * 84 | Answer: 13.44 W

question: Two capacitors 14.7 uF and 22.8 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 14.7, C2 = 22.8 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 14.7*22.8 / (14.7+22.8) | Answer: 8.938 uF

question: A resistor 29 kohm and capacitor 9.6 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 29, C = 9.6 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (29k)(9.6u) = 278.4 ms | Answer: 278.4 ms

question: An inductor 267 mH is in series with 139 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 267, R = 139 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (267e-3) / 139 | Answer: 1.921 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 135.1 mH inductor at 120 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 135.1, f = 120 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (120)(135.1e-3) | Answer: 101.9 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 38.7 uF capacitor at 130 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 38.7, f = 130 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (130)(38.7e-6)) | Answer: 31.63 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 5 ohm, XL = 72 ohm and XC = 49 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 5, XL = 72, XC = 49 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(5^2 + (72 - 49)^2) | Answer: 23.54 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 48.7 mH and C = 8.3 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 48.7, C = 8.3 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(48.7e-3 * 8.3e-6)) | Answer: 250.3 Hz

question: A capacitor of 71.4 uF is charged to 170 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 71.4, V = 170 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*71.4e-6*(170)^2 | Answer: 1032 mJ

question: An alternating voltage has a peak value of 178 V. Find its RMS value.
solution: Given: Vp = 178 | Formula: Vrms = Vp / sqrt(2) | Substitute: Vrms = 178 / sqrt(2) | Answer: 125.9 V

question: A transformer has primary voltage 310 V with 450 primary turns and 450 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 310, N1 = 450, N2 = 450 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 310 * 450/450 | Answer: 310 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 430 V and draws an armature current of 55 A. If the armature resistance is 1.45 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 430, Ia = 55, Ra = 1.45 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 430 - 55*1.45 | Answer: 350.2 V

question: A 6-pole induction motor on a 60 Hz supply runs at 1110 rpm. Find the slip (%).
formula: s = (Ns - N) / Ns,  Ns = 120 f / P

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 140 A at 433 V (line) with a power factor of 0.86. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 140, VL = 433, pf = 0.86 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*433*140*0.86 / 1000 | Answer: 90.3 kW

question: A load has real power 150 kW and apparent power 205 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 150, S = 205 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 150 / 205 | Answer: 0.7317

question: A machine delivers 10 kW output while drawing 37 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 10, Pi = 37 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 10/37 * 100 | Answer: 27.03 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 13 V across R1 = 28 ohm and R2 = 50 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 13, R1 = 28, R2 = 50 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 13*50 / (28+50) | Answer: 8.333 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 100 kohm and Rin = 2 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 100, Rin = 2 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 100 / 2 | Answer: 50

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 180 kohm and Rg = 4 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 180, Rg = 4 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 180/4 | Answer: 46

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 7743. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 7743 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(7743) | Answer: 38.89 dB

question: A first-order system has a time constant of 5.7 s. Find the time (in s) to reach 63.2% of its final value.
solution: For a first-order step response, y = 1 - e^(-t/tau) | y = 0.632 when t = tau | Answer: 5.7 s
formula: At t = tau the response reaches 63.2% (one time constant)

question: A signal is sampled at 88 kHz. According to the Nyquist criterion, what is the maximum signal frequency that can be represented (in kHz)?
solution: Given: fs = 88 | Formula: f_max = fs / 2 | Substitute: f_max = 88 / 2 | Answer: 44 kHz

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.1 m carries a central point load of 50 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 9.1, W = 50 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 50*9.1 / 4 | Answer: 113.8 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 5.8 m carries a UDL of 50 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.8, w = 50 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 50*(5.8)^2 / 8 | Answer: 210.2 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 5.6 m carries a point load 20 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.6, W = 20 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 20*5.6 | Answer: 112 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 3.6 m carries a UDL of 30 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.6, w = 30 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 30*(3.6)^2 / 2 | Answer: 194.4 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 7.5 m carries a point load 60 kN at distance 1.5 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 7.5, a = 1.5, W = 60 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 60*(7.5 - 1.5) / 7.5 | Answer: 48 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 7.7 m) carries a central point load 60 kN. With E = 30 GPa and I = 460e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=60000 N, L=7700.0 mm, E=30000 MPa, I=460e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 41.35 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 4.6 m carries a UDL of 42 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.6, w = 42 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 42*(4.6)^2 / 12 | Answer: 74.06 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 510 mm, clear cover 30 mm and main bars of diameter 12 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 510, c = 30, dia = 12 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 510 - 30 - 12/2 | Answer: 474 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 37.6 m^2 carrying a factored load of 17.5 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 37.6, w = 17.5 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 17.5 * 37.6 | Answer: 658 kN

question: For a bar of diameter 25 mm with design bond stress 2.3 MPa and steel stress 395 MPa, find the development length in mm.
solution: Given: dia = 25, tbd = 2.3, fs = 395 | Formula: Ld = phi fs / (4 tau_bd) | Substitute: Ld = 25*395 / (4*2.3) | Answer: 1073 mm

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 3.6 m, unit weight 17 kN/m^3, phi = 33 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 10.2 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 20 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 10.2, g = 20 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (20 - 9.81)*10.2 | Answer: 103.9 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 1.1e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.3, area = 6.3e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 1.1, i = 0.3, A = 6.3 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (1.1e-4)*0.3*(6.3e-3) | Answer: 207.9 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 2.1 m, bed slope 0.004 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.013. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 3.8 m under a head of 0.3 m. Taking Cd = 0.6 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 3.4 m wide carries a discharge of 27.3 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 130 m and design speed 90 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 130, V = 90 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (90)^2 / (127*130) | Answer: 0.4906
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: For a design speed of 85 km/h with allowable superelevation 0.06 and lateral friction 0.14, find the minimum curve radius in m.
A tank of volume 570 m^3 treats a flow of 85 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 570, Q = 85 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 570 / 85 | Answer: 6.706 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 150 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.34 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 6 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 150, k = 0.34, t = 6 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 150*(1 - e^(-0.34*6)) | Answer: 130.5 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.71, rainfall intensity 35 mm/h over a catchment of 9.7 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.71, i = 35, A = 9.7 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.71*35*9.7 / 360 | Answer: 0.6696 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.02 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 780 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.02, M = 780 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 780*(20+0.02)/20 | Answer: 780.8 m

question: Convert the decimal number 102 to binary.
solution: Divide 102 by 2 repeatedly, recording remainders | Reading remainders in reverse gives 1100110 | Answer: 1100110 (binary)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 2 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the decimal number 518 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 518 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 206 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the 8-bit binary number 10010011 to decimal.
solution: Binary 10010011 = sum of bit-weights | Answer: 147 (decimal)
formula: Sum each bit times its positional weight (2^i)

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 10011001 and 11111000.
solution: XOR: 01100001 | Count of 1s = 3 | Answer: 3
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 40 megabits is sent over a link of 80 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 40, B = 80 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 40 / 80 | Answer: 0.5 s

question: A link has bandwidth 72 Mbps and round-trip time 80 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 72, R = 80 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 72e6 * 80e-3 bits = 5760 kb | Answer: 5760 kilobits

question: A channel of bandwidth 3 kHz has a signal-to-noise ratio of 31 (linear). Using Shannon's theorem, find the channel capacity in kbps.
solution: Given: B = 3, SNR = 31 | Formula: C = B log2(1 + SNR) | Substitute: C = 3*log2(1 + 31) | Answer: 15 kbps

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.85, cache access time 6 ns and main-memory access time 130 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.85, tc = 6, tm = 130 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.85*6 + (1 - 0.85)*130 | Answer: 24.6 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 101238 elements?
solution: Given: n = 101238 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(101238)) + 1 | Answer: 17

question: An O(n^2) algorithm performs c*n^2 basic operations. If c = 1 and n = 1100, how many operations are performed?
solution: Given: n = 1100 | Formula: operations = n^2 | Substitute: = (1100)^2 | Answer: 1210000

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.01, memory access time 150 ns and page-fault service time 8 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 8 ms = 8000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.01)*150 + 0.01*8000000.0 ns | Answer: 80.15 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 0.7 m^3 at 330 kPa and 350 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 0.7, P = 330, Tk = 350 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (330e3)*0.7 / (8.314*350) | Answer: 79.38 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.3 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 20 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.3, t = 20 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.3*20) | Answer: 0.9975

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.16 /min) is to reach 75% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.16, X = 75 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.75) / 0.16 | Answer: 8.664 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.24 /min) reaches 85% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.24, X = 85 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.85 / (0.24*(1 - 0.85)) | Answer: 23.61 min

question: For a reaction with A = 9e10 /s and activation energy 70 kJ/mol at 400 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 9, Ea = 70, Tk = 400 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 9e10 * exp(-70e3 / (8.314*400)) | Answer: 64.99 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.93 and bottoms xW = 0.04, with relative volatility alpha = 2.5. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.93, xw = 0.04, al = 2.5 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.93/0.07)(0.96/0.04)] / ln(2.5) | Answer: 6.291 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.83 and x = 0.44. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.83, x = 0.44 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.83/0.17) / (0.44/0.56) | Answer: 6.214

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.4 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 40 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.4, Psat = 40 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.4 * 40 | Answer: 16 kPa

question: A stream of 9.9 kg/s with specific heat 3.7 kJ/kg-K is heated through 40 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 9.9, cp = 3.7, dT = 40 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 9.9*3.7*40 | Answer: 1465 kW

question: A reactor of volume 9.3 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 1.7 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 9.3, Q = 1.7 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 9.3 / 1.7 | Answer: 5.471 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 8e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 4 mm with a concentration difference of 160 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 8, L = 4, dC = 160 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (8e-9)*160 / (4e-3) | Answer: 320 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 2.7 min and steady-state gain 1.2. For a step input of magnitude 5, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 2.7, K = 1.2, M = 5 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 1.2 * 5 | Answer: 6 units

question: A reactor operates at a space time of 1.6 min. Find its space velocity in per hour.
solution: Given: tau = 1.6 | Formula: SV = 60 / tau  (per hour) | Substitute: SV = 60 / 1.6 | Answer: 37.5 /h

question: An aircraft wing of area 100 m^2 flies at 210 m/s (air density 1 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.9. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 100, V = 210, rho = 1, CL = 0.9 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1*(210)^2*100*0.9 / 1000 | Answer: 1984 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 45 m^2 flies at 190 m/s (density 0.7 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.03. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 45, V = 190, rho = 0.7, CD = 0.03 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.7*(190)^2*45*0.03 / 1000 | Answer: 17.06 kN

question: An aircraft flies at 390 m/s where the speed of sound is 340 m/s. Find the Mach number.
solution: Given: V = 390, a = 340 | Formula: M = V / a | Substitute: M = 390 / 340 | Answer: 1.147

question: A specimen under stress 260 MPa shows an elastic strain of 1.2e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 260, eps = 1.2 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 260 / (1.2e-3) MPa = 216.7 GPa | Answer: 216.7 GPa

question: A block of mass 7 kg has a volume of 1.6e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 7, V = 1.6 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 7 / (1.6e-3) | Answer: 4375 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 800 mm is heated through 120 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 17e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 800, dT = 120, al = 17 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 800*17e-6*120 | Answer: 1.632 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 155 ohm, R2 = 40 ohm and R3 = 75 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 155, R2 = 40, R3 = 75 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 40*75 / 155 | Answer: 19.35 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 1000 ohm and gauge factor 2.1 experiences a strain of 1200e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 1000, GF = 2.1, eps = 1200 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 1000*2.1*1200e-6 | Answer: 2520 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 10.77 when the true value is 10. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10.77, true = 10 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10.77 - 10| / 10 * 100 | Answer: 7.7 %

question: Annual demand is 34500 units, ordering cost 220 per order and holding cost 19 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 34500, S = 220, H = 19 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*34500*220 / 19) | Answer: 893.8 units

question: An asset costs 360000 with salvage value 30000 after 15 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 360000, Sv = 30000, n = 15 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (360000 - 30000) / 15 | Answer: 22000 per year

question: A product sells for 210 per unit with variable cost 60 per unit and fixed costs 155000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 210, V = 60, F = 155000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 155000 / (210 - 60) | Answer: 1033 units

question: Find the present worth of 75000 received 7 years from now at an interest rate of 11% per year.
solution: Given: F = 75000, n = 7, i = 11 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 75000 / (1 + 0.11)^7 | Answer: 36124 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.9, 0.96 and 0.93 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.9, r2 = 0.96, r3 = 0.93 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.9*0.96*0.93 | Answer: 0.8035

question: A process produces 35 defective items in a batch of 15000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 35, N = 15000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 35/15000 * 1e6 | Answer: 2333 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = x^3 + 6x^2 + 8x + 4 evaluated at x = -2.
For f(x) = 2x^3 - 2x^2 - 7x - 6, find f''(x) at x = 2.
Evaluate the definite integral of (3x^2 - 5x - 8) dx from x = -2 to x = 4.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = 3x^3/3 + -5x^2/2 + -8x | Evaluate F(4) - F(-2) | Answer: -6

question: Find the larger real root of 5x^2 - 9x - 7 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[9, 7], [-9, -8]].
solution: Given: a = 9, b = 7, c = -9, d = -8 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (9)(-8) - (7)(-9) | Answer: -9

question: Find the determinant of [[-6, 3, 4], [4, -5, 4], [5, 2, 3]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: 294

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[-1, 5], [8, 1]].
solution: Trace tr = 0, Determinant = -41 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 6.403

question: Solve for x: -5x + 1y = 2 and 5x + -2y = -6.
solution: Determinant = -5*-2 - 1*5 = 5 | x = (e d - b f) / det = 0.4 | Answer: x = 0.4
