question: A stream of 5.5 kg/s with specific heat 1.1 kJ/kg-K is heated through 20 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 5.5, cp = 1.1, dT = 20 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 5.5*1.1*20 | Answer: 121 kW

question: A reactor of volume 14.2 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 2.9 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 14.2, Q = 2.9 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 14.2 / 2.9 | Answer: 4.897 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 3.6e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 1 mm with a concentration difference of 90 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 3.6, L = 1, dC = 90 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (3.6e-9)*90 / (1e-3) | Answer: 324 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 3.5 min and steady-state gain 1.1. For a step input of magnitude 15, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 3.5, K = 1.1, M = 15 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 1.1 * 15 | Answer: 16.5 units

question: A reactor operates at a space time of 5.7 min. Find its space velocity in per hour.
solution: Given: tau = 5.7 | Formula: SV = 60 / tau  (per hour) | Substitute: SV = 60 / 5.7 | Answer: 10.53 /h

question: An aircraft wing of area 80 m^2 flies at 70 m/s (air density 0.4 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 1. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 80, V = 70, rho = 0.4, CL = 1 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.4*(70)^2*80*1 / 1000 | Answer: 78.4 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 80 m^2 flies at 110 m/s (density 1.225 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.11. Find the drag force in kN.
Find the dynamic pressure for air of density 1 kg/m^3 moving at 290 m/s, in Pa.
solution: Given: rho = 1, V = 290 | Formula: q = 0.5 rho V^2 | Substitute: q = 0.5*1*(290)^2 | Answer: 42050 Pa

question: An aircraft flies at 280 m/s where the speed of sound is 340 m/s. Find the Mach number.
solution: Given: V = 280, a = 340 | Formula: M = V / a | Substitute: M = 280 / 340 | Answer: 0.8235

question: A specimen under stress 360 MPa shows an elastic strain of 2.5e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 360, eps = 2.5 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 360 / (2.5e-3) MPa = 144 GPa | Answer: 144 GPa

question: A block of mass 28 kg has a volume of 4.9e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 28, V = 4.9 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 28 / (4.9e-3) | Answer: 5714 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 1800 mm is heated through 90 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 12e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 1800, dT = 90, al = 12 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 1800*12e-6*90 | Answer: 1.944 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 15 ohm, R2 = 45 ohm and R3 = 335 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 15, R2 = 45, R3 = 335 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 45*335 / 15 | Answer: 1005 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 1000 ohm and gauge factor 2.1 experiences a strain of 1250e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 1000, GF = 2.1, eps = 1250 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 1000*2.1*1250e-6 | Answer: 2625 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 9.3 when the true value is 100. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.3, true = 100 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.3 - 100| / 100 * 100 | Answer: 90.7 %

question: Annual demand is 4500 units, ordering cost 300 per order and holding cost 31 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 4500, S = 300, H = 31 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*4500*300 / 31) | Answer: 295.1 units

question: An asset costs 350000 with salvage value 4000 after 15 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 350000, Sv = 4000, n = 15 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (350000 - 4000) / 15 | Answer: 23067 per year

question: A product sells for 270 per unit with variable cost 110 per unit and fixed costs 165000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 270, V = 110, F = 165000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 165000 / (270 - 110) | Answer: 1031 units

question: Find the present worth of 85000 received 10 years from now at an interest rate of 11% per year.
solution: Given: F = 85000, n = 10, i = 11 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 85000 / (1 + 0.11)^10 | Answer: 29936 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.95, 0.94 and 0.95 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.95, r2 = 0.94, r3 = 0.95 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.95*0.94*0.95 | Answer: 0.8483

question: A process produces 1 defective items in a batch of 4000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 1, N = 4000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 1/4000 * 1e6 | Answer: 250 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = 4x^3 - 7x^2 - x - 2 evaluated at x = 1.

question: Find the larger real root of 2x^2 - 11x + 4 = 0.

solution: Given: a = -3, b = -7, c = -5, d = -3 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (-3)(-3) - (-7)(-5) | Answer: -26

question: Find the determinant of [[2, -5, -4], [3, 5, 0], [0, -3, -6]].

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 86, 92, 18, 23, 74.

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 12, 14, 50, 36, 30.
solution: Mean = 28.4 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 15.84

question: Find the slope of the line through (2, 2) and (-5, -6).
solution: Given: x1 = 2, y1 = 2, x2 = -5, y2 = -6 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (-6 - 2) / (-5 - 2) | Answer: 1.143

question: Find the distance between the points (-2, -7) and (-7, 1).
solution: Given: x1 = -2, y1 = -7, x2 = -7, y2 = 1 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-5)^2 + (8)^2) | Answer: 9.434 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (7,-5), (-4,-3), (0,3).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 37 sq units

question: Evaluate the number of combinations C(17, 5).
solution: Given: n = 17, r = 5 | Formula: C(n, r) = n! / (r! (n - r)!) | Substitute: C(17, 5) = 17! / (5! * 12!) | Answer: 6188

question: Evaluate the number of permutations P(14, 7).
solution: Given: n = 14, r = 7 | Formula: P(n, r) = n! / (n - r)! | Substitute: P(14, 7) = 14! / 7! | Answer: 17297280

question: Find the 31th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -10 and common difference -2.
solution: Given: a = -10, d = -2, n = 31 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -10 + (31 - 1)*-2 | Answer: -70

question: Find the sum of the first 34 terms of an AP with first term 2 and common difference -6.
solution: Given: a = 2, d = -6, n = 34 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 34/2 [2*2 + (34-1)*-6] | Answer: -3298

question: Find the 5th term of a geometric progression with first term 4 and common ratio 3.
solution: Given: a = 4, r = 3, n = 5 | Formula: a_n = a r^(n-1) | Substitute: a_n = 4 * 3^(5-1) | Answer: 324

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 31500 at 9.6% per annum for 5 years.
solution: Given: P = 31500, R = 9.6, Tt = 5 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 31500 * 9.6 * 5 / 100 | Answer: 15120 currency units

question: Find the amount when 10000 is invested at 5.2% per annum compounded annually for 4 years.
solution: Given: P = 10000, R = 5.2, Tt = 4 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 10000 * (1 + 5.2/100)^4 | Answer: 12248 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (-8, 6, 7) and (-6, 1, -4).

solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 17.12

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (6, -4, -4) and (6, 2, -1).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 52.7 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number 11 + 11i.
solution: Given: a = 11, b = 11 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((11)^2 + (11)^2) | Answer: 15.56

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number 5 + 0i.
solution: Given: a = 5, b = 0 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(0, 5) | Answer: 0 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -3x^3 + 3x^2 - 5x - 6 at x = -3.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-66 with initial guess x0=10, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.1 and ordinates 9, 8, 18, 14, 4, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 239 and 347.

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 9 and 17.
solution: Given: a = 9, b = 17 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 9*17 / 1 | Answer: 153

question: A circular rod of diameter 57 mm carries an axial tensile load of 9 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 20 mm and length 2900 mm carries an axial load of 10 kN. Take E = 70 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 22 mm transmits a torque of 1150 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 22, Tt = 1150 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(1150*1000) / (pi*(22)^3) | Answer: 550 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 68 mm and length 900 mm carries a torque of 850 N-m. With G = 80 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (68)^4 / 32 = 2099112 mm^4 | theta = (850*1000)(900) / (80000 * 2099112) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 0.261 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 38 mm wide and 190 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 38, h = 190 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 38*(190)^2 / 6 | Answer: 228633 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (47 mm x 80 mm) carries a bending moment of 36 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (64 mm x 160 mm) has effective length 2800 mm and E = 200 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 320 MPa is designed for a working stress of 140 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 320, sw = 140 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 320 / 140 | Answer: 2.286

question: A steel bar is fully restrained and heated through 30 deg C. With E = 210 GPa and alpha = 11e-6 /deg C, find the thermal stress in MPa.
solution: Given: dT = 30, E = 210, al = 11 | Formula: sigma = E alpha (dT) | Substitute: sigma = 210000 * 11e-6 * 30 | Answer: 69.3 MPa

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1200 mm and wall thickness 16 mm carries an internal pressure of 1 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1200, t = 16, P = 1 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 1*1200 / (2*16) | Answer: 37.5 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 620 K and 360 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 620, Tc = 360 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 360/620) * 100 | Answer: 41.94 %

question: A refrigerator works between 262 K (cold) and 318 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 262, Th = 318 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 262 / (318 - 262) | Answer: 4.679

question: A heat pump operates between 272 K and 326 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 272, Th = 326 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 326 / (326 - 272) | Answer: 6.037

question: 6.9 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 175 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 6.9, dT = 175 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 6.9 * 0.718 * 175 | Answer: 867 kJ

question: 2.9 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 50 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.9, dT = 50 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 2.9 * 1.005 * 50 | Answer: 145.7 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 3.8 m^3 at 550 K with mass 1.3 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 3.8, Tk = 550, m = 1.3 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 1.3*0.287*550 / 3.8 | Answer: 54 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 3.1 kg of air expands isothermally at 340 K from volume V1 to 4*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.1, Tk = 340, ratio = 4 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 3.1*0.287*340*ln(4) | Answer: 419.4 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 4.4 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.39 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 4.4, D = 0.39 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*4.4*0.39 / 0.001 | Answer: 1716000

question: Water flows at 1.9 m/s through a pipe of diameter 230 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 1.4 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 1.4 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*1.4 / 1000 | Answer: 13.73 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 3.2 m. Taking Cv = 0.99, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 3.2, cv = 0.99 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.99*sqrt(2*9.81*3.2) | Answer: 7.844 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 380 mm) water flows at 1.3 m/s. It contracts to diameter 50 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 380, d2 = 50, V1 = 1.3 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 1.3*(380/50)^2 | Answer: 75.09 m/s

question: Water flows at 1.2 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.25 m and length 170 m. With friction factor f = 0.032, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 16 teeth drives a gear of 68 teeth. If the pinion runs at 550 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 16, z2 = 68, N1 = 550 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 550*16 / 68 | Answer: 129.4 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 490 mm rotates at 1500 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 490, N = 1500 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.49)*1500 / 60 | Answer: 38.48 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 12.2 kW at 900 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 12.2, N = 900 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(12.2*1000) / (2*pi*900) | Answer: 129.4 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 4.6 kg rotates at radius 0.29 m at 950 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 10200 N/m and mass 13.4 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.

question: A plane wall of area 10 m^2 and thickness 0.37 m has conductivity k = 29.1 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 115 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 10, L = 0.37, k = 29.1, dT = 115 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 29.1*10*115 / 0.37 | Answer: 90446 W

question: A surface of area 0.8 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 25 W/m^2-K to surroundings 100 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 0.8, h = 25, dT = 100 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 25*0.8*100 | Answer: 2000 W

question: In a counter-flow heat exchanger the terminal temperature differences are 70 deg C and 20 deg C. Find the log mean temperature difference (LMTD) in deg C.
solution: Given: dT1 = 70, dT2 = 20 | Formula: LMTD = (dT1 - dT2) / ln(dT1/dT2) | Substitute: LMTD = (70 - 20) / ln(70/20) | Answer: 39.91 deg C

question: In turning, cutting speed = 110 m/min, feed = 0.28 mm/rev, depth of cut = 0.9 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 110, f = 0.28, d = 0.9 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*110*0.28*0.9 | Answer: 27720 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 110 mm is turned at 200 rpm with a feed of 0.11 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 110, N = 200, f = 0.11 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 110 / (0.11*200) | Answer: 5 min

question: A resistor of 151 ohm carries a current of 9.6 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 151, I = 9.6 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 9.6 * 151 | Answer: 145 V

question: Three resistors 28 ohm, 87 ohm and 42 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 28, R2 = 87, R3 = 42 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 28 + 87 + 42 | Answer: 157 ohm

question: Two resistors 7 ohm and 13 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 7, R2 = 13 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 7*13 / (7+13) | Answer: 4.55 ohm

question: A device draws 4.7 A at 205 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 205, I = 4.7 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 205 * 4.7 | Answer: 963.5 W

question: A current of 0.9 A flows through a 128 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 0.9, R = 128 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (0.9)^2 * 128 | Answer: 103.7 W

question: Two capacitors 46.8 uF and 38.2 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 46.8, C2 = 38.2 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 46.8*38.2 / (46.8+38.2) | Answer: 21.03 uF

question: A resistor 34 kohm and capacitor 8.5 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 34, C = 8.5 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (34k)(8.5u) = 289 ms | Answer: 289 ms

question: An inductor 414.3 mH is in series with 96 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 414.3, R = 96 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (414.3e-3) / 96 | Answer: 4.316 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 146.7 mH inductor at 720 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 146.7, f = 720 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (720)(146.7e-3) | Answer: 663.7 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 17.9 uF capacitor at 270 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 17.9, f = 270 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (270)(17.9e-6)) | Answer: 32.93 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 76 ohm, XL = 132 ohm and XC = 136 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 76, XL = 132, XC = 136 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(76^2 + (132 - 136)^2) | Answer: 76.11 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 43.3 mH and C = 9.6 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 43.3, C = 9.6 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(43.3e-3 * 9.6e-6)) | Answer: 246.9 Hz

question: A capacitor of 75.7 uF is charged to 20 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 75.7, V = 20 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*75.7e-6*(20)^2 | Answer: 15.14 mJ

question: An alternating voltage has a peak value of 314 V. Find its RMS value.
solution: Given: Vp = 314 | Formula: Vrms = Vp / sqrt(2) | Substitute: Vrms = 314 / sqrt(2) | Answer: 222 V

question: A transformer has primary voltage 250 V with 310 primary turns and 410 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 250, N1 = 310, N2 = 410 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 250 * 410/310 | Answer: 330.6 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 140 V and draws an armature current of 34 A. If the armature resistance is 1.41 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 140, Ia = 34, Ra = 1.41 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 140 - 34*1.41 | Answer: 92.06 V

question: A 4-pole induction motor on a 60 Hz supply runs at 720 rpm. Find the slip (%).

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 110 A at 415 V (line) with a power factor of 0.93. Find the total real power in kW.

question: A load has real power 65 kW and apparent power 120 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 65, S = 120 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 65 / 120 | Answer: 0.5417

question: A machine delivers 45 kW output while drawing 207 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 45, Pi = 207 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 45/207 * 100 | Answer: 21.74 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 22 V across R1 = 15 ohm and R2 = 6 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 22, R1 = 15, R2 = 6 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 22*6 / (15+6) | Answer: 6.286 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 170 kohm and Rin = 29 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 170, Rin = 29 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 170 / 29 | Answer: 5.862

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 10 kohm and Rg = 35 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 10, Rg = 35 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 10/35 | Answer: 1.286

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 6319. Express the gain in decibels (power).

question: A first-order system has a time constant of 5 s. Find the time (in s) to reach 63.2% of its final value.

question: A signal is sampled at 60 kHz. According to the Nyquist criterion, what is the maximum signal frequency that can be represented (in kHz)?

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.2 m carries a central point load of 20 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.5 m carries a UDL of 55 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.5, w = 55 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 55*(4.5)^2 / 8 | Answer: 139.2 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 3.2 m carries a point load 75 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.2, W = 75 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 75*3.2 | Answer: 240 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 3.8 m carries a UDL of 6 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.8, w = 6 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 6*(3.8)^2 / 2 | Answer: 43.32 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 5.4 m carries a point load 10 kN at distance 2.1 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 5.4, a = 2.1, W = 10 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 10*(5.4 - 2.1) / 5.4 | Answer: 6.111 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 7.3 m) carries a central point load 80 kN. With E = 25 GPa and I = 230e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=80000 N, L=7300.0 mm, E=25000 MPa, I=230e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 112.8 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 7.9 m carries a UDL of 9 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7.9, w = 9 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 9*(7.9)^2 / 12 | Answer: 46.81 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 320 mm, clear cover 45 mm and main bars of diameter 20 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 320, c = 45, dia = 20 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 320 - 45 - 20/2 | Answer: 265 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 14.8 m^2 carrying a factored load of 11.6 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 14.8, w = 11.6 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 11.6 * 14.8 | Answer: 171.7 kN

question: For a bar of diameter 12 mm with design bond stress 1.6 MPa and steel stress 360 MPa, find the development length in mm.
solution: Given: dia = 12, tbd = 1.6, fs = 360 | Formula: Ld = phi fs / (4 tau_bd) | Substitute: Ld = 12*360 / (4*1.6) | Answer: 675 mm

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 3.5 m, unit weight 20 kN/m^3, phi = 29 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 8.3 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 21 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 8.3, g = 21 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (21 - 9.81)*8.3 | Answer: 92.88 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 4.3e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1, area = 3.3e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 4.3, i = 1, A = 3.3 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (4.3e-4)*1*(3.3e-3) | Answer: 1419 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 2 m, bed slope 0.005 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.014. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 2.4 m under a head of 1 m. Taking Cd = 0.62 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 2.3 m wide carries a discharge of 5 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 550 m and design speed 55 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 550, V = 55 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (55)^2 / (127*550) | Answer: 0.04331
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: For a design speed of 100 km/h with allowable superelevation 0.08 and lateral friction 0.15, find the minimum curve radius in m.
A tank of volume 330 m^3 treats a flow of 25 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 330, Q = 25 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 330 / 25 | Answer: 13.2 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 210 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.23 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 8 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 210, k = 0.23, t = 8 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 210*(1 - e^(-0.23*8)) | Answer: 176.6 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.73, rainfall intensity 40 mm/h over a catchment of 60 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.73, i = 40, A = 60 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.73*40*60 / 360 | Answer: 4.867 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.07 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 320 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.07, M = 320 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 320*(30+0.07)/30 | Answer: 320.7 m

question: Convert the decimal number 43 to binary.
solution: Divide 43 by 2 repeatedly, recording remainders | Reading remainders in reverse gives 101011 | Answer: 101011 (binary)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 2 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the decimal number 3852 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 3852 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: F0C (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the 8-bit binary number 10100111 to decimal.
solution: Binary 10100111 = sum of bit-weights | Answer: 167 (decimal)
formula: Sum each bit times its positional weight (2^i)

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 10100001 and 00010111.
solution: XOR: 10110110 | Count of 1s = 5 | Answer: 5
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 90 megabits is sent over a link of 22 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 90, B = 22 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 90 / 22 | Answer: 4.091 s

question: A link has bandwidth 17 Mbps and round-trip time 40 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 17, R = 40 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 17e6 * 40e-3 bits = 680 kb | Answer: 680 kilobits

question: A channel of bandwidth 12 kHz has a signal-to-noise ratio of 15 (linear). Using Shannon's theorem, find the channel capacity in kbps.
solution: Given: B = 12, SNR = 15 | Formula: C = B log2(1 + SNR) | Substitute: C = 12*log2(1 + 15) | Answer: 48 kbps

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.91, cache access time 8 ns and main-memory access time 80 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.91, tc = 8, tm = 80 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.91*8 + (1 - 0.91)*80 | Answer: 14.48 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 250996 elements?
solution: Given: n = 250996 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(250996)) + 1 | Answer: 18

question: An O(n^2) algorithm performs c*n^2 basic operations. If c = 1 and n = 2990, how many operations are performed?
solution: Given: n = 2990 | Formula: operations = n^2 | Substitute: = (2990)^2 | Answer: 8940100

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.009, memory access time 100 ns and page-fault service time 5 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 5 ms = 5000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.009)*100 + 0.009*5000000.0 ns | Answer: 45.1 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 1.5 m^3 at 160 kPa and 530 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 1.5, P = 160, Tk = 530 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (160e3)*1.5 / (8.314*530) | Answer: 54.47 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.08 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 11 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.08, t = 11 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.08*11) | Answer: 0.5852

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.4 /min) is to reach 70% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.4, X = 70 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.7) / 0.4 | Answer: 3.01 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.33 /min) reaches 65% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.33, X = 65 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.65 / (0.33*(1 - 0.65)) | Answer: 5.628 min

question: For a reaction with A = 6e10 /s and activation energy 55 kJ/mol at 370 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 6, Ea = 55, Tk = 370 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 6e10 * exp(-55e3 / (8.314*370)) | Answer: 1031 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.99 and bottoms xW = 0.09, with relative volatility alpha = 1.6. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.99, xw = 0.09, al = 1.6 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.99/0.01)(0.91/0.09)] / ln(1.6) | Answer: 14.7 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.74 and x = 0.42. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.74, x = 0.42 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.74/0.26) / (0.42/0.58) | Answer: 3.93

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.36 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 65 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.36, Psat = 65 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.36 * 65 | Answer: 23.4 kPa

question: A stream of 4.4 kg/s with specific heat 3.6 kJ/kg-K is heated through 20 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 4.4, cp = 3.6, dT = 20 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 4.4*3.6*20 | Answer: 316.8 kW

question: A reactor of volume 12.8 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 4.3 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 12.8, Q = 4.3 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 12.8 / 4.3 | Answer: 2.977 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 2.9e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 5 mm with a concentration difference of 190 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 2.9, L = 5, dC = 190 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (2.9e-9)*190 / (5e-3) | Answer: 110.2 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 9.3 min and steady-state gain 1.8. For a step input of magnitude 12, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 9.3, K = 1.8, M = 12 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 1.8 * 12 | Answer: 21.6 units

question: A reactor operates at a space time of 8.3 min. Find its space velocity in per hour.
solution: Given: tau = 8.3 | Formula: SV = 60 / tau  (per hour) | Substitute: SV = 60 / 8.3 | Answer: 7.229 /h

question: An aircraft wing of area 80 m^2 flies at 90 m/s (air density 0.4 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.6. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 80, V = 90, rho = 0.4, CL = 0.6 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.4*(90)^2*80*0.6 / 1000 | Answer: 77.76 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 115 m^2 flies at 140 m/s (density 1 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.07. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 115, V = 140, rho = 1, CD = 0.07 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*1*(140)^2*115*0.07 / 1000 | Answer: 78.89 kN

question: Find the dynamic pressure for air of density 0.7 kg/m^3 moving at 270 m/s, in Pa.
solution: Given: rho = 0.7, V = 270 | Formula: q = 0.5 rho V^2 | Substitute: q = 0.5*0.7*(270)^2 | Answer: 25515 Pa

question: An aircraft flies at 520 m/s where the speed of sound is 340 m/s. Find the Mach number.
solution: Given: V = 520, a = 340 | Formula: M = V / a | Substitute: M = 520 / 340 | Answer: 1.529

question: A specimen under stress 110 MPa shows an elastic strain of 0.5e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 110, eps = 0.5 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 110 / (0.5e-3) MPa = 220 GPa | Answer: 220 GPa

question: A block of mass 14 kg has a volume of 5.4e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 14, V = 5.4 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 14 / (5.4e-3) | Answer: 2593 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 800 mm is heated through 95 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 11e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 800, dT = 95, al = 11 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 800*11e-6*95 | Answer: 0.836 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 155 ohm, R2 = 45 ohm and R3 = 370 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 155, R2 = 45, R3 = 370 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 45*370 / 155 | Answer: 107.4 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 350 ohm and gauge factor 2.2 experiences a strain of 800e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 350, GF = 2.2, eps = 800 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 350*2.2*800e-6 | Answer: 616 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 9.56 when the true value is 10. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.56, true = 10 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.56 - 10| / 10 * 100 | Answer: 4.4 %

question: Annual demand is 48500 units, ordering cost 140 per order and holding cost 20 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 48500, S = 140, H = 20 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*48500*140 / 20) | Answer: 824 units

question: An asset costs 80000 with salvage value 32000 after 20 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 80000, Sv = 32000, n = 20 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (80000 - 32000) / 20 | Answer: 2400 per year

question: A product sells for 210 per unit with variable cost 60 per unit and fixed costs 105000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 210, V = 60, F = 105000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 105000 / (210 - 60) | Answer: 700 units

question: Find the present worth of 105000 received 7 years from now at an interest rate of 5% per year.
solution: Given: F = 105000, n = 7, i = 5 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 105000 / (1 + 0.05)^7 | Answer: 74622 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.95, 0.98 and 0.95 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.95, r2 = 0.98, r3 = 0.95 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.95*0.98*0.95 | Answer: 0.8844

question: A process produces 13 defective items in a batch of 4500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 13, N = 4500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 13/4500 * 1e6 | Answer: 2889 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -6x^3 - 5x^2 - 7x - 8 evaluated at x = 3.
For f(x) = 2x^3 + 4x + 9, find f''(x) at x = 1.

question: Find the slope of the line through (8, 0) and (-6, 4).
solution: Given: x1 = 8, y1 = 0, x2 = -6, y2 = 4 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (4 - 0) / (-6 - 8) | Answer: -0.2857

question: Find the distance between the points (-2, 3) and (-5, 3).
solution: Given: x1 = -2, y1 = 3, x2 = -5, y2 = 3 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-3)^2 + (0)^2) | Answer: 3 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (-7,-8), (0,4), (-1,-1).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 11.5 sq units

question: Evaluate the number of combinations C(9, 8).
solution: Given: n = 9, r = 8 | Formula: C(n, r) = n! / (r! (n - r)!) | Substitute: C(9, 8) = 9! / (8! * 1!) | Answer: 9

question: Evaluate the number of permutations P(10, 9).
solution: Given: n = 10, r = 9 | Formula: P(n, r) = n! / (n - r)! | Substitute: P(10, 9) = 10! / 1! | Answer: 3628800

question: Find the 40th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -4 and common difference 6.
solution: Given: a = -4, d = 6, n = 40 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -4 + (40 - 1)*6 | Answer: 230

question: Find the sum of the first 33 terms of an AP with first term 7 and common difference 8.
solution: Given: a = 7, d = 8, n = 33 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 33/2 [2*7 + (33-1)*8] | Answer: 4455

question: Find the 7th term of a geometric progression with first term 9 and common ratio 3.
solution: Given: a = 9, r = 3, n = 7 | Formula: a_n = a r^(n-1) | Substitute: a_n = 9 * 3^(7-1) | Answer: 6561

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 46500 at 12.8% per annum for 4 years.
solution: Given: P = 46500, R = 12.8, Tt = 4 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 46500 * 12.8 * 4 / 100 | Answer: 23808 currency units

question: Find the amount when 1000 is invested at 7.1% per annum compounded annually for 3 years.
solution: Given: P = 1000, R = 7.1, Tt = 3 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 1000 * (1 + 7.1/100)^3 | Answer: 1228 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (7, 2, 5) and (-4, -6, -8).

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (-6, 6, -5) and (3, 5, -1).

question: Find the modulus of the complex number -10 + -7i.
solution: Given: a = -10, b = -7 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((-10)^2 + (-7)^2) | Answer: 12.21

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number -6 + -6i.
solution: Given: a = -6, b = -6 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(-6, -6) | Answer: -135 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = 5x^3 - x^2 + 9x + 1 at x = 0.
solution: Given: a = 5, b = -1, c = 9, d = 1, x0 = 0 | Formula: f(x0) = a x0^3 + b x0^2 + c x0 + d | Substitute: f(0) = 5(0)^3 + -1(0)^2 + 9(0) + 1 | Answer: 1

question: Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-134 with initial guess x0=2, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.6 and ordinates 11, 16, 18, 17, 11, estimate the integral.

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 18 and 12.

question: A circular rod of diameter 40 mm carries an axial tensile load of 59 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 18 mm and length 700 mm carries an axial load of 51 kN. Take E = 110 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 39 mm transmits a torque of 600 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 39, Tt = 600 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(600*1000) / (pi*(39)^3) | Answer: 51.51 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 59 mm and length 900 mm carries a torque of 200 N-m. With G = 80 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (59)^4 / 32 = 1189619 mm^4 | theta = (200*1000)(900) / (80000 * 1189619) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 0.1084 degrees

question: A rectangular beam section is 149 mm wide and 250 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 149, h = 250 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 149*(250)^2 / 6 | Answer: 1552083 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (62 mm x 220 mm) carries a bending moment of 6 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (49 mm x 140 mm) has effective length 4000 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 890 MPa is designed for a working stress of 110 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 890, sw = 110 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 890 / 110 | Answer: 8.091

question: A steel bar is fully restrained and heated through 100 deg C. With E = 210 GPa and alpha = 13e-6 /deg C, find the thermal stress in MPa.
solution: Given: dT = 100, E = 210, al = 13 | Formula: sigma = E alpha (dT) | Substitute: sigma = 210000 * 13e-6 * 100 | Answer: 273 MPa

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 600 mm and wall thickness 11 mm carries an internal pressure of 2.4 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 600, t = 11, P = 2.4 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 2.4*600 / (2*11) | Answer: 65.45 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 1200 K and 350 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 1200, Tc = 350 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 350/1200) * 100 | Answer: 70.83 %

question: A refrigerator works between 254 K (cold) and 310 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 254, Th = 310 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 254 / (310 - 254) | Answer: 4.536

question: A heat pump operates between 262 K and 320 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 262, Th = 320 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 320 / (320 - 262) | Answer: 5.517

question: 2.6 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 85 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.6, dT = 85 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 2.6 * 0.718 * 85 | Answer: 158.7 kJ

question: 6 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 100 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 6, dT = 100 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 6 * 1.005 * 100 | Answer: 603 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 3.3 m^3 at 550 K with mass 2 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 3.3, Tk = 550, m = 2 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 2*0.287*550 / 3.3 | Answer: 95.67 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 3.6 kg of air expands isothermally at 430 K from volume V1 to 2*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.6, Tk = 430, ratio = 2 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 3.6*0.287*430*ln(2) | Answer: 307.9 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 3.5 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.26 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 3.5, D = 0.26 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*3.5*0.26 / 0.001 | Answer: 910000

question: Water flows at 3.2 m/s through a pipe of diameter 120 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 1.2 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 1.2 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*1.2 / 1000 | Answer: 11.77 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 16.5 m. Taking Cv = 0.97, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 16.5, cv = 0.97 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.97*sqrt(2*9.81*16.5) | Answer: 17.45 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 260 mm) water flows at 2.5 m/s. It contracts to diameter 90 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 260, d2 = 90, V1 = 2.5 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 2.5*(260/90)^2 | Answer: 20.86 m/s

question: Water flows at 1.3 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.42 m and length 220 m. With friction factor f = 0.036, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 31 teeth drives a gear of 102 teeth. If the pinion runs at 500 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 31, z2 = 102, N1 = 500 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 500*31 / 102 | Answer: 152 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 510 mm rotates at 1200 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 510, N = 1200 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.51)*1200 / 60 | Answer: 32.04 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 23.6 kW at 500 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 23.6, N = 500 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(23.6*1000) / (2*pi*500) | Answer: 450.7 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 5.9 kg rotates at radius 0.25 m at 800 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 7900 N/m and mass 7 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 7900, m = 7 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(7900/7) | Answer: 5.347 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 1.5 m^2 and thickness 0.36 m has conductivity k = 49.7 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 100 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 1.5, L = 0.36, k = 49.7, dT = 100 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 49.7*1.5*100 / 0.36 | Answer: 20708 W

question: A surface of area 5.1 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 90 W/m^2-K to surroundings 95 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 5.1, h = 90, dT = 95 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 90*5.1*95 | Answer: 43605 W

question: In a counter-flow heat exchanger the terminal temperature differences are 85 deg C and 5 deg C. Find the log mean temperature difference (LMTD) in deg C.
solution: Given: dT1 = 85, dT2 = 5 | Formula: LMTD = (dT1 - dT2) / ln(dT1/dT2) | Substitute: LMTD = (85 - 5) / ln(85/5) | Answer: 28.24 deg C

question: In turning, cutting speed = 130 m/min, feed = 0.5 mm/rev, depth of cut = 0.5 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 130, f = 0.5, d = 0.5 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*130*0.5*0.5 | Answer: 32500 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 200 mm is turned at 1050 rpm with a feed of 0.31 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 200, N = 1050, f = 0.31 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 200 / (0.31*1050) | Answer: 0.6144 min

question: A resistor of 29 ohm carries a current of 8.7 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 29, I = 8.7 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 8.7 * 29 | Answer: 252.3 V

question: Three resistors 99 ohm, 16 ohm and 92 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 99, R2 = 16, R3 = 92 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 99 + 16 + 92 | Answer: 207 ohm

question: Two resistors 43 ohm and 7 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 43, R2 = 7 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 43*7 / (43+7) | Answer: 6.02 ohm

question: A device draws 8.1 A at 215 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 215, I = 8.1 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 215 * 8.1 | Answer: 1742 W

question: A current of 9.2 A flows through a 113 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 9.2, R = 113 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (9.2)^2 * 113 | Answer: 9564 W

question: Two capacitors 37.1 uF and 2.8 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 37.1, C2 = 2.8 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 37.1*2.8 / (37.1+2.8) | Answer: 2.604 uF

question: A resistor 18 kohm and capacitor 15.4 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 18, C = 15.4 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (18k)(15.4u) = 277.2 ms | Answer: 277.2 ms

question: An inductor 375.4 mH is in series with 136 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 375.4, R = 136 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (375.4e-3) / 136 | Answer: 2.76 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 94.5 mH inductor at 790 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 94.5, f = 790 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (790)(94.5e-3) | Answer: 469.1 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 27.3 uF capacitor at 770 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 27.3, f = 770 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (770)(27.3e-6)) | Answer: 7.571 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 13 ohm, XL = 90 ohm and XC = 54 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 13, XL = 90, XC = 54 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(13^2 + (90 - 54)^2) | Answer: 38.28 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 78.7 mH and C = 4.9 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 78.7, C = 4.9 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(78.7e-3 * 4.9e-6)) | Answer: 256.3 Hz

question: A capacitor of 29.9 uF is charged to 95 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 29.9, V = 95 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*29.9e-6*(95)^2 | Answer: 134.9 mJ

question: An alternating voltage has a peak value of 150 V. Find its RMS value.
solution: Given: Vp = 150 | Formula: Vrms = Vp / sqrt(2) | Substitute: Vrms = 150 / sqrt(2) | Answer: 106.1 V

question: A transformer has primary voltage 270 V with 360 primary turns and 440 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 270, N1 = 360, N2 = 440 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 270 * 440/360 | Answer: 330 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 390 V and draws an armature current of 33 A. If the armature resistance is 1.07 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 390, Ia = 33, Ra = 1.07 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 390 - 33*1.07 | Answer: 354.7 V

question: A 4-pole induction motor on a 60 Hz supply runs at 860 rpm. Find the slip (%).
formula: s = (Ns - N) / Ns,  Ns = 120 f / P

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 130 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.72. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 130, VL = 400, pf = 0.72 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*400*130*0.72 / 1000 | Answer: 64.85 kW

question: A load has real power 95 kW and apparent power 220 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 95, S = 220 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 95 / 220 | Answer: 0.4318

question: A machine delivers 60 kW output while drawing 187 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 60, Pi = 187 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 60/187 * 100 | Answer: 32.09 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 26 V across R1 = 43 ohm and R2 = 30 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 26, R1 = 43, R2 = 30 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 26*30 / (43+30) | Answer: 10.68 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 180 kohm and Rin = 6 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 180, Rin = 6 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 180 / 6 | Answer: 30

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 190 kohm and Rg = 10 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 190, Rg = 10 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 190/10 | Answer: 20

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 4220. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 4220 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(4220) | Answer: 36.25 dB

question: A first-order system has a time constant of 5.1 s. Find the time (in s) to reach 63.2% of its final value.
solution: For a first-order step response, y = 1 - e^(-t/tau) | y = 0.632 when t = tau | Answer: 5.1 s
formula: At t = tau the response reaches 63.2% (one time constant)

question: A simply supported beam of span 7.2 m carries a central point load of 105 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7.2, W = 105 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 105*7.2 / 4 | Answer: 189 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 5.4 m carries a UDL of 15 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.4, w = 15 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 15*(5.4)^2 / 8 | Answer: 54.68 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 1.2 m carries a point load 10 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 1.2, W = 10 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 10*1.2 | Answer: 12 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 5.4 m carries a UDL of 8 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.4, w = 8 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 8*(5.4)^2 / 2 | Answer: 116.6 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.2 m carries a point load 10 kN at distance 1.6 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 6.2, a = 1.6, W = 10 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 10*(6.2 - 1.6) / 6.2 | Answer: 7.419 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 3.8 m) carries a central point load 70 kN. With E = 30 GPa and I = 590e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=70000 N, L=3800.0 mm, E=30000 MPa, I=590e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 4.521 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 4.3 m carries a UDL of 39 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.3, w = 39 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 39*(4.3)^2 / 12 | Answer: 60.09 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 600 mm, clear cover 25 mm and main bars of diameter 25 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 600, c = 25, dia = 25 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 600 - 25 - 25/2 | Answer: 562.5 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 18 m^2 carrying a factored load of 17.3 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 18, w = 17.3 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 17.3 * 18 | Answer: 311.4 kN

question: For a bar of diameter 20 mm with design bond stress 2.1 MPa and steel stress 435 MPa, find the development length in mm.
solution: Given: dia = 20, tbd = 2.1, fs = 435 | Formula: Ld = phi fs / (4 tau_bd) | Substitute: Ld = 20*435 / (4*2.1) | Answer: 1036 mm

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 6.4 m, unit weight 17 kN/m^3, phi = 38 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 10.8 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 19 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 10.8, g = 19 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (19 - 9.81)*10.8 | Answer: 99.25 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 7.3e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1.2, area = 2.3e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 7.3, i = 1.2, A = 2.3 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (7.3e-4)*1.2*(2.3e-3) | Answer: 2015 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.9 m, bed slope 0.004 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.025. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 4.7 m under a head of 0.9 m. Taking Cd = 0.63 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 4.5 m wide carries a discharge of 7.3 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 350 m and design speed 65 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 350, V = 65 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (65)^2 / (127*350) | Answer: 0.09505
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: For a design speed of 70 km/h with allowable superelevation 0.05 and lateral friction 0.14, find the minimum curve radius in m.
A tank of volume 640 m^3 treats a flow of 30 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 640, Q = 30 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 640 / 30 | Answer: 21.33 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 310 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.33 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 5 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 310, k = 0.33, t = 5 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 310*(1 - e^(-0.33*5)) | Answer: 250.5 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.89, rainfall intensity 50 mm/h over a catchment of 46.8 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.89, i = 50, A = 46.8 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.89*50*46.8 / 360 | Answer: 5.785 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.07 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 270 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.07, M = 270 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 270*(20+0.07)/20 | Answer: 270.9 m

question: Convert the decimal number 175 to binary.
solution: Divide 175 by 2 repeatedly, recording remainders | Reading remainders in reverse gives 10101111 | Answer: 10101111 (binary)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 2 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the decimal number 2966 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 2966 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: B96 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the 8-bit binary number 01011000 to decimal.
solution: Binary 01011000 = sum of bit-weights | Answer: 88 (decimal)
formula: Sum each bit times its positional weight (2^i)

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 11011011 and 11001001.
solution: XOR: 00010010 | Count of 1s = 2 | Answer: 2
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 870 megabits is sent over a link of 82 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 870, B = 82 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 870 / 82 | Answer: 10.61 s

question: A link has bandwidth 76 Mbps and round-trip time 150 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 76, R = 150 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 76e6 * 150e-3 bits = 11400 kb | Answer: 11400 kilobits

question: A channel has bandwidth 9 kHz. Using Nyquist's theorem with 2 signal levels, find the maximum data rate in kbps (noiseless).
solution: Given: B = 9, M = 2 | Formula: C = 2 B log2(M) | Substitute: C = 2*9*log2(2) | Answer: 18 kbps

question: A channel of bandwidth 7 kHz has a signal-to-noise ratio of 63 (linear). Using Shannon's theorem, find the channel capacity in kbps.
solution: Given: B = 7, SNR = 63 | Formula: C = B log2(1 + SNR) | Substitute: C = 7*log2(1 + 63) | Answer: 42 kbps

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.83, cache access time 1 ns and main-memory access time 70 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.83, tc = 1, tm = 70 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.83*1 + (1 - 0.83)*70 | Answer: 12.73 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 590102 elements?
solution: Given: n = 590102 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(590102)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: An O(n^2) algorithm performs c*n^2 basic operations. If c = 1 and n = 160, how many operations are performed?
solution: Given: n = 160 | Formula: operations = n^2 | Substitute: = (160)^2 | Answer: 25600

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.01, memory access time 200 ns and page-fault service time 4 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 4 ms = 4000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.01)*200 + 0.01*4000000.0 ns | Answer: 40.2 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: A modem transmits at 3000 baud using 4-level signalling. Find the bit rate in bps.
solution: Given: baud = 3000, M = 4 | Formula: bit rate = baud * log2(M) | Substitute: bit rate = 3000 * log2(4) | Answer: 6000 bps

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 1.7 m^3 at 160 kPa and 560 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 1.7, P = 160, Tk = 560 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (160e3)*1.7 / (8.314*560) | Answer: 58.42 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.23 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 12 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.23, t = 12 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.23*12) | Answer: 0.9367

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.11 /min) is to reach 85% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.11, X = 85 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.85) / 0.11 | Answer: 17.25 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.14 /min) reaches 85% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.14, X = 85 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.85 / (0.14*(1 - 0.85)) | Answer: 40.48 min

question: For a reaction with A = 3e10 /s and activation energy 75 kJ/mol at 390 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 3, Ea = 75, Tk = 390 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 3e10 * exp(-75e3 / (8.314*390)) | Answer: 2.702 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.95 and bottoms xW = 0.06, with relative volatility alpha = 3.4. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.95, xw = 0.06, al = 3.4 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.95/0.05)(0.94/0.06)] / ln(3.4) | Answer: 4.654 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.69 and x = 0.41. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.69, x = 0.41 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.69/0.31) / (0.41/0.59) | Answer: 3.203

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.59 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 40 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.59, Psat = 40 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.59 * 40 | Answer: 23.6 kPa

question: A stream of 9.4 kg/s with specific heat 2 kJ/kg-K is heated through 80 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 9.4, cp = 2, dT = 80 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 9.4*2*80 | Answer: 1504 kW

question: A reactor of volume 12.8 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 1.8 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 12.8, Q = 1.8 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 12.8 / 1.8 | Answer: 7.111 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 8.8e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 3 mm with a concentration difference of 20 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 8.8, L = 3, dC = 20 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (8.8e-9)*20 / (3e-3) | Answer: 58.67 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 5.7 min and steady-state gain 3.4. For a step input of magnitude 4, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 5.7, K = 3.4, M = 4 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 3.4 * 4 | Answer: 13.6 units

question: A reactor operates at a space time of 13.2 min. Find its space velocity in per hour.
solution: Given: tau = 13.2 | Formula: SV = 60 / tau  (per hour) | Substitute: SV = 60 / 13.2 | Answer: 4.545 /h

question: An aircraft wing of area 30 m^2 flies at 80 m/s (air density 0.4 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 1. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 30, V = 80, rho = 0.4, CL = 1 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.4*(80)^2*30*1 / 1000 | Answer: 38.4 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 65 m^2 flies at 190 m/s (density 0.7 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.08. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 65, V = 190, rho = 0.7, CD = 0.08 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.7*(190)^2*65*0.08 / 1000 | Answer: 65.7 kN

question: An aircraft flies at 190 m/s where the speed of sound is 340 m/s. Find the Mach number.
solution: Given: V = 190, a = 340 | Formula: M = V / a | Substitute: M = 190 / 340 | Answer: 0.5588

question: A specimen under stress 360 MPa shows an elastic strain of 3e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 360, eps = 3 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 360 / (3e-3) MPa = 120 GPa | Answer: 120 GPa

question: A block of mass 39 kg has a volume of 3.9e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 39, V = 3.9 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 39 / (3.9e-3) | Answer: 10000 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 1600 mm is heated through 125 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 11e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 1600, dT = 125, al = 11 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 1600*11e-6*125 | Answer: 2.2 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 65 ohm, R2 = 195 ohm and R3 = 40 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 65, R2 = 195, R3 = 40 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 195*40 / 65 | Answer: 120 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 350 ohm and gauge factor 2.1 experiences a strain of 1450e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 350, GF = 2.1, eps = 1450 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 350*2.1*1450e-6 | Answer: 1066 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 9.58 when the true value is 20. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.58, true = 20 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.58 - 20| / 20 * 100 | Answer: 52.1 %

question: Annual demand is 26500 units, ordering cost 30 per order and holding cost 6 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 26500, S = 30, H = 6 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*26500*30 / 6) | Answer: 514.8 units

question: An asset costs 290000 with salvage value 20000 after 7 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 290000, Sv = 20000, n = 7 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (290000 - 20000) / 7 | Answer: 38571 per year

question: A product sells for 360 per unit with variable cost 160 per unit and fixed costs 15000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 360, V = 160, F = 15000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 15000 / (360 - 160) | Answer: 75 units

question: Find the present worth of 150000 received 10 years from now at an interest rate of 8% per year.
solution: Given: F = 150000, n = 10, i = 8 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 150000 / (1 + 0.08)^10 | Answer: 69479 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.9, 0.96 and 0.95 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.9, r2 = 0.96, r3 = 0.95 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.9*0.96*0.95 | Answer: 0.8208

question: A process produces 49 defective items in a batch of 13500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 49, N = 13500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 49/13500 * 1e6 | Answer: 363 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = 4x^3 - 3x - 3 evaluated at x = -1.
For f(x) = -4x^3 - 3x + 6, find f''(x) at x = -3.
Evaluate the definite integral of (2x^2 + 5x + 6) dx from x = 1 to x = 4.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = 2x^3/3 + 5x^2/2 + 6x | Evaluate F(4) - F(1) | Answer: 97.5
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of x^2 - 5x + 1 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[-9, -7], [-7, -2]].
solution: Given: a = -9, b = -7, c = -7, d = -2 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (-9)(-2) - (-7)(-7) | Answer: -31

question: Find the determinant of [[2, -6, 0], [4, -4, 0], [0, -2, -2]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: -32

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[6, -5], [-3, 8]].
solution: Trace tr = 14, Determinant = 33 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 11

question: Solve for x: 1x + -2y = 1 and 6x + 2y = -6.
solution: Determinant = 1*2 - -2*6 = 14 | x = (e d - b f) / det = -0.7143 | Answer: x = -0.7143
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 1, 36, 74, 28, 18.
solution: Sum = 157 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 31.4 | Answer: 31.4

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 5, 9, 6, 9, 29.
solution: Mean = 11.6 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 9.889

question: Find the slope of the line through (9, 5) and (1, 8).
solution: Given: x1 = 9, y1 = 5, x2 = 1, y2 = 8 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (8 - 5) / (1 - 9) | Answer: -0.375

question: Find the distance between the points (-2, 9) and (3, 2).
solution: Given: x1 = -2, y1 = 9, x2 = 3, y2 = 2 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((5)^2 + (-7)^2) | Answer: 8.602 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (6,-3), (2,-7), (6,-8).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 10 sq units

question: Evaluate the number of combinations C(5, 3).
solution: Given: n = 5, r = 3 | Formula: C(n, r) = n! / (r! (n - r)!) | Substitute: C(5, 3) = 5! / (3! * 2!) | Answer: 10

question: Find the 15th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -7 and common difference 0.
solution: Given: a = -7, d = 0, n = 15 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -7 + (15 - 1)*0 | Answer: -7

question: Find the sum of the first 13 terms of an AP with first term 11 and common difference -5.
solution: Given: a = 11, d = -5, n = 13 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 13/2 [2*11 + (13-1)*-5] | Answer: -247

question: Find the 8th term of a geometric progression with first term 3 and common ratio 3.
solution: Given: a = 3, r = 3, n = 8 | Formula: a_n = a r^(n-1) | Substitute: a_n = 3 * 3^(8-1) | Answer: 6561

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 46500 at 7.3% per annum for 9 years.
solution: Given: P = 46500, R = 7.3, Tt = 9 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 46500 * 7.3 * 9 / 100 | Answer: 3055 currency units

question: Find the amount when 25000 is invested at 7.6% per annum compounded annually for 4 years.
solution: Given: P = 25000, R = 7.6, Tt = 4 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 25000 * (1 + 7.6/100)^4 | Answer: 33511 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (1, -8, 7) and (2, -5, -1).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (2, -3, -3) and (-2, 2, 1).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 5.385

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (6, -1, -2) and (6, 6, 6).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 74.31 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number -2 + -6i.
solution: Given: a = -2, b = -6 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((-2)^2 + (-6)^2) | Answer: 6.325

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number 6 + 12i.
solution: Given: a = 6, b = 12 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(12, 6) | Answer: 63.43 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = x^3 - 2x^2 + 2x + 5 at x = 4.
solution: Given: a = 1, b = -2, c = 2, d = 5, x0 = 4 | Formula: f(x0) = a x0^3 + b x0^2 + c x0 + d | Substitute: f(4) = 1(4)^3 + -2(4)^2 + 2(4) + 5 | Answer: 45

question: Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-105 with initial guess x0=10, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.6 and ordinates 1, 20, 1, 9, 1, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 553 and 570.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 553 and 570 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 43 and 73.
solution: Given: a = 43, b = 73 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 43*73 / 1 | Answer: 3139
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 15 mm carries an axial tensile load of 63 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 25 mm and length 2200 mm carries an axial load of 57 kN. Take E = 210 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 53 mm transmits a torque of 500 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 53, Tt = 500 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(500*1000) / (pi*(53)^3) | Answer: 17.1 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 26 mm and length 1000 mm carries a torque of 500 N-m. With G = 45 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (26)^4 / 32 = 44864 mm^4 | theta = (500*1000)(1000) / (45000 * 44864) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 14.19 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 96 mm wide and 90 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 96, h = 90 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 96*(90)^2 / 6 | Answer: 129600 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (105 mm x 130 mm) carries a bending moment of 25 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (40 mm x 150 mm) has effective length 3000 mm and E = 200 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 400 MPa is designed for a working stress of 240 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 400, sw = 240 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 400 / 240 | Answer: 1.667

question: A steel bar is fully restrained and heated through 90 deg C. With E = 210 GPa and alpha = 12e-6 /deg C, find the thermal stress in MPa.
solution: Given: dT = 90, E = 210, al = 12 | Formula: sigma = E alpha (dT) | Substitute: sigma = 210000 * 12e-6 * 90 | Answer: 226.8 MPa

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 550 mm and wall thickness 12 mm carries an internal pressure of 2.7 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 550, t = 12, P = 2.7 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 2.7*550 / (2*12) | Answer: 61.88 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 1140 K and 380 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 1140, Tc = 380 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 380/1140) * 100 | Answer: 66.67 %

question: A refrigerator works between 266 K (cold) and 300 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 266, Th = 300 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 266 / (300 - 266) | Answer: 7.824

question: A heat pump operates between 276 K and 302 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 276, Th = 302 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 302 / (302 - 276) | Answer: 11.62

question: 7.8 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 195 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 7.8, dT = 195 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 7.8 * 0.718 * 195 | Answer: 1092 kJ

question: 6 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 115 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 6, dT = 115 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 6 * 1.005 * 115 | Answer: 693.4 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 2.2 m^3 at 580 K with mass 3.5 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 2.2, Tk = 580, m = 3.5 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 3.5*0.287*580 / 2.2 | Answer: 264.8 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 3.6 kg of air expands isothermally at 310 K from volume V1 to 2*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.6, Tk = 310, ratio = 2 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 3.6*0.287*310*ln(2) | Answer: 222 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 0.6 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.21 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 0.6, D = 0.21 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*0.6*0.21 / 0.001 | Answer: 126000

question: Water flows at 2 m/s through a pipe of diameter 210 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 5.4 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 5.4 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*5.4 / 1000 | Answer: 52.97 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 11.9 m. Taking Cv = 0.97, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 11.9, cv = 0.97 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.97*sqrt(2*9.81*11.9) | Answer: 14.82 m/s
