question: In a pipe (diameter 220 mm) water flows at 1.1 m/s. It contracts to diameter 50 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 220, d2 = 50, V1 = 1.1 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 1.1*(220/50)^2 | Answer: 21.3 m/s

question: Water flows at 2.1 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.38 m and length 320 m. With friction factor f = 0.036, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 25 teeth drives a gear of 117 teeth. If the pinion runs at 900 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 25, z2 = 117, N1 = 900 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 900*25 / 117 | Answer: 192.3 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 280 mm rotates at 1250 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 280, N = 1250 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.28)*1250 / 60 | Answer: 18.33 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 39 kW at 1100 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 39, N = 1100 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(39*1000) / (2*pi*1100) | Answer: 338.6 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 3.1 kg rotates at radius 0.41 m at 1150 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 2500 N/m and mass 19.6 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 2500, m = 19.6 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(2500/19.6) | Answer: 1.797 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 3.5 m^2 and thickness 0.38 m has conductivity k = 49.4 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 200 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 3.5, L = 0.38, k = 49.4, dT = 200 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 49.4*3.5*200 / 0.38 | Answer: 91000 W

question: A surface of area 4.6 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 80 W/m^2-K to surroundings 135 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 4.6, h = 80, dT = 135 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 80*4.6*135 | Answer: 49680 W

question: In a counter-flow heat exchanger the terminal temperature differences are 120 deg C and 15 deg C. Find the log mean temperature difference (LMTD) in deg C.
solution: Given: dT1 = 120, dT2 = 15 | Formula: LMTD = (dT1 - dT2) / ln(dT1/dT2) | Substitute: LMTD = (120 - 15) / ln(120/15) | Answer: 50.49 deg C

question: In turning, cutting speed = 170 m/min, feed = 0.42 mm/rev, depth of cut = 1.7 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 170, f = 0.42, d = 1.7 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*170*0.42*1.7 | Answer: 121380 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 360 mm is turned at 550 rpm with a feed of 0.33 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 360, N = 550, f = 0.33 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 360 / (0.33*550) | Answer: 1.983 min

question: A resistor of 88 ohm carries a current of 3.2 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 88, I = 3.2 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 3.2 * 88 | Answer: 281.6 V

question: Three resistors 2 ohm, 15 ohm and 63 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 2, R2 = 15, R3 = 63 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 2 + 15 + 63 | Answer: 80 ohm

question: Two resistors 64 ohm and 69 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 64, R2 = 69 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 64*69 / (64+69) | Answer: 33.2 ohm

question: A device draws 0.3 A at 110 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 110, I = 0.3 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 110 * 0.3 | Answer: 33 W

question: A current of 8.6 A flows through a 32 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 8.6, R = 32 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (8.6)^2 * 32 | Answer: 2367 W

question: Two capacitors 42.7 uF and 39.6 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 42.7, C2 = 39.6 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 42.7*39.6 / (42.7+39.6) | Answer: 20.55 uF

question: A resistor 42 kohm and capacitor 11.4 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 42, C = 11.4 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (42k)(11.4u) = 478.8 ms | Answer: 478.8 ms

question: An inductor 183.7 mH is in series with 86 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 183.7, R = 86 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (183.7e-3) / 86 | Answer: 2.136 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 78.4 mH inductor at 860 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 78.4, f = 860 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (860)(78.4e-3) | Answer: 423.6 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 33.4 uF capacitor at 380 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 33.4, f = 380 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (380)(33.4e-6)) | Answer: 12.54 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 52 ohm, XL = 121 ohm and XC = 13 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 52, XL = 121, XC = 13 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(52^2 + (121 - 13)^2) | Answer: 119.9 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 23.9 mH and C = 9.5 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 23.9, C = 9.5 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(23.9e-3 * 9.5e-6)) | Answer: 334 Hz

question: A capacitor of 96.6 uF is charged to 235 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 96.6, V = 235 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*96.6e-6*(235)^2 | Answer: 2667 mJ

question: An alternating voltage has a peak value of 310 V. Find its RMS value.
solution: Given: Vp = 310 | Formula: Vrms = Vp / sqrt(2) | Substitute: Vrms = 310 / sqrt(2) | Answer: 219.2 V

question: A transformer has primary voltage 420 V with 250 primary turns and 430 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 420, N1 = 250, N2 = 430 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 420 * 430/250 | Answer: 722.4 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 160 V and draws an armature current of 22 A. If the armature resistance is 0.64 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 160, Ia = 22, Ra = 0.64 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 160 - 22*0.64 | Answer: 145.9 V

question: A 4-pole induction motor on a 50 Hz supply runs at 940 rpm. Find the slip (%).
formula: s = (Ns - N) / Ns,  Ns = 120 f / P

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 180 A at 415 V (line) with a power factor of 0.74. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 180, VL = 415, pf = 0.74 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*415*180*0.74 / 1000 | Answer: 95.74 kW

question: A load has real power 60 kW and apparent power 75 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 60, S = 75 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 60 / 75 | Answer: 0.8

question: A machine delivers 60 kW output while drawing 172 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 60, Pi = 172 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 60/172 * 100 | Answer: 34.88 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 27 V across R1 = 8 ohm and R2 = 14 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 27, R1 = 8, R2 = 14 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 27*14 / (8+14) | Answer: 17.18 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 20 kohm and Rin = 41 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 20, Rin = 41 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 20 / 41 | Answer: 0.4878

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 150 kohm and Rg = 19 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 150, Rg = 19 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 150/19 | Answer: 8.895

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 6946. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 6946 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(6946) | Answer: 38.42 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.3 m carries a central point load of 65 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6.3, W = 65 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 65*6.3 / 4 | Answer: 102.4 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 7.8 m carries a UDL of 60 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7.8, w = 60 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 60*(7.8)^2 / 8 | Answer: 456.3 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 2.9 m carries a point load 35 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 2.9, W = 35 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 35*2.9 | Answer: 101.5 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 1.7 m carries a UDL of 8 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 1.7, w = 8 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 8*(1.7)^2 / 2 | Answer: 11.56 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 8.6 m carries a point load 100 kN at distance 3.7 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 8.6, a = 3.7, W = 100 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 100*(8.6 - 3.7) / 8.6 | Answer: 56.98 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 6.1 m) carries a central point load 40 kN. With E = 30 GPa and I = 360e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=40000 N, L=6100.0 mm, E=30000 MPa, I=360e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 17.51 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 8.4 m carries a UDL of 42 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 8.4, w = 42 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 42*(8.4)^2 / 12 | Answer: 247 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 630 mm, clear cover 50 mm and main bars of diameter 12 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 630, c = 50, dia = 12 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 630 - 50 - 12/2 | Answer: 574 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 17.8 m^2 carrying a factored load of 13.1 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 17.8, w = 13.1 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 13.1 * 17.8 | Answer: 233.2 kN

question: For a bar of diameter 16 mm with design bond stress 1.4 MPa and steel stress 395 MPa, find the development length in mm.
solution: Given: dia = 16, tbd = 1.4, fs = 395 | Formula: Ld = phi fs / (4 tau_bd) | Substitute: Ld = 16*395 / (4*1.4) | Answer: 1129 mm

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 6.4 m, unit weight 20 kN/m^3, phi = 29 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 6.3 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 20 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 6.3, g = 20 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (20 - 9.81)*6.3 | Answer: 64.2 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 8.5e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1.1, area = 2.7e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 8.5, i = 1.1, A = 2.7 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (8.5e-4)*1.1*(2.7e-3) | Answer: 2525 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 0.6 m, bed slope 0.01 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.014. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 2.4 m under a head of 0.3 m. Taking Cd = 0.64 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 5.6 m wide carries a discharge of 14.8 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 460 m and design speed 60 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 460, V = 60 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (60)^2 / (127*460) | Answer: 0.06162
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: For a design speed of 45 km/h with allowable superelevation 0.07 and lateral friction 0.16, find the minimum curve radius in m.
A tank of volume 670 m^3 treats a flow of 165 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 670, Q = 165 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 670 / 165 | Answer: 4.061 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 190 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.34 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 7 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 190, k = 0.34, t = 7 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 190*(1 - e^(-0.34*7)) | Answer: 172.4 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.69, rainfall intensity 70 mm/h over a catchment of 23.7 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.69, i = 70, A = 23.7 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.69*70*23.7 / 360 | Answer: 3.18 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.05 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 740 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.05, M = 740 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 740*(20+0.05)/20 | Answer: 741.9 m

question: Convert the decimal number 155 to binary.
solution: Divide 155 by 2 repeatedly, recording remainders | Reading remainders in reverse gives 10011011 | Answer: 10011011 (binary)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 2 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the decimal number 3645 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 3645 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: E3D (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the 8-bit binary number 00111011 to decimal.
solution: Binary 00111011 = sum of bit-weights | Answer: 59 (decimal)
formula: Sum each bit times its positional weight (2^i)

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 10110011 and 10010000.
solution: XOR: 00100011 | Count of 1s = 3 | Answer: 3
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 860 megabits is sent over a link of 97 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 860, B = 97 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 860 / 97 | Answer: 8.866 s

question: A link has bandwidth 16 Mbps and round-trip time 160 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 16, R = 160 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 16e6 * 160e-3 bits = 2560 kb | Answer: 2560 kilobits

question: A channel has bandwidth 4 kHz. Using Nyquist's theorem with 4 signal levels, find the maximum data rate in kbps (noiseless).
solution: Given: B = 4, M = 4 | Formula: C = 2 B log2(M) | Substitute: C = 2*4*log2(4) | Answer: 16 kbps

question: A channel of bandwidth 4 kHz has a signal-to-noise ratio of 63 (linear). Using Shannon's theorem, find the channel capacity in kbps.
solution: Given: B = 4, SNR = 63 | Formula: C = B log2(1 + SNR) | Substitute: C = 4*log2(1 + 63) | Answer: 24 kbps

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.93, cache access time 7 ns and main-memory access time 150 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.93, tc = 7, tm = 150 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.93*7 + (1 - 0.93)*150 | Answer: 17.01 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 418545 elements?
solution: Given: n = 418545 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(418545)) + 1 | Answer: 19

question: An O(n^2) algorithm performs c*n^2 basic operations. If c = 1 and n = 2220, how many operations are performed?
solution: Given: n = 2220 | Formula: operations = n^2 | Substitute: = (2220)^2 | Answer: 4928400

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.014, memory access time 140 ns and page-fault service time 8 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 8 ms = 8000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.014)*140 + 0.014*8000000.0 ns | Answer: 112.1 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 2.6 m^3 at 190 kPa and 510 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 2.6, P = 190, Tk = 510 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (190e3)*2.6 / (8.314*510) | Answer: 116.5 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.38 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 18 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.38, t = 18 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.38*18) | Answer: 0.9989

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.24 /min) is to reach 60% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.24, X = 60 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.6) / 0.24 | Answer: 3.818 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.32 /min) reaches 65% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.32, X = 65 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.65 / (0.32*(1 - 0.65)) | Answer: 5.804 min

question: For a reaction with A = 8e10 /s and activation energy 70 kJ/mol at 370 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 8, Ea = 70, Tk = 370 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 8e10 * exp(-70e3 / (8.314*370)) | Answer: 10.48 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.95 and bottoms xW = 0.07, with relative volatility alpha = 2. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.95, xw = 0.07, al = 2 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.95/0.05)(0.93/0.07)] / ln(2) | Answer: 7.98 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.85 and x = 0.22. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.85, x = 0.22 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.85/0.15) / (0.22/0.78) | Answer: 20.09

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.47 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 55 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.47, Psat = 55 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.47 * 55 | Answer: 25.85 kPa

question: A stream of 7.1 kg/s with specific heat 2.4 kJ/kg-K is heated through 75 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 7.1, cp = 2.4, dT = 75 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 7.1*2.4*75 | Answer: 1278 kW

question: A reactor of volume 15.3 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 4.4 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 15.3, Q = 4.4 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 15.3 / 4.4 | Answer: 3.477 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 1.8e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 2 mm with a concentration difference of 110 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 1.8, L = 2, dC = 110 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (1.8e-9)*110 / (2e-3) | Answer: 99 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 5.7 min and steady-state gain 3.7. For a step input of magnitude 6, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 5.7, K = 3.7, M = 6 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 3.7 * 6 | Answer: 22.2 units

question: A reactor operates at a space time of 10.2 min. Find its space velocity in per hour.
solution: Given: tau = 10.2 | Formula: SV = 60 / tau  (per hour) | Substitute: SV = 60 / 10.2 | Answer: 5.882 /h

question: An aircraft wing of area 15 m^2 flies at 90 m/s (air density 1 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.9. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 15, V = 90, rho = 1, CL = 0.9 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1*(90)^2*15*0.9 / 1000 | Answer: 54.67 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 85 m^2 flies at 120 m/s (density 1.225 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.09. Find the drag force in kN.
Find the dynamic pressure for air of density 1 kg/m^3 moving at 160 m/s, in Pa.
solution: Given: rho = 1, V = 160 | Formula: q = 0.5 rho V^2 | Substitute: q = 0.5*1*(160)^2 | Answer: 12800 Pa

question: An aircraft flies at 310 m/s where the speed of sound is 310 m/s. Find the Mach number.
solution: Given: V = 310, a = 310 | Formula: M = V / a | Substitute: M = 310 / 310 | Answer: 1

question: A specimen under stress 170 MPa shows an elastic strain of 2.7e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 170, eps = 2.7 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 170 / (2.7e-3) MPa = 62.96 GPa | Answer: 62.96 GPa

question: A block of mass 47 kg has a volume of 4.6e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 47, V = 4.6 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 47 / (4.6e-3) | Answer: 10217 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 2100 mm is heated through 120 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 23e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 2100, dT = 120, al = 23 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 2100*23e-6*120 | Answer: 5.796 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 30 ohm, R2 = 200 ohm and R3 = 460 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 30, R2 = 200, R3 = 460 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 200*460 / 30 | Answer: 3067 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 350 ohm and gauge factor 2.2 experiences a strain of 1450e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 350, GF = 2.2, eps = 1450 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 350*2.2*1450e-6 | Answer: 1116 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 10.98 when the true value is 50. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10.98, true = 50 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10.98 - 50| / 50 * 100 | Answer: 78.04 %

question: Annual demand is 28000 units, ordering cost 120 per order and holding cost 11 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 28000, S = 120, H = 11 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*28000*120 / 11) | Answer: 781.6 units

question: An asset costs 300000 with salvage value 26000 after 9 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 300000, Sv = 26000, n = 9 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (300000 - 26000) / 9 | Answer: 30444 per year

question: A product sells for 260 per unit with variable cost 200 per unit and fixed costs 10000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 260, V = 200, F = 10000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 10000 / (260 - 200) | Answer: 166.7 units

question: Find the present worth of 140000 received 6 years from now at an interest rate of 10% per year.
solution: Given: F = 140000, n = 6, i = 10 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 140000 / (1 + 0.1)^6 | Answer: 79026 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.97, 0.97 and 0.98 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.97, r2 = 0.97, r3 = 0.98 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.97*0.97*0.98 | Answer: 0.9221

question: A process produces 24 defective items in a batch of 5500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 24, N = 5500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 24/5500 * 1e6 | Answer: 4364 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = 2x^3 + 7x^2 - 2x - 5 evaluated at x = -2.
For f(x) = 3x^3 - 5x^2 - 8x - 5, find f''(x) at x = -2.
Evaluate the definite integral of (5x^2 + 2x - 7) dx from x = -2 to x = 6.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = 5x^3/3 + 2x^2/2 + -7x | Evaluate F(6) - F(-2) | Answer: 349.3
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 6x^2 + 12x = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[4, 5], [-1, 6]].
solution: Given: a = 4, b = 5, c = -1, d = 6 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (4)(6) - (5)(-1) | Answer: 29

question: Find the determinant of [[1, 3, 0], [-1, 3, -3], [-1, -4, 3]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: 15

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[-6, 2], [3, -6]].
solution: Trace tr = -12, Determinant = 30 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: -3.551

question: Solve for x: -5x + -6y = -12 and -3x + -2y = -3.
solution: Determinant = -5*-2 - -6*-3 = -8 | x = (e d - b f) / det = -0.75 | Answer: x = -0.75
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 21, 92, 79, 92, 68.
solution: Sum = 352 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 70.4 | Answer: 70.4

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 7, 8, 47, 35, 40.
solution: Mean = 27.4 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 18.66

question: Find the slope of the line through (4, 5) and (6, 5).
solution: Given: x1 = 4, y1 = 5, x2 = 6, y2 = 5 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (5 - 5) / (6 - 4) | Answer: 0

question: Find the distance between the points (-5, -3) and (3, -4).
solution: Given: x1 = -5, y1 = -3, x2 = 3, y2 = -4 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((8)^2 + (-1)^2) | Answer: 8.062 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (7,2), (-6,4), (3,1).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 10.5 sq units

question: Evaluate the number of combinations C(12, 5).
solution: Given: n = 12, r = 5 | Formula: C(n, r) = n! / (r! (n - r)!) | Substitute: C(12, 5) = 12! / (5! * 7!) | Answer: 792

question: Evaluate the number of permutations P(13, 10).
solution: Given: n = 13, r = 10 | Formula: P(n, r) = n! / (n - r)! | Substitute: P(13, 10) = 13! / 3! | Answer: 1037836800

question: Find the 16th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 20 and common difference 8.
solution: Given: a = 20, d = 8, n = 16 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = 20 + (16 - 1)*8 | Answer: 140

question: Find the sum of the first 18 terms of an AP with first term 11 and common difference -8.
solution: Given: a = 11, d = -8, n = 18 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 18/2 [2*11 + (18-1)*-8] | Answer: -1026

question: Find the 7th term of a geometric progression with first term 7 and common ratio 4.
solution: Given: a = 7, r = 4, n = 7 | Formula: a_n = a r^(n-1) | Substitute: a_n = 7 * 4^(7-1) | Answer: 28672

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 40000 at 11.7% per annum for 8 years.
solution: Given: P = 40000, R = 11.7, Tt = 8 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 40000 * 11.7 * 8 / 100 | Answer: 37440 currency units

question: Find the amount when 25500 is invested at 9.8% per annum compounded annually for 3 years.
solution: Given: P = 25500, R = 9.8, Tt = 3 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 25500 * (1 + 9.8/100)^3 | Answer: 33756 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (1, 2, 4) and (8, 8, -2).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (6, 1, -4) and (4, 3, 1).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 29.14

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (-5, -5, 3) and (-6, 2, 4).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 56.17 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number -12 + 7i.
solution: Given: a = -12, b = 7 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((-12)^2 + (7)^2) | Answer: 13.89

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number -8 + -5i.
solution: Given: a = -8, b = -5 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(-5, -8) | Answer: -148 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = 5x^3 + 6x + 8 at x = -4.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-112 with initial guess x0=11, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=0.5 and ordinates 0, 20, 1, 19, 17, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 467 and 464.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 467 and 464 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 16 and 21.
solution: Given: a = 16, b = 21 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 16*21 / 1 | Answer: 336
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 12 mm carries an axial tensile load of 56 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 29 mm and length 1900 mm carries an axial load of 37 kN. Take E = 200 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 28 mm transmits a torque of 100 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 28, Tt = 100 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(100*1000) / (pi*(28)^3) | Answer: 23.2 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 61 mm and length 1800 mm carries a torque of 1900 N-m. With G = 77 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (61)^4 / 32 = 1359312 mm^4 | theta = (1900*1000)(1800) / (77000 * 1359312) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 1.872 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 135 mm wide and 230 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 135, h = 230 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 135*(230)^2 / 6 | Answer: 1190250 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (118 mm x 230 mm) carries a bending moment of 25 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (35 mm x 120 mm) has effective length 3000 mm and E = 200 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 470 MPa is designed for a working stress of 60 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 470, sw = 60 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 470 / 60 | Answer: 7.833

question: A steel bar is fully restrained and heated through 55 deg C. With E = 200 GPa and alpha = 13e-6 /deg C, find the thermal stress in MPa.
solution: Given: dT = 55, E = 200, al = 13 | Formula: sigma = E alpha (dT) | Substitute: sigma = 200000 * 13e-6 * 55 | Answer: 143 MPa

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1500 mm and wall thickness 10 mm carries an internal pressure of 1 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1500, t = 10, P = 1 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 1*1500 / (2*10) | Answer: 75 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 1060 K and 350 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 1060, Tc = 350 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 350/1060) * 100 | Answer: 66.98 %

question: A refrigerator works between 252 K (cold) and 320 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 252, Th = 320 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 252 / (320 - 252) | Answer: 3.706

question: A heat pump operates between 277 K and 326 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 277, Th = 326 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 326 / (326 - 277) | Answer: 6.653

question: 4.6 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 155 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.6, dT = 155 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 4.6 * 0.718 * 155 | Answer: 511.9 kJ

question: 1.8 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 85 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1.8, dT = 85 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 1.8 * 1.005 * 85 | Answer: 153.8 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 0.6 m^3 at 470 K with mass 1.8 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 0.6, Tk = 470, m = 1.8 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 1.8*0.287*470 / 0.6 | Answer: 404.7 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 4 kg of air expands isothermally at 490 K from volume V1 to 3*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4, Tk = 490, ratio = 3 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 4*0.287*490*ln(3) | Answer: 618 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 2.5 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.38 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 2.5, D = 0.38 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*2.5*0.38 / 0.001 | Answer: 950000

question: Water flows at 3.9 m/s through a pipe of diameter 260 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 11.5 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 11.5 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*11.5 / 1000 | Answer: 112.8 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 5.6 m. Taking Cv = 0.97, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 5.6, cv = 0.97 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.97*sqrt(2*9.81*5.6) | Answer: 10.17 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 180 mm) water flows at 2.5 m/s. It contracts to diameter 80 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 180, d2 = 80, V1 = 2.5 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 2.5*(180/80)^2 | Answer: 12.66 m/s

question: Water flows at 2.8 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.28 m and length 170 m. With friction factor f = 0.021, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 40 teeth drives a gear of 102 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1400 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 40, z2 = 102, N1 = 1400 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1400*40 / 102 | Answer: 549 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 370 mm rotates at 1350 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 370, N = 1350 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.37)*1350 / 60 | Answer: 26.15 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 46.8 kW at 1200 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 46.8, N = 1200 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(46.8*1000) / (2*pi*1200) | Answer: 372.4 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 9.8 kg rotates at radius 0.43 m at 700 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 5200 N/m and mass 3.6 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 5200, m = 3.6 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(5200/3.6) | Answer: 6.049 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 4.2 m^2 and thickness 0.19 m has conductivity k = 41.4 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 25 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 4.2, L = 0.19, k = 41.4, dT = 25 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 41.4*4.2*25 / 0.19 | Answer: 22879 W

question: A surface of area 0.9 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 180 W/m^2-K to surroundings 90 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 0.9, h = 180, dT = 90 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 180*0.9*90 | Answer: 14580 W

question: In a counter-flow heat exchanger the terminal temperature differences are 120 deg C and 20 deg C. Find the log mean temperature difference (LMTD) in deg C.
solution: Given: dT1 = 120, dT2 = 20 | Formula: LMTD = (dT1 - dT2) / ln(dT1/dT2) | Substitute: LMTD = (120 - 20) / ln(120/20) | Answer: 55.81 deg C

question: In turning, cutting speed = 120 m/min, feed = 0.47 mm/rev, depth of cut = 0.6 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 120, f = 0.47, d = 0.6 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*120*0.47*0.6 | Answer: 33840 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 330 mm is turned at 450 rpm with a feed of 0.36 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 330, N = 450, f = 0.36 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 330 / (0.36*450) | Answer: 2.037 min

question: A resistor of 114 ohm carries a current of 6.6 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 114, I = 6.6 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 6.6 * 114 | Answer: 752.4 V

question: Three resistors 38 ohm, 15 ohm and 32 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 38, R2 = 15, R3 = 32 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 38 + 15 + 32 | Answer: 85 ohm

question: Two resistors 37 ohm and 48 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 37, R2 = 48 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 37*48 / (37+48) | Answer: 20.89 ohm

question: A device draws 8.3 A at 230 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 230, I = 8.3 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 230 * 8.3 | Answer: 1909 W

question: A current of 8.2 A flows through a 74 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 8.2, R = 74 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (8.2)^2 * 74 | Answer: 4976 W

question: Two capacitors 25 uF and 30.7 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 25, C2 = 30.7 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 25*30.7 / (25+30.7) | Answer: 13.78 uF

question: A resistor 54 kohm and capacitor 6.3 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 54, C = 6.3 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (54k)(6.3u) = 340.2 ms | Answer: 340.2 ms

question: An inductor 480.9 mH is in series with 157 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 480.9, R = 157 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (480.9e-3) / 157 | Answer: 3.063 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 49.1 mH inductor at 670 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 49.1, f = 670 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (670)(49.1e-3) | Answer: 206.7 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 45 uF capacitor at 460 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 45, f = 460 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (460)(45e-6)) | Answer: 7.689 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 57 ohm, XL = 81 ohm and XC = 143 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 57, XL = 81, XC = 143 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(57^2 + (81 - 143)^2) | Answer: 84.22 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 75.7 mH and C = 4.2 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 75.7, C = 4.2 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(75.7e-3 * 4.2e-6)) | Answer: 282.3 Hz

question: A capacitor of 37.7 uF is charged to 135 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 37.7, V = 135 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*37.7e-6*(135)^2 | Answer: 343.5 mJ

question: An alternating voltage has a peak value of 94 V. Find its RMS value.
solution: Given: Vp = 94 | Formula: Vrms = Vp / sqrt(2) | Substitute: Vrms = 94 / sqrt(2) | Answer: 66.47 V

question: A transformer has primary voltage 440 V with 290 primary turns and 40 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 440, N1 = 290, N2 = 40 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 440 * 40/290 | Answer: 60.69 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 320 V and draws an armature current of 13 A. If the armature resistance is 0.23 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 320, Ia = 13, Ra = 0.23 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 320 - 13*0.23 | Answer: 317 V

question: A 6-pole induction motor on a 60 Hz supply runs at 800 rpm. Find the slip (%).
formula: s = (Ns - N) / Ns,  Ns = 120 f / P

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 65 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.88. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 65, VL = 400, pf = 0.88 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*400*65*0.88 / 1000 | Answer: 39.63 kW

question: A load has real power 100 kW and apparent power 105 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 100, S = 105 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 100 / 105 | Answer: 0.9524

question: A machine delivers 160 kW output while drawing 192 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 160, Pi = 192 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 160/192 * 100 | Answer: 83.33 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 8 V across R1 = 20 ohm and R2 = 17 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 8, R1 = 20, R2 = 17 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 8*17 / (20+17) | Answer: 3.676 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 70 kohm and Rin = 4 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 70, Rin = 4 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 70 / 4 | Answer: 17.5

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 120 kohm and Rg = 21 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 120, Rg = 21 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 120/21 | Answer: 6.714

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 7991. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 7991 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(7991) | Answer: 39.03 dB

question: A first-order system has a time constant of 6.7 s. Find the time (in s) to reach 63.2% of its final value.
solution: For a first-order step response, y = 1 - e^(-t/tau) | y = 0.632 when t = tau | Answer: 6.7 s
formula: At t = tau the response reaches 63.2% (one time constant)

question: A signal is sampled at 66 kHz. According to the Nyquist criterion, what is the maximum signal frequency that can be represented (in kHz)?
solution: Given: fs = 66 | Formula: f_max = fs / 2 | Substitute: f_max = 66 / 2 | Answer: 33 kHz

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.1 m carries a central point load of 30 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6.1, W = 30 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 30*6.1 / 4 | Answer: 45.75 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 5.2 m carries a UDL of 45 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.2, w = 45 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 45*(5.2)^2 / 8 | Answer: 152.1 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 2.8 m carries a point load 55 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 2.8, W = 55 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 55*2.8 | Answer: 154 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 5.2 m carries a UDL of 24 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.2, w = 24 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 24*(5.2)^2 / 2 | Answer: 324.5 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 7.5 m carries a point load 60 kN at distance 1.8 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 7.5, a = 1.8, W = 60 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 60*(7.5 - 1.8) / 7.5 | Answer: 45.6 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 6.3 m) carries a central point load 60 kN. With E = 25 GPa and I = 60e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=60000 N, L=6300.0 mm, E=25000 MPa, I=60e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 208.4 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 4.3 m carries a UDL of 6 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.3, w = 6 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 6*(4.3)^2 / 12 | Answer: 9.245 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 500 mm, clear cover 45 mm and main bars of diameter 16 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 500, c = 45, dia = 16 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 500 - 45 - 16/2 | Answer: 447 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 20.4 m^2 carrying a factored load of 15 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 20.4, w = 15 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 15 * 20.4 | Answer: 306 kN

question: For a bar of diameter 25 mm with design bond stress 1.6 MPa and steel stress 395 MPa, find the development length in mm.
solution: Given: dia = 25, tbd = 1.6, fs = 395 | Formula: Ld = phi fs / (4 tau_bd) | Substitute: Ld = 25*395 / (4*1.6) | Answer: 1543 mm

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 5 m, unit weight 19 kN/m^3, phi = 32 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 3.6 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 21 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 3.6, g = 21 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (21 - 9.81)*3.6 | Answer: 40.28 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 5.5e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1, area = 4.1e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 5.5, i = 1, A = 4.1 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (5.5e-4)*1*(4.1e-3) | Answer: 2255 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 0.6 m, bed slope 0.004 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.021. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 3.7 m under a head of 1.1 m. Taking Cd = 0.61 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 5.1 m wide carries a discharge of 17.9 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 110 m and design speed 100 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 110, V = 100 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (100)^2 / (127*110) | Answer: 0.7158
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: For a design speed of 65 km/h with allowable superelevation 0.06 and lateral friction 0.13, find the minimum curve radius in m.
A tank of volume 590 m^3 treats a flow of 175 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 590, Q = 175 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 590 / 175 | Answer: 3.371 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 190 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.17 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 4 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 190, k = 0.17, t = 4 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 190*(1 - e^(-0.17*4)) | Answer: 93.74 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.41, rainfall intensity 40 mm/h over a catchment of 9.6 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.41, i = 40, A = 9.6 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.41*40*9.6 / 360 | Answer: 0.4373 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.04 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 410 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.04, M = 410 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 410*(20+0.04)/20 | Answer: 410.8 m

question: Convert the decimal number 94 to binary.
solution: Divide 94 by 2 repeatedly, recording remainders | Reading remainders in reverse gives 1011110 | Answer: 1011110 (binary)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 2 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the decimal number 1000 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 1000 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 3E8 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the 8-bit binary number 11001001 to decimal.
solution: Binary 11001001 = sum of bit-weights | Answer: 201 (decimal)
formula: Sum each bit times its positional weight (2^i)

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 10100011 and 01000100.
solution: XOR: 11100111 | Count of 1s = 6 | Answer: 6
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 720 megabits is sent over a link of 46 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 720, B = 46 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 720 / 46 | Answer: 15.65 s

question: A link has bandwidth 88 Mbps and round-trip time 50 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 88, R = 50 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 88e6 * 50e-3 bits = 4400 kb | Answer: 4400 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.89, cache access time 2 ns and main-memory access time 200 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.89, tc = 2, tm = 200 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.89*2 + (1 - 0.89)*200 | Answer: 23.78 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 618135 elements?
solution: Given: n = 618135 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(618135)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: An O(n^2) algorithm performs c*n^2 basic operations. If c = 1 and n = 270, how many operations are performed?
solution: Given: n = 270 | Formula: operations = n^2 | Substitute: = (270)^2 | Answer: 72900

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.013, memory access time 150 ns and page-fault service time 9 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 9 ms = 9000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.013)*150 + 0.013*9000000.0 ns | Answer: 117.1 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 1.2 m^3 at 210 kPa and 580 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 1.2, P = 210, Tk = 580 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (210e3)*1.2 / (8.314*580) | Answer: 52.26 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.09 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 20 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.09, t = 20 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.09*20) | Answer: 0.8347

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.24 /min) is to reach 90% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.24, X = 90 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.9) / 0.24 | Answer: 9.594 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.37 /min) reaches 80% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.37, X = 80 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.8 / (0.37*(1 - 0.8)) | Answer: 10.81 min

question: For a reaction with A = 1e10 /s and activation energy 50 kJ/mol at 470 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 1, Ea = 50, Tk = 470 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 1e10 * exp(-50e3 / (8.314*470)) | Answer: 27728 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.9 and bottoms xW = 0.09, with relative volatility alpha = 1.9. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.9, xw = 0.09, al = 1.9 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.9/0.1)(0.91/0.09)] / ln(1.9) | Answer: 7.028 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.6 and x = 0.32. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.6, x = 0.32 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.6/0.4) / (0.32/0.68) | Answer: 3.187

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.44 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 30 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.44, Psat = 30 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.44 * 30 | Answer: 13.2 kPa

question: A stream of 0.9 kg/s with specific heat 1 kJ/kg-K is heated through 95 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 0.9, cp = 1, dT = 95 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 0.9*1*95 | Answer: 85.5 kW

question: A reactor of volume 5.3 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 2.7 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 5.3, Q = 2.7 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 5.3 / 2.7 | Answer: 1.963 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 5.4e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 2 mm with a concentration difference of 100 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 5.4, L = 2, dC = 100 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (5.4e-9)*100 / (2e-3) | Answer: 270 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 7.8 min and steady-state gain 2.7. For a step input of magnitude 6, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 7.8, K = 2.7, M = 6 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 2.7 * 6 | Answer: 16.2 units

question: A reactor operates at a space time of 7.5 min. Find its space velocity in per hour.
solution: Given: tau = 7.5 | Formula: SV = 60 / tau  (per hour) | Substitute: SV = 60 / 7.5 | Answer: 8 /h

question: An aircraft wing of area 110 m^2 flies at 200 m/s (air density 1.225 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.8. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 110, V = 200, rho = 1.225, CL = 0.8 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1.225*(200)^2*110*0.8 / 1000 | Answer: 2156 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 30 m^2 flies at 160 m/s (density 1.225 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.09. Find the drag force in kN.
Find the dynamic pressure for air of density 0.7 kg/m^3 moving at 90 m/s, in Pa.
solution: Given: rho = 0.7, V = 90 | Formula: q = 0.5 rho V^2 | Substitute: q = 0.5*0.7*(90)^2 | Answer: 2835 Pa

question: An aircraft flies at 240 m/s where the speed of sound is 310 m/s. Find the Mach number.
solution: Given: V = 240, a = 310 | Formula: M = V / a | Substitute: M = 240 / 310 | Answer: 0.7742

question: A specimen under stress 370 MPa shows an elastic strain of 1.1e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 370, eps = 1.1 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 370 / (1.1e-3) MPa = 336.4 GPa | Answer: 336.4 GPa

question: A block of mass 37 kg has a volume of 4.2e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 37, V = 4.2 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 37 / (4.2e-3) | Answer: 881 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 1800 mm is heated through 150 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 23e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 1800, dT = 150, al = 23 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 1800*23e-6*150 | Answer: 6.21 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 10 ohm, R2 = 25 ohm and R3 = 185 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 10, R2 = 25, R3 = 185 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 25*185 / 10 | Answer: 462.5 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 120 ohm and gauge factor 2.2 experiences a strain of 900e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 120, GF = 2.2, eps = 900 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 120*2.2*900e-6 | Answer: 237.6 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 9.84 when the true value is 10. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.84, true = 10 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.84 - 10| / 10 * 100 | Answer: 1.6 %

question: Annual demand is 16500 units, ordering cost 240 per order and holding cost 8 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 16500, S = 240, H = 8 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*16500*240 / 8) | Answer: 995 units

question: An asset costs 280000 with salvage value 12000 after 15 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 280000, Sv = 12000, n = 15 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (280000 - 12000) / 15 | Answer: 17867 per year

question: A product sells for 370 per unit with variable cost 40 per unit and fixed costs 90000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 370, V = 40, F = 90000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 90000 / (370 - 40) | Answer: 272.7 units

question: Find the present worth of 125000 received 7 years from now at an interest rate of 9% per year.
solution: Given: F = 125000, n = 7, i = 9 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 125000 / (1 + 0.09)^7 | Answer: 68379 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.94, 0.95 and 0.92 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.94, r2 = 0.95, r3 = 0.92 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.94*0.95*0.92 | Answer: 0.8216

question: A process produces 3 defective items in a batch of 15500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 3, N = 15500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 3/15500 * 1e6 | Answer: 193.5 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = x^3 + 8x^2 + 3x - 1 evaluated at x = -4.
For f(x) = 4x^3 - 4x^2 + 2x + 7, find f''(x) at x = -2.
Evaluate the definite integral of (4x^2 - 2x - 8) dx from x = -1 to x = 3.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = 4x^3/3 + -2x^2/2 + -8x | Evaluate F(3) - F(-1) | Answer: -2.667
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 2x^2 + 3x - 2 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[5, 0], [9, -7]].
solution: Given: a = 5, b = 0, c = 9, d = -7 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (5)(-7) - (0)(9) | Answer: -35

question: Find the determinant of [[3, 0, 1], [1, -5, -4], [4, 1, 3]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: -12

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[-5, -7], [-5, 3]].
solution: Trace tr = -2, Determinant = -50 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 6.141

question: Solve for x: 3x + -2y = -6 and 0x + -6y = 7.
solution: Determinant = 3*-6 - -2*0 = -18 | x = (e d - b f) / det = -2.778 | Answer: x = -2.778
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 57, 97, 41, 21, 90.
solution: Sum = 306 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 61.2 | Answer: 61.2

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 26, 11, 24, 27, 41.
solution: Mean = 25.8 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 10.66

question: Find the slope of the line through (1, 4) and (6, -4).
solution: Given: x1 = 1, y1 = 4, x2 = 6, y2 = -4 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (-4 - 4) / (6 - 1) | Answer: -1.6

question: Find the distance between the points (5, 4) and (-3, 2).
solution: Given: x1 = 5, y1 = 4, x2 = -3, y2 = 2 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-8)^2 + (-2)^2) | Answer: 8.246 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (3,-1), (-3,2), (-2,5).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 10.5 sq units

question: Evaluate the number of combinations C(8, 2).
solution: Given: n = 8, r = 2 | Formula: C(n, r) = n! / (r! (n - r)!) | Substitute: C(8, 2) = 8! / (2! * 6!) | Answer: 28

question: Find the 21th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -12 and common difference 5.
solution: Given: a = -12, d = 5, n = 21 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -12 + (21 - 1)*5 | Answer: 88

question: Find the sum of the first 37 terms of an AP with first term -10 and common difference 4.
solution: Given: a = -10, d = 4, n = 37 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 37/2 [2*-10 + (37-1)*4] | Answer: 2294

question: Find the 3th term of a geometric progression with first term 2 and common ratio 2.
solution: Given: a = 2, r = 2, n = 3 | Formula: a_n = a r^(n-1) | Substitute: a_n = 2 * 2^(3-1) | Answer: 8

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 26500 at 5.6% per annum for 9 years.
solution: Given: P = 26500, R = 5.6, Tt = 9 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 26500 * 5.6 * 9 / 100 | Answer: 13356 currency units

question: Find the amount when 11500 is invested at 7.3% per annum compounded annually for 3 years.
solution: Given: P = 11500, R = 7.3, Tt = 3 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 11500 * (1 + 7.3/100)^3 | Answer: 14207 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (5, 2, 6) and (-3, 4, 6).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (6, -2, -4) and (-5, -5, -6).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 69.28

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (-4, 5, -3) and (6, 6, 4).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 95.19 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number 8 + 1i.
solution: Given: a = 8, b = 1 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((8)^2 + (1)^2) | Answer: 8.062

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number -4 + -8i.
solution: Given: a = -4, b = -8 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(-8, -4) | Answer: -116.6 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -4x^3 - 7x^2 + 7x + 4 at x = 1.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-42 with initial guess x0=14, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.6 and ordinates 19, 13, 12, 8, 2, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 155 and 511.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 155 and 511 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 29 and 55.
solution: Given: a = 29, b = 55 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 29*55 / 1 | Answer: 1595
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 33 mm carries an axial tensile load of 29 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 27 mm and length 800 mm carries an axial load of 72 kN. Take E = 210 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 62 mm transmits a torque of 1050 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 62, Tt = 1050 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(1050*1000) / (pi*(62)^3) | Answer: 22.44 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 62 mm and length 1500 mm carries a torque of 1900 N-m. With G = 80 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (62)^4 / 32 = 1450663 mm^4 | theta = (1900*1000)(1500) / (80000 * 1450663) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 1.407 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 112 mm wide and 90 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 112, h = 90 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 112*(90)^2 / 6 | Answer: 151200 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (74 mm x 220 mm) carries a bending moment of 29 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (47 mm x 90 mm) has effective length 2800 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 570 MPa is designed for a working stress of 230 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 570, sw = 230 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 570 / 230 | Answer: 2.478

question: A steel bar is fully restrained and heated through 100 deg C. With E = 200 GPa and alpha = 13e-6 /deg C, find the thermal stress in MPa.
solution: Given: dT = 100, E = 200, al = 13 | Formula: sigma = E alpha (dT) | Substitute: sigma = 200000 * 13e-6 * 100 | Answer: 260 MPa

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1300 mm and wall thickness 9 mm carries an internal pressure of 2.3 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1300, t = 9, P = 2.3 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 2.3*1300 / (2*9) | Answer: 166.1 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 920 K and 330 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 920, Tc = 330 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 330/920) * 100 | Answer: 64.13 %

question: A refrigerator works between 264 K (cold) and 320 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 264, Th = 320 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 264 / (320 - 264) | Answer: 4.714

question: A heat pump operates between 273 K and 330 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 273, Th = 330 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 330 / (330 - 273) | Answer: 5.789

question: 2.9 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 150 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.9, dT = 150 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 2.9 * 0.718 * 150 | Answer: 312.3 kJ

question: 2.2 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 95 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.2, dT = 95 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 2.2 * 1.005 * 95 | Answer: 210 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 2.2 m^3 at 330 K with mass 4.1 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 2.2, Tk = 330, m = 4.1 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 4.1*0.287*330 / 2.2 | Answer: 176.5 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 3.8 kg of air expands isothermally at 410 K from volume V1 to 4*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.8, Tk = 410, ratio = 4 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 3.8*0.287*410*ln(4) | Answer: 619.9 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 2 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.35 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 2, D = 0.35 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*2*0.35 / 0.001 | Answer: 700000

question: Water flows at 2.1 m/s through a pipe of diameter 170 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 3.6 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 3.6 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*3.6 / 1000 | Answer: 35.32 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 16.8 m. Taking Cv = 0.96, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 16.8, cv = 0.96 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.96*sqrt(2*9.81*16.8) | Answer: 17.43 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 280 mm) water flows at 0.8 m/s. It contracts to diameter 110 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
Water flows at 1.2 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.44 m and length 500 m. With friction factor f = 0.036, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 26 teeth drives a gear of 78 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1450 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 26, z2 = 78, N1 = 1450 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1450*26 / 78 | Answer: 483.3 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 230 mm rotates at 400 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 230, N = 400 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.23)*400 / 60 | Answer: 4.817 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 41.4 kW at 900 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 41.4, N = 900 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(41.4*1000) / (2*pi*900) | Answer: 439.3 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 3.7 kg rotates at radius 0.56 m at 850 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 17200 N/m and mass 1.7 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 17200, m = 1.7 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(17200/1.7) | Answer: 16.01 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 4 m^2 and thickness 0.11 m has conductivity k = 26.1 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 70 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 4, L = 0.11, k = 26.1, dT = 70 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 26.1*4*70 / 0.11 | Answer: 66436 W

question: A surface of area 5.2 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 125 W/m^2-K to surroundings 140 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 5.2, h = 125, dT = 140 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 125*5.2*140 | Answer: 91000 W

question: In a counter-flow heat exchanger the terminal temperature differences are 110 deg C and 5 deg C. Find the log mean temperature difference (LMTD) in deg C.
solution: Given: dT1 = 110, dT2 = 5 | Formula: LMTD = (dT1 - dT2) / ln(dT1/dT2) | Substitute: LMTD = (110 - 5) / ln(110/5) | Answer: 33.97 deg C

question: In turning, cutting speed = 180 m/min, feed = 0.32 mm/rev, depth of cut = 1.3 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 180, f = 0.32, d = 1.3 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*180*0.32*1.3 | Answer: 74880 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 170 mm is turned at 1000 rpm with a feed of 0.32 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 170, N = 1000, f = 0.32 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 170 / (0.32*1000) | Answer: 0.5312 min

question: A resistor of 3 ohm carries a current of 5.2 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 3, I = 5.2 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 5.2 * 3 | Answer: 15.6 V

question: Three resistors 70 ohm, 16 ohm and 27 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 70, R2 = 16, R3 = 27 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 70 + 16 + 27 | Answer: 113 ohm

question: Two resistors 11 ohm and 67 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 11, R2 = 67 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 11*67 / (11+67) | Answer: 9.449 ohm

question: A device draws 8.6 A at 75 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 75, I = 8.6 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 75 * 8.6 | Answer: 645 W

question: A current of 7.9 A flows through a 83 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 7.9, R = 83 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (7.9)^2 * 83 | Answer: 518 W

question: Two capacitors 24.8 uF and 1.7 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 24.8, C2 = 1.7 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 24.8*1.7 / (24.8+1.7) | Answer: 1.591 uF

question: A resistor 94 kohm and capacitor 16.6 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 94, C = 16.6 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (94k)(16.6u) = 156 ms | Answer: 156 ms

question: An inductor 291.9 mH is in series with 96 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 291.9, R = 96 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (291.9e-3) / 96 | Answer: 3.041 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 88.2 mH inductor at 360 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 88.2, f = 360 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (360)(88.2e-3) | Answer: 199.5 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 24.7 uF capacitor at 430 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 24.7, f = 430 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (430)(24.7e-6)) | Answer: 14.98 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 13 ohm, XL = 78 ohm and XC = 114 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 13, XL = 78, XC = 114 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(13^2 + (78 - 114)^2) | Answer: 38.28 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 51.2 mH and C = 2.5 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 51.2, C = 2.5 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(51.2e-3 * 2.5e-6)) | Answer: 444.9 Hz

question: A capacitor of 93.6 uF is charged to 200 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 93.6, V = 200 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*93.6e-6*(200)^2 | Answer: 1872 mJ

question: An alternating voltage has a peak value of 286 V. Find its RMS value.
solution: Given: Vp = 286 | Formula: Vrms = Vp / sqrt(2) | Substitute: Vrms = 286 / sqrt(2) | Answer: 202.2 V

question: A transformer has primary voltage 390 V with 890 primary turns and 360 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 390, N1 = 890, N2 = 360 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 390 * 360/890 | Answer: 157.8 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 160 V and draws an armature current of 46 A. If the armature resistance is 1.4 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 160, Ia = 46, Ra = 1.4 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 160 - 46*1.4 | Answer: 95.6 V

question: A 4-pole induction motor on a 60 Hz supply runs at 830 rpm. Find the slip (%).
formula: s = (Ns - N) / Ns,  Ns = 120 f / P

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 115 A at 415 V (line) with a power factor of 0.76. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 115, VL = 415, pf = 0.76 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*415*115*0.76 / 1000 | Answer: 62.82 kW

question: A load has real power 15 kW and apparent power 120 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 15, S = 120 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 15 / 120 | Answer: 0.125

question: A machine delivers 110 kW output while drawing 207 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 110, Pi = 207 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 110/207 * 100 | Answer: 53.14 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 15 V across R1 = 43 ohm and R2 = 19 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 15, R1 = 43, R2 = 19 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 15*19 / (43+19) | Answer: 4.597 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 10 kohm and Rin = 21 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 10, Rin = 21 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 10 / 21 | Answer: 0.4762

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 140 kohm and Rg = 12 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 140, Rg = 12 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 140/12 | Answer: 12.67

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 5418. Express the gain in decibels (power).

question: A first-order system has a time constant of 7.3 s. Find the time (in s) to reach 63.2% of its final value.
