solution: Given: dT = 95, E = 210, al = 11 | Formula: sigma = E alpha (dT) | Substitute: sigma = 210000 * 11e-6 * 95 | Answer: 219.5 MPa

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 400 mm and wall thickness 17 mm carries an internal pressure of 0.9 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 400, t = 17, P = 0.9 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 0.9*400 / (2*17) | Answer: 10.59 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 700 K and 370 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 700, Tc = 370 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 370/700) * 100 | Answer: 47.14 %

question: A refrigerator works between 264 K (cold) and 326 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 264, Th = 326 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 264 / (326 - 264) | Answer: 4.258

question: A heat pump operates between 285 K and 310 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 285, Th = 310 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 310 / (310 - 285) | Answer: 12.4

question: 7.1 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 150 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 7.1, dT = 150 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 7.1 * 0.718 * 150 | Answer: 764.7 kJ

question: 2.4 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 145 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.4, dT = 145 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 2.4 * 1.005 * 145 | Answer: 349.7 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 0.6 m^3 at 590 K with mass 4.7 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 0.6, Tk = 590, m = 4.7 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 4.7*0.287*590 / 0.6 | Answer: 1326 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 1.6 kg of air expands isothermally at 340 K from volume V1 to 5*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1.6, Tk = 340, ratio = 5 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 1.6*0.287*340*ln(5) | Answer: 251.3 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 1.4 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.35 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 1.4, D = 0.35 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*1.4*0.35 / 0.001 | Answer: 490000

question: Water flows at 2.6 m/s through a pipe of diameter 50 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 25 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 25 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*25 / 1000 | Answer: 245.2 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 14 m. Taking Cv = 0.97, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 14, cv = 0.97 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.97*sqrt(2*9.81*14) | Answer: 16.08 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 330 mm) water flows at 1.5 m/s. It contracts to diameter 60 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 330, d2 = 60, V1 = 1.5 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 1.5*(330/60)^2 | Answer: 45.38 m/s

question: Water flows at 1.2 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.13 m and length 430 m. With friction factor f = 0.039, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 15 teeth drives a gear of 55 teeth. If the pinion runs at 700 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 15, z2 = 55, N1 = 700 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 700*15 / 55 | Answer: 190.9 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 380 mm rotates at 950 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 380, N = 950 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.38)*950 / 60 | Answer: 18.9 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 18.7 kW at 250 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 18.7, N = 250 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(18.7*1000) / (2*pi*250) | Answer: 714.3 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 5.8 kg rotates at radius 0.32 m at 200 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 19400 N/m and mass 7.5 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 19400, m = 7.5 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(19400/7.5) | Answer: 8.095 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 1.8 m^2 and thickness 0.4 m has conductivity k = 41.3 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 35 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 1.8, L = 0.4, k = 41.3, dT = 35 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 41.3*1.8*35 / 0.4 | Answer: 6505 W

question: A surface of area 3.1 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 80 W/m^2-K to surroundings 100 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 3.1, h = 80, dT = 100 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 80*3.1*100 | Answer: 24800 W

question: In a counter-flow heat exchanger the terminal temperature differences are 65 deg C and 35 deg C. Find the log mean temperature difference (LMTD) in deg C.
solution: Given: dT1 = 65, dT2 = 35 | Formula: LMTD = (dT1 - dT2) / ln(dT1/dT2) | Substitute: LMTD = (65 - 35) / ln(65/35) | Answer: 48.46 deg C

question: In turning, cutting speed = 120 m/min, feed = 0.18 mm/rev, depth of cut = 0.7 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 120, f = 0.18, d = 0.7 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*120*0.18*0.7 | Answer: 15120 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 100 mm is turned at 850 rpm with a feed of 0.15 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 100, N = 850, f = 0.15 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 100 / (0.15*850) | Answer: 0.7843 min

question: A resistor of 89 ohm carries a current of 0.2 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 89, I = 0.2 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 0.2 * 89 | Answer: 17.8 V

question: Three resistors 79 ohm, 58 ohm and 43 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 79, R2 = 58, R3 = 43 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 79 + 58 + 43 | Answer: 180 ohm

question: Two resistors 108 ohm and 111 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 108, R2 = 111 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 108*111 / (108+111) | Answer: 54.74 ohm

question: A device draws 13.7 A at 80 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 80, I = 13.7 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 80 * 13.7 | Answer: 1096 W

question: A current of 0.3 A flows through a 119 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 0.3, R = 119 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (0.3)^2 * 119 | Answer: 10.71 W

question: Two capacitors 24.4 uF and 15.8 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 24.4, C2 = 15.8 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 24.4*15.8 / (24.4+15.8) | Answer: 9.59 uF

question: A resistor 37 kohm and capacitor 13.7 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 37, C = 13.7 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (37k)(13.7u) = 506.9 ms | Answer: 506.9 ms

question: An inductor 221 mH is in series with 7 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 221, R = 7 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (221e-3) / 7 | Answer: 31.57 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 115 mH inductor at 410 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 115, f = 410 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (410)(115e-3) | Answer: 296.3 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 28.6 uF capacitor at 640 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 28.6, f = 640 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (640)(28.6e-6)) | Answer: 8.695 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 81 ohm, XL = 150 ohm and XC = 119 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 81, XL = 150, XC = 119 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(81^2 + (150 - 119)^2) | Answer: 86.73 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 25.4 mH and C = 3.7 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 25.4, C = 3.7 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(25.4e-3 * 3.7e-6)) | Answer: 519.2 Hz

question: A capacitor of 90.3 uF is charged to 320 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 90.3, V = 320 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*90.3e-6*(320)^2 | Answer: 4623 mJ

question: An alternating voltage has a peak value of 170 V. Find its RMS value.
solution: Given: Vp = 170 | Formula: Vrms = Vp / sqrt(2) | Substitute: Vrms = 170 / sqrt(2) | Answer: 120.2 V

question: A transformer has primary voltage 370 V with 800 primary turns and 500 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 370, N1 = 800, N2 = 500 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 370 * 500/800 | Answer: 231.2 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 110 V and draws an armature current of 50 A. If the armature resistance is 0.21 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 110, Ia = 50, Ra = 0.21 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 110 - 50*0.21 | Answer: 99.5 V

question: A 4-pole induction motor on a 50 Hz supply runs at 780 rpm. Find the slip (%).
formula: s = (Ns - N) / Ns,  Ns = 120 f / P

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 180 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.83. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 180, VL = 400, pf = 0.83 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*400*180*0.83 / 1000 | Answer: 103.5 kW

question: A load has real power 160 kW and apparent power 175 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 160, S = 175 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 160 / 175 | Answer: 0.9143

question: A machine delivers 75 kW output while drawing 177 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 75, Pi = 177 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 75/177 * 100 | Answer: 42.37 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 12 V across R1 = 33 ohm and R2 = 40 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 12, R1 = 33, R2 = 40 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 12*40 / (33+40) | Answer: 6.575 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 180 kohm and Rin = 42 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 180, Rin = 42 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 180 / 42 | Answer: 4.286

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 190 kohm and Rg = 24 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 190, Rg = 24 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 190/24 | Answer: 8.917

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 5099. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 5099 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(5099) | Answer: 37.07 dB

question: A signal is sampled at 112 kHz. According to the Nyquist criterion, what is the maximum signal frequency that can be represented (in kHz)?
solution: Given: fs = 112 | Formula: f_max = fs / 2 | Substitute: f_max = 112 / 2 | Answer: 56 kHz

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.9 m carries a central point load of 65 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6.9, W = 65 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 65*6.9 / 4 | Answer: 112.1 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 7.1 m carries a UDL of 30 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7.1, w = 30 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 30*(7.1)^2 / 8 | Answer: 189 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 2.4 m carries a point load 30 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 2.4, W = 30 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 30*2.4 | Answer: 72 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 2.4 m carries a UDL of 10 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 2.4, w = 10 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 10*(2.4)^2 / 2 | Answer: 28.8 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.9 m carries a point load 75 kN at distance 3.8 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 9.9, a = 3.8, W = 75 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 75*(9.9 - 3.8) / 9.9 | Answer: 46.21 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 3.3 m) carries a central point load 35 kN. With E = 200 GPa and I = 560e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=35000 N, L=3300.0 mm, E=200000 MPa, I=560e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 0.234 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 6.2 m carries a UDL of 45 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6.2, w = 45 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 45*(6.2)^2 / 12 | Answer: 144.2 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 630 mm, clear cover 30 mm and main bars of diameter 20 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 630, c = 30, dia = 20 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 630 - 30 - 20/2 | Answer: 590 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 17.3 m^2 carrying a factored load of 13 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 17.3, w = 13 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 13 * 17.3 | Answer: 224.9 kN

question: For a bar of diameter 20 mm with design bond stress 1.7 MPa and steel stress 435 MPa, find the development length in mm.
solution: Given: dia = 20, tbd = 1.7, fs = 435 | Formula: Ld = phi fs / (4 tau_bd) | Substitute: Ld = 20*435 / (4*1.7) | Answer: 1279 mm

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 4.3 m, unit weight 19 kN/m^3, phi = 38 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 7.7 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 19 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 7.7, g = 19 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (19 - 9.81)*7.7 | Answer: 70.76 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 1.6e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1.1, area = 5.4e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 1.6, i = 1.1, A = 5.4 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (1.6e-4)*1.1*(5.4e-3) | Answer: 950.4 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 2.4 m, bed slope 0.006 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.028. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 2.3 m under a head of 1.1 m. Taking Cd = 0.62 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 2.2 m wide carries a discharge of 15.5 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 590 m and design speed 60 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 590, V = 60 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (60)^2 / (127*590) | Answer: 0.04804
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: For a design speed of 85 km/h with allowable superelevation 0.07 and lateral friction 0.16, find the minimum curve radius in m.
A tank of volume 460 m^3 treats a flow of 70 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 460, Q = 70 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 460 / 70 | Answer: 6.571 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 320 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.17 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 8 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 320, k = 0.17, t = 8 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 320*(1 - e^(-0.17*8)) | Answer: 237.9 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.71, rainfall intensity 75 mm/h over a catchment of 7.4 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.71, i = 75, A = 7.4 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.71*75*7.4 / 360 | Answer: 1.095 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.01 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 610 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.01, M = 610 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 610*(30+0.01)/30 | Answer: 610.2 m

question: Convert the decimal number 36 to binary.
solution: Divide 36 by 2 repeatedly, recording remainders | Reading remainders in reverse gives 100100 | Answer: 100100 (binary)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 2 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the decimal number 1755 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 1755 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 6DB (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the 8-bit binary number 11110110 to decimal.
solution: Binary 11110110 = sum of bit-weights | Answer: 246 (decimal)
formula: Sum each bit times its positional weight (2^i)

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 11111101 and 10011100.
solution: XOR: 01100001 | Count of 1s = 3 | Answer: 3
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 800 megabits is sent over a link of 64 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 800, B = 64 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 800 / 64 | Answer: 12.5 s

question: A link has bandwidth 98 Mbps and round-trip time 170 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 98, R = 170 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 98e6 * 170e-3 bits = 16660 kb | Answer: 16660 kilobits

question: A channel of bandwidth 16 kHz has a signal-to-noise ratio of 15 (linear). Using Shannon's theorem, find the channel capacity in kbps.
solution: Given: B = 16, SNR = 15 | Formula: C = B log2(1 + SNR) | Substitute: C = 16*log2(1 + 15) | Answer: 64 kbps

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.94, cache access time 7 ns and main-memory access time 200 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.94, tc = 7, tm = 200 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.94*7 + (1 - 0.94)*200 | Answer: 18.58 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 470529 elements?
solution: Given: n = 470529 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(470529)) + 1 | Answer: 19

question: An O(n^2) algorithm performs c*n^2 basic operations. If c = 1 and n = 2160, how many operations are performed?
solution: Given: n = 2160 | Formula: operations = n^2 | Substitute: = (2160)^2 | Answer: 4665600

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.004, memory access time 130 ns and page-fault service time 3 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 3 ms = 3000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.004)*130 + 0.004*3000000.0 ns | Answer: 12.13 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 0.1 m^3 at 380 kPa and 410 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 0.1, P = 380, Tk = 410 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (380e3)*0.1 / (8.314*410) | Answer: 11.15 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.18 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 16 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.18, t = 16 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.18*16) | Answer: 0.9439

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.31 /min) is to reach 75% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.31, X = 75 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.75) / 0.31 | Answer: 4.472 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.46 /min) reaches 65% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.46, X = 65 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.65 / (0.46*(1 - 0.65)) | Answer: 4.037 min

question: For a reaction with A = 5e10 /s and activation energy 60 kJ/mol at 460 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 5, Ea = 60, Tk = 460 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 5e10 * exp(-60e3 / (8.314*460)) | Answer: 7683 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.91 and bottoms xW = 0.03, with relative volatility alpha = 2.2. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.91, xw = 0.03, al = 2.2 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.91/0.09)(0.97/0.03)] / ln(2.2) | Answer: 7.343 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.64 and x = 0.21. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.64, x = 0.21 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.64/0.36) / (0.21/0.79) | Answer: 6.688

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.66 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 110 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.66, Psat = 110 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.66 * 110 | Answer: 72.6 kPa

question: A stream of 7.2 kg/s with specific heat 2.9 kJ/kg-K is heated through 20 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 7.2, cp = 2.9, dT = 20 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 7.2*2.9*20 | Answer: 417.6 kW

question: A reactor of volume 9.7 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 1.1 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 9.7, Q = 1.1 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 9.7 / 1.1 | Answer: 8.818 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 7.4e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 4 mm with a concentration difference of 170 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 7.4, L = 4, dC = 170 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (7.4e-9)*170 / (4e-3) | Answer: 314.5 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 7.4 min and steady-state gain 1.2. For a step input of magnitude 13, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 7.4, K = 1.2, M = 13 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 1.2 * 13 | Answer: 15.6 units

question: A reactor operates at a space time of 18.9 min. Find its space velocity in per hour.
solution: Given: tau = 18.9 | Formula: SV = 60 / tau  (per hour) | Substitute: SV = 60 / 18.9 | Answer: 3.175 /h

question: An aircraft wing of area 55 m^2 flies at 160 m/s (air density 0.7 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 1.3. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 55, V = 160, rho = 0.7, CL = 1.3 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.7*(160)^2*55*1.3 / 1000 | Answer: 640.6 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 120 m^2 flies at 220 m/s (density 0.4 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.11. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 120, V = 220, rho = 0.4, CD = 0.11 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.4*(220)^2*120*0.11 / 1000 | Answer: 127.8 kN

question: An aircraft flies at 600 m/s where the speed of sound is 310 m/s. Find the Mach number.
solution: Given: V = 600, a = 310 | Formula: M = V / a | Substitute: M = 600 / 310 | Answer: 1.935

question: A specimen under stress 300 MPa shows an elastic strain of 2.7e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 300, eps = 2.7 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 300 / (2.7e-3) MPa = 111.1 GPa | Answer: 111.1 GPa

question: A block of mass 17 kg has a volume of 3.7e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 17, V = 3.7 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 17 / (3.7e-3) | Answer: 4595 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 2500 mm is heated through 140 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 23e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 2500, dT = 140, al = 23 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 2500*23e-6*140 | Answer: 8.05 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 115 ohm, R2 = 190 ohm and R3 = 190 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 115, R2 = 190, R3 = 190 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 190*190 / 115 | Answer: 313.9 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 120 ohm and gauge factor 2.1 experiences a strain of 1350e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 120, GF = 2.1, eps = 1350 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 120*2.1*1350e-6 | Answer: 340.2 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 10.59 when the true value is 10. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10.59, true = 10 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10.59 - 10| / 10 * 100 | Answer: 5.9 %

question: Annual demand is 48500 units, ordering cost 70 per order and holding cost 6 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 48500, S = 70, H = 6 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*48500*70 / 6) | Answer: 1064 units

question: An asset costs 370000 with salvage value 2000 after 19 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 370000, Sv = 2000, n = 19 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (370000 - 2000) / 19 | Answer: 19368 per year

question: A product sells for 130 per unit with variable cost 110 per unit and fixed costs 40000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 130, V = 110, F = 40000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 40000 / (130 - 110) | Answer: 2000 units

question: Find the present worth of 50000 received 7 years from now at an interest rate of 12% per year.
solution: Given: F = 50000, n = 7, i = 12 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 50000 / (1 + 0.12)^7 | Answer: 22617 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.92, 0.92 and 0.91 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.92, r2 = 0.92, r3 = 0.91 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.92*0.92*0.91 | Answer: 0.7702

question: A process produces 9 defective items in a batch of 14000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 9, N = 14000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 9/14000 * 1e6 | Answer: 642.9 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -2x^3 + 5x^2 - 4x - 6 evaluated at x = -2.
For f(x) = -6x^3 - x^2 + 4x - 4, find f''(x) at x = 2.
Evaluate the definite integral of (2x^2 + 6x) dx from x = 0 to x = 3.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = 2x^3/3 + 6x^2/2 + 0x | Evaluate F(3) - F(0) | Answer: 45
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 5x^2 + 5x = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[8, 7], [7, 7]].
solution: Given: a = 8, b = 7, c = 7, d = 7 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (8)(7) - (7)(7) | Answer: 7

question: Find the determinant of [[4, -4, 3], [-6, 2, -4], [-3, -3, -1]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: -8

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[-6, 8], [4, 6]].
solution: Trace tr = 0, Determinant = -68 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 8.246

question: Solve for x: -3x + -2y = -8 and -6x + 0y = -8.
solution: Determinant = -3*0 - -2*-6 = -12 | x = (e d - b f) / det = 1.333 | Answer: x = 1.333
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 75, 3, 29, 41, 2.
solution: Sum = 150 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 30 | Answer: 30

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 44, 33, 38, 46, 5.
solution: Mean = 33.2 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 16.57

question: Find the slope of the line through (2, 1) and (-2, -6).
solution: Given: x1 = 2, y1 = 1, x2 = -2, y2 = -6 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (-6 - 1) / (-2 - 2) | Answer: 1.75

question: Find the distance between the points (9, -7) and (8, -8).
solution: Given: x1 = 9, y1 = -7, x2 = 8, y2 = -8 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-1)^2 + (-1)^2) | Answer: 1.414 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (5,-2), (-6,-3), (5,-7).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 27.5 sq units

question: Evaluate the number of combinations C(20, 8).
solution: Given: n = 20, r = 8 | Formula: C(n, r) = n! / (r! (n - r)!) | Substitute: C(20, 8) = 20! / (8! * 12!) | Answer: 125970

question: Find the 24th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 19 and common difference -9.
solution: Given: a = 19, d = -9, n = 24 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = 19 + (24 - 1)*-9 | Answer: -188

question: Find the sum of the first 14 terms of an AP with first term -4 and common difference 8.
solution: Given: a = -4, d = 8, n = 14 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 14/2 [2*-4 + (14-1)*8] | Answer: 672

question: Find the 4th term of a geometric progression with first term 6 and common ratio 4.
solution: Given: a = 6, r = 4, n = 4 | Formula: a_n = a r^(n-1) | Substitute: a_n = 6 * 4^(4-1) | Answer: 384

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 46500 at 6.8% per annum for 3 years.
solution: Given: P = 46500, R = 6.8, Tt = 3 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 46500 * 6.8 * 3 / 100 | Answer: 9486 currency units

question: Find the amount when 18500 is invested at 6.1% per annum compounded annually for 2 years.
solution: Given: P = 18500, R = 6.1, Tt = 2 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 18500 * (1 + 6.1/100)^2 | Answer: 20826 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (6, -5, -4) and (6, 3, -3).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (-3, 1, 4) and (-2, 2, -1).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 14.76

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (-4, 4, 4) and (3, 6, -6).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 101.1 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number 1 + 3i.
solution: Given: a = 1, b = 3 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((1)^2 + (3)^2) | Answer: 3.162

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number -5 + 0i.
solution: Given: a = -5, b = 0 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(0, -5) | Answer: 180 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = 4x^3 + 2x^2 + 7x + 7 at x = 2.
solution: Given: a = 4, b = 2, c = 7, d = 7, x0 = 2 | Formula: f(x0) = a x0^3 + b x0^2 + c x0 + d | Substitute: f(2) = 4(2)^3 + 2(2)^2 + 7(2) + 7 | Answer: 61

question: Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-41 with initial guess x0=5, find x1 (one iteration).
solution: Given: N = 41, x0 = 5 | Formula: x1 = x0 - (x0^2 - N)/(2 x0) | Substitute: x1 = 5 - ((5)^2 - 41)/(2*5) | Answer: 6.6

question: Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.1 and ordinates 5, 2, 8, 10, 20, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 484 and 301.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 484 and 301 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 20 and 41.
solution: Given: a = 20, b = 41 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 20*41 / 1 | Answer: 820
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 29 mm carries an axial tensile load of 65 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 15 mm and length 2700 mm carries an axial load of 73 kN. Take E = 200 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 72 mm transmits a torque of 2350 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 72, Tt = 2350 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(2350*1000) / (pi*(72)^3) | Answer: 32.07 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 64 mm and length 2000 mm carries a torque of 500 N-m. With G = 45 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (64)^4 / 32 = 1647099 mm^4 | theta = (500*1000)(2000) / (45000 * 1647099) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 0.773 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 115 mm wide and 140 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 115, h = 140 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 115*(140)^2 / 6 | Answer: 375667 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (99 mm x 160 mm) carries a bending moment of 8 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (54 mm x 160 mm) has effective length 3800 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 700 MPa is designed for a working stress of 100 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 700, sw = 100 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 700 / 100 | Answer: 7

question: A steel bar is fully restrained and heated through 110 deg C. With E = 210 GPa and alpha = 13e-6 /deg C, find the thermal stress in MPa.
solution: Given: dT = 110, E = 210, al = 13 | Formula: sigma = E alpha (dT) | Substitute: sigma = 210000 * 13e-6 * 110 | Answer: 300.3 MPa

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 500 mm and wall thickness 11 mm carries an internal pressure of 2.2 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 500, t = 11, P = 2.2 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 2.2*500 / (2*11) | Answer: 50 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 940 K and 360 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 940, Tc = 360 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 360/940) * 100 | Answer: 61.7 %

question: A refrigerator works between 260 K (cold) and 322 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 260, Th = 322 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 260 / (322 - 260) | Answer: 4.194

question: A heat pump operates between 283 K and 320 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 283, Th = 320 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 320 / (320 - 283) | Answer: 8.649

question: 1.7 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 145 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1.7, dT = 145 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 1.7 * 0.718 * 145 | Answer: 177 kJ

question: 6.6 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 190 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 6.6, dT = 190 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 6.6 * 1.005 * 190 | Answer: 126 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 0.8 m^3 at 440 K with mass 3.7 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 0.8, Tk = 440, m = 3.7 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 3.7*0.287*440 / 0.8 | Answer: 584 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 1.2 kg of air expands isothermally at 500 K from volume V1 to 3*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1.2, Tk = 500, ratio = 3 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 1.2*0.287*500*ln(3) | Answer: 189.2 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 4.2 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.13 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 4.2, D = 0.13 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*4.2*0.13 / 0.001 | Answer: 546000

question: Water flows at 3.3 m/s through a pipe of diameter 230 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 4.6 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 4.6 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*4.6 / 1000 | Answer: 45.13 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 5.2 m. Taking Cv = 0.99, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 5.2, cv = 0.99 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.99*sqrt(2*9.81*5.2) | Answer: 10 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 150 mm) water flows at 0.9 m/s. It contracts to diameter 140 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
Water flows at 3.2 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.18 m and length 270 m. With friction factor f = 0.033, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 25 teeth drives a gear of 46 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1450 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 25, z2 = 46, N1 = 1450 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1450*25 / 46 | Answer: 788 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 510 mm rotates at 500 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 510, N = 500 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.51)*500 / 60 | Answer: 13.35 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 12.1 kW at 600 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 12.1, N = 600 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(12.1*1000) / (2*pi*600) | Answer: 192.6 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 0.8 kg rotates at radius 0.57 m at 400 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 1400 N/m and mass 6.6 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 1400, m = 6.6 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(1400/6.6) | Answer: 2.318 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 6.3 m^2 and thickness 0.18 m has conductivity k = 46.3 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 140 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 6.3, L = 0.18, k = 46.3, dT = 140 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 46.3*6.3*140 / 0.18 | Answer: 226870 W

question: A surface of area 3.4 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 40 W/m^2-K to surroundings 65 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 3.4, h = 40, dT = 65 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 40*3.4*65 | Answer: 8840 W

question: In a counter-flow heat exchanger the terminal temperature differences are 65 deg C and 20 deg C. Find the log mean temperature difference (LMTD) in deg C.
solution: Given: dT1 = 65, dT2 = 20 | Formula: LMTD = (dT1 - dT2) / ln(dT1/dT2) | Substitute: LMTD = (65 - 20) / ln(65/20) | Answer: 38.18 deg C

question: In turning, cutting speed = 130 m/min, feed = 0.46 mm/rev, depth of cut = 1 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 130, f = 0.46, d = 1 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*130*0.46*1 | Answer: 59800 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 440 mm is turned at 1050 rpm with a feed of 0.25 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 440, N = 1050, f = 0.25 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 440 / (0.25*1050) | Answer: 1.676 min

question: A resistor of 80 ohm carries a current of 2.1 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 80, I = 2.1 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 2.1 * 80 | Answer: 168 V

question: Three resistors 43 ohm, 36 ohm and 25 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 43, R2 = 36, R3 = 25 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 43 + 36 + 25 | Answer: 104 ohm

question: Two resistors 94 ohm and 23 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 94, R2 = 23 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 94*23 / (94+23) | Answer: 18.48 ohm

question: A device draws 1.4 A at 50 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 50, I = 1.4 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 50 * 1.4 | Answer: 70 W

question: A current of 4.5 A flows through a 25 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 4.5, R = 25 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (4.5)^2 * 25 | Answer: 506.2 W

question: Two capacitors 39.1 uF and 16.8 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 39.1, C2 = 16.8 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 39.1*16.8 / (39.1+16.8) | Answer: 11.75 uF

question: A resistor 1 kohm and capacitor 7.1 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 1, C = 7.1 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (1k)(7.1u) = 7.1 ms | Answer: 7.1 ms

question: An inductor 37.5 mH is in series with 93 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 37.5, R = 93 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (37.5e-3) / 93 | Answer: 0.4032 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 43 mH inductor at 910 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 43, f = 910 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (910)(43e-3) | Answer: 245.9 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 14.1 uF capacitor at 70 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 14.1, f = 70 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (70)(14.1e-6)) | Answer: 161.3 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 11 ohm, XL = 134 ohm and XC = 128 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 11, XL = 134, XC = 128 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(11^2 + (134 - 128)^2) | Answer: 12.53 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 39.1 mH and C = 4.2 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 39.1, C = 4.2 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(39.1e-3 * 4.2e-6)) | Answer: 392.7 Hz

question: A capacitor of 73.6 uF is charged to 130 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 73.6, V = 130 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*73.6e-6*(130)^2 | Answer: 621.9 mJ

question: An alternating voltage has a peak value of 324 V. Find its RMS value.
solution: Given: Vp = 324 | Formula: Vrms = Vp / sqrt(2) | Substitute: Vrms = 324 / sqrt(2) | Answer: 229.1 V

question: A transformer has primary voltage 260 V with 890 primary turns and 420 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 260, N1 = 890, N2 = 420 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 260 * 420/890 | Answer: 122.7 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 120 V and draws an armature current of 37 A. If the armature resistance is 0.44 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 120, Ia = 37, Ra = 0.44 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 120 - 37*0.44 | Answer: 103.7 V

question: A 4-pole induction motor on a 60 Hz supply runs at 770 rpm. Find the slip (%).
formula: s = (Ns - N) / Ns,  Ns = 120 f / P

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 80 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.97. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 80, VL = 400, pf = 0.97 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*400*80*0.97 / 1000 | Answer: 53.76 kW

question: A load has real power 20 kW and apparent power 155 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 20, S = 155 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 20 / 155 | Answer: 0.129

question: A machine delivers 55 kW output while drawing 172 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 55, Pi = 172 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 55/172 * 100 | Answer: 31.98 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 5 V across R1 = 5 ohm and R2 = 30 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 5, R1 = 5, R2 = 30 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 5*30 / (5+30) | Answer: 4.286 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 210 kohm and Rin = 20 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 210, Rin = 20 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 210 / 20 | Answer: 10.5

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 110 kohm and Rg = 27 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 110, Rg = 27 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 110/27 | Answer: 5.074

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 7300. Express the gain in decibels (power).

question: A simply supported beam of span 8.7 m carries a UDL of 20 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.

question: A cantilever of length 5.4 m carries a point load 50 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.4, W = 50 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 50*5.4 | Answer: 270 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 5.6 m carries a UDL of 22 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.6, w = 22 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 22*(5.6)^2 / 2 | Answer: 345 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 8.4 m carries a point load 75 kN at distance 3 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.

question: A simply supported beam (span 4.9 m) carries a central point load 65 kN. With E = 200 GPa and I = 570e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.

question: A fixed beam of span 7.2 m carries a UDL of 27 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.

question: An RC beam has overall depth 580 mm, clear cover 50 mm and main bars of diameter 16 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.

question: A column supports a floor area of 33.9 m^2 carrying a factored load of 13.1 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.

question: For a bar of diameter 25 mm with design bond stress 1.5 MPa and steel stress 435 MPa, find the development length in mm.

question: At a depth of 4.2 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 20 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 8.7e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.5, area = 6.4e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 8.7, i = 0.5, A = 6.4 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (8.7e-4)*0.5*(6.4e-3) | Answer: 2784 mm^3/s

question: For a design speed of 60 km/h with allowable superelevation 0.08 and lateral friction 0.13, find the minimum curve radius in m.

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 230 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.23 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 7 days.

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.55, rainfall intensity 30 mm/h over a catchment of 14.6 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.

formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.07 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 500 m with this tape.

question: A file of 860 megabits is sent over a link of 82 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.

question: A link has bandwidth 52 Mbps and round-trip time 70 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 52, R = 70 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 52e6 * 70e-3 bits = 3640 kb | Answer: 3640 kilobits

question: A channel has bandwidth 14 kHz. Using Nyquist's theorem with 2 signal levels, find the maximum data rate in kbps (noiseless).
solution: Given: B = 14, M = 2 | Formula: C = 2 B log2(M) | Substitute: C = 2*14*log2(2) | Answer: 28 kbps

question: A channel of bandwidth 15 kHz has a signal-to-noise ratio of 15 (linear). Using Shannon's theorem, find the channel capacity in kbps.
solution: Given: B = 15, SNR = 15 | Formula: C = B log2(1 + SNR) | Substitute: C = 15*log2(1 + 15) | Answer: 60 kbps

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.95, cache access time 7 ns and main-memory access time 140 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.95, tc = 7, tm = 140 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.95*7 + (1 - 0.95)*140 | Answer: 13.65 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 412716 elements?

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.001, memory access time 140 ns and page-fault service time 7 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 7 ms = 7000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.001)*140 + 0.001*7000000.0 ns | Answer: 7.14 microseconds

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 0.8 m^3 at 150 kPa and 460 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 0.8, P = 150, Tk = 460 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (150e3)*0.8 / (8.314*460) | Answer: 31.38 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.17 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 7 minutes.

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.16 /min) is to reach 85% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.27 /min) reaches 90% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.27, X = 90 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.9 / (0.27*(1 - 0.9)) | Answer: 33.33 min

question: For a reaction with A = 6e10 /s and activation energy 70 kJ/mol at 500 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 6, Ea = 70, Tk = 500 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 6e10 * exp(-70e3 / (8.314*500)) | Answer: 2918 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.96 and bottoms xW = 0.08, with relative volatility alpha = 1.8. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.96, xw = 0.08, al = 1.8 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.96/0.04)(0.92/0.08)] / ln(1.8) | Answer: 9.562 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.82 and x = 0.22. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.57 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 25 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.

question: A stream of 2.9 kg/s with specific heat 3.3 kJ/kg-K is heated through 15 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 2.9, cp = 3.3, dT = 15 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 2.9*3.3*15 | Answer: 143.5 kW

question: A reactor of volume 19.1 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 4.5 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 2.3e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 3 mm with a concentration difference of 50 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.

question: A first-order process has time constant 6.2 min and steady-state gain 1.5. For a step input of magnitude 5, find the final (steady-state) change in output.

question: An aircraft wing of area 120 m^2 flies at 180 m/s (air density 1 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 1. Find the lift force in kN.

question: A specimen under stress 380 MPa shows an elastic strain of 1.4e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.

question: A block of mass 27 kg has a volume of 4e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.

question: A rod of length 2100 mm is heated through 75 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 11e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 130 ohm, R2 = 40 ohm and R3 = 340 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).

question: A strain gauge of resistance 350 ohm and gauge factor 2 experiences a strain of 1300e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.

question: A measurement reads 10.74 when the true value is 100. Find the percentage error.

question: Find the present worth of 55000 received 5 years from now at an interest rate of 10% per year.

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.95, 0.98 and 0.91 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.

question: A process produces 24 defective items in a batch of 1500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).

question: Evaluate the number of combinations C(8, 8).

question: Find the 7th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 6 and common difference -4.

question: Find the 5th term of a geometric progression with first term 8 and common ratio 2.

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 47000 at 13.5% per annum for 3 years.

question: Find the amount when 26000 is invested at 6.8% per annum compounded annually for 6 years.

formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 900 MPa is designed for a working stress of 60 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 900, sw = 60 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 900 / 60 | Answer: 15

question: A steel bar is fully restrained and heated through 105 deg C. With E = 210 GPa and alpha = 12e-6 /deg C, find the thermal stress in MPa.
solution: Given: dT = 105, E = 210, al = 12 | Formula: sigma = E alpha (dT) | Substitute: sigma = 210000 * 12e-6 * 105 | Answer: 264.6 MPa

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 300 mm and wall thickness 14 mm carries an internal pressure of 2.2 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 300, t = 14, P = 2.2 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 2.2*300 / (2*14) | Answer: 23.57 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 1140 K and 330 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 1140, Tc = 330 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 330/1140) * 100 | Answer: 71.05 %

question: A refrigerator works between 274 K (cold) and 308 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 274, Th = 308 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 274 / (308 - 274) | Answer: 8.059

question: A heat pump operates between 260 K and 320 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 260, Th = 320 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 320 / (320 - 260) | Answer: 5.333

question: 1.4 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 45 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1.4, dT = 45 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 1.4 * 0.718 * 45 | Answer: 45.23 kJ

question: 3.6 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 30 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.6, dT = 30 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 3.6 * 1.005 * 30 | Answer: 108.5 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 3.9 m^3 at 350 K with mass 2.3 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 3.9, Tk = 350, m = 2.3 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 2.3*0.287*350 / 3.9 | Answer: 59.24 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 2.9 kg of air expands isothermally at 470 K from volume V1 to 5*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.9, Tk = 470, ratio = 5 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 2.9*0.287*470*ln(5) | Answer: 629.6 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 4.9 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.24 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 4.9, D = 0.24 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*4.9*0.24 / 0.001 | Answer: 1176000

question: Water flows at 1.9 m/s through a pipe of diameter 290 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 24.5 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 24.5 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*24.5 / 1000 | Answer: 240.3 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 16.9 m. Taking Cv = 0.95, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 16.9, cv = 0.95 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.95*sqrt(2*9.81*16.9) | Answer: 17.3 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 290 mm) water flows at 1.3 m/s. It contracts to diameter 50 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 290, d2 = 50, V1 = 1.3 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 1.3*(290/50)^2 | Answer: 43.73 m/s

question: Water flows at 2.3 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.19 m and length 490 m. With friction factor f = 0.031, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 24 teeth drives a gear of 92 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1450 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 24, z2 = 92, N1 = 1450 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1450*24 / 92 | Answer: 378.3 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 310 mm rotates at 750 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 310, N = 750 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.31)*750 / 60 | Answer: 12.17 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 35.9 kW at 1200 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 35.9, N = 1200 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(35.9*1000) / (2*pi*1200) | Answer: 285.7 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 1.7 kg rotates at radius 0.14 m at 950 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 3600 N/m and mass 4.5 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 3600, m = 4.5 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(3600/4.5) | Answer: 4.502 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 3.5 m^2 and thickness 0.39 m has conductivity k = 25.6 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 55 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 3.5, L = 0.39, k = 25.6, dT = 55 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 25.6*3.5*55 / 0.39 | Answer: 12636 W

question: A surface of area 0.7 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 165 W/m^2-K to surroundings 75 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 0.7, h = 165, dT = 75 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 165*0.7*75 | Answer: 8662 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 200 m/min, feed = 0.3 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2.6 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 200, f = 0.3, d = 2.6 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*200*0.3*2.6 | Answer: 156000 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 290 mm is turned at 300 rpm with a feed of 0.39 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 290, N = 300, f = 0.39 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 290 / (0.39*300) | Answer: 2.479 min

question: A resistor of 106 ohm carries a current of 9.7 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 106, I = 9.7 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 9.7 * 106 | Answer: 1028 V

question: Three resistors 53 ohm, 17 ohm and 26 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 53, R2 = 17, R3 = 26 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 53 + 17 + 26 | Answer: 96 ohm

question: Two resistors 12 ohm and 34 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 12, R2 = 34 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 12*34 / (12+34) | Answer: 8.87 ohm

question: A device draws 13.6 A at 190 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 190, I = 13.6 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 190 * 13.6 | Answer: 2584 W

question: A current of 6.5 A flows through a 34 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 6.5, R = 34 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (6.5)^2 * 34 | Answer: 1436 W

question: Two capacitors 46.5 uF and 28 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 46.5, C2 = 28 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 46.5*28 / (46.5+28) | Answer: 17.48 uF

question: A resistor 48 kohm and capacitor 3.7 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 48, C = 3.7 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (48k)(3.7u) = 177.6 ms | Answer: 177.6 ms

question: An inductor 284.4 mH is in series with 110 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 284.4, R = 110 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (284.4e-3) / 110 | Answer: 2.585 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 5.1 mH inductor at 870 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 5.1, f = 870 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (870)(5.1e-3) | Answer: 27.88 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 41.8 uF capacitor at 390 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 41.8, f = 390 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (390)(41.8e-6)) | Answer: 9.763 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 55 ohm, XL = 25 ohm and XC = 122 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 55, XL = 25, XC = 122 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(55^2 + (25 - 122)^2) | Answer: 111.5 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 49.3 mH and C = 5.5 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 49.3, C = 5.5 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(49.3e-3 * 5.5e-6)) | Answer: 305.6 Hz

question: A capacitor of 37.7 uF is charged to 285 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 37.7, V = 285 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*37.7e-6*(285)^2 | Answer: 1531 mJ

question: An alternating voltage has a peak value of 116 V. Find its RMS value.
solution: Given: Vp = 116 | Formula: Vrms = Vp / sqrt(2) | Substitute: Vrms = 116 / sqrt(2) | Answer: 82.02 V

question: A transformer has primary voltage 300 V with 440 primary turns and 470 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 300, N1 = 440, N2 = 470 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 300 * 470/440 | Answer: 320.5 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 440 V and draws an armature current of 34 A. If the armature resistance is 0.75 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 440, Ia = 34, Ra = 0.75 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 440 - 34*0.75 | Answer: 414.5 V

question: A 4-pole induction motor on a 50 Hz supply runs at 860 rpm. Find the slip (%).
formula: s = (Ns - N) / Ns,  Ns = 120 f / P

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 185 A at 433 V (line) with a power factor of 0.83. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 185, VL = 433, pf = 0.83 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*433*185*0.83 / 1000 | Answer: 115.2 kW

question: A load has real power 130 kW and apparent power 190 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 130, S = 190 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 130 / 190 | Answer: 0.6842

question: A machine delivers 80 kW output while drawing 102 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 80, Pi = 102 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 80/102 * 100 | Answer: 78.43 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 25 V across R1 = 3 ohm and R2 = 33 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 25, R1 = 3, R2 = 33 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 25*33 / (3+33) | Answer: 22.92 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 160 kohm and Rin = 17 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 160, Rin = 17 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 160 / 17 | Answer: 9.412

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 200 kohm and Rg = 8 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 200, Rg = 8 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 200/8 | Answer: 26

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 2388. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 2388 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(2388) | Answer: 33.78 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 7 m carries a central point load of 20 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7, W = 20 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 20*7 / 4 | Answer: 35 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.3 m carries a UDL of 45 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.3, w = 45 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 45*(4.3)^2 / 8 | Answer: 104 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 2.6 m carries a point load 80 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 2.6, W = 80 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 80*2.6 | Answer: 208 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 3.7 m carries a UDL of 32 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.7, w = 32 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 32*(3.7)^2 / 2 | Answer: 219 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.4 m carries a point load 50 kN at distance 1.6 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 9.4, a = 1.6, W = 50 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 50*(9.4 - 1.6) / 9.4 | Answer: 41.49 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 7 m) carries a central point load 10 kN. With E = 30 GPa and I = 390e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=10000 N, L=7000.0 mm, E=30000 MPa, I=390e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 6.108 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 5.5 m carries a UDL of 27 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.5, w = 27 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 27*(5.5)^2 / 12 | Answer: 68.06 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 410 mm, clear cover 25 mm and main bars of diameter 25 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 410, c = 25, dia = 25 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 410 - 25 - 25/2 | Answer: 372.5 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 14.6 m^2 carrying a factored load of 12.9 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 14.6, w = 12.9 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 12.9 * 14.6 | Answer: 188.3 kN

question: For a bar of diameter 12 mm with design bond stress 2.2 MPa and steel stress 435 MPa, find the development length in mm.
solution: Given: dia = 12, tbd = 2.2, fs = 435 | Formula: Ld = phi fs / (4 tau_bd) | Substitute: Ld = 12*435 / (4*2.2) | Answer: 593.2 mm

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 6.4 m, unit weight 19 kN/m^3, phi = 35 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 8.3 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 20 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 8.3, g = 20 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (20 - 9.81)*8.3 | Answer: 84.58 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 7.9e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.7, area = 2.7e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 7.9, i = 0.7, A = 2.7 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (7.9e-4)*0.7*(2.7e-3) | Answer: 1493 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 2.1 m, bed slope 0.006 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.026. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 1.9 m under a head of 0.8 m. Taking Cd = 0.6 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 4.8 m wide carries a discharge of 26.4 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 130 m and design speed 55 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 130, V = 55 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (55)^2 / (127*130) | Answer: 0.1832
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: For a design speed of 70 km/h with allowable superelevation 0.07 and lateral friction 0.14, find the minimum curve radius in m.
A tank of volume 190 m^3 treats a flow of 45 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 190, Q = 45 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 190 / 45 | Answer: 4.222 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 260 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.12 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 6 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 260, k = 0.12, t = 6 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 260*(1 - e^(-0.12*6)) | Answer: 133.4 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.4, rainfall intensity 40 mm/h over a catchment of 52.6 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.4, i = 40, A = 52.6 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.4*40*52.6 / 360 | Answer: 2.338 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.01 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 440 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.01, M = 440 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 440*(30+0.01)/30 | Answer: 440.1 m

question: Convert the decimal number 24 to binary.
solution: Divide 24 by 2 repeatedly, recording remainders | Reading remainders in reverse gives 11000 | Answer: 11000 (binary)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 2 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the decimal number 244 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 244 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: F4 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the 8-bit binary number 10110010 to decimal.
solution: Binary 10110010 = sum of bit-weights | Answer: 178 (decimal)
formula: Sum each bit times its positional weight (2^i)

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 10101111 and 00000010.
solution: XOR: 10101101 | Count of 1s = 5 | Answer: 5
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 640 megabits is sent over a link of 9 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 640, B = 9 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 640 / 9 | Answer: 71.11 s

question: A link has bandwidth 55 Mbps and round-trip time 50 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 55, R = 50 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 55e6 * 50e-3 bits = 2750 kb | Answer: 2750 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.81, cache access time 7 ns and main-memory access time 110 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.81, tc = 7, tm = 110 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.81*7 + (1 - 0.81)*110 | Answer: 26.57 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 121979 elements?
solution: Given: n = 121979 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(121979)) + 1 | Answer: 17

question: An O(n^2) algorithm performs c*n^2 basic operations. If c = 1 and n = 1720, how many operations are performed?
solution: Given: n = 1720 | Formula: operations = n^2 | Substitute: = (1720)^2 | Answer: 2958400

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.01, memory access time 80 ns and page-fault service time 10 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 10 ms = 10000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.01)*80 + 0.01*10000000.0 ns | Answer: 100.1 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 1.3 m^3 at 320 kPa and 540 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 1.3, P = 320, Tk = 540 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (320e3)*1.3 / (8.314*540) | Answer: 92.66 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.36 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 9 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.36, t = 9 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.36*9) | Answer: 0.9608

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.14 /min) is to reach 85% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.14, X = 85 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.85) / 0.14 | Answer: 13.55 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.4 /min) reaches 70% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.4, X = 70 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.7 / (0.4*(1 - 0.7)) | Answer: 5.833 min

question: For a reaction with A = 7e10 /s and activation energy 85 kJ/mol at 330 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 7, Ea = 85, Tk = 330 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 7e10 * exp(-85e3 / (8.314*330)) | Answer: 0.002456 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.95 and bottoms xW = 0.04, with relative volatility alpha = 2.8. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.95, xw = 0.04, al = 2.8 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.95/0.05)(0.96/0.04)] / ln(2.8) | Answer: 5.946 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.73 and x = 0.46. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.73, x = 0.46 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.73/0.27) / (0.46/0.54) | Answer: 3.174

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.43 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 120 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.43, Psat = 120 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.43 * 120 | Answer: 51.6 kPa

question: A stream of 3.6 kg/s with specific heat 3.7 kJ/kg-K is heated through 50 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 3.6, cp = 3.7, dT = 50 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 3.6*3.7*50 | Answer: 666 kW

question: A reactor of volume 2.2 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 1 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 2.2, Q = 1 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 2.2 / 1 | Answer: 2.2 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 7.5e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 1 mm with a concentration difference of 100 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 7.5, L = 1, dC = 100 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (7.5e-9)*100 / (1e-3) | Answer: 750 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 3.3 min and steady-state gain 2.2. For a step input of magnitude 18, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 3.3, K = 2.2, M = 18 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 2.2 * 18 | Answer: 39.6 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 25 m^2 flies at 240 m/s (air density 0.7 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.3. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 25, V = 240, rho = 0.7, CL = 0.3 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.7*(240)^2*25*0.3 / 1000 | Answer: 151.2 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 35 m^2 flies at 200 m/s (density 0.4 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.08. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 35, V = 200, rho = 0.4, CD = 0.08 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.4*(200)^2*35*0.08 / 1000 | Answer: 22.4 kN

question: Find the dynamic pressure for air of density 1.225 kg/m^3 moving at 50 m/s, in Pa.
solution: Given: rho = 1.225, V = 50 | Formula: q = 0.5 rho V^2 | Substitute: q = 0.5*1.225*(50)^2 | Answer: 1531 Pa

question: An aircraft flies at 600 m/s where the speed of sound is 295 m/s. Find the Mach number.
solution: Given: V = 600, a = 295 | Formula: M = V / a | Substitute: M = 600 / 295 | Answer: 2.034

question: A specimen under stress 140 MPa shows an elastic strain of 1.5e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 140, eps = 1.5 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 140 / (1.5e-3) MPa = 93.33 GPa | Answer: 93.33 GPa

question: A block of mass 48 kg has a volume of 3.4e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 48, V = 3.4 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 48 / (3.4e-3) | Answer: 14118 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 2600 mm is heated through 105 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 11e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 2600, dT = 105, al = 11 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 2600*11e-6*105 | Answer: 3.003 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 15 ohm, R2 = 110 ohm and R3 = 425 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 15, R2 = 110, R3 = 425 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 110*425 / 15 | Answer: 3117 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 120 ohm and gauge factor 2.2 experiences a strain of 1750e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 120, GF = 2.2, eps = 1750 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 120*2.2*1750e-6 | Answer: 462 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 10.71 when the true value is 100. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10.71, true = 100 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10.71 - 100| / 100 * 100 | Answer: 89.29 %

question: Annual demand is 38000 units, ordering cost 30 per order and holding cost 33 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 38000, S = 30, H = 33 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*38000*30 / 33) | Answer: 262.9 units

question: An asset costs 320000 with salvage value 12000 after 5 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 320000, Sv = 12000, n = 5 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (320000 - 12000) / 5 | Answer: 61600 per year

question: A product sells for 390 per unit with variable cost 180 per unit and fixed costs 135000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 390, V = 180, F = 135000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 135000 / (390 - 180) | Answer: 642.9 units

question: Find the present worth of 75000 received 5 years from now at an interest rate of 11% per year.
solution: Given: F = 75000, n = 5, i = 11 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 75000 / (1 + 0.11)^5 | Answer: 44509 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.92, 0.95 and 0.96 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.92, r2 = 0.95, r3 = 0.96 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.92*0.95*0.96 | Answer: 0.839

question: A process produces 14 defective items in a batch of 4000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 14, N = 4000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 14/4000 * 1e6 | Answer: 3500 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -2x^3 - 4x^2 - 7x - 2 evaluated at x = 3.
For f(x) = -3x^3 - 7x^2 + 9x + 8, find f''(x) at x = 5.
