question: Two resistors 56 ohm and 81 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 56, R2 = 81 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 56*81 / (56+81) | Answer: 33.11 ohm

question: A device draws 13.1 A at 125 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 125, I = 13.1 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 125 * 13.1 | Answer: 1638 W

question: A current of 2.5 A flows through a 95 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 2.5, R = 95 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (2.5)^2 * 95 | Answer: 593.8 W

question: Two capacitors 41.9 uF and 36 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 41.9, C2 = 36 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 41.9*36 / (41.9+36) | Answer: 19.36 uF

question: A resistor 27 kohm and capacitor 19 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 27, C = 19 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (27k)(19u) = 513 ms | Answer: 513 ms

question: An inductor 354.7 mH is in series with 143 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 354.7, R = 143 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (354.7e-3) / 143 | Answer: 2.48 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 58.4 mH inductor at 160 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 58.4, f = 160 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (160)(58.4e-3) | Answer: 58.71 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 39.6 uF capacitor at 410 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 39.6, f = 410 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (410)(39.6e-6)) | Answer: 9.803 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 79 ohm, XL = 128 ohm and XC = 125 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 79, XL = 128, XC = 125 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(79^2 + (128 - 125)^2) | Answer: 79.06 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 22.9 mH and C = 2.1 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 22.9, C = 2.1 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(22.9e-3 * 2.1e-6)) | Answer: 725.8 Hz

question: A capacitor of 32.8 uF is charged to 270 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 32.8, V = 270 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*32.8e-6*(270)^2 | Answer: 1196 mJ

question: An alternating voltage has a peak value of 70 V. Find its RMS value.
solution: Given: Vp = 70 | Formula: Vrms = Vp / sqrt(2) | Substitute: Vrms = 70 / sqrt(2) | Answer: 49.5 V

question: A transformer has primary voltage 380 V with 510 primary turns and 130 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 380, N1 = 510, N2 = 130 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 380 * 130/510 | Answer: 96.86 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 110 V and draws an armature current of 50 A. If the armature resistance is 1.27 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 110, Ia = 50, Ra = 1.27 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 110 - 50*1.27 | Answer: 46.5 V

question: A 8-pole induction motor on a 60 Hz supply runs at 730 rpm. Find the slip (%).
formula: s = (Ns - N) / Ns,  Ns = 120 f / P

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 125 A at 433 V (line) with a power factor of 0.78. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 125, VL = 433, pf = 0.78 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*433*125*0.78 / 1000 | Answer: 73.12 kW

question: A load has real power 10 kW and apparent power 75 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 10, S = 75 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 10 / 75 | Answer: 0.1333

question: A machine delivers 185 kW output while drawing 187 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 185, Pi = 187 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 185/187 * 100 | Answer: 98.93 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 20 V across R1 = 2 ohm and R2 = 34 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 20, R1 = 2, R2 = 34 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 20*34 / (2+34) | Answer: 18.89 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 20 kohm and Rin = 16 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 20, Rin = 16 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 20 / 16 | Answer: 1.25

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 80 kohm and Rg = 46 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 80, Rg = 46 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 80/46 | Answer: 2.739

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 2792. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 2792 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(2792) | Answer: 34.46 dB

question: A first-order system has a time constant of 2.6 s. Find the time (in s) to reach 63.2% of its final value.
solution: For a first-order step response, y = 1 - e^(-t/tau) | y = 0.632 when t = tau | Answer: 2.6 s
formula: At t = tau the response reaches 63.2% (one time constant)

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.9 m carries a central point load of 40 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 9.9, W = 40 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 40*9.9 / 4 | Answer: 99 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.3 m carries a UDL of 35 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6.3, w = 35 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 35*(6.3)^2 / 8 | Answer: 173.6 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 3.5 m carries a point load 5 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.5, W = 5 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 5*3.5 | Answer: 17.5 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 4.5 m carries a UDL of 38 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.5, w = 38 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 38*(4.5)^2 / 2 | Answer: 384.8 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 8.3 m carries a point load 100 kN at distance 3.5 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 8.3, a = 3.5, W = 100 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 100*(8.3 - 3.5) / 8.3 | Answer: 57.83 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 7 m) carries a central point load 20 kN. With E = 25 GPa and I = 510e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=20000 N, L=7000.0 mm, E=25000 MPa, I=510e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 11.21 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 8.6 m carries a UDL of 30 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 8.6, w = 30 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 30*(8.6)^2 / 12 | Answer: 184.9 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 590 mm, clear cover 25 mm and main bars of diameter 16 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 590, c = 25, dia = 16 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 590 - 25 - 16/2 | Answer: 557 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 35.7 m^2 carrying a factored load of 11.3 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 35.7, w = 11.3 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 11.3 * 35.7 | Answer: 403.4 kN

question: For a bar of diameter 25 mm with design bond stress 1.7 MPa and steel stress 360 MPa, find the development length in mm.
solution: Given: dia = 25, tbd = 1.7, fs = 360 | Formula: Ld = phi fs / (4 tau_bd) | Substitute: Ld = 25*360 / (4*1.7) | Answer: 1324 mm

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 3.7 m, unit weight 17 kN/m^3, phi = 28 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 10.9 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 21 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 10.9, g = 21 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (21 - 9.81)*10.9 | Answer: 122 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 4.1e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.4, area = 4.6e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 4.1, i = 0.4, A = 4.6 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (4.1e-4)*0.4*(4.6e-3) | Answer: 754.4 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.1 m, bed slope 0.008 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.018. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 2.1 m under a head of 1.2 m. Taking Cd = 0.62 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 3 m wide carries a discharge of 20 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 470 m and design speed 75 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 470, V = 75 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (75)^2 / (127*470) | Answer: 0.09424
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: For a design speed of 80 km/h with allowable superelevation 0.07 and lateral friction 0.12, find the minimum curve radius in m.
A tank of volume 170 m^3 treats a flow of 20 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 170, Q = 20 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 170 / 20 | Answer: 8.5 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 320 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.25 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 4 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 320, k = 0.25, t = 4 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 320*(1 - e^(-0.25*4)) | Answer: 202.3 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.81, rainfall intensity 75 mm/h over a catchment of 45.6 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.81, i = 75, A = 45.6 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.81*75*45.6 / 360 | Answer: 7.695 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.06 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 230 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.06, M = 230 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 230*(20+0.06)/20 | Answer: 230.7 m

question: Convert the decimal number 103 to binary.
solution: Divide 103 by 2 repeatedly, recording remainders | Reading remainders in reverse gives 1100111 | Answer: 1100111 (binary)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 2 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the decimal number 1118 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 1118 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 45E (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the 8-bit binary number 00101101 to decimal.
solution: Binary 00101101 = sum of bit-weights | Answer: 45 (decimal)
formula: Sum each bit times its positional weight (2^i)

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 00101001 and 01100101.
solution: XOR: 01001100 | Count of 1s = 3 | Answer: 3
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 800 megabits is sent over a link of 48 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 800, B = 48 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 800 / 48 | Answer: 16.67 s

question: A link has bandwidth 64 Mbps and round-trip time 170 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 64, R = 170 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 64e6 * 170e-3 bits = 10880 kb | Answer: 10880 kilobits

question: A channel has bandwidth 12 kHz. Using Nyquist's theorem with 16 signal levels, find the maximum data rate in kbps (noiseless).
solution: Given: B = 12, M = 16 | Formula: C = 2 B log2(M) | Substitute: C = 2*12*log2(16) | Answer: 96 kbps

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.82, cache access time 9 ns and main-memory access time 170 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.82, tc = 9, tm = 170 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.82*9 + (1 - 0.82)*170 | Answer: 37.98 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 750255 elements?
solution: Given: n = 750255 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(750255)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: An O(n^2) algorithm performs c*n^2 basic operations. If c = 1 and n = 1380, how many operations are performed?
solution: Given: n = 1380 | Formula: operations = n^2 | Substitute: = (1380)^2 | Answer: 1904400

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.015, memory access time 110 ns and page-fault service time 7 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 7 ms = 7000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.015)*110 + 0.015*7000000.0 ns | Answer: 105.1 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 0.1 m^3 at 120 kPa and 400 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 0.1, P = 120, Tk = 400 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (120e3)*0.1 / (8.314*400) | Answer: 3.608 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.23 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 7 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.23, t = 7 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.23*7) | Answer: 0.8001

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.17 /min) is to reach 90% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.17, X = 90 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.9) / 0.17 | Answer: 13.54 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.49 /min) reaches 75% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.49, X = 75 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.75 / (0.49*(1 - 0.75)) | Answer: 6.122 min

question: For a reaction with A = 5e10 /s and activation energy 65 kJ/mol at 490 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 5, Ea = 65, Tk = 490 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 5e10 * exp(-65e3 / (8.314*490)) | Answer: 5883 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.93 and bottoms xW = 0.03, with relative volatility alpha = 3.5. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.93, xw = 0.03, al = 3.5 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.93/0.07)(0.97/0.03)] / ln(3.5) | Answer: 4.84 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.81 and x = 0.23. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.81, x = 0.23 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.81/0.19) / (0.23/0.77) | Answer: 14.27

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.88 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 25 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.88, Psat = 25 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.88 * 25 | Answer: 22 kPa

question: A stream of 6.1 kg/s with specific heat 4.1 kJ/kg-K is heated through 20 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 6.1, cp = 4.1, dT = 20 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 6.1*4.1*20 | Answer: 500.2 kW

question: A reactor of volume 8.3 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 2.1 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 8.3, Q = 2.1 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 8.3 / 2.1 | Answer: 3.952 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 3.6e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 2 mm with a concentration difference of 30 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 3.6, L = 2, dC = 30 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (3.6e-9)*30 / (2e-3) | Answer: 54 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 6.6 min and steady-state gain 0.6. For a step input of magnitude 10, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 6.6, K = 0.6, M = 10 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 0.6 * 10 | Answer: 6 units

question: A reactor operates at a space time of 9 min. Find its space velocity in per hour.
solution: Given: tau = 9 | Formula: SV = 60 / tau  (per hour) | Substitute: SV = 60 / 9 | Answer: 6.667 /h

question: An aircraft wing of area 65 m^2 flies at 240 m/s (air density 0.4 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.5. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 65, V = 240, rho = 0.4, CL = 0.5 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.4*(240)^2*65*0.5 / 1000 | Answer: 374.4 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 70 m^2 flies at 190 m/s (density 1.225 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.11. Find the drag force in kN.
An aircraft flies at 470 m/s where the speed of sound is 295 m/s. Find the Mach number.
solution: Given: V = 470, a = 295 | Formula: M = V / a | Substitute: M = 470 / 295 | Answer: 1.593

question: A specimen under stress 200 MPa shows an elastic strain of 0.9e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 200, eps = 0.9 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 200 / (0.9e-3) MPa = 222.2 GPa | Answer: 222.2 GPa

question: A block of mass 29 kg has a volume of 6e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 29, V = 6 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 29 / (6e-3) | Answer: 4833 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 1100 mm is heated through 45 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 11e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 1100, dT = 45, al = 11 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 1100*11e-6*45 | Answer: 0.5445 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 60 ohm, R2 = 35 ohm and R3 = 245 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 60, R2 = 35, R3 = 245 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 35*245 / 60 | Answer: 142.9 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 1000 ohm and gauge factor 2 experiences a strain of 450e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 1000, GF = 2, eps = 450 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 1000*2*450e-6 | Answer: 900 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 10.83 when the true value is 50. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10.83, true = 50 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10.83 - 50| / 50 * 100 | Answer: 78.34 %

question: Annual demand is 43000 units, ordering cost 260 per order and holding cost 35 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 43000, S = 260, H = 35 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*43000*260 / 35) | Answer: 799.3 units

question: An asset costs 80000 with salvage value 14000 after 19 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 80000, Sv = 14000, n = 19 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (80000 - 14000) / 19 | Answer: 3474 per year

question: A product sells for 400 per unit with variable cost 180 per unit and fixed costs 40000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 400, V = 180, F = 40000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 40000 / (400 - 180) | Answer: 181.8 units

question: Find the present worth of 115000 received 7 years from now at an interest rate of 9% per year.
solution: Given: F = 115000, n = 7, i = 9 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 115000 / (1 + 0.09)^7 | Answer: 62909 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.94, 0.94 and 0.95 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.94, r2 = 0.94, r3 = 0.95 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.94*0.94*0.95 | Answer: 0.8394

question: A process produces 31 defective items in a batch of 1000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 31, N = 1000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 31/1000 * 1e6 | Answer: 31000 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = 5x^3 + 6x^2 - 5x + 5 evaluated at x = 0.
For f(x) = -x^3 - 2x^2 - 9x - 5, find f''(x) at x = -2.
Evaluate the definite integral of (-2x^2 - 2x + 2) dx from x = 1 to x = 4.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = -2x^3/3 + -2x^2/2 + 2x | Evaluate F(4) - F(1) | Answer: -51
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 3x^2 - 11x + 1 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[-5, 0], [2, 1]].
solution: Given: a = -5, b = 0, c = 2, d = 1 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (-5)(1) - (0)(2) | Answer: -5

question: Find the determinant of [[-1, -3, 1], [1, 2, -2], [-6, 2, -4]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: -30

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[0, 5], [6, 8]].
solution: Trace tr = 8, Determinant = -30 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 10.78

question: Solve for x: -6x + 5y = 2 and 2x + 2y = 4.
solution: Determinant = -6*2 - 5*2 = -22 | x = (e d - b f) / det = 0.7273 | Answer: x = 0.7273
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 60, 80, 30, 4, 10.
solution: Sum = 184 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 36.8 | Answer: 36.8

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 7, 13, 9, 29, 37.
solution: Mean = 19 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 13.27

question: Find the slope of the line through (6, 8) and (-3, -5).
solution: Given: x1 = 6, y1 = 8, x2 = -3, y2 = -5 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (-5 - 8) / (-3 - 6) | Answer: 1.444

question: Find the distance between the points (-8, -5) and (5, -7).
solution: Given: x1 = -8, y1 = -5, x2 = 5, y2 = -7 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((13)^2 + (-2)^2) | Answer: 13.15 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (5,5), (8,-8), (0,-3).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 44.5 sq units

question: Evaluate the number of combinations C(17, 15).
solution: Given: n = 17, r = 15 | Formula: C(n, r) = n! / (r! (n - r)!) | Substitute: C(17, 15) = 17! / (15! * 2!) | Answer: 136

question: Find the 14th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -6 and common difference 4.
solution: Given: a = -6, d = 4, n = 14 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -6 + (14 - 1)*4 | Answer: 46

question: Find the sum of the first 14 terms of an AP with first term -14 and common difference 3.
solution: Given: a = -14, d = 3, n = 14 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 14/2 [2*-14 + (14-1)*3] | Answer: 77

question: Find the 3th term of a geometric progression with first term 2 and common ratio 3.
solution: Given: a = 2, r = 3, n = 3 | Formula: a_n = a r^(n-1) | Substitute: a_n = 2 * 3^(3-1) | Answer: 18

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 12000 at 14% per annum for 6 years.
solution: Given: P = 12000, R = 14, Tt = 6 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 12000 * 14 * 6 / 100 | Answer: 10080 currency units

question: Find the amount when 30500 is invested at 9.3% per annum compounded annually for 3 years.
solution: Given: P = 30500, R = 9.3, Tt = 3 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 30500 * (1 + 9.3/100)^3 | Answer: 39825 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (1, 8, -1) and (-5, -8, -3).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (-3, 1, 4) and (2, 5, 4).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 30.74

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (-4, 4, -5) and (-5, -4, 6).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 113.1 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number 7 + 5i.
solution: Given: a = 7, b = 5 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((7)^2 + (5)^2) | Answer: 8.602

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number 3 + -10i.
solution: Given: a = 3, b = -10 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(-10, 3) | Answer: -73.3 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -4x^3 + 3x^2 - 4x - 9 at x = 2.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-116 with initial guess x0=3, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=0.8 and ordinates 15, 9, 19, 17, 10, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 334 and 118.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 334 and 118 | Answer: GCD = 2

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 35 and 22.
solution: Given: a = 35, b = 22 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 35*22 / 1 | Answer: 770
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 27 mm carries an axial tensile load of 43 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 33 mm and length 1800 mm carries an axial load of 39 kN. Take E = 200 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 30 mm transmits a torque of 2100 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 30, Tt = 2100 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(2100*1000) / (pi*(30)^3) | Answer: 396.1 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 25 mm and length 700 mm carries a torque of 1200 N-m. With G = 77 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (25)^4 / 32 = 3835 mm^4 | theta = (1200*1000)(700) / (77000 * 3835) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 16.3 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 42 mm wide and 120 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 42, h = 120 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 42*(120)^2 / 6 | Answer: 100800 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (98 mm x 170 mm) carries a bending moment of 18 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (66 mm x 160 mm) has effective length 2800 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 540 MPa is designed for a working stress of 160 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 540, sw = 160 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 540 / 160 | Answer: 3.375

question: A steel bar is fully restrained and heated through 20 deg C. With E = 210 GPa and alpha = 11e-6 /deg C, find the thermal stress in MPa.
solution: Given: dT = 20, E = 210, al = 11 | Formula: sigma = E alpha (dT) | Substitute: sigma = 210000 * 11e-6 * 20 | Answer: 46.2 MPa

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1300 mm and wall thickness 6 mm carries an internal pressure of 1.8 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1300, t = 6, P = 1.8 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 1.8*1300 / (2*6) | Answer: 195 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 1140 K and 440 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 1140, Tc = 440 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 440/1140) * 100 | Answer: 61.4 %

question: A refrigerator works between 261 K (cold) and 304 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 261, Th = 304 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 261 / (304 - 261) | Answer: 6.07

question: A heat pump operates between 268 K and 328 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 268, Th = 328 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 328 / (328 - 268) | Answer: 5.467

question: 4.4 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 135 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.4, dT = 135 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 4.4 * 0.718 * 135 | Answer: 426.5 kJ

question: 3.5 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 140 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.5, dT = 140 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 3.5 * 1.005 * 140 | Answer: 492.4 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 1.8 m^3 at 400 K with mass 2 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 1.8, Tk = 400, m = 2 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 2*0.287*400 / 1.8 | Answer: 127.6 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 3.1 kg of air expands isothermally at 480 K from volume V1 to 2*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.1, Tk = 480, ratio = 2 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 3.1*0.287*480*ln(2) | Answer: 296 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 4.9 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.23 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 4.9, D = 0.23 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*4.9*0.23 / 0.001 | Answer: 1127000

question: Water flows at 1.4 m/s through a pipe of diameter 150 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 29.6 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 29.6 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*29.6 / 1000 | Answer: 290.4 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 16.3 m. Taking Cv = 0.98, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 16.3, cv = 0.98 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.98*sqrt(2*9.81*16.3) | Answer: 17.53 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 210 mm) water flows at 1.9 m/s. It contracts to diameter 110 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
Water flows at 1.4 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.32 m and length 130 m. With friction factor f = 0.025, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 28 teeth drives a gear of 96 teeth. If the pinion runs at 550 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 28, z2 = 96, N1 = 550 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 550*28 / 96 | Answer: 160.4 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 140 mm rotates at 500 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 140, N = 500 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.14)*500 / 60 | Answer: 3.665 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 8.8 kW at 800 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 8.8, N = 800 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(8.8*1000) / (2*pi*800) | Answer: 105 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 9.3 kg rotates at radius 0.13 m at 400 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 8900 N/m and mass 10.5 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 8900, m = 10.5 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(8900/10.5) | Answer: 4.634 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 5.5 m^2 and thickness 0.22 m has conductivity k = 41.5 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 130 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 5.5, L = 0.22, k = 41.5, dT = 130 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 41.5*5.5*130 / 0.22 | Answer: 134875 W

question: A surface of area 4.6 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 165 W/m^2-K to surroundings 125 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 4.6, h = 165, dT = 125 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 165*4.6*125 | Answer: 94875 W

question: In a counter-flow heat exchanger the terminal temperature differences are 70 deg C and 10 deg C. Find the log mean temperature difference (LMTD) in deg C.
solution: Given: dT1 = 70, dT2 = 10 | Formula: LMTD = (dT1 - dT2) / ln(dT1/dT2) | Substitute: LMTD = (70 - 10) / ln(70/10) | Answer: 30.83 deg C

question: In turning, cutting speed = 90 m/min, feed = 0.34 mm/rev, depth of cut = 0.8 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 90, f = 0.34, d = 0.8 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*90*0.34*0.8 | Answer: 24480 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 100 mm is turned at 500 rpm with a feed of 0.28 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 100, N = 500, f = 0.28 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 100 / (0.28*500) | Answer: 0.7143 min

question: A resistor of 106 ohm carries a current of 3.7 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 106, I = 3.7 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 3.7 * 106 | Answer: 392.2 V

question: Three resistors 6 ohm, 98 ohm and 82 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 6, R2 = 98, R3 = 82 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 6 + 98 + 82 | Answer: 186 ohm

question: Two resistors 89 ohm and 106 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 89, R2 = 106 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 89*106 / (89+106) | Answer: 48.38 ohm

question: A device draws 1.1 A at 200 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 200, I = 1.1 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 200 * 1.1 | Answer: 220 W

question: A current of 2.2 A flows through a 33 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 2.2, R = 33 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (2.2)^2 * 33 | Answer: 159.7 W

question: Two capacitors 9.2 uF and 29.4 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 9.2, C2 = 29.4 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 9.2*29.4 / (9.2+29.4) | Answer: 7.007 uF

question: A resistor 38 kohm and capacitor 0.3 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 38, C = 0.3 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (38k)(0.3u) = 11.4 ms | Answer: 11.4 ms

question: An inductor 445.7 mH is in series with 156 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 445.7, R = 156 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (445.7e-3) / 156 | Answer: 2.857 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 179.8 mH inductor at 180 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 179.8, f = 180 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (180)(179.8e-3) | Answer: 203.3 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 31.7 uF capacitor at 130 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 31.7, f = 130 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (130)(31.7e-6)) | Answer: 38.62 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 19 ohm, XL = 39 ohm and XC = 109 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 19, XL = 39, XC = 109 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(19^2 + (39 - 109)^2) | Answer: 72.53 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 29.2 mH and C = 4.7 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 29.2, C = 4.7 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(29.2e-3 * 4.7e-6)) | Answer: 429.6 Hz

question: A capacitor of 18.6 uF is charged to 375 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 18.6, V = 375 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*18.6e-6*(375)^2 | Answer: 1308 mJ

question: An alternating voltage has a peak value of 276 V. Find its RMS value.
solution: Given: Vp = 276 | Formula: Vrms = Vp / sqrt(2) | Substitute: Vrms = 276 / sqrt(2) | Answer: 195.2 V

question: A transformer has primary voltage 210 V with 900 primary turns and 500 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 210, N1 = 900, N2 = 500 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 210 * 500/900 | Answer: 116.7 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 430 V and draws an armature current of 21 A. If the armature resistance is 0.83 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 430, Ia = 21, Ra = 0.83 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 430 - 21*0.83 | Answer: 412.6 V

question: A 4-pole induction motor on a 50 Hz supply runs at 1040 rpm. Find the slip (%).
formula: s = (Ns - N) / Ns,  Ns = 120 f / P

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 120 A at 433 V (line) with a power factor of 0.73. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 120, VL = 433, pf = 0.73 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*433*120*0.73 / 1000 | Answer: 65.7 kW

question: A load has real power 80 kW and apparent power 180 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 80, S = 180 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 80 / 180 | Answer: 0.4444

question: A machine delivers 10 kW output while drawing 112 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 10, Pi = 112 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 10/112 * 100 | Answer: 8.929 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 8 V across R1 = 3 ohm and R2 = 34 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 8, R1 = 3, R2 = 34 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 8*34 / (3+34) | Answer: 7.351 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 210 kohm and Rin = 33 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 210, Rin = 33 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 210 / 33 | Answer: 6.364

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 40 kohm and Rg = 23 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 40, Rg = 23 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 40/23 | Answer: 2.739

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 1466. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 1466 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(1466) | Answer: 31.66 dB

question: A first-order system has a time constant of 4.6 s. Find the time (in s) to reach 63.2% of its final value.
solution: For a first-order step response, y = 1 - e^(-t/tau) | y = 0.632 when t = tau | Answer: 4.6 s
formula: At t = tau the response reaches 63.2% (one time constant)

question: A simply supported beam of span 5.1 m carries a central point load of 65 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.1, W = 65 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 65*5.1 / 4 | Answer: 82.88 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 7.9 m carries a UDL of 30 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7.9, w = 30 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 30*(7.9)^2 / 8 | Answer: 234 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 4.4 m carries a point load 70 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.4, W = 70 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 70*4.4 | Answer: 308 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 2.4 m carries a UDL of 4 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 2.4, w = 4 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 4*(2.4)^2 / 2 | Answer: 11.52 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 5.7 m carries a point load 75 kN at distance 1.4 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 5.7, a = 1.4, W = 75 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 75*(5.7 - 1.4) / 5.7 | Answer: 56.58 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 3.1 m) carries a central point load 50 kN. With E = 30 GPa and I = 570e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=50000 N, L=3100.0 mm, E=30000 MPa, I=570e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 1.815 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 5.8 m carries a UDL of 9 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.8, w = 9 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 9*(5.8)^2 / 12 | Answer: 25.23 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 350 mm, clear cover 40 mm and main bars of diameter 12 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 350, c = 40, dia = 12 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 350 - 40 - 12/2 | Answer: 304 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 34.3 m^2 carrying a factored load of 18.6 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 34.3, w = 18.6 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 18.6 * 34.3 | Answer: 638 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 4.2 m, unit weight 16 kN/m^3, phi = 35 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 7.9 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 19 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 7.9, g = 19 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (19 - 9.81)*7.9 | Answer: 72.6 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 1.8e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1.5, area = 5.7e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 1.8, i = 1.5, A = 5.7 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (1.8e-4)*1.5*(5.7e-3) | Answer: 1539 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 0.9 m, bed slope 0.004 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.025. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 2.3 m under a head of 0.3 m. Taking Cd = 0.61 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 5.4 m wide carries a discharge of 5.2 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 510 m and design speed 40 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 510, V = 40 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (40)^2 / (127*510) | Answer: 0.0247
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: For a design speed of 80 km/h with allowable superelevation 0.05 and lateral friction 0.14, find the minimum curve radius in m.
A tank of volume 610 m^3 treats a flow of 175 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 610, Q = 175 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 610 / 175 | Answer: 3.486 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 330 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.24 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 5 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 330, k = 0.24, t = 5 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 330*(1 - e^(-0.24*5)) | Answer: 230.6 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.74, rainfall intensity 120 mm/h over a catchment of 21.3 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.74, i = 120, A = 21.3 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.74*120*21.3 / 360 | Answer: 5.254 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.03 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 380 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.03, M = 380 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 380*(30+0.03)/30 | Answer: 380.4 m

question: Convert the decimal number 231 to binary.
solution: Divide 231 by 2 repeatedly, recording remainders | Reading remainders in reverse gives 11100111 | Answer: 11100111 (binary)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 2 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the decimal number 2899 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 2899 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: B53 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the 8-bit binary number 00011111 to decimal.
solution: Binary 00011111 = sum of bit-weights | Answer: 31 (decimal)
formula: Sum each bit times its positional weight (2^i)

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 11001110 and 01111111.
solution: XOR: 10110001 | Count of 1s = 4 | Answer: 4
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 1000 megabits is sent over a link of 61 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 1000, B = 61 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 1000 / 61 | Answer: 16.39 s

question: A link has bandwidth 12 Mbps and round-trip time 170 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 12, R = 170 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 12e6 * 170e-3 bits = 2040 kb | Answer: 2040 kilobits

question: A channel of bandwidth 8 kHz has a signal-to-noise ratio of 15 (linear). Using Shannon's theorem, find the channel capacity in kbps.
solution: Given: B = 8, SNR = 15 | Formula: C = B log2(1 + SNR) | Substitute: C = 8*log2(1 + 15) | Answer: 32 kbps

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.87, cache access time 2 ns and main-memory access time 100 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.87, tc = 2, tm = 100 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.87*2 + (1 - 0.87)*100 | Answer: 14.74 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 800952 elements?
solution: Given: n = 800952 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(800952)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: An O(n^2) algorithm performs c*n^2 basic operations. If c = 1 and n = 2600, how many operations are performed?
solution: Given: n = 2600 | Formula: operations = n^2 | Substitute: = (2600)^2 | Answer: 6760000

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.006, memory access time 200 ns and page-fault service time 7 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 7 ms = 7000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.006)*200 + 0.006*7000000.0 ns | Answer: 42.2 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 2.5 m^3 at 270 kPa and 490 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 2.5, P = 270, Tk = 490 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (270e3)*2.5 / (8.314*490) | Answer: 165.7 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.36 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 16 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.36, t = 16 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.36*16) | Answer: 0.9968

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.43 /min) is to reach 75% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.43, X = 75 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.75) / 0.43 | Answer: 3.224 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.16 /min) reaches 60% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.16, X = 60 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.6 / (0.16*(1 - 0.6)) | Answer: 9.375 min

question: For a reaction with A = 7e10 /s and activation energy 90 kJ/mol at 460 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 7, Ea = 90, Tk = 460 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 7e10 * exp(-90e3 / (8.314*460)) | Answer: 4.216 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.98 and bottoms xW = 0.09, with relative volatility alpha = 2.5. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.98, xw = 0.09, al = 2.5 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.98/0.02)(0.91/0.09)] / ln(2.5) | Answer: 6.772 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.9 and x = 0.31. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.9, x = 0.31 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.9/0.1) / (0.31/0.69) | Answer: 20.03

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.17 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 25 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.17, Psat = 25 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.17 * 25 | Answer: 4.25 kPa

question: A stream of 8.7 kg/s with specific heat 1.5 kJ/kg-K is heated through 65 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 8.7, cp = 1.5, dT = 65 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 8.7*1.5*65 | Answer: 848.2 kW

question: A reactor of volume 15.9 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 0.2 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 15.9, Q = 0.2 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 15.9 / 0.2 | Answer: 79.5 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 7.5e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 4 mm with a concentration difference of 100 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 7.5, L = 4, dC = 100 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (7.5e-9)*100 / (4e-3) | Answer: 187.5 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 3.2 min and steady-state gain 1.6. For a step input of magnitude 14, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 3.2, K = 1.6, M = 14 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 1.6 * 14 | Answer: 22.4 units

question: A reactor operates at a space time of 6.3 min. Find its space velocity in per hour.
solution: Given: tau = 6.3 | Formula: SV = 60 / tau  (per hour) | Substitute: SV = 60 / 6.3 | Answer: 9.524 /h

question: An aircraft wing of area 110 m^2 flies at 170 m/s (air density 1 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.6. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 110, V = 170, rho = 1, CL = 0.6 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1*(170)^2*110*0.6 / 1000 | Answer: 953.7 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 40 m^2 flies at 130 m/s (density 0.7 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.08. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 40, V = 130, rho = 0.7, CD = 0.08 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.7*(130)^2*40*0.08 / 1000 | Answer: 18.93 kN

question: An aircraft flies at 200 m/s where the speed of sound is 340 m/s. Find the Mach number.
solution: Given: V = 200, a = 340 | Formula: M = V / a | Substitute: M = 200 / 340 | Answer: 0.5882

question: A specimen under stress 220 MPa shows an elastic strain of 1.6e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 220, eps = 1.6 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 220 / (1.6e-3) MPa = 137.5 GPa | Answer: 137.5 GPa

question: A block of mass 16 kg has a volume of 3.2e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 16, V = 3.2 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 16 / (3.2e-3) | Answer: 5000 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 800 mm is heated through 50 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 12e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 800, dT = 50, al = 12 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 800*12e-6*50 | Answer: 0.48 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 30 ohm, R2 = 40 ohm and R3 = 80 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 30, R2 = 40, R3 = 80 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 40*80 / 30 | Answer: 106.7 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 350 ohm and gauge factor 2.1 experiences a strain of 700e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 350, GF = 2.1, eps = 700 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 350*2.1*700e-6 | Answer: 514.5 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 10.96 when the true value is 100. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10.96, true = 100 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10.96 - 100| / 100 * 100 | Answer: 89.04 %

question: Annual demand is 22000 units, ordering cost 290 per order and holding cost 33 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 22000, S = 290, H = 33 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*22000*290 / 33) | Answer: 621.8 units

question: An asset costs 150000 with salvage value 38000 after 7 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 150000, Sv = 38000, n = 7 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (150000 - 38000) / 7 | Answer: 16000 per year

question: A product sells for 340 per unit with variable cost 90 per unit and fixed costs 45000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 340, V = 90, F = 45000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 45000 / (340 - 90) | Answer: 180 units

question: Find the present worth of 175000 received 8 years from now at an interest rate of 6% per year.
solution: Given: F = 175000, n = 8, i = 6 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 175000 / (1 + 0.06)^8 | Answer: 109797 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.94, 0.91 and 0.94 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.94, r2 = 0.91, r3 = 0.94 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.94*0.91*0.94 | Answer: 0.8041

question: A process produces 43 defective items in a batch of 4000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 43, N = 4000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 43/4000 * 1e6 | Answer: 10750 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = 2x^3 + 8x^2 - 4x - 5 evaluated at x = 0.
For f(x) = -2x^3 + 4x^2 + x + 3, find f''(x) at x = 2.

question: Find the larger real root of 3x^2 + 4x - 11 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[-4, 1], [7, 0]].
solution: Given: a = -4, b = 1, c = 7, d = 0 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (-4)(0) - (1)(7) | Answer: -7

question: Find the determinant of [[4, -5, 1], [1, 4, -4], [-2, 4, 1]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: 57

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[3, 3], [3, 8]].
solution: Trace tr = 11, Determinant = 15 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 9.405

question: Solve for x: 3x + -6y = 0 and -4x + 6y = -9.

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 52, 68, 88, 67, 11.
solution: Sum = 286 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 57.2 | Answer: 57.2

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 17, 40, 25, 29, 6.
solution: Mean = 23.4 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 12.78

question: Find the slope of the line through (-7, 9) and (8, -5).
solution: Given: x1 = -7, y1 = 9, x2 = 8, y2 = -5 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (-5 - 9) / (8 - -7) | Answer: -0.9333

question: Find the distance between the points (4, 4) and (9, -7).
solution: Given: x1 = 4, y1 = 4, x2 = 9, y2 = -7 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((5)^2 + (-11)^2) | Answer: 12.08 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (-8,-1), (3,4), (-8,8).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 49.5 sq units

question: Evaluate the number of combinations C(14, 7).
solution: Given: n = 14, r = 7 | Formula: C(n, r) = n! / (r! (n - r)!) | Substitute: C(14, 7) = 14! / (7! * 7!) | Answer: 3432

question: Find the 40th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 8 and common difference 7.
solution: Given: a = 8, d = 7, n = 40 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = 8 + (40 - 1)*7 | Answer: 281

question: Find the sum of the first 29 terms of an AP with first term 0 and common difference 6.
solution: Given: a = 0, d = 6, n = 29 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 29/2 [2*0 + (29-1)*6] | Answer: 2436

question: Find the 5th term of a geometric progression with first term 7 and common ratio 4.
solution: Given: a = 7, r = 4, n = 5 | Formula: a_n = a r^(n-1) | Substitute: a_n = 7 * 4^(5-1) | Answer: 1792

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 36500 at 7.4% per annum for 8 years.
solution: Given: P = 36500, R = 7.4, Tt = 8 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 36500 * 7.4 * 8 / 100 | Answer: 21608 currency units

question: Find the amount when 28500 is invested at 6.9% per annum compounded annually for 6 years.
solution: Given: P = 28500, R = 6.9, Tt = 6 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 28500 * (1 + 6.9/100)^6 | Answer: 42532 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (2, 1, -4) and (0, 5, -4).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 8.307

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (5, -3, 6) and (2, -2, -2).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 82.07 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number 12 + -9i.
solution: Given: a = 12, b = -9 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((12)^2 + (-9)^2) | Answer: 15

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number 2 + 3i.
solution: Given: a = 2, b = 3 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(3, 2) | Answer: 56.31 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -3x^3 + 4x^2 - 6x + 5 at x = 1.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-181 with initial guess x0=10, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.6 and ordinates 4, 1, 4, 20, 4, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 586 and 428.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 586 and 428 | Answer: GCD = 2

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 31 and 22.
solution: Given: a = 31, b = 22 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 31*22 / 1 | Answer: 682
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 46 mm carries an axial tensile load of 81 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 12 mm and length 1400 mm carries an axial load of 70 kN. Take E = 210 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 63 mm transmits a torque of 1000 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 63, Tt = 1000 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(1000*1000) / (pi*(63)^3) | Answer: 20.37 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 62 mm and length 2000 mm carries a torque of 1450 N-m. With G = 80 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (62)^4 / 32 = 1450663 mm^4 | theta = (1450*1000)(2000) / (80000 * 1450663) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 1.432 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 60 mm wide and 150 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 60, h = 150 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 60*(150)^2 / 6 | Answer: 225000 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (44 mm x 240 mm) carries a bending moment of 25 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (75 mm x 110 mm) has effective length 3900 mm and E = 200 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 550 MPa is designed for a working stress of 60 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 550, sw = 60 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 550 / 60 | Answer: 9.167

question: A steel bar is fully restrained and heated through 100 deg C. With E = 200 GPa and alpha = 12e-6 /deg C, find the thermal stress in MPa.
solution: Given: dT = 100, E = 200, al = 12 | Formula: sigma = E alpha (dT) | Substitute: sigma = 200000 * 12e-6 * 100 | Answer: 240 MPa

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 900 mm and wall thickness 18 mm carries an internal pressure of 1.8 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 900, t = 18, P = 1.8 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 1.8*900 / (2*18) | Answer: 45 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 960 K and 330 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 960, Tc = 330 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 330/960) * 100 | Answer: 65.62 %

question: A refrigerator works between 259 K (cold) and 304 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 259, Th = 304 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 259 / (304 - 259) | Answer: 5.756

question: A heat pump operates between 284 K and 304 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 284, Th = 304 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 304 / (304 - 284) | Answer: 15.2

question: 5.5 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 180 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 5.5, dT = 180 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 5.5 * 0.718 * 180 | Answer: 710.8 kJ

question: 3.2 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 25 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.2, dT = 25 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 3.2 * 1.005 * 25 | Answer: 80.4 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 2.7 m^3 at 490 K with mass 5.8 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 2.7, Tk = 490, m = 5.8 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 5.8*0.287*490 / 2.7 | Answer: 302.1 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 4.5 kg of air expands isothermally at 340 K from volume V1 to 5*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.5, Tk = 340, ratio = 5 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 4.5*0.287*340*ln(5) | Answer: 706.7 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 2.4 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.1 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 2.4, D = 0.1 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*2.4*0.1 / 0.001 | Answer: 240000

question: Water flows at 3.6 m/s through a pipe of diameter 110 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 23.2 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 23.2 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*23.2 / 1000 | Answer: 227.6 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 14.3 m. Taking Cv = 0.95, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 14.3, cv = 0.95 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.95*sqrt(2*9.81*14.3) | Answer: 15.91 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 200 mm) water flows at 1.8 m/s. It contracts to diameter 70 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 200, d2 = 70, V1 = 1.8 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 1.8*(200/70)^2 | Answer: 14.69 m/s

question: Water flows at 3.7 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.11 m and length 220 m. With friction factor f = 0.028, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 32 teeth drives a gear of 97 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1400 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 32, z2 = 97, N1 = 1400 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1400*32 / 97 | Answer: 461.9 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 310 mm rotates at 900 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 310, N = 900 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.31)*900 / 60 | Answer: 14.61 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 44.8 kW at 300 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 44.8, N = 300 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(44.8*1000) / (2*pi*300) | Answer: 1426 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 5.2 kg rotates at radius 0.56 m at 650 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 17000 N/m and mass 18.3 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.

question: A plane wall of area 1.5 m^2 and thickness 0.17 m has conductivity k = 49.8 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 95 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 1.5, L = 0.17, k = 49.8, dT = 95 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 49.8*1.5*95 / 0.17 | Answer: 41744 W

question: A surface of area 2.7 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 160 W/m^2-K to surroundings 150 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 2.7, h = 160, dT = 150 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 160*2.7*150 | Answer: 64800 W

question: In a counter-flow heat exchanger the terminal temperature differences are 95 deg C and 30 deg C. Find the log mean temperature difference (LMTD) in deg C.
solution: Given: dT1 = 95, dT2 = 30 | Formula: LMTD = (dT1 - dT2) / ln(dT1/dT2) | Substitute: LMTD = (95 - 30) / ln(95/30) | Answer: 56.39 deg C

question: In turning, cutting speed = 190 m/min, feed = 0.41 mm/rev, depth of cut = 1.7 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 190, f = 0.41, d = 1.7 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*190*0.41*1.7 | Answer: 132430 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 130 mm is turned at 400 rpm with a feed of 0.25 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 130, N = 400, f = 0.25 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 130 / (0.25*400) | Answer: 1.3 min

question: A resistor of 175 ohm carries a current of 3.3 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 175, I = 3.3 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 3.3 * 175 | Answer: 577.5 V

question: Three resistors 71 ohm, 90 ohm and 73 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 71, R2 = 90, R3 = 73 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 71 + 90 + 73 | Answer: 234 ohm

question: Two resistors 10 ohm and 31 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 10, R2 = 31 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 10*31 / (10+31) | Answer: 7.561 ohm

question: A device draws 14.2 A at 10 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 10, I = 14.2 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 10 * 14.2 | Answer: 142 W

question: A current of 10.8 A flows through a 100 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 10.8, R = 100 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (10.8)^2 * 100 | Answer: 11664 W

question: Two capacitors 3 uF and 30.3 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 3, C2 = 30.3 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 3*30.3 / (3+30.3) | Answer: 2.73 uF

question: A resistor 89 kohm and capacitor 1.3 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 89, C = 1.3 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (89k)(1.3u) = 115.7 ms | Answer: 115.7 ms

question: An inductor 85.7 mH is in series with 101 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 85.7, R = 101 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (85.7e-3) / 101 | Answer: 0.8485 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 193.4 mH inductor at 820 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 193.4, f = 820 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (820)(193.4e-3) | Answer: 996.4 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 5.8 uF capacitor at 230 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 5.8, f = 230 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (230)(5.8e-6)) | Answer: 119.3 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 57 ohm, XL = 27 ohm and XC = 31 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 57, XL = 27, XC = 31 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(57^2 + (27 - 31)^2) | Answer: 57.14 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 93.8 mH and C = 6 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 93.8, C = 6 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(93.8e-3 * 6e-6)) | Answer: 212.2 Hz

question: A capacitor of 10.6 uF is charged to 310 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 10.6, V = 310 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*10.6e-6*(310)^2 | Answer: 509.3 mJ

question: An alternating voltage has a peak value of 158 V. Find its RMS value.
solution: Given: Vp = 158 | Formula: Vrms = Vp / sqrt(2) | Substitute: Vrms = 158 / sqrt(2) | Answer: 111.7 V

question: A transformer has primary voltage 250 V with 720 primary turns and 250 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 250, N1 = 720, N2 = 250 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 250 * 250/720 | Answer: 86.81 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 380 V and draws an armature current of 32 A. If the armature resistance is 1.09 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 380, Ia = 32, Ra = 1.09 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 380 - 32*1.09 | Answer: 345.1 V

question: A 6-pole induction motor on a 60 Hz supply runs at 1140 rpm. Find the slip (%).
formula: s = (Ns - N) / Ns,  Ns = 120 f / P

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 115 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.86. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 115, VL = 400, pf = 0.86 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*400*115*0.86 / 1000 | Answer: 68.52 kW

question: A load has real power 135 kW and apparent power 200 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 135, S = 200 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 135 / 200 | Answer: 0.675

question: A machine delivers 165 kW output while drawing 187 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 165, Pi = 187 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 165/187 * 100 | Answer: 88.24 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 6 V across R1 = 21 ohm and R2 = 25 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 6, R1 = 21, R2 = 25 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 6*25 / (21+25) | Answer: 3.261 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 90 kohm and Rin = 2 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 90, Rin = 2 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 90 / 2 | Answer: 45

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 10 kohm and Rg = 36 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 10, Rg = 36 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 10/36 | Answer: 1.278

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 668. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 668 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(668) | Answer: 28.25 dB

question: A signal is sampled at 80 kHz. According to the Nyquist criterion, what is the maximum signal frequency that can be represented (in kHz)?
solution: Given: fs = 80 | Formula: f_max = fs / 2 | Substitute: f_max = 80 / 2 | Answer: 40 kHz

question: A simply supported beam of span 3.7 m carries a central point load of 85 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.

question: A simply supported beam of span 3.9 m carries a UDL of 10 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.9, w = 10 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 10*(3.9)^2 / 8 | Answer: 19.01 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 5.8 m carries a point load 15 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.8, W = 15 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 15*5.8 | Answer: 87 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 1 m carries a UDL of 26 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 1, w = 26 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 26*(1)^2 / 2 | Answer: 13 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 6 m carries a point load 40 kN at distance 1.2 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 6, a = 1.2, W = 40 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 40*(6 - 1.2) / 6 | Answer: 32 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 3.1 m) carries a central point load 30 kN. With E = 25 GPa and I = 450e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=30000 N, L=3100.0 mm, E=25000 MPa, I=450e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 1.655 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 6.3 m carries a UDL of 21 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6.3, w = 21 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 21*(6.3)^2 / 12 | Answer: 69.46 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 560 mm, clear cover 40 mm and main bars of diameter 16 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 560, c = 40, dia = 16 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 560 - 40 - 16/2 | Answer: 512 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 26.4 m^2 carrying a factored load of 19.4 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 26.4, w = 19.4 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 19.4 * 26.4 | Answer: 512.2 kN

question: For a bar of diameter 25 mm with design bond stress 1.2 MPa and steel stress 435 MPa, find the development length in mm.
solution: Given: dia = 25, tbd = 1.2, fs = 435 | Formula: Ld = phi fs / (4 tau_bd) | Substitute: Ld = 25*435 / (4*1.2) | Answer: 2266 mm

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 6.2 m, unit weight 17 kN/m^3, phi = 28 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).

question: At a depth of 11.3 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 20 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 11.3, g = 20 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (20 - 9.81)*11.3 | Answer: 115.1 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 7.8e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1.3, area = 7.8e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 7.8, i = 1.3, A = 7.8 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (7.8e-4)*1.3*(7.8e-3) | Answer: 7909 mm^3/s

Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 3.6 m under a head of 1 m. Taking Cd = 0.62 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.

question: A rectangular channel 2.8 m wide carries a discharge of 23.5 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).

question: For a design speed of 70 km/h with allowable superelevation 0.06 and lateral friction 0.16, find the minimum curve radius in m.
A tank of volume 790 m^3 treats a flow of 120 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 270 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.25 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 5 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 270, k = 0.25, t = 5 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 270*(1 - e^(-0.25*5)) | Answer: 192.6 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.89, rainfall intensity 85 mm/h over a catchment of 35 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.89, i = 85, A = 35 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.89*85*35 / 360 | Answer: 7.355 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.03 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 700 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.03, M = 700 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 700*(20+0.03)/20 | Answer: 701 m

question: Convert the decimal number 124 to binary.
solution: Divide 124 by 2 repeatedly, recording remainders | Reading remainders in reverse gives 1111100 | Answer: 1111100 (binary)

question: Convert the decimal number 3456 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 3456 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: D80 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the 8-bit binary number 10000100 to decimal.
solution: Binary 10000100 = sum of bit-weights | Answer: 132 (decimal)
