solution: Given: m = 4.9, Tk = 400, ratio = 4 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 4.9*0.287*400*ln(4) | Answer: 779.8 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 3.1 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.32 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 3.1, D = 0.32 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*3.1*0.32 / 0.001 | Answer: 992000

question: Water flows at 0.9 m/s through a pipe of diameter 90 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 3.2 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 3.2 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*3.2 / 1000 | Answer: 31.39 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 3.3 m. Taking Cv = 0.97, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 3.3, cv = 0.97 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.97*sqrt(2*9.81*3.3) | Answer: 7.805 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 270 mm) water flows at 1.5 m/s. It contracts to diameter 90 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 270, d2 = 90, V1 = 1.5 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 1.5*(270/90)^2 | Answer: 13.5 m/s

question: Water flows at 3 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.34 m and length 230 m. With friction factor f = 0.032, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 24 teeth drives a gear of 57 teeth. If the pinion runs at 400 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 24, z2 = 57, N1 = 400 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 400*24 / 57 | Answer: 168.4 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 500 mm rotates at 250 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 500, N = 250 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.5)*250 / 60 | Answer: 6.545 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 20 kW at 1500 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 20, N = 1500 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(20*1000) / (2*pi*1500) | Answer: 127.3 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 6.9 kg rotates at radius 0.18 m at 250 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 800 N/m and mass 3.7 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 800, m = 3.7 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(800/3.7) | Answer: 2.34 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 9 m^2 and thickness 0.16 m has conductivity k = 9.4 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 45 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 9, L = 0.16, k = 9.4, dT = 45 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 9.4*9*45 / 0.16 | Answer: 23794 W

question: A surface of area 2.9 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 10 W/m^2-K to surroundings 50 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 2.9, h = 10, dT = 50 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 10*2.9*50 | Answer: 1450 W

question: In a counter-flow heat exchanger the terminal temperature differences are 75 deg C and 25 deg C. Find the log mean temperature difference (LMTD) in deg C.
solution: Given: dT1 = 75, dT2 = 25 | Formula: LMTD = (dT1 - dT2) / ln(dT1/dT2) | Substitute: LMTD = (75 - 25) / ln(75/25) | Answer: 45.51 deg C

question: In turning, cutting speed = 110 m/min, feed = 0.15 mm/rev, depth of cut = 1.4 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 110, f = 0.15, d = 1.4 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*110*0.15*1.4 | Answer: 23100 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 290 mm is turned at 1200 rpm with a feed of 0.11 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 290, N = 1200, f = 0.11 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 290 / (0.11*1200) | Answer: 2.197 min

question: A resistor of 124 ohm carries a current of 9.2 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 124, I = 9.2 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 9.2 * 124 | Answer: 1141 V

question: Three resistors 60 ohm, 15 ohm and 12 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 60, R2 = 15, R3 = 12 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 60 + 15 + 12 | Answer: 87 ohm

question: Two resistors 99 ohm and 85 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 99, R2 = 85 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 99*85 / (99+85) | Answer: 45.73 ohm

question: A device draws 11.5 A at 125 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 125, I = 11.5 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 125 * 11.5 | Answer: 1438 W

question: A current of 11.9 A flows through a 57 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 11.9, R = 57 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (11.9)^2 * 57 | Answer: 8072 W

question: Two capacitors 14.3 uF and 27.3 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 14.3, C2 = 27.3 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 14.3*27.3 / (14.3+27.3) | Answer: 9.384 uF

question: A resistor 75 kohm and capacitor 12.9 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 75, C = 12.9 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (75k)(12.9u) = 967.5 ms | Answer: 967.5 ms

question: An inductor 48.2 mH is in series with 9 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 48.2, R = 9 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (48.2e-3) / 9 | Answer: 5.356 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 6.3 mH inductor at 60 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 6.3, f = 60 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (60)(6.3e-3) | Answer: 2.375 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 42.2 uF capacitor at 300 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 42.2, f = 300 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (300)(42.2e-6)) | Answer: 12.57 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 56 ohm, XL = 102 ohm and XC = 73 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 56, XL = 102, XC = 73 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(56^2 + (102 - 73)^2) | Answer: 63.06 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 98.7 mH and C = 8.7 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 98.7, C = 8.7 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(98.7e-3 * 8.7e-6)) | Answer: 171.8 Hz

question: A capacitor of 6.7 uF is charged to 145 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 6.7, V = 145 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*6.7e-6*(145)^2 | Answer: 70.43 mJ

question: An alternating voltage has a peak value of 332 V. Find its RMS value.
solution: Given: Vp = 332 | Formula: Vrms = Vp / sqrt(2) | Substitute: Vrms = 332 / sqrt(2) | Answer: 234.8 V

question: A transformer has primary voltage 410 V with 530 primary turns and 260 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 410, N1 = 530, N2 = 260 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 410 * 260/530 | Answer: 201.1 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 440 V and draws an armature current of 50 A. If the armature resistance is 0.58 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 440, Ia = 50, Ra = 0.58 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 440 - 50*0.58 | Answer: 411 V

question: A 6-pole induction motor on a 50 Hz supply runs at 880 rpm. Find the slip (%).
formula: s = (Ns - N) / Ns,  Ns = 120 f / P

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 155 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.96. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 155, VL = 400, pf = 0.96 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*400*155*0.96 / 1000 | Answer: 103.1 kW

question: A load has real power 30 kW and apparent power 75 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 30, S = 75 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 30 / 75 | Answer: 0.4

question: A machine delivers 45 kW output while drawing 67 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 45, Pi = 67 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 45/67 * 100 | Answer: 67.16 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 26 V across R1 = 34 ohm and R2 = 49 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 26, R1 = 34, R2 = 49 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 26*49 / (34+49) | Answer: 15.35 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 70 kohm and Rin = 23 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 70, Rin = 23 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 70 / 23 | Answer: 3.043

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 170 kohm and Rg = 14 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 170, Rg = 14 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 170/14 | Answer: 13.14

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 566. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 566 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(566) | Answer: 27.53 dB

question: A first-order system has a time constant of 6.2 s. Find the time (in s) to reach 63.2% of its final value.
solution: For a first-order step response, y = 1 - e^(-t/tau) | y = 0.632 when t = tau | Answer: 6.2 s
formula: At t = tau the response reaches 63.2% (one time constant)

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.8 m carries a central point load of 85 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6.8, W = 85 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 85*6.8 / 4 | Answer: 144.5 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.8 m carries a UDL of 50 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 9.8, w = 50 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 50*(9.8)^2 / 8 | Answer: 600.3 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 3.6 m carries a point load 65 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.6, W = 65 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 65*3.6 | Answer: 234 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 2.5 m carries a UDL of 14 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 2.5, w = 14 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 14*(2.5)^2 / 2 | Answer: 43.75 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 7.9 m carries a point load 45 kN at distance 1 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 7.9, a = 1, W = 45 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 45*(7.9 - 1) / 7.9 | Answer: 39.3 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 7.3 m) carries a central point load 80 kN. With E = 30 GPa and I = 170e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=80000 N, L=7300.0 mm, E=30000 MPa, I=170e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 127.1 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 8.8 m carries a UDL of 39 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 8.8, w = 39 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 39*(8.8)^2 / 12 | Answer: 251.7 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 310 mm, clear cover 35 mm and main bars of diameter 25 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 310, c = 35, dia = 25 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 310 - 35 - 25/2 | Answer: 262.5 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 22.2 m^2 carrying a factored load of 17.3 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 22.2, w = 17.3 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 17.3 * 22.2 | Answer: 384.1 kN

question: For a bar of diameter 16 mm with design bond stress 1.3 MPa and steel stress 435 MPa, find the development length in mm.
solution: Given: dia = 16, tbd = 1.3, fs = 435 | Formula: Ld = phi fs / (4 tau_bd) | Substitute: Ld = 16*435 / (4*1.3) | Answer: 1338 mm

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 5.9 m, unit weight 17 kN/m^3, phi = 35 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 10.9 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 20 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 10.9, g = 20 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (20 - 9.81)*10.9 | Answer: 111.1 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 8.9e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1.5, area = 2e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 8.9, i = 1.5, A = 2 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (8.9e-4)*1.5*(2e-3) | Answer: 2670 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 0.5 m, bed slope 0.008 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.017. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 4.7 m under a head of 1.2 m. Taking Cd = 0.62 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 5.6 m wide carries a discharge of 18.5 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 330 m and design speed 45 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 330, V = 45 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (45)^2 / (127*330) | Answer: 0.04832
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: For a design speed of 45 km/h with allowable superelevation 0.07 and lateral friction 0.15, find the minimum curve radius in m.
A tank of volume 790 m^3 treats a flow of 155 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 790, Q = 155 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 790 / 155 | Answer: 5.097 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 210 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.15 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 3 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 210, k = 0.15, t = 3 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 210*(1 - e^(-0.15*3)) | Answer: 76.1 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.31, rainfall intensity 75 mm/h over a catchment of 5.9 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.31, i = 75, A = 5.9 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.31*75*5.9 / 360 | Answer: 0.381 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.07 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 760 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.07, M = 760 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 760*(20+0.07)/20 | Answer: 762.7 m

question: Convert the decimal number 96 to binary.
solution: Divide 96 by 2 repeatedly, recording remainders | Reading remainders in reverse gives 1100000 | Answer: 1100000 (binary)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 2 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the decimal number 615 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 615 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 267 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the 8-bit binary number 10100000 to decimal.
solution: Binary 10100000 = sum of bit-weights | Answer: 160 (decimal)
formula: Sum each bit times its positional weight (2^i)

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 01001010 and 11101010.
solution: XOR: 10100000 | Count of 1s = 2 | Answer: 2
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 160 megabits is sent over a link of 62 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 160, B = 62 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 160 / 62 | Answer: 2.581 s

question: A link has bandwidth 39 Mbps and round-trip time 90 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 39, R = 90 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 39e6 * 90e-3 bits = 3510 kb | Answer: 3510 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.86, cache access time 4 ns and main-memory access time 190 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.86, tc = 4, tm = 190 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.86*4 + (1 - 0.86)*190 | Answer: 30.04 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 675959 elements?
solution: Given: n = 675959 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(675959)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: An O(n^2) algorithm performs c*n^2 basic operations. If c = 1 and n = 1510, how many operations are performed?
solution: Given: n = 1510 | Formula: operations = n^2 | Substitute: = (1510)^2 | Answer: 2280100

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.014, memory access time 90 ns and page-fault service time 4 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 4 ms = 4000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.014)*90 + 0.014*4000000.0 ns | Answer: 56.09 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 0.6 m^3 at 360 kPa and 370 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 0.6, P = 360, Tk = 370 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (360e3)*0.6 / (8.314*370) | Answer: 70.22 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.36 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 13 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.36, t = 13 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.36*13) | Answer: 0.9907

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.18 /min) is to reach 75% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.18, X = 75 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.75) / 0.18 | Answer: 7.702 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.11 /min) reaches 80% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.11, X = 80 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.8 / (0.11*(1 - 0.8)) | Answer: 36.36 min

question: For a reaction with A = 8e10 /s and activation energy 85 kJ/mol at 500 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 8, Ea = 85, Tk = 500 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 8e10 * exp(-85e3 / (8.314*500)) | Answer: 105.4 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.95 and bottoms xW = 0.1, with relative volatility alpha = 3.1. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.95, xw = 0.1, al = 3.1 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.95/0.05)(0.9/0.1)] / ln(3.1) | Answer: 4.545 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.62 and x = 0.47. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.62, x = 0.47 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.62/0.38) / (0.47/0.53) | Answer: 1.84

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.11 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 60 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.11, Psat = 60 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.11 * 60 | Answer: 6.6 kPa

question: A stream of 9.2 kg/s with specific heat 3 kJ/kg-K is heated through 65 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 9.2, cp = 3, dT = 65 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 9.2*3*65 | Answer: 1794 kW

question: A reactor of volume 19.9 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 2.3 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 19.9, Q = 2.3 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 19.9 / 2.3 | Answer: 8.652 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 8.1e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 2 mm with a concentration difference of 110 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 8.1, L = 2, dC = 110 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (8.1e-9)*110 / (2e-3) | Answer: 445.5 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 4.7 min and steady-state gain 1.9. For a step input of magnitude 18, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 4.7, K = 1.9, M = 18 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 1.9 * 18 | Answer: 34.2 units

question: A reactor operates at a space time of 9.3 min. Find its space velocity in per hour.
solution: Given: tau = 9.3 | Formula: SV = 60 / tau  (per hour) | Substitute: SV = 60 / 9.3 | Answer: 6.452 /h

question: An aircraft wing of area 75 m^2 flies at 130 m/s (air density 0.4 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 1. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 75, V = 130, rho = 0.4, CL = 1 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.4*(130)^2*75*1 / 1000 | Answer: 253.5 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 85 m^2 flies at 200 m/s (density 0.4 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.09. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 85, V = 200, rho = 0.4, CD = 0.09 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.4*(200)^2*85*0.09 / 1000 | Answer: 61.2 kN

question: An aircraft flies at 170 m/s where the speed of sound is 340 m/s. Find the Mach number.
solution: Given: V = 170, a = 340 | Formula: M = V / a | Substitute: M = 170 / 340 | Answer: 0.5

question: A specimen under stress 390 MPa shows an elastic strain of 1.9e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 390, eps = 1.9 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 390 / (1.9e-3) MPa = 205.3 GPa | Answer: 205.3 GPa

question: A block of mass 2 kg has a volume of 3.8e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 2, V = 3.8 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 2 / (3.8e-3) | Answer: 526.3 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 1700 mm is heated through 90 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 23e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 1700, dT = 90, al = 23 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 1700*23e-6*90 | Answer: 3.519 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 75 ohm, R2 = 150 ohm and R3 = 120 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 75, R2 = 150, R3 = 120 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 150*120 / 75 | Answer: 240 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 120 ohm and gauge factor 2.2 experiences a strain of 1400e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 120, GF = 2.2, eps = 1400 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 120*2.2*1400e-6 | Answer: 369.6 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 9.76 when the true value is 100. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.76, true = 100 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.76 - 100| / 100 * 100 | Answer: 90.24 %

question: Annual demand is 35500 units, ordering cost 110 per order and holding cost 16 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 35500, S = 110, H = 16 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*35500*110 / 16) | Answer: 698.7 units

question: An asset costs 130000 with salvage value 32000 after 20 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 130000, Sv = 32000, n = 20 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (130000 - 32000) / 20 | Answer: 4900 per year

question: A product sells for 190 per unit with variable cost 120 per unit and fixed costs 75000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 190, V = 120, F = 75000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 75000 / (190 - 120) | Answer: 1071 units

question: Find the present worth of 185000 received 8 years from now at an interest rate of 5% per year.

question: A process produces 49 defective items in a batch of 2000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 49, N = 2000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 49/2000 * 1e6 | Answer: 24500 PPM

question: Find the slope of the line through (-5, -6) and (-1, 4).
solution: Given: x1 = -5, y1 = -6, x2 = -1, y2 = 4 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (4 - -6) / (-1 - -5) | Answer: 2.5

question: Find the distance between the points (8, -9) and (7, 4).
solution: Given: x1 = 8, y1 = -9, x2 = 7, y2 = 4 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-1)^2 + (13)^2) | Answer: 13.04 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (5,3), (6,2), (-7,6).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 4.5 sq units

question: Evaluate the number of combinations C(8, 1).
solution: Given: n = 8, r = 1 | Formula: C(n, r) = n! / (r! (n - r)!) | Substitute: C(8, 1) = 8! / (1! * 7!) | Answer: 8

question: Find the 15th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -10 and common difference 9.
solution: Given: a = -10, d = 9, n = 15 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -10 + (15 - 1)*9 | Answer: 116

question: Find the sum of the first 29 terms of an AP with first term -5 and common difference 1.
solution: Given: a = -5, d = 1, n = 29 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 29/2 [2*-5 + (29-1)*1] | Answer: 261

question: Find the 5th term of a geometric progression with first term 6 and common ratio 3.
solution: Given: a = 6, r = 3, n = 5 | Formula: a_n = a r^(n-1) | Substitute: a_n = 6 * 3^(5-1) | Answer: 486

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 31500 at 14.8% per annum for 3 years.
solution: Given: P = 31500, R = 14.8, Tt = 3 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 31500 * 14.8 * 3 / 100 | Answer: 13986 currency units

question: Find the amount when 38000 is invested at 9.2% per annum compounded annually for 4 years.
solution: Given: P = 38000, R = 9.2, Tt = 4 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 38000 * (1 + 9.2/100)^4 | Answer: 54035 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (0, 0, -4) and (2, -2, 8).

question: Find the modulus of the complex number 4 + 7i.
solution: Given: a = 4, b = 7 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((4)^2 + (7)^2) | Answer: 8.062

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number -12 + 10i.
solution: Given: a = -12, b = 10 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(10, -12) | Answer: 140.2 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = 3x^3 - 7x^2 + 2x - 2 at x = 4.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-143 with initial guess x0=4, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.8 and ordinates 11, 6, 5, 20, 4, estimate the integral.

solution: Given: a = 20, b = 55 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 20*55 / 5 | Answer: 220

question: A circular rod of diameter 18 mm carries an axial tensile load of 97 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 23 mm and length 2100 mm carries an axial load of 73 kN. Take E = 200 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 80 mm transmits a torque of 1400 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 80, Tt = 1400 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(1400*1000) / (pi*(80)^3) | Answer: 13.93 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 57 mm and length 800 mm carries a torque of 1750 N-m. With G = 45 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (57)^4 / 32 = 1036333 mm^4 | theta = (1750*1000)(800) / (45000 * 1036333) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 1.72 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 101 mm wide and 160 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 101, h = 160 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 101*(160)^2 / 6 | Answer: 430933 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (120 mm x 180 mm) carries a bending moment of 5 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (30 mm x 130 mm) has effective length 2300 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 630 MPa is designed for a working stress of 200 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 630, sw = 200 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 630 / 200 | Answer: 3.15

question: A steel bar is fully restrained and heated through 65 deg C. With E = 210 GPa and alpha = 13e-6 /deg C, find the thermal stress in MPa.
solution: Given: dT = 65, E = 210, al = 13 | Formula: sigma = E alpha (dT) | Substitute: sigma = 210000 * 13e-6 * 65 | Answer: 177.4 MPa

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 800 mm and wall thickness 16 mm carries an internal pressure of 0.8 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 800, t = 16, P = 0.8 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 0.8*800 / (2*16) | Answer: 20 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 1180 K and 450 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 1180, Tc = 450 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 450/1180) * 100 | Answer: 61.86 %

question: A refrigerator works between 259 K (cold) and 324 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 259, Th = 324 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 259 / (324 - 259) | Answer: 3.985

question: A heat pump operates between 270 K and 302 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 270, Th = 302 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 302 / (302 - 270) | Answer: 9.438

question: 6.7 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 105 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 6.7, dT = 105 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 6.7 * 0.718 * 105 | Answer: 505.1 kJ

question: 3.9 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 105 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.9, dT = 105 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 3.9 * 1.005 * 105 | Answer: 411.5 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 3.2 m^3 at 510 K with mass 2.7 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 3.2, Tk = 510, m = 2.7 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 2.7*0.287*510 / 3.2 | Answer: 123.5 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 2.9 kg of air expands isothermally at 400 K from volume V1 to 5*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.9, Tk = 400, ratio = 5 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 2.9*0.287*400*ln(5) | Answer: 535.8 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 1.3 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.3 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 1.3, D = 0.3 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*1.3*0.3 / 0.001 | Answer: 390000

question: Water flows at 1.1 m/s through a pipe of diameter 160 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 13.6 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 13.6 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*13.6 / 1000 | Answer: 133.4 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 15 m. Taking Cv = 0.98, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 15, cv = 0.98 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.98*sqrt(2*9.81*15) | Answer: 16.81 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 270 mm) water flows at 2.1 m/s. It contracts to diameter 120 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
Water flows at 1.4 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.32 m and length 340 m. With friction factor f = 0.033, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).

question: A pinion of 19 teeth drives a gear of 115 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1100 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 19, z2 = 115, N1 = 1100 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1100*19 / 115 | Answer: 181.7 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 350 mm rotates at 950 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 350, N = 950 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.35)*950 / 60 | Answer: 17.41 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 19.6 kW at 500 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 19.6, N = 500 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(19.6*1000) / (2*pi*500) | Answer: 374.3 N-m

question: A mass of 7.4 kg rotates at radius 0.21 m at 500 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 14600 N/m and mass 18.6 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.

question: A plane wall of area 9.8 m^2 and thickness 0.24 m has conductivity k = 22.9 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 165 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.

question: A surface of area 5.3 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 175 W/m^2-K to surroundings 110 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.

question: In a counter-flow heat exchanger the terminal temperature differences are 110 deg C and 20 deg C. Find the log mean temperature difference (LMTD) in deg C.
solution: Given: dT1 = 110, dT2 = 20 | Formula: LMTD = (dT1 - dT2) / ln(dT1/dT2) | Substitute: LMTD = (110 - 20) / ln(110/20) | Answer: 52.79 deg C

question: In turning, cutting speed = 190 m/min, feed = 0.13 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2.2 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 190, f = 0.13, d = 2.2 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*190*0.13*2.2 | Answer: 54340 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 320 mm is turned at 350 rpm with a feed of 0.25 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 320, N = 350, f = 0.25 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 320 / (0.25*350) | Answer: 3.657 min

question: A resistor of 115 ohm carries a current of 6.8 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 115, I = 6.8 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 6.8 * 115 | Answer: 782 V

question: Three resistors 24 ohm, 10 ohm and 88 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 24, R2 = 10, R3 = 88 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 24 + 10 + 88 | Answer: 122 ohm

question: Two resistors 112 ohm and 30 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 112, R2 = 30 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 112*30 / (112+30) | Answer: 23.66 ohm

question: A device draws 14.6 A at 185 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 185, I = 14.6 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 185 * 14.6 | Answer: 2701 W

question: A current of 1.5 A flows through a 123 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.

question: Two capacitors 20.4 uF and 40 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 20.4, C2 = 40 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 20.4*40 / (20.4+40) | Answer: 13.51 uF

question: A resistor 33 kohm and capacitor 1.1 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 33, C = 1.1 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (33k)(1.1u) = 36.3 ms | Answer: 36.3 ms

question: An inductor 190.4 mH is in series with 157 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 190.4, R = 157 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (190.4e-3) / 157 | Answer: 1.213 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 117.2 mH inductor at 70 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 117.2, f = 70 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (70)(117.2e-3) | Answer: 51.55 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 28.8 uF capacitor at 470 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 28.8, f = 470 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (470)(28.8e-6)) | Answer: 11.76 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 98 ohm, XL = 97 ohm and XC = 27 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 98, XL = 97, XC = 27 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(98^2 + (97 - 27)^2) | Answer: 120.4 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 38.1 mH and C = 7.2 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 38.1, C = 7.2 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(38.1e-3 * 7.2e-6)) | Answer: 303.9 Hz

question: A capacitor of 17.5 uF is charged to 15 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 17.5, V = 15 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*17.5e-6*(15)^2 | Answer: 1.969 mJ

question: An alternating voltage has a peak value of 280 V. Find its RMS value.

question: A transformer has primary voltage 370 V with 940 primary turns and 500 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.

question: A DC motor is supplied at 180 V and draws an armature current of 32 A. If the armature resistance is 0.53 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 180, Ia = 32, Ra = 0.53 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 180 - 32*0.53 | Answer: 163 V

question: A 6-pole induction motor on a 60 Hz supply runs at 1060 rpm. Find the slip (%).
formula: s = (Ns - N) / Ns,  Ns = 120 f / P

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 195 A at 415 V (line) with a power factor of 0.82. Find the total real power in kW.

question: A load has real power 125 kW and apparent power 205 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 125, S = 205 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 125 / 205 | Answer: 0.6098

question: A machine delivers 60 kW output while drawing 137 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 60, Pi = 137 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 60/137 * 100 | Answer: 43.8 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 24 V across R1 = 33 ohm and R2 = 48 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 24, R1 = 33, R2 = 48 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 24*48 / (33+48) | Answer: 14.22 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 100 kohm and Rin = 22 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 100, Rin = 22 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 100 / 22 | Answer: 4.545

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 20 kohm and Rg = 38 kohm. Find the voltage gain.

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 9875. Express the gain in decibels (power).

question: A simply supported beam of span 7.7 m carries a central point load of 25 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.

question: A simply supported beam of span 4 m carries a UDL of 25 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4, w = 25 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 25*(4)^2 / 8 | Answer: 50 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 5.2 m carries a point load 65 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.2, W = 65 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 65*5.2 | Answer: 338 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 4.1 m carries a UDL of 20 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.1, w = 20 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 20*(4.1)^2 / 2 | Answer: 168.1 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.2 m carries a point load 100 kN at distance 1.2 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 4.2, a = 1.2, W = 100 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 100*(4.2 - 1.2) / 4.2 | Answer: 71.43 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 4.1 m) carries a central point load 60 kN. With E = 30 GPa and I = 490e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=60000 N, L=4100.0 mm, E=30000 MPa, I=490e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 5.861 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 8 m carries a UDL of 18 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 8, w = 18 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 18*(8)^2 / 12 | Answer: 96 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 410 mm, clear cover 35 mm and main bars of diameter 20 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 410, c = 35, dia = 20 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 410 - 35 - 20/2 | Answer: 365 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 12.5 m^2 carrying a factored load of 14.3 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 12.5, w = 14.3 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 14.3 * 12.5 | Answer: 178.8 kN

question: For a bar of diameter 20 mm with design bond stress 2.3 MPa and steel stress 435 MPa, find the development length in mm.
solution: Given: dia = 20, tbd = 2.3, fs = 435 | Formula: Ld = phi fs / (4 tau_bd) | Substitute: Ld = 20*435 / (4*2.3) | Answer: 945.7 mm

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 5.1 m, unit weight 16 kN/m^3, phi = 35 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 9.7 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 21 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 3.3e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.7, area = 1.7e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.3 m, bed slope 0.001 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.027. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 2.8 m under a head of 1.1 m. Taking Cd = 0.6 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.

question: A rectangular channel 5.4 m wide carries a discharge of 11.3 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 400 m and design speed 50 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 400, V = 50 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (50)^2 / (127*400) | Answer: 0.04921
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: For a design speed of 40 km/h with allowable superelevation 0.06 and lateral friction 0.15, find the minimum curve radius in m.
A tank of volume 490 m^3 treats a flow of 100 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 490, Q = 100 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 490 / 100 | Answer: 4.9 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 400 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.26 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 7 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 400, k = 0.26, t = 7 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 400*(1 - e^(-0.26*7)) | Answer: 335.2 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.7, rainfall intensity 65 mm/h over a catchment of 58.6 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.7, i = 65, A = 58.6 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.7*65*58.6 / 360 | Answer: 7.406 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.04 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 230 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.04, M = 230 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 230*(30+0.04)/30 | Answer: 230.3 m

question: Convert the decimal number 213 to binary.
solution: Divide 213 by 2 repeatedly, recording remainders | Reading remainders in reverse gives 11010101 | Answer: 11010101 (binary)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 2 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the decimal number 3419 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 3419 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: D5B (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the 8-bit binary number 01110101 to decimal.
solution: Binary 01110101 = sum of bit-weights | Answer: 117 (decimal)
formula: Sum each bit times its positional weight (2^i)

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 00011111 and 00111101.
solution: XOR: 00100010 | Count of 1s = 2 | Answer: 2
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 750 megabits is sent over a link of 16 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 750, B = 16 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 750 / 16 | Answer: 46.88 s

question: A link has bandwidth 25 Mbps and round-trip time 200 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 25, R = 200 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 25e6 * 200e-3 bits = 5000 kb | Answer: 5000 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.92, cache access time 5 ns and main-memory access time 50 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.92, tc = 5, tm = 50 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.92*5 + (1 - 0.92)*50 | Answer: 8.6 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 471120 elements?
solution: Given: n = 471120 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(471120)) + 1 | Answer: 19

question: An O(n^2) algorithm performs c*n^2 basic operations. If c = 1 and n = 1360, how many operations are performed?
solution: Given: n = 1360 | Formula: operations = n^2 | Substitute: = (1360)^2 | Answer: 1849600

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.002, memory access time 90 ns and page-fault service time 7 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 7 ms = 7000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.002)*90 + 0.002*7000000.0 ns | Answer: 14.09 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 2.4 m^3 at 420 kPa and 560 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 2.4, P = 420, Tk = 560 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (420e3)*2.4 / (8.314*560) | Answer: 216.5 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.08 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 9 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.08, t = 9 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.08*9) | Answer: 0.5132

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.49 /min) is to reach 80% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.49, X = 80 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.8) / 0.49 | Answer: 3.285 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.1 /min) reaches 60% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.1, X = 60 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.6 / (0.1*(1 - 0.6)) | Answer: 15 min

question: For a reaction with A = 8e10 /s and activation energy 50 kJ/mol at 460 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 8, Ea = 50, Tk = 460 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 8e10 * exp(-50e3 / (8.314*460)) | Answer: 16796 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.94 and bottoms xW = 0.04, with relative volatility alpha = 2.6. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.94, xw = 0.04, al = 2.6 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.94/0.06)(0.96/0.04)] / ln(2.6) | Answer: 6.206 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.7 and x = 0.3. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.7, x = 0.3 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.7/0.3) / (0.3/0.7) | Answer: 5.444

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.69 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 120 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.69, Psat = 120 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.69 * 120 | Answer: 82.8 kPa

question: A stream of 2.8 kg/s with specific heat 3.1 kJ/kg-K is heated through 55 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 2.8, cp = 3.1, dT = 55 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 2.8*3.1*55 | Answer: 477.4 kW

question: A reactor of volume 9.6 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 1.8 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 9.6, Q = 1.8 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 9.6 / 1.8 | Answer: 5.333 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 4.8e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 2 mm with a concentration difference of 20 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 4.8, L = 2, dC = 20 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (4.8e-9)*20 / (2e-3) | Answer: 48 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 6.7 min and steady-state gain 1.8. For a step input of magnitude 14, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 6.7, K = 1.8, M = 14 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 1.8 * 14 | Answer: 25.2 units

question: A reactor operates at a space time of 19.4 min. Find its space velocity in per hour.
solution: Given: tau = 19.4 | Formula: SV = 60 / tau  (per hour) | Substitute: SV = 60 / 19.4 | Answer: 3.093 /h

question: An aircraft wing of area 55 m^2 flies at 80 m/s (air density 0.4 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 1.1. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 55, V = 80, rho = 0.4, CL = 1.1 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.4*(80)^2*55*1.1 / 1000 | Answer: 77.44 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 110 m^2 flies at 110 m/s (density 0.4 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.06. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 110, V = 110, rho = 0.4, CD = 0.06 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.4*(110)^2*110*0.06 / 1000 | Answer: 15.97 kN

question: An aircraft flies at 570 m/s where the speed of sound is 310 m/s. Find the Mach number.
solution: Given: V = 570, a = 310 | Formula: M = V / a | Substitute: M = 570 / 310 | Answer: 1.839

question: A specimen under stress 330 MPa shows an elastic strain of 1e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 330, eps = 1 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 330 / (1e-3) MPa = 330 GPa | Answer: 330 GPa

question: A block of mass 37 kg has a volume of 2.1e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 37, V = 2.1 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 37 / (2.1e-3) | Answer: 17619 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 2800 mm is heated through 45 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 23e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 2800, dT = 45, al = 23 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 2800*23e-6*45 | Answer: 2.898 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 105 ohm, R2 = 135 ohm and R3 = 490 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 105, R2 = 135, R3 = 490 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 135*490 / 105 | Answer: 630 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 120 ohm and gauge factor 2.1 experiences a strain of 300e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 120, GF = 2.1, eps = 300 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 120*2.1*300e-6 | Answer: 75.6 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 9.42 when the true value is 100. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.42, true = 100 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.42 - 100| / 100 * 100 | Answer: 90.58 %

question: Annual demand is 1000 units, ordering cost 290 per order and holding cost 6 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 1000, S = 290, H = 6 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*1000*290 / 6) | Answer: 310.9 units

question: An asset costs 350000 with salvage value 2000 after 8 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 350000, Sv = 2000, n = 8 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (350000 - 2000) / 8 | Answer: 43500 per year

question: A product sells for 170 per unit with variable cost 140 per unit and fixed costs 150000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 170, V = 140, F = 150000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 150000 / (170 - 140) | Answer: 5000 units

question: Find the present worth of 70000 received 3 years from now at an interest rate of 7% per year.
solution: Given: F = 70000, n = 3, i = 7 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 70000 / (1 + 0.07)^3 | Answer: 57141 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.98, 0.91 and 0.96 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.98, r2 = 0.91, r3 = 0.96 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.98*0.91*0.96 | Answer: 0.8561

question: A process produces 13 defective items in a batch of 14500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 13, N = 14500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 13/14500 * 1e6 | Answer: 896.6 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -5x^3 - 2x^2 - 4x - 4 evaluated at x = 5.
For f(x) = -4x^3 - 4x + 5, find f''(x) at x = 4.
Evaluate the definite integral of (4x^2 + 6x + 8) dx from x = -1 to x = 6.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = 4x^3/3 + 6x^2/2 + 8x | Evaluate F(6) - F(-1) | Answer: 450.3
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 6x^2 - 4x - 1 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[-9, 7], [-2, -5]].
solution: Given: a = -9, b = 7, c = -2, d = -5 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (-9)(-5) - (7)(-2) | Answer: 59

question: Find the determinant of [[-4, -2, 3], [0, -5, 3], [0, 1, -5]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: -88

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[-5, 8], [8, 7]].
solution: Trace tr = 2, Determinant = -99 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 11

question: Solve for x: 0x + -6y = 6 and -2x + -6y = -4.
solution: Determinant = 0*-6 - -6*-2 = -12 | x = (e d - b f) / det = 5 | Answer: x = 5

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 44, 16, 94, 9, 73.
solution: Sum = 236 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 47.2 | Answer: 47.2

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 45, 3, 19, 14, 5.
solution: Mean = 17.2 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 16.86

question: Find the slope of the line through (8, -5) and (-9, -8).
Find the distance between the points (-5, -9) and (4, 6).
solution: Given: x1 = -5, y1 = -9, x2 = 4, y2 = 6 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((9)^2 + (15)^2) | Answer: 17.49 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (5,-7), (-1,-6), (-2,8).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 41.5 sq units

question: Evaluate the number of combinations C(12, 1).
solution: Given: n = 12, r = 1 | Formula: C(n, r) = n! / (r! (n - r)!) | Substitute: C(12, 1) = 12! / (1! * 11!) | Answer: 12

question: Find the 29th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -20 and common difference -5.
solution: Given: a = -20, d = -5, n = 29 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -20 + (29 - 1)*-5 | Answer: -160

question: Find the sum of the first 37 terms of an AP with first term 7 and common difference 3.
solution: Given: a = 7, d = 3, n = 37 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 37/2 [2*7 + (37-1)*3] | Answer: 2257

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 18000 at 8.5% per annum for 1 years.
solution: Given: P = 18000, R = 8.5, Tt = 1 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 18000 * 8.5 * 1 / 100 | Answer: 1530 currency units

question: Find the amount when 30000 is invested at 9.1% per annum compounded annually for 3 years.
solution: Given: P = 30000, R = 9.1, Tt = 3 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 30000 * (1 + 9.1/100)^3 | Answer: 38958 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (7, 2, -4) and (-6, 3, -3).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (-3, -2, 0) and (-1, 6, 4).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 24.66

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (5, 1, -5) and (-3, -6, 4).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 137.3 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number 10 + 9i.
solution: Given: a = 10, b = 9 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((10)^2 + (9)^2) | Answer: 13.45

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number 5 + 9i.
solution: Given: a = 5, b = 9 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(9, 5) | Answer: 60.95 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = x^3 + 6x^2 - x - 9 at x = -4.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-28 with initial guess x0=8, find x1 (one iteration).
solution: Given: N = 28, x0 = 8 | Formula: x1 = x0 - (x0^2 - N)/(2 x0) | Substitute: x1 = 8 - ((8)^2 - 28)/(2*8) | Answer: 5.75

question: Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=0.6 and ordinates 13, 20, 15, 15, 17, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 402 and 599.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 402 and 599 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 72 and 8.
solution: Given: a = 72, b = 8 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 72*8 / 8 | Answer: 72
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 45 mm carries an axial tensile load of 94 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 38 mm and length 2300 mm carries an axial load of 68 kN. Take E = 210 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 67 mm transmits a torque of 1700 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 67, Tt = 1700 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(1700*1000) / (pi*(67)^3) | Answer: 28.79 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 52 mm and length 900 mm carries a torque of 700 N-m. With G = 77 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (52)^4 / 32 = 717816 mm^4 | theta = (700*1000)(900) / (77000 * 717816) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 0.6531 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 146 mm wide and 130 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 146, h = 130 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 146*(130)^2 / 6 | Answer: 411233 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (96 mm x 80 mm) carries a bending moment of 7 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (45 mm x 120 mm) has effective length 2300 mm and E = 200 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 500 MPa is designed for a working stress of 90 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 500, sw = 90 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 500 / 90 | Answer: 5.556

question: A steel bar is fully restrained and heated through 90 deg C. With E = 200 GPa and alpha = 13e-6 /deg C, find the thermal stress in MPa.
solution: Given: dT = 90, E = 200, al = 13 | Formula: sigma = E alpha (dT) | Substitute: sigma = 200000 * 13e-6 * 90 | Answer: 234 MPa

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 500 mm and wall thickness 17 mm carries an internal pressure of 1.9 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 500, t = 17, P = 1.9 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 1.9*500 / (2*17) | Answer: 27.94 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 1040 K and 360 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 1040, Tc = 360 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 360/1040) * 100 | Answer: 65.38 %

question: A refrigerator works between 252 K (cold) and 312 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 252, Th = 312 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 252 / (312 - 252) | Answer: 4.2

question: A heat pump operates between 275 K and 328 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 275, Th = 328 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 328 / (328 - 275) | Answer: 6.189

question: 5.5 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 160 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 5.5, dT = 160 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 5.5 * 0.718 * 160 | Answer: 631.8 kJ

question: 3.5 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 165 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.5, dT = 165 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 3.5 * 1.005 * 165 | Answer: 580.4 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 2.6 m^3 at 500 K with mass 5.3 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 2.6, Tk = 500, m = 5.3 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 5.3*0.287*500 / 2.6 | Answer: 292.5 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 1.2 kg of air expands isothermally at 480 K from volume V1 to 3*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1.2, Tk = 480, ratio = 3 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 1.2*0.287*480*ln(3) | Answer: 181.6 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 4 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.15 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 4, D = 0.15 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*4*0.15 / 0.001 | Answer: 600000

question: Water flows at 3.4 m/s through a pipe of diameter 110 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 23.9 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 23.9 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*23.9 / 1000 | Answer: 234.5 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 17.2 m. Taking Cv = 0.97, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 17.2, cv = 0.97 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.97*sqrt(2*9.81*17.2) | Answer: 17.82 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 390 mm) water flows at 1.7 m/s. It contracts to diameter 120 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
Water flows at 3.5 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.11 m and length 250 m. With friction factor f = 0.02, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 34 teeth drives a gear of 75 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1100 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 34, z2 = 75, N1 = 1100 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1100*34 / 75 | Answer: 498.7 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 360 mm rotates at 650 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 360, N = 650 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.36)*650 / 60 | Answer: 12.25 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 42.9 kW at 300 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 42.9, N = 300 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(42.9*1000) / (2*pi*300) | Answer: 1366 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 5 kg rotates at radius 0.17 m at 1050 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 4500 N/m and mass 15 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 4500, m = 15 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(4500/15) | Answer: 2.757 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 8.9 m^2 and thickness 0.25 m has conductivity k = 47.1 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 180 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 8.9, L = 0.25, k = 47.1, dT = 180 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 47.1*8.9*180 / 0.25 | Answer: 301817 W

question: A surface of area 5.1 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 155 W/m^2-K to surroundings 125 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 5.1, h = 155, dT = 125 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 155*5.1*125 | Answer: 98812 W

question: In a counter-flow heat exchanger the terminal temperature differences are 110 deg C and 15 deg C. Find the log mean temperature difference (LMTD) in deg C.
solution: Given: dT1 = 110, dT2 = 15 | Formula: LMTD = (dT1 - dT2) / ln(dT1/dT2) | Substitute: LMTD = (110 - 15) / ln(110/15) | Answer: 47.68 deg C

question: In turning, cutting speed = 190 m/min, feed = 0.13 mm/rev, depth of cut = 0.5 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 190, f = 0.13, d = 0.5 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*190*0.13*0.5 | Answer: 12350 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 220 mm is turned at 450 rpm with a feed of 0.1 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 220, N = 450, f = 0.1 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 220 / (0.1*450) | Answer: 4.889 min

question: A resistor of 190 ohm carries a current of 5 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 190, I = 5 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 5 * 190 | Answer: 950 V

question: Three resistors 78 ohm, 60 ohm and 99 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 78, R2 = 60, R3 = 99 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 78 + 60 + 99 | Answer: 237 ohm

question: Two resistors 42 ohm and 92 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 42, R2 = 92 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 42*92 / (42+92) | Answer: 28.84 ohm

question: A device draws 1 A at 45 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 45, I = 1 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 45 * 1 | Answer: 45 W

question: A current of 8.9 A flows through a 26 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 8.9, R = 26 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (8.9)^2 * 26 | Answer: 2059 W

question: Two capacitors 16.5 uF and 16.2 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 16.5, C2 = 16.2 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 16.5*16.2 / (16.5+16.2) | Answer: 8.174 uF

question: A resistor 95 kohm and capacitor 19.1 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 95, C = 19.1 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (95k)(19.1u) = 1815 ms | Answer: 1815 ms

question: An inductor 403.9 mH is in series with 82 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 403.9, R = 82 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (403.9e-3) / 82 | Answer: 4.926 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 68 mH inductor at 190 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 68, f = 190 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (190)(68e-3) | Answer: 81.18 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 23.2 uF capacitor at 900 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 23.2, f = 900 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (900)(23.2e-6)) | Answer: 7.622 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 41 ohm, XL = 104 ohm and XC = 92 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 41, XL = 104, XC = 92 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(41^2 + (104 - 92)^2) | Answer: 42.72 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 44.7 mH and C = 8.6 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 44.7, C = 8.6 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(44.7e-3 * 8.6e-6)) | Answer: 256.7 Hz

question: A capacitor of 64.7 uF is charged to 95 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 64.7, V = 95 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*64.7e-6*(95)^2 | Answer: 292 mJ

question: An alternating voltage has a peak value of 62 V. Find its RMS value.
solution: Given: Vp = 62 | Formula: Vrms = Vp / sqrt(2) | Substitute: Vrms = 62 / sqrt(2) | Answer: 43.84 V

question: A transformer has primary voltage 220 V with 530 primary turns and 410 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 220, N1 = 530, N2 = 410 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 220 * 410/530 | Answer: 170.2 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 290 V and draws an armature current of 29 A. If the armature resistance is 0.73 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 290, Ia = 29, Ra = 0.73 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 290 - 29*0.73 | Answer: 268.8 V

question: A 4-pole induction motor on a 50 Hz supply runs at 1090 rpm. Find the slip (%).
formula: s = (Ns - N) / Ns,  Ns = 120 f / P

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 95 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.91. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 95, VL = 400, pf = 0.91 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*400*95*0.91 / 1000 | Answer: 59.89 kW

question: A load has real power 150 kW and apparent power 175 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 150, S = 175 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 150 / 175 | Answer: 0.8571

question: A machine delivers 30 kW output while drawing 67 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 30, Pi = 67 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 30/67 * 100 | Answer: 44.78 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 14 V across R1 = 30 ohm and R2 = 5 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 14, R1 = 30, R2 = 5 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 14*5 / (30+5) | Answer: 2 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 100 kohm and Rin = 44 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 100, Rin = 44 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 100 / 44 | Answer: 2.273

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 150 kohm and Rg = 3 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 150, Rg = 3 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 150/3 | Answer: 51

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 3204. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 3204 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(3204) | Answer: 35.06 dB

question: A signal is sampled at 138 kHz. According to the Nyquist criterion, what is the maximum signal frequency that can be represented (in kHz)?
solution: Given: fs = 138 | Formula: f_max = fs / 2 | Substitute: f_max = 138 / 2 | Answer: 69 kHz

question: A simply supported beam of span 5.8 m carries a central point load of 80 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.8, W = 80 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 80*5.8 / 4 | Answer: 116 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.5 m carries a UDL of 60 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6.5, w = 60 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 60*(6.5)^2 / 8 | Answer: 316.9 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 1.2 m carries a point load 70 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 1.2, W = 70 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 70*1.2 | Answer: 84 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 5.2 m carries a UDL of 18 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.2, w = 18 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 18*(5.2)^2 / 2 | Answer: 243.4 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 8.4 m carries a point load 50 kN at distance 3.2 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 8.4, a = 3.2, W = 50 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 50*(8.4 - 3.2) / 8.4 | Answer: 30.95 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 6.4 m) carries a central point load 45 kN. With E = 30 GPa and I = 440e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=45000 N, L=6400.0 mm, E=30000 MPa, I=440e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 18.62 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 4.1 m carries a UDL of 33 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.1, w = 33 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 33*(4.1)^2 / 12 | Answer: 46.23 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 400 mm, clear cover 40 mm and main bars of diameter 12 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 400, c = 40, dia = 12 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 400 - 40 - 12/2 | Answer: 354 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 24.6 m^2 carrying a factored load of 15 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 24.6, w = 15 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 15 * 24.6 | Answer: 369 kN

question: For a bar of diameter 25 mm with design bond stress 1.2 MPa and steel stress 395 MPa, find the development length in mm.
solution: Given: dia = 25, tbd = 1.2, fs = 395 | Formula: Ld = phi fs / (4 tau_bd) | Substitute: Ld = 25*395 / (4*1.2) | Answer: 2057 mm

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 6.5 m, unit weight 16 kN/m^3, phi = 35 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 3.1 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 21 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 3.1, g = 21 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (21 - 9.81)*3.1 | Answer: 34.69 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 2.2e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.8, area = 2.3e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 2.2, i = 0.8, A = 2.3 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (2.2e-4)*0.8*(2.3e-3) | Answer: 404.8 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.5 m, bed slope 0.002 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.025. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 2.7 m under a head of 0.3 m. Taking Cd = 0.64 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.

question: A rectangular channel 5 m wide carries a discharge of 26.5 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).

solution: Given: R = 180, V = 100 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (100)^2 / (127*180) | Answer: 0.4374
