question: A shaft of diameter 61 mm and length 700 mm carries a torque of 350 N-m. With G = 80 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (61)^4 / 32 = 1359312 mm^4 | theta = (350*1000)(700) / (80000 * 1359312) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 0.1291 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 140 mm wide and 180 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 140, h = 180 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 140*(180)^2 / 6 | Answer: 756000 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (119 mm x 150 mm) carries a bending moment of 6 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (59 mm x 110 mm) has effective length 2900 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 860 MPa is designed for a working stress of 220 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 860, sw = 220 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 860 / 220 | Answer: 3.909

question: A steel bar is fully restrained and heated through 85 deg C. With E = 200 GPa and alpha = 12e-6 /deg C, find the thermal stress in MPa.
solution: Given: dT = 85, E = 200, al = 12 | Formula: sigma = E alpha (dT) | Substitute: sigma = 200000 * 12e-6 * 85 | Answer: 204 MPa

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1350 mm and wall thickness 17 mm carries an internal pressure of 1.1 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1350, t = 17, P = 1.1 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 1.1*1350 / (2*17) | Answer: 43.68 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 740 K and 420 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 740, Tc = 420 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 420/740) * 100 | Answer: 43.24 %

question: A refrigerator works between 272 K (cold) and 312 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 272, Th = 312 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 272 / (312 - 272) | Answer: 6.8

question: A heat pump operates between 268 K and 332 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 268, Th = 332 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 332 / (332 - 268) | Answer: 5.188

question: 4 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 20 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4, dT = 20 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 4 * 0.718 * 20 | Answer: 57.44 kJ

question: 5.8 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 60 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 5.8, dT = 60 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 5.8 * 1.005 * 60 | Answer: 349.7 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 2.3 m^3 at 340 K with mass 4 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 2.3, Tk = 340, m = 4 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 4*0.287*340 / 2.3 | Answer: 169.7 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 3.9 kg of air expands isothermally at 330 K from volume V1 to 4*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.9, Tk = 330, ratio = 4 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 3.9*0.287*330*ln(4) | Answer: 512.1 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 3.1 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.17 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 3.1, D = 0.17 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*3.1*0.17 / 0.001 | Answer: 527000

question: Water flows at 1.7 m/s through a pipe of diameter 140 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 7 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 7 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*7 / 1000 | Answer: 68.67 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 8.1 m. Taking Cv = 0.97, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 8.1, cv = 0.97 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.97*sqrt(2*9.81*8.1) | Answer: 12.23 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 350 mm) water flows at 2.9 m/s. It contracts to diameter 50 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 350, d2 = 50, V1 = 2.9 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 2.9*(350/50)^2 | Answer: 142.1 m/s

question: Water flows at 2.8 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.14 m and length 210 m. With friction factor f = 0.026, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 30 teeth drives a gear of 96 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1150 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 30, z2 = 96, N1 = 1150 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1150*30 / 96 | Answer: 359.4 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 510 mm rotates at 400 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 510, N = 400 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.51)*400 / 60 | Answer: 10.68 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 40.8 kW at 700 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 40.8, N = 700 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(40.8*1000) / (2*pi*700) | Answer: 556.6 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 4.5 kg rotates at radius 0.2 m at 550 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 16100 N/m and mass 16.2 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 16100, m = 16.2 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(16100/16.2) | Answer: 5.017 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 8.4 m^2 and thickness 0.24 m has conductivity k = 36.3 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 25 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 8.4, L = 0.24, k = 36.3, dT = 25 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 36.3*8.4*25 / 0.24 | Answer: 31762 W

question: A surface of area 0.6 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 85 W/m^2-K to surroundings 105 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 0.6, h = 85, dT = 105 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 85*0.6*105 | Answer: 5355 W

question: In a counter-flow heat exchanger the terminal temperature differences are 95 deg C and 25 deg C. Find the log mean temperature difference (LMTD) in deg C.
solution: Given: dT1 = 95, dT2 = 25 | Formula: LMTD = (dT1 - dT2) / ln(dT1/dT2) | Substitute: LMTD = (95 - 25) / ln(95/25) | Answer: 52.43 deg C

question: In turning, cutting speed = 190 m/min, feed = 0.49 mm/rev, depth of cut = 1.2 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 190, f = 0.49, d = 1.2 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*190*0.49*1.2 | Answer: 111720 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 380 mm is turned at 750 rpm with a feed of 0.2 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 380, N = 750, f = 0.2 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 380 / (0.2*750) | Answer: 2.533 min

question: A resistor of 10 ohm carries a current of 8.4 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 10, I = 8.4 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 8.4 * 10 | Answer: 84 V

question: Three resistors 6 ohm, 80 ohm and 64 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 6, R2 = 80, R3 = 64 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 6 + 80 + 64 | Answer: 150 ohm

question: Two resistors 69 ohm and 41 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 69, R2 = 41 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 69*41 / (69+41) | Answer: 25.72 ohm

question: A device draws 13.6 A at 175 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 175, I = 13.6 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 175 * 13.6 | Answer: 2380 W

question: A current of 4.1 A flows through a 71 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 4.1, R = 71 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (4.1)^2 * 71 | Answer: 1194 W

question: Two capacitors 10.1 uF and 36 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 10.1, C2 = 36 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 10.1*36 / (10.1+36) | Answer: 7.887 uF

question: A resistor 46 kohm and capacitor 2.8 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 46, C = 2.8 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (46k)(2.8u) = 128.8 ms | Answer: 128.8 ms

question: An inductor 468.1 mH is in series with 187 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 468.1, R = 187 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (468.1e-3) / 187 | Answer: 2.503 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 84.7 mH inductor at 830 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 84.7, f = 830 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (830)(84.7e-3) | Answer: 441.7 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 29.1 uF capacitor at 340 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 29.1, f = 340 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (340)(29.1e-6)) | Answer: 16.09 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 65 ohm, XL = 82 ohm and XC = 135 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 65, XL = 82, XC = 135 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(65^2 + (82 - 135)^2) | Answer: 83.87 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 61.6 mH and C = 8.2 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 61.6, C = 8.2 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(61.6e-3 * 8.2e-6)) | Answer: 223.9 Hz

question: A capacitor of 70 uF is charged to 75 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 70, V = 75 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*70e-6*(75)^2 | Answer: 196.9 mJ

question: An alternating voltage has a peak value of 288 V. Find its RMS value.
solution: Given: Vp = 288 | Formula: Vrms = Vp / sqrt(2) | Substitute: Vrms = 288 / sqrt(2) | Answer: 203.6 V

question: A transformer has primary voltage 180 V with 510 primary turns and 230 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 180, N1 = 510, N2 = 230 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 180 * 230/510 | Answer: 81.18 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 320 V and draws an armature current of 29 A. If the armature resistance is 0.86 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 320, Ia = 29, Ra = 0.86 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 320 - 29*0.86 | Answer: 295.1 V

question: A 8-pole induction motor on a 60 Hz supply runs at 790 rpm. Find the slip (%).
formula: s = (Ns - N) / Ns,  Ns = 120 f / P

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 25 A at 415 V (line) with a power factor of 0.77. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 25, VL = 415, pf = 0.77 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*415*25*0.77 / 1000 | Answer: 13.84 kW

question: A load has real power 140 kW and apparent power 190 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 140, S = 190 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 140 / 190 | Answer: 0.7368

question: A machine delivers 190 kW output while drawing 202 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 190, Pi = 202 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 190/202 * 100 | Answer: 94.06 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 11 V across R1 = 39 ohm and R2 = 45 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 11, R1 = 39, R2 = 45 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 11*45 / (39+45) | Answer: 5.893 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 10 kohm and Rin = 5 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 10, Rin = 5 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 10 / 5 | Answer: 2

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 120 kohm and Rg = 38 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 120, Rg = 38 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 120/38 | Answer: 4.158

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 305. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 305 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(305) | Answer: 24.84 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 3.1 m carries a central point load of 55 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.1, W = 55 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 55*3.1 / 4 | Answer: 42.62 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.3 m carries a UDL of 30 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 9.3, w = 30 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 30*(9.3)^2 / 8 | Answer: 324.3 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 3.9 m carries a point load 15 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.9, W = 15 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 15*3.9 | Answer: 58.5 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 5.4 m carries a UDL of 40 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.4, w = 40 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 40*(5.4)^2 / 2 | Answer: 583.2 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 7.7 m carries a point load 45 kN at distance 3 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 7.7, a = 3, W = 45 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 45*(7.7 - 3) / 7.7 | Answer: 27.47 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 5.3 m) carries a central point load 60 kN. With E = 25 GPa and I = 190e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=60000 N, L=5300.0 mm, E=25000 MPa, I=190e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 39.18 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 7.5 m carries a UDL of 39 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7.5, w = 39 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 39*(7.5)^2 / 12 | Answer: 182.8 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 370 mm, clear cover 25 mm and main bars of diameter 16 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 370, c = 25, dia = 16 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 370 - 25 - 16/2 | Answer: 337 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 18.9 m^2 carrying a factored load of 16.8 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 18.9, w = 16.8 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 16.8 * 18.9 | Answer: 317.5 kN

question: For a bar of diameter 16 mm with design bond stress 2.2 MPa and steel stress 395 MPa, find the development length in mm.
solution: Given: dia = 16, tbd = 2.2, fs = 395 | Formula: Ld = phi fs / (4 tau_bd) | Substitute: Ld = 16*395 / (4*2.2) | Answer: 718.2 mm

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 6.1 m, unit weight 20 kN/m^3, phi = 29 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 5.6 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 18 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 5.6, g = 18 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (18 - 9.81)*5.6 | Answer: 45.86 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 1.9e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1.4, area = 6.8e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 1.9, i = 1.4, A = 6.8 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (1.9e-4)*1.4*(6.8e-3) | Answer: 1809 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 2 m, bed slope 0.003 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.016. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 2.4 m under a head of 1.2 m. Taking Cd = 0.62 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 2.7 m wide carries a discharge of 27.7 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 390 m and design speed 60 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 390, V = 60 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (60)^2 / (127*390) | Answer: 0.07268
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: For a design speed of 95 km/h with allowable superelevation 0.08 and lateral friction 0.15, find the minimum curve radius in m.
A tank of volume 370 m^3 treats a flow of 190 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 370, Q = 190 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 370 / 190 | Answer: 1.947 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 320 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.11 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 8 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 320, k = 0.11, t = 8 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 320*(1 - e^(-0.11*8)) | Answer: 187.3 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.79, rainfall intensity 85 mm/h over a catchment of 10.1 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.79, i = 85, A = 10.1 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.79*85*10.1 / 360 | Answer: 1.884 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.04 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 370 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.04, M = 370 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 370*(20+0.04)/20 | Answer: 370.7 m

formula: Repeatedly divide by 2 and read remainders bottom-up

solution: Divide 3032 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: BD8 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the 8-bit binary number 10101000 to decimal.
solution: Binary 10101000 = sum of bit-weights | Answer: 168 (decimal)
formula: Sum each bit times its positional weight (2^i)

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 11100011 and 10001011.
solution: XOR: 01101000 | Count of 1s = 3 | Answer: 3
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 940 megabits is sent over a link of 40 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 940, B = 40 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 940 / 40 | Answer: 23.5 s

question: A link has bandwidth 17 Mbps and round-trip time 200 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 17, R = 200 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 17e6 * 200e-3 bits = 3400 kb | Answer: 3400 kilobits

question: A channel has bandwidth 5 kHz. Using Nyquist's theorem with 8 signal levels, find the maximum data rate in kbps (noiseless).
solution: Given: B = 5, M = 8 | Formula: C = 2 B log2(M) | Substitute: C = 2*5*log2(8) | Answer: 30 kbps

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.95, cache access time 9 ns and main-memory access time 160 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.95, tc = 9, tm = 160 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.95*9 + (1 - 0.95)*160 | Answer: 16.55 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 930959 elements?
solution: Given: n = 930959 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(930959)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: An O(n^2) algorithm performs c*n^2 basic operations. If c = 1 and n = 1230, how many operations are performed?
solution: Given: n = 1230 | Formula: operations = n^2 | Substitute: = (1230)^2 | Answer: 1512900

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.006, memory access time 160 ns and page-fault service time 10 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 10 ms = 10000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.006)*160 + 0.006*10000000.0 ns | Answer: 60.16 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 1.3 m^3 at 240 kPa and 600 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 1.3, P = 240, Tk = 600 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (240e3)*1.3 / (8.314*600) | Answer: 62.55 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.1 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 7 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.1, t = 7 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.1*7) | Answer: 0.5034

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.33 /min) is to reach 55% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.33, X = 55 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.55) / 0.33 | Answer: 2.42 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.13 /min) reaches 55% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.13, X = 55 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.55 / (0.13*(1 - 0.55)) | Answer: 9.402 min

question: For a reaction with A = 2e10 /s and activation energy 55 kJ/mol at 340 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 2, Ea = 55, Tk = 340 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 2e10 * exp(-55e3 / (8.314*340)) | Answer: 70.96 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.96 and bottoms xW = 0.09, with relative volatility alpha = 3. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.96, xw = 0.09, al = 3 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.96/0.04)(0.91/0.09)] / ln(3) | Answer: 4.999 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.75 and x = 0.37. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.75, x = 0.37 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.75/0.25) / (0.37/0.63) | Answer: 5.108

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.51 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 75 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.51, Psat = 75 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.51 * 75 | Answer: 38.25 kPa

question: A stream of 3.7 kg/s with specific heat 2.8 kJ/kg-K is heated through 20 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 3.7, cp = 2.8, dT = 20 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 3.7*2.8*20 | Answer: 207.2 kW

question: A reactor of volume 9.3 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 3.3 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 9.3, Q = 3.3 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 9.3 / 3.3 | Answer: 2.818 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 7e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 1 mm with a concentration difference of 50 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 7, L = 1, dC = 50 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (7e-9)*50 / (1e-3) | Answer: 350 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 4.6 min and steady-state gain 2.2. For a step input of magnitude 6, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 4.6, K = 2.2, M = 6 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 2.2 * 6 | Answer: 13.2 units

question: A reactor operates at a space time of 7.9 min. Find its space velocity in per hour.
solution: Given: tau = 7.9 | Formula: SV = 60 / tau  (per hour) | Substitute: SV = 60 / 7.9 | Answer: 7.595 /h

question: An aircraft wing of area 75 m^2 flies at 250 m/s (air density 1.225 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.9. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 75, V = 250, rho = 1.225, CL = 0.9 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1.225*(250)^2*75*0.9 / 1000 | Answer: 2584 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 35 m^2 flies at 190 m/s (density 0.7 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.05. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 35, V = 190, rho = 0.7, CD = 0.05 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.7*(190)^2*35*0.05 / 1000 | Answer: 22.11 kN

question: An aircraft flies at 530 m/s where the speed of sound is 295 m/s. Find the Mach number.
solution: Given: V = 530, a = 295 | Formula: M = V / a | Substitute: M = 530 / 295 | Answer: 1.797

question: A specimen under stress 370 MPa shows an elastic strain of 2.3e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 370, eps = 2.3 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 370 / (2.3e-3) MPa = 160.9 GPa | Answer: 160.9 GPa

question: A block of mass 25 kg has a volume of 0.9e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 25, V = 0.9 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 25 / (0.9e-3) | Answer: 27778 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 2300 mm is heated through 75 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 23e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 2300, dT = 75, al = 23 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 2300*23e-6*75 | Answer: 3.968 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 155 ohm, R2 = 140 ohm and R3 = 270 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 155, R2 = 140, R3 = 270 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 140*270 / 155 | Answer: 243.9 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 350 ohm and gauge factor 2 experiences a strain of 600e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 350, GF = 2, eps = 600 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 350*2*600e-6 | Answer: 420 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 9.72 when the true value is 20. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.72, true = 20 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.72 - 20| / 20 * 100 | Answer: 51.4 %

question: Annual demand is 15500 units, ordering cost 90 per order and holding cost 4 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 15500, S = 90, H = 4 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*15500*90 / 4) | Answer: 835.2 units

question: An asset costs 330000 with salvage value 34000 after 18 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 330000, Sv = 34000, n = 18 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (330000 - 34000) / 18 | Answer: 16444 per year

question: A product sells for 220 per unit with variable cost 60 per unit and fixed costs 30000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 220, V = 60, F = 30000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 30000 / (220 - 60) | Answer: 187.5 units

question: Find the present worth of 125000 received 2 years from now at an interest rate of 7% per year.
solution: Given: F = 125000, n = 2, i = 7 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 125000 / (1 + 0.07)^2 | Answer: 10918 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.97, 0.96 and 0.98 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.97, r2 = 0.96, r3 = 0.98 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.97*0.96*0.98 | Answer: 0.9126

question: A process produces 27 defective items in a batch of 10500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 27, N = 10500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 27/10500 * 1e6 | Answer: 2571 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -4x^3 + 5x + 9 evaluated at x = 1.
For f(x) = -2x^3 - 7x^2 + 4x - 7, find f''(x) at x = 5.
Evaluate the definite integral of (2x - 1) dx from x = -2 to x = 6.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = 0x^3/3 + 2x^2/2 + -1x | Evaluate F(6) - F(-2) | Answer: 24
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 4x^2 + 6x - 5 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[1, 8], [8, 5]].
solution: Given: a = 1, b = 8, c = 8, d = 5 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (1)(5) - (8)(8) | Answer: -59

question: Find the determinant of [[2, 3, 6], [-3, -3, 1], [5, 0, 0]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: 105

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[-2, -7], [-2, 0]].
solution: Trace tr = -2, Determinant = -14 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 2.873

question: Solve for x: 2x + -1y = -4 and -1x + 1y = -6.
solution: Determinant = 2*1 - -1*-1 = 1 | x = (e d - b f) / det = -10 | Answer: x = -10
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 77, 89, 89, 24, 74.
solution: Sum = 353 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 70.6 | Answer: 70.6

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 7, 36, 48, 25, 30.
solution: Mean = 29.2 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 15.09

question: Find the slope of the line through (-5, 5) and (5, 2).
solution: Given: x1 = -5, y1 = 5, x2 = 5, y2 = 2 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (2 - 5) / (5 - -5) | Answer: -0.3

question: Find the distance between the points (-4, 6) and (-1, 5).
solution: Given: x1 = -4, y1 = 6, x2 = -1, y2 = 5 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((3)^2 + (-1)^2) | Answer: 3.162 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (5,-2), (1,5), (-7,-8).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 54 sq units

question: Evaluate the number of combinations C(10, 4).
solution: Given: n = 10, r = 4 | Formula: C(n, r) = n! / (r! (n - r)!) | Substitute: C(10, 4) = 10! / (4! * 6!) | Answer: 210

question: Evaluate the number of permutations P(7, 7).
solution: Given: n = 7, r = 7 | Formula: P(n, r) = n! / (n - r)! | Substitute: P(7, 7) = 7! / 0! | Answer: 5040

question: Find the 8th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -9 and common difference -1.
solution: Given: a = -9, d = -1, n = 8 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -9 + (8 - 1)*-1 | Answer: -16

question: Find the sum of the first 33 terms of an AP with first term 10 and common difference -5.
solution: Given: a = 10, d = -5, n = 33 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 33/2 [2*10 + (33-1)*-5] | Answer: -2310

question: Find the 8th term of a geometric progression with first term 2 and common ratio 3.
solution: Given: a = 2, r = 3, n = 8 | Formula: a_n = a r^(n-1) | Substitute: a_n = 2 * 3^(8-1) | Answer: 4374

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 35500 at 13.2% per annum for 6 years.
solution: Given: P = 35500, R = 13.2, Tt = 6 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 35500 * 13.2 * 6 / 100 | Answer: 28116 currency units

question: Find the amount when 23500 is invested at 7.3% per annum compounded annually for 5 years.
solution: Given: P = 23500, R = 7.3, Tt = 5 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 23500 * (1 + 7.3/100)^5 | Answer: 33425 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (-4, -5, -1) and (-8, 4, 8).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (4, 0, -5) and (-5, 0, 6).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 1

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (2, 4, -5) and (4, 4, -3).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 24.78 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number -5 + -3i.
solution: Given: a = -5, b = -3 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((-5)^2 + (-3)^2) | Answer: 5.831

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number 4 + -5i.
solution: Given: a = 4, b = -5 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(-5, 4) | Answer: -51.34 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = 2x^3 - x^2 - 6x - 1 at x = -5.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-65 with initial guess x0=2, find x1 (one iteration).
solution: Given: N = 65, x0 = 2 | Formula: x1 = x0 - (x0^2 - N)/(2 x0) | Substitute: x1 = 2 - ((2)^2 - 65)/(2*2) | Answer: 17.25

question: Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.9 and ordinates 5, 0, 2, 20, 16, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 65 and 141.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 65 and 141 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 25 and 40.
solution: Given: a = 25, b = 40 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 25*40 / 5 | Answer: 200
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 22 mm carries an axial tensile load of 70 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 33 mm and length 1400 mm carries an axial load of 56 kN. Take E = 70 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 71 mm transmits a torque of 2450 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 71, Tt = 2450 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(2450*1000) / (pi*(71)^3) | Answer: 34.86 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 29 mm and length 1800 mm carries a torque of 1900 N-m. With G = 77 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (29)^4 / 32 = 69437 mm^4 | theta = (1900*1000)(1800) / (77000 * 69437) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 36.65 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 134 mm wide and 200 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 134, h = 200 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 134*(200)^2 / 6 | Answer: 893333 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (77 mm x 170 mm) carries a bending moment of 4 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (37 mm x 100 mm) has effective length 2000 mm and E = 200 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 520 MPa is designed for a working stress of 200 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 520, sw = 200 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 520 / 200 | Answer: 2.6

question: A steel bar is fully restrained and heated through 65 deg C. With E = 210 GPa and alpha = 11e-6 /deg C, find the thermal stress in MPa.
solution: Given: dT = 65, E = 210, al = 11 | Formula: sigma = E alpha (dT) | Substitute: sigma = 210000 * 11e-6 * 65 | Answer: 150.2 MPa

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 500 mm and wall thickness 12 mm carries an internal pressure of 1.5 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 500, t = 12, P = 1.5 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 1.5*500 / (2*12) | Answer: 31.25 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 680 K and 340 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 680, Tc = 340 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 340/680) * 100 | Answer: 50 %

question: A refrigerator works between 269 K (cold) and 300 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 269, Th = 300 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 269 / (300 - 269) | Answer: 8.677

question: A heat pump operates between 269 K and 314 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 269, Th = 314 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 314 / (314 - 269) | Answer: 6.978

question: 7 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 160 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 7, dT = 160 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 7 * 0.718 * 160 | Answer: 804.2 kJ

question: 1.4 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 110 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1.4, dT = 110 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 1.4 * 1.005 * 110 | Answer: 154.8 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 2.1 m^3 at 360 K with mass 5.3 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 2.1, Tk = 360, m = 5.3 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 5.3*0.287*360 / 2.1 | Answer: 260.8 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 3.8 kg of air expands isothermally at 480 K from volume V1 to 2*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.8, Tk = 480, ratio = 2 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 3.8*0.287*480*ln(2) | Answer: 362.9 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 3.2 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.11 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 3.2, D = 0.11 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*3.2*0.11 / 0.001 | Answer: 352000

question: Water flows at 2 m/s through a pipe of diameter 200 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 3.5 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 3.5 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*3.5 / 1000 | Answer: 34.34 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 12.1 m. Taking Cv = 0.98, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 12.1, cv = 0.98 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.98*sqrt(2*9.81*12.1) | Answer: 15.1 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 380 mm) water flows at 1 m/s. It contracts to diameter 120 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 380, d2 = 120, V1 = 1 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 1*(380/120)^2 | Answer: 10.03 m/s

question: Water flows at 3.8 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.26 m and length 430 m. With friction factor f = 0.033, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 27 teeth drives a gear of 116 teeth. If the pinion runs at 850 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 27, z2 = 116, N1 = 850 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 850*27 / 116 | Answer: 197.8 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 550 mm rotates at 500 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 550, N = 500 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.55)*500 / 60 | Answer: 14.4 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 20.4 kW at 1450 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 20.4, N = 1450 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(20.4*1000) / (2*pi*1450) | Answer: 134.3 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 6.2 kg rotates at radius 0.19 m at 950 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 9100 N/m and mass 7.8 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 9100, m = 7.8 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(9100/7.8) | Answer: 5.436 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 9.9 m^2 and thickness 0.13 m has conductivity k = 13.5 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 30 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 9.9, L = 0.13, k = 13.5, dT = 30 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 13.5*9.9*30 / 0.13 | Answer: 30842 W

question: A surface of area 1.7 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 35 W/m^2-K to surroundings 90 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 1.7, h = 35, dT = 90 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 35*1.7*90 | Answer: 5355 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 220 m/min, feed = 0.43 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2.8 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 220, f = 0.43, d = 2.8 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*220*0.43*2.8 | Answer: 264880 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 360 mm is turned at 900 rpm with a feed of 0.25 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 360, N = 900, f = 0.25 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 360 / (0.25*900) | Answer: 1.6 min

question: A resistor of 5 ohm carries a current of 7.5 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 5, I = 7.5 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 7.5 * 5 | Answer: 37.5 V

question: Three resistors 16 ohm, 70 ohm and 15 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 16, R2 = 70, R3 = 15 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 16 + 70 + 15 | Answer: 101 ohm

question: Two resistors 49 ohm and 71 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 49, R2 = 71 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 49*71 / (49+71) | Answer: 28.99 ohm

question: A device draws 12.2 A at 15 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 15, I = 12.2 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 15 * 12.2 | Answer: 183 W

question: A current of 2.9 A flows through a 83 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 2.9, R = 83 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (2.9)^2 * 83 | Answer: 698 W

question: Two capacitors 6 uF and 7.7 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 6, C2 = 7.7 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 6*7.7 / (6+7.7) | Answer: 3.372 uF

question: A resistor 7 kohm and capacitor 10.2 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 7, C = 10.2 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (7k)(10.2u) = 71.4 ms | Answer: 71.4 ms

question: An inductor 320 mH is in series with 107 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 320, R = 107 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (320e-3) / 107 | Answer: 2.991 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 181.4 mH inductor at 930 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 181.4, f = 930 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (930)(181.4e-3) | Answer: 106 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 33.2 uF capacitor at 340 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 33.2, f = 340 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (340)(33.2e-6)) | Answer: 14.1 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 65 ohm, XL = 128 ohm and XC = 38 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 65, XL = 128, XC = 38 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(65^2 + (128 - 38)^2) | Answer: 111 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 10.5 mH and C = 3.1 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 10.5, C = 3.1 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(10.5e-3 * 3.1e-6)) | Answer: 882.2 Hz

question: A capacitor of 98.3 uF is charged to 50 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 98.3, V = 50 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*98.3e-6*(50)^2 | Answer: 122.9 mJ

question: An alternating voltage has a peak value of 120 V. Find its RMS value.
solution: Given: Vp = 120 | Formula: Vrms = Vp / sqrt(2) | Substitute: Vrms = 120 / sqrt(2) | Answer: 84.85 V

question: A transformer has primary voltage 360 V with 660 primary turns and 460 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 360, N1 = 660, N2 = 460 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 360 * 460/660 | Answer: 250.9 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 140 V and draws an armature current of 25 A. If the armature resistance is 1.02 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 140, Ia = 25, Ra = 1.02 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 140 - 25*1.02 | Answer: 114.5 V

question: A 8-pole induction motor on a 60 Hz supply runs at 890 rpm. Find the slip (%).
formula: s = (Ns - N) / Ns,  Ns = 120 f / P

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 150 A at 415 V (line) with a power factor of 0.95. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 150, VL = 415, pf = 0.95 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*415*150*0.95 / 1000 | Answer: 102.4 kW

question: A load has real power 45 kW and apparent power 45 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 45, S = 45 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 45 / 45 | Answer: 1

question: A machine delivers 50 kW output while drawing 202 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 50, Pi = 202 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 50/202 * 100 | Answer: 24.75 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 22 V across R1 = 31 ohm and R2 = 22 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 22, R1 = 31, R2 = 22 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 22*22 / (31+22) | Answer: 9.132 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 180 kohm and Rin = 14 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 180, Rin = 14 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 180 / 14 | Answer: 12.86

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 80 kohm and Rg = 10 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 80, Rg = 10 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 80/10 | Answer: 9

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 4800. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 4800 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(4800) | Answer: 36.81 dB

question: A first-order system has a time constant of 3.2 s. Find the time (in s) to reach 63.2% of its final value.
solution: For a first-order step response, y = 1 - e^(-t/tau) | y = 0.632 when t = tau | Answer: 3.2 s
formula: At t = tau the response reaches 63.2% (one time constant)

question: A signal is sampled at 16 kHz. According to the Nyquist criterion, what is the maximum signal frequency that can be represented (in kHz)?
solution: Given: fs = 16 | Formula: f_max = fs / 2 | Substitute: f_max = 16 / 2 | Answer: 8 kHz

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.7 m carries a central point load of 20 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.7, W = 20 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 20*4.7 / 4 | Answer: 23.5 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 5.3 m carries a UDL of 20 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.3, w = 20 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 20*(5.3)^2 / 8 | Answer: 70.22 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 2.9 m carries a point load 10 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 2.9, W = 10 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 10*2.9 | Answer: 29 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 3.4 m carries a UDL of 18 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.4, w = 18 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 18*(3.4)^2 / 2 | Answer: 104 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 7.1 m carries a point load 90 kN at distance 1.6 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 7.1, a = 1.6, W = 90 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 90*(7.1 - 1.6) / 7.1 | Answer: 69.72 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 7.7 m) carries a central point load 75 kN. With E = 30 GPa and I = 320e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=75000 N, L=7700.0 mm, E=30000 MPa, I=320e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 74.31 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 6 m carries a UDL of 27 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6, w = 27 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 27*(6)^2 / 12 | Answer: 81 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 450 mm, clear cover 30 mm and main bars of diameter 20 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 450, c = 30, dia = 20 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 450 - 30 - 20/2 | Answer: 410 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 23.5 m^2 carrying a factored load of 8.6 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 23.5, w = 8.6 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 8.6 * 23.5 | Answer: 202.1 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 6.8 m, unit weight 20 kN/m^3, phi = 31 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 4.4 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 19 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 4.4, g = 19 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (19 - 9.81)*4.4 | Answer: 40.44 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 5.1e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.9, area = 1.4e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 5.1, i = 0.9, A = 1.4 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (5.1e-4)*0.9*(1.4e-3) | Answer: 642.6 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 2.3 m, bed slope 0.002 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.026. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 1.5 m under a head of 0.9 m. Taking Cd = 0.63 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 2.6 m wide carries a discharge of 18.3 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 110 m and design speed 65 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 110, V = 65 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (65)^2 / (127*110) | Answer: 0.3024
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: For a design speed of 70 km/h with allowable superelevation 0.08 and lateral friction 0.13, find the minimum curve radius in m.
A tank of volume 220 m^3 treats a flow of 180 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 220, Q = 180 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 220 / 180 | Answer: 1.222 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 210 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.29 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 5 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 210, k = 0.29, t = 5 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 210*(1 - e^(-0.29*5)) | Answer: 160.7 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.69, rainfall intensity 60 mm/h over a catchment of 47.3 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.69, i = 60, A = 47.3 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.69*60*47.3 / 360 | Answer: 5.439 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.05 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 790 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.05, M = 790 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 790*(30+0.05)/30 | Answer: 791.3 m

question: Convert the decimal number 112 to binary.
solution: Divide 112 by 2 repeatedly, recording remainders | Reading remainders in reverse gives 1110000 | Answer: 1110000 (binary)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 2 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the decimal number 468 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 468 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 1D4 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the 8-bit binary number 00001001 to decimal.
solution: Binary 00001001 = sum of bit-weights | Answer: 9 (decimal)
formula: Sum each bit times its positional weight (2^i)

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 00111010 and 10100011.
solution: XOR: 10011001 | Count of 1s = 4 | Answer: 4
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 530 megabits is sent over a link of 85 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 530, B = 85 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 530 / 85 | Answer: 6.235 s

question: A link has bandwidth 62 Mbps and round-trip time 40 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 62, R = 40 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 62e6 * 40e-3 bits = 2480 kb | Answer: 2480 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.93, cache access time 1 ns and main-memory access time 70 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.93, tc = 1, tm = 70 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.93*1 + (1 - 0.93)*70 | Answer: 5.83 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 590820 elements?
solution: Given: n = 590820 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(590820)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: An O(n^2) algorithm performs c*n^2 basic operations. If c = 1 and n = 1120, how many operations are performed?
solution: Given: n = 1120 | Formula: operations = n^2 | Substitute: = (1120)^2 | Answer: 1254400

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.009, memory access time 150 ns and page-fault service time 6 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 6 ms = 6000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.009)*150 + 0.009*6000000.0 ns | Answer: 54.15 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 0.4 m^3 at 320 kPa and 300 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 0.4, P = 320, Tk = 300 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (320e3)*0.4 / (8.314*300) | Answer: 51.32 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.29 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 4 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.29, t = 4 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.29*4) | Answer: 0.6865

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.25 /min) is to reach 90% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.25, X = 90 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.9) / 0.25 | Answer: 9.21 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.42 /min) reaches 75% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.42, X = 75 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.75 / (0.42*(1 - 0.75)) | Answer: 7.143 min

question: For a reaction with A = 3e10 /s and activation energy 50 kJ/mol at 300 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 3, Ea = 50, Tk = 300 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 3e10 * exp(-50e3 / (8.314*300)) | Answer: 59.02 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.96 and bottoms xW = 0.08, with relative volatility alpha = 3.3. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.96, xw = 0.08, al = 3.3 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.96/0.04)(0.92/0.08)] / ln(3.3) | Answer: 4.708 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.71 and x = 0.3. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.71, x = 0.3 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.71/0.29) / (0.3/0.7) | Answer: 5.713

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.26 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 65 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.26, Psat = 65 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.26 * 65 | Answer: 16.9 kPa

question: A stream of 9.6 kg/s with specific heat 2.8 kJ/kg-K is heated through 25 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 9.6, cp = 2.8, dT = 25 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 9.6*2.8*25 | Answer: 672 kW

question: A reactor of volume 15.5 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 4.4 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 15.5, Q = 4.4 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 15.5 / 4.4 | Answer: 3.523 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 6.1e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 5 mm with a concentration difference of 40 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 6.1, L = 5, dC = 40 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (6.1e-9)*40 / (5e-3) | Answer: 48.8 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 4.5 min and steady-state gain 3.2. For a step input of magnitude 18, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 4.5, K = 3.2, M = 18 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 3.2 * 18 | Answer: 57.6 units

question: A reactor operates at a space time of 15.2 min. Find its space velocity in per hour.
solution: Given: tau = 15.2 | Formula: SV = 60 / tau  (per hour) | Substitute: SV = 60 / 15.2 | Answer: 3.947 /h

question: An aircraft wing of area 25 m^2 flies at 170 m/s (air density 0.4 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.9. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 25, V = 170, rho = 0.4, CL = 0.9 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.4*(170)^2*25*0.9 / 1000 | Answer: 130.1 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 30 m^2 flies at 230 m/s (density 0.4 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.03. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 30, V = 230, rho = 0.4, CD = 0.03 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.4*(230)^2*30*0.03 / 1000 | Answer: 9.522 kN

question: An aircraft flies at 190 m/s where the speed of sound is 295 m/s. Find the Mach number.
solution: Given: V = 190, a = 295 | Formula: M = V / a | Substitute: M = 190 / 295 | Answer: 0.6441

question: A specimen under stress 350 MPa shows an elastic strain of 1.9e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 350, eps = 1.9 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 350 / (1.9e-3) MPa = 184.2 GPa | Answer: 184.2 GPa

question: A block of mass 41 kg has a volume of 3.6e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 41, V = 3.6 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 41 / (3.6e-3) | Answer: 11389 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 2300 mm is heated through 145 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 11e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 2300, dT = 145, al = 11 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 2300*11e-6*145 | Answer: 3.668 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 10 ohm, R2 = 50 ohm and R3 = 30 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 10, R2 = 50, R3 = 30 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 50*30 / 10 | Answer: 150 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 350 ohm and gauge factor 2.1 experiences a strain of 950e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 350, GF = 2.1, eps = 950 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 350*2.1*950e-6 | Answer: 698.2 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 10.44 when the true value is 20. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10.44, true = 20 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10.44 - 20| / 20 * 100 | Answer: 47.8 %

question: Annual demand is 35000 units, ordering cost 230 per order and holding cost 35 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 35000, S = 230, H = 35 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*35000*230 / 35) | Answer: 678.2 units

question: An asset costs 320000 with salvage value 30000 after 15 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 320000, Sv = 30000, n = 15 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (320000 - 30000) / 15 | Answer: 19333 per year

question: A product sells for 450 per unit with variable cost 200 per unit and fixed costs 60000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 450, V = 200, F = 60000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 60000 / (450 - 200) | Answer: 240 units

question: Find the present worth of 75000 received 6 years from now at an interest rate of 11% per year.
solution: Given: F = 75000, n = 6, i = 11 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 75000 / (1 + 0.11)^6 | Answer: 40098 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.95, 0.92 and 0.93 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.95, r2 = 0.92, r3 = 0.93 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.95*0.92*0.93 | Answer: 0.8128

question: A process produces 17 defective items in a batch of 2000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 17, N = 2000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 17/2000 * 1e6 | Answer: 8500 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -6x^3 - x^2 - 4x - 7 evaluated at x = 1.
For f(x) = -x^3 + 3x^2 + 5x + 6, find f''(x) at x = 1.
Evaluate the definite integral of (3x^2 + x - 4) dx from x = -3 to x = 3.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = 3x^3/3 + 1x^2/2 + -4x | Evaluate F(3) - F(-3) | Answer: 30
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 4x^2 - 5 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[4, -7], [5, -8]].
solution: Given: a = 4, b = -7, c = 5, d = -8 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (4)(-8) - (-7)(5) | Answer: 3

question: Find the determinant of [[-5, 5, 4], [3, -5, -2], [-2, -5, 5]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: 20

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[-7, -6], [-7, 6]].
solution: Trace tr = -1, Determinant = -84 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 8.679

question: Solve for x: -2x + 3y = -1 and 1x + -4y = -1.
solution: Determinant = -2*-4 - 3*1 = 5 | x = (e d - b f) / det = 1.4 | Answer: x = 1.4
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 52, 31, 96, 44, 85.
solution: Sum = 308 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 61.6 | Answer: 61.6

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 21, 6, 34, 43, 26.
solution: Mean = 26 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 13.95

question: Find the slope of the line through (-7, 5) and (5, -8).
solution: Given: x1 = -7, y1 = 5, x2 = 5, y2 = -8 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (-8 - 5) / (5 - -7) | Answer: -1.083

question: Find the distance between the points (4, 5) and (3, 5).
solution: Given: x1 = 4, y1 = 5, x2 = 3, y2 = 5 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-1)^2 + (0)^2) | Answer: 1 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (7,3), (-6,-3), (-6,1).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 26 sq units

question: Evaluate the number of combinations C(5, 2).
solution: Given: n = 5, r = 2 | Formula: C(n, r) = n! / (r! (n - r)!) | Substitute: C(5, 2) = 5! / (2! * 3!) | Answer: 10

question: Evaluate the number of permutations P(12, 1).
solution: Given: n = 12, r = 1 | Formula: P(n, r) = n! / (n - r)! | Substitute: P(12, 1) = 12! / 11! | Answer: 12

question: Find the 27th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -10 and common difference 5.
solution: Given: a = -10, d = 5, n = 27 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -10 + (27 - 1)*5 | Answer: 120

question: Find the sum of the first 39 terms of an AP with first term 5 and common difference -4.
solution: Given: a = 5, d = -4, n = 39 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 39/2 [2*5 + (39-1)*-4] | Answer: -2769

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 35500 at 6.6% per annum for 10 years.
solution: Given: P = 35500, R = 6.6, Tt = 10 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 35500 * 6.6 * 10 / 100 | Answer: 23430 currency units

question: Find the amount when 2000 is invested at 11.5% per annum compounded annually for 2 years.
solution: Given: P = 2000, R = 11.5, Tt = 2 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 2000 * (1 + 11.5/100)^2 | Answer: 2486 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (6, -7, -2) and (0, 1, -3).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 19

solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 106.8 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number -7 + 5i.
solution: Given: a = -7, b = 5 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((-7)^2 + (5)^2) | Answer: 8.602

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number -3 + -5i.
solution: Given: a = -3, b = -5 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(-5, -3) | Answer: -121 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -x^3 + 7x^2 + 4x at x = 3.
solution: Given: a = -1, b = 7, c = 4, d = 0, x0 = 3 | Formula: f(x0) = a x0^3 + b x0^2 + c x0 + d | Substitute: f(3) = -1(3)^3 + 7(3)^2 + 4(3) + 0 | Answer: 48

question: Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-146 with initial guess x0=5, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.1 and ordinates 2, 18, 15, 1, 11, estimate the integral.
