solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 392 and 429 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 54 and 60.
solution: Given: a = 54, b = 60 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 54*60 / 6 | Answer: 540
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 56 mm carries an axial tensile load of 35 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 16 mm and length 2600 mm carries an axial load of 46 kN. Take E = 210 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 34 mm transmits a torque of 2350 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 34, Tt = 2350 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(2350*1000) / (pi*(34)^3) | Answer: 304.5 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 33 mm and length 1100 mm carries a torque of 850 N-m. With G = 45 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (33)^4 / 32 = 116428 mm^4 | theta = (850*1000)(1100) / (45000 * 116428) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 10.23 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 134 mm wide and 240 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 134, h = 240 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 134*(240)^2 / 6 | Answer: 1286400 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (84 mm x 140 mm) carries a bending moment of 18 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (63 mm x 90 mm) has effective length 2100 mm and E = 200 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 420 MPa is designed for a working stress of 70 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 420, sw = 70 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 420 / 70 | Answer: 6

question: A steel bar is fully restrained and heated through 120 deg C. With E = 210 GPa and alpha = 13e-6 /deg C, find the thermal stress in MPa.
solution: Given: dT = 120, E = 210, al = 13 | Formula: sigma = E alpha (dT) | Substitute: sigma = 210000 * 13e-6 * 120 | Answer: 327.6 MPa

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1150 mm and wall thickness 14 mm carries an internal pressure of 2.4 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1150, t = 14, P = 2.4 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 2.4*1150 / (2*14) | Answer: 98.57 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 680 K and 280 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 680, Tc = 280 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 280/680) * 100 | Answer: 58.82 %

question: A refrigerator works between 251 K (cold) and 314 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 251, Th = 314 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 251 / (314 - 251) | Answer: 3.984

question: A heat pump operates between 265 K and 314 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 265, Th = 314 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 314 / (314 - 265) | Answer: 6.408

question: 4.5 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 30 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.5, dT = 30 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 4.5 * 0.718 * 30 | Answer: 96.93 kJ

question: 3 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 75 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3, dT = 75 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 3 * 1.005 * 75 | Answer: 226.1 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 0.9 m^3 at 480 K with mass 1.1 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 0.9, Tk = 480, m = 1.1 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 1.1*0.287*480 / 0.9 | Answer: 168.4 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 2.7 kg of air expands isothermally at 380 K from volume V1 to 4*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.7, Tk = 380, ratio = 4 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 2.7*0.287*380*ln(4) | Answer: 408.2 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 3.1 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.07 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 3.1, D = 0.07 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*3.1*0.07 / 0.001 | Answer: 217000

question: Water flows at 2.5 m/s through a pipe of diameter 260 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 1.1 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 1.1 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*1.1 / 1000 | Answer: 10.79 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 10.5 m. Taking Cv = 0.96, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 10.5, cv = 0.96 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.96*sqrt(2*9.81*10.5) | Answer: 13.78 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 390 mm) water flows at 1.8 m/s. It contracts to diameter 100 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
Water flows at 3.4 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.28 m and length 420 m. With friction factor f = 0.033, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 26 teeth drives a gear of 54 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1350 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 26, z2 = 54, N1 = 1350 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1350*26 / 54 | Answer: 650 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 290 mm rotates at 350 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 290, N = 350 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.29)*350 / 60 | Answer: 5.315 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 12.4 kW at 200 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 12.4, N = 200 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(12.4*1000) / (2*pi*200) | Answer: 592.1 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 1.5 kg rotates at radius 0.37 m at 300 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 8400 N/m and mass 2.1 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 8400, m = 2.1 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(8400/2.1) | Answer: 10.07 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 8.8 m^2 and thickness 0.36 m has conductivity k = 5.3 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 35 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 8.8, L = 0.36, k = 5.3, dT = 35 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 5.3*8.8*35 / 0.36 | Answer: 4534 W

question: A surface of area 1 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 10 W/m^2-K to surroundings 145 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 1, h = 10, dT = 145 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 10*1*145 | Answer: 1450 W

question: In a counter-flow heat exchanger the terminal temperature differences are 55 deg C and 25 deg C. Find the log mean temperature difference (LMTD) in deg C.
solution: Given: dT1 = 55, dT2 = 25 | Formula: LMTD = (dT1 - dT2) / ln(dT1/dT2) | Substitute: LMTD = (55 - 25) / ln(55/25) | Answer: 38.05 deg C

question: In turning, cutting speed = 200 m/min, feed = 0.43 mm/rev, depth of cut = 1.2 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 200, f = 0.43, d = 1.2 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*200*0.43*1.2 | Answer: 103200 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 380 mm is turned at 400 rpm with a feed of 0.17 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 380, N = 400, f = 0.17 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 380 / (0.17*400) | Answer: 5.588 min

question: A resistor of 86 ohm carries a current of 8.7 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 86, I = 8.7 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 8.7 * 86 | Answer: 748.2 V

question: Three resistors 98 ohm, 52 ohm and 67 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 98, R2 = 52, R3 = 67 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 98 + 52 + 67 | Answer: 217 ohm

question: Two resistors 2 ohm and 90 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 2, R2 = 90 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 2*90 / (2+90) | Answer: 1.957 ohm

question: A device draws 5.1 A at 50 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 50, I = 5.1 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 50 * 5.1 | Answer: 255 W

question: A current of 6.6 A flows through a 68 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 6.6, R = 68 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (6.6)^2 * 68 | Answer: 2962 W

question: Two capacitors 46.3 uF and 30.6 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 46.3, C2 = 30.6 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 46.3*30.6 / (46.3+30.6) | Answer: 18.42 uF

question: A resistor 62 kohm and capacitor 14.1 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 62, C = 14.1 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (62k)(14.1u) = 874.2 ms | Answer: 874.2 ms

question: An inductor 199.6 mH is in series with 101 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 199.6, R = 101 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (199.6e-3) / 101 | Answer: 1.976 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 188.3 mH inductor at 880 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 188.3, f = 880 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (880)(188.3e-3) | Answer: 1041 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 18.2 uF capacitor at 210 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 18.2, f = 210 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (210)(18.2e-6)) | Answer: 41.64 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 70 ohm, XL = 28 ohm and XC = 135 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 70, XL = 28, XC = 135 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(70^2 + (28 - 135)^2) | Answer: 127.9 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 34.9 mH and C = 7.7 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 34.9, C = 7.7 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(34.9e-3 * 7.7e-6)) | Answer: 307 Hz

question: A capacitor of 92.1 uF is charged to 250 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 92.1, V = 250 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*92.1e-6*(250)^2 | Answer: 2878 mJ

question: An alternating voltage has a peak value of 174 V. Find its RMS value.
solution: Given: Vp = 174 | Formula: Vrms = Vp / sqrt(2) | Substitute: Vrms = 174 / sqrt(2) | Answer: 123 V

question: A transformer has primary voltage 270 V with 490 primary turns and 140 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 270, N1 = 490, N2 = 140 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 270 * 140/490 | Answer: 77.14 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 180 V and draws an armature current of 59 A. If the armature resistance is 1.21 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 180, Ia = 59, Ra = 1.21 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 180 - 59*1.21 | Answer: 108.6 V

question: A 6-pole induction motor on a 50 Hz supply runs at 800 rpm. Find the slip (%).
formula: s = (Ns - N) / Ns,  Ns = 120 f / P

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 65 A at 415 V (line) with a power factor of 0.78. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 65, VL = 415, pf = 0.78 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*415*65*0.78 / 1000 | Answer: 36.44 kW

question: A load has real power 130 kW and apparent power 205 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 130, S = 205 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 130 / 205 | Answer: 0.6341

question: A machine delivers 40 kW output while drawing 47 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 40, Pi = 47 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 40/47 * 100 | Answer: 85.11 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 5 V across R1 = 41 ohm and R2 = 35 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 5, R1 = 41, R2 = 35 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 5*35 / (41+35) | Answer: 2.303 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 220 kohm and Rin = 47 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 220, Rin = 47 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 220 / 47 | Answer: 4.681

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 70 kohm and Rg = 44 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 70, Rg = 44 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 70/44 | Answer: 2.591

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 3580. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 3580 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(3580) | Answer: 35.54 dB

question: A first-order system has a time constant of 3.5 s. Find the time (in s) to reach 63.2% of its final value.
solution: For a first-order step response, y = 1 - e^(-t/tau) | y = 0.632 when t = tau | Answer: 3.5 s
formula: At t = tau the response reaches 63.2% (one time constant)

question: A signal is sampled at 140 kHz. According to the Nyquist criterion, what is the maximum signal frequency that can be represented (in kHz)?
solution: Given: fs = 140 | Formula: f_max = fs / 2 | Substitute: f_max = 140 / 2 | Answer: 70 kHz

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.6 m carries a central point load of 80 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6.6, W = 80 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 80*6.6 / 4 | Answer: 132 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 7.5 m carries a UDL of 50 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7.5, w = 50 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 50*(7.5)^2 / 8 | Answer: 351.6 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 1.8 m carries a point load 55 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 1.8, W = 55 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 55*1.8 | Answer: 99 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 5.4 m carries a UDL of 22 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.4, w = 22 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 22*(5.4)^2 / 2 | Answer: 320.8 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.4 m carries a point load 80 kN at distance 1.2 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 9.4, a = 1.2, W = 80 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 80*(9.4 - 1.2) / 9.4 | Answer: 69.79 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 3.8 m) carries a central point load 65 kN. With E = 200 GPa and I = 560e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=65000 N, L=3800.0 mm, E=200000 MPa, I=560e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 0.6634 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 7.6 m carries a UDL of 12 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7.6, w = 12 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 12*(7.6)^2 / 12 | Answer: 57.76 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 430 mm, clear cover 45 mm and main bars of diameter 20 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 430, c = 45, dia = 20 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 430 - 45 - 20/2 | Answer: 375 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 35.6 m^2 carrying a factored load of 17.4 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 35.6, w = 17.4 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 17.4 * 35.6 | Answer: 619.4 kN

question: For a bar of diameter 25 mm with design bond stress 2.3 MPa and steel stress 360 MPa, find the development length in mm.
solution: Given: dia = 25, tbd = 2.3, fs = 360 | Formula: Ld = phi fs / (4 tau_bd) | Substitute: Ld = 25*360 / (4*2.3) | Answer: 978.3 mm

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 6.2 m, unit weight 20 kN/m^3, phi = 28 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 2.1 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 19 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 2.1, g = 19 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (19 - 9.81)*2.1 | Answer: 19.3 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 2.6e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1.3, area = 4e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 2.6, i = 1.3, A = 4 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (2.6e-4)*1.3*(4e-3) | Answer: 1352 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 2.2 m, bed slope 0.002 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.023. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 1.1 m under a head of 0.6 m. Taking Cd = 0.63 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 4.9 m wide carries a discharge of 5.4 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 440 m and design speed 85 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 440, V = 85 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (85)^2 / (127*440) | Answer: 0.1293
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: For a design speed of 75 km/h with allowable superelevation 0.06 and lateral friction 0.13, find the minimum curve radius in m.
A tank of volume 280 m^3 treats a flow of 180 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 280, Q = 180 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 280 / 180 | Answer: 1.556 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 170 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.29 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 4 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 170, k = 0.29, t = 4 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 170*(1 - e^(-0.29*4)) | Answer: 116.7 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.61, rainfall intensity 100 mm/h over a catchment of 44.5 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.61, i = 100, A = 44.5 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.61*100*44.5 / 360 | Answer: 7.54 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.06 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 480 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.06, M = 480 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 480*(30+0.06)/30 | Answer: 481 m

question: Convert the decimal number 21 to binary.
solution: Divide 21 by 2 repeatedly, recording remainders | Reading remainders in reverse gives 10101 | Answer: 10101 (binary)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 2 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the decimal number 741 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 741 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 2E5 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the 8-bit binary number 00110001 to decimal.
solution: Binary 00110001 = sum of bit-weights | Answer: 49 (decimal)
formula: Sum each bit times its positional weight (2^i)

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 11001101 and 00100011.
solution: XOR: 11101110 | Count of 1s = 6 | Answer: 6
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 780 megabits is sent over a link of 50 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 780, B = 50 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 780 / 50 | Answer: 15.6 s

question: A link has bandwidth 65 Mbps and round-trip time 130 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 65, R = 130 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 65e6 * 130e-3 bits = 8450 kb | Answer: 8450 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.82, cache access time 7 ns and main-memory access time 180 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.82, tc = 7, tm = 180 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.82*7 + (1 - 0.82)*180 | Answer: 38.14 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 884397 elements?
solution: Given: n = 884397 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(884397)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: An O(n^2) algorithm performs c*n^2 basic operations. If c = 1 and n = 1520, how many operations are performed?
solution: Given: n = 1520 | Formula: operations = n^2 | Substitute: = (1520)^2 | Answer: 2310400

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.006, memory access time 140 ns and page-fault service time 10 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 10 ms = 10000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.006)*140 + 0.006*10000000.0 ns | Answer: 60.14 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 2 m^3 at 230 kPa and 550 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 2, P = 230, Tk = 550 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (230e3)*2 / (8.314*550) | Answer: 100.6 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.25 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 15 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.25, t = 15 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.25*15) | Answer: 0.9765

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.27 /min) is to reach 75% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.27, X = 75 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.75) / 0.27 | Answer: 5.134 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.23 /min) reaches 70% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.23, X = 70 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.7 / (0.23*(1 - 0.7)) | Answer: 10.14 min

question: For a reaction with A = 6e10 /s and activation energy 70 kJ/mol at 470 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 6, Ea = 70, Tk = 470 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 6e10 * exp(-70e3 / (8.314*470)) | Answer: 996 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.97 and bottoms xW = 0.1, with relative volatility alpha = 3.2. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.97, xw = 0.1, al = 3.2 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.97/0.03)(0.9/0.1)] / ln(3.2) | Answer: 4.878 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.79 and x = 0.5. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.79, x = 0.5 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.79/0.21) / (0.5/0.5) | Answer: 3.762

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.51 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 110 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.51, Psat = 110 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.51 * 110 | Answer: 56.1 kPa

question: A stream of 8.9 kg/s with specific heat 1.2 kJ/kg-K is heated through 70 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 8.9, cp = 1.2, dT = 70 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 8.9*1.2*70 | Answer: 747.6 kW

question: A reactor of volume 10.8 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 0.6 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 10.8, Q = 0.6 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 10.8 / 0.6 | Answer: 18 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 3.4e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 4 mm with a concentration difference of 140 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 3.4, L = 4, dC = 140 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (3.4e-9)*140 / (4e-3) | Answer: 119 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 7.8 min and steady-state gain 2.4. For a step input of magnitude 2, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 7.8, K = 2.4, M = 2 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 2.4 * 2 | Answer: 4.8 units

question: A reactor operates at a space time of 17.2 min. Find its space velocity in per hour.
solution: Given: tau = 17.2 | Formula: SV = 60 / tau  (per hour) | Substitute: SV = 60 / 17.2 | Answer: 3.488 /h

question: An aircraft wing of area 65 m^2 flies at 120 m/s (air density 0.7 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.4. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 65, V = 120, rho = 0.7, CL = 0.4 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.7*(120)^2*65*0.4 / 1000 | Answer: 131 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 20 m^2 flies at 260 m/s (density 0.4 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.08. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 20, V = 260, rho = 0.4, CD = 0.08 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.4*(260)^2*20*0.08 / 1000 | Answer: 21.63 kN

question: An aircraft flies at 360 m/s where the speed of sound is 310 m/s. Find the Mach number.
solution: Given: V = 360, a = 310 | Formula: M = V / a | Substitute: M = 360 / 310 | Answer: 1.161

question: A specimen under stress 110 MPa shows an elastic strain of 1.7e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 110, eps = 1.7 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 110 / (1.7e-3) MPa = 64.71 GPa | Answer: 64.71 GPa

question: A block of mass 41 kg has a volume of 3.1e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 41, V = 3.1 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 41 / (3.1e-3) | Answer: 13226 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 800 mm is heated through 40 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 12e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 800, dT = 40, al = 12 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 800*12e-6*40 | Answer: 0.384 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 35 ohm, R2 = 150 ohm and R3 = 150 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 35, R2 = 150, R3 = 150 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 150*150 / 35 | Answer: 642.9 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 120 ohm and gauge factor 2.1 experiences a strain of 1550e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 120, GF = 2.1, eps = 1550 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 120*2.1*1550e-6 | Answer: 390.6 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 10.6 when the true value is 50. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10.6, true = 50 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10.6 - 50| / 50 * 100 | Answer: 78.8 %

question: Annual demand is 35500 units, ordering cost 100 per order and holding cost 7 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 35500, S = 100, H = 7 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*35500*100 / 7) | Answer: 1007 units

question: An asset costs 490000 with salvage value 36000 after 10 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 490000, Sv = 36000, n = 10 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (490000 - 36000) / 10 | Answer: 45400 per year

question: A product sells for 340 per unit with variable cost 30 per unit and fixed costs 195000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 340, V = 30, F = 195000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 195000 / (340 - 30) | Answer: 629 units

question: Find the present worth of 145000 received 8 years from now at an interest rate of 6% per year.
solution: Given: F = 145000, n = 8, i = 6 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 145000 / (1 + 0.06)^8 | Answer: 90975 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.9, 0.94 and 0.93 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.9, r2 = 0.94, r3 = 0.93 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.9*0.94*0.93 | Answer: 0.7868

question: A process produces 45 defective items in a batch of 4000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 45, N = 4000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 45/4000 * 1e6 | Answer: 11250 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = 5x^3 - 2x^2 + 8x evaluated at x = 2.
For f(x) = 3x^3 + 2x^2 + 2x + 7, find f''(x) at x = -2.
Evaluate the definite integral of (-x^2 - 3x - 1) dx from x = 0 to x = 7.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = -1x^3/3 + -3x^2/2 + -1x | Evaluate F(7) - F(0) | Answer: -194.8
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of x^2 + 6x + 5 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[-6, -5], [9, -7]].
solution: Given: a = -6, b = -5, c = 9, d = -7 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (-6)(-7) - (-5)(9) | Answer: 87

question: Find the determinant of [[-4, 1, 1], [-5, 3, 4], [-4, -6, -5]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: -35

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[5, -6], [-7, 7]].
solution: Trace tr = 12, Determinant = -7 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 12.56

question: Solve for x: 2x + -6y = -8 and -5x + -1y = -9.
solution: Determinant = 2*-1 - -6*-5 = -32 | x = (e d - b f) / det = 1.438 | Answer: x = 1.438
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 37, 54, 35, 31, 88.
solution: Sum = 245 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 49 | Answer: 49

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 12, 28, 3, 30, 46.
solution: Mean = 23.8 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 16.74

question: Find the slope of the line through (-5, -5) and (5, 0).
solution: Given: x1 = -5, y1 = -5, x2 = 5, y2 = 0 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (0 - -5) / (5 - -5) | Answer: 0.5

question: Find the distance between the points (-7, 5) and (6, -1).
solution: Given: x1 = -7, y1 = 5, x2 = 6, y2 = -1 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((13)^2 + (-6)^2) | Answer: 14.32 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (2,4), (-4,-1), (-1,0).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 4.5 sq units

question: Evaluate the number of combinations C(19, 3).
solution: Given: n = 19, r = 3 | Formula: C(n, r) = n! / (r! (n - r)!) | Substitute: C(19, 3) = 19! / (3! * 16!) | Answer: 969

question: Find the 15th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -11 and common difference -7.
solution: Given: a = -11, d = -7, n = 15 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -11 + (15 - 1)*-7 | Answer: -109

question: Find the sum of the first 14 terms of an AP with first term -1 and common difference 8.
solution: Given: a = -1, d = 8, n = 14 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 14/2 [2*-1 + (14-1)*8] | Answer: 714

question: Find the 5th term of a geometric progression with first term 5 and common ratio 2.
solution: Given: a = 5, r = 2, n = 5 | Formula: a_n = a r^(n-1) | Substitute: a_n = 5 * 2^(5-1) | Answer: 80

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 6500 at 8.7% per annum for 9 years.
solution: Given: P = 6500, R = 8.7, Tt = 9 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 6500 * 8.7 * 9 / 100 | Answer: 5089 currency units

question: Find the amount when 34500 is invested at 6.2% per annum compounded annually for 6 years.
solution: Given: P = 34500, R = 6.2, Tt = 6 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 34500 * (1 + 6.2/100)^6 | Answer: 49496 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (0, 7, -8) and (-2, 4, 1).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (6, -5, 4) and (3, 5, 6).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 71.42

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (6, 2, -6) and (-5, 1, 6).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 158.8 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number 8 + -9i.
solution: Given: a = 8, b = -9 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((8)^2 + (-9)^2) | Answer: 12.04

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number -10 + 3i.
solution: Given: a = -10, b = 3 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(3, -10) | Answer: 163.3 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -5x^3 + 6x^2 + 4x - 6 at x = 2.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-180 with initial guess x0=8, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.4 and ordinates 5, 11, 17, 2, 14, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 177 and 495.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 177 and 495 | Answer: GCD = 3

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 15 and 29.
solution: Given: a = 15, b = 29 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 15*29 / 1 | Answer: 435
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 37 mm carries an axial tensile load of 55 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 36 mm and length 1800 mm carries an axial load of 12 kN. Take E = 70 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 74 mm transmits a torque of 2250 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 74, Tt = 2250 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(2250*1000) / (pi*(74)^3) | Answer: 28.28 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 60 mm and length 800 mm carries a torque of 1200 N-m. With G = 80 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (60)^4 / 32 = 1272345 mm^4 | theta = (1200*1000)(800) / (80000 * 1272345) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 0.5404 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 52 mm wide and 220 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 52, h = 220 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 52*(220)^2 / 6 | Answer: 419467 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (49 mm x 230 mm) carries a bending moment of 32 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (37 mm x 160 mm) has effective length 1900 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 660 MPa is designed for a working stress of 110 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 660, sw = 110 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 660 / 110 | Answer: 6

question: A steel bar is fully restrained and heated through 115 deg C. With E = 200 GPa and alpha = 12e-6 /deg C, find the thermal stress in MPa.
solution: Given: dT = 115, E = 200, al = 12 | Formula: sigma = E alpha (dT) | Substitute: sigma = 200000 * 12e-6 * 115 | Answer: 276 MPa

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1100 mm and wall thickness 14 mm carries an internal pressure of 1.8 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1100, t = 14, P = 1.8 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 1.8*1100 / (2*14) | Answer: 70.71 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 1100 K and 400 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 1100, Tc = 400 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 400/1100) * 100 | Answer: 63.64 %

question: A refrigerator works between 267 K (cold) and 300 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 267, Th = 300 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 267 / (300 - 267) | Answer: 8.091

question: A heat pump operates between 279 K and 304 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 279, Th = 304 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 304 / (304 - 279) | Answer: 12.16

question: 8 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 100 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 8, dT = 100 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 8 * 0.718 * 100 | Answer: 574.4 kJ

question: 2 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 130 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2, dT = 130 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 2 * 1.005 * 130 | Answer: 261.3 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 3.3 m^3 at 420 K with mass 2.8 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 3.3, Tk = 420, m = 2.8 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 2.8*0.287*420 / 3.3 | Answer: 102.3 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 2.7 kg of air expands isothermally at 450 K from volume V1 to 2*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.7, Tk = 450, ratio = 2 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 2.7*0.287*450*ln(2) | Answer: 241.7 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 1.5 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.06 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 1.5, D = 0.06 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*1.5*0.06 / 0.001 | Answer: 90000

question: Water flows at 3.2 m/s through a pipe of diameter 250 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 9.3 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 9.3 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*9.3 / 1000 | Answer: 91.23 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 1.8 m. Taking Cv = 0.96, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 1.8, cv = 0.96 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.96*sqrt(2*9.81*1.8) | Answer: 5.705 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 270 mm) water flows at 2.2 m/s. It contracts to diameter 80 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 270, d2 = 80, V1 = 2.2 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 2.2*(270/80)^2 | Answer: 25.06 m/s

question: Water flows at 2.6 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.17 m and length 390 m. With friction factor f = 0.034, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 16 teeth drives a gear of 117 teeth. If the pinion runs at 300 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 16, z2 = 117, N1 = 300 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 300*16 / 117 | Answer: 41.03 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 300 mm rotates at 1450 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 300, N = 1450 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.3)*1450 / 60 | Answer: 22.78 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 20 kW at 1000 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 20, N = 1000 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(20*1000) / (2*pi*1000) | Answer: 191 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 8.3 kg rotates at radius 0.34 m at 600 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 19400 N/m and mass 20 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 19400, m = 20 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(19400/20) | Answer: 4.957 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 9 m^2 and thickness 0.12 m has conductivity k = 3.3 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 35 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 9, L = 0.12, k = 3.3, dT = 35 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 3.3*9*35 / 0.12 | Answer: 8662 W

question: A surface of area 2.2 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 95 W/m^2-K to surroundings 95 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 2.2, h = 95, dT = 95 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 95*2.2*95 | Answer: 19855 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 100 m/min, feed = 0.23 mm/rev, depth of cut = 1.5 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 100, f = 0.23, d = 1.5 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*100*0.23*1.5 | Answer: 34500 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 210 mm is turned at 1150 rpm with a feed of 0.1 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 210, N = 1150, f = 0.1 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 210 / (0.1*1150) | Answer: 1.826 min

question: A resistor of 145 ohm carries a current of 7.2 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 145, I = 7.2 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 7.2 * 145 | Answer: 1044 V

question: Three resistors 65 ohm, 6 ohm and 8 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 65, R2 = 6, R3 = 8 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 65 + 6 + 8 | Answer: 79 ohm

question: Two resistors 46 ohm and 11 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 46, R2 = 11 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 46*11 / (46+11) | Answer: 8.877 ohm

question: A device draws 10.1 A at 10 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 10, I = 10.1 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 10 * 10.1 | Answer: 101 W

question: A current of 6.6 A flows through a 75 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 6.6, R = 75 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (6.6)^2 * 75 | Answer: 3267 W

question: Two capacitors 31.3 uF and 4.7 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 31.3, C2 = 4.7 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 31.3*4.7 / (31.3+4.7) | Answer: 4.086 uF

question: A resistor 84 kohm and capacitor 13.9 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 84, C = 13.9 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (84k)(13.9u) = 1168 ms | Answer: 1168 ms

question: An inductor 307.3 mH is in series with 168 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 307.3, R = 168 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (307.3e-3) / 168 | Answer: 1.829 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 124.9 mH inductor at 100 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 124.9, f = 100 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (100)(124.9e-3) | Answer: 78.48 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 18.5 uF capacitor at 860 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 18.5, f = 860 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (860)(18.5e-6)) | Answer: 10 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 38 ohm, XL = 66 ohm and XC = 21 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 38, XL = 66, XC = 21 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(38^2 + (66 - 21)^2) | Answer: 58.9 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 29.4 mH and C = 5.8 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 29.4, C = 5.8 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(29.4e-3 * 5.8e-6)) | Answer: 385.4 Hz

question: A capacitor of 29.7 uF is charged to 165 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 29.7, V = 165 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*29.7e-6*(165)^2 | Answer: 404.3 mJ

question: An alternating voltage has a peak value of 110 V. Find its RMS value.
solution: Given: Vp = 110 | Formula: Vrms = Vp / sqrt(2) | Substitute: Vrms = 110 / sqrt(2) | Answer: 77.78 V

question: A transformer has primary voltage 260 V with 730 primary turns and 160 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 260, N1 = 730, N2 = 160 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 260 * 160/730 | Answer: 56.99 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 330 V and draws an armature current of 24 A. If the armature resistance is 1.17 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 330, Ia = 24, Ra = 1.17 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 330 - 24*1.17 | Answer: 301.9 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 110 A at 415 V (line) with a power factor of 0.92. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 110, VL = 415, pf = 0.92 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*415*110*0.92 / 1000 | Answer: 72.74 kW

question: A load has real power 95 kW and apparent power 190 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 95, S = 190 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 95 / 190 | Answer: 0.5

question: A machine delivers 135 kW output while drawing 202 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 135, Pi = 202 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 135/202 * 100 | Answer: 66.83 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 29 V across R1 = 1 ohm and R2 = 49 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 29, R1 = 1, R2 = 49 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 29*49 / (1+49) | Answer: 28.42 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 20 kohm and Rin = 37 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 20, Rin = 37 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 20 / 37 | Answer: 0.5405

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 30 kohm and Rg = 22 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 30, Rg = 22 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 30/22 | Answer: 2.364

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 967. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 967 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(967) | Answer: 29.85 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.2 m carries a central point load of 50 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 9.2, W = 50 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 50*9.2 / 4 | Answer: 115 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.3 m carries a UDL of 55 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 9.3, w = 55 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 55*(9.3)^2 / 8 | Answer: 594.6 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 5.8 m carries a point load 70 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.8, W = 70 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 70*5.8 | Answer: 406 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 1.7 m carries a UDL of 6 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 1.7, w = 6 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 6*(1.7)^2 / 2 | Answer: 8.67 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 7.3 m carries a point load 90 kN at distance 2.7 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 7.3, a = 2.7, W = 90 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 90*(7.3 - 2.7) / 7.3 | Answer: 56.71 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 6.2 m) carries a central point load 10 kN. With E = 30 GPa and I = 210e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=10000 N, L=6200.0 mm, E=30000 MPa, I=210e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 7.881 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 7.3 m carries a UDL of 42 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7.3, w = 42 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 42*(7.3)^2 / 12 | Answer: 186.5 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 650 mm, clear cover 45 mm and main bars of diameter 12 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 650, c = 45, dia = 12 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 650 - 45 - 12/2 | Answer: 599 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 31.3 m^2 carrying a factored load of 12.7 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 31.3, w = 12.7 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 12.7 * 31.3 | Answer: 397.5 kN

question: For a bar of diameter 16 mm with design bond stress 2.3 MPa and steel stress 435 MPa, find the development length in mm.
solution: Given: dia = 16, tbd = 2.3, fs = 435 | Formula: Ld = phi fs / (4 tau_bd) | Substitute: Ld = 16*435 / (4*2.3) | Answer: 756.5 mm

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 4 m, unit weight 20 kN/m^3, phi = 38 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).

question: At a depth of 5.5 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 18 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 5.5, g = 18 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (18 - 9.81)*5.5 | Answer: 45.04 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 7.7e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.3, area = 5.3e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 7.7, i = 0.3, A = 5.3 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (7.7e-4)*0.3*(5.3e-3) | Answer: 1224 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 2.3 m, bed slope 0.002 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.017. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 2.1 m under a head of 0.5 m. Taking Cd = 0.64 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.

solution: Given: R = 530, V = 55 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (55)^2 / (127*530) | Answer: 0.04494

question: For a design speed of 55 km/h with allowable superelevation 0.06 and lateral friction 0.13, find the minimum curve radius in m.
A tank of volume 310 m^3 treats a flow of 130 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 340 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.34 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 4 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 340, k = 0.34, t = 4 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 340*(1 - e^(-0.34*4)) | Answer: 252.7 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.45, rainfall intensity 30 mm/h over a catchment of 36.3 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.45, i = 30, A = 36.3 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.45*30*36.3 / 360 | Answer: 1.361 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.03 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 530 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.03, M = 530 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 530*(20+0.03)/20 | Answer: 530.8 m

question: Convert the decimal number 180 to binary.
solution: Divide 180 by 2 repeatedly, recording remainders | Reading remainders in reverse gives 10110100 | Answer: 10110100 (binary)

question: Convert the decimal number 1875 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 1875 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 753 (hex)

solution: Binary 01010000 = sum of bit-weights | Answer: 80 (decimal)

question: A file of 430 megabits is sent over a link of 89 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 430, B = 89 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 430 / 89 | Answer: 4.831 s

question: A link has bandwidth 32 Mbps and round-trip time 160 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 32, R = 160 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 32e6 * 160e-3 bits = 5120 kb | Answer: 5120 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.92, cache access time 2 ns and main-memory access time 150 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.92, tc = 2, tm = 150 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.92*2 + (1 - 0.92)*150 | Answer: 13.84 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 26806 elements?
solution: Given: n = 26806 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(26806)) + 1 | Answer: 15

question: An O(n^2) algorithm performs c*n^2 basic operations. If c = 1 and n = 1710, how many operations are performed?
solution: Given: n = 1710 | Formula: operations = n^2 | Substitute: = (1710)^2 | Answer: 2924100

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.011, memory access time 180 ns and page-fault service time 8 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 8 ms = 8000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.011)*180 + 0.011*8000000.0 ns | Answer: 88.18 microseconds

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 0.6 m^3 at 330 kPa and 310 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 0.6, P = 330, Tk = 310 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (330e3)*0.6 / (8.314*310) | Answer: 76.82 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.2 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 3 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.2, t = 3 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.2*3) | Answer: 0.4512

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.22 /min) is to reach 75% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.22, X = 75 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.75) / 0.22 | Answer: 6.301 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.21 /min) reaches 80% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.21, X = 80 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.8 / (0.21*(1 - 0.8)) | Answer: 19.05 min

question: For a reaction with A = 2e10 /s and activation energy 55 kJ/mol at 450 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 2, Ea = 55, Tk = 450 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 2e10 * exp(-55e3 / (8.314*450)) | Answer: 8252 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.91 and bottoms xW = 0.09, with relative volatility alpha = 2.7. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.91, xw = 0.09, al = 2.7 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.91/0.09)(0.91/0.09)] / ln(2.7) | Answer: 4.659 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.89 and x = 0.4. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.89, x = 0.4 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.89/0.11) / (0.4/0.6) | Answer: 12.14

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.8 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 55 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.8, Psat = 55 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.8 * 55 | Answer: 44 kPa

question: A stream of 0.6 kg/s with specific heat 1.5 kJ/kg-K is heated through 115 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 0.6, cp = 1.5, dT = 115 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 0.6*1.5*115 | Answer: 103.5 kW

question: A reactor of volume 15.3 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 0.9 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 15.3, Q = 0.9 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 15.3 / 0.9 | Answer: 17 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 3.8e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 5 mm with a concentration difference of 80 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 3.8, L = 5, dC = 80 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (3.8e-9)*80 / (5e-3) | Answer: 60.8 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 1.2 min and steady-state gain 3.3. For a step input of magnitude 12, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 1.2, K = 3.3, M = 12 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 3.3 * 12 | Answer: 39.6 units

question: A reactor operates at a space time of 13.8 min. Find its space velocity in per hour.
solution: Given: tau = 13.8 | Formula: SV = 60 / tau  (per hour) | Substitute: SV = 60 / 13.8 | Answer: 4.348 /h

question: An aircraft wing of area 50 m^2 flies at 190 m/s (air density 0.4 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.8. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 50, V = 190, rho = 0.4, CL = 0.8 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.4*(190)^2*50*0.8 / 1000 | Answer: 288.8 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 60 m^2 flies at 130 m/s (density 1 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.12. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 60, V = 130, rho = 1, CD = 0.12 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*1*(130)^2*60*0.12 / 1000 | Answer: 60.84 kN

question: An aircraft flies at 400 m/s where the speed of sound is 295 m/s. Find the Mach number.
solution: Given: V = 400, a = 295 | Formula: M = V / a | Substitute: M = 400 / 295 | Answer: 1.356

question: A specimen under stress 150 MPa shows an elastic strain of 1.9e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 150, eps = 1.9 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 150 / (1.9e-3) MPa = 78.95 GPa | Answer: 78.95 GPa

question: A block of mass 17 kg has a volume of 4.8e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 17, V = 4.8 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 17 / (4.8e-3) | Answer: 3542 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 900 mm is heated through 20 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 17e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 900, dT = 20, al = 17 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 900*17e-6*20 | Answer: 0.306 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 30 ohm, R2 = 30 ohm and R3 = 125 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 30, R2 = 30, R3 = 125 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 30*125 / 30 | Answer: 125 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 120 ohm and gauge factor 2 experiences a strain of 950e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 120, GF = 2, eps = 950 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 120*2*950e-6 | Answer: 228 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 9.42 when the true value is 20. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.42, true = 20 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.42 - 20| / 20 * 100 | Answer: 52.9 %

question: Annual demand is 26000 units, ordering cost 250 per order and holding cost 37 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 26000, S = 250, H = 37 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*26000*250 / 37) | Answer: 592.7 units

question: An asset costs 460000 with salvage value 6000 after 8 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 460000, Sv = 6000, n = 8 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (460000 - 6000) / 8 | Answer: 56750 per year

question: A product sells for 230 per unit with variable cost 10 per unit and fixed costs 100000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 230, V = 10, F = 100000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 100000 / (230 - 10) | Answer: 454.5 units

question: Find the present worth of 50000 received 6 years from now at an interest rate of 10% per year.
solution: Given: F = 50000, n = 6, i = 10 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 50000 / (1 + 0.1)^6 | Answer: 28224 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.95, 0.97 and 0.91 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.95, r2 = 0.97, r3 = 0.91 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.95*0.97*0.91 | Answer: 0.8386

question: A process produces 20 defective items in a batch of 8500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 20, N = 8500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 20/8500 * 1e6 | Answer: 2353 PPM

question: Find the slope of the line through (5, -8) and (8, 5).

question: Find the distance between the points (-4, -8) and (-4, 1).

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (1,-5), (1,2), (5,5).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 14 sq units

question: Evaluate the number of combinations C(20, 4).

question: Evaluate the number of permutations P(15, 9).
solution: Given: n = 15, r = 9 | Formula: P(n, r) = n! / (n - r)! | Substitute: P(15, 9) = 15! / 6! | Answer: 1816214400

question: Find the 30th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 6 and common difference -7.
solution: Given: a = 6, d = -7, n = 30 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = 6 + (30 - 1)*-7 | Answer: -197

question: Find the sum of the first 16 terms of an AP with first term -8 and common difference 6.

question: Find the 6th term of a geometric progression with first term 6 and common ratio 3.
solution: Given: a = 6, r = 3, n = 6 | Formula: a_n = a r^(n-1) | Substitute: a_n = 6 * 3^(6-1) | Answer: 1458

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 31000 at 5.4% per annum for 3 years.
solution: Given: P = 31000, R = 5.4, Tt = 3 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 31000 * 5.4 * 3 / 100 | Answer: 5022 currency units

question: Find the amount when 6000 is invested at 7.1% per annum compounded annually for 4 years.
solution: Given: P = 6000, R = 7.1, Tt = 4 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 6000 * (1 + 7.1/100)^4 | Answer: 7894 currency units

question: Find the modulus of the complex number 0 + -9i.
solution: Given: a = 0, b = -9 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((0)^2 + (-9)^2) | Answer: 9

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number 3 + 4i.
solution: Given: a = 3, b = 4 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(4, 3) | Answer: 53.13 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -x^3 - x^2 + 8x - 1 at x = -5.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-167 with initial guess x0=7, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.3 and ordinates 18, 6, 10, 1, 12, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 579 and 70.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 579 and 70 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 76 and 57.
solution: Given: a = 76, b = 57 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 76*57 / 19 | Answer: 228
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 57 mm carries an axial tensile load of 18 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 29 mm and length 1900 mm carries an axial load of 81 kN. Take E = 70 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 63 mm transmits a torque of 2900 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 63, Tt = 2900 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(2900*1000) / (pi*(63)^3) | Answer: 59.07 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 51 mm and length 500 mm carries a torque of 1400 N-m. With G = 77 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (51)^4 / 32 = 664172 mm^4 | theta = (1400*1000)(500) / (77000 * 664172) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 0.7842 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 145 mm wide and 160 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 145, h = 160 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 145*(160)^2 / 6 | Answer: 618667 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (86 mm x 110 mm) carries a bending moment of 20 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (43 mm x 140 mm) has effective length 3900 mm and E = 200 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 600 MPa is designed for a working stress of 80 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 600, sw = 80 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 600 / 80 | Answer: 7.5

question: A steel bar is fully restrained and heated through 40 deg C. With E = 210 GPa and alpha = 11e-6 /deg C, find the thermal stress in MPa.
solution: Given: dT = 40, E = 210, al = 11 | Formula: sigma = E alpha (dT) | Substitute: sigma = 210000 * 11e-6 * 40 | Answer: 92.4 MPa

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 900 mm and wall thickness 15 mm carries an internal pressure of 0.9 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 900, t = 15, P = 0.9 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 0.9*900 / (2*15) | Answer: 27 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 760 K and 450 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 760, Tc = 450 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 450/760) * 100 | Answer: 40.79 %

question: A refrigerator works between 261 K (cold) and 324 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 261, Th = 324 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 261 / (324 - 261) | Answer: 4.143

question: A heat pump operates between 284 K and 302 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 284, Th = 302 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 302 / (302 - 284) | Answer: 16.78

question: 5 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 80 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 5, dT = 80 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 5 * 0.718 * 80 | Answer: 287.2 kJ

question: 4.1 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 160 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.1, dT = 160 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 4.1 * 1.005 * 160 | Answer: 659.3 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 2.8 m^3 at 330 K with mass 5.4 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 2.8, Tk = 330, m = 5.4 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 5.4*0.287*330 / 2.8 | Answer: 182.7 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 3.2 kg of air expands isothermally at 310 K from volume V1 to 4*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.2, Tk = 310, ratio = 4 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 3.2*0.287*310*ln(4) | Answer: 394.7 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 4.3 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.29 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 4.3, D = 0.29 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*4.3*0.29 / 0.001 | Answer: 1247000

question: Water flows at 3 m/s through a pipe of diameter 60 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 14.6 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 14.6 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*14.6 / 1000 | Answer: 143.2 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 12.6 m. Taking Cv = 0.98, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 12.6, cv = 0.98 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.98*sqrt(2*9.81*12.6) | Answer: 15.41 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 330 mm) water flows at 1.6 m/s. It contracts to diameter 120 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 330, d2 = 120, V1 = 1.6 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 1.6*(330/120)^2 | Answer: 12.1 m/s

question: Water flows at 3.9 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.36 m and length 240 m. With friction factor f = 0.031, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 15 teeth drives a gear of 56 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1200 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 15, z2 = 56, N1 = 1200 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1200*15 / 56 | Answer: 321.4 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 480 mm rotates at 1450 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 480, N = 1450 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.48)*1450 / 60 | Answer: 36.44 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 32.9 kW at 1200 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 32.9, N = 1200 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(32.9*1000) / (2*pi*1200) | Answer: 261.8 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 4.8 kg rotates at radius 0.11 m at 250 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 3900 N/m and mass 16.6 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 3900, m = 16.6 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(3900/16.6) | Answer: 2.439 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 9.5 m^2 and thickness 0.33 m has conductivity k = 12.2 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 50 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 9.5, L = 0.33, k = 12.2, dT = 50 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 12.2*9.5*50 / 0.33 | Answer: 17561 W

question: A surface of area 4.9 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 25 W/m^2-K to surroundings 135 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 4.9, h = 25, dT = 135 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 25*4.9*135 | Answer: 16538 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 60 m/min, feed = 0.37 mm/rev, depth of cut = 1.4 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 60, f = 0.37, d = 1.4 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*60*0.37*1.4 | Answer: 31080 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 190 mm is turned at 750 rpm with a feed of 0.12 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 190, N = 750, f = 0.12 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 190 / (0.12*750) | Answer: 2.111 min

question: A resistor of 189 ohm carries a current of 8.5 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 189, I = 8.5 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 8.5 * 189 | Answer: 1606 V

question: Three resistors 7 ohm, 19 ohm and 43 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 7, R2 = 19, R3 = 43 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 7 + 19 + 43 | Answer: 69 ohm

question: Two resistors 3 ohm and 109 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 3, R2 = 109 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 3*109 / (3+109) | Answer: 2.92 ohm

question: A device draws 10.9 A at 25 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 25, I = 10.9 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 25 * 10.9 | Answer: 272.5 W

question: A current of 3.7 A flows through a 97 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 3.7, R = 97 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (3.7)^2 * 97 | Answer: 1328 W

question: Two capacitors 46.1 uF and 15.5 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 46.1, C2 = 15.5 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 46.1*15.5 / (46.1+15.5) | Answer: 11.6 uF

question: A resistor 88 kohm and capacitor 7.5 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 88, C = 7.5 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (88k)(7.5u) = 660 ms | Answer: 660 ms

question: An inductor 108.9 mH is in series with 108 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 108.9, R = 108 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (108.9e-3) / 108 | Answer: 1.008 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 193.6 mH inductor at 990 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 193.6, f = 990 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (990)(193.6e-3) | Answer: 1204 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 47.6 uF capacitor at 270 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 47.6, f = 270 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (270)(47.6e-6)) | Answer: 12.38 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 39 ohm, XL = 102 ohm and XC = 128 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 39, XL = 102, XC = 128 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(39^2 + (102 - 128)^2) | Answer: 46.87 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 95.7 mH and C = 0.5 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 95.7, C = 0.5 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(95.7e-3 * 0.5e-6)) | Answer: 727.6 Hz

question: A capacitor of 43.5 uF is charged to 20 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 43.5, V = 20 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*43.5e-6*(20)^2 | Answer: 8.7 mJ

question: An alternating voltage has a peak value of 66 V. Find its RMS value.
solution: Given: Vp = 66 | Formula: Vrms = Vp / sqrt(2) | Substitute: Vrms = 66 / sqrt(2) | Answer: 46.67 V

question: A transformer has primary voltage 440 V with 550 primary turns and 80 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 440, N1 = 550, N2 = 80 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 440 * 80/550 | Answer: 64 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 270 V and draws an armature current of 26 A. If the armature resistance is 0.85 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 270, Ia = 26, Ra = 0.85 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 270 - 26*0.85 | Answer: 247.9 V

question: A 6-pole induction motor on a 50 Hz supply runs at 720 rpm. Find the slip (%).
formula: s = (Ns - N) / Ns,  Ns = 120 f / P

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 175 A at 433 V (line) with a power factor of 0.96. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 175, VL = 433, pf = 0.96 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*433*175*0.96 / 1000 | Answer: 126 kW

question: A load has real power 10 kW and apparent power 205 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 10, S = 205 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 10 / 205 | Answer: 0.04878

question: A machine delivers 45 kW output while drawing 157 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 45, Pi = 157 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 45/157 * 100 | Answer: 28.66 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 11 V across R1 = 4 ohm and R2 = 26 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 11, R1 = 4, R2 = 26 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 11*26 / (4+26) | Answer: 9.533 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 120 kohm and Rin = 9 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 120, Rin = 9 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 120 / 9 | Answer: 13.33

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 90 kohm and Rg = 1 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 90, Rg = 1 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 90/1 | Answer: 91

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 7018. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 7018 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(7018) | Answer: 38.46 dB

question: A signal is sampled at 64 kHz. According to the Nyquist criterion, what is the maximum signal frequency that can be represented (in kHz)?
solution: Given: fs = 64 | Formula: f_max = fs / 2 | Substitute: f_max = 64 / 2 | Answer: 32 kHz

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.3 m carries a central point load of 50 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6.3, W = 50 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 50*6.3 / 4 | Answer: 78.75 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 8.4 m carries a UDL of 25 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 8.4, w = 25 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 25*(8.4)^2 / 8 | Answer: 220.5 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 1.9 m carries a point load 5 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 1.9, W = 5 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 5*1.9 | Answer: 9.5 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 1.1 m carries a UDL of 8 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 1.1, w = 8 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 8*(1.1)^2 / 2 | Answer: 4.84 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 7 m carries a point load 30 kN at distance 3 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 7, a = 3, W = 30 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 30*(7 - 3) / 7 | Answer: 17.14 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 7.7 m) carries a central point load 15 kN. With E = 200 GPa and I = 490e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=15000 N, L=7700.0 mm, E=200000 MPa, I=490e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 1.456 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 7.6 m carries a UDL of 9 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7.6, w = 9 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 9*(7.6)^2 / 12 | Answer: 43.32 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 390 mm, clear cover 40 mm and main bars of diameter 12 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 390, c = 40, dia = 12 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 390 - 40 - 12/2 | Answer: 344 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 35 m^2 carrying a factored load of 18.7 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 35, w = 18.7 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 18.7 * 35 | Answer: 654.5 kN

question: For a bar of diameter 12 mm with design bond stress 2.2 MPa and steel stress 395 MPa, find the development length in mm.
solution: Given: dia = 12, tbd = 2.2, fs = 395 | Formula: Ld = phi fs / (4 tau_bd) | Substitute: Ld = 12*395 / (4*2.2) | Answer: 538.6 mm

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 3.2 m, unit weight 18 kN/m^3, phi = 32 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 11.8 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 19 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 11.8, g = 19 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (19 - 9.81)*11.8 | Answer: 108.4 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 6e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.6, area = 3.8e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 6, i = 0.6, A = 3.8 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (6e-4)*0.6*(3.8e-3) | Answer: 1368 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 0.9 m, bed slope 0.008 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.016. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 2.5 m under a head of 0.5 m. Taking Cd = 0.62 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)
