question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 83, 10, 24, 86, 87.
solution: Sum = 290 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 58 | Answer: 58

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 21, 34, 13, 45, 1.
solution: Mean = 22.8 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 17.27

question: Find the slope of the line through (0, 3) and (8, -2).
solution: Given: x1 = 0, y1 = 3, x2 = 8, y2 = -2 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (-2 - 3) / (8 - 0) | Answer: -0.625

question: Find the distance between the points (-2, -3) and (3, -6).
solution: Given: x1 = -2, y1 = -3, x2 = 3, y2 = -6 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((5)^2 + (-3)^2) | Answer: 5.831 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (-7,-5), (-3,0), (3,-5).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 25 sq units

question: Evaluate the number of combinations C(17, 3).
solution: Given: n = 17, r = 3 | Formula: C(n, r) = n! / (r! (n - r)!) | Substitute: C(17, 3) = 17! / (3! * 14!) | Answer: 680

question: Find the 32th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 7 and common difference -8.
solution: Given: a = 7, d = -8, n = 32 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = 7 + (32 - 1)*-8 | Answer: -241

question: Find the sum of the first 28 terms of an AP with first term -1 and common difference 2.
solution: Given: a = -1, d = 2, n = 28 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 28/2 [2*-1 + (28-1)*2] | Answer: 728

question: Find the 4th term of a geometric progression with first term 4 and common ratio 4.
solution: Given: a = 4, r = 4, n = 4 | Formula: a_n = a r^(n-1) | Substitute: a_n = 4 * 4^(4-1) | Answer: 256

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 31000 at 4.3% per annum for 3 years.
solution: Given: P = 31000, R = 4.3, Tt = 3 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 31000 * 4.3 * 3 / 100 | Answer: 3999 currency units

question: Find the amount when 35000 is invested at 9.9% per annum compounded annually for 6 years.
solution: Given: P = 35000, R = 9.9, Tt = 6 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 35000 * (1 + 9.9/100)^6 | Answer: 61667 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (7, -5, 1) and (-4, 3, 0).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (4, -2, 1) and (4, -5, 3).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 14.46

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (3, 3, 3) and (4, -6, 3).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 85.76 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number 12 + 7i.
solution: Given: a = 12, b = 7 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((12)^2 + (7)^2) | Answer: 13.89

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number -1 + 8i.
solution: Given: a = -1, b = 8 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(8, -1) | Answer: 97.13 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -2x^3 - 5x^2 - x at x = -4.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-40 with initial guess x0=8, find x1 (one iteration).
solution: Given: N = 40, x0 = 8 | Formula: x1 = x0 - (x0^2 - N)/(2 x0) | Substitute: x1 = 8 - ((8)^2 - 40)/(2*8) | Answer: 6.5

question: Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.8 and ordinates 17, 4, 17, 19, 17, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 388 and 196.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 388 and 196 | Answer: GCD = 4

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 43 and 56.
solution: Given: a = 43, b = 56 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 43*56 / 1 | Answer: 2408
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 38 mm carries an axial tensile load of 21 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 27 mm and length 2600 mm carries an axial load of 46 kN. Take E = 110 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 79 mm transmits a torque of 2700 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 79, Tt = 2700 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(2700*1000) / (pi*(79)^3) | Answer: 27.89 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 64 mm and length 600 mm carries a torque of 1950 N-m. With G = 77 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (64)^4 / 32 = 1647099 mm^4 | theta = (1950*1000)(600) / (77000 * 1647099) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 0.5286 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 108 mm wide and 210 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 108, h = 210 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 108*(210)^2 / 6 | Answer: 793800 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (41 mm x 120 mm) carries a bending moment of 26 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (33 mm x 110 mm) has effective length 2000 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 740 MPa is designed for a working stress of 180 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 740, sw = 180 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 740 / 180 | Answer: 4.111

question: A steel bar is fully restrained and heated through 120 deg C. With E = 210 GPa and alpha = 11e-6 /deg C, find the thermal stress in MPa.
solution: Given: dT = 120, E = 210, al = 11 | Formula: sigma = E alpha (dT) | Substitute: sigma = 210000 * 11e-6 * 120 | Answer: 277.2 MPa

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 950 mm and wall thickness 11 mm carries an internal pressure of 1.3 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 950, t = 11, P = 1.3 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 1.3*950 / (2*11) | Answer: 56.14 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 920 K and 400 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 920, Tc = 400 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 400/920) * 100 | Answer: 56.52 %

question: A refrigerator works between 260 K (cold) and 306 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 260, Th = 306 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 260 / (306 - 260) | Answer: 5.652

question: A heat pump operates between 278 K and 314 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 278, Th = 314 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 314 / (314 - 278) | Answer: 8.722

question: 4.9 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 65 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.9, dT = 65 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 4.9 * 0.718 * 65 | Answer: 228.7 kJ

question: 5.4 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 20 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 5.4, dT = 20 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 5.4 * 1.005 * 20 | Answer: 108.5 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 2.6 m^3 at 350 K with mass 3.6 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 2.6, Tk = 350, m = 3.6 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 3.6*0.287*350 / 2.6 | Answer: 139.1 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 2.3 kg of air expands isothermally at 330 K from volume V1 to 2*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.3, Tk = 330, ratio = 2 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 2.3*0.287*330*ln(2) | Answer: 151 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 1.8 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.26 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 1.8, D = 0.26 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*1.8*0.26 / 0.001 | Answer: 468000

question: Water flows at 1.6 m/s through a pipe of diameter 190 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 11.2 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 11.2 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*11.2 / 1000 | Answer: 109.9 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 6.7 m. Taking Cv = 0.96, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 6.7, cv = 0.96 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.96*sqrt(2*9.81*6.7) | Answer: 11.01 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 250 mm) water flows at 1.8 m/s. It contracts to diameter 100 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
Water flows at 3.9 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.34 m and length 130 m. With friction factor f = 0.025, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 22 teeth drives a gear of 105 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1350 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 22, z2 = 105, N1 = 1350 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1350*22 / 105 | Answer: 282.9 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 590 mm rotates at 1200 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 590, N = 1200 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.59)*1200 / 60 | Answer: 37.07 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 11.1 kW at 650 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 11.1, N = 650 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(11.1*1000) / (2*pi*650) | Answer: 163.1 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 4.4 kg rotates at radius 0.26 m at 300 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 18100 N/m and mass 10.8 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.

question: A plane wall of area 5 m^2 and thickness 0.17 m has conductivity k = 20.2 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 140 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 5, L = 0.17, k = 20.2, dT = 140 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 20.2*5*140 / 0.17 | Answer: 83176 W

question: A surface of area 4.3 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 105 W/m^2-K to surroundings 55 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 4.3, h = 105, dT = 55 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 105*4.3*55 | Answer: 24832 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 210 m/min, feed = 0.35 mm/rev, depth of cut = 1.9 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 210, f = 0.35, d = 1.9 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*210*0.35*1.9 | Answer: 139650 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 310 mm is turned at 500 rpm with a feed of 0.3 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 310, N = 500, f = 0.3 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 310 / (0.3*500) | Answer: 2.067 min

question: A resistor of 47 ohm carries a current of 4.2 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 47, I = 4.2 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 4.2 * 47 | Answer: 197.4 V

question: Three resistors 55 ohm, 19 ohm and 81 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 55, R2 = 19, R3 = 81 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 55 + 19 + 81 | Answer: 155 ohm

question: Two resistors 76 ohm and 100 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 76, R2 = 100 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 76*100 / (76+100) | Answer: 43.18 ohm

question: A device draws 6.2 A at 55 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 55, I = 6.2 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 55 * 6.2 | Answer: 341 W

question: A current of 8.6 A flows through a 2 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 8.6, R = 2 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (8.6)^2 * 2 | Answer: 147.9 W

question: Two capacitors 12 uF and 46.3 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 12, C2 = 46.3 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 12*46.3 / (12+46.3) | Answer: 9.53 uF

question: A resistor 12 kohm and capacitor 14.6 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 12, C = 14.6 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (12k)(14.6u) = 175.2 ms | Answer: 175.2 ms

question: An inductor 163.4 mH is in series with 152 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 163.4, R = 152 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (163.4e-3) / 152 | Answer: 1.075 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 23.4 mH inductor at 570 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 23.4, f = 570 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (570)(23.4e-3) | Answer: 83.81 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 3.9 uF capacitor at 960 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 3.9, f = 960 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (960)(3.9e-6)) | Answer: 42.51 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 92 ohm, XL = 125 ohm and XC = 149 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 92, XL = 125, XC = 149 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(92^2 + (125 - 149)^2) | Answer: 95.08 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 59.5 mH and C = 4 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 59.5, C = 4 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(59.5e-3 * 4e-6)) | Answer: 326.2 Hz

question: A capacitor of 56.4 uF is charged to 390 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 56.4, V = 390 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*56.4e-6*(390)^2 | Answer: 4289 mJ

question: An alternating voltage has a peak value of 98 V. Find its RMS value.
solution: Given: Vp = 98 | Formula: Vrms = Vp / sqrt(2) | Substitute: Vrms = 98 / sqrt(2) | Answer: 69.3 V

question: A transformer has primary voltage 380 V with 720 primary turns and 80 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 380, N1 = 720, N2 = 80 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 380 * 80/720 | Answer: 42.22 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 200 V and draws an armature current of 36 A. If the armature resistance is 0.8 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 200, Ia = 36, Ra = 0.8 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 200 - 36*0.8 | Answer: 171.2 V

question: A 6-pole induction motor on a 50 Hz supply runs at 930 rpm. Find the slip (%).
formula: s = (Ns - N) / Ns,  Ns = 120 f / P

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 185 A at 415 V (line) with a power factor of 0.96. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 185, VL = 415, pf = 0.96 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*415*185*0.96 / 1000 | Answer: 127.7 kW

question: A load has real power 35 kW and apparent power 90 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 35, S = 90 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 35 / 90 | Answer: 0.3889

question: A machine delivers 180 kW output while drawing 212 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 180, Pi = 212 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 180/212 * 100 | Answer: 84.91 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 14 V across R1 = 37 ohm and R2 = 11 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 14, R1 = 37, R2 = 11 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 14*11 / (37+11) | Answer: 3.208 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 50 kohm and Rin = 36 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 50, Rin = 36 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 50 / 36 | Answer: 1.389

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 80 kohm and Rg = 30 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 80, Rg = 30 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 80/30 | Answer: 3.667

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 4966. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 4966 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(4966) | Answer: 36.96 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 4 m carries a central point load of 20 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4, W = 20 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 20*4 / 4 | Answer: 20 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 5.7 m carries a UDL of 5 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.7, w = 5 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 5*(5.7)^2 / 8 | Answer: 20.31 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 1.7 m carries a point load 25 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 1.7, W = 25 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 25*1.7 | Answer: 42.5 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 5.3 m carries a UDL of 16 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.3, w = 16 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 16*(5.3)^2 / 2 | Answer: 224.7 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.1 m carries a point load 20 kN at distance 1.1 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 6.1, a = 1.1, W = 20 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 20*(6.1 - 1.1) / 6.1 | Answer: 16.39 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 6.9 m) carries a central point load 10 kN. With E = 25 GPa and I = 380e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=10000 N, L=6900.0 mm, E=25000 MPa, I=380e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 7.204 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 4.3 m carries a UDL of 33 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.3, w = 33 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 33*(4.3)^2 / 12 | Answer: 50.85 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 660 mm, clear cover 45 mm and main bars of diameter 16 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 660, c = 45, dia = 16 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 660 - 45 - 16/2 | Answer: 607 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 12.7 m^2 carrying a factored load of 14.6 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 12.7, w = 14.6 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 14.6 * 12.7 | Answer: 185.4 kN

question: For a bar of diameter 16 mm with design bond stress 1.7 MPa and steel stress 395 MPa, find the development length in mm.
solution: Given: dia = 16, tbd = 1.7, fs = 395 | Formula: Ld = phi fs / (4 tau_bd) | Substitute: Ld = 16*395 / (4*1.7) | Answer: 929.4 mm

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 6.9 m, unit weight 17 kN/m^3, phi = 33 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 2.8 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 19 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 2.8, g = 19 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (19 - 9.81)*2.8 | Answer: 25.73 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 4.3e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.8, area = 7.6e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 4.3, i = 0.8, A = 7.6 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (4.3e-4)*0.8*(7.6e-3) | Answer: 2614 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.4 m, bed slope 0.009 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.028. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 4.1 m under a head of 1.2 m. Taking Cd = 0.61 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 4 m wide carries a discharge of 28.9 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 150 m and design speed 50 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 150, V = 50 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (50)^2 / (127*150) | Answer: 0.1312
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: For a design speed of 40 km/h with allowable superelevation 0.06 and lateral friction 0.13, find the minimum curve radius in m.
A tank of volume 340 m^3 treats a flow of 135 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 340, Q = 135 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 340 / 135 | Answer: 2.519 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 180 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.3 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 5 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 180, k = 0.3, t = 5 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 180*(1 - e^(-0.3*5)) | Answer: 139.8 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.82, rainfall intensity 115 mm/h over a catchment of 45.9 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.82, i = 115, A = 45.9 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.82*115*45.9 / 360 | Answer: 12.02 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.08 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 520 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.08, M = 520 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 520*(20+0.08)/20 | Answer: 522.1 m

question: Convert the decimal number 116 to binary.
solution: Divide 116 by 2 repeatedly, recording remainders | Reading remainders in reverse gives 1110100 | Answer: 1110100 (binary)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 2 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the decimal number 1450 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 1450 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 5AA (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the 8-bit binary number 01010011 to decimal.
solution: Binary 01010011 = sum of bit-weights | Answer: 83 (decimal)
formula: Sum each bit times its positional weight (2^i)

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 01110000 and 10110001.
solution: XOR: 11000001 | Count of 1s = 3 | Answer: 3
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 920 megabits is sent over a link of 38 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 920, B = 38 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 920 / 38 | Answer: 24.21 s

question: A link has bandwidth 33 Mbps and round-trip time 120 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 33, R = 120 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 33e6 * 120e-3 bits = 3960 kb | Answer: 3960 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.95, cache access time 2 ns and main-memory access time 110 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.95, tc = 2, tm = 110 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.95*2 + (1 - 0.95)*110 | Answer: 7.4 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 181543 elements?
solution: Given: n = 181543 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(181543)) + 1 | Answer: 18

question: An O(n^2) algorithm performs c*n^2 basic operations. If c = 1 and n = 2710, how many operations are performed?
solution: Given: n = 2710 | Formula: operations = n^2 | Substitute: = (2710)^2 | Answer: 7344100

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.005, memory access time 180 ns and page-fault service time 5 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 5 ms = 5000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.005)*180 + 0.005*5000000.0 ns | Answer: 25.18 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 2.5 m^3 at 320 kPa and 480 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 2.5, P = 320, Tk = 480 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (320e3)*2.5 / (8.314*480) | Answer: 200.5 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.27 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 3 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.27, t = 3 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.27*3) | Answer: 0.5551

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.29 /min) is to reach 90% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.29, X = 90 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.9) / 0.29 | Answer: 7.94 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.18 /min) reaches 70% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.18, X = 70 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.7 / (0.18*(1 - 0.7)) | Answer: 12.96 min

question: For a reaction with A = 2e10 /s and activation energy 75 kJ/mol at 470 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 2, Ea = 75, Tk = 470 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 2e10 * exp(-75e3 / (8.314*470)) | Answer: 92.35 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.99 and bottoms xW = 0.05, with relative volatility alpha = 2.6. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.99, xw = 0.05, al = 2.6 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.99/0.01)(0.95/0.05)] / ln(2.6) | Answer: 7.891 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.86 and x = 0.46. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.86, x = 0.46 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.86/0.14) / (0.46/0.54) | Answer: 7.211

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.29 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 45 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.29, Psat = 45 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.29 * 45 | Answer: 13.05 kPa

question: A stream of 1.6 kg/s with specific heat 3.4 kJ/kg-K is heated through 95 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 1.6, cp = 3.4, dT = 95 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 1.6*3.4*95 | Answer: 516.8 kW

question: A reactor of volume 15.9 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 1.4 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 15.9, Q = 1.4 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 15.9 / 1.4 | Answer: 11.36 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 3.7e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 2 mm with a concentration difference of 20 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 3.7, L = 2, dC = 20 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (3.7e-9)*20 / (2e-3) | Answer: 37 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 2.6 min and steady-state gain 2.8. For a step input of magnitude 19, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 2.6, K = 2.8, M = 19 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 2.8 * 19 | Answer: 53.2 units

question: A reactor operates at a space time of 7.3 min. Find its space velocity in per hour.
solution: Given: tau = 7.3 | Formula: SV = 60 / tau  (per hour) | Substitute: SV = 60 / 7.3 | Answer: 8.219 /h

question: An aircraft wing of area 80 m^2 flies at 100 m/s (air density 1 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.9. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 80, V = 100, rho = 1, CL = 0.9 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1*(100)^2*80*0.9 / 1000 | Answer: 360 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 120 m^2 flies at 250 m/s (density 0.4 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.08. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 120, V = 250, rho = 0.4, CD = 0.08 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.4*(250)^2*120*0.08 / 1000 | Answer: 120 kN

question: An aircraft flies at 430 m/s where the speed of sound is 310 m/s. Find the Mach number.
solution: Given: V = 430, a = 310 | Formula: M = V / a | Substitute: M = 430 / 310 | Answer: 1.387

question: A specimen under stress 90 MPa shows an elastic strain of 2.3e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 90, eps = 2.3 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 90 / (2.3e-3) MPa = 39.13 GPa | Answer: 39.13 GPa

question: A block of mass 26 kg has a volume of 3e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 26, V = 3 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 26 / (3e-3) | Answer: 8667 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 800 mm is heated through 35 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 12e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 800, dT = 35, al = 12 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 800*12e-6*35 | Answer: 0.336 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 150 ohm, R2 = 130 ohm and R3 = 365 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 150, R2 = 130, R3 = 365 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 130*365 / 150 | Answer: 316.3 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 120 ohm and gauge factor 2.2 experiences a strain of 1800e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 120, GF = 2.2, eps = 1800 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 120*2.2*1800e-6 | Answer: 475.2 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 10.56 when the true value is 10. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10.56, true = 10 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10.56 - 10| / 10 * 100 | Answer: 5.6 %

question: Annual demand is 14500 units, ordering cost 270 per order and holding cost 31 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 14500, S = 270, H = 31 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*14500*270 / 31) | Answer: 502.6 units

question: An asset costs 160000 with salvage value 12000 after 13 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 160000, Sv = 12000, n = 13 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (160000 - 12000) / 13 | Answer: 11385 per year

question: A product sells for 340 per unit with variable cost 140 per unit and fixed costs 100000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 340, V = 140, F = 100000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 100000 / (340 - 140) | Answer: 500 units

question: Find the present worth of 70000 received 10 years from now at an interest rate of 7% per year.
solution: Given: F = 70000, n = 10, i = 7 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 70000 / (1 + 0.07)^10 | Answer: 35584 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.97, 0.93 and 0.95 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.97, r2 = 0.93, r3 = 0.95 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.97*0.93*0.95 | Answer: 0.857

question: A process produces 21 defective items in a batch of 11000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 21, N = 11000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 21/11000 * 1e6 | Answer: 1909 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -4x^3 - 3x^2 - 4x + 9 evaluated at x = -2.
For f(x) = -5x^3 - 2x^2 + 5x + 7, find f''(x) at x = -4.
Evaluate the definite integral of (4x^2 + 5x - 6) dx from x = -1 to x = 6.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = 4x^3/3 + 5x^2/2 + -6x | Evaluate F(6) - F(-1) | Answer: 334.8
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 5x^2 - 7x - 3 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[-6, -5], [2, -1]].
solution: Given: a = -6, b = -5, c = 2, d = -1 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (-6)(-1) - (-5)(2) | Answer: 16

question: Find the determinant of [[-4, -6, 3], [-2, -6, 6], [-3, 2, -6]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: 18

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[0, 1], [1, -5]].
solution: Trace tr = -5, Determinant = -1 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 0.1926

question: Solve for x: -2x + 4y = 7 and -5x + -4y = 8.
solution: Determinant = -2*-4 - 4*-5 = 28 | x = (e d - b f) / det = -2.143 | Answer: x = -2.143

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 19, 66, 76, 17, 5.
solution: Sum = 183 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 36.6 | Answer: 36.6

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 34, 21, 5, 32, 43.
solution: Mean = 27 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 14.58

question: Find the slope of the line through (1, 1) and (9, 4).
solution: Given: x1 = 1, y1 = 1, x2 = 9, y2 = 4 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (4 - 1) / (9 - 1) | Answer: 0.375

question: Find the distance between the points (-2, -1) and (4, -6).
solution: Given: x1 = -2, y1 = -1, x2 = 4, y2 = -6 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((6)^2 + (-5)^2) | Answer: 7.81 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (-6,0), (8,-1), (-3,-4).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 26.5 sq units

question: Evaluate the number of combinations C(13, 12).
solution: Given: n = 13, r = 12 | Formula: C(n, r) = n! / (r! (n - r)!) | Substitute: C(13, 12) = 13! / (12! * 1!) | Answer: 13

question: Find the 25th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 0 and common difference -8.
solution: Given: a = 0, d = -8, n = 25 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = 0 + (25 - 1)*-8 | Answer: -192

question: Find the sum of the first 21 terms of an AP with first term -6 and common difference -6.
solution: Given: a = -6, d = -6, n = 21 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 21/2 [2*-6 + (21-1)*-6] | Answer: -1386

question: Find the 3th term of a geometric progression with first term 3 and common ratio 4.
solution: Given: a = 3, r = 4, n = 3 | Formula: a_n = a r^(n-1) | Substitute: a_n = 3 * 4^(3-1) | Answer: 48

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 23000 at 13.6% per annum for 5 years.
solution: Given: P = 23000, R = 13.6, Tt = 5 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 23000 * 13.6 * 5 / 100 | Answer: 15640 currency units

question: Find the amount when 13000 is invested at 8.4% per annum compounded annually for 6 years.
solution: Given: P = 13000, R = 8.4, Tt = 6 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 13000 * (1 + 8.4/100)^6 | Answer: 21092 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (-3, -8, -4) and (-6, 3, 6).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (-4, 3, -1) and (3, -3, -3).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 19.44

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (-5, 3, 5) and (0, 2, 0).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 67.01 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number 3 + -6i.
solution: Given: a = 3, b = -6 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((3)^2 + (-6)^2) | Answer: 6.708

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number 2 + 4i.
solution: Given: a = 2, b = 4 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(4, 2) | Answer: 63.43 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = 5x^3 - x^2 - 2x + 9 at x = -4.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-17 with initial guess x0=3, find x1 (one iteration).
solution: Given: N = 17, x0 = 3 | Formula: x1 = x0 - (x0^2 - N)/(2 x0) | Substitute: x1 = 3 - ((3)^2 - 17)/(2*3) | Answer: 4.333

question: Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.5 and ordinates 14, 4, 3, 5, 17, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 324 and 522.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 324 and 522 | Answer: GCD = 18

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 64 and 21.
solution: Given: a = 64, b = 21 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 64*21 / 1 | Answer: 1344
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 29 mm carries an axial tensile load of 94 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 31 mm and length 1800 mm carries an axial load of 79 kN. Take E = 70 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 47 mm transmits a torque of 2100 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 47, Tt = 2100 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(2100*1000) / (pi*(47)^3) | Answer: 103 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 70 mm and length 1800 mm carries a torque of 1250 N-m. With G = 45 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (70)^4 / 32 = 2357176 mm^4 | theta = (1250*1000)(1800) / (45000 * 2357176) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 1.215 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 35 mm wide and 70 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 35, h = 70 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 35*(70)^2 / 6 | Answer: 28583 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (102 mm x 210 mm) carries a bending moment of 20 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (39 mm x 120 mm) has effective length 3400 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 740 MPa is designed for a working stress of 110 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 740, sw = 110 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 740 / 110 | Answer: 6.727

question: A steel bar is fully restrained and heated through 25 deg C. With E = 200 GPa and alpha = 12e-6 /deg C, find the thermal stress in MPa.
solution: Given: dT = 25, E = 200, al = 12 | Formula: sigma = E alpha (dT) | Substitute: sigma = 200000 * 12e-6 * 25 | Answer: 60 MPa

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1100 mm and wall thickness 10 mm carries an internal pressure of 2.5 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1100, t = 10, P = 2.5 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 2.5*1100 / (2*10) | Answer: 137.5 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 800 K and 360 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 800, Tc = 360 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 360/800) * 100 | Answer: 55 %

question: A refrigerator works between 251 K (cold) and 304 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 251, Th = 304 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 251 / (304 - 251) | Answer: 4.736

question: A heat pump operates between 267 K and 314 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 267, Th = 314 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 314 / (314 - 267) | Answer: 6.681

question: 3.6 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 65 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.6, dT = 65 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 3.6 * 0.718 * 65 | Answer: 168 kJ

question: 5 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 80 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 5, dT = 80 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 5 * 1.005 * 80 | Answer: 402 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 2.2 m^3 at 530 K with mass 2.7 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 2.2, Tk = 530, m = 2.7 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 2.7*0.287*530 / 2.2 | Answer: 186.7 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 3.4 kg of air expands isothermally at 300 K from volume V1 to 3*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.4, Tk = 300, ratio = 3 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 3.4*0.287*300*ln(3) | Answer: 321.6 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 2.6 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.09 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 2.6, D = 0.09 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*2.6*0.09 / 0.001 | Answer: 234000

question: Water flows at 2.3 m/s through a pipe of diameter 200 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 29.4 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 29.4 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*29.4 / 1000 | Answer: 288.4 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 3.4 m. Taking Cv = 0.97, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 3.4, cv = 0.97 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.97*sqrt(2*9.81*3.4) | Answer: 7.922 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 240 mm) water flows at 2.6 m/s. It contracts to diameter 100 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
Water flows at 2 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.45 m and length 430 m. With friction factor f = 0.026, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 34 teeth drives a gear of 55 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1150 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 34, z2 = 55, N1 = 1150 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1150*34 / 55 | Answer: 710.9 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 370 mm rotates at 1300 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 370, N = 1300 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.37)*1300 / 60 | Answer: 25.19 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 4.1 kW at 450 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 4.1, N = 450 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(4.1*1000) / (2*pi*450) | Answer: 87 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 10 kg rotates at radius 0.47 m at 250 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 18100 N/m and mass 15.4 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 18100, m = 15.4 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(18100/15.4) | Answer: 5.456 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 7.7 m^2 and thickness 0.36 m has conductivity k = 45.1 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 55 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 7.7, L = 0.36, k = 45.1, dT = 55 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 45.1*7.7*55 / 0.36 | Answer: 53055 W

question: A surface of area 3.3 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 120 W/m^2-K to surroundings 40 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 3.3, h = 120, dT = 40 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 120*3.3*40 | Answer: 15840 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 120 m/min, feed = 0.39 mm/rev, depth of cut = 0.9 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 120, f = 0.39, d = 0.9 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*120*0.39*0.9 | Answer: 42120 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 210 mm is turned at 700 rpm with a feed of 0.22 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 210, N = 700, f = 0.22 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 210 / (0.22*700) | Answer: 1.364 min

question: A resistor of 29 ohm carries a current of 1.5 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 29, I = 1.5 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 1.5 * 29 | Answer: 43.5 V

question: Three resistors 38 ohm, 26 ohm and 11 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 38, R2 = 26, R3 = 11 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 38 + 26 + 11 | Answer: 75 ohm

question: Two resistors 29 ohm and 87 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 29, R2 = 87 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 29*87 / (29+87) | Answer: 21.75 ohm

question: A device draws 0.4 A at 95 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 95, I = 0.4 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 95 * 0.4 | Answer: 38 W

question: A current of 3.1 A flows through a 89 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 3.1, R = 89 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (3.1)^2 * 89 | Answer: 855.3 W

question: Two capacitors 7.6 uF and 20.4 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 7.6, C2 = 20.4 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 7.6*20.4 / (7.6+20.4) | Answer: 5.537 uF

question: A resistor 28 kohm and capacitor 14.9 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 28, C = 14.9 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (28k)(14.9u) = 417.2 ms | Answer: 417.2 ms

question: An inductor 261.1 mH is in series with 151 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 261.1, R = 151 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (261.1e-3) / 151 | Answer: 1.729 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 98.8 mH inductor at 950 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 98.8, f = 950 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (950)(98.8e-3) | Answer: 589.7 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 48.7 uF capacitor at 320 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 48.7, f = 320 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (320)(48.7e-6)) | Answer: 10.21 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 74 ohm, XL = 16 ohm and XC = 20 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 74, XL = 16, XC = 20 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(74^2 + (16 - 20)^2) | Answer: 74.11 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 74.8 mH and C = 2.1 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 74.8, C = 2.1 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(74.8e-3 * 2.1e-6)) | Answer: 401.6 Hz

question: A capacitor of 92.6 uF is charged to 370 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 92.6, V = 370 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*92.6e-6*(370)^2 | Answer: 6338 mJ

question: An alternating voltage has a peak value of 282 V. Find its RMS value.
solution: Given: Vp = 282 | Formula: Vrms = Vp / sqrt(2) | Substitute: Vrms = 282 / sqrt(2) | Answer: 199.4 V

question: A transformer has primary voltage 250 V with 220 primary turns and 140 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 250, N1 = 220, N2 = 140 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 250 * 140/220 | Answer: 159.1 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 340 V and draws an armature current of 44 A. If the armature resistance is 0.23 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 340, Ia = 44, Ra = 0.23 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 340 - 44*0.23 | Answer: 329.9 V

question: A 4-pole induction motor on a 60 Hz supply runs at 920 rpm. Find the slip (%).
formula: s = (Ns - N) / Ns,  Ns = 120 f / P

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 135 A at 415 V (line) with a power factor of 0.79. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 135, VL = 415, pf = 0.79 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*415*135*0.79 / 1000 | Answer: 76.66 kW

question: A load has real power 80 kW and apparent power 150 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 80, S = 150 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 80 / 150 | Answer: 0.5333

question: A machine delivers 110 kW output while drawing 162 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 110, Pi = 162 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 110/162 * 100 | Answer: 67.9 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 24 V across R1 = 39 ohm and R2 = 29 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 24, R1 = 39, R2 = 29 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 24*29 / (39+29) | Answer: 10.24 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 220 kohm and Rin = 37 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 220, Rin = 37 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 220 / 37 | Answer: 5.946

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 40 kohm and Rg = 17 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 40, Rg = 17 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 40/17 | Answer: 3.353

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 3747. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 3747 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(3747) | Answer: 35.74 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.1 m carries a central point load of 60 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6.1, W = 60 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 60*6.1 / 4 | Answer: 91.5 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 8.5 m carries a UDL of 15 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 8.5, w = 15 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 15*(8.5)^2 / 8 | Answer: 135.5 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 2 m carries a point load 70 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 2, W = 70 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 70*2 | Answer: 140 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 5.5 m carries a UDL of 12 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.5, w = 12 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 12*(5.5)^2 / 2 | Answer: 181.5 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.6 m carries a point load 90 kN at distance 3.4 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 4.6, a = 3.4, W = 90 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 90*(4.6 - 3.4) / 4.6 | Answer: 23.48 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 6 m) carries a central point load 35 kN. With E = 25 GPa and I = 540e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=35000 N, L=6000.0 mm, E=25000 MPa, I=540e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 11.67 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 7.8 m carries a UDL of 12 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7.8, w = 12 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 12*(7.8)^2 / 12 | Answer: 60.84 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 570 mm, clear cover 50 mm and main bars of diameter 25 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 570, c = 50, dia = 25 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 570 - 50 - 25/2 | Answer: 507.5 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 35.5 m^2 carrying a factored load of 17.8 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 35.5, w = 17.8 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 17.8 * 35.5 | Answer: 631.9 kN

question: For a bar of diameter 16 mm with design bond stress 2 MPa and steel stress 360 MPa, find the development length in mm.
solution: Given: dia = 16, tbd = 2, fs = 360 | Formula: Ld = phi fs / (4 tau_bd) | Substitute: Ld = 16*360 / (4*2) | Answer: 720 mm

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 4.7 m, unit weight 19 kN/m^3, phi = 32 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 5.9 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 20 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 5.9, g = 20 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (20 - 9.81)*5.9 | Answer: 60.12 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 2.8e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1.3, area = 1.8e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 2.8, i = 1.3, A = 1.8 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (2.8e-4)*1.3*(1.8e-3) | Answer: 655.2 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 2.3 m, bed slope 0.009 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.02. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 4.9 m under a head of 0.6 m. Taking Cd = 0.61 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 5.9 m wide carries a discharge of 21.7 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 180 m and design speed 70 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 180, V = 70 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (70)^2 / (127*180) | Answer: 0.2143
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: For a design speed of 55 km/h with allowable superelevation 0.08 and lateral friction 0.14, find the minimum curve radius in m.
A tank of volume 140 m^3 treats a flow of 180 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 140, Q = 180 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 140 / 180 | Answer: 0.7778 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 190 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.1 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 3 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 190, k = 0.1, t = 3 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 190*(1 - e^(-0.1*3)) | Answer: 49.24 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.8, rainfall intensity 80 mm/h over a catchment of 29.9 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.8, i = 80, A = 29.9 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.8*80*29.9 / 360 | Answer: 5.316 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.04 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 570 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.04, M = 570 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 570*(30+0.04)/30 | Answer: 570.8 m

question: Convert the decimal number 192 to binary.
solution: Divide 192 by 2 repeatedly, recording remainders | Reading remainders in reverse gives 11000000 | Answer: 11000000 (binary)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 2 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the decimal number 1752 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 1752 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 6D8 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the 8-bit binary number 10001101 to decimal.
solution: Binary 10001101 = sum of bit-weights | Answer: 141 (decimal)
formula: Sum each bit times its positional weight (2^i)

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 01100111 and 01001001.
solution: XOR: 00101110 | Count of 1s = 4 | Answer: 4
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 630 megabits is sent over a link of 54 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 630, B = 54 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 630 / 54 | Answer: 11.67 s

question: A link has bandwidth 87 Mbps and round-trip time 80 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 87, R = 80 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 87e6 * 80e-3 bits = 6960 kb | Answer: 6960 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.92, cache access time 6 ns and main-memory access time 110 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.92, tc = 6, tm = 110 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.92*6 + (1 - 0.92)*110 | Answer: 14.32 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 663108 elements?
solution: Given: n = 663108 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(663108)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: An O(n^2) algorithm performs c*n^2 basic operations. If c = 1 and n = 800, how many operations are performed?
solution: Given: n = 800 | Formula: operations = n^2 | Substitute: = (800)^2 | Answer: 640000

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.002, memory access time 80 ns and page-fault service time 4 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 4 ms = 4000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.002)*80 + 0.002*4000000.0 ns | Answer: 8.08 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 2.1 m^3 at 460 kPa and 430 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 2.1, P = 460, Tk = 430 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (460e3)*2.1 / (8.314*430) | Answer: 270.2 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.13 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 4 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.13, t = 4 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.13*4) | Answer: 0.4055

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.23 /min) is to reach 50% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.23, X = 50 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.5) / 0.23 | Answer: 3.014 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.42 /min) reaches 85% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.42, X = 85 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.85 / (0.42*(1 - 0.85)) | Answer: 13.49 min

question: For a reaction with A = 9e10 /s and activation energy 80 kJ/mol at 350 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 9, Ea = 80, Tk = 350 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 9e10 * exp(-80e3 / (8.314*350)) | Answer: 0.1034 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.9 and bottoms xW = 0.03, with relative volatility alpha = 1.7. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.9, xw = 0.03, al = 1.7 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.9/0.1)(0.97/0.03)] / ln(1.7) | Answer: 10.69 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.72 and x = 0.26. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.72, x = 0.26 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.72/0.28) / (0.26/0.74) | Answer: 7.319

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.78 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 60 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.78, Psat = 60 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.78 * 60 | Answer: 46.8 kPa

question: A stream of 5.5 kg/s with specific heat 1.9 kJ/kg-K is heated through 110 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 5.5, cp = 1.9, dT = 110 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 5.5*1.9*110 | Answer: 115 kW

question: A reactor of volume 18.9 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 2.3 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 18.9, Q = 2.3 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 18.9 / 2.3 | Answer: 8.217 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 2e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 1 mm with a concentration difference of 90 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 2, L = 1, dC = 90 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (2e-9)*90 / (1e-3) | Answer: 180 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 4.8 min and steady-state gain 2.2. For a step input of magnitude 4, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 4.8, K = 2.2, M = 4 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 2.2 * 4 | Answer: 8.8 units

question: A reactor operates at a space time of 10.7 min. Find its space velocity in per hour.
solution: Given: tau = 10.7 | Formula: SV = 60 / tau  (per hour) | Substitute: SV = 60 / 10.7 | Answer: 5.607 /h

question: An aircraft wing of area 105 m^2 flies at 170 m/s (air density 0.4 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 1.2. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 105, V = 170, rho = 0.4, CL = 1.2 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.4*(170)^2*105*1.2 / 1000 | Answer: 728.3 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 90 m^2 flies at 240 m/s (density 0.7 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.04. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 90, V = 240, rho = 0.7, CD = 0.04 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.7*(240)^2*90*0.04 / 1000 | Answer: 72.58 kN

question: An aircraft flies at 360 m/s where the speed of sound is 340 m/s. Find the Mach number.
solution: Given: V = 360, a = 340 | Formula: M = V / a | Substitute: M = 360 / 340 | Answer: 1.059

question: A specimen under stress 340 MPa shows an elastic strain of 1.8e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 340, eps = 1.8 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 340 / (1.8e-3) MPa = 188.9 GPa | Answer: 188.9 GPa

question: A block of mass 22 kg has a volume of 3.1e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 22, V = 3.1 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 22 / (3.1e-3) | Answer: 7097 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 2300 mm is heated through 65 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 17e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 2300, dT = 65, al = 17 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 2300*17e-6*65 | Answer: 2.542 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 165 ohm, R2 = 35 ohm and R3 = 320 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 165, R2 = 35, R3 = 320 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 35*320 / 165 | Answer: 67.88 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 350 ohm and gauge factor 2 experiences a strain of 500e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 350, GF = 2, eps = 500 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 350*2*500e-6 | Answer: 350 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 10.54 when the true value is 50. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10.54, true = 50 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10.54 - 50| / 50 * 100 | Answer: 78.92 %

question: Annual demand is 34500 units, ordering cost 130 per order and holding cost 24 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 34500, S = 130, H = 24 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*34500*130 / 24) | Answer: 611.4 units

question: An asset costs 140000 with salvage value 14000 after 11 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 140000, Sv = 14000, n = 11 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (140000 - 14000) / 11 | Answer: 11455 per year

question: A product sells for 70 per unit with variable cost 50 per unit and fixed costs 70000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 70, V = 50, F = 70000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 70000 / (70 - 50) | Answer: 3500 units

question: Find the present worth of 60000 received 4 years from now at an interest rate of 7% per year.
solution: Given: F = 60000, n = 4, i = 7 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 60000 / (1 + 0.07)^4 | Answer: 45774 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.93, 0.95 and 0.99 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.93, r2 = 0.95, r3 = 0.99 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.93*0.95*0.99 | Answer: 0.8747

question: A process produces 41 defective items in a batch of 5500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 41, N = 5500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 41/5500 * 1e6 | Answer: 7455 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -6x^3 + 5x^2 + 8x + 8 evaluated at x = 2.
For f(x) = 3x^3 + 2x^2 - 9x - 5, find f''(x) at x = 0.
Evaluate the definite integral of (3x^2 - 4x + 5) dx from x = -3 to x = 7.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = 3x^3/3 + -4x^2/2 + 5x | Evaluate F(7) - F(-3) | Answer: 340
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 5x^2 + 5x - 10 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[-8, 4], [-9, -5]].
solution: Given: a = -8, b = 4, c = -9, d = -5 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (-8)(-5) - (4)(-9) | Answer: 76

question: Find the determinant of [[-1, 1, 2], [-3, 2, 3], [4, 2, 1]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: -9

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[-3, 0], [2, 1]].
solution: Trace tr = -2, Determinant = -3 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 1

question: Solve for x: 1x + -5y = 7 and -4x + 5y = -1.
solution: Determinant = 1*5 - -5*-4 = -15 | x = (e d - b f) / det = -2 | Answer: x = -2
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 63, 72, 31, 100, 12.
solution: Sum = 278 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 55.6 | Answer: 55.6

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 5, 27, 49, 26, 27.
solution: Mean = 26.8 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 15.56

question: Find the slope of the line through (4, -2) and (-4, -7).
solution: Given: x1 = 4, y1 = -2, x2 = -4, y2 = -7 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (-7 - -2) / (-4 - 4) | Answer: 0.625

question: Find the distance between the points (6, -5) and (9, -1).
solution: Given: x1 = 6, y1 = -5, x2 = 9, y2 = -1 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((3)^2 + (4)^2) | Answer: 5 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (-2,6), (1,1), (2,0).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 1 sq units

question: Evaluate the number of combinations C(12, 4).
solution: Given: n = 12, r = 4 | Formula: C(n, r) = n! / (r! (n - r)!) | Substitute: C(12, 4) = 12! / (4! * 8!) | Answer: 495

question: Find the 23th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 0 and common difference -2.
solution: Given: a = 0, d = -2, n = 23 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = 0 + (23 - 1)*-2 | Answer: -44

question: Find the sum of the first 39 terms of an AP with first term 8 and common difference -2.
solution: Given: a = 8, d = -2, n = 39 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 39/2 [2*8 + (39-1)*-2] | Answer: -1170

question: Find the 3th term of a geometric progression with first term 9 and common ratio 2.
solution: Given: a = 9, r = 2, n = 3 | Formula: a_n = a r^(n-1) | Substitute: a_n = 9 * 2^(3-1) | Answer: 36

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 31000 at 4% per annum for 4 years.
solution: Given: P = 31000, R = 4, Tt = 4 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 31000 * 4 * 4 / 100 | Answer: 4960 currency units

question: Find the amount when 5000 is invested at 10.8% per annum compounded annually for 5 years.
solution: Given: P = 5000, R = 10.8, Tt = 5 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 5000 * (1 + 10.8/100)^5 | Answer: 835 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (8, -5, 1) and (-4, -7, 8).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (0, 1, -5) and (-5, 2, -5).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 25.98

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (5, 2, 3) and (3, -3, 0).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 69.87 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number 1 + -2i.
solution: Given: a = 1, b = -2 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((1)^2 + (-2)^2) | Answer: 2.236

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number 10 + 10i.
solution: Given: a = 10, b = 10 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(10, 10) | Answer: 45 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -x^3 + 6x^2 - 9x + 9 at x = -3.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-31 with initial guess x0=8, find x1 (one iteration).
solution: Given: N = 31, x0 = 8 | Formula: x1 = x0 - (x0^2 - N)/(2 x0) | Substitute: x1 = 8 - ((8)^2 - 31)/(2*8) | Answer: 5.938

question: Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1 and ordinates 14, 9, 11, 19, 17, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 348 and 391.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 348 and 391 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 39 and 37.
solution: Given: a = 39, b = 37 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 39*37 / 1 | Answer: 1443
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 52 mm carries an axial tensile load of 59 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 19 mm and length 2200 mm carries an axial load of 42 kN. Take E = 70 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 55 mm transmits a torque of 1750 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 55, Tt = 1750 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(1750*1000) / (pi*(55)^3) | Answer: 53.57 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 35 mm and length 1300 mm carries a torque of 200 N-m. With G = 80 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (35)^4 / 32 = 147324 mm^4 | theta = (200*1000)(1300) / (80000 * 147324) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 1.264 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 83 mm wide and 300 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 83, h = 300 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 83*(300)^2 / 6 | Answer: 1245000 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (78 mm x 160 mm) carries a bending moment of 9 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (42 mm x 160 mm) has effective length 1900 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 710 MPa is designed for a working stress of 60 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 710, sw = 60 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 710 / 60 | Answer: 11.83

question: A steel bar is fully restrained and heated through 20 deg C. With E = 200 GPa and alpha = 12e-6 /deg C, find the thermal stress in MPa.
solution: Given: dT = 20, E = 200, al = 12 | Formula: sigma = E alpha (dT) | Substitute: sigma = 200000 * 12e-6 * 20 | Answer: 48 MPa

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 450 mm and wall thickness 10 mm carries an internal pressure of 0.9 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 450, t = 10, P = 0.9 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 0.9*450 / (2*10) | Answer: 20.25 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 1040 K and 310 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 1040, Tc = 310 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 310/1040) * 100 | Answer: 70.19 %

question: A refrigerator works between 254 K (cold) and 326 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 254, Th = 326 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 254 / (326 - 254) | Answer: 3.528

question: A heat pump operates between 274 K and 314 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 274, Th = 314 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 314 / (314 - 274) | Answer: 7.85

question: 4.3 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 75 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.3, dT = 75 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 4.3 * 0.718 * 75 | Answer: 231.6 kJ

question: 7.2 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 60 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 7.2, dT = 60 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 7.2 * 1.005 * 60 | Answer: 434.2 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 1.4 m^3 at 450 K with mass 1.9 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 1.4, Tk = 450, m = 1.9 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 1.9*0.287*450 / 1.4 | Answer: 175.3 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 2.2 kg of air expands isothermally at 350 K from volume V1 to 2*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.2, Tk = 350, ratio = 2 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 2.2*0.287*350*ln(2) | Answer: 153.2 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 0.5 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.13 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 0.5, D = 0.13 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*0.5*0.13 / 0.001 | Answer: 65000

question: Water flows at 3 m/s through a pipe of diameter 230 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 13.4 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 13.4 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*13.4 / 1000 | Answer: 131.5 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 16.8 m. Taking Cv = 0.97, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 16.8, cv = 0.97 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.97*sqrt(2*9.81*16.8) | Answer: 17.61 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 360 mm) water flows at 2.5 m/s. It contracts to diameter 130 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
Water flows at 1.2 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.48 m and length 350 m. With friction factor f = 0.037, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 23 teeth drives a gear of 55 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1200 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 23, z2 = 55, N1 = 1200 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1200*23 / 55 | Answer: 501.8 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 120 mm rotates at 500 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 120, N = 500 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.12)*500 / 60 | Answer: 3.142 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 29.2 kW at 1200 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 29.2, N = 1200 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(29.2*1000) / (2*pi*1200) | Answer: 232.4 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 1.1 kg rotates at radius 0.17 m at 1050 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 12400 N/m and mass 14.3 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 12400, m = 14.3 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(12400/14.3) | Answer: 4.687 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 5.6 m^2 and thickness 0.4 m has conductivity k = 31.4 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 50 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 5.6, L = 0.4, k = 31.4, dT = 50 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 31.4*5.6*50 / 0.4 | Answer: 21980 W

question: A surface of area 0.5 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 190 W/m^2-K to surroundings 60 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 0.5, h = 190, dT = 60 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 190*0.5*60 | Answer: 5700 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 160 m/min, feed = 0.46 mm/rev, depth of cut = 1.7 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 160, f = 0.46, d = 1.7 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*160*0.46*1.7 | Answer: 125120 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 300 mm is turned at 1050 rpm with a feed of 0.14 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 300, N = 1050, f = 0.14 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 300 / (0.14*1050) | Answer: 2.041 min

question: A resistor of 32 ohm carries a current of 9.5 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 32, I = 9.5 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 9.5 * 32 | Answer: 304 V

question: Three resistors 37 ohm, 44 ohm and 73 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 37, R2 = 44, R3 = 73 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 37 + 44 + 73 | Answer: 154 ohm

question: Two resistors 56 ohm and 15 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 56, R2 = 15 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 56*15 / (56+15) | Answer: 11.83 ohm

question: A device draws 2.2 A at 35 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 35, I = 2.2 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 35 * 2.2 | Answer: 77 W

question: A current of 7.3 A flows through a 127 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 7.3, R = 127 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (7.3)^2 * 127 | Answer: 6768 W

question: Two capacitors 24.2 uF and 20.7 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 24.2, C2 = 20.7 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 24.2*20.7 / (24.2+20.7) | Answer: 11.16 uF

question: A resistor 68 kohm and capacitor 4.1 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 68, C = 4.1 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (68k)(4.1u) = 278.8 ms | Answer: 278.8 ms

question: An inductor 149.9 mH is in series with 45 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 149.9, R = 45 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (149.9e-3) / 45 | Answer: 3.331 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 55.4 mH inductor at 530 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 55.4, f = 530 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (530)(55.4e-3) | Answer: 184.5 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 3.5 uF capacitor at 590 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 3.5, f = 590 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (590)(3.5e-6)) | Answer: 77.07 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 69 ohm, XL = 34 ohm and XC = 80 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 69, XL = 34, XC = 80 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(69^2 + (34 - 80)^2) | Answer: 82.93 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 2.8 mH and C = 3.2 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 2.8, C = 3.2 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(2.8e-3 * 3.2e-6)) | Answer: 1681 Hz

question: A capacitor of 31.6 uF is charged to 225 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 31.6, V = 225 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*31.6e-6*(225)^2 | Answer: 799.9 mJ

question: An alternating voltage has a peak value of 338 V. Find its RMS value.
solution: Given: Vp = 338 | Formula: Vrms = Vp / sqrt(2) | Substitute: Vrms = 338 / sqrt(2) | Answer: 239 V

question: A transformer has primary voltage 120 V with 200 primary turns and 80 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 120, N1 = 200, N2 = 80 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 120 * 80/200 | Answer: 48 V
