question: A circular rod of diameter 54 mm carries an axial tensile load of 45 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 18 mm and length 2000 mm carries an axial load of 60 kN. Take E = 110 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 45 mm transmits a torque of 2500 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 45, Tt = 2500 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(2500*1000) / (pi*(45)^3) | Answer: 139.7 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 60 mm and length 1500 mm carries a torque of 1900 N-m. With G = 80 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (60)^4 / 32 = 1272345 mm^4 | theta = (1900*1000)(1500) / (80000 * 1272345) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 1.604 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 97 mm wide and 90 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 97, h = 90 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 97*(90)^2 / 6 | Answer: 130950 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (109 mm x 220 mm) carries a bending moment of 28 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (41 mm x 130 mm) has effective length 3600 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 800 MPa is designed for a working stress of 70 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 800, sw = 70 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 800 / 70 | Answer: 11.43

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 750 mm and wall thickness 15 mm carries an internal pressure of 2.6 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 750, t = 15, P = 2.6 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 2.6*750 / (2*15) | Answer: 65 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 700 K and 360 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 700, Tc = 360 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 360/700) * 100 | Answer: 48.57 %

question: A refrigerator works between 252 K (cold) and 328 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 252, Th = 328 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 252 / (328 - 252) | Answer: 3.316

question: A heat pump operates between 268 K and 308 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 268, Th = 308 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 308 / (308 - 268) | Answer: 7.7

question: 5 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 145 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 5, dT = 145 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 5 * 0.718 * 145 | Answer: 520.5 kJ

question: 7.6 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 185 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 7.6, dT = 185 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 7.6 * 1.005 * 185 | Answer: 1413 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 1.7 m^3 at 300 K with mass 3.2 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 1.7, Tk = 300, m = 3.2 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 3.2*0.287*300 / 1.7 | Answer: 162.1 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 3.8 kg of air expands isothermally at 350 K from volume V1 to 4*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.8, Tk = 350, ratio = 4 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 3.8*0.287*350*ln(4) | Answer: 529.2 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 1.3 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.34 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 1.3, D = 0.34 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*1.3*0.34 / 0.001 | Answer: 442000

question: Water flows at 1.3 m/s through a pipe of diameter 260 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 17.9 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 17.9 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*17.9 / 1000 | Answer: 175.6 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 17.7 m. Taking Cv = 0.97, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 17.7, cv = 0.97 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.97*sqrt(2*9.81*17.7) | Answer: 18.08 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 340 mm) water flows at 1 m/s. It contracts to diameter 110 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 340, d2 = 110, V1 = 1 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 1*(340/110)^2 | Answer: 9.554 m/s

question: Water flows at 3.3 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.3 m and length 200 m. With friction factor f = 0.035, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 17 teeth drives a gear of 89 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1350 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 17, z2 = 89, N1 = 1350 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1350*17 / 89 | Answer: 257.9 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 370 mm rotates at 350 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 370, N = 350 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.37)*350 / 60 | Answer: 6.781 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 48.8 kW at 400 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 48.8, N = 400 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(48.8*1000) / (2*pi*400) | Answer: 1165 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 6.2 kg rotates at radius 0.51 m at 800 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 8200 N/m and mass 19.2 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 8200, m = 19.2 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(8200/19.2) | Answer: 3.289 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 2.3 m^2 and thickness 0.31 m has conductivity k = 40.1 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 125 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 2.3, L = 0.31, k = 40.1, dT = 125 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 40.1*2.3*125 / 0.31 | Answer: 3719 W

question: A surface of area 3.2 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 165 W/m^2-K to surroundings 105 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 3.2, h = 165, dT = 105 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 165*3.2*105 | Answer: 55440 W

question: In a counter-flow heat exchanger the terminal temperature differences are 45 deg C and 35 deg C. Find the log mean temperature difference (LMTD) in deg C.
solution: Given: dT1 = 45, dT2 = 35 | Formula: LMTD = (dT1 - dT2) / ln(dT1/dT2) | Substitute: LMTD = (45 - 35) / ln(45/35) | Answer: 39.79 deg C

question: In turning, cutting speed = 220 m/min, feed = 0.2 mm/rev, depth of cut = 0.9 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 220, f = 0.2, d = 0.9 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*220*0.2*0.9 | Answer: 39600 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 500 mm is turned at 1150 rpm with a feed of 0.19 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 500, N = 1150, f = 0.19 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 500 / (0.19*1150) | Answer: 2.288 min

question: A resistor of 79 ohm carries a current of 7.7 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 79, I = 7.7 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 7.7 * 79 | Answer: 608.3 V

question: Three resistors 31 ohm, 13 ohm and 64 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 31, R2 = 13, R3 = 64 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 31 + 13 + 64 | Answer: 108 ohm

question: Two resistors 64 ohm and 53 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 64, R2 = 53 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 64*53 / (64+53) | Answer: 28.99 ohm

question: A device draws 4.3 A at 90 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 90, I = 4.3 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 90 * 4.3 | Answer: 387 W

question: A current of 3.9 A flows through a 59 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 3.9, R = 59 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (3.9)^2 * 59 | Answer: 897.4 W

question: Two capacitors 45.9 uF and 27.1 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 45.9, C2 = 27.1 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 45.9*27.1 / (45.9+27.1) | Answer: 17.04 uF

question: A resistor 68 kohm and capacitor 11.2 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 68, C = 11.2 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (68k)(11.2u) = 761.6 ms | Answer: 761.6 ms

question: An inductor 439.7 mH is in series with 48 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 439.7, R = 48 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (439.7e-3) / 48 | Answer: 9.16 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 13.8 mH inductor at 840 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 13.8, f = 840 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (840)(13.8e-3) | Answer: 72.83 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 36 uF capacitor at 50 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 36, f = 50 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (50)(36e-6)) | Answer: 88.42 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 75 ohm, XL = 92 ohm and XC = 96 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 75, XL = 92, XC = 96 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(75^2 + (92 - 96)^2) | Answer: 75.11 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 82.2 mH and C = 7.7 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 82.2, C = 7.7 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(82.2e-3 * 7.7e-6)) | Answer: 200.1 Hz

question: A capacitor of 29.2 uF is charged to 85 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 29.2, V = 85 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*29.2e-6*(85)^2 | Answer: 105.5 mJ

question: An alternating voltage has a peak value of 334 V. Find its RMS value.
solution: Given: Vp = 334 | Formula: Vrms = Vp / sqrt(2) | Substitute: Vrms = 334 / sqrt(2) | Answer: 236.2 V

question: A transformer has primary voltage 280 V with 650 primary turns and 380 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 280, N1 = 650, N2 = 380 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 280 * 380/650 | Answer: 163.7 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 330 V and draws an armature current of 11 A. If the armature resistance is 1.33 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 330, Ia = 11, Ra = 1.33 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 330 - 11*1.33 | Answer: 315.4 V

question: A 4-pole induction motor on a 50 Hz supply runs at 1020 rpm. Find the slip (%).
formula: s = (Ns - N) / Ns,  Ns = 120 f / P

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 145 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.98. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 145, VL = 400, pf = 0.98 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*400*145*0.98 / 1000 | Answer: 98.45 kW

question: A load has real power 15 kW and apparent power 55 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 15, S = 55 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 15 / 55 | Answer: 0.2727

question: A machine delivers 35 kW output while drawing 197 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 35, Pi = 197 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 35/197 * 100 | Answer: 17.77 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 17 V across R1 = 45 ohm and R2 = 32 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 17, R1 = 45, R2 = 32 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 17*32 / (45+32) | Answer: 7.065 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 20 kohm and Rin = 26 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 20, Rin = 26 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 20 / 26 | Answer: 0.7692

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 160 kohm and Rg = 45 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 160, Rg = 45 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 160/45 | Answer: 4.556

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 646. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 646 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(646) | Answer: 28.1 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 8.9 m carries a central point load of 105 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 8.9, W = 105 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 105*8.9 / 4 | Answer: 233.6 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 3.2 m carries a UDL of 5 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.2, w = 5 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 5*(3.2)^2 / 8 | Answer: 6.4 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 2.1 m carries a point load 60 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 2.1, W = 60 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 60*2.1 | Answer: 126 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 4.1 m carries a UDL of 26 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.1, w = 26 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 26*(4.1)^2 / 2 | Answer: 218.5 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.1 m carries a point load 90 kN at distance 1.5 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 6.1, a = 1.5, W = 90 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 90*(6.1 - 1.5) / 6.1 | Answer: 67.87 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 7.3 m) carries a central point load 40 kN. With E = 25 GPa and I = 490e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=40000 N, L=7300.0 mm, E=25000 MPa, I=490e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 26.46 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 5.8 m carries a UDL of 30 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.8, w = 30 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 30*(5.8)^2 / 12 | Answer: 84.1 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 370 mm, clear cover 40 mm and main bars of diameter 16 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 370, c = 40, dia = 16 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 370 - 40 - 16/2 | Answer: 322 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 29.8 m^2 carrying a factored load of 14.5 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 29.8, w = 14.5 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 14.5 * 29.8 | Answer: 432.1 kN

question: For a bar of diameter 25 mm with design bond stress 2.2 MPa and steel stress 395 MPa, find the development length in mm.
solution: Given: dia = 25, tbd = 2.2, fs = 395 | Formula: Ld = phi fs / (4 tau_bd) | Substitute: Ld = 25*395 / (4*2.2) | Answer: 1122 mm

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 3.9 m, unit weight 20 kN/m^3, phi = 29 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 5.6 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 19 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 5.6, g = 19 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (19 - 9.81)*5.6 | Answer: 51.46 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 8e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.2, area = 3.8e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 8, i = 0.2, A = 3.8 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (8e-4)*0.2*(3.8e-3) | Answer: 608 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 0.5 m, bed slope 0.006 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.027. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 2.2 m under a head of 0.9 m. Taking Cd = 0.64 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 3.2 m wide carries a discharge of 18.7 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 540 m and design speed 50 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 540, V = 50 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (50)^2 / (127*540) | Answer: 0.03645
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: For a design speed of 85 km/h with allowable superelevation 0.07 and lateral friction 0.13, find the minimum curve radius in m.
A tank of volume 180 m^3 treats a flow of 10 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 180, Q = 10 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 180 / 10 | Answer: 18 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 370 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.1 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 7 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 370, k = 0.1, t = 7 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 370*(1 - e^(-0.1*7)) | Answer: 186.3 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.54, rainfall intensity 80 mm/h over a catchment of 48.7 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.54, i = 80, A = 48.7 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.54*80*48.7 / 360 | Answer: 5.844 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.03 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 130 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.03, M = 130 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 130*(30+0.03)/30 | Answer: 130.1 m

question: Convert the decimal number 255 to binary.
solution: Divide 255 by 2 repeatedly, recording remainders | Reading remainders in reverse gives 11111111 | Answer: 11111111 (binary)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 2 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the decimal number 486 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 486 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 1E6 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the 8-bit binary number 11001110 to decimal.
solution: Binary 11001110 = sum of bit-weights | Answer: 206 (decimal)
formula: Sum each bit times its positional weight (2^i)

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 01111001 and 10011100.
solution: XOR: 11100101 | Count of 1s = 5 | Answer: 5
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 530 megabits is sent over a link of 80 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 530, B = 80 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 530 / 80 | Answer: 6.625 s

question: A link has bandwidth 23 Mbps and round-trip time 160 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 23, R = 160 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 23e6 * 160e-3 bits = 3680 kb | Answer: 3680 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.9, cache access time 5 ns and main-memory access time 70 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.9, tc = 5, tm = 70 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.9*5 + (1 - 0.9)*70 | Answer: 11.5 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 373391 elements?
solution: Given: n = 373391 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(373391)) + 1 | Answer: 19

question: An O(n^2) algorithm performs c*n^2 basic operations. If c = 1 and n = 1610, how many operations are performed?
solution: Given: n = 1610 | Formula: operations = n^2 | Substitute: = (1610)^2 | Answer: 2592100

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.016, memory access time 100 ns and page-fault service time 10 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 10 ms = 10000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.016)*100 + 0.016*10000000.0 ns | Answer: 160.1 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 0.9 m^3 at 490 kPa and 370 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 0.9, P = 490, Tk = 370 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (490e3)*0.9 / (8.314*370) | Answer: 143.4 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.37 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 3 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.37, t = 3 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.37*3) | Answer: 0.6704

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.15 /min) is to reach 70% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.15, X = 70 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.7) / 0.15 | Answer: 8.026 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.32 /min) reaches 70% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.32, X = 70 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.7 / (0.32*(1 - 0.7)) | Answer: 7.292 min

question: For a reaction with A = 4e10 /s and activation energy 70 kJ/mol at 360 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 4, Ea = 70, Tk = 360 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 4e10 * exp(-70e3 / (8.314*360)) | Answer: 2.786 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.94 and bottoms xW = 0.07, with relative volatility alpha = 1.9. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.94, xw = 0.07, al = 1.9 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.94/0.06)(0.93/0.07)] / ln(1.9) | Answer: 8.317 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.87 and x = 0.46. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.87, x = 0.46 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.87/0.13) / (0.46/0.54) | Answer: 7.856

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.86 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 85 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.86, Psat = 85 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.86 * 85 | Answer: 73.1 kPa

question: A stream of 1.6 kg/s with specific heat 2 kJ/kg-K is heated through 15 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 1.6, cp = 2, dT = 15 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 1.6*2*15 | Answer: 48 kW

question: A reactor of volume 18.3 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 1.5 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 18.3, Q = 1.5 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 18.3 / 1.5 | Answer: 12.2 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 3.5e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 2 mm with a concentration difference of 180 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 3.5, L = 2, dC = 180 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (3.5e-9)*180 / (2e-3) | Answer: 315 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 6.2 min and steady-state gain 2.6. For a step input of magnitude 18, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 6.2, K = 2.6, M = 18 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 2.6 * 18 | Answer: 46.8 units

question: A reactor operates at a space time of 0.5 min. Find its space velocity in per hour.
solution: Given: tau = 0.5 | Formula: SV = 60 / tau  (per hour) | Substitute: SV = 60 / 0.5 | Answer: 120 /h

question: An aircraft wing of area 105 m^2 flies at 220 m/s (air density 0.7 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.7. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 105, V = 220, rho = 0.7, CL = 0.7 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.7*(220)^2*105*0.7 / 1000 | Answer: 1245 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 15 m^2 flies at 130 m/s (density 1 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.07. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 15, V = 130, rho = 1, CD = 0.07 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*1*(130)^2*15*0.07 / 1000 | Answer: 8.873 kN

question: An aircraft flies at 560 m/s where the speed of sound is 310 m/s. Find the Mach number.
solution: Given: V = 560, a = 310 | Formula: M = V / a | Substitute: M = 560 / 310 | Answer: 1.806

question: A specimen under stress 180 MPa shows an elastic strain of 0.7e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 180, eps = 0.7 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 180 / (0.7e-3) MPa = 257.1 GPa | Answer: 257.1 GPa

question: A block of mass 47 kg has a volume of 5.3e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 47, V = 5.3 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 47 / (5.3e-3) | Answer: 8868 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 500 mm is heated through 60 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 12e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 500, dT = 60, al = 12 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 500*12e-6*60 | Answer: 0.36 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 195 ohm, R2 = 60 ohm and R3 = 80 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 195, R2 = 60, R3 = 80 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 60*80 / 195 | Answer: 24.62 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 120 ohm and gauge factor 2.1 experiences a strain of 1500e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 120, GF = 2.1, eps = 1500 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 120*2.1*1500e-6 | Answer: 378 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 9.93 when the true value is 50. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.93, true = 50 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.93 - 50| / 50 * 100 | Answer: 80.14 %

question: Annual demand is 3500 units, ordering cost 300 per order and holding cost 40 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 3500, S = 300, H = 40 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*3500*300 / 40) | Answer: 229.1 units

question: An asset costs 250000 with salvage value 26000 after 16 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 250000, Sv = 26000, n = 16 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (250000 - 26000) / 16 | Answer: 14000 per year

question: A product sells for 440 per unit with variable cost 20 per unit and fixed costs 65000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 440, V = 20, F = 65000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 65000 / (440 - 20) | Answer: 154.8 units

question: Find the present worth of 145000 received 2 years from now at an interest rate of 12% per year.
solution: Given: F = 145000, n = 2, i = 12 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 145000 / (1 + 0.12)^2 | Answer: 115593 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.98, 0.98 and 0.91 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.98, r2 = 0.98, r3 = 0.91 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.98*0.98*0.91 | Answer: 0.874

question: A process produces 31 defective items in a batch of 16000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 31, N = 16000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 31/16000 * 1e6 | Answer: 1938 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = 3x^3 + 5x^2 + 1 evaluated at x = -4.
For f(x) = 4x^3 + 6x^2 - 5x + 3, find f''(x) at x = -2.
Evaluate the definite integral of (2x^2 + 5x - 4) dx from x = -2 to x = 4.

question: Find the larger real root of 6x^2 + 4x - 11 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[2, -1], [2, -6]].
solution: Given: a = 2, b = -1, c = 2, d = -6 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (2)(-6) - (-1)(2) | Answer: -10

question: Find the determinant of [[-1, -3, -3], [3, 4, -4], [-1, 6, -3]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: -117

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[6, -2], [-6, 4]].

question: Solve for x: -1x + 1y = -12 and 4x + -1y = 8.

solution: Sum = 337 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 67.4 | Answer: 67.4

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 14, 30, 9, 49, 27.
solution: Mean = 25.8 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 15.64

question: Find the slope of the line through (-1, 2) and (-9, 0).
solution: Given: x1 = -1, y1 = 2, x2 = -9, y2 = 0 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (0 - 2) / (-9 - -1) | Answer: 0.25

question: Find the distance between the points (-5, -3) and (4, -8).
solution: Given: x1 = -5, y1 = -3, x2 = 4, y2 = -8 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((9)^2 + (-5)^2) | Answer: 10.3 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (-3,4), (-3,-3), (5,6).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 28 sq units

question: Evaluate the number of combinations C(17, 11).
solution: Given: n = 17, r = 11 | Formula: C(n, r) = n! / (r! (n - r)!) | Substitute: C(17, 11) = 17! / (11! * 6!) | Answer: 12376

question: Find the 15th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -6 and common difference 6.
solution: Given: a = -6, d = 6, n = 15 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -6 + (15 - 1)*6 | Answer: 78

question: Find the sum of the first 12 terms of an AP with first term 14 and common difference 4.
solution: Given: a = 14, d = 4, n = 12 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 12/2 [2*14 + (12-1)*4] | Answer: 432

question: Find the 5th term of a geometric progression with first term 3 and common ratio 3.
solution: Given: a = 3, r = 3, n = 5 | Formula: a_n = a r^(n-1) | Substitute: a_n = 3 * 3^(5-1) | Answer: 243

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 41500 at 9.2% per annum for 4 years.
solution: Given: P = 41500, R = 9.2, Tt = 4 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 41500 * 9.2 * 4 / 100 | Answer: 15272 currency units

question: Find the amount when 24500 is invested at 8.6% per annum compounded annually for 6 years.
solution: Given: P = 24500, R = 8.6, Tt = 6 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 24500 * (1 + 8.6/100)^6 | Answer: 40193 currency units

solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 8.307

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (-5, -5, 0) and (6, 3, -2).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 155.4 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number 9 + 6i.
solution: Given: a = 9, b = 6 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((9)^2 + (6)^2) | Answer: 10.82

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number 0 + 2i.
solution: Given: a = 0, b = 2 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(2, 0) | Answer: 90 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -3x^3 - 4x^2 - 8x - 5 at x = -5.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-67 with initial guess x0=15, find x1 (one iteration).

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 71 and 35.
solution: Given: a = 71, b = 35 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 71*35 / 1 | Answer: 2485

question: A circular rod of diameter 60 mm carries an axial tensile load of 70 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 38 mm and length 1700 mm carries an axial load of 42 kN. Take E = 210 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 49 mm transmits a torque of 1550 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 49, Tt = 1550 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(1550*1000) / (pi*(49)^3) | Answer: 67.1 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 39 mm and length 1700 mm carries a torque of 550 N-m. With G = 80 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (39)^4 / 32 = 227122 mm^4 | theta = (550*1000)(1700) / (80000 * 227122) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 2.948 degrees
