question: A rectangular beam section is 150 mm wide and 260 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 150, h = 260 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 150*(260)^2 / 6 | Answer: 1690000 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (43 mm x 240 mm) carries a bending moment of 26 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (61 mm x 120 mm) has effective length 3500 mm and E = 200 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 370 MPa is designed for a working stress of 240 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 370, sw = 240 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 370 / 240 | Answer: 1.542

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 850 mm and wall thickness 17 mm carries an internal pressure of 0.5 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 850, t = 17, P = 0.5 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 0.5*850 / (2*17) | Answer: 12.5 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 720 K and 430 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 720, Tc = 430 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 430/720) * 100 | Answer: 40.28 %

question: A refrigerator works between 259 K (cold) and 312 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 259, Th = 312 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 259 / (312 - 259) | Answer: 4.887

question: A heat pump operates between 283 K and 310 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 283, Th = 310 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 310 / (310 - 283) | Answer: 11.48

question: 1.5 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 185 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1.5, dT = 185 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 1.5 * 0.718 * 185 | Answer: 199.2 kJ

question: 1.8 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 25 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1.8, dT = 25 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 1.8 * 1.005 * 25 | Answer: 45.23 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 3.9 m^3 at 540 K with mass 4.5 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 3.9, Tk = 540, m = 4.5 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 4.5*0.287*540 / 3.9 | Answer: 178.8 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 3.8 kg of air expands isothermally at 340 K from volume V1 to 5*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.8, Tk = 340, ratio = 5 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 3.8*0.287*340*ln(5) | Answer: 596.8 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 4.4 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.1 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 4.4, D = 0.1 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*4.4*0.1 / 0.001 | Answer: 440000

question: Water flows at 1.3 m/s through a pipe of diameter 110 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 16.2 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 16.2 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*16.2 / 1000 | Answer: 158.9 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 15.5 m. Taking Cv = 0.97, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 15.5, cv = 0.97 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.97*sqrt(2*9.81*15.5) | Answer: 16.92 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 280 mm) water flows at 1.2 m/s. It contracts to diameter 110 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
Water flows at 2.4 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.37 m and length 240 m. With friction factor f = 0.022, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 24 teeth drives a gear of 86 teeth. If the pinion runs at 550 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 24, z2 = 86, N1 = 550 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 550*24 / 86 | Answer: 153.5 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 490 mm rotates at 1050 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 490, N = 1050 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.49)*1050 / 60 | Answer: 26.94 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 47.6 kW at 1400 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 47.6, N = 1400 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(47.6*1000) / (2*pi*1400) | Answer: 324.7 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 6.3 kg rotates at radius 0.16 m at 1050 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 8500 N/m and mass 10.8 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 8500, m = 10.8 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(8500/10.8) | Answer: 4.465 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 8 m^2 and thickness 0.16 m has conductivity k = 46.7 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 125 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 8, L = 0.16, k = 46.7, dT = 125 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 46.7*8*125 / 0.16 | Answer: 291875 W

question: A surface of area 0.6 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 20 W/m^2-K to surroundings 125 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 0.6, h = 20, dT = 125 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 20*0.6*125 | Answer: 1500 W

question: In a counter-flow heat exchanger the terminal temperature differences are 70 deg C and 30 deg C. Find the log mean temperature difference (LMTD) in deg C.
solution: Given: dT1 = 70, dT2 = 30 | Formula: LMTD = (dT1 - dT2) / ln(dT1/dT2) | Substitute: LMTD = (70 - 30) / ln(70/30) | Answer: 47.21 deg C

question: In turning, cutting speed = 150 m/min, feed = 0.32 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2.4 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 150, f = 0.32, d = 2.4 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*150*0.32*2.4 | Answer: 115200 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 390 mm is turned at 600 rpm with a feed of 0.25 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 390, N = 600, f = 0.25 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 390 / (0.25*600) | Answer: 2.6 min

question: A resistor of 161 ohm carries a current of 1.1 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 161, I = 1.1 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 1.1 * 161 | Answer: 177.1 V

question: Three resistors 7 ohm, 78 ohm and 94 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 7, R2 = 78, R3 = 94 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 7 + 78 + 94 | Answer: 179 ohm

question: Two resistors 78 ohm and 81 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 78, R2 = 81 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 78*81 / (78+81) | Answer: 39.74 ohm

question: A device draws 13.1 A at 85 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 85, I = 13.1 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 85 * 13.1 | Answer: 1114 W

question: A current of 6.6 A flows through a 138 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 6.6, R = 138 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (6.6)^2 * 138 | Answer: 6011 W

question: Two capacitors 33.4 uF and 17.9 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 33.4, C2 = 17.9 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 33.4*17.9 / (33.4+17.9) | Answer: 11.65 uF

question: A resistor 29 kohm and capacitor 5.1 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 29, C = 5.1 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (29k)(5.1u) = 147.9 ms | Answer: 147.9 ms

question: An inductor 147.3 mH is in series with 14 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 147.3, R = 14 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (147.3e-3) / 14 | Answer: 10.52 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 184.3 mH inductor at 490 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 184.3, f = 490 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (490)(184.3e-3) | Answer: 567.4 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 6.9 uF capacitor at 420 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 6.9, f = 420 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (420)(6.9e-6)) | Answer: 54.92 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 100 ohm, XL = 77 ohm and XC = 143 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 100, XL = 77, XC = 143 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(100^2 + (77 - 143)^2) | Answer: 119.8 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 60.6 mH and C = 5.9 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 60.6, C = 5.9 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(60.6e-3 * 5.9e-6)) | Answer: 266.2 Hz

question: A capacitor of 90.9 uF is charged to 40 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 90.9, V = 40 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*90.9e-6*(40)^2 | Answer: 72.72 mJ

question: An alternating voltage has a peak value of 156 V. Find its RMS value.
solution: Given: Vp = 156 | Formula: Vrms = Vp / sqrt(2) | Substitute: Vrms = 156 / sqrt(2) | Answer: 110.3 V

question: A transformer has primary voltage 340 V with 410 primary turns and 470 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 340, N1 = 410, N2 = 470 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 340 * 470/410 | Answer: 389.8 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 210 V and draws an armature current of 39 A. If the armature resistance is 1.17 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 210, Ia = 39, Ra = 1.17 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 210 - 39*1.17 | Answer: 164.4 V

question: A 6-pole induction motor on a 60 Hz supply runs at 760 rpm. Find the slip (%).
formula: s = (Ns - N) / Ns,  Ns = 120 f / P

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 80 A at 433 V (line) with a power factor of 0.8. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 80, VL = 433, pf = 0.8 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*433*80*0.8 / 1000 | Answer: 48 kW

question: A load has real power 125 kW and apparent power 145 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 125, S = 145 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 125 / 145 | Answer: 0.8621

question: A machine delivers 150 kW output while drawing 167 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 150, Pi = 167 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 150/167 * 100 | Answer: 89.82 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 8 V across R1 = 40 ohm and R2 = 29 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 8, R1 = 40, R2 = 29 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 8*29 / (40+29) | Answer: 3.362 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 170 kohm and Rin = 36 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 170, Rin = 36 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 170 / 36 | Answer: 4.722

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 30 kohm and Rg = 15 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 30, Rg = 15 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 30/15 | Answer: 3

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 7901. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 7901 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(7901) | Answer: 38.98 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.7 m carries a central point load of 40 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.7, W = 40 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 40*4.7 / 4 | Answer: 47 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 3.3 m carries a UDL of 45 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.3, w = 45 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 45*(3.3)^2 / 8 | Answer: 61.26 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 3.9 m carries a point load 65 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.9, W = 65 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 65*3.9 | Answer: 253.5 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 3.7 m carries a UDL of 10 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.7, w = 10 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 10*(3.7)^2 / 2 | Answer: 68.45 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 6 m carries a point load 35 kN at distance 3.8 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 6, a = 3.8, W = 35 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 35*(6 - 3.8) / 6 | Answer: 12.83 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 6.3 m) carries a central point load 25 kN. With E = 25 GPa and I = 600e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=25000 N, L=6300.0 mm, E=25000 MPa, I=600e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 8.682 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 5.2 m carries a UDL of 9 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.2, w = 9 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 9*(5.2)^2 / 12 | Answer: 20.28 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 640 mm, clear cover 35 mm and main bars of diameter 20 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 640, c = 35, dia = 20 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 640 - 35 - 20/2 | Answer: 595 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 20.5 m^2 carrying a factored load of 10.6 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 20.5, w = 10.6 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 10.6 * 20.5 | Answer: 217.3 kN

question: For a bar of diameter 20 mm with design bond stress 1.9 MPa and steel stress 395 MPa, find the development length in mm.
solution: Given: dia = 20, tbd = 1.9, fs = 395 | Formula: Ld = phi fs / (4 tau_bd) | Substitute: Ld = 20*395 / (4*1.9) | Answer: 1039 mm

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 6.1 m, unit weight 18 kN/m^3, phi = 35 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 6.5 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 20 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 6.5, g = 20 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (20 - 9.81)*6.5 | Answer: 66.23 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 5.2e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.5, area = 3.7e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 5.2, i = 0.5, A = 3.7 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (5.2e-4)*0.5*(3.7e-3) | Answer: 962 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 0.5 m, bed slope 0.006 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.024. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 5 m under a head of 0.8 m. Taking Cd = 0.63 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 3.8 m wide carries a discharge of 3.3 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 140 m and design speed 85 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 140, V = 85 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (85)^2 / (127*140) | Answer: 0.4064
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: For a design speed of 75 km/h with allowable superelevation 0.07 and lateral friction 0.15, find the minimum curve radius in m.
A tank of volume 900 m^3 treats a flow of 10 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 900, Q = 10 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 900 / 10 | Answer: 90 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 380 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.18 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 7 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 380, k = 0.18, t = 7 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 380*(1 - e^(-0.18*7)) | Answer: 272.2 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.52, rainfall intensity 100 mm/h over a catchment of 58.5 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.52, i = 100, A = 58.5 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.52*100*58.5 / 360 | Answer: 8.45 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.03 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 230 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.03, M = 230 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 230*(30+0.03)/30 | Answer: 230.2 m

question: Convert the decimal number 117 to binary.
solution: Divide 117 by 2 repeatedly, recording remainders | Reading remainders in reverse gives 1110101 | Answer: 1110101 (binary)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 2 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the decimal number 2139 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 2139 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 85B (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the 8-bit binary number 11100111 to decimal.
solution: Binary 11100111 = sum of bit-weights | Answer: 231 (decimal)
formula: Sum each bit times its positional weight (2^i)

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 01101100 and 00011111.
solution: XOR: 01110011 | Count of 1s = 5 | Answer: 5
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 200 megabits is sent over a link of 86 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 200, B = 86 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 200 / 86 | Answer: 2.326 s

question: A link has bandwidth 74 Mbps and round-trip time 50 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 74, R = 50 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 74e6 * 50e-3 bits = 3700 kb | Answer: 3700 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.94, cache access time 7 ns and main-memory access time 130 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.94, tc = 7, tm = 130 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.94*7 + (1 - 0.94)*130 | Answer: 14.38 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 207500 elements?
solution: Given: n = 207500 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(207500)) + 1 | Answer: 18

question: An O(n^2) algorithm performs c*n^2 basic operations. If c = 1 and n = 430, how many operations are performed?
solution: Given: n = 430 | Formula: operations = n^2 | Substitute: = (430)^2 | Answer: 184900

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.009, memory access time 150 ns and page-fault service time 10 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 10 ms = 10000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.009)*150 + 0.009*10000000.0 ns | Answer: 90.15 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 0.6 m^3 at 160 kPa and 520 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 0.6, P = 160, Tk = 520 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (160e3)*0.6 / (8.314*520) | Answer: 22.21 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.17 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 11 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.17, t = 11 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.17*11) | Answer: 0.8459

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.25 /min) is to reach 70% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.25, X = 70 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.7) / 0.25 | Answer: 4.816 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.41 /min) reaches 70% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.41, X = 70 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.7 / (0.41*(1 - 0.7)) | Answer: 5.691 min

question: For a reaction with A = 2e10 /s and activation energy 70 kJ/mol at 410 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 2, Ea = 70, Tk = 410 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 2e10 * exp(-70e3 / (8.314*410)) | Answer: 24.13 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.98 and bottoms xW = 0.06, with relative volatility alpha = 2.4. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.98, xw = 0.06, al = 2.4 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.98/0.02)(0.94/0.06)] / ln(2.4) | Answer: 7.588 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.85 and x = 0.37. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.85, x = 0.37 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.85/0.15) / (0.37/0.63) | Answer: 9.649

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.71 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 45 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.71, Psat = 45 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.71 * 45 | Answer: 31.95 kPa

question: A stream of 1.6 kg/s with specific heat 2.6 kJ/kg-K is heated through 80 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 1.6, cp = 2.6, dT = 80 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 1.6*2.6*80 | Answer: 332.8 kW

question: A reactor of volume 1.6 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 4.4 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 1.6, Q = 4.4 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 1.6 / 4.4 | Answer: 0.3636 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 8.3e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 3 mm with a concentration difference of 150 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 8.3, L = 3, dC = 150 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (8.3e-9)*150 / (3e-3) | Answer: 415 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 9 min and steady-state gain 2. For a step input of magnitude 20, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 9, K = 2, M = 20 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 2 * 20 | Answer: 40 units

question: A reactor operates at a space time of 16.1 min. Find its space velocity in per hour.
solution: Given: tau = 16.1 | Formula: SV = 60 / tau  (per hour) | Substitute: SV = 60 / 16.1 | Answer: 3.727 /h

question: An aircraft wing of area 105 m^2 flies at 170 m/s (air density 1 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 1.1. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 105, V = 170, rho = 1, CL = 1.1 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1*(170)^2*105*1.1 / 1000 | Answer: 1669 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 55 m^2 flies at 180 m/s (density 1.225 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.09. Find the drag force in kN.
A specimen under stress 330 MPa shows an elastic strain of 1.1e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 330, eps = 1.1 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 330 / (1.1e-3) MPa = 300 GPa | Answer: 300 GPa

question: A block of mass 41 kg has a volume of 1e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 41, V = 1 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 41 / (1e-3) | Answer: 41000 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 1400 mm is heated through 65 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 11e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 1400, dT = 65, al = 11 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 1400*11e-6*65 | Answer: 1.001 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 30 ohm, R2 = 55 ohm and R3 = 35 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 30, R2 = 55, R3 = 35 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 55*35 / 30 | Answer: 64.17 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 1000 ohm and gauge factor 2.1 experiences a strain of 1150e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 1000, GF = 2.1, eps = 1150 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 1000*2.1*1150e-6 | Answer: 2415 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 10.32 when the true value is 10. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10.32, true = 10 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10.32 - 10| / 10 * 100 | Answer: 3.2 %

question: Annual demand is 23500 units, ordering cost 150 per order and holding cost 32 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 23500, S = 150, H = 32 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*23500*150 / 32) | Answer: 469.4 units

question: An asset costs 420000 with salvage value 30000 after 7 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 420000, Sv = 30000, n = 7 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (420000 - 30000) / 7 | Answer: 55714 per year

question: A product sells for 500 per unit with variable cost 20 per unit and fixed costs 45000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 500, V = 20, F = 45000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 45000 / (500 - 20) | Answer: 93.75 units

question: Find the present worth of 130000 received 7 years from now at an interest rate of 9% per year.
solution: Given: F = 130000, n = 7, i = 9 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 130000 / (1 + 0.09)^7 | Answer: 71114 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.92, 0.92 and 0.96 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.92, r2 = 0.92, r3 = 0.96 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.92*0.92*0.96 | Answer: 0.8125

question: A process produces 28 defective items in a batch of 15500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 28, N = 15500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 28/15500 * 1e6 | Answer: 1806 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -3x^3 + 5x^2 + x - 7 evaluated at x = 5.
For f(x) = 4x^3 - 6x^2 - 8x + 4, find f''(x) at x = -2.
Evaluate the definite integral of (3x^2 - 6x - 2) dx from x = -2 to x = 3.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = 3x^3/3 + -6x^2/2 + -2x | Evaluate F(3) - F(-2) | Answer: 10
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 3x^2 + 12x - 2 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[0, 3], [0, -7]].
solution: Given: a = 0, b = 3, c = 0, d = -7 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (0)(-7) - (3)(0) | Answer: 0

question: Find the determinant of [[2, -6, -1], [-2, 1, -3], [4, 0, -1]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: 86

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[8, 8], [5, 4]].
solution: Trace tr = 12, Determinant = -8 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 12.63

question: Solve for x: 1x + -5y = -6 and 0x + -2y = 3.
solution: Determinant = 1*-2 - -5*0 = -2 | x = (e d - b f) / det = -13.5 | Answer: x = -13.5
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 50, 15, 81, 31, 39.
solution: Sum = 216 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 43.2 | Answer: 43.2

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 14, 39, 25, 16, 24.
solution: Mean = 23.6 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 9.864

question: Find the slope of the line through (-2, -5) and (-6, -5).
solution: Given: x1 = -2, y1 = -5, x2 = -6, y2 = -5 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (-5 - -5) / (-6 - -2) | Answer: 0

question: Find the distance between the points (7, -6) and (-9, 4).
solution: Given: x1 = 7, y1 = -6, x2 = -9, y2 = 4 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-16)^2 + (10)^2) | Answer: 18.87 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (-5,-2), (8,2), (-5,-3).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 6.5 sq units

question: Evaluate the number of combinations C(20, 10).
solution: Given: n = 20, r = 10 | Formula: C(n, r) = n! / (r! (n - r)!) | Substitute: C(20, 10) = 20! / (10! * 10!) | Answer: 184756

question: Find the 5th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 10 and common difference 2.
solution: Given: a = 10, d = 2, n = 5 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = 10 + (5 - 1)*2 | Answer: 18

question: Find the sum of the first 16 terms of an AP with first term -8 and common difference -7.
solution: Given: a = -8, d = -7, n = 16 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 16/2 [2*-8 + (16-1)*-7] | Answer: -968

question: Find the 6th term of a geometric progression with first term 9 and common ratio 3.
solution: Given: a = 9, r = 3, n = 6 | Formula: a_n = a r^(n-1) | Substitute: a_n = 9 * 3^(6-1) | Answer: 2187

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 28500 at 4.1% per annum for 1 years.
solution: Given: P = 28500, R = 4.1, Tt = 1 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 28500 * 4.1 * 1 / 100 | Answer: 1168 currency units

question: Find the amount when 27500 is invested at 4.3% per annum compounded annually for 3 years.
solution: Given: P = 27500, R = 4.3, Tt = 3 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 27500 * (1 + 4.3/100)^3 | Answer: 31202 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (-1, 7, -2) and (-1, -8, 7).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (-4, -5, -5) and (-6, 2, 6).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 68.99

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (-6, -5, 2) and (-3, 2, 0).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 74.03 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number 5 + 5i.
solution: Given: a = 5, b = 5 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((5)^2 + (5)^2) | Answer: 7.071

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number 4 + -6i.
solution: Given: a = 4, b = -6 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(-6, 4) | Answer: -56.31 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -2x^3 - 5x^2 + 3x + 1 at x = 5.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-126 with initial guess x0=7, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.8 and ordinates 19, 18, 0, 1, 20, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 379 and 244.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 379 and 244 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 44 and 14.
solution: Given: a = 44, b = 14 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 44*14 / 2 | Answer: 308
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 54 mm carries an axial tensile load of 118 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 19 mm and length 2300 mm carries an axial load of 75 kN. Take E = 210 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 75 mm transmits a torque of 2250 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 75, Tt = 2250 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(2250*1000) / (pi*(75)^3) | Answer: 27.16 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 45 mm and length 1200 mm carries a torque of 1800 N-m. With G = 45 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (45)^4 / 32 = 402578 mm^4 | theta = (1800*1000)(1200) / (45000 * 402578) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 6.831 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 101 mm wide and 120 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 101, h = 120 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 101*(120)^2 / 6 | Answer: 242400 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (64 mm x 130 mm) carries a bending moment of 21 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (72 mm x 100 mm) has effective length 1800 mm and E = 200 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 490 MPa is designed for a working stress of 130 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 490, sw = 130 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 490 / 130 | Answer: 3.769

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 300 mm and wall thickness 6 mm carries an internal pressure of 0.7 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 300, t = 6, P = 0.7 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 0.7*300 / (2*6) | Answer: 17.5 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 960 K and 440 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 960, Tc = 440 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 440/960) * 100 | Answer: 54.17 %

question: A refrigerator works between 265 K (cold) and 318 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 265, Th = 318 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 265 / (318 - 265) | Answer: 5

question: A heat pump operates between 260 K and 318 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 260, Th = 318 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 318 / (318 - 260) | Answer: 5.483

question: 7.6 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 80 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 7.6, dT = 80 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 7.6 * 0.718 * 80 | Answer: 436.5 kJ

question: 5.3 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 135 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 5.3, dT = 135 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 5.3 * 1.005 * 135 | Answer: 719.1 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 3.1 m^3 at 450 K with mass 3.5 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 3.1, Tk = 450, m = 3.5 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 3.5*0.287*450 / 3.1 | Answer: 145.8 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 1.7 kg of air expands isothermally at 300 K from volume V1 to 5*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1.7, Tk = 300, ratio = 5 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 1.7*0.287*300*ln(5) | Answer: 235.6 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 3 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.12 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 3, D = 0.12 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*3*0.12 / 0.001 | Answer: 360000

question: Water flows at 2.1 m/s through a pipe of diameter 100 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 15.7 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 15.7 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*15.7 / 1000 | Answer: 154 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 6.3 m. Taking Cv = 0.98, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 6.3, cv = 0.98 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.98*sqrt(2*9.81*6.3) | Answer: 10.9 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 400 mm) water flows at 0.8 m/s. It contracts to diameter 130 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
Water flows at 2.1 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.33 m and length 150 m. With friction factor f = 0.039, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 29 teeth drives a gear of 54 teeth. If the pinion runs at 700 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 29, z2 = 54, N1 = 700 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 700*29 / 54 | Answer: 375.9 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 510 mm rotates at 900 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 510, N = 900 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.51)*900 / 60 | Answer: 24.03 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 6.8 kW at 550 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 6.8, N = 550 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(6.8*1000) / (2*pi*550) | Answer: 118.1 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 8.9 kg rotates at radius 0.25 m at 750 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 2600 N/m and mass 1.7 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 2600, m = 1.7 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(2600/1.7) | Answer: 6.224 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 9.4 m^2 and thickness 0.36 m has conductivity k = 48.1 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 25 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 9.4, L = 0.36, k = 48.1, dT = 25 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 48.1*9.4*25 / 0.36 | Answer: 31399 W

question: A surface of area 5.4 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 185 W/m^2-K to surroundings 120 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 5.4, h = 185, dT = 120 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 185*5.4*120 | Answer: 119880 W

question: In a counter-flow heat exchanger the terminal temperature differences are 115 deg C and 20 deg C. Find the log mean temperature difference (LMTD) in deg C.
solution: Given: dT1 = 115, dT2 = 20 | Formula: LMTD = (dT1 - dT2) / ln(dT1/dT2) | Substitute: LMTD = (115 - 20) / ln(115/20) | Answer: 54.31 deg C

question: In turning, cutting speed = 220 m/min, feed = 0.17 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2.7 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 220, f = 0.17, d = 2.7 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*220*0.17*2.7 | Answer: 100980 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 400 mm is turned at 400 rpm with a feed of 0.19 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 400, N = 400, f = 0.19 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 400 / (0.19*400) | Answer: 5.263 min

question: A resistor of 188 ohm carries a current of 1.3 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 188, I = 1.3 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 1.3 * 188 | Answer: 244.4 V

question: Three resistors 78 ohm, 36 ohm and 57 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 78, R2 = 36, R3 = 57 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 78 + 36 + 57 | Answer: 171 ohm

question: Two resistors 54 ohm and 41 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 54, R2 = 41 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 54*41 / (54+41) | Answer: 23.31 ohm

question: A device draws 11.2 A at 240 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 240, I = 11.2 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 240 * 11.2 | Answer: 2688 W

question: A current of 1.1 A flows through a 146 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 1.1, R = 146 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (1.1)^2 * 146 | Answer: 176.7 W

question: Two capacitors 20.2 uF and 30.5 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 20.2, C2 = 30.5 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 20.2*30.5 / (20.2+30.5) | Answer: 12.15 uF

question: A resistor 4 kohm and capacitor 17.9 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 4, C = 17.9 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (4k)(17.9u) = 71.6 ms | Answer: 71.6 ms

question: An inductor 151.9 mH is in series with 77 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 151.9, R = 77 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (151.9e-3) / 77 | Answer: 1.973 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 146.8 mH inductor at 520 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 146.8, f = 520 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (520)(146.8e-3) | Answer: 479.6 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 17.8 uF capacitor at 200 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 17.8, f = 200 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (200)(17.8e-6)) | Answer: 44.71 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 92 ohm, XL = 109 ohm and XC = 137 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 92, XL = 109, XC = 137 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(92^2 + (109 - 137)^2) | Answer: 96.17 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 95.5 mH and C = 6.7 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 95.5, C = 6.7 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(95.5e-3 * 6.7e-6)) | Answer: 199 Hz

question: A capacitor of 59.1 uF is charged to 330 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 59.1, V = 330 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*59.1e-6*(330)^2 | Answer: 3218 mJ

question: An alternating voltage has a peak value of 258 V. Find its RMS value.
solution: Given: Vp = 258 | Formula: Vrms = Vp / sqrt(2) | Substitute: Vrms = 258 / sqrt(2) | Answer: 182.4 V

question: A transformer has primary voltage 340 V with 210 primary turns and 470 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 340, N1 = 210, N2 = 470 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 340 * 470/210 | Answer: 761 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 420 V and draws an armature current of 5 A. If the armature resistance is 1.47 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 420, Ia = 5, Ra = 1.47 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 420 - 5*1.47 | Answer: 412.6 V

question: A 4-pole induction motor on a 60 Hz supply runs at 1080 rpm. Find the slip (%).
formula: s = (Ns - N) / Ns,  Ns = 120 f / P

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 75 A at 433 V (line) with a power factor of 0.79. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 75, VL = 433, pf = 0.79 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*433*75*0.79 / 1000 | Answer: 44.44 kW

question: A load has real power 80 kW and apparent power 120 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 80, S = 120 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 80 / 120 | Answer: 0.6667

question: A machine delivers 90 kW output while drawing 117 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 90, Pi = 117 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 90/117 * 100 | Answer: 76.92 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 30 V across R1 = 48 ohm and R2 = 24 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 30, R1 = 48, R2 = 24 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 30*24 / (48+24) | Answer: 10 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 160 kohm and Rin = 46 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 160, Rin = 46 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 160 / 46 | Answer: 3.478

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 120 kohm and Rg = 34 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 120, Rg = 34 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 120/34 | Answer: 4.529

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 7392. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 7392 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(7392) | Answer: 38.69 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 3.8 m carries a central point load of 50 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.8, W = 50 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 50*3.8 / 4 | Answer: 47.5 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 8.8 m carries a UDL of 10 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 8.8, w = 10 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 10*(8.8)^2 / 8 | Answer: 96.8 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 5.4 m carries a point load 40 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.4, W = 40 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 40*5.4 | Answer: 216 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 2 m carries a UDL of 24 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 2, w = 24 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 24*(2)^2 / 2 | Answer: 48 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.4 m carries a point load 10 kN at distance 3.3 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 6.4, a = 3.3, W = 10 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 10*(6.4 - 3.3) / 6.4 | Answer: 4.844 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 7.3 m) carries a central point load 20 kN. With E = 200 GPa and I = 120e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=20000 N, L=7300.0 mm, E=200000 MPa, I=120e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 6.754 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 5.1 m carries a UDL of 24 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.1, w = 24 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 24*(5.1)^2 / 12 | Answer: 52.02 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 380 mm, clear cover 25 mm and main bars of diameter 16 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 380, c = 25, dia = 16 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 380 - 25 - 16/2 | Answer: 347 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 26.3 m^2 carrying a factored load of 12.8 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 26.3, w = 12.8 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 12.8 * 26.3 | Answer: 336.6 kN

question: For a bar of diameter 12 mm with design bond stress 1.2 MPa and steel stress 435 MPa, find the development length in mm.
solution: Given: dia = 12, tbd = 1.2, fs = 435 | Formula: Ld = phi fs / (4 tau_bd) | Substitute: Ld = 12*435 / (4*1.2) | Answer: 1088 mm

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 4.4 m, unit weight 19 kN/m^3, phi = 28 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 2.3 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 21 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 2.3, g = 21 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (21 - 9.81)*2.3 | Answer: 25.74 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 3.5e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.7, area = 2.2e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 3.5, i = 0.7, A = 2.2 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (3.5e-4)*0.7*(2.2e-3) | Answer: 539 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.2 m, bed slope 0.007 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.03. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 4.1 m under a head of 0.8 m. Taking Cd = 0.62 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 2.2 m wide carries a discharge of 20.9 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 230 m and design speed 80 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 230, V = 80 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (80)^2 / (127*230) | Answer: 0.2191
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: For a design speed of 95 km/h with allowable superelevation 0.08 and lateral friction 0.16, find the minimum curve radius in m.
A tank of volume 310 m^3 treats a flow of 125 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 310, Q = 125 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 310 / 125 | Answer: 2.48 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 350 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.18 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 5 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 350, k = 0.18, t = 5 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 350*(1 - e^(-0.18*5)) | Answer: 207.7 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.45, rainfall intensity 80 mm/h over a catchment of 48.5 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.45, i = 80, A = 48.5 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.45*80*48.5 / 360 | Answer: 4.85 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.04 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 560 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.04, M = 560 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 560*(30+0.04)/30 | Answer: 560.7 m

question: Convert the decimal number 161 to binary.
solution: Divide 161 by 2 repeatedly, recording remainders | Reading remainders in reverse gives 10100001 | Answer: 10100001 (binary)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 2 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the decimal number 4043 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 4043 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: FCB (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the 8-bit binary number 00010001 to decimal.
solution: Binary 00010001 = sum of bit-weights | Answer: 17 (decimal)
formula: Sum each bit times its positional weight (2^i)

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 10010101 and 11001000.
solution: XOR: 01011101 | Count of 1s = 5 | Answer: 5
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 800 megabits is sent over a link of 32 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 800, B = 32 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 800 / 32 | Answer: 25 s

question: A link has bandwidth 77 Mbps and round-trip time 140 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 77, R = 140 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 77e6 * 140e-3 bits = 10780 kb | Answer: 10780 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.97, cache access time 7 ns and main-memory access time 60 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.97, tc = 7, tm = 60 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.97*7 + (1 - 0.97)*60 | Answer: 8.59 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 232134 elements?
solution: Given: n = 232134 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(232134)) + 1 | Answer: 18

question: An O(n^2) algorithm performs c*n^2 basic operations. If c = 1 and n = 300, how many operations are performed?
solution: Given: n = 300 | Formula: operations = n^2 | Substitute: = (300)^2 | Answer: 90000

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.007, memory access time 180 ns and page-fault service time 3 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 3 ms = 3000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.007)*180 + 0.007*3000000.0 ns | Answer: 21.18 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 3 m^3 at 290 kPa and 510 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 3, P = 290, Tk = 510 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (290e3)*3 / (8.314*510) | Answer: 205.2 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.33 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 4 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.33, t = 4 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.33*4) | Answer: 0.7329

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.47 /min) is to reach 65% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.47, X = 65 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.65) / 0.47 | Answer: 2.234 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.47 /min) reaches 70% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.47, X = 70 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.7 / (0.47*(1 - 0.7)) | Answer: 4.965 min

question: For a reaction with A = 3e10 /s and activation energy 75 kJ/mol at 400 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 3, Ea = 75, Tk = 400 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 3e10 * exp(-75e3 / (8.314*400)) | Answer: 4.817 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.96 and bottoms xW = 0.09, with relative volatility alpha = 2.4. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.96, xw = 0.09, al = 2.4 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.96/0.04)(0.91/0.09)] / ln(2.4) | Answer: 6.273 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.72 and x = 0.35. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.72, x = 0.35 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.72/0.28) / (0.35/0.65) | Answer: 4.776

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.74 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 35 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.74, Psat = 35 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.74 * 35 | Answer: 25.9 kPa

question: A stream of 1.1 kg/s with specific heat 1.5 kJ/kg-K is heated through 110 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 1.1, cp = 1.5, dT = 110 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 1.1*1.5*110 | Answer: 181.5 kW

question: A reactor of volume 18.2 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 4.5 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 18.2, Q = 4.5 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 18.2 / 4.5 | Answer: 4.044 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 5.7e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 2 mm with a concentration difference of 10 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 5.7, L = 2, dC = 10 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (5.7e-9)*10 / (2e-3) | Answer: 28.5 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 5.5 min and steady-state gain 1.8. For a step input of magnitude 9, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 5.5, K = 1.8, M = 9 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 1.8 * 9 | Answer: 16.2 units

question: A reactor operates at a space time of 19.7 min. Find its space velocity in per hour.
solution: Given: tau = 19.7 | Formula: SV = 60 / tau  (per hour) | Substitute: SV = 60 / 19.7 | Answer: 3.046 /h

question: An aircraft wing of area 40 m^2 flies at 210 m/s (air density 0.7 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 1.1. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 40, V = 210, rho = 0.7, CL = 1.1 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.7*(210)^2*40*1.1 / 1000 | Answer: 679.1 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 25 m^2 flies at 150 m/s (density 0.7 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.04. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 25, V = 150, rho = 0.7, CD = 0.04 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.7*(150)^2*25*0.04 / 1000 | Answer: 7.875 kN

question: An aircraft flies at 270 m/s where the speed of sound is 340 m/s. Find the Mach number.
solution: Given: V = 270, a = 340 | Formula: M = V / a | Substitute: M = 270 / 340 | Answer: 0.7941

question: A specimen under stress 350 MPa shows an elastic strain of 1.4e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 350, eps = 1.4 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 350 / (1.4e-3) MPa = 250 GPa | Answer: 250 GPa

question: A block of mass 27 kg has a volume of 5e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 27, V = 5 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 27 / (5e-3) | Answer: 5400 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 2900 mm is heated through 115 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 12e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 2900, dT = 115, al = 12 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 2900*12e-6*115 | Answer: 4.002 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 25 ohm, R2 = 95 ohm and R3 = 255 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 25, R2 = 95, R3 = 255 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 95*255 / 25 | Answer: 969 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 120 ohm and gauge factor 2 experiences a strain of 200e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 120, GF = 2, eps = 200 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 120*2*200e-6 | Answer: 48 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 9.18 when the true value is 100. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.18, true = 100 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.18 - 100| / 100 * 100 | Answer: 90.82 %

question: Annual demand is 31000 units, ordering cost 90 per order and holding cost 3 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 31000, S = 90, H = 3 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*31000*90 / 3) | Answer: 1364 units

question: An asset costs 110000 with salvage value 14000 after 20 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 110000, Sv = 14000, n = 20 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (110000 - 14000) / 20 | Answer: 4800 per year

question: A product sells for 400 per unit with variable cost 130 per unit and fixed costs 40000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 400, V = 130, F = 40000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 40000 / (400 - 130) | Answer: 148.1 units

question: Find the present worth of 25000 received 6 years from now at an interest rate of 8% per year.
solution: Given: F = 25000, n = 6, i = 8 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 25000 / (1 + 0.08)^6 | Answer: 15754 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.95, 0.95 and 0.93 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.95, r2 = 0.95, r3 = 0.93 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.95*0.95*0.93 | Answer: 0.8393

question: A process produces 11 defective items in a batch of 11500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 11, N = 11500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 11/11500 * 1e6 | Answer: 956.5 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -5x^3 - 6x^2 - 2x - 3 evaluated at x = -4.
For f(x) = -5x^3 + 5x^2 + 4x + 6, find f''(x) at x = -3.
Evaluate the definite integral of (3x^2 + x + 7) dx from x = -1 to x = 3.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = 3x^3/3 + 1x^2/2 + 7x | Evaluate F(3) - F(-1) | Answer: 60
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 5x^2 - 4x - 4 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[1, -5], [2, -6]].
solution: Given: a = 1, b = -5, c = 2, d = -6 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (1)(-6) - (-5)(2) | Answer: 4

question: Find the determinant of [[-5, -1, 1], [1, 3, 1], [-6, 1, -2]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: 58

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[3, 1], [7, -8]].
solution: Trace tr = -5, Determinant = -31 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 3.603

question: Solve for x: 6x + -3y = 1 and 3x + -5y = 8.
solution: Determinant = 6*-5 - -3*3 = -21 | x = (e d - b f) / det = -0.9048 | Answer: x = -0.9048
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 69, 61, 77, 69, 63.
solution: Sum = 339 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 67.8 | Answer: 67.8

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 28, 37, 46, 13, 45.
solution: Mean = 33.8 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 13.7

question: Find the slope of the line through (-2, -8) and (-3, 8).
solution: Given: x1 = -2, y1 = -8, x2 = -3, y2 = 8 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (8 - -8) / (-3 - -2) | Answer: -16

question: Find the distance between the points (5, 3) and (2, 4).
solution: Given: x1 = 5, y1 = 3, x2 = 2, y2 = 4 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-3)^2 + (1)^2) | Answer: 3.162 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (3,1), (-2,2), (3,-7).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 20 sq units

question: Evaluate the number of combinations C(7, 1).
solution: Given: n = 7, r = 1 | Formula: C(n, r) = n! / (r! (n - r)!) | Substitute: C(7, 1) = 7! / (1! * 6!) | Answer: 7

question: Find the 40th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -16 and common difference -3.
solution: Given: a = -16, d = -3, n = 40 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -16 + (40 - 1)*-3 | Answer: -133

question: Find the sum of the first 21 terms of an AP with first term 13 and common difference 7.
solution: Given: a = 13, d = 7, n = 21 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 21/2 [2*13 + (21-1)*7] | Answer: 1743

question: Find the 7th term of a geometric progression with first term 3 and common ratio 2.
solution: Given: a = 3, r = 2, n = 7 | Formula: a_n = a r^(n-1) | Substitute: a_n = 3 * 2^(7-1) | Answer: 192

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 48500 at 13.4% per annum for 9 years.
solution: Given: P = 48500, R = 13.4, Tt = 9 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 48500 * 13.4 * 9 / 100 | Answer: 58491 currency units

question: Find the amount when 19000 is invested at 5.7% per annum compounded annually for 4 years.
solution: Given: P = 19000, R = 5.7, Tt = 4 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 19000 * (1 + 5.7/100)^4 | Answer: 23717 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (-8, 0, -3) and (1, -7, 4).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (2, -1, -2) and (-5, -5, 6).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 22.02

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (-4, 5, -4) and (3, -3, -1).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 134.3 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number -12 + 6i.
solution: Given: a = -12, b = 6 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((-12)^2 + (6)^2) | Answer: 13.42

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number -5 + -2i.
solution: Given: a = -5, b = -2 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(-2, -5) | Answer: -158.2 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -3x^3 - 6x^2 - 7x + 2 at x = -4.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-74 with initial guess x0=2, find x1 (one iteration).
solution: Given: N = 74, x0 = 2 | Formula: x1 = x0 - (x0^2 - N)/(2 x0) | Substitute: x1 = 2 - ((2)^2 - 74)/(2*2) | Answer: 19.5

question: Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.8 and ordinates 2, 20, 18, 3, 0, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 280 and 559.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 280 and 559 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 13 and 74.
solution: Given: a = 13, b = 74 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 13*74 / 1 | Answer: 962
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 25 mm carries an axial tensile load of 107 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 26 mm and length 2500 mm carries an axial load of 53 kN. Take E = 70 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 34 mm transmits a torque of 2850 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 34, Tt = 2850 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(2850*1000) / (pi*(34)^3) | Answer: 369.3 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 34 mm and length 1600 mm carries a torque of 450 N-m. With G = 80 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (34)^4 / 32 = 131194 mm^4 | theta = (450*1000)(1600) / (80000 * 131194) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 3.931 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 50 mm wide and 120 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 50, h = 120 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 50*(120)^2 / 6 | Answer: 120000 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (64 mm x 250 mm) carries a bending moment of 33 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (43 mm x 140 mm) has effective length 2800 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 760 MPa is designed for a working stress of 70 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 760, sw = 70 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 760 / 70 | Answer: 10.86

question: A steel bar is fully restrained and heated through 75 deg C. With E = 210 GPa and alpha = 11e-6 /deg C, find the thermal stress in MPa.
solution: Given: dT = 75, E = 210, al = 11 | Formula: sigma = E alpha (dT) | Substitute: sigma = 210000 * 11e-6 * 75 | Answer: 173.2 MPa

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 800 mm and wall thickness 20 mm carries an internal pressure of 2 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 800, t = 20, P = 2 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 2*800 / (2*20) | Answer: 40 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 820 K and 450 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 820, Tc = 450 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 450/820) * 100 | Answer: 45.12 %

question: A refrigerator works between 275 K (cold) and 310 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 275, Th = 310 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 275 / (310 - 275) | Answer: 7.857

question: A heat pump operates between 269 K and 302 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 269, Th = 302 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 302 / (302 - 269) | Answer: 9.152

question: 2.4 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 150 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.4, dT = 150 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 2.4 * 0.718 * 150 | Answer: 258.5 kJ

question: 4 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 115 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4, dT = 115 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 4 * 1.005 * 115 | Answer: 462.3 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 3.2 m^3 at 550 K with mass 2.7 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 3.2, Tk = 550, m = 2.7 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 2.7*0.287*550 / 3.2 | Answer: 133.2 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 2 kg of air expands isothermally at 420 K from volume V1 to 5*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2, Tk = 420, ratio = 5 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 2*0.287*420*ln(5) | Answer: 388 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 0.6 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.25 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 0.6, D = 0.25 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*0.6*0.25 / 0.001 | Answer: 150000

question: Water flows at 2.1 m/s through a pipe of diameter 160 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 12.7 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 12.7 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*12.7 / 1000 | Answer: 124.6 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 9.6 m. Taking Cv = 0.97, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 9.6, cv = 0.97 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.97*sqrt(2*9.81*9.6) | Answer: 13.31 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 330 mm) water flows at 0.6 m/s. It contracts to diameter 50 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 330, d2 = 50, V1 = 0.6 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 0.6*(330/50)^2 | Answer: 26.14 m/s

question: Water flows at 2.3 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.33 m and length 330 m. With friction factor f = 0.028, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 24 teeth drives a gear of 67 teeth. If the pinion runs at 300 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 24, z2 = 67, N1 = 300 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 300*24 / 67 | Answer: 107.5 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 460 mm rotates at 250 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 460, N = 250 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.46)*250 / 60 | Answer: 6.021 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 35.7 kW at 250 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 35.7, N = 250 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(35.7*1000) / (2*pi*250) | Answer: 1364 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 6.4 kg rotates at radius 0.24 m at 750 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 11000 N/m and mass 5.4 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 11000, m = 5.4 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(11000/5.4) | Answer: 7.183 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 7.6 m^2 and thickness 0.34 m has conductivity k = 26.9 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 85 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 7.6, L = 0.34, k = 26.9, dT = 85 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 26.9*7.6*85 / 0.34 | Answer: 51110 W

question: A surface of area 3.2 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 110 W/m^2-K to surroundings 95 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 3.2, h = 110, dT = 95 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 110*3.2*95 | Answer: 33440 W

question: In a counter-flow heat exchanger the terminal temperature differences are 85 deg C and 30 deg C. Find the log mean temperature difference (LMTD) in deg C.
solution: Given: dT1 = 85, dT2 = 30 | Formula: LMTD = (dT1 - dT2) / ln(dT1/dT2) | Substitute: LMTD = (85 - 30) / ln(85/30) | Answer: 52.81 deg C

question: In turning, cutting speed = 110 m/min, feed = 0.11 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2.2 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 110, f = 0.11, d = 2.2 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*110*0.11*2.2 | Answer: 26620 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 210 mm is turned at 650 rpm with a feed of 0.14 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 210, N = 650, f = 0.14 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 210 / (0.14*650) | Answer: 2.308 min

question: A resistor of 86 ohm carries a current of 6.2 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 86, I = 6.2 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 6.2 * 86 | Answer: 533.2 V

question: Three resistors 66 ohm, 65 ohm and 97 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 66, R2 = 65, R3 = 97 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 66 + 65 + 97 | Answer: 228 ohm

question: Two resistors 23 ohm and 65 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 23, R2 = 65 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 23*65 / (23+65) | Answer: 16.99 ohm

question: A device draws 5.3 A at 60 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 60, I = 5.3 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 60 * 5.3 | Answer: 318 W

question: A current of 0.6 A flows through a 31 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 0.6, R = 31 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (0.6)^2 * 31 | Answer: 11.16 W

question: Two capacitors 36.3 uF and 49.7 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 36.3, C2 = 49.7 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 36.3*49.7 / (36.3+49.7) | Answer: 20.98 uF

question: A resistor 4 kohm and capacitor 8.9 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 4, C = 8.9 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (4k)(8.9u) = 35.6 ms | Answer: 35.6 ms

question: An inductor 311.5 mH is in series with 175 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 311.5, R = 175 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (311.5e-3) / 175 | Answer: 1.78 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 53 mH inductor at 60 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 53, f = 60 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (60)(53e-3) | Answer: 19.98 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 42.9 uF capacitor at 680 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 42.9, f = 680 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (680)(42.9e-6)) | Answer: 5.456 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 95 ohm, XL = 83 ohm and XC = 120 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 95, XL = 83, XC = 120 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(95^2 + (83 - 120)^2) | Answer: 102 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 62.8 mH and C = 3.9 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 62.8, C = 3.9 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(62.8e-3 * 3.9e-6)) | Answer: 321.6 Hz

question: A capacitor of 35.1 uF is charged to 45 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 35.1, V = 45 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*35.1e-6*(45)^2 | Answer: 35.54 mJ

question: An alternating voltage has a peak value of 300 V. Find its RMS value.
solution: Given: Vp = 300 | Formula: Vrms = Vp / sqrt(2) | Substitute: Vrms = 300 / sqrt(2) | Answer: 212.1 V

question: A transformer has primary voltage 140 V with 350 primary turns and 290 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 140, N1 = 350, N2 = 290 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 140 * 290/350 | Answer: 116 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 210 V and draws an armature current of 18 A. If the armature resistance is 0.94 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 210, Ia = 18, Ra = 0.94 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 210 - 18*0.94 | Answer: 193.1 V

question: A 6-pole induction motor on a 50 Hz supply runs at 760 rpm. Find the slip (%).
formula: s = (Ns - N) / Ns,  Ns = 120 f / P

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 30 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.82. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 30, VL = 400, pf = 0.82 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*400*30*0.82 / 1000 | Answer: 17.04 kW

question: A load has real power 70 kW and apparent power 190 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 70, S = 190 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 70 / 190 | Answer: 0.3684

question: A machine delivers 120 kW output while drawing 202 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 120, Pi = 202 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 120/202 * 100 | Answer: 59.41 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 23 V across R1 = 27 ohm and R2 = 3 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 23, R1 = 27, R2 = 3 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 23*3 / (27+3) | Answer: 2.3 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 160 kohm and Rin = 30 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 160, Rin = 30 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 160 / 30 | Answer: 5.333

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 30 kohm and Rg = 19 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 30, Rg = 19 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 30/19 | Answer: 2.579

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 6526. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 6526 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(6526) | Answer: 38.15 dB

question: A first-order system has a time constant of 4.2 s. Find the time (in s) to reach 63.2% of its final value.
solution: For a first-order step response, y = 1 - e^(-t/tau) | y = 0.632 when t = tau | Answer: 4.2 s
formula: At t = tau the response reaches 63.2% (one time constant)

question: A simply supported beam of span 7.9 m carries a central point load of 70 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.12 /min) is to reach 70% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.93 and bottoms xW = 0.05, with relative volatility alpha = 2.8. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).

solution: Given: Tc = 274, Th = 316 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 316 / (316 - 274) | Answer: 7.524

question: 3.7 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 70 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.7, dT = 70 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 3.7 * 0.718 * 70 | Answer: 186 kJ

question: 7.5 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 155 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 7.5, dT = 155 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 7.5 * 1.005 * 155 | Answer: 1168 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 1.8 m^3 at 460 K with mass 5.4 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 1.8, Tk = 460, m = 5.4 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 5.4*0.287*460 / 1.8 | Answer: 396.1 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 4.7 kg of air expands isothermally at 330 K from volume V1 to 2*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.7, Tk = 330, ratio = 2 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 4.7*0.287*330*ln(2) | Answer: 308.5 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 4 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.19 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 4, D = 0.19 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*4*0.19 / 0.001 | Answer: 760000

question: Water flows at 1.8 m/s through a pipe of diameter 250 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 3.7 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
