solution: Given: h = 3.7 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*3.7 / 1000 | Answer: 36.3 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 10.1 m. Taking Cv = 0.99, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 10.1, cv = 0.99 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.99*sqrt(2*9.81*10.1) | Answer: 13.94 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 230 mm) water flows at 1.3 m/s. It contracts to diameter 60 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 230, d2 = 60, V1 = 1.3 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 1.3*(230/60)^2 | Answer: 19.1 m/s

question: Water flows at 1.2 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.12 m and length 140 m. With friction factor f = 0.035, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 29 teeth drives a gear of 63 teeth. If the pinion runs at 900 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 29, z2 = 63, N1 = 900 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 900*29 / 63 | Answer: 414.3 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 210 mm rotates at 350 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 210, N = 350 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.21)*350 / 60 | Answer: 3.848 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 11.1 kW at 1200 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 11.1, N = 1200 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(11.1*1000) / (2*pi*1200) | Answer: 88.33 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 4 kg rotates at radius 0.45 m at 600 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 4300 N/m and mass 19.5 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 4300, m = 19.5 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(4300/19.5) | Answer: 2.363 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 6.8 m^2 and thickness 0.23 m has conductivity k = 34.2 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 30 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 6.8, L = 0.23, k = 34.2, dT = 30 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 34.2*6.8*30 / 0.23 | Answer: 30334 W

question: A surface of area 3.2 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 125 W/m^2-K to surroundings 125 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 3.2, h = 125, dT = 125 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 125*3.2*125 | Answer: 50000 W

question: In a counter-flow heat exchanger the terminal temperature differences are 105 deg C and 25 deg C. Find the log mean temperature difference (LMTD) in deg C.
solution: Given: dT1 = 105, dT2 = 25 | Formula: LMTD = (dT1 - dT2) / ln(dT1/dT2) | Substitute: LMTD = (105 - 25) / ln(105/25) | Answer: 55.75 deg C

question: In turning, cutting speed = 130 m/min, feed = 0.48 mm/rev, depth of cut = 1.5 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 130, f = 0.48, d = 1.5 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*130*0.48*1.5 | Answer: 93600 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 210 mm is turned at 950 rpm with a feed of 0.13 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 210, N = 950, f = 0.13 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 210 / (0.13*950) | Answer: 1.7 min

question: A resistor of 180 ohm carries a current of 1.2 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 180, I = 1.2 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 1.2 * 180 | Answer: 216 V

question: Three resistors 87 ohm, 48 ohm and 83 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 87, R2 = 48, R3 = 83 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 87 + 48 + 83 | Answer: 218 ohm

question: Two resistors 72 ohm and 63 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 72, R2 = 63 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 72*63 / (72+63) | Answer: 33.6 ohm

question: A device draws 0.5 A at 105 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 105, I = 0.5 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 105 * 0.5 | Answer: 52.5 W

question: A current of 7.5 A flows through a 62 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 7.5, R = 62 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (7.5)^2 * 62 | Answer: 3488 W

question: Two capacitors 35.8 uF and 43.8 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 35.8, C2 = 43.8 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 35.8*43.8 / (35.8+43.8) | Answer: 19.7 uF

question: A resistor 22 kohm and capacitor 7.3 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 22, C = 7.3 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (22k)(7.3u) = 160.6 ms | Answer: 160.6 ms

question: An inductor 136.2 mH is in series with 154 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 136.2, R = 154 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (136.2e-3) / 154 | Answer: 0.8844 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 125.7 mH inductor at 380 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 125.7, f = 380 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (380)(125.7e-3) | Answer: 300.1 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 48.5 uF capacitor at 800 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 48.5, f = 800 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (800)(48.5e-6)) | Answer: 4.102 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 46 ohm, XL = 36 ohm and XC = 140 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 46, XL = 36, XC = 140 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(46^2 + (36 - 140)^2) | Answer: 113.7 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 83.6 mH and C = 3.7 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 83.6, C = 3.7 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(83.6e-3 * 3.7e-6)) | Answer: 286.2 Hz

question: A capacitor of 28.3 uF is charged to 165 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 28.3, V = 165 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*28.3e-6*(165)^2 | Answer: 385.2 mJ

question: An alternating voltage has a peak value of 138 V. Find its RMS value.
solution: Given: Vp = 138 | Formula: Vrms = Vp / sqrt(2) | Substitute: Vrms = 138 / sqrt(2) | Answer: 97.58 V

question: A transformer has primary voltage 260 V with 860 primary turns and 430 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 260, N1 = 860, N2 = 430 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 260 * 430/860 | Answer: 130 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 140 V and draws an armature current of 47 A. If the armature resistance is 0.57 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 140, Ia = 47, Ra = 0.57 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 140 - 47*0.57 | Answer: 113.2 V

question: A 6-pole induction motor on a 60 Hz supply runs at 1100 rpm. Find the slip (%).
formula: s = (Ns - N) / Ns,  Ns = 120 f / P

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 45 A at 415 V (line) with a power factor of 0.96. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 45, VL = 415, pf = 0.96 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*415*45*0.96 / 1000 | Answer: 31.05 kW

question: A load has real power 15 kW and apparent power 185 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 15, S = 185 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 15 / 185 | Answer: 0.08108

question: A machine delivers 130 kW output while drawing 202 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 130, Pi = 202 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 130/202 * 100 | Answer: 64.36 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 20 V across R1 = 7 ohm and R2 = 16 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 20, R1 = 7, R2 = 16 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 20*16 / (7+16) | Answer: 13.91 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 110 kohm and Rin = 14 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 110, Rin = 14 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 110 / 14 | Answer: 7.857

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 90 kohm and Rg = 13 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 90, Rg = 13 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 90/13 | Answer: 7.923

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 9574. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 9574 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(9574) | Answer: 39.81 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 7.9 m carries a central point load of 55 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7.9, W = 55 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 55*7.9 / 4 | Answer: 108.6 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.6 m carries a UDL of 45 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.6, w = 45 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 45*(4.6)^2 / 8 | Answer: 119 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 1.1 m carries a point load 80 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 1.1, W = 80 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 80*1.1 | Answer: 88 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 2.6 m carries a UDL of 24 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 2.6, w = 24 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 24*(2.6)^2 / 2 | Answer: 81.12 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 6 m carries a point load 90 kN at distance 1.9 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 6, a = 1.9, W = 90 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 90*(6 - 1.9) / 6 | Answer: 61.5 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 6.4 m) carries a central point load 75 kN. With E = 200 GPa and I = 530e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=75000 N, L=6400.0 mm, E=200000 MPa, I=530e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 3.864 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 6.1 m carries a UDL of 15 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6.1, w = 15 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 15*(6.1)^2 / 12 | Answer: 46.51 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 300 mm, clear cover 45 mm and main bars of diameter 12 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 300, c = 45, dia = 12 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 300 - 45 - 12/2 | Answer: 249 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 13.6 m^2 carrying a factored load of 14.1 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 13.6, w = 14.1 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 14.1 * 13.6 | Answer: 191.8 kN

question: For a bar of diameter 12 mm with design bond stress 1.3 MPa and steel stress 435 MPa, find the development length in mm.
solution: Given: dia = 12, tbd = 1.3, fs = 435 | Formula: Ld = phi fs / (4 tau_bd) | Substitute: Ld = 12*435 / (4*1.3) | Answer: 1004 mm

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 4.2 m, unit weight 16 kN/m^3, phi = 32 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 8.7 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 19 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 8.7, g = 19 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (19 - 9.81)*8.7 | Answer: 79.95 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 2.8e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.6, area = 3.4e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 2.8, i = 0.6, A = 3.4 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (2.8e-4)*0.6*(3.4e-3) | Answer: 571.2 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 2.4 m, bed slope 0.002 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.029. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 1 m under a head of 0.9 m. Taking Cd = 0.63 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 2.2 m wide carries a discharge of 9.1 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 380 m and design speed 50 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 380, V = 50 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (50)^2 / (127*380) | Answer: 0.0518
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: For a design speed of 45 km/h with allowable superelevation 0.07 and lateral friction 0.14, find the minimum curve radius in m.
A tank of volume 760 m^3 treats a flow of 10 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 760, Q = 10 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 760 / 10 | Answer: 76 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 400 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.21 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 8 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 400, k = 0.21, t = 8 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 400*(1 - e^(-0.21*8)) | Answer: 325.5 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.66, rainfall intensity 100 mm/h over a catchment of 5.2 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.66, i = 100, A = 5.2 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.66*100*5.2 / 360 | Answer: 0.9533 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.02 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 180 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.02, M = 180 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 180*(20+0.02)/20 | Answer: 180.2 m

question: Convert the decimal number 80 to binary.
solution: Divide 80 by 2 repeatedly, recording remainders | Reading remainders in reverse gives 1010000 | Answer: 1010000 (binary)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 2 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the decimal number 2970 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 2970 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: B9A (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the 8-bit binary number 10001001 to decimal.
solution: Binary 10001001 = sum of bit-weights | Answer: 137 (decimal)
formula: Sum each bit times its positional weight (2^i)

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 00010011 and 01001110.
solution: XOR: 01011101 | Count of 1s = 5 | Answer: 5
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 960 megabits is sent over a link of 91 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 960, B = 91 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 960 / 91 | Answer: 10.55 s

question: A link has bandwidth 74 Mbps and round-trip time 190 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 74, R = 190 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 74e6 * 190e-3 bits = 14060 kb | Answer: 14060 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.84, cache access time 8 ns and main-memory access time 90 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.84, tc = 8, tm = 90 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.84*8 + (1 - 0.84)*90 | Answer: 21.12 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 450431 elements?
solution: Given: n = 450431 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(450431)) + 1 | Answer: 19

question: An O(n^2) algorithm performs c*n^2 basic operations. If c = 1 and n = 680, how many operations are performed?
solution: Given: n = 680 | Formula: operations = n^2 | Substitute: = (680)^2 | Answer: 462400

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.014, memory access time 180 ns and page-fault service time 7 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 7 ms = 7000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.014)*180 + 0.014*7000000.0 ns | Answer: 98.18 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 2.2 m^3 at 290 kPa and 300 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 2.2, P = 290, Tk = 300 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (290e3)*2.2 / (8.314*300) | Answer: 255.8 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.23 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 15 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.23, t = 15 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.23*15) | Answer: 0.9683

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.31 /min) is to reach 90% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.31, X = 90 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.9) / 0.31 | Answer: 7.428 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.48 /min) reaches 55% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.48, X = 55 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.55 / (0.48*(1 - 0.55)) | Answer: 2.546 min

question: For a reaction with A = 1e10 /s and activation energy 60 kJ/mol at 440 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 1, Ea = 60, Tk = 440 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 1e10 * exp(-60e3 / (8.314*440)) | Answer: 753.1 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.96 and bottoms xW = 0.09, with relative volatility alpha = 2.7. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.96, xw = 0.09, al = 2.7 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.96/0.04)(0.91/0.09)] / ln(2.7) | Answer: 5.529 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.85 and x = 0.42. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.85, x = 0.42 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.85/0.15) / (0.42/0.58) | Answer: 7.825

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.54 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 20 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.54, Psat = 20 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.54 * 20 | Answer: 10.8 kPa

question: A stream of 1.9 kg/s with specific heat 1.4 kJ/kg-K is heated through 30 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 1.9, cp = 1.4, dT = 30 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 1.9*1.4*30 | Answer: 79.8 kW

question: A reactor of volume 10.3 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 1.8 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 10.3, Q = 1.8 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 10.3 / 1.8 | Answer: 5.722 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 3.2e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 5 mm with a concentration difference of 40 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 3.2, L = 5, dC = 40 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (3.2e-9)*40 / (5e-3) | Answer: 25.6 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 4.3 min and steady-state gain 0.8. For a step input of magnitude 13, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 4.3, K = 0.8, M = 13 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 0.8 * 13 | Answer: 10.4 units

question: A reactor operates at a space time of 13.7 min. Find its space velocity in per hour.
solution: Given: tau = 13.7 | Formula: SV = 60 / tau  (per hour) | Substitute: SV = 60 / 13.7 | Answer: 4.38 /h

question: An aircraft wing of area 85 m^2 flies at 120 m/s (air density 1 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 1.2. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 85, V = 120, rho = 1, CL = 1.2 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1*(120)^2*85*1.2 / 1000 | Answer: 734.4 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 80 m^2 flies at 90 m/s (density 0.4 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.05. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 80, V = 90, rho = 0.4, CD = 0.05 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.4*(90)^2*80*0.05 / 1000 | Answer: 6.48 kN

question: A specimen under stress 280 MPa shows an elastic strain of 2.3e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 280, eps = 2.3 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 280 / (2.3e-3) MPa = 121.7 GPa | Answer: 121.7 GPa

question: A block of mass 42 kg has a volume of 4e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 42, V = 4 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 42 / (4e-3) | Answer: 10500 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 1900 mm is heated through 140 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 12e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 1900, dT = 140, al = 12 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 1900*12e-6*140 | Answer: 3.192 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 25 ohm, R2 = 105 ohm and R3 = 80 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 25, R2 = 105, R3 = 80 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 105*80 / 25 | Answer: 336 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 1000 ohm and gauge factor 2.1 experiences a strain of 1350e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 1000, GF = 2.1, eps = 1350 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 1000*2.1*1350e-6 | Answer: 2835 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 10.57 when the true value is 10. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10.57, true = 10 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10.57 - 10| / 10 * 100 | Answer: 5.7 %

question: Annual demand is 31500 units, ordering cost 240 per order and holding cost 40 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 31500, S = 240, H = 40 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*31500*240 / 40) | Answer: 614.8 units

question: An asset costs 140000 with salvage value 6000 after 6 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 140000, Sv = 6000, n = 6 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (140000 - 6000) / 6 | Answer: 22333 per year

question: A product sells for 220 per unit with variable cost 120 per unit and fixed costs 100000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 220, V = 120, F = 100000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 100000 / (220 - 120) | Answer: 1000 units

question: Find the present worth of 60000 received 10 years from now at an interest rate of 8% per year.
solution: Given: F = 60000, n = 10, i = 8 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 60000 / (1 + 0.08)^10 | Answer: 27792 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.9, 0.91 and 0.97 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.9, r2 = 0.91, r3 = 0.97 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.9*0.91*0.97 | Answer: 0.7944

question: A process produces 37 defective items in a batch of 2500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 37, N = 2500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 37/2500 * 1e6 | Answer: 14800 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -x^3 + 4x^2 + 2x - 6 evaluated at x = -2.
For f(x) = 4x^3 - 5x^2 - 8x - 1, find f''(x) at x = -1.
Evaluate the definite integral of (x^2 - 6x - 5) dx from x = -1 to x = 7.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = 1x^3/3 + -6x^2/2 + -5x | Evaluate F(7) - F(-1) | Answer: -69.33
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 2x^2 + 3x - 9 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[4, 7], [5, -9]].
solution: Given: a = 4, b = 7, c = 5, d = -9 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (4)(-9) - (7)(5) | Answer: -71

question: Find the determinant of [[-1, -5, -5], [4, -3, 2], [-3, 0, 1]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: 98

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[3, -1], [-5, -4]].
solution: Trace tr = -1, Determinant = -17 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 3.653

question: Solve for x: 1x + -4y = 10 and 6x + 5y = 10.
solution: Determinant = 1*5 - -4*6 = 29 | x = (e d - b f) / det = 3.103 | Answer: x = 3.103
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 71, 84, 86, 38, 92.
solution: Sum = 371 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 74.2 | Answer: 74.2

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 5, 43, 23, 3, 14.
solution: Mean = 17.6 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 16.27

question: Find the slope of the line through (-1, 5) and (4, -2).
solution: Given: x1 = -1, y1 = 5, x2 = 4, y2 = -2 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (-2 - 5) / (4 - -1) | Answer: -1.4

question: Find the distance between the points (-3, 3) and (3, 1).
solution: Given: x1 = -3, y1 = 3, x2 = 3, y2 = 1 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((6)^2 + (-2)^2) | Answer: 6.325 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (4,-4), (1,-1), (1,-6).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 7.5 sq units

question: Evaluate the number of combinations C(16, 3).
solution: Given: n = 16, r = 3 | Formula: C(n, r) = n! / (r! (n - r)!) | Substitute: C(16, 3) = 16! / (3! * 13!) | Answer: 560

question: Find the 36th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -18 and common difference 5.
solution: Given: a = -18, d = 5, n = 36 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -18 + (36 - 1)*5 | Answer: 157

question: Find the sum of the first 24 terms of an AP with first term 12 and common difference -7.
solution: Given: a = 12, d = -7, n = 24 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 24/2 [2*12 + (24-1)*-7] | Answer: -1644

question: Find the 8th term of a geometric progression with first term 4 and common ratio 2.
solution: Given: a = 4, r = 2, n = 8 | Formula: a_n = a r^(n-1) | Substitute: a_n = 4 * 2^(8-1) | Answer: 512

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 40000 at 4.1% per annum for 7 years.
solution: Given: P = 40000, R = 4.1, Tt = 7 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 40000 * 4.1 * 7 / 100 | Answer: 11480 currency units

question: Find the amount when 16500 is invested at 5% per annum compounded annually for 6 years.
solution: Given: P = 16500, R = 5, Tt = 6 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 16500 * (1 + 5/100)^6 | Answer: 22112 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (8, -3, -6) and (-7, -2, 2).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (5, -1, 1) and (6, -4, -1).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 18.49

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (6, 1, 0) and (1, -2, -4).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 81.75 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number -11 + 8i.
solution: Given: a = -11, b = 8 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((-11)^2 + (8)^2) | Answer: 13.6

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number 8 + -1i.
solution: Given: a = 8, b = -1 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(-1, 8) | Answer: -7.125 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -x^3 - 2x^2 + 8x + 8 at x = -2.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-74 with initial guess x0=8, find x1 (one iteration).
solution: Given: N = 74, x0 = 8 | Formula: x1 = x0 - (x0^2 - N)/(2 x0) | Substitute: x1 = 8 - ((8)^2 - 74)/(2*8) | Answer: 8.625

question: Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.6 and ordinates 6, 8, 5, 18, 13, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 221 and 554.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 221 and 554 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 75 and 26.
solution: Given: a = 75, b = 26 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 75*26 / 1 | Answer: 1950
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 56 mm carries an axial tensile load of 92 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 26 mm and length 1900 mm carries an axial load of 19 kN. Take E = 200 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 36 mm transmits a torque of 2100 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 36, Tt = 2100 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(2100*1000) / (pi*(36)^3) | Answer: 229.2 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 58 mm and length 1100 mm carries a torque of 800 N-m. With G = 77 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (58)^4 / 32 = 1110994 mm^4 | theta = (800*1000)(1100) / (77000 * 1110994) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 0.5894 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 145 mm wide and 120 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 145, h = 120 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 145*(120)^2 / 6 | Answer: 348000 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (45 mm x 80 mm) carries a bending moment of 27 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (44 mm x 100 mm) has effective length 3100 mm and E = 200 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 540 MPa is designed for a working stress of 120 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 540, sw = 120 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 540 / 120 | Answer: 4.5

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1250 mm and wall thickness 6 mm carries an internal pressure of 0.6 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1250, t = 6, P = 0.6 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 0.6*1250 / (2*6) | Answer: 62.5 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 780 K and 280 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 780, Tc = 280 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 280/780) * 100 | Answer: 64.1 %

question: A refrigerator works between 275 K (cold) and 316 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 275, Th = 316 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 275 / (316 - 275) | Answer: 6.707

question: A heat pump operates between 282 K and 308 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 282, Th = 308 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 308 / (308 - 282) | Answer: 11.85

question: 4 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 90 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4, dT = 90 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 4 * 0.718 * 90 | Answer: 258.5 kJ

question: 4.5 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 125 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.5, dT = 125 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 4.5 * 1.005 * 125 | Answer: 565.3 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 2 m^3 at 580 K with mass 5.3 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 2, Tk = 580, m = 5.3 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 5.3*0.287*580 / 2 | Answer: 441.1 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 1.9 kg of air expands isothermally at 340 K from volume V1 to 2*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1.9, Tk = 340, ratio = 2 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 1.9*0.287*340*ln(2) | Answer: 128.5 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 4.7 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.22 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 4.7, D = 0.22 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*4.7*0.22 / 0.001 | Answer: 1034000

question: Water flows at 3 m/s through a pipe of diameter 110 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 10.5 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 10.5 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*10.5 / 1000 | Answer: 103 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 14.7 m. Taking Cv = 0.95, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 14.7, cv = 0.95 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.95*sqrt(2*9.81*14.7) | Answer: 16.13 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 350 mm) water flows at 2.7 m/s. It contracts to diameter 60 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 350, d2 = 60, V1 = 2.7 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 2.7*(350/60)^2 | Answer: 91.87 m/s

question: Water flows at 2 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.28 m and length 170 m. With friction factor f = 0.031, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 15 teeth drives a gear of 65 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1350 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 15, z2 = 65, N1 = 1350 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1350*15 / 65 | Answer: 311.5 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 270 mm rotates at 1000 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 270, N = 1000 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.27)*1000 / 60 | Answer: 14.14 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 29.9 kW at 1200 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 29.9, N = 1200 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(29.9*1000) / (2*pi*1200) | Answer: 237.9 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 5.7 kg rotates at radius 0.5 m at 1150 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 11200 N/m and mass 14.5 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 11200, m = 14.5 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(11200/14.5) | Answer: 4.423 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 2.9 m^2 and thickness 0.39 m has conductivity k = 15.1 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 85 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 2.9, L = 0.39, k = 15.1, dT = 85 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 15.1*2.9*85 / 0.39 | Answer: 9544 W

question: A surface of area 4.9 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 75 W/m^2-K to surroundings 25 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 4.9, h = 75, dT = 25 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 75*4.9*25 | Answer: 9188 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 100 m/min, feed = 0.29 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2.4 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 100, f = 0.29, d = 2.4 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*100*0.29*2.4 | Answer: 69600 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 500 mm is turned at 800 rpm with a feed of 0.18 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 500, N = 800, f = 0.18 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 500 / (0.18*800) | Answer: 3.472 min

question: A resistor of 46 ohm carries a current of 7.5 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 46, I = 7.5 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 7.5 * 46 | Answer: 345 V

question: Three resistors 15 ohm, 100 ohm and 89 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 15, R2 = 100, R3 = 89 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 15 + 100 + 89 | Answer: 204 ohm

question: Two resistors 59 ohm and 2 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 59, R2 = 2 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 59*2 / (59+2) | Answer: 1.934 ohm

question: A device draws 0.7 A at 130 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 130, I = 0.7 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 130 * 0.7 | Answer: 91 W

question: A current of 11.4 A flows through a 117 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 11.4, R = 117 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (11.4)^2 * 117 | Answer: 15205 W

question: Two capacitors 28 uF and 3.6 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 28, C2 = 3.6 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 28*3.6 / (28+3.6) | Answer: 3.19 uF

question: A resistor 84 kohm and capacitor 1.5 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 84, C = 1.5 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (84k)(1.5u) = 126 ms | Answer: 126 ms

question: An inductor 198.8 mH is in series with 195 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 198.8, R = 195 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (198.8e-3) / 195 | Answer: 1.019 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 61.5 mH inductor at 430 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 61.5, f = 430 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (430)(61.5e-3) | Answer: 166.2 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 15.1 uF capacitor at 140 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 15.1, f = 140 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (140)(15.1e-6)) | Answer: 75.29 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 66 ohm, XL = 105 ohm and XC = 16 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 66, XL = 105, XC = 16 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(66^2 + (105 - 16)^2) | Answer: 110.8 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 59.9 mH and C = 1.2 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 59.9, C = 1.2 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(59.9e-3 * 1.2e-6)) | Answer: 593.6 Hz

question: A capacitor of 87 uF is charged to 360 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 87, V = 360 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*87e-6*(360)^2 | Answer: 5638 mJ

question: An alternating voltage has a peak value of 304 V. Find its RMS value.
solution: Given: Vp = 304 | Formula: Vrms = Vp / sqrt(2) | Substitute: Vrms = 304 / sqrt(2) | Answer: 215 V

question: A transformer has primary voltage 210 V with 490 primary turns and 250 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 210, N1 = 490, N2 = 250 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 210 * 250/490 | Answer: 107.1 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 130 V and draws an armature current of 11 A. If the armature resistance is 0.38 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 130, Ia = 11, Ra = 0.38 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 130 - 11*0.38 | Answer: 125.8 V

question: A 8-pole induction motor on a 60 Hz supply runs at 870 rpm. Find the slip (%).
formula: s = (Ns - N) / Ns,  Ns = 120 f / P

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 80 A at 433 V (line) with a power factor of 0.92. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 80, VL = 433, pf = 0.92 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*433*80*0.92 / 1000 | Answer: 55.2 kW

question: A load has real power 45 kW and apparent power 145 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 45, S = 145 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 45 / 145 | Answer: 0.3103

question: A machine delivers 175 kW output while drawing 187 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 175, Pi = 187 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 175/187 * 100 | Answer: 93.58 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 23 V across R1 = 44 ohm and R2 = 46 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 23, R1 = 44, R2 = 46 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 23*46 / (44+46) | Answer: 11.76 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 30 kohm and Rin = 1 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 30, Rin = 1 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 30 / 1 | Answer: 30

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 130 kohm and Rg = 41 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 130, Rg = 41 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 130/41 | Answer: 4.171

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 7389. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 7389 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(7389) | Answer: 38.69 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 4 m carries a central point load of 30 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4, W = 30 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 30*4 / 4 | Answer: 30 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 7.9 m carries a UDL of 40 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7.9, w = 40 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 40*(7.9)^2 / 8 | Answer: 312.1 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 2.4 m carries a point load 65 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 2.4, W = 65 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 65*2.4 | Answer: 156 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 3 m carries a UDL of 32 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3, w = 32 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 32*(3)^2 / 2 | Answer: 144 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 5.1 m carries a point load 15 kN at distance 4 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 5.1, a = 4, W = 15 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 15*(5.1 - 4) / 5.1 | Answer: 3.235 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 4.8 m) carries a central point load 80 kN. With E = 25 GPa and I = 540e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=80000 N, L=4800.0 mm, E=25000 MPa, I=540e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 13.65 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 5.4 m carries a UDL of 30 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.4, w = 30 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 30*(5.4)^2 / 12 | Answer: 72.9 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 470 mm, clear cover 45 mm and main bars of diameter 25 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 470, c = 45, dia = 25 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 470 - 45 - 25/2 | Answer: 412.5 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 18.4 m^2 carrying a factored load of 11.6 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 18.4, w = 11.6 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 11.6 * 18.4 | Answer: 213.4 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 3.9 m, unit weight 16 kN/m^3, phi = 30 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 7.9 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 20 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 7.9, g = 20 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (20 - 9.81)*7.9 | Answer: 80.5 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 1.8e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.3, area = 5.1e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 1.8, i = 0.3, A = 5.1 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (1.8e-4)*0.3*(5.1e-3) | Answer: 275.4 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 0.6 m, bed slope 0.005 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.014. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 2.4 m under a head of 0.7 m. Taking Cd = 0.61 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 2.7 m wide carries a discharge of 13.7 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 240 m and design speed 90 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 240, V = 90 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (90)^2 / (127*240) | Answer: 0.2657
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: For a design speed of 95 km/h with allowable superelevation 0.07 and lateral friction 0.14, find the minimum curve radius in m.
A tank of volume 670 m^3 treats a flow of 40 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 670, Q = 40 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 670 / 40 | Answer: 16.75 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 250 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.3 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 3 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 250, k = 0.3, t = 3 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 250*(1 - e^(-0.3*3)) | Answer: 148.4 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.73, rainfall intensity 65 mm/h over a catchment of 20.7 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.73, i = 65, A = 20.7 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.73*65*20.7 / 360 | Answer: 2.728 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.07 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 800 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.07, M = 800 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 800*(20+0.07)/20 | Answer: 802.8 m

question: Convert the decimal number 198 to binary.
solution: Divide 198 by 2 repeatedly, recording remainders | Reading remainders in reverse gives 11000110 | Answer: 11000110 (binary)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 2 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the decimal number 2863 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 2863 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: B2F (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the 8-bit binary number 00111101 to decimal.
solution: Binary 00111101 = sum of bit-weights | Answer: 61 (decimal)
formula: Sum each bit times its positional weight (2^i)

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 00000001 and 01110011.
solution: XOR: 01110010 | Count of 1s = 4 | Answer: 4
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 150 megabits is sent over a link of 85 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 150, B = 85 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 150 / 85 | Answer: 1.765 s

question: A link has bandwidth 70 Mbps and round-trip time 150 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 70, R = 150 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 70e6 * 150e-3 bits = 10500 kb | Answer: 10500 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.96, cache access time 5 ns and main-memory access time 90 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.96, tc = 5, tm = 90 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.96*5 + (1 - 0.96)*90 | Answer: 8.4 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 618969 elements?
solution: Given: n = 618969 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(618969)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: An O(n^2) algorithm performs c*n^2 basic operations. If c = 1 and n = 2820, how many operations are performed?
solution: Given: n = 2820 | Formula: operations = n^2 | Substitute: = (2820)^2 | Answer: 7952400

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.018, memory access time 130 ns and page-fault service time 5 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 5 ms = 5000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.018)*130 + 0.018*5000000.0 ns | Answer: 90.13 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 1.3 m^3 at 500 kPa and 500 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 1.3, P = 500, Tk = 500 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (500e3)*1.3 / (8.314*500) | Answer: 156.4 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.23 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 20 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.23, t = 20 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.23*20) | Answer: 0.9899

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.42 /min) is to reach 80% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.42, X = 80 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.8) / 0.42 | Answer: 3.832 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.24 /min) reaches 65% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.24, X = 65 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.65 / (0.24*(1 - 0.65)) | Answer: 7.738 min

question: For a reaction with A = 1e10 /s and activation energy 60 kJ/mol at 460 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 1, Ea = 60, Tk = 460 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 1e10 * exp(-60e3 / (8.314*460)) | Answer: 1537 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.92 and bottoms xW = 0.03, with relative volatility alpha = 2.5. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.92, xw = 0.03, al = 2.5 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.92/0.08)(0.97/0.03)] / ln(2.5) | Answer: 6.459 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.88 and x = 0.47. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.88, x = 0.47 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.88/0.12) / (0.47/0.53) | Answer: 8.27

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.23 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 75 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.23, Psat = 75 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.23 * 75 | Answer: 17.25 kPa

question: A stream of 2.1 kg/s with specific heat 1.2 kJ/kg-K is heated through 60 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 2.1, cp = 1.2, dT = 60 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 2.1*1.2*60 | Answer: 151.2 kW

question: A reactor of volume 1.7 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 4.2 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 1.7, Q = 4.2 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 1.7 / 4.2 | Answer: 0.4048 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 5.1e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 4 mm with a concentration difference of 30 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 5.1, L = 4, dC = 30 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (5.1e-9)*30 / (4e-3) | Answer: 38.25 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 2.6 min and steady-state gain 1. For a step input of magnitude 8, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 2.6, K = 1, M = 8 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 1 * 8 | Answer: 8 units

question: A reactor operates at a space time of 8.9 min. Find its space velocity in per hour.
solution: Given: tau = 8.9 | Formula: SV = 60 / tau  (per hour) | Substitute: SV = 60 / 8.9 | Answer: 6.742 /h

question: An aircraft wing of area 35 m^2 flies at 150 m/s (air density 0.7 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.5. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 35, V = 150, rho = 0.7, CL = 0.5 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.7*(150)^2*35*0.5 / 1000 | Answer: 137.8 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 40 m^2 flies at 160 m/s (density 1.225 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.07. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 40, V = 160, rho = 1.225, CD = 0.07 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*1.225*(160)^2*40*0.07 / 1000 | Answer: 43.9 kN

question: A specimen under stress 400 MPa shows an elastic strain of 0.8e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 400, eps = 0.8 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 400 / (0.8e-3) MPa = 500 GPa | Answer: 500 GPa

question: A block of mass 11 kg has a volume of 4.6e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 11, V = 4.6 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 11 / (4.6e-3) | Answer: 2391 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 1600 mm is heated through 110 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 11e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 1600, dT = 110, al = 11 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 1600*11e-6*110 | Answer: 1.936 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 190 ohm, R2 = 45 ohm and R3 = 400 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 190, R2 = 45, R3 = 400 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 45*400 / 190 | Answer: 94.74 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 1000 ohm and gauge factor 2 experiences a strain of 1350e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 1000, GF = 2, eps = 1350 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 1000*2*1350e-6 | Answer: 2700 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 9.87 when the true value is 20. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.87, true = 20 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.87 - 20| / 20 * 100 | Answer: 50.65 %

question: Annual demand is 42500 units, ordering cost 20 per order and holding cost 17 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 42500, S = 20, H = 17 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*42500*20 / 17) | Answer: 316.2 units

question: An asset costs 290000 with salvage value 32000 after 15 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 290000, Sv = 32000, n = 15 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (290000 - 32000) / 15 | Answer: 17200 per year

question: A product sells for 190 per unit with variable cost 160 per unit and fixed costs 190000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 190, V = 160, F = 190000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 190000 / (190 - 160) | Answer: 6333 units

question: Find the present worth of 165000 received 7 years from now at an interest rate of 7% per year.
solution: Given: F = 165000, n = 7, i = 7 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 165000 / (1 + 0.07)^7 | Answer: 102754 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.97, 0.93 and 0.94 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.97, r2 = 0.93, r3 = 0.94 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.97*0.93*0.94 | Answer: 0.848

question: A process produces 1 defective items in a batch of 14500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 1, N = 14500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 1/14500 * 1e6 | Answer: 68.97 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -4x^3 - 8x - 8 evaluated at x = 3.
For f(x) = 2x^3 + 5x^2 - x - 4, find f''(x) at x = -5.
Evaluate the definite integral of (x^2 + 3x - 4) dx from x = -1 to x = 4.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = 1x^3/3 + 3x^2/2 + -4x | Evaluate F(4) - F(-1) | Answer: 24.17
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of x^2 - 7x - 4 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[8, -7], [-7, 5]].
solution: Given: a = 8, b = -7, c = -7, d = 5 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (8)(5) - (-7)(-7) | Answer: -9

question: Find the determinant of [[-1, -1, -6], [5, -1, -3], [5, -2, 1]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: 57

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[3, 0], [-7, -5]].
solution: Trace tr = -2, Determinant = -15 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 3

question: Solve for x: -6x + -1y = -2 and 4x + -2y = -5.
solution: Determinant = -6*-2 - -1*4 = 16 | x = (e d - b f) / det = -0.0625 | Answer: x = -0.0625
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 23, 70, 57, 19, 12.
solution: Sum = 181 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 36.2 | Answer: 36.2

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 38, 18, 8, 38, 2.
solution: Mean = 20.8 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 16.71

question: Find the slope of the line through (-7, 4) and (6, 8).
solution: Given: x1 = -7, y1 = 4, x2 = 6, y2 = 8 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (8 - 4) / (6 - -7) | Answer: 0.3077

question: Find the distance between the points (3, 3) and (-2, -2).
solution: Given: x1 = 3, y1 = 3, x2 = -2, y2 = -2 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-5)^2 + (-5)^2) | Answer: 7.071 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (1,-7), (8,3), (8,2).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 3.5 sq units

question: Evaluate the number of combinations C(10, 7).
solution: Given: n = 10, r = 7 | Formula: C(n, r) = n! / (r! (n - r)!) | Substitute: C(10, 7) = 10! / (7! * 3!) | Answer: 120

question: Evaluate the number of permutations P(13, 4).
solution: Given: n = 13, r = 4 | Formula: P(n, r) = n! / (n - r)! | Substitute: P(13, 4) = 13! / 9! | Answer: 17160

question: Find the 13th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -19 and common difference 5.
solution: Given: a = -19, d = 5, n = 13 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -19 + (13 - 1)*5 | Answer: 41

question: Find the sum of the first 34 terms of an AP with first term -4 and common difference -1.
solution: Given: a = -4, d = -1, n = 34 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 34/2 [2*-4 + (34-1)*-1] | Answer: -697

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 44500 at 9.3% per annum for 2 years.
solution: Given: P = 44500, R = 9.3, Tt = 2 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 44500 * 9.3 * 2 / 100 | Answer: 8277 currency units

question: Find the amount when 5000 is invested at 6.6% per annum compounded annually for 6 years.
solution: Given: P = 5000, R = 6.6, Tt = 6 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 5000 * (1 + 6.6/100)^6 | Answer: 7337 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (-4, 5, 1) and (3, 7, -1).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (2, -6, -1) and (3, -1, -6).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 39.52

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (-3, 5, -3) and (-1, 5, -6).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 27.01 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number 11 + -3i.
solution: Given: a = 11, b = -3 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((11)^2 + (-3)^2) | Answer: 11.4

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number -5 + 6i.
solution: Given: a = -5, b = 6 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(6, -5) | Answer: 129.8 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -2x^3 + 7x^2 + 6x - 1 at x = 1.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-151 with initial guess x0=11, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.3 and ordinates 19, 12, 14, 19, 18, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 429 and 315.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 429 and 315 | Answer: GCD = 3

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 17 and 29.
solution: Given: a = 17, b = 29 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 17*29 / 1 | Answer: 493
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 34 mm carries an axial tensile load of 51 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 30 mm and length 2100 mm carries an axial load of 73 kN. Take E = 70 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 72 mm transmits a torque of 2250 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 72, Tt = 2250 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(2250*1000) / (pi*(72)^3) | Answer: 30.7 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 48 mm and length 1800 mm carries a torque of 1150 N-m. With G = 80 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (48)^4 / 32 = 521153 mm^4 | theta = (1150*1000)(1800) / (80000 * 521153) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 2.845 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 33 mm wide and 100 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 33, h = 100 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 33*(100)^2 / 6 | Answer: 55000 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (61 mm x 220 mm) carries a bending moment of 32 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (63 mm x 90 mm) has effective length 3400 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 340 MPa is designed for a working stress of 130 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 340, sw = 130 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 340 / 130 | Answer: 2.615

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 550 mm and wall thickness 9 mm carries an internal pressure of 2.9 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 550, t = 9, P = 2.9 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 2.9*550 / (2*9) | Answer: 88.61 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 820 K and 300 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 820, Tc = 300 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 300/820) * 100 | Answer: 63.41 %

question: A refrigerator works between 270 K (cold) and 302 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 270, Th = 302 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 270 / (302 - 270) | Answer: 8.438

question: A heat pump operates between 273 K and 314 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 273, Th = 314 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 314 / (314 - 273) | Answer: 7.659

question: 3.9 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 40 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.9, dT = 40 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 3.9 * 0.718 * 40 | Answer: 112 kJ

question: 4.9 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 90 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.9, dT = 90 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 4.9 * 1.005 * 90 | Answer: 443.2 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 0.8 m^3 at 420 K with mass 3.4 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 0.8, Tk = 420, m = 3.4 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 3.4*0.287*420 / 0.8 | Answer: 512.3 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 1.3 kg of air expands isothermally at 480 K from volume V1 to 2*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1.3, Tk = 480, ratio = 2 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 1.3*0.287*480*ln(2) | Answer: 124.1 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 2.7 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.37 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 2.7, D = 0.37 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*2.7*0.37 / 0.001 | Answer: 999000

question: Water flows at 1.2 m/s through a pipe of diameter 300 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 25.3 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 25.3 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*25.3 / 1000 | Answer: 248.2 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 14.5 m. Taking Cv = 0.96, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 14.5, cv = 0.96 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.96*sqrt(2*9.81*14.5) | Answer: 16.19 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 260 mm) water flows at 2.4 m/s. It contracts to diameter 60 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 260, d2 = 60, V1 = 2.4 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 2.4*(260/60)^2 | Answer: 45.07 m/s

question: Water flows at 1.2 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.13 m and length 490 m. With friction factor f = 0.025, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 39 teeth drives a gear of 117 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1300 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 39, z2 = 117, N1 = 1300 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1300*39 / 117 | Answer: 433.3 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 280 mm rotates at 1100 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 280, N = 1100 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.28)*1100 / 60 | Answer: 16.13 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 17 kW at 1150 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 17, N = 1150 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(17*1000) / (2*pi*1150) | Answer: 141.2 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 5.9 kg rotates at radius 0.59 m at 450 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 6300 N/m and mass 14.6 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 6300, m = 14.6 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(6300/14.6) | Answer: 3.306 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 1.4 m^2 and thickness 0.3 m has conductivity k = 45.4 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 140 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 1.4, L = 0.3, k = 45.4, dT = 140 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 45.4*1.4*140 / 0.3 | Answer: 29661 W

question: A surface of area 5.3 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 20 W/m^2-K to surroundings 90 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 5.3, h = 20, dT = 90 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 20*5.3*90 | Answer: 9540 W

question: In a counter-flow heat exchanger the terminal temperature differences are 80 deg C and 25 deg C. Find the log mean temperature difference (LMTD) in deg C.
solution: Given: dT1 = 80, dT2 = 25 | Formula: LMTD = (dT1 - dT2) / ln(dT1/dT2) | Substitute: LMTD = (80 - 25) / ln(80/25) | Answer: 47.29 deg C

question: In turning, cutting speed = 110 m/min, feed = 0.19 mm/rev, depth of cut = 1.1 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 110, f = 0.19, d = 1.1 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*110*0.19*1.1 | Answer: 22990 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 280 mm is turned at 850 rpm with a feed of 0.33 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 280, N = 850, f = 0.33 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 280 / (0.33*850) | Answer: 0.9982 min

question: A resistor of 9 ohm carries a current of 6.1 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 9, I = 6.1 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 6.1 * 9 | Answer: 54.9 V

question: Three resistors 76 ohm, 90 ohm and 33 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 76, R2 = 90, R3 = 33 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 76 + 90 + 33 | Answer: 199 ohm

question: Two resistors 68 ohm and 105 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 68, R2 = 105 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 68*105 / (68+105) | Answer: 41.27 ohm

question: A device draws 4 A at 45 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 45, I = 4 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 45 * 4 | Answer: 180 W

question: A current of 8 A flows through a 62 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 8, R = 62 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (8)^2 * 62 | Answer: 3968 W

question: Two capacitors 2.6 uF and 48.6 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 2.6, C2 = 48.6 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 2.6*48.6 / (2.6+48.6) | Answer: 2.468 uF

question: A resistor 19 kohm and capacitor 1.4 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 19, C = 1.4 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (19k)(1.4u) = 26.6 ms | Answer: 26.6 ms

question: An inductor 255.6 mH is in series with 10 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 255.6, R = 10 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (255.6e-3) / 10 | Answer: 25.56 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 160.7 mH inductor at 350 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 160.7, f = 350 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (350)(160.7e-3) | Answer: 353.4 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 30.6 uF capacitor at 260 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 30.6, f = 260 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (260)(30.6e-6)) | Answer: 20 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 98 ohm, XL = 101 ohm and XC = 34 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 98, XL = 101, XC = 34 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(98^2 + (101 - 34)^2) | Answer: 118.7 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 85 mH and C = 1.7 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 85, C = 1.7 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(85e-3 * 1.7e-6)) | Answer: 418.7 Hz

question: A capacitor of 2.8 uF is charged to 375 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 2.8, V = 375 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*2.8e-6*(375)^2 | Answer: 196.9 mJ

question: An alternating voltage has a peak value of 38 V. Find its RMS value.
solution: Given: Vp = 38 | Formula: Vrms = Vp / sqrt(2) | Substitute: Vrms = 38 / sqrt(2) | Answer: 26.87 V

question: A transformer has primary voltage 290 V with 270 primary turns and 320 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 290, N1 = 270, N2 = 320 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 290 * 320/270 | Answer: 343.7 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 250 V and draws an armature current of 56 A. If the armature resistance is 1.15 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 250, Ia = 56, Ra = 1.15 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 250 - 56*1.15 | Answer: 185.6 V

question: A 6-pole induction motor on a 60 Hz supply runs at 810 rpm. Find the slip (%).
formula: s = (Ns - N) / Ns,  Ns = 120 f / P

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 50 A at 415 V (line) with a power factor of 0.85. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 50, VL = 415, pf = 0.85 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*415*50*0.85 / 1000 | Answer: 30.55 kW

question: A load has real power 90 kW and apparent power 165 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 90, S = 165 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 90 / 165 | Answer: 0.5455

question: A machine delivers 115 kW output while drawing 167 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 115, Pi = 167 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 115/167 * 100 | Answer: 68.86 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 24 V across R1 = 28 ohm and R2 = 10 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 24, R1 = 28, R2 = 10 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 24*10 / (28+10) | Answer: 6.316 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 170 kohm and Rin = 19 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 170, Rin = 19 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 170 / 19 | Answer: 8.947

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 30 kohm and Rg = 3 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 30, Rg = 3 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 30/3 | Answer: 11

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 9563. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 9563 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(9563) | Answer: 39.81 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 7.7 m carries a central point load of 120 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7.7, W = 120 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 120*7.7 / 4 | Answer: 231 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.8 m carries a UDL of 20 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.8, w = 20 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 20*(4.8)^2 / 8 | Answer: 57.6 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 3.9 m carries a point load 25 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.9, W = 25 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 25*3.9 | Answer: 97.5 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 3.9 m carries a UDL of 8 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.9, w = 8 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 8*(3.9)^2 / 2 | Answer: 60.84 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 8.2 m carries a point load 55 kN at distance 2.1 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 8.2, a = 2.1, W = 55 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 55*(8.2 - 2.1) / 8.2 | Answer: 40.91 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 4.6 m) carries a central point load 25 kN. With E = 25 GPa and I = 160e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=25000 N, L=4600.0 mm, E=25000 MPa, I=160e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 12.67 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 7.4 m carries a UDL of 24 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7.4, w = 24 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 24*(7.4)^2 / 12 | Answer: 109.5 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 400 mm, clear cover 30 mm and main bars of diameter 20 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 400, c = 30, dia = 20 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 400 - 30 - 20/2 | Answer: 360 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 26.2 m^2 carrying a factored load of 18.3 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 26.2, w = 18.3 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 18.3 * 26.2 | Answer: 479.5 kN

question: For a bar of diameter 12 mm with design bond stress 1.4 MPa and steel stress 435 MPa, find the development length in mm.
solution: Given: dia = 12, tbd = 1.4, fs = 435 | Formula: Ld = phi fs / (4 tau_bd) | Substitute: Ld = 12*435 / (4*1.4) | Answer: 932.1 mm

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 5.7 m, unit weight 16 kN/m^3, phi = 32 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 6.2 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 20 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 6.2, g = 20 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (20 - 9.81)*6.2 | Answer: 63.18 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 5.5e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.2, area = 1.9e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 5.5, i = 0.2, A = 1.9 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (5.5e-4)*0.2*(1.9e-3) | Answer: 209 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.4 m, bed slope 0.01 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.013. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 5 m under a head of 0.5 m. Taking Cd = 0.6 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
solution: Given: L = 5, H = 0.5, cd = 0.6 | Formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2) | Substitute: Q = (2/3)*0.6*sqrt(2*9.81)*5*(0.5)^1.5 | Answer: 3.132 m^3/s
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 4.6 m wide carries a discharge of 6.7 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 400 m and design speed 55 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 400, V = 55 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (55)^2 / (127*400) | Answer: 0.05955
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: For a design speed of 70 km/h with allowable superelevation 0.07 and lateral friction 0.15, find the minimum curve radius in m.
A tank of volume 980 m^3 treats a flow of 80 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 980, Q = 80 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 980 / 80 | Answer: 12.25 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 180 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.23 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 7 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 180, k = 0.23, t = 7 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 180*(1 - e^(-0.23*7)) | Answer: 144 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.65, rainfall intensity 50 mm/h over a catchment of 29.4 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.65, i = 50, A = 29.4 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.65*50*29.4 / 360 | Answer: 2.654 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.04 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 240 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.04, M = 240 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 240*(30+0.04)/30 | Answer: 240.3 m

question: Convert the decimal number 48 to binary.
solution: Divide 48 by 2 repeatedly, recording remainders | Reading remainders in reverse gives 110000 | Answer: 110000 (binary)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 2 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the decimal number 3237 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 3237 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: CA5 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the 8-bit binary number 01011101 to decimal.
solution: Binary 01011101 = sum of bit-weights | Answer: 93 (decimal)
formula: Sum each bit times its positional weight (2^i)

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 00110001 and 00101111.
solution: XOR: 00011110 | Count of 1s = 4 | Answer: 4
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions
