question: A circular rod of diameter 59 mm carries an axial tensile load of 61 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 24 mm and length 900 mm carries an axial load of 12 kN. Take E = 210 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 34 mm transmits a torque of 2300 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 34, Tt = 2300 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(2300*1000) / (pi*(34)^3) | Answer: 298 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 68 mm and length 800 mm carries a torque of 650 N-m. With G = 77 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (68)^4 / 32 = 2099112 mm^4 | theta = (650*1000)(800) / (77000 * 2099112) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 0.1843 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 124 mm wide and 200 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 124, h = 200 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 124*(200)^2 / 6 | Answer: 826667 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (107 mm x 100 mm) carries a bending moment of 21 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (62 mm x 160 mm) has effective length 2200 mm and E = 200 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 620 MPa is designed for a working stress of 210 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 620, sw = 210 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 620 / 210 | Answer: 2.952

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 700 mm and wall thickness 20 mm carries an internal pressure of 3 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 700, t = 20, P = 3 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 3*700 / (2*20) | Answer: 52.5 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 700 K and 450 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 700, Tc = 450 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 450/700) * 100 | Answer: 35.71 %

question: A refrigerator works between 268 K (cold) and 312 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 268, Th = 312 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 268 / (312 - 268) | Answer: 6.091

question: A heat pump operates between 261 K and 326 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 261, Th = 326 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 326 / (326 - 261) | Answer: 5.015

question: 5.4 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 190 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 5.4, dT = 190 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 5.4 * 0.718 * 190 | Answer: 736.7 kJ

question: 4.7 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 100 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.7, dT = 100 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 4.7 * 1.005 * 100 | Answer: 472.3 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 3.1 m^3 at 390 K with mass 2.9 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 3.1, Tk = 390, m = 2.9 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 2.9*0.287*390 / 3.1 | Answer: 104.7 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 3.6 kg of air expands isothermally at 330 K from volume V1 to 2*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.6, Tk = 330, ratio = 2 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 3.6*0.287*330*ln(2) | Answer: 236.3 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 3.1 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.06 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 3.1, D = 0.06 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*3.1*0.06 / 0.001 | Answer: 186000

question: Water flows at 3.7 m/s through a pipe of diameter 90 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 8.9 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 8.9 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*8.9 / 1000 | Answer: 87.31 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 8.1 m. Taking Cv = 0.98, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 8.1, cv = 0.98 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.98*sqrt(2*9.81*8.1) | Answer: 12.35 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 250 mm) water flows at 0.6 m/s. It contracts to diameter 50 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 250, d2 = 50, V1 = 0.6 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 0.6*(250/50)^2 | Answer: 15 m/s

question: Water flows at 2.6 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.4 m and length 250 m. With friction factor f = 0.034, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 22 teeth drives a gear of 101 teeth. If the pinion runs at 900 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 22, z2 = 101, N1 = 900 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 900*22 / 101 | Answer: 196 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 590 mm rotates at 450 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 590, N = 450 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.59)*450 / 60 | Answer: 13.9 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 2.3 kW at 400 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 2.3, N = 400 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(2.3*1000) / (2*pi*400) | Answer: 54.91 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 1.9 kg rotates at radius 0.34 m at 300 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 17400 N/m and mass 16.9 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 17400, m = 16.9 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(17400/16.9) | Answer: 5.107 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 7.8 m^2 and thickness 0.35 m has conductivity k = 42.2 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 35 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 7.8, L = 0.35, k = 42.2, dT = 35 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 42.2*7.8*35 / 0.35 | Answer: 32916 W

question: A surface of area 5.8 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 120 W/m^2-K to surroundings 105 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 5.8, h = 120, dT = 105 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 120*5.8*105 | Answer: 73080 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 160 m/min, feed = 0.48 mm/rev, depth of cut = 1 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 160, f = 0.48, d = 1 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*160*0.48*1 | Answer: 76800 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 350 mm is turned at 1200 rpm with a feed of 0.22 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 350, N = 1200, f = 0.22 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 350 / (0.22*1200) | Answer: 1.326 min

question: A resistor of 175 ohm carries a current of 7.5 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 175, I = 7.5 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 7.5 * 175 | Answer: 1312 V

question: Three resistors 50 ohm, 100 ohm and 50 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 50, R2 = 100, R3 = 50 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 50 + 100 + 50 | Answer: 200 ohm

question: Two resistors 72 ohm and 33 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 72, R2 = 33 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 72*33 / (72+33) | Answer: 22.63 ohm

question: A device draws 4.7 A at 5 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 5, I = 4.7 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 5 * 4.7 | Answer: 23.5 W

question: A current of 3.9 A flows through a 52 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 3.9, R = 52 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (3.9)^2 * 52 | Answer: 790.9 W

question: Two capacitors 15.1 uF and 22.7 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 15.1, C2 = 22.7 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 15.1*22.7 / (15.1+22.7) | Answer: 9.068 uF

question: A resistor 10 kohm and capacitor 17.5 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 10, C = 17.5 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (10k)(17.5u) = 175 ms | Answer: 175 ms

question: An inductor 406.6 mH is in series with 25 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 406.6, R = 25 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (406.6e-3) / 25 | Answer: 16.26 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 171.1 mH inductor at 130 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 171.1, f = 130 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (130)(171.1e-3) | Answer: 139.8 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 17.2 uF capacitor at 390 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 17.2, f = 390 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (390)(17.2e-6)) | Answer: 23.73 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 83 ohm, XL = 122 ohm and XC = 104 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 83, XL = 122, XC = 104 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(83^2 + (122 - 104)^2) | Answer: 84.93 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 71.8 mH and C = 9.7 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 71.8, C = 9.7 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(71.8e-3 * 9.7e-6)) | Answer: 190.7 Hz

question: A capacitor of 74.9 uF is charged to 160 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 74.9, V = 160 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*74.9e-6*(160)^2 | Answer: 958.7 mJ

question: An alternating voltage has a peak value of 184 V. Find its RMS value.
solution: Given: Vp = 184 | Formula: Vrms = Vp / sqrt(2) | Substitute: Vrms = 184 / sqrt(2) | Answer: 130.1 V

question: A transformer has primary voltage 150 V with 570 primary turns and 30 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 150, N1 = 570, N2 = 30 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 150 * 30/570 | Answer: 7.895 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 130 V and draws an armature current of 6 A. If the armature resistance is 1.38 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 130, Ia = 6, Ra = 1.38 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 130 - 6*1.38 | Answer: 121.7 V

question: A 4-pole induction motor on a 60 Hz supply runs at 1130 rpm. Find the slip (%).
formula: s = (Ns - N) / Ns,  Ns = 120 f / P

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 155 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.83. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 155, VL = 400, pf = 0.83 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*400*155*0.83 / 1000 | Answer: 89.13 kW

question: A load has real power 70 kW and apparent power 180 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 70, S = 180 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 70 / 180 | Answer: 0.3889

question: A machine delivers 65 kW output while drawing 197 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 65, Pi = 197 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 65/197 * 100 | Answer: 32.99 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 27 V across R1 = 50 ohm and R2 = 25 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 27, R1 = 50, R2 = 25 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 27*25 / (50+25) | Answer: 9 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 60 kohm and Rin = 23 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 60, Rin = 23 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 60 / 23 | Answer: 2.609

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 120 kohm and Rg = 16 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 120, Rg = 16 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 120/16 | Answer: 8.5

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 7935. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 7935 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(7935) | Answer: 39 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.2 m carries a central point load of 100 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.2, W = 100 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 100*4.2 / 4 | Answer: 105 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 7 m carries a UDL of 5 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7, w = 5 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 5*(7)^2 / 8 | Answer: 30.62 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 4 m carries a point load 80 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4, W = 80 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 80*4 | Answer: 320 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 5.7 m carries a UDL of 22 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.7, w = 22 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 22*(5.7)^2 / 2 | Answer: 357.4 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.4 m carries a point load 55 kN at distance 2.1 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 6.4, a = 2.1, W = 55 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 55*(6.4 - 2.1) / 6.4 | Answer: 36.95 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 5.6 m) carries a central point load 60 kN. With E = 30 GPa and I = 260e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=60000 N, L=5600.0 mm, E=30000 MPa, I=260e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 28.14 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 6.7 m carries a UDL of 27 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6.7, w = 27 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 27*(6.7)^2 / 12 | Answer: 101 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 570 mm, clear cover 25 mm and main bars of diameter 25 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 570, c = 25, dia = 25 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 570 - 25 - 25/2 | Answer: 532.5 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 22.8 m^2 carrying a factored load of 10.8 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 22.8, w = 10.8 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 10.8 * 22.8 | Answer: 246.2 kN

question: For a bar of diameter 20 mm with design bond stress 1.3 MPa and steel stress 395 MPa, find the development length in mm.
solution: Given: dia = 20, tbd = 1.3, fs = 395 | Formula: Ld = phi fs / (4 tau_bd) | Substitute: Ld = 20*395 / (4*1.3) | Answer: 1519 mm

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 4.9 m, unit weight 16 kN/m^3, phi = 37 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 5.2 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 21 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 5.2, g = 21 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (21 - 9.81)*5.2 | Answer: 58.19 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 3.9e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.7, area = 5.6e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 3.9, i = 0.7, A = 5.6 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (3.9e-4)*0.7*(5.6e-3) | Answer: 1529 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 2.4 m, bed slope 0.001 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.017. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 3.1 m under a head of 1 m. Taking Cd = 0.61 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 2.7 m wide carries a discharge of 18.1 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 140 m and design speed 70 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 140, V = 70 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (70)^2 / (127*140) | Answer: 0.2756
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: For a design speed of 55 km/h with allowable superelevation 0.08 and lateral friction 0.13, find the minimum curve radius in m.
A tank of volume 440 m^3 treats a flow of 100 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 440, Q = 100 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 440 / 100 | Answer: 4.4 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 300 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.18 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 7 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 300, k = 0.18, t = 7 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 300*(1 - e^(-0.18*7)) | Answer: 214.9 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.46, rainfall intensity 80 mm/h over a catchment of 18 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.46, i = 80, A = 18 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.46*80*18 / 360 | Answer: 1.84 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.01 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 350 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.01, M = 350 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 350*(30+0.01)/30 | Answer: 350.1 m

question: Convert the decimal number 193 to binary.
solution: Divide 193 by 2 repeatedly, recording remainders | Reading remainders in reverse gives 11000001 | Answer: 11000001 (binary)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 2 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the decimal number 1012 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 1012 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 3F4 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the 8-bit binary number 10010001 to decimal.
solution: Binary 10010001 = sum of bit-weights | Answer: 145 (decimal)
formula: Sum each bit times its positional weight (2^i)

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 01000001 and 00111111.
solution: XOR: 01111110 | Count of 1s = 6 | Answer: 6
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 1000 megabits is sent over a link of 44 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 1000, B = 44 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 1000 / 44 | Answer: 22.73 s

question: A link has bandwidth 97 Mbps and round-trip time 190 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 97, R = 190 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 97e6 * 190e-3 bits = 18430 kb | Answer: 18430 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.82, cache access time 6 ns and main-memory access time 160 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.82, tc = 6, tm = 160 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.82*6 + (1 - 0.82)*160 | Answer: 33.72 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 841008 elements?
solution: Given: n = 841008 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(841008)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: An O(n^2) algorithm performs c*n^2 basic operations. If c = 1 and n = 2860, how many operations are performed?
solution: Given: n = 2860 | Formula: operations = n^2 | Substitute: = (2860)^2 | Answer: 8179600

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.007, memory access time 130 ns and page-fault service time 10 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 10 ms = 10000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.007)*130 + 0.007*10000000.0 ns | Answer: 70.13 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 0.8 m^3 at 420 kPa and 500 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 0.8, P = 420, Tk = 500 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (420e3)*0.8 / (8.314*500) | Answer: 80.83 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.06 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 9 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.06, t = 9 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.06*9) | Answer: 0.4173

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.16 /min) is to reach 65% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.16, X = 65 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.65) / 0.16 | Answer: 6.561 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.2 /min) reaches 90% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.2, X = 90 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.9 / (0.2*(1 - 0.9)) | Answer: 45 min

question: For a reaction with A = 4e10 /s and activation energy 80 kJ/mol at 370 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 4, Ea = 80, Tk = 370 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 4e10 * exp(-80e3 / (8.314*370)) | Answer: 0.2031 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.97 and bottoms xW = 0.06, with relative volatility alpha = 2.2. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.97, xw = 0.06, al = 2.2 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.97/0.03)(0.94/0.06)] / ln(2.2) | Answer: 7.899 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.76 and x = 0.39. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.76, x = 0.39 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.76/0.24) / (0.39/0.61) | Answer: 4.953

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.15 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 100 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.15, Psat = 100 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.15 * 100 | Answer: 15 kPa

question: A stream of 7.1 kg/s with specific heat 1.1 kJ/kg-K is heated through 105 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 7.1, cp = 1.1, dT = 105 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 7.1*1.1*105 | Answer: 820.1 kW

question: A reactor of volume 17.1 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 3.1 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 17.1, Q = 3.1 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 17.1 / 3.1 | Answer: 5.516 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 7.6e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 1 mm with a concentration difference of 150 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 7.6, L = 1, dC = 150 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (7.6e-9)*150 / (1e-3) | Answer: 1140 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 6.3 min and steady-state gain 2.5. For a step input of magnitude 8, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 6.3, K = 2.5, M = 8 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 2.5 * 8 | Answer: 20 units

question: A reactor operates at a space time of 15.7 min. Find its space velocity in per hour.
solution: Given: tau = 15.7 | Formula: SV = 60 / tau  (per hour) | Substitute: SV = 60 / 15.7 | Answer: 3.822 /h

question: An aircraft wing of area 100 m^2 flies at 220 m/s (air density 1 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.7. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 100, V = 220, rho = 1, CL = 0.7 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1*(220)^2*100*0.7 / 1000 | Answer: 1694 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 115 m^2 flies at 250 m/s (density 1.225 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.1. Find the drag force in kN.
A specimen under stress 260 MPa shows an elastic strain of 2.1e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 260, eps = 2.1 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 260 / (2.1e-3) MPa = 123.8 GPa | Answer: 123.8 GPa

question: A block of mass 3 kg has a volume of 4.3e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 3, V = 4.3 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 3 / (4.3e-3) | Answer: 697.7 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 600 mm is heated through 100 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 12e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 600, dT = 100, al = 12 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 600*12e-6*100 | Answer: 0.72 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 110 ohm, R2 = 45 ohm and R3 = 430 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 110, R2 = 45, R3 = 430 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 45*430 / 110 | Answer: 175.9 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 350 ohm and gauge factor 2.1 experiences a strain of 500e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 350, GF = 2.1, eps = 500 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 350*2.1*500e-6 | Answer: 367.5 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 9.93 when the true value is 100. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.93, true = 100 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.93 - 100| / 100 * 100 | Answer: 90.07 %

question: Annual demand is 45500 units, ordering cost 90 per order and holding cost 30 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 45500, S = 90, H = 30 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*45500*90 / 30) | Answer: 522.5 units

question: An asset costs 130000 with salvage value 4000 after 16 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 130000, Sv = 4000, n = 16 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (130000 - 4000) / 16 | Answer: 7875 per year

question: A product sells for 370 per unit with variable cost 20 per unit and fixed costs 55000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 370, V = 20, F = 55000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 55000 / (370 - 20) | Answer: 157.1 units

question: Find the present worth of 180000 received 5 years from now at an interest rate of 5% per year.
solution: Given: F = 180000, n = 5, i = 5 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 180000 / (1 + 0.05)^5 | Answer: 141035 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.98, 0.97 and 0.98 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.98, r2 = 0.97, r3 = 0.98 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.98*0.97*0.98 | Answer: 0.9316

question: A process produces 26 defective items in a batch of 7500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 26, N = 7500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 26/7500 * 1e6 | Answer: 3467 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = 4x^3 + 4x^2 + 2x + 7 evaluated at x = -3.
For f(x) = -4x^3 - 8x^2 - 7x + 7, find f''(x) at x = 5.
Evaluate the definite integral of (-5x^2 - x) dx from x = -1 to x = 7.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = -5x^3/3 + -1x^2/2 + 0x | Evaluate F(7) - F(-1) | Answer: -597.3
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 5x^2 + 5x - 4 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[-2, 2], [8, 5]].
solution: Given: a = -2, b = 2, c = 8, d = 5 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (-2)(5) - (2)(8) | Answer: -26

question: Find the determinant of [[-1, 4, -3], [5, -1, -4], [1, 6, -5]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: -38

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[7, -7], [1, -2]].
solution: Trace tr = 5, Determinant = -7 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 6.14

question: Solve for x: 3x + 6y = 1 and 4x + 1y = 2.
solution: Determinant = 3*1 - 6*4 = -21 | x = (e d - b f) / det = 0.5238 | Answer: x = 0.5238
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 95, 22, 42, 37, 45.
solution: Sum = 241 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 48.2 | Answer: 48.2

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 43, 5, 38, 36, 20.
solution: Mean = 28.4 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 15.66

question: Find the slope of the line through (-3, 4) and (-7, 7).
solution: Given: x1 = -3, y1 = 4, x2 = -7, y2 = 7 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (7 - 4) / (-7 - -3) | Answer: -0.75

question: Find the distance between the points (3, -9) and (3, 4).
solution: Given: x1 = 3, y1 = -9, x2 = 3, y2 = 4 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((0)^2 + (13)^2) | Answer: 13 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (5,2), (-4,-5), (5,-7).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 40.5 sq units

question: Evaluate the number of combinations C(12, 3).
solution: Given: n = 12, r = 3 | Formula: C(n, r) = n! / (r! (n - r)!) | Substitute: C(12, 3) = 12! / (3! * 9!) | Answer: 220

question: Find the 7th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 9 and common difference 1.
solution: Given: a = 9, d = 1, n = 7 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = 9 + (7 - 1)*1 | Answer: 15

question: Find the sum of the first 36 terms of an AP with first term -6 and common difference 5.
solution: Given: a = -6, d = 5, n = 36 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 36/2 [2*-6 + (36-1)*5] | Answer: 2934

question: Find the 4th term of a geometric progression with first term 9 and common ratio 3.
solution: Given: a = 9, r = 3, n = 4 | Formula: a_n = a r^(n-1) | Substitute: a_n = 9 * 3^(4-1) | Answer: 243

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 11500 at 4.6% per annum for 2 years.
solution: Given: P = 11500, R = 4.6, Tt = 2 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 11500 * 4.6 * 2 / 100 | Answer: 1058 currency units

question: Find the amount when 7000 is invested at 10.1% per annum compounded annually for 3 years.
solution: Given: P = 7000, R = 10.1, Tt = 3 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 7000 * (1 + 10.1/100)^3 | Answer: 9342 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (-2, 3, 3) and (-2, -5, 8).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (1, -4, -2) and (-3, -1, 0).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 14.46

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (5, -3, 4) and (-3, -5, -5).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 111.6 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number -9 + 7i.
solution: Given: a = -9, b = 7 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((-9)^2 + (7)^2) | Answer: 11.4

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number -7 + -4i.
solution: Given: a = -7, b = -4 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(-4, -7) | Answer: -150.3 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -5x^3 - 2x^2 + x - 1 at x = 5.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-124 with initial guess x0=9, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=0.7 and ordinates 5, 3, 20, 6, 13, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 112 and 576.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 112 and 576 | Answer: GCD = 16

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 15 and 47.
solution: Given: a = 15, b = 47 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 15*47 / 1 | Answer: 705
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 24 mm carries an axial tensile load of 13 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 12 mm and length 2900 mm carries an axial load of 84 kN. Take E = 110 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 42 mm transmits a torque of 1550 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 42, Tt = 1550 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(1550*1000) / (pi*(42)^3) | Answer: 106.6 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 57 mm and length 1800 mm carries a torque of 1550 N-m. With G = 45 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (57)^4 / 32 = 1036333 mm^4 | theta = (1550*1000)(1800) / (45000 * 1036333) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 3.428 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 63 mm wide and 270 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 63, h = 270 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 63*(270)^2 / 6 | Answer: 765450 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (65 mm x 180 mm) carries a bending moment of 32 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (35 mm x 90 mm) has effective length 4000 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 450 MPa is designed for a working stress of 140 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 450, sw = 140 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 450 / 140 | Answer: 3.214

question: A steel bar is fully restrained and heated through 45 deg C. With E = 200 GPa and alpha = 11e-6 /deg C, find the thermal stress in MPa.
solution: Given: dT = 45, E = 200, al = 11 | Formula: sigma = E alpha (dT) | Substitute: sigma = 200000 * 11e-6 * 45 | Answer: 99 MPa

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 750 mm and wall thickness 12 mm carries an internal pressure of 1.1 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 750, t = 12, P = 1.1 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 1.1*750 / (2*12) | Answer: 34.38 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 1060 K and 430 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 1060, Tc = 430 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 430/1060) * 100 | Answer: 59.43 %

question: A refrigerator works between 250 K (cold) and 300 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 250, Th = 300 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 250 / (300 - 250) | Answer: 5

question: A heat pump operates between 265 K and 324 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 265, Th = 324 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 324 / (324 - 265) | Answer: 5.492

question: 7 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 150 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 7, dT = 150 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 7 * 0.718 * 150 | Answer: 753.9 kJ

question: 2.7 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 130 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.7, dT = 130 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 2.7 * 1.005 * 130 | Answer: 352.8 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 1.4 m^3 at 380 K with mass 4.2 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 1.4, Tk = 380, m = 4.2 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 4.2*0.287*380 / 1.4 | Answer: 327.2 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 2.8 kg of air expands isothermally at 450 K from volume V1 to 5*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.8, Tk = 450, ratio = 5 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 2.8*0.287*450*ln(5) | Answer: 582 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 2 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.26 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 2, D = 0.26 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*2*0.26 / 0.001 | Answer: 520000

question: Water flows at 1.6 m/s through a pipe of diameter 130 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 5.6 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 5.6 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*5.6 / 1000 | Answer: 54.94 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 13.2 m. Taking Cv = 0.98, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 13.2, cv = 0.98 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.98*sqrt(2*9.81*13.2) | Answer: 15.77 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 150 mm) water flows at 0.6 m/s. It contracts to diameter 120 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
Water flows at 3.8 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.3 m and length 340 m. With friction factor f = 0.035, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 29 teeth drives a gear of 87 teeth. If the pinion runs at 950 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 29, z2 = 87, N1 = 950 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 950*29 / 87 | Answer: 316.7 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 180 mm rotates at 1100 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 180, N = 1100 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.18)*1100 / 60 | Answer: 10.37 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 20.1 kW at 900 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 20.1, N = 900 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(20.1*1000) / (2*pi*900) | Answer: 213.3 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 7.2 kg rotates at radius 0.23 m at 750 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 12500 N/m and mass 16.2 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 12500, m = 16.2 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(12500/16.2) | Answer: 4.421 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 4.6 m^2 and thickness 0.11 m has conductivity k = 2 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 20 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 4.6, L = 0.11, k = 2, dT = 20 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 2*4.6*20 / 0.11 | Answer: 1673 W

question: A surface of area 2.5 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 180 W/m^2-K to surroundings 40 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 2.5, h = 180, dT = 40 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 180*2.5*40 | Answer: 18000 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 120 m/min, feed = 0.16 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2.7 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 120, f = 0.16, d = 2.7 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*120*0.16*2.7 | Answer: 51840 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 140 mm is turned at 400 rpm with a feed of 0.31 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 140, N = 400, f = 0.31 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 140 / (0.31*400) | Answer: 1.129 min

question: A resistor of 23 ohm carries a current of 2.6 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 23, I = 2.6 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 2.6 * 23 | Answer: 59.8 V

question: Three resistors 69 ohm, 32 ohm and 47 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 69, R2 = 32, R3 = 47 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 69 + 32 + 47 | Answer: 148 ohm

question: Two resistors 20 ohm and 32 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 20, R2 = 32 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 20*32 / (20+32) | Answer: 12.31 ohm

question: A device draws 14.5 A at 115 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 115, I = 14.5 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 115 * 14.5 | Answer: 1668 W

question: A current of 7.3 A flows through a 110 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 7.3, R = 110 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (7.3)^2 * 110 | Answer: 5862 W

question: Two capacitors 20 uF and 15.5 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 20, C2 = 15.5 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 20*15.5 / (20+15.5) | Answer: 8.732 uF

question: A resistor 74 kohm and capacitor 15.5 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 74, C = 15.5 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (74k)(15.5u) = 1147 ms | Answer: 1147 ms

question: An inductor 42.9 mH is in series with 143 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 42.9, R = 143 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (42.9e-3) / 143 | Answer: 0.3 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 19.9 mH inductor at 620 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 19.9, f = 620 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (620)(19.9e-3) | Answer: 77.52 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 29.9 uF capacitor at 100 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 29.9, f = 100 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (100)(29.9e-6)) | Answer: 53.23 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 63 ohm, XL = 135 ohm and XC = 100 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 63, XL = 135, XC = 100 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(63^2 + (135 - 100)^2) | Answer: 72.07 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 66.4 mH and C = 2.4 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 66.4, C = 2.4 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(66.4e-3 * 2.4e-6)) | Answer: 398.7 Hz

question: A capacitor of 98.2 uF is charged to 145 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 98.2, V = 145 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*98.2e-6*(145)^2 | Answer: 1032 mJ

question: An alternating voltage has a peak value of 136 V. Find its RMS value.
solution: Given: Vp = 136 | Formula: Vrms = Vp / sqrt(2) | Substitute: Vrms = 136 / sqrt(2) | Answer: 96.17 V

question: A transformer has primary voltage 250 V with 670 primary turns and 170 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 250, N1 = 670, N2 = 170 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 250 * 170/670 | Answer: 63.43 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 270 V and draws an armature current of 24 A. If the armature resistance is 1.16 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 270, Ia = 24, Ra = 1.16 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 270 - 24*1.16 | Answer: 242.2 V

question: A 6-pole induction motor on a 60 Hz supply runs at 880 rpm. Find the slip (%).
formula: s = (Ns - N) / Ns,  Ns = 120 f / P

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 190 A at 415 V (line) with a power factor of 0.72. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 190, VL = 415, pf = 0.72 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*415*190*0.72 / 1000 | Answer: 98.33 kW

question: A load has real power 10 kW and apparent power 65 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 10, S = 65 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 10 / 65 | Answer: 0.1538

question: A machine delivers 25 kW output while drawing 77 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 25, Pi = 77 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 25/77 * 100 | Answer: 32.47 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 17 V across R1 = 2 ohm and R2 = 46 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 17, R1 = 2, R2 = 46 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 17*46 / (2+46) | Answer: 16.29 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 120 kohm and Rin = 39 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 120, Rin = 39 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 120 / 39 | Answer: 3.077

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 30 kohm and Rg = 32 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 30, Rg = 32 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 30/32 | Answer: 1.938

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 3701. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 3701 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(3701) | Answer: 35.68 dB

question: A first-order system has a time constant of 6.8 s. Find the time (in s) to reach 63.2% of its final value.
solution: For a first-order step response, y = 1 - e^(-t/tau) | y = 0.632 when t = tau | Answer: 6.8 s

question: A simply supported beam of span 3 m carries a central point load of 15 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3, W = 15 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 15*3 / 4 | Answer: 11.25 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.2 m carries a UDL of 10 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6.2, w = 10 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 10*(6.2)^2 / 8 | Answer: 48.05 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 3.9 m carries a point load 80 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.9, W = 80 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 80*3.9 | Answer: 312 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 3.1 m carries a UDL of 4 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.1, w = 4 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 4*(3.1)^2 / 2 | Answer: 19.22 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.8 m carries a point load 50 kN at distance 2.8 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 4.8, a = 2.8, W = 50 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 50*(4.8 - 2.8) / 4.8 | Answer: 20.83 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 4.3 m) carries a central point load 60 kN. With E = 30 GPa and I = 120e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=60000 N, L=4300.0 mm, E=30000 MPa, I=120e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 27.61 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 4 m carries a UDL of 18 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4, w = 18 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 18*(4)^2 / 12 | Answer: 24 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 420 mm, clear cover 40 mm and main bars of diameter 12 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 420, c = 40, dia = 12 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 420 - 40 - 12/2 | Answer: 374 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 27.2 m^2 carrying a factored load of 11.4 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 27.2, w = 11.4 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 11.4 * 27.2 | Answer: 310.1 kN

question: For a bar of diameter 25 mm with design bond stress 1.8 MPa and steel stress 395 MPa, find the development length in mm.
solution: Given: dia = 25, tbd = 1.8, fs = 395 | Formula: Ld = phi fs / (4 tau_bd) | Substitute: Ld = 25*395 / (4*1.8) | Answer: 1372 mm

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 4.2 m, unit weight 17 kN/m^3, phi = 35 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 4.9 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 18 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 4.9, g = 18 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (18 - 9.81)*4.9 | Answer: 40.13 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 3.8e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1.5, area = 2.1e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 3.8, i = 1.5, A = 2.1 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (3.8e-4)*1.5*(2.1e-3) | Answer: 1197 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.9 m, bed slope 0.002 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.013. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 3.7 m under a head of 0.8 m. Taking Cd = 0.64 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 4.3 m wide carries a discharge of 3.9 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).

solution: Given: R = 590, V = 45 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (45)^2 / (127*590) | Answer: 0.02703

question: For a design speed of 40 km/h with allowable superelevation 0.08 and lateral friction 0.13, find the minimum curve radius in m.
A tank of volume 970 m^3 treats a flow of 85 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 210 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.28 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 7 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 210, k = 0.28, t = 7 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 210*(1 - e^(-0.28*7)) | Answer: 180.4 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.48, rainfall intensity 60 mm/h over a catchment of 27.8 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.48, i = 60, A = 27.8 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.48*60*27.8 / 360 | Answer: 2.224 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.04 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 340 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.04, M = 340 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 340*(20+0.04)/20 | Answer: 340.7 m

question: Convert the decimal number 230 to binary.
solution: Divide 230 by 2 repeatedly, recording remainders | Reading remainders in reverse gives 11100110 | Answer: 11100110 (binary)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 2 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the decimal number 1828 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 1828 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 724 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the 8-bit binary number 00000101 to decimal.
solution: Binary 00000101 = sum of bit-weights | Answer: 5 (decimal)

solution: XOR: 00001010 | Count of 1s = 2 | Answer: 2
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 990 megabits is sent over a link of 74 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 990, B = 74 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 990 / 74 | Answer: 13.38 s

question: A link has bandwidth 31 Mbps and round-trip time 110 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 31, R = 110 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 31e6 * 110e-3 bits = 3410 kb | Answer: 3410 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.9, cache access time 8 ns and main-memory access time 150 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.9, tc = 8, tm = 150 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.9*8 + (1 - 0.9)*150 | Answer: 22.2 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 595325 elements?
solution: Given: n = 595325 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(595325)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: An O(n^2) algorithm performs c*n^2 basic operations. If c = 1 and n = 1290, how many operations are performed?
solution: Given: n = 1290 | Formula: operations = n^2 | Substitute: = (1290)^2 | Answer: 1664100

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.011, memory access time 120 ns and page-fault service time 9 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 9 ms = 9000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.011)*120 + 0.011*9000000.0 ns | Answer: 99.12 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 1.4 m^3 at 400 kPa and 510 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 1.4, P = 400, Tk = 510 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (400e3)*1.4 / (8.314*510) | Answer: 132.1 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.21 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 7 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.21, t = 7 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.21*7) | Answer: 0.7701

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.41 /min) is to reach 80% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.41, X = 80 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.8) / 0.41 | Answer: 3.925 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.35 /min) reaches 75% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.35, X = 75 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.75 / (0.35*(1 - 0.75)) | Answer: 8.571 min

question: For a reaction with A = 2e10 /s and activation energy 80 kJ/mol at 390 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 2, Ea = 80, Tk = 390 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 2e10 * exp(-80e3 / (8.314*390)) | Answer: 0.3853 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.92 and bottoms xW = 0.05, with relative volatility alpha = 3. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.92, xw = 0.05, al = 3 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.92/0.08)(0.95/0.05)] / ln(3) | Answer: 4.903 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.63 and x = 0.46. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.63, x = 0.46 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.63/0.37) / (0.46/0.54) | Answer: 1.999

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.7 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 110 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.7, Psat = 110 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.7 * 110 | Answer: 77 kPa

question: A stream of 7.3 kg/s with specific heat 2.3 kJ/kg-K is heated through 100 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 7.3, cp = 2.3, dT = 100 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 7.3*2.3*100 | Answer: 1679 kW

question: A reactor of volume 5.8 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 1.9 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 5.8, Q = 1.9 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 5.8 / 1.9 | Answer: 3.053 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 5.6e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 5 mm with a concentration difference of 20 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 5.6, L = 5, dC = 20 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (5.6e-9)*20 / (5e-3) | Answer: 22.4 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 4.5 min and steady-state gain 3.4. For a step input of magnitude 16, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 4.5, K = 3.4, M = 16 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 3.4 * 16 | Answer: 54.4 units

question: A reactor operates at a space time of 16.4 min. Find its space velocity in per hour.
solution: Given: tau = 16.4 | Formula: SV = 60 / tau  (per hour) | Substitute: SV = 60 / 16.4 | Answer: 3.659 /h

question: An aircraft wing of area 70 m^2 flies at 250 m/s (air density 1.225 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.5. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 70, V = 250, rho = 1.225, CL = 0.5 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1.225*(250)^2*70*0.5 / 1000 | Answer: 134 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 35 m^2 flies at 140 m/s (density 1.225 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.1. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 35, V = 140, rho = 1.225, CD = 0.1 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*1.225*(140)^2*35*0.1 / 1000 | Answer: 42.02 kN

question: An aircraft flies at 150 m/s where the speed of sound is 340 m/s. Find the Mach number.
solution: Given: V = 150, a = 340 | Formula: M = V / a | Substitute: M = 150 / 340 | Answer: 0.4412

question: A specimen under stress 280 MPa shows an elastic strain of 1.7e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 280, eps = 1.7 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 280 / (1.7e-3) MPa = 164.7 GPa | Answer: 164.7 GPa

question: A block of mass 8 kg has a volume of 2.6e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 8, V = 2.6 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 8 / (2.6e-3) | Answer: 3077 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 1900 mm is heated through 110 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 17e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 1900, dT = 110, al = 17 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 1900*17e-6*110 | Answer: 3.553 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 75 ohm, R2 = 20 ohm and R3 = 205 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 75, R2 = 20, R3 = 205 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 20*205 / 75 | Answer: 54.67 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 1000 ohm and gauge factor 2.2 experiences a strain of 1700e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 1000, GF = 2.2, eps = 1700 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 1000*2.2*1700e-6 | Answer: 3740 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 10.35 when the true value is 50. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10.35, true = 50 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10.35 - 50| / 50 * 100 | Answer: 79.3 %

question: Annual demand is 45500 units, ordering cost 40 per order and holding cost 25 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 45500, S = 40, H = 25 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*45500*40 / 25) | Answer: 381.6 units

question: An asset costs 180000 with salvage value 34000 after 10 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 180000, Sv = 34000, n = 10 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (180000 - 34000) / 10 | Answer: 14600 per year

question: A product sells for 350 per unit with variable cost 110 per unit and fixed costs 95000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 350, V = 110, F = 95000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 95000 / (350 - 110) | Answer: 395.8 units

question: Find the present worth of 105000 received 4 years from now at an interest rate of 9% per year.
solution: Given: F = 105000, n = 4, i = 9 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 105000 / (1 + 0.09)^4 | Answer: 74385 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.94, 0.91 and 0.99 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.94, r2 = 0.91, r3 = 0.99 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.94*0.91*0.99 | Answer: 0.8468

question: A process produces 28 defective items in a batch of 7500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 28, N = 7500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 28/7500 * 1e6 | Answer: 3733 PPM

question: Find the slope of the line through (-4, 1) and (3, 5).
solution: Given: x1 = -4, y1 = 1, x2 = 3, y2 = 5 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (5 - 1) / (3 - -4) | Answer: 0.5714

question: Find the distance between the points (4, 0) and (-6, 3).
solution: Given: x1 = 4, y1 = 0, x2 = -6, y2 = 3 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-10)^2 + (3)^2) | Answer: 10.44 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (-4,-1), (-6,8), (-2,5).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 15 sq units

question: Evaluate the number of combinations C(6, 6).
solution: Given: n = 6, r = 6 | Formula: C(n, r) = n! / (r! (n - r)!) | Substitute: C(6, 6) = 6! / (6! * 0!) | Answer: 1

question: Find the 20th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 18 and common difference 7.
solution: Given: a = 18, d = 7, n = 20 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = 18 + (20 - 1)*7 | Answer: 151

question: Find the sum of the first 35 terms of an AP with first term -9 and common difference 4.
solution: Given: a = -9, d = 4, n = 35 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 35/2 [2*-9 + (35-1)*4] | Answer: 2065

question: Find the 4th term of a geometric progression with first term 3 and common ratio 2.
solution: Given: a = 3, r = 2, n = 4 | Formula: a_n = a r^(n-1) | Substitute: a_n = 3 * 2^(4-1) | Answer: 24

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 46500 at 5.2% per annum for 7 years.
solution: Given: P = 46500, R = 5.2, Tt = 7 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 46500 * 5.2 * 7 / 100 | Answer: 16926 currency units

question: Find the amount when 8500 is invested at 9.5% per annum compounded annually for 3 years.
solution: Given: P = 8500, R = 9.5, Tt = 3 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 8500 * (1 + 9.5/100)^3 | Answer: 1116 currency units

question: Find the modulus of the complex number 11 + -9i.
solution: Given: a = 11, b = -9 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((11)^2 + (-9)^2) | Answer: 14.21

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number 5 + -10i.
solution: Given: a = 5, b = -10 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(-10, 5) | Answer: -63.43 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = x^3 - 2x^2 - 7x + 1 at x = -5.

Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.6 and ordinates 20, 9, 10, 4, 15, estimate the integral.

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 78 and 25.

question: A circular rod of diameter 57 mm carries an axial tensile load of 85 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 21 mm and length 500 mm carries an axial load of 87 kN. Take E = 200 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 28 mm transmits a torque of 1550 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.

question: A shaft of diameter 29 mm and length 800 mm carries a torque of 1550 N-m. With G = 45 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.

question: A rectangular beam section is 38 mm wide and 60 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 38, h = 60 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 38*(60)^2 / 6 | Answer: 22800 mm^3
