formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (41 mm x 140 mm) has effective length 2700 mm and E = 200 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 490 MPa is designed for a working stress of 240 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 490, sw = 240 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 490 / 240 | Answer: 2.042

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 350 mm and wall thickness 10 mm carries an internal pressure of 2 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 350, t = 10, P = 2 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 2*350 / (2*10) | Answer: 35 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 980 K and 390 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 980, Tc = 390 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 390/980) * 100 | Answer: 60.2 %

question: A refrigerator works between 267 K (cold) and 324 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 267, Th = 324 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 267 / (324 - 267) | Answer: 4.684

question: A heat pump operates between 264 K and 318 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 264, Th = 318 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 318 / (318 - 264) | Answer: 5.889

question: 2.4 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 110 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.4, dT = 110 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 2.4 * 0.718 * 110 | Answer: 189.6 kJ

question: 2 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 175 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2, dT = 175 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 2 * 1.005 * 175 | Answer: 351.7 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 3.5 m^3 at 410 K with mass 1.9 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 3.5, Tk = 410, m = 1.9 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 1.9*0.287*410 / 3.5 | Answer: 63.88 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 2.6 kg of air expands isothermally at 410 K from volume V1 to 5*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.6, Tk = 410, ratio = 5 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 2.6*0.287*410*ln(5) | Answer: 492.4 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 2.8 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.33 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 2.8, D = 0.33 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*2.8*0.33 / 0.001 | Answer: 924000

question: Water flows at 0.8 m/s through a pipe of diameter 160 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 21.1 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 21.1 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*21.1 / 1000 | Answer: 207 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 13.4 m. Taking Cv = 0.95, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 13.4, cv = 0.95 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.95*sqrt(2*9.81*13.4) | Answer: 15.4 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 330 mm) water flows at 2.5 m/s. It contracts to diameter 60 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 330, d2 = 60, V1 = 2.5 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 2.5*(330/60)^2 | Answer: 75.62 m/s

question: Water flows at 2.7 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.29 m and length 480 m. With friction factor f = 0.03, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 38 teeth drives a gear of 96 teeth. If the pinion runs at 500 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 38, z2 = 96, N1 = 500 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 500*38 / 96 | Answer: 197.9 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 220 mm rotates at 500 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 220, N = 500 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.22)*500 / 60 | Answer: 5.76 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 35.6 kW at 1200 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 35.6, N = 1200 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(35.6*1000) / (2*pi*1200) | Answer: 283.3 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 6.8 kg rotates at radius 0.48 m at 250 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 20000 N/m and mass 4.5 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 20000, m = 4.5 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(20000/4.5) | Answer: 10.61 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 5.2 m^2 and thickness 0.33 m has conductivity k = 9.5 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 125 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 5.2, L = 0.33, k = 9.5, dT = 125 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 9.5*5.2*125 / 0.33 | Answer: 18712 W

question: A surface of area 3.2 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 30 W/m^2-K to surroundings 120 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 3.2, h = 30, dT = 120 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 30*3.2*120 | Answer: 11520 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 170 m/min, feed = 0.18 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2.3 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 170, f = 0.18, d = 2.3 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*170*0.18*2.3 | Answer: 70380 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 450 mm is turned at 500 rpm with a feed of 0.13 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 450, N = 500, f = 0.13 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 450 / (0.13*500) | Answer: 6.923 min

question: A resistor of 101 ohm carries a current of 4.7 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 101, I = 4.7 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 4.7 * 101 | Answer: 474.7 V

question: Three resistors 56 ohm, 49 ohm and 60 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 56, R2 = 49, R3 = 60 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 56 + 49 + 60 | Answer: 165 ohm

question: Two resistors 51 ohm and 102 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 51, R2 = 102 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 51*102 / (51+102) | Answer: 34 ohm

question: A device draws 13.4 A at 85 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 85, I = 13.4 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 85 * 13.4 | Answer: 1139 W

question: A current of 4.8 A flows through a 14 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 4.8, R = 14 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (4.8)^2 * 14 | Answer: 322.6 W

question: Two capacitors 45.4 uF and 21.9 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 45.4, C2 = 21.9 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 45.4*21.9 / (45.4+21.9) | Answer: 14.77 uF

question: A resistor 6 kohm and capacitor 11.1 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 6, C = 11.1 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (6k)(11.1u) = 66.6 ms | Answer: 66.6 ms

question: An inductor 275.2 mH is in series with 125 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 275.2, R = 125 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (275.2e-3) / 125 | Answer: 2.202 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 160.5 mH inductor at 340 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 160.5, f = 340 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (340)(160.5e-3) | Answer: 342.9 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 37.1 uF capacitor at 410 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 37.1, f = 410 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (410)(37.1e-6)) | Answer: 10.46 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 41 ohm, XL = 113 ohm and XC = 56 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 41, XL = 113, XC = 56 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(41^2 + (113 - 56)^2) | Answer: 70.21 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 81.3 mH and C = 0.2 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 81.3, C = 0.2 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(81.3e-3 * 0.2e-6)) | Answer: 1248 Hz

question: A capacitor of 26.6 uF is charged to 75 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 26.6, V = 75 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*26.6e-6*(75)^2 | Answer: 74.81 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 410 V with 510 primary turns and 220 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 410, N1 = 510, N2 = 220 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 410 * 220/510 | Answer: 176.9 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 400 V and draws an armature current of 14 A. If the armature resistance is 0.22 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 400, Ia = 14, Ra = 0.22 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 400 - 14*0.22 | Answer: 396.9 V

question: A 4-pole induction motor on a 50 Hz supply runs at 910 rpm. Find the slip (%).
formula: s = (Ns - N) / Ns,  Ns = 120 f / P

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 35 A at 415 V (line) with a power factor of 0.82. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 35, VL = 415, pf = 0.82 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*415*35*0.82 / 1000 | Answer: 20.63 kW

question: A load has real power 90 kW and apparent power 200 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 90, S = 200 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 90 / 200 | Answer: 0.45

question: A machine delivers 190 kW output while drawing 217 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 190, Pi = 217 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 190/217 * 100 | Answer: 87.56 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 25 V across R1 = 2 ohm and R2 = 38 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 25, R1 = 2, R2 = 38 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 25*38 / (2+38) | Answer: 23.75 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 30 kohm and Rin = 46 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 30, Rin = 46 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 30 / 46 | Answer: 0.6522

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 90 kohm and Rg = 46 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 90, Rg = 46 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 90/46 | Answer: 2.957

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 4999. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 4999 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(4999) | Answer: 36.99 dB

question: A signal is sampled at 186 kHz. According to the Nyquist criterion, what is the maximum signal frequency that can be represented (in kHz)?
solution: Given: fs = 186 | Formula: f_max = fs / 2 | Substitute: f_max = 186 / 2 | Answer: 93 kHz

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.4 m carries a central point load of 65 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.4, W = 65 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 65*4.4 / 4 | Answer: 71.5 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.2 m carries a UDL of 25 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.2, w = 25 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 25*(4.2)^2 / 8 | Answer: 55.12 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 2 m carries a point load 50 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 2, W = 50 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 50*2 | Answer: 100 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 1.2 m carries a UDL of 38 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 1.2, w = 38 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 38*(1.2)^2 / 2 | Answer: 27.36 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.1 m carries a point load 30 kN at distance 3.2 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 4.1, a = 3.2, W = 30 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 30*(4.1 - 3.2) / 4.1 | Answer: 6.585 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 3.2 m) carries a central point load 15 kN. With E = 25 GPa and I = 410e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=15000 N, L=3200.0 mm, E=25000 MPa, I=410e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 0.999 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 5.6 m carries a UDL of 30 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.6, w = 30 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 30*(5.6)^2 / 12 | Answer: 78.4 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 660 mm, clear cover 40 mm and main bars of diameter 12 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 660, c = 40, dia = 12 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 660 - 40 - 12/2 | Answer: 614 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 10.4 m^2 carrying a factored load of 17 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 10.4, w = 17 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 17 * 10.4 | Answer: 176.8 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 4.6 m, unit weight 19 kN/m^3, phi = 36 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 8.9 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 18 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 8.9, g = 18 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (18 - 9.81)*8.9 | Answer: 72.89 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 6.5e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.4, area = 7.9e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 6.5, i = 0.4, A = 7.9 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (6.5e-4)*0.4*(7.9e-3) | Answer: 2054 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 0.8 m, bed slope 0.003 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.02. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 1.3 m under a head of 0.2 m. Taking Cd = 0.62 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 2.3 m wide carries a discharge of 24.1 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 290 m and design speed 55 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 290, V = 55 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (55)^2 / (127*290) | Answer: 0.08213
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: For a design speed of 80 km/h with allowable superelevation 0.07 and lateral friction 0.13, find the minimum curve radius in m.
A tank of volume 630 m^3 treats a flow of 75 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 630, Q = 75 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 630 / 75 | Answer: 8.4 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 160 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.24 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 5 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 160, k = 0.24, t = 5 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 160*(1 - e^(-0.24*5)) | Answer: 111.8 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.83, rainfall intensity 105 mm/h over a catchment of 55.6 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.83, i = 105, A = 55.6 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.83*105*55.6 / 360 | Answer: 13.46 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.07 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 650 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.07, M = 650 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 650*(30+0.07)/30 | Answer: 651.5 m

question: Convert the decimal number 91 to binary.
solution: Divide 91 by 2 repeatedly, recording remainders | Reading remainders in reverse gives 1011011 | Answer: 1011011 (binary)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 2 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the decimal number 3371 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 3371 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: D2B (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the 8-bit binary number 01001011 to decimal.
solution: Binary 01001011 = sum of bit-weights | Answer: 75 (decimal)
formula: Sum each bit times its positional weight (2^i)

solution: XOR: 00000010 | Count of 1s = 1 | Answer: 1
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 1000 megabits is sent over a link of 82 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 1000, B = 82 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 1000 / 82 | Answer: 12.2 s

question: A link has bandwidth 61 Mbps and round-trip time 130 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 61, R = 130 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 61e6 * 130e-3 bits = 7930 kb | Answer: 7930 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.96, cache access time 3 ns and main-memory access time 100 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.96, tc = 3, tm = 100 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.96*3 + (1 - 0.96)*100 | Answer: 6.88 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 45482 elements?
solution: Given: n = 45482 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(45482)) + 1 | Answer: 16

question: An O(n^2) algorithm performs c*n^2 basic operations. If c = 1 and n = 2960, how many operations are performed?
solution: Given: n = 2960 | Formula: operations = n^2 | Substitute: = (2960)^2 | Answer: 8761600

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.019, memory access time 140 ns and page-fault service time 10 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 10 ms = 10000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.019)*140 + 0.019*10000000.0 ns | Answer: 190.1 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 1.9 m^3 at 230 kPa and 410 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 1.9, P = 230, Tk = 410 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (230e3)*1.9 / (8.314*410) | Answer: 128.2 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.39 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 11 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.39, t = 11 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.39*11) | Answer: 0.9863

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.4 /min) is to reach 80% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.4, X = 80 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.8) / 0.4 | Answer: 4.024 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.21 /min) reaches 70% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.21, X = 70 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.7 / (0.21*(1 - 0.7)) | Answer: 11.11 min

question: For a reaction with A = 5e10 /s and activation energy 90 kJ/mol at 490 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 5, Ea = 90, Tk = 490 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 5e10 * exp(-90e3 / (8.314*490)) | Answer: 12.72 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.96 and bottoms xW = 0.08, with relative volatility alpha = 1.5. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.96, xw = 0.08, al = 1.5 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.96/0.04)(0.92/0.08)] / ln(1.5) | Answer: 13.86 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.89 and x = 0.31. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.89, x = 0.31 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.89/0.11) / (0.31/0.69) | Answer: 18.01

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.82 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 70 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.82, Psat = 70 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.82 * 70 | Answer: 57.4 kPa

question: A stream of 8.2 kg/s with specific heat 3.6 kJ/kg-K is heated through 55 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 8.2, cp = 3.6, dT = 55 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 8.2*3.6*55 | Answer: 1624 kW

question: A reactor of volume 9.3 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 3.4 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 9.3, Q = 3.4 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 9.3 / 3.4 | Answer: 2.735 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 1.4e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 2 mm with a concentration difference of 90 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 1.4, L = 2, dC = 90 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (1.4e-9)*90 / (2e-3) | Answer: 63 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 4.8 min and steady-state gain 1.8. For a step input of magnitude 18, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 4.8, K = 1.8, M = 18 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 1.8 * 18 | Answer: 32.4 units

question: A reactor operates at a space time of 8.1 min. Find its space velocity in per hour.
solution: Given: tau = 8.1 | Formula: SV = 60 / tau  (per hour) | Substitute: SV = 60 / 8.1 | Answer: 7.407 /h

question: An aircraft wing of area 85 m^2 flies at 110 m/s (air density 0.7 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 1.4. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 85, V = 110, rho = 0.7, CL = 1.4 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.7*(110)^2*85*1.4 / 1000 | Answer: 504 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 55 m^2 flies at 180 m/s (density 0.4 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.08. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 55, V = 180, rho = 0.4, CD = 0.08 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.4*(180)^2*55*0.08 / 1000 | Answer: 28.51 kN

question: A specimen under stress 220 MPa shows an elastic strain of 2.5e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 220, eps = 2.5 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 220 / (2.5e-3) MPa = 88 GPa | Answer: 88 GPa

question: A block of mass 40 kg has a volume of 1.4e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 40, V = 1.4 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 40 / (1.4e-3) | Answer: 28571 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 1200 mm is heated through 35 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 11e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 1200, dT = 35, al = 11 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 1200*11e-6*35 | Answer: 0.462 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 115 ohm, R2 = 10 ohm and R3 = 400 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 115, R2 = 10, R3 = 400 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 10*400 / 115 | Answer: 34.78 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 120 ohm and gauge factor 2.2 experiences a strain of 550e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 120, GF = 2.2, eps = 550 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 120*2.2*550e-6 | Answer: 145.2 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 10.21 when the true value is 20. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10.21, true = 20 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10.21 - 20| / 20 * 100 | Answer: 48.95 %

question: Annual demand is 4500 units, ordering cost 290 per order and holding cost 15 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 4500, S = 290, H = 15 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*4500*290 / 15) | Answer: 417.1 units

question: An asset costs 230000 with salvage value 22000 after 14 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 230000, Sv = 22000, n = 14 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (230000 - 22000) / 14 | Answer: 14857 per year

question: A product sells for 390 per unit with variable cost 200 per unit and fixed costs 50000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 390, V = 200, F = 50000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 50000 / (390 - 200) | Answer: 263.2 units

question: Find the present worth of 170000 received 8 years from now at an interest rate of 5% per year.
solution: Given: F = 170000, n = 8, i = 5 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 170000 / (1 + 0.05)^8 | Answer: 115063 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.98, 0.98 and 0.97 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.98, r2 = 0.98, r3 = 0.97 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.98*0.98*0.97 | Answer: 0.9316

question: A process produces 5 defective items in a batch of 10000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 5, N = 10000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 5/10000 * 1e6 | Answer: 500 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -2x^3 - 7x^2 - x - 1 evaluated at x = 0.
For f(x) = 3x^3 - 5x^2 + 5x + 3, find f''(x) at x = 0.
Evaluate the definite integral of (2x^2 - 4x - 3) dx from x = 2 to x = 6.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = 2x^3/3 + -4x^2/2 + -3x | Evaluate F(6) - F(2) | Answer: 62.67
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of x^2 + 12x + 10 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[-6, 3], [6, 8]].
solution: Given: a = -6, b = 3, c = 6, d = 8 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (-6)(8) - (3)(6) | Answer: -66

question: Find the determinant of [[6, 2, -6], [-3, -6, 3], [-4, 2, -3]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: 210

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[6, -7], [-3, -1]].
solution: Trace tr = 5, Determinant = -27 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 8.266

question: Solve for x: 2x + 1y = -1 and 6x + 5y = -6.
solution: Determinant = 2*5 - 1*6 = 4 | x = (e d - b f) / det = 0.25 | Answer: x = 0.25
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 49, 47, 13, 63, 29.
solution: Sum = 201 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 40.2 | Answer: 40.2

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 44, 8, 47, 43, 21.
solution: Mean = 32.6 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 17.21

question: Find the slope of the line through (5, -1) and (-5, 2).
solution: Given: x1 = 5, y1 = -1, x2 = -5, y2 = 2 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (2 - -1) / (-5 - 5) | Answer: -0.3

question: Find the distance between the points (7, -1) and (-5, 0).
solution: Given: x1 = 7, y1 = -1, x2 = -5, y2 = 0 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-12)^2 + (1)^2) | Answer: 12.04 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (-4,-1), (-6,3), (8,-8).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 17 sq units

question: Evaluate the number of combinations C(18, 11).
solution: Given: n = 18, r = 11 | Formula: C(n, r) = n! / (r! (n - r)!) | Substitute: C(18, 11) = 18! / (11! * 7!) | Answer: 31824

question: Find the 13th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 1 and common difference -6.
solution: Given: a = 1, d = -6, n = 13 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = 1 + (13 - 1)*-6 | Answer: -71

question: Find the sum of the first 38 terms of an AP with first term 10 and common difference -6.
solution: Given: a = 10, d = -6, n = 38 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 38/2 [2*10 + (38-1)*-6] | Answer: -3838

question: Find the 6th term of a geometric progression with first term 8 and common ratio 3.
solution: Given: a = 8, r = 3, n = 6 | Formula: a_n = a r^(n-1) | Substitute: a_n = 8 * 3^(6-1) | Answer: 1944

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 22500 at 10.3% per annum for 7 years.
solution: Given: P = 22500, R = 10.3, Tt = 7 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 22500 * 10.3 * 7 / 100 | Answer: 16223 currency units

question: Find the amount when 12000 is invested at 8.7% per annum compounded annually for 3 years.
solution: Given: P = 12000, R = 8.7, Tt = 3 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 12000 * (1 + 8.7/100)^3 | Answer: 15412 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (-6, 6, 4) and (5, -2, -7).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (1, -4, -1) and (2, -2, 4).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 19.9

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (2, 1, 5) and (-1, -5, 5).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 62.6 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number -2 + -2i.
solution: Given: a = -2, b = -2 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((-2)^2 + (-2)^2) | Answer: 2.828

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number 9 + -6i.
solution: Given: a = 9, b = -6 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(-6, 9) | Answer: -33.69 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -x^3 - 3x^2 - 5x + 4 at x = 5.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-186 with initial guess x0=4, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=2 and ordinates 3, 14, 2, 12, 9, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 542 and 24.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 542 and 24 | Answer: GCD = 2

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 28 and 22.
solution: Given: a = 28, b = 22 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 28*22 / 2 | Answer: 308
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 50 mm carries an axial tensile load of 110 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 22 mm and length 500 mm carries an axial load of 85 kN. Take E = 70 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 47 mm transmits a torque of 950 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 47, Tt = 950 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(950*1000) / (pi*(47)^3) | Answer: 46.6 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 61 mm and length 1100 mm carries a torque of 700 N-m. With G = 45 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (61)^4 / 32 = 1359312 mm^4 | theta = (700*1000)(1100) / (45000 * 1359312) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 0.7212 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 147 mm wide and 60 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 147, h = 60 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 147*(60)^2 / 6 | Answer: 88200 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (64 mm x 140 mm) carries a bending moment of 2 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (78 mm x 90 mm) has effective length 1500 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 850 MPa is designed for a working stress of 160 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 850, sw = 160 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 850 / 160 | Answer: 5.312

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 550 mm and wall thickness 9 mm carries an internal pressure of 1 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 550, t = 9, P = 1 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 1*550 / (2*9) | Answer: 30.56 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 1180 K and 330 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 1180, Tc = 330 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 330/1180) * 100 | Answer: 72.03 %

question: A refrigerator works between 263 K (cold) and 302 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 263, Th = 302 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 263 / (302 - 263) | Answer: 6.744

question: A heat pump operates between 283 K and 312 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 283, Th = 312 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 312 / (312 - 283) | Answer: 10.76

question: 5.6 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 55 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 5.6, dT = 55 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 5.6 * 0.718 * 55 | Answer: 221.1 kJ

question: 6.6 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 25 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 6.6, dT = 25 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 6.6 * 1.005 * 25 | Answer: 165.8 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 1.6 m^3 at 580 K with mass 5.7 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 1.6, Tk = 580, m = 5.7 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 5.7*0.287*580 / 1.6 | Answer: 593 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 3.8 kg of air expands isothermally at 400 K from volume V1 to 4*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.8, Tk = 400, ratio = 4 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 3.8*0.287*400*ln(4) | Answer: 604.8 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 3.2 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.38 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 3.2, D = 0.38 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*3.2*0.38 / 0.001 | Answer: 1216000

question: Water flows at 0.9 m/s through a pipe of diameter 180 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 2.1 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 2.1 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*2.1 / 1000 | Answer: 20.6 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 11.1 m. Taking Cv = 0.95, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 11.1, cv = 0.95 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.95*sqrt(2*9.81*11.1) | Answer: 14.02 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 290 mm) water flows at 0.6 m/s. It contracts to diameter 70 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 290, d2 = 70, V1 = 0.6 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 0.6*(290/70)^2 | Answer: 10.3 m/s

question: Water flows at 1.1 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.47 m and length 240 m. With friction factor f = 0.034, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 25 teeth drives a gear of 69 teeth. If the pinion runs at 850 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 25, z2 = 69, N1 = 850 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 850*25 / 69 | Answer: 308 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 480 mm rotates at 1350 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 480, N = 1350 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.48)*1350 / 60 | Answer: 33.93 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 31.1 kW at 1300 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 31.1, N = 1300 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(31.1*1000) / (2*pi*1300) | Answer: 228.4 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 3.9 kg rotates at radius 0.34 m at 200 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 600 N/m and mass 15.8 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 600, m = 15.8 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(600/15.8) | Answer: 0.9808 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 1.9 m^2 and thickness 0.26 m has conductivity k = 30.9 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 30 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 1.9, L = 0.26, k = 30.9, dT = 30 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 30.9*1.9*30 / 0.26 | Answer: 6774 W

question: A surface of area 0.9 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 155 W/m^2-K to surroundings 130 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 0.9, h = 155, dT = 130 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 155*0.9*130 | Answer: 18135 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 90 m/min, feed = 0.5 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2.5 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 90, f = 0.5, d = 2.5 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*90*0.5*2.5 | Answer: 112500 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 240 mm is turned at 200 rpm with a feed of 0.3 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 240, N = 200, f = 0.3 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 240 / (0.3*200) | Answer: 4 min

question: A resistor of 129 ohm carries a current of 0.6 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 129, I = 0.6 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 0.6 * 129 | Answer: 77.4 V

question: Three resistors 67 ohm, 99 ohm and 29 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 67, R2 = 99, R3 = 29 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 67 + 99 + 29 | Answer: 195 ohm

question: Two resistors 49 ohm and 117 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 49, R2 = 117 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 49*117 / (49+117) | Answer: 34.54 ohm

question: A device draws 7.4 A at 125 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 125, I = 7.4 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 125 * 7.4 | Answer: 925 W

question: A current of 4.6 A flows through a 92 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 4.6, R = 92 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (4.6)^2 * 92 | Answer: 1947 W

question: Two capacitors 1.3 uF and 3 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 1.3, C2 = 3 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 1.3*3 / (1.3+3) | Answer: 0.907 uF

question: A resistor 64 kohm and capacitor 5.1 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 64, C = 5.1 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (64k)(5.1u) = 326.4 ms | Answer: 326.4 ms

question: An inductor 471.2 mH is in series with 48 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 471.2, R = 48 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (471.2e-3) / 48 | Answer: 9.817 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 130.9 mH inductor at 390 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 130.9, f = 390 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (390)(130.9e-3) | Answer: 320.8 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 2.9 uF capacitor at 800 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 2.9, f = 800 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (800)(2.9e-6)) | Answer: 68.6 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 31 ohm, XL = 12 ohm and XC = 87 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 31, XL = 12, XC = 87 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(31^2 + (12 - 87)^2) | Answer: 81.15 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 54.1 mH and C = 3.8 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 54.1, C = 3.8 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(54.1e-3 * 3.8e-6)) | Answer: 351 Hz

question: A capacitor of 94.1 uF is charged to 125 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 94.1, V = 125 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*94.1e-6*(125)^2 | Answer: 735.2 mJ

question: An alternating voltage has a peak value of 204 V. Find its RMS value.
solution: Given: Vp = 204 | Formula: Vrms = Vp / sqrt(2) | Substitute: Vrms = 204 / sqrt(2) | Answer: 144.2 V

question: A transformer has primary voltage 390 V with 530 primary turns and 420 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 390, N1 = 530, N2 = 420 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 390 * 420/530 | Answer: 309.1 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 430 V and draws an armature current of 56 A. If the armature resistance is 0.81 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 430, Ia = 56, Ra = 0.81 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 430 - 56*0.81 | Answer: 384.6 V

question: A 4-pole induction motor on a 60 Hz supply runs at 1010 rpm. Find the slip (%).
formula: s = (Ns - N) / Ns,  Ns = 120 f / P

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 20 A at 415 V (line) with a power factor of 0.81. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 20, VL = 415, pf = 0.81 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*415*20*0.81 / 1000 | Answer: 11.64 kW

question: A load has real power 35 kW and apparent power 170 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 35, S = 170 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 35 / 170 | Answer: 0.2059

question: A machine delivers 190 kW output while drawing 207 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 190, Pi = 207 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 190/207 * 100 | Answer: 91.79 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 19 V across R1 = 6 ohm and R2 = 1 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 19, R1 = 6, R2 = 1 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 19*1 / (6+1) | Answer: 2.714 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 30 kohm and Rin = 19 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 30, Rin = 19 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 30 / 19 | Answer: 1.579

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 50 kohm and Rg = 29 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 50, Rg = 29 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 50/29 | Answer: 2.724

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 5943. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 5943 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(5943) | Answer: 37.74 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.7 m carries a central point load of 95 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 9.7, W = 95 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 95*9.7 / 4 | Answer: 230.4 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 5.5 m carries a UDL of 5 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.5, w = 5 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 5*(5.5)^2 / 8 | Answer: 18.91 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 2.6 m carries a point load 40 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 2.6, W = 40 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 40*2.6 | Answer: 104 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 1.6 m carries a UDL of 10 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 1.6, w = 10 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 10*(1.6)^2 / 2 | Answer: 12.8 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 8.5 m carries a point load 85 kN at distance 1.3 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 8.5, a = 1.3, W = 85 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 85*(8.5 - 1.3) / 8.5 | Answer: 72 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 3.2 m) carries a central point load 65 kN. With E = 25 GPa and I = 530e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=65000 N, L=3200.0 mm, E=25000 MPa, I=530e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 3.349 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 4.1 m carries a UDL of 30 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.1, w = 30 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 30*(4.1)^2 / 12 | Answer: 42.02 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 580 mm, clear cover 35 mm and main bars of diameter 16 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 580, c = 35, dia = 16 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 580 - 35 - 16/2 | Answer: 537 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 24.5 m^2 carrying a factored load of 9.7 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 24.5, w = 9.7 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 9.7 * 24.5 | Answer: 237.6 kN

question: For a bar of diameter 20 mm with design bond stress 2.4 MPa and steel stress 435 MPa, find the development length in mm.
solution: Given: dia = 20, tbd = 2.4, fs = 435 | Formula: Ld = phi fs / (4 tau_bd) | Substitute: Ld = 20*435 / (4*2.4) | Answer: 906.2 mm

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 3.5 m, unit weight 17 kN/m^3, phi = 37 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 8.1 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 18 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 8.1, g = 18 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (18 - 9.81)*8.1 | Answer: 66.34 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 8.3e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1.1, area = 6.4e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 8.3, i = 1.1, A = 6.4 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (8.3e-4)*1.1*(6.4e-3) | Answer: 5843 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.7 m, bed slope 0.009 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.019. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 2.8 m under a head of 0.6 m. Taking Cd = 0.62 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 3.2 m wide carries a discharge of 8 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 430 m and design speed 100 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 430, V = 100 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (100)^2 / (127*430) | Answer: 0.1831
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: For a design speed of 55 km/h with allowable superelevation 0.07 and lateral friction 0.13, find the minimum curve radius in m.
A tank of volume 1000 m^3 treats a flow of 160 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 1000, Q = 160 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 1000 / 160 | Answer: 6.25 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 280 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.16 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 4 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 280, k = 0.16, t = 4 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 280*(1 - e^(-0.16*4)) | Answer: 132.4 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.64, rainfall intensity 50 mm/h over a catchment of 20 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.64, i = 50, A = 20 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.64*50*20 / 360 | Answer: 1.778 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.04 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 220 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.04, M = 220 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 220*(20+0.04)/20 | Answer: 220.4 m

question: Convert the decimal number 77 to binary.
solution: Divide 77 by 2 repeatedly, recording remainders | Reading remainders in reverse gives 1001101 | Answer: 1001101 (binary)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 2 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the decimal number 2235 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 2235 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 8BB (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the 8-bit binary number 11111110 to decimal.
solution: Binary 11111110 = sum of bit-weights | Answer: 254 (decimal)
formula: Sum each bit times its positional weight (2^i)

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 10010001 and 10100101.
solution: XOR: 00110100 | Count of 1s = 3 | Answer: 3
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 210 megabits is sent over a link of 20 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 210, B = 20 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 210 / 20 | Answer: 10.5 s

question: A link has bandwidth 72 Mbps and round-trip time 130 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 72, R = 130 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 72e6 * 130e-3 bits = 9360 kb | Answer: 9360 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.81, cache access time 6 ns and main-memory access time 140 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.81, tc = 6, tm = 140 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.81*6 + (1 - 0.81)*140 | Answer: 31.46 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 729855 elements?
solution: Given: n = 729855 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(729855)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: An O(n^2) algorithm performs c*n^2 basic operations. If c = 1 and n = 2800, how many operations are performed?
solution: Given: n = 2800 | Formula: operations = n^2 | Substitute: = (2800)^2 | Answer: 7840000

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.014, memory access time 150 ns and page-fault service time 9 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 9 ms = 9000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.014)*150 + 0.014*9000000.0 ns | Answer: 126.1 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 2.2 m^3 at 120 kPa and 300 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 2.2, P = 120, Tk = 300 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (120e3)*2.2 / (8.314*300) | Answer: 105.8 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.23 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 8 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.23, t = 8 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.23*8) | Answer: 0.8412

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.26 /min) is to reach 70% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.26, X = 70 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.7) / 0.26 | Answer: 4.631 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.25 /min) reaches 75% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.25, X = 75 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.75 / (0.25*(1 - 0.75)) | Answer: 12 min

question: For a reaction with A = 7e10 /s and activation energy 85 kJ/mol at 430 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 7, Ea = 85, Tk = 430 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 7e10 * exp(-85e3 / (8.314*430)) | Answer: 3.306 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.91 and bottoms xW = 0.03, with relative volatility alpha = 1.7. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.91, xw = 0.03, al = 1.7 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.91/0.09)(0.97/0.03)] / ln(1.7) | Answer: 10.91 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.71 and x = 0.35. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.71, x = 0.35 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.71/0.29) / (0.35/0.65) | Answer: 4.547

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.1 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 50 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.1, Psat = 50 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.1 * 50 | Answer: 5 kPa

question: A stream of 3.2 kg/s with specific heat 2.9 kJ/kg-K is heated through 80 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 3.2, cp = 2.9, dT = 80 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 3.2*2.9*80 | Answer: 742.4 kW

question: A reactor of volume 15.4 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 4.1 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 15.4, Q = 4.1 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 15.4 / 4.1 | Answer: 3.756 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 1.5e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 4 mm with a concentration difference of 110 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 1.5, L = 4, dC = 110 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (1.5e-9)*110 / (4e-3) | Answer: 41.25 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 2.3 min and steady-state gain 2.5. For a step input of magnitude 7, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 2.3, K = 2.5, M = 7 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 2.5 * 7 | Answer: 17.5 units

question: A reactor operates at a space time of 2.2 min. Find its space velocity in per hour.
solution: Given: tau = 2.2 | Formula: SV = 60 / tau  (per hour) | Substitute: SV = 60 / 2.2 | Answer: 27.27 /h

question: An aircraft wing of area 45 m^2 flies at 200 m/s (air density 0.7 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 1. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 45, V = 200, rho = 0.7, CL = 1 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.7*(200)^2*45*1 / 1000 | Answer: 630 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 80 m^2 flies at 250 m/s (density 1 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.11. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 80, V = 250, rho = 1, CD = 0.11 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*1*(250)^2*80*0.11 / 1000 | Answer: 275 kN

question: A specimen under stress 110 MPa shows an elastic strain of 2.1e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 110, eps = 2.1 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 110 / (2.1e-3) MPa = 52.38 GPa | Answer: 52.38 GPa

question: A block of mass 15 kg has a volume of 5.8e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 15, V = 5.8 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 15 / (5.8e-3) | Answer: 2586 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 2900 mm is heated through 100 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 12e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 2900, dT = 100, al = 12 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 2900*12e-6*100 | Answer: 3.48 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 130 ohm, R2 = 125 ohm and R3 = 450 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 130, R2 = 125, R3 = 450 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 125*450 / 130 | Answer: 432.7 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 120 ohm and gauge factor 2.1 experiences a strain of 1000e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 120, GF = 2.1, eps = 1000 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 120*2.1*1000e-6 | Answer: 252 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 10.79 when the true value is 20. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10.79, true = 20 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10.79 - 20| / 20 * 100 | Answer: 46.05 %

question: Annual demand is 14500 units, ordering cost 260 per order and holding cost 17 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 14500, S = 260, H = 17 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*14500*260 / 17) | Answer: 666 units

question: An asset costs 190000 with salvage value 18000 after 20 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 190000, Sv = 18000, n = 20 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (190000 - 18000) / 20 | Answer: 8600 per year

question: A product sells for 420 per unit with variable cost 30 per unit and fixed costs 145000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 420, V = 30, F = 145000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 145000 / (420 - 30) | Answer: 371.8 units

question: Find the present worth of 100000 received 4 years from now at an interest rate of 11% per year.
solution: Given: F = 100000, n = 4, i = 11 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 100000 / (1 + 0.11)^4 | Answer: 65873 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.95, 0.97 and 0.93 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.95, r2 = 0.97, r3 = 0.93 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.95*0.97*0.93 | Answer: 0.857

question: A process produces 8 defective items in a batch of 19500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 8, N = 19500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 8/19500 * 1e6 | Answer: 410.3 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -3x^3 - 7x^2 + 9x - 7 evaluated at x = 4.
For f(x) = -4x^3 - 2x^2 - 9x, find f''(x) at x = -5.
Evaluate the definite integral of (4x^2 - 2x - 5) dx from x = -2 to x = 4.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = 4x^3/3 + -2x^2/2 + -5x | Evaluate F(4) - F(-2) | Answer: 54

question: Find the larger real root of 3x^2 + 10x - 2 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[1, -9], [-7, -2]].
solution: Given: a = 1, b = -9, c = -7, d = -2 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (1)(-2) - (-9)(-7) | Answer: -65

question: Find the determinant of [[4, 3, 0], [3, 0, -3], [-3, 0, -5]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: 72

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[5, -8], [-3, 4]].
solution: Trace tr = 9, Determinant = -4 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 9.424

question: Solve for x: 0x + -6y = 8 and 5x + 3y = 8.
solution: Determinant = 0*3 - -6*5 = 30 | x = (e d - b f) / det = 2.4 | Answer: x = 2.4

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 50, 25, 8, 66, 32.
solution: Sum = 181 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 36.2 | Answer: 36.2

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 25, 9, 38, 31, 22.
solution: Mean = 25 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 10.84

question: Find the slope of the line through (-3, 3) and (-8, -5).
solution: Given: x1 = -3, y1 = 3, x2 = -8, y2 = -5 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (-5 - 3) / (-8 - -3) | Answer: 1.6

question: Find the distance between the points (-8, 9) and (-3, -9).
solution: Given: x1 = -8, y1 = 9, x2 = -3, y2 = -9 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((5)^2 + (-18)^2) | Answer: 18.68 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (-4,-8), (-5,7), (-1,2).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 27.5 sq units

question: Evaluate the number of combinations C(18, 14).
solution: Given: n = 18, r = 14 | Formula: C(n, r) = n! / (r! (n - r)!) | Substitute: C(18, 14) = 18! / (14! * 4!) | Answer: 3060

question: Find the 27th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 7 and common difference 6.
solution: Given: a = 7, d = 6, n = 27 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = 7 + (27 - 1)*6 | Answer: 163

question: Find the sum of the first 6 terms of an AP with first term 2 and common difference -3.
solution: Given: a = 2, d = -3, n = 6 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 6/2 [2*2 + (6-1)*-3] | Answer: -33

question: Find the 4th term of a geometric progression with first term 6 and common ratio 3.
solution: Given: a = 6, r = 3, n = 4 | Formula: a_n = a r^(n-1) | Substitute: a_n = 6 * 3^(4-1) | Answer: 162

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 27500 at 13.7% per annum for 3 years.
solution: Given: P = 27500, R = 13.7, Tt = 3 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 27500 * 13.7 * 3 / 100 | Answer: 11302 currency units

question: Find the amount when 31000 is invested at 7.6% per annum compounded annually for 5 years.
solution: Given: P = 31000, R = 7.6, Tt = 5 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 31000 * (1 + 7.6/100)^5 | Answer: 44712 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (7, 5, -4) and (-3, -8, 8).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (-4, 1, -4) and (6, 1, 5).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 14.04

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (6, 0, 5) and (6, -2, -1).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 51.69 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number 6 + -1i.
solution: Given: a = 6, b = -1 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((6)^2 + (-1)^2) | Answer: 6.083

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number 8 + -12i.
solution: Given: a = 8, b = -12 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(-12, 8) | Answer: -56.31 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = 5x^3 + 6x^2 - 5x + 9 at x = -2.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-162 with initial guess x0=7, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.4 and ordinates 2, 6, 19, 7, 8, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 70 and 301.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 70 and 301 | Answer: GCD = 7

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 12 and 10.
solution: Given: a = 12, b = 10 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 12*10 / 2 | Answer: 60
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 17 mm carries an axial tensile load of 33 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 39 mm and length 700 mm carries an axial load of 68 kN. Take E = 70 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 42 mm transmits a torque of 2950 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 42, Tt = 2950 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(2950*1000) / (pi*(42)^3) | Answer: 202.8 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 58 mm and length 900 mm carries a torque of 1600 N-m. With G = 77 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (58)^4 / 32 = 1110994 mm^4 | theta = (1600*1000)(900) / (77000 * 1110994) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 0.9645 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 125 mm wide and 220 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 125, h = 220 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 125*(220)^2 / 6 | Answer: 1008333 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (40 mm x 260 mm) carries a bending moment of 2 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (62 mm x 110 mm) has effective length 1800 mm and E = 200 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 410 MPa is designed for a working stress of 70 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 410, sw = 70 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 410 / 70 | Answer: 5.857

question: A steel bar is fully restrained and heated through 100 deg C. With E = 210 GPa and alpha = 12e-6 /deg C, find the thermal stress in MPa.
solution: Given: dT = 100, E = 210, al = 12 | Formula: sigma = E alpha (dT) | Substitute: sigma = 210000 * 12e-6 * 100 | Answer: 252 MPa

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1250 mm and wall thickness 15 mm carries an internal pressure of 2.7 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1250, t = 15, P = 2.7 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 2.7*1250 / (2*15) | Answer: 112.5 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 720 K and 300 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 720, Tc = 300 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 300/720) * 100 | Answer: 58.33 %

question: A refrigerator works between 255 K (cold) and 304 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 255, Th = 304 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 255 / (304 - 255) | Answer: 5.204

question: A heat pump operates between 261 K and 320 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 261, Th = 320 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 320 / (320 - 261) | Answer: 5.424

question: 7.6 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 45 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 7.6, dT = 45 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 7.6 * 0.718 * 45 | Answer: 245.6 kJ

question: 4 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 30 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4, dT = 30 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 4 * 1.005 * 30 | Answer: 120.6 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 1.7 m^3 at 320 K with mass 3.4 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 1.7, Tk = 320, m = 3.4 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 3.4*0.287*320 / 1.7 | Answer: 183.7 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 4.3 kg of air expands isothermally at 310 K from volume V1 to 2*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.3, Tk = 310, ratio = 2 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 4.3*0.287*310*ln(2) | Answer: 265.2 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 3.8 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.29 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 3.8, D = 0.29 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*3.8*0.29 / 0.001 | Answer: 1102000

question: Water flows at 0.6 m/s through a pipe of diameter 190 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 2.2 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 2.2 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*2.2 / 1000 | Answer: 21.58 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 7.4 m. Taking Cv = 0.95, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 7.4, cv = 0.95 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.95*sqrt(2*9.81*7.4) | Answer: 11.45 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 380 mm) water flows at 2.7 m/s. It contracts to diameter 140 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
Water flows at 3 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.25 m and length 150 m. With friction factor f = 0.031, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 25 teeth drives a gear of 89 teeth. If the pinion runs at 650 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 25, z2 = 89, N1 = 650 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 650*25 / 89 | Answer: 182.6 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 170 mm rotates at 950 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 170, N = 950 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.17)*950 / 60 | Answer: 8.456 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 15.3 kW at 700 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 15.3, N = 700 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(15.3*1000) / (2*pi*700) | Answer: 208.7 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 0.5 kg rotates at radius 0.43 m at 700 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 1000 N/m and mass 6.3 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 1000, m = 6.3 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(1000/6.3) | Answer: 2.005 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 2.2 m^2 and thickness 0.28 m has conductivity k = 13.4 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 145 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 2.2, L = 0.28, k = 13.4, dT = 145 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 13.4*2.2*145 / 0.28 | Answer: 15266 W

question: A surface of area 2.7 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 30 W/m^2-K to surroundings 70 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 2.7, h = 30, dT = 70 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 30*2.7*70 | Answer: 5670 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 250 m/min, feed = 0.15 mm/rev, depth of cut = 0.9 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 250, f = 0.15, d = 0.9 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*250*0.15*0.9 | Answer: 33750 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 250 mm is turned at 550 rpm with a feed of 0.23 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 250, N = 550, f = 0.23 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 250 / (0.23*550) | Answer: 1.976 min

question: A resistor of 180 ohm carries a current of 7 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 180, I = 7 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 7 * 180 | Answer: 1260 V

question: Three resistors 85 ohm, 99 ohm and 33 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 85, R2 = 99, R3 = 33 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 85 + 99 + 33 | Answer: 217 ohm

question: Two resistors 50 ohm and 40 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 50, R2 = 40 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 50*40 / (50+40) | Answer: 22.22 ohm

question: A device draws 7.8 A at 165 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 165, I = 7.8 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 165 * 7.8 | Answer: 1287 W

question: A current of 7.2 A flows through a 94 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 7.2, R = 94 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (7.2)^2 * 94 | Answer: 4873 W

question: Two capacitors 8 uF and 1.1 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 8, C2 = 1.1 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 8*1.1 / (8+1.1) | Answer: 0.967 uF

question: A resistor 51 kohm and capacitor 19.8 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 51, C = 19.8 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (51k)(19.8u) = 101 ms | Answer: 101 ms

question: An inductor 369.9 mH is in series with 60 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 369.9, R = 60 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (369.9e-3) / 60 | Answer: 6.165 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 184.1 mH inductor at 800 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 184.1, f = 800 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (800)(184.1e-3) | Answer: 925.4 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 3.7 uF capacitor at 350 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 3.7, f = 350 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (350)(3.7e-6)) | Answer: 122.9 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 8 ohm, XL = 65 ohm and XC = 48 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 8, XL = 65, XC = 48 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(8^2 + (65 - 48)^2) | Answer: 18.79 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 41 mH and C = 0.5 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 41, C = 0.5 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(41e-3 * 0.5e-6)) | Answer: 1112 Hz

question: A capacitor of 46.7 uF is charged to 155 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 46.7, V = 155 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*46.7e-6*(155)^2 | Answer: 561 mJ

question: An alternating voltage has a peak value of 254 V. Find its RMS value.
solution: Given: Vp = 254 | Formula: Vrms = Vp / sqrt(2) | Substitute: Vrms = 254 / sqrt(2) | Answer: 179.6 V

question: A transformer has primary voltage 430 V with 920 primary turns and 210 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 430, N1 = 920, N2 = 210 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 430 * 210/920 | Answer: 98.15 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 130 V and draws an armature current of 5 A. If the armature resistance is 0.83 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 130, Ia = 5, Ra = 0.83 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 130 - 5*0.83 | Answer: 125.8 V

question: A 6-pole induction motor on a 50 Hz supply runs at 710 rpm. Find the slip (%).
formula: s = (Ns - N) / Ns,  Ns = 120 f / P

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 175 A at 433 V (line) with a power factor of 0.83. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 175, VL = 433, pf = 0.83 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*433*175*0.83 / 1000 | Answer: 108.9 kW

question: A load has real power 90 kW and apparent power 135 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 90, S = 135 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 90 / 135 | Answer: 0.6667

question: A machine delivers 40 kW output while drawing 67 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 40, Pi = 67 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 40/67 * 100 | Answer: 59.7 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 18 V across R1 = 13 ohm and R2 = 36 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 18, R1 = 13, R2 = 36 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 18*36 / (13+36) | Answer: 13.22 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 160 kohm and Rin = 39 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 160, Rin = 39 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 160 / 39 | Answer: 4.103

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 10 kohm and Rg = 38 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 10, Rg = 38 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 10/38 | Answer: 1.263

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 8494. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 8494 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(8494) | Answer: 39.29 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.6 m carries a central point load of 55 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 9.6, W = 55 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 55*9.6 / 4 | Answer: 132 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.4 m carries a UDL of 15 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 9.4, w = 15 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 15*(9.4)^2 / 8 | Answer: 165.7 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 3.5 m carries a point load 50 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.5, W = 50 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 50*3.5 | Answer: 175 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 1.1 m carries a UDL of 38 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 1.1, w = 38 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 38*(1.1)^2 / 2 | Answer: 22.99 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.6 m carries a point load 75 kN at distance 2.4 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 4.6, a = 2.4, W = 75 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 75*(4.6 - 2.4) / 4.6 | Answer: 35.87 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 3.6 m) carries a central point load 80 kN. With E = 200 GPa and I = 280e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=80000 N, L=3600.0 mm, E=200000 MPa, I=280e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 1.389 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 7.5 m carries a UDL of 24 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7.5, w = 24 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 24*(7.5)^2 / 12 | Answer: 112.5 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 420 mm, clear cover 35 mm and main bars of diameter 12 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 420, c = 35, dia = 12 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 420 - 35 - 12/2 | Answer: 379 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 12.6 m^2 carrying a factored load of 11.7 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 12.6, w = 11.7 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 11.7 * 12.6 | Answer: 147.4 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 6.4 m, unit weight 16 kN/m^3, phi = 29 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 4.7 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 20 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 4.7, g = 20 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (20 - 9.81)*4.7 | Answer: 47.89 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 5.5e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.5, area = 4.1e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 5.5, i = 0.5, A = 4.1 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (5.5e-4)*0.5*(4.1e-3) | Answer: 1128 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 2.5 m, bed slope 0.005 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.019. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 1.4 m under a head of 0.3 m. Taking Cd = 0.64 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 3.1 m wide carries a discharge of 28.5 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 100 m and design speed 90 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 100, V = 90 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (90)^2 / (127*100) | Answer: 0.6378
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: For a design speed of 80 km/h with allowable superelevation 0.08 and lateral friction 0.14, find the minimum curve radius in m.
A tank of volume 630 m^3 treats a flow of 10 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
