solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 314 and 370 | Answer: GCD = 2

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 14 and 35.
solution: Given: a = 14, b = 35 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 14*35 / 7 | Answer: 70
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 28 mm carries an axial tensile load of 12 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 36 mm and length 700 mm carries an axial load of 73 kN. Take E = 110 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 76 mm transmits a torque of 1600 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 76, Tt = 1600 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(1600*1000) / (pi*(76)^3) | Answer: 18.56 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 26 mm and length 1900 mm carries a torque of 1400 N-m. With G = 77 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (26)^4 / 32 = 44864 mm^4 | theta = (1400*1000)(1900) / (77000 * 44864) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 44.12 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 90 mm wide and 270 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 90, h = 270 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 90*(270)^2 / 6 | Answer: 1093500 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (103 mm x 230 mm) carries a bending moment of 15 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (80 mm x 100 mm) has effective length 1500 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 680 MPa is designed for a working stress of 60 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 680, sw = 60 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 680 / 60 | Answer: 11.33

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 300 mm and wall thickness 20 mm carries an internal pressure of 0.9 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 300, t = 20, P = 0.9 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 0.9*300 / (2*20) | Answer: 6.75 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 600 K and 300 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 600, Tc = 300 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 300/600) * 100 | Answer: 50 %

question: A refrigerator works between 265 K (cold) and 308 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 265, Th = 308 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 265 / (308 - 265) | Answer: 6.163

question: A heat pump operates between 264 K and 300 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 264, Th = 300 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 300 / (300 - 264) | Answer: 8.333

question: 3.6 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 85 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.6, dT = 85 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 3.6 * 0.718 * 85 | Answer: 219.7 kJ

question: 1 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 45 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1, dT = 45 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 1 * 1.005 * 45 | Answer: 45.22 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 3 m^3 at 410 K with mass 1.9 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 3, Tk = 410, m = 1.9 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 1.9*0.287*410 / 3 | Answer: 74.52 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 1.1 kg of air expands isothermally at 300 K from volume V1 to 4*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1.1, Tk = 300, ratio = 4 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 1.1*0.287*300*ln(4) | Answer: 131.3 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 3.8 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.27 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 3.8, D = 0.27 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*3.8*0.27 / 0.001 | Answer: 1026000

question: Water flows at 3.5 m/s through a pipe of diameter 80 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 10.8 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 10.8 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*10.8 / 1000 | Answer: 105.9 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 19.6 m. Taking Cv = 0.96, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 19.6, cv = 0.96 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.96*sqrt(2*9.81*19.6) | Answer: 18.83 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 170 mm) water flows at 2.1 m/s. It contracts to diameter 50 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 170, d2 = 50, V1 = 2.1 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 2.1*(170/50)^2 | Answer: 24.28 m/s

question: Water flows at 3.4 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.41 m and length 210 m. With friction factor f = 0.028, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 22 teeth drives a gear of 72 teeth. If the pinion runs at 750 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 22, z2 = 72, N1 = 750 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 750*22 / 72 | Answer: 229.2 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 490 mm rotates at 800 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 490, N = 800 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.49)*800 / 60 | Answer: 20.53 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 42.3 kW at 350 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 42.3, N = 350 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(42.3*1000) / (2*pi*350) | Answer: 1154 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 6.1 kg rotates at radius 0.18 m at 250 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 18500 N/m and mass 8.8 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 18500, m = 8.8 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(18500/8.8) | Answer: 7.297 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 9.7 m^2 and thickness 0.14 m has conductivity k = 48.6 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 165 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 9.7, L = 0.14, k = 48.6, dT = 165 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 48.6*9.7*165 / 0.14 | Answer: 555602 W

question: A surface of area 0.7 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 125 W/m^2-K to surroundings 55 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 0.7, h = 125, dT = 55 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 125*0.7*55 | Answer: 4812 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 60 m/min, feed = 0.17 mm/rev, depth of cut = 1 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 60, f = 0.17, d = 1 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*60*0.17*1 | Answer: 10200 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 290 mm is turned at 950 rpm with a feed of 0.26 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 290, N = 950, f = 0.26 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 290 / (0.26*950) | Answer: 1.174 min

question: A resistor of 146 ohm carries a current of 9.7 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 146, I = 9.7 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 9.7 * 146 | Answer: 1416 V

question: Three resistors 37 ohm, 64 ohm and 35 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 37, R2 = 64, R3 = 35 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 37 + 64 + 35 | Answer: 136 ohm

question: Two resistors 29 ohm and 23 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 29, R2 = 23 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 29*23 / (29+23) | Answer: 12.83 ohm

question: A device draws 7.3 A at 30 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 30, I = 7.3 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 30 * 7.3 | Answer: 219 W

question: A current of 10.9 A flows through a 137 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 10.9, R = 137 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (10.9)^2 * 137 | Answer: 16277 W

question: Two capacitors 12.7 uF and 29.3 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 12.7, C2 = 29.3 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 12.7*29.3 / (12.7+29.3) | Answer: 8.86 uF

question: A resistor 53 kohm and capacitor 14.6 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 53, C = 14.6 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (53k)(14.6u) = 773.8 ms | Answer: 773.8 ms

question: An inductor 57.2 mH is in series with 189 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 57.2, R = 189 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (57.2e-3) / 189 | Answer: 0.3026 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 189.4 mH inductor at 240 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 189.4, f = 240 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (240)(189.4e-3) | Answer: 285.6 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 31.6 uF capacitor at 980 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 31.6, f = 980 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (980)(31.6e-6)) | Answer: 5.139 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 70 ohm, XL = 85 ohm and XC = 126 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 70, XL = 85, XC = 126 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(70^2 + (85 - 126)^2) | Answer: 81.12 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 24 mH and C = 1 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 24, C = 1 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(24e-3 * 1e-6)) | Answer: 1027 Hz

question: A capacitor of 50.9 uF is charged to 130 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 50.9, V = 130 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*50.9e-6*(130)^2 | Answer: 430.1 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 330 V with 630 primary turns and 20 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 330, N1 = 630, N2 = 20 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 330 * 20/630 | Answer: 10.48 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 430 V and draws an armature current of 41 A. If the armature resistance is 0.24 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 430, Ia = 41, Ra = 0.24 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 430 - 41*0.24 | Answer: 420.2 V

question: A 6-pole induction motor on a 60 Hz supply runs at 900 rpm. Find the slip (%).
formula: s = (Ns - N) / Ns,  Ns = 120 f / P

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 90 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.86. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 90, VL = 400, pf = 0.86 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*400*90*0.86 / 1000 | Answer: 53.62 kW

question: A load has real power 30 kW and apparent power 55 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 30, S = 55 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 30 / 55 | Answer: 0.5455

question: A machine delivers 10 kW output while drawing 42 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 10, Pi = 42 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 10/42 * 100 | Answer: 23.81 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 22 V across R1 = 17 ohm and R2 = 7 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 22, R1 = 17, R2 = 7 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 22*7 / (17+7) | Answer: 6.417 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 160 kohm and Rin = 35 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 160, Rin = 35 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 160 / 35 | Answer: 4.571

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 160 kohm and Rg = 41 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 160, Rg = 41 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 160/41 | Answer: 4.902

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 2389. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 2389 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(2389) | Answer: 33.78 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.4 m carries a central point load of 115 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6.4, W = 115 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 115*6.4 / 4 | Answer: 184 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.2 m carries a UDL of 55 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6.2, w = 55 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 55*(6.2)^2 / 8 | Answer: 264.3 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 2 m carries a point load 10 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 2, W = 10 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 10*2 | Answer: 20 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 5.2 m carries a UDL of 20 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.2, w = 20 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 20*(5.2)^2 / 2 | Answer: 270.4 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 7.2 m carries a point load 55 kN at distance 2.5 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 7.2, a = 2.5, W = 55 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 55*(7.2 - 2.5) / 7.2 | Answer: 35.9 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 5.6 m) carries a central point load 30 kN. With E = 30 GPa and I = 270e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=30000 N, L=5600.0 mm, E=30000 MPa, I=270e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 13.55 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 5 m carries a UDL of 42 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5, w = 42 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 42*(5)^2 / 12 | Answer: 87.5 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 590 mm, clear cover 30 mm and main bars of diameter 20 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 590, c = 30, dia = 20 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 590 - 30 - 20/2 | Answer: 550 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 31.8 m^2 carrying a factored load of 10 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 31.8, w = 10 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 10 * 31.8 | Answer: 318 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 4.7 m, unit weight 17 kN/m^3, phi = 28 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 2 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 19 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 2, g = 19 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (19 - 9.81)*2 | Answer: 18.38 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 1.2e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.7, area = 2.4e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 1.2, i = 0.7, A = 2.4 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (1.2e-4)*0.7*(2.4e-3) | Answer: 201.6 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 0.6 m, bed slope 0.004 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.019. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 1.7 m under a head of 0.4 m. Taking Cd = 0.64 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 2 m wide carries a discharge of 6.6 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 180 m and design speed 65 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 180, V = 65 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (65)^2 / (127*180) | Answer: 0.1848
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: For a design speed of 70 km/h with allowable superelevation 0.06 and lateral friction 0.12, find the minimum curve radius in m.
A tank of volume 880 m^3 treats a flow of 155 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 880, Q = 155 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 880 / 155 | Answer: 5.677 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 320 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.26 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 3 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 320, k = 0.26, t = 3 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 320*(1 - e^(-0.26*3)) | Answer: 173.3 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.81, rainfall intensity 30 mm/h over a catchment of 53.7 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.81, i = 30, A = 53.7 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.81*30*53.7 / 360 | Answer: 3.625 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.08 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 580 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.08, M = 580 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 580*(30+0.08)/30 | Answer: 581.5 m

question: Convert the decimal number 106 to binary.
solution: Divide 106 by 2 repeatedly, recording remainders | Reading remainders in reverse gives 1101010 | Answer: 1101010 (binary)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 2 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the decimal number 561 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 561 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 231 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the 8-bit binary number 01111011 to decimal.
solution: Binary 01111011 = sum of bit-weights | Answer: 123 (decimal)
formula: Sum each bit times its positional weight (2^i)

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 00100101 and 10000100.
solution: XOR: 10100001 | Count of 1s = 3 | Answer: 3
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 270 megabits is sent over a link of 53 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 270, B = 53 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 270 / 53 | Answer: 5.094 s

question: A link has bandwidth 65 Mbps and round-trip time 80 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 65, R = 80 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 65e6 * 80e-3 bits = 5200 kb | Answer: 5200 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.88, cache access time 4 ns and main-memory access time 190 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.88, tc = 4, tm = 190 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.88*4 + (1 - 0.88)*190 | Answer: 26.32 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 72966 elements?
solution: Given: n = 72966 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(72966)) + 1 | Answer: 17

question: An O(n^2) algorithm performs c*n^2 basic operations. If c = 1 and n = 350, how many operations are performed?
solution: Given: n = 350 | Formula: operations = n^2 | Substitute: = (350)^2 | Answer: 122500

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.016, memory access time 110 ns and page-fault service time 3 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 3 ms = 3000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.016)*110 + 0.016*3000000.0 ns | Answer: 48.11 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 1 m^3 at 430 kPa and 410 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 1, P = 430, Tk = 410 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (430e3)*1 / (8.314*410) | Answer: 126.1 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.25 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 14 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.25, t = 14 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.25*14) | Answer: 0.9698

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.16 /min) is to reach 50% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.16, X = 50 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.5) / 0.16 | Answer: 4.332 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.46 /min) reaches 90% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.46, X = 90 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.9 / (0.46*(1 - 0.9)) | Answer: 19.57 min

question: For a reaction with A = 5e10 /s and activation energy 85 kJ/mol at 350 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 5, Ea = 85, Tk = 350 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 5e10 * exp(-85e3 / (8.314*350)) | Answer: 0.0103 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.98 and bottoms xW = 0.04, with relative volatility alpha = 2.5. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.98, xw = 0.04, al = 2.5 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.98/0.02)(0.96/0.04)] / ln(2.5) | Answer: 7.716 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.58 and x = 0.43. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.58, x = 0.43 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.58/0.42) / (0.43/0.57) | Answer: 1.831

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.11 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 90 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.11, Psat = 90 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.11 * 90 | Answer: 9.9 kPa

question: A stream of 2.4 kg/s with specific heat 2.2 kJ/kg-K is heated through 45 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 2.4, cp = 2.2, dT = 45 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 2.4*2.2*45 | Answer: 237.6 kW

question: A reactor of volume 15.9 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 4.6 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 15.9, Q = 4.6 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 15.9 / 4.6 | Answer: 3.457 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 1e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 2 mm with a concentration difference of 80 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 1, L = 2, dC = 80 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (1e-9)*80 / (2e-3) | Answer: 40 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 9.8 min and steady-state gain 0.7. For a step input of magnitude 19, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 9.8, K = 0.7, M = 19 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 0.7 * 19 | Answer: 13.3 units

question: A reactor operates at a space time of 7.4 min. Find its space velocity in per hour.
solution: Given: tau = 7.4 | Formula: SV = 60 / tau  (per hour) | Substitute: SV = 60 / 7.4 | Answer: 8.108 /h

question: An aircraft wing of area 60 m^2 flies at 120 m/s (air density 0.7 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 1.3. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 60, V = 120, rho = 0.7, CL = 1.3 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.7*(120)^2*60*1.3 / 1000 | Answer: 393.1 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 70 m^2 flies at 160 m/s (density 1 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.1. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 70, V = 160, rho = 1, CD = 0.1 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*1*(160)^2*70*0.1 / 1000 | Answer: 89.6 kN

question: A specimen under stress 400 MPa shows an elastic strain of 2.4e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 400, eps = 2.4 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 400 / (2.4e-3) MPa = 166.7 GPa | Answer: 166.7 GPa

question: A block of mass 32 kg has a volume of 3.9e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 32, V = 3.9 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 32 / (3.9e-3) | Answer: 8205 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 800 mm is heated through 30 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 17e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 800, dT = 30, al = 17 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 800*17e-6*30 | Answer: 0.408 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 145 ohm, R2 = 145 ohm and R3 = 350 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 145, R2 = 145, R3 = 350 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 145*350 / 145 | Answer: 350 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 120 ohm and gauge factor 2.2 experiences a strain of 1000e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 120, GF = 2.2, eps = 1000 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 120*2.2*1000e-6 | Answer: 264 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 10.27 when the true value is 10. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10.27, true = 10 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10.27 - 10| / 10 * 100 | Answer: 2.7 %

question: Annual demand is 8000 units, ordering cost 240 per order and holding cost 13 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 8000, S = 240, H = 13 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*8000*240 / 13) | Answer: 543.5 units

question: An asset costs 110000 with salvage value 12000 after 11 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 110000, Sv = 12000, n = 11 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (110000 - 12000) / 11 | Answer: 8909 per year

question: A product sells for 430 per unit with variable cost 10 per unit and fixed costs 105000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 430, V = 10, F = 105000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 105000 / (430 - 10) | Answer: 250 units

question: Find the present worth of 25000 received 2 years from now at an interest rate of 5% per year.
solution: Given: F = 25000, n = 2, i = 5 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 25000 / (1 + 0.05)^2 | Answer: 22676 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.94, 0.91 and 0.93 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.94, r2 = 0.91, r3 = 0.93 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.94*0.91*0.93 | Answer: 0.7955

question: A process produces 27 defective items in a batch of 2500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 27, N = 2500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 27/2500 * 1e6 | Answer: 10800 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = 2x^3 - 5x^2 + 6x - 4 evaluated at x = 0.
For f(x) = 5x^3 + 6x^2 + 5x + 6, find f''(x) at x = 1.
Evaluate the definite integral of (-4x^2 + 2x + 2) dx from x = -2 to x = 6.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = -4x^3/3 + 2x^2/2 + 2x | Evaluate F(6) - F(-2) | Answer: -250.7
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 3x^2 + 3x - 10 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[6, -3], [2, -5]].
solution: Given: a = 6, b = -3, c = 2, d = -5 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (6)(-5) - (-3)(2) | Answer: -24

question: Find the determinant of [[4, -3, 1], [-2, -4, -6], [0, 0, 5]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: -110

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[3, 1], [3, 2]].
solution: Trace tr = 5, Determinant = 3 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 4.303

question: Solve for x: 6x + 6y = -6 and 4x + 6y = -12.
solution: Determinant = 6*6 - 6*4 = 12 | x = (e d - b f) / det = 3 | Answer: x = 3
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 5, 82, 59, 24, 35.
solution: Sum = 205 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 41 | Answer: 41

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 11, 50, 44, 8, 42.
solution: Mean = 31 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 19.87

question: Find the slope of the line through (-2, 8) and (0, 9).
solution: Given: x1 = -2, y1 = 8, x2 = 0, y2 = 9 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (9 - 8) / (0 - -2) | Answer: 0.5

question: Find the distance between the points (9, 4) and (9, 9).
solution: Given: x1 = 9, y1 = 4, x2 = 9, y2 = 9 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((0)^2 + (5)^2) | Answer: 5 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (-3,5), (5,-3), (2,2).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 8 sq units

question: Evaluate the number of combinations C(20, 11).
solution: Given: n = 20, r = 11 | Formula: C(n, r) = n! / (r! (n - r)!) | Substitute: C(20, 11) = 20! / (11! * 9!) | Answer: 167960

question: Find the 24th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -9 and common difference 7.
solution: Given: a = -9, d = 7, n = 24 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -9 + (24 - 1)*7 | Answer: 152

question: Find the sum of the first 21 terms of an AP with first term 2 and common difference 8.
solution: Given: a = 2, d = 8, n = 21 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 21/2 [2*2 + (21-1)*8] | Answer: 1722

question: Find the 8th term of a geometric progression with first term 9 and common ratio 2.
solution: Given: a = 9, r = 2, n = 8 | Formula: a_n = a r^(n-1) | Substitute: a_n = 9 * 2^(8-1) | Answer: 1152

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 1500 at 11% per annum for 6 years.
solution: Given: P = 1500, R = 11, Tt = 6 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 1500 * 11 * 6 / 100 | Answer: 990 currency units

question: Find the amount when 21000 is invested at 10.6% per annum compounded annually for 6 years.
solution: Given: P = 21000, R = 10.6, Tt = 6 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 21000 * (1 + 10.6/100)^6 | Answer: 38437 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (-4, -4, -3) and (-1, 2, -6).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (-1, 0, 3) and (-1, 0, -6).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 9

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (4, -2, -3) and (-5, 6, 5).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 160.2 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number 7 + 0i.
solution: Given: a = 7, b = 0 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((7)^2 + (0)^2) | Answer: 7

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number 3 + -2i.
solution: Given: a = 3, b = -2 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(-2, 3) | Answer: -33.69 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -x^3 - x^2 - 7x + 6 at x = -2.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-20 with initial guess x0=13, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.3 and ordinates 1, 10, 8, 13, 3, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 269 and 250.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 269 and 250 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 66 and 50.
solution: Given: a = 66, b = 50 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 66*50 / 2 | Answer: 1650
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 55 mm carries an axial tensile load of 58 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 18 mm and length 2200 mm carries an axial load of 50 kN. Take E = 200 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 69 mm transmits a torque of 1650 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 69, Tt = 1650 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(1650*1000) / (pi*(69)^3) | Answer: 25.58 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 58 mm and length 1100 mm carries a torque of 1450 N-m. With G = 80 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (58)^4 / 32 = 1110994 mm^4 | theta = (1450*1000)(1100) / (80000 * 1110994) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 1.028 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 37 mm wide and 130 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 37, h = 130 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 37*(130)^2 / 6 | Answer: 104217 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (105 mm x 220 mm) carries a bending moment of 14 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (80 mm x 130 mm) has effective length 3600 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 580 MPa is designed for a working stress of 200 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 580, sw = 200 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 580 / 200 | Answer: 2.9

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1300 mm and wall thickness 6 mm carries an internal pressure of 0.7 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1300, t = 6, P = 0.7 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 0.7*1300 / (2*6) | Answer: 75.83 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 920 K and 430 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 920, Tc = 430 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 430/920) * 100 | Answer: 53.26 %

question: A refrigerator works between 266 K (cold) and 304 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 266, Th = 304 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 266 / (304 - 266) | Answer: 7

question: A heat pump operates between 279 K and 322 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 279, Th = 322 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 322 / (322 - 279) | Answer: 7.488

question: 3.9 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 125 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.9, dT = 125 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 3.9 * 0.718 * 125 | Answer: 350 kJ

question: 4.6 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 35 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.6, dT = 35 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 4.6 * 1.005 * 35 | Answer: 161.8 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 1.1 m^3 at 510 K with mass 3.7 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 1.1, Tk = 510, m = 3.7 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 3.7*0.287*510 / 1.1 | Answer: 492.3 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 2.2 kg of air expands isothermally at 340 K from volume V1 to 5*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.2, Tk = 340, ratio = 5 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 2.2*0.287*340*ln(5) | Answer: 345.5 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 3.9 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.32 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 3.9, D = 0.32 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*3.9*0.32 / 0.001 | Answer: 1248000

question: Water flows at 0.6 m/s through a pipe of diameter 60 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 12 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 12 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*12 / 1000 | Answer: 117.7 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 11.1 m. Taking Cv = 0.97, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 11.1, cv = 0.97 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.97*sqrt(2*9.81*11.1) | Answer: 14.31 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 160 mm) water flows at 2.2 m/s. It contracts to diameter 110 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
Water flows at 3 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.15 m and length 330 m. With friction factor f = 0.021, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 20 teeth drives a gear of 60 teeth. If the pinion runs at 550 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 20, z2 = 60, N1 = 550 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 550*20 / 60 | Answer: 183.3 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 260 mm rotates at 250 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 260, N = 250 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.26)*250 / 60 | Answer: 3.403 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 33.2 kW at 900 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 33.2, N = 900 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(33.2*1000) / (2*pi*900) | Answer: 352.3 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 1.3 kg rotates at radius 0.43 m at 1050 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 3400 N/m and mass 2.6 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 3400, m = 2.6 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(3400/2.6) | Answer: 5.755 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 2.6 m^2 and thickness 0.35 m has conductivity k = 28.5 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 190 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 2.6, L = 0.35, k = 28.5, dT = 190 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 28.5*2.6*190 / 0.35 | Answer: 40226 W

question: A surface of area 0.8 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 85 W/m^2-K to surroundings 95 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 0.8, h = 85, dT = 95 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 85*0.8*95 | Answer: 6460 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 210 m/min, feed = 0.44 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2.7 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 210, f = 0.44, d = 2.7 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*210*0.44*2.7 | Answer: 249480 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 100 mm is turned at 500 rpm with a feed of 0.32 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 100, N = 500, f = 0.32 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 100 / (0.32*500) | Answer: 0.625 min

question: A resistor of 164 ohm carries a current of 5.6 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 164, I = 5.6 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 5.6 * 164 | Answer: 918.4 V

question: Three resistors 72 ohm, 85 ohm and 44 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 72, R2 = 85, R3 = 44 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 72 + 85 + 44 | Answer: 201 ohm

question: Two resistors 36 ohm and 19 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 36, R2 = 19 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 36*19 / (36+19) | Answer: 12.44 ohm

question: A device draws 7.2 A at 100 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 100, I = 7.2 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 100 * 7.2 | Answer: 720 W

question: A current of 2.5 A flows through a 79 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 2.5, R = 79 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (2.5)^2 * 79 | Answer: 493.8 W

question: Two capacitors 36.8 uF and 8.3 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 36.8, C2 = 8.3 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 36.8*8.3 / (36.8+8.3) | Answer: 6.773 uF

question: A resistor 83 kohm and capacitor 13.9 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 83, C = 13.9 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (83k)(13.9u) = 1154 ms | Answer: 1154 ms

question: An inductor 161.6 mH is in series with 166 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 161.6, R = 166 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (161.6e-3) / 166 | Answer: 0.9735 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 51.5 mH inductor at 880 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 51.5, f = 880 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (880)(51.5e-3) | Answer: 284.8 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 28.2 uF capacitor at 200 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 28.2, f = 200 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (200)(28.2e-6)) | Answer: 28.22 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 58 ohm, XL = 42 ohm and XC = 119 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 58, XL = 42, XC = 119 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(58^2 + (42 - 119)^2) | Answer: 96.4 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 13.7 mH and C = 8.6 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 13.7, C = 8.6 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(13.7e-3 * 8.6e-6)) | Answer: 463.7 Hz

question: A capacitor of 35.5 uF is charged to 100 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 35.5, V = 100 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*35.5e-6*(100)^2 | Answer: 177.5 mJ

question: An alternating voltage has a peak value of 230 V. Find its RMS value.
solution: Given: Vp = 230 | Formula: Vrms = Vp / sqrt(2) | Substitute: Vrms = 230 / sqrt(2) | Answer: 162.6 V

question: A transformer has primary voltage 160 V with 490 primary turns and 180 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 160, N1 = 490, N2 = 180 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 160 * 180/490 | Answer: 58.78 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 310 V and draws an armature current of 19 A. If the armature resistance is 0.74 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 310, Ia = 19, Ra = 0.74 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 310 - 19*0.74 | Answer: 295.9 V

question: A 4-pole induction motor on a 50 Hz supply runs at 960 rpm. Find the slip (%).
formula: s = (Ns - N) / Ns,  Ns = 120 f / P

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 15 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.96. Find the total real power in kW.

question: A load has real power 70 kW and apparent power 125 kVA. Find the power factor.

question: A machine delivers 120 kW output while drawing 162 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 19 V across R1 = 29 ohm and R2 = 34 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 30 kohm and Rin = 35 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 170 kohm and Rg = 34 kohm. Find the voltage gain.

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 5516. Express the gain in decibels (power).

question: A simply supported beam of span 8.4 m carries a central point load of 80 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 8.4, W = 80 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 80*8.4 / 4 | Answer: 168 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 8 m carries a UDL of 45 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 8, w = 45 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 45*(8)^2 / 8 | Answer: 360 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 4.9 m carries a point load 40 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.9, W = 40 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 40*4.9 | Answer: 196 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 2.6 m carries a UDL of 40 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 2.6, w = 40 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 40*(2.6)^2 / 2 | Answer: 135.2 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.1 m carries a point load 15 kN at distance 2.4 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.

question: A simply supported beam (span 7.6 m) carries a central point load 10 kN. With E = 30 GPa and I = 320e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.

question: A fixed beam of span 4.3 m carries a UDL of 36 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.3, w = 36 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 36*(4.3)^2 / 12 | Answer: 55.47 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 680 mm, clear cover 50 mm and main bars of diameter 25 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 680, c = 50, dia = 25 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 680 - 50 - 25/2 | Answer: 617.5 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 26.1 m^2 carrying a factored load of 11.2 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.

question: At a depth of 8.8 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 19 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 8.8, g = 19 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (19 - 9.81)*8.8 | Answer: 80.87 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 2.6e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.8, area = 3.5e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 2.6, i = 0.8, A = 3.5 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (2.6e-4)*0.8*(3.5e-3) | Answer: 728 mm^3/s

question: For a design speed of 95 km/h with allowable superelevation 0.08 and lateral friction 0.13, find the minimum curve radius in m.

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 340 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.16 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 7 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 340, k = 0.16, t = 7 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 340*(1 - e^(-0.16*7)) | Answer: 229.1 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.81, rainfall intensity 60 mm/h over a catchment of 35.3 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.81, i = 60, A = 35.3 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.81*60*35.3 / 360 | Answer: 4.765 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.06, M = 440 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 440*(20+0.06)/20 | Answer: 441.3 m

question: A file of 270 megabits is sent over a link of 93 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.

question: A link has bandwidth 77 Mbps and round-trip time 120 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.88, cache access time 3 ns and main-memory access time 160 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.88, tc = 3, tm = 160 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.88*3 + (1 - 0.88)*160 | Answer: 21.84 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 871621 elements?
solution: Given: n = 871621 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(871621)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.007, memory access time 170 ns and page-fault service time 6 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 6 ms = 6000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.007)*170 + 0.007*6000000.0 ns | Answer: 42.17 microseconds

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 1.5 m^3 at 130 kPa and 580 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 1.5, P = 130, Tk = 580 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (130e3)*1.5 / (8.314*580) | Answer: 40.44 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.37 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 19 minutes.

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.32 /min) is to reach 65% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.32, X = 65 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.65) / 0.32 | Answer: 3.281 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.15 /min) reaches 55% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.15, X = 55 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.55 / (0.15*(1 - 0.55)) | Answer: 8.148 min

question: For a reaction with A = 5e10 /s and activation energy 90 kJ/mol at 440 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.96 and bottoms xW = 0.1, with relative volatility alpha = 1.9. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.89 and x = 0.46. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.63 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 115 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.

question: A stream of 1.4 kg/s with specific heat 4 kJ/kg-K is heated through 35 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.

question: A reactor of volume 18.6 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 0.7 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 1.4e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 5 mm with a concentration difference of 40 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.

question: A first-order process has time constant 8.1 min and steady-state gain 3.1. For a step input of magnitude 6, find the final (steady-state) change in output.

question: An aircraft wing of area 85 m^2 flies at 220 m/s (air density 0.4 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.4. Find the lift force in kN.

question: An aircraft of wing area 120 m^2 flies at 240 m/s (density 0.7 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.12. Find the drag force in kN.

question: An aircraft flies at 160 m/s where the speed of sound is 340 m/s. Find the Mach number.

question: A specimen under stress 310 MPa shows an elastic strain of 1.7e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.

question: A block of mass 7 kg has a volume of 3.5e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.

question: A rod of length 800 mm is heated through 45 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 17e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 115 ohm, R2 = 100 ohm and R3 = 125 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).

question: A strain gauge of resistance 350 ohm and gauge factor 2.2 experiences a strain of 1500e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.

question: A measurement reads 9.63 when the true value is 50. Find the percentage error.

question: Annual demand is 9000 units, ordering cost 100 per order and holding cost 31 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).

question: An asset costs 80000 with salvage value 34000 after 19 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.

question: A product sells for 200 per unit with variable cost 130 per unit and fixed costs 10000. Find the break-even quantity in units.

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.91, 0.93 and 0.96 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.

question: A process produces 42 defective items in a batch of 8500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).

question: Evaluate the number of combinations C(13, 10).

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 19500 at 11.6% per annum for 5 years.

question: Find the amount when 38000 is invested at 10.9% per annum compounded annually for 5 years.

solution: Given: su = 580, sw = 240 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 580 / 240 | Answer: 2.417

question: A steel bar is fully restrained and heated through 85 deg C. With E = 200 GPa and alpha = 11e-6 /deg C, find the thermal stress in MPa.
solution: Given: dT = 85, E = 200, al = 11 | Formula: sigma = E alpha (dT) | Substitute: sigma = 200000 * 11e-6 * 85 | Answer: 187 MPa

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 900 mm and wall thickness 12 mm carries an internal pressure of 2.9 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 900, t = 12, P = 2.9 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 2.9*900 / (2*12) | Answer: 108.8 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 1020 K and 410 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 1020, Tc = 410 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 410/1020) * 100 | Answer: 59.8 %

question: A refrigerator works between 263 K (cold) and 324 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 263, Th = 324 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 263 / (324 - 263) | Answer: 4.311

question: A heat pump operates between 283 K and 328 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 283, Th = 328 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 328 / (328 - 283) | Answer: 7.289

question: 3.6 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 60 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.6, dT = 60 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 3.6 * 0.718 * 60 | Answer: 155.1 kJ

question: 5.6 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 80 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 5.6, dT = 80 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 5.6 * 1.005 * 80 | Answer: 450.2 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 2.2 m^3 at 310 K with mass 4.1 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 2.2, Tk = 310, m = 4.1 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 4.1*0.287*310 / 2.2 | Answer: 165.8 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 1.5 kg of air expands isothermally at 470 K from volume V1 to 3*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1.5, Tk = 470, ratio = 3 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 1.5*0.287*470*ln(3) | Answer: 222.3 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 1.6 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.08 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 1.6, D = 0.08 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*1.6*0.08 / 0.001 | Answer: 128000

question: Water flows at 1.2 m/s through a pipe of diameter 250 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 8.8 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 8.8 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*8.8 / 1000 | Answer: 86.33 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 17.3 m. Taking Cv = 0.98, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 17.3, cv = 0.98 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.98*sqrt(2*9.81*17.3) | Answer: 18.06 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 310 mm) water flows at 2.8 m/s. It contracts to diameter 70 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 310, d2 = 70, V1 = 2.8 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 2.8*(310/70)^2 | Answer: 54.91 m/s

question: Water flows at 1 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.41 m and length 450 m. With friction factor f = 0.024, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 34 teeth drives a gear of 78 teeth. If the pinion runs at 600 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 34, z2 = 78, N1 = 600 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 600*34 / 78 | Answer: 261.5 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 130 mm rotates at 1000 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 130, N = 1000 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.13)*1000 / 60 | Answer: 6.807 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 11.6 kW at 600 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 11.6, N = 600 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(11.6*1000) / (2*pi*600) | Answer: 184.6 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 6.9 kg rotates at radius 0.37 m at 500 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 10500 N/m and mass 2.6 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 10500, m = 2.6 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(10500/2.6) | Answer: 10.11 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 3.8 m^2 and thickness 0.22 m has conductivity k = 4.3 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 80 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 3.8, L = 0.22, k = 4.3, dT = 80 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 4.3*3.8*80 / 0.22 | Answer: 5942 W

question: A surface of area 4.6 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 155 W/m^2-K to surroundings 60 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 4.6, h = 155, dT = 60 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 155*4.6*60 | Answer: 42780 W

question: In a counter-flow heat exchanger the terminal temperature differences are 120 deg C and 30 deg C. Find the log mean temperature difference (LMTD) in deg C.
solution: Given: dT1 = 120, dT2 = 30 | Formula: LMTD = (dT1 - dT2) / ln(dT1/dT2) | Substitute: LMTD = (120 - 30) / ln(120/30) | Answer: 64.92 deg C

question: In turning, cutting speed = 180 m/min, feed = 0.4 mm/rev, depth of cut = 1.7 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 180, f = 0.4, d = 1.7 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*180*0.4*1.7 | Answer: 122400 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 150 mm is turned at 600 rpm with a feed of 0.27 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 150, N = 600, f = 0.27 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 150 / (0.27*600) | Answer: 0.9259 min

question: A resistor of 26 ohm carries a current of 4.1 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 26, I = 4.1 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 4.1 * 26 | Answer: 106.6 V

question: Three resistors 59 ohm, 83 ohm and 20 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 59, R2 = 83, R3 = 20 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 59 + 83 + 20 | Answer: 162 ohm

question: Two resistors 58 ohm and 116 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 58, R2 = 116 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 58*116 / (58+116) | Answer: 38.67 ohm

question: A device draws 0.2 A at 95 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 95, I = 0.2 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 95 * 0.2 | Answer: 19 W

question: A current of 1.2 A flows through a 19 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 1.2, R = 19 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (1.2)^2 * 19 | Answer: 27.36 W

question: Two capacitors 28.8 uF and 5.2 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 28.8, C2 = 5.2 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 28.8*5.2 / (28.8+5.2) | Answer: 4.405 uF

question: A resistor 36 kohm and capacitor 13.4 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 36, C = 13.4 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (36k)(13.4u) = 482.4 ms | Answer: 482.4 ms

question: An inductor 275.4 mH is in series with 79 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 275.4, R = 79 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (275.4e-3) / 79 | Answer: 3.486 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 17.2 mH inductor at 220 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 17.2, f = 220 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (220)(17.2e-3) | Answer: 23.78 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 2 uF capacitor at 340 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 2, f = 340 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (340)(2e-6)) | Answer: 234.1 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 27 ohm, XL = 69 ohm and XC = 94 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 27, XL = 69, XC = 94 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(27^2 + (69 - 94)^2) | Answer: 36.8 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 24.3 mH and C = 6.9 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 24.3, C = 6.9 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(24.3e-3 * 6.9e-6)) | Answer: 388.7 Hz

question: A capacitor of 12.7 uF is charged to 375 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 12.7, V = 375 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*12.7e-6*(375)^2 | Answer: 893 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 120 V with 230 primary turns and 500 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 120, N1 = 230, N2 = 500 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 120 * 500/230 | Answer: 260.9 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 170 V and draws an armature current of 12 A. If the armature resistance is 0.51 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 170, Ia = 12, Ra = 0.51 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 170 - 12*0.51 | Answer: 163.9 V

question: A 4-pole induction motor on a 60 Hz supply runs at 950 rpm. Find the slip (%).
formula: s = (Ns - N) / Ns,  Ns = 120 f / P

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 60 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.93. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 60, VL = 400, pf = 0.93 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*400*60*0.93 / 1000 | Answer: 38.66 kW

question: A load has real power 175 kW and apparent power 205 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 175, S = 205 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 175 / 205 | Answer: 0.8537

question: A machine delivers 70 kW output while drawing 192 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 70, Pi = 192 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 70/192 * 100 | Answer: 36.46 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 30 V across R1 = 48 ohm and R2 = 37 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 30, R1 = 48, R2 = 37 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 30*37 / (48+37) | Answer: 13.06 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 20 kohm and Rin = 14 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 20, Rin = 14 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 20 / 14 | Answer: 1.429

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 70 kohm and Rg = 42 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 70, Rg = 42 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 70/42 | Answer: 2.667

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 8612. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 8612 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(8612) | Answer: 39.35 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 9 m carries a central point load of 80 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 9, W = 80 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 80*9 / 4 | Answer: 180 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 8.2 m carries a UDL of 5 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 8.2, w = 5 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 5*(8.2)^2 / 8 | Answer: 42.02 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 2.8 m carries a point load 15 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 2.8, W = 15 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 15*2.8 | Answer: 42 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 4.8 m carries a UDL of 30 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.8, w = 30 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 30*(4.8)^2 / 2 | Answer: 345.6 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.3 m carries a point load 95 kN at distance 2.1 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 9.3, a = 2.1, W = 95 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 95*(9.3 - 2.1) / 9.3 | Answer: 73.55 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 3.8 m) carries a central point load 30 kN. With E = 30 GPa and I = 400e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=30000 N, L=3800.0 mm, E=30000 MPa, I=400e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 2.858 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 6.8 m carries a UDL of 24 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6.8, w = 24 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 24*(6.8)^2 / 12 | Answer: 92.48 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 460 mm, clear cover 50 mm and main bars of diameter 20 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 460, c = 50, dia = 20 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 460 - 50 - 20/2 | Answer: 400 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 15.7 m^2 carrying a factored load of 8.5 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 15.7, w = 8.5 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 8.5 * 15.7 | Answer: 133.4 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 6.3 m, unit weight 16 kN/m^3, phi = 30 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 6.6 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 18 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 6.6, g = 18 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (18 - 9.81)*6.6 | Answer: 54.05 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 3.5e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.9, area = 5e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 3.5, i = 0.9, A = 5 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (3.5e-4)*0.9*(5e-3) | Answer: 1575 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.7 m, bed slope 0.007 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.023. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 3.8 m under a head of 0.2 m. Taking Cd = 0.62 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 2.3 m wide carries a discharge of 19.9 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 570 m and design speed 85 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 570, V = 85 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (85)^2 / (127*570) | Answer: 0.09981
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: For a design speed of 40 km/h with allowable superelevation 0.05 and lateral friction 0.12, find the minimum curve radius in m.
A tank of volume 160 m^3 treats a flow of 185 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 160, Q = 185 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 160 / 185 | Answer: 0.8649 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 200 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.34 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 4 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 200, k = 0.34, t = 4 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 200*(1 - e^(-0.34*4)) | Answer: 148.7 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.31, rainfall intensity 65 mm/h over a catchment of 38.3 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.31, i = 65, A = 38.3 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.31*65*38.3 / 360 | Answer: 2.144 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.06 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 540 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.06, M = 540 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 540*(20+0.06)/20 | Answer: 541.6 m

question: Convert the decimal number 122 to binary.
solution: Divide 122 by 2 repeatedly, recording remainders | Reading remainders in reverse gives 1111010 | Answer: 1111010 (binary)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 2 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the decimal number 2871 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 2871 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: B37 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the 8-bit binary number 10011010 to decimal.
solution: Binary 10011010 = sum of bit-weights | Answer: 154 (decimal)
formula: Sum each bit times its positional weight (2^i)

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 00111001 and 10011010.
solution: XOR: 10100011 | Count of 1s = 4 | Answer: 4
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 600 megabits is sent over a link of 52 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 600, B = 52 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 600 / 52 | Answer: 11.54 s

question: A link has bandwidth 13 Mbps and round-trip time 160 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 13, R = 160 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 13e6 * 160e-3 bits = 2080 kb | Answer: 2080 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.9, cache access time 3 ns and main-memory access time 150 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.9, tc = 3, tm = 150 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.9*3 + (1 - 0.9)*150 | Answer: 17.7 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 383409 elements?
solution: Given: n = 383409 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(383409)) + 1 | Answer: 19

question: An O(n^2) algorithm performs c*n^2 basic operations. If c = 1 and n = 2300, how many operations are performed?
solution: Given: n = 2300 | Formula: operations = n^2 | Substitute: = (2300)^2 | Answer: 5290000

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.009, memory access time 120 ns and page-fault service time 5 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 5 ms = 5000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.009)*120 + 0.009*5000000.0 ns | Answer: 45.12 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 1.2 m^3 at 450 kPa and 510 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 1.2, P = 450, Tk = 510 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (450e3)*1.2 / (8.314*510) | Answer: 127.4 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.26 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 11 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.26, t = 11 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.26*11) | Answer: 0.9427

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.43 /min) is to reach 60% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.43, X = 60 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.6) / 0.43 | Answer: 2.131 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.45 /min) reaches 70% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.45, X = 70 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.7 / (0.45*(1 - 0.7)) | Answer: 5.185 min

question: For a reaction with A = 5e10 /s and activation energy 55 kJ/mol at 450 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 5, Ea = 55, Tk = 450 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 5e10 * exp(-55e3 / (8.314*450)) | Answer: 2063 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.92 and bottoms xW = 0.08, with relative volatility alpha = 3.3. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.92, xw = 0.08, al = 3.3 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.92/0.08)(0.92/0.08)] / ln(3.3) | Answer: 4.091 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.58 and x = 0.39. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.58, x = 0.39 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.58/0.42) / (0.39/0.61) | Answer: 2.16

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.16 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 25 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.16, Psat = 25 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.16 * 25 | Answer: 4 kPa

question: A stream of 7.5 kg/s with specific heat 3.8 kJ/kg-K is heated through 15 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 7.5, cp = 3.8, dT = 15 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 7.5*3.8*15 | Answer: 427.5 kW

question: A reactor of volume 2.7 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 2 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 2.7, Q = 2 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 2.7 / 2 | Answer: 1.35 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 9e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 2 mm with a concentration difference of 40 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 9, L = 2, dC = 40 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (9e-9)*40 / (2e-3) | Answer: 180 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 2.7 min and steady-state gain 0.9. For a step input of magnitude 20, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 2.7, K = 0.9, M = 20 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 0.9 * 20 | Answer: 18 units

question: A reactor operates at a space time of 12 min. Find its space velocity in per hour.
solution: Given: tau = 12 | Formula: SV = 60 / tau  (per hour) | Substitute: SV = 60 / 12 | Answer: 5 /h

question: An aircraft wing of area 65 m^2 flies at 210 m/s (air density 0.7 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.7. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 65, V = 210, rho = 0.7, CL = 0.7 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.7*(210)^2*65*0.7 / 1000 | Answer: 702.3 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 40 m^2 flies at 260 m/s (density 0.7 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.03. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 40, V = 260, rho = 0.7, CD = 0.03 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.7*(260)^2*40*0.03 / 1000 | Answer: 28.39 kN

question: A specimen under stress 180 MPa shows an elastic strain of 1.7e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 180, eps = 1.7 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 180 / (1.7e-3) MPa = 105.9 GPa | Answer: 105.9 GPa

question: A block of mass 49 kg has a volume of 5.4e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 49, V = 5.4 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 49 / (5.4e-3) | Answer: 9074 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 800 mm is heated through 110 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 12e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 800, dT = 110, al = 12 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 800*12e-6*110 | Answer: 1.056 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 85 ohm, R2 = 140 ohm and R3 = 335 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 85, R2 = 140, R3 = 335 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 140*335 / 85 | Answer: 551.8 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 120 ohm and gauge factor 2 experiences a strain of 1100e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 120, GF = 2, eps = 1100 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 120*2*1100e-6 | Answer: 264 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 10.37 when the true value is 10. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10.37, true = 10 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10.37 - 10| / 10 * 100 | Answer: 3.7 %

question: Annual demand is 47000 units, ordering cost 120 per order and holding cost 38 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 47000, S = 120, H = 38 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*47000*120 / 38) | Answer: 544.8 units

question: An asset costs 420000 with salvage value 26000 after 6 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 420000, Sv = 26000, n = 6 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (420000 - 26000) / 6 | Answer: 65667 per year

question: A product sells for 330 per unit with variable cost 40 per unit and fixed costs 115000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 330, V = 40, F = 115000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 115000 / (330 - 40) | Answer: 396.6 units

question: Find the present worth of 70000 received 8 years from now at an interest rate of 5% per year.
solution: Given: F = 70000, n = 8, i = 5 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 70000 / (1 + 0.05)^8 | Answer: 47379 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.96, 0.93 and 0.93 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.96, r2 = 0.93, r3 = 0.93 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.96*0.93*0.93 | Answer: 0.8303

question: A process produces 37 defective items in a batch of 5500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 37, N = 5500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 37/5500 * 1e6 | Answer: 6727 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = 5x^3 + x^2 + 5x - 3 evaluated at x = 2.
For f(x) = -5x^3 + x^2 + 2x - 4, find f''(x) at x = 5.
Evaluate the definite integral of (4x^2 + x - 4) dx from x = -1 to x = 7.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = 4x^3/3 + 1x^2/2 + -4x | Evaluate F(7) - F(-1) | Answer: 450.7
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 2x^2 - 8x - 12 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[0, 9], [-5, 4]].
solution: Given: a = 0, b = 9, c = -5, d = 4 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (0)(4) - (9)(-5) | Answer: 45

question: Find the determinant of [[6, 2, 6], [1, -1, 3], [6, -3, -5]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: 148

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[-3, -1], [-5, 6]].
solution: Trace tr = 3, Determinant = -23 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 6.525

question: Solve for x: 2x + 2y = 4 and -2x + 3y = 10.
solution: Determinant = 2*3 - 2*-2 = 10 | x = (e d - b f) / det = -0.8 | Answer: x = -0.8
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 58, 84, 94, 10, 46.
solution: Sum = 292 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 58.4 | Answer: 58.4

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 22, 40, 32, 20, 21.
solution: Mean = 27 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 8.718

question: Find the slope of the line through (0, -5) and (3, 3).
solution: Given: x1 = 0, y1 = -5, x2 = 3, y2 = 3 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (3 - -5) / (3 - 0) | Answer: 2.667
