question: Find the distance between the points (3, 8) and (1, -3).
solution: Given: x1 = 3, y1 = 8, x2 = 1, y2 = -3 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-2)^2 + (-11)^2) | Answer: 11.18 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (7,-6), (-2,-4), (4,3).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 37.5 sq units

question: Evaluate the number of combinations C(14, 14).
solution: Given: n = 14, r = 14 | Formula: C(n, r) = n! / (r! (n - r)!) | Substitute: C(14, 14) = 14! / (14! * 0!) | Answer: 1

question: Find the 34th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 11 and common difference 1.
solution: Given: a = 11, d = 1, n = 34 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = 11 + (34 - 1)*1 | Answer: 44

question: Find the sum of the first 38 terms of an AP with first term -8 and common difference 1.
solution: Given: a = -8, d = 1, n = 38 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 38/2 [2*-8 + (38-1)*1] | Answer: 399

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 22000 at 12.8% per annum for 9 years.
solution: Given: P = 22000, R = 12.8, Tt = 9 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 22000 * 12.8 * 9 / 100 | Answer: 25344 currency units

question: Find the amount when 10500 is invested at 5% per annum compounded annually for 3 years.
solution: Given: P = 10500, R = 5, Tt = 3 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 10500 * (1 + 5/100)^3 | Answer: 12155 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (1, -4, 7) and (-3, -5, -2).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (-6, 1, -3) and (-6, 6, -4).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 33.65

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (-4, -6, 3) and (-4, 2, -1).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 88.4 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number -6 + 2i.
solution: Given: a = -6, b = 2 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((-6)^2 + (2)^2) | Answer: 6.325

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number -10 + 9i.
solution: Given: a = -10, b = 9 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(9, -10) | Answer: 138 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = 5x^3 + 7x^2 - 4x - 1 at x = 2.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-75 with initial guess x0=2, find x1 (one iteration).
solution: Given: N = 75, x0 = 2 | Formula: x1 = x0 - (x0^2 - N)/(2 x0) | Substitute: x1 = 2 - ((2)^2 - 75)/(2*2) | Answer: 19.75

question: Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.4 and ordinates 0, 5, 13, 19, 15, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 441 and 288.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 441 and 288 | Answer: GCD = 9

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 21 and 26.
solution: Given: a = 21, b = 26 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 21*26 / 1 | Answer: 546
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 27 mm carries an axial tensile load of 86 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 26 mm and length 1600 mm carries an axial load of 72 kN. Take E = 210 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 66 mm transmits a torque of 2900 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 66, Tt = 2900 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(2900*1000) / (pi*(66)^3) | Answer: 51.37 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 45 mm and length 1900 mm carries a torque of 1400 N-m. With G = 80 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (45)^4 / 32 = 402578 mm^4 | theta = (1400*1000)(1900) / (80000 * 402578) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 4.732 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 59 mm wide and 230 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 59, h = 230 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 59*(230)^2 / 6 | Answer: 520183 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (45 mm x 250 mm) carries a bending moment of 34 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (36 mm x 150 mm) has effective length 2500 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 680 MPa is designed for a working stress of 120 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 680, sw = 120 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 680 / 120 | Answer: 5.667

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1250 mm and wall thickness 13 mm carries an internal pressure of 1.8 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1250, t = 13, P = 1.8 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 1.8*1250 / (2*13) | Answer: 86.54 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 900 K and 300 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 900, Tc = 300 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 300/900) * 100 | Answer: 66.67 %

question: A refrigerator works between 268 K (cold) and 316 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 268, Th = 316 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 268 / (316 - 268) | Answer: 5.583

question: A heat pump operates between 282 K and 328 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 282, Th = 328 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 328 / (328 - 282) | Answer: 7.13

question: 1.4 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 70 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1.4, dT = 70 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 1.4 * 0.718 * 70 | Answer: 70.36 kJ

question: 3.8 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 50 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.8, dT = 50 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 3.8 * 1.005 * 50 | Answer: 190.9 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 3.5 m^3 at 390 K with mass 3.4 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 3.5, Tk = 390, m = 3.4 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 3.4*0.287*390 / 3.5 | Answer: 108.7 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 2.2 kg of air expands isothermally at 410 K from volume V1 to 2*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.2, Tk = 410, ratio = 2 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 2.2*0.287*410*ln(2) | Answer: 179.4 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 2.6 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.33 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 2.6, D = 0.33 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*2.6*0.33 / 0.001 | Answer: 858000

question: Water flows at 1 m/s through a pipe of diameter 120 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 24.4 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 24.4 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*24.4 / 1000 | Answer: 239.4 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 2.8 m. Taking Cv = 0.97, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 2.8, cv = 0.97 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.97*sqrt(2*9.81*2.8) | Answer: 7.19 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 290 mm) water flows at 0.6 m/s. It contracts to diameter 100 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
Water flows at 2.5 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.27 m and length 90 m. With friction factor f = 0.04, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 15 teeth drives a gear of 87 teeth. If the pinion runs at 500 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 15, z2 = 87, N1 = 500 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 500*15 / 87 | Answer: 86.21 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 250 mm rotates at 1400 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 250, N = 1400 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.25)*1400 / 60 | Answer: 18.33 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 4.9 kW at 350 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 4.9, N = 350 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(4.9*1000) / (2*pi*350) | Answer: 133.7 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 3.1 kg rotates at radius 0.56 m at 750 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 19500 N/m and mass 11.9 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 19500, m = 11.9 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(19500/11.9) | Answer: 6.443 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 3.5 m^2 and thickness 0.2 m has conductivity k = 21.2 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 160 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 3.5, L = 0.2, k = 21.2, dT = 160 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 21.2*3.5*160 / 0.2 | Answer: 59360 W

question: A surface of area 3.2 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 100 W/m^2-K to surroundings 110 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 3.2, h = 100, dT = 110 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 100*3.2*110 | Answer: 35200 W

question: In a counter-flow heat exchanger the terminal temperature differences are 40 deg C and 35 deg C. Find the log mean temperature difference (LMTD) in deg C.
solution: Given: dT1 = 40, dT2 = 35 | Formula: LMTD = (dT1 - dT2) / ln(dT1/dT2) | Substitute: LMTD = (40 - 35) / ln(40/35) | Answer: 37.44 deg C

question: In turning, cutting speed = 70 m/min, feed = 0.41 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2.1 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 70, f = 0.41, d = 2.1 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*70*0.41*2.1 | Answer: 60270 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 160 mm is turned at 600 rpm with a feed of 0.24 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 160, N = 600, f = 0.24 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 160 / (0.24*600) | Answer: 1.111 min

question: A resistor of 36 ohm carries a current of 6.3 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 36, I = 6.3 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 6.3 * 36 | Answer: 226.8 V

question: Three resistors 50 ohm, 62 ohm and 27 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 50, R2 = 62, R3 = 27 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 50 + 62 + 27 | Answer: 139 ohm

question: Two resistors 53 ohm and 43 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 53, R2 = 43 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 53*43 / (53+43) | Answer: 23.74 ohm

question: A device draws 3.4 A at 175 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 175, I = 3.4 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 175 * 3.4 | Answer: 595 W

question: A current of 4 A flows through a 95 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 4, R = 95 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (4)^2 * 95 | Answer: 1520 W

question: Two capacitors 13 uF and 30.9 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 13, C2 = 30.9 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 13*30.9 / (13+30.9) | Answer: 9.15 uF

question: A resistor 6 kohm and capacitor 6.3 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 6, C = 6.3 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (6k)(6.3u) = 37.8 ms | Answer: 37.8 ms

question: An inductor 456.3 mH is in series with 161 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 456.3, R = 161 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (456.3e-3) / 161 | Answer: 2.834 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 41.8 mH inductor at 570 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 41.8, f = 570 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (570)(41.8e-3) | Answer: 149.7 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 49.1 uF capacitor at 340 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 49.1, f = 340 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (340)(49.1e-6)) | Answer: 9.534 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 76 ohm, XL = 142 ohm and XC = 98 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 76, XL = 142, XC = 98 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(76^2 + (142 - 98)^2) | Answer: 87.82 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 86.4 mH and C = 4.6 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 86.4, C = 4.6 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(86.4e-3 * 4.6e-6)) | Answer: 252.5 Hz

question: A capacitor of 39.9 uF is charged to 265 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 39.9, V = 265 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*39.9e-6*(265)^2 | Answer: 1401 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 160 V with 200 primary turns and 80 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 160, N1 = 200, N2 = 80 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 160 * 80/200 | Answer: 64 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 170 V and draws an armature current of 31 A. If the armature resistance is 0.97 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 170, Ia = 31, Ra = 0.97 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 170 - 31*0.97 | Answer: 139.9 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 40 A at 415 V (line) with a power factor of 0.89. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 40, VL = 415, pf = 0.89 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*415*40*0.89 / 1000 | Answer: 25.59 kW

question: A load has real power 175 kW and apparent power 180 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 175, S = 180 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 175 / 180 | Answer: 0.9722

question: A machine delivers 80 kW output while drawing 147 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 80, Pi = 147 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 80/147 * 100 | Answer: 54.42 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 22 V across R1 = 13 ohm and R2 = 13 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 22, R1 = 13, R2 = 13 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 22*13 / (13+13) | Answer: 11 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 10 kohm and Rin = 32 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 10, Rin = 32 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 10 / 32 | Answer: 0.3125

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 90 kohm and Rg = 11 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 90, Rg = 11 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 90/11 | Answer: 9.182

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 2028. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 2028 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(2028) | Answer: 33.07 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 3.8 m carries a central point load of 20 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.8, W = 20 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 20*3.8 / 4 | Answer: 19 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.7 m carries a UDL of 40 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 9.7, w = 40 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 40*(9.7)^2 / 8 | Answer: 470.4 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 4.4 m carries a point load 80 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.4, W = 80 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 80*4.4 | Answer: 352 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 5.8 m carries a UDL of 40 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.8, w = 40 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 40*(5.8)^2 / 2 | Answer: 672.8 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 7.2 m carries a point load 55 kN at distance 3.1 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 7.2, a = 3.1, W = 55 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 55*(7.2 - 3.1) / 7.2 | Answer: 31.32 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 8 m) carries a central point load 50 kN. With E = 25 GPa and I = 330e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=50000 N, L=8000.0 mm, E=25000 MPa, I=330e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 64.65 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 4.3 m carries a UDL of 27 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.3, w = 27 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 27*(4.3)^2 / 12 | Answer: 41.6 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 570 mm, clear cover 40 mm and main bars of diameter 20 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 570, c = 40, dia = 20 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 570 - 40 - 20/2 | Answer: 520 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 21.9 m^2 carrying a factored load of 15.8 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 21.9, w = 15.8 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 15.8 * 21.9 | Answer: 346 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 3.6 m, unit weight 19 kN/m^3, phi = 31 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 5.4 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 20 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 5.4, g = 20 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (20 - 9.81)*5.4 | Answer: 55.03 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 8.6e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.4, area = 3.5e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 8.6, i = 0.4, A = 3.5 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (8.6e-4)*0.4*(3.5e-3) | Answer: 1204 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 0.8 m, bed slope 0.005 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.012. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 2.3 m under a head of 1.1 m. Taking Cd = 0.64 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 2.8 m wide carries a discharge of 14.2 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 180 m and design speed 60 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 180, V = 60 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (60)^2 / (127*180) | Answer: 0.1575
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: For a design speed of 70 km/h with allowable superelevation 0.06 and lateral friction 0.14, find the minimum curve radius in m.
A tank of volume 320 m^3 treats a flow of 30 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 320, Q = 30 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 320 / 30 | Answer: 10.67 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 270 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.18 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 8 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 270, k = 0.18, t = 8 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 270*(1 - e^(-0.18*8)) | Answer: 206 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.89, rainfall intensity 55 mm/h over a catchment of 8.5 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.89, i = 55, A = 8.5 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.89*55*8.5 / 360 | Answer: 1.156 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.08 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 740 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.08, M = 740 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 740*(20+0.08)/20 | Answer: 743 m

question: Convert the decimal number 246 to binary.
solution: Divide 246 by 2 repeatedly, recording remainders | Reading remainders in reverse gives 11110110 | Answer: 11110110 (binary)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 2 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the decimal number 3583 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 3583 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: DFF (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the 8-bit binary number 11000110 to decimal.
solution: Binary 11000110 = sum of bit-weights | Answer: 198 (decimal)
formula: Sum each bit times its positional weight (2^i)

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 10011001 and 11011010.
solution: XOR: 01000011 | Count of 1s = 3 | Answer: 3
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 410 megabits is sent over a link of 62 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 410, B = 62 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 410 / 62 | Answer: 6.613 s

question: A link has bandwidth 82 Mbps and round-trip time 10 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 82, R = 10 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 82e6 * 10e-3 bits = 820 kb | Answer: 820 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.83, cache access time 5 ns and main-memory access time 70 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.83, tc = 5, tm = 70 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.83*5 + (1 - 0.83)*70 | Answer: 16.05 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 436090 elements?
solution: Given: n = 436090 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(436090)) + 1 | Answer: 19

question: An O(n^2) algorithm performs c*n^2 basic operations. If c = 1 and n = 2200, how many operations are performed?
solution: Given: n = 2200 | Formula: operations = n^2 | Substitute: = (2200)^2 | Answer: 4840000

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.003, memory access time 140 ns and page-fault service time 10 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 10 ms = 10000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.003)*140 + 0.003*10000000.0 ns | Answer: 30.14 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 0.4 m^3 at 180 kPa and 330 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 0.4, P = 180, Tk = 330 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (180e3)*0.4 / (8.314*330) | Answer: 26.24 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.18 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 20 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.18, t = 20 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.18*20) | Answer: 0.9727

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.18 /min) is to reach 90% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.18, X = 90 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.9) / 0.18 | Answer: 12.79 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.44 /min) reaches 85% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.44, X = 85 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.85 / (0.44*(1 - 0.85)) | Answer: 12.88 min

question: For a reaction with A = 2e10 /s and activation energy 75 kJ/mol at 320 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 2, Ea = 75, Tk = 320 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 2e10 * exp(-75e3 / (8.314*320)) | Answer: 0.01143 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.98 and bottoms xW = 0.05, with relative volatility alpha = 2.3. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.98, xw = 0.05, al = 2.3 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.98/0.02)(0.95/0.05)] / ln(2.3) | Answer: 8.208 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.59 and x = 0.34. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.59, x = 0.34 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.59/0.41) / (0.34/0.66) | Answer: 2.793

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.22 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 110 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.22, Psat = 110 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.22 * 110 | Answer: 24.2 kPa

question: A stream of 4.6 kg/s with specific heat 3.1 kJ/kg-K is heated through 20 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 4.6, cp = 3.1, dT = 20 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 4.6*3.1*20 | Answer: 285.2 kW

question: A reactor of volume 6.4 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 3 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 6.4, Q = 3 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 6.4 / 3 | Answer: 2.133 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 7.5e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 4 mm with a concentration difference of 60 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 7.5, L = 4, dC = 60 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (7.5e-9)*60 / (4e-3) | Answer: 112.5 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 6.1 min and steady-state gain 3.4. For a step input of magnitude 20, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 6.1, K = 3.4, M = 20 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 3.4 * 20 | Answer: 68 units

question: A reactor operates at a space time of 15.4 min. Find its space velocity in per hour.
solution: Given: tau = 15.4 | Formula: SV = 60 / tau  (per hour) | Substitute: SV = 60 / 15.4 | Answer: 3.896 /h

question: An aircraft wing of area 35 m^2 flies at 130 m/s (air density 1.225 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 1.4. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 35, V = 130, rho = 1.225, CL = 1.4 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1.225*(130)^2*35*1.4 / 1000 | Answer: 507.2 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 80 m^2 flies at 100 m/s (density 1.225 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.06. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 80, V = 100, rho = 1.225, CD = 0.06 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*1.225*(100)^2*80*0.06 / 1000 | Answer: 29.4 kN

question: A specimen under stress 220 MPa shows an elastic strain of 1.2e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 220, eps = 1.2 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 220 / (1.2e-3) MPa = 183.3 GPa | Answer: 183.3 GPa

question: A block of mass 33 kg has a volume of 2.6e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 33, V = 2.6 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 33 / (2.6e-3) | Answer: 12692 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 1300 mm is heated through 95 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 12e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 1300, dT = 95, al = 12 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 1300*12e-6*95 | Answer: 1.482 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 50 ohm, R2 = 170 ohm and R3 = 390 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 50, R2 = 170, R3 = 390 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 170*390 / 50 | Answer: 1326 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 1000 ohm and gauge factor 2 experiences a strain of 350e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 1000, GF = 2, eps = 350 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 1000*2*350e-6 | Answer: 700 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 10.06 when the true value is 100. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10.06, true = 100 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10.06 - 100| / 100 * 100 | Answer: 89.94 %

question: Annual demand is 18500 units, ordering cost 290 per order and holding cost 15 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 18500, S = 290, H = 15 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*18500*290 / 15) | Answer: 845.8 units

question: An asset costs 350000 with salvage value 2000 after 13 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 350000, Sv = 2000, n = 13 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (350000 - 2000) / 13 | Answer: 26769 per year

question: A product sells for 300 per unit with variable cost 140 per unit and fixed costs 70000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 300, V = 140, F = 70000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 70000 / (300 - 140) | Answer: 437.5 units

question: Find the present worth of 70000 received 7 years from now at an interest rate of 7% per year.
solution: Given: F = 70000, n = 7, i = 7 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 70000 / (1 + 0.07)^7 | Answer: 43592 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.94, 0.93 and 0.98 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.94, r2 = 0.93, r3 = 0.98 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.94*0.93*0.98 | Answer: 0.8567

question: A process produces 11 defective items in a batch of 12000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 11, N = 12000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 11/12000 * 1e6 | Answer: 916.7 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -2x^3 + 3x^2 + 5x - 2 evaluated at x = 4.
For f(x) = -5x^3 + x^2 - 3x - 9, find f''(x) at x = 0.
Evaluate the definite integral of (5x^2 - 4x) dx from x = 1 to x = 4.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = 5x^3/3 + -4x^2/2 + 0x | Evaluate F(4) - F(1) | Answer: 75
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 2x^2 + 5x - 2 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[5, 8], [1, -1]].
solution: Given: a = 5, b = 8, c = 1, d = -1 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (5)(-1) - (8)(1) | Answer: -13

question: Find the determinant of [[-5, -6, -3], [-6, -6, 3], [0, 6, 4]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: 174

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[0, 7], [3, -2]].
solution: Trace tr = -2, Determinant = -21 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 3.69

question: Solve for x: 6x + -3y = 1 and 2x + 0y = 7.
solution: Determinant = 6*0 - -3*2 = 6 | x = (e d - b f) / det = 3.5 | Answer: x = 3.5
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 72, 86, 4, 37, 22.
solution: Sum = 221 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 44.2 | Answer: 44.2

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 19, 30, 26, 23, 26.
solution: Mean = 24.8 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 4.087

question: Find the slope of the line through (6, 8) and (-3, 8).
solution: Given: x1 = 6, y1 = 8, x2 = -3, y2 = 8 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (8 - 8) / (-3 - 6) | Answer: 0

question: Find the distance between the points (7, -4) and (-7, 4).
solution: Given: x1 = 7, y1 = -4, x2 = -7, y2 = 4 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-14)^2 + (8)^2) | Answer: 16.12 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (-7,-1), (-6,5), (4,-1).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 33 sq units

question: Evaluate the number of combinations C(17, 10).
solution: Given: n = 17, r = 10 | Formula: C(n, r) = n! / (r! (n - r)!) | Substitute: C(17, 10) = 17! / (10! * 7!) | Answer: 19448

question: Find the 17th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 9 and common difference -8.
solution: Given: a = 9, d = -8, n = 17 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = 9 + (17 - 1)*-8 | Answer: -119

question: Find the sum of the first 17 terms of an AP with first term 5 and common difference -7.
solution: Given: a = 5, d = -7, n = 17 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 17/2 [2*5 + (17-1)*-7] | Answer: -867

question: Find the 5th term of a geometric progression with first term 3 and common ratio 2.
solution: Given: a = 3, r = 2, n = 5 | Formula: a_n = a r^(n-1) | Substitute: a_n = 3 * 2^(5-1) | Answer: 48

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 46500 at 5% per annum for 3 years.
solution: Given: P = 46500, R = 5, Tt = 3 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 46500 * 5 * 3 / 100 | Answer: 6975 currency units

question: Find the amount when 37000 is invested at 9.3% per annum compounded annually for 6 years.
solution: Given: P = 37000, R = 9.3, Tt = 6 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 37000 * (1 + 9.3/100)^6 | Answer: 63085 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (-2, 0, 6) and (3, -8, -4).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (-6, -2, 4) and (-6, 3, -2).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 47.54

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (3, -1, 1) and (-5, -6, 0).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 110.3 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number -9 + -10i.
solution: Given: a = -9, b = -10 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((-9)^2 + (-10)^2) | Answer: 13.45

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number -9 + -11i.
solution: Given: a = -9, b = -11 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(-11, -9) | Answer: -129.3 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -5x^3 + 5x^2 + x + 1 at x = 2.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-19 with initial guess x0=14, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.5 and ordinates 6, 4, 12, 7, 2, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 249 and 170.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 249 and 170 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 23 and 13.
solution: Given: a = 23, b = 13 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 23*13 / 1 | Answer: 299
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 32 mm carries an axial tensile load of 9 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 35 mm and length 1000 mm carries an axial load of 81 kN. Take E = 110 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 20 mm transmits a torque of 2600 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 20, Tt = 2600 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(2600*1000) / (pi*(20)^3) | Answer: 1655 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 60 mm and length 1500 mm carries a torque of 1750 N-m. With G = 80 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (60)^4 / 32 = 1272345 mm^4 | theta = (1750*1000)(1500) / (80000 * 1272345) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 1.478 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 136 mm wide and 260 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 136, h = 260 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 136*(260)^2 / 6 | Answer: 1532267 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (88 mm x 170 mm) carries a bending moment of 8 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (30 mm x 130 mm) has effective length 3200 mm and E = 200 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 740 MPa is designed for a working stress of 210 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 740, sw = 210 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 740 / 210 | Answer: 3.524

question: A steel bar is fully restrained and heated through 65 deg C. With E = 200 GPa and alpha = 12e-6 /deg C, find the thermal stress in MPa.
solution: Given: dT = 65, E = 200, al = 12 | Formula: sigma = E alpha (dT) | Substitute: sigma = 200000 * 12e-6 * 65 | Answer: 156 MPa

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1300 mm and wall thickness 12 mm carries an internal pressure of 2.4 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1300, t = 12, P = 2.4 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 2.4*1300 / (2*12) | Answer: 130 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 660 K and 300 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 660, Tc = 300 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 300/660) * 100 | Answer: 54.55 %

question: A refrigerator works between 253 K (cold) and 316 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 253, Th = 316 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 253 / (316 - 253) | Answer: 4.016

question: A heat pump operates between 281 K and 320 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 281, Th = 320 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 320 / (320 - 281) | Answer: 8.205

question: 6.2 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 155 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 6.2, dT = 155 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 6.2 * 0.718 * 155 | Answer: 690 kJ

question: 2.7 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 70 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.7, dT = 70 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 2.7 * 1.005 * 70 | Answer: 189.9 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 2.4 m^3 at 490 K with mass 3.7 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 2.4, Tk = 490, m = 3.7 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 3.7*0.287*490 / 2.4 | Answer: 216.8 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 4.8 kg of air expands isothermally at 480 K from volume V1 to 3*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.8, Tk = 480, ratio = 3 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 4.8*0.287*480*ln(3) | Answer: 726.5 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 1.1 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.37 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 1.1, D = 0.37 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*1.1*0.37 / 0.001 | Answer: 407000

question: Water flows at 3.6 m/s through a pipe of diameter 80 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 13.8 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 13.8 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*13.8 / 1000 | Answer: 135.4 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 1.5 m. Taking Cv = 0.98, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 1.5, cv = 0.98 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.98*sqrt(2*9.81*1.5) | Answer: 5.316 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 260 mm) water flows at 1.9 m/s. It contracts to diameter 130 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 260, d2 = 130, V1 = 1.9 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 1.9*(260/130)^2 | Answer: 7.6 m/s

question: Water flows at 3.8 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.31 m and length 390 m. With friction factor f = 0.025, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 24 teeth drives a gear of 60 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1250 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 24, z2 = 60, N1 = 1250 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1250*24 / 60 | Answer: 500 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 520 mm rotates at 250 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 520, N = 250 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.52)*250 / 60 | Answer: 6.807 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 47.9 kW at 700 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 47.9, N = 700 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(47.9*1000) / (2*pi*700) | Answer: 653.4 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 1.6 kg rotates at radius 0.53 m at 1150 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 11200 N/m and mass 18.2 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 11200, m = 18.2 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(11200/18.2) | Answer: 3.948 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 7.8 m^2 and thickness 0.33 m has conductivity k = 48.5 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 60 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 7.8, L = 0.33, k = 48.5, dT = 60 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 48.5*7.8*60 / 0.33 | Answer: 68782 W

question: A surface of area 5 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 90 W/m^2-K to surroundings 80 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 5, h = 90, dT = 80 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 90*5*80 | Answer: 36000 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 90 m/min, feed = 0.25 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2.2 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 90, f = 0.25, d = 2.2 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*90*0.25*2.2 | Answer: 49500 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 400 mm is turned at 1150 rpm with a feed of 0.12 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 400, N = 1150, f = 0.12 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 400 / (0.12*1150) | Answer: 2.899 min

question: A resistor of 139 ohm carries a current of 7 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 139, I = 7 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 7 * 139 | Answer: 973 V

question: Three resistors 79 ohm, 15 ohm and 69 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 79, R2 = 15, R3 = 69 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 79 + 15 + 69 | Answer: 163 ohm

question: Two resistors 65 ohm and 120 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 65, R2 = 120 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 65*120 / (65+120) | Answer: 42.16 ohm

question: A device draws 14.6 A at 90 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 90, I = 14.6 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 90 * 14.6 | Answer: 1314 W

question: A current of 5.9 A flows through a 49 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 5.9, R = 49 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (5.9)^2 * 49 | Answer: 1706 W

question: Two capacitors 44.4 uF and 32.1 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 44.4, C2 = 32.1 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 44.4*32.1 / (44.4+32.1) | Answer: 18.63 uF

question: A resistor 11 kohm and capacitor 19.5 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 11, C = 19.5 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (11k)(19.5u) = 214.5 ms | Answer: 214.5 ms

question: An inductor 439.1 mH is in series with 70 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 439.1, R = 70 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (439.1e-3) / 70 | Answer: 6.273 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 180.8 mH inductor at 990 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 180.8, f = 990 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (990)(180.8e-3) | Answer: 1125 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 45.5 uF capacitor at 440 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 45.5, f = 440 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (440)(45.5e-6)) | Answer: 7.95 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 71 ohm, XL = 101 ohm and XC = 53 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 71, XL = 101, XC = 53 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(71^2 + (101 - 53)^2) | Answer: 85.7 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 9.2 mH and C = 2.7 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 9.2, C = 2.7 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(9.2e-3 * 2.7e-6)) | Answer: 101 Hz

question: A capacitor of 24.7 uF is charged to 130 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 24.7, V = 130 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*24.7e-6*(130)^2 | Answer: 208.7 mJ

question: An alternating voltage has a peak value of 40 V. Find its RMS value.
solution: Given: Vp = 40 | Formula: Vrms = Vp / sqrt(2) | Substitute: Vrms = 40 / sqrt(2) | Answer: 28.28 V

question: A transformer has primary voltage 240 V with 540 primary turns and 310 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 240, N1 = 540, N2 = 310 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 240 * 310/540 | Answer: 137.8 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 290 V and draws an armature current of 40 A. If the armature resistance is 0.5 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 290, Ia = 40, Ra = 0.5 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 290 - 40*0.5 | Answer: 270 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 125 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.83. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 125, VL = 400, pf = 0.83 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*400*125*0.83 / 1000 | Answer: 71.88 kW

question: A load has real power 135 kW and apparent power 150 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 135, S = 150 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 135 / 150 | Answer: 0.9

question: A machine delivers 145 kW output while drawing 177 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 145, Pi = 177 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 145/177 * 100 | Answer: 81.92 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 20 V across R1 = 44 ohm and R2 = 20 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 20, R1 = 44, R2 = 20 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 20*20 / (44+20) | Answer: 6.25 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 90 kohm and Rin = 6 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 90, Rin = 6 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 90 / 6 | Answer: 15

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 160 kohm and Rg = 23 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 160, Rg = 23 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 160/23 | Answer: 7.957

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 9270. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 9270 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(9270) | Answer: 39.67 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 8.4 m carries a central point load of 60 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 8.4, W = 60 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 60*8.4 / 4 | Answer: 126 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 8.6 m carries a UDL of 55 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 8.6, w = 55 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 55*(8.6)^2 / 8 | Answer: 508.5 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 4 m carries a point load 20 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4, W = 20 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 20*4 | Answer: 80 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 4 m carries a UDL of 32 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4, w = 32 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 32*(4)^2 / 2 | Answer: 256 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 7.8 m carries a point load 100 kN at distance 1.8 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 7.8, a = 1.8, W = 100 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 100*(7.8 - 1.8) / 7.8 | Answer: 76.92 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 5.8 m) carries a central point load 80 kN. With E = 30 GPa and I = 510e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=80000 N, L=5800.0 mm, E=30000 MPa, I=510e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 21.25 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 7.2 m carries a UDL of 6 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7.2, w = 6 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 6*(7.2)^2 / 12 | Answer: 25.92 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 320 mm, clear cover 50 mm and main bars of diameter 16 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 320, c = 50, dia = 16 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 320 - 50 - 16/2 | Answer: 262 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 13.9 m^2 carrying a factored load of 9.5 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 13.9, w = 9.5 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 9.5 * 13.9 | Answer: 132.1 kN

question: For a bar of diameter 20 mm with design bond stress 2.3 MPa and steel stress 360 MPa, find the development length in mm.
solution: Given: dia = 20, tbd = 2.3, fs = 360 | Formula: Ld = phi fs / (4 tau_bd) | Substitute: Ld = 20*360 / (4*2.3) | Answer: 782.6 mm

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 4.2 m, unit weight 18 kN/m^3, phi = 28 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 7.3 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 19 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 7.3, g = 19 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (19 - 9.81)*7.3 | Answer: 67.09 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 6.7e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.3, area = 1.6e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 6.7, i = 0.3, A = 1.6 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (6.7e-4)*0.3*(1.6e-3) | Answer: 321.6 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.9 m, bed slope 0.004 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.024. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 1.1 m under a head of 1.1 m. Taking Cd = 0.61 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 6 m wide carries a discharge of 13.3 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 450 m and design speed 70 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 450, V = 70 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (70)^2 / (127*450) | Answer: 0.08574
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: For a design speed of 95 km/h with allowable superelevation 0.06 and lateral friction 0.14, find the minimum curve radius in m.
A tank of volume 730 m^3 treats a flow of 105 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 730, Q = 105 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 730 / 105 | Answer: 6.952 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 400 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.33 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 3 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 400, k = 0.33, t = 3 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 400*(1 - e^(-0.33*3)) | Answer: 251.4 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.59, rainfall intensity 95 mm/h over a catchment of 37.3 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.59, i = 95, A = 37.3 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.59*95*37.3 / 360 | Answer: 5.807 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.05 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 260 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.05, M = 260 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 260*(20+0.05)/20 | Answer: 260.6 m

question: Convert the decimal number 27 to binary.
solution: Divide 27 by 2 repeatedly, recording remainders | Reading remainders in reverse gives 11011 | Answer: 11011 (binary)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 2 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the decimal number 1833 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 1833 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 729 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the 8-bit binary number 11011100 to decimal.
solution: Binary 11011100 = sum of bit-weights | Answer: 220 (decimal)
formula: Sum each bit times its positional weight (2^i)

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 11010110 and 00111000.
solution: XOR: 11101110 | Count of 1s = 6 | Answer: 6
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 140 megabits is sent over a link of 6 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 140, B = 6 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 140 / 6 | Answer: 23.33 s

question: A link has bandwidth 69 Mbps and round-trip time 80 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 69, R = 80 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 69e6 * 80e-3 bits = 5520 kb | Answer: 5520 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.95, cache access time 7 ns and main-memory access time 120 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.95, tc = 7, tm = 120 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.95*7 + (1 - 0.95)*120 | Answer: 12.65 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 156624 elements?
solution: Given: n = 156624 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(156624)) + 1 | Answer: 18

question: An O(n^2) algorithm performs c*n^2 basic operations. If c = 1 and n = 130, how many operations are performed?
solution: Given: n = 130 | Formula: operations = n^2 | Substitute: = (130)^2 | Answer: 16900

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.007, memory access time 90 ns and page-fault service time 9 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 9 ms = 9000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.007)*90 + 0.007*9000000.0 ns | Answer: 63.09 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 0.3 m^3 at 350 kPa and 360 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 0.3, P = 350, Tk = 360 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (350e3)*0.3 / (8.314*360) | Answer: 35.08 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.05 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 4 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.05, t = 4 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.05*4) | Answer: 0.1813

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.34 /min) is to reach 55% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.34, X = 55 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.55) / 0.34 | Answer: 2.349 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.26 /min) reaches 60% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.26, X = 60 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.6 / (0.26*(1 - 0.6)) | Answer: 5.769 min

question: For a reaction with A = 2e10 /s and activation energy 70 kJ/mol at 320 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 2, Ea = 70, Tk = 320 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 2e10 * exp(-70e3 / (8.314*320)) | Answer: 0.07487 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.92 and bottoms xW = 0.1, with relative volatility alpha = 1.8. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.92, xw = 0.1, al = 1.8 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.92/0.08)(0.9/0.1)] / ln(1.8) | Answer: 7.893 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.83 and x = 0.41. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.83, x = 0.41 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.83/0.17) / (0.41/0.59) | Answer: 7.026

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.64 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 25 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.64, Psat = 25 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.64 * 25 | Answer: 16 kPa

question: A stream of 3.8 kg/s with specific heat 3.7 kJ/kg-K is heated through 80 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 3.8, cp = 3.7, dT = 80 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 3.8*3.7*80 | Answer: 1125 kW

question: A reactor of volume 1.1 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 1 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 1.1, Q = 1 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 1.1 / 1 | Answer: 1.1 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 1.9e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 1 mm with a concentration difference of 130 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 1.9, L = 1, dC = 130 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (1.9e-9)*130 / (1e-3) | Answer: 247 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 3.8 min and steady-state gain 2.8. For a step input of magnitude 3, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 3.8, K = 2.8, M = 3 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 2.8 * 3 | Answer: 8.4 units

question: A reactor operates at a space time of 8.2 min. Find its space velocity in per hour.
solution: Given: tau = 8.2 | Formula: SV = 60 / tau  (per hour) | Substitute: SV = 60 / 8.2 | Answer: 7.317 /h

question: An aircraft wing of area 40 m^2 flies at 200 m/s (air density 0.7 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.5. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 40, V = 200, rho = 0.7, CL = 0.5 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.7*(200)^2*40*0.5 / 1000 | Answer: 280 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 95 m^2 flies at 140 m/s (density 1.225 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.09. Find the drag force in kN.
An aircraft flies at 380 m/s where the speed of sound is 340 m/s. Find the Mach number.
solution: Given: V = 380, a = 340 | Formula: M = V / a | Substitute: M = 380 / 340 | Answer: 1.118

question: A specimen under stress 190 MPa shows an elastic strain of 1.5e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 190, eps = 1.5 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 190 / (1.5e-3) MPa = 126.7 GPa | Answer: 126.7 GPa

question: A block of mass 20 kg has a volume of 3.5e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 20, V = 3.5 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 20 / (3.5e-3) | Answer: 5714 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 2100 mm is heated through 75 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 17e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 2100, dT = 75, al = 17 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 2100*17e-6*75 | Answer: 2.678 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 135 ohm, R2 = 195 ohm and R3 = 180 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 135, R2 = 195, R3 = 180 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 195*180 / 135 | Answer: 260 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 120 ohm and gauge factor 2.1 experiences a strain of 1650e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 120, GF = 2.1, eps = 1650 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 120*2.1*1650e-6 | Answer: 415.8 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 10.92 when the true value is 20. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10.92, true = 20 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10.92 - 20| / 20 * 100 | Answer: 45.4 %

question: Annual demand is 3500 units, ordering cost 150 per order and holding cost 34 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 3500, S = 150, H = 34 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*3500*150 / 34) | Answer: 175.7 units

question: An asset costs 480000 with salvage value 38000 after 15 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 480000, Sv = 38000, n = 15 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (480000 - 38000) / 15 | Answer: 29467 per year

question: A product sells for 230 per unit with variable cost 110 per unit and fixed costs 50000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 230, V = 110, F = 50000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 50000 / (230 - 110) | Answer: 416.7 units

question: Find the present worth of 145000 received 9 years from now at an interest rate of 9% per year.
solution: Given: F = 145000, n = 9, i = 9 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 145000 / (1 + 0.09)^9 | Answer: 66762 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.93, 0.91 and 0.94 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.93, r2 = 0.91, r3 = 0.94 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.93*0.91*0.94 | Answer: 0.7955

question: A process produces 28 defective items in a batch of 8500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 28, N = 8500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 28/8500 * 1e6 | Answer: 3294 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -6x^3 - 4x^2 + x + 8 evaluated at x = -5.
For f(x) = 6x^3 - 2x^2 - 3x - 9, find f''(x) at x = 5.
Evaluate the definite integral of (3x^2 - 5x + 4) dx from x = 1 to x = 4.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = 3x^3/3 + -5x^2/2 + 4x | Evaluate F(4) - F(1) | Answer: 37.5
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of x^2 - 3x - 11 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[-4, -2], [-1, 8]].
solution: Given: a = -4, b = -2, c = -1, d = 8 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (-4)(8) - (-2)(-1) | Answer: -34

question: Find the determinant of [[0, 6, -6], [-6, -6, 4], [-5, -3, -5]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: -228

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[-5, -1], [5, 1]].
solution: Trace tr = -4, Determinant = 0 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 0

question: Solve for x: 3x + -6y = 5 and -6x + 0y = -5.
solution: Determinant = 3*0 - -6*-6 = -36 | x = (e d - b f) / det = 0.8333 | Answer: x = 0.8333
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 64, 16, 57, 34, 9.
solution: Sum = 180 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 36 | Answer: 36

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 5, 43, 2, 43, 47.
solution: Mean = 28 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 22.45

question: Find the slope of the line through (7, 3) and (-6, 1).
solution: Given: x1 = 7, y1 = 3, x2 = -6, y2 = 1 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (1 - 3) / (-6 - 7) | Answer: 0.1538

question: Find the distance between the points (0, -5) and (8, 0).
solution: Given: x1 = 0, y1 = -5, x2 = 8, y2 = 0 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((8)^2 + (5)^2) | Answer: 9.434 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (6,0), (-4,7), (2,5).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 11 sq units

question: Evaluate the number of combinations C(15, 4).
solution: Given: n = 15, r = 4 | Formula: C(n, r) = n! / (r! (n - r)!) | Substitute: C(15, 4) = 15! / (4! * 11!) | Answer: 1365

question: Find the 17th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 14 and common difference -8.
solution: Given: a = 14, d = -8, n = 17 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = 14 + (17 - 1)*-8 | Answer: -114

question: Find the sum of the first 32 terms of an AP with first term 11 and common difference 0.
solution: Given: a = 11, d = 0, n = 32 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 32/2 [2*11 + (32-1)*0] | Answer: 352

question: Find the 6th term of a geometric progression with first term 9 and common ratio 2.
solution: Given: a = 9, r = 2, n = 6 | Formula: a_n = a r^(n-1) | Substitute: a_n = 9 * 2^(6-1) | Answer: 288

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 38000 at 12.8% per annum for 10 years.
solution: Given: P = 38000, R = 12.8, Tt = 10 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 38000 * 12.8 * 10 / 100 | Answer: 48640 currency units

question: Find the amount when 10500 is invested at 11.7% per annum compounded annually for 2 years.
solution: Given: P = 10500, R = 11.7, Tt = 2 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 10500 * (1 + 11.7/100)^2 | Answer: 13101 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (-8, -7, 6) and (-3, 8, -7).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (4, 0, 0) and (0, 4, 1).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 16.49

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (-1, 2, 6) and (2, 4, 3).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 45.89 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number 4 + -3i.
solution: Given: a = 4, b = -3 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((4)^2 + (-3)^2) | Answer: 5

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number -2 + -5i.
solution: Given: a = -2, b = -5 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(-5, -2) | Answer: -111.8 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -2x^3 + 2x^2 - 3x - 1 at x = 3.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-134 with initial guess x0=15, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.2 and ordinates 2, 4, 12, 9, 16, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 21 and 354.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 21 and 354 | Answer: GCD = 3

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 30 and 18.
solution: Given: a = 30, b = 18 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 30*18 / 6 | Answer: 90
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 10 mm carries an axial tensile load of 71 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 34 mm and length 1600 mm carries an axial load of 25 kN. Take E = 70 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 21 mm transmits a torque of 2150 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 21, Tt = 2150 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(2150*1000) / (pi*(21)^3) | Answer: 1182 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 43 mm and length 500 mm carries a torque of 800 N-m. With G = 45 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (43)^4 / 32 = 33564 mm^4 | theta = (800*1000)(500) / (45000 * 33564) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 1.517 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 64 mm wide and 210 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 64, h = 210 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 64*(210)^2 / 6 | Answer: 470400 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (77 mm x 220 mm) carries a bending moment of 36 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (42 mm x 160 mm) has effective length 3000 mm and E = 200 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 330 MPa is designed for a working stress of 190 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 330, sw = 190 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 330 / 190 | Answer: 1.737

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1200 mm and wall thickness 9 mm carries an internal pressure of 2.5 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1200, t = 9, P = 2.5 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 2.5*1200 / (2*9) | Answer: 166.7 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 600 K and 430 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 600, Tc = 430 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 430/600) * 100 | Answer: 28.33 %

question: A refrigerator works between 256 K (cold) and 314 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 256, Th = 314 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 256 / (314 - 256) | Answer: 4.414

question: A heat pump operates between 263 K and 304 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 263, Th = 304 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 304 / (304 - 263) | Answer: 7.415

question: 6.6 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 120 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 6.6, dT = 120 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 6.6 * 0.718 * 120 | Answer: 568.7 kJ

question: 6.7 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 75 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 6.7, dT = 75 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 6.7 * 1.005 * 75 | Answer: 505 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 1.4 m^3 at 500 K with mass 2.1 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 1.4, Tk = 500, m = 2.1 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 2.1*0.287*500 / 1.4 | Answer: 215.3 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 3 kg of air expands isothermally at 310 K from volume V1 to 3*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3, Tk = 310, ratio = 3 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 3*0.287*310*ln(3) | Answer: 293.2 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 2.9 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.07 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 2.9, D = 0.07 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*2.9*0.07 / 0.001 | Answer: 203000

question: Water flows at 1.3 m/s through a pipe of diameter 120 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 29.7 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 29.7 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*29.7 / 1000 | Answer: 291.4 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 19.2 m. Taking Cv = 0.98, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 19.2, cv = 0.98 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.98*sqrt(2*9.81*19.2) | Answer: 19.02 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 160 mm) water flows at 2.4 m/s. It contracts to diameter 80 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 160, d2 = 80, V1 = 2.4 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 2.4*(160/80)^2 | Answer: 9.6 m/s

question: Water flows at 2.4 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.26 m and length 360 m. With friction factor f = 0.023, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 39 teeth drives a gear of 46 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1400 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 39, z2 = 46, N1 = 1400 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1400*39 / 46 | Answer: 1187 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 270 mm rotates at 800 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 270, N = 800 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.27)*800 / 60 | Answer: 11.31 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 11.8 kW at 600 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 11.8, N = 600 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(11.8*1000) / (2*pi*600) | Answer: 187.8 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 9.3 kg rotates at radius 0.58 m at 300 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 5000 N/m and mass 16.7 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 5000, m = 16.7 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(5000/16.7) | Answer: 2.754 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 1.7 m^2 and thickness 0.35 m has conductivity k = 1.4 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 65 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 1.7, L = 0.35, k = 1.4, dT = 65 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 1.4*1.7*65 / 0.35 | Answer: 442 W

question: A surface of area 2.7 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 170 W/m^2-K to surroundings 95 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 2.7, h = 170, dT = 95 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 170*2.7*95 | Answer: 43605 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 190 m/min, feed = 0.17 mm/rev, depth of cut = 1.3 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 190, f = 0.17, d = 1.3 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*190*0.17*1.3 | Answer: 41990 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 350 mm is turned at 700 rpm with a feed of 0.38 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 350, N = 700, f = 0.38 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 350 / (0.38*700) | Answer: 1.316 min

question: A resistor of 171 ohm carries a current of 4 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 171, I = 4 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 4 * 171 | Answer: 684 V

question: Three resistors 44 ohm, 26 ohm and 95 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 44, R2 = 26, R3 = 95 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 44 + 26 + 95 | Answer: 165 ohm

question: Two resistors 41 ohm and 117 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 41, R2 = 117 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 41*117 / (41+117) | Answer: 30.36 ohm

question: A device draws 4.9 A at 225 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 225, I = 4.9 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 225 * 4.9 | Answer: 1102 W

question: A current of 7.4 A flows through a 144 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 7.4, R = 144 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (7.4)^2 * 144 | Answer: 7885 W

question: Two capacitors 17.1 uF and 22.9 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 17.1, C2 = 22.9 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 17.1*22.9 / (17.1+22.9) | Answer: 9.79 uF

question: A resistor 41 kohm and capacitor 7.1 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 41, C = 7.1 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (41k)(7.1u) = 291.1 ms | Answer: 291.1 ms

question: An inductor 327.3 mH is in series with 115 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 327.3, R = 115 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (327.3e-3) / 115 | Answer: 2.846 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 122.7 mH inductor at 540 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 122.7, f = 540 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (540)(122.7e-3) | Answer: 416.3 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 22.4 uF capacitor at 800 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 22.4, f = 800 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (800)(22.4e-6)) | Answer: 8.881 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 70 ohm, XL = 14 ohm and XC = 77 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 70, XL = 14, XC = 77 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(70^2 + (14 - 77)^2) | Answer: 94.18 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 85.6 mH and C = 8.1 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 85.6, C = 8.1 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(85.6e-3 * 8.1e-6)) | Answer: 191.1 Hz

question: A capacitor of 18.9 uF is charged to 120 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 18.9, V = 120 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*18.9e-6*(120)^2 | Answer: 136.1 mJ

question: An alternating voltage has a peak value of 76 V. Find its RMS value.
solution: Given: Vp = 76 | Formula: Vrms = Vp / sqrt(2) | Substitute: Vrms = 76 / sqrt(2) | Answer: 53.74 V

question: A transformer has primary voltage 350 V with 360 primary turns and 30 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 350, N1 = 360, N2 = 30 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 350 * 30/360 | Answer: 29.17 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 390 V and draws an armature current of 30 A. If the armature resistance is 0.1 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 390, Ia = 30, Ra = 0.1 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 390 - 30*0.1 | Answer: 387 V

question: A 8-pole induction motor on a 60 Hz supply runs at 800 rpm. Find the slip (%).
formula: s = (Ns - N) / Ns,  Ns = 120 f / P

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 30 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.94. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 30, VL = 400, pf = 0.94 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*400*30*0.94 / 1000 | Answer: 19.54 kW

question: A load has real power 15 kW and apparent power 150 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 15, S = 150 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 15 / 150 | Answer: 0.1

question: A machine delivers 55 kW output while drawing 197 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 55, Pi = 197 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 55/197 * 100 | Answer: 27.92 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 18 V across R1 = 36 ohm and R2 = 25 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 18, R1 = 36, R2 = 25 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 18*25 / (36+25) | Answer: 7.377 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 190 kohm and Rin = 1 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 190, Rin = 1 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 190 / 1 | Answer: 190

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 20 kohm and Rg = 32 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 20, Rg = 32 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 20/32 | Answer: 1.625

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 8355. Express the gain in decibels (power).
