question: A rod of length 2300 mm is heated through 80 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 23e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 2300, dT = 80, al = 23 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 2300*23e-6*80 | Answer: 4.232 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 155 ohm, R2 = 130 ohm and R3 = 495 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 155, R2 = 130, R3 = 495 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 130*495 / 155 | Answer: 415.2 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 350 ohm and gauge factor 2 experiences a strain of 2000e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 350, GF = 2, eps = 2000 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 350*2*2000e-6 | Answer: 1400 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 10.66 when the true value is 50. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10.66, true = 50 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10.66 - 50| / 50 * 100 | Answer: 78.68 %

question: Annual demand is 33000 units, ordering cost 60 per order and holding cost 4 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 33000, S = 60, H = 4 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*33000*60 / 4) | Answer: 995 units

question: An asset costs 320000 with salvage value 8000 after 17 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 320000, Sv = 8000, n = 17 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (320000 - 8000) / 17 | Answer: 18353 per year

question: A product sells for 260 per unit with variable cost 70 per unit and fixed costs 135000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 260, V = 70, F = 135000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 135000 / (260 - 70) | Answer: 710.5 units

question: Find the present worth of 10000 received 3 years from now at an interest rate of 6% per year.
solution: Given: F = 10000, n = 3, i = 6 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 10000 / (1 + 0.06)^3 | Answer: 8396 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.95, 0.94 and 0.98 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.95, r2 = 0.94, r3 = 0.98 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.95*0.94*0.98 | Answer: 0.8751

question: A process produces 31 defective items in a batch of 18000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 31, N = 18000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 31/18000 * 1e6 | Answer: 1722 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = 3x^3 - 3x^2 + x - 6 evaluated at x = 1.
For f(x) = 6x^3 + 5x^2 + 6x + 4, find f''(x) at x = -1.
Evaluate the definite integral of (6x) dx from x = 1 to x = 5.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = 0x^3/3 + 6x^2/2 + 0x | Evaluate F(5) - F(1) | Answer: 72
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 5x^2 - 4x = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[-3, 4], [1, -9]].
solution: Given: a = -3, b = 4, c = 1, d = -9 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (-3)(-9) - (4)(1) | Answer: 23

question: Find the determinant of [[1, 4, -4], [6, 0, 1], [-1, 4, 3]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: -176

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[-1, -8], [-1, -7]].
solution: Trace tr = -8, Determinant = -1 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 0.1231

question: Solve for x: 6x + -1y = 10 and -3x + 0y = -7.
solution: Determinant = 6*0 - -1*-3 = -3 | x = (e d - b f) / det = 2.333 | Answer: x = 2.333
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 97, 14, 33, 16, 37.
solution: Sum = 197 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 39.4 | Answer: 39.4

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 35, 21, 4, 10, 19.
solution: Mean = 17.8 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 11.82

question: Find the slope of the line through (3, -4) and (7, -4).
solution: Given: x1 = 3, y1 = -4, x2 = 7, y2 = -4 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (-4 - -4) / (7 - 3) | Answer: 0

question: Find the distance between the points (3, -3) and (0, -9).
solution: Given: x1 = 3, y1 = -3, x2 = 0, y2 = -9 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-3)^2 + (-6)^2) | Answer: 6.708 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (7,1), (-3,2), (-8,-5).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 37.5 sq units

question: Evaluate the number of combinations C(6, 3).
solution: Given: n = 6, r = 3 | Formula: C(n, r) = n! / (r! (n - r)!) | Substitute: C(6, 3) = 6! / (3! * 3!) | Answer: 20

question: Find the 31th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 19 and common difference 0.
solution: Given: a = 19, d = 0, n = 31 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = 19 + (31 - 1)*0 | Answer: 19

question: Find the sum of the first 11 terms of an AP with first term 6 and common difference 6.
solution: Given: a = 6, d = 6, n = 11 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 11/2 [2*6 + (11-1)*6] | Answer: 396

question: Find the 3th term of a geometric progression with first term 8 and common ratio 4.
solution: Given: a = 8, r = 4, n = 3 | Formula: a_n = a r^(n-1) | Substitute: a_n = 8 * 4^(3-1) | Answer: 128

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 40000 at 11.7% per annum for 1 years.
solution: Given: P = 40000, R = 11.7, Tt = 1 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 40000 * 11.7 * 1 / 100 | Answer: 4680 currency units

question: Find the amount when 11500 is invested at 6.1% per annum compounded annually for 3 years.
solution: Given: P = 11500, R = 6.1, Tt = 3 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 11500 * (1 + 6.1/100)^3 | Answer: 13735 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (1, -3, -8) and (-7, 5, 3).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (-4, 4, -3) and (0, -5, 3).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 23.52

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (-6, 5, 6) and (5, -5, -3).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 164.8 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number -11 + 0i.
solution: Given: a = -11, b = 0 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((-11)^2 + (0)^2) | Answer: 11

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number -5 + 4i.
solution: Given: a = -5, b = 4 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(4, -5) | Answer: 141.3 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = 5x^3 + 4x^2 - 5x + 2 at x = 0.
solution: Given: a = 5, b = 4, c = -5, d = 2, x0 = 0 | Formula: f(x0) = a x0^3 + b x0^2 + c x0 + d | Substitute: f(0) = 5(0)^3 + 4(0)^2 + -5(0) + 2 | Answer: 2

question: Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-166 with initial guess x0=11, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.5 and ordinates 16, 20, 20, 14, 10, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 474 and 520.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 474 and 520 | Answer: GCD = 2

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 78 and 4.
solution: Given: a = 78, b = 4 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 78*4 / 2 | Answer: 156
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 56 mm carries an axial tensile load of 10 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 31 mm and length 1800 mm carries an axial load of 74 kN. Take E = 200 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 26 mm transmits a torque of 1950 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 26, Tt = 1950 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(1950*1000) / (pi*(26)^3) | Answer: 565 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 53 mm and length 800 mm carries a torque of 1300 N-m. With G = 45 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (53)^4 / 32 = 774646 mm^4 | theta = (1300*1000)(800) / (45000 * 774646) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 1.709 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 114 mm wide and 80 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 114, h = 80 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 114*(80)^2 / 6 | Answer: 121600 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (61 mm x 250 mm) carries a bending moment of 13 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (73 mm x 140 mm) has effective length 2200 mm and E = 200 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 420 MPa is designed for a working stress of 210 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 420, sw = 210 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 420 / 210 | Answer: 2

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1250 mm and wall thickness 19 mm carries an internal pressure of 1.7 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1250, t = 19, P = 1.7 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 1.7*1250 / (2*19) | Answer: 55.92 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 1040 K and 330 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 1040, Tc = 330 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 330/1040) * 100 | Answer: 68.27 %

question: A refrigerator works between 259 K (cold) and 322 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 259, Th = 322 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 259 / (322 - 259) | Answer: 4.111

question: A heat pump operates between 263 K and 310 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 263, Th = 310 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 310 / (310 - 263) | Answer: 6.596

question: 3.3 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 185 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.3, dT = 185 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 3.3 * 0.718 * 185 | Answer: 438.3 kJ

question: 5.6 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 75 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 5.6, dT = 75 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 5.6 * 1.005 * 75 | Answer: 422.1 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 1.7 m^3 at 410 K with mass 3.5 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 1.7, Tk = 410, m = 3.5 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 3.5*0.287*410 / 1.7 | Answer: 242.3 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 1.4 kg of air expands isothermally at 460 K from volume V1 to 3*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1.4, Tk = 460, ratio = 3 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 1.4*0.287*460*ln(3) | Answer: 203.1 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 2.8 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.21 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 2.8, D = 0.21 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*2.8*0.21 / 0.001 | Answer: 588000

question: Water flows at 3.8 m/s through a pipe of diameter 160 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 29.8 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 29.8 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*29.8 / 1000 | Answer: 292.3 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 12.5 m. Taking Cv = 0.98, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 12.5, cv = 0.98 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.98*sqrt(2*9.81*12.5) | Answer: 15.35 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 200 mm) water flows at 0.8 m/s. It contracts to diameter 100 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 200, d2 = 100, V1 = 0.8 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 0.8*(200/100)^2 | Answer: 3.2 m/s

question: Water flows at 1.5 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.16 m and length 440 m. With friction factor f = 0.023, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 23 teeth drives a gear of 98 teeth. If the pinion runs at 350 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 23, z2 = 98, N1 = 350 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 350*23 / 98 | Answer: 82.14 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 570 mm rotates at 300 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 570, N = 300 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.57)*300 / 60 | Answer: 8.954 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 36.1 kW at 300 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 36.1, N = 300 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(36.1*1000) / (2*pi*300) | Answer: 1149 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 2.8 kg rotates at radius 0.24 m at 200 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 3900 N/m and mass 18 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 3900, m = 18 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(3900/18) | Answer: 2.343 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 1 m^2 and thickness 0.26 m has conductivity k = 27.6 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 60 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 1, L = 0.26, k = 27.6, dT = 60 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 27.6*1*60 / 0.26 | Answer: 6369 W

question: A surface of area 5.4 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 45 W/m^2-K to surroundings 105 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 5.4, h = 45, dT = 105 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 45*5.4*105 | Answer: 25515 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 90 m/min, feed = 0.35 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2.6 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 90, f = 0.35, d = 2.6 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*90*0.35*2.6 | Answer: 81900 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 290 mm is turned at 800 rpm with a feed of 0.24 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 290, N = 800, f = 0.24 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 290 / (0.24*800) | Answer: 1.51 min

question: A resistor of 43 ohm carries a current of 9.4 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 43, I = 9.4 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 9.4 * 43 | Answer: 404.2 V

question: Three resistors 21 ohm, 2 ohm and 67 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 21, R2 = 2, R3 = 67 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 21 + 2 + 67 | Answer: 90 ohm

question: Two resistors 104 ohm and 57 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 104, R2 = 57 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 104*57 / (104+57) | Answer: 36.82 ohm

question: A device draws 3.1 A at 235 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 235, I = 3.1 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 235 * 3.1 | Answer: 728.5 W

question: A current of 0.2 A flows through a 68 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 0.2, R = 68 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (0.2)^2 * 68 | Answer: 2.72 W

question: Two capacitors 20.6 uF and 8.7 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 20.6, C2 = 8.7 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 20.6*8.7 / (20.6+8.7) | Answer: 6.117 uF

question: A resistor 68 kohm and capacitor 18.1 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 68, C = 18.1 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (68k)(18.1u) = 1231 ms | Answer: 1231 ms

question: An inductor 159.6 mH is in series with 85 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 159.6, R = 85 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (159.6e-3) / 85 | Answer: 1.878 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 7.1 mH inductor at 390 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 7.1, f = 390 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (390)(7.1e-3) | Answer: 17.4 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 41.9 uF capacitor at 740 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 41.9, f = 740 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (740)(41.9e-6)) | Answer: 5.133 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 81 ohm, XL = 55 ohm and XC = 108 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 81, XL = 55, XC = 108 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(81^2 + (55 - 108)^2) | Answer: 96.8 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 78.9 mH and C = 6.1 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 78.9, C = 6.1 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(78.9e-3 * 6.1e-6)) | Answer: 229.4 Hz

question: A capacitor of 32.1 uF is charged to 375 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 32.1, V = 375 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*32.1e-6*(375)^2 | Answer: 2257 mJ

question: An alternating voltage has a peak value of 270 V. Find its RMS value.
solution: Given: Vp = 270 | Formula: Vrms = Vp / sqrt(2) | Substitute: Vrms = 270 / sqrt(2) | Answer: 190.9 V

question: A transformer has primary voltage 330 V with 560 primary turns and 470 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 330, N1 = 560, N2 = 470 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 330 * 470/560 | Answer: 277 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 410 V and draws an armature current of 20 A. If the armature resistance is 1.15 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 410, Ia = 20, Ra = 1.15 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 410 - 20*1.15 | Answer: 387 V

question: A 8-pole induction motor on a 50 Hz supply runs at 700 rpm. Find the slip (%).
formula: s = (Ns - N) / Ns,  Ns = 120 f / P

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 70 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.8. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 70, VL = 400, pf = 0.8 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*400*70*0.8 / 1000 | Answer: 38.8 kW

question: A load has real power 165 kW and apparent power 190 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 165, S = 190 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 165 / 190 | Answer: 0.8684

question: A machine delivers 45 kW output while drawing 177 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 45, Pi = 177 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 45/177 * 100 | Answer: 25.42 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 7 V across R1 = 11 ohm and R2 = 37 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 7, R1 = 11, R2 = 37 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 7*37 / (11+37) | Answer: 5.396 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 180 kohm and Rin = 31 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 180, Rin = 31 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 180 / 31 | Answer: 5.806

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 100 kohm and Rg = 16 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 100, Rg = 16 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 100/16 | Answer: 7.25

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 4772. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 4772 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(4772) | Answer: 36.79 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.3 m carries a central point load of 105 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.3, W = 105 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 105*4.3 / 4 | Answer: 112.9 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.8 m carries a UDL of 25 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 9.8, w = 25 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 25*(9.8)^2 / 8 | Answer: 300.1 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 5.1 m carries a point load 50 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.1, W = 50 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 50*5.1 | Answer: 255 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 3.5 m carries a UDL of 40 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.5, w = 40 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 40*(3.5)^2 / 2 | Answer: 245 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.6 m carries a point load 80 kN at distance 3.7 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 9.6, a = 3.7, W = 80 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 80*(9.6 - 3.7) / 9.6 | Answer: 49.17 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 7.1 m) carries a central point load 75 kN. With E = 200 GPa and I = 560e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=75000 N, L=7100.0 mm, E=200000 MPa, I=560e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 4.993 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 4.4 m carries a UDL of 9 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.4, w = 9 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 9*(4.4)^2 / 12 | Answer: 14.52 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 600 mm, clear cover 35 mm and main bars of diameter 20 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 600, c = 35, dia = 20 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 600 - 35 - 20/2 | Answer: 555 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 16.7 m^2 carrying a factored load of 17 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 16.7, w = 17 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 17 * 16.7 | Answer: 283.9 kN

question: For a bar of diameter 16 mm with design bond stress 2.3 MPa and steel stress 360 MPa, find the development length in mm.
solution: Given: dia = 16, tbd = 2.3, fs = 360 | Formula: Ld = phi fs / (4 tau_bd) | Substitute: Ld = 16*360 / (4*2.3) | Answer: 626.1 mm

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 4.8 m, unit weight 20 kN/m^3, phi = 28 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 11.2 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 18 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 11.2, g = 18 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (18 - 9.81)*11.2 | Answer: 91.73 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 3.6e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1.1, area = 6.8e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 3.6, i = 1.1, A = 6.8 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (3.6e-4)*1.1*(6.8e-3) | Answer: 2693 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 0.9 m, bed slope 0.006 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.026. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 2.7 m under a head of 1.1 m. Taking Cd = 0.63 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 5.4 m wide carries a discharge of 7.1 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 490 m and design speed 50 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 490, V = 50 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (50)^2 / (127*490) | Answer: 0.04017
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: For a design speed of 80 km/h with allowable superelevation 0.06 and lateral friction 0.16, find the minimum curve radius in m.
A tank of volume 770 m^3 treats a flow of 10 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 770, Q = 10 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 770 / 10 | Answer: 77 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 290 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.28 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 6 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 290, k = 0.28, t = 6 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 290*(1 - e^(-0.28*6)) | Answer: 236 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.64, rainfall intensity 30 mm/h over a catchment of 24.3 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.64, i = 30, A = 24.3 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.64*30*24.3 / 360 | Answer: 1.296 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.06 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 250 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.06, M = 250 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 250*(20+0.06)/20 | Answer: 250.8 m

question: Convert the decimal number 16 to binary.
solution: Divide 16 by 2 repeatedly, recording remainders | Reading remainders in reverse gives 10000 | Answer: 10000 (binary)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 2 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the decimal number 1377 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 1377 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 561 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the 8-bit binary number 11110111 to decimal.
solution: Binary 11110111 = sum of bit-weights | Answer: 247 (decimal)
formula: Sum each bit times its positional weight (2^i)

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 01101011 and 01000101.
solution: XOR: 00101110 | Count of 1s = 4 | Answer: 4
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 820 megabits is sent over a link of 42 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 820, B = 42 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 820 / 42 | Answer: 19.52 s

question: A link has bandwidth 51 Mbps and round-trip time 40 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 51, R = 40 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 51e6 * 40e-3 bits = 2040 kb | Answer: 2040 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.81, cache access time 1 ns and main-memory access time 160 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.81, tc = 1, tm = 160 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.81*1 + (1 - 0.81)*160 | Answer: 31.21 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 363606 elements?
solution: Given: n = 363606 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(363606)) + 1 | Answer: 19

question: An O(n^2) algorithm performs c*n^2 basic operations. If c = 1 and n = 1650, how many operations are performed?
solution: Given: n = 1650 | Formula: operations = n^2 | Substitute: = (1650)^2 | Answer: 2722500

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.006, memory access time 120 ns and page-fault service time 5 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 5 ms = 5000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.006)*120 + 0.006*5000000.0 ns | Answer: 30.12 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 0.9 m^3 at 350 kPa and 590 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 0.9, P = 350, Tk = 590 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (350e3)*0.9 / (8.314*590) | Answer: 64.22 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.35 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 13 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.35, t = 13 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.35*13) | Answer: 0.9894

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.27 /min) is to reach 70% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.27, X = 70 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.7) / 0.27 | Answer: 4.459 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.4 /min) reaches 50% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.4, X = 50 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.5 / (0.4*(1 - 0.5)) | Answer: 2.5 min

question: For a reaction with A = 8e10 /s and activation energy 65 kJ/mol at 450 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 8, Ea = 65, Tk = 450 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 8e10 * exp(-65e3 / (8.314*450)) | Answer: 2279 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.91 and bottoms xW = 0.06, with relative volatility alpha = 3.2. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.91, xw = 0.06, al = 3.2 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.91/0.09)(0.94/0.06)] / ln(3.2) | Answer: 4.355 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.83 and x = 0.47. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.83, x = 0.47 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.83/0.17) / (0.47/0.53) | Answer: 5.506

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.41 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 65 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.41, Psat = 65 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.41 * 65 | Answer: 26.65 kPa

question: A stream of 9 kg/s with specific heat 1.1 kJ/kg-K is heated through 85 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 9, cp = 1.1, dT = 85 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 9*1.1*85 | Answer: 841.5 kW

question: A reactor of volume 11.4 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 2.1 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 11.4, Q = 2.1 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 11.4 / 2.1 | Answer: 5.429 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 3.7e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 4 mm with a concentration difference of 130 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 3.7, L = 4, dC = 130 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (3.7e-9)*130 / (4e-3) | Answer: 120.3 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 9.3 min and steady-state gain 2.5. For a step input of magnitude 10, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 9.3, K = 2.5, M = 10 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 2.5 * 10 | Answer: 25 units

question: A reactor operates at a space time of 12.8 min. Find its space velocity in per hour.
solution: Given: tau = 12.8 | Formula: SV = 60 / tau  (per hour) | Substitute: SV = 60 / 12.8 | Answer: 4.688 /h

question: An aircraft wing of area 30 m^2 flies at 70 m/s (air density 0.7 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.4. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 30, V = 70, rho = 0.7, CL = 0.4 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.7*(70)^2*30*0.4 / 1000 | Answer: 20.58 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 110 m^2 flies at 100 m/s (density 0.4 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.02. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 110, V = 100, rho = 0.4, CD = 0.02 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.4*(100)^2*110*0.02 / 1000 | Answer: 4.4 kN

question: An aircraft flies at 440 m/s where the speed of sound is 310 m/s. Find the Mach number.
solution: Given: V = 440, a = 310 | Formula: M = V / a | Substitute: M = 440 / 310 | Answer: 1.419

question: A specimen under stress 160 MPa shows an elastic strain of 2.9e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 160, eps = 2.9 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 160 / (2.9e-3) MPa = 55.17 GPa | Answer: 55.17 GPa

question: A block of mass 27 kg has a volume of 1.6e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 27, V = 1.6 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 27 / (1.6e-3) | Answer: 16875 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 2100 mm is heated through 110 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 11e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 2100, dT = 110, al = 11 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 2100*11e-6*110 | Answer: 2.541 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 190 ohm, R2 = 130 ohm and R3 = 185 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 190, R2 = 130, R3 = 185 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 130*185 / 190 | Answer: 126.6 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 350 ohm and gauge factor 2.1 experiences a strain of 1050e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 350, GF = 2.1, eps = 1050 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 350*2.1*1050e-6 | Answer: 771.7 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 10.07 when the true value is 50. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10.07, true = 50 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10.07 - 50| / 50 * 100 | Answer: 79.86 %

question: Annual demand is 13500 units, ordering cost 80 per order and holding cost 30 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 13500, S = 80, H = 30 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*13500*80 / 30) | Answer: 268.3 units

question: An asset costs 400000 with salvage value 36000 after 9 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 400000, Sv = 36000, n = 9 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (400000 - 36000) / 9 | Answer: 40444 per year

question: A product sells for 80 per unit with variable cost 30 per unit and fixed costs 75000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 80, V = 30, F = 75000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 75000 / (80 - 30) | Answer: 1500 units

question: Find the present worth of 50000 received 7 years from now at an interest rate of 9% per year.
solution: Given: F = 50000, n = 7, i = 9 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 50000 / (1 + 0.09)^7 | Answer: 27352 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.98, 0.9 and 0.96 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.98, r2 = 0.9, r3 = 0.96 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.98*0.9*0.96 | Answer: 0.8467

question: A process produces 34 defective items in a batch of 1500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 34, N = 1500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 34/1500 * 1e6 | Answer: 22667 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = 5x^3 - 2x^2 - 3x + 8 evaluated at x = 3.
For f(x) = -x^3 + 3x^2 + 8x + 6, find f''(x) at x = -3.

question: Find the larger real root of 3x^2 + 3x - 3 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[-9, 6], [1, 4]].

question: Find the determinant of [[-1, 1, -4], [6, 0, 6], [3, -6, 1]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: 120

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[-4, 0], [-6, 0]].
solution: Trace tr = -4, Determinant = 0 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 0

question: Solve for x: 3x + -5y = 8 and 1x + -4y = -5.

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 14, 26, 14, 79, 56.
solution: Sum = 189 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 37.8 | Answer: 37.8

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 25, 44, 48, 18, 38.
solution: Mean = 34.6 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 12.72

question: Find the slope of the line through (2, 9) and (-9, 9).
solution: Given: x1 = 2, y1 = 9, x2 = -9, y2 = 9 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (9 - 9) / (-9 - 2) | Answer: 0

question: Find the distance between the points (-6, -4) and (-6, 5).
solution: Given: x1 = -6, y1 = -4, x2 = -6, y2 = 5 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((0)^2 + (9)^2) | Answer: 9 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (0,-4), (3,-2), (4,8).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 14 sq units

question: Evaluate the number of combinations C(9, 9).
solution: Given: n = 9, r = 9 | Formula: C(n, r) = n! / (r! (n - r)!) | Substitute: C(9, 9) = 9! / (9! * 0!) | Answer: 1

question: Find the 9th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 7 and common difference -2.
solution: Given: a = 7, d = -2, n = 9 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = 7 + (9 - 1)*-2 | Answer: -9

question: Find the sum of the first 13 terms of an AP with first term 5 and common difference -5.
solution: Given: a = 5, d = -5, n = 13 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 13/2 [2*5 + (13-1)*-5] | Answer: -325

question: Find the 6th term of a geometric progression with first term 1 and common ratio 2.
solution: Given: a = 1, r = 2, n = 6 | Formula: a_n = a r^(n-1) | Substitute: a_n = 1 * 2^(6-1) | Answer: 32

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 32500 at 11.7% per annum for 6 years.
solution: Given: P = 32500, R = 11.7, Tt = 6 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 32500 * 11.7 * 6 / 100 | Answer: 22815 currency units

question: Find the amount when 4000 is invested at 4.5% per annum compounded annually for 4 years.
solution: Given: P = 4000, R = 4.5, Tt = 4 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 4000 * (1 + 4.5/100)^4 | Answer: 477 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (-2, -3, 4) and (-4, -4, -6).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (-3, -4, 6) and (4, -5, -5).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 59.51

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (1, 1, 3) and (2, -2, 5).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 38.07 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number -5 + -4i.
solution: Given: a = -5, b = -4 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((-5)^2 + (-4)^2) | Answer: 6.403

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number 5 + 1i.
solution: Given: a = 5, b = 1 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(1, 5) | Answer: 11.31 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = 4x^3 + 5x^2 + 6x + 2 at x = 1.
solution: Given: a = 4, b = 5, c = 6, d = 2, x0 = 1 | Formula: f(x0) = a x0^3 + b x0^2 + c x0 + d | Substitute: f(1) = 4(1)^3 + 5(1)^2 + 6(1) + 2 | Answer: 17

question: Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-125 with initial guess x0=13, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.1 and ordinates 15, 6, 18, 4, 3, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 42 and 360.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 42 and 360 | Answer: GCD = 6

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 64 and 40.
solution: Given: a = 64, b = 40 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 64*40 / 8 | Answer: 320
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 19 mm carries an axial tensile load of 117 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 16 mm and length 900 mm carries an axial load of 48 kN. Take E = 200 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 34 mm transmits a torque of 200 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 34, Tt = 200 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(200*1000) / (pi*(34)^3) | Answer: 25.92 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 53 mm and length 1400 mm carries a torque of 1000 N-m. With G = 45 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (53)^4 / 32 = 774646 mm^4 | theta = (1000*1000)(1400) / (45000 * 774646) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 2.301 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 146 mm wide and 200 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 146, h = 200 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 146*(200)^2 / 6 | Answer: 973333 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (70 mm x 90 mm) carries a bending moment of 2 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (30 mm x 150 mm) has effective length 1700 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 750 MPa is designed for a working stress of 220 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 750, sw = 220 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 750 / 220 | Answer: 3.409

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 950 mm and wall thickness 16 mm carries an internal pressure of 1.3 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 950, t = 16, P = 1.3 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 1.3*950 / (2*16) | Answer: 38.59 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 1000 K and 440 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 1000, Tc = 440 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 440/1000) * 100 | Answer: 56 %

question: A refrigerator works between 255 K (cold) and 322 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 255, Th = 322 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 255 / (322 - 255) | Answer: 3.806

question: A heat pump operates between 283 K and 318 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 283, Th = 318 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 318 / (318 - 283) | Answer: 9.086

question: 1.6 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 105 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1.6, dT = 105 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 1.6 * 0.718 * 105 | Answer: 120.6 kJ

question: 7.5 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 85 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 7.5, dT = 85 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 7.5 * 1.005 * 85 | Answer: 640.7 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 3.5 m^3 at 310 K with mass 4 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 3.5, Tk = 310, m = 4 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 4*0.287*310 / 3.5 | Answer: 101.7 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 2.4 kg of air expands isothermally at 430 K from volume V1 to 4*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.4, Tk = 430, ratio = 4 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 2.4*0.287*430*ln(4) | Answer: 410.6 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 4.2 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.14 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 4.2, D = 0.14 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*4.2*0.14 / 0.001 | Answer: 588000

question: Water flows at 3.5 m/s through a pipe of diameter 290 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 8.1 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 8.1 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*8.1 / 1000 | Answer: 79.46 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 9.4 m. Taking Cv = 0.95, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 9.4, cv = 0.95 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.95*sqrt(2*9.81*9.4) | Answer: 12.9 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 240 mm) water flows at 1 m/s. It contracts to diameter 90 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 240, d2 = 90, V1 = 1 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 1*(240/90)^2 | Answer: 7.111 m/s

question: Water flows at 3.8 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.13 m and length 290 m. With friction factor f = 0.023, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 36 teeth drives a gear of 84 teeth. If the pinion runs at 750 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 36, z2 = 84, N1 = 750 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 750*36 / 84 | Answer: 321.4 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 260 mm rotates at 1450 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 260, N = 1450 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.26)*1450 / 60 | Answer: 19.74 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 31.1 kW at 900 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 31.1, N = 900 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(31.1*1000) / (2*pi*900) | Answer: 330 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 1.3 kg rotates at radius 0.17 m at 300 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 6600 N/m and mass 13.1 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 6600, m = 13.1 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(6600/13.1) | Answer: 3.572 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 6.3 m^2 and thickness 0.17 m has conductivity k = 7.3 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 165 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 6.3, L = 0.17, k = 7.3, dT = 165 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 7.3*6.3*165 / 0.17 | Answer: 44637 W

question: A surface of area 2.3 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 175 W/m^2-K to surroundings 40 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 2.3, h = 175, dT = 40 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 175*2.3*40 | Answer: 16100 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 140 m/min, feed = 0.43 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2.3 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 140, f = 0.43, d = 2.3 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*140*0.43*2.3 | Answer: 138460 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 290 mm is turned at 750 rpm with a feed of 0.19 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 290, N = 750, f = 0.19 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 290 / (0.19*750) | Answer: 2.035 min

question: A resistor of 22 ohm carries a current of 8 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 22, I = 8 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 8 * 22 | Answer: 176 V

question: Three resistors 28 ohm, 37 ohm and 37 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 28, R2 = 37, R3 = 37 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 28 + 37 + 37 | Answer: 102 ohm

question: Two resistors 35 ohm and 84 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 35, R2 = 84 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 35*84 / (35+84) | Answer: 24.71 ohm

question: A device draws 14.3 A at 85 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 85, I = 14.3 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 85 * 14.3 | Answer: 1216 W

question: A current of 2.3 A flows through a 94 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 2.3, R = 94 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (2.3)^2 * 94 | Answer: 497.3 W

question: Two capacitors 40 uF and 3.2 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 40, C2 = 3.2 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 40*3.2 / (40+3.2) | Answer: 2.963 uF

question: A resistor 80 kohm and capacitor 2.8 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 80, C = 2.8 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (80k)(2.8u) = 224 ms | Answer: 224 ms

question: An inductor 407.7 mH is in series with 65 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 407.7, R = 65 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (407.7e-3) / 65 | Answer: 6.272 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 34.5 mH inductor at 310 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 34.5, f = 310 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (310)(34.5e-3) | Answer: 67.2 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 7.5 uF capacitor at 680 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 7.5, f = 680 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (680)(7.5e-6)) | Answer: 31.21 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 49 ohm, XL = 112 ohm and XC = 64 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 49, XL = 112, XC = 64 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(49^2 + (112 - 64)^2) | Answer: 68.59 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 19 mH and C = 2 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 19, C = 2 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(19e-3 * 2e-6)) | Answer: 816.4 Hz

question: A capacitor of 43.8 uF is charged to 215 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 43.8, V = 215 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*43.8e-6*(215)^2 | Answer: 1012 mJ

question: An alternating voltage has a peak value of 10 V. Find its RMS value.
solution: Given: Vp = 10 | Formula: Vrms = Vp / sqrt(2) | Substitute: Vrms = 10 / sqrt(2) | Answer: 7.071 V

question: A transformer has primary voltage 190 V with 950 primary turns and 240 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 190, N1 = 950, N2 = 240 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 190 * 240/950 | Answer: 48 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 180 V and draws an armature current of 14 A. If the armature resistance is 1.13 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 180, Ia = 14, Ra = 1.13 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 180 - 14*1.13 | Answer: 164.2 V

question: A 8-pole induction motor on a 60 Hz supply runs at 720 rpm. Find the slip (%).
formula: s = (Ns - N) / Ns,  Ns = 120 f / P

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 85 A at 433 V (line) with a power factor of 0.86. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 85, VL = 433, pf = 0.86 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*433*85*0.86 / 1000 | Answer: 54.82 kW

question: A load has real power 85 kW and apparent power 215 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 85, S = 215 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 85 / 215 | Answer: 0.3953

question: A machine delivers 30 kW output while drawing 77 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 30, Pi = 77 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 30/77 * 100 | Answer: 38.96 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 16 V across R1 = 8 ohm and R2 = 10 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 16, R1 = 8, R2 = 10 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 16*10 / (8+10) | Answer: 8.889 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 120 kohm and Rin = 8 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 120, Rin = 8 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 120 / 8 | Answer: 15

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 180 kohm and Rg = 35 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 180, Rg = 35 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 180/35 | Answer: 6.143

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 7557. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 7557 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(7557) | Answer: 38.78 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 3.8 m carries a central point load of 45 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.8, W = 45 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 45*3.8 / 4 | Answer: 42.75 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 4 m carries a UDL of 30 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4, w = 30 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 30*(4)^2 / 8 | Answer: 60 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 2.3 m carries a point load 80 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 2.3, W = 80 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 80*2.3 | Answer: 184 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 3.3 m carries a UDL of 4 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.3, w = 4 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 4*(3.3)^2 / 2 | Answer: 21.78 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.7 m carries a point load 95 kN at distance 1.7 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 9.7, a = 1.7, W = 95 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 95*(9.7 - 1.7) / 9.7 | Answer: 78.35 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 6.5 m) carries a central point load 45 kN. With E = 200 GPa and I = 120e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=45000 N, L=6500.0 mm, E=200000 MPa, I=120e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 10.73 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 6.5 m carries a UDL of 9 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6.5, w = 9 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 9*(6.5)^2 / 12 | Answer: 31.69 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 570 mm, clear cover 35 mm and main bars of diameter 12 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 570, c = 35, dia = 12 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 570 - 35 - 12/2 | Answer: 529 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 36.8 m^2 carrying a factored load of 14.3 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 36.8, w = 14.3 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 14.3 * 36.8 | Answer: 526.2 kN

question: For a bar of diameter 12 mm with design bond stress 1.9 MPa and steel stress 435 MPa, find the development length in mm.
solution: Given: dia = 12, tbd = 1.9, fs = 435 | Formula: Ld = phi fs / (4 tau_bd) | Substitute: Ld = 12*435 / (4*1.9) | Answer: 686.8 mm

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 5.7 m, unit weight 18 kN/m^3, phi = 29 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 9.3 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 21 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 9.3, g = 21 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (21 - 9.81)*9.3 | Answer: 104.1 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 5e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1.1, area = 3.5e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 5, i = 1.1, A = 3.5 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (5e-4)*1.1*(3.5e-3) | Answer: 1925 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.3 m, bed slope 0.003 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.021. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 4.8 m under a head of 0.9 m. Taking Cd = 0.61 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 5.5 m wide carries a discharge of 5.5 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 300 m and design speed 100 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 300, V = 100 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (100)^2 / (127*300) | Answer: 0.2625
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: For a design speed of 65 km/h with allowable superelevation 0.07 and lateral friction 0.16, find the minimum curve radius in m.
A tank of volume 600 m^3 treats a flow of 55 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 600, Q = 55 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 600 / 55 | Answer: 10.91 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 150 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.3 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 5 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 150, k = 0.3, t = 5 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 150*(1 - e^(-0.3*5)) | Answer: 116.5 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.62, rainfall intensity 80 mm/h over a catchment of 27.1 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.62, i = 80, A = 27.1 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.62*80*27.1 / 360 | Answer: 3.734 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.02 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 410 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.02, M = 410 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 410*(30+0.02)/30 | Answer: 410.3 m

question: Convert the decimal number 107 to binary.
solution: Divide 107 by 2 repeatedly, recording remainders | Reading remainders in reverse gives 1101011 | Answer: 1101011 (binary)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 2 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the decimal number 899 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 899 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 383 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the 8-bit binary number 01110011 to decimal.
solution: Binary 01110011 = sum of bit-weights | Answer: 115 (decimal)
formula: Sum each bit times its positional weight (2^i)

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 11010110 and 01011011.
solution: XOR: 10001101 | Count of 1s = 4 | Answer: 4
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 320 megabits is sent over a link of 80 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 320, B = 80 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 320 / 80 | Answer: 4 s

question: A link has bandwidth 21 Mbps and round-trip time 70 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 21, R = 70 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 21e6 * 70e-3 bits = 1470 kb | Answer: 1470 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.85, cache access time 7 ns and main-memory access time 110 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.85, tc = 7, tm = 110 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.85*7 + (1 - 0.85)*110 | Answer: 22.45 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 444469 elements?
solution: Given: n = 444469 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(444469)) + 1 | Answer: 19

question: An O(n^2) algorithm performs c*n^2 basic operations. If c = 1 and n = 2340, how many operations are performed?
solution: Given: n = 2340 | Formula: operations = n^2 | Substitute: = (2340)^2 | Answer: 5475600

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.019, memory access time 80 ns and page-fault service time 6 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 6 ms = 6000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.019)*80 + 0.019*6000000.0 ns | Answer: 114.1 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 1.3 m^3 at 140 kPa and 500 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 1.3, P = 140, Tk = 500 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (140e3)*1.3 / (8.314*500) | Answer: 43.78 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.1 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 6 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.1, t = 6 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.1*6) | Answer: 0.4512

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.15 /min) is to reach 50% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.15, X = 50 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.5) / 0.15 | Answer: 4.621 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.34 /min) reaches 70% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.34, X = 70 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.7 / (0.34*(1 - 0.7)) | Answer: 6.863 min

question: For a reaction with A = 7e10 /s and activation energy 50 kJ/mol at 480 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 7, Ea = 50, Tk = 480 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 7e10 * exp(-50e3 / (8.314*480)) | Answer: 253392 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.97 and bottoms xW = 0.09, with relative volatility alpha = 3.3. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.97, xw = 0.09, al = 3.3 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.97/0.03)(0.91/0.09)] / ln(3.3) | Answer: 4.849 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.7 and x = 0.25. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.7, x = 0.25 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.7/0.3) / (0.25/0.75) | Answer: 7

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.71 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 60 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.71, Psat = 60 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.71 * 60 | Answer: 42.6 kPa

question: A stream of 4.6 kg/s with specific heat 1.6 kJ/kg-K is heated through 95 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 4.6, cp = 1.6, dT = 95 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 4.6*1.6*95 | Answer: 699.2 kW

question: A reactor of volume 6.9 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 4.8 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 6.9, Q = 4.8 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 6.9 / 4.8 | Answer: 1.438 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 6.2e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 2 mm with a concentration difference of 80 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 6.2, L = 2, dC = 80 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (6.2e-9)*80 / (2e-3) | Answer: 248 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 6 min and steady-state gain 2.6. For a step input of magnitude 18, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 6, K = 2.6, M = 18 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 2.6 * 18 | Answer: 46.8 units

question: A reactor operates at a space time of 5.4 min. Find its space velocity in per hour.
solution: Given: tau = 5.4 | Formula: SV = 60 / tau  (per hour) | Substitute: SV = 60 / 5.4 | Answer: 11.11 /h

question: An aircraft wing of area 20 m^2 flies at 80 m/s (air density 1.225 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.7. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 20, V = 80, rho = 1.225, CL = 0.7 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1.225*(80)^2*20*0.7 / 1000 | Answer: 54.88 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 35 m^2 flies at 250 m/s (density 0.7 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.06. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 35, V = 250, rho = 0.7, CD = 0.06 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.7*(250)^2*35*0.06 / 1000 | Answer: 45.94 kN

question: An aircraft flies at 500 m/s where the speed of sound is 340 m/s. Find the Mach number.
solution: Given: V = 500, a = 340 | Formula: M = V / a | Substitute: M = 500 / 340 | Answer: 1.471

question: A specimen under stress 200 MPa shows an elastic strain of 2.5e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 200, eps = 2.5 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 200 / (2.5e-3) MPa = 80 GPa | Answer: 80 GPa

question: A block of mass 50 kg has a volume of 5.2e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 50, V = 5.2 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 50 / (5.2e-3) | Answer: 9615 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 1800 mm is heated through 115 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 12e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 1800, dT = 115, al = 12 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 1800*12e-6*115 | Answer: 2.484 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 165 ohm, R2 = 50 ohm and R3 = 420 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 165, R2 = 50, R3 = 420 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 50*420 / 165 | Answer: 127.3 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 120 ohm and gauge factor 2.2 experiences a strain of 950e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 120, GF = 2.2, eps = 950 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 120*2.2*950e-6 | Answer: 250.8 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 9.68 when the true value is 100. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.68, true = 100 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.68 - 100| / 100 * 100 | Answer: 90.32 %

question: Annual demand is 17000 units, ordering cost 270 per order and holding cost 2 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 17000, S = 270, H = 2 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*17000*270 / 2) | Answer: 2142 units

question: An asset costs 320000 with salvage value 26000 after 15 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 320000, Sv = 26000, n = 15 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (320000 - 26000) / 15 | Answer: 19600 per year

question: A product sells for 470 per unit with variable cost 40 per unit and fixed costs 125000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 470, V = 40, F = 125000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 125000 / (470 - 40) | Answer: 290.7 units

question: Find the present worth of 140000 received 7 years from now at an interest rate of 9% per year.
solution: Given: F = 140000, n = 7, i = 9 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 140000 / (1 + 0.09)^7 | Answer: 76585 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.94, 0.93 and 0.9 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.94, r2 = 0.93, r3 = 0.9 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.94*0.93*0.9 | Answer: 0.7868

question: A process produces 9 defective items in a batch of 17500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 9, N = 17500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 9/17500 * 1e6 | Answer: 514.3 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -x^3 + 6x^2 - 2x + 1 evaluated at x = 4.
For f(x) = 2x^3 + 5x^2 + 4x + 5, find f''(x) at x = -4.
Evaluate the definite integral of (6x - 5) dx from x = 0 to x = 3.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = 0x^3/3 + 6x^2/2 + -5x | Evaluate F(3) - F(0) | Answer: 12
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 5x^2 - x - 6 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[-7, 0], [-9, 2]].
solution: Given: a = -7, b = 0, c = -9, d = 2 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (-7)(2) - (0)(-9) | Answer: -14

question: Find the determinant of [[-1, -4, 0], [5, 3, -2], [0, 2, 4]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: 64

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[2, -4], [-7, -2]].
solution: Trace tr = 0, Determinant = -32 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 5.657

question: Solve for x: 0x + 3y = -7 and 6x + -3y = -9.
solution: Determinant = 0*-3 - 3*6 = -18 | x = (e d - b f) / det = -2.667 | Answer: x = -2.667
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 66, 48, 22, 100, 34.
solution: Sum = 270 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 54 | Answer: 54

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 47, 19, 14, 14, 46.
solution: Mean = 28 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 17.01

question: Find the slope of the line through (9, 4) and (3, -3).
solution: Given: x1 = 9, y1 = 4, x2 = 3, y2 = -3 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (-3 - 4) / (3 - 9) | Answer: 1.167

question: Find the distance between the points (-2, -4) and (1, 1).
solution: Given: x1 = -2, y1 = -4, x2 = 1, y2 = 1 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((3)^2 + (5)^2) | Answer: 5.831 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (-6,3), (-1,6), (5,-3).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 31.5 sq units

question: Evaluate the number of combinations C(15, 8).
solution: Given: n = 15, r = 8 | Formula: C(n, r) = n! / (r! (n - r)!) | Substitute: C(15, 8) = 15! / (8! * 7!) | Answer: 6435

question: Find the 17th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -18 and common difference 1.
solution: Given: a = -18, d = 1, n = 17 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -18 + (17 - 1)*1 | Answer: -2

question: Find the sum of the first 24 terms of an AP with first term -15 and common difference 2.
solution: Given: a = -15, d = 2, n = 24 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 24/2 [2*-15 + (24-1)*2] | Answer: 192

question: Find the 3th term of a geometric progression with first term 6 and common ratio 3.
solution: Given: a = 6, r = 3, n = 3 | Formula: a_n = a r^(n-1) | Substitute: a_n = 6 * 3^(3-1) | Answer: 54

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 47000 at 6.5% per annum for 2 years.
solution: Given: P = 47000, R = 6.5, Tt = 2 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 47000 * 6.5 * 2 / 100 | Answer: 6110 currency units

question: Find the amount when 20500 is invested at 6.4% per annum compounded annually for 5 years.
solution: Given: P = 20500, R = 6.4, Tt = 5 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 20500 * (1 + 6.4/100)^5 | Answer: 27955 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (-8, 2, -7) and (4, 2, -5).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (-6, -6, -2) and (4, 6, -4).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 49.64

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (-2, 1, -1) and (-2, 1, 4).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 84.89 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number 10 + -10i.
solution: Given: a = 10, b = -10 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((10)^2 + (-10)^2) | Answer: 14.14

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number 8 + -11i.
solution: Given: a = 8, b = -11 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(-11, 8) | Answer: -53.97 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -x^3 - 7x^2 + x - 4 at x = 5.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-81 with initial guess x0=13, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=0.7 and ordinates 7, 15, 15, 0, 2, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 295 and 167.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 295 and 167 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 33 and 57.
solution: Given: a = 33, b = 57 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 33*57 / 3 | Answer: 627
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 28 mm carries an axial tensile load of 63 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 37 mm and length 1300 mm carries an axial load of 56 kN. Take E = 70 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 35 mm transmits a torque of 900 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 35, Tt = 900 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(900*1000) / (pi*(35)^3) | Answer: 106.9 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 53 mm and length 600 mm carries a torque of 300 N-m. With G = 45 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (53)^4 / 32 = 774646 mm^4 | theta = (300*1000)(600) / (45000 * 774646) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 0.2959 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 46 mm wide and 170 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 46, h = 170 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 46*(170)^2 / 6 | Answer: 221567 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (60 mm x 170 mm) carries a bending moment of 25 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (76 mm x 150 mm) has effective length 1700 mm and E = 200 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 750 MPa is designed for a working stress of 170 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 750, sw = 170 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 750 / 170 | Answer: 4.412

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 650 mm and wall thickness 15 mm carries an internal pressure of 1.6 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 650, t = 15, P = 1.6 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 1.6*650 / (2*15) | Answer: 34.67 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 1120 K and 320 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 1120, Tc = 320 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 320/1120) * 100 | Answer: 71.43 %

question: A refrigerator works between 263 K (cold) and 322 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 263, Th = 322 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 263 / (322 - 263) | Answer: 4.458

question: A heat pump operates between 271 K and 326 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 271, Th = 326 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 326 / (326 - 271) | Answer: 5.927

question: 3 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 20 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3, dT = 20 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 3 * 0.718 * 20 | Answer: 43.08 kJ

question: 6.4 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 200 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 6.4, dT = 200 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 6.4 * 1.005 * 200 | Answer: 1286 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 0.8 m^3 at 330 K with mass 4.5 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 0.8, Tk = 330, m = 4.5 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 4.5*0.287*330 / 0.8 | Answer: 532.7 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 2.7 kg of air expands isothermally at 480 K from volume V1 to 4*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.7, Tk = 480, ratio = 4 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 2.7*0.287*480*ln(4) | Answer: 515.6 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 1.9 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.15 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 1.9, D = 0.15 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*1.9*0.15 / 0.001 | Answer: 285000

question: Water flows at 3.2 m/s through a pipe of diameter 70 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 11.9 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 11.9 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*11.9 / 1000 | Answer: 116.7 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 16.7 m. Taking Cv = 0.99, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 16.7, cv = 0.99 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.99*sqrt(2*9.81*16.7) | Answer: 17.92 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 270 mm) water flows at 0.9 m/s. It contracts to diameter 50 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 270, d2 = 50, V1 = 0.9 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 0.9*(270/50)^2 | Answer: 26.24 m/s

question: Water flows at 2.7 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.48 m and length 70 m. With friction factor f = 0.04, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 27 teeth drives a gear of 91 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1300 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 27, z2 = 91, N1 = 1300 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1300*27 / 91 | Answer: 385.7 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 440 mm rotates at 850 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 440, N = 850 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.44)*850 / 60 | Answer: 19.58 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 41.3 kW at 1450 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 41.3, N = 1450 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(41.3*1000) / (2*pi*1450) | Answer: 272 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 7.3 kg rotates at radius 0.46 m at 1100 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 16900 N/m and mass 15.8 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 16900, m = 15.8 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(16900/15.8) | Answer: 5.205 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 4.6 m^2 and thickness 0.2 m has conductivity k = 27.6 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 200 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 4.6, L = 0.2, k = 27.6, dT = 200 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 27.6*4.6*200 / 0.2 | Answer: 126960 W

question: A surface of area 5.3 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 115 W/m^2-K to surroundings 125 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 5.3, h = 115, dT = 125 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 115*5.3*125 | Answer: 76188 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 170 m/min, feed = 0.14 mm/rev, depth of cut = 0.8 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 170, f = 0.14, d = 0.8 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*170*0.14*0.8 | Answer: 19040 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 290 mm is turned at 900 rpm with a feed of 0.39 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 290, N = 900, f = 0.39 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 290 / (0.39*900) | Answer: 0.8262 min

question: A resistor of 2 ohm carries a current of 5.1 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 2, I = 5.1 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 5.1 * 2 | Answer: 10.2 V

question: Three resistors 64 ohm, 84 ohm and 78 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
