question: A rectangular beam section is 75 mm wide and 90 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 75, h = 90 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 75*(90)^2 / 6 | Answer: 101250 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (90 mm x 260 mm) carries a bending moment of 17 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (80 mm x 110 mm) has effective length 3600 mm and E = 200 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 350 MPa is designed for a working stress of 120 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 350, sw = 120 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 350 / 120 | Answer: 2.917

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1150 mm and wall thickness 13 mm carries an internal pressure of 1.7 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1150, t = 13, P = 1.7 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 1.7*1150 / (2*13) | Answer: 75.19 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 740 K and 450 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 740, Tc = 450 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 450/740) * 100 | Answer: 39.19 %

question: A refrigerator works between 264 K (cold) and 316 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 264, Th = 316 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 264 / (316 - 264) | Answer: 5.077

question: A heat pump operates between 261 K and 318 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 261, Th = 318 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 318 / (318 - 261) | Answer: 5.579

question: 2.7 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 190 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.7, dT = 190 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 2.7 * 0.718 * 190 | Answer: 368.3 kJ

question: 4.6 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 75 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.6, dT = 75 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 4.6 * 1.005 * 75 | Answer: 346.7 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 3.1 m^3 at 420 K with mass 2.6 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 3.1, Tk = 420, m = 2.6 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 2.6*0.287*420 / 3.1 | Answer: 101.1 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 1.5 kg of air expands isothermally at 400 K from volume V1 to 5*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1.5, Tk = 400, ratio = 5 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 1.5*0.287*400*ln(5) | Answer: 277.1 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 0.9 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.38 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 0.9, D = 0.38 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*0.9*0.38 / 0.001 | Answer: 342000

question: Water flows at 3.5 m/s through a pipe of diameter 100 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 3.4 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 3.4 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*3.4 / 1000 | Answer: 33.35 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 13.7 m. Taking Cv = 0.97, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 13.7, cv = 0.97 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.97*sqrt(2*9.81*13.7) | Answer: 15.9 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 370 mm) water flows at 1.6 m/s. It contracts to diameter 130 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
Water flows at 3.4 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.5 m and length 110 m. With friction factor f = 0.021, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 29 teeth drives a gear of 59 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1300 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 29, z2 = 59, N1 = 1300 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1300*29 / 59 | Answer: 639 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 540 mm rotates at 200 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 540, N = 200 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.54)*200 / 60 | Answer: 5.655 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 47.2 kW at 1250 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 47.2, N = 1250 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(47.2*1000) / (2*pi*1250) | Answer: 360.6 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 6.3 kg rotates at radius 0.48 m at 400 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 17500 N/m and mass 12.1 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 17500, m = 12.1 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(17500/12.1) | Answer: 6.053 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 8.7 m^2 and thickness 0.16 m has conductivity k = 26.2 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 95 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 8.7, L = 0.16, k = 26.2, dT = 95 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 26.2*8.7*95 / 0.16 | Answer: 135339 W

question: A surface of area 4.6 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 165 W/m^2-K to surroundings 35 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 4.6, h = 165, dT = 35 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 165*4.6*35 | Answer: 26565 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 100 m/min, feed = 0.3 mm/rev, depth of cut = 1 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 100, f = 0.3, d = 1 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*100*0.3*1 | Answer: 30000 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 500 mm is turned at 500 rpm with a feed of 0.34 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 500, N = 500, f = 0.34 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 500 / (0.34*500) | Answer: 2.941 min

question: A resistor of 109 ohm carries a current of 7.7 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 109, I = 7.7 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 7.7 * 109 | Answer: 839.3 V

question: Three resistors 42 ohm, 93 ohm and 48 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 42, R2 = 93, R3 = 48 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 42 + 93 + 48 | Answer: 183 ohm

question: Two resistors 58 ohm and 73 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 58, R2 = 73 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 58*73 / (58+73) | Answer: 32.32 ohm

question: A device draws 11.7 A at 75 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 75, I = 11.7 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 75 * 11.7 | Answer: 877.5 W

question: A current of 10.9 A flows through a 37 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 10.9, R = 37 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (10.9)^2 * 37 | Answer: 4396 W

question: Two capacitors 4.8 uF and 8.8 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 4.8, C2 = 8.8 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 4.8*8.8 / (4.8+8.8) | Answer: 3.106 uF

question: A resistor 93 kohm and capacitor 11 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 93, C = 11 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (93k)(11u) = 1023 ms | Answer: 1023 ms

question: An inductor 433.1 mH is in series with 165 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 433.1, R = 165 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (433.1e-3) / 165 | Answer: 2.625 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 9.9 mH inductor at 320 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 9.9, f = 320 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (320)(9.9e-3) | Answer: 19.91 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 15.1 uF capacitor at 610 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 15.1, f = 610 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (610)(15.1e-6)) | Answer: 17.28 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 12 ohm, XL = 107 ohm and XC = 72 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 12, XL = 107, XC = 72 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(12^2 + (107 - 72)^2) | Answer: 37 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 87.1 mH and C = 4.3 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 87.1, C = 4.3 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(87.1e-3 * 4.3e-6)) | Answer: 260.1 Hz

question: A capacitor of 76.6 uF is charged to 115 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 76.6, V = 115 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*76.6e-6*(115)^2 | Answer: 506.5 mJ

question: An alternating voltage has a peak value of 190 V. Find its RMS value.
solution: Given: Vp = 190 | Formula: Vrms = Vp / sqrt(2) | Substitute: Vrms = 190 / sqrt(2) | Answer: 134.4 V

question: A transformer has primary voltage 340 V with 590 primary turns and 260 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 340, N1 = 590, N2 = 260 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 340 * 260/590 | Answer: 149.8 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 210 V and draws an armature current of 29 A. If the armature resistance is 1.42 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 210, Ia = 29, Ra = 1.42 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 210 - 29*1.42 | Answer: 168.8 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 45 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.71. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 45, VL = 400, pf = 0.71 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*400*45*0.71 / 1000 | Answer: 22.14 kW

question: A load has real power 10 kW and apparent power 90 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 10, S = 90 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 10 / 90 | Answer: 0.1111

question: A machine delivers 120 kW output while drawing 182 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 120, Pi = 182 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 120/182 * 100 | Answer: 65.93 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 6 V across R1 = 43 ohm and R2 = 7 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 6, R1 = 43, R2 = 7 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 6*7 / (43+7) | Answer: 0.84 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 140 kohm and Rin = 46 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 140, Rin = 46 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 140 / 46 | Answer: 3.043

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 170 kohm and Rg = 9 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 170, Rg = 9 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 170/9 | Answer: 19.89

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 5738. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 5738 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(5738) | Answer: 37.59 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.9 m carries a central point load of 70 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.9, W = 70 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 70*4.9 / 4 | Answer: 85.75 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 7.7 m carries a UDL of 55 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7.7, w = 55 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 55*(7.7)^2 / 8 | Answer: 407.6 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 5.2 m carries a point load 25 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.2, W = 25 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 25*5.2 | Answer: 130 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 4.4 m carries a UDL of 6 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.4, w = 6 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 6*(4.4)^2 / 2 | Answer: 58.08 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 5.9 m carries a point load 60 kN at distance 1.5 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 5.9, a = 1.5, W = 60 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 60*(5.9 - 1.5) / 5.9 | Answer: 44.75 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 8 m) carries a central point load 65 kN. With E = 30 GPa and I = 190e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=65000 N, L=8000.0 mm, E=30000 MPa, I=190e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 121.6 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 6.2 m carries a UDL of 39 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6.2, w = 39 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 39*(6.2)^2 / 12 | Answer: 124.9 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 620 mm, clear cover 30 mm and main bars of diameter 25 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 620, c = 30, dia = 25 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 620 - 30 - 25/2 | Answer: 577.5 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 23.4 m^2 carrying a factored load of 14.6 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 23.4, w = 14.6 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 14.6 * 23.4 | Answer: 341.6 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 5.1 m, unit weight 19 kN/m^3, phi = 29 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 11.5 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 21 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 11.5, g = 21 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (21 - 9.81)*11.5 | Answer: 128.7 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 8.8e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.3, area = 5.7e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 8.8, i = 0.3, A = 5.7 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (8.8e-4)*0.3*(5.7e-3) | Answer: 1505 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.1 m, bed slope 0.01 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.012. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 4.2 m under a head of 0.8 m. Taking Cd = 0.64 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 5.5 m wide carries a discharge of 22.3 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 530 m and design speed 50 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 530, V = 50 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (50)^2 / (127*530) | Answer: 0.03714
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: For a design speed of 55 km/h with allowable superelevation 0.07 and lateral friction 0.16, find the minimum curve radius in m.
A tank of volume 890 m^3 treats a flow of 75 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 890, Q = 75 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 890 / 75 | Answer: 11.87 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 230 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.21 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 6 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 230, k = 0.21, t = 6 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 230*(1 - e^(-0.21*6)) | Answer: 164.8 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.79, rainfall intensity 120 mm/h over a catchment of 55.2 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.79, i = 120, A = 55.2 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.79*120*55.2 / 360 | Answer: 14.54 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.03 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 350 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.03, M = 350 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 350*(20+0.03)/20 | Answer: 350.5 m

question: Convert the decimal number 60 to binary.
solution: Divide 60 by 2 repeatedly, recording remainders | Reading remainders in reverse gives 111100 | Answer: 111100 (binary)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 2 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the decimal number 2842 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 2842 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: B1A (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the 8-bit binary number 01000010 to decimal.
solution: Binary 01000010 = sum of bit-weights | Answer: 66 (decimal)
formula: Sum each bit times its positional weight (2^i)

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 10100000 and 00010110.
solution: XOR: 10110110 | Count of 1s = 5 | Answer: 5
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 120 megabits is sent over a link of 75 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 120, B = 75 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 120 / 75 | Answer: 1.6 s

question: A link has bandwidth 14 Mbps and round-trip time 30 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 14, R = 30 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 14e6 * 30e-3 bits = 420 kb | Answer: 420 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.92, cache access time 4 ns and main-memory access time 150 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.92, tc = 4, tm = 150 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.92*4 + (1 - 0.92)*150 | Answer: 15.68 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 670962 elements?
solution: Given: n = 670962 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(670962)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: An O(n^2) algorithm performs c*n^2 basic operations. If c = 1 and n = 590, how many operations are performed?
solution: Given: n = 590 | Formula: operations = n^2 | Substitute: = (590)^2 | Answer: 348100

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.014, memory access time 120 ns and page-fault service time 3 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 3 ms = 3000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.014)*120 + 0.014*3000000.0 ns | Answer: 42.12 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 1.1 m^3 at 210 kPa and 530 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 1.1, P = 210, Tk = 530 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (210e3)*1.1 / (8.314*530) | Answer: 52.42 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.26 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 6 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.26, t = 6 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.26*6) | Answer: 0.7899

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.24 /min) is to reach 80% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.24, X = 80 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.8) / 0.24 | Answer: 6.706 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.21 /min) reaches 60% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.21, X = 60 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.6 / (0.21*(1 - 0.6)) | Answer: 7.143 min

question: For a reaction with A = 9e10 /s and activation energy 85 kJ/mol at 480 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 9, Ea = 85, Tk = 480 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 9e10 * exp(-85e3 / (8.314*480)) | Answer: 50.59 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.91 and bottoms xW = 0.07, with relative volatility alpha = 2.1. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.91, xw = 0.07, al = 2.1 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.91/0.09)(0.93/0.07)] / ln(2.1) | Answer: 6.605 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.7 and x = 0.24. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.7, x = 0.24 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.7/0.3) / (0.24/0.76) | Answer: 7.389

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.73 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 100 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.73, Psat = 100 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.73 * 100 | Answer: 73 kPa

question: A stream of 8 kg/s with specific heat 1.3 kJ/kg-K is heated through 50 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 8, cp = 1.3, dT = 50 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 8*1.3*50 | Answer: 520 kW

question: A reactor of volume 2.5 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 0.9 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 2.5, Q = 0.9 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 2.5 / 0.9 | Answer: 2.778 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 3.9e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 1 mm with a concentration difference of 70 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 3.9, L = 1, dC = 70 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (3.9e-9)*70 / (1e-3) | Answer: 273 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 2.6 min and steady-state gain 2.8. For a step input of magnitude 2, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 2.6, K = 2.8, M = 2 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 2.8 * 2 | Answer: 5.6 units

question: A reactor operates at a space time of 19.2 min. Find its space velocity in per hour.
solution: Given: tau = 19.2 | Formula: SV = 60 / tau  (per hour) | Substitute: SV = 60 / 19.2 | Answer: 3.125 /h

question: An aircraft wing of area 35 m^2 flies at 230 m/s (air density 1.225 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 1.3. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 35, V = 230, rho = 1.225, CL = 1.3 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1.225*(230)^2*35*1.3 / 1000 | Answer: 1474 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 60 m^2 flies at 90 m/s (density 1 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.1. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 60, V = 90, rho = 1, CD = 0.1 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*1*(90)^2*60*0.1 / 1000 | Answer: 24.3 kN

question: A specimen under stress 120 MPa shows an elastic strain of 1.4e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 120, eps = 1.4 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 120 / (1.4e-3) MPa = 85.71 GPa | Answer: 85.71 GPa

question: A block of mass 21 kg has a volume of 5.6e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 21, V = 5.6 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 21 / (5.6e-3) | Answer: 3750 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 1700 mm is heated through 30 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 11e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 1700, dT = 30, al = 11 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 1700*11e-6*30 | Answer: 0.561 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 55 ohm, R2 = 25 ohm and R3 = 290 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 55, R2 = 25, R3 = 290 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 25*290 / 55 | Answer: 131.8 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 1000 ohm and gauge factor 2 experiences a strain of 1600e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 1000, GF = 2, eps = 1600 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 1000*2*1600e-6 | Answer: 3200 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 9.09 when the true value is 100. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.09, true = 100 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.09 - 100| / 100 * 100 | Answer: 90.91 %

question: Annual demand is 33500 units, ordering cost 120 per order and holding cost 26 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 33500, S = 120, H = 26 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*33500*120 / 26) | Answer: 556.1 units

question: An asset costs 60000 with salvage value 32000 after 10 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 60000, Sv = 32000, n = 10 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (60000 - 32000) / 10 | Answer: 2800 per year

question: A product sells for 500 per unit with variable cost 110 per unit and fixed costs 140000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 500, V = 110, F = 140000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 140000 / (500 - 110) | Answer: 359 units

question: Find the present worth of 150000 received 4 years from now at an interest rate of 5% per year.
solution: Given: F = 150000, n = 4, i = 5 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 150000 / (1 + 0.05)^4 | Answer: 123405 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.95, 0.95 and 0.99 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.95, r2 = 0.95, r3 = 0.99 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.95*0.95*0.99 | Answer: 0.8935

question: A process produces 44 defective items in a batch of 11500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 44, N = 11500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 44/11500 * 1e6 | Answer: 3826 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -2x^3 + 8x^2 + x + 8 evaluated at x = 2.
For f(x) = -6x^3 - 2x^2 + x + 3, find f''(x) at x = 1.
Evaluate the definite integral of (3x^2 - 2x + 6) dx from x = 2 to x = 5.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = 3x^3/3 + -2x^2/2 + 6x | Evaluate F(5) - F(2) | Answer: 114
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of x^2 - 3x + 2 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[-1, -9], [-6, 4]].
solution: Given: a = -1, b = -9, c = -6, d = 4 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (-1)(4) - (-9)(-6) | Answer: -58

question: Find the determinant of [[4, -2, -2], [0, 3, 5], [-6, -5, -4]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: 76

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[-6, -8], [-8, -1]].
solution: Trace tr = -7, Determinant = -58 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 4.882

question: Solve for x: 3x + -4y = 4 and 4x + 1y = 10.
solution: Determinant = 3*1 - -4*4 = 19 | x = (e d - b f) / det = 2.316 | Answer: x = 2.316
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 63, 24, 100, 26, 74.
solution: Sum = 287 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 57.4 | Answer: 57.4

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 11, 9, 49, 29, 50.
solution: Mean = 29.6 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 19.77

question: Find the slope of the line through (-5, 3) and (-8, -4).
solution: Given: x1 = -5, y1 = 3, x2 = -8, y2 = -4 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (-4 - 3) / (-8 - -5) | Answer: 2.333

question: Find the distance between the points (7, -8) and (8, 8).
solution: Given: x1 = 7, y1 = -8, x2 = 8, y2 = 8 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((1)^2 + (16)^2) | Answer: 16.03 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (0,-4), (4,-2), (5,-7).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 11 sq units

question: Evaluate the number of combinations C(19, 1).
solution: Given: n = 19, r = 1 | Formula: C(n, r) = n! / (r! (n - r)!) | Substitute: C(19, 1) = 19! / (1! * 18!) | Answer: 19

question: Find the 23th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 7 and common difference 6.
solution: Given: a = 7, d = 6, n = 23 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = 7 + (23 - 1)*6 | Answer: 139

question: Find the sum of the first 31 terms of an AP with first term 10 and common difference -7.
solution: Given: a = 10, d = -7, n = 31 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 31/2 [2*10 + (31-1)*-7] | Answer: -2945

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 20000 at 4.2% per annum for 4 years.
solution: Given: P = 20000, R = 4.2, Tt = 4 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 20000 * 4.2 * 4 / 100 | Answer: 3360 currency units

question: Find the amount when 8000 is invested at 4.1% per annum compounded annually for 6 years.
solution: Given: P = 8000, R = 4.1, Tt = 6 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 8000 * (1 + 4.1/100)^6 | Answer: 10181 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (8, -8, -1) and (-6, 5, -6).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (3, 0, 2) and (-4, 0, -5).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 7

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (-6, -3, -1) and (-3, -3, 0).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 20.23 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number -6 + 7i.
solution: Given: a = -6, b = 7 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((-6)^2 + (7)^2) | Answer: 9.22

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number 11 + -4i.
solution: Given: a = 11, b = -4 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(-4, 11) | Answer: -19.98 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -2x^3 + 6x^2 + 5x - 4 at x = -1.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-140 with initial guess x0=5, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=0.9 and ordinates 10, 13, 0, 11, 19, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 510 and 82.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 510 and 82 | Answer: GCD = 2

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 45 and 64.
solution: Given: a = 45, b = 64 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 45*64 / 1 | Answer: 2880
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 45 mm carries an axial tensile load of 47 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 37 mm and length 1300 mm carries an axial load of 13 kN. Take E = 200 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 34 mm transmits a torque of 1650 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 34, Tt = 1650 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(1650*1000) / (pi*(34)^3) | Answer: 213.8 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 37 mm and length 1500 mm carries a torque of 1200 N-m. With G = 77 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (37)^4 / 32 = 183995 mm^4 | theta = (1200*1000)(1500) / (77000 * 183995) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 7.279 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 92 mm wide and 90 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 92, h = 90 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 92*(90)^2 / 6 | Answer: 124200 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (79 mm x 180 mm) carries a bending moment of 14 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (53 mm x 90 mm) has effective length 3900 mm and E = 200 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 320 MPa is designed for a working stress of 230 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 320, sw = 230 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 320 / 230 | Answer: 1.391

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 700 mm and wall thickness 10 mm carries an internal pressure of 1.3 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 700, t = 10, P = 1.3 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 1.3*700 / (2*10) | Answer: 45.5 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 1080 K and 330 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 1080, Tc = 330 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 330/1080) * 100 | Answer: 69.44 %

question: A refrigerator works between 270 K (cold) and 328 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 270, Th = 328 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 270 / (328 - 270) | Answer: 4.655

question: A heat pump operates between 264 K and 330 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 264, Th = 330 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 330 / (330 - 264) | Answer: 5

question: 3.4 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 125 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.4, dT = 125 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 3.4 * 0.718 * 125 | Answer: 305.1 kJ

question: 3.6 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 200 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.6, dT = 200 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 3.6 * 1.005 * 200 | Answer: 723.6 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 3.2 m^3 at 400 K with mass 1.6 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 3.2, Tk = 400, m = 1.6 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 1.6*0.287*400 / 3.2 | Answer: 57.4 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 1.9 kg of air expands isothermally at 350 K from volume V1 to 5*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1.9, Tk = 350, ratio = 5 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 1.9*0.287*350*ln(5) | Answer: 307.2 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 4.4 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.24 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 4.4, D = 0.24 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*4.4*0.24 / 0.001 | Answer: 1056000

question: Water flows at 0.8 m/s through a pipe of diameter 50 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 9.2 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 9.2 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*9.2 / 1000 | Answer: 90.25 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 16 m. Taking Cv = 0.97, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 16, cv = 0.97 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.97*sqrt(2*9.81*16) | Answer: 17.19 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 290 mm) water flows at 0.7 m/s. It contracts to diameter 70 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 290, d2 = 70, V1 = 0.7 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 0.7*(290/70)^2 | Answer: 12.01 m/s

question: Water flows at 1.1 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.15 m and length 300 m. With friction factor f = 0.036, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 29 teeth drives a gear of 80 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1050 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 29, z2 = 80, N1 = 1050 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1050*29 / 80 | Answer: 380.6 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 540 mm rotates at 350 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 540, N = 350 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.54)*350 / 60 | Answer: 9.896 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 21.4 kW at 1050 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 21.4, N = 1050 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(21.4*1000) / (2*pi*1050) | Answer: 194.6 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 6.1 kg rotates at radius 0.52 m at 300 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 8400 N/m and mass 6.9 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 8400, m = 6.9 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(8400/6.9) | Answer: 5.553 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 3.8 m^2 and thickness 0.33 m has conductivity k = 31 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 120 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 3.8, L = 0.33, k = 31, dT = 120 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 31*3.8*120 / 0.33 | Answer: 42836 W

question: A surface of area 2.1 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 140 W/m^2-K to surroundings 130 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 2.1, h = 140, dT = 130 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 140*2.1*130 | Answer: 38220 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 170 m/min, feed = 0.16 mm/rev, depth of cut = 1.2 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 170, f = 0.16, d = 1.2 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*170*0.16*1.2 | Answer: 32640 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 330 mm is turned at 1050 rpm with a feed of 0.12 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 330, N = 1050, f = 0.12 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 330 / (0.12*1050) | Answer: 2.619 min

question: A resistor of 146 ohm carries a current of 6.1 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 146, I = 6.1 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 6.1 * 146 | Answer: 890.6 V

question: Three resistors 10 ohm, 80 ohm and 84 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 10, R2 = 80, R3 = 84 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 10 + 80 + 84 | Answer: 174 ohm

question: Two resistors 113 ohm and 97 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 113, R2 = 97 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 113*97 / (113+97) | Answer: 52.2 ohm

question: A device draws 11.6 A at 130 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 130, I = 11.6 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 130 * 11.6 | Answer: 1508 W

question: A current of 1 A flows through a 65 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 1, R = 65 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (1)^2 * 65 | Answer: 65 W

question: Two capacitors 49.1 uF and 1.9 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 49.1, C2 = 1.9 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 49.1*1.9 / (49.1+1.9) | Answer: 1.829 uF

question: A resistor 3 kohm and capacitor 15.8 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 3, C = 15.8 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (3k)(15.8u) = 47.4 ms | Answer: 47.4 ms

question: An inductor 414.1 mH is in series with 115 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 414.1, R = 115 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (414.1e-3) / 115 | Answer: 3.601 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 112 mH inductor at 230 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 112, f = 230 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (230)(112e-3) | Answer: 161.9 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 11.4 uF capacitor at 730 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 11.4, f = 730 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (730)(11.4e-6)) | Answer: 19.12 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 48 ohm, XL = 83 ohm and XC = 98 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 48, XL = 83, XC = 98 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(48^2 + (83 - 98)^2) | Answer: 50.29 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 34.9 mH and C = 9.8 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 34.9, C = 9.8 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(34.9e-3 * 9.8e-6)) | Answer: 272.1 Hz

question: A capacitor of 57 uF is charged to 205 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 57, V = 205 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*57e-6*(205)^2 | Answer: 1198 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 360 V with 420 primary turns and 480 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 360, N1 = 420, N2 = 480 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 360 * 480/420 | Answer: 411.4 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 130 V and draws an armature current of 44 A. If the armature resistance is 1.05 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 130, Ia = 44, Ra = 1.05 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 130 - 44*1.05 | Answer: 83.8 V

question: A 6-pole induction motor on a 60 Hz supply runs at 1010 rpm. Find the slip (%).
formula: s = (Ns - N) / Ns,  Ns = 120 f / P

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 200 A at 415 V (line) with a power factor of 0.86. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 200, VL = 415, pf = 0.86 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*415*200*0.86 / 1000 | Answer: 123.6 kW

question: A load has real power 90 kW and apparent power 95 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 90, S = 95 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 90 / 95 | Answer: 0.9474

question: A machine delivers 10 kW output while drawing 17 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 10, Pi = 17 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 10/17 * 100 | Answer: 58.82 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 26 V across R1 = 5 ohm and R2 = 42 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 26, R1 = 5, R2 = 42 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 26*42 / (5+42) | Answer: 23.23 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 170 kohm and Rin = 6 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 170, Rin = 6 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 170 / 6 | Answer: 28.33

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 40 kohm and Rg = 12 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 40, Rg = 12 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 40/12 | Answer: 4.333

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 8049. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 8049 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(8049) | Answer: 39.06 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 8.8 m carries a central point load of 25 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 8.8, W = 25 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 25*8.8 / 4 | Answer: 55 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.3 m carries a UDL of 55 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.3, w = 55 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 55*(4.3)^2 / 8 | Answer: 127.1 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 2 m carries a point load 60 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 2, W = 60 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 60*2 | Answer: 120 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 5.4 m carries a UDL of 28 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.4, w = 28 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 28*(5.4)^2 / 2 | Answer: 408.2 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 7.5 m carries a point load 70 kN at distance 3.3 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 7.5, a = 3.3, W = 70 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 70*(7.5 - 3.3) / 7.5 | Answer: 39.2 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 4.5 m) carries a central point load 55 kN. With E = 30 GPa and I = 280e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=55000 N, L=4500.0 mm, E=30000 MPa, I=280e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 12.43 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 8.4 m carries a UDL of 30 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 8.4, w = 30 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 30*(8.4)^2 / 12 | Answer: 176.4 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 380 mm, clear cover 50 mm and main bars of diameter 25 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 380, c = 50, dia = 25 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 380 - 50 - 25/2 | Answer: 317.5 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 12.6 m^2 carrying a factored load of 10.6 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 12.6, w = 10.6 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 10.6 * 12.6 | Answer: 133.6 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 4.3 m, unit weight 19 kN/m^3, phi = 34 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 4.9 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 19 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 4.9, g = 19 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (19 - 9.81)*4.9 | Answer: 45.03 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 7.9e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1, area = 2.8e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 7.9, i = 1, A = 2.8 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (7.9e-4)*1*(2.8e-3) | Answer: 2212 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 2.1 m, bed slope 0.006 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.021. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 4.8 m under a head of 0.8 m. Taking Cd = 0.61 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 5.2 m wide carries a discharge of 17.2 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 420 m and design speed 45 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 420, V = 45 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (45)^2 / (127*420) | Answer: 0.03796
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: For a design speed of 90 km/h with allowable superelevation 0.07 and lateral friction 0.12, find the minimum curve radius in m.
A tank of volume 170 m^3 treats a flow of 140 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 170, Q = 140 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 170 / 140 | Answer: 1.214 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 220 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.11 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 4 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 220, k = 0.11, t = 4 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 220*(1 - e^(-0.11*4)) | Answer: 78.31 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.6, rainfall intensity 120 mm/h over a catchment of 17.6 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.6, i = 120, A = 17.6 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.6*120*17.6 / 360 | Answer: 3.52 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.06 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 440 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.06, M = 440 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 440*(30+0.06)/30 | Answer: 440.9 m

question: Convert the decimal number 243 to binary.
solution: Divide 243 by 2 repeatedly, recording remainders | Reading remainders in reverse gives 11110011 | Answer: 11110011 (binary)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 2 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the decimal number 2529 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 2529 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 9E1 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the 8-bit binary number 10110110 to decimal.
solution: Binary 10110110 = sum of bit-weights | Answer: 182 (decimal)
formula: Sum each bit times its positional weight (2^i)

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 00100111 and 01011100.
solution: XOR: 01111011 | Count of 1s = 6 | Answer: 6
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 320 megabits is sent over a link of 23 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 320, B = 23 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 320 / 23 | Answer: 13.91 s

question: A link has bandwidth 98 Mbps and round-trip time 40 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 98, R = 40 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 98e6 * 40e-3 bits = 3920 kb | Answer: 3920 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.94, cache access time 3 ns and main-memory access time 80 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.94, tc = 3, tm = 80 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.94*3 + (1 - 0.94)*80 | Answer: 7.62 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 834505 elements?
solution: Given: n = 834505 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(834505)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: An O(n^2) algorithm performs c*n^2 basic operations. If c = 1 and n = 1560, how many operations are performed?
solution: Given: n = 1560 | Formula: operations = n^2 | Substitute: = (1560)^2 | Answer: 2433600

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.006, memory access time 160 ns and page-fault service time 6 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 6 ms = 6000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.006)*160 + 0.006*6000000.0 ns | Answer: 36.16 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 0.2 m^3 at 260 kPa and 400 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 0.2, P = 260, Tk = 400 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (260e3)*0.2 / (8.314*400) | Answer: 15.64 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.21 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 5 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.21, t = 5 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.21*5) | Answer: 0.6501

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.34 /min) is to reach 60% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.34, X = 60 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.6) / 0.34 | Answer: 2.695 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.37 /min) reaches 75% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.37, X = 75 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.75 / (0.37*(1 - 0.75)) | Answer: 8.108 min

question: For a reaction with A = 2e10 /s and activation energy 80 kJ/mol at 480 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 2, Ea = 80, Tk = 480 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 2e10 * exp(-80e3 / (8.314*480)) | Answer: 39.35 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.94 and bottoms xW = 0.02, with relative volatility alpha = 2.4. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.94, xw = 0.02, al = 2.4 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.94/0.06)(0.98/0.02)] / ln(2.4) | Answer: 7.588 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.83 and x = 0.36. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.83, x = 0.36 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.83/0.17) / (0.36/0.64) | Answer: 8.68

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.12 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 30 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.12, Psat = 30 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.12 * 30 | Answer: 3.6 kPa

question: A stream of 1.1 kg/s with specific heat 3.9 kJ/kg-K is heated through 60 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 1.1, cp = 3.9, dT = 60 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 1.1*3.9*60 | Answer: 257.4 kW

question: A reactor of volume 11.1 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 2.6 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 11.1, Q = 2.6 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 11.1 / 2.6 | Answer: 4.269 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 6.6e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 4 mm with a concentration difference of 40 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 6.6, L = 4, dC = 40 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (6.6e-9)*40 / (4e-3) | Answer: 66 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 8.8 min and steady-state gain 1.9. For a step input of magnitude 19, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 8.8, K = 1.9, M = 19 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 1.9 * 19 | Answer: 36.1 units

question: A reactor operates at a space time of 15 min. Find its space velocity in per hour.
solution: Given: tau = 15 | Formula: SV = 60 / tau  (per hour) | Substitute: SV = 60 / 15 | Answer: 4 /h

question: An aircraft wing of area 60 m^2 flies at 260 m/s (air density 1 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 1. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 60, V = 260, rho = 1, CL = 1 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1*(260)^2*60*1 / 1000 | Answer: 2028 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 70 m^2 flies at 240 m/s (density 0.4 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.08. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 70, V = 240, rho = 0.4, CD = 0.08 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.4*(240)^2*70*0.08 / 1000 | Answer: 64.51 kN

question: A specimen under stress 150 MPa shows an elastic strain of 2.1e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 150, eps = 2.1 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 150 / (2.1e-3) MPa = 71.43 GPa | Answer: 71.43 GPa

question: A block of mass 34 kg has a volume of 2.6e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 34, V = 2.6 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 34 / (2.6e-3) | Answer: 13077 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 2500 mm is heated through 35 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 11e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 2500, dT = 35, al = 11 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 2500*11e-6*35 | Answer: 0.9625 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 100 ohm, R2 = 170 ohm and R3 = 200 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 100, R2 = 170, R3 = 200 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 170*200 / 100 | Answer: 340 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 120 ohm and gauge factor 2.1 experiences a strain of 1950e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 120, GF = 2.1, eps = 1950 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 120*2.1*1950e-6 | Answer: 491.4 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 9.28 when the true value is 100. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.28, true = 100 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.28 - 100| / 100 * 100 | Answer: 90.72 %

question: Annual demand is 27500 units, ordering cost 90 per order and holding cost 17 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 27500, S = 90, H = 17 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*27500*90 / 17) | Answer: 539.6 units

question: An asset costs 90000 with salvage value 12000 after 14 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 90000, Sv = 12000, n = 14 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (90000 - 12000) / 14 | Answer: 5571 per year

question: A product sells for 330 per unit with variable cost 150 per unit and fixed costs 140000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 330, V = 150, F = 140000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 140000 / (330 - 150) | Answer: 777.8 units

question: Find the present worth of 25000 received 2 years from now at an interest rate of 12% per year.
solution: Given: F = 25000, n = 2, i = 12 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 25000 / (1 + 0.12)^2 | Answer: 1993 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.97, 0.96 and 0.94 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.97, r2 = 0.96, r3 = 0.94 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.97*0.96*0.94 | Answer: 0.8753

question: A process produces 46 defective items in a batch of 8000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 46, N = 8000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 46/8000 * 1e6 | Answer: 5750 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = 3x^3 + 8x^2 - 4x evaluated at x = -3.
For f(x) = -3x^3 + 4x^2 + 3x + 5, find f''(x) at x = 4.
Evaluate the definite integral of (-5x^2 - 2x - 7) dx from x = 2 to x = 5.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = -5x^3/3 + -2x^2/2 + -7x | Evaluate F(5) - F(2) | Answer: -237

question: Find the larger real root of 5x^2 + 9x - 2 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[-5, -5], [-5, -2]].
solution: Given: a = -5, b = -5, c = -5, d = -2 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (-5)(-2) - (-5)(-5) | Answer: -15

question: Find the determinant of [[4, 2, -6], [-6, 1, -2], [-2, -5, 2]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: -192

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[-8, 0], [5, 3]].
solution: Trace tr = -5, Determinant = -24 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 3

question: Solve for x: -4x + 0y = 2 and 4x + 1y = -9.
solution: Determinant = -4*1 - 0*4 = -4 | x = (e d - b f) / det = -0.5 | Answer: x = -0.5
