question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 18 and 46.
solution: Given: a = 18, b = 46 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 18*46 / 2 | Answer: 414
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 10 mm carries an axial tensile load of 58 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 23 mm and length 700 mm carries an axial load of 32 kN. Take E = 210 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 72 mm transmits a torque of 2550 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 72, Tt = 2550 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(2550*1000) / (pi*(72)^3) | Answer: 34.79 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 61 mm and length 1100 mm carries a torque of 1150 N-m. With G = 80 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 124 mm wide and 130 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 124, h = 130 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 124*(130)^2 / 6 | Answer: 349267 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (98 mm x 210 mm) carries a bending moment of 20 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (57 mm x 130 mm) has effective length 1600 mm and E = 200 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 660 MPa is designed for a working stress of 220 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 660, sw = 220 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 660 / 220 | Answer: 3

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 400 mm and wall thickness 18 mm carries an internal pressure of 2.5 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 400, t = 18, P = 2.5 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 2.5*400 / (2*18) | Answer: 27.78 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 980 K and 440 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 980, Tc = 440 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 440/980) * 100 | Answer: 55.1 %

question: A refrigerator works between 258 K (cold) and 308 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 258, Th = 308 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 258 / (308 - 258) | Answer: 5.16

question: A heat pump operates between 264 K and 310 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 264, Th = 310 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 310 / (310 - 264) | Answer: 6.739

question: 4.6 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 90 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.6, dT = 90 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 4.6 * 0.718 * 90 | Answer: 297.3 kJ

question: 1.2 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 160 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1.2, dT = 160 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 1.2 * 1.005 * 160 | Answer: 193 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 0.9 m^3 at 300 K with mass 3.5 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 0.9, Tk = 300, m = 3.5 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 3.5*0.287*300 / 0.9 | Answer: 334.8 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 4.2 kg of air expands isothermally at 360 K from volume V1 to 2*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.2, Tk = 360, ratio = 2 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 4.2*0.287*360*ln(2) | Answer: 300.8 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 3.8 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.07 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 3.8, D = 0.07 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*3.8*0.07 / 0.001 | Answer: 266000

question: Water flows at 2.6 m/s through a pipe of diameter 290 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 11.6 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 11.6 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*11.6 / 1000 | Answer: 113.8 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 7 m. Taking Cv = 0.98, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 7, cv = 0.98 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.98*sqrt(2*9.81*7) | Answer: 11.48 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 200 mm) water flows at 0.7 m/s. It contracts to diameter 100 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 200, d2 = 100, V1 = 0.7 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 0.7*(200/100)^2 | Answer: 2.8 m/s

question: Water flows at 1.8 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.44 m and length 440 m. With friction factor f = 0.026, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 17 teeth drives a gear of 46 teeth. If the pinion runs at 400 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 17, z2 = 46, N1 = 400 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 400*17 / 46 | Answer: 147.8 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 190 mm rotates at 900 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 190, N = 900 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.19)*900 / 60 | Answer: 8.954 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 33 kW at 550 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 33, N = 550 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(33*1000) / (2*pi*550) | Answer: 573 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 7.5 kg rotates at radius 0.58 m at 600 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 600 N/m and mass 8.4 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 600, m = 8.4 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(600/8.4) | Answer: 1.345 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 9.2 m^2 and thickness 0.16 m has conductivity k = 15.5 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 105 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 9.2, L = 0.16, k = 15.5, dT = 105 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 15.5*9.2*105 / 0.16 | Answer: 93581 W

question: A surface of area 5.4 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 110 W/m^2-K to surroundings 65 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 5.4, h = 110, dT = 65 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 110*5.4*65 | Answer: 38610 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 230 m/min, feed = 0.23 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2.6 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 230, f = 0.23, d = 2.6 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*230*0.23*2.6 | Answer: 137540 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 350 mm is turned at 400 rpm with a feed of 0.15 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 350, N = 400, f = 0.15 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 350 / (0.15*400) | Answer: 5.833 min

question: A resistor of 107 ohm carries a current of 2.4 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 107, I = 2.4 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 2.4 * 107 | Answer: 256.8 V

question: Three resistors 56 ohm, 6 ohm and 65 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 56, R2 = 6, R3 = 65 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 56 + 6 + 65 | Answer: 127 ohm

question: Two resistors 55 ohm and 53 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 55, R2 = 53 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 55*53 / (55+53) | Answer: 26.99 ohm

question: A device draws 12.8 A at 185 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 185, I = 12.8 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 185 * 12.8 | Answer: 2368 W

question: A current of 6.5 A flows through a 38 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 6.5, R = 38 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (6.5)^2 * 38 | Answer: 1606 W

question: Two capacitors 3.9 uF and 42 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 3.9, C2 = 42 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 3.9*42 / (3.9+42) | Answer: 3.569 uF

question: A resistor 5 kohm and capacitor 12.3 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 5, C = 12.3 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (5k)(12.3u) = 61.5 ms | Answer: 61.5 ms

question: An inductor 468.9 mH is in series with 143 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 468.9, R = 143 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (468.9e-3) / 143 | Answer: 3.279 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 87.1 mH inductor at 340 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 87.1, f = 340 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (340)(87.1e-3) | Answer: 186.1 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 2.7 uF capacitor at 750 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 2.7, f = 750 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (750)(2.7e-6)) | Answer: 78.6 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 67 ohm, XL = 16 ohm and XC = 35 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 67, XL = 16, XC = 35 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(67^2 + (16 - 35)^2) | Answer: 69.64 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 80.3 mH and C = 1.5 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 80.3, C = 1.5 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(80.3e-3 * 1.5e-6)) | Answer: 458.6 Hz

question: A capacitor of 90.3 uF is charged to 100 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 90.3, V = 100 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*90.3e-6*(100)^2 | Answer: 451.5 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 130 V with 730 primary turns and 350 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 130, N1 = 730, N2 = 350 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 130 * 350/730 | Answer: 62.33 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 140 V and draws an armature current of 15 A. If the armature resistance is 1.16 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 140, Ia = 15, Ra = 1.16 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 140 - 15*1.16 | Answer: 122.6 V

question: A 6-pole induction motor on a 50 Hz supply runs at 750 rpm. Find the slip (%).
formula: s = (Ns - N) / Ns,  Ns = 120 f / P

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 145 A at 433 V (line) with a power factor of 0.98. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 145, VL = 433, pf = 0.98 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*433*145*0.98 / 1000 | Answer: 106.6 kW

question: A load has real power 20 kW and apparent power 220 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 20, S = 220 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 20 / 220 | Answer: 0.09091

question: A machine delivers 50 kW output while drawing 207 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 50, Pi = 207 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 50/207 * 100 | Answer: 24.15 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 6 V across R1 = 7 ohm and R2 = 12 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 6, R1 = 7, R2 = 12 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 6*12 / (7+12) | Answer: 3.789 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 190 kohm and Rin = 42 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 190, Rin = 42 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 190 / 42 | Answer: 4.524

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 140 kohm and Rg = 22 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 140, Rg = 22 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 140/22 | Answer: 7.364

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 5801. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 5801 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(5801) | Answer: 37.64 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 8.8 m carries a central point load of 45 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 8.8, W = 45 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 45*8.8 / 4 | Answer: 99 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.7 m carries a UDL of 55 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6.7, w = 55 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 55*(6.7)^2 / 8 | Answer: 308.6 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 3.8 m carries a point load 5 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.8, W = 5 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 5*3.8 | Answer: 19 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 2.2 m carries a UDL of 38 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 2.2, w = 38 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 38*(2.2)^2 / 2 | Answer: 91.96 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.3 m carries a point load 65 kN at distance 2.4 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 9.3, a = 2.4, W = 65 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 65*(9.3 - 2.4) / 9.3 | Answer: 48.23 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 5 m) carries a central point load 25 kN. With E = 200 GPa and I = 190e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=25000 N, L=5000.0 mm, E=200000 MPa, I=190e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 1.713 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 6.2 m carries a UDL of 36 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6.2, w = 36 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 36*(6.2)^2 / 12 | Answer: 115.3 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 570 mm, clear cover 30 mm and main bars of diameter 20 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 570, c = 30, dia = 20 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 570 - 30 - 20/2 | Answer: 530 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 34.5 m^2 carrying a factored load of 13.9 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 34.5, w = 13.9 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 13.9 * 34.5 | Answer: 479.6 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 6.5 m, unit weight 18 kN/m^3, phi = 30 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 8.1 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 20 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 8.1, g = 20 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (20 - 9.81)*8.1 | Answer: 82.54 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 7.4e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.2, area = 5e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 7.4, i = 0.2, A = 5 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (7.4e-4)*0.2*(5e-3) | Answer: 740 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.8 m, bed slope 0.002 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.016. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 2 m under a head of 1 m. Taking Cd = 0.62 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
solution: Given: L = 2, H = 1, cd = 0.62 | Formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2) | Substitute: Q = (2/3)*0.62*sqrt(2*9.81)*2*(1)^1.5 | Answer: 3.662 m^3/s
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 4 m wide carries a discharge of 29.9 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 160 m and design speed 85 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 160, V = 85 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (85)^2 / (127*160) | Answer: 0.3556
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: For a design speed of 55 km/h with allowable superelevation 0.06 and lateral friction 0.15, find the minimum curve radius in m.
A tank of volume 50 m^3 treats a flow of 100 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 50, Q = 100 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 50 / 100 | Answer: 0.5 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 260 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.22 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 6 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 260, k = 0.22, t = 6 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 260*(1 - e^(-0.22*6)) | Answer: 190.5 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.37, rainfall intensity 70 mm/h over a catchment of 6.9 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.37, i = 70, A = 6.9 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.37*70*6.9 / 360 | Answer: 0.4964 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.05 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 770 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.05, M = 770 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 770*(30+0.05)/30 | Answer: 771.3 m

question: Convert the decimal number 209 to binary.
solution: Divide 209 by 2 repeatedly, recording remainders | Reading remainders in reverse gives 11010001 | Answer: 11010001 (binary)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 2 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the decimal number 582 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 582 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 246 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the 8-bit binary number 11110101 to decimal.
solution: Binary 11110101 = sum of bit-weights | Answer: 245 (decimal)
formula: Sum each bit times its positional weight (2^i)

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 01010101 and 00101000.
solution: XOR: 01111101 | Count of 1s = 6 | Answer: 6
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 880 megabits is sent over a link of 33 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 880, B = 33 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 880 / 33 | Answer: 26.67 s

question: A link has bandwidth 36 Mbps and round-trip time 40 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 36, R = 40 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 36e6 * 40e-3 bits = 1440 kb | Answer: 1440 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.93, cache access time 7 ns and main-memory access time 160 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.93, tc = 7, tm = 160 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.93*7 + (1 - 0.93)*160 | Answer: 17.71 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 40572 elements?
solution: Given: n = 40572 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(40572)) + 1 | Answer: 16

question: An O(n^2) algorithm performs c*n^2 basic operations. If c = 1 and n = 390, how many operations are performed?
solution: Given: n = 390 | Formula: operations = n^2 | Substitute: = (390)^2 | Answer: 152100

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.008, memory access time 140 ns and page-fault service time 5 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 5 ms = 5000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.008)*140 + 0.008*5000000.0 ns | Answer: 40.14 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 2.5 m^3 at 470 kPa and 490 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 2.5, P = 470, Tk = 490 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (470e3)*2.5 / (8.314*490) | Answer: 288.4 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.14 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 4 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.14, t = 4 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.14*4) | Answer: 0.4288

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.47 /min) is to reach 90% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.47, X = 90 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.9) / 0.47 | Answer: 4.899 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.48 /min) reaches 75% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.48, X = 75 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.75 / (0.48*(1 - 0.75)) | Answer: 6.25 min

question: For a reaction with A = 5e10 /s and activation energy 50 kJ/mol at 390 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 5, Ea = 50, Tk = 390 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 5e10 * exp(-50e3 / (8.314*390)) | Answer: 10046 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.91 and bottoms xW = 0.08, with relative volatility alpha = 3.4. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.91, xw = 0.08, al = 3.4 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.91/0.09)(0.92/0.08)] / ln(3.4) | Answer: 3.886 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.85 and x = 0.5. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.85, x = 0.5 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.85/0.15) / (0.5/0.5) | Answer: 5.667

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.18 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 115 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.18, Psat = 115 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.18 * 115 | Answer: 20.7 kPa

question: A stream of 9.6 kg/s with specific heat 3.9 kJ/kg-K is heated through 25 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 9.6, cp = 3.9, dT = 25 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 9.6*3.9*25 | Answer: 936 kW

question: A reactor of volume 12.6 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 1.2 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 12.6, Q = 1.2 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 12.6 / 1.2 | Answer: 10.5 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 6.2e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 5 mm with a concentration difference of 180 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 6.2, L = 5, dC = 180 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (6.2e-9)*180 / (5e-3) | Answer: 223.2 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 5.9 min and steady-state gain 2.1. For a step input of magnitude 17, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 5.9, K = 2.1, M = 17 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 2.1 * 17 | Answer: 35.7 units

question: A reactor operates at a space time of 1.7 min. Find its space velocity in per hour.
solution: Given: tau = 1.7 | Formula: SV = 60 / tau  (per hour) | Substitute: SV = 60 / 1.7 | Answer: 35.29 /h

question: An aircraft wing of area 60 m^2 flies at 180 m/s (air density 1.225 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.8. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 60, V = 180, rho = 1.225, CL = 0.8 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1.225*(180)^2*60*0.8 / 1000 | Answer: 952.6 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 75 m^2 flies at 260 m/s (density 0.7 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.03. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 75, V = 260, rho = 0.7, CD = 0.03 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.7*(260)^2*75*0.03 / 1000 | Answer: 53.23 kN

question: A specimen under stress 330 MPa shows an elastic strain of 2e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 330, eps = 2 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 330 / (2e-3) MPa = 165 GPa | Answer: 165 GPa

question: A block of mass 42 kg has a volume of 3.7e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 42, V = 3.7 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 42 / (3.7e-3) | Answer: 11351 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 3000 mm is heated through 60 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 23e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 3000, dT = 60, al = 23 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 3000*23e-6*60 | Answer: 4.14 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 15 ohm, R2 = 125 ohm and R3 = 255 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 15, R2 = 125, R3 = 255 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 125*255 / 15 | Answer: 2125 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 1000 ohm and gauge factor 2.2 experiences a strain of 600e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 1000, GF = 2.2, eps = 600 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 1000*2.2*600e-6 | Answer: 1320 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 10.98 when the true value is 20. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10.98, true = 20 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10.98 - 20| / 20 * 100 | Answer: 45.1 %

question: Annual demand is 18000 units, ordering cost 280 per order and holding cost 17 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 18000, S = 280, H = 17 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*18000*280 / 17) | Answer: 770 units

question: An asset costs 440000 with salvage value 6000 after 15 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 440000, Sv = 6000, n = 15 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (440000 - 6000) / 15 | Answer: 28933 per year

question: A product sells for 390 per unit with variable cost 10 per unit and fixed costs 175000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 390, V = 10, F = 175000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 175000 / (390 - 10) | Answer: 460.5 units

question: Find the present worth of 50000 received 2 years from now at an interest rate of 8% per year.
solution: Given: F = 50000, n = 2, i = 8 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 50000 / (1 + 0.08)^2 | Answer: 42867 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.98, 0.93 and 0.97 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.98, r2 = 0.93, r3 = 0.97 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.98*0.93*0.97 | Answer: 0.8841

question: A process produces 24 defective items in a batch of 16000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 24, N = 16000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 24/16000 * 1e6 | Answer: 1500 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -4x^3 + x^2 + 3x + 1 evaluated at x = -4.
For f(x) = -3x^3 + 3x^2 - x + 8, find f''(x) at x = 2.
Evaluate the definite integral of (2x^2 + 1) dx from x = 1 to x = 4.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = 2x^3/3 + 0x^2/2 + 1x | Evaluate F(4) - F(1) | Answer: 45
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 4x^2 - 3x - 2 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[6, -1], [-9, 0]].
solution: Given: a = 6, b = -1, c = -9, d = 0 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (6)(0) - (-1)(-9) | Answer: -9

question: Find the determinant of [[-2, 1, 5], [1, 3, 1], [1, -3, 6]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: -77

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[7, -7], [4, -7]].
solution: Trace tr = 0, Determinant = -21 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 4.583

question: Solve for x: -4x + -1y = -11 and 0x + -2y = 0.
solution: Determinant = -4*-2 - -1*0 = 8 | x = (e d - b f) / det = 2.75 | Answer: x = 2.75
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 15, 3, 46, 94, 75.
solution: Sum = 233 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 46.6 | Answer: 46.6

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 4, 4, 22, 38, 29.
solution: Mean = 19.4 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 15.16

question: Find the slope of the line through (9, -4) and (-8, 7).
solution: Given: x1 = 9, y1 = -4, x2 = -8, y2 = 7 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (7 - -4) / (-8 - 9) | Answer: -0.6471

question: Find the distance between the points (7, 2) and (-9, -2).
solution: Given: x1 = 7, y1 = 2, x2 = -9, y2 = -2 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-16)^2 + (-4)^2) | Answer: 16.49 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (4,7), (8,-3), (6,7).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 10 sq units

question: Find the 10th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -6 and common difference -7.
solution: Given: a = -6, d = -7, n = 10 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -6 + (10 - 1)*-7 | Answer: -69

question: Find the sum of the first 26 terms of an AP with first term -7 and common difference 7.
solution: Given: a = -7, d = 7, n = 26 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 26/2 [2*-7 + (26-1)*7] | Answer: 2093

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 45000 at 6% per annum for 5 years.
solution: Given: P = 45000, R = 6, Tt = 5 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 45000 * 6 * 5 / 100 | Answer: 13500 currency units

question: Find the amount when 37500 is invested at 9.5% per annum compounded annually for 6 years.
solution: Given: P = 37500, R = 9.5, Tt = 6 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 37500 * (1 + 9.5/100)^6 | Answer: 64642 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (4, 2, 2) and (-6, 1, 8).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (-3, 4, -5) and (1, 0, -6).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 33.48

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (-5, -5, -1) and (-4, -5, -3).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 18.1 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number -3 + 7i.
solution: Given: a = -3, b = 7 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((-3)^2 + (7)^2) | Answer: 7.616

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number -7 + -9i.
solution: Given: a = -7, b = -9 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(-9, -7) | Answer: -127.9 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = 3x^3 - 3x^2 - 4x + 9 at x = 2.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-146 with initial guess x0=9, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.9 and ordinates 15, 5, 15, 16, 17, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 184 and 45.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 184 and 45 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 67 and 21.
solution: Given: a = 67, b = 21 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 67*21 / 1 | Answer: 1407
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 35 mm carries an axial tensile load of 58 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 32 mm and length 2700 mm carries an axial load of 60 kN. Take E = 210 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 42 mm transmits a torque of 200 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 42, Tt = 200 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(200*1000) / (pi*(42)^3) | Answer: 13.75 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 61 mm and length 600 mm carries a torque of 800 N-m. With G = 77 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (61)^4 / 32 = 1359312 mm^4 | theta = (800*1000)(600) / (77000 * 1359312) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 0.2628 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 99 mm wide and 170 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 99, h = 170 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 99*(170)^2 / 6 | Answer: 476850 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (112 mm x 130 mm) carries a bending moment of 29 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (52 mm x 150 mm) has effective length 2600 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 900 MPa is designed for a working stress of 100 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 900, sw = 100 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 900 / 100 | Answer: 9

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1050 mm and wall thickness 8 mm carries an internal pressure of 1.9 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1050, t = 8, P = 1.9 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 1.9*1050 / (2*8) | Answer: 124.7 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 1120 K and 350 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 1120, Tc = 350 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 350/1120) * 100 | Answer: 68.75 %

question: A refrigerator works between 254 K (cold) and 316 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 254, Th = 316 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 254 / (316 - 254) | Answer: 4.097

question: A heat pump operates between 262 K and 312 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 262, Th = 312 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 312 / (312 - 262) | Answer: 6.24

question: 1.8 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 130 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1.8, dT = 130 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 1.8 * 0.718 * 130 | Answer: 168 kJ

question: 6.3 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 185 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 6.3, dT = 185 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 6.3 * 1.005 * 185 | Answer: 1171 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 0.6 m^3 at 530 K with mass 3.2 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 0.6, Tk = 530, m = 3.2 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 3.2*0.287*530 / 0.6 | Answer: 811.3 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 3.8 kg of air expands isothermally at 310 K from volume V1 to 3*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.8, Tk = 310, ratio = 3 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 3.8*0.287*310*ln(3) | Answer: 371.4 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 4.8 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.19 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 4.8, D = 0.19 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*4.8*0.19 / 0.001 | Answer: 912000

question: Water flows at 0.6 m/s through a pipe of diameter 160 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 5.8 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 5.8 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*5.8 / 1000 | Answer: 56.9 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 19.1 m. Taking Cv = 0.99, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 19.1, cv = 0.99 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.99*sqrt(2*9.81*19.1) | Answer: 19.16 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 250 mm) water flows at 1.6 m/s. It contracts to diameter 140 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
Water flows at 4 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.46 m and length 390 m. With friction factor f = 0.029, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 22 teeth drives a gear of 109 teeth. If the pinion runs at 650 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 22, z2 = 109, N1 = 650 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 650*22 / 109 | Answer: 131.2 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 590 mm rotates at 1400 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 590, N = 1400 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.59)*1400 / 60 | Answer: 43.25 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 10.3 kW at 600 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 10.3, N = 600 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(10.3*1000) / (2*pi*600) | Answer: 163.9 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 2.2 kg rotates at radius 0.2 m at 300 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 19300 N/m and mass 19.1 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 19300, m = 19.1 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(19300/19.1) | Answer: 5.059 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 4.1 m^2 and thickness 0.22 m has conductivity k = 7.6 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 140 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 4.1, L = 0.22, k = 7.6, dT = 140 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 7.6*4.1*140 / 0.22 | Answer: 19829 W

question: A surface of area 1.8 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 95 W/m^2-K to surroundings 100 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 1.8, h = 95, dT = 100 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 95*1.8*100 | Answer: 17100 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 60 m/min, feed = 0.24 mm/rev, depth of cut = 1.3 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 60, f = 0.24, d = 1.3 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*60*0.24*1.3 | Answer: 18720 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 340 mm is turned at 200 rpm with a feed of 0.31 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 340, N = 200, f = 0.31 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 340 / (0.31*200) | Answer: 5.484 min

question: A resistor of 177 ohm carries a current of 2.5 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 177, I = 2.5 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 2.5 * 177 | Answer: 442.5 V

question: Three resistors 89 ohm, 14 ohm and 73 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 89, R2 = 14, R3 = 73 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 89 + 14 + 73 | Answer: 176 ohm

question: Two resistors 23 ohm and 41 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 23, R2 = 41 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 23*41 / (23+41) | Answer: 14.73 ohm

question: A device draws 2.7 A at 85 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 85, I = 2.7 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 85 * 2.7 | Answer: 229.5 W

question: A current of 4.5 A flows through a 19 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 4.5, R = 19 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (4.5)^2 * 19 | Answer: 384.8 W

question: Two capacitors 15 uF and 40.3 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 15, C2 = 40.3 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 15*40.3 / (15+40.3) | Answer: 10.93 uF

question: A resistor 43 kohm and capacitor 15.2 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 43, C = 15.2 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (43k)(15.2u) = 653.6 ms | Answer: 653.6 ms

question: An inductor 31.9 mH is in series with 177 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 31.9, R = 177 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (31.9e-3) / 177 | Answer: 0.1802 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 135.5 mH inductor at 650 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 135.5, f = 650 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (650)(135.5e-3) | Answer: 553.4 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 20.9 uF capacitor at 130 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 20.9, f = 130 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (130)(20.9e-6)) | Answer: 58.58 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 20 ohm, XL = 17 ohm and XC = 39 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 20, XL = 17, XC = 39 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(20^2 + (17 - 39)^2) | Answer: 29.73 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 65.1 mH and C = 9 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 65.1, C = 9 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(65.1e-3 * 9e-6)) | Answer: 207.9 Hz

question: A capacitor of 58.5 uF is charged to 250 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 58.5, V = 250 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*58.5e-6*(250)^2 | Answer: 1828 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 220 V with 420 primary turns and 290 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 220, N1 = 420, N2 = 290 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 220 * 290/420 | Answer: 151.9 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 230 V and draws an armature current of 43 A. If the armature resistance is 0.84 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 230, Ia = 43, Ra = 0.84 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 230 - 43*0.84 | Answer: 193.9 V

question: A 4-pole induction motor on a 50 Hz supply runs at 950 rpm. Find the slip (%).
formula: s = (Ns - N) / Ns,  Ns = 120 f / P

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 85 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.81. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 85, VL = 400, pf = 0.81 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*400*85*0.81 / 1000 | Answer: 47.7 kW

question: A load has real power 125 kW and apparent power 195 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 125, S = 195 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 125 / 195 | Answer: 0.641

question: A machine delivers 40 kW output while drawing 177 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 40, Pi = 177 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 40/177 * 100 | Answer: 22.6 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 26 V across R1 = 23 ohm and R2 = 23 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 26, R1 = 23, R2 = 23 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 26*23 / (23+23) | Answer: 13 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 180 kohm and Rin = 23 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 180, Rin = 23 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 180 / 23 | Answer: 7.826

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 20 kohm and Rg = 9 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 20, Rg = 9 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 20/9 | Answer: 3.222

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 4755. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 4755 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(4755) | Answer: 36.77 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.8 m carries a central point load of 105 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6.8, W = 105 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 105*6.8 / 4 | Answer: 178.5 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.9 m carries a UDL of 5 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.9, w = 5 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 5*(4.9)^2 / 8 | Answer: 15.01 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 5.1 m carries a point load 25 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.1, W = 25 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 25*5.1 | Answer: 127.5 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 2.6 m carries a UDL of 4 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 2.6, w = 4 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 4*(2.6)^2 / 2 | Answer: 13.52 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 8.7 m carries a point load 70 kN at distance 1.5 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 8.7, a = 1.5, W = 70 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 70*(8.7 - 1.5) / 8.7 | Answer: 57.93 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 7.1 m) carries a central point load 60 kN. With E = 200 GPa and I = 170e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=60000 N, L=7100.0 mm, E=200000 MPa, I=170e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 13.16 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 6.1 m carries a UDL of 9 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6.1, w = 9 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 9*(6.1)^2 / 12 | Answer: 27.91 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 500 mm, clear cover 30 mm and main bars of diameter 12 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 500, c = 30, dia = 12 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 500 - 30 - 12/2 | Answer: 464 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 16.1 m^2 carrying a factored load of 9.6 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 16.1, w = 9.6 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 9.6 * 16.1 | Answer: 154.6 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 4.7 m, unit weight 18 kN/m^3, phi = 29 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 2.8 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 20 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 2.8, g = 20 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (20 - 9.81)*2.8 | Answer: 28.53 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 3.9e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.7, area = 6.7e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 3.9, i = 0.7, A = 6.7 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (3.9e-4)*0.7*(6.7e-3) | Answer: 1829 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.3 m, bed slope 0.004 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.025. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 4.9 m under a head of 0.7 m. Taking Cd = 0.63 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 4.7 m wide carries a discharge of 18.4 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 560 m and design speed 45 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 560, V = 45 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (45)^2 / (127*560) | Answer: 0.02847
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: For a design speed of 55 km/h with allowable superelevation 0.07 and lateral friction 0.14, find the minimum curve radius in m.
A tank of volume 60 m^3 treats a flow of 190 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 60, Q = 190 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 60 / 190 | Answer: 0.3158 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 330 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.18 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 7 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 330, k = 0.18, t = 7 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 330*(1 - e^(-0.18*7)) | Answer: 236.4 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.87, rainfall intensity 60 mm/h over a catchment of 33.7 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.87, i = 60, A = 33.7 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.87*60*33.7 / 360 | Answer: 4.887 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.05 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 730 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.05, M = 730 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 730*(30+0.05)/30 | Answer: 731.2 m

question: Convert the decimal number 65 to binary.
solution: Divide 65 by 2 repeatedly, recording remainders | Reading remainders in reverse gives 1000001 | Answer: 1000001 (binary)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 2 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the decimal number 1791 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 1791 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 6FF (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the 8-bit binary number 10011011 to decimal.
solution: Binary 10011011 = sum of bit-weights | Answer: 155 (decimal)
formula: Sum each bit times its positional weight (2^i)

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 01110010 and 11100001.
solution: XOR: 10010011 | Count of 1s = 4 | Answer: 4
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 370 megabits is sent over a link of 48 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 370, B = 48 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 370 / 48 | Answer: 7.708 s

question: A link has bandwidth 86 Mbps and round-trip time 180 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 86, R = 180 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 86e6 * 180e-3 bits = 15480 kb | Answer: 15480 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.84, cache access time 5 ns and main-memory access time 110 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.84, tc = 5, tm = 110 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.84*5 + (1 - 0.84)*110 | Answer: 21.8 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 237541 elements?
solution: Given: n = 237541 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(237541)) + 1 | Answer: 18

question: An O(n^2) algorithm performs c*n^2 basic operations. If c = 1 and n = 850, how many operations are performed?
solution: Given: n = 850 | Formula: operations = n^2 | Substitute: = (850)^2 | Answer: 722500

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.007, memory access time 80 ns and page-fault service time 4 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 4 ms = 4000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.007)*80 + 0.007*4000000.0 ns | Answer: 28.08 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 0.6 m^3 at 340 kPa and 460 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 0.6, P = 340, Tk = 460 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (340e3)*0.6 / (8.314*460) | Answer: 53.34 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.28 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 14 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.28, t = 14 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.28*14) | Answer: 0.9802

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.11 /min) is to reach 90% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.11, X = 90 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.9) / 0.11 | Answer: 20.93 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.34 /min) reaches 55% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.34, X = 55 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.55 / (0.34*(1 - 0.55)) | Answer: 3.595 min

question: For a reaction with A = 1e10 /s and activation energy 65 kJ/mol at 310 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 1, Ea = 65, Tk = 310 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 1e10 * exp(-65e3 / (8.314*310)) | Answer: 0.1115 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.95 and bottoms xW = 0.03, with relative volatility alpha = 2.4. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.95, xw = 0.03, al = 2.4 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.95/0.05)(0.97/0.03)] / ln(2.4) | Answer: 7.334 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.69 and x = 0.47. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.69, x = 0.47 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.69/0.31) / (0.47/0.53) | Answer: 2.51

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.83 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 65 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.83, Psat = 65 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.83 * 65 | Answer: 53.95 kPa

question: A stream of 4 kg/s with specific heat 4 kJ/kg-K is heated through 80 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 4, cp = 4, dT = 80 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 4*4*80 | Answer: 1280 kW

question: A reactor of volume 13.7 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 1.4 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 13.7, Q = 1.4 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 13.7 / 1.4 | Answer: 9.786 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 1.4e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 4 mm with a concentration difference of 20 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 1.4, L = 4, dC = 20 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (1.4e-9)*20 / (4e-3) | Answer: 7 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 7.2 min and steady-state gain 3. For a step input of magnitude 8, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 7.2, K = 3, M = 8 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 3 * 8 | Answer: 24 units

question: A reactor operates at a space time of 6.9 min. Find its space velocity in per hour.
solution: Given: tau = 6.9 | Formula: SV = 60 / tau  (per hour) | Substitute: SV = 60 / 6.9 | Answer: 8.696 /h

question: An aircraft wing of area 25 m^2 flies at 100 m/s (air density 0.4 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.7. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 25, V = 100, rho = 0.4, CL = 0.7 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.4*(100)^2*25*0.7 / 1000 | Answer: 35 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 70 m^2 flies at 70 m/s (density 1 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.09. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 70, V = 70, rho = 1, CD = 0.09 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*1*(70)^2*70*0.09 / 1000 | Answer: 15.44 kN

question: A specimen under stress 350 MPa shows an elastic strain of 1.7e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 350, eps = 1.7 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 350 / (1.7e-3) MPa = 205.9 GPa | Answer: 205.9 GPa

question: A block of mass 37 kg has a volume of 1.3e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 37, V = 1.3 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 37 / (1.3e-3) | Answer: 28462 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 1100 mm is heated through 75 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 23e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 1100, dT = 75, al = 23 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 1100*23e-6*75 | Answer: 1.897 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 165 ohm, R2 = 175 ohm and R3 = 275 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 165, R2 = 175, R3 = 275 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 175*275 / 165 | Answer: 291.7 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 350 ohm and gauge factor 2 experiences a strain of 700e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 350, GF = 2, eps = 700 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 350*2*700e-6 | Answer: 490 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 10.67 when the true value is 100. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10.67, true = 100 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10.67 - 100| / 100 * 100 | Answer: 89.33 %

question: Annual demand is 21500 units, ordering cost 40 per order and holding cost 33 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 21500, S = 40, H = 33 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*21500*40 / 33) | Answer: 228.3 units

question: An asset costs 250000 with salvage value 18000 after 12 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 250000, Sv = 18000, n = 12 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (250000 - 18000) / 12 | Answer: 19333 per year

question: A product sells for 490 per unit with variable cost 60 per unit and fixed costs 185000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 490, V = 60, F = 185000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 185000 / (490 - 60) | Answer: 430.2 units

question: Find the present worth of 130000 received 7 years from now at an interest rate of 6% per year.
solution: Given: F = 130000, n = 7, i = 6 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 130000 / (1 + 0.06)^7 | Answer: 86457 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.97, 0.95 and 0.97 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.97, r2 = 0.95, r3 = 0.97 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.97*0.95*0.97 | Answer: 0.8939

question: A process produces 46 defective items in a batch of 20000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 46, N = 20000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 46/20000 * 1e6 | Answer: 2300 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -5x^3 + 7x^2 - 6x - 1 evaluated at x = 1.
For f(x) = x^3 - 5x^2 - 3x - 7, find f''(x) at x = 4.
Evaluate the definite integral of (-5x^2 + x - 2) dx from x = 1 to x = 3.

question: Find the larger real root of 4x^2 + 6x = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[1, 0], [5, -5]].
solution: Given: a = 1, b = 0, c = 5, d = -5 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (1)(-5) - (0)(5) | Answer: -5

solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: 62

solution: Trace tr = 1, Determinant = -56 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 8

question: Solve for x: 3x + -4y = 3 and -3x + -5y = 11.
solution: Determinant = 3*-5 - -4*-3 = -27 | x = (e d - b f) / det = -1.074 | Answer: x = -1.074

solution: Sum = 295 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 59 | Answer: 59

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 9, 16, 46, 2, 39.
solution: Mean = 22.4 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 19.17

question: Find the slope of the line through (-7, 9) and (-2, -2).
solution: Given: x1 = -7, y1 = 9, x2 = -2, y2 = -2 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (-2 - 9) / (-2 - -7) | Answer: -2.2

question: Find the distance between the points (-3, -6) and (5, 5).
solution: Given: x1 = -3, y1 = -6, x2 = 5, y2 = 5 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((8)^2 + (11)^2) | Answer: 13.6 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (3,-6), (0,-7), (2,-2).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 6.5 sq units

question: Evaluate the number of combinations C(19, 2).
solution: Given: n = 19, r = 2 | Formula: C(n, r) = n! / (r! (n - r)!) | Substitute: C(19, 2) = 19! / (2! * 17!) | Answer: 171

question: Find the 16th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -2 and common difference 0.
solution: Given: a = -2, d = 0, n = 16 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -2 + (16 - 1)*0 | Answer: -2

question: Find the sum of the first 16 terms of an AP with first term -10 and common difference -8.
Find the simple interest on a principal of 32500 at 9.6% per annum for 9 years.
solution: Given: P = 32500, R = 9.6, Tt = 9 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 32500 * 9.6 * 9 / 100 | Answer: 28080 currency units

question: Find the amount when 21000 is invested at 11.6% per annum compounded annually for 6 years.
solution: Given: P = 21000, R = 11.6, Tt = 6 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 21000 * (1 + 11.6/100)^6 | Answer: 4057 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (4, -6, -7) and (6, 1, 3).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3
