solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 15.59

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (-3, 5, 1) and (-3, 4, 4).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 29.41 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number 12 + 1i.
solution: Given: a = 12, b = 1 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((12)^2 + (1)^2) | Answer: 12.04

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number 11 + 3i.
solution: Given: a = 11, b = 3 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(3, 11) | Answer: 15.26 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -4x^3 - 4x^2 + 5x + 1 at x = 5.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-39 with initial guess x0=5, find x1 (one iteration).
solution: Given: N = 39, x0 = 5 | Formula: x1 = x0 - (x0^2 - N)/(2 x0) | Substitute: x1 = 5 - ((5)^2 - 39)/(2*5) | Answer: 6.4

question: Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.1 and ordinates 5, 4, 15, 8, 8, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 137 and 298.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 137 and 298 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 28 and 52.
solution: Given: a = 28, b = 52 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 28*52 / 4 | Answer: 364
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 32 mm carries an axial tensile load of 18 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 32 mm and length 2700 mm carries an axial load of 38 kN. Take E = 200 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 32 mm transmits a torque of 1600 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 32, Tt = 1600 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(1600*1000) / (pi*(32)^3) | Answer: 248.7 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 66 mm and length 1800 mm carries a torque of 1800 N-m. With G = 45 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (66)^4 / 32 = 186284 mm^4 | theta = (1800*1000)(1800) / (45000 * 186284) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 2.215 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 108 mm wide and 60 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 108, h = 60 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 108*(60)^2 / 6 | Answer: 64800 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (101 mm x 190 mm) carries a bending moment of 39 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (34 mm x 110 mm) has effective length 3100 mm and E = 200 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 800 MPa is designed for a working stress of 110 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 800, sw = 110 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 800 / 110 | Answer: 7.273

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1100 mm and wall thickness 7 mm carries an internal pressure of 2.7 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1100, t = 7, P = 2.7 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 2.7*1100 / (2*7) | Answer: 212.1 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 1200 K and 280 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 1200, Tc = 280 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 280/1200) * 100 | Answer: 76.67 %

question: A refrigerator works between 265 K (cold) and 326 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 265, Th = 326 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 265 / (326 - 265) | Answer: 4.344

question: A heat pump operates between 270 K and 318 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 270, Th = 318 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 318 / (318 - 270) | Answer: 6.625

question: 2.5 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 30 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.5, dT = 30 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 2.5 * 0.718 * 30 | Answer: 53.85 kJ

question: 3.1 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 30 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.1, dT = 30 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 3.1 * 1.005 * 30 | Answer: 93.47 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 0.6 m^3 at 340 K with mass 4.4 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 0.6, Tk = 340, m = 4.4 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 4.4*0.287*340 / 0.6 | Answer: 715.6 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 2.8 kg of air expands isothermally at 330 K from volume V1 to 3*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.8, Tk = 330, ratio = 3 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 2.8*0.287*330*ln(3) | Answer: 291.3 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 3.8 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.09 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 3.8, D = 0.09 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*3.8*0.09 / 0.001 | Answer: 342000

question: Water flows at 2.2 m/s through a pipe of diameter 240 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 10.9 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 10.9 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*10.9 / 1000 | Answer: 106.9 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 4.8 m. Taking Cv = 0.99, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 4.8, cv = 0.99 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.99*sqrt(2*9.81*4.8) | Answer: 9.607 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 300 mm) water flows at 1.9 m/s. It contracts to diameter 130 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
Water flows at 2.5 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.36 m and length 500 m. With friction factor f = 0.028, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 29 teeth drives a gear of 96 teeth. If the pinion runs at 850 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 29, z2 = 96, N1 = 850 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 850*29 / 96 | Answer: 256.8 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 550 mm rotates at 950 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 550, N = 950 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.55)*950 / 60 | Answer: 27.36 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 8.8 kW at 300 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 8.8, N = 300 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(8.8*1000) / (2*pi*300) | Answer: 280.1 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 9.3 kg rotates at radius 0.47 m at 800 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 18400 N/m and mass 10.4 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 18400, m = 10.4 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(18400/10.4) | Answer: 6.694 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 2.8 m^2 and thickness 0.24 m has conductivity k = 48.7 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 75 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 2.8, L = 0.24, k = 48.7, dT = 75 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 48.7*2.8*75 / 0.24 | Answer: 42612 W

question: A surface of area 2.6 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 35 W/m^2-K to surroundings 150 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 2.6, h = 35, dT = 150 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 35*2.6*150 | Answer: 13650 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 110 m/min, feed = 0.23 mm/rev, depth of cut = 1.4 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 110, f = 0.23, d = 1.4 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*110*0.23*1.4 | Answer: 35420 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 380 mm is turned at 700 rpm with a feed of 0.21 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 380, N = 700, f = 0.21 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 380 / (0.21*700) | Answer: 2.585 min

question: A resistor of 169 ohm carries a current of 1.8 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 169, I = 1.8 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 1.8 * 169 | Answer: 304.2 V

question: Three resistors 65 ohm, 90 ohm and 99 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 65, R2 = 90, R3 = 99 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 65 + 90 + 99 | Answer: 254 ohm

question: Two resistors 77 ohm and 68 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 77, R2 = 68 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 77*68 / (77+68) | Answer: 36.11 ohm

question: A device draws 8.4 A at 35 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 35, I = 8.4 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 35 * 8.4 | Answer: 294 W

question: A current of 7.6 A flows through a 23 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 7.6, R = 23 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (7.6)^2 * 23 | Answer: 1328 W

question: Two capacitors 43.3 uF and 13 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 43.3, C2 = 13 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 43.3*13 / (43.3+13) | Answer: 9.998 uF

question: A resistor 31 kohm and capacitor 19.3 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 31, C = 19.3 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (31k)(19.3u) = 598.3 ms | Answer: 598.3 ms

question: An inductor 347.7 mH is in series with 53 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 347.7, R = 53 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (347.7e-3) / 53 | Answer: 6.56 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 91.3 mH inductor at 720 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 91.3, f = 720 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (720)(91.3e-3) | Answer: 413 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 4.6 uF capacitor at 660 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 4.6, f = 660 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (660)(4.6e-6)) | Answer: 52.42 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 65 ohm, XL = 28 ohm and XC = 149 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 65, XL = 28, XC = 149 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(65^2 + (28 - 149)^2) | Answer: 137.4 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 91.3 mH and C = 7.9 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 91.3, C = 7.9 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(91.3e-3 * 7.9e-6)) | Answer: 187.4 Hz

question: A capacitor of 89 uF is charged to 50 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 89, V = 50 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*89e-6*(50)^2 | Answer: 111.2 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 430 V with 650 primary turns and 380 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 430, N1 = 650, N2 = 380 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 430 * 380/650 | Answer: 251.4 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 160 V and draws an armature current of 58 A. If the armature resistance is 0.88 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 160, Ia = 58, Ra = 0.88 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 160 - 58*0.88 | Answer: 109 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 160 A at 415 V (line) with a power factor of 0.88. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 160, VL = 415, pf = 0.88 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*415*160*0.88 / 1000 | Answer: 101.2 kW

question: A load has real power 20 kW and apparent power 150 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 20, S = 150 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 20 / 150 | Answer: 0.1333

question: A machine delivers 105 kW output while drawing 197 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 105, Pi = 197 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 105/197 * 100 | Answer: 53.3 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 7 V across R1 = 17 ohm and R2 = 38 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 7, R1 = 17, R2 = 38 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 7*38 / (17+38) | Answer: 4.836 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 180 kohm and Rin = 39 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 180, Rin = 39 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 180 / 39 | Answer: 4.615

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 80 kohm and Rg = 11 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 80, Rg = 11 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 80/11 | Answer: 8.273

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 1298. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 1298 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(1298) | Answer: 31.13 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.2 m carries a central point load of 65 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 9.2, W = 65 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 65*9.2 / 4 | Answer: 149.5 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.9 m carries a UDL of 40 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6.9, w = 40 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 40*(6.9)^2 / 8 | Answer: 238.1 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 5.2 m carries a point load 80 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.2, W = 80 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 80*5.2 | Answer: 416 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 1.2 m carries a UDL of 32 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 1.2, w = 32 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 32*(1.2)^2 / 2 | Answer: 23.04 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.9 m carries a point load 85 kN at distance 1.6 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 6.9, a = 1.6, W = 85 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 85*(6.9 - 1.6) / 6.9 | Answer: 65.29 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 7.1 m) carries a central point load 30 kN. With E = 200 GPa and I = 300e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=30000 N, L=7100.0 mm, E=200000 MPa, I=300e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 3.728 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 5.6 m carries a UDL of 15 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.6, w = 15 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 15*(5.6)^2 / 12 | Answer: 39.2 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 320 mm, clear cover 30 mm and main bars of diameter 25 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 320, c = 30, dia = 25 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 320 - 30 - 25/2 | Answer: 277.5 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 19.6 m^2 carrying a factored load of 17.1 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 19.6, w = 17.1 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 17.1 * 19.6 | Answer: 335.2 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 7 m, unit weight 20 kN/m^3, phi = 29 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 6.1 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 21 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 6.1, g = 21 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (21 - 9.81)*6.1 | Answer: 68.26 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 5.9e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.6, area = 1.3e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 5.9, i = 0.6, A = 1.3 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (5.9e-4)*0.6*(1.3e-3) | Answer: 460.2 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.4 m, bed slope 0.008 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.027. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 2 m under a head of 0.5 m. Taking Cd = 0.61 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 2.4 m wide carries a discharge of 12.5 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 240 m and design speed 70 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 240, V = 70 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (70)^2 / (127*240) | Answer: 0.1608
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: For a design speed of 70 km/h with allowable superelevation 0.07 and lateral friction 0.13, find the minimum curve radius in m.
A tank of volume 820 m^3 treats a flow of 135 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 820, Q = 135 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 820 / 135 | Answer: 6.074 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 370 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.33 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 8 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 370, k = 0.33, t = 8 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 370*(1 - e^(-0.33*8)) | Answer: 343.6 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.64, rainfall intensity 65 mm/h over a catchment of 54.5 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.64, i = 65, A = 54.5 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.64*65*54.5 / 360 | Answer: 6.298 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.03 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 470 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.03, M = 470 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 470*(20+0.03)/20 | Answer: 470.7 m

question: Convert the decimal number 74 to binary.
solution: Divide 74 by 2 repeatedly, recording remainders | Reading remainders in reverse gives 1001010 | Answer: 1001010 (binary)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 2 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the decimal number 3647 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 3647 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: E3F (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the 8-bit binary number 00011011 to decimal.
solution: Binary 00011011 = sum of bit-weights | Answer: 27 (decimal)
formula: Sum each bit times its positional weight (2^i)

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 10011000 and 10010000.
solution: XOR: 00001000 | Count of 1s = 1 | Answer: 1
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 890 megabits is sent over a link of 18 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 890, B = 18 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 890 / 18 | Answer: 49.44 s

question: A link has bandwidth 33 Mbps and round-trip time 20 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 33, R = 20 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 33e6 * 20e-3 bits = 660 kb | Answer: 660 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.94, cache access time 3 ns and main-memory access time 160 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.94, tc = 3, tm = 160 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.94*3 + (1 - 0.94)*160 | Answer: 12.42 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 342800 elements?
solution: Given: n = 342800 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(342800)) + 1 | Answer: 19

question: An O(n^2) algorithm performs c*n^2 basic operations. If c = 1 and n = 500, how many operations are performed?
solution: Given: n = 500 | Formula: operations = n^2 | Substitute: = (500)^2 | Answer: 250000

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.009, memory access time 90 ns and page-fault service time 7 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 7 ms = 7000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.009)*90 + 0.009*7000000.0 ns | Answer: 63.09 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 1.6 m^3 at 290 kPa and 490 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 1.6, P = 290, Tk = 490 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (290e3)*1.6 / (8.314*490) | Answer: 113.9 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.27 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 4 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.27, t = 4 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.27*4) | Answer: 0.6604

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.15 /min) is to reach 60% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.15, X = 60 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.6) / 0.15 | Answer: 6.109 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.49 /min) reaches 55% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.49, X = 55 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.55 / (0.49*(1 - 0.55)) | Answer: 2.494 min

question: For a reaction with A = 2e10 /s and activation energy 85 kJ/mol at 450 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 2, Ea = 85, Tk = 450 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 2e10 * exp(-85e3 / (8.314*450)) | Answer: 2.717 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.98 and bottoms xW = 0.08, with relative volatility alpha = 3. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.98, xw = 0.08, al = 3 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.98/0.02)(0.92/0.08)] / ln(3) | Answer: 5.766 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.85 and x = 0.29. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.85, x = 0.29 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.85/0.15) / (0.29/0.71) | Answer: 13.87

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.24 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 85 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.24, Psat = 85 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.24 * 85 | Answer: 20.4 kPa

question: A stream of 4.9 kg/s with specific heat 2.9 kJ/kg-K is heated through 20 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 4.9, cp = 2.9, dT = 20 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 4.9*2.9*20 | Answer: 284.2 kW

question: A reactor of volume 17.4 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 4.5 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 17.4, Q = 4.5 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 17.4 / 4.5 | Answer: 3.867 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 8.9e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 2 mm with a concentration difference of 20 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 8.9, L = 2, dC = 20 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (8.9e-9)*20 / (2e-3) | Answer: 89 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 3.3 min and steady-state gain 3.6. For a step input of magnitude 6, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 3.3, K = 3.6, M = 6 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 3.6 * 6 | Answer: 21.6 units

question: A reactor operates at a space time of 5.1 min. Find its space velocity in per hour.
solution: Given: tau = 5.1 | Formula: SV = 60 / tau  (per hour) | Substitute: SV = 60 / 5.1 | Answer: 11.76 /h

question: An aircraft wing of area 95 m^2 flies at 130 m/s (air density 0.4 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.6. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 95, V = 130, rho = 0.4, CL = 0.6 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.4*(130)^2*95*0.6 / 1000 | Answer: 192.7 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 50 m^2 flies at 110 m/s (density 0.4 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.06. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 50, V = 110, rho = 0.4, CD = 0.06 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.4*(110)^2*50*0.06 / 1000 | Answer: 7.26 kN

question: An aircraft flies at 310 m/s where the speed of sound is 340 m/s. Find the Mach number.
solution: Given: V = 310, a = 340 | Formula: M = V / a | Substitute: M = 310 / 340 | Answer: 0.9118

question: A specimen under stress 290 MPa shows an elastic strain of 2.1e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 290, eps = 2.1 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 290 / (2.1e-3) MPa = 138.1 GPa | Answer: 138.1 GPa

question: A block of mass 9 kg has a volume of 5.7e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 9, V = 5.7 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 9 / (5.7e-3) | Answer: 1579 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 2700 mm is heated through 50 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 11e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 2700, dT = 50, al = 11 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 2700*11e-6*50 | Answer: 1.485 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 170 ohm, R2 = 60 ohm and R3 = 295 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 170, R2 = 60, R3 = 295 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 60*295 / 170 | Answer: 104.1 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 120 ohm and gauge factor 2.2 experiences a strain of 350e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 120, GF = 2.2, eps = 350 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 120*2.2*350e-6 | Answer: 92.4 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 9.06 when the true value is 10. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.06, true = 10 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.06 - 10| / 10 * 100 | Answer: 9.4 %

question: Annual demand is 11000 units, ordering cost 60 per order and holding cost 39 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 11000, S = 60, H = 39 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*11000*60 / 39) | Answer: 184 units

question: An asset costs 200000 with salvage value 34000 after 16 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 200000, Sv = 34000, n = 16 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (200000 - 34000) / 16 | Answer: 10375 per year

question: A product sells for 410 per unit with variable cost 150 per unit and fixed costs 190000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 410, V = 150, F = 190000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 190000 / (410 - 150) | Answer: 730.8 units

question: Find the present worth of 150000 received 8 years from now at an interest rate of 9% per year.
solution: Given: F = 150000, n = 8, i = 9 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 150000 / (1 + 0.09)^8 | Answer: 7528 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.91, 0.98 and 0.97 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.91, r2 = 0.98, r3 = 0.97 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.91*0.98*0.97 | Answer: 0.865

question: A process produces 1 defective items in a batch of 12500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 1, N = 12500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 1/12500 * 1e6 | Answer: 80 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -4x^3 - 7x^2 + 8 evaluated at x = 3.
For f(x) = x^3 + 3x^2 - 9x - 3, find f''(x) at x = -1.
Evaluate the definite integral of (4x^2 - 6x - 2) dx from x = 1 to x = 3.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = 4x^3/3 + -6x^2/2 + -2x | Evaluate F(3) - F(1) | Answer: 6.667
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 4x^2 - 6 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[4, 7], [-2, -5]].
solution: Given: a = 4, b = 7, c = -2, d = -5 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (4)(-5) - (7)(-2) | Answer: -6

question: Find the determinant of [[2, 1, 3], [6, -5, 2], [6, 3, -1]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: 160

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[8, 8], [3, -7]].
solution: Trace tr = 1, Determinant = -80 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 9.458

question: Solve for x: 1x + 5y = 9 and -6x + 4y = 2.
solution: Determinant = 1*4 - 5*-6 = 34 | x = (e d - b f) / det = 0.7647 | Answer: x = 0.7647
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 29, 67, 83, 28, 27.
solution: Sum = 234 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 46.8 | Answer: 46.8

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 23, 30, 41, 16, 26.
solution: Mean = 27.2 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 9.257

question: Find the slope of the line through (-2, 8) and (5, 4).
solution: Given: x1 = -2, y1 = 8, x2 = 5, y2 = 4 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (4 - 8) / (5 - -2) | Answer: -0.5714

question: Find the distance between the points (9, -1) and (6, -4).
solution: Given: x1 = 9, y1 = -1, x2 = 6, y2 = -4 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-3)^2 + (-3)^2) | Answer: 4.243 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (4,3), (6,-4), (-3,-4).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 31.5 sq units

question: Evaluate the number of combinations C(11, 2).
solution: Given: n = 11, r = 2 | Formula: C(n, r) = n! / (r! (n - r)!) | Substitute: C(11, 2) = 11! / (2! * 9!) | Answer: 55

question: Find the 22th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 11 and common difference 3.
solution: Given: a = 11, d = 3, n = 22 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = 11 + (22 - 1)*3 | Answer: 74

question: Find the sum of the first 12 terms of an AP with first term -5 and common difference 1.
solution: Given: a = -5, d = 1, n = 12 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 12/2 [2*-5 + (12-1)*1] | Answer: 6

question: Find the 3th term of a geometric progression with first term 1 and common ratio 3.
solution: Given: a = 1, r = 3, n = 3 | Formula: a_n = a r^(n-1) | Substitute: a_n = 1 * 3^(3-1) | Answer: 9

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 43000 at 12.7% per annum for 5 years.
solution: Given: P = 43000, R = 12.7, Tt = 5 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 43000 * 12.7 * 5 / 100 | Answer: 27305 currency units

question: Find the amount when 9000 is invested at 4.2% per annum compounded annually for 5 years.
solution: Given: P = 9000, R = 4.2, Tt = 5 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 9000 * (1 + 4.2/100)^5 | Answer: 11056 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (-3, 8, 6) and (-5, -4, -2).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (1, 3, -3) and (0, 5, -3).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 8.367

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (4, -2, -2) and (-6, 1, 4).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 162.4 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number 8 + -3i.
solution: Given: a = 8, b = -3 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((8)^2 + (-3)^2) | Answer: 8.544

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number -8 + 6i.
solution: Given: a = -8, b = 6 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(6, -8) | Answer: 143.1 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -3x^3 + 2x^2 - 2x - 3 at x = 5.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-41 with initial guess x0=6, find x1 (one iteration).
solution: Given: N = 41, x0 = 6 | Formula: x1 = x0 - (x0^2 - N)/(2 x0) | Substitute: x1 = 6 - ((6)^2 - 41)/(2*6) | Answer: 6.417

question: Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.7 and ordinates 10, 7, 11, 16, 2, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 343 and 250.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 343 and 250 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 66 and 48.
solution: Given: a = 66, b = 48 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 66*48 / 6 | Answer: 528
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 29 mm carries an axial tensile load of 73 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 27 mm and length 2600 mm carries an axial load of 53 kN. Take E = 210 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 71 mm transmits a torque of 1950 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 71, Tt = 1950 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(1950*1000) / (pi*(71)^3) | Answer: 27.75 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 55 mm and length 600 mm carries a torque of 1800 N-m. With G = 80 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (55)^4 / 32 = 898361 mm^4 | theta = (1800*1000)(600) / (80000 * 898361) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 0.861 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 135 mm wide and 270 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 135, h = 270 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 135*(270)^2 / 6 | Answer: 1640250 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (96 mm x 190 mm) carries a bending moment of 23 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (32 mm x 160 mm) has effective length 1800 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 560 MPa is designed for a working stress of 200 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 560, sw = 200 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 560 / 200 | Answer: 2.8

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 750 mm and wall thickness 20 mm carries an internal pressure of 0.6 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 750, t = 20, P = 0.6 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 0.6*750 / (2*20) | Answer: 11.25 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 680 K and 350 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 680, Tc = 350 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 350/680) * 100 | Answer: 48.53 %

question: A refrigerator works between 250 K (cold) and 314 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 250, Th = 314 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 250 / (314 - 250) | Answer: 3.906

question: A heat pump operates between 282 K and 320 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 282, Th = 320 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 320 / (320 - 282) | Answer: 8.421

question: 5 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 55 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 5, dT = 55 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 5 * 0.718 * 55 | Answer: 197.4 kJ

question: 1.1 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 115 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1.1, dT = 115 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 1.1 * 1.005 * 115 | Answer: 127.1 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 1.2 m^3 at 480 K with mass 2.7 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 1.2, Tk = 480, m = 2.7 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 2.7*0.287*480 / 1.2 | Answer: 310 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 4 kg of air expands isothermally at 400 K from volume V1 to 5*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4, Tk = 400, ratio = 5 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 4*0.287*400*ln(5) | Answer: 739.1 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 5 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.22 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 5, D = 0.22 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*5*0.22 / 0.001 | Answer: 1100000

question: Water flows at 3.3 m/s through a pipe of diameter 110 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 14.8 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 14.8 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*14.8 / 1000 | Answer: 145.2 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 11 m. Taking Cv = 0.99, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 11, cv = 0.99 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.99*sqrt(2*9.81*11) | Answer: 14.54 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 340 mm) water flows at 0.8 m/s. It contracts to diameter 130 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
Water flows at 1.8 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.42 m and length 450 m. With friction factor f = 0.031, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 27 teeth drives a gear of 45 teeth. If the pinion runs at 800 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 27, z2 = 45, N1 = 800 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 800*27 / 45 | Answer: 480 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 390 mm rotates at 800 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 390, N = 800 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.39)*800 / 60 | Answer: 16.34 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 6.9 kW at 500 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 6.9, N = 500 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(6.9*1000) / (2*pi*500) | Answer: 131.8 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 1.5 kg rotates at radius 0.17 m at 200 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 2500 N/m and mass 14.7 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 2500, m = 14.7 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(2500/14.7) | Answer: 2.076 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 5.2 m^2 and thickness 0.32 m has conductivity k = 30.9 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 40 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 5.2, L = 0.32, k = 30.9, dT = 40 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 30.9*5.2*40 / 0.32 | Answer: 20085 W

question: A surface of area 4.1 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 10 W/m^2-K to surroundings 130 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 4.1, h = 10, dT = 130 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 10*4.1*130 | Answer: 5330 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 140 m/min, feed = 0.19 mm/rev, depth of cut = 1.4 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 140, f = 0.19, d = 1.4 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*140*0.19*1.4 | Answer: 37240 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 380 mm is turned at 950 rpm with a feed of 0.13 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 380, N = 950, f = 0.13 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 380 / (0.13*950) | Answer: 3.077 min

question: A resistor of 39 ohm carries a current of 9.1 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 39, I = 9.1 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 9.1 * 39 | Answer: 354.9 V

question: Three resistors 43 ohm, 13 ohm and 61 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 43, R2 = 13, R3 = 61 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 43 + 13 + 61 | Answer: 117 ohm

question: Two resistors 94 ohm and 10 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 94, R2 = 10 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 94*10 / (94+10) | Answer: 9.038 ohm

question: A device draws 5.5 A at 170 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 170, I = 5.5 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 170 * 5.5 | Answer: 935 W

question: A current of 0.7 A flows through a 20 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 0.7, R = 20 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (0.7)^2 * 20 | Answer: 9.8 W

question: Two capacitors 9.5 uF and 12.1 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 9.5, C2 = 12.1 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 9.5*12.1 / (9.5+12.1) | Answer: 5.322 uF

question: A resistor 51 kohm and capacitor 16.2 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 51, C = 16.2 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (51k)(16.2u) = 826.2 ms | Answer: 826.2 ms

question: An inductor 432.7 mH is in series with 197 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 432.7, R = 197 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (432.7e-3) / 197 | Answer: 2.196 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 16.7 mH inductor at 700 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 16.7, f = 700 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (700)(16.7e-3) | Answer: 73.45 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 27.8 uF capacitor at 710 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 27.8, f = 710 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (710)(27.8e-6)) | Answer: 8.063 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 25 ohm, XL = 88 ohm and XC = 13 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 25, XL = 88, XC = 13 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(25^2 + (88 - 13)^2) | Answer: 79.06 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 85.8 mH and C = 4.3 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 85.8, C = 4.3 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(85.8e-3 * 4.3e-6)) | Answer: 262 Hz

question: A capacitor of 97.7 uF is charged to 110 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 97.7, V = 110 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*97.7e-6*(110)^2 | Answer: 591.1 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 420 V with 240 primary turns and 450 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 420, N1 = 240, N2 = 450 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 420 * 450/240 | Answer: 787.5 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 310 V and draws an armature current of 37 A. If the armature resistance is 0.96 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 310, Ia = 37, Ra = 0.96 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 310 - 37*0.96 | Answer: 274.5 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 170 A at 415 V (line) with a power factor of 0.89. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 170, VL = 415, pf = 0.89 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*415*170*0.89 / 1000 | Answer: 108.8 kW

question: A load has real power 90 kW and apparent power 110 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 90, S = 110 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 90 / 110 | Answer: 0.8182

question: A machine delivers 70 kW output while drawing 147 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 70, Pi = 147 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 70/147 * 100 | Answer: 47.62 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 12 V across R1 = 29 ohm and R2 = 15 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 12, R1 = 29, R2 = 15 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 12*15 / (29+15) | Answer: 4.091 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 180 kohm and Rin = 5 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 180, Rin = 5 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 180 / 5 | Answer: 36

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 100 kohm and Rg = 45 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 100, Rg = 45 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 100/45 | Answer: 3.222

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 8911. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 8911 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(8911) | Answer: 39.5 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 8.5 m carries a central point load of 50 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 8.5, W = 50 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 50*8.5 / 4 | Answer: 106.2 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.9 m carries a UDL of 60 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.9, w = 60 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 60*(4.9)^2 / 8 | Answer: 180.1 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 2 m carries a point load 80 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 2, W = 80 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 80*2 | Answer: 160 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 3.5 m carries a UDL of 8 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.5, w = 8 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 8*(3.5)^2 / 2 | Answer: 49 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.3 m carries a point load 45 kN at distance 3.8 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 6.3, a = 3.8, W = 45 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 45*(6.3 - 3.8) / 6.3 | Answer: 17.86 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 3.8 m) carries a central point load 60 kN. With E = 30 GPa and I = 220e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=60000 N, L=3800.0 mm, E=30000 MPa, I=220e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 10.39 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 8.2 m carries a UDL of 12 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 8.2, w = 12 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 12*(8.2)^2 / 12 | Answer: 67.24 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 430 mm, clear cover 30 mm and main bars of diameter 12 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 430, c = 30, dia = 12 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 430 - 30 - 12/2 | Answer: 394 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 39.2 m^2 carrying a factored load of 19.9 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 39.2, w = 19.9 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 19.9 * 39.2 | Answer: 780.1 kN

question: For a bar of diameter 16 mm with design bond stress 1.9 MPa and steel stress 395 MPa, find the development length in mm.
solution: Given: dia = 16, tbd = 1.9, fs = 395 | Formula: Ld = phi fs / (4 tau_bd) | Substitute: Ld = 16*395 / (4*1.9) | Answer: 831.6 mm

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 6.8 m, unit weight 18 kN/m^3, phi = 35 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 7.1 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 21 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 7.1, g = 21 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (21 - 9.81)*7.1 | Answer: 79.45 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 2.7e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.3, area = 2.5e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 2.7, i = 0.3, A = 2.5 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (2.7e-4)*0.3*(2.5e-3) | Answer: 202.5 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.7 m, bed slope 0.002 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.016. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 2 m under a head of 0.3 m. Taking Cd = 0.64 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 4.4 m wide carries a discharge of 7.2 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 530 m and design speed 65 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 530, V = 65 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (65)^2 / (127*530) | Answer: 0.06277
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: For a design speed of 80 km/h with allowable superelevation 0.08 and lateral friction 0.13, find the minimum curve radius in m.
A tank of volume 620 m^3 treats a flow of 145 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 620, Q = 145 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 620 / 145 | Answer: 4.276 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 200 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.19 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 3 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 200, k = 0.19, t = 3 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 200*(1 - e^(-0.19*3)) | Answer: 86.89 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.36, rainfall intensity 40 mm/h over a catchment of 40.2 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.36, i = 40, A = 40.2 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.36*40*40.2 / 360 | Answer: 1.608 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.06 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 660 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.06, M = 660 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 660*(20+0.06)/20 | Answer: 662 m

question: Convert the decimal number 51 to binary.
solution: Divide 51 by 2 repeatedly, recording remainders | Reading remainders in reverse gives 110011 | Answer: 110011 (binary)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 2 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the decimal number 1888 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 1888 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 760 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the 8-bit binary number 10001110 to decimal.
solution: Binary 10001110 = sum of bit-weights | Answer: 142 (decimal)
formula: Sum each bit times its positional weight (2^i)

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 10001000 and 11000000.
solution: XOR: 01001000 | Count of 1s = 2 | Answer: 2
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 430 megabits is sent over a link of 14 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 430, B = 14 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 430 / 14 | Answer: 30.71 s

question: A link has bandwidth 85 Mbps and round-trip time 150 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 85, R = 150 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 85e6 * 150e-3 bits = 12750 kb | Answer: 12750 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.85, cache access time 1 ns and main-memory access time 100 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.85, tc = 1, tm = 100 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.85*1 + (1 - 0.85)*100 | Answer: 15.85 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 657998 elements?
solution: Given: n = 657998 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(657998)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: An O(n^2) algorithm performs c*n^2 basic operations. If c = 1 and n = 2620, how many operations are performed?
solution: Given: n = 2620 | Formula: operations = n^2 | Substitute: = (2620)^2 | Answer: 6864400

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.011, memory access time 170 ns and page-fault service time 9 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 9 ms = 9000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.011)*170 + 0.011*9000000.0 ns | Answer: 99.17 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 0.6 m^3 at 230 kPa and 470 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 0.6, P = 230, Tk = 470 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (230e3)*0.6 / (8.314*470) | Answer: 35.32 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.17 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 18 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.17, t = 18 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.17*18) | Answer: 0.9531

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.4 /min) is to reach 90% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.4, X = 90 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.9) / 0.4 | Answer: 5.756 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.17 /min) reaches 60% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.17, X = 60 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.6 / (0.17*(1 - 0.6)) | Answer: 8.824 min

question: For a reaction with A = 9e10 /s and activation energy 60 kJ/mol at 320 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 9, Ea = 60, Tk = 320 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 9e10 * exp(-60e3 / (8.314*320)) | Answer: 14.45 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.92 and bottoms xW = 0.03, with relative volatility alpha = 2.3. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.92, xw = 0.03, al = 2.3 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.92/0.08)(0.97/0.03)] / ln(2.3) | Answer: 7.106 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.79 and x = 0.34. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.79, x = 0.34 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.79/0.21) / (0.34/0.66) | Answer: 7.303

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.89 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 25 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.89, Psat = 25 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.89 * 25 | Answer: 22.25 kPa

question: A stream of 3.7 kg/s with specific heat 1.1 kJ/kg-K is heated through 80 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 3.7, cp = 1.1, dT = 80 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 3.7*1.1*80 | Answer: 325.6 kW

question: A reactor of volume 8.6 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 2.7 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 8.6, Q = 2.7 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 8.6 / 2.7 | Answer: 3.185 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 4.3e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 5 mm with a concentration difference of 30 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 4.3, L = 5, dC = 30 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (4.3e-9)*30 / (5e-3) | Answer: 25.8 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 7.3 min and steady-state gain 1.9. For a step input of magnitude 15, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 7.3, K = 1.9, M = 15 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 1.9 * 15 | Answer: 28.5 units

question: A reactor operates at a space time of 19.6 min. Find its space velocity in per hour.
solution: Given: tau = 19.6 | Formula: SV = 60 / tau  (per hour) | Substitute: SV = 60 / 19.6 | Answer: 3.061 /h

question: An aircraft wing of area 110 m^2 flies at 260 m/s (air density 0.7 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.5. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 110, V = 260, rho = 0.7, CL = 0.5 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.7*(260)^2*110*0.5 / 1000 | Answer: 1301 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 85 m^2 flies at 200 m/s (density 0.4 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.03. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 85, V = 200, rho = 0.4, CD = 0.03 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.4*(200)^2*85*0.03 / 1000 | Answer: 20.4 kN

question: A specimen under stress 90 MPa shows an elastic strain of 2.2e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 90, eps = 2.2 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 90 / (2.2e-3) MPa = 40.91 GPa | Answer: 40.91 GPa

question: A block of mass 28 kg has a volume of 4.7e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 28, V = 4.7 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 28 / (4.7e-3) | Answer: 5957 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 1600 mm is heated through 20 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 11e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 1600, dT = 20, al = 11 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 1600*11e-6*20 | Answer: 0.352 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 185 ohm, R2 = 95 ohm and R3 = 100 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 185, R2 = 95, R3 = 100 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 95*100 / 185 | Answer: 51.35 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 1000 ohm and gauge factor 2.1 experiences a strain of 1450e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 1000, GF = 2.1, eps = 1450 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 1000*2.1*1450e-6 | Answer: 3045 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 10.26 when the true value is 10. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10.26, true = 10 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10.26 - 10| / 10 * 100 | Answer: 2.6 %

question: Annual demand is 4000 units, ordering cost 230 per order and holding cost 18 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 4000, S = 230, H = 18 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*4000*230 / 18) | Answer: 319.7 units

question: An asset costs 410000 with salvage value 36000 after 7 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 410000, Sv = 36000, n = 7 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (410000 - 36000) / 7 | Answer: 53429 per year

question: A product sells for 230 per unit with variable cost 40 per unit and fixed costs 195000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 230, V = 40, F = 195000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 195000 / (230 - 40) | Answer: 1026 units

question: Find the present worth of 155000 received 8 years from now at an interest rate of 8% per year.
solution: Given: F = 155000, n = 8, i = 8 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 155000 / (1 + 0.08)^8 | Answer: 83742 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.91, 0.92 and 0.92 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.91, r2 = 0.92, r3 = 0.92 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.91*0.92*0.92 | Answer: 0.7702

question: A process produces 39 defective items in a batch of 16500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 39, N = 16500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 39/16500 * 1e6 | Answer: 2364 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = 2x^3 - 3x^2 - 6x + 3 evaluated at x = 1.
For f(x) = -3x^3 + 8x^2 - 5x - 7, find f''(x) at x = 5.
Evaluate the definite integral of (-4x^2 + x - 7) dx from x = -4 to x = 7.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = -4x^3/3 + 1x^2/2 + -7x | Evaluate F(7) - F(-4) | Answer: -603.2
