question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 25, 12, 25, 1, 12.
solution: Mean = 15 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 10.17

question: Find the slope of the line through (5, 6) and (-1, 3).
solution: Given: x1 = 5, y1 = 6, x2 = -1, y2 = 3 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (3 - 6) / (-1 - 5) | Answer: 0.5

question: Find the distance between the points (5, -8) and (-7, 7).
solution: Given: x1 = 5, y1 = -8, x2 = -7, y2 = 7 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-12)^2 + (15)^2) | Answer: 19.21 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (-7,0), (2,-4), (-2,4).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 28 sq units

question: Evaluate the number of combinations C(13, 7).
solution: Given: n = 13, r = 7 | Formula: C(n, r) = n! / (r! (n - r)!) | Substitute: C(13, 7) = 13! / (7! * 6!) | Answer: 1716

question: Find the 34th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 20 and common difference -6.
solution: Given: a = 20, d = -6, n = 34 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = 20 + (34 - 1)*-6 | Answer: -178

question: Find the sum of the first 32 terms of an AP with first term -8 and common difference -1.
solution: Given: a = -8, d = -1, n = 32 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 32/2 [2*-8 + (32-1)*-1] | Answer: -752

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 10000 at 5.8% per annum for 8 years.
solution: Given: P = 10000, R = 5.8, Tt = 8 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 10000 * 5.8 * 8 / 100 | Answer: 4640 currency units

question: Find the amount when 40000 is invested at 4.1% per annum compounded annually for 5 years.
solution: Given: P = 40000, R = 4.1, Tt = 5 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 40000 * (1 + 4.1/100)^5 | Answer: 48901 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (-4, 3, -8) and (0, -5, -3).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (-1, -3, 3) and (-1, 2, -6).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 15.81

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (-2, -6, 5) and (-2, -6, -2).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 55.88 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number -10 + -8i.
solution: Given: a = -10, b = -8 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((-10)^2 + (-8)^2) | Answer: 12.81

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number -11 + 11i.
solution: Given: a = -11, b = 11 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(11, -11) | Answer: 135 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -2x^3 - 2x^2 - 4x - 1 at x = 4.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-95 with initial guess x0=13, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.7 and ordinates 4, 7, 3, 18, 3, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 378 and 285.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 378 and 285 | Answer: GCD = 3

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 56 and 80.
solution: Given: a = 56, b = 80 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 56*80 / 8 | Answer: 560
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 43 mm carries an axial tensile load of 59 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 27 mm and length 500 mm carries an axial load of 65 kN. Take E = 70 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 44 mm transmits a torque of 650 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 44, Tt = 650 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(650*1000) / (pi*(44)^3) | Answer: 38.86 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 47 mm and length 700 mm carries a torque of 1550 N-m. With G = 80 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (47)^4 / 32 = 479062 mm^4 | theta = (1550*1000)(700) / (80000 * 479062) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 1.622 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 93 mm wide and 280 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 93, h = 280 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 93*(280)^2 / 6 | Answer: 1215200 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (51 mm x 250 mm) carries a bending moment of 32 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (78 mm x 150 mm) has effective length 3000 mm and E = 200 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 780 MPa is designed for a working stress of 120 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 780, sw = 120 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 780 / 120 | Answer: 6.5

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 650 mm and wall thickness 15 mm carries an internal pressure of 2.4 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 650, t = 15, P = 2.4 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 2.4*650 / (2*15) | Answer: 52 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 940 K and 430 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 940, Tc = 430 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 430/940) * 100 | Answer: 54.26 %

question: A refrigerator works between 259 K (cold) and 316 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 259, Th = 316 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 259 / (316 - 259) | Answer: 4.544

question: A heat pump operates between 285 K and 314 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 285, Th = 314 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 314 / (314 - 285) | Answer: 10.83

question: 3.2 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 165 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.2, dT = 165 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 3.2 * 0.718 * 165 | Answer: 379.1 kJ

question: 2.2 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 55 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.2, dT = 55 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 2.2 * 1.005 * 55 | Answer: 121.6 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 1.9 m^3 at 490 K with mass 5.6 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 1.9, Tk = 490, m = 5.6 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 5.6*0.287*490 / 1.9 | Answer: 414.5 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 3.4 kg of air expands isothermally at 500 K from volume V1 to 4*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.4, Tk = 500, ratio = 4 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 3.4*0.287*500*ln(4) | Answer: 676.4 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 4 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.13 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 4, D = 0.13 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*4*0.13 / 0.001 | Answer: 520000

question: Water flows at 2.3 m/s through a pipe of diameter 290 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 13 m. Taking Cv = 0.99, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 13, cv = 0.99 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.99*sqrt(2*9.81*13) | Answer: 15.81 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 220 mm) water flows at 1.2 m/s. It contracts to diameter 70 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 220, d2 = 70, V1 = 1.2 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 1.2*(220/70)^2 | Answer: 11.85 m/s

question: Water flows at 1.5 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.44 m and length 370 m. With friction factor f = 0.037, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 38 teeth drives a gear of 91 teeth. If the pinion runs at 550 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 38, z2 = 91, N1 = 550 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 550*38 / 91 | Answer: 229.7 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 280 mm rotates at 1200 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 280, N = 1200 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.28)*1200 / 60 | Answer: 17.59 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 25.2 kW at 700 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 25.2, N = 700 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(25.2*1000) / (2*pi*700) | Answer: 343.8 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 3.5 kg rotates at radius 0.5 m at 550 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 1200 N/m and mass 19.5 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 1200, m = 19.5 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(1200/19.5) | Answer: 1.249 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 2.8 m^2 and thickness 0.27 m has conductivity k = 30.6 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 95 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 2.8, L = 0.27, k = 30.6, dT = 95 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 30.6*2.8*95 / 0.27 | Answer: 30147 W

question: A surface of area 0.6 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 160 W/m^2-K to surroundings 135 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 0.6, h = 160, dT = 135 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 160*0.6*135 | Answer: 12960 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 90 m/min, feed = 0.34 mm/rev, depth of cut = 1.6 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 90, f = 0.34, d = 1.6 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*90*0.34*1.6 | Answer: 48960 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 430 mm is turned at 950 rpm with a feed of 0.21 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 430, N = 950, f = 0.21 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 430 / (0.21*950) | Answer: 2.155 min

question: A resistor of 14 ohm carries a current of 6.2 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 14, I = 6.2 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 6.2 * 14 | Answer: 86.8 V

question: Three resistors 28 ohm, 29 ohm and 45 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 28, R2 = 29, R3 = 45 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 28 + 29 + 45 | Answer: 102 ohm

question: Two resistors 4 ohm and 34 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 4, R2 = 34 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 4*34 / (4+34) | Answer: 3.579 ohm

question: A device draws 12.1 A at 35 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 35, I = 12.1 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 35 * 12.1 | Answer: 423.5 W

question: A current of 5.6 A flows through a 117 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 5.6, R = 117 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (5.6)^2 * 117 | Answer: 3669 W

question: Two capacitors 3.8 uF and 35.3 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 3.8, C2 = 35.3 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 3.8*35.3 / (3.8+35.3) | Answer: 3.431 uF

question: A resistor 89 kohm and capacitor 17 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 89, C = 17 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (89k)(17u) = 1513 ms | Answer: 1513 ms

question: An inductor 268 mH is in series with 50 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 268, R = 50 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (268e-3) / 50 | Answer: 5.36 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 20.6 mH inductor at 560 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 20.6, f = 560 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (560)(20.6e-3) | Answer: 72.48 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 6.7 uF capacitor at 420 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 6.7, f = 420 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (420)(6.7e-6)) | Answer: 56.56 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 84 ohm, XL = 150 ohm and XC = 14 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 84, XL = 150, XC = 14 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(84^2 + (150 - 14)^2) | Answer: 159.8 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 10.9 mH and C = 3.4 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 10.9, C = 3.4 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(10.9e-3 * 3.4e-6)) | Answer: 826.7 Hz

question: A capacitor of 66.6 uF is charged to 30 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 66.6, V = 30 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*66.6e-6*(30)^2 | Answer: 29.97 mJ

question: An alternating voltage has a peak value of 212 V. Find its RMS value.
solution: Given: Vp = 212 | Formula: Vrms = Vp / sqrt(2) | Substitute: Vrms = 212 / sqrt(2) | Answer: 149.9 V

question: A transformer has primary voltage 350 V with 920 primary turns and 120 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 350, N1 = 920, N2 = 120 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 350 * 120/920 | Answer: 45.65 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 380 V and draws an armature current of 27 A. If the armature resistance is 0.31 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 380, Ia = 27, Ra = 0.31 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 380 - 27*0.31 | Answer: 371.6 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 140 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.77. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 140, VL = 400, pf = 0.77 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*400*140*0.77 / 1000 | Answer: 74.69 kW

question: A load has real power 110 kW and apparent power 210 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 110, S = 210 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 110 / 210 | Answer: 0.5238

question: A machine delivers 80 kW output while drawing 152 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 80, Pi = 152 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 80/152 * 100 | Answer: 52.63 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 12 V across R1 = 43 ohm and R2 = 27 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 12, R1 = 43, R2 = 27 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 12*27 / (43+27) | Answer: 4.629 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 140 kohm and Rin = 33 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 140, Rin = 33 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 140 / 33 | Answer: 4.242

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 10 kohm and Rg = 37 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 10, Rg = 37 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 10/37 | Answer: 1.27

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 8686. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 8686 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(8686) | Answer: 39.39 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 3.2 m carries a central point load of 90 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.2, W = 90 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 90*3.2 / 4 | Answer: 72 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.6 m carries a UDL of 60 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 9.6, w = 60 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 60*(9.6)^2 / 8 | Answer: 691.2 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 1.8 m carries a point load 30 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 1.8, W = 30 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 30*1.8 | Answer: 54 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 1.4 m carries a UDL of 4 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 1.4, w = 4 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 4*(1.4)^2 / 2 | Answer: 3.92 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.5 m carries a point load 15 kN at distance 3.4 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 9.5, a = 3.4, W = 15 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 15*(9.5 - 3.4) / 9.5 | Answer: 9.632 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 5.1 m) carries a central point load 75 kN. With E = 30 GPa and I = 140e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=75000 N, L=5100.0 mm, E=30000 MPa, I=140e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 49.35 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 7 m carries a UDL of 27 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7, w = 27 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 27*(7)^2 / 12 | Answer: 110.2 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 670 mm, clear cover 30 mm and main bars of diameter 16 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 670, c = 30, dia = 16 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 670 - 30 - 16/2 | Answer: 632 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 17.7 m^2 carrying a factored load of 16.8 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 17.7, w = 16.8 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 16.8 * 17.7 | Answer: 297.4 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 3.9 m, unit weight 18 kN/m^3, phi = 36 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 9 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 19 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 9, g = 19 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (19 - 9.81)*9 | Answer: 82.71 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 2e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.9, area = 4e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 2, i = 0.9, A = 4 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (2e-4)*0.9*(4e-3) | Answer: 720 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.9 m, bed slope 0.005 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.023. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 2.8 m under a head of 0.9 m. Taking Cd = 0.61 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 5.3 m wide carries a discharge of 13.4 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 140 m and design speed 45 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 140, V = 45 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (45)^2 / (127*140) | Answer: 0.1139
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: For a design speed of 45 km/h with allowable superelevation 0.08 and lateral friction 0.13, find the minimum curve radius in m.
A tank of volume 240 m^3 treats a flow of 170 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 240, Q = 170 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 240 / 170 | Answer: 1.412 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 150 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.11 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 5 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 150, k = 0.11, t = 5 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 150*(1 - e^(-0.11*5)) | Answer: 63.46 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.82, rainfall intensity 85 mm/h over a catchment of 32.1 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.82, i = 85, A = 32.1 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.82*85*32.1 / 360 | Answer: 6.215 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.04 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 370 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.04, M = 370 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 370*(30+0.04)/30 | Answer: 370.5 m

question: Convert the decimal number 174 to binary.
solution: Divide 174 by 2 repeatedly, recording remainders | Reading remainders in reverse gives 10101110 | Answer: 10101110 (binary)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 2 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the decimal number 2253 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 2253 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 8CD (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the 8-bit binary number 01010101 to decimal.
solution: Binary 01010101 = sum of bit-weights | Answer: 85 (decimal)
formula: Sum each bit times its positional weight (2^i)

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 00100101 and 11010011.
solution: XOR: 11110110 | Count of 1s = 6 | Answer: 6
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 750 megabits is sent over a link of 7 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 750, B = 7 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 750 / 7 | Answer: 107.1 s

question: A link has bandwidth 52 Mbps and round-trip time 110 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 52, R = 110 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 52e6 * 110e-3 bits = 5720 kb | Answer: 5720 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.89, cache access time 1 ns and main-memory access time 200 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.89, tc = 1, tm = 200 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.89*1 + (1 - 0.89)*200 | Answer: 22.89 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 121519 elements?
solution: Given: n = 121519 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(121519)) + 1 | Answer: 17

question: An O(n^2) algorithm performs c*n^2 basic operations. If c = 1 and n = 1620, how many operations are performed?
solution: Given: n = 1620 | Formula: operations = n^2 | Substitute: = (1620)^2 | Answer: 2624400

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.004, memory access time 120 ns and page-fault service time 6 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 6 ms = 6000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.004)*120 + 0.004*6000000.0 ns | Answer: 24.12 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 0.1 m^3 at 470 kPa and 340 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 0.1, P = 470, Tk = 340 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (470e3)*0.1 / (8.314*340) | Answer: 16.63 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.34 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 10 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.34, t = 10 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.34*10) | Answer: 0.9666

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.34 /min) is to reach 70% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.34, X = 70 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.7) / 0.34 | Answer: 3.541 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.43 /min) reaches 70% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.43, X = 70 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.7 / (0.43*(1 - 0.7)) | Answer: 5.426 min

question: For a reaction with A = 8e10 /s and activation energy 85 kJ/mol at 470 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 8, Ea = 85, Tk = 470 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 8e10 * exp(-85e3 / (8.314*470)) | Answer: 28.58 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.95 and bottoms xW = 0.04, with relative volatility alpha = 2.9. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.95, xw = 0.04, al = 2.9 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.95/0.05)(0.96/0.04)] / ln(2.9) | Answer: 5.75 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.88 and x = 0.48. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.88, x = 0.48 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.88/0.12) / (0.48/0.52) | Answer: 7.944

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.35 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 40 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.35, Psat = 40 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.35 * 40 | Answer: 14 kPa

question: A stream of 2.8 kg/s with specific heat 1.8 kJ/kg-K is heated through 105 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 2.8, cp = 1.8, dT = 105 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 2.8*1.8*105 | Answer: 529.2 kW

question: A reactor of volume 14 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 0.6 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 14, Q = 0.6 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 14 / 0.6 | Answer: 23.33 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 6.7e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 1 mm with a concentration difference of 10 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 6.7, L = 1, dC = 10 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (6.7e-9)*10 / (1e-3) | Answer: 67 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 4.3 min and steady-state gain 1. For a step input of magnitude 13, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 4.3, K = 1, M = 13 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 1 * 13 | Answer: 13 units

question: A reactor operates at a space time of 16.8 min. Find its space velocity in per hour.
solution: Given: tau = 16.8 | Formula: SV = 60 / tau  (per hour) | Substitute: SV = 60 / 16.8 | Answer: 3.571 /h

question: An aircraft wing of area 60 m^2 flies at 70 m/s (air density 1 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 1. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 60, V = 70, rho = 1, CL = 1 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1*(70)^2*60*1 / 1000 | Answer: 147 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 110 m^2 flies at 250 m/s (density 1 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.06. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 110, V = 250, rho = 1, CD = 0.06 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*1*(250)^2*110*0.06 / 1000 | Answer: 206.2 kN

question: A specimen under stress 300 MPa shows an elastic strain of 2e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 300, eps = 2 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 300 / (2e-3) MPa = 150 GPa | Answer: 150 GPa

question: A block of mass 11 kg has a volume of 1.4e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 11, V = 1.4 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 11 / (1.4e-3) | Answer: 7857 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 2700 mm is heated through 70 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 17e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 2700, dT = 70, al = 17 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 2700*17e-6*70 | Answer: 3.213 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 155 ohm, R2 = 25 ohm and R3 = 10 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 155, R2 = 25, R3 = 10 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 25*10 / 155 | Answer: 1.613 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 120 ohm and gauge factor 2.1 experiences a strain of 400e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 120, GF = 2.1, eps = 400 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 120*2.1*400e-6 | Answer: 100.8 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 10.42 when the true value is 50. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10.42, true = 50 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10.42 - 50| / 50 * 100 | Answer: 79.16 %

question: Annual demand is 50000 units, ordering cost 250 per order and holding cost 35 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 50000, S = 250, H = 35 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*50000*250 / 35) | Answer: 845.2 units

question: An asset costs 460000 with salvage value 40000 after 7 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 460000, Sv = 40000, n = 7 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (460000 - 40000) / 7 | Answer: 60000 per year

question: A product sells for 420 per unit with variable cost 160 per unit and fixed costs 165000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 420, V = 160, F = 165000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 165000 / (420 - 160) | Answer: 634.6 units

question: Find the present worth of 75000 received 2 years from now at an interest rate of 9% per year.
solution: Given: F = 75000, n = 2, i = 9 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 75000 / (1 + 0.09)^2 | Answer: 63126 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.93, 0.95 and 0.98 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.93, r2 = 0.95, r3 = 0.98 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.93*0.95*0.98 | Answer: 0.8658

question: A process produces 47 defective items in a batch of 16500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 47, N = 16500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 47/16500 * 1e6 | Answer: 2848 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -2x^3 - 5x^2 + 1 evaluated at x = -4.
For f(x) = -6x^3 + x^2 + 5x - 1, find f''(x) at x = -3.
Evaluate the definite integral of (-4x^2 - 6x + 6) dx from x = -1 to x = 4.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = -4x^3/3 + -6x^2/2 + 6x | Evaluate F(4) - F(-1) | Answer: -101.7
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of x^2 - 2x - 8 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[6, 6], [4, 6]].
solution: Given: a = 6, b = 6, c = 4, d = 6 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (6)(6) - (6)(4) | Answer: 12

question: Find the determinant of [[-4, -4, 1], [5, -4, -3], [3, 5, -6]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: -203

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[-4, 3], [8, 7]].
solution: Trace tr = 3, Determinant = -52 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 8.865

question: Solve for x: -3x + 6y = 5 and -5x + 0y = -4.
solution: Determinant = -3*0 - 6*-5 = 30 | x = (e d - b f) / det = 0.8 | Answer: x = 0.8
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 62, 2, 54, 48, 76.
solution: Sum = 242 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 48.4 | Answer: 48.4

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 16, 14, 29, 5, 24.
solution: Mean = 17.6 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 9.29

question: Find the slope of the line through (9, -3) and (-3, -9).
solution: Given: x1 = 9, y1 = -3, x2 = -3, y2 = -9 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (-9 - -3) / (-3 - 9) | Answer: 0.5

question: Find the distance between the points (9, -9) and (9, -5).
solution: Given: x1 = 9, y1 = -9, x2 = 9, y2 = -5 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((0)^2 + (4)^2) | Answer: 4 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (-6,-8), (-6,2), (-1,-3).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 25 sq units

question: Find the 11th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 5 and common difference 1.
solution: Given: a = 5, d = 1, n = 11 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = 5 + (11 - 1)*1 | Answer: 15

question: Find the sum of the first 39 terms of an AP with first term 6 and common difference -3.

question: A rectangular beam section is 41 mm wide and 100 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 41, h = 100 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 41*(100)^2 / 6 | Answer: 68333 mm^3

formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 480 MPa is designed for a working stress of 140 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 480, sw = 140 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 480 / 140 | Answer: 3.429

question: A steel bar is fully restrained and heated through 60 deg C. With E = 210 GPa and alpha = 13e-6 /deg C, find the thermal stress in MPa.
solution: Given: dT = 60, E = 210, al = 13 | Formula: sigma = E alpha (dT) | Substitute: sigma = 210000 * 13e-6 * 60 | Answer: 163.8 MPa

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 600 mm and wall thickness 12 mm carries an internal pressure of 0.9 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 600, t = 12, P = 0.9 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 0.9*600 / (2*12) | Answer: 22.5 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 620 K and 420 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 620, Tc = 420 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 420/620) * 100 | Answer: 32.26 %

question: A refrigerator works between 269 K (cold) and 318 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 269, Th = 318 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 269 / (318 - 269) | Answer: 5.49

question: A heat pump operates between 263 K and 312 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 263, Th = 312 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 312 / (312 - 263) | Answer: 6.367

question: 6.6 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 145 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 6.6, dT = 145 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 6.6 * 0.718 * 145 | Answer: 687.1 kJ

question: 6.6 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 45 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 6.6, dT = 45 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 6.6 * 1.005 * 45 | Answer: 298.5 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 3 m^3 at 310 K with mass 1.2 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).

formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 1.6 kg of air expands isothermally at 330 K from volume V1 to 2*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1.6, Tk = 330, ratio = 2 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 1.6*0.287*330*ln(2) | Answer: 105 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 2.9 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.2 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 2.9, D = 0.2 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*2.9*0.2 / 0.001 | Answer: 580000

question: Water flows at 1.2 m/s through a pipe of diameter 230 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 8.5 m. Taking Cv = 0.97, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).

question: In a pipe (diameter 250 mm) water flows at 1.1 m/s. It contracts to diameter 130 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
Water flows at 3.4 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.11 m and length 170 m. With friction factor f = 0.02, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 27 teeth drives a gear of 84 teeth. If the pinion runs at 800 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.

question: A pulley of diameter 260 mm rotates at 650 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.

question: A shaft transmits 44.3 kW at 450 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 44.3, N = 450 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(44.3*1000) / (2*pi*450) | Answer: 940.1 N-m

question: A mass of 4.5 kg rotates at radius 0.49 m at 300 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 800 N/m and mass 1.3 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 800, m = 1.3 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(800/1.3) | Answer: 3.948 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 6.4 m^2 and thickness 0.38 m has conductivity k = 35.4 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 190 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 6.4, L = 0.38, k = 35.4, dT = 190 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 35.4*6.4*190 / 0.38 | Answer: 113280 W

question: A surface of area 3.9 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 85 W/m^2-K to surroundings 60 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 3.9, h = 85, dT = 60 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 85*3.9*60 | Answer: 19890 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 90 m/min, feed = 0.27 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2.7 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 90, f = 0.27, d = 2.7 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*90*0.27*2.7 | Answer: 65610 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 90 mm is turned at 950 rpm with a feed of 0.24 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 90, N = 950, f = 0.24 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 90 / (0.24*950) | Answer: 0.3947 min

question: A resistor of 136 ohm carries a current of 4.2 A. Find the voltage across it.

question: Three resistors 1 ohm, 72 ohm and 91 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 1, R2 = 72, R3 = 91 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 1 + 72 + 91 | Answer: 164 ohm

question: Two resistors 98 ohm and 9 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 98, R2 = 9 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 98*9 / (98+9) | Answer: 8.243 ohm

question: A device draws 5.2 A at 45 V. Find the power consumed.

question: A current of 1.3 A flows through a 5 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.

question: Two capacitors 25.7 uF and 6.6 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 25.7, C2 = 6.6 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 25.7*6.6 / (25.7+6.6) | Answer: 5.251 uF

question: A resistor 18 kohm and capacitor 19.5 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.

question: An inductor 91.4 mH is in series with 108 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 91.4, R = 108 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (91.4e-3) / 108 | Answer: 0.8463 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 146.4 mH inductor at 270 Hz.

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 48 uF capacitor at 250 Hz.

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 30 ohm, XL = 85 ohm and XC = 104 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.

question: A capacitor of 89.6 uF is charged to 245 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 110 kohm and Rin = 28 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.3 m carries a central point load of 80 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.

question: A cantilever of length 3.3 m carries a point load 80 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.1 m carries a point load 50 kN at distance 1.7 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.

question: A simply supported beam (span 7.5 m) carries a central point load 25 kN. With E = 200 GPa and I = 70e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.

question: A fixed beam of span 6.5 m carries a UDL of 6 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6.5, w = 6 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 6*(6.5)^2 / 12 | Answer: 21.12 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 640 mm, clear cover 45 mm and main bars of diameter 20 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 640, c = 45, dia = 20 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 640 - 45 - 20/2 | Answer: 585 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 23.5 m^2 carrying a factored load of 17.6 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 23.5, w = 17.6 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 17.6 * 23.5 | Answer: 413.6 kN

question: At a depth of 6.4 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 18 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 6.6e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.5, area = 3.9e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.

question: For a design speed of 85 km/h with allowable superelevation 0.05 and lateral friction 0.15, find the minimum curve radius in m.

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 280 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.33 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 6 days.

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.79, rainfall intensity 40 mm/h over a catchment of 9.7 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.

formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A file of 110 megabits is sent over a link of 22 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.

solution: Given: B = 32, R = 10 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 32e6 * 10e-3 bits = 320 kb | Answer: 320 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.85, cache access time 2 ns and main-memory access time 170 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 290386 elements?

question: An O(n^2) algorithm performs c*n^2 basic operations. If c = 1 and n = 2400, how many operations are performed?
solution: Given: n = 2400 | Formula: operations = n^2 | Substitute: = (2400)^2 | Answer: 5760000

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.018, memory access time 180 ns and page-fault service time 10 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 1.6 m^3 at 130 kPa and 590 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.33 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 18 minutes.

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.46 /min) is to reach 50% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.46, X = 50 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.5) / 0.46 | Answer: 1.507 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.26 /min) reaches 85% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.26, X = 85 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.85 / (0.26*(1 - 0.85)) | Answer: 21.79 min

question: For a reaction with A = 2e10 /s and activation energy 50 kJ/mol at 310 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 2, Ea = 50, Tk = 310 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 2e10 * exp(-50e3 / (8.314*310)) | Answer: 75.12 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.95 and bottoms xW = 0.07, with relative volatility alpha = 2.9. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.95, xw = 0.07, al = 2.9 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.95/0.05)(0.93/0.07)] / ln(2.9) | Answer: 5.195 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.85 and x = 0.43. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.85, x = 0.43 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.85/0.15) / (0.43/0.57) | Answer: 7.512

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.29 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 115 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.29, Psat = 115 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.29 * 115 | Answer: 33.35 kPa

question: A stream of 9.3 kg/s with specific heat 2.9 kJ/kg-K is heated through 65 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 9.3, cp = 2.9, dT = 65 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 9.3*2.9*65 | Answer: 1753 kW

question: A reactor of volume 16.6 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 1.4 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 16.6, Q = 1.4 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 16.6 / 1.4 | Answer: 11.86 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 2e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 1 mm with a concentration difference of 80 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 2, L = 1, dC = 80 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (2e-9)*80 / (1e-3) | Answer: 160 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 3.2 min and steady-state gain 1.4. For a step input of magnitude 11, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 3.2, K = 1.4, M = 11 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 1.4 * 11 | Answer: 15.4 units

question: A reactor operates at a space time of 4.3 min. Find its space velocity in per hour.
solution: Given: tau = 4.3 | Formula: SV = 60 / tau  (per hour) | Substitute: SV = 60 / 4.3 | Answer: 13.95 /h

question: An aircraft wing of area 75 m^2 flies at 190 m/s (air density 1.225 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.9. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 75, V = 190, rho = 1.225, CL = 0.9 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1.225*(190)^2*75*0.9 / 1000 | Answer: 1493 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 115 m^2 flies at 250 m/s (density 1 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.08. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 115, V = 250, rho = 1, CD = 0.08 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*1*(250)^2*115*0.08 / 1000 | Answer: 287.5 kN

question: A specimen under stress 400 MPa shows an elastic strain of 1.2e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 400, eps = 1.2 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 400 / (1.2e-3) MPa = 333.3 GPa | Answer: 333.3 GPa

question: A block of mass 2 kg has a volume of 1.3e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 2, V = 1.3 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 2 / (1.3e-3) | Answer: 1538 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 1300 mm is heated through 150 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 11e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 1300, dT = 150, al = 11 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 1300*11e-6*150 | Answer: 2.145 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 65 ohm, R2 = 160 ohm and R3 = 130 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 65, R2 = 160, R3 = 130 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 160*130 / 65 | Answer: 320 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 120 ohm and gauge factor 2.1 experiences a strain of 350e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 120, GF = 2.1, eps = 350 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 120*2.1*350e-6 | Answer: 88.2 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 10.69 when the true value is 10. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10.69, true = 10 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10.69 - 10| / 10 * 100 | Answer: 6.9 %

question: Annual demand is 50000 units, ordering cost 180 per order and holding cost 6 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 50000, S = 180, H = 6 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*50000*180 / 6) | Answer: 1732 units

question: An asset costs 330000 with salvage value 8000 after 18 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 330000, Sv = 8000, n = 18 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (330000 - 8000) / 18 | Answer: 17889 per year

question: A product sells for 50 per unit with variable cost 40 per unit and fixed costs 65000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 50, V = 40, F = 65000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 65000 / (50 - 40) | Answer: 6500 units

question: Find the present worth of 195000 received 6 years from now at an interest rate of 7% per year.
solution: Given: F = 195000, n = 6, i = 7 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 195000 / (1 + 0.07)^6 | Answer: 129937 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.91, 0.95 and 0.98 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.91, r2 = 0.95, r3 = 0.98 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.91*0.95*0.98 | Answer: 0.8472

question: A process produces 7 defective items in a batch of 1500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 7, N = 1500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 7/1500 * 1e6 | Answer: 4667 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -5x^3 + 3x^2 + 6x - 2 evaluated at x = 5.
For f(x) = 2x^3 - 4x + 7, find f''(x) at x = -5.
Evaluate the definite integral of (-5x^2 - 5x - 3) dx from x = -1 to x = 5.

question: Find the larger real root of 4x^2 + 6x + 1 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[-1, 9], [-8, 8]].
solution: Given: a = -1, b = 9, c = -8, d = 8 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (-1)(8) - (9)(-8) | Answer: 64

question: Find the determinant of [[1, -2, -5], [0, 3, -4], [6, -1, 6]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: 152

question: Solve for x: 4x + 2y = 0 and -1x + -2y = -5.
solution: Determinant = 4*-2 - 2*-1 = -6 | x = (e d - b f) / det = -1.667 | Answer: x = -1.667

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 52, 7, 90, 93, 30.
solution: Sum = 272 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 54.4 | Answer: 54.4

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 46, 15, 31, 7, 8.
solution: Mean = 21.4 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 16.77

question: Find the slope of the line through (-5, 7) and (0, 3).
solution: Given: x1 = -5, y1 = 7, x2 = 0, y2 = 3 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (3 - 7) / (0 - -5) | Answer: -0.8

question: Find the distance between the points (7, 3) and (3, 5).
solution: Given: x1 = 7, y1 = 3, x2 = 3, y2 = 5 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-4)^2 + (2)^2) | Answer: 4.472 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (-8,0), (3,-6), (-8,-7).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 38.5 sq units

question: Find the 12th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 3 and common difference -1.
solution: Given: a = 3, d = -1, n = 12 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = 3 + (12 - 1)*-1 | Answer: -8

question: Find the sum of the first 37 terms of an AP with first term 9 and common difference 8.
solution: Given: a = 9, d = 8, n = 37 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 37/2 [2*9 + (37-1)*8] | Answer: 5661

question: Find the 4th term of a geometric progression with first term 7 and common ratio 3.
solution: Given: a = 7, r = 3, n = 4 | Formula: a_n = a r^(n-1) | Substitute: a_n = 7 * 3^(4-1) | Answer: 189

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 9000 at 12.3% per annum for 1 years.
solution: Given: P = 9000, R = 12.3, Tt = 1 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 9000 * 12.3 * 1 / 100 | Answer: 1107 currency units

question: Find the amount when 11000 is invested at 10.1% per annum compounded annually for 6 years.
solution: Given: P = 11000, R = 10.1, Tt = 6 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 11000 * (1 + 10.1/100)^6 | Answer: 19594 currency units

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (4, 1, -2) and (2, 4, 1).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 61.56 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number -3 + -10i.
solution: Given: a = -3, b = -10 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((-3)^2 + (-10)^2) | Answer: 10.44

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number 12 + 10i.
solution: Given: a = 12, b = 10 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(10, 12) | Answer: 39.81 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -5x^3 - 4x^2 + 8x + 8 at x = -5.

Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=0.5 and ordinates 4, 19, 13, 6, 19, estimate the integral.

solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 455 and 238 | Answer: GCD = 7

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 38 and 52.
solution: Given: a = 38, b = 52 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 38*52 / 2 | Answer: 988

question: A circular rod of diameter 28 mm carries an axial tensile load of 94 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 20 mm and length 2900 mm carries an axial load of 90 kN. Take E = 200 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 51 mm transmits a torque of 2850 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 51, Tt = 2850 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(2850*1000) / (pi*(51)^3) | Answer: 109.4 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 47 mm and length 1000 mm carries a torque of 1950 N-m. With G = 80 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (47)^4 / 32 = 479062 mm^4 | theta = (1950*1000)(1000) / (80000 * 479062) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 2.915 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 128 mm wide and 100 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 128, h = 100 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 128*(100)^2 / 6 | Answer: 213333 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (57 mm x 140 mm) carries a bending moment of 30 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (52 mm x 110 mm) has effective length 2800 mm and E = 200 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 720 MPa is designed for a working stress of 230 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 720, sw = 230 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 720 / 230 | Answer: 3.13

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 550 mm and wall thickness 7 mm carries an internal pressure of 1.8 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 550, t = 7, P = 1.8 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 1.8*550 / (2*7) | Answer: 70.71 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 640 K and 420 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 640, Tc = 420 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 420/640) * 100 | Answer: 34.38 %

question: A refrigerator works between 270 K (cold) and 322 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 270, Th = 322 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 270 / (322 - 270) | Answer: 5.192

question: A heat pump operates between 270 K and 300 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 270, Th = 300 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 300 / (300 - 270) | Answer: 10

question: 6.8 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 115 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 6.8, dT = 115 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 6.8 * 0.718 * 115 | Answer: 561.5 kJ

question: 2.4 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 25 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.4, dT = 25 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 2.4 * 1.005 * 25 | Answer: 60.3 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 3.8 m^3 at 330 K with mass 1.2 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 3.8, Tk = 330, m = 1.2 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 1.2*0.287*330 / 3.8 | Answer: 29.91 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 4.5 kg of air expands isothermally at 360 K from volume V1 to 2*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.5, Tk = 360, ratio = 2 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 4.5*0.287*360*ln(2) | Answer: 322.3 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 4 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.39 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 4, D = 0.39 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*4*0.39 / 0.001 | Answer: 1560000

question: Water flows at 1.9 m/s through a pipe of diameter 190 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 15 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 15 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*15 / 1000 | Answer: 147.2 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 7.9 m. Taking Cv = 0.97, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 7.9, cv = 0.97 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.97*sqrt(2*9.81*7.9) | Answer: 12.08 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 290 mm) water flows at 0.9 m/s. It contracts to diameter 60 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 290, d2 = 60, V1 = 0.9 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 0.9*(290/60)^2 | Answer: 21.02 m/s

question: Water flows at 2.7 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.21 m and length 100 m. With friction factor f = 0.033, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 39 teeth drives a gear of 105 teeth. If the pinion runs at 700 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 39, z2 = 105, N1 = 700 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 700*39 / 105 | Answer: 260 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 520 mm rotates at 1150 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 520, N = 1150 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.52)*1150 / 60 | Answer: 31.31 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 24.2 kW at 900 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 24.2, N = 900 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(24.2*1000) / (2*pi*900) | Answer: 256.8 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 7.3 kg rotates at radius 0.38 m at 1100 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 6100 N/m and mass 3 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 6100, m = 3 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(6100/3) | Answer: 7.177 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 2.5 m^2 and thickness 0.35 m has conductivity k = 29.5 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 40 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 2.5, L = 0.35, k = 29.5, dT = 40 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 29.5*2.5*40 / 0.35 | Answer: 8429 W

question: A surface of area 5.4 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 110 W/m^2-K to surroundings 55 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 5.4, h = 110, dT = 55 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 110*5.4*55 | Answer: 32670 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 170 m/min, feed = 0.26 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2.6 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 170, f = 0.26, d = 2.6 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*170*0.26*2.6 | Answer: 114920 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 450 mm is turned at 800 rpm with a feed of 0.24 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 450, N = 800, f = 0.24 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 450 / (0.24*800) | Answer: 2.344 min

question: A resistor of 149 ohm carries a current of 2 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 149, I = 2 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 2 * 149 | Answer: 298 V

question: Three resistors 97 ohm, 82 ohm and 99 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 97, R2 = 82, R3 = 99 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 97 + 82 + 99 | Answer: 278 ohm

question: Two resistors 91 ohm and 7 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 91, R2 = 7 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 91*7 / (91+7) | Answer: 6.5 ohm

question: A device draws 5.2 A at 25 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 25, I = 5.2 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 25 * 5.2 | Answer: 130 W

question: A current of 6 A flows through a 72 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 6, R = 72 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (6)^2 * 72 | Answer: 2592 W

question: Two capacitors 23.9 uF and 47.2 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 23.9, C2 = 47.2 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 23.9*47.2 / (23.9+47.2) | Answer: 15.87 uF

question: A resistor 18 kohm and capacitor 13.1 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 18, C = 13.1 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (18k)(13.1u) = 235.8 ms | Answer: 235.8 ms

question: An inductor 41.8 mH is in series with 183 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 41.8, R = 183 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (41.8e-3) / 183 | Answer: 0.2284 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 135.7 mH inductor at 210 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 135.7, f = 210 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (210)(135.7e-3) | Answer: 179.1 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 11.9 uF capacitor at 930 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 11.9, f = 930 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (930)(11.9e-6)) | Answer: 14.38 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 47 ohm, XL = 137 ohm and XC = 48 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 47, XL = 137, XC = 48 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(47^2 + (137 - 48)^2) | Answer: 100.6 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 38.2 mH and C = 4.5 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 38.2, C = 4.5 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(38.2e-3 * 4.5e-6)) | Answer: 383.9 Hz

question: A capacitor of 17.9 uF is charged to 320 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 17.9, V = 320 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*17.9e-6*(320)^2 | Answer: 916.5 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 270 V with 540 primary turns and 130 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 270, N1 = 540, N2 = 130 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 270 * 130/540 | Answer: 65 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 190 V and draws an armature current of 50 A. If the armature resistance is 0.14 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 190, Ia = 50, Ra = 0.14 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 190 - 50*0.14 | Answer: 183 V

question: A 4-pole induction motor on a 50 Hz supply runs at 820 rpm. Find the slip (%).

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 155 A at 415 V (line) with a power factor of 0.87. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 155, VL = 415, pf = 0.87 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*415*155*0.87 / 1000 | Answer: 96.93 kW

question: A load has real power 160 kW and apparent power 185 kVA. Find the power factor.

question: A machine delivers 105 kW output while drawing 132 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 17 V across R1 = 35 ohm and R2 = 3 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 180 kohm and Rin = 37 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 140 kohm and Rg = 14 kohm. Find the voltage gain.

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 105. Express the gain in decibels (power).

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.4 m carries a central point load of 75 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.4, W = 75 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 75*4.4 / 4 | Answer: 82.5 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.7 m carries a UDL of 25 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 9.7, w = 25 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 25*(9.7)^2 / 8 | Answer: 294 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 3.5 m carries a point load 10 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.5, W = 10 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 10*3.5 | Answer: 35 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 1.8 m carries a UDL of 12 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 1.8, w = 12 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 12*(1.8)^2 / 2 | Answer: 19.44 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 7.3 m carries a point load 35 kN at distance 2.9 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.

question: A simply supported beam (span 7.2 m) carries a central point load 50 kN. With E = 200 GPa and I = 460e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.

question: A fixed beam of span 6.2 m carries a UDL of 21 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6.2, w = 21 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 21*(6.2)^2 / 12 | Answer: 67.27 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 500 mm, clear cover 45 mm and main bars of diameter 20 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 500, c = 45, dia = 20 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 500 - 45 - 20/2 | Answer: 445 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 39 m^2 carrying a factored load of 10.8 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 39, w = 10.8 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 10.8 * 39 | Answer: 421.2 kN

question: For a bar of diameter 20 mm with design bond stress 2.2 MPa and steel stress 435 MPa, find the development length in mm.
solution: Given: dia = 20, tbd = 2.2, fs = 435 | Formula: Ld = phi fs / (4 tau_bd) | Substitute: Ld = 20*435 / (4*2.2) | Answer: 988.6 mm

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 6.9 m, unit weight 18 kN/m^3, phi = 35 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).

question: At a depth of 7.1 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 20 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 7.1, g = 20 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (20 - 9.81)*7.1 | Answer: 72.35 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 2e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.5, area = 7.2e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 180 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.13 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 5 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 180, k = 0.13, t = 5 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 180*(1 - e^(-0.13*5)) | Answer: 86.03 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.58, rainfall intensity 120 mm/h over a catchment of 18.6 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.58, i = 120, A = 18.6 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.58*120*18.6 / 360 | Answer: 3.596 m^3/s

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.06 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 190 m with this tape.

question: A file of 100 megabits is sent over a link of 18 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.

question: A link has bandwidth 37 Mbps and round-trip time 40 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.85, cache access time 6 ns and main-memory access time 70 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.85, tc = 6, tm = 70 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.85*6 + (1 - 0.85)*70 | Answer: 15.6 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 599861 elements?
solution: Given: n = 599861 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(599861)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: An O(n^2) algorithm performs c*n^2 basic operations. If c = 1 and n = 1550, how many operations are performed?
solution: Given: n = 1550 | Formula: operations = n^2 | Substitute: = (1550)^2 | Answer: 2402500

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.009, memory access time 140 ns and page-fault service time 7 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 7 ms = 7000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.009)*140 + 0.009*7000000.0 ns | Answer: 63.14 microseconds

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 0.6 m^3 at 150 kPa and 540 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 0.6, P = 150, Tk = 540 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (150e3)*0.6 / (8.314*540) | Answer: 20.05 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.36 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 2 minutes.

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.34 /min) is to reach 50% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.22 /min) reaches 70% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.

question: For a reaction with A = 3e10 /s and activation energy 75 kJ/mol at 460 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.99 and bottoms xW = 0.02, with relative volatility alpha = 3.3. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.61 and x = 0.3. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.61, x = 0.3 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.61/0.39) / (0.3/0.7) | Answer: 3.65

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.8 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 90 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.

question: A stream of 0.9 kg/s with specific heat 3.3 kJ/kg-K is heated through 105 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.

question: A reactor of volume 8 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 4.4 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 4.8e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 4 mm with a concentration difference of 90 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.

question: A first-order process has time constant 3.4 min and steady-state gain 1. For a step input of magnitude 5, find the final (steady-state) change in output.

question: An aircraft wing of area 65 m^2 flies at 180 m/s (air density 1.225 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 1.4. Find the lift force in kN.

question: An aircraft of wing area 50 m^2 flies at 170 m/s (density 0.4 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.03. Find the drag force in kN.

question: A specimen under stress 240 MPa shows an elastic strain of 1e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.

question: A block of mass 45 kg has a volume of 4e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.

question: A rod of length 1700 mm is heated through 40 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 12e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 15 ohm, R2 = 175 ohm and R3 = 180 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).

question: A strain gauge of resistance 1000 ohm and gauge factor 2.2 experiences a strain of 1850e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.

question: A measurement reads 10.35 when the true value is 100. Find the percentage error.

question: Annual demand is 25000 units, ordering cost 270 per order and holding cost 17 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 25000, S = 270, H = 17 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*25000*270 / 17) | Answer: 891.1 units

question: An asset costs 130000 with salvage value 10000 after 14 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 130000, Sv = 10000, n = 14 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (130000 - 10000) / 14 | Answer: 8571 per year

question: A product sells for 480 per unit with variable cost 90 per unit and fixed costs 100000. Find the break-even quantity in units.

question: Find the present worth of 80000 received 5 years from now at an interest rate of 9% per year.

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.96, 0.92 and 0.98 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.

question: A process produces 6 defective items in a batch of 17000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).

question: Find the distance between the points (7, -7) and (8, 8).

question: Evaluate the number of combinations C(16, 5).

question: Find the 32th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 7 and common difference 7.

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 29000 at 14.9% per annum for 1 years.

solution: Given: su = 830, sw = 130 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 830 / 130 | Answer: 6.385

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 300 mm and wall thickness 14 mm carries an internal pressure of 1.2 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 300, t = 14, P = 1.2 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 1.2*300 / (2*14) | Answer: 12.86 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 800 K and 390 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 800, Tc = 390 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 390/800) * 100 | Answer: 51.25 %

question: A refrigerator works between 274 K (cold) and 316 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 274, Th = 316 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 274 / (316 - 274) | Answer: 6.524

question: A heat pump operates between 275 K and 316 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 275, Th = 316 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 316 / (316 - 275) | Answer: 7.707

question: 5.4 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 20 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 5.4, dT = 20 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 5.4 * 0.718 * 20 | Answer: 77.54 kJ

question: 5.1 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 95 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 5.1, dT = 95 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 5.1 * 1.005 * 95 | Answer: 486.9 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 0.6 m^3 at 370 K with mass 6 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 0.6, Tk = 370, m = 6 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 6*0.287*370 / 0.6 | Answer: 1062 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 3.5 kg of air expands isothermally at 460 K from volume V1 to 3*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.5, Tk = 460, ratio = 3 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 3.5*0.287*460*ln(3) | Answer: 507.6 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 0.9 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.06 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 0.9, D = 0.06 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*0.9*0.06 / 0.001 | Answer: 54000

question: Water flows at 0.7 m/s through a pipe of diameter 50 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 28.9 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 28.9 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*28.9 / 1000 | Answer: 283.5 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 17 m. Taking Cv = 0.95, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 17, cv = 0.95 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.95*sqrt(2*9.81*17) | Answer: 17.35 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 360 mm) water flows at 0.7 m/s. It contracts to diameter 80 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 360, d2 = 80, V1 = 0.7 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 0.7*(360/80)^2 | Answer: 14.17 m/s

question: Water flows at 1.1 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.23 m and length 360 m. With friction factor f = 0.035, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 29 teeth drives a gear of 78 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1200 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 29, z2 = 78, N1 = 1200 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1200*29 / 78 | Answer: 446.2 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 100 mm rotates at 750 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 100, N = 750 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.1)*750 / 60 | Answer: 3.927 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 18.4 kW at 1100 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 18.4, N = 1100 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(18.4*1000) / (2*pi*1100) | Answer: 159.7 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 2.8 kg rotates at radius 0.28 m at 1100 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 10100 N/m and mass 16.7 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 10100, m = 16.7 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(10100/16.7) | Answer: 3.914 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 4.3 m^2 and thickness 0.33 m has conductivity k = 31.9 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 190 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 4.3, L = 0.33, k = 31.9, dT = 190 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 31.9*4.3*190 / 0.33 | Answer: 78977 W

question: A surface of area 0.6 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 155 W/m^2-K to surroundings 35 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 0.6, h = 155, dT = 35 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 155*0.6*35 | Answer: 3255 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 100 m/min, feed = 0.37 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2.8 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 100, f = 0.37, d = 2.8 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*100*0.37*2.8 | Answer: 103600 mm^3/min
