question: A circular rod of diameter 60 mm carries an axial tensile load of 33 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 37 mm and length 700 mm carries an axial load of 16 kN. Take E = 110 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 22 mm transmits a torque of 150 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 22, Tt = 150 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(150*1000) / (pi*(22)^3) | Answer: 71.75 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 34 mm and length 1700 mm carries a torque of 1500 N-m. With G = 45 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (34)^4 / 32 = 131194 mm^4 | theta = (1500*1000)(1700) / (45000 * 131194) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 24.75 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 37 mm wide and 210 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 37, h = 210 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 37*(210)^2 / 6 | Answer: 271950 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (69 mm x 200 mm) carries a bending moment of 27 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (47 mm x 100 mm) has effective length 3900 mm and E = 200 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 600 MPa is designed for a working stress of 110 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 600, sw = 110 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 600 / 110 | Answer: 5.455

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 500 mm and wall thickness 16 mm carries an internal pressure of 2.5 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 500, t = 16, P = 2.5 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 2.5*500 / (2*16) | Answer: 39.06 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 1100 K and 390 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 1100, Tc = 390 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 390/1100) * 100 | Answer: 64.55 %

question: A refrigerator works between 257 K (cold) and 330 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 257, Th = 330 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 257 / (330 - 257) | Answer: 3.521

question: A heat pump operates between 284 K and 312 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 284, Th = 312 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 312 / (312 - 284) | Answer: 11.14

question: 1.1 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 45 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1.1, dT = 45 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 1.1 * 0.718 * 45 | Answer: 35.54 kJ

question: 5.2 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 140 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 5.2, dT = 140 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 5.2 * 1.005 * 140 | Answer: 731.6 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 0.8 m^3 at 450 K with mass 1.7 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 0.8, Tk = 450, m = 1.7 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 1.7*0.287*450 / 0.8 | Answer: 274.4 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 4 kg of air expands isothermally at 310 K from volume V1 to 5*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4, Tk = 310, ratio = 5 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 4*0.287*310*ln(5) | Answer: 572.8 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 3.1 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.31 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 3.1, D = 0.31 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*3.1*0.31 / 0.001 | Answer: 961000

question: Water flows at 2.4 m/s through a pipe of diameter 150 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 20.7 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 20.7 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*20.7 / 1000 | Answer: 203.1 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 19 m. Taking Cv = 0.98, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 19, cv = 0.98 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.98*sqrt(2*9.81*19) | Answer: 18.92 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 190 mm) water flows at 0.6 m/s. It contracts to diameter 110 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 190, d2 = 110, V1 = 0.6 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 0.6*(190/110)^2 | Answer: 1.79 m/s

question: Water flows at 3 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.22 m and length 290 m. With friction factor f = 0.032, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 34 teeth drives a gear of 104 teeth. If the pinion runs at 950 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 34, z2 = 104, N1 = 950 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 950*34 / 104 | Answer: 310.6 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 360 mm rotates at 550 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 360, N = 550 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.36)*550 / 60 | Answer: 10.37 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 3.8 kW at 1250 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 3.8, N = 1250 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(3.8*1000) / (2*pi*1250) | Answer: 29.03 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 6.5 kg rotates at radius 0.13 m at 600 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 13400 N/m and mass 1.7 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 13400, m = 1.7 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(13400/1.7) | Answer: 14.13 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 6.3 m^2 and thickness 0.38 m has conductivity k = 43.4 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 30 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 6.3, L = 0.38, k = 43.4, dT = 30 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 43.4*6.3*30 / 0.38 | Answer: 21586 W

question: A surface of area 2.7 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 190 W/m^2-K to surroundings 30 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 2.7, h = 190, dT = 30 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 190*2.7*30 | Answer: 15390 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 160 m/min, feed = 0.13 mm/rev, depth of cut = 1.4 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 160, f = 0.13, d = 1.4 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*160*0.13*1.4 | Answer: 29120 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 130 mm is turned at 400 rpm with a feed of 0.16 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 130, N = 400, f = 0.16 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 130 / (0.16*400) | Answer: 2.031 min

question: A resistor of 142 ohm carries a current of 3.3 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 142, I = 3.3 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 3.3 * 142 | Answer: 468.6 V

question: Three resistors 40 ohm, 35 ohm and 75 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 40, R2 = 35, R3 = 75 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 40 + 35 + 75 | Answer: 150 ohm

question: Two resistors 7 ohm and 45 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 7, R2 = 45 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 7*45 / (7+45) | Answer: 6.058 ohm

question: A device draws 6.6 A at 165 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 165, I = 6.6 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 165 * 6.6 | Answer: 1089 W

question: A current of 10.9 A flows through a 55 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 10.9, R = 55 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (10.9)^2 * 55 | Answer: 6535 W

question: Two capacitors 2.9 uF and 41.1 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 2.9, C2 = 41.1 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 2.9*41.1 / (2.9+41.1) | Answer: 2.709 uF

question: A resistor 60 kohm and capacitor 2.6 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 60, C = 2.6 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (60k)(2.6u) = 156 ms | Answer: 156 ms

question: An inductor 155.8 mH is in series with 102 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 155.8, R = 102 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (155.8e-3) / 102 | Answer: 1.527 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 54.1 mH inductor at 450 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 54.1, f = 450 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (450)(54.1e-3) | Answer: 153 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 27.1 uF capacitor at 790 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 27.1, f = 790 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (790)(27.1e-6)) | Answer: 7.434 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 52 ohm, XL = 110 ohm and XC = 68 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 52, XL = 110, XC = 68 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(52^2 + (110 - 68)^2) | Answer: 66.84 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 80.4 mH and C = 7.1 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 80.4, C = 7.1 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(80.4e-3 * 7.1e-6)) | Answer: 210.7 Hz

question: A capacitor of 61.2 uF is charged to 65 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 61.2, V = 65 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*61.2e-6*(65)^2 | Answer: 129.3 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 280 V with 320 primary turns and 50 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 280, N1 = 320, N2 = 50 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 280 * 50/320 | Answer: 43.75 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 270 V and draws an armature current of 20 A. If the armature resistance is 0.98 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 270, Ia = 20, Ra = 0.98 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 270 - 20*0.98 | Answer: 250.4 V

question: A 6-pole induction motor on a 60 Hz supply runs at 920 rpm. Find the slip (%).
formula: s = (Ns - N) / Ns,  Ns = 120 f / P

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 145 A at 415 V (line) with a power factor of 0.9. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 145, VL = 415, pf = 0.9 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*415*145*0.9 / 1000 | Answer: 93.8 kW

question: A load has real power 165 kW and apparent power 170 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 165, S = 170 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 165 / 170 | Answer: 0.9706

question: A machine delivers 20 kW output while drawing 92 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 20, Pi = 92 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 20/92 * 100 | Answer: 21.74 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 19 V across R1 = 25 ohm and R2 = 9 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 19, R1 = 25, R2 = 9 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 19*9 / (25+9) | Answer: 5.029 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 50 kohm and Rin = 41 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 50, Rin = 41 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 50 / 41 | Answer: 1.22

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 20 kohm and Rg = 5 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 20, Rg = 5 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 20/5 | Answer: 5

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 129. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 129 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(129) | Answer: 21.11 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 3.3 m carries a central point load of 20 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.3, W = 20 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 20*3.3 / 4 | Answer: 16.5 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 9 m carries a UDL of 5 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 9, w = 5 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 5*(9)^2 / 8 | Answer: 50.62 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 4.2 m carries a point load 40 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.2, W = 40 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 40*4.2 | Answer: 168 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 2.4 m carries a UDL of 26 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 2.4, w = 26 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 26*(2.4)^2 / 2 | Answer: 74.88 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 8.6 m carries a point load 75 kN at distance 3.9 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 8.6, a = 3.9, W = 75 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 75*(8.6 - 3.9) / 8.6 | Answer: 40.99 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 4.4 m) carries a central point load 80 kN. With E = 30 GPa and I = 250e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=80000 N, L=4400.0 mm, E=30000 MPa, I=250e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 18.93 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 7.9 m carries a UDL of 45 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7.9, w = 45 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 45*(7.9)^2 / 12 | Answer: 234 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 300 mm, clear cover 25 mm and main bars of diameter 12 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 300, c = 25, dia = 12 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 300 - 25 - 12/2 | Answer: 269 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 21.5 m^2 carrying a factored load of 9.5 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 21.5, w = 9.5 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 9.5 * 21.5 | Answer: 204.2 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 3.9 m, unit weight 20 kN/m^3, phi = 35 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 11.8 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 18 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 11.8, g = 18 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (18 - 9.81)*11.8 | Answer: 96.64 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 6.3e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1.3, area = 4e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 6.3, i = 1.3, A = 4 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (6.3e-4)*1.3*(4e-3) | Answer: 3276 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.1 m, bed slope 0.008 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.025. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 1.5 m under a head of 0.8 m. Taking Cd = 0.63 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 5.2 m wide carries a discharge of 27.1 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 580 m and design speed 80 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 580, V = 80 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (80)^2 / (127*580) | Answer: 0.08689
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: A tank of volume 700 m^3 treats a flow of 150 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 700, Q = 150 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 700 / 150 | Answer: 4.667 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 230 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.27 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 7 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 230, k = 0.27, t = 7 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 230*(1 - e^(-0.27*7)) | Answer: 195.3 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.57, rainfall intensity 30 mm/h over a catchment of 26.8 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.57, i = 30, A = 26.8 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.57*30*26.8 / 360 | Answer: 1.273 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.02 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 760 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.02, M = 760 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 760*(30+0.02)/30 | Answer: 760.5 m

question: Convert the decimal number 3174 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 3174 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: C66 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the 8-bit binary number 10110111 to decimal.
solution: Binary 10110111 = sum of bit-weights | Answer: 183 (decimal)
formula: Sum each bit times its positional weight (2^i)

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 10010000 and 11110001.
solution: XOR: 01100001 | Count of 1s = 3 | Answer: 3
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 550 megabits is sent over a link of 71 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 550, B = 71 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 550 / 71 | Answer: 7.746 s

question: A link has bandwidth 19 Mbps and round-trip time 10 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 19, R = 10 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 19e6 * 10e-3 bits = 190 kb | Answer: 190 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.81, cache access time 3 ns and main-memory access time 120 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.81, tc = 3, tm = 120 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.81*3 + (1 - 0.81)*120 | Answer: 25.23 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 757570 elements?
solution: Given: n = 757570 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(757570)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: An O(n^2) algorithm performs c*n^2 basic operations. If c = 1 and n = 1790, how many operations are performed?
solution: Given: n = 1790 | Formula: operations = n^2 | Substitute: = (1790)^2 | Answer: 3204100

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.013, memory access time 90 ns and page-fault service time 3 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 3 ms = 3000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.013)*90 + 0.013*3000000.0 ns | Answer: 39.09 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 2.2 m^3 at 210 kPa and 490 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 2.2, P = 210, Tk = 490 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (210e3)*2.2 / (8.314*490) | Answer: 113.4 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.24 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 16 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.24, t = 16 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.24*16) | Answer: 0.9785

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.17 /min) is to reach 85% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.17, X = 85 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.85) / 0.17 | Answer: 11.16 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.5 /min) reaches 90% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.5, X = 90 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.9 / (0.5*(1 - 0.9)) | Answer: 18 min

question: For a reaction with A = 4e10 /s and activation energy 65 kJ/mol at 460 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 4, Ea = 65, Tk = 460 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 4e10 * exp(-65e3 / (8.314*460)) | Answer: 1663 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.95 and bottoms xW = 0.08, with relative volatility alpha = 1.9. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.95, xw = 0.08, al = 1.9 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.95/0.05)(0.92/0.08)] / ln(1.9) | Answer: 8.393 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.84 and x = 0.39. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.84, x = 0.39 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.84/0.16) / (0.39/0.61) | Answer: 8.212

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.75 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 25 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.75, Psat = 25 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.75 * 25 | Answer: 18.75 kPa

question: A stream of 0.7 kg/s with specific heat 2.3 kJ/kg-K is heated through 30 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 0.7, cp = 2.3, dT = 30 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 0.7*2.3*30 | Answer: 48.3 kW

question: A reactor of volume 10.5 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 4.5 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 10.5, Q = 4.5 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 10.5 / 4.5 | Answer: 2.333 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 1.3e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 5 mm with a concentration difference of 150 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 1.3, L = 5, dC = 150 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (1.3e-9)*150 / (5e-3) | Answer: 39 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 6.3 min and steady-state gain 2.2. For a step input of magnitude 15, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 6.3, K = 2.2, M = 15 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 2.2 * 15 | Answer: 33 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 15 m^2 flies at 100 m/s (air density 0.7 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.7. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 15, V = 100, rho = 0.7, CL = 0.7 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.7*(100)^2*15*0.7 / 1000 | Answer: 36.75 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 35 m^2 flies at 130 m/s (density 1 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.1. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 35, V = 130, rho = 1, CD = 0.1 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*1*(130)^2*35*0.1 / 1000 | Answer: 29.57 kN

question: A specimen under stress 400 MPa shows an elastic strain of 2.3e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 400, eps = 2.3 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 400 / (2.3e-3) MPa = 173.9 GPa | Answer: 173.9 GPa

question: A block of mass 4 kg has a volume of 3.6e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 4, V = 3.6 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 4 / (3.6e-3) | Answer: 1111 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 1900 mm is heated through 120 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 17e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 1900, dT = 120, al = 17 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 1900*17e-6*120 | Answer: 3.876 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 120 ohm, R2 = 110 ohm and R3 = 120 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 120, R2 = 110, R3 = 120 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 110*120 / 120 | Answer: 110 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 350 ohm and gauge factor 2.2 experiences a strain of 950e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 350, GF = 2.2, eps = 950 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 350*2.2*950e-6 | Answer: 731.5 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 9.5 when the true value is 100. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.5, true = 100 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.5 - 100| / 100 * 100 | Answer: 90.5 %

question: Annual demand is 30500 units, ordering cost 260 per order and holding cost 36 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 30500, S = 260, H = 36 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*30500*260 / 36) | Answer: 663.7 units

question: An asset costs 300000 with salvage value 6000 after 7 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 300000, Sv = 6000, n = 7 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (300000 - 6000) / 7 | Answer: 42000 per year

question: A product sells for 120 per unit with variable cost 100 per unit and fixed costs 90000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 120, V = 100, F = 90000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 90000 / (120 - 100) | Answer: 4500 units

question: Find the present worth of 75000 received 10 years from now at an interest rate of 6% per year.
solution: Given: F = 75000, n = 10, i = 6 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 75000 / (1 + 0.06)^10 | Answer: 4188 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.91, 0.97 and 0.94 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.91, r2 = 0.97, r3 = 0.94 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.91*0.97*0.94 | Answer: 0.8297

question: A process produces 29 defective items in a batch of 13000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 29, N = 13000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 29/13000 * 1e6 | Answer: 2231 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = 6x^3 + 5x + 9 evaluated at x = -3.
For f(x) = 5x^3 + 4x^2 - 7x - 6, find f''(x) at x = 0.
Evaluate the definite integral of (2x^2 - 6x - 1) dx from x = -3 to x = 6.

question: Find the larger real root of 3x^2 - 8x - 5 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[7, 2], [-9, -9]].

solution: Mean = 19 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 17.85

question: Find the slope of the line through (0, -7) and (-4, -8).
solution: Given: x1 = 0, y1 = -7, x2 = -4, y2 = -8 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (-8 - -7) / (-4 - 0) | Answer: 0.25

question: Find the distance between the points (2, 6) and (-1, -4).
solution: Given: x1 = 2, y1 = 6, x2 = -1, y2 = -4 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-3)^2 + (-10)^2) | Answer: 10.44 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (0,1), (7,-6), (-5,4).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 7 sq units

question: Evaluate the number of combinations C(14, 3).
solution: Given: n = 14, r = 3 | Formula: C(n, r) = n! / (r! (n - r)!) | Substitute: C(14, 3) = 14! / (3! * 11!) | Answer: 364

question: Find the 26th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 16 and common difference 0.
solution: Given: a = 16, d = 0, n = 26 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = 16 + (26 - 1)*0 | Answer: 16

question: Find the sum of the first 5 terms of an AP with first term -3 and common difference -5.
solution: Given: a = -3, d = -5, n = 5 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 5/2 [2*-3 + (5-1)*-5] | Answer: -65

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 24000 at 9.6% per annum for 8 years.
solution: Given: P = 24000, R = 9.6, Tt = 8 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 24000 * 9.6 * 8 / 100 | Answer: 18432 currency units

question: Find the amount when 14500 is invested at 7.8% per annum compounded annually for 5 years.
solution: Given: P = 14500, R = 7.8, Tt = 5 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 14500 * (1 + 7.8/100)^5 | Answer: 21109 currency units

question: Find the modulus of the complex number 6 + 4i.
solution: Given: a = 6, b = 4 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((6)^2 + (4)^2) | Answer: 7.211

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number -9 + -8i.
solution: Given: a = -9, b = -8 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(-8, -9) | Answer: -138.4 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = 5x^3 + 4x^2 + 3x - 2 at x = -2.

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 23 and 72.

question: A circular rod of diameter 34 mm carries an axial tensile load of 13 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.

A solid shaft of diameter 59 mm transmits a torque of 1200 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.

question: A shaft of diameter 46 mm and length 1500 mm carries a torque of 2000 N-m. With G = 77 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (46)^4 / 32 = 439573 mm^4 | theta = (2000*1000)(1500) / (77000 * 439573) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 5.078 degrees

question: A rectangular beam section is 135 mm wide and 200 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 135, h = 200 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 135*(200)^2 / 6 | Answer: 900000 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (75 mm x 260 mm) carries a bending moment of 24 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.

question: A rectangular column (50 mm x 100 mm) has effective length 3300 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 390 MPa is designed for a working stress of 70 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 390, sw = 70 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 390 / 70 | Answer: 5.571

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1500 mm and wall thickness 10 mm carries an internal pressure of 1.4 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1500, t = 10, P = 1.4 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 1.4*1500 / (2*10) | Answer: 105 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 700 K and 330 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 700, Tc = 330 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 330/700) * 100 | Answer: 52.86 %

question: A refrigerator works between 262 K (cold) and 322 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 262, Th = 322 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 262 / (322 - 262) | Answer: 4.367

question: A heat pump operates between 279 K and 300 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 279, Th = 300 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 300 / (300 - 279) | Answer: 14.29

question: 2.6 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 165 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.6, dT = 165 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 2.6 * 0.718 * 165 | Answer: 308 kJ

question: 2.5 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 125 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.5, dT = 125 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 2.5 * 1.005 * 125 | Answer: 314.1 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 2.8 m^3 at 370 K with mass 5.1 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 2.8, Tk = 370, m = 5.1 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 5.1*0.287*370 / 2.8 | Answer: 193.4 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 4.7 kg of air expands isothermally at 500 K from volume V1 to 2*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.7, Tk = 500, ratio = 2 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 4.7*0.287*500*ln(2) | Answer: 467.5 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 3.7 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.18 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 3.7, D = 0.18 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*3.7*0.18 / 0.001 | Answer: 666000

question: Water flows at 2.9 m/s through a pipe of diameter 250 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 5.3 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 5.3 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*5.3 / 1000 | Answer: 51.99 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 1 m. Taking Cv = 0.96, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 1, cv = 0.96 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.96*sqrt(2*9.81*1) | Answer: 4.252 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 190 mm) water flows at 2.1 m/s. It contracts to diameter 140 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
Water flows at 3 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.41 m and length 500 m. With friction factor f = 0.028, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 33 teeth drives a gear of 76 teeth. If the pinion runs at 500 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 33, z2 = 76, N1 = 500 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 500*33 / 76 | Answer: 217.1 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 380 mm rotates at 550 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 380, N = 550 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.38)*550 / 60 | Answer: 10.94 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 20.7 kW at 1300 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 20.7, N = 1300 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(20.7*1000) / (2*pi*1300) | Answer: 152.1 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 3.8 kg rotates at radius 0.52 m at 800 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 19800 N/m and mass 12.9 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 19800, m = 12.9 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(19800/12.9) | Answer: 6.235 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 4.8 m^2 and thickness 0.34 m has conductivity k = 21.3 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 40 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 4.8, L = 0.34, k = 21.3, dT = 40 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 21.3*4.8*40 / 0.34 | Answer: 12028 W

question: A surface of area 4.1 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 80 W/m^2-K to surroundings 40 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 4.1, h = 80, dT = 40 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 80*4.1*40 | Answer: 13120 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 250 m/min, feed = 0.25 mm/rev, depth of cut = 0.7 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 250, f = 0.25, d = 0.7 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*250*0.25*0.7 | Answer: 43750 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 350 mm is turned at 300 rpm with a feed of 0.13 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 350, N = 300, f = 0.13 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 350 / (0.13*300) | Answer: 8.974 min

question: A resistor of 37 ohm carries a current of 2.3 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 37, I = 2.3 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 2.3 * 37 | Answer: 85.1 V

question: Three resistors 81 ohm, 20 ohm and 3 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 81, R2 = 20, R3 = 3 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 81 + 20 + 3 | Answer: 104 ohm

question: Two resistors 82 ohm and 110 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 82, R2 = 110 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 82*110 / (82+110) | Answer: 46.98 ohm

question: A device draws 14.5 A at 195 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 195, I = 14.5 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 195 * 14.5 | Answer: 2828 W

question: A current of 2.9 A flows through a 30 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 2.9, R = 30 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (2.9)^2 * 30 | Answer: 252.3 W

question: Two capacitors 11 uF and 35.9 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 11, C2 = 35.9 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 11*35.9 / (11+35.9) | Answer: 8.42 uF

question: A resistor 32 kohm and capacitor 9.9 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 32, C = 9.9 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (32k)(9.9u) = 316.8 ms | Answer: 316.8 ms

question: An inductor 307.7 mH is in series with 24 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 307.7, R = 24 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (307.7e-3) / 24 | Answer: 12.82 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 171.9 mH inductor at 270 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 171.9, f = 270 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (270)(171.9e-3) | Answer: 291.6 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 30.4 uF capacitor at 440 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 30.4, f = 440 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (440)(30.4e-6)) | Answer: 11.9 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 74 ohm, XL = 122 ohm and XC = 122 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 74, XL = 122, XC = 122 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(74^2 + (122 - 122)^2) | Answer: 74 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 58.6 mH and C = 6.9 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 58.6, C = 6.9 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(58.6e-3 * 6.9e-6)) | Answer: 250.3 Hz

question: A capacitor of 18.7 uF is charged to 240 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 18.7, V = 240 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*18.7e-6*(240)^2 | Answer: 538.6 mJ

question: An alternating voltage has a peak value of 32 V. Find its RMS value.
solution: Given: Vp = 32 | Formula: Vrms = Vp / sqrt(2) | Substitute: Vrms = 32 / sqrt(2) | Answer: 22.63 V

question: A transformer has primary voltage 260 V with 820 primary turns and 270 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 260, N1 = 820, N2 = 270 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 260 * 270/820 | Answer: 85.61 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 130 V and draws an armature current of 37 A. If the armature resistance is 0.28 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 130, Ia = 37, Ra = 0.28 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 130 - 37*0.28 | Answer: 119.6 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 90 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.72. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 90, VL = 400, pf = 0.72 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*400*90*0.72 / 1000 | Answer: 44.89 kW

question: A load has real power 85 kW and apparent power 135 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 85, S = 135 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 85 / 135 | Answer: 0.6296

question: A machine delivers 160 kW output while drawing 212 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 13 V across R1 = 43 ohm and R2 = 5 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 30 kohm and Rin = 16 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.8 m carries a central point load of 95 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.

question: A simply supported beam of span 3.6 m carries a UDL of 30 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.

question: A cantilever of length 5.8 m carries a point load 55 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.8, W = 55 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 55*5.8 | Answer: 319 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 5.8 m carries a UDL of 14 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.

question: A simply supported beam of span 7.7 m carries a point load 60 kN at distance 2.9 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.

question: A simply supported beam (span 4.4 m) carries a central point load 30 kN. With E = 30 GPa and I = 280e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.

question: An RC beam has overall depth 420 mm, clear cover 40 mm and main bars of diameter 16 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.

question: A column supports a floor area of 10.4 m^2 carrying a factored load of 10.8 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.

solution: Given: z = 5.9, g = 19 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (19 - 9.81)*5.9 | Answer: 54.22 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 2.5e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.8, area = 7.1e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.

question: For a design speed of 75 km/h with allowable superelevation 0.05 and lateral friction 0.16, find the minimum curve radius in m.

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 170 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.1 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 5 days.

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.77, rainfall intensity 60 mm/h over a catchment of 29.7 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.

formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.06 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 320 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.06, M = 320 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 320*(30+0.06)/30 | Answer: 320.6 m

question: A file of 960 megabits is sent over a link of 19 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.

question: A link has bandwidth 26 Mbps and round-trip time 150 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 26, R = 150 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 26e6 * 150e-3 bits = 3900 kb | Answer: 3900 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.82, cache access time 2 ns and main-memory access time 90 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.82, tc = 2, tm = 90 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.82*2 + (1 - 0.82)*90 | Answer: 17.84 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 814137 elements?
solution: Given: n = 814137 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(814137)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: An O(n^2) algorithm performs c*n^2 basic operations. If c = 1 and n = 2350, how many operations are performed?
solution: Given: n = 2350 | Formula: operations = n^2 | Substitute: = (2350)^2 | Answer: 5522500

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.015, memory access time 120 ns and page-fault service time 7 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 7 ms = 7000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.015)*120 + 0.015*7000000.0 ns | Answer: 105.1 microseconds

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 0.4 m^3 at 330 kPa and 500 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 0.4, P = 330, Tk = 500 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (330e3)*0.4 / (8.314*500) | Answer: 31.75 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.27 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 11 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.27, t = 11 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.27*11) | Answer: 0.9487

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.5 /min) is to reach 65% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.5, X = 65 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.65) / 0.5 | Answer: 2.1 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.39 /min) reaches 90% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.39, X = 90 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.9 / (0.39*(1 - 0.9)) | Answer: 23.08 min

question: For a reaction with A = 1e10 /s and activation energy 70 kJ/mol at 360 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 1, Ea = 70, Tk = 360 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 1e10 * exp(-70e3 / (8.314*360)) | Answer: 0.6965 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.93 and bottoms xW = 0.08, with relative volatility alpha = 2.6. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.93, xw = 0.08, al = 2.6 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.93/0.07)(0.92/0.08)] / ln(2.6) | Answer: 5.263 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.75 and x = 0.21. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.21 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 95 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.

question: A stream of 2.7 kg/s with specific heat 3.7 kJ/kg-K is heated through 25 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.

question: A reactor of volume 18 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 4.7 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 18, Q = 4.7 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 18 / 4.7 | Answer: 3.83 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 2.9e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 4 mm with a concentration difference of 190 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 2.9, L = 4, dC = 190 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (2.9e-9)*190 / (4e-3) | Answer: 137.8 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 8.1 min and steady-state gain 3.6. For a step input of magnitude 10, find the final (steady-state) change in output.

question: An aircraft wing of area 90 m^2 flies at 170 m/s (air density 0.7 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.5. Find the lift force in kN.

question: An aircraft of wing area 75 m^2 flies at 260 m/s (density 1 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.03. Find the drag force in kN.

question: An aircraft flies at 570 m/s where the speed of sound is 340 m/s. Find the Mach number.

question: A specimen under stress 80 MPa shows an elastic strain of 1.9e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.

question: A block of mass 45 kg has a volume of 2.5e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.

question: A rod of length 1000 mm is heated through 95 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 17e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 25 ohm, R2 = 140 ohm and R3 = 265 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).

question: A strain gauge of resistance 120 ohm and gauge factor 2.2 experiences a strain of 1700e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.

question: A measurement reads 10.69 when the true value is 20. Find the percentage error.

question: Annual demand is 45000 units, ordering cost 290 per order and holding cost 6 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).

question: An asset costs 420000 with salvage value 26000 after 18 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.

question: A product sells for 110 per unit with variable cost 90 per unit and fixed costs 105000. Find the break-even quantity in units.

question: Find the present worth of 50000 received 2 years from now at an interest rate of 12% per year.

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.96, 0.9 and 0.9 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.

question: A process produces 10 defective items in a batch of 2000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).

question: Find the 15th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -10 and common difference 5.

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 46000 at 12.3% per annum for 6 years.

question: Find the amount when 15500 is invested at 5.2% per annum compounded annually for 6 years.

question: A circular rod of diameter 23 mm carries an axial tensile load of 28 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.

question: A component of ultimate strength 450 MPa is designed for a working stress of 120 MPa. Find the factor of safety.

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 350 mm and wall thickness 13 mm carries an internal pressure of 1.1 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.

question: A Carnot engine operates between 1200 K and 330 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).

question: A refrigerator works between 261 K (cold) and 318 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.

question: A heat pump operates between 282 K and 304 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 282, Th = 304 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 304 / (304 - 282) | Answer: 13.82

question: 3.8 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 30 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.8, dT = 30 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 3.8 * 0.718 * 30 | Answer: 81.85 kJ

question: 7.5 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 120 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 7.5, dT = 120 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 7.5 * 1.005 * 120 | Answer: 904.5 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 3 m^3 at 460 K with mass 2.8 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 3, Tk = 460, m = 2.8 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 2.8*0.287*460 / 3 | Answer: 123.2 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 4.2 kg of air expands isothermally at 440 K from volume V1 to 2*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.2, Tk = 440, ratio = 2 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 4.2*0.287*440*ln(2) | Answer: 367.6 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 4 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.22 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 4, D = 0.22 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*4*0.22 / 0.001 | Answer: 880000

question: Water flows at 4 m/s through a pipe of diameter 250 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 29.2 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 29.2 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*29.2 / 1000 | Answer: 286.5 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 15.3 m. Taking Cv = 0.96, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 15.3, cv = 0.96 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.96*sqrt(2*9.81*15.3) | Answer: 16.63 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 300 mm) water flows at 2.4 m/s. It contracts to diameter 90 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 300, d2 = 90, V1 = 2.4 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 2.4*(300/90)^2 | Answer: 26.67 m/s

question: Water flows at 2.9 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.49 m and length 130 m. With friction factor f = 0.026, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 34 teeth drives a gear of 72 teeth. If the pinion runs at 700 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 34, z2 = 72, N1 = 700 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 700*34 / 72 | Answer: 330.6 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 420 mm rotates at 900 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 420, N = 900 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.42)*900 / 60 | Answer: 19.79 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 30 kW at 200 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 30, N = 200 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(30*1000) / (2*pi*200) | Answer: 1432 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 9.9 kg rotates at radius 0.4 m at 1150 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 15400 N/m and mass 14.8 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 15400, m = 14.8 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(15400/14.8) | Answer: 5.134 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 8.3 m^2 and thickness 0.12 m has conductivity k = 3.7 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 85 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 8.3, L = 0.12, k = 3.7, dT = 85 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 3.7*8.3*85 / 0.12 | Answer: 21753 W

question: A surface of area 4.3 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 45 W/m^2-K to surroundings 95 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 4.3, h = 45, dT = 95 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 45*4.3*95 | Answer: 18382 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 130 m/min, feed = 0.25 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2.8 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 130, f = 0.25, d = 2.8 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*130*0.25*2.8 | Answer: 91000 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 190 mm is turned at 1150 rpm with a feed of 0.28 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 190, N = 1150, f = 0.28 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 190 / (0.28*1150) | Answer: 0.5901 min

question: A resistor of 96 ohm carries a current of 4 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 96, I = 4 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 4 * 96 | Answer: 384 V

question: Three resistors 16 ohm, 58 ohm and 89 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 16, R2 = 58, R3 = 89 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 16 + 58 + 89 | Answer: 163 ohm

question: Two resistors 41 ohm and 23 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 41, R2 = 23 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 41*23 / (41+23) | Answer: 14.73 ohm

question: A device draws 11.7 A at 90 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 90, I = 11.7 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 90 * 11.7 | Answer: 1053 W

question: A current of 6.2 A flows through a 61 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 6.2, R = 61 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (6.2)^2 * 61 | Answer: 2345 W

question: Two capacitors 42.8 uF and 36 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 42.8, C2 = 36 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 42.8*36 / (42.8+36) | Answer: 19.55 uF

question: A resistor 25 kohm and capacitor 8.4 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 25, C = 8.4 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (25k)(8.4u) = 210 ms | Answer: 210 ms

question: An inductor 418.8 mH is in series with 120 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 418.8, R = 120 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (418.8e-3) / 120 | Answer: 3.49 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 89.9 mH inductor at 770 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 89.9, f = 770 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (770)(89.9e-3) | Answer: 434.9 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 41.9 uF capacitor at 480 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 41.9, f = 480 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (480)(41.9e-6)) | Answer: 7.913 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 24 ohm, XL = 38 ohm and XC = 54 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 24, XL = 38, XC = 54 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(24^2 + (38 - 54)^2) | Answer: 28.84 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 79.2 mH and C = 8.7 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 79.2, C = 8.7 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(79.2e-3 * 8.7e-6)) | Answer: 191.7 Hz

question: A capacitor of 70.2 uF is charged to 385 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 70.2, V = 385 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*70.2e-6*(385)^2 | Answer: 5203 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 220 V with 890 primary turns and 300 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 220, N1 = 890, N2 = 300 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 220 * 300/890 | Answer: 74.16 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 200 V and draws an armature current of 52 A. If the armature resistance is 0.82 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 200, Ia = 52, Ra = 0.82 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 200 - 52*0.82 | Answer: 157.4 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 175 A at 433 V (line) with a power factor of 0.77. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 175, VL = 433, pf = 0.77 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*433*175*0.77 / 1000 | Answer: 101.1 kW

question: A load has real power 165 kW and apparent power 180 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 165, S = 180 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 165 / 180 | Answer: 0.9167

question: A machine delivers 70 kW output while drawing 102 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 70, Pi = 102 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 70/102 * 100 | Answer: 68.63 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 30 V across R1 = 31 ohm and R2 = 2 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 30, R1 = 31, R2 = 2 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 30*2 / (31+2) | Answer: 1.818 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 40 kohm and Rin = 20 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 40, Rin = 20 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 40 / 20 | Answer: 2

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 10 kohm and Rg = 28 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 10, Rg = 28 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 10/28 | Answer: 1.357

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 3596. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 3596 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(3596) | Answer: 35.56 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 7.8 m carries a central point load of 70 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7.8, W = 70 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 70*7.8 / 4 | Answer: 136.5 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 9 m carries a UDL of 35 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 9, w = 35 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 35*(9)^2 / 8 | Answer: 354.4 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 5.3 m carries a point load 5 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.3, W = 5 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 5*5.3 | Answer: 26.5 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 3.6 m carries a UDL of 20 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.6, w = 20 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 20*(3.6)^2 / 2 | Answer: 129.6 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.2 m carries a point load 30 kN at distance 1.6 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 9.2, a = 1.6, W = 30 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 30*(9.2 - 1.6) / 9.2 | Answer: 24.78 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 7.9 m) carries a central point load 60 kN. With E = 30 GPa and I = 190e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=60000 N, L=7900.0 mm, E=30000 MPa, I=190e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 108.1 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 6.1 m carries a UDL of 30 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6.1, w = 30 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 30*(6.1)^2 / 12 | Answer: 93.02 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 610 mm, clear cover 25 mm and main bars of diameter 20 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 610, c = 25, dia = 20 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 610 - 25 - 20/2 | Answer: 575 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 27.8 m^2 carrying a factored load of 18.9 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 27.8, w = 18.9 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 18.9 * 27.8 | Answer: 525.4 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 5.2 m, unit weight 18 kN/m^3, phi = 31 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 7.2 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 20 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 7.2, g = 20 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (20 - 9.81)*7.2 | Answer: 73.37 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 2.3e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.7, area = 5.6e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 2.3, i = 0.7, A = 5.6 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (2.3e-4)*0.7*(5.6e-3) | Answer: 901.6 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 2.4 m, bed slope 0.008 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.03. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 1.7 m under a head of 0.5 m. Taking Cd = 0.62 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 3.3 m wide carries a discharge of 24.5 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 170 m and design speed 65 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 170, V = 65 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (65)^2 / (127*170) | Answer: 0.1957
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: For a design speed of 75 km/h with allowable superelevation 0.08 and lateral friction 0.15, find the minimum curve radius in m.
A tank of volume 80 m^3 treats a flow of 35 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 80, Q = 35 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 80 / 35 | Answer: 2.286 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 340 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.11 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 6 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 340, k = 0.11, t = 6 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 340*(1 - e^(-0.11*6)) | Answer: 164.3 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.58, rainfall intensity 65 mm/h over a catchment of 48.4 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.58, i = 65, A = 48.4 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.58*65*48.4 / 360 | Answer: 5.069 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.03 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 800 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.03, M = 800 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 800*(20+0.03)/20 | Answer: 801.2 m

question: Convert the decimal number 2008 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 2008 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 7D8 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the 8-bit binary number 11010011 to decimal.
solution: Binary 11010011 = sum of bit-weights | Answer: 211 (decimal)
formula: Sum each bit times its positional weight (2^i)

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 10100110 and 10011011.
solution: XOR: 00111101 | Count of 1s = 5 | Answer: 5
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 220 megabits is sent over a link of 42 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 220, B = 42 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 220 / 42 | Answer: 5.238 s

question: A link has bandwidth 93 Mbps and round-trip time 130 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 93, R = 130 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 93e6 * 130e-3 bits = 12090 kb | Answer: 12090 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.92, cache access time 3 ns and main-memory access time 70 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.92, tc = 3, tm = 70 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.92*3 + (1 - 0.92)*70 | Answer: 8.36 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 630819 elements?
solution: Given: n = 630819 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(630819)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: An O(n^2) algorithm performs c*n^2 basic operations. If c = 1 and n = 1990, how many operations are performed?
solution: Given: n = 1990 | Formula: operations = n^2 | Substitute: = (1990)^2 | Answer: 3960100

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.009, memory access time 80 ns and page-fault service time 7 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 7 ms = 7000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.009)*80 + 0.009*7000000.0 ns | Answer: 63.08 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 1.9 m^3 at 130 kPa and 600 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 1.9, P = 130, Tk = 600 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (130e3)*1.9 / (8.314*600) | Answer: 49.51 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.19 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 13 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.19, t = 13 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.19*13) | Answer: 0.9154

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.4 /min) is to reach 75% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.4, X = 75 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.75) / 0.4 | Answer: 3.466 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.11 /min) reaches 90% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.11, X = 90 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.9 / (0.11*(1 - 0.9)) | Answer: 81.82 min

question: For a reaction with A = 8e10 /s and activation energy 65 kJ/mol at 430 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 8, Ea = 65, Tk = 430 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 8e10 * exp(-65e3 / (8.314*430)) | Answer: 1016 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.94 and bottoms xW = 0.08, with relative volatility alpha = 2.4. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.94, xw = 0.08, al = 2.4 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.94/0.06)(0.92/0.08)] / ln(2.4) | Answer: 5.933 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.58 and x = 0.5. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.58, x = 0.5 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.58/0.42) / (0.5/0.5) | Answer: 1.381

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.6 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 90 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.6, Psat = 90 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.6 * 90 | Answer: 54 kPa

question: A stream of 6 kg/s with specific heat 3.9 kJ/kg-K is heated through 60 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 6, cp = 3.9, dT = 60 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 6*3.9*60 | Answer: 1404 kW

question: A reactor of volume 12.2 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 2.8 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 12.2, Q = 2.8 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 12.2 / 2.8 | Answer: 4.357 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 3.3e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 1 mm with a concentration difference of 190 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 3.3, L = 1, dC = 190 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (3.3e-9)*190 / (1e-3) | Answer: 627 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 1.4 min and steady-state gain 2.6. For a step input of magnitude 9, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 1.4, K = 2.6, M = 9 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 2.6 * 9 | Answer: 23.4 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 115 m^2 flies at 230 m/s (air density 1.225 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.5. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 115, V = 230, rho = 1.225, CL = 0.5 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1.225*(230)^2*115*0.5 / 1000 | Answer: 1863 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 95 m^2 flies at 220 m/s (density 0.4 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.09. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 95, V = 220, rho = 0.4, CD = 0.09 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.4*(220)^2*95*0.09 / 1000 | Answer: 82.76 kN

question: A specimen under stress 100 MPa shows an elastic strain of 2e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 100, eps = 2 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 100 / (2e-3) MPa = 50 GPa | Answer: 50 GPa

question: A block of mass 11 kg has a volume of 4.2e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 11, V = 4.2 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 11 / (4.2e-3) | Answer: 2619 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 2800 mm is heated through 130 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 12e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 2800, dT = 130, al = 12 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 2800*12e-6*130 | Answer: 4.368 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 25 ohm, R2 = 125 ohm and R3 = 10 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 25, R2 = 125, R3 = 10 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 125*10 / 25 | Answer: 50 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 120 ohm and gauge factor 2.1 experiences a strain of 1850e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 120, GF = 2.1, eps = 1850 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 120*2.1*1850e-6 | Answer: 466.2 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 9.97 when the true value is 20. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.97, true = 20 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.97 - 20| / 20 * 100 | Answer: 50.15 %

question: Annual demand is 42500 units, ordering cost 270 per order and holding cost 16 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 42500, S = 270, H = 16 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*42500*270 / 16) | Answer: 1198 units

question: An asset costs 280000 with salvage value 30000 after 12 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 280000, Sv = 30000, n = 12 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (280000 - 30000) / 12 | Answer: 20833 per year

question: A product sells for 250 per unit with variable cost 100 per unit and fixed costs 125000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 250, V = 100, F = 125000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 125000 / (250 - 100) | Answer: 833.3 units

question: Find the present worth of 80000 received 4 years from now at an interest rate of 12% per year.
solution: Given: F = 80000, n = 4, i = 12 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 80000 / (1 + 0.12)^4 | Answer: 50841 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.9, 0.9 and 0.91 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.9, r2 = 0.9, r3 = 0.91 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.9*0.9*0.91 | Answer: 0.7371

question: A process produces 11 defective items in a batch of 7000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 11, N = 7000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 11/7000 * 1e6 | Answer: 1571 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -5x^3 + 2x^2 - 5x - 2 evaluated at x = 1.
For f(x) = 4x^3 - 7x^2 + 2x - 1, find f''(x) at x = -4.
Evaluate the definite integral of (5x^2 + 6x + 1) dx from x = -4 to x = 6.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = 5x^3/3 + 6x^2/2 + 1x | Evaluate F(6) - F(-4) | Answer: 536.7
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 2x^2 + 6x - 10 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[-1, 2], [-5, 4]].
solution: Given: a = -1, b = 2, c = -5, d = 4 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (-1)(4) - (2)(-5) | Answer: 6

question: Find the determinant of [[-4, -2, 0], [6, 2, 3], [0, -5, 4]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: -44

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[-6, -5], [-7, -7]].
solution: Trace tr = -13, Determinant = 7 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: -0.5628

question: Solve for x: 0x + -1y = -2 and 3x + -2y = 3.
solution: Determinant = 0*-2 - -1*3 = 3 | x = (e d - b f) / det = 2.333 | Answer: x = 2.333
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 52, 29, 84, 37, 100.
solution: Sum = 302 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 60.4 | Answer: 60.4

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 49, 20, 1, 11, 9.
solution: Mean = 18 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 18.6

question: Find the slope of the line through (7, 2) and (-6, -9).
solution: Given: x1 = 7, y1 = 2, x2 = -6, y2 = -9 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (-9 - 2) / (-6 - 7) | Answer: 0.8462

question: Find the distance between the points (-7, -9) and (-4, 5).
solution: Given: x1 = -7, y1 = -9, x2 = -4, y2 = 5 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((3)^2 + (14)^2) | Answer: 14.32 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (3,-4), (6,-8), (-3,3).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 1.5 sq units

question: Evaluate the number of combinations C(15, 9).
solution: Given: n = 15, r = 9 | Formula: C(n, r) = n! / (r! (n - r)!) | Substitute: C(15, 9) = 15! / (9! * 6!) | Answer: 5005

question: Find the 39th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 3 and common difference -9.
solution: Given: a = 3, d = -9, n = 39 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = 3 + (39 - 1)*-9 | Answer: -339

question: Find the sum of the first 38 terms of an AP with first term -4 and common difference -7.
solution: Given: a = -4, d = -7, n = 38 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 38/2 [2*-4 + (38-1)*-7] | Answer: -5073

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 42500 at 5.9% per annum for 5 years.
solution: Given: P = 42500, R = 5.9, Tt = 5 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 42500 * 5.9 * 5 / 100 | Answer: 12538 currency units

question: Find the amount when 39500 is invested at 10.5% per annum compounded annually for 3 years.
solution: Given: P = 39500, R = 10.5, Tt = 3 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 39500 * (1 + 10.5/100)^3 | Answer: 53295 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (-2, -5, 2) and (8, -2, -5).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (-5, -2, -5) and (-3, -2, 0).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 18.47

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (-1, -6, 0) and (-4, 3, 4).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 111.1 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number -7 + 2i.
solution: Given: a = -7, b = 2 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((-7)^2 + (2)^2) | Answer: 7.28

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number -4 + 12i.
solution: Given: a = -4, b = 12 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(12, -4) | Answer: 108.4 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -2x^3 + 2x + 3 at x = 5.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-116 with initial guess x0=6, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=0.8 and ordinates 15, 5, 20, 19, 10, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 468 and 336.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 468 and 336 | Answer: GCD = 12

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 44 and 77.
solution: Given: a = 44, b = 77 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 44*77 / 11 | Answer: 308
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 21 mm carries an axial tensile load of 44 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 39 mm and length 1500 mm carries an axial load of 34 kN. Take E = 110 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 75 mm transmits a torque of 2500 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 75, Tt = 2500 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(2500*1000) / (pi*(75)^3) | Answer: 30.18 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 46 mm and length 700 mm carries a torque of 1100 N-m. With G = 77 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (46)^4 / 32 = 439573 mm^4 | theta = (1100*1000)(700) / (77000 * 439573) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 1.303 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 144 mm wide and 180 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 144, h = 180 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 144*(180)^2 / 6 | Answer: 777600 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (53 mm x 220 mm) carries a bending moment of 19 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (66 mm x 90 mm) has effective length 2900 mm and E = 200 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 780 MPa is designed for a working stress of 90 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 780, sw = 90 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 780 / 90 | Answer: 8.667

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 550 mm and wall thickness 6 mm carries an internal pressure of 2.3 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
