solution: Given: d = 550, t = 6, P = 2.3 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 2.3*550 / (2*6) | Answer: 105.4 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 800 K and 370 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 800, Tc = 370 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 370/800) * 100 | Answer: 53.75 %

question: A refrigerator works between 267 K (cold) and 328 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 267, Th = 328 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 267 / (328 - 267) | Answer: 4.377

question: A heat pump operates between 266 K and 332 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 266, Th = 332 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 332 / (332 - 266) | Answer: 5.03

question: 5.1 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 130 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 5.1, dT = 130 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 5.1 * 0.718 * 130 | Answer: 476 kJ

question: 5 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 115 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 5, dT = 115 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 5 * 1.005 * 115 | Answer: 577.9 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 3.3 m^3 at 460 K with mass 5.7 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 3.3, Tk = 460, m = 5.7 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 5.7*0.287*460 / 3.3 | Answer: 228 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 4.1 kg of air expands isothermally at 370 K from volume V1 to 2*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.1, Tk = 370, ratio = 2 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 4.1*0.287*370*ln(2) | Answer: 301.8 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 4.7 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.23 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 4.7, D = 0.23 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*4.7*0.23 / 0.001 | Answer: 1081000

question: Water flows at 3.2 m/s through a pipe of diameter 100 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 17.7 m. Taking Cv = 0.96, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 17.7, cv = 0.96 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.96*sqrt(2*9.81*17.7) | Answer: 17.89 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 170 mm) water flows at 0.9 m/s. It contracts to diameter 140 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
Water flows at 1.5 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.14 m and length 110 m. With friction factor f = 0.033, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 19 teeth drives a gear of 112 teeth. If the pinion runs at 550 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 19, z2 = 112, N1 = 550 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 550*19 / 112 | Answer: 93.3 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 600 mm rotates at 500 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 600, N = 500 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.6)*500 / 60 | Answer: 15.71 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 4.1 kW at 850 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 4.1, N = 850 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(4.1*1000) / (2*pi*850) | Answer: 46.06 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 2.2 kg rotates at radius 0.37 m at 300 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 15100 N/m and mass 7.1 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 15100, m = 7.1 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(15100/7.1) | Answer: 7.34 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 3.6 m^2 and thickness 0.4 m has conductivity k = 47.7 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 45 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 3.6, L = 0.4, k = 47.7, dT = 45 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 47.7*3.6*45 / 0.4 | Answer: 19319 W

question: A surface of area 2.9 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 15 W/m^2-K to surroundings 150 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 2.9, h = 15, dT = 150 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 15*2.9*150 | Answer: 6525 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 240 m/min, feed = 0.48 mm/rev, depth of cut = 0.8 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 240, f = 0.48, d = 0.8 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*240*0.48*0.8 | Answer: 92160 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 380 mm is turned at 200 rpm with a feed of 0.39 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 380, N = 200, f = 0.39 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 380 / (0.39*200) | Answer: 4.872 min

question: A resistor of 3 ohm carries a current of 6 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 3, I = 6 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 6 * 3 | Answer: 18 V

question: Three resistors 8 ohm, 76 ohm and 45 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 8, R2 = 76, R3 = 45 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 8 + 76 + 45 | Answer: 129 ohm

question: Two resistors 38 ohm and 108 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 38, R2 = 108 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 38*108 / (38+108) | Answer: 28.11 ohm

question: A device draws 4.8 A at 75 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 75, I = 4.8 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 75 * 4.8 | Answer: 360 W

question: A current of 11.6 A flows through a 30 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 11.6, R = 30 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (11.6)^2 * 30 | Answer: 4037 W

question: Two capacitors 35.8 uF and 14.1 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 35.8, C2 = 14.1 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 35.8*14.1 / (35.8+14.1) | Answer: 10.12 uF

question: A resistor 84 kohm and capacitor 15 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 84, C = 15 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (84k)(15u) = 1260 ms | Answer: 1260 ms

question: An inductor 499.3 mH is in series with 129 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 499.3, R = 129 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (499.3e-3) / 129 | Answer: 3.871 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 103 mH inductor at 850 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 103, f = 850 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (850)(103e-3) | Answer: 550.1 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 12.9 uF capacitor at 940 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 12.9, f = 940 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (940)(12.9e-6)) | Answer: 13.13 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 51 ohm, XL = 53 ohm and XC = 80 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 51, XL = 53, XC = 80 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(51^2 + (53 - 80)^2) | Answer: 57.71 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 64.3 mH and C = 9.8 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 64.3, C = 9.8 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(64.3e-3 * 9.8e-6)) | Answer: 200.5 Hz

question: A capacitor of 93.2 uF is charged to 80 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 93.2, V = 80 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*93.2e-6*(80)^2 | Answer: 298.2 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 220 V with 660 primary turns and 350 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 220, N1 = 660, N2 = 350 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 220 * 350/660 | Answer: 116.7 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 230 V and draws an armature current of 59 A. If the armature resistance is 1.21 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 230, Ia = 59, Ra = 1.21 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 230 - 59*1.21 | Answer: 158.6 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 80 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.94. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 80, VL = 400, pf = 0.94 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*400*80*0.94 / 1000 | Answer: 52.1 kW

question: A load has real power 25 kW and apparent power 195 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 25, S = 195 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 25 / 195 | Answer: 0.1282

question: A machine delivers 25 kW output while drawing 87 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 25, Pi = 87 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 25/87 * 100 | Answer: 28.74 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 5 V across R1 = 45 ohm and R2 = 14 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 5, R1 = 45, R2 = 14 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 5*14 / (45+14) | Answer: 1.186 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 220 kohm and Rin = 1 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 220, Rin = 1 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 220 / 1 | Answer: 220

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 40 kohm and Rg = 26 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 40, Rg = 26 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 40/26 | Answer: 2.538

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 2869. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 2869 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(2869) | Answer: 34.58 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 7.8 m carries a central point load of 40 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7.8, W = 40 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 40*7.8 / 4 | Answer: 78 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 8.3 m carries a UDL of 5 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 8.3, w = 5 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 5*(8.3)^2 / 8 | Answer: 43.06 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 1.4 m carries a point load 75 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 1.4, W = 75 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 75*1.4 | Answer: 105 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 5.4 m carries a UDL of 6 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.4, w = 6 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 6*(5.4)^2 / 2 | Answer: 87.48 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 5.4 m carries a point load 35 kN at distance 2.3 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 5.4, a = 2.3, W = 35 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 35*(5.4 - 2.3) / 5.4 | Answer: 20.09 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 6 m) carries a central point load 30 kN. With E = 200 GPa and I = 560e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=30000 N, L=6000.0 mm, E=200000 MPa, I=560e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 1.205 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 5.3 m carries a UDL of 6 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.3, w = 6 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 6*(5.3)^2 / 12 | Answer: 14.04 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 650 mm, clear cover 35 mm and main bars of diameter 20 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 650, c = 35, dia = 20 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 650 - 35 - 20/2 | Answer: 605 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 10.1 m^2 carrying a factored load of 10.3 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 10.1, w = 10.3 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 10.3 * 10.1 | Answer: 104 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 5.2 m, unit weight 18 kN/m^3, phi = 37 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 3.4 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 21 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 3.4, g = 21 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (21 - 9.81)*3.4 | Answer: 38.05 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 8.9e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.5, area = 6e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 8.9, i = 0.5, A = 6 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (8.9e-4)*0.5*(6e-3) | Answer: 2670 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 0.5 m, bed slope 0.007 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.025. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 3.9 m under a head of 1.2 m. Taking Cd = 0.61 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 3.8 m wide carries a discharge of 17.7 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 330 m and design speed 90 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 330, V = 90 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (90)^2 / (127*330) | Answer: 0.1933
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: For a design speed of 90 km/h with allowable superelevation 0.08 and lateral friction 0.13, find the minimum curve radius in m.
A tank of volume 410 m^3 treats a flow of 40 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 410, Q = 40 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 410 / 40 | Answer: 10.25 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 290 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.16 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 3 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 290, k = 0.16, t = 3 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 290*(1 - e^(-0.16*3)) | Answer: 110.6 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.54, rainfall intensity 60 mm/h over a catchment of 22.2 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.54, i = 60, A = 22.2 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.54*60*22.2 / 360 | Answer: 1.998 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.04 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 490 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.04, M = 490 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 490*(30+0.04)/30 | Answer: 490.7 m

question: Convert the decimal number 45 to binary.
solution: Divide 45 by 2 repeatedly, recording remainders | Reading remainders in reverse gives 101101 | Answer: 101101 (binary)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 2 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the decimal number 2483 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 2483 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 9B3 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the 8-bit binary number 11111011 to decimal.
solution: Binary 11111011 = sum of bit-weights | Answer: 251 (decimal)
formula: Sum each bit times its positional weight (2^i)

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 00011100 and 01100000.
solution: XOR: 01111100 | Count of 1s = 5 | Answer: 5
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 210 megabits is sent over a link of 41 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 210, B = 41 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 210 / 41 | Answer: 5.122 s

question: A link has bandwidth 68 Mbps and round-trip time 80 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 68, R = 80 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 68e6 * 80e-3 bits = 5440 kb | Answer: 5440 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.88, cache access time 8 ns and main-memory access time 150 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.88, tc = 8, tm = 150 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.88*8 + (1 - 0.88)*150 | Answer: 25.04 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 998771 elements?
solution: Given: n = 998771 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(998771)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: An O(n^2) algorithm performs c*n^2 basic operations. If c = 1 and n = 2780, how many operations are performed?
solution: Given: n = 2780 | Formula: operations = n^2 | Substitute: = (2780)^2 | Answer: 7728400

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.019, memory access time 150 ns and page-fault service time 5 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 5 ms = 5000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.019)*150 + 0.019*5000000.0 ns | Answer: 95.15 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 0.5 m^3 at 240 kPa and 420 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 0.5, P = 240, Tk = 420 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (240e3)*0.5 / (8.314*420) | Answer: 34.37 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.28 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 4 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.28, t = 4 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.28*4) | Answer: 0.6737

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.42 /min) is to reach 70% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.42, X = 70 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.7) / 0.42 | Answer: 2.867 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.18 /min) reaches 80% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.18, X = 80 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.8 / (0.18*(1 - 0.8)) | Answer: 22.22 min

question: For a reaction with A = 7e10 /s and activation energy 75 kJ/mol at 430 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 7, Ea = 75, Tk = 430 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 7e10 * exp(-75e3 / (8.314*430)) | Answer: 54.21 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.94 and bottoms xW = 0.02, with relative volatility alpha = 3.1. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.94, xw = 0.02, al = 3.1 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.94/0.06)(0.98/0.02)] / ln(3.1) | Answer: 5.872 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.73 and x = 0.32. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.73, x = 0.32 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.73/0.27) / (0.32/0.68) | Answer: 5.745

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.46 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 95 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.46, Psat = 95 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.46 * 95 | Answer: 43.7 kPa

question: A stream of 0.7 kg/s with specific heat 3.6 kJ/kg-K is heated through 45 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 0.7, cp = 3.6, dT = 45 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 0.7*3.6*45 | Answer: 113.4 kW

question: A reactor of volume 7 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 0.9 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 7, Q = 0.9 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 7 / 0.9 | Answer: 7.778 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 3.4e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 2 mm with a concentration difference of 20 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 3.4, L = 2, dC = 20 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (3.4e-9)*20 / (2e-3) | Answer: 34 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 10 min and steady-state gain 3.9. For a step input of magnitude 18, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 10, K = 3.9, M = 18 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 3.9 * 18 | Answer: 70.2 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 25 m^2 flies at 230 m/s (air density 0.4 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 1. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 25, V = 230, rho = 0.4, CL = 1 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.4*(230)^2*25*1 / 1000 | Answer: 264.5 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 40 m^2 flies at 80 m/s (density 0.4 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.04. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 40, V = 80, rho = 0.4, CD = 0.04 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.4*(80)^2*40*0.04 / 1000 | Answer: 2.048 kN

question: A specimen under stress 120 MPa shows an elastic strain of 2.7e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 120, eps = 2.7 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 120 / (2.7e-3) MPa = 44.44 GPa | Answer: 44.44 GPa

question: A block of mass 21 kg has a volume of 5.9e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 21, V = 5.9 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 21 / (5.9e-3) | Answer: 3559 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 1100 mm is heated through 55 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 12e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 1100, dT = 55, al = 12 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 1100*12e-6*55 | Answer: 0.726 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 175 ohm, R2 = 40 ohm and R3 = 315 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 175, R2 = 40, R3 = 315 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 40*315 / 175 | Answer: 72 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 350 ohm and gauge factor 2.2 experiences a strain of 1650e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 350, GF = 2.2, eps = 1650 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 350*2.2*1650e-6 | Answer: 1271 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 10.39 when the true value is 50. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10.39, true = 50 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10.39 - 50| / 50 * 100 | Answer: 79.22 %

question: Annual demand is 5000 units, ordering cost 210 per order and holding cost 39 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 5000, S = 210, H = 39 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*5000*210 / 39) | Answer: 232 units

question: An asset costs 50000 with salvage value 36000 after 17 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 50000, Sv = 36000, n = 17 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (50000 - 36000) / 17 | Answer: 823.5 per year

question: A product sells for 210 per unit with variable cost 20 per unit and fixed costs 200000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 210, V = 20, F = 200000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 200000 / (210 - 20) | Answer: 1053 units

question: Find the present worth of 190000 received 5 years from now at an interest rate of 7% per year.
solution: Given: F = 190000, n = 5, i = 7 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 190000 / (1 + 0.07)^5 | Answer: 135467 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.98, 0.92 and 0.94 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.98, r2 = 0.92, r3 = 0.94 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.98*0.92*0.94 | Answer: 0.8475

question: A process produces 43 defective items in a batch of 18500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 43, N = 18500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 43/18500 * 1e6 | Answer: 2324 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -5x^3 - x^2 + 9x + 7 evaluated at x = 4.
For f(x) = -6x^3 + 8x^2 - 3x + 6, find f''(x) at x = 4.
Evaluate the definite integral of (-4x^2 - 5x - 5) dx from x = -3 to x = 7.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = -4x^3/3 + -5x^2/2 + -5x | Evaluate F(7) - F(-3) | Answer: -643.3
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 6x^2 - 7x - 7 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[-8, -7], [5, -5]].
solution: Given: a = -8, b = -7, c = 5, d = -5 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (-8)(-5) - (-7)(5) | Answer: 75

question: Find the determinant of [[3, 6, 6], [-6, -4, -1], [-4, 0, 3]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: 0

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[6, 8], [6, -7]].
solution: Trace tr = -1, Determinant = -90 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 9

question: Solve for x: 4x + 3y = -12 and 4x + -4y = -7.
solution: Determinant = 4*-4 - 3*4 = -28 | x = (e d - b f) / det = -2.464 | Answer: x = -2.464
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 89, 78, 87, 51, 70.
solution: Sum = 375 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 75 | Answer: 75

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 27, 10, 40, 16, 40.
solution: Mean = 26.6 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 13.67

question: Find the slope of the line through (9, 1) and (-4, -4).
solution: Given: x1 = 9, y1 = 1, x2 = -4, y2 = -4 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (-4 - 1) / (-4 - 9) | Answer: 0.3846

question: Find the distance between the points (-2, 0) and (5, 6).
solution: Given: x1 = -2, y1 = 0, x2 = 5, y2 = 6 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((7)^2 + (6)^2) | Answer: 9.22 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (2,2), (3,8), (4,-7).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 10.5 sq units

question: Find the 17th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 11 and common difference 6.
solution: Given: a = 11, d = 6, n = 17 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = 11 + (17 - 1)*6 | Answer: 107

question: Find the sum of the first 40 terms of an AP with first term -11 and common difference 6.
solution: Given: a = -11, d = 6, n = 40 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 40/2 [2*-11 + (40-1)*6] | Answer: 4240

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 5500 at 8.5% per annum for 5 years.
solution: Given: P = 5500, R = 8.5, Tt = 5 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 5500 * 8.5 * 5 / 100 | Answer: 2338 currency units

question: Find the amount when 23000 is invested at 7.8% per annum compounded annually for 3 years.
solution: Given: P = 23000, R = 7.8, Tt = 3 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 23000 * (1 + 7.8/100)^3 | Answer: 28813 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (0, -8, -2) and (7, 5, -6).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (-5, -3, 2) and (3, -4, 3).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 35.82

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (6, 3, 1) and (-2, 0, -5).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 117.7 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number -10 + 10i.
solution: Given: a = -10, b = 10 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((-10)^2 + (10)^2) | Answer: 14.14

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number -4 + -7i.
solution: Given: a = -4, b = -7 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(-7, -4) | Answer: -119.7 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = 5x^3 - 7x^2 + 7x at x = 2.
solution: Given: a = 5, b = -7, c = 7, d = 0, x0 = 2 | Formula: f(x0) = a x0^3 + b x0^2 + c x0 + d | Substitute: f(2) = 5(2)^3 + -7(2)^2 + 7(2) + 0 | Answer: 26

question: Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-44 with initial guess x0=15, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.9 and ordinates 6, 20, 15, 18, 15, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 93 and 276.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 93 and 276 | Answer: GCD = 3

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 25 and 33.
solution: Given: a = 25, b = 33 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 25*33 / 1 | Answer: 825
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 38 mm carries an axial tensile load of 88 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 15 mm and length 1600 mm carries an axial load of 70 kN. Take E = 200 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 68 mm transmits a torque of 2000 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 68, Tt = 2000 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(2000*1000) / (pi*(68)^3) | Answer: 32.39 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 58 mm and length 500 mm carries a torque of 950 N-m. With G = 80 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (58)^4 / 32 = 1110994 mm^4 | theta = (950*1000)(500) / (80000 * 1110994) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 0.3062 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 51 mm wide and 110 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 51, h = 110 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 51*(110)^2 / 6 | Answer: 102850 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (92 mm x 90 mm) carries a bending moment of 5 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (62 mm x 160 mm) has effective length 2900 mm and E = 200 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 810 MPa is designed for a working stress of 180 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 810, sw = 180 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 810 / 180 | Answer: 4.5

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 300 mm and wall thickness 9 mm carries an internal pressure of 0.7 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 300, t = 9, P = 0.7 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 0.7*300 / (2*9) | Answer: 11.67 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 1100 K and 290 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 1100, Tc = 290 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 290/1100) * 100 | Answer: 73.64 %

question: A refrigerator works between 259 K (cold) and 306 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 259, Th = 306 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 259 / (306 - 259) | Answer: 5.511

question: A heat pump operates between 266 K and 314 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 266, Th = 314 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 314 / (314 - 266) | Answer: 6.542

question: 7.6 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 85 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 7.6, dT = 85 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 7.6 * 0.718 * 85 | Answer: 463.8 kJ

question: 5.2 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 65 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 5.2, dT = 65 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 5.2 * 1.005 * 65 | Answer: 339.7 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 3.8 m^3 at 380 K with mass 3.7 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 3.8, Tk = 380, m = 3.7 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 3.7*0.287*380 / 3.8 | Answer: 106.2 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 3.3 kg of air expands isothermally at 370 K from volume V1 to 2*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.3, Tk = 370, ratio = 2 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 3.3*0.287*370*ln(2) | Answer: 242.9 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 0.7 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.23 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 0.7, D = 0.23 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*0.7*0.23 / 0.001 | Answer: 161000

question: Water flows at 1.6 m/s through a pipe of diameter 250 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 27.9 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 27.9 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*27.9 / 1000 | Answer: 273.7 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 14.5 m. Taking Cv = 0.95, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 14.5, cv = 0.95 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.95*sqrt(2*9.81*14.5) | Answer: 16.02 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 300 mm) water flows at 1.8 m/s. It contracts to diameter 140 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
Water flows at 1.6 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.38 m and length 140 m. With friction factor f = 0.037, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 24 teeth drives a gear of 48 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1350 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 24, z2 = 48, N1 = 1350 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1350*24 / 48 | Answer: 675 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 550 mm rotates at 1000 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 550, N = 1000 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.55)*1000 / 60 | Answer: 28.8 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 40.9 kW at 1200 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 40.9, N = 1200 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(40.9*1000) / (2*pi*1200) | Answer: 325.5 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 9.4 kg rotates at radius 0.41 m at 1150 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 700 N/m and mass 16.3 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 700, m = 16.3 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(700/16.3) | Answer: 1.043 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 2.9 m^2 and thickness 0.39 m has conductivity k = 44.6 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 40 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 2.9, L = 0.39, k = 44.6, dT = 40 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 44.6*2.9*40 / 0.39 | Answer: 13266 W

question: A surface of area 2.8 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 75 W/m^2-K to surroundings 45 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 2.8, h = 75, dT = 45 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 75*2.8*45 | Answer: 9450 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 110 m/min, feed = 0.16 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2.3 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 110, f = 0.16, d = 2.3 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*110*0.16*2.3 | Answer: 40480 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 320 mm is turned at 850 rpm with a feed of 0.16 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 320, N = 850, f = 0.16 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 320 / (0.16*850) | Answer: 2.353 min

question: A resistor of 120 ohm carries a current of 2.2 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 120, I = 2.2 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 2.2 * 120 | Answer: 264 V

question: Three resistors 67 ohm, 84 ohm and 7 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 67, R2 = 84, R3 = 7 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 67 + 84 + 7 | Answer: 158 ohm

question: Two resistors 25 ohm and 116 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 25, R2 = 116 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 25*116 / (25+116) | Answer: 20.57 ohm

question: A device draws 12.8 A at 45 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 45, I = 12.8 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 45 * 12.8 | Answer: 576 W

question: A current of 9.7 A flows through a 31 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 9.7, R = 31 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (9.7)^2 * 31 | Answer: 2917 W

question: Two capacitors 29.1 uF and 21.5 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 29.1, C2 = 21.5 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 29.1*21.5 / (29.1+21.5) | Answer: 12.36 uF

question: A resistor 10 kohm and capacitor 4.3 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 10, C = 4.3 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (10k)(4.3u) = 43 ms | Answer: 43 ms

question: An inductor 282 mH is in series with 12 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 282, R = 12 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (282e-3) / 12 | Answer: 23.5 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 185.5 mH inductor at 970 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 185.5, f = 970 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (970)(185.5e-3) | Answer: 1131 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 42.8 uF capacitor at 1000 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 42.8, f = 1000 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (1000)(42.8e-6)) | Answer: 3.719 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 94 ohm, XL = 19 ohm and XC = 16 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 94, XL = 19, XC = 16 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(94^2 + (19 - 16)^2) | Answer: 94.05 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 34.8 mH and C = 8 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 34.8, C = 8 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(34.8e-3 * 8e-6)) | Answer: 301.6 Hz

question: A capacitor of 54 uF is charged to 125 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 54, V = 125 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*54e-6*(125)^2 | Answer: 421.9 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 230 V with 330 primary turns and 100 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 230, N1 = 330, N2 = 100 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 230 * 100/330 | Answer: 69.7 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 230 V and draws an armature current of 44 A. If the armature resistance is 1.14 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 230, Ia = 44, Ra = 1.14 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 230 - 44*1.14 | Answer: 179.8 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 80 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.9. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 80, VL = 400, pf = 0.9 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*400*80*0.9 / 1000 | Answer: 49.88 kW

question: A load has real power 50 kW and apparent power 80 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 50, S = 80 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 50 / 80 | Answer: 0.625

question: A machine delivers 15 kW output while drawing 17 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 15, Pi = 17 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 15/17 * 100 | Answer: 88.24 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 30 V across R1 = 5 ohm and R2 = 11 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 30, R1 = 5, R2 = 11 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 30*11 / (5+11) | Answer: 20.62 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 20 kohm and Rin = 28 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 20, Rin = 28 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 20 / 28 | Answer: 0.7143

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 150 kohm and Rg = 16 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 150, Rg = 16 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 150/16 | Answer: 10.38

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 6915. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 6915 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(6915) | Answer: 38.4 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 7.2 m carries a central point load of 70 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7.2, W = 70 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 70*7.2 / 4 | Answer: 126 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 7 m carries a UDL of 20 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7, w = 20 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 20*(7)^2 / 8 | Answer: 122.5 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 2.7 m carries a point load 70 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 2.7, W = 70 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 70*2.7 | Answer: 189 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 4.8 m carries a UDL of 26 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.8, w = 26 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 26*(4.8)^2 / 2 | Answer: 299.5 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.7 m carries a point load 85 kN at distance 2.9 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 4.7, a = 2.9, W = 85 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 85*(4.7 - 2.9) / 4.7 | Answer: 32.55 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 3.5 m) carries a central point load 25 kN. With E = 200 GPa and I = 170e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=25000 N, L=3500.0 mm, E=200000 MPa, I=170e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 0.6568 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 5.2 m carries a UDL of 36 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.2, w = 36 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 36*(5.2)^2 / 12 | Answer: 81.12 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 480 mm, clear cover 30 mm and main bars of diameter 20 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 480, c = 30, dia = 20 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 480 - 30 - 20/2 | Answer: 440 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 35.6 m^2 carrying a factored load of 16.6 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 35.6, w = 16.6 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 16.6 * 35.6 | Answer: 591 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 6.7 m, unit weight 16 kN/m^3, phi = 28 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 9.9 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 21 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 9.9, g = 21 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (21 - 9.81)*9.9 | Answer: 110.8 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 2.1e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1.3, area = 6.6e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 2.1, i = 1.3, A = 6.6 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (2.1e-4)*1.3*(6.6e-3) | Answer: 1802 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.4 m, bed slope 0.002 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.015. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 4.6 m under a head of 0.4 m. Taking Cd = 0.64 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 4.7 m wide carries a discharge of 11 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 480 m and design speed 100 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 480, V = 100 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (100)^2 / (127*480) | Answer: 0.164
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: For a design speed of 90 km/h with allowable superelevation 0.06 and lateral friction 0.15, find the minimum curve radius in m.
A tank of volume 600 m^3 treats a flow of 25 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 600, Q = 25 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 600 / 25 | Answer: 24 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 250 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.23 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 3 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 250, k = 0.23, t = 3 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 250*(1 - e^(-0.23*3)) | Answer: 124.6 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.83, rainfall intensity 90 mm/h over a catchment of 18 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.83, i = 90, A = 18 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.83*90*18 / 360 | Answer: 3.735 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.07 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 140 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.07, M = 140 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 140*(30+0.07)/30 | Answer: 140.3 m

question: Convert the decimal number 129 to binary.
solution: Divide 129 by 2 repeatedly, recording remainders | Reading remainders in reverse gives 10000001 | Answer: 10000001 (binary)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 2 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the decimal number 3168 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 3168 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: C60 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 00101101 and 11011010.
solution: XOR: 11110111 | Count of 1s = 7 | Answer: 7
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 210 megabits is sent over a link of 46 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 210, B = 46 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 210 / 46 | Answer: 4.565 s

question: A link has bandwidth 20 Mbps and round-trip time 70 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 20, R = 70 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 20e6 * 70e-3 bits = 1400 kb | Answer: 1400 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.98, cache access time 2 ns and main-memory access time 100 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.98, tc = 2, tm = 100 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.98*2 + (1 - 0.98)*100 | Answer: 3.96 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 897901 elements?
solution: Given: n = 897901 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(897901)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: An O(n^2) algorithm performs c*n^2 basic operations. If c = 1 and n = 2700, how many operations are performed?
solution: Given: n = 2700 | Formula: operations = n^2 | Substitute: = (2700)^2 | Answer: 7290000

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.007, memory access time 90 ns and page-fault service time 5 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 5 ms = 5000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.007)*90 + 0.007*5000000.0 ns | Answer: 35.09 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 0.2 m^3 at 230 kPa and 540 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 0.2, P = 230, Tk = 540 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (230e3)*0.2 / (8.314*540) | Answer: 10.25 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.34 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 3 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.34, t = 3 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.34*3) | Answer: 0.6394

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.13 /min) is to reach 75% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.13, X = 75 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.75) / 0.13 | Answer: 10.66 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.22 /min) reaches 50% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.22, X = 50 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.5 / (0.22*(1 - 0.5)) | Answer: 4.545 min

question: For a reaction with A = 8e10 /s and activation energy 85 kJ/mol at 300 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 8, Ea = 85, Tk = 300 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 8e10 * exp(-85e3 / (8.314*300)) | Answer: 0.0001267 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.97 and bottoms xW = 0.03, with relative volatility alpha = 3.4. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.97, xw = 0.03, al = 3.4 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.97/0.03)(0.97/0.03)] / ln(3.4) | Answer: 5.681 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.7 and x = 0.47. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.7, x = 0.47 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.7/0.3) / (0.47/0.53) | Answer: 2.631

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.75 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 55 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.75, Psat = 55 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.75 * 55 | Answer: 41.25 kPa

question: A stream of 9.5 kg/s with specific heat 3.4 kJ/kg-K is heated through 40 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 9.5, cp = 3.4, dT = 40 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 9.5*3.4*40 | Answer: 1292 kW

question: A reactor of volume 12.2 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 3 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 12.2, Q = 3 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 12.2 / 3 | Answer: 4.067 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 7.5e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 5 mm with a concentration difference of 130 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 7.5, L = 5, dC = 130 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (7.5e-9)*130 / (5e-3) | Answer: 195 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 4.7 min and steady-state gain 2. For a step input of magnitude 12, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 4.7, K = 2, M = 12 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 2 * 12 | Answer: 24 units

question: A reactor operates at a space time of 13 min. Find its space velocity in per hour.
solution: Given: tau = 13 | Formula: SV = 60 / tau  (per hour) | Substitute: SV = 60 / 13 | Answer: 4.615 /h

question: An aircraft wing of area 15 m^2 flies at 260 m/s (air density 1 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.4. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 15, V = 260, rho = 1, CL = 0.4 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1*(260)^2*15*0.4 / 1000 | Answer: 202.8 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 45 m^2 flies at 120 m/s (density 1 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.07. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 45, V = 120, rho = 1, CD = 0.07 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*1*(120)^2*45*0.07 / 1000 | Answer: 22.68 kN

question: A specimen under stress 340 MPa shows an elastic strain of 0.8e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 340, eps = 0.8 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 340 / (0.8e-3) MPa = 425 GPa | Answer: 425 GPa

question: A block of mass 48 kg has a volume of 2e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 48, V = 2 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 48 / (2e-3) | Answer: 24000 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 1100 mm is heated through 20 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 23e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 1100, dT = 20, al = 23 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 1100*23e-6*20 | Answer: 0.506 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 60 ohm, R2 = 160 ohm and R3 = 155 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 60, R2 = 160, R3 = 155 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 160*155 / 60 | Answer: 413.3 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 120 ohm and gauge factor 2.2 experiences a strain of 1850e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 120, GF = 2.2, eps = 1850 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 120*2.2*1850e-6 | Answer: 488.4 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 9.29 when the true value is 100. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.29, true = 100 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.29 - 100| / 100 * 100 | Answer: 90.71 %

question: Annual demand is 5000 units, ordering cost 50 per order and holding cost 34 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 5000, S = 50, H = 34 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*5000*50 / 34) | Answer: 121.3 units

question: An asset costs 270000 with salvage value 12000 after 20 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 270000, Sv = 12000, n = 20 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (270000 - 12000) / 20 | Answer: 12900 per year

question: A product sells for 500 per unit with variable cost 90 per unit and fixed costs 175000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 500, V = 90, F = 175000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 175000 / (500 - 90) | Answer: 426.8 units

question: Find the present worth of 50000 received 5 years from now at an interest rate of 10% per year.
solution: Given: F = 50000, n = 5, i = 10 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 50000 / (1 + 0.1)^5 | Answer: 31046 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.98, 0.98 and 0.98 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.98, r2 = 0.98, r3 = 0.98 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.98*0.98*0.98 | Answer: 0.9412

question: A process produces 18 defective items in a batch of 10500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 18, N = 10500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 18/10500 * 1e6 | Answer: 1714 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -6x^3 + 2x^2 - 4x + 9 evaluated at x = -5.
For f(x) = 6x^3 - 2x^2 + 6x + 4, find f''(x) at x = -1.
Evaluate the definite integral of (-5x^2 + 2x + 2) dx from x = -4 to x = 4.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = -5x^3/3 + 2x^2/2 + 2x | Evaluate F(4) - F(-4) | Answer: -197.3
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 5x^2 + 9x - 3 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[-7, 4], [-5, -7]].
solution: Given: a = -7, b = 4, c = -5, d = -7 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (-7)(-7) - (4)(-5) | Answer: 69

question: Find the determinant of [[5, -2, -5], [2, -1, 1], [-1, 3, 0]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: -38

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[6, -5], [-2, -4]].
solution: Trace tr = 2, Determinant = -34 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 6.916

question: Solve for x: -1x + 0y = -2 and -4x + -2y = -11.
solution: Determinant = -1*-2 - 0*-4 = 2 | x = (e d - b f) / det = 2 | Answer: x = 2
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 9, 40, 58, 53, 82.
solution: Sum = 242 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 48.4 | Answer: 48.4

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 47, 3, 7, 14, 11.
solution: Mean = 16.4 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 17.6

question: Find the slope of the line through (-6, -6) and (-5, -4).
solution: Given: x1 = -6, y1 = -6, x2 = -5, y2 = -4 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (-4 - -6) / (-5 - -6) | Answer: 2

question: Find the distance between the points (-4, -1) and (7, 7).
solution: Given: x1 = -4, y1 = -1, x2 = 7, y2 = 7 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((11)^2 + (8)^2) | Answer: 13.6 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (-7,-3), (5,7), (-2,4).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 17 sq units

question: Find the 17th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 18 and common difference 0.
solution: Given: a = 18, d = 0, n = 17 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = 18 + (17 - 1)*0 | Answer: 18

question: Find the sum of the first 36 terms of an AP with first term 8 and common difference 5.
solution: Given: a = 8, d = 5, n = 36 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 36/2 [2*8 + (36-1)*5] | Answer: 3438

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 38000 at 6.4% per annum for 4 years.
solution: Given: P = 38000, R = 6.4, Tt = 4 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 38000 * 6.4 * 4 / 100 | Answer: 9728 currency units

question: Find the amount when 20500 is invested at 9.7% per annum compounded annually for 4 years.
solution: Given: P = 20500, R = 9.7, Tt = 4 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 20500 * (1 + 9.7/100)^4 | Answer: 29688 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (2, -3, 3) and (-2, -1, 5).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (1, 0, 6) and (0, 1, 4).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 7.28

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (-3, 1, 2) and (1, -6, 2).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 102 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number -6 + -12i.
solution: Given: a = -6, b = -12 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((-6)^2 + (-12)^2) | Answer: 13.42

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number -8 + 7i.
solution: Given: a = -8, b = 7 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(7, -8) | Answer: 138.8 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -5x^3 + x^2 + 2x + 4 at x = -2.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-20 with initial guess x0=6, find x1 (one iteration).
solution: Given: N = 20, x0 = 6 | Formula: x1 = x0 - (x0^2 - N)/(2 x0) | Substitute: x1 = 6 - ((6)^2 - 20)/(2*6) | Answer: 4.667

question: Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.7 and ordinates 1, 10, 4, 18, 15, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 262 and 72.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 262 and 72 | Answer: GCD = 2

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 21 and 22.
solution: Given: a = 21, b = 22 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 21*22 / 1 | Answer: 462
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 11 mm carries an axial tensile load of 71 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 30 mm and length 2300 mm carries an axial load of 42 kN. Take E = 70 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 78 mm transmits a torque of 1400 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 78, Tt = 1400 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(1400*1000) / (pi*(78)^3) | Answer: 15.02 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 38 mm and length 1200 mm carries a torque of 1600 N-m. With G = 45 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (38)^4 / 32 = 204708 mm^4 | theta = (1600*1000)(1200) / (45000 * 204708) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 11.94 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 92 mm wide and 270 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 92, h = 270 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 92*(270)^2 / 6 | Answer: 1117800 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (67 mm x 120 mm) carries a bending moment of 35 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (59 mm x 90 mm) has effective length 2600 mm and E = 200 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 630 MPa is designed for a working stress of 190 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 630, sw = 190 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 630 / 190 | Answer: 3.316

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 950 mm and wall thickness 11 mm carries an internal pressure of 2 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 950, t = 11, P = 2 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 2*950 / (2*11) | Answer: 86.36 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 660 K and 350 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 660, Tc = 350 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 350/660) * 100 | Answer: 46.97 %

question: A refrigerator works between 273 K (cold) and 320 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 273, Th = 320 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 273 / (320 - 273) | Answer: 5.809

question: A heat pump operates between 284 K and 314 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 284, Th = 314 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 314 / (314 - 284) | Answer: 10.47

question: 3.3 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 145 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.3, dT = 145 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 3.3 * 0.718 * 145 | Answer: 343.6 kJ

question: 5.2 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 20 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 5.2, dT = 20 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 5.2 * 1.005 * 20 | Answer: 104.5 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 1.1 m^3 at 320 K with mass 4.2 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 1.1, Tk = 320, m = 4.2 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 4.2*0.287*320 / 1.1 | Answer: 350.7 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 2.4 kg of air expands isothermally at 390 K from volume V1 to 4*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.4, Tk = 390, ratio = 4 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 2.4*0.287*390*ln(4) | Answer: 372.4 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 3.9 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.34 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 3.9, D = 0.34 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*3.9*0.34 / 0.001 | Answer: 1326000

question: Water flows at 2.2 m/s through a pipe of diameter 230 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 12.4 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 12.4 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*12.4 / 1000 | Answer: 121.6 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 10.5 m. Taking Cv = 0.98, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 10.5, cv = 0.98 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.98*sqrt(2*9.81*10.5) | Answer: 14.07 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 170 mm) water flows at 2 m/s. It contracts to diameter 130 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 170, d2 = 130, V1 = 2 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 2*(170/130)^2 | Answer: 3.42 m/s

question: Water flows at 3.3 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.26 m and length 450 m. With friction factor f = 0.031, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 18 teeth drives a gear of 117 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1250 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 18, z2 = 117, N1 = 1250 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1250*18 / 117 | Answer: 192.3 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 330 mm rotates at 300 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 330, N = 300 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.33)*300 / 60 | Answer: 5.184 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 20.9 kW at 1100 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 20.9, N = 1100 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(20.9*1000) / (2*pi*1100) | Answer: 181.4 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 6.6 kg rotates at radius 0.25 m at 1150 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 12200 N/m and mass 5.5 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 12200, m = 5.5 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(12200/5.5) | Answer: 7.496 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 5.6 m^2 and thickness 0.11 m has conductivity k = 18.5 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 175 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 5.6, L = 0.11, k = 18.5, dT = 175 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 18.5*5.6*175 / 0.11 | Answer: 164818 W

question: A surface of area 4.1 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 140 W/m^2-K to surroundings 110 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 4.1, h = 140, dT = 110 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 140*4.1*110 | Answer: 63140 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 80 m/min, feed = 0.29 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2.5 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 80, f = 0.29, d = 2.5 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*80*0.29*2.5 | Answer: 58000 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 480 mm is turned at 750 rpm with a feed of 0.25 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 480, N = 750, f = 0.25 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 480 / (0.25*750) | Answer: 2.56 min

question: A resistor of 111 ohm carries a current of 8.9 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 111, I = 8.9 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 8.9 * 111 | Answer: 987.9 V

question: Three resistors 84 ohm, 86 ohm and 24 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 84, R2 = 86, R3 = 24 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 84 + 86 + 24 | Answer: 194 ohm

question: Two resistors 68 ohm and 112 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 68, R2 = 112 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 68*112 / (68+112) | Answer: 42.31 ohm

question: A device draws 6.3 A at 60 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 60, I = 6.3 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 60 * 6.3 | Answer: 378 W

question: A current of 5.1 A flows through a 100 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 5.1, R = 100 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (5.1)^2 * 100 | Answer: 2601 W

question: Two capacitors 20.7 uF and 42.5 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 20.7, C2 = 42.5 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 20.7*42.5 / (20.7+42.5) | Answer: 13.92 uF

question: A resistor 86 kohm and capacitor 19.8 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 86, C = 19.8 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (86k)(19.8u) = 1703 ms | Answer: 1703 ms

question: An inductor 230.3 mH is in series with 106 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 230.3, R = 106 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (230.3e-3) / 106 | Answer: 2.173 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 64.2 mH inductor at 590 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 64.2, f = 590 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (590)(64.2e-3) | Answer: 238 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 10.2 uF capacitor at 150 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 10.2, f = 150 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (150)(10.2e-6)) | Answer: 104 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 62 ohm, XL = 60 ohm and XC = 90 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 62, XL = 60, XC = 90 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(62^2 + (60 - 90)^2) | Answer: 68.88 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 74.4 mH and C = 3.6 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 74.4, C = 3.6 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(74.4e-3 * 3.6e-6)) | Answer: 307.5 Hz

question: A capacitor of 40.8 uF is charged to 330 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 40.8, V = 330 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*40.8e-6*(330)^2 | Answer: 2222 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 360 V with 660 primary turns and 140 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 360, N1 = 660, N2 = 140 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 360 * 140/660 | Answer: 76.36 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 200 V and draws an armature current of 16 A. If the armature resistance is 1.13 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 200, Ia = 16, Ra = 1.13 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 200 - 16*1.13 | Answer: 181.9 V

question: A 6-pole induction motor on a 50 Hz supply runs at 950 rpm. Find the slip (%).
formula: s = (Ns - N) / Ns,  Ns = 120 f / P

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 165 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.83. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 165, VL = 400, pf = 0.83 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*400*165*0.83 / 1000 | Answer: 94.88 kW

question: A load has real power 130 kW and apparent power 160 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 130, S = 160 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 130 / 160 | Answer: 0.8125

question: A machine delivers 55 kW output while drawing 117 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 55, Pi = 117 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 55/117 * 100 | Answer: 47.01 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 23 V across R1 = 2 ohm and R2 = 26 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 23, R1 = 2, R2 = 26 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 23*26 / (2+26) | Answer: 21.36 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 170 kohm and Rin = 4 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 170, Rin = 4 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 170 / 4 | Answer: 42.5

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 140 kohm and Rg = 18 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 140, Rg = 18 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 140/18 | Answer: 8.778

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 332. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 332 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(332) | Answer: 25.21 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 5.6 m carries a central point load of 45 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.6, W = 45 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 45*5.6 / 4 | Answer: 63 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.8 m carries a UDL of 40 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 9.8, w = 40 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 40*(9.8)^2 / 8 | Answer: 480.2 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 2.8 m carries a point load 40 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 2.8, W = 40 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 40*2.8 | Answer: 112 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 1.2 m carries a UDL of 36 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 1.2, w = 36 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 36*(1.2)^2 / 2 | Answer: 25.92 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 7.7 m carries a point load 10 kN at distance 3.1 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 7.7, a = 3.1, W = 10 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 10*(7.7 - 3.1) / 7.7 | Answer: 5.974 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 6.5 m) carries a central point load 50 kN. With E = 25 GPa and I = 120e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=50000 N, L=6500.0 mm, E=25000 MPa, I=120e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 95.36 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 8.9 m carries a UDL of 24 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 8.9, w = 24 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 24*(8.9)^2 / 12 | Answer: 158.4 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 410 mm, clear cover 35 mm and main bars of diameter 25 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 410, c = 35, dia = 25 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 410 - 35 - 25/2 | Answer: 362.5 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 18.6 m^2 carrying a factored load of 10.9 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 18.6, w = 10.9 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 10.9 * 18.6 | Answer: 202.7 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 5.4 m, unit weight 16 kN/m^3, phi = 38 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 3.2 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 21 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 3.2, g = 21 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (21 - 9.81)*3.2 | Answer: 35.81 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 5.3e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1.1, area = 5.1e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 5.3, i = 1.1, A = 5.1 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (5.3e-4)*1.1*(5.1e-3) | Answer: 2973 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.8 m, bed slope 0.004 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.021. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 4.7 m under a head of 0.7 m. Taking Cd = 0.61 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 4.2 m wide carries a discharge of 28.8 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 450 m and design speed 95 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 450, V = 95 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (95)^2 / (127*450) | Answer: 0.1579
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: A tank of volume 200 m^3 treats a flow of 65 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 200, Q = 65 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 200 / 65 | Answer: 3.077 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 290 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.12 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 8 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 290, k = 0.12, t = 8 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 290*(1 - e^(-0.12*8)) | Answer: 179 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.5, rainfall intensity 80 mm/h over a catchment of 21.2 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.5, i = 80, A = 21.2 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.5*80*21.2 / 360 | Answer: 2.356 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.05 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 440 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.05, M = 440 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 440*(30+0.05)/30 | Answer: 440.7 m

question: Convert the decimal number 120 to binary.
solution: Divide 120 by 2 repeatedly, recording remainders | Reading remainders in reverse gives 1111000 | Answer: 1111000 (binary)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 2 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the decimal number 889 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 889 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 379 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the 8-bit binary number 10011110 to decimal.
solution: Binary 10011110 = sum of bit-weights | Answer: 158 (decimal)
formula: Sum each bit times its positional weight (2^i)

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 01100001 and 10011000.
solution: XOR: 11111001 | Count of 1s = 6 | Answer: 6
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 920 megabits is sent over a link of 88 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 920, B = 88 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 920 / 88 | Answer: 10.45 s

question: A link has bandwidth 53 Mbps and round-trip time 140 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 53, R = 140 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 53e6 * 140e-3 bits = 7420 kb | Answer: 7420 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.85, cache access time 4 ns and main-memory access time 200 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.85, tc = 4, tm = 200 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.85*4 + (1 - 0.85)*200 | Answer: 33.4 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 206328 elements?
solution: Given: n = 206328 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(206328)) + 1 | Answer: 18

question: An O(n^2) algorithm performs c*n^2 basic operations. If c = 1 and n = 2640, how many operations are performed?
solution: Given: n = 2640 | Formula: operations = n^2 | Substitute: = (2640)^2 | Answer: 6969600

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.008, memory access time 110 ns and page-fault service time 7 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 7 ms = 7000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.008)*110 + 0.008*7000000.0 ns | Answer: 56.11 microseconds
