A rod of diameter 25 mm and length 900 mm carries an axial load of 86 kN. Take E = 210 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 29 mm transmits a torque of 150 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 29, Tt = 150 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(150*1000) / (pi*(29)^3) | Answer: 31.32 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 38 mm and length 1900 mm carries a torque of 1300 N-m. With G = 80 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (38)^4 / 32 = 204708 mm^4 | theta = (1300*1000)(1900) / (80000 * 204708) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 8.642 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 128 mm wide and 200 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 128, h = 200 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 128*(200)^2 / 6 | Answer: 853333 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (45 mm x 130 mm) carries a bending moment of 16 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (47 mm x 150 mm) has effective length 2800 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 350 MPa is designed for a working stress of 70 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 350, sw = 70 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 350 / 70 | Answer: 5

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 950 mm and wall thickness 20 mm carries an internal pressure of 1 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 950, t = 20, P = 1 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 1*950 / (2*20) | Answer: 23.75 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 760 K and 390 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 760, Tc = 390 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 390/760) * 100 | Answer: 48.68 %

question: A refrigerator works between 271 K (cold) and 328 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 271, Th = 328 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 271 / (328 - 271) | Answer: 4.754

question: A heat pump operates between 275 K and 308 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 275, Th = 308 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 308 / (308 - 275) | Answer: 9.333

question: 7.9 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 110 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 7.9, dT = 110 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 7.9 * 0.718 * 110 | Answer: 623.9 kJ

question: 3.4 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 85 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.4, dT = 85 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 3.4 * 1.005 * 85 | Answer: 290.4 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 3.1 m^3 at 460 K with mass 2.6 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 3.1, Tk = 460, m = 2.6 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 2.6*0.287*460 / 3.1 | Answer: 110.7 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 1.2 kg of air expands isothermally at 390 K from volume V1 to 4*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1.2, Tk = 390, ratio = 4 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 1.2*0.287*390*ln(4) | Answer: 186.2 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 4.4 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.25 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 4.4, D = 0.25 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*4.4*0.25 / 0.001 | Answer: 1100000

question: Water flows at 2.1 m/s through a pipe of diameter 60 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 18 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 18 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*18 / 1000 | Answer: 176.6 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 7.4 m. Taking Cv = 0.99, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 7.4, cv = 0.99 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.99*sqrt(2*9.81*7.4) | Answer: 11.93 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 220 mm) water flows at 1.3 m/s. It contracts to diameter 120 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
Water flows at 1.1 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.3 m and length 50 m. With friction factor f = 0.034, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 39 teeth drives a gear of 78 teeth. If the pinion runs at 450 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 39, z2 = 78, N1 = 450 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 450*39 / 78 | Answer: 225 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 510 mm rotates at 450 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 510, N = 450 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.51)*450 / 60 | Answer: 12.02 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 33.3 kW at 450 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 33.3, N = 450 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(33.3*1000) / (2*pi*450) | Answer: 706.6 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 8.3 kg rotates at radius 0.15 m at 400 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 11400 N/m and mass 3.2 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 11400, m = 3.2 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(11400/3.2) | Answer: 9.499 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 9 m^2 and thickness 0.16 m has conductivity k = 4.5 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 110 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 9, L = 0.16, k = 4.5, dT = 110 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 4.5*9*110 / 0.16 | Answer: 27844 W

question: A surface of area 1.5 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 160 W/m^2-K to surroundings 30 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 1.5, h = 160, dT = 30 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 160*1.5*30 | Answer: 7200 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 250 m/min, feed = 0.39 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2.4 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 250, f = 0.39, d = 2.4 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*250*0.39*2.4 | Answer: 234000 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 120 mm is turned at 1150 rpm with a feed of 0.36 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 120, N = 1150, f = 0.36 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 120 / (0.36*1150) | Answer: 0.2899 min

question: A resistor of 99 ohm carries a current of 2.1 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 99, I = 2.1 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 2.1 * 99 | Answer: 207.9 V

question: Three resistors 34 ohm, 71 ohm and 2 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 34, R2 = 71, R3 = 2 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 34 + 71 + 2 | Answer: 107 ohm

question: Two resistors 111 ohm and 96 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 111, R2 = 96 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 111*96 / (111+96) | Answer: 51.48 ohm

question: A device draws 10.8 A at 220 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 220, I = 10.8 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 220 * 10.8 | Answer: 2376 W

question: A current of 11.4 A flows through a 54 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 11.4, R = 54 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (11.4)^2 * 54 | Answer: 7018 W

question: Two capacitors 47.8 uF and 44.5 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 47.8, C2 = 44.5 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 47.8*44.5 / (47.8+44.5) | Answer: 23.05 uF

question: A resistor 99 kohm and capacitor 6.4 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 99, C = 6.4 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (99k)(6.4u) = 633.6 ms | Answer: 633.6 ms

question: An inductor 143.5 mH is in series with 62 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 143.5, R = 62 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (143.5e-3) / 62 | Answer: 2.315 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 52 mH inductor at 610 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 52, f = 610 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (610)(52e-3) | Answer: 199.3 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 37.9 uF capacitor at 180 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 37.9, f = 180 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (180)(37.9e-6)) | Answer: 23.33 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 81 ohm, XL = 86 ohm and XC = 83 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 81, XL = 86, XC = 83 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(81^2 + (86 - 83)^2) | Answer: 81.06 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 11.7 mH and C = 8.7 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 11.7, C = 8.7 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(11.7e-3 * 8.7e-6)) | Answer: 498.8 Hz

question: A capacitor of 18.5 uF is charged to 105 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 18.5, V = 105 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*18.5e-6*(105)^2 | Answer: 102 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 330 V with 410 primary turns and 250 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 330, N1 = 410, N2 = 250 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 330 * 250/410 | Answer: 201.2 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 150 V and draws an armature current of 41 A. If the armature resistance is 0.71 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 150, Ia = 41, Ra = 0.71 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 150 - 41*0.71 | Answer: 120.9 V

question: A 4-pole induction motor on a 50 Hz supply runs at 770 rpm. Find the slip (%).
formula: s = (Ns - N) / Ns,  Ns = 120 f / P

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 30 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.93. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 30, VL = 400, pf = 0.93 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*400*30*0.93 / 1000 | Answer: 19.33 kW

question: A load has real power 65 kW and apparent power 140 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 65, S = 140 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 65 / 140 | Answer: 0.4643

question: A machine delivers 65 kW output while drawing 152 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 65, Pi = 152 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 65/152 * 100 | Answer: 42.76 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 27 V across R1 = 2 ohm and R2 = 34 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 27, R1 = 2, R2 = 34 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 27*34 / (2+34) | Answer: 25.5 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 210 kohm and Rin = 30 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 210, Rin = 30 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 210 / 30 | Answer: 7

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 10 kohm and Rg = 7 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 10, Rg = 7 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 10/7 | Answer: 2.429

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 4116. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 4116 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(4116) | Answer: 36.14 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.7 m carries a central point load of 10 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6.7, W = 10 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 10*6.7 / 4 | Answer: 16.75 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.3 m carries a UDL of 60 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.3, w = 60 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 60*(4.3)^2 / 8 | Answer: 138.7 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 5.1 m carries a point load 35 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.1, W = 35 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 35*5.1 | Answer: 178.5 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 3.1 m carries a UDL of 32 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.1, w = 32 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 32*(3.1)^2 / 2 | Answer: 153.8 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 7.1 m carries a point load 65 kN at distance 2.2 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 7.1, a = 2.2, W = 65 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 65*(7.1 - 2.2) / 7.1 | Answer: 44.86 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 6.8 m) carries a central point load 70 kN. With E = 30 GPa and I = 390e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=70000 N, L=6800.0 mm, E=30000 MPa, I=390e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 39.19 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 7 m carries a UDL of 24 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7, w = 24 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 24*(7)^2 / 12 | Answer: 98 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 630 mm, clear cover 25 mm and main bars of diameter 20 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 630, c = 25, dia = 20 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 630 - 25 - 20/2 | Answer: 595 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 22.1 m^2 carrying a factored load of 20 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 22.1, w = 20 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 20 * 22.1 | Answer: 442 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 4 m, unit weight 19 kN/m^3, phi = 35 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 6.6 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 20 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 6.6, g = 20 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (20 - 9.81)*6.6 | Answer: 67.25 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 5.3e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.7, area = 3.9e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 5.3, i = 0.7, A = 3.9 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (5.3e-4)*0.7*(3.9e-3) | Answer: 1447 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.2 m, bed slope 0.007 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.019. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 2.7 m under a head of 0.8 m. Taking Cd = 0.6 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 2.6 m wide carries a discharge of 16.1 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 290 m and design speed 50 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 290, V = 50 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (50)^2 / (127*290) | Answer: 0.06788
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: For a design speed of 70 km/h with allowable superelevation 0.08 and lateral friction 0.15, find the minimum curve radius in m.
A tank of volume 900 m^3 treats a flow of 130 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 900, Q = 130 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 900 / 130 | Answer: 6.923 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 280 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.28 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 4 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 280, k = 0.28, t = 4 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 280*(1 - e^(-0.28*4)) | Answer: 188.6 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.41, rainfall intensity 85 mm/h over a catchment of 14.2 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.41, i = 85, A = 14.2 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.41*85*14.2 / 360 | Answer: 1.375 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.04 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 290 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.04, M = 290 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 290*(20+0.04)/20 | Answer: 290.6 m

question: Convert the decimal number 217 to binary.
solution: Divide 217 by 2 repeatedly, recording remainders | Reading remainders in reverse gives 11011001 | Answer: 11011001 (binary)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 2 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the decimal number 4036 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 4036 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: FC4 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the 8-bit binary number 11010110 to decimal.
solution: Binary 11010110 = sum of bit-weights | Answer: 214 (decimal)
formula: Sum each bit times its positional weight (2^i)

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 10001011 and 10111100.
solution: XOR: 00110111 | Count of 1s = 5 | Answer: 5
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 840 megabits is sent over a link of 22 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 840, B = 22 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 840 / 22 | Answer: 38.18 s

question: A link has bandwidth 42 Mbps and round-trip time 50 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 42, R = 50 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 42e6 * 50e-3 bits = 2100 kb | Answer: 2100 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.85, cache access time 10 ns and main-memory access time 170 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.85, tc = 10, tm = 170 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.85*10 + (1 - 0.85)*170 | Answer: 34 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 988219 elements?
solution: Given: n = 988219 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(988219)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: An O(n^2) algorithm performs c*n^2 basic operations. If c = 1 and n = 30, how many operations are performed?
solution: Given: n = 30 | Formula: operations = n^2 | Substitute: = (30)^2 | Answer: 900

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.007, memory access time 200 ns and page-fault service time 4 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 4 ms = 4000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.007)*200 + 0.007*4000000.0 ns | Answer: 28.2 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 0.1 m^3 at 110 kPa and 520 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 0.1, P = 110, Tk = 520 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (110e3)*0.1 / (8.314*520) | Answer: 2.544 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.16 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 2 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.16, t = 2 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.16*2) | Answer: 0.2739

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.41 /min) is to reach 50% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.41, X = 50 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.5) / 0.41 | Answer: 1.691 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.15 /min) reaches 70% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.15, X = 70 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.7 / (0.15*(1 - 0.7)) | Answer: 15.56 min

question: For a reaction with A = 5e10 /s and activation energy 60 kJ/mol at 320 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 5, Ea = 60, Tk = 320 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 5e10 * exp(-60e3 / (8.314*320)) | Answer: 8.028 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.92 and bottoms xW = 0.07, with relative volatility alpha = 3.4. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.92, xw = 0.07, al = 3.4 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.92/0.08)(0.93/0.07)] / ln(3.4) | Answer: 4.109 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.77 and x = 0.31. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.77, x = 0.31 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.77/0.23) / (0.31/0.69) | Answer: 7.452

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.57 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 95 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.57, Psat = 95 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.57 * 95 | Answer: 54.15 kPa

question: A stream of 1.5 kg/s with specific heat 1.7 kJ/kg-K is heated through 30 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 1.5, cp = 1.7, dT = 30 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 1.5*1.7*30 | Answer: 76.5 kW

question: A reactor of volume 15 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 0.4 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 15, Q = 0.4 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 15 / 0.4 | Answer: 37.5 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 6.3e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 4 mm with a concentration difference of 170 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 6.3, L = 4, dC = 170 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (6.3e-9)*170 / (4e-3) | Answer: 267.8 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 8.7 min and steady-state gain 3.8. For a step input of magnitude 2, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 8.7, K = 3.8, M = 2 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 3.8 * 2 | Answer: 7.6 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 20 m^2 flies at 220 m/s (air density 0.4 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.6. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 20, V = 220, rho = 0.4, CL = 0.6 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.4*(220)^2*20*0.6 / 1000 | Answer: 116.2 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 20 m^2 flies at 230 m/s (density 1.225 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.11. Find the drag force in kN.
A specimen under stress 160 MPa shows an elastic strain of 1.3e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 160, eps = 1.3 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 160 / (1.3e-3) MPa = 123.1 GPa | Answer: 123.1 GPa

question: A block of mass 14 kg has a volume of 4.9e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 14, V = 4.9 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 14 / (4.9e-3) | Answer: 2857 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 1000 mm is heated through 125 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 17e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 1000, dT = 125, al = 17 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 1000*17e-6*125 | Answer: 2.125 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 60 ohm, R2 = 30 ohm and R3 = 280 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 60, R2 = 30, R3 = 280 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 30*280 / 60 | Answer: 140 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 1000 ohm and gauge factor 2.1 experiences a strain of 1550e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 1000, GF = 2.1, eps = 1550 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 1000*2.1*1550e-6 | Answer: 3255 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 9.65 when the true value is 10. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.65, true = 10 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.65 - 10| / 10 * 100 | Answer: 3.5 %

question: Annual demand is 27500 units, ordering cost 70 per order and holding cost 18 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 27500, S = 70, H = 18 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*27500*70 / 18) | Answer: 462.5 units

question: An asset costs 210000 with salvage value 12000 after 18 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 210000, Sv = 12000, n = 18 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (210000 - 12000) / 18 | Answer: 11000 per year

question: A product sells for 200 per unit with variable cost 50 per unit and fixed costs 20000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 200, V = 50, F = 20000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 20000 / (200 - 50) | Answer: 133.3 units

question: Find the present worth of 175000 received 10 years from now at an interest rate of 10% per year.
solution: Given: F = 175000, n = 10, i = 10 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 175000 / (1 + 0.1)^10 | Answer: 6747 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.93, 0.94 and 0.92 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.93, r2 = 0.94, r3 = 0.92 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.93*0.94*0.92 | Answer: 0.8043

question: A process produces 33 defective items in a batch of 10000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 33, N = 10000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 33/10000 * 1e6 | Answer: 3300 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = x^3 - 4x^2 + 8x + 8 evaluated at x = -5.
For f(x) = -2x^3 - 2x - 4, find f''(x) at x = -1.
Evaluate the definite integral of (x^2 - 6x - 7) dx from x = -4 to x = 5.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = 1x^3/3 + -6x^2/2 + -7x | Evaluate F(5) - F(-4) | Answer: -27
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 3x^2 - 12x - 7 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[-5, 3], [0, -7]].
solution: Given: a = -5, b = 3, c = 0, d = -7 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (-5)(-7) - (3)(0) | Answer: 35

question: Find the determinant of [[-6, 4, 2], [-5, 3, 2], [3, -6, -3]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: -12

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[8, 1], [-4, 3]].
solution: Trace tr = 11, Determinant = 28 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 7

question: Solve for x: 2x + -3y = 7 and 0x + 3y = -2.
solution: Determinant = 2*3 - -3*0 = 6 | x = (e d - b f) / det = 2.5 | Answer: x = 2.5
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 33, 26, 35, 57, 26.
solution: Sum = 177 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 35.4 | Answer: 35.4

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 16, 7, 29, 9, 3.
solution: Mean = 12.8 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 10.21

question: Find the slope of the line through (-7, 6) and (6, -7).
solution: Given: x1 = -7, y1 = 6, x2 = 6, y2 = -7 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (-7 - 6) / (6 - -7) | Answer: -1

question: Find the distance between the points (8, -5) and (0, -6).
solution: Given: x1 = 8, y1 = -5, x2 = 0, y2 = -6 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-8)^2 + (-1)^2) | Answer: 8.062 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (-5,-5), (-7,-4), (0,1).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 8.5 sq units

question: Find the 5th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -8 and common difference 1.
solution: Given: a = -8, d = 1, n = 5 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -8 + (5 - 1)*1 | Answer: -4

question: Find the sum of the first 30 terms of an AP with first term -9 and common difference -6.
solution: Given: a = -9, d = -6, n = 30 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 30/2 [2*-9 + (30-1)*-6] | Answer: -2880

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 43500 at 9.2% per annum for 10 years.
solution: Given: P = 43500, R = 9.2, Tt = 10 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 43500 * 9.2 * 10 / 100 | Answer: 40020 currency units

question: Find the amount when 1500 is invested at 9.5% per annum compounded annually for 2 years.
solution: Given: P = 1500, R = 9.5, Tt = 2 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 1500 * (1 + 9.5/100)^2 | Answer: 1799 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (-8, -1, 6) and (6, 8, 4).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (-2, 4, -1) and (4, 0, 1).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 16.61

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (-2, 1, -2) and (-4, 1, 1).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 56.63 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number 9 + -11i.
solution: Given: a = 9, b = -11 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((9)^2 + (-11)^2) | Answer: 14.21

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number -2 + -7i.
solution: Given: a = -2, b = -7 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(-7, -2) | Answer: -105.9 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -5x^3 - 5x^2 + 8x - 6 at x = -2.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-82 with initial guess x0=6, find x1 (one iteration).
solution: Given: N = 82, x0 = 6 | Formula: x1 = x0 - (x0^2 - N)/(2 x0) | Substitute: x1 = 6 - ((6)^2 - 82)/(2*6) | Answer: 9.833

question: Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1 and ordinates 12, 10, 12, 0, 14, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 281 and 51.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 281 and 51 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 30 and 55.
solution: Given: a = 30, b = 55 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 30*55 / 5 | Answer: 330
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 59 mm carries an axial tensile load of 51 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 39 mm and length 2100 mm carries an axial load of 32 kN. Take E = 110 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 78 mm transmits a torque of 2450 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 78, Tt = 2450 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(2450*1000) / (pi*(78)^3) | Answer: 26.29 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 39 mm and length 1100 mm carries a torque of 800 N-m. With G = 77 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (39)^4 / 32 = 227122 mm^4 | theta = (800*1000)(1100) / (77000 * 227122) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 2.883 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 108 mm wide and 130 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 108, h = 130 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 108*(130)^2 / 6 | Answer: 304200 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (46 mm x 120 mm) carries a bending moment of 28 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (37 mm x 90 mm) has effective length 1800 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 750 MPa is designed for a working stress of 120 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 750, sw = 120 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 750 / 120 | Answer: 6.25

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1400 mm and wall thickness 11 mm carries an internal pressure of 2.1 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1400, t = 11, P = 2.1 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 2.1*1400 / (2*11) | Answer: 133.6 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 600 K and 340 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 600, Tc = 340 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 340/600) * 100 | Answer: 43.33 %

question: A refrigerator works between 265 K (cold) and 302 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 265, Th = 302 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 265 / (302 - 265) | Answer: 7.162

question: A heat pump operates between 284 K and 316 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 284, Th = 316 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 316 / (316 - 284) | Answer: 9.875

question: 7.6 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 125 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 7.6, dT = 125 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 7.6 * 0.718 * 125 | Answer: 682.1 kJ

question: 4.2 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 170 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.2, dT = 170 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 4.2 * 1.005 * 170 | Answer: 717.6 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 3.8 m^3 at 430 K with mass 3.6 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 3.8, Tk = 430, m = 3.6 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 3.6*0.287*430 / 3.8 | Answer: 116.9 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 1.1 kg of air expands isothermally at 300 K from volume V1 to 3*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1.1, Tk = 300, ratio = 3 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 1.1*0.287*300*ln(3) | Answer: 104 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 2.4 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.09 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 2.4, D = 0.09 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*2.4*0.09 / 0.001 | Answer: 216000

question: Water flows at 3.8 m/s through a pipe of diameter 70 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 14.1 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 14.1 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*14.1 / 1000 | Answer: 138.3 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 5.7 m. Taking Cv = 0.97, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 5.7, cv = 0.97 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.97*sqrt(2*9.81*5.7) | Answer: 10.26 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 180 mm) water flows at 2.3 m/s. It contracts to diameter 100 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
Water flows at 4 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.26 m and length 320 m. With friction factor f = 0.032, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 26 teeth drives a gear of 74 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1150 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 26, z2 = 74, N1 = 1150 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1150*26 / 74 | Answer: 404.1 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 500 mm rotates at 1400 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 500, N = 1400 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.5)*1400 / 60 | Answer: 36.65 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 29.8 kW at 350 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 29.8, N = 350 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(29.8*1000) / (2*pi*350) | Answer: 813.1 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 4.9 kg rotates at radius 0.47 m at 700 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 3100 N/m and mass 14.6 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 3100, m = 14.6 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(3100/14.6) | Answer: 2.319 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 7.5 m^2 and thickness 0.27 m has conductivity k = 37.2 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 65 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 7.5, L = 0.27, k = 37.2, dT = 65 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 37.2*7.5*65 / 0.27 | Answer: 67167 W

question: A surface of area 4.1 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 200 W/m^2-K to surroundings 125 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 4.1, h = 200, dT = 125 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 200*4.1*125 | Answer: 102500 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 70 m/min, feed = 0.23 mm/rev, depth of cut = 0.6 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 70, f = 0.23, d = 0.6 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*70*0.23*0.6 | Answer: 9660 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 210 mm is turned at 950 rpm with a feed of 0.16 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 210, N = 950, f = 0.16 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 210 / (0.16*950) | Answer: 1.382 min

question: A resistor of 133 ohm carries a current of 6.5 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 133, I = 6.5 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 6.5 * 133 | Answer: 864.5 V

question: Three resistors 57 ohm, 60 ohm and 89 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 57, R2 = 60, R3 = 89 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 57 + 60 + 89 | Answer: 206 ohm

question: Two resistors 94 ohm and 48 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 94, R2 = 48 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 94*48 / (94+48) | Answer: 31.77 ohm

question: A device draws 5.2 A at 175 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 175, I = 5.2 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 175 * 5.2 | Answer: 910 W

question: A current of 0.8 A flows through a 43 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 0.8, R = 43 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (0.8)^2 * 43 | Answer: 27.52 W

question: Two capacitors 29.2 uF and 35.4 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 29.2, C2 = 35.4 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 29.2*35.4 / (29.2+35.4) | Answer: 16 uF

question: A resistor 100 kohm and capacitor 0.2 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 100, C = 0.2 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (100k)(0.2u) = 20 ms | Answer: 20 ms

question: An inductor 366.8 mH is in series with 191 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 366.8, R = 191 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (366.8e-3) / 191 | Answer: 1.92 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 29.7 mH inductor at 250 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 29.7, f = 250 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (250)(29.7e-3) | Answer: 46.65 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 4.1 uF capacitor at 250 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 4.1, f = 250 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (250)(4.1e-6)) | Answer: 155.3 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 90 ohm, XL = 124 ohm and XC = 127 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 90, XL = 124, XC = 127 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(90^2 + (124 - 127)^2) | Answer: 90.05 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 28.6 mH and C = 4.3 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 28.6, C = 4.3 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(28.6e-3 * 4.3e-6)) | Answer: 453.8 Hz

question: A capacitor of 17.8 uF is charged to 345 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 17.8, V = 345 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*17.8e-6*(345)^2 | Answer: 1059 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 430 V with 770 primary turns and 270 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 430, N1 = 770, N2 = 270 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 430 * 270/770 | Answer: 150.8 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 320 V and draws an armature current of 56 A. If the armature resistance is 1.18 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 320, Ia = 56, Ra = 1.18 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 320 - 56*1.18 | Answer: 253.9 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 95 A at 415 V (line) with a power factor of 0.72. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 95, VL = 415, pf = 0.72 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*415*95*0.72 / 1000 | Answer: 49.17 kW

question: A load has real power 85 kW and apparent power 175 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 85, S = 175 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 85 / 175 | Answer: 0.4857

question: A machine delivers 45 kW output while drawing 167 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 45, Pi = 167 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 45/167 * 100 | Answer: 26.95 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 19 V across R1 = 22 ohm and R2 = 22 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 19, R1 = 22, R2 = 22 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 19*22 / (22+22) | Answer: 9.5 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 20 kohm and Rin = 30 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 20, Rin = 30 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 20 / 30 | Answer: 0.6667

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 150 kohm and Rg = 10 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 150, Rg = 10 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 150/10 | Answer: 16

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 7331. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 7331 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(7331) | Answer: 38.65 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.8 m carries a central point load of 60 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6.8, W = 60 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 60*6.8 / 4 | Answer: 102 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 7.1 m carries a UDL of 35 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7.1, w = 35 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 35*(7.1)^2 / 8 | Answer: 220.5 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 5.9 m carries a point load 5 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.9, W = 5 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 5*5.9 | Answer: 29.5 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 3 m carries a UDL of 6 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3, w = 6 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 6*(3)^2 / 2 | Answer: 27 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.7 m carries a point load 25 kN at distance 1.3 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 4.7, a = 1.3, W = 25 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 25*(4.7 - 1.3) / 4.7 | Answer: 18.09 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 7.6 m) carries a central point load 65 kN. With E = 25 GPa and I = 260e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=65000 N, L=7600.0 mm, E=25000 MPa, I=260e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 91.45 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 6 m carries a UDL of 36 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6, w = 36 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 36*(6)^2 / 12 | Answer: 108 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 440 mm, clear cover 50 mm and main bars of diameter 25 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 440, c = 50, dia = 25 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 440 - 50 - 25/2 | Answer: 377.5 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 22.9 m^2 carrying a factored load of 19 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 22.9, w = 19 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 19 * 22.9 | Answer: 435.1 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 5.8 m, unit weight 19 kN/m^3, phi = 35 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 11.2 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 21 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 11.2, g = 21 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (21 - 9.81)*11.2 | Answer: 125.3 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 8.9e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.9, area = 2.7e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 8.9, i = 0.9, A = 2.7 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (8.9e-4)*0.9*(2.7e-3) | Answer: 2163 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.3 m, bed slope 0.008 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.02. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 3.9 m under a head of 0.2 m. Taking Cd = 0.64 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 2.2 m wide carries a discharge of 8.7 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 400 m and design speed 90 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 400, V = 90 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (90)^2 / (127*400) | Answer: 0.1594
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: For a design speed of 70 km/h with allowable superelevation 0.05 and lateral friction 0.16, find the minimum curve radius in m.
A tank of volume 1000 m^3 treats a flow of 80 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 1000, Q = 80 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 1000 / 80 | Answer: 12.5 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 170 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.26 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 8 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 170, k = 0.26, t = 8 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 170*(1 - e^(-0.26*8)) | Answer: 148.8 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.9, rainfall intensity 60 mm/h over a catchment of 56.7 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.9, i = 60, A = 56.7 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.9*60*56.7 / 360 | Answer: 8.505 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.04 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 780 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.04, M = 780 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 780*(30+0.04)/30 | Answer: 781 m

question: Convert the decimal number 163 to binary.
solution: Divide 163 by 2 repeatedly, recording remainders | Reading remainders in reverse gives 10100011 | Answer: 10100011 (binary)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 2 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the decimal number 786 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 786 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 312 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the 8-bit binary number 11101010 to decimal.
solution: Binary 11101010 = sum of bit-weights | Answer: 234 (decimal)
formula: Sum each bit times its positional weight (2^i)

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 01110011 and 10111111.
solution: XOR: 11001100 | Count of 1s = 4 | Answer: 4
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 550 megabits is sent over a link of 47 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 550, B = 47 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 550 / 47 | Answer: 11.7 s

question: A link has bandwidth 37 Mbps and round-trip time 60 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 37, R = 60 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 37e6 * 60e-3 bits = 2220 kb | Answer: 2220 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.82, cache access time 7 ns and main-memory access time 130 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.82, tc = 7, tm = 130 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.82*7 + (1 - 0.82)*130 | Answer: 29.14 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 444493 elements?
solution: Given: n = 444493 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(444493)) + 1 | Answer: 19

question: An O(n^2) algorithm performs c*n^2 basic operations. If c = 1 and n = 1700, how many operations are performed?
solution: Given: n = 1700 | Formula: operations = n^2 | Substitute: = (1700)^2 | Answer: 2890000

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.014, memory access time 170 ns and page-fault service time 8 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 8 ms = 8000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.014)*170 + 0.014*8000000.0 ns | Answer: 112.2 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 0.3 m^3 at 410 kPa and 390 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 0.3, P = 410, Tk = 390 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (410e3)*0.3 / (8.314*390) | Answer: 37.93 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.19 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 14 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.19, t = 14 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.19*14) | Answer: 0.9301

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.29 /min) is to reach 60% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.29, X = 60 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.6) / 0.29 | Answer: 3.16 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.24 /min) reaches 90% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.24, X = 90 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.9 / (0.24*(1 - 0.9)) | Answer: 37.5 min

question: For a reaction with A = 6e10 /s and activation energy 60 kJ/mol at 430 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 6, Ea = 60, Tk = 430 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 6e10 * exp(-60e3 / (8.314*430)) | Answer: 3086 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.9 and bottoms xW = 0.07, with relative volatility alpha = 2. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.9, xw = 0.07, al = 2 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.9/0.1)(0.93/0.07)] / ln(2) | Answer: 6.902 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.56 and x = 0.29. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.56, x = 0.29 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.56/0.44) / (0.29/0.71) | Answer: 3.116

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.26 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 85 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.26, Psat = 85 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.26 * 85 | Answer: 22.1 kPa

question: A stream of 7.7 kg/s with specific heat 3.9 kJ/kg-K is heated through 15 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 7.7, cp = 3.9, dT = 15 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 7.7*3.9*15 | Answer: 450.5 kW

question: A reactor of volume 15.9 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 3.8 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 15.9, Q = 3.8 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 15.9 / 3.8 | Answer: 4.184 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 7.6e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 3 mm with a concentration difference of 120 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 7.6, L = 3, dC = 120 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (7.6e-9)*120 / (3e-3) | Answer: 304 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 7.4 min and steady-state gain 1.1. For a step input of magnitude 13, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 7.4, K = 1.1, M = 13 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 1.1 * 13 | Answer: 14.3 units

question: A reactor operates at a space time of 3.4 min. Find its space velocity in per hour.
solution: Given: tau = 3.4 | Formula: SV = 60 / tau  (per hour) | Substitute: SV = 60 / 3.4 | Answer: 17.65 /h

question: An aircraft wing of area 95 m^2 flies at 120 m/s (air density 1 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 1.2. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 95, V = 120, rho = 1, CL = 1.2 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1*(120)^2*95*1.2 / 1000 | Answer: 820.8 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 90 m^2 flies at 80 m/s (density 1 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.04. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 90, V = 80, rho = 1, CD = 0.04 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*1*(80)^2*90*0.04 / 1000 | Answer: 11.52 kN

question: An aircraft flies at 240 m/s where the speed of sound is 295 m/s. Find the Mach number.
solution: Given: V = 240, a = 295 | Formula: M = V / a | Substitute: M = 240 / 295 | Answer: 0.8136

question: A specimen under stress 190 MPa shows an elastic strain of 1e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 190, eps = 1 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 190 / (1e-3) MPa = 190 GPa | Answer: 190 GPa

question: A block of mass 48 kg has a volume of 1.1e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 48, V = 1.1 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 48 / (1.1e-3) | Answer: 43636 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 1500 mm is heated through 105 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 11e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 1500, dT = 105, al = 11 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 1500*11e-6*105 | Answer: 1.733 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 85 ohm, R2 = 60 ohm and R3 = 30 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 85, R2 = 60, R3 = 30 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 60*30 / 85 | Answer: 21.18 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 120 ohm and gauge factor 2.2 experiences a strain of 400e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 120, GF = 2.2, eps = 400 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 120*2.2*400e-6 | Answer: 105.6 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 9.43 when the true value is 50. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.43, true = 50 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.43 - 50| / 50 * 100 | Answer: 81.14 %

question: Annual demand is 37000 units, ordering cost 180 per order and holding cost 2 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 37000, S = 180, H = 2 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*37000*180 / 2) | Answer: 2581 units

question: An asset costs 150000 with salvage value 22000 after 19 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 150000, Sv = 22000, n = 19 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (150000 - 22000) / 19 | Answer: 6737 per year

question: A product sells for 370 per unit with variable cost 60 per unit and fixed costs 70000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 370, V = 60, F = 70000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 70000 / (370 - 60) | Answer: 225.8 units

question: Find the present worth of 165000 received 8 years from now at an interest rate of 10% per year.
solution: Given: F = 165000, n = 8, i = 10 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 165000 / (1 + 0.1)^8 | Answer: 76974 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.91, 0.96 and 0.93 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.91, r2 = 0.96, r3 = 0.93 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.91*0.96*0.93 | Answer: 0.8124

question: A process produces 15 defective items in a batch of 13500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 15, N = 13500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 15/13500 * 1e6 | Answer: 1111 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = 5x^3 + 7x^2 - 9x + 7 evaluated at x = -1.
For f(x) = -4x^3 - 8x^2 + 8x, find f''(x) at x = 1.
Evaluate the definite integral of (-3x^2 + 2x - 8) dx from x = 2 to x = 6.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = -3x^3/3 + 2x^2/2 + -8x | Evaluate F(6) - F(2) | Answer: -208
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 2x^2 - 10x - 7 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[4, 2], [-8, -2]].
solution: Given: a = 4, b = 2, c = -8, d = -2 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (4)(-2) - (2)(-8) | Answer: 8

question: Find the determinant of [[2, 5, -4], [-5, 2, -1], [0, -1, 6]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: 152

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[3, -5], [-1, 8]].
solution: Trace tr = 11, Determinant = 19 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 8.854

question: Solve for x: 0x + -5y = 0 and -1x + 6y = -10.
solution: Determinant = 0*6 - -5*-1 = -5 | x = (e d - b f) / det = 10 | Answer: x = 10
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 45, 38, 63, 27, 18.
solution: Sum = 191 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 38.2 | Answer: 38.2

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 29, 36, 9, 48, 34.
solution: Mean = 31.2 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 14.24

question: Find the slope of the line through (-7, -8) and (-6, -2).
solution: Given: x1 = -7, y1 = -8, x2 = -6, y2 = -2 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (-2 - -8) / (-6 - -7) | Answer: 6

question: Find the distance between the points (4, 7) and (2, 4).
solution: Given: x1 = 4, y1 = 7, x2 = 2, y2 = 4 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-2)^2 + (-3)^2) | Answer: 3.606 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (-7,-8), (3,2), (3,7).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 25 sq units

question: Find the 6th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -11 and common difference -7.
solution: Given: a = -11, d = -7, n = 6 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -11 + (6 - 1)*-7 | Answer: -46

question: Find the sum of the first 29 terms of an AP with first term 12 and common difference 5.
solution: Given: a = 12, d = 5, n = 29 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 29/2 [2*12 + (29-1)*5] | Answer: 2378

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 37000 at 5.5% per annum for 8 years.
solution: Given: P = 37000, R = 5.5, Tt = 8 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 37000 * 5.5 * 8 / 100 | Answer: 16280 currency units

question: Find the amount when 27000 is invested at 7.7% per annum compounded annually for 3 years.
solution: Given: P = 27000, R = 7.7, Tt = 3 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 27000 * (1 + 7.7/100)^3 | Answer: 3373 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (4, 3, -1) and (2, -5, -1).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (2, 0, 2) and (-4, 0, 0).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 8

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (-4, 4, 2) and (3, 5, 4).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 67.84 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number 2 + 1i.
solution: Given: a = 2, b = 1 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((2)^2 + (1)^2) | Answer: 2.236

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number 6 + 1i.
solution: Given: a = 6, b = 1 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(1, 6) | Answer: 9.462 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -4x^3 - 7x^2 + 9x - 1 at x = 1.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-34 with initial guess x0=10, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=0.7 and ordinates 2, 18, 17, 12, 13, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 29 and 64.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 29 and 64 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 49 and 70.
solution: Given: a = 49, b = 70 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 49*70 / 7 | Answer: 490
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 46 mm carries an axial tensile load of 96 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 39 mm and length 1100 mm carries an axial load of 13 kN. Take E = 210 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 71 mm transmits a torque of 2000 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 71, Tt = 2000 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(2000*1000) / (pi*(71)^3) | Answer: 28.46 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 32 mm and length 500 mm carries a torque of 1300 N-m. With G = 77 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (32)^4 / 32 = 102944 mm^4 | theta = (1300*1000)(500) / (77000 * 102944) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 4.698 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 150 mm wide and 230 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 150, h = 230 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 150*(230)^2 / 6 | Answer: 1322500 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (103 mm x 240 mm) carries a bending moment of 33 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (31 mm x 90 mm) has effective length 3900 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 650 MPa is designed for a working stress of 190 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 650, sw = 190 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 650 / 190 | Answer: 3.421

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 800 mm and wall thickness 10 mm carries an internal pressure of 0.8 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 800, t = 10, P = 0.8 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 0.8*800 / (2*10) | Answer: 32 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 880 K and 410 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 880, Tc = 410 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 410/880) * 100 | Answer: 53.41 %

question: A refrigerator works between 253 K (cold) and 326 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 253, Th = 326 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 253 / (326 - 253) | Answer: 3.466

question: A heat pump operates between 268 K and 324 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 268, Th = 324 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 324 / (324 - 268) | Answer: 5.786

question: 6.7 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 60 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 6.7, dT = 60 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 6.7 * 0.718 * 60 | Answer: 288.6 kJ

question: 3.3 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 130 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.3, dT = 130 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 3.3 * 1.005 * 130 | Answer: 431.1 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 1.4 m^3 at 540 K with mass 4.2 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 1.4, Tk = 540, m = 4.2 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 4.2*0.287*540 / 1.4 | Answer: 464.9 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 4.7 kg of air expands isothermally at 500 K from volume V1 to 5*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.7, Tk = 500, ratio = 5 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 4.7*0.287*500*ln(5) | Answer: 1085 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 2.5 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.07 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 2.5, D = 0.07 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*2.5*0.07 / 0.001 | Answer: 175000

question: Water flows at 3.6 m/s through a pipe of diameter 270 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 19.1 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 19.1 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*19.1 / 1000 | Answer: 187.4 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 15.3 m. Taking Cv = 0.99, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 15.3, cv = 0.99 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.99*sqrt(2*9.81*15.3) | Answer: 17.15 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 160 mm) water flows at 1.3 m/s. It contracts to diameter 90 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 160, d2 = 90, V1 = 1.3 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 1.3*(160/90)^2 | Answer: 4.109 m/s

question: Water flows at 3.5 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.49 m and length 150 m. With friction factor f = 0.038, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 38 teeth drives a gear of 83 teeth. If the pinion runs at 600 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 38, z2 = 83, N1 = 600 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 600*38 / 83 | Answer: 274.7 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 220 mm rotates at 300 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 220, N = 300 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.22)*300 / 60 | Answer: 3.456 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 25.8 kW at 250 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 25.8, N = 250 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(25.8*1000) / (2*pi*250) | Answer: 985.5 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 9.1 kg rotates at radius 0.41 m at 650 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 15500 N/m and mass 17.7 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 15500, m = 17.7 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(15500/17.7) | Answer: 4.71 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 6.2 m^2 and thickness 0.3 m has conductivity k = 25.2 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 55 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 6.2, L = 0.3, k = 25.2, dT = 55 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 25.2*6.2*55 / 0.3 | Answer: 28644 W

question: A surface of area 1.4 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 200 W/m^2-K to surroundings 150 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 1.4, h = 200, dT = 150 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 200*1.4*150 | Answer: 42000 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 80 m/min, feed = 0.33 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 80, f = 0.33, d = 2 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*80*0.33*2 | Answer: 52800 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 140 mm is turned at 300 rpm with a feed of 0.16 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 140, N = 300, f = 0.16 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 140 / (0.16*300) | Answer: 2.917 min

question: A resistor of 98 ohm carries a current of 3.8 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 98, I = 3.8 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 3.8 * 98 | Answer: 372.4 V

question: Three resistors 21 ohm, 45 ohm and 4 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 21, R2 = 45, R3 = 4 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 21 + 45 + 4 | Answer: 70 ohm

question: Two resistors 41 ohm and 18 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 41, R2 = 18 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 41*18 / (41+18) | Answer: 12.51 ohm

question: A device draws 5.9 A at 45 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 45, I = 5.9 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 45 * 5.9 | Answer: 265.5 W

question: A current of 8.4 A flows through a 126 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 8.4, R = 126 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (8.4)^2 * 126 | Answer: 8891 W

question: Two capacitors 8.3 uF and 2.2 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 8.3, C2 = 2.2 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 8.3*2.2 / (8.3+2.2) | Answer: 1.739 uF

question: A resistor 34 kohm and capacitor 6.2 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 34, C = 6.2 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (34k)(6.2u) = 210.8 ms | Answer: 210.8 ms

question: An inductor 446.7 mH is in series with 6 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 446.7, R = 6 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (446.7e-3) / 6 | Answer: 74.45 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 143.2 mH inductor at 720 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 143.2, f = 720 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (720)(143.2e-3) | Answer: 647.8 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 5.7 uF capacitor at 360 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 5.7, f = 360 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (360)(5.7e-6)) | Answer: 77.56 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 6 ohm, XL = 44 ohm and XC = 108 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 6, XL = 44, XC = 108 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(6^2 + (44 - 108)^2) | Answer: 64.28 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 78.8 mH and C = 6.4 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 78.8, C = 6.4 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(78.8e-3 * 6.4e-6)) | Answer: 224.1 Hz

question: A capacitor of 82 uF is charged to 225 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 82, V = 225 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*82e-6*(225)^2 | Answer: 2076 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 370 V with 980 primary turns and 300 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 370, N1 = 980, N2 = 300 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 370 * 300/980 | Answer: 113.3 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 410 V and draws an armature current of 18 A. If the armature resistance is 0.63 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 410, Ia = 18, Ra = 0.63 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 410 - 18*0.63 | Answer: 398.7 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 120 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.79. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 120, VL = 400, pf = 0.79 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*400*120*0.79 / 1000 | Answer: 65.68 kW

question: A load has real power 135 kW and apparent power 155 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 135, S = 155 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 135 / 155 | Answer: 0.871

question: A machine delivers 10 kW output while drawing 172 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 10, Pi = 172 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 10/172 * 100 | Answer: 5.814 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 22 V across R1 = 17 ohm and R2 = 33 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 22, R1 = 17, R2 = 33 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 22*33 / (17+33) | Answer: 14.52 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 30 kohm and Rin = 6 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 30, Rin = 6 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 30 / 6 | Answer: 5

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 60 kohm and Rg = 36 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 60, Rg = 36 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 60/36 | Answer: 2.667

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 1143. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 1143 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(1143) | Answer: 30.58 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 7.4 m carries a central point load of 65 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7.4, W = 65 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 65*7.4 / 4 | Answer: 120.2 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 5.8 m carries a UDL of 5 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.8, w = 5 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 5*(5.8)^2 / 8 | Answer: 21.02 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 4.7 m carries a point load 70 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.7, W = 70 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 70*4.7 | Answer: 329 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 5.3 m carries a UDL of 40 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.3, w = 40 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 40*(5.3)^2 / 2 | Answer: 561.8 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.1 m carries a point load 60 kN at distance 3.2 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 4.1, a = 3.2, W = 60 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 60*(4.1 - 3.2) / 4.1 | Answer: 13.17 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 3.4 m) carries a central point load 10 kN. With E = 200 GPa and I = 130e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=10000 N, L=3400.0 mm, E=200000 MPa, I=130e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 0.3149 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 4.7 m carries a UDL of 6 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.7, w = 6 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 6*(4.7)^2 / 12 | Answer: 11.05 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 690 mm, clear cover 35 mm and main bars of diameter 12 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 690, c = 35, dia = 12 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 690 - 35 - 12/2 | Answer: 649 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 31.1 m^2 carrying a factored load of 15.8 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 31.1, w = 15.8 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 15.8 * 31.1 | Answer: 491.4 kN

question: For a bar of diameter 20 mm with design bond stress 1.2 MPa and steel stress 435 MPa, find the development length in mm.
solution: Given: dia = 20, tbd = 1.2, fs = 435 | Formula: Ld = phi fs / (4 tau_bd) | Substitute: Ld = 20*435 / (4*1.2) | Answer: 1812 mm

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 4.6 m, unit weight 19 kN/m^3, phi = 30 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 3.6 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 20 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 3.6, g = 20 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (20 - 9.81)*3.6 | Answer: 36.68 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 2.3e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.5, area = 6.6e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 2.3, i = 0.5, A = 6.6 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (2.3e-4)*0.5*(6.6e-3) | Answer: 759 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.7 m, bed slope 0.007 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.022. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 2.5 m under a head of 0.6 m. Taking Cd = 0.61 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 5.4 m wide carries a discharge of 21 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).

solution: Given: R = 320, V = 95 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (95)^2 / (127*320) | Answer: 0.2221
