solution: Given: R1 = 106, R2 = 18 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 106*18 / (106+18) | Answer: 15.39 ohm

question: A device draws 11.2 A at 205 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 205, I = 11.2 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 205 * 11.2 | Answer: 2296 W

question: A current of 3.8 A flows through a 27 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 3.8, R = 27 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (3.8)^2 * 27 | Answer: 389.9 W

question: Two capacitors 44.7 uF and 35.8 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 44.7, C2 = 35.8 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 44.7*35.8 / (44.7+35.8) | Answer: 19.88 uF

question: A resistor 64 kohm and capacitor 13.3 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 64, C = 13.3 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (64k)(13.3u) = 851.2 ms | Answer: 851.2 ms

question: An inductor 479.9 mH is in series with 142 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 479.9, R = 142 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (479.9e-3) / 142 | Answer: 3.38 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 104.9 mH inductor at 270 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 104.9, f = 270 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (270)(104.9e-3) | Answer: 178 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 14.7 uF capacitor at 530 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 14.7, f = 530 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (530)(14.7e-6)) | Answer: 20.43 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 35 ohm, XL = 130 ohm and XC = 136 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 35, XL = 130, XC = 136 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(35^2 + (130 - 136)^2) | Answer: 35.51 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 96.9 mH and C = 3.7 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 96.9, C = 3.7 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(96.9e-3 * 3.7e-6)) | Answer: 265.8 Hz

question: A capacitor of 3.9 uF is charged to 320 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 3.9, V = 320 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*3.9e-6*(320)^2 | Answer: 199.7 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 120 V with 330 primary turns and 330 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 120, N1 = 330, N2 = 330 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 120 * 330/330 | Answer: 120 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 180 V and draws an armature current of 34 A. If the armature resistance is 1.25 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 180, Ia = 34, Ra = 1.25 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 180 - 34*1.25 | Answer: 137.5 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 55 A at 433 V (line) with a power factor of 0.71. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 55, VL = 433, pf = 0.71 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*433*55*0.71 / 1000 | Answer: 29.29 kW

question: A load has real power 20 kW and apparent power 210 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 20, S = 210 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 20 / 210 | Answer: 0.09524

question: A machine delivers 50 kW output while drawing 62 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 50, Pi = 62 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 50/62 * 100 | Answer: 80.65 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 18 V across R1 = 24 ohm and R2 = 22 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 18, R1 = 24, R2 = 22 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 18*22 / (24+22) | Answer: 8.609 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 170 kohm and Rin = 44 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 170, Rin = 44 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 170 / 44 | Answer: 3.864

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 100 kohm and Rg = 28 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 100, Rg = 28 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 100/28 | Answer: 4.571

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 5522. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 5522 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(5522) | Answer: 37.42 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 7.6 m carries a central point load of 85 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7.6, W = 85 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 85*7.6 / 4 | Answer: 161.5 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 5.2 m carries a UDL of 10 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.2, w = 10 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 10*(5.2)^2 / 8 | Answer: 33.8 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 2.3 m carries a point load 50 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 2.3, W = 50 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 50*2.3 | Answer: 115 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 1.5 m carries a UDL of 24 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 1.5, w = 24 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 24*(1.5)^2 / 2 | Answer: 27 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 5.9 m carries a point load 100 kN at distance 2.1 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 5.9, a = 2.1, W = 100 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 100*(5.9 - 2.1) / 5.9 | Answer: 64.41 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 7.4 m) carries a central point load 65 kN. With E = 200 GPa and I = 360e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=65000 N, L=7400.0 mm, E=200000 MPa, I=360e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 7.621 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 5.7 m carries a UDL of 45 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.7, w = 45 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 45*(5.7)^2 / 12 | Answer: 121.8 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 560 mm, clear cover 35 mm and main bars of diameter 25 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 560, c = 35, dia = 25 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 560 - 35 - 25/2 | Answer: 512.5 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 20.4 m^2 carrying a factored load of 19.6 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 20.4, w = 19.6 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 19.6 * 20.4 | Answer: 399.8 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 3.3 m, unit weight 17 kN/m^3, phi = 34 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 4.4 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 18 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 4.4, g = 18 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (18 - 9.81)*4.4 | Answer: 36.04 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 1.7e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.2, area = 5.4e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 1.7, i = 0.2, A = 5.4 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (1.7e-4)*0.2*(5.4e-3) | Answer: 183.6 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 0.8 m, bed slope 0.004 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.024. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 2.9 m under a head of 1 m. Taking Cd = 0.62 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 2.7 m wide carries a discharge of 10.7 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 230 m and design speed 85 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 230, V = 85 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (85)^2 / (127*230) | Answer: 0.2473
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: A tank of volume 530 m^3 treats a flow of 125 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 530, Q = 125 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 530 / 125 | Answer: 4.24 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 200 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.31 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 7 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 200, k = 0.31, t = 7 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 200*(1 - e^(-0.31*7)) | Answer: 177.2 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.86, rainfall intensity 55 mm/h over a catchment of 45.5 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.86, i = 55, A = 45.5 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.86*55*45.5 / 360 | Answer: 5.978 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.05 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 170 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.05, M = 170 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 170*(30+0.05)/30 | Answer: 170.3 m

question: Convert the decimal number 184 to binary.
solution: Divide 184 by 2 repeatedly, recording remainders | Reading remainders in reverse gives 10111000 | Answer: 10111000 (binary)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 2 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the decimal number 66 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 66 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 42 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 11110001 and 10110100.
solution: XOR: 01000101 | Count of 1s = 3 | Answer: 3
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 260 megabits is sent over a link of 8 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 260, B = 8 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 260 / 8 | Answer: 32.5 s

question: A link has bandwidth 75 Mbps and round-trip time 180 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 75, R = 180 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 75e6 * 180e-3 bits = 13500 kb | Answer: 13500 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.87, cache access time 7 ns and main-memory access time 90 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.87, tc = 7, tm = 90 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.87*7 + (1 - 0.87)*90 | Answer: 17.79 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 239284 elements?
solution: Given: n = 239284 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(239284)) + 1 | Answer: 18

question: An O(n^2) algorithm performs c*n^2 basic operations. If c = 1 and n = 700, how many operations are performed?
solution: Given: n = 700 | Formula: operations = n^2 | Substitute: = (700)^2 | Answer: 490000

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.004, memory access time 140 ns and page-fault service time 3 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 3 ms = 3000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.004)*140 + 0.004*3000000.0 ns | Answer: 12.14 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 1.7 m^3 at 200 kPa and 460 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 1.7, P = 200, Tk = 460 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (200e3)*1.7 / (8.314*460) | Answer: 88.9 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.1 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 10 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.1, t = 10 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.1*10) | Answer: 0.6321

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.36 /min) is to reach 50% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.36, X = 50 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.5) / 0.36 | Answer: 1.925 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.24 /min) reaches 55% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.24, X = 55 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.55 / (0.24*(1 - 0.55)) | Answer: 5.093 min

question: For a reaction with A = 8e10 /s and activation energy 65 kJ/mol at 380 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 8, Ea = 65, Tk = 380 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 8e10 * exp(-65e3 / (8.314*380)) | Answer: 92.87 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.99 and bottoms xW = 0.05, with relative volatility alpha = 1.6. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.99, xw = 0.05, al = 1.6 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.99/0.01)(0.95/0.05)] / ln(1.6) | Answer: 16.04 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.63 and x = 0.26. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.63, x = 0.26 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.63/0.37) / (0.26/0.74) | Answer: 4.846

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.31 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 80 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.31, Psat = 80 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.31 * 80 | Answer: 24.8 kPa

question: A stream of 2.2 kg/s with specific heat 3.5 kJ/kg-K is heated through 50 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 2.2, cp = 3.5, dT = 50 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 2.2*3.5*50 | Answer: 385 kW

question: A reactor of volume 13.9 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 1.6 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 13.9, Q = 1.6 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 13.9 / 1.6 | Answer: 8.688 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 4.8e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 1 mm with a concentration difference of 120 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 4.8, L = 1, dC = 120 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (4.8e-9)*120 / (1e-3) | Answer: 576 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 6.3 min and steady-state gain 3.3. For a step input of magnitude 5, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 6.3, K = 3.3, M = 5 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 3.3 * 5 | Answer: 16.5 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 40 m^2 flies at 80 m/s (air density 1.225 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.8. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 40, V = 80, rho = 1.225, CL = 0.8 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1.225*(80)^2*40*0.8 / 1000 | Answer: 125.4 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 45 m^2 flies at 200 m/s (density 0.7 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.11. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 45, V = 200, rho = 0.7, CD = 0.11 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.7*(200)^2*45*0.11 / 1000 | Answer: 69.3 kN

question: A specimen under stress 80 MPa shows an elastic strain of 0.8e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 80, eps = 0.8 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 80 / (0.8e-3) MPa = 100 GPa | Answer: 100 GPa

question: A block of mass 50 kg has a volume of 2.7e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 50, V = 2.7 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 50 / (2.7e-3) | Answer: 18519 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 1700 mm is heated through 140 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 11e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 1700, dT = 140, al = 11 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 1700*11e-6*140 | Answer: 2.618 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 60 ohm, R2 = 55 ohm and R3 = 230 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 60, R2 = 55, R3 = 230 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 55*230 / 60 | Answer: 210.8 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 1000 ohm and gauge factor 2.2 experiences a strain of 1300e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 1000, GF = 2.2, eps = 1300 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 1000*2.2*1300e-6 | Answer: 2860 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 10.41 when the true value is 100. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10.41, true = 100 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10.41 - 100| / 100 * 100 | Answer: 89.59 %

question: Annual demand is 10000 units, ordering cost 200 per order and holding cost 3 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 10000, S = 200, H = 3 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*10000*200 / 3) | Answer: 1155 units

question: An asset costs 290000 with salvage value 8000 after 14 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 290000, Sv = 8000, n = 14 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (290000 - 8000) / 14 | Answer: 20143 per year

question: A product sells for 430 per unit with variable cost 170 per unit and fixed costs 130000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 430, V = 170, F = 130000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 130000 / (430 - 170) | Answer: 500 units

question: Find the present worth of 120000 received 7 years from now at an interest rate of 11% per year.
solution: Given: F = 120000, n = 7, i = 11 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 120000 / (1 + 0.11)^7 | Answer: 57799 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.91, 0.96 and 0.96 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.91, r2 = 0.96, r3 = 0.96 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.91*0.96*0.96 | Answer: 0.8387

question: A process produces 48 defective items in a batch of 9500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 48, N = 9500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 48/9500 * 1e6 | Answer: 5053 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -5x^3 - x^2 + 9x - 5 evaluated at x = 4.
For f(x) = -6x^3 + 3x^2 + x, find f''(x) at x = 0.
Evaluate the definite integral of (-2x^2 + x - 1) dx from x = -2 to x = 7.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = -2x^3/3 + 1x^2/2 + -1x | Evaluate F(7) - F(-2) | Answer: -220.5
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 3x^2 - 9x + 1 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[9, -3], [-1, 0]].
solution: Given: a = 9, b = -3, c = -1, d = 0 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (9)(0) - (-3)(-1) | Answer: -3

question: Find the determinant of [[6, -2, -3], [-4, 5, 3], [1, -3, 0]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: 27

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[5, 0], [6, 1]].
solution: Trace tr = 6, Determinant = 5 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 5

question: Solve for x: 2x + 3y = 8 and 5x + 1y = -2.
solution: Determinant = 2*1 - 3*5 = -13 | x = (e d - b f) / det = -1.077 | Answer: x = -1.077
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 47, 73, 41, 62, 99.
solution: Sum = 322 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 64.4 | Answer: 64.4

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 18, 28, 50, 16, 21.
solution: Mean = 26.6 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 13.85

question: Find the slope of the line through (-2, -1) and (-1, -5).
solution: Given: x1 = -2, y1 = -1, x2 = -1, y2 = -5 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (-5 - -1) / (-1 - -2) | Answer: -4

question: Find the distance between the points (0, 4) and (-4, -2).
solution: Given: x1 = 0, y1 = 4, x2 = -4, y2 = -2 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-4)^2 + (-6)^2) | Answer: 7.211 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (-5,5), (-6,4), (-5,4).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 0.5 sq units

question: Find the 14th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -4 and common difference -1.
solution: Given: a = -4, d = -1, n = 14 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -4 + (14 - 1)*-1 | Answer: -17

question: Find the sum of the first 13 terms of an AP with first term -5 and common difference -2.
solution: Given: a = -5, d = -2, n = 13 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 13/2 [2*-5 + (13-1)*-2] | Answer: -221

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 50000 at 8.9% per annum for 5 years.
solution: Given: P = 50000, R = 8.9, Tt = 5 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 50000 * 8.9 * 5 / 100 | Answer: 22250 currency units

question: Find the amount when 9500 is invested at 10% per annum compounded annually for 2 years.
solution: Given: P = 9500, R = 10, Tt = 2 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 9500 * (1 + 10/100)^2 | Answer: 11495 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (4, 2, 4) and (-1, -6, -3).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (0, -4, 1) and (1, 2, -1).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 4.583

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (2, 5, 2) and (1, -5, -3).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 148.6 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number -1 + 2i.
solution: Given: a = -1, b = 2 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((-1)^2 + (2)^2) | Answer: 2.236

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number 7 + 2i.
solution: Given: a = 7, b = 2 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(2, 7) | Answer: 15.95 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = x^3 - 5x^2 - 5x + 7 at x = -3.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-140 with initial guess x0=13, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=0.8 and ordinates 14, 20, 1, 10, 0, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 30 and 230.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 30 and 230 | Answer: GCD = 10

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 60 and 40.
solution: Given: a = 60, b = 40 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 60*40 / 20 | Answer: 120
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 36 mm carries an axial tensile load of 51 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 38 mm and length 600 mm carries an axial load of 18 kN. Take E = 200 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 25 mm transmits a torque of 1000 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 25, Tt = 1000 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(1000*1000) / (pi*(25)^3) | Answer: 325.9 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 37 mm and length 1100 mm carries a torque of 1600 N-m. With G = 45 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (37)^4 / 32 = 183995 mm^4 | theta = (1600*1000)(1100) / (45000 * 183995) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 12.18 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 56 mm wide and 190 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 56, h = 190 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 56*(190)^2 / 6 | Answer: 336933 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (118 mm x 80 mm) carries a bending moment of 35 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (75 mm x 100 mm) has effective length 2500 mm and E = 200 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 500 MPa is designed for a working stress of 170 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 500, sw = 170 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 500 / 170 | Answer: 2.941

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1150 mm and wall thickness 17 mm carries an internal pressure of 2.9 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1150, t = 17, P = 2.9 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 2.9*1150 / (2*17) | Answer: 98.09 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 860 K and 450 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 860, Tc = 450 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 450/860) * 100 | Answer: 47.67 %

question: A refrigerator works between 268 K (cold) and 328 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 268, Th = 328 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 268 / (328 - 268) | Answer: 4.467

question: A heat pump operates between 285 K and 304 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 285, Th = 304 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 304 / (304 - 285) | Answer: 16

question: 6.5 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 80 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 6.5, dT = 80 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 6.5 * 0.718 * 80 | Answer: 373.4 kJ

question: 2.4 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 150 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.4, dT = 150 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 2.4 * 1.005 * 150 | Answer: 361.8 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 4 m^3 at 480 K with mass 5.9 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 4, Tk = 480, m = 5.9 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 5.9*0.287*480 / 4 | Answer: 203.2 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 1.5 kg of air expands isothermally at 450 K from volume V1 to 4*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1.5, Tk = 450, ratio = 4 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 1.5*0.287*450*ln(4) | Answer: 268.6 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 4.8 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.12 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 4.8, D = 0.12 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*4.8*0.12 / 0.001 | Answer: 576000

question: Water flows at 1.9 m/s through a pipe of diameter 80 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 6 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 6 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*6 / 1000 | Answer: 58.86 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 3.1 m. Taking Cv = 0.96, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 3.1, cv = 0.96 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.96*sqrt(2*9.81*3.1) | Answer: 7.487 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 170 mm) water flows at 2.7 m/s. It contracts to diameter 120 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
Water flows at 2.8 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.38 m and length 380 m. With friction factor f = 0.024, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 22 teeth drives a gear of 70 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1500 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 22, z2 = 70, N1 = 1500 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1500*22 / 70 | Answer: 471.4 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 160 mm rotates at 900 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 160, N = 900 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.16)*900 / 60 | Answer: 7.54 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 48.1 kW at 300 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 48.1, N = 300 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(48.1*1000) / (2*pi*300) | Answer: 1531 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 7.3 kg rotates at radius 0.45 m at 600 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 18000 N/m and mass 8.6 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 18000, m = 8.6 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(18000/8.6) | Answer: 7.281 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 1.1 m^2 and thickness 0.34 m has conductivity k = 41.7 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 40 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 1.1, L = 0.34, k = 41.7, dT = 40 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 41.7*1.1*40 / 0.34 | Answer: 5396 W

question: A surface of area 1.2 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 165 W/m^2-K to surroundings 45 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 1.2, h = 165, dT = 45 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 165*1.2*45 | Answer: 8910 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 130 m/min, feed = 0.3 mm/rev, depth of cut = 1.5 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 130, f = 0.3, d = 1.5 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*130*0.3*1.5 | Answer: 58500 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 150 mm is turned at 300 rpm with a feed of 0.21 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 150, N = 300, f = 0.21 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 150 / (0.21*300) | Answer: 2.381 min

question: A resistor of 177 ohm carries a current of 5.9 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 177, I = 5.9 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 5.9 * 177 | Answer: 1044 V

question: Three resistors 60 ohm, 9 ohm and 93 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 60, R2 = 9, R3 = 93 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 60 + 9 + 93 | Answer: 162 ohm

question: Two resistors 111 ohm and 107 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 111, R2 = 107 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 111*107 / (111+107) | Answer: 54.48 ohm

question: A device draws 1.4 A at 115 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 115, I = 1.4 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 115 * 1.4 | Answer: 161 W

question: A current of 7 A flows through a 65 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 7, R = 65 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (7)^2 * 65 | Answer: 3185 W

question: Two capacitors 10.4 uF and 29 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 10.4, C2 = 29 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 10.4*29 / (10.4+29) | Answer: 7.655 uF

question: A resistor 29 kohm and capacitor 12.9 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 29, C = 12.9 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (29k)(12.9u) = 374.1 ms | Answer: 374.1 ms

question: An inductor 312.9 mH is in series with 40 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 312.9, R = 40 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (312.9e-3) / 40 | Answer: 7.822 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 87 mH inductor at 540 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 87, f = 540 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (540)(87e-3) | Answer: 295.2 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 37.1 uF capacitor at 740 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 37.1, f = 740 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (740)(37.1e-6)) | Answer: 5.797 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 53 ohm, XL = 42 ohm and XC = 85 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 53, XL = 42, XC = 85 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(53^2 + (42 - 85)^2) | Answer: 68.25 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 87.1 mH and C = 0.4 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 87.1, C = 0.4 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(87.1e-3 * 0.4e-6)) | Answer: 852.7 Hz

question: A capacitor of 59.5 uF is charged to 35 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 59.5, V = 35 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*59.5e-6*(35)^2 | Answer: 36.44 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 190 V with 660 primary turns and 210 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 190, N1 = 660, N2 = 210 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 190 * 210/660 | Answer: 60.45 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 370 V and draws an armature current of 48 A. If the armature resistance is 0.29 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 370, Ia = 48, Ra = 0.29 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 370 - 48*0.29 | Answer: 356.1 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 170 A at 433 V (line) with a power factor of 0.73. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 170, VL = 433, pf = 0.73 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*433*170*0.73 / 1000 | Answer: 93.07 kW

question: A load has real power 175 kW and apparent power 190 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 175, S = 190 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 175 / 190 | Answer: 0.9211

question: A machine delivers 65 kW output while drawing 147 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 65, Pi = 147 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 65/147 * 100 | Answer: 44.22 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 19 V across R1 = 4 ohm and R2 = 34 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 19, R1 = 4, R2 = 34 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 19*34 / (4+34) | Answer: 17 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 110 kohm and Rin = 8 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 110, Rin = 8 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 110 / 8 | Answer: 13.75

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 120 kohm and Rg = 15 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 120, Rg = 15 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 120/15 | Answer: 9

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 6309. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 6309 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(6309) | Answer: 38 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.9 m carries a central point load of 90 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 9.9, W = 90 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 90*9.9 / 4 | Answer: 222.8 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 3.2 m carries a UDL of 10 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.2, w = 10 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 10*(3.2)^2 / 8 | Answer: 12.8 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 3.9 m carries a point load 5 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.9, W = 5 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 5*3.9 | Answer: 19.5 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 4.6 m carries a UDL of 30 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.6, w = 30 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 30*(4.6)^2 / 2 | Answer: 317.4 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.9 m carries a point load 55 kN at distance 3.9 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 9.9, a = 3.9, W = 55 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 55*(9.9 - 3.9) / 9.9 | Answer: 33.33 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 7.9 m) carries a central point load 50 kN. With E = 25 GPa and I = 70e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=50000 N, L=7900.0 mm, E=25000 MPa, I=70e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 293.5 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 8.9 m carries a UDL of 6 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 8.9, w = 6 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 6*(8.9)^2 / 12 | Answer: 39.61 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 580 mm, clear cover 40 mm and main bars of diameter 16 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 580, c = 40, dia = 16 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 580 - 40 - 16/2 | Answer: 532 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 15.9 m^2 carrying a factored load of 18.2 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 15.9, w = 18.2 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 18.2 * 15.9 | Answer: 289.4 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 4.8 m, unit weight 19 kN/m^3, phi = 38 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 8.1 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 19 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 8.1, g = 19 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (19 - 9.81)*8.1 | Answer: 74.44 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 4.3e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1.1, area = 5.7e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 4.3, i = 1.1, A = 5.7 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (4.3e-4)*1.1*(5.7e-3) | Answer: 2696 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 0.6 m, bed slope 0.003 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.017. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 3.2 m under a head of 0.4 m. Taking Cd = 0.61 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 3.1 m wide carries a discharge of 14 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 560 m and design speed 50 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 560, V = 50 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (50)^2 / (127*560) | Answer: 0.03515
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: A tank of volume 730 m^3 treats a flow of 170 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 730, Q = 170 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 730 / 170 | Answer: 4.294 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 150 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.26 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 4 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 150, k = 0.26, t = 4 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 150*(1 - e^(-0.26*4)) | Answer: 96.98 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.88, rainfall intensity 105 mm/h over a catchment of 11.4 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.88, i = 105, A = 11.4 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.88*105*11.4 / 360 | Answer: 2.926 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.03 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 310 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.03, M = 310 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 310*(30+0.03)/30 | Answer: 310.3 m

question: Convert the decimal number 169 to binary.
solution: Divide 169 by 2 repeatedly, recording remainders | Reading remainders in reverse gives 10101001 | Answer: 10101001 (binary)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 2 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the decimal number 170 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 170 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: AA (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the 8-bit binary number 01100111 to decimal.
solution: Binary 01100111 = sum of bit-weights | Answer: 103 (decimal)
formula: Sum each bit times its positional weight (2^i)

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 10011000 and 11111101.
solution: XOR: 01100101 | Count of 1s = 4 | Answer: 4
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 90 megabits is sent over a link of 80 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 90, B = 80 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 90 / 80 | Answer: 1.125 s

question: A link has bandwidth 88 Mbps and round-trip time 70 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 88, R = 70 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 88e6 * 70e-3 bits = 6160 kb | Answer: 6160 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.87, cache access time 7 ns and main-memory access time 70 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.87, tc = 7, tm = 70 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.87*7 + (1 - 0.87)*70 | Answer: 15.19 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 443776 elements?
solution: Given: n = 443776 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(443776)) + 1 | Answer: 19

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.009, memory access time 80 ns and page-fault service time 6 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 6 ms = 6000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.009)*80 + 0.009*6000000.0 ns | Answer: 54.08 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 2.8 m^3 at 150 kPa and 410 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 2.8, P = 150, Tk = 410 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (150e3)*2.8 / (8.314*410) | Answer: 123.2 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.08 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 13 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.08, t = 13 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.08*13) | Answer: 0.6465

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.36 /min) is to reach 55% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.36, X = 55 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.55) / 0.36 | Answer: 2.218 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.35 /min) reaches 90% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.35, X = 90 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.9 / (0.35*(1 - 0.9)) | Answer: 25.71 min

question: For a reaction with A = 2e10 /s and activation energy 80 kJ/mol at 440 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 2, Ea = 80, Tk = 440 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 2e10 * exp(-80e3 / (8.314*440)) | Answer: 6.36 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.96 and bottoms xW = 0.06, with relative volatility alpha = 2.5. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.96, xw = 0.06, al = 2.5 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.96/0.04)(0.94/0.06)] / ln(2.5) | Answer: 6.471 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.74 and x = 0.37. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.74, x = 0.37 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.74/0.26) / (0.37/0.63) | Answer: 4.846

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.45 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 75 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.45, Psat = 75 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.45 * 75 | Answer: 33.75 kPa

question: A stream of 5.4 kg/s with specific heat 1.3 kJ/kg-K is heated through 105 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 5.4, cp = 1.3, dT = 105 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 5.4*1.3*105 | Answer: 737.1 kW

question: A reactor of volume 5.3 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 1.2 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 5.3, Q = 1.2 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 5.3 / 1.2 | Answer: 4.417 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 7.1e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 5 mm with a concentration difference of 120 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 7.1, L = 5, dC = 120 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (7.1e-9)*120 / (5e-3) | Answer: 170.4 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 8.3 min and steady-state gain 1.9. For a step input of magnitude 5, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 8.3, K = 1.9, M = 5 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 1.9 * 5 | Answer: 9.5 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 65 m^2 flies at 110 m/s (air density 1.225 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.6. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 65, V = 110, rho = 1.225, CL = 0.6 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1.225*(110)^2*65*0.6 / 1000 | Answer: 289 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 120 m^2 flies at 250 m/s (density 1.225 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.04. Find the drag force in kN.

question: A block of mass 46 kg has a volume of 0.5e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 46, V = 0.5 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 46 / (0.5e-3) | Answer: 92000 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 1300 mm is heated through 130 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 23e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 1300, dT = 130, al = 23 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 1300*23e-6*130 | Answer: 3.887 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 80 ohm, R2 = 35 ohm and R3 = 225 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 80, R2 = 35, R3 = 225 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 35*225 / 80 | Answer: 98.44 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 1000 ohm and gauge factor 2.2 experiences a strain of 1100e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 1000, GF = 2.2, eps = 1100 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 1000*2.2*1100e-6 | Answer: 2420 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 10.25 when the true value is 20. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10.25, true = 20 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10.25 - 20| / 20 * 100 | Answer: 48.75 %

question: Annual demand is 24000 units, ordering cost 80 per order and holding cost 12 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 24000, S = 80, H = 12 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*24000*80 / 12) | Answer: 565.7 units

question: An asset costs 430000 with salvage value 10000 after 12 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 430000, Sv = 10000, n = 12 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (430000 - 10000) / 12 | Answer: 35000 per year

question: A product sells for 130 per unit with variable cost 40 per unit and fixed costs 195000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 130, V = 40, F = 195000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 195000 / (130 - 40) | Answer: 2167 units

question: Find the present worth of 115000 received 10 years from now at an interest rate of 6% per year.
solution: Given: F = 115000, n = 10, i = 6 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 115000 / (1 + 0.06)^10 | Answer: 64215 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.98, 0.91 and 0.92 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.98, r2 = 0.91, r3 = 0.92 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.98*0.91*0.92 | Answer: 0.8205

question: A process produces 16 defective items in a batch of 3500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 16, N = 3500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 16/3500 * 1e6 | Answer: 4571 PPM

question: Find the slope of the line through (0, -9) and (6, 9).
solution: Given: x1 = 0, y1 = -9, x2 = 6, y2 = 9 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (9 - -9) / (6 - 0) | Answer: 3

question: Find the distance between the points (-7, 3) and (2, -1).
solution: Given: x1 = -7, y1 = 3, x2 = 2, y2 = -1 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((9)^2 + (-4)^2) | Answer: 9.849 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (2,6), (-6,-4), (6,0).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 44 sq units

question: Evaluate the number of combinations C(18, 15).
solution: Given: n = 18, r = 15 | Formula: C(n, r) = n! / (r! (n - r)!) | Substitute: C(18, 15) = 18! / (15! * 3!) | Answer: 816

question: Find the 23th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -8 and common difference -9.
solution: Given: a = -8, d = -9, n = 23 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -8 + (23 - 1)*-9 | Answer: -206

question: Find the sum of the first 21 terms of an AP with first term 14 and common difference -6.
solution: Given: a = 14, d = -6, n = 21 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 21/2 [2*14 + (21-1)*-6] | Answer: -966

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 17000 at 12.2% per annum for 2 years.
solution: Given: P = 17000, R = 12.2, Tt = 2 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 17000 * 12.2 * 2 / 100 | Answer: 4148 currency units

question: Find the amount when 38000 is invested at 9.3% per annum compounded annually for 6 years.
solution: Given: P = 38000, R = 9.3, Tt = 6 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 38000 * (1 + 9.3/100)^6 | Answer: 64789 currency units

question: Find the modulus of the complex number 4 + 1i.
solution: Given: a = 4, b = 1 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((4)^2 + (1)^2) | Answer: 4.123

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number 9 + -1i.
solution: Given: a = 9, b = -1 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(-1, 9) | Answer: -6.34 degrees

question: A circular rod of diameter 42 mm carries an axial tensile load of 78 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.

A solid shaft of diameter 45 mm transmits a torque of 1250 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.

question: A shaft of diameter 64 mm and length 600 mm carries a torque of 1050 N-m. With G = 80 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.

question: A rectangular beam section is 31 mm wide and 130 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.

question: A component of ultimate strength 880 MPa is designed for a working stress of 140 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 880, sw = 140 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 880 / 140 | Answer: 6.286

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 750 mm and wall thickness 7 mm carries an internal pressure of 1.6 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 750, t = 7, P = 1.6 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 1.6*750 / (2*7) | Answer: 85.71 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 880 K and 340 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 880, Tc = 340 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 340/880) * 100 | Answer: 61.36 %

question: A refrigerator works between 256 K (cold) and 324 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 256, Th = 324 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 256 / (324 - 256) | Answer: 3.765

question: A heat pump operates between 263 K and 308 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 263, Th = 308 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 308 / (308 - 263) | Answer: 6.844

question: 2.2 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 25 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.2, dT = 25 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 2.2 * 0.718 * 25 | Answer: 39.49 kJ

question: 6.4 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 40 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 6.4, dT = 40 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 6.4 * 1.005 * 40 | Answer: 257.3 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 3.1 m^3 at 380 K with mass 5.6 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 3.1, Tk = 380, m = 5.6 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 5.6*0.287*380 / 3.1 | Answer: 197 kPa

question: 3.8 kg of air expands isothermally at 500 K from volume V1 to 5*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 2.4 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.24 m. Find the Reynolds number.

question: Water flows at 3.1 m/s through a pipe of diameter 110 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 9.5 m. Taking Cv = 0.98, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 9.5, cv = 0.98 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.98*sqrt(2*9.81*9.5) | Answer: 13.38 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 300 mm) water flows at 2.6 m/s. It contracts to diameter 100 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 300, d2 = 100, V1 = 2.6 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 2.6*(300/100)^2 | Answer: 23.4 m/s

question: Water flows at 2.8 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.28 m and length 500 m. With friction factor f = 0.023, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 15 teeth drives a gear of 79 teeth. If the pinion runs at 650 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 15, z2 = 79, N1 = 650 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 650*15 / 79 | Answer: 123.4 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 390 mm rotates at 1300 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 390, N = 1300 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.39)*1300 / 60 | Answer: 26.55 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 16.5 kW at 1250 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 7500 N/m and mass 11.8 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.

question: A plane wall of area 3.2 m^2 and thickness 0.18 m has conductivity k = 13.3 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 100 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.

question: A surface of area 5.8 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 155 W/m^2-K to surroundings 110 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.

question: In turning, cutting speed = 190 m/min, feed = 0.18 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2.8 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 190, f = 0.18, d = 2.8 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*190*0.18*2.8 | Answer: 95760 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 110 mm is turned at 1200 rpm with a feed of 0.27 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 110, N = 1200, f = 0.27 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 110 / (0.27*1200) | Answer: 0.3395 min

question: A resistor of 79 ohm carries a current of 4.1 A. Find the voltage across it.

question: Three resistors 45 ohm, 4 ohm and 94 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 45, R2 = 4, R3 = 94 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 45 + 4 + 94 | Answer: 143 ohm

question: Two resistors 52 ohm and 59 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 52, R2 = 59 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 52*59 / (52+59) | Answer: 27.64 ohm

question: A device draws 11.9 A at 70 V. Find the power consumed.

question: A current of 1.4 A flows through a 49 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.

question: Two capacitors 16.3 uF and 15.4 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 16.3, C2 = 15.4 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 16.3*15.4 / (16.3+15.4) | Answer: 7.919 uF

question: A resistor 24 kohm and capacitor 11.8 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 24, C = 11.8 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (24k)(11.8u) = 283.2 ms | Answer: 283.2 ms

question: An inductor 129.4 mH is in series with 61 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 129.4, R = 61 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (129.4e-3) / 61 | Answer: 2.121 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 115.3 mH inductor at 670 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 115.3, f = 670 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (670)(115.3e-3) | Answer: 485.4 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 42.1 uF capacitor at 490 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 42.1, f = 490 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (490)(42.1e-6)) | Answer: 7.715 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 33 ohm, XL = 139 ohm and XC = 102 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 33, XL = 139, XC = 102 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(33^2 + (139 - 102)^2) | Answer: 49.58 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 80.3 mH and C = 7.7 uF (in Hz).

question: A capacitor of 28.1 uF is charged to 385 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 28.1, V = 385 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*28.1e-6*(385)^2 | Answer: 2083 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 390 V with 910 primary turns and 420 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 390, N1 = 910, N2 = 420 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 390 * 420/910 | Answer: 180 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 270 V and draws an armature current of 40 A. If the armature resistance is 1.3 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 270, Ia = 40, Ra = 1.3 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 270 - 40*1.3 | Answer: 218 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 155 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.97. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 155, VL = 400, pf = 0.97 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*400*155*0.97 / 1000 | Answer: 104.2 kW

question: A load has real power 75 kW and apparent power 115 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 75, S = 115 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 75 / 115 | Answer: 0.6522

question: A machine delivers 160 kW output while drawing 187 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 13 V across R1 = 37 ohm and R2 = 31 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 80 kohm and Rin = 31 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 120 kohm and Rg = 32 kohm. Find the voltage gain.

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 792. Express the gain in decibels (power).

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.5 m carries a central point load of 35 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.7 m carries a UDL of 50 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.

question: A cantilever of length 3 m carries a point load 80 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.

question: A cantilever of length 4.6 m carries a UDL of 20 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.

question: A simply supported beam of span 10 m carries a point load 90 kN at distance 1.3 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.

question: A simply supported beam (span 7.9 m) carries a central point load 45 kN. With E = 30 GPa and I = 140e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.

question: A fixed beam of span 6.8 m carries a UDL of 21 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.

question: An RC beam has overall depth 300 mm, clear cover 25 mm and main bars of diameter 25 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 300, c = 25, dia = 25 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 300 - 25 - 25/2 | Answer: 262.5 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 19.6 m^2 carrying a factored load of 13 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 19.6, w = 13 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 13 * 19.6 | Answer: 254.8 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 3.1 m, unit weight 19 kN/m^3, phi = 29 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 8.9 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 20 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 8.9, g = 20 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (20 - 9.81)*8.9 | Answer: 90.69 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 7e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.6, area = 4.8e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 7, i = 0.6, A = 4.8 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (7e-4)*0.6*(4.8e-3) | Answer: 2016 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 0.7 m, bed slope 0.001 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.019. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 3.8 m under a head of 0.5 m. Taking Cd = 0.64 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 3.2 m wide carries a discharge of 27.7 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 560 m and design speed 40 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 560, V = 40 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (40)^2 / (127*560) | Answer: 0.0225
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: For a design speed of 75 km/h with allowable superelevation 0.05 and lateral friction 0.14, find the minimum curve radius in m.
A tank of volume 110 m^3 treats a flow of 10 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 110, Q = 10 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 110 / 10 | Answer: 11 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 150 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.29 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 6 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 150, k = 0.29, t = 6 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 150*(1 - e^(-0.29*6)) | Answer: 123.7 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.58, rainfall intensity 80 mm/h over a catchment of 26.2 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.58, i = 80, A = 26.2 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.58*80*26.2 / 360 | Answer: 3.377 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.03 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 210 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.03, M = 210 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 210*(20+0.03)/20 | Answer: 210.3 m

question: Convert the decimal number 54 to binary.
solution: Divide 54 by 2 repeatedly, recording remainders | Reading remainders in reverse gives 110110 | Answer: 110110 (binary)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 2 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the decimal number 1092 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 1092 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 444 (hex)

solution: XOR: 01001000 | Count of 1s = 2 | Answer: 2
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 660 megabits is sent over a link of 53 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 660, B = 53 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 660 / 53 | Answer: 12.45 s

question: A link has bandwidth 79 Mbps and round-trip time 30 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 79, R = 30 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 79e6 * 30e-3 bits = 2370 kb | Answer: 2370 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.91, cache access time 2 ns and main-memory access time 70 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.91, tc = 2, tm = 70 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.91*2 + (1 - 0.91)*70 | Answer: 8.12 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 139048 elements?
solution: Given: n = 139048 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(139048)) + 1 | Answer: 18

question: An O(n^2) algorithm performs c*n^2 basic operations. If c = 1 and n = 1940, how many operations are performed?
solution: Given: n = 1940 | Formula: operations = n^2 | Substitute: = (1940)^2 | Answer: 3763600

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.012, memory access time 160 ns and page-fault service time 9 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 9 ms = 9000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.012)*160 + 0.012*9000000.0 ns | Answer: 108.2 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 2.4 m^3 at 180 kPa and 530 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 2.4, P = 180, Tk = 530 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (180e3)*2.4 / (8.314*530) | Answer: 98.04 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.24 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 9 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.24, t = 9 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.24*9) | Answer: 0.8847

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.22 /min) is to reach 60% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.22, X = 60 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.6) / 0.22 | Answer: 4.165 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.45 /min) reaches 75% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.45, X = 75 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.75 / (0.45*(1 - 0.75)) | Answer: 6.667 min

question: For a reaction with A = 7e10 /s and activation energy 90 kJ/mol at 440 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 7, Ea = 90, Tk = 440 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 7e10 * exp(-90e3 / (8.314*440)) | Answer: 1.447 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.93 and bottoms xW = 0.04, with relative volatility alpha = 3.5. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.93, xw = 0.04, al = 3.5 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.93/0.07)(0.96/0.04)] / ln(3.5) | Answer: 4.602 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.62 and x = 0.43. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.62, x = 0.43 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.62/0.38) / (0.43/0.57) | Answer: 2.163

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.38 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 55 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.38, Psat = 55 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.38 * 55 | Answer: 20.9 kPa

question: A stream of 3.2 kg/s with specific heat 3.9 kJ/kg-K is heated through 100 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 3.2, cp = 3.9, dT = 100 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 3.2*3.9*100 | Answer: 1248 kW

question: A reactor of volume 14 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 3.6 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 14, Q = 3.6 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 14 / 3.6 | Answer: 3.889 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 5.5e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 1 mm with a concentration difference of 150 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 5.5, L = 1, dC = 150 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (5.5e-9)*150 / (1e-3) | Answer: 825 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 4 min and steady-state gain 1.2. For a step input of magnitude 12, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 4, K = 1.2, M = 12 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 1.2 * 12 | Answer: 14.4 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 55 m^2 flies at 180 m/s (air density 1 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 1.3. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 55, V = 180, rho = 1, CL = 1.3 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1*(180)^2*55*1.3 / 1000 | Answer: 1158 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 105 m^2 flies at 140 m/s (density 1.225 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.07. Find the drag force in kN.
A specimen under stress 250 MPa shows an elastic strain of 0.6e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 250, eps = 0.6 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 250 / (0.6e-3) MPa = 416.7 GPa | Answer: 416.7 GPa

question: A block of mass 4 kg has a volume of 2.9e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 4, V = 2.9 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 4 / (2.9e-3) | Answer: 1379 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 2200 mm is heated through 25 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 11e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 2200, dT = 25, al = 11 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 2200*11e-6*25 | Answer: 0.605 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 125 ohm, R2 = 80 ohm and R3 = 265 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 125, R2 = 80, R3 = 265 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 80*265 / 125 | Answer: 169.6 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 350 ohm and gauge factor 2.2 experiences a strain of 1550e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 350, GF = 2.2, eps = 1550 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 350*2.2*1550e-6 | Answer: 1194 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 9.47 when the true value is 50. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.47, true = 50 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.47 - 50| / 50 * 100 | Answer: 81.06 %

question: Annual demand is 28000 units, ordering cost 30 per order and holding cost 4 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 28000, S = 30, H = 4 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*28000*30 / 4) | Answer: 648.1 units

question: An asset costs 80000 with salvage value 34000 after 16 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 80000, Sv = 34000, n = 16 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (80000 - 34000) / 16 | Answer: 2875 per year

question: A product sells for 270 per unit with variable cost 140 per unit and fixed costs 120000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 270, V = 140, F = 120000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 120000 / (270 - 140) | Answer: 923.1 units

question: Find the present worth of 40000 received 10 years from now at an interest rate of 7% per year.
solution: Given: F = 40000, n = 10, i = 7 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 40000 / (1 + 0.07)^10 | Answer: 20334 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.92, 0.9 and 0.98 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.92, r2 = 0.9, r3 = 0.98 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.92*0.9*0.98 | Answer: 0.8114

question: A process produces 6 defective items in a batch of 14000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 6, N = 14000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 6/14000 * 1e6 | Answer: 428.6 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -2x^3 + 4x^2 - 4x - 7 evaluated at x = 0.
For f(x) = 5x^3 - 8x^2 + 5x, find f''(x) at x = -4.

solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: 168

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[7, -4], [-6, 8]].
solution: Trace tr = 15, Determinant = 32 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 12.42

question: Solve for x: -1x + -3y = 11 and 0x + -6y = -5.

question: Find the slope of the line through (-6, -8) and (5, 5).

question: Find the distance between the points (6, -4) and (4, 1).
solution: Given: x1 = 6, y1 = -4, x2 = 4, y2 = 1 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-2)^2 + (5)^2) | Answer: 5.385 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (-2,-3), (-4,-8), (-1,0).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 0.5 sq units

question: Find the 39th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -2 and common difference 8.
solution: Given: a = -2, d = 8, n = 39 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -2 + (39 - 1)*8 | Answer: 302

question: Find the sum of the first 30 terms of an AP with first term -10 and common difference -8.
Find the simple interest on a principal of 26000 at 11.6% per annum for 6 years.
solution: Given: P = 26000, R = 11.6, Tt = 6 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 26000 * 11.6 * 6 / 100 | Answer: 18096 currency units

question: Find the amount when 37500 is invested at 8.5% per annum compounded annually for 3 years.
solution: Given: P = 37500, R = 8.5, Tt = 3 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 37500 * (1 + 8.5/100)^3 | Answer: 47898 currency units

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (-1, -1, 5) and (-2, 0, 4).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 18.79 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number -3 + -9i.
solution: Given: a = -3, b = -9 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((-3)^2 + (-9)^2) | Answer: 9.487

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number 11 + -6i.
solution: Given: a = 11, b = -6 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(-6, 11) | Answer: -28.61 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = x^3 + 7x^2 - 8x + 8 at x = -1.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-87 with initial guess x0=11, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=0.6 and ordinates 14, 11, 20, 9, 19, estimate the integral.

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 9 and 66.
solution: Given: a = 9, b = 66 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 9*66 / 3 | Answer: 198

question: A circular rod of diameter 41 mm carries an axial tensile load of 87 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 28 mm and length 600 mm carries an axial load of 88 kN. Take E = 200 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 44 mm transmits a torque of 2050 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 44, Tt = 2050 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(2050*1000) / (pi*(44)^3) | Answer: 122.6 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 63 mm and length 1600 mm carries a torque of 1400 N-m. With G = 45 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (63)^4 / 32 = 1546543 mm^4 | theta = (1400*1000)(1600) / (45000 * 1546543) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 1.844 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 107 mm wide and 110 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 107, h = 110 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 107*(110)^2 / 6 | Answer: 215783 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (113 mm x 210 mm) carries a bending moment of 22 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (35 mm x 100 mm) has effective length 3900 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 660 MPa is designed for a working stress of 250 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 660, sw = 250 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 660 / 250 | Answer: 2.64

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1200 mm and wall thickness 19 mm carries an internal pressure of 2.7 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1200, t = 19, P = 2.7 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 2.7*1200 / (2*19) | Answer: 85.26 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 780 K and 420 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 780, Tc = 420 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 420/780) * 100 | Answer: 46.15 %

question: A refrigerator works between 261 K (cold) and 300 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 261, Th = 300 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 261 / (300 - 261) | Answer: 6.692

question: A heat pump operates between 282 K and 330 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 282, Th = 330 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 330 / (330 - 282) | Answer: 6.875

question: 5.9 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 60 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 5.9, dT = 60 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 5.9 * 0.718 * 60 | Answer: 254.2 kJ

question: 7.2 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 155 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 7.2, dT = 155 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 7.2 * 1.005 * 155 | Answer: 1122 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 1.4 m^3 at 450 K with mass 5.2 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 1.4, Tk = 450, m = 5.2 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 5.2*0.287*450 / 1.4 | Answer: 479.7 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 3.7 kg of air expands isothermally at 410 K from volume V1 to 4*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.7, Tk = 410, ratio = 4 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 3.7*0.287*410*ln(4) | Answer: 603.6 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 3.4 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.38 m. Find the Reynolds number.
