solution: Given: V = 3.4, D = 0.38 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*3.4*0.38 / 0.001 | Answer: 1292000

question: Water flows at 3 m/s through a pipe of diameter 270 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 29.9 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 29.9 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*29.9 / 1000 | Answer: 293.3 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 6.1 m. Taking Cv = 0.96, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 6.1, cv = 0.96 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.96*sqrt(2*9.81*6.1) | Answer: 10.5 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 380 mm) water flows at 0.9 m/s. It contracts to diameter 100 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 380, d2 = 100, V1 = 0.9 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 0.9*(380/100)^2 | Answer: 13 m/s

question: Water flows at 3.5 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.31 m and length 290 m. With friction factor f = 0.022, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 26 teeth drives a gear of 50 teeth. If the pinion runs at 600 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 26, z2 = 50, N1 = 600 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 600*26 / 50 | Answer: 312 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 390 mm rotates at 1000 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 390, N = 1000 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.39)*1000 / 60 | Answer: 20.42 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 28.6 kW at 500 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 28.6, N = 500 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(28.6*1000) / (2*pi*500) | Answer: 546.2 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 4.4 kg rotates at radius 0.32 m at 1050 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 9100 N/m and mass 1.1 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 9100, m = 1.1 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(9100/1.1) | Answer: 14.48 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 7.8 m^2 and thickness 0.38 m has conductivity k = 34.8 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 190 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 7.8, L = 0.38, k = 34.8, dT = 190 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 34.8*7.8*190 / 0.38 | Answer: 135720 W

question: A surface of area 1.5 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 65 W/m^2-K to surroundings 80 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 1.5, h = 65, dT = 80 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 65*1.5*80 | Answer: 7800 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 220 m/min, feed = 0.41 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2.9 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 220, f = 0.41, d = 2.9 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*220*0.41*2.9 | Answer: 261580 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 450 mm is turned at 850 rpm with a feed of 0.19 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 450, N = 850, f = 0.19 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 450 / (0.19*850) | Answer: 2.786 min

question: A resistor of 72 ohm carries a current of 3 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 72, I = 3 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 3 * 72 | Answer: 216 V

question: Three resistors 52 ohm, 79 ohm and 80 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 52, R2 = 79, R3 = 80 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 52 + 79 + 80 | Answer: 211 ohm

question: Two resistors 99 ohm and 2 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 99, R2 = 2 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 99*2 / (99+2) | Answer: 1.96 ohm

question: A device draws 3 A at 175 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 175, I = 3 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 175 * 3 | Answer: 525 W

question: A current of 0.7 A flows through a 64 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 0.7, R = 64 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (0.7)^2 * 64 | Answer: 31.36 W

question: Two capacitors 7.8 uF and 23 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 7.8, C2 = 23 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 7.8*23 / (7.8+23) | Answer: 5.825 uF

question: A resistor 51 kohm and capacitor 3.5 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 51, C = 3.5 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (51k)(3.5u) = 178.5 ms | Answer: 178.5 ms

question: An inductor 48.8 mH is in series with 67 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 48.8, R = 67 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (48.8e-3) / 67 | Answer: 0.7284 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 14.4 mH inductor at 790 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 14.4, f = 790 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (790)(14.4e-3) | Answer: 71.48 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 25.7 uF capacitor at 170 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 25.7, f = 170 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (170)(25.7e-6)) | Answer: 36.43 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 12 ohm, XL = 20 ohm and XC = 79 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 12, XL = 20, XC = 79 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(12^2 + (20 - 79)^2) | Answer: 60.21 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 52.8 mH and C = 2.7 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 52.8, C = 2.7 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(52.8e-3 * 2.7e-6)) | Answer: 421.5 Hz

question: A capacitor of 3 uF is charged to 280 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 3, V = 280 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*3e-6*(280)^2 | Answer: 117.6 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 130 V with 230 primary turns and 40 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 130, N1 = 230, N2 = 40 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 130 * 40/230 | Answer: 22.61 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 440 V and draws an armature current of 48 A. If the armature resistance is 1.39 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 440, Ia = 48, Ra = 1.39 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 440 - 48*1.39 | Answer: 373.3 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 130 A at 415 V (line) with a power factor of 0.83. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 130, VL = 415, pf = 0.83 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*415*130*0.83 / 1000 | Answer: 77.56 kW

question: A load has real power 40 kW and apparent power 185 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 40, S = 185 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 40 / 185 | Answer: 0.2162

question: A machine delivers 30 kW output while drawing 132 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 30, Pi = 132 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 30/132 * 100 | Answer: 22.73 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 7 V across R1 = 34 ohm and R2 = 32 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 7, R1 = 34, R2 = 32 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 7*32 / (34+32) | Answer: 3.394 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 60 kohm and Rin = 1 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 60, Rin = 1 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 60 / 1 | Answer: 60

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 170 kohm and Rg = 3 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 170, Rg = 3 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 170/3 | Answer: 57.67

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 6734. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 6734 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(6734) | Answer: 38.28 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.5 m carries a central point load of 30 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 9.5, W = 30 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 30*9.5 / 4 | Answer: 71.25 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 8 m carries a UDL of 50 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 8, w = 50 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 50*(8)^2 / 8 | Answer: 400 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 5.7 m carries a point load 65 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.7, W = 65 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 65*5.7 | Answer: 370.5 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 1.4 m carries a UDL of 38 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 1.4, w = 38 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 38*(1.4)^2 / 2 | Answer: 37.24 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 8.6 m carries a point load 30 kN at distance 2.3 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 8.6, a = 2.3, W = 30 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 30*(8.6 - 2.3) / 8.6 | Answer: 21.98 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 7.5 m) carries a central point load 20 kN. With E = 30 GPa and I = 420e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=20000 N, L=7500.0 mm, E=30000 MPa, I=420e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 13.95 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 7 m carries a UDL of 30 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7, w = 30 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 30*(7)^2 / 12 | Answer: 122.5 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 450 mm, clear cover 45 mm and main bars of diameter 12 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 450, c = 45, dia = 12 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 450 - 45 - 12/2 | Answer: 399 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 12.4 m^2 carrying a factored load of 8.8 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 12.4, w = 8.8 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 8.8 * 12.4 | Answer: 109.1 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 5.9 m, unit weight 16 kN/m^3, phi = 36 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 4.2 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 18 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 4.2, g = 18 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (18 - 9.81)*4.2 | Answer: 34.4 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 6.3e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1.3, area = 1.9e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 6.3, i = 1.3, A = 1.9 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (6.3e-4)*1.3*(1.9e-3) | Answer: 1556 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 2.1 m, bed slope 0.005 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.021. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 2.6 m under a head of 0.7 m. Taking Cd = 0.62 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 2.6 m wide carries a discharge of 5.1 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 180 m and design speed 90 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 180, V = 90 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (90)^2 / (127*180) | Answer: 0.3543
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: For a design speed of 55 km/h with allowable superelevation 0.05 and lateral friction 0.15, find the minimum curve radius in m.
A tank of volume 670 m^3 treats a flow of 140 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 670, Q = 140 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 670 / 140 | Answer: 4.786 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 190 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.25 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 4 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 190, k = 0.25, t = 4 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 190*(1 - e^(-0.25*4)) | Answer: 120.1 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.53, rainfall intensity 95 mm/h over a catchment of 24.6 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.53, i = 95, A = 24.6 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.53*95*24.6 / 360 | Answer: 3.441 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.03 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 190 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.03, M = 190 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 190*(30+0.03)/30 | Answer: 190.2 m

question: Convert the decimal number 186 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 186 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: BA (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 00011110 and 10000010.
solution: XOR: 10011100 | Count of 1s = 4 | Answer: 4
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 740 megabits is sent over a link of 15 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 740, B = 15 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 740 / 15 | Answer: 49.33 s

question: A link has bandwidth 57 Mbps and round-trip time 160 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 57, R = 160 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 57e6 * 160e-3 bits = 9120 kb | Answer: 9120 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.98, cache access time 8 ns and main-memory access time 50 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.98, tc = 8, tm = 50 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.98*8 + (1 - 0.98)*50 | Answer: 8.84 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 941081 elements?
solution: Given: n = 941081 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(941081)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: An O(n^2) algorithm performs c*n^2 basic operations. If c = 1 and n = 830, how many operations are performed?
solution: Given: n = 830 | Formula: operations = n^2 | Substitute: = (830)^2 | Answer: 688900

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.009, memory access time 120 ns and page-fault service time 4 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 4 ms = 4000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.009)*120 + 0.009*4000000.0 ns | Answer: 36.12 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 1.4 m^3 at 240 kPa and 330 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 1.4, P = 240, Tk = 330 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (240e3)*1.4 / (8.314*330) | Answer: 122.5 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.11 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 7 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.11, t = 7 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.11*7) | Answer: 0.537

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.15 /min) is to reach 55% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.15, X = 55 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.55) / 0.15 | Answer: 5.323 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.4 /min) reaches 75% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.4, X = 75 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.75 / (0.4*(1 - 0.75)) | Answer: 7.5 min

question: For a reaction with A = 3e10 /s and activation energy 55 kJ/mol at 340 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 3, Ea = 55, Tk = 340 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 3e10 * exp(-55e3 / (8.314*340)) | Answer: 106.4 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.95 and bottoms xW = 0.03, with relative volatility alpha = 3.2. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.95, xw = 0.03, al = 3.2 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.95/0.05)(0.97/0.03)] / ln(3.2) | Answer: 5.52 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.55 and x = 0.34. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.55, x = 0.34 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.55/0.45) / (0.34/0.66) | Answer: 2.373

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.11 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 70 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.11, Psat = 70 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.11 * 70 | Answer: 7.7 kPa

question: A stream of 4.6 kg/s with specific heat 1.7 kJ/kg-K is heated through 75 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 4.6, cp = 1.7, dT = 75 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 4.6*1.7*75 | Answer: 586.5 kW

question: A reactor of volume 12.3 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 0.7 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 12.3, Q = 0.7 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 12.3 / 0.7 | Answer: 17.57 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 8.1e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 5 mm with a concentration difference of 30 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 8.1, L = 5, dC = 30 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (8.1e-9)*30 / (5e-3) | Answer: 48.6 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 1.6 min and steady-state gain 3.6. For a step input of magnitude 11, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 1.6, K = 3.6, M = 11 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 3.6 * 11 | Answer: 39.6 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 60 m^2 flies at 190 m/s (air density 1.225 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.8. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 60, V = 190, rho = 1.225, CL = 0.8 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1.225*(190)^2*60*0.8 / 1000 | Answer: 1061 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 100 m^2 flies at 180 m/s (density 1.225 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.04. Find the drag force in kN.
A specimen under stress 210 MPa shows an elastic strain of 1.3e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 210, eps = 1.3 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 210 / (1.3e-3) MPa = 161.5 GPa | Answer: 161.5 GPa

question: A block of mass 2 kg has a volume of 4.5e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 2, V = 4.5 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 2 / (4.5e-3) | Answer: 444.4 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 900 mm is heated through 40 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 23e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 900, dT = 40, al = 23 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 900*23e-6*40 | Answer: 0.828 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 115 ohm, R2 = 55 ohm and R3 = 50 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 115, R2 = 55, R3 = 50 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 55*50 / 115 | Answer: 23.91 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 120 ohm and gauge factor 2 experiences a strain of 1550e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 120, GF = 2, eps = 1550 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 120*2*1550e-6 | Answer: 372 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 10.09 when the true value is 100. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10.09, true = 100 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10.09 - 100| / 100 * 100 | Answer: 89.91 %

question: Annual demand is 7000 units, ordering cost 250 per order and holding cost 6 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 7000, S = 250, H = 6 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*7000*250 / 6) | Answer: 763.8 units

question: An asset costs 190000 with salvage value 18000 after 5 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 190000, Sv = 18000, n = 5 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (190000 - 18000) / 5 | Answer: 34400 per year

question: A product sells for 500 per unit with variable cost 90 per unit and fixed costs 190000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 500, V = 90, F = 190000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 190000 / (500 - 90) | Answer: 463.4 units

question: Find the present worth of 120000 received 2 years from now at an interest rate of 9% per year.
solution: Given: F = 120000, n = 2, i = 9 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 120000 / (1 + 0.09)^2 | Answer: 101002 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.9, 0.95 and 0.95 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.9, r2 = 0.95, r3 = 0.95 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.9*0.95*0.95 | Answer: 0.8122

question: A process produces 40 defective items in a batch of 18500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 40, N = 18500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 40/18500 * 1e6 | Answer: 2162 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = 5x^3 + 8x^2 + 6x - 7 evaluated at x = -1.
For f(x) = -6x^3 - 6x^2 + 8x + 8, find f''(x) at x = -1.
Evaluate the definite integral of (-5x^2 - 2x + 8) dx from x = -1 to x = 7.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = -5x^3/3 + -2x^2/2 + 8x | Evaluate F(7) - F(-1) | Answer: -557.3
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 3x^2 - 11x + 9 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[-1, -4], [-4, 8]].
solution: Given: a = -1, b = -4, c = -4, d = 8 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (-1)(8) - (-4)(-4) | Answer: -24

question: Find the determinant of [[4, 2, -4], [0, 1, -2], [1, -2, -1]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: -20

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[-4, 0], [8, 7]].
solution: Trace tr = 3, Determinant = -28 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 7

question: Solve for x: -2x + -3y = 0 and 4x + -2y = 12.
solution: Determinant = -2*-2 - -3*4 = 16 | x = (e d - b f) / det = 2.25 | Answer: x = 2.25
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 12, 29, 99, 11, 77.
solution: Sum = 228 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 45.6 | Answer: 45.6

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 26, 15, 7, 30, 44.
solution: Mean = 24.4 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 14.22

question: Find the slope of the line through (6, -5) and (-4, 5).
solution: Given: x1 = 6, y1 = -5, x2 = -4, y2 = 5 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (5 - -5) / (-4 - 6) | Answer: -1

question: Find the distance between the points (9, -7) and (4, 2).
solution: Given: x1 = 9, y1 = -7, x2 = 4, y2 = 2 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-5)^2 + (9)^2) | Answer: 10.3 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (7,-8), (8,1), (-6,-8).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 58.5 sq units

question: Find the 32th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -7 and common difference -1.
solution: Given: a = -7, d = -1, n = 32 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -7 + (32 - 1)*-1 | Answer: -38

question: Find the sum of the first 19 terms of an AP with first term 10 and common difference -1.
solution: Given: a = 10, d = -1, n = 19 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 19/2 [2*10 + (19-1)*-1] | Answer: 19

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 23000 at 7.8% per annum for 10 years.
solution: Given: P = 23000, R = 7.8, Tt = 10 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 23000 * 7.8 * 10 / 100 | Answer: 17940 currency units

question: Find the amount when 18500 is invested at 12% per annum compounded annually for 5 years.
solution: Given: P = 18500, R = 12, Tt = 5 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 18500 * (1 + 12/100)^5 | Answer: 32603 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (-6, 0, -7) and (3, 2, -5).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (-4, 5, 1) and (3, 4, 5).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 43.94

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (1, -4, 0) and (-1, 5, 1).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 168.6 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number -10 + 6i.
solution: Given: a = -10, b = 6 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((-10)^2 + (6)^2) | Answer: 11.66

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number 2 + -8i.
solution: Given: a = 2, b = -8 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(-8, 2) | Answer: -75.96 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = x^3 - 6x^2 + 8x - 3 at x = -2.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-141 with initial guess x0=11, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.1 and ordinates 15, 6, 18, 5, 14, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 452 and 284.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 452 and 284 | Answer: GCD = 4

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 25 and 6.
solution: Given: a = 25, b = 6 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 25*6 / 1 | Answer: 150
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 37 mm carries an axial tensile load of 45 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 28 mm and length 2700 mm carries an axial load of 63 kN. Take E = 210 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 37 mm transmits a torque of 2850 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 37, Tt = 2850 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(2850*1000) / (pi*(37)^3) | Answer: 286.6 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 45 mm and length 1500 mm carries a torque of 1050 N-m. With G = 80 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (45)^4 / 32 = 402578 mm^4 | theta = (1050*1000)(1500) / (80000 * 402578) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 2.802 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 116 mm wide and 80 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 116, h = 80 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 116*(80)^2 / 6 | Answer: 123733 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (54 mm x 130 mm) carries a bending moment of 15 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (70 mm x 120 mm) has effective length 2400 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 870 MPa is designed for a working stress of 170 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 870, sw = 170 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 870 / 170 | Answer: 5.118

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1450 mm and wall thickness 8 mm carries an internal pressure of 2.7 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1450, t = 8, P = 2.7 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 2.7*1450 / (2*8) | Answer: 244.7 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 640 K and 330 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 640, Tc = 330 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 330/640) * 100 | Answer: 48.44 %

question: A refrigerator works between 260 K (cold) and 300 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 260, Th = 300 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 260 / (300 - 260) | Answer: 6.5

question: A heat pump operates between 263 K and 328 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 263, Th = 328 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 328 / (328 - 263) | Answer: 5.046

question: 4.5 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 110 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.5, dT = 110 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 4.5 * 0.718 * 110 | Answer: 355.4 kJ

question: 3.9 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 165 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.9, dT = 165 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 3.9 * 1.005 * 165 | Answer: 646.7 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 2.7 m^3 at 420 K with mass 4.2 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 2.7, Tk = 420, m = 4.2 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 4.2*0.287*420 / 2.7 | Answer: 187.5 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 1.7 kg of air expands isothermally at 410 K from volume V1 to 3*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1.7, Tk = 410, ratio = 3 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 1.7*0.287*410*ln(3) | Answer: 219.8 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 3.3 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.11 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 3.3, D = 0.11 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*3.3*0.11 / 0.001 | Answer: 363000

question: Water flows at 3.5 m/s through a pipe of diameter 270 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 8.7 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 8.7 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*8.7 / 1000 | Answer: 85.35 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 10.8 m. Taking Cv = 0.99, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 10.8, cv = 0.99 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.99*sqrt(2*9.81*10.8) | Answer: 14.41 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 390 mm) water flows at 1.7 m/s. It contracts to diameter 70 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 390, d2 = 70, V1 = 1.7 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 1.7*(390/70)^2 | Answer: 52.77 m/s

question: Water flows at 3.7 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.16 m and length 340 m. With friction factor f = 0.031, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 24 teeth drives a gear of 47 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1200 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 24, z2 = 47, N1 = 1200 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1200*24 / 47 | Answer: 612.8 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 400 mm rotates at 1200 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 400, N = 1200 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.4)*1200 / 60 | Answer: 25.13 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 48.3 kW at 500 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 48.3, N = 500 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(48.3*1000) / (2*pi*500) | Answer: 922.5 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 4.7 kg rotates at radius 0.18 m at 800 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 17100 N/m and mass 11.4 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 17100, m = 11.4 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(17100/11.4) | Answer: 6.164 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 7.9 m^2 and thickness 0.14 m has conductivity k = 12.9 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 25 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 7.9, L = 0.14, k = 12.9, dT = 25 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 12.9*7.9*25 / 0.14 | Answer: 18198 W

question: A surface of area 3.2 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 30 W/m^2-K to surroundings 145 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 3.2, h = 30, dT = 145 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 30*3.2*145 | Answer: 13920 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 80 m/min, feed = 0.22 mm/rev, depth of cut = 0.8 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 80, f = 0.22, d = 0.8 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*80*0.22*0.8 | Answer: 14080 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 140 mm is turned at 600 rpm with a feed of 0.25 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 140, N = 600, f = 0.25 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 140 / (0.25*600) | Answer: 0.9333 min

question: A resistor of 79 ohm carries a current of 7.4 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 79, I = 7.4 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 7.4 * 79 | Answer: 584.6 V

question: Three resistors 59 ohm, 56 ohm and 94 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 59, R2 = 56, R3 = 94 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 59 + 56 + 94 | Answer: 209 ohm

question: Two resistors 116 ohm and 91 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 116, R2 = 91 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 116*91 / (116+91) | Answer: 51 ohm

question: A device draws 9.3 A at 55 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 55, I = 9.3 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 55 * 9.3 | Answer: 511.5 W

question: A current of 1.6 A flows through a 11 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 1.6, R = 11 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (1.6)^2 * 11 | Answer: 28.16 W

question: Two capacitors 35.4 uF and 32.6 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 35.4, C2 = 32.6 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 35.4*32.6 / (35.4+32.6) | Answer: 16.97 uF

question: A resistor 60 kohm and capacitor 18.8 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 60, C = 18.8 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (60k)(18.8u) = 1128 ms | Answer: 1128 ms

question: An inductor 274.4 mH is in series with 170 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 274.4, R = 170 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (274.4e-3) / 170 | Answer: 1.614 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 193.4 mH inductor at 930 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 193.4, f = 930 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (930)(193.4e-3) | Answer: 113 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 19.1 uF capacitor at 760 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 19.1, f = 760 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (760)(19.1e-6)) | Answer: 10.96 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 94 ohm, XL = 126 ohm and XC = 57 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 94, XL = 126, XC = 57 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(94^2 + (126 - 57)^2) | Answer: 116.6 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 24.8 mH and C = 0.8 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 24.8, C = 0.8 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(24.8e-3 * 0.8e-6)) | Answer: 113 Hz

question: A capacitor of 13.4 uF is charged to 80 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 13.4, V = 80 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*13.4e-6*(80)^2 | Answer: 42.88 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 200 V with 500 primary turns and 20 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 200, N1 = 500, N2 = 20 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 200 * 20/500 | Answer: 8 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 190 V and draws an armature current of 35 A. If the armature resistance is 1.42 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 190, Ia = 35, Ra = 1.42 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 190 - 35*1.42 | Answer: 140.3 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 45 A at 415 V (line) with a power factor of 0.72. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 45, VL = 415, pf = 0.72 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*415*45*0.72 / 1000 | Answer: 23.29 kW

question: A load has real power 100 kW and apparent power 170 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 100, S = 170 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 100 / 170 | Answer: 0.5882

question: A machine delivers 75 kW output while drawing 152 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 75, Pi = 152 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 75/152 * 100 | Answer: 49.34 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 8 V across R1 = 37 ohm and R2 = 26 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 8, R1 = 37, R2 = 26 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 8*26 / (37+26) | Answer: 3.302 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 60 kohm and Rin = 41 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 60, Rin = 41 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 60 / 41 | Answer: 1.463

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 170 kohm and Rg = 37 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 170, Rg = 37 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 170/37 | Answer: 5.595

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 4542. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 4542 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(4542) | Answer: 36.57 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.6 m carries a central point load of 75 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.6, W = 75 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 75*4.6 / 4 | Answer: 86.25 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 5.8 m carries a UDL of 10 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.8, w = 10 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 10*(5.8)^2 / 8 | Answer: 42.05 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 1.6 m carries a point load 50 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 1.6, W = 50 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 50*1.6 | Answer: 80 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 1.6 m carries a UDL of 28 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 1.6, w = 28 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 28*(1.6)^2 / 2 | Answer: 35.84 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.2 m carries a point load 40 kN at distance 1.6 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 4.2, a = 1.6, W = 40 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 40*(4.2 - 1.6) / 4.2 | Answer: 24.76 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 4.7 m) carries a central point load 25 kN. With E = 30 GPa and I = 290e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=25000 N, L=4700.0 mm, E=30000 MPa, I=290e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 6.215 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 9 m carries a UDL of 18 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 9, w = 18 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 18*(9)^2 / 12 | Answer: 121.5 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 680 mm, clear cover 35 mm and main bars of diameter 20 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 680, c = 35, dia = 20 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 680 - 35 - 20/2 | Answer: 635 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 11.8 m^2 carrying a factored load of 9.7 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 11.8, w = 9.7 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 9.7 * 11.8 | Answer: 114.5 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 5.1 m, unit weight 18 kN/m^3, phi = 37 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 8.1 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 21 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 8.1, g = 21 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (21 - 9.81)*8.1 | Answer: 90.64 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 2.3e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1.1, area = 2.9e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 2.3, i = 1.1, A = 2.9 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (2.3e-4)*1.1*(2.9e-3) | Answer: 733.7 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 0.6 m, bed slope 0.005 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.028. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 3.5 m under a head of 0.4 m. Taking Cd = 0.6 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 2.4 m wide carries a discharge of 7.9 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 330 m and design speed 85 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 330, V = 85 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (85)^2 / (127*330) | Answer: 0.1724
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: A tank of volume 300 m^3 treats a flow of 190 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 300, Q = 190 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 300 / 190 | Answer: 1.579 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 230 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.16 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 5 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 230, k = 0.16, t = 5 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 230*(1 - e^(-0.16*5)) | Answer: 126.7 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.32, rainfall intensity 110 mm/h over a catchment of 59.1 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.32, i = 110, A = 59.1 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.32*110*59.1 / 360 | Answer: 5.779 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.06 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 260 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.06, M = 260 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 260*(30+0.06)/30 | Answer: 260.5 m

question: Convert the decimal number 3271 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 3271 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: CC7 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 11001000 and 01000011.
solution: XOR: 10001011 | Count of 1s = 4 | Answer: 4
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 870 megabits is sent over a link of 48 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 870, B = 48 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 870 / 48 | Answer: 18.12 s

question: A link has bandwidth 45 Mbps and round-trip time 130 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 45, R = 130 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 45e6 * 130e-3 bits = 5850 kb | Answer: 5850 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.92, cache access time 5 ns and main-memory access time 110 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.92, tc = 5, tm = 110 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.92*5 + (1 - 0.92)*110 | Answer: 13.4 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 879673 elements?
solution: Given: n = 879673 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(879673)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: An O(n^2) algorithm performs c*n^2 basic operations. If c = 1 and n = 2320, how many operations are performed?
solution: Given: n = 2320 | Formula: operations = n^2 | Substitute: = (2320)^2 | Answer: 5382400

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.014, memory access time 150 ns and page-fault service time 5 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 5 ms = 5000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.014)*150 + 0.014*5000000.0 ns | Answer: 70.15 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 1.5 m^3 at 150 kPa and 540 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 1.5, P = 150, Tk = 540 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (150e3)*1.5 / (8.314*540) | Answer: 50.12 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.33 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 11 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.33, t = 11 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.33*11) | Answer: 0.9735

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.5 /min) is to reach 80% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.5, X = 80 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.8) / 0.5 | Answer: 3.219 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.31 /min) reaches 90% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.31, X = 90 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.9 / (0.31*(1 - 0.9)) | Answer: 29.03 min

question: For a reaction with A = 6e10 /s and activation energy 75 kJ/mol at 460 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 6, Ea = 75, Tk = 460 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 6e10 * exp(-75e3 / (8.314*460)) | Answer: 182.5 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.97 and bottoms xW = 0.05, with relative volatility alpha = 3.2. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.97, xw = 0.05, al = 3.2 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.97/0.03)(0.95/0.05)] / ln(3.2) | Answer: 5.52 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.82 and x = 0.39. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.82, x = 0.39 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.82/0.18) / (0.39/0.61) | Answer: 7.125

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.68 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 105 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.68, Psat = 105 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.68 * 105 | Answer: 71.4 kPa

question: A stream of 7.1 kg/s with specific heat 3.7 kJ/kg-K is heated through 90 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 7.1, cp = 3.7, dT = 90 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 7.1*3.7*90 | Answer: 2364 kW

question: A reactor of volume 19.5 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 2.7 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 19.5, Q = 2.7 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 19.5 / 2.7 | Answer: 7.222 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 3e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 2 mm with a concentration difference of 190 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 3, L = 2, dC = 190 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (3e-9)*190 / (2e-3) | Answer: 285 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 6.3 min and steady-state gain 2.9. For a step input of magnitude 20, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 6.3, K = 2.9, M = 20 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 2.9 * 20 | Answer: 58 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 115 m^2 flies at 240 m/s (air density 1.225 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 1.3. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 115, V = 240, rho = 1.225, CL = 1.3 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1.225*(240)^2*115*1.3 / 1000 | Answer: 5274 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 95 m^2 flies at 160 m/s (density 1.225 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.1. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 95, V = 160, rho = 1.225, CD = 0.1 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*1.225*(160)^2*95*0.1 / 1000 | Answer: 149 kN

question: A specimen under stress 140 MPa shows an elastic strain of 2.5e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 140, eps = 2.5 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 140 / (2.5e-3) MPa = 56 GPa | Answer: 56 GPa

question: A block of mass 4 kg has a volume of 1.8e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 4, V = 1.8 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 4 / (1.8e-3) | Answer: 2222 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 1100 mm is heated through 125 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 11e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 1100, dT = 125, al = 11 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 1100*11e-6*125 | Answer: 1.512 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 20 ohm, R2 = 185 ohm and R3 = 210 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 20, R2 = 185, R3 = 210 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 185*210 / 20 | Answer: 1942 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 1000 ohm and gauge factor 2 experiences a strain of 1150e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 1000, GF = 2, eps = 1150 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 1000*2*1150e-6 | Answer: 2300 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 10.92 when the true value is 10. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10.92, true = 10 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10.92 - 10| / 10 * 100 | Answer: 9.2 %

question: Annual demand is 43000 units, ordering cost 280 per order and holding cost 31 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 43000, S = 280, H = 31 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*43000*280 / 31) | Answer: 881.3 units

question: An asset costs 410000 with salvage value 38000 after 8 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 410000, Sv = 38000, n = 8 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (410000 - 38000) / 8 | Answer: 46500 per year

question: A product sells for 220 per unit with variable cost 30 per unit and fixed costs 40000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 220, V = 30, F = 40000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 40000 / (220 - 30) | Answer: 210.5 units

question: Find the present worth of 185000 received 4 years from now at an interest rate of 9% per year.
solution: Given: F = 185000, n = 4, i = 9 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 185000 / (1 + 0.09)^4 | Answer: 131059 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.93, 0.98 and 0.96 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.93, r2 = 0.98, r3 = 0.96 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.93*0.98*0.96 | Answer: 0.8749

question: A process produces 47 defective items in a batch of 9500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 47, N = 9500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 47/9500 * 1e6 | Answer: 4947 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = 3x^3 - 2x^2 + 2x - 8 evaluated at x = 1.
For f(x) = 4x^3 + 2x^2 + 7x - 8, find f''(x) at x = 0.
Evaluate the definite integral of (-4x^2 + 4x - 3) dx from x = 2 to x = 7.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = -4x^3/3 + 4x^2/2 + -3x | Evaluate F(7) - F(2) | Answer: -371.7
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 6x^2 - x - 3 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[0, 1], [7, -9]].
solution: Given: a = 0, b = 1, c = 7, d = -9 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (0)(-9) - (1)(7) | Answer: -7

question: Find the determinant of [[0, -5, -6], [5, 2, 5], [-4, 6, -1]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: -153

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[-7, 2], [2, -6]].
solution: Trace tr = -13, Determinant = 38 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: -4.438

question: Solve for x: -6x + 2y = -10 and 1x + -5y = 3.
solution: Determinant = -6*-5 - 2*1 = 28 | x = (e d - b f) / det = 1.571 | Answer: x = 1.571
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 68, 91, 89, 93, 75.
solution: Sum = 416 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 83.2 | Answer: 83.2

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 5, 11, 38, 18, 20.
solution: Mean = 18.4 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 12.46

question: Find the slope of the line through (8, 2) and (3, 4).
solution: Given: x1 = 8, y1 = 2, x2 = 3, y2 = 4 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (4 - 2) / (3 - 8) | Answer: -0.4

question: Find the distance between the points (0, -7) and (-9, -4).
solution: Given: x1 = 0, y1 = -7, x2 = -9, y2 = -4 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-9)^2 + (3)^2) | Answer: 9.487 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (-1,8), (2,7), (0,-8).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 23.5 sq units

question: Find the 24th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -14 and common difference 3.
solution: Given: a = -14, d = 3, n = 24 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -14 + (24 - 1)*3 | Answer: 55

question: Find the sum of the first 24 terms of an AP with first term 1 and common difference -7.
solution: Given: a = 1, d = -7, n = 24 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 24/2 [2*1 + (24-1)*-7] | Answer: -1908

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 13500 at 8.7% per annum for 7 years.
solution: Given: P = 13500, R = 8.7, Tt = 7 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 13500 * 8.7 * 7 / 100 | Answer: 8221 currency units

question: Find the amount when 31500 is invested at 6.8% per annum compounded annually for 2 years.
solution: Given: P = 31500, R = 6.8, Tt = 2 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 31500 * (1 + 6.8/100)^2 | Answer: 3593 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (-7, 8, -6) and (5, 8, -8).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (1, 2, 3) and (0, -2, 0).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 6.325

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (-6, 6, -3) and (-2, 1, -6).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 51.34 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number 8 + 7i.
solution: Given: a = 8, b = 7 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((8)^2 + (7)^2) | Answer: 10.63

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number 0 + -2i.
solution: Given: a = 0, b = -2 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(-2, 0) | Answer: -90 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = 4x^3 + 2x^2 - 3x + 2 at x = 5.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-50 with initial guess x0=6, find x1 (one iteration).
solution: Given: N = 50, x0 = 6 | Formula: x1 = x0 - (x0^2 - N)/(2 x0) | Substitute: x1 = 6 - ((6)^2 - 50)/(2*6) | Answer: 7.167

question: Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.7 and ordinates 18, 11, 5, 10, 20, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 126 and 128.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 126 and 128 | Answer: GCD = 2

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 53 and 40.
solution: Given: a = 53, b = 40 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 53*40 / 1 | Answer: 2120
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 11 mm carries an axial tensile load of 30 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 29 mm and length 2300 mm carries an axial load of 59 kN. Take E = 200 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 74 mm transmits a torque of 1050 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 74, Tt = 1050 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(1050*1000) / (pi*(74)^3) | Answer: 13.2 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 64 mm and length 900 mm carries a torque of 1750 N-m. With G = 80 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (64)^4 / 32 = 1647099 mm^4 | theta = (1750*1000)(900) / (80000 * 1647099) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 0.6848 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 90 mm wide and 300 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 90, h = 300 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 90*(300)^2 / 6 | Answer: 1350000 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (49 mm x 190 mm) carries a bending moment of 6 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (42 mm x 90 mm) has effective length 1800 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 790 MPa is designed for a working stress of 110 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 790, sw = 110 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 790 / 110 | Answer: 7.182

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1200 mm and wall thickness 12 mm carries an internal pressure of 0.9 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1200, t = 12, P = 0.9 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 0.9*1200 / (2*12) | Answer: 45 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 1020 K and 340 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 1020, Tc = 340 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 340/1020) * 100 | Answer: 66.67 %

question: A refrigerator works between 262 K (cold) and 326 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 262, Th = 326 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 262 / (326 - 262) | Answer: 4.094

question: A heat pump operates between 283 K and 322 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 283, Th = 322 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 322 / (322 - 283) | Answer: 8.256

question: 3.1 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 110 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.1, dT = 110 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 3.1 * 0.718 * 110 | Answer: 244.8 kJ

question: 2.6 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 25 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.6, dT = 25 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 2.6 * 1.005 * 25 | Answer: 65.33 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 1.3 m^3 at 400 K with mass 5.4 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 1.3, Tk = 400, m = 5.4 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 5.4*0.287*400 / 1.3 | Answer: 476.9 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 4.9 kg of air expands isothermally at 430 K from volume V1 to 5*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.9, Tk = 430, ratio = 5 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 4.9*0.287*430*ln(5) | Answer: 973.2 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 4.6 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.09 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 4.6, D = 0.09 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*4.6*0.09 / 0.001 | Answer: 414000

question: Water flows at 2.5 m/s through a pipe of diameter 90 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 9.8 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 9.8 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*9.8 / 1000 | Answer: 96.14 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 8.4 m. Taking Cv = 0.96, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 8.4, cv = 0.96 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.96*sqrt(2*9.81*8.4) | Answer: 12.32 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 360 mm) water flows at 2.4 m/s. It contracts to diameter 80 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 360, d2 = 80, V1 = 2.4 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 2.4*(360/80)^2 | Answer: 48.6 m/s

question: Water flows at 2 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.3 m and length 460 m. With friction factor f = 0.024, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 15 teeth drives a gear of 90 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1300 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 15, z2 = 90, N1 = 1300 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1300*15 / 90 | Answer: 216.7 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 540 mm rotates at 1400 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 540, N = 1400 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.54)*1400 / 60 | Answer: 39.58 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 32.2 kW at 250 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 32.2, N = 250 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(32.2*1000) / (2*pi*250) | Answer: 123 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 9.9 kg rotates at radius 0.11 m at 400 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 14600 N/m and mass 13.8 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 14600, m = 13.8 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(14600/13.8) | Answer: 5.177 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 7.2 m^2 and thickness 0.36 m has conductivity k = 22.1 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 155 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 7.2, L = 0.36, k = 22.1, dT = 155 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 22.1*7.2*155 / 0.36 | Answer: 68510 W

question: A surface of area 5.1 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 50 W/m^2-K to surroundings 80 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 5.1, h = 50, dT = 80 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 50*5.1*80 | Answer: 20400 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 140 m/min, feed = 0.46 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2.2 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 140, f = 0.46, d = 2.2 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*140*0.46*2.2 | Answer: 141680 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 170 mm is turned at 400 rpm with a feed of 0.17 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 170, N = 400, f = 0.17 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 170 / (0.17*400) | Answer: 2.5 min

question: A resistor of 163 ohm carries a current of 3.2 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 163, I = 3.2 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 3.2 * 163 | Answer: 521.6 V

question: Three resistors 80 ohm, 66 ohm and 95 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 80, R2 = 66, R3 = 95 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 80 + 66 + 95 | Answer: 241 ohm

question: Two resistors 41 ohm and 37 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 41, R2 = 37 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 41*37 / (41+37) | Answer: 19.45 ohm

question: A device draws 0.1 A at 190 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 190, I = 0.1 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 190 * 0.1 | Answer: 19 W

question: A current of 6.6 A flows through a 141 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 6.6, R = 141 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (6.6)^2 * 141 | Answer: 6142 W

question: Two capacitors 30 uF and 1.1 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 30, C2 = 1.1 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 30*1.1 / (30+1.1) | Answer: 1.061 uF

question: A resistor 34 kohm and capacitor 16.3 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 34, C = 16.3 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (34k)(16.3u) = 554.2 ms | Answer: 554.2 ms

question: An inductor 63.3 mH is in series with 8 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 63.3, R = 8 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (63.3e-3) / 8 | Answer: 7.912 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 23.9 mH inductor at 330 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 23.9, f = 330 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (330)(23.9e-3) | Answer: 49.56 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 35.5 uF capacitor at 580 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 35.5, f = 580 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (580)(35.5e-6)) | Answer: 7.73 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 86 ohm, XL = 29 ohm and XC = 83 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 86, XL = 29, XC = 83 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(86^2 + (29 - 83)^2) | Answer: 101.5 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 32.3 mH and C = 6.5 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 32.3, C = 6.5 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(32.3e-3 * 6.5e-6)) | Answer: 347.3 Hz

question: A capacitor of 29.9 uF is charged to 130 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 29.9, V = 130 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*29.9e-6*(130)^2 | Answer: 252.7 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 190 V with 340 primary turns and 170 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 190, N1 = 340, N2 = 170 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 190 * 170/340 | Answer: 95 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 390 V and draws an armature current of 25 A. If the armature resistance is 0.66 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 390, Ia = 25, Ra = 0.66 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 390 - 25*0.66 | Answer: 373.5 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 170 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.78. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 170, VL = 400, pf = 0.78 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*400*170*0.78 / 1000 | Answer: 91.87 kW

question: A load has real power 165 kW and apparent power 165 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 165, S = 165 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 165 / 165 | Answer: 1

question: A machine delivers 60 kW output while drawing 122 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 60, Pi = 122 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 60/122 * 100 | Answer: 49.18 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 13 V across R1 = 19 ohm and R2 = 10 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 13, R1 = 19, R2 = 10 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 13*10 / (19+10) | Answer: 4.483 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 170 kohm and Rin = 27 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 170, Rin = 27 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 170 / 27 | Answer: 6.296

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 80 kohm and Rg = 2 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 80, Rg = 2 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 80/2 | Answer: 41

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 144. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 144 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(144) | Answer: 21.58 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.5 m carries a central point load of 50 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 9.5, W = 50 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 50*9.5 / 4 | Answer: 118.8 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.9 m carries a UDL of 55 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6.9, w = 55 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 55*(6.9)^2 / 8 | Answer: 327.3 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 5 m carries a point load 20 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5, W = 20 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 20*5 | Answer: 100 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 1.2 m carries a UDL of 28 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 1.2, w = 28 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 28*(1.2)^2 / 2 | Answer: 20.16 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 5.1 m carries a point load 15 kN at distance 1.5 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 5.1, a = 1.5, W = 15 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 15*(5.1 - 1.5) / 5.1 | Answer: 10.59 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 4.3 m) carries a central point load 50 kN. With E = 30 GPa and I = 510e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=50000 N, L=4300.0 mm, E=30000 MPa, I=510e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 5.413 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 7.9 m carries a UDL of 30 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7.9, w = 30 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 30*(7.9)^2 / 12 | Answer: 156 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 440 mm, clear cover 25 mm and main bars of diameter 16 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 440, c = 25, dia = 16 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 440 - 25 - 16/2 | Answer: 407 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 18.7 m^2 carrying a factored load of 14.1 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 18.7, w = 14.1 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 14.1 * 18.7 | Answer: 263.7 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 3.5 m, unit weight 19 kN/m^3, phi = 34 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 2.2 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 18 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 2.2, g = 18 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (18 - 9.81)*2.2 | Answer: 18.02 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 1.3e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1.2, area = 7.2e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 1.3, i = 1.2, A = 7.2 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (1.3e-4)*1.2*(7.2e-3) | Answer: 1123 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 2.4 m, bed slope 0.004 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.016. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 3.5 m under a head of 0.7 m. Taking Cd = 0.63 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 3.1 m wide carries a discharge of 26.7 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 430 m and design speed 90 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 430, V = 90 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (90)^2 / (127*430) | Answer: 0.1483
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: For a design speed of 45 km/h with allowable superelevation 0.05 and lateral friction 0.12, find the minimum curve radius in m.
A tank of volume 690 m^3 treats a flow of 110 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 690, Q = 110 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 690 / 110 | Answer: 6.273 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 370 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.16 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 8 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 370, k = 0.16, t = 8 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 370*(1 - e^(-0.16*8)) | Answer: 267.1 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.86, rainfall intensity 30 mm/h over a catchment of 44.6 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.86, i = 30, A = 44.6 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.86*30*44.6 / 360 | Answer: 3.196 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.04 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 150 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.04, M = 150 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 150*(20+0.04)/20 | Answer: 150.3 m

question: Convert the decimal number 139 to binary.
solution: Divide 139 by 2 repeatedly, recording remainders | Reading remainders in reverse gives 10001011 | Answer: 10001011 (binary)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 2 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the decimal number 2333 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 2333 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 91D (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 00111101 and 10111010.
solution: XOR: 10000111 | Count of 1s = 4 | Answer: 4
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 870 megabits is sent over a link of 66 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 870, B = 66 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 870 / 66 | Answer: 13.18 s

question: A link has bandwidth 41 Mbps and round-trip time 200 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 41, R = 200 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 41e6 * 200e-3 bits = 8200 kb | Answer: 8200 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.88, cache access time 2 ns and main-memory access time 80 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.88, tc = 2, tm = 80 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.88*2 + (1 - 0.88)*80 | Answer: 11.36 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 562916 elements?
solution: Given: n = 562916 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(562916)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: An O(n^2) algorithm performs c*n^2 basic operations. If c = 1 and n = 2430, how many operations are performed?
solution: Given: n = 2430 | Formula: operations = n^2 | Substitute: = (2430)^2 | Answer: 5904900

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.016, memory access time 80 ns and page-fault service time 8 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 8 ms = 8000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.016)*80 + 0.016*8000000.0 ns | Answer: 128.1 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 1 m^3 at 110 kPa and 570 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 1, P = 110, Tk = 570 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (110e3)*1 / (8.314*570) | Answer: 23.21 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.06 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 19 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.06, t = 19 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.06*19) | Answer: 0.6802

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.43 /min) is to reach 85% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.43, X = 85 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.85) / 0.43 | Answer: 4.412 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.49 /min) reaches 60% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.49, X = 60 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.6 / (0.49*(1 - 0.6)) | Answer: 3.061 min

question: For a reaction with A = 6e10 /s and activation energy 85 kJ/mol at 340 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 6, Ea = 85, Tk = 340 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 6e10 * exp(-85e3 / (8.314*340)) | Answer: 0.005236 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.97 and bottoms xW = 0.09, with relative volatility alpha = 2.6. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.97, xw = 0.09, al = 2.6 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.97/0.03)(0.91/0.09)] / ln(2.6) | Answer: 6.059 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.65 and x = 0.24. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.65, x = 0.24 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.65/0.35) / (0.24/0.76) | Answer: 5.881

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.63 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 55 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.63, Psat = 55 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.63 * 55 | Answer: 34.65 kPa

question: A stream of 0.9 kg/s with specific heat 2.5 kJ/kg-K is heated through 75 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 0.9, cp = 2.5, dT = 75 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 0.9*2.5*75 | Answer: 168.8 kW

question: A reactor of volume 3.2 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 0.2 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 3.2, Q = 0.2 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 3.2 / 0.2 | Answer: 16 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 8.7e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 3 mm with a concentration difference of 30 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
