solution: Given: D = 8.7, L = 3, dC = 30 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (8.7e-9)*30 / (3e-3) | Answer: 87 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 1.6 min and steady-state gain 2.3. For a step input of magnitude 13, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 1.6, K = 2.3, M = 13 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 2.3 * 13 | Answer: 29.9 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 60 m^2 flies at 120 m/s (air density 1.225 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.4. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 60, V = 120, rho = 1.225, CL = 0.4 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1.225*(120)^2*60*0.4 / 1000 | Answer: 211.7 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 55 m^2 flies at 190 m/s (density 0.7 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.1. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 55, V = 190, rho = 0.7, CD = 0.1 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.7*(190)^2*55*0.1 / 1000 | Answer: 69.49 kN

question: A specimen under stress 280 MPa shows an elastic strain of 1.8e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 280, eps = 1.8 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 280 / (1.8e-3) MPa = 155.6 GPa | Answer: 155.6 GPa

question: A block of mass 30 kg has a volume of 1.1e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 30, V = 1.1 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 30 / (1.1e-3) | Answer: 27273 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 2700 mm is heated through 85 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 11e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 2700, dT = 85, al = 11 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 2700*11e-6*85 | Answer: 2.525 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 135 ohm, R2 = 130 ohm and R3 = 335 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 135, R2 = 130, R3 = 335 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 130*335 / 135 | Answer: 322.6 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 120 ohm and gauge factor 2.1 experiences a strain of 1700e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 120, GF = 2.1, eps = 1700 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 120*2.1*1700e-6 | Answer: 428.4 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 9.95 when the true value is 10. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.95, true = 10 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.95 - 10| / 10 * 100 | Answer: 0.5 %

question: Annual demand is 20500 units, ordering cost 70 per order and holding cost 6 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 20500, S = 70, H = 6 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*20500*70 / 6) | Answer: 691.6 units

question: An asset costs 130000 with salvage value 12000 after 7 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 130000, Sv = 12000, n = 7 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (130000 - 12000) / 7 | Answer: 16857 per year

question: A product sells for 480 per unit with variable cost 170 per unit and fixed costs 180000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 480, V = 170, F = 180000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 180000 / (480 - 170) | Answer: 580.6 units

question: Find the present worth of 95000 received 4 years from now at an interest rate of 5% per year.
solution: Given: F = 95000, n = 4, i = 5 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 95000 / (1 + 0.05)^4 | Answer: 78157 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.98, 0.91 and 0.93 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.98, r2 = 0.91, r3 = 0.93 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.98*0.91*0.93 | Answer: 0.8294

question: A process produces 9 defective items in a batch of 5500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 9, N = 5500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 9/5500 * 1e6 | Answer: 1636 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = 2x^3 + 8x - 1 evaluated at x = -5.
For f(x) = 3x^3 - x^2 + 3x + 7, find f''(x) at x = 0.
Evaluate the definite integral of (-2x^2 - x) dx from x = -1 to x = 7.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = -2x^3/3 + -1x^2/2 + 0x | Evaluate F(7) - F(-1) | Answer: -253.3
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 5x^2 - 7x = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[-9, -3], [8, -3]].
solution: Given: a = -9, b = -3, c = 8, d = -3 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (-9)(-3) - (-3)(8) | Answer: 51

question: Find the determinant of [[0, 1, 1], [2, -6, 4], [-3, 2, 0]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: -26

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[-7, -8], [-4, 6]].
solution: Trace tr = -1, Determinant = -74 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 8.117

question: Solve for x: 2x + -2y = 4 and -1x + -5y = 6.
solution: Determinant = 2*-5 - -2*-1 = -12 | x = (e d - b f) / det = 0.6667 | Answer: x = 0.6667
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 14, 31, 35, 87, 3.
solution: Sum = 170 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 34 | Answer: 34

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 2, 26, 40, 27, 31.
solution: Mean = 25.2 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 14.1

question: Find the slope of the line through (-7, 8) and (7, -9).
solution: Given: x1 = -7, y1 = 8, x2 = 7, y2 = -9 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (-9 - 8) / (7 - -7) | Answer: -1.214

question: Find the distance between the points (-5, 6) and (-4, -8).
solution: Given: x1 = -5, y1 = 6, x2 = -4, y2 = -8 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((1)^2 + (-14)^2) | Answer: 14.04 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (-5,2), (4,5), (-1,8).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 21 sq units

question: Find the 39th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -18 and common difference -6.
solution: Given: a = -18, d = -6, n = 39 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -18 + (39 - 1)*-6 | Answer: -246

question: Find the sum of the first 7 terms of an AP with first term 6 and common difference 7.
solution: Given: a = 6, d = 7, n = 7 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 7/2 [2*6 + (7-1)*7] | Answer: 189

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 8500 at 11.7% per annum for 4 years.
solution: Given: P = 8500, R = 11.7, Tt = 4 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 8500 * 11.7 * 4 / 100 | Answer: 3978 currency units

question: Find the amount when 38500 is invested at 11.7% per annum compounded annually for 4 years.
solution: Given: P = 38500, R = 11.7, Tt = 4 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 38500 * (1 + 11.7/100)^4 | Answer: 59934 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (-1, -7, 2) and (-2, -4, 4).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (-2, 2, -2) and (-2, -2, 0).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 9.798

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (-2, 3, -1) and (2, -5, -6).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 115.5 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number 2 + 10i.
solution: Given: a = 2, b = 10 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((2)^2 + (10)^2) | Answer: 10.2

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number 11 + 8i.
solution: Given: a = 11, b = 8 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(8, 11) | Answer: 36.03 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -x^3 - 7x^2 - 3x + 3 at x = 1.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-163 with initial guess x0=2, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=0.8 and ordinates 6, 6, 4, 7, 3, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 125 and 437.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 125 and 437 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 16 and 25.
solution: Given: a = 16, b = 25 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 16*25 / 1 | Answer: 400
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 11 mm carries an axial tensile load of 98 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 36 mm and length 600 mm carries an axial load of 14 kN. Take E = 70 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 33 mm transmits a torque of 2500 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 33, Tt = 2500 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(2500*1000) / (pi*(33)^3) | Answer: 354.3 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 44 mm and length 1100 mm carries a torque of 600 N-m. With G = 45 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (44)^4 / 32 = 367968 mm^4 | theta = (600*1000)(1100) / (45000 * 367968) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 2.284 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 109 mm wide and 240 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 109, h = 240 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 109*(240)^2 / 6 | Answer: 1046400 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (81 mm x 110 mm) carries a bending moment of 36 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (62 mm x 150 mm) has effective length 3200 mm and E = 200 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 710 MPa is designed for a working stress of 70 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 710, sw = 70 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 710 / 70 | Answer: 10.14

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 400 mm and wall thickness 18 mm carries an internal pressure of 2.4 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 400, t = 18, P = 2.4 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 2.4*400 / (2*18) | Answer: 26.67 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 1080 K and 320 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 1080, Tc = 320 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 320/1080) * 100 | Answer: 70.37 %

question: A refrigerator works between 267 K (cold) and 310 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 267, Th = 310 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 267 / (310 - 267) | Answer: 6.209

question: A heat pump operates between 260 K and 332 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 260, Th = 332 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 332 / (332 - 260) | Answer: 4.611

question: 2.7 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 185 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.7, dT = 185 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 2.7 * 0.718 * 185 | Answer: 358.6 kJ

question: 3.3 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 200 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.3, dT = 200 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 3.3 * 1.005 * 200 | Answer: 663.3 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 3.8 m^3 at 550 K with mass 5.7 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 3.8, Tk = 550, m = 5.7 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 5.7*0.287*550 / 3.8 | Answer: 236.8 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 3.9 kg of air expands isothermally at 350 K from volume V1 to 4*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.9, Tk = 350, ratio = 4 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 3.9*0.287*350*ln(4) | Answer: 543.1 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 0.9 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.14 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 0.9, D = 0.14 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*0.9*0.14 / 0.001 | Answer: 126000

question: Water flows at 3.9 m/s through a pipe of diameter 50 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 27.5 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 27.5 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*27.5 / 1000 | Answer: 269.8 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 1.5 m. Taking Cv = 0.97, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 1.5, cv = 0.97 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.97*sqrt(2*9.81*1.5) | Answer: 5.262 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 320 mm) water flows at 1.9 m/s. It contracts to diameter 110 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
Water flows at 1.2 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.38 m and length 380 m. With friction factor f = 0.026, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 29 teeth drives a gear of 109 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1500 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 29, z2 = 109, N1 = 1500 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1500*29 / 109 | Answer: 399.1 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 530 mm rotates at 1200 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 530, N = 1200 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.53)*1200 / 60 | Answer: 33.3 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 37 kW at 250 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 37, N = 250 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(37*1000) / (2*pi*250) | Answer: 1413 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 8.6 kg rotates at radius 0.29 m at 500 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 8000 N/m and mass 19.5 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 8000, m = 19.5 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(8000/19.5) | Answer: 3.224 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 5.6 m^2 and thickness 0.14 m has conductivity k = 18.2 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 85 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 5.6, L = 0.14, k = 18.2, dT = 85 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 18.2*5.6*85 / 0.14 | Answer: 61880 W

question: A surface of area 1.7 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 105 W/m^2-K to surroundings 140 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 1.7, h = 105, dT = 140 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 105*1.7*140 | Answer: 24990 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 240 m/min, feed = 0.12 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 240, f = 0.12, d = 2 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*240*0.12*2 | Answer: 57600 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 460 mm is turned at 200 rpm with a feed of 0.23 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 460, N = 200, f = 0.23 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 460 / (0.23*200) | Answer: 10 min

question: A resistor of 71 ohm carries a current of 9.9 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 71, I = 9.9 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 9.9 * 71 | Answer: 702.9 V

question: Three resistors 12 ohm, 53 ohm and 2 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 12, R2 = 53, R3 = 2 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 12 + 53 + 2 | Answer: 67 ohm

question: Two resistors 40 ohm and 21 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 40, R2 = 21 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 40*21 / (40+21) | Answer: 13.77 ohm

question: A device draws 11.2 A at 230 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 230, I = 11.2 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 230 * 11.2 | Answer: 2576 W

question: A current of 11 A flows through a 59 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 11, R = 59 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (11)^2 * 59 | Answer: 7139 W

question: Two capacitors 17.7 uF and 3.1 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 17.7, C2 = 3.1 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 17.7*3.1 / (17.7+3.1) | Answer: 2.638 uF

question: A resistor 81 kohm and capacitor 0.2 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 81, C = 0.2 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (81k)(0.2u) = 16.2 ms | Answer: 16.2 ms

question: An inductor 30.9 mH is in series with 104 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 30.9, R = 104 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (30.9e-3) / 104 | Answer: 0.2971 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 98.7 mH inductor at 140 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 98.7, f = 140 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (140)(98.7e-3) | Answer: 86.82 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 23.5 uF capacitor at 980 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 23.5, f = 980 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (980)(23.5e-6)) | Answer: 6.911 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 27 ohm, XL = 17 ohm and XC = 50 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 27, XL = 17, XC = 50 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(27^2 + (17 - 50)^2) | Answer: 42.64 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 94.1 mH and C = 8.7 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 94.1, C = 8.7 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(94.1e-3 * 8.7e-6)) | Answer: 175.9 Hz

question: A capacitor of 9.4 uF is charged to 360 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 9.4, V = 360 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*9.4e-6*(360)^2 | Answer: 609.1 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 110 V with 370 primary turns and 330 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 110, N1 = 370, N2 = 330 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 110 * 330/370 | Answer: 98.11 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 230 V and draws an armature current of 18 A. If the armature resistance is 0.33 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 230, Ia = 18, Ra = 0.33 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 230 - 18*0.33 | Answer: 224.1 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 110 A at 433 V (line) with a power factor of 0.95. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 110, VL = 433, pf = 0.95 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*433*110*0.95 / 1000 | Answer: 78.37 kW

question: A load has real power 70 kW and apparent power 155 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 70, S = 155 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 70 / 155 | Answer: 0.4516

question: A machine delivers 115 kW output while drawing 142 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 115, Pi = 142 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 115/142 * 100 | Answer: 80.99 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 30 V across R1 = 35 ohm and R2 = 26 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 30, R1 = 35, R2 = 26 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 30*26 / (35+26) | Answer: 12.79 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 130 kohm and Rin = 20 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 130, Rin = 20 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 130 / 20 | Answer: 6.5

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 160 kohm and Rg = 30 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 160, Rg = 30 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 160/30 | Answer: 6.333

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 9203. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 9203 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(9203) | Answer: 39.64 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 7.8 m carries a central point load of 30 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7.8, W = 30 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 30*7.8 / 4 | Answer: 58.5 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.3 m carries a UDL of 55 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6.3, w = 55 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 55*(6.3)^2 / 8 | Answer: 272.9 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 2.5 m carries a point load 70 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 2.5, W = 70 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 70*2.5 | Answer: 175 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 4.6 m carries a UDL of 22 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.6, w = 22 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 22*(4.6)^2 / 2 | Answer: 232.8 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.7 m carries a point load 30 kN at distance 3.2 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 6.7, a = 3.2, W = 30 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 30*(6.7 - 3.2) / 6.7 | Answer: 15.67 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 6.3 m) carries a central point load 80 kN. With E = 200 GPa and I = 150e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=80000 N, L=6300.0 mm, E=200000 MPa, I=150e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 13.89 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 4.6 m carries a UDL of 30 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.6, w = 30 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 30*(4.6)^2 / 12 | Answer: 52.9 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 610 mm, clear cover 45 mm and main bars of diameter 12 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 610, c = 45, dia = 12 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 610 - 45 - 12/2 | Answer: 559 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 34.1 m^2 carrying a factored load of 11.8 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 34.1, w = 11.8 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 11.8 * 34.1 | Answer: 402.4 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 6.8 m, unit weight 20 kN/m^3, phi = 30 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 7.5 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 18 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 7.5, g = 18 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (18 - 9.81)*7.5 | Answer: 61.42 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 2.9e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.8, area = 6.2e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 2.9, i = 0.8, A = 6.2 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (2.9e-4)*0.8*(6.2e-3) | Answer: 1438 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 2.3 m, bed slope 0.008 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.022. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 2.7 m under a head of 0.2 m. Taking Cd = 0.61 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 5 m wide carries a discharge of 27.5 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 110 m and design speed 60 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 110, V = 60 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (60)^2 / (127*110) | Answer: 0.2577
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: For a design speed of 75 km/h with allowable superelevation 0.08 and lateral friction 0.12, find the minimum curve radius in m.
A tank of volume 660 m^3 treats a flow of 135 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 660, Q = 135 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 660 / 135 | Answer: 4.889 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 400 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.17 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 7 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 400, k = 0.17, t = 7 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 400*(1 - e^(-0.17*7)) | Answer: 278.3 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.79, rainfall intensity 35 mm/h over a catchment of 44.7 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.79, i = 35, A = 44.7 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.79*35*44.7 / 360 | Answer: 3.433 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.02 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 720 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.02, M = 720 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 720*(30+0.02)/30 | Answer: 720.5 m

question: Convert the decimal number 984 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 984 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 3D8 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 10110011 and 01111001.
solution: XOR: 11001010 | Count of 1s = 4 | Answer: 4
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 290 megabits is sent over a link of 94 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 290, B = 94 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 290 / 94 | Answer: 3.085 s

question: A link has bandwidth 79 Mbps and round-trip time 20 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 79, R = 20 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 79e6 * 20e-3 bits = 1580 kb | Answer: 1580 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.82, cache access time 3 ns and main-memory access time 50 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.82, tc = 3, tm = 50 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.82*3 + (1 - 0.82)*50 | Answer: 11.46 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 768386 elements?
solution: Given: n = 768386 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(768386)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: An O(n^2) algorithm performs c*n^2 basic operations. If c = 1 and n = 2190, how many operations are performed?
solution: Given: n = 2190 | Formula: operations = n^2 | Substitute: = (2190)^2 | Answer: 4796100

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.012, memory access time 160 ns and page-fault service time 3 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 3 ms = 3000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.012)*160 + 0.012*3000000.0 ns | Answer: 36.16 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 1.8 m^3 at 150 kPa and 300 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 1.8, P = 150, Tk = 300 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (150e3)*1.8 / (8.314*300) | Answer: 108.3 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.39 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 17 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.39, t = 17 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.39*17) | Answer: 0.9987

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.13 /min) is to reach 50% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.13, X = 50 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.5) / 0.13 | Answer: 5.332 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.39 /min) reaches 70% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.39, X = 70 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.7 / (0.39*(1 - 0.7)) | Answer: 5.983 min

question: For a reaction with A = 4e10 /s and activation energy 75 kJ/mol at 330 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 4, Ea = 75, Tk = 330 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 4e10 * exp(-75e3 / (8.314*330)) | Answer: 0.05372 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.97 and bottoms xW = 0.07, with relative volatility alpha = 3.4. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.97, xw = 0.07, al = 3.4 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.97/0.03)(0.93/0.07)] / ln(3.4) | Answer: 4.954 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.81 and x = 0.45. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.81, x = 0.45 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.81/0.19) / (0.45/0.55) | Answer: 5.211

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.71 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 90 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.71, Psat = 90 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.71 * 90 | Answer: 63.9 kPa

question: A stream of 7.4 kg/s with specific heat 3.4 kJ/kg-K is heated through 55 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 7.4, cp = 3.4, dT = 55 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 7.4*3.4*55 | Answer: 1384 kW

question: A reactor of volume 12.2 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 4.4 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 12.2, Q = 4.4 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 12.2 / 4.4 | Answer: 2.773 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 1.5e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 5 mm with a concentration difference of 30 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 1.5, L = 5, dC = 30 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (1.5e-9)*30 / (5e-3) | Answer: 9 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 6.6 min and steady-state gain 2.6. For a step input of magnitude 4, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 6.6, K = 2.6, M = 4 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 2.6 * 4 | Answer: 10.4 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 90 m^2 flies at 260 m/s (air density 0.7 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 1.2. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 90, V = 260, rho = 0.7, CL = 1.2 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.7*(260)^2*90*1.2 / 1000 | Answer: 2555 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 15 m^2 flies at 170 m/s (density 1 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.08. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 15, V = 170, rho = 1, CD = 0.08 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*1*(170)^2*15*0.08 / 1000 | Answer: 17.34 kN

question: A specimen under stress 310 MPa shows an elastic strain of 0.6e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 310, eps = 0.6 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 310 / (0.6e-3) MPa = 516.7 GPa | Answer: 516.7 GPa

question: A block of mass 26 kg has a volume of 3.2e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 26, V = 3.2 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 26 / (3.2e-3) | Answer: 8125 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 3000 mm is heated through 105 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 11e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 3000, dT = 105, al = 11 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 3000*11e-6*105 | Answer: 3.465 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 80 ohm, R2 = 195 ohm and R3 = 315 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 80, R2 = 195, R3 = 315 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 195*315 / 80 | Answer: 767.8 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 1000 ohm and gauge factor 2.1 experiences a strain of 1700e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 1000, GF = 2.1, eps = 1700 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 1000*2.1*1700e-6 | Answer: 3570 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 9.96 when the true value is 20. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.96, true = 20 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.96 - 20| / 20 * 100 | Answer: 50.2 %

question: Annual demand is 25500 units, ordering cost 40 per order and holding cost 2 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 25500, S = 40, H = 2 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*25500*40 / 2) | Answer: 101 units

question: An asset costs 310000 with salvage value 12000 after 16 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 310000, Sv = 12000, n = 16 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (310000 - 12000) / 16 | Answer: 18625 per year

question: A product sells for 420 per unit with variable cost 170 per unit and fixed costs 105000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 420, V = 170, F = 105000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 105000 / (420 - 170) | Answer: 420 units

question: Find the present worth of 95000 received 7 years from now at an interest rate of 11% per year.
solution: Given: F = 95000, n = 7, i = 11 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 95000 / (1 + 0.11)^7 | Answer: 45758 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.95, 0.97 and 0.96 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.95, r2 = 0.97, r3 = 0.96 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.95*0.97*0.96 | Answer: 0.8846

question: A process produces 48 defective items in a batch of 1500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 48, N = 1500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 48/1500 * 1e6 | Answer: 32000 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = 2x^3 - 4x^2 + 2x + 3 evaluated at x = 5.
For f(x) = -6x^3 - 4x^2 + 6x - 8, find f''(x) at x = -1.
Evaluate the definite integral of (-5x^2 - x - 3) dx from x = -2 to x = 4.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = -5x^3/3 + -1x^2/2 + -3x | Evaluate F(4) - F(-2) | Answer: -144
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of x^2 + 8x - 4 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[2, -3], [3, -9]].
solution: Given: a = 2, b = -3, c = 3, d = -9 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (2)(-9) - (-3)(3) | Answer: -9

question: Find the determinant of [[-2, -3, -4], [3, 0, 4], [-1, -2, 5]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: 65

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[-4, 3], [-8, 8]].
solution: Trace tr = 4, Determinant = -8 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 5.464

question: Solve for x: 6x + -1y = -7 and 1x + -5y = 4.
solution: Determinant = 6*-5 - -1*1 = -29 | x = (e d - b f) / det = -1.345 | Answer: x = -1.345
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 36, 15, 56, 34, 100.
solution: Sum = 241 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 48.2 | Answer: 48.2

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 32, 41, 9, 30, 38.
solution: Mean = 30 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 12.55

question: Find the slope of the line through (5, -2) and (-5, -8).
solution: Given: x1 = 5, y1 = -2, x2 = -5, y2 = -8 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (-8 - -2) / (-5 - 5) | Answer: 0.6

question: Find the distance between the points (-2, 9) and (1, 5).
solution: Given: x1 = -2, y1 = 9, x2 = 1, y2 = 5 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((3)^2 + (-4)^2) | Answer: 5 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (-7,-4), (-6,-3), (1,7).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 1.5 sq units

question: Find the 7th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 1 and common difference 3.
solution: Given: a = 1, d = 3, n = 7 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = 1 + (7 - 1)*3 | Answer: 19

question: Find the sum of the first 5 terms of an AP with first term -12 and common difference -6.
solution: Given: a = -12, d = -6, n = 5 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 5/2 [2*-12 + (5-1)*-6] | Answer: -120

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 34500 at 8.5% per annum for 3 years.
solution: Given: P = 34500, R = 8.5, Tt = 3 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 34500 * 8.5 * 3 / 100 | Answer: 8798 currency units

question: Find the amount when 2500 is invested at 11.1% per annum compounded annually for 3 years.
solution: Given: P = 2500, R = 11.1, Tt = 3 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 2500 * (1 + 11.1/100)^3 | Answer: 3428 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (0, -3, 8) and (4, -4, -3).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (2, -4, -4) and (3, -1, 6).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 38.21

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (-4, 5, -1) and (-1, -3, 5).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 114.7 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number -11 + -9i.
solution: Given: a = -11, b = -9 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((-11)^2 + (-9)^2) | Answer: 14.21

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number 3 + 1i.
solution: Given: a = 3, b = 1 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(1, 3) | Answer: 18.43 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = 2x^3 + 4x^2 - 6x - 1 at x = -1.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-92 with initial guess x0=9, find x1 (one iteration).
solution: Given: N = 92, x0 = 9 | Formula: x1 = x0 - (x0^2 - N)/(2 x0) | Substitute: x1 = 9 - ((9)^2 - 92)/(2*9) | Answer: 9.611

question: Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.8 and ordinates 17, 9, 20, 16, 2, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 187 and 553.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 187 and 553 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 10 and 15.
solution: Given: a = 10, b = 15 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 10*15 / 5 | Answer: 30
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 23 mm carries an axial tensile load of 99 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 21 mm and length 2800 mm carries an axial load of 74 kN. Take E = 200 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 75 mm transmits a torque of 1900 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 75, Tt = 1900 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(1900*1000) / (pi*(75)^3) | Answer: 22.94 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 44 mm and length 900 mm carries a torque of 450 N-m. With G = 77 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (44)^4 / 32 = 367968 mm^4 | theta = (450*1000)(900) / (77000 * 367968) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 0.819 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 138 mm wide and 140 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 138, h = 140 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 138*(140)^2 / 6 | Answer: 450800 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (85 mm x 240 mm) carries a bending moment of 35 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (50 mm x 160 mm) has effective length 1500 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 500 MPa is designed for a working stress of 70 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 500, sw = 70 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 500 / 70 | Answer: 7.143

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1500 mm and wall thickness 7 mm carries an internal pressure of 0.7 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1500, t = 7, P = 0.7 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 0.7*1500 / (2*7) | Answer: 75 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 800 K and 340 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 800, Tc = 340 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 340/800) * 100 | Answer: 57.5 %

question: A refrigerator works between 267 K (cold) and 322 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 267, Th = 322 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 267 / (322 - 267) | Answer: 4.855

question: A heat pump operates between 274 K and 322 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 274, Th = 322 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 322 / (322 - 274) | Answer: 6.708

question: 3.7 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 175 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.7, dT = 175 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 3.7 * 0.718 * 175 | Answer: 464.9 kJ

question: 1 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 200 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1, dT = 200 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 1 * 1.005 * 200 | Answer: 201 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 1.5 m^3 at 440 K with mass 2.3 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 1.5, Tk = 440, m = 2.3 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 2.3*0.287*440 / 1.5 | Answer: 193.6 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 3.9 kg of air expands isothermally at 340 K from volume V1 to 2*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.9, Tk = 340, ratio = 2 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 3.9*0.287*340*ln(2) | Answer: 263.8 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 1.9 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.27 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 1.9, D = 0.27 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*1.9*0.27 / 0.001 | Answer: 513000

question: Water flows at 1.3 m/s through a pipe of diameter 70 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 18.4 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 18.4 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*18.4 / 1000 | Answer: 180.5 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 12.7 m. Taking Cv = 0.99, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 12.7, cv = 0.99 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.99*sqrt(2*9.81*12.7) | Answer: 15.63 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 160 mm) water flows at 2.9 m/s. It contracts to diameter 60 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 160, d2 = 60, V1 = 2.9 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 2.9*(160/60)^2 | Answer: 20.62 m/s

question: Water flows at 1.9 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.34 m and length 310 m. With friction factor f = 0.03, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 37 teeth drives a gear of 50 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1400 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 37, z2 = 50, N1 = 1400 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1400*37 / 50 | Answer: 1036 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 180 mm rotates at 1000 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 180, N = 1000 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.18)*1000 / 60 | Answer: 9.425 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 29.2 kW at 500 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 29.2, N = 500 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(29.2*1000) / (2*pi*500) | Answer: 557.7 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 2.7 kg rotates at radius 0.45 m at 600 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 5600 N/m and mass 8 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 5600, m = 8 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(5600/8) | Answer: 4.211 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 7.1 m^2 and thickness 0.18 m has conductivity k = 36.3 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 60 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 7.1, L = 0.18, k = 36.3, dT = 60 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 36.3*7.1*60 / 0.18 | Answer: 85910 W

question: A surface of area 2.7 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 80 W/m^2-K to surroundings 25 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 2.7, h = 80, dT = 25 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 80*2.7*25 | Answer: 5400 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 190 m/min, feed = 0.2 mm/rev, depth of cut = 1.4 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 190, f = 0.2, d = 1.4 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*190*0.2*1.4 | Answer: 53200 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 180 mm is turned at 600 rpm with a feed of 0.32 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 180, N = 600, f = 0.32 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 180 / (0.32*600) | Answer: 0.9375 min

question: A resistor of 95 ohm carries a current of 5.9 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 95, I = 5.9 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 5.9 * 95 | Answer: 560.5 V

question: Three resistors 14 ohm, 98 ohm and 86 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 14, R2 = 98, R3 = 86 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 14 + 98 + 86 | Answer: 198 ohm

question: Two resistors 75 ohm and 93 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 75, R2 = 93 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 75*93 / (75+93) | Answer: 41.52 ohm

question: A device draws 7.4 A at 220 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 220, I = 7.4 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 220 * 7.4 | Answer: 1628 W

question: A current of 10.1 A flows through a 34 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 10.1, R = 34 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (10.1)^2 * 34 | Answer: 3468 W

question: Two capacitors 22 uF and 7.7 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 22, C2 = 7.7 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 22*7.7 / (22+7.7) | Answer: 5.704 uF

question: A resistor 30 kohm and capacitor 5 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 30, C = 5 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (30k)(5u) = 150 ms | Answer: 150 ms

question: An inductor 238.8 mH is in series with 147 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 238.8, R = 147 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (238.8e-3) / 147 | Answer: 1.624 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 139.1 mH inductor at 590 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 139.1, f = 590 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (590)(139.1e-3) | Answer: 515.7 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 38 uF capacitor at 200 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 38, f = 200 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (200)(38e-6)) | Answer: 20.94 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 65 ohm, XL = 58 ohm and XC = 27 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 65, XL = 58, XC = 27 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(65^2 + (58 - 27)^2) | Answer: 72.01 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 11.9 mH and C = 2.2 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 11.9, C = 2.2 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(11.9e-3 * 2.2e-6)) | Answer: 983.6 Hz

question: A capacitor of 44.1 uF is charged to 200 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 44.1, V = 200 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*44.1e-6*(200)^2 | Answer: 882 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 370 V with 700 primary turns and 110 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 370, N1 = 700, N2 = 110 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 370 * 110/700 | Answer: 58.14 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 230 V and draws an armature current of 22 A. If the armature resistance is 0.19 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 230, Ia = 22, Ra = 0.19 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 230 - 22*0.19 | Answer: 225.8 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 40 A at 415 V (line) with a power factor of 0.75. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 40, VL = 415, pf = 0.75 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*415*40*0.75 / 1000 | Answer: 21.56 kW

question: A load has real power 10 kW and apparent power 70 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 10, S = 70 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 10 / 70 | Answer: 0.1429

question: A machine delivers 65 kW output while drawing 177 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 65, Pi = 177 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 65/177 * 100 | Answer: 36.72 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 29 V across R1 = 29 ohm and R2 = 20 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 29, R1 = 29, R2 = 20 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 29*20 / (29+20) | Answer: 11.84 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 50 kohm and Rin = 44 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 50, Rin = 44 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 50 / 44 | Answer: 1.136

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 90 kohm and Rg = 35 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 90, Rg = 35 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 90/35 | Answer: 3.571

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 2443. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 2443 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(2443) | Answer: 33.88 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 7.2 m carries a central point load of 110 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7.2, W = 110 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 110*7.2 / 4 | Answer: 198 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 8.9 m carries a UDL of 5 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 8.9, w = 5 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 5*(8.9)^2 / 8 | Answer: 49.51 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 4.8 m carries a point load 70 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.8, W = 70 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 70*4.8 | Answer: 336 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 3.4 m carries a UDL of 4 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.4, w = 4 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 4*(3.4)^2 / 2 | Answer: 23.12 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 5.2 m carries a point load 35 kN at distance 3.6 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 5.2, a = 3.6, W = 35 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 35*(5.2 - 3.6) / 5.2 | Answer: 10.77 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 7.5 m) carries a central point load 35 kN. With E = 30 GPa and I = 260e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=35000 N, L=7500.0 mm, E=30000 MPa, I=260e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 39.44 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 5 m carries a UDL of 6 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5, w = 6 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 6*(5)^2 / 12 | Answer: 12.5 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 500 mm, clear cover 35 mm and main bars of diameter 16 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 500, c = 35, dia = 16 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 500 - 35 - 16/2 | Answer: 457 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 13.9 m^2 carrying a factored load of 11.4 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 13.9, w = 11.4 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 11.4 * 13.9 | Answer: 158.5 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 5.3 m, unit weight 19 kN/m^3, phi = 34 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 5 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 21 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 5, g = 21 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (21 - 9.81)*5 | Answer: 55.95 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 8.8e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.4, area = 2e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 8.8, i = 0.4, A = 2 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (8.8e-4)*0.4*(2e-3) | Answer: 704 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.1 m, bed slope 0.004 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.015. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 2.6 m under a head of 1 m. Taking Cd = 0.61 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 5.5 m wide carries a discharge of 20.2 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 170 m and design speed 95 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 170, V = 95 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (95)^2 / (127*170) | Answer: 0.418
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: For a design speed of 50 km/h with allowable superelevation 0.06 and lateral friction 0.13, find the minimum curve radius in m.
A tank of volume 920 m^3 treats a flow of 65 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 920, Q = 65 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 920 / 65 | Answer: 14.15 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 280 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.35 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 3 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 280, k = 0.35, t = 3 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 280*(1 - e^(-0.35*3)) | Answer: 182 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.88, rainfall intensity 90 mm/h over a catchment of 10 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.88, i = 90, A = 10 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.88*90*10 / 360 | Answer: 2.2 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.02 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 710 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.02, M = 710 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 710*(20+0.02)/20 | Answer: 710.7 m

question: Convert the decimal number 1375 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 1375 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 55F (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the 8-bit binary number 10101010 to decimal.
solution: Binary 10101010 = sum of bit-weights | Answer: 170 (decimal)
formula: Sum each bit times its positional weight (2^i)

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 01110001 and 00001100.
solution: XOR: 01111101 | Count of 1s = 6 | Answer: 6
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 620 megabits is sent over a link of 84 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 620, B = 84 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 620 / 84 | Answer: 7.381 s

question: A link has bandwidth 4 Mbps and round-trip time 120 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 4, R = 120 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 4e6 * 120e-3 bits = 480 kb | Answer: 480 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.96, cache access time 3 ns and main-memory access time 150 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.96, tc = 3, tm = 150 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.96*3 + (1 - 0.96)*150 | Answer: 8.88 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 640682 elements?
solution: Given: n = 640682 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(640682)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.002, memory access time 160 ns and page-fault service time 3 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 3 ms = 3000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.002)*160 + 0.002*3000000.0 ns | Answer: 6.16 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 0.6 m^3 at 330 kPa and 550 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 0.6, P = 330, Tk = 550 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (330e3)*0.6 / (8.314*550) | Answer: 43.3 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.24 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 19 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.24, t = 19 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.24*19) | Answer: 0.9895

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.21 /min) is to reach 60% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.21, X = 60 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.6) / 0.21 | Answer: 4.363 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.16 /min) reaches 85% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.16, X = 85 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.85 / (0.16*(1 - 0.85)) | Answer: 35.42 min

question: For a reaction with A = 3e10 /s and activation energy 65 kJ/mol at 490 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 3, Ea = 65, Tk = 490 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 3e10 * exp(-65e3 / (8.314*490)) | Answer: 353 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.98 and bottoms xW = 0.1, with relative volatility alpha = 2.7. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.98, xw = 0.1, al = 2.7 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.98/0.02)(0.9/0.1)] / ln(2.7) | Answer: 6.13 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.84 and x = 0.41. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.84, x = 0.41 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.84/0.16) / (0.41/0.59) | Answer: 7.555

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.56 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 100 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.56, Psat = 100 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.56 * 100 | Answer: 56 kPa

question: A stream of 0.9 kg/s with specific heat 4.1 kJ/kg-K is heated through 115 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 0.9, cp = 4.1, dT = 115 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 0.9*4.1*115 | Answer: 424.3 kW

question: A reactor of volume 10.6 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 4.9 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 10.6, Q = 4.9 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 10.6 / 4.9 | Answer: 2.163 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 4.6e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 2 mm with a concentration difference of 120 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 4.6, L = 2, dC = 120 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (4.6e-9)*120 / (2e-3) | Answer: 276 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 1.8 min and steady-state gain 1. For a step input of magnitude 7, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 1.8, K = 1, M = 7 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 1 * 7 | Answer: 7 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 30 m^2 flies at 80 m/s (air density 1 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 1.2. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 30, V = 80, rho = 1, CL = 1.2 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1*(80)^2*30*1.2 / 1000 | Answer: 115.2 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 45 m^2 flies at 250 m/s (density 1.225 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.08. Find the drag force in kN.
A specimen under stress 140 MPa shows an elastic strain of 2.1e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 140, eps = 2.1 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 140 / (2.1e-3) MPa = 66.67 GPa | Answer: 66.67 GPa

question: A block of mass 40 kg has a volume of 0.8e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 40, V = 0.8 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 40 / (0.8e-3) | Answer: 50000 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 1200 mm is heated through 105 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 12e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 1200, dT = 105, al = 12 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 1200*12e-6*105 | Answer: 1.512 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 20 ohm, R2 = 200 ohm and R3 = 95 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 20, R2 = 200, R3 = 95 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 200*95 / 20 | Answer: 950 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 120 ohm and gauge factor 2.1 experiences a strain of 2000e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 120, GF = 2.1, eps = 2000 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 120*2.1*2000e-6 | Answer: 504 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 10 when the true value is 100. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10, true = 100 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10 - 100| / 100 * 100 | Answer: 90 %

question: Annual demand is 30000 units, ordering cost 190 per order and holding cost 40 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 30000, S = 190, H = 40 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*30000*190 / 40) | Answer: 533.9 units

question: An asset costs 380000 with salvage value 10000 after 20 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 380000, Sv = 10000, n = 20 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (380000 - 10000) / 20 | Answer: 18500 per year

question: A product sells for 200 per unit with variable cost 70 per unit and fixed costs 40000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 200, V = 70, F = 40000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 40000 / (200 - 70) | Answer: 307.7 units

question: Find the present worth of 135000 received 9 years from now at an interest rate of 9% per year.
solution: Given: F = 135000, n = 9, i = 9 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 135000 / (1 + 0.09)^9 | Answer: 62158 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.96, 0.97 and 0.91 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.96, r2 = 0.97, r3 = 0.91 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.96*0.97*0.91 | Answer: 0.8474

question: A process produces 37 defective items in a batch of 13500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 37, N = 13500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 37/13500 * 1e6 | Answer: 2741 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -4x^3 + 7x^2 - 2x - 3 evaluated at x = 4.
For f(x) = -4x^3 - 2x^2 + x + 6, find f''(x) at x = 4.
Evaluate the definite integral of (-4x^2 - 2x - 8) dx from x = 2 to x = 5.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = -4x^3/3 + -2x^2/2 + -8x | Evaluate F(5) - F(2) | Answer: -201
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 3x^2 - x - 2 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[-1, -8], [-1, 3]].
solution: Given: a = -1, b = -8, c = -1, d = 3 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (-1)(3) - (-8)(-1) | Answer: -11

question: Find the determinant of [[-6, -6, 3], [1, -4, -4], [5, 6, 0]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: 54

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[5, 5], [7, 4]].
solution: Trace tr = 9, Determinant = -15 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 10.44

question: Solve for x: 1x + -5y = -6 and 6x + -1y = 2.
solution: Determinant = 1*-1 - -5*6 = 29 | x = (e d - b f) / det = 0.5517 | Answer: x = 0.5517
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 81, 23, 85, 100, 98.
solution: Sum = 387 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 77.4 | Answer: 77.4

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 40, 11, 34, 18, 13.
solution: Mean = 23.2 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 13.03

question: Find the slope of the line through (-3, 5) and (8, -2).
solution: Given: x1 = -3, y1 = 5, x2 = 8, y2 = -2 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (-2 - 5) / (8 - -3) | Answer: -0.6364

question: Find the distance between the points (-6, -7) and (8, -1).
solution: Given: x1 = -6, y1 = -7, x2 = 8, y2 = -1 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((14)^2 + (6)^2) | Answer: 15.23 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (0,-4), (-7,-5), (-2,-5).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 2.5 sq units

question: Find the 35th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -13 and common difference -3.
solution: Given: a = -13, d = -3, n = 35 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -13 + (35 - 1)*-3 | Answer: -115

question: Find the sum of the first 28 terms of an AP with first term -12 and common difference -6.
Find the simple interest on a principal of 15500 at 11.6% per annum for 7 years.
solution: Given: P = 15500, R = 11.6, Tt = 7 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 15500 * 11.6 * 7 / 100 | Answer: 12586 currency units

question: Find the amount when 2000 is invested at 11.2% per annum compounded annually for 3 years.
solution: Given: P = 2000, R = 11.2, Tt = 3 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 2000 * (1 + 11.2/100)^3 | Answer: 275 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (-6, 1, 5) and (8, 3, -6).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (-4, -2, 5) and (-5, 0, 5).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 15

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (-3, 6, 2) and (-3, -4, 0).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 115.4 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number 3 + -12i.
solution: Given: a = 3, b = -12 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((3)^2 + (-12)^2) | Answer: 12.37

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number 3 + -12i.
solution: Given: a = 3, b = -12 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(-12, 3) | Answer: -75.96 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = 2x^3 - 6x^2 - 6x + 5 at x = -4.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-143 with initial guess x0=13, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=0.7 and ordinates 18, 6, 5, 16, 15, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 29 and 322.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 29 and 322 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 47 and 17.
solution: Given: a = 47, b = 17 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 47*17 / 1 | Answer: 799
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 30 mm carries an axial tensile load of 92 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 21 mm and length 2700 mm carries an axial load of 35 kN. Take E = 210 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 41 mm transmits a torque of 1500 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 41, Tt = 1500 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(1500*1000) / (pi*(41)^3) | Answer: 110.8 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 49 mm and length 1200 mm carries a torque of 850 N-m. With G = 77 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (49)^4 / 32 = 565958 mm^4 | theta = (850*1000)(1200) / (77000 * 565958) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 1.341 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 135 mm wide and 300 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 135, h = 300 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 135*(300)^2 / 6 | Answer: 2025000 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (73 mm x 110 mm) carries a bending moment of 28 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (58 mm x 90 mm) has effective length 2400 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 560 MPa is designed for a working stress of 120 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 560, sw = 120 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 560 / 120 | Answer: 4.667

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 700 mm and wall thickness 15 mm carries an internal pressure of 1.5 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 700, t = 15, P = 1.5 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 1.5*700 / (2*15) | Answer: 35 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 1180 K and 280 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 1180, Tc = 280 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 280/1180) * 100 | Answer: 76.27 %

question: A refrigerator works between 265 K (cold) and 322 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 265, Th = 322 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 265 / (322 - 265) | Answer: 4.649

question: A heat pump operates between 280 K and 320 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 280, Th = 320 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 320 / (320 - 280) | Answer: 8

question: 6.9 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 125 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 6.9, dT = 125 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 6.9 * 0.718 * 125 | Answer: 619.3 kJ

question: 1.3 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 90 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1.3, dT = 90 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 1.3 * 1.005 * 90 | Answer: 117.6 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 2.6 m^3 at 350 K with mass 4.9 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 2.6, Tk = 350, m = 4.9 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 4.9*0.287*350 / 2.6 | Answer: 189.3 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 2.8 kg of air expands isothermally at 320 K from volume V1 to 2*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.8, Tk = 320, ratio = 2 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 2.8*0.287*320*ln(2) | Answer: 178.2 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 1.9 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.28 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 1.9, D = 0.28 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*1.9*0.28 / 0.001 | Answer: 532000

question: Water flows at 2.6 m/s through a pipe of diameter 260 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 28.3 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 28.3 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*28.3 / 1000 | Answer: 277.6 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 6.1 m. Taking Cv = 0.97, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 6.1, cv = 0.97 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.97*sqrt(2*9.81*6.1) | Answer: 10.61 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 290 mm) water flows at 2.4 m/s. It contracts to diameter 100 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
Water flows at 3 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.26 m and length 190 m. With friction factor f = 0.032, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 35 teeth drives a gear of 120 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1450 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 35, z2 = 120, N1 = 1450 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1450*35 / 120 | Answer: 422.9 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 170 mm rotates at 1150 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 170, N = 1150 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.17)*1150 / 60 | Answer: 10.24 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 18.8 kW at 1100 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 18.8, N = 1100 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(18.8*1000) / (2*pi*1100) | Answer: 163.2 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 3.2 kg rotates at radius 0.44 m at 1000 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 2900 N/m and mass 16.8 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 2900, m = 16.8 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(2900/16.8) | Answer: 2.091 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 6.6 m^2 and thickness 0.34 m has conductivity k = 42.3 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 165 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 6.6, L = 0.34, k = 42.3, dT = 165 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 42.3*6.6*165 / 0.34 | Answer: 135484 W

question: A surface of area 3.1 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 75 W/m^2-K to surroundings 135 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 3.1, h = 75, dT = 135 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 75*3.1*135 | Answer: 31388 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 100 m/min, feed = 0.2 mm/rev, depth of cut = 0.9 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 100, f = 0.2, d = 0.9 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*100*0.2*0.9 | Answer: 18000 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 200 mm is turned at 1000 rpm with a feed of 0.13 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 200, N = 1000, f = 0.13 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 200 / (0.13*1000) | Answer: 1.538 min

question: A resistor of 28 ohm carries a current of 1.9 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 28, I = 1.9 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 1.9 * 28 | Answer: 53.2 V

question: Three resistors 59 ohm, 78 ohm and 52 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 59, R2 = 78, R3 = 52 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 59 + 78 + 52 | Answer: 189 ohm

question: Two resistors 80 ohm and 108 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 80, R2 = 108 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 80*108 / (80+108) | Answer: 45.96 ohm

question: A device draws 7.9 A at 35 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 35, I = 7.9 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 35 * 7.9 | Answer: 276.5 W

question: A current of 8 A flows through a 7 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 8, R = 7 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (8)^2 * 7 | Answer: 448 W

question: Two capacitors 32.1 uF and 2.7 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 32.1, C2 = 2.7 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 32.1*2.7 / (32.1+2.7) | Answer: 2.491 uF

question: A resistor 74 kohm and capacitor 16.7 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 74, C = 16.7 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (74k)(16.7u) = 1236 ms | Answer: 1236 ms

question: An inductor 97 mH is in series with 84 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 97, R = 84 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (97e-3) / 84 | Answer: 1.155 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 8.3 mH inductor at 240 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 8.3, f = 240 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (240)(8.3e-3) | Answer: 12.52 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 8.5 uF capacitor at 900 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 8.5, f = 900 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (900)(8.5e-6)) | Answer: 20.8 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 41 ohm, XL = 12 ohm and XC = 88 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 41, XL = 12, XC = 88 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(41^2 + (12 - 88)^2) | Answer: 86.35 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 96.4 mH and C = 1.3 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 96.4, C = 1.3 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(96.4e-3 * 1.3e-6)) | Answer: 449.6 Hz

question: A capacitor of 11 uF is charged to 100 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 11, V = 100 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*11e-6*(100)^2 | Answer: 55 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 440 V with 240 primary turns and 250 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 440, N1 = 240, N2 = 250 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 440 * 250/240 | Answer: 458.3 V
