question: A component of ultimate strength 430 MPa is designed for a working stress of 110 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 430, sw = 110 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 430 / 110 | Answer: 3.909

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1500 mm and wall thickness 18 mm carries an internal pressure of 2.7 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1500, t = 18, P = 2.7 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 2.7*1500 / (2*18) | Answer: 112.5 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 720 K and 350 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 720, Tc = 350 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 350/720) * 100 | Answer: 51.39 %

question: A refrigerator works between 258 K (cold) and 330 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 258, Th = 330 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 258 / (330 - 258) | Answer: 3.583

question: 3.5 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 190 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.5, dT = 190 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 3.5 * 0.718 * 190 | Answer: 477.5 kJ

question: 3.1 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 185 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.1, dT = 185 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 3.1 * 1.005 * 185 | Answer: 576.4 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 0.6 m^3 at 590 K with mass 5.9 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 0.6, Tk = 590, m = 5.9 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 5.9*0.287*590 / 0.6 | Answer: 1665 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 4.4 kg of air expands isothermally at 430 K from volume V1 to 2*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.4, Tk = 430, ratio = 2 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 4.4*0.287*430*ln(2) | Answer: 376.4 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 3.3 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.21 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 3.3, D = 0.21 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*3.3*0.21 / 0.001 | Answer: 693000

question: Water flows at 2.5 m/s through a pipe of diameter 220 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 7.8 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 7.8 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*7.8 / 1000 | Answer: 76.52 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 12.6 m. Taking Cv = 0.99, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 12.6, cv = 0.99 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.99*sqrt(2*9.81*12.6) | Answer: 15.57 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 270 mm) water flows at 2.2 m/s. It contracts to diameter 130 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 270, d2 = 130, V1 = 2.2 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 2.2*(270/130)^2 | Answer: 9.49 m/s

question: Water flows at 1.6 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.42 m and length 90 m. With friction factor f = 0.032, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 27 teeth drives a gear of 71 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1100 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 27, z2 = 71, N1 = 1100 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1100*27 / 71 | Answer: 418.3 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 130 mm rotates at 1150 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 130, N = 1150 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.13)*1150 / 60 | Answer: 7.828 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 35.2 kW at 1150 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 35.2, N = 1150 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(35.2*1000) / (2*pi*1150) | Answer: 292.3 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 8.4 kg rotates at radius 0.47 m at 700 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 6100 N/m and mass 17.2 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 6100, m = 17.2 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(6100/17.2) | Answer: 2.997 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 9.2 m^2 and thickness 0.11 m has conductivity k = 7.6 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 150 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 9.2, L = 0.11, k = 7.6, dT = 150 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 7.6*9.2*150 / 0.11 | Answer: 95345 W

question: A surface of area 1 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 70 W/m^2-K to surroundings 50 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 1, h = 70, dT = 50 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 70*1*50 | Answer: 3500 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 250 m/min, feed = 0.26 mm/rev, depth of cut = 1.3 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 250, f = 0.26, d = 1.3 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*250*0.26*1.3 | Answer: 84500 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 390 mm is turned at 650 rpm with a feed of 0.13 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 390, N = 650, f = 0.13 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 390 / (0.13*650) | Answer: 4.615 min

question: A resistor of 52 ohm carries a current of 2.9 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 52, I = 2.9 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 2.9 * 52 | Answer: 150.8 V

question: Three resistors 76 ohm, 28 ohm and 92 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 76, R2 = 28, R3 = 92 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 76 + 28 + 92 | Answer: 196 ohm

question: Two resistors 23 ohm and 88 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 23, R2 = 88 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 23*88 / (23+88) | Answer: 18.23 ohm

question: A device draws 6.2 A at 240 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 240, I = 6.2 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 240 * 6.2 | Answer: 1488 W

question: A current of 11.2 A flows through a 105 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 11.2, R = 105 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (11.2)^2 * 105 | Answer: 13171 W

question: Two capacitors 45.6 uF and 3.4 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 45.6, C2 = 3.4 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 45.6*3.4 / (45.6+3.4) | Answer: 3.164 uF

question: A resistor 55 kohm and capacitor 11.5 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 55, C = 11.5 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (55k)(11.5u) = 632.5 ms | Answer: 632.5 ms

question: An inductor 425.8 mH is in series with 132 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 425.8, R = 132 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (425.8e-3) / 132 | Answer: 3.226 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 27.4 mH inductor at 330 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 27.4, f = 330 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (330)(27.4e-3) | Answer: 56.81 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 41.7 uF capacitor at 210 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 41.7, f = 210 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (210)(41.7e-6)) | Answer: 18.17 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 88 ohm, XL = 47 ohm and XC = 50 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 88, XL = 47, XC = 50 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(88^2 + (47 - 50)^2) | Answer: 88.05 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 38.6 mH and C = 4.1 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 38.6, C = 4.1 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(38.6e-3 * 4.1e-6)) | Answer: 400.1 Hz

question: A capacitor of 50 uF is charged to 340 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 50, V = 340 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*50e-6*(340)^2 | Answer: 2890 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 260 V with 630 primary turns and 360 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 260, N1 = 630, N2 = 360 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 260 * 360/630 | Answer: 148.6 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 110 V and draws an armature current of 44 A. If the armature resistance is 0.75 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 110, Ia = 44, Ra = 0.75 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 110 - 44*0.75 | Answer: 77 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 135 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.81. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 135, VL = 400, pf = 0.81 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*400*135*0.81 / 1000 | Answer: 75.76 kW

question: A load has real power 175 kW and apparent power 175 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 175, S = 175 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 175 / 175 | Answer: 1

question: A machine delivers 65 kW output while drawing 137 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 65, Pi = 137 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 65/137 * 100 | Answer: 47.45 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 28 V across R1 = 19 ohm and R2 = 41 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 28, R1 = 19, R2 = 41 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 28*41 / (19+41) | Answer: 19.13 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 10 kohm and Rin = 24 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 10, Rin = 24 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 10 / 24 | Answer: 0.4167

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 170 kohm and Rg = 1 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 170, Rg = 1 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 170/1 | Answer: 171

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 3388. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 3388 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(3388) | Answer: 35.3 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.6 m carries a central point load of 105 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.6, W = 105 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 105*4.6 / 4 | Answer: 120.7 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 5.9 m carries a UDL of 10 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.9, w = 10 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 10*(5.9)^2 / 8 | Answer: 43.51 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 1.4 m carries a point load 30 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 1.4, W = 30 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 30*1.4 | Answer: 42 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 2.2 m carries a UDL of 40 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 2.2, w = 40 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 40*(2.2)^2 / 2 | Answer: 96.8 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 5.2 m carries a point load 35 kN at distance 3 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 5.2, a = 3, W = 35 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 35*(5.2 - 3) / 5.2 | Answer: 14.81 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 4.9 m) carries a central point load 45 kN. With E = 25 GPa and I = 60e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=45000 N, L=4900.0 mm, E=25000 MPa, I=60e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 73.53 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 5.7 m carries a UDL of 30 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.7, w = 30 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 30*(5.7)^2 / 12 | Answer: 81.23 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 580 mm, clear cover 25 mm and main bars of diameter 12 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 580, c = 25, dia = 12 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 580 - 25 - 12/2 | Answer: 549 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 23.8 m^2 carrying a factored load of 12.4 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 23.8, w = 12.4 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 12.4 * 23.8 | Answer: 295.1 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 5.7 m, unit weight 18 kN/m^3, phi = 35 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 11.1 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 20 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 11.1, g = 20 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (20 - 9.81)*11.1 | Answer: 113.1 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 2.8e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.3, area = 2.7e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 2.8, i = 0.3, A = 2.7 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (2.8e-4)*0.3*(2.7e-3) | Answer: 226.8 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.2 m, bed slope 0.01 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.018. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 4.2 m under a head of 0.3 m. Taking Cd = 0.63 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 3.4 m wide carries a discharge of 5.6 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 170 m and design speed 45 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 170, V = 45 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (45)^2 / (127*170) | Answer: 0.09379
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: For a design speed of 90 km/h with allowable superelevation 0.05 and lateral friction 0.15, find the minimum curve radius in m.
A tank of volume 270 m^3 treats a flow of 135 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 270, Q = 135 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 270 / 135 | Answer: 2 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 160 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.16 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 7 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 160, k = 0.16, t = 7 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 160*(1 - e^(-0.16*7)) | Answer: 107.8 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.78, rainfall intensity 110 mm/h over a catchment of 32.2 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.78, i = 110, A = 32.2 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.78*110*32.2 / 360 | Answer: 7.674 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.03 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 110 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.03, M = 110 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 110*(20+0.03)/20 | Answer: 110.2 m

question: Convert the decimal number 142 to binary.
solution: Divide 142 by 2 repeatedly, recording remainders | Reading remainders in reverse gives 10001110 | Answer: 10001110 (binary)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 2 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the decimal number 533 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 533 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 215 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the 8-bit binary number 11001000 to decimal.
solution: Binary 11001000 = sum of bit-weights | Answer: 200 (decimal)
formula: Sum each bit times its positional weight (2^i)

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 10011000 and 00010011.
solution: XOR: 10001011 | Count of 1s = 4 | Answer: 4
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 950 megabits is sent over a link of 68 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 950, B = 68 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 950 / 68 | Answer: 13.97 s

question: A link has bandwidth 56 Mbps and round-trip time 180 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 56, R = 180 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 56e6 * 180e-3 bits = 10080 kb | Answer: 10080 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.81, cache access time 3 ns and main-memory access time 70 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.81, tc = 3, tm = 70 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.81*3 + (1 - 0.81)*70 | Answer: 15.73 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 557201 elements?
solution: Given: n = 557201 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(557201)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: An O(n^2) algorithm performs c*n^2 basic operations. If c = 1 and n = 1000, how many operations are performed?
solution: Given: n = 1000 | Formula: operations = n^2 | Substitute: = (1000)^2 | Answer: 1000000

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.009, memory access time 130 ns and page-fault service time 8 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 8 ms = 8000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.009)*130 + 0.009*8000000.0 ns | Answer: 72.13 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 2.8 m^3 at 240 kPa and 530 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 2.8, P = 240, Tk = 530 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (240e3)*2.8 / (8.314*530) | Answer: 152.5 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.23 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 17 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.23, t = 17 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.23*17) | Answer: 0.98

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.36 /min) is to reach 65% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.36, X = 65 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.65) / 0.36 | Answer: 2.916 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.13 /min) reaches 65% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.13, X = 65 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.65 / (0.13*(1 - 0.65)) | Answer: 14.29 min

question: For a reaction with A = 5e10 /s and activation energy 85 kJ/mol at 390 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 5, Ea = 85, Tk = 390 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 5e10 * exp(-85e3 / (8.314*390)) | Answer: 0.2061 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.93 and bottoms xW = 0.08, with relative volatility alpha = 3.5. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.93, xw = 0.08, al = 3.5 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.93/0.07)(0.92/0.08)] / ln(3.5) | Answer: 4.014 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.68 and x = 0.35. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.68, x = 0.35 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.68/0.32) / (0.35/0.65) | Answer: 3.946

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.63 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 95 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.63, Psat = 95 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.63 * 95 | Answer: 59.85 kPa

question: A stream of 0.5 kg/s with specific heat 4.2 kJ/kg-K is heated through 115 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 0.5, cp = 4.2, dT = 115 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 0.5*4.2*115 | Answer: 241.5 kW

question: A reactor of volume 18.8 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 3.3 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 18.8, Q = 3.3 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 18.8 / 3.3 | Answer: 5.697 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 7.5e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 5 mm with a concentration difference of 60 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 7.5, L = 5, dC = 60 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (7.5e-9)*60 / (5e-3) | Answer: 90 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 9.3 min and steady-state gain 1. For a step input of magnitude 13, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 9.3, K = 1, M = 13 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 1 * 13 | Answer: 13 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 40 m^2 flies at 120 m/s (air density 1.225 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 1.2. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 40, V = 120, rho = 1.225, CL = 1.2 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1.225*(120)^2*40*1.2 / 1000 | Answer: 423.4 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 110 m^2 flies at 240 m/s (density 0.4 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.1. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 110, V = 240, rho = 0.4, CD = 0.1 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.4*(240)^2*110*0.1 / 1000 | Answer: 126.7 kN

question: A specimen under stress 310 MPa shows an elastic strain of 3e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 310, eps = 3 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 310 / (3e-3) MPa = 103.3 GPa | Answer: 103.3 GPa

question: A block of mass 16 kg has a volume of 2.7e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 16, V = 2.7 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 16 / (2.7e-3) | Answer: 5926 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 3000 mm is heated through 145 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 23e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 3000, dT = 145, al = 23 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 3000*23e-6*145 | Answer: 10.01 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 180 ohm, R2 = 20 ohm and R3 = 300 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 180, R2 = 20, R3 = 300 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 20*300 / 180 | Answer: 33.33 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 350 ohm and gauge factor 2 experiences a strain of 1050e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 350, GF = 2, eps = 1050 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 350*2*1050e-6 | Answer: 735 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 9.27 when the true value is 100. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.27, true = 100 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.27 - 100| / 100 * 100 | Answer: 90.73 %

question: Annual demand is 12500 units, ordering cost 210 per order and holding cost 39 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 12500, S = 210, H = 39 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*12500*210 / 39) | Answer: 366.9 units

question: An asset costs 280000 with salvage value 4000 after 18 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 280000, Sv = 4000, n = 18 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (280000 - 4000) / 18 | Answer: 15333 per year

question: A product sells for 470 per unit with variable cost 60 per unit and fixed costs 165000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 470, V = 60, F = 165000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 165000 / (470 - 60) | Answer: 402.4 units

question: Find the present worth of 185000 received 9 years from now at an interest rate of 10% per year.
solution: Given: F = 185000, n = 9, i = 10 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 185000 / (1 + 0.1)^9 | Answer: 78458 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.99, 0.97 and 0.94 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.99, r2 = 0.97, r3 = 0.94 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.99*0.97*0.94 | Answer: 0.9027

question: A process produces 8 defective items in a batch of 10000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 8, N = 10000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 8/10000 * 1e6 | Answer: 800 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -x^3 - x^2 - 4x + 8 evaluated at x = 0.
For f(x) = 4x^3 - 3x^2 - 5x - 7, find f''(x) at x = -1.
Evaluate the definite integral of (-4x^2 + 6x + 8) dx from x = 1 to x = 7.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = -4x^3/3 + 6x^2/2 + 8x | Evaluate F(7) - F(1) | Answer: -264
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of x^2 - 11x + 7 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[3, 3], [4, -5]].
solution: Given: a = 3, b = 3, c = 4, d = -5 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (3)(-5) - (3)(4) | Answer: -27

question: Find the determinant of [[0, -5, 3], [-6, 3, 1], [4, 5, -4]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: -26

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[6, -7], [-2, 3]].
solution: Trace tr = 9, Determinant = 4 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 8.531

question: Solve for x: -1x + 4y = -5 and -2x + -5y = 7.
solution: Determinant = -1*-5 - 4*-2 = 13 | x = (e d - b f) / det = -0.2308 | Answer: x = -0.2308
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 62, 96, 31, 8, 5.
solution: Sum = 202 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 40.4 | Answer: 40.4

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 31, 22, 9, 17, 37.
solution: Mean = 23.2 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 11.1

question: Find the slope of the line through (-8, 0) and (4, 2).
solution: Given: x1 = -8, y1 = 0, x2 = 4, y2 = 2 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (2 - 0) / (4 - -8) | Answer: 0.1667

question: Find the distance between the points (1, -8) and (-2, -7).
solution: Given: x1 = 1, y1 = -8, x2 = -2, y2 = -7 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-3)^2 + (1)^2) | Answer: 3.162 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (-1,-3), (-2,8), (2,-7).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 14.5 sq units

question: Find the 35th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 12 and common difference -6.
solution: Given: a = 12, d = -6, n = 35 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = 12 + (35 - 1)*-6 | Answer: -192

question: Find the sum of the first 22 terms of an AP with first term -14 and common difference -1.
solution: Given: a = -14, d = -1, n = 22 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 22/2 [2*-14 + (22-1)*-1] | Answer: -539

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 4500 at 6.7% per annum for 10 years.
solution: Given: P = 4500, R = 6.7, Tt = 10 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 4500 * 6.7 * 10 / 100 | Answer: 3015 currency units

question: Find the amount when 11500 is invested at 6.9% per annum compounded annually for 2 years.
solution: Given: P = 11500, R = 6.9, Tt = 2 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 11500 * (1 + 6.9/100)^2 | Answer: 13142 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (-8, 3, -1) and (4, 1, 8).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (-4, 4, 3) and (1, 0, -6).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 32.14

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (-3, -5, -5) and (0, 6, 4).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 154.5 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number -10 + 5i.
solution: Given: a = -10, b = 5 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((-10)^2 + (5)^2) | Answer: 11.18

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number 2 + 5i.
solution: Given: a = 2, b = 5 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(5, 2) | Answer: 68.2 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -2x^3 + 3x^2 + 6x + 9 at x = 2.
solution: Given: a = -2, b = 3, c = 6, d = 9, x0 = 2 | Formula: f(x0) = a x0^3 + b x0^2 + c x0 + d | Substitute: f(2) = -2(2)^3 + 3(2)^2 + 6(2) + 9 | Answer: 17

question: Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-97 with initial guess x0=3, find x1 (one iteration).
solution: Given: N = 97, x0 = 3 | Formula: x1 = x0 - (x0^2 - N)/(2 x0) | Substitute: x1 = 3 - ((3)^2 - 97)/(2*3) | Answer: 17.67

question: Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=2 and ordinates 7, 12, 11, 11, 16, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 527 and 177.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 527 and 177 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 27 and 80.
solution: Given: a = 27, b = 80 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 27*80 / 1 | Answer: 2160
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 52 mm carries an axial tensile load of 117 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 20 mm and length 2900 mm carries an axial load of 48 kN. Take E = 210 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 21 mm transmits a torque of 900 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 21, Tt = 900 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(900*1000) / (pi*(21)^3) | Answer: 494.9 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 52 mm and length 500 mm carries a torque of 1350 N-m. With G = 77 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (52)^4 / 32 = 717816 mm^4 | theta = (1350*1000)(500) / (77000 * 717816) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 0.6997 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 66 mm wide and 130 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 66, h = 130 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 66*(130)^2 / 6 | Answer: 185900 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (64 mm x 240 mm) carries a bending moment of 13 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (49 mm x 90 mm) has effective length 3700 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 730 MPa is designed for a working stress of 130 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 730, sw = 130 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 730 / 130 | Answer: 5.615

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 650 mm and wall thickness 16 mm carries an internal pressure of 2.3 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 650, t = 16, P = 2.3 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 2.3*650 / (2*16) | Answer: 46.72 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 1140 K and 360 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 1140, Tc = 360 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 360/1140) * 100 | Answer: 68.42 %

question: A refrigerator works between 269 K (cold) and 312 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 269, Th = 312 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 269 / (312 - 269) | Answer: 6.256

question: A heat pump operates between 272 K and 314 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 272, Th = 314 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 314 / (314 - 272) | Answer: 7.476

question: 2.6 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 60 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.6, dT = 60 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 2.6 * 0.718 * 60 | Answer: 112 kJ

question: 7.1 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 95 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 7.1, dT = 95 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 7.1 * 1.005 * 95 | Answer: 677.9 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 3.6 m^3 at 470 K with mass 2.4 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 3.6, Tk = 470, m = 2.4 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 2.4*0.287*470 / 3.6 | Answer: 89.93 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 2.9 kg of air expands isothermally at 350 K from volume V1 to 2*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.9, Tk = 350, ratio = 2 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 2.9*0.287*350*ln(2) | Answer: 201.9 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 4.7 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.09 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 4.7, D = 0.09 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*4.7*0.09 / 0.001 | Answer: 423000

question: Water flows at 3.9 m/s through a pipe of diameter 170 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 11 m. Taking Cv = 0.96, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 11, cv = 0.96 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.96*sqrt(2*9.81*11) | Answer: 14.1 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 350 mm) water flows at 0.7 m/s. It contracts to diameter 140 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
Water flows at 3.2 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.42 m and length 100 m. With friction factor f = 0.029, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 15 teeth drives a gear of 61 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1050 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 15, z2 = 61, N1 = 1050 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1050*15 / 61 | Answer: 258.2 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 330 mm rotates at 1000 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 330, N = 1000 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.33)*1000 / 60 | Answer: 17.28 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 3.3 kW at 1000 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 3.3, N = 1000 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(3.3*1000) / (2*pi*1000) | Answer: 31.51 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 9.9 kg rotates at radius 0.53 m at 800 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 8600 N/m and mass 15.3 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 8600, m = 15.3 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(8600/15.3) | Answer: 3.773 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 4.2 m^2 and thickness 0.21 m has conductivity k = 25.8 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 45 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 4.2, L = 0.21, k = 25.8, dT = 45 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 25.8*4.2*45 / 0.21 | Answer: 23220 W

question: A surface of area 5.8 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 80 W/m^2-K to surroundings 65 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 5.8, h = 80, dT = 65 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 80*5.8*65 | Answer: 30160 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 230 m/min, feed = 0.24 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2.4 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 230, f = 0.24, d = 2.4 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*230*0.24*2.4 | Answer: 132480 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 260 mm is turned at 1050 rpm with a feed of 0.28 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 260, N = 1050, f = 0.28 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 260 / (0.28*1050) | Answer: 0.8844 min

question: A resistor of 107 ohm carries a current of 7.9 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 107, I = 7.9 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 7.9 * 107 | Answer: 845.3 V

question: Three resistors 58 ohm, 22 ohm and 18 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 58, R2 = 22, R3 = 18 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 58 + 22 + 18 | Answer: 98 ohm

question: Two resistors 101 ohm and 6 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 101, R2 = 6 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 101*6 / (101+6) | Answer: 5.664 ohm

question: A device draws 6.7 A at 20 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 20, I = 6.7 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 20 * 6.7 | Answer: 134 W

question: A current of 2.2 A flows through a 100 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 2.2, R = 100 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (2.2)^2 * 100 | Answer: 484 W

question: Two capacitors 7.6 uF and 33.7 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 7.6, C2 = 33.7 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 7.6*33.7 / (7.6+33.7) | Answer: 6.201 uF

question: A resistor 4 kohm and capacitor 6.6 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 4, C = 6.6 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (4k)(6.6u) = 26.4 ms | Answer: 26.4 ms

question: An inductor 56.7 mH is in series with 142 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 56.7, R = 142 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (56.7e-3) / 142 | Answer: 0.3993 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 117.6 mH inductor at 280 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 117.6, f = 280 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (280)(117.6e-3) | Answer: 206.9 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 12.4 uF capacitor at 880 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 12.4, f = 880 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (880)(12.4e-6)) | Answer: 14.59 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 64 ohm, XL = 76 ohm and XC = 54 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 64, XL = 76, XC = 54 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(64^2 + (76 - 54)^2) | Answer: 67.68 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 59.4 mH and C = 4.5 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 59.4, C = 4.5 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(59.4e-3 * 4.5e-6)) | Answer: 307.8 Hz

question: A capacitor of 37.6 uF is charged to 400 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 37.6, V = 400 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*37.6e-6*(400)^2 | Answer: 3008 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 340 V with 810 primary turns and 330 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 340, N1 = 810, N2 = 330 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 340 * 330/810 | Answer: 138.5 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 190 V and draws an armature current of 40 A. If the armature resistance is 0.77 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 190, Ia = 40, Ra = 0.77 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 190 - 40*0.77 | Answer: 159.2 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 25 A at 433 V (line) with a power factor of 0.94. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 25, VL = 433, pf = 0.94 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*433*25*0.94 / 1000 | Answer: 17.62 kW

question: A load has real power 155 kW and apparent power 190 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 155, S = 190 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 155 / 190 | Answer: 0.8158

question: A machine delivers 145 kW output while drawing 197 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 145, Pi = 197 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 145/197 * 100 | Answer: 73.6 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 7 V across R1 = 7 ohm and R2 = 25 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 7, R1 = 7, R2 = 25 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 7*25 / (7+25) | Answer: 5.469 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 150 kohm and Rin = 1 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 150, Rin = 1 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 150 / 1 | Answer: 150

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 10 kohm and Rg = 3 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 10, Rg = 3 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 10/3 | Answer: 4.333

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 8619. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 8619 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(8619) | Answer: 39.35 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.2 m carries a central point load of 45 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 9.2, W = 45 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 45*9.2 / 4 | Answer: 103.5 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.8 m carries a UDL of 15 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 9.8, w = 15 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 15*(9.8)^2 / 8 | Answer: 180.1 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 3.4 m carries a point load 45 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.4, W = 45 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 45*3.4 | Answer: 153 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 1.6 m carries a UDL of 14 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 1.6, w = 14 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 14*(1.6)^2 / 2 | Answer: 17.92 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 7.4 m carries a point load 80 kN at distance 3.8 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 7.4, a = 3.8, W = 80 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 80*(7.4 - 3.8) / 7.4 | Answer: 38.92 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 7.7 m) carries a central point load 25 kN. With E = 200 GPa and I = 400e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=25000 N, L=7700.0 mm, E=200000 MPa, I=400e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 2.972 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 5.8 m carries a UDL of 36 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.8, w = 36 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 36*(5.8)^2 / 12 | Answer: 100.9 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 420 mm, clear cover 25 mm and main bars of diameter 12 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 420, c = 25, dia = 12 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 420 - 25 - 12/2 | Answer: 389 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 12.5 m^2 carrying a factored load of 13.4 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 12.5, w = 13.4 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 13.4 * 12.5 | Answer: 167.5 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 3.7 m, unit weight 20 kN/m^3, phi = 38 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 11 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 19 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 11, g = 19 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (19 - 9.81)*11 | Answer: 101.1 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 4.9e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1.1, area = 2.5e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 4.9, i = 1.1, A = 2.5 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (4.9e-4)*1.1*(2.5e-3) | Answer: 1348 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 0.7 m, bed slope 0.002 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.02. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 2.3 m under a head of 0.6 m. Taking Cd = 0.62 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 3.5 m wide carries a discharge of 9.1 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 520 m and design speed 50 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 520, V = 50 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (50)^2 / (127*520) | Answer: 0.03786
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: A tank of volume 550 m^3 treats a flow of 150 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 550, Q = 150 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 550 / 150 | Answer: 3.667 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 150 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.11 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 8 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 150, k = 0.11, t = 8 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 150*(1 - e^(-0.11*8)) | Answer: 87.78 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.68, rainfall intensity 110 mm/h over a catchment of 22.7 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.68, i = 110, A = 22.7 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.68*110*22.7 / 360 | Answer: 4.717 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.02 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 380 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.02, M = 380 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 380*(20+0.02)/20 | Answer: 380.4 m

question: Convert the decimal number 2397 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 2397 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 95D (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 00010011 and 10101000.
solution: XOR: 10111011 | Count of 1s = 6 | Answer: 6
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 910 megabits is sent over a link of 14 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 910, B = 14 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 910 / 14 | Answer: 65 s

question: A link has bandwidth 94 Mbps and round-trip time 100 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 94, R = 100 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 94e6 * 100e-3 bits = 9400 kb | Answer: 9400 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.94, cache access time 3 ns and main-memory access time 170 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.94, tc = 3, tm = 170 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.94*3 + (1 - 0.94)*170 | Answer: 13.02 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 780642 elements?
solution: Given: n = 780642 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(780642)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: An O(n^2) algorithm performs c*n^2 basic operations. If c = 1 and n = 1390, how many operations are performed?
solution: Given: n = 1390 | Formula: operations = n^2 | Substitute: = (1390)^2 | Answer: 1932100

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.002, memory access time 130 ns and page-fault service time 5 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 5 ms = 5000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.002)*130 + 0.002*5000000.0 ns | Answer: 10.13 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 2.2 m^3 at 260 kPa and 300 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 2.2, P = 260, Tk = 300 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (260e3)*2.2 / (8.314*300) | Answer: 229.3 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.12 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 3 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.12, t = 3 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.12*3) | Answer: 0.3023

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.24 /min) is to reach 85% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.24, X = 85 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.85) / 0.24 | Answer: 7.905 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.49 /min) reaches 80% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.49, X = 80 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.8 / (0.49*(1 - 0.8)) | Answer: 8.163 min

question: For a reaction with A = 6e10 /s and activation energy 60 kJ/mol at 420 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 6, Ea = 60, Tk = 420 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 6e10 * exp(-60e3 / (8.314*420)) | Answer: 2069 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.91 and bottoms xW = 0.03, with relative volatility alpha = 2.6. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.91, xw = 0.03, al = 2.6 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.91/0.09)(0.97/0.03)] / ln(2.6) | Answer: 6.059 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.75 and x = 0.36. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.75, x = 0.36 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.75/0.25) / (0.36/0.64) | Answer: 5.333

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.81 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 120 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.81, Psat = 120 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.81 * 120 | Answer: 97.2 kPa

question: A stream of 1.1 kg/s with specific heat 1 kJ/kg-K is heated through 85 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 1.1, cp = 1, dT = 85 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 1.1*1*85 | Answer: 93.5 kW

question: A reactor of volume 2.3 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 4.9 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 2.3, Q = 4.9 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 2.3 / 4.9 | Answer: 0.4694 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 1.8e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 4 mm with a concentration difference of 170 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 1.8, L = 4, dC = 170 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (1.8e-9)*170 / (4e-3) | Answer: 76.5 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 8.2 min and steady-state gain 3.8. For a step input of magnitude 14, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 8.2, K = 3.8, M = 14 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 3.8 * 14 | Answer: 53.2 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 65 m^2 flies at 230 m/s (air density 0.7 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.6. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 65, V = 230, rho = 0.7, CL = 0.6 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.7*(230)^2*65*0.6 / 1000 | Answer: 722.1 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 20 m^2 flies at 90 m/s (density 0.4 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.03. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 20, V = 90, rho = 0.4, CD = 0.03 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.4*(90)^2*20*0.03 / 1000 | Answer: 0.972 kN

question: A specimen under stress 160 MPa shows an elastic strain of 3e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 160, eps = 3 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 160 / (3e-3) MPa = 53.33 GPa | Answer: 53.33 GPa

question: A block of mass 8 kg has a volume of 4.2e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 8, V = 4.2 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 8 / (4.2e-3) | Answer: 1905 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 900 mm is heated through 60 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 17e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 900, dT = 60, al = 17 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 900*17e-6*60 | Answer: 0.918 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 55 ohm, R2 = 160 ohm and R3 = 40 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 55, R2 = 160, R3 = 40 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 160*40 / 55 | Answer: 116.4 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 350 ohm and gauge factor 2.2 experiences a strain of 750e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 350, GF = 2.2, eps = 750 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 350*2.2*750e-6 | Answer: 577.5 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 9.24 when the true value is 50. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.24, true = 50 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.24 - 50| / 50 * 100 | Answer: 81.52 %

question: Annual demand is 3000 units, ordering cost 160 per order and holding cost 26 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 3000, S = 160, H = 26 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*3000*160 / 26) | Answer: 192.2 units

question: An asset costs 230000 with salvage value 16000 after 8 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 230000, Sv = 16000, n = 8 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (230000 - 16000) / 8 | Answer: 26750 per year

question: A product sells for 290 per unit with variable cost 70 per unit and fixed costs 155000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 290, V = 70, F = 155000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 155000 / (290 - 70) | Answer: 704.5 units

question: Find the present worth of 25000 received 4 years from now at an interest rate of 7% per year.
solution: Given: F = 25000, n = 4, i = 7 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 25000 / (1 + 0.07)^4 | Answer: 19072 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.93, 0.97 and 0.9 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.93, r2 = 0.97, r3 = 0.9 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.93*0.97*0.9 | Answer: 0.8119

question: A process produces 21 defective items in a batch of 5000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 21, N = 5000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 21/5000 * 1e6 | Answer: 4200 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -2x^3 - 4x^2 + 3x + 4 evaluated at x = 3.
For f(x) = 4x^3 - 5x^2 - 9x - 2, find f''(x) at x = 5.
Evaluate the definite integral of (2x^2 + 2x - 3) dx from x = -2 to x = 3.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = 2x^3/3 + 2x^2/2 + -3x | Evaluate F(3) - F(-2) | Answer: 13.33
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 4x^2 + 12x + 7 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[4, -6], [2, -6]].
solution: Given: a = 4, b = -6, c = 2, d = -6 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (4)(-6) - (-6)(2) | Answer: -12

question: Find the determinant of [[-4, 5, 5], [-6, -2, -6], [0, -6, -6]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: 96

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[5, 5], [8, -7]].
solution: Trace tr = -2, Determinant = -75 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 7.718

question: Solve for x: -1x + 3y = -8 and 4x + -6y = 12.
solution: Determinant = -1*-6 - 3*4 = -6 | x = (e d - b f) / det = -2 | Answer: x = -2
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 43, 44, 77, 53, 65.
solution: Sum = 282 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 56.4 | Answer: 56.4

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 18, 40, 18, 38, 4.
solution: Mean = 23.6 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 15.19

question: Find the slope of the line through (1, -4) and (8, -3).
solution: Given: x1 = 1, y1 = -4, x2 = 8, y2 = -3 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (-3 - -4) / (8 - 1) | Answer: 0.1429

question: Find the distance between the points (-7, 8) and (4, -4).
solution: Given: x1 = -7, y1 = 8, x2 = 4, y2 = -4 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((11)^2 + (-12)^2) | Answer: 16.28 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (-7,0), (-4,1), (-2,8).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 9.5 sq units

question: Find the 40th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -10 and common difference 8.
solution: Given: a = -10, d = 8, n = 40 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -10 + (40 - 1)*8 | Answer: 302

question: Find the sum of the first 38 terms of an AP with first term 12 and common difference 7.
solution: Given: a = 12, d = 7, n = 38 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 38/2 [2*12 + (38-1)*7] | Answer: 5377

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 27000 at 13.2% per annum for 3 years.
solution: Given: P = 27000, R = 13.2, Tt = 3 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 27000 * 13.2 * 3 / 100 | Answer: 10692 currency units

question: Find the amount when 28000 is invested at 4.1% per annum compounded annually for 2 years.
solution: Given: P = 28000, R = 4.1, Tt = 2 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 28000 * (1 + 4.1/100)^2 | Answer: 30343 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (2, 0, 5) and (6, -5, 5).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (0, 3, -3) and (-6, -5, 3).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 26.15

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (-3, 3, -2) and (3, 6, -2).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 66.68 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number 2 + -12i.
solution: Given: a = 2, b = -12 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((2)^2 + (-12)^2) | Answer: 12.17

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number 0 + -6i.
solution: Given: a = 0, b = -6 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(-6, 0) | Answer: -90 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = 2x^3 - 7x^2 + 5x + 2 at x = 1.
solution: Given: a = 2, b = -7, c = 5, d = 2, x0 = 1 | Formula: f(x0) = a x0^3 + b x0^2 + c x0 + d | Substitute: f(1) = 2(1)^3 + -7(1)^2 + 5(1) + 2 | Answer: 2

question: Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-184 with initial guess x0=14, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=0.6 and ordinates 5, 13, 16, 10, 4, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 396 and 203.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 396 and 203 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 69 and 57.
solution: Given: a = 69, b = 57 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 69*57 / 3 | Answer: 1311
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 14 mm carries an axial tensile load of 97 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 27 mm and length 700 mm carries an axial load of 90 kN. Take E = 200 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 49 mm transmits a torque of 3000 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 49, Tt = 3000 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(3000*1000) / (pi*(49)^3) | Answer: 129.9 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 63 mm and length 1800 mm carries a torque of 1550 N-m. With G = 45 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (63)^4 / 32 = 1546543 mm^4 | theta = (1550*1000)(1800) / (45000 * 1546543) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 2.297 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 104 mm wide and 280 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 104, h = 280 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 104*(280)^2 / 6 | Answer: 1358933 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (46 mm x 160 mm) carries a bending moment of 18 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (62 mm x 90 mm) has effective length 3200 mm and E = 200 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 670 MPa is designed for a working stress of 170 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 670, sw = 170 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 670 / 170 | Answer: 3.941

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 400 mm and wall thickness 13 mm carries an internal pressure of 1.1 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 400, t = 13, P = 1.1 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 1.1*400 / (2*13) | Answer: 16.92 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 1080 K and 290 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 1080, Tc = 290 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 290/1080) * 100 | Answer: 73.15 %

question: A heat pump operates between 275 K and 304 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 275, Th = 304 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 304 / (304 - 275) | Answer: 10.48

question: 4 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 45 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4, dT = 45 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 4 * 0.718 * 45 | Answer: 129.2 kJ

question: 1 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 75 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1, dT = 75 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 1 * 1.005 * 75 | Answer: 75.37 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 4 m^3 at 550 K with mass 4.6 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 4, Tk = 550, m = 4.6 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 4.6*0.287*550 / 4 | Answer: 181.5 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 3 kg of air expands isothermally at 480 K from volume V1 to 5*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3, Tk = 480, ratio = 5 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 3*0.287*480*ln(5) | Answer: 665.1 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 4.4 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.32 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 4.4, D = 0.32 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*4.4*0.32 / 0.001 | Answer: 1408000

question: Water flows at 2.2 m/s through a pipe of diameter 60 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 4.5 m. Taking Cv = 0.97, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 4.5, cv = 0.97 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.97*sqrt(2*9.81*4.5) | Answer: 9.114 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 380 mm) water flows at 2.1 m/s. It contracts to diameter 90 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 380, d2 = 90, V1 = 2.1 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 2.1*(380/90)^2 | Answer: 37.44 m/s

question: Water flows at 3.6 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.41 m and length 160 m. With friction factor f = 0.034, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 25 teeth drives a gear of 101 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1100 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 25, z2 = 101, N1 = 1100 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1100*25 / 101 | Answer: 272.3 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 320 mm rotates at 1400 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 320, N = 1400 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.32)*1400 / 60 | Answer: 23.46 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 9.5 kW at 1200 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 9.5, N = 1200 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(9.5*1000) / (2*pi*1200) | Answer: 75.6 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 4.8 kg rotates at radius 0.36 m at 650 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 18200 N/m and mass 6 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 18200, m = 6 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(18200/6) | Answer: 8.766 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 8.4 m^2 and thickness 0.28 m has conductivity k = 19.7 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 50 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 8.4, L = 0.28, k = 19.7, dT = 50 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 19.7*8.4*50 / 0.28 | Answer: 29550 W

question: A surface of area 2.2 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 50 W/m^2-K to surroundings 60 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 2.2, h = 50, dT = 60 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 50*2.2*60 | Answer: 6600 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 240 m/min, feed = 0.39 mm/rev, depth of cut = 1.1 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 240, f = 0.39, d = 1.1 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*240*0.39*1.1 | Answer: 102960 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 100 mm is turned at 200 rpm with a feed of 0.26 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 100, N = 200, f = 0.26 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 100 / (0.26*200) | Answer: 1.923 min

question: A resistor of 137 ohm carries a current of 0.4 A. Find the voltage across it.

question: Three resistors 98 ohm, 94 ohm and 82 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 98, R2 = 94, R3 = 82 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 98 + 94 + 82 | Answer: 274 ohm

question: Two resistors 63 ohm and 2 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 63, R2 = 2 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 63*2 / (63+2) | Answer: 1.938 ohm

question: A device draws 3.7 A at 35 V. Find the power consumed.

question: A current of 4.3 A flows through a 17 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.

question: Two capacitors 9.1 uF and 32.4 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 9.1, C2 = 32.4 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 9.1*32.4 / (9.1+32.4) | Answer: 7.105 uF

question: A resistor 88 kohm and capacitor 1.1 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 88, C = 1.1 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (88k)(1.1u) = 96.8 ms | Answer: 96.8 ms

question: An inductor 82.2 mH is in series with 179 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 20.4 mH inductor at 960 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 20.4, f = 960 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (960)(20.4e-3) | Answer: 123 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 28.7 uF capacitor at 400 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 28.7, f = 400 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (400)(28.7e-6)) | Answer: 13.86 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 22 ohm, XL = 106 ohm and XC = 125 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 22, XL = 106, XC = 125 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(22^2 + (106 - 125)^2) | Answer: 29.07 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 25.1 mH and C = 3.2 uF (in Hz).

question: A capacitor of 39.6 uF is charged to 365 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 39.6, V = 365 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*39.6e-6*(365)^2 | Answer: 2638 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 390 V with 530 primary turns and 170 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.

question: A DC motor is supplied at 440 V and draws an armature current of 19 A. If the armature resistance is 0.83 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 440, Ia = 19, Ra = 0.83 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 440 - 19*0.83 | Answer: 424.2 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 130 A at 433 V (line) with a power factor of 0.87. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 130, VL = 433, pf = 0.87 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*433*130*0.87 / 1000 | Answer: 84.82 kW

question: A load has real power 170 kW and apparent power 215 kVA. Find the power factor.

question: A machine delivers 110 kW output while drawing 202 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 110, Pi = 202 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 110/202 * 100 | Answer: 54.46 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 17 V across R1 = 14 ohm and R2 = 22 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 17, R1 = 14, R2 = 22 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 17*22 / (14+22) | Answer: 10.39 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 220 kohm and Rin = 32 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 220, Rin = 32 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 220 / 32 | Answer: 6.875

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 120 kohm and Rg = 31 kohm. Find the voltage gain.

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 7699. Express the gain in decibels (power).

question: A simply supported beam of span 7.1 m carries a central point load of 80 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.

question: A simply supported beam of span 3.5 m carries a UDL of 55 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.

question: A cantilever of length 5.4 m carries a point load 20 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.

question: A cantilever of length 5.1 m carries a UDL of 14 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.9 m carries a point load 100 kN at distance 1.9 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.

question: A simply supported beam (span 7.4 m) carries a central point load 15 kN. With E = 30 GPa and I = 370e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.

question: An RC beam has overall depth 580 mm, clear cover 40 mm and main bars of diameter 20 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 580, c = 40, dia = 20 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 580 - 40 - 20/2 | Answer: 530 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 23.2 m^2 carrying a factored load of 16.3 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.

question: A tank of volume 780 m^3 treats a flow of 10 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 260 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.15 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 7 days.

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.8, rainfall intensity 35 mm/h over a catchment of 21.2 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.

question: A link has bandwidth 57 Mbps and round-trip time 150 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.92, cache access time 3 ns and main-memory access time 100 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.92, tc = 3, tm = 100 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.92*3 + (1 - 0.92)*100 | Answer: 10.76 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 395257 elements?

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.017, memory access time 170 ns and page-fault service time 6 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 0.7 m^3 at 370 kPa and 320 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.06 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 12 minutes.

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.37 /min) is to reach 90% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.48 /min) reaches 85% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.48, X = 85 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.85 / (0.48*(1 - 0.85)) | Answer: 11.81 min

question: For a reaction with A = 3e10 /s and activation energy 65 kJ/mol at 340 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.99 and bottoms xW = 0.03, with relative volatility alpha = 2.2. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.71 and x = 0.36. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.54 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 65 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.

question: A stream of 7.4 kg/s with specific heat 2.7 kJ/kg-K is heated through 75 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.

question: A reactor of volume 15.2 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 2.7 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 15.2, Q = 2.7 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 15.2 / 2.7 | Answer: 5.63 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 2.7e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 5 mm with a concentration difference of 160 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 2.7, L = 5, dC = 160 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (2.7e-9)*160 / (5e-3) | Answer: 86.4 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 4.9 min and steady-state gain 2.5. For a step input of magnitude 7, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 4.9, K = 2.5, M = 7 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 2.5 * 7 | Answer: 17.5 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 55 m^2 flies at 60 m/s (air density 1.225 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 1.4. Find the lift force in kN.

question: An aircraft of wing area 75 m^2 flies at 90 m/s (density 0.7 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.08. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 75, V = 90, rho = 0.7, CD = 0.08 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.7*(90)^2*75*0.08 / 1000 | Answer: 17.01 kN

question: A specimen under stress 340 MPa shows an elastic strain of 2.7e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.

question: A block of mass 3 kg has a volume of 2.5e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.

question: A rod of length 1300 mm is heated through 65 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 23e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 15 ohm, R2 = 115 ohm and R3 = 400 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).

question: A strain gauge of resistance 120 ohm and gauge factor 2 experiences a strain of 500e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 120, GF = 2, eps = 500 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 120*2*500e-6 | Answer: 120 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 10.72 when the true value is 100. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10.72, true = 100 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10.72 - 100| / 100 * 100 | Answer: 89.28 %

question: Annual demand is 45500 units, ordering cost 150 per order and holding cost 35 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 45500, S = 150, H = 35 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*45500*150 / 35) | Answer: 624.5 units

question: An asset costs 360000 with salvage value 18000 after 17 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 360000, Sv = 18000, n = 17 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (360000 - 18000) / 17 | Answer: 20118 per year

question: A product sells for 390 per unit with variable cost 150 per unit and fixed costs 170000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 390, V = 150, F = 170000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 170000 / (390 - 150) | Answer: 708.3 units

question: Find the present worth of 180000 received 6 years from now at an interest rate of 9% per year.
solution: Given: F = 180000, n = 6, i = 9 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 180000 / (1 + 0.09)^6 | Answer: 107328 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.96, 0.92 and 0.95 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.96, r2 = 0.92, r3 = 0.95 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.96*0.92*0.95 | Answer: 0.839

question: A process produces 40 defective items in a batch of 8000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 40, N = 8000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 40/8000 * 1e6 | Answer: 5000 PPM

question: Find the 20th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -19 and common difference -8.

question: Find the sum of the first 32 terms of an AP with first term 10 and common difference 3.

formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (-5, 3, -4) and (6, -3, -4).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 50.21

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (-2, -1, -3) and (-4, 1, 1).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 75.41 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number 2 + 3i.
solution: Given: a = 2, b = 3 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((2)^2 + (3)^2) | Answer: 3.606

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number 7 + -8i.
solution: Given: a = 7, b = -8 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(-8, 7) | Answer: -48.81 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = 2x^3 - 6x^2 + x + 2 at x = 3.
solution: Given: a = 2, b = -6, c = 1, d = 2, x0 = 3 | Formula: f(x0) = a x0^3 + b x0^2 + c x0 + d | Substitute: f(3) = 2(3)^3 + -6(3)^2 + 1(3) + 2 | Answer: 5

question: Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-89 with initial guess x0=2, find x1 (one iteration).
