question: Three resistors 55 ohm, 86 ohm and 96 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 55, R2 = 86, R3 = 96 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 55 + 86 + 96 | Answer: 237 ohm

question: Two resistors 120 ohm and 49 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 120, R2 = 49 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 120*49 / (120+49) | Answer: 34.79 ohm

question: A device draws 1.9 A at 75 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 75, I = 1.9 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 75 * 1.9 | Answer: 142.5 W

question: A current of 12 A flows through a 150 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 12, R = 150 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (12)^2 * 150 | Answer: 21600 W

question: Two capacitors 16.4 uF and 18.7 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 16.4, C2 = 18.7 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 16.4*18.7 / (16.4+18.7) | Answer: 8.737 uF

question: A resistor 60 kohm and capacitor 12.4 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 60, C = 12.4 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (60k)(12.4u) = 744 ms | Answer: 744 ms

question: An inductor 282 mH is in series with 71 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 282, R = 71 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (282e-3) / 71 | Answer: 3.972 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 80.6 mH inductor at 770 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 80.6, f = 770 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (770)(80.6e-3) | Answer: 389.9 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 32.1 uF capacitor at 840 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 32.1, f = 840 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (840)(32.1e-6)) | Answer: 5.902 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 90 ohm, XL = 39 ohm and XC = 63 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 90, XL = 39, XC = 63 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(90^2 + (39 - 63)^2) | Answer: 93.15 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 31.2 mH and C = 3.3 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 31.2, C = 3.3 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(31.2e-3 * 3.3e-6)) | Answer: 496 Hz

question: A capacitor of 46.2 uF is charged to 290 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 46.2, V = 290 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*46.2e-6*(290)^2 | Answer: 1943 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 270 V with 680 primary turns and 390 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 270, N1 = 680, N2 = 390 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 270 * 390/680 | Answer: 154.9 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 150 V and draws an armature current of 30 A. If the armature resistance is 0.28 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 150, Ia = 30, Ra = 0.28 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 150 - 30*0.28 | Answer: 141.6 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 20 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.94. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 20, VL = 400, pf = 0.94 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*400*20*0.94 / 1000 | Answer: 13.03 kW

question: A load has real power 85 kW and apparent power 100 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 85, S = 100 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 85 / 100 | Answer: 0.85

question: A machine delivers 35 kW output while drawing 177 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 35, Pi = 177 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 35/177 * 100 | Answer: 19.77 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 19 V across R1 = 12 ohm and R2 = 20 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 19, R1 = 12, R2 = 20 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 19*20 / (12+20) | Answer: 11.88 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 100 kohm and Rin = 17 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 100, Rin = 17 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 100 / 17 | Answer: 5.882

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 180 kohm and Rg = 1 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 180, Rg = 1 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 180/1 | Answer: 181

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 3758. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 3758 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(3758) | Answer: 35.75 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 5.6 m carries a central point load of 25 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.6, W = 25 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 25*5.6 / 4 | Answer: 35 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 5.1 m carries a UDL of 20 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.1, w = 20 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 20*(5.1)^2 / 8 | Answer: 65.02 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 1.2 m carries a point load 35 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 1.2, W = 35 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 35*1.2 | Answer: 42 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 3.4 m carries a UDL of 6 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.4, w = 6 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 6*(3.4)^2 / 2 | Answer: 34.68 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 5.7 m carries a point load 40 kN at distance 2.8 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 5.7, a = 2.8, W = 40 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 40*(5.7 - 2.8) / 5.7 | Answer: 20.35 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 7.5 m) carries a central point load 55 kN. With E = 200 GPa and I = 200e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=55000 N, L=7500.0 mm, E=200000 MPa, I=200e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 12.08 mm

question: An RC beam has overall depth 390 mm, clear cover 30 mm and main bars of diameter 25 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 390, c = 30, dia = 25 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 390 - 30 - 25/2 | Answer: 347.5 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 26.9 m^2 carrying a factored load of 19.5 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 26.9, w = 19.5 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 19.5 * 26.9 | Answer: 524.5 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 5.8 m, unit weight 16 kN/m^3, phi = 32 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 8.7 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 18 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 8.7, g = 18 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (18 - 9.81)*8.7 | Answer: 71.25 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 1.9e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.8, area = 6.7e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 1.9, i = 0.8, A = 6.7 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (1.9e-4)*0.8*(6.7e-3) | Answer: 1018 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 0.5 m, bed slope 0.005 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.028. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 2.1 m under a head of 0.8 m. Taking Cd = 0.63 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 5.3 m wide carries a discharge of 7 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 110 m and design speed 85 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 110, V = 85 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (85)^2 / (127*110) | Answer: 0.5172
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: A tank of volume 980 m^3 treats a flow of 175 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 980, Q = 175 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 980 / 175 | Answer: 5.6 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 380 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.12 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 4 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 380, k = 0.12, t = 4 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 380*(1 - e^(-0.12*4)) | Answer: 144.9 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.78, rainfall intensity 50 mm/h over a catchment of 22.3 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.78, i = 50, A = 22.3 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.78*50*22.3 / 360 | Answer: 2.416 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.06 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 680 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.06, M = 680 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 680*(20+0.06)/20 | Answer: 682 m

question: Convert the decimal number 2044 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 2044 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 7FC (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the 8-bit binary number 10000111 to decimal.
solution: Binary 10000111 = sum of bit-weights | Answer: 135 (decimal)
formula: Sum each bit times its positional weight (2^i)

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 11101101 and 00111010.
solution: XOR: 11010111 | Count of 1s = 6 | Answer: 6
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 430 megabits is sent over a link of 31 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 430, B = 31 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 430 / 31 | Answer: 13.87 s

question: A link has bandwidth 71 Mbps and round-trip time 180 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 71, R = 180 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 71e6 * 180e-3 bits = 12780 kb | Answer: 12780 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.8, cache access time 6 ns and main-memory access time 150 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.8, tc = 6, tm = 150 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.8*6 + (1 - 0.8)*150 | Answer: 34.8 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 402052 elements?
solution: Given: n = 402052 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(402052)) + 1 | Answer: 19

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.01, memory access time 190 ns and page-fault service time 5 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 5 ms = 5000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.01)*190 + 0.01*5000000.0 ns | Answer: 50.19 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 1.3 m^3 at 450 kPa and 440 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 1.3, P = 450, Tk = 440 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (450e3)*1.3 / (8.314*440) | Answer: 159.9 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.1 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 16 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.1, t = 16 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.1*16) | Answer: 0.7981

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.36 /min) is to reach 85% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.36, X = 85 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.85) / 0.36 | Answer: 5.27 min

question: For a reaction with A = 4e10 /s and activation energy 70 kJ/mol at 340 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 4, Ea = 70, Tk = 340 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 4e10 * exp(-70e3 / (8.314*340)) | Answer: 0.7039 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.95 and bottoms xW = 0.08, with relative volatility alpha = 1.7. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.95, xw = 0.08, al = 1.7 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.95/0.05)(0.92/0.08)] / ln(1.7) | Answer: 10.15 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.62 and x = 0.31. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.62, x = 0.31 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.62/0.38) / (0.31/0.69) | Answer: 3.632

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.84 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 35 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.84, Psat = 35 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.84 * 35 | Answer: 29.4 kPa

question: A stream of 5.7 kg/s with specific heat 3.6 kJ/kg-K is heated through 70 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 5.7, cp = 3.6, dT = 70 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 5.7*3.6*70 | Answer: 1436 kW

question: A reactor of volume 13.4 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 0.7 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 13.4, Q = 0.7 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 13.4 / 0.7 | Answer: 19.14 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 8.5e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 1 mm with a concentration difference of 120 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 8.5, L = 1, dC = 120 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (8.5e-9)*120 / (1e-3) | Answer: 1020 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 5.6 min and steady-state gain 2.8. For a step input of magnitude 14, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 5.6, K = 2.8, M = 14 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 2.8 * 14 | Answer: 39.2 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 65 m^2 flies at 110 m/s (air density 0.4 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.9. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 65, V = 110, rho = 0.4, CL = 0.9 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.4*(110)^2*65*0.9 / 1000 | Answer: 141.6 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 85 m^2 flies at 230 m/s (density 0.4 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.04. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 85, V = 230, rho = 0.4, CD = 0.04 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.4*(230)^2*85*0.04 / 1000 | Answer: 35.97 kN

question: A specimen under stress 100 MPa shows an elastic strain of 1e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 100, eps = 1 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 100 / (1e-3) MPa = 100 GPa | Answer: 100 GPa

question: A block of mass 49 kg has a volume of 2.5e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 49, V = 2.5 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 49 / (2.5e-3) | Answer: 19600 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 1200 mm is heated through 120 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 11e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 1200, dT = 120, al = 11 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 1200*11e-6*120 | Answer: 1.584 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 90 ohm, R2 = 135 ohm and R3 = 230 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 90, R2 = 135, R3 = 230 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 135*230 / 90 | Answer: 345 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 1000 ohm and gauge factor 2 experiences a strain of 1100e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 1000, GF = 2, eps = 1100 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 1000*2*1100e-6 | Answer: 2200 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 9.57 when the true value is 50. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.57, true = 50 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.57 - 50| / 50 * 100 | Answer: 80.86 %

question: Annual demand is 50000 units, ordering cost 110 per order and holding cost 28 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 50000, S = 110, H = 28 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*50000*110 / 28) | Answer: 626.8 units

question: An asset costs 270000 with salvage value 24000 after 6 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 270000, Sv = 24000, n = 6 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (270000 - 24000) / 6 | Answer: 41000 per year

question: A product sells for 240 per unit with variable cost 160 per unit and fixed costs 10000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 240, V = 160, F = 10000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 10000 / (240 - 160) | Answer: 125 units

question: Find the present worth of 180000 received 8 years from now at an interest rate of 7% per year.
solution: Given: F = 180000, n = 8, i = 7 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 180000 / (1 + 0.07)^8 | Answer: 104762 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.97, 0.95 and 0.98 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.97, r2 = 0.95, r3 = 0.98 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.97*0.95*0.98 | Answer: 0.9031

question: A process produces 43 defective items in a batch of 5500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 43, N = 5500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 43/5500 * 1e6 | Answer: 7818 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = 6x^3 + 2x^2 + 5x - 5 evaluated at x = 0.
For f(x) = -4x^3 + 8x^2 - 6x + 8, find f''(x) at x = -5.
Evaluate the definite integral of (5x^2 - 5x + 2) dx from x = 2 to x = 7.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = 5x^3/3 + -5x^2/2 + 2x | Evaluate F(7) - F(2) | Answer: 455.8
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 5x^2 + 2x - 11 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[3, -1], [9, 7]].
solution: Given: a = 3, b = -1, c = 9, d = 7 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (3)(7) - (-1)(9) | Answer: 30

question: Find the determinant of [[-3, 0, 6], [1, 2, -1], [4, -3, -6]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: -21

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[-5, -5], [-7, 4]].
solution: Trace tr = -1, Determinant = -55 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 6.933

question: Solve for x: -6x + 4y = 2 and -5x + -6y = 0.
solution: Determinant = -6*-6 - 4*-5 = 56 | x = (e d - b f) / det = -0.2143 | Answer: x = -0.2143
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 96, 36, 31, 94, 86.
solution: Sum = 343 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 68.6 | Answer: 68.6

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 20, 23, 5, 38, 41.
solution: Mean = 25.4 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 14.6

question: Find the slope of the line through (-1, -2) and (-9, 4).
solution: Given: x1 = -1, y1 = -2, x2 = -9, y2 = 4 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (4 - -2) / (-9 - -1) | Answer: -0.75

question: Find the distance between the points (-4, 4) and (-9, 9).
solution: Given: x1 = -4, y1 = 4, x2 = -9, y2 = 9 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-5)^2 + (5)^2) | Answer: 7.071 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (8,1), (-6,0), (0,0).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 3 sq units

question: Find the 26th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -20 and common difference 4.
solution: Given: a = -20, d = 4, n = 26 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -20 + (26 - 1)*4 | Answer: 80

question: Find the sum of the first 36 terms of an AP with first term -9 and common difference -2.
solution: Given: a = -9, d = -2, n = 36 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 36/2 [2*-9 + (36-1)*-2] | Answer: -1584

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 39000 at 4.4% per annum for 4 years.
solution: Given: P = 39000, R = 4.4, Tt = 4 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 39000 * 4.4 * 4 / 100 | Answer: 6864 currency units

question: Find the amount when 6500 is invested at 11.2% per annum compounded annually for 5 years.
solution: Given: P = 6500, R = 11.2, Tt = 5 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 6500 * (1 + 11.2/100)^5 | Answer: 11052 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (0, 4, 8) and (1, -7, 4).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (-4, 1, 4) and (-4, -2, 2).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 17.55

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (-5, -2, 0) and (4, 6, 3).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 139.5 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number -2 + 1i.
solution: Given: a = -2, b = 1 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((-2)^2 + (1)^2) | Answer: 2.236

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number 2 + -5i.
solution: Given: a = 2, b = -5 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(-5, 2) | Answer: -68.2 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = 5x^3 + 4x^2 + 3x - 5 at x = 5.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-173 with initial guess x0=7, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.8 and ordinates 5, 0, 0, 2, 16, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 23 and 173.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 23 and 173 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 62 and 43.
solution: Given: a = 62, b = 43 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 62*43 / 1 | Answer: 2666
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 18 mm carries an axial tensile load of 83 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 12 mm and length 1700 mm carries an axial load of 43 kN. Take E = 110 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 27 mm transmits a torque of 1750 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 27, Tt = 1750 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(1750*1000) / (pi*(27)^3) | Answer: 452.8 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 58 mm and length 1900 mm carries a torque of 450 N-m. With G = 80 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (58)^4 / 32 = 1110994 mm^4 | theta = (450*1000)(1900) / (80000 * 1110994) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 0.5512 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 31 mm wide and 300 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 31, h = 300 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 31*(300)^2 / 6 | Answer: 465000 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (44 mm x 100 mm) carries a bending moment of 34 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (45 mm x 120 mm) has effective length 2200 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 340 MPa is designed for a working stress of 220 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 340, sw = 220 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 340 / 220 | Answer: 1.545

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 700 mm and wall thickness 15 mm carries an internal pressure of 1.7 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 700, t = 15, P = 1.7 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 1.7*700 / (2*15) | Answer: 39.67 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 600 K and 400 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 600, Tc = 400 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 400/600) * 100 | Answer: 33.33 %

question: A refrigerator works between 259 K (cold) and 318 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 259, Th = 318 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 259 / (318 - 259) | Answer: 4.39

question: A heat pump operates between 274 K and 310 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 274, Th = 310 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 310 / (310 - 274) | Answer: 8.611

question: 1.4 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 150 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1.4, dT = 150 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 1.4 * 0.718 * 150 | Answer: 150.8 kJ

question: 7.6 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 100 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 7.6, dT = 100 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 7.6 * 1.005 * 100 | Answer: 763.8 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 2.7 m^3 at 470 K with mass 3.4 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 2.7, Tk = 470, m = 3.4 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 3.4*0.287*470 / 2.7 | Answer: 169.9 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 1.7 kg of air expands isothermally at 400 K from volume V1 to 2*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1.7, Tk = 400, ratio = 2 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 1.7*0.287*400*ln(2) | Answer: 135.3 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 2.9 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.13 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 2.9, D = 0.13 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*2.9*0.13 / 0.001 | Answer: 377000

question: Water flows at 2.1 m/s through a pipe of diameter 290 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 19.7 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 19.7 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*19.7 / 1000 | Answer: 193.3 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 7.2 m. Taking Cv = 0.99, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 7.2, cv = 0.99 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.99*sqrt(2*9.81*7.2) | Answer: 11.77 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 330 mm) water flows at 2.9 m/s. It contracts to diameter 70 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 330, d2 = 70, V1 = 2.9 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 2.9*(330/70)^2 | Answer: 64.45 m/s

question: Water flows at 2.2 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.32 m and length 320 m. With friction factor f = 0.038, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 20 teeth drives a gear of 93 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1400 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 20, z2 = 93, N1 = 1400 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1400*20 / 93 | Answer: 301.1 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 250 mm rotates at 800 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 250, N = 800 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.25)*800 / 60 | Answer: 10.47 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 14.8 kW at 1250 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 14.8, N = 1250 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(14.8*1000) / (2*pi*1250) | Answer: 113.1 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 9.7 kg rotates at radius 0.31 m at 650 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 11800 N/m and mass 18.1 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 11800, m = 18.1 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(11800/18.1) | Answer: 4.064 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 3.9 m^2 and thickness 0.15 m has conductivity k = 34.3 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 25 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 3.9, L = 0.15, k = 34.3, dT = 25 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 34.3*3.9*25 / 0.15 | Answer: 22295 W

question: A surface of area 0.6 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 100 W/m^2-K to surroundings 85 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 0.6, h = 100, dT = 85 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 100*0.6*85 | Answer: 5100 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 180 m/min, feed = 0.4 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2.3 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 180, f = 0.4, d = 2.3 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*180*0.4*2.3 | Answer: 165600 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 160 mm is turned at 800 rpm with a feed of 0.22 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 160, N = 800, f = 0.22 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 160 / (0.22*800) | Answer: 0.9091 min

question: A resistor of 37 ohm carries a current of 6.5 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 37, I = 6.5 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 6.5 * 37 | Answer: 240.5 V

question: Three resistors 42 ohm, 73 ohm and 69 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 42, R2 = 73, R3 = 69 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 42 + 73 + 69 | Answer: 184 ohm

question: Two resistors 66 ohm and 30 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 66, R2 = 30 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 66*30 / (66+30) | Answer: 20.62 ohm

question: A device draws 8.8 A at 170 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 170, I = 8.8 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 170 * 8.8 | Answer: 1496 W

question: A current of 5 A flows through a 92 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 5, R = 92 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (5)^2 * 92 | Answer: 2300 W

question: Two capacitors 40 uF and 46.4 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 40, C2 = 46.4 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 40*46.4 / (40+46.4) | Answer: 21.48 uF

question: A resistor 78 kohm and capacitor 6.3 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 78, C = 6.3 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (78k)(6.3u) = 491.4 ms | Answer: 491.4 ms

question: An inductor 302.2 mH is in series with 123 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 302.2, R = 123 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (302.2e-3) / 123 | Answer: 2.457 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 172.7 mH inductor at 590 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 172.7, f = 590 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (590)(172.7e-3) | Answer: 640.2 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 36.9 uF capacitor at 610 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 36.9, f = 610 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (610)(36.9e-6)) | Answer: 7.071 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 26 ohm, XL = 57 ohm and XC = 123 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 26, XL = 57, XC = 123 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(26^2 + (57 - 123)^2) | Answer: 70.94 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 22.9 mH and C = 6.4 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 22.9, C = 6.4 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(22.9e-3 * 6.4e-6)) | Answer: 415.7 Hz

question: A capacitor of 91.6 uF is charged to 25 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 91.6, V = 25 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*91.6e-6*(25)^2 | Answer: 28.62 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 280 V with 590 primary turns and 400 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 280, N1 = 590, N2 = 400 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 280 * 400/590 | Answer: 189.8 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 140 V and draws an armature current of 32 A. If the armature resistance is 1.43 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 140, Ia = 32, Ra = 1.43 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 140 - 32*1.43 | Answer: 94.24 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 200 A at 415 V (line) with a power factor of 0.92. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 200, VL = 415, pf = 0.92 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*415*200*0.92 / 1000 | Answer: 132.3 kW

question: A load has real power 10 kW and apparent power 45 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 10, S = 45 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 10 / 45 | Answer: 0.2222

question: A machine delivers 80 kW output while drawing 127 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 80, Pi = 127 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 80/127 * 100 | Answer: 62.99 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 23 V across R1 = 42 ohm and R2 = 23 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 23, R1 = 42, R2 = 23 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 23*23 / (42+23) | Answer: 8.138 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 150 kohm and Rin = 24 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 150, Rin = 24 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 150 / 24 | Answer: 6.25

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 100 kohm and Rg = 13 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 100, Rg = 13 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 100/13 | Answer: 8.692

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 5257. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 5257 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(5257) | Answer: 37.21 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 3.3 m carries a central point load of 80 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.3, W = 80 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 80*3.3 / 4 | Answer: 66 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 4 m carries a UDL of 5 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4, w = 5 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 5*(4)^2 / 8 | Answer: 10 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 2.1 m carries a point load 80 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 2.1, W = 80 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 80*2.1 | Answer: 168 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 2 m carries a UDL of 32 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 2, w = 32 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 32*(2)^2 / 2 | Answer: 64 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.6 m carries a point load 60 kN at distance 3.2 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 4.6, a = 3.2, W = 60 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 60*(4.6 - 3.2) / 4.6 | Answer: 18.26 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 4.5 m) carries a central point load 75 kN. With E = 200 GPa and I = 570e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=75000 N, L=4500.0 mm, E=200000 MPa, I=570e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 1.249 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 5.6 m carries a UDL of 33 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.6, w = 33 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 33*(5.6)^2 / 12 | Answer: 86.24 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 360 mm, clear cover 25 mm and main bars of diameter 20 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 360, c = 25, dia = 20 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 360 - 25 - 20/2 | Answer: 325 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 26.4 m^2 carrying a factored load of 10 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 26.4, w = 10 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 10 * 26.4 | Answer: 264 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 6.8 m, unit weight 16 kN/m^3, phi = 34 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 7.7e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.3, area = 2.7e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 7.7, i = 0.3, A = 2.7 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (7.7e-4)*0.3*(2.7e-3) | Answer: 623.7 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 2.1 m, bed slope 0.003 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.019. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 3.7 m under a head of 0.5 m. Taking Cd = 0.62 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 4.2 m wide carries a discharge of 11.1 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 600 m and design speed 45 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 600, V = 45 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (45)^2 / (127*600) | Answer: 0.02657
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: For a design speed of 60 km/h with allowable superelevation 0.08 and lateral friction 0.16, find the minimum curve radius in m.
A tank of volume 490 m^3 treats a flow of 95 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 490, Q = 95 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 490 / 95 | Answer: 5.158 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 220 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.28 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 4 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 220, k = 0.28, t = 4 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 220*(1 - e^(-0.28*4)) | Answer: 148.2 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.61, rainfall intensity 50 mm/h over a catchment of 34.8 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.61, i = 50, A = 34.8 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.61*50*34.8 / 360 | Answer: 2.948 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.01 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 750 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.01, M = 750 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 750*(20+0.01)/20 | Answer: 750.4 m

question: Convert the decimal number 3711 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 3711 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: E7F (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the 8-bit binary number 01101100 to decimal.
solution: Binary 01101100 = sum of bit-weights | Answer: 108 (decimal)
formula: Sum each bit times its positional weight (2^i)

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 01011111 and 00001110.
solution: XOR: 01010001 | Count of 1s = 3 | Answer: 3
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 310 megabits is sent over a link of 50 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 310, B = 50 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 310 / 50 | Answer: 6.2 s

question: A link has bandwidth 39 Mbps and round-trip time 40 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 39, R = 40 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 39e6 * 40e-3 bits = 1560 kb | Answer: 1560 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.95, cache access time 1 ns and main-memory access time 90 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.95, tc = 1, tm = 90 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.95*1 + (1 - 0.95)*90 | Answer: 5.45 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 736733 elements?
solution: Given: n = 736733 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(736733)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: An O(n^2) algorithm performs c*n^2 basic operations. If c = 1 and n = 1890, how many operations are performed?
solution: Given: n = 1890 | Formula: operations = n^2 | Substitute: = (1890)^2 | Answer: 3572100

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.015, memory access time 180 ns and page-fault service time 9 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 9 ms = 9000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.015)*180 + 0.015*9000000.0 ns | Answer: 135.2 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 1.2 m^3 at 110 kPa and 450 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 1.2, P = 110, Tk = 450 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (110e3)*1.2 / (8.314*450) | Answer: 35.28 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.35 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 17 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.35, t = 17 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.35*17) | Answer: 0.9974

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.4 /min) is to reach 55% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.4, X = 55 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.55) / 0.4 | Answer: 1.996 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.23 /min) reaches 90% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.23, X = 90 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.9 / (0.23*(1 - 0.9)) | Answer: 39.13 min

question: For a reaction with A = 2e10 /s and activation energy 90 kJ/mol at 350 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 2, Ea = 90, Tk = 350 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 2e10 * exp(-90e3 / (8.314*350)) | Answer: 0.0007392 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.95 and bottoms xW = 0.06, with relative volatility alpha = 3.1. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.95, xw = 0.06, al = 3.1 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.95/0.05)(0.94/0.06)] / ln(3.1) | Answer: 5.034 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.58 and x = 0.42. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.58, x = 0.42 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.58/0.42) / (0.42/0.58) | Answer: 1.907

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.7 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 115 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.7, Psat = 115 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.7 * 115 | Answer: 80.5 kPa

question: A stream of 9.5 kg/s with specific heat 2.1 kJ/kg-K is heated through 20 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 9.5, cp = 2.1, dT = 20 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 9.5*2.1*20 | Answer: 399 kW

question: A reactor of volume 2.6 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 3.8 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 2.6, Q = 3.8 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 2.6 / 3.8 | Answer: 0.6842 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 5.5e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 5 mm with a concentration difference of 140 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 5.5, L = 5, dC = 140 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (5.5e-9)*140 / (5e-3) | Answer: 154 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 3.5 min and steady-state gain 0.9. For a step input of magnitude 6, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 3.5, K = 0.9, M = 6 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 0.9 * 6 | Answer: 5.4 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 60 m^2 flies at 170 m/s (air density 0.7 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.4. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 60, V = 170, rho = 0.7, CL = 0.4 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.7*(170)^2*60*0.4 / 1000 | Answer: 242.8 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 70 m^2 flies at 240 m/s (density 0.4 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.04. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 70, V = 240, rho = 0.4, CD = 0.04 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.4*(240)^2*70*0.04 / 1000 | Answer: 32.26 kN

question: A specimen under stress 340 MPa shows an elastic strain of 2.5e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 340, eps = 2.5 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 340 / (2.5e-3) MPa = 136 GPa | Answer: 136 GPa

question: A block of mass 25 kg has a volume of 5.9e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 25, V = 5.9 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 25 / (5.9e-3) | Answer: 4237 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 3000 mm is heated through 125 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 11e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 3000, dT = 125, al = 11 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 3000*11e-6*125 | Answer: 4.125 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 115 ohm, R2 = 70 ohm and R3 = 235 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 115, R2 = 70, R3 = 235 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 70*235 / 115 | Answer: 143 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 1000 ohm and gauge factor 2.1 experiences a strain of 800e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 1000, GF = 2.1, eps = 800 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 1000*2.1*800e-6 | Answer: 1680 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 9.79 when the true value is 10. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.79, true = 10 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.79 - 10| / 10 * 100 | Answer: 2.1 %

question: Annual demand is 5500 units, ordering cost 300 per order and holding cost 27 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 5500, S = 300, H = 27 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*5500*300 / 27) | Answer: 349.6 units

question: An asset costs 70000 with salvage value 12000 after 20 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 70000, Sv = 12000, n = 20 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (70000 - 12000) / 20 | Answer: 2900 per year

question: A product sells for 400 per unit with variable cost 110 per unit and fixed costs 190000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 400, V = 110, F = 190000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 190000 / (400 - 110) | Answer: 655.2 units

question: Find the present worth of 150000 received 2 years from now at an interest rate of 7% per year.
solution: Given: F = 150000, n = 2, i = 7 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 150000 / (1 + 0.07)^2 | Answer: 131016 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.96, 0.95 and 0.95 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.96, r2 = 0.95, r3 = 0.95 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.96*0.95*0.95 | Answer: 0.8664

question: A process produces 33 defective items in a batch of 13000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 33, N = 13000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 33/13000 * 1e6 | Answer: 2538 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -x^3 - 6x^2 - 4x - 6 evaluated at x = 5.
For f(x) = -2x^3 - 6x^2 - 9x + 8, find f''(x) at x = -5.
Evaluate the definite integral of (3x^2 + 5x + 5) dx from x = -3 to x = 7.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = 3x^3/3 + 5x^2/2 + 5x | Evaluate F(7) - F(-3) | Answer: 520
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of x^2 - 6x + 4 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[-8, 7], [2, 7]].
solution: Given: a = -8, b = 7, c = 2, d = 7 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (-8)(7) - (7)(2) | Answer: -70

question: Find the determinant of [[3, 3, -5], [6, -4, 6], [3, -2, -3]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: 180

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[2, 2], [-5, -7]].
solution: Trace tr = -5, Determinant = -4 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 0.7016

question: Solve for x: -4x + -3y = -8 and 1x + -4y = -11.
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 81, 43, 72, 24, 89.
solution: Sum = 309 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 61.8 | Answer: 61.8

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 19, 33, 9, 44, 2.
solution: Mean = 21.4 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 17.18

question: Find the slope of the line through (1, 8) and (2, 1).
solution: Given: x1 = 1, y1 = 8, x2 = 2, y2 = 1 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (1 - 8) / (2 - 1) | Answer: -7

question: Find the distance between the points (8, 9) and (-3, -5).
solution: Given: x1 = 8, y1 = 9, x2 = -3, y2 = -5 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-11)^2 + (-14)^2) | Answer: 17.8 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (-4,4), (-6,-5), (5,-4).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 48.5 sq units

question: Find the 32th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 4 and common difference -8.
solution: Given: a = 4, d = -8, n = 32 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = 4 + (32 - 1)*-8 | Answer: -244

question: Find the sum of the first 17 terms of an AP with first term -12 and common difference -3.
solution: Given: a = -12, d = -3, n = 17 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 17/2 [2*-12 + (17-1)*-3] | Answer: -612

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 37500 at 4% per annum for 8 years.
solution: Given: P = 37500, R = 4, Tt = 8 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 37500 * 4 * 8 / 100 | Answer: 12000 currency units

question: Find the amount when 35500 is invested at 7.4% per annum compounded annually for 6 years.
solution: Given: P = 35500, R = 7.4, Tt = 6 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 35500 * (1 + 7.4/100)^6 | Answer: 54482 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (1, -7, -6) and (2, 3, -7).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (4, 3, -5) and (3, 0, 5).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 39.13

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (6, -1, -4) and (-6, -3, -5).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 102.3 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number -5 + 4i.
solution: Given: a = -5, b = 4 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((-5)^2 + (4)^2) | Answer: 6.403

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number -10 + -4i.
solution: Given: a = -10, b = -4 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(-4, -10) | Answer: -158.2 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = 3x^3 + 5x^2 + 7x - 4 at x = 5.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-33 with initial guess x0=2, find x1 (one iteration).
solution: Given: N = 33, x0 = 2 | Formula: x1 = x0 - (x0^2 - N)/(2 x0) | Substitute: x1 = 2 - ((2)^2 - 33)/(2*2) | Answer: 9.25

question: Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.5 and ordinates 15, 18, 2, 18, 18, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 468 and 215.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 468 and 215 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 70 and 64.
solution: Given: a = 70, b = 64 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 70*64 / 2 | Answer: 2240
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 40 mm carries an axial tensile load of 18 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 28 mm and length 3000 mm carries an axial load of 55 kN. Take E = 110 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 57 mm transmits a torque of 1750 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 57, Tt = 1750 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(1750*1000) / (pi*(57)^3) | Answer: 48.13 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 69 mm and length 800 mm carries a torque of 450 N-m. With G = 77 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (69)^4 / 32 = 2225339 mm^4 | theta = (450*1000)(800) / (77000 * 2225339) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 0.1204 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 144 mm wide and 80 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 144, h = 80 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 144*(80)^2 / 6 | Answer: 153600 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (105 mm x 200 mm) carries a bending moment of 8 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (38 mm x 110 mm) has effective length 3300 mm and E = 200 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 480 MPa is designed for a working stress of 60 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 480, sw = 60 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 480 / 60 | Answer: 8

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 650 mm and wall thickness 15 mm carries an internal pressure of 2.7 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 650, t = 15, P = 2.7 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 2.7*650 / (2*15) | Answer: 58.5 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 680 K and 330 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 680, Tc = 330 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 330/680) * 100 | Answer: 51.47 %

question: 7.1 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 70 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 7.1, dT = 70 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 7.1 * 0.718 * 70 | Answer: 356.8 kJ

question: 3.8 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 175 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.8, dT = 175 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 3.8 * 1.005 * 175 | Answer: 668.3 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 1.5 m^3 at 600 K with mass 1.7 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 1.5, Tk = 600, m = 1.7 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 1.7*0.287*600 / 1.5 | Answer: 195.2 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 1 kg of air expands isothermally at 350 K from volume V1 to 2*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1, Tk = 350, ratio = 2 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 1*0.287*350*ln(2) | Answer: 69.63 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 4.1 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.32 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 4.1, D = 0.32 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*4.1*0.32 / 0.001 | Answer: 1312000

question: Water flows at 3.4 m/s through a pipe of diameter 130 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 19.3 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 19.3 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*19.3 / 1000 | Answer: 189.3 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 18 m. Taking Cv = 0.98, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 18, cv = 0.98 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.98*sqrt(2*9.81*18) | Answer: 18.42 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 270 mm) water flows at 2.3 m/s. It contracts to diameter 70 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 270, d2 = 70, V1 = 2.3 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 2.3*(270/70)^2 | Answer: 34.22 m/s

question: Water flows at 3.8 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.31 m and length 70 m. With friction factor f = 0.036, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 31 teeth drives a gear of 119 teeth. If the pinion runs at 800 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 31, z2 = 119, N1 = 800 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 800*31 / 119 | Answer: 208.4 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 150 mm rotates at 1050 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 150, N = 1050 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.15)*1050 / 60 | Answer: 8.247 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 36.5 kW at 250 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 36.5, N = 250 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(36.5*1000) / (2*pi*250) | Answer: 1394 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 6.1 kg rotates at radius 0.49 m at 200 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 15600 N/m and mass 3.2 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 15600, m = 3.2 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(15600/3.2) | Answer: 11.11 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 9.6 m^2 and thickness 0.22 m has conductivity k = 48.8 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 95 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 9.6, L = 0.22, k = 48.8, dT = 95 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 48.8*9.6*95 / 0.22 | Answer: 202298 W

question: A surface of area 2.3 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 200 W/m^2-K to surroundings 145 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 2.3, h = 200, dT = 145 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 200*2.3*145 | Answer: 66700 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 240 m/min, feed = 0.23 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2.6 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 240, f = 0.23, d = 2.6 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*240*0.23*2.6 | Answer: 143520 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 350 mm is turned at 800 rpm with a feed of 0.17 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 350, N = 800, f = 0.17 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 350 / (0.17*800) | Answer: 2.574 min

question: A resistor of 198 ohm carries a current of 4.3 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 198, I = 4.3 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 4.3 * 198 | Answer: 851.4 V

question: Three resistors 77 ohm, 1 ohm and 98 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 77, R2 = 1, R3 = 98 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 77 + 1 + 98 | Answer: 176 ohm

question: Two resistors 42 ohm and 4 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 42, R2 = 4 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 42*4 / (42+4) | Answer: 3.652 ohm

question: A device draws 0.3 A at 215 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 215, I = 0.3 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 215 * 0.3 | Answer: 64.5 W

question: A current of 9.2 A flows through a 78 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 9.2, R = 78 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (9.2)^2 * 78 | Answer: 6602 W

question: Two capacitors 39.6 uF and 5 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 39.6, C2 = 5 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 39.6*5 / (39.6+5) | Answer: 4.439 uF

question: A resistor 15 kohm and capacitor 1.3 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 15, C = 1.3 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (15k)(1.3u) = 19.5 ms | Answer: 19.5 ms

question: An inductor 78.4 mH is in series with 36 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 78.4, R = 36 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (78.4e-3) / 36 | Answer: 2.178 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 173 mH inductor at 620 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 173, f = 620 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (620)(173e-3) | Answer: 673.9 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 34.2 uF capacitor at 250 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 34.2, f = 250 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (250)(34.2e-6)) | Answer: 18.61 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 7 ohm, XL = 113 ohm and XC = 148 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 7, XL = 113, XC = 148 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(7^2 + (113 - 148)^2) | Answer: 35.69 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 11.4 mH and C = 3.9 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 11.4, C = 3.9 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(11.4e-3 * 3.9e-6)) | Answer: 754.8 Hz

question: A capacitor of 64.9 uF is charged to 75 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 64.9, V = 75 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*64.9e-6*(75)^2 | Answer: 182.5 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 280 V with 440 primary turns and 460 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 280, N1 = 440, N2 = 460 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 280 * 460/440 | Answer: 292.7 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 150 V and draws an armature current of 6 A. If the armature resistance is 0.46 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 150, Ia = 6, Ra = 0.46 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 150 - 6*0.46 | Answer: 147.2 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 70 A at 433 V (line) with a power factor of 0.95. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 70, VL = 433, pf = 0.95 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*433*70*0.95 / 1000 | Answer: 49.87 kW

question: A load has real power 15 kW and apparent power 145 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 15, S = 145 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 15 / 145 | Answer: 0.1034

question: A machine delivers 155 kW output while drawing 212 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 155, Pi = 212 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 155/212 * 100 | Answer: 73.11 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 8 V across R1 = 29 ohm and R2 = 24 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 8, R1 = 29, R2 = 24 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 8*24 / (29+24) | Answer: 3.623 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 190 kohm and Rin = 3 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 190, Rin = 3 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 190 / 3 | Answer: 63.33

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 170 kohm and Rg = 31 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 170, Rg = 31 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 170/31 | Answer: 6.484

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 9172. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 9172 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(9172) | Answer: 39.62 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.3 m carries a central point load of 75 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 9.3, W = 75 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 75*9.3 / 4 | Answer: 174.4 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 5.9 m carries a UDL of 30 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.9, w = 30 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 30*(5.9)^2 / 8 | Answer: 130.5 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 4.4 m carries a point load 50 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.4, W = 50 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 50*4.4 | Answer: 220 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 1.5 m carries a UDL of 22 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 1.5, w = 22 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 22*(1.5)^2 / 2 | Answer: 24.75 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 8.8 m carries a point load 40 kN at distance 3.1 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 8.8, a = 3.1, W = 40 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 40*(8.8 - 3.1) / 8.8 | Answer: 25.91 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 3.1 m) carries a central point load 70 kN. With E = 25 GPa and I = 110e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=70000 N, L=3100.0 mm, E=25000 MPa, I=110e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 15.8 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 5.4 m carries a UDL of 39 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.4, w = 39 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 39*(5.4)^2 / 12 | Answer: 94.77 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 330 mm, clear cover 50 mm and main bars of diameter 12 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 330, c = 50, dia = 12 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 330 - 50 - 12/2 | Answer: 274 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 20.6 m^2 carrying a factored load of 17.2 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 20.6, w = 17.2 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 17.2 * 20.6 | Answer: 354.3 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 4 m, unit weight 16 kN/m^3, phi = 35 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 5.2 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 18 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 5.2, g = 18 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (18 - 9.81)*5.2 | Answer: 42.59 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 7.4e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1.4, area = 6e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 7.4, i = 1.4, A = 6 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (7.4e-4)*1.4*(6e-3) | Answer: 6216 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 0.8 m, bed slope 0.01 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.016. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 4.6 m under a head of 0.9 m. Taking Cd = 0.61 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.

question: A rectangular channel 5.8 m wide carries a discharge of 7.6 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).

question: For a design speed of 90 km/h with allowable superelevation 0.07 and lateral friction 0.16, find the minimum curve radius in m.
A tank of volume 590 m^3 treats a flow of 130 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 590, Q = 130 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 590 / 130 | Answer: 4.538 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 170 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.14 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 5 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 170, k = 0.14, t = 5 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 170*(1 - e^(-0.14*5)) | Answer: 85.58 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.88, rainfall intensity 110 mm/h over a catchment of 40.6 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.88, i = 110, A = 40.6 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.88*110*40.6 / 360 | Answer: 10.92 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.05 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 160 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.05, M = 160 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 160*(30+0.05)/30 | Answer: 160.3 m

solution: XOR: 00001100 | Count of 1s = 2 | Answer: 2

question: A file of 820 megabits is sent over a link of 24 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 820, B = 24 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 820 / 24 | Answer: 34.17 s

question: A link has bandwidth 55 Mbps and round-trip time 140 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 55, R = 140 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 55e6 * 140e-3 bits = 7700 kb | Answer: 7700 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.95, cache access time 6 ns and main-memory access time 130 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.95, tc = 6, tm = 130 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.95*6 + (1 - 0.95)*130 | Answer: 12.2 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 93256 elements?
solution: Given: n = 93256 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(93256)) + 1 | Answer: 17

question: An O(n^2) algorithm performs c*n^2 basic operations. If c = 1 and n = 2060, how many operations are performed?
solution: Given: n = 2060 | Formula: operations = n^2 | Substitute: = (2060)^2 | Answer: 4243600

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.011, memory access time 170 ns and page-fault service time 5 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 5 ms = 5000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.011)*170 + 0.011*5000000.0 ns | Answer: 55.17 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 2.3 m^3 at 490 kPa and 500 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 2.3, P = 490, Tk = 500 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (490e3)*2.3 / (8.314*500) | Answer: 271.1 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.09 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 2 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.09, t = 2 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.09*2) | Answer: 0.1647

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.29 /min) is to reach 80% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.29, X = 80 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.8) / 0.29 | Answer: 5.55 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.5 /min) reaches 85% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.5, X = 85 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.85 / (0.5*(1 - 0.85)) | Answer: 11.33 min

question: For a reaction with A = 6e10 /s and activation energy 50 kJ/mol at 330 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 6, Ea = 50, Tk = 330 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 6e10 * exp(-50e3 / (8.314*330)) | Answer: 730.3 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.92 and bottoms xW = 0.04, with relative volatility alpha = 1.9. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.92, xw = 0.04, al = 1.9 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.92/0.08)(0.96/0.04)] / ln(1.9) | Answer: 8.757 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.74 and x = 0.22. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.74, x = 0.22 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.74/0.26) / (0.22/0.78) | Answer: 10.09

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.12 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 95 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.12, Psat = 95 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.12 * 95 | Answer: 11.4 kPa

question: A stream of 1.3 kg/s with specific heat 1 kJ/kg-K is heated through 70 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 1.3, cp = 1, dT = 70 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 1.3*1*70 | Answer: 91 kW

question: A reactor of volume 11.8 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 1.9 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 11.8, Q = 1.9 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 11.8 / 1.9 | Answer: 6.211 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 2.7e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 2 mm with a concentration difference of 80 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 2.7, L = 2, dC = 80 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (2.7e-9)*80 / (2e-3) | Answer: 108 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 1.1 min and steady-state gain 4. For a step input of magnitude 19, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 1.1, K = 4, M = 19 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 4 * 19 | Answer: 76 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 45 m^2 flies at 250 m/s (air density 1.225 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.6. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 45, V = 250, rho = 1.225, CL = 0.6 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1.225*(250)^2*45*0.6 / 1000 | Answer: 1034 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 50 m^2 flies at 140 m/s (density 0.4 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.03. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 50, V = 140, rho = 0.4, CD = 0.03 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.4*(140)^2*50*0.03 / 1000 | Answer: 5.88 kN

question: A specimen under stress 390 MPa shows an elastic strain of 2.4e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 390, eps = 2.4 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 390 / (2.4e-3) MPa = 162.5 GPa | Answer: 162.5 GPa

question: A block of mass 20 kg has a volume of 2.5e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 20, V = 2.5 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 20 / (2.5e-3) | Answer: 8000 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 900 mm is heated through 115 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 12e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 900, dT = 115, al = 12 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 900*12e-6*115 | Answer: 1.242 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 195 ohm, R2 = 195 ohm and R3 = 30 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 195, R2 = 195, R3 = 30 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 195*30 / 195 | Answer: 30 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 350 ohm and gauge factor 2.2 experiences a strain of 150e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 350, GF = 2.2, eps = 150 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 350*2.2*150e-6 | Answer: 115.5 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 9.9 when the true value is 20. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.9, true = 20 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.9 - 20| / 20 * 100 | Answer: 50.5 %

question: Annual demand is 7500 units, ordering cost 270 per order and holding cost 33 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 7500, S = 270, H = 33 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*7500*270 / 33) | Answer: 350.3 units

question: An asset costs 440000 with salvage value 34000 after 13 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 440000, Sv = 34000, n = 13 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (440000 - 34000) / 13 | Answer: 31231 per year

question: A product sells for 220 per unit with variable cost 50 per unit and fixed costs 40000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 220, V = 50, F = 40000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 40000 / (220 - 50) | Answer: 235.3 units

question: Find the present worth of 145000 received 4 years from now at an interest rate of 10% per year.
solution: Given: F = 145000, n = 4, i = 10 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 145000 / (1 + 0.1)^4 | Answer: 99037 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.96, 0.92 and 0.93 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.96, r2 = 0.92, r3 = 0.93 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.96*0.92*0.93 | Answer: 0.8214

question: A process produces 42 defective items in a batch of 15000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 42, N = 15000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 42/15000 * 1e6 | Answer: 2800 PPM

question: Solve for x: 2x + -6y = 1 and -2x + 3y = 8.

question: Find the slope of the line through (7, 7) and (-2, -1).
