question: Find the amount when 17500 is invested at 11.3% per annum compounded annually for 5 years.
solution: Given: P = 17500, R = 11.3, Tt = 5 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 17500 * (1 + 11.3/100)^5 | Answer: 29889 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (7, 3, -3) and (6, -4, -7).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (-6, 1, -1) and (-5, 1, 0).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 5.196

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (-2, -2, -3) and (6, 6, 3).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 152.8 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number 5 + -12i.
solution: Given: a = 5, b = -12 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((5)^2 + (-12)^2) | Answer: 13

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number -9 + -9i.
solution: Given: a = -9, b = -9 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(-9, -9) | Answer: -135 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -5x^3 - 6x^2 + 3x - 4 at x = -4.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-29 with initial guess x0=7, find x1 (one iteration).
solution: Given: N = 29, x0 = 7 | Formula: x1 = x0 - (x0^2 - N)/(2 x0) | Substitute: x1 = 7 - ((7)^2 - 29)/(2*7) | Answer: 5.571

question: Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.7 and ordinates 13, 15, 19, 3, 5, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 377 and 514.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 377 and 514 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 58 and 64.
solution: Given: a = 58, b = 64 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 58*64 / 2 | Answer: 1856
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 20 mm carries an axial tensile load of 87 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 17 mm and length 2900 mm carries an axial load of 48 kN. Take E = 110 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 26 mm transmits a torque of 1000 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 26, Tt = 1000 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(1000*1000) / (pi*(26)^3) | Answer: 289.8 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 25 mm and length 700 mm carries a torque of 1900 N-m. With G = 77 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (25)^4 / 32 = 3835 mm^4 | theta = (1900*1000)(700) / (77000 * 3835) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 25.81 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 33 mm wide and 280 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 33, h = 280 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 33*(280)^2 / 6 | Answer: 431200 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (72 mm x 160 mm) carries a bending moment of 26 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (40 mm x 100 mm) has effective length 2800 mm and E = 200 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 320 MPa is designed for a working stress of 90 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 320, sw = 90 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 320 / 90 | Answer: 3.556

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 900 mm and wall thickness 15 mm carries an internal pressure of 2.3 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 900, t = 15, P = 2.3 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 2.3*900 / (2*15) | Answer: 69 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 940 K and 300 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 940, Tc = 300 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 300/940) * 100 | Answer: 68.09 %

question: A refrigerator works between 269 K (cold) and 326 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 269, Th = 326 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 269 / (326 - 269) | Answer: 4.719

question: A heat pump operates between 284 K and 318 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 284, Th = 318 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 318 / (318 - 284) | Answer: 9.353

question: 1.1 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 120 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1.1, dT = 120 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 1.1 * 0.718 * 120 | Answer: 94.78 kJ

question: 1 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 50 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1, dT = 50 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 1 * 1.005 * 50 | Answer: 50.25 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 1.9 m^3 at 560 K with mass 2.6 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 1.9, Tk = 560, m = 2.6 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 2.6*0.287*560 / 1.9 | Answer: 219.9 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 4.9 kg of air expands isothermally at 460 K from volume V1 to 5*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.9, Tk = 460, ratio = 5 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 4.9*0.287*460*ln(5) | Answer: 1041 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 1.7 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.09 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 1.7, D = 0.09 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*1.7*0.09 / 0.001 | Answer: 153000

question: Water flows at 1.3 m/s through a pipe of diameter 180 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 28.6 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 28.6 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*28.6 / 1000 | Answer: 280.6 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 12.3 m. Taking Cv = 0.99, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 12.3, cv = 0.99 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.99*sqrt(2*9.81*12.3) | Answer: 15.38 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 170 mm) water flows at 1.6 m/s. It contracts to diameter 140 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
Water flows at 1.9 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.12 m and length 300 m. With friction factor f = 0.022, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 39 teeth drives a gear of 69 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1400 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 39, z2 = 69, N1 = 1400 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1400*39 / 69 | Answer: 791.3 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 240 mm rotates at 200 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 240, N = 200 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.24)*200 / 60 | Answer: 2.513 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 11.5 kW at 650 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 11.5, N = 650 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(11.5*1000) / (2*pi*650) | Answer: 168.9 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 5.9 kg rotates at radius 0.29 m at 300 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 2700 N/m and mass 18.4 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 2700, m = 18.4 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(2700/18.4) | Answer: 1.928 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 8 m^2 and thickness 0.3 m has conductivity k = 8.3 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 110 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 8, L = 0.3, k = 8.3, dT = 110 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 8.3*8*110 / 0.3 | Answer: 24347 W

question: A surface of area 3.6 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 75 W/m^2-K to surroundings 150 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 3.6, h = 75, dT = 150 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 75*3.6*150 | Answer: 40500 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 150 m/min, feed = 0.22 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2.3 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 150, f = 0.22, d = 2.3 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*150*0.22*2.3 | Answer: 75900 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 360 mm is turned at 600 rpm with a feed of 0.31 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 360, N = 600, f = 0.31 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 360 / (0.31*600) | Answer: 1.935 min

question: A resistor of 29 ohm carries a current of 0.1 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 29, I = 0.1 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 0.1 * 29 | Answer: 2.9 V

question: Three resistors 14 ohm, 55 ohm and 67 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 14, R2 = 55, R3 = 67 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 14 + 55 + 67 | Answer: 136 ohm

question: Two resistors 34 ohm and 78 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 34, R2 = 78 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 34*78 / (34+78) | Answer: 23.68 ohm

question: A device draws 3.8 A at 50 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 50, I = 3.8 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 50 * 3.8 | Answer: 190 W

question: A current of 10.4 A flows through a 108 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 10.4, R = 108 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (10.4)^2 * 108 | Answer: 11681 W

question: Two capacitors 35 uF and 10.4 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 35, C2 = 10.4 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 35*10.4 / (35+10.4) | Answer: 8.018 uF

question: A resistor 19 kohm and capacitor 18.2 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 19, C = 18.2 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (19k)(18.2u) = 345.8 ms | Answer: 345.8 ms

question: An inductor 374.2 mH is in series with 6 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 374.2, R = 6 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (374.2e-3) / 6 | Answer: 62.37 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 161.9 mH inductor at 190 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 161.9, f = 190 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (190)(161.9e-3) | Answer: 193.3 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 16.2 uF capacitor at 840 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 16.2, f = 840 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (840)(16.2e-6)) | Answer: 11.7 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 54 ohm, XL = 149 ohm and XC = 51 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 54, XL = 149, XC = 51 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(54^2 + (149 - 51)^2) | Answer: 111.9 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 53.6 mH and C = 0.6 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 53.6, C = 0.6 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(53.6e-3 * 0.6e-6)) | Answer: 887.5 Hz

question: A capacitor of 31.9 uF is charged to 260 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 31.9, V = 260 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*31.9e-6*(260)^2 | Answer: 1078 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 370 V with 530 primary turns and 250 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 370, N1 = 530, N2 = 250 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 370 * 250/530 | Answer: 174.5 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 160 V and draws an armature current of 47 A. If the armature resistance is 1.42 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 160, Ia = 47, Ra = 1.42 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 160 - 47*1.42 | Answer: 93.26 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 80 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.81. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 80, VL = 400, pf = 0.81 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*400*80*0.81 / 1000 | Answer: 44.89 kW

question: A load has real power 105 kW and apparent power 130 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 105, S = 130 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 105 / 130 | Answer: 0.8077

question: A machine delivers 100 kW output while drawing 212 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 100, Pi = 212 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 100/212 * 100 | Answer: 47.17 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 6 V across R1 = 13 ohm and R2 = 39 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 6, R1 = 13, R2 = 39 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 6*39 / (13+39) | Answer: 4.5 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 120 kohm and Rin = 19 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 120, Rin = 19 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 120 / 19 | Answer: 6.316

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 180 kohm and Rg = 39 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 180, Rg = 39 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 180/39 | Answer: 5.615

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 5460. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 5460 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(5460) | Answer: 37.37 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.1 m carries a central point load of 55 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6.1, W = 55 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 55*6.1 / 4 | Answer: 83.88 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.9 m carries a UDL of 40 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 9.9, w = 40 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 40*(9.9)^2 / 8 | Answer: 490.1 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 1.1 m carries a point load 30 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 1.1, W = 30 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 30*1.1 | Answer: 33 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 5.6 m carries a UDL of 16 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.6, w = 16 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 16*(5.6)^2 / 2 | Answer: 250.9 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 8.8 m carries a point load 55 kN at distance 3.8 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 8.8, a = 3.8, W = 55 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 55*(8.8 - 3.8) / 8.8 | Answer: 31.25 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 4.8 m) carries a central point load 50 kN. With E = 200 GPa and I = 340e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.

question: A fixed beam of span 7.5 m carries a UDL of 42 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7.5, w = 42 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 42*(7.5)^2 / 12 | Answer: 196.9 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 370 mm, clear cover 45 mm and main bars of diameter 20 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 370, c = 45, dia = 20 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 370 - 45 - 20/2 | Answer: 315 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 24.6 m^2 carrying a factored load of 20 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 24.6, w = 20 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 20 * 24.6 | Answer: 492 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 6.8 m, unit weight 19 kN/m^3, phi = 38 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 9.1 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 19 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 9.1, g = 19 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (19 - 9.81)*9.1 | Answer: 83.63 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 1.1e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.8, area = 3.4e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 1.1, i = 0.8, A = 3.4 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (1.1e-4)*0.8*(3.4e-3) | Answer: 299.2 mm^3/s

question: For a design speed of 95 km/h with allowable superelevation 0.08 and lateral friction 0.14, find the minimum curve radius in m.
A tank of volume 510 m^3 treats a flow of 60 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 510, Q = 60 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 510 / 60 | Answer: 8.5 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 280 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.12 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 4 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 280, k = 0.12, t = 4 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 280*(1 - e^(-0.12*4)) | Answer: 106.7 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.54, rainfall intensity 105 mm/h over a catchment of 57.7 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.54, i = 105, A = 57.7 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.54*105*57.7 / 360 | Answer: 9.088 m^3/s

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.04 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 590 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.04, M = 590 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 590*(30+0.04)/30 | Answer: 590.8 m

solution: Binary 00011101 = sum of bit-weights | Answer: 29 (decimal)

question: A file of 930 megabits is sent over a link of 33 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 930, B = 33 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 930 / 33 | Answer: 28.18 s

question: A link has bandwidth 76 Mbps and round-trip time 80 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 76, R = 80 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 76e6 * 80e-3 bits = 6080 kb | Answer: 6080 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.81, cache access time 3 ns and main-memory access time 190 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.81, tc = 3, tm = 190 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.81*3 + (1 - 0.81)*190 | Answer: 38.53 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 643409 elements?
solution: Given: n = 643409 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(643409)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.004, memory access time 160 ns and page-fault service time 9 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 9 ms = 9000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.004)*160 + 0.004*9000000.0 ns | Answer: 36.16 microseconds

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 0.2 m^3 at 220 kPa and 450 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 0.2, P = 220, Tk = 450 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (220e3)*0.2 / (8.314*450) | Answer: 11.76 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.11 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 17 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.11, t = 17 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.11*17) | Answer: 0.8459

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.16 /min) is to reach 80% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.16, X = 80 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.8) / 0.16 | Answer: 10.06 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.4 /min) reaches 80% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.4, X = 80 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.8 / (0.4*(1 - 0.8)) | Answer: 10 min

question: For a reaction with A = 6e10 /s and activation energy 60 kJ/mol at 350 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 6, Ea = 60, Tk = 350 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 6e10 * exp(-60e3 / (8.314*350)) | Answer: 66.58 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.92 and bottoms xW = 0.03, with relative volatility alpha = 3.1. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.92, xw = 0.03, al = 3.1 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.92/0.08)(0.97/0.03)] / ln(3.1) | Answer: 5.231 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.73 and x = 0.41. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.73, x = 0.41 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.73/0.27) / (0.41/0.59) | Answer: 3.891

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.46 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 40 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.46, Psat = 40 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.46 * 40 | Answer: 18.4 kPa

question: A stream of 4.6 kg/s with specific heat 3.6 kJ/kg-K is heated through 20 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 4.6, cp = 3.6, dT = 20 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 4.6*3.6*20 | Answer: 331.2 kW

question: A reactor of volume 19.6 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 4.1 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 19.6, Q = 4.1 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 19.6 / 4.1 | Answer: 4.78 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 3.5e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 3 mm with a concentration difference of 100 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 3.5, L = 3, dC = 100 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (3.5e-9)*100 / (3e-3) | Answer: 116.7 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 2.6 min and steady-state gain 0.8. For a step input of magnitude 10, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 2.6, K = 0.8, M = 10 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 0.8 * 10 | Answer: 8 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 60 m^2 flies at 150 m/s (air density 1 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.3. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 60, V = 150, rho = 1, CL = 0.3 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1*(150)^2*60*0.3 / 1000 | Answer: 202.5 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 90 m^2 flies at 180 m/s (density 1 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.02. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 90, V = 180, rho = 1, CD = 0.02 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*1*(180)^2*90*0.02 / 1000 | Answer: 29.16 kN

question: A specimen under stress 280 MPa shows an elastic strain of 2.1e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 280, eps = 2.1 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 280 / (2.1e-3) MPa = 133.3 GPa | Answer: 133.3 GPa

question: A block of mass 33 kg has a volume of 5.1e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 33, V = 5.1 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 33 / (5.1e-3) | Answer: 6471 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 500 mm is heated through 75 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 23e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 500, dT = 75, al = 23 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 500*23e-6*75 | Answer: 0.8625 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 55 ohm, R2 = 95 ohm and R3 = 205 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 55, R2 = 95, R3 = 205 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 95*205 / 55 | Answer: 354.1 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 1000 ohm and gauge factor 2.1 experiences a strain of 700e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 1000, GF = 2.1, eps = 700 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 1000*2.1*700e-6 | Answer: 1470 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 9.28 when the true value is 50. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.28, true = 50 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.28 - 50| / 50 * 100 | Answer: 81.44 %

question: Annual demand is 39000 units, ordering cost 160 per order and holding cost 37 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 39000, S = 160, H = 37 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*39000*160 / 37) | Answer: 580.8 units

question: An asset costs 300000 with salvage value 8000 after 12 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 300000, Sv = 8000, n = 12 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (300000 - 8000) / 12 | Answer: 24333 per year

question: A product sells for 270 per unit with variable cost 70 per unit and fixed costs 55000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 270, V = 70, F = 55000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 55000 / (270 - 70) | Answer: 275 units

question: Find the present worth of 50000 received 5 years from now at an interest rate of 11% per year.
solution: Given: F = 50000, n = 5, i = 11 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 50000 / (1 + 0.11)^5 | Answer: 29673 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.9, 0.9 and 0.94 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.9, r2 = 0.9, r3 = 0.94 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.9*0.9*0.94 | Answer: 0.7614

question: A process produces 12 defective items in a batch of 16000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 12, N = 16000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 12/16000 * 1e6 | Answer: 750 PPM

question: Find the slope of the line through (-5, -3) and (-3, -7).
solution: Given: x1 = -5, y1 = -3, x2 = -3, y2 = -7 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (-7 - -3) / (-3 - -5) | Answer: -2

question: Find the distance between the points (6, 4) and (-9, 0).
solution: Given: x1 = 6, y1 = 4, x2 = -9, y2 = 0 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-15)^2 + (-4)^2) | Answer: 15.52 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (-4,3), (-2,4), (-8,-6).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 7 sq units

question: Evaluate the number of combinations C(19, 18).
solution: Given: n = 19, r = 18 | Formula: C(n, r) = n! / (r! (n - r)!) | Substitute: C(19, 18) = 19! / (18! * 1!) | Answer: 19

question: Find the 22th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 13 and common difference 2.
solution: Given: a = 13, d = 2, n = 22 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = 13 + (22 - 1)*2 | Answer: 55

question: Find the sum of the first 34 terms of an AP with first term -1 and common difference 4.
solution: Given: a = -1, d = 4, n = 34 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 34/2 [2*-1 + (34-1)*4] | Answer: 2210

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 10500 at 5.2% per annum for 4 years.
solution: Given: P = 10500, R = 5.2, Tt = 4 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 10500 * 5.2 * 4 / 100 | Answer: 2184 currency units

question: Find the amount when 34000 is invested at 11.7% per annum compounded annually for 5 years.
solution: Given: P = 34000, R = 11.7, Tt = 5 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 34000 * (1 + 11.7/100)^5 | Answer: 59121 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (6, 8, -6) and (-1, 3, -5).

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (6, -1, 5) and (1, 0, 1).

question: Find the modulus of the complex number 0 + 9i.
solution: Given: a = 0, b = 9 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((0)^2 + (9)^2) | Answer: 9

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number -3 + -1i.
solution: Given: a = -3, b = -1 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(-1, -3) | Answer: -161.6 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = 5x^3 - 6x^2 - 6x + 3 at x = -3.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-30 with initial guess x0=8, find x1 (one iteration).
solution: Given: N = 30, x0 = 8 | Formula: x1 = x0 - (x0^2 - N)/(2 x0) | Substitute: x1 = 8 - ((8)^2 - 30)/(2*8) | Answer: 5.875

question: Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.2 and ordinates 3, 5, 9, 12, 0, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 369 and 32.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 369 and 32 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 74 and 4.
solution: Given: a = 74, b = 4 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 74*4 / 2 | Answer: 148
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 40 mm carries an axial tensile load of 86 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 12 mm and length 3000 mm carries an axial load of 13 kN. Take E = 70 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 66 mm transmits a torque of 350 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 66, Tt = 350 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(350*1000) / (pi*(66)^3) | Answer: 6.2 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 69 mm and length 1500 mm carries a torque of 700 N-m. With G = 80 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (69)^4 / 32 = 2225339 mm^4 | theta = (700*1000)(1500) / (80000 * 2225339) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 0.3379 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 126 mm wide and 190 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 126, h = 190 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 126*(190)^2 / 6 | Answer: 758100 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (72 mm x 80 mm) carries a bending moment of 39 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (36 mm x 100 mm) has effective length 2200 mm and E = 200 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 720 MPa is designed for a working stress of 120 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 720, sw = 120 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 720 / 120 | Answer: 6

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 400 mm and wall thickness 15 mm carries an internal pressure of 0.9 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 400, t = 15, P = 0.9 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 0.9*400 / (2*15) | Answer: 12 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 700 K and 310 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 700, Tc = 310 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 310/700) * 100 | Answer: 55.71 %

question: A refrigerator works between 254 K (cold) and 314 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 254, Th = 314 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 254 / (314 - 254) | Answer: 4.233

question: A heat pump operates between 263 K and 322 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 263, Th = 322 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 322 / (322 - 263) | Answer: 5.458

question: 5.4 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 35 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 5.4, dT = 35 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 5.4 * 0.718 * 35 | Answer: 135.7 kJ

question: 2.8 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 25 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.8, dT = 25 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 2.8 * 1.005 * 25 | Answer: 70.35 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 3 m^3 at 430 K with mass 3 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 3, Tk = 430, m = 3 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 3*0.287*430 / 3 | Answer: 123.4 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 3.9 kg of air expands isothermally at 390 K from volume V1 to 4*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.9, Tk = 390, ratio = 4 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 3.9*0.287*390*ln(4) | Answer: 605.2 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 1.1 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.17 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 1.1, D = 0.17 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*1.1*0.17 / 0.001 | Answer: 187000

question: Water flows at 0.7 m/s through a pipe of diameter 200 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 17.5 m. Taking Cv = 0.98, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 17.5, cv = 0.98 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.98*sqrt(2*9.81*17.5) | Answer: 18.16 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 300 mm) water flows at 0.7 m/s. It contracts to diameter 110 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
Water flows at 3.1 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.16 m and length 100 m. With friction factor f = 0.021, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 40 teeth drives a gear of 101 teeth. If the pinion runs at 450 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 40, z2 = 101, N1 = 450 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 450*40 / 101 | Answer: 178.2 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 290 mm rotates at 700 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 290, N = 700 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.29)*700 / 60 | Answer: 10.63 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 16.6 kW at 550 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 16.6, N = 550 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(16.6*1000) / (2*pi*550) | Answer: 288.2 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 4.9 kg rotates at radius 0.26 m at 900 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 7800 N/m and mass 14.4 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 7800, m = 14.4 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(7800/14.4) | Answer: 3.704 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 5.2 m^2 and thickness 0.34 m has conductivity k = 48.4 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 65 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 5.2, L = 0.34, k = 48.4, dT = 65 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 48.4*5.2*65 / 0.34 | Answer: 48115 W

question: A surface of area 3.7 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 125 W/m^2-K to surroundings 90 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 3.7, h = 125, dT = 90 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 125*3.7*90 | Answer: 41625 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 170 m/min, feed = 0.45 mm/rev, depth of cut = 1.5 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 170, f = 0.45, d = 1.5 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*170*0.45*1.5 | Answer: 114750 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 160 mm is turned at 1150 rpm with a feed of 0.1 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 160, N = 1150, f = 0.1 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 160 / (0.1*1150) | Answer: 1.391 min

question: A resistor of 123 ohm carries a current of 4.7 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 123, I = 4.7 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 4.7 * 123 | Answer: 578.1 V

question: Three resistors 66 ohm, 46 ohm and 24 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 66, R2 = 46, R3 = 24 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 66 + 46 + 24 | Answer: 136 ohm

question: Two resistors 11 ohm and 14 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 11, R2 = 14 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 11*14 / (11+14) | Answer: 6.16 ohm

question: A device draws 14.2 A at 35 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 35, I = 14.2 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 35 * 14.2 | Answer: 497 W

question: A current of 10.3 A flows through a 116 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 10.3, R = 116 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (10.3)^2 * 116 | Answer: 12306 W

question: Two capacitors 22.9 uF and 5.3 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 22.9, C2 = 5.3 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 22.9*5.3 / (22.9+5.3) | Answer: 4.304 uF

question: A resistor 37 kohm and capacitor 8.6 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 37, C = 8.6 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (37k)(8.6u) = 318.2 ms | Answer: 318.2 ms

question: An inductor 243.2 mH is in series with 43 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 243.2, R = 43 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (243.2e-3) / 43 | Answer: 5.656 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 64.1 mH inductor at 70 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 64.1, f = 70 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (70)(64.1e-3) | Answer: 28.19 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 21.5 uF capacitor at 380 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 21.5, f = 380 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (380)(21.5e-6)) | Answer: 19.48 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 35 ohm, XL = 52 ohm and XC = 74 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 35, XL = 52, XC = 74 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(35^2 + (52 - 74)^2) | Answer: 41.34 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 98.2 mH and C = 6.5 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 98.2, C = 6.5 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(98.2e-3 * 6.5e-6)) | Answer: 199.2 Hz

question: A capacitor of 99 uF is charged to 155 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 99, V = 155 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*99e-6*(155)^2 | Answer: 1189 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 350 V with 830 primary turns and 270 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 350, N1 = 830, N2 = 270 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 350 * 270/830 | Answer: 113.9 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 210 V and draws an armature current of 16 A. If the armature resistance is 0.24 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 210, Ia = 16, Ra = 0.24 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 210 - 16*0.24 | Answer: 206.2 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 150 A at 433 V (line) with a power factor of 0.85. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 150, VL = 433, pf = 0.85 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*433*150*0.85 / 1000 | Answer: 95.62 kW

question: A load has real power 90 kW and apparent power 170 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 90, S = 170 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 90 / 170 | Answer: 0.5294

question: A machine delivers 175 kW output while drawing 212 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 175, Pi = 212 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 175/212 * 100 | Answer: 82.55 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 11 V across R1 = 18 ohm and R2 = 20 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 11, R1 = 18, R2 = 20 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 11*20 / (18+20) | Answer: 5.789 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 160 kohm and Rin = 4 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 160, Rin = 4 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 160 / 4 | Answer: 40

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 60 kohm and Rg = 15 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 60, Rg = 15 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 60/15 | Answer: 5

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 3582. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 3582 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(3582) | Answer: 35.54 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.8 m carries a central point load of 35 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.8, W = 35 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 35*4.8 / 4 | Answer: 42 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 8.6 m carries a UDL of 50 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 8.6, w = 50 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 50*(8.6)^2 / 8 | Answer: 462.2 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 1.1 m carries a point load 20 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 1.1, W = 20 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 20*1.1 | Answer: 22 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 3.7 m carries a UDL of 6 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.7, w = 6 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 6*(3.7)^2 / 2 | Answer: 41.07 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.2 m carries a point load 90 kN at distance 1.9 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 4.2, a = 1.9, W = 90 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 90*(4.2 - 1.9) / 4.2 | Answer: 49.29 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 6 m) carries a central point load 40 kN. With E = 25 GPa and I = 430e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=40000 N, L=6000.0 mm, E=25000 MPa, I=430e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 16.74 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 7.3 m carries a UDL of 27 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7.3, w = 27 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 27*(7.3)^2 / 12 | Answer: 119.9 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 540 mm, clear cover 45 mm and main bars of diameter 12 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 540, c = 45, dia = 12 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 540 - 45 - 12/2 | Answer: 489 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 29.8 m^2 carrying a factored load of 9.9 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 29.8, w = 9.9 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 9.9 * 29.8 | Answer: 295 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 3.4 m, unit weight 16 kN/m^3, phi = 33 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 8.1e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1.5, area = 4.6e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 8.1, i = 1.5, A = 4.6 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (8.1e-4)*1.5*(4.6e-3) | Answer: 5589 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.2 m, bed slope 0.009 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.018. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 1.3 m under a head of 0.3 m. Taking Cd = 0.61 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 4.8 m wide carries a discharge of 8.2 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 560 m and design speed 95 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 560, V = 95 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (95)^2 / (127*560) | Answer: 0.1269
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: A tank of volume 180 m^3 treats a flow of 145 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 180, Q = 145 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 180 / 145 | Answer: 1.241 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 230 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.27 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 3 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 230, k = 0.27, t = 3 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 230*(1 - e^(-0.27*3)) | Answer: 127.7 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.61, rainfall intensity 65 mm/h over a catchment of 13.6 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.61, i = 65, A = 13.6 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.61*65*13.6 / 360 | Answer: 1.498 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.07 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 730 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.07, M = 730 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 730*(30+0.07)/30 | Answer: 731.7 m

solution: Divide 3468 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: D8C (hex)

solution: Binary 01001100 = sum of bit-weights | Answer: 76 (decimal)
