question: Three resistors 2 ohm, 49 ohm and 99 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 2, R2 = 49, R3 = 99 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 2 + 49 + 99 | Answer: 150 ohm

question: Two resistors 36 ohm and 2 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 36, R2 = 2 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 36*2 / (36+2) | Answer: 1.895 ohm

question: A device draws 13.1 A at 35 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 35, I = 13.1 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 35 * 13.1 | Answer: 458.5 W

question: A current of 10.3 A flows through a 106 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 10.3, R = 106 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (10.3)^2 * 106 | Answer: 11246 W

question: Two capacitors 47.8 uF and 32.5 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 47.8, C2 = 32.5 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 47.8*32.5 / (47.8+32.5) | Answer: 19.35 uF

question: A resistor 65 kohm and capacitor 14.2 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 65, C = 14.2 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (65k)(14.2u) = 923 ms | Answer: 923 ms

question: An inductor 499.6 mH is in series with 200 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 499.6, R = 200 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (499.6e-3) / 200 | Answer: 2.498 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 37.6 mH inductor at 980 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 37.6, f = 980 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (980)(37.6e-3) | Answer: 231.5 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 18.6 uF capacitor at 360 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 18.6, f = 360 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (360)(18.6e-6)) | Answer: 23.77 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 5 ohm, XL = 107 ohm and XC = 85 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 5, XL = 107, XC = 85 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(5^2 + (107 - 85)^2) | Answer: 22.56 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 8 mH and C = 1.8 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 8, C = 1.8 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(8e-3 * 1.8e-6)) | Answer: 1326 Hz

question: A capacitor of 74.5 uF is charged to 145 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 74.5, V = 145 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*74.5e-6*(145)^2 | Answer: 783.2 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 180 V with 860 primary turns and 30 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 180, N1 = 860, N2 = 30 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 180 * 30/860 | Answer: 6.279 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 180 V and draws an armature current of 51 A. If the armature resistance is 0.22 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 180, Ia = 51, Ra = 0.22 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 180 - 51*0.22 | Answer: 168.8 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 60 A at 433 V (line) with a power factor of 0.96. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 60, VL = 433, pf = 0.96 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*433*60*0.96 / 1000 | Answer: 43.2 kW

question: A load has real power 150 kW and apparent power 210 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 150, S = 210 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 150 / 210 | Answer: 0.7143

question: A machine delivers 15 kW output while drawing 217 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 15, Pi = 217 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 15/217 * 100 | Answer: 6.912 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 17 V across R1 = 37 ohm and R2 = 41 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 17, R1 = 37, R2 = 41 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 17*41 / (37+41) | Answer: 8.936 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 90 kohm and Rin = 31 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 90, Rin = 31 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 90 / 31 | Answer: 2.903

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 30 kohm and Rg = 14 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 30, Rg = 14 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 30/14 | Answer: 3.143

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 2365. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 2365 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(2365) | Answer: 33.74 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 5.9 m carries a central point load of 75 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.9, W = 75 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 75*5.9 / 4 | Answer: 110.6 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 7.7 m carries a UDL of 40 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7.7, w = 40 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 40*(7.7)^2 / 8 | Answer: 296.5 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 2.1 m carries a point load 40 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 2.1, W = 40 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 40*2.1 | Answer: 84 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 4 m carries a UDL of 22 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4, w = 22 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 22*(4)^2 / 2 | Answer: 176 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 5.8 m carries a point load 15 kN at distance 3.6 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 5.8, a = 3.6, W = 15 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 15*(5.8 - 3.6) / 5.8 | Answer: 5.69 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 4.2 m) carries a central point load 45 kN. With E = 25 GPa and I = 210e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=45000 N, L=4200.0 mm, E=25000 MPa, I=210e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 13.23 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 5.7 m carries a UDL of 6 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.7, w = 6 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 6*(5.7)^2 / 12 | Answer: 16.25 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 360 mm, clear cover 40 mm and main bars of diameter 20 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 360, c = 40, dia = 20 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 360 - 40 - 20/2 | Answer: 310 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 11.1 m^2 carrying a factored load of 12.9 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 11.1, w = 12.9 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 12.9 * 11.1 | Answer: 143.2 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 5 m, unit weight 16 kN/m^3, phi = 34 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 11.4 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 18 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 11.4, g = 18 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (18 - 9.81)*11.4 | Answer: 93.37 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 2.4e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1.3, area = 5e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 2.4, i = 1.3, A = 5 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (2.4e-4)*1.3*(5e-3) | Answer: 1560 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 0.8 m, bed slope 0.007 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.021. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 4.4 m under a head of 0.9 m. Taking Cd = 0.62 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 4.2 m wide carries a discharge of 26.9 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).

solution: Given: R = 240, V = 55 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (55)^2 / (127*240) | Answer: 0.09925
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: For a design speed of 100 km/h with allowable superelevation 0.05 and lateral friction 0.16, find the minimum curve radius in m.
A tank of volume 560 m^3 treats a flow of 45 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 560, Q = 45 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 560 / 45 | Answer: 12.44 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 180 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.33 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 3 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 180, k = 0.33, t = 3 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 180*(1 - e^(-0.33*3)) | Answer: 113.1 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.48, rainfall intensity 75 mm/h over a catchment of 54.1 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.48, i = 75, A = 54.1 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.48*75*54.1 / 360 | Answer: 5.41 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.04 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 390 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.04, M = 390 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 390*(20+0.04)/20 | Answer: 390.8 m

question: Convert the decimal number 661 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 661 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 295 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 01111101 and 00100011.
solution: XOR: 01011110 | Count of 1s = 5 | Answer: 5
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 460 megabits is sent over a link of 23 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 460, B = 23 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 460 / 23 | Answer: 20 s

question: A link has bandwidth 38 Mbps and round-trip time 140 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 38, R = 140 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 38e6 * 140e-3 bits = 5320 kb | Answer: 5320 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.93, cache access time 8 ns and main-memory access time 150 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.93, tc = 8, tm = 150 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.93*8 + (1 - 0.93)*150 | Answer: 17.94 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 469705 elements?
solution: Given: n = 469705 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(469705)) + 1 | Answer: 19

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.016, memory access time 140 ns and page-fault service time 3 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 3 ms = 3000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.016)*140 + 0.016*3000000.0 ns | Answer: 48.14 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 2.3 m^3 at 350 kPa and 370 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 2.3, P = 350, Tk = 370 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (350e3)*2.3 / (8.314*370) | Answer: 261.7 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.11 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 12 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.11, t = 12 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.11*12) | Answer: 0.7329

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.17 /min) is to reach 55% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.17, X = 55 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.55) / 0.17 | Answer: 4.697 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.13 /min) reaches 75% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.13, X = 75 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.75 / (0.13*(1 - 0.75)) | Answer: 23.08 min

question: For a reaction with A = 3e10 /s and activation energy 85 kJ/mol at 500 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 3, Ea = 85, Tk = 500 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 3e10 * exp(-85e3 / (8.314*500)) | Answer: 39.53 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.98 and bottoms xW = 0.03, with relative volatility alpha = 3. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.98, xw = 0.03, al = 3 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.98/0.02)(0.97/0.03)] / ln(3) | Answer: 6.707 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.66 and x = 0.28. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.66, x = 0.28 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.66/0.34) / (0.28/0.72) | Answer: 4.992

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.56 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 45 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.56, Psat = 45 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.56 * 45 | Answer: 25.2 kPa

question: A stream of 9.8 kg/s with specific heat 4.2 kJ/kg-K is heated through 90 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 9.8, cp = 4.2, dT = 90 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 9.8*4.2*90 | Answer: 3704 kW

question: A reactor of volume 16.4 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 4.6 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 16.4, Q = 4.6 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 16.4 / 4.6 | Answer: 3.565 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 3.1e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 2 mm with a concentration difference of 80 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 3.1, L = 2, dC = 80 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (3.1e-9)*80 / (2e-3) | Answer: 124 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 10 min and steady-state gain 2.3. For a step input of magnitude 14, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 10, K = 2.3, M = 14 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 2.3 * 14 | Answer: 32.2 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 80 m^2 flies at 110 m/s (air density 0.7 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 1.3. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 80, V = 110, rho = 0.7, CL = 1.3 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.7*(110)^2*80*1.3 / 1000 | Answer: 440.4 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 20 m^2 flies at 120 m/s (density 1 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.03. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 20, V = 120, rho = 1, CD = 0.03 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*1*(120)^2*20*0.03 / 1000 | Answer: 4.32 kN

question: A specimen under stress 320 MPa shows an elastic strain of 0.6e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 320, eps = 0.6 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 320 / (0.6e-3) MPa = 533.3 GPa | Answer: 533.3 GPa

question: A block of mass 43 kg has a volume of 1.8e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 43, V = 1.8 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 43 / (1.8e-3) | Answer: 23889 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 2100 mm is heated through 20 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 11e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 2100, dT = 20, al = 11 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 2100*11e-6*20 | Answer: 0.462 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 50 ohm, R2 = 125 ohm and R3 = 155 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 50, R2 = 125, R3 = 155 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 125*155 / 50 | Answer: 387.5 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 1000 ohm and gauge factor 2.2 experiences a strain of 1000e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 1000, GF = 2.2, eps = 1000 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 1000*2.2*1000e-6 | Answer: 2200 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 9.78 when the true value is 10. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.78, true = 10 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.78 - 10| / 10 * 100 | Answer: 2.2 %

question: Annual demand is 27500 units, ordering cost 190 per order and holding cost 20 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 27500, S = 190, H = 20 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*27500*190 / 20) | Answer: 722.8 units

question: An asset costs 370000 with salvage value 6000 after 8 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 370000, Sv = 6000, n = 8 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (370000 - 6000) / 8 | Answer: 45500 per year

question: A product sells for 430 per unit with variable cost 140 per unit and fixed costs 45000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 430, V = 140, F = 45000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 45000 / (430 - 140) | Answer: 155.2 units

question: Find the present worth of 100000 received 6 years from now at an interest rate of 12% per year.
solution: Given: F = 100000, n = 6, i = 12 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 100000 / (1 + 0.12)^6 | Answer: 50663 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.9, 0.92 and 0.91 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.9, r2 = 0.92, r3 = 0.91 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.9*0.92*0.91 | Answer: 0.7535

question: A process produces 18 defective items in a batch of 18500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 18, N = 18500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 18/18500 * 1e6 | Answer: 973 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -x^3 + 5x^2 + 4 evaluated at x = -1.
For f(x) = 4x^3 + 5x^2 - 5x - 7, find f''(x) at x = 3.
Evaluate the definite integral of (-5x - 2) dx from x = 0 to x = 5.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = 0x^3/3 + -5x^2/2 + -2x | Evaluate F(5) - F(0) | Answer: -72.5

question: Find the larger real root of x^2 - 5x - 1 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[-6, -8], [-2, 9]].
solution: Given: a = -6, b = -8, c = -2, d = 9 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (-6)(9) - (-8)(-2) | Answer: -70

question: Find the determinant of [[-2, -2, 2], [-3, 4, 2], [4, 0, 4]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: -104

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[-7, 7], [4, 4]].
solution: Trace tr = -3, Determinant = -56 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 6.132

question: Solve for x: -4x + 4y = -5 and 2x + 4y = 5.
solution: Determinant = -4*4 - 4*2 = -24 | x = (e d - b f) / det = 1.667 | Answer: x = 1.667
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 73, 41, 85, 7, 79.
solution: Sum = 285 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 57 | Answer: 57

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 37, 13, 28, 1, 3.
solution: Mean = 16.4 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 15.71

question: Find the slope of the line through (7, -5) and (8, 0).
solution: Given: x1 = 7, y1 = -5, x2 = 8, y2 = 0 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (0 - -5) / (8 - 7) | Answer: 5

question: Find the distance between the points (-8, 1) and (9, -2).
solution: Given: x1 = -8, y1 = 1, x2 = 9, y2 = -2 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((17)^2 + (-3)^2) | Answer: 17.26 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (-8,7), (3,-6), (-4,1).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 7 sq units

question: Find the 21th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 17 and common difference -1.
solution: Given: a = 17, d = -1, n = 21 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = 17 + (21 - 1)*-1 | Answer: -3

question: Find the sum of the first 7 terms of an AP with first term 6 and common difference -1.
solution: Given: a = 6, d = -1, n = 7 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 7/2 [2*6 + (7-1)*-1] | Answer: 21

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 32000 at 6% per annum for 2 years.
solution: Given: P = 32000, R = 6, Tt = 2 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 32000 * 6 * 2 / 100 | Answer: 3840 currency units

question: Find the amount when 1500 is invested at 9.4% per annum compounded annually for 4 years.
solution: Given: P = 1500, R = 9.4, Tt = 4 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 1500 * (1 + 9.4/100)^4 | Answer: 2149 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (-4, 7, 4) and (6, -3, 1).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (-1, -6, 5) and (5, -2, -1).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 43.08

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (5, 2, -4) and (-2, -5, -4).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 95.1 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number -6 + -4i.
solution: Given: a = -6, b = -4 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((-6)^2 + (-4)^2) | Answer: 7.211

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number -8 + 1i.
solution: Given: a = -8, b = 1 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(1, -8) | Answer: 172.9 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -3x^3 - 5x^2 - x at x = -4.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-196 with initial guess x0=12, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.3 and ordinates 10, 15, 1, 10, 4, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 508 and 167.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 508 and 167 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 20 and 76.
solution: Given: a = 20, b = 76 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 20*76 / 4 | Answer: 380
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 44 mm carries an axial tensile load of 54 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 36 mm and length 2900 mm carries an axial load of 42 kN. Take E = 200 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 41 mm transmits a torque of 950 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 41, Tt = 950 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(950*1000) / (pi*(41)^3) | Answer: 70.2 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 43 mm and length 600 mm carries a torque of 1200 N-m. With G = 80 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (43)^4 / 32 = 33564 mm^4 | theta = (1200*1000)(600) / (80000 * 33564) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 1.536 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 46 mm wide and 110 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 46, h = 110 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 46*(110)^2 / 6 | Answer: 92767 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (86 mm x 230 mm) carries a bending moment of 21 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (72 mm x 150 mm) has effective length 3400 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 660 MPa is designed for a working stress of 210 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 660, sw = 210 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 660 / 210 | Answer: 3.143

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 800 mm and wall thickness 12 mm carries an internal pressure of 2.4 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 800, t = 12, P = 2.4 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 2.4*800 / (2*12) | Answer: 80 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 1180 K and 410 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 1180, Tc = 410 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 410/1180) * 100 | Answer: 65.25 %

question: A refrigerator works between 271 K (cold) and 304 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 271, Th = 304 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 271 / (304 - 271) | Answer: 8.212

question: A heat pump operates between 275 K and 312 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 275, Th = 312 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 312 / (312 - 275) | Answer: 8.432

question: 4.1 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 95 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.1, dT = 95 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 4.1 * 0.718 * 95 | Answer: 279.7 kJ

question: 6.4 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 115 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 6.4, dT = 115 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 6.4 * 1.005 * 115 | Answer: 739.7 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 3.3 m^3 at 430 K with mass 2.7 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 3.3, Tk = 430, m = 2.7 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 2.7*0.287*430 / 3.3 | Answer: 101 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 3.5 kg of air expands isothermally at 500 K from volume V1 to 2*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.5, Tk = 500, ratio = 2 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 3.5*0.287*500*ln(2) | Answer: 348.1 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 1.5 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.19 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 1.5, D = 0.19 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*1.5*0.19 / 0.001 | Answer: 285000

question: Water flows at 1.2 m/s through a pipe of diameter 180 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 15.8 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 15.8 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*15.8 / 1000 | Answer: 155 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 2.6 m. Taking Cv = 0.95, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 2.6, cv = 0.95 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.95*sqrt(2*9.81*2.6) | Answer: 6.785 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 250 mm) water flows at 1.5 m/s. It contracts to diameter 100 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
Water flows at 2.1 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.39 m and length 80 m. With friction factor f = 0.039, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 37 teeth drives a gear of 75 teeth. If the pinion runs at 350 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 37, z2 = 75, N1 = 350 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 350*37 / 75 | Answer: 172.7 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 500 mm rotates at 400 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 500, N = 400 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.5)*400 / 60 | Answer: 10.47 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 49.7 kW at 950 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 49.7, N = 950 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(49.7*1000) / (2*pi*950) | Answer: 499.6 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 2.4 kg rotates at radius 0.28 m at 650 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 17300 N/m and mass 16.9 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 17300, m = 16.9 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(17300/16.9) | Answer: 5.092 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 10 m^2 and thickness 0.3 m has conductivity k = 19.8 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 160 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 10, L = 0.3, k = 19.8, dT = 160 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 19.8*10*160 / 0.3 | Answer: 105600 W

question: A surface of area 1.1 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 45 W/m^2-K to surroundings 65 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 1.1, h = 45, dT = 65 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 45*1.1*65 | Answer: 3218 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 180 m/min, feed = 0.22 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2.6 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 180, f = 0.22, d = 2.6 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*180*0.22*2.6 | Answer: 102960 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 420 mm is turned at 1100 rpm with a feed of 0.39 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 420, N = 1100, f = 0.39 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 420 / (0.39*1100) | Answer: 0.979 min

question: A resistor of 41 ohm carries a current of 7.7 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 41, I = 7.7 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 7.7 * 41 | Answer: 315.7 V

question: Three resistors 19 ohm, 41 ohm and 97 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 19, R2 = 41, R3 = 97 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 19 + 41 + 97 | Answer: 157 ohm

question: Two resistors 84 ohm and 114 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 84, R2 = 114 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 84*114 / (84+114) | Answer: 48.36 ohm

question: A device draws 2.4 A at 25 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 25, I = 2.4 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 25 * 2.4 | Answer: 60 W

question: A current of 9.4 A flows through a 84 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 9.4, R = 84 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (9.4)^2 * 84 | Answer: 7422 W

question: Two capacitors 46.5 uF and 4.1 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 46.5, C2 = 4.1 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 46.5*4.1 / (46.5+4.1) | Answer: 3.768 uF

question: A resistor 65 kohm and capacitor 9.9 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 65, C = 9.9 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (65k)(9.9u) = 643.5 ms | Answer: 643.5 ms

question: An inductor 195 mH is in series with 57 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 195, R = 57 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (195e-3) / 57 | Answer: 3.421 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 121.9 mH inductor at 760 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 121.9, f = 760 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (760)(121.9e-3) | Answer: 582.1 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 19.1 uF capacitor at 330 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 19.1, f = 330 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (330)(19.1e-6)) | Answer: 25.25 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 21 ohm, XL = 36 ohm and XC = 127 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 21, XL = 36, XC = 127 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(21^2 + (36 - 127)^2) | Answer: 93.39 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 86.4 mH and C = 5.9 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 86.4, C = 5.9 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(86.4e-3 * 5.9e-6)) | Answer: 222.9 Hz

question: A capacitor of 64.7 uF is charged to 245 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 64.7, V = 245 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*64.7e-6*(245)^2 | Answer: 1942 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 160 V with 300 primary turns and 160 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 160, N1 = 300, N2 = 160 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 160 * 160/300 | Answer: 85.33 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 130 V and draws an armature current of 42 A. If the armature resistance is 0.8 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 130, Ia = 42, Ra = 0.8 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 130 - 42*0.8 | Answer: 96.4 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 60 A at 433 V (line) with a power factor of 0.72. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 60, VL = 433, pf = 0.72 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*433*60*0.72 / 1000 | Answer: 32.4 kW

question: A load has real power 15 kW and apparent power 70 kVA. Find the power factor.

question: A machine delivers 55 kW output while drawing 127 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 55, Pi = 127 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 55/127 * 100 | Answer: 43.31 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 7 V across R1 = 37 ohm and R2 = 10 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 7, R1 = 37, R2 = 10 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 7*10 / (37+10) | Answer: 1.489 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 150 kohm and Rin = 12 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 150, Rin = 12 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 150 / 12 | Answer: 12.5

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 50 kohm and Rg = 18 kohm. Find the voltage gain.

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 4108. Express the gain in decibels (power).

question: A simply supported beam of span 5.2 m carries a central point load of 110 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.4 m carries a UDL of 35 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6.4, w = 35 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 35*(6.4)^2 / 8 | Answer: 179.2 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 4.9 m carries a point load 60 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.9, W = 60 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 60*4.9 | Answer: 294 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 4.6 m carries a UDL of 16 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.6, w = 16 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 16*(4.6)^2 / 2 | Answer: 169.3 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 8.6 m carries a point load 20 kN at distance 1.6 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 8.6, a = 1.6, W = 20 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 20*(8.6 - 1.6) / 8.6 | Answer: 16.28 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 3.3 m) carries a central point load 80 kN. With E = 30 GPa and I = 530e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=80000 N, L=3300.0 mm, E=30000 MPa, I=530e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 3.767 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 6.6 m carries a UDL of 42 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6.6, w = 42 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 42*(6.6)^2 / 12 | Answer: 152.5 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 650 mm, clear cover 40 mm and main bars of diameter 20 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 650, c = 40, dia = 20 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 650 - 40 - 20/2 | Answer: 600 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 26.3 m^2 carrying a factored load of 8.5 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 26.3, w = 8.5 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 8.5 * 26.3 | Answer: 223.6 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 3.6 m, unit weight 16 kN/m^3, phi = 36 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 7.8 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 21 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 7.8, g = 21 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (21 - 9.81)*7.8 | Answer: 87.28 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 2e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.2, area = 4.6e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.2 m, bed slope 0.004 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.017. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 1.8 m under a head of 0.3 m. Taking Cd = 0.6 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.

question: A rectangular channel 5 m wide carries a discharge of 29.9 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).

question: For a design speed of 55 km/h with allowable superelevation 0.08 and lateral friction 0.16, find the minimum curve radius in m.
A tank of volume 470 m^3 treats a flow of 15 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 470, Q = 15 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 470 / 15 | Answer: 31.33 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 280 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.29 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 7 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 280, k = 0.29, t = 7 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 280*(1 - e^(-0.29*7)) | Answer: 243.2 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.83, rainfall intensity 115 mm/h over a catchment of 41 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.83, i = 115, A = 41 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.83*115*41 / 360 | Answer: 10.87 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.02 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 760 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.02, M = 760 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 760*(20+0.02)/20 | Answer: 760.8 m

question: A file of 110 megabits is sent over a link of 53 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 110, B = 53 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 110 / 53 | Answer: 2.075 s

question: A link has bandwidth 91 Mbps and round-trip time 30 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 91, R = 30 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 91e6 * 30e-3 bits = 2730 kb | Answer: 2730 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.91, cache access time 10 ns and main-memory access time 120 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.91, tc = 10, tm = 120 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.91*10 + (1 - 0.91)*120 | Answer: 19.9 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 891061 elements?
solution: Given: n = 891061 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(891061)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: An O(n^2) algorithm performs c*n^2 basic operations. If c = 1 and n = 2270, how many operations are performed?
solution: Given: n = 2270 | Formula: operations = n^2 | Substitute: = (2270)^2 | Answer: 5152900

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.016, memory access time 150 ns and page-fault service time 9 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 9 ms = 9000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.016)*150 + 0.016*9000000.0 ns | Answer: 144.1 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 0.9 m^3 at 190 kPa and 600 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 0.9, P = 190, Tk = 600 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (190e3)*0.9 / (8.314*600) | Answer: 34.28 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.24 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 4 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.24, t = 4 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.24*4) | Answer: 0.6171

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.38 /min) reaches 60% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.38, X = 60 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.6 / (0.38*(1 - 0.6)) | Answer: 3.947 min

question: For a reaction with A = 2e10 /s and activation energy 85 kJ/mol at 320 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 2, Ea = 85, Tk = 320 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 2e10 * exp(-85e3 / (8.314*320)) | Answer: 0.0002665 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.92 and bottoms xW = 0.07, with relative volatility alpha = 2.9. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.92, xw = 0.07, al = 2.9 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.92/0.08)(0.93/0.07)] / ln(2.9) | Answer: 4.723 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.57 and x = 0.31. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.57, x = 0.31 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.57/0.43) / (0.31/0.69) | Answer: 2.95

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.19 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 70 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.19, Psat = 70 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.19 * 70 | Answer: 13.3 kPa

question: A stream of 7.2 kg/s with specific heat 2.3 kJ/kg-K is heated through 95 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 7.2, cp = 2.3, dT = 95 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 7.2*2.3*95 | Answer: 1573 kW

question: A reactor of volume 10.6 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 0.6 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 10.6, Q = 0.6 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 10.6 / 0.6 | Answer: 17.67 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 6.2e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 1 mm with a concentration difference of 80 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 6.2, L = 1, dC = 80 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (6.2e-9)*80 / (1e-3) | Answer: 496 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 7 min and steady-state gain 2.6. For a step input of magnitude 7, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 7, K = 2.6, M = 7 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 2.6 * 7 | Answer: 18.2 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 15 m^2 flies at 180 m/s (air density 1 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.9. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 15, V = 180, rho = 1, CL = 0.9 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1*(180)^2*15*0.9 / 1000 | Answer: 218.7 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 35 m^2 flies at 150 m/s (density 1.225 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.09. Find the drag force in kN.
A specimen under stress 270 MPa shows an elastic strain of 2.1e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.

question: A block of mass 19 kg has a volume of 4.1e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 19, V = 4.1 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 19 / (4.1e-3) | Answer: 4634 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 2100 mm is heated through 105 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 12e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 2100, dT = 105, al = 12 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 2100*12e-6*105 | Answer: 2.646 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 125 ohm, R2 = 165 ohm and R3 = 60 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 125, R2 = 165, R3 = 60 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 165*60 / 125 | Answer: 79.2 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 120 ohm and gauge factor 2.2 experiences a strain of 450e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 120, GF = 2.2, eps = 450 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 120*2.2*450e-6 | Answer: 118.8 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 10.87 when the true value is 10. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10.87, true = 10 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10.87 - 10| / 10 * 100 | Answer: 8.7 %

question: Annual demand is 36000 units, ordering cost 130 per order and holding cost 5 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 36000, S = 130, H = 5 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*36000*130 / 5) | Answer: 1368 units

question: An asset costs 50000 with salvage value 38000 after 17 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 50000, Sv = 38000, n = 17 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (50000 - 38000) / 17 | Answer: 705.9 per year

question: A product sells for 170 per unit with variable cost 40 per unit and fixed costs 115000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 170, V = 40, F = 115000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 115000 / (170 - 40) | Answer: 884.6 units

question: Find the present worth of 130000 received 5 years from now at an interest rate of 12% per year.
solution: Given: F = 130000, n = 5, i = 12 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 130000 / (1 + 0.12)^5 | Answer: 73765 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.9, 0.94 and 0.99 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.9, r2 = 0.94, r3 = 0.99 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.9*0.94*0.99 | Answer: 0.8375

question: A process produces 29 defective items in a batch of 9500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 29, N = 9500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 29/9500 * 1e6 | Answer: 3053 PPM

question: Find the distance between the points (-7, -6) and (5, 5).

question: Find the 29th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 14 and common difference 4.
solution: Given: a = 14, d = 4, n = 29 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = 14 + (29 - 1)*4 | Answer: 126

question: Find the sum of the first 36 terms of an AP with first term 13 and common difference 4.
solution: Given: a = 13, d = 4, n = 36 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 36/2 [2*13 + (36-1)*4] | Answer: 2988

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 44000 at 7.5% per annum for 5 years.
solution: Given: P = 44000, R = 7.5, Tt = 5 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 44000 * 7.5 * 5 / 100 | Answer: 16500 currency units

question: Find the amount when 12500 is invested at 11.9% per annum compounded annually for 5 years.
solution: Given: P = 12500, R = 11.9, Tt = 5 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 12500 * (1 + 11.9/100)^5 | Answer: 21931 currency units

question: Find the modulus of the complex number 1 + -6i.
solution: Given: a = 1, b = -6 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((1)^2 + (-6)^2) | Answer: 6.083

solution: Given: a = 11, b = -11 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(-11, 11) | Answer: -45 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -3x^3 - 2x^2 - 6x + 6 at x = -1.

question: A circular rod of diameter 53 mm carries an axial tensile load of 111 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 15 mm and length 900 mm carries an axial load of 58 kN. Take E = 200 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 53 mm transmits a torque of 600 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 53, Tt = 600 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(600*1000) / (pi*(53)^3) | Answer: 20.53 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 67 mm and length 1100 mm carries a torque of 1850 N-m. With G = 45 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.

question: A rectangular beam section is 110 mm wide and 120 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
