question: A component of ultimate strength 480 MPa is designed for a working stress of 120 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 480, sw = 120 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 480 / 120 | Answer: 4

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 900 mm and wall thickness 15 mm carries an internal pressure of 1.7 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 900, t = 15, P = 1.7 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 1.7*900 / (2*15) | Answer: 51 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 1200 K and 290 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 1200, Tc = 290 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 290/1200) * 100 | Answer: 75.83 %

question: A refrigerator works between 262 K (cold) and 304 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 262, Th = 304 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 262 / (304 - 262) | Answer: 6.238

question: 3.6 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 55 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.6, dT = 55 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 3.6 * 0.718 * 55 | Answer: 142.2 kJ

question: 2.7 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 145 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.7, dT = 145 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 2.7 * 1.005 * 145 | Answer: 393.5 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 2.9 m^3 at 570 K with mass 4.3 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 2.9, Tk = 570, m = 4.3 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 4.3*0.287*570 / 2.9 | Answer: 242.6 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 3.1 kg of air expands isothermally at 330 K from volume V1 to 3*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.1, Tk = 330, ratio = 3 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 3.1*0.287*330*ln(3) | Answer: 322.6 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 4.9 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.28 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 4.9, D = 0.28 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*4.9*0.28 / 0.001 | Answer: 1372000

question: Water flows at 2.3 m/s through a pipe of diameter 150 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 5.9 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 5.9 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*5.9 / 1000 | Answer: 57.88 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 3 m. Taking Cv = 0.99, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 3, cv = 0.99 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.99*sqrt(2*9.81*3) | Answer: 7.595 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 210 mm) water flows at 2.5 m/s. It contracts to diameter 130 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
Water flows at 1.7 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.19 m and length 380 m. With friction factor f = 0.022, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 29 teeth drives a gear of 117 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1150 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 29, z2 = 117, N1 = 1150 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1150*29 / 117 | Answer: 285 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 550 mm rotates at 750 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 550, N = 750 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.55)*750 / 60 | Answer: 21.6 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 21.2 kW at 1250 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 21.2, N = 1250 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(21.2*1000) / (2*pi*1250) | Answer: 162 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 1.1 kg rotates at radius 0.32 m at 950 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 14500 N/m and mass 11 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 14500, m = 11 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(14500/11) | Answer: 5.778 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 8 m^2 and thickness 0.3 m has conductivity k = 46.6 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 125 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 8, L = 0.3, k = 46.6, dT = 125 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 46.6*8*125 / 0.3 | Answer: 155333 W

question: A surface of area 4.9 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 50 W/m^2-K to surroundings 110 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 4.9, h = 50, dT = 110 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 50*4.9*110 | Answer: 26950 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 120 m/min, feed = 0.19 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2.5 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 120, f = 0.19, d = 2.5 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*120*0.19*2.5 | Answer: 57000 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 190 mm is turned at 1100 rpm with a feed of 0.23 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 190, N = 1100, f = 0.23 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 190 / (0.23*1100) | Answer: 0.751 min

question: A resistor of 97 ohm carries a current of 2.6 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 97, I = 2.6 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 2.6 * 97 | Answer: 252.2 V

question: Three resistors 60 ohm, 42 ohm and 85 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 60, R2 = 42, R3 = 85 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 60 + 42 + 85 | Answer: 187 ohm

question: Two resistors 54 ohm and 38 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 54, R2 = 38 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 54*38 / (54+38) | Answer: 22.3 ohm

question: A device draws 6.7 A at 125 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 125, I = 6.7 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 125 * 6.7 | Answer: 837.5 W

question: A current of 5.7 A flows through a 23 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 5.7, R = 23 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (5.7)^2 * 23 | Answer: 747.3 W

question: Two capacitors 41.1 uF and 17.7 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 41.1, C2 = 17.7 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 41.1*17.7 / (41.1+17.7) | Answer: 12.37 uF

question: A resistor 9 kohm and capacitor 5.1 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 9, C = 5.1 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (9k)(5.1u) = 45.9 ms | Answer: 45.9 ms

question: An inductor 233.9 mH is in series with 16 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 233.9, R = 16 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (233.9e-3) / 16 | Answer: 14.62 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 53.3 mH inductor at 310 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 53.3, f = 310 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (310)(53.3e-3) | Answer: 103.8 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 11.3 uF capacitor at 610 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 11.3, f = 610 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (610)(11.3e-6)) | Answer: 23.09 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 76 ohm, XL = 112 ohm and XC = 112 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 76, XL = 112, XC = 112 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(76^2 + (112 - 112)^2) | Answer: 76 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 4.4 mH and C = 4.2 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 4.4, C = 4.2 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(4.4e-3 * 4.2e-6)) | Answer: 1171 Hz

question: A capacitor of 27.2 uF is charged to 250 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 27.2, V = 250 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*27.2e-6*(250)^2 | Answer: 850 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 170 V with 650 primary turns and 470 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 170, N1 = 650, N2 = 470 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 170 * 470/650 | Answer: 122.9 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 390 V and draws an armature current of 22 A. If the armature resistance is 0.85 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 390, Ia = 22, Ra = 0.85 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 390 - 22*0.85 | Answer: 371.3 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 15 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.9. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 15, VL = 400, pf = 0.9 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*400*15*0.9 / 1000 | Answer: 9.353 kW

question: A load has real power 100 kW and apparent power 190 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 100, S = 190 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 100 / 190 | Answer: 0.5263

question: A machine delivers 15 kW output while drawing 197 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 15, Pi = 197 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 15/197 * 100 | Answer: 7.614 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 30 V across R1 = 11 ohm and R2 = 21 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 30, R1 = 11, R2 = 21 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 30*21 / (11+21) | Answer: 19.69 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 150 kohm and Rin = 36 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 150, Rin = 36 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 150 / 36 | Answer: 4.167

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 20 kohm and Rg = 29 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 20, Rg = 29 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 20/29 | Answer: 1.69

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 6539. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 6539 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(6539) | Answer: 38.16 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 5.1 m carries a central point load of 100 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.1, W = 100 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 100*5.1 / 4 | Answer: 127.5 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 3.9 m carries a UDL of 20 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.9, w = 20 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 20*(3.9)^2 / 8 | Answer: 38.02 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 6 m carries a point load 70 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6, W = 70 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 70*6 | Answer: 420 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 2.7 m carries a UDL of 24 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 2.7, w = 24 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 24*(2.7)^2 / 2 | Answer: 87.48 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.4 m carries a point load 55 kN at distance 3.9 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 4.4, a = 3.9, W = 55 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 55*(4.4 - 3.9) / 4.4 | Answer: 6.25 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 3 m) carries a central point load 60 kN. With E = 200 GPa and I = 600e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=60000 N, L=3000.0 mm, E=200000 MPa, I=600e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 0.2812 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 4.8 m carries a UDL of 45 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.8, w = 45 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 45*(4.8)^2 / 12 | Answer: 86.4 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 530 mm, clear cover 45 mm and main bars of diameter 12 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 530, c = 45, dia = 12 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 530 - 45 - 12/2 | Answer: 479 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 25.6 m^2 carrying a factored load of 9.4 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 25.6, w = 9.4 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 9.4 * 25.6 | Answer: 240.6 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 5 m, unit weight 18 kN/m^3, phi = 32 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 8.5 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 18 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 8.5, g = 18 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (18 - 9.81)*8.5 | Answer: 69.61 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 8.1e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.7, area = 2e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 8.1, i = 0.7, A = 2 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (8.1e-4)*0.7*(2e-3) | Answer: 1134 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 0.9 m, bed slope 0.007 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.028. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 1.4 m under a head of 0.9 m. Taking Cd = 0.61 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 5 m wide carries a discharge of 22.7 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 400 m and design speed 80 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 400, V = 80 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (80)^2 / (127*400) | Answer: 0.126
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: A tank of volume 660 m^3 treats a flow of 145 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 660, Q = 145 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 660 / 145 | Answer: 4.552 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 200 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.18 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 8 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 200, k = 0.18, t = 8 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 200*(1 - e^(-0.18*8)) | Answer: 152.6 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.81, rainfall intensity 60 mm/h over a catchment of 5.6 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.81, i = 60, A = 5.6 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.81*60*5.6 / 360 | Answer: 0.756 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.05 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 240 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.05, M = 240 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 240*(20+0.05)/20 | Answer: 240.6 m

question: Convert the decimal number 2249 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 2249 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 8C9 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 11101111 and 00011101.
solution: XOR: 11110010 | Count of 1s = 5 | Answer: 5
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 130 megabits is sent over a link of 55 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 130, B = 55 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 130 / 55 | Answer: 2.364 s

question: A link has bandwidth 15 Mbps and round-trip time 130 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 15, R = 130 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 15e6 * 130e-3 bits = 1950 kb | Answer: 1950 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.93, cache access time 3 ns and main-memory access time 130 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.93, tc = 3, tm = 130 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.93*3 + (1 - 0.93)*130 | Answer: 11.89 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 189804 elements?
solution: Given: n = 189804 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(189804)) + 1 | Answer: 18

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.009, memory access time 170 ns and page-fault service time 5 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 5 ms = 5000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.009)*170 + 0.009*5000000.0 ns | Answer: 45.17 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 0.7 m^3 at 300 kPa and 430 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 0.7, P = 300, Tk = 430 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (300e3)*0.7 / (8.314*430) | Answer: 58.74 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.31 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 9 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.31, t = 9 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.31*9) | Answer: 0.9386

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.26 /min) is to reach 75% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.26, X = 75 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.75) / 0.26 | Answer: 5.332 min

question: For a reaction with A = 3e10 /s and activation energy 60 kJ/mol at 310 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 3, Ea = 60, Tk = 310 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 3e10 * exp(-60e3 / (8.314*310)) | Answer: 2.327 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.9 and bottoms xW = 0.05, with relative volatility alpha = 2.9. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.9, xw = 0.05, al = 2.9 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.9/0.1)(0.95/0.05)] / ln(2.9) | Answer: 4.829 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.56 and x = 0.28. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.56, x = 0.28 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.56/0.44) / (0.28/0.72) | Answer: 3.273

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.82 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 40 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.82, Psat = 40 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.82 * 40 | Answer: 32.8 kPa

question: A stream of 8 kg/s with specific heat 4.2 kJ/kg-K is heated through 20 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 8, cp = 4.2, dT = 20 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 8*4.2*20 | Answer: 672 kW

question: A reactor of volume 10.7 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 3.1 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 10.7, Q = 3.1 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 10.7 / 3.1 | Answer: 3.452 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 2.6e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 3 mm with a concentration difference of 160 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 2.6, L = 3, dC = 160 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (2.6e-9)*160 / (3e-3) | Answer: 138.7 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 1.3 min and steady-state gain 3.7. For a step input of magnitude 14, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 1.3, K = 3.7, M = 14 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 3.7 * 14 | Answer: 51.8 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 30 m^2 flies at 90 m/s (air density 1.225 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.5. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 30, V = 90, rho = 1.225, CL = 0.5 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1.225*(90)^2*30*0.5 / 1000 | Answer: 74.42 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 45 m^2 flies at 260 m/s (density 0.7 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.05. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 45, V = 260, rho = 0.7, CD = 0.05 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.7*(260)^2*45*0.05 / 1000 | Answer: 53.23 kN

question: A specimen under stress 280 MPa shows an elastic strain of 0.9e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 280, eps = 0.9 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 280 / (0.9e-3) MPa = 311.1 GPa | Answer: 311.1 GPa

question: A block of mass 32 kg has a volume of 3.4e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 32, V = 3.4 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 32 / (3.4e-3) | Answer: 9412 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 1900 mm is heated through 140 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 11e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 1900, dT = 140, al = 11 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 1900*11e-6*140 | Answer: 2.926 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 45 ohm, R2 = 45 ohm and R3 = 205 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 45, R2 = 45, R3 = 205 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 45*205 / 45 | Answer: 205 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 350 ohm and gauge factor 2.1 experiences a strain of 1250e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 350, GF = 2.1, eps = 1250 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 350*2.1*1250e-6 | Answer: 918.8 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 10.2 when the true value is 100. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10.2, true = 100 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10.2 - 100| / 100 * 100 | Answer: 89.8 %

question: Annual demand is 25500 units, ordering cost 130 per order and holding cost 33 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 25500, S = 130, H = 33 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*25500*130 / 33) | Answer: 448.2 units

question: An asset costs 360000 with salvage value 12000 after 19 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 360000, Sv = 12000, n = 19 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (360000 - 12000) / 19 | Answer: 18316 per year

question: A product sells for 110 per unit with variable cost 90 per unit and fixed costs 60000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 110, V = 90, F = 60000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 60000 / (110 - 90) | Answer: 3000 units

question: Find the present worth of 135000 received 8 years from now at an interest rate of 7% per year.
solution: Given: F = 135000, n = 8, i = 7 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 135000 / (1 + 0.07)^8 | Answer: 78571 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.94, 0.91 and 0.97 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.94, r2 = 0.91, r3 = 0.97 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.94*0.91*0.97 | Answer: 0.8297

question: A process produces 2 defective items in a batch of 1000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 2, N = 1000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 2/1000 * 1e6 | Answer: 2000 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -6x^3 - 2x^2 + 9x + 7 evaluated at x = -1.
For f(x) = -3x^3 - 5x + 3, find f''(x) at x = -2.
Evaluate the definite integral of (-4x^2 - 2x + 6) dx from x = -4 to x = 7.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = -4x^3/3 + -2x^2/2 + 6x | Evaluate F(7) - F(-4) | Answer: -509.7
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of x^2 - 8x - 12 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[9, -7], [-6, 6]].
solution: Given: a = 9, b = -7, c = -6, d = 6 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (9)(6) - (-7)(-6) | Answer: 12

question: Find the determinant of [[-2, 0, 5], [-1, 2, 0], [5, -2, -1]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: -36

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[-6, -1], [-1, 1]].
solution: Trace tr = -5, Determinant = -7 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 1.14

question: Solve for x: -2x + -3y = 12 and -1x + 4y = 0.
solution: Determinant = -2*4 - -3*-1 = -11 | x = (e d - b f) / det = -4.364 | Answer: x = -4.364
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 28, 10, 60, 58, 24.
solution: Sum = 180 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 36 | Answer: 36

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 30, 46, 41, 5, 16.
solution: Mean = 27.6 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 17.1

question: Find the slope of the line through (1, 8) and (-1, -9).
solution: Given: x1 = 1, y1 = 8, x2 = -1, y2 = -9 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (-9 - 8) / (-1 - 1) | Answer: 8.5

question: Find the distance between the points (5, -1) and (2, -9).
solution: Given: x1 = 5, y1 = -1, x2 = 2, y2 = -9 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-3)^2 + (-8)^2) | Answer: 8.544 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (4,2), (-4,-5), (8,2).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 14 sq units

question: Find the 6th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -18 and common difference -3.
solution: Given: a = -18, d = -3, n = 6 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -18 + (6 - 1)*-3 | Answer: -33

question: Find the sum of the first 9 terms of an AP with first term 3 and common difference 2.
solution: Given: a = 3, d = 2, n = 9 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 9/2 [2*3 + (9-1)*2] | Answer: 99

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 43000 at 4.5% per annum for 1 years.
solution: Given: P = 43000, R = 4.5, Tt = 1 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 43000 * 4.5 * 1 / 100 | Answer: 1935 currency units

question: Find the amount when 30000 is invested at 11.3% per annum compounded annually for 3 years.
solution: Given: P = 30000, R = 11.3, Tt = 3 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 30000 * (1 + 11.3/100)^3 | Answer: 41362 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (-1, 8, -3) and (-5, 1, -7).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (-5, 5, -5) and (3, 1, 6).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 43.01

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (0, 5, -3) and (2, -2, -2).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 101.4 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number 11 + 0i.
solution: Given: a = 11, b = 0 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((11)^2 + (0)^2) | Answer: 11

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number 0 + -5i.
solution: Given: a = 0, b = -5 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(-5, 0) | Answer: -90 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = 5x^3 + x^2 - 4x - 4 at x = -2.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-193 with initial guess x0=7, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=0.7 and ordinates 8, 14, 7, 13, 5, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 196 and 497.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 196 and 497 | Answer: GCD = 7

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 37 and 25.
solution: Given: a = 37, b = 25 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 37*25 / 1 | Answer: 925
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 16 mm carries an axial tensile load of 12 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 27 mm and length 3000 mm carries an axial load of 67 kN. Take E = 70 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 80 mm transmits a torque of 1100 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 80, Tt = 1100 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(1100*1000) / (pi*(80)^3) | Answer: 10.94 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 63 mm and length 1800 mm carries a torque of 250 N-m. With G = 45 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (63)^4 / 32 = 1546543 mm^4 | theta = (250*1000)(1800) / (45000 * 1546543) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 0.3705 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 64 mm wide and 240 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 64, h = 240 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 64*(240)^2 / 6 | Answer: 614400 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (58 mm x 160 mm) carries a bending moment of 6 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (37 mm x 100 mm) has effective length 2000 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 550 MPa is designed for a working stress of 190 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 550, sw = 190 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 550 / 190 | Answer: 2.895

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 900 mm and wall thickness 8 mm carries an internal pressure of 1.4 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 900, t = 8, P = 1.4 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 1.4*900 / (2*8) | Answer: 78.75 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 880 K and 370 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 880, Tc = 370 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 370/880) * 100 | Answer: 57.95 %

question: A heat pump operates between 274 K and 318 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 274, Th = 318 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 318 / (318 - 274) | Answer: 7.227

question: 2.7 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 20 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.7, dT = 20 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 2.7 * 0.718 * 20 | Answer: 38.77 kJ

question: 5.9 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 135 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 5.9, dT = 135 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 5.9 * 1.005 * 135 | Answer: 800.5 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 3.8 m^3 at 330 K with mass 2.4 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 3.8, Tk = 330, m = 2.4 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 2.4*0.287*330 / 3.8 | Answer: 59.82 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 3.2 kg of air expands isothermally at 460 K from volume V1 to 5*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.2, Tk = 460, ratio = 5 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 3.2*0.287*460*ln(5) | Answer: 679.9 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 1.8 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.37 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 1.8, D = 0.37 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*1.8*0.37 / 0.001 | Answer: 666000

question: Water flows at 3.1 m/s through a pipe of diameter 230 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 2.5 m. Taking Cv = 0.97, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 2.5, cv = 0.97 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.97*sqrt(2*9.81*2.5) | Answer: 6.793 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 180 mm) water flows at 1.1 m/s. It contracts to diameter 110 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
Water flows at 1.5 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.36 m and length 420 m. With friction factor f = 0.035, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 18 teeth drives a gear of 75 teeth. If the pinion runs at 650 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 18, z2 = 75, N1 = 650 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 650*18 / 75 | Answer: 156 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 540 mm rotates at 950 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 540, N = 950 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.54)*950 / 60 | Answer: 26.86 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 30 kW at 900 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 30, N = 900 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(30*1000) / (2*pi*900) | Answer: 318.3 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 3.3 kg rotates at radius 0.53 m at 550 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 7600 N/m and mass 10.4 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 7600, m = 10.4 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(7600/10.4) | Answer: 4.302 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 7.7 m^2 and thickness 0.22 m has conductivity k = 10.1 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 50 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 7.7, L = 0.22, k = 10.1, dT = 50 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 10.1*7.7*50 / 0.22 | Answer: 17675 W

question: A surface of area 4.5 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 30 W/m^2-K to surroundings 105 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 4.5, h = 30, dT = 105 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 30*4.5*105 | Answer: 14175 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 120 m/min, feed = 0.17 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2.3 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 120, f = 0.17, d = 2.3 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*120*0.17*2.3 | Answer: 46920 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 350 mm is turned at 300 rpm with a feed of 0.35 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 350, N = 300, f = 0.35 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 350 / (0.35*300) | Answer: 3.333 min

question: A resistor of 78 ohm carries a current of 4.1 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 78, I = 4.1 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 4.1 * 78 | Answer: 319.8 V

question: Three resistors 83 ohm, 3 ohm and 89 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 83, R2 = 3, R3 = 89 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 83 + 3 + 89 | Answer: 175 ohm

question: Two resistors 107 ohm and 101 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 107, R2 = 101 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 107*101 / (107+101) | Answer: 51.96 ohm

question: A device draws 7.2 A at 95 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 95, I = 7.2 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 95 * 7.2 | Answer: 684 W

question: A current of 1.6 A flows through a 14 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 1.6, R = 14 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (1.6)^2 * 14 | Answer: 35.84 W

question: Two capacitors 9.6 uF and 41.2 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 9.6, C2 = 41.2 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 9.6*41.2 / (9.6+41.2) | Answer: 7.786 uF

question: A resistor 72 kohm and capacitor 5.4 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 72, C = 5.4 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (72k)(5.4u) = 388.8 ms | Answer: 388.8 ms

question: An inductor 244.5 mH is in series with 135 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 244.5, R = 135 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (244.5e-3) / 135 | Answer: 1.811 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 128.4 mH inductor at 690 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 128.4, f = 690 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (690)(128.4e-3) | Answer: 556.7 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 37.1 uF capacitor at 290 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 37.1, f = 290 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (290)(37.1e-6)) | Answer: 14.79 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 24 ohm, XL = 73 ohm and XC = 127 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 24, XL = 73, XC = 127 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(24^2 + (73 - 127)^2) | Answer: 59.09 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 9 mH and C = 3.3 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 9, C = 3.3 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(9e-3 * 3.3e-6)) | Answer: 923.5 Hz

question: A capacitor of 12.9 uF is charged to 150 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 12.9, V = 150 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*12.9e-6*(150)^2 | Answer: 145.1 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 220 V with 490 primary turns and 300 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 220, N1 = 490, N2 = 300 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 220 * 300/490 | Answer: 134.7 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 140 V and draws an armature current of 49 A. If the armature resistance is 0.26 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 140, Ia = 49, Ra = 0.26 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 140 - 49*0.26 | Answer: 127.3 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 160 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.76. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 160, VL = 400, pf = 0.76 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*400*160*0.76 / 1000 | Answer: 84.25 kW

question: A load has real power 65 kW and apparent power 90 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 65, S = 90 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 65 / 90 | Answer: 0.7222

question: A machine delivers 70 kW output while drawing 72 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 70, Pi = 72 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 70/72 * 100 | Answer: 97.22 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 29 V across R1 = 9 ohm and R2 = 1 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 29, R1 = 9, R2 = 1 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 29*1 / (9+1) | Answer: 2.9 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 60 kohm and Rin = 16 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 60, Rin = 16 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 60 / 16 | Answer: 3.75

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 170 kohm and Rg = 33 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 170, Rg = 33 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 170/33 | Answer: 6.152

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 2594. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 2594 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(2594) | Answer: 34.14 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.9 m carries a central point load of 65 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 9.9, W = 65 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 65*9.9 / 4 | Answer: 160.9 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 5.9 m carries a UDL of 60 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.9, w = 60 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 60*(5.9)^2 / 8 | Answer: 261.1 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 1.6 m carries a point load 30 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 1.6, W = 30 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 30*1.6 | Answer: 48 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 1.8 m carries a UDL of 8 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 1.8, w = 8 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 8*(1.8)^2 / 2 | Answer: 12.96 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.9 m carries a point load 70 kN at distance 3.4 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 6.9, a = 3.4, W = 70 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 70*(6.9 - 3.4) / 6.9 | Answer: 35.51 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 7.8 m) carries a central point load 55 kN. With E = 25 GPa and I = 190e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=55000 N, L=7800.0 mm, E=25000 MPa, I=190e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 114.5 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 8.4 m carries a UDL of 18 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 8.4, w = 18 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 18*(8.4)^2 / 12 | Answer: 105.8 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 330 mm, clear cover 45 mm and main bars of diameter 20 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 330, c = 45, dia = 20 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 330 - 45 - 20/2 | Answer: 275 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 13.1 m^2 carrying a factored load of 10.3 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 13.1, w = 10.3 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 10.3 * 13.1 | Answer: 134.9 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 3.3 m, unit weight 17 kN/m^3, phi = 29 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 11.9 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 18 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 11.9, g = 18 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (18 - 9.81)*11.9 | Answer: 97.46 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 7.1e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.9, area = 3.4e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 7.1, i = 0.9, A = 3.4 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (7.1e-4)*0.9*(3.4e-3) | Answer: 2173 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 2.3 m, bed slope 0.003 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.014. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 1.2 m under a head of 1.1 m. Taking Cd = 0.63 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 3.2 m wide carries a discharge of 12.6 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 440 m and design speed 55 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 440, V = 55 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (55)^2 / (127*440) | Answer: 0.05413
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: A tank of volume 650 m^3 treats a flow of 170 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 650, Q = 170 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 650 / 170 | Answer: 3.824 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 280 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.28 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 3 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 280, k = 0.28, t = 3 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 280*(1 - e^(-0.28*3)) | Answer: 159.1 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.75, rainfall intensity 55 mm/h over a catchment of 46.4 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.75, i = 55, A = 46.4 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.75*55*46.4 / 360 | Answer: 5.317 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.06 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 520 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.06, M = 520 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 520*(20+0.06)/20 | Answer: 521.6 m

question: Convert the decimal number 495 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 495 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 1EF (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the 8-bit binary number 00011001 to decimal.
solution: Binary 00011001 = sum of bit-weights | Answer: 25 (decimal)
formula: Sum each bit times its positional weight (2^i)

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 11100010 and 00001011.
solution: XOR: 11101001 | Count of 1s = 5 | Answer: 5
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 700 megabits is sent over a link of 43 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 700, B = 43 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 700 / 43 | Answer: 16.28 s

question: A link has bandwidth 54 Mbps and round-trip time 90 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 54, R = 90 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 54e6 * 90e-3 bits = 4860 kb | Answer: 4860 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.84, cache access time 6 ns and main-memory access time 150 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.84, tc = 6, tm = 150 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.84*6 + (1 - 0.84)*150 | Answer: 29.04 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 955360 elements?
solution: Given: n = 955360 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(955360)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: An O(n^2) algorithm performs c*n^2 basic operations. If c = 1 and n = 690, how many operations are performed?
solution: Given: n = 690 | Formula: operations = n^2 | Substitute: = (690)^2 | Answer: 476100

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.016, memory access time 200 ns and page-fault service time 7 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 7 ms = 7000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.016)*200 + 0.016*7000000.0 ns | Answer: 112.2 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 2.4 m^3 at 360 kPa and 520 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 2.4, P = 360, Tk = 520 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (360e3)*2.4 / (8.314*520) | Answer: 199.8 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.14 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 17 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.14, t = 17 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.14*17) | Answer: 0.9074

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.15 /min) is to reach 90% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.15, X = 90 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.9) / 0.15 | Answer: 15.35 min

question: For a reaction with A = 8e10 /s and activation energy 75 kJ/mol at 330 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 8, Ea = 75, Tk = 330 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 8e10 * exp(-75e3 / (8.314*330)) | Answer: 0.1074 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.91 and bottoms xW = 0.07, with relative volatility alpha = 1.7. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.91, xw = 0.07, al = 1.7 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.91/0.09)(0.93/0.07)] / ln(1.7) | Answer: 9.235 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.88 and x = 0.38. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.88, x = 0.38 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.88/0.12) / (0.38/0.62) | Answer: 11.96

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.77 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 105 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.77, Psat = 105 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.77 * 105 | Answer: 80.85 kPa

question: A stream of 5.9 kg/s with specific heat 2.6 kJ/kg-K is heated through 105 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 5.9, cp = 2.6, dT = 105 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 5.9*2.6*105 | Answer: 1611 kW

question: A reactor of volume 19.5 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 0.3 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 19.5, Q = 0.3 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 19.5 / 0.3 | Answer: 65 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 2.8e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 3 mm with a concentration difference of 190 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 2.8, L = 3, dC = 190 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (2.8e-9)*190 / (3e-3) | Answer: 177.3 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 2.6 min and steady-state gain 2.3. For a step input of magnitude 4, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 2.6, K = 2.3, M = 4 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 2.3 * 4 | Answer: 9.2 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 120 m^2 flies at 200 m/s (air density 0.7 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 1.4. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 120, V = 200, rho = 0.7, CL = 1.4 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.7*(200)^2*120*1.4 / 1000 | Answer: 2352 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 90 m^2 flies at 170 m/s (density 0.7 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.03. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 90, V = 170, rho = 0.7, CD = 0.03 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.7*(170)^2*90*0.03 / 1000 | Answer: 27.31 kN

question: A specimen under stress 210 MPa shows an elastic strain of 1.9e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 210, eps = 1.9 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 210 / (1.9e-3) MPa = 110.5 GPa | Answer: 110.5 GPa

question: A block of mass 38 kg has a volume of 3.1e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 38, V = 3.1 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 38 / (3.1e-3) | Answer: 12258 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 1200 mm is heated through 25 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 12e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 1200, dT = 25, al = 12 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 1200*12e-6*25 | Answer: 0.36 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 65 ohm, R2 = 160 ohm and R3 = 405 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 65, R2 = 160, R3 = 405 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 160*405 / 65 | Answer: 996.9 ohm

question: A measurement reads 9.55 when the true value is 100. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.55, true = 100 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.55 - 100| / 100 * 100 | Answer: 90.45 %

question: Annual demand is 32000 units, ordering cost 30 per order and holding cost 27 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 32000, S = 30, H = 27 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*32000*30 / 27) | Answer: 266.7 units

question: An asset costs 480000 with salvage value 10000 after 16 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 480000, Sv = 10000, n = 16 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (480000 - 10000) / 16 | Answer: 29375 per year

question: A product sells for 70 per unit with variable cost 10 per unit and fixed costs 20000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 70, V = 10, F = 20000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 20000 / (70 - 10) | Answer: 333.3 units

question: Find the present worth of 55000 received 10 years from now at an interest rate of 6% per year.
solution: Given: F = 55000, n = 10, i = 6 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 55000 / (1 + 0.06)^10 | Answer: 30712 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.98, 0.91 and 0.98 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.98, r2 = 0.91, r3 = 0.98 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.98*0.91*0.98 | Answer: 0.874

question: A process produces 49 defective items in a batch of 5500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 49, N = 5500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 49/5500 * 1e6 | Answer: 8909 PPM

question: Find the slope of the line through (-4, -7) and (2, 9).
solution: Given: x1 = -4, y1 = -7, x2 = 2, y2 = 9 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (9 - -7) / (2 - -4) | Answer: 2.667

question: Find the distance between the points (2, -5) and (-4, 0).
solution: Given: x1 = 2, y1 = -5, x2 = -4, y2 = 0 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-6)^2 + (5)^2) | Answer: 7.81 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (-6,7), (6,-8), (5,-7).

question: Find the 37th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -18 and common difference 3.
solution: Given: a = -18, d = 3, n = 37 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -18 + (37 - 1)*3 | Answer: 90

question: Find the sum of the first 22 terms of an AP with first term 13 and common difference 7.
solution: Given: a = 13, d = 7, n = 22 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 22/2 [2*13 + (22-1)*7] | Answer: 1903

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 5000 at 6.2% per annum for 4 years.
solution: Given: P = 5000, R = 6.2, Tt = 4 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 5000 * 6.2 * 4 / 100 | Answer: 1240 currency units

question: Find the amount when 33000 is invested at 6.1% per annum compounded annually for 3 years.

question: Find the modulus of the complex number -8 + 11i.

question: A circular rod of diameter 58 mm carries an axial tensile load of 92 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 27 mm and length 900 mm carries an axial load of 29 kN. Take E = 200 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 70 mm transmits a torque of 1650 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.

question: A shaft of diameter 65 mm and length 1500 mm carries a torque of 1650 N-m. With G = 45 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.

question: A rectangular beam section is 55 mm wide and 200 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 55, h = 200 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 55*(200)^2 / 6 | Answer: 366667 mm^3

question: A component of ultimate strength 510 MPa is designed for a working stress of 230 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 510, sw = 230 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 510 / 230 | Answer: 2.217

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1150 mm and wall thickness 14 mm carries an internal pressure of 1.4 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1150, t = 14, P = 1.4 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 1.4*1150 / (2*14) | Answer: 57.5 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 800 K and 400 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 800, Tc = 400 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 400/800) * 100 | Answer: 50 %

question: A refrigerator works between 253 K (cold) and 322 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 253, Th = 322 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 253 / (322 - 253) | Answer: 3.667

question: A heat pump operates between 281 K and 312 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 281, Th = 312 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 312 / (312 - 281) | Answer: 10.06

question: 3 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 90 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.

question: 5.7 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 50 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 5.7, dT = 50 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 5.7 * 1.005 * 50 | Answer: 286.4 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 3.2 m^3 at 340 K with mass 2.2 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 3.2, Tk = 340, m = 2.2 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 2.2*0.287*340 / 3.2 | Answer: 67.09 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 2.9 kg of air expands isothermally at 450 K from volume V1 to 4*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 0.5 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.3 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 0.5, D = 0.3 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*0.5*0.3 / 0.001 | Answer: 150000

question: Water flows at 2 m/s through a pipe of diameter 70 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.

Water flows at 4 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.42 m and length 390 m. With friction factor f = 0.036, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).

question: A pulley of diameter 120 mm rotates at 1400 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 120, N = 1400 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.12)*1400 / 60 | Answer: 8.796 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 17.3 kW at 800 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 14000 N/m and mass 4 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.

question: A plane wall of area 8.8 m^2 and thickness 0.3 m has conductivity k = 17.5 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 65 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 8.8, L = 0.3, k = 17.5, dT = 65 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 17.5*8.8*65 / 0.3 | Answer: 33367 W

question: A surface of area 3.1 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 35 W/m^2-K to surroundings 100 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 3.1, h = 35, dT = 100 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 35*3.1*100 | Answer: 10850 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 210 m/min, feed = 0.35 mm/rev, depth of cut = 0.9 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 210, f = 0.35, d = 0.9 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*210*0.35*0.9 | Answer: 66150 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 200 mm is turned at 1200 rpm with a feed of 0.17 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 200, N = 1200, f = 0.17 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 200 / (0.17*1200) | Answer: 0.9804 min

question: A resistor of 141 ohm carries a current of 7.6 A. Find the voltage across it.

question: Three resistors 1 ohm, 70 ohm and 54 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.

question: A device draws 3.1 A at 230 V. Find the power consumed.

question: A current of 1.3 A flows through a 140 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.

question: Two capacitors 32.8 uF and 29.9 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 32.8, C2 = 29.9 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 32.8*29.9 / (32.8+29.9) | Answer: 15.64 uF

question: A resistor 5 kohm and capacitor 8.1 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.

question: An inductor 128.7 mH is in series with 141 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 98.2 mH inductor at 550 Hz.

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 34.3 uF capacitor at 330 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 34.3, f = 330 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (330)(34.3e-6)) | Answer: 14.06 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 68 ohm, XL = 92 ohm and XC = 105 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 68, XL = 92, XC = 105 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(68^2 + (92 - 105)^2) | Answer: 69.23 ohm

question: A capacitor of 43.7 uF is charged to 130 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.

question: A transformer has primary voltage 380 V with 700 primary turns and 180 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 380, N1 = 700, N2 = 180 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 380 * 180/700 | Answer: 97.71 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 150 V and draws an armature current of 22 A. If the armature resistance is 1.4 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 150, Ia = 22, Ra = 1.4 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 150 - 22*1.4 | Answer: 119.2 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 75 A at 433 V (line) with a power factor of 0.74. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 75, VL = 433, pf = 0.74 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*433*75*0.74 / 1000 | Answer: 41.62 kW

question: A load has real power 80 kW and apparent power 195 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 80, S = 195 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 80 / 195 | Answer: 0.4103

question: A machine delivers 100 kW output while drawing 167 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 100, Pi = 167 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 100/167 * 100 | Answer: 59.88 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 7 V across R1 = 27 ohm and R2 = 12 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 7, R1 = 27, R2 = 12 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 7*12 / (27+12) | Answer: 2.154 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 150 kohm and Rin = 27 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 150, Rin = 27 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 150 / 27 | Answer: 5.556

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 160 kohm and Rg = 11 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 160, Rg = 11 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 160/11 | Answer: 15.55

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 7734. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 7734 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(7734) | Answer: 38.88 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 9 m carries a central point load of 35 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 9, W = 35 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 35*9 / 4 | Answer: 78.75 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.9 m carries a UDL of 55 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 9.9, w = 55 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 55*(9.9)^2 / 8 | Answer: 673.8 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 2.1 m carries a point load 50 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 2.1, W = 50 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 50*2.1 | Answer: 105 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 3.2 m carries a UDL of 38 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.2, w = 38 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 38*(3.2)^2 / 2 | Answer: 194.6 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 6 m carries a point load 70 kN at distance 1.4 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 6, a = 1.4, W = 70 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 70*(6 - 1.4) / 6 | Answer: 53.67 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 3 m) carries a central point load 25 kN. With E = 200 GPa and I = 390e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=25000 N, L=3000.0 mm, E=200000 MPa, I=390e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 0.1803 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 8.1 m carries a UDL of 9 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 8.1, w = 9 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 9*(8.1)^2 / 12 | Answer: 49.21 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 510 mm, clear cover 50 mm and main bars of diameter 12 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 510, c = 50, dia = 12 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 510 - 50 - 12/2 | Answer: 454 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 28 m^2 carrying a factored load of 19.3 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 28, w = 19.3 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 19.3 * 28 | Answer: 540.4 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 4.7 m, unit weight 16 kN/m^3, phi = 29 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 5.8 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 20 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 5.8, g = 20 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (20 - 9.81)*5.8 | Answer: 59.1 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 3e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.6, area = 4.8e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 3, i = 0.6, A = 4.8 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (3e-4)*0.6*(4.8e-3) | Answer: 864 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.6 m, bed slope 0.008 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.029. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 5 m under a head of 0.4 m. Taking Cd = 0.6 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
solution: Given: L = 5, H = 0.4, cd = 0.6 | Formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2) | Substitute: Q = (2/3)*0.6*sqrt(2*9.81)*5*(0.4)^1.5 | Answer: 2.241 m^3/s
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 3 m wide carries a discharge of 22.7 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 120 m and design speed 80 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 120, V = 80 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (80)^2 / (127*120) | Answer: 0.4199
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: For a design speed of 100 km/h with allowable superelevation 0.07 and lateral friction 0.12, find the minimum curve radius in m.
A tank of volume 190 m^3 treats a flow of 165 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 190, Q = 165 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 190 / 165 | Answer: 1.152 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 200 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.16 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 4 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 200, k = 0.16, t = 4 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 200*(1 - e^(-0.16*4)) | Answer: 94.54 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.45, rainfall intensity 75 mm/h over a catchment of 54.2 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.45, i = 75, A = 54.2 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.45*75*54.2 / 360 | Answer: 5.081 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.06 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 460 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.06, M = 460 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 460*(30+0.06)/30 | Answer: 460.9 m

question: Convert the decimal number 3086 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 3086 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: C0E (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 00100001 and 00010011.
solution: XOR: 00110010 | Count of 1s = 3 | Answer: 3
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 260 megabits is sent over a link of 31 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 260, B = 31 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 260 / 31 | Answer: 8.387 s

question: A link has bandwidth 89 Mbps and round-trip time 10 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 89, R = 10 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 89e6 * 10e-3 bits = 890 kb | Answer: 890 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.93, cache access time 3 ns and main-memory access time 80 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.93, tc = 3, tm = 80 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.93*3 + (1 - 0.93)*80 | Answer: 8.39 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 588947 elements?
solution: Given: n = 588947 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(588947)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.015, memory access time 130 ns and page-fault service time 4 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 4 ms = 4000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.015)*130 + 0.015*4000000.0 ns | Answer: 60.13 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 2.1 m^3 at 150 kPa and 500 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 2.1, P = 150, Tk = 500 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (150e3)*2.1 / (8.314*500) | Answer: 75.78 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.18 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 5 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.18, t = 5 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.18*5) | Answer: 0.5934

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.32 /min) is to reach 85% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.32, X = 85 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.85) / 0.32 | Answer: 5.928 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.37 /min) reaches 60% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.37, X = 60 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.6 / (0.37*(1 - 0.6)) | Answer: 4.054 min

question: For a reaction with A = 4e10 /s and activation energy 85 kJ/mol at 480 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 4, Ea = 85, Tk = 480 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 4e10 * exp(-85e3 / (8.314*480)) | Answer: 22.48 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.97 and bottoms xW = 0.03, with relative volatility alpha = 3.3. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.97, xw = 0.03, al = 3.3 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.97/0.03)(0.97/0.03)] / ln(3.3) | Answer: 5.823 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.69 and x = 0.36. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.69, x = 0.36 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.69/0.31) / (0.36/0.64) | Answer: 3.957

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.75 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 75 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.75, Psat = 75 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.75 * 75 | Answer: 56.25 kPa

question: A stream of 3.1 kg/s with specific heat 2.2 kJ/kg-K is heated through 45 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 3.1, cp = 2.2, dT = 45 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 3.1*2.2*45 | Answer: 306.9 kW

question: A reactor of volume 3.1 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 0.9 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 3.1, Q = 0.9 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 3.1 / 0.9 | Answer: 3.444 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 8.4e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 5 mm with a concentration difference of 180 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 8.4, L = 5, dC = 180 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (8.4e-9)*180 / (5e-3) | Answer: 302.4 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 4.9 min and steady-state gain 1.4. For a step input of magnitude 12, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 4.9, K = 1.4, M = 12 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 1.4 * 12 | Answer: 16.8 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 15 m^2 flies at 100 m/s (air density 0.7 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.6. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 15, V = 100, rho = 0.7, CL = 0.6 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.7*(100)^2*15*0.6 / 1000 | Answer: 31.5 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 90 m^2 flies at 180 m/s (density 1.225 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.02. Find the drag force in kN.
A specimen under stress 140 MPa shows an elastic strain of 1.7e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 140, eps = 1.7 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 140 / (1.7e-3) MPa = 82.35 GPa | Answer: 82.35 GPa

question: A block of mass 32 kg has a volume of 5.2e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 32, V = 5.2 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 32 / (5.2e-3) | Answer: 6154 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 2300 mm is heated through 75 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 11e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 2300, dT = 75, al = 11 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 2300*11e-6*75 | Answer: 1.897 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 190 ohm, R2 = 40 ohm and R3 = 390 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 190, R2 = 40, R3 = 390 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 40*390 / 190 | Answer: 82.11 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 120 ohm and gauge factor 2.2 experiences a strain of 1350e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 120, GF = 2.2, eps = 1350 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 120*2.2*1350e-6 | Answer: 356.4 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 10.55 when the true value is 100. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10.55, true = 100 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10.55 - 100| / 100 * 100 | Answer: 89.45 %

question: Annual demand is 13000 units, ordering cost 160 per order and holding cost 39 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 13000, S = 160, H = 39 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*13000*160 / 39) | Answer: 326.6 units

question: An asset costs 420000 with salvage value 2000 after 14 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 420000, Sv = 2000, n = 14 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (420000 - 2000) / 14 | Answer: 29857 per year

question: A product sells for 470 per unit with variable cost 90 per unit and fixed costs 100000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 470, V = 90, F = 100000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 100000 / (470 - 90) | Answer: 263.2 units

question: Find the present worth of 130000 received 9 years from now at an interest rate of 12% per year.
solution: Given: F = 130000, n = 9, i = 12 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 130000 / (1 + 0.12)^9 | Answer: 46879 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.94, 0.98 and 0.99 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.94, r2 = 0.98, r3 = 0.99 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.94*0.98*0.99 | Answer: 0.912

question: A process produces 10 defective items in a batch of 8000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 10, N = 8000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 10/8000 * 1e6 | Answer: 1250 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = 4x^3 + x^2 + 4x + 4 evaluated at x = 1.
For f(x) = -6x^3 - 3x^2 - 9x, find f''(x) at x = 3.
Evaluate the definite integral of (-x^2 + x - 1) dx from x = 2 to x = 5.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = -1x^3/3 + 1x^2/2 + -1x | Evaluate F(5) - F(2) | Answer: -31.5
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 5x^2 + 9x = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[4, -5], [-5, 8]].
solution: Given: a = 4, b = -5, c = -5, d = 8 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (4)(8) - (-5)(-5) | Answer: 7

question: Find the determinant of [[5, 4, 1], [-2, 3, 5], [-6, -6, -6]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: -78

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[5, -6], [-4, 8]].
solution: Trace tr = 13, Determinant = 16 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 11.62

question: Solve for x: 1x + -1y = -8 and 5x + -3y = 12.
solution: Determinant = 1*-3 - -1*5 = 2 | x = (e d - b f) / det = 18 | Answer: x = 18
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 30, 68, 28, 16, 15.
solution: Sum = 157 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 31.4 | Answer: 31.4

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 30, 9, 16, 37, 28.
solution: Mean = 24 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 11.29

question: Find the slope of the line through (5, -8) and (-2, 7).
solution: Given: x1 = 5, y1 = -8, x2 = -2, y2 = 7 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (7 - -8) / (-2 - 5) | Answer: -2.143

question: Find the distance between the points (-1, -9) and (-9, -5).
solution: Given: x1 = -1, y1 = -9, x2 = -9, y2 = -5 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-8)^2 + (4)^2) | Answer: 8.944 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (8,-5), (-7,2), (-2,-3).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 20 sq units

question: Find the 21th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 6 and common difference 3.
solution: Given: a = 6, d = 3, n = 21 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = 6 + (21 - 1)*3 | Answer: 66

question: Find the sum of the first 14 terms of an AP with first term -2 and common difference 8.
solution: Given: a = -2, d = 8, n = 14 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 14/2 [2*-2 + (14-1)*8] | Answer: 700

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 26000 at 9.2% per annum for 4 years.
