solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 34.58

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (0, -4, 0) and (4, -6, 5).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 46.86 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number 11 + 4i.
solution: Given: a = 11, b = 4 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((11)^2 + (4)^2) | Answer: 11.7

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number -9 + 7i.
solution: Given: a = -9, b = 7 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(7, -9) | Answer: 142.1 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = 2x^3 + x^2 - 8x - 4 at x = 2.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-22 with initial guess x0=14, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.2 and ordinates 0, 13, 12, 14, 15, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 48 and 430.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 48 and 430 | Answer: GCD = 2

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 20 and 40.
solution: Given: a = 20, b = 40 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 20*40 / 20 | Answer: 40
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 23 mm carries an axial tensile load of 16 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 38 mm and length 3000 mm carries an axial load of 50 kN. Take E = 210 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 79 mm transmits a torque of 1550 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 79, Tt = 1550 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(1550*1000) / (pi*(79)^3) | Answer: 16.01 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 46 mm and length 700 mm carries a torque of 1900 N-m. With G = 45 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (46)^4 / 32 = 439573 mm^4 | theta = (1900*1000)(700) / (45000 * 439573) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 3.852 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 120 mm wide and 170 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 120, h = 170 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 120*(170)^2 / 6 | Answer: 578000 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (71 mm x 130 mm) carries a bending moment of 34 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (35 mm x 120 mm) has effective length 2200 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 650 MPa is designed for a working stress of 70 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 650, sw = 70 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 650 / 70 | Answer: 9.286

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 750 mm and wall thickness 12 mm carries an internal pressure of 1.9 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 750, t = 12, P = 1.9 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 1.9*750 / (2*12) | Answer: 59.38 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 740 K and 290 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 740, Tc = 290 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 290/740) * 100 | Answer: 60.81 %

question: A refrigerator works between 264 K (cold) and 312 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 264, Th = 312 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 264 / (312 - 264) | Answer: 5.5

question: A heat pump operates between 266 K and 300 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 266, Th = 300 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 300 / (300 - 266) | Answer: 8.824

question: 7.7 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 90 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 7.7, dT = 90 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 7.7 * 0.718 * 90 | Answer: 497.6 kJ

question: 2.3 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 135 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.3, dT = 135 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 2.3 * 1.005 * 135 | Answer: 312.1 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 3.1 m^3 at 550 K with mass 3.5 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 3.1, Tk = 550, m = 3.5 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 3.5*0.287*550 / 3.1 | Answer: 178.2 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 3.9 kg of air expands isothermally at 380 K from volume V1 to 4*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.9, Tk = 380, ratio = 4 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 3.9*0.287*380*ln(4) | Answer: 589.6 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 1.3 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.09 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 1.3, D = 0.09 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*1.3*0.09 / 0.001 | Answer: 117000

question: Water flows at 2.9 m/s through a pipe of diameter 230 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 12.2 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 12.2 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*12.2 / 1000 | Answer: 119.7 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 12.3 m. Taking Cv = 0.95, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 12.3, cv = 0.95 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.95*sqrt(2*9.81*12.3) | Answer: 14.76 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 180 mm) water flows at 1.2 m/s. It contracts to diameter 120 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 180, d2 = 120, V1 = 1.2 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 1.2*(180/120)^2 | Answer: 2.7 m/s

question: Water flows at 3.5 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.12 m and length 340 m. With friction factor f = 0.039, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 18 teeth drives a gear of 82 teeth. If the pinion runs at 500 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 18, z2 = 82, N1 = 500 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 500*18 / 82 | Answer: 109.8 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 430 mm rotates at 1500 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 430, N = 1500 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.43)*1500 / 60 | Answer: 33.77 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 2.8 kW at 300 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 2.8, N = 300 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(2.8*1000) / (2*pi*300) | Answer: 89.13 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 9.2 kg rotates at radius 0.52 m at 700 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 9200 N/m and mass 7.5 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 9200, m = 7.5 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(9200/7.5) | Answer: 5.574 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 2.6 m^2 and thickness 0.33 m has conductivity k = 11.2 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 70 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 2.6, L = 0.33, k = 11.2, dT = 70 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 11.2*2.6*70 / 0.33 | Answer: 6177 W

question: A surface of area 3.3 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 175 W/m^2-K to surroundings 110 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 3.3, h = 175, dT = 110 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 175*3.3*110 | Answer: 63525 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 230 m/min, feed = 0.24 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 230, f = 0.24, d = 2 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*230*0.24*2 | Answer: 110400 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 300 mm is turned at 450 rpm with a feed of 0.23 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 300, N = 450, f = 0.23 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 300 / (0.23*450) | Answer: 2.899 min

question: A resistor of 188 ohm carries a current of 9.2 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 188, I = 9.2 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 9.2 * 188 | Answer: 173 V

question: Three resistors 56 ohm, 20 ohm and 99 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 56, R2 = 20, R3 = 99 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 56 + 20 + 99 | Answer: 175 ohm

question: Two resistors 18 ohm and 113 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 18, R2 = 113 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 18*113 / (18+113) | Answer: 15.53 ohm

question: A device draws 4 A at 120 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 120, I = 4 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 120 * 4 | Answer: 480 W

question: A current of 6.9 A flows through a 3 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 6.9, R = 3 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (6.9)^2 * 3 | Answer: 142.8 W

question: Two capacitors 46.9 uF and 15.4 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 46.9, C2 = 15.4 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 46.9*15.4 / (46.9+15.4) | Answer: 11.59 uF

question: A resistor 50 kohm and capacitor 19.5 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 50, C = 19.5 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (50k)(19.5u) = 975 ms | Answer: 975 ms

question: An inductor 150.7 mH is in series with 61 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 150.7, R = 61 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (150.7e-3) / 61 | Answer: 2.47 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 84.9 mH inductor at 540 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 84.9, f = 540 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (540)(84.9e-3) | Answer: 288.1 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 14 uF capacitor at 400 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 14, f = 400 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (400)(14e-6)) | Answer: 28.42 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 53 ohm, XL = 13 ohm and XC = 97 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 53, XL = 13, XC = 97 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(53^2 + (13 - 97)^2) | Answer: 99.32 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 31.1 mH and C = 1.8 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 31.1, C = 1.8 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(31.1e-3 * 1.8e-6)) | Answer: 672.7 Hz

question: A capacitor of 21.7 uF is charged to 370 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 21.7, V = 370 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*21.7e-6*(370)^2 | Answer: 1485 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 260 V with 210 primary turns and 30 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 260, N1 = 210, N2 = 30 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 260 * 30/210 | Answer: 37.14 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 420 V and draws an armature current of 16 A. If the armature resistance is 0.26 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 420, Ia = 16, Ra = 0.26 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 420 - 16*0.26 | Answer: 415.8 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 30 A at 433 V (line) with a power factor of 0.72. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 30, VL = 433, pf = 0.72 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*433*30*0.72 / 1000 | Answer: 16.2 kW

question: A load has real power 55 kW and apparent power 85 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 55, S = 85 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 55 / 85 | Answer: 0.6471

question: A machine delivers 25 kW output while drawing 177 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 25, Pi = 177 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 25/177 * 100 | Answer: 14.12 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 5 V across R1 = 34 ohm and R2 = 42 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 5, R1 = 34, R2 = 42 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 5*42 / (34+42) | Answer: 2.763 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 120 kohm and Rin = 18 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 120, Rin = 18 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 120 / 18 | Answer: 6.667

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 180 kohm and Rg = 26 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 180, Rg = 26 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 180/26 | Answer: 7.923

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 2555. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 2555 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(2555) | Answer: 34.07 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.7 m carries a central point load of 105 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.7, W = 105 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 105*4.7 / 4 | Answer: 123.4 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 7.1 m carries a UDL of 45 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7.1, w = 45 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 45*(7.1)^2 / 8 | Answer: 283.6 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 3.6 m carries a point load 70 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.6, W = 70 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 70*3.6 | Answer: 252 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 3.5 m carries a UDL of 12 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.5, w = 12 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 12*(3.5)^2 / 2 | Answer: 73.5 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.5 m carries a point load 95 kN at distance 1 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 9.5, a = 1, W = 95 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 95*(9.5 - 1) / 9.5 | Answer: 85 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 7.9 m) carries a central point load 80 kN. With E = 200 GPa and I = 440e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.

question: A fixed beam of span 5.3 m carries a UDL of 39 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.3, w = 39 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 39*(5.3)^2 / 12 | Answer: 91.29 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 510 mm, clear cover 35 mm and main bars of diameter 12 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 510, c = 35, dia = 12 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 510 - 35 - 12/2 | Answer: 469 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 20.6 m^2 carrying a factored load of 16.2 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 20.6, w = 16.2 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 16.2 * 20.6 | Answer: 333.7 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 4.8 m, unit weight 18 kN/m^3, phi = 29 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).

question: At a depth of 5.4 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 18 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 5.4, g = 18 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (18 - 9.81)*5.4 | Answer: 44.23 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 6.4e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.8, area = 7.3e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.

question: For a design speed of 90 km/h with allowable superelevation 0.08 and lateral friction 0.12, find the minimum curve radius in m.
A tank of volume 240 m^3 treats a flow of 65 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 320 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.12 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 8 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 320, k = 0.12, t = 8 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 320*(1 - e^(-0.12*8)) | Answer: 197.5 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.6, rainfall intensity 45 mm/h over a catchment of 16.4 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.6, i = 45, A = 16.4 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.6*45*16.4 / 360 | Answer: 1.23 m^3/s

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.06 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 260 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.06, M = 260 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 260*(20+0.06)/20 | Answer: 260.8 m

question: A file of 530 megabits is sent over a link of 11 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.

question: A link has bandwidth 34 Mbps and round-trip time 40 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 34, R = 40 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 34e6 * 40e-3 bits = 1360 kb | Answer: 1360 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.89, cache access time 8 ns and main-memory access time 190 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.89, tc = 8, tm = 190 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.89*8 + (1 - 0.89)*190 | Answer: 28.02 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 157673 elements?

question: An O(n^2) algorithm performs c*n^2 basic operations. If c = 1 and n = 2210, how many operations are performed?
solution: Given: n = 2210 | Formula: operations = n^2 | Substitute: = (2210)^2 | Answer: 4884100

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.003, memory access time 150 ns and page-fault service time 5 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 5 ms = 5000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.003)*150 + 0.003*5000000.0 ns | Answer: 15.15 microseconds

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 3 m^3 at 240 kPa and 340 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 3, P = 240, Tk = 340 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (240e3)*3 / (8.314*340) | Answer: 254.7 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.34 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 9 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.34, t = 9 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.34*9) | Answer: 0.9531

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.27 /min) is to reach 60% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.27, X = 60 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.6) / 0.27 | Answer: 3.394 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.35 /min) reaches 65% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.35, X = 65 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.65 / (0.35*(1 - 0.65)) | Answer: 5.306 min

question: For a reaction with A = 2e10 /s and activation energy 70 kJ/mol at 500 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 2, Ea = 70, Tk = 500 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 2e10 * exp(-70e3 / (8.314*500)) | Answer: 972.6 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.9 and bottoms xW = 0.09, with relative volatility alpha = 1.6. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.9, xw = 0.09, al = 1.6 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.9/0.1)(0.91/0.09)] / ln(1.6) | Answer: 9.597 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.75 and x = 0.22. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.75, x = 0.22 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.75/0.25) / (0.22/0.78) | Answer: 10.64

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.5 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 90 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.5, Psat = 90 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.5 * 90 | Answer: 45 kPa

question: A stream of 6.7 kg/s with specific heat 1.9 kJ/kg-K is heated through 115 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 6.7, cp = 1.9, dT = 115 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 6.7*1.9*115 | Answer: 1464 kW

question: A reactor of volume 4.1 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 2.9 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 4.1, Q = 2.9 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 4.1 / 2.9 | Answer: 1.414 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 2e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 5 mm with a concentration difference of 120 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 2, L = 5, dC = 120 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (2e-9)*120 / (5e-3) | Answer: 48 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 8.5 min and steady-state gain 2.4. For a step input of magnitude 3, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 8.5, K = 2.4, M = 3 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 2.4 * 3 | Answer: 7.2 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 75 m^2 flies at 220 m/s (air density 0.7 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.7. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 75, V = 220, rho = 0.7, CL = 0.7 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.7*(220)^2*75*0.7 / 1000 | Answer: 889.4 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 100 m^2 flies at 140 m/s (density 0.4 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.12. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 100, V = 140, rho = 0.4, CD = 0.12 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.4*(140)^2*100*0.12 / 1000 | Answer: 47.04 kN

question: A specimen under stress 370 MPa shows an elastic strain of 2.9e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 370, eps = 2.9 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 370 / (2.9e-3) MPa = 127.6 GPa | Answer: 127.6 GPa

question: A block of mass 29 kg has a volume of 0.8e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 29, V = 0.8 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 29 / (0.8e-3) | Answer: 36250 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 1800 mm is heated through 40 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 23e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 1800, dT = 40, al = 23 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 1800*23e-6*40 | Answer: 1.656 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 40 ohm, R2 = 190 ohm and R3 = 235 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 40, R2 = 190, R3 = 235 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 190*235 / 40 | Answer: 1116 ohm

question: A measurement reads 10.14 when the true value is 100. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10.14, true = 100 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10.14 - 100| / 100 * 100 | Answer: 89.86 %

question: Annual demand is 41000 units, ordering cost 210 per order and holding cost 39 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 41000, S = 210, H = 39 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*41000*210 / 39) | Answer: 664.5 units

question: An asset costs 450000 with salvage value 20000 after 13 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 450000, Sv = 20000, n = 13 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (450000 - 20000) / 13 | Answer: 33077 per year

question: A product sells for 320 per unit with variable cost 100 per unit and fixed costs 100000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 320, V = 100, F = 100000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 100000 / (320 - 100) | Answer: 454.5 units

question: Find the present worth of 175000 received 9 years from now at an interest rate of 6% per year.
solution: Given: F = 175000, n = 9, i = 6 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 175000 / (1 + 0.06)^9 | Answer: 103582 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.94, 0.96 and 0.9 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.94, r2 = 0.96, r3 = 0.9 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.94*0.96*0.9 | Answer: 0.8122

question: A process produces 14 defective items in a batch of 12000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 14, N = 12000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 14/12000 * 1e6 | Answer: 1167 PPM

question: Find the 35th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 8 and common difference 6.
