question: A rectangular beam section is 40 mm wide and 260 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 40, h = 260 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 40*(260)^2 / 6 | Answer: 450667 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (83 mm x 240 mm) carries a bending moment of 39 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (67 mm x 130 mm) has effective length 1800 mm and E = 200 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 530 MPa is designed for a working stress of 190 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 530, sw = 190 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 530 / 190 | Answer: 2.789

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1350 mm and wall thickness 10 mm carries an internal pressure of 1.8 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1350, t = 10, P = 1.8 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 1.8*1350 / (2*10) | Answer: 121.5 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 1120 K and 410 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 1120, Tc = 410 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 410/1120) * 100 | Answer: 63.39 %

question: A refrigerator works between 275 K (cold) and 324 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 275, Th = 324 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 275 / (324 - 275) | Answer: 5.612

question: A heat pump operates between 264 K and 312 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 264, Th = 312 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 312 / (312 - 264) | Answer: 6.5

question: 6 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 45 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 6, dT = 45 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 6 * 0.718 * 45 | Answer: 193.9 kJ

question: 5.9 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 125 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 5.9, dT = 125 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 5.9 * 1.005 * 125 | Answer: 741.2 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 3.9 m^3 at 580 K with mass 3.9 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 3.9, Tk = 580, m = 3.9 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 3.9*0.287*580 / 3.9 | Answer: 166.5 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 4.8 kg of air expands isothermally at 350 K from volume V1 to 3*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.8, Tk = 350, ratio = 3 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 4.8*0.287*350*ln(3) | Answer: 529.7 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 1.2 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.19 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 1.2, D = 0.19 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*1.2*0.19 / 0.001 | Answer: 228000

question: Water flows at 0.8 m/s through a pipe of diameter 60 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 14.5 m. Taking Cv = 0.97, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 14.5, cv = 0.97 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.97*sqrt(2*9.81*14.5) | Answer: 16.36 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 180 mm) water flows at 2.7 m/s. It contracts to diameter 110 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 180, d2 = 110, V1 = 2.7 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 2.7*(180/110)^2 | Answer: 7.23 m/s

question: Water flows at 1.2 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.43 m and length 300 m. With friction factor f = 0.032, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 36 teeth drives a gear of 65 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1300 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 36, z2 = 65, N1 = 1300 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1300*36 / 65 | Answer: 720 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 300 mm rotates at 1000 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 300, N = 1000 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.3)*1000 / 60 | Answer: 15.71 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 4 kW at 1500 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 4, N = 1500 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(4*1000) / (2*pi*1500) | Answer: 25.46 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 4.4 kg rotates at radius 0.29 m at 650 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 19800 N/m and mass 18.9 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 19800, m = 18.9 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(19800/18.9) | Answer: 5.151 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 6 m^2 and thickness 0.34 m has conductivity k = 13.1 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 200 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 6, L = 0.34, k = 13.1, dT = 200 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 13.1*6*200 / 0.34 | Answer: 46235 W

question: A surface of area 4.6 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 125 W/m^2-K to surroundings 100 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 4.6, h = 125, dT = 100 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 125*4.6*100 | Answer: 57500 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 120 m/min, feed = 0.23 mm/rev, depth of cut = 1.1 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 120, f = 0.23, d = 1.1 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*120*0.23*1.1 | Answer: 30360 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 340 mm is turned at 800 rpm with a feed of 0.4 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 340, N = 800, f = 0.4 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 340 / (0.4*800) | Answer: 1.062 min

question: A resistor of 139 ohm carries a current of 5.9 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 139, I = 5.9 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 5.9 * 139 | Answer: 820.1 V

question: Three resistors 29 ohm, 9 ohm and 71 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 29, R2 = 9, R3 = 71 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 29 + 9 + 71 | Answer: 109 ohm

question: Two resistors 109 ohm and 114 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 109, R2 = 114 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 109*114 / (109+114) | Answer: 55.72 ohm

question: A device draws 6.9 A at 125 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 125, I = 6.9 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 125 * 6.9 | Answer: 862.5 W

question: A current of 10.5 A flows through a 62 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 10.5, R = 62 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (10.5)^2 * 62 | Answer: 6836 W

question: Two capacitors 26 uF and 23.1 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 26, C2 = 23.1 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 26*23.1 / (26+23.1) | Answer: 12.23 uF

question: A resistor 45 kohm and capacitor 1.7 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 45, C = 1.7 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (45k)(1.7u) = 76.5 ms | Answer: 76.5 ms

question: An inductor 310.2 mH is in series with 168 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 310.2, R = 168 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (310.2e-3) / 168 | Answer: 1.846 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 13.6 mH inductor at 900 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 13.6, f = 900 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (900)(13.6e-3) | Answer: 76.91 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 49.9 uF capacitor at 520 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 49.9, f = 520 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (520)(49.9e-6)) | Answer: 6.134 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 72 ohm, XL = 123 ohm and XC = 148 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 72, XL = 123, XC = 148 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(72^2 + (123 - 148)^2) | Answer: 76.22 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 96.7 mH and C = 6 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 96.7, C = 6 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(96.7e-3 * 6e-6)) | Answer: 208.9 Hz

question: A capacitor of 83.3 uF is charged to 335 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 83.3, V = 335 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*83.3e-6*(335)^2 | Answer: 4674 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 180 V with 870 primary turns and 20 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 180, N1 = 870, N2 = 20 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 180 * 20/870 | Answer: 4.138 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 270 V and draws an armature current of 18 A. If the armature resistance is 0.16 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 270, Ia = 18, Ra = 0.16 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 270 - 18*0.16 | Answer: 267.1 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 190 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.86. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 190, VL = 400, pf = 0.86 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*400*190*0.86 / 1000 | Answer: 113.2 kW

question: A load has real power 75 kW and apparent power 140 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 75, S = 140 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 75 / 140 | Answer: 0.5357

question: A machine delivers 25 kW output while drawing 197 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 25, Pi = 197 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 25/197 * 100 | Answer: 12.69 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 10 V across R1 = 36 ohm and R2 = 16 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 10, R1 = 36, R2 = 16 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 10*16 / (36+16) | Answer: 3.077 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 150 kohm and Rin = 38 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 150, Rin = 38 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 150 / 38 | Answer: 3.947

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 170 kohm and Rg = 45 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 170, Rg = 45 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 170/45 | Answer: 4.778

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 7262. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 7262 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(7262) | Answer: 38.61 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 7.4 m carries a central point load of 105 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7.4, W = 105 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 105*7.4 / 4 | Answer: 194.2 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 3.8 m carries a UDL of 15 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.8, w = 15 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 15*(3.8)^2 / 8 | Answer: 27.07 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 5.8 m carries a point load 5 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.8, W = 5 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 5*5.8 | Answer: 29 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 4.7 m carries a UDL of 36 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.7, w = 36 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 36*(4.7)^2 / 2 | Answer: 397.6 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.7 m carries a point load 50 kN at distance 2.2 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 4.7, a = 2.2, W = 50 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 50*(4.7 - 2.2) / 4.7 | Answer: 26.6 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 5.2 m) carries a central point load 65 kN. With E = 200 GPa and I = 600e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=65000 N, L=5200.0 mm, E=200000 MPa, I=600e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 1.587 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 4.5 m carries a UDL of 42 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.5, w = 42 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 42*(4.5)^2 / 12 | Answer: 70.88 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 560 mm, clear cover 45 mm and main bars of diameter 20 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 560, c = 45, dia = 20 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 560 - 45 - 20/2 | Answer: 505 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 10.1 m^2 carrying a factored load of 14.9 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 10.1, w = 14.9 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 14.9 * 10.1 | Answer: 150.5 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 5.1 m, unit weight 20 kN/m^3, phi = 35 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 4.6 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 21 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 4.6, g = 21 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (21 - 9.81)*4.6 | Answer: 51.47 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 7e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1.3, area = 7.1e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 7, i = 1.3, A = 7.1 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (7e-4)*1.3*(7.1e-3) | Answer: 6461 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.8 m, bed slope 0.008 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.016. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 1.5 m under a head of 0.5 m. Taking Cd = 0.62 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 3.3 m wide carries a discharge of 27.1 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 320 m and design speed 90 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 320, V = 90 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (90)^2 / (127*320) | Answer: 0.1993
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: A tank of volume 390 m^3 treats a flow of 100 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 390, Q = 100 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 390 / 100 | Answer: 3.9 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 260 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.28 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 6 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 260, k = 0.28, t = 6 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 260*(1 - e^(-0.28*6)) | Answer: 211.5 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.73, rainfall intensity 35 mm/h over a catchment of 59.2 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.73, i = 35, A = 59.2 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.73*35*59.2 / 360 | Answer: 4.202 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.06 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 280 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.06, M = 280 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 280*(20+0.06)/20 | Answer: 280.8 m

question: Convert the decimal number 933 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 933 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 3A5 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 01000101 and 11011011.
solution: XOR: 10011110 | Count of 1s = 5 | Answer: 5
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 240 megabits is sent over a link of 13 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 240, B = 13 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 240 / 13 | Answer: 18.46 s

question: A link has bandwidth 32 Mbps and round-trip time 50 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 32, R = 50 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 32e6 * 50e-3 bits = 1600 kb | Answer: 1600 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.92, cache access time 1 ns and main-memory access time 80 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.92, tc = 1, tm = 80 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.92*1 + (1 - 0.92)*80 | Answer: 7.32 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 770164 elements?
solution: Given: n = 770164 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(770164)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.004, memory access time 80 ns and page-fault service time 4 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 4 ms = 4000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.004)*80 + 0.004*4000000.0 ns | Answer: 16.08 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 2.3 m^3 at 320 kPa and 490 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 2.3, P = 320, Tk = 490 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (320e3)*2.3 / (8.314*490) | Answer: 180.7 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.26 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 14 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.26, t = 14 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.26*14) | Answer: 0.9737

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.47 /min) is to reach 70% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.47, X = 70 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.7) / 0.47 | Answer: 2.562 min

question: For a reaction with A = 9e10 /s and activation energy 75 kJ/mol at 420 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 9, Ea = 75, Tk = 420 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 9e10 * exp(-75e3 / (8.314*420)) | Answer: 42.3 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.96 and bottoms xW = 0.09, with relative volatility alpha = 3.2. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.96, xw = 0.09, al = 3.2 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.96/0.04)(0.91/0.09)] / ln(3.2) | Answer: 4.721 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.74 and x = 0.41. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.74, x = 0.41 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.74/0.26) / (0.41/0.59) | Answer: 4.096

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.3 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 120 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.3, Psat = 120 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.3 * 120 | Answer: 36 kPa

question: A stream of 8.4 kg/s with specific heat 3.6 kJ/kg-K is heated through 120 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 8.4, cp = 3.6, dT = 120 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 8.4*3.6*120 | Answer: 3629 kW

question: A reactor of volume 6.5 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 2 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 6.5, Q = 2 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 6.5 / 2 | Answer: 3.25 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 5.5e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 1 mm with a concentration difference of 140 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 5.5, L = 1, dC = 140 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (5.5e-9)*140 / (1e-3) | Answer: 770 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 6.4 min and steady-state gain 3.6. For a step input of magnitude 3, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 6.4, K = 3.6, M = 3 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 3.6 * 3 | Answer: 10.8 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 35 m^2 flies at 60 m/s (air density 1.225 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.7. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 35, V = 60, rho = 1.225, CL = 0.7 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1.225*(60)^2*35*0.7 / 1000 | Answer: 54.02 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 85 m^2 flies at 240 m/s (density 0.4 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.06. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 85, V = 240, rho = 0.4, CD = 0.06 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.4*(240)^2*85*0.06 / 1000 | Answer: 58.75 kN

question: A specimen under stress 230 MPa shows an elastic strain of 2.5e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 230, eps = 2.5 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 230 / (2.5e-3) MPa = 92 GPa | Answer: 92 GPa

question: A block of mass 42 kg has a volume of 5.6e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 42, V = 5.6 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 42 / (5.6e-3) | Answer: 7500 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 1900 mm is heated through 140 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 23e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 1900, dT = 140, al = 23 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 1900*23e-6*140 | Answer: 6.118 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 135 ohm, R2 = 25 ohm and R3 = 240 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 135, R2 = 25, R3 = 240 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 25*240 / 135 | Answer: 44.44 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 120 ohm and gauge factor 2 experiences a strain of 1300e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 120, GF = 2, eps = 1300 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 120*2*1300e-6 | Answer: 312 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 10.34 when the true value is 100. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10.34, true = 100 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10.34 - 100| / 100 * 100 | Answer: 89.66 %

question: Annual demand is 49000 units, ordering cost 100 per order and holding cost 24 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 49000, S = 100, H = 24 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*49000*100 / 24) | Answer: 639 units

question: An asset costs 120000 with salvage value 6000 after 17 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 120000, Sv = 6000, n = 17 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (120000 - 6000) / 17 | Answer: 6706 per year

question: A product sells for 340 per unit with variable cost 100 per unit and fixed costs 140000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 340, V = 100, F = 140000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 140000 / (340 - 100) | Answer: 583.3 units

question: Find the present worth of 100000 received 8 years from now at an interest rate of 8% per year.
solution: Given: F = 100000, n = 8, i = 8 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 100000 / (1 + 0.08)^8 | Answer: 54027 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.92, 0.99 and 0.91 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.92, r2 = 0.99, r3 = 0.91 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.92*0.99*0.91 | Answer: 0.8288

question: A process produces 49 defective items in a batch of 4000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 49, N = 4000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 49/4000 * 1e6 | Answer: 12250 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -3x^3 - 2x^2 + 5x - 7 evaluated at x = -4.
For f(x) = 4x^3 - 5x^2 - 2x + 1, find f''(x) at x = -1.
Evaluate the definite integral of (2x^2 - 4x - 7) dx from x = -4 to x = 3.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = 2x^3/3 + -4x^2/2 + -7x | Evaluate F(3) - F(-4) | Answer: 25.67
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 2x^2 + 6x - 7 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[-8, -6], [6, -9]].
solution: Given: a = -8, b = -6, c = 6, d = -9 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (-8)(-9) - (-6)(6) | Answer: 108

question: Find the determinant of [[-3, 5, -4], [5, 2, -1], [-3, -1, 2]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: -48

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[0, 2], [5, -1]].
solution: Trace tr = -1, Determinant = -10 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 2.702

question: Solve for x: -2x + 5y = 9 and 6x + -6y = -3.
solution: Determinant = -2*-6 - 5*6 = -18 | x = (e d - b f) / det = 2.167 | Answer: x = 2.167
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 41, 62, 96, 15, 21.
solution: Sum = 235 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 47 | Answer: 47

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 38, 4, 21, 48, 32.
solution: Mean = 28.6 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 16.88

question: Find the slope of the line through (-2, -6) and (-1, -3).
solution: Given: x1 = -2, y1 = -6, x2 = -1, y2 = -3 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (-3 - -6) / (-1 - -2) | Answer: 3

question: Find the distance between the points (6, 8) and (5, 8).
solution: Given: x1 = 6, y1 = 8, x2 = 5, y2 = 8 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-1)^2 + (0)^2) | Answer: 1 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (-7,-7), (4,-8), (-3,-5).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 13 sq units

question: Find the 15th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 6 and common difference 6.
solution: Given: a = 6, d = 6, n = 15 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = 6 + (15 - 1)*6 | Answer: 90

question: Find the sum of the first 8 terms of an AP with first term 0 and common difference -2.
solution: Given: a = 0, d = -2, n = 8 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 8/2 [2*0 + (8-1)*-2] | Answer: -56

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 3500 at 6.1% per annum for 9 years.
solution: Given: P = 3500, R = 6.1, Tt = 9 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 3500 * 6.1 * 9 / 100 | Answer: 1922 currency units

question: Find the amount when 4500 is invested at 5.1% per annum compounded annually for 6 years.
solution: Given: P = 4500, R = 5.1, Tt = 6 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 4500 * (1 + 5.1/100)^6 | Answer: 6065 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (5, -3, 3) and (5, -5, -2).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (4, -4, -5) and (5, 3, 2).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 46.5

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (-3, 1, 5) and (3, 6, -6).

question: Find the modulus of the complex number 11 + 8i.
solution: Given: a = 11, b = 8 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((11)^2 + (8)^2) | Answer: 13.6

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number 4 + 7i.
solution: Given: a = 4, b = 7 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(7, 4) | Answer: 60.26 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -4x^3 + 4x^2 - 2x + 2 at x = 5.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-86 with initial guess x0=9, find x1 (one iteration).
solution: Given: N = 86, x0 = 9 | Formula: x1 = x0 - (x0^2 - N)/(2 x0) | Substitute: x1 = 9 - ((9)^2 - 86)/(2*9) | Answer: 9.278

question: Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.3 and ordinates 4, 20, 20, 6, 13, estimate the integral.

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 53 and 29.
solution: Given: a = 53, b = 29 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 53*29 / 1 | Answer: 1537
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 25 mm carries an axial tensile load of 49 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 36 mm and length 800 mm carries an axial load of 49 kN. Take E = 210 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 48 mm transmits a torque of 2050 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 48, Tt = 2050 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(2050*1000) / (pi*(48)^3) | Answer: 94.41 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 40 mm and length 1500 mm carries a torque of 1200 N-m. With G = 80 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (40)^4 / 32 = 251327 mm^4 | theta = (1200*1000)(1500) / (80000 * 251327) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 5.129 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 32 mm wide and 290 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 32, h = 290 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 32*(290)^2 / 6 | Answer: 448533 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (52 mm x 250 mm) carries a bending moment of 23 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (68 mm x 110 mm) has effective length 1600 mm and E = 200 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 390 MPa is designed for a working stress of 80 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 390, sw = 80 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 390 / 80 | Answer: 4.875

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1100 mm and wall thickness 20 mm carries an internal pressure of 2.8 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1100, t = 20, P = 2.8 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 2.8*1100 / (2*20) | Answer: 77 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 860 K and 390 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 860, Tc = 390 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 390/860) * 100 | Answer: 54.65 %

question: A refrigerator works between 270 K (cold) and 312 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 270, Th = 312 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 270 / (312 - 270) | Answer: 6.429

question: A heat pump operates between 274 K and 324 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 274, Th = 324 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 324 / (324 - 274) | Answer: 6.48

question: 2.7 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 75 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.7, dT = 75 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 2.7 * 0.718 * 75 | Answer: 145.4 kJ

question: 7.1 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 110 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 7.1, dT = 110 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 7.1 * 1.005 * 110 | Answer: 784.9 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 3.7 m^3 at 310 K with mass 3.9 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 3.7, Tk = 310, m = 3.9 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 3.9*0.287*310 / 3.7 | Answer: 93.78 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 4.7 kg of air expands isothermally at 400 K from volume V1 to 3*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.7, Tk = 400, ratio = 3 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 4.7*0.287*400*ln(3) | Answer: 592.8 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 4.4 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.14 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 4.4, D = 0.14 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*4.4*0.14 / 0.001 | Answer: 616000

question: Water flows at 0.5 m/s through a pipe of diameter 60 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 26.6 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 26.6 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*26.6 / 1000 | Answer: 260.9 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 4.3 m. Taking Cv = 0.97, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 4.3, cv = 0.97 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.97*sqrt(2*9.81*4.3) | Answer: 8.91 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 220 mm) water flows at 1.1 m/s. It contracts to diameter 140 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
Water flows at 2.2 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.33 m and length 70 m. With friction factor f = 0.037, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 24 teeth drives a gear of 81 teeth. If the pinion runs at 650 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 24, z2 = 81, N1 = 650 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 650*24 / 81 | Answer: 192.6 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 180 mm rotates at 650 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 180, N = 650 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.18)*650 / 60 | Answer: 6.126 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 19.4 kW at 300 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 19.4, N = 300 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(19.4*1000) / (2*pi*300) | Answer: 617.5 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 9.5 kg rotates at radius 0.31 m at 550 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 3600 N/m and mass 19.5 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 3600, m = 19.5 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(3600/19.5) | Answer: 2.162 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 7.4 m^2 and thickness 0.38 m has conductivity k = 0.9 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 150 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 7.4, L = 0.38, k = 0.9, dT = 150 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 0.9*7.4*150 / 0.38 | Answer: 2629 W

question: A surface of area 3.4 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 125 W/m^2-K to surroundings 70 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 3.4, h = 125, dT = 70 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 125*3.4*70 | Answer: 29750 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 90 m/min, feed = 0.29 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2.4 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 90, f = 0.29, d = 2.4 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*90*0.29*2.4 | Answer: 62640 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 340 mm is turned at 750 rpm with a feed of 0.3 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 340, N = 750, f = 0.3 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 340 / (0.3*750) | Answer: 1.511 min

question: A resistor of 25 ohm carries a current of 6.3 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 25, I = 6.3 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 6.3 * 25 | Answer: 157.5 V

question: Three resistors 87 ohm, 76 ohm and 83 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 87, R2 = 76, R3 = 83 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 87 + 76 + 83 | Answer: 246 ohm

question: Two resistors 120 ohm and 15 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 120, R2 = 15 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 120*15 / (120+15) | Answer: 13.33 ohm

question: A device draws 9.6 A at 225 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 225, I = 9.6 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 225 * 9.6 | Answer: 2160 W

question: A current of 11.7 A flows through a 114 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 11.7, R = 114 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (11.7)^2 * 114 | Answer: 15605 W

question: Two capacitors 27.2 uF and 27.8 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 27.2, C2 = 27.8 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 27.2*27.8 / (27.2+27.8) | Answer: 13.75 uF

question: A resistor 53 kohm and capacitor 7.8 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 53, C = 7.8 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (53k)(7.8u) = 413.4 ms | Answer: 413.4 ms

question: An inductor 132 mH is in series with 148 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 132, R = 148 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (132e-3) / 148 | Answer: 0.8919 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 90.7 mH inductor at 730 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 90.7, f = 730 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (730)(90.7e-3) | Answer: 416 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 11.8 uF capacitor at 390 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 11.8, f = 390 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (390)(11.8e-6)) | Answer: 34.58 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 57 ohm, XL = 147 ohm and XC = 145 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 57, XL = 147, XC = 145 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(57^2 + (147 - 145)^2) | Answer: 57.04 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 81.8 mH and C = 7.5 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 81.8, C = 7.5 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(81.8e-3 * 7.5e-6)) | Answer: 203.2 Hz

question: A capacitor of 58 uF is charged to 135 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 58, V = 135 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*58e-6*(135)^2 | Answer: 528.5 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 260 V with 830 primary turns and 150 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 260, N1 = 830, N2 = 150 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 260 * 150/830 | Answer: 46.99 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 410 V and draws an armature current of 14 A. If the armature resistance is 0.36 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 410, Ia = 14, Ra = 0.36 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 410 - 14*0.36 | Answer: 405 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 80 A at 433 V (line) with a power factor of 0.78. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 80, VL = 433, pf = 0.78 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*433*80*0.78 / 1000 | Answer: 46.8 kW

question: A load has real power 35 kW and apparent power 220 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 35, S = 220 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 35 / 220 | Answer: 0.1591

question: A machine delivers 45 kW output while drawing 142 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 45, Pi = 142 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 45/142 * 100 | Answer: 31.69 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 13 V across R1 = 38 ohm and R2 = 15 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 13, R1 = 38, R2 = 15 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 13*15 / (38+15) | Answer: 3.679 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 220 kohm and Rin = 7 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 220, Rin = 7 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 220 / 7 | Answer: 31.43

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 140 kohm and Rg = 47 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 140, Rg = 47 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 140/47 | Answer: 3.979

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 9424. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 9424 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(9424) | Answer: 39.74 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 3.1 m carries a central point load of 70 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.1, W = 70 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 70*3.1 / 4 | Answer: 54.25 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 7 m carries a UDL of 40 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7, w = 40 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 40*(7)^2 / 8 | Answer: 245 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 3.8 m carries a point load 45 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.8, W = 45 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 45*3.8 | Answer: 171 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 1.9 m carries a UDL of 16 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 1.9, w = 16 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 16*(1.9)^2 / 2 | Answer: 28.88 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 5.1 m carries a point load 75 kN at distance 2.3 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 5.1, a = 2.3, W = 75 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 75*(5.1 - 2.3) / 5.1 | Answer: 41.18 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 6.1 m) carries a central point load 60 kN. With E = 30 GPa and I = 360e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=60000 N, L=6100.0 mm, E=30000 MPa, I=360e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 26.27 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 4.6 m carries a UDL of 12 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.6, w = 12 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 12*(4.6)^2 / 12 | Answer: 21.16 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 680 mm, clear cover 25 mm and main bars of diameter 25 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 680, c = 25, dia = 25 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 680 - 25 - 25/2 | Answer: 642.5 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 32.3 m^2 carrying a factored load of 17.7 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 32.3, w = 17.7 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 17.7 * 32.3 | Answer: 571.7 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 6.6 m, unit weight 16 kN/m^3, phi = 30 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 3 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 20 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 3, g = 20 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (20 - 9.81)*3 | Answer: 30.57 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 2.1e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1.2, area = 4.7e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 2.1, i = 1.2, A = 4.7 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (2.1e-4)*1.2*(4.7e-3) | Answer: 1184 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 2.3 m, bed slope 0.008 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.02. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 4 m under a head of 0.3 m. Taking Cd = 0.61 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 4.4 m wide carries a discharge of 23.8 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 390 m and design speed 40 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 390, V = 40 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (40)^2 / (127*390) | Answer: 0.0323
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: A tank of volume 150 m^3 treats a flow of 145 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 150, Q = 145 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 150 / 145 | Answer: 1.034 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 210 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.22 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 8 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 210, k = 0.22, t = 8 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 210*(1 - e^(-0.22*8)) | Answer: 173.9 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.54, rainfall intensity 50 mm/h over a catchment of 8.7 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.54, i = 50, A = 8.7 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.54*50*8.7 / 360 | Answer: 0.6525 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.07 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 710 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.07, M = 710 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 710*(30+0.07)/30 | Answer: 711.7 m

question: Convert the decimal number 2670 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 2670 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: A6E (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 01111001 and 00110011.
solution: XOR: 01001010 | Count of 1s = 3 | Answer: 3
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 140 megabits is sent over a link of 30 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 140, B = 30 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 140 / 30 | Answer: 4.667 s

question: A link has bandwidth 71 Mbps and round-trip time 80 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 71, R = 80 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 71e6 * 80e-3 bits = 5680 kb | Answer: 5680 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.95, cache access time 3 ns and main-memory access time 60 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.95, tc = 3, tm = 60 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.95*3 + (1 - 0.95)*60 | Answer: 5.85 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 382933 elements?
solution: Given: n = 382933 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(382933)) + 1 | Answer: 19

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.01, memory access time 150 ns and page-fault service time 3 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 3 ms = 3000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.01)*150 + 0.01*3000000.0 ns | Answer: 30.15 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 2.9 m^3 at 230 kPa and 470 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 2.9, P = 230, Tk = 470 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (230e3)*2.9 / (8.314*470) | Answer: 170.7 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.23 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 10 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.23, t = 10 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.23*10) | Answer: 0.8997

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.39 /min) is to reach 65% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.39, X = 65 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.65) / 0.39 | Answer: 2.692 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.11 /min) reaches 70% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.11, X = 70 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.7 / (0.11*(1 - 0.7)) | Answer: 21.21 min

question: For a reaction with A = 8e10 /s and activation energy 70 kJ/mol at 470 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 8, Ea = 70, Tk = 470 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 8e10 * exp(-70e3 / (8.314*470)) | Answer: 1328 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.96 and bottoms xW = 0.09, with relative volatility alpha = 2.1. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.96, xw = 0.09, al = 2.1 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.96/0.04)(0.91/0.09)] / ln(2.1) | Answer: 7.402 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.87 and x = 0.47. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.87, x = 0.47 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.87/0.13) / (0.47/0.53) | Answer: 7.547

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.14 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 20 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.14, Psat = 20 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.14 * 20 | Answer: 2.8 kPa

question: A stream of 1.5 kg/s with specific heat 2.2 kJ/kg-K is heated through 85 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 1.5, cp = 2.2, dT = 85 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 1.5*2.2*85 | Answer: 280.5 kW

question: A reactor of volume 3.7 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 1.1 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 3.7, Q = 1.1 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 3.7 / 1.1 | Answer: 3.364 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 6.4e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 2 mm with a concentration difference of 50 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 6.4, L = 2, dC = 50 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (6.4e-9)*50 / (2e-3) | Answer: 160 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 5.3 min and steady-state gain 3.8. For a step input of magnitude 5, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 5.3, K = 3.8, M = 5 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 3.8 * 5 | Answer: 19 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 100 m^2 flies at 140 m/s (air density 1 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.7. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 100, V = 140, rho = 1, CL = 0.7 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1*(140)^2*100*0.7 / 1000 | Answer: 686 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 45 m^2 flies at 230 m/s (density 1.225 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.03. Find the drag force in kN.
A specimen under stress 310 MPa shows an elastic strain of 2.9e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 310, eps = 2.9 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 310 / (2.9e-3) MPa = 106.9 GPa | Answer: 106.9 GPa

question: A block of mass 12 kg has a volume of 3.8e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 12, V = 3.8 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 12 / (3.8e-3) | Answer: 3158 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 600 mm is heated through 40 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 17e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 600, dT = 40, al = 17 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 600*17e-6*40 | Answer: 0.408 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 75 ohm, R2 = 130 ohm and R3 = 275 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 75, R2 = 130, R3 = 275 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 130*275 / 75 | Answer: 476.7 ohm

question: A measurement reads 10.02 when the true value is 100. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10.02, true = 100 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10.02 - 100| / 100 * 100 | Answer: 89.98 %

question: Annual demand is 33500 units, ordering cost 240 per order and holding cost 8 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 33500, S = 240, H = 8 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*33500*240 / 8) | Answer: 1418 units

question: An asset costs 330000 with salvage value 6000 after 7 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 330000, Sv = 6000, n = 7 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (330000 - 6000) / 7 | Answer: 46286 per year

question: A product sells for 190 per unit with variable cost 60 per unit and fixed costs 140000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 190, V = 60, F = 140000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 140000 / (190 - 60) | Answer: 1077 units

question: Find the present worth of 65000 received 5 years from now at an interest rate of 10% per year.
solution: Given: F = 65000, n = 5, i = 10 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 65000 / (1 + 0.1)^5 | Answer: 4036 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.99, 0.9 and 0.95 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.99, r2 = 0.9, r3 = 0.95 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.99*0.9*0.95 | Answer: 0.8464

question: A process produces 38 defective items in a batch of 10500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 38, N = 10500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 38/10500 * 1e6 | Answer: 3619 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = 2x^3 + x - 5 evaluated at x = 0.
For f(x) = -5x^3 + 3x^2 - 6x - 3, find f''(x) at x = -1.
Evaluate the definite integral of (x - 6) dx from x = -2 to x = 6.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = 0x^3/3 + 1x^2/2 + -6x | Evaluate F(6) - F(-2) | Answer: -32
