question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 9 m. Taking Cv = 0.98, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 9, cv = 0.98 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.98*sqrt(2*9.81*9) | Answer: 13.02 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 230 mm) water flows at 2.8 m/s. It contracts to diameter 80 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 230, d2 = 80, V1 = 2.8 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 2.8*(230/80)^2 | Answer: 23.14 m/s

question: Water flows at 4 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.21 m and length 290 m. With friction factor f = 0.039, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 24 teeth drives a gear of 88 teeth. If the pinion runs at 650 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 24, z2 = 88, N1 = 650 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 650*24 / 88 | Answer: 177.3 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 290 mm rotates at 1250 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 290, N = 1250 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.29)*1250 / 60 | Answer: 18.98 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 7.3 kW at 1250 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 7.3, N = 1250 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(7.3*1000) / (2*pi*1250) | Answer: 55.77 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 4.7 kg rotates at radius 0.46 m at 1150 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 15300 N/m and mass 7.3 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 15300, m = 7.3 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(15300/7.3) | Answer: 7.286 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 1.3 m^2 and thickness 0.21 m has conductivity k = 22.5 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 160 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 1.3, L = 0.21, k = 22.5, dT = 160 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 22.5*1.3*160 / 0.21 | Answer: 22286 W

question: A surface of area 5.1 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 160 W/m^2-K to surroundings 65 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 5.1, h = 160, dT = 65 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 160*5.1*65 | Answer: 53040 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 70 m/min, feed = 0.31 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2.3 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 70, f = 0.31, d = 2.3 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*70*0.31*2.3 | Answer: 49910 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 440 mm is turned at 1100 rpm with a feed of 0.21 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 440, N = 1100, f = 0.21 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 440 / (0.21*1100) | Answer: 1.905 min

question: A resistor of 145 ohm carries a current of 7.4 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 145, I = 7.4 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 7.4 * 145 | Answer: 1073 V

question: Three resistors 67 ohm, 12 ohm and 69 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 67, R2 = 12, R3 = 69 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 67 + 12 + 69 | Answer: 148 ohm

question: Two resistors 97 ohm and 26 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 97, R2 = 26 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 97*26 / (97+26) | Answer: 20.5 ohm

question: A device draws 12.3 A at 215 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 215, I = 12.3 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 215 * 12.3 | Answer: 2644 W

question: A current of 0.6 A flows through a 54 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 0.6, R = 54 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (0.6)^2 * 54 | Answer: 19.44 W

question: Two capacitors 41.6 uF and 43.9 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 41.6, C2 = 43.9 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 41.6*43.9 / (41.6+43.9) | Answer: 21.36 uF

question: A resistor 13 kohm and capacitor 18.5 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 13, C = 18.5 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (13k)(18.5u) = 240.5 ms | Answer: 240.5 ms

question: An inductor 391 mH is in series with 89 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 391, R = 89 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (391e-3) / 89 | Answer: 4.393 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 130.8 mH inductor at 270 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 130.8, f = 270 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (270)(130.8e-3) | Answer: 221.9 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 37.7 uF capacitor at 490 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 37.7, f = 490 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (490)(37.7e-6)) | Answer: 8.616 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 93 ohm, XL = 29 ohm and XC = 101 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 93, XL = 29, XC = 101 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(93^2 + (29 - 101)^2) | Answer: 117.6 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 5.4 mH and C = 7.5 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 5.4, C = 7.5 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(5.4e-3 * 7.5e-6)) | Answer: 790.8 Hz

question: A capacitor of 3.1 uF is charged to 260 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 3.1, V = 260 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*3.1e-6*(260)^2 | Answer: 104.8 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 330 V with 430 primary turns and 240 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 330, N1 = 430, N2 = 240 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 330 * 240/430 | Answer: 184.2 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 440 V and draws an armature current of 7 A. If the armature resistance is 0.64 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 440, Ia = 7, Ra = 0.64 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 440 - 7*0.64 | Answer: 435.5 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 5 A at 415 V (line) with a power factor of 0.88. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 5, VL = 415, pf = 0.88 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*415*5*0.88 / 1000 | Answer: 3.163 kW

question: A load has real power 35 kW and apparent power 210 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 35, S = 210 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 35 / 210 | Answer: 0.1667

question: A machine delivers 40 kW output while drawing 202 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 40, Pi = 202 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 40/202 * 100 | Answer: 19.8 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 26 V across R1 = 36 ohm and R2 = 13 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 26, R1 = 36, R2 = 13 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 26*13 / (36+13) | Answer: 6.898 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 110 kohm and Rin = 4 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 110, Rin = 4 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 110 / 4 | Answer: 27.5

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 150 kohm and Rg = 1 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 150, Rg = 1 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 150/1 | Answer: 151

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 3245. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 3245 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(3245) | Answer: 35.11 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 7.3 m carries a central point load of 75 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7.3, W = 75 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 75*7.3 / 4 | Answer: 136.9 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 3.5 m carries a UDL of 10 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.5, w = 10 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 10*(3.5)^2 / 8 | Answer: 15.31 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 5.9 m carries a point load 65 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.9, W = 65 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 65*5.9 | Answer: 383.5 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 5.4 m carries a UDL of 26 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.4, w = 26 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 26*(5.4)^2 / 2 | Answer: 379.1 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 8.8 m carries a point load 90 kN at distance 2.1 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 8.8, a = 2.1, W = 90 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 90*(8.8 - 2.1) / 8.8 | Answer: 68.52 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 7.7 m) carries a central point load 80 kN. With E = 30 GPa and I = 190e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=80000 N, L=7700.0 mm, E=30000 MPa, I=190e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 133.5 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 8.3 m carries a UDL of 24 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 8.3, w = 24 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 24*(8.3)^2 / 12 | Answer: 137.8 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 490 mm, clear cover 40 mm and main bars of diameter 20 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 490, c = 40, dia = 20 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 490 - 40 - 20/2 | Answer: 440 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 33.5 m^2 carrying a factored load of 8.8 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 33.5, w = 8.8 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 8.8 * 33.5 | Answer: 294.8 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 3 m, unit weight 17 kN/m^3, phi = 38 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 10.2 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 18 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 10.2, g = 18 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (18 - 9.81)*10.2 | Answer: 83.54 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 4.7e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1, area = 3.7e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 4.7, i = 1, A = 3.7 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (4.7e-4)*1*(3.7e-3) | Answer: 1739 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.4 m, bed slope 0.004 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.022. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 1.4 m under a head of 0.3 m. Taking Cd = 0.61 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.

question: A rectangular channel 4.8 m wide carries a discharge of 9.4 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).

formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: A tank of volume 160 m^3 treats a flow of 60 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 160, Q = 60 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 160 / 60 | Answer: 2.667 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 200 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.16 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 7 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 200, k = 0.16, t = 7 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 200*(1 - e^(-0.16*7)) | Answer: 134.7 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.45, rainfall intensity 50 mm/h over a catchment of 43.1 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.45, i = 50, A = 43.1 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.45*50*43.1 / 360 | Answer: 2.694 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.02 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 250 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.02, M = 250 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 250*(20+0.02)/20 | Answer: 250.2 m

question: Convert the decimal number 3489 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 3489 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: DA1 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 01011011 and 11001110.
solution: XOR: 10010101 | Count of 1s = 4 | Answer: 4
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 150 megabits is sent over a link of 29 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 150, B = 29 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 150 / 29 | Answer: 5.172 s

question: A link has bandwidth 5 Mbps and round-trip time 140 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 5, R = 140 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 5e6 * 140e-3 bits = 700 kb | Answer: 700 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.89, cache access time 6 ns and main-memory access time 110 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.89, tc = 6, tm = 110 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.89*6 + (1 - 0.89)*110 | Answer: 17.44 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 394987 elements?
solution: Given: n = 394987 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(394987)) + 1 | Answer: 19

question: An O(n^2) algorithm performs c*n^2 basic operations. If c = 1 and n = 790, how many operations are performed?
solution: Given: n = 790 | Formula: operations = n^2 | Substitute: = (790)^2 | Answer: 624100

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.009, memory access time 90 ns and page-fault service time 3 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 3 ms = 3000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.009)*90 + 0.009*3000000.0 ns | Answer: 27.09 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 2.7 m^3 at 210 kPa and 400 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 2.7, P = 210, Tk = 400 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (210e3)*2.7 / (8.314*400) | Answer: 170.5 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.14 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 19 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.14, t = 19 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.14*19) | Answer: 0.9301

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.15 /min) is to reach 85% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.15, X = 85 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.85) / 0.15 | Answer: 12.65 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.43 /min) reaches 55% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.43, X = 55 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.55 / (0.43*(1 - 0.55)) | Answer: 2.842 min

question: For a reaction with A = 7e10 /s and activation energy 85 kJ/mol at 420 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 7, Ea = 85, Tk = 420 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 7e10 * exp(-85e3 / (8.314*420)) | Answer: 1.877 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.92 and bottoms xW = 0.02, with relative volatility alpha = 2.1. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.92, xw = 0.02, al = 2.1 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.92/0.08)(0.98/0.02)] / ln(2.1) | Answer: 8.537 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.6 and x = 0.39. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.6, x = 0.39 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.6/0.4) / (0.39/0.61) | Answer: 2.346

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.74 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 65 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.74, Psat = 65 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.74 * 65 | Answer: 48.1 kPa

question: A stream of 3.7 kg/s with specific heat 3.8 kJ/kg-K is heated through 110 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 3.7, cp = 3.8, dT = 110 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 3.7*3.8*110 | Answer: 1547 kW

question: A reactor of volume 8.8 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 0.5 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 8.8, Q = 0.5 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 8.8 / 0.5 | Answer: 17.6 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 5.9e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 2 mm with a concentration difference of 100 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 5.9, L = 2, dC = 100 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (5.9e-9)*100 / (2e-3) | Answer: 295 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 2.9 min and steady-state gain 3.5. For a step input of magnitude 11, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 2.9, K = 3.5, M = 11 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 3.5 * 11 | Answer: 38.5 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 80 m^2 flies at 60 m/s (air density 0.7 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.9. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 80, V = 60, rho = 0.7, CL = 0.9 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.7*(60)^2*80*0.9 / 1000 | Answer: 90.72 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 45 m^2 flies at 170 m/s (density 1.225 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.03. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 45, V = 170, rho = 1.225, CD = 0.03 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*1.225*(170)^2*45*0.03 / 1000 | Answer: 23.9 kN

question: A specimen under stress 270 MPa shows an elastic strain of 2.4e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 270, eps = 2.4 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 270 / (2.4e-3) MPa = 112.5 GPa | Answer: 112.5 GPa

question: A block of mass 9 kg has a volume of 3.8e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 9, V = 3.8 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 9 / (3.8e-3) | Answer: 2368 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 1400 mm is heated through 135 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 17e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 1400, dT = 135, al = 17 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 1400*17e-6*135 | Answer: 3.213 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 155 ohm, R2 = 150 ohm and R3 = 395 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 155, R2 = 150, R3 = 395 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 150*395 / 155 | Answer: 382.3 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 350 ohm and gauge factor 2.1 experiences a strain of 1700e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 350, GF = 2.1, eps = 1700 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 350*2.1*1700e-6 | Answer: 1249 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 10.53 when the true value is 20. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10.53, true = 20 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10.53 - 20| / 20 * 100 | Answer: 47.35 %

question: Annual demand is 25500 units, ordering cost 240 per order and holding cost 17 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 25500, S = 240, H = 17 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*25500*240 / 17) | Answer: 848.5 units

question: An asset costs 210000 with salvage value 10000 after 15 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 210000, Sv = 10000, n = 15 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (210000 - 10000) / 15 | Answer: 13333 per year

question: A product sells for 190 per unit with variable cost 10 per unit and fixed costs 30000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 190, V = 10, F = 30000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 30000 / (190 - 10) | Answer: 166.7 units

question: Find the present worth of 145000 received 2 years from now at an interest rate of 5% per year.
solution: Given: F = 145000, n = 2, i = 5 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 145000 / (1 + 0.05)^2 | Answer: 131519 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.94, 0.95 and 0.93 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.94, r2 = 0.95, r3 = 0.93 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.94*0.95*0.93 | Answer: 0.8305

question: A process produces 26 defective items in a batch of 8000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 26, N = 8000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 26/8000 * 1e6 | Answer: 3250 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -5x^3 + 5x^2 - 3x + 1 evaluated at x = 1.
For f(x) = -6x^3 - 8x^2 - 4x - 4, find f''(x) at x = 2.

question: Find the 31th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -3 and common difference 4.

question: Find the sum of the first 35 terms of an AP with first term -7 and common difference -4.
solution: Given: a = -7, d = -4, n = 35 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 35/2 [2*-7 + (35-1)*-4] | Answer: -2625

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 24000 at 11.7% per annum for 7 years.
solution: Given: P = 24000, R = 11.7, Tt = 7 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 24000 * 11.7 * 7 / 100 | Answer: 19656 currency units

question: Find the amount when 40000 is invested at 5.8% per annum compounded annually for 4 years.
solution: Given: P = 40000, R = 5.8, Tt = 4 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 40000 * (1 + 5.8/100)^4 | Answer: 50119 currency units

question: Find the modulus of the complex number -2 + 5i.
solution: Given: a = -2, b = 5 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((-2)^2 + (5)^2) | Answer: 5.385

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number -4 + 10i.
solution: Given: a = -4, b = 10 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(10, -4) | Answer: 111.8 degrees

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 39 and 56.
solution: Given: a = 39, b = 56 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 39*56 / 1 | Answer: 2184
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 30 mm carries an axial tensile load of 30 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 40 mm and length 2900 mm carries an axial load of 46 kN. Take E = 110 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 53 mm transmits a torque of 1400 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 53, Tt = 1400 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(1400*1000) / (pi*(53)^3) | Answer: 47.89 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 33 mm and length 1600 mm carries a torque of 1900 N-m. With G = 77 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (33)^4 / 32 = 116428 mm^4 | theta = (1900*1000)(1600) / (77000 * 116428) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 19.43 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 105 mm wide and 130 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 105, h = 130 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 105*(130)^2 / 6 | Answer: 295750 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (119 mm x 230 mm) carries a bending moment of 31 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (66 mm x 130 mm) has effective length 3000 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 560 MPa is designed for a working stress of 80 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 560, sw = 80 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 560 / 80 | Answer: 7

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 800 mm and wall thickness 17 mm carries an internal pressure of 1 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 800, t = 17, P = 1 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 1*800 / (2*17) | Answer: 23.53 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 1060 K and 390 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 1060, Tc = 390 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 390/1060) * 100 | Answer: 63.21 %

question: A refrigerator works between 264 K (cold) and 324 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 264, Th = 324 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 264 / (324 - 264) | Answer: 4.4

question: A heat pump operates between 263 K and 326 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 263, Th = 326 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 326 / (326 - 263) | Answer: 5.175

question: 7.9 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 170 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 7.9, dT = 170 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 7.9 * 0.718 * 170 | Answer: 964.3 kJ

question: 7.6 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 195 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 7.6, dT = 195 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 7.6 * 1.005 * 195 | Answer: 1489 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 3.6 m^3 at 520 K with mass 3.5 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 3.6, Tk = 520, m = 3.5 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 3.5*0.287*520 / 3.6 | Answer: 145.1 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 3 kg of air expands isothermally at 410 K from volume V1 to 4*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3, Tk = 410, ratio = 4 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 3*0.287*410*ln(4) | Answer: 489.4 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 3.9 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.2 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 3.9, D = 0.2 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*3.9*0.2 / 0.001 | Answer: 780000

question: Water flows at 3.6 m/s through a pipe of diameter 210 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 9.8 m. Taking Cv = 0.96, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 9.8, cv = 0.96 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.96*sqrt(2*9.81*9.8) | Answer: 13.31 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 360 mm) water flows at 2.6 m/s. It contracts to diameter 80 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 360, d2 = 80, V1 = 2.6 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 2.6*(360/80)^2 | Answer: 52.65 m/s

question: Water flows at 2.7 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.41 m and length 420 m. With friction factor f = 0.033, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 32 teeth drives a gear of 50 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1150 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 32, z2 = 50, N1 = 1150 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1150*32 / 50 | Answer: 736 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 480 mm rotates at 1500 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 480, N = 1500 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.48)*1500 / 60 | Answer: 37.7 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 8.5 kW at 1250 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 8.5, N = 1250 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(8.5*1000) / (2*pi*1250) | Answer: 64.94 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 2.2 kg rotates at radius 0.36 m at 350 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 6800 N/m and mass 14.7 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 6800, m = 14.7 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(6800/14.7) | Answer: 3.423 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 8.9 m^2 and thickness 0.3 m has conductivity k = 20.6 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 120 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 8.9, L = 0.3, k = 20.6, dT = 120 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 20.6*8.9*120 / 0.3 | Answer: 73336 W

question: A surface of area 3.8 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 20 W/m^2-K to surroundings 120 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 3.8, h = 20, dT = 120 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 20*3.8*120 | Answer: 9120 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 250 m/min, feed = 0.4 mm/rev, depth of cut = 0.5 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 250, f = 0.4, d = 0.5 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*250*0.4*0.5 | Answer: 50000 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 320 mm is turned at 600 rpm with a feed of 0.19 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 320, N = 600, f = 0.19 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 320 / (0.19*600) | Answer: 2.807 min

question: A resistor of 32 ohm carries a current of 3.2 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 32, I = 3.2 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 3.2 * 32 | Answer: 102.4 V

question: Three resistors 8 ohm, 48 ohm and 33 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 8, R2 = 48, R3 = 33 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 8 + 48 + 33 | Answer: 89 ohm

question: Two resistors 4 ohm and 75 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 4, R2 = 75 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 4*75 / (4+75) | Answer: 3.797 ohm

question: A device draws 0.7 A at 75 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 75, I = 0.7 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 75 * 0.7 | Answer: 52.5 W

question: A current of 10.6 A flows through a 71 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 10.6, R = 71 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (10.6)^2 * 71 | Answer: 7978 W

question: Two capacitors 10.4 uF and 39.6 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 10.4, C2 = 39.6 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 10.4*39.6 / (10.4+39.6) | Answer: 8.237 uF

question: A resistor 15 kohm and capacitor 14.9 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 15, C = 14.9 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (15k)(14.9u) = 223.5 ms | Answer: 223.5 ms

question: An inductor 65.1 mH is in series with 186 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 65.1, R = 186 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (65.1e-3) / 186 | Answer: 0.35 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 103.1 mH inductor at 250 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 103.1, f = 250 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (250)(103.1e-3) | Answer: 161.9 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 30.9 uF capacitor at 450 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 30.9, f = 450 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (450)(30.9e-6)) | Answer: 11.45 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 55 ohm, XL = 45 ohm and XC = 16 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 55, XL = 45, XC = 16 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(55^2 + (45 - 16)^2) | Answer: 62.18 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 47.1 mH and C = 7 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 47.1, C = 7 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(47.1e-3 * 7e-6)) | Answer: 277.2 Hz

question: A capacitor of 11.4 uF is charged to 295 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 11.4, V = 295 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*11.4e-6*(295)^2 | Answer: 496 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 330 V with 760 primary turns and 330 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 330, N1 = 760, N2 = 330 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 330 * 330/760 | Answer: 143.3 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 160 V and draws an armature current of 5 A. If the armature resistance is 0.34 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 160, Ia = 5, Ra = 0.34 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 160 - 5*0.34 | Answer: 158.3 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 10 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.7. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 10, VL = 400, pf = 0.7 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*400*10*0.7 / 1000 | Answer: 4.85 kW

question: A load has real power 140 kW and apparent power 160 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 140, S = 160 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 140 / 160 | Answer: 0.875

question: A machine delivers 110 kW output while drawing 197 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 110, Pi = 197 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 110/197 * 100 | Answer: 55.84 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 15 V across R1 = 29 ohm and R2 = 27 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 15, R1 = 29, R2 = 27 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 15*27 / (29+27) | Answer: 7.232 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 180 kohm and Rin = 26 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 180, Rin = 26 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 180 / 26 | Answer: 6.923

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 20 kohm and Rg = 34 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 20, Rg = 34 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 20/34 | Answer: 1.588

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 2119. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 2119 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(2119) | Answer: 33.26 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 3.7 m carries a central point load of 45 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.7, W = 45 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 45*3.7 / 4 | Answer: 41.62 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 5.4 m carries a UDL of 5 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.4, w = 5 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 5*(5.4)^2 / 8 | Answer: 18.23 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 5.5 m carries a point load 80 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.5, W = 80 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 80*5.5 | Answer: 440 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 1.4 m carries a UDL of 28 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 1.4, w = 28 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 28*(1.4)^2 / 2 | Answer: 27.44 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.6 m carries a point load 25 kN at distance 3.8 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 4.6, a = 3.8, W = 25 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 25*(4.6 - 3.8) / 4.6 | Answer: 4.348 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 3.4 m) carries a central point load 40 kN. With E = 25 GPa and I = 490e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=40000 N, L=3400.0 mm, E=25000 MPa, I=490e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 2.674 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 5.8 m carries a UDL of 42 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.8, w = 42 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 42*(5.8)^2 / 12 | Answer: 117.7 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 300 mm, clear cover 30 mm and main bars of diameter 12 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 300, c = 30, dia = 12 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 300 - 30 - 12/2 | Answer: 264 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 28.5 m^2 carrying a factored load of 10.1 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 28.5, w = 10.1 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 10.1 * 28.5 | Answer: 287.8 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 4.2 m, unit weight 20 kN/m^3, phi = 31 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 7.2 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 19 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 7.2, g = 19 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (19 - 9.81)*7.2 | Answer: 66.17 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 3.2e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1.3, area = 4.1e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 3.2, i = 1.3, A = 4.1 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (3.2e-4)*1.3*(4.1e-3) | Answer: 1706 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.1 m, bed slope 0.002 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.016. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 4.3 m under a head of 1.2 m. Taking Cd = 0.62 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 2.7 m wide carries a discharge of 26.7 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 300 m and design speed 85 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 300, V = 85 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (85)^2 / (127*300) | Answer: 0.1896
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: A tank of volume 610 m^3 treats a flow of 100 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 610, Q = 100 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 610 / 100 | Answer: 6.1 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 260 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.23 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 4 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 260, k = 0.23, t = 4 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 260*(1 - e^(-0.23*4)) | Answer: 156.4 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.62, rainfall intensity 35 mm/h over a catchment of 7.3 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.62, i = 35, A = 7.3 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.62*35*7.3 / 360 | Answer: 0.44 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.07 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 680 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.07, M = 680 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 680*(20+0.07)/20 | Answer: 682.4 m

question: Convert the decimal number 1241 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 1241 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 4D9 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 10100011 and 01010111.
solution: XOR: 11110100 | Count of 1s = 5 | Answer: 5
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 20 megabits is sent over a link of 58 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 20, B = 58 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 20 / 58 | Answer: 0.3448 s

question: A link has bandwidth 44 Mbps and round-trip time 160 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 44, R = 160 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 44e6 * 160e-3 bits = 7040 kb | Answer: 7040 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.82, cache access time 5 ns and main-memory access time 60 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.82, tc = 5, tm = 60 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.82*5 + (1 - 0.82)*60 | Answer: 14.9 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 507480 elements?
solution: Given: n = 507480 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(507480)) + 1 | Answer: 19

question: An O(n^2) algorithm performs c*n^2 basic operations. If c = 1 and n = 200, how many operations are performed?
solution: Given: n = 200 | Formula: operations = n^2 | Substitute: = (200)^2 | Answer: 40000

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.009, memory access time 150 ns and page-fault service time 7 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 7 ms = 7000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.009)*150 + 0.009*7000000.0 ns | Answer: 63.15 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 0.5 m^3 at 310 kPa and 300 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 0.5, P = 310, Tk = 300 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (310e3)*0.5 / (8.314*300) | Answer: 62.14 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.39 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 10 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.39, t = 10 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.39*10) | Answer: 0.9798

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.41 /min) reaches 80% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.41, X = 80 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.8 / (0.41*(1 - 0.8)) | Answer: 9.756 min

question: For a reaction with A = 3e10 /s and activation energy 75 kJ/mol at 320 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 3, Ea = 75, Tk = 320 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 3e10 * exp(-75e3 / (8.314*320)) | Answer: 0.01715 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.97 and bottoms xW = 0.05, with relative volatility alpha = 3.4. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.97, xw = 0.05, al = 3.4 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.97/0.03)(0.95/0.05)] / ln(3.4) | Answer: 5.246 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.56 and x = 0.32. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.56, x = 0.32 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.56/0.44) / (0.32/0.68) | Answer: 2.705

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.82 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 100 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.82, Psat = 100 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.82 * 100 | Answer: 82 kPa

question: A stream of 4.8 kg/s with specific heat 2.7 kJ/kg-K is heated through 10 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 4.8, cp = 2.7, dT = 10 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 4.8*2.7*10 | Answer: 129.6 kW

question: A reactor of volume 9.5 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 4.2 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 9.5, Q = 4.2 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 9.5 / 4.2 | Answer: 2.262 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 4.3e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 2 mm with a concentration difference of 70 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 4.3, L = 2, dC = 70 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (4.3e-9)*70 / (2e-3) | Answer: 150.5 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 2.9 min and steady-state gain 1.8. For a step input of magnitude 4, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 2.9, K = 1.8, M = 4 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 1.8 * 4 | Answer: 7.2 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 15 m^2 flies at 160 m/s (air density 1 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.7. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 15, V = 160, rho = 1, CL = 0.7 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1*(160)^2*15*0.7 / 1000 | Answer: 134.4 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 75 m^2 flies at 80 m/s (density 0.7 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.09. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 75, V = 80, rho = 0.7, CD = 0.09 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.7*(80)^2*75*0.09 / 1000 | Answer: 15.12 kN

question: A specimen under stress 390 MPa shows an elastic strain of 1e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 390, eps = 1 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 390 / (1e-3) MPa = 390 GPa | Answer: 390 GPa

question: A block of mass 12 kg has a volume of 2.5e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 12, V = 2.5 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 12 / (2.5e-3) | Answer: 4800 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 2200 mm is heated through 135 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 11e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 2200, dT = 135, al = 11 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 2200*11e-6*135 | Answer: 3.267 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 80 ohm, R2 = 145 ohm and R3 = 20 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 80, R2 = 145, R3 = 20 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 145*20 / 80 | Answer: 36.25 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 350 ohm and gauge factor 2.2 experiences a strain of 1150e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 350, GF = 2.2, eps = 1150 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 350*2.2*1150e-6 | Answer: 885.5 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 9.2 when the true value is 20. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.2, true = 20 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.2 - 20| / 20 * 100 | Answer: 54 %

question: Annual demand is 8000 units, ordering cost 220 per order and holding cost 5 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 8000, S = 220, H = 5 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*8000*220 / 5) | Answer: 839 units

question: An asset costs 380000 with salvage value 2000 after 17 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 380000, Sv = 2000, n = 17 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (380000 - 2000) / 17 | Answer: 22235 per year

question: A product sells for 410 per unit with variable cost 70 per unit and fixed costs 180000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 410, V = 70, F = 180000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 180000 / (410 - 70) | Answer: 529.4 units

question: Find the present worth of 20000 received 8 years from now at an interest rate of 10% per year.
solution: Given: F = 20000, n = 8, i = 10 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 20000 / (1 + 0.1)^8 | Answer: 933 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.92, 0.92 and 0.9 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.92, r2 = 0.92, r3 = 0.9 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.92*0.92*0.9 | Answer: 0.7618

question: A process produces 47 defective items in a batch of 7000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 47, N = 7000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 47/7000 * 1e6 | Answer: 6714 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -5x^3 - 8x^2 + 4x + 4 evaluated at x = -3.
For f(x) = 2x^3 + 6x^2 - 3x - 3, find f''(x) at x = 5.
Evaluate the definite integral of (-4x^2 - 3x - 7) dx from x = 2 to x = 3.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = -4x^3/3 + -3x^2/2 + -7x | Evaluate F(3) - F(2) | Answer: -39.83
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 2x^2 - 7x - 7 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[-8, 9], [-9, -4]].
solution: Given: a = -8, b = 9, c = -9, d = -4 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (-8)(-4) - (9)(-9) | Answer: 113

question: Find the determinant of [[0, -4, -5], [1, -6, -4], [4, 5, 3]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: -69

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[0, -4], [-8, -8]].
solution: Trace tr = -8, Determinant = -32 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 2.928

question: Solve for x: -3x + -3y = 6 and 1x + -2y = 8.
solution: Determinant = -3*-2 - -3*1 = 9 | x = (e d - b f) / det = 1.333 | Answer: x = 1.333
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 94, 13, 38, 17, 98.
solution: Sum = 260 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 52 | Answer: 52

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 21, 25, 25, 36, 3.
solution: Mean = 22 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 12

question: Find the slope of the line through (7, 5) and (-7, 0).
solution: Given: x1 = 7, y1 = 5, x2 = -7, y2 = 0 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (0 - 5) / (-7 - 7) | Answer: 0.3571

question: Find the distance between the points (6, 5) and (2, 0).
solution: Given: x1 = 6, y1 = 5, x2 = 2, y2 = 0 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-4)^2 + (-5)^2) | Answer: 6.403 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (-1,2), (1,1), (8,-3).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 0.5 sq units

question: Find the 32th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 18 and common difference -2.
solution: Given: a = 18, d = -2, n = 32 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = 18 + (32 - 1)*-2 | Answer: -44

question: Find the sum of the first 19 terms of an AP with first term -4 and common difference -4.
solution: Given: a = -4, d = -4, n = 19 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 19/2 [2*-4 + (19-1)*-4] | Answer: -760

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 35000 at 14.3% per annum for 7 years.
solution: Given: P = 35000, R = 14.3, Tt = 7 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 35000 * 14.3 * 7 / 100 | Answer: 35035 currency units

question: Find the amount when 5000 is invested at 11.6% per annum compounded annually for 2 years.
solution: Given: P = 5000, R = 11.6, Tt = 2 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 5000 * (1 + 11.6/100)^2 | Answer: 6227 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (3, 8, -5) and (1, -2, 2).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (2, 4, -5) and (5, 4, 4).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 50.29

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (-2, 6, 6) and (6, -4, -2).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 137.4 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number -10 + -12i.
solution: Given: a = -10, b = -12 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((-10)^2 + (-12)^2) | Answer: 15.62

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number 12 + 12i.
solution: Given: a = 12, b = 12 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(12, 12) | Answer: 45 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = 5x^3 + 4x^2 - x + 7 at x = 5.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-54 with initial guess x0=15, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.4 and ordinates 9, 4, 18, 12, 1, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 484 and 446.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 484 and 446 | Answer: GCD = 2

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 46 and 74.
solution: Given: a = 46, b = 74 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 46*74 / 2 | Answer: 1702
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 57 mm carries an axial tensile load of 57 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 13 mm and length 2500 mm carries an axial load of 15 kN. Take E = 110 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 67 mm transmits a torque of 2750 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 67, Tt = 2750 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(2750*1000) / (pi*(67)^3) | Answer: 46.57 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 53 mm and length 1000 mm carries a torque of 250 N-m. With G = 77 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (53)^4 / 32 = 774646 mm^4 | theta = (250*1000)(1000) / (77000 * 774646) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 0.2401 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 129 mm wide and 180 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 129, h = 180 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 129*(180)^2 / 6 | Answer: 696600 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (99 mm x 180 mm) carries a bending moment of 20 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (63 mm x 110 mm) has effective length 1800 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 710 MPa is designed for a working stress of 80 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 710, sw = 80 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 710 / 80 | Answer: 8.875

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1300 mm and wall thickness 8 mm carries an internal pressure of 2.5 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1300, t = 8, P = 2.5 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 2.5*1300 / (2*8) | Answer: 203.1 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 880 K and 420 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 880, Tc = 420 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 420/880) * 100 | Answer: 52.27 %

question: A refrigerator works between 268 K (cold) and 330 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 268, Th = 330 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 268 / (330 - 268) | Answer: 4.323

question: A heat pump operates between 285 K and 308 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 285, Th = 308 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 308 / (308 - 285) | Answer: 13.39

question: 4.8 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 140 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.8, dT = 140 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 4.8 * 0.718 * 140 | Answer: 482.5 kJ

question: 8 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 80 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 8, dT = 80 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 8 * 1.005 * 80 | Answer: 643.2 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 1.2 m^3 at 420 K with mass 1.8 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 1.2, Tk = 420, m = 1.8 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 1.8*0.287*420 / 1.2 | Answer: 180.8 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 3.9 kg of air expands isothermally at 500 K from volume V1 to 3*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.9, Tk = 500, ratio = 3 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 3.9*0.287*500*ln(3) | Answer: 614.8 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 2.3 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.19 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 2.3, D = 0.19 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*2.3*0.19 / 0.001 | Answer: 437000

question: Water flows at 2.2 m/s through a pipe of diameter 210 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 3.8 m. Taking Cv = 0.96, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 3.8, cv = 0.96 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.96*sqrt(2*9.81*3.8) | Answer: 8.289 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 230 mm) water flows at 2.5 m/s. It contracts to diameter 100 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
Water flows at 3.6 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.3 m and length 170 m. With friction factor f = 0.028, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 21 teeth drives a gear of 50 teeth. If the pinion runs at 700 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 21, z2 = 50, N1 = 700 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 700*21 / 50 | Answer: 294 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 230 mm rotates at 1350 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 230, N = 1350 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.23)*1350 / 60 | Answer: 16.26 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 2.7 kW at 1300 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 2.7, N = 1300 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(2.7*1000) / (2*pi*1300) | Answer: 19.83 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 4.1 kg rotates at radius 0.3 m at 650 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 15800 N/m and mass 14.8 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 15800, m = 14.8 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(15800/14.8) | Answer: 5.2 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 4.9 m^2 and thickness 0.2 m has conductivity k = 17.7 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 125 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 4.9, L = 0.2, k = 17.7, dT = 125 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 17.7*4.9*125 / 0.2 | Answer: 54206 W

question: A surface of area 3.9 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 85 W/m^2-K to surroundings 85 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 3.9, h = 85, dT = 85 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 85*3.9*85 | Answer: 28178 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 110 m/min, feed = 0.45 mm/rev, depth of cut = 0.6 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 110, f = 0.45, d = 0.6 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*110*0.45*0.6 | Answer: 29700 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 440 mm is turned at 1000 rpm with a feed of 0.11 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 440, N = 1000, f = 0.11 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 440 / (0.11*1000) | Answer: 4 min

question: A resistor of 122 ohm carries a current of 3.2 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 122, I = 3.2 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 3.2 * 122 | Answer: 390.4 V

question: Three resistors 7 ohm, 45 ohm and 44 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 7, R2 = 45, R3 = 44 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 7 + 45 + 44 | Answer: 96 ohm

question: Two resistors 18 ohm and 3 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 18, R2 = 3 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 18*3 / (18+3) | Answer: 2.571 ohm

question: A device draws 5.1 A at 55 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 55, I = 5.1 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 55 * 5.1 | Answer: 280.5 W

question: A current of 8.5 A flows through a 25 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 8.5, R = 25 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (8.5)^2 * 25 | Answer: 1806 W

question: Two capacitors 34 uF and 26.9 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 34, C2 = 26.9 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 34*26.9 / (34+26.9) | Answer: 15.02 uF

question: A resistor 91 kohm and capacitor 1.3 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 91, C = 1.3 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (91k)(1.3u) = 118.3 ms | Answer: 118.3 ms

question: An inductor 157.8 mH is in series with 26 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 157.8, R = 26 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (157.8e-3) / 26 | Answer: 6.069 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 55.6 mH inductor at 350 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 55.6, f = 350 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (350)(55.6e-3) | Answer: 122.3 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 29.8 uF capacitor at 290 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 29.8, f = 290 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (290)(29.8e-6)) | Answer: 18.42 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 96 ohm, XL = 148 ohm and XC = 49 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 96, XL = 148, XC = 49 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(96^2 + (148 - 49)^2) | Answer: 137.9 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 79.7 mH and C = 3.5 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 79.7, C = 3.5 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(79.7e-3 * 3.5e-6)) | Answer: 301.3 Hz

question: A capacitor of 53.4 uF is charged to 160 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 53.4, V = 160 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*53.4e-6*(160)^2 | Answer: 683.5 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 420 V with 270 primary turns and 60 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 420, N1 = 270, N2 = 60 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 420 * 60/270 | Answer: 93.33 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 420 V and draws an armature current of 42 A. If the armature resistance is 0.34 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 420, Ia = 42, Ra = 0.34 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 420 - 42*0.34 | Answer: 405.7 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 110 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.77. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 110, VL = 400, pf = 0.77 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*400*110*0.77 / 1000 | Answer: 58.68 kW

question: A load has real power 80 kW and apparent power 215 kVA. Find the power factor.

question: A machine delivers 70 kW output while drawing 157 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 24 V across R1 = 5 ohm and R2 = 27 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 130 kohm and Rin = 14 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 190 kohm and Rg = 7 kohm. Find the voltage gain.

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 812. Express the gain in decibels (power).

question: A simply supported beam of span 5.7 m carries a central point load of 95 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.

question: A simply supported beam of span 10 m carries a UDL of 30 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 10, w = 30 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 30*(10)^2 / 8 | Answer: 375 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 1.1 m carries a point load 25 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.

question: A cantilever of length 1.7 m carries a UDL of 36 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.

question: A simply supported beam of span 10 m carries a point load 90 kN at distance 1.7 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.

question: A simply supported beam (span 4.6 m) carries a central point load 60 kN. With E = 200 GPa and I = 410e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.

question: A fixed beam of span 4.2 m carries a UDL of 15 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.2, w = 15 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 15*(4.2)^2 / 12 | Answer: 22.05 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 480 mm, clear cover 40 mm and main bars of diameter 25 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 480, c = 40, dia = 25 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 480 - 40 - 25/2 | Answer: 427.5 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 30.5 m^2 carrying a factored load of 11.6 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 30.5, w = 11.6 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 11.6 * 30.5 | Answer: 353.8 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 5.6 m, unit weight 18 kN/m^3, phi = 29 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).

question: At a depth of 3 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 21 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 3, g = 21 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (21 - 9.81)*3 | Answer: 33.57 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 7.7e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.7, area = 2.4e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 7.7, i = 0.7, A = 2.4 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (7.7e-4)*0.7*(2.4e-3) | Answer: 1294 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 0.6 m, bed slope 0.005 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.024. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 1.2 m under a head of 0.8 m. Taking Cd = 0.61 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.

question: A tank of volume 850 m^3 treats a flow of 90 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 850, Q = 90 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 850 / 90 | Answer: 9.444 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 200 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.25 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 4 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 200, k = 0.25, t = 4 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 200*(1 - e^(-0.25*4)) | Answer: 126.4 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.6, rainfall intensity 110 mm/h over a catchment of 48.5 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.6, i = 110, A = 48.5 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.6*110*48.5 / 360 | Answer: 8.892 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.01 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 580 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.01, M = 580 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 580*(30+0.01)/30 | Answer: 580.2 m

question: A file of 330 megabits is sent over a link of 9 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.

question: A link has bandwidth 50 Mbps and round-trip time 40 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 50, R = 40 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 50e6 * 40e-3 bits = 2000 kb | Answer: 2000 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.89, cache access time 6 ns and main-memory access time 160 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.89, tc = 6, tm = 160 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.89*6 + (1 - 0.89)*160 | Answer: 22.94 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 477281 elements?
solution: Given: n = 477281 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(477281)) + 1 | Answer: 19

question: An O(n^2) algorithm performs c*n^2 basic operations. If c = 1 and n = 1370, how many operations are performed?

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.012, memory access time 80 ns and page-fault service time 9 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 9 ms = 9000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.012)*80 + 0.012*9000000.0 ns | Answer: 108.1 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 2.6 m^3 at 480 kPa and 510 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 2.6, P = 480, Tk = 510 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (480e3)*2.6 / (8.314*510) | Answer: 294.3 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.21 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 16 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.21, t = 16 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.21*16) | Answer: 0.9653

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.48 /min) is to reach 75% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.48, X = 75 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.75) / 0.48 | Answer: 2.888 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.36 /min) reaches 80% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.36, X = 80 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.8 / (0.36*(1 - 0.8)) | Answer: 11.11 min

question: For a reaction with A = 3e10 /s and activation energy 60 kJ/mol at 470 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 3, Ea = 60, Tk = 470 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 3e10 * exp(-60e3 / (8.314*470)) | Answer: 6436 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.9 and bottoms xW = 0.04, with relative volatility alpha = 2.6. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.9, xw = 0.04, al = 2.6 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.9/0.1)(0.96/0.04)] / ln(2.6) | Answer: 5.626 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.6 and x = 0.33. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.6, x = 0.33 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.6/0.4) / (0.33/0.67) | Answer: 3.045

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.68 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 95 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.68, Psat = 95 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.68 * 95 | Answer: 64.6 kPa

question: A stream of 6.3 kg/s with specific heat 2.9 kJ/kg-K is heated through 25 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 6.3, cp = 2.9, dT = 25 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 6.3*2.9*25 | Answer: 456.8 kW

question: A reactor of volume 8 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 0.8 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 3.3e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 5 mm with a concentration difference of 120 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 3.3, L = 5, dC = 120 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (3.3e-9)*120 / (5e-3) | Answer: 79.2 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 7 min and steady-state gain 3.9. For a step input of magnitude 2, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 7, K = 3.9, M = 2 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 3.9 * 2 | Answer: 7.8 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 45 m^2 flies at 200 m/s (air density 0.4 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.7. Find the lift force in kN.

question: An aircraft of wing area 45 m^2 flies at 80 m/s (density 0.7 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.04. Find the drag force in kN.

question: A specimen under stress 100 MPa shows an elastic strain of 1.2e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.

question: A block of mass 16 kg has a volume of 4e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.

question: A rod of length 2400 mm is heated through 45 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 12e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 180 ohm, R2 = 35 ohm and R3 = 435 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 180, R2 = 35, R3 = 435 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 35*435 / 180 | Answer: 84.58 ohm

question: A measurement reads 10.38 when the true value is 50. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10.38, true = 50 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10.38 - 50| / 50 * 100 | Answer: 79.24 %

question: Annual demand is 9000 units, ordering cost 180 per order and holding cost 32 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).

question: An asset costs 390000 with salvage value 26000 after 15 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.

question: A product sells for 210 per unit with variable cost 80 per unit and fixed costs 20000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 210, V = 80, F = 20000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 20000 / (210 - 80) | Answer: 153.8 units

question: Find the present worth of 85000 received 10 years from now at an interest rate of 10% per year.
solution: Given: F = 85000, n = 10, i = 10 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 85000 / (1 + 0.1)^10 | Answer: 32771 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.95, 0.93 and 0.94 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.95, r2 = 0.93, r3 = 0.94 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.95*0.93*0.94 | Answer: 0.8305

question: A process produces 10 defective items in a batch of 16000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 10, N = 16000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 10/16000 * 1e6 | Answer: 625 PPM

question: Find the 32th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 8 and common difference -1.

question: Find the sum of the first 31 terms of an AP with first term -6 and common difference 0.
solution: Given: a = -6, d = 0, n = 31 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 31/2 [2*-6 + (31-1)*0] | Answer: -186

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 19500 at 8% per annum for 9 years.
solution: Given: P = 19500, R = 8, Tt = 9 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 19500 * 8 * 9 / 100 | Answer: 14040 currency units

question: Find the amount when 12500 is invested at 8.4% per annum compounded annually for 6 years.

question: Find the modulus of the complex number 12 + -4i.
solution: Given: a = 12, b = -4 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((12)^2 + (-4)^2) | Answer: 12.65

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number -1 + -6i.

question: A circular rod of diameter 48 mm carries an axial tensile load of 32 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.

question: A shaft of diameter 45 mm and length 800 mm carries a torque of 1250 N-m. With G = 77 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.

question: A rectangular beam section is 38 mm wide and 100 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.

question: A component of ultimate strength 680 MPa is designed for a working stress of 240 MPa. Find the factor of safety.

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 800 mm and wall thickness 12 mm carries an internal pressure of 0.9 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.

question: A Carnot engine operates between 1040 K and 350 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 1040, Tc = 350 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 350/1040) * 100 | Answer: 66.35 %

question: A refrigerator works between 251 K (cold) and 300 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 251, Th = 300 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 251 / (300 - 251) | Answer: 5.122

question: A heat pump operates between 275 K and 320 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
