question: 3.9 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 55 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.9, dT = 55 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 3.9 * 0.718 * 55 | Answer: 154 kJ

question: 6.3 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 150 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 6.3, dT = 150 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 6.3 * 1.005 * 150 | Answer: 949.7 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 3 m^3 at 430 K with mass 3.5 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 3, Tk = 430, m = 3.5 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 3.5*0.287*430 / 3 | Answer: 144 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 3.2 kg of air expands isothermally at 440 K from volume V1 to 5*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.2, Tk = 440, ratio = 5 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 3.2*0.287*440*ln(5) | Answer: 650.4 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 2.8 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.13 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 2.8, D = 0.13 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*2.8*0.13 / 0.001 | Answer: 364000

question: Water flows at 3 m/s through a pipe of diameter 150 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 18.4 m. Taking Cv = 0.97, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 18.4, cv = 0.97 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.97*sqrt(2*9.81*18.4) | Answer: 18.43 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 300 mm) water flows at 1.1 m/s. It contracts to diameter 110 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
Water flows at 3.6 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.25 m and length 500 m. With friction factor f = 0.027, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 26 teeth drives a gear of 67 teeth. If the pinion runs at 350 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 26, z2 = 67, N1 = 350 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 350*26 / 67 | Answer: 135.8 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 210 mm rotates at 1050 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 210, N = 1050 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.21)*1050 / 60 | Answer: 11.55 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 31.7 kW at 1250 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 31.7, N = 1250 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(31.7*1000) / (2*pi*1250) | Answer: 242.2 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 2.8 kg rotates at radius 0.31 m at 450 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 2100 N/m and mass 13.3 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 2100, m = 13.3 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(2100/13.3) | Answer: 2 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 1.1 m^2 and thickness 0.18 m has conductivity k = 34.7 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 75 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 1.1, L = 0.18, k = 34.7, dT = 75 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 34.7*1.1*75 / 0.18 | Answer: 15904 W

question: A surface of area 0.9 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 105 W/m^2-K to surroundings 95 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 0.9, h = 105, dT = 95 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 105*0.9*95 | Answer: 8978 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 90 m/min, feed = 0.18 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2.5 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 90, f = 0.18, d = 2.5 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*90*0.18*2.5 | Answer: 40500 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 410 mm is turned at 800 rpm with a feed of 0.4 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 410, N = 800, f = 0.4 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 410 / (0.4*800) | Answer: 1.281 min

question: A resistor of 132 ohm carries a current of 7.6 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 132, I = 7.6 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 7.6 * 132 | Answer: 1003 V

question: Three resistors 95 ohm, 92 ohm and 79 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 95, R2 = 92, R3 = 79 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 95 + 92 + 79 | Answer: 266 ohm

question: Two resistors 46 ohm and 48 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 46, R2 = 48 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 46*48 / (46+48) | Answer: 23.49 ohm

question: A device draws 9.1 A at 40 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 40, I = 9.1 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 40 * 9.1 | Answer: 364 W

question: A current of 6 A flows through a 7 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 6, R = 7 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (6)^2 * 7 | Answer: 252 W

question: Two capacitors 32.1 uF and 38.8 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 32.1, C2 = 38.8 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 32.1*38.8 / (32.1+38.8) | Answer: 17.57 uF

question: A resistor 32 kohm and capacitor 9.8 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 32, C = 9.8 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (32k)(9.8u) = 313.6 ms | Answer: 313.6 ms

question: An inductor 128.9 mH is in series with 76 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 128.9, R = 76 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (128.9e-3) / 76 | Answer: 1.696 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 198.7 mH inductor at 720 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 198.7, f = 720 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (720)(198.7e-3) | Answer: 898.9 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 13.3 uF capacitor at 190 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 13.3, f = 190 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (190)(13.3e-6)) | Answer: 62.98 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 10 ohm, XL = 52 ohm and XC = 22 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 10, XL = 52, XC = 22 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(10^2 + (52 - 22)^2) | Answer: 31.62 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 59.2 mH and C = 4 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 59.2, C = 4 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(59.2e-3 * 4e-6)) | Answer: 327.1 Hz

question: A capacitor of 37.3 uF is charged to 290 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 37.3, V = 290 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*37.3e-6*(290)^2 | Answer: 1568 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 410 V with 750 primary turns and 300 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 410, N1 = 750, N2 = 300 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 410 * 300/750 | Answer: 164 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 400 V and draws an armature current of 23 A. If the armature resistance is 0.86 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 400, Ia = 23, Ra = 0.86 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 400 - 23*0.86 | Answer: 380.2 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 90 A at 433 V (line) with a power factor of 0.7. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 90, VL = 433, pf = 0.7 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*433*90*0.7 / 1000 | Answer: 47.25 kW

question: A load has real power 150 kW and apparent power 190 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 150, S = 190 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 150 / 190 | Answer: 0.7895

question: A machine delivers 15 kW output while drawing 182 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 15, Pi = 182 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 15/182 * 100 | Answer: 8.242 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 28 V across R1 = 25 ohm and R2 = 25 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 28, R1 = 25, R2 = 25 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 28*25 / (25+25) | Answer: 14 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 210 kohm and Rin = 35 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 210, Rin = 35 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 210 / 35 | Answer: 6

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 50 kohm and Rg = 22 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 50, Rg = 22 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 50/22 | Answer: 3.273

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 9040. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 9040 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(9040) | Answer: 39.56 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.4 m carries a central point load of 30 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.4, W = 30 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 30*4.4 / 4 | Answer: 33 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.8 m carries a UDL of 35 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.8, w = 35 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 35*(4.8)^2 / 8 | Answer: 100.8 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 5.1 m carries a point load 70 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.1, W = 70 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 70*5.1 | Answer: 357 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 3 m carries a UDL of 8 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3, w = 8 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 8*(3)^2 / 2 | Answer: 36 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 7.3 m carries a point load 35 kN at distance 3.6 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 7.3, a = 3.6, W = 35 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 35*(7.3 - 3.6) / 7.3 | Answer: 17.74 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 5.5 m) carries a central point load 60 kN. With E = 25 GPa and I = 380e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=60000 N, L=5500.0 mm, E=25000 MPa, I=380e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 21.89 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 8.2 m carries a UDL of 21 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 8.2, w = 21 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 21*(8.2)^2 / 12 | Answer: 117.7 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 440 mm, clear cover 35 mm and main bars of diameter 25 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 440, c = 35, dia = 25 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 440 - 35 - 25/2 | Answer: 392.5 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 22.4 m^2 carrying a factored load of 10.1 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 22.4, w = 10.1 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 10.1 * 22.4 | Answer: 226.2 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 4.1 m, unit weight 17 kN/m^3, phi = 33 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 2e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1.5, area = 4.3e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 2, i = 1.5, A = 4.3 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (2e-4)*1.5*(4.3e-3) | Answer: 1290 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.9 m, bed slope 0.004 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.014. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 2 m under a head of 0.3 m. Taking Cd = 0.63 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 2.8 m wide carries a discharge of 22.6 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 420 m and design speed 70 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 420, V = 70 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (70)^2 / (127*420) | Answer: 0.09186
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: For a design speed of 60 km/h with allowable superelevation 0.05 and lateral friction 0.15, find the minimum curve radius in m.
A tank of volume 770 m^3 treats a flow of 115 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 770, Q = 115 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 770 / 115 | Answer: 6.696 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 300 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.29 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 5 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 300, k = 0.29, t = 5 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 300*(1 - e^(-0.29*5)) | Answer: 229.6 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.77, rainfall intensity 60 mm/h over a catchment of 44.5 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.77, i = 60, A = 44.5 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.77*60*44.5 / 360 | Answer: 5.711 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.08 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 720 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.08, M = 720 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 720*(30+0.08)/30 | Answer: 721.9 m

question: Convert the decimal number 3928 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 3928 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: F58 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 00101100 and 10000101.
solution: XOR: 10101001 | Count of 1s = 4 | Answer: 4
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 460 megabits is sent over a link of 64 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 460, B = 64 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 460 / 64 | Answer: 7.188 s

question: A link has bandwidth 91 Mbps and round-trip time 120 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 91, R = 120 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 91e6 * 120e-3 bits = 10920 kb | Answer: 10920 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.97, cache access time 9 ns and main-memory access time 180 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.97, tc = 9, tm = 180 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.97*9 + (1 - 0.97)*180 | Answer: 14.13 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 853348 elements?
solution: Given: n = 853348 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(853348)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.002, memory access time 120 ns and page-fault service time 4 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 4 ms = 4000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.002)*120 + 0.002*4000000.0 ns | Answer: 8.12 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 0.3 m^3 at 250 kPa and 430 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 0.3, P = 250, Tk = 430 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (250e3)*0.3 / (8.314*430) | Answer: 20.98 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.39 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 8 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.39, t = 8 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.39*8) | Answer: 0.9558

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.38 /min) is to reach 70% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.38, X = 70 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.7) / 0.38 | Answer: 3.168 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.36 /min) reaches 85% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.36, X = 85 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.85 / (0.36*(1 - 0.85)) | Answer: 15.74 min

question: For a reaction with A = 3e10 /s and activation energy 70 kJ/mol at 310 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 3, Ea = 70, Tk = 310 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 3e10 * exp(-70e3 / (8.314*310)) | Answer: 0.04806 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.94 and bottoms xW = 0.06, with relative volatility alpha = 2.7. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.94, xw = 0.06, al = 2.7 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.94/0.06)(0.94/0.06)] / ln(2.7) | Answer: 5.54 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.72 and x = 0.44. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.72, x = 0.44 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.72/0.28) / (0.44/0.56) | Answer: 3.273

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.12 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 90 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.12, Psat = 90 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.12 * 90 | Answer: 10.8 kPa

question: A stream of 1.6 kg/s with specific heat 1.9 kJ/kg-K is heated through 10 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 1.6, cp = 1.9, dT = 10 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 1.6*1.9*10 | Answer: 30.4 kW

question: A reactor of volume 13.7 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 1.2 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 13.7, Q = 1.2 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 13.7 / 1.2 | Answer: 11.42 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 3e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 1 mm with a concentration difference of 100 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 3, L = 1, dC = 100 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (3e-9)*100 / (1e-3) | Answer: 300 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 9.7 min and steady-state gain 1.2. For a step input of magnitude 20, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 9.7, K = 1.2, M = 20 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 1.2 * 20 | Answer: 24 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 100 m^2 flies at 70 m/s (air density 0.4 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.3. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 100, V = 70, rho = 0.4, CL = 0.3 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.4*(70)^2*100*0.3 / 1000 | Answer: 29.4 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 30 m^2 flies at 60 m/s (density 0.7 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.05. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 30, V = 60, rho = 0.7, CD = 0.05 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.7*(60)^2*30*0.05 / 1000 | Answer: 1.89 kN

question: A specimen under stress 280 MPa shows an elastic strain of 1.2e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 280, eps = 1.2 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 280 / (1.2e-3) MPa = 233.3 GPa | Answer: 233.3 GPa

question: A block of mass 4 kg has a volume of 2.3e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 4, V = 2.3 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 4 / (2.3e-3) | Answer: 1739 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 1600 mm is heated through 50 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 23e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 1600, dT = 50, al = 23 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 1600*23e-6*50 | Answer: 1.84 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 140 ohm, R2 = 95 ohm and R3 = 420 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 140, R2 = 95, R3 = 420 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 95*420 / 140 | Answer: 285 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 350 ohm and gauge factor 2.2 experiences a strain of 200e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 350, GF = 2.2, eps = 200 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 350*2.2*200e-6 | Answer: 154 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 10.38 when the true value is 10. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10.38, true = 10 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10.38 - 10| / 10 * 100 | Answer: 3.8 %

question: Annual demand is 21500 units, ordering cost 120 per order and holding cost 28 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 21500, S = 120, H = 28 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*21500*120 / 28) | Answer: 429.3 units

question: An asset costs 320000 with salvage value 20000 after 16 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 320000, Sv = 20000, n = 16 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (320000 - 20000) / 16 | Answer: 18750 per year

question: A product sells for 50 per unit with variable cost 30 per unit and fixed costs 105000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 50, V = 30, F = 105000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 105000 / (50 - 30) | Answer: 5250 units

question: Find the present worth of 120000 received 9 years from now at an interest rate of 8% per year.
solution: Given: F = 120000, n = 9, i = 8 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 120000 / (1 + 0.08)^9 | Answer: 6003 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.98, 0.9 and 0.93 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.98, r2 = 0.9, r3 = 0.93 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.98*0.9*0.93 | Answer: 0.8203

question: A process produces 22 defective items in a batch of 11500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 22, N = 11500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 22/11500 * 1e6 | Answer: 1913 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = 4x^3 - 6x^2 - 6x - 7 evaluated at x = -5.
For f(x) = 4x^3 + 4x^2 + 9x - 2, find f''(x) at x = 1.
Evaluate the definite integral of (-5x^2 + 3x + 7) dx from x = -3 to x = 5.

solution: Given: x1 = -5, y1 = -7, x2 = 0, y2 = 4 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((5)^2 + (11)^2) | Answer: 12.08 units

question: Find the 40th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 0 and common difference -5.
solution: Given: a = 0, d = -5, n = 40 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = 0 + (40 - 1)*-5 | Answer: -195

question: Find the sum of the first 13 terms of an AP with first term -6 and common difference -8.
solution: Given: a = -6, d = -8, n = 13 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 13/2 [2*-6 + (13-1)*-8] | Answer: -702

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 32500 at 7.4% per annum for 7 years.
solution: Given: P = 32500, R = 7.4, Tt = 7 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 32500 * 7.4 * 7 / 100 | Answer: 16835 currency units

question: Find the amount when 32000 is invested at 5.8% per annum compounded annually for 5 years.
solution: Given: P = 32000, R = 5.8, Tt = 5 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 32000 * (1 + 5.8/100)^5 | Answer: 42421 currency units

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (-6, -6, -6) and (4, 3, 3).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 172 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number 0 + -10i.
solution: Given: a = 0, b = -10 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((0)^2 + (-10)^2) | Answer: 10

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number -11 + 4i.
solution: Given: a = -11, b = 4 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(4, -11) | Answer: 160 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -3x^3 + 4x^2 + 6x + 9 at x = 4.
