question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 13 and 36.
solution: Given: a = 13, b = 36 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 13*36 / 1 | Answer: 468
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 43 mm carries an axial tensile load of 90 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 35 mm and length 1900 mm carries an axial load of 35 kN. Take E = 70 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 68 mm transmits a torque of 2400 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 68, Tt = 2400 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(2400*1000) / (pi*(68)^3) | Answer: 38.87 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 68 mm and length 1700 mm carries a torque of 350 N-m. With G = 77 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (68)^4 / 32 = 2099112 mm^4 | theta = (350*1000)(1700) / (77000 * 2099112) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 0.2109 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 86 mm wide and 200 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 86, h = 200 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 86*(200)^2 / 6 | Answer: 573333 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (59 mm x 130 mm) carries a bending moment of 21 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (56 mm x 160 mm) has effective length 3800 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 830 MPa is designed for a working stress of 180 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 830, sw = 180 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 830 / 180 | Answer: 4.611

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 700 mm and wall thickness 19 mm carries an internal pressure of 0.5 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 700, t = 19, P = 0.5 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 0.5*700 / (2*19) | Answer: 9.211 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 700 K and 380 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 700, Tc = 380 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 380/700) * 100 | Answer: 45.71 %

question: A refrigerator works between 270 K (cold) and 330 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 270, Th = 330 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 270 / (330 - 270) | Answer: 4.5

question: A heat pump operates between 278 K and 322 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 278, Th = 322 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 322 / (322 - 278) | Answer: 7.318

question: 6.6 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 200 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 6.6, dT = 200 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 6.6 * 0.718 * 200 | Answer: 947.8 kJ

question: 3.9 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 135 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.9, dT = 135 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 3.9 * 1.005 * 135 | Answer: 529.1 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 1 m^3 at 590 K with mass 4.3 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 1, Tk = 590, m = 4.3 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 4.3*0.287*590 / 1 | Answer: 728.1 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 4.1 kg of air expands isothermally at 320 K from volume V1 to 3*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.1, Tk = 320, ratio = 3 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 4.1*0.287*320*ln(3) | Answer: 413.7 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 1.4 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.32 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 1.4, D = 0.32 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*1.4*0.32 / 0.001 | Answer: 448000

question: Water flows at 0.8 m/s through a pipe of diameter 220 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 20.9 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 20.9 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*20.9 / 1000 | Answer: 205 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 19.7 m. Taking Cv = 0.96, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 19.7, cv = 0.96 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.96*sqrt(2*9.81*19.7) | Answer: 18.87 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 300 mm) water flows at 1 m/s. It contracts to diameter 80 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 300, d2 = 80, V1 = 1 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 1*(300/80)^2 | Answer: 14.06 m/s

question: Water flows at 2.1 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.41 m and length 400 m. With friction factor f = 0.039, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 33 teeth drives a gear of 95 teeth. If the pinion runs at 950 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 33, z2 = 95, N1 = 950 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 950*33 / 95 | Answer: 330 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 490 mm rotates at 1250 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 490, N = 1250 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.49)*1250 / 60 | Answer: 32.07 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 37.3 kW at 600 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 37.3, N = 600 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(37.3*1000) / (2*pi*600) | Answer: 593.6 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 9.9 kg rotates at radius 0.47 m at 1000 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 18900 N/m and mass 16.6 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 18900, m = 16.6 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(18900/16.6) | Answer: 5.37 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 4.5 m^2 and thickness 0.27 m has conductivity k = 34.8 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 90 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 4.5, L = 0.27, k = 34.8, dT = 90 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 34.8*4.5*90 / 0.27 | Answer: 52200 W

question: A surface of area 3.6 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 125 W/m^2-K to surroundings 145 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 3.6, h = 125, dT = 145 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 125*3.6*145 | Answer: 65250 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 160 m/min, feed = 0.36 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2.9 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 160, f = 0.36, d = 2.9 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*160*0.36*2.9 | Answer: 167040 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 120 mm is turned at 1050 rpm with a feed of 0.26 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 120, N = 1050, f = 0.26 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 120 / (0.26*1050) | Answer: 0.4396 min

question: A resistor of 30 ohm carries a current of 9.2 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 30, I = 9.2 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 9.2 * 30 | Answer: 276 V

question: Three resistors 16 ohm, 18 ohm and 38 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 16, R2 = 18, R3 = 38 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 16 + 18 + 38 | Answer: 72 ohm

question: Two resistors 50 ohm and 112 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 50, R2 = 112 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 50*112 / (50+112) | Answer: 34.57 ohm

question: A device draws 14.5 A at 205 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 205, I = 14.5 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 205 * 14.5 | Answer: 2972 W

question: A current of 7.8 A flows through a 81 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 7.8, R = 81 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (7.8)^2 * 81 | Answer: 4928 W

question: Two capacitors 27.8 uF and 5.6 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 27.8, C2 = 5.6 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 27.8*5.6 / (27.8+5.6) | Answer: 4.661 uF

question: A resistor 20 kohm and capacitor 5.9 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 20, C = 5.9 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (20k)(5.9u) = 118 ms | Answer: 118 ms

question: An inductor 175.9 mH is in series with 48 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 175.9, R = 48 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (175.9e-3) / 48 | Answer: 3.665 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 15 mH inductor at 770 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 15, f = 770 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (770)(15e-3) | Answer: 72.57 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 18.2 uF capacitor at 120 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 18.2, f = 120 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (120)(18.2e-6)) | Answer: 72.87 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 98 ohm, XL = 26 ohm and XC = 61 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 98, XL = 26, XC = 61 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(98^2 + (26 - 61)^2) | Answer: 104.1 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 89.6 mH and C = 4.7 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 89.6, C = 4.7 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(89.6e-3 * 4.7e-6)) | Answer: 245.3 Hz

question: A capacitor of 21.9 uF is charged to 165 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 21.9, V = 165 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*21.9e-6*(165)^2 | Answer: 298.1 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 230 V with 560 primary turns and 110 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 230, N1 = 560, N2 = 110 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 230 * 110/560 | Answer: 45.18 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 110 V and draws an armature current of 40 A. If the armature resistance is 0.16 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 110, Ia = 40, Ra = 0.16 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 110 - 40*0.16 | Answer: 103.6 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 50 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.79. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 50, VL = 400, pf = 0.79 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*400*50*0.79 / 1000 | Answer: 27.37 kW

question: A load has real power 95 kW and apparent power 195 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 95, S = 195 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 95 / 195 | Answer: 0.4872

question: A machine delivers 185 kW output while drawing 197 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 185, Pi = 197 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 185/197 * 100 | Answer: 93.91 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 20 V across R1 = 3 ohm and R2 = 41 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 20, R1 = 3, R2 = 41 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 20*41 / (3+41) | Answer: 18.64 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 70 kohm and Rin = 28 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 70, Rin = 28 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 70 / 28 | Answer: 2.5

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 80 kohm and Rg = 13 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 80, Rg = 13 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 80/13 | Answer: 7.154

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 5556. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 5556 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(5556) | Answer: 37.45 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.3 m carries a central point load of 10 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.3, W = 10 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 10*4.3 / 4 | Answer: 10.75 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 6 m carries a UDL of 10 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6, w = 10 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 10*(6)^2 / 8 | Answer: 45 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 1 m carries a point load 5 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 1, W = 5 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 5*1 | Answer: 5 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 1.7 m carries a UDL of 24 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 1.7, w = 24 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 24*(1.7)^2 / 2 | Answer: 34.68 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 8.3 m carries a point load 85 kN at distance 3.9 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 8.3, a = 3.9, W = 85 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 85*(8.3 - 3.9) / 8.3 | Answer: 45.06 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 3.4 m) carries a central point load 45 kN. With E = 30 GPa and I = 120e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=45000 N, L=3400.0 mm, E=30000 MPa, I=120e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 10.24 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 5 m carries a UDL of 12 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5, w = 12 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 12*(5)^2 / 12 | Answer: 25 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 690 mm, clear cover 50 mm and main bars of diameter 20 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 690, c = 50, dia = 20 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 690 - 50 - 20/2 | Answer: 630 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 30.8 m^2 carrying a factored load of 11.2 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 30.8, w = 11.2 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 11.2 * 30.8 | Answer: 345 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 3.4 m, unit weight 20 kN/m^3, phi = 37 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 3.2e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.7, area = 4.5e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 3.2, i = 0.7, A = 4.5 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (3.2e-4)*0.7*(4.5e-3) | Answer: 1008 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.4 m, bed slope 0.004 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.023. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 1.8 m under a head of 0.4 m. Taking Cd = 0.6 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 2.6 m wide carries a discharge of 19.7 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 270 m and design speed 95 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 270, V = 95 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (95)^2 / (127*270) | Answer: 0.2632
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: A tank of volume 330 m^3 treats a flow of 160 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 330, Q = 160 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 330 / 160 | Answer: 2.062 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 360 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.17 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 8 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 360, k = 0.17, t = 8 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 360*(1 - e^(-0.17*8)) | Answer: 267.6 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.76, rainfall intensity 50 mm/h over a catchment of 20.5 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.76, i = 50, A = 20.5 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.76*50*20.5 / 360 | Answer: 2.164 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.03 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 620 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.03, M = 620 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 620*(20+0.03)/20 | Answer: 620.9 m

question: Convert the decimal number 3217 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 3217 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: C91 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 00001110 and 00000010.
solution: XOR: 00001100 | Count of 1s = 2 | Answer: 2
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 60 megabits is sent over a link of 8 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 60, B = 8 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 60 / 8 | Answer: 7.5 s

question: A link has bandwidth 53 Mbps and round-trip time 90 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 53, R = 90 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 53e6 * 90e-3 bits = 4770 kb | Answer: 4770 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.98, cache access time 7 ns and main-memory access time 160 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.98, tc = 7, tm = 160 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.98*7 + (1 - 0.98)*160 | Answer: 10.06 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 695600 elements?
solution: Given: n = 695600 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(695600)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.015, memory access time 80 ns and page-fault service time 7 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 7 ms = 7000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.015)*80 + 0.015*7000000.0 ns | Answer: 105.1 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 3 m^3 at 180 kPa and 550 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 3, P = 180, Tk = 550 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (180e3)*3 / (8.314*550) | Answer: 118.1 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.4 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 6 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.4, t = 6 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.4*6) | Answer: 0.9093

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.47 /min) is to reach 80% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.47, X = 80 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.8) / 0.47 | Answer: 3.424 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.38 /min) reaches 50% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.38, X = 50 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.5 / (0.38*(1 - 0.5)) | Answer: 2.632 min

question: For a reaction with A = 7e10 /s and activation energy 85 kJ/mol at 410 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 7, Ea = 85, Tk = 410 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 7e10 * exp(-85e3 / (8.314*410)) | Answer: 1.037 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.91 and bottoms xW = 0.08, with relative volatility alpha = 1.7. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.91, xw = 0.08, al = 1.7 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.91/0.09)(0.92/0.08)] / ln(1.7) | Answer: 8.963 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.56 and x = 0.49. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.56, x = 0.49 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.56/0.44) / (0.49/0.51) | Answer: 1.325

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.44 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 95 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.44, Psat = 95 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.44 * 95 | Answer: 41.8 kPa

question: A stream of 4.7 kg/s with specific heat 2.9 kJ/kg-K is heated through 60 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 4.7, cp = 2.9, dT = 60 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 4.7*2.9*60 | Answer: 817.8 kW

question: A reactor of volume 19.6 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 2.4 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 19.6, Q = 2.4 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 19.6 / 2.4 | Answer: 8.167 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 8.5e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 5 mm with a concentration difference of 40 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 8.5, L = 5, dC = 40 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (8.5e-9)*40 / (5e-3) | Answer: 68 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 7.8 min and steady-state gain 3.1. For a step input of magnitude 9, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 7.8, K = 3.1, M = 9 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 3.1 * 9 | Answer: 27.9 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 70 m^2 flies at 240 m/s (air density 1.225 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 1.3. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 70, V = 240, rho = 1.225, CL = 1.3 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1.225*(240)^2*70*1.3 / 1000 | Answer: 321 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 80 m^2 flies at 70 m/s (density 1 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.09. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 80, V = 70, rho = 1, CD = 0.09 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*1*(70)^2*80*0.09 / 1000 | Answer: 17.64 kN

question: A specimen under stress 310 MPa shows an elastic strain of 1.5e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 310, eps = 1.5 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 310 / (1.5e-3) MPa = 206.7 GPa | Answer: 206.7 GPa

question: A block of mass 36 kg has a volume of 1e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 36, V = 1 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 36 / (1e-3) | Answer: 36000 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 1300 mm is heated through 70 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 17e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 1300, dT = 70, al = 17 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 1300*17e-6*70 | Answer: 1.547 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 185 ohm, R2 = 135 ohm and R3 = 420 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 185, R2 = 135, R3 = 420 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 135*420 / 185 | Answer: 306.5 ohm

question: A measurement reads 10.4 when the true value is 20. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10.4, true = 20 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10.4 - 20| / 20 * 100 | Answer: 48 %

question: Annual demand is 46000 units, ordering cost 230 per order and holding cost 30 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 46000, S = 230, H = 30 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*46000*230 / 30) | Answer: 839.8 units

question: An asset costs 450000 with salvage value 22000 after 7 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 450000, Sv = 22000, n = 7 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (450000 - 22000) / 7 | Answer: 61143 per year

question: A product sells for 140 per unit with variable cost 80 per unit and fixed costs 75000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 140, V = 80, F = 75000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 75000 / (140 - 80) | Answer: 1250 units

question: Find the present worth of 125000 received 9 years from now at an interest rate of 12% per year.
solution: Given: F = 125000, n = 9, i = 12 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 125000 / (1 + 0.12)^9 | Answer: 45076 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.98, 0.92 and 0.92 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.98, r2 = 0.92, r3 = 0.92 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.98*0.92*0.92 | Answer: 0.8295

question: A process produces 22 defective items in a batch of 3500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 22, N = 3500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 22/3500 * 1e6 | Answer: 6286 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = 4x^3 + 5x^2 + x + 2 evaluated at x = 3.
For f(x) = 3x^3 + 7x^2 + 2x - 8, find f''(x) at x = 0.
Evaluate the definite integral of (-2x^2 + 5x + 4) dx from x = -2 to x = 5.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = -2x^3/3 + 5x^2/2 + 4x | Evaluate F(5) - F(-2) | Answer: -8.167
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 2x^2 - 9x - 6 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[-5, 3], [-4, 7]].
solution: Given: a = -5, b = 3, c = -4, d = 7 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (-5)(7) - (3)(-4) | Answer: -23

question: Find the determinant of [[-5, 2, -2], [-5, -5, 5], [-4, -6, 3]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: -105

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[-2, 1], [5, 5]].
solution: Trace tr = 3, Determinant = -15 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 5.653

question: Solve for x: 2x + -2y = 3 and -6x + -6y = -5.
solution: Determinant = 2*-6 - -2*-6 = -24 | x = (e d - b f) / det = 1.167 | Answer: x = 1.167
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 53, 53, 62, 81, 72.
solution: Sum = 321 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 64.2 | Answer: 64.2

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 22, 1, 7, 45, 8.
solution: Mean = 16.6 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 17.64

question: Find the slope of the line through (5, 7) and (-1, -4).
solution: Given: x1 = 5, y1 = 7, x2 = -1, y2 = -4 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (-4 - 7) / (-1 - 5) | Answer: 1.833

question: Find the distance between the points (-6, 6) and (7, -8).
solution: Given: x1 = -6, y1 = 6, x2 = 7, y2 = -8 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((13)^2 + (-14)^2) | Answer: 19.1 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (-8,-3), (2,-2), (1,-6).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 19.5 sq units

question: Find the 27th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 3 and common difference 4.
solution: Given: a = 3, d = 4, n = 27 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = 3 + (27 - 1)*4 | Answer: 107

question: Find the sum of the first 27 terms of an AP with first term -11 and common difference 1.
solution: Given: a = -11, d = 1, n = 27 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 27/2 [2*-11 + (27-1)*1] | Answer: 54

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 10500 at 13.5% per annum for 4 years.
solution: Given: P = 10500, R = 13.5, Tt = 4 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 10500 * 13.5 * 4 / 100 | Answer: 5670 currency units

question: Find the amount when 28000 is invested at 11.8% per annum compounded annually for 2 years.
solution: Given: P = 28000, R = 11.8, Tt = 2 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 28000 * (1 + 11.8/100)^2 | Answer: 34998 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (8, -3, -2) and (1, -2, 6).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (-5, 6, 5) and (-6, -6, 1).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 79.23

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (-3, 6, 4) and (-2, -5, -5).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 140.1 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number 6 + -5i.
solution: Given: a = 6, b = -5 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((6)^2 + (-5)^2) | Answer: 7.81

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number 8 + 10i.
solution: Given: a = 8, b = 10 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(10, 8) | Answer: 51.34 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -x^3 + 4x^2 + 2x + 5 at x = -1.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-46 with initial guess x0=7, find x1 (one iteration).
solution: Given: N = 46, x0 = 7 | Formula: x1 = x0 - (x0^2 - N)/(2 x0) | Substitute: x1 = 7 - ((7)^2 - 46)/(2*7) | Answer: 6.786

question: Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.3 and ordinates 20, 0, 18, 1, 1, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 161 and 133.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 161 and 133 | Answer: GCD = 7

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 64 and 24.
solution: Given: a = 64, b = 24 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 64*24 / 8 | Answer: 192
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 10 mm carries an axial tensile load of 18 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 32 mm and length 1600 mm carries an axial load of 43 kN. Take E = 70 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 61 mm transmits a torque of 2100 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 61, Tt = 2100 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(2100*1000) / (pi*(61)^3) | Answer: 47.12 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 65 mm and length 1400 mm carries a torque of 1500 N-m. With G = 77 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 34 mm wide and 230 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 34, h = 230 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 34*(230)^2 / 6 | Answer: 299767 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (74 mm x 260 mm) carries a bending moment of 10 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (55 mm x 110 mm) has effective length 3100 mm and E = 200 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 490 MPa is designed for a working stress of 140 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 490, sw = 140 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 490 / 140 | Answer: 3.5

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1500 mm and wall thickness 19 mm carries an internal pressure of 2.1 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1500, t = 19, P = 2.1 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 2.1*1500 / (2*19) | Answer: 82.89 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 980 K and 400 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 980, Tc = 400 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 400/980) * 100 | Answer: 59.18 %

question: A refrigerator works between 251 K (cold) and 302 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 251, Th = 302 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 251 / (302 - 251) | Answer: 4.922

question: A heat pump operates between 262 K and 318 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 262, Th = 318 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 318 / (318 - 262) | Answer: 5.679

question: 2.8 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 180 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.8, dT = 180 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 2.8 * 0.718 * 180 | Answer: 361.9 kJ

question: 4 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 105 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4, dT = 105 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 4 * 1.005 * 105 | Answer: 422.1 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 1.8 m^3 at 470 K with mass 4.1 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 1.8, Tk = 470, m = 4.1 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 4.1*0.287*470 / 1.8 | Answer: 307.2 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 4.7 kg of air expands isothermally at 380 K from volume V1 to 5*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.7, Tk = 380, ratio = 5 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 4.7*0.287*380*ln(5) | Answer: 825 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 1 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.15 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 1, D = 0.15 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*1*0.15 / 0.001 | Answer: 150000

question: Water flows at 1.5 m/s through a pipe of diameter 110 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 3.3 m. Taking Cv = 0.96, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 3.3, cv = 0.96 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.96*sqrt(2*9.81*3.3) | Answer: 7.725 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 250 mm) water flows at 2.2 m/s. It contracts to diameter 50 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 250, d2 = 50, V1 = 2.2 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 2.2*(250/50)^2 | Answer: 55 m/s

question: Water flows at 3.2 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.33 m and length 150 m. With friction factor f = 0.026, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 17 teeth drives a gear of 62 teeth. If the pinion runs at 950 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 17, z2 = 62, N1 = 950 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 950*17 / 62 | Answer: 260.5 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 540 mm rotates at 1000 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 540, N = 1000 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.54)*1000 / 60 | Answer: 28.27 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 43 kW at 500 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 43, N = 500 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(43*1000) / (2*pi*500) | Answer: 821.2 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 7.4 kg rotates at radius 0.45 m at 250 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 4400 N/m and mass 2.1 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 4400, m = 2.1 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(4400/2.1) | Answer: 7.285 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 7.6 m^2 and thickness 0.35 m has conductivity k = 43 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 125 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 7.6, L = 0.35, k = 43, dT = 125 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 43*7.6*125 / 0.35 | Answer: 116714 W

question: A surface of area 4 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 65 W/m^2-K to surroundings 80 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 4, h = 65, dT = 80 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 65*4*80 | Answer: 20800 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 170 m/min, feed = 0.46 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2.1 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 170, f = 0.46, d = 2.1 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*170*0.46*2.1 | Answer: 164220 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 320 mm is turned at 850 rpm with a feed of 0.4 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 320, N = 850, f = 0.4 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 320 / (0.4*850) | Answer: 0.9412 min

question: A resistor of 110 ohm carries a current of 9.1 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 110, I = 9.1 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 9.1 * 110 | Answer: 1001 V

question: Three resistors 9 ohm, 29 ohm and 69 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 9, R2 = 29, R3 = 69 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 9 + 29 + 69 | Answer: 107 ohm

question: Two resistors 16 ohm and 77 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 16, R2 = 77 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 16*77 / (16+77) | Answer: 13.25 ohm

question: A device draws 5.8 A at 150 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 150, I = 5.8 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 150 * 5.8 | Answer: 870 W

question: A current of 6.9 A flows through a 150 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 6.9, R = 150 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (6.9)^2 * 150 | Answer: 7142 W

question: Two capacitors 7.3 uF and 11 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 7.3, C2 = 11 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 7.3*11 / (7.3+11) | Answer: 4.388 uF

question: A resistor 99 kohm and capacitor 16.1 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 99, C = 16.1 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (99k)(16.1u) = 1594 ms | Answer: 1594 ms

question: An inductor 440.8 mH is in series with 28 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 440.8, R = 28 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (440.8e-3) / 28 | Answer: 15.74 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 180.2 mH inductor at 540 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 180.2, f = 540 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (540)(180.2e-3) | Answer: 611.4 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 36.3 uF capacitor at 990 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 36.3, f = 990 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (990)(36.3e-6)) | Answer: 4.429 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 78 ohm, XL = 142 ohm and XC = 44 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 78, XL = 142, XC = 44 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(78^2 + (142 - 44)^2) | Answer: 125.3 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 68.7 mH and C = 5.3 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 68.7, C = 5.3 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(68.7e-3 * 5.3e-6)) | Answer: 263.8 Hz

question: A capacitor of 32.1 uF is charged to 190 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 32.1, V = 190 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*32.1e-6*(190)^2 | Answer: 579.4 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 310 V with 930 primary turns and 60 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 310, N1 = 930, N2 = 60 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 310 * 60/930 | Answer: 20 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 380 V and draws an armature current of 52 A. If the armature resistance is 0.31 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 380, Ia = 52, Ra = 0.31 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 380 - 52*0.31 | Answer: 363.9 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 120 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.85. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 120, VL = 400, pf = 0.85 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*400*120*0.85 / 1000 | Answer: 70.67 kW

question: A load has real power 75 kW and apparent power 175 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 75, S = 175 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 75 / 175 | Answer: 0.4286

question: A machine delivers 25 kW output while drawing 152 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 25, Pi = 152 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 25/152 * 100 | Answer: 16.45 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 23 V across R1 = 13 ohm and R2 = 35 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 23, R1 = 13, R2 = 35 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 23*35 / (13+35) | Answer: 16.77 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 70 kohm and Rin = 13 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 70, Rin = 13 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 70 / 13 | Answer: 5.385

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 180 kohm and Rg = 14 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 180, Rg = 14 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 180/14 | Answer: 13.86

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 4964. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 4964 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(4964) | Answer: 36.96 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 3.7 m carries a central point load of 105 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.7, W = 105 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 105*3.7 / 4 | Answer: 97.12 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.6 m carries a UDL of 20 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 9.6, w = 20 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 20*(9.6)^2 / 8 | Answer: 230.4 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 1 m carries a point load 15 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 1, W = 15 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 15*1 | Answer: 15 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 3.4 m carries a UDL of 36 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.4, w = 36 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 36*(3.4)^2 / 2 | Answer: 208.1 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.4 m carries a point load 95 kN at distance 3.1 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 6.4, a = 3.1, W = 95 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 95*(6.4 - 3.1) / 6.4 | Answer: 48.98 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 4 m) carries a central point load 45 kN. With E = 200 GPa and I = 100e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=45000 N, L=4000.0 mm, E=200000 MPa, I=100e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 3 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 4.1 m carries a UDL of 36 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.1, w = 36 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 36*(4.1)^2 / 12 | Answer: 50.43 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 510 mm, clear cover 30 mm and main bars of diameter 20 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 510, c = 30, dia = 20 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 510 - 30 - 20/2 | Answer: 470 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 35.3 m^2 carrying a factored load of 18 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 35.3, w = 18 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 18 * 35.3 | Answer: 635.4 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 5.5 m, unit weight 16 kN/m^3, phi = 37 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 3.2 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 18 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 3.2, g = 18 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (18 - 9.81)*3.2 | Answer: 26.21 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 6.1e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.8, area = 3.3e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 6.1, i = 0.8, A = 3.3 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (6.1e-4)*0.8*(3.3e-3) | Answer: 161 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.3 m, bed slope 0.007 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.03. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 2.5 m under a head of 0.3 m. Taking Cd = 0.61 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 3.7 m wide carries a discharge of 20.6 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 580 m and design speed 65 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 580, V = 65 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (65)^2 / (127*580) | Answer: 0.05736
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: A tank of volume 980 m^3 treats a flow of 10 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 980, Q = 10 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 980 / 10 | Answer: 98 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 240 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.14 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 8 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 240, k = 0.14, t = 8 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 240*(1 - e^(-0.14*8)) | Answer: 161.7 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.58, rainfall intensity 105 mm/h over a catchment of 30 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.58, i = 105, A = 30 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.58*105*30 / 360 | Answer: 5.075 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.07 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 630 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.07, M = 630 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 630*(20+0.07)/20 | Answer: 632.2 m

question: Convert the decimal number 1596 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 1596 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 63C (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 11101011 and 11010010.
solution: XOR: 00111001 | Count of 1s = 4 | Answer: 4
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 760 megabits is sent over a link of 60 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 760, B = 60 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 760 / 60 | Answer: 12.67 s

question: A link has bandwidth 23 Mbps and round-trip time 40 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 23, R = 40 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 23e6 * 40e-3 bits = 920 kb | Answer: 920 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.91, cache access time 7 ns and main-memory access time 140 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.91, tc = 7, tm = 140 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.91*7 + (1 - 0.91)*140 | Answer: 18.97 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 766151 elements?
solution: Given: n = 766151 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(766151)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.016, memory access time 100 ns and page-fault service time 6 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 6 ms = 6000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.016)*100 + 0.016*6000000.0 ns | Answer: 96.1 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 2.6 m^3 at 250 kPa and 420 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 2.6, P = 250, Tk = 420 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (250e3)*2.6 / (8.314*420) | Answer: 186.1 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.3 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 13 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.3, t = 13 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.3*13) | Answer: 0.9798

question: For a reaction with A = 6e10 /s and activation energy 85 kJ/mol at 330 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 6, Ea = 85, Tk = 330 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 6e10 * exp(-85e3 / (8.314*330)) | Answer: 0.002105 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.92 and bottoms xW = 0.06, with relative volatility alpha = 2. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.92, xw = 0.06, al = 2 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.92/0.08)(0.94/0.06)] / ln(2) | Answer: 7.493 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.89 and x = 0.42. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.89, x = 0.42 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.89/0.11) / (0.42/0.58) | Answer: 11.17

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.66 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 30 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.66, Psat = 30 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.66 * 30 | Answer: 19.8 kPa

question: A stream of 1.1 kg/s with specific heat 3.3 kJ/kg-K is heated through 40 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 1.1, cp = 3.3, dT = 40 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 1.1*3.3*40 | Answer: 145.2 kW

question: A reactor of volume 1.6 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 4 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 1.6, Q = 4 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 1.6 / 4 | Answer: 0.4 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 6.2e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 5 mm with a concentration difference of 130 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 6.2, L = 5, dC = 130 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (6.2e-9)*130 / (5e-3) | Answer: 161.2 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 7.5 min and steady-state gain 2.2. For a step input of magnitude 20, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 7.5, K = 2.2, M = 20 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 2.2 * 20 | Answer: 44 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 90 m^2 flies at 210 m/s (air density 0.4 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.4. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 90, V = 210, rho = 0.4, CL = 0.4 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.4*(210)^2*90*0.4 / 1000 | Answer: 317.5 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 95 m^2 flies at 250 m/s (density 1.225 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.11. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 95, V = 250, rho = 1.225, CD = 0.11 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*1.225*(250)^2*95*0.11 / 1000 | Answer: 400 kN

question: A specimen under stress 100 MPa shows an elastic strain of 2.2e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 100, eps = 2.2 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 100 / (2.2e-3) MPa = 45.45 GPa | Answer: 45.45 GPa

question: A block of mass 48 kg has a volume of 3e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 48, V = 3 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 48 / (3e-3) | Answer: 16000 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 1400 mm is heated through 100 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 17e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 1400, dT = 100, al = 17 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 1400*17e-6*100 | Answer: 2.38 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 160 ohm, R2 = 190 ohm and R3 = 185 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 160, R2 = 190, R3 = 185 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 190*185 / 160 | Answer: 219.7 ohm

question: A measurement reads 9.32 when the true value is 50. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.32, true = 50 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.32 - 50| / 50 * 100 | Answer: 81.36 %

question: Annual demand is 41500 units, ordering cost 260 per order and holding cost 17 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 41500, S = 260, H = 17 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*41500*260 / 17) | Answer: 1127 units

question: An asset costs 310000 with salvage value 10000 after 6 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 310000, Sv = 10000, n = 6 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (310000 - 10000) / 6 | Answer: 50000 per year

question: A product sells for 230 per unit with variable cost 160 per unit and fixed costs 150000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 230, V = 160, F = 150000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 150000 / (230 - 160) | Answer: 2143 units

question: Find the present worth of 60000 received 5 years from now at an interest rate of 11% per year.
solution: Given: F = 60000, n = 5, i = 11 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 60000 / (1 + 0.11)^5 | Answer: 35607 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.97, 0.99 and 0.93 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.97, r2 = 0.99, r3 = 0.93 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.97*0.99*0.93 | Answer: 0.8931

question: A process produces 42 defective items in a batch of 14000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 42, N = 14000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 42/14000 * 1e6 | Answer: 3000 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = x^3 + 8x^2 - 7x - 4 evaluated at x = -1.
For f(x) = 2x^3 + x^2 + 8x - 2, find f''(x) at x = 0.
Evaluate the definite integral of (4x - 6) dx from x = 1 to x = 4.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = 0x^3/3 + 4x^2/2 + -6x | Evaluate F(4) - F(1) | Answer: 12
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of x^2 - 4x - 1 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[9, -4], [-6, -9]].
solution: Given: a = 9, b = -4, c = -6, d = -9 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (9)(-9) - (-4)(-6) | Answer: -105

question: Find the determinant of [[-1, -3, -3], [4, -6, -3], [2, -2, 4]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: 84

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[6, 0], [-7, -3]].
solution: Trace tr = 3, Determinant = -18 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 6

question: Solve for x: 0x + 6y = -10 and -1x + 3y = -4.
solution: Determinant = 0*3 - 6*-1 = 6 | x = (e d - b f) / det = -1 | Answer: x = -1
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 3, 88, 56, 8, 94.
solution: Sum = 249 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 49.8 | Answer: 49.8

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 3, 20, 42, 35, 33.
solution: Mean = 26.6 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 15.4

question: Find the slope of the line through (-5, -1) and (-3, 0).
solution: Given: x1 = -5, y1 = -1, x2 = -3, y2 = 0 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (0 - -1) / (-3 - -5) | Answer: 0.5

question: Find the distance between the points (-7, 4) and (8, 6).
solution: Given: x1 = -7, y1 = 4, x2 = 8, y2 = 6 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((15)^2 + (2)^2) | Answer: 15.13 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (6,1), (8,-8), (-5,7).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 43.5 sq units

question: Find the 21th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -18 and common difference -8.
solution: Given: a = -18, d = -8, n = 21 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -18 + (21 - 1)*-8 | Answer: -178

question: Find the sum of the first 25 terms of an AP with first term -5 and common difference -1.
solution: Given: a = -5, d = -1, n = 25 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 25/2 [2*-5 + (25-1)*-1] | Answer: -425

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 40500 at 7.2% per annum for 2 years.
solution: Given: P = 40500, R = 7.2, Tt = 2 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 40500 * 7.2 * 2 / 100 | Answer: 5832 currency units

question: Find the amount when 26500 is invested at 5.7% per annum compounded annually for 2 years.
solution: Given: P = 26500, R = 5.7, Tt = 2 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 26500 * (1 + 5.7/100)^2 | Answer: 29607 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (1, -1, -7) and (7, -8, -4).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (1, 5, 2) and (-1, 0, 5).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 26.44

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (-3, -2, -6) and (-5, 5, 5).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 114.4 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number 11 + 10i.
solution: Given: a = 11, b = 10 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((11)^2 + (10)^2) | Answer: 14.87

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number 9 + -4i.
solution: Given: a = 9, b = -4 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(-4, 9) | Answer: -23.96 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -3x^3 + 4x^2 - 6x - 2 at x = -2.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-164 with initial guess x0=9, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.7 and ordinates 18, 18, 20, 18, 5, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 518 and 469.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 518 and 469 | Answer: GCD = 7

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 6 and 18.
solution: Given: a = 6, b = 18 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 6*18 / 6 | Answer: 18
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 41 mm carries an axial tensile load of 45 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 19 mm and length 800 mm carries an axial load of 63 kN. Take E = 70 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 51 mm transmits a torque of 1050 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 51, Tt = 1050 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(1050*1000) / (pi*(51)^3) | Answer: 40.31 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 42 mm and length 1900 mm carries a torque of 700 N-m. With G = 80 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (42)^4 / 32 = 30549 mm^4 | theta = (700*1000)(1900) / (80000 * 30549) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 3.118 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 65 mm wide and 240 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 65, h = 240 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 65*(240)^2 / 6 | Answer: 624000 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (105 mm x 210 mm) carries a bending moment of 39 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (34 mm x 160 mm) has effective length 2100 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 480 MPa is designed for a working stress of 170 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 480, sw = 170 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 480 / 170 | Answer: 2.824

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 400 mm and wall thickness 13 mm carries an internal pressure of 1 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 400, t = 13, P = 1 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 1*400 / (2*13) | Answer: 15.38 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 680 K and 440 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 680, Tc = 440 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 440/680) * 100 | Answer: 35.29 %

question: A refrigerator works between 270 K (cold) and 324 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 270, Th = 324 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 270 / (324 - 270) | Answer: 5

question: A heat pump operates between 267 K and 320 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 267, Th = 320 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 320 / (320 - 267) | Answer: 6.038

question: 6.4 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 140 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 6.4, dT = 140 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 6.4 * 0.718 * 140 | Answer: 643.3 kJ

question: 2.5 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 175 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.5, dT = 175 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 2.5 * 1.005 * 175 | Answer: 439.7 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 3.3 m^3 at 440 K with mass 4.6 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 3.3, Tk = 440, m = 4.6 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 4.6*0.287*440 / 3.3 | Answer: 176 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 3.4 kg of air expands isothermally at 360 K from volume V1 to 5*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.4, Tk = 360, ratio = 5 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 3.4*0.287*360*ln(5) | Answer: 565.4 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 3.8 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.21 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 3.8, D = 0.21 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*3.8*0.21 / 0.001 | Answer: 798000

question: Water flows at 1.9 m/s through a pipe of diameter 270 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 18.8 m. Taking Cv = 0.97, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).

question: A pulley of diameter 490 mm rotates at 1200 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 490, N = 1200 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.49)*1200 / 60 | Answer: 30.79 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 27.1 kW at 1150 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.

question: A mass of 4 kg rotates at radius 0.15 m at 950 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 12700 N/m and mass 9.8 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.

question: A plane wall of area 2.2 m^2 and thickness 0.31 m has conductivity k = 20.2 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 165 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 2.2, L = 0.31, k = 20.2, dT = 165 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 20.2*2.2*165 / 0.31 | Answer: 23654 W

question: A surface of area 1.1 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 35 W/m^2-K to surroundings 105 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.

question: In turning, cutting speed = 200 m/min, feed = 0.16 mm/rev, depth of cut = 1.1 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 200, f = 0.16, d = 1.1 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*200*0.16*1.1 | Answer: 35200 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 420 mm is turned at 850 rpm with a feed of 0.3 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 420, N = 850, f = 0.3 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 420 / (0.3*850) | Answer: 1.647 min

question: A resistor of 30 ohm carries a current of 7.2 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 30, I = 7.2 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 7.2 * 30 | Answer: 216 V

question: Three resistors 52 ohm, 36 ohm and 99 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 52, R2 = 36, R3 = 99 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 52 + 36 + 99 | Answer: 187 ohm

question: Two resistors 88 ohm and 76 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 88, R2 = 76 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 88*76 / (88+76) | Answer: 40.78 ohm

question: A device draws 10 A at 160 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 160, I = 10 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 160 * 10 | Answer: 1600 W

question: A current of 8 A flows through a 49 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 8, R = 49 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (8)^2 * 49 | Answer: 3136 W

question: Two capacitors 5.1 uF and 4.3 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 5.1, C2 = 4.3 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 5.1*4.3 / (5.1+4.3) | Answer: 2.333 uF

question: A resistor 97 kohm and capacitor 5.1 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 97, C = 5.1 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (97k)(5.1u) = 494.7 ms | Answer: 494.7 ms

question: An inductor 439.9 mH is in series with 180 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 439.9, R = 180 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (439.9e-3) / 180 | Answer: 2.444 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 31.9 mH inductor at 450 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 31.9, f = 450 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (450)(31.9e-3) | Answer: 90.2 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 24.6 uF capacitor at 270 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 24.6, f = 270 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (270)(24.6e-6)) | Answer: 23.96 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 20 ohm, XL = 16 ohm and XC = 41 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 20, XL = 16, XC = 41 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(20^2 + (16 - 41)^2) | Answer: 32.02 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 79.7 mH and C = 6 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 79.7, C = 6 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(79.7e-3 * 6e-6)) | Answer: 230.2 Hz

question: A capacitor of 82.1 uF is charged to 390 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 82.1, V = 390 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*82.1e-6*(390)^2 | Answer: 6244 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 280 V with 650 primary turns and 200 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 280, N1 = 650, N2 = 200 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 280 * 200/650 | Answer: 86.15 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 120 V and draws an armature current of 10 A. If the armature resistance is 0.63 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 120, Ia = 10, Ra = 0.63 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 120 - 10*0.63 | Answer: 113.7 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 20 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.71. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 20, VL = 400, pf = 0.71 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*400*20*0.71 / 1000 | Answer: 9.838 kW

question: A load has real power 70 kW and apparent power 215 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 70, S = 215 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 70 / 215 | Answer: 0.3256

question: A machine delivers 150 kW output while drawing 172 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 150, Pi = 172 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 150/172 * 100 | Answer: 87.21 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 15 V across R1 = 15 ohm and R2 = 14 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 15, R1 = 15, R2 = 14 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 15*14 / (15+14) | Answer: 7.241 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 180 kohm and Rin = 7 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 180, Rin = 7 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 180 / 7 | Answer: 25.71

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 200 kohm and Rg = 44 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 200, Rg = 44 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 200/44 | Answer: 5.545

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 6646. Express the gain in decibels (power).

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.1 m carries a central point load of 55 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 9.1, W = 55 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 55*9.1 / 4 | Answer: 125.1 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 3.6 m carries a UDL of 15 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.6, w = 15 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 15*(3.6)^2 / 8 | Answer: 24.3 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 1.7 m carries a point load 75 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 1.7, W = 75 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 75*1.7 | Answer: 127.5 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 4.5 m carries a UDL of 24 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.5, w = 24 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 24*(4.5)^2 / 2 | Answer: 243 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 8.6 m carries a point load 100 kN at distance 2.5 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 8.6, a = 2.5, W = 100 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 100*(8.6 - 2.5) / 8.6 | Answer: 70.93 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 6.3 m) carries a central point load 50 kN. With E = 200 GPa and I = 150e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.

question: A fixed beam of span 4.3 m carries a UDL of 30 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.3, w = 30 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 30*(4.3)^2 / 12 | Answer: 46.22 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 670 mm, clear cover 25 mm and main bars of diameter 12 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 670, c = 25, dia = 12 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 670 - 25 - 12/2 | Answer: 639 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 20.1 m^2 carrying a factored load of 13.5 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 20.1, w = 13.5 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 13.5 * 20.1 | Answer: 271.4 kN

question: At a depth of 6.8 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 21 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 7.5e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.8, area = 2.6e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.

question: A tank of volume 470 m^3 treats a flow of 85 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 470, Q = 85 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 470 / 85 | Answer: 5.529 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 240 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.24 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 5 days.

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.36, rainfall intensity 45 mm/h over a catchment of 21 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.36, i = 45, A = 21 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.36*45*21 / 360 | Answer: 0.945 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.07, M = 150 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 150*(30+0.07)/30 | Answer: 150.3 m

question: A file of 1000 megabits is sent over a link of 91 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.

question: A link has bandwidth 75 Mbps and round-trip time 20 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 75, R = 20 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 75e6 * 20e-3 bits = 1500 kb | Answer: 1500 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.94, cache access time 2 ns and main-memory access time 70 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.94, tc = 2, tm = 70 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.94*2 + (1 - 0.94)*70 | Answer: 6.08 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 794181 elements?

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.015, memory access time 80 ns and page-fault service time 5 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 1.9 m^3 at 150 kPa and 340 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.12 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 16 minutes.

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.39 /min) is to reach 55% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.17 /min) reaches 80% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.

question: For a reaction with A = 6e10 /s and activation energy 50 kJ/mol at 480 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.95 and bottoms xW = 0.02, with relative volatility alpha = 3. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.59 and x = 0.37. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.54 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 50 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.54, Psat = 50 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.54 * 50 | Answer: 27 kPa

question: A stream of 3.1 kg/s with specific heat 3.9 kJ/kg-K is heated through 95 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 3.1, cp = 3.9, dT = 95 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 3.1*3.9*95 | Answer: 1149 kW

question: A reactor of volume 2.8 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 2.2 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 2.8, Q = 2.2 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 2.8 / 2.2 | Answer: 1.273 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 5.1e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 1 mm with a concentration difference of 80 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 5.1, L = 1, dC = 80 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (5.1e-9)*80 / (1e-3) | Answer: 408 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 8.1 min and steady-state gain 3.7. For a step input of magnitude 17, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 8.1, K = 3.7, M = 17 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 3.7 * 17 | Answer: 62.9 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 120 m^2 flies at 230 m/s (air density 1.225 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 1. Find the lift force in kN.

question: An aircraft of wing area 40 m^2 flies at 180 m/s (density 1 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.12. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 40, V = 180, rho = 1, CD = 0.12 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*1*(180)^2*40*0.12 / 1000 | Answer: 77.76 kN

question: A specimen under stress 400 MPa shows an elastic strain of 0.9e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 400, eps = 0.9 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 400 / (0.9e-3) MPa = 444.4 GPa | Answer: 444.4 GPa

question: A block of mass 48 kg has a volume of 1.9e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.

question: A rod of length 2300 mm is heated through 45 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 12e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 65 ohm, R2 = 150 ohm and R3 = 390 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 65, R2 = 150, R3 = 390 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 150*390 / 65 | Answer: 900 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 1000 ohm and gauge factor 2.2 experiences a strain of 900e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 1000, GF = 2.2, eps = 900 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 1000*2.2*900e-6 | Answer: 1980 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 9.11 when the true value is 100. Find the percentage error.

question: Annual demand is 16000 units, ordering cost 260 per order and holding cost 26 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 16000, S = 260, H = 26 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*16000*260 / 26) | Answer: 565.7 units

question: An asset costs 200000 with salvage value 36000 after 11 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 200000, Sv = 36000, n = 11 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (200000 - 36000) / 11 | Answer: 14909 per year

question: A product sells for 270 per unit with variable cost 30 per unit and fixed costs 125000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 270, V = 30, F = 125000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 125000 / (270 - 30) | Answer: 520.8 units

question: Find the present worth of 10000 received 4 years from now at an interest rate of 6% per year.
solution: Given: F = 10000, n = 4, i = 6 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 10000 / (1 + 0.06)^4 | Answer: 7921 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.96, 0.96 and 0.98 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.96, r2 = 0.96, r3 = 0.98 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.96*0.96*0.98 | Answer: 0.9032

question: A process produces 14 defective items in a batch of 16500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 14, N = 16500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 14/16500 * 1e6 | Answer: 848.5 PPM
