solution: Given: A = 7.7, L = 0.31, k = 47.1, dT = 135 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 47.1*7.7*135 / 0.31 | Answer: 157937 W

question: A surface of area 3.4 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 200 W/m^2-K to surroundings 40 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 3.4, h = 200, dT = 40 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 200*3.4*40 | Answer: 27200 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 110 m/min, feed = 0.29 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2.5 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 110, f = 0.29, d = 2.5 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*110*0.29*2.5 | Answer: 79750 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 490 mm is turned at 1000 rpm with a feed of 0.23 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 490, N = 1000, f = 0.23 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 490 / (0.23*1000) | Answer: 2.13 min

question: A resistor of 160 ohm carries a current of 0.6 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 160, I = 0.6 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 0.6 * 160 | Answer: 96 V

question: Three resistors 76 ohm, 74 ohm and 96 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 76, R2 = 74, R3 = 96 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 76 + 74 + 96 | Answer: 246 ohm

question: Two resistors 17 ohm and 63 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 17, R2 = 63 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 17*63 / (17+63) | Answer: 13.39 ohm

question: A device draws 9.8 A at 105 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 105, I = 9.8 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 105 * 9.8 | Answer: 1029 W

question: A current of 8.2 A flows through a 22 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 8.2, R = 22 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (8.2)^2 * 22 | Answer: 1479 W

question: Two capacitors 7.7 uF and 37.7 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 7.7, C2 = 37.7 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 7.7*37.7 / (7.7+37.7) | Answer: 6.394 uF

question: A resistor 13 kohm and capacitor 11.5 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 13, C = 11.5 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (13k)(11.5u) = 149.5 ms | Answer: 149.5 ms

question: An inductor 138.8 mH is in series with 110 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 138.8, R = 110 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (138.8e-3) / 110 | Answer: 1.262 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 159.3 mH inductor at 380 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 159.3, f = 380 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (380)(159.3e-3) | Answer: 380.3 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 49.4 uF capacitor at 690 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 49.4, f = 690 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (690)(49.4e-6)) | Answer: 4.669 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 56 ohm, XL = 134 ohm and XC = 150 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 56, XL = 134, XC = 150 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(56^2 + (134 - 150)^2) | Answer: 58.24 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 70.9 mH and C = 3.8 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 70.9, C = 3.8 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(70.9e-3 * 3.8e-6)) | Answer: 306.6 Hz

question: A capacitor of 99.9 uF is charged to 150 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 99.9, V = 150 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*99.9e-6*(150)^2 | Answer: 1124 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 310 V with 530 primary turns and 110 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 310, N1 = 530, N2 = 110 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 310 * 110/530 | Answer: 64.34 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 180 V and draws an armature current of 9 A. If the armature resistance is 0.41 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 180, Ia = 9, Ra = 0.41 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 180 - 9*0.41 | Answer: 176.3 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 135 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.93. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 135, VL = 400, pf = 0.93 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*400*135*0.93 / 1000 | Answer: 86.98 kW

question: A load has real power 60 kW and apparent power 150 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 60, S = 150 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 60 / 150 | Answer: 0.4

question: A machine delivers 45 kW output while drawing 77 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 45, Pi = 77 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 45/77 * 100 | Answer: 58.44 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 19 V across R1 = 19 ohm and R2 = 22 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 19, R1 = 19, R2 = 22 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 19*22 / (19+22) | Answer: 10.2 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 140 kohm and Rin = 1 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 140, Rin = 1 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 140 / 1 | Answer: 140

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 70 kohm and Rg = 35 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 70, Rg = 35 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 70/35 | Answer: 3

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 4274. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 4274 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(4274) | Answer: 36.31 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 7.1 m carries a central point load of 95 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7.1, W = 95 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 95*7.1 / 4 | Answer: 168.6 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 3.2 m carries a UDL of 45 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.2, w = 45 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 45*(3.2)^2 / 8 | Answer: 57.6 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 2.5 m carries a point load 50 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 2.5, W = 50 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 50*2.5 | Answer: 125 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 4.4 m carries a UDL of 12 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.4, w = 12 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 12*(4.4)^2 / 2 | Answer: 116.2 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.3 m carries a point load 25 kN at distance 2.1 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 9.3, a = 2.1, W = 25 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 25*(9.3 - 2.1) / 9.3 | Answer: 19.35 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 6.4 m) carries a central point load 25 kN. With E = 30 GPa and I = 590e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=25000 N, L=6400.0 mm, E=30000 MPa, I=590e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 7.714 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 5.8 m carries a UDL of 24 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.8, w = 24 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 24*(5.8)^2 / 12 | Answer: 67.28 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 670 mm, clear cover 50 mm and main bars of diameter 25 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 670, c = 50, dia = 25 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 670 - 50 - 25/2 | Answer: 607.5 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 28.1 m^2 carrying a factored load of 8.9 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 28.1, w = 8.9 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 8.9 * 28.1 | Answer: 250.1 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 3.7 m, unit weight 20 kN/m^3, phi = 34 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 2.4 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 19 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 2.4, g = 19 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (19 - 9.81)*2.4 | Answer: 22.06 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 1.4e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.6, area = 1.3e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 1.4, i = 0.6, A = 1.3 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (1.4e-4)*0.6*(1.3e-3) | Answer: 109.2 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 0.7 m, bed slope 0.004 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.029. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 1.8 m under a head of 1.2 m. Taking Cd = 0.62 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 3.9 m wide carries a discharge of 5 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 410 m and design speed 55 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 410, V = 55 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (55)^2 / (127*410) | Answer: 0.05809
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: A tank of volume 930 m^3 treats a flow of 100 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 930, Q = 100 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 930 / 100 | Answer: 9.3 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 170 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.27 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 3 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 170, k = 0.27, t = 3 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 170*(1 - e^(-0.27*3)) | Answer: 94.37 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.78, rainfall intensity 80 mm/h over a catchment of 29.8 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.78, i = 80, A = 29.8 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.78*80*29.8 / 360 | Answer: 5.165 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.02 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 650 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.02, M = 650 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 650*(20+0.02)/20 | Answer: 650.6 m

question: Convert the decimal number 2158 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 2158 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 86E (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Convert the 8-bit binary number 00101010 to decimal.
solution: Binary 00101010 = sum of bit-weights | Answer: 42 (decimal)
formula: Sum each bit times its positional weight (2^i)

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 11010101 and 01110100.
solution: XOR: 10100001 | Count of 1s = 3 | Answer: 3
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 180 megabits is sent over a link of 14 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 180, B = 14 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 180 / 14 | Answer: 12.86 s

question: A link has bandwidth 51 Mbps and round-trip time 80 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 51, R = 80 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 51e6 * 80e-3 bits = 4080 kb | Answer: 4080 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.93, cache access time 8 ns and main-memory access time 180 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.93, tc = 8, tm = 180 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.93*8 + (1 - 0.93)*180 | Answer: 20.04 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 312439 elements?
solution: Given: n = 312439 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(312439)) + 1 | Answer: 19

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.003, memory access time 190 ns and page-fault service time 8 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 8 ms = 8000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.003)*190 + 0.003*8000000.0 ns | Answer: 24.19 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 2.8 m^3 at 440 kPa and 380 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 2.8, P = 440, Tk = 380 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (440e3)*2.8 / (8.314*380) | Answer: 390 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.23 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 14 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.23, t = 14 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.23*14) | Answer: 0.96

question: For a reaction with A = 7e10 /s and activation energy 60 kJ/mol at 480 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 7, Ea = 60, Tk = 480 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 7e10 * exp(-60e3 / (8.314*480)) | Answer: 20679 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.95 and bottoms xW = 0.05, with relative volatility alpha = 3.3. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.95, xw = 0.05, al = 3.3 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.95/0.05)(0.95/0.05)] / ln(3.3) | Answer: 4.932 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.85 and x = 0.49. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.85, x = 0.49 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.85/0.15) / (0.49/0.51) | Answer: 5.898

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.89 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 20 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.89, Psat = 20 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.89 * 20 | Answer: 17.8 kPa

question: A stream of 9.8 kg/s with specific heat 3.7 kJ/kg-K is heated through 10 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 9.8, cp = 3.7, dT = 10 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 9.8*3.7*10 | Answer: 362.6 kW

question: A reactor of volume 1.5 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 1.4 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 1.5, Q = 1.4 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 1.5 / 1.4 | Answer: 1.071 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 3.8e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 3 mm with a concentration difference of 50 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 3.8, L = 3, dC = 50 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (3.8e-9)*50 / (3e-3) | Answer: 63.33 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 7.4 min and steady-state gain 3.4. For a step input of magnitude 6, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 7.4, K = 3.4, M = 6 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 3.4 * 6 | Answer: 20.4 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 40 m^2 flies at 220 m/s (air density 1.225 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.6. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 40, V = 220, rho = 1.225, CL = 0.6 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1.225*(220)^2*40*0.6 / 1000 | Answer: 711.5 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 50 m^2 flies at 190 m/s (density 0.4 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.11. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 50, V = 190, rho = 0.4, CD = 0.11 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.4*(190)^2*50*0.11 / 1000 | Answer: 39.71 kN

question: A specimen under stress 320 MPa shows an elastic strain of 3e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 320, eps = 3 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 320 / (3e-3) MPa = 106.7 GPa | Answer: 106.7 GPa

question: A block of mass 24 kg has a volume of 1.9e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 24, V = 1.9 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 24 / (1.9e-3) | Answer: 12632 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 2500 mm is heated through 40 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 12e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 2500, dT = 40, al = 12 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 2500*12e-6*40 | Answer: 1.2 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 190 ohm, R2 = 175 ohm and R3 = 225 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 190, R2 = 175, R3 = 225 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 175*225 / 190 | Answer: 207.2 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 1000 ohm and gauge factor 2 experiences a strain of 1800e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 1000, GF = 2, eps = 1800 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 1000*2*1800e-6 | Answer: 3600 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 9.17 when the true value is 20. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.17, true = 20 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.17 - 20| / 20 * 100 | Answer: 54.15 %

question: Annual demand is 46500 units, ordering cost 30 per order and holding cost 32 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 46500, S = 30, H = 32 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*46500*30 / 32) | Answer: 295.3 units

question: An asset costs 220000 with salvage value 26000 after 17 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 220000, Sv = 26000, n = 17 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (220000 - 26000) / 17 | Answer: 11412 per year

question: A product sells for 190 per unit with variable cost 30 per unit and fixed costs 130000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 190, V = 30, F = 130000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 130000 / (190 - 30) | Answer: 812.5 units

question: Find the present worth of 15000 received 2 years from now at an interest rate of 11% per year.
solution: Given: F = 15000, n = 2, i = 11 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 15000 / (1 + 0.11)^2 | Answer: 12174 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.95, 0.97 and 0.95 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.95, r2 = 0.97, r3 = 0.95 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.95*0.97*0.95 | Answer: 0.8754

question: A process produces 39 defective items in a batch of 6500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 39, N = 6500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 39/6500 * 1e6 | Answer: 6000 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -5x^3 - 8x^2 + 8x + 9 evaluated at x = 3.
For f(x) = 5x^3 - 4x^2 + 9x + 2, find f''(x) at x = -5.
Evaluate the definite integral of (3x^2 + 3x + 7) dx from x = -3 to x = 3.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = 3x^3/3 + 3x^2/2 + 7x | Evaluate F(3) - F(-3) | Answer: 96

question: Find the larger real root of 2x^2 + 2x - 2 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[8, 4], [-9, -3]].
solution: Given: a = 8, b = 4, c = -9, d = -3 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (8)(-3) - (4)(-9) | Answer: 12

question: Find the determinant of [[5, -1, -4], [5, 6, 2], [1, 6, 5]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: 17

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[7, 0], [8, -6]].
solution: Trace tr = 1, Determinant = -42 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 7

question: Solve for x: 0x + 6y = 7 and 2x + 2y = 0.
solution: Determinant = 0*2 - 6*2 = -12 | x = (e d - b f) / det = -1.167 | Answer: x = -1.167
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 66, 52, 3, 62, 20.
solution: Sum = 203 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 40.6 | Answer: 40.6

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 29, 40, 46, 8, 32.
solution: Mean = 31 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 14.49

question: Find the slope of the line through (-1, -5) and (1, 8).
solution: Given: x1 = -1, y1 = -5, x2 = 1, y2 = 8 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (8 - -5) / (1 - -1) | Answer: 6.5

question: Find the distance between the points (-9, -5) and (-5, 9).
solution: Given: x1 = -9, y1 = -5, x2 = -5, y2 = 9 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((4)^2 + (14)^2) | Answer: 14.56 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (2,-1), (-3,7), (5,3).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 22 sq units

question: Find the 17th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -9 and common difference -9.
solution: Given: a = -9, d = -9, n = 17 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -9 + (17 - 1)*-9 | Answer: -153

question: Find the sum of the first 35 terms of an AP with first term 2 and common difference -3.
solution: Given: a = 2, d = -3, n = 35 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 35/2 [2*2 + (35-1)*-3] | Answer: -1715

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 4500 at 5% per annum for 2 years.
solution: Given: P = 4500, R = 5, Tt = 2 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 4500 * 5 * 2 / 100 | Answer: 450 currency units

question: Find the amount when 6000 is invested at 9.2% per annum compounded annually for 5 years.
solution: Given: P = 6000, R = 9.2, Tt = 5 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 6000 * (1 + 9.2/100)^5 | Answer: 9317 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (5, 6, 3) and (4, 4, 1).
solution: Given: a1 = 5, a2 = 6, a3 = 3, b1 = 4, b2 = 4, b3 = 1 | Formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3 | Substitute: = (5)(4) + (6)(4) + (3)(1) | Answer: 47
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (-4, -5, -4) and (-4, -1, 6).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 54.88

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (-4, 1, -4) and (-3, 4, -4).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 29.55 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number -6 + -10i.
solution: Given: a = -6, b = -10 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((-6)^2 + (-10)^2) | Answer: 11.66

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number 9 + 0i.
solution: Given: a = 9, b = 0 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(0, 9) | Answer: 0 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -3x^3 - 4x^2 + 7x - 4 at x = 4.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-90 with initial guess x0=14, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.2 and ordinates 16, 8, 17, 3, 9, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 348 and 371.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 348 and 371 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 9 and 45.
solution: Given: a = 9, b = 45 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 9*45 / 9 | Answer: 45
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 45 mm carries an axial tensile load of 113 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 40 mm and length 1900 mm carries an axial load of 51 kN. Take E = 110 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 68 mm transmits a torque of 2650 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 68, Tt = 2650 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(2650*1000) / (pi*(68)^3) | Answer: 42.92 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 58 mm and length 1900 mm carries a torque of 1000 N-m. With G = 77 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (58)^4 / 32 = 1110994 mm^4 | theta = (1000*1000)(1900) / (77000 * 1110994) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 1.273 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 65 mm wide and 160 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 65, h = 160 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 65*(160)^2 / 6 | Answer: 277333 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (78 mm x 140 mm) carries a bending moment of 37 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (63 mm x 110 mm) has effective length 4000 mm and E = 200 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 710 MPa is designed for a working stress of 110 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 710, sw = 110 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 710 / 110 | Answer: 6.455

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1300 mm and wall thickness 20 mm carries an internal pressure of 1.9 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1300, t = 20, P = 1.9 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 1.9*1300 / (2*20) | Answer: 61.75 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 680 K and 430 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 680, Tc = 430 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 430/680) * 100 | Answer: 36.76 %

question: A refrigerator works between 255 K (cold) and 328 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 255, Th = 328 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 255 / (328 - 255) | Answer: 3.493

question: 3.7 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 55 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.7, dT = 55 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 3.7 * 0.718 * 55 | Answer: 146.1 kJ

question: 6.6 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 35 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 6.6, dT = 35 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 6.6 * 1.005 * 35 | Answer: 232.2 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 3.1 m^3 at 490 K with mass 3.9 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 3.1, Tk = 490, m = 3.9 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 3.9*0.287*490 / 3.1 | Answer: 176.9 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 4.6 kg of air expands isothermally at 490 K from volume V1 to 2*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.6, Tk = 490, ratio = 2 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 4.6*0.287*490*ln(2) | Answer: 448.4 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 2.7 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.08 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 2.7, D = 0.08 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*2.7*0.08 / 0.001 | Answer: 216000

question: Water flows at 1.9 m/s through a pipe of diameter 90 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 3.4 m. Taking Cv = 0.96, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 3.4, cv = 0.96 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.96*sqrt(2*9.81*3.4) | Answer: 7.841 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 160 mm) water flows at 2.6 m/s. It contracts to diameter 60 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 160, d2 = 60, V1 = 2.6 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 2.6*(160/60)^2 | Answer: 18.49 m/s

question: Water flows at 2.2 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.37 m and length 170 m. With friction factor f = 0.023, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 28 teeth drives a gear of 51 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1200 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 28, z2 = 51, N1 = 1200 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1200*28 / 51 | Answer: 658.8 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 430 mm rotates at 600 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 430, N = 600 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.43)*600 / 60 | Answer: 13.51 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 24.8 kW at 300 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 24.8, N = 300 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(24.8*1000) / (2*pi*300) | Answer: 789.4 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 6.5 kg rotates at radius 0.48 m at 1100 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 8800 N/m and mass 9.7 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 8800, m = 9.7 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(8800/9.7) | Answer: 4.794 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 7.3 m^2 and thickness 0.21 m has conductivity k = 34.6 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 190 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 7.3, L = 0.21, k = 34.6, dT = 190 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 34.6*7.3*190 / 0.21 | Answer: 228525 W

question: A surface of area 2.6 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 170 W/m^2-K to surroundings 145 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 2.6, h = 170, dT = 145 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 170*2.6*145 | Answer: 64090 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 110 m/min, feed = 0.43 mm/rev, depth of cut = 0.9 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 110, f = 0.43, d = 0.9 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*110*0.43*0.9 | Answer: 42570 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 300 mm is turned at 850 rpm with a feed of 0.21 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 300, N = 850, f = 0.21 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 300 / (0.21*850) | Answer: 1.681 min

question: A resistor of 128 ohm carries a current of 5 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 128, I = 5 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 5 * 128 | Answer: 640 V

question: Three resistors 12 ohm, 16 ohm and 87 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 12, R2 = 16, R3 = 87 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 12 + 16 + 87 | Answer: 115 ohm

question: Two resistors 86 ohm and 26 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 86, R2 = 26 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 86*26 / (86+26) | Answer: 19.96 ohm

question: A device draws 11.8 A at 225 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 225, I = 11.8 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 225 * 11.8 | Answer: 2655 W

question: A current of 6.6 A flows through a 58 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 6.6, R = 58 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (6.6)^2 * 58 | Answer: 2526 W

question: Two capacitors 30 uF and 11.7 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 30, C2 = 11.7 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 30*11.7 / (30+11.7) | Answer: 8.417 uF

question: A resistor 56 kohm and capacitor 14.7 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 56, C = 14.7 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (56k)(14.7u) = 823.2 ms | Answer: 823.2 ms

question: An inductor 198 mH is in series with 90 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 198, R = 90 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (198e-3) / 90 | Answer: 2.2 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 86 mH inductor at 820 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 86, f = 820 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (820)(86e-3) | Answer: 443.1 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 6.2 uF capacitor at 220 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 6.2, f = 220 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (220)(6.2e-6)) | Answer: 116.7 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 21 ohm, XL = 86 ohm and XC = 103 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 21, XL = 86, XC = 103 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(21^2 + (86 - 103)^2) | Answer: 27.02 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 5.1 mH and C = 5.1 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 5.1, C = 5.1 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(5.1e-3 * 5.1e-6)) | Answer: 986.8 Hz

question: A capacitor of 17.8 uF is charged to 35 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 17.8, V = 35 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*17.8e-6*(35)^2 | Answer: 10.9 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 120 V with 540 primary turns and 70 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 120, N1 = 540, N2 = 70 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 120 * 70/540 | Answer: 15.56 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 320 V and draws an armature current of 23 A. If the armature resistance is 0.25 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 320, Ia = 23, Ra = 0.25 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 320 - 23*0.25 | Answer: 314.2 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 200 A at 415 V (line) with a power factor of 0.83. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 200, VL = 415, pf = 0.83 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*415*200*0.83 / 1000 | Answer: 119.3 kW

question: A load has real power 95 kW and apparent power 175 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 95, S = 175 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 95 / 175 | Answer: 0.5429

question: A machine delivers 85 kW output while drawing 182 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 85, Pi = 182 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 85/182 * 100 | Answer: 46.7 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 10 V across R1 = 36 ohm and R2 = 25 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 10, R1 = 36, R2 = 25 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 10*25 / (36+25) | Answer: 4.098 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 20 kohm and Rin = 36 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 20, Rin = 36 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 20 / 36 | Answer: 0.5556

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 100 kohm and Rg = 36 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 100, Rg = 36 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 100/36 | Answer: 3.778

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 6333. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 6333 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(6333) | Answer: 38.02 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 5.5 m carries a central point load of 80 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.5, W = 80 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 80*5.5 / 4 | Answer: 110 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 5 m carries a UDL of 55 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5, w = 55 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 55*(5)^2 / 8 | Answer: 171.9 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 5.5 m carries a point load 70 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.5, W = 70 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 70*5.5 | Answer: 385 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 1.5 m carries a UDL of 32 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 1.5, w = 32 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 32*(1.5)^2 / 2 | Answer: 36 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.7 m carries a point load 25 kN at distance 1.1 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 6.7, a = 1.1, W = 25 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 25*(6.7 - 1.1) / 6.7 | Answer: 20.9 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 4 m) carries a central point load 75 kN. With E = 200 GPa and I = 380e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=75000 N, L=4000.0 mm, E=200000 MPa, I=380e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 1.316 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 5 m carries a UDL of 9 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5, w = 9 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 9*(5)^2 / 12 | Answer: 18.75 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 400 mm, clear cover 30 mm and main bars of diameter 12 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 400, c = 30, dia = 12 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 400 - 30 - 12/2 | Answer: 364 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 28.8 m^2 carrying a factored load of 17.2 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 28.8, w = 17.2 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 17.2 * 28.8 | Answer: 495.4 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 6.3 m, unit weight 16 kN/m^3, phi = 36 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 2.7e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.5, area = 4.5e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 2.7, i = 0.5, A = 4.5 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (2.7e-4)*0.5*(4.5e-3) | Answer: 607.5 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 2.5 m, bed slope 0.005 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.016. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 2.2 m under a head of 0.7 m. Taking Cd = 0.62 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 2.8 m wide carries a discharge of 20 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 430 m and design speed 80 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 430, V = 80 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (80)^2 / (127*430) | Answer: 0.1172
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: A tank of volume 700 m^3 treats a flow of 125 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 700, Q = 125 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 700 / 125 | Answer: 5.6 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 290 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.16 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 6 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 290, k = 0.16, t = 6 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 290*(1 - e^(-0.16*6)) | Answer: 179 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.86, rainfall intensity 75 mm/h over a catchment of 16.7 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.86, i = 75, A = 16.7 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.86*75*16.7 / 360 | Answer: 2.992 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.03 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 440 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.03, M = 440 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 440*(20+0.03)/20 | Answer: 440.7 m

question: Convert the decimal number 207 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 207 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: CF (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 10001100 and 01100110.
solution: XOR: 11101010 | Count of 1s = 5 | Answer: 5
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 90 megabits is sent over a link of 66 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 90, B = 66 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 90 / 66 | Answer: 1.364 s

question: A link has bandwidth 89 Mbps and round-trip time 20 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 89, R = 20 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 89e6 * 20e-3 bits = 1780 kb | Answer: 1780 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.87, cache access time 8 ns and main-memory access time 140 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.87, tc = 8, tm = 140 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.87*8 + (1 - 0.87)*140 | Answer: 25.16 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 749009 elements?
solution: Given: n = 749009 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(749009)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: An O(n^2) algorithm performs c*n^2 basic operations. If c = 1 and n = 2900, how many operations are performed?
solution: Given: n = 2900 | Formula: operations = n^2 | Substitute: = (2900)^2 | Answer: 8410000

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.013, memory access time 190 ns and page-fault service time 7 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 7 ms = 7000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.013)*190 + 0.013*7000000.0 ns | Answer: 91.19 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 0.9 m^3 at 220 kPa and 390 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 0.9, P = 220, Tk = 390 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (220e3)*0.9 / (8.314*390) | Answer: 61.06 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.19 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 17 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.19, t = 17 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.19*17) | Answer: 0.9604

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.44 /min) reaches 90% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.44, X = 90 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.9 / (0.44*(1 - 0.9)) | Answer: 20.45 min

question: For a reaction with A = 4e10 /s and activation energy 65 kJ/mol at 360 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 4, Ea = 65, Tk = 360 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 4e10 * exp(-65e3 / (8.314*360)) | Answer: 14.81 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.97 and bottoms xW = 0.1, with relative volatility alpha = 2.5. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.97, xw = 0.1, al = 2.5 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.97/0.03)(0.9/0.1)] / ln(2.5) | Answer: 6.192 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.9 and x = 0.45. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.9, x = 0.45 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.9/0.1) / (0.45/0.55) | Answer: 11

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.45 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 95 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.45, Psat = 95 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.45 * 95 | Answer: 42.75 kPa

question: A stream of 8.1 kg/s with specific heat 1.9 kJ/kg-K is heated through 40 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 8.1, cp = 1.9, dT = 40 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 8.1*1.9*40 | Answer: 615.6 kW

question: A reactor of volume 9.8 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 1 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 9.8, Q = 1 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 9.8 / 1 | Answer: 9.8 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 7.4e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 2 mm with a concentration difference of 80 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 7.4, L = 2, dC = 80 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (7.4e-9)*80 / (2e-3) | Answer: 296 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 3.8 min and steady-state gain 3.3. For a step input of magnitude 4, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 3.8, K = 3.3, M = 4 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 3.3 * 4 | Answer: 13.2 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 65 m^2 flies at 110 m/s (air density 0.7 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 1. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 65, V = 110, rho = 0.7, CL = 1 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.7*(110)^2*65*1 / 1000 | Answer: 275.3 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 90 m^2 flies at 260 m/s (density 0.7 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.03. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 90, V = 260, rho = 0.7, CD = 0.03 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.7*(260)^2*90*0.03 / 1000 | Answer: 63.88 kN

question: A specimen under stress 180 MPa shows an elastic strain of 0.9e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 180, eps = 0.9 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 180 / (0.9e-3) MPa = 200 GPa | Answer: 200 GPa

question: A block of mass 34 kg has a volume of 1.8e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 34, V = 1.8 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 34 / (1.8e-3) | Answer: 18889 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 500 mm is heated through 115 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 12e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 500, dT = 115, al = 12 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 500*12e-6*115 | Answer: 0.69 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 145 ohm, R2 = 100 ohm and R3 = 150 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 145, R2 = 100, R3 = 150 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 100*150 / 145 | Answer: 103.4 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 350 ohm and gauge factor 2.2 experiences a strain of 350e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 350, GF = 2.2, eps = 350 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 350*2.2*350e-6 | Answer: 269.5 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 10.46 when the true value is 50. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10.46, true = 50 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10.46 - 50| / 50 * 100 | Answer: 79.08 %

question: Annual demand is 13500 units, ordering cost 80 per order and holding cost 17 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 13500, S = 80, H = 17 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*13500*80 / 17) | Answer: 356.5 units

question: An asset costs 390000 with salvage value 6000 after 10 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 390000, Sv = 6000, n = 10 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (390000 - 6000) / 10 | Answer: 38400 per year

question: A product sells for 390 per unit with variable cost 120 per unit and fixed costs 130000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 390, V = 120, F = 130000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 130000 / (390 - 120) | Answer: 481.5 units

question: Find the present worth of 145000 received 8 years from now at an interest rate of 7% per year.
solution: Given: F = 145000, n = 8, i = 7 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 145000 / (1 + 0.07)^8 | Answer: 84391 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.93, 0.93 and 0.9 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.93, r2 = 0.93, r3 = 0.9 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.93*0.93*0.9 | Answer: 0.7784

question: A process produces 3 defective items in a batch of 2000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).

question: Find the distance between the points (5, 4) and (-8, -3).
solution: Given: x1 = 5, y1 = 4, x2 = -8, y2 = -3 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-13)^2 + (-7)^2) | Answer: 14.76 units

solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 21 sq units

question: Find the 20th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -8 and common difference -3.
solution: Given: a = -8, d = -3, n = 20 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -8 + (20 - 1)*-3 | Answer: -65

question: Find the sum of the first 18 terms of an AP with first term -12 and common difference 4.
solution: Given: a = -12, d = 4, n = 18 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 18/2 [2*-12 + (18-1)*4] | Answer: 396

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 11000 at 9.2% per annum for 6 years.
solution: Given: P = 11000, R = 9.2, Tt = 6 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 11000 * 9.2 * 6 / 100 | Answer: 6072 currency units

question: Find the amount when 15500 is invested at 10.9% per annum compounded annually for 4 years.
solution: Given: P = 15500, R = 10.9, Tt = 4 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 15500 * (1 + 10.9/100)^4 | Answer: 23445 currency units

question: Find the modulus of the complex number -10 + -5i.
solution: Given: a = -10, b = -5 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((-10)^2 + (-5)^2) | Answer: 11.18

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number 5 + -6i.
solution: Given: a = 5, b = -6 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(-6, 5) | Answer: -50.19 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = 3x^3 + x^2 + 2x - 3 at x = 2.
solution: Given: a = 3, b = 1, c = 2, d = -3, x0 = 2 | Formula: f(x0) = a x0^3 + b x0^2 + c x0 + d | Substitute: f(2) = 3(2)^3 + 1(2)^2 + 2(2) + -3 | Answer: 29

question: Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-188 with initial guess x0=5, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.7 and ordinates 11, 3, 19, 15, 1, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 261 and 358.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 261 and 358 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 39 and 24.
solution: Given: a = 39, b = 24 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 39*24 / 3 | Answer: 312
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 24 mm carries an axial tensile load of 48 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 20 mm and length 2400 mm carries an axial load of 27 kN. Take E = 210 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 32 mm transmits a torque of 2950 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 32, Tt = 2950 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(2950*1000) / (pi*(32)^3) | Answer: 458.5 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 45 mm and length 1300 mm carries a torque of 200 N-m. With G = 77 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (45)^4 / 32 = 402578 mm^4 | theta = (200*1000)(1300) / (77000 * 402578) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 0.4806 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 89 mm wide and 120 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 89, h = 120 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 89*(120)^2 / 6 | Answer: 213600 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (53 mm x 200 mm) carries a bending moment of 35 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (47 mm x 100 mm) has effective length 1500 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 880 MPa is designed for a working stress of 80 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 880, sw = 80 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 880 / 80 | Answer: 11

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 550 mm and wall thickness 8 mm carries an internal pressure of 1.2 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 550, t = 8, P = 1.2 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 1.2*550 / (2*8) | Answer: 41.25 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 840 K and 280 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 840, Tc = 280 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 280/840) * 100 | Answer: 66.67 %

question: A refrigerator works between 268 K (cold) and 302 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 268, Th = 302 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 268 / (302 - 268) | Answer: 7.882

question: A heat pump operates between 264 K and 334 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 264, Th = 334 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 334 / (334 - 264) | Answer: 4.771

question: 4.7 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 30 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.7, dT = 30 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 4.7 * 0.718 * 30 | Answer: 101.2 kJ

question: 1 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 70 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1, dT = 70 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 1 * 1.005 * 70 | Answer: 70.35 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 1.6 m^3 at 310 K with mass 3.5 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 1.6, Tk = 310, m = 3.5 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 3.5*0.287*310 / 1.6 | Answer: 194.6 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 1.2 kg of air expands isothermally at 420 K from volume V1 to 3*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1.2, Tk = 420, ratio = 3 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 1.2*0.287*420*ln(3) | Answer: 158.9 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 1.4 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.37 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 1.4, D = 0.37 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*1.4*0.37 / 0.001 | Answer: 518000

question: Water flows at 2.4 m/s through a pipe of diameter 280 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 16.5 m. Taking Cv = 0.96, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 16.5, cv = 0.96 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.96*sqrt(2*9.81*16.5) | Answer: 17.27 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 360 mm) water flows at 2.3 m/s. It contracts to diameter 70 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 360, d2 = 70, V1 = 2.3 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 2.3*(360/70)^2 | Answer: 60.83 m/s

question: Water flows at 1.4 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.44 m and length 250 m. With friction factor f = 0.028, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 36 teeth drives a gear of 74 teeth. If the pinion runs at 450 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 36, z2 = 74, N1 = 450 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 450*36 / 74 | Answer: 218.9 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 270 mm rotates at 1100 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 270, N = 1100 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.27)*1100 / 60 | Answer: 15.55 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 29.5 kW at 1350 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 29.5, N = 1350 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(29.5*1000) / (2*pi*1350) | Answer: 208.7 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 1.6 kg rotates at radius 0.36 m at 550 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 16100 N/m and mass 16.7 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 16100, m = 16.7 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(16100/16.7) | Answer: 4.942 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 6.9 m^2 and thickness 0.39 m has conductivity k = 30.5 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 160 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 6.9, L = 0.39, k = 30.5, dT = 160 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 30.5*6.9*160 / 0.39 | Answer: 86338 W

question: A surface of area 5.8 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 15 W/m^2-K to surroundings 25 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.

question: In turning, cutting speed = 240 m/min, feed = 0.21 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2.8 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.

question: A workpiece of length 250 mm is turned at 300 rpm with a feed of 0.19 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 250, N = 300, f = 0.19 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 250 / (0.19*300) | Answer: 4.386 min

question: A resistor of 26 ohm carries a current of 6.4 A. Find the voltage across it.

question: Three resistors 94 ohm, 66 ohm and 56 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 94, R2 = 66, R3 = 56 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 94 + 66 + 56 | Answer: 216 ohm

question: Two resistors 71 ohm and 51 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 71, R2 = 51 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 71*51 / (71+51) | Answer: 29.68 ohm

question: A device draws 11.8 A at 160 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 160, I = 11.8 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 160 * 11.8 | Answer: 1888 W

question: A current of 7.1 A flows through a 94 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 7.1, R = 94 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (7.1)^2 * 94 | Answer: 4739 W

question: Two capacitors 2.3 uF and 37 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 2.3, C2 = 37 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 2.3*37 / (2.3+37) | Answer: 2.165 uF

question: A resistor 20 kohm and capacitor 8.7 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 20, C = 8.7 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (20k)(8.7u) = 174 ms | Answer: 174 ms

question: An inductor 407.5 mH is in series with 5 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 407.5, R = 5 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (407.5e-3) / 5 | Answer: 81.5 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 163.8 mH inductor at 430 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 163.8, f = 430 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (430)(163.8e-3) | Answer: 442.5 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 20.7 uF capacitor at 740 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 20.7, f = 740 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (740)(20.7e-6)) | Answer: 10.39 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 20 ohm, XL = 108 ohm and XC = 71 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 20, XL = 108, XC = 71 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(20^2 + (108 - 71)^2) | Answer: 42.06 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 1.2 mH and C = 9.6 uF (in Hz).

question: A capacitor of 62.6 uF is charged to 360 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 62.6, V = 360 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*62.6e-6*(360)^2 | Answer: 4056 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 390 V with 900 primary turns and 420 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 390, N1 = 900, N2 = 420 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 390 * 420/900 | Answer: 182 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 430 V and draws an armature current of 60 A. If the armature resistance is 0.16 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 430, Ia = 60, Ra = 0.16 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 430 - 60*0.16 | Answer: 420.4 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 40 A at 433 V (line) with a power factor of 0.97. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 40, VL = 433, pf = 0.97 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*433*40*0.97 / 1000 | Answer: 29.1 kW

question: A load has real power 60 kW and apparent power 160 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 60, S = 160 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 60 / 160 | Answer: 0.375

question: A machine delivers 145 kW output while drawing 182 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 145, Pi = 182 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 145/182 * 100 | Answer: 79.67 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 17 V across R1 = 42 ohm and R2 = 22 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 17, R1 = 42, R2 = 22 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 17*22 / (42+22) | Answer: 5.844 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 220 kohm and Rin = 28 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 220, Rin = 28 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 220 / 28 | Answer: 7.857

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 40 kohm and Rg = 33 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 40, Rg = 33 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 40/33 | Answer: 2.212

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 2821. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 2821 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(2821) | Answer: 34.5 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.3 m carries a central point load of 40 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 9.3, W = 40 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 40*9.3 / 4 | Answer: 93 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.2 m carries a UDL of 45 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 9.2, w = 45 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 45*(9.2)^2 / 8 | Answer: 476.1 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 1.7 m carries a point load 5 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 1.7, W = 5 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 5*1.7 | Answer: 8.5 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 3 m carries a UDL of 36 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3, w = 36 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 36*(3)^2 / 2 | Answer: 162 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 5.3 m carries a point load 60 kN at distance 2.3 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 5.3, a = 2.3, W = 60 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 60*(5.3 - 2.3) / 5.3 | Answer: 33.96 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 6 m) carries a central point load 70 kN. With E = 200 GPa and I = 460e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=70000 N, L=6000.0 mm, E=200000 MPa, I=460e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 3.424 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 6.7 m carries a UDL of 36 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6.7, w = 36 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 36*(6.7)^2 / 12 | Answer: 134.7 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 590 mm, clear cover 30 mm and main bars of diameter 12 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 590, c = 30, dia = 12 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 590 - 30 - 12/2 | Answer: 554 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 39.1 m^2 carrying a factored load of 19.5 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 39.1, w = 19.5 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 19.5 * 39.1 | Answer: 762.5 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 4.8 m, unit weight 16 kN/m^3, phi = 37 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 3.6e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.3, area = 3.6e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 3.6, i = 0.3, A = 3.6 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (3.6e-4)*0.3*(3.6e-3) | Answer: 388.8 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 2.3 m, bed slope 0.001 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.016. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 5 m under a head of 1.1 m. Taking Cd = 0.61 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 4.2 m wide carries a discharge of 11.5 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).

solution: Given: R = 350, V = 60 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (60)^2 / (127*350) | Answer: 0.08099
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: A tank of volume 870 m^3 treats a flow of 170 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 870, Q = 170 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 870 / 170 | Answer: 5.118 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 180 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.12 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 6 days.

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.71, rainfall intensity 55 mm/h over a catchment of 57.3 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
