question: Find the sum of the first 38 terms of an AP with first term -3 and common difference 7.
solution: Given: a = -3, d = 7, n = 38 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 38/2 [2*-3 + (38-1)*7] | Answer: 4807

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 18000 at 13.3% per annum for 10 years.
solution: Given: P = 18000, R = 13.3, Tt = 10 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 18000 * 13.3 * 10 / 100 | Answer: 23940 currency units

question: Find the amount when 18500 is invested at 11.3% per annum compounded annually for 2 years.
solution: Given: P = 18500, R = 11.3, Tt = 2 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 18500 * (1 + 11.3/100)^2 | Answer: 22917 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (-6, 5, -7) and (1, -1, 4).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (-1, -1, 5) and (-5, -2, 4).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 22.05

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (1, 6, -5) and (0, -3, 1).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 157.5 degrees

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number -9 + 6i.
solution: Given: a = -9, b = 6 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(6, -9) | Answer: 146.3 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -3x^3 - 7x^2 - 6 at x = -3.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-96 with initial guess x0=6, find x1 (one iteration).
solution: Given: N = 96, x0 = 6 | Formula: x1 = x0 - (x0^2 - N)/(2 x0) | Substitute: x1 = 6 - ((6)^2 - 96)/(2*6) | Answer: 11

question: Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.1 and ordinates 19, 20, 7, 11, 0, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 492 and 183.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 492 and 183 | Answer: GCD = 3

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 44 and 8.
solution: Given: a = 44, b = 8 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 44*8 / 4 | Answer: 88
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 19 mm carries an axial tensile load of 46 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 17 mm and length 2300 mm carries an axial load of 76 kN. Take E = 210 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 65 mm transmits a torque of 250 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 65, Tt = 250 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(250*1000) / (pi*(65)^3) | Answer: 4.636 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 35 mm and length 1700 mm carries a torque of 700 N-m. With G = 77 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (35)^4 / 32 = 147324 mm^4 | theta = (700*1000)(1700) / (77000 * 147324) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 6.01 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 44 mm wide and 70 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 44, h = 70 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 44*(70)^2 / 6 | Answer: 35933 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (56 mm x 190 mm) carries a bending moment of 6 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (78 mm x 110 mm) has effective length 3300 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 400 MPa is designed for a working stress of 250 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 400, sw = 250 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 400 / 250 | Answer: 1.6

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 950 mm and wall thickness 19 mm carries an internal pressure of 2.6 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 950, t = 19, P = 2.6 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 2.6*950 / (2*19) | Answer: 65 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 1060 K and 330 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 1060, Tc = 330 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 330/1060) * 100 | Answer: 68.87 %

question: A refrigerator works between 252 K (cold) and 302 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 252, Th = 302 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 252 / (302 - 252) | Answer: 5.04

question: A heat pump operates between 266 K and 328 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 266, Th = 328 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 328 / (328 - 266) | Answer: 5.29

question: 6.5 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 130 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 6.5, dT = 130 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 6.5 * 0.718 * 130 | Answer: 606.7 kJ

question: 2.7 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 125 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.7, dT = 125 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 2.7 * 1.005 * 125 | Answer: 339.2 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 3.1 m^3 at 600 K with mass 2.1 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 3.1, Tk = 600, m = 2.1 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 2.1*0.287*600 / 3.1 | Answer: 116.7 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 1.4 kg of air expands isothermally at 360 K from volume V1 to 2*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1.4, Tk = 360, ratio = 2 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 1.4*0.287*360*ln(2) | Answer: 100.3 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 3.2 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.21 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 3.2, D = 0.21 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*3.2*0.21 / 0.001 | Answer: 672000

question: Water flows at 3.1 m/s through a pipe of diameter 200 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 14.7 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 14.7 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*14.7 / 1000 | Answer: 144.2 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 19 m. Taking Cv = 0.96, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 19, cv = 0.96 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.96*sqrt(2*9.81*19) | Answer: 18.54 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 260 mm) water flows at 1.2 m/s. It contracts to diameter 70 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 260, d2 = 70, V1 = 1.2 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 1.2*(260/70)^2 | Answer: 16.56 m/s

question: Water flows at 3.8 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.24 m and length 340 m. With friction factor f = 0.035, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 31 teeth drives a gear of 73 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1350 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 31, z2 = 73, N1 = 1350 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1350*31 / 73 | Answer: 573.3 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 510 mm rotates at 600 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 510, N = 600 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.51)*600 / 60 | Answer: 16.02 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 19.7 kW at 750 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 19.7, N = 750 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(19.7*1000) / (2*pi*750) | Answer: 250.8 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 9.4 kg rotates at radius 0.19 m at 300 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 17000 N/m and mass 14.3 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 17000, m = 14.3 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(17000/14.3) | Answer: 5.488 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 9.8 m^2 and thickness 0.12 m has conductivity k = 13.5 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 70 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 9.8, L = 0.12, k = 13.5, dT = 70 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 13.5*9.8*70 / 0.12 | Answer: 77175 W

question: A surface of area 5.1 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 130 W/m^2-K to surroundings 20 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 5.1, h = 130, dT = 20 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 130*5.1*20 | Answer: 13260 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 190 m/min, feed = 0.15 mm/rev, depth of cut = 0.7 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 190, f = 0.15, d = 0.7 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*190*0.15*0.7 | Answer: 19950 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 460 mm is turned at 700 rpm with a feed of 0.32 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 460, N = 700, f = 0.32 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 460 / (0.32*700) | Answer: 2.054 min

question: A resistor of 151 ohm carries a current of 9.4 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 151, I = 9.4 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 9.4 * 151 | Answer: 1419 V

question: Three resistors 96 ohm, 66 ohm and 16 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 96, R2 = 66, R3 = 16 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 96 + 66 + 16 | Answer: 178 ohm

question: Two resistors 56 ohm and 4 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 56, R2 = 4 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 56*4 / (56+4) | Answer: 3.733 ohm

question: A device draws 1.4 A at 135 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 135, I = 1.4 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 135 * 1.4 | Answer: 189 W

question: A current of 2.5 A flows through a 67 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 2.5, R = 67 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (2.5)^2 * 67 | Answer: 418.8 W

question: Two capacitors 19.9 uF and 32.9 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 19.9, C2 = 32.9 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 19.9*32.9 / (19.9+32.9) | Answer: 12.4 uF

question: A resistor 63 kohm and capacitor 19.5 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 63, C = 19.5 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (63k)(19.5u) = 1228 ms | Answer: 1228 ms

question: An inductor 397.1 mH is in series with 26 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 397.1, R = 26 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (397.1e-3) / 26 | Answer: 15.27 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 57.7 mH inductor at 220 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 57.7, f = 220 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (220)(57.7e-3) | Answer: 79.76 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 33.4 uF capacitor at 450 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 33.4, f = 450 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (450)(33.4e-6)) | Answer: 10.59 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 65 ohm, XL = 126 ohm and XC = 71 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 65, XL = 126, XC = 71 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(65^2 + (126 - 71)^2) | Answer: 85.15 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 54.7 mH and C = 7.6 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 54.7, C = 7.6 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(54.7e-3 * 7.6e-6)) | Answer: 246.8 Hz

question: A capacitor of 9.5 uF is charged to 50 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 9.5, V = 50 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*9.5e-6*(50)^2 | Answer: 11.87 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 190 V with 660 primary turns and 500 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 190, N1 = 660, N2 = 500 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 190 * 500/660 | Answer: 143.9 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 390 V and draws an armature current of 5 A. If the armature resistance is 0.85 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 390, Ia = 5, Ra = 0.85 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 390 - 5*0.85 | Answer: 385.8 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 70 A at 415 V (line) with a power factor of 0.75. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 70, VL = 415, pf = 0.75 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*415*70*0.75 / 1000 | Answer: 37.74 kW

question: A load has real power 10 kW and apparent power 30 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 10, S = 30 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 10 / 30 | Answer: 0.3333

question: A machine delivers 55 kW output while drawing 112 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 55, Pi = 112 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 55/112 * 100 | Answer: 49.11 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 5 V across R1 = 47 ohm and R2 = 19 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 5, R1 = 47, R2 = 19 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 5*19 / (47+19) | Answer: 1.439 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 190 kohm and Rin = 6 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 190, Rin = 6 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 190 / 6 | Answer: 31.67

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 90 kohm and Rg = 33 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 90, Rg = 33 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 90/33 | Answer: 3.727

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 432. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 432 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(432) | Answer: 26.35 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.5 m carries a central point load of 85 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 9.5, W = 85 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 85*9.5 / 4 | Answer: 201.9 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 7.6 m carries a UDL of 35 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7.6, w = 35 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 35*(7.6)^2 / 8 | Answer: 252.7 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 3.1 m carries a point load 25 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.1, W = 25 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 25*3.1 | Answer: 77.5 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 2 m carries a UDL of 34 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 2, w = 34 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 34*(2)^2 / 2 | Answer: 68 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.1 m carries a point load 30 kN at distance 3.6 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 9.1, a = 3.6, W = 30 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 30*(9.1 - 3.6) / 9.1 | Answer: 18.13 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 7.4 m) carries a central point load 60 kN. With E = 25 GPa and I = 600e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=60000 N, L=7400.0 mm, E=25000 MPa, I=600e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 33.77 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 4.1 m carries a UDL of 27 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.1, w = 27 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 27*(4.1)^2 / 12 | Answer: 37.82 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 320 mm, clear cover 45 mm and main bars of diameter 25 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 320, c = 45, dia = 25 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 320 - 45 - 25/2 | Answer: 262.5 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 37.2 m^2 carrying a factored load of 17 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 37.2, w = 17 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 17 * 37.2 | Answer: 632.4 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 6.8 m, unit weight 17 kN/m^3, phi = 30 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 12 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 18 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 12, g = 18 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (18 - 9.81)*12 | Answer: 98.28 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 2.4e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1.4, area = 7.1e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 2.4, i = 1.4, A = 7.1 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (2.4e-4)*1.4*(7.1e-3) | Answer: 2386 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.3 m, bed slope 0.002 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.026. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 4.3 m under a head of 1.2 m. Taking Cd = 0.61 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 3.2 m wide carries a discharge of 25.1 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 100 m and design speed 45 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 100, V = 45 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (45)^2 / (127*100) | Answer: 0.1594
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: A tank of volume 600 m^3 treats a flow of 65 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 600, Q = 65 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 600 / 65 | Answer: 9.231 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 270 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.21 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 3 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 270, k = 0.21, t = 3 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 270*(1 - e^(-0.21*3)) | Answer: 126.2 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.42, rainfall intensity 70 mm/h over a catchment of 18.7 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.42, i = 70, A = 18.7 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.42*70*18.7 / 360 | Answer: 1.527 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.07 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 330 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.07, M = 330 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 330*(30+0.07)/30 | Answer: 330.8 m

question: Convert the decimal number 3409 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 3409 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: D51 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 10111100 and 11010000.
solution: XOR: 01101100 | Count of 1s = 4 | Answer: 4
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 700 megabits is sent over a link of 90 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 700, B = 90 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 700 / 90 | Answer: 7.778 s

question: A link has bandwidth 46 Mbps and round-trip time 190 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 46, R = 190 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 46e6 * 190e-3 bits = 8740 kb | Answer: 8740 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.88, cache access time 5 ns and main-memory access time 190 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.88, tc = 5, tm = 190 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.88*5 + (1 - 0.88)*190 | Answer: 27.2 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 707331 elements?
solution: Given: n = 707331 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(707331)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.002, memory access time 110 ns and page-fault service time 10 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 10 ms = 10000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.002)*110 + 0.002*10000000.0 ns | Answer: 20.11 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 1.7 m^3 at 480 kPa and 500 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 1.7, P = 480, Tk = 500 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (480e3)*1.7 / (8.314*500) | Answer: 196.3 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.28 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 17 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.28, t = 17 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.28*17) | Answer: 0.9914

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.21 /min) is to reach 70% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.21, X = 70 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.7) / 0.21 | Answer: 5.733 min

question: For a reaction with A = 6e10 /s and activation energy 60 kJ/mol at 490 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 6, Ea = 60, Tk = 490 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 6e10 * exp(-60e3 / (8.314*490)) | Answer: 2409 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.9 and bottoms xW = 0.09, with relative volatility alpha = 2.9. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.9, xw = 0.09, al = 2.9 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.9/0.1)(0.91/0.09)] / ln(2.9) | Answer: 4.237 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.67 and x = 0.23. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.67, x = 0.23 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.67/0.33) / (0.23/0.77) | Answer: 6.797

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.73 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 85 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.73, Psat = 85 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.73 * 85 | Answer: 62.05 kPa

question: A stream of 8.9 kg/s with specific heat 3.2 kJ/kg-K is heated through 65 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 8.9, cp = 3.2, dT = 65 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 8.9*3.2*65 | Answer: 1851 kW

question: A reactor of volume 2.9 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 3.2 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 2.9, Q = 3.2 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 2.9 / 3.2 | Answer: 0.9062 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 4.9e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 3 mm with a concentration difference of 110 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 4.9, L = 3, dC = 110 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (4.9e-9)*110 / (3e-3) | Answer: 179.7 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 1.7 min and steady-state gain 2. For a step input of magnitude 11, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 1.7, K = 2, M = 11 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 2 * 11 | Answer: 22 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 105 m^2 flies at 230 m/s (air density 1.225 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.9. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 105, V = 230, rho = 1.225, CL = 0.9 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1.225*(230)^2*105*0.9 / 1000 | Answer: 3062 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 30 m^2 flies at 260 m/s (density 0.4 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.03. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 30, V = 260, rho = 0.4, CD = 0.03 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.4*(260)^2*30*0.03 / 1000 | Answer: 12.17 kN

question: A specimen under stress 390 MPa shows an elastic strain of 1.8e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 390, eps = 1.8 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 390 / (1.8e-3) MPa = 216.7 GPa | Answer: 216.7 GPa

question: A block of mass 13 kg has a volume of 3.3e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 13, V = 3.3 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 13 / (3.3e-3) | Answer: 3939 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 1300 mm is heated through 125 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 17e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 1300, dT = 125, al = 17 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 1300*17e-6*125 | Answer: 2.762 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 60 ohm, R2 = 160 ohm and R3 = 135 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 60, R2 = 160, R3 = 135 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 160*135 / 60 | Answer: 360 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 120 ohm and gauge factor 2.2 experiences a strain of 1300e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 120, GF = 2.2, eps = 1300 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 120*2.2*1300e-6 | Answer: 343.2 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 9.94 when the true value is 10. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.94, true = 10 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.94 - 10| / 10 * 100 | Answer: 0.6 %

question: Annual demand is 29000 units, ordering cost 250 per order and holding cost 23 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 29000, S = 250, H = 23 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*29000*250 / 23) | Answer: 794 units

question: An asset costs 200000 with salvage value 30000 after 11 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 200000, Sv = 30000, n = 11 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (200000 - 30000) / 11 | Answer: 15455 per year

question: A product sells for 260 per unit with variable cost 40 per unit and fixed costs 125000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 260, V = 40, F = 125000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 125000 / (260 - 40) | Answer: 568.2 units

question: Find the present worth of 65000 received 9 years from now at an interest rate of 8% per year.
solution: Given: F = 65000, n = 9, i = 8 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 65000 / (1 + 0.08)^9 | Answer: 32516 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.95, 0.92 and 0.97 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.95, r2 = 0.92, r3 = 0.97 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.95*0.92*0.97 | Answer: 0.8478

question: A process produces 19 defective items in a batch of 16500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 19, N = 16500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 19/16500 * 1e6 | Answer: 1152 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -3x^3 - 6x - 8 evaluated at x = -3.
For f(x) = -4x^3 - 5x^2 + 9x + 2, find f''(x) at x = -4.
Evaluate the definite integral of (2x^2 + 4x - 4) dx from x = 1 to x = 6.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = 2x^3/3 + 4x^2/2 + -4x | Evaluate F(6) - F(1) | Answer: 193.3
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of x^2 - 10x + 7 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[9, 2], [7, 8]].
solution: Given: a = 9, b = 2, c = 7, d = 8 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (9)(8) - (2)(7) | Answer: 58

question: Find the determinant of [[-6, 6, 6], [-4, -6, 3], [-4, -5, -2]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: -306

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[6, 3], [-5, -8]].
solution: Trace tr = -2, Determinant = -33 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 4.831

question: Solve for x: 3x + 2y = -4 and 0x + -1y = -8.
solution: Determinant = 3*-1 - 2*0 = -3 | x = (e d - b f) / det = -6.667 | Answer: x = -6.667
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 71, 39, 79, 2, 33.
solution: Sum = 224 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 44.8 | Answer: 44.8

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 29, 21, 4, 11, 19.
solution: Mean = 16.8 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 9.602

question: Find the slope of the line through (3, 7) and (1, 7).
solution: Given: x1 = 3, y1 = 7, x2 = 1, y2 = 7 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (7 - 7) / (1 - 3) | Answer: 0

question: Find the distance between the points (-5, -5) and (-6, 3).
solution: Given: x1 = -5, y1 = -5, x2 = -6, y2 = 3 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-1)^2 + (8)^2) | Answer: 8.062 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (5,4), (-4,-3), (-6,7).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 52 sq units

question: Find the 31th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 2 and common difference -7.
solution: Given: a = 2, d = -7, n = 31 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = 2 + (31 - 1)*-7 | Answer: -208

question: Find the sum of the first 22 terms of an AP with first term 4 and common difference -1.
solution: Given: a = 4, d = -1, n = 22 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 22/2 [2*4 + (22-1)*-1] | Answer: -143

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 40000 at 11.1% per annum for 9 years.
solution: Given: P = 40000, R = 11.1, Tt = 9 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 40000 * 11.1 * 9 / 100 | Answer: 39960 currency units

question: Find the amount when 22000 is invested at 11% per annum compounded annually for 2 years.
solution: Given: P = 22000, R = 11, Tt = 2 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 22000 * (1 + 11/100)^2 | Answer: 27106 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (4, 5, -8) and (2, 8, 6).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (-1, -1, 5) and (-6, -3, -4).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 39.06

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (-6, -3, -5) and (6, -6, 2).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 112.6 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number -11 + -1i.
solution: Given: a = -11, b = -1 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((-11)^2 + (-1)^2) | Answer: 11.05

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number 5 + -9i.
solution: Given: a = 5, b = -9 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(-9, 5) | Answer: -60.95 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = 4x^3 + x^2 + 8x - 9 at x = 1.
solution: Given: a = 4, b = 1, c = 8, d = -9, x0 = 1 | Formula: f(x0) = a x0^3 + b x0^2 + c x0 + d | Substitute: f(1) = 4(1)^3 + 1(1)^2 + 8(1) + -9 | Answer: 4

question: Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-26 with initial guess x0=6, find x1 (one iteration).
solution: Given: N = 26, x0 = 6 | Formula: x1 = x0 - (x0^2 - N)/(2 x0) | Substitute: x1 = 6 - ((6)^2 - 26)/(2*6) | Answer: 5.167

question: Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.6 and ordinates 3, 6, 18, 11, 1, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 566 and 269.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 566 and 269 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 67 and 25.
solution: Given: a = 67, b = 25 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 67*25 / 1 | Answer: 1675
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 58 mm carries an axial tensile load of 66 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 27 mm and length 2900 mm carries an axial load of 19 kN. Take E = 70 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 21 mm transmits a torque of 850 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 21, Tt = 850 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(850*1000) / (pi*(21)^3) | Answer: 467.4 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 26 mm and length 1800 mm carries a torque of 800 N-m. With G = 80 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (26)^4 / 32 = 44864 mm^4 | theta = (800*1000)(1800) / (80000 * 44864) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 22.99 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 98 mm wide and 190 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 98, h = 190 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 98*(190)^2 / 6 | Answer: 589633 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (84 mm x 170 mm) carries a bending moment of 37 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (61 mm x 90 mm) has effective length 1800 mm and E = 200 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 610 MPa is designed for a working stress of 240 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 610, sw = 240 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 610 / 240 | Answer: 2.542

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 900 mm and wall thickness 20 mm carries an internal pressure of 0.9 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 900, t = 20, P = 0.9 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 0.9*900 / (2*20) | Answer: 20.25 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 1100 K and 280 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 1100, Tc = 280 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 280/1100) * 100 | Answer: 74.55 %

question: A refrigerator works between 272 K (cold) and 330 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 272, Th = 330 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 272 / (330 - 272) | Answer: 4.69

question: A heat pump operates between 284 K and 328 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 284, Th = 328 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 328 / (328 - 284) | Answer: 7.455

question: 2.6 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 125 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.6, dT = 125 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 2.6 * 0.718 * 125 | Answer: 233.3 kJ

question: 6.4 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 25 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 6.4, dT = 25 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 6.4 * 1.005 * 25 | Answer: 160.8 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 2 m^3 at 350 K with mass 4.6 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 2, Tk = 350, m = 4.6 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 4.6*0.287*350 / 2 | Answer: 231 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 3.1 kg of air expands isothermally at 350 K from volume V1 to 3*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.1, Tk = 350, ratio = 3 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 3.1*0.287*350*ln(3) | Answer: 342.1 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 0.6 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.34 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 0.6, D = 0.34 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*0.6*0.34 / 0.001 | Answer: 204000

question: Water flows at 2.3 m/s through a pipe of diameter 130 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 3.5 m. Taking Cv = 0.96, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 3.5, cv = 0.96 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.96*sqrt(2*9.81*3.5) | Answer: 7.955 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 270 mm) water flows at 2 m/s. It contracts to diameter 120 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 270, d2 = 120, V1 = 2 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 2*(270/120)^2 | Answer: 10.12 m/s

question: Water flows at 3.8 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.22 m and length 210 m. With friction factor f = 0.024, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 28 teeth drives a gear of 61 teeth. If the pinion runs at 500 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 28, z2 = 61, N1 = 500 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 500*28 / 61 | Answer: 229.5 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 430 mm rotates at 750 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 430, N = 750 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.43)*750 / 60 | Answer: 16.89 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 47.4 kW at 250 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 47.4, N = 250 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(47.4*1000) / (2*pi*250) | Answer: 1811 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 3.1 kg rotates at radius 0.21 m at 200 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 5400 N/m and mass 16.7 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 5400, m = 16.7 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(5400/16.7) | Answer: 2.862 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 8.7 m^2 and thickness 0.14 m has conductivity k = 32.2 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 85 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 8.7, L = 0.14, k = 32.2, dT = 85 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 32.2*8.7*85 / 0.14 | Answer: 170085 W

question: A surface of area 2.6 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 180 W/m^2-K to surroundings 125 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 2.6, h = 180, dT = 125 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 180*2.6*125 | Answer: 58500 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 250 m/min, feed = 0.5 mm/rev, depth of cut = 1.7 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 250, f = 0.5, d = 1.7 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*250*0.5*1.7 | Answer: 212500 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 480 mm is turned at 450 rpm with a feed of 0.3 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 480, N = 450, f = 0.3 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 480 / (0.3*450) | Answer: 3.556 min

question: A resistor of 91 ohm carries a current of 9.5 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 91, I = 9.5 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 9.5 * 91 | Answer: 864.5 V

question: Three resistors 79 ohm, 38 ohm and 58 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 79, R2 = 38, R3 = 58 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 79 + 38 + 58 | Answer: 175 ohm

question: Two resistors 50 ohm and 57 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 50, R2 = 57 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 50*57 / (50+57) | Answer: 26.64 ohm

question: A device draws 6.6 A at 105 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 105, I = 6.6 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 105 * 6.6 | Answer: 693 W

question: A current of 4.9 A flows through a 128 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 4.9, R = 128 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (4.9)^2 * 128 | Answer: 3073 W

question: Two capacitors 26.2 uF and 2.5 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 26.2, C2 = 2.5 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 26.2*2.5 / (26.2+2.5) | Answer: 2.282 uF

question: A resistor 85 kohm and capacitor 10.9 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 85, C = 10.9 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (85k)(10.9u) = 926.5 ms | Answer: 926.5 ms

question: An inductor 392.5 mH is in series with 35 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 392.5, R = 35 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (392.5e-3) / 35 | Answer: 11.21 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 71.1 mH inductor at 960 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 71.1, f = 960 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (960)(71.1e-3) | Answer: 428.9 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 38.1 uF capacitor at 990 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 38.1, f = 990 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (990)(38.1e-6)) | Answer: 4.219 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 40 ohm, XL = 131 ohm and XC = 33 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 40, XL = 131, XC = 33 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(40^2 + (131 - 33)^2) | Answer: 105.8 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 97.3 mH and C = 2.8 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 97.3, C = 2.8 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(97.3e-3 * 2.8e-6)) | Answer: 304.9 Hz

question: A capacitor of 6.6 uF is charged to 355 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 6.6, V = 355 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*6.6e-6*(355)^2 | Answer: 415.9 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 230 V with 920 primary turns and 420 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 230, N1 = 920, N2 = 420 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 230 * 420/920 | Answer: 105 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 300 V and draws an armature current of 58 A. If the armature resistance is 0.43 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 300, Ia = 58, Ra = 0.43 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 300 - 58*0.43 | Answer: 275.1 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 25 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.93. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 25, VL = 400, pf = 0.93 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*400*25*0.93 / 1000 | Answer: 16.11 kW

question: A load has real power 10 kW and apparent power 85 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 10, S = 85 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 10 / 85 | Answer: 0.1176

question: A machine delivers 85 kW output while drawing 117 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 85, Pi = 117 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 85/117 * 100 | Answer: 72.65 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 30 V across R1 = 27 ohm and R2 = 37 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 30, R1 = 27, R2 = 37 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 30*37 / (27+37) | Answer: 17.34 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 60 kohm and Rin = 21 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 60, Rin = 21 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 60 / 21 | Answer: 2.857

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 40 kohm and Rg = 30 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 40, Rg = 30 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 40/30 | Answer: 2.333

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 3412. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 3412 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(3412) | Answer: 35.33 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.9 m carries a central point load of 25 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6.9, W = 25 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 25*6.9 / 4 | Answer: 43.12 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 7.5 m carries a UDL of 60 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7.5, w = 60 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 60*(7.5)^2 / 8 | Answer: 421.9 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 2.7 m carries a point load 65 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 2.7, W = 65 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 65*2.7 | Answer: 175.5 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 2.8 m carries a UDL of 30 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 2.8, w = 30 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 30*(2.8)^2 / 2 | Answer: 117.6 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.9 m carries a point load 90 kN at distance 1.2 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 6.9, a = 1.2, W = 90 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 90*(6.9 - 1.2) / 6.9 | Answer: 74.35 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 3.4 m) carries a central point load 55 kN. With E = 200 GPa and I = 360e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=55000 N, L=3400.0 mm, E=200000 MPa, I=360e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 0.6255 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 7 m carries a UDL of 15 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7, w = 15 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 15*(7)^2 / 12 | Answer: 61.25 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 330 mm, clear cover 40 mm and main bars of diameter 12 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 330, c = 40, dia = 12 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 330 - 40 - 12/2 | Answer: 284 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 37.4 m^2 carrying a factored load of 10.3 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 37.4, w = 10.3 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 10.3 * 37.4 | Answer: 385.2 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 5.8 m, unit weight 16 kN/m^3, phi = 35 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 6.4 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 21 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 6.4, g = 21 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (21 - 9.81)*6.4 | Answer: 71.62 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 3.2e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1.5, area = 3.9e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 3.2, i = 1.5, A = 3.9 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (3.2e-4)*1.5*(3.9e-3) | Answer: 1872 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 2.2 m, bed slope 0.009 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.015. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 4.9 m under a head of 1.1 m. Taking Cd = 0.62 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 4.2 m wide carries a discharge of 21.7 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 530 m and design speed 45 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 530, V = 45 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (45)^2 / (127*530) | Answer: 0.03008
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: A tank of volume 400 m^3 treats a flow of 170 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 400, Q = 170 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 400 / 170 | Answer: 2.353 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 300 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.24 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 4 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 300, k = 0.24, t = 4 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 300*(1 - e^(-0.24*4)) | Answer: 185.1 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.46, rainfall intensity 50 mm/h over a catchment of 50.5 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.46, i = 50, A = 50.5 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.46*50*50.5 / 360 | Answer: 3.226 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.04 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 310 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.04, M = 310 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 310*(20+0.04)/20 | Answer: 310.6 m

question: Convert the decimal number 1242 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 1242 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 4DA (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 01100000 and 11111010.
solution: XOR: 10011010 | Count of 1s = 4 | Answer: 4
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 570 megabits is sent over a link of 39 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 570, B = 39 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 570 / 39 | Answer: 14.62 s

question: A link has bandwidth 60 Mbps and round-trip time 90 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 60, R = 90 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 60e6 * 90e-3 bits = 5400 kb | Answer: 5400 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.86, cache access time 5 ns and main-memory access time 110 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.86, tc = 5, tm = 110 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.86*5 + (1 - 0.86)*110 | Answer: 19.7 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 352963 elements?
solution: Given: n = 352963 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(352963)) + 1 | Answer: 19

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.002, memory access time 190 ns and page-fault service time 8 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 8 ms = 8000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.002)*190 + 0.002*8000000.0 ns | Answer: 16.19 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 2.5 m^3 at 420 kPa and 340 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 2.5, P = 420, Tk = 340 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (420e3)*2.5 / (8.314*340) | Answer: 371.4 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.3 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 14 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.3, t = 14 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.3*14) | Answer: 0.985

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.5 /min) is to reach 60% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.5, X = 60 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.6) / 0.5 | Answer: 1.833 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.44 /min) reaches 75% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.44, X = 75 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.75 / (0.44*(1 - 0.75)) | Answer: 6.818 min

question: For a reaction with A = 4e10 /s and activation energy 70 kJ/mol at 310 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 4, Ea = 70, Tk = 310 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 4e10 * exp(-70e3 / (8.314*310)) | Answer: 0.06408 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.94 and bottoms xW = 0.03, with relative volatility alpha = 2. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.94, xw = 0.03, al = 2 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.94/0.06)(0.97/0.03)] / ln(2) | Answer: 8.985 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.74 and x = 0.33. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.74, x = 0.33 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.74/0.26) / (0.33/0.67) | Answer: 5.779

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.83 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 95 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.83, Psat = 95 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.83 * 95 | Answer: 78.85 kPa

question: A stream of 5.4 kg/s with specific heat 1.4 kJ/kg-K is heated through 100 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 5.4, cp = 1.4, dT = 100 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 5.4*1.4*100 | Answer: 756 kW

question: A reactor of volume 1.6 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 0.9 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 1.6, Q = 0.9 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 1.6 / 0.9 | Answer: 1.778 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 2.6e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 3 mm with a concentration difference of 10 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 2.6, L = 3, dC = 10 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (2.6e-9)*10 / (3e-3) | Answer: 8.667 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 2.5 min and steady-state gain 2.3. For a step input of magnitude 6, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 2.5, K = 2.3, M = 6 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 2.3 * 6 | Answer: 13.8 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 40 m^2 flies at 120 m/s (air density 1 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.6. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 40, V = 120, rho = 1, CL = 0.6 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1*(120)^2*40*0.6 / 1000 | Answer: 172.8 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 25 m^2 flies at 210 m/s (density 0.7 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.11. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 25, V = 210, rho = 0.7, CD = 0.11 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.7*(210)^2*25*0.11 / 1000 | Answer: 42.45 kN

question: A specimen under stress 390 MPa shows an elastic strain of 1.6e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 390, eps = 1.6 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 390 / (1.6e-3) MPa = 243.8 GPa | Answer: 243.8 GPa

question: A block of mass 45 kg has a volume of 2.4e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 45, V = 2.4 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 45 / (2.4e-3) | Answer: 18750 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 1000 mm is heated through 100 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 17e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 1000, dT = 100, al = 17 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 1000*17e-6*100 | Answer: 1.7 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 50 ohm, R2 = 105 ohm and R3 = 155 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 50, R2 = 105, R3 = 155 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 105*155 / 50 | Answer: 325.5 ohm

question: A measurement reads 9.94 when the true value is 100. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.94, true = 100 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.94 - 100| / 100 * 100 | Answer: 90.06 %

question: Annual demand is 38000 units, ordering cost 60 per order and holding cost 23 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 38000, S = 60, H = 23 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*38000*60 / 23) | Answer: 445.3 units

question: An asset costs 290000 with salvage value 36000 after 8 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 290000, Sv = 36000, n = 8 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (290000 - 36000) / 8 | Answer: 31750 per year

question: A product sells for 240 per unit with variable cost 10 per unit and fixed costs 65000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 240, V = 10, F = 65000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 65000 / (240 - 10) | Answer: 282.6 units

question: Find the present worth of 190000 received 6 years from now at an interest rate of 5% per year.
solution: Given: F = 190000, n = 6, i = 5 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 190000 / (1 + 0.05)^6 | Answer: 141781 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.9, 0.98 and 0.95 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.9, r2 = 0.98, r3 = 0.95 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.9*0.98*0.95 | Answer: 0.8379

question: A process produces 11 defective items in a batch of 15000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 11, N = 15000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 11/15000 * 1e6 | Answer: 733.3 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -4x^3 - 6x^2 + 7x - 8 evaluated at x = 3.
For f(x) = -5x^3 - 3x^2 + 7x - 7, find f''(x) at x = 1.
Evaluate the definite integral of (-2x^2 - 6) dx from x = 0 to x = 6.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = -2x^3/3 + 0x^2/2 + -6x | Evaluate F(6) - F(0) | Answer: -180

question: Find the larger real root of 4x^2 + 8x - 12 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[3, 7], [-5, 0]].
solution: Given: a = 3, b = 7, c = -5, d = 0 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (3)(0) - (7)(-5) | Answer: 35

question: Find the determinant of [[6, 5, 1], [0, 3, -1], [2, 5, -1]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: -4

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[2, -6], [2, -7]].
solution: Trace tr = -5, Determinant = -2 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 0.3723

question: Solve for x: -2x + -2y = -12 and 2x + 6y = 12.
solution: Determinant = -2*6 - -2*2 = -8 | x = (e d - b f) / det = 6 | Answer: x = 6

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 9, 5, 7, 3, 54.
solution: Sum = 78 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 15.6 | Answer: 15.6

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 16, 39, 4, 9, 20.
solution: Mean = 17.6 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 13.46

question: Find the slope of the line through (0, 3) and (-6, -2).
solution: Given: x1 = 0, y1 = 3, x2 = -6, y2 = -2 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (-2 - 3) / (-6 - 0) | Answer: 0.8333

question: Find the distance between the points (1, -3) and (-8, 4).
solution: Given: x1 = 1, y1 = -3, x2 = -8, y2 = 4 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-9)^2 + (7)^2) | Answer: 11.4 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (3,-6), (-6,5), (-3,-8).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 42 sq units

question: Find the 6th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 7 and common difference 1.
solution: Given: a = 7, d = 1, n = 6 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = 7 + (6 - 1)*1 | Answer: 12

question: Find the sum of the first 21 terms of an AP with first term 8 and common difference -3.
solution: Given: a = 8, d = -3, n = 21 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 21/2 [2*8 + (21-1)*-3] | Answer: -462

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 26000 at 7.5% per annum for 2 years.
solution: Given: P = 26000, R = 7.5, Tt = 2 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 26000 * 7.5 * 2 / 100 | Answer: 3900 currency units

question: Find the amount when 14500 is invested at 9.6% per annum compounded annually for 6 years.
solution: Given: P = 14500, R = 9.6, Tt = 6 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 14500 * (1 + 9.6/100)^6 | Answer: 25132 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (-1, -7, 3) and (5, 7, -7).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (-6, 1, -1) and (-5, -1, 2).
