solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 313 and 66 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 51 and 43.
solution: Given: a = 51, b = 43 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 51*43 / 1 | Answer: 2193
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 55 mm carries an axial tensile load of 92 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 14 mm and length 1400 mm carries an axial load of 13 kN. Take E = 110 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 75 mm transmits a torque of 800 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 75, Tt = 800 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(800*1000) / (pi*(75)^3) | Answer: 9.658 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 27 mm and length 800 mm carries a torque of 1650 N-m. With G = 77 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (27)^4 / 32 = 52174 mm^4 | theta = (1650*1000)(800) / (77000 * 52174) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 18.83 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 135 mm wide and 240 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 135, h = 240 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 135*(240)^2 / 6 | Answer: 1296000 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (55 mm x 190 mm) carries a bending moment of 40 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (48 mm x 120 mm) has effective length 2500 mm and E = 200 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 630 MPa is designed for a working stress of 60 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 630, sw = 60 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 630 / 60 | Answer: 10.5

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 400 mm and wall thickness 15 mm carries an internal pressure of 0.8 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 400, t = 15, P = 0.8 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 0.8*400 / (2*15) | Answer: 10.67 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 760 K and 280 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 760, Tc = 280 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 280/760) * 100 | Answer: 63.16 %

question: A refrigerator works between 259 K (cold) and 330 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 259, Th = 330 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 259 / (330 - 259) | Answer: 3.648

question: A heat pump operates between 269 K and 304 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 269, Th = 304 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 304 / (304 - 269) | Answer: 8.686

question: 2.2 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 180 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.2, dT = 180 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 2.2 * 0.718 * 180 | Answer: 284.3 kJ

question: 5.8 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 145 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 5.8, dT = 145 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 5.8 * 1.005 * 145 | Answer: 845.2 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 3.5 m^3 at 600 K with mass 4.3 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 3.5, Tk = 600, m = 4.3 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 4.3*0.287*600 / 3.5 | Answer: 211.6 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 4.3 kg of air expands isothermally at 410 K from volume V1 to 4*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.3, Tk = 410, ratio = 4 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 4.3*0.287*410*ln(4) | Answer: 701.4 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 2.8 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.11 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 2.8, D = 0.11 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*2.8*0.11 / 0.001 | Answer: 308000

question: Water flows at 3.1 m/s through a pipe of diameter 290 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 11.6 m. Taking Cv = 0.98, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 11.6, cv = 0.98 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.98*sqrt(2*9.81*11.6) | Answer: 14.78 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 380 mm) water flows at 2.5 m/s. It contracts to diameter 50 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 380, d2 = 50, V1 = 2.5 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 2.5*(380/50)^2 | Answer: 144.4 m/s

question: Water flows at 3.1 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.1 m and length 80 m. With friction factor f = 0.033, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 21 teeth drives a gear of 45 teeth. If the pinion runs at 700 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 21, z2 = 45, N1 = 700 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 700*21 / 45 | Answer: 326.7 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 400 mm rotates at 1250 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 400, N = 1250 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.4)*1250 / 60 | Answer: 26.18 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 43.5 kW at 1300 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 43.5, N = 1300 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(43.5*1000) / (2*pi*1300) | Answer: 319.5 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 7 kg rotates at radius 0.2 m at 1100 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 19200 N/m and mass 14.1 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 19200, m = 14.1 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(19200/14.1) | Answer: 5.873 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 4.7 m^2 and thickness 0.38 m has conductivity k = 7.1 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 25 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 4.7, L = 0.38, k = 7.1, dT = 25 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 7.1*4.7*25 / 0.38 | Answer: 2195 W

question: A surface of area 5.2 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 85 W/m^2-K to surroundings 90 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 5.2, h = 85, dT = 90 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 85*5.2*90 | Answer: 39780 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 190 m/min, feed = 0.3 mm/rev, depth of cut = 0.6 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 190, f = 0.3, d = 0.6 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*190*0.3*0.6 | Answer: 34200 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 340 mm is turned at 750 rpm with a feed of 0.15 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 340, N = 750, f = 0.15 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 340 / (0.15*750) | Answer: 3.022 min

question: A resistor of 42 ohm carries a current of 5.3 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 42, I = 5.3 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 5.3 * 42 | Answer: 222.6 V

question: Three resistors 33 ohm, 26 ohm and 31 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 33, R2 = 26, R3 = 31 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 33 + 26 + 31 | Answer: 90 ohm

question: Two resistors 90 ohm and 110 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 90, R2 = 110 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 90*110 / (90+110) | Answer: 49.5 ohm

question: A device draws 9.7 A at 65 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 65, I = 9.7 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 65 * 9.7 | Answer: 630.5 W

question: A current of 5.4 A flows through a 135 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 5.4, R = 135 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (5.4)^2 * 135 | Answer: 3937 W

question: Two capacitors 34.4 uF and 45.7 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 34.4, C2 = 45.7 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 34.4*45.7 / (34.4+45.7) | Answer: 19.63 uF

question: A resistor 55 kohm and capacitor 18.3 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 55, C = 18.3 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (55k)(18.3u) = 1006 ms | Answer: 1006 ms

question: An inductor 270 mH is in series with 133 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 270, R = 133 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (270e-3) / 133 | Answer: 2.03 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 58.1 mH inductor at 110 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 58.1, f = 110 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (110)(58.1e-3) | Answer: 40.16 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 23 uF capacitor at 830 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 23, f = 830 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (830)(23e-6)) | Answer: 8.337 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 96 ohm, XL = 104 ohm and XC = 79 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 96, XL = 104, XC = 79 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(96^2 + (104 - 79)^2) | Answer: 99.2 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 61.5 mH and C = 8.1 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 61.5, C = 8.1 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(61.5e-3 * 8.1e-6)) | Answer: 225.5 Hz

question: A capacitor of 26.1 uF is charged to 275 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 26.1, V = 275 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*26.1e-6*(275)^2 | Answer: 986.9 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 170 V with 660 primary turns and 470 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 170, N1 = 660, N2 = 470 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 170 * 470/660 | Answer: 121.1 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 300 V and draws an armature current of 45 A. If the armature resistance is 0.47 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 300, Ia = 45, Ra = 0.47 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 300 - 45*0.47 | Answer: 278.9 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 195 A at 415 V (line) with a power factor of 0.86. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 195, VL = 415, pf = 0.86 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*415*195*0.86 / 1000 | Answer: 120.5 kW

question: A load has real power 125 kW and apparent power 155 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 125, S = 155 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 125 / 155 | Answer: 0.8065

question: A machine delivers 75 kW output while drawing 142 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 75, Pi = 142 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 75/142 * 100 | Answer: 52.82 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 21 V across R1 = 10 ohm and R2 = 47 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 21, R1 = 10, R2 = 47 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 21*47 / (10+47) | Answer: 17.32 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 70 kohm and Rin = 33 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 70, Rin = 33 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 70 / 33 | Answer: 2.121

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 160 kohm and Rg = 19 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 160, Rg = 19 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 160/19 | Answer: 9.421

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 2482. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 2482 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(2482) | Answer: 33.95 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 5 m carries a central point load of 100 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5, W = 100 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 100*5 / 4 | Answer: 125 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 8.9 m carries a UDL of 45 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 8.9, w = 45 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 45*(8.9)^2 / 8 | Answer: 445.6 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 5.6 m carries a point load 45 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.6, W = 45 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 45*5.6 | Answer: 252 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 5.7 m carries a UDL of 14 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.7, w = 14 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 14*(5.7)^2 / 2 | Answer: 227.4 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.6 m carries a point load 30 kN at distance 2.7 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 6.6, a = 2.7, W = 30 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 30*(6.6 - 2.7) / 6.6 | Answer: 17.73 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 3.9 m) carries a central point load 45 kN. With E = 25 GPa and I = 260e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=45000 N, L=3900.0 mm, E=25000 MPa, I=260e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 8.556 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 7.8 m carries a UDL of 6 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7.8, w = 6 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 6*(7.8)^2 / 12 | Answer: 30.42 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 610 mm, clear cover 35 mm and main bars of diameter 16 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 610, c = 35, dia = 16 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 610 - 35 - 16/2 | Answer: 567 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 23.9 m^2 carrying a factored load of 16.6 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 23.9, w = 16.6 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 16.6 * 23.9 | Answer: 396.7 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 5.4 m, unit weight 16 kN/m^3, phi = 35 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 8.8e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.5, area = 5.1e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 8.8, i = 0.5, A = 5.1 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (8.8e-4)*0.5*(5.1e-3) | Answer: 2244 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 0.8 m, bed slope 0.006 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.02. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 3.5 m under a head of 0.9 m. Taking Cd = 0.64 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 3.8 m wide carries a discharge of 18.1 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 120 m and design speed 95 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 120, V = 95 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (95)^2 / (127*120) | Answer: 0.5922
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: A tank of volume 640 m^3 treats a flow of 70 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 640, Q = 70 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 640 / 70 | Answer: 9.143 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 180 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.34 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 4 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 180, k = 0.34, t = 4 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 180*(1 - e^(-0.34*4)) | Answer: 133.8 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.59, rainfall intensity 105 mm/h over a catchment of 59 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.59, i = 105, A = 59 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.59*105*59 / 360 | Answer: 10.15 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.01 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 430 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.01, M = 430 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 430*(20+0.01)/20 | Answer: 430.2 m

question: Convert the decimal number 3484 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 3484 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: D9C (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 10011000 and 11101000.
solution: XOR: 01110000 | Count of 1s = 3 | Answer: 3
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 880 megabits is sent over a link of 93 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 880, B = 93 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 880 / 93 | Answer: 9.462 s

question: A link has bandwidth 20 Mbps and round-trip time 40 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 20, R = 40 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 20e6 * 40e-3 bits = 800 kb | Answer: 800 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.85, cache access time 9 ns and main-memory access time 80 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.85, tc = 9, tm = 80 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.85*9 + (1 - 0.85)*80 | Answer: 19.65 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 128147 elements?
solution: Given: n = 128147 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(128147)) + 1 | Answer: 17

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.013, memory access time 170 ns and page-fault service time 8 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 8 ms = 8000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.013)*170 + 0.013*8000000.0 ns | Answer: 104.2 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 2.1 m^3 at 450 kPa and 570 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 2.1, P = 450, Tk = 570 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (450e3)*2.1 / (8.314*570) | Answer: 199.4 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.21 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 4 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.21, t = 4 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.21*4) | Answer: 0.5683

question: For a reaction with A = 6e10 /s and activation energy 85 kJ/mol at 500 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 6, Ea = 85, Tk = 500 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 6e10 * exp(-85e3 / (8.314*500)) | Answer: 79.06 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.98 and bottoms xW = 0.02, with relative volatility alpha = 3.4. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.98, xw = 0.02, al = 3.4 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.98/0.02)(0.98/0.02)] / ln(3.4) | Answer: 6.36 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.58 and x = 0.34. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.58, x = 0.34 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.58/0.42) / (0.34/0.66) | Answer: 2.681

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.13 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 115 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.13, Psat = 115 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.13 * 115 | Answer: 14.95 kPa

question: A stream of 3.6 kg/s with specific heat 3.9 kJ/kg-K is heated through 60 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 3.6, cp = 3.9, dT = 60 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 3.6*3.9*60 | Answer: 842.4 kW

question: A reactor of volume 9.2 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 4.7 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 9.2, Q = 4.7 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 9.2 / 4.7 | Answer: 1.957 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 1.3e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 4 mm with a concentration difference of 20 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 1.3, L = 4, dC = 20 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (1.3e-9)*20 / (4e-3) | Answer: 6.5 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 2.1 min and steady-state gain 1.4. For a step input of magnitude 20, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 2.1, K = 1.4, M = 20 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 1.4 * 20 | Answer: 28 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 60 m^2 flies at 100 m/s (air density 0.7 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 1.2. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 60, V = 100, rho = 0.7, CL = 1.2 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.7*(100)^2*60*1.2 / 1000 | Answer: 252 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 120 m^2 flies at 240 m/s (density 0.7 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.11. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 120, V = 240, rho = 0.7, CD = 0.11 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.7*(240)^2*120*0.11 / 1000 | Answer: 266.1 kN

question: A specimen under stress 130 MPa shows an elastic strain of 1.4e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 130, eps = 1.4 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 130 / (1.4e-3) MPa = 92.86 GPa | Answer: 92.86 GPa

question: A block of mass 15 kg has a volume of 3.1e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 15, V = 3.1 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 15 / (3.1e-3) | Answer: 4839 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 2100 mm is heated through 75 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 12e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 2100, dT = 75, al = 12 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 2100*12e-6*75 | Answer: 1.89 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 170 ohm, R2 = 175 ohm and R3 = 210 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 170, R2 = 175, R3 = 210 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 175*210 / 170 | Answer: 216.2 ohm

question: A measurement reads 10.81 when the true value is 100. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10.81, true = 100 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10.81 - 100| / 100 * 100 | Answer: 89.19 %

question: Annual demand is 47500 units, ordering cost 250 per order and holding cost 37 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 47500, S = 250, H = 37 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*47500*250 / 37) | Answer: 801.2 units

question: An asset costs 400000 with salvage value 10000 after 5 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 400000, Sv = 10000, n = 5 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (400000 - 10000) / 5 | Answer: 78000 per year

question: A product sells for 130 per unit with variable cost 70 per unit and fixed costs 140000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 130, V = 70, F = 140000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 140000 / (130 - 70) | Answer: 2333 units

question: Find the present worth of 140000 received 2 years from now at an interest rate of 11% per year.
solution: Given: F = 140000, n = 2, i = 11 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 140000 / (1 + 0.11)^2 | Answer: 113627 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.99, 0.95 and 0.99 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.99, r2 = 0.95, r3 = 0.99 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.99*0.95*0.99 | Answer: 0.9311

question: A process produces 28 defective items in a batch of 18500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 28, N = 18500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 28/18500 * 1e6 | Answer: 1514 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = 6x^3 - 5x^2 + 8x - 3 evaluated at x = 0.
For f(x) = x^3 + 5x^2 + 8x - 1, find f''(x) at x = -3.
Evaluate the definite integral of (-5x^2 + 3x + 4) dx from x = 2 to x = 3.

question: Find the larger real root of 6x^2 - 12x - 7 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[4, -7], [-9, -8]].
solution: Given: a = 4, b = -7, c = -9, d = -8 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (4)(-8) - (-7)(-9) | Answer: -95

question: Find the determinant of [[0, -6, -3], [6, -4, 2], [-3, -1, 0]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: 90

question: Solve for x: 6x + -1y = -3 and 1x + -3y = -7.

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 4, 86, 31, 48, 12.
solution: Sum = 181 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 36.2 | Answer: 36.2

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 38, 40, 12, 9, 29.
solution: Mean = 25.6 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 14.43

question: Find the slope of the line through (6, -8) and (-2, 0).
solution: Given: x1 = 6, y1 = -8, x2 = -2, y2 = 0 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (0 - -8) / (-2 - 6) | Answer: -1

question: Find the distance between the points (-7, -7) and (-6, -6).
solution: Given: x1 = -7, y1 = -7, x2 = -6, y2 = -6 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((1)^2 + (1)^2) | Answer: 1.414 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (8,-2), (0,-5), (3,-8).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 16.5 sq units

question: Find the 24th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 20 and common difference 4.
solution: Given: a = 20, d = 4, n = 24 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = 20 + (24 - 1)*4 | Answer: 112

question: Find the sum of the first 13 terms of an AP with first term -4 and common difference 6.
solution: Given: a = -4, d = 6, n = 13 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 13/2 [2*-4 + (13-1)*6] | Answer: 416

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 36500 at 13.8% per annum for 7 years.
solution: Given: P = 36500, R = 13.8, Tt = 7 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 36500 * 13.8 * 7 / 100 | Answer: 35259 currency units

question: Find the amount when 37000 is invested at 10% per annum compounded annually for 6 years.
solution: Given: P = 37000, R = 10, Tt = 6 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 37000 * (1 + 10/100)^6 | Answer: 65548 currency units

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (-4, 3, 5) and (3, -2, -6).
