question: 1.7 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 75 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1.7, dT = 75 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 1.7 * 1.005 * 75 | Answer: 128.1 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 1.4 m^3 at 450 K with mass 1.3 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 1.4, Tk = 450, m = 1.3 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 1.3*0.287*450 / 1.4 | Answer: 119.9 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 2.6 kg of air expands isothermally at 330 K from volume V1 to 4*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.6, Tk = 330, ratio = 4 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 2.6*0.287*330*ln(4) | Answer: 341.4 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 4.1 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.23 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 4.1, D = 0.23 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*4.1*0.23 / 0.001 | Answer: 943000

question: Water flows at 1.9 m/s through a pipe of diameter 160 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Find the gauge pressure at a depth of 9.7 m in water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2), in kPa.
solution: Given: h = 9.7 | Formula: p = rho g h | Substitute: p = 1000*9.81*9.7 / 1000 | Answer: 95.16 kPa

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 16.5 m. Taking Cv = 0.99, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 16.5, cv = 0.99 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.99*sqrt(2*9.81*16.5) | Answer: 17.81 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 260 mm) water flows at 0.7 m/s. It contracts to diameter 140 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
Water flows at 3.8 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.1 m and length 320 m. With friction factor f = 0.037, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 15 teeth drives a gear of 54 teeth. If the pinion runs at 350 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 15, z2 = 54, N1 = 350 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 350*15 / 54 | Answer: 97.22 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 480 mm rotates at 200 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 480, N = 200 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.48)*200 / 60 | Answer: 5.027 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 6.5 kW at 1000 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 6.5, N = 1000 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(6.5*1000) / (2*pi*1000) | Answer: 62.07 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 6 kg rotates at radius 0.14 m at 1150 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 10800 N/m and mass 3.2 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 10800, m = 3.2 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(10800/3.2) | Answer: 9.246 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 9.2 m^2 and thickness 0.16 m has conductivity k = 13.9 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 125 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 9.2, L = 0.16, k = 13.9, dT = 125 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 13.9*9.2*125 / 0.16 | Answer: 99906 W

question: A surface of area 2.1 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 170 W/m^2-K to surroundings 65 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 2.1, h = 170, dT = 65 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 170*2.1*65 | Answer: 23205 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 230 m/min, feed = 0.31 mm/rev, depth of cut = 1.3 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 230, f = 0.31, d = 1.3 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*230*0.31*1.3 | Answer: 92690 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 480 mm is turned at 550 rpm with a feed of 0.34 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 480, N = 550, f = 0.34 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 480 / (0.34*550) | Answer: 2.567 min

question: A resistor of 92 ohm carries a current of 9.2 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 92, I = 9.2 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 9.2 * 92 | Answer: 846.4 V

question: Three resistors 85 ohm, 47 ohm and 76 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 85, R2 = 47, R3 = 76 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 85 + 47 + 76 | Answer: 208 ohm

question: Two resistors 10 ohm and 60 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 10, R2 = 60 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 10*60 / (10+60) | Answer: 8.571 ohm

question: A device draws 4.8 A at 60 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 60, I = 4.8 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 60 * 4.8 | Answer: 288 W

question: A current of 5.4 A flows through a 5 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 5.4, R = 5 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (5.4)^2 * 5 | Answer: 145.8 W

question: Two capacitors 1.3 uF and 38.7 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 1.3, C2 = 38.7 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 1.3*38.7 / (1.3+38.7) | Answer: 1.258 uF

question: A resistor 1 kohm and capacitor 15.1 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 1, C = 15.1 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (1k)(15.1u) = 15.1 ms | Answer: 15.1 ms

question: An inductor 430.2 mH is in series with 12 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 430.2, R = 12 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (430.2e-3) / 12 | Answer: 35.85 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 88 mH inductor at 290 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 88, f = 290 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (290)(88e-3) | Answer: 160.3 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 35.2 uF capacitor at 250 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 35.2, f = 250 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (250)(35.2e-6)) | Answer: 18.09 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 96 ohm, XL = 92 ohm and XC = 76 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 96, XL = 92, XC = 76 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(96^2 + (92 - 76)^2) | Answer: 97.32 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 91.4 mH and C = 2.8 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 91.4, C = 2.8 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(91.4e-3 * 2.8e-6)) | Answer: 314.6 Hz

question: A capacitor of 43.7 uF is charged to 100 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 43.7, V = 100 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*43.7e-6*(100)^2 | Answer: 218.5 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 320 V with 740 primary turns and 20 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 320, N1 = 740, N2 = 20 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 320 * 20/740 | Answer: 8.649 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 300 V and draws an armature current of 32 A. If the armature resistance is 1.41 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 300, Ia = 32, Ra = 1.41 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 300 - 32*1.41 | Answer: 254.9 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 170 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.7. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 170, VL = 400, pf = 0.7 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*400*170*0.7 / 1000 | Answer: 82.45 kW

question: A load has real power 50 kW and apparent power 135 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 50, S = 135 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 50 / 135 | Answer: 0.3704

question: A machine delivers 50 kW output while drawing 112 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 50, Pi = 112 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 50/112 * 100 | Answer: 44.64 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 11 V across R1 = 14 ohm and R2 = 48 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 11, R1 = 14, R2 = 48 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 11*48 / (14+48) | Answer: 8.516 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 220 kohm and Rin = 29 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 220, Rin = 29 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 220 / 29 | Answer: 7.586

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 110 kohm and Rg = 16 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 110, Rg = 16 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 110/16 | Answer: 7.875

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 7813. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 7813 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(7813) | Answer: 38.93 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 8.2 m carries a central point load of 25 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 8.2, W = 25 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 25*8.2 / 4 | Answer: 51.25 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 5.9 m carries a UDL of 40 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.9, w = 40 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 40*(5.9)^2 / 8 | Answer: 174.1 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 4.7 m carries a point load 25 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.7, W = 25 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 25*4.7 | Answer: 117.5 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 5.8 m carries a UDL of 12 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.8, w = 12 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 12*(5.8)^2 / 2 | Answer: 201.8 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.2 m carries a point load 95 kN at distance 3.2 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 6.2, a = 3.2, W = 95 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 95*(6.2 - 3.2) / 6.2 | Answer: 45.97 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 3.8 m) carries a central point load 55 kN. With E = 25 GPa and I = 600e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=55000 N, L=3800.0 mm, E=25000 MPa, I=600e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 4.192 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 5.2 m carries a UDL of 42 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.2, w = 42 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 42*(5.2)^2 / 12 | Answer: 94.64 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 690 mm, clear cover 25 mm and main bars of diameter 16 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 690, c = 25, dia = 16 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 690 - 25 - 16/2 | Answer: 657 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 16.2 m^2 carrying a factored load of 13.6 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 16.2, w = 13.6 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 13.6 * 16.2 | Answer: 220.3 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 5.7 m, unit weight 16 kN/m^3, phi = 35 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 11.4 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 20 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 11.4, g = 20 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (20 - 9.81)*11.4 | Answer: 116.2 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 8.4e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.4, area = 5.2e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 8.4, i = 0.4, A = 5.2 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (8.4e-4)*0.4*(5.2e-3) | Answer: 1747 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 2.4 m, bed slope 0.001 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.014. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 3.4 m under a head of 1 m. Taking Cd = 0.63 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 2.4 m wide carries a discharge of 10.1 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 560 m and design speed 60 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 560, V = 60 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (60)^2 / (127*560) | Answer: 0.05062
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: A tank of volume 290 m^3 treats a flow of 25 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 290, Q = 25 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 290 / 25 | Answer: 11.6 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 340 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.22 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 3 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 340, k = 0.22, t = 3 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 340*(1 - e^(-0.22*3)) | Answer: 164.3 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.85, rainfall intensity 30 mm/h over a catchment of 13.1 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.85, i = 30, A = 13.1 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.85*30*13.1 / 360 | Answer: 0.9279 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.07 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 610 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.07, M = 610 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 610*(30+0.07)/30 | Answer: 611.4 m

question: Convert the decimal number 2776 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 2776 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: AD8 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 11100011 and 00011001.
solution: XOR: 11111010 | Count of 1s = 6 | Answer: 6
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 970 megabits is sent over a link of 76 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 970, B = 76 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 970 / 76 | Answer: 12.76 s

question: A link has bandwidth 58 Mbps and round-trip time 60 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 58, R = 60 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 58e6 * 60e-3 bits = 3480 kb | Answer: 3480 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.81, cache access time 2 ns and main-memory access time 70 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.81, tc = 2, tm = 70 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.81*2 + (1 - 0.81)*70 | Answer: 14.92 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 774041 elements?
solution: Given: n = 774041 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(774041)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: An O(n^2) algorithm performs c*n^2 basic operations. If c = 1 and n = 210, how many operations are performed?
solution: Given: n = 210 | Formula: operations = n^2 | Substitute: = (210)^2 | Answer: 44100

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.019, memory access time 100 ns and page-fault service time 4 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 4 ms = 4000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.019)*100 + 0.019*4000000.0 ns | Answer: 76.1 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 0.3 m^3 at 240 kPa and 420 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 0.3, P = 240, Tk = 420 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (240e3)*0.3 / (8.314*420) | Answer: 20.62 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.12 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 5 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.12, t = 5 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.12*5) | Answer: 0.4512

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.37 /min) reaches 85% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.37, X = 85 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.85 / (0.37*(1 - 0.85)) | Answer: 15.32 min

question: For a reaction with A = 4e10 /s and activation energy 70 kJ/mol at 420 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 4, Ea = 70, Tk = 420 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 4e10 * exp(-70e3 / (8.314*420)) | Answer: 78.7 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.9 and bottoms xW = 0.07, with relative volatility alpha = 2.7. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.9, xw = 0.07, al = 2.7 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.9/0.1)(0.93/0.07)] / ln(2.7) | Answer: 4.816 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.83 and x = 0.42. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.83, x = 0.42 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.83/0.17) / (0.42/0.58) | Answer: 6.742

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.5 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 30 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.5, Psat = 30 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.5 * 30 | Answer: 15 kPa

question: A stream of 2.7 kg/s with specific heat 2.5 kJ/kg-K is heated through 70 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 2.7, cp = 2.5, dT = 70 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 2.7*2.5*70 | Answer: 472.5 kW

question: A reactor of volume 16.3 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 0.4 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 16.3, Q = 0.4 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 16.3 / 0.4 | Answer: 40.75 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 6.1e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 4 mm with a concentration difference of 110 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 6.1, L = 4, dC = 110 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (6.1e-9)*110 / (4e-3) | Answer: 167.8 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 5.1 min and steady-state gain 3.2. For a step input of magnitude 3, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 5.1, K = 3.2, M = 3 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 3.2 * 3 | Answer: 9.6 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 85 m^2 flies at 60 m/s (air density 0.7 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 1.1. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 85, V = 60, rho = 0.7, CL = 1.1 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.7*(60)^2*85*1.1 / 1000 | Answer: 117.8 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 30 m^2 flies at 60 m/s (density 1 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.08. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 30, V = 60, rho = 1, CD = 0.08 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*1*(60)^2*30*0.08 / 1000 | Answer: 4.32 kN

question: A specimen under stress 400 MPa shows an elastic strain of 2.5e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 400, eps = 2.5 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 400 / (2.5e-3) MPa = 160 GPa | Answer: 160 GPa

question: A block of mass 17 kg has a volume of 4.2e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 17, V = 4.2 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 17 / (4.2e-3) | Answer: 4048 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 1800 mm is heated through 80 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 17e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 1800, dT = 80, al = 17 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 1800*17e-6*80 | Answer: 2.448 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 20 ohm, R2 = 190 ohm and R3 = 295 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 20, R2 = 190, R3 = 295 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 190*295 / 20 | Answer: 2802 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 350 ohm and gauge factor 2.2 experiences a strain of 850e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 350, GF = 2.2, eps = 850 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 350*2.2*850e-6 | Answer: 654.5 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 10.77 when the true value is 20. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10.77, true = 20 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10.77 - 20| / 20 * 100 | Answer: 46.15 %

question: Annual demand is 44000 units, ordering cost 200 per order and holding cost 5 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 44000, S = 200, H = 5 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*44000*200 / 5) | Answer: 1876 units

question: An asset costs 370000 with salvage value 18000 after 15 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 370000, Sv = 18000, n = 15 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (370000 - 18000) / 15 | Answer: 23467 per year

question: A product sells for 210 per unit with variable cost 100 per unit and fixed costs 155000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 210, V = 100, F = 155000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 155000 / (210 - 100) | Answer: 1409 units

question: Find the present worth of 190000 received 4 years from now at an interest rate of 10% per year.
solution: Given: F = 190000, n = 4, i = 10 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 190000 / (1 + 0.1)^4 | Answer: 129773 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.99, 0.95 and 0.97 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.99, r2 = 0.95, r3 = 0.97 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.99*0.95*0.97 | Answer: 0.9123

question: A process produces 18 defective items in a batch of 20000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 18, N = 20000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 18/20000 * 1e6 | Answer: 900 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = 4x^3 - 4x^2 + 6x + 8 evaluated at x = 5.
For f(x) = -x^3 + 5x^2 - 9x + 7, find f''(x) at x = -3.
Evaluate the definite integral of (3x - 3) dx from x = -2 to x = 6.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = 0x^3/3 + 3x^2/2 + -3x | Evaluate F(6) - F(-2) | Answer: 24
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of x^2 + 6x - 7 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[6, 0], [-7, -3]].
solution: Given: a = 6, b = 0, c = -7, d = -3 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (6)(-3) - (0)(-7) | Answer: -18

question: Find the determinant of [[-5, -1, -2], [0, 1, -4], [0, -1, 1]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: 15

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[-7, -5], [-2, 6]].
solution: Trace tr = -1, Determinant = -52 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 6.728

question: Solve for x: 1x + 5y = -4 and -3x + 6y = 0.
solution: Determinant = 1*6 - 5*-3 = 21 | x = (e d - b f) / det = -1.143 | Answer: x = -1.143
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 64, 33, 85, 83, 38.
solution: Sum = 303 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 60.6 | Answer: 60.6

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 36, 47, 27, 17, 47.
solution: Mean = 34.8 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 13.01

question: Find the slope of the line through (-2, 7) and (0, 1).
solution: Given: x1 = -2, y1 = 7, x2 = 0, y2 = 1 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (1 - 7) / (0 - -2) | Answer: -3

question: Find the distance between the points (4, -1) and (1, -3).
solution: Given: x1 = 4, y1 = -1, x2 = 1, y2 = -3 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-3)^2 + (-2)^2) | Answer: 3.606 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (-6,-3), (7,1), (-1,-5).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 23 sq units

question: Find the 12th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -18 and common difference 9.
solution: Given: a = -18, d = 9, n = 12 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -18 + (12 - 1)*9 | Answer: 81

question: Find the sum of the first 13 terms of an AP with first term 15 and common difference 5.
solution: Given: a = 15, d = 5, n = 13 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 13/2 [2*15 + (13-1)*5] | Answer: 585

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 29500 at 6.6% per annum for 8 years.
solution: Given: P = 29500, R = 6.6, Tt = 8 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 29500 * 6.6 * 8 / 100 | Answer: 15576 currency units

question: Find the amount when 17500 is invested at 11.1% per annum compounded annually for 6 years.
solution: Given: P = 17500, R = 11.1, Tt = 6 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 17500 * (1 + 11.1/100)^6 | Answer: 3291 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (-1, 0, 6) and (8, -7, 6).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (0, -5, -2) and (-1, -5, 5).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 35.41

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (-4, 6, 4) and (-1, 4, 3).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 17.95 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number 10 + -3i.
solution: Given: a = 10, b = -3 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((10)^2 + (-3)^2) | Answer: 10.44

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number -11 + 0i.
solution: Given: a = -11, b = 0 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(0, -11) | Answer: 180 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = 5x^3 + x^2 + 2x - 8 at x = 1.
solution: Given: a = 5, b = 1, c = 2, d = -8, x0 = 1 | Formula: f(x0) = a x0^3 + b x0^2 + c x0 + d | Substitute: f(1) = 5(1)^3 + 1(1)^2 + 2(1) + -8 | Answer: 0

question: Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-162 with initial guess x0=12, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=0.5 and ordinates 15, 13, 7, 10, 5, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 507 and 514.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 507 and 514 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 48 and 48.
solution: Given: a = 48, b = 48 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 48*48 / 48 | Answer: 48
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 23 mm carries an axial tensile load of 112 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 13 mm and length 2800 mm carries an axial load of 32 kN. Take E = 210 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 39 mm transmits a torque of 1600 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 39, Tt = 1600 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(1600*1000) / (pi*(39)^3) | Answer: 137.4 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 68 mm and length 1700 mm carries a torque of 1700 N-m. With G = 77 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (68)^4 / 32 = 2099112 mm^4 | theta = (1700*1000)(1700) / (77000 * 2099112) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 1.024 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 70 mm wide and 300 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 70, h = 300 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 70*(300)^2 / 6 | Answer: 1050000 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (63 mm x 200 mm) carries a bending moment of 4 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (44 mm x 160 mm) has effective length 1800 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 640 MPa is designed for a working stress of 130 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 640, sw = 130 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 640 / 130 | Answer: 4.923

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1000 mm and wall thickness 14 mm carries an internal pressure of 2.7 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1000, t = 14, P = 2.7 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 2.7*1000 / (2*14) | Answer: 96.43 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 840 K and 440 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 840, Tc = 440 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 440/840) * 100 | Answer: 47.62 %

question: A refrigerator works between 269 K (cold) and 304 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 269, Th = 304 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 269 / (304 - 269) | Answer: 7.686

question: A heat pump operates between 271 K and 304 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 271, Th = 304 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 304 / (304 - 271) | Answer: 9.212

question: 4.9 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 25 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.9, dT = 25 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 4.9 * 0.718 * 25 | Answer: 87.96 kJ

question: 5.1 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 100 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 5.1, dT = 100 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 5.1 * 1.005 * 100 | Answer: 512.5 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 2.9 m^3 at 420 K with mass 4.2 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 2.9, Tk = 420, m = 4.2 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 4.2*0.287*420 / 2.9 | Answer: 174.6 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 4.9 kg of air expands isothermally at 320 K from volume V1 to 5*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.9, Tk = 320, ratio = 5 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 4.9*0.287*320*ln(5) | Answer: 724.3 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 3.3 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.36 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 3.3, D = 0.36 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*3.3*0.36 / 0.001 | Answer: 1188000

question: Water flows at 1.8 m/s through a pipe of diameter 70 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 9.8 m. Taking Cv = 0.98, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 9.8, cv = 0.98 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.98*sqrt(2*9.81*9.8) | Answer: 13.59 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 170 mm) water flows at 2.4 m/s. It contracts to diameter 120 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
Water flows at 2.8 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.13 m and length 80 m. With friction factor f = 0.037, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 23 teeth drives a gear of 112 teeth. If the pinion runs at 700 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 23, z2 = 112, N1 = 700 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 700*23 / 112 | Answer: 143.8 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 450 mm rotates at 450 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 450, N = 450 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.45)*450 / 60 | Answer: 10.6 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 46.8 kW at 1050 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 46.8, N = 1050 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(46.8*1000) / (2*pi*1050) | Answer: 425.6 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 7.7 kg rotates at radius 0.35 m at 900 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 4600 N/m and mass 9.6 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 4600, m = 9.6 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(4600/9.6) | Answer: 3.484 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 7.6 m^2 and thickness 0.34 m has conductivity k = 49.9 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 75 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 7.6, L = 0.34, k = 49.9, dT = 75 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 49.9*7.6*75 / 0.34 | Answer: 83656 W

question: A surface of area 1.7 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 145 W/m^2-K to surroundings 85 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 1.7, h = 145, dT = 85 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 145*1.7*85 | Answer: 20952 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 130 m/min, feed = 0.42 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2.5 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 130, f = 0.42, d = 2.5 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*130*0.42*2.5 | Answer: 136500 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 400 mm is turned at 500 rpm with a feed of 0.31 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 400, N = 500, f = 0.31 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 400 / (0.31*500) | Answer: 2.581 min

question: A resistor of 95 ohm carries a current of 9.5 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 95, I = 9.5 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 9.5 * 95 | Answer: 902.5 V

question: Three resistors 44 ohm, 52 ohm and 29 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 44, R2 = 52, R3 = 29 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 44 + 52 + 29 | Answer: 125 ohm

question: Two resistors 45 ohm and 34 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 45, R2 = 34 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 45*34 / (45+34) | Answer: 19.37 ohm

question: A device draws 9.5 A at 55 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 55, I = 9.5 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 55 * 9.5 | Answer: 522.5 W

question: A current of 5.1 A flows through a 146 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 5.1, R = 146 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (5.1)^2 * 146 | Answer: 3797 W

question: Two capacitors 9.4 uF and 3.2 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 9.4, C2 = 3.2 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 9.4*3.2 / (9.4+3.2) | Answer: 2.387 uF

question: A resistor 20 kohm and capacitor 7.4 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 20, C = 7.4 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (20k)(7.4u) = 148 ms | Answer: 148 ms

question: An inductor 473.4 mH is in series with 85 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 473.4, R = 85 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (473.4e-3) / 85 | Answer: 5.569 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 166.6 mH inductor at 960 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 166.6, f = 960 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (960)(166.6e-3) | Answer: 1005 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 4.1 uF capacitor at 70 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 4.1, f = 70 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (70)(4.1e-6)) | Answer: 554.5 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 8 ohm, XL = 34 ohm and XC = 69 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 8, XL = 34, XC = 69 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(8^2 + (34 - 69)^2) | Answer: 35.9 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 83 mH and C = 0.5 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 83, C = 0.5 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(83e-3 * 0.5e-6)) | Answer: 781.3 Hz

question: A capacitor of 67.6 uF is charged to 15 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 67.6, V = 15 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*67.6e-6*(15)^2 | Answer: 7.605 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 380 V with 850 primary turns and 450 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 380, N1 = 850, N2 = 450 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 380 * 450/850 | Answer: 201.2 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 390 V and draws an armature current of 38 A. If the armature resistance is 0.93 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 390, Ia = 38, Ra = 0.93 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 390 - 38*0.93 | Answer: 354.7 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 45 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.83. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 45, VL = 400, pf = 0.83 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*400*45*0.83 / 1000 | Answer: 25.88 kW

question: A load has real power 65 kW and apparent power 105 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 65, S = 105 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 65 / 105 | Answer: 0.619

question: A machine delivers 20 kW output while drawing 82 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 20, Pi = 82 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 20/82 * 100 | Answer: 24.39 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 5 V across R1 = 1 ohm and R2 = 24 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 5, R1 = 1, R2 = 24 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 5*24 / (1+24) | Answer: 4.8 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 130 kohm and Rin = 17 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 130, Rin = 17 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 130 / 17 | Answer: 7.647

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 20 kohm and Rg = 41 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 20, Rg = 41 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 20/41 | Answer: 1.488

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 3349. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 3349 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(3349) | Answer: 35.25 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 8.4 m carries a central point load of 75 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 8.4, W = 75 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 75*8.4 / 4 | Answer: 157.5 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 2.9 m carries a point load 75 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 2.9, W = 75 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 75*2.9 | Answer: 217.5 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 5.9 m carries a UDL of 28 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.9, w = 28 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 28*(5.9)^2 / 2 | Answer: 487.3 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 8.7 m carries a point load 85 kN at distance 2.5 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 8.7, a = 2.5, W = 85 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 85*(8.7 - 2.5) / 8.7 | Answer: 60.57 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 5.6 m) carries a central point load 45 kN. With E = 30 GPa and I = 360e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=45000 N, L=5600.0 mm, E=30000 MPa, I=360e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 15.24 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 7 m carries a UDL of 42 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7, w = 42 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 42*(7)^2 / 12 | Answer: 171.5 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 540 mm, clear cover 30 mm and main bars of diameter 25 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 540, c = 30, dia = 25 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 540 - 30 - 25/2 | Answer: 497.5 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 25.7 m^2 carrying a factored load of 17.5 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 25.7, w = 17.5 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 17.5 * 25.7 | Answer: 449.8 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 5.6 m, unit weight 19 kN/m^3, phi = 30 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 6 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 18 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 6, g = 18 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (18 - 9.81)*6 | Answer: 49.14 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 1.8e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1.3, area = 3.4e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 1.8, i = 1.3, A = 3.4 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (1.8e-4)*1.3*(3.4e-3) | Answer: 795.6 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 0.6 m, bed slope 0.01 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.021. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 3.2 m under a head of 1.2 m. Taking Cd = 0.64 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 4.4 m wide carries a discharge of 20.1 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 360 m and design speed 65 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 360, V = 65 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (65)^2 / (127*360) | Answer: 0.09241
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: A tank of volume 920 m^3 treats a flow of 70 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 920, Q = 70 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 920 / 70 | Answer: 13.14 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 390 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.22 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 5 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 390, k = 0.22, t = 5 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 390*(1 - e^(-0.22*5)) | Answer: 260.2 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.66, rainfall intensity 85 mm/h over a catchment of 18.4 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.66, i = 85, A = 18.4 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.66*85*18.4 / 360 | Answer: 2.867 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.05 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 340 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.05, M = 340 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 340*(20+0.05)/20 | Answer: 340.9 m

question: Convert the decimal number 3263 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 3263 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: CBF (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 00110100 and 01010110.
solution: XOR: 01100010 | Count of 1s = 3 | Answer: 3
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 430 megabits is sent over a link of 8 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 430, B = 8 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 430 / 8 | Answer: 53.75 s

question: A link has bandwidth 24 Mbps and round-trip time 160 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 24, R = 160 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 24e6 * 160e-3 bits = 3840 kb | Answer: 3840 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.93, cache access time 9 ns and main-memory access time 110 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.93, tc = 9, tm = 110 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.93*9 + (1 - 0.93)*110 | Answer: 16.07 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 362396 elements?
solution: Given: n = 362396 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(362396)) + 1 | Answer: 19

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.016, memory access time 180 ns and page-fault service time 4 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 4 ms = 4000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.016)*180 + 0.016*4000000.0 ns | Answer: 64.18 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 2.1 m^3 at 160 kPa and 570 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 2.1, P = 160, Tk = 570 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (160e3)*2.1 / (8.314*570) | Answer: 70.9 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.12 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 19 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.12, t = 19 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.12*19) | Answer: 0.8977

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.26 /min) reaches 75% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.26, X = 75 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.75 / (0.26*(1 - 0.75)) | Answer: 11.54 min

question: For a reaction with A = 8e10 /s and activation energy 65 kJ/mol at 340 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 8, Ea = 65, Tk = 340 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 8e10 * exp(-65e3 / (8.314*340)) | Answer: 8.255 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.92 and bottoms xW = 0.04, with relative volatility alpha = 3. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.92, xw = 0.04, al = 3 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.92/0.08)(0.96/0.04)] / ln(3) | Answer: 5.116 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.68 and x = 0.28. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.68, x = 0.28 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.68/0.32) / (0.28/0.72) | Answer: 5.464

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.56 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 50 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.56, Psat = 50 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.56 * 50 | Answer: 28 kPa

question: A stream of 5.4 kg/s with specific heat 3.7 kJ/kg-K is heated through 115 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 5.4, cp = 3.7, dT = 115 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 5.4*3.7*115 | Answer: 2298 kW

question: A reactor of volume 1.8 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 2 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 1.8, Q = 2 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 1.8 / 2 | Answer: 0.9 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 5.3e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 1 mm with a concentration difference of 40 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 5.3, L = 1, dC = 40 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (5.3e-9)*40 / (1e-3) | Answer: 212 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 1.3 min and steady-state gain 1.1. For a step input of magnitude 5, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 1.3, K = 1.1, M = 5 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 1.1 * 5 | Answer: 5.5 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 60 m^2 flies at 130 m/s (air density 0.4 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.5. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 60, V = 130, rho = 0.4, CL = 0.5 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.4*(130)^2*60*0.5 / 1000 | Answer: 101.4 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 85 m^2 flies at 140 m/s (density 0.4 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.07. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 85, V = 140, rho = 0.4, CD = 0.07 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.4*(140)^2*85*0.07 / 1000 | Answer: 23.32 kN

question: A specimen under stress 300 MPa shows an elastic strain of 2.6e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 300, eps = 2.6 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 300 / (2.6e-3) MPa = 115.4 GPa | Answer: 115.4 GPa

question: A block of mass 47 kg has a volume of 3.4e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 47, V = 3.4 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 47 / (3.4e-3) | Answer: 13824 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 1200 mm is heated through 120 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 12e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 1200, dT = 120, al = 12 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 1200*12e-6*120 | Answer: 1.728 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 60 ohm, R2 = 175 ohm and R3 = 490 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 60, R2 = 175, R3 = 490 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 175*490 / 60 | Answer: 1429 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 120 ohm and gauge factor 2.2 experiences a strain of 700e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 120, GF = 2.2, eps = 700 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 120*2.2*700e-6 | Answer: 184.8 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 10.46 when the true value is 10. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10.46, true = 10 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10.46 - 10| / 10 * 100 | Answer: 4.6 %

question: Annual demand is 20000 units, ordering cost 240 per order and holding cost 21 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 20000, S = 240, H = 21 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*20000*240 / 21) | Answer: 676.1 units

question: An asset costs 470000 with salvage value 6000 after 10 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 470000, Sv = 6000, n = 10 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (470000 - 6000) / 10 | Answer: 46400 per year

question: A product sells for 430 per unit with variable cost 120 per unit and fixed costs 30000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 430, V = 120, F = 30000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 30000 / (430 - 120) | Answer: 96.77 units

question: Find the present worth of 25000 received 8 years from now at an interest rate of 11% per year.
solution: Given: F = 25000, n = 8, i = 11 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 25000 / (1 + 0.11)^8 | Answer: 10848 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.95, 0.93 and 0.9 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.95, r2 = 0.93, r3 = 0.9 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.95*0.93*0.9 | Answer: 0.7952

question: A process produces 24 defective items in a batch of 13500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 24, N = 13500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 24/13500 * 1e6 | Answer: 1778 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -4x^3 + x^2 + 5x evaluated at x = 1.

Evaluate the definite integral of (-4x^2 + 3x - 3) dx from x = -4 to x = 3.
