question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 68 and 39.
solution: Given: a = 68, b = 39 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 68*39 / 1 | Answer: 2652
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 13 mm carries an axial tensile load of 6 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 26 mm and length 2000 mm carries an axial load of 15 kN. Take E = 70 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 25 mm transmits a torque of 1400 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 25, Tt = 1400 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(1400*1000) / (pi*(25)^3) | Answer: 456.3 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 65 mm and length 800 mm carries a torque of 700 N-m. With G = 77 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (65)^4 / 32 = 1752481 mm^4 | theta = (700*1000)(800) / (77000 * 1752481) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 0.2378 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 143 mm wide and 230 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 143, h = 230 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 143*(230)^2 / 6 | Answer: 1260783 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (65 mm x 190 mm) carries a bending moment of 19 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (53 mm x 150 mm) has effective length 2100 mm and E = 200 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 690 MPa is designed for a working stress of 180 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 690, sw = 180 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 690 / 180 | Answer: 3.833

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1300 mm and wall thickness 13 mm carries an internal pressure of 2.3 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1300, t = 13, P = 2.3 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 2.3*1300 / (2*13) | Answer: 115 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 1080 K and 410 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 1080, Tc = 410 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 410/1080) * 100 | Answer: 62.04 %

question: A refrigerator works between 257 K (cold) and 306 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 257, Th = 306 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 257 / (306 - 257) | Answer: 5.245

question: 5.9 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 65 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 5.9, dT = 65 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 5.9 * 0.718 * 65 | Answer: 275.4 kJ

question: 1.3 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 160 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1.3, dT = 160 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 1.3 * 1.005 * 160 | Answer: 209 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 3.4 m^3 at 370 K with mass 4.3 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 3.4, Tk = 370, m = 4.3 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 4.3*0.287*370 / 3.4 | Answer: 134.3 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 2.4 kg of air expands isothermally at 370 K from volume V1 to 5*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.4, Tk = 370, ratio = 5 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 2.4*0.287*370*ln(5) | Answer: 410.2 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 2.1 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.3 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 2.1, D = 0.3 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*2.1*0.3 / 0.001 | Answer: 630000

question: Water flows at 3.5 m/s through a pipe of diameter 160 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 7.9 m. Taking Cv = 0.95, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 7.9, cv = 0.95 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.95*sqrt(2*9.81*7.9) | Answer: 11.83 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 350 mm) water flows at 1.8 m/s. It contracts to diameter 50 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 350, d2 = 50, V1 = 1.8 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 1.8*(350/50)^2 | Answer: 88.2 m/s

question: Water flows at 1 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.39 m and length 90 m. With friction factor f = 0.033, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 29 teeth drives a gear of 107 teeth. If the pinion runs at 550 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 29, z2 = 107, N1 = 550 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 550*29 / 107 | Answer: 149.1 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 590 mm rotates at 1050 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 590, N = 1050 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.59)*1050 / 60 | Answer: 32.44 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 42.2 kW at 1350 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 42.2, N = 1350 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(42.2*1000) / (2*pi*1350) | Answer: 298.5 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 3.4 kg rotates at radius 0.36 m at 950 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 13000 N/m and mass 3.1 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 13000, m = 3.1 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(13000/3.1) | Answer: 10.31 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 8.3 m^2 and thickness 0.25 m has conductivity k = 41.9 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 175 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 8.3, L = 0.25, k = 41.9, dT = 175 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 41.9*8.3*175 / 0.25 | Answer: 243439 W

question: A surface of area 2.2 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 25 W/m^2-K to surroundings 60 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 2.2, h = 25, dT = 60 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 25*2.2*60 | Answer: 3300 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 230 m/min, feed = 0.37 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2.7 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 230, f = 0.37, d = 2.7 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*230*0.37*2.7 | Answer: 229770 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 420 mm is turned at 450 rpm with a feed of 0.34 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 420, N = 450, f = 0.34 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 420 / (0.34*450) | Answer: 2.745 min

question: A resistor of 2 ohm carries a current of 2.1 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 2, I = 2.1 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 2.1 * 2 | Answer: 4.2 V

question: Three resistors 38 ohm, 50 ohm and 75 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 38, R2 = 50, R3 = 75 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 38 + 50 + 75 | Answer: 163 ohm

question: Two resistors 91 ohm and 111 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 91, R2 = 111 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 91*111 / (91+111) | Answer: 50 ohm

question: A device draws 2.2 A at 130 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 130, I = 2.2 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 130 * 2.2 | Answer: 286 W

question: A current of 7.9 A flows through a 82 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 7.9, R = 82 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (7.9)^2 * 82 | Answer: 5118 W

question: Two capacitors 34.2 uF and 15 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 34.2, C2 = 15 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 34.2*15 / (34.2+15) | Answer: 10.43 uF

question: A resistor 79 kohm and capacitor 10.6 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 79, C = 10.6 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (79k)(10.6u) = 837.4 ms | Answer: 837.4 ms

question: An inductor 446.3 mH is in series with 87 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 446.3, R = 87 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (446.3e-3) / 87 | Answer: 5.13 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 115.6 mH inductor at 450 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 115.6, f = 450 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (450)(115.6e-3) | Answer: 326.9 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 47.1 uF capacitor at 240 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 47.1, f = 240 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (240)(47.1e-6)) | Answer: 14.08 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 29 ohm, XL = 76 ohm and XC = 71 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 29, XL = 76, XC = 71 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(29^2 + (76 - 71)^2) | Answer: 29.43 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 18 mH and C = 7.7 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 18, C = 7.7 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(18e-3 * 7.7e-6)) | Answer: 427.5 Hz

question: A capacitor of 78.5 uF is charged to 240 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 78.5, V = 240 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*78.5e-6*(240)^2 | Answer: 2261 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 140 V with 760 primary turns and 160 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 140, N1 = 760, N2 = 160 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 140 * 160/760 | Answer: 29.47 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 350 V and draws an armature current of 21 A. If the armature resistance is 0.78 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 350, Ia = 21, Ra = 0.78 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 350 - 21*0.78 | Answer: 333.6 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 75 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.79. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 75, VL = 400, pf = 0.79 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*400*75*0.79 / 1000 | Answer: 41.05 kW

question: A load has real power 15 kW and apparent power 35 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 15, S = 35 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 15 / 35 | Answer: 0.4286

question: A machine delivers 10 kW output while drawing 197 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 10, Pi = 197 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 10/197 * 100 | Answer: 5.076 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 14 V across R1 = 15 ohm and R2 = 13 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 14, R1 = 15, R2 = 13 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 14*13 / (15+13) | Answer: 6.5 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 180 kohm and Rin = 28 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 180, Rin = 28 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 180 / 28 | Answer: 6.429

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 30 kohm and Rg = 37 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 30, Rg = 37 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 30/37 | Answer: 1.811

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 5413. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 5413 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(5413) | Answer: 37.33 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 3.6 m carries a central point load of 25 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.6, W = 25 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 25*3.6 / 4 | Answer: 22.5 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 7.6 m carries a UDL of 15 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7.6, w = 15 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 15*(7.6)^2 / 8 | Answer: 108.3 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 5.2 m carries a point load 45 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.2, W = 45 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 45*5.2 | Answer: 234 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 2.9 m carries a UDL of 24 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 2.9, w = 24 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 24*(2.9)^2 / 2 | Answer: 100.9 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 5.3 m carries a point load 50 kN at distance 3.7 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 5.3, a = 3.7, W = 50 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 50*(5.3 - 3.7) / 5.3 | Answer: 15.09 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 4.1 m) carries a central point load 10 kN. With E = 200 GPa and I = 210e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=10000 N, L=4100.0 mm, E=200000 MPa, I=210e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 0.3419 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 4.4 m carries a UDL of 42 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.4, w = 42 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 42*(4.4)^2 / 12 | Answer: 67.76 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 330 mm, clear cover 50 mm and main bars of diameter 20 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 330, c = 50, dia = 20 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 330 - 50 - 20/2 | Answer: 270 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 32.2 m^2 carrying a factored load of 16.4 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 32.2, w = 16.4 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 16.4 * 32.2 | Answer: 528.1 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 4.8 m, unit weight 20 kN/m^3, phi = 36 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 7.1 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 19 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 7.1, g = 19 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (19 - 9.81)*7.1 | Answer: 65.25 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 5.9e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.9, area = 5.1e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 5.9, i = 0.9, A = 5.1 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (5.9e-4)*0.9*(5.1e-3) | Answer: 2708 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.9 m, bed slope 0.001 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.025. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 3.2 m under a head of 1.1 m. Taking Cd = 0.61 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 2.9 m wide carries a discharge of 11 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 590 m and design speed 55 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 590, V = 55 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (55)^2 / (127*590) | Answer: 0.04037
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: A tank of volume 300 m^3 treats a flow of 100 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 300, Q = 100 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 300 / 100 | Answer: 3 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 400 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.31 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 7 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 400, k = 0.31, t = 7 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 400*(1 - e^(-0.31*7)) | Answer: 354.3 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.83, rainfall intensity 65 mm/h over a catchment of 18.7 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.83, i = 65, A = 18.7 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.83*65*18.7 / 360 | Answer: 2.802 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.05 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 130 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.05, M = 130 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 130*(30+0.05)/30 | Answer: 130.2 m

question: Convert the decimal number 1401 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 1401 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 579 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 11101110 and 11010001.
solution: XOR: 00111111 | Count of 1s = 6 | Answer: 6
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 280 megabits is sent over a link of 2 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 280, B = 2 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 280 / 2 | Answer: 140 s

question: A link has bandwidth 46 Mbps and round-trip time 170 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 46, R = 170 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 46e6 * 170e-3 bits = 7820 kb | Answer: 7820 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.84, cache access time 5 ns and main-memory access time 200 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.84, tc = 5, tm = 200 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.84*5 + (1 - 0.84)*200 | Answer: 36.2 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 622377 elements?
solution: Given: n = 622377 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(622377)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: An O(n^2) algorithm performs c*n^2 basic operations. If c = 1 and n = 2380, how many operations are performed?
solution: Given: n = 2380 | Formula: operations = n^2 | Substitute: = (2380)^2 | Answer: 5664400

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.019, memory access time 150 ns and page-fault service time 9 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 9 ms = 9000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.019)*150 + 0.019*9000000.0 ns | Answer: 171.1 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 1.2 m^3 at 250 kPa and 430 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 1.2, P = 250, Tk = 430 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (250e3)*1.2 / (8.314*430) | Answer: 83.92 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.32 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 15 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.32, t = 15 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.32*15) | Answer: 0.9918

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.13 /min) reaches 60% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.13, X = 60 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.6 / (0.13*(1 - 0.6)) | Answer: 11.54 min

question: For a reaction with A = 5e10 /s and activation energy 90 kJ/mol at 500 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 5, Ea = 90, Tk = 500 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 5e10 * exp(-90e3 / (8.314*500)) | Answer: 19.79 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.91 and bottoms xW = 0.04, with relative volatility alpha = 3.1. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.91, xw = 0.04, al = 3.1 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.91/0.09)(0.96/0.04)] / ln(3.1) | Answer: 4.854 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.87 and x = 0.24. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.87, x = 0.24 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.87/0.13) / (0.24/0.76) | Answer: 21.19

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.49 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 110 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.49, Psat = 110 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.49 * 110 | Answer: 53.9 kPa

question: A stream of 7.2 kg/s with specific heat 3.7 kJ/kg-K is heated through 15 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 7.2, cp = 3.7, dT = 15 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 7.2*3.7*15 | Answer: 399.6 kW

question: A reactor of volume 17.4 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 0.9 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 17.4, Q = 0.9 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 17.4 / 0.9 | Answer: 19.33 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 8e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 1 mm with a concentration difference of 110 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 8, L = 1, dC = 110 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (8e-9)*110 / (1e-3) | Answer: 880 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 8.3 min and steady-state gain 3.7. For a step input of magnitude 12, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 8.3, K = 3.7, M = 12 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 3.7 * 12 | Answer: 44.4 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 70 m^2 flies at 190 m/s (air density 0.4 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.4. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 70, V = 190, rho = 0.4, CL = 0.4 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.4*(190)^2*70*0.4 / 1000 | Answer: 202.2 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 60 m^2 flies at 110 m/s (density 1.225 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.11. Find the drag force in kN.
A specimen under stress 90 MPa shows an elastic strain of 1.2e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 90, eps = 1.2 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 90 / (1.2e-3) MPa = 75 GPa | Answer: 75 GPa

question: A block of mass 9 kg has a volume of 1.3e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 9, V = 1.3 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 9 / (1.3e-3) | Answer: 6923 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 700 mm is heated through 130 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 17e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 700, dT = 130, al = 17 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 700*17e-6*130 | Answer: 1.547 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 100 ohm, R2 = 15 ohm and R3 = 490 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 100, R2 = 15, R3 = 490 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 15*490 / 100 | Answer: 73.5 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 350 ohm and gauge factor 2 experiences a strain of 1100e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 350, GF = 2, eps = 1100 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 350*2*1100e-6 | Answer: 770 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 10.78 when the true value is 10. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10.78, true = 10 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10.78 - 10| / 10 * 100 | Answer: 7.8 %

question: Annual demand is 44500 units, ordering cost 130 per order and holding cost 8 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 44500, S = 130, H = 8 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*44500*130 / 8) | Answer: 1203 units

question: An asset costs 170000 with salvage value 14000 after 8 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 170000, Sv = 14000, n = 8 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (170000 - 14000) / 8 | Answer: 19500 per year

question: A product sells for 420 per unit with variable cost 180 per unit and fixed costs 160000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 420, V = 180, F = 160000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 160000 / (420 - 180) | Answer: 666.7 units

question: Find the present worth of 90000 received 7 years from now at an interest rate of 5% per year.
solution: Given: F = 90000, n = 7, i = 5 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 90000 / (1 + 0.05)^7 | Answer: 63961 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.91, 0.99 and 0.95 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.91, r2 = 0.99, r3 = 0.95 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.91*0.99*0.95 | Answer: 0.8559

question: A process produces 42 defective items in a batch of 7500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 42, N = 7500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 42/7500 * 1e6 | Answer: 5600 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = 5x^3 + 5x^2 + 2 evaluated at x = 1.
For f(x) = x^3 + 2x^2 - 4x + 3, find f''(x) at x = 5.
Evaluate the definite integral of (-5x^2 - 2) dx from x = 2 to x = 6.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = -5x^3/3 + 0x^2/2 + -2x | Evaluate F(6) - F(2) | Answer: -354.7
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of x^2 - 12x - 5 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[-6, 8], [3, -6]].
solution: Given: a = -6, b = 8, c = 3, d = -6 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (-6)(-6) - (8)(3) | Answer: 12

question: Find the determinant of [[-2, 4, -6], [0, -2, -4], [-1, -3, -2]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: 44

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[-1, 4], [1, 0]].
solution: Trace tr = -1, Determinant = -4 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 1.562

question: Solve for x: 3x + 0y = -10 and -6x + 4y = 8.
solution: Determinant = 3*4 - 0*-6 = 12 | x = (e d - b f) / det = -3.333 | Answer: x = -3.333
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 18, 89, 57, 22, 70.
solution: Sum = 256 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 51.2 | Answer: 51.2

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 29, 4, 14, 2, 4.
solution: Mean = 10.6 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 11.3

question: Find the slope of the line through (2, 4) and (-6, -9).
solution: Given: x1 = 2, y1 = 4, x2 = -6, y2 = -9 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (-9 - 4) / (-6 - 2) | Answer: 1.625

question: Find the distance between the points (7, -3) and (-2, 4).
solution: Given: x1 = 7, y1 = -3, x2 = -2, y2 = 4 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-9)^2 + (7)^2) | Answer: 11.4 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (-3,2), (-3,3), (0,8).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 1.5 sq units

question: Find the 19th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 15 and common difference -6.
solution: Given: a = 15, d = -6, n = 19 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = 15 + (19 - 1)*-6 | Answer: -93

question: Find the sum of the first 11 terms of an AP with first term -11 and common difference 7.
solution: Given: a = -11, d = 7, n = 11 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 11/2 [2*-11 + (11-1)*7] | Answer: 264

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 33000 at 6.6% per annum for 8 years.
solution: Given: P = 33000, R = 6.6, Tt = 8 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 33000 * 6.6 * 8 / 100 | Answer: 17424 currency units

question: Find the amount when 5500 is invested at 8% per annum compounded annually for 5 years.
solution: Given: P = 5500, R = 8, Tt = 5 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 5500 * (1 + 8/100)^5 | Answer: 8081 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (-4, -3, 5) and (-3, 6, -7).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (-1, -2, 4) and (-2, -5, 5).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 10.49

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (-1, -6, -6) and (3, -2, 5).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 113.5 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number 5 + 10i.
solution: Given: a = 5, b = 10 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((5)^2 + (10)^2) | Answer: 11.18

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number -12 + -3i.
solution: Given: a = -12, b = -3 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(-3, -12) | Answer: -166 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = 4x^3 + 4x^2 + 5x + 1 at x = 0.
solution: Given: a = 4, b = 4, c = 5, d = 1, x0 = 0 | Formula: f(x0) = a x0^3 + b x0^2 + c x0 + d | Substitute: f(0) = 4(0)^3 + 4(0)^2 + 5(0) + 1 | Answer: 1

question: Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-100 with initial guess x0=2, find x1 (one iteration).
solution: Given: N = 100, x0 = 2 | Formula: x1 = x0 - (x0^2 - N)/(2 x0) | Substitute: x1 = 2 - ((2)^2 - 100)/(2*2) | Answer: 26

question: Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.1 and ordinates 13, 3, 6, 4, 1, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 474 and 250.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 474 and 250 | Answer: GCD = 2

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 61 and 31.
solution: Given: a = 61, b = 31 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 61*31 / 1 | Answer: 1891
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 49 mm carries an axial tensile load of 51 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 36 mm and length 2600 mm carries an axial load of 58 kN. Take E = 70 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 35 mm transmits a torque of 150 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 35, Tt = 150 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(150*1000) / (pi*(35)^3) | Answer: 17.82 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 55 mm and length 1900 mm carries a torque of 1150 N-m. With G = 80 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (55)^4 / 32 = 898361 mm^4 | theta = (1150*1000)(1900) / (80000 * 898361) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 1.742 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 59 mm wide and 190 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 59, h = 190 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 59*(190)^2 / 6 | Answer: 354983 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (48 mm x 190 mm) carries a bending moment of 7 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (39 mm x 120 mm) has effective length 1800 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 300 MPa is designed for a working stress of 80 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 300, sw = 80 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 300 / 80 | Answer: 3.75

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 700 mm and wall thickness 9 mm carries an internal pressure of 1.9 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 700, t = 9, P = 1.9 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 1.9*700 / (2*9) | Answer: 73.89 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 880 K and 300 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 880, Tc = 300 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 300/880) * 100 | Answer: 65.91 %

question: A refrigerator works between 273 K (cold) and 302 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 273, Th = 302 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 273 / (302 - 273) | Answer: 9.414

question: A heat pump operates between 273 K and 316 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 273, Th = 316 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 316 / (316 - 273) | Answer: 7.349

question: 5.3 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 200 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 5.3, dT = 200 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 5.3 * 0.718 * 200 | Answer: 761.1 kJ

question: 4.4 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 100 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.4, dT = 100 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 4.4 * 1.005 * 100 | Answer: 442.2 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 2.4 m^3 at 320 K with mass 1.8 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 2.4, Tk = 320, m = 1.8 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 1.8*0.287*320 / 2.4 | Answer: 68.88 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 3.5 kg of air expands isothermally at 440 K from volume V1 to 2*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.5, Tk = 440, ratio = 2 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 3.5*0.287*440*ln(2) | Answer: 306.4 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 1.4 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.09 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 1.4, D = 0.09 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*1.4*0.09 / 0.001 | Answer: 126000

question: Water flows at 1.7 m/s through a pipe of diameter 150 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 6.1 m. Taking Cv = 0.98, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 6.1, cv = 0.98 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.98*sqrt(2*9.81*6.1) | Answer: 10.72 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 260 mm) water flows at 1.3 m/s. It contracts to diameter 100 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
Water flows at 1.7 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.49 m and length 50 m. With friction factor f = 0.023, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 27 teeth drives a gear of 84 teeth. If the pinion runs at 450 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 27, z2 = 84, N1 = 450 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 450*27 / 84 | Answer: 144.6 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 340 mm rotates at 1050 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 340, N = 1050 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.34)*1050 / 60 | Answer: 18.69 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 23 kW at 250 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 23, N = 250 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(23*1000) / (2*pi*250) | Answer: 878.5 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 5.9 kg rotates at radius 0.17 m at 1150 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 7400 N/m and mass 19.5 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 7400, m = 19.5 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(7400/19.5) | Answer: 3.1 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 2.4 m^2 and thickness 0.36 m has conductivity k = 5.8 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 180 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 2.4, L = 0.36, k = 5.8, dT = 180 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 5.8*2.4*180 / 0.36 | Answer: 6960 W

question: A surface of area 2.9 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 35 W/m^2-K to surroundings 55 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 2.9, h = 35, dT = 55 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 35*2.9*55 | Answer: 5582 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 140 m/min, feed = 0.19 mm/rev, depth of cut = 0.9 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 140, f = 0.19, d = 0.9 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*140*0.19*0.9 | Answer: 23940 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 330 mm is turned at 900 rpm with a feed of 0.35 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 330, N = 900, f = 0.35 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 330 / (0.35*900) | Answer: 1.048 min

question: A resistor of 105 ohm carries a current of 0.9 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 105, I = 0.9 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 0.9 * 105 | Answer: 94.5 V

question: Three resistors 44 ohm, 92 ohm and 33 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 44, R2 = 92, R3 = 33 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 44 + 92 + 33 | Answer: 169 ohm

question: Two resistors 111 ohm and 103 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 111, R2 = 103 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 111*103 / (111+103) | Answer: 53.43 ohm

question: A device draws 0.9 A at 80 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 80, I = 0.9 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 80 * 0.9 | Answer: 72 W

question: A current of 11.1 A flows through a 65 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 11.1, R = 65 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (11.1)^2 * 65 | Answer: 8009 W

question: Two capacitors 25.6 uF and 3.8 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 25.6, C2 = 3.8 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 25.6*3.8 / (25.6+3.8) | Answer: 3.309 uF

question: A resistor 77 kohm and capacitor 12.9 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 77, C = 12.9 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (77k)(12.9u) = 993.3 ms | Answer: 993.3 ms

question: An inductor 434.9 mH is in series with 130 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 434.9, R = 130 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (434.9e-3) / 130 | Answer: 3.345 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 26.5 mH inductor at 410 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 26.5, f = 410 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (410)(26.5e-3) | Answer: 68.27 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 6.3 uF capacitor at 1000 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 6.3, f = 1000 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (1000)(6.3e-6)) | Answer: 25.26 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 14 ohm, XL = 75 ohm and XC = 54 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 14, XL = 75, XC = 54 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(14^2 + (75 - 54)^2) | Answer: 25.24 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 69.3 mH and C = 1.8 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 69.3, C = 1.8 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(69.3e-3 * 1.8e-6)) | Answer: 450.6 Hz

question: A capacitor of 98.5 uF is charged to 385 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 98.5, V = 385 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*98.5e-6*(385)^2 | Answer: 73 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 380 V with 280 primary turns and 390 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 380, N1 = 280, N2 = 390 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 380 * 390/280 | Answer: 529.3 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 380 V and draws an armature current of 42 A. If the armature resistance is 1.27 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 380, Ia = 42, Ra = 1.27 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 380 - 42*1.27 | Answer: 326.7 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 160 A at 433 V (line) with a power factor of 0.87. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 160, VL = 433, pf = 0.87 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*433*160*0.87 / 1000 | Answer: 104.4 kW

question: A load has real power 80 kW and apparent power 90 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 80, S = 90 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 80 / 90 | Answer: 0.8889

question: A machine delivers 55 kW output while drawing 202 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 55, Pi = 202 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 55/202 * 100 | Answer: 27.23 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 22 V across R1 = 29 ohm and R2 = 6 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 22, R1 = 29, R2 = 6 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 22*6 / (29+6) | Answer: 3.771 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 50 kohm and Rin = 43 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 50, Rin = 43 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 50 / 43 | Answer: 1.163

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 90 kohm and Rg = 9 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 90, Rg = 9 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 90/9 | Answer: 11

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 2527. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 2527 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(2527) | Answer: 34.03 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.7 m carries a central point load of 15 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.7, W = 15 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 15*4.7 / 4 | Answer: 17.62 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 3.5 m carries a UDL of 25 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.5, w = 25 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 25*(3.5)^2 / 8 | Answer: 38.28 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 4.9 m carries a point load 25 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.9, W = 25 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 25*4.9 | Answer: 122.5 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 6 m carries a UDL of 16 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6, w = 16 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 16*(6)^2 / 2 | Answer: 288 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.5 m carries a point load 45 kN at distance 2.2 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 4.5, a = 2.2, W = 45 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 45*(4.5 - 2.2) / 4.5 | Answer: 23 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 5.9 m) carries a central point load 45 kN. With E = 30 GPa and I = 100e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=45000 N, L=5900.0 mm, E=30000 MPa, I=100e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 64.18 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 6.9 m carries a UDL of 12 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6.9, w = 12 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 12*(6.9)^2 / 12 | Answer: 47.61 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 670 mm, clear cover 25 mm and main bars of diameter 25 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 670, c = 25, dia = 25 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 670 - 25 - 25/2 | Answer: 632.5 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 25.9 m^2 carrying a factored load of 15.2 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 25.9, w = 15.2 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 15.2 * 25.9 | Answer: 393.7 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 5.6 m, unit weight 16 kN/m^3, phi = 34 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 1.6e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.2, area = 6.8e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 1.6, i = 0.2, A = 6.8 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (1.6e-4)*0.2*(6.8e-3) | Answer: 217.6 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 0.5 m, bed slope 0.005 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.022. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 4.5 m under a head of 0.7 m. Taking Cd = 0.6 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 4.4 m wide carries a discharge of 24.3 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 230 m and design speed 50 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 230, V = 50 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (50)^2 / (127*230) | Answer: 0.08559
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: A tank of volume 810 m^3 treats a flow of 35 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 810, Q = 35 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 810 / 35 | Answer: 23.14 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 400 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.27 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 8 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 400, k = 0.27, t = 8 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 400*(1 - e^(-0.27*8)) | Answer: 353.9 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.47, rainfall intensity 95 mm/h over a catchment of 51.8 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.47, i = 95, A = 51.8 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.47*95*51.8 / 360 | Answer: 6.425 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.01 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 700 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.01, M = 700 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 700*(30+0.01)/30 | Answer: 700.2 m

question: Convert the decimal number 2981 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 2981 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: BA5 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 01011000 and 11111010.
solution: XOR: 10100010 | Count of 1s = 3 | Answer: 3
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 810 megabits is sent over a link of 77 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 810, B = 77 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 810 / 77 | Answer: 10.52 s

question: A link has bandwidth 31 Mbps and round-trip time 70 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 31, R = 70 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 31e6 * 70e-3 bits = 2170 kb | Answer: 2170 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.85, cache access time 7 ns and main-memory access time 170 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.85, tc = 7, tm = 170 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.85*7 + (1 - 0.85)*170 | Answer: 31.45 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 784034 elements?
solution: Given: n = 784034 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(784034)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.006, memory access time 180 ns and page-fault service time 3 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 3 ms = 3000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.006)*180 + 0.006*3000000.0 ns | Answer: 18.18 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 2.9 m^3 at 200 kPa and 330 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 2.9, P = 200, Tk = 330 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (200e3)*2.9 / (8.314*330) | Answer: 211.4 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.22 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 20 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.22, t = 20 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.22*20) | Answer: 0.9877

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.48 /min) is to reach 50% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.48, X = 50 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.5) / 0.48 | Answer: 1.444 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.14 /min) reaches 80% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.14, X = 80 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.8 / (0.14*(1 - 0.8)) | Answer: 28.57 min

question: For a reaction with A = 5e10 /s and activation energy 60 kJ/mol at 400 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 5, Ea = 60, Tk = 400 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 5e10 * exp(-60e3 / (8.314*400)) | Answer: 730.3 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.99 and bottoms xW = 0.04, with relative volatility alpha = 2.2. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.99, xw = 0.04, al = 2.2 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.99/0.01)(0.96/0.04)] / ln(2.2) | Answer: 9.859 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.66 and x = 0.42. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.66, x = 0.42 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.66/0.34) / (0.42/0.58) | Answer: 2.681

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.21 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 60 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.21, Psat = 60 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.21 * 60 | Answer: 12.6 kPa

question: A stream of 6.6 kg/s with specific heat 3.7 kJ/kg-K is heated through 105 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 6.6, cp = 3.7, dT = 105 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 6.6*3.7*105 | Answer: 2564 kW

question: A reactor of volume 13.7 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 4.7 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 13.7, Q = 4.7 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 13.7 / 4.7 | Answer: 2.915 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 8.4e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 4 mm with a concentration difference of 60 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 8.4, L = 4, dC = 60 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (8.4e-9)*60 / (4e-3) | Answer: 126 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 8 min and steady-state gain 3. For a step input of magnitude 10, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 8, K = 3, M = 10 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 3 * 10 | Answer: 30 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 60 m^2 flies at 60 m/s (air density 0.7 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.8. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 60, V = 60, rho = 0.7, CL = 0.8 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.7*(60)^2*60*0.8 / 1000 | Answer: 60.48 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 80 m^2 flies at 210 m/s (density 1 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.04. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 80, V = 210, rho = 1, CD = 0.04 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*1*(210)^2*80*0.04 / 1000 | Answer: 70.56 kN

question: A specimen under stress 250 MPa shows an elastic strain of 1.5e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 250, eps = 1.5 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 250 / (1.5e-3) MPa = 166.7 GPa | Answer: 166.7 GPa

question: A block of mass 19 kg has a volume of 1e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 19, V = 1 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 19 / (1e-3) | Answer: 19000 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 1000 mm is heated through 100 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 11e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 1000, dT = 100, al = 11 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 1000*11e-6*100 | Answer: 1.1 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 150 ohm, R2 = 10 ohm and R3 = 230 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 150, R2 = 10, R3 = 230 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 10*230 / 150 | Answer: 15.33 ohm

question: A measurement reads 9.54 when the true value is 10. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.54, true = 10 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.54 - 10| / 10 * 100 | Answer: 4.6 %

question: Annual demand is 13500 units, ordering cost 160 per order and holding cost 4 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 13500, S = 160, H = 4 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*13500*160 / 4) | Answer: 1039 units

question: An asset costs 150000 with salvage value 32000 after 9 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 150000, Sv = 32000, n = 9 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (150000 - 32000) / 9 | Answer: 13111 per year

question: A product sells for 240 per unit with variable cost 110 per unit and fixed costs 150000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 240, V = 110, F = 150000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 150000 / (240 - 110) | Answer: 1154 units

question: Find the present worth of 15000 received 9 years from now at an interest rate of 5% per year.
solution: Given: F = 15000, n = 9, i = 5 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 15000 / (1 + 0.05)^9 | Answer: 9669 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.94, 0.95 and 0.94 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.94, r2 = 0.95, r3 = 0.94 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.94*0.95*0.94 | Answer: 0.8394

question: A process produces 50 defective items in a batch of 18500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).

question: Find the slope of the line through (-3, -6) and (4, 7).
solution: Given: x1 = -3, y1 = -6, x2 = 4, y2 = 7 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (7 - -6) / (4 - -3) | Answer: 1.857

question: Find the distance between the points (-8, -7) and (6, -8).
solution: Given: x1 = -8, y1 = -7, x2 = 6, y2 = -8 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((14)^2 + (-1)^2) | Answer: 14.04 units

question: Find the 38th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -11 and common difference 2.
solution: Given: a = -11, d = 2, n = 38 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -11 + (38 - 1)*2 | Answer: 63

question: Find the sum of the first 40 terms of an AP with first term -5 and common difference -8.
solution: Given: a = -5, d = -8, n = 40 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 40/2 [2*-5 + (40-1)*-8] | Answer: -6440

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 34000 at 10.2% per annum for 5 years.
solution: Given: P = 34000, R = 10.2, Tt = 5 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 34000 * 10.2 * 5 / 100 | Answer: 17340 currency units

question: Find the amount when 24500 is invested at 6.1% per annum compounded annually for 5 years.
solution: Given: P = 24500, R = 6.1, Tt = 5 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 24500 * (1 + 6.1/100)^5 | Answer: 32941 currency units

question: Find the modulus of the complex number -8 + 6i.
solution: Given: a = -8, b = 6 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((-8)^2 + (6)^2) | Answer: 10

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number 1 + 2i.
solution: Given: a = 1, b = 2 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(2, 1) | Answer: 63.43 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -5x^3 + 7x^2 + 5x - 2 at x = 0.

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 36 and 57.
solution: Given: a = 36, b = 57 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 36*57 / 3 | Answer: 684

question: A circular rod of diameter 20 mm carries an axial tensile load of 16 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 30 mm and length 1700 mm carries an axial load of 66 kN. Take E = 70 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 54 mm transmits a torque of 350 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 54, Tt = 350 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(350*1000) / (pi*(54)^3) | Answer: 11.32 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 63 mm and length 1600 mm carries a torque of 450 N-m. With G = 80 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (63)^4 / 32 = 1546543 mm^4 | theta = (450*1000)(1600) / (80000 * 1546543) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 0.3334 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 62 mm wide and 80 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 62, h = 80 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 62*(80)^2 / 6 | Answer: 66133 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (113 mm x 200 mm) carries a bending moment of 32 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (30 mm x 100 mm) has effective length 2900 mm and E = 200 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 770 MPa is designed for a working stress of 110 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 770, sw = 110 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 770 / 110 | Answer: 7

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 950 mm and wall thickness 14 mm carries an internal pressure of 2.1 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 950, t = 14, P = 2.1 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 2.1*950 / (2*14) | Answer: 71.25 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 880 K and 330 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 880, Tc = 330 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 330/880) * 100 | Answer: 62.5 %

question: A refrigerator works between 254 K (cold) and 322 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 254, Th = 322 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 254 / (322 - 254) | Answer: 3.735

question: A heat pump operates between 283 K and 304 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 283, Th = 304 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 304 / (304 - 283) | Answer: 14.48

question: 1 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 35 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1, dT = 35 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 1 * 0.718 * 35 | Answer: 25.13 kJ

question: 5 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 50 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 5, dT = 50 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 5 * 1.005 * 50 | Answer: 251.2 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 3.1 m^3 at 340 K with mass 1.2 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 3.1, Tk = 340, m = 1.2 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 1.2*0.287*340 / 3.1 | Answer: 37.77 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 4.3 kg of air expands isothermally at 410 K from volume V1 to 2*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.3, Tk = 410, ratio = 2 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 4.3*0.287*410*ln(2) | Answer: 350.7 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 2.8 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.27 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 2.8, D = 0.27 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*2.8*0.27 / 0.001 | Answer: 756000

question: Water flows at 0.5 m/s through a pipe of diameter 110 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 1.2 m. Taking Cv = 0.96, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 1.2, cv = 0.96 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.96*sqrt(2*9.81*1.2) | Answer: 4.658 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 290 mm) water flows at 2.1 m/s. It contracts to diameter 90 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 290, d2 = 90, V1 = 2.1 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 2.1*(290/90)^2 | Answer: 21.8 m/s

question: Water flows at 1.6 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.47 m and length 140 m. With friction factor f = 0.022, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 30 teeth drives a gear of 59 teeth. If the pinion runs at 950 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 30, z2 = 59, N1 = 950 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 950*30 / 59 | Answer: 483.1 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 530 mm rotates at 550 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 530, N = 550 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.53)*550 / 60 | Answer: 15.26 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 5.8 kW at 800 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 5.8, N = 800 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(5.8*1000) / (2*pi*800) | Answer: 69.23 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 8.3 kg rotates at radius 0.3 m at 1050 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 13300 N/m and mass 6.6 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 13300, m = 6.6 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(13300/6.6) | Answer: 7.145 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 2.8 m^2 and thickness 0.24 m has conductivity k = 47.9 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 45 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 2.8, L = 0.24, k = 47.9, dT = 45 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 47.9*2.8*45 / 0.24 | Answer: 25147 W

question: A surface of area 3 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 70 W/m^2-K to surroundings 120 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.

question: In turning, cutting speed = 240 m/min, feed = 0.18 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2.9 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.

question: A workpiece of length 330 mm is turned at 1000 rpm with a feed of 0.25 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.

question: A resistor of 179 ohm carries a current of 3.3 A. Find the voltage across it.

question: Three resistors 44 ohm, 94 ohm and 83 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 44, R2 = 94, R3 = 83 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 44 + 94 + 83 | Answer: 221 ohm

question: Two resistors 2 ohm and 70 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 2, R2 = 70 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 2*70 / (2+70) | Answer: 1.944 ohm

question: A device draws 8 A at 50 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 50, I = 8 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 50 * 8 | Answer: 400 W

question: A current of 4.7 A flows through a 117 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.

question: Two capacitors 5.5 uF and 9.1 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 5.5, C2 = 9.1 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 5.5*9.1 / (5.5+9.1) | Answer: 3.428 uF

question: A resistor 93 kohm and capacitor 14.1 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 93, C = 14.1 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (93k)(14.1u) = 1311 ms | Answer: 1311 ms

question: An inductor 150.9 mH is in series with 93 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 90.2 mH inductor at 70 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 90.2, f = 70 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (70)(90.2e-3) | Answer: 39.67 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 45.9 uF capacitor at 650 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 45.9, f = 650 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (650)(45.9e-6)) | Answer: 5.335 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 53 ohm, XL = 51 ohm and XC = 130 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 53, XL = 51, XC = 130 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(53^2 + (51 - 130)^2) | Answer: 95.13 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 84 mH and C = 8.1 uF (in Hz).

question: A capacitor of 70.5 uF is charged to 215 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.

question: A transformer has primary voltage 320 V with 840 primary turns and 210 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 320, N1 = 840, N2 = 210 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 320 * 210/840 | Answer: 80 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 290 V and draws an armature current of 38 A. If the armature resistance is 0.7 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 290, Ia = 38, Ra = 0.7 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 290 - 38*0.7 | Answer: 263.4 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 110 A at 433 V (line) with a power factor of 0.73. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 110, VL = 433, pf = 0.73 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*433*110*0.73 / 1000 | Answer: 60.22 kW

question: A load has real power 20 kW and apparent power 135 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 20, S = 135 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 20 / 135 | Answer: 0.1481

question: A machine delivers 25 kW output while drawing 32 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 25, Pi = 32 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 25/32 * 100 | Answer: 78.12 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 7 V across R1 = 48 ohm and R2 = 28 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 7, R1 = 48, R2 = 28 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 7*28 / (48+28) | Answer: 2.579 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 90 kohm and Rin = 26 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 90 kohm and Rg = 24 kohm. Find the voltage gain.

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 4225. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 4225 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(4225) | Answer: 36.26 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.3 m carries a central point load of 80 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6.3, W = 80 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 80*6.3 / 4 | Answer: 126 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 7.1 m carries a UDL of 5 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7.1, w = 5 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 5*(7.1)^2 / 8 | Answer: 31.51 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 2 m carries a point load 65 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 2, W = 65 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 65*2 | Answer: 130 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 5.3 m carries a UDL of 20 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.3, w = 20 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 20*(5.3)^2 / 2 | Answer: 280.9 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.1 m carries a point load 90 kN at distance 3 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 4.1, a = 3, W = 90 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 90*(4.1 - 3) / 4.1 | Answer: 24.15 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 5.7 m) carries a central point load 55 kN. With E = 200 GPa and I = 240e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=55000 N, L=5700.0 mm, E=200000 MPa, I=240e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 4.421 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 4.3 m carries a UDL of 42 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.3, w = 42 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 42*(4.3)^2 / 12 | Answer: 64.71 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 670 mm, clear cover 50 mm and main bars of diameter 12 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 670, c = 50, dia = 12 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 670 - 50 - 12/2 | Answer: 614 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 37.6 m^2 carrying a factored load of 8.8 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 37.6, w = 8.8 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 8.8 * 37.6 | Answer: 330.9 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 7 m, unit weight 20 kN/m^3, phi = 28 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 6.3e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.7, area = 6.2e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 6.3, i = 0.7, A = 6.2 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (6.3e-4)*0.7*(6.2e-3) | Answer: 2734 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 2.3 m, bed slope 0.005 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.02. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 1.6 m under a head of 0.3 m. Taking Cd = 0.61 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.

question: A rectangular channel 5.1 m wide carries a discharge of 27.9 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).

solution: Given: R = 360, V = 45 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (45)^2 / (127*360) | Answer: 0.04429
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: A tank of volume 790 m^3 treats a flow of 130 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 790, Q = 130 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 790 / 130 | Answer: 6.077 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 370 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.23 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 6 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 370, k = 0.23, t = 6 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 370*(1 - e^(-0.23*6)) | Answer: 276.9 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.79, rainfall intensity 100 mm/h over a catchment of 36.9 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.

formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.05 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 370 m with this tape.

question: A file of 580 megabits is sent over a link of 86 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
