solution: Given: m = 3.8, dT = 25 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 3.8 * 1.005 * 25 | Answer: 95.47 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 2.3 m^3 at 420 K with mass 1.5 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 2.3, Tk = 420, m = 1.5 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 1.5*0.287*420 / 2.3 | Answer: 78.61 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 4.6 kg of air expands isothermally at 410 K from volume V1 to 4*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.6, Tk = 410, ratio = 4 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 4.6*0.287*410*ln(4) | Answer: 750.4 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 1.5 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.08 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 1.5, D = 0.08 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*1.5*0.08 / 0.001 | Answer: 120000

question: Water flows at 2.8 m/s through a pipe of diameter 100 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 14.7 m. Taking Cv = 0.97, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 14.7, cv = 0.97 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.97*sqrt(2*9.81*14.7) | Answer: 16.47 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 310 mm) water flows at 0.7 m/s. It contracts to diameter 60 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 310, d2 = 60, V1 = 0.7 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 0.7*(310/60)^2 | Answer: 18.69 m/s

question: Water flows at 1.6 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.32 m and length 220 m. With friction factor f = 0.027, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 22 teeth drives a gear of 62 teeth. If the pinion runs at 650 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 22, z2 = 62, N1 = 650 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 650*22 / 62 | Answer: 230.6 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 500 mm rotates at 500 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 500, N = 500 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.5)*500 / 60 | Answer: 13.09 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 26.2 kW at 1150 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 26.2, N = 1150 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(26.2*1000) / (2*pi*1150) | Answer: 217.6 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 5.3 kg rotates at radius 0.13 m at 600 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 5200 N/m and mass 7.9 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 5200, m = 7.9 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(5200/7.9) | Answer: 4.083 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 3.4 m^2 and thickness 0.18 m has conductivity k = 37.9 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 160 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 3.4, L = 0.18, k = 37.9, dT = 160 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 37.9*3.4*160 / 0.18 | Answer: 114542 W

question: A surface of area 1.7 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 185 W/m^2-K to surroundings 80 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 1.7, h = 185, dT = 80 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 185*1.7*80 | Answer: 25160 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 140 m/min, feed = 0.15 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2.6 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 140, f = 0.15, d = 2.6 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*140*0.15*2.6 | Answer: 54600 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 120 mm is turned at 1100 rpm with a feed of 0.18 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 120, N = 1100, f = 0.18 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 120 / (0.18*1100) | Answer: 0.6061 min

question: A resistor of 29 ohm carries a current of 6.7 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 29, I = 6.7 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 6.7 * 29 | Answer: 194.3 V

question: Three resistors 4 ohm, 73 ohm and 43 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 4, R2 = 73, R3 = 43 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 4 + 73 + 43 | Answer: 120 ohm

question: Two resistors 35 ohm and 34 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 35, R2 = 34 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 35*34 / (35+34) | Answer: 17.25 ohm

question: A device draws 7.6 A at 155 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 155, I = 7.6 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 155 * 7.6 | Answer: 1178 W

question: A current of 2.5 A flows through a 136 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 2.5, R = 136 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (2.5)^2 * 136 | Answer: 850 W

question: Two capacitors 2.3 uF and 21.3 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 2.3, C2 = 21.3 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 2.3*21.3 / (2.3+21.3) | Answer: 2.076 uF

question: A resistor 27 kohm and capacitor 8.1 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 27, C = 8.1 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (27k)(8.1u) = 218.7 ms | Answer: 218.7 ms

question: An inductor 482.9 mH is in series with 168 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 482.9, R = 168 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (482.9e-3) / 168 | Answer: 2.874 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 192.3 mH inductor at 960 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 192.3, f = 960 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (960)(192.3e-3) | Answer: 116 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 14.2 uF capacitor at 180 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 14.2, f = 180 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (180)(14.2e-6)) | Answer: 62.27 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 97 ohm, XL = 56 ohm and XC = 87 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 97, XL = 56, XC = 87 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(97^2 + (56 - 87)^2) | Answer: 101.8 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 80.8 mH and C = 8.5 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 80.8, C = 8.5 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(80.8e-3 * 8.5e-6)) | Answer: 192 Hz

question: A capacitor of 97.5 uF is charged to 200 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 97.5, V = 200 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*97.5e-6*(200)^2 | Answer: 1950 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 340 V with 820 primary turns and 360 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 340, N1 = 820, N2 = 360 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 340 * 360/820 | Answer: 149.3 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 190 V and draws an armature current of 47 A. If the armature resistance is 0.26 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 190, Ia = 47, Ra = 0.26 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 190 - 47*0.26 | Answer: 177.8 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 65 A at 433 V (line) with a power factor of 0.94. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 65, VL = 433, pf = 0.94 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*433*65*0.94 / 1000 | Answer: 45.82 kW

question: A load has real power 30 kW and apparent power 165 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 30, S = 165 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 30 / 165 | Answer: 0.1818

question: A machine delivers 155 kW output while drawing 192 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 155, Pi = 192 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 155/192 * 100 | Answer: 80.73 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 13 V across R1 = 27 ohm and R2 = 47 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 13, R1 = 27, R2 = 47 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 13*47 / (27+47) | Answer: 8.257 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 110 kohm and Rin = 11 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 110, Rin = 11 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 110 / 11 | Answer: 10

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 80 kohm and Rg = 20 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 80, Rg = 20 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 80/20 | Answer: 5

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 5868. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 5868 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(5868) | Answer: 37.68 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 3.8 m carries a central point load of 10 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.8, W = 10 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 10*3.8 / 4 | Answer: 9.5 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 8.2 m carries a UDL of 40 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 8.2, w = 40 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 40*(8.2)^2 / 8 | Answer: 336.2 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 6 m carries a point load 60 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6, W = 60 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 60*6 | Answer: 360 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 3.7 m carries a UDL of 22 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.7, w = 22 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 22*(3.7)^2 / 2 | Answer: 150.6 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 4 m carries a point load 60 kN at distance 1.6 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 4, a = 1.6, W = 60 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 60*(4 - 1.6) / 4 | Answer: 36 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 5.7 m) carries a central point load 25 kN. With E = 30 GPa and I = 140e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=25000 N, L=5700.0 mm, E=30000 MPa, I=140e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 22.97 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 8.8 m carries a UDL of 9 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 8.8, w = 9 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 9*(8.8)^2 / 12 | Answer: 58.08 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 480 mm, clear cover 25 mm and main bars of diameter 12 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 480, c = 25, dia = 12 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 480 - 25 - 12/2 | Answer: 449 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 17.6 m^2 carrying a factored load of 14.4 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 17.6, w = 14.4 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 14.4 * 17.6 | Answer: 253.4 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 6.6 m, unit weight 19 kN/m^3, phi = 31 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 7.7 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 21 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 7.7, g = 21 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (21 - 9.81)*7.7 | Answer: 86.16 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 8.4e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.3, area = 5.1e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 8.4, i = 0.3, A = 5.1 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (8.4e-4)*0.3*(5.1e-3) | Answer: 1285 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 0.8 m, bed slope 0.008 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.015. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 4 m under a head of 0.2 m. Taking Cd = 0.64 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 2.3 m wide carries a discharge of 24.8 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 380 m and design speed 60 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 380, V = 60 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (60)^2 / (127*380) | Answer: 0.0746
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: A tank of volume 410 m^3 treats a flow of 165 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 410, Q = 165 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 410 / 165 | Answer: 2.485 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 280 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.24 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 4 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 280, k = 0.24, t = 4 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 280*(1 - e^(-0.24*4)) | Answer: 172.8 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.9, rainfall intensity 65 mm/h over a catchment of 29.4 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.9, i = 65, A = 29.4 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.9*65*29.4 / 360 | Answer: 4.777 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.02 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 100 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.02, M = 100 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 100*(20+0.02)/20 | Answer: 100.1 m

question: Convert the decimal number 1156 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 1156 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 484 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 01101100 and 11110011.
solution: XOR: 10011111 | Count of 1s = 6 | Answer: 6
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 130 megabits is sent over a link of 96 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 130, B = 96 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 130 / 96 | Answer: 1.354 s

question: A link has bandwidth 100 Mbps and round-trip time 130 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 100, R = 130 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 100e6 * 130e-3 bits = 13000 kb | Answer: 13000 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.84, cache access time 6 ns and main-memory access time 60 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.84, tc = 6, tm = 60 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.84*6 + (1 - 0.84)*60 | Answer: 14.64 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 93405 elements?
solution: Given: n = 93405 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(93405)) + 1 | Answer: 17

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.003, memory access time 140 ns and page-fault service time 4 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 4 ms = 4000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.003)*140 + 0.003*4000000.0 ns | Answer: 12.14 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 2.6 m^3 at 270 kPa and 480 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 2.6, P = 270, Tk = 480 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (270e3)*2.6 / (8.314*480) | Answer: 175.9 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.28 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 19 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.28, t = 19 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.28*19) | Answer: 0.9951

question: For a reaction with A = 5e10 /s and activation energy 50 kJ/mol at 340 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 5, Ea = 50, Tk = 340 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 5e10 * exp(-50e3 / (8.314*340)) | Answer: 104 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.91 and bottoms xW = 0.09, with relative volatility alpha = 2.6. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.91, xw = 0.09, al = 2.6 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.91/0.09)(0.91/0.09)] / ln(2.6) | Answer: 4.843 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.64 and x = 0.27. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.64, x = 0.27 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.64/0.36) / (0.27/0.73) | Answer: 4.807

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.46 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 45 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.46, Psat = 45 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.46 * 45 | Answer: 20.7 kPa

question: A stream of 6.2 kg/s with specific heat 2 kJ/kg-K is heated through 80 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 6.2, cp = 2, dT = 80 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 6.2*2*80 | Answer: 992 kW

question: A reactor of volume 9.3 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 4.3 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 9.3, Q = 4.3 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 9.3 / 4.3 | Answer: 2.163 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 6.3e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 4 mm with a concentration difference of 110 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 6.3, L = 4, dC = 110 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (6.3e-9)*110 / (4e-3) | Answer: 173.2 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 5.5 min and steady-state gain 1.6. For a step input of magnitude 5, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 5.5, K = 1.6, M = 5 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 1.6 * 5 | Answer: 8 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 45 m^2 flies at 80 m/s (air density 0.7 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.3. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 45, V = 80, rho = 0.7, CL = 0.3 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.7*(80)^2*45*0.3 / 1000 | Answer: 30.24 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 30 m^2 flies at 200 m/s (density 1 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.05. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 30, V = 200, rho = 1, CD = 0.05 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*1*(200)^2*30*0.05 / 1000 | Answer: 30 kN

question: A specimen under stress 180 MPa shows an elastic strain of 2.9e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 180, eps = 2.9 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 180 / (2.9e-3) MPa = 62.07 GPa | Answer: 62.07 GPa

question: A block of mass 24 kg has a volume of 4.3e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 24, V = 4.3 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 24 / (4.3e-3) | Answer: 5581 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 1400 mm is heated through 65 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 17e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 1400, dT = 65, al = 17 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 1400*17e-6*65 | Answer: 1.547 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 35 ohm, R2 = 120 ohm and R3 = 475 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 35, R2 = 120, R3 = 475 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 120*475 / 35 | Answer: 1629 ohm

question: A measurement reads 10.29 when the true value is 20. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10.29, true = 20 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10.29 - 20| / 20 * 100 | Answer: 48.55 %

question: Annual demand is 40500 units, ordering cost 170 per order and holding cost 17 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 40500, S = 170, H = 17 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*40500*170 / 17) | Answer: 900 units

question: An asset costs 300000 with salvage value 40000 after 13 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 300000, Sv = 40000, n = 13 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (300000 - 40000) / 13 | Answer: 20000 per year

question: A product sells for 310 per unit with variable cost 100 per unit and fixed costs 75000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 310, V = 100, F = 75000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 75000 / (310 - 100) | Answer: 357.1 units

question: Find the present worth of 165000 received 9 years from now at an interest rate of 7% per year.
solution: Given: F = 165000, n = 9, i = 7 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 165000 / (1 + 0.07)^9 | Answer: 89749 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.92, 0.9 and 0.9 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.92, r2 = 0.9, r3 = 0.9 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.92*0.9*0.9 | Answer: 0.7452

question: A process produces 34 defective items in a batch of 18000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 34, N = 18000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 34/18000 * 1e6 | Answer: 1889 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -3x^3 + 3x^2 + 5x - 5 evaluated at x = -5.
For f(x) = -6x^3 - 3x^2 + 7x - 4, find f''(x) at x = 3.
Evaluate the definite integral of (3x + 4) dx from x = -2 to x = 7.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = 0x^3/3 + 3x^2/2 + 4x | Evaluate F(7) - F(-2) | Answer: 103.5
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of x^2 - 5x - 3 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[-2, 2], [7, 6]].
solution: Given: a = -2, b = 2, c = 7, d = 6 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (-2)(6) - (2)(7) | Answer: -26

question: Find the determinant of [[-3, 5, -6], [1, 3, -2], [-1, -3, 2]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: 0

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[6, 2], [1, 4]].
solution: Trace tr = 10, Determinant = 22 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 6.732

question: Solve for x: 3x + -5y = -3 and 3x + -3y = 9.
solution: Determinant = 3*-3 - -5*3 = 6 | x = (e d - b f) / det = 9 | Answer: x = 9
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 47, 85, 16, 90, 45.
solution: Sum = 283 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 56.6 | Answer: 56.6

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 46, 43, 18, 25, 3.
solution: Mean = 27 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 17.87

question: Find the slope of the line through (8, -9) and (-3, -4).
Find the distance between the points (1, -5) and (-5, 0).
solution: Given: x1 = 1, y1 = -5, x2 = -5, y2 = 0 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-6)^2 + (5)^2) | Answer: 7.81 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (3,2), (-8,-2), (2,-1).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 14.5 sq units

question: Find the 21th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 8 and common difference 4.
solution: Given: a = 8, d = 4, n = 21 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = 8 + (21 - 1)*4 | Answer: 88

question: Find the sum of the first 13 terms of an AP with first term -11 and common difference -4.
solution: Given: a = -11, d = -4, n = 13 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 13/2 [2*-11 + (13-1)*-4] | Answer: -455

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 36500 at 7.3% per annum for 8 years.
solution: Given: P = 36500, R = 7.3, Tt = 8 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 36500 * 7.3 * 8 / 100 | Answer: 21316 currency units

question: Find the amount when 20000 is invested at 6.1% per annum compounded annually for 4 years.
solution: Given: P = 20000, R = 6.1, Tt = 4 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 20000 * (1 + 6.1/100)^4 | Answer: 25345 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (8, -8, 7) and (-8, 8, 7).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (-3, -1, -5) and (3, 3, -4).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 33.56

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (-4, 3, 3) and (2, 2, -4).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 119.3 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number 4 + -2i.
solution: Given: a = 4, b = -2 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((4)^2 + (-2)^2) | Answer: 4.472

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number -1 + 4i.
solution: Given: a = -1, b = 4 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(4, -1) | Answer: 104 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -x^3 + 7x^2 + 3x - 5 at x = 0.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-172 with initial guess x0=15, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.9 and ordinates 10, 15, 7, 9, 20, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 576 and 433.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 576 and 433 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 54 and 41.
solution: Given: a = 54, b = 41 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 54*41 / 1 | Answer: 2214
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 45 mm carries an axial tensile load of 20 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 40 mm and length 2600 mm carries an axial load of 33 kN. Take E = 70 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 63 mm transmits a torque of 2700 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 63, Tt = 2700 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(2700*1000) / (pi*(63)^3) | Answer: 54.99 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 28 mm and length 1500 mm carries a torque of 1400 N-m. With G = 77 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (28)^4 / 32 = 60344 mm^4 | theta = (1400*1000)(1500) / (77000 * 60344) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 25.9 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 125 mm wide and 250 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 125, h = 250 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 125*(250)^2 / 6 | Answer: 1302083 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (97 mm x 80 mm) carries a bending moment of 37 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (44 mm x 120 mm) has effective length 1700 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 490 MPa is designed for a working stress of 100 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 490, sw = 100 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 490 / 100 | Answer: 4.9

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 500 mm and wall thickness 15 mm carries an internal pressure of 0.6 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 500, t = 15, P = 0.6 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 0.6*500 / (2*15) | Answer: 10 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 1160 K and 310 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 1160, Tc = 310 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 310/1160) * 100 | Answer: 73.28 %

question: A heat pump operates between 267 K and 328 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 267, Th = 328 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 328 / (328 - 267) | Answer: 5.377

question: 6.5 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 195 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 6.5, dT = 195 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 6.5 * 0.718 * 195 | Answer: 910.1 kJ

question: 7.9 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 90 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 7.9, dT = 90 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 7.9 * 1.005 * 90 | Answer: 714.6 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 1.7 m^3 at 590 K with mass 5.5 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 1.7, Tk = 590, m = 5.5 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 5.5*0.287*590 / 1.7 | Answer: 547.8 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 4.4 kg of air expands isothermally at 480 K from volume V1 to 5*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.4, Tk = 480, ratio = 5 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 4.4*0.287*480*ln(5) | Answer: 975.6 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 0.5 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.06 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 0.5, D = 0.06 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*0.5*0.06 / 0.001 | Answer: 30000

question: Water flows at 2.5 m/s through a pipe of diameter 60 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 16.6 m. Taking Cv = 0.96, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 16.6, cv = 0.96 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.96*sqrt(2*9.81*16.6) | Answer: 17.33 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 390 mm) water flows at 2.5 m/s. It contracts to diameter 50 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 390, d2 = 50, V1 = 2.5 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 2.5*(390/50)^2 | Answer: 152.1 m/s

question: Water flows at 2.2 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.43 m and length 400 m. With friction factor f = 0.025, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 26 teeth drives a gear of 52 teeth. If the pinion runs at 300 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 26, z2 = 52, N1 = 300 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 300*26 / 52 | Answer: 150 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 380 mm rotates at 600 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 380, N = 600 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.38)*600 / 60 | Answer: 11.94 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 16.6 kW at 250 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 16.6, N = 250 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(16.6*1000) / (2*pi*250) | Answer: 634.1 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 4.2 kg rotates at radius 0.25 m at 450 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 17800 N/m and mass 13.6 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 17800, m = 13.6 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(17800/13.6) | Answer: 5.758 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 2.8 m^2 and thickness 0.15 m has conductivity k = 1.6 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 175 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 2.8, L = 0.15, k = 1.6, dT = 175 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 1.6*2.8*175 / 0.15 | Answer: 5227 W

question: A surface of area 3.4 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 70 W/m^2-K to surroundings 110 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 3.4, h = 70, dT = 110 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 70*3.4*110 | Answer: 26180 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 60 m/min, feed = 0.21 mm/rev, depth of cut = 1.6 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 60, f = 0.21, d = 1.6 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*60*0.21*1.6 | Answer: 20160 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 240 mm is turned at 1200 rpm with a feed of 0.19 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 240, N = 1200, f = 0.19 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 240 / (0.19*1200) | Answer: 1.053 min

question: A resistor of 55 ohm carries a current of 4.2 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 55, I = 4.2 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 4.2 * 55 | Answer: 231 V

question: Three resistors 71 ohm, 34 ohm and 22 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 71, R2 = 34, R3 = 22 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 71 + 34 + 22 | Answer: 127 ohm

question: Two resistors 101 ohm and 89 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 101, R2 = 89 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 101*89 / (101+89) | Answer: 47.31 ohm

question: A device draws 2.1 A at 230 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 230, I = 2.1 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 230 * 2.1 | Answer: 483 W

question: A current of 9.4 A flows through a 108 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 9.4, R = 108 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (9.4)^2 * 108 | Answer: 9543 W

question: Two capacitors 17.7 uF and 29.1 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 17.7, C2 = 29.1 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 17.7*29.1 / (17.7+29.1) | Answer: 11.01 uF

question: A resistor 60 kohm and capacitor 1.5 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 60, C = 1.5 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (60k)(1.5u) = 90 ms | Answer: 90 ms

question: An inductor 54 mH is in series with 78 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 54, R = 78 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (54e-3) / 78 | Answer: 0.6923 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 31.4 mH inductor at 620 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 31.4, f = 620 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (620)(31.4e-3) | Answer: 122.3 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 39.1 uF capacitor at 360 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 39.1, f = 360 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (360)(39.1e-6)) | Answer: 11.31 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 81 ohm, XL = 76 ohm and XC = 48 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 81, XL = 76, XC = 48 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(81^2 + (76 - 48)^2) | Answer: 85.7 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 37.7 mH and C = 7.4 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 37.7, C = 7.4 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(37.7e-3 * 7.4e-6)) | Answer: 301.3 Hz

question: A capacitor of 80 uF is charged to 305 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 80, V = 305 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*80e-6*(305)^2 | Answer: 3721 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 140 V with 230 primary turns and 500 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 140, N1 = 230, N2 = 500 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 140 * 500/230 | Answer: 304.3 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 260 V and draws an armature current of 42 A. If the armature resistance is 0.42 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 260, Ia = 42, Ra = 0.42 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 260 - 42*0.42 | Answer: 242.4 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 20 A at 415 V (line) with a power factor of 0.8. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 20, VL = 415, pf = 0.8 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*415*20*0.8 / 1000 | Answer: 11.5 kW

question: A load has real power 15 kW and apparent power 105 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 15, S = 105 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 15 / 105 | Answer: 0.1429

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 30 V across R1 = 47 ohm and R2 = 33 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 30, R1 = 47, R2 = 33 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 30*33 / (47+33) | Answer: 12.38 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 90 kohm and Rin = 5 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 90, Rin = 5 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 90 / 5 | Answer: 18

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 190 kohm and Rg = 30 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 190, Rg = 30 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 190/30 | Answer: 7.333

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 239. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 239 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(239) | Answer: 23.78 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 5.5 m carries a central point load of 35 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.5, W = 35 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 35*5.5 / 4 | Answer: 48.12 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.2 m carries a UDL of 40 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 9.2, w = 40 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 40*(9.2)^2 / 8 | Answer: 423.2 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 4.3 m carries a point load 55 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.3, W = 55 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 55*4.3 | Answer: 236.5 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 3.6 m carries a UDL of 36 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.6, w = 36 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 36*(3.6)^2 / 2 | Answer: 233.3 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.5 m carries a point load 100 kN at distance 2.6 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 4.5, a = 2.6, W = 100 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 100*(4.5 - 2.6) / 4.5 | Answer: 42.22 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 5.9 m) carries a central point load 30 kN. With E = 25 GPa and I = 400e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=30000 N, L=5900.0 mm, E=25000 MPa, I=400e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 12.84 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 8.9 m carries a UDL of 33 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 8.9, w = 33 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 33*(8.9)^2 / 12 | Answer: 217.8 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 460 mm, clear cover 35 mm and main bars of diameter 20 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 460, c = 35, dia = 20 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 460 - 35 - 20/2 | Answer: 415 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 12.1 m^2 carrying a factored load of 15.1 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 12.1, w = 15.1 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 15.1 * 12.1 | Answer: 182.7 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 5.2 m, unit weight 17 kN/m^3, phi = 33 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 8.4e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.5, area = 6.4e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 8.4, i = 0.5, A = 6.4 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (8.4e-4)*0.5*(6.4e-3) | Answer: 2688 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 2 m, bed slope 0.003 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.025. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 2 m under a head of 1.1 m. Taking Cd = 0.64 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 2 m wide carries a discharge of 24 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 380 m and design speed 100 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 380, V = 100 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (100)^2 / (127*380) | Answer: 0.2072
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: A tank of volume 650 m^3 treats a flow of 35 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 650, Q = 35 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 650 / 35 | Answer: 18.57 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 400 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.29 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 3 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 400, k = 0.29, t = 3 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 400*(1 - e^(-0.29*3)) | Answer: 232.4 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.64, rainfall intensity 90 mm/h over a catchment of 28.2 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.64, i = 90, A = 28.2 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.64*90*28.2 / 360 | Answer: 4.512 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.03 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 730 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.03, M = 730 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 730*(30+0.03)/30 | Answer: 730.7 m

question: Convert the decimal number 2038 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 2038 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 7F6 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 00000010 and 00001110.
solution: XOR: 00001100 | Count of 1s = 2 | Answer: 2
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 330 megabits is sent over a link of 48 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 330, B = 48 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 330 / 48 | Answer: 6.875 s

question: A link has bandwidth 78 Mbps and round-trip time 60 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 78, R = 60 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 78e6 * 60e-3 bits = 4680 kb | Answer: 4680 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.93, cache access time 3 ns and main-memory access time 150 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.93, tc = 3, tm = 150 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.93*3 + (1 - 0.93)*150 | Answer: 13.29 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 692382 elements?
solution: Given: n = 692382 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(692382)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.003, memory access time 200 ns and page-fault service time 4 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 4 ms = 4000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.003)*200 + 0.003*4000000.0 ns | Answer: 12.2 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 0.2 m^3 at 330 kPa and 580 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 0.2, P = 330, Tk = 580 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (330e3)*0.2 / (8.314*580) | Answer: 13.69 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.15 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 15 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.15, t = 15 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.15*15) | Answer: 0.8946

question: For a reaction with A = 5e10 /s and activation energy 70 kJ/mol at 410 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 5, Ea = 70, Tk = 410 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 5e10 * exp(-70e3 / (8.314*410)) | Answer: 60.33 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.94 and bottoms xW = 0.07, with relative volatility alpha = 1.6. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.94, xw = 0.07, al = 1.6 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.94/0.06)(0.93/0.07)] / ln(1.6) | Answer: 11.36 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.8 and x = 0.32. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.8, x = 0.32 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.8/0.2) / (0.32/0.68) | Answer: 8.5

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.44 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 25 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.44, Psat = 25 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.44 * 25 | Answer: 11 kPa

question: A stream of 4.4 kg/s with specific heat 3.2 kJ/kg-K is heated through 95 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 4.4, cp = 3.2, dT = 95 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 4.4*3.2*95 | Answer: 1338 kW

question: A reactor of volume 9.5 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 2.3 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 9.5, Q = 2.3 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 9.5 / 2.3 | Answer: 4.13 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 2.3e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 4 mm with a concentration difference of 200 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 2.3, L = 4, dC = 200 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (2.3e-9)*200 / (4e-3) | Answer: 115 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 5.5 min and steady-state gain 3.1. For a step input of magnitude 9, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 5.5, K = 3.1, M = 9 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 3.1 * 9 | Answer: 27.9 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 105 m^2 flies at 230 m/s (air density 0.7 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.7. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 105, V = 230, rho = 0.7, CL = 0.7 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.7*(230)^2*105*0.7 / 1000 | Answer: 1361 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 35 m^2 flies at 70 m/s (density 1 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.05. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 35, V = 70, rho = 1, CD = 0.05 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*1*(70)^2*35*0.05 / 1000 | Answer: 4.287 kN

question: A specimen under stress 300 MPa shows an elastic strain of 1e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 300, eps = 1 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 300 / (1e-3) MPa = 300 GPa | Answer: 300 GPa

question: A block of mass 19 kg has a volume of 3.8e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 19, V = 3.8 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 19 / (3.8e-3) | Answer: 5000 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 2600 mm is heated through 45 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 11e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 2600, dT = 45, al = 11 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 2600*11e-6*45 | Answer: 1.287 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 80 ohm, R2 = 160 ohm and R3 = 10 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 80, R2 = 160, R3 = 10 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 160*10 / 80 | Answer: 20 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 350 ohm and gauge factor 2.1 experiences a strain of 1350e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 350, GF = 2.1, eps = 1350 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 350*2.1*1350e-6 | Answer: 992.2 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 9.75 when the true value is 20. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.75, true = 20 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.75 - 20| / 20 * 100 | Answer: 51.25 %

question: Annual demand is 27000 units, ordering cost 70 per order and holding cost 11 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 27000, S = 70, H = 11 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*27000*70 / 11) | Answer: 586.2 units

question: An asset costs 250000 with salvage value 36000 after 7 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 250000, Sv = 36000, n = 7 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (250000 - 36000) / 7 | Answer: 30571 per year

question: A product sells for 180 per unit with variable cost 40 per unit and fixed costs 105000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 180, V = 40, F = 105000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 105000 / (180 - 40) | Answer: 750 units

question: Find the present worth of 140000 received 4 years from now at an interest rate of 7% per year.
solution: Given: F = 140000, n = 4, i = 7 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 140000 / (1 + 0.07)^4 | Answer: 106805 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.92, 0.92 and 0.98 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.92, r2 = 0.92, r3 = 0.98 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.92*0.92*0.98 | Answer: 0.8295

question: A process produces 5 defective items in a batch of 12500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 5, N = 12500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 5/12500 * 1e6 | Answer: 400 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -x^3 - x^2 - 9x + 9 evaluated at x = 4.
For f(x) = 3x^3 - 2x^2 - 3x + 7, find f''(x) at x = 0.
Evaluate the definite integral of (x^2 + 4x + 1) dx from x = -2 to x = 6.

question: Find the larger real root of x^2 + 9x - 10 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[6, -3], [5, -2]].
solution: Given: a = 6, b = -3, c = 5, d = -2 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (6)(-2) - (-3)(5) | Answer: 3

question: Solve for x: -3x + -3y = 9 and 3x + -5y = 7.

solution: Sum = 249 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 49.8 | Answer: 49.8

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 42, 41, 5, 41, 48.

question: Find the slope of the line through (0, -7) and (8, -8).
solution: Given: x1 = 0, y1 = -7, x2 = 8, y2 = -8 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (-8 - -7) / (8 - 0) | Answer: -0.125

question: Find the distance between the points (-6, 9) and (7, -2).
solution: Given: x1 = -6, y1 = 9, x2 = 7, y2 = -2 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((13)^2 + (-11)^2) | Answer: 17.03 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (4,-5), (0,0), (4,-6).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 2 sq units

question: Find the 13th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 18 and common difference 1.
solution: Given: a = 18, d = 1, n = 13 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = 18 + (13 - 1)*1 | Answer: 30

question: Find the sum of the first 12 terms of an AP with first term 11 and common difference -1.
solution: Given: a = 11, d = -1, n = 12 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 12/2 [2*11 + (12-1)*-1] | Answer: 66

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 34500 at 10.1% per annum for 6 years.
solution: Given: P = 34500, R = 10.1, Tt = 6 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 34500 * 10.1 * 6 / 100 | Answer: 20907 currency units

question: Find the amount when 35500 is invested at 8.6% per annum compounded annually for 6 years.
solution: Given: P = 35500, R = 8.6, Tt = 6 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 35500 * (1 + 8.6/100)^6 | Answer: 58238 currency units

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (-6, 6, -6) and (-1, -5, -1).

question: Find the modulus of the complex number 4 + 6i.
solution: Given: a = 4, b = 6 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((4)^2 + (6)^2) | Answer: 7.211

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number -4 + 7i.
solution: Given: a = -4, b = 7 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(7, -4) | Answer: 119.7 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = 2x^3 - 4x^2 - 2x + 6 at x = 0.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-31 with initial guess x0=6, find x1 (one iteration).
solution: Given: N = 31, x0 = 6 | Formula: x1 = x0 - (x0^2 - N)/(2 x0) | Substitute: x1 = 6 - ((6)^2 - 31)/(2*6) | Answer: 5.583

question: Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=2 and ordinates 14, 18, 14, 17, 5, estimate the integral.

solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 391 and 372 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 27 and 78.
solution: Given: a = 27, b = 78 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 27*78 / 3 | Answer: 702
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 36 mm carries an axial tensile load of 72 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 17 mm and length 1700 mm carries an axial load of 26 kN. Take E = 110 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 32 mm transmits a torque of 1700 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 32, Tt = 1700 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(1700*1000) / (pi*(32)^3) | Answer: 264.2 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 39 mm and length 600 mm carries a torque of 1400 N-m. With G = 45 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (39)^4 / 32 = 227122 mm^4 | theta = (1400*1000)(600) / (45000 * 227122) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 4.709 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 106 mm wide and 180 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 106, h = 180 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 106*(180)^2 / 6 | Answer: 572400 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (79 mm x 140 mm) carries a bending moment of 24 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (44 mm x 100 mm) has effective length 3800 mm and E = 200 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 640 MPa is designed for a working stress of 220 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 640, sw = 220 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 640 / 220 | Answer: 2.909

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 500 mm and wall thickness 8 mm carries an internal pressure of 2.7 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 500, t = 8, P = 2.7 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 2.7*500 / (2*8) | Answer: 84.38 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 740 K and 410 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 740, Tc = 410 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 410/740) * 100 | Answer: 44.59 %

question: A refrigerator works between 274 K (cold) and 312 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 274, Th = 312 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 274 / (312 - 274) | Answer: 7.211

question: A heat pump operates between 269 K and 332 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 269, Th = 332 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 332 / (332 - 269) | Answer: 5.27

question: 4.1 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 195 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.1, dT = 195 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 4.1 * 0.718 * 195 | Answer: 574 kJ

question: 3 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 135 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3, dT = 135 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 3 * 1.005 * 135 | Answer: 407 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 3.2 m^3 at 550 K with mass 1.8 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 3.2, Tk = 550, m = 1.8 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 1.8*0.287*550 / 3.2 | Answer: 88.79 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 2 kg of air expands isothermally at 330 K from volume V1 to 5*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2, Tk = 330, ratio = 5 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 2*0.287*330*ln(5) | Answer: 304.9 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 2.2 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.19 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 2.2, D = 0.19 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*2.2*0.19 / 0.001 | Answer: 418000

question: Water flows at 1 m/s through a pipe of diameter 160 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 17.3 m. Taking Cv = 0.95, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 17.3, cv = 0.95 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.95*sqrt(2*9.81*17.3) | Answer: 17.5 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 370 mm) water flows at 1.4 m/s. It contracts to diameter 110 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
Water flows at 2.5 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.12 m and length 310 m. With friction factor f = 0.033, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).

question: A pinion of 25 teeth drives a gear of 100 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1050 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.

question: A pulley of diameter 350 mm rotates at 350 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 350, N = 350 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.35)*350 / 60 | Answer: 6.414 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 17.4 kW at 300 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 17.4, N = 300 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(17.4*1000) / (2*pi*300) | Answer: 553.9 N-m

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 2800 N/m and mass 18.2 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 2800, m = 18.2 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(2800/18.2) | Answer: 1.974 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 3.4 m^2 and thickness 0.2 m has conductivity k = 9.9 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 45 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 3.4, L = 0.2, k = 9.9, dT = 45 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 9.9*3.4*45 / 0.2 | Answer: 7574 W

question: A surface of area 3.3 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 160 W/m^2-K to surroundings 45 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.

question: In turning, cutting speed = 250 m/min, feed = 0.26 mm/rev, depth of cut = 0.7 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 250, f = 0.26, d = 0.7 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*250*0.26*0.7 | Answer: 45500 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 410 mm is turned at 650 rpm with a feed of 0.22 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 410, N = 650, f = 0.22 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 410 / (0.22*650) | Answer: 2.867 min

question: A resistor of 137 ohm carries a current of 9 A. Find the voltage across it.

question: Three resistors 4 ohm, 99 ohm and 47 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.

question: Two resistors 5 ohm and 99 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 5, R2 = 99 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 5*99 / (5+99) | Answer: 4.76 ohm

question: A device draws 7.6 A at 150 V. Find the power consumed.

question: A current of 3.7 A flows through a 48 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 3.7, R = 48 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (3.7)^2 * 48 | Answer: 657.1 W

question: Two capacitors 6.8 uF and 43.6 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 6.8, C2 = 43.6 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 6.8*43.6 / (6.8+43.6) | Answer: 5.883 uF

question: A resistor 13 kohm and capacitor 1.6 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 13, C = 1.6 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (13k)(1.6u) = 20.8 ms | Answer: 20.8 ms

question: An inductor 277.5 mH is in series with 34 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 277.5, R = 34 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (277.5e-3) / 34 | Answer: 8.162 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 180.3 mH inductor at 580 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 180.3, f = 580 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (580)(180.3e-3) | Answer: 657.1 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 37.3 uF capacitor at 960 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 37.3, f = 960 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (960)(37.3e-6)) | Answer: 4.445 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 43 ohm, XL = 75 ohm and XC = 64 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 43, XL = 75, XC = 64 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(43^2 + (75 - 64)^2) | Answer: 44.38 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 47.9 mH and C = 4.7 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 47.9, C = 4.7 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(47.9e-3 * 4.7e-6)) | Answer: 335.4 Hz

question: A capacitor of 3.8 uF is charged to 280 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 3.8, V = 280 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*3.8e-6*(280)^2 | Answer: 149 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 350 V with 590 primary turns and 210 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.

question: A DC motor is supplied at 440 V and draws an armature current of 44 A. If the armature resistance is 0.78 ohm, find the back EMF.

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 200 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.97. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 200, VL = 400, pf = 0.97 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*400*200*0.97 / 1000 | Answer: 134.4 kW

question: A load has real power 110 kW and apparent power 200 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 110, S = 200 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 110 / 200 | Answer: 0.55

question: A machine delivers 45 kW output while drawing 112 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 45, Pi = 112 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 45/112 * 100 | Answer: 40.18 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 14 V across R1 = 2 ohm and R2 = 10 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 14, R1 = 2, R2 = 10 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 14*10 / (2+10) | Answer: 11.67 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 210 kohm and Rin = 42 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 20 kohm and Rg = 43 kohm. Find the voltage gain.

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 7205. Express the gain in decibels (power).

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.8 m carries a central point load of 65 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6.8, W = 65 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 65*6.8 / 4 | Answer: 110.5 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 7.5 m carries a UDL of 15 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.

question: A cantilever of length 2.5 m carries a point load 55 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.

question: A cantilever of length 3.4 m carries a UDL of 38 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.4, w = 38 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 38*(3.4)^2 / 2 | Answer: 219.6 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.8 m carries a point load 45 kN at distance 3.5 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 9.8, a = 3.5, W = 45 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 45*(9.8 - 3.5) / 9.8 | Answer: 28.93 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 5.5 m) carries a central point load 65 kN. With E = 30 GPa and I = 240e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.

question: A fixed beam of span 5.7 m carries a UDL of 18 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.7, w = 18 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 18*(5.7)^2 / 12 | Answer: 48.74 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 600 mm, clear cover 30 mm and main bars of diameter 16 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 600, c = 30, dia = 16 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 600 - 30 - 16/2 | Answer: 562 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 19.7 m^2 carrying a factored load of 15.4 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 19.7, w = 15.4 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 15.4 * 19.7 | Answer: 303.4 kN

question: A tank of volume 940 m^3 treats a flow of 35 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 940, Q = 35 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 940 / 35 | Answer: 26.86 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 360 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.19 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 8 days.

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.74, rainfall intensity 90 mm/h over a catchment of 28.8 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.03 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 700 m with this tape.

question: A file of 560 megabits is sent over a link of 68 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.

question: A link has bandwidth 73 Mbps and round-trip time 160 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 73, R = 160 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 73e6 * 160e-3 bits = 11680 kb | Answer: 11680 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.95, cache access time 2 ns and main-memory access time 100 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.95, tc = 2, tm = 100 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.95*2 + (1 - 0.95)*100 | Answer: 6.9 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 54486 elements?

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.001, memory access time 150 ns and page-fault service time 5 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 2.4 m^3 at 490 kPa and 390 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 2.4, P = 490, Tk = 390 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (490e3)*2.4 / (8.314*390) | Answer: 362.7 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.38 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 3 minutes.

question: For a reaction with A = 2e10 /s and activation energy 60 kJ/mol at 490 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.91 and bottoms xW = 0.05, with relative volatility alpha = 3.4. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.91, xw = 0.05, al = 3.4 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.91/0.09)(0.95/0.05)] / ln(3.4) | Answer: 4.297 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.55 and x = 0.24. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.85 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 110 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.85, Psat = 110 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.85 * 110 | Answer: 93.5 kPa

question: A stream of 6.1 kg/s with specific heat 3.9 kJ/kg-K is heated through 110 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 6.1, cp = 3.9, dT = 110 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 6.1*3.9*110 | Answer: 2617 kW

question: A reactor of volume 16 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 4 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 16, Q = 4 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 16 / 4 | Answer: 4 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 2.3e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 1 mm with a concentration difference of 90 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 2.3, L = 1, dC = 90 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (2.3e-9)*90 / (1e-3) | Answer: 207 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 1.5 min and steady-state gain 3.4. For a step input of magnitude 4, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 1.5, K = 3.4, M = 4 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 3.4 * 4 | Answer: 13.6 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 90 m^2 flies at 60 m/s (air density 1.225 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.6. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 90, V = 60, rho = 1.225, CL = 0.6 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1.225*(60)^2*90*0.6 / 1000 | Answer: 119.1 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 85 m^2 flies at 140 m/s (density 1 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.12. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 85, V = 140, rho = 1, CD = 0.12 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*1*(140)^2*85*0.12 / 1000 | Answer: 99.96 kN

question: A specimen under stress 130 MPa shows an elastic strain of 1.3e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 130, eps = 1.3 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 130 / (1.3e-3) MPa = 100 GPa | Answer: 100 GPa

question: A block of mass 50 kg has a volume of 4.1e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 50, V = 4.1 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 50 / (4.1e-3) | Answer: 12195 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 500 mm is heated through 120 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 23e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 500, dT = 120, al = 23 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 500*23e-6*120 | Answer: 1.38 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 170 ohm, R2 = 155 ohm and R3 = 195 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 170, R2 = 155, R3 = 195 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 155*195 / 170 | Answer: 177.8 ohm

question: A measurement reads 9.58 when the true value is 100. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.58, true = 100 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.58 - 100| / 100 * 100 | Answer: 90.42 %

question: Annual demand is 39500 units, ordering cost 70 per order and holding cost 39 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).

question: An asset costs 130000 with salvage value 14000 after 14 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.

question: A product sells for 200 per unit with variable cost 110 per unit and fixed costs 195000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 200, V = 110, F = 195000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 195000 / (200 - 110) | Answer: 2167 units

question: Find the present worth of 190000 received 5 years from now at an interest rate of 12% per year.

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.93, 0.92 and 0.94 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.93, r2 = 0.92, r3 = 0.94 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.93*0.92*0.94 | Answer: 0.8043

question: A process produces 15 defective items in a batch of 3000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 15, N = 3000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 15/3000 * 1e6 | Answer: 5000 PPM
