question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 7 and 34.
solution: Given: a = 7, b = 34 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 7*34 / 1 | Answer: 238
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 55 mm carries an axial tensile load of 27 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 21 mm and length 900 mm carries an axial load of 33 kN. Take E = 110 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 22 mm transmits a torque of 2050 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 22, Tt = 2050 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(2050*1000) / (pi*(22)^3) | Answer: 980.5 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 27 mm and length 1600 mm carries a torque of 1500 N-m. With G = 77 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (27)^4 / 32 = 52174 mm^4 | theta = (1500*1000)(1600) / (77000 * 52174) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 34.23 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 140 mm wide and 130 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 140, h = 130 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 140*(130)^2 / 6 | Answer: 394333 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (57 mm x 140 mm) carries a bending moment of 35 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (72 mm x 130 mm) has effective length 3100 mm and E = 200 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 610 MPa is designed for a working stress of 130 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 610, sw = 130 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 610 / 130 | Answer: 4.692

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 400 mm and wall thickness 19 mm carries an internal pressure of 2.5 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 400, t = 19, P = 2.5 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 2.5*400 / (2*19) | Answer: 26.32 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 980 K and 360 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 980, Tc = 360 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 360/980) * 100 | Answer: 63.27 %

question: A refrigerator works between 269 K (cold) and 324 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 269, Th = 324 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 269 / (324 - 269) | Answer: 4.891

question: A heat pump operates between 276 K and 326 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 276, Th = 326 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 326 / (326 - 276) | Answer: 6.52

question: 3 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 40 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3, dT = 40 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 3 * 0.718 * 40 | Answer: 86.16 kJ

question: 7.5 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 55 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 7.5, dT = 55 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 7.5 * 1.005 * 55 | Answer: 414.6 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 2.5 m^3 at 410 K with mass 5.5 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 2.5, Tk = 410, m = 5.5 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 5.5*0.287*410 / 2.5 | Answer: 258.9 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 4.5 kg of air expands isothermally at 310 K from volume V1 to 5*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.5, Tk = 310, ratio = 5 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 4.5*0.287*310*ln(5) | Answer: 644.4 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 4 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.2 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 4, D = 0.2 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*4*0.2 / 0.001 | Answer: 800000

question: Water flows at 1.9 m/s through a pipe of diameter 120 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 10.3 m. Taking Cv = 0.98, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 10.3, cv = 0.98 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.98*sqrt(2*9.81*10.3) | Answer: 13.93 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 190 mm) water flows at 1.6 m/s. It contracts to diameter 100 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
Water flows at 2 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.23 m and length 380 m. With friction factor f = 0.027, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 32 teeth drives a gear of 58 teeth. If the pinion runs at 600 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 32, z2 = 58, N1 = 600 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 600*32 / 58 | Answer: 331 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 400 mm rotates at 1400 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 400, N = 1400 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.4)*1400 / 60 | Answer: 29.32 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 45.2 kW at 400 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 45.2, N = 400 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(45.2*1000) / (2*pi*400) | Answer: 1079 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 5.2 kg rotates at radius 0.21 m at 500 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 3600 N/m and mass 13.7 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 3600, m = 13.7 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(3600/13.7) | Answer: 2.58 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 2.7 m^2 and thickness 0.38 m has conductivity k = 48.9 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 105 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 2.7, L = 0.38, k = 48.9, dT = 105 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 48.9*2.7*105 / 0.38 | Answer: 36482 W

question: A surface of area 4.9 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 115 W/m^2-K to surroundings 145 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 4.9, h = 115, dT = 145 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 115*4.9*145 | Answer: 81708 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 90 m/min, feed = 0.48 mm/rev, depth of cut = 1.9 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 90, f = 0.48, d = 1.9 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*90*0.48*1.9 | Answer: 82080 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 480 mm is turned at 950 rpm with a feed of 0.12 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 480, N = 950, f = 0.12 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 480 / (0.12*950) | Answer: 4.211 min

question: A resistor of 182 ohm carries a current of 7.9 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 182, I = 7.9 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 7.9 * 182 | Answer: 1438 V

question: Three resistors 16 ohm, 54 ohm and 20 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 16, R2 = 54, R3 = 20 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 16 + 54 + 20 | Answer: 90 ohm

question: Two resistors 49 ohm and 16 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 49, R2 = 16 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 49*16 / (49+16) | Answer: 12.06 ohm

question: A device draws 0.7 A at 195 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 195, I = 0.7 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 195 * 0.7 | Answer: 136.5 W

question: A current of 5.9 A flows through a 96 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 5.9, R = 96 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (5.9)^2 * 96 | Answer: 3342 W

question: Two capacitors 2.8 uF and 13.2 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 2.8, C2 = 13.2 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 2.8*13.2 / (2.8+13.2) | Answer: 2.31 uF

question: A resistor 99 kohm and capacitor 20 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 99, C = 20 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (99k)(20u) = 1980 ms | Answer: 1980 ms

question: An inductor 16 mH is in series with 135 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 16, R = 135 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (16e-3) / 135 | Answer: 0.1185 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 131.1 mH inductor at 680 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 131.1, f = 680 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (680)(131.1e-3) | Answer: 560.1 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 41.7 uF capacitor at 810 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 41.7, f = 810 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (810)(41.7e-6)) | Answer: 4.712 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 52 ohm, XL = 105 ohm and XC = 60 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 52, XL = 105, XC = 60 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(52^2 + (105 - 60)^2) | Answer: 68.77 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 45.9 mH and C = 7.9 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 45.9, C = 7.9 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(45.9e-3 * 7.9e-6)) | Answer: 264.3 Hz

question: A capacitor of 94.4 uF is charged to 155 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 94.4, V = 155 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*94.4e-6*(155)^2 | Answer: 1134 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 240 V with 710 primary turns and 460 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 240, N1 = 710, N2 = 460 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 240 * 460/710 | Answer: 155.5 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 110 V and draws an armature current of 39 A. If the armature resistance is 0.71 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 110, Ia = 39, Ra = 0.71 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 110 - 39*0.71 | Answer: 82.31 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 95 A at 415 V (line) with a power factor of 0.82. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 95, VL = 415, pf = 0.82 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*415*95*0.82 / 1000 | Answer: 55.99 kW

question: A load has real power 10 kW and apparent power 95 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 10, S = 95 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 10 / 95 | Answer: 0.1053

question: A machine delivers 20 kW output while drawing 152 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 20, Pi = 152 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 20/152 * 100 | Answer: 13.16 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 22 V across R1 = 29 ohm and R2 = 7 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 22, R1 = 29, R2 = 7 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 22*7 / (29+7) | Answer: 4.278 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 50 kohm and Rin = 26 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 50, Rin = 26 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 50 / 26 | Answer: 1.923

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 170 kohm and Rg = 38 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 170, Rg = 38 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 170/38 | Answer: 5.474

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 6762. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 6762 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(6762) | Answer: 38.3 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 8.5 m carries a central point load of 45 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 8.5, W = 45 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 45*8.5 / 4 | Answer: 95.62 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 8.3 m carries a UDL of 20 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 8.3, w = 20 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 20*(8.3)^2 / 8 | Answer: 172.2 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 4.8 m carries a point load 45 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.8, W = 45 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 45*4.8 | Answer: 216 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 1.4 m carries a UDL of 40 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 1.4, w = 40 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 40*(1.4)^2 / 2 | Answer: 39.2 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 7.1 m carries a point load 60 kN at distance 1.3 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 7.1, a = 1.3, W = 60 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 60*(7.1 - 1.3) / 7.1 | Answer: 49.01 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 6.1 m) carries a central point load 80 kN. With E = 25 GPa and I = 380e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=80000 N, L=6100.0 mm, E=25000 MPa, I=380e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 39.82 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 8.2 m carries a UDL of 33 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 8.2, w = 33 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 33*(8.2)^2 / 12 | Answer: 184.9 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 610 mm, clear cover 45 mm and main bars of diameter 16 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 610, c = 45, dia = 16 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 610 - 45 - 16/2 | Answer: 557 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 31.6 m^2 carrying a factored load of 14 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 31.6, w = 14 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 14 * 31.6 | Answer: 442.4 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 4.6 m, unit weight 18 kN/m^3, phi = 35 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 2.2e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.6, area = 3.6e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 2.2, i = 0.6, A = 3.6 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (2.2e-4)*0.6*(3.6e-3) | Answer: 475.2 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 0.9 m, bed slope 0.005 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.026. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 1.2 m under a head of 0.6 m. Taking Cd = 0.64 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 2.7 m wide carries a discharge of 18.8 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 150 m and design speed 95 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 150, V = 95 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (95)^2 / (127*150) | Answer: 0.4738
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: A tank of volume 990 m^3 treats a flow of 75 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 990, Q = 75 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 990 / 75 | Answer: 13.2 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 190 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.19 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 5 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 190, k = 0.19, t = 5 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 190*(1 - e^(-0.19*5)) | Answer: 116.5 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.33, rainfall intensity 85 mm/h over a catchment of 28.4 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.33, i = 85, A = 28.4 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.33*85*28.4 / 360 | Answer: 2.213 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.04 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 470 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.04, M = 470 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 470*(20+0.04)/20 | Answer: 470.9 m

question: Convert the decimal number 544 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 544 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 220 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 10000101 and 11000000.
solution: XOR: 01000101 | Count of 1s = 3 | Answer: 3
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 450 megabits is sent over a link of 14 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 450, B = 14 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 450 / 14 | Answer: 32.14 s

question: A link has bandwidth 99 Mbps and round-trip time 140 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 99, R = 140 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 99e6 * 140e-3 bits = 13860 kb | Answer: 13860 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.93, cache access time 2 ns and main-memory access time 110 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.93, tc = 2, tm = 110 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.93*2 + (1 - 0.93)*110 | Answer: 9.56 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 809328 elements?
solution: Given: n = 809328 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(809328)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.014, memory access time 160 ns and page-fault service time 5 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 5 ms = 5000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.014)*160 + 0.014*5000000.0 ns | Answer: 70.16 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 2.9 m^3 at 120 kPa and 480 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 2.9, P = 120, Tk = 480 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (120e3)*2.9 / (8.314*480) | Answer: 87.2 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.18 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 6 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.18, t = 6 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.18*6) | Answer: 0.6604

question: For a reaction with A = 4e10 /s and activation energy 70 kJ/mol at 400 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 4, Ea = 70, Tk = 400 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 4e10 * exp(-70e3 / (8.314*400)) | Answer: 28.88 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.93 and bottoms xW = 0.09, with relative volatility alpha = 2.4. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.93, xw = 0.09, al = 2.4 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.93/0.07)(0.91/0.09)] / ln(2.4) | Answer: 5.597 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.63 and x = 0.41. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.63, x = 0.41 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.63/0.37) / (0.41/0.59) | Answer: 2.45

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.3 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 25 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.3, Psat = 25 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.3 * 25 | Answer: 7.5 kPa

question: A stream of 6.1 kg/s with specific heat 1.2 kJ/kg-K is heated through 50 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 6.1, cp = 1.2, dT = 50 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 6.1*1.2*50 | Answer: 366 kW

question: A reactor of volume 19.3 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 4.4 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 19.3, Q = 4.4 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 19.3 / 4.4 | Answer: 4.386 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 1.1e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 4 mm with a concentration difference of 180 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 1.1, L = 4, dC = 180 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (1.1e-9)*180 / (4e-3) | Answer: 49.5 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 3.7 min and steady-state gain 2.8. For a step input of magnitude 11, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 3.7, K = 2.8, M = 11 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 2.8 * 11 | Answer: 30.8 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 85 m^2 flies at 120 m/s (air density 1 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.5. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 85, V = 120, rho = 1, CL = 0.5 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1*(120)^2*85*0.5 / 1000 | Answer: 306 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 40 m^2 flies at 60 m/s (density 1 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.04. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 40, V = 60, rho = 1, CD = 0.04 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*1*(60)^2*40*0.04 / 1000 | Answer: 2.88 kN

question: A specimen under stress 320 MPa shows an elastic strain of 2.3e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 320, eps = 2.3 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 320 / (2.3e-3) MPa = 139.1 GPa | Answer: 139.1 GPa

question: A block of mass 43 kg has a volume of 5e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 43, V = 5 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 43 / (5e-3) | Answer: 8600 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 800 mm is heated through 80 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 11e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 800, dT = 80, al = 11 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 800*11e-6*80 | Answer: 0.704 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 180 ohm, R2 = 95 ohm and R3 = 325 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 180, R2 = 95, R3 = 325 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 95*325 / 180 | Answer: 171.5 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 350 ohm and gauge factor 2.1 experiences a strain of 100e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 350, GF = 2.1, eps = 100 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 350*2.1*100e-6 | Answer: 73.5 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 9.64 when the true value is 100. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.64, true = 100 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.64 - 100| / 100 * 100 | Answer: 90.36 %

question: Annual demand is 35500 units, ordering cost 20 per order and holding cost 34 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 35500, S = 20, H = 34 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*35500*20 / 34) | Answer: 204.4 units

question: An asset costs 430000 with salvage value 28000 after 13 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 430000, Sv = 28000, n = 13 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (430000 - 28000) / 13 | Answer: 30923 per year

question: A product sells for 390 per unit with variable cost 140 per unit and fixed costs 115000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 390, V = 140, F = 115000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 115000 / (390 - 140) | Answer: 460 units

question: Find the present worth of 175000 received 9 years from now at an interest rate of 7% per year.
solution: Given: F = 175000, n = 9, i = 7 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 175000 / (1 + 0.07)^9 | Answer: 95188 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.93, 0.96 and 0.95 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.93, r2 = 0.96, r3 = 0.95 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.93*0.96*0.95 | Answer: 0.8482

question: A process produces 19 defective items in a batch of 8000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 19, N = 8000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 19/8000 * 1e6 | Answer: 2375 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = x^3 + 2x^2 - 8x evaluated at x = 5.
For f(x) = -2x^3 - 5x^2 + 4x - 3, find f''(x) at x = 3.
Evaluate the definite integral of (-4x^2 + x + 8) dx from x = -1 to x = 3.

question: Find the larger real root of 3x^2 + 9x = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[2, 0], [-1, -4]].
solution: Given: a = 2, b = 0, c = -1, d = -4 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (2)(-4) - (0)(-1) | Answer: -8

question: Find the determinant of [[2, 0, 0], [2, 0, -4], [-3, 1, 1]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: 8

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[-6, -1], [-5, 2]].
solution: Trace tr = -4, Determinant = -17 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 2.583

question: Solve for x: 4x + -2y = -7 and -6x + 0y = 12.
solution: Determinant = 4*0 - -2*-6 = -12 | x = (e d - b f) / det = -2 | Answer: x = -2
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 70, 36, 66, 61, 17.
solution: Sum = 250 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 50 | Answer: 50

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 2, 25, 7, 45, 6.
solution: Mean = 17 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 17.99

question: Find the slope of the line through (-2, -9) and (-8, -4).
Find the distance between the points (0, -5) and (1, -7).
solution: Given: x1 = 0, y1 = -5, x2 = 1, y2 = -7 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((1)^2 + (-2)^2) | Answer: 2.236 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (-8,2), (-2,-8), (1,7).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 60 sq units

question: Find the 26th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -19 and common difference -7.
solution: Given: a = -19, d = -7, n = 26 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -19 + (26 - 1)*-7 | Answer: -194

question: Find the sum of the first 28 terms of an AP with first term -4 and common difference 3.
solution: Given: a = -4, d = 3, n = 28 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 28/2 [2*-4 + (28-1)*3] | Answer: 1022

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 18500 at 14.9% per annum for 5 years.
solution: Given: P = 18500, R = 14.9, Tt = 5 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 18500 * 14.9 * 5 / 100 | Answer: 13782 currency units

question: Find the amount when 2500 is invested at 11.3% per annum compounded annually for 5 years.
solution: Given: P = 2500, R = 11.3, Tt = 5 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 2500 * (1 + 11.3/100)^5 | Answer: 427 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (6, -3, -3) and (7, -5, 3).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (-4, -6, 1) and (-2, -3, 6).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 39.66

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (-1, 4, 0) and (-2, 2, 6).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 68.55 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number 3 + 5i.
solution: Given: a = 3, b = 5 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((3)^2 + (5)^2) | Answer: 5.831

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number -8 + 4i.
solution: Given: a = -8, b = 4 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(4, -8) | Answer: 153.4 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -2x^3 - 2x^2 - 7x + 9 at x = -5.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-130 with initial guess x0=12, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.7 and ordinates 0, 20, 13, 11, 1, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 172 and 239.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 172 and 239 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 12 and 51.
solution: Given: a = 12, b = 51 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 12*51 / 3 | Answer: 204
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 14 mm carries an axial tensile load of 27 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 27 mm and length 2400 mm carries an axial load of 17 kN. Take E = 70 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 66 mm transmits a torque of 2600 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 66, Tt = 2600 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(2600*1000) / (pi*(66)^3) | Answer: 46.06 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 42 mm and length 1900 mm carries a torque of 450 N-m. With G = 80 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (42)^4 / 32 = 30549 mm^4 | theta = (450*1000)(1900) / (80000 * 30549) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 2.004 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 60 mm wide and 280 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 60, h = 280 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 60*(280)^2 / 6 | Answer: 784000 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (51 mm x 250 mm) carries a bending moment of 13 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (62 mm x 150 mm) has effective length 3700 mm and E = 200 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 760 MPa is designed for a working stress of 240 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 760, sw = 240 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 760 / 240 | Answer: 3.167

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1350 mm and wall thickness 17 mm carries an internal pressure of 1.6 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1350, t = 17, P = 1.6 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 1.6*1350 / (2*17) | Answer: 63.53 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 900 K and 360 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 900, Tc = 360 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 360/900) * 100 | Answer: 60 %

question: A refrigerator works between 266 K (cold) and 314 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 266, Th = 314 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 266 / (314 - 266) | Answer: 5.542

question: A heat pump operates between 273 K and 302 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 273, Th = 302 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 302 / (302 - 273) | Answer: 10.41

question: 2 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 190 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2, dT = 190 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 2 * 0.718 * 190 | Answer: 272.8 kJ

question: 5.6 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 35 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 5.6, dT = 35 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 5.6 * 1.005 * 35 | Answer: 197 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 1.9 m^3 at 390 K with mass 2.1 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 1.9, Tk = 390, m = 2.1 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 2.1*0.287*390 / 1.9 | Answer: 123.7 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 3.6 kg of air expands isothermally at 330 K from volume V1 to 5*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.6, Tk = 330, ratio = 5 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 3.6*0.287*330*ln(5) | Answer: 548.7 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 2.3 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.07 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 2.3, D = 0.07 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*2.3*0.07 / 0.001 | Answer: 161000

question: Water flows at 3 m/s through a pipe of diameter 180 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 18.1 m. Taking Cv = 0.98, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 18.1, cv = 0.98 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.98*sqrt(2*9.81*18.1) | Answer: 18.47 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 260 mm) water flows at 2.5 m/s. It contracts to diameter 70 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 260, d2 = 70, V1 = 2.5 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 2.5*(260/70)^2 | Answer: 34.49 m/s

question: Water flows at 2.7 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.11 m and length 240 m. With friction factor f = 0.035, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 37 teeth drives a gear of 72 teeth. If the pinion runs at 500 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 37, z2 = 72, N1 = 500 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 500*37 / 72 | Answer: 256.9 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 200 mm rotates at 950 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 200, N = 950 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.2)*950 / 60 | Answer: 9.948 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 7.6 kW at 1050 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 7.6, N = 1050 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(7.6*1000) / (2*pi*1050) | Answer: 69.12 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 4.1 kg rotates at radius 0.59 m at 200 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 12700 N/m and mass 3.7 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 12700, m = 3.7 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(12700/3.7) | Answer: 9.324 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 9.4 m^2 and thickness 0.19 m has conductivity k = 12.4 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 150 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 9.4, L = 0.19, k = 12.4, dT = 150 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 12.4*9.4*150 / 0.19 | Answer: 92021 W

question: A surface of area 3.8 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 145 W/m^2-K to surroundings 150 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 3.8, h = 145, dT = 150 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 145*3.8*150 | Answer: 82650 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 140 m/min, feed = 0.3 mm/rev, depth of cut = 0.6 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 140, f = 0.3, d = 0.6 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*140*0.3*0.6 | Answer: 25200 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 120 mm is turned at 750 rpm with a feed of 0.38 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 120, N = 750, f = 0.38 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 120 / (0.38*750) | Answer: 0.4211 min

question: A resistor of 109 ohm carries a current of 1.7 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 109, I = 1.7 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 1.7 * 109 | Answer: 185.3 V

question: Three resistors 8 ohm, 5 ohm and 86 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 8, R2 = 5, R3 = 86 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 8 + 5 + 86 | Answer: 99 ohm

question: Two resistors 59 ohm and 111 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 59, R2 = 111 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 59*111 / (59+111) | Answer: 38.52 ohm

question: A device draws 5 A at 135 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 135, I = 5 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 135 * 5 | Answer: 675 W

question: A current of 7.5 A flows through a 122 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 7.5, R = 122 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (7.5)^2 * 122 | Answer: 6862 W

question: Two capacitors 28.3 uF and 40.2 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 28.3, C2 = 40.2 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 28.3*40.2 / (28.3+40.2) | Answer: 16.61 uF

question: A resistor 38 kohm and capacitor 0.6 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 38, C = 0.6 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (38k)(0.6u) = 22.8 ms | Answer: 22.8 ms

question: An inductor 149.5 mH is in series with 110 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 149.5, R = 110 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (149.5e-3) / 110 | Answer: 1.359 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 127.3 mH inductor at 380 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 127.3, f = 380 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (380)(127.3e-3) | Answer: 303.9 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 37.5 uF capacitor at 550 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 37.5, f = 550 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (550)(37.5e-6)) | Answer: 7.717 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 79 ohm, XL = 135 ohm and XC = 61 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 79, XL = 135, XC = 61 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(79^2 + (135 - 61)^2) | Answer: 108.2 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 79.4 mH and C = 9.3 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 79.4, C = 9.3 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(79.4e-3 * 9.3e-6)) | Answer: 185.2 Hz

question: A capacitor of 56.9 uF is charged to 25 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 56.9, V = 25 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*56.9e-6*(25)^2 | Answer: 17.78 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 220 V with 760 primary turns and 210 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 220, N1 = 760, N2 = 210 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 220 * 210/760 | Answer: 60.79 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 200 V and draws an armature current of 38 A. If the armature resistance is 0.57 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 200, Ia = 38, Ra = 0.57 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 200 - 38*0.57 | Answer: 178.3 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 185 A at 433 V (line) with a power factor of 0.78. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 185, VL = 433, pf = 0.78 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*433*185*0.78 / 1000 | Answer: 108.2 kW

question: A load has real power 20 kW and apparent power 115 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 20, S = 115 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 20 / 115 | Answer: 0.1739

question: A machine delivers 105 kW output while drawing 207 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 105, Pi = 207 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 105/207 * 100 | Answer: 50.72 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 18 V across R1 = 33 ohm and R2 = 50 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 18, R1 = 33, R2 = 50 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 18*50 / (33+50) | Answer: 10.84 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 40 kohm and Rin = 18 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 40, Rin = 18 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 40 / 18 | Answer: 2.222

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 140 kohm and Rg = 8 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 140, Rg = 8 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 140/8 | Answer: 18.5

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 3964. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 3964 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(3964) | Answer: 35.98 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 7.6 m carries a central point load of 95 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7.6, W = 95 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 95*7.6 / 4 | Answer: 180.5 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.5 m carries a UDL of 15 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.5, w = 15 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 15*(4.5)^2 / 8 | Answer: 37.97 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 4.4 m carries a point load 65 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.4, W = 65 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 65*4.4 | Answer: 286 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 3.5 m carries a UDL of 38 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.5, w = 38 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 38*(3.5)^2 / 2 | Answer: 232.8 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.6 m carries a point load 80 kN at distance 1.7 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 9.6, a = 1.7, W = 80 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 80*(9.6 - 1.7) / 9.6 | Answer: 65.83 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 5.9 m) carries a central point load 55 kN. With E = 30 GPa and I = 490e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=55000 N, L=5900.0 mm, E=30000 MPa, I=490e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 16.01 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 7 m carries a UDL of 36 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7, w = 36 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 36*(7)^2 / 12 | Answer: 147 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 430 mm, clear cover 35 mm and main bars of diameter 25 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 430, c = 35, dia = 25 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 430 - 35 - 25/2 | Answer: 382.5 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 25.8 m^2 carrying a factored load of 12.1 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 25.8, w = 12.1 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 12.1 * 25.8 | Answer: 312.2 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 3.9 m, unit weight 20 kN/m^3, phi = 31 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 4.4e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.9, area = 6.5e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 4.4, i = 0.9, A = 6.5 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (4.4e-4)*0.9*(6.5e-3) | Answer: 2574 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 2 m, bed slope 0.007 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.016. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 4.4 m under a head of 1.2 m. Taking Cd = 0.6 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 3.2 m wide carries a discharge of 20.5 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).

solution: Given: R = 360, V = 55 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (55)^2 / (127*360) | Answer: 0.06616
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: A tank of volume 370 m^3 treats a flow of 195 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 370, Q = 195 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 370 / 195 | Answer: 1.897 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 230 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.32 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 5 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 230, k = 0.32, t = 5 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 230*(1 - e^(-0.32*5)) | Answer: 183.6 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.36, rainfall intensity 100 mm/h over a catchment of 31.1 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.36, i = 100, A = 31.1 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.36*100*31.1 / 360 | Answer: 3.11 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.08 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 750 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.08, M = 750 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 750*(20+0.08)/20 | Answer: 753 m

question: Convert the decimal number 491 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 491 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 1EB (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 11000001 and 01110111.
solution: XOR: 10110110 | Count of 1s = 5 | Answer: 5
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 210 megabits is sent over a link of 55 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 210, B = 55 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 210 / 55 | Answer: 3.818 s

question: A link has bandwidth 41 Mbps and round-trip time 170 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 41, R = 170 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 41e6 * 170e-3 bits = 6970 kb | Answer: 6970 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.9, cache access time 5 ns and main-memory access time 110 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.9, tc = 5, tm = 110 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.9*5 + (1 - 0.9)*110 | Answer: 15.5 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 974856 elements?
solution: Given: n = 974856 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(974856)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.014, memory access time 130 ns and page-fault service time 8 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 8 ms = 8000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.014)*130 + 0.014*8000000.0 ns | Answer: 112.1 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 0.8 m^3 at 480 kPa and 570 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 0.8, P = 480, Tk = 570 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (480e3)*0.8 / (8.314*570) | Answer: 81.03 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.21 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 20 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.21, t = 20 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.21*20) | Answer: 0.985

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.19 /min) is to reach 85% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.19, X = 85 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.85) / 0.19 | Answer: 9.985 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.37 /min) reaches 70% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.37, X = 70 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.7 / (0.37*(1 - 0.7)) | Answer: 6.306 min

question: For a reaction with A = 5e10 /s and activation energy 55 kJ/mol at 390 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 5, Ea = 55, Tk = 390 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 5e10 * exp(-55e3 / (8.314*390)) | Answer: 2149 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.91 and bottoms xW = 0.04, with relative volatility alpha = 2.6. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.91, xw = 0.04, al = 2.6 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.91/0.09)(0.96/0.04)] / ln(2.6) | Answer: 5.747 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.86 and x = 0.22. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.86, x = 0.22 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.86/0.14) / (0.22/0.78) | Answer: 21.78

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.27 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 25 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.27, Psat = 25 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.27 * 25 | Answer: 6.75 kPa

question: A stream of 9.3 kg/s with specific heat 1 kJ/kg-K is heated through 20 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 9.3, cp = 1, dT = 20 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 9.3*1*20 | Answer: 186 kW

question: A reactor of volume 10.6 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 4.3 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 10.6, Q = 4.3 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 10.6 / 4.3 | Answer: 2.465 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 2.5e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 2 mm with a concentration difference of 160 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 2.5, L = 2, dC = 160 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (2.5e-9)*160 / (2e-3) | Answer: 200 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 8.8 min and steady-state gain 3.7. For a step input of magnitude 6, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 8.8, K = 3.7, M = 6 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 3.7 * 6 | Answer: 22.2 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 35 m^2 flies at 210 m/s (air density 1 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.4. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 35, V = 210, rho = 1, CL = 0.4 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1*(210)^2*35*0.4 / 1000 | Answer: 308.7 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 20 m^2 flies at 190 m/s (density 1 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.05. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 20, V = 190, rho = 1, CD = 0.05 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*1*(190)^2*20*0.05 / 1000 | Answer: 18.05 kN

question: A specimen under stress 90 MPa shows an elastic strain of 2.1e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 90, eps = 2.1 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 90 / (2.1e-3) MPa = 42.86 GPa | Answer: 42.86 GPa

question: A block of mass 28 kg has a volume of 2.1e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 28, V = 2.1 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 28 / (2.1e-3) | Answer: 13333 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 1600 mm is heated through 45 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 11e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 1600, dT = 45, al = 11 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 1600*11e-6*45 | Answer: 0.792 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 80 ohm, R2 = 120 ohm and R3 = 370 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 80, R2 = 120, R3 = 370 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 120*370 / 80 | Answer: 555 ohm

question: A measurement reads 9.86 when the true value is 10. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.86, true = 10 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.86 - 10| / 10 * 100 | Answer: 1.4 %

question: Annual demand is 36000 units, ordering cost 40 per order and holding cost 19 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 36000, S = 40, H = 19 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*36000*40 / 19) | Answer: 389.3 units

question: An asset costs 50000 with salvage value 8000 after 8 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 50000, Sv = 8000, n = 8 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (50000 - 8000) / 8 | Answer: 5250 per year

question: A product sells for 310 per unit with variable cost 160 per unit and fixed costs 30000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 310, V = 160, F = 30000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 30000 / (310 - 160) | Answer: 200 units

question: Find the present worth of 135000 received 6 years from now at an interest rate of 12% per year.
solution: Given: F = 135000, n = 6, i = 12 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 135000 / (1 + 0.12)^6 | Answer: 68395 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.98, 0.94 and 0.94 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.98, r2 = 0.94, r3 = 0.94 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.98*0.94*0.94 | Answer: 0.8659

question: A process produces 1 defective items in a batch of 17500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 1, N = 17500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 1/17500 * 1e6 | Answer: 57.14 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = 5x^3 - 5x^2 + 3x - 5 evaluated at x = 5.
For f(x) = 5x^3 - 2x^2 + 3x - 3, find f''(x) at x = 3.
Evaluate the definite integral of (-4x^2 - x + 7) dx from x = -1 to x = 6.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = -4x^3/3 + -1x^2/2 + 7x | Evaluate F(6) - F(-1) | Answer: -257.8
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 3x^2 - 12 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[9, -1], [4, -2]].
solution: Given: a = 9, b = -1, c = 4, d = -2 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (9)(-2) - (-1)(4) | Answer: -14

question: Find the determinant of [[6, 1, -2], [6, 2, -1], [-6, 4, -6]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: -78

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[3, 7], [2, 3]].
solution: Trace tr = 6, Determinant = -5 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 6.742

question: Solve for x: -1x + -1y = -7 and 4x + -3y = -2.
solution: Determinant = -1*-3 - -1*4 = 7 | x = (e d - b f) / det = 2.714 | Answer: x = 2.714
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 19, 29, 20, 93, 1.
solution: Sum = 162 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 32.4 | Answer: 32.4

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 16, 27, 15, 21, 43.
solution: Mean = 24.4 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 11.44

question: Find the slope of the line through (2, 4) and (-8, 3).
solution: Given: x1 = 2, y1 = 4, x2 = -8, y2 = 3 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (3 - 4) / (-8 - 2) | Answer: 0.1

question: Find the distance between the points (5, 2) and (9, -3).
solution: Given: x1 = 5, y1 = 2, x2 = 9, y2 = -3 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((4)^2 + (-5)^2) | Answer: 6.403 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (6,0), (4,3), (1,-1).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 8.5 sq units

question: Find the 10th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -7 and common difference -6.
solution: Given: a = -7, d = -6, n = 10 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -7 + (10 - 1)*-6 | Answer: -61

question: Find the sum of the first 20 terms of an AP with first term 6 and common difference 1.
solution: Given: a = 6, d = 1, n = 20 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 20/2 [2*6 + (20-1)*1] | Answer: 310

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 50000 at 8.2% per annum for 2 years.
solution: Given: P = 50000, R = 8.2, Tt = 2 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 50000 * 8.2 * 2 / 100 | Answer: 8200 currency units

question: Find the amount when 11500 is invested at 8.9% per annum compounded annually for 5 years.
solution: Given: P = 11500, R = 8.9, Tt = 5 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 11500 * (1 + 8.9/100)^5 | Answer: 17613 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (-1, -6, -2) and (6, 7, 2).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (6, 1, 5) and (-5, -4, 4).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 57.78

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (-2, -5, 1) and (4, -5, 4).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 59.48 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number 2 + 11i.
solution: Given: a = 2, b = 11 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((2)^2 + (11)^2) | Answer: 11.18

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number -6 + 5i.
solution: Given: a = -6, b = 5 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(5, -6) | Answer: 140.2 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = 3x^3 - 3x^2 + 5x + 3 at x = 4.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-184 with initial guess x0=5, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.1 and ordinates 2, 16, 13, 14, 16, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 359 and 458.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 359 and 458 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 24 and 80.
solution: Given: a = 24, b = 80 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 24*80 / 8 | Answer: 240
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 23 mm carries an axial tensile load of 84 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 29 mm and length 2000 mm carries an axial load of 79 kN. Take E = 110 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 48 mm transmits a torque of 1350 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 48, Tt = 1350 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(1350*1000) / (pi*(48)^3) | Answer: 62.17 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 52 mm and length 1800 mm carries a torque of 1100 N-m. With G = 77 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (52)^4 / 32 = 717816 mm^4 | theta = (1100*1000)(1800) / (77000 * 717816) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 2.053 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 138 mm wide and 70 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 138, h = 70 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 138*(70)^2 / 6 | Answer: 112700 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (107 mm x 170 mm) carries a bending moment of 28 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (42 mm x 90 mm) has effective length 2500 mm and E = 200 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 420 MPa is designed for a working stress of 170 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 420, sw = 170 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 420 / 170 | Answer: 2.471

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1450 mm and wall thickness 8 mm carries an internal pressure of 2.2 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1450, t = 8, P = 2.2 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 2.2*1450 / (2*8) | Answer: 199.4 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 820 K and 370 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 820, Tc = 370 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 370/820) * 100 | Answer: 54.88 %

question: A refrigerator works between 272 K (cold) and 320 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 272, Th = 320 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 272 / (320 - 272) | Answer: 5.667

question: A heat pump operates between 283 K and 330 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 283, Th = 330 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 330 / (330 - 283) | Answer: 7.021

question: 1.8 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 145 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1.8, dT = 145 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 1.8 * 0.718 * 145 | Answer: 187.4 kJ

question: 2.9 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 40 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.9, dT = 40 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 2.9 * 1.005 * 40 | Answer: 116.6 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 1.2 m^3 at 590 K with mass 4.5 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 1.2, Tk = 590, m = 4.5 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 4.5*0.287*590 / 1.2 | Answer: 635 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 4 kg of air expands isothermally at 300 K from volume V1 to 4*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4, Tk = 300, ratio = 4 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 4*0.287*300*ln(4) | Answer: 477.4 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 4.7 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.17 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 4.7, D = 0.17 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*4.7*0.17 / 0.001 | Answer: 799000

question: Water flows at 2.1 m/s through a pipe of diameter 90 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 12.9 m. Taking Cv = 0.97, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 12.9, cv = 0.97 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.97*sqrt(2*9.81*12.9) | Answer: 15.43 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 250 mm) water flows at 1.5 m/s. It contracts to diameter 80 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 250, d2 = 80, V1 = 1.5 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 1.5*(250/80)^2 | Answer: 14.65 m/s

question: Water flows at 3.2 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.27 m and length 190 m. With friction factor f = 0.033, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 33 teeth drives a gear of 85 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1250 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 33, z2 = 85, N1 = 1250 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1250*33 / 85 | Answer: 485.3 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 250 mm rotates at 750 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 250, N = 750 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.25)*750 / 60 | Answer: 9.817 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 16.8 kW at 600 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 16.8, N = 600 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(16.8*1000) / (2*pi*600) | Answer: 267.4 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 1.3 kg rotates at radius 0.22 m at 1000 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 1900 N/m and mass 12.9 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 1900, m = 12.9 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(1900/12.9) | Answer: 1.932 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 8.5 m^2 and thickness 0.35 m has conductivity k = 34.3 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 160 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 8.5, L = 0.35, k = 34.3, dT = 160 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 34.3*8.5*160 / 0.35 | Answer: 133280 W

question: A surface of area 3.3 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 155 W/m^2-K to surroundings 105 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 3.3, h = 155, dT = 105 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 155*3.3*105 | Answer: 53708 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 250 m/min, feed = 0.36 mm/rev, depth of cut = 1.2 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 250, f = 0.36, d = 1.2 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*250*0.36*1.2 | Answer: 108000 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 200 mm is turned at 800 rpm with a feed of 0.23 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 200, N = 800, f = 0.23 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 200 / (0.23*800) | Answer: 1.087 min

question: A resistor of 26 ohm carries a current of 8.8 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 26, I = 8.8 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 8.8 * 26 | Answer: 228.8 V

question: Three resistors 14 ohm, 98 ohm and 73 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 14, R2 = 98, R3 = 73 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 14 + 98 + 73 | Answer: 185 ohm

question: Two resistors 29 ohm and 111 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 29, R2 = 111 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 29*111 / (29+111) | Answer: 22.99 ohm

question: A device draws 4.4 A at 45 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 45, I = 4.4 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 45 * 4.4 | Answer: 198 W

question: A current of 12 A flows through a 7 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 12, R = 7 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (12)^2 * 7 | Answer: 1008 W

question: Two capacitors 19 uF and 11.7 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 19, C2 = 11.7 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 19*11.7 / (19+11.7) | Answer: 7.241 uF

question: A resistor 95 kohm and capacitor 8.8 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 95, C = 8.8 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (95k)(8.8u) = 836 ms | Answer: 836 ms

question: An inductor 286.3 mH is in series with 156 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 286.3, R = 156 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (286.3e-3) / 156 | Answer: 1.835 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 180.5 mH inductor at 560 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 180.5, f = 560 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (560)(180.5e-3) | Answer: 635.1 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 7.7 uF capacitor at 660 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 7.7, f = 660 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (660)(7.7e-6)) | Answer: 31.32 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 38 ohm, XL = 39 ohm and XC = 103 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 38, XL = 39, XC = 103 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(38^2 + (39 - 103)^2) | Answer: 74.43 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 75.9 mH and C = 7.3 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 75.9, C = 7.3 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(75.9e-3 * 7.3e-6)) | Answer: 213.8 Hz

question: A capacitor of 63.5 uF is charged to 110 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 63.5, V = 110 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*63.5e-6*(110)^2 | Answer: 384.2 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 330 V with 590 primary turns and 100 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 330, N1 = 590, N2 = 100 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 330 * 100/590 | Answer: 55.93 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 380 V and draws an armature current of 32 A. If the armature resistance is 0.12 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 380, Ia = 32, Ra = 0.12 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 380 - 32*0.12 | Answer: 376.2 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 50 A at 415 V (line) with a power factor of 0.98. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 50, VL = 415, pf = 0.98 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*415*50*0.98 / 1000 | Answer: 35.22 kW

question: A load has real power 40 kW and apparent power 180 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 40, S = 180 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 40 / 180 | Answer: 0.2222

question: A machine delivers 105 kW output while drawing 202 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 105, Pi = 202 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 105/202 * 100 | Answer: 51.98 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 18 V across R1 = 42 ohm and R2 = 1 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 18, R1 = 42, R2 = 1 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 18*1 / (42+1) | Answer: 0.4186 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 140 kohm and Rin = 25 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 140, Rin = 25 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 140 / 25 | Answer: 5.6

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 170 kohm and Rg = 12 kohm. Find the voltage gain.

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 5009. Express the gain in decibels (power).

question: A simply supported beam of span 7 m carries a central point load of 90 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.

question: A simply supported beam of span 8 m carries a UDL of 55 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 8, w = 55 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 55*(8)^2 / 8 | Answer: 440 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 2 m carries a point load 5 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 2, W = 5 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 5*2 | Answer: 10 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 3.4 m carries a UDL of 34 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.4, w = 34 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 34*(3.4)^2 / 2 | Answer: 196.5 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.3 m carries a point load 85 kN at distance 2.7 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 9.3, a = 2.7, W = 85 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 85*(9.3 - 2.7) / 9.3 | Answer: 60.32 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 4.6 m) carries a central point load 45 kN. With E = 30 GPa and I = 200e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.

question: A fixed beam of span 7.1 m carries a UDL of 27 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7.1, w = 27 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 27*(7.1)^2 / 12 | Answer: 113.4 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 650 mm, clear cover 50 mm and main bars of diameter 16 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 650, c = 50, dia = 16 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 650 - 50 - 16/2 | Answer: 592 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 12.2 m^2 carrying a factored load of 16.9 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 12.2, w = 16.9 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 16.9 * 12.2 | Answer: 206.2 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 6.5 m, unit weight 18 kN/m^3, phi = 38 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 7.2e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.5, area = 3.9e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 7.2, i = 0.5, A = 3.9 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (7.2e-4)*0.5*(3.9e-3) | Answer: 1404 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 2.3 m, bed slope 0.003 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.025. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 2.6 m under a head of 0.5 m. Taking Cd = 0.62 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.

question: A tank of volume 480 m^3 treats a flow of 140 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 480, Q = 140 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 480 / 140 | Answer: 3.429 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 400 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.31 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 4 days.

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.89, rainfall intensity 45 mm/h over a catchment of 32.7 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.89, i = 45, A = 32.7 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.89*45*32.7 / 360 | Answer: 3.638 m^3/s

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.05 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 600 m with this tape.

question: A file of 70 megabits is sent over a link of 14 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.

question: A link has bandwidth 79 Mbps and round-trip time 60 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 79, R = 60 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 79e6 * 60e-3 bits = 4740 kb | Answer: 4740 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.81, cache access time 3 ns and main-memory access time 200 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.81, tc = 3, tm = 200 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.81*3 + (1 - 0.81)*200 | Answer: 40.43 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 276307 elements?
solution: Given: n = 276307 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(276307)) + 1 | Answer: 19

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.004, memory access time 170 ns and page-fault service time 6 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 0.6 m^3 at 410 kPa and 530 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 0.6, P = 410, Tk = 530 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (410e3)*0.6 / (8.314*530) | Answer: 55.83 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.09 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 18 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.09, t = 18 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.09*18) | Answer: 0.8021

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.17 /min) is to reach 70% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.17, X = 70 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.7) / 0.17 | Answer: 7.082 min

question: For a reaction with A = 2e10 /s and activation energy 90 kJ/mol at 380 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 2, Ea = 90, Tk = 380 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 2e10 * exp(-90e3 / (8.314*380)) | Answer: 0.008496 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.9 and bottoms xW = 0.04, with relative volatility alpha = 2. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.9, xw = 0.04, al = 2 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.9/0.1)(0.96/0.04)] / ln(2) | Answer: 7.755 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.78 and x = 0.38. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.5 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 35 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.5, Psat = 35 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.5 * 35 | Answer: 17.5 kPa

question: A stream of 3.3 kg/s with specific heat 2.1 kJ/kg-K is heated through 10 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.

question: A reactor of volume 14.6 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 3.5 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 7.3e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 4 mm with a concentration difference of 100 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 7.3, L = 4, dC = 100 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (7.3e-9)*100 / (4e-3) | Answer: 182.5 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 1.6 min and steady-state gain 2.8. For a step input of magnitude 6, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 1.6, K = 2.8, M = 6 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 2.8 * 6 | Answer: 16.8 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 30 m^2 flies at 240 m/s (air density 1 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 1. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 30, V = 240, rho = 1, CL = 1 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1*(240)^2*30*1 / 1000 | Answer: 864 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 100 m^2 flies at 150 m/s (density 0.7 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.05. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 100, V = 150, rho = 0.7, CD = 0.05 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.7*(150)^2*100*0.05 / 1000 | Answer: 39.38 kN

question: A specimen under stress 270 MPa shows an elastic strain of 1.7e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.

question: A block of mass 12 kg has a volume of 3.2e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.

question: A rod of length 900 mm is heated through 135 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 23e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 145 ohm, R2 = 70 ohm and R3 = 415 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 145, R2 = 70, R3 = 415 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 70*415 / 145 | Answer: 200.3 ohm

question: A measurement reads 9.19 when the true value is 50. Find the percentage error.

question: Annual demand is 26500 units, ordering cost 50 per order and holding cost 18 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 26500, S = 50, H = 18 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*26500*50 / 18) | Answer: 383.7 units

question: An asset costs 440000 with salvage value 14000 after 9 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
