solution: Given: z1 = 17, z2 = 108, N1 = 350 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 350*17 / 108 | Answer: 55.09 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 600 mm rotates at 1150 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 600, N = 1150 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.6)*1150 / 60 | Answer: 36.13 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 46.1 kW at 1500 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 46.1, N = 1500 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(46.1*1000) / (2*pi*1500) | Answer: 293.5 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 1.3 kg rotates at radius 0.59 m at 1200 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 20000 N/m and mass 4.4 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 20000, m = 4.4 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(20000/4.4) | Answer: 10.73 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 6.7 m^2 and thickness 0.36 m has conductivity k = 29.3 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 50 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 6.7, L = 0.36, k = 29.3, dT = 50 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 29.3*6.7*50 / 0.36 | Answer: 27265 W

question: A surface of area 3 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 60 W/m^2-K to surroundings 95 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 3, h = 60, dT = 95 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 60*3*95 | Answer: 17100 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 240 m/min, feed = 0.45 mm/rev, depth of cut = 1.9 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 240, f = 0.45, d = 1.9 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*240*0.45*1.9 | Answer: 205200 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 320 mm is turned at 1050 rpm with a feed of 0.12 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 320, N = 1050, f = 0.12 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 320 / (0.12*1050) | Answer: 2.54 min

question: A resistor of 92 ohm carries a current of 3.1 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 92, I = 3.1 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 3.1 * 92 | Answer: 285.2 V

question: Three resistors 36 ohm, 64 ohm and 59 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 36, R2 = 64, R3 = 59 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 36 + 64 + 59 | Answer: 159 ohm

question: Two resistors 85 ohm and 78 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 85, R2 = 78 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 85*78 / (85+78) | Answer: 40.67 ohm

question: A device draws 1.6 A at 155 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 155, I = 1.6 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 155 * 1.6 | Answer: 248 W

question: A current of 6.3 A flows through a 31 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 6.3, R = 31 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (6.3)^2 * 31 | Answer: 123 W

question: Two capacitors 29.2 uF and 15.4 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 29.2, C2 = 15.4 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 29.2*15.4 / (29.2+15.4) | Answer: 10.08 uF

question: A resistor 90 kohm and capacitor 1.6 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 90, C = 1.6 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (90k)(1.6u) = 144 ms | Answer: 144 ms

question: An inductor 418.3 mH is in series with 166 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 418.3, R = 166 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (418.3e-3) / 166 | Answer: 2.52 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 11.1 mH inductor at 640 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 11.1, f = 640 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (640)(11.1e-3) | Answer: 44.64 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 29.1 uF capacitor at 800 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 29.1, f = 800 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (800)(29.1e-6)) | Answer: 6.837 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 67 ohm, XL = 126 ohm and XC = 77 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 67, XL = 126, XC = 77 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(67^2 + (126 - 77)^2) | Answer: 83.01 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 72 mH and C = 6 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 72, C = 6 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(72e-3 * 6e-6)) | Answer: 242.1 Hz

question: A capacitor of 46.2 uF is charged to 110 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 46.2, V = 110 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*46.2e-6*(110)^2 | Answer: 279.5 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 140 V with 920 primary turns and 370 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 140, N1 = 920, N2 = 370 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 140 * 370/920 | Answer: 56.3 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 300 V and draws an armature current of 37 A. If the armature resistance is 0.92 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 300, Ia = 37, Ra = 0.92 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 300 - 37*0.92 | Answer: 266 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 120 A at 415 V (line) with a power factor of 0.84. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 120, VL = 415, pf = 0.84 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*415*120*0.84 / 1000 | Answer: 72.46 kW

question: A load has real power 170 kW and apparent power 200 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 170, S = 200 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 170 / 200 | Answer: 0.85

question: A machine delivers 75 kW output while drawing 162 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 75, Pi = 162 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 75/162 * 100 | Answer: 46.3 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 19 V across R1 = 13 ohm and R2 = 8 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 19, R1 = 13, R2 = 8 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 19*8 / (13+8) | Answer: 7.238 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 120 kohm and Rin = 6 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 120, Rin = 6 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 120 / 6 | Answer: 20

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 110 kohm and Rg = 35 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 110, Rg = 35 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 110/35 | Answer: 4.143

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 8966. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 8966 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(8966) | Answer: 39.53 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 3.5 m carries a central point load of 85 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.5, W = 85 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 85*3.5 / 4 | Answer: 74.38 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.1 m carries a UDL of 20 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.1, w = 20 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 20*(4.1)^2 / 8 | Answer: 42.02 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 5.8 m carries a point load 50 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.8, W = 50 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 50*5.8 | Answer: 290 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 3.1 m carries a UDL of 26 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.1, w = 26 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 26*(3.1)^2 / 2 | Answer: 124.9 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.7 m carries a point load 15 kN at distance 3.7 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 6.7, a = 3.7, W = 15 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 15*(6.7 - 3.7) / 6.7 | Answer: 6.716 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 6.1 m) carries a central point load 30 kN. With E = 30 GPa and I = 50e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=30000 N, L=6100.0 mm, E=30000 MPa, I=50e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 94.58 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 5.9 m carries a UDL of 9 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.9, w = 9 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 9*(5.9)^2 / 12 | Answer: 26.11 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 460 mm, clear cover 45 mm and main bars of diameter 16 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 460, c = 45, dia = 16 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 460 - 45 - 16/2 | Answer: 407 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 39.7 m^2 carrying a factored load of 15.4 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 39.7, w = 15.4 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 15.4 * 39.7 | Answer: 611.4 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 4.2 m, unit weight 18 kN/m^3, phi = 37 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 3.8 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 20 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 3.8, g = 20 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (20 - 9.81)*3.8 | Answer: 38.72 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 7.9e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.4, area = 3.4e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 7.9, i = 0.4, A = 3.4 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (7.9e-4)*0.4*(3.4e-3) | Answer: 1074 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 0.9 m, bed slope 0.005 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.028. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 1.4 m under a head of 0.4 m. Taking Cd = 0.62 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 3.5 m wide carries a discharge of 22.9 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 220 m and design speed 70 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 220, V = 70 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (70)^2 / (127*220) | Answer: 0.1754
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: A tank of volume 780 m^3 treats a flow of 130 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 780, Q = 130 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 780 / 130 | Answer: 6 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 270 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.31 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 5 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 270, k = 0.31, t = 5 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 270*(1 - e^(-0.31*5)) | Answer: 212.7 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.89, rainfall intensity 70 mm/h over a catchment of 5.9 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.89, i = 70, A = 5.9 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.89*70*5.9 / 360 | Answer: 1.021 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.02 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 410 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.02, M = 410 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 410*(20+0.02)/20 | Answer: 410.4 m

question: Convert the decimal number 516 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 516 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 204 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 11001100 and 01111010.
solution: XOR: 10110110 | Count of 1s = 5 | Answer: 5
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 340 megabits is sent over a link of 57 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 340, B = 57 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 340 / 57 | Answer: 5.965 s

question: A link has bandwidth 33 Mbps and round-trip time 150 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 33, R = 150 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 33e6 * 150e-3 bits = 4950 kb | Answer: 4950 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.96, cache access time 7 ns and main-memory access time 70 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.96, tc = 7, tm = 70 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.96*7 + (1 - 0.96)*70 | Answer: 9.52 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 862863 elements?
solution: Given: n = 862863 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(862863)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.003, memory access time 190 ns and page-fault service time 3 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 3 ms = 3000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.003)*190 + 0.003*3000000.0 ns | Answer: 9.189 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 1.9 m^3 at 250 kPa and 420 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 1.9, P = 250, Tk = 420 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (250e3)*1.9 / (8.314*420) | Answer: 136 mol

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.26 /min) is to reach 80% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.26, X = 80 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.8) / 0.26 | Answer: 6.19 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.22 /min) reaches 60% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.22, X = 60 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.6 / (0.22*(1 - 0.6)) | Answer: 6.818 min

question: For a reaction with A = 4e10 /s and activation energy 90 kJ/mol at 410 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 4, Ea = 90, Tk = 410 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 4e10 * exp(-90e3 / (8.314*410)) | Answer: 0.1366 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.92 and bottoms xW = 0.04, with relative volatility alpha = 3.3. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.92, xw = 0.04, al = 3.3 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.92/0.08)(0.96/0.04)] / ln(3.3) | Answer: 4.708 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.7 and x = 0.42. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.7, x = 0.42 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.7/0.3) / (0.42/0.58) | Answer: 3.222

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.64 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 85 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.64, Psat = 85 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.64 * 85 | Answer: 54.4 kPa

question: A stream of 1.6 kg/s with specific heat 1.3 kJ/kg-K is heated through 30 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 1.6, cp = 1.3, dT = 30 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 1.6*1.3*30 | Answer: 62.4 kW

question: A reactor of volume 5.5 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 4.7 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 5.5, Q = 4.7 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 5.5 / 4.7 | Answer: 1.17 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 3.8e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 1 mm with a concentration difference of 40 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 3.8, L = 1, dC = 40 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (3.8e-9)*40 / (1e-3) | Answer: 152 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 1.2 min and steady-state gain 3.4. For a step input of magnitude 6, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 1.2, K = 3.4, M = 6 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 3.4 * 6 | Answer: 20.4 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 75 m^2 flies at 230 m/s (air density 1 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.4. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 75, V = 230, rho = 1, CL = 0.4 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1*(230)^2*75*0.4 / 1000 | Answer: 793.5 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 20 m^2 flies at 130 m/s (density 1 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.06. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 20, V = 130, rho = 1, CD = 0.06 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*1*(130)^2*20*0.06 / 1000 | Answer: 10.14 kN

question: A specimen under stress 310 MPa shows an elastic strain of 1.3e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 310, eps = 1.3 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 310 / (1.3e-3) MPa = 238.5 GPa | Answer: 238.5 GPa

question: A block of mass 45 kg has a volume of 3.6e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 45, V = 3.6 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 45 / (3.6e-3) | Answer: 12500 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 2500 mm is heated through 145 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 12e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 2500, dT = 145, al = 12 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 2500*12e-6*145 | Answer: 4.35 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 140 ohm, R2 = 95 ohm and R3 = 150 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 140, R2 = 95, R3 = 150 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 95*150 / 140 | Answer: 101.8 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 120 ohm and gauge factor 2.2 experiences a strain of 1650e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 120, GF = 2.2, eps = 1650 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 120*2.2*1650e-6 | Answer: 435.6 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 10.45 when the true value is 10. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10.45, true = 10 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10.45 - 10| / 10 * 100 | Answer: 4.5 %

question: Annual demand is 26500 units, ordering cost 180 per order and holding cost 31 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 26500, S = 180, H = 31 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*26500*180 / 31) | Answer: 554.7 units

question: An asset costs 150000 with salvage value 32000 after 8 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 150000, Sv = 32000, n = 8 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (150000 - 32000) / 8 | Answer: 14750 per year

question: A product sells for 230 per unit with variable cost 50 per unit and fixed costs 155000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 230, V = 50, F = 155000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 155000 / (230 - 50) | Answer: 861.1 units

question: Find the present worth of 80000 received 6 years from now at an interest rate of 10% per year.
solution: Given: F = 80000, n = 6, i = 10 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 80000 / (1 + 0.1)^6 | Answer: 45158 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.93, 0.98 and 0.9 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.93, r2 = 0.98, r3 = 0.9 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.93*0.98*0.9 | Answer: 0.8203

question: A process produces 47 defective items in a batch of 11000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 47, N = 11000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 47/11000 * 1e6 | Answer: 4273 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -5x^3 + 8x^2 - 5x - 5 evaluated at x = 2.
For f(x) = -6x^3 + 6x^2 - 6x + 2, find f''(x) at x = -5.
Evaluate the definite integral of (5x^2 - x + 4) dx from x = -2 to x = 4.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = 5x^3/3 + -1x^2/2 + 4x | Evaluate F(4) - F(-2) | Answer: 138
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 5x^2 - 2x - 10 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[5, 9], [-3, 4]].
solution: Given: a = 5, b = 9, c = -3, d = 4 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (5)(4) - (9)(-3) | Answer: 47

question: Find the determinant of [[2, 1, -6], [3, 5, -1], [-6, -3, -3]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: -147

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[-4, -8], [-2, -7]].
solution: Trace tr = -11, Determinant = 12 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: -1.228

question: Solve for x: -4x + -2y = 11 and 4x + 1y = -10.
solution: Determinant = -4*1 - -2*4 = 4 | x = (e d - b f) / det = -2.25 | Answer: x = -2.25
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 17, 42, 24, 64, 24.
solution: Sum = 171 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 34.2 | Answer: 34.2

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 14, 6, 7, 39, 25.
solution: Mean = 18.2 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 13.88

question: Find the slope of the line through (-5, -8) and (8, 3).
solution: Given: x1 = -5, y1 = -8, x2 = 8, y2 = 3 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (3 - -8) / (8 - -5) | Answer: 0.8462

question: Find the distance between the points (8, -4) and (-5, 2).
solution: Given: x1 = 8, y1 = -4, x2 = -5, y2 = 2 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-13)^2 + (6)^2) | Answer: 14.32 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (3,-1), (-2,-1), (8,-6).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 12.5 sq units

question: Find the 26th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 13 and common difference 1.
solution: Given: a = 13, d = 1, n = 26 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = 13 + (26 - 1)*1 | Answer: 38

question: Find the sum of the first 23 terms of an AP with first term -8 and common difference 3.
solution: Given: a = -8, d = 3, n = 23 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 23/2 [2*-8 + (23-1)*3] | Answer: 575

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 26500 at 13% per annum for 7 years.
solution: Given: P = 26500, R = 13, Tt = 7 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 26500 * 13 * 7 / 100 | Answer: 24115 currency units

question: Find the amount when 5500 is invested at 6.8% per annum compounded annually for 5 years.
solution: Given: P = 5500, R = 6.8, Tt = 5 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 5500 * (1 + 6.8/100)^5 | Answer: 7642 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (-8, -2, -4) and (-3, 7, -2).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (4, -5, -3) and (3, 0, -4).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 25.96

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (3, -4, 3) and (-5, -6, -1).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 82.49 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number -8 + 2i.
solution: Given: a = -8, b = 2 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((-8)^2 + (2)^2) | Answer: 8.246

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number 10 + -8i.
solution: Given: a = 10, b = -8 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(-8, 10) | Answer: -38.66 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -4x^3 + 6x^2 - 9x + 6 at x = -5.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-107 with initial guess x0=5, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.2 and ordinates 4, 1, 7, 7, 1, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 241 and 57.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 241 and 57 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 65 and 21.
solution: Given: a = 65, b = 21 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 65*21 / 1 | Answer: 1365
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 20 mm carries an axial tensile load of 76 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 12 mm and length 2400 mm carries an axial load of 40 kN. Take E = 200 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 52 mm transmits a torque of 1050 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 52, Tt = 1050 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(1050*1000) / (pi*(52)^3) | Answer: 38.03 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 45 mm and length 2000 mm carries a torque of 1250 N-m. With G = 77 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (45)^4 / 32 = 402578 mm^4 | theta = (1250*1000)(2000) / (77000 * 402578) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 4.621 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 68 mm wide and 290 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 68, h = 290 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 68*(290)^2 / 6 | Answer: 953133 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (106 mm x 180 mm) carries a bending moment of 13 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (80 mm x 160 mm) has effective length 2900 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 740 MPa is designed for a working stress of 90 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 740, sw = 90 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 740 / 90 | Answer: 8.222

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1100 mm and wall thickness 16 mm carries an internal pressure of 0.9 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1100, t = 16, P = 0.9 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 0.9*1100 / (2*16) | Answer: 30.94 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 1140 K and 390 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 1140, Tc = 390 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 390/1140) * 100 | Answer: 65.79 %

question: 4.5 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 80 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.5, dT = 80 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 4.5 * 0.718 * 80 | Answer: 258.5 kJ

question: 8 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 165 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 8, dT = 165 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 8 * 1.005 * 165 | Answer: 1327 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 1.2 m^3 at 390 K with mass 1.9 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 1.2, Tk = 390, m = 1.9 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 1.9*0.287*390 / 1.2 | Answer: 177.2 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 2.4 kg of air expands isothermally at 340 K from volume V1 to 3*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.4, Tk = 340, ratio = 3 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 2.4*0.287*340*ln(3) | Answer: 257.3 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 4.4 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.06 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 4.4, D = 0.06 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*4.4*0.06 / 0.001 | Answer: 264000

question: Water flows at 1.7 m/s through a pipe of diameter 70 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 15.4 m. Taking Cv = 0.96, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 15.4, cv = 0.96 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.96*sqrt(2*9.81*15.4) | Answer: 16.69 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 370 mm) water flows at 1.8 m/s. It contracts to diameter 70 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 370, d2 = 70, V1 = 1.8 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 1.8*(370/70)^2 | Answer: 50.29 m/s

question: Water flows at 2.6 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.29 m and length 340 m. With friction factor f = 0.027, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 16 teeth drives a gear of 70 teeth. If the pinion runs at 750 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.

question: A pulley of diameter 560 mm rotates at 750 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 560, N = 750 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.56)*750 / 60 | Answer: 21.99 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 48.5 kW at 1200 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 48.5, N = 1200 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(48.5*1000) / (2*pi*1200) | Answer: 386 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 2.3 kg rotates at radius 0.33 m at 300 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 17600 N/m and mass 4.7 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 17600, m = 4.7 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(17600/4.7) | Answer: 9.739 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 6.7 m^2 and thickness 0.22 m has conductivity k = 31 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 200 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 6.7, L = 0.22, k = 31, dT = 200 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 31*6.7*200 / 0.22 | Answer: 188818 W

question: A surface of area 0.6 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 55 W/m^2-K to surroundings 125 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 0.6, h = 55, dT = 125 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 55*0.6*125 | Answer: 4125 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 170 m/min, feed = 0.39 mm/rev, depth of cut = 1.5 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 170, f = 0.39, d = 1.5 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*170*0.39*1.5 | Answer: 99450 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 500 mm is turned at 350 rpm with a feed of 0.33 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 500, N = 350, f = 0.33 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 500 / (0.33*350) | Answer: 4.329 min

question: A resistor of 101 ohm carries a current of 9.6 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 101, I = 9.6 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 9.6 * 101 | Answer: 969.6 V

question: Three resistors 22 ohm, 18 ohm and 85 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 22, R2 = 18, R3 = 85 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 22 + 18 + 85 | Answer: 125 ohm

question: Two resistors 101 ohm and 34 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 101, R2 = 34 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 101*34 / (101+34) | Answer: 25.44 ohm

question: A device draws 3 A at 180 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 180, I = 3 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 180 * 3 | Answer: 540 W

question: A current of 8.5 A flows through a 71 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 8.5, R = 71 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (8.5)^2 * 71 | Answer: 513 W

question: Two capacitors 44.8 uF and 41.2 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 44.8, C2 = 41.2 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 44.8*41.2 / (44.8+41.2) | Answer: 21.46 uF

question: A resistor 2 kohm and capacitor 1.3 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 2, C = 1.3 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (2k)(1.3u) = 2.6 ms | Answer: 2.6 ms

question: An inductor 486 mH is in series with 88 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 486, R = 88 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (486e-3) / 88 | Answer: 5.523 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 26.3 mH inductor at 330 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 26.3, f = 330 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (330)(26.3e-3) | Answer: 54.53 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 21.5 uF capacitor at 250 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 21.5, f = 250 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (250)(21.5e-6)) | Answer: 29.61 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 42 ohm, XL = 150 ohm and XC = 16 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 42, XL = 150, XC = 16 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(42^2 + (150 - 16)^2) | Answer: 140.4 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 79 mH and C = 6.4 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 79, C = 6.4 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(79e-3 * 6.4e-6)) | Answer: 223.8 Hz

question: A capacitor of 57 uF is charged to 280 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 57, V = 280 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*57e-6*(280)^2 | Answer: 2234 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 240 V with 910 primary turns and 150 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 240, N1 = 910, N2 = 150 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 240 * 150/910 | Answer: 39.56 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 270 V and draws an armature current of 29 A. If the armature resistance is 0.14 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 270, Ia = 29, Ra = 0.14 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 270 - 29*0.14 | Answer: 265.9 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 145 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.78. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 145, VL = 400, pf = 0.78 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*400*145*0.78 / 1000 | Answer: 78.36 kW

question: A load has real power 65 kW and apparent power 160 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 65, S = 160 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 65 / 160 | Answer: 0.4062

question: A machine delivers 100 kW output while drawing 137 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 100, Pi = 137 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 100/137 * 100 | Answer: 72.99 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 8 V across R1 = 46 ohm and R2 = 11 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 8, R1 = 46, R2 = 11 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 8*11 / (46+11) | Answer: 1.544 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 50 kohm and Rin = 14 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 50, Rin = 14 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 50 / 14 | Answer: 3.571

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 70 kohm and Rg = 18 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 70, Rg = 18 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 70/18 | Answer: 4.889

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 6573. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 6573 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(6573) | Answer: 38.18 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 5.7 m carries a central point load of 75 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.7, W = 75 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 75*5.7 / 4 | Answer: 106.9 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 3.2 m carries a UDL of 15 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.2, w = 15 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 15*(3.2)^2 / 8 | Answer: 19.2 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 4.8 m carries a point load 15 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.8, W = 15 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 15*4.8 | Answer: 72 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 2.5 m carries a UDL of 32 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 2.5, w = 32 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 32*(2.5)^2 / 2 | Answer: 100 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.8 m carries a point load 60 kN at distance 1.5 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 9.8, a = 1.5, W = 60 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 60*(9.8 - 1.5) / 9.8 | Answer: 50.82 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 5.4 m) carries a central point load 70 kN. With E = 200 GPa and I = 100e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.

question: A fixed beam of span 7.8 m carries a UDL of 45 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7.8, w = 45 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 45*(7.8)^2 / 12 | Answer: 228.1 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 400 mm, clear cover 25 mm and main bars of diameter 12 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 400, c = 25, dia = 12 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 400 - 25 - 12/2 | Answer: 369 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 26.5 m^2 carrying a factored load of 10.8 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 26.5, w = 10.8 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 10.8 * 26.5 | Answer: 286.2 kN

question: At a depth of 10 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 19 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 6.7e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1, area = 3.4e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.

question: A tank of volume 440 m^3 treats a flow of 50 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 440, Q = 50 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 440 / 50 | Answer: 8.8 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 220 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.21 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 3 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 220, k = 0.21, t = 3 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 220*(1 - e^(-0.21*3)) | Answer: 102.8 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.78, rainfall intensity 120 mm/h over a catchment of 38.2 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.

question: A file of 480 megabits is sent over a link of 59 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 480, B = 59 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 480 / 59 | Answer: 8.136 s

question: A link has bandwidth 94 Mbps and round-trip time 190 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 94, R = 190 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 94e6 * 190e-3 bits = 17860 kb | Answer: 17860 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.87, cache access time 6 ns and main-memory access time 120 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.87, tc = 6, tm = 120 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.87*6 + (1 - 0.87)*120 | Answer: 20.82 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 748751 elements?
solution: Given: n = 748751 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(748751)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.002, memory access time 110 ns and page-fault service time 4 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 4 ms = 4000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.002)*110 + 0.002*4000000.0 ns | Answer: 8.11 microseconds

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 2.9 m^3 at 280 kPa and 420 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 2.9, P = 280, Tk = 420 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (280e3)*2.9 / (8.314*420) | Answer: 232.5 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.29 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 13 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.29, t = 13 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.29*13) | Answer: 0.9769

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.12 /min) reaches 80% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.12, X = 80 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.8 / (0.12*(1 - 0.8)) | Answer: 33.33 min

question: For a reaction with A = 5e10 /s and activation energy 50 kJ/mol at 320 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 5, Ea = 50, Tk = 320 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 5e10 * exp(-50e3 / (8.314*320)) | Answer: 344.4 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.9 and bottoms xW = 0.06, with relative volatility alpha = 1.8. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.9, xw = 0.06, al = 1.8 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.9/0.1)(0.94/0.06)] / ln(1.8) | Answer: 8.419 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.62 and x = 0.23. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.62, x = 0.23 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.62/0.38) / (0.23/0.77) | Answer: 5.462

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.7 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 50 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.7, Psat = 50 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.7 * 50 | Answer: 35 kPa

question: A stream of 1.6 kg/s with specific heat 2.9 kJ/kg-K is heated through 60 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 1.6, cp = 2.9, dT = 60 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 1.6*2.9*60 | Answer: 278.4 kW

question: A reactor of volume 1.6 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 1.4 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 1.6, Q = 1.4 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 1.6 / 1.4 | Answer: 1.143 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 2.9e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 4 mm with a concentration difference of 40 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 2.9, L = 4, dC = 40 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (2.9e-9)*40 / (4e-3) | Answer: 29 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 4.3 min and steady-state gain 2.2. For a step input of magnitude 12, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 4.3, K = 2.2, M = 12 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 2.2 * 12 | Answer: 26.4 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 85 m^2 flies at 220 m/s (air density 0.7 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.3. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 85, V = 220, rho = 0.7, CL = 0.3 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.7*(220)^2*85*0.3 / 1000 | Answer: 432 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 75 m^2 flies at 140 m/s (density 1 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.06. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 75, V = 140, rho = 1, CD = 0.06 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*1*(140)^2*75*0.06 / 1000 | Answer: 44.1 kN

question: A specimen under stress 230 MPa shows an elastic strain of 0.5e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 230, eps = 0.5 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 230 / (0.5e-3) MPa = 460 GPa | Answer: 460 GPa

question: A block of mass 39 kg has a volume of 3.8e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 39, V = 3.8 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 39 / (3.8e-3) | Answer: 10263 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 1100 mm is heated through 50 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 23e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 1100, dT = 50, al = 23 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 1100*23e-6*50 | Answer: 1.265 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 180 ohm, R2 = 75 ohm and R3 = 65 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 180, R2 = 75, R3 = 65 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 75*65 / 180 | Answer: 27.08 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 120 ohm and gauge factor 2.2 experiences a strain of 1550e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 120, GF = 2.2, eps = 1550 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 120*2.2*1550e-6 | Answer: 409.2 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 10.22 when the true value is 10. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10.22, true = 10 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10.22 - 10| / 10 * 100 | Answer: 2.2 %

question: Annual demand is 15000 units, ordering cost 190 per order and holding cost 40 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 15000, S = 190, H = 40 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*15000*190 / 40) | Answer: 377.5 units

question: An asset costs 300000 with salvage value 14000 after 15 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 300000, Sv = 14000, n = 15 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (300000 - 14000) / 15 | Answer: 19067 per year

question: A product sells for 390 per unit with variable cost 110 per unit and fixed costs 115000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 390, V = 110, F = 115000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 115000 / (390 - 110) | Answer: 410.7 units

question: Find the present worth of 195000 received 10 years from now at an interest rate of 12% per year.
solution: Given: F = 195000, n = 10, i = 12 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 195000 / (1 + 0.12)^10 | Answer: 62785 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.93, 0.9 and 0.96 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.93, r2 = 0.9, r3 = 0.96 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.93*0.9*0.96 | Answer: 0.8035

question: A process produces 7 defective items in a batch of 2500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 7, N = 2500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 7/2500 * 1e6 | Answer: 2800 PPM
