question: A component of ultimate strength 680 MPa is designed for a working stress of 200 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 680, sw = 200 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 680 / 200 | Answer: 3.4

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 800 mm and wall thickness 11 mm carries an internal pressure of 0.8 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 800, t = 11, P = 0.8 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 0.8*800 / (2*11) | Answer: 29.09 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 920 K and 280 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 920, Tc = 280 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 280/920) * 100 | Answer: 69.57 %

question: 7.7 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 40 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 7.7, dT = 40 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 7.7 * 0.718 * 40 | Answer: 221.1 kJ

question: 2.4 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 120 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.4, dT = 120 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 2.4 * 1.005 * 120 | Answer: 289.4 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 1.2 m^3 at 560 K with mass 5.6 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 1.2, Tk = 560, m = 5.6 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 5.6*0.287*560 / 1.2 | Answer: 750 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 4 kg of air expands isothermally at 370 K from volume V1 to 2*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4, Tk = 370, ratio = 2 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 4*0.287*370*ln(2) | Answer: 294.4 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 3.1 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.13 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 3.1, D = 0.13 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*3.1*0.13 / 0.001 | Answer: 403000

question: Water flows at 1.1 m/s through a pipe of diameter 220 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 2 m. Taking Cv = 0.96, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 2, cv = 0.96 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.96*sqrt(2*9.81*2) | Answer: 6.014 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 350 mm) water flows at 2.5 m/s. It contracts to diameter 100 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
Water flows at 1.8 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.21 m and length 200 m. With friction factor f = 0.038, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 33 teeth drives a gear of 83 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1100 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 33, z2 = 83, N1 = 1100 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1100*33 / 83 | Answer: 437.3 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 320 mm rotates at 800 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 320, N = 800 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.32)*800 / 60 | Answer: 13.4 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 47.8 kW at 1350 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 47.8, N = 1350 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(47.8*1000) / (2*pi*1350) | Answer: 338.1 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 5.6 kg rotates at radius 0.1 m at 700 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 12100 N/m and mass 14.5 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 12100, m = 14.5 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(12100/14.5) | Answer: 4.598 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 9.7 m^2 and thickness 0.16 m has conductivity k = 37.7 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 40 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 9.7, L = 0.16, k = 37.7, dT = 40 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 37.7*9.7*40 / 0.16 | Answer: 91422 W

question: A surface of area 2.9 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 30 W/m^2-K to surroundings 110 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 2.9, h = 30, dT = 110 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 30*2.9*110 | Answer: 9570 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 170 m/min, feed = 0.26 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2.8 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 170, f = 0.26, d = 2.8 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*170*0.26*2.8 | Answer: 123760 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 160 mm is turned at 1050 rpm with a feed of 0.14 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 160, N = 1050, f = 0.14 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 160 / (0.14*1050) | Answer: 1.088 min

question: A resistor of 24 ohm carries a current of 9.8 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 24, I = 9.8 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 9.8 * 24 | Answer: 235.2 V

question: Three resistors 76 ohm, 17 ohm and 29 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 76, R2 = 17, R3 = 29 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 76 + 17 + 29 | Answer: 122 ohm

question: Two resistors 62 ohm and 10 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 62, R2 = 10 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 62*10 / (62+10) | Answer: 8.611 ohm

question: A device draws 6 A at 120 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 120, I = 6 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 120 * 6 | Answer: 720 W

question: A current of 11.6 A flows through a 117 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 11.6, R = 117 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (11.6)^2 * 117 | Answer: 15744 W

question: Two capacitors 16.9 uF and 27.6 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 16.9, C2 = 27.6 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 16.9*27.6 / (16.9+27.6) | Answer: 10.48 uF

question: A resistor 81 kohm and capacitor 3.9 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 81, C = 3.9 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (81k)(3.9u) = 315.9 ms | Answer: 315.9 ms

question: An inductor 396.7 mH is in series with 189 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 396.7, R = 189 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (396.7e-3) / 189 | Answer: 2.099 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 15 mH inductor at 690 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 15, f = 690 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (690)(15e-3) | Answer: 65.03 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 34.7 uF capacitor at 570 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 34.7, f = 570 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (570)(34.7e-6)) | Answer: 8.047 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 9 ohm, XL = 64 ohm and XC = 131 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 9, XL = 64, XC = 131 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(9^2 + (64 - 131)^2) | Answer: 67.6 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 49.4 mH and C = 2 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 49.4, C = 2 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(49.4e-3 * 2e-6)) | Answer: 506.3 Hz

question: A capacitor of 94.4 uF is charged to 215 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 94.4, V = 215 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*94.4e-6*(215)^2 | Answer: 2182 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 220 V with 660 primary turns and 170 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 220, N1 = 660, N2 = 170 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 220 * 170/660 | Answer: 56.67 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 400 V and draws an armature current of 25 A. If the armature resistance is 1.05 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 400, Ia = 25, Ra = 1.05 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 400 - 25*1.05 | Answer: 373.8 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 5 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.78. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 5, VL = 400, pf = 0.78 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*400*5*0.78 / 1000 | Answer: 2.702 kW

question: A load has real power 135 kW and apparent power 185 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 135, S = 185 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 135 / 185 | Answer: 0.7297

question: A machine delivers 140 kW output while drawing 152 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 140, Pi = 152 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 140/152 * 100 | Answer: 92.11 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 20 V across R1 = 37 ohm and R2 = 11 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 20, R1 = 37, R2 = 11 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 20*11 / (37+11) | Answer: 4.583 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 70 kohm and Rin = 18 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 70, Rin = 18 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 70 / 18 | Answer: 3.889

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 70 kohm and Rg = 19 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 70, Rg = 19 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 70/19 | Answer: 4.684

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 1633. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 1633 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(1633) | Answer: 32.13 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.3 m carries a central point load of 60 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6.3, W = 60 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 60*6.3 / 4 | Answer: 94.5 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.4 m carries a UDL of 40 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6.4, w = 40 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 40*(6.4)^2 / 8 | Answer: 204.8 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 2.7 m carries a point load 55 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 2.7, W = 55 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 55*2.7 | Answer: 148.5 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 5 m carries a UDL of 22 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5, w = 22 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 22*(5)^2 / 2 | Answer: 275 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.4 m carries a point load 55 kN at distance 2.7 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 9.4, a = 2.7, W = 55 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 55*(9.4 - 2.7) / 9.4 | Answer: 39.2 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 4.2 m) carries a central point load 25 kN. With E = 25 GPa and I = 310e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=25000 N, L=4200.0 mm, E=25000 MPa, I=310e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 4.979 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 6.8 m carries a UDL of 27 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6.8, w = 27 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 27*(6.8)^2 / 12 | Answer: 104 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 390 mm, clear cover 30 mm and main bars of diameter 12 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 390, c = 30, dia = 12 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 390 - 30 - 12/2 | Answer: 354 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 31.6 m^2 carrying a factored load of 11.6 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 31.6, w = 11.6 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 11.6 * 31.6 | Answer: 366.6 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 6.2 m, unit weight 19 kN/m^3, phi = 32 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 11.4 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 19 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 11.4, g = 19 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (19 - 9.81)*11.4 | Answer: 104.8 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 8.4e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1.4, area = 6.3e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 8.4, i = 1.4, A = 6.3 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (8.4e-4)*1.4*(6.3e-3) | Answer: 7409 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 2 m, bed slope 0.009 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.027. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 2.9 m under a head of 0.4 m. Taking Cd = 0.6 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 3.4 m wide carries a discharge of 6.6 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 390 m and design speed 85 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 390, V = 85 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (85)^2 / (127*390) | Answer: 0.1459
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: A tank of volume 160 m^3 treats a flow of 120 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 160, Q = 120 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 160 / 120 | Answer: 1.333 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 220 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.13 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 3 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 220, k = 0.13, t = 3 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 220*(1 - e^(-0.13*3)) | Answer: 71.05 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.69, rainfall intensity 45 mm/h over a catchment of 13.9 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.69, i = 45, A = 13.9 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.69*45*13.9 / 360 | Answer: 1.199 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.04 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 100 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.04, M = 100 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 100*(20+0.04)/20 | Answer: 100.2 m

question: Convert the decimal number 2315 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 2315 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 90B (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 10110010 and 10010010.
solution: XOR: 00100000 | Count of 1s = 1 | Answer: 1
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 700 megabits is sent over a link of 57 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 700, B = 57 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 700 / 57 | Answer: 12.28 s

question: A link has bandwidth 56 Mbps and round-trip time 160 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 56, R = 160 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 56e6 * 160e-3 bits = 8960 kb | Answer: 8960 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.85, cache access time 3 ns and main-memory access time 130 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.85, tc = 3, tm = 130 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.85*3 + (1 - 0.85)*130 | Answer: 22.05 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 212709 elements?
solution: Given: n = 212709 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(212709)) + 1 | Answer: 18

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.012, memory access time 120 ns and page-fault service time 10 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 10 ms = 10000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.012)*120 + 0.012*10000000.0 ns | Answer: 120.1 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 2.4 m^3 at 480 kPa and 350 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 2.4, P = 480, Tk = 350 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (480e3)*2.4 / (8.314*350) | Answer: 395.9 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.1 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 18 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.1, t = 18 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.1*18) | Answer: 0.8347

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.11 /min) is to reach 70% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.11, X = 70 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.7) / 0.11 | Answer: 10.95 min

question: For a reaction with A = 1e10 /s and activation energy 50 kJ/mol at 420 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 1, Ea = 50, Tk = 420 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 1e10 * exp(-50e3 / (8.314*420)) | Answer: 6045 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.97 and bottoms xW = 0.09, with relative volatility alpha = 2.8. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.97, xw = 0.09, al = 2.8 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.97/0.03)(0.91/0.09)] / ln(2.8) | Answer: 5.623 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.74 and x = 0.39. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.74, x = 0.39 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.74/0.26) / (0.39/0.61) | Answer: 4.452

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.71 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 50 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.71, Psat = 50 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.71 * 50 | Answer: 35.5 kPa

question: A stream of 8.5 kg/s with specific heat 3 kJ/kg-K is heated through 85 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 8.5, cp = 3, dT = 85 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 8.5*3*85 | Answer: 2168 kW

question: A reactor of volume 11.3 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 1.9 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 11.3, Q = 1.9 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 11.3 / 1.9 | Answer: 5.947 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 8.7e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 3 mm with a concentration difference of 200 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 8.7, L = 3, dC = 200 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (8.7e-9)*200 / (3e-3) | Answer: 580 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 3.1 min and steady-state gain 1.2. For a step input of magnitude 6, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 3.1, K = 1.2, M = 6 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 1.2 * 6 | Answer: 7.2 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 120 m^2 flies at 140 m/s (air density 0.4 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 1. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 120, V = 140, rho = 0.4, CL = 1 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.4*(140)^2*120*1 / 1000 | Answer: 470.4 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 25 m^2 flies at 110 m/s (density 1.225 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.05. Find the drag force in kN.
A specimen under stress 240 MPa shows an elastic strain of 2.4e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 240, eps = 2.4 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 240 / (2.4e-3) MPa = 100 GPa | Answer: 100 GPa

question: A block of mass 4 kg has a volume of 1.2e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 4, V = 1.2 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 4 / (1.2e-3) | Answer: 3333 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 1800 mm is heated through 30 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 12e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 1800, dT = 30, al = 12 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 1800*12e-6*30 | Answer: 0.648 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 165 ohm, R2 = 30 ohm and R3 = 335 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 165, R2 = 30, R3 = 335 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 30*335 / 165 | Answer: 60.91 ohm

question: A measurement reads 10.06 when the true value is 10. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10.06, true = 10 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10.06 - 10| / 10 * 100 | Answer: 0.6 %

question: Annual demand is 6500 units, ordering cost 190 per order and holding cost 17 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 6500, S = 190, H = 17 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*6500*190 / 17) | Answer: 381.2 units

question: An asset costs 190000 with salvage value 16000 after 9 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 190000, Sv = 16000, n = 9 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (190000 - 16000) / 9 | Answer: 19333 per year

question: A product sells for 370 per unit with variable cost 190 per unit and fixed costs 75000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 370, V = 190, F = 75000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 75000 / (370 - 190) | Answer: 416.7 units

question: Find the present worth of 85000 received 8 years from now at an interest rate of 8% per year.
solution: Given: F = 85000, n = 8, i = 8 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 85000 / (1 + 0.08)^8 | Answer: 45923 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.95, 0.97 and 0.97 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.95, r2 = 0.97, r3 = 0.97 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.95*0.97*0.97 | Answer: 0.8939

question: A process produces 13 defective items in a batch of 16500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 13, N = 16500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 13/16500 * 1e6 | Answer: 787.9 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -x^3 + 3x^2 - 9x + 5 evaluated at x = -2.
For f(x) = 4x^3 - 4x^2 - 7x + 5, find f''(x) at x = -5.
Evaluate the definite integral of (3x - 2) dx from x = 1 to x = 4.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = 0x^3/3 + 3x^2/2 + -2x | Evaluate F(4) - F(1) | Answer: 16.5
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 5x^2 + x - 9 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[-9, -3], [-2, 0]].
solution: Given: a = -9, b = -3, c = -2, d = 0 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (-9)(0) - (-3)(-2) | Answer: -6

question: Find the determinant of [[1, 1, 5], [6, 0, 6], [6, -6, -3]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: -90

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[8, 5], [6, 0]].
solution: Trace tr = 8, Determinant = -30 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 10.78

question: Solve for x: -3x + 0y = 2 and 0x + -5y = -1.
solution: Determinant = -3*-5 - 0*0 = 15 | x = (e d - b f) / det = -0.6667 | Answer: x = -0.6667
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 63, 54, 4, 67, 35.
solution: Sum = 223 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 44.6 | Answer: 44.6

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 5, 48, 4, 50, 10.
solution: Mean = 23.4 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 23.49

question: Find the slope of the line through (1, -6) and (-4, -7).
solution: Given: x1 = 1, y1 = -6, x2 = -4, y2 = -7 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (-7 - -6) / (-4 - 1) | Answer: 0.2

question: Find the distance between the points (-4, -1) and (-5, -8).
solution: Given: x1 = -4, y1 = -1, x2 = -5, y2 = -8 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-1)^2 + (-7)^2) | Answer: 7.071 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (-6,7), (4,0), (4,1).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 5 sq units

question: Find the 8th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -8 and common difference -8.
solution: Given: a = -8, d = -8, n = 8 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -8 + (8 - 1)*-8 | Answer: -64

question: Find the sum of the first 18 terms of an AP with first term -12 and common difference 0.
solution: Given: a = -12, d = 0, n = 18 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 18/2 [2*-12 + (18-1)*0] | Answer: -216

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 1000 at 9.1% per annum for 9 years.
solution: Given: P = 1000, R = 9.1, Tt = 9 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 1000 * 9.1 * 9 / 100 | Answer: 819 currency units

question: Find the amount when 38500 is invested at 6.7% per annum compounded annually for 5 years.
solution: Given: P = 38500, R = 6.7, Tt = 5 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 38500 * (1 + 6.7/100)^5 | Answer: 53245 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (-4, -3, 3) and (0, -6, -6).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (2, 6, -4) and (3, 1, 5).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 43.54

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (-6, -1, -6) and (0, -1, 5).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 131.7 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number -2 + -3i.
solution: Given: a = -2, b = -3 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((-2)^2 + (-3)^2) | Answer: 3.606

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number 10 + 8i.
solution: Given: a = 10, b = 8 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(8, 10) | Answer: 38.66 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = 5x^3 - 6x^2 - 6x + 2 at x = -2.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-113 with initial guess x0=2, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=0.9 and ordinates 20, 13, 17, 0, 19, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 476 and 543.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 476 and 543 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 56 and 77.
solution: Given: a = 56, b = 77 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 56*77 / 7 | Answer: 616
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 16 mm carries an axial tensile load of 8 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 30 mm and length 2800 mm carries an axial load of 42 kN. Take E = 70 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 74 mm transmits a torque of 1600 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 74, Tt = 1600 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(1600*1000) / (pi*(74)^3) | Answer: 20.11 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 51 mm and length 700 mm carries a torque of 1800 N-m. With G = 45 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (51)^4 / 32 = 664172 mm^4 | theta = (1800*1000)(700) / (45000 * 664172) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 2.415 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 80 mm wide and 230 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 80, h = 230 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 80*(230)^2 / 6 | Answer: 705333 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (51 mm x 80 mm) carries a bending moment of 10 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (64 mm x 150 mm) has effective length 2700 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 400 MPa is designed for a working stress of 120 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 400, sw = 120 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 400 / 120 | Answer: 3.333

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1500 mm and wall thickness 15 mm carries an internal pressure of 1 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1500, t = 15, P = 1 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 1*1500 / (2*15) | Answer: 50 MPa

question: A refrigerator works between 258 K (cold) and 310 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 258, Th = 310 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 258 / (310 - 258) | Answer: 4.962

question: 6.8 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 200 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 6.8, dT = 200 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 6.8 * 0.718 * 200 | Answer: 976.5 kJ

question: 3.8 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 185 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.8, dT = 185 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 3.8 * 1.005 * 185 | Answer: 706.5 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 1.2 m^3 at 370 K with mass 5.1 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 1.2, Tk = 370, m = 5.1 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 5.1*0.287*370 / 1.2 | Answer: 451.3 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 4.1 kg of air expands isothermally at 480 K from volume V1 to 5*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.1, Tk = 480, ratio = 5 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 4.1*0.287*480*ln(5) | Answer: 909 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 3.6 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.09 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 3.6, D = 0.09 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*3.6*0.09 / 0.001 | Answer: 324000

question: Water flows at 2.8 m/s through a pipe of diameter 260 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 17.1 m. Taking Cv = 0.98, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 17.1, cv = 0.98 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.98*sqrt(2*9.81*17.1) | Answer: 17.95 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 170 mm) water flows at 0.7 m/s. It contracts to diameter 140 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
Water flows at 3.7 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.34 m and length 380 m. With friction factor f = 0.037, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 30 teeth drives a gear of 111 teeth. If the pinion runs at 750 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 30, z2 = 111, N1 = 750 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 750*30 / 111 | Answer: 202.7 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 110 mm rotates at 800 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 110, N = 800 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.11)*800 / 60 | Answer: 4.608 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 24.5 kW at 1250 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 24.5, N = 1250 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(24.5*1000) / (2*pi*1250) | Answer: 187.2 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 8.7 kg rotates at radius 0.28 m at 200 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 800 N/m and mass 15.1 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 800, m = 15.1 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(800/15.1) | Answer: 1.158 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 9 m^2 and thickness 0.32 m has conductivity k = 44.1 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 120 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 9, L = 0.32, k = 44.1, dT = 120 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 44.1*9*120 / 0.32 | Answer: 148838 W

question: A surface of area 4.3 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 35 W/m^2-K to surroundings 100 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 4.3, h = 35, dT = 100 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 35*4.3*100 | Answer: 15050 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 210 m/min, feed = 0.16 mm/rev, depth of cut = 1.2 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 210, f = 0.16, d = 1.2 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*210*0.16*1.2 | Answer: 40320 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 100 mm is turned at 1150 rpm with a feed of 0.26 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 100, N = 1150, f = 0.26 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 100 / (0.26*1150) | Answer: 0.3344 min

question: A resistor of 181 ohm carries a current of 9.2 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 181, I = 9.2 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 9.2 * 181 | Answer: 1665 V

question: Three resistors 90 ohm, 16 ohm and 22 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 90, R2 = 16, R3 = 22 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 90 + 16 + 22 | Answer: 128 ohm

question: Two resistors 12 ohm and 91 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 12, R2 = 91 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 12*91 / (12+91) | Answer: 10.6 ohm

question: A device draws 8.3 A at 20 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 20, I = 8.3 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 20 * 8.3 | Answer: 166 W

question: A current of 10.8 A flows through a 5 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 10.8, R = 5 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (10.8)^2 * 5 | Answer: 583.2 W

question: Two capacitors 47.2 uF and 32.7 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 47.2, C2 = 32.7 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 47.2*32.7 / (47.2+32.7) | Answer: 19.32 uF

question: A resistor 88 kohm and capacitor 3.8 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 88, C = 3.8 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (88k)(3.8u) = 334.4 ms | Answer: 334.4 ms

question: An inductor 492 mH is in series with 89 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 492, R = 89 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (492e-3) / 89 | Answer: 5.528 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 25.2 mH inductor at 880 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 25.2, f = 880 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (880)(25.2e-3) | Answer: 139.3 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 38.2 uF capacitor at 790 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 38.2, f = 790 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (790)(38.2e-6)) | Answer: 5.274 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 52 ohm, XL = 101 ohm and XC = 114 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 52, XL = 101, XC = 114 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(52^2 + (101 - 114)^2) | Answer: 53.6 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 59.5 mH and C = 2.6 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 59.5, C = 2.6 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(59.5e-3 * 2.6e-6)) | Answer: 404.6 Hz

question: A capacitor of 61.3 uF is charged to 300 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 61.3, V = 300 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*61.3e-6*(300)^2 | Answer: 2758 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 290 V with 260 primary turns and 310 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 290, N1 = 260, N2 = 310 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 290 * 310/260 | Answer: 345.8 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 230 V and draws an armature current of 17 A. If the armature resistance is 0.12 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 230, Ia = 17, Ra = 0.12 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 230 - 17*0.12 | Answer: 228 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 185 A at 415 V (line) with a power factor of 0.84. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 185, VL = 415, pf = 0.84 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*415*185*0.84 / 1000 | Answer: 111.7 kW

question: A load has real power 95 kW and apparent power 160 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 95, S = 160 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 95 / 160 | Answer: 0.5938

question: A machine delivers 50 kW output while drawing 57 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 50, Pi = 57 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 50/57 * 100 | Answer: 87.72 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 20 V across R1 = 18 ohm and R2 = 7 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 20, R1 = 18, R2 = 7 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 20*7 / (18+7) | Answer: 5.6 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 90 kohm and Rin = 16 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 90, Rin = 16 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 90 / 16 | Answer: 5.625

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 160 kohm and Rg = 26 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 160, Rg = 26 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 160/26 | Answer: 7.154

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 6639. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 6639 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(6639) | Answer: 38.22 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.7 m carries a central point load of 25 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.7, W = 25 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 25*4.7 / 4 | Answer: 29.38 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 3.7 m carries a UDL of 50 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.7, w = 50 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 50*(3.7)^2 / 8 | Answer: 85.56 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 4.2 m carries a point load 20 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.2, W = 20 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 20*4.2 | Answer: 84 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 4.2 m carries a UDL of 36 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.2, w = 36 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 36*(4.2)^2 / 2 | Answer: 317.5 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.2 m carries a point load 25 kN at distance 3.8 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 4.2, a = 3.8, W = 25 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 25*(4.2 - 3.8) / 4.2 | Answer: 2.381 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 3.8 m) carries a central point load 10 kN. With E = 25 GPa and I = 370e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=10000 N, L=3800.0 mm, E=25000 MPa, I=370e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 1.236 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 5.3 m carries a UDL of 21 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.3, w = 21 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 21*(5.3)^2 / 12 | Answer: 49.16 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 390 mm, clear cover 50 mm and main bars of diameter 25 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 390, c = 50, dia = 25 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 390 - 50 - 25/2 | Answer: 327.5 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 15.4 m^2 carrying a factored load of 12.1 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 15.4, w = 12.1 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 12.1 * 15.4 | Answer: 186.3 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 5.8 m, unit weight 20 kN/m^3, phi = 28 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 8 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 20 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 8, g = 20 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (20 - 9.81)*8 | Answer: 81.52 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 5.2e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.9, area = 3.7e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 5.2, i = 0.9, A = 3.7 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (5.2e-4)*0.9*(3.7e-3) | Answer: 1732 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 2.5 m, bed slope 0.001 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.029. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 1.2 m under a head of 0.6 m. Taking Cd = 0.63 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 4.5 m wide carries a discharge of 19.4 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 310 m and design speed 65 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 310, V = 65 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (65)^2 / (127*310) | Answer: 0.1073
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: A tank of volume 650 m^3 treats a flow of 130 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 650, Q = 130 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 650 / 130 | Answer: 5 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 280 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.27 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 3 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 280, k = 0.27, t = 3 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 280*(1 - e^(-0.27*3)) | Answer: 155.4 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.49, rainfall intensity 120 mm/h over a catchment of 23.6 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.49, i = 120, A = 23.6 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.49*120*23.6 / 360 | Answer: 3.855 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.07 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 670 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.07, M = 670 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 670*(30+0.07)/30 | Answer: 671.6 m

question: Convert the decimal number 1817 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 1817 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 719 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 01010100 and 00011010.
solution: XOR: 01001110 | Count of 1s = 4 | Answer: 4
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 190 megabits is sent over a link of 31 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 190, B = 31 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 190 / 31 | Answer: 6.129 s

question: A link has bandwidth 44 Mbps and round-trip time 30 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 44, R = 30 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 44e6 * 30e-3 bits = 1320 kb | Answer: 1320 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.94, cache access time 4 ns and main-memory access time 170 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.94, tc = 4, tm = 170 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.94*4 + (1 - 0.94)*170 | Answer: 13.96 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 268319 elements?
solution: Given: n = 268319 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(268319)) + 1 | Answer: 19

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.012, memory access time 150 ns and page-fault service time 8 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 8 ms = 8000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.012)*150 + 0.012*8000000.0 ns | Answer: 96.15 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 2 m^3 at 180 kPa and 590 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 2, P = 180, Tk = 590 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (180e3)*2 / (8.314*590) | Answer: 73.39 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.3 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 17 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.3, t = 17 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.3*17) | Answer: 0.9939

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.27 /min) is to reach 80% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.27, X = 80 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.8) / 0.27 | Answer: 5.961 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.38 /min) reaches 75% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.38, X = 75 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.75 / (0.38*(1 - 0.75)) | Answer: 7.895 min

question: For a reaction with A = 6e10 /s and activation energy 70 kJ/mol at 460 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 6, Ea = 70, Tk = 460 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 6e10 * exp(-70e3 / (8.314*460)) | Answer: 674.7 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.98 and bottoms xW = 0.07, with relative volatility alpha = 3. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.98, xw = 0.07, al = 3 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.98/0.02)(0.93/0.07)] / ln(3) | Answer: 5.897 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.77 and x = 0.24. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.77, x = 0.24 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.77/0.23) / (0.24/0.76) | Answer: 10.6

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.32 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 95 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.32, Psat = 95 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.32 * 95 | Answer: 30.4 kPa

question: A stream of 2.4 kg/s with specific heat 4 kJ/kg-K is heated through 105 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 2.4, cp = 4, dT = 105 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 2.4*4*105 | Answer: 1008 kW

question: A reactor of volume 18.9 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 2.5 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 18.9, Q = 2.5 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 18.9 / 2.5 | Answer: 7.56 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 2.6e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 3 mm with a concentration difference of 70 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 2.6, L = 3, dC = 70 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (2.6e-9)*70 / (3e-3) | Answer: 60.67 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 4.8 min and steady-state gain 1. For a step input of magnitude 12, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 4.8, K = 1, M = 12 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 1 * 12 | Answer: 12 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 90 m^2 flies at 170 m/s (air density 0.7 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 1.2. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 90, V = 170, rho = 0.7, CL = 1.2 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.7*(170)^2*90*1.2 / 1000 | Answer: 1092 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 30 m^2 flies at 230 m/s (density 0.7 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.07. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 30, V = 230, rho = 0.7, CD = 0.07 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.7*(230)^2*30*0.07 / 1000 | Answer: 38.88 kN

question: A specimen under stress 130 MPa shows an elastic strain of 2.7e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 130, eps = 2.7 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 130 / (2.7e-3) MPa = 48.15 GPa | Answer: 48.15 GPa

question: A block of mass 11 kg has a volume of 2.8e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 11, V = 2.8 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 11 / (2.8e-3) | Answer: 3929 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 900 mm is heated through 100 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 12e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 900, dT = 100, al = 12 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 900*12e-6*100 | Answer: 1.08 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 10 ohm, R2 = 10 ohm and R3 = 245 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 10, R2 = 10, R3 = 245 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 10*245 / 10 | Answer: 245 ohm

question: A measurement reads 10.37 when the true value is 50. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10.37, true = 50 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10.37 - 50| / 50 * 100 | Answer: 79.26 %

question: Annual demand is 13500 units, ordering cost 130 per order and holding cost 31 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 13500, S = 130, H = 31 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*13500*130 / 31) | Answer: 336.5 units

question: An asset costs 200000 with salvage value 40000 after 11 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 200000, Sv = 40000, n = 11 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (200000 - 40000) / 11 | Answer: 14545 per year

question: A product sells for 130 per unit with variable cost 90 per unit and fixed costs 155000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 130, V = 90, F = 155000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 155000 / (130 - 90) | Answer: 3875 units

question: Find the present worth of 70000 received 8 years from now at an interest rate of 6% per year.
solution: Given: F = 70000, n = 8, i = 6 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 70000 / (1 + 0.06)^8 | Answer: 43919 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.97, 0.94 and 0.96 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.97, r2 = 0.94, r3 = 0.96 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.97*0.94*0.96 | Answer: 0.8753

question: A process produces 20 defective items in a batch of 3500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 20, N = 3500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 20/3500 * 1e6 | Answer: 5714 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -4x^3 - 2x^2 - 5x - 2 evaluated at x = -5.
For f(x) = -x^3 - 7x^2 - 6x - 1, find f''(x) at x = 3.

solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: 54

solution: Trace tr = -4, Determinant = -27 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 3.568

solution: Sum = 283 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 56.6 | Answer: 56.6

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 24, 35, 43, 7, 22.
solution: Mean = 26.2 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 13.7

question: Find the slope of the line through (1, -4) and (9, 0).
solution: Given: x1 = 1, y1 = -4, x2 = 9, y2 = 0 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (0 - -4) / (9 - 1) | Answer: 0.5

question: Find the distance between the points (9, -5) and (-3, 1).
solution: Given: x1 = 9, y1 = -5, x2 = -3, y2 = 1 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-12)^2 + (6)^2) | Answer: 13.42 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (-4,4), (2,2), (3,-8).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 29 sq units

question: Find the 39th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 2 and common difference -6.
solution: Given: a = 2, d = -6, n = 39 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = 2 + (39 - 1)*-6 | Answer: -226

question: Find the sum of the first 15 terms of an AP with first term 5 and common difference -7.
solution: Given: a = 5, d = -7, n = 15 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 15/2 [2*5 + (15-1)*-7] | Answer: -660

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 15500 at 5.2% per annum for 4 years.
solution: Given: P = 15500, R = 5.2, Tt = 4 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 15500 * 5.2 * 4 / 100 | Answer: 3224 currency units

question: Find the amount when 31000 is invested at 9.1% per annum compounded annually for 4 years.
solution: Given: P = 31000, R = 9.1, Tt = 4 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 31000 * (1 + 9.1/100)^4 | Answer: 4392 currency units

solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 34.7 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number -4 + 11i.
solution: Given: a = -4, b = 11 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((-4)^2 + (11)^2) | Answer: 11.7

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number -7 + 12i.
solution: Given: a = -7, b = 12 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(12, -7) | Answer: 120.3 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = 5x^3 + 7x^2 - 9x - 1 at x = 2.

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 60 and 70.

question: A circular rod of diameter 27 mm carries an axial tensile load of 91 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 31 mm and length 1100 mm carries an axial load of 89 kN. Take E = 110 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 25 mm transmits a torque of 1550 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 25, Tt = 1550 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(1550*1000) / (pi*(25)^3) | Answer: 505.2 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 52 mm and length 1300 mm carries a torque of 2000 N-m. With G = 80 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (52)^4 / 32 = 717816 mm^4 | theta = (2000*1000)(1300) / (80000 * 717816) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 2.594 degrees

question: A rectangular beam section is 150 mm wide and 180 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 150, h = 180 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 150*(180)^2 / 6 | Answer: 810000 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (74 mm x 160 mm) carries a bending moment of 30 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (46 mm x 130 mm) has effective length 1700 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
