question: A component of ultimate strength 540 MPa is designed for a working stress of 100 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 540, sw = 100 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 540 / 100 | Answer: 5.4

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 500 mm and wall thickness 20 mm carries an internal pressure of 2.8 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 500, t = 20, P = 2.8 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 2.8*500 / (2*20) | Answer: 35 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 600 K and 380 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 600, Tc = 380 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 380/600) * 100 | Answer: 36.67 %

question: A refrigerator works between 271 K (cold) and 324 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 271, Th = 324 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 271 / (324 - 271) | Answer: 5.113

question: A heat pump operates between 262 K and 328 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 262, Th = 328 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 328 / (328 - 262) | Answer: 4.97

question: 6.1 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 95 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 6.1, dT = 95 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 6.1 * 0.718 * 95 | Answer: 416.1 kJ

question: 6.5 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 90 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 6.5, dT = 90 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 6.5 * 1.005 * 90 | Answer: 587.9 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 1.9 m^3 at 460 K with mass 1.3 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 1.9, Tk = 460, m = 1.3 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 1.3*0.287*460 / 1.9 | Answer: 90.33 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 4.2 kg of air expands isothermally at 480 K from volume V1 to 4*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.2, Tk = 480, ratio = 4 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 4.2*0.287*480*ln(4) | Answer: 802.1 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 4.4 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.37 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 4.4, D = 0.37 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*4.4*0.37 / 0.001 | Answer: 1628000

question: Water flows at 1.6 m/s through a pipe of diameter 50 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 18.5 m. Taking Cv = 0.98, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 18.5, cv = 0.98 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.98*sqrt(2*9.81*18.5) | Answer: 18.67 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 180 mm) water flows at 0.9 m/s. It contracts to diameter 50 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 180, d2 = 50, V1 = 0.9 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 0.9*(180/50)^2 | Answer: 11.66 m/s

question: Water flows at 2 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.4 m and length 50 m. With friction factor f = 0.025, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 38 teeth drives a gear of 110 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1350 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 38, z2 = 110, N1 = 1350 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1350*38 / 110 | Answer: 466.4 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 420 mm rotates at 1500 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 420, N = 1500 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.42)*1500 / 60 | Answer: 32.99 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 38.8 kW at 1200 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 38.8, N = 1200 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(38.8*1000) / (2*pi*1200) | Answer: 308.8 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 2.5 kg rotates at radius 0.16 m at 1050 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 8000 N/m and mass 11.8 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 8000, m = 11.8 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(8000/11.8) | Answer: 4.144 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 3.5 m^2 and thickness 0.14 m has conductivity k = 26.7 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 95 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 3.5, L = 0.14, k = 26.7, dT = 95 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 26.7*3.5*95 / 0.14 | Answer: 63412 W

question: A surface of area 3.1 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 65 W/m^2-K to surroundings 65 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 3.1, h = 65, dT = 65 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 65*3.1*65 | Answer: 13098 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 90 m/min, feed = 0.22 mm/rev, depth of cut = 0.7 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 90, f = 0.22, d = 0.7 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*90*0.22*0.7 | Answer: 13860 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 220 mm is turned at 1000 rpm with a feed of 0.26 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 220, N = 1000, f = 0.26 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 220 / (0.26*1000) | Answer: 0.8462 min

question: A resistor of 126 ohm carries a current of 1.8 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 126, I = 1.8 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 1.8 * 126 | Answer: 226.8 V

question: Three resistors 27 ohm, 28 ohm and 60 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 27, R2 = 28, R3 = 60 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 27 + 28 + 60 | Answer: 115 ohm

question: Two resistors 60 ohm and 6 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 60, R2 = 6 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 60*6 / (60+6) | Answer: 5.455 ohm

question: A device draws 3.9 A at 45 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 45, I = 3.9 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 45 * 3.9 | Answer: 175.5 W

question: A current of 1 A flows through a 35 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 1, R = 35 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (1)^2 * 35 | Answer: 35 W

question: Two capacitors 38.2 uF and 17.9 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 38.2, C2 = 17.9 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 38.2*17.9 / (38.2+17.9) | Answer: 12.19 uF

question: A resistor 67 kohm and capacitor 16.1 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 67, C = 16.1 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (67k)(16.1u) = 1079 ms | Answer: 1079 ms

question: An inductor 56.6 mH is in series with 73 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 56.6, R = 73 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (56.6e-3) / 73 | Answer: 0.7753 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 164.9 mH inductor at 640 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 164.9, f = 640 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (640)(164.9e-3) | Answer: 663.1 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 3.7 uF capacitor at 710 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 3.7, f = 710 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (710)(3.7e-6)) | Answer: 60.58 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 98 ohm, XL = 36 ohm and XC = 128 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 98, XL = 36, XC = 128 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(98^2 + (36 - 128)^2) | Answer: 134.4 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 99.9 mH and C = 5 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 99.9, C = 5 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(99.9e-3 * 5e-6)) | Answer: 225.2 Hz

question: A capacitor of 4.6 uF is charged to 255 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 4.6, V = 255 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*4.6e-6*(255)^2 | Answer: 149.6 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 260 V with 220 primary turns and 100 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 260, N1 = 220, N2 = 100 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 260 * 100/220 | Answer: 118.2 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 340 V and draws an armature current of 28 A. If the armature resistance is 0.95 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 340, Ia = 28, Ra = 0.95 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 340 - 28*0.95 | Answer: 313.4 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 170 A at 415 V (line) with a power factor of 0.83. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 170, VL = 415, pf = 0.83 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*415*170*0.83 / 1000 | Answer: 101.4 kW

question: A load has real power 15 kW and apparent power 50 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 15, S = 50 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 15 / 50 | Answer: 0.3

question: A machine delivers 60 kW output while drawing 77 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 60, Pi = 77 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 60/77 * 100 | Answer: 77.92 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 26 V across R1 = 24 ohm and R2 = 20 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 26, R1 = 24, R2 = 20 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 26*20 / (24+20) | Answer: 11.82 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 150 kohm and Rin = 33 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 150, Rin = 33 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 150 / 33 | Answer: 4.545

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 100 kohm and Rg = 38 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 100, Rg = 38 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 100/38 | Answer: 3.632

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 8504. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 8504 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(8504) | Answer: 39.3 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 7.8 m carries a central point load of 60 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7.8, W = 60 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 60*7.8 / 4 | Answer: 117 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 3.6 m carries a UDL of 10 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.6, w = 10 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 10*(3.6)^2 / 8 | Answer: 16.2 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 3.9 m carries a point load 20 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.9, W = 20 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 20*3.9 | Answer: 78 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 6 m carries a UDL of 40 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6, w = 40 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 40*(6)^2 / 2 | Answer: 720 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.3 m carries a point load 20 kN at distance 2.4 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 6.3, a = 2.4, W = 20 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 20*(6.3 - 2.4) / 6.3 | Answer: 12.38 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 8 m) carries a central point load 35 kN. With E = 30 GPa and I = 390e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=35000 N, L=8000.0 mm, E=30000 MPa, I=390e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 31.91 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 8.7 m carries a UDL of 9 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 8.7, w = 9 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 9*(8.7)^2 / 12 | Answer: 56.77 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 580 mm, clear cover 45 mm and main bars of diameter 16 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 580, c = 45, dia = 16 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 580 - 45 - 16/2 | Answer: 527 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 12.8 m^2 carrying a factored load of 10.2 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 12.8, w = 10.2 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 10.2 * 12.8 | Answer: 130.6 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 4.2 m, unit weight 20 kN/m^3, phi = 38 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 1.5e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.6, area = 6.2e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 1.5, i = 0.6, A = 6.2 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (1.5e-4)*0.6*(6.2e-3) | Answer: 558 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 0.8 m, bed slope 0.009 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.014. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 2.2 m under a head of 0.6 m. Taking Cd = 0.6 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 4.3 m wide carries a discharge of 15.6 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 570 m and design speed 75 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 570, V = 75 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (75)^2 / (127*570) | Answer: 0.0777
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: A tank of volume 700 m^3 treats a flow of 145 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 700, Q = 145 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 700 / 145 | Answer: 4.828 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 340 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.12 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 3 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 340, k = 0.12, t = 3 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 340*(1 - e^(-0.12*3)) | Answer: 102.8 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.44, rainfall intensity 105 mm/h over a catchment of 54.7 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.44, i = 105, A = 54.7 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.44*105*54.7 / 360 | Answer: 7.02 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.05 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 800 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.05, M = 800 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 800*(30+0.05)/30 | Answer: 801.3 m

question: Convert the decimal number 3828 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 3828 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: EF4 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 11001110 and 00111110.
solution: XOR: 11110000 | Count of 1s = 4 | Answer: 4
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 140 megabits is sent over a link of 48 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 140, B = 48 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 140 / 48 | Answer: 2.917 s

question: A link has bandwidth 21 Mbps and round-trip time 110 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 21, R = 110 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 21e6 * 110e-3 bits = 2310 kb | Answer: 2310 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.89, cache access time 8 ns and main-memory access time 160 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.89, tc = 8, tm = 160 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.89*8 + (1 - 0.89)*160 | Answer: 24.72 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 935637 elements?
solution: Given: n = 935637 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(935637)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.019, memory access time 150 ns and page-fault service time 6 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 6 ms = 6000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.019)*150 + 0.019*6000000.0 ns | Answer: 114.1 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 0.8 m^3 at 380 kPa and 470 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 0.8, P = 380, Tk = 470 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (380e3)*0.8 / (8.314*470) | Answer: 77.8 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.33 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 12 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.33, t = 12 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.33*12) | Answer: 0.9809

question: For a reaction with A = 5e10 /s and activation energy 75 kJ/mol at 350 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 5, Ea = 75, Tk = 350 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 5e10 * exp(-75e3 / (8.314*350)) | Answer: 0.3202 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.92 and bottoms xW = 0.07, with relative volatility alpha = 2. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.92, xw = 0.07, al = 2 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.92/0.08)(0.93/0.07)] / ln(2) | Answer: 7.255 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.89 and x = 0.48. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.89, x = 0.48 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.89/0.11) / (0.48/0.52) | Answer: 8.765

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.78 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 100 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.78, Psat = 100 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.78 * 100 | Answer: 78 kPa

question: A stream of 4.7 kg/s with specific heat 2.2 kJ/kg-K is heated through 85 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 4.7, cp = 2.2, dT = 85 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 4.7*2.2*85 | Answer: 878.9 kW

question: A reactor of volume 4.6 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 0.8 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 4.6, Q = 0.8 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 4.6 / 0.8 | Answer: 5.75 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 4.1e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 4 mm with a concentration difference of 150 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 4.1, L = 4, dC = 150 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (4.1e-9)*150 / (4e-3) | Answer: 153.7 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 8.8 min and steady-state gain 2.7. For a step input of magnitude 9, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 8.8, K = 2.7, M = 9 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 2.7 * 9 | Answer: 24.3 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 40 m^2 flies at 180 m/s (air density 1 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.7. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 40, V = 180, rho = 1, CL = 0.7 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1*(180)^2*40*0.7 / 1000 | Answer: 453.6 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 85 m^2 flies at 120 m/s (density 0.4 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.03. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 85, V = 120, rho = 0.4, CD = 0.03 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.4*(120)^2*85*0.03 / 1000 | Answer: 7.344 kN

question: A specimen under stress 100 MPa shows an elastic strain of 2.3e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 100, eps = 2.3 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 100 / (2.3e-3) MPa = 43.48 GPa | Answer: 43.48 GPa

question: A block of mass 35 kg has a volume of 5.1e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 35, V = 5.1 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 35 / (5.1e-3) | Answer: 6863 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 2300 mm is heated through 50 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 17e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 2300, dT = 50, al = 17 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 2300*17e-6*50 | Answer: 1.955 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 55 ohm, R2 = 95 ohm and R3 = 255 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 55, R2 = 95, R3 = 255 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 95*255 / 55 | Answer: 440.5 ohm

question: A measurement reads 9.87 when the true value is 10. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.87, true = 10 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.87 - 10| / 10 * 100 | Answer: 1.3 %

question: Annual demand is 14500 units, ordering cost 120 per order and holding cost 27 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 14500, S = 120, H = 27 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*14500*120 / 27) | Answer: 359 units

question: An asset costs 110000 with salvage value 22000 after 6 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 110000, Sv = 22000, n = 6 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (110000 - 22000) / 6 | Answer: 14667 per year

question: A product sells for 120 per unit with variable cost 40 per unit and fixed costs 45000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 120, V = 40, F = 45000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 45000 / (120 - 40) | Answer: 562.5 units

question: Find the present worth of 145000 received 5 years from now at an interest rate of 5% per year.
solution: Given: F = 145000, n = 5, i = 5 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 145000 / (1 + 0.05)^5 | Answer: 113611 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.96, 0.94 and 0.91 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.96, r2 = 0.94, r3 = 0.91 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.96*0.94*0.91 | Answer: 0.8212

question: A process produces 47 defective items in a batch of 18500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 47, N = 18500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 47/18500 * 1e6 | Answer: 2541 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -2x^3 + 8x^2 - 7x + 5 evaluated at x = 5.
For f(x) = -x^3 + 2x^2 + 6, find f''(x) at x = 0.
Evaluate the definite integral of (-5x^2 - 4x - 7) dx from x = 1 to x = 3.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = -5x^3/3 + -4x^2/2 + -7x | Evaluate F(3) - F(1) | Answer: -73.33
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 4x^2 - 9x + 3 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[-1, -5], [4, -3]].
solution: Given: a = -1, b = -5, c = 4, d = -3 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (-1)(-3) - (-5)(4) | Answer: 23

question: Find the determinant of [[3, 2, -3], [5, 3, 1], [-5, 4, 1]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: -128

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[-3, 2], [-3, 4]].
solution: Trace tr = 1, Determinant = -6 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 3

question: Solve for x: -5x + 3y = -12 and 2x + -5y = 6.
solution: Determinant = -5*-5 - 3*2 = 19 | x = (e d - b f) / det = 2.211 | Answer: x = 2.211
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 28, 41, 28, 9, 53.
solution: Sum = 159 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 31.8 | Answer: 31.8

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 14, 5, 13, 37, 25.
solution: Mean = 18.8 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 12.42

question: Find the slope of the line through (1, -2) and (-3, -2).
solution: Given: x1 = 1, y1 = -2, x2 = -3, y2 = -2 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (-2 - -2) / (-3 - 1) | Answer: 0

question: Find the distance between the points (-1, 8) and (-8, -4).
solution: Given: x1 = -1, y1 = 8, x2 = -8, y2 = -4 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-7)^2 + (-12)^2) | Answer: 13.89 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (-1,7), (-2,1), (-2,6).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 2.5 sq units

question: Find the 40th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -14 and common difference -2.
solution: Given: a = -14, d = -2, n = 40 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -14 + (40 - 1)*-2 | Answer: -92

question: Find the sum of the first 19 terms of an AP with first term 5 and common difference -2.
solution: Given: a = 5, d = -2, n = 19 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 19/2 [2*5 + (19-1)*-2] | Answer: -247

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 22000 at 6.8% per annum for 1 years.
solution: Given: P = 22000, R = 6.8, Tt = 1 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 22000 * 6.8 * 1 / 100 | Answer: 1496 currency units

question: Find the amount when 20000 is invested at 8.8% per annum compounded annually for 3 years.
solution: Given: P = 20000, R = 8.8, Tt = 3 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 20000 * (1 + 8.8/100)^3 | Answer: 25758 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (0, -5, -3) and (8, 8, 4).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (2, -5, -3) and (-5, 6, 1).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 22.52

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (-3, 3, 3) and (0, 6, -1).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 61.67 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number 6 + 11i.
solution: Given: a = 6, b = 11 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((6)^2 + (11)^2) | Answer: 12.53

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number 10 + -7i.
solution: Given: a = 10, b = -7 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(-7, 10) | Answer: -34.99 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -5x^3 - 7x^2 - 3x + 8 at x = -1.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-168 with initial guess x0=5, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.9 and ordinates 5, 8, 13, 20, 5, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 577 and 100.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 577 and 100 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 11 and 56.
solution: Given: a = 11, b = 56 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 11*56 / 1 | Answer: 616
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 48 mm carries an axial tensile load of 49 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 15 mm and length 2800 mm carries an axial load of 70 kN. Take E = 210 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 45 mm transmits a torque of 2250 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 45, Tt = 2250 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(2250*1000) / (pi*(45)^3) | Answer: 125.8 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 35 mm and length 800 mm carries a torque of 1850 N-m. With G = 45 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (35)^4 / 32 = 147324 mm^4 | theta = (1850*1000)(800) / (45000 * 147324) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 12.79 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 132 mm wide and 110 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 132, h = 110 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 132*(110)^2 / 6 | Answer: 266200 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (101 mm x 240 mm) carries a bending moment of 26 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (79 mm x 120 mm) has effective length 2900 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 840 MPa is designed for a working stress of 240 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 840, sw = 240 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 840 / 240 | Answer: 3.5

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 750 mm and wall thickness 11 mm carries an internal pressure of 2.6 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 750, t = 11, P = 2.6 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 2.6*750 / (2*11) | Answer: 88.64 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 800 K and 280 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 800, Tc = 280 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 280/800) * 100 | Answer: 65 %

question: A refrigerator works between 250 K (cold) and 322 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 250, Th = 322 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 250 / (322 - 250) | Answer: 3.472

question: A heat pump operates between 285 K and 316 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 285, Th = 316 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 316 / (316 - 285) | Answer: 10.19

question: 6.4 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 75 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 6.4, dT = 75 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 6.4 * 0.718 * 75 | Answer: 344.6 kJ

question: 1.5 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 140 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1.5, dT = 140 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 1.5 * 1.005 * 140 | Answer: 211 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 2.6 m^3 at 360 K with mass 3.1 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 2.6, Tk = 360, m = 3.1 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 3.1*0.287*360 / 2.6 | Answer: 123.2 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 2.8 kg of air expands isothermally at 380 K from volume V1 to 4*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.8, Tk = 380, ratio = 4 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 2.8*0.287*380*ln(4) | Answer: 423.3 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 1.9 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.14 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 1.9, D = 0.14 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*1.9*0.14 / 0.001 | Answer: 266000

question: Water flows at 3.3 m/s through a pipe of diameter 50 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 5.4 m. Taking Cv = 0.99, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 5.4, cv = 0.99 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.99*sqrt(2*9.81*5.4) | Answer: 10.19 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 190 mm) water flows at 2.3 m/s. It contracts to diameter 50 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 190, d2 = 50, V1 = 2.3 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 2.3*(190/50)^2 | Answer: 33.21 m/s

question: Water flows at 1.2 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.13 m and length 440 m. With friction factor f = 0.022, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 26 teeth drives a gear of 103 teeth. If the pinion runs at 400 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 26, z2 = 103, N1 = 400 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 400*26 / 103 | Answer: 101 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 290 mm rotates at 600 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 290, N = 600 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.29)*600 / 60 | Answer: 9.111 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 45.6 kW at 900 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 45.6, N = 900 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(45.6*1000) / (2*pi*900) | Answer: 483.8 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 5.2 kg rotates at radius 0.6 m at 450 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 16300 N/m and mass 16.2 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 16300, m = 16.2 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(16300/16.2) | Answer: 5.048 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 4.7 m^2 and thickness 0.35 m has conductivity k = 27.8 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 75 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 4.7, L = 0.35, k = 27.8, dT = 75 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 27.8*4.7*75 / 0.35 | Answer: 27999 W

question: A surface of area 6 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 95 W/m^2-K to surroundings 140 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 6, h = 95, dT = 140 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 95*6*140 | Answer: 79800 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 140 m/min, feed = 0.39 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2.3 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 140, f = 0.39, d = 2.3 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*140*0.39*2.3 | Answer: 125580 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 470 mm is turned at 550 rpm with a feed of 0.28 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 470, N = 550, f = 0.28 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 470 / (0.28*550) | Answer: 3.052 min

question: A resistor of 158 ohm carries a current of 6.7 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 158, I = 6.7 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 6.7 * 158 | Answer: 1059 V

question: Three resistors 49 ohm, 39 ohm and 56 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 49, R2 = 39, R3 = 56 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 49 + 39 + 56 | Answer: 144 ohm

question: Two resistors 92 ohm and 15 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 92, R2 = 15 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 92*15 / (92+15) | Answer: 12.9 ohm

question: A device draws 13.2 A at 195 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 195, I = 13.2 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 195 * 13.2 | Answer: 2574 W

question: A current of 8 A flows through a 5 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 8, R = 5 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (8)^2 * 5 | Answer: 320 W

question: Two capacitors 48 uF and 20.3 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 48, C2 = 20.3 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 48*20.3 / (48+20.3) | Answer: 14.27 uF

question: A resistor 70 kohm and capacitor 7.2 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 70, C = 7.2 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (70k)(7.2u) = 504 ms | Answer: 504 ms

question: An inductor 65.7 mH is in series with 178 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 65.7, R = 178 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (65.7e-3) / 178 | Answer: 0.3691 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 168.4 mH inductor at 150 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 168.4, f = 150 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (150)(168.4e-3) | Answer: 158.7 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 44.7 uF capacitor at 250 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 44.7, f = 250 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (250)(44.7e-6)) | Answer: 14.24 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 29 ohm, XL = 26 ohm and XC = 35 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 29, XL = 26, XC = 35 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(29^2 + (26 - 35)^2) | Answer: 30.36 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 82.8 mH and C = 8.9 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 82.8, C = 8.9 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(82.8e-3 * 8.9e-6)) | Answer: 185.4 Hz

question: A capacitor of 27.4 uF is charged to 275 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 27.4, V = 275 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*27.4e-6*(275)^2 | Answer: 1036 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 290 V with 940 primary turns and 40 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 290, N1 = 940, N2 = 40 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 290 * 40/940 | Answer: 12.34 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 110 V and draws an armature current of 14 A. If the armature resistance is 0.48 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 110, Ia = 14, Ra = 0.48 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 110 - 14*0.48 | Answer: 103.3 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 35 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.8. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 35, VL = 400, pf = 0.8 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*400*35*0.8 / 1000 | Answer: 19.4 kW

question: A load has real power 25 kW and apparent power 150 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 25, S = 150 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 25 / 150 | Answer: 0.1667

question: A machine delivers 20 kW output while drawing 67 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 20, Pi = 67 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 20/67 * 100 | Answer: 29.85 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 21 V across R1 = 50 ohm and R2 = 6 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 21, R1 = 50, R2 = 6 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 21*6 / (50+6) | Answer: 2.25 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 100 kohm and Rin = 37 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 100, Rin = 37 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 100 / 37 | Answer: 2.703

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 10 kohm and Rg = 33 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 10, Rg = 33 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 10/33 | Answer: 1.303

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 6567. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 6567 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(6567) | Answer: 38.17 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.4 m carries a central point load of 90 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6.4, W = 90 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 90*6.4 / 4 | Answer: 144 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 7.5 m carries a UDL of 30 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7.5, w = 30 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 30*(7.5)^2 / 8 | Answer: 210.9 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 5.7 m carries a point load 40 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.7, W = 40 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 40*5.7 | Answer: 228 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 3 m carries a UDL of 24 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3, w = 24 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 24*(3)^2 / 2 | Answer: 108 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.7 m carries a point load 100 kN at distance 3.9 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 4.7, a = 3.9, W = 100 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 100*(4.7 - 3.9) / 4.7 | Answer: 17.02 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 7 m) carries a central point load 40 kN. With E = 30 GPa and I = 80e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=40000 N, L=7000.0 mm, E=30000 MPa, I=80e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 119.1 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 4.4 m carries a UDL of 24 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.4, w = 24 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 24*(4.4)^2 / 12 | Answer: 38.72 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 310 mm, clear cover 40 mm and main bars of diameter 16 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 310, c = 40, dia = 16 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 310 - 40 - 16/2 | Answer: 262 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 32.4 m^2 carrying a factored load of 8.5 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 32.4, w = 8.5 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 8.5 * 32.4 | Answer: 275.4 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 5.6 m, unit weight 18 kN/m^3, phi = 33 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 6.1e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1, area = 7.7e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 6.1, i = 1, A = 7.7 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (6.1e-4)*1*(7.7e-3) | Answer: 4697 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 0.8 m, bed slope 0.004 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.019. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 3.5 m under a head of 0.9 m. Taking Cd = 0.63 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 5 m wide carries a discharge of 24.3 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 230 m and design speed 100 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 230, V = 100 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (100)^2 / (127*230) | Answer: 0.3423
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: A tank of volume 680 m^3 treats a flow of 155 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 680, Q = 155 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 680 / 155 | Answer: 4.387 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 270 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.22 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 6 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 270, k = 0.22, t = 6 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 270*(1 - e^(-0.22*6)) | Answer: 197.9 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.4, rainfall intensity 40 mm/h over a catchment of 54.5 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.4, i = 40, A = 54.5 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.4*40*54.5 / 360 | Answer: 2.422 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.02 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 320 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.02, M = 320 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 320*(20+0.02)/20 | Answer: 320.3 m

question: Convert the decimal number 809 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 809 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 329 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 01001001 and 11000100.
solution: XOR: 10001101 | Count of 1s = 4 | Answer: 4
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 970 megabits is sent over a link of 96 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 970, B = 96 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 970 / 96 | Answer: 10.1 s

question: A link has bandwidth 40 Mbps and round-trip time 150 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 40, R = 150 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 40e6 * 150e-3 bits = 6000 kb | Answer: 6000 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.95, cache access time 7 ns and main-memory access time 130 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.95, tc = 7, tm = 130 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.95*7 + (1 - 0.95)*130 | Answer: 13.15 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 760400 elements?
solution: Given: n = 760400 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(760400)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.014, memory access time 120 ns and page-fault service time 7 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 7 ms = 7000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.014)*120 + 0.014*7000000.0 ns | Answer: 98.12 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 1.6 m^3 at 170 kPa and 600 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 1.6, P = 170, Tk = 600 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (170e3)*1.6 / (8.314*600) | Answer: 54.53 mol

question: For a reaction with A = 4e10 /s and activation energy 65 kJ/mol at 340 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 4, Ea = 65, Tk = 340 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 4e10 * exp(-65e3 / (8.314*340)) | Answer: 4.127 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.95 and bottoms xW = 0.04, with relative volatility alpha = 2.4. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.95, xw = 0.04, al = 2.4 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.95/0.05)(0.96/0.04)] / ln(2.4) | Answer: 6.993 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.65 and x = 0.49. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.65, x = 0.49 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.65/0.35) / (0.49/0.51) | Answer: 1.933

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.74 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 90 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.74, Psat = 90 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.74 * 90 | Answer: 66.6 kPa

question: A stream of 9.9 kg/s with specific heat 3.5 kJ/kg-K is heated through 100 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 9.9, cp = 3.5, dT = 100 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 9.9*3.5*100 | Answer: 3465 kW

question: A reactor of volume 1 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 1.9 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 1, Q = 1.9 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 1 / 1.9 | Answer: 0.5263 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 4.9e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 5 mm with a concentration difference of 50 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 4.9, L = 5, dC = 50 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (4.9e-9)*50 / (5e-3) | Answer: 49 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 5.1 min and steady-state gain 2.3. For a step input of magnitude 3, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 5.1, K = 2.3, M = 3 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 2.3 * 3 | Answer: 6.9 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 110 m^2 flies at 170 m/s (air density 0.4 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.9. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 110, V = 170, rho = 0.4, CL = 0.9 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.4*(170)^2*110*0.9 / 1000 | Answer: 572.2 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 90 m^2 flies at 230 m/s (density 0.7 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.07. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 90, V = 230, rho = 0.7, CD = 0.07 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.7*(230)^2*90*0.07 / 1000 | Answer: 116.6 kN

question: A specimen under stress 150 MPa shows an elastic strain of 1.7e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 150, eps = 1.7 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 150 / (1.7e-3) MPa = 88.24 GPa | Answer: 88.24 GPa

question: A block of mass 30 kg has a volume of 3.8e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 30, V = 3.8 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 30 / (3.8e-3) | Answer: 7895 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 2700 mm is heated through 25 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 17e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 2700, dT = 25, al = 17 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 2700*17e-6*25 | Answer: 1.147 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 180 ohm, R2 = 120 ohm and R3 = 305 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 180, R2 = 120, R3 = 305 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 120*305 / 180 | Answer: 203.3 ohm

question: A measurement reads 10.85 when the true value is 10. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10.85, true = 10 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10.85 - 10| / 10 * 100 | Answer: 8.5 %

question: Annual demand is 1500 units, ordering cost 150 per order and holding cost 32 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 1500, S = 150, H = 32 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*1500*150 / 32) | Answer: 118.6 units

question: An asset costs 430000 with salvage value 24000 after 8 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 430000, Sv = 24000, n = 8 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (430000 - 24000) / 8 | Answer: 50750 per year

question: A product sells for 160 per unit with variable cost 70 per unit and fixed costs 185000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 160, V = 70, F = 185000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 185000 / (160 - 70) | Answer: 2056 units

question: Find the present worth of 75000 received 9 years from now at an interest rate of 6% per year.
solution: Given: F = 75000, n = 9, i = 6 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 75000 / (1 + 0.06)^9 | Answer: 44392 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.99, 0.93 and 0.91 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.99, r2 = 0.93, r3 = 0.91 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.99*0.93*0.91 | Answer: 0.8378

question: A process produces 12 defective items in a batch of 13500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 12, N = 13500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 12/13500 * 1e6 | Answer: 888.9 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = x^3 - 5x^2 + 2x + 4 evaluated at x = 0.
For f(x) = -5x^3 + 8x^2 - x - 2, find f''(x) at x = 1.
Evaluate the definite integral of (x^2 - x) dx from x = -1 to x = 3.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = 1x^3/3 + -1x^2/2 + 0x | Evaluate F(3) - F(-1) | Answer: 5.333
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 4x^2 - 6x - 12 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[-4, 3], [-7, -4]].
solution: Given: a = -4, b = 3, c = -7, d = -4 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (-4)(-4) - (3)(-7) | Answer: 37

question: Find the determinant of [[4, -2, 4], [4, 4, -6], [-4, 1, 2]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: 104

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[-2, 5], [1, 3]].
solution: Trace tr = 1, Determinant = -11 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 3.854

question: Solve for x: 1x + -2y = 4 and 0x + -1y = 11.
solution: Determinant = 1*-1 - -2*0 = -1 | x = (e d - b f) / det = -18 | Answer: x = -18
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 76, 61, 10, 17, 74.
solution: Sum = 238 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 47.6 | Answer: 47.6

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 10, 33, 5, 21, 19.
solution: Mean = 17.6 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 10.81

question: Find the slope of the line through (-1, -2) and (4, 7).
solution: Given: x1 = -1, y1 = -2, x2 = 4, y2 = 7 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (7 - -2) / (4 - -1) | Answer: 1.8

question: Find the distance between the points (7, 3) and (8, 4).
solution: Given: x1 = 7, y1 = 3, x2 = 8, y2 = 4 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((1)^2 + (1)^2) | Answer: 1.414 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (-3,-7), (8,7), (-7,-5).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 39 sq units

question: Find the 16th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -10 and common difference 3.
solution: Given: a = -10, d = 3, n = 16 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -10 + (16 - 1)*3 | Answer: 35

question: Find the amount when 31500 is invested at 9.1% per annum compounded annually for 2 years.
solution: Given: P = 31500, R = 9.1, Tt = 2 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 31500 * (1 + 9.1/100)^2 | Answer: 37494 currency units

question: Find the modulus of the complex number -1 + -2i.
solution: Given: a = -1, b = -2 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((-1)^2 + (-2)^2) | Answer: 2.236

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number 9 + -12i.
solution: Given: a = 9, b = -12 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(-12, 9) | Answer: -53.13 degrees

question: A circular rod of diameter 26 mm carries an axial tensile load of 108 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 27 mm and length 1400 mm carries an axial load of 15 kN. Take E = 210 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 26 mm transmits a torque of 2500 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.

question: A shaft of diameter 41 mm and length 500 mm carries a torque of 1750 N-m. With G = 77 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (41)^4 / 32 = 277418 mm^4 | theta = (1750*1000)(500) / (77000 * 277418) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 2.347 degrees

question: A rectangular beam section is 85 mm wide and 210 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 85, h = 210 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 85*(210)^2 / 6 | Answer: 624750 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (100 mm x 130 mm) carries a bending moment of 22 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (78 mm x 160 mm) has effective length 3000 mm and E = 200 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 310 MPa is designed for a working stress of 220 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 310, sw = 220 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 310 / 220 | Answer: 1.409

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 400 mm and wall thickness 17 mm carries an internal pressure of 2.7 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 400, t = 17, P = 2.7 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 2.7*400 / (2*17) | Answer: 31.76 MPa

question: A refrigerator works between 252 K (cold) and 304 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 252, Th = 304 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 252 / (304 - 252) | Answer: 4.846

question: 5.1 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 40 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 5.1, dT = 40 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 5.1 * 0.718 * 40 | Answer: 146.5 kJ

question: 1.3 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 165 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1.3, dT = 165 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 1.3 * 1.005 * 165 | Answer: 215.6 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 1.1 m^3 at 360 K with mass 4 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 1.1, Tk = 360, m = 4 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 4*0.287*360 / 1.1 | Answer: 375.7 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 2.1 kg of air expands isothermally at 400 K from volume V1 to 5*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.1, Tk = 400, ratio = 5 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 2.1*0.287*400*ln(5) | Answer: 388 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 3.3 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.18 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 3.3, D = 0.18 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*3.3*0.18 / 0.001 | Answer: 594000

question: Water flows at 3.2 m/s through a pipe of diameter 280 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 7.7 m. Taking Cv = 0.99, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 7.7, cv = 0.99 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.99*sqrt(2*9.81*7.7) | Answer: 12.17 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 150 mm) water flows at 2.4 m/s. It contracts to diameter 140 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
Water flows at 1.6 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.44 m and length 300 m. With friction factor f = 0.036, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 16 teeth drives a gear of 90 teeth. If the pinion runs at 850 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 16, z2 = 90, N1 = 850 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 850*16 / 90 | Answer: 151.1 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 170 mm rotates at 750 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 170, N = 750 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.17)*750 / 60 | Answer: 6.676 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 6.1 kW at 1350 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 6.1, N = 1350 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(6.1*1000) / (2*pi*1350) | Answer: 43.15 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 6.8 kg rotates at radius 0.5 m at 900 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 18700 N/m and mass 9 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 18700, m = 9 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(18700/9) | Answer: 7.255 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 7.9 m^2 and thickness 0.12 m has conductivity k = 36.6 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 190 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 7.9, L = 0.12, k = 36.6, dT = 190 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 36.6*7.9*190 / 0.12 | Answer: 457805 W

question: A surface of area 1.1 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 170 W/m^2-K to surroundings 40 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 1.1, h = 170, dT = 40 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 170*1.1*40 | Answer: 7480 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 200 m/min, feed = 0.47 mm/rev, depth of cut = 1.4 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 200, f = 0.47, d = 1.4 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*200*0.47*1.4 | Answer: 131600 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 150 mm is turned at 850 rpm with a feed of 0.31 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 150, N = 850, f = 0.31 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 150 / (0.31*850) | Answer: 0.5693 min

question: A resistor of 130 ohm carries a current of 9.3 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 130, I = 9.3 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 9.3 * 130 | Answer: 1209 V

question: Three resistors 88 ohm, 90 ohm and 5 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 88, R2 = 90, R3 = 5 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 88 + 90 + 5 | Answer: 183 ohm

question: Two resistors 48 ohm and 43 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 48, R2 = 43 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 48*43 / (48+43) | Answer: 22.68 ohm

question: A device draws 10.2 A at 75 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 75, I = 10.2 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 75 * 10.2 | Answer: 765 W

question: A current of 5.4 A flows through a 3 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 5.4, R = 3 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (5.4)^2 * 3 | Answer: 87.48 W

question: Two capacitors 3.2 uF and 4.4 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 3.2, C2 = 4.4 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 3.2*4.4 / (3.2+4.4) | Answer: 1.853 uF

question: A resistor 2 kohm and capacitor 6.8 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 2, C = 6.8 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (2k)(6.8u) = 13.6 ms | Answer: 13.6 ms

question: An inductor 211.3 mH is in series with 40 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 211.3, R = 40 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (211.3e-3) / 40 | Answer: 5.283 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 172 mH inductor at 770 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 172, f = 770 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (770)(172e-3) | Answer: 832.1 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 3.4 uF capacitor at 740 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 3.4, f = 740 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (740)(3.4e-6)) | Answer: 63.26 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 16 ohm, XL = 26 ohm and XC = 130 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 16, XL = 26, XC = 130 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(16^2 + (26 - 130)^2) | Answer: 105.2 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 45.7 mH and C = 7.7 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 45.7, C = 7.7 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(45.7e-3 * 7.7e-6)) | Answer: 268.3 Hz

question: A capacitor of 27.7 uF is charged to 215 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 27.7, V = 215 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*27.7e-6*(215)^2 | Answer: 640.2 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 330 V with 980 primary turns and 390 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 330, N1 = 980, N2 = 390 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 330 * 390/980 | Answer: 131.3 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 240 V and draws an armature current of 29 A. If the armature resistance is 0.86 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 240, Ia = 29, Ra = 0.86 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 240 - 29*0.86 | Answer: 215.1 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 110 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.79. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 110, VL = 400, pf = 0.79 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*400*110*0.79 / 1000 | Answer: 60.21 kW

question: A load has real power 75 kW and apparent power 215 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 75, S = 215 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 75 / 215 | Answer: 0.3488

question: A machine delivers 70 kW output while drawing 152 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 70, Pi = 152 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 70/152 * 100 | Answer: 46.05 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 26 V across R1 = 9 ohm and R2 = 21 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 26, R1 = 9, R2 = 21 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 26*21 / (9+21) | Answer: 18.2 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 80 kohm and Rin = 14 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 80, Rin = 14 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 80 / 14 | Answer: 5.714

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 130 kohm and Rg = 36 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 130, Rg = 36 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 130/36 | Answer: 4.611

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 3859. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 3859 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(3859) | Answer: 35.86 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.1 m carries a central point load of 110 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 9.1, W = 110 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 110*9.1 / 4 | Answer: 250.2 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.4 m carries a UDL of 45 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.4, w = 45 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 45*(4.4)^2 / 8 | Answer: 108.9 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 2.4 m carries a point load 75 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 2.4, W = 75 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 75*2.4 | Answer: 180 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 1.3 m carries a UDL of 28 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 1.3, w = 28 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 28*(1.3)^2 / 2 | Answer: 23.66 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 8.8 m carries a point load 15 kN at distance 1.4 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 8.8, a = 1.4, W = 15 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 15*(8.8 - 1.4) / 8.8 | Answer: 12.61 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 5.4 m) carries a central point load 20 kN. With E = 200 GPa and I = 460e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=20000 N, L=5400.0 mm, E=200000 MPa, I=460e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 0.7132 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 7.4 m carries a UDL of 6 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7.4, w = 6 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 6*(7.4)^2 / 12 | Answer: 27.38 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 690 mm, clear cover 30 mm and main bars of diameter 20 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 690, c = 30, dia = 20 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 690 - 30 - 20/2 | Answer: 650 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 27.9 m^2 carrying a factored load of 19.5 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 27.9, w = 19.5 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 19.5 * 27.9 | Answer: 544 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 6.7 m, unit weight 17 kN/m^3, phi = 36 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 10.7 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 18 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 10.7, g = 18 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (18 - 9.81)*10.7 | Answer: 87.63 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 2.9e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1.1, area = 1.4e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 2.9, i = 1.1, A = 1.4 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (2.9e-4)*1.1*(1.4e-3) | Answer: 446.6 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 0.9 m, bed slope 0.008 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.017. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 1.4 m under a head of 0.7 m. Taking Cd = 0.61 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 5 m wide carries a discharge of 27.3 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 230 m and design speed 65 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 230, V = 65 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (65)^2 / (127*230) | Answer: 0.1446
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: A tank of volume 50 m^3 treats a flow of 160 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 50, Q = 160 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 50 / 160 | Answer: 0.3125 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 240 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.31 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 6 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 240, k = 0.31, t = 6 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 240*(1 - e^(-0.31*6)) | Answer: 202.6 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.35, rainfall intensity 100 mm/h over a catchment of 21.6 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.35, i = 100, A = 21.6 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.35*100*21.6 / 360 | Answer: 2.1 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.08 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 140 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.08, M = 140 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 140*(30+0.08)/30 | Answer: 140.4 m

question: Convert the decimal number 2987 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 2987 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: BAB (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 00110010 and 11011011.
solution: XOR: 11101001 | Count of 1s = 5 | Answer: 5
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 330 megabits is sent over a link of 76 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 330, B = 76 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 330 / 76 | Answer: 4.342 s

question: A link has bandwidth 48 Mbps and round-trip time 40 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 48, R = 40 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 48e6 * 40e-3 bits = 1920 kb | Answer: 1920 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.85, cache access time 6 ns and main-memory access time 140 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.85, tc = 6, tm = 140 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.85*6 + (1 - 0.85)*140 | Answer: 26.1 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 907851 elements?
solution: Given: n = 907851 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(907851)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.009, memory access time 160 ns and page-fault service time 9 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 9 ms = 9000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.009)*160 + 0.009*9000000.0 ns | Answer: 81.16 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 2.1 m^3 at 120 kPa and 390 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 2.1, P = 120, Tk = 390 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (120e3)*2.1 / (8.314*390) | Answer: 77.72 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.12 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 8 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.12, t = 8 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.12*8) | Answer: 0.6171

question: For a reaction with A = 5e10 /s and activation energy 85 kJ/mol at 340 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 5, Ea = 85, Tk = 340 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 5e10 * exp(-85e3 / (8.314*340)) | Answer: 0.004364 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.94 and bottoms xW = 0.07, with relative volatility alpha = 3.2. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.94, xw = 0.07, al = 3.2 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.94/0.06)(0.93/0.07)] / ln(3.2) | Answer: 4.589 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.64 and x = 0.26. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.64, x = 0.26 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.64/0.36) / (0.26/0.74) | Answer: 5.06

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.48 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 75 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.48, Psat = 75 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.48 * 75 | Answer: 36 kPa

question: A stream of 4 kg/s with specific heat 2.5 kJ/kg-K is heated through 120 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 4, cp = 2.5, dT = 120 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 4*2.5*120 | Answer: 1200 kW

question: A reactor of volume 1.9 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 0.6 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 1.9, Q = 0.6 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 1.9 / 0.6 | Answer: 3.167 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 7.6e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 3 mm with a concentration difference of 180 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 7.6, L = 3, dC = 180 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (7.6e-9)*180 / (3e-3) | Answer: 456 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 6.3 min and steady-state gain 1.4. For a step input of magnitude 3, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 6.3, K = 1.4, M = 3 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 1.4 * 3 | Answer: 4.2 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 90 m^2 flies at 220 m/s (air density 1.225 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 1.2. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 90, V = 220, rho = 1.225, CL = 1.2 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1.225*(220)^2*90*1.2 / 1000 | Answer: 3202 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 100 m^2 flies at 150 m/s (density 1.225 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.07. Find the drag force in kN.
A block of mass 9 kg has a volume of 3.7e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 9, V = 3.7 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 9 / (3.7e-3) | Answer: 2432 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 600 mm is heated through 85 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 23e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 600, dT = 85, al = 23 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 600*23e-6*85 | Answer: 1.173 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 55 ohm, R2 = 190 ohm and R3 = 360 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 55, R2 = 190, R3 = 360 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 190*360 / 55 | Answer: 1244 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 350 ohm and gauge factor 2 experiences a strain of 650e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 350, GF = 2, eps = 650 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 350*2*650e-6 | Answer: 455 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 10.07 when the true value is 100. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10.07, true = 100 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10.07 - 100| / 100 * 100 | Answer: 89.93 %

question: Annual demand is 46000 units, ordering cost 100 per order and holding cost 16 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 46000, S = 100, H = 16 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*46000*100 / 16) | Answer: 758.3 units

question: An asset costs 240000 with salvage value 38000 after 8 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 240000, Sv = 38000, n = 8 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (240000 - 38000) / 8 | Answer: 25250 per year

question: A product sells for 490 per unit with variable cost 170 per unit and fixed costs 175000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 490, V = 170, F = 175000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 175000 / (490 - 170) | Answer: 546.9 units

question: Find the present worth of 100000 received 10 years from now at an interest rate of 9% per year.
solution: Given: F = 100000, n = 10, i = 9 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 100000 / (1 + 0.09)^10 | Answer: 42241 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.94, 0.96 and 0.91 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.94, r2 = 0.96, r3 = 0.91 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.94*0.96*0.91 | Answer: 0.8212

question: A process produces 35 defective items in a batch of 13000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 35, N = 13000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 35/13000 * 1e6 | Answer: 2692 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = 5x^3 + 2x^2 + 2x - 6 evaluated at x = -5.
For f(x) = -2x^3 + x^2 + 4x + 9, find f''(x) at x = 0.
Evaluate the definite integral of (-5x^2 + 6x - 8) dx from x = 0 to x = 7.

question: Find the larger real root of 2x^2 + 6x - 1 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[7, 0], [0, 9]].
solution: Given: a = 7, b = 0, c = 0, d = 9 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (7)(9) - (0)(0) | Answer: 63

question: Find the determinant of [[-3, 2, 3], [-1, -4, 3], [-1, -4, 3]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: 0

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[0, 1], [1, 0]].
solution: Trace tr = 0, Determinant = -1 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 1

question: Solve for x: 3x + -5y = 10 and -1x + 5y = -10.
solution: Determinant = 3*5 - -5*-1 = 10 | x = (e d - b f) / det = 0 | Answer: x = 0
