formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 47 mm carries an axial tensile load of 65 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 14 mm and length 2500 mm carries an axial load of 51 kN. Take E = 70 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 65 mm transmits a torque of 2750 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 65, Tt = 2750 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(2750*1000) / (pi*(65)^3) | Answer: 51 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 51 mm and length 600 mm carries a torque of 300 N-m. With G = 80 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (51)^4 / 32 = 664172 mm^4 | theta = (300*1000)(600) / (80000 * 664172) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 0.1941 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 146 mm wide and 180 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 146, h = 180 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 146*(180)^2 / 6 | Answer: 788400 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (99 mm x 90 mm) carries a bending moment of 19 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (41 mm x 110 mm) has effective length 3200 mm and E = 200 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 590 MPa is designed for a working stress of 240 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 590, sw = 240 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 590 / 240 | Answer: 2.458

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1100 mm and wall thickness 15 mm carries an internal pressure of 1.3 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1100, t = 15, P = 1.3 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 1.3*1100 / (2*15) | Answer: 47.67 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 760 K and 340 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 760, Tc = 340 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 340/760) * 100 | Answer: 55.26 %

question: A refrigerator works between 275 K (cold) and 320 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 275, Th = 320 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 275 / (320 - 275) | Answer: 6.111

question: 1.2 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 140 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1.2, dT = 140 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 1.2 * 0.718 * 140 | Answer: 120.6 kJ

question: 4.9 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 180 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.9, dT = 180 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 4.9 * 1.005 * 180 | Answer: 886.4 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 1.8 m^3 at 590 K with mass 1.2 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 1.8, Tk = 590, m = 1.2 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 1.2*0.287*590 / 1.8 | Answer: 112.9 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 3 kg of air expands isothermally at 400 K from volume V1 to 2*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3, Tk = 400, ratio = 2 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 3*0.287*400*ln(2) | Answer: 238.7 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 4.1 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.21 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 4.1, D = 0.21 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*4.1*0.21 / 0.001 | Answer: 861000

question: Water flows at 3.8 m/s through a pipe of diameter 110 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 10 m. Taking Cv = 0.98, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 10, cv = 0.98 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.98*sqrt(2*9.81*10) | Answer: 13.73 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 250 mm) water flows at 1.3 m/s. It contracts to diameter 100 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
Water flows at 1.4 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.33 m and length 200 m. With friction factor f = 0.036, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 21 teeth drives a gear of 112 teeth. If the pinion runs at 500 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 21, z2 = 112, N1 = 500 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 500*21 / 112 | Answer: 93.75 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 230 mm rotates at 850 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 230, N = 850 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.23)*850 / 60 | Answer: 10.24 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 48.1 kW at 900 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 48.1, N = 900 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(48.1*1000) / (2*pi*900) | Answer: 510.4 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 3.3 kg rotates at radius 0.42 m at 1100 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 11300 N/m and mass 1.1 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 11300, m = 1.1 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(11300/1.1) | Answer: 16.13 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 3.1 m^2 and thickness 0.39 m has conductivity k = 46.5 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 70 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 3.1, L = 0.39, k = 46.5, dT = 70 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 46.5*3.1*70 / 0.39 | Answer: 25873 W

question: A surface of area 3.5 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 35 W/m^2-K to surroundings 20 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 3.5, h = 35, dT = 20 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 35*3.5*20 | Answer: 2450 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 190 m/min, feed = 0.19 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 190, f = 0.19, d = 2 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*190*0.19*2 | Answer: 72200 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 360 mm is turned at 450 rpm with a feed of 0.26 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 360, N = 450, f = 0.26 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 360 / (0.26*450) | Answer: 3.077 min

question: A resistor of 119 ohm carries a current of 4.2 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 119, I = 4.2 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 4.2 * 119 | Answer: 499.8 V

question: Three resistors 17 ohm, 69 ohm and 67 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 17, R2 = 69, R3 = 67 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 17 + 69 + 67 | Answer: 153 ohm

question: Two resistors 101 ohm and 36 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 101, R2 = 36 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 101*36 / (101+36) | Answer: 26.54 ohm

question: A device draws 1.8 A at 35 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 35, I = 1.8 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 35 * 1.8 | Answer: 63 W

question: A current of 10.7 A flows through a 132 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 10.7, R = 132 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (10.7)^2 * 132 | Answer: 15113 W

question: Two capacitors 44.2 uF and 13.5 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 44.2, C2 = 13.5 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 44.2*13.5 / (44.2+13.5) | Answer: 10.34 uF

question: A resistor 56 kohm and capacitor 15 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 56, C = 15 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (56k)(15u) = 840 ms | Answer: 840 ms

question: An inductor 213.1 mH is in series with 113 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 213.1, R = 113 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (213.1e-3) / 113 | Answer: 1.886 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 153 mH inductor at 520 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 153, f = 520 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (520)(153e-3) | Answer: 499.9 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 27.3 uF capacitor at 930 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 27.3, f = 930 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (930)(27.3e-6)) | Answer: 6.269 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 11 ohm, XL = 63 ohm and XC = 123 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 11, XL = 63, XC = 123 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(11^2 + (63 - 123)^2) | Answer: 61 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 83.7 mH and C = 1.1 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 83.7, C = 1.1 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(83.7e-3 * 1.1e-6)) | Answer: 524.5 Hz

question: A capacitor of 2.8 uF is charged to 195 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 2.8, V = 195 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*2.8e-6*(195)^2 | Answer: 53.23 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 120 V with 610 primary turns and 270 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 120, N1 = 610, N2 = 270 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 120 * 270/610 | Answer: 53.11 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 290 V and draws an armature current of 8 A. If the armature resistance is 1.26 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 290, Ia = 8, Ra = 1.26 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 290 - 8*1.26 | Answer: 279.9 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 55 A at 415 V (line) with a power factor of 0.86. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 55, VL = 415, pf = 0.86 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*415*55*0.86 / 1000 | Answer: 34 kW

question: A load has real power 65 kW and apparent power 85 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 65, S = 85 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 65 / 85 | Answer: 0.7647

question: A machine delivers 155 kW output while drawing 202 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 155, Pi = 202 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 155/202 * 100 | Answer: 76.73 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 9 V across R1 = 23 ohm and R2 = 20 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 9, R1 = 23, R2 = 20 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 9*20 / (23+20) | Answer: 4.186 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 200 kohm and Rin = 4 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 200, Rin = 4 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 200 / 4 | Answer: 50

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 140 kohm and Rg = 11 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 140, Rg = 11 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 140/11 | Answer: 13.73

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 4517. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 4517 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(4517) | Answer: 36.55 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.1 m carries a central point load of 105 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6.1, W = 105 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 105*6.1 / 4 | Answer: 160.1 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 3.8 m carries a UDL of 50 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.8, w = 50 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 50*(3.8)^2 / 8 | Answer: 90.25 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 4 m carries a point load 45 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4, W = 45 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 45*4 | Answer: 180 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 1.6 m carries a UDL of 24 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 1.6, w = 24 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 24*(1.6)^2 / 2 | Answer: 30.72 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.6 m carries a point load 95 kN at distance 3.3 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 6.6, a = 3.3, W = 95 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 95*(6.6 - 3.3) / 6.6 | Answer: 47.5 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 6.7 m) carries a central point load 60 kN. With E = 25 GPa and I = 120e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=60000 N, L=6700.0 mm, E=25000 MPa, I=120e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 125.3 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 4.3 m carries a UDL of 24 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.3, w = 24 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 24*(4.3)^2 / 12 | Answer: 36.98 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 520 mm, clear cover 30 mm and main bars of diameter 25 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 520, c = 30, dia = 25 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 520 - 30 - 25/2 | Answer: 477.5 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 20.9 m^2 carrying a factored load of 9.2 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 20.9, w = 9.2 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 9.2 * 20.9 | Answer: 192.3 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 6.2 m, unit weight 18 kN/m^3, phi = 34 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 7.4 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 21 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 7.4, g = 21 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (21 - 9.81)*7.4 | Answer: 82.81 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 5.3e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1.4, area = 5.4e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 5.3, i = 1.4, A = 5.4 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (5.3e-4)*1.4*(5.4e-3) | Answer: 4007 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.4 m, bed slope 0.007 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.026. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 1.6 m under a head of 1 m. Taking Cd = 0.61 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 2.2 m wide carries a discharge of 17 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 550 m and design speed 40 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 550, V = 40 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (40)^2 / (127*550) | Answer: 0.02291
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: A tank of volume 670 m^3 treats a flow of 100 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 670, Q = 100 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 670 / 100 | Answer: 6.7 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 310 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.12 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 5 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 310, k = 0.12, t = 5 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 310*(1 - e^(-0.12*5)) | Answer: 139.9 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.37, rainfall intensity 40 mm/h over a catchment of 38.7 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.37, i = 40, A = 38.7 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.37*40*38.7 / 360 | Answer: 1.591 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.07 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 680 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.07, M = 680 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 680*(30+0.07)/30 | Answer: 681.6 m

question: Convert the decimal number 3500 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 3500 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: DAC (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 10111111 and 01011001.
solution: XOR: 11100110 | Count of 1s = 5 | Answer: 5
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 860 megabits is sent over a link of 25 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 860, B = 25 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 860 / 25 | Answer: 34.4 s

question: A link has bandwidth 43 Mbps and round-trip time 200 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 43, R = 200 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 43e6 * 200e-3 bits = 8600 kb | Answer: 8600 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.85, cache access time 6 ns and main-memory access time 60 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.85, tc = 6, tm = 60 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.85*6 + (1 - 0.85)*60 | Answer: 14.1 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 969726 elements?
solution: Given: n = 969726 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(969726)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.007, memory access time 120 ns and page-fault service time 7 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 7 ms = 7000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.007)*120 + 0.007*7000000.0 ns | Answer: 49.12 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 2.6 m^3 at 260 kPa and 340 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 2.6, P = 260, Tk = 340 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (260e3)*2.6 / (8.314*340) | Answer: 239.1 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.13 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 13 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.13, t = 13 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.13*13) | Answer: 0.8155

question: For a reaction with A = 1e10 /s and activation energy 75 kJ/mol at 310 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 1, Ea = 75, Tk = 310 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 1e10 * exp(-75e3 / (8.314*310)) | Answer: 0.002302 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.96 and bottoms xW = 0.04, with relative volatility alpha = 2.8. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.96, xw = 0.04, al = 2.8 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.96/0.04)(0.96/0.04)] / ln(2.8) | Answer: 6.173 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.62 and x = 0.25. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.62, x = 0.25 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.62/0.38) / (0.25/0.75) | Answer: 4.895

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.33 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 110 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.33, Psat = 110 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.33 * 110 | Answer: 36.3 kPa

question: A stream of 6.5 kg/s with specific heat 2.2 kJ/kg-K is heated through 35 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 6.5, cp = 2.2, dT = 35 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 6.5*2.2*35 | Answer: 500.5 kW

question: A reactor of volume 6.4 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 5 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 6.4, Q = 5 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 6.4 / 5 | Answer: 1.28 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 8.1e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 4 mm with a concentration difference of 170 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 8.1, L = 4, dC = 170 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (8.1e-9)*170 / (4e-3) | Answer: 344.2 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 4.2 min and steady-state gain 1.8. For a step input of magnitude 14, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 4.2, K = 1.8, M = 14 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 1.8 * 14 | Answer: 25.2 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 35 m^2 flies at 80 m/s (air density 1.225 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.6. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 35, V = 80, rho = 1.225, CL = 0.6 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1.225*(80)^2*35*0.6 / 1000 | Answer: 82.32 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 15 m^2 flies at 210 m/s (density 0.4 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.07. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 15, V = 210, rho = 0.4, CD = 0.07 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.4*(210)^2*15*0.07 / 1000 | Answer: 9.261 kN

question: A specimen under stress 270 MPa shows an elastic strain of 1.1e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 270, eps = 1.1 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 270 / (1.1e-3) MPa = 245.5 GPa | Answer: 245.5 GPa

question: A block of mass 2 kg has a volume of 5.2e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 2, V = 5.2 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 2 / (5.2e-3) | Answer: 384.6 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 1500 mm is heated through 150 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 17e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 1500, dT = 150, al = 17 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 1500*17e-6*150 | Answer: 3.825 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 125 ohm, R2 = 140 ohm and R3 = 480 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 125, R2 = 140, R3 = 480 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 140*480 / 125 | Answer: 537.6 ohm

question: A measurement reads 10.74 when the true value is 20. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10.74, true = 20 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10.74 - 20| / 20 * 100 | Answer: 46.3 %

question: Annual demand is 4000 units, ordering cost 210 per order and holding cost 10 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 4000, S = 210, H = 10 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*4000*210 / 10) | Answer: 409.9 units

question: An asset costs 330000 with salvage value 10000 after 7 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 330000, Sv = 10000, n = 7 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (330000 - 10000) / 7 | Answer: 45714 per year

question: A product sells for 380 per unit with variable cost 30 per unit and fixed costs 35000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 380, V = 30, F = 35000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 35000 / (380 - 30) | Answer: 100 units

question: Find the present worth of 200000 received 5 years from now at an interest rate of 5% per year.
solution: Given: F = 200000, n = 5, i = 5 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 200000 / (1 + 0.05)^5 | Answer: 156705 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.95, 0.9 and 0.91 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.95, r2 = 0.9, r3 = 0.91 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.95*0.9*0.91 | Answer: 0.7781

question: A process produces 33 defective items in a batch of 1000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 33, N = 1000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 33/1000 * 1e6 | Answer: 33000 PPM

question: Solve for x: 1x + 6y = 2 and 2x + -2y = 3.

question: Find the slope of the line through (-3, 7) and (7, 6).
solution: Given: x1 = -3, y1 = 7, x2 = 7, y2 = 6 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (6 - 7) / (7 - -3) | Answer: -0.1

question: Find the distance between the points (5, 2) and (1, 1).
solution: Given: x1 = 5, y1 = 2, x2 = 1, y2 = 1 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-4)^2 + (-1)^2) | Answer: 4.123 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (6,8), (-6,8), (2,7).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 6 sq units

question: Find the 28th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -18 and common difference -5.
solution: Given: a = -18, d = -5, n = 28 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -18 + (28 - 1)*-5 | Answer: -153

question: Find the sum of the first 37 terms of an AP with first term -11 and common difference -7.
Find the simple interest on a principal of 27000 at 7.1% per annum for 5 years.
solution: Given: P = 27000, R = 7.1, Tt = 5 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 27000 * 7.1 * 5 / 100 | Answer: 9585 currency units

question: Find the amount when 7500 is invested at 8.3% per annum compounded annually for 4 years.
solution: Given: P = 7500, R = 8.3, Tt = 4 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 7500 * (1 + 8.3/100)^4 | Answer: 10318 currency units

solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 57.96 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number 8 + -1i.
solution: Given: a = 8, b = -1 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((8)^2 + (-1)^2) | Answer: 8.062

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number 12 + -7i.
solution: Given: a = 12, b = -7 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(-7, 12) | Answer: -30.26 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -2x^3 + 7x^2 + 3x + 6 at x = 1.
solution: Given: a = -2, b = 7, c = 3, d = 6, x0 = 1 | Formula: f(x0) = a x0^3 + b x0^2 + c x0 + d | Substitute: f(1) = -2(1)^3 + 7(1)^2 + 3(1) + 6 | Answer: 14

question: Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-101 with initial guess x0=6, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.5 and ordinates 0, 18, 1, 15, 4, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 484 and 390.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 484 and 390 | Answer: GCD = 2

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 42 and 77.
solution: Given: a = 42, b = 77 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 42*77 / 7 | Answer: 462
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 33 mm carries an axial tensile load of 68 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 26 mm and length 900 mm carries an axial load of 15 kN. Take E = 70 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 38 mm transmits a torque of 2100 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 38, Tt = 2100 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(2100*1000) / (pi*(38)^3) | Answer: 194.9 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 36 mm and length 800 mm carries a torque of 1600 N-m. With G = 77 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (36)^4 / 32 = 164896 mm^4 | theta = (1600*1000)(800) / (77000 * 164896) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 5.776 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 133 mm wide and 140 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 133, h = 140 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 133*(140)^2 / 6 | Answer: 434467 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (62 mm x 220 mm) carries a bending moment of 30 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (64 mm x 150 mm) has effective length 2600 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 680 MPa is designed for a working stress of 100 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 680, sw = 100 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 680 / 100 | Answer: 6.8

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1250 mm and wall thickness 9 mm carries an internal pressure of 1.3 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1250, t = 9, P = 1.3 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 1.3*1250 / (2*9) | Answer: 90.28 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 940 K and 320 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 940, Tc = 320 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 320/940) * 100 | Answer: 65.96 %

question: A refrigerator works between 275 K (cold) and 318 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 275, Th = 318 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 275 / (318 - 275) | Answer: 6.395

question: A heat pump operates between 268 K and 300 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 268, Th = 300 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 300 / (300 - 268) | Answer: 9.375

question: 3.5 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 25 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.5, dT = 25 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 3.5 * 0.718 * 25 | Answer: 62.82 kJ

question: 3.6 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 85 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.6, dT = 85 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 3.6 * 1.005 * 85 | Answer: 307.5 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 3.6 m^3 at 540 K with mass 3.1 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 3.6, Tk = 540, m = 3.1 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 3.1*0.287*540 / 3.6 | Answer: 133.5 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 1.1 kg of air expands isothermally at 490 K from volume V1 to 5*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1.1, Tk = 490, ratio = 5 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 1.1*0.287*490*ln(5) | Answer: 249 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 4.6 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.07 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 4.6, D = 0.07 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*4.6*0.07 / 0.001 | Answer: 322000

question: Water flows at 3.5 m/s through a pipe of diameter 120 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.

question: In a pipe (diameter 200 mm) water flows at 2.1 m/s. It contracts to diameter 80 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 200, d2 = 80, V1 = 2.1 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 2.1*(200/80)^2 | Answer: 13.12 m/s

question: Water flows at 3.6 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.16 m and length 450 m. With friction factor f = 0.035, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 18 teeth drives a gear of 68 teeth. If the pinion runs at 550 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 18, z2 = 68, N1 = 550 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 550*18 / 68 | Answer: 145.6 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 420 mm rotates at 400 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 420, N = 400 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.42)*400 / 60 | Answer: 8.796 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 17.2 kW at 650 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 17.2, N = 650 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(17.2*1000) / (2*pi*650) | Answer: 252.7 N-m

question: A mass of 4 kg rotates at radius 0.31 m at 500 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 19000 N/m and mass 12.3 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 19000, m = 12.3 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(19000/12.3) | Answer: 6.255 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 1.4 m^2 and thickness 0.36 m has conductivity k = 25.8 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 180 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 1.4, L = 0.36, k = 25.8, dT = 180 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 25.8*1.4*180 / 0.36 | Answer: 18060 W

question: A surface of area 3.8 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 30 W/m^2-K to surroundings 115 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.

question: In turning, cutting speed = 80 m/min, feed = 0.43 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2.1 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.

question: A workpiece of length 80 mm is turned at 650 rpm with a feed of 0.22 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 80, N = 650, f = 0.22 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 80 / (0.22*650) | Answer: 0.5594 min

question: A resistor of 158 ohm carries a current of 1.9 A. Find the voltage across it.

question: Three resistors 83 ohm, 14 ohm and 19 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 83, R2 = 14, R3 = 19 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 83 + 14 + 19 | Answer: 116 ohm

question: Two resistors 62 ohm and 101 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 62, R2 = 101 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 62*101 / (62+101) | Answer: 38.42 ohm

question: A device draws 8.1 A at 100 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 100, I = 8.1 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 100 * 8.1 | Answer: 810 W

question: A current of 3.9 A flows through a 14 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 3.9, R = 14 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (3.9)^2 * 14 | Answer: 212.9 W

question: Two capacitors 32 uF and 41.1 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 32, C2 = 41.1 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 32*41.1 / (32+41.1) | Answer: 17.99 uF

question: A resistor 8 kohm and capacitor 16.8 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.

question: An inductor 357 mH is in series with 129 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 357, R = 129 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (357e-3) / 129 | Answer: 2.767 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 163.4 mH inductor at 180 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 163.4, f = 180 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (180)(163.4e-3) | Answer: 184.8 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 23.5 uF capacitor at 200 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 23.5, f = 200 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (200)(23.5e-6)) | Answer: 33.86 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 9 ohm, XL = 82 ohm and XC = 87 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 96.2 mH and C = 6.7 uF (in Hz).

question: A capacitor of 55.7 uF is charged to 190 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 55.7, V = 190 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*55.7e-6*(190)^2 | Answer: 1005 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 310 V with 690 primary turns and 260 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 310, N1 = 690, N2 = 260 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 310 * 260/690 | Answer: 116.8 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 190 V and draws an armature current of 58 A. If the armature resistance is 0.89 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 190, Ia = 58, Ra = 0.89 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 190 - 58*0.89 | Answer: 138.4 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 75 A at 415 V (line) with a power factor of 0.83. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 75, VL = 415, pf = 0.83 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*415*75*0.83 / 1000 | Answer: 44.75 kW

question: A load has real power 120 kW and apparent power 205 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 120, S = 205 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 120 / 205 | Answer: 0.5854

question: A machine delivers 35 kW output while drawing 57 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 35, Pi = 57 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 35/57 * 100 | Answer: 61.4 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 20 V across R1 = 1 ohm and R2 = 20 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 20, R1 = 1, R2 = 20 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 20*20 / (1+20) | Answer: 19.05 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 210 kohm and Rin = 12 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 210, Rin = 12 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 210 / 12 | Answer: 17.5

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 90 kohm and Rg = 18 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 90, Rg = 18 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 90/18 | Answer: 6

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 638. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 638 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(638) | Answer: 28.05 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 3.5 m carries a central point load of 15 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.5, W = 15 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 15*3.5 / 4 | Answer: 13.12 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 7.1 m carries a UDL of 15 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7.1, w = 15 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 15*(7.1)^2 / 8 | Answer: 94.52 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 5.8 m carries a UDL of 38 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.8, w = 38 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 38*(5.8)^2 / 2 | Answer: 639.2 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 5.8 m carries a point load 10 kN at distance 3 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.

question: A simply supported beam (span 3.6 m) carries a central point load 45 kN. With E = 25 GPa and I = 290e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.

question: A fixed beam of span 7.7 m carries a UDL of 21 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7.7, w = 21 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 21*(7.7)^2 / 12 | Answer: 103.8 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 370 mm, clear cover 35 mm and main bars of diameter 20 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 370, c = 35, dia = 20 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 370 - 35 - 20/2 | Answer: 325 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 13.8 m^2 carrying a factored load of 10.8 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 13.8, w = 10.8 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 10.8 * 13.8 | Answer: 149 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 5.3 m, unit weight 16 kN/m^3, phi = 30 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 3.6e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.7, area = 6.7e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 3.6, i = 0.7, A = 6.7 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (3.6e-4)*0.7*(6.7e-3) | Answer: 1688 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 2.4 m, bed slope 0.002 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.025. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 3.2 m under a head of 0.3 m. Taking Cd = 0.61 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.

question: A tank of volume 50 m^3 treats a flow of 10 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 50, Q = 10 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 50 / 10 | Answer: 5 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 280 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.15 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 6 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 280, k = 0.15, t = 6 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 280*(1 - e^(-0.15*6)) | Answer: 166.2 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.41, rainfall intensity 80 mm/h over a catchment of 6.4 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.41, i = 80, A = 6.4 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.41*80*6.4 / 360 | Answer: 0.5831 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.02 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 160 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.02, M = 160 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 160*(20+0.02)/20 | Answer: 160.2 m

question: Convert the decimal number 3515 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 3515 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: DBB (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 11111001 and 10111110.
solution: XOR: 01000111 | Count of 1s = 4 | Answer: 4
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 710 megabits is sent over a link of 99 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 710, B = 99 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 710 / 99 | Answer: 7.172 s

question: A link has bandwidth 16 Mbps and round-trip time 150 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 16, R = 150 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 16e6 * 150e-3 bits = 2400 kb | Answer: 2400 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.88, cache access time 1 ns and main-memory access time 110 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.88, tc = 1, tm = 110 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.88*1 + (1 - 0.88)*110 | Answer: 14.08 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 777860 elements?
solution: Given: n = 777860 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(777860)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.002, memory access time 110 ns and page-fault service time 3 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 3 ms = 3000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.002)*110 + 0.002*3000000.0 ns | Answer: 6.11 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 1.6 m^3 at 150 kPa and 380 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 1.6, P = 150, Tk = 380 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (150e3)*1.6 / (8.314*380) | Answer: 75.97 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.32 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 18 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.32, t = 18 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.32*18) | Answer: 0.9968

question: For a reaction with A = 1e10 /s and activation energy 60 kJ/mol at 420 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 1, Ea = 60, Tk = 420 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 1e10 * exp(-60e3 / (8.314*420)) | Answer: 344.9 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.96 and bottoms xW = 0.07, with relative volatility alpha = 3.4. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.96, xw = 0.07, al = 3.4 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.96/0.04)(0.93/0.07)] / ln(3.4) | Answer: 4.711 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.82 and x = 0.23. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.82, x = 0.23 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.82/0.18) / (0.23/0.77) | Answer: 15.25

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.52 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 50 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.52, Psat = 50 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.52 * 50 | Answer: 26 kPa

question: A stream of 1.5 kg/s with specific heat 3.3 kJ/kg-K is heated through 35 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 1.5, cp = 3.3, dT = 35 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 1.5*3.3*35 | Answer: 173.2 kW

question: A reactor of volume 2.3 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 4.7 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 2.3, Q = 4.7 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 2.3 / 4.7 | Answer: 0.4894 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 7.9e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 4 mm with a concentration difference of 150 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 7.9, L = 4, dC = 150 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (7.9e-9)*150 / (4e-3) | Answer: 296.2 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 3.2 min and steady-state gain 1. For a step input of magnitude 3, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 3.2, K = 1, M = 3 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 1 * 3 | Answer: 3 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 20 m^2 flies at 100 m/s (air density 1.225 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 1. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 20, V = 100, rho = 1.225, CL = 1 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1.225*(100)^2*20*1 / 1000 | Answer: 122.5 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 65 m^2 flies at 80 m/s (density 1.225 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.05. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 65, V = 80, rho = 1.225, CD = 0.05 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*1.225*(80)^2*65*0.05 / 1000 | Answer: 12.74 kN

question: A specimen under stress 400 MPa shows an elastic strain of 0.7e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 400, eps = 0.7 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 400 / (0.7e-3) MPa = 571.4 GPa | Answer: 571.4 GPa

question: A block of mass 46 kg has a volume of 4e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 46, V = 4 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 46 / (4e-3) | Answer: 11500 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 3000 mm is heated through 145 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 12e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 3000, dT = 145, al = 12 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 3000*12e-6*145 | Answer: 5.22 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 70 ohm, R2 = 90 ohm and R3 = 345 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 70, R2 = 90, R3 = 345 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 90*345 / 70 | Answer: 443.6 ohm

question: A measurement reads 10.91 when the true value is 10. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10.91, true = 10 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10.91 - 10| / 10 * 100 | Answer: 9.1 %

question: Annual demand is 3000 units, ordering cost 180 per order and holding cost 18 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 3000, S = 180, H = 18 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*3000*180 / 18) | Answer: 244.9 units

question: An asset costs 410000 with salvage value 26000 after 15 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 410000, Sv = 26000, n = 15 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (410000 - 26000) / 15 | Answer: 25600 per year

question: A product sells for 140 per unit with variable cost 120 per unit and fixed costs 10000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 140, V = 120, F = 10000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 10000 / (140 - 120) | Answer: 500 units

question: Find the present worth of 190000 received 6 years from now at an interest rate of 9% per year.
solution: Given: F = 190000, n = 6, i = 9 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 190000 / (1 + 0.09)^6 | Answer: 113291 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.95, 0.98 and 0.92 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.95, r2 = 0.98, r3 = 0.92 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.95*0.98*0.92 | Answer: 0.8565

question: A process produces 41 defective items in a batch of 11500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 41, N = 11500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 41/11500 * 1e6 | Answer: 3565 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -4x^3 + 3x^2 + 7x + 2 evaluated at x = -3.
For f(x) = 2x^3 + 5x^2 - 5x + 2, find f''(x) at x = 3.
Evaluate the definite integral of (-3x^2 + 4x - 4) dx from x = -3 to x = 4.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = -3x^3/3 + 4x^2/2 + -4x | Evaluate F(4) - F(-3) | Answer: -105
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of x^2 + 5x + 3 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[-3, 0], [5, 8]].
solution: Given: a = -3, b = 0, c = 5, d = 8 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (-3)(8) - (0)(5) | Answer: -24

question: Find the determinant of [[-3, -5, -3], [0, -6, 5], [1, 1, 1]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: -10

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[5, 5], [-3, -3]].
solution: Trace tr = 2, Determinant = 0 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 2

question: Solve for x: -5x + -5y = 9 and -3x + -2y = -5.
solution: Determinant = -5*-2 - -5*-3 = -5 | x = (e d - b f) / det = 8.6 | Answer: x = 8.6
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 21, 77, 43, 3, 24.
solution: Sum = 168 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 33.6 | Answer: 33.6

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 43, 24, 17, 27, 11.
solution: Mean = 24.4 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 12.12

question: Find the slope of the line through (-3, 9) and (-9, 2).
solution: Given: x1 = -3, y1 = 9, x2 = -9, y2 = 2 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (2 - 9) / (-9 - -3) | Answer: 1.167

question: Find the distance between the points (-8, 8) and (-4, -8).
solution: Given: x1 = -8, y1 = 8, x2 = -4, y2 = -8 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((4)^2 + (-16)^2) | Answer: 16.49 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (3,-4), (6,1), (-1,3).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 20.5 sq units

question: Find the 40th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -10 and common difference -8.
solution: Given: a = -10, d = -8, n = 40 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -10 + (40 - 1)*-8 | Answer: -322

question: Find the sum of the first 7 terms of an AP with first term 11 and common difference -5.
solution: Given: a = 11, d = -5, n = 7 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 7/2 [2*11 + (7-1)*-5] | Answer: -28

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 18500 at 7.8% per annum for 4 years.
solution: Given: P = 18500, R = 7.8, Tt = 4 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 18500 * 7.8 * 4 / 100 | Answer: 5772 currency units

question: Find the amount when 28500 is invested at 5.1% per annum compounded annually for 6 years.
solution: Given: P = 28500, R = 5.1, Tt = 6 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 28500 * (1 + 5.1/100)^6 | Answer: 38411 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (3, 5, 4) and (-7, 2, 1).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (1, 6, 3) and (1, -3, 1).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 17.61

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (-4, -4, 2) and (5, -4, -4).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 105.4 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number 9 + 5i.
solution: Given: a = 9, b = 5 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((9)^2 + (5)^2) | Answer: 10.3

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number 2 + 2i.
solution: Given: a = 2, b = 2 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(2, 2) | Answer: 45 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = x^3 + 5x^2 - 7 at x = 4.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-145 with initial guess x0=4, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.5 and ordinates 2, 14, 15, 6, 2, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 59 and 435.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 59 and 435 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 14 and 58.
solution: Given: a = 14, b = 58 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 14*58 / 2 | Answer: 406
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 57 mm carries an axial tensile load of 51 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 13 mm and length 500 mm carries an axial load of 90 kN. Take E = 70 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 76 mm transmits a torque of 1250 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 76, Tt = 1250 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(1250*1000) / (pi*(76)^3) | Answer: 14.5 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 54 mm and length 1600 mm carries a torque of 800 N-m. With G = 45 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (54)^4 / 32 = 834786 mm^4 | theta = (800*1000)(1600) / (45000 * 834786) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 1.952 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 82 mm wide and 200 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 82, h = 200 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 82*(200)^2 / 6 | Answer: 546667 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (82 mm x 190 mm) carries a bending moment of 3 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (44 mm x 160 mm) has effective length 2000 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 360 MPa is designed for a working stress of 150 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 360, sw = 150 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 360 / 150 | Answer: 2.4

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 300 mm and wall thickness 19 mm carries an internal pressure of 2.2 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 300, t = 19, P = 2.2 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 2.2*300 / (2*19) | Answer: 17.37 MPa

question: 4.5 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 105 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.5, dT = 105 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 4.5 * 0.718 * 105 | Answer: 339.3 kJ

question: 7.3 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 25 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 7.3, dT = 25 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 7.3 * 1.005 * 25 | Answer: 183.4 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 2 m^3 at 510 K with mass 5 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 2, Tk = 510, m = 5 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 5*0.287*510 / 2 | Answer: 365.9 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 4 kg of air expands isothermally at 400 K from volume V1 to 4*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4, Tk = 400, ratio = 4 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 4*0.287*400*ln(4) | Answer: 636.6 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 3.1 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.09 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 3.1, D = 0.09 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*3.1*0.09 / 0.001 | Answer: 279000

question: Water flows at 1.1 m/s through a pipe of diameter 50 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 2.5 m. Taking Cv = 0.96, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 2.5, cv = 0.96 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.96*sqrt(2*9.81*2.5) | Answer: 6.723 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 190 mm) water flows at 2.9 m/s. It contracts to diameter 120 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 190, d2 = 120, V1 = 2.9 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 2.9*(190/120)^2 | Answer: 7.27 m/s

question: Water flows at 1.9 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.32 m and length 310 m. With friction factor f = 0.027, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 23 teeth drives a gear of 96 teeth. If the pinion runs at 700 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 23, z2 = 96, N1 = 700 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 700*23 / 96 | Answer: 167.7 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 530 mm rotates at 1450 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 530, N = 1450 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.53)*1450 / 60 | Answer: 40.24 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 30.7 kW at 200 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 30.7, N = 200 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(30.7*1000) / (2*pi*200) | Answer: 1466 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 9.3 kg rotates at radius 0.13 m at 1100 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 15200 N/m and mass 2.6 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 15200, m = 2.6 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(15200/2.6) | Answer: 12.17 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 3.7 m^2 and thickness 0.24 m has conductivity k = 13.6 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 140 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 3.7, L = 0.24, k = 13.6, dT = 140 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 13.6*3.7*140 / 0.24 | Answer: 29353 W

question: A surface of area 0.6 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 35 W/m^2-K to surroundings 150 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 0.6, h = 35, dT = 150 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 35*0.6*150 | Answer: 3150 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 200 m/min, feed = 0.35 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2.5 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 200, f = 0.35, d = 2.5 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*200*0.35*2.5 | Answer: 175000 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 500 mm is turned at 950 rpm with a feed of 0.25 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 500, N = 950, f = 0.25 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 500 / (0.25*950) | Answer: 2.105 min

question: A resistor of 13 ohm carries a current of 0.2 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 13, I = 0.2 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 0.2 * 13 | Answer: 2.6 V

question: Three resistors 80 ohm, 25 ohm and 90 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 80, R2 = 25, R3 = 90 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 80 + 25 + 90 | Answer: 195 ohm

question: Two resistors 56 ohm and 8 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 56, R2 = 8 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 56*8 / (56+8) | Answer: 7 ohm

question: A device draws 1 A at 5 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 5, I = 1 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 5 * 1 | Answer: 5 W

question: A current of 7.5 A flows through a 18 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 7.5, R = 18 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (7.5)^2 * 18 | Answer: 1012 W

question: Two capacitors 36.4 uF and 47.9 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 36.4, C2 = 47.9 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 36.4*47.9 / (36.4+47.9) | Answer: 20.68 uF

question: A resistor 60 kohm and capacitor 7.7 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 60, C = 7.7 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (60k)(7.7u) = 462 ms | Answer: 462 ms

question: An inductor 221.7 mH is in series with 34 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 221.7, R = 34 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (221.7e-3) / 34 | Answer: 6.521 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 160.5 mH inductor at 110 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 160.5, f = 110 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (110)(160.5e-3) | Answer: 110.9 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 37.8 uF capacitor at 460 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 37.8, f = 460 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (460)(37.8e-6)) | Answer: 9.153 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 69 ohm, XL = 117 ohm and XC = 32 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 69, XL = 117, XC = 32 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(69^2 + (117 - 32)^2) | Answer: 109.5 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 1.5 mH and C = 8.8 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 1.5, C = 8.8 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(1.5e-3 * 8.8e-6)) | Answer: 1385 Hz

question: A capacitor of 2.9 uF is charged to 395 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 2.9, V = 395 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*2.9e-6*(395)^2 | Answer: 226.2 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 260 V with 490 primary turns and 40 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 260, N1 = 490, N2 = 40 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 260 * 40/490 | Answer: 21.22 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 190 V and draws an armature current of 53 A. If the armature resistance is 0.46 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 190, Ia = 53, Ra = 0.46 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 190 - 53*0.46 | Answer: 165.6 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 25 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.91. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 25, VL = 400, pf = 0.91 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*400*25*0.91 / 1000 | Answer: 15.76 kW

question: A load has real power 105 kW and apparent power 195 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 105, S = 195 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 105 / 195 | Answer: 0.5385

question: A machine delivers 30 kW output while drawing 57 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 30, Pi = 57 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 30/57 * 100 | Answer: 52.63 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 27 V across R1 = 40 ohm and R2 = 45 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 27, R1 = 40, R2 = 45 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 27*45 / (40+45) | Answer: 14.29 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 190 kohm and Rin = 11 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 190, Rin = 11 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 190 / 11 | Answer: 17.27

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 20 kohm and Rg = 37 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 20, Rg = 37 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 20/37 | Answer: 1.541

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 1429. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 1429 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(1429) | Answer: 31.55 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.1 m carries a central point load of 50 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.1, W = 50 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 50*4.1 / 4 | Answer: 51.25 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 5.8 m carries a UDL of 55 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.8, w = 55 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 55*(5.8)^2 / 8 | Answer: 231.3 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 3.3 m carries a point load 45 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.3, W = 45 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 45*3.3 | Answer: 148.5 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 4.5 m carries a UDL of 6 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.5, w = 6 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 6*(4.5)^2 / 2 | Answer: 60.75 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 8.6 m carries a point load 10 kN at distance 3.9 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 8.6, a = 3.9, W = 10 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 10*(8.6 - 3.9) / 8.6 | Answer: 5.465 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 6.3 m) carries a central point load 15 kN. With E = 200 GPa and I = 130e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=15000 N, L=6300.0 mm, E=200000 MPa, I=130e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 3.005 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 7.2 m carries a UDL of 18 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7.2, w = 18 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 18*(7.2)^2 / 12 | Answer: 77.76 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 370 mm, clear cover 45 mm and main bars of diameter 25 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 370, c = 45, dia = 25 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 370 - 45 - 25/2 | Answer: 312.5 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 32.6 m^2 carrying a factored load of 19.2 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 32.6, w = 19.2 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 19.2 * 32.6 | Answer: 625.9 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 4 m, unit weight 18 kN/m^3, phi = 33 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 5.5e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.9, area = 4.8e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 5.5, i = 0.9, A = 4.8 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (5.5e-4)*0.9*(4.8e-3) | Answer: 2376 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.9 m, bed slope 0.01 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.027. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 4.4 m under a head of 0.8 m. Taking Cd = 0.61 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 5.1 m wide carries a discharge of 29.9 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 300 m and design speed 70 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 300, V = 70 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (70)^2 / (127*300) | Answer: 0.1286
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: A tank of volume 210 m^3 treats a flow of 145 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 210, Q = 145 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 210 / 145 | Answer: 1.448 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 380 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.19 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 8 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 380, k = 0.19, t = 8 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 380*(1 - e^(-0.19*8)) | Answer: 296.9 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.71, rainfall intensity 35 mm/h over a catchment of 17.6 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.71, i = 35, A = 17.6 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.71*35*17.6 / 360 | Answer: 1.215 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.01 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 330 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.01, M = 330 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 330*(30+0.01)/30 | Answer: 330.1 m

question: Convert the decimal number 1978 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 1978 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 7BA (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 01101011 and 11011011.
solution: XOR: 10110000 | Count of 1s = 3 | Answer: 3
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 770 megabits is sent over a link of 61 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 770, B = 61 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 770 / 61 | Answer: 12.62 s

question: A link has bandwidth 87 Mbps and round-trip time 90 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 87, R = 90 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 87e6 * 90e-3 bits = 7830 kb | Answer: 7830 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.97, cache access time 6 ns and main-memory access time 100 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.97, tc = 6, tm = 100 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.97*6 + (1 - 0.97)*100 | Answer: 8.82 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 962302 elements?
solution: Given: n = 962302 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(962302)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.011, memory access time 160 ns and page-fault service time 5 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 5 ms = 5000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.011)*160 + 0.011*5000000.0 ns | Answer: 55.16 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 1.7 m^3 at 260 kPa and 530 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 1.7, P = 260, Tk = 530 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (260e3)*1.7 / (8.314*530) | Answer: 100.3 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.37 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 20 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.37, t = 20 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.37*20) | Answer: 0.9994

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.15 /min) reaches 50% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.15, X = 50 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.5 / (0.15*(1 - 0.5)) | Answer: 6.667 min

question: For a reaction with A = 4e10 /s and activation energy 50 kJ/mol at 500 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 4, Ea = 50, Tk = 500 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 4e10 * exp(-50e3 / (8.314*500)) | Answer: 239005 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.93 and bottoms xW = 0.06, with relative volatility alpha = 2.3. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.93, xw = 0.06, al = 2.3 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.93/0.07)(0.94/0.06)] / ln(2.3) | Answer: 6.409 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.63 and x = 0.36. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.63, x = 0.36 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.63/0.37) / (0.36/0.64) | Answer: 3.027

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.57 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 30 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.57, Psat = 30 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.57 * 30 | Answer: 17.1 kPa

question: A stream of 2.1 kg/s with specific heat 3.6 kJ/kg-K is heated through 55 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 2.1, cp = 3.6, dT = 55 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 2.1*3.6*55 | Answer: 415.8 kW

question: A reactor of volume 2.4 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 4.2 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 2.4, Q = 4.2 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 2.4 / 4.2 | Answer: 0.5714 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 7.6e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 4 mm with a concentration difference of 90 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 7.6, L = 4, dC = 90 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (7.6e-9)*90 / (4e-3) | Answer: 171 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 7.7 min and steady-state gain 3.6. For a step input of magnitude 14, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 7.7, K = 3.6, M = 14 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 3.6 * 14 | Answer: 50.4 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 115 m^2 flies at 160 m/s (air density 1 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 1.3. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 115, V = 160, rho = 1, CL = 1.3 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1*(160)^2*115*1.3 / 1000 | Answer: 1914 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 100 m^2 flies at 100 m/s (density 1.225 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.08. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 100, V = 100, rho = 1.225, CD = 0.08 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*1.225*(100)^2*100*0.08 / 1000 | Answer: 49 kN

question: A specimen under stress 370 MPa shows an elastic strain of 1e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 370, eps = 1 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 370 / (1e-3) MPa = 370 GPa | Answer: 370 GPa

question: A block of mass 45 kg has a volume of 1.4e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 45, V = 1.4 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 45 / (1.4e-3) | Answer: 32143 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 2700 mm is heated through 35 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 11e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 2700, dT = 35, al = 11 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 2700*11e-6*35 | Answer: 1.04 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 150 ohm, R2 = 55 ohm and R3 = 235 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 150, R2 = 55, R3 = 235 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 55*235 / 150 | Answer: 86.17 ohm

question: A measurement reads 9.28 when the true value is 10. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.28, true = 10 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.28 - 10| / 10 * 100 | Answer: 7.2 %

question: Annual demand is 49500 units, ordering cost 280 per order and holding cost 17 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 49500, S = 280, H = 17 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*49500*280 / 17) | Answer: 1277 units

question: An asset costs 140000 with salvage value 28000 after 17 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 140000, Sv = 28000, n = 17 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (140000 - 28000) / 17 | Answer: 6588 per year

question: A product sells for 410 per unit with variable cost 100 per unit and fixed costs 80000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 410, V = 100, F = 80000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 80000 / (410 - 100) | Answer: 258.1 units

question: Find the present worth of 200000 received 5 years from now at an interest rate of 9% per year.
solution: Given: F = 200000, n = 5, i = 9 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 200000 / (1 + 0.09)^5 | Answer: 129986 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.96, 0.95 and 0.91 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.96, r2 = 0.95, r3 = 0.91 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.96*0.95*0.91 | Answer: 0.8299

question: A process produces 28 defective items in a batch of 9500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 28, N = 9500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 28/9500 * 1e6 | Answer: 2947 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -5x^3 - 6x^2 + x + 7 evaluated at x = -2.
For f(x) = x^3 - 7x^2 - 4, find f''(x) at x = -1.
Evaluate the definite integral of (4x^2 + 4x + 6) dx from x = 2 to x = 7.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = 4x^3/3 + 4x^2/2 + 6x | Evaluate F(7) - F(2) | Answer: 566.7
