question: A circular rod of diameter 18 mm carries an axial tensile load of 60 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 38 mm and length 1000 mm carries an axial load of 68 kN. Take E = 210 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 32 mm transmits a torque of 850 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 32, Tt = 850 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(850*1000) / (pi*(32)^3) | Answer: 132.1 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 51 mm and length 1300 mm carries a torque of 1900 N-m. With G = 45 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (51)^4 / 32 = 664172 mm^4 | theta = (1900*1000)(1300) / (45000 * 664172) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 4.735 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 125 mm wide and 200 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 125, h = 200 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 125*(200)^2 / 6 | Answer: 833333 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (47 mm x 110 mm) carries a bending moment of 21 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (59 mm x 90 mm) has effective length 3300 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 460 MPa is designed for a working stress of 130 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 460, sw = 130 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 460 / 130 | Answer: 3.538

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1350 mm and wall thickness 9 mm carries an internal pressure of 1.6 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1350, t = 9, P = 1.6 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 1.6*1350 / (2*9) | Answer: 120 MPa

question: 6.8 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 180 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 6.8, dT = 180 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 6.8 * 0.718 * 180 | Answer: 878.8 kJ

question: 6.5 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 155 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 6.5, dT = 155 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 6.5 * 1.005 * 155 | Answer: 1013 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 1.6 m^3 at 380 K with mass 4.3 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 1.6, Tk = 380, m = 4.3 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 4.3*0.287*380 / 1.6 | Answer: 293.1 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 2.9 kg of air expands isothermally at 430 K from volume V1 to 4*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.9, Tk = 430, ratio = 4 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 2.9*0.287*430*ln(4) | Answer: 496.1 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 0.8 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.27 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 0.8, D = 0.27 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*0.8*0.27 / 0.001 | Answer: 216000

question: Water flows at 2.3 m/s through a pipe of diameter 250 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 1.6 m. Taking Cv = 0.98, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 1.6, cv = 0.98 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.98*sqrt(2*9.81*1.6) | Answer: 5.491 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 360 mm) water flows at 0.7 m/s. It contracts to diameter 70 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 360, d2 = 70, V1 = 0.7 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 0.7*(360/70)^2 | Answer: 18.51 m/s

question: Water flows at 3.3 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.16 m and length 300 m. With friction factor f = 0.031, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 27 teeth drives a gear of 55 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1500 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 27, z2 = 55, N1 = 1500 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1500*27 / 55 | Answer: 736.4 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 230 mm rotates at 1400 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 230, N = 1400 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.23)*1400 / 60 | Answer: 16.86 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 5.8 kW at 300 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 5.8, N = 300 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(5.8*1000) / (2*pi*300) | Answer: 184.6 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 2.6 kg rotates at radius 0.3 m at 500 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 12300 N/m and mass 12 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 12300, m = 12 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(12300/12) | Answer: 5.095 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 1.9 m^2 and thickness 0.27 m has conductivity k = 8.3 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 135 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 1.9, L = 0.27, k = 8.3, dT = 135 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 8.3*1.9*135 / 0.27 | Answer: 7885 W

question: A surface of area 2.9 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 170 W/m^2-K to surroundings 30 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 2.9, h = 170, dT = 30 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 170*2.9*30 | Answer: 14790 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 90 m/min, feed = 0.12 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2.9 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 90, f = 0.12, d = 2.9 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*90*0.12*2.9 | Answer: 31320 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 220 mm is turned at 950 rpm with a feed of 0.32 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 220, N = 950, f = 0.32 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 220 / (0.32*950) | Answer: 0.7237 min

question: A resistor of 132 ohm carries a current of 0.5 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 132, I = 0.5 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 0.5 * 132 | Answer: 66 V

question: Three resistors 17 ohm, 94 ohm and 57 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 17, R2 = 94, R3 = 57 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 17 + 94 + 57 | Answer: 168 ohm

question: Two resistors 9 ohm and 29 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 9, R2 = 29 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 9*29 / (9+29) | Answer: 6.868 ohm

question: A device draws 9.9 A at 150 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 150, I = 9.9 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 150 * 9.9 | Answer: 1485 W

question: A current of 9.4 A flows through a 62 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 9.4, R = 62 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (9.4)^2 * 62 | Answer: 5478 W

question: Two capacitors 49.2 uF and 5.6 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 49.2, C2 = 5.6 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 49.2*5.6 / (49.2+5.6) | Answer: 5.028 uF

question: A resistor 29 kohm and capacitor 19.9 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 29, C = 19.9 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (29k)(19.9u) = 577.1 ms | Answer: 577.1 ms

question: An inductor 76.2 mH is in series with 22 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 76.2, R = 22 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (76.2e-3) / 22 | Answer: 3.464 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 195.7 mH inductor at 990 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 195.7, f = 990 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (990)(195.7e-3) | Answer: 1217 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 49.8 uF capacitor at 910 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 49.8, f = 910 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (910)(49.8e-6)) | Answer: 3.512 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 5 ohm, XL = 45 ohm and XC = 42 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 5, XL = 45, XC = 42 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(5^2 + (45 - 42)^2) | Answer: 5.831 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 84.1 mH and C = 9.8 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 84.1, C = 9.8 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(84.1e-3 * 9.8e-6)) | Answer: 175.3 Hz

question: A capacitor of 99.2 uF is charged to 225 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 99.2, V = 225 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*99.2e-6*(225)^2 | Answer: 2511 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 380 V with 880 primary turns and 120 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 380, N1 = 880, N2 = 120 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 380 * 120/880 | Answer: 51.82 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 330 V and draws an armature current of 29 A. If the armature resistance is 0.97 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 330, Ia = 29, Ra = 0.97 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 330 - 29*0.97 | Answer: 301.9 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 35 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.83. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 35, VL = 400, pf = 0.83 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*400*35*0.83 / 1000 | Answer: 20.13 kW

question: A load has real power 85 kW and apparent power 180 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 85, S = 180 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 85 / 180 | Answer: 0.4722

question: A machine delivers 20 kW output while drawing 137 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 20, Pi = 137 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 20/137 * 100 | Answer: 14.6 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 29 V across R1 = 8 ohm and R2 = 27 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 29, R1 = 8, R2 = 27 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 29*27 / (8+27) | Answer: 22.37 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 170 kohm and Rin = 39 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 170, Rin = 39 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 170 / 39 | Answer: 4.359

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 50 kohm and Rg = 23 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 50, Rg = 23 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 50/23 | Answer: 3.174

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 7754. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 7754 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(7754) | Answer: 38.9 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.8 m carries a central point load of 20 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.8, W = 20 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 20*4.8 / 4 | Answer: 24 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 5.4 m carries a UDL of 45 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.4, w = 45 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 45*(5.4)^2 / 8 | Answer: 164 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 3.8 m carries a point load 25 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.8, W = 25 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 25*3.8 | Answer: 95 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 2.6 m carries a UDL of 36 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 2.6, w = 36 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 36*(2.6)^2 / 2 | Answer: 121.7 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.3 m carries a point load 90 kN at distance 1.7 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 9.3, a = 1.7, W = 90 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 90*(9.3 - 1.7) / 9.3 | Answer: 73.55 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 5.4 m) carries a central point load 80 kN. With E = 25 GPa and I = 430e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=80000 N, L=5400.0 mm, E=25000 MPa, I=430e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 24.41 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 5.8 m carries a UDL of 45 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.8, w = 45 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 45*(5.8)^2 / 12 | Answer: 126.1 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 420 mm, clear cover 50 mm and main bars of diameter 12 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 420, c = 50, dia = 12 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 420 - 50 - 12/2 | Answer: 364 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 32.2 m^2 carrying a factored load of 10.2 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 32.2, w = 10.2 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 10.2 * 32.2 | Answer: 328.4 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 6.1 m, unit weight 19 kN/m^3, phi = 34 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 10.5 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 18 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 10.5, g = 18 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (18 - 9.81)*10.5 | Answer: 85.99 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 1.3e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1.4, area = 6.9e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 1.3, i = 1.4, A = 6.9 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (1.3e-4)*1.4*(6.9e-3) | Answer: 1256 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 0.8 m, bed slope 0.006 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.025. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 2.3 m under a head of 0.3 m. Taking Cd = 0.63 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 2.7 m wide carries a discharge of 21.1 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 570 m and design speed 60 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 570, V = 60 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (60)^2 / (127*570) | Answer: 0.04973
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: A tank of volume 700 m^3 treats a flow of 180 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 700, Q = 180 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 700 / 180 | Answer: 3.889 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 230 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.17 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 3 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 230, k = 0.17, t = 3 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 230*(1 - e^(-0.17*3)) | Answer: 91.89 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.59, rainfall intensity 45 mm/h over a catchment of 56.5 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.59, i = 45, A = 56.5 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.59*45*56.5 / 360 | Answer: 4.167 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.04 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 760 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.04, M = 760 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 760*(20+0.04)/20 | Answer: 761.5 m

question: Convert the decimal number 1609 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 1609 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 649 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 01100010 and 10110110.
solution: XOR: 11010100 | Count of 1s = 4 | Answer: 4
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 680 megabits is sent over a link of 32 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 680, B = 32 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 680 / 32 | Answer: 21.25 s

question: A link has bandwidth 40 Mbps and round-trip time 160 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 40, R = 160 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 40e6 * 160e-3 bits = 6400 kb | Answer: 6400 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.91, cache access time 5 ns and main-memory access time 60 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.91, tc = 5, tm = 60 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.91*5 + (1 - 0.91)*60 | Answer: 9.95 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 803672 elements?
solution: Given: n = 803672 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(803672)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.003, memory access time 190 ns and page-fault service time 10 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 10 ms = 10000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.003)*190 + 0.003*10000000.0 ns | Answer: 30.19 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 0.5 m^3 at 420 kPa and 590 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 0.5, P = 420, Tk = 590 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (420e3)*0.5 / (8.314*590) | Answer: 42.81 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.22 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 7 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.22, t = 7 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.22*7) | Answer: 0.7856

question: For a reaction with A = 5e10 /s and activation energy 90 kJ/mol at 300 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 5, Ea = 90, Tk = 300 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 5e10 * exp(-90e3 / (8.314*300)) | Answer: 0.00001067 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.93 and bottoms xW = 0.09, with relative volatility alpha = 2.2. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.93, xw = 0.09, al = 2.2 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.93/0.07)(0.91/0.09)] / ln(2.2) | Answer: 6.215 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.78 and x = 0.48. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.78, x = 0.48 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.78/0.22) / (0.48/0.52) | Answer: 3.841

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.8 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 100 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.8, Psat = 100 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.8 * 100 | Answer: 80 kPa

question: A stream of 9.1 kg/s with specific heat 3.5 kJ/kg-K is heated through 45 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 9.1, cp = 3.5, dT = 45 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 9.1*3.5*45 | Answer: 1433 kW

question: A reactor of volume 17.3 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 2.3 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 17.3, Q = 2.3 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 17.3 / 2.3 | Answer: 7.522 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 8.9e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 2 mm with a concentration difference of 10 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 8.9, L = 2, dC = 10 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (8.9e-9)*10 / (2e-3) | Answer: 44.5 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 2.4 min and steady-state gain 2.7. For a step input of magnitude 18, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 2.4, K = 2.7, M = 18 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 2.7 * 18 | Answer: 48.6 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 30 m^2 flies at 200 m/s (air density 1 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.8. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 30, V = 200, rho = 1, CL = 0.8 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1*(200)^2*30*0.8 / 1000 | Answer: 480 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 15 m^2 flies at 160 m/s (density 1.225 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.06. Find the drag force in kN.
A specimen under stress 110 MPa shows an elastic strain of 1e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 110, eps = 1 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 110 / (1e-3) MPa = 110 GPa | Answer: 110 GPa

question: A block of mass 49 kg has a volume of 3.9e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 49, V = 3.9 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 49 / (3.9e-3) | Answer: 12564 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 900 mm is heated through 80 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 11e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 900, dT = 80, al = 11 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 900*11e-6*80 | Answer: 0.792 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 40 ohm, R2 = 15 ohm and R3 = 200 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 40, R2 = 15, R3 = 200 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 15*200 / 40 | Answer: 75 ohm

question: A measurement reads 10.72 when the true value is 10. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10.72, true = 10 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10.72 - 10| / 10 * 100 | Answer: 7.2 %

question: Annual demand is 5500 units, ordering cost 20 per order and holding cost 14 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 5500, S = 20, H = 14 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*5500*20 / 14) | Answer: 125.4 units

question: An asset costs 130000 with salvage value 8000 after 20 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 130000, Sv = 8000, n = 20 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (130000 - 8000) / 20 | Answer: 6100 per year

question: A product sells for 310 per unit with variable cost 60 per unit and fixed costs 105000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 310, V = 60, F = 105000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 105000 / (310 - 60) | Answer: 420 units

question: Find the present worth of 65000 received 8 years from now at an interest rate of 6% per year.
solution: Given: F = 65000, n = 8, i = 6 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 65000 / (1 + 0.06)^8 | Answer: 40782 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.93, 0.94 and 0.96 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.93, r2 = 0.94, r3 = 0.96 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.93*0.94*0.96 | Answer: 0.8392

question: A process produces 49 defective items in a batch of 17000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 49, N = 17000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 49/17000 * 1e6 | Answer: 2882 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -4x^3 + 4x^2 - 5x - 1 evaluated at x = -1.
For f(x) = -3x^3 - 2x^2 - 8, find f''(x) at x = -5.
Evaluate the definite integral of (-4x + 2) dx from x = -1 to x = 5.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = 0x^3/3 + -4x^2/2 + 2x | Evaluate F(5) - F(-1) | Answer: -36
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 6x^2 - x - 8 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[-6, 6], [-2, 9]].
solution: Given: a = -6, b = 6, c = -2, d = 9 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (-6)(9) - (6)(-2) | Answer: -42

question: Find the determinant of [[4, -4, 3], [5, 3, -3], [1, 1, 3]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: 126

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[0, 6], [8, -8]].
solution: Trace tr = -8, Determinant = -48 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 4

question: Solve for x: 6x + 4y = -6 and 1x + -6y = -7.
solution: Determinant = 6*-6 - 4*1 = -40 | x = (e d - b f) / det = -1.6 | Answer: x = -1.6
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 15, 17, 59, 68, 45.
solution: Sum = 204 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 40.8 | Answer: 40.8

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 10, 14, 14, 41, 5.
solution: Mean = 16.8 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 14.02

question: Find the slope of the line through (-2, 9) and (-8, -8).
solution: Given: x1 = -2, y1 = 9, x2 = -8, y2 = -8 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (-8 - 9) / (-8 - -2) | Answer: 2.833

question: Find the distance between the points (-6, -2) and (-5, 2).
solution: Given: x1 = -6, y1 = -2, x2 = -5, y2 = 2 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((1)^2 + (4)^2) | Answer: 4.123 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (-7,6), (-4,-8), (-2,-3).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 21.5 sq units

question: Find the 26th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -3 and common difference 7.
solution: Given: a = -3, d = 7, n = 26 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -3 + (26 - 1)*7 | Answer: 172

question: Find the sum of the first 29 terms of an AP with first term -2 and common difference 2.
solution: Given: a = -2, d = 2, n = 29 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 29/2 [2*-2 + (29-1)*2] | Answer: 754

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 43000 at 8.4% per annum for 1 years.
solution: Given: P = 43000, R = 8.4, Tt = 1 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 43000 * 8.4 * 1 / 100 | Answer: 3612 currency units

question: Find the amount when 15000 is invested at 5.3% per annum compounded annually for 5 years.
solution: Given: P = 15000, R = 5.3, Tt = 5 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 15000 * (1 + 5.3/100)^5 | Answer: 19419 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (6, -2, 8) and (-6, -7, 3).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (2, 2, -1) and (3, -1, -2).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 9.487

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (-2, 2, -3) and (-5, 6, -4).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 19.99 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number 11 + 5i.
solution: Given: a = 11, b = 5 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((11)^2 + (5)^2) | Answer: 12.08

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number -1 + 7i.
solution: Given: a = -1, b = 7 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(7, -1) | Answer: 98.13 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -5x^3 - 2x^2 - x + 4 at x = -5.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-97 with initial guess x0=4, find x1 (one iteration).
solution: Given: N = 97, x0 = 4 | Formula: x1 = x0 - (x0^2 - N)/(2 x0) | Substitute: x1 = 4 - ((4)^2 - 97)/(2*4) | Answer: 14.12

question: Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=0.9 and ordinates 16, 18, 7, 0, 17, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 545 and 95.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 545 and 95 | Answer: GCD = 5

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 55 and 63.
solution: Given: a = 55, b = 63 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 55*63 / 1 | Answer: 3465
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 60 mm carries an axial tensile load of 62 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 34 mm and length 2600 mm carries an axial load of 32 kN. Take E = 70 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 48 mm transmits a torque of 500 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 48, Tt = 500 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(500*1000) / (pi*(48)^3) | Answer: 23.03 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 52 mm and length 500 mm carries a torque of 1650 N-m. With G = 80 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (52)^4 / 32 = 717816 mm^4 | theta = (1650*1000)(500) / (80000 * 717816) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 0.8231 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 56 mm wide and 150 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 56, h = 150 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 56*(150)^2 / 6 | Answer: 210000 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (74 mm x 260 mm) carries a bending moment of 28 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (36 mm x 100 mm) has effective length 1700 mm and E = 200 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 740 MPa is designed for a working stress of 130 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 740, sw = 130 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 740 / 130 | Answer: 5.692

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1250 mm and wall thickness 13 mm carries an internal pressure of 2.3 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1250, t = 13, P = 2.3 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 2.3*1250 / (2*13) | Answer: 110.6 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 1040 K and 320 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 1040, Tc = 320 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 320/1040) * 100 | Answer: 69.23 %

question: A refrigerator works between 273 K (cold) and 312 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 273, Th = 312 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 273 / (312 - 273) | Answer: 7

question: A heat pump operates between 266 K and 334 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 266, Th = 334 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 334 / (334 - 266) | Answer: 4.912

question: 6.3 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 190 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 6.3, dT = 190 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 6.3 * 0.718 * 190 | Answer: 859.4 kJ

question: 2 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 145 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2, dT = 145 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 2 * 1.005 * 145 | Answer: 291.4 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 3.2 m^3 at 340 K with mass 4.8 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 3.2, Tk = 340, m = 4.8 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 4.8*0.287*340 / 3.2 | Answer: 146.4 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 1.1 kg of air expands isothermally at 390 K from volume V1 to 4*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1.1, Tk = 390, ratio = 4 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 1.1*0.287*390*ln(4) | Answer: 170.7 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 4.7 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.24 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 4.7, D = 0.24 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*4.7*0.24 / 0.001 | Answer: 1128000

question: Water flows at 1.4 m/s through a pipe of diameter 180 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 4.4 m. Taking Cv = 0.97, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 4.4, cv = 0.97 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.97*sqrt(2*9.81*4.4) | Answer: 9.013 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 340 mm) water flows at 1 m/s. It contracts to diameter 50 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 340, d2 = 50, V1 = 1 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 1*(340/50)^2 | Answer: 46.24 m/s

question: Water flows at 1.3 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.33 m and length 400 m. With friction factor f = 0.036, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 40 teeth drives a gear of 73 teeth. If the pinion runs at 850 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 40, z2 = 73, N1 = 850 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 850*40 / 73 | Answer: 465.8 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 160 mm rotates at 1200 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 160, N = 1200 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.16)*1200 / 60 | Answer: 10.05 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 12.6 kW at 500 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 12.6, N = 500 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(12.6*1000) / (2*pi*500) | Answer: 240.6 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 1.9 kg rotates at radius 0.45 m at 250 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 1400 N/m and mass 9.3 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 1400, m = 9.3 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(1400/9.3) | Answer: 1.953 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 7.5 m^2 and thickness 0.16 m has conductivity k = 7.5 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 80 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 7.5, L = 0.16, k = 7.5, dT = 80 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 7.5*7.5*80 / 0.16 | Answer: 28125 W

question: A surface of area 4.1 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 130 W/m^2-K to surroundings 130 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 4.1, h = 130, dT = 130 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 130*4.1*130 | Answer: 69290 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 240 m/min, feed = 0.36 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2.8 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 240, f = 0.36, d = 2.8 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*240*0.36*2.8 | Answer: 241920 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 440 mm is turned at 1150 rpm with a feed of 0.1 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 440, N = 1150, f = 0.1 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 440 / (0.1*1150) | Answer: 3.826 min

question: A resistor of 156 ohm carries a current of 6.4 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 156, I = 6.4 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 6.4 * 156 | Answer: 998.4 V

question: Three resistors 30 ohm, 48 ohm and 35 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 30, R2 = 48, R3 = 35 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 30 + 48 + 35 | Answer: 113 ohm

question: Two resistors 55 ohm and 85 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 55, R2 = 85 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 55*85 / (55+85) | Answer: 33.39 ohm

question: A device draws 5.4 A at 240 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 240, I = 5.4 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 240 * 5.4 | Answer: 1296 W

question: A current of 8.4 A flows through a 59 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 8.4, R = 59 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (8.4)^2 * 59 | Answer: 4163 W

question: Two capacitors 12.5 uF and 9.2 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 12.5, C2 = 9.2 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 12.5*9.2 / (12.5+9.2) | Answer: 5.3 uF

question: A resistor 83 kohm and capacitor 6.3 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 83, C = 6.3 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (83k)(6.3u) = 522.9 ms | Answer: 522.9 ms

question: An inductor 26.4 mH is in series with 8 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 26.4, R = 8 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (26.4e-3) / 8 | Answer: 3.3 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 188.2 mH inductor at 690 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 188.2, f = 690 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (690)(188.2e-3) | Answer: 815.9 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 21.6 uF capacitor at 470 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 21.6, f = 470 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (470)(21.6e-6)) | Answer: 15.68 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 58 ohm, XL = 116 ohm and XC = 121 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 58, XL = 116, XC = 121 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(58^2 + (116 - 121)^2) | Answer: 58.22 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 51.7 mH and C = 8.8 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 51.7, C = 8.8 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(51.7e-3 * 8.8e-6)) | Answer: 236 Hz

question: A capacitor of 30.1 uF is charged to 120 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 30.1, V = 120 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*30.1e-6*(120)^2 | Answer: 216.7 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 440 V with 340 primary turns and 60 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 440, N1 = 340, N2 = 60 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 440 * 60/340 | Answer: 77.65 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 200 V and draws an armature current of 28 A. If the armature resistance is 0.8 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 200, Ia = 28, Ra = 0.8 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 200 - 28*0.8 | Answer: 177.6 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 140 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.75. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 140, VL = 400, pf = 0.75 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*400*140*0.75 / 1000 | Answer: 72.75 kW

question: A load has real power 20 kW and apparent power 85 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 20, S = 85 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 20 / 85 | Answer: 0.2353

question: A machine delivers 110 kW output while drawing 167 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 110, Pi = 167 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 110/167 * 100 | Answer: 65.87 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 8 V across R1 = 18 ohm and R2 = 38 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 8, R1 = 18, R2 = 38 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 8*38 / (18+38) | Answer: 5.429 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 10 kohm and Rin = 38 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 10, Rin = 38 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 10 / 38 | Answer: 0.2632

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 20 kohm and Rg = 10 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 20, Rg = 10 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 20/10 | Answer: 3

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 3241. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 3241 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(3241) | Answer: 35.11 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.7 m carries a central point load of 50 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6.7, W = 50 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 50*6.7 / 4 | Answer: 83.75 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 9 m carries a UDL of 30 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 9, w = 30 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 30*(9)^2 / 8 | Answer: 303.8 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 3.4 m carries a point load 30 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.4, W = 30 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 30*3.4 | Answer: 102 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 5.5 m carries a UDL of 16 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.5, w = 16 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 16*(5.5)^2 / 2 | Answer: 242 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 5.7 m carries a point load 80 kN at distance 1.4 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 5.7, a = 1.4, W = 80 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 80*(5.7 - 1.4) / 5.7 | Answer: 60.35 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 3.7 m) carries a central point load 25 kN. With E = 200 GPa and I = 270e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=25000 N, L=3700.0 mm, E=200000 MPa, I=270e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 0.4886 mm

question: An RC beam has overall depth 510 mm, clear cover 25 mm and main bars of diameter 20 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 510, c = 25, dia = 20 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 510 - 25 - 20/2 | Answer: 475 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 20.3 m^2 carrying a factored load of 14.5 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 20.3, w = 14.5 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 14.5 * 20.3 | Answer: 294.4 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 7 m, unit weight 19 kN/m^3, phi = 34 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 9 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 21 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 9, g = 21 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (21 - 9.81)*9 | Answer: 100.7 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 1.6e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1.4, area = 2.5e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 1.6, i = 1.4, A = 2.5 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (1.6e-4)*1.4*(2.5e-3) | Answer: 560 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.9 m, bed slope 0.005 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.013. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 2.1 m under a head of 0.7 m. Taking Cd = 0.64 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 2.1 m wide carries a discharge of 3.7 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 260 m and design speed 60 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 260, V = 60 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (60)^2 / (127*260) | Answer: 0.109
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: A tank of volume 560 m^3 treats a flow of 85 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 560, Q = 85 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 560 / 85 | Answer: 6.588 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 320 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.31 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 7 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 320, k = 0.31, t = 7 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 320*(1 - e^(-0.31*7)) | Answer: 283.5 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.88, rainfall intensity 40 mm/h over a catchment of 59 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.88, i = 40, A = 59 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.88*40*59 / 360 | Answer: 5.769 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.06 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 320 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.06, M = 320 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 320*(20+0.06)/20 | Answer: 321 m

question: Convert the decimal number 2799 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 2799 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: AEF (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 01011001 and 00001011.
solution: XOR: 01010010 | Count of 1s = 3 | Answer: 3
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 200 megabits is sent over a link of 36 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 200, B = 36 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 200 / 36 | Answer: 5.556 s

question: A link has bandwidth 30 Mbps and round-trip time 170 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 30, R = 170 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 30e6 * 170e-3 bits = 5100 kb | Answer: 5100 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.95, cache access time 8 ns and main-memory access time 160 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.95, tc = 8, tm = 160 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.95*8 + (1 - 0.95)*160 | Answer: 15.6 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 444125 elements?
solution: Given: n = 444125 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(444125)) + 1 | Answer: 19

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.006, memory access time 110 ns and page-fault service time 3 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 3 ms = 3000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.006)*110 + 0.006*3000000.0 ns | Answer: 18.11 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 2.5 m^3 at 360 kPa and 570 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 2.5, P = 360, Tk = 570 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (360e3)*2.5 / (8.314*570) | Answer: 189.9 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.18 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 17 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.18, t = 17 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.18*17) | Answer: 0.9531

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.26 /min) reaches 50% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.26, X = 50 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.5 / (0.26*(1 - 0.5)) | Answer: 3.846 min

question: For a reaction with A = 6e10 /s and activation energy 75 kJ/mol at 450 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 6, Ea = 75, Tk = 450 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 6e10 * exp(-75e3 / (8.314*450)) | Answer: 118 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.97 and bottoms xW = 0.04, with relative volatility alpha = 2.4. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.97, xw = 0.04, al = 2.4 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.97/0.03)(0.96/0.04)] / ln(2.4) | Answer: 7.601 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.87 and x = 0.48. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.87, x = 0.48 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.87/0.13) / (0.48/0.52) | Answer: 7.25

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.57 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 70 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.57, Psat = 70 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.57 * 70 | Answer: 39.9 kPa

question: A stream of 6.2 kg/s with specific heat 1.5 kJ/kg-K is heated through 55 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 6.2, cp = 1.5, dT = 55 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 6.2*1.5*55 | Answer: 511.5 kW

question: A reactor of volume 15 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 1 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 15, Q = 1 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 15 / 1 | Answer: 15 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 7e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 4 mm with a concentration difference of 70 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 7, L = 4, dC = 70 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (7e-9)*70 / (4e-3) | Answer: 122.5 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 7.6 min and steady-state gain 3.4. For a step input of magnitude 16, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 7.6, K = 3.4, M = 16 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 3.4 * 16 | Answer: 54.4 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 120 m^2 flies at 60 m/s (air density 0.4 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.7. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 120, V = 60, rho = 0.4, CL = 0.7 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.4*(60)^2*120*0.7 / 1000 | Answer: 60.48 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 70 m^2 flies at 90 m/s (density 1 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.12. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 70, V = 90, rho = 1, CD = 0.12 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*1*(90)^2*70*0.12 / 1000 | Answer: 34.02 kN

question: A specimen under stress 140 MPa shows an elastic strain of 1.3e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 140, eps = 1.3 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 140 / (1.3e-3) MPa = 107.7 GPa | Answer: 107.7 GPa

question: A block of mass 46 kg has a volume of 5.6e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 46, V = 5.6 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 46 / (5.6e-3) | Answer: 8214 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 1000 mm is heated through 25 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 17e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 1000, dT = 25, al = 17 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 1000*17e-6*25 | Answer: 0.425 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 190 ohm, R2 = 80 ohm and R3 = 15 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 190, R2 = 80, R3 = 15 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 80*15 / 190 | Answer: 6.316 ohm

question: A measurement reads 10.43 when the true value is 20. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10.43, true = 20 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10.43 - 20| / 20 * 100 | Answer: 47.85 %

question: Annual demand is 13000 units, ordering cost 210 per order and holding cost 32 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 13000, S = 210, H = 32 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*13000*210 / 32) | Answer: 413.1 units

question: An asset costs 240000 with salvage value 32000 after 9 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 240000, Sv = 32000, n = 9 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (240000 - 32000) / 9 | Answer: 23111 per year

question: A product sells for 290 per unit with variable cost 30 per unit and fixed costs 65000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 290, V = 30, F = 65000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 65000 / (290 - 30) | Answer: 250 units

question: Find the present worth of 15000 received 9 years from now at an interest rate of 8% per year.
solution: Given: F = 15000, n = 9, i = 8 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 15000 / (1 + 0.08)^9 | Answer: 7504 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.96, 0.93 and 0.97 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.96, r2 = 0.93, r3 = 0.97 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.96*0.93*0.97 | Answer: 0.866

question: A process produces 25 defective items in a batch of 17000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 25, N = 17000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 25/17000 * 1e6 | Answer: 1471 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -x^3 + 7x^2 + 2x - 3 evaluated at x = 3.
For f(x) = 6x^3 - 6x^2 - 3x + 8, find f''(x) at x = -2.
Evaluate the definite integral of (5x^2 - 4x) dx from x = -4 to x = 4.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = 5x^3/3 + -4x^2/2 + 0x | Evaluate F(4) - F(-4) | Answer: 213.3
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 2x^2 - 10x - 1 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[4, -4], [4, 0]].
solution: Given: a = 4, b = -4, c = 4, d = 0 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (4)(0) - (-4)(4) | Answer: 16

question: Find the determinant of [[2, 1, 3], [-3, -2, -2], [-4, -4, -1]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: 5

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[5, 1], [0, -6]].
solution: Trace tr = -1, Determinant = -30 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 5

question: Solve for x: -4x + 6y = 5 and 4x + 5y = 8.
solution: Determinant = -4*5 - 6*4 = -44 | x = (e d - b f) / det = 0.5227 | Answer: x = 0.5227
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 89, 81, 99, 6, 27.
solution: Sum = 302 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 60.4 | Answer: 60.4

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 29, 45, 33, 13, 24.
solution: Mean = 28.8 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 11.76

question: Find the slope of the line through (9, -7) and (2, 1).
solution: Given: x1 = 9, y1 = -7, x2 = 2, y2 = 1 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (1 - -7) / (2 - 9) | Answer: -1.143

question: Find the distance between the points (-8, 5) and (-9, -2).
solution: Given: x1 = -8, y1 = 5, x2 = -9, y2 = -2 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-1)^2 + (-7)^2) | Answer: 7.071 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (5,-3), (1,1), (0,-4).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 12 sq units

question: Find the 14th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 7 and common difference -3.
solution: Given: a = 7, d = -3, n = 14 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = 7 + (14 - 1)*-3 | Answer: -32

question: Find the sum of the first 30 terms of an AP with first term 12 and common difference -1.
solution: Given: a = 12, d = -1, n = 30 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 30/2 [2*12 + (30-1)*-1] | Answer: -75

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 23500 at 5.1% per annum for 2 years.
solution: Given: P = 23500, R = 5.1, Tt = 2 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 23500 * 5.1 * 2 / 100 | Answer: 2397 currency units

question: Find the amount when 27500 is invested at 9% per annum compounded annually for 5 years.
solution: Given: P = 27500, R = 9, Tt = 5 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 27500 * (1 + 9/100)^5 | Answer: 42312 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (-4, -3, 1) and (-7, -5, -6).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (-4, 0, -2) and (6, 3, -4).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 31.05

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (5, 2, -1) and (-1, 3, -1).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 83.68 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number -1 + -10i.
solution: Given: a = -1, b = -10 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((-1)^2 + (-10)^2) | Answer: 10.05

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number -8 + -10i.
solution: Given: a = -8, b = -10 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(-10, -8) | Answer: -128.7 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -4x^3 + 7x^2 + 6x - 1 at x = 0.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-173 with initial guess x0=11, find x1 (one iteration).
