question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 66 and 46.
solution: Given: a = 66, b = 46 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 66*46 / 2 | Answer: 1518
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 46 mm carries an axial tensile load of 40 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 18 mm and length 1400 mm carries an axial load of 37 kN. Take E = 70 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 22 mm transmits a torque of 1100 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 22, Tt = 1100 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(1100*1000) / (pi*(22)^3) | Answer: 526.1 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 37 mm and length 1800 mm carries a torque of 900 N-m. With G = 45 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (37)^4 / 32 = 183995 mm^4 | theta = (900*1000)(1800) / (45000 * 183995) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 11.21 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 78 mm wide and 90 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 78, h = 90 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 78*(90)^2 / 6 | Answer: 105300 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (51 mm x 190 mm) carries a bending moment of 37 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (67 mm x 150 mm) has effective length 3400 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 670 MPa is designed for a working stress of 140 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 670, sw = 140 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 670 / 140 | Answer: 4.786

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1450 mm and wall thickness 9 mm carries an internal pressure of 2 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1450, t = 9, P = 2 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 2*1450 / (2*9) | Answer: 161.1 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 1160 K and 300 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 1160, Tc = 300 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 300/1160) * 100 | Answer: 74.14 %

question: A heat pump operates between 276 K and 304 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 276, Th = 304 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 304 / (304 - 276) | Answer: 10.86

question: 6.3 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 35 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 6.3, dT = 35 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 6.3 * 0.718 * 35 | Answer: 158.3 kJ

question: 6 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 65 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 6, dT = 65 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 6 * 1.005 * 65 | Answer: 391.9 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 2.4 m^3 at 490 K with mass 5.8 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 2.4, Tk = 490, m = 5.8 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 5.8*0.287*490 / 2.4 | Answer: 339.9 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 2.1 kg of air expands isothermally at 380 K from volume V1 to 5*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.1, Tk = 380, ratio = 5 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 2.1*0.287*380*ln(5) | Answer: 368.6 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 2.4 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.33 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 2.4, D = 0.33 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*2.4*0.33 / 0.001 | Answer: 792000

question: Water flows at 0.7 m/s through a pipe of diameter 70 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 7.2 m. Taking Cv = 0.97, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 7.2, cv = 0.97 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.97*sqrt(2*9.81*7.2) | Answer: 11.53 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 360 mm) water flows at 1.5 m/s. It contracts to diameter 90 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 360, d2 = 90, V1 = 1.5 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 1.5*(360/90)^2 | Answer: 24 m/s

question: Water flows at 2 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.35 m and length 220 m. With friction factor f = 0.031, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 26 teeth drives a gear of 93 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1450 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 26, z2 = 93, N1 = 1450 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1450*26 / 93 | Answer: 405.4 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 450 mm rotates at 400 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 450, N = 400 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.45)*400 / 60 | Answer: 9.425 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 15.8 kW at 1000 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 15.8, N = 1000 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(15.8*1000) / (2*pi*1000) | Answer: 150.9 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 9.6 kg rotates at radius 0.24 m at 850 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 5700 N/m and mass 8.3 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 5700, m = 8.3 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(5700/8.3) | Answer: 4.171 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 9.2 m^2 and thickness 0.3 m has conductivity k = 35.6 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 160 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 9.2, L = 0.3, k = 35.6, dT = 160 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 35.6*9.2*160 / 0.3 | Answer: 174677 W

question: A surface of area 3.7 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 50 W/m^2-K to surroundings 140 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 3.7, h = 50, dT = 140 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 50*3.7*140 | Answer: 25900 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 60 m/min, feed = 0.23 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2.4 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 60, f = 0.23, d = 2.4 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*60*0.23*2.4 | Answer: 33120 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 490 mm is turned at 1050 rpm with a feed of 0.18 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 490, N = 1050, f = 0.18 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 490 / (0.18*1050) | Answer: 2.593 min

question: A resistor of 24 ohm carries a current of 0.2 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 24, I = 0.2 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 0.2 * 24 | Answer: 4.8 V

question: Three resistors 33 ohm, 35 ohm and 78 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 33, R2 = 35, R3 = 78 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 33 + 35 + 78 | Answer: 146 ohm

question: Two resistors 6 ohm and 63 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 6, R2 = 63 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 6*63 / (6+63) | Answer: 5.478 ohm

question: A device draws 8.5 A at 230 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 230, I = 8.5 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 230 * 8.5 | Answer: 1955 W

question: A current of 9.6 A flows through a 147 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 9.6, R = 147 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (9.6)^2 * 147 | Answer: 13548 W

question: Two capacitors 23 uF and 6.5 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 23, C2 = 6.5 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 23*6.5 / (23+6.5) | Answer: 5.068 uF

question: A resistor 64 kohm and capacitor 5.2 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 64, C = 5.2 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (64k)(5.2u) = 332.8 ms | Answer: 332.8 ms

question: An inductor 426.5 mH is in series with 177 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 426.5, R = 177 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (426.5e-3) / 177 | Answer: 2.41 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 181.9 mH inductor at 90 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 181.9, f = 90 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (90)(181.9e-3) | Answer: 102.9 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 2.1 uF capacitor at 280 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 2.1, f = 280 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (280)(2.1e-6)) | Answer: 270.7 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 90 ohm, XL = 63 ohm and XC = 111 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 90, XL = 63, XC = 111 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(90^2 + (63 - 111)^2) | Answer: 102 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 38.2 mH and C = 8.9 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 38.2, C = 8.9 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(38.2e-3 * 8.9e-6)) | Answer: 273 Hz

question: A capacitor of 34.9 uF is charged to 85 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 34.9, V = 85 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*34.9e-6*(85)^2 | Answer: 126.1 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 250 V with 360 primary turns and 370 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 250, N1 = 360, N2 = 370 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 250 * 370/360 | Answer: 256.9 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 290 V and draws an armature current of 52 A. If the armature resistance is 1.16 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 290, Ia = 52, Ra = 1.16 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 290 - 52*1.16 | Answer: 229.7 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 15 A at 415 V (line) with a power factor of 0.84. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 15, VL = 415, pf = 0.84 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*415*15*0.84 / 1000 | Answer: 9.057 kW

question: A load has real power 95 kW and apparent power 120 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 95, S = 120 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 95 / 120 | Answer: 0.7917

question: A machine delivers 75 kW output while drawing 127 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 75, Pi = 127 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 75/127 * 100 | Answer: 59.06 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 30 V across R1 = 23 ohm and R2 = 34 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 30, R1 = 23, R2 = 34 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 30*34 / (23+34) | Answer: 17.89 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 30 kohm and Rin = 3 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 30, Rin = 3 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 30 / 3 | Answer: 10

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 130 kohm and Rg = 32 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 130, Rg = 32 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 130/32 | Answer: 5.062

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 8316. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 8316 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(8316) | Answer: 39.2 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 5.4 m carries a central point load of 35 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.4, W = 35 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 35*5.4 / 4 | Answer: 47.25 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 5.5 m carries a UDL of 10 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.5, w = 10 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 10*(5.5)^2 / 8 | Answer: 37.81 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 4.2 m carries a point load 65 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.2, W = 65 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 65*4.2 | Answer: 273 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 4.5 m carries a UDL of 30 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.5, w = 30 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 30*(4.5)^2 / 2 | Answer: 303.8 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 8.2 m carries a point load 100 kN at distance 1.6 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 8.2, a = 1.6, W = 100 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 100*(8.2 - 1.6) / 8.2 | Answer: 80.49 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 5.6 m) carries a central point load 30 kN. With E = 25 GPa and I = 420e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=30000 N, L=5600.0 mm, E=25000 MPa, I=420e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 10.45 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 9 m carries a UDL of 30 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 9, w = 30 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 30*(9)^2 / 12 | Answer: 202.5 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 520 mm, clear cover 25 mm and main bars of diameter 20 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 520, c = 25, dia = 20 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 520 - 25 - 20/2 | Answer: 485 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 21.4 m^2 carrying a factored load of 18.6 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 21.4, w = 18.6 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 18.6 * 21.4 | Answer: 398 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 4.1 m, unit weight 20 kN/m^3, phi = 30 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 10.4 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 20 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 10.4, g = 20 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (20 - 9.81)*10.4 | Answer: 106 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 1.1e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.5, area = 2.8e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 1.1, i = 0.5, A = 2.8 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (1.1e-4)*0.5*(2.8e-3) | Answer: 154 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.5 m, bed slope 0.006 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.019. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 4.3 m under a head of 1.1 m. Taking Cd = 0.64 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 4.4 m wide carries a discharge of 5.2 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 310 m and design speed 55 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 310, V = 55 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (55)^2 / (127*310) | Answer: 0.07684
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: A tank of volume 860 m^3 treats a flow of 90 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 860, Q = 90 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 860 / 90 | Answer: 9.556 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 220 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.27 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 5 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 220, k = 0.27, t = 5 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 220*(1 - e^(-0.27*5)) | Answer: 163 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.36, rainfall intensity 80 mm/h over a catchment of 16.1 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.36, i = 80, A = 16.1 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.36*80*16.1 / 360 | Answer: 1.288 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.07 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 190 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.07, M = 190 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 190*(20+0.07)/20 | Answer: 190.7 m

question: Convert the decimal number 1881 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 1881 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 759 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 10001001 and 00101110.
solution: XOR: 10100111 | Count of 1s = 5 | Answer: 5
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 130 megabits is sent over a link of 13 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 130, B = 13 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 130 / 13 | Answer: 10 s

question: A link has bandwidth 13 Mbps and round-trip time 120 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 13, R = 120 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 13e6 * 120e-3 bits = 1560 kb | Answer: 1560 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.97, cache access time 5 ns and main-memory access time 100 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.97, tc = 5, tm = 100 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.97*5 + (1 - 0.97)*100 | Answer: 7.85 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 560579 elements?
solution: Given: n = 560579 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(560579)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.019, memory access time 160 ns and page-fault service time 9 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 9 ms = 9000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.019)*160 + 0.019*9000000.0 ns | Answer: 171.2 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 2.8 m^3 at 480 kPa and 600 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 2.8, P = 480, Tk = 600 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (480e3)*2.8 / (8.314*600) | Answer: 269.4 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.16 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 16 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.16, t = 16 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.16*16) | Answer: 0.9227

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.43 /min) reaches 80% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.43, X = 80 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.8 / (0.43*(1 - 0.8)) | Answer: 9.302 min

question: For a reaction with A = 9e10 /s and activation energy 80 kJ/mol at 410 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 9, Ea = 80, Tk = 410 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 9e10 * exp(-80e3 / (8.314*410)) | Answer: 5.778 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.96 and bottoms xW = 0.06, with relative volatility alpha = 2.4. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.96, xw = 0.06, al = 2.4 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.96/0.04)(0.94/0.06)] / ln(2.4) | Answer: 6.773 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.8 and x = 0.36. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.8, x = 0.36 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.8/0.2) / (0.36/0.64) | Answer: 7.111

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.25 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 50 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.25, Psat = 50 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.25 * 50 | Answer: 12.5 kPa

question: A stream of 4.3 kg/s with specific heat 1.4 kJ/kg-K is heated through 70 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 4.3, cp = 1.4, dT = 70 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 4.3*1.4*70 | Answer: 421.4 kW

question: A reactor of volume 14.1 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 0.5 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 14.1, Q = 0.5 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 14.1 / 0.5 | Answer: 28.2 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 7.4e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 5 mm with a concentration difference of 140 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 7.4, L = 5, dC = 140 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (7.4e-9)*140 / (5e-3) | Answer: 207.2 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 1.3 min and steady-state gain 3.6. For a step input of magnitude 12, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 1.3, K = 3.6, M = 12 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 3.6 * 12 | Answer: 43.2 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 105 m^2 flies at 80 m/s (air density 0.7 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.6. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 105, V = 80, rho = 0.7, CL = 0.6 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.7*(80)^2*105*0.6 / 1000 | Answer: 141.1 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 20 m^2 flies at 70 m/s (density 1 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.12. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 20, V = 70, rho = 1, CD = 0.12 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*1*(70)^2*20*0.12 / 1000 | Answer: 5.88 kN

question: A specimen under stress 90 MPa shows an elastic strain of 0.8e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 90, eps = 0.8 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 90 / (0.8e-3) MPa = 112.5 GPa | Answer: 112.5 GPa

question: A block of mass 14 kg has a volume of 4.7e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 14, V = 4.7 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 14 / (4.7e-3) | Answer: 2979 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 800 mm is heated through 150 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 11e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 800, dT = 150, al = 11 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 800*11e-6*150 | Answer: 1.32 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 45 ohm, R2 = 115 ohm and R3 = 225 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 45, R2 = 115, R3 = 225 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 115*225 / 45 | Answer: 575 ohm

question: A measurement reads 9.77 when the true value is 100. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.77, true = 100 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.77 - 100| / 100 * 100 | Answer: 90.23 %

question: Annual demand is 46500 units, ordering cost 50 per order and holding cost 13 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 46500, S = 50, H = 13 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*46500*50 / 13) | Answer: 598.1 units

question: An asset costs 390000 with salvage value 28000 after 18 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 390000, Sv = 28000, n = 18 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (390000 - 28000) / 18 | Answer: 20111 per year

question: A product sells for 90 per unit with variable cost 50 per unit and fixed costs 105000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 90, V = 50, F = 105000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 105000 / (90 - 50) | Answer: 2625 units

question: Find the present worth of 95000 received 3 years from now at an interest rate of 6% per year.
solution: Given: F = 95000, n = 3, i = 6 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 95000 / (1 + 0.06)^3 | Answer: 79764 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.93, 0.97 and 0.91 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.93, r2 = 0.97, r3 = 0.91 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.93*0.97*0.91 | Answer: 0.8209

question: A process produces 42 defective items in a batch of 15500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 42, N = 15500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 42/15500 * 1e6 | Answer: 271 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = 4x^3 - 6x^2 - 8x + 1 evaluated at x = 5.
For f(x) = 4x^3 + 8x^2 - 3x + 4, find f''(x) at x = 3.
Evaluate the definite integral of (x + 4) dx from x = -2 to x = 6.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = 0x^3/3 + 1x^2/2 + 4x | Evaluate F(6) - F(-2) | Answer: 48
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 3x^2 - 3x - 11 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[7, 0], [-9, -6]].
solution: Given: a = 7, b = 0, c = -9, d = -6 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (7)(-6) - (0)(-9) | Answer: -42

question: Find the determinant of [[-5, 5, 5], [4, -3, 2], [-4, 1, -2]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: -60

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[-4, 7], [7, -2]].
solution: Trace tr = -6, Determinant = -41 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 4.071

question: Solve for x: 5x + 5y = 9 and 0x + 4y = 12.
solution: Determinant = 5*4 - 5*0 = 20 | x = (e d - b f) / det = -1.2 | Answer: x = -1.2
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 88, 73, 94, 18, 13.
solution: Sum = 286 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 57.2 | Answer: 57.2

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 44, 21, 11, 27, 31.
solution: Mean = 26.8 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 12.21

question: Find the slope of the line through (-2, 3) and (9, 9).
solution: Given: x1 = -2, y1 = 3, x2 = 9, y2 = 9 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (9 - 3) / (9 - -2) | Answer: 0.5455

question: Find the distance between the points (-1, 2) and (1, -3).
solution: Given: x1 = -1, y1 = 2, x2 = 1, y2 = -3 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((2)^2 + (-5)^2) | Answer: 5.385 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (-2,-2), (3,4), (-8,5).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 35.5 sq units

question: Find the 26th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 14 and common difference 2.
solution: Given: a = 14, d = 2, n = 26 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = 14 + (26 - 1)*2 | Answer: 64

question: Find the sum of the first 35 terms of an AP with first term -15 and common difference -8.
Find the simple interest on a principal of 24000 at 5.1% per annum for 7 years.
solution: Given: P = 24000, R = 5.1, Tt = 7 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 24000 * 5.1 * 7 / 100 | Answer: 8568 currency units

question: Find the amount when 21000 is invested at 10.1% per annum compounded annually for 2 years.
solution: Given: P = 21000, R = 10.1, Tt = 2 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 21000 * (1 + 10.1/100)^2 | Answer: 25456 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (8, -1, -6) and (7, 3, 6).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (5, 0, -4) and (4, 5, -2).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 32.57

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (1, -3, -6) and (-2, 3, 2).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 145.3 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number 5 + -2i.
solution: Given: a = 5, b = -2 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((5)^2 + (-2)^2) | Answer: 5.385

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number 0 + -7i.
solution: Given: a = 0, b = -7 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(-7, 0) | Answer: -90 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = 5x^3 + 7x^2 - 4x + 2 at x = -2.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-151 with initial guess x0=14, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=0.9 and ordinates 2, 11, 4, 1, 14, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 377 and 170.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 377 and 170 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 65 and 27.
solution: Given: a = 65, b = 27 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 65*27 / 1 | Answer: 1755
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 10 mm carries an axial tensile load of 8 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 13 mm and length 1200 mm carries an axial load of 71 kN. Take E = 70 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 29 mm transmits a torque of 3000 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 29, Tt = 3000 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(3000*1000) / (pi*(29)^3) | Answer: 626.5 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 38 mm and length 1200 mm carries a torque of 1700 N-m. With G = 77 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (38)^4 / 32 = 204708 mm^4 | theta = (1700*1000)(1200) / (77000 * 204708) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 7.415 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 96 mm wide and 300 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 96, h = 300 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 96*(300)^2 / 6 | Answer: 1440000 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (69 mm x 170 mm) carries a bending moment of 28 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (57 mm x 100 mm) has effective length 1600 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 300 MPa is designed for a working stress of 230 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 300, sw = 230 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 300 / 230 | Answer: 1.304

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1100 mm and wall thickness 6 mm carries an internal pressure of 2.6 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1100, t = 6, P = 2.6 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 2.6*1100 / (2*6) | Answer: 238.3 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 820 K and 320 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 820, Tc = 320 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 320/820) * 100 | Answer: 60.98 %

question: A refrigerator works between 263 K (cold) and 308 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 263, Th = 308 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 263 / (308 - 263) | Answer: 5.844

question: A heat pump operates between 260 K and 334 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 260, Th = 334 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 334 / (334 - 260) | Answer: 4.514

question: 3.5 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 20 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.5, dT = 20 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 3.5 * 0.718 * 20 | Answer: 50.26 kJ

question: 2.3 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 190 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.3, dT = 190 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 2.3 * 1.005 * 190 | Answer: 439.2 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 0.8 m^3 at 470 K with mass 3.5 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 0.8, Tk = 470, m = 3.5 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 3.5*0.287*470 / 0.8 | Answer: 590.1 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 3.9 kg of air expands isothermally at 460 K from volume V1 to 2*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.9, Tk = 460, ratio = 2 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 3.9*0.287*460*ln(2) | Answer: 356.9 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 3.2 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.32 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 3.2, D = 0.32 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*3.2*0.32 / 0.001 | Answer: 1024000

question: Water flows at 0.9 m/s through a pipe of diameter 290 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 15.9 m. Taking Cv = 0.96, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 15.9, cv = 0.96 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.96*sqrt(2*9.81*15.9) | Answer: 16.96 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 330 mm) water flows at 2.9 m/s. It contracts to diameter 110 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 330, d2 = 110, V1 = 2.9 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 2.9*(330/110)^2 | Answer: 26.1 m/s

question: Water flows at 3.9 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.26 m and length 390 m. With friction factor f = 0.026, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 24 teeth drives a gear of 60 teeth. If the pinion runs at 400 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 24, z2 = 60, N1 = 400 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 400*24 / 60 | Answer: 160 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 400 mm rotates at 850 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 400, N = 850 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.4)*850 / 60 | Answer: 17.8 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 38.5 kW at 400 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 38.5, N = 400 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(38.5*1000) / (2*pi*400) | Answer: 919.1 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 5 kg rotates at radius 0.38 m at 550 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 10200 N/m and mass 18.5 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 10200, m = 18.5 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(10200/18.5) | Answer: 3.737 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 6.1 m^2 and thickness 0.29 m has conductivity k = 14.9 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 155 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 6.1, L = 0.29, k = 14.9, dT = 155 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 14.9*6.1*155 / 0.29 | Answer: 48579 W

question: A surface of area 5.2 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 15 W/m^2-K to surroundings 30 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 5.2, h = 15, dT = 30 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 15*5.2*30 | Answer: 2340 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 220 m/min, feed = 0.47 mm/rev, depth of cut = 1.1 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 220, f = 0.47, d = 1.1 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*220*0.47*1.1 | Answer: 113740 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 130 mm is turned at 350 rpm with a feed of 0.15 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 130, N = 350, f = 0.15 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 130 / (0.15*350) | Answer: 2.476 min

question: A resistor of 175 ohm carries a current of 2 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 175, I = 2 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 2 * 175 | Answer: 350 V

question: Three resistors 98 ohm, 33 ohm and 96 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 98, R2 = 33, R3 = 96 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 98 + 33 + 96 | Answer: 227 ohm

question: Two resistors 37 ohm and 53 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 37, R2 = 53 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 37*53 / (37+53) | Answer: 21.79 ohm

question: A device draws 0.4 A at 80 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 80, I = 0.4 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 80 * 0.4 | Answer: 32 W

question: A current of 0.5 A flows through a 4 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 0.5, R = 4 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (0.5)^2 * 4 | Answer: 1 W

question: Two capacitors 27.2 uF and 5.2 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 27.2, C2 = 5.2 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 27.2*5.2 / (27.2+5.2) | Answer: 4.365 uF

question: A resistor 100 kohm and capacitor 19.1 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 100, C = 19.1 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (100k)(19.1u) = 1910 ms | Answer: 1910 ms

question: An inductor 96.7 mH is in series with 113 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 96.7, R = 113 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (96.7e-3) / 113 | Answer: 0.8558 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 87.5 mH inductor at 560 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 87.5, f = 560 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (560)(87.5e-3) | Answer: 307.9 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 3.6 uF capacitor at 910 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 3.6, f = 910 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (910)(3.6e-6)) | Answer: 48.58 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 31 ohm, XL = 42 ohm and XC = 98 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 31, XL = 42, XC = 98 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(31^2 + (42 - 98)^2) | Answer: 64.01 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 4.3 mH and C = 7.8 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 4.3, C = 7.8 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(4.3e-3 * 7.8e-6)) | Answer: 869 Hz

question: A capacitor of 85.8 uF is charged to 395 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 85.8, V = 395 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*85.8e-6*(395)^2 | Answer: 6693 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 150 V with 290 primary turns and 350 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 150, N1 = 290, N2 = 350 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 150 * 350/290 | Answer: 181 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 360 V and draws an armature current of 11 A. If the armature resistance is 0.43 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 360, Ia = 11, Ra = 0.43 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 360 - 11*0.43 | Answer: 355.3 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 75 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.78. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 75, VL = 400, pf = 0.78 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*400*75*0.78 / 1000 | Answer: 40.53 kW

question: A load has real power 15 kW and apparent power 205 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 15, S = 205 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 15 / 205 | Answer: 0.07317

question: A machine delivers 40 kW output while drawing 77 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 40, Pi = 77 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 40/77 * 100 | Answer: 51.95 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 27 V across R1 = 27 ohm and R2 = 36 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 27, R1 = 27, R2 = 36 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 27*36 / (27+36) | Answer: 15.43 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 110 kohm and Rin = 38 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 110, Rin = 38 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 110 / 38 | Answer: 2.895

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 30 kohm and Rg = 24 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 30, Rg = 24 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 30/24 | Answer: 2.25

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 596. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 596 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(596) | Answer: 27.75 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 8.9 m carries a central point load of 45 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 8.9, W = 45 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 45*8.9 / 4 | Answer: 100.1 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.8 m carries a UDL of 60 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.8, w = 60 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 60*(4.8)^2 / 8 | Answer: 172.8 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 1.9 m carries a point load 10 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 1.9, W = 10 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 10*1.9 | Answer: 19 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 5.5 m carries a UDL of 8 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.5, w = 8 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 8*(5.5)^2 / 2 | Answer: 121 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 5.6 m carries a point load 75 kN at distance 3.9 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 5.6, a = 3.9, W = 75 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 75*(5.6 - 3.9) / 5.6 | Answer: 22.77 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 7.3 m) carries a central point load 15 kN. With E = 30 GPa and I = 240e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=15000 N, L=7300.0 mm, E=30000 MPa, I=240e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 16.88 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 7.8 m carries a UDL of 36 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7.8, w = 36 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 36*(7.8)^2 / 12 | Answer: 182.5 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 320 mm, clear cover 50 mm and main bars of diameter 12 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 320, c = 50, dia = 12 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 320 - 50 - 12/2 | Answer: 264 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 39.4 m^2 carrying a factored load of 14.8 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 39.4, w = 14.8 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 14.8 * 39.4 | Answer: 583.1 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 4.6 m, unit weight 16 kN/m^3, phi = 32 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 7.8e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1.3, area = 3.4e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 7.8, i = 1.3, A = 3.4 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (7.8e-4)*1.3*(3.4e-3) | Answer: 3448 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.9 m, bed slope 0.001 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.022. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 3.5 m under a head of 1.1 m. Taking Cd = 0.64 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 3.5 m wide carries a discharge of 10.6 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 320 m and design speed 45 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 320, V = 45 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (45)^2 / (127*320) | Answer: 0.04983
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: A tank of volume 710 m^3 treats a flow of 90 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 710, Q = 90 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 710 / 90 | Answer: 7.889 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 390 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.21 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 3 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 390, k = 0.21, t = 3 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 390*(1 - e^(-0.21*3)) | Answer: 182.3 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.8, rainfall intensity 55 mm/h over a catchment of 56.1 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.8, i = 55, A = 56.1 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.8*55*56.1 / 360 | Answer: 6.857 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.05 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 120 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.05, M = 120 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 120*(30+0.05)/30 | Answer: 120.2 m

question: Convert the decimal number 3000 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 3000 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: BB8 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 00110001 and 00010101.
solution: XOR: 00100100 | Count of 1s = 2 | Answer: 2
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 200 megabits is sent over a link of 35 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 200, B = 35 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 200 / 35 | Answer: 5.714 s

question: A link has bandwidth 72 Mbps and round-trip time 180 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 72, R = 180 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 72e6 * 180e-3 bits = 12960 kb | Answer: 12960 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.96, cache access time 2 ns and main-memory access time 130 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.96, tc = 2, tm = 130 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.96*2 + (1 - 0.96)*130 | Answer: 7.12 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 682113 elements?
solution: Given: n = 682113 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(682113)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.01, memory access time 180 ns and page-fault service time 7 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 7 ms = 7000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.01)*180 + 0.01*7000000.0 ns | Answer: 70.18 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 2.5 m^3 at 140 kPa and 560 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 2.5, P = 140, Tk = 560 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (140e3)*2.5 / (8.314*560) | Answer: 75.17 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.05 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 10 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.05, t = 10 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.05*10) | Answer: 0.3935

question: For a reaction with A = 2e10 /s and activation energy 85 kJ/mol at 490 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 2, Ea = 85, Tk = 490 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 2e10 * exp(-85e3 / (8.314*490)) | Answer: 17.36 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.99 and bottoms xW = 0.04, with relative volatility alpha = 3.3. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.99, xw = 0.04, al = 3.3 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.99/0.01)(0.96/0.04)] / ln(3.3) | Answer: 6.511 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.73 and x = 0.4. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.73, x = 0.4 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.73/0.27) / (0.4/0.6) | Answer: 4.056

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.59 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 55 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.59, Psat = 55 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.59 * 55 | Answer: 32.45 kPa

question: A stream of 5 kg/s with specific heat 1.4 kJ/kg-K is heated through 75 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 5, cp = 1.4, dT = 75 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 5*1.4*75 | Answer: 525 kW

question: A reactor of volume 19.1 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 3.7 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 19.1, Q = 3.7 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 19.1 / 3.7 | Answer: 5.162 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 1.6e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 5 mm with a concentration difference of 120 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 1.6, L = 5, dC = 120 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (1.6e-9)*120 / (5e-3) | Answer: 38.4 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 9 min and steady-state gain 2. For a step input of magnitude 13, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 9, K = 2, M = 13 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 2 * 13 | Answer: 26 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 55 m^2 flies at 150 m/s (air density 0.4 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.7. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 55, V = 150, rho = 0.4, CL = 0.7 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.4*(150)^2*55*0.7 / 1000 | Answer: 173.2 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 75 m^2 flies at 260 m/s (density 0.7 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.05. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 75, V = 260, rho = 0.7, CD = 0.05 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.7*(260)^2*75*0.05 / 1000 | Answer: 88.72 kN

question: A specimen under stress 320 MPa shows an elastic strain of 1.9e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 320, eps = 1.9 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 320 / (1.9e-3) MPa = 168.4 GPa | Answer: 168.4 GPa

question: A block of mass 33 kg has a volume of 5.5e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 33, V = 5.5 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 33 / (5.5e-3) | Answer: 6000 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 2000 mm is heated through 115 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 12e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 2000, dT = 115, al = 12 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 2000*12e-6*115 | Answer: 2.76 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 20 ohm, R2 = 75 ohm and R3 = 140 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 20, R2 = 75, R3 = 140 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 75*140 / 20 | Answer: 525 ohm

question: A strain gauge of resistance 1000 ohm and gauge factor 2 experiences a strain of 1700e-6. Find the change in resistance in milliohms.
solution: Given: R = 1000, GF = 2, eps = 1700 | Formula: dR = R * GF * strain | Substitute: dR = 1000*2*1700e-6 | Answer: 3400 milliohm

question: A measurement reads 9.63 when the true value is 20. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.63, true = 20 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.63 - 20| / 20 * 100 | Answer: 51.85 %

question: Annual demand is 46000 units, ordering cost 200 per order and holding cost 14 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 46000, S = 200, H = 14 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*46000*200 / 14) | Answer: 1146 units

question: An asset costs 80000 with salvage value 14000 after 7 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 80000, Sv = 14000, n = 7 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (80000 - 14000) / 7 | Answer: 9429 per year

question: A product sells for 380 per unit with variable cost 150 per unit and fixed costs 60000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 380, V = 150, F = 60000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 60000 / (380 - 150) | Answer: 260.9 units

question: Find the present worth of 30000 received 5 years from now at an interest rate of 6% per year.
solution: Given: F = 30000, n = 5, i = 6 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 30000 / (1 + 0.06)^5 | Answer: 22418 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.96, 0.91 and 0.97 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.96, r2 = 0.91, r3 = 0.97 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.96*0.91*0.97 | Answer: 0.8474

question: A process produces 26 defective items in a batch of 6500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 26, N = 6500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 26/6500 * 1e6 | Answer: 4000 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -3x^3 + x^2 - 2x - 6 evaluated at x = -5.
For f(x) = -4x^3 + 3x^2 - x - 6, find f''(x) at x = 2.
Evaluate the definite integral of (-x^2 - x + 4) dx from x = -4 to x = 5.
