question: A component of ultimate strength 500 MPa is designed for a working stress of 110 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 500, sw = 110 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 500 / 110 | Answer: 4.545

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1200 mm and wall thickness 18 mm carries an internal pressure of 2 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1200, t = 18, P = 2 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 2*1200 / (2*18) | Answer: 66.67 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 820 K and 430 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 820, Tc = 430 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 430/820) * 100 | Answer: 47.56 %

question: 7.8 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 110 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 7.8, dT = 110 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 7.8 * 0.718 * 110 | Answer: 616 kJ

question: 3.7 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 60 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.7, dT = 60 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 3.7 * 1.005 * 60 | Answer: 223.1 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 2.7 m^3 at 390 K with mass 3.1 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 2.7, Tk = 390, m = 3.1 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 3.1*0.287*390 / 2.7 | Answer: 128.5 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 4.5 kg of air expands isothermally at 420 K from volume V1 to 2*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.5, Tk = 420, ratio = 2 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 4.5*0.287*420*ln(2) | Answer: 376 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 3 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.21 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 3, D = 0.21 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*3*0.21 / 0.001 | Answer: 630000

question: Water flows at 3.2 m/s through a pipe of diameter 270 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 12.6 m. Taking Cv = 0.95, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 12.6, cv = 0.95 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.95*sqrt(2*9.81*12.6) | Answer: 14.94 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 220 mm) water flows at 2.2 m/s. It contracts to diameter 80 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 220, d2 = 80, V1 = 2.2 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 2.2*(220/80)^2 | Answer: 16.64 m/s

question: Water flows at 1.8 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.49 m and length 50 m. With friction factor f = 0.029, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 29 teeth drives a gear of 80 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1000 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 29, z2 = 80, N1 = 1000 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1000*29 / 80 | Answer: 362.5 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 110 mm rotates at 550 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 110, N = 550 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.11)*550 / 60 | Answer: 3.168 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 36.4 kW at 1100 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 36.4, N = 1100 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(36.4*1000) / (2*pi*1100) | Answer: 316 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 4.7 kg rotates at radius 0.38 m at 1150 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 3400 N/m and mass 11.5 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 3400, m = 11.5 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(3400/11.5) | Answer: 2.737 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 2.6 m^2 and thickness 0.33 m has conductivity k = 25.2 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 95 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 2.6, L = 0.33, k = 25.2, dT = 95 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 25.2*2.6*95 / 0.33 | Answer: 18862 W

question: A surface of area 5 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 150 W/m^2-K to surroundings 100 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 5, h = 150, dT = 100 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 150*5*100 | Answer: 75000 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 220 m/min, feed = 0.47 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2.8 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 220, f = 0.47, d = 2.8 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*220*0.47*2.8 | Answer: 289520 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 160 mm is turned at 900 rpm with a feed of 0.27 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 160, N = 900, f = 0.27 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 160 / (0.27*900) | Answer: 0.6584 min

question: A resistor of 144 ohm carries a current of 4.9 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 144, I = 4.9 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 4.9 * 144 | Answer: 705.6 V

question: Three resistors 53 ohm, 12 ohm and 13 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 53, R2 = 12, R3 = 13 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 53 + 12 + 13 | Answer: 78 ohm

question: Two resistors 80 ohm and 35 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 80, R2 = 35 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 80*35 / (80+35) | Answer: 24.35 ohm

question: A device draws 2 A at 205 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 205, I = 2 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 205 * 2 | Answer: 410 W

question: A current of 1.4 A flows through a 57 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 1.4, R = 57 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (1.4)^2 * 57 | Answer: 111.7 W

question: Two capacitors 38.2 uF and 22.7 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 38.2, C2 = 22.7 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 38.2*22.7 / (38.2+22.7) | Answer: 14.24 uF

question: A resistor 46 kohm and capacitor 19.2 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 46, C = 19.2 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (46k)(19.2u) = 883.2 ms | Answer: 883.2 ms

question: An inductor 271.6 mH is in series with 54 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 271.6, R = 54 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (271.6e-3) / 54 | Answer: 5.03 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 76.4 mH inductor at 890 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 76.4, f = 890 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (890)(76.4e-3) | Answer: 427.2 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 41.3 uF capacitor at 290 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 41.3, f = 290 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (290)(41.3e-6)) | Answer: 13.29 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 60 ohm, XL = 106 ohm and XC = 138 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 60, XL = 106, XC = 138 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(60^2 + (106 - 138)^2) | Answer: 68 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 64.2 mH and C = 8.2 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 64.2, C = 8.2 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(64.2e-3 * 8.2e-6)) | Answer: 219.4 Hz

question: A capacitor of 26.4 uF is charged to 10 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 26.4, V = 10 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*26.4e-6*(10)^2 | Answer: 1.32 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 360 V with 970 primary turns and 400 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 360, N1 = 970, N2 = 400 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 360 * 400/970 | Answer: 148.5 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 430 V and draws an armature current of 29 A. If the armature resistance is 0.93 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 430, Ia = 29, Ra = 0.93 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 430 - 29*0.93 | Answer: 403 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 40 A at 433 V (line) with a power factor of 0.98. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 40, VL = 433, pf = 0.98 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*433*40*0.98 / 1000 | Answer: 29.4 kW

question: A load has real power 170 kW and apparent power 210 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 170, S = 210 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 170 / 210 | Answer: 0.8095

question: A machine delivers 10 kW output while drawing 107 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 10, Pi = 107 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 10/107 * 100 | Answer: 9.346 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 28 V across R1 = 27 ohm and R2 = 36 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 28, R1 = 27, R2 = 36 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 28*36 / (27+36) | Answer: 16 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 100 kohm and Rin = 19 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 100, Rin = 19 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 100 / 19 | Answer: 5.263

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 110 kohm and Rg = 43 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 110, Rg = 43 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 110/43 | Answer: 3.558

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 1215. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 1215 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(1215) | Answer: 30.85 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 8.2 m carries a central point load of 50 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 8.2, W = 50 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 50*8.2 / 4 | Answer: 102.5 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.7 m carries a UDL of 35 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6.7, w = 35 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 35*(6.7)^2 / 8 | Answer: 196.4 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 3.3 m carries a point load 50 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.3, W = 50 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 50*3.3 | Answer: 165 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 3.4 m carries a UDL of 32 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.4, w = 32 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 32*(3.4)^2 / 2 | Answer: 185 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 7.4 m carries a point load 40 kN at distance 1.2 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 7.4, a = 1.2, W = 40 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 40*(7.4 - 1.2) / 7.4 | Answer: 33.51 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 3.1 m) carries a central point load 20 kN. With E = 200 GPa and I = 370e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=20000 N, L=3100.0 mm, E=200000 MPa, I=370e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 0.1677 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 7.5 m carries a UDL of 45 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7.5, w = 45 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 45*(7.5)^2 / 12 | Answer: 210.9 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 350 mm, clear cover 50 mm and main bars of diameter 12 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 350, c = 50, dia = 12 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 350 - 50 - 12/2 | Answer: 294 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 10.1 m^2 carrying a factored load of 10.4 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 10.1, w = 10.4 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 10.4 * 10.1 | Answer: 105 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 6.7 m, unit weight 18 kN/m^3, phi = 38 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 2.7 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 19 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 2.7, g = 19 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (19 - 9.81)*2.7 | Answer: 24.81 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 3.2e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.9, area = 7e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 3.2, i = 0.9, A = 7 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (3.2e-4)*0.9*(7e-3) | Answer: 2016 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.4 m, bed slope 0.003 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.026. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 2.9 m under a head of 1.1 m. Taking Cd = 0.64 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 3.9 m wide carries a discharge of 17.2 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 400 m and design speed 45 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 400, V = 45 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (45)^2 / (127*400) | Answer: 0.03986
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: A tank of volume 850 m^3 treats a flow of 55 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 850, Q = 55 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 850 / 55 | Answer: 15.45 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 150 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.29 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 7 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 150, k = 0.29, t = 7 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 150*(1 - e^(-0.29*7)) | Answer: 130.3 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.6, rainfall intensity 100 mm/h over a catchment of 36.3 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.6, i = 100, A = 36.3 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.6*100*36.3 / 360 | Answer: 6.05 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.02 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 480 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.02, M = 480 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 480*(20+0.02)/20 | Answer: 480.5 m

question: Convert the decimal number 987 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 987 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 3DB (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 00011011 and 01111011.
solution: XOR: 01100000 | Count of 1s = 2 | Answer: 2
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 340 megabits is sent over a link of 63 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 340, B = 63 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 340 / 63 | Answer: 5.397 s

question: A link has bandwidth 43 Mbps and round-trip time 170 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 43, R = 170 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 43e6 * 170e-3 bits = 7310 kb | Answer: 7310 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.92, cache access time 1 ns and main-memory access time 180 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.92, tc = 1, tm = 180 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.92*1 + (1 - 0.92)*180 | Answer: 15.32 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 34802 elements?
solution: Given: n = 34802 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(34802)) + 1 | Answer: 16

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.009, memory access time 130 ns and page-fault service time 9 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 9 ms = 9000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.009)*130 + 0.009*9000000.0 ns | Answer: 81.13 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 2.6 m^3 at 370 kPa and 320 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 2.6, P = 370, Tk = 320 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (370e3)*2.6 / (8.314*320) | Answer: 361.6 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.32 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 19 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.32, t = 19 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.32*19) | Answer: 0.9977

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.23 /min) is to reach 55% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.23, X = 55 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.55) / 0.23 | Answer: 3.472 min

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.5 /min) reaches 75% conversion in a CSTR. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.5, X = 75 | Formula: tau = X / (k (1 - X)) | Substitute: tau = 0.75 / (0.5*(1 - 0.75)) | Answer: 6 min

question: For a reaction with A = 6e10 /s and activation energy 55 kJ/mol at 460 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 6, Ea = 55, Tk = 460 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 6e10 * exp(-55e3 / (8.314*460)) | Answer: 34078 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.96 and bottoms xW = 0.08, with relative volatility alpha = 2.5. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.96, xw = 0.08, al = 2.5 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.96/0.04)(0.92/0.08)] / ln(2.5) | Answer: 6.134 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.55 and x = 0.43. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.55, x = 0.43 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.55/0.45) / (0.43/0.57) | Answer: 1.62

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.8 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 25 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.8, Psat = 25 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.8 * 25 | Answer: 20 kPa

question: A stream of 8.9 kg/s with specific heat 1.2 kJ/kg-K is heated through 75 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 8.9, cp = 1.2, dT = 75 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 8.9*1.2*75 | Answer: 801 kW

question: A reactor of volume 2 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 1.6 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 2, Q = 1.6 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 2 / 1.6 | Answer: 1.25 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 6.7e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 1 mm with a concentration difference of 110 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 6.7, L = 1, dC = 110 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (6.7e-9)*110 / (1e-3) | Answer: 737 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 8.5 min and steady-state gain 0.8. For a step input of magnitude 12, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 8.5, K = 0.8, M = 12 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 0.8 * 12 | Answer: 9.6 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 60 m^2 flies at 200 m/s (air density 1.225 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.7. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 60, V = 200, rho = 1.225, CL = 0.7 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1.225*(200)^2*60*0.7 / 1000 | Answer: 1029 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 60 m^2 flies at 260 m/s (density 1 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.07. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 60, V = 260, rho = 1, CD = 0.07 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*1*(260)^2*60*0.07 / 1000 | Answer: 142 kN

question: A specimen under stress 380 MPa shows an elastic strain of 2.2e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 380, eps = 2.2 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 380 / (2.2e-3) MPa = 172.7 GPa | Answer: 172.7 GPa

question: A block of mass 31 kg has a volume of 0.6e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 31, V = 0.6 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 31 / (0.6e-3) | Answer: 51667 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 2100 mm is heated through 130 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 12e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 2100, dT = 130, al = 12 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 2100*12e-6*130 | Answer: 3.276 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 120 ohm, R2 = 45 ohm and R3 = 465 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 120, R2 = 45, R3 = 465 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 45*465 / 120 | Answer: 174.4 ohm

question: A measurement reads 10.1 when the true value is 50. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10.1, true = 50 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10.1 - 50| / 50 * 100 | Answer: 79.8 %

question: Annual demand is 6000 units, ordering cost 270 per order and holding cost 22 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 6000, S = 270, H = 22 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*6000*270 / 22) | Answer: 383.8 units

question: An asset costs 140000 with salvage value 40000 after 13 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 140000, Sv = 40000, n = 13 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (140000 - 40000) / 13 | Answer: 7692 per year

question: A product sells for 410 per unit with variable cost 40 per unit and fixed costs 100000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 410, V = 40, F = 100000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 100000 / (410 - 40) | Answer: 270.3 units

question: Find the present worth of 100000 received 6 years from now at an interest rate of 5% per year.
solution: Given: F = 100000, n = 6, i = 5 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 100000 / (1 + 0.05)^6 | Answer: 74622 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.99, 0.96 and 0.98 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.99, r2 = 0.96, r3 = 0.98 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.99*0.96*0.98 | Answer: 0.9314

question: A process produces 50 defective items in a batch of 8500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 50, N = 8500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 50/8500 * 1e6 | Answer: 5882 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = x^3 - 8x^2 - 3x + 3 evaluated at x = -2.
For f(x) = -6x^3 - 4x + 1, find f''(x) at x = 3.
Evaluate the definite integral of (x + 4) dx from x = 1 to x = 6.

question: Find the larger real root of 3x^2 + 7x - 7 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[-2, 8], [9, 1]].
solution: Given: a = -2, b = 8, c = 9, d = 1 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (-2)(1) - (8)(9) | Answer: -74

solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: 30

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[6, -5], [7, -8]].
solution: Trace tr = -2, Determinant = -13 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 2.742

question: Solve for x: 0x + -1y = 1 and -3x + -5y = 12.
solution: Determinant = 0*-5 - -1*-3 = -3 | x = (e d - b f) / det = -2.333 | Answer: x = -2.333
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 13, 95, 17, 81, 32.
solution: Sum = 238 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 47.6 | Answer: 47.6

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 10, 34, 9, 17, 28.

question: Find the slope of the line through (-7, 3) and (7, -8).
solution: Given: x1 = -7, y1 = 3, x2 = 7, y2 = -8 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (-8 - 3) / (7 - -7) | Answer: -0.7857

question: Find the distance between the points (9, 8) and (-4, -9).
solution: Given: x1 = 9, y1 = 8, x2 = -4, y2 = -9 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-13)^2 + (-17)^2) | Answer: 21.4 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (6,6), (-1,-4), (-4,4).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 43 sq units

question: Find the 22th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 9 and common difference -4.
solution: Given: a = 9, d = -4, n = 22 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = 9 + (22 - 1)*-4 | Answer: -75

question: Find the sum of the first 28 terms of an AP with first term 15 and common difference 7.
solution: Given: a = 15, d = 7, n = 28 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 28/2 [2*15 + (28-1)*7] | Answer: 3066

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 13500 at 13.6% per annum for 3 years.
solution: Given: P = 13500, R = 13.6, Tt = 3 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 13500 * 13.6 * 3 / 100 | Answer: 5508 currency units

question: Find the amount when 24500 is invested at 7% per annum compounded annually for 2 years.
solution: Given: P = 24500, R = 7, Tt = 2 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 24500 * (1 + 7/100)^2 | Answer: 2805 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (5, 8, 4) and (6, 3, -1).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (0, 2, -4) and (3, -3, 6).

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (6, 2, 1) and (5, -4, 6).

question: Find the modulus of the complex number 9 + -6i.
solution: Given: a = 9, b = -6 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((9)^2 + (-6)^2) | Answer: 10.82

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number 6 + 0i.
solution: Given: a = 6, b = 0 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(0, 6) | Answer: 0 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -5x^3 - 6x^2 + 8 at x = 0.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-39 with initial guess x0=9, find x1 (one iteration).
solution: Given: N = 39, x0 = 9 | Formula: x1 = x0 - (x0^2 - N)/(2 x0) | Substitute: x1 = 9 - ((9)^2 - 39)/(2*9) | Answer: 6.667

question: Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.2 and ordinates 6, 5, 6, 13, 10, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 530 and 403.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 530 and 403 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 29 and 7.
solution: Given: a = 29, b = 7 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 29*7 / 1 | Answer: 203
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 42 mm carries an axial tensile load of 30 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 37 mm and length 2800 mm carries an axial load of 45 kN. Take E = 200 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 35 mm transmits a torque of 1850 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 35, Tt = 1850 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(1850*1000) / (pi*(35)^3) | Answer: 219.8 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 26 mm and length 1500 mm carries a torque of 800 N-m. With G = 80 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (26)^4 / 32 = 44864 mm^4 | theta = (800*1000)(1500) / (80000 * 44864) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 19.16 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 135 mm wide and 60 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 135, h = 60 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 135*(60)^2 / 6 | Answer: 81000 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (106 mm x 190 mm) carries a bending moment of 37 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (45 mm x 160 mm) has effective length 2000 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 490 MPa is designed for a working stress of 120 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 490, sw = 120 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 490 / 120 | Answer: 4.083

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 550 mm and wall thickness 8 mm carries an internal pressure of 0.8 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 550, t = 8, P = 0.8 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 0.8*550 / (2*8) | Answer: 27.5 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 600 K and 370 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 600, Tc = 370 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 370/600) * 100 | Answer: 38.33 %

question: A heat pump operates between 265 K and 320 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 265, Th = 320 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 320 / (320 - 265) | Answer: 5.818

question: 5.7 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 65 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 5.7, dT = 65 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 5.7 * 0.718 * 65 | Answer: 266 kJ

question: 4.9 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 75 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.9, dT = 75 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 4.9 * 1.005 * 75 | Answer: 369.3 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 1.7 m^3 at 450 K with mass 3.7 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 1.7, Tk = 450, m = 3.7 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 3.7*0.287*450 / 1.7 | Answer: 281.1 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 4.4 kg of air expands isothermally at 500 K from volume V1 to 3*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.4, Tk = 500, ratio = 3 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 4.4*0.287*500*ln(3) | Answer: 693.7 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 2.7 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.13 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 2.7, D = 0.13 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*2.7*0.13 / 0.001 | Answer: 351000

question: Water flows at 3.6 m/s through a pipe of diameter 100 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 2.3 m. Taking Cv = 0.96, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).

question: In a pipe (diameter 340 mm) water flows at 2.6 m/s. It contracts to diameter 120 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
Water flows at 3.8 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.38 m and length 330 m. With friction factor f = 0.032, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 27 teeth drives a gear of 119 teeth. If the pinion runs at 750 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 27, z2 = 119, N1 = 750 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 750*27 / 119 | Answer: 170.2 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 130 mm rotates at 200 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 130, N = 200 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.13)*200 / 60 | Answer: 1.361 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 29.9 kW at 1450 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 29.9, N = 1450 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(29.9*1000) / (2*pi*1450) | Answer: 196.9 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 0.8 kg rotates at radius 0.57 m at 550 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 15400 N/m and mass 8.2 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 15400, m = 8.2 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(15400/8.2) | Answer: 6.897 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 4.8 m^2 and thickness 0.36 m has conductivity k = 48.4 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 125 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 4.8, L = 0.36, k = 48.4, dT = 125 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 48.4*4.8*125 / 0.36 | Answer: 80667 W

question: A surface of area 4.2 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 135 W/m^2-K to surroundings 100 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 4.2, h = 135, dT = 100 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 135*4.2*100 | Answer: 56700 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 70 m/min, feed = 0.12 mm/rev, depth of cut = 1 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 70, f = 0.12, d = 1 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*70*0.12*1 | Answer: 8400 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 390 mm is turned at 950 rpm with a feed of 0.39 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 390, N = 950, f = 0.39 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 390 / (0.39*950) | Answer: 1.053 min

question: A resistor of 79 ohm carries a current of 6.7 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 79, I = 6.7 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 6.7 * 79 | Answer: 529.3 V

question: Three resistors 28 ohm, 43 ohm and 92 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 28, R2 = 43, R3 = 92 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 28 + 43 + 92 | Answer: 163 ohm

question: Two resistors 5 ohm and 73 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 5, R2 = 73 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 5*73 / (5+73) | Answer: 4.679 ohm

question: A device draws 14.5 A at 225 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 225, I = 14.5 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 225 * 14.5 | Answer: 3262 W

question: A current of 8.6 A flows through a 33 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 8.6, R = 33 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (8.6)^2 * 33 | Answer: 2441 W

question: Two capacitors 40.8 uF and 25.2 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 40.8, C2 = 25.2 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 40.8*25.2 / (40.8+25.2) | Answer: 15.58 uF

question: A resistor 62 kohm and capacitor 7.4 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 62, C = 7.4 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (62k)(7.4u) = 458.8 ms | Answer: 458.8 ms

question: An inductor 486 mH is in series with 189 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 486, R = 189 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (486e-3) / 189 | Answer: 2.571 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 128.2 mH inductor at 670 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 128.2, f = 670 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (670)(128.2e-3) | Answer: 539.7 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 43.9 uF capacitor at 300 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 43.9, f = 300 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (300)(43.9e-6)) | Answer: 12.08 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 33 ohm, XL = 77 ohm and XC = 72 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 33, XL = 77, XC = 72 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(33^2 + (77 - 72)^2) | Answer: 33.38 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 33.3 mH and C = 3.3 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 33.3, C = 3.3 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(33.3e-3 * 3.3e-6)) | Answer: 480.1 Hz

question: A capacitor of 97.9 uF is charged to 285 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 97.9, V = 285 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*97.9e-6*(285)^2 | Answer: 3976 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 160 V with 200 primary turns and 180 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 160, N1 = 200, N2 = 180 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 160 * 180/200 | Answer: 144 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 190 V and draws an armature current of 35 A. If the armature resistance is 0.48 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 190, Ia = 35, Ra = 0.48 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 190 - 35*0.48 | Answer: 173.2 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 115 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.77. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 115, VL = 400, pf = 0.77 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*400*115*0.77 / 1000 | Answer: 61.35 kW

question: A load has real power 35 kW and apparent power 155 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 35, S = 155 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 35 / 155 | Answer: 0.2258

question: A machine delivers 130 kW output while drawing 137 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 130, Pi = 137 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 130/137 * 100 | Answer: 94.89 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 27 V across R1 = 45 ohm and R2 = 50 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 27, R1 = 45, R2 = 50 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 27*50 / (45+50) | Answer: 14.21 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 50 kohm and Rin = 18 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 50, Rin = 18 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 50 / 18 | Answer: 2.778

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 80 kohm and Rg = 19 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 80, Rg = 19 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 80/19 | Answer: 5.211

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 3402. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 3402 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(3402) | Answer: 35.32 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 3.7 m carries a central point load of 110 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.7, W = 110 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 110*3.7 / 4 | Answer: 101.8 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 8.8 m carries a UDL of 15 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 8.8, w = 15 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 15*(8.8)^2 / 8 | Answer: 145.2 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 2 m carries a point load 40 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 2, W = 40 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 40*2 | Answer: 80 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 4.1 m carries a UDL of 4 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.1, w = 4 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 4*(4.1)^2 / 2 | Answer: 33.62 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.6 m carries a point load 95 kN at distance 1.9 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 6.6, a = 1.9, W = 95 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 95*(6.6 - 1.9) / 6.6 | Answer: 67.65 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 6.5 m) carries a central point load 80 kN. With E = 30 GPa and I = 220e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=80000 N, L=6500.0 mm, E=30000 MPa, I=220e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 69.35 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 8.3 m carries a UDL of 18 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 8.3, w = 18 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 18*(8.3)^2 / 12 | Answer: 103.3 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 310 mm, clear cover 25 mm and main bars of diameter 25 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 310, c = 25, dia = 25 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 310 - 25 - 25/2 | Answer: 272.5 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 33.2 m^2 carrying a factored load of 15 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 33.2, w = 15 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 15 * 33.2 | Answer: 498 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 6.2 m, unit weight 17 kN/m^3, phi = 31 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 10.1 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 19 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 10.1, g = 19 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (19 - 9.81)*10.1 | Answer: 92.82 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 2.1e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1.3, area = 4.8e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 2.1, i = 1.3, A = 4.8 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (2.1e-4)*1.3*(4.8e-3) | Answer: 131 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.2 m, bed slope 0.006 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.026. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 3.6 m under a head of 0.9 m. Taking Cd = 0.6 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 5.3 m wide carries a discharge of 10.8 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).

formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: A tank of volume 420 m^3 treats a flow of 80 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 420, Q = 80 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 420 / 80 | Answer: 5.25 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 350 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.23 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 8 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 350, k = 0.23, t = 8 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 350*(1 - e^(-0.23*8)) | Answer: 294.4 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.71, rainfall intensity 50 mm/h over a catchment of 30.3 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.71, i = 50, A = 30.3 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.71*50*30.3 / 360 | Answer: 2.988 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.01 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 210 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.01, M = 210 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 210*(30+0.01)/30 | Answer: 210.1 m

question: Convert the decimal number 1668 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 1668 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 684 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 10110110 and 10010100.
solution: XOR: 00100010 | Count of 1s = 2 | Answer: 2
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 540 megabits is sent over a link of 92 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 540, B = 92 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 540 / 92 | Answer: 5.87 s

question: A link has bandwidth 99 Mbps and round-trip time 90 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 99, R = 90 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 99e6 * 90e-3 bits = 8910 kb | Answer: 8910 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.89, cache access time 4 ns and main-memory access time 120 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.89, tc = 4, tm = 120 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.89*4 + (1 - 0.89)*120 | Answer: 16.76 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 414406 elements?
solution: Given: n = 414406 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(414406)) + 1 | Answer: 19

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.011, memory access time 150 ns and page-fault service time 4 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 4 ms = 4000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.011)*150 + 0.011*4000000.0 ns | Answer: 44.15 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 1.9 m^3 at 460 kPa and 370 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 1.9, P = 460, Tk = 370 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (460e3)*1.9 / (8.314*370) | Answer: 284.1 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.25 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 8 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.25, t = 8 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.25*8) | Answer: 0.8647

question: For a reaction with A = 4e10 /s and activation energy 60 kJ/mol at 390 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 4, Ea = 60, Tk = 390 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 4e10 * exp(-60e3 / (8.314*390)) | Answer: 367.9 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.92 and bottoms xW = 0.05, with relative volatility alpha = 2.3. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.92, xw = 0.05, al = 2.3 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.92/0.08)(0.95/0.05)] / ln(2.3) | Answer: 6.467 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.65 and x = 0.42. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.65, x = 0.42 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.65/0.35) / (0.42/0.58) | Answer: 2.565

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.44 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 105 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.44, Psat = 105 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.44 * 105 | Answer: 46.2 kPa

question: A stream of 0.8 kg/s with specific heat 2.9 kJ/kg-K is heated through 45 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 0.8, cp = 2.9, dT = 45 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 0.8*2.9*45 | Answer: 104.4 kW

question: A reactor of volume 12.9 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 2.8 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 12.9, Q = 2.8 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 12.9 / 2.8 | Answer: 4.607 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 5.4e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 5 mm with a concentration difference of 20 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 5.4, L = 5, dC = 20 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (5.4e-9)*20 / (5e-3) | Answer: 21.6 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 5.2 min and steady-state gain 0.7. For a step input of magnitude 2, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 5.2, K = 0.7, M = 2 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 0.7 * 2 | Answer: 1.4 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 95 m^2 flies at 100 m/s (air density 0.7 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 1.1. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 95, V = 100, rho = 0.7, CL = 1.1 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.7*(100)^2*95*1.1 / 1000 | Answer: 365.8 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 30 m^2 flies at 190 m/s (density 1.225 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.05. Find the drag force in kN.
A specimen under stress 120 MPa shows an elastic strain of 1.8e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 120, eps = 1.8 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 120 / (1.8e-3) MPa = 66.67 GPa | Answer: 66.67 GPa

question: A block of mass 42 kg has a volume of 1.8e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 42, V = 1.8 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 42 / (1.8e-3) | Answer: 23333 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 1300 mm is heated through 80 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 12e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 1300, dT = 80, al = 12 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 1300*12e-6*80 | Answer: 1.248 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 155 ohm, R2 = 145 ohm and R3 = 390 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 155, R2 = 145, R3 = 390 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 145*390 / 155 | Answer: 364.8 ohm

question: A measurement reads 9.83 when the true value is 20. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.83, true = 20 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.83 - 20| / 20 * 100 | Answer: 50.85 %

question: Annual demand is 7000 units, ordering cost 190 per order and holding cost 37 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 7000, S = 190, H = 37 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*7000*190 / 37) | Answer: 268.1 units

question: An asset costs 100000 with salvage value 22000 after 20 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 100000, Sv = 22000, n = 20 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (100000 - 22000) / 20 | Answer: 3900 per year

question: A product sells for 210 per unit with variable cost 140 per unit and fixed costs 100000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 210, V = 140, F = 100000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 100000 / (210 - 140) | Answer: 1429 units

question: Find the present worth of 85000 received 10 years from now at an interest rate of 8% per year.
solution: Given: F = 85000, n = 10, i = 8 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 85000 / (1 + 0.08)^10 | Answer: 39371 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.92, 0.9 and 0.92 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.92, r2 = 0.9, r3 = 0.92 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.92*0.9*0.92 | Answer: 0.7618

question: A process produces 45 defective items in a batch of 3000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 45, N = 3000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 45/3000 * 1e6 | Answer: 15000 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -2x^3 - 2x^2 - x + 7 evaluated at x = -2.
For f(x) = -x^3 + 4x^2 - 4x + 1, find f''(x) at x = 3.
Evaluate the definite integral of (3x^2 + 5x + 4) dx from x = -4 to x = 7.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = 3x^3/3 + 5x^2/2 + 4x | Evaluate F(7) - F(-4) | Answer: 533.5

question: Find the larger real root of 4x^2 - 11x - 1 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[-2, -9], [-8, -9]].
solution: Given: a = -2, b = -9, c = -8, d = -9 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (-2)(-9) - (-9)(-8) | Answer: -54

solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: -120

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[3, 1], [8, 0]].
solution: Trace tr = 3, Determinant = -8 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 4.702

question: Solve for x: 0x + -2y = -8 and 2x + -5y = -1.
solution: Determinant = 0*-5 - -2*2 = 4 | x = (e d - b f) / det = 9.5 | Answer: x = 9.5
