solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 522 and 45 | Answer: GCD = 9

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 17 and 41.
solution: Given: a = 17, b = 41 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 17*41 / 1 | Answer: 697
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 52 mm carries an axial tensile load of 58 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 21 mm and length 3000 mm carries an axial load of 21 kN. Take E = 70 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 20 mm transmits a torque of 650 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 20, Tt = 650 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(650*1000) / (pi*(20)^3) | Answer: 413.8 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 40 mm and length 900 mm carries a torque of 1000 N-m. With G = 45 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (40)^4 / 32 = 251327 mm^4 | theta = (1000*1000)(900) / (45000 * 251327) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 4.559 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 144 mm wide and 190 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 144, h = 190 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 144*(190)^2 / 6 | Answer: 866400 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (46 mm x 160 mm) carries a bending moment of 21 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (31 mm x 160 mm) has effective length 1900 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 770 MPa is designed for a working stress of 170 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 770, sw = 170 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 770 / 170 | Answer: 4.529

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1150 mm and wall thickness 8 mm carries an internal pressure of 2.9 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1150, t = 8, P = 2.9 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 2.9*1150 / (2*8) | Answer: 208.4 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 1080 K and 300 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 1080, Tc = 300 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 300/1080) * 100 | Answer: 72.22 %

question: A heat pump operates between 278 K and 308 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 278, Th = 308 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 308 / (308 - 278) | Answer: 10.27

question: 2.5 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 70 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.5, dT = 70 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 2.5 * 0.718 * 70 | Answer: 125.6 kJ

question: 6.5 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 135 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 6.5, dT = 135 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 6.5 * 1.005 * 135 | Answer: 881.9 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 1.5 m^3 at 590 K with mass 3 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 1.5, Tk = 590, m = 3 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 3*0.287*590 / 1.5 | Answer: 338.7 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 3.2 kg of air expands isothermally at 450 K from volume V1 to 2*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.2, Tk = 450, ratio = 2 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 3.2*0.287*450*ln(2) | Answer: 286.5 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 5 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.07 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 5, D = 0.07 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*5*0.07 / 0.001 | Answer: 350000

question: Water flows at 3.1 m/s through a pipe of diameter 190 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 3.6 m. Taking Cv = 0.96, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 3.6, cv = 0.96 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.96*sqrt(2*9.81*3.6) | Answer: 8.068 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 170 mm) water flows at 2.4 m/s. It contracts to diameter 80 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 170, d2 = 80, V1 = 2.4 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 2.4*(170/80)^2 | Answer: 10.84 m/s

question: Water flows at 2.1 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.36 m and length 350 m. With friction factor f = 0.028, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 20 teeth drives a gear of 112 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1350 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 20, z2 = 112, N1 = 1350 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1350*20 / 112 | Answer: 241.1 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 130 mm rotates at 600 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 130, N = 600 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.13)*600 / 60 | Answer: 4.084 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 39.7 kW at 1150 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 39.7, N = 1150 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(39.7*1000) / (2*pi*1150) | Answer: 329.7 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 7.6 kg rotates at radius 0.39 m at 450 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 8700 N/m and mass 20 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 8700, m = 20 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(8700/20) | Answer: 3.319 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 2.5 m^2 and thickness 0.28 m has conductivity k = 2.4 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 90 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 2.5, L = 0.28, k = 2.4, dT = 90 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 2.4*2.5*90 / 0.28 | Answer: 1929 W

question: A surface of area 3.5 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 165 W/m^2-K to surroundings 30 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 3.5, h = 165, dT = 30 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 165*3.5*30 | Answer: 17325 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 90 m/min, feed = 0.5 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2.1 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 90, f = 0.5, d = 2.1 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*90*0.5*2.1 | Answer: 94500 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 420 mm is turned at 1100 rpm with a feed of 0.15 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 420, N = 1100, f = 0.15 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 420 / (0.15*1100) | Answer: 2.545 min

question: A resistor of 137 ohm carries a current of 7.5 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 137, I = 7.5 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 7.5 * 137 | Answer: 1028 V

question: Three resistors 72 ohm, 62 ohm and 84 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 72, R2 = 62, R3 = 84 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 72 + 62 + 84 | Answer: 218 ohm

question: Two resistors 18 ohm and 78 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 18, R2 = 78 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 18*78 / (18+78) | Answer: 14.62 ohm

question: A device draws 7.5 A at 90 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 90, I = 7.5 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 90 * 7.5 | Answer: 675 W

question: A current of 6.8 A flows through a 56 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 6.8, R = 56 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (6.8)^2 * 56 | Answer: 2589 W

question: Two capacitors 35.4 uF and 25.8 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 35.4, C2 = 25.8 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 35.4*25.8 / (35.4+25.8) | Answer: 14.92 uF

question: A resistor 57 kohm and capacitor 7.3 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 57, C = 7.3 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (57k)(7.3u) = 416.1 ms | Answer: 416.1 ms

question: An inductor 89.2 mH is in series with 183 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 89.2, R = 183 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (89.2e-3) / 183 | Answer: 0.4874 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 16.6 mH inductor at 610 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 16.6, f = 610 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (610)(16.6e-3) | Answer: 63.62 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 1.4 uF capacitor at 900 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 1.4, f = 900 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (900)(1.4e-6)) | Answer: 126.3 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 49 ohm, XL = 105 ohm and XC = 77 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 49, XL = 105, XC = 77 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(49^2 + (105 - 77)^2) | Answer: 56.44 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 14.4 mH and C = 5.2 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 14.4, C = 5.2 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(14.4e-3 * 5.2e-6)) | Answer: 581.6 Hz

question: A capacitor of 2 uF is charged to 270 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 2, V = 270 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*2e-6*(270)^2 | Answer: 72.9 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 420 V with 450 primary turns and 30 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 420, N1 = 450, N2 = 30 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 420 * 30/450 | Answer: 28 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 200 V and draws an armature current of 9 A. If the armature resistance is 1.03 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 200, Ia = 9, Ra = 1.03 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 200 - 9*1.03 | Answer: 190.7 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 35 A at 433 V (line) with a power factor of 0.75. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 35, VL = 433, pf = 0.75 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*433*35*0.75 / 1000 | Answer: 19.69 kW

question: A load has real power 120 kW and apparent power 120 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 120, S = 120 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 120 / 120 | Answer: 1

question: A machine delivers 40 kW output while drawing 117 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 40, Pi = 117 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 40/117 * 100 | Answer: 34.19 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 30 V across R1 = 50 ohm and R2 = 5 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 30, R1 = 50, R2 = 5 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 30*5 / (50+5) | Answer: 2.727 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 170 kohm and Rin = 18 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 170, Rin = 18 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 170 / 18 | Answer: 9.444

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 110 kohm and Rg = 14 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 110, Rg = 14 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 110/14 | Answer: 8.857

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 1468. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 1468 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(1468) | Answer: 31.67 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.6 m carries a central point load of 105 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 9.6, W = 105 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 105*9.6 / 4 | Answer: 252 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 4 m carries a UDL of 60 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4, w = 60 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 60*(4)^2 / 8 | Answer: 120 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 5.9 m carries a point load 60 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.9, W = 60 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 60*5.9 | Answer: 354 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 3.1 m carries a UDL of 36 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.1, w = 36 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 36*(3.1)^2 / 2 | Answer: 173 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.7 m carries a point load 70 kN at distance 1.1 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 6.7, a = 1.1, W = 70 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 70*(6.7 - 1.1) / 6.7 | Answer: 58.51 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 4.6 m) carries a central point load 25 kN. With E = 30 GPa and I = 80e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=25000 N, L=4600.0 mm, E=30000 MPa, I=80e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 21.12 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 6.6 m carries a UDL of 18 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6.6, w = 18 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 18*(6.6)^2 / 12 | Answer: 65.34 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 390 mm, clear cover 50 mm and main bars of diameter 20 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 390, c = 50, dia = 20 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 390 - 50 - 20/2 | Answer: 330 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 33.9 m^2 carrying a factored load of 8.1 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 33.9, w = 8.1 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 8.1 * 33.9 | Answer: 274.6 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 3 m, unit weight 16 kN/m^3, phi = 32 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 6.3e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.5, area = 1.5e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 6.3, i = 0.5, A = 1.5 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (6.3e-4)*0.5*(1.5e-3) | Answer: 472.5 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.6 m, bed slope 0.005 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.029. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 3.4 m under a head of 0.5 m. Taking Cd = 0.6 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 4.7 m wide carries a discharge of 3.4 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 460 m and design speed 75 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 460, V = 75 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (75)^2 / (127*460) | Answer: 0.09629
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: A tank of volume 50 m^3 treats a flow of 200 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 50, Q = 200 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 50 / 200 | Answer: 0.25 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 180 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.12 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 8 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 180, k = 0.12, t = 8 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 180*(1 - e^(-0.12*8)) | Answer: 111.1 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.65, rainfall intensity 45 mm/h over a catchment of 58.5 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.65, i = 45, A = 58.5 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.65*45*58.5 / 360 | Answer: 4.753 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.03 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 610 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.03, M = 610 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 610*(20+0.03)/20 | Answer: 610.9 m

question: Convert the decimal number 1476 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 1476 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 5C4 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 01111110 and 10001011.
solution: XOR: 11110101 | Count of 1s = 6 | Answer: 6
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 220 megabits is sent over a link of 24 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 220, B = 24 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 220 / 24 | Answer: 9.167 s

question: A link has bandwidth 59 Mbps and round-trip time 100 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 59, R = 100 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 59e6 * 100e-3 bits = 5900 kb | Answer: 5900 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.89, cache access time 3 ns and main-memory access time 190 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.89, tc = 3, tm = 190 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.89*3 + (1 - 0.89)*190 | Answer: 23.57 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 536837 elements?
solution: Given: n = 536837 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(536837)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.003, memory access time 180 ns and page-fault service time 8 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 8 ms = 8000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.003)*180 + 0.003*8000000.0 ns | Answer: 24.18 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 2.7 m^3 at 500 kPa and 570 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 2.7, P = 500, Tk = 570 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (500e3)*2.7 / (8.314*570) | Answer: 284.9 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.08 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 6 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.08, t = 6 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.08*6) | Answer: 0.3812

question: For a reaction with A = 6e10 /s and activation energy 80 kJ/mol at 330 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 6, Ea = 80, Tk = 330 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 6e10 * exp(-80e3 / (8.314*330)) | Answer: 0.01302 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.96 and bottoms xW = 0.08, with relative volatility alpha = 3.4. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.96, xw = 0.08, al = 3.4 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.96/0.04)(0.92/0.08)] / ln(3.4) | Answer: 4.593 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.67 and x = 0.22. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.67, x = 0.22 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.67/0.33) / (0.22/0.78) | Answer: 7.198

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.29 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 30 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.29, Psat = 30 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.29 * 30 | Answer: 8.7 kPa

question: A stream of 3.3 kg/s with specific heat 3.3 kJ/kg-K is heated through 85 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 3.3, cp = 3.3, dT = 85 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 3.3*3.3*85 | Answer: 925.6 kW

question: A reactor of volume 7 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 0.8 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 7, Q = 0.8 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 7 / 0.8 | Answer: 8.75 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 6.1e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 2 mm with a concentration difference of 140 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 6.1, L = 2, dC = 140 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (6.1e-9)*140 / (2e-3) | Answer: 427 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 7 min and steady-state gain 2.2. For a step input of magnitude 14, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 7, K = 2.2, M = 14 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 2.2 * 14 | Answer: 30.8 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 120 m^2 flies at 150 m/s (air density 0.4 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 1.1. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 120, V = 150, rho = 0.4, CL = 1.1 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.4*(150)^2*120*1.1 / 1000 | Answer: 594 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 85 m^2 flies at 180 m/s (density 1 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.05. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 85, V = 180, rho = 1, CD = 0.05 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*1*(180)^2*85*0.05 / 1000 | Answer: 68.85 kN

question: A specimen under stress 330 MPa shows an elastic strain of 1.8e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 330, eps = 1.8 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 330 / (1.8e-3) MPa = 183.3 GPa | Answer: 183.3 GPa

question: A block of mass 18 kg has a volume of 3.6e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 18, V = 3.6 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 18 / (3.6e-3) | Answer: 5000 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 2400 mm is heated through 60 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 12e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 2400, dT = 60, al = 12 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 2400*12e-6*60 | Answer: 1.728 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 95 ohm, R2 = 30 ohm and R3 = 165 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 95, R2 = 30, R3 = 165 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 30*165 / 95 | Answer: 52.11 ohm

question: A measurement reads 9.41 when the true value is 50. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.41, true = 50 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.41 - 50| / 50 * 100 | Answer: 81.18 %

question: Annual demand is 16500 units, ordering cost 60 per order and holding cost 25 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 16500, S = 60, H = 25 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*16500*60 / 25) | Answer: 281.4 units

question: An asset costs 190000 with salvage value 6000 after 5 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 190000, Sv = 6000, n = 5 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (190000 - 6000) / 5 | Answer: 36800 per year

question: A product sells for 240 per unit with variable cost 150 per unit and fixed costs 55000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 240, V = 150, F = 55000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 55000 / (240 - 150) | Answer: 611.1 units

question: Find the present worth of 50000 received 3 years from now at an interest rate of 7% per year.
solution: Given: F = 50000, n = 3, i = 7 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 50000 / (1 + 0.07)^3 | Answer: 40815 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.92, 0.91 and 0.91 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.92, r2 = 0.91, r3 = 0.91 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.92*0.91*0.91 | Answer: 0.7619

question: A process produces 36 defective items in a batch of 4000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 36, N = 4000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 36/4000 * 1e6 | Answer: 9000 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -3x^3 - 3x^2 + 6x - 4 evaluated at x = 0.
For f(x) = -3x^3 - 3x^2 - 4x - 7, find f''(x) at x = -4.
Evaluate the definite integral of (-x^2 + 4x + 4) dx from x = -2 to x = 5.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = -1x^3/3 + 4x^2/2 + 4x | Evaluate F(5) - F(-2) | Answer: 25.67
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 6x^2 - 8x - 11 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[7, -6], [3, 4]].
solution: Given: a = 7, b = -6, c = 3, d = 4 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (7)(4) - (-6)(3) | Answer: 46

question: Find the determinant of [[1, -2, -5], [0, -4, -5], [3, -6, 1]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: -64

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[-3, 6], [3, 8]].
solution: Trace tr = 5, Determinant = -42 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 9.446

question: Solve for x: -5x + -6y = 5 and -2x + 1y = 0.
solution: Determinant = -5*1 - -6*-2 = -17 | x = (e d - b f) / det = -0.2941 | Answer: x = -0.2941
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 23, 51, 71, 29, 28.
solution: Sum = 202 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 40.4 | Answer: 40.4

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 37, 4, 11, 26, 7.
solution: Mean = 17 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 14.02

question: Find the slope of the line through (6, -7) and (-6, -7).
solution: Given: x1 = 6, y1 = -7, x2 = -6, y2 = -7 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (-7 - -7) / (-6 - 6) | Answer: 0

question: Find the distance between the points (-5, 5) and (4, -5).
solution: Given: x1 = -5, y1 = 5, x2 = 4, y2 = -5 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((9)^2 + (-10)^2) | Answer: 13.45 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (0,-8), (3,3), (-3,6).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 37.5 sq units

question: Find the 21th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 3 and common difference -8.
solution: Given: a = 3, d = -8, n = 21 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = 3 + (21 - 1)*-8 | Answer: -157

question: Find the sum of the first 25 terms of an AP with first term 9 and common difference 1.
solution: Given: a = 9, d = 1, n = 25 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 25/2 [2*9 + (25-1)*1] | Answer: 525

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 18000 at 14% per annum for 4 years.
solution: Given: P = 18000, R = 14, Tt = 4 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 18000 * 14 * 4 / 100 | Answer: 10080 currency units

question: Find the amount when 31000 is invested at 10% per annum compounded annually for 2 years.
solution: Given: P = 31000, R = 10, Tt = 2 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 31000 * (1 + 10/100)^2 | Answer: 37510 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (-1, 6, 6) and (2, -4, -7).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (-2, 6, -4) and (-4, 0, -1).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 28.43

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (-6, 0, 0) and (-6, -4, 1).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 34.5 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number 2 + 9i.
solution: Given: a = 2, b = 9 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((2)^2 + (9)^2) | Answer: 9.22

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number 6 + -6i.
solution: Given: a = 6, b = -6 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(-6, 6) | Answer: -45 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -x^3 - 5x^2 + 3x at x = -4.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-158 with initial guess x0=7, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.2 and ordinates 5, 18, 17, 20, 18, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 423 and 389.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 423 and 389 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 43 and 77.
solution: Given: a = 43, b = 77 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 43*77 / 1 | Answer: 3311
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 12 mm carries an axial tensile load of 72 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 31 mm and length 1800 mm carries an axial load of 68 kN. Take E = 110 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 59 mm transmits a torque of 950 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 59, Tt = 950 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(950*1000) / (pi*(59)^3) | Answer: 23.56 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 35 mm and length 1000 mm carries a torque of 1500 N-m. With G = 80 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (35)^4 / 32 = 147324 mm^4 | theta = (1500*1000)(1000) / (80000 * 147324) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 7.292 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 96 mm wide and 280 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 96, h = 280 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 96*(280)^2 / 6 | Answer: 1254400 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (105 mm x 120 mm) carries a bending moment of 7 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (34 mm x 90 mm) has effective length 3600 mm and E = 200 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 710 MPa is designed for a working stress of 160 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 710, sw = 160 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 710 / 160 | Answer: 4.438

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1250 mm and wall thickness 14 mm carries an internal pressure of 1.3 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1250, t = 14, P = 1.3 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 1.3*1250 / (2*14) | Answer: 58.04 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 680 K and 310 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 680, Tc = 310 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 310/680) * 100 | Answer: 54.41 %

question: A heat pump operates between 281 K and 330 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 281, Th = 330 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 330 / (330 - 281) | Answer: 6.735

question: 7.7 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 70 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 7.7, dT = 70 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 7.7 * 0.718 * 70 | Answer: 387 kJ

question: 1.6 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 170 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1.6, dT = 170 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 1.6 * 1.005 * 170 | Answer: 273.4 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 3.6 m^3 at 600 K with mass 4.4 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 3.6, Tk = 600, m = 4.4 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 4.4*0.287*600 / 3.6 | Answer: 210.5 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 1.4 kg of air expands isothermally at 320 K from volume V1 to 2*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1.4, Tk = 320, ratio = 2 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 1.4*0.287*320*ln(2) | Answer: 89.12 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 2.1 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.16 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 2.1, D = 0.16 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*2.1*0.16 / 0.001 | Answer: 336000

question: Water flows at 3.9 m/s through a pipe of diameter 100 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 5.2 m. Taking Cv = 0.98, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 5.2, cv = 0.98 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.98*sqrt(2*9.81*5.2) | Answer: 9.899 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 210 mm) water flows at 2.4 m/s. It contracts to diameter 100 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
Water flows at 1.1 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.48 m and length 350 m. With friction factor f = 0.027, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 15 teeth drives a gear of 105 teeth. If the pinion runs at 450 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 15, z2 = 105, N1 = 450 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 450*15 / 105 | Answer: 64.29 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 540 mm rotates at 500 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 540, N = 500 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.54)*500 / 60 | Answer: 14.14 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 24.9 kW at 1400 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 24.9, N = 1400 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(24.9*1000) / (2*pi*1400) | Answer: 169.8 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 3.2 kg rotates at radius 0.25 m at 350 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 2600 N/m and mass 5.1 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 2600, m = 5.1 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(2600/5.1) | Answer: 3.594 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 2.6 m^2 and thickness 0.39 m has conductivity k = 13.7 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 150 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 2.6, L = 0.39, k = 13.7, dT = 150 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 13.7*2.6*150 / 0.39 | Answer: 13700 W

question: A surface of area 1 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 110 W/m^2-K to surroundings 75 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 1, h = 110, dT = 75 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 110*1*75 | Answer: 8250 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 220 m/min, feed = 0.19 mm/rev, depth of cut = 0.8 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 220, f = 0.19, d = 0.8 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*220*0.19*0.8 | Answer: 33440 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 350 mm is turned at 1100 rpm with a feed of 0.39 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 350, N = 1100, f = 0.39 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 350 / (0.39*1100) | Answer: 0.8159 min

question: A resistor of 11 ohm carries a current of 2.9 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 11, I = 2.9 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 2.9 * 11 | Answer: 31.9 V

question: Three resistors 11 ohm, 74 ohm and 40 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 11, R2 = 74, R3 = 40 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 11 + 74 + 40 | Answer: 125 ohm

question: Two resistors 17 ohm and 33 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 17, R2 = 33 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 17*33 / (17+33) | Answer: 11.22 ohm

question: A device draws 5.2 A at 225 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 225, I = 5.2 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 225 * 5.2 | Answer: 1170 W

question: A current of 3.6 A flows through a 98 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 3.6, R = 98 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (3.6)^2 * 98 | Answer: 127 W

question: Two capacitors 24.6 uF and 23 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 24.6, C2 = 23 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 24.6*23 / (24.6+23) | Answer: 11.89 uF

question: A resistor 9 kohm and capacitor 3.2 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 9, C = 3.2 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (9k)(3.2u) = 28.8 ms | Answer: 28.8 ms

question: An inductor 418.1 mH is in series with 128 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 418.1, R = 128 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (418.1e-3) / 128 | Answer: 3.266 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 43.2 mH inductor at 450 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 43.2, f = 450 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (450)(43.2e-3) | Answer: 122.1 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 17.4 uF capacitor at 700 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 17.4, f = 700 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (700)(17.4e-6)) | Answer: 13.07 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 99 ohm, XL = 83 ohm and XC = 146 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 99, XL = 83, XC = 146 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(99^2 + (83 - 146)^2) | Answer: 117.3 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 77.8 mH and C = 1.2 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 77.8, C = 1.2 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(77.8e-3 * 1.2e-6)) | Answer: 520.9 Hz

question: A capacitor of 79.3 uF is charged to 230 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 79.3, V = 230 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*79.3e-6*(230)^2 | Answer: 2097 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 250 V with 560 primary turns and 400 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 250, N1 = 560, N2 = 400 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 250 * 400/560 | Answer: 178.6 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 150 V and draws an armature current of 26 A. If the armature resistance is 1.47 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 150, Ia = 26, Ra = 1.47 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 150 - 26*1.47 | Answer: 111.8 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 30 A at 433 V (line) with a power factor of 0.9. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 30, VL = 433, pf = 0.9 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*433*30*0.9 / 1000 | Answer: 20.25 kW

question: A load has real power 45 kW and apparent power 180 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 45, S = 180 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 45 / 180 | Answer: 0.25

question: A machine delivers 95 kW output while drawing 152 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 95, Pi = 152 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 95/152 * 100 | Answer: 62.5 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 20 V across R1 = 27 ohm and R2 = 25 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 20, R1 = 27, R2 = 25 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 20*25 / (27+25) | Answer: 9.615 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 140 kohm and Rin = 30 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 140, Rin = 30 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 140 / 30 | Answer: 4.667

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 140 kohm and Rg = 20 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 140, Rg = 20 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 140/20 | Answer: 8

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 598. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 598 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(598) | Answer: 27.77 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 3.7 m carries a central point load of 25 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.7, W = 25 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 25*3.7 / 4 | Answer: 23.12 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.7 m carries a UDL of 50 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6.7, w = 50 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 50*(6.7)^2 / 8 | Answer: 280.6 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 1.3 m carries a point load 45 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 1.3, W = 45 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 45*1.3 | Answer: 58.5 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 2.6 m carries a UDL of 26 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 2.6, w = 26 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 26*(2.6)^2 / 2 | Answer: 87.88 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 5 m carries a point load 35 kN at distance 1.6 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 5, a = 1.6, W = 35 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 35*(5 - 1.6) / 5 | Answer: 23.8 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 3.9 m) carries a central point load 70 kN. With E = 200 GPa and I = 380e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=70000 N, L=3900.0 mm, E=200000 MPa, I=380e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 1.138 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 8.2 m carries a UDL of 9 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 8.2, w = 9 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 9*(8.2)^2 / 12 | Answer: 50.43 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 620 mm, clear cover 40 mm and main bars of diameter 12 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 620, c = 40, dia = 12 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 620 - 40 - 12/2 | Answer: 574 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 29 m^2 carrying a factored load of 12 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 29, w = 12 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 12 * 29 | Answer: 348 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 3.5 m, unit weight 20 kN/m^3, phi = 32 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 1.5e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.3, area = 1.1e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 1.5, i = 0.3, A = 1.1 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (1.5e-4)*0.3*(1.1e-3) | Answer: 49.5 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 0.5 m, bed slope 0.001 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.019. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 3.2 m under a head of 0.3 m. Taking Cd = 0.6 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.

question: A rectangular channel 2.3 m wide carries a discharge of 11.8 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).

formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: A tank of volume 390 m^3 treats a flow of 130 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 390, Q = 130 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 390 / 130 | Answer: 3 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 250 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.13 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 3 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 250, k = 0.13, t = 3 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 250*(1 - e^(-0.13*3)) | Answer: 80.74 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.5, rainfall intensity 60 mm/h over a catchment of 12.8 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.5, i = 60, A = 12.8 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.5*60*12.8 / 360 | Answer: 1.067 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.07 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 160 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.07, M = 160 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 160*(20+0.07)/20 | Answer: 160.6 m

question: Convert the decimal number 1128 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 1128 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 468 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 11011010 and 10110111.
solution: XOR: 01101101 | Count of 1s = 5 | Answer: 5
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 810 megabits is sent over a link of 72 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 810, B = 72 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 810 / 72 | Answer: 11.25 s

question: A link has bandwidth 90 Mbps and round-trip time 130 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 90, R = 130 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 90e6 * 130e-3 bits = 11700 kb | Answer: 11700 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.91, cache access time 10 ns and main-memory access time 70 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.91, tc = 10, tm = 70 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.91*10 + (1 - 0.91)*70 | Answer: 15.4 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 634174 elements?
solution: Given: n = 634174 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(634174)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.002, memory access time 90 ns and page-fault service time 5 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 5 ms = 5000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.002)*90 + 0.002*5000000.0 ns | Answer: 10.09 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 1.1 m^3 at 490 kPa and 560 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 1.1, P = 490, Tk = 560 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (490e3)*1.1 / (8.314*560) | Answer: 115.8 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.32 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 14 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.32, t = 14 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.32*14) | Answer: 0.9887

question: For a reaction with A = 9e10 /s and activation energy 70 kJ/mol at 320 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 9, Ea = 70, Tk = 320 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 9e10 * exp(-70e3 / (8.314*320)) | Answer: 0.3369 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.96 and bottoms xW = 0.09, with relative volatility alpha = 2.5. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.96, xw = 0.09, al = 2.5 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.96/0.04)(0.91/0.09)] / ln(2.5) | Answer: 5.993 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.76 and x = 0.5. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.76, x = 0.5 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.76/0.24) / (0.5/0.5) | Answer: 3.167

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.63 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 120 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.63, Psat = 120 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.63 * 120 | Answer: 75.6 kPa

question: A stream of 0.8 kg/s with specific heat 2.7 kJ/kg-K is heated through 60 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 0.8, cp = 2.7, dT = 60 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 0.8*2.7*60 | Answer: 129.6 kW

question: A reactor of volume 4.6 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 1.7 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 4.6, Q = 1.7 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 4.6 / 1.7 | Answer: 2.706 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 4.6e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 5 mm with a concentration difference of 180 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 4.6, L = 5, dC = 180 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (4.6e-9)*180 / (5e-3) | Answer: 165.6 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 9.2 min and steady-state gain 2. For a step input of magnitude 13, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 9.2, K = 2, M = 13 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 2 * 13 | Answer: 26 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 25 m^2 flies at 90 m/s (air density 1 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.8. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 25, V = 90, rho = 1, CL = 0.8 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1*(90)^2*25*0.8 / 1000 | Answer: 81 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 50 m^2 flies at 110 m/s (density 1 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.04. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 50, V = 110, rho = 1, CD = 0.04 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*1*(110)^2*50*0.04 / 1000 | Answer: 12.1 kN

question: A specimen under stress 160 MPa shows an elastic strain of 2.6e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 160, eps = 2.6 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 160 / (2.6e-3) MPa = 61.54 GPa | Answer: 61.54 GPa

question: A block of mass 7 kg has a volume of 1.1e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 7, V = 1.1 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 7 / (1.1e-3) | Answer: 6364 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 1600 mm is heated through 150 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 17e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 1600, dT = 150, al = 17 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 1600*17e-6*150 | Answer: 4.08 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 185 ohm, R2 = 45 ohm and R3 = 285 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 185, R2 = 45, R3 = 285 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 45*285 / 185 | Answer: 69.32 ohm

question: A measurement reads 9.37 when the true value is 100. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.37, true = 100 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.37 - 100| / 100 * 100 | Answer: 90.63 %

question: Annual demand is 46500 units, ordering cost 70 per order and holding cost 31 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 46500, S = 70, H = 31 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*46500*70 / 31) | Answer: 458.3 units

question: An asset costs 220000 with salvage value 12000 after 10 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 220000, Sv = 12000, n = 10 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (220000 - 12000) / 10 | Answer: 20800 per year

question: A product sells for 130 per unit with variable cost 50 per unit and fixed costs 60000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 130, V = 50, F = 60000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 60000 / (130 - 50) | Answer: 750 units

question: Find the present worth of 120000 received 8 years from now at an interest rate of 8% per year.
solution: Given: F = 120000, n = 8, i = 8 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 120000 / (1 + 0.08)^8 | Answer: 64832 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.92, 0.96 and 0.9 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.92, r2 = 0.96, r3 = 0.9 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.92*0.96*0.9 | Answer: 0.7949

question: A process produces 30 defective items in a batch of 9000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 30, N = 9000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 30/9000 * 1e6 | Answer: 3333 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -4x^3 - 5x^2 - 9x + 7 evaluated at x = 1.
For f(x) = -x^3 + 8x^2 - 4x + 8, find f''(x) at x = -3.

question: Find the larger real root of 5x^2 - 9x - 5 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[-4, -5], [3, -1]].

question: Find the slope of the line through (1, 3) and (-6, 3).
solution: Given: x1 = 1, y1 = 3, x2 = -6, y2 = 3 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (3 - 3) / (-6 - 1) | Answer: 0

question: Find the distance between the points (0, 8) and (-4, -1).
solution: Given: x1 = 0, y1 = 8, x2 = -4, y2 = -1 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-4)^2 + (-9)^2) | Answer: 9.849 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (-5,6), (-6,1), (3,-5).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 25.5 sq units

question: Find the 26th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -12 and common difference 2.
solution: Given: a = -12, d = 2, n = 26 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -12 + (26 - 1)*2 | Answer: 38

question: Find the sum of the first 33 terms of an AP with first term 3 and common difference -7.
solution: Given: a = 3, d = -7, n = 33 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 33/2 [2*3 + (33-1)*-7] | Answer: -3597

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 6500 at 10% per annum for 5 years.
solution: Given: P = 6500, R = 10, Tt = 5 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 6500 * 10 * 5 / 100 | Answer: 3250 currency units

question: Find the amount when 6000 is invested at 10.8% per annum compounded annually for 5 years.
solution: Given: P = 6000, R = 10.8, Tt = 5 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 6000 * (1 + 10.8/100)^5 | Answer: 1002 currency units

question: Find the modulus of the complex number -12 + 5i.
solution: Given: a = -12, b = 5 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((-12)^2 + (5)^2) | Answer: 13

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number -5 + 7i.
solution: Given: a = -5, b = 7 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(7, -5) | Answer: 125.5 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = 3x^3 + x^2 - 4x - 5 at x = 0.

solution: Given: N = 94, x0 = 4 | Formula: x1 = x0 - (x0^2 - N)/(2 x0) | Substitute: x1 = 4 - ((4)^2 - 94)/(2*4) | Answer: 13.75

question: Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.1 and ordinates 18, 20, 3, 17, 9, estimate the integral.

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 22 and 58.

question: A circular rod of diameter 31 mm carries an axial tensile load of 7 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 17 mm and length 2500 mm carries an axial load of 78 kN. Take E = 200 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 47 mm transmits a torque of 1300 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.

question: A shaft of diameter 52 mm and length 2000 mm carries a torque of 2000 N-m. With G = 80 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.

question: A rectangular beam section is 145 mm wide and 270 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 145, h = 270 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 145*(270)^2 / 6 | Answer: 1761750 mm^3
