question: A component of ultimate strength 540 MPa is designed for a working stress of 190 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 540, sw = 190 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 540 / 190 | Answer: 2.842

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 700 mm and wall thickness 12 mm carries an internal pressure of 2.3 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 700, t = 12, P = 2.3 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 2.3*700 / (2*12) | Answer: 67.08 MPa

question: A refrigerator works between 273 K (cold) and 310 K (hot). Find the maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 273, Th = 310 | Formula: COP_ref = Tc / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 273 / (310 - 273) | Answer: 7.378

question: A heat pump operates between 261 K and 312 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 261, Th = 312 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 312 / (312 - 261) | Answer: 6.118

question: 6.1 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 135 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 6.1, dT = 135 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 6.1 * 0.718 * 135 | Answer: 591.3 kJ

question: 7.2 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 110 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 7.2, dT = 110 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 7.2 * 1.005 * 110 | Answer: 796 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 3.7 m^3 at 400 K with mass 2.1 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 3.7, Tk = 400, m = 2.1 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 2.1*0.287*400 / 3.7 | Answer: 65.16 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 2.4 kg of air expands isothermally at 450 K from volume V1 to 3*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.4, Tk = 450, ratio = 3 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 2.4*0.287*450*ln(3) | Answer: 340.5 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 2.9 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.18 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 2.9, D = 0.18 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*2.9*0.18 / 0.001 | Answer: 522000

question: Water flows at 0.7 m/s through a pipe of diameter 230 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 11.4 m. Taking Cv = 0.98, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 11.4, cv = 0.98 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.98*sqrt(2*9.81*11.4) | Answer: 14.66 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 210 mm) water flows at 2.7 m/s. It contracts to diameter 110 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 210, d2 = 110, V1 = 2.7 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 2.7*(210/110)^2 | Answer: 9.84 m/s

question: Water flows at 2.3 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.29 m and length 60 m. With friction factor f = 0.036, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 35 teeth drives a gear of 116 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1050 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 35, z2 = 116, N1 = 1050 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1050*35 / 116 | Answer: 316.8 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 520 mm rotates at 1000 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 520, N = 1000 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.52)*1000 / 60 | Answer: 27.23 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 17.7 kW at 1000 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 17.7, N = 1000 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(17.7*1000) / (2*pi*1000) | Answer: 169 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 1.2 kg rotates at radius 0.45 m at 1000 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 2300 N/m and mass 3.3 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 2300, m = 3.3 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(2300/3.3) | Answer: 4.202 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 5.5 m^2 and thickness 0.39 m has conductivity k = 12.4 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 135 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 5.5, L = 0.39, k = 12.4, dT = 135 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 12.4*5.5*135 / 0.39 | Answer: 23608 W

question: A surface of area 2.6 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 90 W/m^2-K to surroundings 105 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 2.6, h = 90, dT = 105 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 90*2.6*105 | Answer: 24570 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 130 m/min, feed = 0.13 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2.9 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 130, f = 0.13, d = 2.9 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*130*0.13*2.9 | Answer: 49010 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 400 mm is turned at 1200 rpm with a feed of 0.35 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 400, N = 1200, f = 0.35 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 400 / (0.35*1200) | Answer: 0.9524 min

question: A resistor of 3 ohm carries a current of 9.4 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 3, I = 9.4 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 9.4 * 3 | Answer: 28.2 V

question: Three resistors 77 ohm, 22 ohm and 22 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 77, R2 = 22, R3 = 22 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 77 + 22 + 22 | Answer: 121 ohm

question: Two resistors 90 ohm and 120 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 90, R2 = 120 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 90*120 / (90+120) | Answer: 51.43 ohm

question: A device draws 14.9 A at 15 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 15, I = 14.9 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 15 * 14.9 | Answer: 223.5 W

question: A current of 11.7 A flows through a 33 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 11.7, R = 33 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (11.7)^2 * 33 | Answer: 4517 W

question: Two capacitors 11.2 uF and 8.1 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 11.2, C2 = 8.1 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 11.2*8.1 / (11.2+8.1) | Answer: 4.701 uF

question: A resistor 81 kohm and capacitor 10 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 81, C = 10 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (81k)(10u) = 810 ms | Answer: 810 ms

question: An inductor 203.7 mH is in series with 66 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 203.7, R = 66 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (203.7e-3) / 66 | Answer: 3.086 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 57.4 mH inductor at 800 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 57.4, f = 800 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (800)(57.4e-3) | Answer: 288.5 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 44.9 uF capacitor at 820 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 44.9, f = 820 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (820)(44.9e-6)) | Answer: 4.323 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 82 ohm, XL = 91 ohm and XC = 112 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 82, XL = 91, XC = 112 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(82^2 + (91 - 112)^2) | Answer: 84.65 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 49 mH and C = 1.2 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 49, C = 1.2 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(49e-3 * 1.2e-6)) | Answer: 656.3 Hz

question: A capacitor of 82.9 uF is charged to 355 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 82.9, V = 355 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*82.9e-6*(355)^2 | Answer: 5224 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 130 V with 660 primary turns and 30 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 130, N1 = 660, N2 = 30 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 130 * 30/660 | Answer: 5.909 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 300 V and draws an armature current of 21 A. If the armature resistance is 1.4 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 300, Ia = 21, Ra = 1.4 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 300 - 21*1.4 | Answer: 270.6 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 100 A at 415 V (line) with a power factor of 0.76. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 100, VL = 415, pf = 0.76 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*415*100*0.76 / 1000 | Answer: 54.63 kW

question: A load has real power 100 kW and apparent power 125 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 100, S = 125 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 100 / 125 | Answer: 0.8

question: A machine delivers 55 kW output while drawing 87 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 55, Pi = 87 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 55/87 * 100 | Answer: 63.22 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 25 V across R1 = 6 ohm and R2 = 14 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 25, R1 = 6, R2 = 14 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 25*14 / (6+14) | Answer: 17.5 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 20 kohm and Rin = 11 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 20, Rin = 11 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 20 / 11 | Answer: 1.818

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 130 kohm and Rg = 37 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 130, Rg = 37 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 130/37 | Answer: 4.514

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 7444. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 7444 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(7444) | Answer: 38.72 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 5.7 m carries a central point load of 120 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.7, W = 120 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 120*5.7 / 4 | Answer: 171 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.7 m carries a UDL of 55 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 9.7, w = 55 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 55*(9.7)^2 / 8 | Answer: 646.9 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 5.9 m carries a point load 15 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.9, W = 15 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 15*5.9 | Answer: 88.5 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 3.5 m carries a UDL of 10 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.5, w = 10 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 10*(3.5)^2 / 2 | Answer: 61.25 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 8.6 m carries a point load 45 kN at distance 2 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 8.6, a = 2, W = 45 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 45*(8.6 - 2) / 8.6 | Answer: 34.53 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 7.8 m) carries a central point load 25 kN. With E = 25 GPa and I = 340e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=25000 N, L=7800.0 mm, E=25000 MPa, I=340e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 29.08 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 5.2 m carries a UDL of 6 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.2, w = 6 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 6*(5.2)^2 / 12 | Answer: 13.52 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 400 mm, clear cover 40 mm and main bars of diameter 25 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 400, c = 40, dia = 25 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 400 - 40 - 25/2 | Answer: 347.5 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 27 m^2 carrying a factored load of 19.6 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 27, w = 19.6 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 19.6 * 27 | Answer: 529.2 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 5.4 m, unit weight 20 kN/m^3, phi = 35 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 3.8 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 19 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 3.8, g = 19 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (19 - 9.81)*3.8 | Answer: 34.92 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 1.3e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1, area = 1.2e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 1.3, i = 1, A = 1.2 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (1.3e-4)*1*(1.2e-3) | Answer: 156 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.9 m, bed slope 0.007 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.029. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 4.5 m under a head of 0.9 m. Taking Cd = 0.64 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 4.9 m wide carries a discharge of 14.5 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 560 m and design speed 65 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 560, V = 65 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (65)^2 / (127*560) | Answer: 0.05941
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: A tank of volume 480 m^3 treats a flow of 175 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 480, Q = 175 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 480 / 175 | Answer: 2.743 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 210 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.24 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 8 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 210, k = 0.24, t = 8 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 210*(1 - e^(-0.24*8)) | Answer: 179.2 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.71, rainfall intensity 105 mm/h over a catchment of 10.1 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.71, i = 105, A = 10.1 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.71*105*10.1 / 360 | Answer: 2.092 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.05 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 570 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.05, M = 570 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 570*(30+0.05)/30 | Answer: 571 m

question: Convert the decimal number 1313 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 1313 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 521 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 10010111 and 00001010.
solution: XOR: 10011101 | Count of 1s = 5 | Answer: 5
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 980 megabits is sent over a link of 33 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 980, B = 33 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 980 / 33 | Answer: 29.7 s

question: A link has bandwidth 64 Mbps and round-trip time 40 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 64, R = 40 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 64e6 * 40e-3 bits = 2560 kb | Answer: 2560 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.85, cache access time 5 ns and main-memory access time 60 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.85, tc = 5, tm = 60 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.85*5 + (1 - 0.85)*60 | Answer: 13.25 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 970083 elements?
solution: Given: n = 970083 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(970083)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.01, memory access time 80 ns and page-fault service time 4 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 4 ms = 4000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.01)*80 + 0.01*4000000.0 ns | Answer: 40.08 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 0.4 m^3 at 260 kPa and 420 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 0.4, P = 260, Tk = 420 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (260e3)*0.4 / (8.314*420) | Answer: 29.78 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.3 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 8 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.3, t = 8 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.3*8) | Answer: 0.9093

question: For a reaction with A = 8e10 /s and activation energy 85 kJ/mol at 450 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 8, Ea = 85, Tk = 450 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 8e10 * exp(-85e3 / (8.314*450)) | Answer: 10.87 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.98 and bottoms xW = 0.09, with relative volatility alpha = 2.8. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.98, xw = 0.09, al = 2.8 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.98/0.02)(0.91/0.09)] / ln(2.8) | Answer: 6.027 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.69 and x = 0.39. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.69, x = 0.39 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.69/0.31) / (0.39/0.61) | Answer: 3.481

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.32 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 100 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.32, Psat = 100 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.32 * 100 | Answer: 32 kPa

question: A stream of 6.9 kg/s with specific heat 2.5 kJ/kg-K is heated through 100 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 6.9, cp = 2.5, dT = 100 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 6.9*2.5*100 | Answer: 1725 kW

question: A reactor of volume 1.8 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 0.5 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 1.8, Q = 0.5 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 1.8 / 0.5 | Answer: 3.6 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 5.7e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 3 mm with a concentration difference of 200 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 5.7, L = 3, dC = 200 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (5.7e-9)*200 / (3e-3) | Answer: 380 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 3.7 min and steady-state gain 4. For a step input of magnitude 4, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 3.7, K = 4, M = 4 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 4 * 4 | Answer: 16 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 35 m^2 flies at 230 m/s (air density 1.225 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.8. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 35, V = 230, rho = 1.225, CL = 0.8 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1.225*(230)^2*35*0.8 / 1000 | Answer: 907.2 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 55 m^2 flies at 130 m/s (density 1.225 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.04. Find the drag force in kN.
A specimen under stress 200 MPa shows an elastic strain of 2.4e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 200, eps = 2.4 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 200 / (2.4e-3) MPa = 83.33 GPa | Answer: 83.33 GPa

question: A block of mass 37 kg has a volume of 1e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 37, V = 1 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 37 / (1e-3) | Answer: 37000 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 1100 mm is heated through 35 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 23e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 1100, dT = 35, al = 23 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 1100*23e-6*35 | Answer: 0.8855 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 105 ohm, R2 = 125 ohm and R3 = 295 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 105, R2 = 125, R3 = 295 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 125*295 / 105 | Answer: 351.2 ohm

question: A measurement reads 9.66 when the true value is 100. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.66, true = 100 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.66 - 100| / 100 * 100 | Answer: 90.34 %

question: Annual demand is 22500 units, ordering cost 170 per order and holding cost 33 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 22500, S = 170, H = 33 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*22500*170 / 33) | Answer: 481.5 units

question: An asset costs 400000 with salvage value 22000 after 14 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 400000, Sv = 22000, n = 14 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (400000 - 22000) / 14 | Answer: 27000 per year

question: A product sells for 420 per unit with variable cost 140 per unit and fixed costs 115000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 420, V = 140, F = 115000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 115000 / (420 - 140) | Answer: 410.7 units

question: Find the present worth of 180000 received 10 years from now at an interest rate of 5% per year.
solution: Given: F = 180000, n = 10, i = 5 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 180000 / (1 + 0.05)^10 | Answer: 110504 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.97, 0.96 and 0.97 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.97, r2 = 0.96, r3 = 0.97 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.97*0.96*0.97 | Answer: 0.9033

question: A process produces 46 defective items in a batch of 10500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 46, N = 10500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 46/10500 * 1e6 | Answer: 4381 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = 2x^3 + 5x^2 + x + 5 evaluated at x = -1.
For f(x) = -6x^3 - x^2 - 8x + 8, find f''(x) at x = -2.
Evaluate the definite integral of (-5x^2 - 3x + 4) dx from x = 2 to x = 5.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = -5x^3/3 + -3x^2/2 + 4x | Evaluate F(5) - F(2) | Answer: -214.5
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 6x^2 + 11x + 2 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[0, -6], [0, -8]].
solution: Given: a = 0, b = -6, c = 0, d = -8 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (0)(-8) - (-6)(0) | Answer: 0

question: Find the determinant of [[-5, 6, -6], [-3, -1, -6], [0, 1, -6]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: -150

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[8, -8], [-8, -4]].
solution: Trace tr = 4, Determinant = -96 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 12

question: Solve for x: 6x + -2y = 10 and -6x + 4y = -9.
solution: Determinant = 6*4 - -2*-6 = 12 | x = (e d - b f) / det = 1.833 | Answer: x = 1.833
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 8, 20, 20, 4, 60.
solution: Sum = 112 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 22.4 | Answer: 22.4

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 29, 26, 8, 21, 18.
solution: Mean = 20.4 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 8.142

question: Find the slope of the line through (0, 4) and (7, -2).
solution: Given: x1 = 0, y1 = 4, x2 = 7, y2 = -2 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (-2 - 4) / (7 - 0) | Answer: -0.8571

question: Find the distance between the points (-8, 3) and (-4, 6).
solution: Given: x1 = -8, y1 = 3, x2 = -4, y2 = 6 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((4)^2 + (3)^2) | Answer: 5 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (2,6), (-1,-4), (-2,6).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 20 sq units

question: Find the 5th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -18 and common difference -4.
solution: Given: a = -18, d = -4, n = 5 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -18 + (5 - 1)*-4 | Answer: -34

question: Find the sum of the first 20 terms of an AP with first term 9 and common difference 2.
solution: Given: a = 9, d = 2, n = 20 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 20/2 [2*9 + (20-1)*2] | Answer: 560

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 17000 at 10.8% per annum for 2 years.
solution: Given: P = 17000, R = 10.8, Tt = 2 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 17000 * 10.8 * 2 / 100 | Answer: 3672 currency units

question: Find the amount when 6000 is invested at 6.2% per annum compounded annually for 5 years.
solution: Given: P = 6000, R = 6.2, Tt = 5 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 6000 * (1 + 6.2/100)^5 | Answer: 8105 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (7, 1, 5) and (-7, 4, 8).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (0, 4, -5) and (3, -6, 1).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 32.33

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (3, -6, 1) and (4, -5, 4).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 26.06 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number 10 + 10i.
solution: Given: a = 10, b = 10 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((10)^2 + (10)^2) | Answer: 14.14

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number 7 + -2i.
solution: Given: a = 7, b = -2 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(-2, 7) | Answer: -15.95 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -x^3 - 5x^2 - 4x + 6 at x = 4.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-164 with initial guess x0=15, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.9 and ordinates 9, 13, 12, 4, 3, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 202 and 320.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 202 and 320 | Answer: GCD = 2

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 73 and 19.
solution: Given: a = 73, b = 19 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 73*19 / 1 | Answer: 1387
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 30 mm carries an axial tensile load of 47 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 20 mm and length 2200 mm carries an axial load of 11 kN. Take E = 200 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 67 mm transmits a torque of 600 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 67, Tt = 600 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(600*1000) / (pi*(67)^3) | Answer: 10.16 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 34 mm and length 1800 mm carries a torque of 750 N-m. With G = 80 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (34)^4 / 32 = 131194 mm^4 | theta = (750*1000)(1800) / (80000 * 131194) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 7.37 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 74 mm wide and 150 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 74, h = 150 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 74*(150)^2 / 6 | Answer: 277500 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (92 mm x 220 mm) carries a bending moment of 8 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (49 mm x 90 mm) has effective length 2500 mm and E = 200 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 430 MPa is designed for a working stress of 140 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 430, sw = 140 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 430 / 140 | Answer: 3.071

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 600 mm and wall thickness 20 mm carries an internal pressure of 1.5 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 600, t = 20, P = 1.5 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 1.5*600 / (2*20) | Answer: 22.5 MPa

question: 7.2 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 140 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 7.2, dT = 140 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 7.2 * 0.718 * 140 | Answer: 723.7 kJ

question: 4.8 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 75 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.8, dT = 75 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 4.8 * 1.005 * 75 | Answer: 361.8 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 1.7 m^3 at 540 K with mass 4.4 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 1.7, Tk = 540, m = 4.4 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 4.4*0.287*540 / 1.7 | Answer: 401.1 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 2.6 kg of air expands isothermally at 350 K from volume V1 to 5*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.6, Tk = 350, ratio = 5 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 2.6*0.287*350*ln(5) | Answer: 420.3 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 2.3 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.4 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 2.3, D = 0.4 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*2.3*0.4 / 0.001 | Answer: 920000

question: Water flows at 3 m/s through a pipe of diameter 90 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 14.1 m. Taking Cv = 0.97, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 14.1, cv = 0.97 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.97*sqrt(2*9.81*14.1) | Answer: 16.13 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 320 mm) water flows at 2.2 m/s. It contracts to diameter 130 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
Water flows at 1.7 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.14 m and length 220 m. With friction factor f = 0.039, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 38 teeth drives a gear of 78 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1450 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 38, z2 = 78, N1 = 1450 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1450*38 / 78 | Answer: 706.4 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 230 mm rotates at 950 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 230, N = 950 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.23)*950 / 60 | Answer: 11.44 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 4 kW at 1000 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 4, N = 1000 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(4*1000) / (2*pi*1000) | Answer: 38.2 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 6.6 kg rotates at radius 0.22 m at 600 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 6600 N/m and mass 1.6 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 6600, m = 1.6 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(6600/1.6) | Answer: 10.22 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 7 m^2 and thickness 0.37 m has conductivity k = 39.2 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 140 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 7, L = 0.37, k = 39.2, dT = 140 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 39.2*7*140 / 0.37 | Answer: 103827 W

question: A surface of area 3.4 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 35 W/m^2-K to surroundings 100 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 3.4, h = 35, dT = 100 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 35*3.4*100 | Answer: 11900 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 200 m/min, feed = 0.22 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2.8 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 200, f = 0.22, d = 2.8 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*200*0.22*2.8 | Answer: 123200 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 330 mm is turned at 350 rpm with a feed of 0.19 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 330, N = 350, f = 0.19 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 330 / (0.19*350) | Answer: 4.962 min

question: A resistor of 103 ohm carries a current of 6.3 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 103, I = 6.3 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 6.3 * 103 | Answer: 648.9 V

question: Three resistors 73 ohm, 3 ohm and 51 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 73, R2 = 3, R3 = 51 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 73 + 3 + 51 | Answer: 127 ohm

question: Two resistors 16 ohm and 119 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 16, R2 = 119 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 16*119 / (16+119) | Answer: 14.1 ohm

question: A device draws 5.8 A at 45 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 45, I = 5.8 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 45 * 5.8 | Answer: 261 W

question: A current of 7 A flows through a 53 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 7, R = 53 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (7)^2 * 53 | Answer: 2597 W

question: Two capacitors 8 uF and 45.2 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 8, C2 = 45.2 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 8*45.2 / (8+45.2) | Answer: 6.797 uF

question: A resistor 21 kohm and capacitor 6.3 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 21, C = 6.3 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (21k)(6.3u) = 132.3 ms | Answer: 132.3 ms

question: An inductor 269.2 mH is in series with 113 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 269.2, R = 113 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (269.2e-3) / 113 | Answer: 2.382 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 90.3 mH inductor at 270 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 90.3, f = 270 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (270)(90.3e-3) | Answer: 153.2 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 27.1 uF capacitor at 210 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 27.1, f = 210 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (210)(27.1e-6)) | Answer: 27.97 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 73 ohm, XL = 81 ohm and XC = 137 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 73, XL = 81, XC = 137 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(73^2 + (81 - 137)^2) | Answer: 92.01 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 55.3 mH and C = 3.9 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 55.3, C = 3.9 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(55.3e-3 * 3.9e-6)) | Answer: 342.7 Hz

question: A capacitor of 17.6 uF is charged to 45 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 17.6, V = 45 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*17.6e-6*(45)^2 | Answer: 17.82 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 140 V with 450 primary turns and 380 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 140, N1 = 450, N2 = 380 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 140 * 380/450 | Answer: 118.2 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 360 V and draws an armature current of 8 A. If the armature resistance is 1.03 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 360, Ia = 8, Ra = 1.03 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 360 - 8*1.03 | Answer: 351.8 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 105 A at 415 V (line) with a power factor of 0.78. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 105, VL = 415, pf = 0.78 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*415*105*0.78 / 1000 | Answer: 58.87 kW

question: A load has real power 10 kW and apparent power 175 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 10, S = 175 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 10 / 175 | Answer: 0.05714

question: A machine delivers 10 kW output while drawing 102 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 10, Pi = 102 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 10/102 * 100 | Answer: 9.804 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 12 V across R1 = 26 ohm and R2 = 37 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 12, R1 = 26, R2 = 37 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 12*37 / (26+37) | Answer: 7.048 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 170 kohm and Rin = 21 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 170, Rin = 21 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 170 / 21 | Answer: 8.095

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 130 kohm and Rg = 42 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 130, Rg = 42 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 130/42 | Answer: 4.095

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 6117. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 6117 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(6117) | Answer: 37.87 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 7.3 m carries a central point load of 95 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7.3, W = 95 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 95*7.3 / 4 | Answer: 173.4 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.6 m carries a UDL of 55 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6.6, w = 55 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 55*(6.6)^2 / 8 | Answer: 299.5 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 5.7 m carries a point load 20 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.7, W = 20 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 20*5.7 | Answer: 114 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 5.8 m carries a UDL of 32 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.8, w = 32 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 32*(5.8)^2 / 2 | Answer: 538.2 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 7 m carries a point load 70 kN at distance 2.6 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 7, a = 2.6, W = 70 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 70*(7 - 2.6) / 7 | Answer: 44 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 3.7 m) carries a central point load 60 kN. With E = 30 GPa and I = 390e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=60000 N, L=3700.0 mm, E=30000 MPa, I=390e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 5.412 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 6.7 m carries a UDL of 18 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6.7, w = 18 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 18*(6.7)^2 / 12 | Answer: 67.33 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 590 mm, clear cover 45 mm and main bars of diameter 25 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 590, c = 45, dia = 25 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 590 - 45 - 25/2 | Answer: 532.5 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 21.3 m^2 carrying a factored load of 19.8 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 21.3, w = 19.8 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 19.8 * 21.3 | Answer: 421.7 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 3.7 m, unit weight 18 kN/m^3, phi = 35 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 4.1e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.7, area = 1.4e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 4.1, i = 0.7, A = 1.4 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (4.1e-4)*0.7*(1.4e-3) | Answer: 401.8 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.9 m, bed slope 0.006 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.028. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 2 m under a head of 0.8 m. Taking Cd = 0.61 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 4.4 m wide carries a discharge of 14.6 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 240 m and design speed 80 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 240, V = 80 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (80)^2 / (127*240) | Answer: 0.21
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: A tank of volume 320 m^3 treats a flow of 115 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 320, Q = 115 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 320 / 115 | Answer: 2.783 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 290 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.15 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 3 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 290, k = 0.15, t = 3 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 290*(1 - e^(-0.15*3)) | Answer: 105.1 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.62, rainfall intensity 90 mm/h over a catchment of 23.9 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.62, i = 90, A = 23.9 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.62*90*23.9 / 360 | Answer: 3.704 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.06 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 380 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.06, M = 380 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 380*(20+0.06)/20 | Answer: 381.1 m

question: Convert the decimal number 515 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 515 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 203 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 10111100 and 11010110.
solution: XOR: 01101010 | Count of 1s = 4 | Answer: 4
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 940 megabits is sent over a link of 41 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 940, B = 41 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 940 / 41 | Answer: 22.93 s

question: A link has bandwidth 64 Mbps and round-trip time 140 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 64, R = 140 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 64e6 * 140e-3 bits = 8960 kb | Answer: 8960 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.88, cache access time 7 ns and main-memory access time 160 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.88, tc = 7, tm = 160 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.88*7 + (1 - 0.88)*160 | Answer: 25.36 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 695954 elements?
solution: Given: n = 695954 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(695954)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.018, memory access time 120 ns and page-fault service time 4 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 4 ms = 4000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.018)*120 + 0.018*4000000.0 ns | Answer: 72.12 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 1.1 m^3 at 410 kPa and 410 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 1.1, P = 410, Tk = 410 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (410e3)*1.1 / (8.314*410) | Answer: 132.3 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.22 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 14 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.22, t = 14 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.22*14) | Answer: 0.954

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.13 /min) is to reach 85% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.13, X = 85 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.85) / 0.13 | Answer: 14.59 min

question: For a reaction with A = 3e10 /s and activation energy 85 kJ/mol at 300 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 3, Ea = 85, Tk = 300 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 3e10 * exp(-85e3 / (8.314*300)) | Answer: 0.00004751 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.96 and bottoms xW = 0.02, with relative volatility alpha = 2.3. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.96, xw = 0.02, al = 2.3 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.96/0.04)(0.98/0.02)] / ln(2.3) | Answer: 8.488 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.72 and x = 0.45. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.72, x = 0.45 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.72/0.28) / (0.45/0.55) | Answer: 3.143

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.34 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 85 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.34, Psat = 85 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.34 * 85 | Answer: 28.9 kPa

question: A stream of 2.4 kg/s with specific heat 3 kJ/kg-K is heated through 15 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 2.4, cp = 3, dT = 15 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 2.4*3*15 | Answer: 108 kW

question: A reactor of volume 10.5 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 0.4 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 10.5, Q = 0.4 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 10.5 / 0.4 | Answer: 26.25 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 6.5e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 2 mm with a concentration difference of 200 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 6.5, L = 2, dC = 200 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (6.5e-9)*200 / (2e-3) | Answer: 650 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 8 min and steady-state gain 3.5. For a step input of magnitude 18, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 8, K = 3.5, M = 18 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 3.5 * 18 | Answer: 63 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 70 m^2 flies at 60 m/s (air density 1 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.5. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 70, V = 60, rho = 1, CL = 0.5 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1*(60)^2*70*0.5 / 1000 | Answer: 63 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 105 m^2 flies at 110 m/s (density 1 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.12. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 105, V = 110, rho = 1, CD = 0.12 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*1*(110)^2*105*0.12 / 1000 | Answer: 76.23 kN

question: A specimen under stress 110 MPa shows an elastic strain of 0.8e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 110, eps = 0.8 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 110 / (0.8e-3) MPa = 137.5 GPa | Answer: 137.5 GPa

question: A block of mass 25 kg has a volume of 3.7e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 25, V = 3.7 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 25 / (3.7e-3) | Answer: 6757 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 1300 mm is heated through 135 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 23e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 1300, dT = 135, al = 23 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 1300*23e-6*135 | Answer: 4.037 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 80 ohm, R2 = 190 ohm and R3 = 340 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 80, R2 = 190, R3 = 340 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 190*340 / 80 | Answer: 807.5 ohm

question: A measurement reads 10.84 when the true value is 10. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10.84, true = 10 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10.84 - 10| / 10 * 100 | Answer: 8.4 %

question: Annual demand is 50000 units, ordering cost 20 per order and holding cost 10 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 50000, S = 20, H = 10 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*50000*20 / 10) | Answer: 447.2 units

question: An asset costs 130000 with salvage value 14000 after 15 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 130000, Sv = 14000, n = 15 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (130000 - 14000) / 15 | Answer: 7733 per year

question: A product sells for 250 per unit with variable cost 40 per unit and fixed costs 70000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 250, V = 40, F = 70000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 70000 / (250 - 40) | Answer: 333.3 units

question: Find the present worth of 40000 received 5 years from now at an interest rate of 5% per year.
solution: Given: F = 40000, n = 5, i = 5 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 40000 / (1 + 0.05)^5 | Answer: 31341 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.99, 0.94 and 0.94 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.99, r2 = 0.94, r3 = 0.94 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.99*0.94*0.94 | Answer: 0.8748

question: A process produces 16 defective items in a batch of 13000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 16, N = 13000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 16/13000 * 1e6 | Answer: 1231 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -3x^3 - 6x^2 - 9x evaluated at x = 4.
For f(x) = -4x^3 + 5x^2 + 6x - 7, find f''(x) at x = -4.
Evaluate the definite integral of (-2x^2 + x + 1) dx from x = -2 to x = 3.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = -2x^3/3 + 1x^2/2 + 1x | Evaluate F(3) - F(-2) | Answer: -15.83
