solution: Given: z1 = 22, z2 = 75, N1 = 1400 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1400*22 / 75 | Answer: 410.7 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 230 mm rotates at 1450 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 230, N = 1450 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.23)*1450 / 60 | Answer: 17.46 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 10.6 kW at 450 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 10.6, N = 450 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(10.6*1000) / (2*pi*450) | Answer: 224.9 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 8.6 kg rotates at radius 0.4 m at 350 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 13300 N/m and mass 19.7 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 13300, m = 19.7 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(13300/19.7) | Answer: 4.135 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 2.4 m^2 and thickness 0.11 m has conductivity k = 40.3 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 120 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 2.4, L = 0.11, k = 40.3, dT = 120 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 40.3*2.4*120 / 0.11 | Answer: 105513 W

question: A surface of area 2.9 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 160 W/m^2-K to surroundings 125 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 2.9, h = 160, dT = 125 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 160*2.9*125 | Answer: 58000 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 80 m/min, feed = 0.21 mm/rev, depth of cut = 3 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 80, f = 0.21, d = 3 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*80*0.21*3 | Answer: 50400 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 170 mm is turned at 700 rpm with a feed of 0.11 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 170, N = 700, f = 0.11 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 170 / (0.11*700) | Answer: 2.208 min

question: A resistor of 30 ohm carries a current of 0.3 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 30, I = 0.3 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 0.3 * 30 | Answer: 9 V

question: Three resistors 21 ohm, 20 ohm and 66 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 21, R2 = 20, R3 = 66 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 21 + 20 + 66 | Answer: 107 ohm

question: Two resistors 46 ohm and 95 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 46, R2 = 95 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 46*95 / (46+95) | Answer: 30.99 ohm

question: A device draws 2 A at 130 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 130, I = 2 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 130 * 2 | Answer: 260 W

question: A current of 0.5 A flows through a 32 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 0.5, R = 32 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (0.5)^2 * 32 | Answer: 8 W

question: Two capacitors 36.2 uF and 19.2 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 36.2, C2 = 19.2 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 36.2*19.2 / (36.2+19.2) | Answer: 12.55 uF

question: A resistor 38 kohm and capacitor 3.9 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 38, C = 3.9 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (38k)(3.9u) = 148.2 ms | Answer: 148.2 ms

question: An inductor 68 mH is in series with 76 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 68, R = 76 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (68e-3) / 76 | Answer: 0.8947 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 77.8 mH inductor at 230 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 77.8, f = 230 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (230)(77.8e-3) | Answer: 112.4 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 33.2 uF capacitor at 380 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 33.2, f = 380 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (380)(33.2e-6)) | Answer: 12.62 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 79 ohm, XL = 39 ohm and XC = 32 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 79, XL = 39, XC = 32 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(79^2 + (39 - 32)^2) | Answer: 79.31 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 86.4 mH and C = 3.3 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 86.4, C = 3.3 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(86.4e-3 * 3.3e-6)) | Answer: 298.1 Hz

question: A capacitor of 26.4 uF is charged to 115 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 26.4, V = 115 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*26.4e-6*(115)^2 | Answer: 174.6 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 310 V with 610 primary turns and 90 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 310, N1 = 610, N2 = 90 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 310 * 90/610 | Answer: 45.74 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 170 V and draws an armature current of 54 A. If the armature resistance is 1.01 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 170, Ia = 54, Ra = 1.01 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 170 - 54*1.01 | Answer: 115.5 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 185 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.7. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 185, VL = 400, pf = 0.7 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*400*185*0.7 / 1000 | Answer: 89.72 kW

question: A load has real power 25 kW and apparent power 205 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 25, S = 205 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 25 / 205 | Answer: 0.122

question: A machine delivers 125 kW output while drawing 147 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 125, Pi = 147 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 125/147 * 100 | Answer: 85.03 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 28 V across R1 = 42 ohm and R2 = 20 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 28, R1 = 42, R2 = 20 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 28*20 / (42+20) | Answer: 9.032 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 70 kohm and Rin = 46 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 70, Rin = 46 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 70 / 46 | Answer: 1.522

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 20 kohm and Rg = 17 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 20, Rg = 17 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 20/17 | Answer: 2.176

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 7593. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 7593 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(7593) | Answer: 38.8 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.6 m carries a central point load of 45 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 9.6, W = 45 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 45*9.6 / 4 | Answer: 108 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 8.8 m carries a UDL of 45 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 8.8, w = 45 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 45*(8.8)^2 / 8 | Answer: 435.6 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 1.5 m carries a point load 70 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 1.5, W = 70 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 70*1.5 | Answer: 105 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 5.7 m carries a UDL of 32 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.7, w = 32 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 32*(5.7)^2 / 2 | Answer: 519.8 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.3 m carries a point load 55 kN at distance 1.6 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 9.3, a = 1.6, W = 55 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 55*(9.3 - 1.6) / 9.3 | Answer: 45.54 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 3.3 m) carries a central point load 55 kN. With E = 25 GPa and I = 520e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=55000 N, L=3300.0 mm, E=25000 MPa, I=520e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 3.168 mm

question: An RC beam has overall depth 650 mm, clear cover 50 mm and main bars of diameter 20 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 650, c = 50, dia = 20 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 650 - 50 - 20/2 | Answer: 590 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 20.9 m^2 carrying a factored load of 18.6 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 20.9, w = 18.6 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 18.6 * 20.9 | Answer: 388.7 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 6.6 m, unit weight 18 kN/m^3, phi = 30 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: At a depth of 10.3 m in a saturated soil (saturated unit weight 21 kN/m^3, water table at surface), find the effective vertical stress in kPa (gamma_w = 9.81).
solution: Given: z = 10.3, g = 21 | Formula: sigma' = (gamma_sat - gamma_w) z | Substitute: sigma' = (21 - 9.81)*10.3 | Answer: 115.3 kPa

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 1.4e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1, area = 2.6e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 1.4, i = 1, A = 2.6 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (1.4e-4)*1*(2.6e-3) | Answer: 364 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.2 m, bed slope 0.009 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.014. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 4.9 m under a head of 0.4 m. Taking Cd = 0.6 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 3.8 m wide carries a discharge of 16.2 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 440 m and design speed 75 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 440, V = 75 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (75)^2 / (127*440) | Answer: 0.1007
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: A tank of volume 170 m^3 treats a flow of 95 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 170, Q = 95 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 170 / 95 | Answer: 1.789 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 170 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.29 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 7 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 170, k = 0.29, t = 7 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 170*(1 - e^(-0.29*7)) | Answer: 147.7 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.48, rainfall intensity 45 mm/h over a catchment of 39.2 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.48, i = 45, A = 39.2 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.48*45*39.2 / 360 | Answer: 2.352 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.08 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 680 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.08, M = 680 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 680*(30+0.08)/30 | Answer: 681.8 m

question: Convert the decimal number 1207 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 1207 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 4B7 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 10111101 and 00110110.
solution: XOR: 10001011 | Count of 1s = 4 | Answer: 4
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 40 megabits is sent over a link of 8 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 40, B = 8 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 40 / 8 | Answer: 5 s

question: A link has bandwidth 85 Mbps and round-trip time 190 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 85, R = 190 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 85e6 * 190e-3 bits = 16150 kb | Answer: 16150 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.94, cache access time 10 ns and main-memory access time 80 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.94, tc = 10, tm = 80 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.94*10 + (1 - 0.94)*80 | Answer: 14.2 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 772229 elements?
solution: Given: n = 772229 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(772229)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.017, memory access time 160 ns and page-fault service time 7 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 7 ms = 7000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.017)*160 + 0.017*7000000.0 ns | Answer: 119.2 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 1.6 m^3 at 400 kPa and 400 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 1.6, P = 400, Tk = 400 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (400e3)*1.6 / (8.314*400) | Answer: 192.4 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.09 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 9 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.09, t = 9 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.09*9) | Answer: 0.5551

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.12 /min) is to reach 50% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.12, X = 50 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.5) / 0.12 | Answer: 5.776 min

question: For a reaction with A = 8e10 /s and activation energy 90 kJ/mol at 330 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 8, Ea = 90, Tk = 330 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 8e10 * exp(-90e3 / (8.314*330)) | Answer: 0.0004537 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.95 and bottoms xW = 0.09, with relative volatility alpha = 1.9. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.95, xw = 0.09, al = 1.9 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.95/0.05)(0.91/0.09)] / ln(1.9) | Answer: 8.192 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.68 and x = 0.3. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.68, x = 0.3 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.68/0.32) / (0.3/0.7) | Answer: 4.958

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.22 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 65 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.22, Psat = 65 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.22 * 65 | Answer: 14.3 kPa

question: A stream of 2 kg/s with specific heat 1.2 kJ/kg-K is heated through 70 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 2, cp = 1.2, dT = 70 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 2*1.2*70 | Answer: 168 kW

question: A reactor of volume 9.6 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 1.7 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 9.6, Q = 1.7 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 9.6 / 1.7 | Answer: 5.647 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 1.3e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 4 mm with a concentration difference of 70 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 1.3, L = 4, dC = 70 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (1.3e-9)*70 / (4e-3) | Answer: 22.75 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 2 min and steady-state gain 3.4. For a step input of magnitude 2, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 2, K = 3.4, M = 2 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 3.4 * 2 | Answer: 6.8 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 35 m^2 flies at 260 m/s (air density 0.7 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.6. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 35, V = 260, rho = 0.7, CL = 0.6 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.7*(260)^2*35*0.6 / 1000 | Answer: 496.9 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 40 m^2 flies at 120 m/s (density 0.4 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.1. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 40, V = 120, rho = 0.4, CD = 0.1 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.4*(120)^2*40*0.1 / 1000 | Answer: 11.52 kN

question: A specimen under stress 120 MPa shows an elastic strain of 3e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 120, eps = 3 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 120 / (3e-3) MPa = 40 GPa | Answer: 40 GPa

question: A block of mass 15 kg has a volume of 5.9e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 15, V = 5.9 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 15 / (5.9e-3) | Answer: 2542 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 2900 mm is heated through 65 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 23e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 2900, dT = 65, al = 23 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 2900*23e-6*65 | Answer: 4.335 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 90 ohm, R2 = 60 ohm and R3 = 285 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 90, R2 = 60, R3 = 285 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 60*285 / 90 | Answer: 190 ohm

question: A measurement reads 9.62 when the true value is 20. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.62, true = 20 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.62 - 20| / 20 * 100 | Answer: 51.9 %

question: Annual demand is 3500 units, ordering cost 180 per order and holding cost 39 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 3500, S = 180, H = 39 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*3500*180 / 39) | Answer: 179.7 units

question: An asset costs 350000 with salvage value 40000 after 9 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 350000, Sv = 40000, n = 9 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (350000 - 40000) / 9 | Answer: 34444 per year

question: A product sells for 340 per unit with variable cost 120 per unit and fixed costs 145000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 340, V = 120, F = 145000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 145000 / (340 - 120) | Answer: 659.1 units

question: Find the present worth of 15000 received 9 years from now at an interest rate of 12% per year.
solution: Given: F = 15000, n = 9, i = 12 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 15000 / (1 + 0.12)^9 | Answer: 5409 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.91, 0.97 and 0.92 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.91, r2 = 0.97, r3 = 0.92 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.91*0.97*0.92 | Answer: 0.8121

question: A process produces 42 defective items in a batch of 9500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 42, N = 9500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 42/9500 * 1e6 | Answer: 4421 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = 3x^3 + x^2 - 6x - 9 evaluated at x = -4.
For f(x) = -2x^3 + 4x^2 + 5x - 9, find f''(x) at x = 4.
Evaluate the definite integral of (-5x^2 - x - 2) dx from x = -4 to x = 5.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = -5x^3/3 + -1x^2/2 + -2x | Evaluate F(5) - F(-4) | Answer: -337.5
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 6x^2 + 11x - 3 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[-5, -4], [-5, 7]].
solution: Given: a = -5, b = -4, c = -5, d = 7 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (-5)(7) - (-4)(-5) | Answer: -55

question: Find the determinant of [[6, 6, 0], [-3, 1, -5], [-1, 5, 0]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: 180

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[-3, -4], [2, 4]].
solution: Trace tr = 1, Determinant = -4 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 2.562

question: Solve for x: 5x + -5y = -11 and 2x + 4y = 8.
solution: Determinant = 5*4 - -5*2 = 30 | x = (e d - b f) / det = -0.1333 | Answer: x = -0.1333
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 54, 12, 95, 33, 82.
solution: Sum = 276 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 55.2 | Answer: 55.2

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 18, 9, 40, 39, 36.
solution: Mean = 28.4 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 14.05

question: Find the slope of the line through (5, 7) and (7, 1).
solution: Given: x1 = 5, y1 = 7, x2 = 7, y2 = 1 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (1 - 7) / (7 - 5) | Answer: -3

question: Find the distance between the points (-5, -9) and (4, 4).
solution: Given: x1 = -5, y1 = -9, x2 = 4, y2 = 4 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((9)^2 + (13)^2) | Answer: 15.81 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (7,-2), (1,-8), (0,5).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 42 sq units

question: Find the 10th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -2 and common difference 7.
solution: Given: a = -2, d = 7, n = 10 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -2 + (10 - 1)*7 | Answer: 61

question: Find the sum of the first 30 terms of an AP with first term -9 and common difference 8.
solution: Given: a = -9, d = 8, n = 30 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 30/2 [2*-9 + (30-1)*8] | Answer: 3210

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 18500 at 9.3% per annum for 2 years.
solution: Given: P = 18500, R = 9.3, Tt = 2 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 18500 * 9.3 * 2 / 100 | Answer: 3441 currency units

question: Find the amount when 40000 is invested at 5.8% per annum compounded annually for 3 years.
solution: Given: P = 40000, R = 5.8, Tt = 3 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 40000 * (1 + 5.8/100)^3 | Answer: 47371 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (5, 7, -8) and (4, 4, -8).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (2, -2, 4) and (-6, 1, 0).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 26.31

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (3, 6, 0) and (4, 1, -4).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 62.15 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number -2 + -11i.
solution: Given: a = -2, b = -11 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((-2)^2 + (-11)^2) | Answer: 11.18

question: Evaluate f(x) = 3x^3 + 3x^2 - 2x - 9 at x = -1.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-65 with initial guess x0=7, find x1 (one iteration).
solution: Given: N = 65, x0 = 7 | Formula: x1 = x0 - (x0^2 - N)/(2 x0) | Substitute: x1 = 7 - ((7)^2 - 65)/(2*7) | Answer: 8.143

question: Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.4 and ordinates 17, 6, 17, 19, 10, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 75 and 517.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 75 and 517 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 13 and 67.
solution: Given: a = 13, b = 67 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 13*67 / 1 | Answer: 871
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 39 mm carries an axial tensile load of 22 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 12 mm and length 1400 mm carries an axial load of 43 kN. Take E = 70 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 46 mm transmits a torque of 2100 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 46, Tt = 2100 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(2100*1000) / (pi*(46)^3) | Answer: 109.9 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 33 mm and length 1500 mm carries a torque of 450 N-m. With G = 77 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (33)^4 / 32 = 116428 mm^4 | theta = (450*1000)(1500) / (77000 * 116428) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 4.314 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 107 mm wide and 210 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 107, h = 210 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 107*(210)^2 / 6 | Answer: 786450 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (55 mm x 230 mm) carries a bending moment of 34 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (49 mm x 160 mm) has effective length 2300 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 850 MPa is designed for a working stress of 60 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 850, sw = 60 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 850 / 60 | Answer: 14.17

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1400 mm and wall thickness 18 mm carries an internal pressure of 2.3 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1400, t = 18, P = 2.3 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 2.3*1400 / (2*18) | Answer: 89.44 MPa

question: A heat pump operates between 268 K and 312 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 268, Th = 312 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 312 / (312 - 268) | Answer: 7.091

question: 4.7 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 125 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.7, dT = 125 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 4.7 * 0.718 * 125 | Answer: 421.8 kJ

question: 6.6 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 135 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 6.6, dT = 135 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 6.6 * 1.005 * 135 | Answer: 895.5 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 2.1 m^3 at 360 K with mass 2.3 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 2.1, Tk = 360, m = 2.3 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 2.3*0.287*360 / 2.1 | Answer: 113.2 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 4.1 kg of air expands isothermally at 310 K from volume V1 to 5*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.1, Tk = 310, ratio = 5 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 4.1*0.287*310*ln(5) | Answer: 587.1 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 2.9 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.09 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 2.9, D = 0.09 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*2.9*0.09 / 0.001 | Answer: 261000

question: Water flows at 3.7 m/s through a pipe of diameter 70 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 11.2 m. Taking Cv = 0.97, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 11.2, cv = 0.97 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.97*sqrt(2*9.81*11.2) | Answer: 14.38 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 230 mm) water flows at 0.9 m/s. It contracts to diameter 60 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 230, d2 = 60, V1 = 0.9 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 0.9*(230/60)^2 | Answer: 13.23 m/s

question: Water flows at 3.7 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.48 m and length 110 m. With friction factor f = 0.021, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 25 teeth drives a gear of 108 teeth. If the pinion runs at 400 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 25, z2 = 108, N1 = 400 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 400*25 / 108 | Answer: 92.59 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 260 mm rotates at 1150 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 260, N = 1150 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.26)*1150 / 60 | Answer: 15.66 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 8.8 kW at 1350 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 8.8, N = 1350 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(8.8*1000) / (2*pi*1350) | Answer: 62.25 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 7.1 kg rotates at radius 0.22 m at 600 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 10300 N/m and mass 17.7 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 10300, m = 17.7 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(10300/17.7) | Answer: 3.839 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 1.8 m^2 and thickness 0.27 m has conductivity k = 2.5 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 145 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 1.8, L = 0.27, k = 2.5, dT = 145 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 2.5*1.8*145 / 0.27 | Answer: 2417 W

question: A surface of area 1.8 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 190 W/m^2-K to surroundings 120 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 1.8, h = 190, dT = 120 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 190*1.8*120 | Answer: 41040 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 110 m/min, feed = 0.44 mm/rev, depth of cut = 0.5 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 110, f = 0.44, d = 0.5 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*110*0.44*0.5 | Answer: 24200 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 310 mm is turned at 1050 rpm with a feed of 0.32 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 310, N = 1050, f = 0.32 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 310 / (0.32*1050) | Answer: 0.9226 min

question: A resistor of 94 ohm carries a current of 8.5 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 94, I = 8.5 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 8.5 * 94 | Answer: 799 V

question: Three resistors 55 ohm, 28 ohm and 42 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 55, R2 = 28, R3 = 42 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 55 + 28 + 42 | Answer: 125 ohm

question: Two resistors 66 ohm and 59 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 66, R2 = 59 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 66*59 / (66+59) | Answer: 31.15 ohm

question: A device draws 1.7 A at 185 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 185, I = 1.7 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 185 * 1.7 | Answer: 314.5 W

question: A current of 5.4 A flows through a 111 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 5.4, R = 111 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (5.4)^2 * 111 | Answer: 3237 W

question: Two capacitors 18.9 uF and 13.3 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 18.9, C2 = 13.3 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 18.9*13.3 / (18.9+13.3) | Answer: 7.807 uF

question: A resistor 13 kohm and capacitor 5.3 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 13, C = 5.3 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (13k)(5.3u) = 68.9 ms | Answer: 68.9 ms

question: An inductor 273.7 mH is in series with 10 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 273.7, R = 10 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (273.7e-3) / 10 | Answer: 27.37 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 144.2 mH inductor at 920 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 144.2, f = 920 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (920)(144.2e-3) | Answer: 833.6 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 31.8 uF capacitor at 320 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 31.8, f = 320 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (320)(31.8e-6)) | Answer: 15.64 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 11 ohm, XL = 132 ohm and XC = 40 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 11, XL = 132, XC = 40 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(11^2 + (132 - 40)^2) | Answer: 92.66 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 79.6 mH and C = 2.6 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 79.6, C = 2.6 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(79.6e-3 * 2.6e-6)) | Answer: 349.8 Hz

question: A capacitor of 33.1 uF is charged to 40 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 33.1, V = 40 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*33.1e-6*(40)^2 | Answer: 26.48 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 250 V with 530 primary turns and 300 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 250, N1 = 530, N2 = 300 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 250 * 300/530 | Answer: 141.5 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 120 V and draws an armature current of 9 A. If the armature resistance is 1.31 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 120, Ia = 9, Ra = 1.31 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 120 - 9*1.31 | Answer: 108.2 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 165 A at 415 V (line) with a power factor of 0.77. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 165, VL = 415, pf = 0.77 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*415*165*0.77 / 1000 | Answer: 91.32 kW

question: A load has real power 10 kW and apparent power 160 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 10, S = 160 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 10 / 160 | Answer: 0.0625

question: A machine delivers 130 kW output while drawing 217 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 130, Pi = 217 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 130/217 * 100 | Answer: 59.91 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 11 V across R1 = 21 ohm and R2 = 12 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 11, R1 = 21, R2 = 12 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 11*12 / (21+12) | Answer: 4 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 20 kohm and Rin = 19 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 20, Rin = 19 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 20 / 19 | Answer: 1.053

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 90 kohm and Rg = 8 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 90, Rg = 8 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 90/8 | Answer: 12.25

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 1363. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 1363 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(1363) | Answer: 31.34 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 7.8 m carries a central point load of 100 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7.8, W = 100 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 100*7.8 / 4 | Answer: 195 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 5.1 m carries a UDL of 45 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.1, w = 45 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 45*(5.1)^2 / 8 | Answer: 146.3 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 2.4 m carries a point load 40 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 2.4, W = 40 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 40*2.4 | Answer: 96 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 5.2 m carries a UDL of 16 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.2, w = 16 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 16*(5.2)^2 / 2 | Answer: 216.3 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 8.3 m carries a point load 65 kN at distance 3.8 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 8.3, a = 3.8, W = 65 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 65*(8.3 - 3.8) / 8.3 | Answer: 35.24 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 6.5 m) carries a central point load 20 kN. With E = 25 GPa and I = 560e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=20000 N, L=6500.0 mm, E=25000 MPa, I=560e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 8.173 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 4.5 m carries a UDL of 15 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.5, w = 15 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 15*(4.5)^2 / 12 | Answer: 25.31 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 660 mm, clear cover 40 mm and main bars of diameter 25 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 660, c = 40, dia = 25 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 660 - 40 - 25/2 | Answer: 607.5 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 18.1 m^2 carrying a factored load of 12.8 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 18.1, w = 12.8 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 12.8 * 18.1 | Answer: 231.7 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 3 m, unit weight 16 kN/m^3, phi = 33 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 4.6e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.6, area = 7e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 4.6, i = 0.6, A = 7 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (4.6e-4)*0.6*(7e-3) | Answer: 1932 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 2.4 m, bed slope 0.009 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.028. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 1.2 m under a head of 0.6 m. Taking Cd = 0.6 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 3.1 m wide carries a discharge of 3.6 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A tank of volume 130 m^3 treats a flow of 100 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 130, Q = 100 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 130 / 100 | Answer: 1.3 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 150 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.23 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 3 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 150, k = 0.23, t = 3 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 150*(1 - e^(-0.23*3)) | Answer: 74.76 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.76, rainfall intensity 40 mm/h over a catchment of 29.8 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.76, i = 40, A = 29.8 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.76*40*29.8 / 360 | Answer: 2.516 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.07 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 480 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.07, M = 480 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 480*(30+0.07)/30 | Answer: 481.1 m

question: Convert the decimal number 2475 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 2475 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 9AB (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 11101110 and 00110100.
solution: XOR: 11011010 | Count of 1s = 5 | Answer: 5
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 600 megabits is sent over a link of 10 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 600, B = 10 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 600 / 10 | Answer: 60 s

question: A link has bandwidth 1 Mbps and round-trip time 150 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 1, R = 150 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 1e6 * 150e-3 bits = 150 kb | Answer: 150 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.95, cache access time 5 ns and main-memory access time 160 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.95, tc = 5, tm = 160 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.95*5 + (1 - 0.95)*160 | Answer: 12.75 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 774303 elements?
solution: Given: n = 774303 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(774303)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.012, memory access time 80 ns and page-fault service time 4 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 4 ms = 4000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.012)*80 + 0.012*4000000.0 ns | Answer: 48.08 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 1 m^3 at 100 kPa and 360 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 1, P = 100, Tk = 360 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (100e3)*1 / (8.314*360) | Answer: 33.41 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.31 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 17 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.31, t = 17 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.31*17) | Answer: 0.9949

question: For a reaction with A = 5e10 /s and activation energy 55 kJ/mol at 350 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 5, Ea = 55, Tk = 350 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 5e10 * exp(-55e3 / (8.314*350)) | Answer: 309.3 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.98 and bottoms xW = 0.07, with relative volatility alpha = 2.9. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.98, xw = 0.07, al = 2.9 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.98/0.02)(0.93/0.07)] / ln(2.9) | Answer: 6.085 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.78 and x = 0.42. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.78, x = 0.42 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.78/0.22) / (0.42/0.58) | Answer: 4.896

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.67 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 70 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.67, Psat = 70 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.67 * 70 | Answer: 46.9 kPa

question: A stream of 7.3 kg/s with specific heat 3.2 kJ/kg-K is heated through 40 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 7.3, cp = 3.2, dT = 40 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 7.3*3.2*40 | Answer: 934.4 kW

question: A reactor of volume 5.6 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 2.6 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 5.6, Q = 2.6 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 5.6 / 2.6 | Answer: 2.154 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 3.4e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 4 mm with a concentration difference of 50 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 3.4, L = 4, dC = 50 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (3.4e-9)*50 / (4e-3) | Answer: 42.5 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 6.6 min and steady-state gain 1. For a step input of magnitude 3, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 6.6, K = 1, M = 3 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 1 * 3 | Answer: 3 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 100 m^2 flies at 200 m/s (air density 1.225 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 1.3. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 100, V = 200, rho = 1.225, CL = 1.3 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1.225*(200)^2*100*1.3 / 1000 | Answer: 3185 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 15 m^2 flies at 220 m/s (density 0.4 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.07. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 15, V = 220, rho = 0.4, CD = 0.07 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.4*(220)^2*15*0.07 / 1000 | Answer: 10.16 kN

question: A specimen under stress 360 MPa shows an elastic strain of 2.8e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 360, eps = 2.8 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 360 / (2.8e-3) MPa = 128.6 GPa | Answer: 128.6 GPa

question: A block of mass 25 kg has a volume of 1.4e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 25, V = 1.4 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 25 / (1.4e-3) | Answer: 17857 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 2800 mm is heated through 65 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 11e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 2800, dT = 65, al = 11 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 2800*11e-6*65 | Answer: 2.002 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 100 ohm, R2 = 110 ohm and R3 = 440 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 100, R2 = 110, R3 = 440 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 110*440 / 100 | Answer: 484 ohm

question: A measurement reads 9.64 when the true value is 10. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.64, true = 10 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.64 - 10| / 10 * 100 | Answer: 3.6 %

question: Annual demand is 13500 units, ordering cost 290 per order and holding cost 29 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 13500, S = 290, H = 29 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*13500*290 / 29) | Answer: 519.6 units

question: An asset costs 60000 with salvage value 22000 after 6 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 60000, Sv = 22000, n = 6 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (60000 - 22000) / 6 | Answer: 6333 per year

question: A product sells for 460 per unit with variable cost 110 per unit and fixed costs 35000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 460, V = 110, F = 35000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 35000 / (460 - 110) | Answer: 100 units

question: Find the present worth of 60000 received 6 years from now at an interest rate of 11% per year.
solution: Given: F = 60000, n = 6, i = 11 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 60000 / (1 + 0.11)^6 | Answer: 32078 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.93, 0.95 and 0.96 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.93, r2 = 0.95, r3 = 0.96 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.93*0.95*0.96 | Answer: 0.8482

question: A process produces 42 defective items in a batch of 19000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 42, N = 19000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 42/19000 * 1e6 | Answer: 2211 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = x^3 + 7x^2 + 7x - 1 evaluated at x = 0.
For f(x) = -5x^3 + 2x^2 - x - 2, find f''(x) at x = -4.
Evaluate the definite integral of (-x^2 - 5x - 1) dx from x = 2 to x = 4.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = -1x^3/3 + -5x^2/2 + -1x | Evaluate F(4) - F(2) | Answer: -50.67
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 5x^2 + x - 3 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[-4, -8], [-3, -1]].
solution: Given: a = -4, b = -8, c = -3, d = -1 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (-4)(-1) - (-8)(-3) | Answer: -20

question: Find the determinant of [[-2, 2, 0], [-1, 4, 0], [-5, 4, 5]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: -30

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[-4, 5], [3, -2]].
solution: Trace tr = -6, Determinant = -7 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 1

question: Solve for x: 2x + -5y = 6 and -5x + -6y = -1.
solution: Determinant = 2*-6 - -5*-5 = -37 | x = (e d - b f) / det = 1.108 | Answer: x = 1.108
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 45, 91, 66, 89, 44.
solution: Sum = 335 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 67 | Answer: 67

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 25, 30, 11, 29, 17.
solution: Mean = 22.4 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 8.173

question: Find the slope of the line through (7, 3) and (-8, 9).
solution: Given: x1 = 7, y1 = 3, x2 = -8, y2 = 9 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (9 - 3) / (-8 - 7) | Answer: -0.4

question: Find the distance between the points (-8, 2) and (-3, 3).
solution: Given: x1 = -8, y1 = 2, x2 = -3, y2 = 3 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((5)^2 + (1)^2) | Answer: 5.099 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (0,1), (4,1), (2,6).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 10 sq units

question: Find the 8th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 20 and common difference 6.
solution: Given: a = 20, d = 6, n = 8 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = 20 + (8 - 1)*6 | Answer: 62

question: Find the sum of the first 15 terms of an AP with first term 5 and common difference 1.
solution: Given: a = 5, d = 1, n = 15 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 15/2 [2*5 + (15-1)*1] | Answer: 180

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 34000 at 14% per annum for 4 years.
solution: Given: P = 34000, R = 14, Tt = 4 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 34000 * 14 * 4 / 100 | Answer: 19040 currency units

question: Find the amount when 8500 is invested at 12% per annum compounded annually for 4 years.
solution: Given: P = 8500, R = 12, Tt = 4 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 8500 * (1 + 12/100)^4 | Answer: 13375 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (3, -4, 4) and (-1, -8, 6).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (-6, 1, 6) and (-3, -5, -1).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 50.06

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (-2, 2, 4) and (6, 0, -3).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 136.9 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number 6 + 8i.
solution: Given: a = 6, b = 8 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((6)^2 + (8)^2) | Answer: 10

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number -4 + 1i.
solution: Given: a = -4, b = 1 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(1, -4) | Answer: 166 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -4x^3 - 5x^2 - 2x - 2 at x = 0.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-30 with initial guess x0=2, find x1 (one iteration).
solution: Given: N = 30, x0 = 2 | Formula: x1 = x0 - (x0^2 - N)/(2 x0) | Substitute: x1 = 2 - ((2)^2 - 30)/(2*2) | Answer: 8.5

question: Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=0.6 and ordinates 2, 17, 19, 11, 10, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 244 and 428.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 244 and 428 | Answer: GCD = 4

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 65 and 34.
solution: Given: a = 65, b = 34 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 65*34 / 1 | Answer: 2210
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 32 mm carries an axial tensile load of 114 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 24 mm and length 2900 mm carries an axial load of 38 kN. Take E = 70 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 59 mm transmits a torque of 100 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 59, Tt = 100 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(100*1000) / (pi*(59)^3) | Answer: 2.48 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 41 mm and length 1500 mm carries a torque of 1900 N-m. With G = 80 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (41)^4 / 32 = 277418 mm^4 | theta = (1900*1000)(1500) / (80000 * 277418) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 7.358 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 139 mm wide and 220 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 139, h = 220 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 139*(220)^2 / 6 | Answer: 1121267 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (77 mm x 190 mm) carries a bending moment of 17 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (76 mm x 140 mm) has effective length 3400 mm and E = 200 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 670 MPa is designed for a working stress of 210 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 670, sw = 210 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 670 / 210 | Answer: 3.19

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1300 mm and wall thickness 6 mm carries an internal pressure of 1 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1300, t = 6, P = 1 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 1*1300 / (2*6) | Answer: 108.3 MPa

question: 1 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 25 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1, dT = 25 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 1 * 0.718 * 25 | Answer: 17.95 kJ

question: 3.2 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 195 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.2, dT = 195 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 3.2 * 1.005 * 195 | Answer: 627.1 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 2.7 m^3 at 470 K with mass 3.8 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 2.7, Tk = 470, m = 3.8 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 3.8*0.287*470 / 2.7 | Answer: 189.8 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 3.1 kg of air expands isothermally at 300 K from volume V1 to 4*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.1, Tk = 300, ratio = 4 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 3.1*0.287*300*ln(4) | Answer: 370 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 3.6 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.2 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 3.6, D = 0.2 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*3.6*0.2 / 0.001 | Answer: 720000

question: Water flows at 3.7 m/s through a pipe of diameter 290 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 15.9 m. Taking Cv = 0.98, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 15.9, cv = 0.98 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.98*sqrt(2*9.81*15.9) | Answer: 17.31 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 340 mm) water flows at 1 m/s. It contracts to diameter 140 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 340, d2 = 140, V1 = 1 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 1*(340/140)^2 | Answer: 5.898 m/s

question: Water flows at 2.8 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.49 m and length 290 m. With friction factor f = 0.02, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 36 teeth drives a gear of 61 teeth. If the pinion runs at 300 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 36, z2 = 61, N1 = 300 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 300*36 / 61 | Answer: 177 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 120 mm rotates at 400 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 120, N = 400 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.12)*400 / 60 | Answer: 2.513 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 3.3 kW at 200 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 3.3, N = 200 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(3.3*1000) / (2*pi*200) | Answer: 157.6 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 9.2 kg rotates at radius 0.22 m at 950 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 1900 N/m and mass 14.3 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 1900, m = 14.3 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(1900/14.3) | Answer: 1.835 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 9.2 m^2 and thickness 0.39 m has conductivity k = 16.2 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 45 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 9.2, L = 0.39, k = 16.2, dT = 45 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 16.2*9.2*45 / 0.39 | Answer: 17197 W

question: A surface of area 5.7 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 60 W/m^2-K to surroundings 120 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 5.7, h = 60, dT = 120 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 60*5.7*120 | Answer: 41040 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 70 m/min, feed = 0.44 mm/rev, depth of cut = 0.5 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 70, f = 0.44, d = 0.5 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*70*0.44*0.5 | Answer: 15400 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 500 mm is turned at 300 rpm with a feed of 0.13 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 500, N = 300, f = 0.13 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 500 / (0.13*300) | Answer: 12.82 min

question: A resistor of 192 ohm carries a current of 9 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 192, I = 9 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 9 * 192 | Answer: 1728 V

question: Three resistors 26 ohm, 57 ohm and 45 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 26, R2 = 57, R3 = 45 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 26 + 57 + 45 | Answer: 128 ohm

question: Two resistors 33 ohm and 5 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 33, R2 = 5 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 33*5 / (33+5) | Answer: 4.342 ohm

question: A device draws 11 A at 70 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 70, I = 11 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 70 * 11 | Answer: 770 W

question: A current of 1.6 A flows through a 58 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 1.6, R = 58 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (1.6)^2 * 58 | Answer: 148.5 W

question: Two capacitors 33.3 uF and 31.3 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 33.3, C2 = 31.3 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 33.3*31.3 / (33.3+31.3) | Answer: 16.13 uF

question: A resistor 31 kohm and capacitor 16.3 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 31, C = 16.3 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (31k)(16.3u) = 505.3 ms | Answer: 505.3 ms

question: An inductor 86.6 mH is in series with 181 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 86.6, R = 181 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (86.6e-3) / 181 | Answer: 0.4785 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 167 mH inductor at 100 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 167, f = 100 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (100)(167e-3) | Answer: 104.9 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 41.1 uF capacitor at 180 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 41.1, f = 180 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (180)(41.1e-6)) | Answer: 21.51 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 96 ohm, XL = 68 ohm and XC = 85 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 96, XL = 68, XC = 85 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(96^2 + (68 - 85)^2) | Answer: 97.49 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 61 mH and C = 1 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 61, C = 1 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(61e-3 * 1e-6)) | Answer: 644.4 Hz

question: A capacitor of 61.6 uF is charged to 380 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 61.6, V = 380 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*61.6e-6*(380)^2 | Answer: 4448 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 340 V with 240 primary turns and 100 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 340, N1 = 240, N2 = 100 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 340 * 100/240 | Answer: 141.7 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 370 V and draws an armature current of 43 A. If the armature resistance is 1.18 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 370, Ia = 43, Ra = 1.18 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 370 - 43*1.18 | Answer: 319.3 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 65 A at 433 V (line) with a power factor of 0.73. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 65, VL = 433, pf = 0.73 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*433*65*0.73 / 1000 | Answer: 35.59 kW

question: A load has real power 25 kW and apparent power 155 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 25, S = 155 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 25 / 155 | Answer: 0.1613

question: A machine delivers 20 kW output while drawing 142 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 20, Pi = 142 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 20/142 * 100 | Answer: 14.08 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 7 V across R1 = 10 ohm and R2 = 50 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 7, R1 = 10, R2 = 50 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 7*50 / (10+50) | Answer: 5.833 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 10 kohm and Rin = 35 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 10, Rin = 35 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 10 / 35 | Answer: 0.2857

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 60 kohm and Rg = 4 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 60, Rg = 4 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 60/4 | Answer: 16

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 817. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 817 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(817) | Answer: 29.12 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 8.8 m carries a central point load of 95 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 8.8, W = 95 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 95*8.8 / 4 | Answer: 209 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 3.5 m carries a UDL of 15 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.5, w = 15 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 15*(3.5)^2 / 8 | Answer: 22.97 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 1.8 m carries a point load 25 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 1.8, W = 25 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 25*1.8 | Answer: 45 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 2.9 m carries a UDL of 20 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 2.9, w = 20 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 20*(2.9)^2 / 2 | Answer: 84.1 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 8.2 m carries a point load 55 kN at distance 4 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 8.2, a = 4, W = 55 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 55*(8.2 - 4) / 8.2 | Answer: 28.17 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 4.1 m) carries a central point load 70 kN. With E = 30 GPa and I = 390e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=70000 N, L=4100.0 mm, E=30000 MPa, I=390e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 8.591 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 7.1 m carries a UDL of 33 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7.1, w = 33 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 33*(7.1)^2 / 12 | Answer: 138.6 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 330 mm, clear cover 25 mm and main bars of diameter 25 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 330, c = 25, dia = 25 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 330 - 25 - 25/2 | Answer: 292.5 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 21.2 m^2 carrying a factored load of 16.7 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 21.2, w = 16.7 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 16.7 * 21.2 | Answer: 354 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 5.8 m, unit weight 17 kN/m^3, phi = 30 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 6.6e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.9, area = 3.3e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 6.6, i = 0.9, A = 3.3 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (6.6e-4)*0.9*(3.3e-3) | Answer: 196 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 0.6 m, bed slope 0.006 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.016. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 3.9 m under a head of 0.4 m. Taking Cd = 0.62 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 5.8 m wide carries a discharge of 23.1 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 290 m and design speed 70 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 290, V = 70 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (70)^2 / (127*290) | Answer: 0.133
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: A tank of volume 940 m^3 treats a flow of 195 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 940, Q = 195 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 940 / 195 | Answer: 4.821 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 150 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.17 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 6 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 150, k = 0.17, t = 6 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 150*(1 - e^(-0.17*6)) | Answer: 95.91 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.67, rainfall intensity 50 mm/h over a catchment of 43.3 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.67, i = 50, A = 43.3 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.67*50*43.3 / 360 | Answer: 4.029 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.02 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 570 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.02, M = 570 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 570*(20+0.02)/20 | Answer: 570.6 m

question: Convert the decimal number 2376 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 2376 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 948 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 01010010 and 10100000.
solution: XOR: 11110010 | Count of 1s = 5 | Answer: 5
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 470 megabits is sent over a link of 76 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 470, B = 76 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 470 / 76 | Answer: 6.184 s

question: A link has bandwidth 1 Mbps and round-trip time 100 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 1, R = 100 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 1e6 * 100e-3 bits = 100 kb | Answer: 100 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.87, cache access time 4 ns and main-memory access time 140 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.87, tc = 4, tm = 140 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.87*4 + (1 - 0.87)*140 | Answer: 21.68 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 711645 elements?
solution: Given: n = 711645 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(711645)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.018, memory access time 100 ns and page-fault service time 10 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 10 ms = 10000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.018)*100 + 0.018*10000000.0 ns | Answer: 180.1 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 2.4 m^3 at 260 kPa and 580 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 2.4, P = 260, Tk = 580 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (260e3)*2.4 / (8.314*580) | Answer: 129.4 mol

question: For a reaction with A = 4e10 /s and activation energy 90 kJ/mol at 370 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 4, Ea = 90, Tk = 370 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 4e10 * exp(-90e3 / (8.314*370)) | Answer: 0.007868 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.92 and bottoms xW = 0.09, with relative volatility alpha = 3.2. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.92, xw = 0.09, al = 3.2 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.92/0.08)(0.91/0.09)] / ln(3.2) | Answer: 4.089 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.71 and x = 0.22. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.71, x = 0.22 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.71/0.29) / (0.22/0.78) | Answer: 8.68

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.76 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 50 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.76, Psat = 50 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.76 * 50 | Answer: 38 kPa

question: A stream of 5.4 kg/s with specific heat 1.1 kJ/kg-K is heated through 100 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 5.4, cp = 1.1, dT = 100 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 5.4*1.1*100 | Answer: 594 kW

question: A reactor of volume 2.4 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 0.2 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 2.4, Q = 0.2 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 2.4 / 0.2 | Answer: 12 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 7.2e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 2 mm with a concentration difference of 180 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 7.2, L = 2, dC = 180 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (7.2e-9)*180 / (2e-3) | Answer: 648 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 9.8 min and steady-state gain 2.9. For a step input of magnitude 18, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 9.8, K = 2.9, M = 18 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 2.9 * 18 | Answer: 52.2 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 20 m^2 flies at 190 m/s (air density 0.7 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 1.1. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 20, V = 190, rho = 0.7, CL = 1.1 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.7*(190)^2*20*1.1 / 1000 | Answer: 278 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 55 m^2 flies at 170 m/s (density 0.7 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.1. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 55, V = 170, rho = 0.7, CD = 0.1 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.7*(170)^2*55*0.1 / 1000 | Answer: 55.63 kN

question: A specimen under stress 370 MPa shows an elastic strain of 0.7e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 370, eps = 0.7 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 370 / (0.7e-3) MPa = 528.6 GPa | Answer: 528.6 GPa

question: A block of mass 50 kg has a volume of 2.2e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 50, V = 2.2 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 50 / (2.2e-3) | Answer: 22727 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 800 mm is heated through 90 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 12e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 800, dT = 90, al = 12 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 800*12e-6*90 | Answer: 0.864 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 40 ohm, R2 = 170 ohm and R3 = 175 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 40, R2 = 170, R3 = 175 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 170*175 / 40 | Answer: 743.8 ohm

question: A measurement reads 10.8 when the true value is 50. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10.8, true = 50 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10.8 - 50| / 50 * 100 | Answer: 78.4 %

question: Annual demand is 22500 units, ordering cost 90 per order and holding cost 33 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 22500, S = 90, H = 33 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*22500*90 / 33) | Answer: 350.3 units

question: An asset costs 190000 with salvage value 22000 after 10 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 190000, Sv = 22000, n = 10 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (190000 - 22000) / 10 | Answer: 16800 per year

question: A product sells for 370 per unit with variable cost 160 per unit and fixed costs 125000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 370, V = 160, F = 125000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 125000 / (370 - 160) | Answer: 595.2 units

question: Find the present worth of 185000 received 4 years from now at an interest rate of 8% per year.
solution: Given: F = 185000, n = 4, i = 8 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 185000 / (1 + 0.08)^4 | Answer: 135981 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.96, 0.9 and 0.99 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.96, r2 = 0.9, r3 = 0.99 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.96*0.9*0.99 | Answer: 0.8554

question: A process produces 34 defective items in a batch of 10000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 34, N = 10000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 34/10000 * 1e6 | Answer: 3400 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -2x^3 + 4x^2 - 7x + 3 evaluated at x = 2.
For f(x) = 3x^3 - 4x^2 - 3x - 3, find f''(x) at x = 1.
Evaluate the definite integral of (2x^2 + x - 6) dx from x = 2 to x = 6.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = 2x^3/3 + 1x^2/2 + -6x | Evaluate F(6) - F(2) | Answer: 130.7
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 6x^2 + 4x - 7 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[0, -8], [-4, 1]].
solution: Given: a = 0, b = -8, c = -4, d = 1 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (0)(1) - (-8)(-4) | Answer: -32

question: Find the determinant of [[5, -4, 1], [-4, 1, -2], [6, -3, -1]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: 35

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[7, -5], [-7, -3]].

question: Find the amount when 13500 is invested at 5% per annum compounded annually for 5 years.

question: A circular rod of diameter 12 mm carries an axial tensile load of 69 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 32 mm and length 700 mm carries an axial load of 83 kN. Take E = 110 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.

question: A rectangular beam section is 45 mm wide and 130 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 45, h = 130 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 45*(130)^2 / 6 | Answer: 126750 mm^3
