question: A component of ultimate strength 900 MPa is designed for a working stress of 190 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 900, sw = 190 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 900 / 190 | Answer: 4.737

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 300 mm and wall thickness 6 mm carries an internal pressure of 1.3 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 300, t = 6, P = 1.3 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 1.3*300 / (2*6) | Answer: 32.5 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 1140 K and 280 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 1140, Tc = 280 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 280/1140) * 100 | Answer: 75.44 %

question: A heat pump operates between 271 K and 312 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 271, Th = 312 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 312 / (312 - 271) | Answer: 7.61

question: 4.1 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 100 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.1, dT = 100 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 4.1 * 0.718 * 100 | Answer: 294.4 kJ

question: 4.6 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 190 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.6, dT = 190 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 4.6 * 1.005 * 190 | Answer: 878.4 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 2 m^3 at 340 K with mass 4.6 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 2, Tk = 340, m = 4.6 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 4.6*0.287*340 / 2 | Answer: 224.4 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 3.9 kg of air expands isothermally at 300 K from volume V1 to 5*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.9, Tk = 300, ratio = 5 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 3.9*0.287*300*ln(5) | Answer: 540.4 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 2.7 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.28 m. Find the Reynolds number.

question: Water flows at 3.2 m/s through a pipe of diameter 230 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 16.3 m. Taking Cv = 0.99, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).

formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 31 teeth drives a gear of 64 teeth. If the pinion runs at 650 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 31, z2 = 64, N1 = 650 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 650*31 / 64 | Answer: 314.8 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 600 mm rotates at 950 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.

question: A shaft transmits 44.3 kW at 350 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 44.3, N = 350 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(44.3*1000) / (2*pi*350) | Answer: 1209 N-m

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 15000 N/m and mass 8 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.

question: A plane wall of area 3.4 m^2 and thickness 0.31 m has conductivity k = 2 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 155 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.

question: A surface of area 4.8 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 75 W/m^2-K to surroundings 125 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 4.8, h = 75, dT = 125 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 75*4.8*125 | Answer: 45000 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 240 m/min, feed = 0.18 mm/rev, depth of cut = 1.9 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 240, f = 0.18, d = 1.9 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*240*0.18*1.9 | Answer: 82080 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 370 mm is turned at 650 rpm with a feed of 0.17 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.

question: A resistor of 193 ohm carries a current of 5 A. Find the voltage across it.

question: Three resistors 77 ohm, 52 ohm and 90 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.

question: Two resistors 110 ohm and 77 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 110, R2 = 77 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 110*77 / (110+77) | Answer: 45.29 ohm

question: A device draws 7.8 A at 145 V. Find the power consumed.

question: A current of 5.8 A flows through a 31 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.

question: Two capacitors 38.6 uF and 41.9 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 38.6, C2 = 41.9 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 38.6*41.9 / (38.6+41.9) | Answer: 20.09 uF

question: A resistor 89 kohm and capacitor 15.8 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.

question: An inductor 362.7 mH is in series with 116 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 106.5 mH inductor at 970 Hz.

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 10 ohm, XL = 59 ohm and XC = 134 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.

question: A capacitor of 57.3 uF is charged to 355 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.

question: A transformer has primary voltage 160 V with 800 primary turns and 390 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.

question: A DC motor is supplied at 230 V and draws an armature current of 14 A. If the armature resistance is 0.82 ohm, find the back EMF.

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 15 A at 415 V (line) with a power factor of 0.88. Find the total real power in kW.

question: A machine delivers 30 kW output while drawing 127 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 20 V across R1 = 10 ohm and R2 = 36 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 50 kohm and Rin = 39 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).

question: A simply supported beam of span 3.5 m carries a central point load of 10 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.

solution: Given: L = 3.1, w = 40 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 40*(3.1)^2 / 2 | Answer: 192.2 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.6 m carries a point load 100 kN at distance 2.6 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.

question: An RC beam has overall depth 580 mm, clear cover 40 mm and main bars of diameter 25 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 580, c = 40, dia = 25 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 580 - 40 - 25/2 | Answer: 527.5 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 29.8 m^2 carrying a factored load of 10 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 29.8, w = 10 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 10 * 29.8 | Answer: 298 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 6.6 m, unit weight 18 kN/m^3, phi = 37 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: A tank of volume 320 m^3 treats a flow of 200 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 320, Q = 200 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 320 / 200 | Answer: 1.6 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 360 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.26 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 6 days.

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.89, rainfall intensity 85 mm/h over a catchment of 24 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.05 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 780 m with this tape.

question: A file of 530 megabits is sent over a link of 55 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.

question: A link has bandwidth 14 Mbps and round-trip time 20 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.85, cache access time 2 ns and main-memory access time 160 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.85, tc = 2, tm = 160 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.85*2 + (1 - 0.85)*160 | Answer: 25.7 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 25702 elements?

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.007, memory access time 120 ns and page-fault service time 8 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 1.8 m^3 at 340 kPa and 520 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 1.8, P = 340, Tk = 520 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (340e3)*1.8 / (8.314*520) | Answer: 141.6 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.07 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 8 minutes.

question: For a reaction with A = 7e10 /s and activation energy 50 kJ/mol at 300 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 7, Ea = 50, Tk = 300 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 7e10 * exp(-50e3 / (8.314*300)) | Answer: 137.7 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.94 and bottoms xW = 0.03, with relative volatility alpha = 3.3. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.94, xw = 0.03, al = 3.3 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.94/0.06)(0.97/0.03)] / ln(3.3) | Answer: 5.216 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.8 and x = 0.23. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.8, x = 0.23 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.8/0.2) / (0.23/0.77) | Answer: 13.39

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.43 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 60 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.43, Psat = 60 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.43 * 60 | Answer: 25.8 kPa

question: A stream of 8.4 kg/s with specific heat 3.5 kJ/kg-K is heated through 60 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 8.4, cp = 3.5, dT = 60 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 8.4*3.5*60 | Answer: 1764 kW

question: A reactor of volume 16.7 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 4.1 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 16.7, Q = 4.1 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 16.7 / 4.1 | Answer: 4.073 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 8.2e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 1 mm with a concentration difference of 60 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 8.2, L = 1, dC = 60 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (8.2e-9)*60 / (1e-3) | Answer: 492 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 5.1 min and steady-state gain 3.5. For a step input of magnitude 3, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 5.1, K = 3.5, M = 3 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 3.5 * 3 | Answer: 10.5 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 55 m^2 flies at 190 m/s (air density 1 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 1.1. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 55, V = 190, rho = 1, CL = 1.1 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1*(190)^2*55*1.1 / 1000 | Answer: 1092 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 95 m^2 flies at 200 m/s (density 0.4 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.05. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 95, V = 200, rho = 0.4, CD = 0.05 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.4*(200)^2*95*0.05 / 1000 | Answer: 38 kN

question: A specimen under stress 230 MPa shows an elastic strain of 0.9e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 230, eps = 0.9 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 230 / (0.9e-3) MPa = 255.6 GPa | Answer: 255.6 GPa

question: A block of mass 10 kg has a volume of 1.6e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 10, V = 1.6 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 10 / (1.6e-3) | Answer: 6250 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 1700 mm is heated through 70 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 11e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 1700, dT = 70, al = 11 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 1700*11e-6*70 | Answer: 1.309 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 125 ohm, R2 = 90 ohm and R3 = 250 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 125, R2 = 90, R3 = 250 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 90*250 / 125 | Answer: 180 ohm

question: A measurement reads 9.18 when the true value is 50. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.18, true = 50 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.18 - 50| / 50 * 100 | Answer: 81.64 %

question: Annual demand is 7000 units, ordering cost 280 per order and holding cost 28 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 7000, S = 280, H = 28 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*7000*280 / 28) | Answer: 374.2 units

question: An asset costs 280000 with salvage value 12000 after 12 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 280000, Sv = 12000, n = 12 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (280000 - 12000) / 12 | Answer: 22333 per year

question: A product sells for 480 per unit with variable cost 140 per unit and fixed costs 200000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 480, V = 140, F = 200000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 200000 / (480 - 140) | Answer: 588.2 units

question: Find the present worth of 135000 received 10 years from now at an interest rate of 10% per year.
solution: Given: F = 135000, n = 10, i = 10 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 135000 / (1 + 0.1)^10 | Answer: 52048 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.95, 0.95 and 0.96 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.95, r2 = 0.95, r3 = 0.96 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.95*0.95*0.96 | Answer: 0.8664

question: A process produces 3 defective items in a batch of 18500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 3, N = 18500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 3/18500 * 1e6 | Answer: 162.2 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = x^3 - 5x^2 + x + 1 evaluated at x = -5.
For f(x) = -3x^3 - 3x^2 - 3x - 2, find f''(x) at x = -4.
Evaluate the definite integral of (4x^2 + 4x - 1) dx from x = -2 to x = 3.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = 4x^3/3 + 4x^2/2 + -1x | Evaluate F(3) - F(-2) | Answer: 51.67
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 3x^2 - 9x + 4 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[-8, 5], [-4, 2]].
solution: Given: a = -8, b = 5, c = -4, d = 2 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (-8)(2) - (5)(-4) | Answer: 4

question: Find the determinant of [[-6, 0, -2], [2, 1, -3], [1, -1, 5]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: -6

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[4, 2], [-8, -7]].
solution: Trace tr = -3, Determinant = -12 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 2.275

question: Solve for x: 2x + -4y = 3 and -4x + -2y = -10.
solution: Determinant = 2*-2 - -4*-4 = -20 | x = (e d - b f) / det = 2.3 | Answer: x = 2.3
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 24, 90, 77, 69, 65.
solution: Sum = 325 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 65 | Answer: 65

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 29, 42, 6, 27, 35.
solution: Mean = 27.8 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 13.52

question: Find the slope of the line through (-9, -4) and (-6, -7).
solution: Given: x1 = -9, y1 = -4, x2 = -6, y2 = -7 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (-7 - -4) / (-6 - -9) | Answer: -1

question: Find the distance between the points (-6, -7) and (-3, -2).
solution: Given: x1 = -6, y1 = -7, x2 = -3, y2 = -2 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((3)^2 + (5)^2) | Answer: 5.831 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (4,-5), (4,-6), (1,-4).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 1.5 sq units

question: Find the 24th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -1 and common difference -9.
solution: Given: a = -1, d = -9, n = 24 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -1 + (24 - 1)*-9 | Answer: -208

question: Find the sum of the first 11 terms of an AP with first term -15 and common difference 7.
solution: Given: a = -15, d = 7, n = 11 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 11/2 [2*-15 + (11-1)*7] | Answer: 220

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 1500 at 6.7% per annum for 7 years.
solution: Given: P = 1500, R = 6.7, Tt = 7 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 1500 * 6.7 * 7 / 100 | Answer: 703.5 currency units

question: Find the amount when 15500 is invested at 6.9% per annum compounded annually for 4 years.
solution: Given: P = 15500, R = 6.9, Tt = 4 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 15500 * (1 + 6.9/100)^4 | Answer: 20241 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (4, 5, -2) and (-3, 3, 8).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (3, 4, -1) and (-3, 1, -4).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 25.98

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (0, 1, -2) and (4, 3, -6).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 30.81 degrees

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number 2 + -9i.
solution: Given: a = 2, b = -9 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(-9, 2) | Answer: -77.47 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = 4x^3 + 5x^2 - 5x at x = -4.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-144 with initial guess x0=9, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.3 and ordinates 3, 20, 1, 15, 9, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 435 and 585.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 435 and 585 | Answer: GCD = 15

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 10 and 56.
solution: Given: a = 10, b = 56 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 10*56 / 2 | Answer: 280
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 44 mm carries an axial tensile load of 71 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 40 mm and length 1300 mm carries an axial load of 35 kN. Take E = 200 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 45 mm transmits a torque of 550 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 45, Tt = 550 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(550*1000) / (pi*(45)^3) | Answer: 30.74 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 26 mm and length 2000 mm carries a torque of 950 N-m. With G = 80 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (26)^4 / 32 = 44864 mm^4 | theta = (950*1000)(2000) / (80000 * 44864) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 30.33 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 36 mm wide and 200 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 36, h = 200 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 36*(200)^2 / 6 | Answer: 240000 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (62 mm x 120 mm) carries a bending moment of 15 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (48 mm x 120 mm) has effective length 3100 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 440 MPa is designed for a working stress of 90 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 440, sw = 90 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 440 / 90 | Answer: 4.889

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1150 mm and wall thickness 16 mm carries an internal pressure of 1.8 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1150, t = 16, P = 1.8 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 1.8*1150 / (2*16) | Answer: 64.69 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 1100 K and 380 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 1100, Tc = 380 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 380/1100) * 100 | Answer: 65.45 %

question: 2.5 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 65 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.5, dT = 65 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 2.5 * 0.718 * 65 | Answer: 116.7 kJ

question: 4 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 75 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4, dT = 75 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 4 * 1.005 * 75 | Answer: 301.5 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 1.8 m^3 at 400 K with mass 4 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 1.8, Tk = 400, m = 4 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 4*0.287*400 / 1.8 | Answer: 255.1 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 1.8 kg of air expands isothermally at 490 K from volume V1 to 2*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1.8, Tk = 490, ratio = 2 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 1.8*0.287*490*ln(2) | Answer: 175.5 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 4.2 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.05 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 4.2, D = 0.05 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*4.2*0.05 / 0.001 | Answer: 210000

question: Water flows at 3.9 m/s through a pipe of diameter 190 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 18.6 m. Taking Cv = 0.95, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 18.6, cv = 0.95 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.95*sqrt(2*9.81*18.6) | Answer: 18.15 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 270 mm) water flows at 2 m/s. It contracts to diameter 80 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 270, d2 = 80, V1 = 2 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 2*(270/80)^2 | Answer: 22.78 m/s

question: Water flows at 3.7 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.18 m and length 90 m. With friction factor f = 0.029, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 25 teeth drives a gear of 95 teeth. If the pinion runs at 450 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 25, z2 = 95, N1 = 450 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 450*25 / 95 | Answer: 118.4 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 230 mm rotates at 1300 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 230, N = 1300 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.23)*1300 / 60 | Answer: 15.66 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 2.5 kW at 500 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 2.5, N = 500 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(2.5*1000) / (2*pi*500) | Answer: 47.75 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 6.1 kg rotates at radius 0.52 m at 1100 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 9000 N/m and mass 11 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 9000, m = 11 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(9000/11) | Answer: 4.552 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 5.3 m^2 and thickness 0.27 m has conductivity k = 12.7 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 55 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 5.3, L = 0.27, k = 12.7, dT = 55 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 12.7*5.3*55 / 0.27 | Answer: 13711 W

question: A surface of area 0.7 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 15 W/m^2-K to surroundings 30 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 0.7, h = 15, dT = 30 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 15*0.7*30 | Answer: 315 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 70 m/min, feed = 0.24 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2.3 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 70, f = 0.24, d = 2.3 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*70*0.24*2.3 | Answer: 38640 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 500 mm is turned at 1200 rpm with a feed of 0.22 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 500, N = 1200, f = 0.22 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 500 / (0.22*1200) | Answer: 1.894 min

question: A resistor of 199 ohm carries a current of 9 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 199, I = 9 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 9 * 199 | Answer: 1791 V

question: Three resistors 3 ohm, 82 ohm and 63 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 3, R2 = 82, R3 = 63 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 3 + 82 + 63 | Answer: 148 ohm

question: Two resistors 92 ohm and 91 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 92, R2 = 91 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 92*91 / (92+91) | Answer: 45.75 ohm

question: A device draws 1.3 A at 135 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 135, I = 1.3 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 135 * 1.3 | Answer: 175.5 W

question: A current of 4.2 A flows through a 48 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 4.2, R = 48 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (4.2)^2 * 48 | Answer: 846.7 W

question: Two capacitors 9.2 uF and 24.7 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 9.2, C2 = 24.7 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 9.2*24.7 / (9.2+24.7) | Answer: 6.703 uF

question: A resistor 46 kohm and capacitor 2.4 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 46, C = 2.4 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (46k)(2.4u) = 110.4 ms | Answer: 110.4 ms

question: An inductor 470.2 mH is in series with 24 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 470.2, R = 24 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (470.2e-3) / 24 | Answer: 19.59 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 36.8 mH inductor at 390 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 36.8, f = 390 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (390)(36.8e-3) | Answer: 90.18 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 36.4 uF capacitor at 150 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 36.4, f = 150 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (150)(36.4e-6)) | Answer: 29.15 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 96 ohm, XL = 101 ohm and XC = 61 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 96, XL = 101, XC = 61 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(96^2 + (101 - 61)^2) | Answer: 104 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 65.8 mH and C = 3.2 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 65.8, C = 3.2 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(65.8e-3 * 3.2e-6)) | Answer: 346.8 Hz

question: A capacitor of 76.4 uF is charged to 75 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 76.4, V = 75 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*76.4e-6*(75)^2 | Answer: 214.9 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 180 V with 240 primary turns and 330 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 180, N1 = 240, N2 = 330 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 180 * 330/240 | Answer: 247.5 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 160 V and draws an armature current of 8 A. If the armature resistance is 1.32 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 160, Ia = 8, Ra = 1.32 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 160 - 8*1.32 | Answer: 149.4 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 170 A at 433 V (line) with a power factor of 0.94. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 170, VL = 433, pf = 0.94 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*433*170*0.94 / 1000 | Answer: 119.8 kW

question: A load has real power 45 kW and apparent power 80 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 45, S = 80 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 45 / 80 | Answer: 0.5625

question: A machine delivers 15 kW output while drawing 22 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 15, Pi = 22 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 15/22 * 100 | Answer: 68.18 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 29 V across R1 = 22 ohm and R2 = 24 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 29, R1 = 22, R2 = 24 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 29*24 / (22+24) | Answer: 15.13 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 210 kohm and Rin = 38 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 210, Rin = 38 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 210 / 38 | Answer: 5.526

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 150 kohm and Rg = 23 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 150, Rg = 23 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 150/23 | Answer: 7.522

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 2152. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 2152 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(2152) | Answer: 33.33 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.9 m carries a central point load of 45 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6.9, W = 45 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 45*6.9 / 4 | Answer: 77.62 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 8.2 m carries a UDL of 55 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 8.2, w = 55 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 55*(8.2)^2 / 8 | Answer: 462.3 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 5.6 m carries a point load 50 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.6, W = 50 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 50*5.6 | Answer: 280 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 2.4 m carries a UDL of 22 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 2.4, w = 22 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 22*(2.4)^2 / 2 | Answer: 63.36 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.4 m carries a point load 60 kN at distance 1.6 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 6.4, a = 1.6, W = 60 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 60*(6.4 - 1.6) / 6.4 | Answer: 45 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 6.9 m) carries a central point load 60 kN. With E = 30 GPa and I = 230e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=60000 N, L=6900.0 mm, E=30000 MPa, I=230e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 59.51 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 4.3 m carries a UDL of 18 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.3, w = 18 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 18*(4.3)^2 / 12 | Answer: 27.73 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 480 mm, clear cover 40 mm and main bars of diameter 12 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 480, c = 40, dia = 12 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 480 - 40 - 12/2 | Answer: 434 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 27.5 m^2 carrying a factored load of 11.4 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 27.5, w = 11.4 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 11.4 * 27.5 | Answer: 313.5 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 5.7 m, unit weight 16 kN/m^3, phi = 37 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 4.6e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.8, area = 6.9e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 4.6, i = 0.8, A = 6.9 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (4.6e-4)*0.8*(6.9e-3) | Answer: 2539 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.6 m, bed slope 0.01 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.029. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 3.3 m under a head of 1 m. Taking Cd = 0.64 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 3 m wide carries a discharge of 13.7 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 490 m and design speed 45 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 490, V = 45 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (45)^2 / (127*490) | Answer: 0.03254
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: A tank of volume 610 m^3 treats a flow of 80 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 610, Q = 80 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 610 / 80 | Answer: 7.625 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 250 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.31 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 4 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 250, k = 0.31, t = 4 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 250*(1 - e^(-0.31*4)) | Answer: 177.7 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.43, rainfall intensity 35 mm/h over a catchment of 57.4 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.43, i = 35, A = 57.4 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.43*35*57.4 / 360 | Answer: 2.4 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.06 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 710 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.06, M = 710 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 710*(30+0.06)/30 | Answer: 711.4 m

question: Convert the decimal number 471 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 471 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 1D7 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 01110011 and 00000001.
solution: XOR: 01110010 | Count of 1s = 4 | Answer: 4
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 360 megabits is sent over a link of 55 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 360, B = 55 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 360 / 55 | Answer: 6.545 s

question: A link has bandwidth 84 Mbps and round-trip time 200 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 84, R = 200 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 84e6 * 200e-3 bits = 16800 kb | Answer: 16800 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.95, cache access time 8 ns and main-memory access time 180 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.95, tc = 8, tm = 180 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.95*8 + (1 - 0.95)*180 | Answer: 16.6 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 473780 elements?
solution: Given: n = 473780 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(473780)) + 1 | Answer: 19

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.018, memory access time 90 ns and page-fault service time 5 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 5 ms = 5000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.018)*90 + 0.018*5000000.0 ns | Answer: 90.09 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 2 m^3 at 480 kPa and 570 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 2, P = 480, Tk = 570 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (480e3)*2 / (8.314*570) | Answer: 202.6 mol

question: For a reaction with A = 1e10 /s and activation energy 75 kJ/mol at 340 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 1, Ea = 75, Tk = 340 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 1e10 * exp(-75e3 / (8.314*340)) | Answer: 0.03001 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.97 and bottoms xW = 0.03, with relative volatility alpha = 2.1. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.97, xw = 0.03, al = 2.1 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.97/0.03)(0.97/0.03)] / ln(2.1) | Answer: 9.37 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.59 and x = 0.27. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.59, x = 0.27 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.59/0.41) / (0.27/0.73) | Answer: 3.891

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.51 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 90 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.51, Psat = 90 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.51 * 90 | Answer: 45.9 kPa

question: A stream of 4.1 kg/s with specific heat 2.1 kJ/kg-K is heated through 55 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 4.1, cp = 2.1, dT = 55 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 4.1*2.1*55 | Answer: 473.5 kW

question: A reactor of volume 4.5 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 2.7 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 4.5, Q = 2.7 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 4.5 / 2.7 | Answer: 1.667 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 6.5e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 2 mm with a concentration difference of 180 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 6.5, L = 2, dC = 180 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (6.5e-9)*180 / (2e-3) | Answer: 585 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 3.2 min and steady-state gain 0.7. For a step input of magnitude 9, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 3.2, K = 0.7, M = 9 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 0.7 * 9 | Answer: 6.3 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 30 m^2 flies at 110 m/s (air density 1.225 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.8. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 30, V = 110, rho = 1.225, CL = 0.8 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1.225*(110)^2*30*0.8 / 1000 | Answer: 177.9 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 90 m^2 flies at 60 m/s (density 1 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.04. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 90, V = 60, rho = 1, CD = 0.04 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*1*(60)^2*90*0.04 / 1000 | Answer: 6.48 kN

question: A specimen under stress 100 MPa shows an elastic strain of 0.9e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 100, eps = 0.9 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 100 / (0.9e-3) MPa = 111.1 GPa | Answer: 111.1 GPa

question: A block of mass 40 kg has a volume of 5e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 40, V = 5 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 40 / (5e-3) | Answer: 8000 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 2300 mm is heated through 115 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 17e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 2300, dT = 115, al = 17 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 2300*17e-6*115 | Answer: 4.497 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 170 ohm, R2 = 100 ohm and R3 = 175 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 170, R2 = 100, R3 = 175 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 100*175 / 170 | Answer: 102.9 ohm

question: A measurement reads 10.86 when the true value is 20. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10.86, true = 20 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10.86 - 20| / 20 * 100 | Answer: 45.7 %

question: Annual demand is 28500 units, ordering cost 40 per order and holding cost 12 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 28500, S = 40, H = 12 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*28500*40 / 12) | Answer: 435.9 units

question: An asset costs 360000 with salvage value 40000 after 12 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 360000, Sv = 40000, n = 12 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (360000 - 40000) / 12 | Answer: 26667 per year

question: A product sells for 420 per unit with variable cost 80 per unit and fixed costs 150000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 420, V = 80, F = 150000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 150000 / (420 - 80) | Answer: 441.2 units

question: Find the present worth of 40000 received 8 years from now at an interest rate of 5% per year.
solution: Given: F = 40000, n = 8, i = 5 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 40000 / (1 + 0.05)^8 | Answer: 27074 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.96, 0.92 and 0.9 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.96, r2 = 0.92, r3 = 0.9 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.96*0.92*0.9 | Answer: 0.7949

question: A process produces 39 defective items in a batch of 15500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 39, N = 15500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 39/15500 * 1e6 | Answer: 2516 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -5x^3 + 7x^2 - 5x - 1 evaluated at x = 5.
For f(x) = -x^3 - 3x^2 - 4x + 3, find f''(x) at x = 2.
Evaluate the definite integral of (-2x^2 + 2x + 7) dx from x = 0 to x = 7.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = -2x^3/3 + 2x^2/2 + 7x | Evaluate F(7) - F(0) | Answer: -130.7
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of x^2 + 9x + 2 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[2, 1], [7, 9]].
solution: Given: a = 2, b = 1, c = 7, d = 9 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (2)(9) - (1)(7) | Answer: 11

question: Find the determinant of [[-6, -5, 2], [-6, -3, -6], [-4, 6, 0]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: -432

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[6, -6], [6, -7]].
solution: Trace tr = -1, Determinant = -6 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 2

question: Solve for x: 5x + -6y = -12 and 5x + 1y = -3.
solution: Determinant = 5*1 - -6*5 = 35 | x = (e d - b f) / det = -0.8571 | Answer: x = -0.8571
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 7, 13, 100, 12, 6.
solution: Sum = 138 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 27.6 | Answer: 27.6

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 20, 16, 21, 25, 41.
solution: Mean = 24.6 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 9.711

question: Find the slope of the line through (-4, 7) and (-5, 4).
solution: Given: x1 = -4, y1 = 7, x2 = -5, y2 = 4 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (4 - 7) / (-5 - -4) | Answer: 3

question: Find the distance between the points (-6, -4) and (-5, -3).
solution: Given: x1 = -6, y1 = -4, x2 = -5, y2 = -3 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((1)^2 + (1)^2) | Answer: 1.414 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (-2,5), (-6,8), (-3,-1).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 13.5 sq units

question: Find the 16th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 14 and common difference 3.
solution: Given: a = 14, d = 3, n = 16 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = 14 + (16 - 1)*3 | Answer: 59

question: Find the sum of the first 19 terms of an AP with first term -9 and common difference -2.
solution: Given: a = -9, d = -2, n = 19 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 19/2 [2*-9 + (19-1)*-2] | Answer: -513

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 12000 at 11.4% per annum for 3 years.
solution: Given: P = 12000, R = 11.4, Tt = 3 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 12000 * 11.4 * 3 / 100 | Answer: 4104 currency units

question: Find the amount when 30000 is invested at 5.4% per annum compounded annually for 6 years.
solution: Given: P = 30000, R = 5.4, Tt = 6 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 30000 * (1 + 5.4/100)^6 | Answer: 41131 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (-7, 0, 7) and (4, -2, 2).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (2, 1, -6) and (4, -2, -5).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 23.43

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (5, 3, -5) and (-5, 5, 5).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 121.7 degrees

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number 5 + 5i.
solution: Given: a = 5, b = 5 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(5, 5) | Answer: 45 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -4x^3 - 6x^2 + 2x - 7 at x = 3.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-198 with initial guess x0=15, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=0.7 and ordinates 13, 13, 15, 12, 16, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 313 and 539.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 313 and 539 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 55 and 13.
solution: Given: a = 55, b = 13 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 55*13 / 1 | Answer: 715
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 12 mm carries an axial tensile load of 25 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 16 mm and length 2600 mm carries an axial load of 38 kN. Take E = 200 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 64 mm transmits a torque of 450 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 64, Tt = 450 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(450*1000) / (pi*(64)^3) | Answer: 8.743 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 64 mm and length 1300 mm carries a torque of 600 N-m. With G = 80 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (64)^4 / 32 = 1647099 mm^4 | theta = (600*1000)(1300) / (80000 * 1647099) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 0.3392 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 38 mm wide and 290 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 38, h = 290 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 38*(290)^2 / 6 | Answer: 532633 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (63 mm x 240 mm) carries a bending moment of 29 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (78 mm x 160 mm) has effective length 2800 mm and E = 200 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 410 MPa is designed for a working stress of 180 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 410, sw = 180 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 410 / 180 | Answer: 2.278

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1450 mm and wall thickness 7 mm carries an internal pressure of 2.6 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1450, t = 7, P = 2.6 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 2.6*1450 / (2*7) | Answer: 269.3 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 820 K and 380 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 820, Tc = 380 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 380/820) * 100 | Answer: 53.66 %

question: 5.3 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 150 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 5.3, dT = 150 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 5.3 * 0.718 * 150 | Answer: 570.8 kJ

question: 1.4 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 160 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1.4, dT = 160 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 1.4 * 1.005 * 160 | Answer: 225.1 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 2.7 m^3 at 550 K with mass 4.1 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 2.7, Tk = 550, m = 4.1 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 4.1*0.287*550 / 2.7 | Answer: 239.7 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 4.7 kg of air expands isothermally at 310 K from volume V1 to 4*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.7, Tk = 310, ratio = 4 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 4.7*0.287*310*ln(4) | Answer: 579.7 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 0.9 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.26 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 0.9, D = 0.26 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*0.9*0.26 / 0.001 | Answer: 234000

question: Water flows at 3 m/s through a pipe of diameter 290 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 11 m. Taking Cv = 0.97, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 11, cv = 0.97 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.97*sqrt(2*9.81*11) | Answer: 14.25 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 300 mm) water flows at 0.9 m/s. It contracts to diameter 140 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
Water flows at 2.4 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.21 m and length 150 m. With friction factor f = 0.037, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 29 teeth drives a gear of 79 teeth. If the pinion runs at 650 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 29, z2 = 79, N1 = 650 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 650*29 / 79 | Answer: 238.6 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 200 mm rotates at 450 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 200, N = 450 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.2)*450 / 60 | Answer: 4.712 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 6.2 kW at 850 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 6.2, N = 850 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(6.2*1000) / (2*pi*850) | Answer: 69.65 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 9.4 kg rotates at radius 0.18 m at 1000 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 9300 N/m and mass 9.3 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 9300, m = 9.3 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(9300/9.3) | Answer: 5.033 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 1.1 m^2 and thickness 0.35 m has conductivity k = 17.6 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 65 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 1.1, L = 0.35, k = 17.6, dT = 65 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 17.6*1.1*65 / 0.35 | Answer: 3595 W

question: A surface of area 3.7 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 155 W/m^2-K to surroundings 125 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 3.7, h = 155, dT = 125 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 155*3.7*125 | Answer: 71688 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 90 m/min, feed = 0.14 mm/rev, depth of cut = 1.1 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 90, f = 0.14, d = 1.1 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*90*0.14*1.1 | Answer: 13860 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 210 mm is turned at 600 rpm with a feed of 0.23 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 210, N = 600, f = 0.23 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 210 / (0.23*600) | Answer: 1.522 min

question: A resistor of 115 ohm carries a current of 8.7 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 115, I = 8.7 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 8.7 * 115 | Answer: 1 V

question: Three resistors 27 ohm, 18 ohm and 63 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 27, R2 = 18, R3 = 63 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 27 + 18 + 63 | Answer: 108 ohm

question: Two resistors 30 ohm and 63 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 30, R2 = 63 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 30*63 / (30+63) | Answer: 20.32 ohm

question: A device draws 6.1 A at 50 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 50, I = 6.1 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 50 * 6.1 | Answer: 305 W

question: A current of 7.8 A flows through a 108 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 7.8, R = 108 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (7.8)^2 * 108 | Answer: 6571 W

question: Two capacitors 35.3 uF and 30.5 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 35.3, C2 = 30.5 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 35.3*30.5 / (35.3+30.5) | Answer: 16.36 uF

question: A resistor 14 kohm and capacitor 5.7 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 14, C = 5.7 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (14k)(5.7u) = 79.8 ms | Answer: 79.8 ms

question: An inductor 381.9 mH is in series with 84 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 381.9, R = 84 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (381.9e-3) / 84 | Answer: 4.546 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 135.8 mH inductor at 670 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 135.8, f = 670 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (670)(135.8e-3) | Answer: 571.7 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 3.3 uF capacitor at 280 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 3.3, f = 280 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (280)(3.3e-6)) | Answer: 172.2 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 33 ohm, XL = 48 ohm and XC = 77 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 33, XL = 48, XC = 77 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(33^2 + (48 - 77)^2) | Answer: 43.93 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 27.3 mH and C = 0.7 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 27.3, C = 0.7 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(27.3e-3 * 0.7e-6)) | Answer: 1151 Hz

question: A capacitor of 93.6 uF is charged to 225 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 93.6, V = 225 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*93.6e-6*(225)^2 | Answer: 2369 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 300 V with 780 primary turns and 150 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 300, N1 = 780, N2 = 150 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 300 * 150/780 | Answer: 57.69 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 420 V and draws an armature current of 34 A. If the armature resistance is 0.4 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 420, Ia = 34, Ra = 0.4 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 420 - 34*0.4 | Answer: 406.4 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 140 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.98. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 140, VL = 400, pf = 0.98 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*400*140*0.98 / 1000 | Answer: 95.05 kW

question: A load has real power 15 kW and apparent power 220 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 15, S = 220 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 15 / 220 | Answer: 0.06818

question: A machine delivers 60 kW output while drawing 217 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 60, Pi = 217 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 60/217 * 100 | Answer: 27.65 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 23 V across R1 = 16 ohm and R2 = 40 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 23, R1 = 16, R2 = 40 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 23*40 / (16+40) | Answer: 16.43 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 110 kohm and Rin = 39 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 110, Rin = 39 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 110 / 39 | Answer: 2.821

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 40 kohm and Rg = 20 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 40, Rg = 20 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 40/20 | Answer: 3

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 7586. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 7586 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(7586) | Answer: 38.8 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.4 m carries a central point load of 20 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 9.4, W = 20 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 20*9.4 / 4 | Answer: 47 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 4 m carries a UDL of 35 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4, w = 35 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 35*(4)^2 / 8 | Answer: 70 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 1.8 m carries a point load 75 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 1.8, W = 75 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 75*1.8 | Answer: 135 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 2.4 m carries a UDL of 24 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 2.4, w = 24 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 24*(2.4)^2 / 2 | Answer: 69.12 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.3 m carries a point load 85 kN at distance 3.8 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 4.3, a = 3.8, W = 85 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 85*(4.3 - 3.8) / 4.3 | Answer: 9.884 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 3.1 m) carries a central point load 60 kN. With E = 200 GPa and I = 330e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=60000 N, L=3100.0 mm, E=200000 MPa, I=330e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 0.5642 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 4.2 m carries a UDL of 6 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.2, w = 6 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 6*(4.2)^2 / 12 | Answer: 8.82 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 350 mm, clear cover 50 mm and main bars of diameter 16 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 350, c = 50, dia = 16 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 350 - 50 - 16/2 | Answer: 292 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 38.4 m^2 carrying a factored load of 17.6 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 38.4, w = 17.6 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 17.6 * 38.4 | Answer: 675.8 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 3.8 m, unit weight 18 kN/m^3, phi = 35 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 2.4e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1.2, area = 3.8e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 2.4, i = 1.2, A = 3.8 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (2.4e-4)*1.2*(3.8e-3) | Answer: 1094 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.2 m, bed slope 0.006 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.029. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 2.1 m under a head of 0.3 m. Taking Cd = 0.64 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 3.1 m wide carries a discharge of 5.5 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 260 m and design speed 95 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 260, V = 95 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (95)^2 / (127*260) | Answer: 0.2733
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: A tank of volume 160 m^3 treats a flow of 30 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 160, Q = 30 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 160 / 30 | Answer: 5.333 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 310 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.12 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 8 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 310, k = 0.12, t = 8 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 310*(1 - e^(-0.12*8)) | Answer: 191.3 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.36, rainfall intensity 100 mm/h over a catchment of 24.9 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.36, i = 100, A = 24.9 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.36*100*24.9 / 360 | Answer: 2.49 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.07 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 100 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.07, M = 100 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 100*(30+0.07)/30 | Answer: 100.2 m

question: Convert the decimal number 434 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 434 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 1B2 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 01001110 and 00101000.
solution: XOR: 01100110 | Count of 1s = 4 | Answer: 4
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 480 megabits is sent over a link of 25 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 480, B = 25 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 480 / 25 | Answer: 19.2 s

question: A link has bandwidth 80 Mbps and round-trip time 110 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 80, R = 110 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 80e6 * 110e-3 bits = 8800 kb | Answer: 8800 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.92, cache access time 9 ns and main-memory access time 180 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.92, tc = 9, tm = 180 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.92*9 + (1 - 0.92)*180 | Answer: 22.68 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 427019 elements?
solution: Given: n = 427019 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(427019)) + 1 | Answer: 19

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.02, memory access time 190 ns and page-fault service time 7 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 7 ms = 7000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.02)*190 + 0.02*7000000.0 ns | Answer: 140.2 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 2.3 m^3 at 160 kPa and 550 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 2.3, P = 160, Tk = 550 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (160e3)*2.3 / (8.314*550) | Answer: 80.48 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.31 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 18 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.31, t = 18 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.31*18) | Answer: 0.9962

question: For a reaction with A = 1e10 /s and activation energy 50 kJ/mol at 370 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 1, Ea = 50, Tk = 370 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 1e10 * exp(-50e3 / (8.314*370)) | Answer: 873 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.91 and bottoms xW = 0.08, with relative volatility alpha = 2.7. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.91, xw = 0.08, al = 2.7 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.91/0.09)(0.92/0.08)] / ln(2.7) | Answer: 4.788 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.68 and x = 0.24. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.68, x = 0.24 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.68/0.32) / (0.24/0.76) | Answer: 6.729

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.89 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 80 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.89, Psat = 80 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.89 * 80 | Answer: 71.2 kPa

question: A stream of 8.6 kg/s with specific heat 4 kJ/kg-K is heated through 90 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 8.6, cp = 4, dT = 90 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 8.6*4*90 | Answer: 3096 kW

question: A reactor of volume 16.5 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 2.7 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 16.5, Q = 2.7 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 16.5 / 2.7 | Answer: 6.111 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 7.5e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 1 mm with a concentration difference of 200 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 7.5, L = 1, dC = 200 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (7.5e-9)*200 / (1e-3) | Answer: 1500 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 9.3 min and steady-state gain 3.3. For a step input of magnitude 13, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 9.3, K = 3.3, M = 13 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 3.3 * 13 | Answer: 42.9 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 75 m^2 flies at 150 m/s (air density 1.225 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.6. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 75, V = 150, rho = 1.225, CL = 0.6 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1.225*(150)^2*75*0.6 / 1000 | Answer: 620.2 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 25 m^2 flies at 80 m/s (density 1.225 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.02. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 25, V = 80, rho = 1.225, CD = 0.02 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*1.225*(80)^2*25*0.02 / 1000 | Answer: 1.96 kN

question: A specimen under stress 220 MPa shows an elastic strain of 2.7e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 220, eps = 2.7 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 220 / (2.7e-3) MPa = 81.48 GPa | Answer: 81.48 GPa

question: A block of mass 13 kg has a volume of 4.4e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 13, V = 4.4 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 13 / (4.4e-3) | Answer: 2955 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 1400 mm is heated through 90 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 11e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 1400, dT = 90, al = 11 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 1400*11e-6*90 | Answer: 1.386 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 190 ohm, R2 = 120 ohm and R3 = 220 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 190, R2 = 120, R3 = 220 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 120*220 / 190 | Answer: 138.9 ohm

question: A measurement reads 9.32 when the true value is 20. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.32, true = 20 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.32 - 20| / 20 * 100 | Answer: 53.4 %

question: Annual demand is 7000 units, ordering cost 30 per order and holding cost 32 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 7000, S = 30, H = 32 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*7000*30 / 32) | Answer: 114.6 units

question: An asset costs 90000 with salvage value 34000 after 13 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 90000, Sv = 34000, n = 13 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (90000 - 34000) / 13 | Answer: 4308 per year

question: A product sells for 500 per unit with variable cost 120 per unit and fixed costs 110000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 500, V = 120, F = 110000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 110000 / (500 - 120) | Answer: 289.5 units

question: Find the present worth of 130000 received 10 years from now at an interest rate of 7% per year.
solution: Given: F = 130000, n = 10, i = 7 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 130000 / (1 + 0.07)^10 | Answer: 66085 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.93, 0.9 and 0.94 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.93, r2 = 0.9, r3 = 0.94 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.93*0.9*0.94 | Answer: 0.7868

question: A process produces 27 defective items in a batch of 18000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 27, N = 18000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 27/18000 * 1e6 | Answer: 1500 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -3x^3 - 3x^2 + 3 evaluated at x = -2.
For f(x) = 2x^3 + 6x^2 - 3, find f''(x) at x = -4.
Evaluate the definite integral of (3x^2 + x - 3) dx from x = 1 to x = 4.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = 3x^3/3 + 1x^2/2 + -3x | Evaluate F(4) - F(1) | Answer: 61.5
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 2x^2 + 3x = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[6, 4], [7, -4]].
solution: Given: a = 6, b = 4, c = 7, d = -4 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (6)(-4) - (4)(7) | Answer: -52

question: Find the determinant of [[-2, 3, -5], [5, 3, -1], [2, 0, -5]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: 129

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[-8, -3], [-6, -8]].
solution: Trace tr = -16, Determinant = 46 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: -3.757

question: Solve for x: -3x + -6y = 12 and 6x + 2y = -10.
solution: Determinant = -3*2 - -6*6 = 30 | x = (e d - b f) / det = -1.2 | Answer: x = -1.2
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 5, 42, 41, 92, 96.
solution: Sum = 276 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 55.2 | Answer: 55.2

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 16, 38, 2, 9, 39.
solution: Mean = 20.8 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 16.9

question: Find the slope of the line through (5, -1) and (-1, 6).
solution: Given: x1 = 5, y1 = -1, x2 = -1, y2 = 6 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (6 - -1) / (-1 - 5) | Answer: -1.167

question: Find the distance between the points (2, 2) and (7, 2).
solution: Given: x1 = 2, y1 = 2, x2 = 7, y2 = 2 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((5)^2 + (0)^2) | Answer: 5 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (-3,8), (8,-2), (-8,-2).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 80 sq units

question: Find the 39th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 14 and common difference -1.
solution: Given: a = 14, d = -1, n = 39 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = 14 + (39 - 1)*-1 | Answer: -24

question: Find the sum of the first 18 terms of an AP with first term -8 and common difference 2.
solution: Given: a = -8, d = 2, n = 18 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 18/2 [2*-8 + (18-1)*2] | Answer: 162

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 7000 at 8.2% per annum for 6 years.
solution: Given: P = 7000, R = 8.2, Tt = 6 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 7000 * 8.2 * 6 / 100 | Answer: 3444 currency units

question: Find the amount when 39500 is invested at 8.2% per annum compounded annually for 6 years.
solution: Given: P = 39500, R = 8.2, Tt = 6 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 39500 * (1 + 8.2/100)^6 | Answer: 63381 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (-1, -2, -4) and (-4, 1, 7).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (-6, 4, 0) and (-5, 2, 2).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 16.49

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (-4, 4, 4) and (3, -4, 1).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 132.8 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number -5 + 0i.
solution: Given: a = -5, b = 0 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((-5)^2 + (0)^2) | Answer: 5

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number 10 + -11i.
solution: Given: a = 10, b = -11 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(-11, 10) | Answer: -47.73 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = x^3 - 4x^2 - 5x - 1 at x = 1.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-78 with initial guess x0=13, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=0.9 and ordinates 19, 17, 4, 3, 3, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 72 and 366.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 72 and 366 | Answer: GCD = 6

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 4 and 15.
solution: Given: a = 4, b = 15 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 4*15 / 1 | Answer: 60
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 32 mm carries an axial tensile load of 47 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 18 mm and length 1400 mm carries an axial load of 52 kN. Take E = 200 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 41 mm transmits a torque of 1650 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 41, Tt = 1650 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(1650*1000) / (pi*(41)^3) | Answer: 121.9 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 46 mm and length 1900 mm carries a torque of 1100 N-m. With G = 80 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (46)^4 / 32 = 439573 mm^4 | theta = (1100*1000)(1900) / (80000 * 439573) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 3.405 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 150 mm wide and 200 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 150, h = 200 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 150*(200)^2 / 6 | Answer: 1000000 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (80 mm x 200 mm) carries a bending moment of 19 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (38 mm x 100 mm) has effective length 2800 mm and E = 200 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 450 MPa is designed for a working stress of 180 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 450, sw = 180 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 450 / 180 | Answer: 2.5

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1150 mm and wall thickness 20 mm carries an internal pressure of 2 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1150, t = 20, P = 2 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 2*1150 / (2*20) | Answer: 57.5 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 1200 K and 420 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 1200, Tc = 420 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 420/1200) * 100 | Answer: 65 %

question: 1.1 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 80 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1.1, dT = 80 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 1.1 * 0.718 * 80 | Answer: 63.18 kJ

question: 5.1 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 35 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 5.1, dT = 35 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 5.1 * 1.005 * 35 | Answer: 179.4 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 1.6 m^3 at 380 K with mass 1.5 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 1.6, Tk = 380, m = 1.5 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 1.5*0.287*380 / 1.6 | Answer: 102.2 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 1.8 kg of air expands isothermally at 300 K from volume V1 to 5*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1.8, Tk = 300, ratio = 5 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 1.8*0.287*300*ln(5) | Answer: 249.4 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 2.4 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.05 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 2.4, D = 0.05 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*2.4*0.05 / 0.001 | Answer: 120000

question: Water flows at 2.2 m/s through a pipe of diameter 280 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
In a pipe (diameter 360 mm) water flows at 1.8 m/s. It contracts to diameter 50 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 360, d2 = 50, V1 = 1.8 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 1.8*(360/50)^2 | Answer: 93.31 m/s

question: Water flows at 2.6 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.46 m and length 300 m. With friction factor f = 0.024, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 25 teeth drives a gear of 117 teeth. If the pinion runs at 600 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
