solution: Given: z1 = 25, z2 = 117, N1 = 600 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 600*25 / 117 | Answer: 128.2 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 370 mm rotates at 1100 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 370, N = 1100 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.37)*1100 / 60 | Answer: 21.31 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 38.4 kW at 1100 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 38.4, N = 1100 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(38.4*1000) / (2*pi*1100) | Answer: 333.4 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 9.3 kg rotates at radius 0.59 m at 350 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 12100 N/m and mass 14.2 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 12100, m = 14.2 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(12100/14.2) | Answer: 4.646 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 9.8 m^2 and thickness 0.28 m has conductivity k = 45.5 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 155 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 9.8, L = 0.28, k = 45.5, dT = 155 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 45.5*9.8*155 / 0.28 | Answer: 246837 W

question: A surface of area 1.7 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 30 W/m^2-K to surroundings 30 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 1.7, h = 30, dT = 30 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 30*1.7*30 | Answer: 1530 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 80 m/min, feed = 0.46 mm/rev, depth of cut = 1.5 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 80, f = 0.46, d = 1.5 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*80*0.46*1.5 | Answer: 55200 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 310 mm is turned at 1100 rpm with a feed of 0.19 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 310, N = 1100, f = 0.19 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 310 / (0.19*1100) | Answer: 1.483 min

question: A resistor of 107 ohm carries a current of 5.1 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 107, I = 5.1 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 5.1 * 107 | Answer: 545.7 V

question: Three resistors 69 ohm, 55 ohm and 81 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 69, R2 = 55, R3 = 81 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 69 + 55 + 81 | Answer: 205 ohm

question: Two resistors 13 ohm and 84 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 13, R2 = 84 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 13*84 / (13+84) | Answer: 11.26 ohm

question: A device draws 2.4 A at 215 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 215, I = 2.4 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 215 * 2.4 | Answer: 516 W

question: A current of 5.2 A flows through a 128 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 5.2, R = 128 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (5.2)^2 * 128 | Answer: 3461 W

question: Two capacitors 41.6 uF and 24.7 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 41.6, C2 = 24.7 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 41.6*24.7 / (41.6+24.7) | Answer: 15.5 uF

question: A resistor 58 kohm and capacitor 11.6 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 58, C = 11.6 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (58k)(11.6u) = 672.8 ms | Answer: 672.8 ms

question: An inductor 322.1 mH is in series with 185 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 322.1, R = 185 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (322.1e-3) / 185 | Answer: 1.741 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 32.3 mH inductor at 390 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 32.3, f = 390 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (390)(32.3e-3) | Answer: 79.15 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 27.8 uF capacitor at 600 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 27.8, f = 600 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (600)(27.8e-6)) | Answer: 9.542 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 20 ohm, XL = 69 ohm and XC = 140 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 20, XL = 69, XC = 140 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(20^2 + (69 - 140)^2) | Answer: 73.76 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 27.2 mH and C = 3.6 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 27.2, C = 3.6 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(27.2e-3 * 3.6e-6)) | Answer: 508.6 Hz

question: A capacitor of 21.1 uF is charged to 270 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 21.1, V = 270 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*21.1e-6*(270)^2 | Answer: 769.1 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 350 V with 720 primary turns and 320 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 350, N1 = 720, N2 = 320 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 350 * 320/720 | Answer: 155.6 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 210 V and draws an armature current of 6 A. If the armature resistance is 1.41 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 210, Ia = 6, Ra = 1.41 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 210 - 6*1.41 | Answer: 201.5 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 45 A at 415 V (line) with a power factor of 0.78. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 45, VL = 415, pf = 0.78 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*415*45*0.78 / 1000 | Answer: 25.23 kW

question: A load has real power 25 kW and apparent power 105 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 25, S = 105 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 25 / 105 | Answer: 0.2381

question: A machine delivers 95 kW output while drawing 142 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 95, Pi = 142 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 95/142 * 100 | Answer: 66.9 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 12 V across R1 = 23 ohm and R2 = 32 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 12, R1 = 23, R2 = 32 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 12*32 / (23+32) | Answer: 6.982 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 200 kohm and Rin = 36 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 200, Rin = 36 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 200 / 36 | Answer: 5.556

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 100 kohm and Rg = 1 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 100, Rg = 1 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 100/1 | Answer: 101

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 2697. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 2697 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(2697) | Answer: 34.31 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 5.1 m carries a central point load of 70 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.1, W = 70 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 70*5.1 / 4 | Answer: 89.25 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 5.7 m carries a UDL of 20 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.7, w = 20 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 20*(5.7)^2 / 8 | Answer: 81.23 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 2.4 m carries a point load 20 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 2.4, W = 20 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 20*2.4 | Answer: 48 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 2 m carries a UDL of 40 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 2, w = 40 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 40*(2)^2 / 2 | Answer: 80 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 8.3 m carries a point load 55 kN at distance 3.6 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 8.3, a = 3.6, W = 55 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 55*(8.3 - 3.6) / 8.3 | Answer: 31.14 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 7.3 m) carries a central point load 65 kN. With E = 200 GPa and I = 220e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=65000 N, L=7300.0 mm, E=200000 MPa, I=220e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 11.97 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 4.4 m carries a UDL of 12 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.4, w = 12 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 12*(4.4)^2 / 12 | Answer: 19.36 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 400 mm, clear cover 35 mm and main bars of diameter 25 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 400, c = 35, dia = 25 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 400 - 35 - 25/2 | Answer: 352.5 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 35.1 m^2 carrying a factored load of 14.6 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 35.1, w = 14.6 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 14.6 * 35.1 | Answer: 512.5 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 4.9 m, unit weight 16 kN/m^3, phi = 28 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 4.9e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1.3, area = 3.7e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 4.9, i = 1.3, A = 3.7 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (4.9e-4)*1.3*(3.7e-3) | Answer: 2357 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.9 m, bed slope 0.001 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.018. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 2.7 m under a head of 0.4 m. Taking Cd = 0.61 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 3.4 m wide carries a discharge of 4.7 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 160 m and design speed 45 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 160, V = 45 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (45)^2 / (127*160) | Answer: 0.09966
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: A tank of volume 770 m^3 treats a flow of 135 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 770, Q = 135 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 770 / 135 | Answer: 5.704 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 330 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.15 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 3 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 330, k = 0.15, t = 3 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 330*(1 - e^(-0.15*3)) | Answer: 119.6 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.42, rainfall intensity 35 mm/h over a catchment of 19.1 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.42, i = 35, A = 19.1 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.42*35*19.1 / 360 | Answer: 0.7799 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.03 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 430 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.03, M = 430 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 430*(20+0.03)/20 | Answer: 430.6 m

question: Convert the decimal number 1705 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 1705 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 6A9 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 00000100 and 11000101.
solution: XOR: 11000001 | Count of 1s = 3 | Answer: 3
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 320 megabits is sent over a link of 59 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 320, B = 59 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 320 / 59 | Answer: 5.424 s

question: A link has bandwidth 98 Mbps and round-trip time 50 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 98, R = 50 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 98e6 * 50e-3 bits = 4900 kb | Answer: 4900 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.94, cache access time 7 ns and main-memory access time 90 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.94, tc = 7, tm = 90 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.94*7 + (1 - 0.94)*90 | Answer: 11.98 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 458387 elements?
solution: Given: n = 458387 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(458387)) + 1 | Answer: 19

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.004, memory access time 190 ns and page-fault service time 8 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 8 ms = 8000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.004)*190 + 0.004*8000000.0 ns | Answer: 32.19 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 0.2 m^3 at 150 kPa and 330 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 0.2, P = 150, Tk = 330 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (150e3)*0.2 / (8.314*330) | Answer: 10.93 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.2 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 7 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.2, t = 7 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.2*7) | Answer: 0.7534

question: For a reaction with A = 6e10 /s and activation energy 75 kJ/mol at 410 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 6, Ea = 75, Tk = 410 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 6e10 * exp(-75e3 / (8.314*410)) | Answer: 16.7 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.95 and bottoms xW = 0.07, with relative volatility alpha = 2.4. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.95, xw = 0.07, al = 2.4 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.95/0.05)(0.93/0.07)] / ln(2.4) | Answer: 6.318 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.64 and x = 0.45. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.64, x = 0.45 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.64/0.36) / (0.45/0.55) | Answer: 2.173

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.82 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 110 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.82, Psat = 110 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.82 * 110 | Answer: 90.2 kPa

question: A stream of 2.4 kg/s with specific heat 3.1 kJ/kg-K is heated through 115 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 2.4, cp = 3.1, dT = 115 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 2.4*3.1*115 | Answer: 855.6 kW

question: A reactor of volume 19.4 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 2.3 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 19.4, Q = 2.3 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 19.4 / 2.3 | Answer: 8.435 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 4e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 4 mm with a concentration difference of 70 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 4, L = 4, dC = 70 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (4e-9)*70 / (4e-3) | Answer: 70 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 2.7 min and steady-state gain 1. For a step input of magnitude 8, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 2.7, K = 1, M = 8 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 1 * 8 | Answer: 8 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 95 m^2 flies at 250 m/s (air density 1.225 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.7. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 95, V = 250, rho = 1.225, CL = 0.7 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1.225*(250)^2*95*0.7 / 1000 | Answer: 2546 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 25 m^2 flies at 260 m/s (density 1.225 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.11. Find the drag force in kN.
A specimen under stress 390 MPa shows an elastic strain of 0.5e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 390, eps = 0.5 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 390 / (0.5e-3) MPa = 780 GPa | Answer: 780 GPa

question: A block of mass 6 kg has a volume of 1.6e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 6, V = 1.6 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 6 / (1.6e-3) | Answer: 3750 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 900 mm is heated through 100 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 23e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 900, dT = 100, al = 23 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 900*23e-6*100 | Answer: 2.07 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 200 ohm, R2 = 200 ohm and R3 = 55 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 200, R2 = 200, R3 = 55 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 200*55 / 200 | Answer: 55 ohm

question: A measurement reads 10.81 when the true value is 20. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10.81, true = 20 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10.81 - 20| / 20 * 100 | Answer: 45.95 %

question: Annual demand is 4000 units, ordering cost 180 per order and holding cost 24 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 4000, S = 180, H = 24 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*4000*180 / 24) | Answer: 244.9 units

question: An asset costs 320000 with salvage value 28000 after 12 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 320000, Sv = 28000, n = 12 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (320000 - 28000) / 12 | Answer: 24333 per year

question: A product sells for 370 per unit with variable cost 120 per unit and fixed costs 135000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 370, V = 120, F = 135000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 135000 / (370 - 120) | Answer: 540 units

question: Find the present worth of 35000 received 10 years from now at an interest rate of 6% per year.
solution: Given: F = 35000, n = 10, i = 6 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 35000 / (1 + 0.06)^10 | Answer: 19544 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.97, 0.95 and 0.92 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.97, r2 = 0.95, r3 = 0.92 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.97*0.95*0.92 | Answer: 0.8478

question: A process produces 49 defective items in a batch of 9500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 49, N = 9500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 49/9500 * 1e6 | Answer: 5158 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -4x^3 - 8x^2 - 6x + 5 evaluated at x = 1.
For f(x) = -5x^3 - 5x^2 - 4, find f''(x) at x = 5.
Evaluate the definite integral of (-2x^2 - 6x + 2) dx from x = -1 to x = 5.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = -2x^3/3 + -6x^2/2 + 2x | Evaluate F(5) - F(-1) | Answer: -144
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 3x^2 + 11x - 10 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[2, -7], [4, 2]].
solution: Given: a = 2, b = -7, c = 4, d = 2 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (2)(2) - (-7)(4) | Answer: 32

question: Find the determinant of [[-6, 5, -1], [5, -2, 0], [3, 4, 0]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: -26

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[3, 4], [2, -3]].
solution: Trace tr = 0, Determinant = -17 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 4.123

question: Solve for x: 0x + -1y = -3 and -6x + 0y = 9.
solution: Determinant = 0*0 - -1*-6 = -6 | x = (e d - b f) / det = -1.5 | Answer: x = -1.5
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 33, 98, 16, 65, 46.
solution: Sum = 258 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 51.6 | Answer: 51.6

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 17, 24, 6, 1, 35.
solution: Mean = 16.6 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 13.69

question: Find the slope of the line through (5, -4) and (-5, -5).
solution: Given: x1 = 5, y1 = -4, x2 = -5, y2 = -5 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (-5 - -4) / (-5 - 5) | Answer: 0.1

question: Find the distance between the points (0, -8) and (-6, -7).
solution: Given: x1 = 0, y1 = -8, x2 = -6, y2 = -7 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-6)^2 + (1)^2) | Answer: 6.083 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (-1,3), (8,-4), (5,6).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 34.5 sq units

question: Find the 39th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -19 and common difference -1.
solution: Given: a = -19, d = -1, n = 39 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -19 + (39 - 1)*-1 | Answer: -57

question: Find the sum of the first 16 terms of an AP with first term 5 and common difference -3.
solution: Given: a = 5, d = -3, n = 16 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 16/2 [2*5 + (16-1)*-3] | Answer: -280

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 30500 at 5.9% per annum for 4 years.
solution: Given: P = 30500, R = 5.9, Tt = 4 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 30500 * 5.9 * 4 / 100 | Answer: 7198 currency units

question: Find the amount when 14000 is invested at 5.4% per annum compounded annually for 6 years.
solution: Given: P = 14000, R = 5.4, Tt = 6 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 14000 * (1 + 5.4/100)^6 | Answer: 19194 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (1, -7, 0) and (2, -4, -6).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (-5, -3, 4) and (-6, 1, 4).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 28.3

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (2, 2, -2) and (-5, -2, 3).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 159.5 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number -3 + 11i.
solution: Given: a = -3, b = 11 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((-3)^2 + (11)^2) | Answer: 11.4

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number -2 + 4i.
solution: Given: a = -2, b = 4 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(4, -2) | Answer: 116.6 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = x^3 - x^2 - 9x - 9 at x = 4.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-81 with initial guess x0=10, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=0.8 and ordinates 20, 13, 6, 9, 3, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 459 and 129.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 459 and 129 | Answer: GCD = 3

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 31 and 25.
solution: Given: a = 31, b = 25 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 31*25 / 1 | Answer: 775
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 36 mm carries an axial tensile load of 21 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 15 mm and length 600 mm carries an axial load of 52 kN. Take E = 110 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 58 mm transmits a torque of 1550 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 58, Tt = 1550 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(1550*1000) / (pi*(58)^3) | Answer: 40.46 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 45 mm and length 500 mm carries a torque of 550 N-m. With G = 77 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (45)^4 / 32 = 402578 mm^4 | theta = (550*1000)(500) / (77000 * 402578) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 0.5083 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 61 mm wide and 190 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 61, h = 190 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 61*(190)^2 / 6 | Answer: 367017 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (72 mm x 240 mm) carries a bending moment of 14 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (51 mm x 160 mm) has effective length 2300 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 630 MPa is designed for a working stress of 170 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 630, sw = 170 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 630 / 170 | Answer: 3.706

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 800 mm and wall thickness 9 mm carries an internal pressure of 3 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 800, t = 9, P = 3 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 3*800 / (2*9) | Answer: 133.3 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 920 K and 310 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 920, Tc = 310 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 310/920) * 100 | Answer: 66.3 %

question: A heat pump operates between 268 K and 318 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 268, Th = 318 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 318 / (318 - 268) | Answer: 6.36

question: 6.4 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 55 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 6.4, dT = 55 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 6.4 * 0.718 * 55 | Answer: 252.7 kJ

question: 6.2 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 190 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 6.2, dT = 190 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 6.2 * 1.005 * 190 | Answer: 1184 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 0.7 m^3 at 530 K with mass 3 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 0.7, Tk = 530, m = 3 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 3*0.287*530 / 0.7 | Answer: 651.9 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 2.2 kg of air expands isothermally at 420 K from volume V1 to 2*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.2, Tk = 420, ratio = 2 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 2.2*0.287*420*ln(2) | Answer: 183.8 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 4.4 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.18 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 4.4, D = 0.18 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*4.4*0.18 / 0.001 | Answer: 792000

question: Water flows at 4 m/s through a pipe of diameter 160 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 10.4 m. Taking Cv = 0.98, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 10.4, cv = 0.98 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.98*sqrt(2*9.81*10.4) | Answer: 14 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 400 mm) water flows at 1.9 m/s. It contracts to diameter 100 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 400, d2 = 100, V1 = 1.9 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 1.9*(400/100)^2 | Answer: 30.4 m/s

question: Water flows at 2.1 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.28 m and length 110 m. With friction factor f = 0.031, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 19 teeth drives a gear of 83 teeth. If the pinion runs at 850 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 19, z2 = 83, N1 = 850 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 850*19 / 83 | Answer: 194.6 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 390 mm rotates at 200 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 390, N = 200 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.39)*200 / 60 | Answer: 4.084 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 28.5 kW at 1400 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 28.5, N = 1400 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(28.5*1000) / (2*pi*1400) | Answer: 194.4 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 0.6 kg rotates at radius 0.28 m at 500 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 7600 N/m and mass 11.8 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 7600, m = 11.8 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(7600/11.8) | Answer: 4.039 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 9.6 m^2 and thickness 0.35 m has conductivity k = 16.8 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 185 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 9.6, L = 0.35, k = 16.8, dT = 185 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 16.8*9.6*185 / 0.35 | Answer: 85248 W

question: A surface of area 4.2 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 140 W/m^2-K to surroundings 55 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 4.2, h = 140, dT = 55 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 140*4.2*55 | Answer: 32340 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 80 m/min, feed = 0.1 mm/rev, depth of cut = 0.5 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 80, f = 0.1, d = 0.5 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*80*0.1*0.5 | Answer: 4000 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 210 mm is turned at 600 rpm with a feed of 0.39 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 210, N = 600, f = 0.39 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 210 / (0.39*600) | Answer: 0.8974 min

question: A resistor of 141 ohm carries a current of 0.4 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 141, I = 0.4 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 0.4 * 141 | Answer: 56.4 V

question: Three resistors 11 ohm, 2 ohm and 66 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 11, R2 = 2, R3 = 66 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 11 + 2 + 66 | Answer: 79 ohm

question: Two resistors 93 ohm and 28 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 93, R2 = 28 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 93*28 / (93+28) | Answer: 21.52 ohm

question: A device draws 7.7 A at 20 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 20, I = 7.7 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 20 * 7.7 | Answer: 154 W

question: A current of 7.6 A flows through a 78 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 7.6, R = 78 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (7.6)^2 * 78 | Answer: 4505 W

question: Two capacitors 32.7 uF and 16.2 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 32.7, C2 = 16.2 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 32.7*16.2 / (32.7+16.2) | Answer: 10.83 uF

question: A resistor 83 kohm and capacitor 9.5 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 83, C = 9.5 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (83k)(9.5u) = 788.5 ms | Answer: 788.5 ms

question: An inductor 500 mH is in series with 182 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 500, R = 182 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (500e-3) / 182 | Answer: 2.747 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 145.5 mH inductor at 240 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 145.5, f = 240 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (240)(145.5e-3) | Answer: 219.4 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 48.3 uF capacitor at 530 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 48.3, f = 530 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (530)(48.3e-6)) | Answer: 6.217 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 16 ohm, XL = 128 ohm and XC = 81 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 16, XL = 128, XC = 81 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(16^2 + (128 - 81)^2) | Answer: 49.65 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 65.5 mH and C = 7.6 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 65.5, C = 7.6 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(65.5e-3 * 7.6e-6)) | Answer: 225.6 Hz

question: A capacitor of 4.7 uF is charged to 270 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 4.7, V = 270 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*4.7e-6*(270)^2 | Answer: 171.3 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 200 V with 570 primary turns and 390 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 200, N1 = 570, N2 = 390 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 200 * 390/570 | Answer: 136.8 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 170 V and draws an armature current of 28 A. If the armature resistance is 0.95 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 170, Ia = 28, Ra = 0.95 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 170 - 28*0.95 | Answer: 143.4 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 15 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.72. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 15, VL = 400, pf = 0.72 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*400*15*0.72 / 1000 | Answer: 7.482 kW

question: A load has real power 60 kW and apparent power 80 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 60, S = 80 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 60 / 80 | Answer: 0.75

question: A machine delivers 15 kW output while drawing 187 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 15, Pi = 187 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 15/187 * 100 | Answer: 8.021 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 21 V across R1 = 28 ohm and R2 = 21 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 21, R1 = 28, R2 = 21 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 21*21 / (28+21) | Answer: 9 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 50 kohm and Rin = 38 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 50, Rin = 38 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 50 / 38 | Answer: 1.316

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 259. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 259 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(259) | Answer: 24.13 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 7.1 m carries a central point load of 75 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7.1, W = 75 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 75*7.1 / 4 | Answer: 133.1 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 7.1 m carries a UDL of 25 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7.1, w = 25 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 25*(7.1)^2 / 8 | Answer: 157.5 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 6 m carries a point load 65 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6, W = 65 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 65*6 | Answer: 390 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 1.8 m carries a UDL of 40 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 1.8, w = 40 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 40*(1.8)^2 / 2 | Answer: 64.8 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.1 m carries a point load 35 kN at distance 2.5 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 9.1, a = 2.5, W = 35 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 35*(9.1 - 2.5) / 9.1 | Answer: 25.38 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 4.4 m) carries a central point load 75 kN. With E = 30 GPa and I = 70e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=75000 N, L=4400.0 mm, E=30000 MPa, I=70e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 63.38 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 5.7 m carries a UDL of 33 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.7, w = 33 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 33*(5.7)^2 / 12 | Answer: 89.35 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 680 mm, clear cover 40 mm and main bars of diameter 25 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 680, c = 40, dia = 25 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 680 - 40 - 25/2 | Answer: 627.5 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 21.3 m^2 carrying a factored load of 17.1 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 21.3, w = 17.1 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 17.1 * 21.3 | Answer: 364.2 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 6.4 m, unit weight 18 kN/m^3, phi = 31 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 6.7e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.3, area = 1.3e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 6.7, i = 0.3, A = 1.3 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (6.7e-4)*0.3*(1.3e-3) | Answer: 261.3 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.7 m, bed slope 0.007 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.016. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 2.9 m under a head of 0.8 m. Taking Cd = 0.6 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 2.4 m wide carries a discharge of 12.1 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 500 m and design speed 100 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 500, V = 100 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (100)^2 / (127*500) | Answer: 0.1575
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: A tank of volume 830 m^3 treats a flow of 85 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 830, Q = 85 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 830 / 85 | Answer: 9.765 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 330 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.2 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 3 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 330, k = 0.2, t = 3 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 330*(1 - e^(-0.2*3)) | Answer: 148.9 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.51, rainfall intensity 65 mm/h over a catchment of 25.1 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.51, i = 65, A = 25.1 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.51*65*25.1 / 360 | Answer: 2.311 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.05 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 740 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.05, M = 740 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 740*(30+0.05)/30 | Answer: 741.2 m

question: Convert the decimal number 646 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 646 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 286 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 00011011 and 00101101.
solution: XOR: 00110110 | Count of 1s = 4 | Answer: 4
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 640 megabits is sent over a link of 36 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 640, B = 36 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 640 / 36 | Answer: 17.78 s

question: A link has bandwidth 78 Mbps and round-trip time 10 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 78, R = 10 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 78e6 * 10e-3 bits = 780 kb | Answer: 780 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.9, cache access time 7 ns and main-memory access time 120 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.9, tc = 7, tm = 120 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.9*7 + (1 - 0.9)*120 | Answer: 18.3 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 737925 elements?
solution: Given: n = 737925 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(737925)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.004, memory access time 100 ns and page-fault service time 10 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 10 ms = 10000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.004)*100 + 0.004*10000000.0 ns | Answer: 40.1 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 1.1 m^3 at 390 kPa and 390 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 1.1, P = 390, Tk = 390 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (390e3)*1.1 / (8.314*390) | Answer: 132.3 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.35 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 19 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.35, t = 19 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.35*19) | Answer: 0.9987

question: For a reaction with A = 7e10 /s and activation energy 65 kJ/mol at 330 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 7, Ea = 65, Tk = 330 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 7e10 * exp(-65e3 / (8.314*330)) | Answer: 3.598 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.9 and bottoms xW = 0.06, with relative volatility alpha = 2.8. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.9, xw = 0.06, al = 2.8 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.9/0.1)(0.94/0.06)] / ln(2.8) | Answer: 4.806 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.83 and x = 0.31. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.83, x = 0.31 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.83/0.17) / (0.31/0.69) | Answer: 10.87

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.45 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 50 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.45, Psat = 50 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.45 * 50 | Answer: 22.5 kPa

question: A stream of 8.2 kg/s with specific heat 3.3 kJ/kg-K is heated through 35 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 8.2, cp = 3.3, dT = 35 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 8.2*3.3*35 | Answer: 947.1 kW

question: A reactor of volume 13.9 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 4.3 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 13.9, Q = 4.3 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 13.9 / 4.3 | Answer: 3.233 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 5.2e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 1 mm with a concentration difference of 150 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 5.2, L = 1, dC = 150 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (5.2e-9)*150 / (1e-3) | Answer: 780 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 3.4 min and steady-state gain 3.6. For a step input of magnitude 13, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 3.4, K = 3.6, M = 13 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 3.6 * 13 | Answer: 46.8 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 115 m^2 flies at 160 m/s (air density 1.225 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.6. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 115, V = 160, rho = 1.225, CL = 0.6 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1.225*(160)^2*115*0.6 / 1000 | Answer: 1082 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 100 m^2 flies at 90 m/s (density 0.4 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.11. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 100, V = 90, rho = 0.4, CD = 0.11 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.4*(90)^2*100*0.11 / 1000 | Answer: 17.82 kN

question: A specimen under stress 370 MPa shows an elastic strain of 1.4e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 370, eps = 1.4 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 370 / (1.4e-3) MPa = 264.3 GPa | Answer: 264.3 GPa

question: A block of mass 8 kg has a volume of 0.6e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 8, V = 0.6 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 8 / (0.6e-3) | Answer: 13333 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 2800 mm is heated through 105 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 12e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 2800, dT = 105, al = 12 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 2800*12e-6*105 | Answer: 3.528 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 80 ohm, R2 = 180 ohm and R3 = 105 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 80, R2 = 180, R3 = 105 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 180*105 / 80 | Answer: 236.2 ohm

question: A measurement reads 9.26 when the true value is 100. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.26, true = 100 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.26 - 100| / 100 * 100 | Answer: 90.74 %

question: Annual demand is 34500 units, ordering cost 140 per order and holding cost 26 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 34500, S = 140, H = 26 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*34500*140 / 26) | Answer: 609.5 units

question: An asset costs 460000 with salvage value 26000 after 7 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 460000, Sv = 26000, n = 7 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (460000 - 26000) / 7 | Answer: 62000 per year

question: A product sells for 150 per unit with variable cost 70 per unit and fixed costs 55000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 150, V = 70, F = 55000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 55000 / (150 - 70) | Answer: 687.5 units

question: Find the present worth of 75000 received 10 years from now at an interest rate of 12% per year.
solution: Given: F = 75000, n = 10, i = 12 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 75000 / (1 + 0.12)^10 | Answer: 24148 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.97, 0.98 and 0.9 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.97, r2 = 0.98, r3 = 0.9 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.97*0.98*0.9 | Answer: 0.8555

question: A process produces 9 defective items in a batch of 18500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 9, N = 18500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 9/18500 * 1e6 | Answer: 486.5 PPM

question: Find the slope of the line through (-7, 6) and (-1, -4).
Find the distance between the points (-7, -2) and (1, -7).
solution: Given: x1 = -7, y1 = -2, x2 = 1, y2 = -7 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((8)^2 + (-5)^2) | Answer: 9.434 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (-3,7), (-7,0), (5,8).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 26 sq units

question: Find the 22th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -6 and common difference 5.
solution: Given: a = -6, d = 5, n = 22 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -6 + (22 - 1)*5 | Answer: 99

question: Find the sum of the first 14 terms of an AP with first term 9 and common difference 0.
solution: Given: a = 9, d = 0, n = 14 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 14/2 [2*9 + (14-1)*0] | Answer: 126

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 41000 at 13.9% per annum for 6 years.
solution: Given: P = 41000, R = 13.9, Tt = 6 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 41000 * 13.9 * 6 / 100 | Answer: 34194 currency units

question: Find the amount when 13000 is invested at 9.8% per annum compounded annually for 2 years.
solution: Given: P = 13000, R = 9.8, Tt = 2 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 13000 * (1 + 9.8/100)^2 | Answer: 15673 currency units

question: Find the modulus of the complex number 3 + -9i.
solution: Given: a = 3, b = -9 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((3)^2 + (-9)^2) | Answer: 9.487

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number 6 + -1i.
solution: Given: a = 6, b = -1 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(-1, 6) | Answer: -9.462 degrees

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 38 and 39.

question: A circular rod of diameter 50 mm carries an axial tensile load of 26 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 22 mm and length 500 mm carries an axial load of 33 kN. Take E = 200 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 65 mm transmits a torque of 700 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 65, Tt = 700 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(700*1000) / (pi*(65)^3) | Answer: 12.98 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 41 mm and length 900 mm carries a torque of 350 N-m. With G = 80 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (41)^4 / 32 = 277418 mm^4 | theta = (350*1000)(900) / (80000 * 277418) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 0.8132 degrees

question: A rectangular beam section is 95 mm wide and 190 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 95, h = 190 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 95*(190)^2 / 6 | Answer: 571583 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (70 mm x 260 mm) carries a bending moment of 7 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.

question: A component of ultimate strength 610 MPa is designed for a working stress of 140 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 610, sw = 140 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 610 / 140 | Answer: 4.357

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 800 mm and wall thickness 6 mm carries an internal pressure of 1.2 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 800, t = 6, P = 1.2 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 1.2*800 / (2*6) | Answer: 80 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 740 K and 380 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 740, Tc = 380 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 380/740) * 100 | Answer: 48.65 %

question: A heat pump operates between 281 K and 316 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 281, Th = 316 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 316 / (316 - 281) | Answer: 9.029

question: 3.2 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 100 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.2, dT = 100 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 3.2 * 0.718 * 100 | Answer: 229.8 kJ

question: 4.3 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 200 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.3, dT = 200 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 4.3 * 1.005 * 200 | Answer: 864.3 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 4 m^3 at 490 K with mass 4.9 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 4, Tk = 490, m = 4.9 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 4.9*0.287*490 / 4 | Answer: 172.3 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 2.5 kg of air expands isothermally at 380 K from volume V1 to 4*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.5, Tk = 380, ratio = 4 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 2.5*0.287*380*ln(4) | Answer: 378 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 2.7 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.1 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 2.7, D = 0.1 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*2.7*0.1 / 0.001 | Answer: 270000

question: Water flows at 3.5 m/s through a pipe of diameter 240 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 4.5 m. Taking Cv = 0.95, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 4.5, cv = 0.95 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.95*sqrt(2*9.81*4.5) | Answer: 8.926 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 300 mm) water flows at 0.8 m/s. It contracts to diameter 80 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 300, d2 = 80, V1 = 0.8 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 0.8*(300/80)^2 | Answer: 11.25 m/s

question: Water flows at 3.4 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.49 m and length 110 m. With friction factor f = 0.025, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 33 teeth drives a gear of 70 teeth. If the pinion runs at 500 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 33, z2 = 70, N1 = 500 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 500*33 / 70 | Answer: 235.7 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 550 mm rotates at 800 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 550, N = 800 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.55)*800 / 60 | Answer: 23.04 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 18.1 kW at 850 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 18.1, N = 850 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(18.1*1000) / (2*pi*850) | Answer: 203.3 N-m

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 2700 N/m and mass 1.1 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 2700, m = 1.1 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(2700/1.1) | Answer: 7.885 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 6 m^2 and thickness 0.16 m has conductivity k = 22.4 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 190 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 6, L = 0.16, k = 22.4, dT = 190 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 22.4*6*190 / 0.16 | Answer: 159600 W

question: A surface of area 3.7 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 180 W/m^2-K to surroundings 95 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 3.7, h = 180, dT = 95 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 180*3.7*95 | Answer: 63270 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 230 m/min, feed = 0.16 mm/rev, depth of cut = 1.2 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 230, f = 0.16, d = 1.2 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*230*0.16*1.2 | Answer: 44160 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 340 mm is turned at 900 rpm with a feed of 0.12 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 340, N = 900, f = 0.12 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 340 / (0.12*900) | Answer: 3.148 min

question: A resistor of 193 ohm carries a current of 8.6 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 193, I = 8.6 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 8.6 * 193 | Answer: 166 V

question: Three resistors 58 ohm, 61 ohm and 6 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 58, R2 = 61, R3 = 6 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 58 + 61 + 6 | Answer: 125 ohm

question: Two resistors 17 ohm and 109 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 17, R2 = 109 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 17*109 / (17+109) | Answer: 14.71 ohm

question: A device draws 5.9 A at 170 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 170, I = 5.9 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 170 * 5.9 | Answer: 1003 W

question: A current of 11.8 A flows through a 106 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 11.8, R = 106 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (11.8)^2 * 106 | Answer: 14759 W

question: Two capacitors 20.1 uF and 12.9 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 20.1, C2 = 12.9 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 20.1*12.9 / (20.1+12.9) | Answer: 7.857 uF

question: A resistor 7 kohm and capacitor 11 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 7, C = 11 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (7k)(11u) = 77 ms | Answer: 77 ms

question: An inductor 52.1 mH is in series with 184 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 52.1, R = 184 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (52.1e-3) / 184 | Answer: 0.2832 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 141.8 mH inductor at 260 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 141.8, f = 260 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (260)(141.8e-3) | Answer: 231.6 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 27.9 uF capacitor at 630 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 27.9, f = 630 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (630)(27.9e-6)) | Answer: 9.055 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 74 ohm, XL = 16 ohm and XC = 91 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 74, XL = 16, XC = 91 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(74^2 + (16 - 91)^2) | Answer: 105.4 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 98.9 mH and C = 4.6 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 98.9, C = 4.6 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(98.9e-3 * 4.6e-6)) | Answer: 236 Hz

question: A capacitor of 6.7 uF is charged to 245 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 6.7, V = 245 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*6.7e-6*(245)^2 | Answer: 201.1 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 240 V with 400 primary turns and 290 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 240, N1 = 400, N2 = 290 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 240 * 290/400 | Answer: 174 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 400 V and draws an armature current of 57 A. If the armature resistance is 0.98 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 400, Ia = 57, Ra = 0.98 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 400 - 57*0.98 | Answer: 344.1 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 50 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.72. Find the total real power in kW.

question: A load has real power 40 kW and apparent power 160 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 40, S = 160 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 40 / 160 | Answer: 0.25

question: A machine delivers 30 kW output while drawing 197 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 16 V across R1 = 30 ohm and R2 = 37 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 180 kohm and Rin = 27 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 40 kohm and Rg = 38 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 40, Rg = 38 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 40/38 | Answer: 2.053

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 8532. Express the gain in decibels (power).

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.8 m carries a central point load of 80 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.

question: A simply supported beam of span 5.4 m carries a UDL of 40 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.4, w = 40 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 40*(5.4)^2 / 8 | Answer: 145.8 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 1.6 m carries a point load 75 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 1.6, W = 75 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 75*1.6 | Answer: 120 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 1.1 m carries a UDL of 36 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 1.1, w = 36 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 36*(1.1)^2 / 2 | Answer: 21.78 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.4 m carries a point load 40 kN at distance 2.6 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 4.4, a = 2.6, W = 40 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 40*(4.4 - 2.6) / 4.4 | Answer: 16.36 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 7.6 m) carries a central point load 20 kN. With E = 30 GPa and I = 320e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=20000 N, L=7600.0 mm, E=30000 MPa, I=320e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 19.05 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 6.5 m carries a UDL of 45 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6.5, w = 45 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 45*(6.5)^2 / 12 | Answer: 158.4 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 630 mm, clear cover 45 mm and main bars of diameter 12 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 630, c = 45, dia = 12 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 630 - 45 - 12/2 | Answer: 579 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 22.7 m^2 carrying a factored load of 14.2 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 22.7, w = 14.2 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 14.2 * 22.7 | Answer: 322.3 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 3.6 m, unit weight 18 kN/m^3, phi = 35 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 8.2e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.8, area = 2.3e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 8.2, i = 0.8, A = 2.3 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (8.2e-4)*0.8*(2.3e-3) | Answer: 1509 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.6 m, bed slope 0.001 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.016. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 1.8 m under a head of 0.9 m. Taking Cd = 0.61 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.

question: A rectangular channel 2.3 m wide carries a discharge of 14.4 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).

question: A tank of volume 90 m^3 treats a flow of 145 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 90, Q = 145 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 90 / 145 | Answer: 0.6207 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 290 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.18 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 3 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 290, k = 0.18, t = 3 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 290*(1 - e^(-0.18*3)) | Answer: 121 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.46, rainfall intensity 70 mm/h over a catchment of 39.2 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.46, i = 70, A = 39.2 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.46*70*39.2 / 360 | Answer: 3.506 m^3/s

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.05 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 300 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.05, M = 300 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 300*(30+0.05)/30 | Answer: 300.5 m

question: Convert the decimal number 2447 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 2447 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 98F (hex)

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 00001111 and 10010011.
solution: XOR: 10011100 | Count of 1s = 4 | Answer: 4
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 1000 megabits is sent over a link of 35 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 1000, B = 35 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 1000 / 35 | Answer: 28.57 s

question: A link has bandwidth 61 Mbps and round-trip time 30 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 61, R = 30 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 61e6 * 30e-3 bits = 1830 kb | Answer: 1830 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.87, cache access time 9 ns and main-memory access time 160 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.87, tc = 9, tm = 160 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.87*9 + (1 - 0.87)*160 | Answer: 28.63 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 243537 elements?
solution: Given: n = 243537 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(243537)) + 1 | Answer: 18

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.017, memory access time 80 ns and page-fault service time 10 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 10 ms = 10000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.017)*80 + 0.017*10000000.0 ns | Answer: 170.1 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 2.3 m^3 at 280 kPa and 340 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 2.3, P = 280, Tk = 340 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (280e3)*2.3 / (8.314*340) | Answer: 227.8 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.38 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 5 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.38, t = 5 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.38*5) | Answer: 0.8504

question: For a reaction with A = 6e10 /s and activation energy 50 kJ/mol at 440 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 6, Ea = 50, Tk = 440 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 6e10 * exp(-50e3 / (8.314*440)) | Answer: 69532 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.94 and bottoms xW = 0.09, with relative volatility alpha = 2. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.94, xw = 0.09, al = 2 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.94/0.06)(0.91/0.09)] / ln(2) | Answer: 7.307 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.55 and x = 0.36. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.55, x = 0.36 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.55/0.45) / (0.36/0.64) | Answer: 2.173

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.34 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 50 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.34, Psat = 50 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.34 * 50 | Answer: 17 kPa

question: A stream of 3.6 kg/s with specific heat 3.4 kJ/kg-K is heated through 35 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 3.6, cp = 3.4, dT = 35 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 3.6*3.4*35 | Answer: 428.4 kW

question: A reactor of volume 9.6 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 2.4 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 9.6, Q = 2.4 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 9.6 / 2.4 | Answer: 4 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 2e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 1 mm with a concentration difference of 170 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 2, L = 1, dC = 170 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (2e-9)*170 / (1e-3) | Answer: 340 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 9.8 min and steady-state gain 3.8. For a step input of magnitude 15, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 9.8, K = 3.8, M = 15 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 3.8 * 15 | Answer: 57 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 35 m^2 flies at 170 m/s (air density 1 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.3. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 35, V = 170, rho = 1, CL = 0.3 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1*(170)^2*35*0.3 / 1000 | Answer: 151.7 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 95 m^2 flies at 60 m/s (density 0.7 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.03. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 95, V = 60, rho = 0.7, CD = 0.03 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.7*(60)^2*95*0.03 / 1000 | Answer: 3.591 kN

question: A specimen under stress 340 MPa shows an elastic strain of 1e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 340, eps = 1 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 340 / (1e-3) MPa = 340 GPa | Answer: 340 GPa

question: A block of mass 10 kg has a volume of 1.7e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.

question: A rod of length 2300 mm is heated through 30 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 12e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 2300, dT = 30, al = 12 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 2300*12e-6*30 | Answer: 0.828 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 125 ohm, R2 = 35 ohm and R3 = 155 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 125, R2 = 35, R3 = 155 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 35*155 / 125 | Answer: 43.4 ohm

question: A measurement reads 9.37 when the true value is 10. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.37, true = 10 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.37 - 10| / 10 * 100 | Answer: 6.3 %

question: Annual demand is 43500 units, ordering cost 130 per order and holding cost 5 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 43500, S = 130, H = 5 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*43500*130 / 5) | Answer: 1504 units

question: An asset costs 440000 with salvage value 16000 after 13 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 440000, Sv = 16000, n = 13 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (440000 - 16000) / 13 | Answer: 32615 per year

question: A product sells for 370 per unit with variable cost 200 per unit and fixed costs 90000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 370, V = 200, F = 90000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 90000 / (370 - 200) | Answer: 529.4 units

question: Find the present worth of 115000 received 7 years from now at an interest rate of 11% per year.
solution: Given: F = 115000, n = 7, i = 11 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 115000 / (1 + 0.11)^7 | Answer: 55391 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.93, 0.96 and 0.97 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.93, r2 = 0.96, r3 = 0.97 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.93*0.96*0.97 | Answer: 0.866

question: A process produces 5 defective items in a batch of 14000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 5, N = 14000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 5/14000 * 1e6 | Answer: 357.1 PPM

question: Find the distance between the points (8, -1) and (-5, 9).

question: Find the 31th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -9 and common difference -6.

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 26500 at 8.3% per annum for 2 years.
solution: Given: P = 26500, R = 8.3, Tt = 2 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 26500 * 8.3 * 2 / 100 | Answer: 4399 currency units

question: Find the amount when 12000 is invested at 4.1% per annum compounded annually for 3 years.

question: Find the modulus of the complex number -4 + -9i.

question: A circular rod of diameter 28 mm carries an axial tensile load of 95 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.

A solid shaft of diameter 25 mm transmits a torque of 2250 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.

question: A shaft of diameter 36 mm and length 900 mm carries a torque of 1050 N-m. With G = 80 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.

question: A rectangular beam section is 63 mm wide and 160 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.

question: A component of ultimate strength 600 MPa is designed for a working stress of 190 MPa. Find the factor of safety.

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1100 mm and wall thickness 8 mm carries an internal pressure of 1.9 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1100, t = 8, P = 1.9 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 1.9*1100 / (2*8) | Answer: 130.6 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 660 K and 280 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 660, Tc = 280 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 280/660) * 100 | Answer: 57.58 %

question: A heat pump operates between 280 K and 302 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.

question: 5.2 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 80 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 5.2, dT = 80 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 5.2 * 0.718 * 80 | Answer: 298.7 kJ

question: 6.3 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 190 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 6.3, dT = 190 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 6.3 * 1.005 * 190 | Answer: 1203 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 1.4 m^3 at 560 K with mass 4.7 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).

formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 3.4 kg of air expands isothermally at 440 K from volume V1 to 4*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.4, Tk = 440, ratio = 4 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 3.4*0.287*440*ln(4) | Answer: 595.2 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 3.1 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.37 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 3.1, D = 0.37 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*3.1*0.37 / 0.001 | Answer: 1147000

question: Water flows at 1.6 m/s through a pipe of diameter 100 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
