Water flows at 1.2 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.34 m and length 60 m. With friction factor f = 0.023, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 26 teeth drives a gear of 60 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1300 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 26, z2 = 60, N1 = 1300 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1300*26 / 60 | Answer: 563.3 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 260 mm rotates at 500 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 260, N = 500 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.26)*500 / 60 | Answer: 6.807 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 22.6 kW at 750 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 22.6, N = 750 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(22.6*1000) / (2*pi*750) | Answer: 287.8 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 2.9 kg rotates at radius 0.13 m at 250 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 17000 N/m and mass 4.4 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 17000, m = 4.4 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(17000/4.4) | Answer: 9.893 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 9.1 m^2 and thickness 0.18 m has conductivity k = 38.3 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 95 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 9.1, L = 0.18, k = 38.3, dT = 95 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 38.3*9.1*95 / 0.18 | Answer: 183946 W

question: A surface of area 2.7 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 100 W/m^2-K to surroundings 65 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 2.7, h = 100, dT = 65 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 100*2.7*65 | Answer: 17550 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 200 m/min, feed = 0.33 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2.4 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 200, f = 0.33, d = 2.4 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*200*0.33*2.4 | Answer: 158400 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 80 mm is turned at 700 rpm with a feed of 0.3 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 80, N = 700, f = 0.3 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 80 / (0.3*700) | Answer: 0.381 min

question: A resistor of 93 ohm carries a current of 9.5 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 93, I = 9.5 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 9.5 * 93 | Answer: 883.5 V

question: Three resistors 76 ohm, 37 ohm and 30 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 76, R2 = 37, R3 = 30 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 76 + 37 + 30 | Answer: 143 ohm

question: Two resistors 100 ohm and 16 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 100, R2 = 16 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 100*16 / (100+16) | Answer: 13.79 ohm

question: A device draws 2.1 A at 190 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 190, I = 2.1 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 190 * 2.1 | Answer: 399 W

question: A current of 6.7 A flows through a 109 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 6.7, R = 109 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (6.7)^2 * 109 | Answer: 4893 W

question: Two capacitors 6.8 uF and 29 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 6.8, C2 = 29 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 6.8*29 / (6.8+29) | Answer: 5.508 uF

question: A resistor 86 kohm and capacitor 12 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 86, C = 12 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (86k)(12u) = 1032 ms | Answer: 1032 ms

question: An inductor 351.5 mH is in series with 43 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 351.5, R = 43 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (351.5e-3) / 43 | Answer: 8.174 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 17.8 mH inductor at 60 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 17.8, f = 60 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (60)(17.8e-3) | Answer: 6.71 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 19 uF capacitor at 780 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 19, f = 780 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (780)(19e-6)) | Answer: 10.74 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 13 ohm, XL = 52 ohm and XC = 36 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 13, XL = 52, XC = 36 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(13^2 + (52 - 36)^2) | Answer: 20.62 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 2.8 mH and C = 2.8 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 2.8, C = 2.8 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(2.8e-3 * 2.8e-6)) | Answer: 1797 Hz

question: A capacitor of 80.7 uF is charged to 140 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 80.7, V = 140 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*80.7e-6*(140)^2 | Answer: 790.9 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 140 V with 1000 primary turns and 150 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 140, N1 = 1000, N2 = 150 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 140 * 150/1000 | Answer: 21 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 430 V and draws an armature current of 25 A. If the armature resistance is 0.38 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 430, Ia = 25, Ra = 0.38 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 430 - 25*0.38 | Answer: 420.5 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 60 A at 433 V (line) with a power factor of 0.74. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 60, VL = 433, pf = 0.74 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*433*60*0.74 / 1000 | Answer: 33.3 kW

question: A load has real power 85 kW and apparent power 120 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 85, S = 120 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 85 / 120 | Answer: 0.7083

question: A machine delivers 85 kW output while drawing 92 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 85, Pi = 92 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 85/92 * 100 | Answer: 92.39 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 18 V across R1 = 25 ohm and R2 = 27 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 18, R1 = 25, R2 = 27 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 18*27 / (25+27) | Answer: 9.346 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 110 kohm and Rin = 16 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 110, Rin = 16 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 110 / 16 | Answer: 6.875

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 70 kohm and Rg = 43 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 70, Rg = 43 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 70/43 | Answer: 2.628

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 1380. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 1380 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(1380) | Answer: 31.4 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 3.5 m carries a central point load of 65 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.5, W = 65 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 65*3.5 / 4 | Answer: 56.88 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 8.9 m carries a UDL of 10 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 8.9, w = 10 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 10*(8.9)^2 / 8 | Answer: 99.01 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 1.5 m carries a point load 20 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 1.5, W = 20 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 20*1.5 | Answer: 30 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 1.1 m carries a UDL of 34 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 1.1, w = 34 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 34*(1.1)^2 / 2 | Answer: 20.57 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.6 m carries a point load 55 kN at distance 1.6 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 6.6, a = 1.6, W = 55 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 55*(6.6 - 1.6) / 6.6 | Answer: 41.67 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 6.7 m) carries a central point load 45 kN. With E = 30 GPa and I = 290e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=45000 N, L=6700.0 mm, E=30000 MPa, I=290e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 32.41 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 8.3 m carries a UDL of 27 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 8.3, w = 27 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 27*(8.3)^2 / 12 | Answer: 155 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 640 mm, clear cover 25 mm and main bars of diameter 20 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 640, c = 25, dia = 20 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 640 - 25 - 20/2 | Answer: 605 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 27.6 m^2 carrying a factored load of 11.7 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 27.6, w = 11.7 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 11.7 * 27.6 | Answer: 322.9 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 4.2 m, unit weight 18 kN/m^3, phi = 35 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 4.8e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.7, area = 4.9e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 4.8, i = 0.7, A = 4.9 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (4.8e-4)*0.7*(4.9e-3) | Answer: 1646 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.7 m, bed slope 0.009 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.023. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 4.8 m under a head of 0.5 m. Taking Cd = 0.61 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 3.6 m wide carries a discharge of 25.3 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 250 m and design speed 70 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 250, V = 70 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (70)^2 / (127*250) | Answer: 0.1543
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: A tank of volume 480 m^3 treats a flow of 20 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 480, Q = 20 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 480 / 20 | Answer: 24 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 200 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.28 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 8 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 200, k = 0.28, t = 8 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 200*(1 - e^(-0.28*8)) | Answer: 178.7 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.69, rainfall intensity 85 mm/h over a catchment of 40 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.69, i = 85, A = 40 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.69*85*40 / 360 | Answer: 6.517 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.03 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 150 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.03, M = 150 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 150*(30+0.03)/30 | Answer: 150.2 m

question: Convert the decimal number 1094 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 1094 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 446 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 11111111 and 01011001.
solution: XOR: 10100110 | Count of 1s = 4 | Answer: 4
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 680 megabits is sent over a link of 71 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 680, B = 71 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 680 / 71 | Answer: 9.577 s

question: A link has bandwidth 7 Mbps and round-trip time 120 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 7, R = 120 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 7e6 * 120e-3 bits = 840 kb | Answer: 840 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.85, cache access time 1 ns and main-memory access time 140 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.85, tc = 1, tm = 140 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.85*1 + (1 - 0.85)*140 | Answer: 21.85 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 686016 elements?
solution: Given: n = 686016 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(686016)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.019, memory access time 170 ns and page-fault service time 4 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 4 ms = 4000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.019)*170 + 0.019*4000000.0 ns | Answer: 76.17 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 2.1 m^3 at 470 kPa and 540 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 2.1, P = 470, Tk = 540 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (470e3)*2.1 / (8.314*540) | Answer: 219.8 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.19 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 9 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.19, t = 9 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.19*9) | Answer: 0.8191

question: For a reaction with A = 3e10 /s and activation energy 90 kJ/mol at 350 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 3, Ea = 90, Tk = 350 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 3e10 * exp(-90e3 / (8.314*350)) | Answer: 0.001109 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.9 and bottoms xW = 0.04, with relative volatility alpha = 3. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.9, xw = 0.04, al = 3 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.9/0.1)(0.96/0.04)] / ln(3) | Answer: 4.893 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.7 and x = 0.26. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.7, x = 0.26 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.7/0.3) / (0.26/0.74) | Answer: 6.641

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.83 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 80 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.83, Psat = 80 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.83 * 80 | Answer: 66.4 kPa

question: A stream of 3.5 kg/s with specific heat 3 kJ/kg-K is heated through 20 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 3.5, cp = 3, dT = 20 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 3.5*3*20 | Answer: 210 kW

question: A reactor of volume 9.8 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 0.3 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 9.8, Q = 0.3 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 9.8 / 0.3 | Answer: 32.67 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 7e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 3 mm with a concentration difference of 110 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 7, L = 3, dC = 110 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (7e-9)*110 / (3e-3) | Answer: 256.7 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 8.5 min and steady-state gain 2.9. For a step input of magnitude 18, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 8.5, K = 2.9, M = 18 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 2.9 * 18 | Answer: 52.2 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 40 m^2 flies at 240 m/s (air density 0.4 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 1.1. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 40, V = 240, rho = 0.4, CL = 1.1 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.4*(240)^2*40*1.1 / 1000 | Answer: 506.9 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 25 m^2 flies at 230 m/s (density 0.7 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.03. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 25, V = 230, rho = 0.7, CD = 0.03 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.7*(230)^2*25*0.03 / 1000 | Answer: 13.89 kN

question: A specimen under stress 350 MPa shows an elastic strain of 2e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 350, eps = 2 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 350 / (2e-3) MPa = 175 GPa | Answer: 175 GPa

question: A block of mass 6 kg has a volume of 4.2e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 6, V = 4.2 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 6 / (4.2e-3) | Answer: 1429 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 1700 mm is heated through 105 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 17e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 1700, dT = 105, al = 17 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 1700*17e-6*105 | Answer: 3.034 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 65 ohm, R2 = 40 ohm and R3 = 75 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 65, R2 = 40, R3 = 75 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 40*75 / 65 | Answer: 46.15 ohm

question: A measurement reads 9.74 when the true value is 20. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.74, true = 20 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.74 - 20| / 20 * 100 | Answer: 51.3 %

question: Annual demand is 12500 units, ordering cost 280 per order and holding cost 12 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 12500, S = 280, H = 12 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*12500*280 / 12) | Answer: 763.8 units

question: An asset costs 270000 with salvage value 38000 after 19 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 270000, Sv = 38000, n = 19 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (270000 - 38000) / 19 | Answer: 12211 per year

question: A product sells for 340 per unit with variable cost 160 per unit and fixed costs 35000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 340, V = 160, F = 35000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 35000 / (340 - 160) | Answer: 194.4 units

question: Find the present worth of 85000 received 5 years from now at an interest rate of 8% per year.
solution: Given: F = 85000, n = 5, i = 8 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 85000 / (1 + 0.08)^5 | Answer: 5785 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.99, 0.91 and 0.97 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.99, r2 = 0.91, r3 = 0.97 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.99*0.91*0.97 | Answer: 0.8739

question: A process produces 15 defective items in a batch of 17500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 15, N = 17500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 15/17500 * 1e6 | Answer: 857.1 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -6x^3 + x^2 + 3x - 8 evaluated at x = -2.
For f(x) = 2x^3 + 8x^2 - 6x + 4, find f''(x) at x = -5.
Evaluate the definite integral of (x^2 + 3x - 7) dx from x = 1 to x = 5.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = 1x^3/3 + 3x^2/2 + -7x | Evaluate F(5) - F(1) | Answer: 49.33
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 4x^2 + 7x - 3 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[-1, 4], [5, -5]].
solution: Given: a = -1, b = 4, c = 5, d = -5 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (-1)(-5) - (4)(5) | Answer: -15

question: Find the determinant of [[-4, -3, 6], [0, 3, -5], [1, 3, -1]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: -51

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[0, -5], [-3, 8]].
solution: Trace tr = 8, Determinant = -15 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 9.568

question: Solve for x: -5x + 6y = 2 and -3x + 2y = 0.
solution: Determinant = -5*2 - 6*-3 = 8 | x = (e d - b f) / det = 0.5 | Answer: x = 0.5
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 69, 23, 45, 49, 81.
solution: Sum = 267 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 53.4 | Answer: 53.4

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 35, 44, 33, 43, 32.
solution: Mean = 37.4 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 5.683

question: Find the slope of the line through (4, -6) and (6, 4).
solution: Given: x1 = 4, y1 = -6, x2 = 6, y2 = 4 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (4 - -6) / (6 - 4) | Answer: 5

question: Find the distance between the points (5, 5) and (-4, -3).
solution: Given: x1 = 5, y1 = 5, x2 = -4, y2 = -3 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-9)^2 + (-8)^2) | Answer: 12.04 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (-4,3), (-1,6), (2,0).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 13.5 sq units

question: Find the 9th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 17 and common difference 1.
solution: Given: a = 17, d = 1, n = 9 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = 17 + (9 - 1)*1 | Answer: 25

question: Find the sum of the first 30 terms of an AP with first term 5 and common difference -3.
solution: Given: a = 5, d = -3, n = 30 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 30/2 [2*5 + (30-1)*-3] | Answer: -1155

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 34500 at 5.2% per annum for 10 years.
solution: Given: P = 34500, R = 5.2, Tt = 10 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 34500 * 5.2 * 10 / 100 | Answer: 17940 currency units

question: Find the amount when 1500 is invested at 8.6% per annum compounded annually for 5 years.
solution: Given: P = 1500, R = 8.6, Tt = 5 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 1500 * (1 + 8.6/100)^5 | Answer: 2266 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (2, 1, 4) and (4, -3, 5).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (2, 3, -2) and (-5, 4, 5).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 32.53

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (1, -6, 3) and (-5, 4, -1).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 136.7 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number 5 + 3i.
solution: Given: a = 5, b = 3 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((5)^2 + (3)^2) | Answer: 5.831

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number 12 + 6i.
solution: Given: a = 12, b = 6 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(6, 12) | Answer: 26.57 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = 5x^3 - x^2 - 5x - 3 at x = -1.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-155 with initial guess x0=3, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.6 and ordinates 19, 2, 5, 4, 4, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 413 and 47.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 413 and 47 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 52 and 23.
solution: Given: a = 52, b = 23 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 52*23 / 1 | Answer: 1196
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 34 mm carries an axial tensile load of 15 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 12 mm and length 1800 mm carries an axial load of 63 kN. Take E = 110 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 70 mm transmits a torque of 1850 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 70, Tt = 1850 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(1850*1000) / (pi*(70)^3) | Answer: 27.47 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 61 mm and length 2000 mm carries a torque of 1250 N-m. With G = 80 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (61)^4 / 32 = 1359312 mm^4 | theta = (1250*1000)(2000) / (80000 * 1359312) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 1.317 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 55 mm wide and 250 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 55, h = 250 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 55*(250)^2 / 6 | Answer: 572917 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (94 mm x 140 mm) carries a bending moment of 5 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (52 mm x 130 mm) has effective length 4000 mm and E = 200 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 780 MPa is designed for a working stress of 210 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 780, sw = 210 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 780 / 210 | Answer: 3.714

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 850 mm and wall thickness 13 mm carries an internal pressure of 1 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 850, t = 13, P = 1 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 1*850 / (2*13) | Answer: 32.69 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 880 K and 400 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 880, Tc = 400 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 400/880) * 100 | Answer: 54.55 %

question: A heat pump operates between 267 K and 326 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 267, Th = 326 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 326 / (326 - 267) | Answer: 5.525

question: 2.6 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 180 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.6, dT = 180 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 2.6 * 0.718 * 180 | Answer: 336 kJ

question: 2.6 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 195 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.6, dT = 195 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 2.6 * 1.005 * 195 | Answer: 509.5 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 2.8 m^3 at 470 K with mass 5.5 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 2.8, Tk = 470, m = 5.5 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 5.5*0.287*470 / 2.8 | Answer: 265 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 3.3 kg of air expands isothermally at 470 K from volume V1 to 5*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.3, Tk = 470, ratio = 5 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 3.3*0.287*470*ln(5) | Answer: 716.4 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 2.2 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.16 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 2.2, D = 0.16 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*2.2*0.16 / 0.001 | Answer: 352000

question: Water flows at 3.6 m/s through a pipe of diameter 60 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 15.5 m. Taking Cv = 0.96, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 15.5, cv = 0.96 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.96*sqrt(2*9.81*15.5) | Answer: 16.74 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 330 mm) water flows at 0.7 m/s. It contracts to diameter 50 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 330, d2 = 50, V1 = 0.7 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 0.7*(330/50)^2 | Answer: 30.49 m/s

question: Water flows at 1.6 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.21 m and length 450 m. With friction factor f = 0.039, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 37 teeth drives a gear of 85 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1000 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 37, z2 = 85, N1 = 1000 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1000*37 / 85 | Answer: 435.3 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 280 mm rotates at 1400 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 280, N = 1400 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.28)*1400 / 60 | Answer: 20.53 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 33.6 kW at 1200 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 33.6, N = 1200 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(33.6*1000) / (2*pi*1200) | Answer: 267.4 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 0.8 kg rotates at radius 0.52 m at 800 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 7700 N/m and mass 10.8 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 7700, m = 10.8 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(7700/10.8) | Answer: 4.25 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 3.1 m^2 and thickness 0.3 m has conductivity k = 35.5 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 125 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 3.1, L = 0.3, k = 35.5, dT = 125 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 35.5*3.1*125 / 0.3 | Answer: 45854 W

question: A surface of area 5.2 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 35 W/m^2-K to surroundings 45 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 5.2, h = 35, dT = 45 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 35*5.2*45 | Answer: 8190 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 60 m/min, feed = 0.36 mm/rev, depth of cut = 1.4 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 60, f = 0.36, d = 1.4 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*60*0.36*1.4 | Answer: 30240 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 210 mm is turned at 350 rpm with a feed of 0.32 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 210, N = 350, f = 0.32 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 210 / (0.32*350) | Answer: 1.875 min

question: A resistor of 196 ohm carries a current of 5.6 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 196, I = 5.6 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 5.6 * 196 | Answer: 1098 V

question: Three resistors 40 ohm, 67 ohm and 88 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 40, R2 = 67, R3 = 88 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 40 + 67 + 88 | Answer: 195 ohm

question: Two resistors 111 ohm and 6 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 111, R2 = 6 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 111*6 / (111+6) | Answer: 5.692 ohm

question: A device draws 2.5 A at 130 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 130, I = 2.5 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 130 * 2.5 | Answer: 325 W

question: A current of 4.3 A flows through a 126 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 4.3, R = 126 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (4.3)^2 * 126 | Answer: 233 W

question: Two capacitors 23.8 uF and 45.1 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 23.8, C2 = 45.1 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 23.8*45.1 / (23.8+45.1) | Answer: 15.58 uF

question: A resistor 25 kohm and capacitor 18.7 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 25, C = 18.7 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (25k)(18.7u) = 467.5 ms | Answer: 467.5 ms

question: An inductor 167.6 mH is in series with 30 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 167.6, R = 30 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (167.6e-3) / 30 | Answer: 5.587 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 87.5 mH inductor at 370 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 87.5, f = 370 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (370)(87.5e-3) | Answer: 203.4 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 40 uF capacitor at 210 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 40, f = 210 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (210)(40e-6)) | Answer: 18.95 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 18 ohm, XL = 21 ohm and XC = 49 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 18, XL = 21, XC = 49 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(18^2 + (21 - 49)^2) | Answer: 33.29 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 92.6 mH and C = 2.6 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 92.6, C = 2.6 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(92.6e-3 * 2.6e-6)) | Answer: 324.4 Hz

question: A capacitor of 48.7 uF is charged to 175 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 48.7, V = 175 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*48.7e-6*(175)^2 | Answer: 745.7 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 400 V with 330 primary turns and 270 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 400, N1 = 330, N2 = 270 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 400 * 270/330 | Answer: 327.3 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 390 V and draws an armature current of 16 A. If the armature resistance is 0.2 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 390, Ia = 16, Ra = 0.2 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 390 - 16*0.2 | Answer: 386.8 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 110 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.74. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 110, VL = 400, pf = 0.74 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*400*110*0.74 / 1000 | Answer: 56.4 kW

question: A load has real power 10 kW and apparent power 220 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 10, S = 220 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 10 / 220 | Answer: 0.04545

question: A machine delivers 100 kW output while drawing 117 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 100, Pi = 117 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 100/117 * 100 | Answer: 85.47 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 11 V across R1 = 1 ohm and R2 = 42 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 11, R1 = 1, R2 = 42 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 11*42 / (1+42) | Answer: 10.74 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 210 kohm and Rin = 39 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 210, Rin = 39 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 210 / 39 | Answer: 5.385

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 40 kohm and Rg = 16 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 40, Rg = 16 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 40/16 | Answer: 3.5

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 3732. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 3732 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(3732) | Answer: 35.72 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.7 m carries a central point load of 60 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.7, W = 60 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 60*4.7 / 4 | Answer: 70.5 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.3 m carries a UDL of 45 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6.3, w = 45 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 45*(6.3)^2 / 8 | Answer: 223.3 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 2.7 m carries a point load 5 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 2.7, W = 5 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 5*2.7 | Answer: 13.5 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 1.1 m carries a UDL of 28 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 1.1, w = 28 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 28*(1.1)^2 / 2 | Answer: 16.94 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 8.6 m carries a point load 85 kN at distance 3.6 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 8.6, a = 3.6, W = 85 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 85*(8.6 - 3.6) / 8.6 | Answer: 49.42 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 5.1 m) carries a central point load 35 kN. With E = 200 GPa and I = 460e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=35000 N, L=5100.0 mm, E=200000 MPa, I=460e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 1.051 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 5.8 m carries a UDL of 12 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.8, w = 12 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 12*(5.8)^2 / 12 | Answer: 33.64 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 610 mm, clear cover 30 mm and main bars of diameter 25 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 610, c = 30, dia = 25 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 610 - 30 - 25/2 | Answer: 567.5 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 23.8 m^2 carrying a factored load of 13.7 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 23.8, w = 13.7 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 13.7 * 23.8 | Answer: 326.1 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 6.2 m, unit weight 18 kN/m^3, phi = 38 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 5.4e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.5, area = 5.8e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 5.4, i = 0.5, A = 5.8 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (5.4e-4)*0.5*(5.8e-3) | Answer: 1566 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 0.8 m, bed slope 0.004 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.028. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 4.1 m under a head of 1.1 m. Taking Cd = 0.64 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 5.9 m wide carries a discharge of 8.6 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 540 m and design speed 55 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 540, V = 55 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (55)^2 / (127*540) | Answer: 0.04411
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: A tank of volume 600 m^3 treats a flow of 180 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 600, Q = 180 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 600 / 180 | Answer: 3.333 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 320 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.17 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 6 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 320, k = 0.17, t = 6 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 320*(1 - e^(-0.17*6)) | Answer: 204.6 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.61, rainfall intensity 55 mm/h over a catchment of 10.5 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.61, i = 55, A = 10.5 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.61*55*10.5 / 360 | Answer: 0.9785 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.04 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 500 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.04, M = 500 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 500*(20+0.04)/20 | Answer: 501 m

question: Convert the decimal number 3251 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 3251 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: CB3 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 01110100 and 01100111.
solution: XOR: 00010011 | Count of 1s = 3 | Answer: 3
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 160 megabits is sent over a link of 98 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 160, B = 98 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 160 / 98 | Answer: 1.633 s

question: A link has bandwidth 61 Mbps and round-trip time 50 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 61, R = 50 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 61e6 * 50e-3 bits = 3050 kb | Answer: 3050 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.86, cache access time 2 ns and main-memory access time 170 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.86, tc = 2, tm = 170 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.86*2 + (1 - 0.86)*170 | Answer: 25.52 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 235792 elements?
solution: Given: n = 235792 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(235792)) + 1 | Answer: 18

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.005, memory access time 200 ns and page-fault service time 7 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 7 ms = 7000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.005)*200 + 0.005*7000000.0 ns | Answer: 35.2 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 0.9 m^3 at 230 kPa and 390 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 0.9, P = 230, Tk = 390 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (230e3)*0.9 / (8.314*390) | Answer: 63.84 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.06 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 17 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.06, t = 17 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.06*17) | Answer: 0.6394

question: For a reaction with A = 4e10 /s and activation energy 75 kJ/mol at 480 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 4, Ea = 75, Tk = 480 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 4e10 * exp(-75e3 / (8.314*480)) | Answer: 275.5 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.98 and bottoms xW = 0.06, with relative volatility alpha = 1.7. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.98, xw = 0.06, al = 1.7 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.98/0.02)(0.94/0.06)] / ln(1.7) | Answer: 12.52 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.7 and x = 0.49. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.7, x = 0.49 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.7/0.3) / (0.49/0.51) | Answer: 2.429

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.42 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 105 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.42, Psat = 105 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.42 * 105 | Answer: 44.1 kPa

question: A stream of 8.9 kg/s with specific heat 3.3 kJ/kg-K is heated through 85 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 8.9, cp = 3.3, dT = 85 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 8.9*3.3*85 | Answer: 2496 kW

question: A reactor of volume 2.9 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 0.8 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 2.9, Q = 0.8 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 2.9 / 0.8 | Answer: 3.625 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 5.9e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 4 mm with a concentration difference of 10 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 5.9, L = 4, dC = 10 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (5.9e-9)*10 / (4e-3) | Answer: 14.75 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 4.1 min and steady-state gain 2.6. For a step input of magnitude 5, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 4.1, K = 2.6, M = 5 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 2.6 * 5 | Answer: 13 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 30 m^2 flies at 130 m/s (air density 0.7 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 1.3. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 30, V = 130, rho = 0.7, CL = 1.3 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.7*(130)^2*30*1.3 / 1000 | Answer: 230.7 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 40 m^2 flies at 200 m/s (density 0.7 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.05. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 40, V = 200, rho = 0.7, CD = 0.05 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.7*(200)^2*40*0.05 / 1000 | Answer: 28 kN

question: A specimen under stress 80 MPa shows an elastic strain of 2.2e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 80, eps = 2.2 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 80 / (2.2e-3) MPa = 36.36 GPa | Answer: 36.36 GPa

question: A block of mass 30 kg has a volume of 0.9e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 30, V = 0.9 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 30 / (0.9e-3) | Answer: 33333 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 2000 mm is heated through 130 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 17e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 2000, dT = 130, al = 17 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 2000*17e-6*130 | Answer: 4.42 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 65 ohm, R2 = 45 ohm and R3 = 145 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 65, R2 = 45, R3 = 145 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 45*145 / 65 | Answer: 100.4 ohm

question: Annual demand is 15500 units, ordering cost 140 per order and holding cost 3 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 15500, S = 140, H = 3 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*15500*140 / 3) | Answer: 1203 units

question: An asset costs 190000 with salvage value 40000 after 7 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 190000, Sv = 40000, n = 7 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (190000 - 40000) / 7 | Answer: 21429 per year

question: A product sells for 250 per unit with variable cost 60 per unit and fixed costs 165000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 250, V = 60, F = 165000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 165000 / (250 - 60) | Answer: 868.4 units

question: Find the present worth of 160000 received 5 years from now at an interest rate of 7% per year.
solution: Given: F = 160000, n = 5, i = 7 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 160000 / (1 + 0.07)^5 | Answer: 114078 currency units

question: A process produces 20 defective items in a batch of 15500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 20, N = 15500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 20/15500 * 1e6 | Answer: 129 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = x^3 - 2x^2 + 8x + 9 evaluated at x = 0.
For f(x) = x^3 - 6x^2 - 8x - 5, find f''(x) at x = 1.
Evaluate the definite integral of (4x^2 + 6) dx from x = 2 to x = 4.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = 4x^3/3 + 0x^2/2 + 6x | Evaluate F(4) - F(2) | Answer: 86.67

question: Find the larger real root of x^2 + 9x - 11 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[-4, 4], [-9, -1]].
solution: Given: a = -4, b = 4, c = -9, d = -1 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (-4)(-1) - (4)(-9) | Answer: 40

solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: -8

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[1, -7], [-4, -6]].
solution: Trace tr = -5, Determinant = -34 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 3.844

question: Solve for x: 6x + 3y = -3 and 5x + 5y = 5.
solution: Determinant = 6*5 - 3*5 = 15 | x = (e d - b f) / det = -2 | Answer: x = -2

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 44, 84, 14, 58, 79.
solution: Sum = 279 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 55.8 | Answer: 55.8

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 31, 33, 5, 22, 9.
solution: Mean = 20 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 12.65

question: Find the slope of the line through (-1, 2) and (-3, -1).
solution: Given: x1 = -1, y1 = 2, x2 = -3, y2 = -1 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (-1 - 2) / (-3 - -1) | Answer: 1.5

question: Find the distance between the points (5, 8) and (-1, 4).
solution: Given: x1 = 5, y1 = 8, x2 = -1, y2 = 4 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-6)^2 + (-4)^2) | Answer: 7.211 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (-6,7), (-4,5), (-3,7).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 3 sq units

question: Find the 23th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -9 and common difference 0.
solution: Given: a = -9, d = 0, n = 23 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -9 + (23 - 1)*0 | Answer: -9

question: Find the sum of the first 24 terms of an AP with first term 10 and common difference -2.
solution: Given: a = 10, d = -2, n = 24 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 24/2 [2*10 + (24-1)*-2] | Answer: -312

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 16000 at 9.2% per annum for 3 years.
solution: Given: P = 16000, R = 9.2, Tt = 3 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 16000 * 9.2 * 3 / 100 | Answer: 4416 currency units

question: Find the amount when 29500 is invested at 5.7% per annum compounded annually for 2 years.
solution: Given: P = 29500, R = 5.7, Tt = 2 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 29500 * (1 + 5.7/100)^2 | Answer: 32959 currency units

formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (-6, -3, 2) and (2, 3, 3).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 29.21

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (5, 0, -1) and (5, 6, -5).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 50.62 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number -10 + -3i.
solution: Given: a = -10, b = -3 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((-10)^2 + (-3)^2) | Answer: 10.44

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number 1 + 11i.
solution: Given: a = 1, b = 11 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(11, 1) | Answer: 84.81 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -2x^3 + 4x^2 + 3x - 6 at x = -5.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-21 with initial guess x0=10, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.6 and ordinates 7, 10, 1, 13, 9, estimate the integral.

solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 359 and 573 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 62 and 51.
solution: Given: a = 62, b = 51 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 62*51 / 1 | Answer: 3162
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 21 mm carries an axial tensile load of 8 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 17 mm and length 2900 mm carries an axial load of 72 kN. Take E = 200 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 64 mm transmits a torque of 2550 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 64, Tt = 2550 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(2550*1000) / (pi*(64)^3) | Answer: 49.54 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 56 mm and length 2000 mm carries a torque of 1600 N-m. With G = 45 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (56)^4 / 32 = 965499 mm^4 | theta = (1600*1000)(2000) / (45000 * 965499) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 4.22 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 39 mm wide and 260 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 39, h = 260 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 39*(260)^2 / 6 | Answer: 439400 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (43 mm x 240 mm) carries a bending moment of 23 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (66 mm x 160 mm) has effective length 2100 mm and E = 200 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 330 MPa is designed for a working stress of 100 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 330, sw = 100 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 330 / 100 | Answer: 3.3

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 900 mm and wall thickness 15 mm carries an internal pressure of 2.2 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 900, t = 15, P = 2.2 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 2.2*900 / (2*15) | Answer: 66 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 860 K and 420 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 860, Tc = 420 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 420/860) * 100 | Answer: 51.16 %

question: A heat pump operates between 277 K and 306 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 277, Th = 306 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 306 / (306 - 277) | Answer: 10.55

question: 3.6 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 90 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.6, dT = 90 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 3.6 * 0.718 * 90 | Answer: 232.6 kJ

question: 7.8 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 110 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 7.8, dT = 110 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 7.8 * 1.005 * 110 | Answer: 862.3 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 3.7 m^3 at 300 K with mass 3 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 3.7, Tk = 300, m = 3 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 3*0.287*300 / 3.7 | Answer: 69.81 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 4.9 kg of air expands isothermally at 360 K from volume V1 to 5*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.9, Tk = 360, ratio = 5 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 4.9*0.287*360*ln(5) | Answer: 814.8 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 1.4 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.23 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 1.4, D = 0.23 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*1.4*0.23 / 0.001 | Answer: 322000

question: Water flows at 3.7 m/s through a pipe of diameter 140 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 3.7 m. Taking Cv = 0.95, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 3.7, cv = 0.95 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.95*sqrt(2*9.81*3.7) | Answer: 8.094 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 190 mm) water flows at 1 m/s. It contracts to diameter 60 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 190, d2 = 60, V1 = 1 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 1*(190/60)^2 | Answer: 10.03 m/s

question: Water flows at 2 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.1 m and length 80 m. With friction factor f = 0.025, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 37 teeth drives a gear of 58 teeth. If the pinion runs at 900 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 37, z2 = 58, N1 = 900 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 900*37 / 58 | Answer: 574.1 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 410 mm rotates at 1150 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 410, N = 1150 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.41)*1150 / 60 | Answer: 24.69 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 38.2 kW at 1000 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 38.2, N = 1000 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(38.2*1000) / (2*pi*1000) | Answer: 364.8 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 3.3 kg rotates at radius 0.57 m at 1050 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 5700 N/m and mass 17.3 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 5700, m = 17.3 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(5700/17.3) | Answer: 2.889 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 9 m^2 and thickness 0.21 m has conductivity k = 2.1 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 150 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 9, L = 0.21, k = 2.1, dT = 150 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 2.1*9*150 / 0.21 | Answer: 13500 W

question: A surface of area 4.9 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 45 W/m^2-K to surroundings 20 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 4.9, h = 45, dT = 20 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 45*4.9*20 | Answer: 4410 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 60 m/min, feed = 0.32 mm/rev, depth of cut = 0.6 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 60, f = 0.32, d = 0.6 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*60*0.32*0.6 | Answer: 11520 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 110 mm is turned at 400 rpm with a feed of 0.21 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 110, N = 400, f = 0.21 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 110 / (0.21*400) | Answer: 1.31 min

question: A resistor of 101 ohm carries a current of 4.5 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 101, I = 4.5 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 4.5 * 101 | Answer: 454.5 V

question: Three resistors 17 ohm, 45 ohm and 74 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 17, R2 = 45, R3 = 74 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 17 + 45 + 74 | Answer: 136 ohm

question: Two resistors 33 ohm and 94 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 33, R2 = 94 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 33*94 / (33+94) | Answer: 24.43 ohm

question: A device draws 11.1 A at 50 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 50, I = 11.1 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 50 * 11.1 | Answer: 555 W

question: A current of 2.3 A flows through a 59 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 2.3, R = 59 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (2.3)^2 * 59 | Answer: 312.1 W

question: Two capacitors 43.6 uF and 13.9 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 43.6, C2 = 13.9 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 43.6*13.9 / (43.6+13.9) | Answer: 10.54 uF

question: A resistor 42 kohm and capacitor 14 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 42, C = 14 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (42k)(14u) = 588 ms | Answer: 588 ms

question: An inductor 153.2 mH is in series with 163 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 153.2, R = 163 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (153.2e-3) / 163 | Answer: 0.9399 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 185.3 mH inductor at 370 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 185.3, f = 370 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (370)(185.3e-3) | Answer: 430.8 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 11 uF capacitor at 980 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 11, f = 980 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (980)(11e-6)) | Answer: 14.76 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 70 ohm, XL = 37 ohm and XC = 77 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 70, XL = 37, XC = 77 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(70^2 + (37 - 77)^2) | Answer: 80.62 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 96.7 mH and C = 3.5 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 96.7, C = 3.5 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(96.7e-3 * 3.5e-6)) | Answer: 273.6 Hz

question: A capacitor of 15.1 uF is charged to 120 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 15.1, V = 120 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*15.1e-6*(120)^2 | Answer: 108.7 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 150 V with 760 primary turns and 490 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 150, N1 = 760, N2 = 490 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 150 * 490/760 | Answer: 96.71 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 150 V and draws an armature current of 30 A. If the armature resistance is 0.67 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 150, Ia = 30, Ra = 0.67 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 150 - 30*0.67 | Answer: 129.9 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 45 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.76. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 45, VL = 400, pf = 0.76 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*400*45*0.76 / 1000 | Answer: 23.69 kW

question: A load has real power 35 kW and apparent power 125 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 35, S = 125 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 35 / 125 | Answer: 0.28

question: A machine delivers 170 kW output while drawing 172 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 170, Pi = 172 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 170/172 * 100 | Answer: 98.84 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 19 V across R1 = 40 ohm and R2 = 41 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 19, R1 = 40, R2 = 41 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 19*41 / (40+41) | Answer: 9.617 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 220 kohm and Rin = 42 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 220, Rin = 42 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 220 / 42 | Answer: 5.238

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 190 kohm and Rg = 39 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 190, Rg = 39 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 190/39 | Answer: 5.872

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 614. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 614 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(614) | Answer: 27.88 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 3.8 m carries a central point load of 120 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.8, W = 120 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 120*3.8 / 4 | Answer: 114 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 7.9 m carries a UDL of 10 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7.9, w = 10 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 10*(7.9)^2 / 8 | Answer: 78.01 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 5 m carries a UDL of 28 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5, w = 28 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 28*(5)^2 / 2 | Answer: 350 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 8.8 m carries a point load 30 kN at distance 2.7 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 8.8, a = 2.7, W = 30 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 30*(8.8 - 2.7) / 8.8 | Answer: 20.8 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 3.9 m) carries a central point load 20 kN. With E = 25 GPa and I = 80e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=20000 N, L=3900.0 mm, E=25000 MPa, I=80e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 12.36 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 8 m carries a UDL of 21 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 8, w = 21 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 21*(8)^2 / 12 | Answer: 112 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 340 mm, clear cover 35 mm and main bars of diameter 25 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 340, c = 35, dia = 25 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 340 - 35 - 25/2 | Answer: 292.5 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 18 m^2 carrying a factored load of 18.9 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 18, w = 18.9 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 18.9 * 18 | Answer: 340.2 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 6 m, unit weight 18 kN/m^3, phi = 36 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 6.6e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.5, area = 1.2e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 6.6, i = 0.5, A = 1.2 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (6.6e-4)*0.5*(1.2e-3) | Answer: 396 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.8 m, bed slope 0.008 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.025. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 4.6 m under a head of 0.2 m. Taking Cd = 0.63 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 2.9 m wide carries a discharge of 8.7 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 430 m and design speed 40 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 430, V = 40 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (40)^2 / (127*430) | Answer: 0.0293
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: A tank of volume 800 m^3 treats a flow of 185 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 800, Q = 185 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 800 / 185 | Answer: 4.324 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 170 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.12 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 7 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 170, k = 0.12, t = 7 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 170*(1 - e^(-0.12*7)) | Answer: 96.61 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.62, rainfall intensity 65 mm/h over a catchment of 7.2 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.62, i = 65, A = 7.2 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.62*65*7.2 / 360 | Answer: 0.806 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.03 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 170 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.03, M = 170 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 170*(20+0.03)/20 | Answer: 170.3 m

question: Convert the decimal number 896 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 896 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 380 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 11000110 and 10100111.
solution: XOR: 01100001 | Count of 1s = 3 | Answer: 3
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 180 megabits is sent over a link of 73 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 180, B = 73 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 180 / 73 | Answer: 2.466 s

question: A link has bandwidth 62 Mbps and round-trip time 80 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 62, R = 80 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 62e6 * 80e-3 bits = 4960 kb | Answer: 4960 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.83, cache access time 8 ns and main-memory access time 170 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.83, tc = 8, tm = 170 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.83*8 + (1 - 0.83)*170 | Answer: 35.54 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 551614 elements?
solution: Given: n = 551614 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(551614)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.008, memory access time 130 ns and page-fault service time 7 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 7 ms = 7000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.008)*130 + 0.008*7000000.0 ns | Answer: 56.13 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 0.2 m^3 at 140 kPa and 480 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 0.2, P = 140, Tk = 480 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (140e3)*0.2 / (8.314*480) | Answer: 7.016 mol

question: For a reaction with A = 2e10 /s and activation energy 80 kJ/mol at 410 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 2, Ea = 80, Tk = 410 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 2e10 * exp(-80e3 / (8.314*410)) | Answer: 1.284 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.97 and bottoms xW = 0.07, with relative volatility alpha = 2.2. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.97, xw = 0.07, al = 2.2 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.97/0.03)(0.93/0.07)] / ln(2.2) | Answer: 7.689 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.79 and x = 0.26. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.79, x = 0.26 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.79/0.21) / (0.26/0.74) | Answer: 10.71

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.42 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 115 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.42, Psat = 115 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.42 * 115 | Answer: 48.3 kPa

question: A stream of 5.4 kg/s with specific heat 2.1 kJ/kg-K is heated through 15 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 5.4, cp = 2.1, dT = 15 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 5.4*2.1*15 | Answer: 170.1 kW

question: A reactor of volume 17.8 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 3.1 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 17.8, Q = 3.1 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 17.8 / 3.1 | Answer: 5.742 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 2.5e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 4 mm with a concentration difference of 170 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 2.5, L = 4, dC = 170 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (2.5e-9)*170 / (4e-3) | Answer: 106.2 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 7.1 min and steady-state gain 2.5. For a step input of magnitude 14, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 7.1, K = 2.5, M = 14 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 2.5 * 14 | Answer: 35 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 75 m^2 flies at 180 m/s (air density 0.7 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 1.3. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 75, V = 180, rho = 0.7, CL = 1.3 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.7*(180)^2*75*1.3 / 1000 | Answer: 1106 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 120 m^2 flies at 190 m/s (density 0.7 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.08. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 120, V = 190, rho = 0.7, CD = 0.08 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.7*(190)^2*120*0.08 / 1000 | Answer: 121.3 kN

question: A specimen under stress 140 MPa shows an elastic strain of 0.6e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 140, eps = 0.6 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 140 / (0.6e-3) MPa = 233.3 GPa | Answer: 233.3 GPa

question: A block of mass 9 kg has a volume of 0.7e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 9, V = 0.7 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 9 / (0.7e-3) | Answer: 12857 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 2500 mm is heated through 150 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 11e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 2500, dT = 150, al = 11 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 2500*11e-6*150 | Answer: 4.125 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 100 ohm, R2 = 55 ohm and R3 = 340 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 100, R2 = 55, R3 = 340 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 55*340 / 100 | Answer: 187 ohm

question: A measurement reads 10.06 when the true value is 50. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10.06, true = 50 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10.06 - 50| / 50 * 100 | Answer: 79.88 %

question: Annual demand is 46000 units, ordering cost 150 per order and holding cost 13 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 46000, S = 150, H = 13 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*46000*150 / 13) | Answer: 103 units

question: An asset costs 90000 with salvage value 38000 after 15 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 90000, Sv = 38000, n = 15 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (90000 - 38000) / 15 | Answer: 3467 per year

question: A product sells for 290 per unit with variable cost 30 per unit and fixed costs 155000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 290, V = 30, F = 155000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 155000 / (290 - 30) | Answer: 596.2 units

question: Find the present worth of 20000 received 6 years from now at an interest rate of 9% per year.
solution: Given: F = 20000, n = 6, i = 9 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 20000 / (1 + 0.09)^6 | Answer: 11925 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.9, 0.94 and 0.91 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.9, r2 = 0.94, r3 = 0.91 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.9*0.94*0.91 | Answer: 0.7699

question: A process produces 1 defective items in a batch of 6000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 1, N = 6000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 1/6000 * 1e6 | Answer: 166.7 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = 6x^3 - 7x^2 + 8x - 9 evaluated at x = -4.
For f(x) = 2x^3 - 5x^2 - x - 2, find f''(x) at x = 1.
Evaluate the definite integral of (-3x^2 - 4x + 8) dx from x = -3 to x = 4.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = -3x^3/3 + -4x^2/2 + 8x | Evaluate F(4) - F(-3) | Answer: -49
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 5x^2 - 9x - 3 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[5, 4], [-9, 4]].
solution: Given: a = 5, b = 4, c = -9, d = 4 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (5)(4) - (4)(-9) | Answer: 56

question: Find the determinant of [[2, 6, -4], [-2, -4, -5], [-2, 0, -4]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: 76

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[-7, 0], [2, -4]].
solution: Trace tr = -11, Determinant = 28 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: -4

question: Solve for x: 6x + -4y = 7 and -2x + 0y = -3.
solution: Determinant = 6*0 - -4*-2 = -8 | x = (e d - b f) / det = 1.5 | Answer: x = 1.5
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 74, 38, 49, 65, 55.

question: Find the slope of the line through (-9, -6) and (-3, -3).
solution: Given: x1 = -9, y1 = -6, x2 = -3, y2 = -3 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (-3 - -6) / (-3 - -9) | Answer: 0.5

question: Find the distance between the points (-6, 4) and (5, 8).
solution: Given: x1 = -6, y1 = 4, x2 = 5, y2 = 8 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((11)^2 + (4)^2) | Answer: 11.7 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (7,-4), (7,1), (8,-8).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 2.5 sq units

question: Find the 19th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -2 and common difference -5.
solution: Given: a = -2, d = -5, n = 19 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -2 + (19 - 1)*-5 | Answer: -92

question: Find the sum of the first 34 terms of an AP with first term 2 and common difference 7.
solution: Given: a = 2, d = 7, n = 34 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 34/2 [2*2 + (34-1)*7] | Answer: 3995

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 43000 at 12.5% per annum for 4 years.
solution: Given: P = 43000, R = 12.5, Tt = 4 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 43000 * 12.5 * 4 / 100 | Answer: 21500 currency units

question: Find the amount when 15000 is invested at 5.1% per annum compounded annually for 6 years.
solution: Given: P = 15000, R = 5.1, Tt = 6 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 15000 * (1 + 5.1/100)^6 | Answer: 20217 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (7, 0, -4) and (8, 5, 2).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (-6, 5, 5) and (2, -6, -6).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 36.77

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (4, -1, -2) and (2, 2, 2).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 82.76 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number -8 + 8i.
solution: Given: a = -8, b = 8 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((-8)^2 + (8)^2) | Answer: 11.31

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number 9 + 8i.
solution: Given: a = 9, b = 8 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(8, 9) | Answer: 41.63 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -x^3 + 5x^2 - 4x + 2 at x = -4.
