Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-13 with initial guess x0=3, find x1 (one iteration).
solution: Given: N = 13, x0 = 3 | Formula: x1 = x0 - (x0^2 - N)/(2 x0) | Substitute: x1 = 3 - ((3)^2 - 13)/(2*3) | Answer: 3.667

question: Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=2 and ordinates 9, 8, 3, 19, 20, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 209 and 502.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 209 and 502 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 78 and 10.
solution: Given: a = 78, b = 10 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 78*10 / 2 | Answer: 390
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 11 mm carries an axial tensile load of 22 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 19 mm and length 1600 mm carries an axial load of 24 kN. Take E = 210 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 80 mm transmits a torque of 2100 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 80, Tt = 2100 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(2100*1000) / (pi*(80)^3) | Answer: 20.89 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 59 mm and length 1300 mm carries a torque of 1250 N-m. With G = 80 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 124 mm wide and 300 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 124, h = 300 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 124*(300)^2 / 6 | Answer: 1860000 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (85 mm x 230 mm) carries a bending moment of 19 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (42 mm x 130 mm) has effective length 2900 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 760 MPa is designed for a working stress of 190 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 760, sw = 190 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 760 / 190 | Answer: 4

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1350 mm and wall thickness 7 mm carries an internal pressure of 1.7 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1350, t = 7, P = 1.7 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 1.7*1350 / (2*7) | Answer: 163.9 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 840 K and 450 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 840, Tc = 450 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 450/840) * 100 | Answer: 46.43 %

question: 5.7 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 120 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 5.7, dT = 120 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 5.7 * 0.718 * 120 | Answer: 491.1 kJ

question: 7.8 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 135 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 7.8, dT = 135 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 7.8 * 1.005 * 135 | Answer: 1058 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 1.1 m^3 at 510 K with mass 4.9 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 1.1, Tk = 510, m = 4.9 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 4.9*0.287*510 / 1.1 | Answer: 652 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 2.4 kg of air expands isothermally at 330 K from volume V1 to 2*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.4, Tk = 330, ratio = 2 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 2.4*0.287*330*ln(2) | Answer: 157.6 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 1.6 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.22 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 1.6, D = 0.22 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*1.6*0.22 / 0.001 | Answer: 352000

question: Water flows at 3.3 m/s through a pipe of diameter 200 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 1.8 m. Taking Cv = 0.99, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 1.8, cv = 0.99 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.99*sqrt(2*9.81*1.8) | Answer: 5.883 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 280 mm) water flows at 0.6 m/s. It contracts to diameter 110 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
Water flows at 3.8 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.42 m and length 430 m. With friction factor f = 0.039, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 33 teeth drives a gear of 49 teeth. If the pinion runs at 750 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 33, z2 = 49, N1 = 750 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 750*33 / 49 | Answer: 505.1 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 450 mm rotates at 1250 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 450, N = 1250 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.45)*1250 / 60 | Answer: 29.45 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 30 kW at 650 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 30, N = 650 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(30*1000) / (2*pi*650) | Answer: 440.7 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 2.5 kg rotates at radius 0.37 m at 950 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 2300 N/m and mass 17.1 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 2300, m = 17.1 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(2300/17.1) | Answer: 1.846 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 3.8 m^2 and thickness 0.32 m has conductivity k = 1.7 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 50 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 3.8, L = 0.32, k = 1.7, dT = 50 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 1.7*3.8*50 / 0.32 | Answer: 1009 W

question: A surface of area 5.3 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 140 W/m^2-K to surroundings 85 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 5.3, h = 140, dT = 85 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 140*5.3*85 | Answer: 63070 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 170 m/min, feed = 0.24 mm/rev, depth of cut = 0.6 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 170, f = 0.24, d = 0.6 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*170*0.24*0.6 | Answer: 24480 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 500 mm is turned at 450 rpm with a feed of 0.18 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 500, N = 450, f = 0.18 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 500 / (0.18*450) | Answer: 6.173 min

question: A resistor of 113 ohm carries a current of 6.4 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 113, I = 6.4 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 6.4 * 113 | Answer: 723.2 V

question: Three resistors 78 ohm, 17 ohm and 72 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 78, R2 = 17, R3 = 72 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 78 + 17 + 72 | Answer: 167 ohm

question: Two resistors 24 ohm and 19 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 24, R2 = 19 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 24*19 / (24+19) | Answer: 10.6 ohm

question: A device draws 8.9 A at 130 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 130, I = 8.9 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 130 * 8.9 | Answer: 1157 W

question: A current of 5.7 A flows through a 110 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 5.7, R = 110 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (5.7)^2 * 110 | Answer: 3574 W

question: Two capacitors 40.8 uF and 15.1 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 40.8, C2 = 15.1 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 40.8*15.1 / (40.8+15.1) | Answer: 11.02 uF

question: A resistor 34 kohm and capacitor 3.9 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 34, C = 3.9 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (34k)(3.9u) = 132.6 ms | Answer: 132.6 ms

question: An inductor 143.6 mH is in series with 159 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 143.6, R = 159 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (143.6e-3) / 159 | Answer: 0.9031 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 121.8 mH inductor at 350 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 121.8, f = 350 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (350)(121.8e-3) | Answer: 267.9 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 16.3 uF capacitor at 640 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 16.3, f = 640 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (640)(16.3e-6)) | Answer: 15.26 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 54 ohm, XL = 117 ohm and XC = 117 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 54, XL = 117, XC = 117 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(54^2 + (117 - 117)^2) | Answer: 54 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 96.3 mH and C = 2.4 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 96.3, C = 2.4 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(96.3e-3 * 2.4e-6)) | Answer: 331.1 Hz

question: A capacitor of 53.9 uF is charged to 155 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 53.9, V = 155 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*53.9e-6*(155)^2 | Answer: 647.5 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 320 V with 870 primary turns and 330 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 320, N1 = 870, N2 = 330 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 320 * 330/870 | Answer: 121.4 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 430 V and draws an armature current of 29 A. If the armature resistance is 0.11 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 430, Ia = 29, Ra = 0.11 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 430 - 29*0.11 | Answer: 426.8 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 115 A at 415 V (line) with a power factor of 0.88. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 115, VL = 415, pf = 0.88 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*415*115*0.88 / 1000 | Answer: 72.74 kW

question: A load has real power 50 kW and apparent power 180 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 50, S = 180 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 50 / 180 | Answer: 0.2778

question: A machine delivers 165 kW output while drawing 197 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 165, Pi = 197 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 165/197 * 100 | Answer: 83.76 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 10 V across R1 = 11 ohm and R2 = 4 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 10, R1 = 11, R2 = 4 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 10*4 / (11+4) | Answer: 2.667 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 40 kohm and Rin = 1 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 40, Rin = 1 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 40 / 1 | Answer: 40

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 190 kohm and Rg = 31 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 190, Rg = 31 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 190/31 | Answer: 7.129

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 2345. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 2345 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(2345) | Answer: 33.7 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 7.4 m carries a central point load of 15 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7.4, W = 15 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 15*7.4 / 4 | Answer: 27.75 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.5 m carries a UDL of 25 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6.5, w = 25 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 25*(6.5)^2 / 8 | Answer: 132 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 2.9 m carries a point load 40 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 2.9, W = 40 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 40*2.9 | Answer: 116 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 5.1 m carries a UDL of 10 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.1, w = 10 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 10*(5.1)^2 / 2 | Answer: 130 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 5.8 m carries a point load 45 kN at distance 3.5 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 5.8, a = 3.5, W = 45 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 45*(5.8 - 3.5) / 5.8 | Answer: 17.84 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 6.2 m) carries a central point load 45 kN. With E = 30 GPa and I = 430e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=45000 N, L=6200.0 mm, E=30000 MPa, I=430e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 17.32 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 5 m carries a UDL of 33 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5, w = 33 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 33*(5)^2 / 12 | Answer: 68.75 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 570 mm, clear cover 30 mm and main bars of diameter 25 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 570, c = 30, dia = 25 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 570 - 30 - 25/2 | Answer: 527.5 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 29.4 m^2 carrying a factored load of 17.6 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 29.4, w = 17.6 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 17.6 * 29.4 | Answer: 517.4 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 3 m, unit weight 18 kN/m^3, phi = 33 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 3.5e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1, area = 4.9e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 3.5, i = 1, A = 4.9 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (3.5e-4)*1*(4.9e-3) | Answer: 1715 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.3 m, bed slope 0.009 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.021. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 3.2 m under a head of 0.8 m. Taking Cd = 0.62 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 5.6 m wide carries a discharge of 18.4 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A tank of volume 620 m^3 treats a flow of 195 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 620, Q = 195 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 620 / 195 | Answer: 3.179 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 350 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.34 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 8 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 350, k = 0.34, t = 8 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 350*(1 - e^(-0.34*8)) | Answer: 326.9 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.58, rainfall intensity 90 mm/h over a catchment of 45.7 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.58, i = 90, A = 45.7 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.58*90*45.7 / 360 | Answer: 6.627 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.04 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 720 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.04, M = 720 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 720*(30+0.04)/30 | Answer: 721 m

question: Convert the decimal number 3197 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 3197 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: C7D (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 11000011 and 01111000.
solution: XOR: 10111011 | Count of 1s = 6 | Answer: 6
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 240 megabits is sent over a link of 38 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 240, B = 38 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 240 / 38 | Answer: 6.316 s

question: A link has bandwidth 67 Mbps and round-trip time 110 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 67, R = 110 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 67e6 * 110e-3 bits = 7370 kb | Answer: 7370 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.81, cache access time 3 ns and main-memory access time 110 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.81, tc = 3, tm = 110 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.81*3 + (1 - 0.81)*110 | Answer: 23.33 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 977335 elements?
solution: Given: n = 977335 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(977335)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.002, memory access time 150 ns and page-fault service time 8 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 8 ms = 8000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.002)*150 + 0.002*8000000.0 ns | Answer: 16.15 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 0.9 m^3 at 440 kPa and 320 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 0.9, P = 440, Tk = 320 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (440e3)*0.9 / (8.314*320) | Answer: 148.8 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.19 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 5 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.19, t = 5 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.19*5) | Answer: 0.6133

question: A first-order liquid reaction (k = 0.35 /min) is to reach 60% conversion in a plug-flow reactor. Find the required space time in minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.35, X = 60 | Formula: tau = -ln(1 - X) / k | Substitute: tau = -ln(1 - 0.6) / 0.35 | Answer: 2.618 min

question: For a reaction with A = 5e10 /s and activation energy 60 kJ/mol at 300 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 5, Ea = 60, Tk = 300 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 5e10 * exp(-60e3 / (8.314*300)) | Answer: 1.785 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.99 and bottoms xW = 0.03, with relative volatility alpha = 2.7. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.99, xw = 0.03, al = 2.7 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.99/0.01)(0.97/0.03)] / ln(2.7) | Answer: 8.126 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.89 and x = 0.29. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.89, x = 0.29 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.89/0.11) / (0.29/0.71) | Answer: 19.81

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.55 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 100 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.55, Psat = 100 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.55 * 100 | Answer: 55 kPa

question: A stream of 2.4 kg/s with specific heat 2.8 kJ/kg-K is heated through 30 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 2.4, cp = 2.8, dT = 30 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 2.4*2.8*30 | Answer: 201.6 kW

question: A reactor of volume 5.8 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 4.5 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 5.8, Q = 4.5 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 5.8 / 4.5 | Answer: 1.289 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 3.8e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 4 mm with a concentration difference of 110 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 3.8, L = 4, dC = 110 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (3.8e-9)*110 / (4e-3) | Answer: 104.5 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 1 min and steady-state gain 3.9. For a step input of magnitude 13, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 1, K = 3.9, M = 13 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 3.9 * 13 | Answer: 50.7 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 15 m^2 flies at 240 m/s (air density 1 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.4. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 15, V = 240, rho = 1, CL = 0.4 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1*(240)^2*15*0.4 / 1000 | Answer: 172.8 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 95 m^2 flies at 130 m/s (density 0.7 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.08. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 95, V = 130, rho = 0.7, CD = 0.08 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.7*(130)^2*95*0.08 / 1000 | Answer: 44.95 kN

question: A specimen under stress 400 MPa shows an elastic strain of 1e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 400, eps = 1 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 400 / (1e-3) MPa = 400 GPa | Answer: 400 GPa

question: A block of mass 42 kg has a volume of 1.1e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 42, V = 1.1 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 42 / (1.1e-3) | Answer: 38182 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 2200 mm is heated through 145 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 17e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 2200, dT = 145, al = 17 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 2200*17e-6*145 | Answer: 5.423 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 45 ohm, R2 = 110 ohm and R3 = 445 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 45, R2 = 110, R3 = 445 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 110*445 / 45 | Answer: 1088 ohm

question: A measurement reads 10.56 when the true value is 50. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10.56, true = 50 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10.56 - 50| / 50 * 100 | Answer: 78.88 %

question: Annual demand is 3000 units, ordering cost 180 per order and holding cost 28 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 3000, S = 180, H = 28 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*3000*180 / 28) | Answer: 196.4 units

question: An asset costs 330000 with salvage value 14000 after 13 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 330000, Sv = 14000, n = 13 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (330000 - 14000) / 13 | Answer: 24308 per year

question: A product sells for 360 per unit with variable cost 160 per unit and fixed costs 45000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 360, V = 160, F = 45000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 45000 / (360 - 160) | Answer: 225 units

question: Find the present worth of 85000 received 3 years from now at an interest rate of 8% per year.
solution: Given: F = 85000, n = 3, i = 8 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 85000 / (1 + 0.08)^3 | Answer: 67476 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.91, 0.97 and 0.96 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.91, r2 = 0.97, r3 = 0.96 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.91*0.97*0.96 | Answer: 0.8474

question: A process produces 42 defective items in a batch of 2000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 42, N = 2000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 42/2000 * 1e6 | Answer: 21000 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -5x^3 - 6x^2 - 8x + 9 evaluated at x = 3.
For f(x) = 5x^3 - x^2 - x - 6, find f''(x) at x = -4.
Evaluate the definite integral of (2x^2 + 5x - 2) dx from x = -1 to x = 3.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = 2x^3/3 + 5x^2/2 + -2x | Evaluate F(3) - F(-1) | Answer: 30.67
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 2x^2 + x - 7 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[-1, 1], [5, 8]].
solution: Given: a = -1, b = 1, c = 5, d = 8 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (-1)(8) - (1)(5) | Answer: -13

question: Find the determinant of [[-1, 5, -1], [0, 4, 1], [6, 0, -5]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: 74

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[-2, -1], [-3, -4]].
solution: Trace tr = -6, Determinant = 5 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: -1

question: Solve for x: 2x + -6y = 4 and 2x + 4y = 12.
solution: Determinant = 2*4 - -6*2 = 20 | x = (e d - b f) / det = 4.4 | Answer: x = 4.4
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 75, 32, 100, 95, 13.
solution: Sum = 315 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 63 | Answer: 63

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 30, 6, 12, 46, 50.
solution: Mean = 28.8 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 19.68

question: Find the slope of the line through (-6, 1) and (-5, 9).
solution: Given: x1 = -6, y1 = 1, x2 = -5, y2 = 9 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (9 - 1) / (-5 - -6) | Answer: 8

question: Find the distance between the points (-5, 3) and (-9, 6).
solution: Given: x1 = -5, y1 = 3, x2 = -9, y2 = 6 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-4)^2 + (3)^2) | Answer: 5 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (1,1), (-4,0), (-2,-6).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 16 sq units

question: Find the 7th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 15 and common difference 5.
solution: Given: a = 15, d = 5, n = 7 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = 15 + (7 - 1)*5 | Answer: 45

question: Find the sum of the first 30 terms of an AP with first term 1 and common difference 6.
solution: Given: a = 1, d = 6, n = 30 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 30/2 [2*1 + (30-1)*6] | Answer: 2640

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 22500 at 6.1% per annum for 3 years.
solution: Given: P = 22500, R = 6.1, Tt = 3 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 22500 * 6.1 * 3 / 100 | Answer: 4118 currency units

question: Find the amount when 22500 is invested at 7.7% per annum compounded annually for 2 years.
solution: Given: P = 22500, R = 7.7, Tt = 2 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 22500 * (1 + 7.7/100)^2 | Answer: 26098 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (8, 1, -4) and (-1, -7, -3).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (-2, -2, 4) and (6, -6, 6).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 44.9

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (-3, 5, -3) and (3, 6, 1).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 66.13 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number -10 + 12i.
solution: Given: a = -10, b = 12 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((-10)^2 + (12)^2) | Answer: 15.62

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number -10 + 2i.
solution: Given: a = -10, b = 2 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(2, -10) | Answer: 168.7 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = 3x^3 - 2x^2 - 7 at x = 1.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-110 with initial guess x0=3, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.4 and ordinates 14, 0, 0, 16, 11, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 482 and 397.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 482 and 397 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 62 and 7.
solution: Given: a = 62, b = 7 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 62*7 / 1 | Answer: 434
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 44 mm carries an axial tensile load of 41 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 40 mm and length 2800 mm carries an axial load of 87 kN. Take E = 200 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 78 mm transmits a torque of 350 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 78, Tt = 350 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(350*1000) / (pi*(78)^3) | Answer: 3.756 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 60 mm and length 1400 mm carries a torque of 400 N-m. With G = 80 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (60)^4 / 32 = 1272345 mm^4 | theta = (400*1000)(1400) / (80000 * 1272345) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 0.3152 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 150 mm wide and 300 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 150, h = 300 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 150*(300)^2 / 6 | Answer: 2250000 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (74 mm x 210 mm) carries a bending moment of 32 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (42 mm x 90 mm) has effective length 1900 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 850 MPa is designed for a working stress of 230 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 850, sw = 230 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 850 / 230 | Answer: 3.696

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1250 mm and wall thickness 16 mm carries an internal pressure of 1 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1250, t = 16, P = 1 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 1*1250 / (2*16) | Answer: 39.06 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 980 K and 320 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 980, Tc = 320 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 320/980) * 100 | Answer: 67.35 %

question: 3.8 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 100 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.8, dT = 100 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 3.8 * 0.718 * 100 | Answer: 272.8 kJ

question: 7.3 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 195 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 7.3, dT = 195 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 7.3 * 1.005 * 195 | Answer: 1431 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 3.9 m^3 at 360 K with mass 2 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 3.9, Tk = 360, m = 2 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 2*0.287*360 / 3.9 | Answer: 52.98 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 1.9 kg of air expands isothermally at 340 K from volume V1 to 5*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1.9, Tk = 340, ratio = 5 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 1.9*0.287*340*ln(5) | Answer: 298.4 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 4.2 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.32 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 4.2, D = 0.32 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*4.2*0.32 / 0.001 | Answer: 1344000

question: Water flows at 2.1 m/s through a pipe of diameter 300 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 6.1 m. Taking Cv = 0.95, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 6.1, cv = 0.95 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.95*sqrt(2*9.81*6.1) | Answer: 10.39 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 220 mm) water flows at 2.5 m/s. It contracts to diameter 60 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 220, d2 = 60, V1 = 2.5 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 2.5*(220/60)^2 | Answer: 33.61 m/s

question: Water flows at 3.8 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.28 m and length 430 m. With friction factor f = 0.021, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 31 teeth drives a gear of 120 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1200 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 31, z2 = 120, N1 = 1200 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1200*31 / 120 | Answer: 310 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 290 mm rotates at 500 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 290, N = 500 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.29)*500 / 60 | Answer: 7.592 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 33 kW at 1500 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 33, N = 1500 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(33*1000) / (2*pi*1500) | Answer: 210.1 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 0.8 kg rotates at radius 0.57 m at 1150 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 5300 N/m and mass 19.6 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 5300, m = 19.6 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(5300/19.6) | Answer: 2.617 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 2 m^2 and thickness 0.1 m has conductivity k = 3.2 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 175 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 2, L = 0.1, k = 3.2, dT = 175 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 3.2*2*175 / 0.1 | Answer: 11200 W

question: A surface of area 3.1 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 25 W/m^2-K to surroundings 95 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 3.1, h = 25, dT = 95 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 25*3.1*95 | Answer: 7362 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 220 m/min, feed = 0.36 mm/rev, depth of cut = 0.9 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 220, f = 0.36, d = 0.9 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*220*0.36*0.9 | Answer: 71280 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 240 mm is turned at 850 rpm with a feed of 0.23 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 240, N = 850, f = 0.23 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 240 / (0.23*850) | Answer: 1.228 min

question: A resistor of 65 ohm carries a current of 2 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 65, I = 2 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 2 * 65 | Answer: 130 V

question: Three resistors 67 ohm, 30 ohm and 77 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 67, R2 = 30, R3 = 77 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 67 + 30 + 77 | Answer: 174 ohm

question: Two resistors 65 ohm and 86 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 65, R2 = 86 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 65*86 / (65+86) | Answer: 37.02 ohm

question: A device draws 12.5 A at 235 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 235, I = 12.5 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 235 * 12.5 | Answer: 2938 W

question: A current of 1.5 A flows through a 147 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 1.5, R = 147 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (1.5)^2 * 147 | Answer: 330.8 W

question: Two capacitors 28.2 uF and 13.9 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 28.2, C2 = 13.9 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 28.2*13.9 / (28.2+13.9) | Answer: 9.311 uF

question: A resistor 78 kohm and capacitor 19.8 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 78, C = 19.8 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (78k)(19.8u) = 1544 ms | Answer: 1544 ms

question: An inductor 336.2 mH is in series with 116 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 336.2, R = 116 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (336.2e-3) / 116 | Answer: 2.898 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 181.7 mH inductor at 270 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 181.7, f = 270 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (270)(181.7e-3) | Answer: 308.2 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 13.2 uF capacitor at 570 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 13.2, f = 570 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (570)(13.2e-6)) | Answer: 21.15 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 64 ohm, XL = 120 ohm and XC = 27 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 64, XL = 120, XC = 27 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(64^2 + (120 - 27)^2) | Answer: 112.9 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 64.4 mH and C = 1.5 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 64.4, C = 1.5 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(64.4e-3 * 1.5e-6)) | Answer: 512.1 Hz

question: A capacitor of 25.3 uF is charged to 190 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 25.3, V = 190 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*25.3e-6*(190)^2 | Answer: 456.7 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 160 V with 560 primary turns and 270 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 160, N1 = 560, N2 = 270 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 160 * 270/560 | Answer: 77.14 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 130 V and draws an armature current of 26 A. If the armature resistance is 0.22 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 130, Ia = 26, Ra = 0.22 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 130 - 26*0.22 | Answer: 124.3 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 85 A at 415 V (line) with a power factor of 0.94. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 85, VL = 415, pf = 0.94 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*415*85*0.94 / 1000 | Answer: 57.43 kW

question: A load has real power 30 kW and apparent power 30 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 30, S = 30 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 30 / 30 | Answer: 1

question: A machine delivers 115 kW output while drawing 207 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 115, Pi = 207 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 115/207 * 100 | Answer: 55.56 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 5 V across R1 = 31 ohm and R2 = 21 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 5, R1 = 31, R2 = 21 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 5*21 / (31+21) | Answer: 2.019 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 220 kohm and Rin = 12 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 220, Rin = 12 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 220 / 12 | Answer: 18.33

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 70 kohm and Rg = 11 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 70, Rg = 11 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 70/11 | Answer: 7.364

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 6022. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 6022 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(6022) | Answer: 37.8 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 8.8 m carries a central point load of 120 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 8.8, W = 120 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 120*8.8 / 4 | Answer: 264 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.6 m carries a UDL of 30 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.6, w = 30 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 30*(4.6)^2 / 8 | Answer: 79.35 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 2.2 m carries a point load 70 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 2.2, W = 70 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 70*2.2 | Answer: 154 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 5 m carries a UDL of 4 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5, w = 4 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 4*(5)^2 / 2 | Answer: 50 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 9 m carries a point load 40 kN at distance 2 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 9, a = 2, W = 40 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 40*(9 - 2) / 9 | Answer: 31.11 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 5.3 m) carries a central point load 50 kN. With E = 25 GPa and I = 520e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=50000 N, L=5300.0 mm, E=25000 MPa, I=520e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 11.93 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 4.9 m carries a UDL of 18 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.9, w = 18 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 18*(4.9)^2 / 12 | Answer: 36.02 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 610 mm, clear cover 30 mm and main bars of diameter 20 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 610, c = 30, dia = 20 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 610 - 30 - 20/2 | Answer: 570 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 39.3 m^2 carrying a factored load of 10.3 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 39.3, w = 10.3 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 10.3 * 39.3 | Answer: 404.8 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 6.7 m, unit weight 19 kN/m^3, phi = 37 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 1.9e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.8, area = 2.5e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 1.9, i = 0.8, A = 2.5 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (1.9e-4)*0.8*(2.5e-3) | Answer: 380 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1 m, bed slope 0.001 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.019. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 3.7 m under a head of 1 m. Taking Cd = 0.62 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 5.2 m wide carries a discharge of 17.7 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 310 m and design speed 75 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 310, V = 75 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (75)^2 / (127*310) | Answer: 0.1429
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: A tank of volume 360 m^3 treats a flow of 75 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 360, Q = 75 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 360 / 75 | Answer: 4.8 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 170 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.34 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 5 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 170, k = 0.34, t = 5 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 170*(1 - e^(-0.34*5)) | Answer: 138.9 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.52, rainfall intensity 100 mm/h over a catchment of 21.3 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.52, i = 100, A = 21.3 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.52*100*21.3 / 360 | Answer: 3.077 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.08 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 110 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.08, M = 110 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 110*(30+0.08)/30 | Answer: 110.3 m

question: Convert the decimal number 3531 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 3531 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: DCB (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 01110100 and 01011000.
solution: XOR: 00101100 | Count of 1s = 3 | Answer: 3
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 10 megabits is sent over a link of 97 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 10, B = 97 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 10 / 97 | Answer: 0.1031 s

question: A link has bandwidth 60 Mbps and round-trip time 180 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 60, R = 180 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 60e6 * 180e-3 bits = 10800 kb | Answer: 10800 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.84, cache access time 4 ns and main-memory access time 100 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.84, tc = 4, tm = 100 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.84*4 + (1 - 0.84)*100 | Answer: 19.36 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 237700 elements?
solution: Given: n = 237700 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(237700)) + 1 | Answer: 18

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.018, memory access time 200 ns and page-fault service time 10 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 10 ms = 10000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.018)*200 + 0.018*10000000.0 ns | Answer: 180.2 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 0.8 m^3 at 480 kPa and 330 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 0.8, P = 480, Tk = 330 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (480e3)*0.8 / (8.314*330) | Answer: 140 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.24 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 18 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.24, t = 18 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.24*18) | Answer: 0.9867

question: For a reaction with A = 7e10 /s and activation energy 90 kJ/mol at 350 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 7, Ea = 90, Tk = 350 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 7e10 * exp(-90e3 / (8.314*350)) | Answer: 0.002587 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.92 and bottoms xW = 0.08, with relative volatility alpha = 3. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.92, xw = 0.08, al = 3 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.92/0.08)(0.92/0.08)] / ln(3) | Answer: 4.446 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.7 and x = 0.35. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.7, x = 0.35 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.7/0.3) / (0.35/0.65) | Answer: 4.333

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.22 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 75 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.22, Psat = 75 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.22 * 75 | Answer: 16.5 kPa

question: A stream of 4.9 kg/s with specific heat 2.9 kJ/kg-K is heated through 110 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 4.9, cp = 2.9, dT = 110 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 4.9*2.9*110 | Answer: 1563 kW

question: A reactor of volume 18 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 4 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 18, Q = 4 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 18 / 4 | Answer: 4.5 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 3e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 4 mm with a concentration difference of 10 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 3, L = 4, dC = 10 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (3e-9)*10 / (4e-3) | Answer: 7.5 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 3.1 min and steady-state gain 3.1. For a step input of magnitude 4, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 3.1, K = 3.1, M = 4 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 3.1 * 4 | Answer: 12.4 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 45 m^2 flies at 160 m/s (air density 1 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.6. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 45, V = 160, rho = 1, CL = 0.6 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1*(160)^2*45*0.6 / 1000 | Answer: 345.6 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 35 m^2 flies at 220 m/s (density 0.7 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.05. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 35, V = 220, rho = 0.7, CD = 0.05 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.7*(220)^2*35*0.05 / 1000 | Answer: 29.64 kN

question: A specimen under stress 280 MPa shows an elastic strain of 3e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 280, eps = 3 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 280 / (3e-3) MPa = 93.33 GPa | Answer: 93.33 GPa

question: A block of mass 48 kg has a volume of 4.1e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 48, V = 4.1 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 48 / (4.1e-3) | Answer: 11707 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 1000 mm is heated through 75 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 11e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 1000, dT = 75, al = 11 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 1000*11e-6*75 | Answer: 0.825 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 45 ohm, R2 = 75 ohm and R3 = 170 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 45, R2 = 75, R3 = 170 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 75*170 / 45 | Answer: 283.3 ohm

question: A measurement reads 9.4 when the true value is 10. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.4, true = 10 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.4 - 10| / 10 * 100 | Answer: 6 %

question: Annual demand is 26000 units, ordering cost 230 per order and holding cost 33 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 26000, S = 230, H = 33 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*26000*230 / 33) | Answer: 602 units

question: An asset costs 330000 with salvage value 38000 after 16 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 330000, Sv = 38000, n = 16 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (330000 - 38000) / 16 | Answer: 18250 per year

question: A product sells for 200 per unit with variable cost 170 per unit and fixed costs 160000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 200, V = 170, F = 160000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 160000 / (200 - 170) | Answer: 5333 units

question: Find the present worth of 170000 received 2 years from now at an interest rate of 5% per year.
solution: Given: F = 170000, n = 2, i = 5 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 170000 / (1 + 0.05)^2 | Answer: 154195 currency units

question: A process produces 4 defective items in a batch of 7500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 4, N = 7500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 4/7500 * 1e6 | Answer: 533.3 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = 2x^3 - 2x - 9 evaluated at x = -1.
For f(x) = -3x^3 + 7x + 1, find f''(x) at x = -3.
Evaluate the definite integral of (-x^2 - 4x - 3) dx from x = -4 to x = 6.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = -1x^3/3 + -4x^2/2 + -3x | Evaluate F(6) - F(-4) | Answer: -163.3
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 5x^2 - 2x - 2 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[1, 8], [-6, 1]].
solution: Given: a = 1, b = 8, c = -6, d = 1 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (1)(1) - (8)(-6) | Answer: 49

question: Find the determinant of [[-5, 4, 6], [-5, 6, 3], [-1, -6, 6]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: 54

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[1, 2], [6, 4]].
solution: Trace tr = 5, Determinant = -8 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 6.275

question: Solve for x: 4x + -5y = -8 and 1x + 5y = 1.
solution: Determinant = 4*5 - -5*1 = 25 | x = (e d - b f) / det = -1.4 | Answer: x = -1.4
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 21, 7, 48, 19, 27.
solution: Sum = 122 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 24.4 | Answer: 24.4

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 7, 31, 41, 48, 6.
solution: Mean = 26.6 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 19.32

question: Find the slope of the line through (-1, 2) and (-6, -6).
solution: Given: x1 = -1, y1 = 2, x2 = -6, y2 = -6 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (-6 - 2) / (-6 - -1) | Answer: 1.6

question: Find the distance between the points (3, 1) and (-4, -3).
solution: Given: x1 = 3, y1 = 1, x2 = -4, y2 = -3 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-7)^2 + (-4)^2) | Answer: 8.062 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (3,-1), (-7,-1), (6,-7).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 30 sq units

question: Find the 5th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 20 and common difference 8.
solution: Given: a = 20, d = 8, n = 5 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = 20 + (5 - 1)*8 | Answer: 52

question: Find the sum of the first 37 terms of an AP with first term -1 and common difference 5.
solution: Given: a = -1, d = 5, n = 37 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 37/2 [2*-1 + (37-1)*5] | Answer: 3293

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 5500 at 8.7% per annum for 6 years.
solution: Given: P = 5500, R = 8.7, Tt = 6 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 5500 * 8.7 * 6 / 100 | Answer: 2871 currency units

question: Find the amount when 31000 is invested at 6.1% per annum compounded annually for 4 years.
solution: Given: P = 31000, R = 6.1, Tt = 4 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 31000 * (1 + 6.1/100)^4 | Answer: 39285 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (-7, -7, 1) and (-7, -7, 4).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (-1, 4, -4) and (5, 3, -4).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 33.48

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (-3, -4, 5) and (0, -6, 1).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 47.61 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number 6 + 3i.
solution: Given: a = 6, b = 3 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((6)^2 + (3)^2) | Answer: 6.708

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number -1 + 9i.
solution: Given: a = -1, b = 9 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(9, -1) | Answer: 96.34 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -2x^3 + 2x - 8 at x = 2.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-75 with initial guess x0=5, find x1 (one iteration).
solution: Given: N = 75, x0 = 5 | Formula: x1 = x0 - (x0^2 - N)/(2 x0) | Substitute: x1 = 5 - ((5)^2 - 75)/(2*5) | Answer: 10

question: Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.9 and ordinates 11, 6, 10, 4, 10, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 416 and 582.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 416 and 582 | Answer: GCD = 2

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 66 and 10.
solution: Given: a = 66, b = 10 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 66*10 / 2 | Answer: 330
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 37 mm carries an axial tensile load of 23 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 34 mm and length 900 mm carries an axial load of 26 kN. Take E = 200 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 52 mm transmits a torque of 1700 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 52, Tt = 1700 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(1700*1000) / (pi*(52)^3) | Answer: 61.58 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 52 mm and length 1600 mm carries a torque of 1700 N-m. With G = 45 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (52)^4 / 32 = 717816 mm^4 | theta = (1700*1000)(1600) / (45000 * 717816) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 4.825 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 49 mm wide and 220 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 49, h = 220 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 49*(220)^2 / 6 | Answer: 395267 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (58 mm x 80 mm) carries a bending moment of 6 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (72 mm x 90 mm) has effective length 2100 mm and E = 200 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 810 MPa is designed for a working stress of 240 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 810, sw = 240 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 810 / 240 | Answer: 3.375

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 700 mm and wall thickness 9 mm carries an internal pressure of 2.5 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 700, t = 9, P = 2.5 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 2.5*700 / (2*9) | Answer: 97.22 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 1200 K and 320 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 1200, Tc = 320 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 320/1200) * 100 | Answer: 73.33 %

question: 3.9 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 30 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.9, dT = 30 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 3.9 * 0.718 * 30 | Answer: 84.01 kJ

question: 1.4 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 150 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1.4, dT = 150 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 1.4 * 1.005 * 150 | Answer: 211 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 1.9 m^3 at 400 K with mass 1.3 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 1.9, Tk = 400, m = 1.3 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 1.3*0.287*400 / 1.9 | Answer: 78.55 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 1.6 kg of air expands isothermally at 340 K from volume V1 to 4*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1.6, Tk = 340, ratio = 4 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 1.6*0.287*340*ln(4) | Answer: 216.4 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 2.6 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.37 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 2.6, D = 0.37 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*2.6*0.37 / 0.001 | Answer: 962000

question: Water flows at 4 m/s through a pipe of diameter 70 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 15.4 m. Taking Cv = 0.99, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 15.4, cv = 0.99 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.99*sqrt(2*9.81*15.4) | Answer: 17.21 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 160 mm) water flows at 0.8 m/s. It contracts to diameter 120 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
Water flows at 2 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.44 m and length 220 m. With friction factor f = 0.033, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 19 teeth drives a gear of 89 teeth. If the pinion runs at 950 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 19, z2 = 89, N1 = 950 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 950*19 / 89 | Answer: 202.8 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 460 mm rotates at 500 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 460, N = 500 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.46)*500 / 60 | Answer: 12.04 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 26.1 kW at 550 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 26.1, N = 550 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(26.1*1000) / (2*pi*550) | Answer: 453.2 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 1 kg rotates at radius 0.4 m at 700 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 18200 N/m and mass 12.2 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 18200, m = 12.2 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(18200/12.2) | Answer: 6.147 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 5.9 m^2 and thickness 0.35 m has conductivity k = 8 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 40 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 5.9, L = 0.35, k = 8, dT = 40 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 8*5.9*40 / 0.35 | Answer: 5394 W

question: A surface of area 0.8 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 140 W/m^2-K to surroundings 100 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 0.8, h = 140, dT = 100 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 140*0.8*100 | Answer: 11200 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 240 m/min, feed = 0.47 mm/rev, depth of cut = 1.4 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 240, f = 0.47, d = 1.4 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*240*0.47*1.4 | Answer: 157920 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 430 mm is turned at 300 rpm with a feed of 0.27 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 430, N = 300, f = 0.27 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 430 / (0.27*300) | Answer: 5.309 min

question: A resistor of 91 ohm carries a current of 6.8 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 91, I = 6.8 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 6.8 * 91 | Answer: 618.8 V

question: Three resistors 56 ohm, 27 ohm and 69 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 56, R2 = 27, R3 = 69 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 56 + 27 + 69 | Answer: 152 ohm

question: Two resistors 58 ohm and 61 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 58, R2 = 61 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 58*61 / (58+61) | Answer: 29.73 ohm

question: A device draws 0.3 A at 25 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 25, I = 0.3 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 25 * 0.3 | Answer: 7.5 W

question: A current of 6.1 A flows through a 143 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 6.1, R = 143 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (6.1)^2 * 143 | Answer: 5321 W

question: Two capacitors 43.3 uF and 16.5 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 43.3, C2 = 16.5 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 43.3*16.5 / (43.3+16.5) | Answer: 11.95 uF

question: A resistor 18 kohm and capacitor 14.9 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 18, C = 14.9 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (18k)(14.9u) = 268.2 ms | Answer: 268.2 ms

question: An inductor 82.3 mH is in series with 160 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 82.3, R = 160 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (82.3e-3) / 160 | Answer: 0.5144 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 25.7 mH inductor at 190 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 25.7, f = 190 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (190)(25.7e-3) | Answer: 30.68 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 8 uF capacitor at 140 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 8, f = 140 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (140)(8e-6)) | Answer: 142.1 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 30 ohm, XL = 139 ohm and XC = 140 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 30, XL = 139, XC = 140 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(30^2 + (139 - 140)^2) | Answer: 30.02 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 51.1 mH and C = 4.3 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 51.1, C = 4.3 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(51.1e-3 * 4.3e-6)) | Answer: 339.5 Hz

question: A capacitor of 49.9 uF is charged to 265 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 49.9, V = 265 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*49.9e-6*(265)^2 | Answer: 1752 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 150 V with 980 primary turns and 450 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 150, N1 = 980, N2 = 450 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 150 * 450/980 | Answer: 68.88 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 170 V and draws an armature current of 29 A. If the armature resistance is 1.31 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 170, Ia = 29, Ra = 1.31 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 170 - 29*1.31 | Answer: 132 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 140 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.92. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 140, VL = 400, pf = 0.92 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*400*140*0.92 / 1000 | Answer: 89.24 kW

question: A load has real power 175 kW and apparent power 185 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 175, S = 185 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 175 / 185 | Answer: 0.9459

question: A machine delivers 30 kW output while drawing 202 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 30, Pi = 202 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 30/202 * 100 | Answer: 14.85 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 27 V across R1 = 42 ohm and R2 = 19 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 27, R1 = 42, R2 = 19 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 27*19 / (42+19) | Answer: 8.41 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 150 kohm and Rin = 18 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 150, Rin = 18 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 150 / 18 | Answer: 8.333

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 130 kohm and Rg = 22 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 130, Rg = 22 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 130/22 | Answer: 6.909

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 1239. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 1239 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(1239) | Answer: 30.93 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.1 m carries a central point load of 70 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 9.1, W = 70 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 70*9.1 / 4 | Answer: 159.2 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 8.8 m carries a UDL of 25 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 8.8, w = 25 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 25*(8.8)^2 / 8 | Answer: 242 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 3.4 m carries a point load 80 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.4, W = 80 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 80*3.4 | Answer: 272 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 2.9 m carries a UDL of 36 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 2.9, w = 36 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 36*(2.9)^2 / 2 | Answer: 151.4 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.9 m carries a point load 20 kN at distance 3.9 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 4.9, a = 3.9, W = 20 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 20*(4.9 - 3.9) / 4.9 | Answer: 4.082 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 4.4 m) carries a central point load 65 kN. With E = 30 GPa and I = 190e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=65000 N, L=4400.0 mm, E=30000 MPa, I=190e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 20.24 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 7.3 m carries a UDL of 36 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7.3, w = 36 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 36*(7.3)^2 / 12 | Answer: 159.9 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 600 mm, clear cover 35 mm and main bars of diameter 12 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 600, c = 35, dia = 12 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 600 - 35 - 12/2 | Answer: 559 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 35.5 m^2 carrying a factored load of 14.7 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 35.5, w = 14.7 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 14.7 * 35.5 | Answer: 521.9 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 3.2 m, unit weight 17 kN/m^3, phi = 31 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 8.2e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1.1, area = 2.5e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 8.2, i = 1.1, A = 2.5 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (8.2e-4)*1.1*(2.5e-3) | Answer: 2255 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 0.6 m, bed slope 0.008 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.017. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 2.3 m under a head of 0.6 m. Taking Cd = 0.61 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 3.6 m wide carries a discharge of 26.6 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 430 m and design speed 55 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 430, V = 55 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (55)^2 / (127*430) | Answer: 0.05539
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: A tank of volume 590 m^3 treats a flow of 160 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 590, Q = 160 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 590 / 160 | Answer: 3.688 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 290 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.33 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 3 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 290, k = 0.33, t = 3 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 290*(1 - e^(-0.33*3)) | Answer: 182.2 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.45, rainfall intensity 35 mm/h over a catchment of 17.8 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.45, i = 35, A = 17.8 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.45*35*17.8 / 360 | Answer: 0.7788 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.02 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 550 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.02, M = 550 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 550*(20+0.02)/20 | Answer: 550.5 m

question: Convert the decimal number 2151 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 2151 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 867 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 01000010 and 00011000.
solution: XOR: 01011010 | Count of 1s = 4 | Answer: 4
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 330 megabits is sent over a link of 54 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 330, B = 54 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 330 / 54 | Answer: 6.111 s

question: A link has bandwidth 48 Mbps and round-trip time 190 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 48, R = 190 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 48e6 * 190e-3 bits = 9120 kb | Answer: 9120 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.93, cache access time 5 ns and main-memory access time 140 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.93, tc = 5, tm = 140 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.93*5 + (1 - 0.93)*140 | Answer: 14.45 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 5489 elements?
solution: Given: n = 5489 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(5489)) + 1 | Answer: 13

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.002, memory access time 130 ns and page-fault service time 8 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 8 ms = 8000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.002)*130 + 0.002*8000000.0 ns | Answer: 16.13 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 0.8 m^3 at 410 kPa and 460 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 0.8, P = 410, Tk = 460 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (410e3)*0.8 / (8.314*460) | Answer: 85.76 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.16 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 7 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.16, t = 7 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.16*7) | Answer: 0.6737

question: For a reaction with A = 9e10 /s and activation energy 50 kJ/mol at 360 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 9, Ea = 50, Tk = 360 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 9e10 * exp(-50e3 / (8.314*360)) | Answer: 5002 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.98 and bottoms xW = 0.06, with relative volatility alpha = 2.5. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.98, xw = 0.06, al = 2.5 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.98/0.02)(0.94/0.06)] / ln(2.5) | Answer: 7.25 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.73 and x = 0.43. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.73, x = 0.43 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.73/0.27) / (0.43/0.57) | Answer: 3.584

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.12 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 80 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.12, Psat = 80 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.12 * 80 | Answer: 9.6 kPa

question: A stream of 4.4 kg/s with specific heat 4 kJ/kg-K is heated through 90 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 4.4, cp = 4, dT = 90 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 4.4*4*90 | Answer: 1584 kW

question: A reactor of volume 13.9 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 0.4 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 13.9, Q = 0.4 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 13.9 / 0.4 | Answer: 34.75 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 6.5e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 3 mm with a concentration difference of 60 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 6.5, L = 3, dC = 60 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (6.5e-9)*60 / (3e-3) | Answer: 130 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 5.7 min and steady-state gain 1.3. For a step input of magnitude 19, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 5.7, K = 1.3, M = 19 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 1.3 * 19 | Answer: 24.7 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 60 m^2 flies at 80 m/s (air density 0.4 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 1. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 60, V = 80, rho = 0.4, CL = 1 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.4*(80)^2*60*1 / 1000 | Answer: 76.8 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 85 m^2 flies at 70 m/s (density 1 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.1. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 85, V = 70, rho = 1, CD = 0.1 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*1*(70)^2*85*0.1 / 1000 | Answer: 20.82 kN

question: A specimen under stress 240 MPa shows an elastic strain of 2e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 240, eps = 2 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 240 / (2e-3) MPa = 120 GPa | Answer: 120 GPa

question: A block of mass 27 kg has a volume of 4.4e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 27, V = 4.4 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 27 / (4.4e-3) | Answer: 6136 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 700 mm is heated through 85 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 12e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 700, dT = 85, al = 12 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 700*12e-6*85 | Answer: 0.714 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 115 ohm, R2 = 165 ohm and R3 = 45 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 115, R2 = 165, R3 = 45 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 165*45 / 115 | Answer: 64.57 ohm

question: A measurement reads 9.95 when the true value is 20. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.95, true = 20 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.95 - 20| / 20 * 100 | Answer: 50.25 %

question: Annual demand is 31000 units, ordering cost 150 per order and holding cost 15 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
