solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 248 and 363 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 80 and 61.
solution: Given: a = 80, b = 61 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 80*61 / 1 | Answer: 4880
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 36 mm carries an axial tensile load of 87 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 39 mm and length 500 mm carries an axial load of 40 kN. Take E = 110 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 49 mm transmits a torque of 700 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 49, Tt = 700 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(700*1000) / (pi*(49)^3) | Answer: 30.3 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 52 mm and length 800 mm carries a torque of 1400 N-m. With G = 45 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (52)^4 / 32 = 717816 mm^4 | theta = (1400*1000)(800) / (45000 * 717816) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 1.987 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 120 mm wide and 140 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 120, h = 140 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 120*(140)^2 / 6 | Answer: 392000 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (50 mm x 260 mm) carries a bending moment of 34 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (69 mm x 90 mm) has effective length 1500 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 840 MPa is designed for a working stress of 130 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 840, sw = 130 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 840 / 130 | Answer: 6.462

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1200 mm and wall thickness 20 mm carries an internal pressure of 1.7 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1200, t = 20, P = 1.7 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 1.7*1200 / (2*20) | Answer: 51 MPa

question: A heat pump operates between 265 K and 312 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 265, Th = 312 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 312 / (312 - 265) | Answer: 6.638

question: 3 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 140 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3, dT = 140 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 3 * 0.718 * 140 | Answer: 301.6 kJ

question: 2.6 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 95 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.6, dT = 95 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 2.6 * 1.005 * 95 | Answer: 248.2 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 0.6 m^3 at 310 K with mass 5.6 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 0.6, Tk = 310, m = 5.6 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 5.6*0.287*310 / 0.6 | Answer: 830.4 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 1 kg of air expands isothermally at 410 K from volume V1 to 4*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1, Tk = 410, ratio = 4 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 1*0.287*410*ln(4) | Answer: 163.1 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 1 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.06 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 1, D = 0.06 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*1*0.06 / 0.001 | Answer: 60000

question: Water flows at 1.7 m/s through a pipe of diameter 80 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 3.6 m. Taking Cv = 0.97, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 3.6, cv = 0.97 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.97*sqrt(2*9.81*3.6) | Answer: 8.152 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 170 mm) water flows at 2.8 m/s. It contracts to diameter 130 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
Water flows at 3.9 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.45 m and length 380 m. With friction factor f = 0.033, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 26 teeth drives a gear of 84 teeth. If the pinion runs at 450 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 26, z2 = 84, N1 = 450 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 450*26 / 84 | Answer: 139.3 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 140 mm rotates at 1350 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 140, N = 1350 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.14)*1350 / 60 | Answer: 9.896 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 17.3 kW at 600 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 17.3, N = 600 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(17.3*1000) / (2*pi*600) | Answer: 275.3 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 4.7 kg rotates at radius 0.45 m at 850 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 2900 N/m and mass 14.2 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 2900, m = 14.2 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(2900/14.2) | Answer: 2.274 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 4.8 m^2 and thickness 0.22 m has conductivity k = 46.3 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 45 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 4.8, L = 0.22, k = 46.3, dT = 45 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 46.3*4.8*45 / 0.22 | Answer: 45458 W

question: A surface of area 4.6 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 55 W/m^2-K to surroundings 130 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 4.6, h = 55, dT = 130 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 55*4.6*130 | Answer: 32890 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 210 m/min, feed = 0.3 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2.1 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 210, f = 0.3, d = 2.1 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*210*0.3*2.1 | Answer: 132300 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 300 mm is turned at 200 rpm with a feed of 0.12 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 300, N = 200, f = 0.12 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 300 / (0.12*200) | Answer: 12.5 min

question: A resistor of 134 ohm carries a current of 4.9 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 134, I = 4.9 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 4.9 * 134 | Answer: 656.6 V

question: Three resistors 2 ohm, 95 ohm and 40 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 2, R2 = 95, R3 = 40 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 2 + 95 + 40 | Answer: 137 ohm

question: Two resistors 108 ohm and 32 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 108, R2 = 32 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 108*32 / (108+32) | Answer: 24.69 ohm

question: A device draws 8.8 A at 195 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 195, I = 8.8 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 195 * 8.8 | Answer: 1716 W

question: A current of 9.4 A flows through a 116 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 9.4, R = 116 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (9.4)^2 * 116 | Answer: 1025 W

question: Two capacitors 31.7 uF and 44.4 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 31.7, C2 = 44.4 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 31.7*44.4 / (31.7+44.4) | Answer: 18.5 uF

question: A resistor 77 kohm and capacitor 10.6 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 77, C = 10.6 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (77k)(10.6u) = 816.2 ms | Answer: 816.2 ms

question: An inductor 486.2 mH is in series with 10 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 486.2, R = 10 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (486.2e-3) / 10 | Answer: 48.62 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 198.1 mH inductor at 610 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 198.1, f = 610 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (610)(198.1e-3) | Answer: 759.3 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 29.8 uF capacitor at 580 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 29.8, f = 580 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (580)(29.8e-6)) | Answer: 9.208 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 19 ohm, XL = 36 ohm and XC = 92 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 19, XL = 36, XC = 92 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(19^2 + (36 - 92)^2) | Answer: 59.14 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 55.5 mH and C = 9.5 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 55.5, C = 9.5 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(55.5e-3 * 9.5e-6)) | Answer: 219.2 Hz

question: A capacitor of 2.6 uF is charged to 295 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 2.6, V = 295 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*2.6e-6*(295)^2 | Answer: 113.1 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 280 V with 800 primary turns and 360 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 280, N1 = 800, N2 = 360 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 280 * 360/800 | Answer: 126 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 340 V and draws an armature current of 57 A. If the armature resistance is 1.22 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 340, Ia = 57, Ra = 1.22 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 340 - 57*1.22 | Answer: 270.5 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 120 A at 415 V (line) with a power factor of 0.94. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 120, VL = 415, pf = 0.94 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*415*120*0.94 / 1000 | Answer: 81.08 kW

question: A load has real power 10 kW and apparent power 215 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 10, S = 215 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 10 / 215 | Answer: 0.04651

question: A machine delivers 50 kW output while drawing 197 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 50, Pi = 197 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 50/197 * 100 | Answer: 25.38 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 16 V across R1 = 6 ohm and R2 = 44 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 16, R1 = 6, R2 = 44 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 16*44 / (6+44) | Answer: 14.08 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 200 kohm and Rin = 47 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 200, Rin = 47 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 200 / 47 | Answer: 4.255

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 160 kohm and Rg = 13 kohm. Find the voltage gain.

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 660. Express the gain in decibels (power).

question: A simply supported beam of span 8.8 m carries a central point load of 20 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 8.8, W = 20 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 20*8.8 / 4 | Answer: 44 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 3.6 m carries a UDL of 50 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.6, w = 50 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 50*(3.6)^2 / 8 | Answer: 81 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 5.1 m carries a UDL of 8 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.1, w = 8 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 8*(5.1)^2 / 2 | Answer: 104 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 5.1 m carries a point load 55 kN at distance 4 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 5.1, a = 4, W = 55 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 55*(5.1 - 4) / 5.1 | Answer: 11.86 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 6.1 m) carries a central point load 30 kN. With E = 25 GPa and I = 460e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=30000 N, L=6100.0 mm, E=25000 MPa, I=460e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 12.34 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 5.8 m carries a UDL of 18 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.8, w = 18 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 18*(5.8)^2 / 12 | Answer: 50.46 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 550 mm, clear cover 30 mm and main bars of diameter 12 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 550, c = 30, dia = 12 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 550 - 30 - 12/2 | Answer: 514 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 11.6 m^2 carrying a factored load of 19 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 11.6, w = 19 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 19 * 11.6 | Answer: 220.4 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 3.4 m, unit weight 19 kN/m^3, phi = 37 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 7.9e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1.3, area = 5.7e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 7.9, i = 1.3, A = 5.7 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (7.9e-4)*1.3*(5.7e-3) | Answer: 5854 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.2 m, bed slope 0.009 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.028. Find the mean velocity in m/s.

question: A tank of volume 150 m^3 treats a flow of 95 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 150, Q = 95 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 150 / 95 | Answer: 1.579 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 160 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.24 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 7 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 160, k = 0.24, t = 7 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 160*(1 - e^(-0.24*7)) | Answer: 130.2 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.55, rainfall intensity 75 mm/h over a catchment of 26.6 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.55, i = 75, A = 26.6 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.55*75*26.6 / 360 | Answer: 3.048 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.01 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 530 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.01, M = 530 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 530*(20+0.01)/20 | Answer: 530.3 m

question: A file of 40 megabits is sent over a link of 96 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.

question: A link has bandwidth 88 Mbps and round-trip time 60 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 88, R = 60 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 88e6 * 60e-3 bits = 5280 kb | Answer: 5280 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.88, cache access time 6 ns and main-memory access time 170 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.88, tc = 6, tm = 170 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.88*6 + (1 - 0.88)*170 | Answer: 25.68 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 591837 elements?
solution: Given: n = 591837 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(591837)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.02, memory access time 140 ns and page-fault service time 6 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 6 ms = 6000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.02)*140 + 0.02*6000000.0 ns | Answer: 120.1 microseconds

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 0.1 m^3 at 410 kPa and 440 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 0.1, P = 410, Tk = 440 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (410e3)*0.1 / (8.314*440) | Answer: 11.21 mol

question: For a reaction with A = 9e10 /s and activation energy 55 kJ/mol at 360 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 9, Ea = 55, Tk = 360 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 9e10 * exp(-55e3 / (8.314*360)) | Answer: 941.2 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.94 and bottoms xW = 0.02, with relative volatility alpha = 1.5. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.94, xw = 0.02, al = 1.5 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.94/0.06)(0.98/0.02)] / ln(1.5) | Answer: 16.38 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.61 and x = 0.35. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.77 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 100 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.77, Psat = 100 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.77 * 100 | Answer: 77 kPa

question: A stream of 3.9 kg/s with specific heat 3 kJ/kg-K is heated through 90 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 3.9, cp = 3, dT = 90 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 3.9*3*90 | Answer: 1053 kW

question: A reactor of volume 6.8 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 4.4 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 6.8, Q = 4.4 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 6.8 / 4.4 | Answer: 1.545 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 6.9e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 3 mm with a concentration difference of 10 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 6.9, L = 3, dC = 10 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (6.9e-9)*10 / (3e-3) | Answer: 23 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 7.9 min and steady-state gain 1. For a step input of magnitude 18, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 7.9, K = 1, M = 18 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 1 * 18 | Answer: 18 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 70 m^2 flies at 220 m/s (air density 0.4 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.9. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 70, V = 220, rho = 0.4, CL = 0.9 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.4*(220)^2*70*0.9 / 1000 | Answer: 609.8 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 110 m^2 flies at 120 m/s (density 0.4 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.06. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 110, V = 120, rho = 0.4, CD = 0.06 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.4*(120)^2*110*0.06 / 1000 | Answer: 19.01 kN

question: A specimen under stress 120 MPa shows an elastic strain of 1.6e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 120, eps = 1.6 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 120 / (1.6e-3) MPa = 75 GPa | Answer: 75 GPa

question: A block of mass 5 kg has a volume of 5.2e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 5, V = 5.2 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 5 / (5.2e-3) | Answer: 961.5 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 1200 mm is heated through 110 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 11e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 110 ohm, R2 = 25 ohm and R3 = 500 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 110, R2 = 25, R3 = 500 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 25*500 / 110 | Answer: 113.6 ohm

question: A measurement reads 10.78 when the true value is 50. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10.78, true = 50 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10.78 - 50| / 50 * 100 | Answer: 78.44 %

question: Annual demand is 28500 units, ordering cost 270 per order and holding cost 25 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 28500, S = 270, H = 25 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*28500*270 / 25) | Answer: 784.6 units

question: An asset costs 420000 with salvage value 12000 after 16 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 420000, Sv = 12000, n = 16 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (420000 - 12000) / 16 | Answer: 25500 per year

question: A product sells for 490 per unit with variable cost 120 per unit and fixed costs 35000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 490, V = 120, F = 35000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 35000 / (490 - 120) | Answer: 94.59 units

question: Find the present worth of 145000 received 6 years from now at an interest rate of 6% per year.

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.91, 0.91 and 0.99 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.91, r2 = 0.91, r3 = 0.99 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.91*0.91*0.99 | Answer: 0.8198

question: A process produces 28 defective items in a batch of 17500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 28, N = 17500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 28/17500 * 1e6 | Answer: 1600 PPM

question: Find the distance between the points (7, -8) and (-8, -6).

question: Find the 17th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -4 and common difference -9.

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 26000 at 4.3% per annum for 10 years.

question: Find the amount when 15500 is invested at 10.8% per annum compounded annually for 6 years.

question: A circular rod of diameter 36 mm carries an axial tensile load of 77 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.

question: A shaft of diameter 47 mm and length 2000 mm carries a torque of 1050 N-m. With G = 77 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.

question: A rectangular beam section is 101 mm wide and 250 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 101, h = 250 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 101*(250)^2 / 6 | Answer: 1052083 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (52 mm x 210 mm) carries a bending moment of 9 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (50 mm x 140 mm) has effective length 2400 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 640 MPa is designed for a working stress of 150 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 640, sw = 150 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 640 / 150 | Answer: 4.267

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 750 mm and wall thickness 18 mm carries an internal pressure of 2.5 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 750, t = 18, P = 2.5 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 2.5*750 / (2*18) | Answer: 52.08 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 860 K and 340 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 860, Tc = 340 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 340/860) * 100 | Answer: 60.47 %

question: 3.9 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 190 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.9, dT = 190 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 3.9 * 0.718 * 190 | Answer: 532 kJ

question: 6.3 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 135 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 6.3, dT = 135 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 6.3 * 1.005 * 135 | Answer: 854.8 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 1.8 m^3 at 380 K with mass 3.2 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 1.8, Tk = 380, m = 3.2 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 3.2*0.287*380 / 1.8 | Answer: 193.9 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 4.6 kg of air expands isothermally at 370 K from volume V1 to 5*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.6, Tk = 370, ratio = 5 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 4.6*0.287*370*ln(5) | Answer: 786.2 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 0.7 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.35 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 0.7, D = 0.35 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*0.7*0.35 / 0.001 | Answer: 245000

question: Water flows at 0.5 m/s through a pipe of diameter 120 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 17.5 m. Taking Cv = 0.95, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 17.5, cv = 0.95 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.95*sqrt(2*9.81*17.5) | Answer: 17.6 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 350 mm) water flows at 2.3 m/s. It contracts to diameter 110 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
Water flows at 1.2 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.41 m and length 400 m. With friction factor f = 0.039, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 36 teeth drives a gear of 101 teeth. If the pinion runs at 950 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 36, z2 = 101, N1 = 950 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 950*36 / 101 | Answer: 338.6 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 290 mm rotates at 1000 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 290, N = 1000 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.29)*1000 / 60 | Answer: 15.18 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 11.5 kW at 1400 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 11.5, N = 1400 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(11.5*1000) / (2*pi*1400) | Answer: 78.44 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 7.3 kg rotates at radius 0.11 m at 350 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 6800 N/m and mass 4.7 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 6800, m = 4.7 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(6800/4.7) | Answer: 6.054 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 3.8 m^2 and thickness 0.33 m has conductivity k = 25.5 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 190 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 3.8, L = 0.33, k = 25.5, dT = 190 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 25.5*3.8*190 / 0.33 | Answer: 55791 W

question: A surface of area 4.4 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 120 W/m^2-K to surroundings 75 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 4.4, h = 120, dT = 75 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 120*4.4*75 | Answer: 39600 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 70 m/min, feed = 0.15 mm/rev, depth of cut = 1.1 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 70, f = 0.15, d = 1.1 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*70*0.15*1.1 | Answer: 11550 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 310 mm is turned at 1200 rpm with a feed of 0.13 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 310, N = 1200, f = 0.13 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 310 / (0.13*1200) | Answer: 1.987 min

question: A resistor of 56 ohm carries a current of 2.2 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 56, I = 2.2 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 2.2 * 56 | Answer: 123.2 V

question: Three resistors 54 ohm, 85 ohm and 26 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 54, R2 = 85, R3 = 26 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 54 + 85 + 26 | Answer: 165 ohm

question: Two resistors 114 ohm and 66 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 114, R2 = 66 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 114*66 / (114+66) | Answer: 41.8 ohm

question: A device draws 12.3 A at 150 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 150, I = 12.3 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 150 * 12.3 | Answer: 1845 W

question: A current of 8.3 A flows through a 98 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 8.3, R = 98 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (8.3)^2 * 98 | Answer: 6751 W

question: Two capacitors 29.4 uF and 16.5 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 29.4, C2 = 16.5 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 29.4*16.5 / (29.4+16.5) | Answer: 10.57 uF

question: A resistor 56 kohm and capacitor 9.3 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 56, C = 9.3 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (56k)(9.3u) = 520.8 ms | Answer: 520.8 ms

question: An inductor 243.4 mH is in series with 20 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 243.4, R = 20 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (243.4e-3) / 20 | Answer: 12.17 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 121.8 mH inductor at 490 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 121.8, f = 490 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (490)(121.8e-3) | Answer: 375 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 2.1 uF capacitor at 830 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 2.1, f = 830 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (830)(2.1e-6)) | Answer: 91.31 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 55 ohm, XL = 102 ohm and XC = 110 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 55, XL = 102, XC = 110 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(55^2 + (102 - 110)^2) | Answer: 55.58 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 63.7 mH and C = 9.4 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 63.7, C = 9.4 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(63.7e-3 * 9.4e-6)) | Answer: 205.7 Hz

question: A capacitor of 97.5 uF is charged to 350 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 97.5, V = 350 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*97.5e-6*(350)^2 | Answer: 5972 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 120 V with 890 primary turns and 310 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 120, N1 = 890, N2 = 310 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 120 * 310/890 | Answer: 41.8 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 160 V and draws an armature current of 42 A. If the armature resistance is 0.49 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 160, Ia = 42, Ra = 0.49 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 160 - 42*0.49 | Answer: 139.4 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 155 A at 433 V (line) with a power factor of 0.74. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 155, VL = 433, pf = 0.74 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*433*155*0.74 / 1000 | Answer: 86.02 kW

question: A load has real power 45 kW and apparent power 165 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 45, S = 165 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 45 / 165 | Answer: 0.2727

question: A machine delivers 20 kW output while drawing 57 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 20, Pi = 57 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 20/57 * 100 | Answer: 35.09 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 6 V across R1 = 4 ohm and R2 = 26 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 6, R1 = 4, R2 = 26 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 6*26 / (4+26) | Answer: 5.2 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 60 kohm and Rin = 47 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 60, Rin = 47 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 60 / 47 | Answer: 1.277

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 120 kohm and Rg = 47 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 120, Rg = 47 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 120/47 | Answer: 3.553

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 9119. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 9119 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(9119) | Answer: 39.6 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 3.8 m carries a central point load of 15 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.8, W = 15 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 15*3.8 / 4 | Answer: 14.25 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 3.7 m carries a UDL of 45 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.7, w = 45 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 45*(3.7)^2 / 8 | Answer: 77.01 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 3.6 m carries a point load 35 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.6, W = 35 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 35*3.6 | Answer: 126 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 4.5 m carries a UDL of 18 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.5, w = 18 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 18*(4.5)^2 / 2 | Answer: 182.2 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 5.6 m carries a point load 70 kN at distance 2.9 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 5.6, a = 2.9, W = 70 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 70*(5.6 - 2.9) / 5.6 | Answer: 33.75 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 7.7 m) carries a central point load 65 kN. With E = 25 GPa and I = 190e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=65000 N, L=7700.0 mm, E=25000 MPa, I=190e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 130.2 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 5.5 m carries a UDL of 15 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.5, w = 15 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 15*(5.5)^2 / 12 | Answer: 37.81 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 410 mm, clear cover 50 mm and main bars of diameter 12 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 410, c = 50, dia = 12 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 410 - 50 - 12/2 | Answer: 354 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 30.2 m^2 carrying a factored load of 12.5 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 30.2, w = 12.5 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 12.5 * 30.2 | Answer: 377.5 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 4 m, unit weight 18 kN/m^3, phi = 38 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 8e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1.3, area = 7.5e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 8, i = 1.3, A = 7.5 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (8e-4)*1.3*(7.5e-3) | Answer: 7800 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 2.1 m, bed slope 0.01 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.029. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 1.8 m under a head of 1.1 m. Taking Cd = 0.63 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 4.5 m wide carries a discharge of 20.5 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 520 m and design speed 70 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 520, V = 70 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (70)^2 / (127*520) | Answer: 0.0742
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: A tank of volume 120 m^3 treats a flow of 20 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 120, Q = 20 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 120 / 20 | Answer: 6 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 340 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.11 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 8 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 340, k = 0.11, t = 8 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 340*(1 - e^(-0.11*8)) | Answer: 199 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.68, rainfall intensity 70 mm/h over a catchment of 14.1 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.68, i = 70, A = 14.1 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.68*70*14.1 / 360 | Answer: 1.864 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.05 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 460 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.05, M = 460 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 460*(30+0.05)/30 | Answer: 460.8 m

question: Convert the decimal number 2486 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 2486 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 9B6 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 01000110 and 01000100.
solution: XOR: 00000010 | Count of 1s = 1 | Answer: 1
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 870 megabits is sent over a link of 36 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 870, B = 36 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 870 / 36 | Answer: 24.17 s

question: A link has bandwidth 25 Mbps and round-trip time 50 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 25, R = 50 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 25e6 * 50e-3 bits = 1250 kb | Answer: 1250 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.91, cache access time 5 ns and main-memory access time 50 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.91, tc = 5, tm = 50 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.91*5 + (1 - 0.91)*50 | Answer: 9.05 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 885492 elements?
solution: Given: n = 885492 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(885492)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.008, memory access time 180 ns and page-fault service time 3 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 3 ms = 3000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.008)*180 + 0.008*3000000.0 ns | Answer: 24.18 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 1.9 m^3 at 230 kPa and 400 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 1.9, P = 230, Tk = 400 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (230e3)*1.9 / (8.314*400) | Answer: 131.4 mol

question: For a reaction with A = 2e10 /s and activation energy 85 kJ/mol at 360 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 2, Ea = 85, Tk = 360 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 2e10 * exp(-85e3 / (8.314*360)) | Answer: 0.009277 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.98 and bottoms xW = 0.09, with relative volatility alpha = 3.5. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.98, xw = 0.09, al = 3.5 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.98/0.02)(0.91/0.09)] / ln(3.5) | Answer: 4.953 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.74 and x = 0.21. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.74, x = 0.21 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.74/0.26) / (0.21/0.79) | Answer: 10.71

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.21 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 100 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.21, Psat = 100 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.21 * 100 | Answer: 21 kPa

question: A stream of 6.3 kg/s with specific heat 3.9 kJ/kg-K is heated through 75 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 6.3, cp = 3.9, dT = 75 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 6.3*3.9*75 | Answer: 1843 kW

question: A reactor of volume 15.4 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 3.6 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 15.4, Q = 3.6 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 15.4 / 3.6 | Answer: 4.278 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 8.4e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 5 mm with a concentration difference of 170 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 8.4, L = 5, dC = 170 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (8.4e-9)*170 / (5e-3) | Answer: 285.6 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 4 min and steady-state gain 3.9. For a step input of magnitude 10, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 4, K = 3.9, M = 10 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 3.9 * 10 | Answer: 39 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 35 m^2 flies at 240 m/s (air density 1 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.5. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 35, V = 240, rho = 1, CL = 0.5 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1*(240)^2*35*0.5 / 1000 | Answer: 504 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 60 m^2 flies at 80 m/s (density 0.4 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.11. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 60, V = 80, rho = 0.4, CD = 0.11 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.4*(80)^2*60*0.11 / 1000 | Answer: 8.448 kN

question: A block of mass 21 kg has a volume of 2.6e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 21, V = 2.6 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 21 / (2.6e-3) | Answer: 8077 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 2200 mm is heated through 150 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 23e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 2200, dT = 150, al = 23 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 2200*23e-6*150 | Answer: 7.59 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 75 ohm, R2 = 10 ohm and R3 = 455 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 75, R2 = 10, R3 = 455 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 10*455 / 75 | Answer: 60.67 ohm

question: A measurement reads 10.54 when the true value is 100. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10.54, true = 100 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10.54 - 100| / 100 * 100 | Answer: 89.46 %

question: Annual demand is 2500 units, ordering cost 30 per order and holding cost 12 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 2500, S = 30, H = 12 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*2500*30 / 12) | Answer: 111.8 units

question: An asset costs 470000 with salvage value 14000 after 5 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 470000, Sv = 14000, n = 5 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (470000 - 14000) / 5 | Answer: 91200 per year

question: A product sells for 400 per unit with variable cost 70 per unit and fixed costs 60000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 400, V = 70, F = 60000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 60000 / (400 - 70) | Answer: 181.8 units

question: Find the present worth of 10000 received 10 years from now at an interest rate of 10% per year.
solution: Given: F = 10000, n = 10, i = 10 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 10000 / (1 + 0.1)^10 | Answer: 3855 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.99, 0.97 and 0.93 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.99, r2 = 0.97, r3 = 0.93 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.99*0.97*0.93 | Answer: 0.8931

question: A process produces 25 defective items in a batch of 18000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 25, N = 18000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 25/18000 * 1e6 | Answer: 1389 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -2x^3 + 6x^2 - x evaluated at x = 3.
For f(x) = x^3 + x^2 + 4x - 4, find f''(x) at x = 5.
Evaluate the definite integral of (3x^2 + 8) dx from x = 1 to x = 4.

question: Find the larger real root of 2x^2 + 8x + 3 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[-2, 4], [-8, -3]].
solution: Given: a = -2, b = 4, c = -8, d = -3 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (-2)(-3) - (4)(-8) | Answer: 38

question: Find the determinant of [[-2, 1, 6], [5, -1, -3], [2, -2, -4]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: -30

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[-7, 0], [-1, 1]].
solution: Trace tr = -6, Determinant = -7 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 1

question: Solve for x: -4x + 0y = 8 and -3x + -2y = -5.
solution: Determinant = -4*-2 - 0*-3 = 8 | x = (e d - b f) / det = -2 | Answer: x = -2
