solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 367 and 96 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 10 and 74.
solution: Given: a = 10, b = 74 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 10*74 / 2 | Answer: 370
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 47 mm carries an axial tensile load of 74 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 33 mm and length 2400 mm carries an axial load of 88 kN. Take E = 210 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 48 mm transmits a torque of 2650 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 48, Tt = 2650 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(2650*1000) / (pi*(48)^3) | Answer: 122 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 37 mm and length 700 mm carries a torque of 1950 N-m. With G = 77 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (37)^4 / 32 = 183995 mm^4 | theta = (1950*1000)(700) / (77000 * 183995) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 5.52 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 145 mm wide and 130 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 145, h = 130 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 145*(130)^2 / 6 | Answer: 408417 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (120 mm x 90 mm) carries a bending moment of 12 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (62 mm x 90 mm) has effective length 2300 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 840 MPa is designed for a working stress of 250 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 840, sw = 250 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 840 / 250 | Answer: 3.36

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1350 mm and wall thickness 12 mm carries an internal pressure of 2.5 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1350, t = 12, P = 2.5 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 2.5*1350 / (2*12) | Answer: 140.6 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 1140 K and 420 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 1140, Tc = 420 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 420/1140) * 100 | Answer: 63.16 %

question: A heat pump operates between 276 K and 300 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 276, Th = 300 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 300 / (300 - 276) | Answer: 12.5

question: 3.5 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 195 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.5, dT = 195 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 3.5 * 0.718 * 195 | Answer: 490 kJ

question: 6.5 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 100 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 6.5, dT = 100 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 6.5 * 1.005 * 100 | Answer: 653.2 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 1.5 m^3 at 510 K with mass 2.9 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 1.5, Tk = 510, m = 2.9 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 2.9*0.287*510 / 1.5 | Answer: 283 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 1.6 kg of air expands isothermally at 320 K from volume V1 to 5*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1.6, Tk = 320, ratio = 5 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 1.6*0.287*320*ln(5) | Answer: 236.5 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 3.8 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.25 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 3.8, D = 0.25 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*3.8*0.25 / 0.001 | Answer: 950000

question: Water flows at 2.1 m/s through a pipe of diameter 180 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 5.5 m. Taking Cv = 0.96, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 5.5, cv = 0.96 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.96*sqrt(2*9.81*5.5) | Answer: 9.972 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 360 mm) water flows at 1.1 m/s. It contracts to diameter 130 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
Water flows at 3.7 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.35 m and length 340 m. With friction factor f = 0.023, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 31 teeth drives a gear of 103 teeth. If the pinion runs at 900 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 31, z2 = 103, N1 = 900 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 900*31 / 103 | Answer: 270.9 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 240 mm rotates at 500 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 240, N = 500 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.24)*500 / 60 | Answer: 6.283 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 13.4 kW at 200 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 13.4, N = 200 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(13.4*1000) / (2*pi*200) | Answer: 639.8 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 6.2 kg rotates at radius 0.47 m at 900 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 3300 N/m and mass 19.1 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 3300, m = 19.1 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(3300/19.1) | Answer: 2.092 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 6 m^2 and thickness 0.4 m has conductivity k = 9.7 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 140 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 6, L = 0.4, k = 9.7, dT = 140 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 9.7*6*140 / 0.4 | Answer: 20370 W

question: A surface of area 5.8 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 70 W/m^2-K to surroundings 75 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 5.8, h = 70, dT = 75 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 70*5.8*75 | Answer: 30450 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 140 m/min, feed = 0.24 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2.8 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 140, f = 0.24, d = 2.8 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*140*0.24*2.8 | Answer: 94080 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 360 mm is turned at 750 rpm with a feed of 0.16 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 360, N = 750, f = 0.16 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 360 / (0.16*750) | Answer: 3 min

question: A resistor of 4 ohm carries a current of 1.9 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 4, I = 1.9 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 1.9 * 4 | Answer: 7.6 V

question: Three resistors 81 ohm, 39 ohm and 6 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 81, R2 = 39, R3 = 6 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 81 + 39 + 6 | Answer: 126 ohm

question: Two resistors 19 ohm and 6 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 19, R2 = 6 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 19*6 / (19+6) | Answer: 4.56 ohm

question: A device draws 7.3 A at 25 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 25, I = 7.3 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 25 * 7.3 | Answer: 182.5 W

question: A current of 4.5 A flows through a 126 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 4.5, R = 126 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (4.5)^2 * 126 | Answer: 2552 W

question: Two capacitors 32 uF and 48.5 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 32, C2 = 48.5 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 32*48.5 / (32+48.5) | Answer: 19.28 uF

question: A resistor 5 kohm and capacitor 8.9 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 5, C = 8.9 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (5k)(8.9u) = 44.5 ms | Answer: 44.5 ms

question: An inductor 418.7 mH is in series with 154 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 418.7, R = 154 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (418.7e-3) / 154 | Answer: 2.719 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 129.6 mH inductor at 480 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 129.6, f = 480 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (480)(129.6e-3) | Answer: 390.9 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 33.7 uF capacitor at 510 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 33.7, f = 510 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (510)(33.7e-6)) | Answer: 9.26 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 85 ohm, XL = 43 ohm and XC = 114 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 85, XL = 43, XC = 114 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(85^2 + (43 - 114)^2) | Answer: 110.8 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 40.9 mH and C = 3.5 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 40.9, C = 3.5 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(40.9e-3 * 3.5e-6)) | Answer: 420.7 Hz

question: A capacitor of 50.6 uF is charged to 295 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 50.6, V = 295 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*50.6e-6*(295)^2 | Answer: 2202 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 170 V with 360 primary turns and 260 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 170, N1 = 360, N2 = 260 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 170 * 260/360 | Answer: 122.8 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 360 V and draws an armature current of 9 A. If the armature resistance is 0.4 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 360, Ia = 9, Ra = 0.4 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 360 - 9*0.4 | Answer: 356.4 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 200 A at 415 V (line) with a power factor of 0.98. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 200, VL = 415, pf = 0.98 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*415*200*0.98 / 1000 | Answer: 140.9 kW

question: A load has real power 120 kW and apparent power 165 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 120, S = 165 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 120 / 165 | Answer: 0.7273

question: A machine delivers 40 kW output while drawing 217 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 40, Pi = 217 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 40/217 * 100 | Answer: 18.43 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 7 V across R1 = 13 ohm and R2 = 42 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 7, R1 = 13, R2 = 42 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 7*42 / (13+42) | Answer: 5.345 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 80 kohm and Rin = 15 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 80, Rin = 15 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 80 / 15 | Answer: 5.333

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 90 kohm and Rg = 43 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 90, Rg = 43 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 90/43 | Answer: 3.093

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 4165. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 4165 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(4165) | Answer: 36.2 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 5.2 m carries a central point load of 55 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.2, W = 55 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 55*5.2 / 4 | Answer: 71.5 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 7.4 m carries a UDL of 25 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7.4, w = 25 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 25*(7.4)^2 / 8 | Answer: 171.1 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 1.1 m carries a point load 35 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 1.1, W = 35 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 35*1.1 | Answer: 38.5 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 4.4 m carries a UDL of 14 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.4, w = 14 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 14*(4.4)^2 / 2 | Answer: 135.5 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 5.7 m carries a point load 65 kN at distance 3.1 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 5.7, a = 3.1, W = 65 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 65*(5.7 - 3.1) / 5.7 | Answer: 29.65 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 3 m) carries a central point load 50 kN. With E = 30 GPa and I = 160e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=50000 N, L=3000.0 mm, E=30000 MPa, I=160e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 5.859 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 4 m carries a UDL of 42 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4, w = 42 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 42*(4)^2 / 12 | Answer: 56 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 310 mm, clear cover 30 mm and main bars of diameter 16 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 310, c = 30, dia = 16 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 310 - 30 - 16/2 | Answer: 272 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 37.3 m^2 carrying a factored load of 15.6 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 37.3, w = 15.6 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 15.6 * 37.3 | Answer: 581.9 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 5.3 m, unit weight 20 kN/m^3, phi = 38 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 1.8e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1.4, area = 5.8e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 1.8, i = 1.4, A = 5.8 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (1.8e-4)*1.4*(5.8e-3) | Answer: 1462 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.9 m, bed slope 0.008 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.014. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 3.2 m under a head of 0.2 m. Taking Cd = 0.63 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 2.9 m wide carries a discharge of 24.8 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 390 m and design speed 90 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 390, V = 90 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (90)^2 / (127*390) | Answer: 0.1635
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: A tank of volume 170 m^3 treats a flow of 130 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 170, Q = 130 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 170 / 130 | Answer: 1.308 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 250 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.22 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 8 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 250, k = 0.22, t = 8 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 250*(1 - e^(-0.22*8)) | Answer: 207 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.44, rainfall intensity 95 mm/h over a catchment of 40.1 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.44, i = 95, A = 40.1 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.44*95*40.1 / 360 | Answer: 4.656 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.08 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 250 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.08, M = 250 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 250*(20+0.08)/20 | Answer: 251 m

question: Convert the decimal number 3866 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 3866 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: F1A (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 10001111 and 00011111.
solution: XOR: 10010000 | Count of 1s = 2 | Answer: 2
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 100 megabits is sent over a link of 29 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 100, B = 29 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 100 / 29 | Answer: 3.448 s

question: A link has bandwidth 32 Mbps and round-trip time 80 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 32, R = 80 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 32e6 * 80e-3 bits = 2560 kb | Answer: 2560 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.98, cache access time 3 ns and main-memory access time 200 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.98, tc = 3, tm = 200 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.98*3 + (1 - 0.98)*200 | Answer: 6.94 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 917303 elements?
solution: Given: n = 917303 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(917303)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.011, memory access time 200 ns and page-fault service time 9 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 9 ms = 9000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.011)*200 + 0.011*9000000.0 ns | Answer: 99.2 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 2.1 m^3 at 160 kPa and 400 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 2.1, P = 160, Tk = 400 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (160e3)*2.1 / (8.314*400) | Answer: 101 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.22 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 12 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.22, t = 12 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.22*12) | Answer: 0.9286

question: For a reaction with A = 3e10 /s and activation energy 55 kJ/mol at 410 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 3, Ea = 55, Tk = 410 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 3e10 * exp(-55e3 / (8.314*410)) | Answer: 295 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.93 and bottoms xW = 0.02, with relative volatility alpha = 2.4. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.93, xw = 0.02, al = 2.4 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.93/0.07)(0.98/0.02)] / ln(2.4) | Answer: 7.4 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.68 and x = 0.46. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.68, x = 0.46 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.68/0.32) / (0.46/0.54) | Answer: 2.495

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.75 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 85 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.75, Psat = 85 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.75 * 85 | Answer: 63.75 kPa

question: A stream of 8.8 kg/s with specific heat 4 kJ/kg-K is heated through 45 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 8.8, cp = 4, dT = 45 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 8.8*4*45 | Answer: 1584 kW

question: A reactor of volume 13.7 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 2.4 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 13.7, Q = 2.4 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 13.7 / 2.4 | Answer: 5.708 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 2.1e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 4 mm with a concentration difference of 20 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 2.1, L = 4, dC = 20 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (2.1e-9)*20 / (4e-3) | Answer: 10.5 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 3.6 min and steady-state gain 0.7. For a step input of magnitude 19, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 3.6, K = 0.7, M = 19 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 0.7 * 19 | Answer: 13.3 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 35 m^2 flies at 160 m/s (air density 1.225 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 1. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 35, V = 160, rho = 1.225, CL = 1 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1.225*(160)^2*35*1 / 1000 | Answer: 548.8 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 20 m^2 flies at 100 m/s (density 1 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.12. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 20, V = 100, rho = 1, CD = 0.12 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*1*(100)^2*20*0.12 / 1000 | Answer: 12 kN

question: A specimen under stress 300 MPa shows an elastic strain of 1.9e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 300, eps = 1.9 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 300 / (1.9e-3) MPa = 157.9 GPa | Answer: 157.9 GPa

question: A block of mass 49 kg has a volume of 4.5e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 49, V = 4.5 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 49 / (4.5e-3) | Answer: 10889 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 2500 mm is heated through 55 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 12e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 2500, dT = 55, al = 12 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 2500*12e-6*55 | Answer: 1.65 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 60 ohm, R2 = 120 ohm and R3 = 90 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 60, R2 = 120, R3 = 90 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 120*90 / 60 | Answer: 180 ohm

question: A measurement reads 10.5 when the true value is 100. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10.5, true = 100 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10.5 - 100| / 100 * 100 | Answer: 89.5 %

question: Annual demand is 13000 units, ordering cost 170 per order and holding cost 8 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 13000, S = 170, H = 8 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*13000*170 / 8) | Answer: 743.3 units

question: An asset costs 260000 with salvage value 34000 after 12 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 260000, Sv = 34000, n = 12 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (260000 - 34000) / 12 | Answer: 18833 per year

question: A product sells for 380 per unit with variable cost 140 per unit and fixed costs 165000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 380, V = 140, F = 165000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 165000 / (380 - 140) | Answer: 687.5 units

question: Find the present worth of 60000 received 7 years from now at an interest rate of 9% per year.
solution: Given: F = 60000, n = 7, i = 9 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 60000 / (1 + 0.09)^7 | Answer: 32822 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.93, 0.98 and 0.98 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.93, r2 = 0.98, r3 = 0.98 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.93*0.98*0.98 | Answer: 0.8932

question: A process produces 33 defective items in a batch of 11500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 33, N = 11500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 33/11500 * 1e6 | Answer: 287 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -6x^3 - 6x^2 - 3x + 4 evaluated at x = -5.
For f(x) = -5x^3 - x^2 - 3x + 8, find f''(x) at x = 4.
Evaluate the definite integral of (-x^2 + 6x - 5) dx from x = -4 to x = 5.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = -1x^3/3 + 6x^2/2 + -5x | Evaluate F(5) - F(-4) | Answer: -81
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of x^2 - 4x - 10 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[8, 4], [8, -1]].
solution: Given: a = 8, b = 4, c = 8, d = -1 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (8)(-1) - (4)(8) | Answer: -40

question: Find the determinant of [[-3, 3, 0], [3, -4, 1], [1, -3, 6]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: 12

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[-7, -1], [-4, -8]].
solution: Trace tr = -15, Determinant = 52 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: -5.438

question: Solve for x: -3x + 5y = 0 and 2x + -3y = 3.
solution: Determinant = -3*-3 - 5*2 = -1 | x = (e d - b f) / det = 15 | Answer: x = 15
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 36, 15, 76, 47, 81.
solution: Sum = 255 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 51 | Answer: 51

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 20, 25, 50, 22, 9.
solution: Mean = 25.2 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 15.12

question: Find the slope of the line through (-2, -8) and (7, -6).
Find the distance between the points (-9, -6) and (-7, 5).
solution: Given: x1 = -9, y1 = -6, x2 = -7, y2 = 5 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((2)^2 + (11)^2) | Answer: 11.18 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (-4,7), (7,5), (-3,-6).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 70.5 sq units

question: Find the 14th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 20 and common difference -5.
solution: Given: a = 20, d = -5, n = 14 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = 20 + (14 - 1)*-5 | Answer: -45

question: Find the sum of the first 8 terms of an AP with first term -3 and common difference 4.
solution: Given: a = -3, d = 4, n = 8 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 8/2 [2*-3 + (8-1)*4] | Answer: 88

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 8500 at 8.7% per annum for 8 years.
solution: Given: P = 8500, R = 8.7, Tt = 8 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 8500 * 8.7 * 8 / 100 | Answer: 5916 currency units

question: Find the amount when 28500 is invested at 11.3% per annum compounded annually for 5 years.
solution: Given: P = 28500, R = 11.3, Tt = 5 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 28500 * (1 + 11.3/100)^5 | Answer: 48677 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (7, -1, -7) and (-7, 8, -5).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (-1, -6, 6) and (-5, 3, -2).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 46.36

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (5, 1, 2) and (1, 1, 6).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 57.78 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number 8 + -12i.
solution: Given: a = 8, b = -12 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((8)^2 + (-12)^2) | Answer: 14.42

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number -3 + -3i.
solution: Given: a = -3, b = -3 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(-3, -3) | Answer: -135 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -2x^3 + 3x^2 - 8x + 3 at x = 5.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-67 with initial guess x0=7, find x1 (one iteration).
solution: Given: N = 67, x0 = 7 | Formula: x1 = x0 - (x0^2 - N)/(2 x0) | Substitute: x1 = 7 - ((7)^2 - 67)/(2*7) | Answer: 8.286

question: Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.1 and ordinates 17, 16, 0, 17, 10, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 166 and 565.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 166 and 565 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 31 and 39.
solution: Given: a = 31, b = 39 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 31*39 / 1 | Answer: 1209
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 58 mm carries an axial tensile load of 80 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 18 mm and length 2100 mm carries an axial load of 54 kN. Take E = 70 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 74 mm transmits a torque of 300 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 74, Tt = 300 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(300*1000) / (pi*(74)^3) | Answer: 3.77 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 51 mm and length 600 mm carries a torque of 250 N-m. With G = 77 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (51)^4 / 32 = 664172 mm^4 | theta = (250*1000)(600) / (77000 * 664172) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 0.1681 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 126 mm wide and 110 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 126, h = 110 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 126*(110)^2 / 6 | Answer: 254100 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (63 mm x 260 mm) carries a bending moment of 11 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (30 mm x 140 mm) has effective length 3700 mm and E = 200 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 790 MPa is designed for a working stress of 250 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 790, sw = 250 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 790 / 250 | Answer: 3.16

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1350 mm and wall thickness 7 mm carries an internal pressure of 1.5 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1350, t = 7, P = 1.5 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 1.5*1350 / (2*7) | Answer: 144.6 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 760 K and 330 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 760, Tc = 330 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 330/760) * 100 | Answer: 56.58 %

question: 1.7 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 40 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1.7, dT = 40 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 1.7 * 0.718 * 40 | Answer: 48.82 kJ

question: 7.7 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 125 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 7.7, dT = 125 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 7.7 * 1.005 * 125 | Answer: 967.3 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 0.7 m^3 at 540 K with mass 2 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 0.7, Tk = 540, m = 2 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 2*0.287*540 / 0.7 | Answer: 442.8 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 2.7 kg of air expands isothermally at 420 K from volume V1 to 5*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.7, Tk = 420, ratio = 5 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 2.7*0.287*420*ln(5) | Answer: 523.8 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 2.7 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.15 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 2.7, D = 0.15 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*2.7*0.15 / 0.001 | Answer: 405000

question: Water flows at 0.9 m/s through a pipe of diameter 130 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 12.3 m. Taking Cv = 0.97, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 12.3, cv = 0.97 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.97*sqrt(2*9.81*12.3) | Answer: 15.07 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 270 mm) water flows at 2.5 m/s. It contracts to diameter 90 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 270, d2 = 90, V1 = 2.5 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 2.5*(270/90)^2 | Answer: 22.5 m/s

question: Water flows at 1.4 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.23 m and length 260 m. With friction factor f = 0.037, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 30 teeth drives a gear of 114 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1150 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 30, z2 = 114, N1 = 1150 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1150*30 / 114 | Answer: 302.6 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 390 mm rotates at 1400 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 390, N = 1400 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.39)*1400 / 60 | Answer: 28.59 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 3 kW at 850 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 3, N = 850 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(3*1000) / (2*pi*850) | Answer: 33.7 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 3.8 kg rotates at radius 0.39 m at 950 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 19200 N/m and mass 15.8 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 19200, m = 15.8 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(19200/15.8) | Answer: 5.548 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 2 m^2 and thickness 0.16 m has conductivity k = 15.4 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 70 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 2, L = 0.16, k = 15.4, dT = 70 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 15.4*2*70 / 0.16 | Answer: 13475 W

question: A surface of area 6 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 25 W/m^2-K to surroundings 45 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 6, h = 25, dT = 45 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 25*6*45 | Answer: 6750 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 60 m/min, feed = 0.2 mm/rev, depth of cut = 0.6 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 60, f = 0.2, d = 0.6 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*60*0.2*0.6 | Answer: 7200 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 160 mm is turned at 1200 rpm with a feed of 0.25 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 160, N = 1200, f = 0.25 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 160 / (0.25*1200) | Answer: 0.5333 min

question: A resistor of 180 ohm carries a current of 5.3 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 180, I = 5.3 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 5.3 * 180 | Answer: 954 V

question: Three resistors 50 ohm, 38 ohm and 51 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 50, R2 = 38, R3 = 51 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 50 + 38 + 51 | Answer: 139 ohm

question: Two resistors 111 ohm and 34 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 111, R2 = 34 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 111*34 / (111+34) | Answer: 26.03 ohm

question: A device draws 5.4 A at 160 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 160, I = 5.4 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 160 * 5.4 | Answer: 864 W

question: A current of 1.4 A flows through a 45 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 1.4, R = 45 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (1.4)^2 * 45 | Answer: 88.2 W

question: Two capacitors 29.8 uF and 46.4 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 29.8, C2 = 46.4 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 29.8*46.4 / (29.8+46.4) | Answer: 18.15 uF

question: A resistor 100 kohm and capacitor 6.7 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 100, C = 6.7 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (100k)(6.7u) = 670 ms | Answer: 670 ms

question: An inductor 184 mH is in series with 138 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 184, R = 138 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (184e-3) / 138 | Answer: 1.333 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 165.3 mH inductor at 610 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 165.3, f = 610 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (610)(165.3e-3) | Answer: 633.6 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 5.7 uF capacitor at 490 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 5.7, f = 490 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (490)(5.7e-6)) | Answer: 56.98 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 34 ohm, XL = 29 ohm and XC = 60 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 34, XL = 29, XC = 60 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(34^2 + (29 - 60)^2) | Answer: 46.01 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 53.2 mH and C = 1.1 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 53.2, C = 1.1 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(53.2e-3 * 1.1e-6)) | Answer: 657.9 Hz

question: A capacitor of 71.5 uF is charged to 50 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 71.5, V = 50 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*71.5e-6*(50)^2 | Answer: 89.38 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 210 V with 710 primary turns and 190 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 210, N1 = 710, N2 = 190 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 210 * 190/710 | Answer: 56.2 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 110 V and draws an armature current of 27 A. If the armature resistance is 0.19 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 110, Ia = 27, Ra = 0.19 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 110 - 27*0.19 | Answer: 104.9 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 190 A at 415 V (line) with a power factor of 0.94. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 190, VL = 415, pf = 0.94 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*415*190*0.94 / 1000 | Answer: 128.4 kW

question: A load has real power 40 kW and apparent power 60 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 40, S = 60 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 40 / 60 | Answer: 0.6667

question: A machine delivers 10 kW output while drawing 177 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 10, Pi = 177 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 10/177 * 100 | Answer: 5.65 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 21 V across R1 = 9 ohm and R2 = 21 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 21, R1 = 9, R2 = 21 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 21*21 / (9+21) | Answer: 14.7 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 40 kohm and Rin = 22 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 40, Rin = 22 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 40 / 22 | Answer: 1.818

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 60 kohm and Rg = 33 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 60, Rg = 33 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 60/33 | Answer: 2.818

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 7131. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 7131 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(7131) | Answer: 38.53 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 3.3 m carries a central point load of 40 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.3, W = 40 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 40*3.3 / 4 | Answer: 33 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.4 m carries a UDL of 10 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.4, w = 10 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 10*(4.4)^2 / 8 | Answer: 24.2 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 2.8 m carries a point load 25 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 2.8, W = 25 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 25*2.8 | Answer: 70 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 4.8 m carries a UDL of 32 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.8, w = 32 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 32*(4.8)^2 / 2 | Answer: 368.6 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 5.8 m carries a point load 55 kN at distance 2.8 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 5.8, a = 2.8, W = 55 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 55*(5.8 - 2.8) / 5.8 | Answer: 28.45 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 8 m) carries a central point load 10 kN. With E = 30 GPa and I = 160e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=10000 N, L=8000.0 mm, E=30000 MPa, I=160e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 22.22 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 4.4 m carries a UDL of 30 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.4, w = 30 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 30*(4.4)^2 / 12 | Answer: 48.4 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 470 mm, clear cover 25 mm and main bars of diameter 20 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 470, c = 25, dia = 20 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 470 - 25 - 20/2 | Answer: 435 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 10.2 m^2 carrying a factored load of 8.5 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 10.2, w = 8.5 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 8.5 * 10.2 | Answer: 86.7 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 4.8 m, unit weight 20 kN/m^3, phi = 29 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 2.1e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1.3, area = 5.1e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 2.1, i = 1.3, A = 5.1 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (2.1e-4)*1.3*(5.1e-3) | Answer: 1392 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.1 m, bed slope 0.004 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.017. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 1.6 m under a head of 0.2 m. Taking Cd = 0.64 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 3.1 m wide carries a discharge of 19.1 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 230 m and design speed 90 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 230, V = 90 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (90)^2 / (127*230) | Answer: 0.2773
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: A tank of volume 340 m^3 treats a flow of 100 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 340, Q = 100 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 340 / 100 | Answer: 3.4 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 280 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.31 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 5 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 280, k = 0.31, t = 5 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 280*(1 - e^(-0.31*5)) | Answer: 220.6 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.64, rainfall intensity 100 mm/h over a catchment of 55.5 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.64, i = 100, A = 55.5 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.64*100*55.5 / 360 | Answer: 9.867 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.01 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 170 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.01, M = 170 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 170*(20+0.01)/20 | Answer: 170.1 m

question: Convert the decimal number 3892 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 3892 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: F34 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 10111011 and 10101000.
solution: XOR: 00010011 | Count of 1s = 3 | Answer: 3
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 470 megabits is sent over a link of 79 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.

question: A link has bandwidth 82 Mbps and round-trip time 20 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 82, R = 20 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 82e6 * 20e-3 bits = 1640 kb | Answer: 1640 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.96, cache access time 5 ns and main-memory access time 60 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.96, tc = 5, tm = 60 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.96*5 + (1 - 0.96)*60 | Answer: 7.2 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 464508 elements?

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.013, memory access time 190 ns and page-fault service time 8 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 8 ms = 8000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.013)*190 + 0.013*8000000.0 ns | Answer: 104.2 microseconds

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 1.7 m^3 at 290 kPa and 390 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 1.7, P = 290, Tk = 390 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (290e3)*1.7 / (8.314*390) | Answer: 152 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.2 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 12 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.2, t = 12 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.2*12) | Answer: 0.9093

question: For a reaction with A = 2e10 /s and activation energy 85 kJ/mol at 460 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 2, Ea = 85, Tk = 460 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 2e10 * exp(-85e3 / (8.314*460)) | Answer: 4.453 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.91 and bottoms xW = 0.08, with relative volatility alpha = 2. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.91, xw = 0.08, al = 2 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.91/0.09)(0.92/0.08)] / ln(2) | Answer: 6.861 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.62 and x = 0.48. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.62, x = 0.48 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.62/0.38) / (0.48/0.52) | Answer: 1.768

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.23 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 105 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.23, Psat = 105 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.23 * 105 | Answer: 24.15 kPa

question: A stream of 5.1 kg/s with specific heat 3 kJ/kg-K is heated through 85 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 5.1, cp = 3, dT = 85 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 5.1*3*85 | Answer: 13 kW

question: A reactor of volume 16.3 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 4.7 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 16.3, Q = 4.7 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 16.3 / 4.7 | Answer: 3.468 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 3.7e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 3 mm with a concentration difference of 80 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 3.7, L = 3, dC = 80 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (3.7e-9)*80 / (3e-3) | Answer: 98.67 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 6 min and steady-state gain 1.9. For a step input of magnitude 17, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 6, K = 1.9, M = 17 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 1.9 * 17 | Answer: 32.3 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 110 m^2 flies at 230 m/s (air density 0.7 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 1. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 110, V = 230, rho = 0.7, CL = 1 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.7*(230)^2*110*1 / 1000 | Answer: 2037 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 55 m^2 flies at 110 m/s (density 0.4 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.06. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 55, V = 110, rho = 0.4, CD = 0.06 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.4*(110)^2*55*0.06 / 1000 | Answer: 7.986 kN

question: A specimen under stress 80 MPa shows an elastic strain of 2e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 80, eps = 2 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 80 / (2e-3) MPa = 40 GPa | Answer: 40 GPa

question: A block of mass 23 kg has a volume of 2.6e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.

question: A rod of length 1700 mm is heated through 75 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 23e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 1700, dT = 75, al = 23 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 1700*23e-6*75 | Answer: 2.933 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 20 ohm, R2 = 90 ohm and R3 = 70 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 20, R2 = 90, R3 = 70 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 90*70 / 20 | Answer: 315 ohm

question: A measurement reads 10.3 when the true value is 10. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10.3, true = 10 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10.3 - 10| / 10 * 100 | Answer: 3 %

question: Annual demand is 47500 units, ordering cost 290 per order and holding cost 25 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 47500, S = 290, H = 25 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*47500*290 / 25) | Answer: 105 units

question: An asset costs 390000 with salvage value 20000 after 16 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 390000, Sv = 20000, n = 16 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (390000 - 20000) / 16 | Answer: 23125 per year

question: A product sells for 500 per unit with variable cost 70 per unit and fixed costs 75000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 500, V = 70, F = 75000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 75000 / (500 - 70) | Answer: 174.4 units

question: Find the present worth of 185000 received 2 years from now at an interest rate of 7% per year.

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.9, 0.95 and 0.91 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.9, r2 = 0.95, r3 = 0.91 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.9*0.95*0.91 | Answer: 0.7781

question: A process produces 9 defective items in a batch of 13000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).

question: Find the distance between the points (7, 3) and (-9, -4).

question: Find the 20th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -4 and common difference 4.

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 40500 at 8.6% per annum for 8 years.

question: 1.5 kg of air expands isothermally at 410 K from volume V1 to 4*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1.5, Tk = 410, ratio = 4 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 1.5*0.287*410*ln(4) | Answer: 244.7 kJ

question: In turning, cutting speed = 160 m/min, feed = 0.37 mm/rev, depth of cut = 1.1 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.

question: A workpiece of length 150 mm is turned at 850 rpm with a feed of 0.2 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 150, N = 850, f = 0.2 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 150 / (0.2*850) | Answer: 0.8824 min

question: Three resistors 30 ohm, 52 ohm and 84 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.

question: An inductor 489.5 mH is in series with 189 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 197.5 mH inductor at 740 Hz.

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 86 ohm, XL = 24 ohm and XC = 94 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.

question: A capacitor of 17.9 uF is charged to 255 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.

question: A transformer has primary voltage 120 V with 710 primary turns and 490 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 19 V across R1 = 9 ohm and R2 = 22 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 19, R1 = 9, R2 = 22 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 19*22 / (9+22) | Answer: 13.48 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 80 kohm and Rin = 29 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 80, Rin = 29 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 80 / 29 | Answer: 2.759

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 60 kohm and Rg = 11 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 60, Rg = 11 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 60/11 | Answer: 6.455

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 1361. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 1361 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(1361) | Answer: 31.34 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.1 m carries a central point load of 75 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.1, W = 75 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 75*4.1 / 4 | Answer: 76.88 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.7 m carries a UDL of 15 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.7, w = 15 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 15*(4.7)^2 / 8 | Answer: 41.42 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 5.2 m carries a point load 5 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.2, W = 5 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 5*5.2 | Answer: 26 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 3.9 m carries a UDL of 26 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.9, w = 26 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 26*(3.9)^2 / 2 | Answer: 197.7 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.1 m carries a point load 80 kN at distance 2.5 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 4.1, a = 2.5, W = 80 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 80*(4.1 - 2.5) / 4.1 | Answer: 31.22 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 3.5 m) carries a central point load 40 kN. With E = 25 GPa and I = 190e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=40000 N, L=3500.0 mm, E=25000 MPa, I=190e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 7.522 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 6.9 m carries a UDL of 36 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6.9, w = 36 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 36*(6.9)^2 / 12 | Answer: 142.8 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 470 mm, clear cover 45 mm and main bars of diameter 12 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 470, c = 45, dia = 12 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 470 - 45 - 12/2 | Answer: 419 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 23.2 m^2 carrying a factored load of 20 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 23.2, w = 20 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 20 * 23.2 | Answer: 464 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 4.6 m, unit weight 17 kN/m^3, phi = 30 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 8.1e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1.4, area = 2e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 8.1, i = 1.4, A = 2 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (8.1e-4)*1.4*(2e-3) | Answer: 2268 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 2.3 m, bed slope 0.008 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.018. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 1.5 m under a head of 1.1 m. Taking Cd = 0.63 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 4.5 m wide carries a discharge of 9.6 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A tank of volume 640 m^3 treats a flow of 180 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 640, Q = 180 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 640 / 180 | Answer: 3.556 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 260 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.26 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 6 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 260, k = 0.26, t = 6 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 260*(1 - e^(-0.26*6)) | Answer: 205.4 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.62, rainfall intensity 60 mm/h over a catchment of 30.6 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.62, i = 60, A = 30.6 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.62*60*30.6 / 360 | Answer: 3.162 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.03 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 290 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.03, M = 290 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 290*(20+0.03)/20 | Answer: 290.4 m

question: Convert the decimal number 2997 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 2997 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: BB5 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 10110000 and 10101010.
solution: XOR: 00011010 | Count of 1s = 3 | Answer: 3
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 280 megabits is sent over a link of 59 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 280, B = 59 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 280 / 59 | Answer: 4.746 s

question: A link has bandwidth 56 Mbps and round-trip time 100 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 56, R = 100 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 56e6 * 100e-3 bits = 5600 kb | Answer: 5600 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.84, cache access time 5 ns and main-memory access time 80 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.84, tc = 5, tm = 80 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.84*5 + (1 - 0.84)*80 | Answer: 17 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 828178 elements?
solution: Given: n = 828178 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(828178)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.011, memory access time 140 ns and page-fault service time 6 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 6 ms = 6000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.011)*140 + 0.011*6000000.0 ns | Answer: 66.14 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 0.3 m^3 at 410 kPa and 600 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 0.3, P = 410, Tk = 600 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (410e3)*0.3 / (8.314*600) | Answer: 24.66 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.19 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 15 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.19, t = 15 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.19*15) | Answer: 0.9422

question: For a reaction with A = 8e10 /s and activation energy 60 kJ/mol at 330 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 8, Ea = 60, Tk = 330 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 8e10 * exp(-60e3 / (8.314*330)) | Answer: 25.44 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.98 and bottoms xW = 0.08, with relative volatility alpha = 3.3. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.98, xw = 0.08, al = 3.3 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.98/0.02)(0.92/0.08)] / ln(3.3) | Answer: 5.305 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.59 and x = 0.22. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.59, x = 0.22 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.59/0.41) / (0.22/0.78) | Answer: 5.102

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.61 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 40 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.61, Psat = 40 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.61 * 40 | Answer: 24.4 kPa

question: A stream of 9.6 kg/s with specific heat 3 kJ/kg-K is heated through 80 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 9.6, cp = 3, dT = 80 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 9.6*3*80 | Answer: 2304 kW

question: A reactor of volume 16.7 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 4.8 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 16.7, Q = 4.8 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 16.7 / 4.8 | Answer: 3.479 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 1.9e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 4 mm with a concentration difference of 200 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 1.9, L = 4, dC = 200 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (1.9e-9)*200 / (4e-3) | Answer: 95 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 6.8 min and steady-state gain 4. For a step input of magnitude 14, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 6.8, K = 4, M = 14 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 4 * 14 | Answer: 56 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 55 m^2 flies at 180 m/s (air density 0.4 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.7. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 55, V = 180, rho = 0.4, CL = 0.7 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.4*(180)^2*55*0.7 / 1000 | Answer: 249.5 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 85 m^2 flies at 230 m/s (density 1.225 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.1. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 85, V = 230, rho = 1.225, CD = 0.1 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*1.225*(230)^2*85*0.1 / 1000 | Answer: 275.4 kN

question: A specimen under stress 80 MPa shows an elastic strain of 1.7e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 80, eps = 1.7 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 80 / (1.7e-3) MPa = 47.06 GPa | Answer: 47.06 GPa

question: A block of mass 49 kg has a volume of 3.5e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 49, V = 3.5 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 49 / (3.5e-3) | Answer: 14000 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 1000 mm is heated through 45 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 12e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 1000, dT = 45, al = 12 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 1000*12e-6*45 | Answer: 0.54 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 85 ohm, R2 = 40 ohm and R3 = 500 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 85, R2 = 40, R3 = 500 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 40*500 / 85 | Answer: 235.3 ohm

question: A measurement reads 10.33 when the true value is 100. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10.33, true = 100 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10.33 - 100| / 100 * 100 | Answer: 89.67 %

question: Annual demand is 34000 units, ordering cost 260 per order and holding cost 25 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 34000, S = 260, H = 25 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*34000*260 / 25) | Answer: 841 units

question: An asset costs 410000 with salvage value 24000 after 18 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 410000, Sv = 24000, n = 18 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (410000 - 24000) / 18 | Answer: 21444 per year

question: A product sells for 380 per unit with variable cost 140 per unit and fixed costs 55000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 380, V = 140, F = 55000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 55000 / (380 - 140) | Answer: 229.2 units

question: Find the present worth of 40000 received 10 years from now at an interest rate of 12% per year.
solution: Given: F = 40000, n = 10, i = 12 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 40000 / (1 + 0.12)^10 | Answer: 12879 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.92, 0.99 and 0.95 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.92, r2 = 0.99, r3 = 0.95 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.92*0.99*0.95 | Answer: 0.8653

question: A process produces 15 defective items in a batch of 16000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 15, N = 16000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 15/16000 * 1e6 | Answer: 937.5 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = 4x^3 + 3x^2 + 2x - 4 evaluated at x = 1.
For f(x) = -3x^3 + x^2 - 6x + 7, find f''(x) at x = 5.
Evaluate the definite integral of (3x^2 + 3x - 4) dx from x = -3 to x = 5.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = 3x^3/3 + 3x^2/2 + -4x | Evaluate F(5) - F(-3) | Answer: 144
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 3x^2 + 7x - 9 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[9, 1], [2, 5]].
solution: Given: a = 9, b = 1, c = 2, d = 5 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (9)(5) - (1)(2) | Answer: 43

question: Find the determinant of [[4, 5, 0], [-1, -5, -6], [-4, -1, 2]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: 66

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[1, -2], [7, -7]].
solution: Trace tr = -6, Determinant = 7 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: -1.586

question: Solve for x: -5x + 1y = -1 and 4x + 2y = -6.
solution: Determinant = -5*2 - 1*4 = -14 | x = (e d - b f) / det = -0.2857 | Answer: x = -0.2857
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 43, 85, 26, 74, 98.
solution: Sum = 326 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 65.2 | Answer: 65.2

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 48, 4, 12, 38, 22.
solution: Mean = 24.8 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 18.14

question: Find the slope of the line through (6, -7) and (0, -9).
solution: Given: x1 = 6, y1 = -7, x2 = 0, y2 = -9 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (-9 - -7) / (0 - 6) | Answer: 0.3333

question: Find the distance between the points (7, 5) and (-9, 5).
solution: Given: x1 = 7, y1 = 5, x2 = -9, y2 = 5 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-16)^2 + (0)^2) | Answer: 16 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (3,-1), (-1,6), (-1,4).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 4 sq units

question: Find the 36th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -11 and common difference 4.
solution: Given: a = -11, d = 4, n = 36 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -11 + (36 - 1)*4 | Answer: 129

question: Find the sum of the first 9 terms of an AP with first term -9 and common difference -1.
solution: Given: a = -9, d = -1, n = 9 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 9/2 [2*-9 + (9-1)*-1] | Answer: -117

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 47000 at 13% per annum for 5 years.
solution: Given: P = 47000, R = 13, Tt = 5 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 47000 * 13 * 5 / 100 | Answer: 30550 currency units

question: Find the amount when 38000 is invested at 10.3% per annum compounded annually for 2 years.
solution: Given: P = 38000, R = 10.3, Tt = 2 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 38000 * (1 + 10.3/100)^2 | Answer: 46231 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (-7, 3, 5) and (4, 6, -5).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (-4, 5, -5) and (-4, 0, -6).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 36.28

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (-3, 1, 1) and (3, 0, -3).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 148.5 degrees

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number 8 + -2i.
solution: Given: a = 8, b = -2 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(-2, 8) | Answer: -14.04 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = 5x^3 + 3x^2 + 2x + 9 at x = 1.
solution: Given: a = 5, b = 3, c = 2, d = 9, x0 = 1 | Formula: f(x0) = a x0^3 + b x0^2 + c x0 + d | Substitute: f(1) = 5(1)^3 + 3(1)^2 + 2(1) + 9 | Answer: 19

question: Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-196 with initial guess x0=14, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.3 and ordinates 9, 20, 14, 12, 10, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 514 and 580.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 514 and 580 | Answer: GCD = 2

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 41 and 63.
solution: Given: a = 41, b = 63 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 41*63 / 1 | Answer: 2583
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 20 mm carries an axial tensile load of 36 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 15 mm and length 2500 mm carries an axial load of 44 kN. Take E = 210 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 26 mm transmits a torque of 2250 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 26, Tt = 2250 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(2250*1000) / (pi*(26)^3) | Answer: 652 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 51 mm and length 1600 mm carries a torque of 650 N-m. With G = 80 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (51)^4 / 32 = 664172 mm^4 | theta = (650*1000)(1600) / (80000 * 664172) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 1.121 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 90 mm wide and 200 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 90, h = 200 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 90*(200)^2 / 6 | Answer: 600000 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (54 mm x 230 mm) carries a bending moment of 27 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (30 mm x 160 mm) has effective length 1700 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 300 MPa is designed for a working stress of 70 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 300, sw = 70 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 300 / 70 | Answer: 4.286

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 700 mm and wall thickness 18 mm carries an internal pressure of 0.8 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 700, t = 18, P = 0.8 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 0.8*700 / (2*18) | Answer: 15.56 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 660 K and 410 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 660, Tc = 410 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 410/660) * 100 | Answer: 37.88 %

question: A heat pump operates between 283 K and 324 K. Find its maximum (Carnot) COP.
solution: Given: Tc = 283, Th = 324 | Formula: COP_hp = Th / (Th - Tc) | Substitute: COP = 324 / (324 - 283) | Answer: 7.902

question: 6.4 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 60 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 6.4, dT = 60 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 6.4 * 0.718 * 60 | Answer: 275.7 kJ

question: 5.4 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 125 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 5.4, dT = 125 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 5.4 * 1.005 * 125 | Answer: 678.4 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 1 m^3 at 400 K with mass 4.9 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 1, Tk = 400, m = 4.9 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 4.9*0.287*400 / 1 | Answer: 562.5 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 3.3 kg of air expands isothermally at 440 K from volume V1 to 3*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.3, Tk = 440, ratio = 3 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 3.3*0.287*440*ln(3) | Answer: 457.8 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 2.3 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.05 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 2.3, D = 0.05 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*2.3*0.05 / 0.001 | Answer: 115000

question: Water flows at 1.6 m/s through a pipe of diameter 150 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 14.9 m. Taking Cv = 0.98, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 14.9, cv = 0.98 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.98*sqrt(2*9.81*14.9) | Answer: 16.76 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 200 mm) water flows at 1.1 m/s. It contracts to diameter 110 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
Water flows at 3.6 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.47 m and length 120 m. With friction factor f = 0.036, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 34 teeth drives a gear of 87 teeth. If the pinion runs at 600 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 34, z2 = 87, N1 = 600 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 600*34 / 87 | Answer: 234.5 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 140 mm rotates at 550 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 140, N = 550 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.14)*550 / 60 | Answer: 4.032 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 6 kW at 900 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 2700 N/m and mass 16.4 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.

question: A plane wall of area 3.7 m^2 and thickness 0.12 m has conductivity k = 21.1 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 180 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 3.7, L = 0.12, k = 21.1, dT = 180 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 21.1*3.7*180 / 0.12 | Answer: 117105 W

question: A surface of area 2.3 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 20 W/m^2-K to surroundings 70 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.

question: In turning, cutting speed = 110 m/min, feed = 0.21 mm/rev, depth of cut = 0.7 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 110, f = 0.21, d = 0.7 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*110*0.21*0.7 | Answer: 16170 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 370 mm is turned at 500 rpm with a feed of 0.16 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 370, N = 500, f = 0.16 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 370 / (0.16*500) | Answer: 4.625 min

question: A resistor of 145 ohm carries a current of 9 A. Find the voltage across it.

question: Three resistors 6 ohm, 23 ohm and 41 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 6, R2 = 23, R3 = 41 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 6 + 23 + 41 | Answer: 70 ohm

question: Two resistors 100 ohm and 118 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 100, R2 = 118 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 100*118 / (100+118) | Answer: 54.13 ohm

question: A device draws 1.5 A at 45 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 45, I = 1.5 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 45 * 1.5 | Answer: 67.5 W

question: A current of 10 A flows through a 77 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
