question: Two capacitors 45.3 uF and 26.6 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 45.3, C2 = 26.6 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 45.3*26.6 / (45.3+26.6) | Answer: 16.76 uF

question: A resistor 31 kohm and capacitor 0.8 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 31, C = 0.8 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (31k)(0.8u) = 24.8 ms | Answer: 24.8 ms

question: An inductor 186 mH is in series with 120 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 186, R = 120 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (186e-3) / 120 | Answer: 1.55 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 70.9 mH inductor at 510 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 70.9, f = 510 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (510)(70.9e-3) | Answer: 227.2 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 40.8 uF capacitor at 80 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 40.8, f = 80 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (80)(40.8e-6)) | Answer: 48.76 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 87 ohm, XL = 114 ohm and XC = 92 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 87, XL = 114, XC = 92 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(87^2 + (114 - 92)^2) | Answer: 89.74 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 72.7 mH and C = 1 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 72.7, C = 1 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(72.7e-3 * 1e-6)) | Answer: 590.3 Hz

question: A capacitor of 37.3 uF is charged to 340 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 37.3, V = 340 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*37.3e-6*(340)^2 | Answer: 2156 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 160 V with 250 primary turns and 230 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 160, N1 = 250, N2 = 230 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 160 * 230/250 | Answer: 147.2 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 400 V and draws an armature current of 38 A. If the armature resistance is 0.9 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 400, Ia = 38, Ra = 0.9 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 400 - 38*0.9 | Answer: 365.8 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 15 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.71. Find the total real power in kW.

question: A load has real power 145 kW and apparent power 170 kVA. Find the power factor.

question: A machine delivers 110 kW output while drawing 212 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 8 V across R1 = 42 ohm and R2 = 45 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 10 kohm and Rin = 15 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 6648. Express the gain in decibels (power).

question: A simply supported beam of span 5 m carries a central point load of 85 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.

question: A simply supported beam of span 8.1 m carries a UDL of 25 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 8.1, w = 25 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 25*(8.1)^2 / 8 | Answer: 205 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 3.9 m carries a point load 45 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.9, W = 45 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 45*3.9 | Answer: 175.5 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 3.2 m carries a UDL of 16 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.2, w = 16 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 16*(3.2)^2 / 2 | Answer: 81.92 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.6 m carries a point load 30 kN at distance 3.4 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.

question: A simply supported beam (span 4 m) carries a central point load 45 kN. With E = 30 GPa and I = 590e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.

question: An RC beam has overall depth 660 mm, clear cover 50 mm and main bars of diameter 12 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.

question: A column supports a floor area of 28.8 m^2 carrying a factored load of 14.9 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 5.1 m, unit weight 17 kN/m^3, phi = 35 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 3.6e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.3, area = 4.9e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.

question: A tank of volume 550 m^3 treats a flow of 25 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 550, Q = 25 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 550 / 25 | Answer: 22 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 150 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.14 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 4 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 150, k = 0.14, t = 4 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 150*(1 - e^(-0.14*4)) | Answer: 64.32 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.7, rainfall intensity 95 mm/h over a catchment of 11.1 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.7, i = 95, A = 11.1 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.7*95*11.1 / 360 | Answer: 2.05 m^3/s

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.01 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 360 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.01, M = 360 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 360*(20+0.01)/20 | Answer: 360.2 m

question: A file of 60 megabits is sent over a link of 61 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.

question: A link has bandwidth 90 Mbps and round-trip time 150 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 90, R = 150 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 90e6 * 150e-3 bits = 13500 kb | Answer: 13500 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.96, cache access time 8 ns and main-memory access time 170 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.96, tc = 8, tm = 170 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.96*8 + (1 - 0.96)*170 | Answer: 14.48 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 967208 elements?

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.009, memory access time 160 ns and page-fault service time 4 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 1.7 m^3 at 320 kPa and 440 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.11 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 8 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.11, t = 8 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.11*8) | Answer: 0.5852

question: For a reaction with A = 2e10 /s and activation energy 75 kJ/mol at 430 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 2, Ea = 75, Tk = 430 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 2e10 * exp(-75e3 / (8.314*430)) | Answer: 15.49 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.94 and bottoms xW = 0.05, with relative volatility alpha = 1.8. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.94, xw = 0.05, al = 1.8 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.94/0.06)(0.95/0.05)] / ln(1.8) | Answer: 9.691 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.86 and x = 0.26. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.26 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 90 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.26, Psat = 90 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.26 * 90 | Answer: 23.4 kPa

question: A stream of 6.8 kg/s with specific heat 2.4 kJ/kg-K is heated through 95 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 6.8, cp = 2.4, dT = 95 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 6.8*2.4*95 | Answer: 155 kW

question: A reactor of volume 13.4 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 3.8 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 4e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 5 mm with a concentration difference of 10 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.

question: A first-order process has time constant 7.2 min and steady-state gain 1.5. For a step input of magnitude 17, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 7.2, K = 1.5, M = 17 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 1.5 * 17 | Answer: 25.5 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 15 m^2 flies at 210 m/s (air density 1.225 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.6. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 15, V = 210, rho = 1.225, CL = 0.6 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1.225*(210)^2*15*0.6 / 1000 | Answer: 243.1 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 85 m^2 flies at 150 m/s (density 1 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.09. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 85, V = 150, rho = 1, CD = 0.09 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*1*(150)^2*85*0.09 / 1000 | Answer: 86.06 kN

question: A specimen under stress 210 MPa shows an elastic strain of 1.8e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 210, eps = 1.8 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 210 / (1.8e-3) MPa = 116.7 GPa | Answer: 116.7 GPa

question: A block of mass 9 kg has a volume of 3.2e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 9, V = 3.2 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 9 / (3.2e-3) | Answer: 2812 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 800 mm is heated through 80 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 23e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 800, dT = 80, al = 23 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 800*23e-6*80 | Answer: 1.472 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 60 ohm, R2 = 155 ohm and R3 = 160 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 60, R2 = 155, R3 = 160 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 155*160 / 60 | Answer: 413.3 ohm

question: A measurement reads 9.1 when the true value is 20. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.1, true = 20 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.1 - 20| / 20 * 100 | Answer: 54.5 %

question: Annual demand is 2500 units, ordering cost 210 per order and holding cost 7 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 2500, S = 210, H = 7 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*2500*210 / 7) | Answer: 387.3 units

question: An asset costs 360000 with salvage value 32000 after 9 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 360000, Sv = 32000, n = 9 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (360000 - 32000) / 9 | Answer: 36444 per year

question: A product sells for 360 per unit with variable cost 30 per unit and fixed costs 50000. Find the break-even quantity in units.

question: Find the present worth of 60000 received 7 years from now at an interest rate of 12% per year.
solution: Given: F = 60000, n = 7, i = 12 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 60000 / (1 + 0.12)^7 | Answer: 27141 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.9, 0.96 and 0.96 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.9, r2 = 0.96, r3 = 0.96 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.9*0.96*0.96 | Answer: 0.8294

question: A process produces 36 defective items in a batch of 11500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 36, N = 11500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 36/11500 * 1e6 | Answer: 313 PPM

question: Find the distance between the points (9, -2) and (-6, 3).

question: Find the 6th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -14 and common difference -7.

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 6500 at 5.8% per annum for 9 years.

question: Find the amount when 18500 is invested at 8.7% per annum compounded annually for 3 years.

question: Find the modulus of the complex number -2 + 7i.
solution: Given: a = -2, b = 7 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((-2)^2 + (7)^2) | Answer: 7.28

question: Evaluate f(x) = -4x^3 + 7x^2 + 7x - 4 at x = 3.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-58 with initial guess x0=9, find x1 (one iteration).
solution: Given: N = 58, x0 = 9 | Formula: x1 = x0 - (x0^2 - N)/(2 x0) | Substitute: x1 = 9 - ((9)^2 - 58)/(2*9) | Answer: 7.722

question: Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.9 and ordinates 9, 9, 15, 10, 16, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 127 and 49.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 127 and 49 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 61 and 61.
solution: Given: a = 61, b = 61 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 61*61 / 61 | Answer: 61
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 42 mm carries an axial tensile load of 13 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 15 mm and length 1200 mm carries an axial load of 60 kN. Take E = 210 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 80 mm transmits a torque of 1350 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 80, Tt = 1350 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(1350*1000) / (pi*(80)^3) | Answer: 13.43 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 50 mm and length 1400 mm carries a torque of 1450 N-m. With G = 77 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (50)^4 / 32 = 613592 mm^4 | theta = (1450*1000)(1400) / (77000 * 613592) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 2.462 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 78 mm wide and 270 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 78, h = 270 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 78*(270)^2 / 6 | Answer: 947700 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (114 mm x 230 mm) carries a bending moment of 15 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (79 mm x 90 mm) has effective length 3700 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 510 MPa is designed for a working stress of 180 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 510, sw = 180 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 510 / 180 | Answer: 2.833

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 800 mm and wall thickness 7 mm carries an internal pressure of 1 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 800, t = 7, P = 1 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 1*800 / (2*7) | Answer: 57.14 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 600 K and 410 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 600, Tc = 410 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 410/600) * 100 | Answer: 31.67 %

question: 6 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 20 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 6, dT = 20 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 6 * 0.718 * 20 | Answer: 86.16 kJ

question: 1.8 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 150 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1.8, dT = 150 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 1.8 * 1.005 * 150 | Answer: 271.3 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 2 m^3 at 350 K with mass 5.1 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 2, Tk = 350, m = 5.1 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 5.1*0.287*350 / 2 | Answer: 256.1 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 2.1 kg of air expands isothermally at 310 K from volume V1 to 3*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.1, Tk = 310, ratio = 3 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 2.1*0.287*310*ln(3) | Answer: 205.3 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 4.7 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.06 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 4.7, D = 0.06 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*4.7*0.06 / 0.001 | Answer: 282000

question: Water flows at 3.4 m/s through a pipe of diameter 290 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 8.9 m. Taking Cv = 0.98, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 8.9, cv = 0.98 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.98*sqrt(2*9.81*8.9) | Answer: 12.95 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 170 mm) water flows at 0.9 m/s. It contracts to diameter 110 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 170, d2 = 110, V1 = 0.9 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 0.9*(170/110)^2 | Answer: 2.15 m/s

question: Water flows at 2.7 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.28 m and length 380 m. With friction factor f = 0.027, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 21 teeth drives a gear of 92 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1250 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 21, z2 = 92, N1 = 1250 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1250*21 / 92 | Answer: 285.3 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 530 mm rotates at 450 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 530, N = 450 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.53)*450 / 60 | Answer: 12.49 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 12 kW at 1150 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 12, N = 1150 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(12*1000) / (2*pi*1150) | Answer: 99.64 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 4 kg rotates at radius 0.2 m at 450 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 15800 N/m and mass 6.7 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 15800, m = 6.7 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(15800/6.7) | Answer: 7.729 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 9.2 m^2 and thickness 0.16 m has conductivity k = 33.7 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 25 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 9.2, L = 0.16, k = 33.7, dT = 25 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 33.7*9.2*25 / 0.16 | Answer: 48444 W

question: A surface of area 5.5 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 175 W/m^2-K to surroundings 90 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 5.5, h = 175, dT = 90 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 175*5.5*90 | Answer: 86625 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 210 m/min, feed = 0.46 mm/rev, depth of cut = 1.2 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 210, f = 0.46, d = 1.2 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*210*0.46*1.2 | Answer: 115920 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 390 mm is turned at 200 rpm with a feed of 0.12 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 390, N = 200, f = 0.12 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 390 / (0.12*200) | Answer: 16.25 min

question: A resistor of 69 ohm carries a current of 3.3 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 69, I = 3.3 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 3.3 * 69 | Answer: 227.7 V

question: Three resistors 52 ohm, 83 ohm and 13 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 52, R2 = 83, R3 = 13 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 52 + 83 + 13 | Answer: 148 ohm

question: Two resistors 69 ohm and 109 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 69, R2 = 109 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 69*109 / (69+109) | Answer: 42.25 ohm

question: A device draws 0.5 A at 120 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 120, I = 0.5 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 120 * 0.5 | Answer: 60 W

question: A current of 6.2 A flows through a 13 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 6.2, R = 13 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (6.2)^2 * 13 | Answer: 499.7 W

question: Two capacitors 19.4 uF and 38 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 19.4, C2 = 38 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 19.4*38 / (19.4+38) | Answer: 12.84 uF

question: A resistor 64 kohm and capacitor 9.5 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 64, C = 9.5 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (64k)(9.5u) = 608 ms | Answer: 608 ms

question: An inductor 132.9 mH is in series with 104 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 132.9, R = 104 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (132.9e-3) / 104 | Answer: 1.278 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 106 mH inductor at 520 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 106, f = 520 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (520)(106e-3) | Answer: 346.3 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 43 uF capacitor at 420 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 43, f = 420 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (420)(43e-6)) | Answer: 8.813 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 99 ohm, XL = 86 ohm and XC = 58 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 99, XL = 86, XC = 58 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(99^2 + (86 - 58)^2) | Answer: 102.9 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 2.6 mH and C = 3.1 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 2.6, C = 3.1 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(2.6e-3 * 3.1e-6)) | Answer: 1773 Hz

question: A capacitor of 81.7 uF is charged to 290 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 81.7, V = 290 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*81.7e-6*(290)^2 | Answer: 3435 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 360 V with 280 primary turns and 150 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 360, N1 = 280, N2 = 150 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 360 * 150/280 | Answer: 192.9 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 290 V and draws an armature current of 18 A. If the armature resistance is 0.91 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 290, Ia = 18, Ra = 0.91 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 290 - 18*0.91 | Answer: 273.6 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 20 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.89. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 20, VL = 400, pf = 0.89 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*400*20*0.89 / 1000 | Answer: 12.33 kW

question: A load has real power 165 kW and apparent power 195 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 165, S = 195 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 165 / 195 | Answer: 0.8462

question: A machine delivers 15 kW output while drawing 112 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 15, Pi = 112 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 15/112 * 100 | Answer: 13.39 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 16 V across R1 = 50 ohm and R2 = 15 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 16, R1 = 50, R2 = 15 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 16*15 / (50+15) | Answer: 3.692 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 30 kohm and Rin = 39 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 30, Rin = 39 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 30 / 39 | Answer: 0.7692

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 150 kohm and Rg = 30 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 150, Rg = 30 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 150/30 | Answer: 6

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 7640. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 7640 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(7640) | Answer: 38.83 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 5.9 m carries a central point load of 70 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.9, W = 70 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 70*5.9 / 4 | Answer: 103.2 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 7.4 m carries a UDL of 60 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7.4, w = 60 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 60*(7.4)^2 / 8 | Answer: 410.7 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 5.6 m carries a UDL of 32 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.6, w = 32 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 32*(5.6)^2 / 2 | Answer: 501.8 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 5.6 m carries a point load 20 kN at distance 3.4 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 5.6, a = 3.4, W = 20 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 20*(5.6 - 3.4) / 5.6 | Answer: 7.857 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 7.8 m) carries a central point load 25 kN. With E = 25 GPa and I = 560e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=25000 N, L=7800.0 mm, E=25000 MPa, I=560e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 17.65 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 8.5 m carries a UDL of 21 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 8.5, w = 21 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 21*(8.5)^2 / 12 | Answer: 126.4 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 350 mm, clear cover 50 mm and main bars of diameter 20 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 350, c = 50, dia = 20 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 350 - 50 - 20/2 | Answer: 290 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 11.8 m^2 carrying a factored load of 15 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 11.8, w = 15 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 15 * 11.8 | Answer: 177 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 4.6 m, unit weight 16 kN/m^3, phi = 29 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 8.6e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1.1, area = 2.9e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 8.6, i = 1.1, A = 2.9 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (8.6e-4)*1.1*(2.9e-3) | Answer: 2743 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.3 m, bed slope 0.009 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.016. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 1.4 m under a head of 0.8 m. Taking Cd = 0.63 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 2.4 m wide carries a discharge of 20.8 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 520 m and design speed 60 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 520, V = 60 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (60)^2 / (127*520) | Answer: 0.05451
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: A tank of volume 990 m^3 treats a flow of 45 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 990, Q = 45 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 990 / 45 | Answer: 22 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 220 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.22 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 6 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 220, k = 0.22, t = 6 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 220*(1 - e^(-0.22*6)) | Answer: 161.2 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.49, rainfall intensity 100 mm/h over a catchment of 9.8 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.49, i = 100, A = 9.8 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.49*100*9.8 / 360 | Answer: 1.334 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.05 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 220 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.05, M = 220 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 220*(20+0.05)/20 | Answer: 220.6 m

question: Convert the decimal number 406 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 406 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 196 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 00101011 and 11101111.
solution: XOR: 11000100 | Count of 1s = 3 | Answer: 3
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 280 megabits is sent over a link of 18 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 280, B = 18 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 280 / 18 | Answer: 15.56 s

question: A link has bandwidth 28 Mbps and round-trip time 90 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 28, R = 90 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 28e6 * 90e-3 bits = 2520 kb | Answer: 2520 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.87, cache access time 2 ns and main-memory access time 80 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.87, tc = 2, tm = 80 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.87*2 + (1 - 0.87)*80 | Answer: 12.14 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 682380 elements?
solution: Given: n = 682380 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(682380)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.015, memory access time 90 ns and page-fault service time 10 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 10 ms = 10000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.015)*90 + 0.015*10000000.0 ns | Answer: 150.1 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 2.8 m^3 at 340 kPa and 410 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 2.8, P = 340, Tk = 410 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (340e3)*2.8 / (8.314*410) | Answer: 279.3 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.17 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 6 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.17, t = 6 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.17*6) | Answer: 0.6394

question: For a reaction with A = 9e10 /s and activation energy 90 kJ/mol at 460 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 9, Ea = 90, Tk = 460 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 9e10 * exp(-90e3 / (8.314*460)) | Answer: 5.421 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.98 and bottoms xW = 0.05, with relative volatility alpha = 2.5. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.98, xw = 0.05, al = 2.5 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.98/0.02)(0.95/0.05)] / ln(2.5) | Answer: 7.461 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.9 and x = 0.46. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.9, x = 0.46 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.9/0.1) / (0.46/0.54) | Answer: 10.57

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.16 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 80 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.16, Psat = 80 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.16 * 80 | Answer: 12.8 kPa

question: A stream of 9 kg/s with specific heat 2 kJ/kg-K is heated through 35 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 9, cp = 2, dT = 35 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 9*2*35 | Answer: 630 kW

question: A reactor of volume 12.2 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 1.9 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 12.2, Q = 1.9 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 12.2 / 1.9 | Answer: 6.421 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 3.6e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 1 mm with a concentration difference of 130 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 3.6, L = 1, dC = 130 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (3.6e-9)*130 / (1e-3) | Answer: 468 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 9 min and steady-state gain 3.7. For a step input of magnitude 7, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 9, K = 3.7, M = 7 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 3.7 * 7 | Answer: 25.9 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 15 m^2 flies at 110 m/s (air density 1.225 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 1.2. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 15, V = 110, rho = 1.225, CL = 1.2 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1.225*(110)^2*15*1.2 / 1000 | Answer: 133.4 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 80 m^2 flies at 150 m/s (density 0.7 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.08. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 80, V = 150, rho = 0.7, CD = 0.08 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.7*(150)^2*80*0.08 / 1000 | Answer: 50.4 kN

question: A block of mass 23 kg has a volume of 4.8e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 23, V = 4.8 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 23 / (4.8e-3) | Answer: 4792 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 2400 mm is heated through 135 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 23e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 2400, dT = 135, al = 23 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 2400*23e-6*135 | Answer: 7.452 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 75 ohm, R2 = 105 ohm and R3 = 90 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 75, R2 = 105, R3 = 90 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 105*90 / 75 | Answer: 126 ohm

question: A measurement reads 9.91 when the true value is 50. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.91, true = 50 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.91 - 50| / 50 * 100 | Answer: 80.18 %

question: Annual demand is 32000 units, ordering cost 100 per order and holding cost 15 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 32000, S = 100, H = 15 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*32000*100 / 15) | Answer: 653.2 units

question: An asset costs 470000 with salvage value 26000 after 6 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 470000, Sv = 26000, n = 6 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (470000 - 26000) / 6 | Answer: 74000 per year

question: A product sells for 240 per unit with variable cost 90 per unit and fixed costs 100000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 240, V = 90, F = 100000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 100000 / (240 - 90) | Answer: 666.7 units

question: Find the present worth of 165000 received 5 years from now at an interest rate of 12% per year.
solution: Given: F = 165000, n = 5, i = 12 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 165000 / (1 + 0.12)^5 | Answer: 93625 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.95, 0.95 and 0.91 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.95, r2 = 0.95, r3 = 0.91 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.95*0.95*0.91 | Answer: 0.8213

question: A process produces 30 defective items in a batch of 10000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 30, N = 10000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 30/10000 * 1e6 | Answer: 3000 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -x^3 - 5x^2 - 5x + 4 evaluated at x = 2.
For f(x) = -6x^3 - 8x^2 - 9x + 3, find f''(x) at x = -5.
Evaluate the definite integral of (-2x^2 + 3x + 3) dx from x = 1 to x = 3.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = -2x^3/3 + 3x^2/2 + 3x | Evaluate F(3) - F(1) | Answer: 0.6667
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 4x^2 + 8x - 6 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[-5, 3], [-2, -8]].
solution: Given: a = -5, b = 3, c = -2, d = -8 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (-5)(-8) - (3)(-2) | Answer: 46

question: Find the determinant of [[0, -5, -4], [0, -1, -3], [4, -3, 1]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: 44

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[8, 3], [7, 7]].
solution: Trace tr = 15, Determinant = 35 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 12.11

question: Solve for x: 0x + -2y = -3 and 3x + 6y = 0.
solution: Determinant = 0*6 - -2*3 = 6 | x = (e d - b f) / det = -3 | Answer: x = -3
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 91, 13, 85, 47, 50.
solution: Sum = 286 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 57.2 | Answer: 57.2

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 42, 11, 1, 33, 29.
solution: Mean = 23.2 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 16.77

question: Find the slope of the line through (-6, -1) and (-4, 8).
solution: Given: x1 = -6, y1 = -1, x2 = -4, y2 = 8 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (8 - -1) / (-4 - -6) | Answer: 4.5

question: Find the distance between the points (-8, 3) and (7, 6).
solution: Given: x1 = -8, y1 = 3, x2 = 7, y2 = 6 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((15)^2 + (3)^2) | Answer: 15.3 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (4,0), (-3,2), (2,6).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 19 sq units

question: Find the 18th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 14 and common difference -4.
solution: Given: a = 14, d = -4, n = 18 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = 14 + (18 - 1)*-4 | Answer: -54

question: Find the sum of the first 13 terms of an AP with first term 10 and common difference 4.
solution: Given: a = 10, d = 4, n = 13 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 13/2 [2*10 + (13-1)*4] | Answer: 442

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 27000 at 13.9% per annum for 3 years.
solution: Given: P = 27000, R = 13.9, Tt = 3 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 27000 * 13.9 * 3 / 100 | Answer: 11259 currency units

question: Find the amount when 7000 is invested at 8.7% per annum compounded annually for 5 years.
solution: Given: P = 7000, R = 8.7, Tt = 5 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 7000 * (1 + 8.7/100)^5 | Answer: 10623 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (-4, -6, -3) and (-8, 2, -7).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (-2, 6, -6) and (2, 0, 3).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 22.45

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (6, -6, -5) and (-3, 5, -4).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 113.7 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number -3 + 0i.
solution: Given: a = -3, b = 0 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((-3)^2 + (0)^2) | Answer: 3

question: Evaluate f(x) = -2x^3 - 7x^2 + 8x - 9 at x = -5.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-81 with initial guess x0=4, find x1 (one iteration).
solution: Given: N = 81, x0 = 4 | Formula: x1 = x0 - (x0^2 - N)/(2 x0) | Substitute: x1 = 4 - ((4)^2 - 81)/(2*4) | Answer: 12.12

question: Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=0.7 and ordinates 12, 7, 7, 8, 19, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 116 and 32.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 116 and 32 | Answer: GCD = 4

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 19 and 47.
solution: Given: a = 19, b = 47 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 19*47 / 1 | Answer: 893
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 57 mm carries an axial tensile load of 12 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 32 mm and length 1700 mm carries an axial load of 63 kN. Take E = 110 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 51 mm transmits a torque of 2300 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 51, Tt = 2300 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(2300*1000) / (pi*(51)^3) | Answer: 88.31 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 46 mm and length 1800 mm carries a torque of 1700 N-m. With G = 45 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (46)^4 / 32 = 439573 mm^4 | theta = (1700*1000)(1800) / (45000 * 439573) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 8.863 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 60 mm wide and 70 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 60, h = 70 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 60*(70)^2 / 6 | Answer: 49000 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (93 mm x 250 mm) carries a bending moment of 18 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (56 mm x 100 mm) has effective length 1700 mm and E = 200 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 390 MPa is designed for a working stress of 220 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 390, sw = 220 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 390 / 220 | Answer: 1.773

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 500 mm and wall thickness 9 mm carries an internal pressure of 0.8 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 500, t = 9, P = 0.8 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 0.8*500 / (2*9) | Answer: 22.22 MPa

question: 1 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 135 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1, dT = 135 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 1 * 0.718 * 135 | Answer: 96.93 kJ

question: 4.1 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 190 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.1, dT = 190 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 4.1 * 1.005 * 190 | Answer: 782.9 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 1.1 m^3 at 450 K with mass 3.7 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 1.1, Tk = 450, m = 3.7 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 3.7*0.287*450 / 1.1 | Answer: 434.4 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 2 kg of air expands isothermally at 460 K from volume V1 to 4*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2, Tk = 460, ratio = 4 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 2*0.287*460*ln(4) | Answer: 366 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 4.6 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.27 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 4.6, D = 0.27 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*4.6*0.27 / 0.001 | Answer: 1242000

question: Water flows at 3.8 m/s through a pipe of diameter 280 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 16.4 m. Taking Cv = 0.99, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 16.4, cv = 0.99 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.99*sqrt(2*9.81*16.4) | Answer: 17.76 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 250 mm) water flows at 2.2 m/s. It contracts to diameter 80 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 250, d2 = 80, V1 = 2.2 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 2.2*(250/80)^2 | Answer: 21.48 m/s

question: Water flows at 2 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.3 m and length 150 m. With friction factor f = 0.033, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 31 teeth drives a gear of 119 teeth. If the pinion runs at 400 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 31, z2 = 119, N1 = 400 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 400*31 / 119 | Answer: 104.2 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 540 mm rotates at 850 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 540, N = 850 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.54)*850 / 60 | Answer: 24.03 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 20.9 kW at 500 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 20.9, N = 500 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(20.9*1000) / (2*pi*500) | Answer: 399.2 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 3.9 kg rotates at radius 0.44 m at 250 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 19700 N/m and mass 11.4 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 19700, m = 11.4 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(19700/11.4) | Answer: 6.616 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 5.5 m^2 and thickness 0.3 m has conductivity k = 10 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 105 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 5.5, L = 0.3, k = 10, dT = 105 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 10*5.5*105 / 0.3 | Answer: 19250 W

question: A surface of area 5.6 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 145 W/m^2-K to surroundings 135 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 5.6, h = 145, dT = 135 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 145*5.6*135 | Answer: 109620 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 90 m/min, feed = 0.24 mm/rev, depth of cut = 0.6 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 90, f = 0.24, d = 0.6 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*90*0.24*0.6 | Answer: 12960 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 190 mm is turned at 300 rpm with a feed of 0.38 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 190, N = 300, f = 0.38 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 190 / (0.38*300) | Answer: 1.667 min

question: A resistor of 50 ohm carries a current of 4.2 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 50, I = 4.2 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 4.2 * 50 | Answer: 210 V

question: Three resistors 96 ohm, 13 ohm and 33 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 96, R2 = 13, R3 = 33 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 96 + 13 + 33 | Answer: 142 ohm

question: Two resistors 79 ohm and 12 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 79, R2 = 12 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 79*12 / (79+12) | Answer: 10.42 ohm

question: A device draws 10.1 A at 185 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 185, I = 10.1 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 185 * 10.1 | Answer: 1868 W

question: A current of 1.4 A flows through a 65 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 1.4, R = 65 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (1.4)^2 * 65 | Answer: 127.4 W

question: Two capacitors 25.8 uF and 1.4 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 25.8, C2 = 1.4 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 25.8*1.4 / (25.8+1.4) | Answer: 1.328 uF

question: A resistor 76 kohm and capacitor 1.6 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 76, C = 1.6 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (76k)(1.6u) = 121.6 ms | Answer: 121.6 ms

question: An inductor 204.9 mH is in series with 191 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 204.9, R = 191 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (204.9e-3) / 191 | Answer: 1.073 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 27.3 mH inductor at 770 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 27.3, f = 770 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (770)(27.3e-3) | Answer: 132.1 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 24.6 uF capacitor at 70 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 24.6, f = 70 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (70)(24.6e-6)) | Answer: 92.42 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 20 ohm, XL = 124 ohm and XC = 112 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 20, XL = 124, XC = 112 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(20^2 + (124 - 112)^2) | Answer: 23.32 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 41.9 mH and C = 6.1 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 41.9, C = 6.1 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(41.9e-3 * 6.1e-6)) | Answer: 314.8 Hz

question: A capacitor of 34.2 uF is charged to 100 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 34.2, V = 100 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*34.2e-6*(100)^2 | Answer: 171 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 160 V with 200 primary turns and 290 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 160, N1 = 200, N2 = 290 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 160 * 290/200 | Answer: 232 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 340 V and draws an armature current of 30 A. If the armature resistance is 0.5 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 340, Ia = 30, Ra = 0.5 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 340 - 30*0.5 | Answer: 325 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 175 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.81. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 175, VL = 400, pf = 0.81 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*400*175*0.81 / 1000 | Answer: 98.21 kW

question: A load has real power 75 kW and apparent power 155 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 75, S = 155 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 75 / 155 | Answer: 0.4839

question: A machine delivers 30 kW output while drawing 137 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 30, Pi = 137 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 30/137 * 100 | Answer: 21.9 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 30 V across R1 = 26 ohm and R2 = 11 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 30, R1 = 26, R2 = 11 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 30*11 / (26+11) | Answer: 8.919 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 10 kohm and Rin = 29 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 10, Rin = 29 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 10 / 29 | Answer: 0.3448

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 140 kohm and Rg = 23 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 140, Rg = 23 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 140/23 | Answer: 7.087

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 8231. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 8231 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(8231) | Answer: 39.15 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 7 m carries a central point load of 120 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7, W = 120 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 120*7 / 4 | Answer: 210 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 3 m carries a UDL of 15 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3, w = 15 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 15*(3)^2 / 8 | Answer: 16.88 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 3.1 m carries a point load 75 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.1, W = 75 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 75*3.1 | Answer: 232.5 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 4.3 m carries a UDL of 36 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.3, w = 36 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 36*(4.3)^2 / 2 | Answer: 332.8 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 7.1 m carries a point load 50 kN at distance 1.4 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 7.1, a = 1.4, W = 50 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 50*(7.1 - 1.4) / 7.1 | Answer: 40.14 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 3.8 m) carries a central point load 15 kN. With E = 30 GPa and I = 510e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=15000 N, L=3800.0 mm, E=30000 MPa, I=510e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 1.121 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 8.4 m carries a UDL of 21 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 8.4, w = 21 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 21*(8.4)^2 / 12 | Answer: 123.5 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 640 mm, clear cover 35 mm and main bars of diameter 12 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 640, c = 35, dia = 12 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 640 - 35 - 12/2 | Answer: 599 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 18.6 m^2 carrying a factored load of 10.3 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 18.6, w = 10.3 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 10.3 * 18.6 | Answer: 191.6 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 6.1 m, unit weight 16 kN/m^3, phi = 35 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 2.8e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.8, area = 5.1e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 2.8, i = 0.8, A = 5.1 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (2.8e-4)*0.8*(5.1e-3) | Answer: 1142 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.5 m, bed slope 0.003 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.026. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 2 m under a head of 1 m. Taking Cd = 0.64 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
solution: Given: L = 2, H = 1, cd = 0.64 | Formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2) | Substitute: Q = (2/3)*0.64*sqrt(2*9.81)*2*(1)^1.5 | Answer: 3.78 m^3/s
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 4.8 m wide carries a discharge of 27.6 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 450 m and design speed 55 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 450, V = 55 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (55)^2 / (127*450) | Answer: 0.05293
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: A tank of volume 940 m^3 treats a flow of 185 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 940, Q = 185 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 940 / 185 | Answer: 5.081 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 310 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.27 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 5 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 310, k = 0.27, t = 5 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 310*(1 - e^(-0.27*5)) | Answer: 229.6 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.57, rainfall intensity 115 mm/h over a catchment of 43.9 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.57, i = 115, A = 43.9 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.57*115*43.9 / 360 | Answer: 7.993 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.02 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 350 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.02, M = 350 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 350*(30+0.02)/30 | Answer: 350.2 m

question: Convert the decimal number 1110 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 1110 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 456 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 01010010 and 00101011.
solution: XOR: 01111001 | Count of 1s = 5 | Answer: 5
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 970 megabits is sent over a link of 30 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 970, B = 30 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 970 / 30 | Answer: 32.33 s

question: A link has bandwidth 19 Mbps and round-trip time 20 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 19, R = 20 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 19e6 * 20e-3 bits = 380 kb | Answer: 380 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.97, cache access time 5 ns and main-memory access time 50 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.97, tc = 5, tm = 50 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.97*5 + (1 - 0.97)*50 | Answer: 6.35 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 951944 elements?
solution: Given: n = 951944 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(951944)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.009, memory access time 200 ns and page-fault service time 8 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 8 ms = 8000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.009)*200 + 0.009*8000000.0 ns | Answer: 72.2 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 2.8 m^3 at 260 kPa and 320 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 2.8, P = 260, Tk = 320 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (260e3)*2.8 / (8.314*320) | Answer: 273.6 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.15 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 11 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.15, t = 11 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.15*11) | Answer: 0.808

question: For a reaction with A = 8e10 /s and activation energy 65 kJ/mol at 400 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 8, Ea = 65, Tk = 400 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 8e10 * exp(-65e3 / (8.314*400)) | Answer: 259.8 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.9 and bottoms xW = 0.04, with relative volatility alpha = 3.3. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.9, xw = 0.04, al = 3.3 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.9/0.1)(0.96/0.04)] / ln(3.3) | Answer: 4.502 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.78 and x = 0.24. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.78, x = 0.24 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.78/0.22) / (0.24/0.76) | Answer: 11.23

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.64 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 100 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.64, Psat = 100 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.64 * 100 | Answer: 64 kPa

question: A stream of 6.7 kg/s with specific heat 2.8 kJ/kg-K is heated through 60 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 6.7, cp = 2.8, dT = 60 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 6.7*2.8*60 | Answer: 1126 kW

question: A reactor of volume 6.2 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 3.3 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 6.2, Q = 3.3 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 6.2 / 3.3 | Answer: 1.879 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 4.3e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 2 mm with a concentration difference of 50 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 4.3, L = 2, dC = 50 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (4.3e-9)*50 / (2e-3) | Answer: 107.5 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 6.9 min and steady-state gain 0.5. For a step input of magnitude 7, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 6.9, K = 0.5, M = 7 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 0.5 * 7 | Answer: 3.5 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 80 m^2 flies at 200 m/s (air density 1 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 1.1. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 80, V = 200, rho = 1, CL = 1.1 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1*(200)^2*80*1.1 / 1000 | Answer: 1760 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 55 m^2 flies at 190 m/s (density 0.7 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.12. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 55, V = 190, rho = 0.7, CD = 0.12 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.7*(190)^2*55*0.12 / 1000 | Answer: 83.39 kN

question: A specimen under stress 140 MPa shows an elastic strain of 1.4e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 140, eps = 1.4 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 140 / (1.4e-3) MPa = 100 GPa | Answer: 100 GPa

question: A block of mass 4 kg has a volume of 5.8e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 4, V = 5.8 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 4 / (5.8e-3) | Answer: 689.7 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 1100 mm is heated through 110 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 17e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 1100, dT = 110, al = 17 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 1100*17e-6*110 | Answer: 2.057 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 35 ohm, R2 = 75 ohm and R3 = 270 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 35, R2 = 75, R3 = 270 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 75*270 / 35 | Answer: 578.6 ohm

question: Annual demand is 34500 units, ordering cost 130 per order and holding cost 10 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 34500, S = 130, H = 10 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*34500*130 / 10) | Answer: 947.1 units

question: An asset costs 60000 with salvage value 20000 after 10 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 60000, Sv = 20000, n = 10 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (60000 - 20000) / 10 | Answer: 4000 per year

question: A product sells for 300 per unit with variable cost 70 per unit and fixed costs 195000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 300, V = 70, F = 195000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 195000 / (300 - 70) | Answer: 847.8 units

question: Find the present worth of 140000 received 6 years from now at an interest rate of 9% per year.
solution: Given: F = 140000, n = 6, i = 9 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 140000 / (1 + 0.09)^6 | Answer: 83477 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.91, 0.93 and 0.92 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.91, r2 = 0.93, r3 = 0.92 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.91*0.93*0.92 | Answer: 0.7786

question: A process produces 23 defective items in a batch of 6000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 23, N = 6000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 23/6000 * 1e6 | Answer: 3833 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -x^3 - 2x^2 - 7x - 6 evaluated at x = -1.
For f(x) = -x^3 - 6x^2 + 5x + 5, find f''(x) at x = -1.
Evaluate the definite integral of (5x^2 - 2x - 8) dx from x = -4 to x = 6.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = 5x^3/3 + -2x^2/2 + -8x | Evaluate F(6) - F(-4) | Answer: 366.7
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 2x^2 - 11x + 9 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[5, -1], [-5, -2]].
solution: Given: a = 5, b = -1, c = -5, d = -2 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (5)(-2) - (-1)(-5) | Answer: -15

question: Find the determinant of [[-4, 5, -1], [3, 0, 4], [1, 6, 4]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: 38

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[8, -7], [-8, -4]].
solution: Trace tr = 4, Determinant = -88 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 11.59

question: Solve for x: -2x + 4y = 0 and -1x + 0y = 5.
solution: Determinant = -2*0 - 4*-1 = 4 | x = (e d - b f) / det = -5 | Answer: x = -5
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 70, 43, 58, 2, 88.
solution: Sum = 261 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 52.2 | Answer: 52.2

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 15, 12, 22, 47, 25.
solution: Mean = 24.2 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 13.77

question: Find the slope of the line through (-8, 7) and (4, -1).
solution: Given: x1 = -8, y1 = 7, x2 = 4, y2 = -1 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (-1 - 7) / (4 - -8) | Answer: -0.6667

question: Find the distance between the points (-3, 3) and (-7, 2).
solution: Given: x1 = -3, y1 = 3, x2 = -7, y2 = 2 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-4)^2 + (-1)^2) | Answer: 4.123 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (1,-6), (7,-4), (6,-2).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 7 sq units

question: Find the 34th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -10 and common difference 3.
solution: Given: a = -10, d = 3, n = 34 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -10 + (34 - 1)*3 | Answer: 89

question: Find the sum of the first 11 terms of an AP with first term -14 and common difference -3.
solution: Given: a = -14, d = -3, n = 11 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 11/2 [2*-14 + (11-1)*-3] | Answer: -319

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 17500 at 6.2% per annum for 9 years.
solution: Given: P = 17500, R = 6.2, Tt = 9 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 17500 * 6.2 * 9 / 100 | Answer: 9765 currency units

question: Find the amount when 18500 is invested at 7.2% per annum compounded annually for 2 years.
solution: Given: P = 18500, R = 7.2, Tt = 2 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 18500 * (1 + 7.2/100)^2 | Answer: 2126 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (-1, -3, -6) and (5, 3, 3).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (1, 1, 3) and (1, -4, -4).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 11.75

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (6, 6, 5) and (5, -3, -2).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 88.11 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number -8 + -8i.
solution: Given: a = -8, b = -8 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((-8)^2 + (-8)^2) | Answer: 11.31

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number -1 + 11i.
solution: Given: a = -1, b = 11 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(11, -1) | Answer: 95.19 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = 2x^3 - 3x^2 + 3x + 9 at x = -4.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-50 with initial guess x0=9, find x1 (one iteration).
solution: Given: N = 50, x0 = 9 | Formula: x1 = x0 - (x0^2 - N)/(2 x0) | Substitute: x1 = 9 - ((9)^2 - 50)/(2*9) | Answer: 7.278

question: Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=0.8 and ordinates 17, 9, 13, 3, 17, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 154 and 246.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 154 and 246 | Answer: GCD = 2

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 80 and 77.
solution: Given: a = 80, b = 77 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 80*77 / 1 | Answer: 6160
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 11 mm carries an axial tensile load of 32 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 31 mm and length 1500 mm carries an axial load of 84 kN. Take E = 210 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 48 mm transmits a torque of 300 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 48, Tt = 300 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(300*1000) / (pi*(48)^3) | Answer: 13.82 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 42 mm and length 1900 mm carries a torque of 500 N-m. With G = 45 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (42)^4 / 32 = 30549 mm^4 | theta = (500*1000)(1900) / (45000 * 30549) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 3.959 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 91 mm wide and 170 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 91, h = 170 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 91*(170)^2 / 6 | Answer: 438317 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (49 mm x 100 mm) carries a bending moment of 11 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (60 mm x 130 mm) has effective length 2500 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 460 MPa is designed for a working stress of 80 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 460, sw = 80 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 460 / 80 | Answer: 5.75

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1500 mm and wall thickness 14 mm carries an internal pressure of 1.6 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1500, t = 14, P = 1.6 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 1.6*1500 / (2*14) | Answer: 85.71 MPa

question: 1.9 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 135 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1.9, dT = 135 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 1.9 * 0.718 * 135 | Answer: 184.2 kJ

question: 5.2 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 170 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 5.2, dT = 170 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 5.2 * 1.005 * 170 | Answer: 888.4 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 0.9 m^3 at 490 K with mass 4.9 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 0.9, Tk = 490, m = 4.9 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 4.9*0.287*490 / 0.9 | Answer: 765.7 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 4.9 kg of air expands isothermally at 320 K from volume V1 to 4*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.9, Tk = 320, ratio = 4 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 4.9*0.287*320*ln(4) | Answer: 623.9 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 1.4 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.39 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 1.4, D = 0.39 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*1.4*0.39 / 0.001 | Answer: 546000

question: Water flows at 3.4 m/s through a pipe of diameter 80 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 14.1 m. Taking Cv = 0.96, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 14.1, cv = 0.96 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.96*sqrt(2*9.81*14.1) | Answer: 15.97 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 360 mm) water flows at 1.8 m/s. It contracts to diameter 120 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 360, d2 = 120, V1 = 1.8 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 1.8*(360/120)^2 | Answer: 16.2 m/s

question: Water flows at 2.1 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.36 m and length 130 m. With friction factor f = 0.021, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 23 teeth drives a gear of 93 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1450 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 23, z2 = 93, N1 = 1450 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1450*23 / 93 | Answer: 358.6 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 310 mm rotates at 600 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 310, N = 600 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.31)*600 / 60 | Answer: 9.739 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 8.6 kW at 1500 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 8.6, N = 1500 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(8.6*1000) / (2*pi*1500) | Answer: 54.75 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 8.8 kg rotates at radius 0.35 m at 650 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 4400 N/m and mass 18 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 4400, m = 18 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(4400/18) | Answer: 2.488 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 3.7 m^2 and thickness 0.21 m has conductivity k = 9.5 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 45 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 3.7, L = 0.21, k = 9.5, dT = 45 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 9.5*3.7*45 / 0.21 | Answer: 7532 W

question: A surface of area 2.3 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 165 W/m^2-K to surroundings 90 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 2.3, h = 165, dT = 90 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 165*2.3*90 | Answer: 34155 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 250 m/min, feed = 0.44 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2.1 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 250, f = 0.44, d = 2.1 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*250*0.44*2.1 | Answer: 231000 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 430 mm is turned at 950 rpm with a feed of 0.22 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 430, N = 950, f = 0.22 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 430 / (0.22*950) | Answer: 2.057 min

question: A resistor of 124 ohm carries a current of 9.5 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 124, I = 9.5 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 9.5 * 124 | Answer: 1178 V

question: Three resistors 50 ohm, 62 ohm and 52 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 50, R2 = 62, R3 = 52 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 50 + 62 + 52 | Answer: 164 ohm

question: Two resistors 93 ohm and 10 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 93, R2 = 10 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 93*10 / (93+10) | Answer: 9.029 ohm

question: A device draws 7.2 A at 235 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 235, I = 7.2 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 235 * 7.2 | Answer: 1692 W

question: A current of 7.1 A flows through a 10 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 7.1, R = 10 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (7.1)^2 * 10 | Answer: 504.1 W

question: Two capacitors 44.2 uF and 25.8 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 44.2, C2 = 25.8 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 44.2*25.8 / (44.2+25.8) | Answer: 16.29 uF

question: A resistor 91 kohm and capacitor 2.6 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 91, C = 2.6 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (91k)(2.6u) = 236.6 ms | Answer: 236.6 ms

question: An inductor 287 mH is in series with 107 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 287, R = 107 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (287e-3) / 107 | Answer: 2.682 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 153.9 mH inductor at 540 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 153.9, f = 540 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (540)(153.9e-3) | Answer: 522.2 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 23.5 uF capacitor at 500 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 23.5, f = 500 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (500)(23.5e-6)) | Answer: 13.55 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 99 ohm, XL = 58 ohm and XC = 127 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 99, XL = 58, XC = 127 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(99^2 + (58 - 127)^2) | Answer: 120.7 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 94.4 mH and C = 0.3 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 94.4, C = 0.3 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(94.4e-3 * 0.3e-6)) | Answer: 945.7 Hz

question: A capacitor of 44.9 uF is charged to 205 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 44.9, V = 205 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*44.9e-6*(205)^2 | Answer: 943.5 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 140 V with 610 primary turns and 250 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 140, N1 = 610, N2 = 250 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 140 * 250/610 | Answer: 57.38 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 170 V and draws an armature current of 11 A. If the armature resistance is 0.11 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 170, Ia = 11, Ra = 0.11 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 170 - 11*0.11 | Answer: 168.8 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 10 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.97. Find the total real power in kW.
