question: A rectangular column (47 mm x 110 mm) has effective length 4000 mm and E = 200 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 370 MPa is designed for a working stress of 90 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 370, sw = 90 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 370 / 90 | Answer: 4.111

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 800 mm and wall thickness 16 mm carries an internal pressure of 2.1 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 800, t = 16, P = 2.1 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 2.1*800 / (2*16) | Answer: 52.5 MPa

question: 5.8 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 75 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 5.8, dT = 75 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 5.8 * 0.718 * 75 | Answer: 312.3 kJ

question: 1.1 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 65 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1.1, dT = 65 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 1.1 * 1.005 * 65 | Answer: 71.86 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 3 m^3 at 570 K with mass 3 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 3, Tk = 570, m = 3 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 3*0.287*570 / 3 | Answer: 163.6 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 1.5 kg of air expands isothermally at 380 K from volume V1 to 3*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1.5, Tk = 380, ratio = 3 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 1.5*0.287*380*ln(3) | Answer: 179.7 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 4.6 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.39 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 4.6, D = 0.39 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*4.6*0.39 / 0.001 | Answer: 1794000

question: Water flows at 2.1 m/s through a pipe of diameter 150 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 7.1 m. Taking Cv = 0.98, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 7.1, cv = 0.98 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.98*sqrt(2*9.81*7.1) | Answer: 11.57 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 210 mm) water flows at 1.9 m/s. It contracts to diameter 100 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
Water flows at 3.1 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.43 m and length 50 m. With friction factor f = 0.021, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 29 teeth drives a gear of 72 teeth. If the pinion runs at 850 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 29, z2 = 72, N1 = 850 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 850*29 / 72 | Answer: 342.4 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 400 mm rotates at 600 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 400, N = 600 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.4)*600 / 60 | Answer: 12.57 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 40.4 kW at 200 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 40.4, N = 200 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(40.4*1000) / (2*pi*200) | Answer: 1929 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 9.7 kg rotates at radius 0.46 m at 600 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 16400 N/m and mass 6.4 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 16400, m = 6.4 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(16400/6.4) | Answer: 8.057 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 2.5 m^2 and thickness 0.32 m has conductivity k = 18.2 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 95 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 2.5, L = 0.32, k = 18.2, dT = 95 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 18.2*2.5*95 / 0.32 | Answer: 13508 W

question: A surface of area 5.4 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 150 W/m^2-K to surroundings 130 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 5.4, h = 150, dT = 130 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 150*5.4*130 | Answer: 105300 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 60 m/min, feed = 0.34 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2.6 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 60, f = 0.34, d = 2.6 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*60*0.34*2.6 | Answer: 53040 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 340 mm is turned at 1100 rpm with a feed of 0.34 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 340, N = 1100, f = 0.34 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 340 / (0.34*1100) | Answer: 0.9091 min

question: A resistor of 78 ohm carries a current of 6.1 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 78, I = 6.1 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 6.1 * 78 | Answer: 475.8 V

question: Three resistors 25 ohm, 19 ohm and 57 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 25, R2 = 19, R3 = 57 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 25 + 19 + 57 | Answer: 101 ohm

question: Two resistors 89 ohm and 54 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 89, R2 = 54 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 89*54 / (89+54) | Answer: 33.61 ohm

question: A device draws 11.7 A at 230 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 230, I = 11.7 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 230 * 11.7 | Answer: 2691 W

question: A current of 5.4 A flows through a 138 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 5.4, R = 138 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (5.4)^2 * 138 | Answer: 4024 W

question: Two capacitors 16.2 uF and 31.6 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 16.2, C2 = 31.6 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 16.2*31.6 / (16.2+31.6) | Answer: 10.71 uF

question: A resistor 22 kohm and capacitor 19.9 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 22, C = 19.9 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (22k)(19.9u) = 437.8 ms | Answer: 437.8 ms

question: An inductor 204.7 mH is in series with 173 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 204.7, R = 173 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (204.7e-3) / 173 | Answer: 1.183 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 105.3 mH inductor at 570 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 105.3, f = 570 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (570)(105.3e-3) | Answer: 377.1 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 2.3 uF capacitor at 870 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 2.3, f = 870 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (870)(2.3e-6)) | Answer: 79.54 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 93 ohm, XL = 137 ohm and XC = 114 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 93, XL = 137, XC = 114 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(93^2 + (137 - 114)^2) | Answer: 95.8 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 96.6 mH and C = 1 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 96.6, C = 1 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(96.6e-3 * 1e-6)) | Answer: 512.1 Hz

question: A capacitor of 89.1 uF is charged to 215 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 89.1, V = 215 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*89.1e-6*(215)^2 | Answer: 2059 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 420 V with 780 primary turns and 130 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 420, N1 = 780, N2 = 130 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 420 * 130/780 | Answer: 70 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 290 V and draws an armature current of 33 A. If the armature resistance is 0.84 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 290, Ia = 33, Ra = 0.84 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 290 - 33*0.84 | Answer: 262.3 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 180 A at 433 V (line) with a power factor of 0.76. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 180, VL = 433, pf = 0.76 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*433*180*0.76 / 1000 | Answer: 102.6 kW

question: A load has real power 80 kW and apparent power 110 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 80, S = 110 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 80 / 110 | Answer: 0.7273

question: A machine delivers 120 kW output while drawing 167 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 120, Pi = 167 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 120/167 * 100 | Answer: 71.86 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 22 V across R1 = 34 ohm and R2 = 20 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 22, R1 = 34, R2 = 20 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 22*20 / (34+20) | Answer: 8.148 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 10 kohm and Rin = 9 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 10, Rin = 9 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 10 / 9 | Answer: 1.111

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 40 kohm and Rg = 45 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 40, Rg = 45 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 40/45 | Answer: 1.889

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 7233. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 7233 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(7233) | Answer: 38.59 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.8 m carries a central point load of 30 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 9.8, W = 30 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 30*9.8 / 4 | Answer: 73.5 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 3.8 m carries a UDL of 10 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.8, w = 10 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 10*(3.8)^2 / 8 | Answer: 18.05 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 5.1 m carries a point load 55 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.1, W = 55 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 55*5.1 | Answer: 280.5 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 4.2 m carries a UDL of 24 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.2, w = 24 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 24*(4.2)^2 / 2 | Answer: 211.7 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.6 m carries a point load 15 kN at distance 3 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 9.6, a = 3, W = 15 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 15*(9.6 - 3) / 9.6 | Answer: 10.31 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 3 m) carries a central point load 20 kN. With E = 30 GPa and I = 590e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=20000 N, L=3000.0 mm, E=30000 MPa, I=590e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 0.6356 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 5.4 m carries a UDL of 9 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.4, w = 9 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 9*(5.4)^2 / 12 | Answer: 21.87 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 540 mm, clear cover 40 mm and main bars of diameter 12 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 540, c = 40, dia = 12 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 540 - 40 - 12/2 | Answer: 494 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 29.3 m^2 carrying a factored load of 14.4 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 29.3, w = 14.4 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 14.4 * 29.3 | Answer: 421.9 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 4.4 m, unit weight 16 kN/m^3, phi = 38 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 3.8e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.4, area = 6.8e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 3.8, i = 0.4, A = 6.8 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (3.8e-4)*0.4*(6.8e-3) | Answer: 1034 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 2 m, bed slope 0.01 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.018. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 4.7 m under a head of 0.8 m. Taking Cd = 0.62 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 4.2 m wide carries a discharge of 20.5 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 210 m and design speed 85 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 210, V = 85 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (85)^2 / (127*210) | Answer: 0.2709
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: A tank of volume 170 m^3 treats a flow of 175 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 170, Q = 175 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 170 / 175 | Answer: 0.9714 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 350 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.13 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 8 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 350, k = 0.13, t = 8 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 350*(1 - e^(-0.13*8)) | Answer: 226.3 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.51, rainfall intensity 110 mm/h over a catchment of 22.6 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.51, i = 110, A = 22.6 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.51*110*22.6 / 360 | Answer: 3.522 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.02 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 640 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.02, M = 640 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 640*(30+0.02)/30 | Answer: 640.4 m

question: Convert the decimal number 236 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 236 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: EC (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 11000110 and 01100110.
solution: XOR: 10100000 | Count of 1s = 2 | Answer: 2
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 120 megabits is sent over a link of 42 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 120, B = 42 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 120 / 42 | Answer: 2.857 s

question: A link has bandwidth 55 Mbps and round-trip time 30 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 55, R = 30 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 55e6 * 30e-3 bits = 1650 kb | Answer: 1650 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.85, cache access time 9 ns and main-memory access time 180 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.85, tc = 9, tm = 180 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.85*9 + (1 - 0.85)*180 | Answer: 34.65 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 747377 elements?
solution: Given: n = 747377 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(747377)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.015, memory access time 180 ns and page-fault service time 5 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 5 ms = 5000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.015)*180 + 0.015*5000000.0 ns | Answer: 75.18 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 2.6 m^3 at 410 kPa and 560 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 2.6, P = 410, Tk = 560 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (410e3)*2.6 / (8.314*560) | Answer: 229 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.23 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 5 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.23, t = 5 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.23*5) | Answer: 0.6834

question: For a reaction with A = 5e10 /s and activation energy 65 kJ/mol at 360 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 5, Ea = 65, Tk = 360 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 5e10 * exp(-65e3 / (8.314*360)) | Answer: 18.51 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.93 and bottoms xW = 0.02, with relative volatility alpha = 2.2. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.93, xw = 0.02, al = 2.2 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.93/0.07)(0.98/0.02)] / ln(2.2) | Answer: 8.217 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.61 and x = 0.32. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.61, x = 0.32 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.61/0.39) / (0.32/0.68) | Answer: 3.324

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.7 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 105 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.7, Psat = 105 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.7 * 105 | Answer: 73.5 kPa

question: A stream of 4.9 kg/s with specific heat 3.6 kJ/kg-K is heated through 115 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 4.9, cp = 3.6, dT = 115 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 4.9*3.6*115 | Answer: 2029 kW

question: A reactor of volume 1.2 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 4.8 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 1.2, Q = 4.8 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 1.2 / 4.8 | Answer: 0.25 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 6.2e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 2 mm with a concentration difference of 30 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 6.2, L = 2, dC = 30 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (6.2e-9)*30 / (2e-3) | Answer: 93 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 7.2 min and steady-state gain 1.3. For a step input of magnitude 13, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 7.2, K = 1.3, M = 13 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 1.3 * 13 | Answer: 16.9 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 95 m^2 flies at 210 m/s (air density 0.7 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 1.2. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 95, V = 210, rho = 0.7, CL = 1.2 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.7*(210)^2*95*1.2 / 1000 | Answer: 176 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 30 m^2 flies at 90 m/s (density 0.7 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.1. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 30, V = 90, rho = 0.7, CD = 0.1 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.7*(90)^2*30*0.1 / 1000 | Answer: 8.505 kN

question: A specimen under stress 340 MPa shows an elastic strain of 2.1e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 340, eps = 2.1 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 340 / (2.1e-3) MPa = 161.9 GPa | Answer: 161.9 GPa

question: A block of mass 13 kg has a volume of 5e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 13, V = 5 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 13 / (5e-3) | Answer: 2600 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 700 mm is heated through 95 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 11e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 700, dT = 95, al = 11 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 700*11e-6*95 | Answer: 0.7315 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 105 ohm, R2 = 145 ohm and R3 = 40 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 105, R2 = 145, R3 = 40 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 145*40 / 105 | Answer: 55.24 ohm

question: A measurement reads 9.03 when the true value is 10. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.03, true = 10 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.03 - 10| / 10 * 100 | Answer: 9.7 %

question: Annual demand is 42000 units, ordering cost 260 per order and holding cost 28 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 42000, S = 260, H = 28 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*42000*260 / 28) | Answer: 883.2 units

question: An asset costs 400000 with salvage value 18000 after 14 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 400000, Sv = 18000, n = 14 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (400000 - 18000) / 14 | Answer: 27286 per year

question: A product sells for 450 per unit with variable cost 50 per unit and fixed costs 55000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 450, V = 50, F = 55000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 55000 / (450 - 50) | Answer: 137.5 units

question: Find the present worth of 185000 received 5 years from now at an interest rate of 10% per year.
solution: Given: F = 185000, n = 5, i = 10 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 185000 / (1 + 0.1)^5 | Answer: 11487 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.93, 0.95 and 0.92 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.93, r2 = 0.95, r3 = 0.92 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.93*0.95*0.92 | Answer: 0.8128

question: A process produces 50 defective items in a batch of 12000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 50, N = 12000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 50/12000 * 1e6 | Answer: 4167 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = x^3 - 3x^2 - 6x + 8 evaluated at x = 3.
For f(x) = 2x^3 - 2x^2 + 7x + 5, find f''(x) at x = 2.
Evaluate the definite integral of (x^2 - 6x - 1) dx from x = 2 to x = 5.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = 1x^3/3 + -6x^2/2 + -1x | Evaluate F(5) - F(2) | Answer: -27
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 6x^2 - 7x - 2 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[0, 5], [5, 7]].
solution: Given: a = 0, b = 5, c = 5, d = 7 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (0)(7) - (5)(5) | Answer: -25

question: Find the determinant of [[4, -6, 1], [5, -1, -3], [4, 4, -5]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: 14

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[-3, -8], [-4, 7]].
solution: Trace tr = 4, Determinant = -53 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 9.55

question: Solve for x: -1x + 0y = 10 and -3x + 4y = -4.
solution: Determinant = -1*4 - 0*-3 = -4 | x = (e d - b f) / det = -10 | Answer: x = -10
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 10, 30, 99, 95, 53.
solution: Sum = 287 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 57.4 | Answer: 57.4

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 15, 35, 2, 50, 20.
solution: Mean = 24.4 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 18.56

question: Find the slope of the line through (2, 9) and (0, 1).
solution: Given: x1 = 2, y1 = 9, x2 = 0, y2 = 1 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (1 - 9) / (0 - 2) | Answer: 4

question: Find the distance between the points (-7, -1) and (-3, 5).
solution: Given: x1 = -7, y1 = -1, x2 = -3, y2 = 5 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((4)^2 + (6)^2) | Answer: 7.211 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (4,1), (-4,-3), (-2,8).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 40 sq units

question: Find the 21th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 14 and common difference 9.
solution: Given: a = 14, d = 9, n = 21 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = 14 + (21 - 1)*9 | Answer: 194

question: Find the sum of the first 17 terms of an AP with first term 3 and common difference -1.
solution: Given: a = 3, d = -1, n = 17 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 17/2 [2*3 + (17-1)*-1] | Answer: -85

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 25500 at 12.8% per annum for 6 years.
solution: Given: P = 25500, R = 12.8, Tt = 6 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 25500 * 12.8 * 6 / 100 | Answer: 19584 currency units

question: Find the amount when 28500 is invested at 10.9% per annum compounded annually for 6 years.
solution: Given: P = 28500, R = 10.9, Tt = 6 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 28500 * (1 + 10.9/100)^6 | Answer: 53019 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (8, 8, 1) and (6, 1, -2).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (-6, -4, 2) and (-2, 5, -3).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 43.95

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (-2, 2, -1) and (5, 4, 0).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 95.98 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number -2 + -5i.
solution: Given: a = -2, b = -5 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((-2)^2 + (-5)^2) | Answer: 5.385

question: Evaluate f(x) = -2x^3 - x^2 - 6x + 7 at x = -3.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-45 with initial guess x0=15, find x1 (one iteration).
solution: Given: N = 45, x0 = 15 | Formula: x1 = x0 - (x0^2 - N)/(2 x0) | Substitute: x1 = 15 - ((15)^2 - 45)/(2*15) | Answer: 9

question: Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.1 and ordinates 10, 6, 11, 10, 9, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 502 and 45.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 502 and 45 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 59 and 74.
solution: Given: a = 59, b = 74 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 59*74 / 1 | Answer: 4366
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 59 mm carries an axial tensile load of 112 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 39 mm and length 900 mm carries an axial load of 60 kN. Take E = 210 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 76 mm transmits a torque of 950 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 76, Tt = 950 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(950*1000) / (pi*(76)^3) | Answer: 11.02 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 33 mm and length 1700 mm carries a torque of 1950 N-m. With G = 77 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (33)^4 / 32 = 116428 mm^4 | theta = (1950*1000)(1700) / (77000 * 116428) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 21.19 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 126 mm wide and 270 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 126, h = 270 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 126*(270)^2 / 6 | Answer: 1530900 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (60 mm x 170 mm) carries a bending moment of 36 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (41 mm x 150 mm) has effective length 1800 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 890 MPa is designed for a working stress of 150 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 890, sw = 150 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 890 / 150 | Answer: 5.933

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1500 mm and wall thickness 8 mm carries an internal pressure of 2.3 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1500, t = 8, P = 2.3 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 2.3*1500 / (2*8) | Answer: 215.6 MPa

question: 7.6 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 40 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 7.6, dT = 40 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 7.6 * 0.718 * 40 | Answer: 218.3 kJ

question: 4.4 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 85 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.4, dT = 85 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 4.4 * 1.005 * 85 | Answer: 375.9 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 2 m^3 at 540 K with mass 5.8 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 2, Tk = 540, m = 5.8 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 5.8*0.287*540 / 2 | Answer: 449.4 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 1.1 kg of air expands isothermally at 500 K from volume V1 to 3*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1.1, Tk = 500, ratio = 3 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 1.1*0.287*500*ln(3) | Answer: 173.4 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 4.5 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.34 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 4.5, D = 0.34 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*4.5*0.34 / 0.001 | Answer: 1530000

question: Water flows at 2.2 m/s through a pipe of diameter 140 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 18.5 m. Taking Cv = 0.95, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 18.5, cv = 0.95 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.95*sqrt(2*9.81*18.5) | Answer: 18.1 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 300 mm) water flows at 2.2 m/s. It contracts to diameter 70 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 300, d2 = 70, V1 = 2.2 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 2.2*(300/70)^2 | Answer: 40.41 m/s

question: Water flows at 3.6 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.13 m and length 380 m. With friction factor f = 0.026, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 27 teeth drives a gear of 48 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1050 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 27, z2 = 48, N1 = 1050 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1050*27 / 48 | Answer: 590.6 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 560 mm rotates at 200 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 560, N = 200 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.56)*200 / 60 | Answer: 5.864 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 39.7 kW at 550 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 39.7, N = 550 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(39.7*1000) / (2*pi*550) | Answer: 689.3 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 7.7 kg rotates at radius 0.2 m at 650 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 19100 N/m and mass 1.7 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 19100, m = 1.7 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(19100/1.7) | Answer: 16.87 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 9.8 m^2 and thickness 0.25 m has conductivity k = 26.8 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 70 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 9.8, L = 0.25, k = 26.8, dT = 70 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 26.8*9.8*70 / 0.25 | Answer: 73539 W

question: A surface of area 2.8 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 185 W/m^2-K to surroundings 65 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 2.8, h = 185, dT = 65 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 185*2.8*65 | Answer: 33670 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 250 m/min, feed = 0.42 mm/rev, depth of cut = 1.6 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 250, f = 0.42, d = 1.6 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*250*0.42*1.6 | Answer: 168000 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 340 mm is turned at 800 rpm with a feed of 0.14 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 340, N = 800, f = 0.14 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 340 / (0.14*800) | Answer: 3.036 min

question: A resistor of 128 ohm carries a current of 5.4 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 128, I = 5.4 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 5.4 * 128 | Answer: 691.2 V

question: Three resistors 65 ohm, 11 ohm and 28 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 65, R2 = 11, R3 = 28 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 65 + 11 + 28 | Answer: 104 ohm

question: Two resistors 82 ohm and 6 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 82, R2 = 6 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 82*6 / (82+6) | Answer: 5.591 ohm

question: A device draws 13.9 A at 175 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 175, I = 13.9 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 175 * 13.9 | Answer: 2432 W

question: A current of 5.5 A flows through a 121 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 5.5, R = 121 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (5.5)^2 * 121 | Answer: 366 W

question: Two capacitors 19.2 uF and 29.5 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 19.2, C2 = 29.5 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 19.2*29.5 / (19.2+29.5) | Answer: 11.63 uF

question: A resistor 29 kohm and capacitor 0.3 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 29, C = 0.3 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (29k)(0.3u) = 8.7 ms | Answer: 8.7 ms

question: An inductor 443.3 mH is in series with 118 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 443.3, R = 118 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (443.3e-3) / 118 | Answer: 3.757 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 183.3 mH inductor at 600 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 183.3, f = 600 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (600)(183.3e-3) | Answer: 691 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 19.4 uF capacitor at 1000 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 19.4, f = 1000 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (1000)(19.4e-6)) | Answer: 8.204 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 78 ohm, XL = 44 ohm and XC = 129 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 78, XL = 44, XC = 129 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(78^2 + (44 - 129)^2) | Answer: 115.4 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 2.3 mH and C = 8.5 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 2.3, C = 8.5 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(2.3e-3 * 8.5e-6)) | Answer: 1138 Hz

question: A capacitor of 88.8 uF is charged to 190 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 88.8, V = 190 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*88.8e-6*(190)^2 | Answer: 1603 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 180 V with 950 primary turns and 470 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 180, N1 = 950, N2 = 470 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 180 * 470/950 | Answer: 89.05 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 130 V and draws an armature current of 42 A. If the armature resistance is 1.46 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 130, Ia = 42, Ra = 1.46 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 130 - 42*1.46 | Answer: 68.68 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 90 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.8. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 90, VL = 400, pf = 0.8 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*400*90*0.8 / 1000 | Answer: 49.88 kW

question: A machine delivers 30 kW output while drawing 117 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 30, Pi = 117 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 30/117 * 100 | Answer: 25.64 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 18 V across R1 = 43 ohm and R2 = 46 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 18, R1 = 43, R2 = 46 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 18*46 / (43+46) | Answer: 9.303 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 200 kohm and Rin = 7 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 200, Rin = 7 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 200 / 7 | Answer: 28.57

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 140 kohm and Rg = 37 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 140, Rg = 37 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 140/37 | Answer: 4.784

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 8547. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 8547 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(8547) | Answer: 39.32 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 3 m carries a central point load of 70 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3, W = 70 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 70*3 / 4 | Answer: 52.5 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 10 m carries a UDL of 60 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 10, w = 60 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 60*(10)^2 / 8 | Answer: 750 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 2.5 m carries a point load 65 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 2.5, W = 65 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 65*2.5 | Answer: 162.5 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 3.1 m carries a UDL of 8 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.1, w = 8 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 8*(3.1)^2 / 2 | Answer: 38.44 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.6 m carries a point load 15 kN at distance 3.8 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 4.6, a = 3.8, W = 15 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 15*(4.6 - 3.8) / 4.6 | Answer: 2.609 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 7.8 m) carries a central point load 15 kN. With E = 25 GPa and I = 380e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=15000 N, L=7800.0 mm, E=25000 MPa, I=380e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 15.61 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 7.4 m carries a UDL of 30 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7.4, w = 30 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 30*(7.4)^2 / 12 | Answer: 136.9 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 610 mm, clear cover 50 mm and main bars of diameter 16 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 610, c = 50, dia = 16 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 610 - 50 - 16/2 | Answer: 552 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 22.7 m^2 carrying a factored load of 16 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 22.7, w = 16 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 16 * 22.7 | Answer: 363.2 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 4.3 m, unit weight 16 kN/m^3, phi = 38 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 3.4e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1.2, area = 6e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 3.4, i = 1.2, A = 6 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (3.4e-4)*1.2*(6e-3) | Answer: 2448 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 0.9 m, bed slope 0.009 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.013. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 5 m under a head of 1.1 m. Taking Cd = 0.63 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 2.8 m wide carries a discharge of 22.8 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A tank of volume 220 m^3 treats a flow of 60 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 220, Q = 60 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 220 / 60 | Answer: 3.667 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 260 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.26 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 8 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 260, k = 0.26, t = 8 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 260*(1 - e^(-0.26*8)) | Answer: 227.5 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.76, rainfall intensity 90 mm/h over a catchment of 32 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.76, i = 90, A = 32 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.76*90*32 / 360 | Answer: 6.08 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.01 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 110 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.01, M = 110 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 110*(20+0.01)/20 | Answer: 110.1 m

question: Convert the decimal number 2232 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 2232 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 8B8 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 10100110 and 00001010.
solution: XOR: 10101100 | Count of 1s = 4 | Answer: 4
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 910 megabits is sent over a link of 39 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 910, B = 39 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 910 / 39 | Answer: 23.33 s

question: A link has bandwidth 77 Mbps and round-trip time 150 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 77, R = 150 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 77e6 * 150e-3 bits = 11550 kb | Answer: 11550 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.97, cache access time 10 ns and main-memory access time 170 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.97, tc = 10, tm = 170 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.97*10 + (1 - 0.97)*170 | Answer: 14.8 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 718224 elements?
solution: Given: n = 718224 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(718224)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.018, memory access time 130 ns and page-fault service time 7 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 7 ms = 7000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.018)*130 + 0.018*7000000.0 ns | Answer: 126.1 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 0.3 m^3 at 280 kPa and 550 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 0.3, P = 280, Tk = 550 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (280e3)*0.3 / (8.314*550) | Answer: 18.37 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.31 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 11 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.31, t = 11 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.31*11) | Answer: 0.967

question: For a reaction with A = 1e10 /s and activation energy 85 kJ/mol at 490 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 1, Ea = 85, Tk = 490 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 1e10 * exp(-85e3 / (8.314*490)) | Answer: 8.681 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.97 and bottoms xW = 0.02, with relative volatility alpha = 1.6. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.97, xw = 0.02, al = 1.6 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.97/0.03)(0.98/0.02)] / ln(1.6) | Answer: 15.68 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.82 and x = 0.42. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.82, x = 0.42 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.82/0.18) / (0.42/0.58) | Answer: 6.291

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.53 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 105 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.53, Psat = 105 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.53 * 105 | Answer: 55.65 kPa

question: A stream of 3.5 kg/s with specific heat 2.3 kJ/kg-K is heated through 10 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 3.5, cp = 2.3, dT = 10 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 3.5*2.3*10 | Answer: 80.5 kW

question: A reactor of volume 15.6 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 3.3 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 15.6, Q = 3.3 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 15.6 / 3.3 | Answer: 4.727 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 8.5e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 2 mm with a concentration difference of 30 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 8.5, L = 2, dC = 30 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (8.5e-9)*30 / (2e-3) | Answer: 127.5 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 9.5 min and steady-state gain 2.4. For a step input of magnitude 14, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 9.5, K = 2.4, M = 14 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 2.4 * 14 | Answer: 33.6 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 20 m^2 flies at 100 m/s (air density 0.7 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.5. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 20, V = 100, rho = 0.7, CL = 0.5 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.7*(100)^2*20*0.5 / 1000 | Answer: 35 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 95 m^2 flies at 90 m/s (density 0.7 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.1. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 95, V = 90, rho = 0.7, CD = 0.1 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.7*(90)^2*95*0.1 / 1000 | Answer: 26.93 kN

question: A specimen under stress 250 MPa shows an elastic strain of 1.8e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 250, eps = 1.8 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 250 / (1.8e-3) MPa = 138.9 GPa | Answer: 138.9 GPa

question: A block of mass 10 kg has a volume of 1.8e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 10, V = 1.8 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 10 / (1.8e-3) | Answer: 5556 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 1400 mm is heated through 30 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 12e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 1400, dT = 30, al = 12 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 1400*12e-6*30 | Answer: 0.504 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 135 ohm, R2 = 65 ohm and R3 = 390 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 135, R2 = 65, R3 = 390 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 65*390 / 135 | Answer: 187.8 ohm

question: A measurement reads 9.53 when the true value is 10. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.53, true = 10 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.53 - 10| / 10 * 100 | Answer: 4.7 %

question: Annual demand is 46000 units, ordering cost 220 per order and holding cost 35 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 46000, S = 220, H = 35 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*46000*220 / 35) | Answer: 760.5 units

question: An asset costs 200000 with salvage value 6000 after 7 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 200000, Sv = 6000, n = 7 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (200000 - 6000) / 7 | Answer: 27714 per year

question: A product sells for 440 per unit with variable cost 30 per unit and fixed costs 85000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 440, V = 30, F = 85000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 85000 / (440 - 30) | Answer: 207.3 units

question: Find the present worth of 175000 received 8 years from now at an interest rate of 5% per year.
solution: Given: F = 175000, n = 8, i = 5 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 175000 / (1 + 0.05)^8 | Answer: 118447 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.94, 0.94 and 0.91 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.94, r2 = 0.94, r3 = 0.91 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.94*0.94*0.91 | Answer: 0.8041

question: A process produces 30 defective items in a batch of 5500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 30, N = 5500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 30/5500 * 1e6 | Answer: 5455 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = 3x^3 + 6x^2 + 4x - 5 evaluated at x = 2.
For f(x) = -x^3 + 7x^2 - x + 5, find f''(x) at x = 4.
Evaluate the definite integral of (-x^2 - 6x - 2) dx from x = -4 to x = 5.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = -1x^3/3 + -6x^2/2 + -2x | Evaluate F(5) - F(-4) | Answer: -108
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of x^2 + 3x - 2 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[-3, -4], [5, -2]].
solution: Given: a = -3, b = -4, c = 5, d = -2 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (-3)(-2) - (-4)(5) | Answer: 26

question: Find the determinant of [[-1, 0, 3], [-6, 1, 4], [-3, 5, 3]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: -64

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[5, -1], [-1, -6]].
solution: Trace tr = -1, Determinant = -31 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 5.09

question: Solve for x: 4x + 4y = 3 and 1x + 2y = 0.
solution: Determinant = 4*2 - 4*1 = 4 | x = (e d - b f) / det = 1.5 | Answer: x = 1.5
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 25, 78, 22, 73, 69.
solution: Sum = 267 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 53.4 | Answer: 53.4

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 48, 36, 36, 28, 19.
solution: Mean = 33.4 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 10.76

question: Find the slope of the line through (2, -5) and (0, 2).
solution: Given: x1 = 2, y1 = -5, x2 = 0, y2 = 2 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (2 - -5) / (0 - 2) | Answer: -3.5

question: Find the distance between the points (5, 6) and (4, 8).
solution: Given: x1 = 5, y1 = 6, x2 = 4, y2 = 8 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-1)^2 + (2)^2) | Answer: 2.236 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (-4,-7), (7,-8), (-1,-1).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 34.5 sq units

question: Find the 11th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 11 and common difference -7.
solution: Given: a = 11, d = -7, n = 11 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = 11 + (11 - 1)*-7 | Answer: -59

question: Find the sum of the first 23 terms of an AP with first term 15 and common difference -7.
solution: Given: a = 15, d = -7, n = 23 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 23/2 [2*15 + (23-1)*-7] | Answer: -1426

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 23000 at 9.6% per annum for 4 years.
solution: Given: P = 23000, R = 9.6, Tt = 4 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 23000 * 9.6 * 4 / 100 | Answer: 8832 currency units

question: Find the amount when 6500 is invested at 6.7% per annum compounded annually for 6 years.
solution: Given: P = 6500, R = 6.7, Tt = 6 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 6500 * (1 + 6.7/100)^6 | Answer: 9592 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (6, 7, 1) and (-5, -2, -1).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (-4, 1, -2) and (1, 6, -6).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 36.57

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (-3, 5, -1) and (3, -6, -6).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 128.3 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number 11 + -1i.
solution: Given: a = 11, b = -1 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((11)^2 + (-1)^2) | Answer: 11.05

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number -6 + -8i.
solution: Given: a = -6, b = -8 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(-8, -6) | Answer: -126.9 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -5x^3 + 3x^2 - 7x + 6 at x = 2.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-132 with initial guess x0=9, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.3 and ordinates 3, 11, 4, 7, 7, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 299 and 463.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 299 and 463 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 31 and 50.
solution: Given: a = 31, b = 50 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 31*50 / 1 | Answer: 1550
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 32 mm carries an axial tensile load of 66 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 37 mm and length 1600 mm carries an axial load of 76 kN. Take E = 200 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 69 mm transmits a torque of 200 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 69, Tt = 200 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(200*1000) / (pi*(69)^3) | Answer: 3.101 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 50 mm and length 1500 mm carries a torque of 900 N-m. With G = 77 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (50)^4 / 32 = 613592 mm^4 | theta = (900*1000)(1500) / (77000 * 613592) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 1.637 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 122 mm wide and 200 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 122, h = 200 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 122*(200)^2 / 6 | Answer: 813333 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (99 mm x 80 mm) carries a bending moment of 35 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (68 mm x 110 mm) has effective length 3700 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 520 MPa is designed for a working stress of 130 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 520, sw = 130 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 520 / 130 | Answer: 4

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1400 mm and wall thickness 15 mm carries an internal pressure of 0.8 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1400, t = 15, P = 0.8 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 0.8*1400 / (2*15) | Answer: 37.33 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 780 K and 440 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 780, Tc = 440 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 440/780) * 100 | Answer: 43.59 %

question: 2 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 75 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2, dT = 75 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 2 * 0.718 * 75 | Answer: 107.7 kJ

question: 3.2 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 40 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.2, dT = 40 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 3.2 * 1.005 * 40 | Answer: 128.6 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 3.6 m^3 at 490 K with mass 1.2 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 3.6, Tk = 490, m = 1.2 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 1.2*0.287*490 / 3.6 | Answer: 46.88 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 4.5 kg of air expands isothermally at 480 K from volume V1 to 3*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.5, Tk = 480, ratio = 3 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 4.5*0.287*480*ln(3) | Answer: 681.1 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 4 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.27 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 4, D = 0.27 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*4*0.27 / 0.001 | Answer: 1080000

question: Water flows at 0.9 m/s through a pipe of diameter 100 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 6.5 m. Taking Cv = 0.97, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 6.5, cv = 0.97 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.97*sqrt(2*9.81*6.5) | Answer: 10.95 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 350 mm) water flows at 1.6 m/s. It contracts to diameter 100 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 350, d2 = 100, V1 = 1.6 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 1.6*(350/100)^2 | Answer: 19.6 m/s

question: Water flows at 3.2 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.13 m and length 270 m. With friction factor f = 0.035, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 40 teeth drives a gear of 68 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1250 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 40, z2 = 68, N1 = 1250 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1250*40 / 68 | Answer: 735.3 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 140 mm rotates at 250 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 140, N = 250 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.14)*250 / 60 | Answer: 1.833 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 21.3 kW at 1500 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 21.3, N = 1500 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(21.3*1000) / (2*pi*1500) | Answer: 135.6 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 8 kg rotates at radius 0.36 m at 650 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 7700 N/m and mass 6.6 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 7700, m = 6.6 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(7700/6.6) | Answer: 5.436 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 4.1 m^2 and thickness 0.36 m has conductivity k = 19.9 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 110 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 4.1, L = 0.36, k = 19.9, dT = 110 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 19.9*4.1*110 / 0.36 | Answer: 2493 W

question: A surface of area 3.8 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 155 W/m^2-K to surroundings 100 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 3.8, h = 155, dT = 100 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 155*3.8*100 | Answer: 58900 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 190 m/min, feed = 0.13 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 190, f = 0.13, d = 2 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*190*0.13*2 | Answer: 49400 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 110 mm is turned at 300 rpm with a feed of 0.39 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 110, N = 300, f = 0.39 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 110 / (0.39*300) | Answer: 0.9402 min

question: A resistor of 8 ohm carries a current of 1.8 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 8, I = 1.8 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 1.8 * 8 | Answer: 14.4 V

question: Three resistors 85 ohm, 32 ohm and 17 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 85, R2 = 32, R3 = 17 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 85 + 32 + 17 | Answer: 134 ohm

question: Two resistors 34 ohm and 3 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 34, R2 = 3 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 34*3 / (34+3) | Answer: 2.757 ohm

question: A device draws 6 A at 40 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 40, I = 6 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 40 * 6 | Answer: 240 W

question: A current of 4.6 A flows through a 50 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 4.6, R = 50 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (4.6)^2 * 50 | Answer: 1058 W

question: Two capacitors 5.1 uF and 7.4 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 5.1, C2 = 7.4 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 5.1*7.4 / (5.1+7.4) | Answer: 3.019 uF

question: A resistor 89 kohm and capacitor 3.6 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 89, C = 3.6 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (89k)(3.6u) = 320.4 ms | Answer: 320.4 ms

question: An inductor 486.4 mH is in series with 182 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 486.4, R = 182 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (486.4e-3) / 182 | Answer: 2.673 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 21.3 mH inductor at 350 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 21.3, f = 350 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (350)(21.3e-3) | Answer: 46.84 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 26.7 uF capacitor at 960 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 26.7, f = 960 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (960)(26.7e-6)) | Answer: 6.209 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 45 ohm, XL = 138 ohm and XC = 114 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 45, XL = 138, XC = 114 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(45^2 + (138 - 114)^2) | Answer: 51 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 42.8 mH and C = 6.1 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 42.8, C = 6.1 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(42.8e-3 * 6.1e-6)) | Answer: 311.5 Hz

question: A capacitor of 74.8 uF is charged to 350 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 74.8, V = 350 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*74.8e-6*(350)^2 | Answer: 4581 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 300 V with 380 primary turns and 40 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 300, N1 = 380, N2 = 40 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 300 * 40/380 | Answer: 31.58 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 430 V and draws an armature current of 13 A. If the armature resistance is 1.04 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 430, Ia = 13, Ra = 1.04 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 430 - 13*1.04 | Answer: 416.5 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 25 A at 433 V (line) with a power factor of 0.89. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 25, VL = 433, pf = 0.89 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*433*25*0.89 / 1000 | Answer: 16.69 kW

question: A load has real power 90 kW and apparent power 150 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 90, S = 150 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 90 / 150 | Answer: 0.6

question: A machine delivers 25 kW output while drawing 117 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 25, Pi = 117 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 25/117 * 100 | Answer: 21.37 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 27 V across R1 = 33 ohm and R2 = 3 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 27, R1 = 33, R2 = 3 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 27*3 / (33+3) | Answer: 2.25 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 20 kohm and Rin = 38 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 20, Rin = 38 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 20 / 38 | Answer: 0.5263

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 120 kohm and Rg = 24 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 120, Rg = 24 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 120/24 | Answer: 6

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 1107. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 1107 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(1107) | Answer: 30.44 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 5.3 m carries a central point load of 30 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.3, W = 30 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 30*5.3 / 4 | Answer: 39.75 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 5.4 m carries a UDL of 10 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.4, w = 10 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 10*(5.4)^2 / 8 | Answer: 36.45 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 1.9 m carries a point load 15 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 1.9, W = 15 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 15*1.9 | Answer: 28.5 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.1 m carries a point load 20 kN at distance 1.4 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 9.1, a = 1.4, W = 20 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 20*(9.1 - 1.4) / 9.1 | Answer: 16.92 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 6.3 m) carries a central point load 10 kN. With E = 30 GPa and I = 240e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=10000 N, L=6300.0 mm, E=30000 MPa, I=240e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 7.235 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 35.7 m^2 carrying a factored load of 9.5 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 35.7, w = 9.5 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 9.5 * 35.7 | Answer: 339.2 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 4.4 m, unit weight 19 kN/m^3, phi = 32 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 2.2e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1.4, area = 8e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 2.2, i = 1.4, A = 8 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (2.2e-4)*1.4*(8e-3) | Answer: 2464 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.9 m, bed slope 0.006 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.02. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 4.2 m under a head of 1.1 m. Taking Cd = 0.6 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 4.6 m wide carries a discharge of 29.7 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 140 m and design speed 100 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 140, V = 100 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (100)^2 / (127*140) | Answer: 0.5624
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: A tank of volume 190 m^3 treats a flow of 85 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 190, Q = 85 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 190 / 85 | Answer: 2.235 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 280 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.3 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 5 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 280, k = 0.3, t = 5 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 280*(1 - e^(-0.3*5)) | Answer: 217.5 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.87, rainfall intensity 60 mm/h over a catchment of 5.2 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.87, i = 60, A = 5.2 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.87*60*5.2 / 360 | Answer: 0.754 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.05 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 600 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.05, M = 600 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 600*(30+0.05)/30 | Answer: 601 m

question: Convert the decimal number 1693 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 1693 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 69D (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 11000101 and 11010001.
solution: XOR: 00010100 | Count of 1s = 2 | Answer: 2
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 570 megabits is sent over a link of 52 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 570, B = 52 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 570 / 52 | Answer: 10.96 s

question: A link has bandwidth 86 Mbps and round-trip time 10 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 86, R = 10 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 86e6 * 10e-3 bits = 860 kb | Answer: 860 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.83, cache access time 10 ns and main-memory access time 150 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.83, tc = 10, tm = 150 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.83*10 + (1 - 0.83)*150 | Answer: 33.8 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 528218 elements?
solution: Given: n = 528218 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(528218)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.005, memory access time 160 ns and page-fault service time 3 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 3 ms = 3000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.005)*160 + 0.005*3000000.0 ns | Answer: 15.16 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 2.6 m^3 at 150 kPa and 490 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 2.6, P = 150, Tk = 490 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (150e3)*2.6 / (8.314*490) | Answer: 95.73 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.12 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 12 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.12, t = 12 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.12*12) | Answer: 0.7631

question: For a reaction with A = 8e10 /s and activation energy 80 kJ/mol at 300 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 8, Ea = 80, Tk = 300 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 8e10 * exp(-80e3 / (8.314*300)) | Answer: 0.0009405 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.9 and bottoms xW = 0.09, with relative volatility alpha = 3.1. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.9, xw = 0.09, al = 3.1 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.9/0.1)(0.91/0.09)] / ln(3.1) | Answer: 3.987 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.56 and x = 0.21. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.56, x = 0.21 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.56/0.44) / (0.21/0.79) | Answer: 4.788

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.53 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 100 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.53, Psat = 100 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.53 * 100 | Answer: 53 kPa

question: A stream of 8.8 kg/s with specific heat 3.3 kJ/kg-K is heated through 95 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 8.8, cp = 3.3, dT = 95 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 8.8*3.3*95 | Answer: 2759 kW

question: A reactor of volume 1.8 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 4.3 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 1.8, Q = 4.3 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 1.8 / 4.3 | Answer: 0.4186 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 7.9e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 2 mm with a concentration difference of 30 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 7.9, L = 2, dC = 30 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (7.9e-9)*30 / (2e-3) | Answer: 118.5 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 5.2 min and steady-state gain 1.8. For a step input of magnitude 7, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 5.2, K = 1.8, M = 7 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 1.8 * 7 | Answer: 12.6 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 45 m^2 flies at 250 m/s (air density 0.7 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.4. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 45, V = 250, rho = 0.7, CL = 0.4 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.7*(250)^2*45*0.4 / 1000 | Answer: 393.8 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 50 m^2 flies at 100 m/s (density 1.225 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.08. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 50, V = 100, rho = 1.225, CD = 0.08 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*1.225*(100)^2*50*0.08 / 1000 | Answer: 24.5 kN

question: A specimen under stress 230 MPa shows an elastic strain of 2.1e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 230, eps = 2.1 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 230 / (2.1e-3) MPa = 109.5 GPa | Answer: 109.5 GPa

question: A block of mass 46 kg has a volume of 3.9e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 46, V = 3.9 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 46 / (3.9e-3) | Answer: 11795 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 2200 mm is heated through 100 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 11e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 2200, dT = 100, al = 11 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 2200*11e-6*100 | Answer: 2.42 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 185 ohm, R2 = 80 ohm and R3 = 390 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 185, R2 = 80, R3 = 390 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 80*390 / 185 | Answer: 168.6 ohm

question: A measurement reads 10.52 when the true value is 50. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10.52, true = 50 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10.52 - 50| / 50 * 100 | Answer: 78.96 %

question: Annual demand is 8500 units, ordering cost 70 per order and holding cost 18 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 8500, S = 70, H = 18 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*8500*70 / 18) | Answer: 257.1 units

question: An asset costs 90000 with salvage value 16000 after 10 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 90000, Sv = 16000, n = 10 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (90000 - 16000) / 10 | Answer: 7400 per year

question: A product sells for 80 per unit with variable cost 50 per unit and fixed costs 25000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 80, V = 50, F = 25000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 25000 / (80 - 50) | Answer: 833.3 units

question: Find the present worth of 105000 received 7 years from now at an interest rate of 10% per year.
solution: Given: F = 105000, n = 7, i = 10 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 105000 / (1 + 0.1)^7 | Answer: 53882 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.96, 0.95 and 0.97 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.96, r2 = 0.95, r3 = 0.97 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.96*0.95*0.97 | Answer: 0.8846

question: A process produces 3 defective items in a batch of 2500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 3, N = 2500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 3/2500 * 1e6 | Answer: 1200 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -3x^3 + 3x^2 + 6x - 6 evaluated at x = -1.
For f(x) = -x^3 - 2x^2 - x - 8, find f''(x) at x = -4.
Evaluate the definite integral of (5x^2 - 2x - 2) dx from x = 0 to x = 5.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = 5x^3/3 + -2x^2/2 + -2x | Evaluate F(5) - F(0) | Answer: 173.3
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of x^2 + 3x - 11 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[-4, -4], [6, -5]].
solution: Given: a = -4, b = -4, c = 6, d = -5 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (-4)(-5) - (-4)(6) | Answer: 44

question: Find the determinant of [[-2, 2, -3], [-1, 5, -5], [-4, -6, 4]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: -10

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[-8, 3], [-6, 7]].
solution: Trace tr = -1, Determinant = -38 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 5.685

question: Solve for x: 1x + 0y = 2 and -5x + -2y = -1.
solution: Determinant = 1*-2 - 0*-5 = -2 | x = (e d - b f) / det = 2 | Answer: x = 2
