solution: Given: R1 = 82, R2 = 64, R3 = 46 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 82 + 64 + 46 | Answer: 192 ohm

question: Two resistors 87 ohm and 107 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 87, R2 = 107 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 87*107 / (87+107) | Answer: 47.98 ohm

question: A device draws 11.3 A at 190 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 190, I = 11.3 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 190 * 11.3 | Answer: 2147 W

question: A current of 6.3 A flows through a 7 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 6.3, R = 7 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (6.3)^2 * 7 | Answer: 277.8 W

question: Two capacitors 1.6 uF and 11.3 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 1.6, C2 = 11.3 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 1.6*11.3 / (1.6+11.3) | Answer: 1.402 uF

question: A resistor 15 kohm and capacitor 12.7 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 15, C = 12.7 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (15k)(12.7u) = 190.5 ms | Answer: 190.5 ms

question: An inductor 173.3 mH is in series with 149 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 173.3, R = 149 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (173.3e-3) / 149 | Answer: 1.163 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 15.3 mH inductor at 360 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 15.3, f = 360 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (360)(15.3e-3) | Answer: 34.61 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 39.3 uF capacitor at 800 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 39.3, f = 800 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (800)(39.3e-6)) | Answer: 5.062 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 66 ohm, XL = 142 ohm and XC = 116 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 66, XL = 142, XC = 116 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(66^2 + (142 - 116)^2) | Answer: 70.94 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 38.5 mH and C = 3.1 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 38.5, C = 3.1 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(38.5e-3 * 3.1e-6)) | Answer: 460.7 Hz

question: A capacitor of 18.1 uF is charged to 210 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 18.1, V = 210 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*18.1e-6*(210)^2 | Answer: 399.1 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 350 V with 810 primary turns and 210 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 350, N1 = 810, N2 = 210 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 350 * 210/810 | Answer: 90.74 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 290 V and draws an armature current of 10 A. If the armature resistance is 0.17 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 290, Ia = 10, Ra = 0.17 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 290 - 10*0.17 | Answer: 288.3 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 60 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.72. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 60, VL = 400, pf = 0.72 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*400*60*0.72 / 1000 | Answer: 29.93 kW

question: A load has real power 75 kW and apparent power 170 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 75, S = 170 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 75 / 170 | Answer: 0.4412

question: A machine delivers 50 kW output while drawing 137 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 50, Pi = 137 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 50/137 * 100 | Answer: 36.5 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 22 V across R1 = 35 ohm and R2 = 39 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 22, R1 = 35, R2 = 39 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 22*39 / (35+39) | Answer: 11.59 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 60 kohm and Rin = 25 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 60, Rin = 25 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 60 / 25 | Answer: 2.4

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 1657. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 1657 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(1657) | Answer: 32.19 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.8 m carries a central point load of 90 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6.8, W = 90 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 90*6.8 / 4 | Answer: 153 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 5.2 m carries a UDL of 55 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.2, w = 55 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 55*(5.2)^2 / 8 | Answer: 185.9 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 1.3 m carries a point load 20 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 1.3, W = 20 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 20*1.3 | Answer: 26 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 4.6 m carries a UDL of 6 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.6, w = 6 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 6*(4.6)^2 / 2 | Answer: 63.48 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 8.1 m carries a point load 100 kN at distance 2.5 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 8.1, a = 2.5, W = 100 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 100*(8.1 - 2.5) / 8.1 | Answer: 69.14 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 5.9 m) carries a central point load 80 kN. With E = 200 GPa and I = 330e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=80000 N, L=5900.0 mm, E=200000 MPa, I=330e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 5.186 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 8.8 m carries a UDL of 45 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 8.8, w = 45 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 45*(8.8)^2 / 12 | Answer: 290.4 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 690 mm, clear cover 50 mm and main bars of diameter 12 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 690, c = 50, dia = 12 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 690 - 50 - 12/2 | Answer: 634 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 21 m^2 carrying a factored load of 14.2 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 21, w = 14.2 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 14.2 * 21 | Answer: 298.2 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 6.7 m, unit weight 20 kN/m^3, phi = 30 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 2.6e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.8, area = 1.6e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 2.6, i = 0.8, A = 1.6 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (2.6e-4)*0.8*(1.6e-3) | Answer: 332.8 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.3 m, bed slope 0.006 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.017. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 3.3 m under a head of 0.6 m. Taking Cd = 0.6 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 4 m wide carries a discharge of 8.9 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 450 m and design speed 90 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 450, V = 90 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (90)^2 / (127*450) | Answer: 0.1417
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: A tank of volume 600 m^3 treats a flow of 115 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 600, Q = 115 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 600 / 115 | Answer: 5.217 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 350 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.21 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 6 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 350, k = 0.21, t = 6 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 350*(1 - e^(-0.21*6)) | Answer: 250.7 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.77, rainfall intensity 105 mm/h over a catchment of 53.5 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.77, i = 105, A = 53.5 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.77*105*53.5 / 360 | Answer: 12.02 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.01 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 670 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.01, M = 670 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 670*(20+0.01)/20 | Answer: 670.3 m

question: Convert the decimal number 3286 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 3286 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: CD6 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 00010001 and 10100100.
solution: XOR: 10110101 | Count of 1s = 5 | Answer: 5
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 380 megabits is sent over a link of 46 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 380, B = 46 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 380 / 46 | Answer: 8.261 s

question: A link has bandwidth 14 Mbps and round-trip time 40 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 14, R = 40 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 14e6 * 40e-3 bits = 560 kb | Answer: 560 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.93, cache access time 1 ns and main-memory access time 80 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.93, tc = 1, tm = 80 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.93*1 + (1 - 0.93)*80 | Answer: 6.53 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 839846 elements?
solution: Given: n = 839846 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(839846)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.01, memory access time 150 ns and page-fault service time 5 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 5 ms = 5000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.01)*150 + 0.01*5000000.0 ns | Answer: 50.15 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 0.3 m^3 at 300 kPa and 600 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 0.3, P = 300, Tk = 600 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (300e3)*0.3 / (8.314*600) | Answer: 18.04 mol

question: For a reaction with A = 4e10 /s and activation energy 85 kJ/mol at 390 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 4, Ea = 85, Tk = 390 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 4e10 * exp(-85e3 / (8.314*390)) | Answer: 0.1649 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.9 and bottoms xW = 0.1, with relative volatility alpha = 3. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.9, xw = 0.1, al = 3 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.9/0.1)(0.9/0.1)] / ln(3) | Answer: 4 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.75 and x = 0.42. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.75, x = 0.42 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.75/0.25) / (0.42/0.58) | Answer: 4.143

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.7 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 40 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.7, Psat = 40 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.7 * 40 | Answer: 28 kPa

question: A stream of 6.5 kg/s with specific heat 1.9 kJ/kg-K is heated through 75 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 6.5, cp = 1.9, dT = 75 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 6.5*1.9*75 | Answer: 926.2 kW

question: A reactor of volume 6.3 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 4.8 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 6.3, Q = 4.8 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 6.3 / 4.8 | Answer: 1.312 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 5.2e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 3 mm with a concentration difference of 70 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 5.2, L = 3, dC = 70 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (5.2e-9)*70 / (3e-3) | Answer: 121.3 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 7.4 min and steady-state gain 1.7. For a step input of magnitude 4, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 7.4, K = 1.7, M = 4 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 1.7 * 4 | Answer: 6.8 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 45 m^2 flies at 110 m/s (air density 0.7 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.5. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 45, V = 110, rho = 0.7, CL = 0.5 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.7*(110)^2*45*0.5 / 1000 | Answer: 95.29 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 70 m^2 flies at 130 m/s (density 1.225 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.12. Find the drag force in kN.
A specimen under stress 170 MPa shows an elastic strain of 1.7e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 170, eps = 1.7 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 170 / (1.7e-3) MPa = 100 GPa | Answer: 100 GPa

question: A block of mass 5 kg has a volume of 2.5e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 5, V = 2.5 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 5 / (2.5e-3) | Answer: 2000 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 900 mm is heated through 70 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 12e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 900, dT = 70, al = 12 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 900*12e-6*70 | Answer: 0.756 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 155 ohm, R2 = 180 ohm and R3 = 325 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 155, R2 = 180, R3 = 325 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 180*325 / 155 | Answer: 377.4 ohm

question: A measurement reads 9.38 when the true value is 20. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.38, true = 20 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.38 - 20| / 20 * 100 | Answer: 53.1 %

question: Annual demand is 10000 units, ordering cost 160 per order and holding cost 23 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 10000, S = 160, H = 23 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*10000*160 / 23) | Answer: 373 units

question: An asset costs 490000 with salvage value 36000 after 20 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 490000, Sv = 36000, n = 20 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (490000 - 36000) / 20 | Answer: 22700 per year

question: A product sells for 350 per unit with variable cost 180 per unit and fixed costs 185000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 350, V = 180, F = 185000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 185000 / (350 - 180) | Answer: 1088 units

question: Find the present worth of 160000 received 5 years from now at an interest rate of 12% per year.
solution: Given: F = 160000, n = 5, i = 12 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 160000 / (1 + 0.12)^5 | Answer: 90788 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.95, 0.93 and 0.98 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.95, r2 = 0.93, r3 = 0.98 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.95*0.93*0.98 | Answer: 0.8658

question: A process produces 49 defective items in a batch of 16000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 49, N = 16000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 49/16000 * 1e6 | Answer: 3062 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = 5x^3 + 2x^2 - 5x + 6 evaluated at x = 4.
For f(x) = -3x^3 + 5x^2 - 5x - 8, find f''(x) at x = -5.
Evaluate the definite integral of (-4x^2 + 6x - 6) dx from x = -1 to x = 4.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = -4x^3/3 + 6x^2/2 + -6x | Evaluate F(4) - F(-1) | Answer: -71.67
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 2x^2 + x - 1 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[-8, 9], [-1, -8]].
solution: Given: a = -8, b = 9, c = -1, d = -8 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (-8)(-8) - (9)(-1) | Answer: 73

question: Find the determinant of [[0, 0, -6], [3, 0, 4], [4, 6, 2]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: -108

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[6, 3], [2, -1]].
solution: Trace tr = 5, Determinant = -12 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 6.772

question: Solve for x: 4x + -6y = 9 and -1x + 3y = 2.
solution: Determinant = 4*3 - -6*-1 = 6 | x = (e d - b f) / det = 6.5 | Answer: x = 6.5
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 37, 63, 100, 53, 25.
solution: Sum = 278 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 55.6 | Answer: 55.6

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 41, 49, 19, 32, 27.
solution: Mean = 33.6 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 11.74

question: Find the slope of the line through (-4, 1) and (-5, 3).
solution: Given: x1 = -4, y1 = 1, x2 = -5, y2 = 3 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (3 - 1) / (-5 - -4) | Answer: -2

question: Find the distance between the points (9, -7) and (-1, 4).
solution: Given: x1 = 9, y1 = -7, x2 = -1, y2 = 4 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-10)^2 + (11)^2) | Answer: 14.87 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (1,7), (-1,-7), (3,1).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 20 sq units

question: Find the 20th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -18 and common difference -6.
solution: Given: a = -18, d = -6, n = 20 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -18 + (20 - 1)*-6 | Answer: -132

question: Find the sum of the first 13 terms of an AP with first term 13 and common difference -6.
solution: Given: a = 13, d = -6, n = 13 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 13/2 [2*13 + (13-1)*-6] | Answer: -299

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 45500 at 14.8% per annum for 6 years.
solution: Given: P = 45500, R = 14.8, Tt = 6 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 45500 * 14.8 * 6 / 100 | Answer: 40404 currency units

question: Find the amount when 34000 is invested at 5.3% per annum compounded annually for 6 years.
solution: Given: P = 34000, R = 5.3, Tt = 6 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 34000 * (1 + 5.3/100)^6 | Answer: 4635 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (5, 3, -1) and (4, -3, -6).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (-4, -4, 5) and (3, -4, 3).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 39.71

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (2, 2, -5) and (6, -3, 2).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 95.71 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number -3 + -2i.
solution: Given: a = -3, b = -2 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((-3)^2 + (-2)^2) | Answer: 3.606

question: Evaluate f(x) = -x^3 - 6x^2 + 7x + 6 at x = -4.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-15 with initial guess x0=4, find x1 (one iteration).
solution: Given: N = 15, x0 = 4 | Formula: x1 = x0 - (x0^2 - N)/(2 x0) | Substitute: x1 = 4 - ((4)^2 - 15)/(2*4) | Answer: 3.875

question: Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=2 and ordinates 6, 6, 8, 17, 16, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 481 and 259.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 481 and 259 | Answer: GCD = 37

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 20 and 38.
solution: Given: a = 20, b = 38 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 20*38 / 2 | Answer: 380
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 20 mm carries an axial tensile load of 97 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 32 mm and length 2200 mm carries an axial load of 10 kN. Take E = 200 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 31 mm transmits a torque of 1950 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 31, Tt = 1950 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(1950*1000) / (pi*(31)^3) | Answer: 333.4 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 49 mm and length 1200 mm carries a torque of 950 N-m. With G = 80 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (49)^4 / 32 = 565958 mm^4 | theta = (950*1000)(1200) / (80000 * 565958) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 1.443 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 134 mm wide and 210 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 134, h = 210 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 134*(210)^2 / 6 | Answer: 984900 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (68 mm x 150 mm) carries a bending moment of 15 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (58 mm x 140 mm) has effective length 3100 mm and E = 200 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 540 MPa is designed for a working stress of 70 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 540, sw = 70 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 540 / 70 | Answer: 7.714

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1400 mm and wall thickness 10 mm carries an internal pressure of 1.3 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1400, t = 10, P = 1.3 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 1.3*1400 / (2*10) | Answer: 91 MPa

question: 5.3 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 115 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 5.3, dT = 115 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 5.3 * 0.718 * 115 | Answer: 437.6 kJ

question: 7.9 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 95 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 7.9, dT = 95 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 7.9 * 1.005 * 95 | Answer: 754.3 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 1.8 m^3 at 470 K with mass 4.2 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 1.8, Tk = 470, m = 4.2 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 4.2*0.287*470 / 1.8 | Answer: 314.7 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 4.3 kg of air expands isothermally at 460 K from volume V1 to 4*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.3, Tk = 460, ratio = 4 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 4.3*0.287*460*ln(4) | Answer: 787 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 4.8 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.37 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 4.8, D = 0.37 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*4.8*0.37 / 0.001 | Answer: 1776000

question: Water flows at 4 m/s through a pipe of diameter 220 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 5.6 m. Taking Cv = 0.96, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 5.6, cv = 0.96 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.96*sqrt(2*9.81*5.6) | Answer: 10.06 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 290 mm) water flows at 2.8 m/s. It contracts to diameter 140 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
Water flows at 1.7 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.46 m and length 310 m. With friction factor f = 0.038, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 40 teeth drives a gear of 97 teeth. If the pinion runs at 300 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 40, z2 = 97, N1 = 300 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 300*40 / 97 | Answer: 123.7 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 420 mm rotates at 800 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 420, N = 800 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.42)*800 / 60 | Answer: 17.59 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 40 kW at 1150 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 40, N = 1150 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(40*1000) / (2*pi*1150) | Answer: 332.1 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 1.7 kg rotates at radius 0.51 m at 1200 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 10600 N/m and mass 7.6 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 10600, m = 7.6 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(10600/7.6) | Answer: 5.944 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 1.1 m^2 and thickness 0.31 m has conductivity k = 2.5 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 160 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 1.1, L = 0.31, k = 2.5, dT = 160 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 2.5*1.1*160 / 0.31 | Answer: 1419 W

question: A surface of area 5.2 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 10 W/m^2-K to surroundings 55 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 5.2, h = 10, dT = 55 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 10*5.2*55 | Answer: 2860 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 140 m/min, feed = 0.16 mm/rev, depth of cut = 1.4 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 140, f = 0.16, d = 1.4 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*140*0.16*1.4 | Answer: 31360 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 270 mm is turned at 650 rpm with a feed of 0.11 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 270, N = 650, f = 0.11 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 270 / (0.11*650) | Answer: 3.776 min

question: A resistor of 23 ohm carries a current of 0.1 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 23, I = 0.1 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 0.1 * 23 | Answer: 2.3 V

question: Three resistors 2 ohm, 47 ohm and 37 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 2, R2 = 47, R3 = 37 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 2 + 47 + 37 | Answer: 86 ohm

question: Two resistors 116 ohm and 115 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 116, R2 = 115 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 116*115 / (116+115) | Answer: 57.75 ohm

question: A device draws 4.1 A at 150 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 150, I = 4.1 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 150 * 4.1 | Answer: 615 W

question: A current of 5.6 A flows through a 32 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 5.6, R = 32 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (5.6)^2 * 32 | Answer: 1004 W

question: Two capacitors 4.2 uF and 23.1 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 4.2, C2 = 23.1 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 4.2*23.1 / (4.2+23.1) | Answer: 3.554 uF

question: A resistor 34 kohm and capacitor 2.6 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 34, C = 2.6 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (34k)(2.6u) = 88.4 ms | Answer: 88.4 ms

question: An inductor 330.2 mH is in series with 66 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 330.2, R = 66 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (330.2e-3) / 66 | Answer: 5.003 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 9.7 mH inductor at 150 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 9.7, f = 150 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (150)(9.7e-3) | Answer: 9.142 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 29.8 uF capacitor at 570 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 29.8, f = 570 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (570)(29.8e-6)) | Answer: 9.37 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 93 ohm, XL = 129 ohm and XC = 128 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 93, XL = 129, XC = 128 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(93^2 + (129 - 128)^2) | Answer: 93.01 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 90.9 mH and C = 0.5 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 90.9, C = 0.5 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(90.9e-3 * 0.5e-6)) | Answer: 746.5 Hz

question: A capacitor of 61.4 uF is charged to 50 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 61.4, V = 50 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*61.4e-6*(50)^2 | Answer: 76.75 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 110 V with 400 primary turns and 480 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 110, N1 = 400, N2 = 480 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 110 * 480/400 | Answer: 132 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 370 V and draws an armature current of 39 A. If the armature resistance is 0.7 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 370, Ia = 39, Ra = 0.7 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 370 - 39*0.7 | Answer: 342.7 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 10 A at 415 V (line) with a power factor of 0.7. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 10, VL = 415, pf = 0.7 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*415*10*0.7 / 1000 | Answer: 5.032 kW

question: A load has real power 125 kW and apparent power 160 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 125, S = 160 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 125 / 160 | Answer: 0.7812

question: A machine delivers 105 kW output while drawing 152 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 105, Pi = 152 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 105/152 * 100 | Answer: 69.08 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 6 V across R1 = 44 ohm and R2 = 46 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 6, R1 = 44, R2 = 46 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 6*46 / (44+46) | Answer: 3.067 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 220 kohm and Rin = 21 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 220, Rin = 21 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 220 / 21 | Answer: 10.48

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 130 kohm and Rg = 19 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 130, Rg = 19 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 130/19 | Answer: 7.842

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 8133. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 8133 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(8133) | Answer: 39.1 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.8 m carries a central point load of 60 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 9.8, W = 60 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 60*9.8 / 4 | Answer: 147 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.1 m carries a UDL of 15 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 9.1, w = 15 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 15*(9.1)^2 / 8 | Answer: 155.3 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 5.2 m carries a point load 60 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.2, W = 60 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 60*5.2 | Answer: 312 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 2.7 m carries a UDL of 40 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 2.7, w = 40 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 40*(2.7)^2 / 2 | Answer: 145.8 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 9 m carries a point load 35 kN at distance 1.4 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 9, a = 1.4, W = 35 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 35*(9 - 1.4) / 9 | Answer: 29.56 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 4.2 m) carries a central point load 30 kN. With E = 30 GPa and I = 150e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=30000 N, L=4200.0 mm, E=30000 MPa, I=150e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 10.29 mm

question: An RC beam has overall depth 490 mm, clear cover 50 mm and main bars of diameter 20 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 490, c = 50, dia = 20 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 490 - 50 - 20/2 | Answer: 430 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 18.2 m^2 carrying a factored load of 15.6 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 18.2, w = 15.6 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 15.6 * 18.2 | Answer: 283.9 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 4.9 m, unit weight 17 kN/m^3, phi = 35 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 5.9e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1.4, area = 6.7e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 5.9, i = 1.4, A = 6.7 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (5.9e-4)*1.4*(6.7e-3) | Answer: 5534 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 2.4 m, bed slope 0.002 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.024. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 1.6 m under a head of 1 m. Taking Cd = 0.62 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 3.5 m wide carries a discharge of 29.9 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 250 m and design speed 60 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 250, V = 60 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (60)^2 / (127*250) | Answer: 0.1134
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: A tank of volume 970 m^3 treats a flow of 75 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 970, Q = 75 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 970 / 75 | Answer: 12.93 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 380 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.27 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 5 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 380, k = 0.27, t = 5 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 380*(1 - e^(-0.27*5)) | Answer: 281.5 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.39, rainfall intensity 85 mm/h over a catchment of 20.1 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.39, i = 85, A = 20.1 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.39*85*20.1 / 360 | Answer: 1.851 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.07 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 390 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.07, M = 390 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 390*(30+0.07)/30 | Answer: 390.9 m

question: Convert the decimal number 549 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 549 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 225 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 11100101 and 10001011.
solution: XOR: 01101110 | Count of 1s = 5 | Answer: 5
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 120 megabits is sent over a link of 14 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 120, B = 14 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 120 / 14 | Answer: 8.571 s

question: A link has bandwidth 2 Mbps and round-trip time 70 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 2, R = 70 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 2e6 * 70e-3 bits = 140 kb | Answer: 140 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.86, cache access time 9 ns and main-memory access time 110 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.86, tc = 9, tm = 110 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.86*9 + (1 - 0.86)*110 | Answer: 23.14 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 706814 elements?
solution: Given: n = 706814 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(706814)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.019, memory access time 110 ns and page-fault service time 10 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 10 ms = 10000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.019)*110 + 0.019*10000000.0 ns | Answer: 190.1 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 2.7 m^3 at 160 kPa and 530 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 2.7, P = 160, Tk = 530 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (160e3)*2.7 / (8.314*530) | Answer: 98.04 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.26 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 10 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.26, t = 10 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.26*10) | Answer: 0.9257

question: For a reaction with A = 1e10 /s and activation energy 75 kJ/mol at 380 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 1, Ea = 75, Tk = 380 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 1e10 * exp(-75e3 / (8.314*380)) | Answer: 0.49 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.93 and bottoms xW = 0.04, with relative volatility alpha = 2.8. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.93, xw = 0.04, al = 2.8 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.93/0.07)(0.96/0.04)] / ln(2.8) | Answer: 5.599 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.83 and x = 0.26. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.83, x = 0.26 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.83/0.17) / (0.26/0.74) | Answer: 13.9

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.42 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 65 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.42, Psat = 65 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.42 * 65 | Answer: 27.3 kPa

question: A stream of 4.9 kg/s with specific heat 3.9 kJ/kg-K is heated through 85 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 4.9, cp = 3.9, dT = 85 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 4.9*3.9*85 | Answer: 1624 kW

question: A reactor of volume 5 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 2.7 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 5, Q = 2.7 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 5 / 2.7 | Answer: 1.852 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 3.4e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 4 mm with a concentration difference of 90 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 3.4, L = 4, dC = 90 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (3.4e-9)*90 / (4e-3) | Answer: 76.5 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 6.6 min and steady-state gain 3.2. For a step input of magnitude 8, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 6.6, K = 3.2, M = 8 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 3.2 * 8 | Answer: 25.6 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 45 m^2 flies at 190 m/s (air density 1 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.8. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 45, V = 190, rho = 1, CL = 0.8 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1*(190)^2*45*0.8 / 1000 | Answer: 649.8 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 80 m^2 flies at 70 m/s (density 0.4 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.05. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 80, V = 70, rho = 0.4, CD = 0.05 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.4*(70)^2*80*0.05 / 1000 | Answer: 3.92 kN

question: A specimen under stress 250 MPa shows an elastic strain of 1.1e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 250, eps = 1.1 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 250 / (1.1e-3) MPa = 227.3 GPa | Answer: 227.3 GPa

question: A block of mass 5 kg has a volume of 3.9e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 5, V = 3.9 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 5 / (3.9e-3) | Answer: 1282 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 3000 mm is heated through 45 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 17e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 3000, dT = 45, al = 17 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 3000*17e-6*45 | Answer: 2.295 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 135 ohm, R2 = 100 ohm and R3 = 125 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 135, R2 = 100, R3 = 125 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 100*125 / 135 | Answer: 92.59 ohm

question: A measurement reads 9.85 when the true value is 50. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.85, true = 50 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.85 - 50| / 50 * 100 | Answer: 80.3 %

question: Annual demand is 23000 units, ordering cost 170 per order and holding cost 18 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 23000, S = 170, H = 18 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*23000*170 / 18) | Answer: 659.1 units

question: An asset costs 310000 with salvage value 40000 after 13 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 310000, Sv = 40000, n = 13 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (310000 - 40000) / 13 | Answer: 20769 per year

question: A product sells for 440 per unit with variable cost 170 per unit and fixed costs 175000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 440, V = 170, F = 175000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 175000 / (440 - 170) | Answer: 648.1 units

question: Find the present worth of 130000 received 8 years from now at an interest rate of 5% per year.
solution: Given: F = 130000, n = 8, i = 5 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 130000 / (1 + 0.05)^8 | Answer: 87989 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.95, 0.92 and 0.94 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.95, r2 = 0.92, r3 = 0.94 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.95*0.92*0.94 | Answer: 0.8216

question: A process produces 12 defective items in a batch of 15500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 12, N = 15500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 12/15500 * 1e6 | Answer: 774.2 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = x^3 + x^2 + x + 5 evaluated at x = -3.
For f(x) = 3x^3 - 6x^2 - 9x - 5, find f''(x) at x = -2.
Evaluate the definite integral of (4x^2 + 4x + 1) dx from x = 0 to x = 5.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = 4x^3/3 + 4x^2/2 + 1x | Evaluate F(5) - F(0) | Answer: 221.7
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 2x^2 + 3x - 1 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[6, -8], [-3, 4]].
solution: Given: a = 6, b = -8, c = -3, d = 4 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (6)(4) - (-8)(-3) | Answer: 0

question: Find the determinant of [[-4, 5, 6], [4, 3, -5], [3, -1, 6]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: -325

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[3, -6], [-2, 8]].
solution: Trace tr = 11, Determinant = 12 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 9.772

question: Solve for x: 6x + -6y = 12 and -4x + 0y = 8.
solution: Determinant = 6*0 - -6*-4 = -24 | x = (e d - b f) / det = -2 | Answer: x = -2
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 42, 69, 82, 86, 16.
solution: Sum = 295 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 59 | Answer: 59

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 48, 30, 42, 23, 7.
solution: Mean = 30 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 16.17

question: Find the slope of the line through (3, -9) and (8, -1).
solution: Given: x1 = 3, y1 = -9, x2 = 8, y2 = -1 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (-1 - -9) / (8 - 3) | Answer: 1.6

question: Find the distance between the points (9, -4) and (8, 2).
solution: Given: x1 = 9, y1 = -4, x2 = 8, y2 = 2 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-1)^2 + (6)^2) | Answer: 6.083 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (-4,5), (-6,8), (-7,7).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 2.5 sq units

question: Find the 30th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -19 and common difference 4.
solution: Given: a = -19, d = 4, n = 30 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -19 + (30 - 1)*4 | Answer: 97

question: Find the sum of the first 38 terms of an AP with first term -8 and common difference -5.
solution: Given: a = -8, d = -5, n = 38 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 38/2 [2*-8 + (38-1)*-5] | Answer: -3819

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 4000 at 13.6% per annum for 5 years.
solution: Given: P = 4000, R = 13.6, Tt = 5 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 4000 * 13.6 * 5 / 100 | Answer: 2720 currency units

question: Find the amount when 33000 is invested at 6.1% per annum compounded annually for 2 years.
solution: Given: P = 33000, R = 6.1, Tt = 2 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 33000 * (1 + 6.1/100)^2 | Answer: 37149 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (1, 6, -2) and (-4, -4, -3).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (-2, 6, 5) and (-5, -2, -2).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 44.73

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (-6, -3, 0) and (-5, -6, -3).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 31.21 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number 0 + 4i.
solution: Given: a = 0, b = 4 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((0)^2 + (4)^2) | Answer: 4

question: Evaluate f(x) = x^3 + 4x^2 + 9x - 6 at x = -5.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-174 with initial guess x0=2, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.5 and ordinates 19, 2, 1, 10, 20, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 372 and 383.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 372 and 383 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 65 and 5.
solution: Given: a = 65, b = 5 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 65*5 / 5 | Answer: 65
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 51 mm carries an axial tensile load of 26 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 20 mm and length 2800 mm carries an axial load of 39 kN. Take E = 200 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 60 mm transmits a torque of 2400 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 60, Tt = 2400 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(2400*1000) / (pi*(60)^3) | Answer: 56.59 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 38 mm and length 1900 mm carries a torque of 750 N-m. With G = 45 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (38)^4 / 32 = 204708 mm^4 | theta = (750*1000)(1900) / (45000 * 204708) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 8.863 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 81 mm wide and 70 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 81, h = 70 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 81*(70)^2 / 6 | Answer: 66150 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (49 mm x 230 mm) carries a bending moment of 25 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (38 mm x 120 mm) has effective length 3100 mm and E = 200 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 730 MPa is designed for a working stress of 200 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 730, sw = 200 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 730 / 200 | Answer: 3.65

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1000 mm and wall thickness 7 mm carries an internal pressure of 2.7 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1000, t = 7, P = 2.7 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 2.7*1000 / (2*7) | Answer: 192.9 MPa

question: 7.8 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 165 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 7.8, dT = 165 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 7.8 * 0.718 * 165 | Answer: 924.1 kJ

question: 6.4 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 175 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 6.4, dT = 175 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 6.4 * 1.005 * 175 | Answer: 1126 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 3.4 m^3 at 310 K with mass 4.5 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 3.4, Tk = 310, m = 4.5 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 4.5*0.287*310 / 3.4 | Answer: 117.8 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 1.9 kg of air expands isothermally at 470 K from volume V1 to 2*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1.9, Tk = 470, ratio = 2 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 1.9*0.287*470*ln(2) | Answer: 177.6 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 3.9 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.22 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 3.9, D = 0.22 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*3.9*0.22 / 0.001 | Answer: 858000

question: Water flows at 2.3 m/s through a pipe of diameter 120 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 15.8 m. Taking Cv = 0.97, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 15.8, cv = 0.97 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.97*sqrt(2*9.81*15.8) | Answer: 17.08 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 320 mm) water flows at 2.6 m/s. It contracts to diameter 100 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
Water flows at 2.2 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.46 m and length 340 m. With friction factor f = 0.022, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 27 teeth drives a gear of 84 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1400 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 27, z2 = 84, N1 = 1400 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1400*27 / 84 | Answer: 450 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 130 mm rotates at 450 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 130, N = 450 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.13)*450 / 60 | Answer: 3.063 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 44.2 kW at 950 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 44.2, N = 950 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(44.2*1000) / (2*pi*950) | Answer: 444.3 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 4.3 kg rotates at radius 0.47 m at 300 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 12200 N/m and mass 8.7 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 12200, m = 8.7 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(12200/8.7) | Answer: 5.96 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 8.9 m^2 and thickness 0.23 m has conductivity k = 18 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 100 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 8.9, L = 0.23, k = 18, dT = 100 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 18*8.9*100 / 0.23 | Answer: 69652 W

question: A surface of area 0.6 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 80 W/m^2-K to surroundings 70 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 0.6, h = 80, dT = 70 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 80*0.6*70 | Answer: 3360 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 70 m/min, feed = 0.44 mm/rev, depth of cut = 3 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 70, f = 0.44, d = 3 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*70*0.44*3 | Answer: 92400 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 390 mm is turned at 600 rpm with a feed of 0.1 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 390, N = 600, f = 0.1 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 390 / (0.1*600) | Answer: 6.5 min

question: A resistor of 191 ohm carries a current of 0.2 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 191, I = 0.2 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 0.2 * 191 | Answer: 38.2 V

question: Three resistors 29 ohm, 3 ohm and 3 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 29, R2 = 3, R3 = 3 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 29 + 3 + 3 | Answer: 35 ohm

question: Two resistors 23 ohm and 28 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 23, R2 = 28 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 23*28 / (23+28) | Answer: 12.63 ohm

question: A device draws 8.7 A at 80 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 80, I = 8.7 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 80 * 8.7 | Answer: 696 W

question: A current of 7.1 A flows through a 48 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 7.1, R = 48 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (7.1)^2 * 48 | Answer: 242 W

question: Two capacitors 40.7 uF and 29.5 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 40.7, C2 = 29.5 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 40.7*29.5 / (40.7+29.5) | Answer: 17.1 uF

question: A resistor 72 kohm and capacitor 7.4 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 72, C = 7.4 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (72k)(7.4u) = 532.8 ms | Answer: 532.8 ms

question: An inductor 142 mH is in series with 187 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 142, R = 187 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (142e-3) / 187 | Answer: 0.7594 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 12.9 mH inductor at 430 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 12.9, f = 430 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (430)(12.9e-3) | Answer: 34.85 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 40.3 uF capacitor at 380 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 40.3, f = 380 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (380)(40.3e-6)) | Answer: 10.39 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 19 ohm, XL = 121 ohm and XC = 43 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 19, XL = 121, XC = 43 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(19^2 + (121 - 43)^2) | Answer: 80.28 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 86.9 mH and C = 4.3 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 86.9, C = 4.3 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(86.9e-3 * 4.3e-6)) | Answer: 260.4 Hz

question: A capacitor of 11.4 uF is charged to 155 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 11.4, V = 155 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*11.4e-6*(155)^2 | Answer: 136.9 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 350 V with 220 primary turns and 490 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 350, N1 = 220, N2 = 490 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 350 * 490/220 | Answer: 779.5 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 190 V and draws an armature current of 34 A. If the armature resistance is 1.01 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 190, Ia = 34, Ra = 1.01 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 190 - 34*1.01 | Answer: 155.7 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 195 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.93. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 195, VL = 400, pf = 0.93 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*400*195*0.93 / 1000 | Answer: 125.6 kW

question: A load has real power 115 kW and apparent power 120 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 115, S = 120 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 115 / 120 | Answer: 0.9583

question: A machine delivers 90 kW output while drawing 152 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 90, Pi = 152 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 90/152 * 100 | Answer: 59.21 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 6 V across R1 = 6 ohm and R2 = 15 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 6, R1 = 6, R2 = 15 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 6*15 / (6+15) | Answer: 4.286 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 70 kohm and Rin = 11 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 70, Rin = 11 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 70 / 11 | Answer: 6.364

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 20 kohm and Rg = 44 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 20, Rg = 44 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 20/44 | Answer: 1.455

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 111. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 111 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(111) | Answer: 20.45 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 3.2 m carries a central point load of 95 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.2, W = 95 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 95*3.2 / 4 | Answer: 76 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.3 m carries a UDL of 25 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.3, w = 25 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 25*(4.3)^2 / 8 | Answer: 57.78 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 4.7 m carries a point load 15 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.7, W = 15 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 15*4.7 | Answer: 70.5 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 4.7 m carries a UDL of 4 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.7, w = 4 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 4*(4.7)^2 / 2 | Answer: 44.18 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 8 m carries a point load 30 kN at distance 1.8 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 8, a = 1.8, W = 30 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 30*(8 - 1.8) / 8 | Answer: 23.25 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 5 m) carries a central point load 25 kN. With E = 200 GPa and I = 130e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=25000 N, L=5000.0 mm, E=200000 MPa, I=130e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 2.504 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 5.4 m carries a UDL of 33 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.4, w = 33 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 33*(5.4)^2 / 12 | Answer: 80.19 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 590 mm, clear cover 35 mm and main bars of diameter 16 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 590, c = 35, dia = 16 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 590 - 35 - 16/2 | Answer: 547 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 37.5 m^2 carrying a factored load of 16.5 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 37.5, w = 16.5 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 16.5 * 37.5 | Answer: 618.8 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 3.5 m, unit weight 20 kN/m^3, phi = 38 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 1.2e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1.3, area = 6.4e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 1.2, i = 1.3, A = 6.4 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (1.2e-4)*1.3*(6.4e-3) | Answer: 998.4 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1 m, bed slope 0.006 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.026. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 3.1 m under a head of 0.7 m. Taking Cd = 0.64 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 2.2 m wide carries a discharge of 3.2 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A tank of volume 390 m^3 treats a flow of 75 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 390, Q = 75 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 390 / 75 | Answer: 5.2 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 190 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.29 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 3 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 190, k = 0.29, t = 3 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 190*(1 - e^(-0.29*3)) | Answer: 110.4 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.55, rainfall intensity 40 mm/h over a catchment of 32.5 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.55, i = 40, A = 32.5 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.55*40*32.5 / 360 | Answer: 1.986 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.04 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 240 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.04, M = 240 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 240*(20+0.04)/20 | Answer: 240.5 m

question: Convert the decimal number 2830 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 2830 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: B0E (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 00011110 and 01100011.
solution: XOR: 01111101 | Count of 1s = 6 | Answer: 6
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 690 megabits is sent over a link of 45 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 690, B = 45 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 690 / 45 | Answer: 15.33 s

question: A link has bandwidth 11 Mbps and round-trip time 20 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 11, R = 20 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 11e6 * 20e-3 bits = 220 kb | Answer: 220 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.88, cache access time 7 ns and main-memory access time 180 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.88, tc = 7, tm = 180 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.88*7 + (1 - 0.88)*180 | Answer: 27.76 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 267390 elements?
solution: Given: n = 267390 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(267390)) + 1 | Answer: 19

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.015, memory access time 190 ns and page-fault service time 9 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 9 ms = 9000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.015)*190 + 0.015*9000000.0 ns | Answer: 135.2 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 2.9 m^3 at 430 kPa and 420 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 2.9, P = 430, Tk = 420 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (430e3)*2.9 / (8.314*420) | Answer: 357.1 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.4 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 19 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.4, t = 19 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.4*19) | Answer: 0.9995

question: For a reaction with A = 8e10 /s and activation energy 80 kJ/mol at 310 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 8, Ea = 80, Tk = 310 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 8e10 * exp(-80e3 / (8.314*310)) | Answer: 0.002647 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.97 and bottoms xW = 0.05, with relative volatility alpha = 2.9. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.97, xw = 0.05, al = 2.9 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.97/0.03)(0.95/0.05)] / ln(2.9) | Answer: 6.03 stages

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.33 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 20 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.33, Psat = 20 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.33 * 20 | Answer: 6.6 kPa

question: A stream of 6.4 kg/s with specific heat 3.6 kJ/kg-K is heated through 15 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 6.4, cp = 3.6, dT = 15 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 6.4*3.6*15 | Answer: 345.6 kW

question: A reactor of volume 7.8 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 1.5 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 7.8, Q = 1.5 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 7.8 / 1.5 | Answer: 5.2 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 6.2e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 1 mm with a concentration difference of 180 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 6.2, L = 1, dC = 180 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (6.2e-9)*180 / (1e-3) | Answer: 1116 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 4.9 min and steady-state gain 3.9. For a step input of magnitude 8, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 4.9, K = 3.9, M = 8 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 3.9 * 8 | Answer: 31.2 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 100 m^2 flies at 220 m/s (air density 0.4 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 1.2. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 100, V = 220, rho = 0.4, CL = 1.2 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.4*(220)^2*100*1.2 / 1000 | Answer: 1162 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 75 m^2 flies at 220 m/s (density 1.225 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.07. Find the drag force in kN.
A specimen under stress 180 MPa shows an elastic strain of 0.5e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 180, eps = 0.5 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 180 / (0.5e-3) MPa = 360 GPa | Answer: 360 GPa

question: A block of mass 30 kg has a volume of 4.5e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 30, V = 4.5 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 30 / (4.5e-3) | Answer: 6667 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 2200 mm is heated through 35 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 12e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 2200, dT = 35, al = 12 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 2200*12e-6*35 | Answer: 0.924 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 105 ohm, R2 = 125 ohm and R3 = 235 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 105, R2 = 125, R3 = 235 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 125*235 / 105 | Answer: 279.8 ohm

question: A measurement reads 9.49 when the true value is 50. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.49, true = 50 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.49 - 50| / 50 * 100 | Answer: 81.02 %

question: Annual demand is 1000 units, ordering cost 80 per order and holding cost 3 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 1000, S = 80, H = 3 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*1000*80 / 3) | Answer: 230.9 units

question: An asset costs 290000 with salvage value 34000 after 6 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 290000, Sv = 34000, n = 6 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (290000 - 34000) / 6 | Answer: 42667 per year

question: A product sells for 310 per unit with variable cost 160 per unit and fixed costs 25000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 310, V = 160, F = 25000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 25000 / (310 - 160) | Answer: 166.7 units

question: Find the present worth of 140000 received 5 years from now at an interest rate of 11% per year.
solution: Given: F = 140000, n = 5, i = 11 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 140000 / (1 + 0.11)^5 | Answer: 83083 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.93, 0.91 and 0.95 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.93, r2 = 0.91, r3 = 0.95 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.93*0.91*0.95 | Answer: 0.804

question: A process produces 38 defective items in a batch of 13000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 38, N = 13000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 38/13000 * 1e6 | Answer: 2923 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -x^3 - x^2 - 9x + 4 evaluated at x = 3.
For f(x) = -5x^3 - 3x^2 + x + 1, find f''(x) at x = -2.
Evaluate the definite integral of (3x^2 - 2x - 5) dx from x = 2 to x = 7.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = 3x^3/3 + -2x^2/2 + -5x | Evaluate F(7) - F(2) | Answer: 265
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 2x^2 + 12x + 3 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[-6, -5], [3, -4]].
solution: Given: a = -6, b = -5, c = 3, d = -4 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (-6)(-4) - (-5)(3) | Answer: 39

question: Find the determinant of [[0, -6, 2], [-4, -4, 5], [-3, 0, -5]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: 186

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[-6, -1], [-5, -2]].
solution: Trace tr = -8, Determinant = 7 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: -1

question: Solve for x: -4x + 4y = 1 and 6x + -2y = -2.
solution: Determinant = -4*-2 - 4*6 = -16 | x = (e d - b f) / det = -0.375 | Answer: x = -0.375
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 84, 33, 94, 56, 20.
solution: Sum = 287 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 57.4 | Answer: 57.4

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 18, 23, 18, 31, 20.
solution: Mean = 22 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 5.431

question: Find the slope of the line through (2, 9) and (-8, 9).
solution: Given: x1 = 2, y1 = 9, x2 = -8, y2 = 9 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (9 - 9) / (-8 - 2) | Answer: 0

question: Find the distance between the points (-1, 1) and (-1, 6).
solution: Given: x1 = -1, y1 = 1, x2 = -1, y2 = 6 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((0)^2 + (5)^2) | Answer: 5 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (-6,-1), (-5,3), (7,5).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 23 sq units

question: Find the 11th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 0 and common difference -4.
solution: Given: a = 0, d = -4, n = 11 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = 0 + (11 - 1)*-4 | Answer: -40

question: Find the sum of the first 25 terms of an AP with first term -10 and common difference -3.
Find the simple interest on a principal of 2500 at 14% per annum for 2 years.
solution: Given: P = 2500, R = 14, Tt = 2 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 2500 * 14 * 2 / 100 | Answer: 700 currency units

question: Find the amount when 2000 is invested at 6.4% per annum compounded annually for 5 years.
solution: Given: P = 2000, R = 6.4, Tt = 5 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 2000 * (1 + 6.4/100)^5 | Answer: 2727 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (-3, -7, 7) and (-5, -5, -8).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (3, 3, -2) and (6, 3, 4).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 31.32

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (-2, -1, 0) and (-5, 4, 1).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 65.54 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number 5 + 8i.
solution: Given: a = 5, b = 8 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((5)^2 + (8)^2) | Answer: 9.434

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number -12 + -7i.
solution: Given: a = -12, b = -7 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(-7, -12) | Answer: -149.7 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -5x^3 - 2x^2 - 7x - 6 at x = 2.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-151 with initial guess x0=12, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.8 and ordinates 13, 0, 13, 9, 13, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 96 and 200.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 96 and 200 | Answer: GCD = 8

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 71 and 80.
solution: Given: a = 71, b = 80 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 71*80 / 1 | Answer: 5680
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 49 mm carries an axial tensile load of 23 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 32 mm and length 1100 mm carries an axial load of 41 kN. Take E = 210 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 67 mm transmits a torque of 200 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 67, Tt = 200 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(200*1000) / (pi*(67)^3) | Answer: 3.387 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 28 mm and length 1800 mm carries a torque of 1650 N-m. With G = 45 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (28)^4 / 32 = 60344 mm^4 | theta = (1650*1000)(1800) / (45000 * 60344) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 62.67 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 102 mm wide and 170 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 102, h = 170 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 102*(170)^2 / 6 | Answer: 491300 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (83 mm x 90 mm) carries a bending moment of 5 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (45 mm x 140 mm) has effective length 3300 mm and E = 200 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 330 MPa is designed for a working stress of 170 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 330, sw = 170 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 330 / 170 | Answer: 1.941

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1450 mm and wall thickness 8 mm carries an internal pressure of 2.5 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1450, t = 8, P = 2.5 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 2.5*1450 / (2*8) | Answer: 226.6 MPa

question: 7 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 175 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 7, dT = 175 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 7 * 0.718 * 175 | Answer: 879.5 kJ

question: 7.7 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 185 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 7.7, dT = 185 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 7.7 * 1.005 * 185 | Answer: 1432 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 0.9 m^3 at 530 K with mass 5.7 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 0.9, Tk = 530, m = 5.7 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 5.7*0.287*530 / 0.9 | Answer: 963.4 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 5 kg of air expands isothermally at 400 K from volume V1 to 5*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 5, Tk = 400, ratio = 5 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 5*0.287*400*ln(5) | Answer: 923.8 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 0.8 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.09 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 0.8, D = 0.09 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*0.8*0.09 / 0.001 | Answer: 72000

question: Water flows at 1.4 m/s through a pipe of diameter 130 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 13.8 m. Taking Cv = 0.99, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 13.8, cv = 0.99 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.99*sqrt(2*9.81*13.8) | Answer: 16.29 m/s
