question: In a pipe (diameter 190 mm) water flows at 2.7 m/s. It contracts to diameter 140 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
Water flows at 3.7 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.35 m and length 300 m. With friction factor f = 0.037, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 22 teeth drives a gear of 120 teeth. If the pinion runs at 850 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 22, z2 = 120, N1 = 850 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 850*22 / 120 | Answer: 155.8 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 280 mm rotates at 700 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 280, N = 700 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.28)*700 / 60 | Answer: 10.26 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 31.2 kW at 1050 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 31.2, N = 1050 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(31.2*1000) / (2*pi*1050) | Answer: 283.8 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 3.4 kg rotates at radius 0.24 m at 550 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 11900 N/m and mass 3.3 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 11900, m = 3.3 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(11900/3.3) | Answer: 9.557 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 4.6 m^2 and thickness 0.16 m has conductivity k = 46.5 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 160 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 4.6, L = 0.16, k = 46.5, dT = 160 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 46.5*4.6*160 / 0.16 | Answer: 213900 W

question: A surface of area 3.8 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 45 W/m^2-K to surroundings 140 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 3.8, h = 45, dT = 140 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 45*3.8*140 | Answer: 23940 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 180 m/min, feed = 0.19 mm/rev, depth of cut = 1.9 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 180, f = 0.19, d = 1.9 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*180*0.19*1.9 | Answer: 64980 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 260 mm is turned at 550 rpm with a feed of 0.15 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 260, N = 550, f = 0.15 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 260 / (0.15*550) | Answer: 3.152 min

question: A resistor of 150 ohm carries a current of 8.8 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 150, I = 8.8 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 8.8 * 150 | Answer: 1320 V

question: Three resistors 58 ohm, 90 ohm and 60 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 58, R2 = 90, R3 = 60 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 58 + 90 + 60 | Answer: 208 ohm

question: Two resistors 61 ohm and 38 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 61, R2 = 38 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 61*38 / (61+38) | Answer: 23.41 ohm

question: A device draws 11.4 A at 170 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 170, I = 11.4 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 170 * 11.4 | Answer: 1938 W

question: A current of 0.3 A flows through a 58 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 0.3, R = 58 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (0.3)^2 * 58 | Answer: 5.22 W

question: Two capacitors 49.7 uF and 6.4 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 49.7, C2 = 6.4 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 49.7*6.4 / (49.7+6.4) | Answer: 5.67 uF

question: A resistor 8 kohm and capacitor 9.9 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 8, C = 9.9 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (8k)(9.9u) = 79.2 ms | Answer: 79.2 ms

question: An inductor 473.4 mH is in series with 50 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 473.4, R = 50 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (473.4e-3) / 50 | Answer: 9.468 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 123.6 mH inductor at 440 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 123.6, f = 440 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (440)(123.6e-3) | Answer: 341.7 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 16.3 uF capacitor at 290 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 16.3, f = 290 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (290)(16.3e-6)) | Answer: 33.67 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 63 ohm, XL = 89 ohm and XC = 145 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 63, XL = 89, XC = 145 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(63^2 + (89 - 145)^2) | Answer: 84.29 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 57.9 mH and C = 8.4 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 57.9, C = 8.4 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(57.9e-3 * 8.4e-6)) | Answer: 228.2 Hz

question: A capacitor of 28.2 uF is charged to 225 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 28.2, V = 225 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*28.2e-6*(225)^2 | Answer: 713.8 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 140 V with 550 primary turns and 330 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 140, N1 = 550, N2 = 330 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 140 * 330/550 | Answer: 84 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 180 V and draws an armature current of 9 A. If the armature resistance is 1.21 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 180, Ia = 9, Ra = 1.21 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 180 - 9*1.21 | Answer: 169.1 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 170 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.98. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 170, VL = 400, pf = 0.98 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*400*170*0.98 / 1000 | Answer: 115.4 kW

question: A load has real power 25 kW and apparent power 140 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 25, S = 140 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 25 / 140 | Answer: 0.1786

question: A machine delivers 145 kW output while drawing 192 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 145, Pi = 192 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 145/192 * 100 | Answer: 75.52 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 30 V across R1 = 45 ohm and R2 = 8 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 30, R1 = 45, R2 = 8 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 30*8 / (45+8) | Answer: 4.528 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 200 kohm and Rin = 43 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 200, Rin = 43 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 200 / 43 | Answer: 4.651

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 90 kohm and Rg = 25 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 90, Rg = 25 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 90/25 | Answer: 4.6

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 2933. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 2933 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(2933) | Answer: 34.67 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 8.1 m carries a central point load of 70 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 8.1, W = 70 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 70*8.1 / 4 | Answer: 141.8 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 3.4 m carries a UDL of 10 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.4, w = 10 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 10*(3.4)^2 / 8 | Answer: 14.45 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 4.6 m carries a point load 55 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.6, W = 55 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 55*4.6 | Answer: 253 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 5.6 m carries a UDL of 24 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.6, w = 24 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 24*(5.6)^2 / 2 | Answer: 376.3 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 5 m carries a point load 100 kN at distance 1.3 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 5, a = 1.3, W = 100 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 100*(5 - 1.3) / 5 | Answer: 74 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 5.2 m) carries a central point load 80 kN. With E = 200 GPa and I = 180e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=80000 N, L=5200.0 mm, E=200000 MPa, I=180e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 6.51 mm

question: An RC beam has overall depth 700 mm, clear cover 40 mm and main bars of diameter 12 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 700, c = 40, dia = 12 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 700 - 40 - 12/2 | Answer: 654 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 21.4 m^2 carrying a factored load of 8.1 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 21.4, w = 8.1 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 8.1 * 21.4 | Answer: 173.3 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 6.9 m, unit weight 19 kN/m^3, phi = 31 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 3.9e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.3, area = 4.1e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 3.9, i = 0.3, A = 4.1 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (3.9e-4)*0.3*(4.1e-3) | Answer: 479.7 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 0.7 m, bed slope 0.009 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.025. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 2.6 m under a head of 0.9 m. Taking Cd = 0.64 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 4.5 m wide carries a discharge of 8.4 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A tank of volume 510 m^3 treats a flow of 170 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 510, Q = 170 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 510 / 170 | Answer: 3 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 210 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.33 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 5 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 210, k = 0.33, t = 5 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 210*(1 - e^(-0.33*5)) | Answer: 169.7 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.64, rainfall intensity 30 mm/h over a catchment of 15.5 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.64, i = 30, A = 15.5 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.64*30*15.5 / 360 | Answer: 0.8267 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.01 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 450 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.01, M = 450 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 450*(20+0.01)/20 | Answer: 450.2 m

question: Convert the decimal number 3167 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 3167 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: C5F (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 00000110 and 01011011.
solution: XOR: 01011101 | Count of 1s = 5 | Answer: 5
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 950 megabits is sent over a link of 50 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 950, B = 50 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 950 / 50 | Answer: 19 s

question: A link has bandwidth 9 Mbps and round-trip time 70 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 9, R = 70 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 9e6 * 70e-3 bits = 630 kb | Answer: 630 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.97, cache access time 10 ns and main-memory access time 190 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.97, tc = 10, tm = 190 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.97*10 + (1 - 0.97)*190 | Answer: 15.4 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 240128 elements?
solution: Given: n = 240128 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(240128)) + 1 | Answer: 18

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.002, memory access time 130 ns and page-fault service time 4 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 4 ms = 4000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.002)*130 + 0.002*4000000.0 ns | Answer: 8.13 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 2.3 m^3 at 430 kPa and 490 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 2.3, P = 430, Tk = 490 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (430e3)*2.3 / (8.314*490) | Answer: 242.8 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.16 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 20 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.16, t = 20 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.16*20) | Answer: 0.9592

question: For a reaction with A = 2e10 /s and activation energy 85 kJ/mol at 480 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 2, Ea = 85, Tk = 480 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 2e10 * exp(-85e3 / (8.314*480)) | Answer: 11.24 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.98 and bottoms xW = 0.02, with relative volatility alpha = 2.5. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.98, xw = 0.02, al = 2.5 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.98/0.02)(0.98/0.02)] / ln(2.5) | Answer: 8.495 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.56 and x = 0.24. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.56, x = 0.24 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.56/0.44) / (0.24/0.76) | Answer: 4.03

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.22 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 95 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.22, Psat = 95 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.22 * 95 | Answer: 20.9 kPa

question: A stream of 3.6 kg/s with specific heat 2.9 kJ/kg-K is heated through 20 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 3.6, cp = 2.9, dT = 20 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 3.6*2.9*20 | Answer: 208.8 kW

question: A reactor of volume 11 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 0.7 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 11, Q = 0.7 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 11 / 0.7 | Answer: 15.71 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 3.9e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 2 mm with a concentration difference of 10 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 3.9, L = 2, dC = 10 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (3.9e-9)*10 / (2e-3) | Answer: 19.5 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 7 min and steady-state gain 2.5. For a step input of magnitude 15, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 7, K = 2.5, M = 15 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 2.5 * 15 | Answer: 37.5 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 85 m^2 flies at 230 m/s (air density 1 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 1.2. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 85, V = 230, rho = 1, CL = 1.2 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1*(230)^2*85*1.2 / 1000 | Answer: 2698 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 90 m^2 flies at 110 m/s (density 0.7 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.04. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 90, V = 110, rho = 0.7, CD = 0.04 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.7*(110)^2*90*0.04 / 1000 | Answer: 15.25 kN

question: A specimen under stress 380 MPa shows an elastic strain of 2.5e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 380, eps = 2.5 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 380 / (2.5e-3) MPa = 152 GPa | Answer: 152 GPa

question: A block of mass 17 kg has a volume of 3.3e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 17, V = 3.3 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 17 / (3.3e-3) | Answer: 5152 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 3000 mm is heated through 145 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 11e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 3000, dT = 145, al = 11 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 3000*11e-6*145 | Answer: 4.785 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 50 ohm, R2 = 70 ohm and R3 = 190 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 50, R2 = 70, R3 = 190 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 70*190 / 50 | Answer: 266 ohm

question: A measurement reads 9.96 when the true value is 10. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.96, true = 10 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.96 - 10| / 10 * 100 | Answer: 0.4 %

question: Annual demand is 38000 units, ordering cost 60 per order and holding cost 6 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 38000, S = 60, H = 6 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*38000*60 / 6) | Answer: 871.8 units

question: An asset costs 190000 with salvage value 38000 after 10 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 190000, Sv = 38000, n = 10 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (190000 - 38000) / 10 | Answer: 15200 per year

question: A product sells for 460 per unit with variable cost 100 per unit and fixed costs 110000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 460, V = 100, F = 110000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 110000 / (460 - 100) | Answer: 305.6 units

question: Find the present worth of 165000 received 5 years from now at an interest rate of 8% per year.
solution: Given: F = 165000, n = 5, i = 8 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 165000 / (1 + 0.08)^5 | Answer: 112296 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.9, 0.91 and 0.99 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.9, r2 = 0.91, r3 = 0.99 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.9*0.91*0.99 | Answer: 0.8108

question: A process produces 23 defective items in a batch of 15000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 23, N = 15000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 23/15000 * 1e6 | Answer: 1533 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = 3x^3 + x^2 - 6x - 8 evaluated at x = 4.
For f(x) = -5x^3 - 5x^2 + 4x + 1, find f''(x) at x = -1.
Evaluate the definite integral of (5x^2 - 3x + 6) dx from x = 1 to x = 5.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = 5x^3/3 + -3x^2/2 + 6x | Evaluate F(5) - F(1) | Answer: 194.7
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 2x^2 + 10x - 10 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[7, 8], [1, -3]].
solution: Given: a = 7, b = 8, c = 1, d = -3 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (7)(-3) - (8)(1) | Answer: -29

question: Find the determinant of [[-4, -4, -2], [0, 6, 6], [-4, -3, 3]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: -96

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[2, -1], [0, 7]].
solution: Trace tr = 9, Determinant = 14 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 7

question: Solve for x: 0x + 2y = -11 and -5x + -5y = 6.
solution: Determinant = 0*-5 - 2*-5 = 10 | x = (e d - b f) / det = 4.3 | Answer: x = 4.3
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 63, 65, 22, 1, 82.
solution: Sum = 233 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 46.6 | Answer: 46.6

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 30, 24, 15, 23, 12.
solution: Mean = 20.8 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 7.259

question: Find the slope of the line through (5, 4) and (-4, 7).
solution: Given: x1 = 5, y1 = 4, x2 = -4, y2 = 7 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (7 - 4) / (-4 - 5) | Answer: -0.3333

question: Find the distance between the points (-1, 6) and (9, 6).
solution: Given: x1 = -1, y1 = 6, x2 = 9, y2 = 6 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((10)^2 + (0)^2) | Answer: 10 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (-7,-4), (1,-8), (-7,3).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 28 sq units

question: Find the 6th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -8 and common difference 9.
solution: Given: a = -8, d = 9, n = 6 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -8 + (6 - 1)*9 | Answer: 37

question: Find the sum of the first 12 terms of an AP with first term 8 and common difference -5.
solution: Given: a = 8, d = -5, n = 12 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 12/2 [2*8 + (12-1)*-5] | Answer: -234

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 33000 at 9.8% per annum for 5 years.
solution: Given: P = 33000, R = 9.8, Tt = 5 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 33000 * 9.8 * 5 / 100 | Answer: 16170 currency units

question: Find the amount when 7000 is invested at 4.3% per annum compounded annually for 5 years.
solution: Given: P = 7000, R = 4.3, Tt = 5 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 7000 * (1 + 4.3/100)^5 | Answer: 864 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (-6, -4, 3) and (-5, 2, 8).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (-6, 4, 1) and (-2, -3, 6).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 50.61

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (3, 4, -5) and (3, -3, 4).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 123.9 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number 1 + 5i.
solution: Given: a = 1, b = 5 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((1)^2 + (5)^2) | Answer: 5.099

question: Evaluate f(x) = 5x^3 + 3x^2 + 5x + 6 at x = 2.
solution: Given: a = 5, b = 3, c = 5, d = 6, x0 = 2 | Formula: f(x0) = a x0^3 + b x0^2 + c x0 + d | Substitute: f(2) = 5(2)^3 + 3(2)^2 + 5(2) + 6 | Answer: 68

question: Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-173 with initial guess x0=3, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.4 and ordinates 3, 18, 20, 6, 4, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 201 and 93.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 201 and 93 | Answer: GCD = 3

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 22 and 70.
solution: Given: a = 22, b = 70 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 22*70 / 2 | Answer: 770
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 32 mm carries an axial tensile load of 28 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 14 mm and length 2400 mm carries an axial load of 61 kN. Take E = 70 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 35 mm transmits a torque of 500 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 35, Tt = 500 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(500*1000) / (pi*(35)^3) | Answer: 59.39 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 49 mm and length 1100 mm carries a torque of 550 N-m. With G = 45 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (49)^4 / 32 = 565958 mm^4 | theta = (550*1000)(1100) / (45000 * 565958) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 1.361 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 49 mm wide and 230 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 49, h = 230 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 49*(230)^2 / 6 | Answer: 432017 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (64 mm x 130 mm) carries a bending moment of 11 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (53 mm x 150 mm) has effective length 1800 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 620 MPa is designed for a working stress of 140 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 620, sw = 140 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 620 / 140 | Answer: 4.429

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 900 mm and wall thickness 9 mm carries an internal pressure of 1.9 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 900, t = 9, P = 1.9 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 1.9*900 / (2*9) | Answer: 95 MPa

question: 7.4 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 195 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 7.4, dT = 195 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 7.4 * 0.718 * 195 | Answer: 1036 kJ

question: 6.6 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 120 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 6.6, dT = 120 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 6.6 * 1.005 * 120 | Answer: 796 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 2.1 m^3 at 390 K with mass 1.4 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 2.1, Tk = 390, m = 1.4 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 1.4*0.287*390 / 2.1 | Answer: 74.62 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 4.8 kg of air expands isothermally at 370 K from volume V1 to 2*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.8, Tk = 370, ratio = 2 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 4.8*0.287*370*ln(2) | Answer: 353.3 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 1.3 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.08 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 1.3, D = 0.08 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*1.3*0.08 / 0.001 | Answer: 104000

question: Water flows at 1.7 m/s through a pipe of diameter 130 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 17.1 m. Taking Cv = 0.97, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 17.1, cv = 0.97 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.97*sqrt(2*9.81*17.1) | Answer: 17.77 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 360 mm) water flows at 2.4 m/s. It contracts to diameter 60 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 360, d2 = 60, V1 = 2.4 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 2.4*(360/60)^2 | Answer: 86.4 m/s

question: Water flows at 2 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.39 m and length 350 m. With friction factor f = 0.024, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 38 teeth drives a gear of 110 teeth. If the pinion runs at 900 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 38, z2 = 110, N1 = 900 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 900*38 / 110 | Answer: 310.9 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 370 mm rotates at 400 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 370, N = 400 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.37)*400 / 60 | Answer: 7.749 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 48.3 kW at 1100 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 48.3, N = 1100 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(48.3*1000) / (2*pi*1100) | Answer: 419.3 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 3.2 kg rotates at radius 0.32 m at 500 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 7200 N/m and mass 14.5 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 7200, m = 14.5 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(7200/14.5) | Answer: 3.547 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 7.2 m^2 and thickness 0.27 m has conductivity k = 30.3 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 90 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 7.2, L = 0.27, k = 30.3, dT = 90 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 30.3*7.2*90 / 0.27 | Answer: 72720 W

question: A surface of area 2.8 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 150 W/m^2-K to surroundings 145 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 2.8, h = 150, dT = 145 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 150*2.8*145 | Answer: 60900 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 140 m/min, feed = 0.41 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2.6 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 140, f = 0.41, d = 2.6 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*140*0.41*2.6 | Answer: 149240 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 300 mm is turned at 400 rpm with a feed of 0.25 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 300, N = 400, f = 0.25 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 300 / (0.25*400) | Answer: 3 min

question: A resistor of 189 ohm carries a current of 0.3 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 189, I = 0.3 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 0.3 * 189 | Answer: 56.7 V

question: Three resistors 17 ohm, 80 ohm and 22 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 17, R2 = 80, R3 = 22 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 17 + 80 + 22 | Answer: 119 ohm

question: Two resistors 43 ohm and 103 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 43, R2 = 103 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 43*103 / (43+103) | Answer: 30.34 ohm

question: A device draws 10.9 A at 105 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 105, I = 10.9 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 105 * 10.9 | Answer: 1144 W

question: A current of 5.5 A flows through a 55 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 5.5, R = 55 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (5.5)^2 * 55 | Answer: 1664 W

question: Two capacitors 47.9 uF and 4.2 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 47.9, C2 = 4.2 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 47.9*4.2 / (47.9+4.2) | Answer: 3.861 uF

question: A resistor 8 kohm and capacitor 6 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 8, C = 6 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (8k)(6u) = 48 ms | Answer: 48 ms

question: An inductor 124.6 mH is in series with 22 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 124.6, R = 22 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (124.6e-3) / 22 | Answer: 5.664 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 175.9 mH inductor at 210 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 175.9, f = 210 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (210)(175.9e-3) | Answer: 232.1 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 27.1 uF capacitor at 680 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 27.1, f = 680 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (680)(27.1e-6)) | Answer: 8.637 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 77 ohm, XL = 129 ohm and XC = 39 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 77, XL = 129, XC = 39 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(77^2 + (129 - 39)^2) | Answer: 118.4 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 92.3 mH and C = 3.9 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 92.3, C = 3.9 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(92.3e-3 * 3.9e-6)) | Answer: 265.3 Hz

question: A capacitor of 71.8 uF is charged to 375 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 71.8, V = 375 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*71.8e-6*(375)^2 | Answer: 5048 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 320 V with 680 primary turns and 310 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 320, N1 = 680, N2 = 310 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 320 * 310/680 | Answer: 145.9 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 370 V and draws an armature current of 57 A. If the armature resistance is 0.81 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 370, Ia = 57, Ra = 0.81 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 370 - 57*0.81 | Answer: 323.8 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 190 A at 415 V (line) with a power factor of 0.79. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 190, VL = 415, pf = 0.79 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*415*190*0.79 / 1000 | Answer: 107.9 kW

question: A load has real power 10 kW and apparent power 195 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 10, S = 195 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 10 / 195 | Answer: 0.05128

question: A machine delivers 45 kW output while drawing 162 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 45, Pi = 162 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 45/162 * 100 | Answer: 27.78 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 11 V across R1 = 45 ohm and R2 = 37 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 11, R1 = 45, R2 = 37 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 11*37 / (45+37) | Answer: 4.963 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 110 kohm and Rin = 20 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 110, Rin = 20 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 110 / 20 | Answer: 5.5

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 50 kohm and Rg = 5 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 50, Rg = 5 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 50/5 | Answer: 11

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 5829. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 5829 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(5829) | Answer: 37.66 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 8 m carries a central point load of 120 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 8, W = 120 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 120*8 / 4 | Answer: 240 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.1 m carries a UDL of 60 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.1, w = 60 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 60*(4.1)^2 / 8 | Answer: 126.1 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 2.7 m carries a point load 60 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 2.7, W = 60 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 60*2.7 | Answer: 162 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 3.5 m carries a UDL of 30 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.5, w = 30 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 30*(3.5)^2 / 2 | Answer: 183.8 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 5.7 m carries a point load 75 kN at distance 2.5 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 5.7, a = 2.5, W = 75 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 75*(5.7 - 2.5) / 5.7 | Answer: 42.11 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 3.7 m) carries a central point load 80 kN. With E = 30 GPa and I = 170e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=80000 N, L=3700.0 mm, E=30000 MPa, I=170e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 16.55 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 7.2 m carries a UDL of 9 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7.2, w = 9 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 9*(7.2)^2 / 12 | Answer: 38.88 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 460 mm, clear cover 50 mm and main bars of diameter 16 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 460, c = 50, dia = 16 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 460 - 50 - 16/2 | Answer: 402 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 36.6 m^2 carrying a factored load of 17.6 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 36.6, w = 17.6 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 17.6 * 36.6 | Answer: 644.2 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 3.2 m, unit weight 20 kN/m^3, phi = 30 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 6.9e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.3, area = 4.6e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 6.9, i = 0.3, A = 4.6 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (6.9e-4)*0.3*(4.6e-3) | Answer: 952.2 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.7 m, bed slope 0.007 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.025. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 2.8 m under a head of 0.7 m. Taking Cd = 0.62 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 5.6 m wide carries a discharge of 6.7 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A tank of volume 520 m^3 treats a flow of 195 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 520, Q = 195 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 520 / 195 | Answer: 2.667 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 390 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.15 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 4 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 390, k = 0.15, t = 4 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 390*(1 - e^(-0.15*4)) | Answer: 176 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.76, rainfall intensity 105 mm/h over a catchment of 37.1 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.76, i = 105, A = 37.1 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.76*105*37.1 / 360 | Answer: 8.224 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.07 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 230 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.07, M = 230 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 230*(30+0.07)/30 | Answer: 230.5 m

question: Convert the decimal number 3621 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 3621 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: E25 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 10110001 and 10010100.
solution: XOR: 00100101 | Count of 1s = 3 | Answer: 3
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 940 megabits is sent over a link of 53 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 940, B = 53 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 940 / 53 | Answer: 17.74 s

question: A link has bandwidth 66 Mbps and round-trip time 80 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 66, R = 80 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 66e6 * 80e-3 bits = 5280 kb | Answer: 5280 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.85, cache access time 6 ns and main-memory access time 170 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.85, tc = 6, tm = 170 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.85*6 + (1 - 0.85)*170 | Answer: 30.6 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 925799 elements?
solution: Given: n = 925799 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(925799)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.016, memory access time 80 ns and page-fault service time 4 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 4 ms = 4000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.016)*80 + 0.016*4000000.0 ns | Answer: 64.08 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 0.1 m^3 at 410 kPa and 460 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 0.1, P = 410, Tk = 460 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (410e3)*0.1 / (8.314*460) | Answer: 10.72 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.28 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 20 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.28, t = 20 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.28*20) | Answer: 0.9963

question: For a reaction with A = 2e10 /s and activation energy 90 kJ/mol at 450 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 2, Ea = 90, Tk = 450 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 2e10 * exp(-90e3 / (8.314*450)) | Answer: 0.714 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.9 and bottoms xW = 0.07, with relative volatility alpha = 2.9. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.9, xw = 0.07, al = 2.9 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.9/0.1)(0.93/0.07)] / ln(2.9) | Answer: 4.493 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.61 and x = 0.49. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.61, x = 0.49 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.61/0.39) / (0.49/0.51) | Answer: 1.628

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.13 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 75 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.13, Psat = 75 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.13 * 75 | Answer: 9.75 kPa

question: A stream of 7.7 kg/s with specific heat 1.4 kJ/kg-K is heated through 20 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 7.7, cp = 1.4, dT = 20 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 7.7*1.4*20 | Answer: 215.6 kW

question: A reactor of volume 13.6 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 3.4 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 13.6, Q = 3.4 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 13.6 / 3.4 | Answer: 4 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 5.6e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 4 mm with a concentration difference of 170 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 5.6, L = 4, dC = 170 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (5.6e-9)*170 / (4e-3) | Answer: 238 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 5.9 min and steady-state gain 3.8. For a step input of magnitude 2, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 5.9, K = 3.8, M = 2 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 3.8 * 2 | Answer: 7.6 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 30 m^2 flies at 150 m/s (air density 1 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 1.1. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 30, V = 150, rho = 1, CL = 1.1 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1*(150)^2*30*1.1 / 1000 | Answer: 371.3 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 40 m^2 flies at 180 m/s (density 1.225 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.03. Find the drag force in kN.
A specimen under stress 170 MPa shows an elastic strain of 2e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 170, eps = 2 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 170 / (2e-3) MPa = 85 GPa | Answer: 85 GPa

question: A block of mass 32 kg has a volume of 4.5e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 32, V = 4.5 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 32 / (4.5e-3) | Answer: 7111 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 2900 mm is heated through 105 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 23e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 2900, dT = 105, al = 23 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 2900*23e-6*105 | Answer: 7.003 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 25 ohm, R2 = 165 ohm and R3 = 460 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 25, R2 = 165, R3 = 460 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 165*460 / 25 | Answer: 3036 ohm

question: A measurement reads 9.27 when the true value is 10. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.27, true = 10 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.27 - 10| / 10 * 100 | Answer: 7.3 %

question: Annual demand is 23000 units, ordering cost 170 per order and holding cost 39 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 23000, S = 170, H = 39 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*23000*170 / 39) | Answer: 447.8 units

question: An asset costs 270000 with salvage value 40000 after 19 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 270000, Sv = 40000, n = 19 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (270000 - 40000) / 19 | Answer: 12105 per year

question: A product sells for 450 per unit with variable cost 70 per unit and fixed costs 100000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 450, V = 70, F = 100000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 100000 / (450 - 70) | Answer: 263.2 units

question: Find the present worth of 100000 received 2 years from now at an interest rate of 10% per year.
solution: Given: F = 100000, n = 2, i = 10 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 100000 / (1 + 0.1)^2 | Answer: 82645 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.95, 0.91 and 0.92 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.95, r2 = 0.91, r3 = 0.92 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.95*0.91*0.92 | Answer: 0.7953

question: A process produces 5 defective items in a batch of 1500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 5, N = 1500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 5/1500 * 1e6 | Answer: 3333 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -3x^3 - 5x - 7 evaluated at x = 5.
For f(x) = 3x^3 - x^2 + 7x - 9, find f''(x) at x = 1.
Evaluate the definite integral of (-x^2 - 2x - 8) dx from x = -3 to x = 5.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = -1x^3/3 + -2x^2/2 + -8x | Evaluate F(5) - F(-3) | Answer: -130.7
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 5x^2 - 12x + 4 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[-4, -5], [5, -3]].
solution: Given: a = -4, b = -5, c = 5, d = -3 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (-4)(-3) - (-5)(5) | Answer: 37

question: Find the determinant of [[-6, 4, 4], [6, -2, 4], [2, -4, 4]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: -192

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[0, 0], [8, 6]].
solution: Trace tr = 6, Determinant = 0 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 6

question: Solve for x: -6x + -3y = -2 and 0x + -6y = -9.
solution: Determinant = -6*-6 - -3*0 = 36 | x = (e d - b f) / det = -0.4167 | Answer: x = -0.4167
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 51, 81, 67, 18, 31.
solution: Sum = 248 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 49.6 | Answer: 49.6

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 48, 41, 19, 41, 4.
solution: Mean = 30.6 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 18.45

question: Find the slope of the line through (2, 4) and (3, 8).
solution: Given: x1 = 2, y1 = 4, x2 = 3, y2 = 8 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (8 - 4) / (3 - 2) | Answer: 4

question: Find the distance between the points (5, 7) and (6, -9).
solution: Given: x1 = 5, y1 = 7, x2 = 6, y2 = -9 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((1)^2 + (-16)^2) | Answer: 16.03 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (4,6), (-3,4), (-2,4).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 1 sq units

question: Find the 31th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -19 and common difference 8.
solution: Given: a = -19, d = 8, n = 31 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -19 + (31 - 1)*8 | Answer: 221

question: Find the sum of the first 21 terms of an AP with first term -8 and common difference -6.
solution: Given: a = -8, d = -6, n = 21 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 21/2 [2*-8 + (21-1)*-6] | Answer: -1428

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 20000 at 12.7% per annum for 2 years.
solution: Given: P = 20000, R = 12.7, Tt = 2 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 20000 * 12.7 * 2 / 100 | Answer: 5080 currency units

question: Find the amount when 11000 is invested at 8.5% per annum compounded annually for 3 years.
solution: Given: P = 11000, R = 8.5, Tt = 3 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 11000 * (1 + 8.5/100)^3 | Answer: 1405 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (-3, -8, -5) and (6, 5, -1).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (5, -2, 6) and (-6, -5, 0).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 59.71

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (1, -2, 3) and (2, -1, 0).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 61.44 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -5x^3 - 4x^2 - 6x + 2 at x = 2.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-38 with initial guess x0=4, find x1 (one iteration).
solution: Given: N = 38, x0 = 4 | Formula: x1 = x0 - (x0^2 - N)/(2 x0) | Substitute: x1 = 4 - ((4)^2 - 38)/(2*4) | Answer: 6.75

question: Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.1 and ordinates 7, 9, 4, 9, 2, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 184 and 293.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 184 and 293 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 18 and 39.
solution: Given: a = 18, b = 39 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 18*39 / 3 | Answer: 234
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 41 mm carries an axial tensile load of 112 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 16 mm and length 1600 mm carries an axial load of 23 kN. Take E = 70 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 47 mm transmits a torque of 1500 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 47, Tt = 1500 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(1500*1000) / (pi*(47)^3) | Answer: 73.58 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 59 mm and length 1000 mm carries a torque of 250 N-m. With G = 77 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (59)^4 / 32 = 1189619 mm^4 | theta = (250*1000)(1000) / (77000 * 1189619) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 0.1564 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 145 mm wide and 140 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 145, h = 140 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 145*(140)^2 / 6 | Answer: 473667 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (85 mm x 120 mm) carries a bending moment of 20 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (45 mm x 140 mm) has effective length 1700 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 650 MPa is designed for a working stress of 160 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 650, sw = 160 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 650 / 160 | Answer: 4.062

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 450 mm and wall thickness 20 mm carries an internal pressure of 0.6 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 450, t = 20, P = 0.6 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 0.6*450 / (2*20) | Answer: 6.75 MPa

question: 5.7 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 140 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 5.7, dT = 140 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 5.7 * 0.718 * 140 | Answer: 573 kJ

question: 3.3 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 50 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.3, dT = 50 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 3.3 * 1.005 * 50 | Answer: 165.8 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 3.8 m^3 at 480 K with mass 4.5 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 3.8, Tk = 480, m = 4.5 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 4.5*0.287*480 / 3.8 | Answer: 163.1 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 2.8 kg of air expands isothermally at 480 K from volume V1 to 5*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.8, Tk = 480, ratio = 5 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 2.8*0.287*480*ln(5) | Answer: 620.8 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 0.5 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.22 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 0.5, D = 0.22 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*0.5*0.22 / 0.001 | Answer: 110000

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 10.9 m. Taking Cv = 0.96, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 10.9, cv = 0.96 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.96*sqrt(2*9.81*10.9) | Answer: 14.04 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 390 mm) water flows at 1.6 m/s. It contracts to diameter 90 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 390, d2 = 90, V1 = 1.6 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 1.6*(390/90)^2 | Answer: 30.04 m/s

question: Water flows at 2.3 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.46 m and length 160 m. With friction factor f = 0.022, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 39 teeth drives a gear of 111 teeth. If the pinion runs at 850 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 39, z2 = 111, N1 = 850 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 850*39 / 111 | Answer: 298.6 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 430 mm rotates at 350 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 430, N = 350 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.43)*350 / 60 | Answer: 7.88 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 36.1 kW at 850 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 36.1, N = 850 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(36.1*1000) / (2*pi*850) | Answer: 405.6 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 1.4 kg rotates at radius 0.22 m at 500 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 2700 N/m and mass 16.3 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 2700, m = 16.3 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(2700/16.3) | Answer: 2.048 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 4.8 m^2 and thickness 0.2 m has conductivity k = 46.1 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 30 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 4.8, L = 0.2, k = 46.1, dT = 30 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 46.1*4.8*30 / 0.2 | Answer: 33192 W

question: A surface of area 4.3 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 160 W/m^2-K to surroundings 110 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 4.3, h = 160, dT = 110 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 160*4.3*110 | Answer: 75680 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 200 m/min, feed = 0.27 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2.3 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 200, f = 0.27, d = 2.3 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*200*0.27*2.3 | Answer: 124200 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 160 mm is turned at 500 rpm with a feed of 0.13 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 160, N = 500, f = 0.13 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 160 / (0.13*500) | Answer: 2.462 min

question: A resistor of 128 ohm carries a current of 3 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 128, I = 3 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 3 * 128 | Answer: 384 V

question: Three resistors 92 ohm, 3 ohm and 24 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 92, R2 = 3, R3 = 24 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 92 + 3 + 24 | Answer: 119 ohm

question: Two resistors 20 ohm and 16 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 20, R2 = 16 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 20*16 / (20+16) | Answer: 8.889 ohm

question: A device draws 14.1 A at 100 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 100, I = 14.1 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 100 * 14.1 | Answer: 1410 W

question: A current of 3.2 A flows through a 30 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 3.2, R = 30 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (3.2)^2 * 30 | Answer: 307.2 W

question: Two capacitors 25.4 uF and 16 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 25.4, C2 = 16 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 25.4*16 / (25.4+16) | Answer: 9.816 uF

question: A resistor 37 kohm and capacitor 9.4 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 37, C = 9.4 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (37k)(9.4u) = 347.8 ms | Answer: 347.8 ms

question: An inductor 336.9 mH is in series with 67 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 336.9, R = 67 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (336.9e-3) / 67 | Answer: 5.028 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 153.5 mH inductor at 740 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 153.5, f = 740 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (740)(153.5e-3) | Answer: 713.7 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 46.3 uF capacitor at 400 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 46.3, f = 400 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (400)(46.3e-6)) | Answer: 8.594 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 17 ohm, XL = 133 ohm and XC = 146 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 17, XL = 133, XC = 146 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(17^2 + (133 - 146)^2) | Answer: 21.4 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 37.1 mH and C = 6.2 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 37.1, C = 6.2 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(37.1e-3 * 6.2e-6)) | Answer: 331.8 Hz

question: A capacitor of 24.5 uF is charged to 90 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 24.5, V = 90 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*24.5e-6*(90)^2 | Answer: 99.22 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 200 V with 520 primary turns and 150 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 200, N1 = 520, N2 = 150 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 200 * 150/520 | Answer: 57.69 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 180 V and draws an armature current of 48 A. If the armature resistance is 0.74 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 180, Ia = 48, Ra = 0.74 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 180 - 48*0.74 | Answer: 144.5 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 140 A at 415 V (line) with a power factor of 0.79. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 140, VL = 415, pf = 0.79 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*415*140*0.79 / 1000 | Answer: 79.5 kW

question: A load has real power 100 kW and apparent power 185 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 100, S = 185 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 100 / 185 | Answer: 0.5405

question: A machine delivers 10 kW output while drawing 27 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 10, Pi = 27 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 10/27 * 100 | Answer: 37.04 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 7 V across R1 = 16 ohm and R2 = 4 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 7, R1 = 16, R2 = 4 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 7*4 / (16+4) | Answer: 1.4 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 130 kohm and Rin = 29 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 130, Rin = 29 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 130 / 29 | Answer: 4.483

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 200 kohm and Rg = 12 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 200, Rg = 12 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 200/12 | Answer: 17.67

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 5707. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 5707 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(5707) | Answer: 37.56 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 8.3 m carries a central point load of 115 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 8.3, W = 115 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 115*8.3 / 4 | Answer: 238.6 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 8.8 m carries a UDL of 40 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 8.8, w = 40 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 40*(8.8)^2 / 8 | Answer: 387.2 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 4.9 m carries a UDL of 12 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.9, w = 12 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 12*(4.9)^2 / 2 | Answer: 144.1 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 5.8 m carries a point load 50 kN at distance 1.6 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 5.8, a = 1.6, W = 50 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 50*(5.8 - 1.6) / 5.8 | Answer: 36.21 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 3.1 m) carries a central point load 65 kN. With E = 200 GPa and I = 190e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=65000 N, L=3100.0 mm, E=200000 MPa, I=190e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 1.062 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 5.6 m carries a UDL of 6 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.6, w = 6 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 6*(5.6)^2 / 12 | Answer: 15.68 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 540 mm, clear cover 25 mm and main bars of diameter 12 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 540, c = 25, dia = 12 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 540 - 25 - 12/2 | Answer: 509 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 11.2 m^2 carrying a factored load of 12.8 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 11.2, w = 12.8 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 12.8 * 11.2 | Answer: 143.4 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 5 m, unit weight 17 kN/m^3, phi = 29 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 3.9e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1.2, area = 6.2e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 3.9, i = 1.2, A = 6.2 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (3.9e-4)*1.2*(6.2e-3) | Answer: 2902 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 0.7 m, bed slope 0.007 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.028. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 4.5 m under a head of 0.4 m. Taking Cd = 0.62 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 3.3 m wide carries a discharge of 13.8 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 170 m and design speed 100 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 170, V = 100 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (100)^2 / (127*170) | Answer: 0.4632
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: A tank of volume 900 m^3 treats a flow of 40 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 900, Q = 40 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 900 / 40 | Answer: 22.5 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 290 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.22 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 8 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 290, k = 0.22, t = 8 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 290*(1 - e^(-0.22*8)) | Answer: 240.1 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.83, rainfall intensity 30 mm/h over a catchment of 10.9 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.83, i = 30, A = 10.9 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.83*30*10.9 / 360 | Answer: 0.7539 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.03 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 270 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.03, M = 270 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 270*(30+0.03)/30 | Answer: 270.3 m

question: Convert the decimal number 1871 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 1871 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 74F (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 11101101 and 11111011.
solution: XOR: 00010110 | Count of 1s = 3 | Answer: 3
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 580 megabits is sent over a link of 40 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 580, B = 40 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 580 / 40 | Answer: 14.5 s

question: A link has bandwidth 66 Mbps and round-trip time 10 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 66, R = 10 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 66e6 * 10e-3 bits = 660 kb | Answer: 660 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.93, cache access time 3 ns and main-memory access time 90 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.93, tc = 3, tm = 90 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.93*3 + (1 - 0.93)*90 | Answer: 9.09 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 881970 elements?
solution: Given: n = 881970 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(881970)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.003, memory access time 200 ns and page-fault service time 10 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 10 ms = 10000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.003)*200 + 0.003*10000000.0 ns | Answer: 30.2 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 0.3 m^3 at 450 kPa and 430 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 0.3, P = 450, Tk = 430 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (450e3)*0.3 / (8.314*430) | Answer: 37.76 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.35 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 11 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.35, t = 11 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.35*11) | Answer: 0.9787

question: For a reaction with A = 8e10 /s and activation energy 80 kJ/mol at 420 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 8, Ea = 80, Tk = 420 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 8e10 * exp(-80e3 / (8.314*420)) | Answer: 8.98 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.94 and bottoms xW = 0.09, with relative volatility alpha = 3. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.94, xw = 0.09, al = 3 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.94/0.06)(0.91/0.09)] / ln(3) | Answer: 4.611 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.8 and x = 0.22. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.8, x = 0.22 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.8/0.2) / (0.22/0.78) | Answer: 14.18

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.2 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 95 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.2, Psat = 95 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.2 * 95 | Answer: 19 kPa

question: A stream of 1.5 kg/s with specific heat 3.7 kJ/kg-K is heated through 120 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 1.5, cp = 3.7, dT = 120 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 1.5*3.7*120 | Answer: 666 kW

question: A reactor of volume 17.4 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 3.9 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 17.4, Q = 3.9 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 17.4 / 3.9 | Answer: 4.462 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 3.7e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 3 mm with a concentration difference of 160 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 3.7, L = 3, dC = 160 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (3.7e-9)*160 / (3e-3) | Answer: 197.3 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 3.3 min and steady-state gain 1.8. For a step input of magnitude 15, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 3.3, K = 1.8, M = 15 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 1.8 * 15 | Answer: 27 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 90 m^2 flies at 240 m/s (air density 1.225 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.3. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 90, V = 240, rho = 1.225, CL = 0.3 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1.225*(240)^2*90*0.3 / 1000 | Answer: 952.6 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 15 m^2 flies at 70 m/s (density 0.7 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.1. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 15, V = 70, rho = 0.7, CD = 0.1 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.7*(70)^2*15*0.1 / 1000 | Answer: 2.572 kN

question: A specimen under stress 330 MPa shows an elastic strain of 0.6e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 330, eps = 0.6 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 330 / (0.6e-3) MPa = 550 GPa | Answer: 550 GPa

question: A block of mass 2 kg has a volume of 4.7e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 2, V = 4.7 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 2 / (4.7e-3) | Answer: 425.5 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 2400 mm is heated through 60 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 23e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 2400, dT = 60, al = 23 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 2400*23e-6*60 | Answer: 3.312 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 80 ohm, R2 = 195 ohm and R3 = 475 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 80, R2 = 195, R3 = 475 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 195*475 / 80 | Answer: 1158 ohm

question: A measurement reads 9.77 when the true value is 10. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.77, true = 10 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.77 - 10| / 10 * 100 | Answer: 2.3 %

question: Annual demand is 24500 units, ordering cost 300 per order and holding cost 26 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 24500, S = 300, H = 26 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*24500*300 / 26) | Answer: 751.9 units

question: An asset costs 420000 with salvage value 2000 after 10 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 420000, Sv = 2000, n = 10 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (420000 - 2000) / 10 | Answer: 41800 per year

question: A product sells for 260 per unit with variable cost 90 per unit and fixed costs 45000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 260, V = 90, F = 45000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 45000 / (260 - 90) | Answer: 264.7 units

question: Find the present worth of 50000 received 3 years from now at an interest rate of 5% per year.
solution: Given: F = 50000, n = 3, i = 5 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 50000 / (1 + 0.05)^3 | Answer: 43192 currency units

question: A process produces 15 defective items in a batch of 12500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 15, N = 12500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 15/12500 * 1e6 | Answer: 1200 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -5x^3 - 5x^2 + 3x - 8 evaluated at x = 1.
For f(x) = 4x^3 - 2x^2 + 6x + 4, find f''(x) at x = 4.
Evaluate the definite integral of (-2x^2 + 5x - 3) dx from x = -3 to x = 3.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = -2x^3/3 + 5x^2/2 + -3x | Evaluate F(3) - F(-3) | Answer: -54
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 4x^2 + 12x - 7 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[-4, 1], [3, -1]].
solution: Given: a = -4, b = 1, c = 3, d = -1 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (-4)(-1) - (1)(3) | Answer: 1

question: Find the determinant of [[2, -3, 0], [-2, -5, 3], [5, 6, 2]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: -113

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[7, -3], [1, -6]].
solution: Trace tr = 1, Determinant = -39 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 6.765

question: Solve for x: 4x + 3y = -11 and -4x + 3y = -3.
solution: Determinant = 4*3 - 3*-4 = 24 | x = (e d - b f) / det = -1 | Answer: x = -1
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 47, 27, 25, 91, 24.
solution: Sum = 214 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 42.8 | Answer: 42.8

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 44, 23, 13, 39, 20.
solution: Mean = 27.8 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 13.14

question: Find the slope of the line through (1, 0) and (5, -4).
solution: Given: x1 = 1, y1 = 0, x2 = 5, y2 = -4 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (-4 - 0) / (5 - 1) | Answer: -1

question: Find the distance between the points (8, 9) and (7, -9).
solution: Given: x1 = 8, y1 = 9, x2 = 7, y2 = -9 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-1)^2 + (-18)^2) | Answer: 18.03 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (4,-7), (3,1), (0,-8).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 16.5 sq units

question: Find the 20th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 0 and common difference -8.
solution: Given: a = 0, d = -8, n = 20 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = 0 + (20 - 1)*-8 | Answer: -152

question: Find the sum of the first 20 terms of an AP with first term 8 and common difference 7.
solution: Given: a = 8, d = 7, n = 20 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 20/2 [2*8 + (20-1)*7] | Answer: 1490

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 43500 at 6.9% per annum for 6 years.
solution: Given: P = 43500, R = 6.9, Tt = 6 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 43500 * 6.9 * 6 / 100 | Answer: 18009 currency units

question: Find the amount when 16500 is invested at 5% per annum compounded annually for 4 years.
solution: Given: P = 16500, R = 5, Tt = 4 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 16500 * (1 + 5/100)^4 | Answer: 20056 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (4, -7, -6) and (-2, -2, 8).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (-3, -6, -2) and (2, 2, -5).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 39.41

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (6, -4, 0) and (-3, -2, 5).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 103 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number -9 + 0i.
solution: Given: a = -9, b = 0 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((-9)^2 + (0)^2) | Answer: 9

question: Evaluate f(x) = 2x^3 - 2x^2 + 9x + 7 at x = 3.
solution: Given: a = 2, b = -2, c = 9, d = 7, x0 = 3 | Formula: f(x0) = a x0^3 + b x0^2 + c x0 + d | Substitute: f(3) = 2(3)^3 + -2(3)^2 + 9(3) + 7 | Answer: 70

question: Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-18 with initial guess x0=7, find x1 (one iteration).
solution: Given: N = 18, x0 = 7 | Formula: x1 = x0 - (x0^2 - N)/(2 x0) | Substitute: x1 = 7 - ((7)^2 - 18)/(2*7) | Answer: 4.786

question: Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=0.9 and ordinates 6, 18, 18, 4, 7, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 87 and 14.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 87 and 14 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 48 and 29.
solution: Given: a = 48, b = 29 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 48*29 / 1 | Answer: 1392
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 36 mm carries an axial tensile load of 30 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 35 mm and length 1900 mm carries an axial load of 80 kN. Take E = 200 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 30 mm transmits a torque of 2900 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
