question: Find the larger real root of 2x^2 + 9x - 8 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[-7, 3], [9, -9]].
solution: Given: a = -7, b = 3, c = 9, d = -9 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (-7)(-9) - (3)(9) | Answer: 36

question: Find the determinant of [[-5, -3, 2], [0, -1, 3], [-2, -1, -5]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: -26

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[-5, -6], [-4, -2]].
solution: Trace tr = -7, Determinant = -14 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 1.623

question: Solve for x: -6x + -2y = 9 and -2x + -3y = 10.
solution: Determinant = -6*-3 - -2*-2 = 14 | x = (e d - b f) / det = -0.5 | Answer: x = -0.5
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 30, 24, 75, 95, 99.
solution: Sum = 323 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 64.6 | Answer: 64.6

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 16, 24, 1, 44, 23.
solution: Mean = 21.6 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 15.53

question: Find the slope of the line through (3, -5) and (-5, 3).
solution: Given: x1 = 3, y1 = -5, x2 = -5, y2 = 3 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (3 - -5) / (-5 - 3) | Answer: -1

question: Find the distance between the points (-1, -4) and (-9, 8).
solution: Given: x1 = -1, y1 = -4, x2 = -9, y2 = 8 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-8)^2 + (12)^2) | Answer: 14.42 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (-2,-2), (-1,-4), (-2,3).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 2.5 sq units

question: Find the 36th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -19 and common difference -9.
solution: Given: a = -19, d = -9, n = 36 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -19 + (36 - 1)*-9 | Answer: -334

question: Find the sum of the first 24 terms of an AP with first term 11 and common difference -2.
solution: Given: a = 11, d = -2, n = 24 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 24/2 [2*11 + (24-1)*-2] | Answer: -288

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 7000 at 11.5% per annum for 1 years.
solution: Given: P = 7000, R = 11.5, Tt = 1 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 7000 * 11.5 * 1 / 100 | Answer: 805 currency units

question: Find the amount when 28500 is invested at 11.4% per annum compounded annually for 3 years.
solution: Given: P = 28500, R = 11.4, Tt = 3 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 28500 * (1 + 11.4/100)^3 | Answer: 394 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (2, 8, -7) and (-8, 6, 0).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (-3, 5, 6) and (-1, -4, -5).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 27.04

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (5, -2, 5) and (2, -2, 4).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 19.19 degrees

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number 5 + -11i.
solution: Given: a = 5, b = -11 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(-11, 5) | Answer: -65.56 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -5x^3 - 2x^2 + 3x + 3 at x = -2.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-119 with initial guess x0=10, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.8 and ordinates 1, 4, 2, 5, 5, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 204 and 173.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 204 and 173 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 51 and 59.
solution: Given: a = 51, b = 59 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 51*59 / 1 | Answer: 3009
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 44 mm carries an axial tensile load of 103 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 13 mm and length 600 mm carries an axial load of 30 kN. Take E = 70 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 25 mm transmits a torque of 1900 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 25, Tt = 1900 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(1900*1000) / (pi*(25)^3) | Answer: 619.3 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 57 mm and length 1900 mm carries a torque of 1500 N-m. With G = 77 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (57)^4 / 32 = 1036333 mm^4 | theta = (1500*1000)(1900) / (77000 * 1036333) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 2.046 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 119 mm wide and 160 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 119, h = 160 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 119*(160)^2 / 6 | Answer: 507733 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (101 mm x 90 mm) carries a bending moment of 18 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (46 mm x 160 mm) has effective length 2700 mm and E = 200 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 700 MPa is designed for a working stress of 220 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 700, sw = 220 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 700 / 220 | Answer: 3.182

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 700 mm and wall thickness 15 mm carries an internal pressure of 2 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 700, t = 15, P = 2 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 2*700 / (2*15) | Answer: 46.67 MPa

question: 3.6 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 140 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.6, dT = 140 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 3.6 * 0.718 * 140 | Answer: 361.9 kJ

question: 4.5 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 180 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.5, dT = 180 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 4.5 * 1.005 * 180 | Answer: 814 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 3.8 m^3 at 470 K with mass 3.8 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 3.8, Tk = 470, m = 3.8 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 3.8*0.287*470 / 3.8 | Answer: 134.9 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 2.6 kg of air expands isothermally at 420 K from volume V1 to 4*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.6, Tk = 420, ratio = 4 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 2.6*0.287*420*ln(4) | Answer: 434.5 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 3.7 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.39 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 3.7, D = 0.39 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*3.7*0.39 / 0.001 | Answer: 1443000

question: Water flows at 0.9 m/s through a pipe of diameter 60 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 3.7 m. Taking Cv = 0.97, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 3.7, cv = 0.97 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.97*sqrt(2*9.81*3.7) | Answer: 8.265 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 230 mm) water flows at 1.8 m/s. It contracts to diameter 80 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 230, d2 = 80, V1 = 1.8 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 1.8*(230/80)^2 | Answer: 14.88 m/s

question: Water flows at 2.4 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.29 m and length 340 m. With friction factor f = 0.034, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).

question: A pinion of 25 teeth drives a gear of 76 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1050 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.

question: A pulley of diameter 530 mm rotates at 1300 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 530, N = 1300 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.53)*1300 / 60 | Answer: 36.08 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 19.9 kW at 1000 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 19.9, N = 1000 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(19.9*1000) / (2*pi*1000) | Answer: 190 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 7.7 kg rotates at radius 0.52 m at 550 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 3200 N/m and mass 11 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 3200, m = 11 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(3200/11) | Answer: 2.715 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 8.4 m^2 and thickness 0.34 m has conductivity k = 44 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 160 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 8.4, L = 0.34, k = 44, dT = 160 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 44*8.4*160 / 0.34 | Answer: 173929 W

question: A surface of area 4.2 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 135 W/m^2-K to surroundings 150 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 4.2, h = 135, dT = 150 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 135*4.2*150 | Answer: 85050 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 210 m/min, feed = 0.33 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2.3 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 210, f = 0.33, d = 2.3 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*210*0.33*2.3 | Answer: 159390 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 160 mm is turned at 800 rpm with a feed of 0.15 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 160, N = 800, f = 0.15 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 160 / (0.15*800) | Answer: 1.333 min

question: A resistor of 175 ohm carries a current of 0.4 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 175, I = 0.4 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 0.4 * 175 | Answer: 70 V

question: Three resistors 22 ohm, 12 ohm and 31 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 22, R2 = 12, R3 = 31 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 22 + 12 + 31 | Answer: 65 ohm

question: Two resistors 94 ohm and 53 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 94, R2 = 53 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 94*53 / (94+53) | Answer: 33.89 ohm

question: A device draws 3.6 A at 145 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 145, I = 3.6 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 145 * 3.6 | Answer: 522 W

question: A current of 8.4 A flows through a 88 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 8.4, R = 88 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (8.4)^2 * 88 | Answer: 6209 W

question: Two capacitors 42.4 uF and 28.1 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 42.4, C2 = 28.1 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 42.4*28.1 / (42.4+28.1) | Answer: 16.9 uF

question: A resistor 5 kohm and capacitor 10.4 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 5, C = 10.4 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (5k)(10.4u) = 52 ms | Answer: 52 ms

question: An inductor 490 mH is in series with 161 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 490, R = 161 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (490e-3) / 161 | Answer: 3.043 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 56.4 mH inductor at 420 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 56.4, f = 420 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (420)(56.4e-3) | Answer: 148.8 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 46.2 uF capacitor at 1000 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 46.2, f = 1000 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (1000)(46.2e-6)) | Answer: 3.445 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 76 ohm, XL = 27 ohm and XC = 53 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 76, XL = 27, XC = 53 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(76^2 + (27 - 53)^2) | Answer: 80.32 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 98.8 mH and C = 7.4 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 98.8, C = 7.4 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(98.8e-3 * 7.4e-6)) | Answer: 186.1 Hz

question: A capacitor of 61.2 uF is charged to 30 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 61.2, V = 30 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*61.2e-6*(30)^2 | Answer: 27.54 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 120 V with 690 primary turns and 100 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 120, N1 = 690, N2 = 100 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 120 * 100/690 | Answer: 17.39 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 170 V and draws an armature current of 47 A. If the armature resistance is 0.1 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 170, Ia = 47, Ra = 0.1 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 170 - 47*0.1 | Answer: 165.3 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 140 A at 415 V (line) with a power factor of 0.87. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 140, VL = 415, pf = 0.87 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*415*140*0.87 / 1000 | Answer: 87.55 kW

question: A machine delivers 90 kW output while drawing 162 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 90, Pi = 162 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 90/162 * 100 | Answer: 55.56 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 9 V across R1 = 3 ohm and R2 = 22 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 220 kohm and Rin = 2 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 140 kohm and Rg = 13 kohm. Find the voltage gain.

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 6695. Express the gain in decibels (power).

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.5 m carries a central point load of 80 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.

question: A simply supported beam of span 5.1 m carries a UDL of 10 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.1, w = 10 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 10*(5.1)^2 / 8 | Answer: 32.51 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 4.1 m carries a point load 30 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.1, W = 30 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 30*4.1 | Answer: 123 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 1.4 m carries a UDL of 36 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.8 m carries a point load 45 kN at distance 2.1 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 4.8, a = 2.1, W = 45 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 45*(4.8 - 2.1) / 4.8 | Answer: 25.31 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 6.6 m) carries a central point load 25 kN. With E = 25 GPa and I = 370e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.

question: An RC beam has overall depth 430 mm, clear cover 50 mm and main bars of diameter 16 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.

question: A column supports a floor area of 24.7 m^2 carrying a factored load of 12.5 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 24.7, w = 12.5 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 12.5 * 24.7 | Answer: 308.8 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 6 m, unit weight 19 kN/m^3, phi = 37 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 1.2e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1.4, area = 3.9e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 1.2, i = 1.4, A = 3.9 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (1.2e-4)*1.4*(3.9e-3) | Answer: 655.2 mm^3/s

question: A tank of volume 120 m^3 treats a flow of 120 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 400 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.18 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 3 days.

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.67, rainfall intensity 60 mm/h over a catchment of 50 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.67, i = 60, A = 50 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.67*60*50 / 360 | Answer: 5.583 m^3/s

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.05 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 430 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.05, M = 430 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 430*(20+0.05)/20 | Answer: 431.1 m

question: A file of 980 megabits is sent over a link of 90 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.

question: A link has bandwidth 13 Mbps and round-trip time 180 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 13, R = 180 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 13e6 * 180e-3 bits = 2340 kb | Answer: 2340 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.82, cache access time 6 ns and main-memory access time 60 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.82, tc = 6, tm = 60 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.82*6 + (1 - 0.82)*60 | Answer: 15.72 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 594504 elements?

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.004, memory access time 120 ns and page-fault service time 4 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 4 ms = 4000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.004)*120 + 0.004*4000000.0 ns | Answer: 16.12 microseconds

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 2.4 m^3 at 290 kPa and 460 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 2.4, P = 290, Tk = 460 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (290e3)*2.4 / (8.314*460) | Answer: 182 mol

question: For a reaction with A = 6e10 /s and activation energy 70 kJ/mol at 450 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 6, Ea = 70, Tk = 450 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 6e10 * exp(-70e3 / (8.314*450)) | Answer: 449.2 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.93 and bottoms xW = 0.06, with relative volatility alpha = 1.5. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.93, xw = 0.06, al = 1.5 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.93/0.07)(0.94/0.06)] / ln(1.5) | Answer: 13.17 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.65 and x = 0.47. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.64 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 55 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.64, Psat = 55 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.64 * 55 | Answer: 35.2 kPa

question: A stream of 2 kg/s with specific heat 1.6 kJ/kg-K is heated through 120 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 2, cp = 1.6, dT = 120 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 2*1.6*120 | Answer: 384 kW

question: A reactor of volume 19.6 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 3.3 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 19.6, Q = 3.3 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 19.6 / 3.3 | Answer: 5.939 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 5.7e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 3 mm with a concentration difference of 110 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 5.7, L = 3, dC = 110 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (5.7e-9)*110 / (3e-3) | Answer: 209 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 2.1 min and steady-state gain 1.7. For a step input of magnitude 13, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 2.1, K = 1.7, M = 13 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 1.7 * 13 | Answer: 22.1 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 80 m^2 flies at 220 m/s (air density 1.225 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.8. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 80, V = 220, rho = 1.225, CL = 0.8 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1.225*(220)^2*80*0.8 / 1000 | Answer: 1897 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 85 m^2 flies at 150 m/s (density 1 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.05. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 85, V = 150, rho = 1, CD = 0.05 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*1*(150)^2*85*0.05 / 1000 | Answer: 47.81 kN

question: A specimen under stress 340 MPa shows an elastic strain of 1.3e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 340, eps = 1.3 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 340 / (1.3e-3) MPa = 261.5 GPa | Answer: 261.5 GPa

question: A block of mass 6 kg has a volume of 0.7e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 6, V = 0.7 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 6 / (0.7e-3) | Answer: 8571 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 2300 mm is heated through 130 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 12e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 2300, dT = 130, al = 12 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 2300*12e-6*130 | Answer: 3.588 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 20 ohm, R2 = 135 ohm and R3 = 45 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 20, R2 = 135, R3 = 45 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 135*45 / 20 | Answer: 303.8 ohm

question: A measurement reads 10.36 when the true value is 50. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10.36, true = 50 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10.36 - 50| / 50 * 100 | Answer: 79.28 %

question: Annual demand is 43000 units, ordering cost 20 per order and holding cost 11 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 43000, S = 20, H = 11 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*43000*20 / 11) | Answer: 395.4 units

question: An asset costs 370000 with salvage value 10000 after 5 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 370000, Sv = 10000, n = 5 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (370000 - 10000) / 5 | Answer: 72000 per year

question: A product sells for 70 per unit with variable cost 30 per unit and fixed costs 95000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 70, V = 30, F = 95000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 95000 / (70 - 30) | Answer: 2375 units

question: Find the present worth of 90000 received 3 years from now at an interest rate of 6% per year.
solution: Given: F = 90000, n = 3, i = 6 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 90000 / (1 + 0.06)^3 | Answer: 75566 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.98, 0.92 and 0.91 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.

question: A process produces 50 defective items in a batch of 12500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 50, N = 12500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 50/12500 * 1e6 | Answer: 4000 PPM

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (-4, 2, 5) and (-2, -4, -3).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 114.5 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number -12 + -1i.
solution: Given: a = -12, b = -1 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((-12)^2 + (-1)^2) | Answer: 12.04

question: Evaluate f(x) = -x^3 + 3x^2 + 7x + 7 at x = 2.
solution: Given: a = -1, b = 3, c = 7, d = 7, x0 = 2 | Formula: f(x0) = a x0^3 + b x0^2 + c x0 + d | Substitute: f(2) = -1(2)^3 + 3(2)^2 + 7(2) + 7 | Answer: 25

question: Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-19 with initial guess x0=7, find x1 (one iteration).
solution: Given: N = 19, x0 = 7 | Formula: x1 = x0 - (x0^2 - N)/(2 x0) | Substitute: x1 = 7 - ((7)^2 - 19)/(2*7) | Answer: 4.857

question: Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.9 and ordinates 8, 14, 0, 20, 6, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 462 and 239.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 462 and 239 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 38 and 51.
solution: Given: a = 38, b = 51 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 38*51 / 1 | Answer: 1938
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 42 mm carries an axial tensile load of 106 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 34 mm and length 2800 mm carries an axial load of 42 kN. Take E = 70 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 77 mm transmits a torque of 2950 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 77, Tt = 2950 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(2950*1000) / (pi*(77)^3) | Answer: 32.91 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 55 mm and length 800 mm carries a torque of 900 N-m. With G = 80 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (55)^4 / 32 = 898361 mm^4 | theta = (900*1000)(800) / (80000 * 898361) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 0.574 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 143 mm wide and 300 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 143, h = 300 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 143*(300)^2 / 6 | Answer: 2145000 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (43 mm x 150 mm) carries a bending moment of 8 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (68 mm x 100 mm) has effective length 3000 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 550 MPa is designed for a working stress of 170 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 550, sw = 170 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 550 / 170 | Answer: 3.235

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 350 mm and wall thickness 15 mm carries an internal pressure of 1 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 350, t = 15, P = 1 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 1*350 / (2*15) | Answer: 11.67 MPa

question: 2.5 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 175 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.5, dT = 175 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 2.5 * 0.718 * 175 | Answer: 314.1 kJ

question: 1.9 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 165 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1.9, dT = 165 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 1.9 * 1.005 * 165 | Answer: 315.1 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 2.8 m^3 at 400 K with mass 1.6 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 2.8, Tk = 400, m = 1.6 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 1.6*0.287*400 / 2.8 | Answer: 65.6 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 1.3 kg of air expands isothermally at 330 K from volume V1 to 3*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1.3, Tk = 330, ratio = 3 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 1.3*0.287*330*ln(3) | Answer: 135.3 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 1.9 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.36 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 1.9, D = 0.36 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*1.9*0.36 / 0.001 | Answer: 684000

question: Water flows at 2.4 m/s through a pipe of diameter 210 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 16.3 m. Taking Cv = 0.95, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 16.3, cv = 0.95 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.95*sqrt(2*9.81*16.3) | Answer: 16.99 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 290 mm) water flows at 1.7 m/s. It contracts to diameter 90 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 290, d2 = 90, V1 = 1.7 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 1.7*(290/90)^2 | Answer: 17.65 m/s

question: Water flows at 3 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.49 m and length 110 m. With friction factor f = 0.039, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 27 teeth drives a gear of 69 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1300 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 27, z2 = 69, N1 = 1300 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1300*27 / 69 | Answer: 508.7 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 420 mm rotates at 550 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 420, N = 550 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.42)*550 / 60 | Answer: 12.1 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 4.5 kW at 1350 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 4.5, N = 1350 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(4.5*1000) / (2*pi*1350) | Answer: 31.83 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 7.3 kg rotates at radius 0.13 m at 1150 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 900 N/m and mass 2.6 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 900, m = 2.6 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(900/2.6) | Answer: 2.961 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 1.2 m^2 and thickness 0.25 m has conductivity k = 26.8 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 125 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 1.2, L = 0.25, k = 26.8, dT = 125 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 26.8*1.2*125 / 0.25 | Answer: 16080 W

question: A surface of area 5.3 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 10 W/m^2-K to surroundings 65 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 5.3, h = 10, dT = 65 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 10*5.3*65 | Answer: 3445 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 60 m/min, feed = 0.4 mm/rev, depth of cut = 1.5 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 60, f = 0.4, d = 1.5 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*60*0.4*1.5 | Answer: 36000 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 270 mm is turned at 500 rpm with a feed of 0.13 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 270, N = 500, f = 0.13 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 270 / (0.13*500) | Answer: 4.154 min

question: A resistor of 92 ohm carries a current of 6.6 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 92, I = 6.6 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 6.6 * 92 | Answer: 607.2 V

question: Three resistors 72 ohm, 14 ohm and 60 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 72, R2 = 14, R3 = 60 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 72 + 14 + 60 | Answer: 146 ohm

question: Two resistors 102 ohm and 10 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 102, R2 = 10 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 102*10 / (102+10) | Answer: 9.107 ohm

question: A device draws 0.1 A at 15 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 15, I = 0.1 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 15 * 0.1 | Answer: 1.5 W

question: A current of 5.3 A flows through a 52 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 5.3, R = 52 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (5.3)^2 * 52 | Answer: 1461 W

question: Two capacitors 49.9 uF and 1 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 49.9, C2 = 1 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 49.9*1 / (49.9+1) | Answer: 0.9804 uF

question: A resistor 47 kohm and capacitor 2.7 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 47, C = 2.7 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (47k)(2.7u) = 126.9 ms | Answer: 126.9 ms

question: An inductor 314.3 mH is in series with 53 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 314.3, R = 53 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (314.3e-3) / 53 | Answer: 5.93 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 168.7 mH inductor at 260 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 168.7, f = 260 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (260)(168.7e-3) | Answer: 275.6 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 16.5 uF capacitor at 550 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 16.5, f = 550 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (550)(16.5e-6)) | Answer: 17.54 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 77 ohm, XL = 52 ohm and XC = 62 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 77, XL = 52, XC = 62 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(77^2 + (52 - 62)^2) | Answer: 77.65 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 26.1 mH and C = 6.4 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 26.1, C = 6.4 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(26.1e-3 * 6.4e-6)) | Answer: 389.4 Hz

question: A capacitor of 13.8 uF is charged to 170 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 13.8, V = 170 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*13.8e-6*(170)^2 | Answer: 199.4 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 190 V with 210 primary turns and 30 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 190, N1 = 210, N2 = 30 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 190 * 30/210 | Answer: 27.14 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 270 V and draws an armature current of 59 A. If the armature resistance is 0.15 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 270, Ia = 59, Ra = 0.15 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 270 - 59*0.15 | Answer: 261.1 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 45 A at 433 V (line) with a power factor of 0.86. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 45, VL = 433, pf = 0.86 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*433*45*0.86 / 1000 | Answer: 29.02 kW

question: A load has real power 155 kW and apparent power 160 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 155, S = 160 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 155 / 160 | Answer: 0.9688

question: A machine delivers 90 kW output while drawing 127 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 90, Pi = 127 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 90/127 * 100 | Answer: 70.87 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 25 V across R1 = 15 ohm and R2 = 5 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 25, R1 = 15, R2 = 5 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 25*5 / (15+5) | Answer: 6.25 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 130 kohm and Rin = 2 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 130, Rin = 2 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 130 / 2 | Answer: 65

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 200 kohm and Rg = 34 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 200, Rg = 34 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 200/34 | Answer: 6.882

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 519. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 519 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(519) | Answer: 27.15 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 7.6 m carries a central point load of 60 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7.6, W = 60 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 60*7.6 / 4 | Answer: 114 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.5 m carries a UDL of 25 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.5, w = 25 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 25*(4.5)^2 / 8 | Answer: 63.28 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 1.3 m carries a point load 60 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 1.3, W = 60 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 60*1.3 | Answer: 78 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 5.2 m carries a UDL of 34 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.2, w = 34 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 34*(5.2)^2 / 2 | Answer: 459.7 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 10 m carries a point load 70 kN at distance 3.8 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 10, a = 3.8, W = 70 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 70*(10 - 3.8) / 10 | Answer: 43.4 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 5.6 m) carries a central point load 20 kN. With E = 200 GPa and I = 540e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=20000 N, L=5600.0 mm, E=200000 MPa, I=540e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 0.6775 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 27.4 m^2 carrying a factored load of 19.5 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 27.4, w = 19.5 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 19.5 * 27.4 | Answer: 534.3 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 6.3 m, unit weight 17 kN/m^3, phi = 37 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 8e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1.4, area = 4.2e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 8, i = 1.4, A = 4.2 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (8e-4)*1.4*(4.2e-3) | Answer: 4704 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 2.5 m, bed slope 0.004 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.024. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 2.6 m under a head of 0.9 m. Taking Cd = 0.61 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 3.7 m wide carries a discharge of 22.5 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 200 m and design speed 90 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 200, V = 90 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (90)^2 / (127*200) | Answer: 0.3189
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: A tank of volume 770 m^3 treats a flow of 155 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 770, Q = 155 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 770 / 155 | Answer: 4.968 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 220 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.22 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 8 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 220, k = 0.22, t = 8 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 220*(1 - e^(-0.22*8)) | Answer: 182.2 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.65, rainfall intensity 70 mm/h over a catchment of 54.9 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.65, i = 70, A = 54.9 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.65*70*54.9 / 360 | Answer: 6.939 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.07 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 690 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.07, M = 690 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 690*(20+0.07)/20 | Answer: 692.4 m

question: Convert the decimal number 2779 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 2779 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: ADB (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 11010010 and 01111000.
solution: XOR: 10101010 | Count of 1s = 4 | Answer: 4
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 80 megabits is sent over a link of 56 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 80, B = 56 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 80 / 56 | Answer: 1.429 s

question: A link has bandwidth 4 Mbps and round-trip time 50 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 4, R = 50 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 4e6 * 50e-3 bits = 200 kb | Answer: 200 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.8, cache access time 10 ns and main-memory access time 120 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.8, tc = 10, tm = 120 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.8*10 + (1 - 0.8)*120 | Answer: 32 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 516340 elements?
solution: Given: n = 516340 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(516340)) + 1 | Answer: 19

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.014, memory access time 130 ns and page-fault service time 7 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 7 ms = 7000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.014)*130 + 0.014*7000000.0 ns | Answer: 98.13 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 2.8 m^3 at 150 kPa and 380 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 2.8, P = 150, Tk = 380 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (150e3)*2.8 / (8.314*380) | Answer: 132.9 mol

question: For a reaction with A = 3e10 /s and activation energy 55 kJ/mol at 300 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 3, Ea = 55, Tk = 300 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 3e10 * exp(-55e3 / (8.314*300)) | Answer: 7.951 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.94 and bottoms xW = 0.09, with relative volatility alpha = 2.8. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.94, xw = 0.09, al = 2.8 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.94/0.06)(0.91/0.09)] / ln(2.8) | Answer: 4.919 stages

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.18 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 60 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.18, Psat = 60 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.18 * 60 | Answer: 10.8 kPa

question: A stream of 3.6 kg/s with specific heat 2 kJ/kg-K is heated through 35 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 3.6, cp = 2, dT = 35 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 3.6*2*35 | Answer: 252 kW

question: A reactor of volume 5.4 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 2 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 5.4, Q = 2 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 5.4 / 2 | Answer: 2.7 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 1.9e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 4 mm with a concentration difference of 120 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 1.9, L = 4, dC = 120 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (1.9e-9)*120 / (4e-3) | Answer: 57 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 2.2 min and steady-state gain 3. For a step input of magnitude 12, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 2.2, K = 3, M = 12 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 3 * 12 | Answer: 36 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 20 m^2 flies at 250 m/s (air density 1.225 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 1.4. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 20, V = 250, rho = 1.225, CL = 1.4 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1.225*(250)^2*20*1.4 / 1000 | Answer: 1072 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 35 m^2 flies at 60 m/s (density 0.7 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.03. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 35, V = 60, rho = 0.7, CD = 0.03 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.7*(60)^2*35*0.03 / 1000 | Answer: 1.323 kN

question: A specimen under stress 330 MPa shows an elastic strain of 1.7e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 330, eps = 1.7 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 330 / (1.7e-3) MPa = 194.1 GPa | Answer: 194.1 GPa

question: A block of mass 46 kg has a volume of 5.3e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 46, V = 5.3 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 46 / (5.3e-3) | Answer: 8679 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 2600 mm is heated through 50 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 11e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 2600, dT = 50, al = 11 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 2600*11e-6*50 | Answer: 1.43 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 195 ohm, R2 = 195 ohm and R3 = 130 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 195, R2 = 195, R3 = 130 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 195*130 / 195 | Answer: 130 ohm

question: A measurement reads 9.53 when the true value is 100. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.53, true = 100 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.53 - 100| / 100 * 100 | Answer: 90.47 %

question: Annual demand is 45500 units, ordering cost 200 per order and holding cost 21 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 45500, S = 200, H = 21 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*45500*200 / 21) | Answer: 930.9 units

question: An asset costs 310000 with salvage value 16000 after 8 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 310000, Sv = 16000, n = 8 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (310000 - 16000) / 8 | Answer: 36750 per year

question: A product sells for 290 per unit with variable cost 60 per unit and fixed costs 85000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 290, V = 60, F = 85000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 85000 / (290 - 60) | Answer: 369.6 units

question: Find the present worth of 110000 received 10 years from now at an interest rate of 11% per year.
solution: Given: F = 110000, n = 10, i = 11 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 110000 / (1 + 0.11)^10 | Answer: 3874 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.97, 0.94 and 0.9 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.97, r2 = 0.94, r3 = 0.9 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.97*0.94*0.9 | Answer: 0.8206

question: A process produces 48 defective items in a batch of 11500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 48, N = 11500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 48/11500 * 1e6 | Answer: 4174 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = 6x^3 + 3x^2 - 5x - 7 evaluated at x = -4.
For f(x) = 6x^3 - 5x^2 - 2x + 5, find f''(x) at x = 0.

question: Find the larger real root of x^2 + 12x + 2 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[2, -6], [1, 1]].
solution: Given: a = 2, b = -6, c = 1, d = 1 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (2)(1) - (-6)(1) | Answer: 8

question: Find the determinant of [[0, 2, 1], [3, 2, -3], [3, 3, -3]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: 3

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[-2, -8], [-4, 0]].
solution: Trace tr = -2, Determinant = -32 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 4.745

question: Solve for x: -2x + -2y = 6 and -1x + 2y = -10.
solution: Determinant = -2*2 - -2*-1 = -6 | x = (e d - b f) / det = 1.333 | Answer: x = 1.333

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 77, 22, 82, 94, 96.
solution: Sum = 371 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 74.2 | Answer: 74.2

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 34, 36, 9, 19, 28.
solution: Mean = 25.2 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 11.21

question: Find the slope of the line through (-6, 0) and (4, 2).
solution: Given: x1 = -6, y1 = 0, x2 = 4, y2 = 2 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (2 - 0) / (4 - -6) | Answer: 0.2

question: Find the distance between the points (9, -1) and (-3, -1).
solution: Given: x1 = 9, y1 = -1, x2 = -3, y2 = -1 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-12)^2 + (0)^2) | Answer: 12 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (6,1), (-8,4), (-5,-1).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 30.5 sq units

question: Find the 29th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -12 and common difference -4.
solution: Given: a = -12, d = -4, n = 29 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -12 + (29 - 1)*-4 | Answer: -124

question: Find the sum of the first 17 terms of an AP with first term -7 and common difference -2.
solution: Given: a = -7, d = -2, n = 17 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 17/2 [2*-7 + (17-1)*-2] | Answer: -391

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 42000 at 11.6% per annum for 8 years.
solution: Given: P = 42000, R = 11.6, Tt = 8 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 42000 * 11.6 * 8 / 100 | Answer: 38976 currency units

question: Find the amount when 3500 is invested at 6% per annum compounded annually for 5 years.
solution: Given: P = 3500, R = 6, Tt = 5 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 3500 * (1 + 6/100)^5 | Answer: 4684 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (-8, 1, 3) and (4, -6, 7).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (-5, 6, -6) and (0, 5, 4).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 62.78

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (-4, 4, -1) and (2, 4, 3).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 80.7 degrees

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number 7 + -9i.
solution: Given: a = 7, b = -9 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(-9, 7) | Answer: -52.13 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -4x^3 + 7x^2 - 7x + 7 at x = -2.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-59 with initial guess x0=14, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.4 and ordinates 1, 9, 7, 16, 18, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 515 and 279.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 515 and 279 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 16 and 49.
solution: Given: a = 16, b = 49 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 16*49 / 1 | Answer: 784
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 18 mm carries an axial tensile load of 86 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 37 mm and length 1100 mm carries an axial load of 77 kN. Take E = 110 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 37 mm transmits a torque of 1300 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 37, Tt = 1300 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(1300*1000) / (pi*(37)^3) | Answer: 130.7 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 33 mm and length 1800 mm carries a torque of 1300 N-m. With G = 80 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (33)^4 / 32 = 116428 mm^4 | theta = (1300*1000)(1800) / (80000 * 116428) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 14.39 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 79 mm wide and 60 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 79, h = 60 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 79*(60)^2 / 6 | Answer: 47400 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (48 mm x 110 mm) carries a bending moment of 38 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (43 mm x 100 mm) has effective length 3500 mm and E = 200 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 900 MPa is designed for a working stress of 90 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 900, sw = 90 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 900 / 90 | Answer: 10

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 350 mm and wall thickness 12 mm carries an internal pressure of 1.2 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 350, t = 12, P = 1.2 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 1.2*350 / (2*12) | Answer: 17.5 MPa

question: 4.4 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 200 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.4, dT = 200 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 4.4 * 0.718 * 200 | Answer: 631.8 kJ

question: 6.1 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 185 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 6.1, dT = 185 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 6.1 * 1.005 * 185 | Answer: 1134 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 1 m^3 at 580 K with mass 2.8 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 1, Tk = 580, m = 2.8 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 2.8*0.287*580 / 1 | Answer: 466.1 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 3.1 kg of air expands isothermally at 330 K from volume V1 to 5*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.1, Tk = 330, ratio = 5 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 3.1*0.287*330*ln(5) | Answer: 472.5 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 5 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.34 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 5, D = 0.34 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*5*0.34 / 0.001 | Answer: 1700000

question: Water flows at 3.7 m/s through a pipe of diameter 250 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 7.5 m. Taking Cv = 0.95, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 7.5, cv = 0.95 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.95*sqrt(2*9.81*7.5) | Answer: 11.52 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 330 mm) water flows at 1.7 m/s. It contracts to diameter 90 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 330, d2 = 90, V1 = 1.7 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 1.7*(330/90)^2 | Answer: 22.86 m/s

question: Water flows at 3.5 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.11 m and length 260 m. With friction factor f = 0.035, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 22 teeth drives a gear of 114 teeth. If the pinion runs at 300 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 22, z2 = 114, N1 = 300 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 300*22 / 114 | Answer: 57.89 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 520 mm rotates at 750 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 520, N = 750 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.52)*750 / 60 | Answer: 20.42 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 21.5 kW at 600 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 21.5, N = 600 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(21.5*1000) / (2*pi*600) | Answer: 342.2 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 9.7 kg rotates at radius 0.56 m at 550 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 6200 N/m and mass 15.9 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 6200, m = 15.9 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(6200/15.9) | Answer: 3.143 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 8.1 m^2 and thickness 0.14 m has conductivity k = 46.9 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 55 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 8.1, L = 0.14, k = 46.9, dT = 55 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 46.9*8.1*55 / 0.14 | Answer: 149242 W

question: A surface of area 5.5 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 80 W/m^2-K to surroundings 25 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 5.5, h = 80, dT = 25 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 80*5.5*25 | Answer: 11000 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 80 m/min, feed = 0.18 mm/rev, depth of cut = 0.7 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 80, f = 0.18, d = 0.7 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*80*0.18*0.7 | Answer: 10080 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 190 mm is turned at 650 rpm with a feed of 0.19 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 190, N = 650, f = 0.19 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 190 / (0.19*650) | Answer: 1.538 min

question: A resistor of 86 ohm carries a current of 2.1 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 86, I = 2.1 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 2.1 * 86 | Answer: 180.6 V

question: Three resistors 81 ohm, 70 ohm and 21 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 81, R2 = 70, R3 = 21 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 81 + 70 + 21 | Answer: 172 ohm

question: Two resistors 59 ohm and 56 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 59, R2 = 56 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 59*56 / (59+56) | Answer: 28.73 ohm

question: A device draws 4.5 A at 185 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 185, I = 4.5 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 185 * 4.5 | Answer: 832.5 W

question: A current of 3.4 A flows through a 143 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 3.4, R = 143 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (3.4)^2 * 143 | Answer: 1653 W

question: Two capacitors 49.4 uF and 7.4 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 49.4, C2 = 7.4 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 49.4*7.4 / (49.4+7.4) | Answer: 6.436 uF

question: A resistor 27 kohm and capacitor 19.6 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 27, C = 19.6 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (27k)(19.6u) = 529.2 ms | Answer: 529.2 ms

question: An inductor 268.2 mH is in series with 140 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 268.2, R = 140 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (268.2e-3) / 140 | Answer: 1.916 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 102 mH inductor at 420 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 102, f = 420 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (420)(102e-3) | Answer: 269.2 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 31.4 uF capacitor at 130 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 31.4, f = 130 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (130)(31.4e-6)) | Answer: 38.99 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 30 ohm, XL = 141 ohm and XC = 31 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 30, XL = 141, XC = 31 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(30^2 + (141 - 31)^2) | Answer: 114 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 72.2 mH and C = 8.7 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 72.2, C = 8.7 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(72.2e-3 * 8.7e-6)) | Answer: 200.8 Hz

question: A capacitor of 77 uF is charged to 260 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 77, V = 260 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*77e-6*(260)^2 | Answer: 2603 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 300 V with 260 primary turns and 110 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 300, N1 = 260, N2 = 110 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 300 * 110/260 | Answer: 126.9 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 190 V and draws an armature current of 53 A. If the armature resistance is 1.07 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 190, Ia = 53, Ra = 1.07 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 190 - 53*1.07 | Answer: 133.3 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 100 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.85. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 100, VL = 400, pf = 0.85 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*400*100*0.85 / 1000 | Answer: 58.89 kW

question: A load has real power 15 kW and apparent power 195 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 15, S = 195 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 15 / 195 | Answer: 0.07692

question: A machine delivers 120 kW output while drawing 132 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 120, Pi = 132 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 120/132 * 100 | Answer: 90.91 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 26 V across R1 = 34 ohm and R2 = 48 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 26, R1 = 34, R2 = 48 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 26*48 / (34+48) | Answer: 15.22 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 200 kohm and Rin = 17 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 200, Rin = 17 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 200 / 17 | Answer: 11.76

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 5790. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 5790 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(5790) | Answer: 37.63 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 3.5 m carries a central point load of 20 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.5, W = 20 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 20*3.5 / 4 | Answer: 17.5 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 8.6 m carries a UDL of 35 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 8.6, w = 35 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 35*(8.6)^2 / 8 | Answer: 323.6 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 1.5 m carries a point load 55 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 1.5, W = 55 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 55*1.5 | Answer: 82.5 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 4.9 m carries a UDL of 10 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.9, w = 10 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 10*(4.9)^2 / 2 | Answer: 120.1 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 8.3 m carries a point load 65 kN at distance 2.6 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 8.3, a = 2.6, W = 65 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 65*(8.3 - 2.6) / 8.3 | Answer: 44.64 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 3.9 m) carries a central point load 25 kN. With E = 25 GPa and I = 250e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=25000 N, L=3900.0 mm, E=25000 MPa, I=250e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 4.943 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 9 m carries a UDL of 27 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 9, w = 27 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 27*(9)^2 / 12 | Answer: 182.2 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 300 mm, clear cover 50 mm and main bars of diameter 25 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 300, c = 50, dia = 25 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 300 - 50 - 25/2 | Answer: 237.5 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 22.2 m^2 carrying a factored load of 16 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 22.2, w = 16 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 16 * 22.2 | Answer: 355.2 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 4.2 m, unit weight 18 kN/m^3, phi = 33 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 5.1e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1.1, area = 6.7e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 5.1, i = 1.1, A = 6.7 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (5.1e-4)*1.1*(6.7e-3) | Answer: 3759 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 2 m, bed slope 0.009 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.016. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 3.8 m under a head of 0.8 m. Taking Cd = 0.63 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 2.9 m wide carries a discharge of 22 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
