question: Find the sum of the first 23 terms of an AP with first term 1 and common difference -6.
solution: Given: a = 1, d = -6, n = 23 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 23/2 [2*1 + (23-1)*-6] | Answer: -1495

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 25000 at 14.9% per annum for 8 years.
solution: Given: P = 25000, R = 14.9, Tt = 8 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 25000 * 14.9 * 8 / 100 | Answer: 29800 currency units

question: Find the amount when 2000 is invested at 6% per annum compounded annually for 5 years.
solution: Given: P = 2000, R = 6, Tt = 5 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 2000 * (1 + 6/100)^5 | Answer: 2676 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (-4, 2, -4) and (1, -5, -1).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (-6, -6, -1) and (-1, 0, 5).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 43.55

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (-5, -3, 1) and (6, 2, -5).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 149.3 degrees

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number 8 + 4i.
solution: Given: a = 8, b = 4 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(4, 8) | Answer: 26.57 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -2x^3 + 6x^2 - 5x - 7 at x = 1.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-53 with initial guess x0=7, find x1 (one iteration).
solution: Given: N = 53, x0 = 7 | Formula: x1 = x0 - (x0^2 - N)/(2 x0) | Substitute: x1 = 7 - ((7)^2 - 53)/(2*7) | Answer: 7.286

question: Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=0.6 and ordinates 5, 11, 1, 17, 2, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 301 and 250.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 301 and 250 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 75 and 10.
solution: Given: a = 75, b = 10 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 75*10 / 5 | Answer: 150
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 47 mm carries an axial tensile load of 15 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 19 mm and length 2200 mm carries an axial load of 71 kN. Take E = 110 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 43 mm transmits a torque of 2100 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 43, Tt = 2100 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(2100*1000) / (pi*(43)^3) | Answer: 134.5 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 43 mm and length 1300 mm carries a torque of 1300 N-m. With G = 77 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (43)^4 / 32 = 33564 mm^4 | theta = (1300*1000)(1300) / (77000 * 33564) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 3.747 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 133 mm wide and 280 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 133, h = 280 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 133*(280)^2 / 6 | Answer: 1737867 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (108 mm x 210 mm) carries a bending moment of 23 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (53 mm x 150 mm) has effective length 2000 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 890 MPa is designed for a working stress of 170 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 890, sw = 170 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 890 / 170 | Answer: 5.235

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 500 mm and wall thickness 8 mm carries an internal pressure of 2.3 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 500, t = 8, P = 2.3 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 2.3*500 / (2*8) | Answer: 71.88 MPa

question: 1.9 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 35 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1.9, dT = 35 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 1.9 * 0.718 * 35 | Answer: 47.75 kJ

question: 5.8 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 45 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 5.8, dT = 45 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 5.8 * 1.005 * 45 | Answer: 262.3 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 0.5 m^3 at 490 K with mass 4.8 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 0.5, Tk = 490, m = 4.8 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 4.8*0.287*490 / 0.5 | Answer: 135 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 2.6 kg of air expands isothermally at 310 K from volume V1 to 5*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.6, Tk = 310, ratio = 5 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 2.6*0.287*310*ln(5) | Answer: 372.3 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 4.1 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.37 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 4.1, D = 0.37 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*4.1*0.37 / 0.001 | Answer: 1517000

question: Water flows at 0.5 m/s through a pipe of diameter 50 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 18.5 m. Taking Cv = 0.96, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 18.5, cv = 0.96 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.96*sqrt(2*9.81*18.5) | Answer: 18.29 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 360 mm) water flows at 2.8 m/s. It contracts to diameter 50 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 360, d2 = 50, V1 = 2.8 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 2.8*(360/50)^2 | Answer: 145.2 m/s

question: Water flows at 1 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.11 m and length 300 m. With friction factor f = 0.031, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 35 teeth drives a gear of 55 teeth. If the pinion runs at 850 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 35, z2 = 55, N1 = 850 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 850*35 / 55 | Answer: 540.9 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 280 mm rotates at 550 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 280, N = 550 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.28)*550 / 60 | Answer: 8.063 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 8.7 kW at 450 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 8.7, N = 450 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(8.7*1000) / (2*pi*450) | Answer: 184.6 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 0.9 kg rotates at radius 0.18 m at 550 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 1400 N/m and mass 8 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 1400, m = 8 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(1400/8) | Answer: 2.105 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 3 m^2 and thickness 0.32 m has conductivity k = 26.6 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 200 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 3, L = 0.32, k = 26.6, dT = 200 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 26.6*3*200 / 0.32 | Answer: 49875 W

question: A surface of area 0.9 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 15 W/m^2-K to surroundings 115 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 0.9, h = 15, dT = 115 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 15*0.9*115 | Answer: 1552 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 140 m/min, feed = 0.43 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2.2 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 140, f = 0.43, d = 2.2 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*140*0.43*2.2 | Answer: 132440 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 370 mm is turned at 400 rpm with a feed of 0.25 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 370, N = 400, f = 0.25 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 370 / (0.25*400) | Answer: 3.7 min

question: A resistor of 113 ohm carries a current of 3.1 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 113, I = 3.1 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 3.1 * 113 | Answer: 350.3 V

question: Three resistors 51 ohm, 35 ohm and 68 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 51, R2 = 35, R3 = 68 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 51 + 35 + 68 | Answer: 154 ohm

question: Two resistors 42 ohm and 5 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 42, R2 = 5 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 42*5 / (42+5) | Answer: 4.468 ohm

question: A device draws 9.2 A at 225 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 225, I = 9.2 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 225 * 9.2 | Answer: 2070 W

question: A current of 5 A flows through a 26 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 5, R = 26 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (5)^2 * 26 | Answer: 650 W

question: Two capacitors 47.8 uF and 36.1 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 47.8, C2 = 36.1 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 47.8*36.1 / (47.8+36.1) | Answer: 20.57 uF

question: A resistor 14 kohm and capacitor 16.1 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 14, C = 16.1 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (14k)(16.1u) = 225.4 ms | Answer: 225.4 ms

question: An inductor 215.3 mH is in series with 116 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 215.3, R = 116 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (215.3e-3) / 116 | Answer: 1.856 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 62.1 mH inductor at 860 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 62.1, f = 860 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (860)(62.1e-3) | Answer: 335.6 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 23.1 uF capacitor at 690 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 23.1, f = 690 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (690)(23.1e-6)) | Answer: 9.985 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 39 ohm, XL = 70 ohm and XC = 60 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 39, XL = 70, XC = 60 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(39^2 + (70 - 60)^2) | Answer: 40.26 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 47 mH and C = 4.6 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 47, C = 4.6 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(47e-3 * 4.6e-6)) | Answer: 342.3 Hz

question: A capacitor of 87.3 uF is charged to 140 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 87.3, V = 140 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*87.3e-6*(140)^2 | Answer: 855.5 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 200 V with 480 primary turns and 310 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 200, N1 = 480, N2 = 310 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 200 * 310/480 | Answer: 129.2 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 360 V and draws an armature current of 53 A. If the armature resistance is 0.4 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 360, Ia = 53, Ra = 0.4 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 360 - 53*0.4 | Answer: 338.8 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 10 A at 433 V (line) with a power factor of 0.94. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 10, VL = 433, pf = 0.94 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*433*10*0.94 / 1000 | Answer: 7.05 kW

question: A load has real power 80 kW and apparent power 125 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 80, S = 125 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 80 / 125 | Answer: 0.64

question: A machine delivers 175 kW output while drawing 177 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 175, Pi = 177 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 175/177 * 100 | Answer: 98.87 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 23 V across R1 = 28 ohm and R2 = 38 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 23, R1 = 28, R2 = 38 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 23*38 / (28+38) | Answer: 13.24 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 100 kohm and Rin = 8 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 100, Rin = 8 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 100 / 8 | Answer: 12.5

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 170 kohm and Rg = 16 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 170, Rg = 16 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 170/16 | Answer: 11.62

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 3634. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 3634 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(3634) | Answer: 35.6 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 5.7 m carries a central point load of 30 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.7, W = 30 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 30*5.7 / 4 | Answer: 42.75 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 6 m carries a UDL of 35 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6, w = 35 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 35*(6)^2 / 8 | Answer: 157.5 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 5.1 m carries a point load 5 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.1, W = 5 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 5*5.1 | Answer: 25.5 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 3.5 m carries a UDL of 32 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.5, w = 32 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 32*(3.5)^2 / 2 | Answer: 196 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 7.7 m carries a point load 55 kN at distance 2.1 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 7.7, a = 2.1, W = 55 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 55*(7.7 - 2.1) / 7.7 | Answer: 40 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 7 m) carries a central point load 15 kN. With E = 30 GPa and I = 560e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=15000 N, L=7000.0 mm, E=30000 MPa, I=560e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 6.38 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 4.1 m carries a UDL of 24 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.1, w = 24 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 24*(4.1)^2 / 12 | Answer: 33.62 kN-m

question: A column supports a floor area of 27.4 m^2 carrying a factored load of 8.6 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 27.4, w = 8.6 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 8.6 * 27.4 | Answer: 235.6 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 6.1 m, unit weight 18 kN/m^3, phi = 33 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 8e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1.1, area = 6.6e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 8, i = 1.1, A = 6.6 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (8e-4)*1.1*(6.6e-3) | Answer: 5808 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.7 m, bed slope 0.004 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.029. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 2.9 m under a head of 0.6 m. Taking Cd = 0.6 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 5.3 m wide carries a discharge of 5.9 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A tank of volume 170 m^3 treats a flow of 170 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 170, Q = 170 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 170 / 170 | Answer: 1 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 280 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.13 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 3 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 280, k = 0.13, t = 3 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 280*(1 - e^(-0.13*3)) | Answer: 90.42 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.63, rainfall intensity 120 mm/h over a catchment of 51.6 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.63, i = 120, A = 51.6 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.63*120*51.6 / 360 | Answer: 10.84 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.05 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 340 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.05, M = 340 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 340*(30+0.05)/30 | Answer: 340.6 m

question: Convert the decimal number 1229 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 1229 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 4CD (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 01100001 and 10110111.
solution: XOR: 11010110 | Count of 1s = 5 | Answer: 5
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 700 megabits is sent over a link of 32 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 700, B = 32 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 700 / 32 | Answer: 21.88 s

question: A link has bandwidth 34 Mbps and round-trip time 180 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 34, R = 180 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 34e6 * 180e-3 bits = 6120 kb | Answer: 6120 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.8, cache access time 6 ns and main-memory access time 120 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.8, tc = 6, tm = 120 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.8*6 + (1 - 0.8)*120 | Answer: 28.8 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 317453 elements?
solution: Given: n = 317453 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(317453)) + 1 | Answer: 19

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.01, memory access time 140 ns and page-fault service time 6 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 6 ms = 6000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.01)*140 + 0.01*6000000.0 ns | Answer: 60.14 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 1.5 m^3 at 140 kPa and 340 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 1.5, P = 140, Tk = 340 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (140e3)*1.5 / (8.314*340) | Answer: 74.29 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.29 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 17 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.29, t = 17 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.29*17) | Answer: 0.9928

question: For a reaction with A = 1e10 /s and activation energy 65 kJ/mol at 300 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 1, Ea = 65, Tk = 300 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 1e10 * exp(-65e3 / (8.314*300)) | Answer: 0.04809 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.97 and bottoms xW = 0.06, with relative volatility alpha = 3.1. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.97, xw = 0.06, al = 3.1 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.97/0.03)(0.94/0.06)] / ln(3.1) | Answer: 5.504 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.62 and x = 0.45. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.62, x = 0.45 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.62/0.38) / (0.45/0.55) | Answer: 1.994

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.1 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 100 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.1, Psat = 100 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.1 * 100 | Answer: 10 kPa

question: A stream of 8.5 kg/s with specific heat 1.5 kJ/kg-K is heated through 65 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 8.5, cp = 1.5, dT = 65 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 8.5*1.5*65 | Answer: 828.8 kW

question: A reactor of volume 12.7 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 4.5 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 12.7, Q = 4.5 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 12.7 / 4.5 | Answer: 2.822 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 2e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 5 mm with a concentration difference of 70 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 2, L = 5, dC = 70 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (2e-9)*70 / (5e-3) | Answer: 28 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 8.1 min and steady-state gain 3.6. For a step input of magnitude 9, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 8.1, K = 3.6, M = 9 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 3.6 * 9 | Answer: 32.4 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 40 m^2 flies at 230 m/s (air density 0.7 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.5. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 40, V = 230, rho = 0.7, CL = 0.5 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.7*(230)^2*40*0.5 / 1000 | Answer: 370.3 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 100 m^2 flies at 180 m/s (density 0.7 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.09. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 100, V = 180, rho = 0.7, CD = 0.09 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.7*(180)^2*100*0.09 / 1000 | Answer: 102.1 kN

question: A specimen under stress 120 MPa shows an elastic strain of 2e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 120, eps = 2 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 120 / (2e-3) MPa = 60 GPa | Answer: 60 GPa

question: A block of mass 21 kg has a volume of 3.1e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 21, V = 3.1 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 21 / (3.1e-3) | Answer: 6774 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 700 mm is heated through 125 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 12e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 700, dT = 125, al = 12 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 700*12e-6*125 | Answer: 1.05 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 125 ohm, R2 = 40 ohm and R3 = 485 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 125, R2 = 40, R3 = 485 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 40*485 / 125 | Answer: 155.2 ohm

question: A measurement reads 10.37 when the true value is 100. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10.37, true = 100 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10.37 - 100| / 100 * 100 | Answer: 89.63 %

question: Annual demand is 33500 units, ordering cost 130 per order and holding cost 27 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 33500, S = 130, H = 27 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*33500*130 / 27) | Answer: 568 units

question: An asset costs 450000 with salvage value 36000 after 19 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 450000, Sv = 36000, n = 19 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (450000 - 36000) / 19 | Answer: 21789 per year

question: A product sells for 200 per unit with variable cost 50 per unit and fixed costs 160000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 200, V = 50, F = 160000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 160000 / (200 - 50) | Answer: 1067 units

question: Find the present worth of 115000 received 5 years from now at an interest rate of 5% per year.
solution: Given: F = 115000, n = 5, i = 5 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 115000 / (1 + 0.05)^5 | Answer: 90106 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.98, 0.92 and 0.9 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.98, r2 = 0.92, r3 = 0.9 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.98*0.92*0.9 | Answer: 0.8114

question: A process produces 50 defective items in a batch of 1000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 50, N = 1000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 50/1000 * 1e6 | Answer: 50000 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -5x^3 - x^2 - 4x + 9 evaluated at x = 1.
For f(x) = 5x^3 - 4x, find f''(x) at x = 0.
Evaluate the definite integral of (-5x^2 - x - 7) dx from x = 0 to x = 7.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = -5x^3/3 + -1x^2/2 + -7x | Evaluate F(7) - F(0) | Answer: -645.2
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 5x^2 - 7x - 11 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[-8, -3], [0, -3]].
solution: Given: a = -8, b = -3, c = 0, d = -3 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (-8)(-3) - (-3)(0) | Answer: 24

question: Find the determinant of [[6, 0, 6], [-4, -4, -3], [6, -3, 1]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: 138

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[2, 1], [3, -5]].
solution: Trace tr = -3, Determinant = -13 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 2.405

question: Solve for x: 1x + 6y = 6 and -4x + 0y = 12.
solution: Determinant = 1*0 - 6*-4 = 24 | x = (e d - b f) / det = -3 | Answer: x = -3
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 27, 79, 39, 28, 99.
solution: Sum = 272 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 54.4 | Answer: 54.4

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 43, 19, 11, 32, 16.
solution: Mean = 24.2 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 13.07

question: Find the slope of the line through (-6, -9) and (-8, 4).
solution: Given: x1 = -6, y1 = -9, x2 = -8, y2 = 4 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (4 - -9) / (-8 - -6) | Answer: -6.5

question: Find the distance between the points (0, -2) and (-9, 9).
solution: Given: x1 = 0, y1 = -2, x2 = -9, y2 = 9 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-9)^2 + (11)^2) | Answer: 14.21 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (7,-6), (2,-4), (-5,-8).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 17 sq units

question: Find the 8th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -19 and common difference 4.
solution: Given: a = -19, d = 4, n = 8 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -19 + (8 - 1)*4 | Answer: 9

question: Find the sum of the first 8 terms of an AP with first term 13 and common difference 3.
solution: Given: a = 13, d = 3, n = 8 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 8/2 [2*13 + (8-1)*3] | Answer: 188

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 11500 at 4.7% per annum for 9 years.
solution: Given: P = 11500, R = 4.7, Tt = 9 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 11500 * 4.7 * 9 / 100 | Answer: 4864 currency units

question: Find the amount when 19000 is invested at 6% per annum compounded annually for 3 years.
solution: Given: P = 19000, R = 6, Tt = 3 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 19000 * (1 + 6/100)^3 | Answer: 22629 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (1, 0, 1) and (5, 0, 1).
solution: Given: a1 = 1, a2 = 0, a3 = 1, b1 = 5, b2 = 0, b3 = 1 | Formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3 | Substitute: = (1)(5) + (0)(0) + (1)(1) | Answer: 6
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (3, -1, -5) and (-3, -1, -3).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 24.82

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (3, -3, 1) and (-4, -3, -1).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 100.4 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -x^3 - 4x^2 + 9x + 8 at x = 1.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-149 with initial guess x0=5, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.5 and ordinates 11, 10, 5, 19, 16, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 126 and 519.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 126 and 519 | Answer: GCD = 3

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 48 and 44.
solution: Given: a = 48, b = 44 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 48*44 / 4 | Answer: 528
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 57 mm carries an axial tensile load of 100 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 39 mm and length 2300 mm carries an axial load of 86 kN. Take E = 210 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 76 mm transmits a torque of 1900 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 76, Tt = 1900 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(1900*1000) / (pi*(76)^3) | Answer: 22.04 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 70 mm and length 700 mm carries a torque of 1150 N-m. With G = 80 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (70)^4 / 32 = 2357176 mm^4 | theta = (1150*1000)(700) / (80000 * 2357176) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 0.2446 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 106 mm wide and 280 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 106, h = 280 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 106*(280)^2 / 6 | Answer: 1385067 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (93 mm x 220 mm) carries a bending moment of 40 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (74 mm x 100 mm) has effective length 3000 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 740 MPa is designed for a working stress of 140 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 740, sw = 140 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 740 / 140 | Answer: 5.286

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 550 mm and wall thickness 15 mm carries an internal pressure of 1.1 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 550, t = 15, P = 1.1 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 1.1*550 / (2*15) | Answer: 20.17 MPa

question: 5 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 50 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 5, dT = 50 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 5 * 0.718 * 50 | Answer: 179.5 kJ

question: 6.9 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 185 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 6.9, dT = 185 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 6.9 * 1.005 * 185 | Answer: 1283 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 3.9 m^3 at 440 K with mass 5.7 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 3.9, Tk = 440, m = 5.7 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 5.7*0.287*440 / 3.9 | Answer: 184.6 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 4.1 kg of air expands isothermally at 450 K from volume V1 to 2*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.1, Tk = 450, ratio = 2 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 4.1*0.287*450*ln(2) | Answer: 367 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 1.5 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.4 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 1.5, D = 0.4 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*1.5*0.4 / 0.001 | Answer: 600000

question: Water flows at 0.5 m/s through a pipe of diameter 270 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 11.5 m. Taking Cv = 0.98, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 11.5, cv = 0.98 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.98*sqrt(2*9.81*11.5) | Answer: 14.72 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 230 mm) water flows at 1.9 m/s. It contracts to diameter 60 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 230, d2 = 60, V1 = 1.9 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 1.9*(230/60)^2 | Answer: 27.92 m/s

question: Water flows at 2.5 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.2 m and length 440 m. With friction factor f = 0.029, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 21 teeth drives a gear of 54 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1350 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 21, z2 = 54, N1 = 1350 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1350*21 / 54 | Answer: 525 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 250 mm rotates at 1250 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 250, N = 1250 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.25)*1250 / 60 | Answer: 16.36 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 25.6 kW at 250 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 25.6, N = 250 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(25.6*1000) / (2*pi*250) | Answer: 977.8 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 5.3 kg rotates at radius 0.44 m at 1150 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 5600 N/m and mass 18 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 5600, m = 18 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(5600/18) | Answer: 2.807 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 1.8 m^2 and thickness 0.35 m has conductivity k = 20 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 30 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 1.8, L = 0.35, k = 20, dT = 30 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 20*1.8*30 / 0.35 | Answer: 3086 W

question: A surface of area 3.5 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 20 W/m^2-K to surroundings 25 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 3.5, h = 20, dT = 25 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 20*3.5*25 | Answer: 1750 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 200 m/min, feed = 0.21 mm/rev, depth of cut = 1.4 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 200, f = 0.21, d = 1.4 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*200*0.21*1.4 | Answer: 58800 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 450 mm is turned at 950 rpm with a feed of 0.33 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 450, N = 950, f = 0.33 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 450 / (0.33*950) | Answer: 1.435 min

question: A resistor of 108 ohm carries a current of 1.8 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 108, I = 1.8 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 1.8 * 108 | Answer: 194.4 V

question: Three resistors 84 ohm, 71 ohm and 27 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 84, R2 = 71, R3 = 27 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 84 + 71 + 27 | Answer: 182 ohm

question: Two resistors 91 ohm and 72 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 91, R2 = 72 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 91*72 / (91+72) | Answer: 40.2 ohm

question: A device draws 6.8 A at 175 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 175, I = 6.8 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 175 * 6.8 | Answer: 1190 W

question: A current of 6.8 A flows through a 95 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 6.8, R = 95 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (6.8)^2 * 95 | Answer: 4393 W

question: Two capacitors 29.5 uF and 43.2 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 29.5, C2 = 43.2 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 29.5*43.2 / (29.5+43.2) | Answer: 17.53 uF

question: A resistor 16 kohm and capacitor 9.9 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 16, C = 9.9 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (16k)(9.9u) = 158.4 ms | Answer: 158.4 ms

question: An inductor 175.4 mH is in series with 22 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 175.4, R = 22 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (175.4e-3) / 22 | Answer: 7.973 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 199.2 mH inductor at 780 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 199.2, f = 780 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (780)(199.2e-3) | Answer: 976.3 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 18.7 uF capacitor at 690 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 18.7, f = 690 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (690)(18.7e-6)) | Answer: 12.33 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 94 ohm, XL = 42 ohm and XC = 138 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 94, XL = 42, XC = 138 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(94^2 + (42 - 138)^2) | Answer: 134.4 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 99.3 mH and C = 8 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 99.3, C = 8 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(99.3e-3 * 8e-6)) | Answer: 178.6 Hz

question: A capacitor of 31.7 uF is charged to 265 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 31.7, V = 265 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*31.7e-6*(265)^2 | Answer: 1113 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 150 V with 980 primary turns and 340 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 150, N1 = 980, N2 = 340 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 150 * 340/980 | Answer: 52.04 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 340 V and draws an armature current of 54 A. If the armature resistance is 1 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 340, Ia = 54, Ra = 1 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 340 - 54*1 | Answer: 286 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 180 A at 415 V (line) with a power factor of 0.78. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 180, VL = 415, pf = 0.78 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*415*180*0.78 / 1000 | Answer: 100.9 kW

question: A load has real power 110 kW and apparent power 125 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 110, S = 125 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 110 / 125 | Answer: 0.88

question: A machine delivers 40 kW output while drawing 102 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 40, Pi = 102 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 40/102 * 100 | Answer: 39.22 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 27 V across R1 = 5 ohm and R2 = 17 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 27, R1 = 5, R2 = 17 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 27*17 / (5+17) | Answer: 20.86 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 180 kohm and Rin = 22 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 180, Rin = 22 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 180 / 22 | Answer: 8.182

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 80 kohm and Rg = 23 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 80, Rg = 23 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 80/23 | Answer: 4.478

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 3757. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 3757 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(3757) | Answer: 35.75 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 7.2 m carries a central point load of 40 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7.2, W = 40 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 40*7.2 / 4 | Answer: 72 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 8.1 m carries a UDL of 20 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 8.1, w = 20 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 20*(8.1)^2 / 8 | Answer: 164 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 3.1 m carries a UDL of 12 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.1, w = 12 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 12*(3.1)^2 / 2 | Answer: 57.66 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 8.7 m carries a point load 15 kN at distance 3.4 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 8.7, a = 3.4, W = 15 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 15*(8.7 - 3.4) / 8.7 | Answer: 9.138 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 5.5 m) carries a central point load 70 kN. With E = 25 GPa and I = 340e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=70000 N, L=5500.0 mm, E=25000 MPa, I=340e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 28.54 mm

question: An RC beam has overall depth 610 mm, clear cover 30 mm and main bars of diameter 16 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 610, c = 30, dia = 16 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 610 - 30 - 16/2 | Answer: 572 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 14.2 m^2 carrying a factored load of 10.6 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 14.2, w = 10.6 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 10.6 * 14.2 | Answer: 150.5 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 5.7 m, unit weight 20 kN/m^3, phi = 34 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 9e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.4, area = 2.6e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 9, i = 0.4, A = 2.6 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (9e-4)*0.4*(2.6e-3) | Answer: 936 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1 m, bed slope 0.008 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.023. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 2 m under a head of 0.7 m. Taking Cd = 0.6 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
solution: Given: L = 2, H = 0.7, cd = 0.6 | Formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2) | Substitute: Q = (2/3)*0.6*sqrt(2*9.81)*2*(0.7)^1.5 | Answer: 2.075 m^3/s
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 2.4 m wide carries a discharge of 28.7 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 420 m and design speed 85 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 420, V = 85 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (85)^2 / (127*420) | Answer: 0.1355
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: A tank of volume 900 m^3 treats a flow of 120 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 900, Q = 120 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 900 / 120 | Answer: 7.5 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 260 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.34 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 8 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 260, k = 0.34, t = 8 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 260*(1 - e^(-0.34*8)) | Answer: 242.9 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.46, rainfall intensity 115 mm/h over a catchment of 31.8 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.46, i = 115, A = 31.8 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.46*115*31.8 / 360 | Answer: 4.673 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.07 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 310 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.07, M = 310 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 310*(30+0.07)/30 | Answer: 310.7 m

question: Convert the decimal number 2962 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 2962 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: B92 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 01110010 and 11000111.
solution: XOR: 10110101 | Count of 1s = 5 | Answer: 5
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 790 megabits is sent over a link of 11 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 790, B = 11 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 790 / 11 | Answer: 71.82 s

question: A link has bandwidth 96 Mbps and round-trip time 200 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 96, R = 200 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 96e6 * 200e-3 bits = 19200 kb | Answer: 19200 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.94, cache access time 7 ns and main-memory access time 120 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.94, tc = 7, tm = 120 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.94*7 + (1 - 0.94)*120 | Answer: 13.78 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 433338 elements?
solution: Given: n = 433338 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(433338)) + 1 | Answer: 19

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.002, memory access time 160 ns and page-fault service time 5 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 5 ms = 5000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.002)*160 + 0.002*5000000.0 ns | Answer: 10.16 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 2.8 m^3 at 290 kPa and 530 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 2.8, P = 290, Tk = 530 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (290e3)*2.8 / (8.314*530) | Answer: 184.3 mol

question: For a reaction with A = 7e10 /s and activation energy 85 kJ/mol at 390 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 7, Ea = 85, Tk = 390 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 7e10 * exp(-85e3 / (8.314*390)) | Answer: 0.2885 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.91 and bottoms xW = 0.03, with relative volatility alpha = 3.5. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.91, xw = 0.03, al = 3.5 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.91/0.09)(0.97/0.03)] / ln(3.5) | Answer: 4.622 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.76 and x = 0.4. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.76, x = 0.4 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.76/0.24) / (0.4/0.6) | Answer: 4.75

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.13 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 45 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.13, Psat = 45 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.13 * 45 | Answer: 5.85 kPa

question: A stream of 9.4 kg/s with specific heat 4 kJ/kg-K is heated through 80 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 9.4, cp = 4, dT = 80 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 9.4*4*80 | Answer: 3008 kW

question: A reactor of volume 6.5 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 1.2 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 6.5, Q = 1.2 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 6.5 / 1.2 | Answer: 5.417 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 2.7e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 4 mm with a concentration difference of 40 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 2.7, L = 4, dC = 40 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (2.7e-9)*40 / (4e-3) | Answer: 27 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 2.4 min and steady-state gain 2.7. For a step input of magnitude 9, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 2.4, K = 2.7, M = 9 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 2.7 * 9 | Answer: 24.3 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 20 m^2 flies at 150 m/s (air density 1.225 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.9. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 20, V = 150, rho = 1.225, CL = 0.9 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1.225*(150)^2*20*0.9 / 1000 | Answer: 248.1 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 40 m^2 flies at 240 m/s (density 1.225 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.12. Find the drag force in kN.
A specimen under stress 190 MPa shows an elastic strain of 2.6e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 190, eps = 2.6 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 190 / (2.6e-3) MPa = 73.08 GPa | Answer: 73.08 GPa

question: A block of mass 44 kg has a volume of 2.1e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 44, V = 2.1 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 44 / (2.1e-3) | Answer: 20952 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 2900 mm is heated through 120 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 17e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 2900, dT = 120, al = 17 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 2900*17e-6*120 | Answer: 5.916 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 35 ohm, R2 = 25 ohm and R3 = 225 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 35, R2 = 25, R3 = 225 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 25*225 / 35 | Answer: 160.7 ohm

question: A measurement reads 9.01 when the true value is 100. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.01, true = 100 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.01 - 100| / 100 * 100 | Answer: 90.99 %

question: Annual demand is 2500 units, ordering cost 240 per order and holding cost 32 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 2500, S = 240, H = 32 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*2500*240 / 32) | Answer: 193.6 units

question: An asset costs 80000 with salvage value 8000 after 13 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 80000, Sv = 8000, n = 13 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (80000 - 8000) / 13 | Answer: 5538 per year

question: A product sells for 290 per unit with variable cost 70 per unit and fixed costs 90000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 290, V = 70, F = 90000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 90000 / (290 - 70) | Answer: 409.1 units

question: Find the present worth of 195000 received 4 years from now at an interest rate of 6% per year.
solution: Given: F = 195000, n = 4, i = 6 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 195000 / (1 + 0.06)^4 | Answer: 154458 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.92, 0.98 and 0.98 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.92, r2 = 0.98, r3 = 0.98 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.92*0.98*0.98 | Answer: 0.8836

question: A process produces 9 defective items in a batch of 7500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 9, N = 7500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 9/7500 * 1e6 | Answer: 1200 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -5x^3 + 3x^2 + 6x + 1 evaluated at x = 0.
For f(x) = x^3 - 4x^2 + 8x + 8, find f''(x) at x = -4.
Evaluate the definite integral of (-2x^2 + 4x - 4) dx from x = 1 to x = 3.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = -2x^3/3 + 4x^2/2 + -4x | Evaluate F(3) - F(1) | Answer: -9.333
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 2x^2 - 12x + 3 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[2, -7], [-3, -1]].
solution: Given: a = 2, b = -7, c = -3, d = -1 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (2)(-1) - (-7)(-3) | Answer: -23

question: Find the determinant of [[1, 2, 0], [-5, 1, -5], [6, 6, -6]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: -96

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[-4, 6], [3, 7]].
solution: Trace tr = 3, Determinant = -46 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 8.446

question: Solve for x: -6x + 1y = 1 and 3x + 1y = -5.
solution: Determinant = -6*1 - 1*3 = -9 | x = (e d - b f) / det = -0.6667 | Answer: x = -0.6667
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 31, 26, 12, 59, 72.
solution: Sum = 200 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 40 | Answer: 40

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 41, 3, 45, 23, 41.
solution: Mean = 30.6 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 17.63

question: Find the slope of the line through (7, 4) and (-9, 8).
solution: Given: x1 = 7, y1 = 4, x2 = -9, y2 = 8 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (8 - 4) / (-9 - 7) | Answer: -0.25

question: Find the distance between the points (-8, 5) and (6, 3).
solution: Given: x1 = -8, y1 = 5, x2 = 6, y2 = 3 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((14)^2 + (-2)^2) | Answer: 14.14 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (-4,7), (-2,8), (-8,0).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 5 sq units

question: Find the 8th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -19 and common difference 1.
solution: Given: a = -19, d = 1, n = 8 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -19 + (8 - 1)*1 | Answer: -12

question: Find the sum of the first 12 terms of an AP with first term 15 and common difference -7.
solution: Given: a = 15, d = -7, n = 12 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 12/2 [2*15 + (12-1)*-7] | Answer: -282

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 19500 at 8% per annum for 2 years.
solution: Given: P = 19500, R = 8, Tt = 2 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 19500 * 8 * 2 / 100 | Answer: 3120 currency units

question: Find the amount when 8000 is invested at 11.2% per annum compounded annually for 3 years.
solution: Given: P = 8000, R = 11.2, Tt = 3 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 8000 * (1 + 11.2/100)^3 | Answer: 11 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (5, 2, -5) and (-5, -6, 7).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (3, 1, 0) and (-6, -5, -1).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 9.539

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (3, -2, 6) and (-6, 5, 0).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 120.8 degrees

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number -9 + -3i.
solution: Given: a = -9, b = -3 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(-3, -9) | Answer: -161.6 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -3x^3 + 6x^2 - 5x + 8 at x = 0.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-159 with initial guess x0=7, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.9 and ordinates 4, 16, 17, 20, 14, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 67 and 102.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 67 and 102 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 37 and 14.
solution: Given: a = 37, b = 14 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 37*14 / 1 | Answer: 518
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 25 mm carries an axial tensile load of 48 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 18 mm and length 2600 mm carries an axial load of 69 kN. Take E = 70 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 29 mm transmits a torque of 550 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 29, Tt = 550 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(550*1000) / (pi*(29)^3) | Answer: 114.9 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 62 mm and length 2000 mm carries a torque of 750 N-m. With G = 80 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (62)^4 / 32 = 1450663 mm^4 | theta = (750*1000)(2000) / (80000 * 1450663) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 0.7406 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 49 mm wide and 300 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 49, h = 300 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 49*(300)^2 / 6 | Answer: 735000 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (66 mm x 190 mm) carries a bending moment of 32 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (67 mm x 100 mm) has effective length 3600 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 850 MPa is designed for a working stress of 120 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 850, sw = 120 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 850 / 120 | Answer: 7.083

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1350 mm and wall thickness 19 mm carries an internal pressure of 1.4 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1350, t = 19, P = 1.4 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 1.4*1350 / (2*19) | Answer: 49.74 MPa

question: 5.1 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 65 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 5.1, dT = 65 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 5.1 * 0.718 * 65 | Answer: 238 kJ

question: 2.1 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 55 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.1, dT = 55 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 2.1 * 1.005 * 55 | Answer: 116.1 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 2.5 m^3 at 450 K with mass 2.4 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 2.5, Tk = 450, m = 2.4 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 2.4*0.287*450 / 2.5 | Answer: 124 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 3.5 kg of air expands isothermally at 370 K from volume V1 to 4*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.5, Tk = 370, ratio = 4 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 3.5*0.287*370*ln(4) | Answer: 515.2 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 2.5 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.19 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 2.5, D = 0.19 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*2.5*0.19 / 0.001 | Answer: 475000

question: Water flows at 1.5 m/s through a pipe of diameter 70 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 9.2 m. Taking Cv = 0.99, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 9.2, cv = 0.99 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.99*sqrt(2*9.81*9.2) | Answer: 13.3 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 170 mm) water flows at 1.3 m/s. It contracts to diameter 120 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
Water flows at 2.5 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.2 m and length 70 m. With friction factor f = 0.021, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 37 teeth drives a gear of 105 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1500 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 37, z2 = 105, N1 = 1500 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1500*37 / 105 | Answer: 528.6 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 470 mm rotates at 250 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 470, N = 250 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.47)*250 / 60 | Answer: 6.152 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 26.8 kW at 1000 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 26.8, N = 1000 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(26.8*1000) / (2*pi*1000) | Answer: 255.9 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 4.5 kg rotates at radius 0.39 m at 400 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 13500 N/m and mass 19 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 13500, m = 19 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(13500/19) | Answer: 4.242 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 1.3 m^2 and thickness 0.24 m has conductivity k = 23.2 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 160 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 1.3, L = 0.24, k = 23.2, dT = 160 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 23.2*1.3*160 / 0.24 | Answer: 20107 W

question: A surface of area 3.4 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 145 W/m^2-K to surroundings 135 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 3.4, h = 145, dT = 135 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 145*3.4*135 | Answer: 66555 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 100 m/min, feed = 0.48 mm/rev, depth of cut = 1.6 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 100, f = 0.48, d = 1.6 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*100*0.48*1.6 | Answer: 76800 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 430 mm is turned at 600 rpm with a feed of 0.19 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 430, N = 600, f = 0.19 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 430 / (0.19*600) | Answer: 3.772 min

question: A resistor of 131 ohm carries a current of 0.7 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 131, I = 0.7 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 0.7 * 131 | Answer: 91.7 V

question: Three resistors 29 ohm, 26 ohm and 96 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 29, R2 = 26, R3 = 96 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 29 + 26 + 96 | Answer: 151 ohm

question: Two resistors 95 ohm and 8 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 95, R2 = 8 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 95*8 / (95+8) | Answer: 7.379 ohm

question: A device draws 0.4 A at 185 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 185, I = 0.4 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 185 * 0.4 | Answer: 74 W

question: A current of 7.9 A flows through a 86 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 7.9, R = 86 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (7.9)^2 * 86 | Answer: 5367 W

question: Two capacitors 33.4 uF and 6.8 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 33.4, C2 = 6.8 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 33.4*6.8 / (33.4+6.8) | Answer: 5.65 uF

question: A resistor 86 kohm and capacitor 3 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 86, C = 3 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (86k)(3u) = 258 ms | Answer: 258 ms

question: An inductor 386.3 mH is in series with 139 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 386.3, R = 139 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (386.3e-3) / 139 | Answer: 2.779 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 101.5 mH inductor at 170 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 101.5, f = 170 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (170)(101.5e-3) | Answer: 108.4 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 14 uF capacitor at 750 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 14, f = 750 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (750)(14e-6)) | Answer: 15.16 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 50 ohm, XL = 99 ohm and XC = 105 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 50, XL = 99, XC = 105 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(50^2 + (99 - 105)^2) | Answer: 50.36 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 99.7 mH and C = 1.2 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 99.7, C = 1.2 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(99.7e-3 * 1.2e-6)) | Answer: 460.1 Hz

question: A capacitor of 90.1 uF is charged to 210 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 90.1, V = 210 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*90.1e-6*(210)^2 | Answer: 1987 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 320 V with 480 primary turns and 350 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 320, N1 = 480, N2 = 350 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 320 * 350/480 | Answer: 233.3 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 360 V and draws an armature current of 5 A. If the armature resistance is 0.2 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 360, Ia = 5, Ra = 0.2 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 360 - 5*0.2 | Answer: 359 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 100 A at 415 V (line) with a power factor of 0.75. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 100, VL = 415, pf = 0.75 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*415*100*0.75 / 1000 | Answer: 53.91 kW

question: A load has real power 25 kW and apparent power 60 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 25, S = 60 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 25 / 60 | Answer: 0.4167

question: A machine delivers 45 kW output while drawing 122 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 45, Pi = 122 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 45/122 * 100 | Answer: 36.89 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 12 V across R1 = 24 ohm and R2 = 37 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 12, R1 = 24, R2 = 37 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 12*37 / (24+37) | Answer: 7.279 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 150 kohm and Rin = 26 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 150, Rin = 26 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 150 / 26 | Answer: 5.769

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 130 kohm and Rg = 33 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 130, Rg = 33 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 130/33 | Answer: 4.939

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 2146. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 2146 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(2146) | Answer: 33.32 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 8 m carries a central point load of 20 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 8, W = 20 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 20*8 / 4 | Answer: 40 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 7.1 m carries a UDL of 10 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7.1, w = 10 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 10*(7.1)^2 / 8 | Answer: 63.01 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 4.2 m carries a point load 70 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.2, W = 70 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 70*4.2 | Answer: 294 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 4.6 m carries a UDL of 24 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.6, w = 24 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 24*(4.6)^2 / 2 | Answer: 253.9 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 8.2 m carries a point load 20 kN at distance 2.8 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 8.2, a = 2.8, W = 20 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 20*(8.2 - 2.8) / 8.2 | Answer: 13.17 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 4.4 m) carries a central point load 35 kN. With E = 25 GPa and I = 290e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=35000 N, L=4400.0 mm, E=25000 MPa, I=290e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 8.567 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 8.4 m carries a UDL of 15 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 8.4, w = 15 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 15*(8.4)^2 / 12 | Answer: 88.2 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 640 mm, clear cover 45 mm and main bars of diameter 12 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 640, c = 45, dia = 12 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 640 - 45 - 12/2 | Answer: 589 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 13.6 m^2 carrying a factored load of 16.2 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 13.6, w = 16.2 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 16.2 * 13.6 | Answer: 220.3 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 4.8 m, unit weight 19 kN/m^3, phi = 32 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 8.9e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.3, area = 5e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 8.9, i = 0.3, A = 5 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (8.9e-4)*0.3*(5e-3) | Answer: 1335 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1 m, bed slope 0.005 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.022. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 3.4 m under a head of 0.4 m. Taking Cd = 0.64 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 5.6 m wide carries a discharge of 8.5 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A tank of volume 930 m^3 treats a flow of 60 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 930, Q = 60 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 930 / 60 | Answer: 15.5 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 220 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.15 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 3 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 220, k = 0.15, t = 3 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 220*(1 - e^(-0.15*3)) | Answer: 79.72 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.77, rainfall intensity 60 mm/h over a catchment of 14.7 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.77, i = 60, A = 14.7 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.77*60*14.7 / 360 | Answer: 1.887 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.01 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 360 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.01, M = 360 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 360*(30+0.01)/30 | Answer: 360.1 m

question: Convert the decimal number 1278 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 1278 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 4FE (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 11111001 and 10011110.
solution: XOR: 01100111 | Count of 1s = 5 | Answer: 5
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 890 megabits is sent over a link of 57 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 890, B = 57 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 890 / 57 | Answer: 15.61 s

question: A link has bandwidth 52 Mbps and round-trip time 20 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 52, R = 20 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 52e6 * 20e-3 bits = 1040 kb | Answer: 1040 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.82, cache access time 5 ns and main-memory access time 200 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.82, tc = 5, tm = 200 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.82*5 + (1 - 0.82)*200 | Answer: 40.1 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 929739 elements?
solution: Given: n = 929739 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(929739)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.019, memory access time 150 ns and page-fault service time 4 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 4 ms = 4000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.019)*150 + 0.019*4000000.0 ns | Answer: 76.15 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 2.6 m^3 at 390 kPa and 510 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 2.6, P = 390, Tk = 510 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (390e3)*2.6 / (8.314*510) | Answer: 239.1 mol

question: For a reaction with A = 9e10 /s and activation energy 65 kJ/mol at 430 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 9, Ea = 65, Tk = 430 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 9e10 * exp(-65e3 / (8.314*430)) | Answer: 1143 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.95 and bottoms xW = 0.04, with relative volatility alpha = 1.5. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.95, xw = 0.04, al = 1.5 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.95/0.05)(0.96/0.04)] / ln(1.5) | Answer: 15.1 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.8 and x = 0.4. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.8, x = 0.4 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.8/0.2) / (0.4/0.6) | Answer: 6

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.11 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 95 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.11, Psat = 95 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.11 * 95 | Answer: 10.45 kPa

question: A stream of 1.9 kg/s with specific heat 2.7 kJ/kg-K is heated through 80 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 1.9, cp = 2.7, dT = 80 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 1.9*2.7*80 | Answer: 410.4 kW

question: A reactor of volume 9.2 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 1.3 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 9.2, Q = 1.3 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 9.2 / 1.3 | Answer: 7.077 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 1.9e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 2 mm with a concentration difference of 130 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 1.9, L = 2, dC = 130 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (1.9e-9)*130 / (2e-3) | Answer: 123.5 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 4.1 min and steady-state gain 2.2. For a step input of magnitude 17, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 4.1, K = 2.2, M = 17 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 2.2 * 17 | Answer: 37.4 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 20 m^2 flies at 200 m/s (air density 0.4 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.6. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 20, V = 200, rho = 0.4, CL = 0.6 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.4*(200)^2*20*0.6 / 1000 | Answer: 96 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 85 m^2 flies at 100 m/s (density 1 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.05. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 85, V = 100, rho = 1, CD = 0.05 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*1*(100)^2*85*0.05 / 1000 | Answer: 21.25 kN

question: A specimen under stress 380 MPa shows an elastic strain of 3e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 380, eps = 3 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 380 / (3e-3) MPa = 126.7 GPa | Answer: 126.7 GPa

question: A block of mass 16 kg has a volume of 2.9e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 16, V = 2.9 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 16 / (2.9e-3) | Answer: 5517 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 600 mm is heated through 20 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 11e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 600, dT = 20, al = 11 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 600*11e-6*20 | Answer: 0.132 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 110 ohm, R2 = 15 ohm and R3 = 100 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 110, R2 = 15, R3 = 100 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 15*100 / 110 | Answer: 13.64 ohm

question: Annual demand is 43000 units, ordering cost 280 per order and holding cost 33 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 43000, S = 280, H = 33 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*43000*280 / 33) | Answer: 854.2 units

question: An asset costs 340000 with salvage value 12000 after 6 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 340000, Sv = 12000, n = 6 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (340000 - 12000) / 6 | Answer: 54667 per year

question: A product sells for 310 per unit with variable cost 70 per unit and fixed costs 95000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 310, V = 70, F = 95000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 95000 / (310 - 70) | Answer: 395.8 units

question: Find the present worth of 115000 received 3 years from now at an interest rate of 10% per year.
solution: Given: F = 115000, n = 3, i = 10 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 115000 / (1 + 0.1)^3 | Answer: 86401 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.98, 0.91 and 0.97 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.98, r2 = 0.91, r3 = 0.97 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.98*0.91*0.97 | Answer: 0.865
