question: A current of 6.6 A flows through a 2 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 6.6, R = 2 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (6.6)^2 * 2 | Answer: 87.12 W

question: Two capacitors 27.3 uF and 38.8 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 27.3, C2 = 38.8 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 27.3*38.8 / (27.3+38.8) | Answer: 16.02 uF

question: A resistor 80 kohm and capacitor 10.4 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 80, C = 10.4 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (80k)(10.4u) = 832 ms | Answer: 832 ms

question: An inductor 127.2 mH is in series with 60 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 127.2, R = 60 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (127.2e-3) / 60 | Answer: 2.12 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 176.7 mH inductor at 360 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 176.7, f = 360 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (360)(176.7e-3) | Answer: 399.7 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 13.4 uF capacitor at 480 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 13.4, f = 480 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (480)(13.4e-6)) | Answer: 24.74 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 78 ohm, XL = 30 ohm and XC = 105 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 78, XL = 30, XC = 105 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(78^2 + (30 - 105)^2) | Answer: 108.2 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 69.6 mH and C = 0.9 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 69.6, C = 0.9 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(69.6e-3 * 0.9e-6)) | Answer: 635.9 Hz

question: A capacitor of 49.6 uF is charged to 125 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 49.6, V = 125 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*49.6e-6*(125)^2 | Answer: 387.5 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 390 V with 950 primary turns and 140 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 390, N1 = 950, N2 = 140 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 390 * 140/950 | Answer: 57.47 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 270 V and draws an armature current of 51 A. If the armature resistance is 0.95 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 270, Ia = 51, Ra = 0.95 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 270 - 51*0.95 | Answer: 221.6 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 170 A at 433 V (line) with a power factor of 0.89. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 170, VL = 433, pf = 0.89 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*433*170*0.89 / 1000 | Answer: 113.5 kW

question: A machine delivers 180 kW output while drawing 182 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 180, Pi = 182 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 180/182 * 100 | Answer: 98.9 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 15 V across R1 = 33 ohm and R2 = 37 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 15, R1 = 33, R2 = 37 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 15*37 / (33+37) | Answer: 7.929 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 110 kohm and Rin = 46 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 110, Rin = 46 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 110 / 46 | Answer: 2.391

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 50 kohm and Rg = 21 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 50, Rg = 21 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 50/21 | Answer: 3.381

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 1175. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 1175 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(1175) | Answer: 30.7 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 8.6 m carries a central point load of 85 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 8.6, W = 85 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 85*8.6 / 4 | Answer: 182.8 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.5 m carries a UDL of 25 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 9.5, w = 25 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 25*(9.5)^2 / 8 | Answer: 282 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 1.8 m carries a point load 50 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 1.8, W = 50 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 50*1.8 | Answer: 90 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 4.2 m carries a UDL of 4 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.2, w = 4 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 4*(4.2)^2 / 2 | Answer: 35.28 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 5.1 m carries a point load 30 kN at distance 1.9 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 5.1, a = 1.9, W = 30 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 30*(5.1 - 1.9) / 5.1 | Answer: 18.82 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 3 m) carries a central point load 15 kN. With E = 30 GPa and I = 420e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=15000 N, L=3000.0 mm, E=30000 MPa, I=420e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 0.6696 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 4.5 m carries a UDL of 9 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.5, w = 9 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 9*(4.5)^2 / 12 | Answer: 15.19 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 540 mm, clear cover 25 mm and main bars of diameter 16 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 540, c = 25, dia = 16 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 540 - 25 - 16/2 | Answer: 507 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 16.9 m^2 carrying a factored load of 13.2 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 16.9, w = 13.2 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 13.2 * 16.9 | Answer: 223.1 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 3.4 m, unit weight 18 kN/m^3, phi = 38 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 2.3e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.7, area = 3.2e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 2.3, i = 0.7, A = 3.2 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (2.3e-4)*0.7*(3.2e-3) | Answer: 515.2 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 2.1 m, bed slope 0.008 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.012. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 3 m under a head of 0.4 m. Taking Cd = 0.62 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 5 m wide carries a discharge of 29.2 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A tank of volume 380 m^3 treats a flow of 145 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 380, Q = 145 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 380 / 145 | Answer: 2.621 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 290 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.21 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 7 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 290, k = 0.21, t = 7 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 290*(1 - e^(-0.21*7)) | Answer: 223.3 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.73, rainfall intensity 115 mm/h over a catchment of 20.5 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.73, i = 115, A = 20.5 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.73*115*20.5 / 360 | Answer: 4.78 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.04 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 220 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.04, M = 220 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 220*(30+0.04)/30 | Answer: 220.3 m

question: Convert the decimal number 1989 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 1989 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 7C5 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 10101011 and 11000101.
solution: XOR: 01101110 | Count of 1s = 5 | Answer: 5
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 90 megabits is sent over a link of 72 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 90, B = 72 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 90 / 72 | Answer: 1.25 s

question: A link has bandwidth 12 Mbps and round-trip time 200 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 12, R = 200 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 12e6 * 200e-3 bits = 2400 kb | Answer: 2400 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.97, cache access time 7 ns and main-memory access time 120 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.97, tc = 7, tm = 120 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.97*7 + (1 - 0.97)*120 | Answer: 10.39 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 517255 elements?
solution: Given: n = 517255 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(517255)) + 1 | Answer: 19

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.015, memory access time 110 ns and page-fault service time 3 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 3 ms = 3000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.015)*110 + 0.015*3000000.0 ns | Answer: 45.11 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 3 m^3 at 410 kPa and 370 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 3, P = 410, Tk = 370 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (410e3)*3 / (8.314*370) | Answer: 399.8 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.11 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 2 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.11, t = 2 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.11*2) | Answer: 0.1975

question: For a reaction with A = 3e10 /s and activation energy 90 kJ/mol at 380 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 3, Ea = 90, Tk = 380 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 3e10 * exp(-90e3 / (8.314*380)) | Answer: 0.01274 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.94 and bottoms xW = 0.05, with relative volatility alpha = 2. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.94, xw = 0.05, al = 2 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.94/0.06)(0.95/0.05)] / ln(2) | Answer: 8.218 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.84 and x = 0.28. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.84, x = 0.28 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.84/0.16) / (0.28/0.72) | Answer: 13.5

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.51 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 35 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.51, Psat = 35 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.51 * 35 | Answer: 17.85 kPa

question: A stream of 6 kg/s with specific heat 4 kJ/kg-K is heated through 45 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 6, cp = 4, dT = 45 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 6*4*45 | Answer: 1080 kW

question: A reactor of volume 1.9 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 2.6 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 1.9, Q = 2.6 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 1.9 / 2.6 | Answer: 0.7308 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 7.6e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 1 mm with a concentration difference of 30 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 7.6, L = 1, dC = 30 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (7.6e-9)*30 / (1e-3) | Answer: 228 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 5 min and steady-state gain 2.8. For a step input of magnitude 14, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 5, K = 2.8, M = 14 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 2.8 * 14 | Answer: 39.2 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 100 m^2 flies at 150 m/s (air density 1.225 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.4. Find the lift force in kN.
An aircraft of wing area 30 m^2 flies at 60 m/s (density 0.7 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.03. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 30, V = 60, rho = 0.7, CD = 0.03 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.7*(60)^2*30*0.03 / 1000 | Answer: 1.134 kN

question: A specimen under stress 130 MPa shows an elastic strain of 2e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 130, eps = 2 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 130 / (2e-3) MPa = 65 GPa | Answer: 65 GPa

question: A block of mass 32 kg has a volume of 4.3e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 32, V = 4.3 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 32 / (4.3e-3) | Answer: 7442 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 800 mm is heated through 120 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 11e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 800, dT = 120, al = 11 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 800*11e-6*120 | Answer: 1.056 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 165 ohm, R2 = 105 ohm and R3 = 480 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 165, R2 = 105, R3 = 480 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 105*480 / 165 | Answer: 305.5 ohm

question: A measurement reads 9.84 when the true value is 20. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.84, true = 20 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.84 - 20| / 20 * 100 | Answer: 50.8 %

question: Annual demand is 8500 units, ordering cost 220 per order and holding cost 38 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 8500, S = 220, H = 38 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*8500*220 / 38) | Answer: 313.7 units

question: An asset costs 410000 with salvage value 40000 after 19 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 410000, Sv = 40000, n = 19 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (410000 - 40000) / 19 | Answer: 19474 per year

question: A product sells for 440 per unit with variable cost 140 per unit and fixed costs 15000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 440, V = 140, F = 15000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 15000 / (440 - 140) | Answer: 50 units

question: Find the present worth of 120000 received 5 years from now at an interest rate of 6% per year.
solution: Given: F = 120000, n = 5, i = 6 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 120000 / (1 + 0.06)^5 | Answer: 89671 currency units

question: A process produces 18 defective items in a batch of 7500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 18, N = 7500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 18/7500 * 1e6 | Answer: 2400 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -5x^3 - 3x^2 - 5x - 3 evaluated at x = -4.
For f(x) = -4x^3 + 8x^2 + 2, find f''(x) at x = 4.
Evaluate the definite integral of (3x^2 + x + 8) dx from x = -2 to x = 7.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = 3x^3/3 + 1x^2/2 + 8x | Evaluate F(7) - F(-2) | Answer: 445.5
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 5x^2 + 7x - 12 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[-8, -5], [1, 4]].
solution: Given: a = -8, b = -5, c = 1, d = 4 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (-8)(4) - (-5)(1) | Answer: -27

question: Find the determinant of [[-6, -4, -1], [0, 4, -2], [-2, -2, 1]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: -24

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[-1, 1], [7, 0]].
solution: Trace tr = -1, Determinant = -7 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 2.193

question: Solve for x: 5x + 2y = -9 and 2x + 1y = -4.
solution: Determinant = 5*1 - 2*2 = 1 | x = (e d - b f) / det = -1 | Answer: x = -1
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 84, 85, 54, 93, 90.
solution: Sum = 406 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 81.2 | Answer: 81.2

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 13, 47, 43, 27, 45.
solution: Mean = 35 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 14.63

question: Find the slope of the line through (6, 1) and (-3, 0).
solution: Given: x1 = 6, y1 = 1, x2 = -3, y2 = 0 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (0 - 1) / (-3 - 6) | Answer: 0.1111

question: Find the distance between the points (1, -5) and (6, 2).
solution: Given: x1 = 1, y1 = -5, x2 = 6, y2 = 2 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((5)^2 + (7)^2) | Answer: 8.602 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (4,-1), (-7,7), (-5,6).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 2.5 sq units

question: Find the 35th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 6 and common difference -9.
solution: Given: a = 6, d = -9, n = 35 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = 6 + (35 - 1)*-9 | Answer: -300

question: Find the sum of the first 16 terms of an AP with first term -2 and common difference -4.
solution: Given: a = -2, d = -4, n = 16 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 16/2 [2*-2 + (16-1)*-4] | Answer: -512

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 22000 at 9% per annum for 4 years.
solution: Given: P = 22000, R = 9, Tt = 4 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 22000 * 9 * 4 / 100 | Answer: 7920 currency units

question: Find the amount when 20000 is invested at 5.4% per annum compounded annually for 3 years.
solution: Given: P = 20000, R = 5.4, Tt = 3 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 20000 * (1 + 5.4/100)^3 | Answer: 23418 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (1, -8, 7) and (-2, 6, -2).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (-5, 6, -4) and (-1, 6, 2).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 45.48

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (6, -1, 1) and (-5, 1, -3).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 158.8 degrees

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number 6 + -2i.
solution: Given: a = 6, b = -2 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(-2, 6) | Answer: -18.43 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -2x^3 + 2x^2 - 7x - 5 at x = 1.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-33 with initial guess x0=8, find x1 (one iteration).
solution: Given: N = 33, x0 = 8 | Formula: x1 = x0 - (x0^2 - N)/(2 x0) | Substitute: x1 = 8 - ((8)^2 - 33)/(2*8) | Answer: 6.062

question: Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.8 and ordinates 13, 13, 20, 9, 10, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 171 and 285.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 171 and 285 | Answer: GCD = 57

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 43 and 54.
solution: Given: a = 43, b = 54 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 43*54 / 1 | Answer: 2322
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 23 mm carries an axial tensile load of 18 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 30 mm and length 1800 mm carries an axial load of 52 kN. Take E = 110 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 21 mm transmits a torque of 1700 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 21, Tt = 1700 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(1700*1000) / (pi*(21)^3) | Answer: 934.9 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 44 mm and length 1700 mm carries a torque of 1100 N-m. With G = 77 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (44)^4 / 32 = 367968 mm^4 | theta = (1100*1000)(1700) / (77000 * 367968) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 3.781 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 38 mm wide and 210 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 38, h = 210 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 38*(210)^2 / 6 | Answer: 279300 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (64 mm x 130 mm) carries a bending moment of 34 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (72 mm x 120 mm) has effective length 3700 mm and E = 200 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 490 MPa is designed for a working stress of 70 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 490, sw = 70 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 490 / 70 | Answer: 7

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1450 mm and wall thickness 14 mm carries an internal pressure of 0.9 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1450, t = 14, P = 0.9 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 0.9*1450 / (2*14) | Answer: 46.61 MPa

question: 6.7 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 100 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 6.7, dT = 100 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 6.7 * 0.718 * 100 | Answer: 481.1 kJ

question: 2.2 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 130 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.2, dT = 130 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 2.2 * 1.005 * 130 | Answer: 287.4 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 1.4 m^3 at 300 K with mass 5 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 1.4, Tk = 300, m = 5 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 5*0.287*300 / 1.4 | Answer: 307.5 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 3.7 kg of air expands isothermally at 380 K from volume V1 to 5*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.7, Tk = 380, ratio = 5 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 3.7*0.287*380*ln(5) | Answer: 649.4 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 2.3 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.2 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 2.3, D = 0.2 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*2.3*0.2 / 0.001 | Answer: 460000

question: Water flows at 3 m/s through a pipe of diameter 210 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 3 m. Taking Cv = 0.97, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 3, cv = 0.97 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.97*sqrt(2*9.81*3) | Answer: 7.442 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 270 mm) water flows at 2.2 m/s. It contracts to diameter 50 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 270, d2 = 50, V1 = 2.2 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 2.2*(270/50)^2 | Answer: 64.15 m/s

question: Water flows at 3.9 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.21 m and length 440 m. With friction factor f = 0.032, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 20 teeth drives a gear of 57 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1350 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 20, z2 = 57, N1 = 1350 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1350*20 / 57 | Answer: 473.7 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 460 mm rotates at 1350 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 460, N = 1350 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.46)*1350 / 60 | Answer: 32.52 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 33.8 kW at 350 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 33.8, N = 350 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(33.8*1000) / (2*pi*350) | Answer: 922.2 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 3.5 kg rotates at radius 0.59 m at 1000 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 14600 N/m and mass 9.3 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 14600, m = 9.3 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(14600/9.3) | Answer: 6.306 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 8 m^2 and thickness 0.27 m has conductivity k = 31.1 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 95 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 8, L = 0.27, k = 31.1, dT = 95 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 31.1*8*95 / 0.27 | Answer: 87541 W

question: A surface of area 2.2 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 35 W/m^2-K to surroundings 95 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 2.2, h = 35, dT = 95 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 35*2.2*95 | Answer: 7315 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 240 m/min, feed = 0.4 mm/rev, depth of cut = 1.9 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 240, f = 0.4, d = 1.9 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*240*0.4*1.9 | Answer: 182400 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 280 mm is turned at 350 rpm with a feed of 0.14 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 280, N = 350, f = 0.14 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 280 / (0.14*350) | Answer: 5.714 min

question: A resistor of 146 ohm carries a current of 3.5 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 146, I = 3.5 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 3.5 * 146 | Answer: 511 V

question: Three resistors 6 ohm, 37 ohm and 31 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 6, R2 = 37, R3 = 31 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 6 + 37 + 31 | Answer: 74 ohm

question: Two resistors 24 ohm and 107 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 24, R2 = 107 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 24*107 / (24+107) | Answer: 19.6 ohm

question: A device draws 8.7 A at 100 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 100, I = 8.7 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 100 * 8.7 | Answer: 870 W

question: A current of 10.8 A flows through a 48 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 10.8, R = 48 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (10.8)^2 * 48 | Answer: 5599 W

question: Two capacitors 13 uF and 16.1 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 13, C2 = 16.1 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 13*16.1 / (13+16.1) | Answer: 7.192 uF

question: A resistor 78 kohm and capacitor 14.5 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 78, C = 14.5 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (78k)(14.5u) = 1131 ms | Answer: 1131 ms

question: An inductor 350.8 mH is in series with 75 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 350.8, R = 75 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (350.8e-3) / 75 | Answer: 4.677 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 190.3 mH inductor at 260 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 190.3, f = 260 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (260)(190.3e-3) | Answer: 310.9 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 48.3 uF capacitor at 890 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 48.3, f = 890 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (890)(48.3e-6)) | Answer: 3.702 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 57 ohm, XL = 63 ohm and XC = 120 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 57, XL = 63, XC = 120 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(57^2 + (63 - 120)^2) | Answer: 80.61 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 21.1 mH and C = 1.7 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 21.1, C = 1.7 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(21.1e-3 * 1.7e-6)) | Answer: 840.3 Hz

question: A capacitor of 33.6 uF is charged to 400 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 33.6, V = 400 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*33.6e-6*(400)^2 | Answer: 2688 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 250 V with 980 primary turns and 170 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 250, N1 = 980, N2 = 170 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 250 * 170/980 | Answer: 43.37 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 190 V and draws an armature current of 55 A. If the armature resistance is 0.24 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 190, Ia = 55, Ra = 0.24 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 190 - 55*0.24 | Answer: 176.8 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 110 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.73. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 110, VL = 400, pf = 0.73 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*400*110*0.73 / 1000 | Answer: 55.63 kW

question: A load has real power 55 kW and apparent power 200 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 55, S = 200 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 55 / 200 | Answer: 0.275

question: A machine delivers 55 kW output while drawing 157 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 55, Pi = 157 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 55/157 * 100 | Answer: 35.03 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 6 V across R1 = 26 ohm and R2 = 21 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 6, R1 = 26, R2 = 21 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 6*21 / (26+21) | Answer: 2.681 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 100 kohm and Rin = 35 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 100, Rin = 35 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 100 / 35 | Answer: 2.857

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 20 kohm and Rg = 28 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 20, Rg = 28 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 20/28 | Answer: 1.714

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 8972. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 8972 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(8972) | Answer: 39.53 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 10 m carries a central point load of 80 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 10, W = 80 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 80*10 / 4 | Answer: 200 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 7.2 m carries a UDL of 45 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7.2, w = 45 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 45*(7.2)^2 / 8 | Answer: 291.6 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 2.5 m carries a point load 40 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 2.5, W = 40 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 40*2.5 | Answer: 100 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 1.4 m carries a UDL of 34 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 1.4, w = 34 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 34*(1.4)^2 / 2 | Answer: 33.32 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.3 m carries a point load 40 kN at distance 1.4 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 6.3, a = 1.4, W = 40 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 40*(6.3 - 1.4) / 6.3 | Answer: 31.11 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 4.7 m) carries a central point load 45 kN. With E = 25 GPa and I = 50e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=45000 N, L=4700.0 mm, E=25000 MPa, I=50e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 77.87 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 5.2 m carries a UDL of 18 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.2, w = 18 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 18*(5.2)^2 / 12 | Answer: 40.56 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 390 mm, clear cover 40 mm and main bars of diameter 16 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 390, c = 40, dia = 16 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 390 - 40 - 16/2 | Answer: 342 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 13.6 m^2 carrying a factored load of 18.9 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 13.6, w = 18.9 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 18.9 * 13.6 | Answer: 257 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 6.9 m, unit weight 16 kN/m^3, phi = 38 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 3.6e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1.5, area = 2.8e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 3.6, i = 1.5, A = 2.8 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (3.6e-4)*1.5*(2.8e-3) | Answer: 1512 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.2 m, bed slope 0.005 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.025. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 1.2 m under a head of 0.9 m. Taking Cd = 0.62 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 4.2 m wide carries a discharge of 21.3 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A tank of volume 670 m^3 treats a flow of 15 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 670, Q = 15 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 670 / 15 | Answer: 44.67 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 280 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.14 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 3 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 280, k = 0.14, t = 3 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 280*(1 - e^(-0.14*3)) | Answer: 96.03 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.88, rainfall intensity 55 mm/h over a catchment of 33.7 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.88, i = 55, A = 33.7 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.88*55*33.7 / 360 | Answer: 4.531 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.06 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 400 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.06, M = 400 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 400*(30+0.06)/30 | Answer: 400.8 m

question: Convert the decimal number 3282 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 3282 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: CD2 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 11011010 and 11010000.
solution: XOR: 00001010 | Count of 1s = 2 | Answer: 2
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 920 megabits is sent over a link of 66 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 920, B = 66 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 920 / 66 | Answer: 13.94 s

question: A link has bandwidth 92 Mbps and round-trip time 20 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 92, R = 20 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 92e6 * 20e-3 bits = 1840 kb | Answer: 1840 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.93, cache access time 6 ns and main-memory access time 130 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.93, tc = 6, tm = 130 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.93*6 + (1 - 0.93)*130 | Answer: 14.68 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 389492 elements?
solution: Given: n = 389492 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(389492)) + 1 | Answer: 19

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.009, memory access time 150 ns and page-fault service time 5 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 5 ms = 5000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.009)*150 + 0.009*5000000.0 ns | Answer: 45.15 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 1.7 m^3 at 260 kPa and 470 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 1.7, P = 260, Tk = 470 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (260e3)*1.7 / (8.314*470) | Answer: 113.1 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.05 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 2 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.05, t = 2 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.05*2) | Answer: 0.09516

question: For a reaction with A = 2e10 /s and activation energy 50 kJ/mol at 410 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 2, Ea = 50, Tk = 410 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 2e10 * exp(-50e3 / (8.314*410)) | Answer: 8526 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.92 and bottoms xW = 0.02, with relative volatility alpha = 3.2. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.92, xw = 0.02, al = 3.2 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.92/0.08)(0.98/0.02)] / ln(3.2) | Answer: 5.446 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.74 and x = 0.32. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.74, x = 0.32 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.74/0.26) / (0.32/0.68) | Answer: 6.048

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.33 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 30 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.33, Psat = 30 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.33 * 30 | Answer: 9.9 kPa

question: A stream of 2.3 kg/s with specific heat 1.7 kJ/kg-K is heated through 100 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 2.3, cp = 1.7, dT = 100 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 2.3*1.7*100 | Answer: 391 kW

question: A reactor of volume 12.2 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 1.8 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 12.2, Q = 1.8 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 12.2 / 1.8 | Answer: 6.778 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 3.1e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 1 mm with a concentration difference of 180 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 3.1, L = 1, dC = 180 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (3.1e-9)*180 / (1e-3) | Answer: 558 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 7.4 min and steady-state gain 2.7. For a step input of magnitude 6, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 7.4, K = 2.7, M = 6 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 2.7 * 6 | Answer: 16.2 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 95 m^2 flies at 260 m/s (air density 1.225 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.7. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 95, V = 260, rho = 1.225, CL = 0.7 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1.225*(260)^2*95*0.7 / 1000 | Answer: 2753 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 115 m^2 flies at 170 m/s (density 0.7 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.04. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 115, V = 170, rho = 0.7, CD = 0.04 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.7*(170)^2*115*0.04 / 1000 | Answer: 46.53 kN

question: A specimen under stress 370 MPa shows an elastic strain of 2.6e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 370, eps = 2.6 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 370 / (2.6e-3) MPa = 142.3 GPa | Answer: 142.3 GPa

question: A block of mass 11 kg has a volume of 5.3e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 11, V = 5.3 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 11 / (5.3e-3) | Answer: 2075 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 2900 mm is heated through 125 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 23e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 2900, dT = 125, al = 23 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 2900*23e-6*125 | Answer: 8.337 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 185 ohm, R2 = 165 ohm and R3 = 120 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 185, R2 = 165, R3 = 120 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 165*120 / 185 | Answer: 107 ohm

question: A measurement reads 10.64 when the true value is 50. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10.64, true = 50 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10.64 - 50| / 50 * 100 | Answer: 78.72 %

question: Annual demand is 30000 units, ordering cost 270 per order and holding cost 25 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 30000, S = 270, H = 25 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*30000*270 / 25) | Answer: 805 units

question: An asset costs 400000 with salvage value 24000 after 8 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 400000, Sv = 24000, n = 8 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (400000 - 24000) / 8 | Answer: 47000 per year

question: A product sells for 190 per unit with variable cost 170 per unit and fixed costs 125000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 190, V = 170, F = 125000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 125000 / (190 - 170) | Answer: 6250 units

question: Find the present worth of 30000 received 4 years from now at an interest rate of 8% per year.
solution: Given: F = 30000, n = 4, i = 8 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 30000 / (1 + 0.08)^4 | Answer: 22051 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.94, 0.95 and 0.99 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.94, r2 = 0.95, r3 = 0.99 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.94*0.95*0.99 | Answer: 0.8841

question: A process produces 39 defective items in a batch of 19000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 39, N = 19000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 39/19000 * 1e6 | Answer: 2053 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -x^3 - 5x - 8 evaluated at x = -5.
For f(x) = -x^3 + 5x^2 - 9x + 9, find f''(x) at x = -4.
Evaluate the definite integral of (x^2 + x - 2) dx from x = -4 to x = 6.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = 1x^3/3 + 1x^2/2 + -2x | Evaluate F(6) - F(-4) | Answer: 83.33
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 4x^2 - 11x - 8 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[-4, -7], [-5, 9]].
solution: Given: a = -4, b = -7, c = -5, d = 9 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (-4)(9) - (-7)(-5) | Answer: -71

question: Find the determinant of [[5, -6, 2], [3, -4, 0], [0, -6, -2]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: -32

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[0, 1], [5, -4]].
solution: Trace tr = -4, Determinant = -5 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 1

question: Solve for x: -1x + -2y = 3 and 0x + -2y = 4.
solution: Determinant = -1*-2 - -2*0 = 2 | x = (e d - b f) / det = 1 | Answer: x = 1
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 85, 78, 45, 9, 24.
solution: Sum = 241 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 48.2 | Answer: 48.2

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 13, 36, 46, 50, 29.
solution: Mean = 34.8 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 14.72

question: Find the slope of the line through (3, -6) and (8, 6).
solution: Given: x1 = 3, y1 = -6, x2 = 8, y2 = 6 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (6 - -6) / (8 - 3) | Answer: 2.4

question: Find the distance between the points (-1, -9) and (0, 3).
solution: Given: x1 = -1, y1 = -9, x2 = 0, y2 = 3 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((1)^2 + (12)^2) | Answer: 12.04 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (-4,-6), (-5,8), (1,1).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 38.5 sq units

question: Find the 27th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -11 and common difference -1.
solution: Given: a = -11, d = -1, n = 27 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -11 + (27 - 1)*-1 | Answer: -37

question: Find the sum of the first 8 terms of an AP with first term -15 and common difference -3.
solution: Given: a = -15, d = -3, n = 8 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 8/2 [2*-15 + (8-1)*-3] | Answer: -204

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 1000 at 6.9% per annum for 10 years.
solution: Given: P = 1000, R = 6.9, Tt = 10 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 1000 * 6.9 * 10 / 100 | Answer: 690 currency units

question: Find the amount when 34000 is invested at 11.8% per annum compounded annually for 2 years.
solution: Given: P = 34000, R = 11.8, Tt = 2 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 34000 * (1 + 11.8/100)^2 | Answer: 42497 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (-8, 2, 1) and (8, 0, -3).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (-1, -1, 2) and (6, -1, -2).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 12.85

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (-4, 2, 5) and (-5, 0, -6).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 101 degrees

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number -11 + -12i.
solution: Given: a = -11, b = -12 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(-12, -11) | Answer: -132.5 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = 5x^3 - 5x - 5 at x = -3.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-163 with initial guess x0=6, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.8 and ordinates 4, 16, 12, 20, 20, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 358 and 149.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 358 and 149 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 56 and 53.
solution: Given: a = 56, b = 53 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 56*53 / 1 | Answer: 2968
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 38 mm carries an axial tensile load of 63 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 24 mm and length 2500 mm carries an axial load of 77 kN. Take E = 70 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 57 mm transmits a torque of 750 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 57, Tt = 750 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(750*1000) / (pi*(57)^3) | Answer: 20.63 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 58 mm and length 900 mm carries a torque of 1600 N-m. With G = 80 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (58)^4 / 32 = 1110994 mm^4 | theta = (1600*1000)(900) / (80000 * 1110994) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 0.9283 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 96 mm wide and 240 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 96, h = 240 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 96*(240)^2 / 6 | Answer: 921600 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (72 mm x 80 mm) carries a bending moment of 15 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (42 mm x 110 mm) has effective length 3700 mm and E = 200 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 490 MPa is designed for a working stress of 80 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 490, sw = 80 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 490 / 80 | Answer: 6.125

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 500 mm and wall thickness 11 mm carries an internal pressure of 2.3 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 500, t = 11, P = 2.3 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 2.3*500 / (2*11) | Answer: 52.27 MPa

question: 5.4 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 155 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 5.4, dT = 155 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 5.4 * 0.718 * 155 | Answer: 601 kJ

question: 2.3 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 55 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.3, dT = 55 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 2.3 * 1.005 * 55 | Answer: 127.1 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 1 m^3 at 370 K with mass 3.3 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 1, Tk = 370, m = 3.3 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 3.3*0.287*370 / 1 | Answer: 350.4 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 1.8 kg of air expands isothermally at 320 K from volume V1 to 4*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1.8, Tk = 320, ratio = 4 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 1.8*0.287*320*ln(4) | Answer: 229.2 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 4.7 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.25 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 4.7, D = 0.25 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*4.7*0.25 / 0.001 | Answer: 1175000

question: Water flows at 0.8 m/s through a pipe of diameter 140 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
In a pipe (diameter 230 mm) water flows at 0.6 m/s. It contracts to diameter 80 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 230, d2 = 80, V1 = 0.6 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 0.6*(230/80)^2 | Answer: 4.959 m/s

question: Water flows at 1.9 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.12 m and length 390 m. With friction factor f = 0.022, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 30 teeth drives a gear of 107 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1500 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 30, z2 = 107, N1 = 1500 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1500*30 / 107 | Answer: 420.6 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 390 mm rotates at 500 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 390, N = 500 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.39)*500 / 60 | Answer: 10.21 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 30.3 kW at 650 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 30.3, N = 650 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(30.3*1000) / (2*pi*650) | Answer: 445.1 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 8.4 kg rotates at radius 0.27 m at 350 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 13500 N/m and mass 12.5 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 13500, m = 12.5 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(13500/12.5) | Answer: 5.23 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 6.8 m^2 and thickness 0.32 m has conductivity k = 40.7 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 55 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 6.8, L = 0.32, k = 40.7, dT = 55 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 40.7*6.8*55 / 0.32 | Answer: 47568 W

question: A surface of area 5.3 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 50 W/m^2-K to surroundings 100 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 5.3, h = 50, dT = 100 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 50*5.3*100 | Answer: 26500 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 170 m/min, feed = 0.18 mm/rev, depth of cut = 1.2 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 170, f = 0.18, d = 1.2 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*170*0.18*1.2 | Answer: 36720 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 130 mm is turned at 850 rpm with a feed of 0.33 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 130, N = 850, f = 0.33 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 130 / (0.33*850) | Answer: 0.4635 min

question: A resistor of 176 ohm carries a current of 7.5 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 176, I = 7.5 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 7.5 * 176 | Answer: 1320 V

question: Three resistors 26 ohm, 97 ohm and 2 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 26, R2 = 97, R3 = 2 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 26 + 97 + 2 | Answer: 125 ohm

question: Two resistors 6 ohm and 2 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 6, R2 = 2 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 6*2 / (6+2) | Answer: 1.5 ohm

question: A device draws 9.3 A at 20 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 20, I = 9.3 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 20 * 9.3 | Answer: 186 W

question: A current of 8 A flows through a 104 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 8, R = 104 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (8)^2 * 104 | Answer: 6656 W

question: Two capacitors 47.1 uF and 20.7 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 47.1, C2 = 20.7 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 47.1*20.7 / (47.1+20.7) | Answer: 14.38 uF

question: A resistor 51 kohm and capacitor 2.5 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 51, C = 2.5 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (51k)(2.5u) = 127.5 ms | Answer: 127.5 ms

question: An inductor 44.3 mH is in series with 64 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 44.3, R = 64 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (44.3e-3) / 64 | Answer: 0.6922 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 109.6 mH inductor at 160 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 109.6, f = 160 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (160)(109.6e-3) | Answer: 110.2 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 33.5 uF capacitor at 660 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 33.5, f = 660 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (660)(33.5e-6)) | Answer: 7.198 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 67 ohm, XL = 118 ohm and XC = 20 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 67, XL = 118, XC = 20 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(67^2 + (118 - 20)^2) | Answer: 118.7 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 89.2 mH and C = 7.7 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 89.2, C = 7.7 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(89.2e-3 * 7.7e-6)) | Answer: 192 Hz

question: A capacitor of 14.3 uF is charged to 120 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 14.3, V = 120 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*14.3e-6*(120)^2 | Answer: 103 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 340 V with 560 primary turns and 110 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 340, N1 = 560, N2 = 110 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 340 * 110/560 | Answer: 66.79 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 440 V and draws an armature current of 25 A. If the armature resistance is 0.29 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 440, Ia = 25, Ra = 0.29 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 440 - 25*0.29 | Answer: 432.8 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 165 A at 433 V (line) with a power factor of 0.87. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 165, VL = 433, pf = 0.87 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*433*165*0.87 / 1000 | Answer: 107.7 kW

question: A load has real power 90 kW and apparent power 100 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 90, S = 100 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 90 / 100 | Answer: 0.9

question: A machine delivers 20 kW output while drawing 202 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 20, Pi = 202 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 20/202 * 100 | Answer: 9.901 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 14 V across R1 = 29 ohm and R2 = 40 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 14, R1 = 29, R2 = 40 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 14*40 / (29+40) | Answer: 8.116 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 180 kohm and Rin = 38 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 180, Rin = 38 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 180 / 38 | Answer: 4.737

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 170 kohm and Rg = 6 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 170, Rg = 6 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 170/6 | Answer: 29.33

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 2899. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 2899 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(2899) | Answer: 34.62 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 4 m carries a central point load of 50 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4, W = 50 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 50*4 / 4 | Answer: 50 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 7.4 m carries a UDL of 50 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7.4, w = 50 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 50*(7.4)^2 / 8 | Answer: 342.3 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 3.3 m carries a point load 35 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.3, W = 35 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 35*3.3 | Answer: 115.5 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 1.9 m carries a UDL of 36 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 1.9, w = 36 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 36*(1.9)^2 / 2 | Answer: 64.98 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 7.3 m carries a point load 65 kN at distance 3.8 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 7.3, a = 3.8, W = 65 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 65*(7.3 - 3.8) / 7.3 | Answer: 31.16 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 5.8 m) carries a central point load 10 kN. With E = 30 GPa and I = 110e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=10000 N, L=5800.0 mm, E=30000 MPa, I=110e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 12.32 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 6.9 m carries a UDL of 21 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6.9, w = 21 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 21*(6.9)^2 / 12 | Answer: 83.32 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 550 mm, clear cover 40 mm and main bars of diameter 25 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 550, c = 40, dia = 25 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 550 - 40 - 25/2 | Answer: 497.5 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 18.9 m^2 carrying a factored load of 13.3 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 18.9, w = 13.3 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 13.3 * 18.9 | Answer: 251.4 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 5.1 m, unit weight 16 kN/m^3, phi = 32 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 6.6e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.7, area = 1.1e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 6.6, i = 0.7, A = 1.1 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (6.6e-4)*0.7*(1.1e-3) | Answer: 508.2 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 2.3 m, bed slope 0.007 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.021. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 3 m under a head of 0.3 m. Taking Cd = 0.63 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 4.7 m wide carries a discharge of 25.8 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A tank of volume 430 m^3 treats a flow of 110 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 430, Q = 110 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 430 / 110 | Answer: 3.909 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 270 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.22 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 4 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 270, k = 0.22, t = 4 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 270*(1 - e^(-0.22*4)) | Answer: 158 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.44, rainfall intensity 45 mm/h over a catchment of 22.9 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.44, i = 45, A = 22.9 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.44*45*22.9 / 360 | Answer: 1.26 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.06 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 180 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.06, M = 180 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 180*(30+0.06)/30 | Answer: 180.4 m

question: Convert the decimal number 447 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 447 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 1BF (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 00110000 and 01011000.
solution: XOR: 01101000 | Count of 1s = 3 | Answer: 3
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 660 megabits is sent over a link of 32 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 660, B = 32 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 660 / 32 | Answer: 20.62 s

question: A link has bandwidth 97 Mbps and round-trip time 100 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 97, R = 100 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 97e6 * 100e-3 bits = 9700 kb | Answer: 9700 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.97, cache access time 1 ns and main-memory access time 60 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.97, tc = 1, tm = 60 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.97*1 + (1 - 0.97)*60 | Answer: 2.77 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 967822 elements?
solution: Given: n = 967822 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(967822)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.017, memory access time 190 ns and page-fault service time 5 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 5 ms = 5000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.017)*190 + 0.017*5000000.0 ns | Answer: 85.19 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 0.9 m^3 at 300 kPa and 350 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 0.9, P = 300, Tk = 350 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (300e3)*0.9 / (8.314*350) | Answer: 92.79 mol

question: For a reaction with A = 2e10 /s and activation energy 50 kJ/mol at 300 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 2, Ea = 50, Tk = 300 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 2e10 * exp(-50e3 / (8.314*300)) | Answer: 39.35 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.97 and bottoms xW = 0.08, with relative volatility alpha = 1.7. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.97, xw = 0.08, al = 1.7 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.97/0.03)(0.92/0.08)] / ln(1.7) | Answer: 11.15 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.69 and x = 0.34. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.69, x = 0.34 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.69/0.31) / (0.34/0.66) | Answer: 4.321

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.32 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 65 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.32, Psat = 65 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.32 * 65 | Answer: 20.8 kPa

question: A stream of 6.5 kg/s with specific heat 1.4 kJ/kg-K is heated through 75 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 6.5, cp = 1.4, dT = 75 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 6.5*1.4*75 | Answer: 682.5 kW

question: A reactor of volume 14.7 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 3 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 14.7, Q = 3 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 14.7 / 3 | Answer: 4.9 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 3.2e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 1 mm with a concentration difference of 160 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 3.2, L = 1, dC = 160 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (3.2e-9)*160 / (1e-3) | Answer: 512 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 9.2 min and steady-state gain 1.8. For a step input of magnitude 7, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 9.2, K = 1.8, M = 7 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 1.8 * 7 | Answer: 12.6 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 75 m^2 flies at 90 m/s (air density 1 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.7. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 75, V = 90, rho = 1, CL = 0.7 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1*(90)^2*75*0.7 / 1000 | Answer: 212.6 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 95 m^2 flies at 150 m/s (density 0.4 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.04. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 95, V = 150, rho = 0.4, CD = 0.04 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.4*(150)^2*95*0.04 / 1000 | Answer: 17.1 kN

question: A specimen under stress 110 MPa shows an elastic strain of 1.4e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 110, eps = 1.4 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 110 / (1.4e-3) MPa = 78.57 GPa | Answer: 78.57 GPa

question: A block of mass 38 kg has a volume of 3.9e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 38, V = 3.9 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 38 / (3.9e-3) | Answer: 9744 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 1300 mm is heated through 105 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 23e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 1300, dT = 105, al = 23 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 1300*23e-6*105 | Answer: 3.139 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 75 ohm, R2 = 130 ohm and R3 = 485 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 75, R2 = 130, R3 = 485 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 130*485 / 75 | Answer: 840.7 ohm

question: Annual demand is 42500 units, ordering cost 40 per order and holding cost 31 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 42500, S = 40, H = 31 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*42500*40 / 31) | Answer: 331.2 units

question: An asset costs 90000 with salvage value 30000 after 10 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 90000, Sv = 30000, n = 10 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (90000 - 30000) / 10 | Answer: 6000 per year

question: A product sells for 370 per unit with variable cost 110 per unit and fixed costs 140000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 370, V = 110, F = 140000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 140000 / (370 - 110) | Answer: 538.5 units

question: Find the present worth of 110000 received 6 years from now at an interest rate of 9% per year.
solution: Given: F = 110000, n = 6, i = 9 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 110000 / (1 + 0.09)^6 | Answer: 65589 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.96, 0.91 and 0.94 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.96, r2 = 0.91, r3 = 0.94 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.96*0.91*0.94 | Answer: 0.8212

question: A process produces 6 defective items in a batch of 8000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 6, N = 8000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 6/8000 * 1e6 | Answer: 750 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = 4x^3 + x^2 + 6x - 4 evaluated at x = 1.
For f(x) = 6x^3 + 8x^2 + 9x + 8, find f''(x) at x = 4.
Evaluate the definite integral of (4x - 2) dx from x = 2 to x = 3.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = 0x^3/3 + 4x^2/2 + -2x | Evaluate F(3) - F(2) | Answer: 8
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 6x^2 - 7x - 9 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[-6, 2], [-3, -4]].
solution: Given: a = -6, b = 2, c = -3, d = -4 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (-6)(-4) - (2)(-3) | Answer: 30

question: Find the determinant of [[3, 6, 6], [-2, -1, 2], [0, 5, 0]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: -90

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[4, -6], [-3, 5]].
solution: Trace tr = 9, Determinant = 2 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 8.772

question: Solve for x: -1x + 5y = 12 and -4x + 5y = 11.
solution: Determinant = -1*5 - 5*-4 = 15 | x = (e d - b f) / det = 0.3333 | Answer: x = 0.3333
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 7, 56, 78, 37, 10.
solution: Sum = 188 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 37.6 | Answer: 37.6

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 1, 24, 19, 22, 30.
solution: Mean = 19.2 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 10.94

question: Find the slope of the line through (3, -5) and (-7, 5).
solution: Given: x1 = 3, y1 = -5, x2 = -7, y2 = 5 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (5 - -5) / (-7 - 3) | Answer: -1

question: Find the distance between the points (-9, -7) and (2, -5).
solution: Given: x1 = -9, y1 = -7, x2 = 2, y2 = -5 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((11)^2 + (2)^2) | Answer: 11.18 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (0,-8), (7,0), (-1,7).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 56.5 sq units

question: Find the 33th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 14 and common difference -3.
solution: Given: a = 14, d = -3, n = 33 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = 14 + (33 - 1)*-3 | Answer: -82

question: Find the sum of the first 38 terms of an AP with first term 14 and common difference 6.
solution: Given: a = 14, d = 6, n = 38 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 38/2 [2*14 + (38-1)*6] | Answer: 4750

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 21500 at 8.8% per annum for 8 years.
solution: Given: P = 21500, R = 8.8, Tt = 8 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 21500 * 8.8 * 8 / 100 | Answer: 15136 currency units

question: Find the amount when 35500 is invested at 4.7% per annum compounded annually for 2 years.
solution: Given: P = 35500, R = 4.7, Tt = 2 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 35500 * (1 + 4.7/100)^2 | Answer: 38915 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (3, 5, 6) and (-7, 1, -6).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (-3, 0, 6) and (2, 4, 3).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 34.07

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (2, -2, 5) and (5, -3, 3).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 34.62 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number 0 + -12i.
solution: Given: a = 0, b = -12 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((0)^2 + (-12)^2) | Answer: 12

question: Evaluate f(x) = 2x^3 - 3x^2 - 8x + 2 at x = -5.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-122 with initial guess x0=8, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=0.5 and ordinates 17, 8, 11, 16, 12, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 584 and 297.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 584 and 297 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 25 and 24.
solution: Given: a = 25, b = 24 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 25*24 / 1 | Answer: 600
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 56 mm carries an axial tensile load of 28 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 23 mm and length 2400 mm carries an axial load of 41 kN. Take E = 200 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 56 mm transmits a torque of 2800 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 56, Tt = 2800 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(2800*1000) / (pi*(56)^3) | Answer: 81.2 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 54 mm and length 1700 mm carries a torque of 1050 N-m. With G = 80 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (54)^4 / 32 = 834786 mm^4 | theta = (1050*1000)(1700) / (80000 * 834786) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 1.531 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 77 mm wide and 300 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 77, h = 300 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 77*(300)^2 / 6 | Answer: 1155000 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (75 mm x 230 mm) carries a bending moment of 22 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (47 mm x 150 mm) has effective length 3700 mm and E = 200 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 770 MPa is designed for a working stress of 190 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 770, sw = 190 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 770 / 190 | Answer: 4.053

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 850 mm and wall thickness 16 mm carries an internal pressure of 2.9 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 850, t = 16, P = 2.9 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 2.9*850 / (2*16) | Answer: 77.03 MPa

question: 6.6 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 25 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 6.6, dT = 25 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 6.6 * 0.718 * 25 | Answer: 118.5 kJ

question: 2.6 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 165 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.6, dT = 165 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 2.6 * 1.005 * 165 | Answer: 431.1 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 3.3 m^3 at 590 K with mass 3.1 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 3.3, Tk = 590, m = 3.1 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 3.1*0.287*590 / 3.3 | Answer: 159.1 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 2.8 kg of air expands isothermally at 320 K from volume V1 to 3*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.8, Tk = 320, ratio = 3 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 2.8*0.287*320*ln(3) | Answer: 282.5 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 1.5 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.14 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 1.5, D = 0.14 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*1.5*0.14 / 0.001 | Answer: 210000

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 16.1 m. Taking Cv = 0.97, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 16.1, cv = 0.97 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.97*sqrt(2*9.81*16.1) | Answer: 17.24 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 280 mm) water flows at 0.9 m/s. It contracts to diameter 100 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
Water flows at 2.3 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.18 m and length 90 m. With friction factor f = 0.028, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 23 teeth drives a gear of 96 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1050 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 23, z2 = 96, N1 = 1050 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1050*23 / 96 | Answer: 251.6 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 330 mm rotates at 1200 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 330, N = 1200 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.33)*1200 / 60 | Answer: 20.73 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 2.4 kW at 1450 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 2.4, N = 1450 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(2.4*1000) / (2*pi*1450) | Answer: 15.81 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)
