question: A mass of 7.9 kg rotates at radius 0.57 m at 200 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 16700 N/m and mass 8.7 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 16700, m = 8.7 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(16700/8.7) | Answer: 6.973 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 1.5 m^2 and thickness 0.21 m has conductivity k = 34.9 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 155 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 1.5, L = 0.21, k = 34.9, dT = 155 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 34.9*1.5*155 / 0.21 | Answer: 38639 W

question: A surface of area 0.5 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 35 W/m^2-K to surroundings 75 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 0.5, h = 35, dT = 75 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 35*0.5*75 | Answer: 1312 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 130 m/min, feed = 0.44 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2.7 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 130, f = 0.44, d = 2.7 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*130*0.44*2.7 | Answer: 154440 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 390 mm is turned at 800 rpm with a feed of 0.23 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 390, N = 800, f = 0.23 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 390 / (0.23*800) | Answer: 2.12 min

question: A resistor of 3 ohm carries a current of 6.3 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 3, I = 6.3 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 6.3 * 3 | Answer: 18.9 V

question: Three resistors 66 ohm, 56 ohm and 72 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 66, R2 = 56, R3 = 72 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 66 + 56 + 72 | Answer: 194 ohm

question: Two resistors 95 ohm and 96 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 95, R2 = 96 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 95*96 / (95+96) | Answer: 47.75 ohm

question: A device draws 5.2 A at 230 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 230, I = 5.2 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 230 * 5.2 | Answer: 1196 W

question: A current of 9.6 A flows through a 53 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 9.6, R = 53 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (9.6)^2 * 53 | Answer: 4884 W

question: Two capacitors 44 uF and 29.5 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 44, C2 = 29.5 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 44*29.5 / (44+29.5) | Answer: 17.66 uF

question: A resistor 59 kohm and capacitor 17.9 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 59, C = 17.9 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (59k)(17.9u) = 1056 ms | Answer: 1056 ms

question: An inductor 69.9 mH is in series with 90 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 69.9, R = 90 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (69.9e-3) / 90 | Answer: 0.7767 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 143 mH inductor at 720 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 143, f = 720 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (720)(143e-3) | Answer: 646.9 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 28.6 uF capacitor at 570 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 28.6, f = 570 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (570)(28.6e-6)) | Answer: 9.763 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 63 ohm, XL = 78 ohm and XC = 106 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 63, XL = 78, XC = 106 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(63^2 + (78 - 106)^2) | Answer: 68.94 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 60.5 mH and C = 6.7 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 60.5, C = 6.7 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(60.5e-3 * 6.7e-6)) | Answer: 250 Hz

question: A capacitor of 66.8 uF is charged to 290 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 66.8, V = 290 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*66.8e-6*(290)^2 | Answer: 2809 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 240 V with 990 primary turns and 330 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 240, N1 = 990, N2 = 330 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 240 * 330/990 | Answer: 80 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 110 V and draws an armature current of 59 A. If the armature resistance is 0.53 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 110, Ia = 59, Ra = 0.53 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 110 - 59*0.53 | Answer: 78.73 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 10 A at 433 V (line) with a power factor of 0.98. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 10, VL = 433, pf = 0.98 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*433*10*0.98 / 1000 | Answer: 7.35 kW

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 15 V across R1 = 40 ohm and R2 = 23 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 15, R1 = 40, R2 = 23 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 15*23 / (40+23) | Answer: 5.476 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 160 kohm and Rin = 22 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 160, Rin = 22 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 160 / 22 | Answer: 7.273

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 20 kohm and Rg = 8 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 20, Rg = 8 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 20/8 | Answer: 3.5

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 8713. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 8713 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(8713) | Answer: 39.4 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.2 m carries a central point load of 95 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.2, W = 95 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 95*4.2 / 4 | Answer: 99.75 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 3.7 m carries a UDL of 35 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.7, w = 35 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 35*(3.7)^2 / 8 | Answer: 59.89 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 4.1 m carries a point load 50 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.1, W = 50 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 50*4.1 | Answer: 205 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 5.9 m carries a UDL of 34 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.9, w = 34 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 34*(5.9)^2 / 2 | Answer: 591.8 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.6 m carries a point load 85 kN at distance 1.2 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 4.6, a = 1.2, W = 85 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 85*(4.6 - 1.2) / 4.6 | Answer: 62.83 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 6.2 m) carries a central point load 25 kN. With E = 30 GPa and I = 260e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=25000 N, L=6200.0 mm, E=30000 MPa, I=260e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 15.91 mm

question: An RC beam has overall depth 650 mm, clear cover 40 mm and main bars of diameter 25 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 650, c = 40, dia = 25 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 650 - 40 - 25/2 | Answer: 597.5 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 33.9 m^2 carrying a factored load of 16.6 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 33.9, w = 16.6 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 16.6 * 33.9 | Answer: 562.7 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 4.9 m, unit weight 16 kN/m^3, phi = 35 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 8e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.7, area = 6.6e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 8, i = 0.7, A = 6.6 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (8e-4)*0.7*(6.6e-3) | Answer: 3696 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.2 m, bed slope 0.005 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.014. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 3.7 m under a head of 0.7 m. Taking Cd = 0.62 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 4.4 m wide carries a discharge of 14.7 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A tank of volume 860 m^3 treats a flow of 70 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 860, Q = 70 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 860 / 70 | Answer: 12.29 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 200 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.11 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 3 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 200, k = 0.11, t = 3 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 200*(1 - e^(-0.11*3)) | Answer: 56.22 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.59, rainfall intensity 35 mm/h over a catchment of 45 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.59, i = 35, A = 45 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.59*35*45 / 360 | Answer: 2.581 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.03 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 110 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.03, M = 110 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 110*(30+0.03)/30 | Answer: 110.1 m

question: Convert the decimal number 187 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 187 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: BB (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 10000010 and 10010111.
solution: XOR: 00010101 | Count of 1s = 3 | Answer: 3
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 880 megabits is sent over a link of 22 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 880, B = 22 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 880 / 22 | Answer: 40 s

question: A link has bandwidth 91 Mbps and round-trip time 160 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 91, R = 160 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 91e6 * 160e-3 bits = 14560 kb | Answer: 14560 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.9, cache access time 10 ns and main-memory access time 190 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.9, tc = 10, tm = 190 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.9*10 + (1 - 0.9)*190 | Answer: 28 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 892734 elements?
solution: Given: n = 892734 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(892734)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.018, memory access time 190 ns and page-fault service time 7 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 7 ms = 7000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.018)*190 + 0.018*7000000.0 ns | Answer: 126.2 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 1 m^3 at 130 kPa and 500 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 1, P = 130, Tk = 500 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (130e3)*1 / (8.314*500) | Answer: 31.27 mol

question: For a reaction with A = 5e10 /s and activation energy 80 kJ/mol at 350 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 5, Ea = 80, Tk = 350 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 5e10 * exp(-80e3 / (8.314*350)) | Answer: 0.05744 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.97 and bottoms xW = 0.09, with relative volatility alpha = 2.5. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.97, xw = 0.09, al = 2.5 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.97/0.03)(0.91/0.09)] / ln(2.5) | Answer: 6.319 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.57 and x = 0.28. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.57, x = 0.28 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.57/0.43) / (0.28/0.72) | Answer: 3.409

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.59 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 50 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.59, Psat = 50 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.59 * 50 | Answer: 29.5 kPa

question: A stream of 4.9 kg/s with specific heat 1.8 kJ/kg-K is heated through 25 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 4.9, cp = 1.8, dT = 25 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 4.9*1.8*25 | Answer: 220.5 kW

question: A reactor of volume 18.4 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 2.3 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 18.4, Q = 2.3 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 18.4 / 2.3 | Answer: 8 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 7.6e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 4 mm with a concentration difference of 140 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 7.6, L = 4, dC = 140 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (7.6e-9)*140 / (4e-3) | Answer: 266 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 5.5 min and steady-state gain 3.4. For a step input of magnitude 20, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 5.5, K = 3.4, M = 20 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 3.4 * 20 | Answer: 68 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 75 m^2 flies at 140 m/s (air density 1.225 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 1.3. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 75, V = 140, rho = 1.225, CL = 1.3 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1.225*(140)^2*75*1.3 / 1000 | Answer: 117 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 60 m^2 flies at 150 m/s (density 1 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.11. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 60, V = 150, rho = 1, CD = 0.11 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*1*(150)^2*60*0.11 / 1000 | Answer: 74.25 kN

question: A specimen under stress 310 MPa shows an elastic strain of 2.8e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 310, eps = 2.8 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 310 / (2.8e-3) MPa = 110.7 GPa | Answer: 110.7 GPa

question: A block of mass 13 kg has a volume of 2.2e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 13, V = 2.2 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 13 / (2.2e-3) | Answer: 5909 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 1200 mm is heated through 60 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 23e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 1200, dT = 60, al = 23 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 1200*23e-6*60 | Answer: 1.656 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 165 ohm, R2 = 45 ohm and R3 = 430 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 165, R2 = 45, R3 = 430 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 45*430 / 165 | Answer: 117.3 ohm

question: A measurement reads 10.41 when the true value is 50. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10.41, true = 50 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10.41 - 50| / 50 * 100 | Answer: 79.18 %

question: Annual demand is 18000 units, ordering cost 270 per order and holding cost 29 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 18000, S = 270, H = 29 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*18000*270 / 29) | Answer: 578.9 units

question: An asset costs 200000 with salvage value 34000 after 13 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 200000, Sv = 34000, n = 13 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (200000 - 34000) / 13 | Answer: 12769 per year

question: A product sells for 430 per unit with variable cost 160 per unit and fixed costs 20000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 430, V = 160, F = 20000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 20000 / (430 - 160) | Answer: 74.07 units

question: Find the present worth of 55000 received 7 years from now at an interest rate of 11% per year.
solution: Given: F = 55000, n = 7, i = 11 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 55000 / (1 + 0.11)^7 | Answer: 26491 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.92, 0.95 and 0.97 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.92, r2 = 0.95, r3 = 0.97 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.92*0.95*0.97 | Answer: 0.8478

question: A process produces 2 defective items in a batch of 17500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 2, N = 17500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 2/17500 * 1e6 | Answer: 114.3 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = 5x^3 - 3x^2 + 4x - 4 evaluated at x = 0.
For f(x) = x^3 + 7x^2 + 5x, find f''(x) at x = -3.
Evaluate the definite integral of (6x) dx from x = -1 to x = 7.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = 0x^3/3 + 6x^2/2 + 0x | Evaluate F(7) - F(-1) | Answer: 144
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 2x^2 - 11x - 4 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[8, -5], [-2, -9]].
solution: Given: a = 8, b = -5, c = -2, d = -9 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (8)(-9) - (-5)(-2) | Answer: -82

question: Find the determinant of [[-4, -1, -5], [1, 0, -4], [2, -5, -5]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: 108

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[7, 7], [-3, -8]].
solution: Trace tr = -1, Determinant = -35 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 5.437

question: Solve for x: -2x + -1y = 4 and -2x + 5y = -8.
solution: Determinant = -2*5 - -1*-2 = -12 | x = (e d - b f) / det = -1 | Answer: x = -1

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 66, 96, 47, 33, 88.
solution: Sum = 330 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 66 | Answer: 66

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 36, 5, 31, 38, 12.
solution: Mean = 24.4 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 14.94

question: Find the slope of the line through (-3, 4) and (4, -3).
solution: Given: x1 = -3, y1 = 4, x2 = 4, y2 = -3 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (-3 - 4) / (4 - -3) | Answer: -1

question: Find the distance between the points (-4, -7) and (5, 4).
solution: Given: x1 = -4, y1 = -7, x2 = 5, y2 = 4 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((9)^2 + (11)^2) | Answer: 14.21 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (-8,7), (4,-1), (6,4).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 38 sq units

question: Find the 11th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -18 and common difference -3.
solution: Given: a = -18, d = -3, n = 11 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -18 + (11 - 1)*-3 | Answer: -48

question: Find the sum of the first 29 terms of an AP with first term 13 and common difference -8.
solution: Given: a = 13, d = -8, n = 29 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 29/2 [2*13 + (29-1)*-8] | Answer: -2871

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 3000 at 5.5% per annum for 10 years.
solution: Given: P = 3000, R = 5.5, Tt = 10 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 3000 * 5.5 * 10 / 100 | Answer: 1650 currency units

question: Find the amount when 14000 is invested at 8.4% per annum compounded annually for 5 years.
solution: Given: P = 14000, R = 8.4, Tt = 5 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 14000 * (1 + 8.4/100)^5 | Answer: 20954 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (3, -7, 1) and (3, -4, 4).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (3, -2, 3) and (-6, -5, 0).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 35.75

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (1, 0, 2) and (-3, 2, -2).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 139.4 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = 2x^3 - 6x^2 - 4x + 8 at x = 2.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-67 with initial guess x0=8, find x1 (one iteration).
solution: Given: N = 67, x0 = 8 | Formula: x1 = x0 - (x0^2 - N)/(2 x0) | Substitute: x1 = 8 - ((8)^2 - 67)/(2*8) | Answer: 8.188

question: Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.6 and ordinates 13, 9, 8, 18, 10, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 423 and 148.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 423 and 148 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 46 and 39.
solution: Given: a = 46, b = 39 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 46*39 / 1 | Answer: 1794
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 54 mm carries an axial tensile load of 53 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 33 mm and length 900 mm carries an axial load of 39 kN. Take E = 70 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 34 mm transmits a torque of 2650 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 34, Tt = 2650 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(2650*1000) / (pi*(34)^3) | Answer: 343.4 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 70 mm and length 1700 mm carries a torque of 1950 N-m. With G = 77 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (70)^4 / 32 = 2357176 mm^4 | theta = (1950*1000)(1700) / (77000 * 2357176) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 1.046 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 54 mm wide and 60 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 54, h = 60 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 54*(60)^2 / 6 | Answer: 32400 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (117 mm x 260 mm) carries a bending moment of 25 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (72 mm x 150 mm) has effective length 3200 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 750 MPa is designed for a working stress of 200 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 750, sw = 200 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 750 / 200 | Answer: 3.75

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1000 mm and wall thickness 12 mm carries an internal pressure of 2.6 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1000, t = 12, P = 2.6 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 2.6*1000 / (2*12) | Answer: 108.3 MPa

question: 5.1 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 70 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 5.1, dT = 70 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 5.1 * 0.718 * 70 | Answer: 256.3 kJ

question: 3.9 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 130 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.9, dT = 130 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 3.9 * 1.005 * 130 | Answer: 509.5 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 2.6 m^3 at 420 K with mass 2.9 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 2.6, Tk = 420, m = 2.9 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 2.9*0.287*420 / 2.6 | Answer: 134.4 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 3.5 kg of air expands isothermally at 300 K from volume V1 to 5*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.5, Tk = 300, ratio = 5 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 3.5*0.287*300*ln(5) | Answer: 485 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 3.4 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.32 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 3.4, D = 0.32 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*3.4*0.32 / 0.001 | Answer: 1088000

question: Water flows at 4 m/s through a pipe of diameter 120 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 5.7 m. Taking Cv = 0.96, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 5.7, cv = 0.96 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.96*sqrt(2*9.81*5.7) | Answer: 10.15 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 200 mm) water flows at 0.7 m/s. It contracts to diameter 60 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 200, d2 = 60, V1 = 0.7 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 0.7*(200/60)^2 | Answer: 7.778 m/s

question: Water flows at 1.5 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.12 m and length 310 m. With friction factor f = 0.04, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 23 teeth drives a gear of 100 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1250 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 23, z2 = 100, N1 = 1250 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1250*23 / 100 | Answer: 287.5 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 220 mm rotates at 850 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 220, N = 850 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.22)*850 / 60 | Answer: 9.791 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 14.8 kW at 1400 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 14.8, N = 1400 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(14.8*1000) / (2*pi*1400) | Answer: 100.9 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 1.7 kg rotates at radius 0.45 m at 250 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 3700 N/m and mass 9.1 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 3700, m = 9.1 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(3700/9.1) | Answer: 3.209 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 6.5 m^2 and thickness 0.11 m has conductivity k = 8.2 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 190 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 6.5, L = 0.11, k = 8.2, dT = 190 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 8.2*6.5*190 / 0.11 | Answer: 92064 W

question: A surface of area 1.4 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 145 W/m^2-K to surroundings 90 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 1.4, h = 145, dT = 90 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 145*1.4*90 | Answer: 18270 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 210 m/min, feed = 0.48 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2.3 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 210, f = 0.48, d = 2.3 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*210*0.48*2.3 | Answer: 231840 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 370 mm is turned at 600 rpm with a feed of 0.29 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 370, N = 600, f = 0.29 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 370 / (0.29*600) | Answer: 2.126 min

question: A resistor of 188 ohm carries a current of 1.5 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 188, I = 1.5 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 1.5 * 188 | Answer: 282 V

question: Three resistors 72 ohm, 29 ohm and 13 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 72, R2 = 29, R3 = 13 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 72 + 29 + 13 | Answer: 114 ohm

question: Two resistors 80 ohm and 94 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 80, R2 = 94 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 80*94 / (80+94) | Answer: 43.22 ohm

question: A device draws 13.2 A at 190 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 190, I = 13.2 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 190 * 13.2 | Answer: 2508 W

question: A current of 5.9 A flows through a 34 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 5.9, R = 34 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (5.9)^2 * 34 | Answer: 1184 W

question: Two capacitors 44.8 uF and 31.3 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 44.8, C2 = 31.3 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 44.8*31.3 / (44.8+31.3) | Answer: 18.43 uF

question: A resistor 97 kohm and capacitor 8.5 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 97, C = 8.5 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (97k)(8.5u) = 824.5 ms | Answer: 824.5 ms

question: An inductor 310.9 mH is in series with 144 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 310.9, R = 144 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (310.9e-3) / 144 | Answer: 2.159 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 128.3 mH inductor at 320 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 128.3, f = 320 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (320)(128.3e-3) | Answer: 258 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 13 uF capacitor at 560 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 13, f = 560 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (560)(13e-6)) | Answer: 21.86 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 51 ohm, XL = 81 ohm and XC = 64 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 51, XL = 81, XC = 64 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(51^2 + (81 - 64)^2) | Answer: 53.76 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 8.5 mH and C = 9.8 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 8.5, C = 9.8 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(8.5e-3 * 9.8e-6)) | Answer: 551.4 Hz

question: A capacitor of 52.3 uF is charged to 35 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 52.3, V = 35 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*52.3e-6*(35)^2 | Answer: 32.03 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 160 V with 970 primary turns and 490 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 160, N1 = 970, N2 = 490 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 160 * 490/970 | Answer: 80.82 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 240 V and draws an armature current of 55 A. If the armature resistance is 1.26 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 240, Ia = 55, Ra = 1.26 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 240 - 55*1.26 | Answer: 170.7 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 150 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.86. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 150, VL = 400, pf = 0.86 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*400*150*0.86 / 1000 | Answer: 89.37 kW

question: A load has real power 35 kW and apparent power 215 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 35, S = 215 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 35 / 215 | Answer: 0.1628

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 6 V across R1 = 4 ohm and R2 = 27 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 6, R1 = 4, R2 = 27 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 6*27 / (4+27) | Answer: 5.226 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 70 kohm and Rin = 38 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 70, Rin = 38 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 70 / 38 | Answer: 1.842

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 100 kohm and Rg = 33 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 100, Rg = 33 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 100/33 | Answer: 4.03

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 8987. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 8987 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(8987) | Answer: 39.54 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 7.9 m carries a central point load of 80 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7.9, W = 80 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 80*7.9 / 4 | Answer: 158 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 9 m carries a UDL of 20 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 9, w = 20 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 20*(9)^2 / 8 | Answer: 202.5 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 4.6 m carries a point load 45 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.6, W = 45 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 45*4.6 | Answer: 207 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 4.9 m carries a UDL of 20 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.9, w = 20 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 20*(4.9)^2 / 2 | Answer: 240.1 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 9 m carries a point load 55 kN at distance 2.9 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 9, a = 2.9, W = 55 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 55*(9 - 2.9) / 9 | Answer: 37.28 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 5.4 m) carries a central point load 65 kN. With E = 200 GPa and I = 60e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=65000 N, L=5400.0 mm, E=200000 MPa, I=60e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 17.77 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 7.9 m carries a UDL of 12 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7.9, w = 12 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 12*(7.9)^2 / 12 | Answer: 62.41 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 550 mm, clear cover 35 mm and main bars of diameter 12 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 550, c = 35, dia = 12 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 550 - 35 - 12/2 | Answer: 509 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 21.5 m^2 carrying a factored load of 17.2 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 21.5, w = 17.2 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 17.2 * 21.5 | Answer: 369.8 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 6.4 m, unit weight 18 kN/m^3, phi = 35 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 4.4e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.4, area = 4.1e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 4.4, i = 0.4, A = 4.1 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (4.4e-4)*0.4*(4.1e-3) | Answer: 721.6 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 0.5 m, bed slope 0.009 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.027. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 4.4 m under a head of 0.4 m. Taking Cd = 0.63 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 4.9 m wide carries a discharge of 8.9 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 250 m and design speed 75 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 250, V = 75 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (75)^2 / (127*250) | Answer: 0.1772
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: A tank of volume 540 m^3 treats a flow of 90 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 540, Q = 90 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 540 / 90 | Answer: 6 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 400 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.12 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 4 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 400, k = 0.12, t = 4 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 400*(1 - e^(-0.12*4)) | Answer: 152.5 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.89, rainfall intensity 60 mm/h over a catchment of 31.4 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.89, i = 60, A = 31.4 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.89*60*31.4 / 360 | Answer: 4.658 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.07 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 260 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.07, M = 260 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 260*(20+0.07)/20 | Answer: 260.9 m

question: Convert the decimal number 1463 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 1463 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 5B7 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 10111001 and 01010011.
solution: XOR: 11101010 | Count of 1s = 5 | Answer: 5
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 820 megabits is sent over a link of 27 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 820, B = 27 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 820 / 27 | Answer: 30.37 s

question: A link has bandwidth 87 Mbps and round-trip time 40 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 87, R = 40 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 87e6 * 40e-3 bits = 3480 kb | Answer: 3480 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.96, cache access time 8 ns and main-memory access time 110 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.96, tc = 8, tm = 110 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.96*8 + (1 - 0.96)*110 | Answer: 12.08 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 680860 elements?
solution: Given: n = 680860 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(680860)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.015, memory access time 130 ns and page-fault service time 9 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 9 ms = 9000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.015)*130 + 0.015*9000000.0 ns | Answer: 135.1 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 2.6 m^3 at 500 kPa and 340 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 2.6, P = 500, Tk = 340 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (500e3)*2.6 / (8.314*340) | Answer: 459.9 mol

question: For a reaction with A = 2e10 /s and activation energy 50 kJ/mol at 450 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 2, Ea = 50, Tk = 450 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 2e10 * exp(-50e3 / (8.314*450)) | Answer: 31403 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.91 and bottoms xW = 0.06, with relative volatility alpha = 3. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.91, xw = 0.06, al = 3 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.91/0.09)(0.94/0.06)] / ln(3) | Answer: 4.611 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.75 and x = 0.47. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.75, x = 0.47 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.75/0.25) / (0.47/0.53) | Answer: 3.383

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.89 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 35 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.89, Psat = 35 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.89 * 35 | Answer: 31.15 kPa

question: A stream of 7.6 kg/s with specific heat 2.3 kJ/kg-K is heated through 20 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 7.6, cp = 2.3, dT = 20 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 7.6*2.3*20 | Answer: 349.6 kW

question: A reactor of volume 6 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 1.3 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 6, Q = 1.3 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 6 / 1.3 | Answer: 4.615 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 4.6e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 1 mm with a concentration difference of 120 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 4.6, L = 1, dC = 120 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (4.6e-9)*120 / (1e-3) | Answer: 552 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 7.5 min and steady-state gain 3.2. For a step input of magnitude 7, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 7.5, K = 3.2, M = 7 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 3.2 * 7 | Answer: 22.4 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 40 m^2 flies at 190 m/s (air density 0.7 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.9. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 40, V = 190, rho = 0.7, CL = 0.9 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.7*(190)^2*40*0.9 / 1000 | Answer: 454.9 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 50 m^2 flies at 210 m/s (density 0.4 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.12. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 50, V = 210, rho = 0.4, CD = 0.12 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.4*(210)^2*50*0.12 / 1000 | Answer: 52.92 kN

question: A specimen under stress 240 MPa shows an elastic strain of 2.9e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 240, eps = 2.9 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 240 / (2.9e-3) MPa = 82.76 GPa | Answer: 82.76 GPa

question: A block of mass 12 kg has a volume of 1.7e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 12, V = 1.7 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 12 / (1.7e-3) | Answer: 7059 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 2900 mm is heated through 25 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 11e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 2900, dT = 25, al = 11 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 2900*11e-6*25 | Answer: 0.7975 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 110 ohm, R2 = 35 ohm and R3 = 225 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 110, R2 = 35, R3 = 225 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 35*225 / 110 | Answer: 71.59 ohm

question: A measurement reads 10.5 when the true value is 20. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10.5, true = 20 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10.5 - 20| / 20 * 100 | Answer: 47.5 %

question: Annual demand is 45000 units, ordering cost 50 per order and holding cost 16 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 45000, S = 50, H = 16 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*45000*50 / 16) | Answer: 530.3 units

question: An asset costs 440000 with salvage value 32000 after 11 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 440000, Sv = 32000, n = 11 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (440000 - 32000) / 11 | Answer: 37091 per year

question: A product sells for 300 per unit with variable cost 140 per unit and fixed costs 20000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 300, V = 140, F = 20000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 20000 / (300 - 140) | Answer: 125 units

question: Find the present worth of 150000 received 9 years from now at an interest rate of 5% per year.
solution: Given: F = 150000, n = 9, i = 5 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 150000 / (1 + 0.05)^9 | Answer: 96691 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.96, 0.99 and 0.9 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.96, r2 = 0.99, r3 = 0.9 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.96*0.99*0.9 | Answer: 0.8554

question: A process produces 39 defective items in a batch of 11500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 39, N = 11500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 39/11500 * 1e6 | Answer: 3391 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -3x^3 - 5x^2 + x + 2 evaluated at x = -1.
For f(x) = 4x^3 - 2x^2 + 6x + 8, find f''(x) at x = 0.
Evaluate the definite integral of (5x^2 + 6x - 7) dx from x = -3 to x = 5.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = 5x^3/3 + 6x^2/2 + -7x | Evaluate F(5) - F(-3) | Answer: 245.3
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 2x^2 + 9x - 4 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[1, -5], [-9, -8]].
solution: Given: a = 1, b = -5, c = -9, d = -8 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (1)(-8) - (-5)(-9) | Answer: -53

question: Find the determinant of [[4, 3, 1], [4, -6, 1], [6, 4, -1]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: 90

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[1, -2], [1, 7]].
solution: Trace tr = 8, Determinant = 9 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 6.646

question: Solve for x: 3x + 5y = 9 and -3x + 6y = 2.
solution: Determinant = 3*6 - 5*-3 = 33 | x = (e d - b f) / det = 1.333 | Answer: x = 1.333
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 27, 90, 79, 72, 40.
solution: Sum = 308 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 61.6 | Answer: 61.6

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 23, 17, 8, 25, 46.
solution: Mean = 23.8 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 14.06

question: Find the slope of the line through (-6, -9) and (0, -8).
Find the distance between the points (7, -6) and (-4, 7).
solution: Given: x1 = 7, y1 = -6, x2 = -4, y2 = 7 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-11)^2 + (13)^2) | Answer: 17.03 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (2,-3), (-2,4), (7,7).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 37.5 sq units

question: Find the 18th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 6 and common difference 8.
solution: Given: a = 6, d = 8, n = 18 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = 6 + (18 - 1)*8 | Answer: 142

question: Find the sum of the first 40 terms of an AP with first term -2 and common difference -4.
solution: Given: a = -2, d = -4, n = 40 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 40/2 [2*-2 + (40-1)*-4] | Answer: -3200

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 29500 at 6.8% per annum for 4 years.
solution: Given: P = 29500, R = 6.8, Tt = 4 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 29500 * 6.8 * 4 / 100 | Answer: 8024 currency units

question: Find the amount when 23000 is invested at 8.4% per annum compounded annually for 4 years.
solution: Given: P = 23000, R = 8.4, Tt = 4 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 23000 * (1 + 8.4/100)^4 | Answer: 31757 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (5, 2, -6) and (0, 8, 0).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (-4, 4, -5) and (-2, -3, -5).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 41.53

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (-5, -2, 1) and (3, -1, 3).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 114.8 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = x^3 + 2x^2 - 8x - 6 at x = -3.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-79 with initial guess x0=12, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.3 and ordinates 18, 7, 20, 18, 14, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 19 and 224.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 19 and 224 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 50 and 13.
solution: Given: a = 50, b = 13 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 50*13 / 1 | Answer: 650
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 37 mm carries an axial tensile load of 102 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 24 mm and length 1900 mm carries an axial load of 46 kN. Take E = 70 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 41 mm transmits a torque of 2550 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 41, Tt = 2550 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(2550*1000) / (pi*(41)^3) | Answer: 188.4 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 36 mm and length 1400 mm carries a torque of 1600 N-m. With G = 80 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (36)^4 / 32 = 164896 mm^4 | theta = (1600*1000)(1400) / (80000 * 164896) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 9.729 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 58 mm wide and 240 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 58, h = 240 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 58*(240)^2 / 6 | Answer: 556800 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (93 mm x 170 mm) carries a bending moment of 31 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (60 mm x 90 mm) has effective length 3000 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 730 MPa is designed for a working stress of 210 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 730, sw = 210 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 730 / 210 | Answer: 3.476

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 400 mm and wall thickness 11 mm carries an internal pressure of 1.6 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 400, t = 11, P = 1.6 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 1.6*400 / (2*11) | Answer: 29.09 MPa

question: 4.5 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 35 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.5, dT = 35 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 4.5 * 0.718 * 35 | Answer: 113.1 kJ

question: 3.2 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 75 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.2, dT = 75 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 3.2 * 1.005 * 75 | Answer: 241.2 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 0.9 m^3 at 570 K with mass 1.8 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 0.9, Tk = 570, m = 1.8 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 1.8*0.287*570 / 0.9 | Answer: 327.2 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 4.3 kg of air expands isothermally at 490 K from volume V1 to 4*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.3, Tk = 490, ratio = 4 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 4.3*0.287*490*ln(4) | Answer: 838.3 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 2.2 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.17 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 2.2, D = 0.17 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*2.2*0.17 / 0.001 | Answer: 374000

question: Water flows at 2.5 m/s through a pipe of diameter 150 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 18.9 m. Taking Cv = 0.95, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 18.9, cv = 0.95 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.95*sqrt(2*9.81*18.9) | Answer: 18.29 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 150 mm) water flows at 1.6 m/s. It contracts to diameter 80 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 150, d2 = 80, V1 = 1.6 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 1.6*(150/80)^2 | Answer: 5.625 m/s

question: Water flows at 2.9 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.17 m and length 100 m. With friction factor f = 0.032, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 37 teeth drives a gear of 75 teeth. If the pinion runs at 800 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 37, z2 = 75, N1 = 800 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 800*37 / 75 | Answer: 394.7 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 510 mm rotates at 850 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 510, N = 850 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.51)*850 / 60 | Answer: 22.7 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 29.4 kW at 750 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 29.4, N = 750 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(29.4*1000) / (2*pi*750) | Answer: 374.3 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 1.7 kg rotates at radius 0.39 m at 1150 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 3300 N/m and mass 18.8 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 3300, m = 18.8 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(3300/18.8) | Answer: 2.109 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 5.8 m^2 and thickness 0.29 m has conductivity k = 15.1 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 130 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 5.8, L = 0.29, k = 15.1, dT = 130 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 15.1*5.8*130 / 0.29 | Answer: 39260 W

question: A surface of area 1.5 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 175 W/m^2-K to surroundings 75 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 1.5, h = 175, dT = 75 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 175*1.5*75 | Answer: 19688 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 200 m/min, feed = 0.47 mm/rev, depth of cut = 1 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 200, f = 0.47, d = 1 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*200*0.47*1 | Answer: 94000 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 230 mm is turned at 700 rpm with a feed of 0.1 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 230, N = 700, f = 0.1 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 230 / (0.1*700) | Answer: 3.286 min

question: A resistor of 41 ohm carries a current of 7.3 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 41, I = 7.3 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 7.3 * 41 | Answer: 299.3 V

question: Three resistors 97 ohm, 10 ohm and 13 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 97, R2 = 10, R3 = 13 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 97 + 10 + 13 | Answer: 120 ohm

question: Two resistors 85 ohm and 21 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 85, R2 = 21 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 85*21 / (85+21) | Answer: 16.84 ohm

question: A device draws 13.8 A at 135 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 135, I = 13.8 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 135 * 13.8 | Answer: 1863 W

question: A current of 7.6 A flows through a 95 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 7.6, R = 95 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (7.6)^2 * 95 | Answer: 5487 W

question: Two capacitors 24.5 uF and 34 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 24.5, C2 = 34 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 24.5*34 / (24.5+34) | Answer: 14.24 uF

question: A resistor 92 kohm and capacitor 3.4 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 92, C = 3.4 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (92k)(3.4u) = 312.8 ms | Answer: 312.8 ms

question: An inductor 241.2 mH is in series with 169 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 241.2, R = 169 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (241.2e-3) / 169 | Answer: 1.427 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 153.7 mH inductor at 570 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 153.7, f = 570 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (570)(153.7e-3) | Answer: 550.5 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 30 uF capacitor at 250 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 30, f = 250 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (250)(30e-6)) | Answer: 21.22 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 13 ohm, XL = 31 ohm and XC = 74 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 13, XL = 31, XC = 74 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(13^2 + (31 - 74)^2) | Answer: 44.92 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 35.2 mH and C = 5.7 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 35.2, C = 5.7 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(35.2e-3 * 5.7e-6)) | Answer: 355.3 Hz

question: A capacitor of 55.3 uF is charged to 360 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 55.3, V = 360 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*55.3e-6*(360)^2 | Answer: 3583 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 410 V with 950 primary turns and 480 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 410, N1 = 950, N2 = 480 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 410 * 480/950 | Answer: 207.2 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 200 V and draws an armature current of 45 A. If the armature resistance is 0.52 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 200, Ia = 45, Ra = 0.52 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 200 - 45*0.52 | Answer: 176.6 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 50 A at 433 V (line) with a power factor of 0.75. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 50, VL = 433, pf = 0.75 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*433*50*0.75 / 1000 | Answer: 28.12 kW

question: A load has real power 25 kW and apparent power 170 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 25, S = 170 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 25 / 170 | Answer: 0.1471

question: A machine delivers 55 kW output while drawing 82 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 55, Pi = 82 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 55/82 * 100 | Answer: 67.07 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 29 V across R1 = 32 ohm and R2 = 11 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 29, R1 = 32, R2 = 11 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 29*11 / (32+11) | Answer: 7.419 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 190 kohm and Rin = 34 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 190, Rin = 34 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 190 / 34 | Answer: 5.588

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 120 kohm and Rg = 46 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 120, Rg = 46 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 120/46 | Answer: 3.609

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 3932. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 3932 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(3932) | Answer: 35.95 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 5.5 m carries a central point load of 75 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.5, W = 75 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 75*5.5 / 4 | Answer: 103.1 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 3.2 m carries a UDL of 55 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.2, w = 55 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 55*(3.2)^2 / 8 | Answer: 70.4 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 3.4 m carries a point load 75 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.4, W = 75 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 75*3.4 | Answer: 255 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 4.1 m carries a UDL of 6 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.1, w = 6 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 6*(4.1)^2 / 2 | Answer: 50.43 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 7.5 m carries a point load 40 kN at distance 1.1 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 7.5, a = 1.1, W = 40 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 40*(7.5 - 1.1) / 7.5 | Answer: 34.13 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 7.3 m) carries a central point load 40 kN. With E = 30 GPa and I = 590e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=40000 N, L=7300.0 mm, E=30000 MPa, I=590e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 18.32 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 6.3 m carries a UDL of 42 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6.3, w = 42 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 42*(6.3)^2 / 12 | Answer: 138.9 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 660 mm, clear cover 40 mm and main bars of diameter 16 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 660, c = 40, dia = 16 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 660 - 40 - 16/2 | Answer: 612 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 30.9 m^2 carrying a factored load of 12.6 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 30.9, w = 12.6 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 12.6 * 30.9 | Answer: 389.3 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 6.4 m, unit weight 16 kN/m^3, phi = 36 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 8.7e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.4, area = 3.5e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 8.7, i = 0.4, A = 3.5 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (8.7e-4)*0.4*(3.5e-3) | Answer: 1218 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.1 m, bed slope 0.004 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.026. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 3.8 m under a head of 1.1 m. Taking Cd = 0.6 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 5.4 m wide carries a discharge of 18.6 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 490 m and design speed 65 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 490, V = 65 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (65)^2 / (127*490) | Answer: 0.06789
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: A tank of volume 80 m^3 treats a flow of 15 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 80, Q = 15 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 80 / 15 | Answer: 5.333 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 380 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.25 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 7 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 380, k = 0.25, t = 7 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 380*(1 - e^(-0.25*7)) | Answer: 314 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.81, rainfall intensity 75 mm/h over a catchment of 37 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.81, i = 75, A = 37 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.81*75*37 / 360 | Answer: 6.244 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.01 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 190 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.01, M = 190 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 190*(20+0.01)/20 | Answer: 190.1 m

question: Convert the decimal number 359 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 359 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 167 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 00001000 and 11001101.
solution: XOR: 11000101 | Count of 1s = 4 | Answer: 4
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 250 megabits is sent over a link of 87 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 250, B = 87 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 250 / 87 | Answer: 2.874 s

question: A link has bandwidth 70 Mbps and round-trip time 50 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 70, R = 50 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 70e6 * 50e-3 bits = 3500 kb | Answer: 3500 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.89, cache access time 5 ns and main-memory access time 160 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.89, tc = 5, tm = 160 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.89*5 + (1 - 0.89)*160 | Answer: 22.05 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 158459 elements?
solution: Given: n = 158459 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(158459)) + 1 | Answer: 18

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.005, memory access time 130 ns and page-fault service time 9 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 9 ms = 9000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.005)*130 + 0.005*9000000.0 ns | Answer: 45.13 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 1.6 m^3 at 470 kPa and 410 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 1.6, P = 470, Tk = 410 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (470e3)*1.6 / (8.314*410) | Answer: 220.6 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.22 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 9 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.22, t = 9 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.22*9) | Answer: 0.8619

question: For a reaction with A = 1e10 /s and activation energy 80 kJ/mol at 460 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 1, Ea = 80, Tk = 460 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 1e10 * exp(-80e3 / (8.314*460)) | Answer: 8.23 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.94 and bottoms xW = 0.1, with relative volatility alpha = 1.9. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.94, xw = 0.1, al = 1.9 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.94/0.06)(0.9/0.1)] / ln(1.9) | Answer: 7.71 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.81 and x = 0.29. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.81, x = 0.29 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.81/0.19) / (0.29/0.71) | Answer: 10.44

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.9 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 50 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.9, Psat = 50 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.9 * 50 | Answer: 45 kPa

question: A stream of 3.5 kg/s with specific heat 3.5 kJ/kg-K is heated through 80 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 3.5, cp = 3.5, dT = 80 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 3.5*3.5*80 | Answer: 980 kW

question: A reactor of volume 16.7 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 3.8 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 16.7, Q = 3.8 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 16.7 / 3.8 | Answer: 4.395 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 2e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 4 mm with a concentration difference of 160 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 2, L = 4, dC = 160 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (2e-9)*160 / (4e-3) | Answer: 80 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 6.2 min and steady-state gain 3.1. For a step input of magnitude 3, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 6.2, K = 3.1, M = 3 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 3.1 * 3 | Answer: 9.3 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 15 m^2 flies at 80 m/s (air density 1 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 1.2. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 15, V = 80, rho = 1, CL = 1.2 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1*(80)^2*15*1.2 / 1000 | Answer: 57.6 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 40 m^2 flies at 180 m/s (density 1.225 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.04. Find the drag force in kN.
A specimen under stress 390 MPa shows an elastic strain of 2.3e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 390, eps = 2.3 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 390 / (2.3e-3) MPa = 169.6 GPa | Answer: 169.6 GPa

question: A block of mass 38 kg has a volume of 5.7e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 38, V = 5.7 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 38 / (5.7e-3) | Answer: 6667 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 2300 mm is heated through 80 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 11e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 2300, dT = 80, al = 11 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 2300*11e-6*80 | Answer: 2.024 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 135 ohm, R2 = 170 ohm and R3 = 430 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 135, R2 = 170, R3 = 430 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 170*430 / 135 | Answer: 541.5 ohm

question: A measurement reads 10.36 when the true value is 20. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10.36, true = 20 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10.36 - 20| / 20 * 100 | Answer: 48.2 %

question: Annual demand is 50000 units, ordering cost 290 per order and holding cost 21 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 50000, S = 290, H = 21 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*50000*290 / 21) | Answer: 1175 units

question: An asset costs 100000 with salvage value 20000 after 8 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 100000, Sv = 20000, n = 8 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (100000 - 20000) / 8 | Answer: 10000 per year

question: A product sells for 300 per unit with variable cost 40 per unit and fixed costs 160000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 300, V = 40, F = 160000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 160000 / (300 - 40) | Answer: 615.4 units

question: Find the present worth of 195000 received 6 years from now at an interest rate of 9% per year.
solution: Given: F = 195000, n = 6, i = 9 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 195000 / (1 + 0.09)^6 | Answer: 116272 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.96, 0.93 and 0.9 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.96, r2 = 0.93, r3 = 0.9 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.96*0.93*0.9 | Answer: 0.8035

question: A process produces 1 defective items in a batch of 7000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 1, N = 7000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 1/7000 * 1e6 | Answer: 142.9 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -4x^3 + 4x^2 + x - 4 evaluated at x = 2.
For f(x) = -x^3 - 8x^2 + 2x + 8, find f''(x) at x = -3.
Evaluate the definite integral of (4x^2 + 1) dx from x = -4 to x = 7.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = 4x^3/3 + 0x^2/2 + 1x | Evaluate F(7) - F(-4) | Answer: 553.7
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of x^2 - 2x - 7 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[7, 2], [-4, -7]].
solution: Given: a = 7, b = 2, c = -4, d = -7 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (7)(-7) - (2)(-4) | Answer: -41

question: Find the determinant of [[0, 6, 2], [1, -4, -1], [-4, 3, 1]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: -8

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[-6, -4], [-5, 4]].
solution: Trace tr = -2, Determinant = -44 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 5.708

question: Solve for x: 6x + 4y = -8 and -4x + -4y = 9.
solution: Determinant = 6*-4 - 4*-4 = -8 | x = (e d - b f) / det = 0.5 | Answer: x = 0.5
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 41, 97, 80, 4, 8.
solution: Sum = 230 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 46 | Answer: 46

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 43, 25, 50, 39, 40.
solution: Mean = 39.4 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 9.127

question: Find the slope of the line through (-5, 6) and (7, 5).
solution: Given: x1 = -5, y1 = 6, x2 = 7, y2 = 5 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (5 - 6) / (7 - -5) | Answer: -0.08333

question: Find the distance between the points (4, -6) and (-5, 0).
solution: Given: x1 = 4, y1 = -6, x2 = -5, y2 = 0 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-9)^2 + (6)^2) | Answer: 10.82 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (-2,-8), (-5,-3), (-1,-3).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 10 sq units

question: Find the 27th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -3 and common difference -3.
solution: Given: a = -3, d = -3, n = 27 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -3 + (27 - 1)*-3 | Answer: -81

question: Find the sum of the first 8 terms of an AP with first term -15 and common difference -4.
solution: Given: a = -15, d = -4, n = 8 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 8/2 [2*-15 + (8-1)*-4] | Answer: -232

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 27500 at 5.8% per annum for 4 years.
solution: Given: P = 27500, R = 5.8, Tt = 4 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 27500 * 5.8 * 4 / 100 | Answer: 6380 currency units

question: Find the amount when 4500 is invested at 8% per annum compounded annually for 5 years.
solution: Given: P = 4500, R = 8, Tt = 5 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 4500 * (1 + 8/100)^5 | Answer: 6612 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (0, 2, 0) and (-3, -6, -6).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (5, -5, 2) and (-3, 3, 0).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 8.485

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (-1, 2, 4) and (4, 3, -1).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 94.91 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -5x^3 + x^2 + 6x - 5 at x = 3.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-118 with initial guess x0=11, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.4 and ordinates 3, 16, 13, 19, 7, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 456 and 36.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 456 and 36 | Answer: GCD = 12

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 12 and 71.
solution: Given: a = 12, b = 71 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 12*71 / 1 | Answer: 852
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 29 mm carries an axial tensile load of 31 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 27 mm and length 900 mm carries an axial load of 36 kN. Take E = 110 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 35 mm transmits a torque of 800 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 35, Tt = 800 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(800*1000) / (pi*(35)^3) | Answer: 95.03 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 61 mm and length 1300 mm carries a torque of 850 N-m. With G = 77 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (61)^4 / 32 = 1359312 mm^4 | theta = (850*1000)(1300) / (77000 * 1359312) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 0.6049 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 48 mm wide and 170 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 48, h = 170 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 48*(170)^2 / 6 | Answer: 231200 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (100 mm x 110 mm) carries a bending moment of 15 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (63 mm x 130 mm) has effective length 2000 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 550 MPa is designed for a working stress of 100 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 550, sw = 100 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 550 / 100 | Answer: 5.5

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1350 mm and wall thickness 19 mm carries an internal pressure of 2.5 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1350, t = 19, P = 2.5 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 2.5*1350 / (2*19) | Answer: 88.82 MPa

question: 5.7 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 60 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 5.7, dT = 60 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 5.7 * 0.718 * 60 | Answer: 245.6 kJ

question: 7.9 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 200 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 7.9, dT = 200 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 7.9 * 1.005 * 200 | Answer: 1588 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 3 m^3 at 510 K with mass 3.9 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
