solution: Given: V = 3, Tk = 510, m = 3.9 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 3.9*0.287*510 / 3 | Answer: 190.3 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 1.2 kg of air expands isothermally at 320 K from volume V1 to 4*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1.2, Tk = 320, ratio = 4 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 1.2*0.287*320*ln(4) | Answer: 152.8 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 3.4 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.2 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 3.4, D = 0.2 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*3.4*0.2 / 0.001 | Answer: 680000

question: Water flows at 2.7 m/s through a pipe of diameter 50 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 12.3 m. Taking Cv = 0.96, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 12.3, cv = 0.96 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.96*sqrt(2*9.81*12.3) | Answer: 14.91 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 170 mm) water flows at 2.3 m/s. It contracts to diameter 100 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
Water flows at 2.3 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.2 m and length 60 m. With friction factor f = 0.033, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 26 teeth drives a gear of 56 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1100 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 26, z2 = 56, N1 = 1100 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1100*26 / 56 | Answer: 510.7 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 400 mm rotates at 300 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 400, N = 300 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.4)*300 / 60 | Answer: 6.283 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 19.8 kW at 1100 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 19.8, N = 1100 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(19.8*1000) / (2*pi*1100) | Answer: 171.9 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 9 kg rotates at radius 0.5 m at 600 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 12100 N/m and mass 18.1 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 12100, m = 18.1 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(12100/18.1) | Answer: 4.115 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 4.4 m^2 and thickness 0.23 m has conductivity k = 41.2 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 55 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 4.4, L = 0.23, k = 41.2, dT = 55 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 41.2*4.4*55 / 0.23 | Answer: 4335 W

question: A surface of area 0.6 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 105 W/m^2-K to surroundings 20 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 0.6, h = 105, dT = 20 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 105*0.6*20 | Answer: 1260 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 110 m/min, feed = 0.46 mm/rev, depth of cut = 0.9 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 110, f = 0.46, d = 0.9 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*110*0.46*0.9 | Answer: 45540 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 140 mm is turned at 600 rpm with a feed of 0.19 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 140, N = 600, f = 0.19 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 140 / (0.19*600) | Answer: 1.228 min

question: A resistor of 157 ohm carries a current of 0.5 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 157, I = 0.5 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 0.5 * 157 | Answer: 78.5 V

question: Three resistors 60 ohm, 24 ohm and 94 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 60, R2 = 24, R3 = 94 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 60 + 24 + 94 | Answer: 178 ohm

question: Two resistors 64 ohm and 108 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 64, R2 = 108 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 64*108 / (64+108) | Answer: 40.19 ohm

question: A device draws 14.4 A at 215 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 215, I = 14.4 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 215 * 14.4 | Answer: 3096 W

question: A current of 5.2 A flows through a 36 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 5.2, R = 36 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (5.2)^2 * 36 | Answer: 973.4 W

question: Two capacitors 26 uF and 37.4 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 26, C2 = 37.4 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 26*37.4 / (26+37.4) | Answer: 15.34 uF

question: A resistor 45 kohm and capacitor 1 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 45, C = 1 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (45k)(1u) = 45 ms | Answer: 45 ms

question: An inductor 463.4 mH is in series with 32 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 463.4, R = 32 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (463.4e-3) / 32 | Answer: 14.48 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 180.4 mH inductor at 750 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 180.4, f = 750 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (750)(180.4e-3) | Answer: 850.1 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 21.5 uF capacitor at 850 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 21.5, f = 850 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (850)(21.5e-6)) | Answer: 8.709 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 92 ohm, XL = 35 ohm and XC = 84 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 92, XL = 35, XC = 84 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(92^2 + (35 - 84)^2) | Answer: 104.2 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 61.8 mH and C = 5.8 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 61.8, C = 5.8 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(61.8e-3 * 5.8e-6)) | Answer: 265.8 Hz

question: A capacitor of 39.8 uF is charged to 375 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 39.8, V = 375 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*39.8e-6*(375)^2 | Answer: 2798 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 130 V with 570 primary turns and 500 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 130, N1 = 570, N2 = 500 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 130 * 500/570 | Answer: 114 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 340 V and draws an armature current of 27 A. If the armature resistance is 0.44 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 340, Ia = 27, Ra = 0.44 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 340 - 27*0.44 | Answer: 328.1 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 65 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.96. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 65, VL = 400, pf = 0.96 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*400*65*0.96 / 1000 | Answer: 43.23 kW

question: A load has real power 45 kW and apparent power 65 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 45, S = 65 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 45 / 65 | Answer: 0.6923

question: A machine delivers 85 kW output while drawing 142 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 85, Pi = 142 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 85/142 * 100 | Answer: 59.86 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 24 V across R1 = 38 ohm and R2 = 48 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 24, R1 = 38, R2 = 48 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 24*48 / (38+48) | Answer: 13.4 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 180 kohm and Rin = 9 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 180, Rin = 9 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 180 / 9 | Answer: 20

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 90 kohm and Rg = 21 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 90, Rg = 21 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 90/21 | Answer: 5.286

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 9537. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 9537 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(9537) | Answer: 39.79 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.3 m carries a central point load of 110 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6.3, W = 110 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 110*6.3 / 4 | Answer: 173.2 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 8.8 m carries a UDL of 20 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 8.8, w = 20 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 20*(8.8)^2 / 8 | Answer: 193.6 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 1.4 m carries a point load 20 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 1.4, W = 20 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 20*1.4 | Answer: 28 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 4 m carries a UDL of 10 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4, w = 10 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 10*(4)^2 / 2 | Answer: 80 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.2 m carries a point load 70 kN at distance 2 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 6.2, a = 2, W = 70 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 70*(6.2 - 2) / 6.2 | Answer: 47.42 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 3.2 m) carries a central point load 20 kN. With E = 200 GPa and I = 140e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=20000 N, L=3200.0 mm, E=200000 MPa, I=140e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 0.4876 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 6 m carries a UDL of 15 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6, w = 15 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 15*(6)^2 / 12 | Answer: 45 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 610 mm, clear cover 30 mm and main bars of diameter 12 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 610, c = 30, dia = 12 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 610 - 30 - 12/2 | Answer: 574 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 37.9 m^2 carrying a factored load of 17.5 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 37.9, w = 17.5 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 17.5 * 37.9 | Answer: 663.2 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 4.7 m, unit weight 16 kN/m^3, phi = 36 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 2.8e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1.3, area = 2e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 2.8, i = 1.3, A = 2 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (2.8e-4)*1.3*(2e-3) | Answer: 728 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 2.3 m, bed slope 0.004 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.029. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 1.5 m under a head of 0.7 m. Taking Cd = 0.61 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 3.1 m wide carries a discharge of 10.9 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 580 m and design speed 70 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 580, V = 70 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (70)^2 / (127*580) | Answer: 0.06652
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: A tank of volume 850 m^3 treats a flow of 185 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 850, Q = 185 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 850 / 185 | Answer: 4.595 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 340 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.18 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 4 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 340, k = 0.18, t = 4 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 340*(1 - e^(-0.18*4)) | Answer: 174.5 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.84, rainfall intensity 70 mm/h over a catchment of 31.3 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.84, i = 70, A = 31.3 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.84*70*31.3 / 360 | Answer: 5.112 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.01 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 640 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.01, M = 640 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 640*(30+0.01)/30 | Answer: 640.2 m

question: Convert the decimal number 3893 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 3893 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: F35 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 01111001 and 11000010.
solution: XOR: 10111011 | Count of 1s = 6 | Answer: 6
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 300 megabits is sent over a link of 40 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 300, B = 40 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 300 / 40 | Answer: 7.5 s

question: A link has bandwidth 64 Mbps and round-trip time 70 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 64, R = 70 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 64e6 * 70e-3 bits = 4480 kb | Answer: 4480 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.96, cache access time 5 ns and main-memory access time 180 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.96, tc = 5, tm = 180 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.96*5 + (1 - 0.96)*180 | Answer: 12 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 246610 elements?
solution: Given: n = 246610 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(246610)) + 1 | Answer: 18

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.015, memory access time 150 ns and page-fault service time 5 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 5 ms = 5000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.015)*150 + 0.015*5000000.0 ns | Answer: 75.15 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 1.6 m^3 at 300 kPa and 330 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 1.6, P = 300, Tk = 330 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (300e3)*1.6 / (8.314*330) | Answer: 175 mol

question: For a reaction with A = 9e10 /s and activation energy 70 kJ/mol at 460 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 9, Ea = 70, Tk = 460 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 9e10 * exp(-70e3 / (8.314*460)) | Answer: 1012 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.95 and bottoms xW = 0.02, with relative volatility alpha = 2.4. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.95, xw = 0.02, al = 2.4 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.95/0.05)(0.98/0.02)] / ln(2.4) | Answer: 7.809 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.76 and x = 0.34. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.76, x = 0.34 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.76/0.24) / (0.34/0.66) | Answer: 6.147

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.69 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 85 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.69, Psat = 85 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.69 * 85 | Answer: 58.65 kPa

question: A stream of 5.4 kg/s with specific heat 2.1 kJ/kg-K is heated through 95 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 5.4, cp = 2.1, dT = 95 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 5.4*2.1*95 | Answer: 1077 kW

question: A reactor of volume 16.3 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 4.1 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 16.3, Q = 4.1 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 16.3 / 4.1 | Answer: 3.976 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 8.7e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 3 mm with a concentration difference of 140 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 8.7, L = 3, dC = 140 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (8.7e-9)*140 / (3e-3) | Answer: 406 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 2.1 min and steady-state gain 2.1. For a step input of magnitude 6, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 2.1, K = 2.1, M = 6 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 2.1 * 6 | Answer: 12.6 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 95 m^2 flies at 90 m/s (air density 1.225 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.4. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 95, V = 90, rho = 1.225, CL = 0.4 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1.225*(90)^2*95*0.4 / 1000 | Answer: 188.5 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 55 m^2 flies at 160 m/s (density 0.7 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.04. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 55, V = 160, rho = 0.7, CD = 0.04 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.7*(160)^2*55*0.04 / 1000 | Answer: 19.71 kN

question: A specimen under stress 390 MPa shows an elastic strain of 2.5e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 390, eps = 2.5 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 390 / (2.5e-3) MPa = 156 GPa | Answer: 156 GPa

question: A block of mass 37 kg has a volume of 6e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 37, V = 6 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 37 / (6e-3) | Answer: 6167 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 1900 mm is heated through 150 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 12e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 1900, dT = 150, al = 12 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 1900*12e-6*150 | Answer: 3.42 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 15 ohm, R2 = 125 ohm and R3 = 455 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 15, R2 = 125, R3 = 455 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 125*455 / 15 | Answer: 3792 ohm

question: A measurement reads 10.17 when the true value is 100. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10.17, true = 100 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10.17 - 100| / 100 * 100 | Answer: 89.83 %

question: Annual demand is 21500 units, ordering cost 180 per order and holding cost 11 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 21500, S = 180, H = 11 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*21500*180 / 11) | Answer: 838.8 units

question: An asset costs 150000 with salvage value 16000 after 19 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 150000, Sv = 16000, n = 19 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (150000 - 16000) / 19 | Answer: 7053 per year

question: A product sells for 400 per unit with variable cost 40 per unit and fixed costs 55000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 400, V = 40, F = 55000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 55000 / (400 - 40) | Answer: 152.8 units

question: Find the present worth of 110000 received 9 years from now at an interest rate of 9% per year.
solution: Given: F = 110000, n = 9, i = 9 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 110000 / (1 + 0.09)^9 | Answer: 50647 currency units

question: A process produces 49 defective items in a batch of 7500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 49, N = 7500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 49/7500 * 1e6 | Answer: 6533 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = x^3 + 2x^2 - 6x + 4 evaluated at x = 1.
For f(x) = -2x^3 + 7x - 4, find f''(x) at x = 4.
Evaluate the definite integral of (-4x^2 - 6x) dx from x = 1 to x = 4.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = -4x^3/3 + -6x^2/2 + 0x | Evaluate F(4) - F(1) | Answer: -129
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 2x^2 - x - 1 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[-9, -2], [-6, -2]].
solution: Given: a = -9, b = -2, c = -6, d = -2 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (-9)(-2) - (-2)(-6) | Answer: 6

question: Find the determinant of [[-2, 6, 3], [3, -4, -6], [3, 2, 6]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: -138

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[-8, 6], [0, -2]].
solution: Trace tr = -10, Determinant = 16 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: -2

question: Solve for x: -1x + 5y = 5 and 6x + -2y = 2.
solution: Determinant = -1*-2 - 5*6 = -28 | x = (e d - b f) / det = 0.7143 | Answer: x = 0.7143

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 2, 64, 19, 30, 21.
solution: Sum = 136 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 27.2 | Answer: 27.2

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 17, 49, 35, 34, 26.
solution: Mean = 32.2 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 11.86

question: Find the slope of the line through (4, 0) and (9, -4).
solution: Given: x1 = 4, y1 = 0, x2 = 9, y2 = -4 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (-4 - 0) / (9 - 4) | Answer: -0.8

question: Find the distance between the points (-2, 8) and (7, 2).
solution: Given: x1 = -2, y1 = 8, x2 = 7, y2 = 2 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((9)^2 + (-6)^2) | Answer: 10.82 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (-7,2), (1,0), (-6,1).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 3 sq units

question: Find the 11th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -5 and common difference 8.
solution: Given: a = -5, d = 8, n = 11 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -5 + (11 - 1)*8 | Answer: 75

question: Find the sum of the first 20 terms of an AP with first term 2 and common difference -3.
solution: Given: a = 2, d = -3, n = 20 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 20/2 [2*2 + (20-1)*-3] | Answer: -530

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 50000 at 11.4% per annum for 10 years.
solution: Given: P = 50000, R = 11.4, Tt = 10 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 50000 * 11.4 * 10 / 100 | Answer: 57000 currency units

question: Find the amount when 20500 is invested at 11.9% per annum compounded annually for 4 years.
solution: Given: P = 20500, R = 11.9, Tt = 4 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 20500 * (1 + 11.9/100)^4 | Answer: 32142 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (0, -3, 8) and (7, -4, -2).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (3, 2, 2) and (1, 6, 1).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 18.89

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (6, -3, -1) and (1, -5, -6).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 59.63 degrees

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number 9 + 10i.
solution: Given: a = 9, b = 10 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(10, 9) | Answer: 48.01 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -2x^3 + 5x^2 + 3x + 5 at x = 2.
solution: Given: a = -2, b = 5, c = 3, d = 5, x0 = 2 | Formula: f(x0) = a x0^3 + b x0^2 + c x0 + d | Substitute: f(2) = -2(2)^3 + 5(2)^2 + 3(2) + 5 | Answer: 15

question: Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-145 with initial guess x0=5, find x1 (one iteration).
solution: Given: N = 145, x0 = 5 | Formula: x1 = x0 - (x0^2 - N)/(2 x0) | Substitute: x1 = 5 - ((5)^2 - 145)/(2*5) | Answer: 17

question: Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=0.7 and ordinates 14, 10, 13, 13, 1, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 504 and 366.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 504 and 366 | Answer: GCD = 6

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 76 and 31.
solution: Given: a = 76, b = 31 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 76*31 / 1 | Answer: 2356
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 11 mm carries an axial tensile load of 85 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 26 mm and length 700 mm carries an axial load of 39 kN. Take E = 110 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 22 mm transmits a torque of 3000 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 22, Tt = 3000 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(3000*1000) / (pi*(22)^3) | Answer: 1435 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 46 mm and length 1100 mm carries a torque of 1700 N-m. With G = 80 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (46)^4 / 32 = 439573 mm^4 | theta = (1700*1000)(1100) / (80000 * 439573) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 3.047 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 48 mm wide and 140 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 48, h = 140 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 48*(140)^2 / 6 | Answer: 156800 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (115 mm x 140 mm) carries a bending moment of 16 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (54 mm x 130 mm) has effective length 1900 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 860 MPa is designed for a working stress of 80 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 860, sw = 80 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 860 / 80 | Answer: 10.75

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1350 mm and wall thickness 17 mm carries an internal pressure of 1.3 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1350, t = 17, P = 1.3 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 1.3*1350 / (2*17) | Answer: 51.62 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 820 K and 350 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 820, Tc = 350 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 350/820) * 100 | Answer: 57.32 %

question: 2.8 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 100 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.8, dT = 100 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 2.8 * 0.718 * 100 | Answer: 201 kJ

question: 4.1 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 120 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.1, dT = 120 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 4.1 * 1.005 * 120 | Answer: 494.5 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 3 m^3 at 550 K with mass 1.5 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 3, Tk = 550, m = 1.5 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 1.5*0.287*550 / 3 | Answer: 78.92 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 3.5 kg of air expands isothermally at 460 K from volume V1 to 2*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.5, Tk = 460, ratio = 2 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 3.5*0.287*460*ln(2) | Answer: 320.3 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 1.3 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.16 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 1.3, D = 0.16 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*1.3*0.16 / 0.001 | Answer: 208000

question: In a pipe (diameter 310 mm) water flows at 1 m/s. It contracts to diameter 60 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 310, d2 = 60, V1 = 1 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 1*(310/60)^2 | Answer: 26.69 m/s

question: Water flows at 3.8 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.18 m and length 330 m. With friction factor f = 0.029, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 31 teeth drives a gear of 61 teeth. If the pinion runs at 600 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 31, z2 = 61, N1 = 600 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 600*31 / 61 | Answer: 304.9 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 530 mm rotates at 1000 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 530, N = 1000 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.53)*1000 / 60 | Answer: 27.75 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 6.7 kW at 300 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 6.7, N = 300 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(6.7*1000) / (2*pi*300) | Answer: 213.3 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 1 kg rotates at radius 0.16 m at 1200 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 5700 N/m and mass 19.7 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 5700, m = 19.7 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(5700/19.7) | Answer: 2.707 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 2.8 m^2 and thickness 0.32 m has conductivity k = 24.7 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 65 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 2.8, L = 0.32, k = 24.7, dT = 65 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 24.7*2.8*65 / 0.32 | Answer: 14048 W

question: A surface of area 6 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 80 W/m^2-K to surroundings 75 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 6, h = 80, dT = 75 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 80*6*75 | Answer: 36000 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 240 m/min, feed = 0.11 mm/rev, depth of cut = 1.2 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 240, f = 0.11, d = 1.2 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*240*0.11*1.2 | Answer: 31680 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 220 mm is turned at 550 rpm with a feed of 0.39 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 220, N = 550, f = 0.39 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 220 / (0.39*550) | Answer: 1.026 min

question: A resistor of 98 ohm carries a current of 5 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 98, I = 5 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 5 * 98 | Answer: 490 V

question: Three resistors 15 ohm, 59 ohm and 2 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 15, R2 = 59, R3 = 2 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 15 + 59 + 2 | Answer: 76 ohm

question: Two resistors 40 ohm and 58 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 40, R2 = 58 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 40*58 / (40+58) | Answer: 23.67 ohm

question: A device draws 2.8 A at 35 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 35, I = 2.8 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 35 * 2.8 | Answer: 98 W

question: A current of 6.5 A flows through a 114 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 6.5, R = 114 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (6.5)^2 * 114 | Answer: 4816 W

question: Two capacitors 26.4 uF and 35.7 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 26.4, C2 = 35.7 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 26.4*35.7 / (26.4+35.7) | Answer: 15.18 uF

question: A resistor 18 kohm and capacitor 15.3 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 18, C = 15.3 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (18k)(15.3u) = 275.4 ms | Answer: 275.4 ms

question: An inductor 345.2 mH is in series with 180 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 345.2, R = 180 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (345.2e-3) / 180 | Answer: 1.918 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 180.3 mH inductor at 750 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 180.3, f = 750 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (750)(180.3e-3) | Answer: 849.6 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 11.8 uF capacitor at 640 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 11.8, f = 640 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (640)(11.8e-6)) | Answer: 21.07 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 25 ohm, XL = 102 ohm and XC = 137 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 25, XL = 102, XC = 137 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(25^2 + (102 - 137)^2) | Answer: 43.01 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 16.5 mH and C = 2.9 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 16.5, C = 2.9 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(16.5e-3 * 2.9e-6)) | Answer: 727.6 Hz

question: A capacitor of 7.6 uF is charged to 215 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 7.6, V = 215 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*7.6e-6*(215)^2 | Answer: 175.7 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 130 V with 620 primary turns and 500 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 130, N1 = 620, N2 = 500 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 130 * 500/620 | Answer: 104.8 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 170 V and draws an armature current of 26 A. If the armature resistance is 1.4 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 170, Ia = 26, Ra = 1.4 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 170 - 26*1.4 | Answer: 133.6 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 190 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.73. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 190, VL = 400, pf = 0.73 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*400*190*0.73 / 1000 | Answer: 96.09 kW

question: A load has real power 30 kW and apparent power 70 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 30, S = 70 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 30 / 70 | Answer: 0.4286

question: A machine delivers 125 kW output while drawing 202 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 125, Pi = 202 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 125/202 * 100 | Answer: 61.88 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 29 V across R1 = 43 ohm and R2 = 27 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 29, R1 = 43, R2 = 27 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 29*27 / (43+27) | Answer: 11.19 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 200 kohm and Rin = 35 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 200, Rin = 35 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 200 / 35 | Answer: 5.714

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 657. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 657 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(657) | Answer: 28.18 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.9 m carries a central point load of 110 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.9, W = 110 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 110*4.9 / 4 | Answer: 134.8 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.7 m carries a UDL of 30 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6.7, w = 30 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 30*(6.7)^2 / 8 | Answer: 168.3 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 7.1 m carries a point load 95 kN at distance 2.7 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 7.1, a = 2.7, W = 95 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 95*(7.1 - 2.7) / 7.1 | Answer: 58.87 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 7.5 m) carries a central point load 80 kN. With E = 25 GPa and I = 170e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=80000 N, L=7500.0 mm, E=25000 MPa, I=170e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 165.4 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 6.1 m carries a UDL of 42 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6.1, w = 42 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 42*(6.1)^2 / 12 | Answer: 130.2 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 700 mm, clear cover 25 mm and main bars of diameter 25 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 700, c = 25, dia = 25 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 700 - 25 - 25/2 | Answer: 662.5 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 30.5 m^2 carrying a factored load of 9.7 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 30.5, w = 9.7 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 9.7 * 30.5 | Answer: 295.8 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 6.5 m, unit weight 17 kN/m^3, phi = 29 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 1.1e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.5, area = 3.4e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 1.1, i = 0.5, A = 3.4 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (1.1e-4)*0.5*(3.4e-3) | Answer: 187 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.5 m, bed slope 0.005 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.024. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 2.8 m under a head of 0.4 m. Taking Cd = 0.63 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 4.3 m wide carries a discharge of 6.7 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A tank of volume 890 m^3 treats a flow of 30 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 890, Q = 30 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 890 / 30 | Answer: 29.67 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 300 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.16 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 7 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 300, k = 0.16, t = 7 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 300*(1 - e^(-0.16*7)) | Answer: 202.1 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.8, rainfall intensity 95 mm/h over a catchment of 47.6 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.8, i = 95, A = 47.6 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.8*95*47.6 / 360 | Answer: 10.05 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.06 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 470 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.06, M = 470 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 470*(30+0.06)/30 | Answer: 470.9 m

question: Convert the decimal number 2309 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 2309 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 905 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 10110000 and 01101011.
solution: XOR: 11011011 | Count of 1s = 6 | Answer: 6
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 500 megabits is sent over a link of 71 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 500, B = 71 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 500 / 71 | Answer: 7.042 s

question: A link has bandwidth 76 Mbps and round-trip time 60 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 76, R = 60 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 76e6 * 60e-3 bits = 4560 kb | Answer: 4560 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.92, cache access time 3 ns and main-memory access time 190 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.92, tc = 3, tm = 190 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.92*3 + (1 - 0.92)*190 | Answer: 17.96 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 531638 elements?
solution: Given: n = 531638 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(531638)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.012, memory access time 90 ns and page-fault service time 7 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 7 ms = 7000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.012)*90 + 0.012*7000000.0 ns | Answer: 84.09 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 1.6 m^3 at 390 kPa and 440 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 1.6, P = 390, Tk = 440 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (390e3)*1.6 / (8.314*440) | Answer: 170.6 mol

question: For a reaction with A = 1e10 /s and activation energy 70 kJ/mol at 410 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 1, Ea = 70, Tk = 410 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 1e10 * exp(-70e3 / (8.314*410)) | Answer: 12.07 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.9 and bottoms xW = 0.06, with relative volatility alpha = 3.1. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.9, xw = 0.06, al = 3.1 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.9/0.1)(0.94/0.06)] / ln(3.1) | Answer: 4.374 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.8 and x = 0.45. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.8, x = 0.45 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.8/0.2) / (0.45/0.55) | Answer: 4.889

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.37 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 30 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.37, Psat = 30 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.37 * 30 | Answer: 11.1 kPa

question: A stream of 9.1 kg/s with specific heat 3.7 kJ/kg-K is heated through 80 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 9.1, cp = 3.7, dT = 80 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 9.1*3.7*80 | Answer: 2694 kW

question: A reactor of volume 14.2 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 2.8 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 14.2, Q = 2.8 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 14.2 / 2.8 | Answer: 5.071 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 1.3e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 1 mm with a concentration difference of 20 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 1.3, L = 1, dC = 20 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (1.3e-9)*20 / (1e-3) | Answer: 26 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 7.3 min and steady-state gain 1.7. For a step input of magnitude 6, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 7.3, K = 1.7, M = 6 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 1.7 * 6 | Answer: 10.2 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 110 m^2 flies at 60 m/s (air density 1.225 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.6. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 110, V = 60, rho = 1.225, CL = 0.6 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1.225*(60)^2*110*0.6 / 1000 | Answer: 145.5 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 90 m^2 flies at 190 m/s (density 0.7 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.12. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 90, V = 190, rho = 0.7, CD = 0.12 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.7*(190)^2*90*0.12 / 1000 | Answer: 136.5 kN

question: A block of mass 4 kg has a volume of 4.8e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 4, V = 4.8 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 4 / (4.8e-3) | Answer: 833.3 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 900 mm is heated through 130 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 23e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 900, dT = 130, al = 23 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 900*23e-6*130 | Answer: 2.691 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 165 ohm, R2 = 100 ohm and R3 = 400 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 165, R2 = 100, R3 = 400 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 100*400 / 165 | Answer: 242.4 ohm

question: Annual demand is 10500 units, ordering cost 190 per order and holding cost 22 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 10500, S = 190, H = 22 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*10500*190 / 22) | Answer: 425.9 units

question: An asset costs 260000 with salvage value 36000 after 20 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 260000, Sv = 36000, n = 20 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (260000 - 36000) / 20 | Answer: 11200 per year

question: A product sells for 270 per unit with variable cost 140 per unit and fixed costs 65000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 270, V = 140, F = 65000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 65000 / (270 - 140) | Answer: 500 units

question: Find the present worth of 90000 received 6 years from now at an interest rate of 7% per year.
solution: Given: F = 90000, n = 6, i = 7 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 90000 / (1 + 0.07)^6 | Answer: 59971 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.91, 0.97 and 0.98 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.91, r2 = 0.97, r3 = 0.98 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.91*0.97*0.98 | Answer: 0.865

question: A process produces 25 defective items in a batch of 11500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 25, N = 11500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 25/11500 * 1e6 | Answer: 2174 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -2x^3 - 4x^2 + 5 evaluated at x = -2.
For f(x) = -2x^3 - 4x^2 + x, find f''(x) at x = 2.
Evaluate the definite integral of (x^2 + 4x + 3) dx from x = -2 to x = 7.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = 1x^3/3 + 4x^2/2 + 3x | Evaluate F(7) - F(-2) | Answer: 234
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of x^2 + 4x - 9 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[-9, -5], [-1, -4]].
solution: Given: a = -9, b = -5, c = -1, d = -4 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (-9)(-4) - (-5)(-1) | Answer: 31

question: Find the determinant of [[3, -2, 6], [-5, 3, 6], [-6, 1, -2]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: 134

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[-3, 5], [7, 7]].
solution: Trace tr = 4, Determinant = -56 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 9.746

question: Solve for x: -5x + 6y = 6 and -4x + -4y = -1.
solution: Determinant = -5*-4 - 6*-4 = 44 | x = (e d - b f) / det = -0.4091 | Answer: x = -0.4091
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 68, 89, 6, 42, 14.
solution: Sum = 219 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 43.8 | Answer: 43.8

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 8, 31, 49, 37, 6.
solution: Mean = 26.2 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 18.7

question: Find the slope of the line through (4, -5) and (1, 4).
solution: Given: x1 = 4, y1 = -5, x2 = 1, y2 = 4 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (4 - -5) / (1 - 4) | Answer: -3

question: Find the distance between the points (5, 5) and (-6, -5).
solution: Given: x1 = 5, y1 = 5, x2 = -6, y2 = -5 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-11)^2 + (-10)^2) | Answer: 14.87 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (-4,5), (6,4), (4,6).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 9 sq units

question: Find the 21th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 7 and common difference -4.
solution: Given: a = 7, d = -4, n = 21 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = 7 + (21 - 1)*-4 | Answer: -73

question: Find the sum of the first 33 terms of an AP with first term -1 and common difference -3.
solution: Given: a = -1, d = -3, n = 33 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 33/2 [2*-1 + (33-1)*-3] | Answer: -1617

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 23000 at 9.5% per annum for 10 years.
solution: Given: P = 23000, R = 9.5, Tt = 10 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 23000 * 9.5 * 10 / 100 | Answer: 21850 currency units

question: Find the amount when 9500 is invested at 11.9% per annum compounded annually for 3 years.
solution: Given: P = 9500, R = 11.9, Tt = 3 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 9500 * (1 + 11.9/100)^3 | Answer: 13311 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (-2, -5, 4) and (2, 3, -7).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (1, -6, -1) and (2, 1, 4).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 27.09

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (-4, 1, 2) and (-1, -4, 3).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 75.12 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -5x^3 + x^2 - x + 2 at x = -3.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-81 with initial guess x0=11, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1 and ordinates 3, 3, 14, 8, 18, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 353 and 21.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 353 and 21 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 55 and 68.
solution: Given: a = 55, b = 68 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 55*68 / 1 | Answer: 3740

question: A circular rod of diameter 28 mm carries an axial tensile load of 14 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 13 mm and length 1600 mm carries an axial load of 73 kN. Take E = 200 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 53 mm transmits a torque of 1650 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 53, Tt = 1650 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(1650*1000) / (pi*(53)^3) | Answer: 56.45 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 58 mm and length 700 mm carries a torque of 1750 N-m. With G = 45 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (58)^4 / 32 = 1110994 mm^4 | theta = (1750*1000)(700) / (45000 * 1110994) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 1.404 degrees

question: A rectangular beam section is 81 mm wide and 150 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 81, h = 150 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 81*(150)^2 / 6 | Answer: 303750 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (112 mm x 240 mm) carries a bending moment of 17 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (55 mm x 120 mm) has effective length 2600 mm and E = 200 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 490 MPa is designed for a working stress of 60 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 490, sw = 60 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 490 / 60 | Answer: 8.167

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1150 mm and wall thickness 6 mm carries an internal pressure of 1.1 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1150, t = 6, P = 1.1 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 1.1*1150 / (2*6) | Answer: 105.4 MPa

question: 3.3 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 110 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.3, dT = 110 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 3.3 * 0.718 * 110 | Answer: 260.6 kJ

question: 6.7 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 125 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 6.7, dT = 125 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 6.7 * 1.005 * 125 | Answer: 841.7 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 4 m^3 at 310 K with mass 2.9 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 4, Tk = 310, m = 2.9 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 2.9*0.287*310 / 4 | Answer: 64.5 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 4 kg of air expands isothermally at 350 K from volume V1 to 4*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4, Tk = 350, ratio = 4 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 4*0.287*350*ln(4) | Answer: 557 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 1.4 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.06 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 1.4, D = 0.06 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*1.4*0.06 / 0.001 | Answer: 84000

question: Water flows at 2.5 m/s through a pipe of diameter 280 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
In a pipe (diameter 210 mm) water flows at 1.5 m/s. It contracts to diameter 110 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
Water flows at 3.1 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.25 m and length 190 m. With friction factor f = 0.027, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 26 teeth drives a gear of 71 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1400 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 26, z2 = 71, N1 = 1400 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1400*26 / 71 | Answer: 512.7 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 470 mm rotates at 400 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 470, N = 400 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.47)*400 / 60 | Answer: 9.844 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 23.3 kW at 1200 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 23.3, N = 1200 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(23.3*1000) / (2*pi*1200) | Answer: 185.4 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 6.3 kg rotates at radius 0.38 m at 700 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 10000 N/m and mass 12.1 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 10000, m = 12.1 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(10000/12.1) | Answer: 4.575 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 4.6 m^2 and thickness 0.13 m has conductivity k = 21.8 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 180 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 4.6, L = 0.13, k = 21.8, dT = 180 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 21.8*4.6*180 / 0.13 | Answer: 138849 W

question: A surface of area 2.2 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 135 W/m^2-K to surroundings 105 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 2.2, h = 135, dT = 105 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 135*2.2*105 | Answer: 31185 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 190 m/min, feed = 0.21 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2.9 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 190, f = 0.21, d = 2.9 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*190*0.21*2.9 | Answer: 115710 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 180 mm is turned at 800 rpm with a feed of 0.39 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 180, N = 800, f = 0.39 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 180 / (0.39*800) | Answer: 0.5769 min

question: A resistor of 144 ohm carries a current of 3 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 144, I = 3 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 3 * 144 | Answer: 432 V

question: Three resistors 35 ohm, 92 ohm and 39 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 35, R2 = 92, R3 = 39 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 35 + 92 + 39 | Answer: 166 ohm

question: Two resistors 76 ohm and 105 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 76, R2 = 105 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 76*105 / (76+105) | Answer: 44.09 ohm

question: A device draws 6.6 A at 10 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 10, I = 6.6 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 10 * 6.6 | Answer: 66 W

question: A current of 1.5 A flows through a 47 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 1.5, R = 47 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (1.5)^2 * 47 | Answer: 105.8 W

question: Two capacitors 30.1 uF and 37.7 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 30.1, C2 = 37.7 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 30.1*37.7 / (30.1+37.7) | Answer: 16.74 uF

question: A resistor 23 kohm and capacitor 11.1 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 23, C = 11.1 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (23k)(11.1u) = 255.3 ms | Answer: 255.3 ms

question: An inductor 488 mH is in series with 151 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 488, R = 151 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (488e-3) / 151 | Answer: 3.232 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 180.1 mH inductor at 740 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 180.1, f = 740 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (740)(180.1e-3) | Answer: 837.4 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 37.6 uF capacitor at 960 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 37.6, f = 960 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (960)(37.6e-6)) | Answer: 4.409 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 85 ohm, XL = 64 ohm and XC = 51 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 85, XL = 64, XC = 51 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(85^2 + (64 - 51)^2) | Answer: 85.99 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 36.3 mH and C = 6 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 36.3, C = 6 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(36.3e-3 * 6e-6)) | Answer: 341 Hz

question: A capacitor of 82 uF is charged to 30 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 82, V = 30 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*82e-6*(30)^2 | Answer: 36.9 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 230 V with 430 primary turns and 490 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 230, N1 = 430, N2 = 490 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 230 * 490/430 | Answer: 262.1 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 120 V and draws an armature current of 23 A. If the armature resistance is 1.44 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 120, Ia = 23, Ra = 1.44 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 120 - 23*1.44 | Answer: 86.88 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 180 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.95. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 180, VL = 400, pf = 0.95 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*400*180*0.95 / 1000 | Answer: 118.5 kW

question: A load has real power 55 kW and apparent power 185 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 55, S = 185 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 55 / 185 | Answer: 0.2973

question: A machine delivers 105 kW output while drawing 217 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 105, Pi = 217 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 105/217 * 100 | Answer: 48.39 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 23 V across R1 = 16 ohm and R2 = 27 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 23, R1 = 16, R2 = 27 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 23*27 / (16+27) | Answer: 14.44 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 40 kohm and Rin = 15 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 40, Rin = 15 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 40 / 15 | Answer: 2.667

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 40 kohm and Rg = 25 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 40, Rg = 25 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 40/25 | Answer: 2.6

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 4374. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 4374 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(4374) | Answer: 36.41 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.6 m carries a central point load of 85 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.6, W = 85 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 85*4.6 / 4 | Answer: 97.75 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.6 m carries a point load 30 kN at distance 2.3 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 4.6, a = 2.3, W = 30 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 30*(4.6 - 2.3) / 4.6 | Answer: 15 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 5.5 m) carries a central point load 50 kN. With E = 30 GPa and I = 210e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=50000 N, L=5500.0 mm, E=30000 MPa, I=210e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 27.51 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 8.1 m carries a UDL of 33 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 8.1, w = 33 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 33*(8.1)^2 / 12 | Answer: 180.4 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 680 mm, clear cover 35 mm and main bars of diameter 12 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 680, c = 35, dia = 12 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 680 - 35 - 12/2 | Answer: 639 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 34.6 m^2 carrying a factored load of 19.3 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 34.6, w = 19.3 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 19.3 * 34.6 | Answer: 667.8 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 5.1 m, unit weight 18 kN/m^3, phi = 36 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 2.1e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.4, area = 3.6e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 2.1, i = 0.4, A = 3.6 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (2.1e-4)*0.4*(3.6e-3) | Answer: 302.4 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.7 m, bed slope 0.008 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.028. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 1.9 m under a head of 1.1 m. Taking Cd = 0.61 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 5.2 m wide carries a discharge of 7.2 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A tank of volume 110 m^3 treats a flow of 20 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 110, Q = 20 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 110 / 20 | Answer: 5.5 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 160 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.26 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 4 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 160, k = 0.26, t = 4 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 160*(1 - e^(-0.26*4)) | Answer: 103.4 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.87, rainfall intensity 95 mm/h over a catchment of 44.1 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.87, i = 95, A = 44.1 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.87*95*44.1 / 360 | Answer: 10.12 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.02 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 330 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.02, M = 330 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 330*(30+0.02)/30 | Answer: 330.2 m

question: Convert the decimal number 453 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 453 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 1C5 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 00000000 and 01111100.
solution: XOR: 01111100 | Count of 1s = 5 | Answer: 5
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 590 megabits is sent over a link of 85 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 590, B = 85 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 590 / 85 | Answer: 6.941 s

question: A link has bandwidth 57 Mbps and round-trip time 90 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 57, R = 90 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 57e6 * 90e-3 bits = 5130 kb | Answer: 5130 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.84, cache access time 2 ns and main-memory access time 190 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.84, tc = 2, tm = 190 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.84*2 + (1 - 0.84)*190 | Answer: 32.08 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 421008 elements?
solution: Given: n = 421008 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(421008)) + 1 | Answer: 19

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.019, memory access time 190 ns and page-fault service time 9 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 9 ms = 9000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.019)*190 + 0.019*9000000.0 ns | Answer: 171.2 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 2.3 m^3 at 400 kPa and 390 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 2.3, P = 400, Tk = 390 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (400e3)*2.3 / (8.314*390) | Answer: 283.7 mol

question: For a reaction with A = 3e10 /s and activation energy 75 kJ/mol at 410 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 3, Ea = 75, Tk = 410 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 3e10 * exp(-75e3 / (8.314*410)) | Answer: 8.349 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.98 and bottoms xW = 0.09, with relative volatility alpha = 2. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.98, xw = 0.09, al = 2 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.98/0.02)(0.91/0.09)] / ln(2) | Answer: 8.953 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.6 and x = 0.38. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.6, x = 0.38 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.6/0.4) / (0.38/0.62) | Answer: 2.447

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.78 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 115 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.78, Psat = 115 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.78 * 115 | Answer: 89.7 kPa

question: A stream of 6.9 kg/s with specific heat 1.9 kJ/kg-K is heated through 30 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 6.9, cp = 1.9, dT = 30 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 6.9*1.9*30 | Answer: 393.3 kW

question: A reactor of volume 2.1 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 4.3 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 2.1, Q = 4.3 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 2.1 / 4.3 | Answer: 0.4884 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 6.7e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 1 mm with a concentration difference of 40 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 6.7, L = 1, dC = 40 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (6.7e-9)*40 / (1e-3) | Answer: 268 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 2.1 min and steady-state gain 3.5. For a step input of magnitude 12, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 2.1, K = 3.5, M = 12 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 3.5 * 12 | Answer: 42 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 35 m^2 flies at 70 m/s (air density 1.225 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.3. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 35, V = 70, rho = 1.225, CL = 0.3 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1.225*(70)^2*35*0.3 / 1000 | Answer: 31.51 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 20 m^2 flies at 240 m/s (density 0.7 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.12. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 20, V = 240, rho = 0.7, CD = 0.12 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.7*(240)^2*20*0.12 / 1000 | Answer: 48.38 kN

question: A specimen under stress 380 MPa shows an elastic strain of 2.4e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 380, eps = 2.4 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 380 / (2.4e-3) MPa = 158.3 GPa | Answer: 158.3 GPa

question: A block of mass 28 kg has a volume of 5.2e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 28, V = 5.2 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 28 / (5.2e-3) | Answer: 5385 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 1000 mm is heated through 70 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 17e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 1000, dT = 70, al = 17 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 1000*17e-6*70 | Answer: 1.19 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 155 ohm, R2 = 120 ohm and R3 = 325 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 155, R2 = 120, R3 = 325 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 120*325 / 155 | Answer: 251.6 ohm

question: Annual demand is 29500 units, ordering cost 100 per order and holding cost 15 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 29500, S = 100, H = 15 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*29500*100 / 15) | Answer: 627.2 units

question: An asset costs 370000 with salvage value 32000 after 13 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 370000, Sv = 32000, n = 13 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (370000 - 32000) / 13 | Answer: 26000 per year

question: A product sells for 300 per unit with variable cost 170 per unit and fixed costs 15000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 300, V = 170, F = 15000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 15000 / (300 - 170) | Answer: 115.4 units

question: Find the present worth of 25000 received 6 years from now at an interest rate of 6% per year.
solution: Given: F = 25000, n = 6, i = 6 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 25000 / (1 + 0.06)^6 | Answer: 17624 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.9, 0.98 and 0.9 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.9, r2 = 0.98, r3 = 0.9 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.9*0.98*0.9 | Answer: 0.7938

question: A process produces 43 defective items in a batch of 11000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 43, N = 11000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 43/11000 * 1e6 | Answer: 3909 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -4x^3 - 8x^2 - 2x + 5 evaluated at x = 4.
For f(x) = 2x^3 + 5x^2 + 8x + 8, find f''(x) at x = -4.

solution: Antiderivative F(x) = 0x^3/3 + -1x^2/2 + -8x | Evaluate F(7) - F(-3) | Answer: -100

question: Find the larger real root of x^2 + 6x + 6 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[5, 1], [7, 5]].
solution: Given: a = 5, b = 1, c = 7, d = 5 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (5)(5) - (1)(7) | Answer: 18

question: Find the determinant of [[0, -1, -3], [-3, 5, 4], [2, 6, 2]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: 70

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[5, 1], [8, -3]].
solution: Trace tr = 2, Determinant = -23 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 5.899

question: Solve for x: 1x + 0y = 11 and -3x + 4y = -8.
solution: Determinant = 1*4 - 0*-3 = 4 | x = (e d - b f) / det = 11 | Answer: x = 11
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 31, 31, 45, 54, 32.
solution: Sum = 193 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 38.6 | Answer: 38.6

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 28, 9, 16, 33, 28.
solution: Mean = 22.8 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 9.935

question: Find the slope of the line through (-8, 8) and (4, -3).
solution: Given: x1 = -8, y1 = 8, x2 = 4, y2 = -3 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (-3 - 8) / (4 - -8) | Answer: -0.9167

question: Find the distance between the points (-6, 0) and (-1, -2).
solution: Given: x1 = -6, y1 = 0, x2 = -1, y2 = -2 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((5)^2 + (-2)^2) | Answer: 5.385 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (-3,-5), (-1,8), (4,7).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 33.5 sq units

question: Find the 13th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 19 and common difference -6.
solution: Given: a = 19, d = -6, n = 13 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = 19 + (13 - 1)*-6 | Answer: -53

question: Find the sum of the first 13 terms of an AP with first term -9 and common difference 0.
solution: Given: a = -9, d = 0, n = 13 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 13/2 [2*-9 + (13-1)*0] | Answer: -117

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 18000 at 9.7% per annum for 1 years.
solution: Given: P = 18000, R = 9.7, Tt = 1 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 18000 * 9.7 * 1 / 100 | Answer: 1746 currency units

question: Find the amount when 28500 is invested at 8.1% per annum compounded annually for 4 years.
solution: Given: P = 28500, R = 8.1, Tt = 4 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 28500 * (1 + 8.1/100)^4 | Answer: 38918 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (2, -1, -6) and (-1, 5, 7).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (5, -5, 2) and (-3, 0, 1).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 19.26

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (5, -4, -1) and (0, 2, -4).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 97.93 degrees

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number -3 + -2i.
solution: Given: a = -3, b = -2 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(-2, -3) | Answer: -146.3 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -3x^3 - 7x^2 + 6x - 7 at x = 3.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-126 with initial guess x0=12, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=0.8 and ordinates 9, 14, 0, 18, 17, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 138 and 244.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 138 and 244 | Answer: GCD = 2

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 77 and 47.
solution: Given: a = 77, b = 47 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 77*47 / 1 | Answer: 3619
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 28 mm carries an axial tensile load of 87 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 30 mm and length 2800 mm carries an axial load of 78 kN. Take E = 210 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 58 mm transmits a torque of 2800 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 58, Tt = 2800 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(2800*1000) / (pi*(58)^3) | Answer: 73.09 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 29 mm and length 1100 mm carries a torque of 1300 N-m. With G = 80 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (29)^4 / 32 = 69437 mm^4 | theta = (1300*1000)(1100) / (80000 * 69437) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 14.75 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 92 mm wide and 110 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 92, h = 110 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 92*(110)^2 / 6 | Answer: 185533 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (49 mm x 130 mm) carries a bending moment of 33 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (56 mm x 150 mm) has effective length 3900 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 350 MPa is designed for a working stress of 110 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 350, sw = 110 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 350 / 110 | Answer: 3.182

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 500 mm and wall thickness 12 mm carries an internal pressure of 2.6 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 500, t = 12, P = 2.6 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 2.6*500 / (2*12) | Answer: 54.17 MPa

question: 2.4 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 55 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.4, dT = 55 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 2.4 * 0.718 * 55 | Answer: 94.78 kJ

question: 8 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 180 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 8, dT = 180 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 8 * 1.005 * 180 | Answer: 1447 kJ
