question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 0.9 m^3 at 410 K with mass 1.3 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 0.9, Tk = 410, m = 1.3 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 1.3*0.287*410 / 0.9 | Answer: 170 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 1 kg of air expands isothermally at 480 K from volume V1 to 5*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1, Tk = 480, ratio = 5 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 1*0.287*480*ln(5) | Answer: 221.7 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 0.7 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.26 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 0.7, D = 0.26 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*0.7*0.26 / 0.001 | Answer: 182000

question: Water flows at 0.5 m/s through a pipe of diameter 150 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 8 m. Taking Cv = 0.95, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 8, cv = 0.95 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.95*sqrt(2*9.81*8) | Answer: 11.9 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 330 mm) water flows at 2.2 m/s. It contracts to diameter 80 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 330, d2 = 80, V1 = 2.2 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 2.2*(330/80)^2 | Answer: 37.43 m/s

question: Water flows at 4 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.13 m and length 380 m. With friction factor f = 0.035, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 23 teeth drives a gear of 79 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1250 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 23, z2 = 79, N1 = 1250 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1250*23 / 79 | Answer: 363.9 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 570 mm rotates at 600 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 570, N = 600 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.57)*600 / 60 | Answer: 17.91 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 18.8 kW at 900 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 18.8, N = 900 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(18.8*1000) / (2*pi*900) | Answer: 199.5 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 0.9 kg rotates at radius 0.37 m at 950 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 800 N/m and mass 11.4 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 800, m = 11.4 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(800/11.4) | Answer: 1.333 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 7.7 m^2 and thickness 0.39 m has conductivity k = 8 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 90 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 7.7, L = 0.39, k = 8, dT = 90 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 8*7.7*90 / 0.39 | Answer: 14215 W

question: A surface of area 1.9 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 15 W/m^2-K to surroundings 65 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 1.9, h = 15, dT = 65 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 15*1.9*65 | Answer: 1852 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 200 m/min, feed = 0.32 mm/rev, depth of cut = 0.7 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 200, f = 0.32, d = 0.7 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*200*0.32*0.7 | Answer: 44800 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 200 mm is turned at 1100 rpm with a feed of 0.28 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 200, N = 1100, f = 0.28 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 200 / (0.28*1100) | Answer: 0.6494 min

question: A resistor of 199 ohm carries a current of 3.7 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 199, I = 3.7 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 3.7 * 199 | Answer: 736.3 V

question: Three resistors 72 ohm, 9 ohm and 75 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 72, R2 = 9, R3 = 75 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 72 + 9 + 75 | Answer: 156 ohm

question: Two resistors 56 ohm and 31 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 56, R2 = 31 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 56*31 / (56+31) | Answer: 19.95 ohm

question: A device draws 11.2 A at 215 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 215, I = 11.2 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 215 * 11.2 | Answer: 2408 W

question: A current of 0.7 A flows through a 73 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 0.7, R = 73 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (0.7)^2 * 73 | Answer: 35.77 W

question: Two capacitors 36.2 uF and 44.9 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 36.2, C2 = 44.9 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 36.2*44.9 / (36.2+44.9) | Answer: 20.04 uF

question: A resistor 51 kohm and capacitor 15.7 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 51, C = 15.7 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (51k)(15.7u) = 800.7 ms | Answer: 800.7 ms

question: An inductor 103 mH is in series with 77 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 103, R = 77 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (103e-3) / 77 | Answer: 1.338 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 137.6 mH inductor at 900 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 137.6, f = 900 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (900)(137.6e-3) | Answer: 778.1 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 48.8 uF capacitor at 70 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 48.8, f = 70 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (70)(48.8e-6)) | Answer: 46.59 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 54 ohm, XL = 35 ohm and XC = 32 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 54, XL = 35, XC = 32 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(54^2 + (35 - 32)^2) | Answer: 54.08 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 25.1 mH and C = 10 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 25.1, C = 10 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(25.1e-3 * 10e-6)) | Answer: 317.7 Hz

question: A capacitor of 80 uF is charged to 20 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 80, V = 20 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*80e-6*(20)^2 | Answer: 16 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 400 V with 540 primary turns and 480 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 400, N1 = 540, N2 = 480 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 400 * 480/540 | Answer: 355.6 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 280 V and draws an armature current of 6 A. If the armature resistance is 1.3 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 280, Ia = 6, Ra = 1.3 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 280 - 6*1.3 | Answer: 272.2 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 110 A at 415 V (line) with a power factor of 0.88. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 110, VL = 415, pf = 0.88 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*415*110*0.88 / 1000 | Answer: 69.58 kW

question: A load has real power 90 kW and apparent power 120 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 90, S = 120 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 90 / 120 | Answer: 0.75

question: A machine delivers 160 kW output while drawing 197 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 160, Pi = 197 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 160/197 * 100 | Answer: 81.22 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 15 V across R1 = 16 ohm and R2 = 29 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 15, R1 = 16, R2 = 29 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 15*29 / (16+29) | Answer: 9.667 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 80 kohm and Rin = 41 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 80, Rin = 41 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 80 / 41 | Answer: 1.951

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 70 kohm and Rg = 38 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 70, Rg = 38 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 70/38 | Answer: 2.842

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 373. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 373 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(373) | Answer: 25.72 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.1 m carries a central point load of 45 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.1, W = 45 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 45*4.1 / 4 | Answer: 46.12 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 3.1 m carries a point load 45 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.1, W = 45 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 45*3.1 | Answer: 139.5 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 2 m carries a UDL of 26 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 2, w = 26 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 26*(2)^2 / 2 | Answer: 52 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 7.2 m carries a point load 90 kN at distance 3.8 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 7.2, a = 3.8, W = 90 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 90*(7.2 - 3.8) / 7.2 | Answer: 42.5 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 4.9 m) carries a central point load 20 kN. With E = 200 GPa and I = 70e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=20000 N, L=4900.0 mm, E=200000 MPa, I=70e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 3.501 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 5.8 m carries a UDL of 6 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.8, w = 6 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 6*(5.8)^2 / 12 | Answer: 16.82 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 510 mm, clear cover 30 mm and main bars of diameter 16 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 510, c = 30, dia = 16 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 510 - 30 - 16/2 | Answer: 472 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 18.2 m^2 carrying a factored load of 9.6 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 18.2, w = 9.6 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 9.6 * 18.2 | Answer: 174.7 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 3.1 m, unit weight 19 kN/m^3, phi = 36 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 8.3e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.9, area = 1.4e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 8.3, i = 0.9, A = 1.4 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (8.3e-4)*0.9*(1.4e-3) | Answer: 1046 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.5 m, bed slope 0.008 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.018. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 2.8 m under a head of 0.9 m. Taking Cd = 0.62 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 3.7 m wide carries a discharge of 17.2 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 410 m and design speed 50 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 410, V = 50 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (50)^2 / (127*410) | Answer: 0.04801
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: A tank of volume 640 m^3 treats a flow of 115 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 640, Q = 115 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 640 / 115 | Answer: 5.565 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 370 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.32 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 8 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 370, k = 0.32, t = 8 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 370*(1 - e^(-0.32*8)) | Answer: 341.4 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.39, rainfall intensity 60 mm/h over a catchment of 50.5 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.39, i = 60, A = 50.5 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.39*60*50.5 / 360 | Answer: 3.283 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.03 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 100 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.03, M = 100 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 100*(20+0.03)/20 | Answer: 100.2 m

question: Convert the decimal number 1117 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 1117 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 45D (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 10001100 and 00111110.
solution: XOR: 10110010 | Count of 1s = 4 | Answer: 4
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 240 megabits is sent over a link of 42 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 240, B = 42 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 240 / 42 | Answer: 5.714 s

question: A link has bandwidth 47 Mbps and round-trip time 190 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 47, R = 190 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 47e6 * 190e-3 bits = 8930 kb | Answer: 8930 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.8, cache access time 10 ns and main-memory access time 150 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.8, tc = 10, tm = 150 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.8*10 + (1 - 0.8)*150 | Answer: 38 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 607572 elements?
solution: Given: n = 607572 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(607572)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.011, memory access time 120 ns and page-fault service time 5 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 5 ms = 5000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.011)*120 + 0.011*5000000.0 ns | Answer: 55.12 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 0.5 m^3 at 470 kPa and 590 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 0.5, P = 470, Tk = 590 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (470e3)*0.5 / (8.314*590) | Answer: 47.91 mol

question: For a reaction with A = 7e10 /s and activation energy 90 kJ/mol at 310 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 7, Ea = 90, Tk = 310 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 7e10 * exp(-90e3 / (8.314*310)) | Answer: 0.00004782 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.9 and bottoms xW = 0.09, with relative volatility alpha = 2.6. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.9, xw = 0.09, al = 2.6 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.9/0.1)(0.91/0.09)] / ln(2.6) | Answer: 4.721 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.68 and x = 0.41. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.68, x = 0.41 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.68/0.32) / (0.41/0.59) | Answer: 3.058

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.85 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 120 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.85, Psat = 120 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.85 * 120 | Answer: 102 kPa

question: A stream of 4.5 kg/s with specific heat 3.5 kJ/kg-K is heated through 20 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 4.5, cp = 3.5, dT = 20 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 4.5*3.5*20 | Answer: 315 kW

question: A reactor of volume 11.8 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 4.2 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 11.8, Q = 4.2 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 11.8 / 4.2 | Answer: 2.81 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 8.7e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 3 mm with a concentration difference of 70 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 8.7, L = 3, dC = 70 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (8.7e-9)*70 / (3e-3) | Answer: 203 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 5.1 min and steady-state gain 1.4. For a step input of magnitude 5, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 5.1, K = 1.4, M = 5 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 1.4 * 5 | Answer: 7 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 80 m^2 flies at 80 m/s (air density 0.4 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.9. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 80, V = 80, rho = 0.4, CL = 0.9 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.4*(80)^2*80*0.9 / 1000 | Answer: 92.16 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 85 m^2 flies at 240 m/s (density 0.7 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.02. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 85, V = 240, rho = 0.7, CD = 0.02 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.7*(240)^2*85*0.02 / 1000 | Answer: 34.27 kN

question: A specimen under stress 330 MPa shows an elastic strain of 1.3e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 330, eps = 1.3 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 330 / (1.3e-3) MPa = 253.8 GPa | Answer: 253.8 GPa

question: A block of mass 11 kg has a volume of 3.3e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 11, V = 3.3 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 11 / (3.3e-3) | Answer: 3333 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 2200 mm is heated through 60 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 23e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 2200, dT = 60, al = 23 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 2200*23e-6*60 | Answer: 3.036 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 160 ohm, R2 = 155 ohm and R3 = 485 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 160, R2 = 155, R3 = 485 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 155*485 / 160 | Answer: 469.8 ohm

question: Annual demand is 4500 units, ordering cost 170 per order and holding cost 5 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 4500, S = 170, H = 5 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*4500*170 / 5) | Answer: 553.2 units

question: An asset costs 320000 with salvage value 10000 after 12 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 320000, Sv = 10000, n = 12 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (320000 - 10000) / 12 | Answer: 25833 per year

question: A product sells for 60 per unit with variable cost 10 per unit and fixed costs 130000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 60, V = 10, F = 130000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 130000 / (60 - 10) | Answer: 2600 units

question: Find the present worth of 55000 received 6 years from now at an interest rate of 9% per year.
solution: Given: F = 55000, n = 6, i = 9 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 55000 / (1 + 0.09)^6 | Answer: 32795 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.96, 0.93 and 0.98 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.96, r2 = 0.93, r3 = 0.98 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.96*0.93*0.98 | Answer: 0.8749

question: A process produces 1 defective items in a batch of 11000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 1, N = 11000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 1/11000 * 1e6 | Answer: 90.91 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = 4x^3 + 5x^2 + 2 evaluated at x = 0.
For f(x) = 5x^3 - 3x^2 + 2x - 2, find f''(x) at x = 0.
Evaluate the definite integral of (5x - 5) dx from x = 1 to x = 4.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = 0x^3/3 + 5x^2/2 + -5x | Evaluate F(4) - F(1) | Answer: 22.5
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of x^2 - 8x + 3 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[7, 0], [1, -4]].
solution: Given: a = 7, b = 0, c = 1, d = -4 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (7)(-4) - (0)(1) | Answer: -28

question: Find the determinant of [[1, -1, -2], [5, 5, -2], [-5, -4, -2]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: -48

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[-8, -6], [-7, -1]].
solution: Trace tr = -9, Determinant = -34 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 2.865

question: Solve for x: 5x + 6y = -2 and 1x + 2y = 3.
solution: Determinant = 5*2 - 6*1 = 4 | x = (e d - b f) / det = -5.5 | Answer: x = -5.5
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 31, 37, 34, 64, 31.
solution: Sum = 197 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 39.4 | Answer: 39.4

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 28, 48, 5, 23, 49.
solution: Mean = 30.6 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 18.45

question: Find the slope of the line through (2, 7) and (8, -1).
solution: Given: x1 = 2, y1 = 7, x2 = 8, y2 = -1 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (-1 - 7) / (8 - 2) | Answer: -1.333

question: Find the distance between the points (1, 8) and (-8, 3).
solution: Given: x1 = 1, y1 = 8, x2 = -8, y2 = 3 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-9)^2 + (-5)^2) | Answer: 10.3 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (6,8), (-5,-4), (5,4).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 16 sq units

question: Find the 23th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -20 and common difference -7.
solution: Given: a = -20, d = -7, n = 23 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -20 + (23 - 1)*-7 | Answer: -174

question: Find the sum of the first 39 terms of an AP with first term -12 and common difference 7.
solution: Given: a = -12, d = 7, n = 39 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 39/2 [2*-12 + (39-1)*7] | Answer: 4719

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 1500 at 6% per annum for 8 years.
solution: Given: P = 1500, R = 6, Tt = 8 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 1500 * 6 * 8 / 100 | Answer: 720 currency units

question: Find the amount when 8500 is invested at 7.2% per annum compounded annually for 5 years.
solution: Given: P = 8500, R = 7.2, Tt = 5 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 8500 * (1 + 7.2/100)^5 | Answer: 12034 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (8, -4, -5) and (-2, 6, 4).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (5, -2, 2) and (-6, 4, -1).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 12.21

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (-3, -6, -2) and (-2, 1, 1).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 96.7 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number 1 + 12i.
solution: Given: a = 1, b = 12 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((1)^2 + (12)^2) | Answer: 12.04

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number 6 + -9i.
solution: Given: a = 6, b = -9 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(-9, 6) | Answer: -56.31 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = 4x^3 - 6x^2 + x - 8 at x = 2.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-80 with initial guess x0=2, find x1 (one iteration).
solution: Given: N = 80, x0 = 2 | Formula: x1 = x0 - (x0^2 - N)/(2 x0) | Substitute: x1 = 2 - ((2)^2 - 80)/(2*2) | Answer: 21

question: Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1 and ordinates 0, 13, 6, 13, 12, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 559 and 586.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 559 and 586 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 67 and 53.
solution: Given: a = 67, b = 53 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 67*53 / 1 | Answer: 3551
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 38 mm carries an axial tensile load of 56 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 27 mm and length 2400 mm carries an axial load of 47 kN. Take E = 210 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 52 mm transmits a torque of 2100 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 52, Tt = 2100 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(2100*1000) / (pi*(52)^3) | Answer: 76.06 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 45 mm and length 1900 mm carries a torque of 250 N-m. With G = 45 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (45)^4 / 32 = 402578 mm^4 | theta = (250*1000)(1900) / (45000 * 402578) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 1.502 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 65 mm wide and 140 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 65, h = 140 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 65*(140)^2 / 6 | Answer: 212333 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (57 mm x 160 mm) carries a bending moment of 16 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (58 mm x 140 mm) has effective length 2600 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 390 MPa is designed for a working stress of 240 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 390, sw = 240 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 390 / 240 | Answer: 1.625

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 850 mm and wall thickness 8 mm carries an internal pressure of 2.9 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 850, t = 8, P = 2.9 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 2.9*850 / (2*8) | Answer: 154.1 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 660 K and 450 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 660, Tc = 450 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 450/660) * 100 | Answer: 31.82 %

question: 4 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 115 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4, dT = 115 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 4 * 0.718 * 115 | Answer: 330.3 kJ

question: 6.1 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 115 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 6.1, dT = 115 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 6.1 * 1.005 * 115 | Answer: 705 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 0.7 m^3 at 440 K with mass 4.3 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 0.7, Tk = 440, m = 4.3 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 4.3*0.287*440 / 0.7 | Answer: 775.7 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 2.6 kg of air expands isothermally at 430 K from volume V1 to 2*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.6, Tk = 430, ratio = 2 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 2.6*0.287*430*ln(2) | Answer: 222.4 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 4.7 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.35 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 4.7, D = 0.35 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*4.7*0.35 / 0.001 | Answer: 1645000

question: Water flows at 1.4 m/s through a pipe of diameter 190 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 17 m. Taking Cv = 0.99, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 17, cv = 0.99 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.99*sqrt(2*9.81*17) | Answer: 18.08 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 210 mm) water flows at 0.9 m/s. It contracts to diameter 110 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 210, d2 = 110, V1 = 0.9 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 0.9*(210/110)^2 | Answer: 3.28 m/s

question: Water flows at 3.6 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.45 m and length 140 m. With friction factor f = 0.028, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 34 teeth drives a gear of 48 teeth. If the pinion runs at 550 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 34, z2 = 48, N1 = 550 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 550*34 / 48 | Answer: 389.6 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 170 mm rotates at 700 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 170, N = 700 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.17)*700 / 60 | Answer: 6.231 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 6.4 kW at 1350 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 6.4, N = 1350 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(6.4*1000) / (2*pi*1350) | Answer: 45.27 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 5.3 kg rotates at radius 0.54 m at 300 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 17200 N/m and mass 12.6 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 17200, m = 12.6 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(17200/12.6) | Answer: 5.88 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 1.5 m^2 and thickness 0.36 m has conductivity k = 3.7 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 40 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 1.5, L = 0.36, k = 3.7, dT = 40 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 3.7*1.5*40 / 0.36 | Answer: 616.7 W

question: A surface of area 5.5 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 125 W/m^2-K to surroundings 35 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 5.5, h = 125, dT = 35 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 125*5.5*35 | Answer: 24062 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 100 m/min, feed = 0.27 mm/rev, depth of cut = 0.5 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 100, f = 0.27, d = 0.5 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*100*0.27*0.5 | Answer: 13500 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 430 mm is turned at 600 rpm with a feed of 0.33 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 430, N = 600, f = 0.33 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 430 / (0.33*600) | Answer: 2.172 min

question: A resistor of 77 ohm carries a current of 1.1 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 77, I = 1.1 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 1.1 * 77 | Answer: 84.7 V

question: Three resistors 29 ohm, 18 ohm and 50 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 29, R2 = 18, R3 = 50 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 29 + 18 + 50 | Answer: 97 ohm

question: Two resistors 76 ohm and 55 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 76, R2 = 55 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 76*55 / (76+55) | Answer: 31.91 ohm

question: A device draws 1.6 A at 130 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 130, I = 1.6 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 130 * 1.6 | Answer: 208 W

question: A current of 10.7 A flows through a 121 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 10.7, R = 121 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (10.7)^2 * 121 | Answer: 13853 W

question: Two capacitors 6.7 uF and 40.7 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 6.7, C2 = 40.7 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 6.7*40.7 / (6.7+40.7) | Answer: 5.753 uF

question: A resistor 72 kohm and capacitor 18.3 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 72, C = 18.3 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (72k)(18.3u) = 1318 ms | Answer: 1318 ms

question: An inductor 58.5 mH is in series with 37 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 58.5, R = 37 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (58.5e-3) / 37 | Answer: 1.581 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 158.2 mH inductor at 830 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 158.2, f = 830 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (830)(158.2e-3) | Answer: 825 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 14.1 uF capacitor at 920 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 14.1, f = 920 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (920)(14.1e-6)) | Answer: 12.27 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 40 ohm, XL = 129 ohm and XC = 121 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 40, XL = 129, XC = 121 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(40^2 + (129 - 121)^2) | Answer: 40.79 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 55.7 mH and C = 4.5 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 55.7, C = 4.5 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(55.7e-3 * 4.5e-6)) | Answer: 317.9 Hz

question: A capacitor of 68.2 uF is charged to 215 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 68.2, V = 215 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*68.2e-6*(215)^2 | Answer: 1576 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 430 V with 550 primary turns and 390 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 430, N1 = 550, N2 = 390 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 430 * 390/550 | Answer: 304.9 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 170 V and draws an armature current of 6 A. If the armature resistance is 0.12 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 170, Ia = 6, Ra = 0.12 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 170 - 6*0.12 | Answer: 169.3 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 5 A at 415 V (line) with a power factor of 0.97. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 5, VL = 415, pf = 0.97 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*415*5*0.97 / 1000 | Answer: 3.486 kW

question: A load has real power 25 kW and apparent power 55 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 25, S = 55 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 25 / 55 | Answer: 0.4545

question: A machine delivers 175 kW output while drawing 197 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 175, Pi = 197 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 175/197 * 100 | Answer: 88.83 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 5 V across R1 = 44 ohm and R2 = 29 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 5, R1 = 44, R2 = 29 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 5*29 / (44+29) | Answer: 1.986 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 200 kohm and Rin = 16 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 200, Rin = 16 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 200 / 16 | Answer: 12.5

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 20 kohm and Rg = 20 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 20, Rg = 20 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 20/20 | Answer: 2

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 3186. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 3186 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(3186) | Answer: 35.03 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 8.4 m carries a central point load of 25 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 8.4, W = 25 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 25*8.4 / 4 | Answer: 52.5 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 2.6 m carries a point load 45 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 2.6, W = 45 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 45*2.6 | Answer: 117 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 2.1 m carries a UDL of 24 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 2.1, w = 24 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 24*(2.1)^2 / 2 | Answer: 52.92 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.5 m carries a point load 100 kN at distance 2.4 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 9.5, a = 2.4, W = 100 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 100*(9.5 - 2.4) / 9.5 | Answer: 74.74 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 3.5 m) carries a central point load 10 kN. With E = 25 GPa and I = 300e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=10000 N, L=3500.0 mm, E=25000 MPa, I=300e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 1.191 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 9 m carries a UDL of 45 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 9, w = 45 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 45*(9)^2 / 12 | Answer: 303.8 kN-m

question: A column supports a floor area of 28.4 m^2 carrying a factored load of 14.5 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 28.4, w = 14.5 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 14.5 * 28.4 | Answer: 411.8 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 3.3 m, unit weight 19 kN/m^3, phi = 38 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 4.6e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1.4, area = 2.8e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 4.6, i = 1.4, A = 2.8 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (4.6e-4)*1.4*(2.8e-3) | Answer: 1803 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 2.1 m, bed slope 0.003 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.027. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 3.3 m under a head of 0.7 m. Taking Cd = 0.6 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 5.3 m wide carries a discharge of 7.3 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A tank of volume 690 m^3 treats a flow of 145 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 690, Q = 145 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 690 / 145 | Answer: 4.759 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 290 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.18 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 4 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 290, k = 0.18, t = 4 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 290*(1 - e^(-0.18*4)) | Answer: 148.8 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.47, rainfall intensity 40 mm/h over a catchment of 43.5 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.47, i = 40, A = 43.5 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.47*40*43.5 / 360 | Answer: 2.272 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.04 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 460 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.04, M = 460 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 460*(30+0.04)/30 | Answer: 460.6 m

question: Convert the decimal number 1022 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 1022 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 3FE (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 00011010 and 01111100.
solution: XOR: 01100110 | Count of 1s = 4 | Answer: 4
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 190 megabits is sent over a link of 45 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 190, B = 45 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 190 / 45 | Answer: 4.222 s

question: A link has bandwidth 86 Mbps and round-trip time 110 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 86, R = 110 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 86e6 * 110e-3 bits = 9460 kb | Answer: 9460 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.88, cache access time 7 ns and main-memory access time 120 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.88, tc = 7, tm = 120 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.88*7 + (1 - 0.88)*120 | Answer: 20.56 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 660677 elements?
solution: Given: n = 660677 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(660677)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.006, memory access time 180 ns and page-fault service time 10 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 10 ms = 10000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.006)*180 + 0.006*10000000.0 ns | Answer: 60.18 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 2.3 m^3 at 180 kPa and 300 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 2.3, P = 180, Tk = 300 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (180e3)*2.3 / (8.314*300) | Answer: 166 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.37 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 15 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.37, t = 15 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.37*15) | Answer: 0.9961

question: For a reaction with A = 8e10 /s and activation energy 90 kJ/mol at 400 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 8, Ea = 90, Tk = 400 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 8e10 * exp(-90e3 / (8.314*400)) | Answer: 0.1412 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.95 and bottoms xW = 0.07, with relative volatility alpha = 2.5. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.95, xw = 0.07, al = 2.5 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.95/0.05)(0.93/0.07)] / ln(2.5) | Answer: 6.036 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.78 and x = 0.41. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.78, x = 0.41 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.78/0.22) / (0.41/0.59) | Answer: 5.102

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.27 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 55 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.27, Psat = 55 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.27 * 55 | Answer: 14.85 kPa

question: A stream of 5.2 kg/s with specific heat 1.7 kJ/kg-K is heated through 75 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 5.2, cp = 1.7, dT = 75 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 5.2*1.7*75 | Answer: 663 kW

question: A reactor of volume 18.7 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 0.3 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 18.7, Q = 0.3 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 18.7 / 0.3 | Answer: 62.33 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 3.3e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 5 mm with a concentration difference of 110 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 3.3, L = 5, dC = 110 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (3.3e-9)*110 / (5e-3) | Answer: 72.6 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 2.7 min and steady-state gain 3.2. For a step input of magnitude 6, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 2.7, K = 3.2, M = 6 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 3.2 * 6 | Answer: 19.2 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 105 m^2 flies at 160 m/s (air density 1.225 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 1.3. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 105, V = 160, rho = 1.225, CL = 1.3 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1.225*(160)^2*105*1.3 / 1000 | Answer: 214 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 75 m^2 flies at 250 m/s (density 0.7 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.04. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 75, V = 250, rho = 0.7, CD = 0.04 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.7*(250)^2*75*0.04 / 1000 | Answer: 65.62 kN

question: A specimen under stress 170 MPa shows an elastic strain of 2.9e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 170, eps = 2.9 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 170 / (2.9e-3) MPa = 58.62 GPa | Answer: 58.62 GPa

question: A block of mass 17 kg has a volume of 2.8e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 17, V = 2.8 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 17 / (2.8e-3) | Answer: 6071 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 2100 mm is heated through 140 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 11e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 2100, dT = 140, al = 11 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 2100*11e-6*140 | Answer: 3.234 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 65 ohm, R2 = 75 ohm and R3 = 145 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 65, R2 = 75, R3 = 145 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 75*145 / 65 | Answer: 167.3 ohm

question: A measurement reads 10.09 when the true value is 20. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10.09, true = 20 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10.09 - 20| / 20 * 100 | Answer: 49.55 %

question: Annual demand is 14000 units, ordering cost 150 per order and holding cost 22 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 14000, S = 150, H = 22 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*14000*150 / 22) | Answer: 436.9 units

question: An asset costs 130000 with salvage value 30000 after 15 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 130000, Sv = 30000, n = 15 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (130000 - 30000) / 15 | Answer: 6667 per year

question: A product sells for 210 per unit with variable cost 10 per unit and fixed costs 120000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 210, V = 10, F = 120000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 120000 / (210 - 10) | Answer: 600 units

question: Find the present worth of 115000 received 9 years from now at an interest rate of 7% per year.
solution: Given: F = 115000, n = 9, i = 7 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 115000 / (1 + 0.07)^9 | Answer: 62552 currency units

question: A process produces 17 defective items in a batch of 12500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 17, N = 12500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 17/12500 * 1e6 | Answer: 1360 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -x^3 - 8x^2 - 8x - 2 evaluated at x = 0.
For f(x) = -4x^3 - 3x^2 - 4x, find f''(x) at x = 3.
Evaluate the definite integral of (2x^2 - 5x + 1) dx from x = -4 to x = 5.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = 2x^3/3 + -5x^2/2 + 1x | Evaluate F(5) - F(-4) | Answer: 112.5
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 4x^2 + 8x - 3 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[-7, 6], [-3, 3]].
solution: Given: a = -7, b = 6, c = -3, d = 3 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (-7)(3) - (6)(-3) | Answer: -3

question: Find the determinant of [[-6, -3, -4], [0, -5, -6], [6, 3, 0]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: -120

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[0, 4], [4, 7]].
solution: Trace tr = 7, Determinant = -16 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 8.815

question: Solve for x: -5x + -5y = -2 and 6x + 2y = -3.
solution: Determinant = -5*2 - -5*6 = 20 | x = (e d - b f) / det = -0.95 | Answer: x = -0.95
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 44, 20, 20, 77, 56.
solution: Sum = 217 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 43.4 | Answer: 43.4

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 19, 10, 46, 2, 50.
solution: Mean = 25.4 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 21.54

question: Find the slope of the line through (4, -6) and (-9, 2).
solution: Given: x1 = 4, y1 = -6, x2 = -9, y2 = 2 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (2 - -6) / (-9 - 4) | Answer: -0.6154

question: Find the distance between the points (3, 6) and (5, 8).
solution: Given: x1 = 3, y1 = 6, x2 = 5, y2 = 8 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((2)^2 + (2)^2) | Answer: 2.828 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (-2,1), (7,1), (-4,6).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 22.5 sq units

question: Find the 33th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -18 and common difference -9.
solution: Given: a = -18, d = -9, n = 33 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -18 + (33 - 1)*-9 | Answer: -306

question: Find the sum of the first 20 terms of an AP with first term -14 and common difference 6.
solution: Given: a = -14, d = 6, n = 20 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 20/2 [2*-14 + (20-1)*6] | Answer: 860

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 4500 at 14.3% per annum for 7 years.
solution: Given: P = 4500, R = 14.3, Tt = 7 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 4500 * 14.3 * 7 / 100 | Answer: 4504 currency units

question: Find the amount when 2000 is invested at 8.1% per annum compounded annually for 2 years.
solution: Given: P = 2000, R = 8.1, Tt = 2 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 2000 * (1 + 8.1/100)^2 | Answer: 2337 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (3, 1, -1) and (3, -7, -6).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (-1, -5, 1) and (-1, -3, -6).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 33.79

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (5, -3, 0) and (0, -3, 5).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 74.65 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number 1 + 1i.
solution: Given: a = 1, b = 1 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((1)^2 + (1)^2) | Answer: 1.414

question: Evaluate f(x) = 2x^3 + 7x^2 - 5x at x = -5.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-96 with initial guess x0=8, find x1 (one iteration).
solution: Given: N = 96, x0 = 8 | Formula: x1 = x0 - (x0^2 - N)/(2 x0) | Substitute: x1 = 8 - ((8)^2 - 96)/(2*8) | Answer: 10

question: Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=0.6 and ordinates 20, 19, 9, 5, 7, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 563 and 599.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 563 and 599 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 51 and 58.
solution: Given: a = 51, b = 58 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 51*58 / 1 | Answer: 2958
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 45 mm carries an axial tensile load of 62 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 23 mm and length 2200 mm carries an axial load of 29 kN. Take E = 110 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 50 mm transmits a torque of 1550 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 50, Tt = 1550 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(1550*1000) / (pi*(50)^3) | Answer: 63.15 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 25 mm and length 1000 mm carries a torque of 200 N-m. With G = 77 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (25)^4 / 32 = 3835 mm^4 | theta = (200*1000)(1000) / (77000 * 3835) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 3.881 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 65 mm wide and 190 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 65, h = 190 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 65*(190)^2 / 6 | Answer: 391083 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (63 mm x 200 mm) carries a bending moment of 2 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (43 mm x 110 mm) has effective length 3800 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 370 MPa is designed for a working stress of 110 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 370, sw = 110 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 370 / 110 | Answer: 3.364

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 950 mm and wall thickness 13 mm carries an internal pressure of 2.9 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 950, t = 13, P = 2.9 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 2.9*950 / (2*13) | Answer: 106 MPa

question: 7.3 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 65 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 7.3, dT = 65 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 7.3 * 0.718 * 65 | Answer: 340.7 kJ

question: 2 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 65 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2, dT = 65 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 2 * 1.005 * 65 | Answer: 130.6 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 2.6 m^3 at 510 K with mass 1 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 2.6, Tk = 510, m = 1 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 1*0.287*510 / 2.6 | Answer: 56.3 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 3.6 kg of air expands isothermally at 330 K from volume V1 to 4*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.6, Tk = 330, ratio = 4 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 3.6*0.287*330*ln(4) | Answer: 472.7 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 1.9 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.4 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 1.9, D = 0.4 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*1.9*0.4 / 0.001 | Answer: 760000

question: Water flows at 1.3 m/s through a pipe of diameter 250 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 6.4 m. Taking Cv = 0.99, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 6.4, cv = 0.99 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.99*sqrt(2*9.81*6.4) | Answer: 11.09 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 300 mm) water flows at 2.4 m/s. It contracts to diameter 120 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 300, d2 = 120, V1 = 2.4 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 2.4*(300/120)^2 | Answer: 15 m/s

question: Water flows at 3.9 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.49 m and length 50 m. With friction factor f = 0.039, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 33 teeth drives a gear of 81 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1350 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 33, z2 = 81, N1 = 1350 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1350*33 / 81 | Answer: 550 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 410 mm rotates at 900 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 410, N = 900 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.41)*900 / 60 | Answer: 19.32 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 7.5 kW at 1000 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 7.5, N = 1000 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(7.5*1000) / (2*pi*1000) | Answer: 71.62 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 8.7 kg rotates at radius 0.1 m at 700 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 16500 N/m and mass 10.8 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 16500, m = 10.8 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(16500/10.8) | Answer: 6.221 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 3.9 m^2 and thickness 0.27 m has conductivity k = 47.8 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 70 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 3.9, L = 0.27, k = 47.8, dT = 70 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 47.8*3.9*70 / 0.27 | Answer: 48331 W

question: A surface of area 1.6 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 95 W/m^2-K to surroundings 140 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 1.6, h = 95, dT = 140 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 95*1.6*140 | Answer: 21280 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 220 m/min, feed = 0.26 mm/rev, depth of cut = 0.6 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 220, f = 0.26, d = 0.6 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*220*0.26*0.6 | Answer: 34320 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 340 mm is turned at 400 rpm with a feed of 0.14 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 340, N = 400, f = 0.14 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 340 / (0.14*400) | Answer: 6.071 min

question: A resistor of 101 ohm carries a current of 2.8 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 101, I = 2.8 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 2.8 * 101 | Answer: 282.8 V

question: Three resistors 59 ohm, 24 ohm and 9 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 59, R2 = 24, R3 = 9 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 59 + 24 + 9 | Answer: 92 ohm

question: Two resistors 119 ohm and 91 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 119, R2 = 91 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 119*91 / (119+91) | Answer: 51.57 ohm

question: A device draws 12.1 A at 60 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 60, I = 12.1 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 60 * 12.1 | Answer: 726 W

question: A current of 5.6 A flows through a 7 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 5.6, R = 7 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (5.6)^2 * 7 | Answer: 219.5 W

question: Two capacitors 6.9 uF and 28.9 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 6.9, C2 = 28.9 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 6.9*28.9 / (6.9+28.9) | Answer: 5.57 uF

question: A resistor 21 kohm and capacitor 15.9 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 21, C = 15.9 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (21k)(15.9u) = 333.9 ms | Answer: 333.9 ms

question: An inductor 147.8 mH is in series with 132 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 147.8, R = 132 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (147.8e-3) / 132 | Answer: 1.12 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 94.2 mH inductor at 470 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 94.2, f = 470 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (470)(94.2e-3) | Answer: 278.2 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 4.9 uF capacitor at 800 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 4.9, f = 800 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (800)(4.9e-6)) | Answer: 40.6 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 84 ohm, XL = 57 ohm and XC = 44 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 84, XL = 57, XC = 44 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(84^2 + (57 - 44)^2) | Answer: 85 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 47.5 mH and C = 8.6 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 47.5, C = 8.6 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(47.5e-3 * 8.6e-6)) | Answer: 249 Hz

question: A capacitor of 38.3 uF is charged to 70 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 38.3, V = 70 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*38.3e-6*(70)^2 | Answer: 93.83 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 440 V with 380 primary turns and 120 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 440, N1 = 380, N2 = 120 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 440 * 120/380 | Answer: 138.9 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 380 V and draws an armature current of 12 A. If the armature resistance is 0.81 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 380, Ia = 12, Ra = 0.81 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 380 - 12*0.81 | Answer: 370.3 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 145 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.85. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 145, VL = 400, pf = 0.85 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*400*145*0.85 / 1000 | Answer: 85.39 kW

question: A load has real power 45 kW and apparent power 205 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 45, S = 205 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 45 / 205 | Answer: 0.2195

question: A machine delivers 70 kW output while drawing 107 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 70, Pi = 107 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 70/107 * 100 | Answer: 65.42 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 21 V across R1 = 28 ohm and R2 = 43 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 21, R1 = 28, R2 = 43 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 21*43 / (28+43) | Answer: 12.72 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 210 kohm and Rin = 18 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 210, Rin = 18 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 210 / 18 | Answer: 11.67

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 120 kohm and Rg = 8 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 120, Rg = 8 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 120/8 | Answer: 16

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 2041. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 2041 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(2041) | Answer: 33.1 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.9 m carries a central point load of 120 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.9, W = 120 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 120*4.9 / 4 | Answer: 147 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.6 m carries a UDL of 15 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6.6, w = 15 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 15*(6.6)^2 / 8 | Answer: 81.67 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 4.3 m carries a point load 15 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.3, W = 15 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 15*4.3 | Answer: 64.5 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 1.3 m carries a UDL of 24 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 1.3, w = 24 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 24*(1.3)^2 / 2 | Answer: 20.28 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 7.2 m carries a point load 60 kN at distance 1.9 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 7.2, a = 1.9, W = 60 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 60*(7.2 - 1.9) / 7.2 | Answer: 44.17 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 6.4 m) carries a central point load 70 kN. With E = 200 GPa and I = 490e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=70000 N, L=6400.0 mm, E=200000 MPa, I=490e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 3.901 mm

question: An RC beam has overall depth 380 mm, clear cover 30 mm and main bars of diameter 16 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 380, c = 30, dia = 16 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 380 - 30 - 16/2 | Answer: 342 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 28.4 m^2 carrying a factored load of 15.4 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 28.4, w = 15.4 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 15.4 * 28.4 | Answer: 437.4 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 4.3 m, unit weight 18 kN/m^3, phi = 29 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 3.8e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.3, area = 3.9e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 3.8, i = 0.3, A = 3.9 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (3.8e-4)*0.3*(3.9e-3) | Answer: 444.6 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 2.3 m, bed slope 0.008 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.016. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 2.4 m under a head of 0.8 m. Taking Cd = 0.61 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 2.2 m wide carries a discharge of 26.8 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 470 m and design speed 95 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 470, V = 95 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (95)^2 / (127*470) | Answer: 0.1512
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: A tank of volume 140 m^3 treats a flow of 150 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 140, Q = 150 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 140 / 150 | Answer: 0.9333 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 210 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.3 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 3 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 210, k = 0.3, t = 3 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 210*(1 - e^(-0.3*3)) | Answer: 124.6 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.44, rainfall intensity 100 mm/h over a catchment of 8.5 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.44, i = 100, A = 8.5 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.44*100*8.5 / 360 | Answer: 1.039 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.05 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 380 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.05, M = 380 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 380*(30+0.05)/30 | Answer: 380.6 m

question: Convert the decimal number 177 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 177 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: B1 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 10010000 and 00011001.
solution: XOR: 10001001 | Count of 1s = 3 | Answer: 3
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 80 megabits is sent over a link of 23 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 80, B = 23 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 80 / 23 | Answer: 3.478 s

question: A link has bandwidth 12 Mbps and round-trip time 40 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 12, R = 40 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 12e6 * 40e-3 bits = 480 kb | Answer: 480 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.89, cache access time 9 ns and main-memory access time 170 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.89, tc = 9, tm = 170 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.89*9 + (1 - 0.89)*170 | Answer: 26.71 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 206794 elements?
solution: Given: n = 206794 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(206794)) + 1 | Answer: 18

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.005, memory access time 140 ns and page-fault service time 4 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 4 ms = 4000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.005)*140 + 0.005*4000000.0 ns | Answer: 20.14 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 1.5 m^3 at 480 kPa and 550 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 1.5, P = 480, Tk = 550 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (480e3)*1.5 / (8.314*550) | Answer: 157.5 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.26 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 5 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.26, t = 5 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.26*5) | Answer: 0.7275

question: For a reaction with A = 6e10 /s and activation energy 50 kJ/mol at 310 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 6, Ea = 50, Tk = 310 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 6e10 * exp(-50e3 / (8.314*310)) | Answer: 225.4 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.9 and bottoms xW = 0.03, with relative volatility alpha = 2. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.9, xw = 0.03, al = 2 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.9/0.1)(0.97/0.03)] / ln(2) | Answer: 8.185 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.73 and x = 0.39. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.73, x = 0.39 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.73/0.27) / (0.39/0.61) | Answer: 4.229

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.48 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 65 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.48, Psat = 65 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.48 * 65 | Answer: 31.2 kPa

question: A stream of 7.7 kg/s with specific heat 3.8 kJ/kg-K is heated through 50 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 7.7, cp = 3.8, dT = 50 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 7.7*3.8*50 | Answer: 1463 kW

question: A reactor of volume 4.2 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 1.8 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 4.2, Q = 1.8 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 4.2 / 1.8 | Answer: 2.333 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 8.5e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 1 mm with a concentration difference of 50 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 8.5, L = 1, dC = 50 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (8.5e-9)*50 / (1e-3) | Answer: 425 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 2.2 min and steady-state gain 0.9. For a step input of magnitude 20, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 2.2, K = 0.9, M = 20 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 0.9 * 20 | Answer: 18 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 35 m^2 flies at 150 m/s (air density 1.225 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.7. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 35, V = 150, rho = 1.225, CL = 0.7 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1.225*(150)^2*35*0.7 / 1000 | Answer: 337.6 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 100 m^2 flies at 90 m/s (density 1.225 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.1. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 100, V = 90, rho = 1.225, CD = 0.1 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*1.225*(90)^2*100*0.1 / 1000 | Answer: 49.61 kN

question: A specimen under stress 140 MPa shows an elastic strain of 3e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 140, eps = 3 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 140 / (3e-3) MPa = 46.67 GPa | Answer: 46.67 GPa

question: A block of mass 8 kg has a volume of 1.3e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 8, V = 1.3 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 8 / (1.3e-3) | Answer: 6154 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 800 mm is heated through 75 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 12e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 800, dT = 75, al = 12 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 800*12e-6*75 | Answer: 0.72 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 55 ohm, R2 = 135 ohm and R3 = 185 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 55, R2 = 135, R3 = 185 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 135*185 / 55 | Answer: 454.1 ohm

question: Annual demand is 31500 units, ordering cost 160 per order and holding cost 16 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 31500, S = 160, H = 16 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*31500*160 / 16) | Answer: 793.7 units

question: An asset costs 470000 with salvage value 20000 after 14 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 470000, Sv = 20000, n = 14 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (470000 - 20000) / 14 | Answer: 32143 per year

question: A product sells for 460 per unit with variable cost 60 per unit and fixed costs 120000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 460, V = 60, F = 120000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 120000 / (460 - 60) | Answer: 300 units

question: Find the present worth of 110000 received 7 years from now at an interest rate of 12% per year.
solution: Given: F = 110000, n = 7, i = 12 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 110000 / (1 + 0.12)^7 | Answer: 49758 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.96, 0.94 and 0.96 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.96, r2 = 0.94, r3 = 0.96 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.96*0.94*0.96 | Answer: 0.8663

question: A process produces 37 defective items in a batch of 14500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 37, N = 14500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 37/14500 * 1e6 | Answer: 2552 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -x^3 + 6x^2 + 6x evaluated at x = 0.
For f(x) = x^3 - 5x^2 - 7x - 6, find f''(x) at x = 0.
Evaluate the definite integral of (5x^2 - 3x - 3) dx from x = -4 to x = 5.

question: Find the larger real root of 5x^2 + 5x - 12 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[1, -3], [-2, -9]].
solution: Given: a = 1, b = -3, c = -2, d = -9 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (1)(-9) - (-3)(-2) | Answer: -15

solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: 241

solution: Trace tr = 4, Determinant = -30 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 7.831

question: Solve for x: 5x + 6y = -10 and 1x + 5y = -4.

question: Find the slope of the line through (6, 0) and (4, -4).
solution: Given: x1 = 6, y1 = 0, x2 = 4, y2 = -4 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (-4 - 0) / (4 - 6) | Answer: 2

question: Find the distance between the points (-6, 5) and (-7, 5).
solution: Given: x1 = -6, y1 = 5, x2 = -7, y2 = 5 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-1)^2 + (0)^2) | Answer: 1 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (5,-5), (6,3), (-5,4).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 44.5 sq units

question: Find the 13th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 2 and common difference 3.
solution: Given: a = 2, d = 3, n = 13 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = 2 + (13 - 1)*3 | Answer: 38

question: Find the sum of the first 12 terms of an AP with first term -4 and common difference -5.
solution: Given: a = -4, d = -5, n = 12 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 12/2 [2*-4 + (12-1)*-5] | Answer: -378

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 18500 at 13.3% per annum for 10 years.
solution: Given: P = 18500, R = 13.3, Tt = 10 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 18500 * 13.3 * 10 / 100 | Answer: 24605 currency units

question: Find the amount when 18500 is invested at 4.1% per annum compounded annually for 5 years.
solution: Given: P = 18500, R = 4.1, Tt = 5 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 18500 * (1 + 4.1/100)^5 | Answer: 22616 currency units

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (0, -1, 3) and (-4, -3, -6).

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number 9 + -7i.
solution: Given: a = 9, b = -7 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(-7, 9) | Answer: -37.87 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = x^3 - 2x^2 - 2x - 6 at x = 4.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-58 with initial guess x0=5, find x1 (one iteration).
solution: Given: N = 58, x0 = 5 | Formula: x1 = x0 - (x0^2 - N)/(2 x0) | Substitute: x1 = 5 - ((5)^2 - 58)/(2*5) | Answer: 8.3

question: Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.3 and ordinates 16, 2, 11, 10, 17, estimate the integral.

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 58 and 48.
