question: A circular rod of diameter 12 mm carries an axial tensile load of 109 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 25 mm and length 3000 mm carries an axial load of 68 kN. Take E = 210 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 62 mm transmits a torque of 1700 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 62, Tt = 1700 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(1700*1000) / (pi*(62)^3) | Answer: 36.33 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 34 mm and length 800 mm carries a torque of 1050 N-m. With G = 77 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (34)^4 / 32 = 131194 mm^4 | theta = (1050*1000)(800) / (77000 * 131194) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 4.764 degrees

question: A rectangular beam section is 33 mm wide and 110 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 33, h = 110 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 33*(110)^2 / 6 | Answer: 66550 mm^3

question: A component of ultimate strength 730 MPa is designed for a working stress of 180 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 730, sw = 180 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 730 / 180 | Answer: 4.056

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 400 mm and wall thickness 11 mm carries an internal pressure of 2.7 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 400, t = 11, P = 2.7 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 2.7*400 / (2*11) | Answer: 49.09 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 760 K and 410 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 760, Tc = 410 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 410/760) * 100 | Answer: 46.05 %

question: 6.4 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 135 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 6.4, dT = 135 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 6.4 * 0.718 * 135 | Answer: 620.4 kJ

question: 6.7 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 110 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 6.7, dT = 110 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 6.7 * 1.005 * 110 | Answer: 740.7 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 3.4 m^3 at 490 K with mass 4.9 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 3.4, Tk = 490, m = 4.9 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 4.9*0.287*490 / 3.4 | Answer: 202.7 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 2.6 kg of air expands isothermally at 460 K from volume V1 to 2*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.6, Tk = 460, ratio = 2 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 2.6*0.287*460*ln(2) | Answer: 237.9 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 4.1 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.35 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 4.1, D = 0.35 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*4.1*0.35 / 0.001 | Answer: 1435000

question: Water flows at 3.9 m/s through a pipe of diameter 200 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 1.5 m. Taking Cv = 0.99, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 1.5, cv = 0.99 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.99*sqrt(2*9.81*1.5) | Answer: 5.371 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 320 mm) water flows at 2 m/s. It contracts to diameter 140 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 320, d2 = 140, V1 = 2 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 2*(320/140)^2 | Answer: 10.45 m/s

question: Water flows at 3.9 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.11 m and length 430 m. With friction factor f = 0.02, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 17 teeth drives a gear of 62 teeth. If the pinion runs at 550 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 17, z2 = 62, N1 = 550 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 550*17 / 62 | Answer: 150.8 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 540 mm rotates at 1500 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 540, N = 1500 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.54)*1500 / 60 | Answer: 42.41 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 48.9 kW at 1400 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 48.9, N = 1400 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(48.9*1000) / (2*pi*1400) | Answer: 333.5 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 7.3 kg rotates at radius 0.26 m at 600 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 19900 N/m and mass 7.4 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 19900, m = 7.4 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(19900/7.4) | Answer: 8.253 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 3 m^2 and thickness 0.13 m has conductivity k = 34.8 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 145 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 3, L = 0.13, k = 34.8, dT = 145 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 34.8*3*145 / 0.13 | Answer: 116446 W

question: A surface of area 3.3 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 200 W/m^2-K to surroundings 45 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 3.3, h = 200, dT = 45 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 200*3.3*45 | Answer: 29700 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 110 m/min, feed = 0.26 mm/rev, depth of cut = 1.2 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 110, f = 0.26, d = 1.2 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*110*0.26*1.2 | Answer: 34320 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 240 mm is turned at 800 rpm with a feed of 0.24 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 240, N = 800, f = 0.24 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 240 / (0.24*800) | Answer: 1.25 min

question: A resistor of 26 ohm carries a current of 9.9 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 26, I = 9.9 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 9.9 * 26 | Answer: 257.4 V

question: Three resistors 30 ohm, 49 ohm and 25 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 30, R2 = 49, R3 = 25 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 30 + 49 + 25 | Answer: 104 ohm

question: Two resistors 32 ohm and 77 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 32, R2 = 77 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 32*77 / (32+77) | Answer: 22.61 ohm

question: A device draws 5.7 A at 150 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 150, I = 5.7 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 150 * 5.7 | Answer: 855 W

question: A current of 5.1 A flows through a 107 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 5.1, R = 107 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (5.1)^2 * 107 | Answer: 2783 W

question: Two capacitors 16.3 uF and 12.3 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 16.3, C2 = 12.3 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 16.3*12.3 / (16.3+12.3) | Answer: 7.01 uF

question: A resistor 42 kohm and capacitor 2.8 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 42, C = 2.8 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (42k)(2.8u) = 117.6 ms | Answer: 117.6 ms

question: An inductor 386 mH is in series with 147 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 386, R = 147 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (386e-3) / 147 | Answer: 2.626 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 176.9 mH inductor at 150 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 176.9, f = 150 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (150)(176.9e-3) | Answer: 166.7 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 22.9 uF capacitor at 370 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 22.9, f = 370 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (370)(22.9e-6)) | Answer: 18.78 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 69 ohm, XL = 140 ohm and XC = 63 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 69, XL = 140, XC = 63 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(69^2 + (140 - 63)^2) | Answer: 103.4 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 91.7 mH and C = 6.7 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 91.7, C = 6.7 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(91.7e-3 * 6.7e-6)) | Answer: 203 Hz

question: A capacitor of 31.7 uF is charged to 400 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 31.7, V = 400 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*31.7e-6*(400)^2 | Answer: 2536 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 180 V with 570 primary turns and 140 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 180, N1 = 570, N2 = 140 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 180 * 140/570 | Answer: 44.21 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 290 V and draws an armature current of 35 A. If the armature resistance is 0.31 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 290, Ia = 35, Ra = 0.31 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 290 - 35*0.31 | Answer: 279.1 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 190 A at 415 V (line) with a power factor of 0.78. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 190, VL = 415, pf = 0.78 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*415*190*0.78 / 1000 | Answer: 106.5 kW

question: A load has real power 110 kW and apparent power 155 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 110, S = 155 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 110 / 155 | Answer: 0.7097

question: A machine delivers 30 kW output while drawing 212 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 30, Pi = 212 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 30/212 * 100 | Answer: 14.15 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 12 V across R1 = 29 ohm and R2 = 12 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 12, R1 = 29, R2 = 12 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 12*12 / (29+12) | Answer: 3.512 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 90 kohm and Rin = 39 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 90, Rin = 39 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 90 / 39 | Answer: 2.308

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 200 kohm and Rg = 3 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 200, Rg = 3 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 200/3 | Answer: 67.67

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 2548. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 2548 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(2548) | Answer: 34.06 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.6 m carries a central point load of 30 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.6, W = 30 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 30*4.6 / 4 | Answer: 34.5 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 5 m carries a UDL of 25 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5, w = 25 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 25*(5)^2 / 8 | Answer: 78.12 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 5.5 m carries a point load 60 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.5, W = 60 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 60*5.5 | Answer: 330 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 5.5 m carries a UDL of 20 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.5, w = 20 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 20*(5.5)^2 / 2 | Answer: 302.5 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 5.8 m carries a point load 95 kN at distance 2 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 5.8, a = 2, W = 95 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 95*(5.8 - 2) / 5.8 | Answer: 62.24 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 4.5 m) carries a central point load 75 kN. With E = 25 GPa and I = 330e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=75000 N, L=4500.0 mm, E=25000 MPa, I=330e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 17.26 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 8.8 m carries a UDL of 6 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 8.8, w = 6 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 6*(8.8)^2 / 12 | Answer: 38.72 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 680 mm, clear cover 30 mm and main bars of diameter 25 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 680, c = 30, dia = 25 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 680 - 30 - 25/2 | Answer: 637.5 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 37.8 m^2 carrying a factored load of 12.4 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 37.8, w = 12.4 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 12.4 * 37.8 | Answer: 468.7 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 5.6 m, unit weight 18 kN/m^3, phi = 37 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 3.4e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.2, area = 7.6e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 3.4, i = 0.2, A = 7.6 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (3.4e-4)*0.2*(7.6e-3) | Answer: 516.8 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 2 m, bed slope 0.01 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.013. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 4.3 m under a head of 0.7 m. Taking Cd = 0.62 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 2.8 m wide carries a discharge of 12 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 600 m and design speed 75 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 600, V = 75 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (75)^2 / (127*600) | Answer: 0.07382
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: A tank of volume 520 m^3 treats a flow of 185 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 520, Q = 185 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 520 / 185 | Answer: 2.811 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 380 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.12 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 7 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 380, k = 0.12, t = 7 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 380*(1 - e^(-0.12*7)) | Answer: 216 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.31, rainfall intensity 30 mm/h over a catchment of 40.3 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.31, i = 30, A = 40.3 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.31*30*40.3 / 360 | Answer: 1.041 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.08 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 230 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.08, M = 230 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 230*(20+0.08)/20 | Answer: 230.9 m

question: Convert the decimal number 3128 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 3128 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: C38 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 01101011 and 00010000.
solution: XOR: 01111011 | Count of 1s = 6 | Answer: 6
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 960 megabits is sent over a link of 17 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 960, B = 17 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 960 / 17 | Answer: 56.47 s

question: A link has bandwidth 12 Mbps and round-trip time 50 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 12, R = 50 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 12e6 * 50e-3 bits = 600 kb | Answer: 600 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.9, cache access time 6 ns and main-memory access time 130 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.9, tc = 6, tm = 130 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.9*6 + (1 - 0.9)*130 | Answer: 18.4 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 111503 elements?
solution: Given: n = 111503 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(111503)) + 1 | Answer: 17

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.003, memory access time 150 ns and page-fault service time 9 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 9 ms = 9000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.003)*150 + 0.003*9000000.0 ns | Answer: 27.15 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 0.9 m^3 at 280 kPa and 330 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 0.9, P = 280, Tk = 330 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (280e3)*0.9 / (8.314*330) | Answer: 91.85 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.08 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 2 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.08, t = 2 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.08*2) | Answer: 0.1479

question: For a reaction with A = 2e10 /s and activation energy 90 kJ/mol at 420 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 2, Ea = 90, Tk = 420 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 2e10 * exp(-90e3 / (8.314*420)) | Answer: 0.1281 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.98 and bottoms xW = 0.03, with relative volatility alpha = 1.7. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.98, xw = 0.03, al = 1.7 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.98/0.02)(0.97/0.03)] / ln(1.7) | Answer: 13.89 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.72 and x = 0.42. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.72, x = 0.42 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.72/0.28) / (0.42/0.58) | Answer: 3.551

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.25 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 85 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.25, Psat = 85 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.25 * 85 | Answer: 21.25 kPa

question: A stream of 5 kg/s with specific heat 1.7 kJ/kg-K is heated through 25 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 5, cp = 1.7, dT = 25 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 5*1.7*25 | Answer: 212.5 kW

question: A reactor of volume 9.8 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 3.8 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 9.8, Q = 3.8 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 9.8 / 3.8 | Answer: 2.579 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 6.7e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 4 mm with a concentration difference of 70 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 6.7, L = 4, dC = 70 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (6.7e-9)*70 / (4e-3) | Answer: 117.2 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 5 min and steady-state gain 3. For a step input of magnitude 12, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 5, K = 3, M = 12 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 3 * 12 | Answer: 36 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 25 m^2 flies at 160 m/s (air density 0.4 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 1. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 25, V = 160, rho = 0.4, CL = 1 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.4*(160)^2*25*1 / 1000 | Answer: 128 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 70 m^2 flies at 100 m/s (density 1.225 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.08. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 70, V = 100, rho = 1.225, CD = 0.08 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*1.225*(100)^2*70*0.08 / 1000 | Answer: 34.3 kN

question: A specimen under stress 390 MPa shows an elastic strain of 2.6e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 390, eps = 2.6 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 390 / (2.6e-3) MPa = 150 GPa | Answer: 150 GPa

question: A block of mass 19 kg has a volume of 0.8e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 19, V = 0.8 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 19 / (0.8e-3) | Answer: 23750 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 3000 mm is heated through 90 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 12e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 3000, dT = 90, al = 12 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 3000*12e-6*90 | Answer: 3.24 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 110 ohm, R2 = 170 ohm and R3 = 140 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 110, R2 = 170, R3 = 140 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 170*140 / 110 | Answer: 216.4 ohm

question: A measurement reads 9.4 when the true value is 20. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.4, true = 20 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.4 - 20| / 20 * 100 | Answer: 53 %

question: Annual demand is 12000 units, ordering cost 110 per order and holding cost 23 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 12000, S = 110, H = 23 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*12000*110 / 23) | Answer: 338.8 units

question: An asset costs 50000 with salvage value 24000 after 16 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 50000, Sv = 24000, n = 16 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (50000 - 24000) / 16 | Answer: 1625 per year

question: A product sells for 350 per unit with variable cost 140 per unit and fixed costs 35000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 350, V = 140, F = 35000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 35000 / (350 - 140) | Answer: 166.7 units

question: Find the present worth of 75000 received 2 years from now at an interest rate of 10% per year.
solution: Given: F = 75000, n = 2, i = 10 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 75000 / (1 + 0.1)^2 | Answer: 61983 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.91, 0.95 and 0.96 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.91, r2 = 0.95, r3 = 0.96 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.91*0.95*0.96 | Answer: 0.8299

question: A process produces 50 defective items in a batch of 13500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 50, N = 13500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 50/13500 * 1e6 | Answer: 3704 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = 3x^3 - 6x^2 + 5x + 8 evaluated at x = 4.
For f(x) = -2x^3 - 3x^2 - 8x - 2, find f''(x) at x = 5.
Evaluate the definite integral of (x^2 - x + 7) dx from x = 2 to x = 7.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = 1x^3/3 + -1x^2/2 + 7x | Evaluate F(7) - F(2) | Answer: 124.2
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 2x^2 + 11x - 3 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[-3, -7], [5, 4]].
solution: Given: a = -3, b = -7, c = 5, d = 4 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (-3)(4) - (-7)(5) | Answer: 23

question: Find the determinant of [[2, 6, -5], [1, -3, 5], [-2, 2, -6]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: 12

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[4, 7], [7, 6]].
solution: Trace tr = 10, Determinant = -25 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 12.07

question: Solve for x: 5x + -2y = -9 and -3x + 1y = 4.
solution: Determinant = 5*1 - -2*-3 = -1 | x = (e d - b f) / det = 1 | Answer: x = 1
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 31, 55, 61, 11, 40.
solution: Sum = 198 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 39.6 | Answer: 39.6

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 11, 33, 39, 12, 46.
solution: Mean = 28.2 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 15.93

question: Find the slope of the line through (-5, 5) and (-7, -6).
solution: Given: x1 = -5, y1 = 5, x2 = -7, y2 = -6 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (-6 - 5) / (-7 - -5) | Answer: 5.5

question: Find the distance between the points (-2, -4) and (-5, 0).
solution: Given: x1 = -2, y1 = -4, x2 = -5, y2 = 0 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-3)^2 + (4)^2) | Answer: 5 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (4,2), (-8,7), (-4,-4).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 56 sq units

question: Find the 7th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 11 and common difference -2.
solution: Given: a = 11, d = -2, n = 7 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = 11 + (7 - 1)*-2 | Answer: -1

question: Find the sum of the first 20 terms of an AP with first term -3 and common difference -6.
solution: Given: a = -3, d = -6, n = 20 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 20/2 [2*-3 + (20-1)*-6] | Answer: -1200

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 17500 at 12.2% per annum for 8 years.
solution: Given: P = 17500, R = 12.2, Tt = 8 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 17500 * 12.2 * 8 / 100 | Answer: 17080 currency units

question: Find the amount when 35500 is invested at 7.4% per annum compounded annually for 5 years.
solution: Given: P = 35500, R = 7.4, Tt = 5 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 35500 * (1 + 7.4/100)^5 | Answer: 50728 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (4, 4, 4) and (-4, 7, -4).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (-3, -6, 2) and (-1, 3, 5).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 41.11

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (4, 3, 5) and (1, 6, 0).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 59.24 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -3x^3 - x^2 + 2x - 7 at x = 3.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-140 with initial guess x0=12, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.9 and ordinates 20, 2, 1, 8, 4, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 15 and 118.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 15 and 118 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 63 and 74.
solution: Given: a = 63, b = 74 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 63*74 / 1 | Answer: 4662
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 48 mm carries an axial tensile load of 33 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 36 mm and length 2800 mm carries an axial load of 76 kN. Take E = 200 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 20 mm transmits a torque of 900 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 20, Tt = 900 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(900*1000) / (pi*(20)^3) | Answer: 573 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 58 mm and length 1500 mm carries a torque of 1250 N-m. With G = 77 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (58)^4 / 32 = 1110994 mm^4 | theta = (1250*1000)(1500) / (77000 * 1110994) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 1.256 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 117 mm wide and 250 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 117, h = 250 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 117*(250)^2 / 6 | Answer: 1218750 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (91 mm x 120 mm) carries a bending moment of 17 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (32 mm x 140 mm) has effective length 1700 mm and E = 200 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 450 MPa is designed for a working stress of 220 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 450, sw = 220 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 450 / 220 | Answer: 2.045

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1500 mm and wall thickness 18 mm carries an internal pressure of 2 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1500, t = 18, P = 2 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 2*1500 / (2*18) | Answer: 83.33 MPa

question: 3.9 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 175 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.9, dT = 175 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 3.9 * 0.718 * 175 | Answer: 490 kJ

question: 2.4 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 75 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.4, dT = 75 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 2.4 * 1.005 * 75 | Answer: 180.9 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 3.6 m^3 at 370 K with mass 4.9 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 3.6, Tk = 370, m = 4.9 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 4.9*0.287*370 / 3.6 | Answer: 144.5 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 1.5 kg of air expands isothermally at 320 K from volume V1 to 2*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1.5, Tk = 320, ratio = 2 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 1.5*0.287*320*ln(2) | Answer: 95.49 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 1.4 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.14 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 1.4, D = 0.14 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*1.4*0.14 / 0.001 | Answer: 196000

question: Water flows at 2.9 m/s through a pipe of diameter 190 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 18 m. Taking Cv = 0.97, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 18, cv = 0.97 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.97*sqrt(2*9.81*18) | Answer: 18.23 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 360 mm) water flows at 2.9 m/s. It contracts to diameter 120 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 360, d2 = 120, V1 = 2.9 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 2.9*(360/120)^2 | Answer: 26.1 m/s

question: Water flows at 2.8 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.19 m and length 480 m. With friction factor f = 0.027, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 32 teeth drives a gear of 82 teeth. If the pinion runs at 400 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 32, z2 = 82, N1 = 400 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 400*32 / 82 | Answer: 156.1 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 550 mm rotates at 400 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 550, N = 400 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.55)*400 / 60 | Answer: 11.52 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 26 kW at 850 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 26, N = 850 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(26*1000) / (2*pi*850) | Answer: 292.1 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 7.8 kg rotates at radius 0.13 m at 1000 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 14600 N/m and mass 9.7 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 14600, m = 9.7 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(14600/9.7) | Answer: 6.175 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 3.2 m^2 and thickness 0.1 m has conductivity k = 8.4 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 110 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 3.2, L = 0.1, k = 8.4, dT = 110 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 8.4*3.2*110 / 0.1 | Answer: 29568 W

question: A surface of area 0.7 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 170 W/m^2-K to surroundings 140 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 0.7, h = 170, dT = 140 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 170*0.7*140 | Answer: 16660 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 180 m/min, feed = 0.28 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2.9 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 180, f = 0.28, d = 2.9 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*180*0.28*2.9 | Answer: 146160 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 230 mm is turned at 200 rpm with a feed of 0.11 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 230, N = 200, f = 0.11 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 230 / (0.11*200) | Answer: 10.45 min

question: A resistor of 176 ohm carries a current of 1.8 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 176, I = 1.8 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 1.8 * 176 | Answer: 316.8 V

question: Three resistors 99 ohm, 59 ohm and 17 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 99, R2 = 59, R3 = 17 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 99 + 59 + 17 | Answer: 175 ohm

question: Two resistors 38 ohm and 111 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 38, R2 = 111 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 38*111 / (38+111) | Answer: 28.31 ohm

question: A device draws 9.1 A at 210 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 210, I = 9.1 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 210 * 9.1 | Answer: 1911 W

question: A current of 3.6 A flows through a 85 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 3.6, R = 85 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (3.6)^2 * 85 | Answer: 1102 W

question: Two capacitors 11.1 uF and 43 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 11.1, C2 = 43 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 11.1*43 / (11.1+43) | Answer: 8.823 uF

question: A resistor 38 kohm and capacitor 17.9 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 38, C = 17.9 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (38k)(17.9u) = 680.2 ms | Answer: 680.2 ms

question: An inductor 310.3 mH is in series with 154 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 310.3, R = 154 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (310.3e-3) / 154 | Answer: 2.015 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 129.5 mH inductor at 310 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 129.5, f = 310 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (310)(129.5e-3) | Answer: 252.2 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 21.7 uF capacitor at 630 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 21.7, f = 630 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (630)(21.7e-6)) | Answer: 11.64 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 87 ohm, XL = 136 ohm and XC = 76 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 87, XL = 136, XC = 76 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(87^2 + (136 - 76)^2) | Answer: 105.7 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 96.7 mH and C = 5.3 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 96.7, C = 5.3 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(96.7e-3 * 5.3e-6)) | Answer: 222.3 Hz

question: A capacitor of 54.1 uF is charged to 20 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 54.1, V = 20 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*54.1e-6*(20)^2 | Answer: 10.82 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 170 V with 220 primary turns and 180 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 170, N1 = 220, N2 = 180 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 170 * 180/220 | Answer: 139.1 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 210 V and draws an armature current of 17 A. If the armature resistance is 1.16 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 210, Ia = 17, Ra = 1.16 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 210 - 17*1.16 | Answer: 190.3 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 135 A at 415 V (line) with a power factor of 0.86. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 135, VL = 415, pf = 0.86 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*415*135*0.86 / 1000 | Answer: 83.45 kW

question: A load has real power 35 kW and apparent power 120 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 35, S = 120 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 35 / 120 | Answer: 0.2917

question: A machine delivers 35 kW output while drawing 107 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 35, Pi = 107 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 35/107 * 100 | Answer: 32.71 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 29 V across R1 = 42 ohm and R2 = 27 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 29, R1 = 42, R2 = 27 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 29*27 / (42+27) | Answer: 11.35 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 170 kohm and Rin = 38 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 170, Rin = 38 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 170 / 38 | Answer: 4.474

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 170 kohm and Rg = 8 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 170, Rg = 8 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 170/8 | Answer: 22.25

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 784. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 784 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(784) | Answer: 28.94 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 4 m carries a central point load of 10 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4, W = 10 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 10*4 / 4 | Answer: 10 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 3.4 m carries a UDL of 55 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.4, w = 55 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 55*(3.4)^2 / 8 | Answer: 79.47 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 2.2 m carries a point load 80 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 2.2, W = 80 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 80*2.2 | Answer: 176 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 4.2 m carries a UDL of 8 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.2, w = 8 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 8*(4.2)^2 / 2 | Answer: 70.56 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.2 m carries a point load 75 kN at distance 1.4 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 6.2, a = 1.4, W = 75 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 75*(6.2 - 1.4) / 6.2 | Answer: 58.06 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 4.1 m) carries a central point load 65 kN. With E = 25 GPa and I = 450e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=65000 N, L=4100.0 mm, E=25000 MPa, I=450e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 8.296 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 6.8 m carries a UDL of 33 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6.8, w = 33 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 33*(6.8)^2 / 12 | Answer: 127.2 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 390 mm, clear cover 45 mm and main bars of diameter 25 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 390, c = 45, dia = 25 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 390 - 45 - 25/2 | Answer: 332.5 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 14.3 m^2 carrying a factored load of 13.5 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 14.3, w = 13.5 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 13.5 * 14.3 | Answer: 193.1 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 5.4 m, unit weight 19 kN/m^3, phi = 34 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 4.3e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1.4, area = 4.6e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 4.3, i = 1.4, A = 4.6 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (4.3e-4)*1.4*(4.6e-3) | Answer: 2769 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.5 m, bed slope 0.007 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.022. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 1 m under a head of 0.5 m. Taking Cd = 0.6 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 4.9 m wide carries a discharge of 6.7 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 290 m and design speed 40 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 290, V = 40 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (40)^2 / (127*290) | Answer: 0.04344
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: A tank of volume 300 m^3 treats a flow of 150 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 300, Q = 150 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 300 / 150 | Answer: 2 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 160 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.11 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 5 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 160, k = 0.11, t = 5 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 160*(1 - e^(-0.11*5)) | Answer: 67.69 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.49, rainfall intensity 80 mm/h over a catchment of 16 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.49, i = 80, A = 16 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.49*80*16 / 360 | Answer: 1.742 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.03 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 430 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.03, M = 430 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 430*(30+0.03)/30 | Answer: 430.4 m

question: Convert the decimal number 83 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 83 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 53 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 00000000 and 11110101.
solution: XOR: 11110101 | Count of 1s = 6 | Answer: 6
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 430 megabits is sent over a link of 50 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 430, B = 50 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 430 / 50 | Answer: 8.6 s

question: A link has bandwidth 74 Mbps and round-trip time 150 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 74, R = 150 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 74e6 * 150e-3 bits = 11100 kb | Answer: 11100 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.9, cache access time 1 ns and main-memory access time 150 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.9, tc = 1, tm = 150 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.9*1 + (1 - 0.9)*150 | Answer: 15.9 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 582611 elements?
solution: Given: n = 582611 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(582611)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.003, memory access time 90 ns and page-fault service time 7 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 7 ms = 7000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.003)*90 + 0.003*7000000.0 ns | Answer: 21.09 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 1.9 m^3 at 210 kPa and 540 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 1.9, P = 210, Tk = 540 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (210e3)*1.9 / (8.314*540) | Answer: 88.87 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.2 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 5 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.2, t = 5 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.2*5) | Answer: 0.6321

question: For a reaction with A = 6e10 /s and activation energy 90 kJ/mol at 320 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 6, Ea = 90, Tk = 320 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 6e10 * exp(-90e3 / (8.314*320)) | Answer: 0.0001221 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.92 and bottoms xW = 0.04, with relative volatility alpha = 2.4. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.92, xw = 0.04, al = 2.4 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.92/0.08)(0.96/0.04)] / ln(2.4) | Answer: 6.42 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.8 and x = 0.46. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.8, x = 0.46 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.8/0.2) / (0.46/0.54) | Answer: 4.696

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.15 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 55 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.15, Psat = 55 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.15 * 55 | Answer: 8.25 kPa

question: A stream of 1.5 kg/s with specific heat 1.8 kJ/kg-K is heated through 55 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 1.5, cp = 1.8, dT = 55 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 1.5*1.8*55 | Answer: 148.5 kW

question: A reactor of volume 1.9 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 3.7 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 1.9, Q = 3.7 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 1.9 / 3.7 | Answer: 0.5135 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 2.3e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 5 mm with a concentration difference of 10 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 2.3, L = 5, dC = 10 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (2.3e-9)*10 / (5e-3) | Answer: 4.6 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 7.2 min and steady-state gain 3.1. For a step input of magnitude 18, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 7.2, K = 3.1, M = 18 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 3.1 * 18 | Answer: 55.8 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 70 m^2 flies at 150 m/s (air density 1.225 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 1.3. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 70, V = 150, rho = 1.225, CL = 1.3 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1.225*(150)^2*70*1.3 / 1000 | Answer: 1254 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 120 m^2 flies at 260 m/s (density 0.7 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.07. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 120, V = 260, rho = 0.7, CD = 0.07 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.7*(260)^2*120*0.07 / 1000 | Answer: 198.7 kN

question: A specimen under stress 190 MPa shows an elastic strain of 2.2e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 190, eps = 2.2 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 190 / (2.2e-3) MPa = 86.36 GPa | Answer: 86.36 GPa

question: A block of mass 3 kg has a volume of 5.1e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 3, V = 5.1 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 3 / (5.1e-3) | Answer: 588.2 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 2600 mm is heated through 60 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 11e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 2600, dT = 60, al = 11 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 2600*11e-6*60 | Answer: 1.716 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 70 ohm, R2 = 135 ohm and R3 = 55 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 70, R2 = 135, R3 = 55 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 135*55 / 70 | Answer: 106.1 ohm

question: A measurement reads 10.82 when the true value is 50. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10.82, true = 50 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10.82 - 50| / 50 * 100 | Answer: 78.36 %

question: Annual demand is 40000 units, ordering cost 80 per order and holding cost 10 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 40000, S = 80, H = 10 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*40000*80 / 10) | Answer: 800 units

question: An asset costs 350000 with salvage value 2000 after 9 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 350000, Sv = 2000, n = 9 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (350000 - 2000) / 9 | Answer: 38667 per year

question: A product sells for 170 per unit with variable cost 130 per unit and fixed costs 25000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 170, V = 130, F = 25000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 25000 / (170 - 130) | Answer: 625 units

question: Find the present worth of 130000 received 7 years from now at an interest rate of 12% per year.
solution: Given: F = 130000, n = 7, i = 12 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 130000 / (1 + 0.12)^7 | Answer: 58805 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.96, 0.98 and 0.92 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.96, r2 = 0.98, r3 = 0.92 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.96*0.98*0.92 | Answer: 0.8655

question: A process produces 45 defective items in a batch of 11500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 45, N = 11500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 45/11500 * 1e6 | Answer: 3913 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = x^3 - 3x^2 + 5x + 5 evaluated at x = 3.
For f(x) = -3x^3 + 2x^2 + 8x - 6, find f''(x) at x = 2.
Evaluate the definite integral of (x^2 + 6x - 5) dx from x = -1 to x = 5.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = 1x^3/3 + 6x^2/2 + -5x | Evaluate F(5) - F(-1) | Answer: 84
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of x^2 - 10x - 7 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[-9, 1], [-3, -1]].
solution: Given: a = -9, b = 1, c = -3, d = -1 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (-9)(-1) - (1)(-3) | Answer: 12

question: Find the determinant of [[5, -6, -5], [-4, 5, 0], [-4, -4, 1]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: -179

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[7, 4], [4, 3]].
solution: Trace tr = 10, Determinant = 5 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 9.472

question: Solve for x: -1x + -4y = 12 and 0x + -3y = 7.
solution: Determinant = -1*-3 - -4*0 = 3 | x = (e d - b f) / det = -2.667 | Answer: x = -2.667
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 69, 79, 39, 34, 50.
solution: Sum = 271 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 54.2 | Answer: 54.2

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 23, 2, 26, 40, 4.
solution: Mean = 19 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 15.97

question: Find the slope of the line through (5, -1) and (-8, 8).
solution: Given: x1 = 5, y1 = -1, x2 = -8, y2 = 8 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (8 - -1) / (-8 - 5) | Answer: -0.6923

question: Find the distance between the points (9, 0) and (-4, -1).
solution: Given: x1 = 9, y1 = 0, x2 = -4, y2 = -1 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-13)^2 + (-1)^2) | Answer: 13.04 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (2,7), (8,1), (4,1).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 12 sq units

question: Find the 37th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 10 and common difference 9.
solution: Given: a = 10, d = 9, n = 37 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = 10 + (37 - 1)*9 | Answer: 334

question: Find the sum of the first 23 terms of an AP with first term 7 and common difference -3.
solution: Given: a = 7, d = -3, n = 23 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 23/2 [2*7 + (23-1)*-3] | Answer: -598

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 34500 at 11.3% per annum for 1 years.
solution: Given: P = 34500, R = 11.3, Tt = 1 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 34500 * 11.3 * 1 / 100 | Answer: 3898 currency units

question: Find the amount when 38000 is invested at 4.6% per annum compounded annually for 3 years.
solution: Given: P = 38000, R = 4.6, Tt = 3 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 38000 * (1 + 4.6/100)^3 | Answer: 43489 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (-6, 2, -8) and (-3, 3, -7).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (1, 3, 4) and (-2, 2, 0).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 13.86

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (5, -5, 0) and (-2, 0, -4).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 108.4 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = 5x^3 - 3x^2 - 7x - 8 at x = 5.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-115 with initial guess x0=12, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.8 and ordinates 15, 14, 4, 17, 16, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 372 and 543.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 372 and 543 | Answer: GCD = 3

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 10 and 25.
solution: Given: a = 10, b = 25 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 10*25 / 5 | Answer: 50
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 55 mm carries an axial tensile load of 94 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 27 mm and length 1900 mm carries an axial load of 67 kN. Take E = 70 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 59 mm transmits a torque of 1900 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 59, Tt = 1900 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(1900*1000) / (pi*(59)^3) | Answer: 47.12 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 30 mm and length 1500 mm carries a torque of 750 N-m. With G = 77 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (30)^4 / 32 = 79522 mm^4 | theta = (750*1000)(1500) / (77000 * 79522) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 10.53 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 143 mm wide and 280 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 143, h = 280 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 143*(280)^2 / 6 | Answer: 1868533 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (61 mm x 180 mm) carries a bending moment of 24 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (49 mm x 130 mm) has effective length 2700 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 740 MPa is designed for a working stress of 80 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 740, sw = 80 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 740 / 80 | Answer: 9.25

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1050 mm and wall thickness 18 mm carries an internal pressure of 2.6 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1050, t = 18, P = 2.6 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 2.6*1050 / (2*18) | Answer: 75.83 MPa

question: 2 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 60 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2, dT = 60 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 2 * 0.718 * 60 | Answer: 86.16 kJ

question: 6.2 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 130 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 6.2, dT = 130 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 6.2 * 1.005 * 130 | Answer: 810 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 2.4 m^3 at 580 K with mass 4.6 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 2.4, Tk = 580, m = 4.6 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 4.6*0.287*580 / 2.4 | Answer: 319 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 4.7 kg of air expands isothermally at 420 K from volume V1 to 2*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.7, Tk = 420, ratio = 2 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 4.7*0.287*420*ln(2) | Answer: 392.7 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 4.1 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.15 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 4.1, D = 0.15 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*4.1*0.15 / 0.001 | Answer: 615000

question: Water flows at 2.6 m/s through a pipe of diameter 270 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 19.2 m. Taking Cv = 0.96, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 19.2, cv = 0.96 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.96*sqrt(2*9.81*19.2) | Answer: 18.63 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 340 mm) water flows at 2.8 m/s. It contracts to diameter 100 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
Water flows at 3.2 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.49 m and length 100 m. With friction factor f = 0.04, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 23 teeth drives a gear of 63 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1000 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 23, z2 = 63, N1 = 1000 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1000*23 / 63 | Answer: 365.1 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 530 mm rotates at 1350 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 530, N = 1350 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.53)*1350 / 60 | Answer: 37.46 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 45.3 kW at 700 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 45.3, N = 700 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(45.3*1000) / (2*pi*700) | Answer: 618 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 2.1 kg rotates at radius 0.53 m at 1100 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 4400 N/m and mass 14 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 4400, m = 14 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(4400/14) | Answer: 2.822 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 1.1 m^2 and thickness 0.12 m has conductivity k = 35 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 170 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 1.1, L = 0.12, k = 35, dT = 170 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 35*1.1*170 / 0.12 | Answer: 54542 W

question: A surface of area 5.9 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 100 W/m^2-K to surroundings 115 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 5.9, h = 100, dT = 115 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 100*5.9*115 | Answer: 67850 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 210 m/min, feed = 0.47 mm/rev, depth of cut = 1.6 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 210, f = 0.47, d = 1.6 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*210*0.47*1.6 | Answer: 157920 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 210 mm is turned at 1200 rpm with a feed of 0.25 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 210, N = 1200, f = 0.25 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 210 / (0.25*1200) | Answer: 0.7 min

question: A resistor of 52 ohm carries a current of 4.8 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 52, I = 4.8 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 4.8 * 52 | Answer: 249.6 V

question: Three resistors 88 ohm, 64 ohm and 10 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 88, R2 = 64, R3 = 10 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 88 + 64 + 10 | Answer: 162 ohm

question: Two resistors 44 ohm and 2 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 44, R2 = 2 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 44*2 / (44+2) | Answer: 1.913 ohm

question: A device draws 7.8 A at 65 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 65, I = 7.8 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 65 * 7.8 | Answer: 507 W

question: A current of 7.4 A flows through a 86 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 7.4, R = 86 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (7.4)^2 * 86 | Answer: 4709 W

question: Two capacitors 30.1 uF and 12.7 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 30.1, C2 = 12.7 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 30.1*12.7 / (30.1+12.7) | Answer: 8.932 uF

question: A resistor 49 kohm and capacitor 11.7 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 49, C = 11.7 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (49k)(11.7u) = 573.3 ms | Answer: 573.3 ms

question: An inductor 368.6 mH is in series with 66 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 368.6, R = 66 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (368.6e-3) / 66 | Answer: 5.585 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 16.6 mH inductor at 110 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 16.6, f = 110 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (110)(16.6e-3) | Answer: 11.47 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 6.1 uF capacitor at 60 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 6.1, f = 60 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (60)(6.1e-6)) | Answer: 434.8 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 32 ohm, XL = 104 ohm and XC = 20 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 32, XL = 104, XC = 20 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(32^2 + (104 - 20)^2) | Answer: 89.89 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 5.8 mH and C = 9.3 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 5.8, C = 9.3 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(5.8e-3 * 9.3e-6)) | Answer: 685.3 Hz

question: A capacitor of 50.7 uF is charged to 345 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 50.7, V = 345 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*50.7e-6*(345)^2 | Answer: 3017 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 410 V with 970 primary turns and 150 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 410, N1 = 970, N2 = 150 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 410 * 150/970 | Answer: 63.4 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 130 V and draws an armature current of 18 A. If the armature resistance is 0.5 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 130, Ia = 18, Ra = 0.5 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 130 - 18*0.5 | Answer: 121 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 85 A at 433 V (line) with a power factor of 0.76. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 85, VL = 433, pf = 0.76 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*433*85*0.76 / 1000 | Answer: 48.45 kW

question: A load has real power 145 kW and apparent power 145 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 145, S = 145 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 145 / 145 | Answer: 1

question: A machine delivers 160 kW output while drawing 177 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 160, Pi = 177 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 160/177 * 100 | Answer: 90.4 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 20 V across R1 = 3 ohm and R2 = 23 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 20, R1 = 3, R2 = 23 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 20*23 / (3+23) | Answer: 17.69 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 70 kohm and Rin = 31 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 70, Rin = 31 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 70 / 31 | Answer: 2.258

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 50 kohm and Rg = 17 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 50, Rg = 17 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 50/17 | Answer: 3.941

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 5524. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 5524 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(5524) | Answer: 37.42 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 7.5 m carries a central point load of 30 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7.5, W = 30 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 30*7.5 / 4 | Answer: 56.25 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 5.2 m carries a UDL of 20 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.2, w = 20 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 20*(5.2)^2 / 8 | Answer: 67.6 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 4.7 m carries a UDL of 10 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.7, w = 10 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 10*(4.7)^2 / 2 | Answer: 110.5 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 7.9 m carries a point load 90 kN at distance 1.9 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 7.9, a = 1.9, W = 90 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 90*(7.9 - 1.9) / 7.9 | Answer: 68.35 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 4.3 m) carries a central point load 45 kN. With E = 200 GPa and I = 280e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=45000 N, L=4300.0 mm, E=200000 MPa, I=280e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 1.331 mm

question: An RC beam has overall depth 310 mm, clear cover 45 mm and main bars of diameter 16 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 310, c = 45, dia = 16 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 310 - 45 - 16/2 | Answer: 257 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 34.3 m^2 carrying a factored load of 19.9 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 34.3, w = 19.9 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 19.9 * 34.3 | Answer: 682.6 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 4.3 m, unit weight 19 kN/m^3, phi = 36 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 4.8e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1, area = 2.5e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 4.8, i = 1, A = 2.5 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (4.8e-4)*1*(2.5e-3) | Answer: 1200 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1 m, bed slope 0.008 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.024. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 4.6 m under a head of 0.5 m. Taking Cd = 0.64 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 4.9 m wide carries a discharge of 22.6 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A tank of volume 630 m^3 treats a flow of 70 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 630, Q = 70 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 630 / 70 | Answer: 9 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 290 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.11 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 6 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 290, k = 0.11, t = 6 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 290*(1 - e^(-0.11*6)) | Answer: 140.1 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.83, rainfall intensity 60 mm/h over a catchment of 51.2 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.83, i = 60, A = 51.2 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.83*60*51.2 / 360 | Answer: 7.083 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.07 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 400 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.07, M = 400 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 400*(30+0.07)/30 | Answer: 400.9 m

question: Convert the decimal number 2551 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 2551 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 9F7 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 00010000 and 01011110.
solution: XOR: 01001110 | Count of 1s = 4 | Answer: 4
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 790 megabits is sent over a link of 1 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 790, B = 1 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 790 / 1 | Answer: 790 s

question: A link has bandwidth 66 Mbps and round-trip time 140 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 66, R = 140 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 66e6 * 140e-3 bits = 9240 kb | Answer: 9240 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.9, cache access time 8 ns and main-memory access time 80 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.9, tc = 8, tm = 80 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.9*8 + (1 - 0.9)*80 | Answer: 15.2 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 588917 elements?
solution: Given: n = 588917 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(588917)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.017, memory access time 150 ns and page-fault service time 10 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 10 ms = 10000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.017)*150 + 0.017*10000000.0 ns | Answer: 170.1 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 2 m^3 at 470 kPa and 520 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 2, P = 470, Tk = 520 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (470e3)*2 / (8.314*520) | Answer: 217.4 mol

question: For a reaction with A = 1e10 /s and activation energy 55 kJ/mol at 390 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 1, Ea = 55, Tk = 390 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 1e10 * exp(-55e3 / (8.314*390)) | Answer: 429.8 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.98 and bottoms xW = 0.05, with relative volatility alpha = 1.7. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.98, xw = 0.05, al = 1.7 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.98/0.02)(0.95/0.05)] / ln(1.7) | Answer: 12.88 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.81 and x = 0.22. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.81, x = 0.22 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.81/0.19) / (0.22/0.78) | Answer: 15.11

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.89 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 65 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.89, Psat = 65 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.89 * 65 | Answer: 57.85 kPa

question: A stream of 5.1 kg/s with specific heat 2.9 kJ/kg-K is heated through 105 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 5.1, cp = 2.9, dT = 105 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 5.1*2.9*105 | Answer: 1553 kW

question: A reactor of volume 15.7 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 2.4 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 15.7, Q = 2.4 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 15.7 / 2.4 | Answer: 6.542 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 5e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 1 mm with a concentration difference of 130 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 5, L = 1, dC = 130 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (5e-9)*130 / (1e-3) | Answer: 650 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 6.1 min and steady-state gain 3.2. For a step input of magnitude 8, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 6.1, K = 3.2, M = 8 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 3.2 * 8 | Answer: 25.6 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 90 m^2 flies at 210 m/s (air density 0.7 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 1.2. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 90, V = 210, rho = 0.7, CL = 1.2 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.7*(210)^2*90*1.2 / 1000 | Answer: 1667 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 120 m^2 flies at 150 m/s (density 0.7 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.08. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 120, V = 150, rho = 0.7, CD = 0.08 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.7*(150)^2*120*0.08 / 1000 | Answer: 75.6 kN

question: A specimen under stress 160 MPa shows an elastic strain of 2.7e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 160, eps = 2.7 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 160 / (2.7e-3) MPa = 59.26 GPa | Answer: 59.26 GPa

question: A block of mass 22 kg has a volume of 4.7e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 22, V = 4.7 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 22 / (4.7e-3) | Answer: 4681 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 2900 mm is heated through 100 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 17e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 2900, dT = 100, al = 17 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 2900*17e-6*100 | Answer: 4.93 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 115 ohm, R2 = 150 ohm and R3 = 150 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 115, R2 = 150, R3 = 150 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 150*150 / 115 | Answer: 195.7 ohm

question: A measurement reads 10.69 when the true value is 100. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10.69, true = 100 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10.69 - 100| / 100 * 100 | Answer: 89.31 %

question: Annual demand is 39000 units, ordering cost 140 per order and holding cost 25 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 39000, S = 140, H = 25 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*39000*140 / 25) | Answer: 660.9 units

question: An asset costs 390000 with salvage value 28000 after 7 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 390000, Sv = 28000, n = 7 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (390000 - 28000) / 7 | Answer: 51714 per year

question: A product sells for 420 per unit with variable cost 130 per unit and fixed costs 60000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 420, V = 130, F = 60000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 60000 / (420 - 130) | Answer: 206.9 units

question: Find the present worth of 60000 received 8 years from now at an interest rate of 12% per year.
solution: Given: F = 60000, n = 8, i = 12 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 60000 / (1 + 0.12)^8 | Answer: 24233 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.91, 0.94 and 0.95 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.91, r2 = 0.94, r3 = 0.95 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.91*0.94*0.95 | Answer: 0.8126

question: A process produces 49 defective items in a batch of 3000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 49, N = 3000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 49/3000 * 1e6 | Answer: 16333 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = 2x^3 + 8x^2 + 4x - 4 evaluated at x = 5.
For f(x) = 5x^3 + 7x^2 - 2x - 4, find f''(x) at x = 1.
Evaluate the definite integral of (2x + 4) dx from x = -3 to x = 3.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = 0x^3/3 + 2x^2/2 + 4x | Evaluate F(3) - F(-3) | Answer: 24
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 4x^2 - 10x - 7 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[5, 5], [-9, 6]].
solution: Given: a = 5, b = 5, c = -9, d = 6 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (5)(6) - (5)(-9) | Answer: 75

question: Find the determinant of [[-5, -3, 3], [1, -3, -1], [3, 5, 1]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: 44

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[8, -5], [1, -5]].
solution: Trace tr = 3, Determinant = -35 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 7.603

question: Solve for x: 5x + 2y = 1 and 4x + -5y = 4.
solution: Determinant = 5*-5 - 2*4 = -33 | x = (e d - b f) / det = 0.3939 | Answer: x = 0.3939
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 52, 86, 14, 72, 2.
solution: Sum = 226 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 45.2 | Answer: 45.2

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 20, 21, 27, 31, 49.
