question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 48, 30, 38, 11, 17.
solution: Mean = 28.8 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 15.09

question: Find the slope of the line through (1, -1) and (-7, 1).
solution: Given: x1 = 1, y1 = -1, x2 = -7, y2 = 1 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (1 - -1) / (-7 - 1) | Answer: -0.25

question: Find the distance between the points (9, -6) and (-9, -3).
solution: Given: x1 = 9, y1 = -6, x2 = -9, y2 = -3 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-18)^2 + (3)^2) | Answer: 18.25 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (8,4), (-1,-2), (3,4).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 15 sq units

question: Find the 22th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -20 and common difference 3.
solution: Given: a = -20, d = 3, n = 22 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -20 + (22 - 1)*3 | Answer: 43

question: Find the sum of the first 16 terms of an AP with first term -2 and common difference -5.
solution: Given: a = -2, d = -5, n = 16 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 16/2 [2*-2 + (16-1)*-5] | Answer: -632

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 23500 at 11.3% per annum for 10 years.
solution: Given: P = 23500, R = 11.3, Tt = 10 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 23500 * 11.3 * 10 / 100 | Answer: 26555 currency units

question: Find the amount when 8500 is invested at 4.1% per annum compounded annually for 4 years.
solution: Given: P = 8500, R = 4.1, Tt = 4 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 8500 * (1 + 4.1/100)^4 | Answer: 9982 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (-5, -2, 6) and (5, 2, -7).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (-1, 3, 0) and (-3, 4, -3).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 10.72

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (-4, 0, 5) and (-5, 1, 4).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 15.44 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = 4x^3 + 3x^2 - 5x - 5 at x = -5.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-102 with initial guess x0=4, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.6 and ordinates 3, 2, 10, 7, 20, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 215 and 230.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 215 and 230 | Answer: GCD = 5

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 42 and 62.
solution: Given: a = 42, b = 62 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 42*62 / 2 | Answer: 1302
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 19 mm carries an axial tensile load of 50 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 15 mm and length 1400 mm carries an axial load of 48 kN. Take E = 110 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 57 mm transmits a torque of 2500 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 57, Tt = 2500 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(2500*1000) / (pi*(57)^3) | Answer: 68.75 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 39 mm and length 800 mm carries a torque of 1850 N-m. With G = 80 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (39)^4 / 32 = 227122 mm^4 | theta = (1850*1000)(800) / (80000 * 227122) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 4.667 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 44 mm wide and 110 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 44, h = 110 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 44*(110)^2 / 6 | Answer: 88733 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (99 mm x 100 mm) carries a bending moment of 27 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (61 mm x 160 mm) has effective length 3800 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 860 MPa is designed for a working stress of 130 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 860, sw = 130 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 860 / 130 | Answer: 6.615

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1150 mm and wall thickness 18 mm carries an internal pressure of 2.2 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1150, t = 18, P = 2.2 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 2.2*1150 / (2*18) | Answer: 70.28 MPa

question: 7.7 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 175 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 7.7, dT = 175 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 7.7 * 0.718 * 175 | Answer: 967.5 kJ

question: 6.6 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 50 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 6.6, dT = 50 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 6.6 * 1.005 * 50 | Answer: 331.6 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 3.1 m^3 at 370 K with mass 5.2 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 3.1, Tk = 370, m = 5.2 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 5.2*0.287*370 / 3.1 | Answer: 178.1 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 4.2 kg of air expands isothermally at 450 K from volume V1 to 4*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.2, Tk = 450, ratio = 4 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 4.2*0.287*450*ln(4) | Answer: 752 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 4.6 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.34 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 4.6, D = 0.34 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*4.6*0.34 / 0.001 | Answer: 1564000

question: Water flows at 2.3 m/s through a pipe of diameter 50 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 8.8 m. Taking Cv = 0.99, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 8.8, cv = 0.99 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.99*sqrt(2*9.81*8.8) | Answer: 13.01 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 200 mm) water flows at 2.1 m/s. It contracts to diameter 130 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 200, d2 = 130, V1 = 2.1 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 2.1*(200/130)^2 | Answer: 4.97 m/s

question: Water flows at 3.8 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.49 m and length 280 m. With friction factor f = 0.039, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 17 teeth drives a gear of 71 teeth. If the pinion runs at 300 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 17, z2 = 71, N1 = 300 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 300*17 / 71 | Answer: 71.83 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 370 mm rotates at 600 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 370, N = 600 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.37)*600 / 60 | Answer: 11.62 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 48.3 kW at 1400 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 48.3, N = 1400 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(48.3*1000) / (2*pi*1400) | Answer: 329.5 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 8.6 kg rotates at radius 0.15 m at 950 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 15000 N/m and mass 2.2 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 15000, m = 2.2 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(15000/2.2) | Answer: 13.14 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 6.3 m^2 and thickness 0.26 m has conductivity k = 17.9 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 145 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 6.3, L = 0.26, k = 17.9, dT = 145 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 17.9*6.3*145 / 0.26 | Answer: 62891 W

question: A surface of area 0.9 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 50 W/m^2-K to surroundings 120 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 0.9, h = 50, dT = 120 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 50*0.9*120 | Answer: 5400 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 160 m/min, feed = 0.27 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2.7 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 160, f = 0.27, d = 2.7 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*160*0.27*2.7 | Answer: 116640 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 370 mm is turned at 700 rpm with a feed of 0.35 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 370, N = 700, f = 0.35 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 370 / (0.35*700) | Answer: 1.51 min

question: A resistor of 197 ohm carries a current of 0.6 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 197, I = 0.6 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 0.6 * 197 | Answer: 118.2 V

question: Three resistors 7 ohm, 95 ohm and 74 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 7, R2 = 95, R3 = 74 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 7 + 95 + 74 | Answer: 176 ohm

question: Two resistors 68 ohm and 44 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 68, R2 = 44 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 68*44 / (68+44) | Answer: 26.71 ohm

question: A device draws 4.4 A at 20 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 20, I = 4.4 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 20 * 4.4 | Answer: 88 W

question: A current of 0.7 A flows through a 17 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 0.7, R = 17 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (0.7)^2 * 17 | Answer: 8.33 W

question: Two capacitors 12.1 uF and 40.9 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 12.1, C2 = 40.9 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 12.1*40.9 / (12.1+40.9) | Answer: 9.338 uF

question: A resistor 72 kohm and capacitor 15.2 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 72, C = 15.2 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (72k)(15.2u) = 1094 ms | Answer: 1094 ms

question: An inductor 445.8 mH is in series with 57 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 445.8, R = 57 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (445.8e-3) / 57 | Answer: 7.821 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 133.7 mH inductor at 320 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 133.7, f = 320 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (320)(133.7e-3) | Answer: 268.8 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 30.2 uF capacitor at 380 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 30.2, f = 380 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (380)(30.2e-6)) | Answer: 13.87 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 54 ohm, XL = 43 ohm and XC = 113 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 54, XL = 43, XC = 113 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(54^2 + (43 - 113)^2) | Answer: 88.41 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 60.4 mH and C = 5.5 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 60.4, C = 5.5 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(60.4e-3 * 5.5e-6)) | Answer: 276.1 Hz

question: A capacitor of 67.7 uF is charged to 165 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 67.7, V = 165 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*67.7e-6*(165)^2 | Answer: 921.6 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 270 V with 630 primary turns and 470 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 270, N1 = 630, N2 = 470 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 270 * 470/630 | Answer: 201.4 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 380 V and draws an armature current of 20 A. If the armature resistance is 1.33 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 380, Ia = 20, Ra = 1.33 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 380 - 20*1.33 | Answer: 353.4 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 160 A at 433 V (line) with a power factor of 0.82. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 160, VL = 433, pf = 0.82 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*433*160*0.82 / 1000 | Answer: 98.4 kW

question: A load has real power 55 kW and apparent power 90 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 55, S = 90 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 55 / 90 | Answer: 0.6111

question: A machine delivers 80 kW output while drawing 117 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 80, Pi = 117 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 80/117 * 100 | Answer: 68.38 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 22 V across R1 = 23 ohm and R2 = 14 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 22, R1 = 23, R2 = 14 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 22*14 / (23+14) | Answer: 8.324 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 90 kohm and Rin = 19 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 90, Rin = 19 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 90 / 19 | Answer: 4.737

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 9784. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 9784 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(9784) | Answer: 39.91 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 5.8 m carries a central point load of 105 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.8, W = 105 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 105*5.8 / 4 | Answer: 152.2 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.9 m carries a UDL of 10 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 9.9, w = 10 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 10*(9.9)^2 / 8 | Answer: 122.5 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 1.8 m carries a point load 15 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 1.8, W = 15 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 15*1.8 | Answer: 27 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 2.7 m carries a UDL of 18 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 2.7, w = 18 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 18*(2.7)^2 / 2 | Answer: 65.61 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 5.1 m carries a point load 90 kN at distance 3.6 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 5.1, a = 3.6, W = 90 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 90*(5.1 - 3.6) / 5.1 | Answer: 26.47 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 5.1 m) carries a central point load 50 kN. With E = 30 GPa and I = 370e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=50000 N, L=5100.0 mm, E=30000 MPa, I=370e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 12.45 mm

question: An RC beam has overall depth 330 mm, clear cover 35 mm and main bars of diameter 20 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 330, c = 35, dia = 20 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 330 - 35 - 20/2 | Answer: 285 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 31.5 m^2 carrying a factored load of 18.7 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 31.5, w = 18.7 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 18.7 * 31.5 | Answer: 589 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 4.5 m, unit weight 18 kN/m^3, phi = 31 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 3.7e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.5, area = 5.3e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 3.7, i = 0.5, A = 5.3 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (3.7e-4)*0.5*(5.3e-3) | Answer: 980.5 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.4 m, bed slope 0.005 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.024. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 4.9 m under a head of 0.6 m. Taking Cd = 0.62 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 4.3 m wide carries a discharge of 10 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A tank of volume 470 m^3 treats a flow of 55 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 470, Q = 55 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 470 / 55 | Answer: 8.545 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 340 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.29 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 3 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 340, k = 0.29, t = 3 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 340*(1 - e^(-0.29*3)) | Answer: 197.6 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.5, rainfall intensity 90 mm/h over a catchment of 32.7 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.5, i = 90, A = 32.7 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.5*90*32.7 / 360 | Answer: 4.088 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.04 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 650 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.04, M = 650 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 650*(30+0.04)/30 | Answer: 650.9 m

question: Convert the decimal number 1764 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 1764 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 6E4 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 10100011 and 11010111.
solution: XOR: 01110100 | Count of 1s = 4 | Answer: 4
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 90 megabits is sent over a link of 51 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 90, B = 51 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 90 / 51 | Answer: 1.765 s

question: A link has bandwidth 45 Mbps and round-trip time 60 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 45, R = 60 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 45e6 * 60e-3 bits = 2700 kb | Answer: 2700 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.85, cache access time 7 ns and main-memory access time 150 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.85, tc = 7, tm = 150 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.85*7 + (1 - 0.85)*150 | Answer: 28.45 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 287519 elements?
solution: Given: n = 287519 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(287519)) + 1 | Answer: 19

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.017, memory access time 200 ns and page-fault service time 7 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 7 ms = 7000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.017)*200 + 0.017*7000000.0 ns | Answer: 119.2 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 2.6 m^3 at 360 kPa and 420 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 2.6, P = 360, Tk = 420 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (360e3)*2.6 / (8.314*420) | Answer: 268.1 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.29 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 7 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.29, t = 7 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.29*7) | Answer: 0.8687

question: For a reaction with A = 7e10 /s and activation energy 60 kJ/mol at 320 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 7, Ea = 60, Tk = 320 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 7e10 * exp(-60e3 / (8.314*320)) | Answer: 11.24 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.93 and bottoms xW = 0.02, with relative volatility alpha = 3.1. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.93, xw = 0.02, al = 3.1 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.93/0.07)(0.98/0.02)] / ln(3.1) | Answer: 5.726 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.6 and x = 0.29. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.6, x = 0.29 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.6/0.4) / (0.29/0.71) | Answer: 3.672

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.38 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 120 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.38, Psat = 120 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.38 * 120 | Answer: 45.6 kPa

question: A stream of 2.9 kg/s with specific heat 1.9 kJ/kg-K is heated through 15 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 2.9, cp = 1.9, dT = 15 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 2.9*1.9*15 | Answer: 82.65 kW

question: A reactor of volume 12.6 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 0.8 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 12.6, Q = 0.8 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 12.6 / 0.8 | Answer: 15.75 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 7.3e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 5 mm with a concentration difference of 60 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 7.3, L = 5, dC = 60 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (7.3e-9)*60 / (5e-3) | Answer: 87.6 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 9.1 min and steady-state gain 2.9. For a step input of magnitude 6, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 9.1, K = 2.9, M = 6 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 2.9 * 6 | Answer: 17.4 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 110 m^2 flies at 180 m/s (air density 1 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 1. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 110, V = 180, rho = 1, CL = 1 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1*(180)^2*110*1 / 1000 | Answer: 1782 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 70 m^2 flies at 60 m/s (density 1 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.03. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 70, V = 60, rho = 1, CD = 0.03 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*1*(60)^2*70*0.03 / 1000 | Answer: 3.78 kN

question: A specimen under stress 170 MPa shows an elastic strain of 0.6e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 170, eps = 0.6 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 170 / (0.6e-3) MPa = 283.3 GPa | Answer: 283.3 GPa

question: A block of mass 41 kg has a volume of 5e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 41, V = 5 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 41 / (5e-3) | Answer: 8200 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 2500 mm is heated through 120 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 12e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 2500, dT = 120, al = 12 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 2500*12e-6*120 | Answer: 3.6 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 100 ohm, R2 = 130 ohm and R3 = 190 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 100, R2 = 130, R3 = 190 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 130*190 / 100 | Answer: 247 ohm

question: A measurement reads 9.57 when the true value is 20. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.57, true = 20 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.57 - 20| / 20 * 100 | Answer: 52.15 %

question: Annual demand is 35500 units, ordering cost 150 per order and holding cost 40 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 35500, S = 150, H = 40 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*35500*150 / 40) | Answer: 516 units

question: An asset costs 50000 with salvage value 10000 after 9 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 50000, Sv = 10000, n = 9 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (50000 - 10000) / 9 | Answer: 4444 per year

question: A product sells for 160 per unit with variable cost 40 per unit and fixed costs 25000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 160, V = 40, F = 25000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 25000 / (160 - 40) | Answer: 208.3 units

question: Find the present worth of 145000 received 3 years from now at an interest rate of 6% per year.
solution: Given: F = 145000, n = 3, i = 6 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 145000 / (1 + 0.06)^3 | Answer: 121745 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.92, 0.96 and 0.97 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.92, r2 = 0.96, r3 = 0.97 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.92*0.96*0.97 | Answer: 0.8567

question: A process produces 28 defective items in a batch of 18000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 28, N = 18000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 28/18000 * 1e6 | Answer: 1556 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = 3x^3 + 8x^2 + x evaluated at x = 0.
For f(x) = 6x^3 - 4x^2 + 6x - 3, find f''(x) at x = -4.
Evaluate the definite integral of (-5x^2 - 6x - 5) dx from x = -1 to x = 3.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = -5x^3/3 + -6x^2/2 + -5x | Evaluate F(3) - F(-1) | Answer: -90.67
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of x^2 - 6x - 9 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[-3, 9], [0, 4]].
solution: Given: a = -3, b = 9, c = 0, d = 4 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (-3)(4) - (9)(0) | Answer: -12

question: Find the determinant of [[-6, 5, 2], [-4, -5, -2], [5, 5, 3]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: 50

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[-8, 5], [6, 2]].
solution: Trace tr = -6, Determinant = -46 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 4.416

question: Solve for x: 2x + 1y = 1 and -5x + 1y = -5.
solution: Determinant = 2*1 - 1*-5 = 7 | x = (e d - b f) / det = 0.8571 | Answer: x = 0.8571
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 54, 50, 93, 90, 30.
solution: Sum = 317 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 63.4 | Answer: 63.4

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 41, 40, 26, 27, 8.
solution: Mean = 28.4 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 13.39

question: Find the slope of the line through (-9, -8) and (8, -2).
Find the distance between the points (9, -3) and (-8, 4).
solution: Given: x1 = 9, y1 = -3, x2 = -8, y2 = 4 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-17)^2 + (7)^2) | Answer: 18.38 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (-1,5), (5,3), (2,3).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 3 sq units

question: Find the 11th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -17 and common difference 6.
solution: Given: a = -17, d = 6, n = 11 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -17 + (11 - 1)*6 | Answer: 43

question: Find the sum of the first 26 terms of an AP with first term -14 and common difference -4.
Find the simple interest on a principal of 14500 at 5.5% per annum for 1 years.
solution: Given: P = 14500, R = 5.5, Tt = 1 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 14500 * 5.5 * 1 / 100 | Answer: 797.5 currency units

question: Find the amount when 16500 is invested at 9.5% per annum compounded annually for 4 years.
solution: Given: P = 16500, R = 9.5, Tt = 4 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 16500 * (1 + 9.5/100)^4 | Answer: 23721 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (7, 3, 4) and (-1, 4, 6).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (-4, -4, -4) and (3, -4, -4).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 39.6

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (-4, -6, 5) and (-5, 4, -4).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 111.2 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -2x^3 - 7x^2 - 3 at x = 5.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-104 with initial guess x0=6, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.3 and ordinates 2, 16, 3, 15, 9, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 55 and 71.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 55 and 71 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 30 and 76.
solution: Given: a = 30, b = 76 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 30*76 / 2 | Answer: 1140
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 59 mm carries an axial tensile load of 104 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 20 mm and length 2900 mm carries an axial load of 23 kN. Take E = 200 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 49 mm transmits a torque of 1750 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 49, Tt = 1750 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(1750*1000) / (pi*(49)^3) | Answer: 75.76 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 46 mm and length 600 mm carries a torque of 1100 N-m. With G = 80 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (46)^4 / 32 = 439573 mm^4 | theta = (1100*1000)(600) / (80000 * 439573) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 1.075 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 134 mm wide and 190 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 134, h = 190 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 134*(190)^2 / 6 | Answer: 806233 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (96 mm x 170 mm) carries a bending moment of 21 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (46 mm x 120 mm) has effective length 3200 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 400 MPa is designed for a working stress of 230 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 400, sw = 230 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 400 / 230 | Answer: 1.739

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 800 mm and wall thickness 9 mm carries an internal pressure of 2.7 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 800, t = 9, P = 2.7 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 2.7*800 / (2*9) | Answer: 120 MPa

question: 4.3 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 90 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.3, dT = 90 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 4.3 * 0.718 * 90 | Answer: 277.9 kJ

question: 6.4 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 55 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 6.4, dT = 55 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 6.4 * 1.005 * 55 | Answer: 353.8 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 1.8 m^3 at 410 K with mass 2.2 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 1.8, Tk = 410, m = 2.2 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 2.2*0.287*410 / 1.8 | Answer: 143.8 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 2.7 kg of air expands isothermally at 380 K from volume V1 to 3*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.7, Tk = 380, ratio = 3 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 2.7*0.287*380*ln(3) | Answer: 323.5 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 2.8 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.34 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 2.8, D = 0.34 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*2.8*0.34 / 0.001 | Answer: 952000

question: Water flows at 0.6 m/s through a pipe of diameter 80 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
In a pipe (diameter 170 mm) water flows at 2.8 m/s. It contracts to diameter 120 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
Water flows at 1.4 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.18 m and length 250 m. With friction factor f = 0.029, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 28 teeth drives a gear of 111 teeth. If the pinion runs at 450 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 28, z2 = 111, N1 = 450 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 450*28 / 111 | Answer: 113.5 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 230 mm rotates at 750 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 230, N = 750 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.23)*750 / 60 | Answer: 9.032 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 2.6 kW at 250 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 2.6, N = 250 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(2.6*1000) / (2*pi*250) | Answer: 99.31 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 4 kg rotates at radius 0.26 m at 200 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 6500 N/m and mass 7.9 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 6500, m = 7.9 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(6500/7.9) | Answer: 4.565 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 1.5 m^2 and thickness 0.16 m has conductivity k = 27.9 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 75 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 1.5, L = 0.16, k = 27.9, dT = 75 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 27.9*1.5*75 / 0.16 | Answer: 19617 W

question: A surface of area 2.1 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 115 W/m^2-K to surroundings 90 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 2.1, h = 115, dT = 90 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 115*2.1*90 | Answer: 21735 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 220 m/min, feed = 0.38 mm/rev, depth of cut = 3 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 220, f = 0.38, d = 3 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*220*0.38*3 | Answer: 250800 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 340 mm is turned at 250 rpm with a feed of 0.16 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 340, N = 250, f = 0.16 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 340 / (0.16*250) | Answer: 8.5 min

question: A resistor of 174 ohm carries a current of 7.4 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 174, I = 7.4 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 7.4 * 174 | Answer: 1288 V

question: Three resistors 80 ohm, 78 ohm and 34 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 80, R2 = 78, R3 = 34 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 80 + 78 + 34 | Answer: 192 ohm

question: Two resistors 101 ohm and 46 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 101, R2 = 46 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 101*46 / (101+46) | Answer: 31.61 ohm

question: A device draws 13.1 A at 40 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 40, I = 13.1 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 40 * 13.1 | Answer: 524 W

question: A current of 11.5 A flows through a 25 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 11.5, R = 25 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (11.5)^2 * 25 | Answer: 3306 W

question: Two capacitors 27.8 uF and 47.1 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 27.8, C2 = 47.1 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 27.8*47.1 / (27.8+47.1) | Answer: 17.48 uF

question: A resistor 55 kohm and capacitor 6.1 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 55, C = 6.1 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (55k)(6.1u) = 335.5 ms | Answer: 335.5 ms

question: An inductor 238 mH is in series with 79 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 238, R = 79 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (238e-3) / 79 | Answer: 3.013 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 154.6 mH inductor at 50 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 154.6, f = 50 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (50)(154.6e-3) | Answer: 48.57 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 25.5 uF capacitor at 500 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 25.5, f = 500 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (500)(25.5e-6)) | Answer: 12.48 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 34 ohm, XL = 116 ohm and XC = 58 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 34, XL = 116, XC = 58 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(34^2 + (116 - 58)^2) | Answer: 67.23 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 92.8 mH and C = 0.4 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 92.8, C = 0.4 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(92.8e-3 * 0.4e-6)) | Answer: 826.1 Hz

question: A capacitor of 54.6 uF is charged to 75 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 54.6, V = 75 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*54.6e-6*(75)^2 | Answer: 153.6 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 400 V with 500 primary turns and 280 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 400, N1 = 500, N2 = 280 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 400 * 280/500 | Answer: 224 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 320 V and draws an armature current of 50 A. If the armature resistance is 1.43 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 320, Ia = 50, Ra = 1.43 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 320 - 50*1.43 | Answer: 248.5 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 120 A at 415 V (line) with a power factor of 0.78. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 120, VL = 415, pf = 0.78 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*415*120*0.78 / 1000 | Answer: 67.28 kW

question: A load has real power 120 kW and apparent power 125 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 120, S = 125 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 120 / 125 | Answer: 0.96

question: A machine delivers 60 kW output while drawing 117 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 60, Pi = 117 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 60/117 * 100 | Answer: 51.28 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 27 V across R1 = 39 ohm and R2 = 22 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 27, R1 = 39, R2 = 22 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 27*22 / (39+22) | Answer: 9.738 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 80 kohm and Rin = 33 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 80, Rin = 33 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 80 / 33 | Answer: 2.424

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 120 kohm and Rg = 22 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 120, Rg = 22 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 120/22 | Answer: 6.455

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 7010. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 7010 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(7010) | Answer: 38.46 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 9 m carries a central point load of 55 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 9, W = 55 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 55*9 / 4 | Answer: 123.8 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 2.1 m carries a point load 5 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 2.1, W = 5 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 5*2.1 | Answer: 10.5 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 4.4 m carries a UDL of 40 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.4, w = 40 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 40*(4.4)^2 / 2 | Answer: 387.2 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.8 m carries a point load 10 kN at distance 3.9 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 9.8, a = 3.9, W = 10 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 10*(9.8 - 3.9) / 9.8 | Answer: 6.02 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 7.8 m) carries a central point load 30 kN. With E = 25 GPa and I = 300e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=30000 N, L=7800.0 mm, E=25000 MPa, I=300e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 39.55 mm

question: An RC beam has overall depth 340 mm, clear cover 50 mm and main bars of diameter 12 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 340, c = 50, dia = 12 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 340 - 50 - 12/2 | Answer: 284 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 30.9 m^2 carrying a factored load of 8.3 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 30.9, w = 8.3 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 8.3 * 30.9 | Answer: 256.5 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 7 m, unit weight 16 kN/m^3, phi = 36 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 3.7e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1, area = 6.1e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 3.7, i = 1, A = 6.1 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (3.7e-4)*1*(6.1e-3) | Answer: 2257 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.9 m, bed slope 0.009 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.016. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 2.1 m under a head of 0.9 m. Taking Cd = 0.62 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 2.3 m wide carries a discharge of 26.1 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A tank of volume 50 m^3 treats a flow of 185 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 50, Q = 185 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 50 / 185 | Answer: 0.2703 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 150 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.13 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 8 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 150, k = 0.13, t = 8 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 150*(1 - e^(-0.13*8)) | Answer: 96.98 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.46, rainfall intensity 40 mm/h over a catchment of 10.7 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.46, i = 40, A = 10.7 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.46*40*10.7 / 360 | Answer: 0.5469 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.02 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 460 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.02, M = 460 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 460*(20+0.02)/20 | Answer: 460.5 m

question: Convert the decimal number 3797 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 3797 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: ED5 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 00010111 and 01011001.
solution: XOR: 01001110 | Count of 1s = 4 | Answer: 4
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 270 megabits is sent over a link of 43 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 270, B = 43 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 270 / 43 | Answer: 6.279 s

question: A link has bandwidth 59 Mbps and round-trip time 170 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 59, R = 170 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 59e6 * 170e-3 bits = 10030 kb | Answer: 10030 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.92, cache access time 5 ns and main-memory access time 130 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.92, tc = 5, tm = 130 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.92*5 + (1 - 0.92)*130 | Answer: 15 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 929463 elements?
solution: Given: n = 929463 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(929463)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.01, memory access time 150 ns and page-fault service time 10 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 10 ms = 10000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.01)*150 + 0.01*10000000.0 ns | Answer: 100.1 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 1.9 m^3 at 140 kPa and 490 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 1.9, P = 140, Tk = 490 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (140e3)*1.9 / (8.314*490) | Answer: 65.29 mol

question: For a reaction with A = 2e10 /s and activation energy 55 kJ/mol at 330 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 2, Ea = 55, Tk = 330 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 2e10 * exp(-55e3 / (8.314*330)) | Answer: 39.35 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.94 and bottoms xW = 0.08, with relative volatility alpha = 2.8. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.94, xw = 0.08, al = 2.8 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.94/0.06)(0.92/0.08)] / ln(2.8) | Answer: 5.044 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.73 and x = 0.33. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.73, x = 0.33 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.73/0.27) / (0.33/0.67) | Answer: 5.489

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.65 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 105 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.65, Psat = 105 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.65 * 105 | Answer: 68.25 kPa

question: A stream of 4.8 kg/s with specific heat 1.9 kJ/kg-K is heated through 95 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 4.8, cp = 1.9, dT = 95 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 4.8*1.9*95 | Answer: 866.4 kW

question: A reactor of volume 13.2 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 4.5 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 13.2, Q = 4.5 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 13.2 / 4.5 | Answer: 2.933 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 8.2e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 5 mm with a concentration difference of 190 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 8.2, L = 5, dC = 190 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (8.2e-9)*190 / (5e-3) | Answer: 311.6 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 3.3 min and steady-state gain 3.3. For a step input of magnitude 3, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 3.3, K = 3.3, M = 3 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 3.3 * 3 | Answer: 9.9 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 70 m^2 flies at 80 m/s (air density 1 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.9. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 70, V = 80, rho = 1, CL = 0.9 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1*(80)^2*70*0.9 / 1000 | Answer: 201.6 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 95 m^2 flies at 260 m/s (density 1.225 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.07. Find the drag force in kN.
A specimen under stress 390 MPa shows an elastic strain of 1.3e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 390, eps = 1.3 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 390 / (1.3e-3) MPa = 300 GPa | Answer: 300 GPa

question: A block of mass 9 kg has a volume of 4e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 9, V = 4 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 9 / (4e-3) | Answer: 2250 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 1900 mm is heated through 40 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 17e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 1900, dT = 40, al = 17 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 1900*17e-6*40 | Answer: 1.292 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 95 ohm, R2 = 30 ohm and R3 = 215 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 95, R2 = 30, R3 = 215 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 30*215 / 95 | Answer: 67.89 ohm

question: Annual demand is 4500 units, ordering cost 30 per order and holding cost 28 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 4500, S = 30, H = 28 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*4500*30 / 28) | Answer: 98.2 units

question: An asset costs 240000 with salvage value 2000 after 10 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 240000, Sv = 2000, n = 10 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (240000 - 2000) / 10 | Answer: 23800 per year

question: A product sells for 420 per unit with variable cost 180 per unit and fixed costs 50000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 420, V = 180, F = 50000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 50000 / (420 - 180) | Answer: 208.3 units

question: Find the present worth of 190000 received 6 years from now at an interest rate of 6% per year.
solution: Given: F = 190000, n = 6, i = 6 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 190000 / (1 + 0.06)^6 | Answer: 133943 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.98, 0.97 and 0.95 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.98, r2 = 0.97, r3 = 0.95 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.98*0.97*0.95 | Answer: 0.9031

question: A process produces 37 defective items in a batch of 17500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 37, N = 17500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 37/17500 * 1e6 | Answer: 2114 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = 3x^3 + 7x evaluated at x = 2.
For f(x) = 3x^3 + x^2 - 7x + 5, find f''(x) at x = 3.
Evaluate the definite integral of (x + 7) dx from x = -4 to x = 3.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = 0x^3/3 + 1x^2/2 + 7x | Evaluate F(3) - F(-4) | Answer: 45.5
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 4x^2 + 12x - 6 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[-4, -7], [-1, 8]].
solution: Given: a = -4, b = -7, c = -1, d = 8 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (-4)(8) - (-7)(-1) | Answer: -39

question: Find the determinant of [[1, -2, -3], [5, 1, 0], [1, 0, -2]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: -19

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[2, 8], [1, -3]].
solution: Trace tr = -1, Determinant = -14 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 3.275

question: Solve for x: 3x + -6y = 2 and -6x + -3y = 11.
solution: Determinant = 3*-3 - -6*-6 = -45 | x = (e d - b f) / det = -1.333 | Answer: x = -1.333
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 58, 70, 68, 62, 1.
solution: Sum = 259 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 51.8 | Answer: 51.8

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 32, 19, 46, 4, 25.
solution: Mean = 25.2 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 15.55

question: Find the slope of the line through (-3, 7) and (-5, 7).
solution: Given: x1 = -3, y1 = 7, x2 = -5, y2 = 7 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (7 - 7) / (-5 - -3) | Answer: 0

question: Find the distance between the points (1, 7) and (6, -7).
solution: Given: x1 = 1, y1 = 7, x2 = 6, y2 = -7 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((5)^2 + (-14)^2) | Answer: 14.87 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (0,8), (5,0), (5,-3).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 7.5 sq units

question: Find the 37th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -15 and common difference 8.
solution: Given: a = -15, d = 8, n = 37 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -15 + (37 - 1)*8 | Answer: 273

question: Find the sum of the first 22 terms of an AP with first term -15 and common difference -4.
Find the simple interest on a principal of 40500 at 6.6% per annum for 3 years.
solution: Given: P = 40500, R = 6.6, Tt = 3 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 40500 * 6.6 * 3 / 100 | Answer: 8019 currency units

question: Find the amount when 11000 is invested at 9.9% per annum compounded annually for 6 years.
solution: Given: P = 11000, R = 9.9, Tt = 6 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 11000 * (1 + 9.9/100)^6 | Answer: 19381 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (-4, 4, -2) and (-6, 6, 1).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (0, 5, -3) and (2, 5, -1).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 15.36

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (-3, 6, -1) and (5, 1, 3).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 107.4 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -5x^3 + 6x^2 + 6x at x = 2.
solution: Given: a = -5, b = 6, c = 6, d = 0, x0 = 2 | Formula: f(x0) = a x0^3 + b x0^2 + c x0 + d | Substitute: f(2) = -5(2)^3 + 6(2)^2 + 6(2) + 0 | Answer: -4

question: Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-194 with initial guess x0=7, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.1 and ordinates 18, 6, 9, 5, 11, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 50 and 487.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 50 and 487 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 31 and 41.
solution: Given: a = 31, b = 41 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 31*41 / 1 | Answer: 1271
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 16 mm carries an axial tensile load of 88 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 20 mm and length 2500 mm carries an axial load of 49 kN. Take E = 110 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 70 mm transmits a torque of 1200 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 70, Tt = 1200 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(1200*1000) / (pi*(70)^3) | Answer: 17.82 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 67 mm and length 700 mm carries a torque of 250 N-m. With G = 77 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (67)^4 / 32 = 1978332 mm^4 | theta = (250*1000)(700) / (77000 * 1978332) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 0.06582 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 79 mm wide and 180 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 79, h = 180 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 79*(180)^2 / 6 | Answer: 426600 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (44 mm x 190 mm) carries a bending moment of 35 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (79 mm x 140 mm) has effective length 1600 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 320 MPa is designed for a working stress of 250 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 320, sw = 250 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 320 / 250 | Answer: 1.28

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1200 mm and wall thickness 12 mm carries an internal pressure of 1.2 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1200, t = 12, P = 1.2 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 1.2*1200 / (2*12) | Answer: 60 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 760 K and 350 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 760, Tc = 350 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 350/760) * 100 | Answer: 53.95 %

question: 2.3 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 85 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.3, dT = 85 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 2.3 * 0.718 * 85 | Answer: 140.4 kJ

question: 1.3 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 45 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1.3, dT = 45 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 1.3 * 1.005 * 45 | Answer: 58.79 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 3.1 m^3 at 370 K with mass 3.5 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 3.1, Tk = 370, m = 3.5 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 3.5*0.287*370 / 3.1 | Answer: 119.9 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 3.4 kg of air expands isothermally at 480 K from volume V1 to 3*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.4, Tk = 480, ratio = 3 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 3.4*0.287*480*ln(3) | Answer: 514.6 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 2.8 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.14 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 2.8, D = 0.14 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*2.8*0.14 / 0.001 | Answer: 392000

question: Water flows at 3.3 m/s through a pipe of diameter 220 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 19.7 m. Taking Cv = 0.99, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 19.7, cv = 0.99 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.99*sqrt(2*9.81*19.7) | Answer: 19.46 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 270 mm) water flows at 2.5 m/s. It contracts to diameter 70 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 270, d2 = 70, V1 = 2.5 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 2.5*(270/70)^2 | Answer: 37.19 m/s

question: Water flows at 2.6 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.3 m and length 370 m. With friction factor f = 0.023, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 20 teeth drives a gear of 80 teeth. If the pinion runs at 500 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 20, z2 = 80, N1 = 500 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 500*20 / 80 | Answer: 125 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 520 mm rotates at 450 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 520, N = 450 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.52)*450 / 60 | Answer: 12.25 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 11.2 kW at 800 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 11.2, N = 800 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(11.2*1000) / (2*pi*800) | Answer: 133.7 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 4.6 kg rotates at radius 0.3 m at 700 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 7000 N/m and mass 11.5 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 7000, m = 11.5 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(7000/11.5) | Answer: 3.927 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 1.6 m^2 and thickness 0.32 m has conductivity k = 6.8 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 100 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 1.6, L = 0.32, k = 6.8, dT = 100 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 6.8*1.6*100 / 0.32 | Answer: 3400 W

question: A surface of area 2.9 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 50 W/m^2-K to surroundings 120 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 2.9, h = 50, dT = 120 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 50*2.9*120 | Answer: 17400 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 70 m/min, feed = 0.32 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2.4 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 70, f = 0.32, d = 2.4 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*70*0.32*2.4 | Answer: 53760 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 480 mm is turned at 200 rpm with a feed of 0.23 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 480, N = 200, f = 0.23 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 480 / (0.23*200) | Answer: 10.43 min

question: A resistor of 56 ohm carries a current of 1.7 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 56, I = 1.7 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 1.7 * 56 | Answer: 95.2 V

question: Three resistors 88 ohm, 66 ohm and 55 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 88, R2 = 66, R3 = 55 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 88 + 66 + 55 | Answer: 209 ohm

question: Two resistors 112 ohm and 52 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 112, R2 = 52 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 112*52 / (112+52) | Answer: 35.51 ohm

question: A device draws 0.6 A at 150 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 150, I = 0.6 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 150 * 0.6 | Answer: 90 W

question: A current of 3 A flows through a 57 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 3, R = 57 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (3)^2 * 57 | Answer: 513 W

question: Two capacitors 34.3 uF and 20.5 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 34.3, C2 = 20.5 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 34.3*20.5 / (34.3+20.5) | Answer: 12.83 uF

question: A resistor 34 kohm and capacitor 6.7 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 34, C = 6.7 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (34k)(6.7u) = 227.8 ms | Answer: 227.8 ms

question: An inductor 420.1 mH is in series with 71 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 420.1, R = 71 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (420.1e-3) / 71 | Answer: 5.917 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 8.8 mH inductor at 840 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 8.8, f = 840 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (840)(8.8e-3) | Answer: 46.45 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 3 uF capacitor at 380 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 3, f = 380 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (380)(3e-6)) | Answer: 139.6 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 63 ohm, XL = 18 ohm and XC = 74 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 63, XL = 18, XC = 74 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(63^2 + (18 - 74)^2) | Answer: 84.29 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 13.7 mH and C = 5.2 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 13.7, C = 5.2 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(13.7e-3 * 5.2e-6)) | Answer: 596.3 Hz

question: A capacitor of 53.7 uF is charged to 255 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 53.7, V = 255 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*53.7e-6*(255)^2 | Answer: 1746 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 440 V with 410 primary turns and 370 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 440, N1 = 410, N2 = 370 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 440 * 370/410 | Answer: 397.1 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 340 V and draws an armature current of 29 A. If the armature resistance is 0.15 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 340, Ia = 29, Ra = 0.15 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 340 - 29*0.15 | Answer: 335.6 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 25 A at 415 V (line) with a power factor of 0.87. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 25, VL = 415, pf = 0.87 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*415*25*0.87 / 1000 | Answer: 15.63 kW

question: A load has real power 100 kW and apparent power 215 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 100, S = 215 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 100 / 215 | Answer: 0.4651

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 7 V across R1 = 25 ohm and R2 = 31 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 7, R1 = 25, R2 = 31 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 7*31 / (25+31) | Answer: 3.875 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 40 kohm and Rin = 47 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 40, Rin = 47 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 40 / 47 | Answer: 0.8511

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 80 kohm and Rg = 5 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 80, Rg = 5 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 80/5 | Answer: 17

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 8795. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 8795 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(8795) | Answer: 39.44 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.3 m carries a central point load of 100 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 9.3, W = 100 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 100*9.3 / 4 | Answer: 232.5 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.8 m carries a UDL of 5 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 9.8, w = 5 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 5*(9.8)^2 / 8 | Answer: 60.03 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 2.1 m carries a point load 65 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 2.1, W = 65 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 65*2.1 | Answer: 136.5 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 1.8 m carries a UDL of 36 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 1.8, w = 36 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 36*(1.8)^2 / 2 | Answer: 58.32 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.8 m carries a point load 100 kN at distance 3.5 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 6.8, a = 3.5, W = 100 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 100*(6.8 - 3.5) / 6.8 | Answer: 48.53 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 4.6 m) carries a central point load 30 kN. With E = 200 GPa and I = 150e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=30000 N, L=4600.0 mm, E=200000 MPa, I=150e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 2.028 mm

question: An RC beam has overall depth 500 mm, clear cover 50 mm and main bars of diameter 16 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 500, c = 50, dia = 16 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 500 - 50 - 16/2 | Answer: 442 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 28.9 m^2 carrying a factored load of 13.3 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 28.9, w = 13.3 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 13.3 * 28.9 | Answer: 384.4 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 4.7 m, unit weight 18 kN/m^3, phi = 35 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 8.4e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1, area = 1.6e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 8.4, i = 1, A = 1.6 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (8.4e-4)*1*(1.6e-3) | Answer: 1344 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 2.5 m, bed slope 0.007 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.014. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 3.6 m under a head of 0.7 m. Taking Cd = 0.63 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 2.7 m wide carries a discharge of 6.9 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 270 m and design speed 85 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 270, V = 85 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (85)^2 / (127*270) | Answer: 0.2107
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: A tank of volume 950 m^3 treats a flow of 50 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 950, Q = 50 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 950 / 50 | Answer: 19 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 280 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.19 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 4 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 280, k = 0.19, t = 4 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 280*(1 - e^(-0.19*4)) | Answer: 149.1 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.66, rainfall intensity 70 mm/h over a catchment of 7.1 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.66, i = 70, A = 7.1 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.66*70*7.1 / 360 | Answer: 0.9112 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.04 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 710 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.04, M = 710 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 710*(20+0.04)/20 | Answer: 711.4 m

question: Convert the decimal number 579 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 579 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 243 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 11011100 and 10010011.
solution: XOR: 01001111 | Count of 1s = 5 | Answer: 5
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 500 megabits is sent over a link of 18 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 500, B = 18 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 500 / 18 | Answer: 27.78 s

question: A link has bandwidth 52 Mbps and round-trip time 140 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 52, R = 140 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 52e6 * 140e-3 bits = 7280 kb | Answer: 7280 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.98, cache access time 1 ns and main-memory access time 190 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.98, tc = 1, tm = 190 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.98*1 + (1 - 0.98)*190 | Answer: 4.78 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 849676 elements?
solution: Given: n = 849676 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(849676)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.01, memory access time 120 ns and page-fault service time 3 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 3 ms = 3000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.01)*120 + 0.01*3000000.0 ns | Answer: 30.12 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 2.9 m^3 at 280 kPa and 360 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 2.9, P = 280, Tk = 360 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (280e3)*2.9 / (8.314*360) | Answer: 271.3 mol

question: For a reaction with A = 2e10 /s and activation energy 85 kJ/mol at 340 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 2, Ea = 85, Tk = 340 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 2e10 * exp(-85e3 / (8.314*340)) | Answer: 0.001745 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.99 and bottoms xW = 0.03, with relative volatility alpha = 2.1. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.99, xw = 0.03, al = 2.1 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.99/0.01)(0.97/0.03)] / ln(2.1) | Answer: 10.88 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.78 and x = 0.27. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.78, x = 0.27 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.78/0.22) / (0.27/0.73) | Answer: 9.586

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.9 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 105 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.9, Psat = 105 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.9 * 105 | Answer: 94.5 kPa

question: A stream of 1.8 kg/s with specific heat 3.9 kJ/kg-K is heated through 80 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 1.8, cp = 3.9, dT = 80 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 1.8*3.9*80 | Answer: 561.6 kW

question: A reactor of volume 12.6 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 4.3 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 12.6, Q = 4.3 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 12.6 / 4.3 | Answer: 2.93 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 4.5e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 3 mm with a concentration difference of 20 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 4.5, L = 3, dC = 20 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (4.5e-9)*20 / (3e-3) | Answer: 30 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 10 min and steady-state gain 3.5. For a step input of magnitude 18, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 10, K = 3.5, M = 18 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 3.5 * 18 | Answer: 63 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 50 m^2 flies at 250 m/s (air density 0.7 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.5. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 50, V = 250, rho = 0.7, CL = 0.5 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.7*(250)^2*50*0.5 / 1000 | Answer: 546.9 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 30 m^2 flies at 200 m/s (density 1 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.06. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 30, V = 200, rho = 1, CD = 0.06 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*1*(200)^2*30*0.06 / 1000 | Answer: 36 kN

question: A specimen under stress 180 MPa shows an elastic strain of 1e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 180, eps = 1 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 180 / (1e-3) MPa = 180 GPa | Answer: 180 GPa

question: A block of mass 7 kg has a volume of 4e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 7, V = 4 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 7 / (4e-3) | Answer: 1750 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 1900 mm is heated through 90 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 12e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 1900, dT = 90, al = 12 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 1900*12e-6*90 | Answer: 2.052 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 55 ohm, R2 = 195 ohm and R3 = 220 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 55, R2 = 195, R3 = 220 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 195*220 / 55 | Answer: 780 ohm

question: Annual demand is 8500 units, ordering cost 30 per order and holding cost 2 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 8500, S = 30, H = 2 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*8500*30 / 2) | Answer: 505 units

question: An asset costs 300000 with salvage value 14000 after 17 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 300000, Sv = 14000, n = 17 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (300000 - 14000) / 17 | Answer: 16824 per year

question: A product sells for 460 per unit with variable cost 120 per unit and fixed costs 45000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 460, V = 120, F = 45000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 45000 / (460 - 120) | Answer: 132.4 units

question: Find the present worth of 170000 received 4 years from now at an interest rate of 10% per year.
solution: Given: F = 170000, n = 4, i = 10 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 170000 / (1 + 0.1)^4 | Answer: 116112 currency units

question: A process produces 12 defective items in a batch of 4500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 12, N = 4500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 12/4500 * 1e6 | Answer: 2667 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -6x^3 + 4x^2 - 8x + 5 evaluated at x = -5.
For f(x) = x^3 + x^2 + 8x + 6, find f''(x) at x = 0.
Evaluate the definite integral of (-x^2 + 4x + 1) dx from x = -2 to x = 4.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = -1x^3/3 + 4x^2/2 + 1x | Evaluate F(4) - F(-2) | Answer: 6
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 5x^2 + 10x - 7 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[-6, 5], [6, -3]].
solution: Given: a = -6, b = 5, c = 6, d = -3 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (-6)(-3) - (5)(6) | Answer: -12

question: Find the determinant of [[1, -2, -2], [5, 4, -3], [4, 1, 0]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: 49

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[-7, -7], [-8, 4]].
solution: Trace tr = -3, Determinant = -84 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 7.787

question: Solve for x: -5x + -3y = -6 and -3x + -1y = 2.
