solution: Determinant = -5*-1 - -3*-3 = -4 | x = (e d - b f) / det = -3 | Answer: x = -3
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 81, 98, 83, 10, 85.
solution: Sum = 357 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 71.4 | Answer: 71.4

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 42, 4, 15, 22, 13.
solution: Mean = 19.2 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 14.27

question: Find the slope of the line through (-8, 4) and (-7, 9).
solution: Given: x1 = -8, y1 = 4, x2 = -7, y2 = 9 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (9 - 4) / (-7 - -8) | Answer: 5

question: Find the distance between the points (2, 6) and (-8, 3).
solution: Given: x1 = 2, y1 = 6, x2 = -8, y2 = 3 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-10)^2 + (-3)^2) | Answer: 10.44 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (4,-1), (-1,5), (-5,7).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 7 sq units

question: Find the 39th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 10 and common difference -3.
solution: Given: a = 10, d = -3, n = 39 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = 10 + (39 - 1)*-3 | Answer: -104

question: Find the sum of the first 6 terms of an AP with first term 3 and common difference 4.
solution: Given: a = 3, d = 4, n = 6 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 6/2 [2*3 + (6-1)*4] | Answer: 78

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 24000 at 5.2% per annum for 1 years.
solution: Given: P = 24000, R = 5.2, Tt = 1 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 24000 * 5.2 * 1 / 100 | Answer: 1248 currency units

question: Find the amount when 14500 is invested at 4.7% per annum compounded annually for 4 years.
solution: Given: P = 14500, R = 4.7, Tt = 4 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 14500 * (1 + 4.7/100)^4 | Answer: 17424 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (-1, 4, 5) and (-4, 7, 7).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (-3, -1, -3) and (-3, -5, -4).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 16.55

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (5, 4, 2) and (6, 6, 2).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 7.352 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -2x^3 - 3x^2 + 7x + 6 at x = 2.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-58 with initial guess x0=15, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.9 and ordinates 4, 14, 10, 16, 10, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 589 and 12.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 589 and 12 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 59 and 25.
solution: Given: a = 59, b = 25 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 59*25 / 1 | Answer: 1475
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 24 mm carries an axial tensile load of 50 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 22 mm and length 2200 mm carries an axial load of 88 kN. Take E = 110 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 49 mm transmits a torque of 100 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 49, Tt = 100 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(100*1000) / (pi*(49)^3) | Answer: 4.329 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 48 mm and length 1200 mm carries a torque of 1800 N-m. With G = 80 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (48)^4 / 32 = 521153 mm^4 | theta = (1800*1000)(1200) / (80000 * 521153) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 2.968 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 121 mm wide and 160 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 121, h = 160 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 121*(160)^2 / 6 | Answer: 516267 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (81 mm x 220 mm) carries a bending moment of 25 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (41 mm x 150 mm) has effective length 2500 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 530 MPa is designed for a working stress of 200 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 530, sw = 200 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 530 / 200 | Answer: 2.65

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 550 mm and wall thickness 16 mm carries an internal pressure of 1.3 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 550, t = 16, P = 1.3 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 1.3*550 / (2*16) | Answer: 22.34 MPa

question: A Carnot engine operates between 980 K and 450 K. Find its thermal efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Th = 980, Tc = 450 | Formula: eta = 1 - Tc/Th | Substitute: eta = (1 - 450/980) * 100 | Answer: 54.08 %

question: 5.4 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 170 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 5.4, dT = 170 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 5.4 * 0.718 * 170 | Answer: 659.1 kJ

question: 2.4 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 185 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.4, dT = 185 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 2.4 * 1.005 * 185 | Answer: 446.2 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 1 m^3 at 370 K with mass 4.4 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 1, Tk = 370, m = 4.4 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 4.4*0.287*370 / 1 | Answer: 467.2 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 3.8 kg of air expands isothermally at 360 K from volume V1 to 5*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.8, Tk = 360, ratio = 5 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 3.8*0.287*360*ln(5) | Answer: 631.9 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 3.9 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.27 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 3.9, D = 0.27 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*3.9*0.27 / 0.001 | Answer: 1053000

question: Water flows at 3.3 m/s through a pipe of diameter 140 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 6 m. Taking Cv = 0.98, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 6, cv = 0.98 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.98*sqrt(2*9.81*6) | Answer: 10.63 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 320 mm) water flows at 3 m/s. It contracts to diameter 130 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 320, d2 = 130, V1 = 3 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 3*(320/130)^2 | Answer: 18.18 m/s

question: Water flows at 1.8 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.14 m and length 110 m. With friction factor f = 0.021, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 29 teeth drives a gear of 53 teeth. If the pinion runs at 300 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 29, z2 = 53, N1 = 300 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 300*29 / 53 | Answer: 164.2 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 470 mm rotates at 950 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 470, N = 950 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.47)*950 / 60 | Answer: 23.38 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 44.2 kW at 1450 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 44.2, N = 1450 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(44.2*1000) / (2*pi*1450) | Answer: 291.1 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 4.9 kg rotates at radius 0.11 m at 900 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 19800 N/m and mass 16.4 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 19800, m = 16.4 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(19800/16.4) | Answer: 5.53 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 7.2 m^2 and thickness 0.22 m has conductivity k = 19.4 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 35 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 7.2, L = 0.22, k = 19.4, dT = 35 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 19.4*7.2*35 / 0.22 | Answer: 22222 W

question: A surface of area 2.9 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 45 W/m^2-K to surroundings 85 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 2.9, h = 45, dT = 85 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 45*2.9*85 | Answer: 11092 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 240 m/min, feed = 0.27 mm/rev, depth of cut = 0.6 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 240, f = 0.27, d = 0.6 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*240*0.27*0.6 | Answer: 38880 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 360 mm is turned at 750 rpm with a feed of 0.36 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 360, N = 750, f = 0.36 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 360 / (0.36*750) | Answer: 1.333 min

question: A resistor of 173 ohm carries a current of 0.2 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 173, I = 0.2 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 0.2 * 173 | Answer: 34.6 V

question: Three resistors 61 ohm, 74 ohm and 89 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 61, R2 = 74, R3 = 89 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 61 + 74 + 89 | Answer: 224 ohm

question: Two resistors 42 ohm and 43 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 42, R2 = 43 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 42*43 / (42+43) | Answer: 21.25 ohm

question: A device draws 5.2 A at 70 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 70, I = 5.2 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 70 * 5.2 | Answer: 364 W

question: A current of 11.7 A flows through a 2 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 11.7, R = 2 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (11.7)^2 * 2 | Answer: 273.8 W

question: Two capacitors 38.6 uF and 8.4 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 38.6, C2 = 8.4 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 38.6*8.4 / (38.6+8.4) | Answer: 6.899 uF

question: A resistor 62 kohm and capacitor 18.2 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 62, C = 18.2 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (62k)(18.2u) = 1128 ms | Answer: 1128 ms

question: An inductor 269.2 mH is in series with 25 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 269.2, R = 25 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (269.2e-3) / 25 | Answer: 10.77 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 82.6 mH inductor at 910 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 82.6, f = 910 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (910)(82.6e-3) | Answer: 472.3 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 2.9 uF capacitor at 590 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 2.9, f = 590 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (590)(2.9e-6)) | Answer: 93.02 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 51 ohm, XL = 99 ohm and XC = 80 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 51, XL = 99, XC = 80 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(51^2 + (99 - 80)^2) | Answer: 54.42 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 93.7 mH and C = 4.3 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 93.7, C = 4.3 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(93.7e-3 * 4.3e-6)) | Answer: 250.7 Hz

question: A capacitor of 28.3 uF is charged to 15 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 28.3, V = 15 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*28.3e-6*(15)^2 | Answer: 3.184 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 290 V with 340 primary turns and 410 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 290, N1 = 340, N2 = 410 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 290 * 410/340 | Answer: 349.7 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 140 V and draws an armature current of 24 A. If the armature resistance is 0.96 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 140, Ia = 24, Ra = 0.96 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 140 - 24*0.96 | Answer: 117 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 160 A at 433 V (line) with a power factor of 0.85. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 160, VL = 433, pf = 0.85 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*433*160*0.85 / 1000 | Answer: 102 kW

question: A load has real power 140 kW and apparent power 165 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 140, S = 165 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 140 / 165 | Answer: 0.8485

question: A machine delivers 125 kW output while drawing 212 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 125, Pi = 212 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 125/212 * 100 | Answer: 58.96 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 25 V across R1 = 5 ohm and R2 = 13 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 25, R1 = 5, R2 = 13 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 25*13 / (5+13) | Answer: 18.06 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 90 kohm and Rin = 24 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 90, Rin = 24 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 90 / 24 | Answer: 3.75

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 200 kohm and Rg = 33 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 200, Rg = 33 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 200/33 | Answer: 7.061

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 8514. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 8514 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(8514) | Answer: 39.3 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 8.2 m carries a central point load of 65 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 8.2, W = 65 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 65*8.2 / 4 | Answer: 133.2 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.6 m carries a UDL of 40 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.6, w = 40 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 40*(4.6)^2 / 8 | Answer: 105.8 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 5.9 m carries a UDL of 26 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.9, w = 26 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 26*(5.9)^2 / 2 | Answer: 452.5 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.9 m carries a point load 40 kN at distance 1.1 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 6.9, a = 1.1, W = 40 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 40*(6.9 - 1.1) / 6.9 | Answer: 33.62 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 6.4 m) carries a central point load 30 kN. With E = 25 GPa and I = 100e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=30000 N, L=6400.0 mm, E=25000 MPa, I=100e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 65.54 mm

question: An RC beam has overall depth 350 mm, clear cover 50 mm and main bars of diameter 25 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 350, c = 50, dia = 25 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 350 - 50 - 25/2 | Answer: 287.5 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 33.1 m^2 carrying a factored load of 17.8 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 33.1, w = 17.8 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 17.8 * 33.1 | Answer: 589.2 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 5.8 m, unit weight 16 kN/m^3, phi = 36 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 3.8e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1, area = 1.7e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 3.8, i = 1, A = 1.7 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (3.8e-4)*1*(1.7e-3) | Answer: 646 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 0.6 m, bed slope 0.004 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.015. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 1.7 m under a head of 0.4 m. Taking Cd = 0.61 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 4.7 m wide carries a discharge of 23.5 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A tank of volume 390 m^3 treats a flow of 110 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 390, Q = 110 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 390 / 110 | Answer: 3.545 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 250 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.27 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 3 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 250, k = 0.27, t = 3 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 250*(1 - e^(-0.27*3)) | Answer: 138.8 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.89, rainfall intensity 45 mm/h over a catchment of 40.6 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.89, i = 45, A = 40.6 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.89*45*40.6 / 360 | Answer: 4.517 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.08 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 420 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.08, M = 420 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 420*(20+0.08)/20 | Answer: 421.7 m

question: Convert the decimal number 3557 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 3557 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: DE5 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 00110001 and 00111101.
solution: XOR: 00001100 | Count of 1s = 2 | Answer: 2
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 660 megabits is sent over a link of 31 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 660, B = 31 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 660 / 31 | Answer: 21.29 s

question: A link has bandwidth 10 Mbps and round-trip time 180 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 10, R = 180 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 10e6 * 180e-3 bits = 1800 kb | Answer: 1800 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.94, cache access time 3 ns and main-memory access time 150 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.94, tc = 3, tm = 150 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.94*3 + (1 - 0.94)*150 | Answer: 11.82 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 752966 elements?
solution: Given: n = 752966 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(752966)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.017, memory access time 170 ns and page-fault service time 3 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 3 ms = 3000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.017)*170 + 0.017*3000000.0 ns | Answer: 51.17 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 1.8 m^3 at 410 kPa and 400 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 1.8, P = 410, Tk = 400 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (410e3)*1.8 / (8.314*400) | Answer: 221.9 mol

question: For a reaction with A = 2e10 /s and activation energy 55 kJ/mol at 440 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 2, Ea = 55, Tk = 440 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 2e10 * exp(-55e3 / (8.314*440)) | Answer: 5908 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.95 and bottoms xW = 0.05, with relative volatility alpha = 2.8. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.95, xw = 0.05, al = 2.8 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.95/0.05)(0.95/0.05)] / ln(2.8) | Answer: 5.719 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.84 and x = 0.42. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.84, x = 0.42 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.84/0.16) / (0.42/0.58) | Answer: 7.25

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.57 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 45 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.57, Psat = 45 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.57 * 45 | Answer: 25.65 kPa

question: A stream of 5.5 kg/s with specific heat 3.2 kJ/kg-K is heated through 115 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 5.5, cp = 3.2, dT = 115 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 5.5*3.2*115 | Answer: 2024 kW

question: A reactor of volume 8.4 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 2.3 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 8.4, Q = 2.3 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 8.4 / 2.3 | Answer: 3.652 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 6.1e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 1 mm with a concentration difference of 40 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 6.1, L = 1, dC = 40 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (6.1e-9)*40 / (1e-3) | Answer: 244 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 7.8 min and steady-state gain 1.5. For a step input of magnitude 2, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 7.8, K = 1.5, M = 2 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 1.5 * 2 | Answer: 3 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 60 m^2 flies at 90 m/s (air density 0.7 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 1.3. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 60, V = 90, rho = 0.7, CL = 1.3 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.7*(90)^2*60*1.3 / 1000 | Answer: 221.1 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 30 m^2 flies at 210 m/s (density 0.7 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.05. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 30, V = 210, rho = 0.7, CD = 0.05 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.7*(210)^2*30*0.05 / 1000 | Answer: 23.15 kN

question: A specimen under stress 360 MPa shows an elastic strain of 0.9e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 360, eps = 0.9 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 360 / (0.9e-3) MPa = 400 GPa | Answer: 400 GPa

question: A block of mass 35 kg has a volume of 3.8e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 35, V = 3.8 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 35 / (3.8e-3) | Answer: 9211 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 2300 mm is heated through 135 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 11e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 2300, dT = 135, al = 11 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 2300*11e-6*135 | Answer: 3.415 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 135 ohm, R2 = 10 ohm and R3 = 415 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 135, R2 = 10, R3 = 415 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 10*415 / 135 | Answer: 30.74 ohm

question: Annual demand is 22000 units, ordering cost 230 per order and holding cost 31 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 22000, S = 230, H = 31 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*22000*230 / 31) | Answer: 571.4 units

question: An asset costs 340000 with salvage value 2000 after 19 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 340000, Sv = 2000, n = 19 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (340000 - 2000) / 19 | Answer: 17789 per year

question: A product sells for 310 per unit with variable cost 120 per unit and fixed costs 45000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 310, V = 120, F = 45000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 45000 / (310 - 120) | Answer: 236.8 units

question: Find the present worth of 100000 received 4 years from now at an interest rate of 12% per year.
solution: Given: F = 100000, n = 4, i = 12 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 100000 / (1 + 0.12)^4 | Answer: 63552 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.99, 0.95 and 0.91 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.99, r2 = 0.95, r3 = 0.91 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.99*0.95*0.91 | Answer: 0.8559

question: A process produces 50 defective items in a batch of 6000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 50, N = 6000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 50/6000 * 1e6 | Answer: 8333 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = 2x^3 + 6x^2 - 2x - 2 evaluated at x = 1.
For f(x) = -x^3 - 2x^2 + 6x - 3, find f''(x) at x = 5.
Evaluate the definite integral of (-x^2 + 2x + 4) dx from x = 1 to x = 3.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = -1x^3/3 + 2x^2/2 + 4x | Evaluate F(3) - F(1) | Answer: 7.333
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 2x^2 - 2x = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[-1, 2], [6, -8]].
solution: Given: a = -1, b = 2, c = 6, d = -8 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (-1)(-8) - (2)(6) | Answer: -4

question: Find the determinant of [[6, -2, 5], [-6, 3, 5], [-6, 6, 5]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: -180

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[2, 0], [5, 6]].
solution: Trace tr = 8, Determinant = 12 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 6

question: Solve for x: 2x + 6y = -4 and -1x + 0y = -5.
solution: Determinant = 2*0 - 6*-1 = 6 | x = (e d - b f) / det = 5 | Answer: x = 5
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 94, 1, 32, 35, 77.
solution: Sum = 239 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 47.8 | Answer: 47.8

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 28, 11, 27, 9, 11.
solution: Mean = 17.2 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 9.445

question: Find the slope of the line through (-9, -1) and (6, -4).
solution: Given: x1 = -9, y1 = -1, x2 = 6, y2 = -4 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (-4 - -1) / (6 - -9) | Answer: -0.2

question: Find the distance between the points (3, 7) and (-7, -5).
solution: Given: x1 = 3, y1 = 7, x2 = -7, y2 = -5 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-10)^2 + (-12)^2) | Answer: 15.62 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (5,7), (4,-2), (8,1).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 16.5 sq units

question: Find the 26th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -19 and common difference -9.
solution: Given: a = -19, d = -9, n = 26 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -19 + (26 - 1)*-9 | Answer: -244

question: Find the sum of the first 10 terms of an AP with first term -11 and common difference -5.
solution: Given: a = -11, d = -5, n = 10 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 10/2 [2*-11 + (10-1)*-5] | Answer: -335

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 26000 at 4.8% per annum for 5 years.
solution: Given: P = 26000, R = 4.8, Tt = 5 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 26000 * 4.8 * 5 / 100 | Answer: 6240 currency units

question: Find the amount when 29500 is invested at 9.6% per annum compounded annually for 3 years.
solution: Given: P = 29500, R = 9.6, Tt = 3 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 29500 * (1 + 9.6/100)^3 | Answer: 38838 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (6, -1, 3) and (0, -4, -5).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (-2, 2, -4) and (-3, 2, -5).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 3.464

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (5, -6, -4) and (5, -2, 5).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 74.71 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number -12 + 10i.
solution: Given: a = -12, b = 10 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((-12)^2 + (10)^2) | Answer: 15.62

question: Evaluate f(x) = -5x^3 - 5x^2 + 4x + 5 at x = -1.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-147 with initial guess x0=14, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.2 and ordinates 8, 12, 5, 3, 20, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 343 and 595.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 343 and 595 | Answer: GCD = 7

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 24 and 79.
solution: Given: a = 24, b = 79 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 24*79 / 1 | Answer: 1896
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 41 mm carries an axial tensile load of 66 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 27 mm and length 1400 mm carries an axial load of 71 kN. Take E = 210 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 54 mm transmits a torque of 2000 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 54, Tt = 2000 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(2000*1000) / (pi*(54)^3) | Answer: 64.69 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 49 mm and length 1000 mm carries a torque of 200 N-m. With G = 45 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (49)^4 / 32 = 565958 mm^4 | theta = (200*1000)(1000) / (45000 * 565958) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 0.4499 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 91 mm wide and 240 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 91, h = 240 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 91*(240)^2 / 6 | Answer: 873600 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (84 mm x 240 mm) carries a bending moment of 21 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (62 mm x 110 mm) has effective length 2700 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 610 MPa is designed for a working stress of 210 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 610, sw = 210 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 610 / 210 | Answer: 2.905

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1300 mm and wall thickness 11 mm carries an internal pressure of 2.9 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1300, t = 11, P = 2.9 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 2.9*1300 / (2*11) | Answer: 171.4 MPa

question: 4.2 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 70 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.2, dT = 70 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 4.2 * 0.718 * 70 | Answer: 211.1 kJ

question: 1.7 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 150 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1.7, dT = 150 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 1.7 * 1.005 * 150 | Answer: 256.3 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 3.9 m^3 at 550 K with mass 2.8 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 3.9, Tk = 550, m = 2.8 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 2.8*0.287*550 / 3.9 | Answer: 113.3 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 4.2 kg of air expands isothermally at 340 K from volume V1 to 2*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.2, Tk = 340, ratio = 2 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 4.2*0.287*340*ln(2) | Answer: 284.1 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 2.2 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.3 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 2.2, D = 0.3 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*2.2*0.3 / 0.001 | Answer: 660000

question: Water flows at 0.7 m/s through a pipe of diameter 160 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 13.9 m. Taking Cv = 0.97, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 13.9, cv = 0.97 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.97*sqrt(2*9.81*13.9) | Answer: 16.02 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 180 mm) water flows at 1.8 m/s. It contracts to diameter 110 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 180, d2 = 110, V1 = 1.8 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 1.8*(180/110)^2 | Answer: 4.82 m/s

question: Water flows at 2.2 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.18 m and length 150 m. With friction factor f = 0.02, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 18 teeth drives a gear of 69 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1350 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 18, z2 = 69, N1 = 1350 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1350*18 / 69 | Answer: 352.2 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 520 mm rotates at 1050 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 520, N = 1050 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.52)*1050 / 60 | Answer: 28.59 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 34.7 kW at 1150 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 34.7, N = 1150 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(34.7*1000) / (2*pi*1150) | Answer: 288.1 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 0.9 kg rotates at radius 0.24 m at 1150 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 19600 N/m and mass 1 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 19600, m = 1 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(19600/1) | Answer: 22.28 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 2.8 m^2 and thickness 0.35 m has conductivity k = 8.4 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 170 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 2.8, L = 0.35, k = 8.4, dT = 170 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 8.4*2.8*170 / 0.35 | Answer: 11424 W

question: A surface of area 2.6 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 50 W/m^2-K to surroundings 45 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 2.6, h = 50, dT = 45 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 50*2.6*45 | Answer: 5850 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 60 m/min, feed = 0.28 mm/rev, depth of cut = 0.7 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 60, f = 0.28, d = 0.7 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*60*0.28*0.7 | Answer: 11760 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 410 mm is turned at 550 rpm with a feed of 0.21 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 410, N = 550, f = 0.21 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 410 / (0.21*550) | Answer: 3.55 min

question: A resistor of 161 ohm carries a current of 8.5 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 161, I = 8.5 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 8.5 * 161 | Answer: 1368 V

question: Three resistors 47 ohm, 91 ohm and 59 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 47, R2 = 91, R3 = 59 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 47 + 91 + 59 | Answer: 197 ohm

question: Two resistors 110 ohm and 109 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 110, R2 = 109 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 110*109 / (110+109) | Answer: 54.75 ohm

question: A device draws 3.5 A at 125 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 125, I = 3.5 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 125 * 3.5 | Answer: 437.5 W

question: A current of 1.2 A flows through a 145 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 1.2, R = 145 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (1.2)^2 * 145 | Answer: 208.8 W

question: Two capacitors 30 uF and 3.1 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 30, C2 = 3.1 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 30*3.1 / (30+3.1) | Answer: 2.81 uF

question: A resistor 96 kohm and capacitor 2.2 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 96, C = 2.2 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (96k)(2.2u) = 211.2 ms | Answer: 211.2 ms

question: An inductor 431.4 mH is in series with 93 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 431.4, R = 93 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (431.4e-3) / 93 | Answer: 4.639 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 169.7 mH inductor at 110 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 169.7, f = 110 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (110)(169.7e-3) | Answer: 117.3 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 12 uF capacitor at 620 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 12, f = 620 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (620)(12e-6)) | Answer: 21.39 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 18 ohm, XL = 62 ohm and XC = 73 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 18, XL = 62, XC = 73 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(18^2 + (62 - 73)^2) | Answer: 21.1 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 63.9 mH and C = 6.9 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 63.9, C = 6.9 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(63.9e-3 * 6.9e-6)) | Answer: 239.7 Hz

question: A capacitor of 13.9 uF is charged to 60 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 13.9, V = 60 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*13.9e-6*(60)^2 | Answer: 25.02 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 250 V with 730 primary turns and 340 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 250, N1 = 730, N2 = 340 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 250 * 340/730 | Answer: 116.4 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 120 V and draws an armature current of 52 A. If the armature resistance is 0.42 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 120, Ia = 52, Ra = 0.42 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 120 - 52*0.42 | Answer: 98.16 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 165 A at 415 V (line) with a power factor of 0.82. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 165, VL = 415, pf = 0.82 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*415*165*0.82 / 1000 | Answer: 97.25 kW

question: A load has real power 70 kW and apparent power 120 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 70, S = 120 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 70 / 120 | Answer: 0.5833

question: A machine delivers 120 kW output while drawing 212 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 120, Pi = 212 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 120/212 * 100 | Answer: 56.6 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 8 V across R1 = 33 ohm and R2 = 45 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 8, R1 = 33, R2 = 45 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 8*45 / (33+45) | Answer: 4.615 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 220 kohm and Rin = 22 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 220, Rin = 22 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 220 / 22 | Answer: 10

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 60 kohm and Rg = 14 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 60, Rg = 14 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 60/14 | Answer: 5.286

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 6197. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 6197 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(6197) | Answer: 37.92 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 3.9 m carries a central point load of 50 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.9, W = 50 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 50*3.9 / 4 | Answer: 48.75 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 3.1 m carries a UDL of 5 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.1, w = 5 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 5*(3.1)^2 / 8 | Answer: 6.006 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 3.6 m carries a UDL of 34 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.6, w = 34 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 34*(3.6)^2 / 2 | Answer: 220.3 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.3 m carries a point load 35 kN at distance 2.3 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 9.3, a = 2.3, W = 35 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 35*(9.3 - 2.3) / 9.3 | Answer: 26.34 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 5.6 m) carries a central point load 40 kN. With E = 25 GPa and I = 580e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=40000 N, L=5600.0 mm, E=25000 MPa, I=580e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 10.09 mm

question: An RC beam has overall depth 510 mm, clear cover 40 mm and main bars of diameter 25 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 510, c = 40, dia = 25 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 510 - 40 - 25/2 | Answer: 457.5 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 35.1 m^2 carrying a factored load of 11 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 35.1, w = 11 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 11 * 35.1 | Answer: 386.1 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 3.2 m, unit weight 16 kN/m^3, phi = 29 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 8.3e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.5, area = 8e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 8.3, i = 0.5, A = 8 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (8.3e-4)*0.5*(8e-3) | Answer: 3320 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.5 m, bed slope 0.007 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.013. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 4.7 m under a head of 0.6 m. Taking Cd = 0.62 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 5.4 m wide carries a discharge of 8.1 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A tank of volume 990 m^3 treats a flow of 195 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 990, Q = 195 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 990 / 195 | Answer: 5.077 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 220 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.14 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 7 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 220, k = 0.14, t = 7 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 220*(1 - e^(-0.14*7)) | Answer: 137.4 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.73, rainfall intensity 110 mm/h over a catchment of 58.7 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.73, i = 110, A = 58.7 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.73*110*58.7 / 360 | Answer: 13.09 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.08 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 730 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.08, M = 730 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 730*(20+0.08)/20 | Answer: 732.9 m

question: Convert the decimal number 3760 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 3760 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: EB0 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 10101011 and 11110101.
solution: XOR: 01011110 | Count of 1s = 5 | Answer: 5
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 190 megabits is sent over a link of 74 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 190, B = 74 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 190 / 74 | Answer: 2.568 s

question: A link has bandwidth 38 Mbps and round-trip time 20 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 38, R = 20 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 38e6 * 20e-3 bits = 760 kb | Answer: 760 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.83, cache access time 6 ns and main-memory access time 100 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.83, tc = 6, tm = 100 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.83*6 + (1 - 0.83)*100 | Answer: 21.98 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 222777 elements?
solution: Given: n = 222777 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(222777)) + 1 | Answer: 18

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.015, memory access time 110 ns and page-fault service time 9 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 9 ms = 9000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.015)*110 + 0.015*9000000.0 ns | Answer: 135.1 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 1.2 m^3 at 360 kPa and 400 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 1.2, P = 360, Tk = 400 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (360e3)*1.2 / (8.314*400) | Answer: 129.9 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.3 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 12 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.3, t = 12 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.3*12) | Answer: 0.9727

question: For a reaction with A = 4e10 /s and activation energy 75 kJ/mol at 380 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 4, Ea = 75, Tk = 380 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 4e10 * exp(-75e3 / (8.314*380)) | Answer: 1.96 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.96 and bottoms xW = 0.1, with relative volatility alpha = 2.3. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.96, xw = 0.1, al = 2.3 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.96/0.04)(0.9/0.1)] / ln(2.3) | Answer: 6.454 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.77 and x = 0.38. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.77, x = 0.38 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.77/0.23) / (0.38/0.62) | Answer: 5.462

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.34 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 95 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.34, Psat = 95 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.34 * 95 | Answer: 32.3 kPa

question: A stream of 6.4 kg/s with specific heat 3 kJ/kg-K is heated through 120 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 6.4, cp = 3, dT = 120 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 6.4*3*120 | Answer: 2304 kW

question: A reactor of volume 11.2 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 2.5 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 11.2, Q = 2.5 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 11.2 / 2.5 | Answer: 4.48 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 8e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 4 mm with a concentration difference of 90 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 8, L = 4, dC = 90 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (8e-9)*90 / (4e-3) | Answer: 180 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 4.3 min and steady-state gain 1. For a step input of magnitude 18, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 4.3, K = 1, M = 18 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 1 * 18 | Answer: 18 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 95 m^2 flies at 180 m/s (air density 1 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.6. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 95, V = 180, rho = 1, CL = 0.6 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1*(180)^2*95*0.6 / 1000 | Answer: 923.4 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 20 m^2 flies at 260 m/s (density 0.7 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.06. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 20, V = 260, rho = 0.7, CD = 0.06 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.7*(260)^2*20*0.06 / 1000 | Answer: 28.39 kN

question: A specimen under stress 270 MPa shows an elastic strain of 0.8e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 270, eps = 0.8 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 270 / (0.8e-3) MPa = 337.5 GPa | Answer: 337.5 GPa

question: A block of mass 5 kg has a volume of 0.7e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 5, V = 0.7 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 5 / (0.7e-3) | Answer: 7143 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 2200 mm is heated through 30 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 17e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 2200, dT = 30, al = 17 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 2200*17e-6*30 | Answer: 1.122 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 15 ohm, R2 = 140 ohm and R3 = 85 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 15, R2 = 140, R3 = 85 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 140*85 / 15 | Answer: 793.3 ohm

question: Annual demand is 39500 units, ordering cost 160 per order and holding cost 37 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 39500, S = 160, H = 37 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*39500*160 / 37) | Answer: 584.5 units

question: An asset costs 440000 with salvage value 40000 after 14 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 440000, Sv = 40000, n = 14 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (440000 - 40000) / 14 | Answer: 28571 per year

question: A product sells for 100 per unit with variable cost 90 per unit and fixed costs 50000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 100, V = 90, F = 50000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 50000 / (100 - 90) | Answer: 5000 units

question: Find the present worth of 195000 received 10 years from now at an interest rate of 5% per year.
solution: Given: F = 195000, n = 10, i = 5 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 195000 / (1 + 0.05)^10 | Answer: 119713 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.94, 0.98 and 0.93 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.94, r2 = 0.98, r3 = 0.93 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.94*0.98*0.93 | Answer: 0.8567

question: A process produces 36 defective items in a batch of 18000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 36, N = 18000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 36/18000 * 1e6 | Answer: 2000 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -6x^3 - 4x^2 + 5x + 1 evaluated at x = 0.
For f(x) = -5x^3 - 7x^2 + 7x - 8, find f''(x) at x = 4.
Evaluate the definite integral of (5x^2 + 3x - 4) dx from x = 1 to x = 5.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = 5x^3/3 + 3x^2/2 + -4x | Evaluate F(5) - F(1) | Answer: 226.7
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 3x^2 + 6x - 9 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[-9, -2], [1, 0]].
solution: Given: a = -9, b = -2, c = 1, d = 0 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (-9)(0) - (-2)(1) | Answer: 2

question: Find the determinant of [[5, 0, 3], [-1, 5, 0], [-3, -5, -6]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: -90

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[0, 0], [8, -6]].
solution: Trace tr = -6, Determinant = 0 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 0

question: Solve for x: -1x + -4y = 6 and 3x + -5y = 4.
solution: Determinant = -1*-5 - -4*3 = 17 | x = (e d - b f) / det = -0.8235 | Answer: x = -0.8235
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 25, 10, 91, 27, 26.
solution: Sum = 179 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 35.8 | Answer: 35.8

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 20, 16, 7, 35, 6.
solution: Mean = 16.8 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 11.78

question: Find the slope of the line through (7, -5) and (2, -7).
solution: Given: x1 = 7, y1 = -5, x2 = 2, y2 = -7 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (-7 - -5) / (2 - 7) | Answer: 0.4

question: Find the distance between the points (-2, 9) and (1, 6).
solution: Given: x1 = -2, y1 = 9, x2 = 1, y2 = 6 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((3)^2 + (-3)^2) | Answer: 4.243 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (-7,-6), (-5,-1), (-6,7).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 10.5 sq units

question: Find the 7th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -5 and common difference 1.
solution: Given: a = -5, d = 1, n = 7 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -5 + (7 - 1)*1 | Answer: 1

question: Find the sum of the first 14 terms of an AP with first term 11 and common difference 6.
solution: Given: a = 11, d = 6, n = 14 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 14/2 [2*11 + (14-1)*6] | Answer: 700

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 50000 at 4.2% per annum for 6 years.
solution: Given: P = 50000, R = 4.2, Tt = 6 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 50000 * 4.2 * 6 / 100 | Answer: 12600 currency units

question: Find the amount when 7000 is invested at 11% per annum compounded annually for 4 years.
solution: Given: P = 7000, R = 11, Tt = 4 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 7000 * (1 + 11/100)^4 | Answer: 10626 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (5, 3, -6) and (5, 1, 8).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (6, 1, -6) and (5, 0, 6).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 66.46

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (2, -1, 3) and (-2, 5, -1).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 125.8 degrees

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number 9 + -2i.
solution: Given: a = 9, b = -2 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(-2, 9) | Answer: -12.53 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = 4x^3 - x^2 - 8x - 7 at x = 0.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-190 with initial guess x0=14, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=2 and ordinates 14, 9, 3, 0, 18, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 131 and 380.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 131 and 380 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 24 and 8.
solution: Given: a = 24, b = 8 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 24*8 / 8 | Answer: 24
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 36 mm carries an axial tensile load of 66 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 40 mm and length 2500 mm carries an axial load of 42 kN. Take E = 200 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 77 mm transmits a torque of 1200 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 77, Tt = 1200 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(1200*1000) / (pi*(77)^3) | Answer: 13.39 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 53 mm and length 1300 mm carries a torque of 1850 N-m. With G = 45 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (53)^4 / 32 = 774646 mm^4 | theta = (1850*1000)(1300) / (45000 * 774646) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 3.953 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 38 mm wide and 170 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 38, h = 170 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 38*(170)^2 / 6 | Answer: 183033 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (44 mm x 230 mm) carries a bending moment of 36 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (45 mm x 160 mm) has effective length 1800 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 840 MPa is designed for a working stress of 140 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 840, sw = 140 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 840 / 140 | Answer: 6

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 650 mm and wall thickness 17 mm carries an internal pressure of 1.6 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 650, t = 17, P = 1.6 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 1.6*650 / (2*17) | Answer: 30.59 MPa

question: 6.5 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 120 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 6.5, dT = 120 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 6.5 * 0.718 * 120 | Answer: 560 kJ

question: 6.5 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 50 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 6.5, dT = 50 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 6.5 * 1.005 * 50 | Answer: 326.6 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 3.3 m^3 at 540 K with mass 1.1 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 3.3, Tk = 540, m = 1.1 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 1.1*0.287*540 / 3.3 | Answer: 51.66 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 4.9 kg of air expands isothermally at 300 K from volume V1 to 3*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.9, Tk = 300, ratio = 3 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 4.9*0.287*300*ln(3) | Answer: 463.5 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 4.8 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.31 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 4.8, D = 0.31 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*4.8*0.31 / 0.001 | Answer: 1488000

question: Water flows at 3.9 m/s through a pipe of diameter 250 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
In a pipe (diameter 290 mm) water flows at 1.3 m/s. It contracts to diameter 70 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 290, d2 = 70, V1 = 1.3 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 1.3*(290/70)^2 | Answer: 22.31 m/s

question: Water flows at 3.9 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.31 m and length 140 m. With friction factor f = 0.03, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 18 teeth drives a gear of 85 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1400 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 18, z2 = 85, N1 = 1400 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1400*18 / 85 | Answer: 296.5 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 290 mm rotates at 300 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 290, N = 300 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.29)*300 / 60 | Answer: 4.555 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 29.3 kW at 1200 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 29.3, N = 1200 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(29.3*1000) / (2*pi*1200) | Answer: 233.2 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 1.1 kg rotates at radius 0.3 m at 850 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 18300 N/m and mass 12 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 18300, m = 12 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(18300/12) | Answer: 6.215 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 4.9 m^2 and thickness 0.15 m has conductivity k = 36 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 50 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 4.9, L = 0.15, k = 36, dT = 50 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 36*4.9*50 / 0.15 | Answer: 58800 W

question: A surface of area 4.3 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 95 W/m^2-K to surroundings 35 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 4.3, h = 95, dT = 35 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 95*4.3*35 | Answer: 14298 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 70 m/min, feed = 0.36 mm/rev, depth of cut = 0.5 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 70, f = 0.36, d = 0.5 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*70*0.36*0.5 | Answer: 12600 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 480 mm is turned at 750 rpm with a feed of 0.29 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 480, N = 750, f = 0.29 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 480 / (0.29*750) | Answer: 2.207 min

question: A resistor of 28 ohm carries a current of 6.2 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 28, I = 6.2 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 6.2 * 28 | Answer: 173.6 V

question: Three resistors 43 ohm, 33 ohm and 13 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 43, R2 = 33, R3 = 13 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 43 + 33 + 13 | Answer: 89 ohm

question: Two resistors 108 ohm and 86 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 108, R2 = 86 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 108*86 / (108+86) | Answer: 47.88 ohm

question: A device draws 7.1 A at 210 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 210, I = 7.1 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 210 * 7.1 | Answer: 1491 W

question: A current of 5.8 A flows through a 4 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 5.8, R = 4 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (5.8)^2 * 4 | Answer: 134.6 W

question: Two capacitors 49.5 uF and 21.3 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 49.5, C2 = 21.3 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 49.5*21.3 / (49.5+21.3) | Answer: 14.89 uF

question: A resistor 40 kohm and capacitor 17.1 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 40, C = 17.1 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (40k)(17.1u) = 684 ms | Answer: 684 ms

question: An inductor 247.6 mH is in series with 83 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 247.6, R = 83 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (247.6e-3) / 83 | Answer: 2.983 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 72.6 mH inductor at 390 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 72.6, f = 390 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (390)(72.6e-3) | Answer: 177.9 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 32.4 uF capacitor at 210 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 32.4, f = 210 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (210)(32.4e-6)) | Answer: 23.39 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 72 ohm, XL = 110 ohm and XC = 142 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 72, XL = 110, XC = 142 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(72^2 + (110 - 142)^2) | Answer: 78.79 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 67.3 mH and C = 7 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 67.3, C = 7 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(67.3e-3 * 7e-6)) | Answer: 231.9 Hz

question: A capacitor of 19.8 uF is charged to 160 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 19.8, V = 160 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*19.8e-6*(160)^2 | Answer: 253.4 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 140 V with 740 primary turns and 140 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 140, N1 = 740, N2 = 140 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 140 * 140/740 | Answer: 26.49 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 260 V and draws an armature current of 26 A. If the armature resistance is 0.64 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 260, Ia = 26, Ra = 0.64 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 260 - 26*0.64 | Answer: 243.4 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 180 A at 415 V (line) with a power factor of 0.82. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 180, VL = 415, pf = 0.82 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*415*180*0.82 / 1000 | Answer: 106.1 kW

question: A load has real power 140 kW and apparent power 155 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 140, S = 155 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 140 / 155 | Answer: 0.9032

question: A machine delivers 35 kW output while drawing 132 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 35, Pi = 132 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 35/132 * 100 | Answer: 26.52 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 24 V across R1 = 37 ohm and R2 = 27 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 24, R1 = 37, R2 = 27 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 24*27 / (37+27) | Answer: 10.12 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 20 kohm and Rin = 33 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 20, Rin = 33 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 20 / 33 | Answer: 0.6061

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 80 kohm and Rg = 42 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 80, Rg = 42 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 80/42 | Answer: 2.905

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 9857. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 9857 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(9857) | Answer: 39.94 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.9 m carries a central point load of 90 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6.9, W = 90 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 90*6.9 / 4 | Answer: 155.2 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 2.8 m carries a point load 20 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 2.8, W = 20 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 20*2.8 | Answer: 56 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 2.5 m carries a UDL of 38 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 2.5, w = 38 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 38*(2.5)^2 / 2 | Answer: 118.8 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.4 m carries a point load 80 kN at distance 1.4 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 9.4, a = 1.4, W = 80 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 80*(9.4 - 1.4) / 9.4 | Answer: 68.09 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 5.6 m) carries a central point load 80 kN. With E = 25 GPa and I = 110e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=80000 N, L=5600.0 mm, E=25000 MPa, I=110e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 106.4 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 4.2 m carries a UDL of 42 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.2, w = 42 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 42*(4.2)^2 / 12 | Answer: 61.74 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 700 mm, clear cover 45 mm and main bars of diameter 16 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 700, c = 45, dia = 16 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 700 - 45 - 16/2 | Answer: 647 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 10.4 m^2 carrying a factored load of 19.7 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 10.4, w = 19.7 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 19.7 * 10.4 | Answer: 204.9 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 4.1 m, unit weight 19 kN/m^3, phi = 38 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 7.1e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1, area = 1.6e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 7.1, i = 1, A = 1.6 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (7.1e-4)*1*(1.6e-3) | Answer: 1136 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 0.6 m, bed slope 0.007 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.028. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 2.5 m under a head of 0.4 m. Taking Cd = 0.63 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 5.6 m wide carries a discharge of 29.4 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 150 m and design speed 70 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 150, V = 70 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (70)^2 / (127*150) | Answer: 0.2572
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: A tank of volume 180 m^3 treats a flow of 125 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 180, Q = 125 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 180 / 125 | Answer: 1.44 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 200 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.2 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 6 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 200, k = 0.2, t = 6 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 200*(1 - e^(-0.2*6)) | Answer: 139.8 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.87, rainfall intensity 30 mm/h over a catchment of 50 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.87, i = 30, A = 50 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.87*30*50 / 360 | Answer: 3.625 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.01 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 540 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.01, M = 540 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 540*(20+0.01)/20 | Answer: 540.3 m

question: Convert the decimal number 2451 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 2451 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 993 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 10001010 and 11101001.
solution: XOR: 01100011 | Count of 1s = 4 | Answer: 4
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 220 megabits is sent over a link of 10 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 220, B = 10 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 220 / 10 | Answer: 22 s

question: A link has bandwidth 52 Mbps and round-trip time 150 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 52, R = 150 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 52e6 * 150e-3 bits = 7800 kb | Answer: 7800 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.88, cache access time 4 ns and main-memory access time 100 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.88, tc = 4, tm = 100 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.88*4 + (1 - 0.88)*100 | Answer: 15.52 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 71890 elements?
solution: Given: n = 71890 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(71890)) + 1 | Answer: 17

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.004, memory access time 140 ns and page-fault service time 6 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 6 ms = 6000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.004)*140 + 0.004*6000000.0 ns | Answer: 24.14 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 1.8 m^3 at 180 kPa and 440 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 1.8, P = 180, Tk = 440 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (180e3)*1.8 / (8.314*440) | Answer: 88.57 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.32 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 7 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.32, t = 7 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.32*7) | Answer: 0.8935

question: For a reaction with A = 7e10 /s and activation energy 75 kJ/mol at 390 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 7, Ea = 75, Tk = 390 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 7e10 * exp(-75e3 / (8.314*390)) | Answer: 6.304 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.91 and bottoms xW = 0.02, with relative volatility alpha = 2.1. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.91, xw = 0.02, al = 2.1 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.91/0.09)(0.98/0.02)] / ln(2.1) | Answer: 8.364 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.76 and x = 0.29. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.76, x = 0.29 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.76/0.24) / (0.29/0.71) | Answer: 7.753

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.7 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 90 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.7, Psat = 90 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.7 * 90 | Answer: 63 kPa

question: A stream of 9.7 kg/s with specific heat 4 kJ/kg-K is heated through 60 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 9.7, cp = 4, dT = 60 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 9.7*4*60 | Answer: 2328 kW

question: A reactor of volume 3.3 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 3 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 3.3, Q = 3 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 3.3 / 3 | Answer: 1.1 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 2e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 5 mm with a concentration difference of 30 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 2, L = 5, dC = 30 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (2e-9)*30 / (5e-3) | Answer: 12 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 2.8 min and steady-state gain 1.2. For a step input of magnitude 15, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 2.8, K = 1.2, M = 15 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 1.2 * 15 | Answer: 18 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 20 m^2 flies at 210 m/s (air density 0.7 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.9. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 20, V = 210, rho = 0.7, CL = 0.9 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.7*(210)^2*20*0.9 / 1000 | Answer: 277.8 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 90 m^2 flies at 240 m/s (density 1.225 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.04. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 90, V = 240, rho = 1.225, CD = 0.04 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*1.225*(240)^2*90*0.04 / 1000 | Answer: 127 kN

question: A specimen under stress 180 MPa shows an elastic strain of 2.1e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 180, eps = 2.1 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 180 / (2.1e-3) MPa = 85.71 GPa | Answer: 85.71 GPa

question: A block of mass 34 kg has a volume of 2.7e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 34, V = 2.7 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 34 / (2.7e-3) | Answer: 12593 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 1500 mm is heated through 20 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 11e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 1500, dT = 20, al = 11 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 1500*11e-6*20 | Answer: 0.33 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 100 ohm, R2 = 85 ohm and R3 = 265 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 100, R2 = 85, R3 = 265 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 85*265 / 100 | Answer: 225.2 ohm

question: A measurement reads 11 when the true value is 10. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 11, true = 10 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |11 - 10| / 10 * 100 | Answer: 10 %

question: Annual demand is 44000 units, ordering cost 300 per order and holding cost 16 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 44000, S = 300, H = 16 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*44000*300 / 16) | Answer: 1285 units

question: An asset costs 110000 with salvage value 36000 after 13 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 110000, Sv = 36000, n = 13 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (110000 - 36000) / 13 | Answer: 5692 per year
