question: Find the slope of the line through (-2, 5) and (9, -5).
solution: Given: x1 = -2, y1 = 5, x2 = 9, y2 = -5 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (-5 - 5) / (9 - -2) | Answer: -0.9091

question: Find the distance between the points (-8, -5) and (-7, 3).
solution: Given: x1 = -8, y1 = -5, x2 = -7, y2 = 3 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((1)^2 + (8)^2) | Answer: 8.062 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (3,-6), (-8,-8), (5,8).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 75 sq units

question: Find the 34th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 16 and common difference -8.
solution: Given: a = 16, d = -8, n = 34 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = 16 + (34 - 1)*-8 | Answer: -248

question: Find the sum of the first 8 terms of an AP with first term -8 and common difference 1.
solution: Given: a = -8, d = 1, n = 8 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 8/2 [2*-8 + (8-1)*1] | Answer: -36

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 13000 at 4.8% per annum for 3 years.
solution: Given: P = 13000, R = 4.8, Tt = 3 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 13000 * 4.8 * 3 / 100 | Answer: 1872 currency units

question: Find the amount when 7500 is invested at 10.6% per annum compounded annually for 3 years.
solution: Given: P = 7500, R = 10.6, Tt = 3 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 7500 * (1 + 10.6/100)^3 | Answer: 10147 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (8, -7, 1) and (1, -2, 2).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (4, -5, -4) and (6, -6, -3).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 16.16

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (-6, -5, 4) and (1, 1, 1).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 117.4 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = 5x^3 + 6x^2 - 5x - 5 at x = 0.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-61 with initial guess x0=15, find x1 (one iteration).

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 12 and 32.
solution: Given: a = 12, b = 32 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 12*32 / 4 | Answer: 96
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 55 mm carries an axial tensile load of 109 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 27 mm and length 2200 mm carries an axial load of 65 kN. Take E = 110 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 43 mm transmits a torque of 1450 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 43, Tt = 1450 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(1450*1000) / (pi*(43)^3) | Answer: 92.88 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 41 mm and length 1300 mm carries a torque of 1650 N-m. With G = 45 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (41)^4 / 32 = 277418 mm^4 | theta = (1650*1000)(1300) / (45000 * 277418) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 9.845 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 85 mm wide and 140 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 85, h = 140 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 85*(140)^2 / 6 | Answer: 277667 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (102 mm x 240 mm) carries a bending moment of 19 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (38 mm x 110 mm) has effective length 1900 mm and E = 200 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 560 MPa is designed for a working stress of 130 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 560, sw = 130 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 560 / 130 | Answer: 4.308

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1250 mm and wall thickness 15 mm carries an internal pressure of 0.7 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1250, t = 15, P = 0.7 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 0.7*1250 / (2*15) | Answer: 29.17 MPa

question: 5.4 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 140 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 5.4, dT = 140 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 5.4 * 0.718 * 140 | Answer: 542.8 kJ

question: 3.2 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 90 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.2, dT = 90 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 3.2 * 1.005 * 90 | Answer: 289.4 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 2.1 m^3 at 580 K with mass 3.4 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 2.1, Tk = 580, m = 3.4 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 3.4*0.287*580 / 2.1 | Answer: 269.5 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 1.6 kg of air expands isothermally at 340 K from volume V1 to 3*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1.6, Tk = 340, ratio = 3 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 1.6*0.287*340*ln(3) | Answer: 171.5 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 0.7 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.31 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 0.7, D = 0.31 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*0.7*0.31 / 0.001 | Answer: 217000

question: Water flows at 1.6 m/s through a pipe of diameter 270 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 10 m. Taking Cv = 0.95, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 10, cv = 0.95 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.95*sqrt(2*9.81*10) | Answer: 13.31 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 160 mm) water flows at 2.7 m/s. It contracts to diameter 50 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 160, d2 = 50, V1 = 2.7 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 2.7*(160/50)^2 | Answer: 27.65 m/s

question: Water flows at 1.3 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.48 m and length 50 m. With friction factor f = 0.038, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 36 teeth drives a gear of 91 teeth. If the pinion runs at 750 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 36, z2 = 91, N1 = 750 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 750*36 / 91 | Answer: 296.7 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 480 mm rotates at 250 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 480, N = 250 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.48)*250 / 60 | Answer: 6.283 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 39 kW at 800 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 39, N = 800 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(39*1000) / (2*pi*800) | Answer: 465.5 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 8.8 kg rotates at radius 0.56 m at 250 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 3600 N/m and mass 12.5 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 3600, m = 12.5 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(3600/12.5) | Answer: 2.701 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 3.9 m^2 and thickness 0.24 m has conductivity k = 38.9 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 30 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 3.9, L = 0.24, k = 38.9, dT = 30 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 38.9*3.9*30 / 0.24 | Answer: 18964 W

question: A surface of area 4.5 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 190 W/m^2-K to surroundings 115 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 4.5, h = 190, dT = 115 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 190*4.5*115 | Answer: 98325 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 200 m/min, feed = 0.46 mm/rev, depth of cut = 1.9 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 200, f = 0.46, d = 1.9 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*200*0.46*1.9 | Answer: 174800 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 460 mm is turned at 250 rpm with a feed of 0.33 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 460, N = 250, f = 0.33 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 460 / (0.33*250) | Answer: 5.576 min

question: A resistor of 120 ohm carries a current of 9.3 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 120, I = 9.3 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 9.3 * 120 | Answer: 1116 V

question: Three resistors 98 ohm, 45 ohm and 31 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 98, R2 = 45, R3 = 31 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 98 + 45 + 31 | Answer: 174 ohm

question: Two resistors 6 ohm and 70 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 6, R2 = 70 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 6*70 / (6+70) | Answer: 5.526 ohm

question: A device draws 1.4 A at 110 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 110, I = 1.4 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 110 * 1.4 | Answer: 154 W

question: A current of 8.6 A flows through a 146 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 8.6, R = 146 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (8.6)^2 * 146 | Answer: 10798 W

question: Two capacitors 6.2 uF and 16 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 6.2, C2 = 16 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 6.2*16 / (6.2+16) | Answer: 4.468 uF

question: A resistor 19 kohm and capacitor 16.5 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 19, C = 16.5 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (19k)(16.5u) = 313.5 ms | Answer: 313.5 ms

question: An inductor 306.5 mH is in series with 187 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 306.5, R = 187 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (306.5e-3) / 187 | Answer: 1.639 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 19.5 mH inductor at 170 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 19.5, f = 170 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (170)(19.5e-3) | Answer: 20.83 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 20.3 uF capacitor at 700 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 20.3, f = 700 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (700)(20.3e-6)) | Answer: 11.2 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 68 ohm, XL = 74 ohm and XC = 41 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 68, XL = 74, XC = 41 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(68^2 + (74 - 41)^2) | Answer: 75.58 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 97.3 mH and C = 6.4 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 97.3, C = 6.4 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(97.3e-3 * 6.4e-6)) | Answer: 201.7 Hz

question: A capacitor of 22.9 uF is charged to 55 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 22.9, V = 55 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*22.9e-6*(55)^2 | Answer: 34.64 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 280 V with 760 primary turns and 230 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 280, N1 = 760, N2 = 230 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 280 * 230/760 | Answer: 84.74 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 150 V and draws an armature current of 51 A. If the armature resistance is 0.18 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 150, Ia = 51, Ra = 0.18 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 150 - 51*0.18 | Answer: 140.8 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 50 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.97. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 50, VL = 400, pf = 0.97 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*400*50*0.97 / 1000 | Answer: 33.6 kW

question: A load has real power 100 kW and apparent power 160 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 100, S = 160 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 100 / 160 | Answer: 0.625

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 24 V across R1 = 19 ohm and R2 = 11 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 24, R1 = 19, R2 = 11 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 24*11 / (19+11) | Answer: 8.8 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 30 kohm and Rin = 36 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 30, Rin = 36 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 30 / 36 | Answer: 0.8333

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 4062. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 4062 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(4062) | Answer: 36.09 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.2 m carries a central point load of 105 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.2, W = 105 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 105*4.2 / 4 | Answer: 110.2 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.9 m carries a UDL of 50 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.9, w = 50 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 50*(4.9)^2 / 8 | Answer: 150.1 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 4.2 m carries a point load 45 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.2, W = 45 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 45*4.2 | Answer: 189 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 1.2 m carries a UDL of 20 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 1.2, w = 20 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 20*(1.2)^2 / 2 | Answer: 14.4 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.6 m carries a point load 10 kN at distance 3.3 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 6.6, a = 3.3, W = 10 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 10*(6.6 - 3.3) / 6.6 | Answer: 5 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 5.4 m) carries a central point load 80 kN. With E = 200 GPa and I = 280e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=80000 N, L=5400.0 mm, E=200000 MPa, I=280e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 4.686 mm

question: An RC beam has overall depth 310 mm, clear cover 50 mm and main bars of diameter 16 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 310, c = 50, dia = 16 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 310 - 50 - 16/2 | Answer: 252 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 34.5 m^2 carrying a factored load of 14.5 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 34.5, w = 14.5 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 14.5 * 34.5 | Answer: 500.2 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 4.6 m, unit weight 20 kN/m^3, phi = 32 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 2.6e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.7, area = 6.1e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 2.6, i = 0.7, A = 6.1 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (2.6e-4)*0.7*(6.1e-3) | Answer: 111 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 2 m, bed slope 0.006 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.029. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 1.5 m under a head of 1 m. Taking Cd = 0.64 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 5.3 m wide carries a discharge of 28.8 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 180 m and design speed 50 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 180, V = 50 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (50)^2 / (127*180) | Answer: 0.1094
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: A tank of volume 160 m^3 treats a flow of 145 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 160, Q = 145 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 160 / 145 | Answer: 1.103 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 350 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.35 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 6 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 350, k = 0.35, t = 6 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 350*(1 - e^(-0.35*6)) | Answer: 307.1 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.63, rainfall intensity 50 mm/h over a catchment of 16.7 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.63, i = 50, A = 16.7 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.63*50*16.7 / 360 | Answer: 1.461 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.01 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 310 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.01, M = 310 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 310*(30+0.01)/30 | Answer: 310.1 m

question: Convert the decimal number 1149 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 1149 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 47D (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 10010100 and 01001011.
solution: XOR: 11011111 | Count of 1s = 7 | Answer: 7
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 390 megabits is sent over a link of 82 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 390, B = 82 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 390 / 82 | Answer: 4.756 s

question: A link has bandwidth 98 Mbps and round-trip time 30 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 98, R = 30 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 98e6 * 30e-3 bits = 2940 kb | Answer: 2940 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.88, cache access time 10 ns and main-memory access time 160 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.88, tc = 10, tm = 160 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.88*10 + (1 - 0.88)*160 | Answer: 28 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 11053 elements?
solution: Given: n = 11053 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(11053)) + 1 | Answer: 14

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.007, memory access time 170 ns and page-fault service time 9 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 9 ms = 9000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.007)*170 + 0.007*9000000.0 ns | Answer: 63.17 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 1.5 m^3 at 430 kPa and 320 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 1.5, P = 430, Tk = 320 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (430e3)*1.5 / (8.314*320) | Answer: 242.4 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.26 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 4 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.26, t = 4 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.26*4) | Answer: 0.6465

question: For a reaction with A = 6e10 /s and activation energy 75 kJ/mol at 330 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 6, Ea = 75, Tk = 330 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 6e10 * exp(-75e3 / (8.314*330)) | Answer: 0.08058 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.97 and bottoms xW = 0.06, with relative volatility alpha = 2.1. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.97, xw = 0.06, al = 2.1 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.97/0.03)(0.94/0.06)] / ln(2.1) | Answer: 8.394 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.83 and x = 0.5. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.83, x = 0.5 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.83/0.17) / (0.5/0.5) | Answer: 4.882

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.89 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 95 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.89, Psat = 95 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.89 * 95 | Answer: 84.55 kPa

question: A stream of 8.7 kg/s with specific heat 2.8 kJ/kg-K is heated through 35 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 8.7, cp = 2.8, dT = 35 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 8.7*2.8*35 | Answer: 852.6 kW

question: A reactor of volume 14.3 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 1.2 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 14.3, Q = 1.2 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 14.3 / 1.2 | Answer: 11.92 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 3.5e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 4 mm with a concentration difference of 200 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 3.5, L = 4, dC = 200 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (3.5e-9)*200 / (4e-3) | Answer: 175 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 1.9 min and steady-state gain 1.5. For a step input of magnitude 5, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 1.9, K = 1.5, M = 5 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 1.5 * 5 | Answer: 7.5 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 95 m^2 flies at 170 m/s (air density 0.7 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.4. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 95, V = 170, rho = 0.7, CL = 0.4 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.7*(170)^2*95*0.4 / 1000 | Answer: 384.4 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 100 m^2 flies at 80 m/s (density 0.4 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.03. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 100, V = 80, rho = 0.4, CD = 0.03 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.4*(80)^2*100*0.03 / 1000 | Answer: 3.84 kN

question: A block of mass 13 kg has a volume of 3.8e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 13, V = 3.8 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 13 / (3.8e-3) | Answer: 3421 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 1800 mm is heated through 80 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 12e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 1800, dT = 80, al = 12 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 1800*12e-6*80 | Answer: 1.728 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 35 ohm, R2 = 85 ohm and R3 = 180 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 35, R2 = 85, R3 = 180 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 85*180 / 35 | Answer: 437.1 ohm

question: A measurement reads 9.69 when the true value is 10. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.69, true = 10 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.69 - 10| / 10 * 100 | Answer: 3.1 %

question: Annual demand is 45000 units, ordering cost 220 per order and holding cost 9 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 45000, S = 220, H = 9 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*45000*220 / 9) | Answer: 1483 units

question: An asset costs 370000 with salvage value 20000 after 7 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 370000, Sv = 20000, n = 7 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (370000 - 20000) / 7 | Answer: 50000 per year

question: A product sells for 330 per unit with variable cost 80 per unit and fixed costs 75000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 330, V = 80, F = 75000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 75000 / (330 - 80) | Answer: 300 units

question: Find the present worth of 170000 received 10 years from now at an interest rate of 7% per year.
solution: Given: F = 170000, n = 10, i = 7 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 170000 / (1 + 0.07)^10 | Answer: 86419 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.95, 0.92 and 0.96 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.95, r2 = 0.92, r3 = 0.96 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.95*0.92*0.96 | Answer: 0.839

question: A process produces 38 defective items in a batch of 18000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 38, N = 18000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 38/18000 * 1e6 | Answer: 2111 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = 5x^3 - x^2 + 8x - 2 evaluated at x = -3.
For f(x) = 5x^3 - 5x^2 - 5x + 6, find f''(x) at x = -1.
Evaluate the definite integral of (4x^2 - 6x - 6) dx from x = 0 to x = 5.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = 4x^3/3 + -6x^2/2 + -6x | Evaluate F(5) - F(0) | Answer: 61.67
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 3x^2 - 5x - 4 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[-5, 9], [8, 1]].
solution: Given: a = -5, b = 9, c = 8, d = 1 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (-5)(1) - (9)(8) | Answer: -77

question: Find the determinant of [[3, -2, -4], [3, 2, 5], [2, -1, 6]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: 95

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[8, 5], [1, -2]].
solution: Trace tr = 6, Determinant = -21 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 8.477

question: Solve for x: 4x + -1y = -5 and -1x + -4y = -5.
solution: Determinant = 4*-4 - -1*-1 = -17 | x = (e d - b f) / det = -0.8824 | Answer: x = -0.8824
