question: A circular rod of diameter 29 mm carries an axial tensile load of 35 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 30 mm and length 700 mm carries an axial load of 31 kN. Take E = 70 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 51 mm transmits a torque of 2500 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 51, Tt = 2500 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(2500*1000) / (pi*(51)^3) | Answer: 95.98 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 39 mm and length 1900 mm carries a torque of 200 N-m. With G = 45 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (39)^4 / 32 = 227122 mm^4 | theta = (200*1000)(1900) / (45000 * 227122) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 2.13 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 112 mm wide and 60 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 112, h = 60 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 112*(60)^2 / 6 | Answer: 67200 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (81 mm x 150 mm) carries a bending moment of 5 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (49 mm x 90 mm) has effective length 3200 mm and E = 200 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 320 MPa is designed for a working stress of 100 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 320, sw = 100 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 320 / 100 | Answer: 3.2

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1000 mm and wall thickness 18 mm carries an internal pressure of 1.1 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1000, t = 18, P = 1.1 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 1.1*1000 / (2*18) | Answer: 30.56 MPa

question: 4.7 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 145 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.7, dT = 145 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 4.7 * 0.718 * 145 | Answer: 489.3 kJ

question: 1.9 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 70 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1.9, dT = 70 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 1.9 * 1.005 * 70 | Answer: 133.7 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 2.2 m^3 at 600 K with mass 2.4 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 2.2, Tk = 600, m = 2.4 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 2.4*0.287*600 / 2.2 | Answer: 187.9 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 4.6 kg of air expands isothermally at 340 K from volume V1 to 4*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.6, Tk = 340, ratio = 4 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 4.6*0.287*340*ln(4) | Answer: 622.3 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 3.9 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.19 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 3.9, D = 0.19 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*3.9*0.19 / 0.001 | Answer: 741000

question: Water flows at 3.8 m/s through a pipe of diameter 50 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 17.4 m. Taking Cv = 0.96, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 17.4, cv = 0.96 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.96*sqrt(2*9.81*17.4) | Answer: 17.74 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 230 mm) water flows at 1.2 m/s. It contracts to diameter 140 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
Water flows at 3.6 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.31 m and length 410 m. With friction factor f = 0.038, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 26 teeth drives a gear of 63 teeth. If the pinion runs at 300 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 26, z2 = 63, N1 = 300 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 300*26 / 63 | Answer: 123.8 rpm

question: A shaft transmits 25.4 kW at 400 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 25.4, N = 400 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(25.4*1000) / (2*pi*400) | Answer: 606.4 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 3.3 kg rotates at radius 0.55 m at 400 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 13700 N/m and mass 7.2 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 13700, m = 7.2 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(13700/7.2) | Answer: 6.942 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 9.2 m^2 and thickness 0.36 m has conductivity k = 13.5 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 160 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 9.2, L = 0.36, k = 13.5, dT = 160 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 13.5*9.2*160 / 0.36 | Answer: 55200 W

question: A surface of area 4.4 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 65 W/m^2-K to surroundings 150 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 4.4, h = 65, dT = 150 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 65*4.4*150 | Answer: 42900 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 140 m/min, feed = 0.43 mm/rev, depth of cut = 0.9 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 140, f = 0.43, d = 0.9 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*140*0.43*0.9 | Answer: 54180 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 370 mm is turned at 900 rpm with a feed of 0.38 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 370, N = 900, f = 0.38 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 370 / (0.38*900) | Answer: 1.082 min

question: A resistor of 52 ohm carries a current of 1.8 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 52, I = 1.8 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 1.8 * 52 | Answer: 93.6 V

question: Three resistors 91 ohm, 71 ohm and 80 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 91, R2 = 71, R3 = 80 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 91 + 71 + 80 | Answer: 242 ohm

question: Two resistors 69 ohm and 4 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 69, R2 = 4 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 69*4 / (69+4) | Answer: 3.781 ohm

question: A device draws 0.5 A at 85 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 85, I = 0.5 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 85 * 0.5 | Answer: 42.5 W

question: A current of 11 A flows through a 140 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 11, R = 140 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (11)^2 * 140 | Answer: 16940 W

question: Two capacitors 5.5 uF and 18.4 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 5.5, C2 = 18.4 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 5.5*18.4 / (5.5+18.4) | Answer: 4.234 uF

question: A resistor 41 kohm and capacitor 14.6 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 41, C = 14.6 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (41k)(14.6u) = 598.6 ms | Answer: 598.6 ms

question: An inductor 376.2 mH is in series with 192 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 376.2, R = 192 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (376.2e-3) / 192 | Answer: 1.959 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 8.5 mH inductor at 670 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 8.5, f = 670 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (670)(8.5e-3) | Answer: 35.78 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 2.6 uF capacitor at 720 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 2.6, f = 720 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (720)(2.6e-6)) | Answer: 85.02 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 99 ohm, XL = 79 ohm and XC = 65 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 99, XL = 79, XC = 65 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(99^2 + (79 - 65)^2) | Answer: 99.98 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 45.7 mH and C = 3.6 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 45.7, C = 3.6 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(45.7e-3 * 3.6e-6)) | Answer: 392.4 Hz

question: A capacitor of 25.8 uF is charged to 350 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 25.8, V = 350 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*25.8e-6*(350)^2 | Answer: 158 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 190 V with 560 primary turns and 430 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 190, N1 = 560, N2 = 430 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 190 * 430/560 | Answer: 145.9 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 300 V and draws an armature current of 28 A. If the armature resistance is 0.53 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 300, Ia = 28, Ra = 0.53 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 300 - 28*0.53 | Answer: 285.2 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 5 A at 433 V (line) with a power factor of 0.77. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 5, VL = 433, pf = 0.77 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*433*5*0.77 / 1000 | Answer: 2.887 kW

question: A load has real power 95 kW and apparent power 170 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 95, S = 170 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 95 / 170 | Answer: 0.5588

question: A machine delivers 115 kW output while drawing 122 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 115, Pi = 122 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 115/122 * 100 | Answer: 94.26 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 8 V across R1 = 32 ohm and R2 = 42 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 8, R1 = 32, R2 = 42 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 8*42 / (32+42) | Answer: 4.541 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 90 kohm and Rin = 20 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 90, Rin = 20 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 90 / 20 | Answer: 4.5

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 40 kohm and Rg = 22 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 40, Rg = 22 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 40/22 | Answer: 2.818

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 499. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 499 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(499) | Answer: 26.98 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 8.6 m carries a central point load of 65 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 8.6, W = 65 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 65*8.6 / 4 | Answer: 139.8 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.7 m carries a UDL of 60 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6.7, w = 60 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 60*(6.7)^2 / 8 | Answer: 336.7 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 1.2 m carries a UDL of 22 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 1.2, w = 22 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 22*(1.2)^2 / 2 | Answer: 15.84 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 8.7 m carries a point load 40 kN at distance 1.5 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 8.7, a = 1.5, W = 40 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 40*(8.7 - 1.5) / 8.7 | Answer: 33.1 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 4.2 m) carries a central point load 65 kN. With E = 25 GPa and I = 510e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=65000 N, L=4200.0 mm, E=25000 MPa, I=510e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 7.869 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 8.7 m carries a UDL of 39 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 8.7, w = 39 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 39*(8.7)^2 / 12 | Answer: 246 kN-m

question: A column supports a floor area of 27.3 m^2 carrying a factored load of 8.4 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 27.3, w = 8.4 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 8.4 * 27.3 | Answer: 229.3 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 4.2 m, unit weight 18 kN/m^3, phi = 38 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 4.2e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.5, area = 4.9e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 4.2, i = 0.5, A = 4.9 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (4.2e-4)*0.5*(4.9e-3) | Answer: 1029 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.8 m, bed slope 0.007 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.026. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 4.5 m under a head of 1.2 m. Taking Cd = 0.63 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 5.3 m wide carries a discharge of 11.7 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A tank of volume 150 m^3 treats a flow of 120 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 150, Q = 120 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 150 / 120 | Answer: 1.25 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 220 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.19 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 8 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 220, k = 0.19, t = 8 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 220*(1 - e^(-0.19*8)) | Answer: 171.9 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.9, rainfall intensity 95 mm/h over a catchment of 48.5 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.9, i = 95, A = 48.5 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.9*95*48.5 / 360 | Answer: 11.52 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.06 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 270 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.06, M = 270 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 270*(20+0.06)/20 | Answer: 270.8 m

question: Convert the decimal number 3679 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 3679 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: E5F (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 10000000 and 01111001.
solution: XOR: 11111001 | Count of 1s = 6 | Answer: 6
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 400 megabits is sent over a link of 7 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 400, B = 7 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 400 / 7 | Answer: 57.14 s

question: A link has bandwidth 89 Mbps and round-trip time 190 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 89, R = 190 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 89e6 * 190e-3 bits = 16910 kb | Answer: 16910 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.83, cache access time 3 ns and main-memory access time 180 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.83, tc = 3, tm = 180 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.83*3 + (1 - 0.83)*180 | Answer: 33.09 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 432947 elements?
solution: Given: n = 432947 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(432947)) + 1 | Answer: 19

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.012, memory access time 130 ns and page-fault service time 4 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 4 ms = 4000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.012)*130 + 0.012*4000000.0 ns | Answer: 48.13 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 0.8 m^3 at 390 kPa and 450 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 0.8, P = 390, Tk = 450 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (390e3)*0.8 / (8.314*450) | Answer: 83.39 mol

question: For a reaction with A = 4e10 /s and activation energy 80 kJ/mol at 360 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 4, Ea = 80, Tk = 360 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 4e10 * exp(-80e3 / (8.314*360)) | Answer: 0.09861 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.95 and bottoms xW = 0.06, with relative volatility alpha = 3.2. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.95, xw = 0.06, al = 3.2 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.95/0.05)(0.94/0.06)] / ln(3.2) | Answer: 4.897 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.88 and x = 0.46. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.88, x = 0.46 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.88/0.12) / (0.46/0.54) | Answer: 8.609

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.77 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 40 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.77, Psat = 40 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.77 * 40 | Answer: 30.8 kPa

question: A stream of 9.3 kg/s with specific heat 1.2 kJ/kg-K is heated through 45 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 9.3, cp = 1.2, dT = 45 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 9.3*1.2*45 | Answer: 502.2 kW

question: A reactor of volume 3.9 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 4.5 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 3.9, Q = 4.5 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 3.9 / 4.5 | Answer: 0.8667 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 7.6e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 5 mm with a concentration difference of 140 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 7.6, L = 5, dC = 140 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (7.6e-9)*140 / (5e-3) | Answer: 212.8 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 7.7 min and steady-state gain 1.6. For a step input of magnitude 20, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 7.7, K = 1.6, M = 20 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 1.6 * 20 | Answer: 32 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 95 m^2 flies at 90 m/s (air density 0.7 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.8. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 95, V = 90, rho = 0.7, CL = 0.8 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.7*(90)^2*95*0.8 / 1000 | Answer: 215.5 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 60 m^2 flies at 90 m/s (density 0.7 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.12. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 60, V = 90, rho = 0.7, CD = 0.12 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.7*(90)^2*60*0.12 / 1000 | Answer: 20.41 kN

question: A block of mass 33 kg has a volume of 2.3e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 33, V = 2.3 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 33 / (2.3e-3) | Answer: 14348 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 1400 mm is heated through 85 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 12e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 1400, dT = 85, al = 12 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 1400*12e-6*85 | Answer: 1.428 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 195 ohm, R2 = 75 ohm and R3 = 230 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 195, R2 = 75, R3 = 230 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 75*230 / 195 | Answer: 88.46 ohm

question: Annual demand is 49000 units, ordering cost 100 per order and holding cost 30 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 49000, S = 100, H = 30 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*49000*100 / 30) | Answer: 571.5 units

question: An asset costs 420000 with salvage value 28000 after 16 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 420000, Sv = 28000, n = 16 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (420000 - 28000) / 16 | Answer: 24500 per year

question: A product sells for 140 per unit with variable cost 10 per unit and fixed costs 155000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 140, V = 10, F = 155000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 155000 / (140 - 10) | Answer: 1192 units

question: Find the present worth of 90000 received 8 years from now at an interest rate of 11% per year.
solution: Given: F = 90000, n = 8, i = 11 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 90000 / (1 + 0.11)^8 | Answer: 39053 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.9, 0.98 and 0.99 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.9, r2 = 0.98, r3 = 0.99 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.9*0.98*0.99 | Answer: 0.8732

question: A process produces 20 defective items in a batch of 14500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 20, N = 14500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 20/14500 * 1e6 | Answer: 1379 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -4x^3 + 3x + 8 evaluated at x = -5.
For f(x) = -6x^3 + 4x^2 + 4x - 4, find f''(x) at x = 5.
Evaluate the definite integral of (5x^2 - 3x + 7) dx from x = 1 to x = 3.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = 5x^3/3 + -3x^2/2 + 7x | Evaluate F(3) - F(1) | Answer: 45.33
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 5x^2 - 8x - 12 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[-7, 5], [-1, 6]].
solution: Given: a = -7, b = 5, c = -1, d = 6 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (-7)(6) - (5)(-1) | Answer: -37

question: Find the determinant of [[0, 4, -6], [2, -2, 4], [5, 2, 5]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: -44

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[-4, 6], [4, 0]].
solution: Trace tr = -4, Determinant = -24 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 3.292

question: Solve for x: 4x + 4y = -7 and 1x + -1y = 2.
solution: Determinant = 4*-1 - 4*1 = -8 | x = (e d - b f) / det = 0.125 | Answer: x = 0.125
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 63, 72, 23, 3, 19.
solution: Sum = 180 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 36 | Answer: 36

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 10, 2, 22, 13, 14.
solution: Mean = 12.2 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 7.225

question: Find the slope of the line through (-7, -2) and (-5, -8).
solution: Given: x1 = -7, y1 = -2, x2 = -5, y2 = -8 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (-8 - -2) / (-5 - -7) | Answer: -3

question: Find the distance between the points (7, 0) and (6, 9).
solution: Given: x1 = 7, y1 = 0, x2 = 6, y2 = 9 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-1)^2 + (9)^2) | Answer: 9.055 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (-1,7), (7,0), (-8,7).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 24.5 sq units

question: Find the 33th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -10 and common difference -7.
solution: Given: a = -10, d = -7, n = 33 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -10 + (33 - 1)*-7 | Answer: -234

question: Find the sum of the first 9 terms of an AP with first term -9 and common difference 2.
solution: Given: a = -9, d = 2, n = 9 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 9/2 [2*-9 + (9-1)*2] | Answer: -9

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 8500 at 10.3% per annum for 10 years.
solution: Given: P = 8500, R = 10.3, Tt = 10 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 8500 * 10.3 * 10 / 100 | Answer: 8755 currency units

question: Find the amount when 3000 is invested at 5.4% per annum compounded annually for 5 years.
solution: Given: P = 3000, R = 5.4, Tt = 5 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 3000 * (1 + 5.4/100)^5 | Answer: 3902 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (2, 2, -4) and (-6, 2, 3).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (3, -3, -6) and (-1, 0, 4).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 13.75

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (3, 3, 0) and (2, 4, -2).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 30 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number 2 + -2i.
solution: Given: a = 2, b = -2 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((2)^2 + (-2)^2) | Answer: 2.828

question: Evaluate f(x) = -3x^3 - x^2 + 6x + 1 at x = -5.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-168 with initial guess x0=2, find x1 (one iteration).
solution: Given: N = 168, x0 = 2 | Formula: x1 = x0 - (x0^2 - N)/(2 x0) | Substitute: x1 = 2 - ((2)^2 - 168)/(2*2) | Answer: 43

question: Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1 and ordinates 17, 12, 16, 8, 16, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 50 and 465.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 50 and 465 | Answer: GCD = 5

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 70 and 52.
solution: Given: a = 70, b = 52 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 70*52 / 2 | Answer: 1820
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 56 mm carries an axial tensile load of 22 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 23 mm and length 2800 mm carries an axial load of 85 kN. Take E = 200 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 55 mm transmits a torque of 850 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 55, Tt = 850 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(850*1000) / (pi*(55)^3) | Answer: 26.02 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 45 mm and length 1600 mm carries a torque of 250 N-m. With G = 77 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (45)^4 / 32 = 402578 mm^4 | theta = (250*1000)(1600) / (77000 * 402578) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 0.7393 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 88 mm wide and 60 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 88, h = 60 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 88*(60)^2 / 6 | Answer: 52800 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (77 mm x 160 mm) carries a bending moment of 37 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (65 mm x 120 mm) has effective length 1700 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 340 MPa is designed for a working stress of 190 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 340, sw = 190 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 340 / 190 | Answer: 1.789

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 450 mm and wall thickness 10 mm carries an internal pressure of 1.3 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 450, t = 10, P = 1.3 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 1.3*450 / (2*10) | Answer: 29.25 MPa

question: 2 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 80 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2, dT = 80 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 2 * 0.718 * 80 | Answer: 114.9 kJ

question: 5.6 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 85 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 5.6, dT = 85 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 5.6 * 1.005 * 85 | Answer: 478.4 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 3.9 m^3 at 400 K with mass 3.1 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 3.9, Tk = 400, m = 3.1 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 3.1*0.287*400 / 3.9 | Answer: 91.25 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 2.8 kg of air expands isothermally at 460 K from volume V1 to 3*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.8, Tk = 460, ratio = 3 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 2.8*0.287*460*ln(3) | Answer: 406.1 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 4.5 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.32 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 4.5, D = 0.32 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*4.5*0.32 / 0.001 | Answer: 1440000

question: Water flows at 3.1 m/s through a pipe of diameter 130 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 16.8 m. Taking Cv = 0.95, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 16.8, cv = 0.95 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.95*sqrt(2*9.81*16.8) | Answer: 17.25 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 190 mm) water flows at 2.9 m/s. It contracts to diameter 90 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 190, d2 = 90, V1 = 2.9 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 2.9*(190/90)^2 | Answer: 12.92 m/s

question: Water flows at 2.9 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.29 m and length 410 m. With friction factor f = 0.023, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 29 teeth drives a gear of 119 teeth. If the pinion runs at 800 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 29, z2 = 119, N1 = 800 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 800*29 / 119 | Answer: 195 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 250 mm rotates at 300 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 250, N = 300 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.25)*300 / 60 | Answer: 3.927 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 34.1 kW at 1500 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 34.1, N = 1500 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(34.1*1000) / (2*pi*1500) | Answer: 217.1 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 7.8 kg rotates at radius 0.17 m at 300 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 11100 N/m and mass 18 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 11100, m = 18 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(11100/18) | Answer: 3.952 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 5.6 m^2 and thickness 0.14 m has conductivity k = 14.5 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 175 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 5.6, L = 0.14, k = 14.5, dT = 175 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 14.5*5.6*175 / 0.14 | Answer: 101500 W

question: A surface of area 0.7 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 120 W/m^2-K to surroundings 85 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 0.7, h = 120, dT = 85 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 120*0.7*85 | Answer: 7140 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 250 m/min, feed = 0.14 mm/rev, depth of cut = 1.4 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 250, f = 0.14, d = 1.4 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*250*0.14*1.4 | Answer: 49000 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 270 mm is turned at 1150 rpm with a feed of 0.16 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 270, N = 1150, f = 0.16 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 270 / (0.16*1150) | Answer: 1.467 min

question: A resistor of 61 ohm carries a current of 2.1 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 61, I = 2.1 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 2.1 * 61 | Answer: 128.1 V

question: Three resistors 24 ohm, 94 ohm and 45 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 24, R2 = 94, R3 = 45 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 24 + 94 + 45 | Answer: 163 ohm

question: Two resistors 51 ohm and 36 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 51, R2 = 36 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 51*36 / (51+36) | Answer: 21.1 ohm

question: A device draws 12.1 A at 220 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 220, I = 12.1 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 220 * 12.1 | Answer: 2662 W

question: A current of 4.9 A flows through a 2 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 4.9, R = 2 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (4.9)^2 * 2 | Answer: 48.02 W

question: Two capacitors 39.2 uF and 7.1 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 39.2, C2 = 7.1 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 39.2*7.1 / (39.2+7.1) | Answer: 6.011 uF

question: A resistor 68 kohm and capacitor 12.7 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 68, C = 12.7 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (68k)(12.7u) = 863.6 ms | Answer: 863.6 ms

question: An inductor 241 mH is in series with 152 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 241, R = 152 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (241e-3) / 152 | Answer: 1.586 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 184.7 mH inductor at 480 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 184.7, f = 480 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (480)(184.7e-3) | Answer: 557 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 45.3 uF capacitor at 170 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 45.3, f = 170 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (170)(45.3e-6)) | Answer: 20.67 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 67 ohm, XL = 123 ohm and XC = 149 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 67, XL = 123, XC = 149 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(67^2 + (123 - 149)^2) | Answer: 71.87 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 44.2 mH and C = 4 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 44.2, C = 4 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(44.2e-3 * 4e-6)) | Answer: 378.5 Hz

question: A capacitor of 29.9 uF is charged to 340 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 29.9, V = 340 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*29.9e-6*(340)^2 | Answer: 1728 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 250 V with 760 primary turns and 430 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 250, N1 = 760, N2 = 430 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 250 * 430/760 | Answer: 141.4 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 310 V and draws an armature current of 25 A. If the armature resistance is 1.46 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 310, Ia = 25, Ra = 1.46 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 310 - 25*1.46 | Answer: 273.5 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 100 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.96. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 100, VL = 400, pf = 0.96 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*400*100*0.96 / 1000 | Answer: 66.51 kW

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 24 V across R1 = 10 ohm and R2 = 8 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 24, R1 = 10, R2 = 8 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 24*8 / (10+8) | Answer: 10.67 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 130 kohm and Rin = 32 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 130, Rin = 32 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 130 / 32 | Answer: 4.062

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 5526. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 5526 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(5526) | Answer: 37.42 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.8 m carries a central point load of 50 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.8, W = 50 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 50*4.8 / 4 | Answer: 60 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.4 m carries a UDL of 60 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.4, w = 60 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 60*(4.4)^2 / 8 | Answer: 145.2 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 5.1 m carries a point load 80 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.1, W = 80 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 80*5.1 | Answer: 408 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 4.1 m carries a UDL of 14 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.1, w = 14 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 14*(4.1)^2 / 2 | Answer: 117.7 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 5.9 m carries a point load 85 kN at distance 1.7 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 5.9, a = 1.7, W = 85 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 85*(5.9 - 1.7) / 5.9 | Answer: 60.51 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 4.4 m) carries a central point load 45 kN. With E = 30 GPa and I = 190e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=45000 N, L=4400.0 mm, E=30000 MPa, I=190e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 14.01 mm

question: An RC beam has overall depth 350 mm, clear cover 25 mm and main bars of diameter 25 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 350, c = 25, dia = 25 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 350 - 25 - 25/2 | Answer: 312.5 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 11.5 m^2 carrying a factored load of 17 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 11.5, w = 17 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 17 * 11.5 | Answer: 195.5 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 6.8 m, unit weight 18 kN/m^3, phi = 28 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 1.7e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1.2, area = 2.8e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 1.7, i = 1.2, A = 2.8 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (1.7e-4)*1.2*(2.8e-3) | Answer: 571.2 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.4 m, bed slope 0.001 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.027. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 3.2 m under a head of 1.1 m. Taking Cd = 0.62 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 4.6 m wide carries a discharge of 20.4 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A tank of volume 770 m^3 treats a flow of 85 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 770, Q = 85 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 770 / 85 | Answer: 9.059 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 400 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.3 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 7 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 400, k = 0.3, t = 7 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 400*(1 - e^(-0.3*7)) | Answer: 351 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.4, rainfall intensity 75 mm/h over a catchment of 39.4 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.4, i = 75, A = 39.4 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.4*75*39.4 / 360 | Answer: 3.283 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.05 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 690 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.05, M = 690 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 690*(20+0.05)/20 | Answer: 691.7 m

question: Convert the decimal number 758 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 758 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 2F6 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 10111110 and 00100011.
solution: XOR: 10011101 | Count of 1s = 5 | Answer: 5
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 240 megabits is sent over a link of 77 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 240, B = 77 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 240 / 77 | Answer: 3.117 s

question: A link has bandwidth 75 Mbps and round-trip time 50 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 75, R = 50 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 75e6 * 50e-3 bits = 3750 kb | Answer: 3750 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.89, cache access time 5 ns and main-memory access time 170 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.89, tc = 5, tm = 170 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.89*5 + (1 - 0.89)*170 | Answer: 23.15 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 328280 elements?
solution: Given: n = 328280 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(328280)) + 1 | Answer: 19

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.004, memory access time 170 ns and page-fault service time 4 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 4 ms = 4000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.004)*170 + 0.004*4000000.0 ns | Answer: 16.17 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 0.4 m^3 at 430 kPa and 430 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 0.4, P = 430, Tk = 430 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (430e3)*0.4 / (8.314*430) | Answer: 48.11 mol

question: For a reaction with A = 2e10 /s and activation energy 80 kJ/mol at 300 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 2, Ea = 80, Tk = 300 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 2e10 * exp(-80e3 / (8.314*300)) | Answer: 0.0002351 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.97 and bottoms xW = 0.04, with relative volatility alpha = 2.2. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.97, xw = 0.04, al = 2.2 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.97/0.03)(0.96/0.04)] / ln(2.2) | Answer: 8.439 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.86 and x = 0.2. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.86, x = 0.2 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.86/0.14) / (0.2/0.8) | Answer: 24.57

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.59 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 30 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.59, Psat = 30 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.59 * 30 | Answer: 17.7 kPa

question: A stream of 8.5 kg/s with specific heat 2.8 kJ/kg-K is heated through 80 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 8.5, cp = 2.8, dT = 80 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 8.5*2.8*80 | Answer: 1904 kW

question: A reactor of volume 7.7 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 3.9 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 7.7, Q = 3.9 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 7.7 / 3.9 | Answer: 1.974 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 7e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 1 mm with a concentration difference of 180 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 7, L = 1, dC = 180 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (7e-9)*180 / (1e-3) | Answer: 1260 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 6.8 min and steady-state gain 3.6. For a step input of magnitude 19, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 6.8, K = 3.6, M = 19 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 3.6 * 19 | Answer: 68.4 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 110 m^2 flies at 130 m/s (air density 1.225 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.4. Find the lift force in kN.
An aircraft of wing area 70 m^2 flies at 210 m/s (density 0.4 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.06. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 70, V = 210, rho = 0.4, CD = 0.06 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.4*(210)^2*70*0.06 / 1000 | Answer: 37.04 kN

question: A specimen under stress 150 MPa shows an elastic strain of 1.1e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 150, eps = 1.1 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 150 / (1.1e-3) MPa = 136.4 GPa | Answer: 136.4 GPa

question: A block of mass 6 kg has a volume of 4.5e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 6, V = 4.5 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 6 / (4.5e-3) | Answer: 1333 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 2300 mm is heated through 95 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 12e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 2300, dT = 95, al = 12 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 2300*12e-6*95 | Answer: 2.622 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 100 ohm, R2 = 180 ohm and R3 = 500 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 100, R2 = 180, R3 = 500 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 180*500 / 100 | Answer: 900 ohm

question: Annual demand is 50000 units, ordering cost 290 per order and holding cost 35 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 50000, S = 290, H = 35 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*50000*290 / 35) | Answer: 910.3 units

question: An asset costs 200000 with salvage value 38000 after 6 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 200000, Sv = 38000, n = 6 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (200000 - 38000) / 6 | Answer: 27000 per year

question: A product sells for 160 per unit with variable cost 20 per unit and fixed costs 200000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 160, V = 20, F = 200000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 200000 / (160 - 20) | Answer: 1429 units

question: Find the present worth of 130000 received 10 years from now at an interest rate of 8% per year.
solution: Given: F = 130000, n = 10, i = 8 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 130000 / (1 + 0.08)^10 | Answer: 60215 currency units

question: A process produces 31 defective items in a batch of 6500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 31, N = 6500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 31/6500 * 1e6 | Answer: 4769 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = 3x^3 - x^2 - 8x - 7 evaluated at x = -1.
For f(x) = -2x^3 + 2x^2 + 8, find f''(x) at x = 5.
Evaluate the definite integral of (3x^2 + 5x + 1) dx from x = 0 to x = 5.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = 3x^3/3 + 5x^2/2 + 1x | Evaluate F(5) - F(0) | Answer: 192.5
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 5x^2 - x - 5 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[-5, -6], [9, 2]].
solution: Given: a = -5, b = -6, c = 9, d = 2 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (-5)(2) - (-6)(9) | Answer: 44

question: Find the determinant of [[-6, 5, -4], [4, -6, -3], [-1, -4, -1]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: 159

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[-4, -5], [-7, 7]].
solution: Trace tr = 3, Determinant = -63 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 9.578

question: Solve for x: 4x + -4y = -10 and -6x + -6y = -3.
solution: Determinant = 4*-6 - -4*-6 = -48 | x = (e d - b f) / det = -1 | Answer: x = -1
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 1, 63, 26, 35, 13.
solution: Sum = 138 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 27.6 | Answer: 27.6

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 5, 7, 30, 25, 19.
solution: Mean = 17.2 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 10.96

question: Find the slope of the line through (7, 0) and (2, -1).
solution: Given: x1 = 7, y1 = 0, x2 = 2, y2 = -1 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (-1 - 0) / (2 - 7) | Answer: 0.2

question: Find the distance between the points (2, 8) and (2, -3).
solution: Given: x1 = 2, y1 = 8, x2 = 2, y2 = -3 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((0)^2 + (-11)^2) | Answer: 11 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (5,5), (-1,-2), (5,7).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 6 sq units

question: Find the 16th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 17 and common difference 4.
solution: Given: a = 17, d = 4, n = 16 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = 17 + (16 - 1)*4 | Answer: 77

question: Find the sum of the first 8 terms of an AP with first term 2 and common difference 7.
solution: Given: a = 2, d = 7, n = 8 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 8/2 [2*2 + (8-1)*7] | Answer: 212

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 34500 at 11.8% per annum for 5 years.
solution: Given: P = 34500, R = 11.8, Tt = 5 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 34500 * 11.8 * 5 / 100 | Answer: 20355 currency units

question: Find the amount when 15500 is invested at 6.8% per annum compounded annually for 3 years.
solution: Given: P = 15500, R = 6.8, Tt = 3 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 15500 * (1 + 6.8/100)^3 | Answer: 18882 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (6, 7, 7) and (-5, -4, -2).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (1, 2, 3) and (-1, 6, -6).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 31.19

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (0, 2, 0) and (2, -1, -1).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 114.1 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -5x^3 + 4x^2 + x + 5 at x = 1.
solution: Given: a = -5, b = 4, c = 1, d = 5, x0 = 1 | Formula: f(x0) = a x0^3 + b x0^2 + c x0 + d | Substitute: f(1) = -5(1)^3 + 4(1)^2 + 1(1) + 5 | Answer: 5

question: Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-32 with initial guess x0=5, find x1 (one iteration).
solution: Given: N = 32, x0 = 5 | Formula: x1 = x0 - (x0^2 - N)/(2 x0) | Substitute: x1 = 5 - ((5)^2 - 32)/(2*5) | Answer: 5.7

question: Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.6 and ordinates 4, 12, 7, 14, 6, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 391 and 95.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 391 and 95 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 73 and 62.
solution: Given: a = 73, b = 62 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 73*62 / 1 | Answer: 4526
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 37 mm carries an axial tensile load of 17 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 35 mm and length 2900 mm carries an axial load of 25 kN. Take E = 70 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 46 mm transmits a torque of 2900 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 46, Tt = 2900 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(2900*1000) / (pi*(46)^3) | Answer: 151.7 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 68 mm and length 1900 mm carries a torque of 1150 N-m. With G = 77 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 130 mm wide and 70 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 130, h = 70 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 130*(70)^2 / 6 | Answer: 106167 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (77 mm x 240 mm) carries a bending moment of 3 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (69 mm x 140 mm) has effective length 3900 mm and E = 200 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 660 MPa is designed for a working stress of 230 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 660, sw = 230 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 660 / 230 | Answer: 2.87

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 350 mm and wall thickness 6 mm carries an internal pressure of 2.2 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 350, t = 6, P = 2.2 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 2.2*350 / (2*6) | Answer: 64.17 MPa

question: 2.8 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 130 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.8, dT = 130 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 2.8 * 0.718 * 130 | Answer: 261.4 kJ

question: 3.1 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 180 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.1, dT = 180 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 3.1 * 1.005 * 180 | Answer: 560.8 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 3 m^3 at 470 K with mass 2.2 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 3, Tk = 470, m = 2.2 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 2.2*0.287*470 / 3 | Answer: 98.92 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 2.8 kg of air expands isothermally at 490 K from volume V1 to 2*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.8, Tk = 490, ratio = 2 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 2.8*0.287*490*ln(2) | Answer: 272.9 kJ

question: Water flows at 0.5 m/s through a pipe of diameter 230 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 7.8 m. Taking Cv = 0.99, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 7.8, cv = 0.99 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.99*sqrt(2*9.81*7.8) | Answer: 12.25 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 310 mm) water flows at 0.6 m/s. It contracts to diameter 80 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 310, d2 = 80, V1 = 0.6 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 0.6*(310/80)^2 | Answer: 9.009 m/s

question: Water flows at 2.5 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.26 m and length 460 m. With friction factor f = 0.03, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 27 teeth drives a gear of 102 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1150 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 27, z2 = 102, N1 = 1150 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1150*27 / 102 | Answer: 304.4 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 520 mm rotates at 550 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 520, N = 550 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.52)*550 / 60 | Answer: 14.97 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 36.2 kW at 550 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 36.2, N = 550 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(36.2*1000) / (2*pi*550) | Answer: 628.5 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 3.7 kg rotates at radius 0.36 m at 950 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 11900 N/m and mass 12 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 11900, m = 12 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(11900/12) | Answer: 5.012 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 1.2 m^2 and thickness 0.23 m has conductivity k = 0.9 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 30 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 1.2, L = 0.23, k = 0.9, dT = 30 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 0.9*1.2*30 / 0.23 | Answer: 140.9 W

question: A surface of area 1.6 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 165 W/m^2-K to surroundings 95 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 1.6, h = 165, dT = 95 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 165*1.6*95 | Answer: 25080 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 110 m/min, feed = 0.15 mm/rev, depth of cut = 1.2 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 110, f = 0.15, d = 1.2 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*110*0.15*1.2 | Answer: 19800 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 500 mm is turned at 500 rpm with a feed of 0.31 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 500, N = 500, f = 0.31 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 500 / (0.31*500) | Answer: 3.226 min

question: A resistor of 82 ohm carries a current of 5.9 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 82, I = 5.9 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 5.9 * 82 | Answer: 483.8 V

question: Three resistors 74 ohm, 39 ohm and 50 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 74, R2 = 39, R3 = 50 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 74 + 39 + 50 | Answer: 163 ohm

question: Two resistors 69 ohm and 101 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 69, R2 = 101 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 69*101 / (69+101) | Answer: 40.99 ohm

question: A device draws 6.3 A at 160 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 160, I = 6.3 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 160 * 6.3 | Answer: 1008 W

question: A current of 9.7 A flows through a 67 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 9.7, R = 67 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (9.7)^2 * 67 | Answer: 6304 W

question: Two capacitors 3.1 uF and 48.3 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 3.1, C2 = 48.3 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 3.1*48.3 / (3.1+48.3) | Answer: 2.913 uF

question: A resistor 46 kohm and capacitor 16.6 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 46, C = 16.6 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (46k)(16.6u) = 763.6 ms | Answer: 763.6 ms

question: An inductor 328.7 mH is in series with 128 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 328.7, R = 128 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (328.7e-3) / 128 | Answer: 2.568 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 14.9 mH inductor at 810 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 14.9, f = 810 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (810)(14.9e-3) | Answer: 75.83 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 17.2 uF capacitor at 730 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 17.2, f = 730 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (730)(17.2e-6)) | Answer: 12.68 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 63 ohm, XL = 62 ohm and XC = 115 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 63, XL = 62, XC = 115 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(63^2 + (62 - 115)^2) | Answer: 82.33 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 74.4 mH and C = 9.9 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 74.4, C = 9.9 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(74.4e-3 * 9.9e-6)) | Answer: 185.4 Hz

question: A capacitor of 54.6 uF is charged to 295 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 54.6, V = 295 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*54.6e-6*(295)^2 | Answer: 2376 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 180 V with 680 primary turns and 290 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 180, N1 = 680, N2 = 290 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 180 * 290/680 | Answer: 76.76 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 390 V and draws an armature current of 59 A. If the armature resistance is 0.56 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 390, Ia = 59, Ra = 0.56 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 390 - 59*0.56 | Answer: 357 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 25 A at 415 V (line) with a power factor of 0.78. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 25, VL = 415, pf = 0.78 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*415*25*0.78 / 1000 | Answer: 14.02 kW

question: A load has real power 15 kW and apparent power 175 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 15, S = 175 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 15 / 175 | Answer: 0.08571

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 6 V across R1 = 8 ohm and R2 = 12 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 6, R1 = 8, R2 = 12 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 6*12 / (8+12) | Answer: 3.6 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 60 kohm and Rin = 9 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 60, Rin = 9 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 60 / 9 | Answer: 6.667

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 90 kohm and Rg = 47 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 90, Rg = 47 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 90/47 | Answer: 2.915

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 5562. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 5562 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(5562) | Answer: 37.45 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.8 m carries a central point load of 115 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.8, W = 115 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 115*4.8 / 4 | Answer: 138 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.6 m carries a UDL of 5 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.6, w = 5 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 5*(4.6)^2 / 8 | Answer: 13.22 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 4.6 m carries a point load 20 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.6, W = 20 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 20*4.6 | Answer: 92 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 1.2 m carries a UDL of 10 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 1.2, w = 10 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 10*(1.2)^2 / 2 | Answer: 7.2 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 8.1 m carries a point load 65 kN at distance 2.2 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 8.1, a = 2.2, W = 65 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 65*(8.1 - 2.2) / 8.1 | Answer: 47.35 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 4.4 m) carries a central point load 65 kN. With E = 25 GPa and I = 480e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=65000 N, L=4400.0 mm, E=25000 MPa, I=480e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 9.613 mm

question: An RC beam has overall depth 410 mm, clear cover 35 mm and main bars of diameter 12 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 410, c = 35, dia = 12 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 410 - 35 - 12/2 | Answer: 369 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 11.7 m^2 carrying a factored load of 15.9 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 11.7, w = 15.9 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 15.9 * 11.7 | Answer: 186 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 5.4 m, unit weight 17 kN/m^3, phi = 34 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 6.3e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1.2, area = 2.8e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 6.3, i = 1.2, A = 2.8 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (6.3e-4)*1.2*(2.8e-3) | Answer: 2117 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 0.7 m, bed slope 0.006 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.02. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 4.8 m under a head of 0.3 m. Taking Cd = 0.63 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 5.9 m wide carries a discharge of 12.4 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A tank of volume 380 m^3 treats a flow of 25 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 380, Q = 25 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 380 / 25 | Answer: 15.2 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 300 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.21 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 7 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 300, k = 0.21, t = 7 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 300*(1 - e^(-0.21*7)) | Answer: 231 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.86, rainfall intensity 40 mm/h over a catchment of 59.6 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.86, i = 40, A = 59.6 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.86*40*59.6 / 360 | Answer: 5.695 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.02 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 230 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.02, M = 230 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 230*(30+0.02)/30 | Answer: 230.2 m

question: Convert the decimal number 1566 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 1566 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 61E (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 01001011 and 00101001.
solution: XOR: 01100010 | Count of 1s = 3 | Answer: 3
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 720 megabits is sent over a link of 67 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 720, B = 67 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 720 / 67 | Answer: 10.75 s

question: A link has bandwidth 13 Mbps and round-trip time 190 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 13, R = 190 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 13e6 * 190e-3 bits = 2470 kb | Answer: 2470 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.94, cache access time 8 ns and main-memory access time 200 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.94, tc = 8, tm = 200 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.94*8 + (1 - 0.94)*200 | Answer: 19.52 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 634772 elements?
solution: Given: n = 634772 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(634772)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.011, memory access time 140 ns and page-fault service time 5 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 5 ms = 5000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.011)*140 + 0.011*5000000.0 ns | Answer: 55.14 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 0.8 m^3 at 220 kPa and 310 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 0.8, P = 220, Tk = 310 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (220e3)*0.8 / (8.314*310) | Answer: 68.29 mol

question: For a reaction with A = 3e10 /s and activation energy 60 kJ/mol at 490 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 3, Ea = 60, Tk = 490 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 3e10 * exp(-60e3 / (8.314*490)) | Answer: 12045 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.97 and bottoms xW = 0.1, with relative volatility alpha = 2.9. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.97, xw = 0.1, al = 2.9 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.97/0.03)(0.9/0.1)] / ln(2.9) | Answer: 5.329 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.64 and x = 0.43. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.64, x = 0.43 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.64/0.36) / (0.43/0.57) | Answer: 2.357

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.48 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 30 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.48, Psat = 30 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.48 * 30 | Answer: 14.4 kPa

question: A stream of 8.9 kg/s with specific heat 2 kJ/kg-K is heated through 85 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 8.9, cp = 2, dT = 85 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 8.9*2*85 | Answer: 1513 kW

question: A reactor of volume 6.1 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 3.2 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 6.1, Q = 3.2 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 6.1 / 3.2 | Answer: 1.906 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 7.5e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 3 mm with a concentration difference of 40 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 7.5, L = 3, dC = 40 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (7.5e-9)*40 / (3e-3) | Answer: 100 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 5.2 min and steady-state gain 1.4. For a step input of magnitude 19, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 5.2, K = 1.4, M = 19 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 1.4 * 19 | Answer: 26.6 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 35 m^2 flies at 250 m/s (air density 1 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.7. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 35, V = 250, rho = 1, CL = 0.7 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1*(250)^2*35*0.7 / 1000 | Answer: 765.6 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 105 m^2 flies at 130 m/s (density 1.225 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.1. Find the drag force in kN.
A block of mass 43 kg has a volume of 4.6e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 43, V = 4.6 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 43 / (4.6e-3) | Answer: 9348 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 2600 mm is heated through 65 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 12e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 2600, dT = 65, al = 12 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 2600*12e-6*65 | Answer: 2.028 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 40 ohm, R2 = 105 ohm and R3 = 145 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 40, R2 = 105, R3 = 145 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 105*145 / 40 | Answer: 380.6 ohm

question: A measurement reads 9.36 when the true value is 100. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.36, true = 100 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.36 - 100| / 100 * 100 | Answer: 90.64 %

question: Annual demand is 27000 units, ordering cost 120 per order and holding cost 5 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 27000, S = 120, H = 5 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*27000*120 / 5) | Answer: 1138 units

question: An asset costs 120000 with salvage value 22000 after 10 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 120000, Sv = 22000, n = 10 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (120000 - 22000) / 10 | Answer: 9800 per year

question: A product sells for 460 per unit with variable cost 20 per unit and fixed costs 160000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 460, V = 20, F = 160000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 160000 / (460 - 20) | Answer: 363.6 units

question: Find the present worth of 110000 received 3 years from now at an interest rate of 9% per year.
solution: Given: F = 110000, n = 3, i = 9 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 110000 / (1 + 0.09)^3 | Answer: 8494 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.95, 0.95 and 0.95 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.95, r2 = 0.95, r3 = 0.95 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.95*0.95*0.95 | Answer: 0.8574

question: A process produces 38 defective items in a batch of 20000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 38, N = 20000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 38/20000 * 1e6 | Answer: 1900 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -4x^3 + 2x^2 + 3x - 3 evaluated at x = -1.
For f(x) = 6x^3 + 6x^2 - 9x + 5, find f''(x) at x = 2.

question: Find the larger real root of x^2 - x - 6 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[2, -4], [4, 6]].
solution: Given: a = 2, b = -4, c = 4, d = 6 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (2)(6) - (-4)(4) | Answer: 28

question: Find the determinant of [[-4, -5, 1], [2, -3, -4], [0, 2, -2]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: -72

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[6, -8], [-4, 3]].
solution: Trace tr = 9, Determinant = -14 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 10.35

question: Solve for x: 6x + -2y = 5 and 4x + -5y = -6.

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 31, 66, 41, 45, 42.
solution: Sum = 225 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 45 | Answer: 45

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 39, 34, 32, 25, 32.
solution: Mean = 32.4 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 5.03

question: Find the slope of the line through (-5, -5) and (-4, -1).
solution: Given: x1 = -5, y1 = -5, x2 = -4, y2 = -1 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (-1 - -5) / (-4 - -5) | Answer: 4

question: Find the distance between the points (-9, 9) and (-9, -8).
solution: Given: x1 = -9, y1 = 9, x2 = -9, y2 = -8 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((0)^2 + (-17)^2) | Answer: 17 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (0,-4), (-1,3), (3,-8).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 8.5 sq units

question: Find the 19th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 14 and common difference 1.
solution: Given: a = 14, d = 1, n = 19 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = 14 + (19 - 1)*1 | Answer: 32

question: Find the sum of the first 28 terms of an AP with first term 15 and common difference 4.
solution: Given: a = 15, d = 4, n = 28 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 28/2 [2*15 + (28-1)*4] | Answer: 1932

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 41000 at 4.6% per annum for 1 years.
solution: Given: P = 41000, R = 4.6, Tt = 1 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 41000 * 4.6 * 1 / 100 | Answer: 1886 currency units

question: Find the amount when 26500 is invested at 8.7% per annum compounded annually for 2 years.
solution: Given: P = 26500, R = 8.7, Tt = 2 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 26500 * (1 + 8.7/100)^2 | Answer: 31312 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (7, 5, 4) and (-1, 2, -7).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (-2, -6, -1) and (-5, 5, 2).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 41.59

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (3, -5, 4) and (-6, -1, -1).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 113 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number 12 + -2i.
solution: Given: a = 12, b = -2 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((12)^2 + (-2)^2) | Answer: 12.17

question: Evaluate f(x) = -4x^3 + 3x^2 + 5x - 2 at x = 1.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-140 with initial guess x0=11, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.3 and ordinates 16, 15, 5, 0, 4, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 320 and 62.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 320 and 62 | Answer: GCD = 2

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 80 and 64.
solution: Given: a = 80, b = 64 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 80*64 / 16 | Answer: 320
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 23 mm carries an axial tensile load of 74 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 36 mm and length 1700 mm carries an axial load of 33 kN. Take E = 70 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 72 mm transmits a torque of 1200 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 72, Tt = 1200 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(1200*1000) / (pi*(72)^3) | Answer: 16.37 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 31 mm and length 1200 mm carries a torque of 1100 N-m. With G = 77 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (31)^4 / 32 = 90666 mm^4 | theta = (1100*1000)(1200) / (77000 * 90666) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 10.83 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 52 mm wide and 90 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 52, h = 90 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 52*(90)^2 / 6 | Answer: 70200 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (47 mm x 190 mm) carries a bending moment of 22 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6
