question: A component of ultimate strength 570 MPa is designed for a working stress of 110 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 570, sw = 110 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 570 / 110 | Answer: 5.182

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1050 mm and wall thickness 8 mm carries an internal pressure of 1.5 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1050, t = 8, P = 1.5 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 1.5*1050 / (2*8) | Answer: 98.44 MPa

question: 2.9 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 160 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.9, dT = 160 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 2.9 * 0.718 * 160 | Answer: 333.2 kJ

question: 5 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 165 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 5, dT = 165 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 5 * 1.005 * 165 | Answer: 829.1 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 3.7 m^3 at 490 K with mass 4.8 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 3.7, Tk = 490, m = 4.8 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 4.8*0.287*490 / 3.7 | Answer: 182.4 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 2.7 kg of air expands isothermally at 330 K from volume V1 to 4*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.7, Tk = 330, ratio = 4 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 2.7*0.287*330*ln(4) | Answer: 354.5 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 2.6 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.1 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 2.6, D = 0.1 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*2.6*0.1 / 0.001 | Answer: 260000

question: Water flows at 3.5 m/s through a pipe of diameter 190 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 2.9 m. Taking Cv = 0.95, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 2.9, cv = 0.95 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.95*sqrt(2*9.81*2.9) | Answer: 7.166 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 230 mm) water flows at 2.7 m/s. It contracts to diameter 120 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
Water flows at 3.5 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.2 m and length 60 m. With friction factor f = 0.021, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 36 teeth drives a gear of 78 teeth. If the pinion runs at 800 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 36, z2 = 78, N1 = 800 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 800*36 / 78 | Answer: 369.2 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 150 mm rotates at 200 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 150, N = 200 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.15)*200 / 60 | Answer: 1.571 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 34.6 kW at 1450 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 34.6, N = 1450 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(34.6*1000) / (2*pi*1450) | Answer: 227.9 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 3 kg rotates at radius 0.26 m at 450 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 9000 N/m and mass 11.1 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 9000, m = 11.1 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(9000/11.1) | Answer: 4.532 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 1.6 m^2 and thickness 0.13 m has conductivity k = 20.9 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 175 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 1.6, L = 0.13, k = 20.9, dT = 175 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 20.9*1.6*175 / 0.13 | Answer: 45015 W

question: A surface of area 4.9 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 75 W/m^2-K to surroundings 35 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 4.9, h = 75, dT = 35 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 75*4.9*35 | Answer: 12862 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 70 m/min, feed = 0.17 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2.7 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 70, f = 0.17, d = 2.7 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*70*0.17*2.7 | Answer: 32130 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 80 mm is turned at 1150 rpm with a feed of 0.2 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 80, N = 1150, f = 0.2 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 80 / (0.2*1150) | Answer: 0.3478 min

question: A resistor of 90 ohm carries a current of 1.4 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 90, I = 1.4 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 1.4 * 90 | Answer: 126 V

question: Three resistors 3 ohm, 87 ohm and 27 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 3, R2 = 87, R3 = 27 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 3 + 87 + 27 | Answer: 117 ohm

question: Two resistors 98 ohm and 23 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 98, R2 = 23 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 98*23 / (98+23) | Answer: 18.63 ohm

question: A device draws 3.9 A at 195 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 195, I = 3.9 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 195 * 3.9 | Answer: 760.5 W

question: A current of 8.1 A flows through a 44 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 8.1, R = 44 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (8.1)^2 * 44 | Answer: 2887 W

question: Two capacitors 4 uF and 38.3 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 4, C2 = 38.3 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 4*38.3 / (4+38.3) | Answer: 3.622 uF

question: A resistor 18 kohm and capacitor 0.8 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 18, C = 0.8 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (18k)(0.8u) = 14.4 ms | Answer: 14.4 ms

question: An inductor 93.1 mH is in series with 195 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 93.1, R = 195 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (93.1e-3) / 195 | Answer: 0.4774 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 71.1 mH inductor at 890 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 71.1, f = 890 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (890)(71.1e-3) | Answer: 397.6 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 42.3 uF capacitor at 480 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 42.3, f = 480 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (480)(42.3e-6)) | Answer: 7.839 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 46 ohm, XL = 63 ohm and XC = 117 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 46, XL = 63, XC = 117 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(46^2 + (63 - 117)^2) | Answer: 70.94 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 74.9 mH and C = 4.7 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 74.9, C = 4.7 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(74.9e-3 * 4.7e-6)) | Answer: 268.2 Hz

question: A capacitor of 34.8 uF is charged to 110 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 34.8, V = 110 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*34.8e-6*(110)^2 | Answer: 210.5 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 440 V with 420 primary turns and 160 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 440, N1 = 420, N2 = 160 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 440 * 160/420 | Answer: 167.6 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 440 V and draws an armature current of 38 A. If the armature resistance is 0.71 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 440, Ia = 38, Ra = 0.71 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 440 - 38*0.71 | Answer: 413 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 170 A at 415 V (line) with a power factor of 0.79. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 170, VL = 415, pf = 0.79 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*415*170*0.79 / 1000 | Answer: 96.53 kW

question: A load has real power 80 kW and apparent power 190 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 80, S = 190 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 80 / 190 | Answer: 0.4211

question: A machine delivers 60 kW output while drawing 132 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 60, Pi = 132 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 60/132 * 100 | Answer: 45.45 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 29 V across R1 = 5 ohm and R2 = 9 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 29, R1 = 5, R2 = 9 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 29*9 / (5+9) | Answer: 18.64 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 60 kohm and Rin = 37 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 60, Rin = 37 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 60 / 37 | Answer: 1.622

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 140 kohm and Rg = 6 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 140, Rg = 6 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 140/6 | Answer: 24.33

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 4775. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 4775 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(4775) | Answer: 36.79 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.9 m carries a central point load of 55 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.9, W = 55 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 55*4.9 / 4 | Answer: 67.38 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.6 m carries a UDL of 40 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 9.6, w = 40 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 40*(9.6)^2 / 8 | Answer: 460.8 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 5.1 m carries a point load 15 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.1, W = 15 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 15*5.1 | Answer: 76.5 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 5.2 m carries a UDL of 8 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.2, w = 8 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 8*(5.2)^2 / 2 | Answer: 108.2 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 8.5 m carries a point load 65 kN at distance 3.2 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 8.5, a = 3.2, W = 65 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 65*(8.5 - 3.2) / 8.5 | Answer: 40.53 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 7.3 m) carries a central point load 60 kN. With E = 200 GPa and I = 390e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=60000 N, L=7300.0 mm, E=200000 MPa, I=390e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 6.234 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 7.9 m carries a UDL of 15 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7.9, w = 15 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 15*(7.9)^2 / 12 | Answer: 78.01 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 340 mm, clear cover 45 mm and main bars of diameter 16 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 340, c = 45, dia = 16 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 340 - 45 - 16/2 | Answer: 287 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 25.7 m^2 carrying a factored load of 10.7 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 25.7, w = 10.7 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 10.7 * 25.7 | Answer: 275 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 3.3 m, unit weight 16 kN/m^3, phi = 38 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 5.7e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1.2, area = 1.7e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 5.7, i = 1.2, A = 1.7 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (5.7e-4)*1.2*(1.7e-3) | Answer: 1163 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 0.5 m, bed slope 0.008 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.016. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 1.5 m under a head of 1.1 m. Taking Cd = 0.64 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 3 m wide carries a discharge of 11.3 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 530 m and design speed 90 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 530, V = 90 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (90)^2 / (127*530) | Answer: 0.1203
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: A tank of volume 390 m^3 treats a flow of 85 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 390, Q = 85 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 390 / 85 | Answer: 4.588 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 360 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.2 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 5 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 360, k = 0.2, t = 5 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 360*(1 - e^(-0.2*5)) | Answer: 227.6 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.61, rainfall intensity 105 mm/h over a catchment of 22.9 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.61, i = 105, A = 22.9 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.61*105*22.9 / 360 | Answer: 4.074 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.07 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 370 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.07, M = 370 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 370*(20+0.07)/20 | Answer: 371.3 m

question: Convert the decimal number 458 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 458 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 1CA (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 10001001 and 00110001.
solution: XOR: 10111000 | Count of 1s = 4 | Answer: 4
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 670 megabits is sent over a link of 85 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 670, B = 85 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 670 / 85 | Answer: 7.882 s

question: A link has bandwidth 67 Mbps and round-trip time 30 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 67, R = 30 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 67e6 * 30e-3 bits = 2010 kb | Answer: 2010 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.87, cache access time 3 ns and main-memory access time 100 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.87, tc = 3, tm = 100 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.87*3 + (1 - 0.87)*100 | Answer: 15.61 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 998972 elements?
solution: Given: n = 998972 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(998972)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.01, memory access time 90 ns and page-fault service time 9 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 9 ms = 9000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.01)*90 + 0.01*9000000.0 ns | Answer: 90.09 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 2.3 m^3 at 170 kPa and 490 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 2.3, P = 170, Tk = 490 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (170e3)*2.3 / (8.314*490) | Answer: 95.98 mol

question: For a reaction with A = 9e10 /s and activation energy 70 kJ/mol at 380 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 9, Ea = 70, Tk = 380 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 9e10 * exp(-70e3 / (8.314*380)) | Answer: 21.46 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.97 and bottoms xW = 0.05, with relative volatility alpha = 3.1. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.97, xw = 0.05, al = 3.1 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.97/0.03)(0.95/0.05)] / ln(3.1) | Answer: 5.675 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.9 and x = 0.28. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.9, x = 0.28 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.9/0.1) / (0.28/0.72) | Answer: 23.14

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.18 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 110 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.18, Psat = 110 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.18 * 110 | Answer: 19.8 kPa

question: A stream of 7.8 kg/s with specific heat 4 kJ/kg-K is heated through 20 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 7.8, cp = 4, dT = 20 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 7.8*4*20 | Answer: 624 kW

question: A reactor of volume 19.2 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 4 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 19.2, Q = 4 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 19.2 / 4 | Answer: 4.8 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 3.8e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 1 mm with a concentration difference of 110 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 3.8, L = 1, dC = 110 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (3.8e-9)*110 / (1e-3) | Answer: 418 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 7.2 min and steady-state gain 2. For a step input of magnitude 11, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 7.2, K = 2, M = 11 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 2 * 11 | Answer: 22 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 55 m^2 flies at 70 m/s (air density 0.4 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.9. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 55, V = 70, rho = 0.4, CL = 0.9 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.4*(70)^2*55*0.9 / 1000 | Answer: 48.51 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 50 m^2 flies at 150 m/s (density 0.4 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.07. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 50, V = 150, rho = 0.4, CD = 0.07 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.4*(150)^2*50*0.07 / 1000 | Answer: 15.75 kN

question: A specimen under stress 310 MPa shows an elastic strain of 1.2e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 310, eps = 1.2 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 310 / (1.2e-3) MPa = 258.3 GPa | Answer: 258.3 GPa

question: A block of mass 13 kg has a volume of 4.7e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 13, V = 4.7 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 13 / (4.7e-3) | Answer: 2766 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 2100 mm is heated through 125 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 17e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 2100, dT = 125, al = 17 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 2100*17e-6*125 | Answer: 4.463 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 110 ohm, R2 = 60 ohm and R3 = 155 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 110, R2 = 60, R3 = 155 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 60*155 / 110 | Answer: 84.55 ohm

question: A measurement reads 9.64 when the true value is 50. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.64, true = 50 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.64 - 50| / 50 * 100 | Answer: 80.72 %

question: Annual demand is 7000 units, ordering cost 50 per order and holding cost 5 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 7000, S = 50, H = 5 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*7000*50 / 5) | Answer: 374.2 units

question: An asset costs 120000 with salvage value 22000 after 6 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 120000, Sv = 22000, n = 6 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (120000 - 22000) / 6 | Answer: 16333 per year

question: A product sells for 420 per unit with variable cost 80 per unit and fixed costs 75000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 420, V = 80, F = 75000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 75000 / (420 - 80) | Answer: 220.6 units

question: Find the present worth of 70000 received 6 years from now at an interest rate of 9% per year.
solution: Given: F = 70000, n = 6, i = 9 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 70000 / (1 + 0.09)^6 | Answer: 41739 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.92, 0.91 and 0.97 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.92, r2 = 0.91, r3 = 0.97 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.92*0.91*0.97 | Answer: 0.8121

question: A process produces 34 defective items in a batch of 1000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 34, N = 1000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 34/1000 * 1e6 | Answer: 34000 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = 4x^3 - 2x^2 + 5x + 4 evaluated at x = 1.
For f(x) = -x^3 + 2x^2 - 9x + 9, find f''(x) at x = -5.
Evaluate the definite integral of (-5x^2 + x + 3) dx from x = -3 to x = 3.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = -5x^3/3 + 1x^2/2 + 3x | Evaluate F(3) - F(-3) | Answer: -72
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 5x^2 - 10x + 2 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[-6, 1], [8, -2]].
solution: Given: a = -6, b = 1, c = 8, d = -2 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (-6)(-2) - (1)(8) | Answer: 4

question: Find the determinant of [[3, 2, -2], [5, 2, -6], [-5, -4, 0]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: 8

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[-5, -5], [-4, 4]].
solution: Trace tr = -1, Determinant = -40 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 5.844

question: Solve for x: -6x + -1y = 0 and 5x + 0y = 7.
solution: Determinant = -6*0 - -1*5 = 5 | x = (e d - b f) / det = 1.4 | Answer: x = 1.4
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 75, 98, 48, 53, 68.
solution: Sum = 342 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 68.4 | Answer: 68.4

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 27, 15, 36, 8, 28.
solution: Mean = 22.8 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 11.17

question: Find the slope of the line through (7, -9) and (6, -2).
solution: Given: x1 = 7, y1 = -9, x2 = 6, y2 = -2 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (-2 - -9) / (6 - 7) | Answer: -7

question: Find the distance between the points (1, -8) and (-4, 2).
solution: Given: x1 = 1, y1 = -8, x2 = -4, y2 = 2 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-5)^2 + (10)^2) | Answer: 11.18 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (8,2), (-4,7), (-3,-1).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 45.5 sq units

question: Find the 26th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -11 and common difference -5.
solution: Given: a = -11, d = -5, n = 26 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -11 + (26 - 1)*-5 | Answer: -136

question: Find the sum of the first 12 terms of an AP with first term -13 and common difference 0.
solution: Given: a = -13, d = 0, n = 12 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 12/2 [2*-13 + (12-1)*0] | Answer: -156

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 23000 at 13.7% per annum for 6 years.
solution: Given: P = 23000, R = 13.7, Tt = 6 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 23000 * 13.7 * 6 / 100 | Answer: 18906 currency units

question: Find the amount when 12000 is invested at 10.6% per annum compounded annually for 4 years.
solution: Given: P = 12000, R = 10.6, Tt = 4 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 12000 * (1 + 10.6/100)^4 | Answer: 17956 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (7, 6, -8) and (-2, 0, -6).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (-5, -5, -1) and (2, 1, -5).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 37.82

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (-3, 3, -2) and (-5, -5, 5).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 104.3 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number -6 + 11i.
solution: Given: a = -6, b = 11 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((-6)^2 + (11)^2) | Answer: 12.53

question: Evaluate f(x) = -x^3 - 4x^2 - x at x = 5.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-90 with initial guess x0=11, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1 and ordinates 19, 14, 2, 17, 10, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 146 and 62.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 146 and 62 | Answer: GCD = 2

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 42 and 56.
solution: Given: a = 42, b = 56 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 42*56 / 14 | Answer: 168
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 36 mm carries an axial tensile load of 116 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 30 mm and length 2700 mm carries an axial load of 79 kN. Take E = 200 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 56 mm transmits a torque of 1950 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 56, Tt = 1950 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(1950*1000) / (pi*(56)^3) | Answer: 56.55 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 52 mm and length 1900 mm carries a torque of 700 N-m. With G = 80 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (52)^4 / 32 = 717816 mm^4 | theta = (700*1000)(1900) / (80000 * 717816) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 1.327 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 121 mm wide and 100 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 121, h = 100 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 121*(100)^2 / 6 | Answer: 201667 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (115 mm x 180 mm) carries a bending moment of 26 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (52 mm x 160 mm) has effective length 2600 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 300 MPa is designed for a working stress of 240 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 300, sw = 240 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 300 / 240 | Answer: 1.25

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1100 mm and wall thickness 15 mm carries an internal pressure of 2.6 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1100, t = 15, P = 2.6 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 2.6*1100 / (2*15) | Answer: 95.33 MPa

question: 5.3 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 85 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 5.3, dT = 85 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 5.3 * 0.718 * 85 | Answer: 323.5 kJ

question: 4.8 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 170 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.8, dT = 170 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 4.8 * 1.005 * 170 | Answer: 820.1 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 1.6 m^3 at 360 K with mass 5.2 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 1.6, Tk = 360, m = 5.2 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 5.2*0.287*360 / 1.6 | Answer: 335.8 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 1.3 kg of air expands isothermally at 430 K from volume V1 to 5*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1.3, Tk = 430, ratio = 5 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 1.3*0.287*430*ln(5) | Answer: 258.2 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 4.6 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.06 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 4.6, D = 0.06 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*4.6*0.06 / 0.001 | Answer: 276000

question: Water flows at 2.5 m/s through a pipe of diameter 240 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 8.7 m. Taking Cv = 0.99, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 8.7, cv = 0.99 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.99*sqrt(2*9.81*8.7) | Answer: 12.93 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 290 mm) water flows at 1.8 m/s. It contracts to diameter 50 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 290, d2 = 50, V1 = 1.8 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 1.8*(290/50)^2 | Answer: 60.55 m/s

question: Water flows at 2 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.24 m and length 50 m. With friction factor f = 0.039, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 34 teeth drives a gear of 53 teeth. If the pinion runs at 950 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 34, z2 = 53, N1 = 950 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 950*34 / 53 | Answer: 609.4 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 170 mm rotates at 1400 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 170, N = 1400 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.17)*1400 / 60 | Answer: 12.46 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 2.8 kW at 450 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 2.8, N = 450 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(2.8*1000) / (2*pi*450) | Answer: 59.42 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 5.9 kg rotates at radius 0.23 m at 500 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 16500 N/m and mass 18.3 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 16500, m = 18.3 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(16500/18.3) | Answer: 4.779 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 8.8 m^2 and thickness 0.14 m has conductivity k = 8.6 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 135 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 8.8, L = 0.14, k = 8.6, dT = 135 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 8.6*8.8*135 / 0.14 | Answer: 72977 W

question: A surface of area 4.5 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 155 W/m^2-K to surroundings 115 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 4.5, h = 155, dT = 115 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 155*4.5*115 | Answer: 80212 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 60 m/min, feed = 0.44 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2.4 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 60, f = 0.44, d = 2.4 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*60*0.44*2.4 | Answer: 63360 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 80 mm is turned at 500 rpm with a feed of 0.13 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 80, N = 500, f = 0.13 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 80 / (0.13*500) | Answer: 1.231 min

question: A resistor of 62 ohm carries a current of 3.4 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 62, I = 3.4 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 3.4 * 62 | Answer: 210.8 V

question: Three resistors 31 ohm, 3 ohm and 66 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 31, R2 = 3, R3 = 66 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 31 + 3 + 66 | Answer: 100 ohm

question: Two resistors 81 ohm and 32 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 81, R2 = 32 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 81*32 / (81+32) | Answer: 22.94 ohm

question: A device draws 9 A at 55 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 55, I = 9 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 55 * 9 | Answer: 495 W

question: A current of 4.9 A flows through a 125 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 4.9, R = 125 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (4.9)^2 * 125 | Answer: 3001 W

question: Two capacitors 32.3 uF and 34.9 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 32.3, C2 = 34.9 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 32.3*34.9 / (32.3+34.9) | Answer: 16.77 uF

question: A resistor 8 kohm and capacitor 2.1 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 8, C = 2.1 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (8k)(2.1u) = 16.8 ms | Answer: 16.8 ms

question: An inductor 145.3 mH is in series with 60 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 145.3, R = 60 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (145.3e-3) / 60 | Answer: 2.422 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 178.8 mH inductor at 90 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 178.8, f = 90 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (90)(178.8e-3) | Answer: 101.1 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 4.1 uF capacitor at 850 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 4.1, f = 850 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (850)(4.1e-6)) | Answer: 45.67 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 53 ohm, XL = 18 ohm and XC = 90 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 53, XL = 18, XC = 90 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(53^2 + (18 - 90)^2) | Answer: 89.4 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 45.1 mH and C = 5 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 45.1, C = 5 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(45.1e-3 * 5e-6)) | Answer: 335.2 Hz

question: A capacitor of 4.1 uF is charged to 395 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 4.1, V = 395 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*4.1e-6*(395)^2 | Answer: 319.9 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 270 V with 720 primary turns and 380 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 270, N1 = 720, N2 = 380 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 270 * 380/720 | Answer: 142.5 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 300 V and draws an armature current of 9 A. If the armature resistance is 1.2 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 300, Ia = 9, Ra = 1.2 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 300 - 9*1.2 | Answer: 289.2 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 165 A at 415 V (line) with a power factor of 0.8. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 165, VL = 415, pf = 0.8 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*415*165*0.8 / 1000 | Answer: 94.88 kW

question: A machine delivers 25 kW output while drawing 172 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 25, Pi = 172 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 25/172 * 100 | Answer: 14.53 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 16 V across R1 = 28 ohm and R2 = 37 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 16, R1 = 28, R2 = 37 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 16*37 / (28+37) | Answer: 9.108 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 10 kohm and Rin = 33 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 10, Rin = 33 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 10 / 33 | Answer: 0.303

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 80 kohm and Rg = 22 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 80, Rg = 22 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 80/22 | Answer: 4.636

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 3999. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 3999 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(3999) | Answer: 36.02 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 8.6 m carries a central point load of 100 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 8.6, W = 100 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 100*8.6 / 4 | Answer: 215 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 1.7 m carries a point load 80 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 1.7, W = 80 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 80*1.7 | Answer: 136 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 6 m carries a UDL of 18 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6, w = 18 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 18*(6)^2 / 2 | Answer: 324 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.8 m carries a point load 65 kN at distance 1.7 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 4.8, a = 1.7, W = 65 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 65*(4.8 - 1.7) / 4.8 | Answer: 41.98 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 7.8 m) carries a central point load 60 kN. With E = 30 GPa and I = 180e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=60000 N, L=7800.0 mm, E=30000 MPa, I=180e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 109.8 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 7.9 m carries a UDL of 21 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7.9, w = 21 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 21*(7.9)^2 / 12 | Answer: 109.2 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 550 mm, clear cover 50 mm and main bars of diameter 16 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 550, c = 50, dia = 16 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 550 - 50 - 16/2 | Answer: 492 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 25.5 m^2 carrying a factored load of 11.9 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 25.5, w = 11.9 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 11.9 * 25.5 | Answer: 303.4 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 5.4 m, unit weight 17 kN/m^3, phi = 28 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 6e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.6, area = 7.9e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 6, i = 0.6, A = 7.9 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (6e-4)*0.6*(7.9e-3) | Answer: 2844 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 0.8 m, bed slope 0.001 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.012. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 2.1 m under a head of 0.2 m. Taking Cd = 0.64 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 5.9 m wide carries a discharge of 26.9 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A tank of volume 760 m^3 treats a flow of 125 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 760, Q = 125 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 760 / 125 | Answer: 6.08 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 220 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.32 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 3 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 220, k = 0.32, t = 3 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 220*(1 - e^(-0.32*3)) | Answer: 135.8 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.67, rainfall intensity 35 mm/h over a catchment of 52.6 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.67, i = 35, A = 52.6 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.67*35*52.6 / 360 | Answer: 3.426 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.03 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 660 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.03, M = 660 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 660*(20+0.03)/20 | Answer: 661 m

question: Convert the decimal number 2573 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 2573 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: A0D (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 11110001 and 11111110.
solution: XOR: 00001111 | Count of 1s = 4 | Answer: 4
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 390 megabits is sent over a link of 57 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 390, B = 57 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 390 / 57 | Answer: 6.842 s

question: A link has bandwidth 69 Mbps and round-trip time 70 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 69, R = 70 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 69e6 * 70e-3 bits = 4830 kb | Answer: 4830 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.8, cache access time 5 ns and main-memory access time 110 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.8, tc = 5, tm = 110 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.8*5 + (1 - 0.8)*110 | Answer: 26 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 65833 elements?
solution: Given: n = 65833 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(65833)) + 1 | Answer: 17

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.019, memory access time 180 ns and page-fault service time 4 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 4 ms = 4000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.019)*180 + 0.019*4000000.0 ns | Answer: 76.18 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 0.2 m^3 at 410 kPa and 390 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 0.2, P = 410, Tk = 390 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (410e3)*0.2 / (8.314*390) | Answer: 25.29 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.4 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 17 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.4, t = 17 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.4*17) | Answer: 0.9989

question: For a reaction with A = 3e10 /s and activation energy 80 kJ/mol at 320 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 3, Ea = 80, Tk = 320 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 3e10 * exp(-80e3 / (8.314*320)) | Answer: 0.002618 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.92 and bottoms xW = 0.06, with relative volatility alpha = 1.8. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.92, xw = 0.06, al = 1.8 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.92/0.08)(0.94/0.06)] / ln(1.8) | Answer: 8.836 stages

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.29 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 40 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.29, Psat = 40 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.29 * 40 | Answer: 11.6 kPa

question: A stream of 6.9 kg/s with specific heat 2.8 kJ/kg-K is heated through 55 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 6.9, cp = 2.8, dT = 55 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 6.9*2.8*55 | Answer: 1063 kW

question: A reactor of volume 5.5 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 3.7 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 5.5, Q = 3.7 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 5.5 / 3.7 | Answer: 1.486 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 7.7e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 2 mm with a concentration difference of 10 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 7.7, L = 2, dC = 10 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (7.7e-9)*10 / (2e-3) | Answer: 38.5 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 1.2 min and steady-state gain 3.1. For a step input of magnitude 5, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 1.2, K = 3.1, M = 5 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 3.1 * 5 | Answer: 15.5 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 110 m^2 flies at 130 m/s (air density 0.7 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.4. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 110, V = 130, rho = 0.7, CL = 0.4 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.7*(130)^2*110*0.4 / 1000 | Answer: 260.3 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 85 m^2 flies at 150 m/s (density 1 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.04. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 85, V = 150, rho = 1, CD = 0.04 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*1*(150)^2*85*0.04 / 1000 | Answer: 38.25 kN

question: A block of mass 34 kg has a volume of 3.9e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 34, V = 3.9 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 34 / (3.9e-3) | Answer: 8718 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 1900 mm is heated through 35 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 11e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 1900, dT = 35, al = 11 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 1900*11e-6*35 | Answer: 0.7315 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 190 ohm, R2 = 120 ohm and R3 = 275 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 190, R2 = 120, R3 = 275 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 120*275 / 190 | Answer: 173.7 ohm

question: A measurement reads 9.31 when the true value is 20. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.31, true = 20 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.31 - 20| / 20 * 100 | Answer: 53.45 %

question: Annual demand is 34000 units, ordering cost 130 per order and holding cost 13 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 34000, S = 130, H = 13 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*34000*130 / 13) | Answer: 824.6 units

question: An asset costs 410000 with salvage value 16000 after 17 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 410000, Sv = 16000, n = 17 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (410000 - 16000) / 17 | Answer: 23176 per year

question: A product sells for 400 per unit with variable cost 60 per unit and fixed costs 180000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 400, V = 60, F = 180000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 180000 / (400 - 60) | Answer: 529.4 units

question: Find the present worth of 35000 received 6 years from now at an interest rate of 7% per year.
solution: Given: F = 35000, n = 6, i = 7 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 35000 / (1 + 0.07)^6 | Answer: 23322 currency units

question: A process produces 16 defective items in a batch of 17000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 16, N = 17000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 16/17000 * 1e6 | Answer: 941.2 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = 6x^3 + 7x^2 - 8x - 7 evaluated at x = -1.
For f(x) = -x^3 - 6x^2 - 4x + 7, find f''(x) at x = -2.
Evaluate the definite integral of (5x^2 + 3x - 6) dx from x = 0 to x = 3.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = 5x^3/3 + 3x^2/2 + -6x | Evaluate F(3) - F(0) | Answer: 40.5
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 3x^2 - 11x - 12 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[-9, -8], [-5, 7]].
solution: Given: a = -9, b = -8, c = -5, d = 7 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (-9)(7) - (-8)(-5) | Answer: -103

question: Find the determinant of [[4, 4, -5], [2, -6, -2], [-4, 5, 1]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: 110

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[1, 6], [0, -3]].
solution: Trace tr = -2, Determinant = -3 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 1

question: Solve for x: 3x + 1y = -5 and -4x + 0y = 3.
solution: Determinant = 3*0 - 1*-4 = 4 | x = (e d - b f) / det = -0.75 | Answer: x = -0.75
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 89, 46, 76, 62, 85.
solution: Sum = 358 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 71.6 | Answer: 71.6

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 48, 1, 15, 5, 13.
solution: Mean = 16.4 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 18.57

question: Find the slope of the line through (9, -6) and (4, 3).
solution: Given: x1 = 9, y1 = -6, x2 = 4, y2 = 3 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (3 - -6) / (4 - 9) | Answer: -1.8

question: Find the distance between the points (-8, 0) and (7, -7).
solution: Given: x1 = -8, y1 = 0, x2 = 7, y2 = -7 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((15)^2 + (-7)^2) | Answer: 16.55 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (-2,2), (2,1), (-3,6).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 7.5 sq units

question: Find the 7th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 2 and common difference 2.
solution: Given: a = 2, d = 2, n = 7 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = 2 + (7 - 1)*2 | Answer: 14

question: Find the sum of the first 10 terms of an AP with first term 1 and common difference -1.
solution: Given: a = 1, d = -1, n = 10 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 10/2 [2*1 + (10-1)*-1] | Answer: -35

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 39000 at 12.5% per annum for 4 years.
solution: Given: P = 39000, R = 12.5, Tt = 4 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 39000 * 12.5 * 4 / 100 | Answer: 19500 currency units

question: Find the amount when 33500 is invested at 4.1% per annum compounded annually for 4 years.
solution: Given: P = 33500, R = 4.1, Tt = 4 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 33500 * (1 + 4.1/100)^4 | Answer: 39341 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (8, 6, -1) and (-2, 6, 6).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (-3, -4, 5) and (1, -4, -3).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 36

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (5, -1, 3) and (-6, -6, 0).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 118.6 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number 8 + 6i.
solution: Given: a = 8, b = 6 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((8)^2 + (6)^2) | Answer: 10

question: Evaluate f(x) = -3x^3 - 7x^2 - 3x + 9 at x = 2.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-191 with initial guess x0=11, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.1 and ordinates 18, 20, 7, 15, 11, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 161 and 325.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 161 and 325 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 46 and 30.
solution: Given: a = 46, b = 30 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 46*30 / 2 | Answer: 690
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 31 mm carries an axial tensile load of 9 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 29 mm and length 1800 mm carries an axial load of 71 kN. Take E = 110 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 37 mm transmits a torque of 150 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 37, Tt = 150 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(150*1000) / (pi*(37)^3) | Answer: 15.08 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 28 mm and length 1700 mm carries a torque of 1300 N-m. With G = 80 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (28)^4 / 32 = 60344 mm^4 | theta = (1300*1000)(1700) / (80000 * 60344) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 26.23 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 59 mm wide and 150 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 59, h = 150 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 59*(150)^2 / 6 | Answer: 221250 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (80 mm x 160 mm) carries a bending moment of 27 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (46 mm x 90 mm) has effective length 3900 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 320 MPa is designed for a working stress of 190 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 320, sw = 190 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 320 / 190 | Answer: 1.684

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 500 mm and wall thickness 17 mm carries an internal pressure of 0.8 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 500, t = 17, P = 0.8 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 0.8*500 / (2*17) | Answer: 11.76 MPa

question: 6.4 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 105 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 6.4, dT = 105 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 6.4 * 0.718 * 105 | Answer: 482.5 kJ

question: 1.7 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 40 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1.7, dT = 40 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 1.7 * 1.005 * 40 | Answer: 68.34 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 3.1 m^3 at 410 K with mass 2.9 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 3.1, Tk = 410, m = 2.9 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 2.9*0.287*410 / 3.1 | Answer: 110.1 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 4.5 kg of air expands isothermally at 500 K from volume V1 to 3*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.5, Tk = 500, ratio = 3 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 4.5*0.287*500*ln(3) | Answer: 709.4 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 3.6 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.15 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 3.6, D = 0.15 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*3.6*0.15 / 0.001 | Answer: 540000

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 15.4 m. Taking Cv = 0.97, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 15.4, cv = 0.97 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.97*sqrt(2*9.81*15.4) | Answer: 16.86 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 360 mm) water flows at 1.9 m/s. It contracts to diameter 80 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 360, d2 = 80, V1 = 1.9 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 1.9*(360/80)^2 | Answer: 38.48 m/s

question: Water flows at 3.6 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.18 m and length 170 m. With friction factor f = 0.039, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 22 teeth drives a gear of 84 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1450 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 22, z2 = 84, N1 = 1450 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1450*22 / 84 | Answer: 379.8 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 160 mm rotates at 1150 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 160, N = 1150 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.16)*1150 / 60 | Answer: 9.634 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 28.2 kW at 400 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 28.2, N = 400 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(28.2*1000) / (2*pi*400) | Answer: 673.2 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 4.8 kg rotates at radius 0.44 m at 1100 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 7700 N/m and mass 11.4 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 7700, m = 11.4 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(7700/11.4) | Answer: 4.136 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 3.4 m^2 and thickness 0.2 m has conductivity k = 26 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 110 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 3.4, L = 0.2, k = 26, dT = 110 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 26*3.4*110 / 0.2 | Answer: 48620 W

question: A surface of area 4.9 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 95 W/m^2-K to surroundings 50 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 4.9, h = 95, dT = 50 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 95*4.9*50 | Answer: 23275 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 220 m/min, feed = 0.19 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2.8 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 220, f = 0.19, d = 2.8 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*220*0.19*2.8 | Answer: 117040 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 430 mm is turned at 200 rpm with a feed of 0.33 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 430, N = 200, f = 0.33 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 430 / (0.33*200) | Answer: 6.515 min

question: A resistor of 199 ohm carries a current of 3.1 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 199, I = 3.1 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 3.1 * 199 | Answer: 616.9 V

question: Three resistors 35 ohm, 53 ohm and 92 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 35, R2 = 53, R3 = 92 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 35 + 53 + 92 | Answer: 180 ohm

question: Two resistors 73 ohm and 55 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 73, R2 = 55 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 73*55 / (73+55) | Answer: 31.37 ohm

question: A device draws 7.4 A at 215 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 215, I = 7.4 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 215 * 7.4 | Answer: 1591 W

question: A current of 7.9 A flows through a 117 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 7.9, R = 117 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (7.9)^2 * 117 | Answer: 7302 W

question: Two capacitors 4.5 uF and 15.4 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 4.5, C2 = 15.4 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 4.5*15.4 / (4.5+15.4) | Answer: 3.482 uF

question: A resistor 21 kohm and capacitor 15.5 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 21, C = 15.5 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (21k)(15.5u) = 325.5 ms | Answer: 325.5 ms

question: An inductor 21.9 mH is in series with 45 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 21.9, R = 45 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (21.9e-3) / 45 | Answer: 0.4867 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 58.1 mH inductor at 520 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 58.1, f = 520 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (520)(58.1e-3) | Answer: 189.8 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 10.4 uF capacitor at 990 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 10.4, f = 990 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (990)(10.4e-6)) | Answer: 15.46 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 92 ohm, XL = 89 ohm and XC = 121 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 92, XL = 89, XC = 121 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(92^2 + (89 - 121)^2) | Answer: 97.41 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 51.8 mH and C = 3 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 51.8, C = 3 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(51.8e-3 * 3e-6)) | Answer: 403.7 Hz

question: A capacitor of 50.1 uF is charged to 240 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 50.1, V = 240 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*50.1e-6*(240)^2 | Answer: 1443 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 250 V with 220 primary turns and 120 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 250, N1 = 220, N2 = 120 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 250 * 120/220 | Answer: 136.4 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 180 V and draws an armature current of 38 A. If the armature resistance is 0.18 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 180, Ia = 38, Ra = 0.18 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 180 - 38*0.18 | Answer: 173.2 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 75 A at 415 V (line) with a power factor of 0.85. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 75, VL = 415, pf = 0.85 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*415*75*0.85 / 1000 | Answer: 45.82 kW

question: A load has real power 35 kW and apparent power 55 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 35, S = 55 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 35 / 55 | Answer: 0.6364

question: A machine delivers 115 kW output while drawing 197 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 115, Pi = 197 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 115/197 * 100 | Answer: 58.38 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 13 V across R1 = 38 ohm and R2 = 6 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 13, R1 = 38, R2 = 6 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 13*6 / (38+6) | Answer: 1.773 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 170 kohm and Rin = 31 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 170, Rin = 31 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 170 / 31 | Answer: 5.484

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 100 kohm and Rg = 15 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 100, Rg = 15 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 100/15 | Answer: 7.667

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 127. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 127 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(127) | Answer: 21.04 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 3.9 m carries a central point load of 20 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.9, W = 20 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 20*3.9 / 4 | Answer: 19.5 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.4 m carries a UDL of 30 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6.4, w = 30 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 30*(6.4)^2 / 8 | Answer: 153.6 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 5.3 m carries a point load 60 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.3, W = 60 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 60*5.3 | Answer: 318 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.9 m carries a point load 95 kN at distance 2.1 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 6.9, a = 2.1, W = 95 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 95*(6.9 - 2.1) / 6.9 | Answer: 66.09 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 7.2 m) carries a central point load 45 kN. With E = 25 GPa and I = 330e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=45000 N, L=7200.0 mm, E=25000 MPa, I=330e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 42.41 mm

question: An RC beam has overall depth 420 mm, clear cover 30 mm and main bars of diameter 25 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 420, c = 30, dia = 25 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 420 - 30 - 25/2 | Answer: 377.5 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 16.6 m^2 carrying a factored load of 15.4 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 16.6, w = 15.4 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 15.4 * 16.6 | Answer: 255.6 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 5.2 m, unit weight 20 kN/m^3, phi = 31 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 7e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.3, area = 4.3e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 7, i = 0.3, A = 4.3 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (7e-4)*0.3*(4.3e-3) | Answer: 903 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.4 m, bed slope 0.002 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.027. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 1 m under a head of 0.9 m. Taking Cd = 0.64 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 4.9 m wide carries a discharge of 20 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A tank of volume 590 m^3 treats a flow of 40 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 590, Q = 40 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 590 / 40 | Answer: 14.75 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 270 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.23 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 4 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 270, k = 0.23, t = 4 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 270*(1 - e^(-0.23*4)) | Answer: 162.4 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.65, rainfall intensity 60 mm/h over a catchment of 38.3 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.65, i = 60, A = 38.3 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.65*60*38.3 / 360 | Answer: 4.149 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.01 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 130 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.01, M = 130 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 130*(20+0.01)/20 | Answer: 130.1 m

question: Convert the decimal number 1135 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 1135 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 46F (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 10001100 and 00100000.
solution: XOR: 10101100 | Count of 1s = 4 | Answer: 4
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 770 megabits is sent over a link of 52 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 770, B = 52 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 770 / 52 | Answer: 14.81 s

question: A link has bandwidth 82 Mbps and round-trip time 70 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 82, R = 70 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 82e6 * 70e-3 bits = 5740 kb | Answer: 5740 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.87, cache access time 10 ns and main-memory access time 140 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.87, tc = 10, tm = 140 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.87*10 + (1 - 0.87)*140 | Answer: 26.9 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 881612 elements?
solution: Given: n = 881612 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(881612)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.01, memory access time 110 ns and page-fault service time 6 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 6 ms = 6000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.01)*110 + 0.01*6000000.0 ns | Answer: 60.11 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 0.9 m^3 at 100 kPa and 480 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 0.9, P = 100, Tk = 480 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (100e3)*0.9 / (8.314*480) | Answer: 22.55 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.13 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 7 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.13, t = 7 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.13*7) | Answer: 0.5975

question: For a reaction with A = 5e10 /s and activation energy 70 kJ/mol at 430 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 5, Ea = 70, Tk = 430 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 5e10 * exp(-70e3 / (8.314*430)) | Answer: 156.8 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.96 and bottoms xW = 0.07, with relative volatility alpha = 2.4. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.96, xw = 0.07, al = 2.4 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.96/0.04)(0.93/0.07)] / ln(2.4) | Answer: 6.585 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.55 and x = 0.35. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.55, x = 0.35 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.55/0.45) / (0.35/0.65) | Answer: 2.27

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.3 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 50 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.3, Psat = 50 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.3 * 50 | Answer: 15 kPa

question: A stream of 5.5 kg/s with specific heat 3.8 kJ/kg-K is heated through 80 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 5.5, cp = 3.8, dT = 80 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 5.5*3.8*80 | Answer: 1672 kW

question: A reactor of volume 9.1 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 2.1 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 9.1, Q = 2.1 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 9.1 / 2.1 | Answer: 4.333 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 7.7e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 2 mm with a concentration difference of 20 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 7.7, L = 2, dC = 20 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (7.7e-9)*20 / (2e-3) | Answer: 77 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 4 min and steady-state gain 1.4. For a step input of magnitude 18, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 4, K = 1.4, M = 18 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 1.4 * 18 | Answer: 25.2 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 60 m^2 flies at 250 m/s (air density 1 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.7. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 60, V = 250, rho = 1, CL = 0.7 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1*(250)^2*60*0.7 / 1000 | Answer: 1312 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 60 m^2 flies at 240 m/s (density 0.4 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.11. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 60, V = 240, rho = 0.4, CD = 0.11 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.4*(240)^2*60*0.11 / 1000 | Answer: 76.03 kN

question: A block of mass 24 kg has a volume of 2.3e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 24, V = 2.3 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 24 / (2.3e-3) | Answer: 10435 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 2600 mm is heated through 45 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 23e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 2600, dT = 45, al = 23 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 2600*23e-6*45 | Answer: 2.691 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 60 ohm, R2 = 180 ohm and R3 = 10 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 60, R2 = 180, R3 = 10 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 180*10 / 60 | Answer: 30 ohm

question: A measurement reads 9.66 when the true value is 50. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.66, true = 50 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.66 - 50| / 50 * 100 | Answer: 80.68 %

question: Annual demand is 2000 units, ordering cost 30 per order and holding cost 15 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 2000, S = 30, H = 15 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*2000*30 / 15) | Answer: 89.44 units

question: An asset costs 340000 with salvage value 12000 after 8 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 340000, Sv = 12000, n = 8 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (340000 - 12000) / 8 | Answer: 41000 per year

question: A product sells for 500 per unit with variable cost 10 per unit and fixed costs 85000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 500, V = 10, F = 85000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 85000 / (500 - 10) | Answer: 173.5 units

question: Find the present worth of 40000 received 2 years from now at an interest rate of 7% per year.
solution: Given: F = 40000, n = 2, i = 7 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 40000 / (1 + 0.07)^2 | Answer: 34938 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.9, 0.94 and 0.95 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.9, r2 = 0.94, r3 = 0.95 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.9*0.94*0.95 | Answer: 0.8037

question: A process produces 23 defective items in a batch of 16000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 23, N = 16000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 23/16000 * 1e6 | Answer: 1438 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = 2x^3 - 3x^2 + x - 1 evaluated at x = -5.
For f(x) = x^3 - 4x^2 + 3x + 3, find f''(x) at x = 3.
Evaluate the definite integral of (5x^2 - 4x - 2) dx from x = -1 to x = 6.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = 5x^3/3 + -4x^2/2 + -2x | Evaluate F(6) - F(-1) | Answer: 277.7
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 3x^2 - 12x + 11 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[7, -3], [6, -4]].
solution: Given: a = 7, b = -3, c = 6, d = -4 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (7)(-4) - (-3)(6) | Answer: -10

question: Find the determinant of [[3, -1, 6], [4, 1, -6], [-1, 6, -2]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: 238

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[3, 7], [2, -5]].
solution: Trace tr = -2, Determinant = -29 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 4.477

question: Solve for x: -3x + 0y = 0 and -2x + -3y = -2.
solution: Determinant = -3*-3 - 0*-2 = 9 | x = (e d - b f) / det = 0 | Answer: x = 0
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 42, 5, 55, 30, 26.
solution: Sum = 158 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 31.6 | Answer: 31.6

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 36, 18, 13, 26, 33.
solution: Mean = 25.2 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 9.731

question: Find the slope of the line through (-6, 3) and (-5, 2).
solution: Given: x1 = -6, y1 = 3, x2 = -5, y2 = 2 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (2 - 3) / (-5 - -6) | Answer: -1

question: Find the distance between the points (-1, 7) and (0, -5).
solution: Given: x1 = -1, y1 = 7, x2 = 0, y2 = -5 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((1)^2 + (-12)^2) | Answer: 12.04 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (1,-5), (0,-3), (8,-3).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 8 sq units

question: Find the 8th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -4 and common difference 0.
solution: Given: a = -4, d = 0, n = 8 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -4 + (8 - 1)*0 | Answer: -4

question: Find the sum of the first 10 terms of an AP with first term 3 and common difference -1.
solution: Given: a = 3, d = -1, n = 10 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 10/2 [2*3 + (10-1)*-1] | Answer: -15

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 10000 at 12.9% per annum for 9 years.
solution: Given: P = 10000, R = 12.9, Tt = 9 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 10000 * 12.9 * 9 / 100 | Answer: 11610 currency units

question: Find the amount when 34000 is invested at 9.5% per annum compounded annually for 4 years.
solution: Given: P = 34000, R = 9.5, Tt = 4 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 34000 * (1 + 9.5/100)^4 | Answer: 4888 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (6, 4, -4) and (-1, 6, -2).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (0, 3, 5) and (-3, 0, 4).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 21.21

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (2, 0, 5) and (-5, 5, 5).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 71.24 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -5x^3 - 6x^2 - 7x + 6 at x = -5.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-76 with initial guess x0=5, find x1 (one iteration).
solution: Given: N = 76, x0 = 5 | Formula: x1 = x0 - (x0^2 - N)/(2 x0) | Substitute: x1 = 5 - ((5)^2 - 76)/(2*5) | Answer: 10.1

question: Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.6 and ordinates 8, 4, 0, 18, 14, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 398 and 533.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 398 and 533 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 75 and 63.
solution: Given: a = 75, b = 63 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 75*63 / 3 | Answer: 1575
