formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 54 mm carries an axial tensile load of 86 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 40 mm and length 800 mm carries an axial load of 72 kN. Take E = 70 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 68 mm transmits a torque of 1550 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 68, Tt = 1550 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(1550*1000) / (pi*(68)^3) | Answer: 25.11 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 50 mm and length 800 mm carries a torque of 1400 N-m. With G = 80 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (50)^4 / 32 = 613592 mm^4 | theta = (1400*1000)(800) / (80000 * 613592) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 1.307 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 90 mm wide and 290 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 90, h = 290 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 90*(290)^2 / 6 | Answer: 1261500 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (47 mm x 240 mm) carries a bending moment of 10 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (38 mm x 90 mm) has effective length 1900 mm and E = 200 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 520 MPa is designed for a working stress of 90 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 520, sw = 90 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 520 / 90 | Answer: 5.778

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 300 mm and wall thickness 18 mm carries an internal pressure of 2.9 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 300, t = 18, P = 2.9 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 2.9*300 / (2*18) | Answer: 24.17 MPa

question: 6.9 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 95 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 6.9, dT = 95 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 6.9 * 0.718 * 95 | Answer: 470.6 kJ

question: 3.3 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 185 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.3, dT = 185 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 3.3 * 1.005 * 185 | Answer: 613.6 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 2.9 m^3 at 370 K with mass 5.9 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 2.9, Tk = 370, m = 5.9 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 5.9*0.287*370 / 2.9 | Answer: 216 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 2.9 kg of air expands isothermally at 330 K from volume V1 to 3*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.9, Tk = 330, ratio = 3 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 2.9*0.287*330*ln(3) | Answer: 301.7 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 2 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.4 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 2, D = 0.4 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*2*0.4 / 0.001 | Answer: 800000

question: Water flows at 3.5 m/s through a pipe of diameter 140 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
In a pipe (diameter 170 mm) water flows at 2.9 m/s. It contracts to diameter 100 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
Water flows at 1.3 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.23 m and length 90 m. With friction factor f = 0.033, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 39 teeth drives a gear of 52 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1350 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 39, z2 = 52, N1 = 1350 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1350*39 / 52 | Answer: 1012 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 360 mm rotates at 400 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 360, N = 400 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.36)*400 / 60 | Answer: 7.54 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 8.9 kW at 200 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 8.9, N = 200 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(8.9*1000) / (2*pi*200) | Answer: 424.9 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 4.9 kg rotates at radius 0.59 m at 800 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 7800 N/m and mass 1.2 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 7800, m = 1.2 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(7800/1.2) | Answer: 12.83 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 9.1 m^2 and thickness 0.36 m has conductivity k = 40.5 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 130 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 9.1, L = 0.36, k = 40.5, dT = 130 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 40.5*9.1*130 / 0.36 | Answer: 133088 W

question: A surface of area 3.4 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 100 W/m^2-K to surroundings 25 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 3.4, h = 100, dT = 25 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 100*3.4*25 | Answer: 8500 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 200 m/min, feed = 0.39 mm/rev, depth of cut = 0.8 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 200, f = 0.39, d = 0.8 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*200*0.39*0.8 | Answer: 62400 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 170 mm is turned at 850 rpm with a feed of 0.26 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 170, N = 850, f = 0.26 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 170 / (0.26*850) | Answer: 0.7692 min

question: A resistor of 3 ohm carries a current of 5.8 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 3, I = 5.8 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 5.8 * 3 | Answer: 17.4 V

question: Three resistors 31 ohm, 31 ohm and 81 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 31, R2 = 31, R3 = 81 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 31 + 31 + 81 | Answer: 143 ohm

question: Two resistors 54 ohm and 48 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 54, R2 = 48 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 54*48 / (54+48) | Answer: 25.41 ohm

question: A device draws 7.7 A at 25 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 25, I = 7.7 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 25 * 7.7 | Answer: 192.5 W

question: A current of 5.2 A flows through a 10 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 5.2, R = 10 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (5.2)^2 * 10 | Answer: 270.4 W

question: Two capacitors 24 uF and 15.3 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 24, C2 = 15.3 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 24*15.3 / (24+15.3) | Answer: 9.344 uF

question: A resistor 34 kohm and capacitor 16.4 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 34, C = 16.4 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (34k)(16.4u) = 557.6 ms | Answer: 557.6 ms

question: An inductor 442.7 mH is in series with 186 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 442.7, R = 186 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (442.7e-3) / 186 | Answer: 2.38 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 128.3 mH inductor at 480 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 128.3, f = 480 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (480)(128.3e-3) | Answer: 386.9 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 15.2 uF capacitor at 990 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 15.2, f = 990 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (990)(15.2e-6)) | Answer: 10.58 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 77 ohm, XL = 105 ohm and XC = 128 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 77, XL = 105, XC = 128 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(77^2 + (105 - 128)^2) | Answer: 80.36 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 78 mH and C = 9.2 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 78, C = 9.2 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(78e-3 * 9.2e-6)) | Answer: 187.9 Hz

question: A capacitor of 32.6 uF is charged to 240 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 32.6, V = 240 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*32.6e-6*(240)^2 | Answer: 938.9 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 230 V with 380 primary turns and 350 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 230, N1 = 380, N2 = 350 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 230 * 350/380 | Answer: 211.8 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 380 V and draws an armature current of 11 A. If the armature resistance is 0.26 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 380, Ia = 11, Ra = 0.26 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 380 - 11*0.26 | Answer: 377.1 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 180 A at 433 V (line) with a power factor of 0.98. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 180, VL = 433, pf = 0.98 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*433*180*0.98 / 1000 | Answer: 132.3 kW

question: A machine delivers 60 kW output while drawing 147 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 60, Pi = 147 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 60/147 * 100 | Answer: 40.82 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 25 V across R1 = 16 ohm and R2 = 50 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 25, R1 = 16, R2 = 50 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 25*50 / (16+50) | Answer: 18.94 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 220 kohm and Rin = 39 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 220, Rin = 39 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 220 / 39 | Answer: 5.641

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 180 kohm and Rg = 25 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 180, Rg = 25 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 180/25 | Answer: 8.2

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 1602. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 1602 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(1602) | Answer: 32.05 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.9 m carries a central point load of 95 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 9.9, W = 95 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 95*9.9 / 4 | Answer: 235.1 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.6 m carries a UDL of 50 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 9.6, w = 50 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 50*(9.6)^2 / 8 | Answer: 576 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 3.4 m carries a point load 15 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.4, W = 15 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 15*3.4 | Answer: 51 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 4.4 m carries a UDL of 28 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.4, w = 28 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 28*(4.4)^2 / 2 | Answer: 271 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 9 m carries a point load 25 kN at distance 2 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 9, a = 2, W = 25 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 25*(9 - 2) / 9 | Answer: 19.44 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 7.4 m) carries a central point load 45 kN. With E = 200 GPa and I = 80e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=45000 N, L=7400.0 mm, E=200000 MPa, I=80e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 23.74 mm

question: An RC beam has overall depth 320 mm, clear cover 35 mm and main bars of diameter 16 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 320, c = 35, dia = 16 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 320 - 35 - 16/2 | Answer: 277 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 30.6 m^2 carrying a factored load of 9.2 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 30.6, w = 9.2 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 9.2 * 30.6 | Answer: 281.5 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 4.6 m, unit weight 19 kN/m^3, phi = 29 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 1.2e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1.4, area = 7.8e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 1.2, i = 1.4, A = 7.8 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (1.2e-4)*1.4*(7.8e-3) | Answer: 131 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.1 m, bed slope 0.01 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.016. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 3.8 m under a head of 0.6 m. Taking Cd = 0.62 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 4.8 m wide carries a discharge of 25.3 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A tank of volume 190 m^3 treats a flow of 155 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 190, Q = 155 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 190 / 155 | Answer: 1.226 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 360 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.25 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 3 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 360, k = 0.25, t = 3 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 360*(1 - e^(-0.25*3)) | Answer: 189.9 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.36, rainfall intensity 120 mm/h over a catchment of 58.7 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.36, i = 120, A = 58.7 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.36*120*58.7 / 360 | Answer: 7.044 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.06 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 760 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.06, M = 760 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 760*(30+0.06)/30 | Answer: 761.5 m

question: Convert the decimal number 1084 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 1084 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 43C (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 10111011 and 00010010.
solution: XOR: 10101001 | Count of 1s = 4 | Answer: 4
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 810 megabits is sent over a link of 80 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 810, B = 80 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 810 / 80 | Answer: 10.12 s

question: A link has bandwidth 50 Mbps and round-trip time 30 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 50, R = 30 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 50e6 * 30e-3 bits = 1500 kb | Answer: 1500 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.95, cache access time 4 ns and main-memory access time 110 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.95, tc = 4, tm = 110 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.95*4 + (1 - 0.95)*110 | Answer: 9.3 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 250077 elements?
solution: Given: n = 250077 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(250077)) + 1 | Answer: 18

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.019, memory access time 110 ns and page-fault service time 3 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 3 ms = 3000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.019)*110 + 0.019*3000000.0 ns | Answer: 57.11 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 0.7 m^3 at 240 kPa and 560 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 0.7, P = 240, Tk = 560 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (240e3)*0.7 / (8.314*560) | Answer: 36.08 mol

question: For a reaction with A = 1e10 /s and activation energy 50 kJ/mol at 300 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 1, Ea = 50, Tk = 300 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 1e10 * exp(-50e3 / (8.314*300)) | Answer: 19.67 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.92 and bottoms xW = 0.05, with relative volatility alpha = 2.9. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.92, xw = 0.05, al = 2.9 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.92/0.08)(0.95/0.05)] / ln(2.9) | Answer: 5.059 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.74 and x = 0.3. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.74, x = 0.3 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.74/0.26) / (0.3/0.7) | Answer: 6.641

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.7 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 100 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.7, Psat = 100 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.7 * 100 | Answer: 70 kPa

question: A stream of 4.9 kg/s with specific heat 1.3 kJ/kg-K is heated through 40 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 4.9, cp = 1.3, dT = 40 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 4.9*1.3*40 | Answer: 254.8 kW

question: A reactor of volume 3.5 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 3.6 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 3.5, Q = 3.6 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 3.5 / 3.6 | Answer: 0.9722 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 7.9e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 1 mm with a concentration difference of 40 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 7.9, L = 1, dC = 40 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (7.9e-9)*40 / (1e-3) | Answer: 316 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 9.5 min and steady-state gain 1.6. For a step input of magnitude 11, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 9.5, K = 1.6, M = 11 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 1.6 * 11 | Answer: 17.6 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 105 m^2 flies at 110 m/s (air density 0.7 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 1. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 105, V = 110, rho = 0.7, CL = 1 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.7*(110)^2*105*1 / 1000 | Answer: 444.7 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 55 m^2 flies at 240 m/s (density 1.225 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.09. Find the drag force in kN.
A specimen under stress 340 MPa shows an elastic strain of 1.5e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 340, eps = 1.5 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 340 / (1.5e-3) MPa = 226.7 GPa | Answer: 226.7 GPa

question: A block of mass 21 kg has a volume of 1.5e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 21, V = 1.5 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 21 / (1.5e-3) | Answer: 14000 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 2600 mm is heated through 135 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 11e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 2600, dT = 135, al = 11 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 2600*11e-6*135 | Answer: 3.861 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 105 ohm, R2 = 110 ohm and R3 = 225 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 105, R2 = 110, R3 = 225 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 110*225 / 105 | Answer: 235.7 ohm

question: A measurement reads 10.01 when the true value is 50. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10.01, true = 50 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10.01 - 50| / 50 * 100 | Answer: 79.98 %

question: Annual demand is 6000 units, ordering cost 30 per order and holding cost 29 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 6000, S = 30, H = 29 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*6000*30 / 29) | Answer: 111.4 units

question: An asset costs 200000 with salvage value 36000 after 5 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 200000, Sv = 36000, n = 5 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (200000 - 36000) / 5 | Answer: 32800 per year

question: A product sells for 290 per unit with variable cost 100 per unit and fixed costs 30000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 290, V = 100, F = 30000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 30000 / (290 - 100) | Answer: 157.9 units

question: Find the present worth of 90000 received 9 years from now at an interest rate of 9% per year.
solution: Given: F = 90000, n = 9, i = 9 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 90000 / (1 + 0.09)^9 | Answer: 41439 currency units

question: A process produces 23 defective items in a batch of 8500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 23, N = 8500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 23/8500 * 1e6 | Answer: 2706 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -5x^3 - 2x + 3 evaluated at x = -5.
For f(x) = -x^3 - x^2 + 7x + 3, find f''(x) at x = -3.
Evaluate the definite integral of (-3x^2 - 6x - 7) dx from x = 2 to x = 3.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = -3x^3/3 + -6x^2/2 + -7x | Evaluate F(3) - F(2) | Answer: -41
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 5x^2 - 11x + 1 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[3, 3], [-5, -1]].
solution: Given: a = 3, b = 3, c = -5, d = -1 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (3)(-1) - (3)(-5) | Answer: 12

question: Find the determinant of [[-6, -3, -3], [6, 2, -3], [-5, 2, -6]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: -183

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[-8, -7], [-6, 0]].
solution: Trace tr = -8, Determinant = -42 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 3.616

question: Solve for x: 0x + 5y = -8 and -4x + -5y = -2.
solution: Determinant = 0*-5 - 5*-4 = 20 | x = (e d - b f) / det = 2.5 | Answer: x = 2.5
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 77, 92, 35, 48, 89.
solution: Sum = 341 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 68.2 | Answer: 68.2

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 49, 6, 38, 19, 15.
solution: Mean = 25.4 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 17.62

question: Find the slope of the line through (8, -9) and (-9, 5).
solution: Given: x1 = 8, y1 = -9, x2 = -9, y2 = 5 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (5 - -9) / (-9 - 8) | Answer: -0.8235

question: Find the distance between the points (-4, -4) and (4, 3).
solution: Given: x1 = -4, y1 = -4, x2 = 4, y2 = 3 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((8)^2 + (7)^2) | Answer: 10.63 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (5,-7), (0,-1), (4,3).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 22 sq units

question: Find the 31th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 5 and common difference 7.
solution: Given: a = 5, d = 7, n = 31 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = 5 + (31 - 1)*7 | Answer: 215

question: Find the sum of the first 5 terms of an AP with first term -1 and common difference 5.
solution: Given: a = -1, d = 5, n = 5 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 5/2 [2*-1 + (5-1)*5] | Answer: 45

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 30500 at 11% per annum for 3 years.
solution: Given: P = 30500, R = 11, Tt = 3 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 30500 * 11 * 3 / 100 | Answer: 10065 currency units

question: Find the amount when 35500 is invested at 10.7% per annum compounded annually for 4 years.
solution: Given: P = 35500, R = 10.7, Tt = 4 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 35500 * (1 + 10.7/100)^4 | Answer: 53311 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (6, -7, 2) and (-8, 8, 3).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (-5, 3, -5) and (-1, 6, -4).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 35.75

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (4, -6, -1) and (1, 5, 4).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 129.5 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -3x^3 - 7x^2 + 5x - 2 at x = 2.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-172 with initial guess x0=14, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.8 and ordinates 7, 2, 13, 18, 4, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 56 and 234.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 56 and 234 | Answer: GCD = 2

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 20 and 5.
solution: Given: a = 20, b = 5 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 20*5 / 5 | Answer: 20
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 31 mm carries an axial tensile load of 110 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 13 mm and length 3000 mm carries an axial load of 14 kN. Take E = 110 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 70 mm transmits a torque of 2800 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 70, Tt = 2800 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(2800*1000) / (pi*(70)^3) | Answer: 41.58 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 33 mm and length 800 mm carries a torque of 1600 N-m. With G = 80 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (33)^4 / 32 = 116428 mm^4 | theta = (1600*1000)(800) / (80000 * 116428) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 7.874 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 128 mm wide and 80 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 128, h = 80 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 128*(80)^2 / 6 | Answer: 136533 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (89 mm x 210 mm) carries a bending moment of 32 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (41 mm x 90 mm) has effective length 1700 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 580 MPa is designed for a working stress of 150 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 580, sw = 150 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 580 / 150 | Answer: 3.867

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1100 mm and wall thickness 11 mm carries an internal pressure of 2.4 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1100, t = 11, P = 2.4 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 2.4*1100 / (2*11) | Answer: 120 MPa

question: 6.2 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 120 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 6.2, dT = 120 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 6.2 * 0.718 * 120 | Answer: 534.2 kJ

question: 1.1 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 150 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1.1, dT = 150 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 1.1 * 1.005 * 150 | Answer: 165.8 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 3.2 m^3 at 350 K with mass 1.3 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 3.2, Tk = 350, m = 1.3 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 1.3*0.287*350 / 3.2 | Answer: 40.81 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 2.5 kg of air expands isothermally at 490 K from volume V1 to 3*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.5, Tk = 490, ratio = 3 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 2.5*0.287*490*ln(3) | Answer: 386.2 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 1.5 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.38 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 1.5, D = 0.38 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*1.5*0.38 / 0.001 | Answer: 570000

question: Water flows at 3 m/s through a pipe of diameter 220 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 16.5 m. Taking Cv = 0.98, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 16.5, cv = 0.98 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.98*sqrt(2*9.81*16.5) | Answer: 17.63 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 330 mm) water flows at 0.6 m/s. It contracts to diameter 130 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
Water flows at 1.5 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.12 m and length 180 m. With friction factor f = 0.031, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 29 teeth drives a gear of 62 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1000 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 29, z2 = 62, N1 = 1000 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1000*29 / 62 | Answer: 467.7 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 260 mm rotates at 1500 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 260, N = 1500 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.26)*1500 / 60 | Answer: 20.42 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 26.1 kW at 950 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 26.1, N = 950 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(26.1*1000) / (2*pi*950) | Answer: 262.4 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 4.2 kg rotates at radius 0.12 m at 1200 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 18000 N/m and mass 15.4 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 18000, m = 15.4 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(18000/15.4) | Answer: 5.441 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 2.7 m^2 and thickness 0.22 m has conductivity k = 4.4 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 105 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 2.7, L = 0.22, k = 4.4, dT = 105 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 4.4*2.7*105 / 0.22 | Answer: 5670 W

question: A surface of area 4.9 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 200 W/m^2-K to surroundings 85 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 4.9, h = 200, dT = 85 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 200*4.9*85 | Answer: 83300 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 130 m/min, feed = 0.41 mm/rev, depth of cut = 1.5 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 130, f = 0.41, d = 1.5 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*130*0.41*1.5 | Answer: 79950 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 320 mm is turned at 600 rpm with a feed of 0.12 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 320, N = 600, f = 0.12 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 320 / (0.12*600) | Answer: 4.444 min

question: A resistor of 64 ohm carries a current of 8.1 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 64, I = 8.1 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 8.1 * 64 | Answer: 518.4 V

question: Three resistors 37 ohm, 70 ohm and 33 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 37, R2 = 70, R3 = 33 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 37 + 70 + 33 | Answer: 140 ohm

question: Two resistors 91 ohm and 27 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 91, R2 = 27 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 91*27 / (91+27) | Answer: 20.82 ohm

question: A device draws 4.6 A at 55 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 55, I = 4.6 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 55 * 4.6 | Answer: 253 W

question: A current of 9.7 A flows through a 143 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 9.7, R = 143 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (9.7)^2 * 143 | Answer: 13455 W

question: Two capacitors 46 uF and 34.9 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 46, C2 = 34.9 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 46*34.9 / (46+34.9) | Answer: 19.84 uF

question: A resistor 9 kohm and capacitor 16.4 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 9, C = 16.4 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (9k)(16.4u) = 147.6 ms | Answer: 147.6 ms

question: An inductor 386.9 mH is in series with 133 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 386.9, R = 133 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (386.9e-3) / 133 | Answer: 2.909 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 131.6 mH inductor at 180 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 131.6, f = 180 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (180)(131.6e-3) | Answer: 148.8 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 35.4 uF capacitor at 890 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 35.4, f = 890 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (890)(35.4e-6)) | Answer: 5.052 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 33 ohm, XL = 36 ohm and XC = 107 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 33, XL = 36, XC = 107 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(33^2 + (36 - 107)^2) | Answer: 78.29 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 63.9 mH and C = 5.8 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 63.9, C = 5.8 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(63.9e-3 * 5.8e-6)) | Answer: 261.4 Hz

question: A capacitor of 58.6 uF is charged to 305 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 58.6, V = 305 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*58.6e-6*(305)^2 | Answer: 2726 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 390 V with 890 primary turns and 200 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 390, N1 = 890, N2 = 200 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 390 * 200/890 | Answer: 87.64 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 140 V and draws an armature current of 27 A. If the armature resistance is 1.12 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 140, Ia = 27, Ra = 1.12 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 140 - 27*1.12 | Answer: 109.8 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 70 A at 433 V (line) with a power factor of 0.91. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 70, VL = 433, pf = 0.91 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*433*70*0.91 / 1000 | Answer: 47.77 kW

question: A load has real power 100 kW and apparent power 150 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 100, S = 150 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 100 / 150 | Answer: 0.6667

question: A machine delivers 45 kW output while drawing 152 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 45, Pi = 152 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 45/152 * 100 | Answer: 29.61 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 8 V across R1 = 13 ohm and R2 = 23 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 8, R1 = 13, R2 = 23 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 8*23 / (13+23) | Answer: 5.111 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 220 kohm and Rin = 41 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 220, Rin = 41 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 220 / 41 | Answer: 5.366

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 6167. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 6167 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(6167) | Answer: 37.9 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.2 m carries a central point load of 35 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6.2, W = 35 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 35*6.2 / 4 | Answer: 54.25 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 7.1 m carries a UDL of 55 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7.1, w = 55 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 55*(7.1)^2 / 8 | Answer: 346.6 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 2.6 m carries a point load 55 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 2.6, W = 55 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 55*2.6 | Answer: 143 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 3 m carries a UDL of 12 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3, w = 12 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 12*(3)^2 / 2 | Answer: 54 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.1 m carries a point load 20 kN at distance 3.9 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 4.1, a = 3.9, W = 20 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 20*(4.1 - 3.9) / 4.1 | Answer: 0.9756 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 6.6 m) carries a central point load 75 kN. With E = 25 GPa and I = 280e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=75000 N, L=6600.0 mm, E=25000 MPa, I=280e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 64.17 mm

question: An RC beam has overall depth 450 mm, clear cover 50 mm and main bars of diameter 16 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 450, c = 50, dia = 16 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 450 - 50 - 16/2 | Answer: 392 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 21.4 m^2 carrying a factored load of 9.5 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 21.4, w = 9.5 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 9.5 * 21.4 | Answer: 203.3 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 6.9 m, unit weight 17 kN/m^3, phi = 37 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 5.4e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1.1, area = 1.5e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 5.4, i = 1.1, A = 1.5 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (5.4e-4)*1.1*(1.5e-3) | Answer: 891 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 0.7 m, bed slope 0.008 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.017. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 3.5 m under a head of 0.4 m. Taking Cd = 0.63 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 3.7 m wide carries a discharge of 20.5 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A tank of volume 780 m^3 treats a flow of 150 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 780, Q = 150 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 780 / 150 | Answer: 5.2 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 250 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.14 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 6 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 250, k = 0.14, t = 6 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 250*(1 - e^(-0.14*6)) | Answer: 142.1 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.37, rainfall intensity 80 mm/h over a catchment of 42.3 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.37, i = 80, A = 42.3 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.37*80*42.3 / 360 | Answer: 3.478 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.01 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 760 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.01, M = 760 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 760*(20+0.01)/20 | Answer: 760.4 m

question: Convert the decimal number 3662 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 3662 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: E4E (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 11010100 and 11111010.
solution: XOR: 00101110 | Count of 1s = 4 | Answer: 4
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 410 megabits is sent over a link of 92 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 410, B = 92 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 410 / 92 | Answer: 4.457 s

question: A link has bandwidth 18 Mbps and round-trip time 190 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 18, R = 190 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 18e6 * 190e-3 bits = 3420 kb | Answer: 3420 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.88, cache access time 3 ns and main-memory access time 110 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.88, tc = 3, tm = 110 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.88*3 + (1 - 0.88)*110 | Answer: 15.84 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 788141 elements?
solution: Given: n = 788141 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(788141)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.01, memory access time 200 ns and page-fault service time 10 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 10 ms = 10000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.01)*200 + 0.01*10000000.0 ns | Answer: 100.2 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 0.2 m^3 at 290 kPa and 550 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 0.2, P = 290, Tk = 550 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (290e3)*0.2 / (8.314*550) | Answer: 12.68 mol

question: For a reaction with A = 7e10 /s and activation energy 75 kJ/mol at 470 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 7, Ea = 75, Tk = 470 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 7e10 * exp(-75e3 / (8.314*470)) | Answer: 323.2 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.97 and bottoms xW = 0.04, with relative volatility alpha = 3.3. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.97, xw = 0.04, al = 3.3 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.97/0.03)(0.96/0.04)] / ln(3.3) | Answer: 5.573 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.66 and x = 0.47. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.66, x = 0.47 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.66/0.34) / (0.47/0.53) | Answer: 2.189

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.47 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 45 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.47, Psat = 45 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.47 * 45 | Answer: 21.15 kPa

question: A stream of 7.1 kg/s with specific heat 4.2 kJ/kg-K is heated through 65 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 7.1, cp = 4.2, dT = 65 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 7.1*4.2*65 | Answer: 1938 kW

question: A reactor of volume 2.9 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 3.8 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 2.9, Q = 3.8 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 2.9 / 3.8 | Answer: 0.7632 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 1.1e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 1 mm with a concentration difference of 170 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 1.1, L = 1, dC = 170 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (1.1e-9)*170 / (1e-3) | Answer: 187 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 8 min and steady-state gain 1.5. For a step input of magnitude 2, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 8, K = 1.5, M = 2 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 1.5 * 2 | Answer: 3 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 110 m^2 flies at 220 m/s (air density 0.4 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.5. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 110, V = 220, rho = 0.4, CL = 0.5 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.4*(220)^2*110*0.5 / 1000 | Answer: 532.4 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 95 m^2 flies at 160 m/s (density 0.7 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.02. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 95, V = 160, rho = 0.7, CD = 0.02 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.7*(160)^2*95*0.02 / 1000 | Answer: 17.02 kN

question: A block of mass 40 kg has a volume of 1.1e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 40, V = 1.1 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 40 / (1.1e-3) | Answer: 36364 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 2800 mm is heated through 70 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 12e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 2800, dT = 70, al = 12 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 2800*12e-6*70 | Answer: 2.352 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 125 ohm, R2 = 20 ohm and R3 = 465 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 125, R2 = 20, R3 = 465 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 20*465 / 125 | Answer: 74.4 ohm

question: Annual demand is 43500 units, ordering cost 290 per order and holding cost 15 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 43500, S = 290, H = 15 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*43500*290 / 15) | Answer: 1297 units

question: An asset costs 270000 with salvage value 38000 after 10 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 270000, Sv = 38000, n = 10 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (270000 - 38000) / 10 | Answer: 23200 per year

question: A product sells for 420 per unit with variable cost 130 per unit and fixed costs 45000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 420, V = 130, F = 45000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 45000 / (420 - 130) | Answer: 155.2 units

question: Find the present worth of 155000 received 8 years from now at an interest rate of 10% per year.
solution: Given: F = 155000, n = 8, i = 10 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 155000 / (1 + 0.1)^8 | Answer: 72309 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.96, 0.91 and 0.9 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.96, r2 = 0.91, r3 = 0.9 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.96*0.91*0.9 | Answer: 0.7862

question: A process produces 8 defective items in a batch of 6500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 8, N = 6500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 8/6500 * 1e6 | Answer: 1231 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = 3x^3 - 5x^2 + 4x + 1 evaluated at x = -3.
For f(x) = x^3 - 8x^2 + 3x + 7, find f''(x) at x = 5.
Evaluate the definite integral of (-2x^2 + 2x - 6) dx from x = -1 to x = 3.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = -2x^3/3 + 2x^2/2 + -6x | Evaluate F(3) - F(-1) | Answer: -34.67
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 3x^2 - 10 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[3, -4], [-7, 8]].
solution: Given: a = 3, b = -4, c = -7, d = 8 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (3)(8) - (-4)(-7) | Answer: -4

question: Find the determinant of [[4, -2, -4], [6, 3, -5], [-5, -4, 3]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: -22

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[0, 3], [0, -1]].
solution: Trace tr = -1, Determinant = 0 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 0

question: Solve for x: 2x + 4y = -8 and -5x + -3y = 6.
solution: Determinant = 2*-3 - 4*-5 = 14 | x = (e d - b f) / det = 0 | Answer: x = 0
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 54, 75, 29, 74, 32.
solution: Sum = 264 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 52.8 | Answer: 52.8

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 35, 16, 11, 25, 30.
solution: Mean = 23.4 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 9.864

question: Find the slope of the line through (7, -2) and (5, -1).
solution: Given: x1 = 7, y1 = -2, x2 = 5, y2 = -1 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (-1 - -2) / (5 - 7) | Answer: -0.5

question: Find the distance between the points (2, 1) and (-1, -1).
solution: Given: x1 = 2, y1 = 1, x2 = -1, y2 = -1 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-3)^2 + (-2)^2) | Answer: 3.606 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (7,6), (1,-4), (0,-5).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 2 sq units

question: Find the 10th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 13 and common difference 6.
solution: Given: a = 13, d = 6, n = 10 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = 13 + (10 - 1)*6 | Answer: 67

question: Find the sum of the first 20 terms of an AP with first term 0 and common difference -8.
solution: Given: a = 0, d = -8, n = 20 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 20/2 [2*0 + (20-1)*-8] | Answer: -1520

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 13000 at 14.8% per annum for 3 years.
solution: Given: P = 13000, R = 14.8, Tt = 3 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 13000 * 14.8 * 3 / 100 | Answer: 5772 currency units

question: Find the amount when 18000 is invested at 8.7% per annum compounded annually for 5 years.
solution: Given: P = 18000, R = 8.7, Tt = 5 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 18000 * (1 + 8.7/100)^5 | Answer: 27316 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (-5, -6, 5) and (4, -1, -2).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (-2, 2, 4) and (-5, -6, -5).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 39.75

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (-4, -3, 5) and (3, -5, 4).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 62.61 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number -7 + -10i.
solution: Given: a = -7, b = -10 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((-7)^2 + (-10)^2) | Answer: 12.21

question: Evaluate f(x) = 3x^3 - 6x^2 - 9x - 6 at x = 0.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-91 with initial guess x0=10, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.5 and ordinates 18, 20, 14, 19, 7, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 336 and 569.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 336 and 569 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 63 and 37.
solution: Given: a = 63, b = 37 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 63*37 / 1 | Answer: 2331
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 14 mm carries an axial tensile load of 109 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 23 mm and length 3000 mm carries an axial load of 47 kN. Take E = 70 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 76 mm transmits a torque of 2400 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 76, Tt = 2400 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(2400*1000) / (pi*(76)^3) | Answer: 27.84 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 58 mm and length 700 mm carries a torque of 550 N-m. With G = 77 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (58)^4 / 32 = 1110994 mm^4 | theta = (550*1000)(700) / (77000 * 1110994) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 0.2579 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 67 mm wide and 150 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 67, h = 150 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 67*(150)^2 / 6 | Answer: 251250 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (77 mm x 170 mm) carries a bending moment of 14 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (47 mm x 130 mm) has effective length 2200 mm and E = 200 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 510 MPa is designed for a working stress of 110 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 510, sw = 110 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 510 / 110 | Answer: 4.636

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 750 mm and wall thickness 16 mm carries an internal pressure of 1.9 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 750, t = 16, P = 1.9 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 1.9*750 / (2*16) | Answer: 44.53 MPa

question: 5.4 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 70 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 5.4, dT = 70 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 5.4 * 0.718 * 70 | Answer: 271.4 kJ

question: 3.2 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 160 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.2, dT = 160 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 3.2 * 1.005 * 160 | Answer: 514.6 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 2.5 m^3 at 560 K with mass 5.6 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 2.5, Tk = 560, m = 5.6 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 5.6*0.287*560 / 2.5 | Answer: 360 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 3.8 kg of air expands isothermally at 370 K from volume V1 to 5*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.8, Tk = 370, ratio = 5 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 3.8*0.287*370*ln(5) | Answer: 649.4 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 3.5 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.39 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 3.5, D = 0.39 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*3.5*0.39 / 0.001 | Answer: 1365000

question: Water flows at 3.6 m/s through a pipe of diameter 90 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 3.3 m. Taking Cv = 0.98, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 3.3, cv = 0.98 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.98*sqrt(2*9.81*3.3) | Answer: 7.886 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 230 mm) water flows at 1.2 m/s. It contracts to diameter 80 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 230, d2 = 80, V1 = 1.2 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 1.2*(230/80)^2 | Answer: 9.919 m/s

question: Water flows at 3.8 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.36 m and length 390 m. With friction factor f = 0.04, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 20 teeth drives a gear of 56 teeth. If the pinion runs at 550 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 20, z2 = 56, N1 = 550 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 550*20 / 56 | Answer: 196.4 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 140 mm rotates at 900 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 140, N = 900 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.14)*900 / 60 | Answer: 6.597 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 39 kW at 1150 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 39, N = 1150 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(39*1000) / (2*pi*1150) | Answer: 323.8 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 8.5 kg rotates at radius 0.46 m at 650 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 18900 N/m and mass 16.3 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 18900, m = 16.3 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(18900/16.3) | Answer: 5.419 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 9.4 m^2 and thickness 0.34 m has conductivity k = 11.8 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 60 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 9.4, L = 0.34, k = 11.8, dT = 60 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 11.8*9.4*60 / 0.34 | Answer: 19574 W

question: A surface of area 2.9 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 65 W/m^2-K to surroundings 80 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 2.9, h = 65, dT = 80 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 65*2.9*80 | Answer: 15080 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 230 m/min, feed = 0.46 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2.5 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 230, f = 0.46, d = 2.5 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*230*0.46*2.5 | Answer: 264500 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 450 mm is turned at 1150 rpm with a feed of 0.15 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 450, N = 1150, f = 0.15 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 450 / (0.15*1150) | Answer: 2.609 min

question: A resistor of 162 ohm carries a current of 9.6 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 162, I = 9.6 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 9.6 * 162 | Answer: 1555 V

question: Three resistors 20 ohm, 60 ohm and 15 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 20, R2 = 60, R3 = 15 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 20 + 60 + 15 | Answer: 95 ohm

question: Two resistors 90 ohm and 54 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 90, R2 = 54 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 90*54 / (90+54) | Answer: 33.75 ohm

question: A device draws 12.2 A at 135 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 135, I = 12.2 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 135 * 12.2 | Answer: 1647 W

question: A current of 6.2 A flows through a 83 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 6.2, R = 83 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (6.2)^2 * 83 | Answer: 3191 W

question: Two capacitors 7 uF and 2.4 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 7, C2 = 2.4 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 7*2.4 / (7+2.4) | Answer: 1.787 uF

question: A resistor 52 kohm and capacitor 5 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 52, C = 5 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (52k)(5u) = 260 ms | Answer: 260 ms

question: An inductor 151 mH is in series with 15 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 151, R = 15 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (151e-3) / 15 | Answer: 10.07 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 103.9 mH inductor at 720 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 103.9, f = 720 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (720)(103.9e-3) | Answer: 470 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 14.5 uF capacitor at 550 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 14.5, f = 550 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (550)(14.5e-6)) | Answer: 19.96 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 76 ohm, XL = 130 ohm and XC = 39 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 76, XL = 130, XC = 39 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(76^2 + (130 - 39)^2) | Answer: 118.6 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 13.9 mH and C = 8.1 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 13.9, C = 8.1 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(13.9e-3 * 8.1e-6)) | Answer: 474.3 Hz

question: A capacitor of 60.2 uF is charged to 55 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 60.2, V = 55 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*60.2e-6*(55)^2 | Answer: 91.05 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 380 V with 740 primary turns and 280 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 380, N1 = 740, N2 = 280 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 380 * 280/740 | Answer: 143.8 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 310 V and draws an armature current of 40 A. If the armature resistance is 1.17 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 310, Ia = 40, Ra = 1.17 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 310 - 40*1.17 | Answer: 263.2 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 160 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.87. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 160, VL = 400, pf = 0.87 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*400*160*0.87 / 1000 | Answer: 96.44 kW

question: A machine delivers 10 kW output while drawing 87 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 10, Pi = 87 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 10/87 * 100 | Answer: 11.49 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 5 V across R1 = 22 ohm and R2 = 39 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 5, R1 = 22, R2 = 39 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 5*39 / (22+39) | Answer: 3.197 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 100 kohm and Rin = 46 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 100, Rin = 46 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 100 / 46 | Answer: 2.174

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 100 kohm and Rg = 20 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 100, Rg = 20 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 100/20 | Answer: 6

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 3677. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 3677 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(3677) | Answer: 35.65 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.5 m carries a central point load of 70 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 9.5, W = 70 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 70*9.5 / 4 | Answer: 166.2 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 2.5 m carries a point load 60 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 2.5, W = 60 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 60*2.5 | Answer: 150 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 8.2 m carries a point load 75 kN at distance 1.8 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 8.2, a = 1.8, W = 75 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 75*(8.2 - 1.8) / 8.2 | Answer: 58.54 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 4.9 m) carries a central point load 75 kN. With E = 200 GPa and I = 450e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=75000 N, L=4900.0 mm, E=200000 MPa, I=450e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 2.043 mm

question: An RC beam has overall depth 390 mm, clear cover 35 mm and main bars of diameter 12 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 390, c = 35, dia = 12 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 390 - 35 - 12/2 | Answer: 349 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 18.5 m^2 carrying a factored load of 18.3 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 18.5, w = 18.3 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 18.3 * 18.5 | Answer: 338.6 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 5.7 m, unit weight 18 kN/m^3, phi = 33 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 2e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1.4, area = 6.8e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 2, i = 1.4, A = 6.8 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (2e-4)*1.4*(6.8e-3) | Answer: 1904 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.4 m, bed slope 0.009 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.03. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 2.6 m under a head of 0.9 m. Taking Cd = 0.63 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 2.9 m wide carries a discharge of 9.6 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A tank of volume 430 m^3 treats a flow of 20 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 430, Q = 20 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 430 / 20 | Answer: 21.5 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 300 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.35 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 3 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 300, k = 0.35, t = 3 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 300*(1 - e^(-0.35*3)) | Answer: 195 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.86, rainfall intensity 65 mm/h over a catchment of 15.4 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.86, i = 65, A = 15.4 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.86*65*15.4 / 360 | Answer: 2.391 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.07 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 460 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.07, M = 460 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 460*(20+0.07)/20 | Answer: 461.6 m

question: Convert the decimal number 1769 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 1769 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 6E9 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 10101101 and 01011000.
solution: XOR: 11110101 | Count of 1s = 6 | Answer: 6
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 140 megabits is sent over a link of 4 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 140, B = 4 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 140 / 4 | Answer: 35 s

question: A link has bandwidth 56 Mbps and round-trip time 80 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 56, R = 80 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 56e6 * 80e-3 bits = 4480 kb | Answer: 4480 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.81, cache access time 9 ns and main-memory access time 100 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.81, tc = 9, tm = 100 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.81*9 + (1 - 0.81)*100 | Answer: 26.29 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 100966 elements?
solution: Given: n = 100966 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(100966)) + 1 | Answer: 17

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.006, memory access time 140 ns and page-fault service time 8 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 8 ms = 8000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.006)*140 + 0.006*8000000.0 ns | Answer: 48.14 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 1.3 m^3 at 480 kPa and 540 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 1.3, P = 480, Tk = 540 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (480e3)*1.3 / (8.314*540) | Answer: 139 mol

question: For a reaction with A = 9e10 /s and activation energy 55 kJ/mol at 380 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 9, Ea = 55, Tk = 380 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 9e10 * exp(-55e3 / (8.314*380)) | Answer: 2476 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.95 and bottoms xW = 0.07, with relative volatility alpha = 3.2. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.95, xw = 0.07, al = 3.2 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.95/0.05)(0.93/0.07)] / ln(3.2) | Answer: 4.755 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.77 and x = 0.35. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.77, x = 0.35 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.77/0.23) / (0.35/0.65) | Answer: 6.217

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.43 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 35 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.43, Psat = 35 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.43 * 35 | Answer: 15.05 kPa

question: A stream of 2.8 kg/s with specific heat 1.3 kJ/kg-K is heated through 25 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 2.8, cp = 1.3, dT = 25 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 2.8*1.3*25 | Answer: 91 kW

question: A reactor of volume 18.2 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 3 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 18.2, Q = 3 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 18.2 / 3 | Answer: 6.067 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 4.4e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 2 mm with a concentration difference of 70 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 4.4, L = 2, dC = 70 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (4.4e-9)*70 / (2e-3) | Answer: 154 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 6.2 min and steady-state gain 3.3. For a step input of magnitude 3, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 6.2, K = 3.3, M = 3 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 3.3 * 3 | Answer: 9.9 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 30 m^2 flies at 210 m/s (air density 1 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.5. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 30, V = 210, rho = 1, CL = 0.5 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1*(210)^2*30*0.5 / 1000 | Answer: 330.8 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 45 m^2 flies at 80 m/s (density 1.225 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.09. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 45, V = 80, rho = 1.225, CD = 0.09 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*1.225*(80)^2*45*0.09 / 1000 | Answer: 15.88 kN

question: A specimen under stress 150 MPa shows an elastic strain of 1e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 150, eps = 1 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 150 / (1e-3) MPa = 150 GPa | Answer: 150 GPa

question: A block of mass 13 kg has a volume of 1e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 13, V = 1 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 13 / (1e-3) | Answer: 13000 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 2200 mm is heated through 55 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 12e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 2200, dT = 55, al = 12 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 2200*12e-6*55 | Answer: 1.452 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 20 ohm, R2 = 75 ohm and R3 = 260 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 20, R2 = 75, R3 = 260 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 75*260 / 20 | Answer: 975 ohm

question: A measurement reads 10.1 when the true value is 10. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10.1, true = 10 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10.1 - 10| / 10 * 100 | Answer: 1 %

question: Annual demand is 6500 units, ordering cost 50 per order and holding cost 12 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 6500, S = 50, H = 12 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*6500*50 / 12) | Answer: 232.7 units

question: An asset costs 410000 with salvage value 8000 after 10 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 410000, Sv = 8000, n = 10 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (410000 - 8000) / 10 | Answer: 40200 per year

question: A product sells for 490 per unit with variable cost 30 per unit and fixed costs 105000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 490, V = 30, F = 105000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 105000 / (490 - 30) | Answer: 228.3 units

question: Find the present worth of 10000 received 2 years from now at an interest rate of 11% per year.
solution: Given: F = 10000, n = 2, i = 11 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 10000 / (1 + 0.11)^2 | Answer: 8116 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.91, 0.96 and 0.91 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.91, r2 = 0.96, r3 = 0.91 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.91*0.96*0.91 | Answer: 0.795

question: A process produces 5 defective items in a batch of 10500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 5, N = 10500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 5/10500 * 1e6 | Answer: 476.2 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -2x^3 + 3x^2 + 6x + 4 evaluated at x = 4.
For f(x) = 5x^3 + x^2 + 3x - 3, find f''(x) at x = -4.

question: Find the larger real root of x^2 + 2x = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[3, 0], [-8, -6]].
solution: Given: a = 3, b = 0, c = -8, d = -6 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (3)(-6) - (0)(-8) | Answer: -18

question: Find the slope of the line through (0, 0) and (5, 9).
solution: Given: x1 = 0, y1 = 0, x2 = 5, y2 = 9 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (9 - 0) / (5 - 0) | Answer: 1.8

question: Find the distance between the points (-4, -3) and (2, 3).
solution: Given: x1 = -4, y1 = -3, x2 = 2, y2 = 3 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((6)^2 + (6)^2) | Answer: 8.485 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (5,4), (-8,3), (-1,-1).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 29.5 sq units

question: Find the 14th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -8 and common difference 5.
solution: Given: a = -8, d = 5, n = 14 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -8 + (14 - 1)*5 | Answer: 57

question: Find the sum of the first 31 terms of an AP with first term -11 and common difference 3.
solution: Given: a = -11, d = 3, n = 31 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 31/2 [2*-11 + (31-1)*3] | Answer: 1054

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 46500 at 7.7% per annum for 9 years.
solution: Given: P = 46500, R = 7.7, Tt = 9 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 46500 * 7.7 * 9 / 100 | Answer: 32224 currency units

question: Find the amount when 1000 is invested at 9.8% per annum compounded annually for 4 years.
solution: Given: P = 1000, R = 9.8, Tt = 4 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 1000 * (1 + 9.8/100)^4 | Answer: 1453 currency units

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number 0 + -9i.
solution: Given: a = 0, b = -9 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(-9, 0) | Answer: -90 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -4x^3 - x^2 + 4x + 9 at x = 5.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-121 with initial guess x0=7, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.7 and ordinates 0, 4, 6, 17, 0, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 350 and 541.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 350 and 541 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 10 and 27.
solution: Given: a = 10, b = 27 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 10*27 / 1 | Answer: 270
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 52 mm carries an axial tensile load of 34 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 32 mm and length 2100 mm carries an axial load of 18 kN. Take E = 210 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 65 mm transmits a torque of 1400 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 65, Tt = 1400 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(1400*1000) / (pi*(65)^3) | Answer: 25.96 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 50 mm and length 2000 mm carries a torque of 1750 N-m. With G = 80 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (50)^4 / 32 = 613592 mm^4 | theta = (1750*1000)(2000) / (80000 * 613592) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 4.085 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 108 mm wide and 280 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 108, h = 280 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 108*(280)^2 / 6 | Answer: 1411200 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (53 mm x 130 mm) carries a bending moment of 17 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (33 mm x 110 mm) has effective length 1500 mm and E = 200 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 740 MPa is designed for a working stress of 60 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 740, sw = 60 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 740 / 60 | Answer: 12.33

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1100 mm and wall thickness 18 mm carries an internal pressure of 1.2 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
