solution: Given: d = 1100, t = 18, P = 1.2 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 1.2*1100 / (2*18) | Answer: 36.67 MPa

question: 1.9 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 90 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1.9, dT = 90 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 1.9 * 0.718 * 90 | Answer: 122.8 kJ

question: 2.2 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 100 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.2, dT = 100 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 2.2 * 1.005 * 100 | Answer: 221.1 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 2 m^3 at 600 K with mass 4.6 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 2, Tk = 600, m = 4.6 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 4.6*0.287*600 / 2 | Answer: 396.1 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 2.4 kg of air expands isothermally at 370 K from volume V1 to 3*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.4, Tk = 370, ratio = 3 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 2.4*0.287*370*ln(3) | Answer: 280 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 2.7 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.35 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 2.7, D = 0.35 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*2.7*0.35 / 0.001 | Answer: 945000

question: Water flows at 3.1 m/s through a pipe of diameter 120 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 7.1 m. Taking Cv = 0.97, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 7.1, cv = 0.97 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.97*sqrt(2*9.81*7.1) | Answer: 11.45 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 290 mm) water flows at 2.6 m/s. It contracts to diameter 110 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
Water flows at 3.9 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.32 m and length 360 m. With friction factor f = 0.033, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 18 teeth drives a gear of 83 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1100 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 18, z2 = 83, N1 = 1100 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1100*18 / 83 | Answer: 238.6 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 410 mm rotates at 950 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 410, N = 950 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.41)*950 / 60 | Answer: 20.39 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 19.7 kW at 950 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 19.7, N = 950 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(19.7*1000) / (2*pi*950) | Answer: 198 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 4.7 kg rotates at radius 0.12 m at 500 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 14800 N/m and mass 3 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 14800, m = 3 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(14800/3) | Answer: 11.18 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 2.4 m^2 and thickness 0.2 m has conductivity k = 41.4 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 110 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 2.4, L = 0.2, k = 41.4, dT = 110 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 41.4*2.4*110 / 0.2 | Answer: 54648 W

question: A surface of area 6 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 135 W/m^2-K to surroundings 55 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 6, h = 135, dT = 55 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 135*6*55 | Answer: 44550 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 130 m/min, feed = 0.34 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 130, f = 0.34, d = 2 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*130*0.34*2 | Answer: 88400 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 250 mm is turned at 650 rpm with a feed of 0.28 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 250, N = 650, f = 0.28 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 250 / (0.28*650) | Answer: 1.374 min

question: A resistor of 113 ohm carries a current of 4.1 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 113, I = 4.1 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 4.1 * 113 | Answer: 463.3 V

question: Three resistors 59 ohm, 29 ohm and 16 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 59, R2 = 29, R3 = 16 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 59 + 29 + 16 | Answer: 104 ohm

question: Two resistors 99 ohm and 96 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 99, R2 = 96 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 99*96 / (99+96) | Answer: 48.74 ohm

question: A device draws 4.7 A at 150 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 150, I = 4.7 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 150 * 4.7 | Answer: 705 W

question: A current of 9.6 A flows through a 102 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 9.6, R = 102 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (9.6)^2 * 102 | Answer: 94 W

question: Two capacitors 8.8 uF and 28.4 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 8.8, C2 = 28.4 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 8.8*28.4 / (8.8+28.4) | Answer: 6.718 uF

question: A resistor 27 kohm and capacitor 1.8 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 27, C = 1.8 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (27k)(1.8u) = 48.6 ms | Answer: 48.6 ms

question: An inductor 18.2 mH is in series with 61 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 18.2, R = 61 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (18.2e-3) / 61 | Answer: 0.2984 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 179.6 mH inductor at 480 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 179.6, f = 480 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (480)(179.6e-3) | Answer: 541.7 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 12.8 uF capacitor at 90 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 12.8, f = 90 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (90)(12.8e-6)) | Answer: 138.2 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 53 ohm, XL = 84 ohm and XC = 10 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 53, XL = 84, XC = 10 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(53^2 + (84 - 10)^2) | Answer: 91.02 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 53.8 mH and C = 6.8 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 53.8, C = 6.8 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(53.8e-3 * 6.8e-6)) | Answer: 263.1 Hz

question: A capacitor of 48 uF is charged to 200 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 48, V = 200 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*48e-6*(200)^2 | Answer: 960 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 180 V with 230 primary turns and 440 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 180, N1 = 230, N2 = 440 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 180 * 440/230 | Answer: 344.3 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 370 V and draws an armature current of 41 A. If the armature resistance is 0.84 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 370, Ia = 41, Ra = 0.84 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 370 - 41*0.84 | Answer: 335.6 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 25 A at 415 V (line) with a power factor of 0.93. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 25, VL = 415, pf = 0.93 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*415*25*0.93 / 1000 | Answer: 16.71 kW

question: A load has real power 115 kW and apparent power 220 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 115, S = 220 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 115 / 220 | Answer: 0.5227

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 28 V across R1 = 32 ohm and R2 = 29 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 28, R1 = 32, R2 = 29 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 28*29 / (32+29) | Answer: 13.31 V

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 180 kohm and Rg = 38 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 180, Rg = 38 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 180/38 | Answer: 5.737

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 1586. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 1586 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(1586) | Answer: 32 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 5 m carries a central point load of 65 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5, W = 65 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 65*5 / 4 | Answer: 81.25 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.4 m carries a UDL of 20 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 9.4, w = 20 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 20*(9.4)^2 / 8 | Answer: 220.9 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.1 m carries a point load 100 kN at distance 2.4 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 4.1, a = 2.4, W = 100 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 100*(4.1 - 2.4) / 4.1 | Answer: 41.46 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 6.8 m) carries a central point load 65 kN. With E = 30 GPa and I = 330e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=65000 N, L=6800.0 mm, E=30000 MPa, I=330e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 43.01 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 5.2 m carries a UDL of 21 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.2, w = 21 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 21*(5.2)^2 / 12 | Answer: 47.32 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 670 mm, clear cover 35 mm and main bars of diameter 25 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 670, c = 35, dia = 25 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 670 - 35 - 25/2 | Answer: 622.5 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 36.5 m^2 carrying a factored load of 8.7 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 36.5, w = 8.7 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 8.7 * 36.5 | Answer: 317.5 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 5.2 m, unit weight 20 kN/m^3, phi = 32 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 8.1e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.7, area = 1.4e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 8.1, i = 0.7, A = 1.4 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (8.1e-4)*0.7*(1.4e-3) | Answer: 793.8 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.2 m, bed slope 0.007 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.022. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 2.8 m under a head of 1 m. Taking Cd = 0.62 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 4.2 m wide carries a discharge of 27.9 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A tank of volume 240 m^3 treats a flow of 125 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 240, Q = 125 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 240 / 125 | Answer: 1.92 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 370 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.12 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 4 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 370, k = 0.12, t = 4 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 370*(1 - e^(-0.12*4)) | Answer: 141.1 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.81, rainfall intensity 50 mm/h over a catchment of 7.4 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.81, i = 50, A = 7.4 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.81*50*7.4 / 360 | Answer: 0.8325 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.01 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 110 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.01, M = 110 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 110*(30+0.01)/30 | Answer: 110 m

question: Convert the decimal number 1900 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 1900 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 76C (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 00100100 and 01100001.
solution: XOR: 01000101 | Count of 1s = 3 | Answer: 3
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 890 megabits is sent over a link of 9 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 890, B = 9 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 890 / 9 | Answer: 98.89 s

question: A link has bandwidth 34 Mbps and round-trip time 160 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 34, R = 160 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 34e6 * 160e-3 bits = 5440 kb | Answer: 5440 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.83, cache access time 7 ns and main-memory access time 90 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.83, tc = 7, tm = 90 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.83*7 + (1 - 0.83)*90 | Answer: 21.11 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 336231 elements?
solution: Given: n = 336231 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(336231)) + 1 | Answer: 19

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.015, memory access time 190 ns and page-fault service time 7 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 7 ms = 7000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.015)*190 + 0.015*7000000.0 ns | Answer: 105.2 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 1.5 m^3 at 300 kPa and 440 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 1.5, P = 300, Tk = 440 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (300e3)*1.5 / (8.314*440) | Answer: 123 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.17 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 20 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.17, t = 20 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.17*20) | Answer: 0.9666

question: For a reaction with A = 1e10 /s and activation energy 65 kJ/mol at 430 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 1, Ea = 65, Tk = 430 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 1e10 * exp(-65e3 / (8.314*430)) | Answer: 127 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.9 and bottoms xW = 0.08, with relative volatility alpha = 3.1. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.9, xw = 0.08, al = 3.1 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.9/0.1)(0.92/0.08)] / ln(3.1) | Answer: 4.101 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.78 and x = 0.31. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.78, x = 0.31 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.78/0.22) / (0.31/0.69) | Answer: 7.891

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.85 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 65 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.85, Psat = 65 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.85 * 65 | Answer: 55.25 kPa

question: A stream of 8.2 kg/s with specific heat 3.8 kJ/kg-K is heated through 120 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 8.2, cp = 3.8, dT = 120 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 8.2*3.8*120 | Answer: 3739 kW

question: A reactor of volume 3 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 2.6 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 3, Q = 2.6 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 3 / 2.6 | Answer: 1.154 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 7.8e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 1 mm with a concentration difference of 10 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 7.8, L = 1, dC = 10 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (7.8e-9)*10 / (1e-3) | Answer: 78 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 7.5 min and steady-state gain 1. For a step input of magnitude 3, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 7.5, K = 1, M = 3 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 1 * 3 | Answer: 3 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 110 m^2 flies at 90 m/s (air density 0.4 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.9. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 110, V = 90, rho = 0.4, CL = 0.9 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.4*(90)^2*110*0.9 / 1000 | Answer: 160.4 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 40 m^2 flies at 240 m/s (density 1.225 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.08. Find the drag force in kN.
A specimen under stress 90 MPa shows an elastic strain of 1.3e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 90, eps = 1.3 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 90 / (1.3e-3) MPa = 69.23 GPa | Answer: 69.23 GPa

question: A block of mass 7 kg has a volume of 5.6e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 7, V = 5.6 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 7 / (5.6e-3) | Answer: 1250 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 1400 mm is heated through 75 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 23e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 1400, dT = 75, al = 23 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 1400*23e-6*75 | Answer: 2.415 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 55 ohm, R2 = 125 ohm and R3 = 295 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 55, R2 = 125, R3 = 295 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 125*295 / 55 | Answer: 670.5 ohm

question: Annual demand is 27500 units, ordering cost 200 per order and holding cost 25 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 27500, S = 200, H = 25 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*27500*200 / 25) | Answer: 663.3 units

question: An asset costs 240000 with salvage value 2000 after 13 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 240000, Sv = 2000, n = 13 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (240000 - 2000) / 13 | Answer: 18308 per year

question: A product sells for 220 per unit with variable cost 180 per unit and fixed costs 135000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 220, V = 180, F = 135000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 135000 / (220 - 180) | Answer: 3375 units

question: Find the present worth of 55000 received 4 years from now at an interest rate of 12% per year.
solution: Given: F = 55000, n = 4, i = 12 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 55000 / (1 + 0.12)^4 | Answer: 34953 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.97, 0.9 and 0.92 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.97, r2 = 0.9, r3 = 0.92 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.97*0.9*0.92 | Answer: 0.8032

question: A process produces 5 defective items in a batch of 20000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 5, N = 20000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 5/20000 * 1e6 | Answer: 250 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = 6x^3 - 3x^2 + 4x - 1 evaluated at x = 3.
For f(x) = 4x^3 + 4x^2 + 9x + 9, find f''(x) at x = -5.
Evaluate the definite integral of (6x - 3) dx from x = -3 to x = 5.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = 0x^3/3 + 6x^2/2 + -3x | Evaluate F(5) - F(-3) | Answer: 24
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of x^2 + 9x - 8 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[-4, 2], [0, -8]].
solution: Given: a = -4, b = 2, c = 0, d = -8 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (-4)(-8) - (2)(0) | Answer: 32

question: Find the determinant of [[-3, -6, 3], [-5, 1, 5], [-5, 5, -3]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: 264

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[2, -3], [-8, 8]].
solution: Trace tr = 10, Determinant = -8 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 10.74

question: Solve for x: -5x + -4y = 11 and 5x + 0y = -12.
solution: Determinant = -5*0 - -4*5 = 20 | x = (e d - b f) / det = -2.4 | Answer: x = -2.4
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 21, 34, 80, 88, 15.
solution: Sum = 238 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 47.6 | Answer: 47.6

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 50, 30, 40, 45, 49.
solution: Mean = 42.8 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 8.167

question: Find the slope of the line through (2, -9) and (1, 6).
solution: Given: x1 = 2, y1 = -9, x2 = 1, y2 = 6 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (6 - -9) / (1 - 2) | Answer: -15

question: Find the distance between the points (-2, 2) and (4, 8).
solution: Given: x1 = -2, y1 = 2, x2 = 4, y2 = 8 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((6)^2 + (6)^2) | Answer: 8.485 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (-6,-3), (6,4), (6,6).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 12 sq units

question: Find the 32th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -13 and common difference -9.
solution: Given: a = -13, d = -9, n = 32 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -13 + (32 - 1)*-9 | Answer: -292

question: Find the sum of the first 36 terms of an AP with first term -6 and common difference -1.
solution: Given: a = -6, d = -1, n = 36 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 36/2 [2*-6 + (36-1)*-1] | Answer: -846

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 16000 at 11.1% per annum for 7 years.
solution: Given: P = 16000, R = 11.1, Tt = 7 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 16000 * 11.1 * 7 / 100 | Answer: 12432 currency units

question: Find the amount when 13000 is invested at 5.9% per annum compounded annually for 6 years.
solution: Given: P = 13000, R = 5.9, Tt = 6 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 13000 * (1 + 5.9/100)^6 | Answer: 18337 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (8, -5, 3) and (-7, 4, -3).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (2, -1, -1) and (5, -6, 2).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 13.93

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (5, 5, -1) and (4, -3, -3).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 78.92 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = 3x^3 - 5x + 7 at x = -1.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-176 with initial guess x0=5, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.7 and ordinates 8, 2, 12, 2, 8, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 407 and 549.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 407 and 549 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 61 and 76.
solution: Given: a = 61, b = 76 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 61*76 / 1 | Answer: 4636
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 20 mm carries an axial tensile load of 69 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 35 mm and length 1400 mm carries an axial load of 73 kN. Take E = 210 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 75 mm transmits a torque of 2600 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 75, Tt = 2600 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(2600*1000) / (pi*(75)^3) | Answer: 31.39 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 27 mm and length 1500 mm carries a torque of 1150 N-m. With G = 77 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (27)^4 / 32 = 52174 mm^4 | theta = (1150*1000)(1500) / (77000 * 52174) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 24.6 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 150 mm wide and 140 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 150, h = 140 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 150*(140)^2 / 6 | Answer: 490000 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (71 mm x 110 mm) carries a bending moment of 36 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (32 mm x 100 mm) has effective length 3600 mm and E = 200 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 330 MPa is designed for a working stress of 160 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 330, sw = 160 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 330 / 160 | Answer: 2.062

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 800 mm and wall thickness 19 mm carries an internal pressure of 1.6 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 800, t = 19, P = 1.6 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 1.6*800 / (2*19) | Answer: 33.68 MPa

question: 1.8 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 110 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1.8, dT = 110 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 1.8 * 0.718 * 110 | Answer: 142.2 kJ

question: 4.2 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 175 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.2, dT = 175 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 4.2 * 1.005 * 175 | Answer: 738.7 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 2.2 m^3 at 440 K with mass 3.3 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 2.2, Tk = 440, m = 3.3 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 3.3*0.287*440 / 2.2 | Answer: 189.4 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 1.9 kg of air expands isothermally at 470 K from volume V1 to 5*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1.9, Tk = 470, ratio = 5 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 1.9*0.287*470*ln(5) | Answer: 412.5 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 1.2 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.09 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 1.2, D = 0.09 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*1.2*0.09 / 0.001 | Answer: 108000

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 9 m. Taking Cv = 0.95, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 9, cv = 0.95 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.95*sqrt(2*9.81*9) | Answer: 12.62 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 260 mm) water flows at 0.7 m/s. It contracts to diameter 90 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 260, d2 = 90, V1 = 0.7 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 0.7*(260/90)^2 | Answer: 5.842 m/s

question: Water flows at 2.1 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.29 m and length 100 m. With friction factor f = 0.032, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 24 teeth drives a gear of 100 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1450 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 24, z2 = 100, N1 = 1450 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1450*24 / 100 | Answer: 348 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 410 mm rotates at 1450 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 410, N = 1450 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.41)*1450 / 60 | Answer: 31.13 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 15.6 kW at 1300 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 15.6, N = 1300 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(15.6*1000) / (2*pi*1300) | Answer: 114.6 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 9.8 kg rotates at radius 0.16 m at 550 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 2100 N/m and mass 18.2 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 2100, m = 18.2 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(2100/18.2) | Answer: 1.71 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 5.3 m^2 and thickness 0.11 m has conductivity k = 8.8 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 115 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 5.3, L = 0.11, k = 8.8, dT = 115 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 8.8*5.3*115 / 0.11 | Answer: 48760 W

question: A surface of area 4.6 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 125 W/m^2-K to surroundings 120 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 4.6, h = 125, dT = 120 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 125*4.6*120 | Answer: 69000 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 160 m/min, feed = 0.45 mm/rev, depth of cut = 0.8 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 160, f = 0.45, d = 0.8 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*160*0.45*0.8 | Answer: 57600 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 190 mm is turned at 800 rpm with a feed of 0.31 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 190, N = 800, f = 0.31 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 190 / (0.31*800) | Answer: 0.7661 min

question: A resistor of 90 ohm carries a current of 2.1 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 90, I = 2.1 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 2.1 * 90 | Answer: 189 V

question: Three resistors 14 ohm, 28 ohm and 83 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 14, R2 = 28, R3 = 83 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 14 + 28 + 83 | Answer: 125 ohm

question: Two resistors 50 ohm and 58 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 50, R2 = 58 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 50*58 / (50+58) | Answer: 26.85 ohm

question: A device draws 11.1 A at 230 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 230, I = 11.1 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 230 * 11.1 | Answer: 2553 W

question: A current of 1.2 A flows through a 15 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 1.2, R = 15 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (1.2)^2 * 15 | Answer: 21.6 W

question: Two capacitors 10.7 uF and 7.4 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 10.7, C2 = 7.4 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 10.7*7.4 / (10.7+7.4) | Answer: 4.375 uF

question: A resistor 26 kohm and capacitor 16.2 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 26, C = 16.2 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (26k)(16.2u) = 421.2 ms | Answer: 421.2 ms

question: An inductor 80.7 mH is in series with 144 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 80.7, R = 144 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (80.7e-3) / 144 | Answer: 0.5604 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 195 mH inductor at 340 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 195, f = 340 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (340)(195e-3) | Answer: 416.6 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 41.1 uF capacitor at 280 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 41.1, f = 280 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (280)(41.1e-6)) | Answer: 13.83 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 94 ohm, XL = 12 ohm and XC = 31 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 94, XL = 12, XC = 31 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(94^2 + (12 - 31)^2) | Answer: 95.9 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 36.6 mH and C = 6.2 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 36.6, C = 6.2 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(36.6e-3 * 6.2e-6)) | Answer: 334.1 Hz

question: A capacitor of 18.3 uF is charged to 85 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 18.3, V = 85 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*18.3e-6*(85)^2 | Answer: 66.11 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 390 V with 390 primary turns and 140 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 390, N1 = 390, N2 = 140 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 390 * 140/390 | Answer: 140 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 270 V and draws an armature current of 39 A. If the armature resistance is 0.14 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 270, Ia = 39, Ra = 0.14 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 270 - 39*0.14 | Answer: 264.5 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 95 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.79. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 95, VL = 400, pf = 0.79 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*400*95*0.79 / 1000 | Answer: 52 kW

question: A load has real power 125 kW and apparent power 200 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 125, S = 200 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 125 / 200 | Answer: 0.625

question: A machine delivers 15 kW output while drawing 162 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 15, Pi = 162 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 15/162 * 100 | Answer: 9.259 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 14 V across R1 = 5 ohm and R2 = 39 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 14, R1 = 5, R2 = 39 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 14*39 / (5+39) | Answer: 12.41 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 80 kohm and Rin = 5 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 80, Rin = 5 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 80 / 5 | Answer: 16

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 10 kohm and Rg = 6 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 10, Rg = 6 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 10/6 | Answer: 2.667

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 5979. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 5979 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(5979) | Answer: 37.77 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.3 m carries a central point load of 115 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 9.3, W = 115 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 115*9.3 / 4 | Answer: 267.4 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 3.6 m carries a point load 80 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.6, W = 80 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 80*3.6 | Answer: 288 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 3.2 m carries a UDL of 36 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.2, w = 36 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 36*(3.2)^2 / 2 | Answer: 184.3 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 8.3 m carries a point load 70 kN at distance 1.8 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 8.3, a = 1.8, W = 70 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 70*(8.3 - 1.8) / 8.3 | Answer: 54.82 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 7.6 m) carries a central point load 30 kN. With E = 30 GPa and I = 300e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=30000 N, L=7600.0 mm, E=30000 MPa, I=300e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 30.48 mm

question: An RC beam has overall depth 640 mm, clear cover 30 mm and main bars of diameter 20 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 640, c = 30, dia = 20 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 640 - 30 - 20/2 | Answer: 600 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 26.7 m^2 carrying a factored load of 17.3 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 26.7, w = 17.3 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 17.3 * 26.7 | Answer: 461.9 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 4.9 m, unit weight 17 kN/m^3, phi = 33 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 4.7e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.7, area = 7.7e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 4.7, i = 0.7, A = 7.7 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (4.7e-4)*0.7*(7.7e-3) | Answer: 2533 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.5 m, bed slope 0.004 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.018. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 3 m under a head of 0.8 m. Taking Cd = 0.61 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 4 m wide carries a discharge of 5.4 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A tank of volume 610 m^3 treats a flow of 170 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 610, Q = 170 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 610 / 170 | Answer: 3.588 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 390 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.27 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 8 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 390, k = 0.27, t = 8 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 390*(1 - e^(-0.27*8)) | Answer: 345 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.82, rainfall intensity 110 mm/h over a catchment of 46.5 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.82, i = 110, A = 46.5 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.82*110*46.5 / 360 | Answer: 11.65 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: Convert the decimal number 2640 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 2640 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: A50 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 00001010 and 01110101.
solution: XOR: 01111111 | Count of 1s = 7 | Answer: 7
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 80 megabits is sent over a link of 19 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 80, B = 19 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 80 / 19 | Answer: 4.211 s

question: A link has bandwidth 93 Mbps and round-trip time 170 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 93, R = 170 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 93e6 * 170e-3 bits = 15810 kb | Answer: 15810 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.93, cache access time 10 ns and main-memory access time 160 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.93, tc = 10, tm = 160 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.93*10 + (1 - 0.93)*160 | Answer: 20.5 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 708241 elements?
solution: Given: n = 708241 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(708241)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.01, memory access time 200 ns and page-fault service time 3 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 3 ms = 3000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.01)*200 + 0.01*3000000.0 ns | Answer: 30.2 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 2.5 m^3 at 240 kPa and 400 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 2.5, P = 240, Tk = 400 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (240e3)*2.5 / (8.314*400) | Answer: 180.4 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.07 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 7 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.07, t = 7 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.07*7) | Answer: 0.3874

question: For a reaction with A = 1e10 /s and activation energy 65 kJ/mol at 480 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 1, Ea = 65, Tk = 480 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 1e10 * exp(-65e3 / (8.314*480)) | Answer: 843.9 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.93 and bottoms xW = 0.03, with relative volatility alpha = 2.8. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.93, xw = 0.03, al = 2.8 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.93/0.07)(0.97/0.03)] / ln(2.8) | Answer: 5.888 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.73 and x = 0.34. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.73, x = 0.34 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.73/0.27) / (0.34/0.66) | Answer: 5.248

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.87 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 100 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.87, Psat = 100 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.87 * 100 | Answer: 87 kPa

question: A stream of 2.3 kg/s with specific heat 3 kJ/kg-K is heated through 85 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 2.3, cp = 3, dT = 85 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 2.3*3*85 | Answer: 586.5 kW

question: A reactor of volume 14 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 4.2 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 14, Q = 4.2 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 14 / 4.2 | Answer: 3.333 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 8.6e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 1 mm with a concentration difference of 110 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 8.6, L = 1, dC = 110 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (8.6e-9)*110 / (1e-3) | Answer: 946 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 2.6 min and steady-state gain 0.6. For a step input of magnitude 6, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 2.6, K = 0.6, M = 6 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 0.6 * 6 | Answer: 3.6 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 120 m^2 flies at 160 m/s (air density 0.7 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 1. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 120, V = 160, rho = 0.7, CL = 1 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.7*(160)^2*120*1 / 1000 | Answer: 1075 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 15 m^2 flies at 140 m/s (density 1.225 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.07. Find the drag force in kN.
A specimen under stress 150 MPa shows an elastic strain of 2.6e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 150, eps = 2.6 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 150 / (2.6e-3) MPa = 57.69 GPa | Answer: 57.69 GPa

question: A block of mass 29 kg has a volume of 3.2e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 29, V = 3.2 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 29 / (3.2e-3) | Answer: 9062 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 2600 mm is heated through 20 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 11e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 2600, dT = 20, al = 11 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 2600*11e-6*20 | Answer: 0.572 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 50 ohm, R2 = 200 ohm and R3 = 395 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 50, R2 = 200, R3 = 395 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 200*395 / 50 | Answer: 1580 ohm

question: A measurement reads 9.46 when the true value is 10. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.46, true = 10 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.46 - 10| / 10 * 100 | Answer: 5.4 %

question: Annual demand is 16500 units, ordering cost 230 per order and holding cost 9 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 16500, S = 230, H = 9 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*16500*230 / 9) | Answer: 918.3 units

question: An asset costs 250000 with salvage value 10000 after 7 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 250000, Sv = 10000, n = 7 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (250000 - 10000) / 7 | Answer: 34286 per year

question: A product sells for 310 per unit with variable cost 60 per unit and fixed costs 80000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 310, V = 60, F = 80000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 80000 / (310 - 60) | Answer: 320 units

question: Find the present worth of 105000 received 9 years from now at an interest rate of 8% per year.
solution: Given: F = 105000, n = 9, i = 8 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 105000 / (1 + 0.08)^9 | Answer: 52526 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.99, 0.99 and 0.93 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.99, r2 = 0.99, r3 = 0.93 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.99*0.99*0.93 | Answer: 0.9115

question: A process produces 45 defective items in a batch of 10000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 45, N = 10000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 45/10000 * 1e6 | Answer: 4500 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = 4x^3 + 5x^2 + 4x - 5 evaluated at x = 0.
For f(x) = -x^3 + 5x^2 - 9x - 8, find f''(x) at x = -5.
Evaluate the definite integral of (2x^2 + 3x - 1) dx from x = 2 to x = 5.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = 2x^3/3 + 3x^2/2 + -1x | Evaluate F(5) - F(2) | Answer: 106.5
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of x^2 - 4x - 8 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[0, 6], [2, -2]].
solution: Given: a = 0, b = 6, c = 2, d = -2 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (0)(-2) - (6)(2) | Answer: -12

question: Find the determinant of [[3, 4, 1], [-1, 5, -4], [1, 4, 5]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: 118

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[1, -3], [5, -8]].
solution: Trace tr = -7, Determinant = 7 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: -1.209

question: Solve for x: -2x + 0y = -1 and -1x + -6y = -7.
solution: Determinant = -2*-6 - 0*-1 = 12 | x = (e d - b f) / det = 0.5 | Answer: x = 0.5
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 72, 62, 29, 2, 40.
solution: Sum = 205 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 41 | Answer: 41

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 14, 31, 19, 25, 4.
solution: Mean = 18.6 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 10.36

question: Find the slope of the line through (-3, 2) and (7, -1).
solution: Given: x1 = -3, y1 = 2, x2 = 7, y2 = -1 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (-1 - 2) / (7 - -3) | Answer: -0.3

question: Find the distance between the points (-6, -8) and (-2, -8).
solution: Given: x1 = -6, y1 = -8, x2 = -2, y2 = -8 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((4)^2 + (0)^2) | Answer: 4 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (7,-5), (-4,4), (-2,-8).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 57 sq units

question: Find the 10th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -17 and common difference -4.
solution: Given: a = -17, d = -4, n = 10 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -17 + (10 - 1)*-4 | Answer: -53

question: Find the sum of the first 19 terms of an AP with first term 13 and common difference -2.
solution: Given: a = 13, d = -2, n = 19 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 19/2 [2*13 + (19-1)*-2] | Answer: -95

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 17500 at 6.5% per annum for 7 years.
solution: Given: P = 17500, R = 6.5, Tt = 7 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 17500 * 6.5 * 7 / 100 | Answer: 7962 currency units

question: Find the amount when 30000 is invested at 9.6% per annum compounded annually for 4 years.
solution: Given: P = 30000, R = 9.6, Tt = 4 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 30000 * (1 + 9.6/100)^4 | Answer: 43288 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (1, -1, 2) and (1, 0, 1).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (-6, -6, -3) and (6, 6, -2).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 42.43

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (-6, 5, -2) and (-4, -6, 5).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 103.1 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -4x^3 - 6x^2 + x - 3 at x = -5.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-144 with initial guess x0=15, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.6 and ordinates 5, 13, 14, 7, 3, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 156 and 570.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 156 and 570 | Answer: GCD = 6

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 76 and 62.
solution: Given: a = 76, b = 62 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 76*62 / 2 | Answer: 2356
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 45 mm carries an axial tensile load of 106 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 16 mm and length 2300 mm carries an axial load of 55 kN. Take E = 110 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 51 mm transmits a torque of 1900 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 51, Tt = 1900 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(1900*1000) / (pi*(51)^3) | Answer: 72.95 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 37 mm and length 1900 mm carries a torque of 1300 N-m. With G = 45 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (37)^4 / 32 = 183995 mm^4 | theta = (1300*1000)(1900) / (45000 * 183995) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 17.09 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 61 mm wide and 200 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 61, h = 200 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 61*(200)^2 / 6 | Answer: 406667 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (86 mm x 120 mm) carries a bending moment of 24 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (34 mm x 130 mm) has effective length 4000 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 340 MPa is designed for a working stress of 80 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 340, sw = 80 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 340 / 80 | Answer: 4.25

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1100 mm and wall thickness 15 mm carries an internal pressure of 2.2 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1100, t = 15, P = 2.2 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 2.2*1100 / (2*15) | Answer: 80.67 MPa

question: 4.5 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 190 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.5, dT = 190 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 4.5 * 0.718 * 190 | Answer: 613.9 kJ

question: 4.1 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 100 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.1, dT = 100 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 4.1 * 1.005 * 100 | Answer: 412 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 3.6 m^3 at 500 K with mass 1.4 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 3.6, Tk = 500, m = 1.4 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 1.4*0.287*500 / 3.6 | Answer: 55.81 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 4.8 kg of air expands isothermally at 360 K from volume V1 to 4*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.8, Tk = 360, ratio = 4 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 4.8*0.287*360*ln(4) | Answer: 687.5 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 3.3 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.17 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 3.3, D = 0.17 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*3.3*0.17 / 0.001 | Answer: 561000

question: Water flows at 0.6 m/s through a pipe of diameter 300 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
In a pipe (diameter 320 mm) water flows at 0.8 m/s. It contracts to diameter 140 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 320, d2 = 140, V1 = 0.8 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 0.8*(320/140)^2 | Answer: 4.18 m/s

question: Water flows at 3.4 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.12 m and length 380 m. With friction factor f = 0.025, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 18 teeth drives a gear of 62 teeth. If the pinion runs at 450 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 18, z2 = 62, N1 = 450 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 450*18 / 62 | Answer: 130.6 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 260 mm rotates at 400 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 260, N = 400 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.26)*400 / 60 | Answer: 5.445 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 2.3 kW at 1400 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 2.3, N = 1400 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(2.3*1000) / (2*pi*1400) | Answer: 15.69 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 8.1 kg rotates at radius 0.18 m at 1000 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 8700 N/m and mass 10.1 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 8700, m = 10.1 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(8700/10.1) | Answer: 4.671 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 6 m^2 and thickness 0.29 m has conductivity k = 2.8 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 125 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 6, L = 0.29, k = 2.8, dT = 125 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 2.8*6*125 / 0.29 | Answer: 7241 W

question: A surface of area 4.6 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 80 W/m^2-K to surroundings 100 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 4.6, h = 80, dT = 100 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 80*4.6*100 | Answer: 36800 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 60 m/min, feed = 0.11 mm/rev, depth of cut = 0.6 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 60, f = 0.11, d = 0.6 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*60*0.11*0.6 | Answer: 3960 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 220 mm is turned at 600 rpm with a feed of 0.4 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 220, N = 600, f = 0.4 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 220 / (0.4*600) | Answer: 0.9167 min

question: A resistor of 137 ohm carries a current of 7.7 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 137, I = 7.7 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 7.7 * 137 | Answer: 1055 V

question: Three resistors 6 ohm, 53 ohm and 51 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 6, R2 = 53, R3 = 51 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 6 + 53 + 51 | Answer: 110 ohm

question: Two resistors 101 ohm and 58 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 101, R2 = 58 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 101*58 / (101+58) | Answer: 36.84 ohm

question: A device draws 14.4 A at 235 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 235, I = 14.4 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 235 * 14.4 | Answer: 3384 W

question: A current of 5.3 A flows through a 147 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 5.3, R = 147 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (5.3)^2 * 147 | Answer: 4129 W

question: Two capacitors 12.7 uF and 28.2 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 12.7, C2 = 28.2 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 12.7*28.2 / (12.7+28.2) | Answer: 8.756 uF

question: A resistor 61 kohm and capacitor 19.3 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 61, C = 19.3 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (61k)(19.3u) = 1177 ms | Answer: 1177 ms

question: An inductor 75 mH is in series with 107 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 75, R = 107 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (75e-3) / 107 | Answer: 0.7009 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 22.8 mH inductor at 180 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 22.8, f = 180 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (180)(22.8e-3) | Answer: 25.79 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 12.2 uF capacitor at 1000 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 12.2, f = 1000 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (1000)(12.2e-6)) | Answer: 13.05 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 21 ohm, XL = 17 ohm and XC = 67 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 21, XL = 17, XC = 67 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(21^2 + (17 - 67)^2) | Answer: 54.23 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 47.3 mH and C = 3.4 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 47.3, C = 3.4 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(47.3e-3 * 3.4e-6)) | Answer: 396.9 Hz

question: A capacitor of 37.2 uF is charged to 350 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 37.2, V = 350 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*37.2e-6*(350)^2 | Answer: 2278 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 330 V with 390 primary turns and 250 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 330, N1 = 390, N2 = 250 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 330 * 250/390 | Answer: 211.5 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 140 V and draws an armature current of 38 A. If the armature resistance is 0.33 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 140, Ia = 38, Ra = 0.33 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 140 - 38*0.33 | Answer: 127.5 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 40 A at 415 V (line) with a power factor of 0.74. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 40, VL = 415, pf = 0.74 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*415*40*0.74 / 1000 | Answer: 21.28 kW

question: A load has real power 165 kW and apparent power 200 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 165, S = 200 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 165 / 200 | Answer: 0.825

question: A machine delivers 135 kW output while drawing 207 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 135, Pi = 207 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 135/207 * 100 | Answer: 65.22 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 19 V across R1 = 40 ohm and R2 = 7 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 19, R1 = 40, R2 = 7 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 19*7 / (40+7) | Answer: 2.83 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 100 kohm and Rin = 10 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 100, Rin = 10 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 100 / 10 | Answer: 10

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 130 kohm and Rg = 43 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 130, Rg = 43 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 130/43 | Answer: 4.023

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 1651. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 1651 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(1651) | Answer: 32.18 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 5.2 m carries a central point load of 90 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.2, W = 90 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 90*5.2 / 4 | Answer: 117 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 4 m carries a UDL of 10 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4, w = 10 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 10*(4)^2 / 8 | Answer: 20 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 5.5 m carries a point load 65 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.5, W = 65 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 65*5.5 | Answer: 357.5 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 1.2 m carries a UDL of 4 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 1.2, w = 4 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 4*(1.2)^2 / 2 | Answer: 2.88 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 7.8 m carries a point load 35 kN at distance 2.2 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 7.8, a = 2.2, W = 35 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 35*(7.8 - 2.2) / 7.8 | Answer: 25.13 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 7.5 m) carries a central point load 10 kN. With E = 25 GPa and I = 480e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=10000 N, L=7500.0 mm, E=25000 MPa, I=480e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 7.324 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 6.8 m carries a UDL of 30 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6.8, w = 30 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 30*(6.8)^2 / 12 | Answer: 115.6 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 390 mm, clear cover 45 mm and main bars of diameter 12 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 390, c = 45, dia = 12 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 390 - 45 - 12/2 | Answer: 339 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 25.8 m^2 carrying a factored load of 15.9 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 25.8, w = 15.9 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 15.9 * 25.8 | Answer: 410.2 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 3.3 m, unit weight 16 kN/m^3, phi = 33 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 5.2e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.6, area = 2.3e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 5.2, i = 0.6, A = 2.3 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (5.2e-4)*0.6*(2.3e-3) | Answer: 717.6 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.9 m, bed slope 0.01 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.021. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 2.9 m under a head of 0.3 m. Taking Cd = 0.64 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 4.9 m wide carries a discharge of 8.3 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A tank of volume 980 m^3 treats a flow of 110 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 980, Q = 110 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 980 / 110 | Answer: 8.909 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 160 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.19 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 5 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 160, k = 0.19, t = 5 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 160*(1 - e^(-0.19*5)) | Answer: 98.12 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.3, rainfall intensity 120 mm/h over a catchment of 39.7 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.3, i = 120, A = 39.7 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.3*120*39.7 / 360 | Answer: 3.97 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.03 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 750 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.03, M = 750 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 750*(30+0.03)/30 | Answer: 750.8 m

question: Convert the decimal number 1648 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 1648 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 670 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 11110010 and 10001011.
solution: XOR: 01111001 | Count of 1s = 5 | Answer: 5
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 510 megabits is sent over a link of 95 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 510, B = 95 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 510 / 95 | Answer: 5.368 s

question: A link has bandwidth 58 Mbps and round-trip time 130 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 58, R = 130 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 58e6 * 130e-3 bits = 7540 kb | Answer: 7540 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.92, cache access time 10 ns and main-memory access time 190 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.92, tc = 10, tm = 190 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.92*10 + (1 - 0.92)*190 | Answer: 24.4 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 685012 elements?
solution: Given: n = 685012 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(685012)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.003, memory access time 180 ns and page-fault service time 5 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 5 ms = 5000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.003)*180 + 0.003*5000000.0 ns | Answer: 15.18 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 0.4 m^3 at 120 kPa and 320 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 0.4, P = 120, Tk = 320 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (120e3)*0.4 / (8.314*320) | Answer: 18.04 mol

question: For a reaction with A = 9e10 /s and activation energy 60 kJ/mol at 470 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 9, Ea = 60, Tk = 470 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 9e10 * exp(-60e3 / (8.314*470)) | Answer: 19309 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.92 and bottoms xW = 0.03, with relative volatility alpha = 1.8. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.92, xw = 0.03, al = 1.8 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.92/0.08)(0.97/0.03)] / ln(1.8) | Answer: 10.07 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.57 and x = 0.24. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.57, x = 0.24 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.57/0.43) / (0.24/0.76) | Answer: 4.198

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.87 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 105 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.87, Psat = 105 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.87 * 105 | Answer: 91.35 kPa

question: A stream of 5.7 kg/s with specific heat 4.1 kJ/kg-K is heated through 35 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 5.7, cp = 4.1, dT = 35 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 5.7*4.1*35 | Answer: 817.9 kW

question: A reactor of volume 9.6 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 0.9 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 9.6, Q = 0.9 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 9.6 / 0.9 | Answer: 10.67 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 8.5e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 5 mm with a concentration difference of 70 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 8.5, L = 5, dC = 70 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (8.5e-9)*70 / (5e-3) | Answer: 119 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 4.7 min and steady-state gain 2.5. For a step input of magnitude 11, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 4.7, K = 2.5, M = 11 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 2.5 * 11 | Answer: 27.5 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 20 m^2 flies at 220 m/s (air density 1 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 1.3. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 20, V = 220, rho = 1, CL = 1.3 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1*(220)^2*20*1.3 / 1000 | Answer: 629.2 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 15 m^2 flies at 200 m/s (density 0.4 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.03. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 15, V = 200, rho = 0.4, CD = 0.03 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.4*(200)^2*15*0.03 / 1000 | Answer: 3.6 kN

question: A block of mass 32 kg has a volume of 0.7e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 32, V = 0.7 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 32 / (0.7e-3) | Answer: 45714 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 2400 mm is heated through 100 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 12e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 2400, dT = 100, al = 12 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 2400*12e-6*100 | Answer: 2.88 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 85 ohm, R2 = 75 ohm and R3 = 160 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 85, R2 = 75, R3 = 160 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 75*160 / 85 | Answer: 141.2 ohm

question: A measurement reads 9.6 when the true value is 20. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.6, true = 20 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.6 - 20| / 20 * 100 | Answer: 52 %

question: Annual demand is 17000 units, ordering cost 200 per order and holding cost 19 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 17000, S = 200, H = 19 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*17000*200 / 19) | Answer: 598.2 units

question: An asset costs 210000 with salvage value 22000 after 7 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 210000, Sv = 22000, n = 7 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (210000 - 22000) / 7 | Answer: 26857 per year

question: A product sells for 460 per unit with variable cost 30 per unit and fixed costs 115000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 460, V = 30, F = 115000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 115000 / (460 - 30) | Answer: 267.4 units

question: Find the present worth of 90000 received 8 years from now at an interest rate of 5% per year.
solution: Given: F = 90000, n = 8, i = 5 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 90000 / (1 + 0.05)^8 | Answer: 60916 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.92, 0.93 and 0.91 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.92, r2 = 0.93, r3 = 0.91 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.92*0.93*0.91 | Answer: 0.7786

question: A process produces 11 defective items in a batch of 9000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 11, N = 9000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 11/9000 * 1e6 | Answer: 1222 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -5x^3 - 3x^2 - 2x - 7 evaluated at x = 5.
For f(x) = 2x^3 - 7x^2 - 2x + 6, find f''(x) at x = 5.
Evaluate the definite integral of (5x^2 - 2x + 4) dx from x = -4 to x = 7.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = 5x^3/3 + -2x^2/2 + 4x | Evaluate F(7) - F(-4) | Answer: 689.3
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 6x^2 + 7x - 1 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[8, -8], [3, -1]].
solution: Given: a = 8, b = -8, c = 3, d = -1 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (8)(-1) - (-8)(3) | Answer: 16

question: Find the determinant of [[-4, -6, 1], [-6, 4, 2], [-4, -4, 1]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: 4

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[-8, -1], [-7, 2]].
solution: Trace tr = -6, Determinant = -23 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 2.657

question: Solve for x: -3x + -3y = 9 and -6x + 2y = 10.
solution: Determinant = -3*2 - -3*-6 = -24 | x = (e d - b f) / det = -2 | Answer: x = -2
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 93, 56, 78, 79, 99.
solution: Sum = 405 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 81 | Answer: 81

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 41, 49, 17, 9, 12.
solution: Mean = 25.6 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 18.16

question: Find the slope of the line through (5, -3) and (-1, 2).
solution: Given: x1 = 5, y1 = -3, x2 = -1, y2 = 2 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (2 - -3) / (-1 - 5) | Answer: -0.8333

question: Find the distance between the points (8, 9) and (1, 0).
solution: Given: x1 = 8, y1 = 9, x2 = 1, y2 = 0 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-7)^2 + (-9)^2) | Answer: 11.4 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (0,-3), (6,5), (-7,-3).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 28 sq units

question: Find the 20th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -13 and common difference -2.
solution: Given: a = -13, d = -2, n = 20 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -13 + (20 - 1)*-2 | Answer: -51

question: Find the sum of the first 24 terms of an AP with first term -11 and common difference -5.
Find the simple interest on a principal of 39500 at 8.8% per annum for 2 years.
solution: Given: P = 39500, R = 8.8, Tt = 2 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 39500 * 8.8 * 2 / 100 | Answer: 6952 currency units

question: Find the amount when 29500 is invested at 8.8% per annum compounded annually for 6 years.
solution: Given: P = 29500, R = 8.8, Tt = 6 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 29500 * (1 + 8.8/100)^6 | Answer: 48932 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (-3, -5, 8) and (4, -1, -8).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (3, 3, -1) and (6, 0, -3).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 20.35

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (1, 5, 5) and (0, 1, -6).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 125.1 degrees

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number 3 + 5i.
solution: Given: a = 3, b = 5 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(5, 3) | Answer: 59.04 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -2x^3 + 3x^2 - 7x - 4 at x = 4.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-157 with initial guess x0=14, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.2 and ordinates 11, 0, 9, 12, 2, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 550 and 46.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 550 and 46 | Answer: GCD = 2

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 25 and 78.
solution: Given: a = 25, b = 78 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 25*78 / 1 | Answer: 1950
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 50 mm carries an axial tensile load of 56 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 36 mm and length 2500 mm carries an axial load of 31 kN. Take E = 110 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 33 mm transmits a torque of 700 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 33, Tt = 700 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(700*1000) / (pi*(33)^3) | Answer: 99.2 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 60 mm and length 1800 mm carries a torque of 250 N-m. With G = 45 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (60)^4 / 32 = 1272345 mm^4 | theta = (250*1000)(1800) / (45000 * 1272345) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 0.4503 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 141 mm wide and 190 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 141, h = 190 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 141*(190)^2 / 6 | Answer: 848350 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (66 mm x 200 mm) carries a bending moment of 6 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (61 mm x 140 mm) has effective length 3100 mm and E = 200 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 880 MPa is designed for a working stress of 90 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 880, sw = 90 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 880 / 90 | Answer: 9.778

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1250 mm and wall thickness 6 mm carries an internal pressure of 1.9 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
