solution: Given: b = 140, h = 100 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 140*(100)^2 / 6 | Answer: 233333 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (84 mm x 90 mm) carries a bending moment of 27 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (33 mm x 90 mm) has effective length 1700 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 540 MPa is designed for a working stress of 200 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 540, sw = 200 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 540 / 200 | Answer: 2.7

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 350 mm and wall thickness 9 mm carries an internal pressure of 1.9 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 350, t = 9, P = 1.9 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 1.9*350 / (2*9) | Answer: 36.94 MPa

question: 1.4 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 185 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1.4, dT = 185 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 1.4 * 0.718 * 185 | Answer: 186 kJ

question: 3.3 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 170 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.3, dT = 170 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 3.3 * 1.005 * 170 | Answer: 563.8 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 0.5 m^3 at 440 K with mass 1.4 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 0.5, Tk = 440, m = 1.4 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 1.4*0.287*440 / 0.5 | Answer: 353.6 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 3.5 kg of air expands isothermally at 400 K from volume V1 to 4*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.5, Tk = 400, ratio = 4 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 3.5*0.287*400*ln(4) | Answer: 557 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 1.8 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.13 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 1.8, D = 0.13 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*1.8*0.13 / 0.001 | Answer: 234000

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 9.2 m. Taking Cv = 0.98, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 9.2, cv = 0.98 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.98*sqrt(2*9.81*9.2) | Answer: 13.17 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 270 mm) water flows at 2.2 m/s. It contracts to diameter 60 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 270, d2 = 60, V1 = 2.2 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 2.2*(270/60)^2 | Answer: 44.55 m/s

question: Water flows at 1.1 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.25 m and length 50 m. With friction factor f = 0.027, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 17 teeth drives a gear of 112 teeth. If the pinion runs at 500 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 17, z2 = 112, N1 = 500 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 500*17 / 112 | Answer: 75.89 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 240 mm rotates at 1200 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 240, N = 1200 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.24)*1200 / 60 | Answer: 15.08 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 31.9 kW at 850 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 31.9, N = 850 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(31.9*1000) / (2*pi*850) | Answer: 358.4 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 7.1 kg rotates at radius 0.23 m at 900 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 2300 N/m and mass 10 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 2300, m = 10 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(2300/10) | Answer: 2.414 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 7.7 m^2 and thickness 0.26 m has conductivity k = 45 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 125 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 7.7, L = 0.26, k = 45, dT = 125 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 45*7.7*125 / 0.26 | Answer: 166587 W

question: A surface of area 4.9 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 110 W/m^2-K to surroundings 40 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 4.9, h = 110, dT = 40 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 110*4.9*40 | Answer: 21560 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 60 m/min, feed = 0.17 mm/rev, depth of cut = 1.3 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 60, f = 0.17, d = 1.3 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*60*0.17*1.3 | Answer: 13260 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 240 mm is turned at 350 rpm with a feed of 0.12 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 240, N = 350, f = 0.12 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 240 / (0.12*350) | Answer: 5.714 min

question: A resistor of 129 ohm carries a current of 6.5 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 129, I = 6.5 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 6.5 * 129 | Answer: 838.5 V

question: Three resistors 37 ohm, 36 ohm and 89 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 37, R2 = 36, R3 = 89 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 37 + 36 + 89 | Answer: 162 ohm

question: Two resistors 94 ohm and 63 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 94, R2 = 63 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 94*63 / (94+63) | Answer: 37.72 ohm

question: A device draws 13.8 A at 65 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 65, I = 13.8 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 65 * 13.8 | Answer: 897 W

question: A current of 3.1 A flows through a 47 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 3.1, R = 47 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (3.1)^2 * 47 | Answer: 451.7 W

question: Two capacitors 26.6 uF and 19.6 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 26.6, C2 = 19.6 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 26.6*19.6 / (26.6+19.6) | Answer: 11.28 uF

question: A resistor 90 kohm and capacitor 0.9 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 90, C = 0.9 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (90k)(0.9u) = 81 ms | Answer: 81 ms

question: An inductor 478.7 mH is in series with 9 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 478.7, R = 9 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (478.7e-3) / 9 | Answer: 53.19 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 173.7 mH inductor at 890 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 173.7, f = 890 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (890)(173.7e-3) | Answer: 971.3 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 8.6 uF capacitor at 810 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 8.6, f = 810 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (810)(8.6e-6)) | Answer: 22.85 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 80 ohm, XL = 111 ohm and XC = 98 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 80, XL = 111, XC = 98 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(80^2 + (111 - 98)^2) | Answer: 81.05 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 75.6 mH and C = 5.3 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 75.6, C = 5.3 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(75.6e-3 * 5.3e-6)) | Answer: 251.4 Hz

question: A capacitor of 37.5 uF is charged to 325 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 37.5, V = 325 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*37.5e-6*(325)^2 | Answer: 198 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 400 V with 370 primary turns and 130 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 400, N1 = 370, N2 = 130 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 400 * 130/370 | Answer: 140.5 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 220 V and draws an armature current of 51 A. If the armature resistance is 0.99 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 220, Ia = 51, Ra = 0.99 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 220 - 51*0.99 | Answer: 169.5 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 125 A at 415 V (line) with a power factor of 0.73. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 125, VL = 415, pf = 0.73 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*415*125*0.73 / 1000 | Answer: 65.59 kW

question: A load has real power 40 kW and apparent power 155 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 40, S = 155 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 40 / 155 | Answer: 0.2581

question: A machine delivers 15 kW output while drawing 87 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 15, Pi = 87 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 15/87 * 100 | Answer: 17.24 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 23 V across R1 = 24 ohm and R2 = 18 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 23, R1 = 24, R2 = 18 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 23*18 / (24+18) | Answer: 9.857 V

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 120 kohm and Rg = 43 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 120, Rg = 43 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 120/43 | Answer: 3.791

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 64. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 64 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(64) | Answer: 18.06 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 8.4 m carries a central point load of 30 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 8.4, W = 30 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 30*8.4 / 4 | Answer: 63 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 4.3 m carries a point load 25 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.3, W = 25 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 25*4.3 | Answer: 107.5 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 2.3 m carries a UDL of 38 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 2.3, w = 38 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 38*(2.3)^2 / 2 | Answer: 100.5 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.6 m carries a point load 85 kN at distance 3.9 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 6.6, a = 3.9, W = 85 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 85*(6.6 - 3.9) / 6.6 | Answer: 34.77 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 5.3 m) carries a central point load 45 kN. With E = 200 GPa and I = 120e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=45000 N, L=5300.0 mm, E=200000 MPa, I=120e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 5.816 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 6 m carries a UDL of 18 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6, w = 18 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 18*(6)^2 / 12 | Answer: 54 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 570 mm, clear cover 40 mm and main bars of diameter 16 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 570, c = 40, dia = 16 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 570 - 40 - 16/2 | Answer: 522 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 27.4 m^2 carrying a factored load of 13.4 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 27.4, w = 13.4 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 13.4 * 27.4 | Answer: 367.2 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 6.4 m, unit weight 16 kN/m^3, phi = 37 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 7.2e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1.1, area = 5.1e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 7.2, i = 1.1, A = 5.1 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (7.2e-4)*1.1*(5.1e-3) | Answer: 4039 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1 m, bed slope 0.003 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.02. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 3.8 m under a head of 0.9 m. Taking Cd = 0.63 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 3.3 m wide carries a discharge of 9 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A tank of volume 620 m^3 treats a flow of 60 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 620, Q = 60 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 620 / 60 | Answer: 10.33 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 310 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.14 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 6 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 310, k = 0.14, t = 6 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 310*(1 - e^(-0.14*6)) | Answer: 176.2 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.71, rainfall intensity 95 mm/h over a catchment of 40.8 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.71, i = 95, A = 40.8 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.71*95*40.8 / 360 | Answer: 7.644 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.05 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 750 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.05, M = 750 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 750*(30+0.05)/30 | Answer: 751.2 m

question: Convert the decimal number 3938 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 3938 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: F62 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 00101000 and 00001100.
solution: XOR: 00100100 | Count of 1s = 2 | Answer: 2
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 120 megabits is sent over a link of 73 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 120, B = 73 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 120 / 73 | Answer: 1.644 s

question: A link has bandwidth 81 Mbps and round-trip time 20 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 81, R = 20 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 81e6 * 20e-3 bits = 1620 kb | Answer: 1620 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.86, cache access time 6 ns and main-memory access time 200 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.86, tc = 6, tm = 200 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.86*6 + (1 - 0.86)*200 | Answer: 33.16 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 819523 elements?
solution: Given: n = 819523 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(819523)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.013, memory access time 110 ns and page-fault service time 6 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 6 ms = 6000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.013)*110 + 0.013*6000000.0 ns | Answer: 78.11 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 2.1 m^3 at 380 kPa and 360 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 2.1, P = 380, Tk = 360 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (380e3)*2.1 / (8.314*360) | Answer: 266.6 mol

question: For a reaction with A = 9e10 /s and activation energy 80 kJ/mol at 400 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 9, Ea = 80, Tk = 400 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 9e10 * exp(-80e3 / (8.314*400)) | Answer: 3.213 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.96 and bottoms xW = 0.05, with relative volatility alpha = 3.2. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.96, xw = 0.05, al = 3.2 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.96/0.04)(0.95/0.05)] / ln(3.2) | Answer: 5.264 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.71 and x = 0.31. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.71, x = 0.31 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.71/0.29) / (0.31/0.69) | Answer: 5.449

question: A stream of 9.1 kg/s with specific heat 1.3 kJ/kg-K is heated through 115 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 9.1, cp = 1.3, dT = 115 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 9.1*1.3*115 | Answer: 136 kW

question: A reactor of volume 11.8 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 2.6 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 11.8, Q = 2.6 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 11.8 / 2.6 | Answer: 4.538 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 6.5e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 5 mm with a concentration difference of 180 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 6.5, L = 5, dC = 180 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (6.5e-9)*180 / (5e-3) | Answer: 234 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 9.6 min and steady-state gain 3.7. For a step input of magnitude 3, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 9.6, K = 3.7, M = 3 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 3.7 * 3 | Answer: 11.1 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 65 m^2 flies at 90 m/s (air density 1.225 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.3. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 65, V = 90, rho = 1.225, CL = 0.3 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1.225*(90)^2*65*0.3 / 1000 | Answer: 96.74 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 35 m^2 flies at 70 m/s (density 0.4 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.08. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 35, V = 70, rho = 0.4, CD = 0.08 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.4*(70)^2*35*0.08 / 1000 | Answer: 2.744 kN

question: A block of mass 37 kg has a volume of 1.4e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 37, V = 1.4 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 37 / (1.4e-3) | Answer: 26429 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 1800 mm is heated through 35 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 17e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 1800, dT = 35, al = 17 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 1800*17e-6*35 | Answer: 1.071 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 35 ohm, R2 = 175 ohm and R3 = 130 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 35, R2 = 175, R3 = 130 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 175*130 / 35 | Answer: 650 ohm

question: A measurement reads 9.75 when the true value is 50. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.75, true = 50 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.75 - 50| / 50 * 100 | Answer: 80.5 %

question: Annual demand is 21500 units, ordering cost 220 per order and holding cost 20 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 21500, S = 220, H = 20 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*21500*220 / 20) | Answer: 687.7 units

question: An asset costs 430000 with salvage value 40000 after 13 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 430000, Sv = 40000, n = 13 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (430000 - 40000) / 13 | Answer: 30000 per year

question: A product sells for 110 per unit with variable cost 10 per unit and fixed costs 190000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 110, V = 10, F = 190000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 190000 / (110 - 10) | Answer: 1900 units

question: Find the present worth of 60000 received 5 years from now at an interest rate of 5% per year.
solution: Given: F = 60000, n = 5, i = 5 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 60000 / (1 + 0.05)^5 | Answer: 47012 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.91, 0.95 and 0.91 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.91, r2 = 0.95, r3 = 0.91 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.91*0.95*0.91 | Answer: 0.7867

question: A process produces 20 defective items in a batch of 13500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 20, N = 13500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 20/13500 * 1e6 | Answer: 1481 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -x^3 - 5x^2 + 7x - 6 evaluated at x = 1.
For f(x) = 6x^3 - x^2 + 2x - 7, find f''(x) at x = 3.
Evaluate the definite integral of (-x^2 + 3x - 8) dx from x = -1 to x = 4.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = -1x^3/3 + 3x^2/2 + -8x | Evaluate F(4) - F(-1) | Answer: -39.17
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 3x^2 - 5x - 9 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[-6, -1], [4, 4]].
solution: Given: a = -6, b = -1, c = 4, d = 4 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (-6)(4) - (-1)(4) | Answer: -20

question: Find the determinant of [[2, 1, -4], [1, 1, -6], [-5, 1, 4]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: 22

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[8, 6], [1, -6]].
solution: Trace tr = 2, Determinant = -54 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 8.416

question: Solve for x: 3x + 3y = 8 and -4x + 5y = 1.
solution: Determinant = 3*5 - 3*-4 = 27 | x = (e d - b f) / det = 1.37 | Answer: x = 1.37
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 62, 36, 98, 59, 69.
solution: Sum = 324 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 64.8 | Answer: 64.8

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 24, 50, 45, 17, 26.
solution: Mean = 32.4 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 14.29

question: Find the slope of the line through (8, 1) and (3, 0).
solution: Given: x1 = 8, y1 = 1, x2 = 3, y2 = 0 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (0 - 1) / (3 - 8) | Answer: 0.2

question: Find the distance between the points (-1, 9) and (8, 6).
solution: Given: x1 = -1, y1 = 9, x2 = 8, y2 = 6 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((9)^2 + (-3)^2) | Answer: 9.487 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (0,8), (-7,-1), (7,0).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 59.5 sq units

question: Find the 5th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -18 and common difference -1.
solution: Given: a = -18, d = -1, n = 5 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -18 + (5 - 1)*-1 | Answer: -22

question: Find the sum of the first 13 terms of an AP with first term -1 and common difference 1.
solution: Given: a = -1, d = 1, n = 13 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 13/2 [2*-1 + (13-1)*1] | Answer: 65

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 35500 at 13.9% per annum for 7 years.
solution: Given: P = 35500, R = 13.9, Tt = 7 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 35500 * 13.9 * 7 / 100 | Answer: 34542 currency units

question: Find the amount when 8000 is invested at 11.7% per annum compounded annually for 3 years.
solution: Given: P = 8000, R = 11.7, Tt = 3 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 8000 * (1 + 11.7/100)^3 | Answer: 11149 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (7, -8, -8) and (-6, 8, -8).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (-2, 6, 2) and (0, -4, -5).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 25.46

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (6, -4, 5) and (-2, 2, -3).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 165.3 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = 5x^3 - 6x^2 + x + 4 at x = -2.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-33 with initial guess x0=10, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.2 and ordinates 14, 9, 3, 17, 8, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 89 and 226.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 89 and 226 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 56 and 26.
solution: Given: a = 56, b = 26 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 56*26 / 2 | Answer: 728
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 36 mm carries an axial tensile load of 11 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 25 mm and length 700 mm carries an axial load of 40 kN. Take E = 110 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 34 mm transmits a torque of 800 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 34, Tt = 800 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(800*1000) / (pi*(34)^3) | Answer: 103.7 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 56 mm and length 2000 mm carries a torque of 250 N-m. With G = 77 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (56)^4 / 32 = 965499 mm^4 | theta = (250*1000)(2000) / (77000 * 965499) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 0.3853 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 54 mm wide and 210 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 54, h = 210 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 54*(210)^2 / 6 | Answer: 396900 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (58 mm x 160 mm) carries a bending moment of 21 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (47 mm x 90 mm) has effective length 2500 mm and E = 200 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1150 mm and wall thickness 17 mm carries an internal pressure of 0.7 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1150, t = 17, P = 0.7 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 0.7*1150 / (2*17) | Answer: 23.68 MPa

question: 4.3 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 55 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.3, dT = 55 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 4.3 * 0.718 * 55 | Answer: 169.8 kJ

question: 1.1 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 145 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1.1, dT = 145 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 1.1 * 1.005 * 145 | Answer: 160.3 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 2.8 m^3 at 550 K with mass 2 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 2.8, Tk = 550, m = 2 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 2*0.287*550 / 2.8 | Answer: 112.8 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 1.3 kg of air expands isothermally at 420 K from volume V1 to 3*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1.3, Tk = 420, ratio = 3 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 1.3*0.287*420*ln(3) | Answer: 172.2 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 4.2 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.4 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 4.2, D = 0.4 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*4.2*0.4 / 0.001 | Answer: 1680000

question: Water flows at 2.5 m/s through a pipe of diameter 270 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 16.9 m. Taking Cv = 0.99, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 16.9, cv = 0.99 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.99*sqrt(2*9.81*16.9) | Answer: 18.03 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 240 mm) water flows at 2.4 m/s. It contracts to diameter 130 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 240, d2 = 130, V1 = 2.4 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 2.4*(240/130)^2 | Answer: 8.18 m/s

question: Water flows at 1.7 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.15 m and length 370 m. With friction factor f = 0.037, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 21 teeth drives a gear of 96 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1300 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 21, z2 = 96, N1 = 1300 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1300*21 / 96 | Answer: 284.4 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 600 mm rotates at 200 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 600, N = 200 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.6)*200 / 60 | Answer: 6.283 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 45.8 kW at 350 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 45.8, N = 350 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(45.8*1000) / (2*pi*350) | Answer: 125 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 4.7 kg rotates at radius 0.54 m at 650 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 15000 N/m and mass 14.1 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 15000, m = 14.1 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(15000/14.1) | Answer: 5.191 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 1.8 m^2 and thickness 0.24 m has conductivity k = 12.1 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 85 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 1.8, L = 0.24, k = 12.1, dT = 85 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 12.1*1.8*85 / 0.24 | Answer: 7714 W

question: A surface of area 4.7 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 50 W/m^2-K to surroundings 75 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 4.7, h = 50, dT = 75 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 50*4.7*75 | Answer: 17625 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 170 m/min, feed = 0.44 mm/rev, depth of cut = 1.2 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 170, f = 0.44, d = 1.2 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*170*0.44*1.2 | Answer: 89760 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 470 mm is turned at 1200 rpm with a feed of 0.13 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 470, N = 1200, f = 0.13 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 470 / (0.13*1200) | Answer: 3.013 min

question: A resistor of 114 ohm carries a current of 6.3 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 114, I = 6.3 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 6.3 * 114 | Answer: 718.2 V

question: Three resistors 65 ohm, 66 ohm and 19 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 65, R2 = 66, R3 = 19 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 65 + 66 + 19 | Answer: 150 ohm

question: Two resistors 16 ohm and 39 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 16, R2 = 39 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 16*39 / (16+39) | Answer: 11.35 ohm

question: A device draws 12.1 A at 215 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 215, I = 12.1 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 215 * 12.1 | Answer: 2602 W

question: A current of 10.2 A flows through a 37 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 10.2, R = 37 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (10.2)^2 * 37 | Answer: 3849 W

question: Two capacitors 8.4 uF and 34.2 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 8.4, C2 = 34.2 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 8.4*34.2 / (8.4+34.2) | Answer: 6.744 uF

question: A resistor 47 kohm and capacitor 13.8 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 47, C = 13.8 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (47k)(13.8u) = 648.6 ms | Answer: 648.6 ms

question: An inductor 307.5 mH is in series with 56 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 307.5, R = 56 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (307.5e-3) / 56 | Answer: 5.491 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 120.4 mH inductor at 860 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 120.4, f = 860 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (860)(120.4e-3) | Answer: 650.6 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 36.9 uF capacitor at 720 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 36.9, f = 720 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (720)(36.9e-6)) | Answer: 5.99 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 91 ohm, XL = 142 ohm and XC = 30 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 91, XL = 142, XC = 30 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(91^2 + (142 - 30)^2) | Answer: 144.3 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 38.7 mH and C = 2.9 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 38.7, C = 2.9 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(38.7e-3 * 2.9e-6)) | Answer: 475.1 Hz

question: A capacitor of 22.8 uF is charged to 305 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 22.8, V = 305 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*22.8e-6*(305)^2 | Answer: 106 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 290 V with 810 primary turns and 370 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 290, N1 = 810, N2 = 370 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 290 * 370/810 | Answer: 132.5 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 170 V and draws an armature current of 11 A. If the armature resistance is 0.36 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 170, Ia = 11, Ra = 0.36 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 170 - 11*0.36 | Answer: 166 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 55 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.76. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 55, VL = 400, pf = 0.76 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*400*55*0.76 / 1000 | Answer: 28.96 kW

question: A load has real power 65 kW and apparent power 115 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 65, S = 115 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 65 / 115 | Answer: 0.5652

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 30 V across R1 = 16 ohm and R2 = 43 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 30, R1 = 16, R2 = 43 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 30*43 / (16+43) | Answer: 21.86 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 10 kohm and Rin = 4 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 10, Rin = 4 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 10 / 4 | Answer: 2.5

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 70 kohm and Rg = 15 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 70, Rg = 15 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 70/15 | Answer: 5.667

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 4099. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 4099 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(4099) | Answer: 36.13 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 5.9 m carries a central point load of 55 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.9, W = 55 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 55*5.9 / 4 | Answer: 81.12 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.7 m carries a UDL of 25 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6.7, w = 25 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 25*(6.7)^2 / 8 | Answer: 140.3 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 4.4 m carries a UDL of 22 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.4, w = 22 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 22*(4.4)^2 / 2 | Answer: 213 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.3 m carries a point load 80 kN at distance 2.6 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 9.3, a = 2.6, W = 80 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 80*(9.3 - 2.6) / 9.3 | Answer: 57.63 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 5.4 m) carries a central point load 75 kN. With E = 200 GPa and I = 190e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=75000 N, L=5400.0 mm, E=200000 MPa, I=190e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 6.475 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 4.5 m carries a UDL of 12 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.5, w = 12 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 12*(4.5)^2 / 12 | Answer: 20.25 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 400 mm, clear cover 25 mm and main bars of diameter 25 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 400, c = 25, dia = 25 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 400 - 25 - 25/2 | Answer: 362.5 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 39.5 m^2 carrying a factored load of 13.2 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 39.5, w = 13.2 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 13.2 * 39.5 | Answer: 521.4 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 3.4 m, unit weight 18 kN/m^3, phi = 37 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 8.8e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1.4, area = 7.7e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 8.8, i = 1.4, A = 7.7 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (8.8e-4)*1.4*(7.7e-3) | Answer: 9486 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.3 m, bed slope 0.009 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.025. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 2.8 m under a head of 0.9 m. Taking Cd = 0.64 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 2.8 m wide carries a discharge of 28.1 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A tank of volume 650 m^3 treats a flow of 105 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 650, Q = 105 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 650 / 105 | Answer: 6.19 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 290 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.32 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 5 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 290, k = 0.32, t = 5 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 290*(1 - e^(-0.32*5)) | Answer: 231.5 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.56, rainfall intensity 100 mm/h over a catchment of 58.6 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.56, i = 100, A = 58.6 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.56*100*58.6 / 360 | Answer: 9.116 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.08 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 410 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.08, M = 410 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 410*(20+0.08)/20 | Answer: 411.6 m

question: Convert the decimal number 1904 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 1904 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 770 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 10110010 and 00011110.
solution: XOR: 10101100 | Count of 1s = 4 | Answer: 4
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 750 megabits is sent over a link of 60 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 750, B = 60 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 750 / 60 | Answer: 12.5 s

question: A link has bandwidth 34 Mbps and round-trip time 10 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 34, R = 10 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 34e6 * 10e-3 bits = 340 kb | Answer: 340 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.89, cache access time 9 ns and main-memory access time 150 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.89, tc = 9, tm = 150 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.89*9 + (1 - 0.89)*150 | Answer: 24.51 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 855031 elements?
solution: Given: n = 855031 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(855031)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.012, memory access time 120 ns and page-fault service time 9 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 9 ms = 9000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.012)*120 + 0.012*9000000.0 ns | Answer: 108.1 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 0.3 m^3 at 480 kPa and 500 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 0.3, P = 480, Tk = 500 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (480e3)*0.3 / (8.314*500) | Answer: 34.64 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.05 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 19 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.05, t = 19 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.05*19) | Answer: 0.6133

question: For a reaction with A = 4e10 /s and activation energy 90 kJ/mol at 320 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 4, Ea = 90, Tk = 320 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 4e10 * exp(-90e3 / (8.314*320)) | Answer: 0.00008138 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.96 and bottoms xW = 0.1, with relative volatility alpha = 2.1. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.96, xw = 0.1, al = 2.1 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.96/0.04)(0.9/0.1)] / ln(2.1) | Answer: 7.245 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.78 and x = 0.45. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.78, x = 0.45 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.78/0.22) / (0.45/0.55) | Answer: 4.333

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.87 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 70 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.87, Psat = 70 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.87 * 70 | Answer: 60.9 kPa

question: A stream of 7 kg/s with specific heat 4.2 kJ/kg-K is heated through 65 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 7, cp = 4.2, dT = 65 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 7*4.2*65 | Answer: 1911 kW

question: A reactor of volume 17.2 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 3.2 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 17.2, Q = 3.2 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 17.2 / 3.2 | Answer: 5.375 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 2.3e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 1 mm with a concentration difference of 170 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 2.3, L = 1, dC = 170 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (2.3e-9)*170 / (1e-3) | Answer: 391 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 2 min and steady-state gain 2.6. For a step input of magnitude 13, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 2, K = 2.6, M = 13 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 2.6 * 13 | Answer: 33.8 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 20 m^2 flies at 90 m/s (air density 0.7 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.8. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 20, V = 90, rho = 0.7, CL = 0.8 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.7*(90)^2*20*0.8 / 1000 | Answer: 45.36 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 85 m^2 flies at 240 m/s (density 0.4 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.1. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 85, V = 240, rho = 0.4, CD = 0.1 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.4*(240)^2*85*0.1 / 1000 | Answer: 97.92 kN

question: A specimen under stress 260 MPa shows an elastic strain of 2.8e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 260, eps = 2.8 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 260 / (2.8e-3) MPa = 92.86 GPa | Answer: 92.86 GPa

question: A block of mass 44 kg has a volume of 2.2e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 44, V = 2.2 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 44 / (2.2e-3) | Answer: 20000 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 1400 mm is heated through 50 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 23e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 1400, dT = 50, al = 23 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 1400*23e-6*50 | Answer: 1.61 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 130 ohm, R2 = 50 ohm and R3 = 455 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 130, R2 = 50, R3 = 455 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 50*455 / 130 | Answer: 175 ohm

question: A measurement reads 9.48 when the true value is 10. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.48, true = 10 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.48 - 10| / 10 * 100 | Answer: 5.2 %

question: Annual demand is 6000 units, ordering cost 50 per order and holding cost 34 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 6000, S = 50, H = 34 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*6000*50 / 34) | Answer: 132.8 units

question: An asset costs 200000 with salvage value 4000 after 6 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 200000, Sv = 4000, n = 6 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (200000 - 4000) / 6 | Answer: 32667 per year

question: A product sells for 200 per unit with variable cost 90 per unit and fixed costs 90000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 200, V = 90, F = 90000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 90000 / (200 - 90) | Answer: 818.2 units

question: Find the present worth of 70000 received 8 years from now at an interest rate of 7% per year.
solution: Given: F = 70000, n = 8, i = 7 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 70000 / (1 + 0.07)^8 | Answer: 40741 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.92, 0.94 and 0.98 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.92, r2 = 0.94, r3 = 0.98 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.92*0.94*0.98 | Answer: 0.8475

question: A process produces 20 defective items in a batch of 2500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 20, N = 2500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 20/2500 * 1e6 | Answer: 8000 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -3x^3 + x^2 + 3x - 2 evaluated at x = -1.
For f(x) = x^3 - 8x^2 - 9x + 3, find f''(x) at x = 3.
Evaluate the definite integral of (2x^2 + x + 3) dx from x = 0 to x = 5.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = 2x^3/3 + 1x^2/2 + 3x | Evaluate F(5) - F(0) | Answer: 110.8
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 4x^2 - 12x + 5 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[9, 2], [-9, -8]].
solution: Given: a = 9, b = 2, c = -9, d = -8 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (9)(-8) - (2)(-9) | Answer: -54

question: Find the determinant of [[5, 5, -5], [6, -2, -4], [-5, 6, 4]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: -70

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[-3, 7], [2, 3]].
solution: Trace tr = 0, Determinant = -23 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 4.796

question: Solve for x: -5x + 4y = 2 and -4x + 2y = -3.
solution: Determinant = -5*2 - 4*-4 = 6 | x = (e d - b f) / det = 2.667 | Answer: x = 2.667
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 35, 14, 95, 42, 82.
solution: Sum = 268 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 53.6 | Answer: 53.6

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 3, 48, 24, 18, 30.
solution: Mean = 24.6 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 16.49

question: Find the slope of the line through (2, 4) and (5, -1).
solution: Given: x1 = 2, y1 = 4, x2 = 5, y2 = -1 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (-1 - 4) / (5 - 2) | Answer: -1.667

question: Find the distance between the points (-3, 6) and (4, -8).
solution: Given: x1 = -3, y1 = 6, x2 = 4, y2 = -8 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((7)^2 + (-14)^2) | Answer: 15.65 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (-6,-6), (-5,0), (-5,-6).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 3 sq units

question: Find the 29th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -17 and common difference -9.
solution: Given: a = -17, d = -9, n = 29 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -17 + (29 - 1)*-9 | Answer: -269

question: Find the sum of the first 24 terms of an AP with first term -13 and common difference -6.
Find the simple interest on a principal of 38000 at 9% per annum for 2 years.
solution: Given: P = 38000, R = 9, Tt = 2 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 38000 * 9 * 2 / 100 | Answer: 6840 currency units

question: Find the amount when 26000 is invested at 9.1% per annum compounded annually for 6 years.
solution: Given: P = 26000, R = 9.1, Tt = 6 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 26000 * (1 + 9.1/100)^6 | Answer: 43845 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (1, 0, 7) and (-2, 7, 6).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (1, -6, 6) and (-5, -1, 4).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 49.41

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (-2, -4, -6) and (-1, -2, -6).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 16.26 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -4x^3 + 3x^2 - 6x - 4 at x = 2.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-115 with initial guess x0=13, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=0.5 and ordinates 2, 3, 18, 4, 15, estimate the integral.
