question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (-3, 4, 1) and (0, -4, -4).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 20.78

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (3, -5, 6) and (5, -5, -2).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 62.91 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number 10 + -2i.
solution: Given: a = 10, b = -2 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((10)^2 + (-2)^2) | Answer: 10.2

question: Evaluate f(x) = -5x^3 + 6x^2 + 9x - 2 at x = -2.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-125 with initial guess x0=6, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.3 and ordinates 7, 7, 18, 4, 16, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 356 and 110.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 356 and 110 | Answer: GCD = 2

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 32 and 29.
solution: Given: a = 32, b = 29 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 32*29 / 1 | Answer: 928
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 17 mm carries an axial tensile load of 56 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 33 mm and length 2400 mm carries an axial load of 68 kN. Take E = 70 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 56 mm transmits a torque of 200 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 56, Tt = 200 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(200*1000) / (pi*(56)^3) | Answer: 5.8 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 50 mm and length 500 mm carries a torque of 1800 N-m. With G = 80 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (50)^4 / 32 = 613592 mm^4 | theta = (1800*1000)(500) / (80000 * 613592) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 1.05 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 123 mm wide and 260 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 123, h = 260 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 123*(260)^2 / 6 | Answer: 1385800 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (100 mm x 240 mm) carries a bending moment of 35 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (64 mm x 120 mm) has effective length 2200 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 850 MPa is designed for a working stress of 180 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 850, sw = 180 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 850 / 180 | Answer: 4.722

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1300 mm and wall thickness 15 mm carries an internal pressure of 1.6 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1300, t = 15, P = 1.6 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 1.6*1300 / (2*15) | Answer: 69.33 MPa

question: 7 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 20 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 7, dT = 20 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 7 * 0.718 * 20 | Answer: 100.5 kJ

question: 4.9 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 200 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.9, dT = 200 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 4.9 * 1.005 * 200 | Answer: 984.9 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 1.6 m^3 at 470 K with mass 4.1 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 1.6, Tk = 470, m = 4.1 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 4.1*0.287*470 / 1.6 | Answer: 345.7 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 3.7 kg of air expands isothermally at 320 K from volume V1 to 4*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.7, Tk = 320, ratio = 4 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 3.7*0.287*320*ln(4) | Answer: 471.1 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 4.1 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.27 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 4.1, D = 0.27 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*4.1*0.27 / 0.001 | Answer: 1107000

question: Water flows at 1.8 m/s through a pipe of diameter 300 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
In a pipe (diameter 280 mm) water flows at 2.1 m/s. It contracts to diameter 60 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 280, d2 = 60, V1 = 2.1 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 2.1*(280/60)^2 | Answer: 45.73 m/s

question: Water flows at 1.2 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.2 m and length 370 m. With friction factor f = 0.036, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 19 teeth drives a gear of 80 teeth. If the pinion runs at 550 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 19, z2 = 80, N1 = 550 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 550*19 / 80 | Answer: 130.6 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 260 mm rotates at 800 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 260, N = 800 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.26)*800 / 60 | Answer: 10.89 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 33.9 kW at 1150 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 33.9, N = 1150 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(33.9*1000) / (2*pi*1150) | Answer: 281.5 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 6 kg rotates at radius 0.33 m at 1000 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 18500 N/m and mass 5 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 18500, m = 5 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(18500/5) | Answer: 9.681 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 6.9 m^2 and thickness 0.17 m has conductivity k = 5.5 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 85 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 6.9, L = 0.17, k = 5.5, dT = 85 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 5.5*6.9*85 / 0.17 | Answer: 18975 W

question: A surface of area 1.7 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 145 W/m^2-K to surroundings 30 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 1.7, h = 145, dT = 30 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 145*1.7*30 | Answer: 7395 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 200 m/min, feed = 0.37 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2.4 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 200, f = 0.37, d = 2.4 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*200*0.37*2.4 | Answer: 177600 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 440 mm is turned at 500 rpm with a feed of 0.39 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 440, N = 500, f = 0.39 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 440 / (0.39*500) | Answer: 2.256 min

question: A resistor of 164 ohm carries a current of 1.7 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 164, I = 1.7 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 1.7 * 164 | Answer: 278.8 V

question: Three resistors 92 ohm, 31 ohm and 20 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 92, R2 = 31, R3 = 20 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 92 + 31 + 20 | Answer: 143 ohm

question: Two resistors 53 ohm and 47 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 53, R2 = 47 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 53*47 / (53+47) | Answer: 24.91 ohm

question: A device draws 14.6 A at 145 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 145, I = 14.6 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 145 * 14.6 | Answer: 2117 W

question: A current of 0.9 A flows through a 87 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 0.9, R = 87 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (0.9)^2 * 87 | Answer: 70.47 W

question: Two capacitors 44.8 uF and 34.7 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 44.8, C2 = 34.7 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 44.8*34.7 / (44.8+34.7) | Answer: 19.55 uF

question: A resistor 12 kohm and capacitor 7.8 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 12, C = 7.8 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (12k)(7.8u) = 93.6 ms | Answer: 93.6 ms

question: An inductor 447 mH is in series with 9 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 447, R = 9 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (447e-3) / 9 | Answer: 49.67 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 24.1 mH inductor at 850 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 24.1, f = 850 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (850)(24.1e-3) | Answer: 128.7 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 45.8 uF capacitor at 450 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 45.8, f = 450 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (450)(45.8e-6)) | Answer: 7.722 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 5 ohm, XL = 71 ohm and XC = 76 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 5, XL = 71, XC = 76 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(5^2 + (71 - 76)^2) | Answer: 7.071 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 7 mH and C = 8.6 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 7, C = 8.6 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(7e-3 * 8.6e-6)) | Answer: 648.7 Hz

question: A capacitor of 78.4 uF is charged to 95 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 78.4, V = 95 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*78.4e-6*(95)^2 | Answer: 353.8 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 160 V with 530 primary turns and 420 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 160, N1 = 530, N2 = 420 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 160 * 420/530 | Answer: 126.8 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 240 V and draws an armature current of 13 A. If the armature resistance is 0.39 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 240, Ia = 13, Ra = 0.39 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 240 - 13*0.39 | Answer: 234.9 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 95 A at 415 V (line) with a power factor of 0.76. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 95, VL = 415, pf = 0.76 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*415*95*0.76 / 1000 | Answer: 51.9 kW

question: A load has real power 40 kW and apparent power 215 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 40, S = 215 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 40 / 215 | Answer: 0.186

question: A machine delivers 75 kW output while drawing 137 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 75, Pi = 137 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 75/137 * 100 | Answer: 54.74 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 12 V across R1 = 39 ohm and R2 = 38 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 12, R1 = 39, R2 = 38 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 12*38 / (39+38) | Answer: 5.922 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 80 kohm and Rin = 47 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 80, Rin = 47 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 80 / 47 | Answer: 1.702

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 150 kohm and Rg = 13 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 150, Rg = 13 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 150/13 | Answer: 12.54

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 4351. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 4351 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(4351) | Answer: 36.39 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 10 m carries a central point load of 70 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 10, W = 70 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 70*10 / 4 | Answer: 175 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.9 m carries a UDL of 10 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6.9, w = 10 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 10*(6.9)^2 / 8 | Answer: 59.51 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 1.9 m carries a point load 60 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 1.9, W = 60 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 60*1.9 | Answer: 114 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 2 m carries a UDL of 8 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 2, w = 8 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 8*(2)^2 / 2 | Answer: 16 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 5.9 m carries a point load 100 kN at distance 1.7 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 5.9, a = 1.7, W = 100 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 100*(5.9 - 1.7) / 5.9 | Answer: 71.19 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 3.6 m) carries a central point load 45 kN. With E = 200 GPa and I = 400e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=45000 N, L=3600.0 mm, E=200000 MPa, I=400e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 0.5467 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 6.8 m carries a UDL of 39 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6.8, w = 39 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 39*(6.8)^2 / 12 | Answer: 150.3 kN-m

question: A column supports a floor area of 15.3 m^2 carrying a factored load of 17.9 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 15.3, w = 17.9 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 17.9 * 15.3 | Answer: 273.9 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 5 m, unit weight 18 kN/m^3, phi = 38 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 6.5e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.4, area = 1.3e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 6.5, i = 0.4, A = 1.3 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (6.5e-4)*0.4*(1.3e-3) | Answer: 338 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 2.3 m, bed slope 0.002 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.019. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 3.3 m under a head of 0.6 m. Taking Cd = 0.62 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 4.3 m wide carries a discharge of 11.6 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A tank of volume 610 m^3 treats a flow of 140 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 610, Q = 140 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 610 / 140 | Answer: 4.357 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 220 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.26 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 4 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 220, k = 0.26, t = 4 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 220*(1 - e^(-0.26*4)) | Answer: 142.2 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.77, rainfall intensity 75 mm/h over a catchment of 11.7 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.77, i = 75, A = 11.7 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.77*75*11.7 / 360 | Answer: 1.877 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.02 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 200 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.02, M = 200 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 200*(20+0.02)/20 | Answer: 200.2 m

question: Convert the decimal number 878 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 878 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 36E (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 10101101 and 01011010.
solution: XOR: 11110111 | Count of 1s = 7 | Answer: 7
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 960 megabits is sent over a link of 55 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 960, B = 55 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 960 / 55 | Answer: 17.45 s

question: A link has bandwidth 92 Mbps and round-trip time 140 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 92, R = 140 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 92e6 * 140e-3 bits = 12880 kb | Answer: 12880 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.96, cache access time 9 ns and main-memory access time 110 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.96, tc = 9, tm = 110 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.96*9 + (1 - 0.96)*110 | Answer: 13.04 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 586651 elements?
solution: Given: n = 586651 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(586651)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.02, memory access time 130 ns and page-fault service time 3 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 3 ms = 3000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.02)*130 + 0.02*3000000.0 ns | Answer: 60.13 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 0.3 m^3 at 500 kPa and 570 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 0.3, P = 500, Tk = 570 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (500e3)*0.3 / (8.314*570) | Answer: 31.65 mol

question: For a reaction with A = 9e10 /s and activation energy 60 kJ/mol at 410 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 9, Ea = 60, Tk = 410 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 9e10 * exp(-60e3 / (8.314*410)) | Answer: 2041 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.95 and bottoms xW = 0.04, with relative volatility alpha = 3.4. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.95, xw = 0.04, al = 3.4 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.95/0.05)(0.96/0.04)] / ln(3.4) | Answer: 5.003 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.67 and x = 0.4. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.67, x = 0.4 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.67/0.33) / (0.4/0.6) | Answer: 3.045

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.58 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 60 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.58, Psat = 60 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.58 * 60 | Answer: 34.8 kPa

question: A stream of 2.4 kg/s with specific heat 1.5 kJ/kg-K is heated through 70 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 2.4, cp = 1.5, dT = 70 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 2.4*1.5*70 | Answer: 252 kW

question: A reactor of volume 3.2 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 4.2 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 3.2, Q = 4.2 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 3.2 / 4.2 | Answer: 0.7619 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 1.7e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 2 mm with a concentration difference of 150 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 1.7, L = 2, dC = 150 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (1.7e-9)*150 / (2e-3) | Answer: 127.5 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 7 min and steady-state gain 3.7. For a step input of magnitude 11, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 7, K = 3.7, M = 11 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 3.7 * 11 | Answer: 40.7 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 100 m^2 flies at 130 m/s (air density 0.7 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 1.3. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 100, V = 130, rho = 0.7, CL = 1.3 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.7*(130)^2*100*1.3 / 1000 | Answer: 769 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 70 m^2 flies at 140 m/s (density 0.7 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.06. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 70, V = 140, rho = 0.7, CD = 0.06 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.7*(140)^2*70*0.06 / 1000 | Answer: 28.81 kN

question: A specimen under stress 280 MPa shows an elastic strain of 2e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 280, eps = 2 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 280 / (2e-3) MPa = 140 GPa | Answer: 140 GPa

question: A block of mass 39 kg has a volume of 4.6e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 39, V = 4.6 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 39 / (4.6e-3) | Answer: 8478 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 900 mm is heated through 50 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 23e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 900, dT = 50, al = 23 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 900*23e-6*50 | Answer: 1.035 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 170 ohm, R2 = 80 ohm and R3 = 295 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 170, R2 = 80, R3 = 295 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 80*295 / 170 | Answer: 138.8 ohm

question: Annual demand is 22000 units, ordering cost 170 per order and holding cost 40 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 22000, S = 170, H = 40 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*22000*170 / 40) | Answer: 432.4 units

question: An asset costs 420000 with salvage value 36000 after 20 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 420000, Sv = 36000, n = 20 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (420000 - 36000) / 20 | Answer: 19200 per year

question: A product sells for 160 per unit with variable cost 140 per unit and fixed costs 200000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 160, V = 140, F = 200000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 200000 / (160 - 140) | Answer: 10000 units

question: Find the present worth of 85000 received 6 years from now at an interest rate of 7% per year.
solution: Given: F = 85000, n = 6, i = 7 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 85000 / (1 + 0.07)^6 | Answer: 56639 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.96, 0.99 and 0.97 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.96, r2 = 0.99, r3 = 0.97 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.96*0.99*0.97 | Answer: 0.9219

question: A process produces 27 defective items in a batch of 4500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 27, N = 4500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 27/4500 * 1e6 | Answer: 6000 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -x^3 - x^2 + x - 9 evaluated at x = 1.
For f(x) = -5x^3 + 4x^2 - 7x + 6, find f''(x) at x = -2.
Evaluate the definite integral of (x - 6) dx from x = -4 to x = 4.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = 0x^3/3 + 1x^2/2 + -6x | Evaluate F(4) - F(-4) | Answer: -48
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 3x^2 + 10x - 1 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[7, 9], [-9, 2]].
solution: Given: a = 7, b = 9, c = -9, d = 2 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (7)(2) - (9)(-9) | Answer: 95

question: Find the determinant of [[-4, 3, 0], [1, -1, 1], [-1, -6, 4]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: -23

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[-5, 7], [0, 2]].
solution: Trace tr = -3, Determinant = -10 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 2

question: Solve for x: -2x + -2y = 7 and -6x + -4y = -12.
solution: Determinant = -2*-4 - -2*-6 = -4 | x = (e d - b f) / det = 13 | Answer: x = 13
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 86, 73, 1, 42, 45.
solution: Sum = 247 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 49.4 | Answer: 49.4

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 49, 36, 28, 15, 17.
solution: Mean = 29 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 14.05

question: Find the slope of the line through (7, -6) and (6, 4).
solution: Given: x1 = 7, y1 = -6, x2 = 6, y2 = 4 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (4 - -6) / (6 - 7) | Answer: -10

question: Find the distance between the points (-1, -9) and (7, 9).
solution: Given: x1 = -1, y1 = -9, x2 = 7, y2 = 9 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((8)^2 + (18)^2) | Answer: 19.7 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (-6,-2), (-6,3), (4,-8).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 25 sq units

question: Find the 6th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 16 and common difference -4.
solution: Given: a = 16, d = -4, n = 6 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = 16 + (6 - 1)*-4 | Answer: -4

question: Find the sum of the first 16 terms of an AP with first term 1 and common difference 3.
solution: Given: a = 1, d = 3, n = 16 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 16/2 [2*1 + (16-1)*3] | Answer: 376

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 17000 at 5.2% per annum for 4 years.
solution: Given: P = 17000, R = 5.2, Tt = 4 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 17000 * 5.2 * 4 / 100 | Answer: 3536 currency units

question: Find the amount when 39000 is invested at 10.6% per annum compounded annually for 6 years.
solution: Given: P = 39000, R = 10.6, Tt = 6 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 39000 * (1 + 10.6/100)^6 | Answer: 71383 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (0, 3, 6) and (-5, 6, -2).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (2, -6, -4) and (-4, 6, 5).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 14.7

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (3, -6, 3) and (6, -3, 4).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 33.25 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = 5x^3 - 5x^2 + 3 at x = -3.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-115 with initial guess x0=15, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.9 and ordinates 20, 0, 10, 15, 13, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 498 and 205.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 498 and 205 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 54 and 7.
solution: Given: a = 54, b = 7 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 54*7 / 1 | Answer: 378
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 37 mm carries an axial tensile load of 10 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 35 mm and length 1800 mm carries an axial load of 52 kN. Take E = 200 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 72 mm transmits a torque of 1000 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 72, Tt = 1000 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(1000*1000) / (pi*(72)^3) | Answer: 13.64 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 47 mm and length 700 mm carries a torque of 1600 N-m. With G = 45 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (47)^4 / 32 = 479062 mm^4 | theta = (1600*1000)(700) / (45000 * 479062) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 2.977 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 131 mm wide and 270 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 131, h = 270 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 131*(270)^2 / 6 | Answer: 1591650 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (45 mm x 230 mm) carries a bending moment of 25 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (42 mm x 150 mm) has effective length 2400 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 650 MPa is designed for a working stress of 230 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 650, sw = 230 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 650 / 230 | Answer: 2.826

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 350 mm and wall thickness 6 mm carries an internal pressure of 2.3 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 350, t = 6, P = 2.3 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 2.3*350 / (2*6) | Answer: 67.08 MPa

question: 7.3 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 190 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 7.3, dT = 190 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 7.3 * 0.718 * 190 | Answer: 995.9 kJ

question: 6.1 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 50 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 6.1, dT = 50 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 6.1 * 1.005 * 50 | Answer: 306.5 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 0.5 m^3 at 560 K with mass 2.8 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 0.5, Tk = 560, m = 2.8 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 2.8*0.287*560 / 0.5 | Answer: 900 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 3.4 kg of air expands isothermally at 320 K from volume V1 to 4*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.4, Tk = 320, ratio = 4 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 3.4*0.287*320*ln(4) | Answer: 432.9 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 3 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.24 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 3, D = 0.24 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*3*0.24 / 0.001 | Answer: 720000

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 8.4 m. Taking Cv = 0.95, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 8.4, cv = 0.95 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.95*sqrt(2*9.81*8.4) | Answer: 12.2 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 190 mm) water flows at 3 m/s. It contracts to diameter 110 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 190, d2 = 110, V1 = 3 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 3*(190/110)^2 | Answer: 8.95 m/s

question: Water flows at 2.1 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.3 m and length 150 m. With friction factor f = 0.028, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 17 teeth drives a gear of 119 teeth. If the pinion runs at 900 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 17, z2 = 119, N1 = 900 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 900*17 / 119 | Answer: 128.6 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 560 mm rotates at 1150 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 560, N = 1150 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.56)*1150 / 60 | Answer: 33.72 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 13.3 kW at 1450 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 13.3, N = 1450 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(13.3*1000) / (2*pi*1450) | Answer: 87.59 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 1 kg rotates at radius 0.22 m at 700 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 12300 N/m and mass 9.9 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 12300, m = 9.9 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(12300/9.9) | Answer: 5.61 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 4.2 m^2 and thickness 0.11 m has conductivity k = 22.9 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 40 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 4.2, L = 0.11, k = 22.9, dT = 40 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 22.9*4.2*40 / 0.11 | Answer: 34975 W

question: A surface of area 1.7 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 65 W/m^2-K to surroundings 60 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 1.7, h = 65, dT = 60 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 65*1.7*60 | Answer: 6630 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 70 m/min, feed = 0.24 mm/rev, depth of cut = 3 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 70, f = 0.24, d = 3 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*70*0.24*3 | Answer: 50400 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 220 mm is turned at 600 rpm with a feed of 0.1 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 220, N = 600, f = 0.1 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 220 / (0.1*600) | Answer: 3.667 min

question: A resistor of 5 ohm carries a current of 5.6 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 5, I = 5.6 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 5.6 * 5 | Answer: 28 V

question: Three resistors 80 ohm, 65 ohm and 38 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 80, R2 = 65, R3 = 38 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 80 + 65 + 38 | Answer: 183 ohm

question: Two resistors 80 ohm and 120 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 80, R2 = 120 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 80*120 / (80+120) | Answer: 48 ohm

question: A device draws 1.3 A at 85 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 85, I = 1.3 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 85 * 1.3 | Answer: 110.5 W

question: A current of 11.5 A flows through a 28 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 11.5, R = 28 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (11.5)^2 * 28 | Answer: 3703 W

question: Two capacitors 21.9 uF and 17.6 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 21.9, C2 = 17.6 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 21.9*17.6 / (21.9+17.6) | Answer: 9.758 uF

question: A resistor 81 kohm and capacitor 14.4 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 81, C = 14.4 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (81k)(14.4u) = 1166 ms | Answer: 1166 ms

question: An inductor 477.2 mH is in series with 105 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 477.2, R = 105 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (477.2e-3) / 105 | Answer: 4.545 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 178.6 mH inductor at 850 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 178.6, f = 850 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (850)(178.6e-3) | Answer: 953.9 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 3.7 uF capacitor at 850 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 3.7, f = 850 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (850)(3.7e-6)) | Answer: 50.61 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 76 ohm, XL = 60 ohm and XC = 122 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 76, XL = 60, XC = 122 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(76^2 + (60 - 122)^2) | Answer: 98.08 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 82.8 mH and C = 9 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 82.8, C = 9 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(82.8e-3 * 9e-6)) | Answer: 184.4 Hz

question: A capacitor of 34.6 uF is charged to 170 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 34.6, V = 170 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*34.6e-6*(170)^2 | Answer: 500 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 260 V with 480 primary turns and 250 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 260, N1 = 480, N2 = 250 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 260 * 250/480 | Answer: 135.4 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 340 V and draws an armature current of 53 A. If the armature resistance is 0.53 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 340, Ia = 53, Ra = 0.53 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 340 - 53*0.53 | Answer: 311.9 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 135 A at 415 V (line) with a power factor of 0.9. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 135, VL = 415, pf = 0.9 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*415*135*0.9 / 1000 | Answer: 87.33 kW

question: A load has real power 180 kW and apparent power 185 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 180, S = 185 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 180 / 185 | Answer: 0.973

question: A machine delivers 135 kW output while drawing 182 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 135, Pi = 182 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 135/182 * 100 | Answer: 74.18 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 9 V across R1 = 18 ohm and R2 = 19 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 9, R1 = 18, R2 = 19 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 9*19 / (18+19) | Answer: 4.622 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 210 kohm and Rin = 10 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 210, Rin = 10 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 210 / 10 | Answer: 21

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 60 kohm and Rg = 7 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 60, Rg = 7 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 60/7 | Answer: 9.571

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 5013. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 5013 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(5013) | Answer: 37 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 5.3 m carries a central point load of 55 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.3, W = 55 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 55*5.3 / 4 | Answer: 72.88 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 8.8 m carries a UDL of 35 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 8.8, w = 35 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 35*(8.8)^2 / 8 | Answer: 338.8 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 3.9 m carries a UDL of 22 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.9, w = 22 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 22*(3.9)^2 / 2 | Answer: 167.3 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.6 m carries a point load 45 kN at distance 1.1 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 9.6, a = 1.1, W = 45 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 45*(9.6 - 1.1) / 9.6 | Answer: 39.84 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 7.7 m) carries a central point load 30 kN. With E = 200 GPa and I = 80e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=30000 N, L=7700.0 mm, E=200000 MPa, I=80e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 17.83 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 7 m carries a UDL of 45 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7, w = 45 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 45*(7)^2 / 12 | Answer: 183.8 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 540 mm, clear cover 25 mm and main bars of diameter 20 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 540, c = 25, dia = 20 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 540 - 25 - 20/2 | Answer: 505 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 34.2 m^2 carrying a factored load of 13.4 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 34.2, w = 13.4 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 13.4 * 34.2 | Answer: 458.3 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 4.9 m, unit weight 20 kN/m^3, phi = 32 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 1.5e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1.2, area = 7e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 1.5, i = 1.2, A = 7 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (1.5e-4)*1.2*(7e-3) | Answer: 1260 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.8 m, bed slope 0.002 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.027. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 2.5 m under a head of 0.7 m. Taking Cd = 0.61 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 5.2 m wide carries a discharge of 23.9 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A tank of volume 860 m^3 treats a flow of 30 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 860, Q = 30 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 860 / 30 | Answer: 28.67 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 300 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.23 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 6 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 300, k = 0.23, t = 6 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 300*(1 - e^(-0.23*6)) | Answer: 224.5 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.4, rainfall intensity 90 mm/h over a catchment of 43.4 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.4, i = 90, A = 43.4 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.4*90*43.4 / 360 | Answer: 4.34 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.06 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 660 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.06, M = 660 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 660*(30+0.06)/30 | Answer: 661.3 m

question: Convert the decimal number 3758 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 3758 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: EAE (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 00101000 and 01000000.
solution: XOR: 01101000 | Count of 1s = 3 | Answer: 3
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 300 megabits is sent over a link of 91 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 300, B = 91 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 300 / 91 | Answer: 3.297 s

question: A link has bandwidth 94 Mbps and round-trip time 90 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 94, R = 90 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 94e6 * 90e-3 bits = 8460 kb | Answer: 8460 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.81, cache access time 1 ns and main-memory access time 110 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.81, tc = 1, tm = 110 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.81*1 + (1 - 0.81)*110 | Answer: 21.71 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 472521 elements?
solution: Given: n = 472521 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(472521)) + 1 | Answer: 19

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.017, memory access time 190 ns and page-fault service time 6 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 6 ms = 6000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.017)*190 + 0.017*6000000.0 ns | Answer: 102.2 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 1.9 m^3 at 140 kPa and 530 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 1.9, P = 140, Tk = 530 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (140e3)*1.9 / (8.314*530) | Answer: 60.37 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.27 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 12 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.27, t = 12 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.27*12) | Answer: 0.9608

question: For a reaction with A = 3e10 /s and activation energy 85 kJ/mol at 420 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 3, Ea = 85, Tk = 420 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 3e10 * exp(-85e3 / (8.314*420)) | Answer: 0.8043 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.97 and bottoms xW = 0.06, with relative volatility alpha = 3.5. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.97, xw = 0.06, al = 3.5 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.97/0.03)(0.94/0.06)] / ln(3.5) | Answer: 4.971 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.79 and x = 0.45. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.79, x = 0.45 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.79/0.21) / (0.45/0.55) | Answer: 4.598

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.34 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 115 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.34, Psat = 115 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.34 * 115 | Answer: 39.1 kPa

question: A stream of 5.3 kg/s with specific heat 2 kJ/kg-K is heated through 55 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 5.3, cp = 2, dT = 55 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 5.3*2*55 | Answer: 583 kW

question: A reactor of volume 20 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 0.5 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 20, Q = 0.5 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 20 / 0.5 | Answer: 40 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 1.5e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 4 mm with a concentration difference of 140 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 1.5, L = 4, dC = 140 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (1.5e-9)*140 / (4e-3) | Answer: 52.5 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 5.7 min and steady-state gain 0.6. For a step input of magnitude 6, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 5.7, K = 0.6, M = 6 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 0.6 * 6 | Answer: 3.6 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 115 m^2 flies at 260 m/s (air density 0.7 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.7. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 115, V = 260, rho = 0.7, CL = 0.7 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.7*(260)^2*115*0.7 / 1000 | Answer: 1905 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 95 m^2 flies at 70 m/s (density 1.225 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.03. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 95, V = 70, rho = 1.225, CD = 0.03 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*1.225*(70)^2*95*0.03 / 1000 | Answer: 8.554 kN

question: A block of mass 30 kg has a volume of 0.7e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 30, V = 0.7 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 30 / (0.7e-3) | Answer: 42857 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 1000 mm is heated through 150 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 11e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 1000, dT = 150, al = 11 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 1000*11e-6*150 | Answer: 1.65 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 70 ohm, R2 = 105 ohm and R3 = 160 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 70, R2 = 105, R3 = 160 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 105*160 / 70 | Answer: 240 ohm

question: A measurement reads 9.3 when the true value is 50. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.3, true = 50 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.3 - 50| / 50 * 100 | Answer: 81.4 %

question: Annual demand is 25000 units, ordering cost 120 per order and holding cost 14 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 25000, S = 120, H = 14 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*25000*120 / 14) | Answer: 654.7 units

question: An asset costs 390000 with salvage value 14000 after 18 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 390000, Sv = 14000, n = 18 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (390000 - 14000) / 18 | Answer: 20889 per year

question: A product sells for 190 per unit with variable cost 70 per unit and fixed costs 175000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 190, V = 70, F = 175000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 175000 / (190 - 70) | Answer: 1458 units

question: Find the present worth of 15000 received 7 years from now at an interest rate of 10% per year.
solution: Given: F = 15000, n = 7, i = 10 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 15000 / (1 + 0.1)^7 | Answer: 7697 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.93, 0.97 and 0.93 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.93, r2 = 0.97, r3 = 0.93 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.93*0.97*0.93 | Answer: 0.839

question: A process produces 29 defective items in a batch of 15000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 29, N = 15000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 29/15000 * 1e6 | Answer: 1933 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -x^3 + 4x^2 - 2x + 8 evaluated at x = 5.
For f(x) = x^3 - 6x^2 - 7x - 2, find f''(x) at x = -4.
Evaluate the definite integral of (-x^2 + 2) dx from x = 1 to x = 6.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = -1x^3/3 + 0x^2/2 + 2x | Evaluate F(6) - F(1) | Answer: -61.67
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 5x^2 + 2x - 4 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[9, 3], [-4, 3]].
solution: Given: a = 9, b = 3, c = -4, d = 3 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (9)(3) - (3)(-4) | Answer: 39

question: Find the determinant of [[-6, -2, 6], [5, 2, -1], [-5, 4, 3]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: 140

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[7, -7], [-8, -2]].
solution: Trace tr = 5, Determinant = -70 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 11.23

question: Solve for x: 2x + 3y = -6 and 5x + -1y = 10.
solution: Determinant = 2*-1 - 3*5 = -17 | x = (e d - b f) / det = 1.412 | Answer: x = 1.412

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 53, 96, 65, 41, 47.
solution: Sum = 302 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 60.4 | Answer: 60.4

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 18, 17, 13, 36, 7.
solution: Mean = 18.2 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 10.85

question: Find the slope of the line through (-4, -5) and (-1, 9).
solution: Given: x1 = -4, y1 = -5, x2 = -1, y2 = 9 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (9 - -5) / (-1 - -4) | Answer: 4.667

question: Find the distance between the points (1, 0) and (-3, -9).
solution: Given: x1 = 1, y1 = 0, x2 = -3, y2 = -9 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-4)^2 + (-9)^2) | Answer: 9.849 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (4,6), (-2,-2), (-6,5).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 37 sq units

question: Find the 23th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 12 and common difference 2.
solution: Given: a = 12, d = 2, n = 23 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = 12 + (23 - 1)*2 | Answer: 56

question: Find the sum of the first 39 terms of an AP with first term -14 and common difference -3.
Find the simple interest on a principal of 19000 at 5.3% per annum for 5 years.
solution: Given: P = 19000, R = 5.3, Tt = 5 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 19000 * 5.3 * 5 / 100 | Answer: 5035 currency units

question: Find the amount when 22500 is invested at 10% per annum compounded annually for 5 years.
solution: Given: P = 22500, R = 10, Tt = 5 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 22500 * (1 + 10/100)^5 | Answer: 36236 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (7, -7, -8) and (-2, 0, -2).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (-6, -1, -3) and (2, -4, -3).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 36.51

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (-2, -4, -2) and (2, 1, -2).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 105.8 degrees

question: Find the modulus of the complex number -11 + -12i.
solution: Given: a = -11, b = -12 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((-11)^2 + (-12)^2) | Answer: 16.28

question: Evaluate f(x) = 4x^3 + x^2 + 4 at x = 4.
solution: Given: a = 4, b = 1, c = 0, d = 4, x0 = 4 | Formula: f(x0) = a x0^3 + b x0^2 + c x0 + d | Substitute: f(4) = 4(4)^3 + 1(4)^2 + 0(4) + 4 | Answer: 276

question: Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-139 with initial guess x0=5, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.8 and ordinates 3, 4, 1, 11, 5, estimate the integral.

solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 433 and 126 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 74 and 35.
solution: Given: a = 74, b = 35 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 74*35 / 1 | Answer: 2590

question: A circular rod of diameter 19 mm carries an axial tensile load of 113 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 16 mm and length 2000 mm carries an axial load of 30 kN. Take E = 210 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 62 mm transmits a torque of 2200 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 62, Tt = 2200 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(2200*1000) / (pi*(62)^3) | Answer: 47.01 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 31 mm and length 900 mm carries a torque of 1650 N-m. With G = 80 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (31)^4 / 32 = 90666 mm^4 | theta = (1650*1000)(900) / (80000 * 90666) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 11.73 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 56 mm wide and 230 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 56, h = 230 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 56*(230)^2 / 6 | Answer: 493733 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (103 mm x 180 mm) carries a bending moment of 20 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (55 mm x 90 mm) has effective length 2000 mm and E = 200 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).

question: A component of ultimate strength 720 MPa is designed for a working stress of 240 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 720, sw = 240 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 720 / 240 | Answer: 3

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 750 mm and wall thickness 15 mm carries an internal pressure of 1.7 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 750, t = 15, P = 1.7 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 1.7*750 / (2*15) | Answer: 42.5 MPa

question: 5.5 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 140 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 5.5, dT = 140 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 5.5 * 0.718 * 140 | Answer: 552.9 kJ

question: 5.3 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 110 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 5.3, dT = 110 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 5.3 * 1.005 * 110 | Answer: 585.9 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 2.8 m^3 at 590 K with mass 2.5 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 2.8, Tk = 590, m = 2.5 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 2.5*0.287*590 / 2.8 | Answer: 151.2 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 3.7 kg of air expands isothermally at 480 K from volume V1 to 4*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.7, Tk = 480, ratio = 4 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 3.7*0.287*480*ln(4) | Answer: 706.6 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 3.6 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.24 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 3.6, D = 0.24 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*3.6*0.24 / 0.001 | Answer: 864000

question: Water flows at 0.7 m/s through a pipe of diameter 80 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 11.5 m. Taking Cv = 0.95, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 11.5, cv = 0.95 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.95*sqrt(2*9.81*11.5) | Answer: 14.27 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 240 mm) water flows at 1.1 m/s. It contracts to diameter 70 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 240, d2 = 70, V1 = 1.1 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 1.1*(240/70)^2 | Answer: 12.93 m/s

question: Water flows at 1.4 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.22 m and length 60 m. With friction factor f = 0.033, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 31 teeth drives a gear of 100 teeth. If the pinion runs at 300 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 31, z2 = 100, N1 = 300 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 300*31 / 100 | Answer: 93 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 360 mm rotates at 1500 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 360, N = 1500 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.36)*1500 / 60 | Answer: 28.27 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 11.9 kW at 1500 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 11.9, N = 1500 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(11.9*1000) / (2*pi*1500) | Answer: 75.76 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 8.7 kg rotates at radius 0.6 m at 550 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 16200 N/m and mass 14 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 16200, m = 14 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(16200/14) | Answer: 5.414 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 5.9 m^2 and thickness 0.37 m has conductivity k = 37.3 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 130 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 5.9, L = 0.37, k = 37.3, dT = 130 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 37.3*5.9*130 / 0.37 | Answer: 77322 W

question: A surface of area 2.5 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 165 W/m^2-K to surroundings 70 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 2.5, h = 165, dT = 70 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 165*2.5*70 | Answer: 28875 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 210 m/min, feed = 0.18 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2.5 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 210, f = 0.18, d = 2.5 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*210*0.18*2.5 | Answer: 94500 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 470 mm is turned at 750 rpm with a feed of 0.16 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 470, N = 750, f = 0.16 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 470 / (0.16*750) | Answer: 3.917 min

question: A resistor of 81 ohm carries a current of 0.9 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 81, I = 0.9 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 0.9 * 81 | Answer: 72.9 V

question: Three resistors 65 ohm, 94 ohm and 24 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 65, R2 = 94, R3 = 24 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 65 + 94 + 24 | Answer: 183 ohm

question: Two resistors 100 ohm and 69 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 100, R2 = 69 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 100*69 / (100+69) | Answer: 40.83 ohm

question: A device draws 12 A at 35 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 35, I = 12 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 35 * 12 | Answer: 420 W

question: A current of 9.1 A flows through a 138 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 9.1, R = 138 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (9.1)^2 * 138 | Answer: 11428 W

question: Two capacitors 14.2 uF and 11 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 14.2, C2 = 11 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 14.2*11 / (14.2+11) | Answer: 6.198 uF

question: A resistor 40 kohm and capacitor 6.9 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 40, C = 6.9 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (40k)(6.9u) = 276 ms | Answer: 276 ms

question: An inductor 282.6 mH is in series with 173 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 282.6, R = 173 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (282.6e-3) / 173 | Answer: 1.634 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 25.3 mH inductor at 150 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 25.3, f = 150 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (150)(25.3e-3) | Answer: 23.84 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 8.4 uF capacitor at 370 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 8.4, f = 370 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (370)(8.4e-6)) | Answer: 51.21 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 90 ohm, XL = 86 ohm and XC = 53 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 90, XL = 86, XC = 53 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(90^2 + (86 - 53)^2) | Answer: 95.86 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 94.6 mH and C = 7 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 94.6, C = 7 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(94.6e-3 * 7e-6)) | Answer: 195.6 Hz

question: A capacitor of 66.4 uF is charged to 250 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 66.4, V = 250 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*66.4e-6*(250)^2 | Answer: 2075 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 430 V with 200 primary turns and 280 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 430, N1 = 200, N2 = 280 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 430 * 280/200 | Answer: 602 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 220 V and draws an armature current of 56 A. If the armature resistance is 0.11 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 220, Ia = 56, Ra = 0.11 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 220 - 56*0.11 | Answer: 213.8 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 10 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.81. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 10, VL = 400, pf = 0.81 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*400*10*0.81 / 1000 | Answer: 5.612 kW

question: A load has real power 60 kW and apparent power 120 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 60, S = 120 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 60 / 120 | Answer: 0.5

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 20 V across R1 = 2 ohm and R2 = 45 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 20, R1 = 2, R2 = 45 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 20*45 / (2+45) | Answer: 19.15 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 10 kohm and Rin = 40 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 10, Rin = 40 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 10 / 40 | Answer: 0.25

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 40 kohm and Rg = 13 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 40, Rg = 13 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 40/13 | Answer: 4.077

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 5469. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 5469 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(5469) | Answer: 37.38 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.3 m carries a central point load of 25 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6.3, W = 25 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 25*6.3 / 4 | Answer: 39.38 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 3 m carries a point load 40 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3, W = 40 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 40*3 | Answer: 120 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 4.6 m carries a UDL of 10 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.6, w = 10 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 10*(4.6)^2 / 2 | Answer: 105.8 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.2 m carries a point load 100 kN at distance 2.4 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 9.2, a = 2.4, W = 100 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 100*(9.2 - 2.4) / 9.2 | Answer: 73.91 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 7.4 m) carries a central point load 60 kN. With E = 25 GPa and I = 530e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=60000 N, L=7400.0 mm, E=25000 MPa, I=530e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 38.23 mm

question: An RC beam has overall depth 450 mm, clear cover 50 mm and main bars of diameter 12 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 450, c = 50, dia = 12 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 450 - 50 - 12/2 | Answer: 394 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 30.8 m^2 carrying a factored load of 17.4 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 30.8, w = 17.4 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 17.4 * 30.8 | Answer: 535.9 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 4.6 m, unit weight 18 kN/m^3, phi = 36 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 2.7e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1, area = 5.8e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 2.7, i = 1, A = 5.8 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (2.7e-4)*1*(5.8e-3) | Answer: 1566 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 2.1 m, bed slope 0.001 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.024. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 1 m under a head of 0.8 m. Taking Cd = 0.6 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
solution: Given: L = 1, H = 0.8, cd = 0.6 | Formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2) | Substitute: Q = (2/3)*0.6*sqrt(2*9.81)*1*(0.8)^1.5 | Answer: 1.268 m^3/s
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 5.9 m wide carries a discharge of 14.1 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A tank of volume 280 m^3 treats a flow of 110 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 280, Q = 110 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 280 / 110 | Answer: 2.545 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 240 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.33 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 3 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 240, k = 0.33, t = 3 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 240*(1 - e^(-0.33*3)) | Answer: 150.8 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.6, rainfall intensity 60 mm/h over a catchment of 35.2 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.6, i = 60, A = 35.2 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.6*60*35.2 / 360 | Answer: 3.52 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.08 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 100 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.08, M = 100 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 100*(20+0.08)/20 | Answer: 100.4 m

question: Convert the decimal number 1336 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 1336 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 538 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 00110101 and 11110000.
solution: XOR: 11000101 | Count of 1s = 4 | Answer: 4
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 220 megabits is sent over a link of 52 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 220, B = 52 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 220 / 52 | Answer: 4.231 s

question: A link has bandwidth 81 Mbps and round-trip time 200 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 81, R = 200 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 81e6 * 200e-3 bits = 16200 kb | Answer: 16200 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.88, cache access time 5 ns and main-memory access time 60 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.88, tc = 5, tm = 60 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.88*5 + (1 - 0.88)*60 | Answer: 11.6 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 285796 elements?
solution: Given: n = 285796 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(285796)) + 1 | Answer: 19

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.004, memory access time 170 ns and page-fault service time 8 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 8 ms = 8000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.004)*170 + 0.004*8000000.0 ns | Answer: 32.17 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 1.2 m^3 at 420 kPa and 430 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 1.2, P = 420, Tk = 430 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (420e3)*1.2 / (8.314*430) | Answer: 141 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.32 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 2 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.32, t = 2 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.32*2) | Answer: 0.4727

question: For a reaction with A = 3e10 /s and activation energy 70 kJ/mol at 350 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 3, Ea = 70, Tk = 350 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 3e10 * exp(-70e3 / (8.314*350)) | Answer: 1.071 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.93 and bottoms xW = 0.03, with relative volatility alpha = 3.3. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.93, xw = 0.03, al = 3.3 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.93/0.07)(0.97/0.03)] / ln(3.3) | Answer: 5.078 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.55 and x = 0.38. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.55, x = 0.38 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.55/0.45) / (0.38/0.62) | Answer: 1.994

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.61 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 65 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.61, Psat = 65 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.61 * 65 | Answer: 39.65 kPa

question: A stream of 4.3 kg/s with specific heat 1.9 kJ/kg-K is heated through 75 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 4.3, cp = 1.9, dT = 75 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 4.3*1.9*75 | Answer: 612.8 kW

question: A reactor of volume 17.9 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 1.6 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 17.9, Q = 1.6 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 17.9 / 1.6 | Answer: 11.19 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 1.4e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 3 mm with a concentration difference of 100 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 1.4, L = 3, dC = 100 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (1.4e-9)*100 / (3e-3) | Answer: 46.67 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 3.9 min and steady-state gain 2. For a step input of magnitude 4, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 3.9, K = 2, M = 4 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 2 * 4 | Answer: 8 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 15 m^2 flies at 70 m/s (air density 1 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 1.3. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 15, V = 70, rho = 1, CL = 1.3 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1*(70)^2*15*1.3 / 1000 | Answer: 47.77 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 95 m^2 flies at 130 m/s (density 0.4 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.05. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 95, V = 130, rho = 0.4, CD = 0.05 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.4*(130)^2*95*0.05 / 1000 | Answer: 16.05 kN

question: A specimen under stress 270 MPa shows an elastic strain of 0.7e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 270, eps = 0.7 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 270 / (0.7e-3) MPa = 385.7 GPa | Answer: 385.7 GPa

question: A block of mass 21 kg has a volume of 0.7e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 21, V = 0.7 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 21 / (0.7e-3) | Answer: 30000 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 2600 mm is heated through 75 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 23e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 2600, dT = 75, al = 23 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 2600*23e-6*75 | Answer: 4.485 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 95 ohm, R2 = 140 ohm and R3 = 380 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 95, R2 = 140, R3 = 380 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 140*380 / 95 | Answer: 560 ohm

question: Annual demand is 1500 units, ordering cost 90 per order and holding cost 34 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 1500, S = 90, H = 34 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*1500*90 / 34) | Answer: 89.11 units

question: An asset costs 210000 with salvage value 34000 after 11 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 210000, Sv = 34000, n = 11 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (210000 - 34000) / 11 | Answer: 16000 per year

question: A product sells for 390 per unit with variable cost 160 per unit and fixed costs 140000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 390, V = 160, F = 140000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 140000 / (390 - 160) | Answer: 608.7 units

question: Find the present worth of 200000 received 9 years from now at an interest rate of 11% per year.
solution: Given: F = 200000, n = 9, i = 11 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 200000 / (1 + 0.11)^9 | Answer: 78185 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.97, 0.91 and 0.97 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.97, r2 = 0.91, r3 = 0.97 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.97*0.91*0.97 | Answer: 0.8562

question: A process produces 39 defective items in a batch of 6000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 39, N = 6000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 39/6000 * 1e6 | Answer: 6500 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = x^3 - 8x^2 + 7x - 7 evaluated at x = -3.
For f(x) = -5x^3 - 4x^2 - 7x - 6, find f''(x) at x = -4.
Evaluate the definite integral of (x^2 + 4x - 2) dx from x = 0 to x = 7.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = 1x^3/3 + 4x^2/2 + -2x | Evaluate F(7) - F(0) | Answer: 198.3
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of x^2 + 11x - 10 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[3, -8], [-9, 0]].
solution: Given: a = 3, b = -8, c = -9, d = 0 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (3)(0) - (-8)(-9) | Answer: -72

question: Find the determinant of [[4, 5, 4], [-3, -6, -6], [1, -5, 4]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: -102

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[-6, 8], [3, 4]].
solution: Trace tr = -2, Determinant = -48 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 6

question: Solve for x: -2x + -5y = 9 and -1x + -3y = -10.
solution: Determinant = -2*-3 - -5*-1 = 1 | x = (e d - b f) / det = -77 | Answer: x = -77
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 21, 56, 36, 94, 82.
solution: Sum = 289 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 57.8 | Answer: 57.8

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 1, 36, 49, 5, 17.
solution: Mean = 21.6 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 20.49

question: Find the slope of the line through (-4, 6) and (1, 8).
solution: Given: x1 = -4, y1 = 6, x2 = 1, y2 = 8 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (8 - 6) / (1 - -4) | Answer: 0.4

question: Find the distance between the points (-1, -5) and (-8, 7).
solution: Given: x1 = -1, y1 = -5, x2 = -8, y2 = 7 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-7)^2 + (12)^2) | Answer: 13.89 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (-5,-3), (3,-1), (8,7).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 27 sq units

question: Find the 31th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 3 and common difference 4.
