question: Find the sum of the first 18 terms of an AP with first term 9 and common difference 2.
solution: Given: a = 9, d = 2, n = 18 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 18/2 [2*9 + (18-1)*2] | Answer: 468

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 43000 at 13.6% per annum for 1 years.
solution: Given: P = 43000, R = 13.6, Tt = 1 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 43000 * 13.6 * 1 / 100 | Answer: 5848 currency units

question: Find the amount when 3500 is invested at 9.6% per annum compounded annually for 2 years.
solution: Given: P = 3500, R = 9.6, Tt = 2 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 3500 * (1 + 9.6/100)^2 | Answer: 4204 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (6, 0, 3) and (-3, 2, -3).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (2, -4, -2) and (5, 5, 0).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 33.17

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (-1, -6, 2) and (0, -3, 3).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 27.94 degrees

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number -5 + -10i.
solution: Given: a = -5, b = -10 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(-10, -5) | Answer: -116.6 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -x^3 + 7x^2 - 6x + 9 at x = 1.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-104 with initial guess x0=7, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.3 and ordinates 19, 2, 15, 15, 3, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 276 and 278.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 276 and 278 | Answer: GCD = 2

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 37 and 64.
solution: Given: a = 37, b = 64 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 37*64 / 1 | Answer: 2368
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 45 mm carries an axial tensile load of 100 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 32 mm and length 2000 mm carries an axial load of 32 kN. Take E = 200 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 77 mm transmits a torque of 2200 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 77, Tt = 2200 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(2200*1000) / (pi*(77)^3) | Answer: 24.54 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 31 mm and length 1300 mm carries a torque of 650 N-m. With G = 45 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (31)^4 / 32 = 90666 mm^4 | theta = (650*1000)(1300) / (45000 * 90666) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 11.87 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 55 mm wide and 100 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 55, h = 100 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 55*(100)^2 / 6 | Answer: 91667 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (97 mm x 210 mm) carries a bending moment of 39 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (40 mm x 160 mm) has effective length 2800 mm and E = 200 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 770 MPa is designed for a working stress of 160 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 770, sw = 160 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 770 / 160 | Answer: 4.812

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1050 mm and wall thickness 16 mm carries an internal pressure of 0.9 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1050, t = 16, P = 0.9 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 0.9*1050 / (2*16) | Answer: 29.53 MPa

question: 5.8 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 45 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 5.8, dT = 45 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 5.8 * 0.718 * 45 | Answer: 187.4 kJ

question: 3 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 200 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3, dT = 200 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 3 * 1.005 * 200 | Answer: 603 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 1.3 m^3 at 600 K with mass 2.1 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 1.3, Tk = 600, m = 2.1 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 2.1*0.287*600 / 1.3 | Answer: 278.2 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 1.9 kg of air expands isothermally at 390 K from volume V1 to 2*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1.9, Tk = 390, ratio = 2 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 1.9*0.287*390*ln(2) | Answer: 147.4 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 2.5 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.29 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 2.5, D = 0.29 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*2.5*0.29 / 0.001 | Answer: 725000

question: Water flows at 3.1 m/s through a pipe of diameter 70 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 19.4 m. Taking Cv = 0.96, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 19.4, cv = 0.96 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.96*sqrt(2*9.81*19.4) | Answer: 18.73 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 220 mm) water flows at 1.8 m/s. It contracts to diameter 90 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 220, d2 = 90, V1 = 1.8 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 1.8*(220/90)^2 | Answer: 10.76 m/s

question: Water flows at 2.2 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.19 m and length 350 m. With friction factor f = 0.038, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 36 teeth drives a gear of 57 teeth. If the pinion runs at 300 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 36, z2 = 57, N1 = 300 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 300*36 / 57 | Answer: 189.5 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 330 mm rotates at 800 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 330, N = 800 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.33)*800 / 60 | Answer: 13.82 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 20.7 kW at 1150 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 20.7, N = 1150 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(20.7*1000) / (2*pi*1150) | Answer: 171.9 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 5.5 kg rotates at radius 0.36 m at 1000 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 3000 N/m and mass 10.8 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 3000, m = 10.8 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(3000/10.8) | Answer: 2.653 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 6.8 m^2 and thickness 0.15 m has conductivity k = 10.4 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 110 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 6.8, L = 0.15, k = 10.4, dT = 110 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 10.4*6.8*110 / 0.15 | Answer: 51861 W

question: A surface of area 5.2 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 15 W/m^2-K to surroundings 95 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 5.2, h = 15, dT = 95 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 15*5.2*95 | Answer: 7410 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 110 m/min, feed = 0.16 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2.8 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 110, f = 0.16, d = 2.8 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*110*0.16*2.8 | Answer: 49280 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 210 mm is turned at 1100 rpm with a feed of 0.1 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 210, N = 1100, f = 0.1 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 210 / (0.1*1100) | Answer: 1.909 min

question: A resistor of 172 ohm carries a current of 5.1 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 172, I = 5.1 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 5.1 * 172 | Answer: 877.2 V

question: Three resistors 24 ohm, 47 ohm and 51 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 24, R2 = 47, R3 = 51 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 24 + 47 + 51 | Answer: 122 ohm

question: Two resistors 57 ohm and 27 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 57, R2 = 27 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 57*27 / (57+27) | Answer: 18.32 ohm

question: A device draws 5.3 A at 145 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 145, I = 5.3 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 145 * 5.3 | Answer: 768.5 W

question: A current of 8.1 A flows through a 75 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 8.1, R = 75 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (8.1)^2 * 75 | Answer: 4921 W

question: Two capacitors 42 uF and 38.3 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 42, C2 = 38.3 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 42*38.3 / (42+38.3) | Answer: 20.03 uF

question: A resistor 48 kohm and capacitor 10.4 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 48, C = 10.4 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (48k)(10.4u) = 499.2 ms | Answer: 499.2 ms

question: An inductor 98.2 mH is in series with 141 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 98.2, R = 141 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (98.2e-3) / 141 | Answer: 0.6965 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 89.2 mH inductor at 780 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 89.2, f = 780 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (780)(89.2e-3) | Answer: 437.2 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 6.5 uF capacitor at 730 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 6.5, f = 730 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (730)(6.5e-6)) | Answer: 33.54 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 57 ohm, XL = 72 ohm and XC = 97 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 57, XL = 72, XC = 97 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(57^2 + (72 - 97)^2) | Answer: 62.24 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 76.4 mH and C = 2.1 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 76.4, C = 2.1 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(76.4e-3 * 2.1e-6)) | Answer: 397.3 Hz

question: A capacitor of 80.5 uF is charged to 220 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 80.5, V = 220 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*80.5e-6*(220)^2 | Answer: 1948 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 170 V with 910 primary turns and 380 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 170, N1 = 910, N2 = 380 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 170 * 380/910 | Answer: 70.99 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 290 V and draws an armature current of 5 A. If the armature resistance is 0.66 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 290, Ia = 5, Ra = 0.66 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 290 - 5*0.66 | Answer: 286.7 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 25 A at 415 V (line) with a power factor of 0.73. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 25, VL = 415, pf = 0.73 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*415*25*0.73 / 1000 | Answer: 13.12 kW

question: A load has real power 50 kW and apparent power 120 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 50, S = 120 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 50 / 120 | Answer: 0.4167

question: A machine delivers 20 kW output while drawing 32 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 20, Pi = 32 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 20/32 * 100 | Answer: 62.5 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 21 V across R1 = 6 ohm and R2 = 14 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 21, R1 = 6, R2 = 14 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 21*14 / (6+14) | Answer: 14.7 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 220 kohm and Rin = 26 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 220, Rin = 26 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 220 / 26 | Answer: 8.462

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 90 kohm and Rg = 44 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 90, Rg = 44 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 90/44 | Answer: 3.045

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 3238. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 3238 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(3238) | Answer: 35.1 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 7.6 m carries a central point load of 45 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7.6, W = 45 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 45*7.6 / 4 | Answer: 85.5 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 7.7 m carries a UDL of 25 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7.7, w = 25 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 25*(7.7)^2 / 8 | Answer: 185.3 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.6 m carries a point load 70 kN at distance 1.3 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 4.6, a = 1.3, W = 70 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 70*(4.6 - 1.3) / 4.6 | Answer: 50.22 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 7.8 m) carries a central point load 65 kN. With E = 25 GPa and I = 290e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=65000 N, L=7800.0 mm, E=25000 MPa, I=290e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 88.64 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 5.8 m carries a UDL of 39 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.8, w = 39 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 39*(5.8)^2 / 12 | Answer: 109.3 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 310 mm, clear cover 25 mm and main bars of diameter 12 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 310, c = 25, dia = 12 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 310 - 25 - 12/2 | Answer: 279 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 12 m^2 carrying a factored load of 11.9 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 12, w = 11.9 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 11.9 * 12 | Answer: 142.8 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 5.7 m, unit weight 17 kN/m^3, phi = 33 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 3e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1.3, area = 2.8e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 3, i = 1.3, A = 2.8 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (3e-4)*1.3*(2.8e-3) | Answer: 1092 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 2.4 m, bed slope 0.007 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.028. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 1.8 m under a head of 0.3 m. Taking Cd = 0.63 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 4.3 m wide carries a discharge of 7.9 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A tank of volume 340 m^3 treats a flow of 155 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 340, Q = 155 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 340 / 155 | Answer: 2.194 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 320 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.31 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 8 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 320, k = 0.31, t = 8 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 320*(1 - e^(-0.31*8)) | Answer: 293.2 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.48, rainfall intensity 115 mm/h over a catchment of 16 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.48, i = 115, A = 16 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.48*115*16 / 360 | Answer: 2.453 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.08 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 160 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.08, M = 160 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 160*(30+0.08)/30 | Answer: 160.4 m

question: Convert the decimal number 664 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 664 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 298 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 11001001 and 11100100.
solution: XOR: 00101101 | Count of 1s = 4 | Answer: 4
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 700 megabits is sent over a link of 19 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 700, B = 19 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 700 / 19 | Answer: 36.84 s

question: A link has bandwidth 3 Mbps and round-trip time 40 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 3, R = 40 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 3e6 * 40e-3 bits = 120 kb | Answer: 120 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.91, cache access time 5 ns and main-memory access time 80 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.91, tc = 5, tm = 80 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.91*5 + (1 - 0.91)*80 | Answer: 11.75 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 750130 elements?
solution: Given: n = 750130 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(750130)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.006, memory access time 180 ns and page-fault service time 5 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 5 ms = 5000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.006)*180 + 0.006*5000000.0 ns | Answer: 30.18 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 0.3 m^3 at 220 kPa and 580 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 0.3, P = 220, Tk = 580 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (220e3)*0.3 / (8.314*580) | Answer: 13.69 mol

question: For a reaction with A = 7e10 /s and activation energy 65 kJ/mol at 470 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 7, Ea = 65, Tk = 470 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 7e10 * exp(-65e3 / (8.314*470)) | Answer: 4177 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.96 and bottoms xW = 0.04, with relative volatility alpha = 3.4. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.96, xw = 0.04, al = 3.4 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.96/0.04)(0.96/0.04)] / ln(3.4) | Answer: 5.194 stages

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.79 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 50 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.79, Psat = 50 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.79 * 50 | Answer: 39.5 kPa

question: A stream of 5.8 kg/s with specific heat 1.2 kJ/kg-K is heated through 65 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 5.8, cp = 1.2, dT = 65 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 5.8*1.2*65 | Answer: 452.4 kW

question: A reactor of volume 16 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 2.6 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 16, Q = 2.6 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 16 / 2.6 | Answer: 6.154 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 1.6e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 2 mm with a concentration difference of 30 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 1.6, L = 2, dC = 30 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (1.6e-9)*30 / (2e-3) | Answer: 24 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 1.8 min and steady-state gain 0.6. For a step input of magnitude 2, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 1.8, K = 0.6, M = 2 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 0.6 * 2 | Answer: 1.2 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 25 m^2 flies at 90 m/s (air density 0.7 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.5. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 25, V = 90, rho = 0.7, CL = 0.5 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.7*(90)^2*25*0.5 / 1000 | Answer: 35.44 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 115 m^2 flies at 250 m/s (density 1 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.12. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 115, V = 250, rho = 1, CD = 0.12 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*1*(250)^2*115*0.12 / 1000 | Answer: 431.2 kN

question: A block of mass 44 kg has a volume of 5.6e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 44, V = 5.6 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 44 / (5.6e-3) | Answer: 7857 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 2600 mm is heated through 30 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 11e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 2600, dT = 30, al = 11 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 2600*11e-6*30 | Answer: 0.858 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 170 ohm, R2 = 145 ohm and R3 = 490 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 170, R2 = 145, R3 = 490 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 145*490 / 170 | Answer: 417.9 ohm

question: Annual demand is 32000 units, ordering cost 250 per order and holding cost 21 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 32000, S = 250, H = 21 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*32000*250 / 21) | Answer: 872.9 units

question: An asset costs 210000 with salvage value 8000 after 15 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 210000, Sv = 8000, n = 15 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (210000 - 8000) / 15 | Answer: 13467 per year

question: A product sells for 200 per unit with variable cost 30 per unit and fixed costs 35000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 200, V = 30, F = 35000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 35000 / (200 - 30) | Answer: 205.9 units

question: Find the present worth of 150000 received 4 years from now at an interest rate of 8% per year.
solution: Given: F = 150000, n = 4, i = 8 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 150000 / (1 + 0.08)^4 | Answer: 110254 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.91, 0.91 and 0.9 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.91, r2 = 0.91, r3 = 0.9 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.91*0.91*0.9 | Answer: 0.7453

question: A process produces 28 defective items in a batch of 1000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 28, N = 1000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 28/1000 * 1e6 | Answer: 28000 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -2x^3 + 4x^2 - 8x - 5 evaluated at x = 2.
For f(x) = 4x^3 - 5x^2 - 9x - 9, find f''(x) at x = 2.
Evaluate the definite integral of (x^2 + 2x - 8) dx from x = 0 to x = 7.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = 1x^3/3 + 2x^2/2 + -8x | Evaluate F(7) - F(0) | Answer: 107.3
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 4x^2 + 7x - 4 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[-7, -6], [-4, 7]].
solution: Given: a = -7, b = -6, c = -4, d = 7 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (-7)(7) - (-6)(-4) | Answer: -73

question: Find the determinant of [[-4, 0, -2], [0, -1, -2], [5, -5, 6]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: 54

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[-7, -8], [-6, 8]].
solution: Trace tr = 1, Determinant = -104 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 10.71

question: Solve for x: -2x + 6y = -11 and -3x + 3y = -9.
solution: Determinant = -2*3 - 6*-3 = 12 | x = (e d - b f) / det = 1.75 | Answer: x = 1.75
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 43, 19, 62, 38, 69.
solution: Sum = 231 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 46.2 | Answer: 46.2

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 29, 14, 8, 47, 23.
solution: Mean = 24.2 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 15.09

question: Find the slope of the line through (0, 1) and (9, -9).
solution: Given: x1 = 0, y1 = 1, x2 = 9, y2 = -9 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (-9 - 1) / (9 - 0) | Answer: -1.111

question: Find the distance between the points (9, 2) and (9, -5).
solution: Given: x1 = 9, y1 = 2, x2 = 9, y2 = -5 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((0)^2 + (-7)^2) | Answer: 7 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (8,-8), (2,6), (-3,4).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 41 sq units

question: Find the 18th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -14 and common difference -2.
solution: Given: a = -14, d = -2, n = 18 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -14 + (18 - 1)*-2 | Answer: -48

question: Find the sum of the first 17 terms of an AP with first term 9 and common difference -7.
solution: Given: a = 9, d = -7, n = 17 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 17/2 [2*9 + (17-1)*-7] | Answer: -799

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 48500 at 12.7% per annum for 7 years.
solution: Given: P = 48500, R = 12.7, Tt = 7 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 48500 * 12.7 * 7 / 100 | Answer: 43116 currency units

question: Find the amount when 1000 is invested at 11.3% per annum compounded annually for 2 years.
solution: Given: P = 1000, R = 11.3, Tt = 2 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 1000 * (1 + 11.3/100)^2 | Answer: 1239 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (5, 2, -5) and (-3, 3, -3).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (4, -4, -2) and (4, 2, 2).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 29.12

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (-1, 3, -1) and (-2, 4, -6).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 36.31 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -5x^3 + 4x^2 + 9x + 7 at x = 0.
solution: Given: a = -5, b = 4, c = 9, d = 7, x0 = 0 | Formula: f(x0) = a x0^3 + b x0^2 + c x0 + d | Substitute: f(0) = -5(0)^3 + 4(0)^2 + 9(0) + 7 | Answer: 7

question: Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-61 with initial guess x0=10, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.9 and ordinates 20, 17, 15, 20, 13, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 462 and 294.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 462 and 294 | Answer: GCD = 42

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 32 and 39.
solution: Given: a = 32, b = 39 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 32*39 / 1 | Answer: 1248
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 35 mm carries an axial tensile load of 97 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 14 mm and length 2500 mm carries an axial load of 76 kN. Take E = 210 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 66 mm transmits a torque of 1750 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 66, Tt = 1750 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(1750*1000) / (pi*(66)^3) | Answer: 31 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 56 mm and length 1500 mm carries a torque of 1500 N-m. With G = 77 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (56)^4 / 32 = 965499 mm^4 | theta = (1500*1000)(1500) / (77000 * 965499) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 1.734 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 53 mm wide and 130 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 53, h = 130 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 53*(130)^2 / 6 | Answer: 149283 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (117 mm x 120 mm) carries a bending moment of 23 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (70 mm x 130 mm) has effective length 3300 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 390 MPa is designed for a working stress of 120 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 390, sw = 120 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 390 / 120 | Answer: 3.25

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 900 mm and wall thickness 19 mm carries an internal pressure of 1.8 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 900, t = 19, P = 1.8 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 1.8*900 / (2*19) | Answer: 42.63 MPa

question: 4.3 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 125 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.3, dT = 125 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 4.3 * 0.718 * 125 | Answer: 385.9 kJ

question: 3.6 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 75 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.6, dT = 75 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 3.6 * 1.005 * 75 | Answer: 271.3 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 1.2 m^3 at 420 K with mass 1.1 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 1.2, Tk = 420, m = 1.1 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 1.1*0.287*420 / 1.2 | Answer: 110.5 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 2.7 kg of air expands isothermally at 300 K from volume V1 to 2*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.7, Tk = 300, ratio = 2 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 2.7*0.287*300*ln(2) | Answer: 161.1 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 1.3 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.15 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 1.3, D = 0.15 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*1.3*0.15 / 0.001 | Answer: 195000

question: Water flows at 1 m/s through a pipe of diameter 180 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 3.4 m. Taking Cv = 0.95, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 3.4, cv = 0.95 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.95*sqrt(2*9.81*3.4) | Answer: 7.759 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 210 mm) water flows at 1.5 m/s. It contracts to diameter 130 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
Water flows at 3.1 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.44 m and length 430 m. With friction factor f = 0.028, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 27 teeth drives a gear of 56 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1300 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 27, z2 = 56, N1 = 1300 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1300*27 / 56 | Answer: 626.8 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 560 mm rotates at 950 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 560, N = 950 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.56)*950 / 60 | Answer: 27.86 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 33.1 kW at 950 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 33.1, N = 950 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(33.1*1000) / (2*pi*950) | Answer: 332.7 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 8.4 kg rotates at radius 0.28 m at 200 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 20000 N/m and mass 9.7 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 20000, m = 9.7 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(20000/9.7) | Answer: 7.227 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 5.6 m^2 and thickness 0.3 m has conductivity k = 12.4 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 200 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 5.6, L = 0.3, k = 12.4, dT = 200 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 12.4*5.6*200 / 0.3 | Answer: 46293 W

question: A surface of area 0.7 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 185 W/m^2-K to surroundings 40 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 0.7, h = 185, dT = 40 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 185*0.7*40 | Answer: 5180 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 60 m/min, feed = 0.12 mm/rev, depth of cut = 0.9 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 60, f = 0.12, d = 0.9 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*60*0.12*0.9 | Answer: 6480 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 400 mm is turned at 450 rpm with a feed of 0.17 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 400, N = 450, f = 0.17 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 400 / (0.17*450) | Answer: 5.229 min

question: A resistor of 11 ohm carries a current of 0.7 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 11, I = 0.7 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 0.7 * 11 | Answer: 7.7 V

question: Three resistors 17 ohm, 48 ohm and 94 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 17, R2 = 48, R3 = 94 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 17 + 48 + 94 | Answer: 159 ohm

question: Two resistors 79 ohm and 88 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 79, R2 = 88 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 79*88 / (79+88) | Answer: 41.63 ohm

question: A device draws 8.2 A at 45 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 45, I = 8.2 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 45 * 8.2 | Answer: 369 W

question: A current of 6.4 A flows through a 105 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 6.4, R = 105 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (6.4)^2 * 105 | Answer: 4301 W

question: Two capacitors 25.1 uF and 37.7 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 25.1, C2 = 37.7 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 25.1*37.7 / (25.1+37.7) | Answer: 15.07 uF

question: A resistor 2 kohm and capacitor 17.4 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 2, C = 17.4 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (2k)(17.4u) = 34.8 ms | Answer: 34.8 ms

question: An inductor 433.7 mH is in series with 132 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 433.7, R = 132 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (433.7e-3) / 132 | Answer: 3.286 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 39.6 mH inductor at 160 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 39.6, f = 160 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (160)(39.6e-3) | Answer: 39.81 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 11.1 uF capacitor at 200 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 11.1, f = 200 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (200)(11.1e-6)) | Answer: 71.69 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 18 ohm, XL = 22 ohm and XC = 108 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 18, XL = 22, XC = 108 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(18^2 + (22 - 108)^2) | Answer: 87.86 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 81.1 mH and C = 5.2 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 81.1, C = 5.2 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(81.1e-3 * 5.2e-6)) | Answer: 245.1 Hz

question: A capacitor of 94.1 uF is charged to 300 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 94.1, V = 300 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*94.1e-6*(300)^2 | Answer: 4234 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 290 V with 890 primary turns and 290 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 290, N1 = 890, N2 = 290 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 290 * 290/890 | Answer: 94.49 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 160 V and draws an armature current of 60 A. If the armature resistance is 0.39 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 160, Ia = 60, Ra = 0.39 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 160 - 60*0.39 | Answer: 136.6 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 70 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.78. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 70, VL = 400, pf = 0.78 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*400*70*0.78 / 1000 | Answer: 37.83 kW

question: A machine delivers 35 kW output while drawing 52 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 35, Pi = 52 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 35/52 * 100 | Answer: 67.31 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 16 V across R1 = 5 ohm and R2 = 45 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 16, R1 = 5, R2 = 45 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 16*45 / (5+45) | Answer: 14.4 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 90 kohm and Rin = 4 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 90, Rin = 4 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 90 / 4 | Answer: 22.5

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 40 kohm and Rg = 18 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 40, Rg = 18 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 40/18 | Answer: 3.222

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 6840. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 6840 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(6840) | Answer: 38.35 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.7 m carries a central point load of 100 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 9.7, W = 100 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 100*9.7 / 4 | Answer: 242.5 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 4.3 m carries a point load 40 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.3, W = 40 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 40*4.3 | Answer: 172 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 5.4 m carries a point load 40 kN at distance 1.4 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 5.4, a = 1.4, W = 40 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 40*(5.4 - 1.4) / 5.4 | Answer: 29.63 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 4.4 m) carries a central point load 25 kN. With E = 30 GPa and I = 180e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=25000 N, L=4400.0 mm, E=30000 MPa, I=180e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 8.216 mm

question: An RC beam has overall depth 580 mm, clear cover 40 mm and main bars of diameter 12 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 580, c = 40, dia = 12 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 580 - 40 - 12/2 | Answer: 534 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 19.8 m^2 carrying a factored load of 9.6 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 19.8, w = 9.6 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 9.6 * 19.8 | Answer: 190.1 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 6.3 m, unit weight 19 kN/m^3, phi = 29 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 5.4e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1.1, area = 3.3e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 5.4, i = 1.1, A = 3.3 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (5.4e-4)*1.1*(3.3e-3) | Answer: 196 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.8 m, bed slope 0.01 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.028. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 3.8 m under a head of 0.5 m. Taking Cd = 0.62 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 4.4 m wide carries a discharge of 15.4 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 520 m and design speed 45 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 520, V = 45 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (45)^2 / (127*520) | Answer: 0.03066
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: A tank of volume 470 m^3 treats a flow of 170 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 470, Q = 170 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 470 / 170 | Answer: 2.765 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 160 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.27 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 5 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 160, k = 0.27, t = 5 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 160*(1 - e^(-0.27*5)) | Answer: 118.5 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.43, rainfall intensity 90 mm/h over a catchment of 21.8 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.43, i = 90, A = 21.8 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.43*90*21.8 / 360 | Answer: 2.344 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.08 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 350 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.08, M = 350 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 350*(20+0.08)/20 | Answer: 351.4 m

question: Convert the decimal number 1361 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 1361 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 551 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 01111110 and 01011100.
solution: XOR: 00100010 | Count of 1s = 2 | Answer: 2
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 930 megabits is sent over a link of 38 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 930, B = 38 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 930 / 38 | Answer: 24.47 s

question: A link has bandwidth 59 Mbps and round-trip time 120 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 59, R = 120 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 59e6 * 120e-3 bits = 7080 kb | Answer: 7080 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.97, cache access time 1 ns and main-memory access time 70 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.97, tc = 1, tm = 70 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.97*1 + (1 - 0.97)*70 | Answer: 3.07 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 869572 elements?
solution: Given: n = 869572 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(869572)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.009, memory access time 130 ns and page-fault service time 4 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 4 ms = 4000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.009)*130 + 0.009*4000000.0 ns | Answer: 36.13 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 2.7 m^3 at 290 kPa and 410 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 2.7, P = 290, Tk = 410 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (290e3)*2.7 / (8.314*410) | Answer: 229.7 mol

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.95 and bottoms xW = 0.07, with relative volatility alpha = 2.8. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.95, xw = 0.07, al = 2.8 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.95/0.05)(0.93/0.07)] / ln(2.8) | Answer: 5.372 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.67 and x = 0.39. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.67, x = 0.39 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.67/0.33) / (0.39/0.61) | Answer: 3.176

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.62 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 70 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.62, Psat = 70 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.62 * 70 | Answer: 43.4 kPa

question: A stream of 10 kg/s with specific heat 3.4 kJ/kg-K is heated through 35 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 10, cp = 3.4, dT = 35 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 10*3.4*35 | Answer: 1190 kW

question: A reactor of volume 3.7 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 4.8 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 3.7, Q = 4.8 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 3.7 / 4.8 | Answer: 0.7708 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 3.3e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 4 mm with a concentration difference of 100 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 3.3, L = 4, dC = 100 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (3.3e-9)*100 / (4e-3) | Answer: 82.5 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 4.6 min and steady-state gain 3.9. For a step input of magnitude 7, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 4.6, K = 3.9, M = 7 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 3.9 * 7 | Answer: 27.3 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 30 m^2 flies at 130 m/s (air density 1.225 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 1.3. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 30, V = 130, rho = 1.225, CL = 1.3 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1.225*(130)^2*30*1.3 / 1000 | Answer: 403.7 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 30 m^2 flies at 70 m/s (density 0.7 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.05. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 30, V = 70, rho = 0.7, CD = 0.05 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.7*(70)^2*30*0.05 / 1000 | Answer: 2.572 kN

question: A specimen under stress 380 MPa shows an elastic strain of 0.7e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 380, eps = 0.7 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 380 / (0.7e-3) MPa = 542.9 GPa | Answer: 542.9 GPa

question: A block of mass 6 kg has a volume of 2.1e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 6, V = 2.1 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 6 / (2.1e-3) | Answer: 2857 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 1900 mm is heated through 95 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 17e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 1900, dT = 95, al = 17 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 1900*17e-6*95 | Answer: 3.069 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 40 ohm, R2 = 45 ohm and R3 = 480 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 40, R2 = 45, R3 = 480 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 45*480 / 40 | Answer: 540 ohm

question: Annual demand is 33500 units, ordering cost 120 per order and holding cost 21 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 33500, S = 120, H = 21 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*33500*120 / 21) | Answer: 618.8 units

question: An asset costs 60000 with salvage value 36000 after 20 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 60000, Sv = 36000, n = 20 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (60000 - 36000) / 20 | Answer: 1200 per year

question: A product sells for 310 per unit with variable cost 120 per unit and fixed costs 145000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 310, V = 120, F = 145000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 145000 / (310 - 120) | Answer: 763.2 units

question: Find the present worth of 160000 received 5 years from now at an interest rate of 5% per year.
solution: Given: F = 160000, n = 5, i = 5 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 160000 / (1 + 0.05)^5 | Answer: 125364 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.92, 0.98 and 0.99 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.92, r2 = 0.98, r3 = 0.99 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.92*0.98*0.99 | Answer: 0.8926

question: A process produces 36 defective items in a batch of 14500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 36, N = 14500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 36/14500 * 1e6 | Answer: 2483 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = 6x^3 - 5x^2 - 7 evaluated at x = -4.
For f(x) = 6x^3 + 6x^2 - 3x + 1, find f''(x) at x = 3.
Evaluate the definite integral of (2x^2 + 4) dx from x = -1 to x = 3.

formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 3x^2 - 12x - 4 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[1, 6], [9, 2]].
solution: Given: a = 1, b = 6, c = 9, d = 2 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (1)(2) - (6)(9) | Answer: -52

solution: Trace tr = -1, Determinant = -50 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 6.589

question: Solve for x: 4x + 0y = 2 and 5x + 3y = 9.

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 90, 23, 13, 92, 37.

question: Find the slope of the line through (-2, 9) and (-4, -9).
solution: Given: x1 = -2, y1 = 9, x2 = -4, y2 = -9 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (-9 - 9) / (-4 - -2) | Answer: 9

question: Find the distance between the points (-7, -9) and (-3, 9).
solution: Given: x1 = -7, y1 = -9, x2 = -3, y2 = 9 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((4)^2 + (18)^2) | Answer: 18.44 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (-5,-5), (-1,0), (7,8).

question: Find the 40th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 5 and common difference -9.
solution: Given: a = 5, d = -9, n = 40 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = 5 + (40 - 1)*-9 | Answer: -346

question: Find the sum of the first 36 terms of an AP with first term 1 and common difference -8.
solution: Given: a = 1, d = -8, n = 36 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 36/2 [2*1 + (36-1)*-8] | Answer: -5004

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 49000 at 6% per annum for 1 years.
solution: Given: P = 49000, R = 6, Tt = 1 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 49000 * 6 * 1 / 100 | Answer: 2940 currency units

question: Find the amount when 22500 is invested at 8.7% per annum compounded annually for 3 years.
solution: Given: P = 22500, R = 8.7, Tt = 3 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 22500 * (1 + 8.7/100)^3 | Answer: 28898 currency units

question: Find the modulus of the complex number 10 + 0i.
solution: Given: a = 10, b = 0 | Formula: |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) | Substitute: |z| = sqrt((10)^2 + (0)^2) | Answer: 10

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 55 and 70.

question: A circular rod of diameter 39 mm carries an axial tensile load of 100 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 27 mm and length 2400 mm carries an axial load of 57 kN. Take E = 200 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 46 mm transmits a torque of 500 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 46, Tt = 500 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(500*1000) / (pi*(46)^3) | Answer: 26.16 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 48 mm and length 500 mm carries a torque of 750 N-m. With G = 80 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (48)^4 / 32 = 521153 mm^4 | theta = (750*1000)(500) / (80000 * 521153) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 0.5153 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 45 mm wide and 230 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 45, h = 230 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 45*(230)^2 / 6 | Answer: 396750 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (114 mm x 160 mm) carries a bending moment of 5 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (73 mm x 90 mm) has effective length 1900 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 890 MPa is designed for a working stress of 160 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 890, sw = 160 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 890 / 160 | Answer: 5.562

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1150 mm and wall thickness 8 mm carries an internal pressure of 2.8 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1150, t = 8, P = 2.8 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 2.8*1150 / (2*8) | Answer: 201.2 MPa

question: 6.5 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 50 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 6.5, dT = 50 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 6.5 * 0.718 * 50 | Answer: 233.3 kJ

question: 6.1 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 140 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 6.1, dT = 140 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 6.1 * 1.005 * 140 | Answer: 858.3 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 2.9 m^3 at 540 K with mass 4.8 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 2.9, Tk = 540, m = 4.8 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 4.8*0.287*540 / 2.9 | Answer: 256.5 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 1.6 kg of air expands isothermally at 350 K from volume V1 to 5*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1.6, Tk = 350, ratio = 5 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 1.6*0.287*350*ln(5) | Answer: 258.7 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 2.9 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.31 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 2.9, D = 0.31 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*2.9*0.31 / 0.001 | Answer: 899000

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 2.9 m. Taking Cv = 0.96, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 2.9, cv = 0.96 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.96*sqrt(2*9.81*2.9) | Answer: 7.241 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 250 mm) water flows at 2.1 m/s. It contracts to diameter 140 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
Water flows at 2.7 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.22 m and length 160 m. With friction factor f = 0.029, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
