question: A pinion of 25 teeth drives a gear of 70 teeth. If the pinion runs at 850 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 25, z2 = 70, N1 = 850 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 850*25 / 70 | Answer: 303.6 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 500 mm rotates at 1250 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 500, N = 1250 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.5)*1250 / 60 | Answer: 32.72 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 32.3 kW at 1350 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 32.3, N = 1350 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(32.3*1000) / (2*pi*1350) | Answer: 228.5 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 6.8 kg rotates at radius 0.52 m at 550 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 15300 N/m and mass 18.1 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 15300, m = 18.1 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(15300/18.1) | Answer: 4.627 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 6.5 m^2 and thickness 0.17 m has conductivity k = 16.5 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 120 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 6.5, L = 0.17, k = 16.5, dT = 120 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 16.5*6.5*120 / 0.17 | Answer: 75706 W

question: A surface of area 2.6 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 30 W/m^2-K to surroundings 35 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 2.6, h = 30, dT = 35 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 30*2.6*35 | Answer: 2730 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 130 m/min, feed = 0.44 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2.2 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 130, f = 0.44, d = 2.2 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*130*0.44*2.2 | Answer: 125840 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 380 mm is turned at 250 rpm with a feed of 0.36 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 380, N = 250, f = 0.36 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 380 / (0.36*250) | Answer: 4.222 min

question: A resistor of 38 ohm carries a current of 9.4 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 38, I = 9.4 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 9.4 * 38 | Answer: 357.2 V

question: Three resistors 1 ohm, 30 ohm and 64 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 1, R2 = 30, R3 = 64 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 1 + 30 + 64 | Answer: 95 ohm

question: Two resistors 43 ohm and 79 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 43, R2 = 79 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 43*79 / (43+79) | Answer: 27.84 ohm

question: A device draws 5.6 A at 60 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 60, I = 5.6 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 60 * 5.6 | Answer: 336 W

question: A current of 4.5 A flows through a 45 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 4.5, R = 45 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (4.5)^2 * 45 | Answer: 911.2 W

question: Two capacitors 44.4 uF and 9.3 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 44.4, C2 = 9.3 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 44.4*9.3 / (44.4+9.3) | Answer: 7.689 uF

question: A resistor 41 kohm and capacitor 18.2 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 41, C = 18.2 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (41k)(18.2u) = 746.2 ms | Answer: 746.2 ms

question: An inductor 333.7 mH is in series with 159 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 333.7, R = 159 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (333.7e-3) / 159 | Answer: 2.099 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 48.7 mH inductor at 220 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 48.7, f = 220 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (220)(48.7e-3) | Answer: 67.32 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 46.2 uF capacitor at 70 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 46.2, f = 70 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (70)(46.2e-6)) | Answer: 49.21 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 68 ohm, XL = 98 ohm and XC = 93 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 68, XL = 98, XC = 93 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(68^2 + (98 - 93)^2) | Answer: 68.18 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 77.5 mH and C = 7.1 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 77.5, C = 7.1 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(77.5e-3 * 7.1e-6)) | Answer: 214.6 Hz

question: A capacitor of 38.2 uF is charged to 45 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 38.2, V = 45 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*38.2e-6*(45)^2 | Answer: 38.68 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 350 V with 370 primary turns and 450 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 350, N1 = 370, N2 = 450 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 350 * 450/370 | Answer: 425.7 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 120 V and draws an armature current of 40 A. If the armature resistance is 0.3 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 120, Ia = 40, Ra = 0.3 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 120 - 40*0.3 | Answer: 108 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 40 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.77. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 40, VL = 400, pf = 0.77 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*400*40*0.77 / 1000 | Answer: 21.34 kW

question: A load has real power 55 kW and apparent power 160 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 55, S = 160 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 55 / 160 | Answer: 0.3438

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 14 V across R1 = 31 ohm and R2 = 22 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 14, R1 = 31, R2 = 22 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 14*22 / (31+22) | Answer: 5.811 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 50 kohm and Rin = 15 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 50, Rin = 15 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 50 / 15 | Answer: 3.333

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 130 kohm and Rg = 25 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 130, Rg = 25 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 130/25 | Answer: 6.2

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 1904. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 1904 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(1904) | Answer: 32.8 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.8 m carries a central point load of 110 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 9.8, W = 110 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 110*9.8 / 4 | Answer: 269.5 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 2.6 m carries a point load 25 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 2.6, W = 25 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 25*2.6 | Answer: 65 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 5.8 m carries a UDL of 10 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.8, w = 10 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 10*(5.8)^2 / 2 | Answer: 168.2 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.6 m carries a point load 15 kN at distance 2 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 6.6, a = 2, W = 15 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 15*(6.6 - 2) / 6.6 | Answer: 10.45 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 5.9 m) carries a central point load 50 kN. With E = 200 GPa and I = 550e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=50000 N, L=5900.0 mm, E=200000 MPa, I=550e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 1.945 mm

question: An RC beam has overall depth 480 mm, clear cover 30 mm and main bars of diameter 25 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 480, c = 30, dia = 25 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 480 - 30 - 25/2 | Answer: 437.5 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 32.2 m^2 carrying a factored load of 9.7 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 32.2, w = 9.7 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 9.7 * 32.2 | Answer: 312.3 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 5.9 m, unit weight 17 kN/m^3, phi = 37 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 6.3e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.8, area = 7.5e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 6.3, i = 0.8, A = 7.5 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (6.3e-4)*0.8*(7.5e-3) | Answer: 3780 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.2 m, bed slope 0.01 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.026. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 4.8 m under a head of 0.2 m. Taking Cd = 0.6 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 4.1 m wide carries a discharge of 12.3 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 370 m and design speed 50 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 370, V = 50 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (50)^2 / (127*370) | Answer: 0.0532
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: A tank of volume 570 m^3 treats a flow of 10 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 570, Q = 10 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 570 / 10 | Answer: 57 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 290 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.14 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 7 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 290, k = 0.14, t = 7 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 290*(1 - e^(-0.14*7)) | Answer: 181.2 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.71, rainfall intensity 65 mm/h over a catchment of 29.6 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.71, i = 65, A = 29.6 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.71*65*29.6 / 360 | Answer: 3.795 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.03 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 780 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.03, M = 780 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 780*(20+0.03)/20 | Answer: 781.2 m

question: Convert the decimal number 3523 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 3523 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: DC3 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 10000011 and 11001100.
solution: XOR: 01001111 | Count of 1s = 5 | Answer: 5
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 90 megabits is sent over a link of 82 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 90, B = 82 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 90 / 82 | Answer: 1.098 s

question: A link has bandwidth 35 Mbps and round-trip time 110 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 35, R = 110 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 35e6 * 110e-3 bits = 3850 kb | Answer: 3850 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.88, cache access time 2 ns and main-memory access time 90 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.88, tc = 2, tm = 90 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.88*2 + (1 - 0.88)*90 | Answer: 12.56 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 113538 elements?
solution: Given: n = 113538 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(113538)) + 1 | Answer: 17

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.008, memory access time 140 ns and page-fault service time 3 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 3 ms = 3000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.008)*140 + 0.008*3000000.0 ns | Answer: 24.14 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 2.2 m^3 at 400 kPa and 490 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 2.2, P = 400, Tk = 490 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (400e3)*2.2 / (8.314*490) | Answer: 216 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.05 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 14 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.05, t = 14 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.05*14) | Answer: 0.5034

question: For a reaction with A = 9e10 /s and activation energy 55 kJ/mol at 370 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 9, Ea = 55, Tk = 370 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 9e10 * exp(-55e3 / (8.314*370)) | Answer: 1547 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.98 and bottoms xW = 0.05, with relative volatility alpha = 1.8. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.98, xw = 0.05, al = 1.8 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.98/0.02)(0.95/0.05)] / ln(1.8) | Answer: 11.63 stages

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.89 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 75 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.89, Psat = 75 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.89 * 75 | Answer: 66.75 kPa

question: A stream of 3.9 kg/s with specific heat 3.3 kJ/kg-K is heated through 40 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 3.9, cp = 3.3, dT = 40 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 3.9*3.3*40 | Answer: 514.8 kW

question: A reactor of volume 3.1 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 2.9 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 3.1, Q = 2.9 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 3.1 / 2.9 | Answer: 1.069 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 4e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 5 mm with a concentration difference of 130 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 4, L = 5, dC = 130 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (4e-9)*130 / (5e-3) | Answer: 104 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 4.8 min and steady-state gain 2.9. For a step input of magnitude 11, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 4.8, K = 2.9, M = 11 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 2.9 * 11 | Answer: 31.9 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 25 m^2 flies at 130 m/s (air density 0.4 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.6. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 25, V = 130, rho = 0.4, CL = 0.6 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.4*(130)^2*25*0.6 / 1000 | Answer: 50.7 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 45 m^2 flies at 110 m/s (density 1 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.11. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 45, V = 110, rho = 1, CD = 0.11 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*1*(110)^2*45*0.11 / 1000 | Answer: 29.95 kN

question: A block of mass 31 kg has a volume of 1e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 31, V = 1 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 31 / (1e-3) | Answer: 31000 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 1400 mm is heated through 150 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 23e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 1400, dT = 150, al = 23 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 1400*23e-6*150 | Answer: 4.83 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 65 ohm, R2 = 185 ohm and R3 = 435 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 65, R2 = 185, R3 = 435 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 185*435 / 65 | Answer: 1238 ohm

question: A measurement reads 9.26 when the true value is 10. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.26, true = 10 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.26 - 10| / 10 * 100 | Answer: 7.4 %

question: Annual demand is 39000 units, ordering cost 170 per order and holding cost 23 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 39000, S = 170, H = 23 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*39000*170 / 23) | Answer: 759.3 units

question: An asset costs 50000 with salvage value 14000 after 14 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 50000, Sv = 14000, n = 14 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (50000 - 14000) / 14 | Answer: 2571 per year

question: A product sells for 320 per unit with variable cost 110 per unit and fixed costs 75000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 320, V = 110, F = 75000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 75000 / (320 - 110) | Answer: 357.1 units

question: Find the present worth of 25000 received 8 years from now at an interest rate of 12% per year.
solution: Given: F = 25000, n = 8, i = 12 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 25000 / (1 + 0.12)^8 | Answer: 10097 currency units

question: A process produces 46 defective items in a batch of 8500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 46, N = 8500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 46/8500 * 1e6 | Answer: 5412 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = 5x^3 + x^2 - 9x + 1 evaluated at x = 4.
For f(x) = -5x^3 + x^2 + 4x - 9, find f''(x) at x = -1.
Evaluate the definite integral of (-3x^2) dx from x = -2 to x = 5.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = -3x^3/3 + 0x^2/2 + 0x | Evaluate F(5) - F(-2) | Answer: -133
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 3x^2 + 7x - 2 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[-4, -7], [5, -2]].
solution: Given: a = -4, b = -7, c = 5, d = -2 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (-4)(-2) - (-7)(5) | Answer: 43

question: Find the determinant of [[6, -2, -3], [-1, 6, 4], [1, -3, -6]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: -131

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[-4, 6], [6, -7]].
solution: Trace tr = -11, Determinant = -8 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 0.6847

question: Solve for x: -6x + -1y = -7 and 5x + 2y = 8.
solution: Determinant = -6*2 - -1*5 = -7 | x = (e d - b f) / det = 0.8571 | Answer: x = 0.8571
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 30, 50, 34, 76, 35.
solution: Sum = 225 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 45 | Answer: 45

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 45, 36, 38, 44, 37.
solution: Mean = 40 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 4.183

question: Find the slope of the line through (-4, -7) and (-6, 3).
solution: Given: x1 = -4, y1 = -7, x2 = -6, y2 = 3 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (3 - -7) / (-6 - -4) | Answer: -5

question: Find the distance between the points (1, -4) and (8, 6).
solution: Given: x1 = 1, y1 = -4, x2 = 8, y2 = 6 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((7)^2 + (10)^2) | Answer: 12.21 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (-7,0), (-3,-6), (2,8).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 43 sq units

question: Find the 16th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 16 and common difference -6.
solution: Given: a = 16, d = -6, n = 16 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = 16 + (16 - 1)*-6 | Answer: -74

question: Find the sum of the first 22 terms of an AP with first term -9 and common difference 8.
solution: Given: a = -9, d = 8, n = 22 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 22/2 [2*-9 + (22-1)*8] | Answer: 1650

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 35500 at 9.5% per annum for 2 years.
solution: Given: P = 35500, R = 9.5, Tt = 2 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 35500 * 9.5 * 2 / 100 | Answer: 6745 currency units

question: Find the amount when 19000 is invested at 6.4% per annum compounded annually for 2 years.
solution: Given: P = 19000, R = 6.4, Tt = 2 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 19000 * (1 + 6.4/100)^2 | Answer: 2151 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (1, -3, -7) and (5, -1, 4).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (-4, 0, -5) and (-3, 5, -3).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 32.16

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (0, 4, -6) and (-1, -3, -3).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 79 degrees

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number -3 + 4i.
solution: Given: a = -3, b = 4 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(4, -3) | Answer: 126.9 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -5x^3 + 3x^2 + 6x + 6 at x = -1.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-172 with initial guess x0=8, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=0.8 and ordinates 6, 6, 1, 1, 0, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 560 and 380.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 560 and 380 | Answer: GCD = 20

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 66 and 42.
solution: Given: a = 66, b = 42 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 66*42 / 6 | Answer: 462
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 48 mm carries an axial tensile load of 8 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 23 mm and length 3000 mm carries an axial load of 83 kN. Take E = 110 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 56 mm transmits a torque of 650 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 56, Tt = 650 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(650*1000) / (pi*(56)^3) | Answer: 18.85 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 54 mm and length 900 mm carries a torque of 1850 N-m. With G = 80 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (54)^4 / 32 = 834786 mm^4 | theta = (1850*1000)(900) / (80000 * 834786) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 1.428 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 40 mm wide and 300 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 40, h = 300 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 40*(300)^2 / 6 | Answer: 600000 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (79 mm x 80 mm) carries a bending moment of 3 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (40 mm x 120 mm) has effective length 3200 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 520 MPa is designed for a working stress of 120 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 520, sw = 120 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 520 / 120 | Answer: 4.333

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1250 mm and wall thickness 18 mm carries an internal pressure of 1.1 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1250, t = 18, P = 1.1 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 1.1*1250 / (2*18) | Answer: 38.19 MPa

question: 7.1 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 160 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 7.1, dT = 160 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 7.1 * 0.718 * 160 | Answer: 815.6 kJ

question: 3.3 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 190 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.3, dT = 190 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 3.3 * 1.005 * 190 | Answer: 630.1 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 1.9 m^3 at 400 K with mass 1.2 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 1.9, Tk = 400, m = 1.2 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 1.2*0.287*400 / 1.9 | Answer: 72.51 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 2.6 kg of air expands isothermally at 490 K from volume V1 to 3*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.6, Tk = 490, ratio = 3 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 2.6*0.287*490*ln(3) | Answer: 401.7 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 0.5 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.09 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 0.5, D = 0.09 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*0.5*0.09 / 0.001 | Answer: 45000

question: Water flows at 3.8 m/s through a pipe of diameter 220 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
In a pipe (diameter 290 mm) water flows at 2.1 m/s. It contracts to diameter 120 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
Water flows at 2.3 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.17 m and length 360 m. With friction factor f = 0.039, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 36 teeth drives a gear of 88 teeth. If the pinion runs at 550 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 36, z2 = 88, N1 = 550 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 550*36 / 88 | Answer: 225 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 150 mm rotates at 300 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 150, N = 300 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.15)*300 / 60 | Answer: 2.356 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 32.4 kW at 250 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 32.4, N = 250 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(32.4*1000) / (2*pi*250) | Answer: 1238 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 1 kg rotates at radius 0.3 m at 700 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 9800 N/m and mass 3.9 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 9800, m = 3.9 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(9800/3.9) | Answer: 7.978 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 6.1 m^2 and thickness 0.23 m has conductivity k = 13.9 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 55 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 6.1, L = 0.23, k = 13.9, dT = 55 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 13.9*6.1*55 / 0.23 | Answer: 20276 W

question: A surface of area 0.6 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 130 W/m^2-K to surroundings 130 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 0.6, h = 130, dT = 130 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 130*0.6*130 | Answer: 10140 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 150 m/min, feed = 0.32 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2.2 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 150, f = 0.32, d = 2.2 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*150*0.32*2.2 | Answer: 105600 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 140 mm is turned at 600 rpm with a feed of 0.13 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 140, N = 600, f = 0.13 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 140 / (0.13*600) | Answer: 1.795 min

question: A resistor of 199 ohm carries a current of 1.9 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 199, I = 1.9 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 1.9 * 199 | Answer: 378.1 V

question: Three resistors 72 ohm, 51 ohm and 52 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 72, R2 = 51, R3 = 52 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 72 + 51 + 52 | Answer: 175 ohm

question: Two resistors 26 ohm and 85 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 26, R2 = 85 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 26*85 / (26+85) | Answer: 19.91 ohm

question: A device draws 11.9 A at 55 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 55, I = 11.9 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 55 * 11.9 | Answer: 654.5 W

question: A current of 6.8 A flows through a 138 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 6.8, R = 138 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (6.8)^2 * 138 | Answer: 6381 W

question: Two capacitors 40 uF and 37.2 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 40, C2 = 37.2 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 40*37.2 / (40+37.2) | Answer: 19.27 uF

question: A resistor 11 kohm and capacitor 4.2 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 11, C = 4.2 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (11k)(4.2u) = 46.2 ms | Answer: 46.2 ms

question: An inductor 19.2 mH is in series with 48 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 19.2, R = 48 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (19.2e-3) / 48 | Answer: 0.4 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 182.9 mH inductor at 470 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 182.9, f = 470 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (470)(182.9e-3) | Answer: 540.1 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 24.8 uF capacitor at 560 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 24.8, f = 560 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (560)(24.8e-6)) | Answer: 11.46 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 100 ohm, XL = 97 ohm and XC = 29 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 100, XL = 97, XC = 29 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(100^2 + (97 - 29)^2) | Answer: 120.9 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 23.7 mH and C = 7.1 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 23.7, C = 7.1 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(23.7e-3 * 7.1e-6)) | Answer: 388 Hz

question: A capacitor of 42.2 uF is charged to 345 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 42.2, V = 345 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*42.2e-6*(345)^2 | Answer: 2511 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 130 V with 800 primary turns and 160 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 130, N1 = 800, N2 = 160 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 130 * 160/800 | Answer: 26 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 400 V and draws an armature current of 43 A. If the armature resistance is 0.65 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 400, Ia = 43, Ra = 0.65 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 400 - 43*0.65 | Answer: 372.1 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 5 A at 415 V (line) with a power factor of 0.94. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 5, VL = 415, pf = 0.94 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*415*5*0.94 / 1000 | Answer: 3.378 kW

question: A load has real power 65 kW and apparent power 135 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 65, S = 135 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 65 / 135 | Answer: 0.4815

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 11 V across R1 = 16 ohm and R2 = 35 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 11, R1 = 16, R2 = 35 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 11*35 / (16+35) | Answer: 7.549 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 20 kohm and Rin = 8 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 20, Rin = 8 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 20 / 8 | Answer: 2.5

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 4835. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 4835 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(4835) | Answer: 36.84 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 7.4 m carries a central point load of 25 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7.4, W = 25 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 25*7.4 / 4 | Answer: 46.25 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 3.2 m carries a UDL of 30 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.2, w = 30 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 30*(3.2)^2 / 2 | Answer: 153.6 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 8.4 m carries a point load 20 kN at distance 1.9 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 8.4, a = 1.9, W = 20 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 20*(8.4 - 1.9) / 8.4 | Answer: 15.48 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 4.3 m) carries a central point load 55 kN. With E = 30 GPa and I = 380e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=55000 N, L=4300.0 mm, E=30000 MPa, I=380e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 7.991 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 8.4 m carries a UDL of 33 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 8.4, w = 33 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 33*(8.4)^2 / 12 | Answer: 194 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 500 mm, clear cover 40 mm and main bars of diameter 25 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 500, c = 40, dia = 25 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 500 - 40 - 25/2 | Answer: 447.5 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 34.1 m^2 carrying a factored load of 18.2 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 34.1, w = 18.2 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 18.2 * 34.1 | Answer: 620.6 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 4.5 m, unit weight 20 kN/m^3, phi = 36 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 6.6e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.2, area = 2.6e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 6.6, i = 0.2, A = 2.6 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (6.6e-4)*0.2*(2.6e-3) | Answer: 343.2 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 2.4 m, bed slope 0.005 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.026. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 3 m under a head of 1.2 m. Taking Cd = 0.64 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 5.3 m wide carries a discharge of 16.9 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A tank of volume 90 m^3 treats a flow of 10 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 90, Q = 10 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 90 / 10 | Answer: 9 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 160 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.13 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 8 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 160, k = 0.13, t = 8 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 160*(1 - e^(-0.13*8)) | Answer: 103.4 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.55, rainfall intensity 80 mm/h over a catchment of 34.8 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.55, i = 80, A = 34.8 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.55*80*34.8 / 360 | Answer: 4.253 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.07 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 360 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.07, M = 360 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 360*(20+0.07)/20 | Answer: 361.3 m

question: Convert the decimal number 1042 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 1042 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 412 (hex)

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 00101110 and 11001110.
solution: XOR: 11100000 | Count of 1s = 3 | Answer: 3

question: A file of 910 megabits is sent over a link of 94 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 910, B = 94 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 910 / 94 | Answer: 9.681 s

question: A link has bandwidth 78 Mbps and round-trip time 190 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 78, R = 190 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 78e6 * 190e-3 bits = 14820 kb | Answer: 14820 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.97, cache access time 7 ns and main-memory access time 130 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.97, tc = 7, tm = 130 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.97*7 + (1 - 0.97)*130 | Answer: 10.69 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 477478 elements?
solution: Given: n = 477478 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(477478)) + 1 | Answer: 19

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.008, memory access time 190 ns and page-fault service time 10 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 10 ms = 10000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.008)*190 + 0.008*10000000.0 ns | Answer: 80.19 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 0.7 m^3 at 410 kPa and 470 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 0.7, P = 410, Tk = 470 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (410e3)*0.7 / (8.314*470) | Answer: 73.45 mol

question: For a reaction with A = 9e10 /s and activation energy 60 kJ/mol at 330 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 9, Ea = 60, Tk = 330 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 9e10 * exp(-60e3 / (8.314*330)) | Answer: 28.62 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.97 and bottoms xW = 0.09, with relative volatility alpha = 2.4. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.97, xw = 0.09, al = 2.4 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.97/0.03)(0.91/0.09)] / ln(2.4) | Answer: 6.613 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.83 and x = 0.22. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.83, x = 0.22 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.83/0.17) / (0.22/0.78) | Answer: 17.31

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.6 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 115 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.6, Psat = 115 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.6 * 115 | Answer: 69 kPa

question: A stream of 2.7 kg/s with specific heat 1.4 kJ/kg-K is heated through 85 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 2.7, cp = 1.4, dT = 85 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 2.7*1.4*85 | Answer: 321.3 kW

question: A reactor of volume 6.3 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 3.2 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 6.3, Q = 3.2 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 6.3 / 3.2 | Answer: 1.969 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 5.8e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 1 mm with a concentration difference of 50 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 5.8, L = 1, dC = 50 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (5.8e-9)*50 / (1e-3) | Answer: 290 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 9.4 min and steady-state gain 1.9. For a step input of magnitude 3, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 9.4, K = 1.9, M = 3 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 1.9 * 3 | Answer: 5.7 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 55 m^2 flies at 70 m/s (air density 1 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 1.3. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 55, V = 70, rho = 1, CL = 1.3 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1*(70)^2*55*1.3 / 1000 | Answer: 175.2 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 15 m^2 flies at 260 m/s (density 1.225 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.1. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 15, V = 260, rho = 1.225, CD = 0.1 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*1.225*(260)^2*15*0.1 / 1000 | Answer: 62.11 kN

question: A specimen under stress 240 MPa shows an elastic strain of 1.4e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 240, eps = 1.4 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 240 / (1.4e-3) MPa = 171.4 GPa | Answer: 171.4 GPa

question: A block of mass 45 kg has a volume of 2.9e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 45, V = 2.9 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 45 / (2.9e-3) | Answer: 15517 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 1700 mm is heated through 65 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 17e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 1700, dT = 65, al = 17 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 1700*17e-6*65 | Answer: 1.878 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 90 ohm, R2 = 55 ohm and R3 = 210 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 90, R2 = 55, R3 = 210 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 55*210 / 90 | Answer: 128.3 ohm

question: Annual demand is 6000 units, ordering cost 60 per order and holding cost 40 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 6000, S = 60, H = 40 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*6000*60 / 40) | Answer: 134.2 units

question: An asset costs 80000 with salvage value 36000 after 13 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 80000, Sv = 36000, n = 13 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (80000 - 36000) / 13 | Answer: 3385 per year

question: A product sells for 250 per unit with variable cost 120 per unit and fixed costs 165000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 250, V = 120, F = 165000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 165000 / (250 - 120) | Answer: 1269 units

question: Find the present worth of 105000 received 5 years from now at an interest rate of 5% per year.
solution: Given: F = 105000, n = 5, i = 5 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 105000 / (1 + 0.05)^5 | Answer: 8227 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.99, 0.93 and 0.92 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.99, r2 = 0.93, r3 = 0.92 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.99*0.93*0.92 | Answer: 0.847

question: A process produces 16 defective items in a batch of 4000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 16, N = 4000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 16/4000 * 1e6 | Answer: 4000 PPM

question: Find the slope of the line through (-8, -2) and (-9, 9).

question: Find the distance between the points (1, -1) and (0, 9).
solution: Given: x1 = 1, y1 = -1, x2 = 0, y2 = 9 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-1)^2 + (10)^2) | Answer: 10.05 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (-3,-3), (5,8), (8,2).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 40.5 sq units

question: Find the 21th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -7 and common difference -3.
solution: Given: a = -7, d = -3, n = 21 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -7 + (21 - 1)*-3 | Answer: -67

question: Find the sum of the first 28 terms of an AP with first term -5 and common difference 2.
solution: Given: a = -5, d = 2, n = 28 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 28/2 [2*-5 + (28-1)*2] | Answer: 616

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 39000 at 10.9% per annum for 9 years.
solution: Given: P = 39000, R = 10.9, Tt = 9 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 39000 * 10.9 * 9 / 100 | Answer: 38259 currency units

question: Find the amount when 20500 is invested at 5.1% per annum compounded annually for 5 years.
solution: Given: P = 20500, R = 5.1, Tt = 5 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 20500 * (1 + 5.1/100)^5 | Answer: 26289 currency units

question: Evaluate f(x) = 4x^3 + 6x^2 - 6x - 7 at x = 2.

question: A circular rod of diameter 28 mm carries an axial tensile load of 65 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 28 mm and length 800 mm carries an axial load of 45 kN. Take E = 210 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 73 mm transmits a torque of 2950 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 73, Tt = 2950 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(2950*1000) / (pi*(73)^3) | Answer: 38.62 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 27 mm and length 600 mm carries a torque of 1200 N-m. With G = 77 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (27)^4 / 32 = 52174 mm^4 | theta = (1200*1000)(600) / (77000 * 52174) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 10.27 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 64 mm wide and 170 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 64, h = 170 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 64*(170)^2 / 6 | Answer: 308267 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (46 mm x 150 mm) carries a bending moment of 34 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (57 mm x 160 mm) has effective length 3000 mm and E = 200 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 650 MPa is designed for a working stress of 60 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 650, sw = 60 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 650 / 60 | Answer: 10.83

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 500 mm and wall thickness 18 mm carries an internal pressure of 1.4 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 500, t = 18, P = 1.4 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 1.4*500 / (2*18) | Answer: 19.44 MPa

question: 3.3 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 55 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.3, dT = 55 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 3.3 * 0.718 * 55 | Answer: 130.3 kJ

question: 5.7 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 70 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 5.7, dT = 70 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 5.7 * 1.005 * 70 | Answer: 401 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 2.1 m^3 at 600 K with mass 5.9 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 2.1, Tk = 600, m = 5.9 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 5.9*0.287*600 / 2.1 | Answer: 483.8 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 4.3 kg of air expands isothermally at 430 K from volume V1 to 3*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.3, Tk = 430, ratio = 3 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 4.3*0.287*430*ln(3) | Answer: 583 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 2.1 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.21 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 2.1, D = 0.21 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*2.1*0.21 / 0.001 | Answer: 441000

question: Water flows at 3.1 m/s through a pipe of diameter 150 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 8.2 m. Taking Cv = 0.98, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 8.2, cv = 0.98 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.98*sqrt(2*9.81*8.2) | Answer: 12.43 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 190 mm) water flows at 2.2 m/s. It contracts to diameter 130 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
Water flows at 2.5 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.38 m and length 190 m. With friction factor f = 0.032, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 17 teeth drives a gear of 104 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1000 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 17, z2 = 104, N1 = 1000 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1000*17 / 104 | Answer: 163.5 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 530 mm rotates at 400 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 530, N = 400 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.53)*400 / 60 | Answer: 11.1 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 43.6 kW at 400 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 43.6, N = 400 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(43.6*1000) / (2*pi*400) | Answer: 1041 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 3.3 kg rotates at radius 0.29 m at 800 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 10200 N/m and mass 9.6 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 10200, m = 9.6 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(10200/9.6) | Answer: 5.188 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 4.3 m^2 and thickness 0.18 m has conductivity k = 10.6 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 140 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 4.3, L = 0.18, k = 10.6, dT = 140 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 10.6*4.3*140 / 0.18 | Answer: 35451 W

question: A surface of area 5.2 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 150 W/m^2-K to surroundings 25 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 5.2, h = 150, dT = 25 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 150*5.2*25 | Answer: 19500 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 250 m/min, feed = 0.3 mm/rev, depth of cut = 0.8 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 250, f = 0.3, d = 0.8 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*250*0.3*0.8 | Answer: 60000 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 180 mm is turned at 350 rpm with a feed of 0.33 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 180, N = 350, f = 0.33 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 180 / (0.33*350) | Answer: 1.558 min

question: A resistor of 189 ohm carries a current of 7.5 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 189, I = 7.5 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 7.5 * 189 | Answer: 1418 V

question: Three resistors 21 ohm, 100 ohm and 96 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 21, R2 = 100, R3 = 96 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 21 + 100 + 96 | Answer: 217 ohm

question: Two resistors 52 ohm and 114 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 52, R2 = 114 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 52*114 / (52+114) | Answer: 35.71 ohm

question: A device draws 0.2 A at 10 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 10, I = 0.2 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 10 * 0.2 | Answer: 2 W

question: A current of 5.3 A flows through a 64 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 5.3, R = 64 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (5.3)^2 * 64 | Answer: 1798 W

question: Two capacitors 11.8 uF and 22.2 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 11.8, C2 = 22.2 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 11.8*22.2 / (11.8+22.2) | Answer: 7.705 uF

question: A resistor 49 kohm and capacitor 5.4 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 49, C = 5.4 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (49k)(5.4u) = 264.6 ms | Answer: 264.6 ms

question: An inductor 86.6 mH is in series with 70 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 86.6, R = 70 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (86.6e-3) / 70 | Answer: 1.237 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 134.4 mH inductor at 920 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 134.4, f = 920 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (920)(134.4e-3) | Answer: 776.9 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 49.6 uF capacitor at 570 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 49.6, f = 570 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (570)(49.6e-6)) | Answer: 5.629 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 28 ohm, XL = 26 ohm and XC = 103 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 28, XL = 26, XC = 103 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(28^2 + (26 - 103)^2) | Answer: 81.93 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 73.1 mH and C = 1.3 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 73.1, C = 1.3 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(73.1e-3 * 1.3e-6)) | Answer: 516.3 Hz

question: A capacitor of 64.8 uF is charged to 190 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 64.8, V = 190 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*64.8e-6*(190)^2 | Answer: 117 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 160 V with 640 primary turns and 310 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 160, N1 = 640, N2 = 310 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 160 * 310/640 | Answer: 77.5 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 140 V and draws an armature current of 16 A. If the armature resistance is 1.01 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 140, Ia = 16, Ra = 1.01 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 140 - 16*1.01 | Answer: 123.8 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 110 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.76. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 110, VL = 400, pf = 0.76 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*400*110*0.76 / 1000 | Answer: 57.92 kW

question: A load has real power 45 kW and apparent power 195 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 45, S = 195 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 45 / 195 | Answer: 0.2308

question: A machine delivers 70 kW output while drawing 197 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 70, Pi = 197 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 70/197 * 100 | Answer: 35.53 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 9 V across R1 = 39 ohm and R2 = 14 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 9, R1 = 39, R2 = 14 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 9*14 / (39+14) | Answer: 2.377 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 60 kohm and Rin = 44 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 60, Rin = 44 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 60 / 44 | Answer: 1.364

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 190 kohm and Rg = 29 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 190, Rg = 29 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 190/29 | Answer: 7.552

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 7814. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 7814 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(7814) | Answer: 38.93 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 3.3 m carries a central point load of 95 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.3, W = 95 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 95*3.3 / 4 | Answer: 78.38 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 2.4 m carries a point load 45 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 2.4, W = 45 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 45*2.4 | Answer: 108 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.3 m carries a point load 70 kN at distance 3.2 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 9.3, a = 3.2, W = 70 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 70*(9.3 - 3.2) / 9.3 | Answer: 45.91 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 5 m) carries a central point load 50 kN. With E = 25 GPa and I = 50e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=50000 N, L=5000.0 mm, E=25000 MPa, I=50e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 104.2 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 4 m carries a UDL of 27 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4, w = 27 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 27*(4)^2 / 12 | Answer: 36 kN-m

question: A column supports a floor area of 28.6 m^2 carrying a factored load of 10.6 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 28.6, w = 10.6 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 10.6 * 28.6 | Answer: 303.2 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 6.7 m, unit weight 18 kN/m^3, phi = 32 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 6.4e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.9, area = 1.8e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 6.4, i = 0.9, A = 1.8 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (6.4e-4)*0.9*(1.8e-3) | Answer: 1037 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 2.4 m, bed slope 0.005 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.028. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 4.9 m under a head of 0.9 m. Taking Cd = 0.6 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 4.4 m wide carries a discharge of 7.6 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A tank of volume 760 m^3 treats a flow of 190 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 760, Q = 190 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 760 / 190 | Answer: 4 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 350 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.13 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 5 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 350, k = 0.13, t = 5 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 350*(1 - e^(-0.13*5)) | Answer: 167.3 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.87, rainfall intensity 45 mm/h over a catchment of 7.4 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.87, i = 45, A = 7.4 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.87*45*7.4 / 360 | Answer: 0.8047 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.04 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 230 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.04, M = 230 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 230*(20+0.04)/20 | Answer: 230.5 m

question: Convert the decimal number 826 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 826 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 33A (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 00001101 and 01001111.
solution: XOR: 01000010 | Count of 1s = 2 | Answer: 2
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 840 megabits is sent over a link of 69 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 840, B = 69 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 840 / 69 | Answer: 12.17 s

question: A link has bandwidth 95 Mbps and round-trip time 60 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 95, R = 60 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 95e6 * 60e-3 bits = 5700 kb | Answer: 5700 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.81, cache access time 10 ns and main-memory access time 140 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.81, tc = 10, tm = 140 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.81*10 + (1 - 0.81)*140 | Answer: 34.7 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 904527 elements?
solution: Given: n = 904527 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(904527)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.003, memory access time 90 ns and page-fault service time 4 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 4 ms = 4000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.003)*90 + 0.003*4000000.0 ns | Answer: 12.09 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 2.6 m^3 at 190 kPa and 460 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 2.6, P = 190, Tk = 460 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (190e3)*2.6 / (8.314*460) | Answer: 129.2 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.05 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 6 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.05, t = 6 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.05*6) | Answer: 0.2592

question: For a reaction with A = 3e10 /s and activation energy 65 kJ/mol at 410 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 3, Ea = 65, Tk = 410 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 3e10 * exp(-65e3 / (8.314*410)) | Answer: 156.9 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.96 and bottoms xW = 0.03, with relative volatility alpha = 2.2. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.96, xw = 0.03, al = 2.2 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.96/0.04)(0.97/0.03)] / ln(2.2) | Answer: 8.439 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.71 and x = 0.21. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.71, x = 0.21 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.71/0.29) / (0.21/0.79) | Answer: 9.21

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.22 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 20 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.22, Psat = 20 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.22 * 20 | Answer: 4.4 kPa

question: A stream of 6.3 kg/s with specific heat 1.4 kJ/kg-K is heated through 55 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 6.3, cp = 1.4, dT = 55 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 6.3*1.4*55 | Answer: 485.1 kW

question: A reactor of volume 12.1 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 0.4 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 12.1, Q = 0.4 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 12.1 / 0.4 | Answer: 30.25 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 4.6e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 4 mm with a concentration difference of 160 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 4.6, L = 4, dC = 160 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (4.6e-9)*160 / (4e-3) | Answer: 184 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 5.7 min and steady-state gain 2.3. For a step input of magnitude 4, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 5.7, K = 2.3, M = 4 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 2.3 * 4 | Answer: 9.2 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 95 m^2 flies at 120 m/s (air density 1 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.4. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 95, V = 120, rho = 1, CL = 0.4 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1*(120)^2*95*0.4 / 1000 | Answer: 273.6 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 60 m^2 flies at 230 m/s (density 0.4 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.07. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 60, V = 230, rho = 0.4, CD = 0.07 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.4*(230)^2*60*0.07 / 1000 | Answer: 44.44 kN

question: A block of mass 42 kg has a volume of 1.7e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 42, V = 1.7 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 42 / (1.7e-3) | Answer: 24706 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 2400 mm is heated through 110 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 12e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 2400, dT = 110, al = 12 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 2400*12e-6*110 | Answer: 3.168 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 60 ohm, R2 = 15 ohm and R3 = 25 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 60, R2 = 15, R3 = 25 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 15*25 / 60 | Answer: 6.25 ohm

question: A measurement reads 9.82 when the true value is 100. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.82, true = 100 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.82 - 100| / 100 * 100 | Answer: 90.18 %

question: Annual demand is 39000 units, ordering cost 110 per order and holding cost 20 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 39000, S = 110, H = 20 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*39000*110 / 20) | Answer: 655 units

question: An asset costs 170000 with salvage value 10000 after 5 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 170000, Sv = 10000, n = 5 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (170000 - 10000) / 5 | Answer: 32000 per year

question: A product sells for 70 per unit with variable cost 40 per unit and fixed costs 200000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 70, V = 40, F = 200000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 200000 / (70 - 40) | Answer: 6667 units

question: Find the present worth of 45000 received 8 years from now at an interest rate of 9% per year.
solution: Given: F = 45000, n = 8, i = 9 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 45000 / (1 + 0.09)^8 | Answer: 22584 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.98, 0.96 and 0.9 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.98, r2 = 0.96, r3 = 0.9 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.98*0.96*0.9 | Answer: 0.8467

question: A process produces 35 defective items in a batch of 10000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 35, N = 10000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 35/10000 * 1e6 | Answer: 3500 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -2x^3 - 6x^2 + 9x + 1 evaluated at x = 2.
For f(x) = 5x^3 - 6x^2 + 4x + 3, find f''(x) at x = 5.
Evaluate the definite integral of (-4x^2 + 4x + 4) dx from x = -4 to x = 5.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = -4x^3/3 + 4x^2/2 + 4x | Evaluate F(5) - F(-4) | Answer: -198
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 3x^2 - 2x - 11 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[9, -2], [2, 0]].
solution: Given: a = 9, b = -2, c = 2, d = 0 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (9)(0) - (-2)(2) | Answer: 4

question: Find the determinant of [[-1, -4, 4], [4, -5, 5], [-4, 4, 3]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: 147

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[-6, -8], [-3, 2]].
solution: Trace tr = -4, Determinant = -36 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 4.325

question: Solve for x: 3x + -4y = 0 and 4x + -3y = 6.
solution: Determinant = 3*-3 - -4*4 = 7 | x = (e d - b f) / det = 3.429 | Answer: x = 3.429
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 42, 5, 2, 66, 7.
solution: Sum = 122 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 24.4 | Answer: 24.4

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 36, 43, 9, 43, 14.
solution: Mean = 29 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 16.32

question: Find the slope of the line through (-8, 3) and (8, -3).
solution: Given: x1 = -8, y1 = 3, x2 = 8, y2 = -3 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (-3 - 3) / (8 - -8) | Answer: -0.375

question: Find the distance between the points (-4, -7) and (5, 3).
solution: Given: x1 = -4, y1 = -7, x2 = 5, y2 = 3 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((9)^2 + (10)^2) | Answer: 13.45 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (-7,0), (4,-5), (-4,-3).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 9 sq units

question: Find the 39th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 20 and common difference 3.
solution: Given: a = 20, d = 3, n = 39 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = 20 + (39 - 1)*3 | Answer: 134

question: Find the sum of the first 32 terms of an AP with first term -5 and common difference -4.
solution: Given: a = -5, d = -4, n = 32 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 32/2 [2*-5 + (32-1)*-4] | Answer: -2144

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 45500 at 12.2% per annum for 9 years.
solution: Given: P = 45500, R = 12.2, Tt = 9 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 45500 * 12.2 * 9 / 100 | Answer: 49959 currency units

question: Find the amount when 8000 is invested at 9.8% per annum compounded annually for 4 years.
solution: Given: P = 8000, R = 9.8, Tt = 4 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 8000 * (1 + 9.8/100)^4 | Answer: 11628 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (-7, -2, -4) and (-3, 7, -6).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (4, -5, 5) and (5, 3, -2).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 49.83

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (5, 1, 3) and (0, 5, -6).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 106.3 degrees

question: Find the argument (in degrees) of the complex number 0 + 11i.
solution: Given: a = 0, b = 11 | Formula: arg(z) = atan2(b, a) | Substitute: arg = atan2(11, 0) | Answer: 90 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = 4x^3 + 7x^2 - x - 8 at x = 2.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-68 with initial guess x0=7, find x1 (one iteration).
solution: Given: N = 68, x0 = 7 | Formula: x1 = x0 - (x0^2 - N)/(2 x0) | Substitute: x1 = 7 - ((7)^2 - 68)/(2*7) | Answer: 8.357

question: Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.3 and ordinates 16, 0, 15, 19, 20, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 465 and 409.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 465 and 409 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 48 and 52.
solution: Given: a = 48, b = 52 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 48*52 / 4 | Answer: 624
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 29 mm carries an axial tensile load of 27 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 28 mm and length 1000 mm carries an axial load of 77 kN. Take E = 200 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 78 mm transmits a torque of 2950 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 78, Tt = 2950 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(2950*1000) / (pi*(78)^3) | Answer: 31.66 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 62 mm and length 1600 mm carries a torque of 450 N-m. With G = 45 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (62)^4 / 32 = 1450663 mm^4 | theta = (450*1000)(1600) / (45000 * 1450663) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 0.6319 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 37 mm wide and 250 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 37, h = 250 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 37*(250)^2 / 6 | Answer: 385417 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (97 mm x 170 mm) carries a bending moment of 40 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (61 mm x 100 mm) has effective length 3900 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 860 MPa is designed for a working stress of 190 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 860, sw = 190 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 860 / 190 | Answer: 4.526

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1150 mm and wall thickness 15 mm carries an internal pressure of 0.6 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1150, t = 15, P = 0.6 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 0.6*1150 / (2*15) | Answer: 23 MPa

question: 1.9 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 160 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1.9, dT = 160 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 1.9 * 0.718 * 160 | Answer: 218.3 kJ

question: 3.2 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 65 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.2, dT = 65 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 3.2 * 1.005 * 65 | Answer: 209 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 2.2 m^3 at 470 K with mass 3.5 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 2.2, Tk = 470, m = 3.5 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 3.5*0.287*470 / 2.2 | Answer: 214.6 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 2.1 kg of air expands isothermally at 350 K from volume V1 to 2*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.1, Tk = 350, ratio = 2 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 2.1*0.287*350*ln(2) | Answer: 146.2 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 2.8 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.3 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 2.8, D = 0.3 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*2.8*0.3 / 0.001 | Answer: 840000

question: Water flows at 3.9 m/s through a pipe of diameter 80 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 11.3 m. Taking Cv = 0.97, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 11.3, cv = 0.97 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.97*sqrt(2*9.81*11.3) | Answer: 14.44 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 200 mm) water flows at 1.6 m/s. It contracts to diameter 60 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 200, d2 = 60, V1 = 1.6 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 1.6*(200/60)^2 | Answer: 17.78 m/s

question: Water flows at 1.4 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.16 m and length 120 m. With friction factor f = 0.025, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 18 teeth drives a gear of 45 teeth. If the pinion runs at 850 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 18, z2 = 45, N1 = 850 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 850*18 / 45 | Answer: 340 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 220 mm rotates at 350 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 220, N = 350 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.22)*350 / 60 | Answer: 4.032 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 48.8 kW at 1000 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 48.8, N = 1000 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(48.8*1000) / (2*pi*1000) | Answer: 466 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 6.7 kg rotates at radius 0.31 m at 1150 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 6100 N/m and mass 14.1 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 6100, m = 14.1 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(6100/14.1) | Answer: 3.31 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 8.9 m^2 and thickness 0.15 m has conductivity k = 46.3 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 130 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 8.9, L = 0.15, k = 46.3, dT = 130 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 46.3*8.9*130 / 0.15 | Answer: 357127 W

question: A surface of area 0.5 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 35 W/m^2-K to surroundings 105 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 0.5, h = 35, dT = 105 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 35*0.5*105 | Answer: 1838 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 210 m/min, feed = 0.16 mm/rev, depth of cut = 1.6 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 210, f = 0.16, d = 1.6 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*210*0.16*1.6 | Answer: 53760 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 240 mm is turned at 550 rpm with a feed of 0.33 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 240, N = 550, f = 0.33 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 240 / (0.33*550) | Answer: 1.322 min

question: A resistor of 200 ohm carries a current of 5.8 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 200, I = 5.8 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 5.8 * 200 | Answer: 1160 V

question: Three resistors 34 ohm, 74 ohm and 27 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 34, R2 = 74, R3 = 27 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 34 + 74 + 27 | Answer: 135 ohm

question: Two resistors 22 ohm and 95 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 22, R2 = 95 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 22*95 / (22+95) | Answer: 17.86 ohm

question: A device draws 4.3 A at 145 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 145, I = 4.3 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 145 * 4.3 | Answer: 623.5 W
