question: A current of 6.6 A flows through a 114 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 6.6, R = 114 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (6.6)^2 * 114 | Answer: 4966 W

question: Two capacitors 44.5 uF and 29.3 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 44.5, C2 = 29.3 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 44.5*29.3 / (44.5+29.3) | Answer: 17.67 uF

question: A resistor 46 kohm and capacitor 13.5 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 46, C = 13.5 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (46k)(13.5u) = 621 ms | Answer: 621 ms

question: An inductor 340.4 mH is in series with 32 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 340.4, R = 32 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (340.4e-3) / 32 | Answer: 10.64 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 111.4 mH inductor at 620 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 111.4, f = 620 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (620)(111.4e-3) | Answer: 434 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 21.4 uF capacitor at 460 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 21.4, f = 460 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (460)(21.4e-6)) | Answer: 16.17 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 90 ohm, XL = 22 ohm and XC = 83 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 90, XL = 22, XC = 83 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(90^2 + (22 - 83)^2) | Answer: 108.7 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 21.4 mH and C = 4 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 21.4, C = 4 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(21.4e-3 * 4e-6)) | Answer: 544 Hz

question: A capacitor of 11.2 uF is charged to 210 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 11.2, V = 210 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*11.2e-6*(210)^2 | Answer: 247 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 110 V with 510 primary turns and 460 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 110, N1 = 510, N2 = 460 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 110 * 460/510 | Answer: 99.22 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 240 V and draws an armature current of 33 A. If the armature resistance is 0.9 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 240, Ia = 33, Ra = 0.9 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 240 - 33*0.9 | Answer: 210.3 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 45 A at 415 V (line) with a power factor of 0.77. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 45, VL = 415, pf = 0.77 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*415*45*0.77 / 1000 | Answer: 24.91 kW

question: A load has real power 160 kW and apparent power 215 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 160, S = 215 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 160 / 215 | Answer: 0.7442

question: A machine delivers 35 kW output while drawing 82 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 35, Pi = 82 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 35/82 * 100 | Answer: 42.68 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 12 V across R1 = 4 ohm and R2 = 46 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 12, R1 = 4, R2 = 46 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 12*46 / (4+46) | Answer: 11.04 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 40 kohm and Rin = 9 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 40, Rin = 9 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 40 / 9 | Answer: 4.444

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 120 kohm and Rg = 44 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 120, Rg = 44 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 120/44 | Answer: 3.727

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 6943. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 6943 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(6943) | Answer: 38.42 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 7.4 m carries a central point load of 30 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7.4, W = 30 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 30*7.4 / 4 | Answer: 55.5 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 9 m carries a UDL of 15 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 9, w = 15 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 15*(9)^2 / 8 | Answer: 151.9 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 2.8 m carries a point load 10 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 2.8, W = 10 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 10*2.8 | Answer: 28 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 4 m carries a UDL of 8 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4, w = 8 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 8*(4)^2 / 2 | Answer: 64 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 5.3 m carries a point load 65 kN at distance 3.5 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 5.3, a = 3.5, W = 65 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 65*(5.3 - 3.5) / 5.3 | Answer: 22.08 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 7.6 m) carries a central point load 30 kN. With E = 25 GPa and I = 570e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=30000 N, L=7600.0 mm, E=25000 MPa, I=570e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 19.25 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 4.6 m carries a UDL of 18 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.6, w = 18 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 18*(4.6)^2 / 12 | Answer: 31.74 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 530 mm, clear cover 50 mm and main bars of diameter 16 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 530, c = 50, dia = 16 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 530 - 50 - 16/2 | Answer: 472 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 32.1 m^2 carrying a factored load of 12.9 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 32.1, w = 12.9 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 12.9 * 32.1 | Answer: 414.1 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 6.6 m, unit weight 16 kN/m^3, phi = 29 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 3e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.3, area = 5.3e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 3, i = 0.3, A = 5.3 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (3e-4)*0.3*(5.3e-3) | Answer: 477 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.1 m, bed slope 0.003 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.017. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 1.1 m under a head of 1.1 m. Taking Cd = 0.63 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 4.6 m wide carries a discharge of 25 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 250 m and design speed 45 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 250, V = 45 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (45)^2 / (127*250) | Answer: 0.06378
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: A tank of volume 490 m^3 treats a flow of 35 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 490, Q = 35 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 490 / 35 | Answer: 14 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 360 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.21 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 5 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 360, k = 0.21, t = 5 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 360*(1 - e^(-0.21*5)) | Answer: 234 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.64, rainfall intensity 45 mm/h over a catchment of 30 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.64, i = 45, A = 30 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.64*45*30 / 360 | Answer: 2.4 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.02 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 350 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.02, M = 350 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 350*(20+0.02)/20 | Answer: 350.4 m

question: Convert the decimal number 1206 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 1206 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 4B6 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 11010000 and 10001101.
solution: XOR: 01011101 | Count of 1s = 5 | Answer: 5
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 890 megabits is sent over a link of 33 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 890, B = 33 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 890 / 33 | Answer: 26.97 s

question: A link has bandwidth 51 Mbps and round-trip time 180 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 51, R = 180 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 51e6 * 180e-3 bits = 9180 kb | Answer: 9180 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.94, cache access time 9 ns and main-memory access time 150 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.94, tc = 9, tm = 150 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.94*9 + (1 - 0.94)*150 | Answer: 17.46 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 452077 elements?
solution: Given: n = 452077 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(452077)) + 1 | Answer: 19

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.017, memory access time 80 ns and page-fault service time 6 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 6 ms = 6000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.017)*80 + 0.017*6000000.0 ns | Answer: 102.1 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 1.8 m^3 at 260 kPa and 590 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 1.8, P = 260, Tk = 590 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (260e3)*1.8 / (8.314*590) | Answer: 95.41 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.05 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 13 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.05, t = 13 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.05*13) | Answer: 0.478

question: For a reaction with A = 3e10 /s and activation energy 60 kJ/mol at 370 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 3, Ea = 60, Tk = 370 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 3e10 * exp(-60e3 / (8.314*370)) | Answer: 101.5 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.98 and bottoms xW = 0.08, with relative volatility alpha = 2.1. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.98, xw = 0.08, al = 2.1 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.98/0.02)(0.92/0.08)] / ln(2.1) | Answer: 8.537 stages

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.61 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 60 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.61, Psat = 60 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.61 * 60 | Answer: 36.6 kPa

question: A stream of 3.9 kg/s with specific heat 4 kJ/kg-K is heated through 40 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 3.9, cp = 4, dT = 40 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 3.9*4*40 | Answer: 624 kW

question: A reactor of volume 16.3 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 3.7 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 16.3, Q = 3.7 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 16.3 / 3.7 | Answer: 4.405 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 1.4e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 1 mm with a concentration difference of 60 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 1.4, L = 1, dC = 60 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (1.4e-9)*60 / (1e-3) | Answer: 84 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 8.8 min and steady-state gain 1.6. For a step input of magnitude 11, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 8.8, K = 1.6, M = 11 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 1.6 * 11 | Answer: 17.6 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 70 m^2 flies at 100 m/s (air density 1.225 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 1.1. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 70, V = 100, rho = 1.225, CL = 1.1 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1.225*(100)^2*70*1.1 / 1000 | Answer: 471.6 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 60 m^2 flies at 190 m/s (density 0.7 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.06. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 60, V = 190, rho = 0.7, CD = 0.06 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.7*(190)^2*60*0.06 / 1000 | Answer: 45.49 kN

question: A block of mass 39 kg has a volume of 0.7e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 39, V = 0.7 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 39 / (0.7e-3) | Answer: 55714 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 1200 mm is heated through 85 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 11e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 1200, dT = 85, al = 11 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 1200*11e-6*85 | Answer: 1.122 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 170 ohm, R2 = 70 ohm and R3 = 265 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 170, R2 = 70, R3 = 265 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 70*265 / 170 | Answer: 109.1 ohm

question: A measurement reads 9.55 when the true value is 20. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.55, true = 20 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.55 - 20| / 20 * 100 | Answer: 52.25 %

question: Annual demand is 24500 units, ordering cost 290 per order and holding cost 35 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 24500, S = 290, H = 35 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*24500*290 / 35) | Answer: 637.2 units

question: An asset costs 150000 with salvage value 4000 after 20 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 150000, Sv = 4000, n = 20 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (150000 - 4000) / 20 | Answer: 7300 per year

question: A product sells for 210 per unit with variable cost 190 per unit and fixed costs 90000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 210, V = 190, F = 90000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 90000 / (210 - 190) | Answer: 4500 units

question: Find the present worth of 45000 received 8 years from now at an interest rate of 11% per year.
solution: Given: F = 45000, n = 8, i = 11 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 45000 / (1 + 0.11)^8 | Answer: 19527 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.97, 0.97 and 0.96 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.97, r2 = 0.97, r3 = 0.96 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.97*0.97*0.96 | Answer: 0.9033

question: A process produces 24 defective items in a batch of 15500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 24, N = 15500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 24/15500 * 1e6 | Answer: 1548 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -3x^3 + 6x^2 + 2x - 3 evaluated at x = 0.
For f(x) = 5x^3 - 7x^2 + 9x - 2, find f''(x) at x = 0.
Evaluate the definite integral of (-3x^2 - x + 2) dx from x = 2 to x = 5.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = -3x^3/3 + -1x^2/2 + 2x | Evaluate F(5) - F(2) | Answer: -121.5
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 4x^2 - 8x - 6 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[-9, 2], [7, -9]].
solution: Given: a = -9, b = 2, c = 7, d = -9 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (-9)(-9) - (2)(7) | Answer: 67

question: Find the determinant of [[6, 0, 0], [4, -5, 6], [4, -2, 4]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: -48

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[-4, -2], [-2, -2]].
solution: Trace tr = -6, Determinant = 4 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: -0.7639

question: Solve for x: -3x + -6y = -8 and 6x + 4y = 10.
solution: Determinant = -3*4 - -6*6 = 24 | x = (e d - b f) / det = 1.167 | Answer: x = 1.167
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 75, 65, 62, 89, 52.
solution: Sum = 343 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 68.6 | Answer: 68.6

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 28, 49, 2, 50, 29.
solution: Mean = 31.6 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 19.6

question: Find the slope of the line through (-3, -1) and (1, -6).
solution: Given: x1 = -3, y1 = -1, x2 = 1, y2 = -6 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (-6 - -1) / (1 - -3) | Answer: -1.25

question: Find the distance between the points (3, 9) and (2, -2).
solution: Given: x1 = 3, y1 = 9, x2 = 2, y2 = -2 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-1)^2 + (-11)^2) | Answer: 11.05 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (1,-8), (2,5), (0,8).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 14.5 sq units

question: Find the 40th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 19 and common difference 2.
solution: Given: a = 19, d = 2, n = 40 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = 19 + (40 - 1)*2 | Answer: 97

question: Find the sum of the first 16 terms of an AP with first term 11 and common difference 2.
solution: Given: a = 11, d = 2, n = 16 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 16/2 [2*11 + (16-1)*2] | Answer: 416

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 26500 at 11.4% per annum for 6 years.
solution: Given: P = 26500, R = 11.4, Tt = 6 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 26500 * 11.4 * 6 / 100 | Answer: 18126 currency units

question: Find the amount when 25000 is invested at 10.1% per annum compounded annually for 5 years.
solution: Given: P = 25000, R = 10.1, Tt = 5 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 25000 * (1 + 10.1/100)^5 | Answer: 40446 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (-1, 5, -8) and (-3, 6, 6).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (1, -5, 1) and (1, -1, -3).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 16.97

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (-2, 1, -3) and (4, -4, 4).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 157.8 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -x^3 + 7x^2 + 9x - 7 at x = -5.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-68 with initial guess x0=14, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=0.7 and ordinates 10, 17, 9, 1, 2, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 294 and 164.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 294 and 164 | Answer: GCD = 2

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 29 and 21.
solution: Given: a = 29, b = 21 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 29*21 / 1 | Answer: 609
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 54 mm carries an axial tensile load of 117 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 19 mm and length 1700 mm carries an axial load of 49 kN. Take E = 110 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 36 mm transmits a torque of 150 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 36, Tt = 150 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(150*1000) / (pi*(36)^3) | Answer: 16.37 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 31 mm and length 1300 mm carries a torque of 800 N-m. With G = 45 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (31)^4 / 32 = 90666 mm^4 | theta = (800*1000)(1300) / (45000 * 90666) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 14.6 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 86 mm wide and 220 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 86, h = 220 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 86*(220)^2 / 6 | Answer: 693733 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (100 mm x 110 mm) carries a bending moment of 5 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (37 mm x 140 mm) has effective length 1500 mm and E = 200 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 760 MPa is designed for a working stress of 220 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 760, sw = 220 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 760 / 220 | Answer: 3.455

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1250 mm and wall thickness 10 mm carries an internal pressure of 1.6 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1250, t = 10, P = 1.6 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 1.6*1250 / (2*10) | Answer: 100 MPa

question: 7.3 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 145 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 7.3, dT = 145 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 7.3 * 0.718 * 145 | Answer: 760 kJ

question: 6.3 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 35 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 6.3, dT = 35 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 6.3 * 1.005 * 35 | Answer: 221.6 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 3.8 m^3 at 500 K with mass 4.3 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 3.8, Tk = 500, m = 4.3 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 4.3*0.287*500 / 3.8 | Answer: 162.4 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 4.1 kg of air expands isothermally at 430 K from volume V1 to 3*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.1, Tk = 430, ratio = 3 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 4.1*0.287*430*ln(3) | Answer: 555.9 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 3.6 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.19 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 3.6, D = 0.19 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*3.6*0.19 / 0.001 | Answer: 684000

question: Water flows at 3.2 m/s through a pipe of diameter 210 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 19.5 m. Taking Cv = 0.96, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 19.5, cv = 0.96 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.96*sqrt(2*9.81*19.5) | Answer: 18.78 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 210 mm) water flows at 2.1 m/s. It contracts to diameter 120 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
Water flows at 2.2 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.1 m and length 460 m. With friction factor f = 0.028, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 35 teeth drives a gear of 75 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1050 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 35, z2 = 75, N1 = 1050 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1050*35 / 75 | Answer: 490 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 220 mm rotates at 1300 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 220, N = 1300 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.22)*1300 / 60 | Answer: 14.97 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 23.5 kW at 600 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 23.5, N = 600 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(23.5*1000) / (2*pi*600) | Answer: 374 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 7.4 kg rotates at radius 0.5 m at 600 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 11100 N/m and mass 3.1 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 11100, m = 3.1 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(11100/3.1) | Answer: 9.524 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 9.2 m^2 and thickness 0.26 m has conductivity k = 40.5 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 110 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 9.2, L = 0.26, k = 40.5, dT = 110 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 40.5*9.2*110 / 0.26 | Answer: 157638 W

question: A surface of area 5.8 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 45 W/m^2-K to surroundings 20 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 5.8, h = 45, dT = 20 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 45*5.8*20 | Answer: 5220 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 100 m/min, feed = 0.26 mm/rev, depth of cut = 1.8 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 100, f = 0.26, d = 1.8 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*100*0.26*1.8 | Answer: 46800 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 270 mm is turned at 700 rpm with a feed of 0.21 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 270, N = 700, f = 0.21 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 270 / (0.21*700) | Answer: 1.837 min

question: A resistor of 22 ohm carries a current of 9.3 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 22, I = 9.3 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 9.3 * 22 | Answer: 204.6 V

question: Three resistors 44 ohm, 97 ohm and 93 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 44, R2 = 97, R3 = 93 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 44 + 97 + 93 | Answer: 234 ohm

question: Two resistors 45 ohm and 12 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 45, R2 = 12 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 45*12 / (45+12) | Answer: 9.474 ohm

question: A device draws 3.1 A at 240 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 240, I = 3.1 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 240 * 3.1 | Answer: 744 W

question: A current of 6.1 A flows through a 75 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 6.1, R = 75 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (6.1)^2 * 75 | Answer: 2791 W

question: Two capacitors 8.8 uF and 34.2 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 8.8, C2 = 34.2 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 8.8*34.2 / (8.8+34.2) | Answer: 6.999 uF

question: A resistor 18 kohm and capacitor 14.4 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 18, C = 14.4 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (18k)(14.4u) = 259.2 ms | Answer: 259.2 ms

question: An inductor 109 mH is in series with 157 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 109, R = 157 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (109e-3) / 157 | Answer: 0.6943 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 98.8 mH inductor at 490 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 98.8, f = 490 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (490)(98.8e-3) | Answer: 304.2 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 47.3 uF capacitor at 980 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 47.3, f = 980 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (980)(47.3e-6)) | Answer: 3.433 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 9 ohm, XL = 100 ohm and XC = 56 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 9, XL = 100, XC = 56 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(9^2 + (100 - 56)^2) | Answer: 44.91 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 52.1 mH and C = 3.1 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 52.1, C = 3.1 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(52.1e-3 * 3.1e-6)) | Answer: 396 Hz

question: A capacitor of 34.2 uF is charged to 85 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 34.2, V = 85 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*34.2e-6*(85)^2 | Answer: 123.5 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 240 V with 720 primary turns and 150 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 240, N1 = 720, N2 = 150 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 240 * 150/720 | Answer: 50 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 230 V and draws an armature current of 33 A. If the armature resistance is 0.61 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 230, Ia = 33, Ra = 0.61 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 230 - 33*0.61 | Answer: 209.9 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 185 A at 433 V (line) with a power factor of 0.81. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 185, VL = 433, pf = 0.81 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*433*185*0.81 / 1000 | Answer: 112.4 kW

question: A load has real power 15 kW and apparent power 85 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 15, S = 85 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 15 / 85 | Answer: 0.1765

question: A machine delivers 185 kW output while drawing 217 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 185, Pi = 217 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 185/217 * 100 | Answer: 85.25 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 16 V across R1 = 24 ohm and R2 = 17 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 16, R1 = 24, R2 = 17 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 16*17 / (24+17) | Answer: 6.634 V

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 120 kohm and Rg = 17 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 120, Rg = 17 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 120/17 | Answer: 8.059

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 9549. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 9549 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(9549) | Answer: 39.8 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.2 m carries a central point load of 45 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6.2, W = 45 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 45*6.2 / 4 | Answer: 69.75 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 7.8 m carries a UDL of 40 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7.8, w = 40 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 40*(7.8)^2 / 8 | Answer: 304.2 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 7.3 m carries a point load 80 kN at distance 1.8 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 7.3, a = 1.8, W = 80 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 80*(7.3 - 1.8) / 7.3 | Answer: 60.27 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 7 m) carries a central point load 75 kN. With E = 30 GPa and I = 70e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=75000 N, L=7000.0 mm, E=30000 MPa, I=70e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 255.2 mm

question: An RC beam has overall depth 450 mm, clear cover 40 mm and main bars of diameter 16 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 450, c = 40, dia = 16 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 450 - 40 - 16/2 | Answer: 402 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 25.4 m^2 carrying a factored load of 19.8 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 25.4, w = 19.8 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 19.8 * 25.4 | Answer: 502.9 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 3.9 m, unit weight 17 kN/m^3, phi = 32 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 6.3e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.6, area = 7.6e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 6.3, i = 0.6, A = 7.6 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (6.3e-4)*0.6*(7.6e-3) | Answer: 2873 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 0.8 m, bed slope 0.009 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.017. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 3.3 m under a head of 1 m. Taking Cd = 0.61 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 3.5 m wide carries a discharge of 23.1 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 250 m and design speed 55 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 250, V = 55 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (55)^2 / (127*250) | Answer: 0.09528
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: A tank of volume 230 m^3 treats a flow of 155 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 230, Q = 155 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 230 / 155 | Answer: 1.484 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 370 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.2 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 6 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 370, k = 0.2, t = 6 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 370*(1 - e^(-0.2*6)) | Answer: 258.6 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.3, rainfall intensity 55 mm/h over a catchment of 22.2 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.3, i = 55, A = 22.2 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.3*55*22.2 / 360 | Answer: 1.018 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.08 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 660 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.08, M = 660 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 660*(20+0.08)/20 | Answer: 662.6 m

question: Convert the decimal number 1722 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 1722 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 6BA (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 11001110 and 10000100.
solution: XOR: 01001010 | Count of 1s = 3 | Answer: 3
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 590 megabits is sent over a link of 38 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 590, B = 38 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 590 / 38 | Answer: 15.53 s

question: A link has bandwidth 80 Mbps and round-trip time 100 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 80, R = 100 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 80e6 * 100e-3 bits = 8000 kb | Answer: 8000 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.92, cache access time 4 ns and main-memory access time 200 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.92, tc = 4, tm = 200 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.92*4 + (1 - 0.92)*200 | Answer: 19.68 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 956309 elements?
solution: Given: n = 956309 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(956309)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.014, memory access time 90 ns and page-fault service time 9 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 9 ms = 9000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.014)*90 + 0.014*9000000.0 ns | Answer: 126.1 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 1.2 m^3 at 290 kPa and 340 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 1.2, P = 290, Tk = 340 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (290e3)*1.2 / (8.314*340) | Answer: 123.1 mol

question: For a reaction with A = 7e10 /s and activation energy 80 kJ/mol at 370 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 7, Ea = 80, Tk = 370 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 7e10 * exp(-80e3 / (8.314*370)) | Answer: 0.3554 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.95 and bottoms xW = 0.08, with relative volatility alpha = 1.8. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.95, xw = 0.08, al = 1.8 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.95/0.05)(0.92/0.08)] / ln(1.8) | Answer: 9.165 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.65 and x = 0.35. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.65, x = 0.35 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.65/0.35) / (0.35/0.65) | Answer: 3.449

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.58 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 70 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.58, Psat = 70 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.58 * 70 | Answer: 40.6 kPa

question: A stream of 5.2 kg/s with specific heat 3.1 kJ/kg-K is heated through 120 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 5.2, cp = 3.1, dT = 120 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 5.2*3.1*120 | Answer: 1934 kW

question: A reactor of volume 6.7 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 0.9 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 6.7, Q = 0.9 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 6.7 / 0.9 | Answer: 7.444 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 7.5e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 5 mm with a concentration difference of 190 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 7.5, L = 5, dC = 190 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (7.5e-9)*190 / (5e-3) | Answer: 285 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 6.5 min and steady-state gain 1.2. For a step input of magnitude 19, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 6.5, K = 1.2, M = 19 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 1.2 * 19 | Answer: 22.8 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 100 m^2 flies at 100 m/s (air density 0.4 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 0.8. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 100, V = 100, rho = 0.4, CL = 0.8 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.4*(100)^2*100*0.8 / 1000 | Answer: 160 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 50 m^2 flies at 220 m/s (density 0.4 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.04. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 50, V = 220, rho = 0.4, CD = 0.04 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.4*(220)^2*50*0.04 / 1000 | Answer: 19.36 kN

question: A specimen under stress 280 MPa shows an elastic strain of 2.4e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 280, eps = 2.4 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 280 / (2.4e-3) MPa = 116.7 GPa | Answer: 116.7 GPa

question: A block of mass 35 kg has a volume of 0.9e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 35, V = 0.9 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 35 / (0.9e-3) | Answer: 38889 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 2500 mm is heated through 25 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 11e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 2500, dT = 25, al = 11 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 2500*11e-6*25 | Answer: 0.6875 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 140 ohm, R2 = 155 ohm and R3 = 485 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 140, R2 = 155, R3 = 485 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 155*485 / 140 | Answer: 537 ohm

question: Annual demand is 2500 units, ordering cost 160 per order and holding cost 36 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 2500, S = 160, H = 36 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*2500*160 / 36) | Answer: 149.1 units

question: An asset costs 430000 with salvage value 22000 after 14 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 430000, Sv = 22000, n = 14 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (430000 - 22000) / 14 | Answer: 29143 per year

question: A product sells for 180 per unit with variable cost 90 per unit and fixed costs 120000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 180, V = 90, F = 120000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 120000 / (180 - 90) | Answer: 1333 units

question: Find the present worth of 80000 received 9 years from now at an interest rate of 9% per year.
solution: Given: F = 80000, n = 9, i = 9 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 80000 / (1 + 0.09)^9 | Answer: 36834 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.93, 0.94 and 0.95 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.93, r2 = 0.94, r3 = 0.95 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.93*0.94*0.95 | Answer: 0.8305

question: A process produces 17 defective items in a batch of 3000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 17, N = 3000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 17/3000 * 1e6 | Answer: 5667 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = 3x^3 + 7x^2 - 9x + 9 evaluated at x = -2.
For f(x) = -6x^3 - 4x^2 + 3x + 7, find f''(x) at x = 2.
Evaluate the definite integral of (4x^2 + 6x + 8) dx from x = 0 to x = 5.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = 4x^3/3 + 6x^2/2 + 8x | Evaluate F(5) - F(0) | Answer: 281.7
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 6x^2 + 2x - 4 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[-9, 1], [4, -8]].
solution: Given: a = -9, b = 1, c = 4, d = -8 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (-9)(-8) - (1)(4) | Answer: 68

question: Find the determinant of [[-2, -2, 1], [-4, -5, 1], [-2, 5, 5]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: -6

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[2, -1], [0, 0]].
solution: Trace tr = 2, Determinant = 0 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 2

question: Solve for x: -4x + 6y = 3 and 6x + -6y = 3.
solution: Determinant = -4*-6 - 6*6 = -12 | x = (e d - b f) / det = 3 | Answer: x = 3
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 55, 59, 59, 40, 17.
solution: Sum = 230 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 46 | Answer: 46

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 12, 38, 7, 19, 4.
solution: Mean = 16 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 13.55

question: Find the slope of the line through (4, -7) and (9, 2).
solution: Given: x1 = 4, y1 = -7, x2 = 9, y2 = 2 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (2 - -7) / (9 - 4) | Answer: 1.8

question: Find the distance between the points (7, 0) and (-5, -4).
solution: Given: x1 = 7, y1 = 0, x2 = -5, y2 = -4 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-12)^2 + (-4)^2) | Answer: 12.65 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (6,2), (8,-3), (7,-8).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 7.5 sq units

question: Find the 8th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 12 and common difference -5.
solution: Given: a = 12, d = -5, n = 8 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = 12 + (8 - 1)*-5 | Answer: -23

question: Find the sum of the first 39 terms of an AP with first term -3 and common difference 3.
solution: Given: a = -3, d = 3, n = 39 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 39/2 [2*-3 + (39-1)*3] | Answer: 2106

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 28000 at 11.9% per annum for 5 years.
solution: Given: P = 28000, R = 11.9, Tt = 5 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 28000 * 11.9 * 5 / 100 | Answer: 16660 currency units

question: Find the amount when 15000 is invested at 8.6% per annum compounded annually for 2 years.
solution: Given: P = 15000, R = 8.6, Tt = 2 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 15000 * (1 + 8.6/100)^2 | Answer: 17691 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (7, 0, 4) and (-1, 8, 1).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (0, 6, 0) and (-1, -2, 4).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 24.74

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (-1, -3, -4) and (2, -3, -6).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 29.71 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -5x^3 + x^2 - 3x + 8 at x = -5.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-148 with initial guess x0=9, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.3 and ordinates 2, 8, 3, 9, 14, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 125 and 265.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 125 and 265 | Answer: GCD = 5

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 11 and 44.
solution: Given: a = 11, b = 44 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 11*44 / 11 | Answer: 44
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 41 mm carries an axial tensile load of 47 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 19 mm and length 1700 mm carries an axial load of 89 kN. Take E = 200 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 80 mm transmits a torque of 2400 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 80, Tt = 2400 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(2400*1000) / (pi*(80)^3) | Answer: 23.87 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 34 mm and length 1900 mm carries a torque of 1550 N-m. With G = 45 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (34)^4 / 32 = 131194 mm^4 | theta = (1550*1000)(1900) / (45000 * 131194) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 28.58 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 126 mm wide and 60 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 126, h = 60 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 126*(60)^2 / 6 | Answer: 75600 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (46 mm x 80 mm) carries a bending moment of 22 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (45 mm x 140 mm) has effective length 2900 mm and E = 200 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 510 MPa is designed for a working stress of 200 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 510, sw = 200 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 510 / 200 | Answer: 2.55

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1300 mm and wall thickness 14 mm carries an internal pressure of 1.5 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1300, t = 14, P = 1.5 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 1.5*1300 / (2*14) | Answer: 69.64 MPa

question: 2 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 70 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2, dT = 70 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 2 * 0.718 * 70 | Answer: 100.5 kJ

question: 3.3 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 55 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.3, dT = 55 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 3.3 * 1.005 * 55 | Answer: 182.4 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 1.8 m^3 at 540 K with mass 3.7 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 1.8, Tk = 540, m = 3.7 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 3.7*0.287*540 / 1.8 | Answer: 318.6 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 3.2 kg of air expands isothermally at 480 K from volume V1 to 5*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.2, Tk = 480, ratio = 5 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 3.2*0.287*480*ln(5) | Answer: 709.5 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 0.7 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.09 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 0.7, D = 0.09 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*0.7*0.09 / 0.001 | Answer: 63000

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 20 m. Taking Cv = 0.99, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 20, cv = 0.99 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.99*sqrt(2*9.81*20) | Answer: 19.61 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 230 mm) water flows at 2.4 m/s. It contracts to diameter 130 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
Water flows at 1.4 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.43 m and length 450 m. With friction factor f = 0.039, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 35 teeth drives a gear of 75 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1500 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 35, z2 = 75, N1 = 1500 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1500*35 / 75 | Answer: 700 rpm

question: A shaft transmits 41 kW at 1450 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 41, N = 1450 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(41*1000) / (2*pi*1450) | Answer: 270 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 9.6 kg rotates at radius 0.17 m at 850 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 3100 N/m and mass 9.2 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 3100, m = 9.2 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(3100/9.2) | Answer: 2.922 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 7.1 m^2 and thickness 0.21 m has conductivity k = 27.1 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 45 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 7.1, L = 0.21, k = 27.1, dT = 45 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 27.1*7.1*45 / 0.21 | Answer: 41231 W

question: A surface of area 5.5 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 175 W/m^2-K to surroundings 150 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 5.5, h = 175, dT = 150 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 175*5.5*150 | Answer: 144375 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 150 m/min, feed = 0.27 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2.4 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 150, f = 0.27, d = 2.4 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*150*0.27*2.4 | Answer: 97200 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 360 mm is turned at 1050 rpm with a feed of 0.14 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 360, N = 1050, f = 0.14 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 360 / (0.14*1050) | Answer: 2.449 min

question: A resistor of 72 ohm carries a current of 4.3 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 72, I = 4.3 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 4.3 * 72 | Answer: 309.6 V

question: Three resistors 1 ohm, 52 ohm and 8 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 1, R2 = 52, R3 = 8 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 1 + 52 + 8 | Answer: 61 ohm

question: Two resistors 102 ohm and 16 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 102, R2 = 16 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 102*16 / (102+16) | Answer: 13.83 ohm

question: A device draws 11.8 A at 10 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 10, I = 11.8 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 10 * 11.8 | Answer: 118 W

question: A current of 6.1 A flows through a 10 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 6.1, R = 10 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (6.1)^2 * 10 | Answer: 372.1 W

question: Two capacitors 31.8 uF and 33.6 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 31.8, C2 = 33.6 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 31.8*33.6 / (31.8+33.6) | Answer: 16.34 uF

question: A resistor 81 kohm and capacitor 1.1 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 81, C = 1.1 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (81k)(1.1u) = 89.1 ms | Answer: 89.1 ms

question: An inductor 168.1 mH is in series with 7 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 168.1, R = 7 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (168.1e-3) / 7 | Answer: 24.01 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 129.3 mH inductor at 390 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 129.3, f = 390 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (390)(129.3e-3) | Answer: 316.8 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 43.3 uF capacitor at 50 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 43.3, f = 50 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (50)(43.3e-6)) | Answer: 73.51 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 88 ohm, XL = 89 ohm and XC = 22 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 88, XL = 89, XC = 22 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(88^2 + (89 - 22)^2) | Answer: 110.6 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 99.9 mH and C = 1.3 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 99.9, C = 1.3 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(99.9e-3 * 1.3e-6)) | Answer: 441.6 Hz

question: A capacitor of 99.8 uF is charged to 230 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 99.8, V = 230 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*99.8e-6*(230)^2 | Answer: 264 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 130 V with 890 primary turns and 470 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 130, N1 = 890, N2 = 470 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 130 * 470/890 | Answer: 68.65 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 120 V and draws an armature current of 19 A. If the armature resistance is 0.79 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 120, Ia = 19, Ra = 0.79 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 120 - 19*0.79 | Answer: 105 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 160 A at 400 V (line) with a power factor of 0.89. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 160, VL = 400, pf = 0.89 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*400*160*0.89 / 1000 | Answer: 98.66 kW

question: A load has real power 60 kW and apparent power 90 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 60, S = 90 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 60 / 90 | Answer: 0.6667

question: A machine delivers 10 kW output while drawing 137 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 10, Pi = 137 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 10/137 * 100 | Answer: 7.299 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 6 V across R1 = 44 ohm and R2 = 19 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 6, R1 = 44, R2 = 19 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 6*19 / (44+19) | Answer: 1.81 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 110 kohm and Rin = 25 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 110, Rin = 25 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 110 / 25 | Answer: 4.4

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 60 kohm and Rg = 21 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 60, Rg = 21 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 60/21 | Answer: 3.857

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 6. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 6 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(6) | Answer: 7.782 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.8 m carries a central point load of 45 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6.8, W = 45 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 45*6.8 / 4 | Answer: 76.5 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 5.8 m carries a UDL of 40 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.8, w = 40 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 40*(5.8)^2 / 8 | Answer: 168.2 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 3.8 m carries a point load 80 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.8, W = 80 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 80*3.8 | Answer: 304 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 3.9 m carries a UDL of 16 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 3.9, w = 16 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 16*(3.9)^2 / 2 | Answer: 121.7 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 6 m carries a point load 50 kN at distance 1.5 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 6, a = 1.5, W = 50 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 50*(6 - 1.5) / 6 | Answer: 37.5 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 3.3 m) carries a central point load 40 kN. With E = 200 GPa and I = 450e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=40000 N, L=3300.0 mm, E=200000 MPa, I=450e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 0.3327 mm

question: An RC beam has overall depth 430 mm, clear cover 30 mm and main bars of diameter 20 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 430, c = 30, dia = 20 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 430 - 30 - 20/2 | Answer: 390 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 33.8 m^2 carrying a factored load of 11.8 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 33.8, w = 11.8 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 11.8 * 33.8 | Answer: 398.8 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 4.1 m, unit weight 19 kN/m^3, phi = 32 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 6.4e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1.5, area = 5.8e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 6.4, i = 1.5, A = 5.8 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (6.4e-4)*1.5*(5.8e-3) | Answer: 5568 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.3 m, bed slope 0.003 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.016. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 1.5 m under a head of 0.7 m. Taking Cd = 0.64 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 3.3 m wide carries a discharge of 25 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A highway curve has radius 220 m and design speed 80 km/h. Ignoring friction, find the superelevation required (as a ratio).
solution: Given: R = 220, V = 80 | Formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m) | Substitute: e = (80)^2 / (127*220) | Answer: 0.2291
formula: e = V^2 / (127 R)  (V in km/h, R in m)

question: A tank of volume 470 m^3 treats a flow of 115 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 470, Q = 115 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 470 / 115 | Answer: 4.087 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 330 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.21 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 3 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 330, k = 0.21, t = 3 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 330*(1 - e^(-0.21*3)) | Answer: 154.2 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.82, rainfall intensity 80 mm/h over a catchment of 22.5 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.82, i = 80, A = 22.5 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.82*80*22.5 / 360 | Answer: 4.1 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: Convert the decimal number 426 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 426 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 1AA (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 01110110 and 01100011.
solution: XOR: 00010101 | Count of 1s = 3 | Answer: 3
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 980 megabits is sent over a link of 77 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 980, B = 77 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 980 / 77 | Answer: 12.73 s

question: A link has bandwidth 29 Mbps and round-trip time 70 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 29, R = 70 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 29e6 * 70e-3 bits = 2030 kb | Answer: 2030 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.89, cache access time 6 ns and main-memory access time 50 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.89, tc = 6, tm = 50 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.89*6 + (1 - 0.89)*50 | Answer: 10.84 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 875127 elements?
solution: Given: n = 875127 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(875127)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.018, memory access time 120 ns and page-fault service time 10 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 10 ms = 10000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.018)*120 + 0.018*10000000.0 ns | Answer: 180.1 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 1.2 m^3 at 350 kPa and 510 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 1.2, P = 350, Tk = 510 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (350e3)*1.2 / (8.314*510) | Answer: 99.05 mol

question: For a reaction with A = 2e10 /s and activation energy 80 kJ/mol at 360 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 2, Ea = 80, Tk = 360 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 2e10 * exp(-80e3 / (8.314*360)) | Answer: 0.04931 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.91 and bottoms xW = 0.04, with relative volatility alpha = 2.3. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.91, xw = 0.04, al = 2.3 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.91/0.09)(0.96/0.04)] / ln(2.3) | Answer: 6.593 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.55 and x = 0.44. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.55, x = 0.44 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.55/0.45) / (0.44/0.56) | Answer: 1.556

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.21 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 55 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.21, Psat = 55 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.21 * 55 | Answer: 11.55 kPa

question: A stream of 6.7 kg/s with specific heat 1.4 kJ/kg-K is heated through 80 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 6.7, cp = 1.4, dT = 80 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 6.7*1.4*80 | Answer: 750.4 kW

question: A reactor of volume 2.7 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 0.7 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 2.7, Q = 0.7 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 2.7 / 0.7 | Answer: 3.857 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 4.2e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 2 mm with a concentration difference of 10 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 4.2, L = 2, dC = 10 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (4.2e-9)*10 / (2e-3) | Answer: 21 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 5.2 min and steady-state gain 3.9. For a step input of magnitude 12, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 5.2, K = 3.9, M = 12 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 3.9 * 12 | Answer: 46.8 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 90 m^2 flies at 220 m/s (air density 1 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 1. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 90, V = 220, rho = 1, CL = 1 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*1*(220)^2*90*1 / 1000 | Answer: 2178 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 35 m^2 flies at 70 m/s (density 0.4 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.05. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 35, V = 70, rho = 0.4, CD = 0.05 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*0.4*(70)^2*35*0.05 / 1000 | Answer: 1.715 kN

question: A specimen under stress 260 MPa shows an elastic strain of 0.8e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 260, eps = 0.8 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 260 / (0.8e-3) MPa = 325 GPa | Answer: 325 GPa

question: A block of mass 37 kg has a volume of 1.1e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 37, V = 1.1 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 37 / (1.1e-3) | Answer: 33636 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 700 mm is heated through 75 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 17e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 700, dT = 75, al = 17 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 700*17e-6*75 | Answer: 0.8925 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 180 ohm, R2 = 155 ohm and R3 = 330 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 180, R2 = 155, R3 = 330 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 155*330 / 180 | Answer: 284.2 ohm

question: Annual demand is 28500 units, ordering cost 150 per order and holding cost 5 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 28500, S = 150, H = 5 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*28500*150 / 5) | Answer: 1308 units

question: An asset costs 310000 with salvage value 12000 after 6 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 310000, Sv = 12000, n = 6 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (310000 - 12000) / 6 | Answer: 49667 per year

question: A product sells for 260 per unit with variable cost 120 per unit and fixed costs 50000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 260, V = 120, F = 50000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 50000 / (260 - 120) | Answer: 357.1 units

question: Find the present worth of 60000 received 10 years from now at an interest rate of 5% per year.
solution: Given: F = 60000, n = 10, i = 5 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 60000 / (1 + 0.05)^10 | Answer: 36835 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.93, 0.99 and 0.95 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.93, r2 = 0.99, r3 = 0.95 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.93*0.99*0.95 | Answer: 0.8747

question: A process produces 5 defective items in a batch of 3000. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 5, N = 3000 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 5/3000 * 1e6 | Answer: 1667 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = 3x^3 + 7x^2 + 6x + 4 evaluated at x = -3.
For f(x) = -3x^3 + 7x^2 + 6x - 4, find f''(x) at x = -1.
Evaluate the definite integral of (-x^2 + x + 6) dx from x = -2 to x = 3.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = -1x^3/3 + 1x^2/2 + 6x | Evaluate F(3) - F(-2) | Answer: 20.83
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 3x^2 + 3x - 2 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[-8, -9], [7, -1]].
solution: Given: a = -8, b = -9, c = 7, d = -1 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (-8)(-1) - (-9)(7) | Answer: 71

question: Find the determinant of [[-1, -5, 6], [-1, 5, 4], [5, -4, -6]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: -182

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[-4, 0], [-1, 5]].
solution: Trace tr = 1, Determinant = -20 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 5

question: Solve for x: -1x + 2y = -10 and -1x + -5y = -12.
solution: Determinant = -1*-5 - 2*-1 = 7 | x = (e d - b f) / det = 10.57 | Answer: x = 10.57
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 29, 71, 98, 48, 16.
solution: Sum = 262 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 52.4 | Answer: 52.4

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 6, 34, 4, 7, 41.
solution: Mean = 18.4 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 17.64

question: Find the slope of the line through (4, -6) and (-7, -8).
Find the distance between the points (9, -2) and (4, 1).
solution: Given: x1 = 9, y1 = -2, x2 = 4, y2 = 1 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-5)^2 + (3)^2) | Answer: 5.831 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (-4,6), (5,-3), (-8,6).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 18 sq units

question: Find the 30th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -8 and common difference 1.
solution: Given: a = -8, d = 1, n = 30 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -8 + (30 - 1)*1 | Answer: 21

question: Find the sum of the first 33 terms of an AP with first term 10 and common difference -4.
solution: Given: a = 10, d = -4, n = 33 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 33/2 [2*10 + (33-1)*-4] | Answer: -1782

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 46500 at 9.2% per annum for 3 years.
solution: Given: P = 46500, R = 9.2, Tt = 3 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 46500 * 9.2 * 3 / 100 | Answer: 12834 currency units

question: Find the amount when 2500 is invested at 11.3% per annum compounded annually for 2 years.
solution: Given: P = 2500, R = 11.3, Tt = 2 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 2500 * (1 + 11.3/100)^2 | Answer: 3097 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (3, -7, -8) and (7, -6, 1).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (-3, 2, -4) and (5, -5, -5).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 46.37

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (-4, -1, 5) and (2, -6, 3).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 73.35 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = x^3 - 5x^2 + 6x - 1 at x = -3.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-48 with initial guess x0=7, find x1 (one iteration).
solution: Given: N = 48, x0 = 7 | Formula: x1 = x0 - (x0^2 - N)/(2 x0) | Substitute: x1 = 7 - ((7)^2 - 48)/(2*7) | Answer: 6.929

question: Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.8 and ordinates 3, 14, 4, 6, 9, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 80 and 390.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 80 and 390 | Answer: GCD = 10

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 25 and 68.
solution: Given: a = 25, b = 68 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 25*68 / 1 | Answer: 1700
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 45 mm carries an axial tensile load of 64 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 39 mm and length 1100 mm carries an axial load of 33 kN. Take E = 110 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 50 mm transmits a torque of 2800 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 50, Tt = 2800 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(2800*1000) / (pi*(50)^3) | Answer: 114.1 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 70 mm and length 1400 mm carries a torque of 250 N-m. With G = 80 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (70)^4 / 32 = 2357176 mm^4 | theta = (250*1000)(1400) / (80000 * 2357176) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 0.1063 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 43 mm wide and 60 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 43, h = 60 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 43*(60)^2 / 6 | Answer: 25800 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (49 mm x 250 mm) carries a bending moment of 12 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (59 mm x 120 mm) has effective length 3900 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 500 MPa is designed for a working stress of 60 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 500, sw = 60 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 500 / 60 | Answer: 8.333

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 500 mm and wall thickness 15 mm carries an internal pressure of 0.9 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 500, t = 15, P = 0.9 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 0.9*500 / (2*15) | Answer: 15 MPa

question: 3.8 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 70 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.8, dT = 70 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 3.8 * 0.718 * 70 | Answer: 191 kJ

question: 5.2 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 150 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 5.2, dT = 150 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 5.2 * 1.005 * 150 | Answer: 783.9 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 2.4 m^3 at 570 K with mass 4.6 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 2.4, Tk = 570, m = 4.6 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 4.6*0.287*570 / 2.4 | Answer: 313.5 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 2.2 kg of air expands isothermally at 340 K from volume V1 to 2*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2.2, Tk = 340, ratio = 2 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 2.2*0.287*340*ln(2) | Answer: 148.8 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 1.5 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.1 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 1.5, D = 0.1 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*1.5*0.1 / 0.001 | Answer: 150000

question: Water issues from an orifice under a head of 9.8 m. Taking Cv = 0.99, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 9.8, cv = 0.99 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.99*sqrt(2*9.81*9.8) | Answer: 13.73 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 230 mm) water flows at 1.8 m/s. It contracts to diameter 60 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
solution: Given: d1 = 230, d2 = 60, V1 = 1.8 | Formula: A1 V1 = A2 V2  =>  V2 = V1 (d1/d2)^2 | Substitute: V2 = 1.8*(230/60)^2 | Answer: 26.45 m/s

question: Water flows at 1.4 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.4 m and length 270 m. With friction factor f = 0.034, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 36 teeth drives a gear of 83 teeth. If the pinion runs at 450 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 36, z2 = 83, N1 = 450 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 450*36 / 83 | Answer: 195.2 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 320 mm rotates at 450 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 320, N = 450 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.32)*450 / 60 | Answer: 7.54 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 45.9 kW at 400 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 45.9, N = 400 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(45.9*1000) / (2*pi*400) | Answer: 1096 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 7.9 kg rotates at radius 0.36 m at 500 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 9800 N/m and mass 17.5 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 9800, m = 17.5 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(9800/17.5) | Answer: 3.766 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 5.1 m^2 and thickness 0.1 m has conductivity k = 8.1 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 80 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 5.1, L = 0.1, k = 8.1, dT = 80 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 8.1*5.1*80 / 0.1 | Answer: 33048 W

question: A surface of area 3.7 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 85 W/m^2-K to surroundings 35 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 3.7, h = 85, dT = 35 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 85*3.7*35 | Answer: 11008 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 80 m/min, feed = 0.49 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2.6 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 80, f = 0.49, d = 2.6 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*80*0.49*2.6 | Answer: 101920 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 260 mm is turned at 550 rpm with a feed of 0.22 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 260, N = 550, f = 0.22 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 260 / (0.22*550) | Answer: 2.149 min

question: A resistor of 100 ohm carries a current of 7.1 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 100, I = 7.1 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 7.1 * 100 | Answer: 710 V

question: Three resistors 47 ohm, 96 ohm and 93 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 47, R2 = 96, R3 = 93 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 47 + 96 + 93 | Answer: 236 ohm
