question: A workpiece of length 210 mm is turned at 500 rpm with a feed of 0.32 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 210, N = 500, f = 0.32 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 210 / (0.32*500) | Answer: 1.312 min

question: A resistor of 84 ohm carries a current of 3 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 84, I = 3 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 3 * 84 | Answer: 252 V

question: Three resistors 29 ohm, 6 ohm and 43 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 29, R2 = 6, R3 = 43 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 29 + 6 + 43 | Answer: 78 ohm

question: Two resistors 96 ohm and 57 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 96, R2 = 57 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 96*57 / (96+57) | Answer: 35.76 ohm

question: A device draws 0.2 A at 140 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 140, I = 0.2 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 140 * 0.2 | Answer: 28 W

question: A current of 3 A flows through a 91 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 3, R = 91 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (3)^2 * 91 | Answer: 819 W

question: Two capacitors 21.8 uF and 47.8 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 21.8, C2 = 47.8 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 21.8*47.8 / (21.8+47.8) | Answer: 14.97 uF

question: A resistor 72 kohm and capacitor 9.5 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 72, C = 9.5 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (72k)(9.5u) = 684 ms | Answer: 684 ms

question: An inductor 92.6 mH is in series with 39 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 92.6, R = 39 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (92.6e-3) / 39 | Answer: 2.374 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 73.1 mH inductor at 330 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 73.1, f = 330 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (330)(73.1e-3) | Answer: 151.6 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 43.9 uF capacitor at 880 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 43.9, f = 880 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (880)(43.9e-6)) | Answer: 4.12 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 89 ohm, XL = 99 ohm and XC = 83 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 89, XL = 99, XC = 83 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(89^2 + (99 - 83)^2) | Answer: 90.43 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 86.2 mH and C = 1.9 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 86.2, C = 1.9 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(86.2e-3 * 1.9e-6)) | Answer: 393.3 Hz

question: A capacitor of 19.8 uF is charged to 210 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 19.8, V = 210 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*19.8e-6*(210)^2 | Answer: 436.6 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 160 V with 490 primary turns and 420 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 160, N1 = 490, N2 = 420 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 160 * 420/490 | Answer: 137.1 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 430 V and draws an armature current of 37 A. If the armature resistance is 0.69 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 430, Ia = 37, Ra = 0.69 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 430 - 37*0.69 | Answer: 404.5 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 90 A at 433 V (line) with a power factor of 0.89. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 90, VL = 433, pf = 0.89 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*433*90*0.89 / 1000 | Answer: 60.07 kW

question: A load has real power 130 kW and apparent power 140 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 130, S = 140 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 130 / 140 | Answer: 0.9286

question: A machine delivers 160 kW output while drawing 162 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 160, Pi = 162 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 160/162 * 100 | Answer: 98.77 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 30 V across R1 = 47 ohm and R2 = 12 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 30, R1 = 47, R2 = 12 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 30*12 / (47+12) | Answer: 6.102 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 200 kohm and Rin = 32 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 200, Rin = 32 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 200 / 32 | Answer: 6.25

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 160 kohm and Rg = 16 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 160, Rg = 16 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 160/16 | Answer: 11

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 8320. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 8320 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(8320) | Answer: 39.2 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 4.8 m carries a central point load of 100 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.8, W = 100 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 100*4.8 / 4 | Answer: 120 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 8.8 m carries a UDL of 50 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 8.8, w = 50 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 8 | Substitute: Mmax = 50*(8.8)^2 / 8 | Answer: 484 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 5 m carries a UDL of 36 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5, w = 36 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 36*(5)^2 / 2 | Answer: 450 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 7.9 m carries a point load 75 kN at distance 1.7 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 7.9, a = 1.7, W = 75 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 75*(7.9 - 1.7) / 7.9 | Answer: 58.86 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 3.6 m) carries a central point load 45 kN. With E = 25 GPa and I = 480e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=45000 N, L=3600.0 mm, E=25000 MPa, I=480e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 3.645 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 6.1 m carries a UDL of 21 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6.1, w = 21 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 21*(6.1)^2 / 12 | Answer: 65.12 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 430 mm, clear cover 45 mm and main bars of diameter 25 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 430, c = 45, dia = 25 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 430 - 45 - 25/2 | Answer: 372.5 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 15 m^2 carrying a factored load of 11.5 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 15, w = 11.5 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 11.5 * 15 | Answer: 172.5 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 6.6 m, unit weight 19 kN/m^3, phi = 37 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 1.7e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1.4, area = 6.5e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 1.7, i = 1.4, A = 6.5 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (1.7e-4)*1.4*(6.5e-3) | Answer: 1547 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 0.9 m, bed slope 0.006 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.025. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 1.3 m under a head of 0.4 m. Taking Cd = 0.61 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 4.6 m wide carries a discharge of 8.1 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A tank of volume 390 m^3 treats a flow of 20 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 390, Q = 20 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 390 / 20 | Answer: 19.5 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 310 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.23 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 3 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 310, k = 0.23, t = 3 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 310*(1 - e^(-0.23*3)) | Answer: 154.5 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.57, rainfall intensity 55 mm/h over a catchment of 38.4 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.57, i = 55, A = 38.4 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.57*55*38.4 / 360 | Answer: 3.344 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.06 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 450 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.06, M = 450 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 450*(30+0.06)/30 | Answer: 450.9 m

question: Convert the decimal number 3924 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 3924 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: F54 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 11110001 and 00001100.
solution: XOR: 11111101 | Count of 1s = 7 | Answer: 7
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 990 megabits is sent over a link of 72 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 990, B = 72 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 990 / 72 | Answer: 13.75 s

question: A link has bandwidth 41 Mbps and round-trip time 70 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 41, R = 70 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 41e6 * 70e-3 bits = 2870 kb | Answer: 2870 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.92, cache access time 1 ns and main-memory access time 200 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.92, tc = 1, tm = 200 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.92*1 + (1 - 0.92)*200 | Answer: 16.92 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 492892 elements?
solution: Given: n = 492892 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(492892)) + 1 | Answer: 19

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.004, memory access time 100 ns and page-fault service time 8 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 8 ms = 8000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.004)*100 + 0.004*8000000.0 ns | Answer: 32.1 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 1.2 m^3 at 140 kPa and 460 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 1.2, P = 140, Tk = 460 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (140e3)*1.2 / (8.314*460) | Answer: 43.93 mol

question: For a reaction with A = 4e10 /s and activation energy 80 kJ/mol at 470 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 4, Ea = 80, Tk = 470 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 4e10 * exp(-80e3 / (8.314*470)) | Answer: 51.37 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.98 and bottoms xW = 0.1, with relative volatility alpha = 1.7. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.98, xw = 0.1, al = 1.7 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.98/0.02)(0.9/0.1)] / ln(1.7) | Answer: 11.48 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.66 and x = 0.31. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.66, x = 0.31 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.66/0.34) / (0.31/0.69) | Answer: 4.321

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.41 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 40 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.41, Psat = 40 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.41 * 40 | Answer: 16.4 kPa

question: A stream of 4.2 kg/s with specific heat 3.9 kJ/kg-K is heated through 25 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 4.2, cp = 3.9, dT = 25 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 4.2*3.9*25 | Answer: 409.5 kW

question: A reactor of volume 12.5 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 2.2 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 12.5, Q = 2.2 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 12.5 / 2.2 | Answer: 5.682 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 3.8e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 3 mm with a concentration difference of 140 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 3.8, L = 3, dC = 140 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (3.8e-9)*140 / (3e-3) | Answer: 177.3 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 2.6 min and steady-state gain 2.7. For a step input of magnitude 2, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 2.6, K = 2.7, M = 2 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 2.7 * 2 | Answer: 5.4 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 45 m^2 flies at 120 m/s (air density 0.4 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 1.2. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 45, V = 120, rho = 0.4, CL = 1.2 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.4*(120)^2*45*1.2 / 1000 | Answer: 155.5 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 115 m^2 flies at 170 m/s (density 1.225 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.09. Find the drag force in kN.
A specimen under stress 380 MPa shows an elastic strain of 1.3e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 380, eps = 1.3 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 380 / (1.3e-3) MPa = 292.3 GPa | Answer: 292.3 GPa

question: A block of mass 46 kg has a volume of 5.7e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 46, V = 5.7 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 46 / (5.7e-3) | Answer: 807 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 700 mm is heated through 35 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 11e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 700, dT = 35, al = 11 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 700*11e-6*35 | Answer: 0.2695 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 115 ohm, R2 = 10 ohm and R3 = 40 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 115, R2 = 10, R3 = 40 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 10*40 / 115 | Answer: 3.478 ohm

question: A measurement reads 10.7 when the true value is 10. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 10.7, true = 10 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |10.7 - 10| / 10 * 100 | Answer: 7 %

question: Annual demand is 10000 units, ordering cost 80 per order and holding cost 19 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 10000, S = 80, H = 19 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*10000*80 / 19) | Answer: 290.2 units

question: An asset costs 340000 with salvage value 36000 after 15 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 340000, Sv = 36000, n = 15 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (340000 - 36000) / 15 | Answer: 20267 per year

question: A product sells for 90 per unit with variable cost 30 per unit and fixed costs 150000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 90, V = 30, F = 150000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 150000 / (90 - 30) | Answer: 2500 units

question: Find the present worth of 85000 received 2 years from now at an interest rate of 12% per year.
solution: Given: F = 85000, n = 2, i = 12 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 85000 / (1 + 0.12)^2 | Answer: 67761 currency units

question: A process produces 45 defective items in a batch of 6500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 45, N = 6500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 45/6500 * 1e6 | Answer: 6923 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = 5x^3 + 7x^2 - 5x + 9 evaluated at x = 5.
For f(x) = x^3 + 6x^2 - 6x - 1, find f''(x) at x = -2.
Evaluate the definite integral of (-5x^2 - 5x + 5) dx from x = 2 to x = 6.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = -5x^3/3 + -5x^2/2 + 5x | Evaluate F(6) - F(2) | Answer: -406.7
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 6x^2 - 6x - 6 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[-7, 1], [-3, -5]].
solution: Given: a = -7, b = 1, c = -3, d = -5 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (-7)(-5) - (1)(-3) | Answer: 38

question: Find the determinant of [[-3, 1, 5], [6, 2, -2], [-6, -1, -1]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: 60

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[5, 0], [-3, -3]].
solution: Trace tr = 2, Determinant = -15 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 5

question: Solve for x: -2x + 1y = 9 and 0x + 6y = 0.
solution: Determinant = -2*6 - 1*0 = -12 | x = (e d - b f) / det = -4.5 | Answer: x = -4.5
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 99, 15, 49, 1, 92.
solution: Sum = 256 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 51.2 | Answer: 51.2

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 33, 40, 13, 44, 6.
solution: Mean = 27.2 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 16.81

question: Find the slope of the line through (-2, 0) and (-3, 9).
solution: Given: x1 = -2, y1 = 0, x2 = -3, y2 = 9 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (9 - 0) / (-3 - -2) | Answer: -9

question: Find the distance between the points (-5, 1) and (-8, 8).
solution: Given: x1 = -5, y1 = 1, x2 = -8, y2 = 8 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-3)^2 + (7)^2) | Answer: 7.616 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (3,-1), (1,-7), (0,-2).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 8 sq units

question: Find the 24th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 4 and common difference -1.
solution: Given: a = 4, d = -1, n = 24 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = 4 + (24 - 1)*-1 | Answer: -19

question: Find the sum of the first 20 terms of an AP with first term 4 and common difference 8.
solution: Given: a = 4, d = 8, n = 20 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 20/2 [2*4 + (20-1)*8] | Answer: 1600

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 15000 at 13.4% per annum for 10 years.
solution: Given: P = 15000, R = 13.4, Tt = 10 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 15000 * 13.4 * 10 / 100 | Answer: 20100 currency units

question: Find the amount when 33000 is invested at 8.3% per annum compounded annually for 5 years.
solution: Given: P = 33000, R = 8.3, Tt = 5 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 33000 * (1 + 8.3/100)^5 | Answer: 49165 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (-1, 5, 4) and (1, 6, -8).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (-2, -4, -4) and (-5, 0, 5).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 41.23

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (2, -1, -5) and (-3, -4, 5).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 134.2 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = x^3 + x^2 - 2x + 8 at x = -3.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-96 with initial guess x0=11, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.3 and ordinates 20, 11, 16, 12, 20, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 31 and 106.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 31 and 106 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 39 and 78.
solution: Given: a = 39, b = 78 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 39*78 / 39 | Answer: 78
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 52 mm carries an axial tensile load of 62 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 18 mm and length 3000 mm carries an axial load of 76 kN. Take E = 70 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 22 mm transmits a torque of 1050 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 22, Tt = 1050 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(1050*1000) / (pi*(22)^3) | Answer: 502.2 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 59 mm and length 1200 mm carries a torque of 1100 N-m. With G = 45 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (59)^4 / 32 = 1189619 mm^4 | theta = (1100*1000)(1200) / (45000 * 1189619) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 1.413 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 32 mm wide and 240 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 32, h = 240 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 32*(240)^2 / 6 | Answer: 307200 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (95 mm x 100 mm) carries a bending moment of 16 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (64 mm x 90 mm) has effective length 1800 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 610 MPa is designed for a working stress of 60 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 610, sw = 60 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 610 / 60 | Answer: 10.17

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 1500 mm and wall thickness 13 mm carries an internal pressure of 1.4 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 1500, t = 13, P = 1.4 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 1.4*1500 / (2*13) | Answer: 80.77 MPa

question: 3.5 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 135 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.5, dT = 135 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 3.5 * 0.718 * 135 | Answer: 339.3 kJ

question: 6.2 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 50 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 6.2, dT = 50 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 6.2 * 1.005 * 50 | Answer: 311.6 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 1.8 m^3 at 350 K with mass 5.1 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 1.8, Tk = 350, m = 5.1 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 5.1*0.287*350 / 1.8 | Answer: 284.6 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 3 kg of air expands isothermally at 370 K from volume V1 to 3*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3, Tk = 370, ratio = 3 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 3*0.287*370*ln(3) | Answer: 350 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 4.5 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.38 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 4.5, D = 0.38 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*4.5*0.38 / 0.001 | Answer: 1710000

question: Water flows at 2 m/s through a pipe of diameter 190 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
In a pipe (diameter 230 mm) water flows at 2.8 m/s. It contracts to diameter 130 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
Water flows at 4 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.13 m and length 340 m. With friction factor f = 0.039, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 33 teeth drives a gear of 91 teeth. If the pinion runs at 850 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 33, z2 = 91, N1 = 850 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 850*33 / 91 | Answer: 308.2 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 150 mm rotates at 450 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 150, N = 450 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.15)*450 / 60 | Answer: 3.534 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 48.8 kW at 650 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 48.8, N = 650 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(48.8*1000) / (2*pi*650) | Answer: 716.9 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 7.3 kg rotates at radius 0.4 m at 650 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 800 N/m and mass 7.2 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 800, m = 7.2 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(800/7.2) | Answer: 1.678 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 3.9 m^2 and thickness 0.25 m has conductivity k = 34.7 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 145 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 3.9, L = 0.25, k = 34.7, dT = 145 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 34.7*3.9*145 / 0.25 | Answer: 78491 W

question: A surface of area 4.8 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 10 W/m^2-K to surroundings 65 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 4.8, h = 10, dT = 65 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 10*4.8*65 | Answer: 3120 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 170 m/min, feed = 0.19 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2.8 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 170, f = 0.19, d = 2.8 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*170*0.19*2.8 | Answer: 90440 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 230 mm is turned at 450 rpm with a feed of 0.38 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 230, N = 450, f = 0.38 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 230 / (0.38*450) | Answer: 1.345 min

question: A resistor of 91 ohm carries a current of 1.4 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 91, I = 1.4 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 1.4 * 91 | Answer: 127.4 V

question: Three resistors 47 ohm, 14 ohm and 40 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 47, R2 = 14, R3 = 40 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 47 + 14 + 40 | Answer: 101 ohm

question: Two resistors 95 ohm and 13 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 95, R2 = 13 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 95*13 / (95+13) | Answer: 11.44 ohm

question: A device draws 1.8 A at 105 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 105, I = 1.8 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 105 * 1.8 | Answer: 189 W

question: A current of 5.1 A flows through a 24 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 5.1, R = 24 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (5.1)^2 * 24 | Answer: 624.2 W

question: Two capacitors 24.8 uF and 43.1 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 24.8, C2 = 43.1 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 24.8*43.1 / (24.8+43.1) | Answer: 15.74 uF

question: A resistor 51 kohm and capacitor 14.7 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 51, C = 14.7 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (51k)(14.7u) = 749.7 ms | Answer: 749.7 ms

question: An inductor 380.9 mH is in series with 105 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 380.9, R = 105 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (380.9e-3) / 105 | Answer: 3.628 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 62.9 mH inductor at 310 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 62.9, f = 310 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (310)(62.9e-3) | Answer: 122.5 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 24.8 uF capacitor at 370 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 24.8, f = 370 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (370)(24.8e-6)) | Answer: 17.34 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 46 ohm, XL = 35 ohm and XC = 33 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 46, XL = 35, XC = 33 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(46^2 + (35 - 33)^2) | Answer: 46.04 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 29.6 mH and C = 1.8 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 29.6, C = 1.8 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(29.6e-3 * 1.8e-6)) | Answer: 689.5 Hz

question: A capacitor of 7.7 uF is charged to 60 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 7.7, V = 60 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*7.7e-6*(60)^2 | Answer: 13.86 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 340 V with 910 primary turns and 40 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 340, N1 = 910, N2 = 40 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 340 * 40/910 | Answer: 14.95 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 240 V and draws an armature current of 46 A. If the armature resistance is 1.38 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 240, Ia = 46, Ra = 1.38 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 240 - 46*1.38 | Answer: 176.5 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 135 A at 433 V (line) with a power factor of 0.84. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 135, VL = 433, pf = 0.84 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*433*135*0.84 / 1000 | Answer: 85.05 kW

question: A load has real power 125 kW and apparent power 185 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 125, S = 185 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 125 / 185 | Answer: 0.6757

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 19 V across R1 = 21 ohm and R2 = 14 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 19, R1 = 21, R2 = 14 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 19*14 / (21+14) | Answer: 7.6 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 190 kohm and Rin = 21 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 190, Rin = 21 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 190 / 21 | Answer: 9.048

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 190 kohm and Rg = 35 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 190, Rg = 35 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 190/35 | Answer: 6.429

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 2649. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 2649 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(2649) | Answer: 34.23 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 7.6 m carries a central point load of 110 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 7.6, W = 110 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 110*7.6 / 4 | Answer: 209 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 1 m carries a point load 55 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 1, W = 55 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 55*1 | Answer: 55 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 2.8 m carries a UDL of 32 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 2.8, w = 32 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 32*(2.8)^2 / 2 | Answer: 125.4 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 5.3 m carries a point load 40 kN at distance 1.9 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 5.3, a = 1.9, W = 40 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 40*(5.3 - 1.9) / 5.3 | Answer: 25.66 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 5.1 m) carries a central point load 55 kN. With E = 200 GPa and I = 270e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=55000 N, L=5100.0 mm, E=200000 MPa, I=270e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 2.815 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 5.3 m carries a UDL of 36 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 5.3, w = 36 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 36*(5.3)^2 / 12 | Answer: 84.27 kN-m

question: A column supports a floor area of 29.5 m^2 carrying a factored load of 16.2 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 29.5, w = 16.2 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 16.2 * 29.5 | Answer: 477.9 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 5.7 m, unit weight 20 kN/m^3, phi = 37 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 1.8e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 0.9, area = 2.1e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 1.8, i = 0.9, A = 2.1 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (1.8e-4)*0.9*(2.1e-3) | Answer: 340.2 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 2 m, bed slope 0.008 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.025. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 4.4 m under a head of 0.7 m. Taking Cd = 0.6 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 5.3 m wide carries a discharge of 4.2 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A tank of volume 630 m^3 treats a flow of 160 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 630, Q = 160 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 630 / 160 | Answer: 3.938 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 300 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.19 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 7 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 300, k = 0.19, t = 7 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 300*(1 - e^(-0.19*7)) | Answer: 220.7 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.57, rainfall intensity 120 mm/h over a catchment of 47 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.57, i = 120, A = 47 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.57*120*47 / 360 | Answer: 8.93 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 20 m is actually 0.01 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 660 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 20, e = 0.01, M = 660 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 660*(20+0.01)/20 | Answer: 660.3 m

question: Convert the decimal number 2945 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 2945 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: B81 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 11110101 and 11010101.
solution: XOR: 00100000 | Count of 1s = 1 | Answer: 1
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 90 megabits is sent over a link of 98 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 90, B = 98 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 90 / 98 | Answer: 0.9184 s

question: A link has bandwidth 73 Mbps and round-trip time 110 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 73, R = 110 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 73e6 * 110e-3 bits = 8030 kb | Answer: 8030 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.91, cache access time 2 ns and main-memory access time 200 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.91, tc = 2, tm = 200 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.91*2 + (1 - 0.91)*200 | Answer: 19.82 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 421179 elements?
solution: Given: n = 421179 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(421179)) + 1 | Answer: 19

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.01, memory access time 90 ns and page-fault service time 5 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 5 ms = 5000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.01)*90 + 0.01*5000000.0 ns | Answer: 50.09 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 2.8 m^3 at 450 kPa and 380 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 2.8, P = 450, Tk = 380 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (450e3)*2.8 / (8.314*380) | Answer: 398.8 mol

question: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.37 /min. Find the fractional conversion after 9 minutes.
solution: Given: k = 0.37, t = 9 | Formula: X = 1 - e^(-k t) | Substitute: X = 1 - e^(-0.37*9) | Answer: 0.9642

question: For a reaction with A = 9e10 /s and activation energy 90 kJ/mol at 400 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 9, Ea = 90, Tk = 400 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 9e10 * exp(-90e3 / (8.314*400)) | Answer: 0.1589 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.98 and bottoms xW = 0.1, with relative volatility alpha = 2.9. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.98, xw = 0.1, al = 2.9 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.98/0.02)(0.9/0.1)] / ln(2.9) | Answer: 5.719 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.68 and x = 0.36. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.68, x = 0.36 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.68/0.32) / (0.36/0.64) | Answer: 3.778

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.65 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 25 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.65, Psat = 25 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.65 * 25 | Answer: 16.25 kPa

question: A stream of 3.4 kg/s with specific heat 3.4 kJ/kg-K is heated through 90 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 3.4, cp = 3.4, dT = 90 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 3.4*3.4*90 | Answer: 104 kW

question: A reactor of volume 5.9 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 4.9 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 5.9, Q = 4.9 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 5.9 / 4.9 | Answer: 1.204 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 1e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 5 mm with a concentration difference of 60 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 1, L = 5, dC = 60 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (1e-9)*60 / (5e-3) | Answer: 12 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 7 min and steady-state gain 0.5. For a step input of magnitude 17, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 7, K = 0.5, M = 17 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 0.5 * 17 | Answer: 8.5 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 115 m^2 flies at 140 m/s (air density 0.7 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 1. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 115, V = 140, rho = 0.7, CL = 1 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.7*(140)^2*115*1 / 1000 | Answer: 788.9 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 50 m^2 flies at 160 m/s (density 1 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.12. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 50, V = 160, rho = 1, CD = 0.12 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*1*(160)^2*50*0.12 / 1000 | Answer: 76.8 kN

question: A specimen under stress 300 MPa shows an elastic strain of 1.3e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 300, eps = 1.3 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 300 / (1.3e-3) MPa = 230.8 GPa | Answer: 230.8 GPa

question: A block of mass 10 kg has a volume of 4.7e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 10, V = 4.7 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 10 / (4.7e-3) | Answer: 2128 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 600 mm is heated through 110 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 11e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 600, dT = 110, al = 11 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 600*11e-6*110 | Answer: 0.726 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 190 ohm, R2 = 60 ohm and R3 = 230 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 190, R2 = 60, R3 = 230 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 60*230 / 190 | Answer: 72.63 ohm

question: Annual demand is 21000 units, ordering cost 30 per order and holding cost 19 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 21000, S = 30, H = 19 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*21000*30 / 19) | Answer: 257.5 units

question: An asset costs 170000 with salvage value 38000 after 12 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 170000, Sv = 38000, n = 12 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (170000 - 38000) / 12 | Answer: 11000 per year

question: A product sells for 430 per unit with variable cost 80 per unit and fixed costs 125000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 430, V = 80, F = 125000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 125000 / (430 - 80) | Answer: 357.1 units

question: Find the present worth of 160000 received 7 years from now at an interest rate of 9% per year.
solution: Given: F = 160000, n = 7, i = 9 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 160000 / (1 + 0.09)^7 | Answer: 87525 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.9, 0.93 and 0.9 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.9, r2 = 0.93, r3 = 0.9 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.9*0.93*0.9 | Answer: 0.7533

question: A process produces 33 defective items in a batch of 7500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 33, N = 7500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 33/7500 * 1e6 | Answer: 4400 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = -x^3 - 5x^2 + 2x - 4 evaluated at x = -3.
For f(x) = x^3 + 3x^2 + 6, find f''(x) at x = -2.
Evaluate the definite integral of (-x^2 - 2x - 3) dx from x = -2 to x = 4.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = -1x^3/3 + -2x^2/2 + -3x | Evaluate F(4) - F(-2) | Answer: -54
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 6x^2 - 10x - 3 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[0, 7], [5, 2]].
solution: Given: a = 0, b = 7, c = 5, d = 2 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (0)(2) - (7)(5) | Answer: -35

question: Find the determinant of [[3, -3, -5], [-4, -5, 2], [4, -3, -1]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: -139

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[4, 5], [-1, -7]].
solution: Trace tr = -3, Determinant = -23 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 3.525

question: Solve for x: 3x + -1y = 11 and -4x + 2y = 11.
solution: Determinant = 3*2 - -1*-4 = 2 | x = (e d - b f) / det = 16.5 | Answer: x = 16.5
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 91, 95, 29, 1, 57.
solution: Sum = 273 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 54.6 | Answer: 54.6

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 37, 50, 32, 22, 49.
solution: Mean = 38 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 11.81

question: Find the slope of the line through (-5, 5) and (-6, -5).
solution: Given: x1 = -5, y1 = 5, x2 = -6, y2 = -5 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (-5 - 5) / (-6 - -5) | Answer: 10

question: Find the distance between the points (4, 9) and (-1, 0).
solution: Given: x1 = 4, y1 = 9, x2 = -1, y2 = 0 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-5)^2 + (-9)^2) | Answer: 10.3 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (-4,7), (-5,7), (-7,1).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 3 sq units

question: Find the 18th term of an arithmetic progression with first term -16 and common difference 7.
solution: Given: a = -16, d = 7, n = 18 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = -16 + (18 - 1)*7 | Answer: 103

question: Find the sum of the first 9 terms of an AP with first term 7 and common difference 3.
solution: Given: a = 7, d = 3, n = 9 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 9/2 [2*7 + (9-1)*3] | Answer: 171

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 13500 at 6.2% per annum for 9 years.
solution: Given: P = 13500, R = 6.2, Tt = 9 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 13500 * 6.2 * 9 / 100 | Answer: 7533 currency units

question: Find the amount when 6500 is invested at 6.3% per annum compounded annually for 4 years.
solution: Given: P = 6500, R = 6.3, Tt = 4 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 6500 * (1 + 6.3/100)^4 | Answer: 8299 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (4, 1, 4) and (8, -5, -1).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (3, 5, -3) and (-3, 4, 3).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 38.18

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (1, 1, -4) and (5, -5, -5).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 57.02 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = 5x^3 + 7x^2 + 2x - 8 at x = -5.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-190 with initial guess x0=11, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.3 and ordinates 16, 11, 19, 16, 18, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 541 and 342.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 541 and 342 | Answer: GCD = 1

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 35 and 31.
solution: Given: a = 35, b = 31 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 35*31 / 1 | Answer: 1085
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 24 mm carries an axial tensile load of 92 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 18 mm and length 2400 mm carries an axial load of 35 kN. Take E = 110 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 69 mm transmits a torque of 2750 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 69, Tt = 2750 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(2750*1000) / (pi*(69)^3) | Answer: 42.63 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 47 mm and length 1500 mm carries a torque of 1650 N-m. With G = 80 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (47)^4 / 32 = 479062 mm^4 | theta = (1650*1000)(1500) / (80000 * 479062) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 3.7 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 144 mm wide and 70 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 144, h = 70 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 144*(70)^2 / 6 | Answer: 117600 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (69 mm x 250 mm) carries a bending moment of 25 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (40 mm x 100 mm) has effective length 3500 mm and E = 200 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 830 MPa is designed for a working stress of 170 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 830, sw = 170 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 830 / 170 | Answer: 4.882

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 550 mm and wall thickness 12 mm carries an internal pressure of 0.6 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 550, t = 12, P = 0.6 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 0.6*550 / (2*12) | Answer: 13.75 MPa

question: 2 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 175 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 2, dT = 175 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 2 * 0.718 * 175 | Answer: 251.3 kJ

question: 5.8 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 140 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 5.8, dT = 140 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 5.8 * 1.005 * 140 | Answer: 816.1 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 3.4 m^3 at 340 K with mass 1.3 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 3.4, Tk = 340, m = 1.3 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 1.3*0.287*340 / 3.4 | Answer: 37.31 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 1.3 kg of air expands isothermally at 400 K from volume V1 to 5*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1.3, Tk = 400, ratio = 5 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 1.3*0.287*400*ln(5) | Answer: 240.2 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 2 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.3 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 2, D = 0.3 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*2*0.3 / 0.001 | Answer: 600000

question: Water flows at 1.9 m/s through a pipe of diameter 300 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 17.1 m. Taking Cv = 0.96, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 17.1, cv = 0.96 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.96*sqrt(2*9.81*17.1) | Answer: 17.58 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 380 mm) water flows at 2.7 m/s. It contracts to diameter 130 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
Water flows at 1.9 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.45 m and length 120 m. With friction factor f = 0.027, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 40 teeth drives a gear of 57 teeth. If the pinion runs at 1500 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 40, z2 = 57, N1 = 1500 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 1500*40 / 57 | Answer: 1053 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 500 mm rotates at 1000 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 500, N = 1000 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.5)*1000 / 60 | Answer: 26.18 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 11.7 kW at 550 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 11.7, N = 550 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(11.7*1000) / (2*pi*550) | Answer: 203.1 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 2.5 kg rotates at radius 0.54 m at 1150 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 14800 N/m and mass 18.5 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 14800, m = 18.5 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(14800/18.5) | Answer: 4.502 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 3.4 m^2 and thickness 0.39 m has conductivity k = 22.5 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 90 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 3.4, L = 0.39, k = 22.5, dT = 90 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 22.5*3.4*90 / 0.39 | Answer: 17654 W

question: A surface of area 2.9 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 155 W/m^2-K to surroundings 120 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 2.9, h = 155, dT = 120 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 155*2.9*120 | Answer: 53940 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 60 m/min, feed = 0.15 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2.2 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
solution: Given: v = 60, f = 0.15, d = 2.2 | Formula: MRR = 1000 v f d | Substitute: MRR = 1000*60*0.15*2.2 | Answer: 19800 mm^3/min

question: A workpiece of length 440 mm is turned at 850 rpm with a feed of 0.11 mm/rev. Find the machining time for one pass in minutes.
solution: Given: L = 440, N = 850, f = 0.11 | Formula: t = L / (f N) | Substitute: t = 440 / (0.11*850) | Answer: 4.706 min

question: A resistor of 173 ohm carries a current of 9 A. Find the voltage across it.
solution: Given: R = 173, I = 9 | Formula: V = I R | Substitute: V = 9 * 173 | Answer: 1557 V

question: Three resistors 37 ohm, 14 ohm and 55 ohm are connected in series. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 37, R2 = 14, R3 = 55 | Formula: Req = R1 + R2 + R3 | Substitute: Req = 37 + 14 + 55 | Answer: 106 ohm

question: Two resistors 26 ohm and 20 ohm are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
solution: Given: R1 = 26, R2 = 20 | Formula: Req = R1 R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Req = 26*20 / (26+20) | Answer: 11.3 ohm

question: A device draws 2.4 A at 15 V. Find the power consumed.
solution: Given: V = 15, I = 2.4 | Formula: P = V I | Substitute: P = 15 * 2.4 | Answer: 36 W

question: A current of 0.3 A flows through a 20 ohm resistor. Find the power dissipated.
solution: Given: I = 0.3, R = 20 | Formula: P = I^2 R | Substitute: P = (0.3)^2 * 20 | Answer: 1.8 W

question: Two capacitors 35.9 uF and 39.5 uF are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance in uF.
solution: Given: C1 = 35.9, C2 = 39.5 | Formula: Ceq = C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) | Substitute: Ceq = 35.9*39.5 / (35.9+39.5) | Answer: 18.81 uF

question: A resistor 40 kohm and capacitor 19.4 uF form a series RC circuit. Find the time constant in ms.
solution: Given: R = 40, C = 19.4 | Formula: tau = R C | Substitute: tau = (40k)(19.4u) = 776 ms | Answer: 776 ms

question: An inductor 41.2 mH is in series with 195 ohm. Find the time constant of the RL circuit in ms.
solution: Given: L = 41.2, R = 195 | Formula: tau = L / R | Substitute: tau = (41.2e-3) / 195 | Answer: 0.2113 ms

question: Find the inductive reactance of a 21.1 mH inductor at 290 Hz.
solution: Given: L = 21.1, f = 290 | Formula: XL = 2 pi f L | Substitute: XL = 2 pi (290)(21.1e-3) | Answer: 38.45 ohm

question: Find the capacitive reactance of a 25.4 uF capacitor at 150 Hz.
solution: Given: C = 25.4, f = 150 | Formula: XC = 1 / (2 pi f C) | Substitute: XC = 1 / (2 pi (150)(25.4e-6)) | Answer: 41.77 ohm

question: A series RLC circuit has R = 67 ohm, XL = 23 ohm and XC = 107 ohm. Find the magnitude of the impedance.
solution: Given: R = 67, XL = 23, XC = 107 | Formula: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) | Substitute: Z = sqrt(67^2 + (23 - 107)^2) | Answer: 107.4 ohm

question: Find the resonant frequency of a series circuit with L = 35.7 mH and C = 3.9 uF (in Hz).
solution: Given: L = 35.7, C = 3.9 | Formula: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) | Substitute: f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(35.7e-3 * 3.9e-6)) | Answer: 426.5 Hz

question: A capacitor of 12.3 uF is charged to 110 V. Find the energy stored in millijoules.
solution: Given: C = 12.3, V = 110 | Formula: E = 0.5 C V^2 | Substitute: E = 0.5*12.3e-6*(110)^2 | Answer: 74.42 mJ

question: A transformer has primary voltage 400 V with 990 primary turns and 410 secondary turns. Find the secondary voltage.
solution: Given: V1 = 400, N1 = 990, N2 = 410 | Formula: V2 = V1 (N2 / N1) | Substitute: V2 = 400 * 410/990 | Answer: 165.7 V

question: A DC motor is supplied at 250 V and draws an armature current of 28 A. If the armature resistance is 1.27 ohm, find the back EMF.
solution: Given: V = 250, Ia = 28, Ra = 1.27 | Formula: Eb = V - Ia Ra | Substitute: Eb = 250 - 28*1.27 | Answer: 214.4 V

question: A balanced 3-phase load draws a line current of 55 A at 433 V (line) with a power factor of 0.85. Find the total real power in kW.
solution: Given: IL = 55, VL = 433, pf = 0.85 | Formula: P = sqrt(3) VL IL cos(phi) | Substitute: P = sqrt(3)*433*55*0.85 / 1000 | Answer: 35.06 kW

question: A load has real power 155 kW and apparent power 195 kVA. Find the power factor.
solution: Given: P = 155, S = 195 | Formula: pf = P / S | Substitute: pf = 155 / 195 | Answer: 0.7949

question: A machine delivers 80 kW output while drawing 217 kW input. Find its efficiency (%).
solution: Given: Po = 80, Pi = 217 | Formula: eta = (P_out / P_in) * 100 | Substitute: eta = 80/217 * 100 | Answer: 36.87 %

question: In a voltage divider, Vin = 28 V across R1 = 20 ohm and R2 = 12 ohm in series. Find the output voltage across R2.
solution: Given: Vin = 28, R1 = 20, R2 = 12 | Formula: Vout = Vin R2 / (R1 + R2) | Substitute: Vout = 28*12 / (20+12) | Answer: 10.5 V

question: An inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 140 kohm and Rin = 40 kohm. Find the voltage gain (magnitude).
solution: Given: Rf = 140, Rin = 40 | Formula: |A| = Rf / Rin | Substitute: |A| = 140 / 40 | Answer: 3.5

question: A non-inverting op-amp amplifier has Rf = 180 kohm and Rg = 30 kohm. Find the voltage gain.
solution: Given: Rf = 180, Rg = 30 | Formula: A = 1 + Rf / Rg | Substitute: A = 1 + 180/30 | Answer: 7

question: An amplifier has an output/input power ratio of 6651. Express the gain in decibels (power).
solution: Given: ratio = 6651 | Formula: Gain(dB) = 10 log10(Pout/Pin) | Substitute: Gain = 10 log10(6651) | Answer: 38.23 dB

question: A simply supported beam of span 6.2 m carries a central point load of 80 kN. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6.2, W = 80 | Formula: Mmax = W L / 4 | Substitute: Mmax = 80*6.2 / 4 | Answer: 124 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 2.6 m carries a point load 15 kN at its free end. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 2.6, W = 15 | Formula: Mmax = W L | Substitute: Mmax = 15*2.6 | Answer: 39 kN-m

question: A cantilever of length 4.5 m carries a UDL of 8 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 4.5, w = 8 | Formula: Mmax = w L^2 / 2 | Substitute: Mmax = 8*(4.5)^2 / 2 | Answer: 81 kN-m

question: A simply supported beam of span 9.9 m carries a point load 15 kN at distance 1.2 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
solution: Given: L = 9.9, a = 1.2, W = 15 | Formula: R_left = W (L - a) / L | Substitute: R_left = 15*(9.9 - 1.2) / 9.9 | Answer: 13.18 kN

question: A simply supported beam (span 7 m) carries a central point load 20 kN. With E = 30 GPa and I = 260e6 mm^4, find the maximum deflection in mm.
solution: Use consistent N-mm units: W=20000 N, L=7000.0 mm, E=30000 MPa, I=260e6 mm^4 | delta = W L^3 / (48 E I) | Answer: 18.32 mm

question: A fixed beam of span 6.9 m carries a UDL of 45 kN/m. Find the magnitude of the fixed-end moment in kN-m.
solution: Given: L = 6.9, w = 45 | Formula: M = w L^2 / 12 | Substitute: M = 45*(6.9)^2 / 12 | Answer: 178.5 kN-m

question: An RC beam has overall depth 360 mm, clear cover 50 mm and main bars of diameter 12 mm. Find the effective depth in mm.
solution: Given: D = 360, c = 50, dia = 12 | Formula: d = D - cover - (bar diameter)/2 | Substitute: d = 360 - 50 - 12/2 | Answer: 304 mm

question: A column supports a floor area of 39.7 m^2 carrying a factored load of 14 kN/m^2. Find the total factored axial load in kN.
solution: Given: A = 39.7, w = 14 | Formula: P = w * tributary area | Substitute: P = 14 * 39.7 | Answer: 555.8 kN

question: A smooth vertical wall retains cohesionless backfill of height 4.7 m, unit weight 18 kN/m^3, phi = 34 degrees. Find the total active thrust per metre run (kN/m).
formula: Pa = 0.5 Ka gamma H^2,  Ka = (1 - sin phi)/(1 + sin phi)

question: In a constant-head permeameter, k = 6.4e-4 m/s, hydraulic gradient i = 1.1, area = 1.1e-3 m^2. Find the seepage discharge in mm^3/s.
solution: Given: k = 6.4, i = 1.1, A = 1.1 | Formula: q = k i A | Substitute: q = (6.4e-4)*1.1*(1.1e-3) | Answer: 774.4 mm^3/s

question: An open channel has hydraulic radius 1.7 m, bed slope 0.009 (as a fraction) and Manning's n = 0.022. Find the mean velocity in m/s.
Water flows over a rectangular weir of crest length 3.5 m under a head of 1.1 m. Taking Cd = 0.63 (g = 9.81), find the discharge in m^3/s.
formula: Q = (2/3) Cd sqrt(2 g) L H^(3/2)

question: A rectangular channel 2 m wide carries a discharge of 18.1 m^3/s. Find the critical depth in m (g = 9.81).
A tank of volume 800 m^3 treats a flow of 130 m^3/h. Find the hydraulic retention time in hours.
solution: Given: V = 800, Q = 130 | Formula: HRT = Volume / Flow rate | Substitute: HRT = 800 / 130 | Answer: 6.154 h

question: The ultimate BOD of a sample is 270 mg/L and the deoxygenation rate constant k = 0.17 /day. Find the BOD exerted in 7 days.
solution: Given: L0 = 270, k = 0.17, t = 7 | Formula: BOD_t = L0 (1 - e^(-k t)) | Substitute: BOD_t = 270*(1 - e^(-0.17*7)) | Answer: 187.9 mg/L

question: Using the rational method with runoff coefficient C = 0.48, rainfall intensity 50 mm/h over a catchment of 19.6 hectares, find the peak runoff in m^3/s.
solution: Given: C = 0.48, i = 50, A = 19.6 | Formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares) | Substitute: Q = 0.48*50*19.6 / 360 | Answer: 1.307 m^3/s
formula: Q = C i A / 360  (i in mm/h, A in hectares)

question: A tape of nominal length 30 m is actually 0.07 m too long. Find the correct length of a line measured as 190 m with this tape.
solution: Given: L = 30, e = 0.07, M = 190 | Formula: True length = Measured * (L + e) / L | Substitute: True = 190*(30+0.07)/30 | Answer: 190.4 m

question: Convert the decimal number 260 to hexadecimal (uppercase).
solution: Divide 260 by 16 repeatedly, recording remainders | Answer: 104 (hex)
formula: Repeatedly divide by 16 and read remainders bottom-up

question: Compute the Hamming distance between the 8-bit words 11010110 and 01011100.
solution: XOR: 10001010 | Count of 1s = 3 | Answer: 3
formula: Hamming distance = number of differing bit positions

question: A file of 500 megabits is sent over a link of 38 Mbps. Find the transmission time in seconds.
solution: Given: S = 500, B = 38 | Formula: t = size / bandwidth | Substitute: t = 500 / 38 | Answer: 13.16 s

question: A link has bandwidth 68 Mbps and round-trip time 60 ms. Find the bandwidth-delay product in kilobits.
solution: Given: B = 68, R = 60 | Formula: BDP = bandwidth * RTT | Substitute: BDP = 68e6 * 60e-3 bits = 4080 kb | Answer: 4080 kilobits

question: A cache has a hit ratio of 0.88, cache access time 10 ns and main-memory access time 170 ns. Find the effective (average) memory access time in ns.
solution: Given: h = 0.88, tc = 10, tm = 170 | Formula: EAT = h * tc + (1 - h) * tm | Substitute: EAT = 0.88*10 + (1 - 0.88)*170 | Answer: 29.2 ns

question: In the worst case, how many comparisons does binary search make on a sorted array of 586605 elements?
solution: Given: n = 586605 | Formula: comparisons = floor(log2(n)) + 1 | Substitute: floor(log2(586605)) + 1 | Answer: 20

question: A demand-paging system has page-fault rate 0.019, memory access time 130 ns and page-fault service time 10 ms. Find the effective access time in microseconds.
solution: Service time = 10 ms = 10000000.0 ns | EAT = (1 - 0.019)*130 + 0.019*10000000.0 ns | Answer: 190.1 microseconds
formula: EAT = (1 - pf) * ma + pf * (page-fault service time)

question: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying 0.8 m^3 at 380 kPa and 480 K (R = 8.314 J/mol-K).
solution: Given: V = 0.8, P = 380, Tk = 480 | Formula: n = P V / (R T) | Substitute: n = (380e3)*0.8 / (8.314*480) | Answer: 76.18 mol

question: For a reaction with A = 1e10 /s and activation energy 60 kJ/mol at 400 K, find the rate constant (per second). Take R = 8.314 J/mol-K.
solution: Given: A = 1, Ea = 60, Tk = 400 | Formula: k = A exp(-Ea / (R T)) | Substitute: k = 1e10 * exp(-60e3 / (8.314*400)) | Answer: 146.1 /s

question: In a binary distillation, distillate mole fraction xD = 0.98 and bottoms xW = 0.03, with relative volatility alpha = 3.2. Find the minimum number of theoretical stages (Fenske).
solution: Given: xd = 0.98, xw = 0.03, al = 3.2 | Formula: Nmin = ln[(xD/(1-xD)) ((1-xW)/xW)] / ln(alpha) | Substitute: Nmin = ln[(0.98/0.02)(0.97/0.03)] / ln(3.2) | Answer: 6.334 stages

question: Vapour and liquid mole fractions of the light component are y = 0.82 and x = 0.34. Find the relative volatility alpha (binary).
solution: Given: y = 0.82, x = 0.34 | Formula: alpha = [y/(1-y)] / [x/(1-x)] | Substitute: alpha = (0.82/0.18) / (0.34/0.66) | Answer: 8.843

question: A liquid has mole fraction 0.55 of a component whose pure-component vapour pressure is 60 kPa. Using Raoult's law, find its partial pressure in kPa.
solution: Given: x = 0.55, Psat = 60 | Formula: p_i = x_i Psat | Substitute: p_i = 0.55 * 60 | Answer: 33 kPa

question: A stream of 5.6 kg/s with specific heat 3 kJ/kg-K is heated through 120 deg C. Find the heat duty in kW.
solution: Given: m = 5.6, cp = 3, dT = 120 | Formula: Q = m cp dT | Substitute: Q = 5.6*3*120 | Answer: 2016 kW

question: A reactor of volume 1.1 m^3 is fed at a volumetric rate of 2.6 m^3/min. Find the mean residence time in minutes.
solution: Given: V = 1.1, Q = 2.6 | Formula: tau = V / Q | Substitute: tau = 1.1 / 2.6 | Answer: 0.4231 min

question: Steady diffusion occurs with D = 4.3e-9 m^2/s across a film of thickness 1 mm with a concentration difference of 50 mol/m^3. Find the molar flux in micromol/m^2-s.
solution: Given: D = 4.3, L = 1, dC = 50 | Formula: J = D (dC / L) | Substitute: J = (4.3e-9)*50 / (1e-3) | Answer: 215 micromol/m^2-s

question: A first-order process has time constant 6.6 min and steady-state gain 3.4. For a step input of magnitude 20, find the final (steady-state) change in output.
solution: Given: tau = 6.6, K = 3.4, M = 20 | Formula: Delta y(inf) = K * M | Substitute: Delta y = 3.4 * 20 | Answer: 68 units

question: An aircraft wing of area 40 m^2 flies at 110 m/s (air density 0.4 kg/m^3) with lift coefficient 1. Find the lift force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 40, V = 110, rho = 0.4, CL = 1 | Formula: L = 0.5 rho V^2 S CL | Substitute: L = 0.5*0.4*(110)^2*40*1 / 1000 | Answer: 96.8 kN

question: An aircraft of wing area 110 m^2 flies at 110 m/s (density 1 kg/m^3) with drag coefficient 0.07. Find the drag force in kN.
solution: Given: S = 110, V = 110, rho = 1, CD = 0.07 | Formula: D = 0.5 rho V^2 S CD | Substitute: D = 0.5*1*(110)^2*110*0.07 / 1000 | Answer: 46.59 kN

question: A specimen under stress 300 MPa shows an elastic strain of 0.9e-3. Find the Young's modulus in GPa.
solution: Given: sig = 300, eps = 0.9 | Formula: E = stress / strain | Substitute: E = 300 / (0.9e-3) MPa = 333.3 GPa | Answer: 333.3 GPa

question: A block of mass 44 kg has a volume of 3.9e-3 m^3. Find its density in kg/m^3.
solution: Given: m = 44, V = 3.9 | Formula: density = mass / volume | Substitute: rho = 44 / (3.9e-3) | Answer: 11282 kg/m^3

question: A rod of length 1800 mm is heated through 55 deg C. With coefficient of thermal expansion 11e-6 /deg C, find the change in length in mm.
solution: Given: L = 1800, dT = 55, al = 11 | Formula: dL = L alpha dT | Substitute: dL = 1800*11e-6*55 | Answer: 1.089 mm

question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with R1 = 75 ohm, R2 = 80 ohm and R3 = 130 ohm. Find the unknown resistance R4 (R1/R2 = R3/R4).
solution: Given: R1 = 75, R2 = 80, R3 = 130 | Formula: R4 = R2 R3 / R1 | Substitute: R4 = 80*130 / 75 | Answer: 138.7 ohm

question: A measurement reads 9.67 when the true value is 20. Find the percentage error.
solution: Given: meas = 9.67, true = 20 | Formula: % error = |measured - true| / true * 100 | Substitute: % error = |9.67 - 20| / 20 * 100 | Answer: 51.65 %

question: Annual demand is 23500 units, ordering cost 180 per order and holding cost 6 per unit per year. Find the economic order quantity (EOQ).
solution: Given: D = 23500, S = 180, H = 6 | Formula: EOQ = sqrt(2 D S / H) | Substitute: EOQ = sqrt(2*23500*180 / 6) | Answer: 1187 units

question: An asset costs 390000 with salvage value 16000 after 14 years. Find the annual straight-line depreciation.
solution: Given: C = 390000, Sv = 16000, n = 14 | Formula: Depreciation = (Cost - Salvage) / life | Substitute: D = (390000 - 16000) / 14 | Answer: 26714 per year

question: A product sells for 210 per unit with variable cost 170 per unit and fixed costs 175000. Find the break-even quantity in units.
solution: Given: P = 210, V = 170, F = 175000 | Formula: Q_be = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost) | Substitute: Q = 175000 / (210 - 170) | Answer: 4375 units

question: Find the present worth of 160000 received 9 years from now at an interest rate of 8% per year.
solution: Given: F = 160000, n = 9, i = 8 | Formula: PW = F / (1 + i)^n | Substitute: PW = 160000 / (1 + 0.08)^9 | Answer: 8004 currency units

question: Three components with reliabilities 0.93, 0.95 and 0.97 are connected in series. Find the system reliability.
solution: Given: r1 = 0.93, r2 = 0.95, r3 = 0.97 | Formula: R_series = r1 * r2 * r3 | Substitute: R = 0.93*0.95*0.97 | Answer: 0.857

question: A process produces 9 defective items in a batch of 6500. Find the defect rate in parts per million (PPM).
solution: Given: def = 9, N = 6500 | Formula: PPM = (defects / total) * 1e6 | Substitute: PPM = 9/6500 * 1e6 | Answer: 1385 PPM

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = 6x^3 - 4x^2 - 3x + 5 evaluated at x = -5.
For f(x) = 6x^3 + x^2 + 9x + 6, find f''(x) at x = -2.
Evaluate the definite integral of (5x^2 - x + 8) dx from x = -4 to x = 3.
solution: Antiderivative F(x) = 5x^3/3 + -1x^2/2 + 8x | Evaluate F(3) - F(-4) | Answer: 211.2
formula: integral = a x^3/3 + b x^2/2 + c x

question: Find the larger real root of 4x^2 + 10x - 7 = 0.
Find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix [[7, 8], [5, 2]].
solution: Given: a = 7, b = 8, c = 5, d = 2 | Formula: det = ad - bc | Substitute: det = (7)(2) - (8)(5) | Answer: -26

question: Find the determinant of [[0, 4, -3], [-5, 0, -3], [3, 6, -5]].
solution: Expand along the first row: | det = a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) | Answer: -46

question: Find the larger eigenvalue of [[5, -3], [-1, 2]].
solution: Trace tr = 7, Determinant = 7 | lambda = (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)) / 2 | Answer: 5.791

question: Solve for x: 2x + 3y = 4 and 0x + 2y = -5.
solution: Determinant = 2*2 - 3*0 = 4 | x = (e d - b f) / det = 5.75 | Answer: x = 5.75
formula: x = (e d - b f) / (a d - b c)  [Cramer's rule]

question: Find the arithmetic mean of the data set: 85, 64, 74, 97, 30.
solution: Sum = 350 | Mean = Sum / 5 = 70 | Answer: 70

question: Find the sample standard deviation of: 27, 5, 2, 50, 8.
solution: Mean = 18.4 | Compute squared deviations, sum them, divide by (n-1)=4, take the square root | Answer: s = 20.18

question: Find the slope of the line through (7, -3) and (-1, 1).
solution: Given: x1 = 7, y1 = -3, x2 = -1, y2 = 1 | Formula: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) | Substitute: m = (1 - -3) / (-1 - 7) | Answer: -0.5

question: Find the distance between the points (3, -4) and (-2, 0).
solution: Given: x1 = 3, y1 = -4, x2 = -2, y2 = 0 | Formula: d = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) | Substitute: d = sqrt((-5)^2 + (4)^2) | Answer: 6.403 units

question: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (7,5), (4,2), (6,5).
solution: Apply the shoelace formula: | Area = 0.5 |x1(y2-y3) + x2(y3-y1) + x3(y1-y2)| | Answer: 1.5 sq units

question: Find the 29th term of an arithmetic progression with first term 14 and common difference 5.
solution: Given: a = 14, d = 5, n = 29 | Formula: a_n = a + (n - 1) d | Substitute: a_n = 14 + (29 - 1)*5 | Answer: 154

question: Find the sum of the first 25 terms of an AP with first term 8 and common difference 8.
solution: Given: a = 8, d = 8, n = 25 | Formula: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] | Substitute: S_n = 25/2 [2*8 + (25-1)*8] | Answer: 2600

question: Find the simple interest on a principal of 19000 at 10.9% per annum for 2 years.
solution: Given: P = 19000, R = 10.9, Tt = 2 | Formula: SI = P R T / 100 | Substitute: SI = 19000 * 10.9 * 2 / 100 | Answer: 4142 currency units

question: Find the amount when 7500 is invested at 10.5% per annum compounded annually for 6 years.
solution: Given: P = 7500, R = 10.5, Tt = 6 | Formula: A = P (1 + R/100)^T | Substitute: A = 7500 * (1 + 10.5/100)^6 | Answer: 13653 currency units

question: Find the dot product of vectors (-2, 7, -7) and (6, 6, 0).
formula: a . b = a1 b1 + a2 b2 + a3 b3

question: Find the magnitude of the cross product of (-2, -2, -3) and (1, -6, -2).
solution: Cross product c = a x b, then take its magnitude | Answer: 21

question: Find the angle (in degrees) between (6, 2, 0) and (6, -4, -4).
solution: Compute a.b, |a| and |b|, then theta = arccos(a.b/(|a||b|)) | Answer: 57.53 degrees

question: Evaluate f(x) = -4x^3 + 3x^2 - 7x - 3 at x = -4.
Using Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x^2-189 with initial guess x0=12, find x1 (one iteration).
Using the trapezoidal rule with step h=1.5 and ordinates 8, 10, 5, 5, 11, estimate the integral.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of 50 and 450.
solution: Apply the Euclidean algorithm to 50 and 450 | Answer: GCD = 50

question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 8 and 29.
solution: Given: a = 8, b = 29 | Formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b) | Substitute: LCM = 8*29 / 1 | Answer: 232
formula: LCM(a, b) = a b / GCD(a, b)

question: A circular rod of diameter 21 mm carries an axial tensile load of 50 kN. Find the direct stress in MPa.
A rod of diameter 40 mm and length 1100 mm carries an axial load of 32 kN. Take E = 210 GPa. Find the elongation in mm.
A solid shaft of diameter 61 mm transmits a torque of 2650 N-m. Find the maximum torsional shear stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 61, Tt = 2650 | Formula: tau = 16 T / (pi d^3) | Substitute: tau = 16*(2650*1000) / (pi*(61)^3) | Answer: 59.46 MPa

question: A shaft of diameter 56 mm and length 600 mm carries a torque of 850 N-m. With G = 80 GPa, find the angle of twist in degrees.
solution: J = pi (56)^4 / 32 = 965499 mm^4 | theta = (850*1000)(600) / (80000 * 965499) rad | Convert to degrees. Answer: 0.3783 degrees
formula: theta = T L / (G J),  J = pi d^4 / 32

question: A rectangular beam section is 106 mm wide and 80 mm deep. Find its section modulus about the horizontal axis in mm^3.
solution: Given: b = 106, h = 80 | Formula: Z = b h^2 / 6 | Substitute: Z = 106*(80)^2 / 6 | Answer: 113067 mm^3

question: A rectangular cross-section beam (70 mm x 260 mm) carries a bending moment of 34 kN-m. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
formula: sigma = M / Z,  Z = b h^2 / 6

question: A rectangular column (39 mm x 110 mm) has effective length 1900 mm and E = 210 GPa. Find the Euler buckling load in kN (buckling about the weak axis).
formula: Pcr = pi^2 E I / Le^2,  I = h b^3 / 12 (weak axis)

question: A component of ultimate strength 750 MPa is designed for a working stress of 210 MPa. Find the factor of safety.
solution: Given: su = 750, sw = 210 | Formula: FoS = ultimate strength / working stress | Substitute: FoS = 750 / 210 | Answer: 3.571

question: A thin cylindrical shell of internal diameter 900 mm and wall thickness 10 mm carries an internal pressure of 1.9 MPa. Find the hoop (circumferential) stress in MPa.
solution: Given: d = 900, t = 10, P = 1.9 | Formula: sigma_h = P d / (2 t) | Substitute: sigma_h = 1.9*900 / (2*10) | Answer: 85.5 MPa

question: 3.3 kg of air is heated at constant volume through 65 deg C. Taking cv = 0.718 kJ/kg-K, find the change in internal energy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 3.3, dT = 65 | Formula: dU = m cv dT | Substitute: dU = 3.3 * 0.718 * 65 | Answer: 154 kJ

question: 4.3 kg of air is heated at constant pressure through 170 deg C. Taking cp = 1.005 kJ/kg-K, find the change in enthalpy in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 4.3, dT = 170 | Formula: dH = m cp dT | Substitute: dH = 4.3 * 1.005 * 170 | Answer: 734.7 kJ

question: Air (R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K) occupies 3.4 m^3 at 590 K with mass 3.3 kg. Find the pressure in kPa (ideal gas).
solution: Given: V = 3.4, Tk = 590, m = 3.3 | Formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V | Substitute: p = 3.3*0.287*590 / 3.4 | Answer: 164.3 kPa
formula: p V = m R T  =>  p = m R T / V

question: 1.4 kg of air expands isothermally at 430 K from volume V1 to 2*V1. Take R = 0.287 kJ/kg-K. Find the work done in kJ.
solution: Given: m = 1.4, Tk = 430, ratio = 2 | Formula: W = m R T ln(V2/V1) | Substitute: W = 1.4*0.287*430*ln(2) | Answer: 119.8 kJ

question: Water (rho = 1000 kg/m^3, mu = 0.001 Pa-s) flows at 4.6 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.25 m. Find the Reynolds number.
solution: Given: V = 4.6, D = 0.25 | Formula: Re = rho V D / mu | Substitute: Re = 1000*4.6*0.25 / 0.001 | Answer: 1150000

question: Water flows at 3.2 m/s through a pipe of diameter 60 mm. Find the volumetric discharge in litres/second.
Water issues from an orifice under a head of 11.4 m. Taking Cv = 0.99, find the actual jet velocity in m/s (g = 9.81).
solution: Given: h = 11.4, cv = 0.99 | Formula: V = Cv sqrt(2 g h) | Substitute: V = 0.99*sqrt(2*9.81*11.4) | Answer: 14.81 m/s

question: In a pipe (diameter 190 mm) water flows at 0.9 m/s. It contracts to diameter 120 mm. Find the velocity in the smaller pipe (m/s).
Water flows at 3.7 m/s through a pipe of diameter 0.37 m and length 60 m. With friction factor f = 0.025, find the head loss due to friction in m (Darcy, g = 9.81).
formula: hf = f L V^2 / (2 g D)

question: A pinion of 31 teeth drives a gear of 76 teeth. If the pinion runs at 550 rpm, find the gear speed in rpm.
solution: Given: z1 = 31, z2 = 76, N1 = 550 | Formula: N1 z1 = N2 z2  =>  N2 = N1 z1 / z2 | Substitute: N2 = 550*31 / 76 | Answer: 224.3 rpm

question: A pulley of diameter 210 mm rotates at 1100 rpm. Find the belt (peripheral) speed in m/s.
solution: Given: D = 210, N = 1100 | Formula: v = pi D N / 60 | Substitute: v = pi*(0.21)*1100 / 60 | Answer: 12.1 m/s

question: A shaft transmits 35.8 kW at 600 rpm. Find the mean torque transmitted in N-m.
solution: Given: P = 35.8, N = 600 | Formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W) | Substitute: T = 60*(35.8*1000) / (2*pi*600) | Answer: 569.8 N-m
formula: T = 60 P / (2 pi N)  (P in W)

question: A mass of 7.3 kg rotates at radius 0.15 m at 1200 rpm. Find the centrifugal force in N.
formula: F = m w^2 r,  w = 2 pi N / 60

question: A spring-mass system has stiffness 16500 N/m and mass 12.1 kg. Find the natural frequency in Hz.
solution: Given: k = 16500, m = 12.1 | Formula: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(k/m) | Substitute: fn = (1/2pi) sqrt(16500/12.1) | Answer: 5.877 Hz

question: A plane wall of area 2.3 m^2 and thickness 0.36 m has conductivity k = 20.3 W/m-K. The temperature difference across it is 45 deg C. Find the heat conduction rate in W.
solution: Given: A = 2.3, L = 0.36, k = 20.3, dT = 45 | Formula: Q = k A dT / L | Substitute: Q = 20.3*2.3*45 / 0.36 | Answer: 5836 W

question: A surface of area 1.6 m^2 loses heat by convection with h = 155 W/m^2-K to surroundings 35 deg C cooler. Find the heat loss in W.
solution: Given: A = 1.6, h = 155, dT = 35 | Formula: Q = h A dT | Substitute: Q = 155*1.6*35 | Answer: 8680 W

question: In turning, cutting speed = 180 m/min, feed = 0.26 mm/rev, depth of cut = 2.8 mm. Find the material removal rate in mm^3/min.
